But story-wise, it's well worth my time and money and is just the right game for people for enjoy some D&D aspects to sit back, relax and enjoy at your own pace. Haven't finished it yet, but I know I'm loving what little 7 hours I went through and will probably enjoy the rest as well. And the artworks are absolutely stunning!!
_childDocuments_.name: Voice of Cards: The Isle Dragon Roars

_childDocuments_.name: Voice of Cards: The Isle Dragon Roars

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't played for too long yet, but so far this games aesthetic and writing has made the purchase worthwhile While under the guise of a table top game this is a jrpg to it's core and so far a really well done one. Will be way more detailed when I actually finish the game but am very impressed so farEdit 11/4/21  After just finishing the game I can safely say, that this a great entry to what i hope is a long lasting series of semishort rpgs done in a tabletop style.  I enjoyed my entire time with the game  and while i didn't do the superboss I had done most everything else outside of a few monster logs i missed. The character interactions, the occasional humor coming from the narrator  and beautiful (if a little narrow) music made this a great rpg that enjoyed from start to finish. Things i'd like in a sequel include more interpersonal dialog  outside of scens similar to the skits in tales of games,  the ability to change characters mid battle, and more skills and interplay between the members the game wasn't too difficult and for me that's fine as  I don't conflate difficulty with enjoyment but having more difficulty options would be best. Even more events and side quests would be enjoyable for me, and being able to do a little more customization of character and of the ui (more costume skins, card covers dice and boards.  I want to come back to this world, and i genuinely hope i can in the next year or two, whether with the current characters or a while new cast , I eagerly await what happens next in Voice of Cards.
_childDocuments_.name: Voice of Cards: The Isle Dragon Roars

_childDocuments_.review: As a die-hard Yoko Taro fan, it is hard not to see his influences throughout this game. From the synesthesia you get from listening to the music and events happening, to the quirky gameplay with questionable mechanics, its all here. This isn't a nier automata/replicant level game. This is more like a cute passion project that comes with unlimited creative freedom. Lasting no longer than 10-15 hours at a slow methodical pace, this game is short and sweet. Although this isn't a very deep story, it's still extremely well told for what it is. You can pretty much guess most plot points well before they happen. The music is great, the game is very immersive. I'd recommend this to any storytelling fan, and especially any yoko taro fan.Biggest annoyance, is the same I had with Nier games. Once you have what ever overtuned thing is in the game, the combat becomes rather trivial. Not much skill expression exists here, and it always makes me nervous with skilless combat meets RPG. All it takes is one overtuned encounter and you can be completely stuck. The way they work around this, is they make it more of a battle of attrition, managing resources so you don't run out of health before you beat the entire dungeon. The last fight is the only difficult one, and is remarkably more difficult than ANY other fight in the game. If you know how to meta game RPG's you likely will not see the game over screen regardless. I also would of liked to see individual card art for every NPC in the game. I think the reason they did this was stylistic, Old Final fantasy games and such would reuse assets to populate a town. So just a personal preference. Unlike nier the gameplay isn't really as enthralling, I mostlikely will wait till someone completes the game multiple times and shows off the payoff.

_childDocuments_.review: So far Voice of Cards: The Isle Dragon Roars has been fun to play (barely scratching the surface however with about an hour and a half played only) and I like the idea of the whole game being done with the card aesthetic. I can see some issues (or maybe personal nit picks) where I can think of a lot of ways in which the concept of the game could have been taken further and maybe even over the top more with wild ideas.Overall I like it though. This has been fun to play so far even if the story seems a bit basic so far. I would recommend this if you want an ok'ish rpg story (from what I can gather so far) with a unique look. I would pick up a sequel if one was to be made but I would want the card concept pushed even further with more wild idea's.

_childDocuments_.review: I Love This GameThe creator of NieR and Drakengard helms a turn-based RPG with a tabletop aesthetic, where a fantasy world is represented entirely by cards.Battles also possess random elements. The power of special attacks, or the affliction of status effects like paralysis or freeze, is often dictated by whether you throw a high enough number. You pull off these attacks by spending crystals you accumulate between turns, with stronger attacks costing more crystals. This combines with happenstance cards which change the power of certain elements or alter character stats for a turn randomly. As such, battles are about exploiting weaknesses, balancing your party’s skills, and hoping luck is on your side.Surprisingly, the best comparison for Voice Of Cards might be Paper Mario, with a similar reliance on a flat, 2D aesthetic for its visual charm. It’s satisfying to turn over cards to uncover a whole area, and transitions between menus and landscapes all share the snappy, tactile feeling of flicking through a deck of cards.Beautiful card design, gameplay and interesting story 	(*˘︶˘*).｡.:*♡----------------------------------------------------------------------Thank you Square Enix ⊂(´• ω •`⊂)

_childDocuments_.review: Only an hour in, but I'm really enjoying it. The narrator and sound design combined with the writing makes for a highly immersive experience with a lot of visual charm. Looking forward to more, but if you like JRPGs or Table Top RPGs, you'll likely find a lot of enjoyment here.After a total of around 10 hours, with 7.5 logged in a single save game file, I can definitely say this game was worth every penny. The storytelling was some of the best I've ever experienced out of a videogame. The story wasn't making me rethink my life or anything like that, but it was told in such a refreshing and fun way, that I was on the hook the entire time. The characters are dripping with personality, and the gameplay was simple, yet enjoyable. I might revisit the game in the future, but more likely, I would be eager to play another game by this studio of this style, as the journey is more important than the destination. I wholeheartedly recommend this game for any fan of dramatic narrative, such as DnD fans. Otherwise, make sure you collect all 10 event cards by the time you end the story, you'll thank me later...

_childDocuments_.review: I won't pretend that my own expectations didn't set me up for disappointment.When the creative director is Yoko Taro you kind of go in expecting some strange and memorable experience along the lines of drakengarde or Nier which will be unusual but ultimately something you'd consider worthwhile. that is NOT the case here.This is just a JRPG with a neat aesthetic. It LOOKS cool but it's just a basic JRPG and does very little to differentiate it from any other JRPG out there.Maybe get this on sale for 15 bucks if you're interested but i'll definitely temper my expectations for works with Yoko Taro's name on it from now on because this was a massive disappointment from the guy behind one of my favorite JRPGs to date.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the Demo and knew what I was buying before getting the game. It's not a card game, the cards are just an aesthetic - but it's an overall nice aesthetic that is fairly unique for just a typical JRPG. So far, the story is pretty good, but the systems are simplistic. This could be a problem for some, to be each their own on that one. I thoroughly suggest playing the Demo before making the blind purchase on this game, because in the 3 hours I've gotten the chance to play I've not had a lot of things thrown at me that wasn't present in the Demo. Overall, would I recommend? Absolutely, I'm really enjoying it - but I'm enjoying it for the Nier vibes and the uniqueness of it at a $30 price point. If that's not a selling enough point for you, I'd suggest waiting for it to be on sale.Also - the DLC is just cosmetic stuff, it in no way shape or form changes or influences the game.

Open your mind and let the story unfold. Voice of Cards: The Isle Dragon Roars is an RPG set in a world of swords and sorcery, told entirely through the medium of cards.
The story follows a self proclaimed hero as they set off to slay a recently awakened dragon, presented in the manner of a tabletop RPG and playing out through narration from the gamesmaster.
Enjoy an all new, yet appealingly nostalgic gaming experience from YOKO TARO (Creative Director), Keiichi Okabe (Music), Kimihiko Fujisaka (Character Design.)

name: Windjammers 2
detailed_description: 25 years later, throwing flying discs at your opponents is still as cool as back in the days. Sequel to the NEOGEO cult classic Windjammers, Windjammers 2 is the perfect mix between what you loved about the classic title and brand-new mechanics. Fast-paced, strategic, easy to learn but hard to master: Windjammers 2 follows the steps of the first episode and brings back what makes the Windjammers series an amazing fun and competitive game! A brand new, free update brings two new playable characters, Jamma GX03 and Anna Szalinski, a new training mode with dedicated lessons and customizable training course and a reworked online system, now with full crossplay, dedicated lobbies and spectator mode. Game on! New challengers, new stages, brand-new mechanics and awesome new power moves will make your head spin and enhance your windjammin’ experience. Master the slapshot, dropshot, the jump, the smash and the powerful super moves, and enjoy the kickass soundtrack coming straight out of the ’90s. Sophie De Lys 'Soyez prêts !' It's time to meet the French fashionable fast and furious Sophie De Lys and her super moves. One simple advice: choose the right way to go. Max Hurricane With his impressive silhouette, the Canadian champion isn’t here to joke around. He’s ready to blow anything out of his way with only one throw. Klaus Wessel, you’ve been warned. Jao Raposa Absolute fan of Steve Miller, Jao spent his childhood in Brazil watching the original Windjammers’ own his opponents on the jammin’ court, and it’s now his time to shine. His best weapons? His speed and head-spinning throws. Sammy Ho Sammy is a very well balanced athlete. The Chinese player is powerful but fast enough to catch every frisbee that comes to him. Beware of his tricky shots! He’ll take the title away from you if you’re not careful enough! Jamma GX03 The well-balanced android can rival the best on the court. Major sponsor Todemu created Jamma GX03 to combat a drop in audience numbers, but in doing so their creation promises to herald a new era of competition in the prestigious windjamming sport. Anna Szalinski The Polish powerhouse is a slow but extremely powerful weightlifter and determined to go for gold. Hiromi Mita 10 years later, you would have thought Japan gave up on the jam? Hiromi Mita is still around with her fast and tricky curve shots shots that will make you regret facing her. Klaus Wessel After a decade of hard training, Klaus Wessel, also known as the Colossus from Germany due to his powerful shots, is back and ready to show Max Hurricane who's the strongest jammer alive. Loris Biaggi Swift, strong, versatile… the Italian Loris Biaggi is still the great champion he was back in the days. Steve Miller He’s agile and a natural at pulling off reversals along with tricky curved shots. He's back to prove that he is still in the game. Gary Scott The extremely muscular American competitor is once again here to show to his opponents how powerful he is. Get ready to see one of the most impressive shots of the game! Jordi Costa The all-round athlete Jordi comes back in the game after 10 years of training. His clinical shots and his speed are the assets that can lead him to win the championship! ● The return of the cult classic Windjammers ● Kickass hand-drawn 2D animations ● Brand-new characters and stages ● Slapshot, dropshot, super moves, jump and smash… a ton of new gameplay mechanics for a complete new windjamming experience ● An amazing Arcade mode that allows superstars to conquer championships while playing solo ● Rad tracks to headbang like a dude ● Local and Online multiplayer - now with full crossplay support, private lobbies and spectator mode ● Brand new training mode, with dedicated lessons and customizable training course

_childDocuments_.review: So I played a lot of Windjammers 1 over the last few weeks leading up to this release to get to know the basic mechanics and also get the hype up. And I was hoping WJ2 could expand on the formula of a fighting-game vibe but packed into a sports-game, similarly to how Mario Tennis Aces did - and man, this game does not disappoint. It's smooth, fast, got great depth due to the different characters but mainly due to all the different possiblities in the moves you have, even  though it's "just" a 4-button game. And I got the feeling, just like the first one, it's always fair, if that makes sense. Every disk I don't catch, slapshot or dropshot is my fault - there always would have been a way to counter or deal with it, if I was either fast, smart or bold enough. And I like that about a game. Makes me feel like my skill is the limit to what I can do, not randomness or op characters.The only thing I'd really mention as a negative is the complete lack of a tutorial. So while there aren't that many buttons you use, they do different things depending on wether you have the disc in your hands or not. Combined with the fact that your stick or d-pad also can influence shots it starts to get a bit more complex quickly. There is a kind of "tutorial" which more or less explains the buttons, how you use them and what they do in specific situations but it's basically just a couple of pictures in a slideshow. No short videoclips showing the moves, let alone an interactive tutorial letting you try and practice some of the stuff. It's probably best to head over to YouTube and check out video tutorials, I'm sure there are some nice people from the WJ community who put up stuff to help new players out.I got a couple of online matches in, too, and so far the netcode is working really fine. Had a few hickups and stuttery movements in one high-ping match that messed up some moves on both my opponent's and my side, but other than that - almost perfect product, Dotemu. Kudos to you and thank you for this revival of a classic I've only just recently discovered. ;)

_childDocuments_.review: Way too fun.I used to play this with my friends many years ago, and now I'm convinced after Streets of Rage 4 that DotEmu have some of the most competent developers in the gaming industry.The entire experience is 1:1 but BETTER. They kept it simple and clean.I'm a die-hard pixel art fan (Windjammers 1), but the same style they went with SOR4 also works here. Works even better honestly.If you're worried about Netplay then don't: I had no hiccups what-so-ever, and if there were any they were too insignificant to care about.Keep in mind that there is a learning curve, so my best advice is to check the tutorial - don't try to learn everything at once! Go to arcade mode and do a couple of matches on Easy or Medium, get your ass kicked and check the tutorial again to put emphasis on other mechanics until everything sinks in.Really good game. A 10/10 of whatever genre this is. 👍👍

_childDocuments_.review: A good natured action arcade sports game which seems to be based on a original that was created a long time ago and which i never played. This one worth a buy today? Oh yes definitely. Full price or sales price. I'd say somewhat small risk that the game would be a complete miss. Even against AI this is a good game that will give you good time. Just don't expect this to last too long due to the fact thata) netplay community is quite dead. Devs did not add proper lobbies so this pretty much ensure the online that SHOULD be the main thing about this game will never rise up. A true pity which is obvious after a while. This one just screams of newbies duking it out and pros doing tournaments. There is a big potential for 'wow' factor here and it just goes to waste here. I can so imagine this being a thing to watch on video and see your favorites showing how it's done. b) Steep learning curve. Against human, particularly another disc thrower sitting right next to you this point would be moot as fun is very much a menu item when none know the game properly but against AI you NEED to learn to be able to beat it. Even Easy mode AI is quite tough at the finals. So...It is  a good buy with some small caveats. Not bad.

_childDocuments_.review: On the surface - a fresh revival of a classic title, with fantastic new graphics, and new mechanics that help expand the game's depth without over-complicating it. Only real aspect I'm not huge into is the addition of the Super meter, but maybe through extended play I could warm up to it.Only thing is, the online play is woefully barebones.The matchmaking is virtually non-existent, as both main options, Ranked and Quick Play will pair you with a random player, regardless of factors like Ping, which can lead to horrible matches with plenty of teleporting with a nice side of input lag.Invite matches are possible, but not via Crossplay, so no Steam + Gamepass matchups. Unless possibly in Quick/Ranked. Lobbies are also left in the cold, so no spectator mode, which hammers the last nail in the coffin for any online tournaments.Game is worth a look if you can get local play going, but as I'm writing this we are in Year 3 of a pandemic and local play just isn't feasible for most.Very disappointing. Hard to recommend playing this over the original when you can access it on a service like Fightcade with superior online play.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're playing on Deck, launch using Open GL otherwise it'll load to a black screen. Great game to play with friends though, runs flawlessly, the only downfall is the lack of people playing to play ranked or any other online games. So if you purchase this, be sure you have a friend or two to play with. I view this as a Smash Bros like competitive game. It gets super intense when you're playing with someone that knows how to play and it's a fun a time.

_childDocuments_.review: So here's the thing: The game itself is great. Why the thumbs down?Windjammers has a very, very small community. On top of that, the devs are absent. Missing features such as spectator mode, lobbies, and full cross play are left out. (Xbox/Steam can match, but they can't invite each other) Outside of a barebones arcade mode the game has no single player content. It doesn't even have a proper tutorial, it has picture slides and not only are they not very informative, some are flat out wrong or leave out certain mechanics.Now, to the community. There are a group of top players. A very, very small group. Since the devs are absent, these people keep the game alive and decide how it's going to work out and be played in tournaments. This is fine, and they are a group of good people for the most part, but outside of these people are a bunch of 200+ ping players. This is because the game is primarily played in France. So.... you either fit in with the cool kids, or you just lag in netcode that isn't that great. Rollback netcode is good when it is done right. Here, you just teleport and ping pong. It is SUPER aggressive, and makes a good portion of the matches just frustrating to play whether I win or lose.This game could match Rocket League popularity if the devs cared about it, but it seems they just made it to appease the players from Windjammers 1. They might have done that, they might have not. As for me, I'm not playing anymore. The highs don't feel as good as the lows do bad. Winning is winning, losing is losing, but with Steam numbers dwindling and the player base virtually non existent (even with Gamepass), this game will be a nice Steam Sale purchase for somebody wanting to play some air hockey with a friend. Otherwise? It's a good game that is bogged down by lack of direction.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: A brilliant old-school, arcade game!Think of Pong but modernised and crossed with tennis. Now add characters with over-the-top special moves.  That is the basic gist of Windjammers 2.Dotemu love their throwback games and this was another pleasantly unexpected revival.  It's strange to think that going back a few years I would associate the Dotemu name with abysmally ported SNK titles and now I look forward to each of their releases!  You can tell from the titles that they are licensing/releasing that they are true fans of these 90's classics.Whilst not nearly as popular amongst fans as Streets of Rage or Ninja Turtles, the original Windjammers gained a cult following years after it's release due to a dedicated fan base in Europe championing it and culminating in it being brought to Evo (the largest fighting game tournament) and gaining it even more recognition amongst the fighting game community.Whilst you would primarily consider it a sports game, it has a lot of fighting game fundamentals contained within.  I played the demo with my friend when it released and we were shouting with joy whilst playing the game. So simple to pick up and play but also hard to master.  It was like video game crack!Graphics are simple, yet colourful and appealing.Music also fits the on-screen action and there are some really catchy themes amongst the different arenas.The arenas themselves come in different sizes as well as having different gimmicks to differentiate them so try to learn the best strategies for each one.  The characters come in different weight classes, with speed and power being varied between them.The single player experience is very limited with just the arcade mode to entertain you so either play this one with friends or play online.  Speaking of online play I have to give huge props to Dotemu for delaying the release of this game in order implement rollback netcode.I played online during the release of the first demo a couple of years back and it was extremely laggy which really had me worried about the final release especially in this day and age where all modern games where rollback is expected.  I am pleased to say that the netcode is a huge improvement from the original beta.  I've played a number of games now and the online play is very smooth most of the time but you will play matches where the player character or the disc will magically teleport.  Of course if you play someone with 200 ping then don't expect miracles!The game truly needs a training mode as all there are currently static screens with instructions and even then the game features a number of mechanics and nuances that aren't explained in the game.Another thing that will be disappointing is that the only cross-platform to speak of is between Steam and Xbox players but only in Ranked.  If you want to play Quick Play with a friend on Xbox then you'll have to get the Microsoft Store version.  I really hope they implement cross play with all systems so that we can play with Microsoft, Sony and Nintendo players in future.  The game is niche as is so we need to be able to play as many players as possible anyway.There are other things I would improve such as being able to cancel your character selection for example, a lobby system for online play a more robust single player mode but honestly these are just nitpicks and QoL changes. More character colour options would also be nice (and a way of choosing alternate colours).  Implementing a robust training mode and cross play would be the highest priority in my opinion.  Also players should be penalised for disconnecting from matches. Deduct their ranked points anyway and give the win to the player that didn't disconnect to discourage this kind of behaviour.I really wish this game got the recognition it deserves as it just goes back to the days when a game could just be simply fun without needing some a deep storyline or epic set pieces and letting the gameplay speak for itself.If the game ended up on the free PSN monthly giveaway and found success there (like Rocket League did) then that would be a dream come true because games like this need to be played by as many people as possible.Thanks Dotemu. Now roll on TMNT and Metal Slug Tactics!

_childDocuments_.review: Having once again found myself dumping nearly fifty hours into it, I decided now was the time to write a piece on why you should play Windjammers 2...For full disclosure, I played the first Windjammers, the original NeoGeo classic, but only many years after the fact as it garnered a cult reputation from places like Giant Bomb. For the broad strokes of it, Windjammers is a version of tennis that gimmicks itself around Ultimate Frisbee. With the way it is formatted, I always described it as "Pong on steroids" since the layout of the field mimicked that game but Windjammers stood out in it’s bombasity, with a loud personality of which you would expect from a 90s Data East arcade title. An arcade playthrough is similar enough to any 1 vs. 1 fighter as you make you way through a number of different stages, each with their own design, with differing hazards (like barriers), and a couple bonus rounds thrown in there for good measure.Windjammers 2 continues the same winning formula, and then some: Doubling the amount of playable characters while also adding extra stages and new features that only build on the existing depth found in the original game. For instance, the staple of fighting games, a power meter, racks up throughout play and can be activated to give you a super shot on command, becoming the ultimate crutch in late games as an offensive move, or to be used as a means of stopping an opponent’s move dead in it’s tracks during defence. Another new feature is the jump, a new means of disorientating play, as it becomes very helpful in disguising where your next move will go, and can unsettle play to your advantage. Both of these additions completely change the flow of play in Windjammers 2, creating different outcomes depending on how heavy, host fast or how tricky your character’s throws can be.Mechanically, DotEmu’s update to Windjammers is sound and responsive. Movement around each field feels natural and distinctive, regardless of whoever you decide to play as, the execution of the intricate super spins and curved shots are satisfying when they pick up results. The animation of Windjammers 2 is also very slick, with plenty of frames for idle animations and specific tells that give the cast a lot of identity. I can appreciate that even joke picks, like Disc Man, can be completely viable in competitive play when so many other games will forego a carefully balanced roster in favour of just amassing the biggest number of paywall locked options, and dumb crossover fighters, as possible. I can also appreciate the attention to detail when it comes to acknowledging the culture around Windjammers, it’s fans, and general lore, around the likes of S. Miller/B. Hoo, the different dialects and languages represented in the international cast, the memorable musical beats that make up the mood of Windjammers in the arcade. Windjammers 2 released a couple decades too late to truly experience life in a busy Akihabara amusement space, but it would have been right at home with the way in which it looks and plays right now. The interface is snappy and quick, with responsive toggles for different mode and setting, with the very colours popping right from the game’s intro, as the blue skies and yellow beaches fulfil the intended summer vibes.Where Windjammers 2 falters might only be in the manner of which arcade scores are ultimately tallied, given your total is more designed to give you lifelines in the form of extra credits, rather than collecting your sheer stage times and ability to rack up wins in high point scorelines and keeping clean sheets. Weirdly, you’d rack up more points in prolonging games into sudden death by virtue of keeping rallies going and, inevitably, sending out more charged shots (of which the game rewards you points for executing). The AI in Windjammers 2 is also ruthless, granted, this applied in the original game as well but you can’t excuse cheating input reading computers quite as easily now as perhaps in the year 1994. Although no AI can prepare itself for the RNG nature of barrier stages like Clay, Rooftop and Junkyard, which could likely confuse even the most grizzled of Windjammers veterans. But ofcourse the real kicker isn’t a fault specifically with the game but more the community, or lack thereof in the online space. Windjammers 2 does support competitive netbased multiplayer, and possesses an MLG-like progression system based on your accumulated wins against different skilled opponents. The problem stems more from the lack of direction around this, as separating ranked and player lobbies is entirely pointless, and even with crossplay support, with the player pool very rarely gets any higher than the lower double digits. That said, the games I had played of Windjammers 2 online were a lot of fun, and it runs stable enough if your connection to the other party is consistent. The brunt of the fun comes from local multiplayer however and having friends partake in games at get-togethers. Windjammers is simple enough that it has instant pick up and play accessibility, as previously mentioned, it really isn’t that far removed from Pong or Tennis itself.Given it is now a couple years old, Windjammers 2 is regularly on sale for PC. You can’t really go wrong with any platform that you decide to play it on although it is undeniably cheaper through Steam than on PlayStation, Xbox or Nintendo Switch, and is lightweight enough that the game could operate on a laptop without much headache either. Although please, please, PLEASE, play Windjammers 2 with a controller, even if it is a janky knock-off from AliExpress. I personally prefer using a Sega Saturn style six button controller since the looser D-Pad makes circle motions that easier to pull-off but anything will do.And, in closing this review, I have to give DotEmu credit for providing free updates to Windjammers 2 and not simply taking their playerbase for granted. In an era where Tekken can paywall new characters behind four(!) different season passes, Windjammers 2 has given us two great additions in Jamma GX03 and Anna Szalinski at no extra cost. For a frugal gamer that is a big deal since supposing you bought a £30-40 (RRP) release, the last thing you want to see is extra content effectively being foisted onto you at an extra £25 a pop. Fighting game fans are a different breed when it comes to DLC but this practice is indicative of a worrying trend in making whales out of a trusting audience, rather than rewarding them for their support. Studios should be more like DotEmu and less like Namco Bandai in that way, and that honestly is the cherry on-top for me. Anyway, give this game a go, oh, and **** H. Max Players!Thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: -Played on Microsoft Game Pass-Top down two player sports title that is an update of the 94' Neo Geo classic, this sequel adding new characters, stage options, and gameplay mechanics. Each player takes one half of a court and must throw a frisbee into their opponents goals or cause them to miss a dropped shot on their side. Points can be earned from one to eight based on the arena and scoring location and most matches are played with the winner needing to win two sets and a set being won at 15 points.Fun, fast paced, and good looking game with more strategy than you might originally think. You can rotate your movement stick to curve your throws, jump to slam down shots, perform drop shots, flip the frisbee up to allow for charged shots if you hit the throw button right before you would have caught it, do a melee like attack to hit the frisbee back quickly, and you can perform quick short range dashes. When the frisbee is up in the air getting under it allows you to charge up shots with the effects being different for each character or you can perform a charged drop shot that lands the frisbee on its side quickly propelling it forward to the goal. Frisbees bounce of the arena's walls and as you throw you build up a meter for a super shot that can be used offensively or defensively as using it when you aren't shooting can cause the frisbee to bounce up into the air saving you from missing opponents shots.You have 11 characters to choose from with each having a different amount of speed and power and each with their own special charged throws. 10 different stages are available with each having a different look, zones worth different amounts of points, size, or possibly obstacles in the center that can give your frisbee more to bounce off of gives you more options for more interesting matches.The only problems are that there really isn't much to the arcade mode, you are just playing one on one vs the computer or one on one vs friends or online opponents. There's no team games, story mode with a plot or interesting mechanics, there is a tutorial you can read that does a poor job getting you ready to play the game, and the only modifiers are just changing the number of sets to win or the number of points to win a set.What is there is well worth it if you have friends to play with or a desire to play online.Screenshots: Online Matches:

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this a little nervous, I won't lie. It's been in development for four years, and every time I'd revisit the store page, I'd still see that TBD release date. That started to change when they released the mini documentary. I could see the insane amount of love, passion, dedication and research done for this new sequel, and I won't lie, not only did it hype me up but it really made me happy for the original Japanese team that a modern dev was doing this game justice.Here we are on release day, and I can safely say this game is simply perfect. This isn't rose tinted glasses or anything, either. I was prepared for this to be a Hotshot Racing situation where the game seemed like a nice nod to the past, but severely "off" in control. Within seconds, it was easy to tell all these fears were quickly dismissed. The game literally feels exactly like what you'd expect.Toss in new moves that feel like they've always been in the game, like the power shots and the jump/spike, and it feels like a proper sequel / refresh to an already masterpiece of a game. I was nervous about the new art style from watching youtube vids, but the game is astounding in 4k. The color palette is perfect, with lots of teals, sky blues, pinks, yellows and other vibrant colors to be found throughout. Characters are simple with a high contrast appearance (shadows are flat black) with the backgrounds being more detailed with non-harsh shadows. This creates a nice separation between the backgrounds and players that feels like a match made in heaven.Backgrounds are highly detailed, and are done with love and care. I can safely say the game wasn't churned out as quick as possible, or done as a quick cash grab. This game oozes polish, from art to control. I can genuinely say I absolutely love this game. I hope this is the first of many original works to come from this developer, and I want to thank them for DOING THIS RIGHT. I wish them all the love and success in this project and others in the future. And I'll be there with you guys for every step.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for May 2023, this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before June 6th, 2022, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.An Arcade Sports game, a sequel to the original. On Neo-Geo, there was an interesting game called Windjammers where players would fling a disc back and forth to score points.  Windjammers 2 came out of nowhere reviving a game that had a cult following.   This is like a HD remake of the original, now with online play, and the same arcade mode.Did you notice I didn’t say they made it better?   This feels very much like a remake of the original, and I’m sure fans of both might be able to point to different pieces, such as four new characters and such.  However, they also are the target audience.  This game doesn’t have a good tutorial, amounting to about 20 static images.  The Main game is just a line of battles with three difficulties, where nothing is explained when you reach the bonus games, and online is just play against an opponent and that’s it.   The problem is there is enough strategy to the game that it could have used a small tutorial mode, but it’s clear the developer made this a very bare-bones experience, perhaps because if it wasn’t trial and error, it would be even more straightforward.Pick this up if you want to play a sports game against friends.  The computer is way too good at the game, but also, playing through the game against the CPU will only take 30 minutes once you’re good enough.  This is meant to be played against other players and online had only 5 players when I started the game.  Play this in local mode, or maybe just play something else. _childDocuments_.review: Windjammers can be a hard game to get into. Lethal League is one of the only games that can be compared directly to Windjammers, I think WJ inspired LL though. We're talking the disc going speeds and in ways you can barely perceive.There really is nothing to be ashamed of or too proud of when it comes to games like WJ. The gameplay in WJ2 is fairly retained in WJ2. The visuals, while initially I wrote off as cheap and in a way still is cheap, has nice art to it in other fields such as the stage designs and how the disc moves with flashy effects. Don't be too hard on yourself if you can't immediately stop a character's special, because you're going to miss it more than you'll have those times where you narrowly stop it. Such is the case of the general WJ2 gameplay and yes it was also like this in the classic WJ arcade.The thumbs down is strictly because of DotEmu. These guys are responsible for why so many Neo-Geo arcade games that are released digitally, underperform and don't live up to the flow of their originals. They've slowed down the Metal Slug series for no reason. They've crippled KOF2002 from working some of the time. They've done the same slow-down with Raiden Legacy.So yes, these guys are on a list of developers to be wary of. They're like the Anti-NightdiveStudios of bringing classics back to modern light. Just make sure it runs at all and call it good, next project kind of deal.Get WJ2 dirt cheap. Do not support DotEmu fully.

_childDocuments_.review: Windjammers 2 is a console ported 2D retro arcade/sports game where you play a 1v1 flying disk game (that plays somewhat poorly more like air hockey than something like Ultimate).  Throw the disk and try get it past your opponent.  If they throw the disk at you, catch it before it goes past you.  Points are scored for getting the disk past your opponent.   That's all there is to it. There's a long list of technical defects that will disenfranchise PC gamers very quickly here.  Let's break it down.From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.There's no options to change the resolution for the game or customise the graphics settings.  There's no way for gamers to ensure this is running at the native resolution of their displays... there's no guarantee this game will look right on any PC as a result of this hamfisted design decision.  There's no way for gamers to try improve the low quality graphics. PC gamers will be insulted by the presence of console peasant children's toy controller prompts, despite this being on PC.  Developers should try to be aware which platform they're developing for.Because this is a console game, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the inferior console gaming appliances that the game was designed for.  These are unfortunate compromises and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was a second thought for the console-centric developers.  The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for consoles forces upon a game.  Once more, console peasants have made gaming worse for everyone.Some of the defects in the game can be attributed to the choice of using the GameMaker Studio construction kit/toolset.  While this is of notably higher quality than most GameMaker Studio games, and is modestly well polished, it's still generally defective because it started from an inferior position.  GameMaker Studio is a very poor quality toolset favoured by amateur developers as it's cheap and requires little in the way of development skill, but unfortunately has very limited capabilities.  Just as you can't make a silk purse out of a sows ear, you can't make a great video game if you use a terrible engine.  GameMaker Studio is most commonly used to make retro pixel shovelware and cash grabs, although in this case the developers made the highly questionable decision to genuinely try to make a serious game with the construction kit... and it's not worked out particularly well. A strong argument can be made that construction kits like GameMaker Studio should never be used to make games for profit, as the "developer", Dotemu has done here.  These construction kits are intended to teach people some of the basic principles of game development, and to make small demos to pass around with friends.  They're not intended to replace to actual work of real, professional game developers and real, professional game engines.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.Reviewing SteamDB to check how popular this game was with players reveals a surprise... there's a very healthy spike in player counts for the game.  But this only appears around the same time that trading cards were applied to the game... so this is just card idlers getting their cards and moving on.  A closer look at the numbers shows the game just has a couple of players every week running up the game and idling it for cards, then deleting it.  SteamDB does show a very small handful of players idling at any time, and this may be misleading to gamers because you might think you can get into an online game (because there's players... right?).  But because it's just card idlers, matchmaking is next to impossible.  The online component of this game should be disregarded due to this unfortunate reality. Windjammers 2 has the completely insane price of $20 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games.  This is also competing with over 9,000 free games available on Steam, many of them far better than this paid product.  The developer has priced this higher than games like The Mass Effect Trilogy, Red Dead Redemption 2, Subnautica... the list goes on.  They genuinely think their console ported GameMaker Studio 2D retro game is superior to games like Euro Truck Sim 2 and Deep Rock Galactic.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the insulting price, this is impossible to recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Windjammers 2 has burst onto the gaming scene with an infectious energy that's impossible to ignore. As a fan of classic arcade sports games, I couldn't be more thrilled with the sequel to the cult favorite, and it exceeds all expectations with its fast-paced action, stylish visuals, and addictive multiplayer mayhem.Right from the start, Windjammers 2 captures the essence of the original while elevating it to new heights. The hand-drawn art style is a visual feast, combining vibrant colors with smooth animations that bring the characters and courts to life. The attention to detail in the design is impressive, and it perfectly complements the frenetic gameplay.Speaking of gameplay, Windjammers 2 retains the simple yet incredibly engaging mechanics of its predecessor. The core frisbee-throwing concept remains intact, but the developers have introduced new moves, special abilities, and enhanced controls that add layers of strategy to the matches. It's easy to pick up and play, but mastering the nuances of each character's playstyle offers a rewarding learning curve.The multiplayer aspect of Windjammers 2 is where the game truly shines. Whether you're challenging friends locally or testing your skills against opponents online, the competitive nature of the matches is nothing short of exhilarating. The netcode ensures smooth online play, and the ranking system adds a competitive edge, making every victory a hard-fought achievement.The variety of game modes keeps the experience fresh and exciting. From classic one-on-one matches to intense doubles competitions and a robust single-player campaign, Windjammers 2 offers something for everyone. The inclusion of local and online tournaments adds a sense of community, fostering a competitive spirit that will keep players coming back for more.The soundtrack deserves special mention for its infectious beats that perfectly complement the fast-paced action. The music not only enhances the overall atmosphere but also contributes to the adrenaline-fueled excitement of each match.In conclusion, Windjammers 2 is a triumphant return for the franchise. It successfully marries nostalgia with modern design, delivering an arcade sports experience that is both accessible to newcomers and a blast for longtime fans. The combination of stylish visuals, tight gameplay mechanics, and robust multiplayer options makes Windjammers 2 a must-have for anyone seeking a dose of pure, unadulterated fun. Strap in, grab a frisbee, and get ready for an arcade sports extravaganza like no other!

_childDocuments_.review: I can now fully endorse this game. If you want a pretty niche arcade game and are willing to look the the community to find some matches it's a great time.  It might be worth wish-listing and grabbing when it drops on sale a bit.  I hope they push sales more aggressively, as I think they could get a lot of people who ignored the game due to the rocky online at launch.

_childDocuments_.review: The original windjammer was a huge hit in the arcade in the 90s, and one of the flagship titles on the Neo Geo console (which was however, unaffordable to most except in its native Japan).This reboot is done just right: it doesn't change massively the mechanics of the original, which is a good thing as they were pretty much perfect (think the original Street Fighter 2 as a comparison of sorts), but it manages to innovate just enough to make it more interesting than just playing the original on the emulator. Unfortunately, not to the fault of the game I believe, the online component is pretty much unusable as very few players are available at any given time, so few that I still haven't managed to match anybody. So if you buy it for that, you might want to reconsider.The single player campaign, at least, offers quite a few hours of fun it you want to complete it in hard mode, and it's probably nice to support these developers who made really a lovely job. Too bad it's not been that successful it seems - there are just too many games released every day so it seems to have kinda been lost in the mix.

_childDocuments_.review: Windjammers 2 is a love letter to the old SNK arcade days, bringing back the classic gameplay of the original Windjammers with a fresh new coat of paint. There's no denying the positive feelings it evokes, from the fast-paced gameplay to the catchy soundtrack. It's all there. A lesson written in capital letters about how to modernize a classic (SF6 cought, cought...)But, as with any game, there are a few minor complaints worth mentioning. (No graphic options???. Really...) However, this does not detract from the overall gameplay experience.In the end, Windjammers 2 is a fantastic sequel to a classic arcade game. It is clear that a lot of passion went into creating this game, and it shows in the attention to detail and overall fun factor. It is highly recommended for fans of the original and anyone looking for a fun, fast-paced sports game.
_childDocuments_.name: Windjammers 2

_childDocuments_.review: Hard but fair game with seemingly simple mechanics that have tons of depth. Recommended with the unfortunate caveat that the online is pretty much dead  (EDIT: The input delay issue was fixed as of November 2023, and it's great!). I have played a lot more offline than online with other people at LAN events and in that context it is one of my favorite games.The game is like pong if it was turned up to eleven with things being centered on a ricocheting disk that you have to catch and return to the other side, the goal being to get it in their net. There are three types of ways to hit the ball that mix up timing and positioning, as well as character-specific signature moves, all of which can be angled, curved, and delayed to mix them up even further. Receiving at a high level is very intense and requires clean reactions, and pivoting those returns into offensive plays then further requires even quicker thinking and outplaying your opponent. Once you really get into the swing of it and everything clicks it delivers an intensity that very few other games can say they have accomplished.If you have people to get into it with locally, or if you're lucky enough to have a local competitive scene, I beg you to check it out. If you are into fighting game theory it will be like crack for you in how it is able to apply it to something so different from any other popular fighting game. It really is that good.

_childDocuments_.review: Another successful sequel, rollback netcode, stylized graphics, expanding the 28 year formula with new offensive and defensive options, the character roster was expanded too, mantaining the excellent balance the previous game had and last but not least, an interesting arcade mode with bonus stages and a great soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: Windjammers 2

_childDocuments_.review: Windjammers is Pong meets Street Fighter. It has radical music, clean visuals, and responsive, fair, and clean design. It will make you yell. It will make you and your friends feel like super sports stars in a Tron disc battle. And when you dig into the deeper mechanics, you will find yourself learning an actual Video Sport. They played Windjammers 1 at EVO, and they should play this one now instead.Pros: This is almost identical to the classic Windjammers game, but with new crisp visuals, some new mechanics, and some new characters and stages. It's Windjammers but new and better. The online seems to work just fine (with some caveats). Latency feels good, and there are currently plenty of players to play with. This feels like a Real Game and it's real fun.Cons: Currently there IS crossplay, but only via random matchmaking in quickplay. If you want to private match someone on a different platform there doesn't seem to be a solution. There is also no Training Mode yet, and the in-game tutorial, while a good place to start, leaves out a whole lot of the detailed mechanics and character specific information. Basically, no Move List yet.Overall: Please play if you like local multiplayer sports fighters like Videoball and Street Fighter. It's a real good time and I believe in it.
_childDocuments_.name: Windjammers 2

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to leave a "mixed" review.But in 2022 we know what it takes to sustain a community and what should be in a game that needs a community to survive.What this game is missing:1. Crossplay private lobbies (you can't play with friends on a different console directly. You have to queue and hope to be matched).2. A quality tutorial. This is a deep game and newbies will turn away fast if they can't grasp the basics. I'd like to practice throws and service angles w/o having a braindead cpu or one that button reads.3. Unlockables.... there's literally nothing to unlock..... nothing. No gallery mode. You beat arcade mode for some interesting stills that tell... random stuff about the characters and then the game is over. The art is great. Would have been nice to view it w/o beating the game again.5. A means to filter high ping players online: It's a miracle when I play against someone under 164 ms. It plays okay on that ping, but it's not the best. It's punishing to have a to play through a match with someone using Instant Transmission and some players manipulate their wifi when they are losing... plenty of videos online with that happening.6. Comparable support from their other popular tiles, Streets of Rage 4 and not TNMT. Those games have the works and they put a lot of effort in it. This game is barebones which is stupid because the old game was an arcade game and has pretty much all the current fixings minus a few characters, slap/drop/jump shots, and online play (which is a moot point thanks to Fightcade supporting multiplay).7. Polish: There are sound and visual bugs galore which doesn't make sense since they weren't present in the beta. The difficulty to landing slap shots with Mita and De Lys character is likely a bug.8. Poor character balance: Everyone is playable, but lighter characters have poor defensive options and tighter offensive options. They are harder to play. Heavier characters have a widen hit box, slapshot easier, throw faster shots and have a longer window to do so, aren't moved to far back when receiving a super shot, and outside of Gary Scott, all have effective super customs shots. Their "downside" is that their dash isn't that fast, their curve shots aren't as curvy, and they initially have a smaller window to throw sonic shots (which is a moot point, because they can slap like mad). Too many advantages.. plus smaller arenas benefit them and wider arenas can capatilze on their strengthen and supers... I don't want the heavies to be nerfed, but I would like the lighter characters to be taken a look at.9. No plans to fix current issues. The devs have commented on a number of the communities complaints. I think they knew the game wasn't going to sell well, so they stopped development, launched the game, and will backpedal away to focus on SoF4 and the TMNT game in development. If they come back to support this game, the owe the community to addreee our top issues.  This game didn’t make them any money, so it’s doubtful we will see quality changes. This is abandonwear upon release. I will never support a Dotemu game and tell others to do the same.Average 13 players online and most of they aren’t North America. The game is dead.

_childDocuments_.review: The 90s era of arcade gaming was really packed with underrated gems, especially on the Neo Geo arcade hardware. If there’s one game that really, REALLY needs to make a comeback from the SNK and Neo Geo 90s arcade 1v1 days, it’s clearly the versus shmup Twinkle Star Sprites, which has gone on for far too long without a 2D-art sequel.But, if I were to put away my biases and pick a close second, it’ll definitely be Data East’s Windjammers. The Dotemu folks have taken up the task of bringing a true sequel to life in 2022. And damn, does it deliver!Full review:

_childDocuments_.review: This is all about core gameplay. There's no story mode, no battle pass, no unlockables, for better or worse. What gameplay there is, however, is immaculate. Easy to parse, but deeply technical, I think this one is as enjoyable to play for fun as it is to compete with. Each character has different spins, weights, and specials, and if you go deep there's a lot to learn with them all. Going back and forth, switching up angles and throws, launching specials all feel satisfying and controlled. There's little here that you feel like you've been cheated by; in a loss, I always say "I should've done *x*".If you enjoy head to head games, fighting games, or pong, I highly recommend. Just know that you need to really love that main gameplay to get the most out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: To be a gamer in 2022, where possibilities are near infinite and experiences are beyond bountiful ; to experience Windjammers 2 and recall the days spent on a Neo Geo emulator playing the original title ; to recall all of it, from the smell of your mother baking a chocolate cake on a saturday afternoon to the little CRT monitor that encased all the victories and defeats for hours on end. To be alive in this day and age. What a time to be alive.Windjammers 2 is everything I remember about the original game - which I must've last played 20 years ago - and more. Single player content is limited but challenging and extremely fun. In my opinion, super moves present an interesting addition and as I learned the game again, they always felt a natural mechanic in the experience. Online content is present, stable and already a great source of replayability. Only thing I'm trying to come to terms with that is currently sapping my enjoyment of the game is that I've spent 3 hours playing on the left side of the field and when I go online there's a chance I get matched on the right side, which feels completely unnatural and intrusive. I suppose this is a distinct design choice, so I figure this will never change. My only hope is that the rage doesn't eject me from this beautiful game.Special shoutout to everyone born in the 90's and before, who had played the original Windjammers and is currently experiencing feelings of nostalgia like yer boi Raffu. We out here jamming wind together, boys. And may we jam the damned wind forevermore.

name: Ayo the Clown
detailed_description: In Ayo’s hometown, things are generally peaceful. Accompanied by his talented circus dog, Bo, Ayo juggles in the park, hangs out at the carnival and longs after the Shoemaker’s granddaughter. Until one day, Bo goes missing! You play as Ayo, your not-so-average clown, in search of his best friend and beloved dog who has mysteriously disappeared. What happened to Bo? Will they ever juggle together at the park again? Or set up that circus act they’ve always planned? You’ll find out along this incredible adventure as you strive to reunite clown and dog. Like all good adventures, you won’t be all on your own. Ayo’s world is full of friendly people and interesting creatures that are willing to lend a helping hand. FEATURES: Unique Platforms- The most important part of any platform game. Each stage has a unique theme and interesting platforms to ensure gaming is fun and not repetitive because Ayo is not the kind of clown to make the same old jokes over and over again. His jokes get better each time. Huge Bosses and loads of enemies- Take on bosses bigger than life itself and prove that clowns are much tougher than they seem. Don’t be fooled by Ayo’s sweet demeanor! Weapons - Tanks, helicopters, dinosaurs, toy hammers, balloon swords, water balloons, you name it. They can help uncover hidden places, extinguish fire, defeat enemies, prank your friends...etc. Skills- Head stomps, wall jumps, slope slides, and many more, Ayo sure has a lot of tricks up his sleeve. Side Quests- There’s plenty of side quests you can take on in Town or along your journey, so be prepared for some surprising rewards. Collectibles- Can you find and collect all the hidden items throughout the game? Rubber chicken and fart bag anyone?

_childDocuments_.review: Ayo the Clown is an adorable platformer with gorgeous, vibrant visuals that is severely underrated and underappreciated. Its childish appearance is obnoxiously cute, but its gameplay also holds strong. It is not the hardest platformer to exist but is more a decent introduction to the genre itself. That being said, the difficulty does steadily increase but maintains a calmer pace throughout, which I enjoyedTo be blunt, the story of Ayo the Clown is not very interesting. It really is a children's feel-good narrative with good morals and kind acts inserted throughout. Despite the art in the cutscenes being gorgeous, there is not much of a focus on the story, with most story components lasting less than a minute. When I began playing this game and raving about how much I unexpectantly enjoyed it, I was hit with many questions regarding the intended age of players. Understandable, considering everything is bright, childish and reminiscent of classic platformers from the 80-90's. Whilst I do think children would enjoy this game, I also think adults can as well, which will be better explained in the gameplay section. Players take control of Ayo, a joyful young clown in the circus. Everything is peaceful as Ayo follows his passion of making people smile and bringing goodness to the world (sound cliche? I did warn you). One day, Ayo's beloved companion and canine friend Bo, goes missing. This is the entire premise of the game and Ayo sets out on a somewhat frivolous adventure to reunite with his beloved pet. Along the journey, he interacts with many friendly characters and can choose to aid them in their own problems. Without spoilers, the story is utterly predictable and is exactly what you would expect out of a children's picture storybook. Admittedly, I did not care for the story, nor did I pay much attention to it and yet, I thoroughly enjoyed my experience simply due to the visuals and entertaining gameplay.Despite being somewhat unimpressed with such a childish story, I found the gameplay to be absolutely fantastic. Is this what I would recommend for hardcore platformers, or even those who strive to play everything on the hardest difficulty? Definitely not. But for those who think the visuals look endearing and want a more relaxed platformer, then certainly, give it a go.Ayo the Clown features 8 worlds, made up of 3-4 levels each and also features a bonus world that is unlockable with enough gems. I completed all levels and all side quests which totalled around 9 hours and I loved every minute of it. At the beginning, Ayo has no skills, not even the ability to jump. This quickly changes and as more skills are introduced, the difficulty slightly does as well. Levels begin increasing in length and more difficult foes are introduced. Ayo will learn to "double jump" will the assistance of his balloon, slide, climb and more. What I especially loved about this title was its variability in gameplay. Each world is exceptionally diverse and features differing themes such as candy land, farmland, aliens, the circus and more. Gameplay is also kept fresh with varying boss fights and introduces areas where we take control of a tank, helicopter or even ride in a rollercoaster. There is a world map where players walk to each level and can also come across some optional fishing sections for more gems. Players can also go back to the town to purchase more lives, upgrade your balloon or acquire side quests from the many town’s inhabitants. There is a large replayability value as in every level, there are 6 collectables to find, which of course are needed for achievement hunters. The side quests also take a bit of time as well and add more diversity to the game. In the actual levels, Ayo can jump on most enemies’ heads to kill them or pick up a weapon such as a sword, hammer or water balloon. The levels themselves I found to be quite extensive and well designed, with different ways to proceed and many hidden spots to explore. With a constant barrage of new traps, enemies and themes, it never felt stale. I was mainly quite impressed with the polished nature of the game, every aspect felt well designed, and I encountered very few bugs. My one complaint relates to the camera angles in the fast-moving areas. In levels such as the balloon stage where Ayo continuously floats upwards and must dodge enemies and traps to navigate the environment, the camera angles were far too slow and clunky. If you move too fast, the camera does not follow  you and you will automatically die from "falling" due to being so far in front that you cannot see anything. This made these level designs extremely frustrating, trying to keep up by being purposefully slow is not enjoyable. Luckily, these areas are not very common and thus did not dampen my experience too much.I took one look at the screenshots and was immediately intrigued. The adorable, vibrant art style was a welcome rainbow explosion to my eyes. Across the 9 worlds, each section was bursting with cute enemies and features. Despite each world being remarkably different to each other,  they are all equally overflowing with its pleasantly charming, cute and childish aesthetic. Jump across pigs in the farmland, ride pink dolphins in the ocean world, navigate circus equipment and much more.The sound was reminiscent of other classic platformers such as Spyro, Croc and Crash Bandicoot. The overly perky sound effects and joyful soundtrack were exactly what I expected in a game such as this. Thankfully, the soundtrack is not on a loop and does change from level to level, especially in boss battles.It can be played on a controller or keyboard. For reference, I played using keyboard and encountered no issues in functionality.I launched this expecting some cute visuals and not much else, but I was wrong. Ayo the Clown is a hidden gem for cute platformers and is critically underrated. Its gameplay can stand on its own two feet with steady progression and an abundance of evolving features. Although it is not a difficult title, it serves as a more relaxing addition to the genre that children and adults alike, can enjoy. With over 9 hours of content for one playthrough and great replayability value, I highly recommend this title for all casual platformer fans.This review copy was provided to the Devils in the Detail curator.

_childDocuments_.review: Kickstarter backer here. Just started playing the game with my xbox controller and I love it. What a wonderful 2.5D platformer! I dig the color scheme so much, it's so fun and whimsical and vibrant. There's a balloon ability that you can basically use whenever you land, so you don't have to collect any items to activate, which allows you to float--it's a lot of fun! There's plenty of secrets with hidden treasure and stuff to climb (so usually there's a path above you you may want to explore as well). The game isn't very hard but there are many pits which insta kill you. Luckily, there are plenty of checkpoints, so you never lose a lot of progress. The only two things I'll criticize are: there may be micro slowdowns here and there, for no apparent reason. It's brief, but noticeable. And the second thing is--the snot, why is it there? :P If you enjoy 2.5D platformers such as Super Lucky's Tale (well, it's partly 2.5D), then you'll love this game!

_childDocuments_.review: Featuring a cute story and playful graphics, Ayo the Clown brings new life to old platformers. You progress through a variety of stages and environments to unlock new abilities and meet new characters. The 2.5D art style is bright and clean, secrets are hidden behind false walls and special challenges, and the overall aesthetic takes obvious inspiration from the old retro platformers.Positives:- Great sense of achievement just by playing the game: There are many skills to unlock, each changing the way you will approach future levels. Gameplay never gets stale, as every single level is different from the previous one. You may have to go out of your way to find collectibles, increasing replayability. Recorded times after finishing levels encourages speedrunning.- Art is very lighthearted and very polished. Enemies and obstacles catch your attention, and every stage has a different backdrop. The music matches the way you are progressing through the stage, whimsical and energetic.- The game is challenging but not punishing, featuring multiple difficulty levels. One frustration may come from the arcade platformer system of restarting a stage from the beginning if you lose all your lives, but this can be circumvented by lowering the difficulty, giving you more hearts. You can add your own artificial difficulty if need be by going a completionist route or trying for a low time.- The game is very nostalgic about games of old such as Mario and Donkey Kong, featuring novel movement options, changing scenery, and powerups that help you and last until you take damage.Criticism:- Having pits taking out an entire life may be annoying when you only have a certain number before you must restart the level. Fortunately there are ways to gain extra lives.Overall, the game is artistically and technically polished, reminiscent of the height of platformer video games. A modern spin on a popular trope, this game is recommended for both fans and people interested in the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: So good I bought it three times!After seeing me play the Steam version both my Kids (5 & 7) wanted me to get this for their Switches.The game is beautiful looking, charming and with a great soundtrack. As others have mentioned the game is a throwback to the platformers of the 90's so you will see inspiration from all your favourites like Mario, Sonic, Donkey Kong, Kirby etc, however I also felt there was a Little Big Planet vibe as well showing some more modern inspirations.The game has plenty of varied locations and the game play is different enough in each level to keep you entertained with some levels stepping very much outside the traditional 2D platformer genre. Whilst there is nothing genre defining in this game, its cute graphical style, relaxing soundtrack and familiar game play mean you cant help but enjoy yourself. Its not overly challenging as an adult, although I did find that  a few of the final levels required a number of tries and both the Candy boss and the final boss were more challenging than any of the others. Younger kids might find some of the levels frustrating but I would say no more so that I did as a kid playing this style of game in the 90's however kids games tend to be a little more forgiving now.There are a few niggling issues, the odd buggy space where something might not quite work as it should but nothing that spoils the experience. The Gems seem arbitrary and I can't figure out how many i need for an extra life or what the purpose of having the differ denominations of gems is rather than just one type, but again this didn't impact my experience negatively.Thoroughly recommend for anyone who enjoys platformers, and think its a great wholesome, fun and charming game for the kids.

_childDocuments_.review: Me say boom boom boom, now everybody say Ay-ooh (AY-OOH).Right?I backed this on Kickstarter because it looked delightfully joyful and I as a joyless man in a joyless world need to get a fix where I can. I will say that it provided plenty of levity but was I to find deep emotional resonance at the end of my experience? Read on to find out...As a side scrolling platformer, there are obvious comparisons to be made to all kinds of gaming legends and system mascots. None of these much matter as there are only four things (IMO) that really make or break such a game.1) Mario is kinda the de facto king of movement when it comes to the whole genre of PLATFORMER. Whether in second or third dimension, few other characters control quite like Mario. The immediacy, the fluidity, the convention defining pedigree.Ayo is NOT Mario. He controls perfectly fine though. He moves in the directions, he jumps, he crouches and he does all the things you'd expect. He'll maybe just travel a little further than you planned, or maybe he'll pull off an unstoppable butt slam while you're trying to jump over a chasm and plummet to his death. He's a little fiddly at times, but that's fine. This is not a major studio release, this has some old fashioned and totally forgivable Indie Janky Goodness.2) Camera is so critical to the overall user experience. I read some reviews complaining about the camera in Ayo. I will admit that on a handful of instances I was a little perplexed by the choices made by the camera, but one could favourably look at this as raising the skill ceiling for those able to make it so far in the game as to reach those moments. There are definitely some irritating sections, but overall I thought the camera was perfectly workable. Again, see the Janky Indie Goodness.3) A very basic description of any platformer might be "character  moves from THE LEFT  to THE RIGHT ."Unsurprisingly this will get dull quite quickly, so games in the genre become really good at distracting the player from the limited nature of the task at hand.Ayo is incredibly good at throwing new mechanics, new gameplay, new moves, new challenges and new puzzles at the player all the way to the very last few levels. While following the general beats of the genre, Ayo does enough to stand above many lesser imitation platform heroes.4) Deep emotional resonance? Sure, why not.

name: Yes, Your Grace
detailed_description: In this kingdom management RPG, petitioners will arrive in the throne room each turn to ask for your advice and assistance. Decide whether to help them with their problems, or to conserve resources for more important matters. Remember: supplies are limited, and not everyone has the kingdom’s best interests at heart... Listen to petitioners each turn and decide who needs your support. Aid your family with their personal problems and decide upon their fate. Hire Generals, Witches and Hunters to aid your efforts. Prepare for battle and make alliances by satisfying the whims of lords and kings. Follow the stories of the quirky and determined characters that visit your halls. Yes, Your Grace tells a tale of Davern, a medieval kingdom ruled by King Eryk. The game is set in a fictional world where monsters and arcane practices inspired by Slavic folklore are the order of the day. Villagers will ask for your help with various problems, from monsters attacking the village to a lack of places to relax and enjoy themselves. Some will bring humour to your throne room and some will present you with difficult choices. Your family is important too, and throughout your time as King, you will have to support them in their struggles. You will face lords with a variety of personalities; you will need their support in order to win an upcoming battle, but some may ask you to perform dirty deeds to cement the alliance. One thing is clear: It won’t be easy to keep everyone happy...

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very small recommendation, so read on for the cons if you're on the fence about getting this.The game has a lot of charm and an above-average story, but nothing really stands out about it. It says it's a "kingdom management RPG", but I found nothing of that inside. It's more an elaborate visual novel, and so my critics stem for there.It says you are a King, but that's in name only. You have no army, any peasant in the kingdom has more gold than you, and basically you depend on anyone but you to actually run the kingdom (but is there a kingdom to begin with? Why is everyone listening to your decisions when you don't even have enough men to make a patrol?). The tough choices, gameplay wise, are very similar all throughout, where you have to decide to spend resources (gold or supplies) or use an agent to solve a situation. Please note you do not control when you unlock agents, and they cost gold to maintain.And that's it, I've covered all the gameplay aspects of the game. That's no kingdom management, imo. That's barely a resource allocation gameplay, but even then, the game is designed to be played a certain way, and you will be punished if you stray from it.The game also does the cardinal sin of making you think what you do matter, and makes a big deal of preparing the kingdom for big events, but in the end, what you do matters very little, as the story beats are pre-determined and will move on almost regardless of how you prepared.So why do I recommend it? Well, it has a lot of nice staging ideas and the story is better than what I was expecting coming in. I became attached to the characters and some annoyed me, and I wanted to see how it unfolded until the end. I'm almost tempted to do another playthrough to see the other options, but then I remember I'll have to go through the "management" part again and I'm just discouraged.Another strong point of the game is that some of your decisions do matter. Who you decide to help in the beginning can have an impact on what you can do in the end.I still think it's worth getting the game to do a single playthrough; for me it was around 6h, so I'll let you judge how much money that is worth to you.
