_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good game that tells an interesting and very very well written story blended with just the right amount of game mechanics. Should you buy it? SURE!But there are 2 things that you need to know. Things that in, my opinion, are precisely what makes this game so good but that might not be to your liking (or what you are expecting):1- Do not come to this game expecting a Mass Effect style "your choices have huge consequences", no. This game feels more like a mix of an interactive book with a good amount of gameplay, where you get the pleasure to tweak relatively minor or "side" aspects of the story here and there, instead of changing things that have major consequences. It's a like a book that tells a tale and that invites you to color it with the details of how things unfolded the way they did.2- The gameplay serves the narrative. It is not meant to be really challenging, but it is still fun and you certainly can still fail at it. But again, the main purpose of the gameplay elements are to serve the story and enrich the lore. They work well, add flavor, and will keep you busy, but this is not a strategy game. It is a narrative-driven game that plays out through a series of "mini-games" (not necessarily in the sense that they are short, but that they are not deep).Regarding replayability, yea, maybe this is where the game could have gone a little further. I would certainly play the game again but it is not like "oh I missed so much the first time" or "man, I really want to see what happens if I choose that this time".Finally, for those who don't know, this game is such a comeback. It was a small kickstarter project that achieved funding, ran into problems and then 2 years (I think) of radio silence. And then, our of nowhere, came back with a full apology, refunds for everyone who desired one, and more importantly: they came back with a game 2 or 3 times the size they originally promised. Basically, instead of just giving up and disappearing with the money they got, they somehow spent those silent years trying and eventually managing to secure the extra funding they actually needed to execute what they had promised. Not that I'm defending them for their radio silence, that is still very not ok to do, BUT their efforts in order to try to fulfill their project despite things going south, that is commendable.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Giving a thumbs up because I liked the game overall. I liked the art and I felt how much effort went into the making of this. I think it's important to note that your choices don't really change how the plot flows, though they do have consequences. It's kind of like a visual novel that you can put some flavour into. It's surprisingly dark and did make me cry!I feel like there should be more strategy-related options than what you're given, such as the ability to get more recruits etc. because after a while it felt like I wasn't doing much. I imagine I would have ended up given the game a thumbs down if I had pursued a "perfect route" type scenario because of how repetitive it would be. That said, I had no problems managing preparations without having to reload anything.Personally, I don't want to replay it to get the achievements because I know the process will be stressful. I found the game intense without being immersive enough for me to be curious. I wish at least some of the characters were more rounded out. So yes, overall enjoyable, but not raving about it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is truly amazing. I got so interested in the characters and so invested in their futures. I think this is easily in my top 5 favorite games I have played so far this year.~The Story~You play a king trying to protect his family and his kingdom.... and that is all the info I will give you <3. Seriously. Only because this game had me so captivated. These characters became my family! Especially Cedani! That is my little pumpkin and I love her to the moon and back. If there were figures of this little girl I ♥♥♥♥ you not I would be adding her to my figure collection because I love her character that much.Honestly though there wasn't a single character in this game that I DIDN'T like. Even the bad guy I liked. Not that I liked him as a person... but his over all character design and how he was written. I loved it <3~The Graphics~These are pretty simple looking graphics but to me they are gorgeous. I absolutely loved looking at this game the entire time I was playing.~The Sound Design~OMG honestly.... probably my favorite part of the game.... Which is saying something because I'm in love with every other aspect of the story. Like I almost never plan on buying soundtracks for games but I have ever intention of getting the soundtrack for this game. I loved listening to the music (especially Cedani's song because omg that mood change was perfect) and I loved listening to the sounds of my people in the back ground. The sounds of everything around me. I loved it.~The Mechanics~The game is very heavily choice based and the choices CAN come back to bite you heavily in the ass if you aren't careful. I honestly and truly love that. I love when a game makes me make hard choices. I love when I get punished for doing something I should have. There is also resource management in having to keep your people happy, sending your helpers out on missions on the map, negotiating with possible allies, watching your resouces, and watching your money. It can feel like a lot to juggle at times, but it never felt like it was a lot to handle constantly. Just that every now and then a choice would bite me hard in the ass and I needed to find a way to recover quickly.~Replay-ability~Honestly you could play this game a ton. Even if you get to the end of it like I did, you can still do tons of play throughs to get more story. For instance I have no idea what happens if I work with Lord Etton or Lady Lena. No clue. I did two playthroughs of this game and neither of them did I work with the two of them. I have no idea what happens if I get to the last battle and am no prepared. I have no clue what happens if specific people are lost at a certain point in the game and what that does to the story. And even though I got the good end of the game.... I am assuming anyways because the explaination cards at the end were all colored and not grey... I want to play it again... so that I can see what was possible. See what could have happened if I wasn't careful. Though I have to admit.... I don't know that I could ever do something that would put Cedani in danger.... because that is my Pumpkin damn it!~Overall~HIGHLY recommend this game to anyone who likes choices matter games and/or resource management games. There wasn't a single moment of playing this game that I didn't love.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is enjoyable, albeit quite short. I completed it on my first run through, without much trouble in terms of resource management. One thing that really let me down, is that the game is very linear. Choices don't seem to matter in the first instance, I loaded up a new game to try a different route, but it takes you the same way, with some minor detail changes. I do feel that the characters have been fleshed out quite well. There is your wife and three daughters, and I found myself very attached to each of them. There are others as well, but I don't really want to spoil the rest of them Overall the game has been done very well. The pixel art style is very pleasing, the music fits perfectly and the story has been done well. The downside is that choices don't change the story (unless I'm mistaken) and the only way for the game to be difficult in terms of resource management, is if you end up being a c*nt to your subjects.For the price it is at, I wouldn't recommend it
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Play as a king and manage your people and your family. Each in-game week, you will have to attend to a line of your people with various requests from helping out in a peasant's wedding to managing the kingdom's dungeon to settling your daughters' disupute. Which all are prelude to the impending invasion from another army.  Will you manage the people and the wealth well enough to fight off the invasion or not.That's about the premise of the game. You manage the gold and supplies in the kingdom, and decide how it is spent on the kingdom and the people, and hope it eventuallys help out in the invasion of the kingdom. Truly a financial management simulator with a flavour of relationship management. Exactly how a King should be. Isn't that lovely?If you have ever wanted to be a (medieval) king, this game is for you!Else, it is still an ok game with some creative plot/gameplay.Still don't know a vast majority of the games. Will recommend this game as a simple management simulation with probably some interesting plot points.Overall? So far with my few minutes with the game... It is still recommended, just because I am just a little intrigue by the story. Eager to see how it plays out.Recommended for now. But you won't be missing out much even if you were not getting it
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful crash course to leadership/any role that looks after others (not terribly hard or stressful however! unlike its inspiration Papers Please) that's also a terrific story of family with an fantastic soundtrack. Worth every penny of asking price. Played through twice, second time for the best possible ending.Depicts a king that seems both relatively easy to access and depending on how you play through, also relatively resourced and capable of helping. May make you unrealistically wish for more benevolent dictatorships vs the world we have today.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of choices don't matter. When they do, it usually always follows:Do the "Good/Naive" option = eh, consequences didn't matter! It all worked out anyway against impossible odds!Do the "Machiavellian/Jerk" option = shame shame shame BIG consequences!Game is also railroaded into 3 major acts, so for example you're pushed into an offensive conflict without choice and characters jump to conclusions about the opposition. In a later act, it becomes a point of moral contention that "clearly, you messed up" when the choice wasn't even in your hands to begin with.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Story was railroaded, gameplay was nothing but clicking the "don't be a ♥♥♥♥" dialogue option. Resource management was stupidly simple. Just invest as much as possible in pop happiness to snowball taxes and buy all upgrades before battles. Army size does not matter one bit. No matter what you do, you will be drained to the brink of defeat in battle, then divine intervention will save you at the last moment. Only options to be "bad" provide no real benefit, so there is not reason to take them. Removes all moral depth to choices. Feel like the animation budget ran out halfway through as well. Went from a very nice opening "like the awesome wedding scene) so the ending cinematic being nothing but a 2 frame microsoft powerpoint of recycled assets. There are plenty of much better choice making games. Give this a pass.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: What began as a slow, somewhat underwhelming tale unfolded into a heartfelt, deep enriching narrative about love, home, fortune and power.without giving anything away. have the wisdom to see truth from falsehood, but always have the strength of your convictions. love your kingdom, love its people, love your family and cherish your house pets.loyal sons of Davern i salute you.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good if a bit basic for what it is. If you have any understanding with how medieval courts actually functioned be prepared to be rolling your eyes a lot. I wish certain things mattered more than they did and that the choices with petioners were more complex but overall this is a fine enough game if you are looking for that kingly decision making fantasy.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game. So much passion and love has gone into a game that pretends to be something it isn't. This isn't a kingdom management simulator as the marketing would have you believe. This is at best a linear adventure game and at worst a visual novel. The decisions that you have to make are interesting, the mechanic of balancing your books at the beginning of the day and having to deal with your visitors was engaging until the first half of the game drew to a close. It turns out that, in fact, literally nothing mattered except a few dialog choices with your wife and daughters. As soon as you realize that your kingdom will not be burned to the ground even if you send half a dozen troops to the battle the game spends 18 in game weeks building up, the passion to play the game or care your choices goes away. See This is the Police for an example of this gameplay and story structure done just as wrong.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Little to none replay ability but dammm i love my wife and daughters, it's definitely a tough game and I'm excited to see what the studio is cooking up next. Also this is one of those games that when you are done playing it, you want to get into the genre, it leaves you wanting more grounded medieval type games.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: I... wow.  I didn't expect this to be as good as it was. I just finished my first play-through and did well, I ... think.  There's a great deal of choices to make in the game and they seem to all have an impact on the flow of the to some degree.  The game forces you to make some dramatic moral choices.  Sometimes they play out well, sometimes terribly, and the game never fails to remind you, continuously, of the outcomes you have to live with.  Spoilers aside, I found the story very engaging.  I enjoyed it thoroughly.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Stumbled across this game at a time when I was thinking something like "what kind of experience would my favourite game need, and why has it not been made yet?".I've got to say, "Yes, Your Grace" comes extremely close to what I had in mind and goes beyond.- Amazing medieval setting- Exciting and surprising (+funny) storyline; a feeling of belonging, "This is my family & kingdom"- Chance to make actually important (sometimes difficult) decisions that will affect future outcomes, and a good degree of complexity- Beautiful pixel graphics with eye to detail, same for the music- A good scope. You basically want to play longer, but given the overall setting and mechanics available etc., I think the developers nailed it. It's not too short but you also don't feel like you're counting the hours for it to finally end.You can simply tell this project was made with a lot of passion and commitment. I would love to play a sequel one day, and in general there should be more games like this. Are there things that could be better with this? Not many at all, maybe a bit more depth to strategic approaches and allowing for the player's political talent to unfold. Making the individual path less black/white and exploring ways to compromise.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a rare gem among games. It's got the right mix of story, resource management, and tension to keep you interested and playing for hours. My single, only complaint about the game is that it's slightly glitchy. For example: there was a petitioner building a church and I'd sent my general to help him. When my general came back and told me the petitioner was probably coming back to ask for gold, I saved up some to help him out, but when it came time to give the petitioner the gold (which the quest text told me SPECIFICALLY was gold), my advisor told me we didn't have enough resources! I think there was a glitch and the game was asking me to pay supplies instead of gold, but the quest text wasn't properly updated.This is just one example of minor annoying glitches (the rest being graphical glitches) messing with an otherwise outstanding game. I am sure some patches are coming out after I write this. It came out yesterday after all.I highly recommend the game! Please make more like this!
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, Your Grace is an absolutely charming, engaging, and surprisingly complex game (moreso than I thought at first, anyway). I didn't feel bored at all during any of the 5 hours I spent on my first playthrough, and I was thoroughly invested in the story that the game had to tell. I appreciated how much the choices you make can affect the game, both in the short and long term. I loved how each character had their own personalities and quirks, for better or for worse. The graphics are so pretty and the style worked really well for the genre of game. It made seeing the graphics at the end that much cooler! If you like strategy/management/story games, I'd absolutely recommend checking this out.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: This game manages to both be frustrating and compelling, often in quick succession.It does a few things really good:The art is detailed and nice to look at. The animations aren't anything to write home about, but it gets more impressive when you learn it was mostly all done by one or two guys.The way the game has you jumping between different people trying to please all of them is stressful and upsetting in all of the right ways.The real consequences to your actions are executed in a way that makes you actually think it over a little bit.The variety of gameplay systems intersect with each other in interesting ways that allow for cool storytelling.The music is above average. No masterpiece, but enjoyable enough and does a lot of the legwork in setting the tone.The overarching story is pretty interesting, but the execution is flawed.Which brings me to the bad:The dramatic tension and suspension of disbelief is ruined at every opportunity. The climactic battles are turned into busywork and watching meaningless numbers tick down. Dramatic moments involving important character deaths are just interrupted with abrupt scene changes. The dialog is really cringey whenever the game tries to take itself seriously, or when it tries to be funny. Separate storylines involving the same character don't effect each other, meaning depending on my choices I can have my daughter screaming at me to never talk to her again in one moment and then sobbing in my arms and telling me she loves me the next (and no this is not intentional).You are railroaded into some obviously bad choices for the sake of plot. It's very noticeable juxtaposed against the freedom you have to mess up or do well everywhere else.The way the dialog is presented makes me want to smash my computer. It's given one. terse. sentence. after. another. So you find yourself spam clicking if you're even a moderately fast reader and then make wrong decisions or miss important points. These guys need to learn about paragraphs. Also it plays this gibberish noise when they speak which fades out the music and then back in at the end. This makes the music very choppy and irritating so you need to turn off voices in the settings if you don't want to experience that.There are some pretty major bugs I experienced with just one playthrough and they were all related to the item system. Honestly the item system seems sort of out of place with all the other mechanics and doesn't add much, except letting you miss out on some stuff if you're not mousing over every detail in every room. It should just not be in the game.The walking animations. why.Verdict: It's a pretty cool game. It's unique and well thought out enough to be worth a try. The story and web of characters are complex and compelling. But it can be VERY frustrating, especially in the beginning pseudo-tutorial sequence and the points of climax. Do not buy if you can't handle a huge helping of kitsch.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable game, you're given some very interesting choices to make and it's not always obvious how they will play out. You can make mistakes and still finish the game, the game mechanics are fairly forgiving so you can spread yourself out and see different storylines and choices play out, I strongly enjoy the freedom to make stupid decisions because you misunderstand the situation, or just feel like being an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ for no reason.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, Your Grace! is a (Decision Making Simulator) which fallows a Polish Game of Thrones themed plot. The game is set in Medieval time period, sprinkled with sorcery and magical tales. It’s quite clear that the developer has taken inspiration from the Witcher & GoT, instead of creating an original story. Yes, Your Grace. Is portraying itself to have this overarching storyline with different branching plots, that somehow are woven together to form these consequential decision-making moments by the player. Its not. What the game is, it’s a very strict path from point A to B, C, D in the storytelling experience. There is a heavy illusion of choice in (Yes, your Grace), you are literally being shoved in the back with a stick with total disregard for player choices, making the gameplay very linear.If there is a hidden adventure somewhere in this game, with numerous branching plots attached to the main tale, I have certainly not seen it with my three start to finish playthroughs.The experience you are getting can be describe as something similar to a game called (The Oregon Trail), where the wagon has been replaced with a Kings throne. Yes, Your Grace. Is not bad game, overall, and there are parts of the game that I love very much. Like the pixelated Art-Style oozes with brilliant atmosphere in every scene, the different ambiance sounds are amazing, and the soundtrack is just superb. You really feel like you’re in the world of (Yes, Your Grace.)All the Royal family members are well defined, each with their own personality and traits. Again, I wish there was more originality in this area. As I could easily trace back references being drawn in each Royal family member to Game of Throne (Stark Family). Both in how they behaved and how the main story played out.In that sense (Yes, Your Grace) story felt predictable, I mean for God sake, they even had the “The Wall” made out of Ice mountains with “Wildlings” attacking the kingdom. Come on…Even though the main plot gives you tiny side steps, none of it is really explored nor does your decision-making process really materialises into something significant, no (story-driven-branching-treeline), here! My impression after finishing the game three times, is that you’re on this roller coaster and if you try sidestepping from it, you are quickly slapped back into place. People might say that (Yes, Your Grace) is a Kingdom management game, it isn’t. You do not administrate anything within your kingdom, not even taxes. Let alone, the vast area you control, its all very basic gameplay. As a King, you have subjects and lords that visit your hall, they ask you for favours, give me gold, give me food, or do A for me and I will give you B in return. That is the extent of your diplomatic abilities, its shallow as the dead sea. If you run out of food, Game Over. Your Kingdom doesn’t starve to death slowly, the civil servants don’t go apesh1it eating each other, there are no rebellions flaming up nor angry mobs that are pounding on your castle doors demanding food for their families, its just Game Over. Try again!I came across a few problems while playing “Yes, Your Grace”. -	31st week – after the Battle. Lady Lena Bugged out in the court hall and was teleporting all over the place.-	2nd bug I came across was a farmer didn’t want to leave my hall after talking to him, had to restart the game entirely.-	One of my advisers was missing his legs, “texture problem”, which looked pretty funny, seeing him levitating above the ground. -	The delivery bird gives me same letter twice about my daughter running away. Which was odd, because I specifically remember her running away once! -	I could marry away my daughter even though she ran away to live in the forest with a lesbian, which is strange! Anyway, this is my overview of the game, I hope you got some meat on the bones, and that my point of view helped you out in your purchase decision! Have fun.As for the price, 17 Euros, I think its to high for what it is, this is definitely a wait for a sale kind of game.

_childDocuments_.review: I have only play this game for 5 hours but all I can say is that this game is great! The story behind it is perfect and doesn't force all of it on you all at once but in a nice orderly manner that you can follow but doesn't interrupt to much of the game itself. I feel like the decision in this game actually has weight to it, Either you help this one small village can effect the game within itself either good or bad! The interactions you can have with the people and your family always brings something to the table! this is so much better than any telltale game I can say in my personal opinion The art style in this game is good, simple but beautiful at the same time. You can easily get lost look at the environment. This game is an amazing game and this game actually went so far beyond than what I was expecting from a game like this since there have been games like this before but never went far unlike Yes Your Grace. The perfect game and the best game to play!

_childDocuments_.review: This game has very limited choises that actually matter, but it does however have hundreds of little quests that can really screw you up if you arn't careful, choises that will either make you either rich or poor, choises that can grow or greatly weaken your army, choises that can make your people pretty much throw their money at you with joy or anger them to riot.You also have a family, sadens me that not as much was done as it could have been with them, many of the family options either feel or just are forced, other than that they are very loveable characters that will make you consider the wellbeing of them over the commonfolk, despite the family not giving any real advantages. In a nutshell, become the king you want to be, executing anybody that has ever dared to threaten you, your family or your kingdom despite their pleading for mercy and desperate excuses, not kneeling for anybody as you are the one chosen by god and you alone! or perhaps be merciful and see reason in their cries for mercy and excuses, as karma might come around and aid you later on, putting aside your diffrences and look at the bigger picture?
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Despite its pretenses this is a point-and-click game with a linear storyline. After playing through it once, I tried to replay and change the really important decisions... only to find there was no way to do so. The only options were 'fine' or 'pay me more, and then I'll agree'. Meanwhile most of the rest of the game were making minor decisions which turned out to be a chore before long. With these two factors put together, I dropped the very idea of a second playthrough and left it as it was.The storyline itself is irksome. I guess they were trying to go for a 'game of thrones' feel, where things just keep getting worse no matter what you do, and the best you can hope for is a bad outcome that isn't as bad as the others. I did get a few good laughs in, but despite one or two fun little side stories, the main flow of the game was just... gross. I ended up toiling for a few hours just trying to get an ending that wasn't too horrible, and I think I got it, but it didn't feel satisfying at all.I honestly never want to play it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Very Linear Storyline, Not a whole lot of replay ability as all the choices come down to about 4-5 possible outcomes. however upon replaying, recently I have revelled in the wonderful plot and cast of characters. While I still believe the game should only be priced at around $10 It is an extremely rich story that while not over replayable is good to come back into and be immersed in.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: An on rails light novel with plenty of false choices, weak mechanics, woke politics which punishes you for having a worldview different than the designers and doesn't give you an option to avoid false moral dilemmas. this combined with repetitive mechanics and worst of all: Memory as game-play. Seriously the memorization bits are the worst part of the game as the game doesn't inform you that you have to memorize things. Especially given it gives you extensive logs of information as if memorization isn't necessary. The Two combat encounters are less complicated than rock paper scissors. It's literally just "do you remember what we told you this thing counters?" and the moral choices come down to pick a side or be fortunate enough to have the requisite resources which is incredibly easy as the game is more interested in telling a story than giving any sort of challenge. The only challenge is from the artificial risk generated from unavoidable scripted events that of course give no actual challenge aside from the aforementioned memorization sequences. The only really good mechanic in the game is the list of choices made with the peasants and the associated resource management. But the UI and records for this mechanic are lacking at best and so the mechanic is only passable, which is really bad given so much of the rest of the game is atrocious. The story is too much on rails to be seen as very good even though the writing is quite well done. Though there's an obvious hatred of history and bizarre infusion of modern culture into ancient times that you so often get with woke type games. The makers of the game seem to just want to vilify this era which comes off as especially weird in a low fantasy series. Really a bad product. I hate that I played it just over the refund limit. Absurdly over priced too as it's a 5 hour game easily unless you want to look for alternate endings which will involve memorization, which is hardly gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Yes your grace is a beautifully crafted experience. I came into this game having no knowledge of it and I was instantly absorbed into the world being built and the characters I was meant to care about. May have even gotten emotional over a few story beats.Game play itself is nothing extremely special. It is a resource management game at its' core. Your decisions impact many things and at points it can become a little stressful. Though I will say I never actually lost (though reading online, many people did lose) so I don't know if that's a testament to my super tactical brain or they just....aren't very good lol. Either way, I never found it to be too hard. I am curious if I ever truly came close to losing. After winning, I did reload the last save to change one decision to get what I assume is the best ending, but I only didn't get that ending due to the game not forecasting a specific cut off point at all. Regardless.Story wise, this game was beautiful. I was genuinely shocked that I grew as attached to some of the family as quickly as I did and how much anger I felt towards the antagonist. I am a sucker for stories centered around a fathers and their children so it definitely got a leg up on me for that. Overall, this game could have benefited from better save states (reloading that final save to change a decision was another like....30 minutes of playing) and pairing that with unskippable cutscenes and occasional slow text boxes makes for a very tiring replay when you aren't wanting to re-read/experience it all again. The sequel looks very good though and I'm extremely excited to play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Good game! I couldn't say much about replayability, because for me it's a one-walkthrough game, but I really enjoyed it.This game is obviously their first real product, so expect sometimes glitches, unpolished mechanics, something rough at the edges... But behind all these drawbacks you can clearly see brilliant decisions in both art and story-telling.Can I call this game a perfect game? Not at al.Can I see the potential behind this game? Yes!!! I'm sure that the next product from these guys would be just brilliant. They are very original and have lots of cool ideas. And the artstyle of the game is veeery good. Definitely look forward to their next game!

_childDocuments_.review: It's very rare I make reviews for games, however Yes, Your Grace hasn't gotten the attention I think it deserves. For context, I went into this game completely blind; it was in a bundle with The Life and Suffering of Sir Brante, and Suzerain, which were both games I'd been interested in, so thought "why not".I'd read no guides, seen no videos, and I've finished the only run I'll ever do in 7 hours.The important bits first:- How long to finish the game? * I beat the whole thing in almost exactly 7hrs.- Is there replayability? * Depends; I'd say no once you've got an ending you're satisfied with unless achievement hunting.- Is it worth the cost? * Ehhh... I'd say maybe. I really enjoyed it, but I can understand it won't be everyone's thing.- Is the music fire? * The Music Is Fire.Yes Your Grace, at its core, is a "choices matter" resource management game. With many people within your kingdom in need of your help, but war with an overwhelmingly powerful foe on the horizon, its your job to try and provide stability and security for yourself, your family, and your kingdom. To that end, the general storyline is set in stone - you will either fail or succeed. However the fates of individual characters, and how you arrive at your ending, are the bits that can be affected. I got what I would consider to be almost the perfect ending on my first go, but there were still plenty of times where I figured I was very close to losing outright.Resource management is not too difficult, but you can still be caught out by poor choices - spend your gold on one village, you may not have enough for another, and if you give to someone undeserving expect to see no benefit at all; there's a loan system from the bank if you need help, but those weekly fees start to get real annoying; things like that. You're essentially trying to prepare for the worst at all times, but if you neglect any one area for too long then you're going to be in trouble regardless.Criticisms of the game for me were the lack of transparency in some mechanics; inventory items have no description so it's hard to know what happens when you use them, or indeed when they can be used - know that items may have multiple occasions when they could be useful, but each one pretty much only does one thing. The "archives" menu too, which acts as your quest tracker, is sometimes missing important bits of information which can make it difficult to remember what exactly you need to do at certain points - the fact that you can't open it during dialogue is especially frustrating, and punishes heavily not playing the game in one sitting.There are also some elements that can feel frustratingly forced upon you, but I feel it's the game trying to say "immerse yourself into the character of the king, don't approach it like you're a player who can just reload with no consequences". Forcing yourself not to reload can be difficult, but trust me when I say that most minor mistakes can be recovered from, and the game's best played when every decision feels tense - it forces you to pick choices that can feel immoral because you just can't guarantee that your greater objectives will be safe if you don't.I don't want to spoil anything, but I'll say that overall my experience with this game was one of increasing stress and tension right up until the achievements popped up informing me of the final outcome; the rush of relief and joy that came from the positive conclusion of seven hours of careful management for a situation I never felt quite prepared for was enough to make me want to leave this review. Yes, Your Grace excellently captures that feeling of escalating tension, without ever making you feel quite hopeless enough to give up, nor quite comfortable enough to relax.

_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute MASTERPIECE. I thoroughly enjoyed the story, even though it wasn't the "perfect" ending, I'm still happy with MY ending. That's where a potential weak point comes in: replayability. Because I don't see any. If you're completely engaged in the story, it feels weird to just erase it and start anew. At least that's how I feel. I really cared about these characters and I feel that I can now empathize better with both parents and monarchs. It was a GREAT experience, the gameplay and most choices were "easy" to maybe "mediocre". I had one choice where I actually had to think REALLY long about. But story... It's just so good. The only thing is the price point. For what you get, I think on Sale it's a no brainer. To some full price might be alright, but only if you can enjoy the story. If you'll just click through the dialogue options, than this game is not for you! I give this a 98/100. Probably my Number 1 Game I played this year.

_childDocuments_.review: Spoiler Alert! I have to say the game itself is great. Yet it is too short and I have to make many decisions based on the plot. I never had the intention of marrying my daughter to that bastard and I knew he must be the one behind the murder. Still, I could change nothing. I hope this game could give us more options(free choices) in the future if developers ever have the intention to make some modifications on this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Intriguing to begin with, but quickly becomes tedious as you are relentlessly without gold, constantly hounded for general/witch/hunter for 2weeks with sometimes two people in line asking for the same person so if you helped the first person in line you are instantly punished by the second unless you are banking 30 gold 30 supplies to give them that instead even though it's near impossible to bank those kind of resources unless you knew what was coming up each day through simply having played before. You decline to help X person and receive -5 public approval, then you could help someone else with an agent or resources of which they ask exorbitant amounts of and the game can quite literally, and often, reward you with zero approval increase despite breaking the bank to help. Quickly found myself skipping through dialogue that wasn't with Asalia or Cedani because any dialogue with the wife/advisor/peasants is simply too predictable with too many text boxes that it is actually tedious to even skip them by spam clicking!
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Real quality Indie Game.  Pixel art design was smooth and a pleasure to interact with, including user interface elements.  Music was awesome as well.The game got pretty difficult near the end where you just absolutely cannot please everybody.  Part of me really wants to replay from different points to see if I could get some different story outcomes, but man that would be a grind.I was a little disappointed that the second half of the game seemed to heavily scale back use of the diplomacy screen and strategy shifted even more toward resource scarcity.  And it didn't really become clear as to why certain characters remained on the screen while others did not.  Some characters had displayed "dead" symbols next to them, after all.  And like, after I get introduced to a bunch of Kings, why only show one on this screen?  Earlier in the game, if you couldn't meet with a character they would just have a "Busy/Away" status symbol.  Ohwell.The only minor bug I noticed was if you sent the Witch on a mission that might usually be fulfilled by your General, the mission summary would refer to her as a "He."Despite those two points, the entire project was lovely and I am glad I tried it out.This game is an Art piece.  It was a really enjoyable experience and I would highly recommend taking a break and immersing yourself in their world to see it and feel it for yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

I don't see much reason to play through again as I'm not a completionist and the overall story won't change much at all. The surviving characters might just change. _childDocuments_.review: Incredibly dull point and click adventure with no real meaningful decisions. I'm not sure any of my choices mattered beyond slightly different text outcomes. The most egregious offense, however is the time it takes to walk across the screen and load into each area; probably bloated the game by 10%.Cannot recommend any feature and incredibly overpriced for 4 hours leisurely going through the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: I thought this game was really dark and scary at times in that you were not sure what was actually a good or bad decision. It was not crystal clear like a lot of games. I enjoyed that lack of clarity. It made it feel very real.The music was great and I enjoyed it immensely.Managing the family dynamic was perhaps at time slow, but it was still fun.Overall, I am very glad to have purchased this game. It was a great play through and I am very curious to see what the various other major decisions would result in at the finale.I recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece, that's all there really is to it. From the artstyle choices and the somewhat dynamic story all the way to each individual character, this game is perfect. But I do have some things to say about my new favorite game, so be warned: Spoilers ahead!During my first run of Yes Your Grace I had no clue what to do really, I just did what I thought was right and I followed my moral compass into almost certain doom. Ofcourse some events are scripted but it always felt like I was following the wrong path with the right directions. I was also filled with honest dread of the upcoming battles you keep preparing for. As it always felt like I fell short of what I needed. The game does that particularly well, it keeps you on your toes. When the game tells you that you must make tough decisions it is not lying to you. The decisions I had to make were tough ones, and I could not always do what I wanted to help everyone. But that's what being a medieval ruler is like, even with the best intentions a king can rarely live up to the expectations he has set for himself. And neither can you. The story is amazing, as I expected it to be. Each individual character felt like it belonged to the story. Far too often do I see characters that are made around a story, where they are made to fit in. But in Yes Your Grace it truly felt like the story was made around the characters. Where each and every npc was an integral part to the story one way or another. I stood perplexed at every turn. For instance when some seemingly random NPC needed help, only for them to come to my aid in the most important of battles and save the day by my side. It makes every choice you make feel important, which they are.The game also made me feel terrible at times, and no I do not mean this is a bad way. This is a major spoiler so be warned again. Your daughter Lorsulia is wed to the young prince Ivo who turns king rather shortly after the marriage is solidified. He abuses Lorsulia and eventually burns her like a witch, for he has accused her of witchcraft. When I read the damned letter, her final words to me, I cried. And not for just a moment, for over several minutes. I have never felt more anger for a pixelated videogame character as for Ivo. That ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Ivo. Through pure story telling, decision making and amazing music and dramatic effect the game did to me what no movie has ever done. It made me feel involved, it made me feel like I was truly there. And that's the end of it really, that's all I could ever want from a game. The game immersed me, it swallowed me whole and then gracefully spit me out when it was all over. I have played the game three times as of the writing of this review, everytime trying to save my beloved daughter Lorsulia. Which is not possible. I hope I have told you all you need to know, now all I am wondering is why you haven't bought the bloody game yet. Honestly what on earth are you waiting for. It's worth every penny.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: A buggy visual novel with no branching paths and a story that gets boring halfway through.I was really looking forward to this game, but it ended up being a disappointment. The music is excellent, and the pixel art is beautiful. Though there is not a lot of art: If you played the demo you have seen all the screens there are! You play discount Ned Stark and must manage your family and your kingdom. The first hour is well written and seems promising. After that you realize that your decisions have no real consequences and you are railroaded along the same plot. Halfway through the game there is a big revel after which you already know how everything is going to play out.At about this point the developers seem to have lost interest as well. There are little more interactions with characters or point and click elements. You just have to balance three resources which is no challenge at this point.The writing is also very shallow. Don’t expect medieval themes, but rather trite modern political issues. Apparently medieval teens are just like modern American ones. With the exception that the medieval bored, pierced, green haired lesbians are not fat. That is about as fantastical as the character development got.It is a shame really: The game had potential but was killed by lame writing / worldbuilding and the lack of a fun core mechanic. Also: post launch there were game breaking bugs. I could not get the game to even start without diving into the forums and fiddling with start settings.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Way better then i expected. amazing music/ambient sounds the 'voice acting' is kinda >.> but it has its own charm. the gameplay is interesting and has consequences. I felt emotionally invested in the characters.My only complaint would be i didnt get to explore everything/everywhere and i end up playing games as a klepto/completionist.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: i really only wish that this game were longer and included even more frequent, even heavier choices. i was hoping for a game in which every single choice i make has pros and cons to it, and was looking forward to stroking my kingly beard at every new issue the townsfolk presented to me. my expectations might've been set a bit too high, however, as this game doesn't have *that* many crazy-impactful choices to make, and most of the major story beats are kinda decided *for* you.  the story managed to keep me hooked all the way throughout, even if oftentimes the "correct" option was so heavily suggested it basically felt mandatory. it does feel like there's a certain level of replayability once youre finished, so that you can correct the parts of your ending you weren't satisfied with, but its pretty easy to tell which parts of the story you *can't* change, so it'd likely be best if you wait a while before replaying, so that it feels less like a chore to wait through those parts. i was pretty deeply emotionally invested in the story and characters, at times tearing up or feeling anger towards them as if they had hurt me in real life. initially, i thought it would be difficult to sympathize with literal royalty, but the main family's dynamic remained realistic and sympathetic throughout. i have mixed feelings on the resource management, as its not much fun when your dwindling income feels impossible to recover from, but it could also be argued that that's the entire point. as the game went on, i had to keep turning down more and more peasants because i simply didn't have the resources, which was annoying at times, but mostly made me feel the level of guilt and regret that was probably intentional. even if its not the deepest game in the world, i'd still definitely recommend it if youve got the itch for a solid decision-making game. despite my nitpicks, i still had an engaging time overall and i wish it lasted longer.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: So... it's pro-homosexual, and for a game that offers "choice", you have no say in the matter.I was "enjoying" the game, but you're mostly rail-roaded on so much, I can't say I really felt like I was a king managing his kingdom.  Neverwinter Nights 2 did a much better job at this, and it wasn't really focused on that aspect of the game.  It has the appearance of kingdom management, but it's really just a balancing act on 5 resources (your three agents, and gold + supplies).This game is basically an interactive visual novel; not really a "game".
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: What a fantastic ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game this is! The music, the resource management, the choices, the story, the pixel graphics! I adore this game! This game is freaking amazing. The characters and story made me laugh, tear up, get angry. I was so invested!Just the right amount of strategy, story, and choices! And the visuals were gorgeous for a pixel game. _childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: This was literally a digital Choose Your Own Adventure book...  but slower. _childDocuments_.review: This game is so good. I played it in one sitting and it messed me up. It really made me care for my (Eryk's) family, and had me crying at points. Only complaint is it is too short honestly. I would love a sequel from these devs with a new story, expanded kingdom building mechanics, and that is longer. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Played on Steam Deck, but there's no controller support so it's a bit awkward. A bit too scripted for me, didn't feel like the choices mattered and I was just being railroaded at times into certain story beats. I like the choices that affect your commodities (gold and supplies) but the choices involving your ONE general were not satisfying, because in one week multiple people may ask for your general to help them but you only see one at a time instead of being presented with a choice between them, and once you make the decision that's it even if you would wish to change it and it could lock off other options as well. There are multiple points with no option to reject an offer, or three options just for flavor that all result in the same action.Essentially this is just a visual novel. If you want to make decisions then play one of the Reign games, or if you do want a visual novel but with choices that actually matter then Suzerain was really good. _childDocuments_.review: In case you are wondering, there's a lot of similarities but this is not Reigns! There's a resource management aspect but the main focus here is on storytelling with there being a lot of character interactions in the form of dialogue options and even a detective subplot. There's a lot of replayability here with but with all the text it might be a slog to get back to the main choices to see the different endings. I would recommend for at least one play-through!
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: A perfect example of short and sweet storytelling in an admittedly narrow yet satisfying sandbox experience. With beautiful design and colorful characters, a single playthrough comes to a satisfying conclusion, while leaving the option to approach many beats of the story from different perspectives for those more invested. Mechanics are introduced throughout that keeps the game fresh, with a nostalgic feeling of point and click adventure games of old.Any challenge as a consequence, however, remains near to non-existent, the few considered 'wrong' decisions are easily rectified, and only through intentional sabotage could the player really bring themselves to ruin. So really recommend for those who are seeking a polished narrative and an unpredictable, casual experience, yet none the less a fantastic interactive adventure. Personally eager to see anything else the developers may make in the hinted larger universe they have created.★★★★☆

_childDocuments_.review: While this game is easy to play and understand. What makes it special is the story, the lore and the brilliant soundtrack. You are forced to make hard choices and face some hard consequences for those choices. There are only a few games that made me cry, and this is one of them that I highly recommend. _childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: The story and surprisingly the animations are great. There are many games where your goal is to manage simple resources through decisions but this one has a really engaging story attached to it which significantly elevates it above the others.The core of the actual game play is deciding whether to grant subjects their request or decline it, each affecting resources you have. Without the story, it wouldn't be able to hold the game by itself so best to think of it as a story delivering tool.The biggest  problem I have with the game is how agents are handled. Agents cost a lot to have around for the week and some requests require a specific agent. In the later part of the game it happens a lot that you can't afford to keep all of them all the time so you pick one and HOPE it's the one that people request that week. If not, you basically lost money.Requests themselves are also weird. You have to decide as soon as you here the request instead of hearing them all and then deciding how to allocate resources. It makes everything a guessing game, which isn't particularly fun.But these are minor complaints and the game is definitely worth a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Really well told story, thoroughly enjoyable and emotionally engaging. Finished it in 6.6 hours.For the content the game provides, I'd recommend at least 40% off before purchasing. The main reason I say this is that there's no roguelite / endless mode, which I'm honestly very surprised by. The main game is great, and I can see some replayability there, but it seems like such a no brainer that it would also have a more procedurally generated mode.Also, the game is really begging for mod support. The game itself is a great storytelling device and could be used to great effect with added content.With things as they are now though, I still recommend the game, but try not to pay more than A$15.--- (Very minor spoiler below) ---There was one moment that I felt was designed poorly; when a peasant had a problem that could only be solved by an agent which you only get one of, and then the very next person in line also had a problem that could only be solved by said agent. I think that's poor design; if the devs really only wanted one of those peasants to be helped, then it should be handled as a single choice between the two, rather than an unknowable and impossible request. There's just no meaningful choice there, and it feels cheap. Thankfully that only happened once though.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: A very enjoyable experience, Yes, Your Grace is just long enought to make you care about its characters and give the decisions you make the weight they need without overstaying its welcome.The story itself is nothing groundbreaking, but it is told so well and with such good pace that it kept me hooked throughout the entire game. Some moments really shocked me, which is no small feat for a game this short.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: A breath of fresh air.Really neatly done story-driven resource management game. While the core gameplay may not be the most fascinating thing ever (decide to give gold/resources to peasants or not), the story is really great and broke my heart a couple of times 😢The graphics, the music, the writing -- everything's great. _childDocuments_.review: This is... a pretty good game, but with plenty of flaws.  It's short (took be approx. 7.5 hours to complete), and has limited replayability, I think.  The premise is interesting, and the gameplay reminds me a bit of Papers, Please, except that while things are often bleak, it doesn't quite have the same soul-crushing air of Papers, Please, for better or for worse.  The art style is good, and the characters are generally enjoyable.  It's got good tension, music, and atmosphere, fun lighter moments, and even some bona fide poignancy.  Overall, I'd recommend as a game to buy when it goes on sale 60%+ off, but otherwise there's not enough game here to be worth the cost.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10Shortish good management game based off of the classic web browser game. You play as a king who sits on his throne and finds solutions to peoples problems through yes and no answers. The game expands on said browser game quite nicely, but not as much as I would have liked. After a short playtime the games main mechanics become quite dull and don't change in any unique way feeling you bored with the core gameplay. The games story and features are quite nice, but I feel it takes too much from the core. Sometimes it feels like you have to fight the devs and the game at the same time. Some encounters are queued in a way that the first option is less unfavourable then the second one. Because you don't know the second option you usually pick the first option not wanting to risk too much and then end up regretting picking the first one as the second one usually is the better one. This trolling went a little too far as it seemed to happen to me over five times at least and made me significantly enjoy the game less. This concept kind of management game which I remembered playing a long time ago was fun then and was fun now. I feel like there is still A LOT of room to improve, but the story elements and characters really made it enjoyable at the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: I really went through a range of emotions playing this game, the storytelling has been done very well. The story is very thought provoking, and really makes you consider your morals and integrity. Looking forward to part two!

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely little game. Great story, interesting characters, even with it's simple design they have personalities of their own that you actually start to like and care for trough the game. I even laughed out loud a few times of the jokes and situations in the game.You do have to prioritize, and the choices, both big and small have consequenses, also late in the game. Either positive outcomes and rewards, or negative losses.Also it has some seemingly random outcomes that mimic chance and real life. Some characters are scheming liars who try to trick you, others are honest, and some are even honest with their intentions, but simply unlucky struck either by bandits or natural causes. You'll never quite know what will happen, but have to take calculated risks and gambles. And sometimes even struggle with ethical and principal dilemmas. Great artwork, lots of charm, details in gameplay and dialogue. I've only had one playtrough, but the outcomes and endings are multiple, and the choices you take in the game will affect the outcome in the end, making it replayable for quite a few times. I can recommend this gem of a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun game, it reminds of me of that flash game Sort the Court where you play as a king who makes decisions. this game is more detailed than that and has difficult choice story elements like "Papers, Please". The writing is good and the characters are likable. the outcome of decisions are sometimes wildly different than I assumed, which is half of the fun. You wont get a perfect score but the game is short enough and fun enough to reply and try different paths.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: While inherently not a bad game, it still feels lacking.From the description, it sounds like there are many conflicting, hard choices, but you'll quickly realize a clear distinction between your choices being either 'evil' or 'good'.It doesn't really help that the character you're playing already has his own worldview, so some decisions kinda depend on that already and don't really feel like your own.With roughly 5-6 hours for a playthrough it also feels rather short.While you could argue that "you could always play it again to have different outcomes", the choices aren't really as interesting and don't give as big of a diffrence to the game as you'd hope for.Maybe okay to get in a sale, but not something grand.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: I don’t understand the appeal of this game. The illusion of choice doesn’t matter to me, I’m used to linear stories with fixed events and outcomes. However, the characters and story are so unmemorable. Not to mention how slow the King moves just to have a few insignificant dialogues with anyone, simply not worth the time and effort. Unfortunately a chore to start and finish.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty simple game revolving around keeping 4 stats above 0 for your kingdom with your kingdom's people all requesting one of the 4 stats. The gameplay is simple but enjoyable, similar to how tycoon games revolve around profit. While the gameplay is fine, the story is enthralling. I highly recommend giving this a playthrough for its short but great story.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: It's a one and done with 0 replayability. It should be a series, not just 1 single game. If they added multiple stories, then it would be legit, and you could even go back and play the stories you played before if you want, but it's really just a story that gives you choices and at the end of the game you see how your choices effected the kingdom, which is cool and not an original idea, but it's still a good idea. However, you'll be done with this game in no time, with 0 replayability because you'd just be repeating the exact same story, just clicking a different button this time to pick a different choice. The game itself isn't fun, it's the story that can be interesting, but like I said, it's over quickly... It's worth maybe $2, but they could do a compilation of these, not just one, and it'd be interesting. But for only 1 of these? $20 is robbery lmao... I beat the game while reading everything, in 5 hours. I went back and tried to replay it just for the achievements, but I couldn't do it, its just not replayable at all, I would be forcing myself to do it.

_childDocuments_.review: Grabbed it on sale. Very happy with the purchase. I managed to luck the hell out and I think get the best ending in my first playthrough (after restarting a couple of times before the third turn). Even then, the ~4 hours I spent with this title were some of the best I've invested in a game in 2023.The art works well. The music caught me in the feels more than once, and is well-timed. Apart from the (especially for the setting) heavy-handed and comparatively jagged introduction of a lesbian daughter, the story was brilliantly executed with a series of lows and muted highs. Great stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: It's tough to care. Being a dad/husband, I thought this story and character would resonate with me, but i quickly found myself not caring much for the story or this family. I thought I would be making meaningful decisions in a story driven stint as a medieval king and father. Instead I felt brow beat with poor choices I didn't make and a miserable family I can't help. Then the game tries really hard to force me to make choices based on its backwards fantasy, 100% modern emotions/problems/situations, and pretty much every character being, just the worst. Couple that with the story being largely on rails, reinforcing my lack of ability to do/decide anything meaningful and the whole thing ended up feeling childish and manipulative.  When I game overed due to having no supplies, I just wished i hadn't played.

_childDocuments_.review: Less like Game of Thrones and more like King of Queens - you're a moronic king that spends most of his time talking to your uninteresting, spoiled daughters. The peasants come to you with the dumbest problems, such as one peasant being constipated and asking for help. Can you imagine a real king dealing with a peasant's bowels? _childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: In short: it's entertaining, but once you discover it's all the same if you make an effort or not, the game becomes quite lame and loses its appeal.Why do I say so? I finished it after 5 hours. It was entertaining but half-way into the game I got a suspicion that my decisions/actions didn't really matter for the critical outcomes, so I intentionally did most stuff wrong: starved my soldiers, didn't buy any upgrades, etc. and yeah... it ended in a success all the same.This game could have been good, but the outcomes of the choices many times don't make any sense and feel very forced. Also what's the point of making an effort if even trying to lose I still win? Also there are many cliches. Wouldn't recommend it.pd: For achievement hunters: this game has several story-related achievements which will force you to play the entire thing at least a couple of times. The game having practically zero replayability, it may not be the most enjoyable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I've just finished my first run and this game is one hell of emotional roller-coaster.It's like watching GOT (but better) and be able to make decision for the character.I started this game with the intention of not caring about the relationship and just focus on resources but end up having so much bonding with the characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Great, bite-sized game with immersive story about juggling family, court and resources.To save new players some frustration, keep in mind:* Returning agents (generals etc.) won't be available for new missions until you've spoken to them, even if they're waiting in line in the throne room. -So be sure to talk to them first so they can be available for new missions for the other petitioners in the queue.* The same is true for carrier pigeons, who won't be available until you've talked to the person you summoned on the last turn.* You can actually leave the throne room to check up on other stuff, and return to continue receiving petitioners. This is extremely useful when you have returning agents you want to talk to about other stuff, before potentially sending them out on a new petitioner mission on the same turn.* There's actually stuff around to be picked up into inventory and used. Not much, but it's there.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: You play as the king of Devern managing your kingdom by solving your people’s problems, managing your kingdoms scarce resources, and trying to survive.The story is really good, it caught me off guard the highs and lows that this story has, while maybe not the most replayable game the story is certainly good enough to play through once or twice. Sometimes the decisions you make can really bite you in the ass. The core gameplay loop was for me enjoyable and scratched that kingdom management itch.The pixel animation is very smooth and really goes well with the game’s aesthetic, the sense of humour in this game is also really good at times during the game.  Overall, I highly recommend this game. The story kept me interested throughout and at times you can really get swept away by the events that are unfolding. The characters are all interesting and have their unique stories. It’s by no means a perfect game but I really enjoyed it and I’m looking forward to the sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: it's a game that can't decide if it's a tough choice management game (think a game where doing the right thing is mostly not beificial so you have to be greedy and not help the poor, along the lines of papers please) and a liniar story game with fake choices. i played trough the initial part of the game twice. the first time i was invested cause i though i had chosen to marry my daughter to the rival king. the king gets poisoned and dies. but wait, earlier on there was a merchant who sells a potion that will cure anything. i replay the game again up to that point and realize that i didn't actually have a say in the marrage and i didn't even get a choice to use the potion...

_childDocuments_.review: I wish the in game illustrations would be prettier, or that some of the characters illustrations would show up when they speak because we only get to the them on the end game. _childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Bought the game because I thought it was a Kingdom Management/Builder focused on choices you make.  Didn't realize it is actually a soul-crushing waste of time.  The game is balanced towards crushing you under with random and petty demands by the Peasants, which if you do not cater too causes a spiral of disapproval that results in dwindling funds & supplies, which means you cannot pay your 3 hirelings, which means you cannot satisfy your peasants wants...until game loss.In the second act of the game, you have ridiculous demands of gold and supplies from your peasants which would beggar you even faster if met.  These cause heavy contentment losses, and just as your ability to make gold, this is not countered by the few you do help as their contentment gains are literally a quarter or half of the losses.  Combine this by 4 to 7 supplicants, most not able to be helped...The game is ridiculously unbalanced in the second act.  I actually thought I was doing okay up until it started, but it immediately spiraled into a depressing series of events that you have no ability to prevent.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite a fun game, however it's really a one and done from what I can tell, after playing through once I tried to play again and explore other decisions and there isn't any randomization at all, makes it super boring to replay IMO, you literally go through the same dialog you went through already. That being said it's a bit pricey for essentially a 10 hour game but still very fun and you can get quite invested in the good writing and characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: i really wish this game was better. The choices matter very little, in the end. What's stands out to me is the writing, which is surprisingly bad, honestly. The story is quite uninteresting, and there's very little lore to dive into. The plot is super linear, and the mechanics are very slow and tedious. Moving around a dead and unresponsive castle just to skip through boring and uninteresting dialogues of the characters, it's not exciting at all. The resource management is bland and not strategic at all, it all comes down to having enough to thick one or two things before a couple of events. The art is not awe inspiring, and the "battles" have no tension at all. And most importantly, yes, your choices matter very little if not at the very end where a couple of summary on 5 or 6 characters on what happens next to them, which you won't care at all. I am sorry, but even if this could be a good take on a new genre, and i really hope to see more of this in the future, this game has little to add. TLDR: Scholastic execution and boring, tedious gameplay, boring uninteresting story, choices don't matter.

I'm absolutely loving this and for those that like royal intrigues and such and multi-path chooses matter sort of games, you wlll too.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game.Especially to Poles - but Polish texts are sometimes misleading. This game is, in general, an artistic expression. The vision on how it is conducted, moved forward and shown to the player is absolutely great. The game took me around 15h of gameplay (although it was a binge gaming) but it gripped my heart no less then some long AAA titles.Pixel art is fitting and shows that less is more. Music is so great and on point. Sometimes bizarre but after you finish it, you will know what it was all about.The mixture of strategy with point&click was very interesting but probably made the game too wide.The game is not without problems unfortunately.QoL is just bad. Not being able to open Log during talks. Totally obscured decision outcomes, bugs and sometimes the game just cheats. You will be close friends with the Load button and online solutions in this one. And don’t be shy to check things online. There are blatantly good/bad decisions and it’s not fun to load 3 “turns” back to fix it.Also the Load button and autosave every “turn” is an obvious workaround for this lack of QoL. It is necessary to get very familiar with the game to know how the UI works (especially when talking, which dialog ends it and which doesn't). This should be done better and after 50 years of computer games I just don’t know why it wasn’t.Two tips so you don’t have to do this too much:The “it’s current year” plot point was (as they too often are) too forced.

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game with deep impactful story telling. Really enjoyed it and glad I played it on a whim. As a whole, Id highly recommend it. At no point did it feel like a slog, managing your resources and the individual requests of your citizens was engaging and fun. You just need to accept you can not say yes to everything, hard choices must be made and you might regret your decisions.From a value proposition I want to say that the value at full price is there, if you really enjoy story driven games such as this. Fantastic game and I got about 8 solid hours out of it. Although at 50% off is where I would say Id be satisfied with the purchase and feel like it was money well spent.There are some cons though to the game, starting with the UI. Unfortunately the game made it extremely difficult to understand on exactly what day events would be happening. Did I have 2 weeks to complete the upgrade system, or was it one day and one more chance in that menu? Or was it ending today? I cant tell, and I found myself having to make rash decisions or stop paying my agents in the hope that Id be able to afford upgrades the following days, but there was never any "This is your last day" or "You have ONE more chance to do this" type of message. In the menu of the end of the week summary, there was no total value indicated. Essentially what I mean is that you had to add and subtract every 1 digit number to try to find how much gold your making, and then subtract the amount of gold your losing. Why isent there a total to do that math for me at a glance? I spend about 8 weeks thinking I was on the right path to managing my resources before I forgot that I wasent taking into account my agents payments. I was losing 7 gold per week rather then making 22 gold.There were several points in the game I had an idea of a decision in mind, but because I asked a clarifying question I felt like I was forced into that path. I didnt like that. Its like someone coming up to you and asking "Do you want to buy this horse?", your options being "Whats the horses name?" and "NO!". If you asked the horses name, you can not go back to say no.

Also, and this may be a very minor spoiler, so stop now if you don't want to know: (SPOILER) I am so sick and tired of all the pet death in the game. Pets being killed for laughs(and a few actually tragic ones) is one of my least favorite tropes in media and this game is filled with that, constantly.  I would have never even considered buying it if I had known just how frequently that would be happening in game. Also, I realized what the scarf was before showing it to the little girl, but of course since there are no real choices I can't finish that story point without showing it to her anyway, even knowing it would be a bad idea.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a weird one. It's good, it has a sprawling story (in a good way), the music is good, it is pretty much "less is more" come to life. The dialogs are also done right, for a change. Short and to the point, no irritating slow mode, "voice acting" sounds are juuuust short of cringy, and the story passes quickly. But... It wears out its welcome after a while.First, the choices. They seem like they matter, but you start to realize there is really only one way the story can go. If the game offers you the choice to promise something, then takes away the option to deliver (or to fail to), it's just unfair, and makes it so that there really is only one "working" choice. This starts right at the beginning, and it adds up. Now, I get it as a lesson "don't promise things you can't avoid", but you end up simply never promising anything.Which leads me to the second grief... The King's character. Sorry, but he's a wimp. A soap/sitcom dad. A weak, stressed, meek individual. Which would be great if it was the result of choices or actions, but it's not. I don't want to role play as this character because apparently it doesn't change, in fact it gets worse.The third one is a technical one. The controls are simple and easy in the beginning, but once you progress to <15 days or so, it becomes really cumbersome to constantly have to browse through ever-increasing dialog archives without having the option to filter, and trotting slowly through the same 5 game venues where the same people are at the same places doing the same thing without so much as a "double click to skip walking", gets old.As simple and 'less is more' as this is, it ends up biting itself in the ass, which is a shame because it starts out so great. If only the controls were better, at least we could move through the story with less annoyances. Also, it seems like a pretty high price for what it gives.My verdict would be: starts out as a solid 7/10, but drags itself down to a 5/10 later on. For half the price, it would be a much better sell.I probably won't be finishing this, and i really can't make up my mind on a +/- verdict. But as I did have a good hour or two of ok-ish fun, I guess it deserves a +./edit: ok, decided to push through and finished it after all. I guess I did relatively good, as seeing the ending notes, things could apparently have ended a lot worse. So maybe the choices matter after all.
