_childDocuments_.review: A fascinating, unique take on the Political Choice-making game, where individual choices really do ripple until the endgame. Leads to an absolute case of "just one more turn", where you're desperate to see the next events, even if it means staying up until 2 am. If you are a fan of Papers Please, you will absolutely love the bureaucratic, asset-management style of this game, as you're forced to weigh the options of your decisions.The game is tough, but at the same time, it is not nearly as tough as it tries to make itself sound. On a blind, very imperfect playthrough, I was able to successfully complete the game with only a little bit of breathing room left, a sign of good game design. Story wise, while not being much special, it is certainly not bad. The major twist towards the end certainly did elicit a gasp from me, as I had to reread the lines to make sure I was reading it properly. It wasn't gripping at all, but it definitely does its job well.Overall, an excellent experience that is definitely worth the price to pick up and play.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of those perfect examples of "You don't need good graphics to make a good game."To give a brief description, you are pretty much playing as the king and you run your own little kingdom. There are "choice making" features. Some are major and some are minor. You have to decide which gets top priority and those that can be put to the side. For the artwork, despite it being pixelated, they designed the game enough that the pixels can be ignored. They still managed to create good backgrounds and your vision will not be messed up whatsoever. To be more specific, I have played pixel games where items or characters may have blended with the background. In this game, I have not had that trouble at all.For the gameplay itself, majority of it is making choices that can either benefit you or hurt you. There are also side quests that you could explore. However, keep in mind, these side quests can either help you or hold you back. I will say this, the gameplay is not random. The layout is pretty much set and you will soon realize there is actually not a wide range of choices. If you play this game once, then you will probably play it again to better the outcome or witness your downfall.The music in this game is actually atmospheric. I have actually been touched and hurt by some cutscenes because of it. So I can say that the music fit with every scene and every situation.The biggest complaint I have about this game is that I wish that it had offered a little more as it had so much potential. Not in terms of how long the game lasts, but there are a couple times where it felt like the choices you made didn't matter. So, it truly made you wish there was alternative routes to take. Also, *SPOILER* you are only exploring the castle. You don't get to explore the kingdom you are running. So it offered a lot, but didn't feel like it was utilized it to its fullest. With that being said, say if they released some DLC's to make up for it, I would TOTALLY purchase them!In conclusion, I am someone who loves to play "choice making" games and this was a fun game. However, the only problem I have with those is that I usually only play that kind of game once because those are the choices that I originally made. I sort of treat it like reality where I can't go back to fix what I think I could have done better. However, for this one, I played again anyway because I did want to fix certain choices, see what I could have done better, and overall it was still fun. You all might have noticed that I only played a little more than 10 hrs of the game and that was 2 playthroughs. So I guess the average time to beat it is 5 hr or so. It is fun, but there is little replay value in here. As I have said, I felt it didn't utilize its full potential, but that doesn't make this game bad at all. I still recommend this!I give this one an 8 out of 10!

_childDocuments_.review: Bravo to this excellent soundtrack that really sets the tone (which I shamelessly purchased when all said and done). One of my larger complaints out the gates from myself is that you don't get to hear this exemplary Nordic soundtrack for as much as you deserve, and I only say this because I was simply wanting more of it. If you're a music savant like I am, you will likely love this feature of it, but let's get to the gameplay!:Keep note that it's a point-and-click item inventory management game with some dialogue. It features "Sims-like" voice mumbles, rather than voice-acting, that seem superior and cute/funny in very many ways in comparison, but the dialogue itself seems quite well-written, and THAT is a key takeaway here--because, as a King, you need to have key communication with the citizens around you, the visitors and lords that come in, your advisors, as well as your family. Learning your family, opponent, and ally needs, are a key part of this game, as well as driving out deviants and others trying to dig a few fingers deep into your pocketbook. Without giving spoilers, I feel as if "critical" or "end-game" actions don't matter much (a major complaint-feel here)--and could be wrong here, but it was clear the more minor-game actions (such as denying a peasant's plea for more supplies, or perhaps a villager's request to investigate a suspicious chicken-killer) absolutely take a toll on your kingdom, which makes this a fun sim, and seems to really negate the end-game and drive the satisfaction that YOU can absolutely be YOUR worst enemy. It provides you with a unique position that allows you to use your SJW power (or abuse it) in your fashion, which will help shape the endings that occur.  I recommend this to anyone who wants to play a King for a day (or few) with a few family strings attached, knowing that the game itself hinges upon your survival.

_childDocuments_.review: The writing is alright for the most part except for the inconsistencies in terms of world building. The world is very much inspired by feudal Europe and the medieval era, yet your character is constantly not taking action where a normal king would or is just incredibly weak when compared to lords who are meant to be below you in power and status yet they somehow have armies twice your size.  I'd say there are only two well written characters in the game, the wife, who is pretty believable and the cute youngest daughter. The middle daughter is just a generic tomboy that you always see in this type of setting and you never spend that much time with the oldest daughter.  The secondary antagonist and their decisions just don't make any sense either, their entire character goes from 0 to 100 in a laughable manner. If you've played the game you'll know what I mean. The game falls into the same pit every "your choice matters" game does, your choice just doesn't matter nor do they really give you the illusion of choice.  Sometimes your only response is "Yes" or "Yes, but I also want this thing". I was able to get through two playthroughs of it in about 8 hours, which shows just how short the game is, and there are only two forks for almost every "meaningful" decision but that's mostly because either a character dies or they don't, which leads to some really disappointing and lackluster moments. If you're a fan of static novels with some pseudo choices thrown in you might like it or even love it but it's pretty disappointing for those who thought it was actually driven by player choice.

_childDocuments_.review: The nostalgic art style of this game really resonated home for me.  The care and thought that went into the little details programming this game is what makes it a wonderful play!  From little things such as the intro music fading instead of stopping abruptly when you select to start or load the game, to animated animals, the stunning use of colors in different scenes and being able to  (my personal favorite) makes this game fun to play through multiple times.  It's not all light and sunshine and sweetness either, as we've come to expect with most games.  There are some tough decisions to make, and some serious consequences to your actions...I'm not gonna lie that I may have reloaded more than once to help one peasant over another, which then had dire consequences later down the road that I never could have foreseen.  If you like this game, please try , the original game is a fun play, same art style and care put into it, yet with a different enough game play which is still hauntingly familiar to keep you captivated for multiple play throughs...and the DLC was worth the purchase!Here's to hoping for more games from Brave at Night, as well as some future DLC for Yes, Your Grace!  I look forward to seeing where this company goes in the future!!

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to enjoy Yes, Your Grace, but the choices are far too forced. There's no incentive to do anything beyond exact requirements because the game has a thumb on the scales to ensure specific outcomes. It doesn't matter how amazing your army is, it will still take the same losses for the sake of a story.Many of the specific requirements to help characters live etc are just "lol you didn't know that somehow, you have to replay" and there was genuinely no way to know the better outcome before-hand beyond luck.The choices you make throughout are generally about being naive or harsh, and you need to be just naive enough to not have your people be discontent. _childDocuments_.review: I don’t review games at all. But, I really want to give a game like this one a review, as it’s very unique to me.I loved the game. The characters are interesting, and your youngest daughter is adorable and hilarious. The story is good, and the twist took me by surprise. I love the art and the music. However despite my love of this game, it also has many flaws. First of all….. your choices really don’t matter overall. Your first daughter is railroaded into a marriage, for the story’s sake. Now, I don’t mind. But….. it’s an early warning how little stuff matters in this game. Your daughters marriages should be a major point of the game. They’re not. A huge missed opportunity.Next, I didn’t like how a seemingly major part of the story, a drug called “Oracle Dust”….. doesn’t matter. I was hoping it would tie into the main story, or you could take it. Unfortunately, it just takes up space in your inventory. Another major missed opportunity.Third, I was disappointed in how the game does very little with the fantasy elements of the game. It has witchcraft…… but despite being mentioned, dragons and monsters have no role in the story. It’s very disappointing, and makes me wonder why they didn’t just make it a medieval game.One other thing I disliked was that the game felt far too short. Not all games need to be long, but, I think the short length prevented the game from having a lot more interesting stuff to do, and prevented the player from really getting to know the characters. I feel two years would’ve been better than only one year of gameplay. My final complaint is that the game feels too modern. Everyone uses modern slang, modern swears, and it can take you out of the story easily.So, yeah. I loved it. I recommend it to everyone. Yet I still only rate it a 7/10. Why? Because I think everyone should experience a less than stellar game every once in a while. Plus, I just wanted to help out the devs for future games. They have something good going with this, and I hope they take our criticisms to heart.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, Your Grace - A Kingdom Management Sim with Heart and Tough ChoicesYes, Your Grace is a unique blend of a kingdom management sim and a narrative-driven adventure, developed by Brave at Night. Set in a medieval fantasy world, this game puts you in the shoes of King Eryk, a ruler trying to balance the demands of his kingdom, his family, and the ever-present threats from outside forces. With its charming pixel art style and emotionally resonant storytelling, Yes, Your Grace offers a compelling experience, albeit one that may not be for everyone.Story and AtmosphereThe heart of Yes, Your Grace lies in its storytelling. You play as King Eryk, who is constantly faced with difficult decisions that affect not only the kingdom of Davern but also his family. The game’s narrative is deeply rooted in the struggles of leadership, the sacrifices one must make, and the weight of responsibility that comes with ruling a kingdom.The story is full of twists and turns, with a cast of memorable characters that you’ll grow attached to over the course of the game. Your interactions with your family—your wife and three daughters—are particularly poignant, as their fates are closely tied to the decisions you make as king. The game does an excellent job of making you feel the emotional weight of your choices, especially as the consequences of your decisions become apparent.The atmosphere is further enhanced by the game’s beautiful pixel art and evocative soundtrack. The visuals, while simple, are rich in detail and do a great job of bringing the world of Davern to life. The music, with its haunting melodies and medieval instruments, sets the tone perfectly for the game’s blend of hope and despair.Gameplay and MechanicsYes, Your Grace combines elements of resource management, strategy, and narrative choice. Each week, you’ll hold court, where petitioners from across the kingdom come to you with their requests. These can range from asking for gold or supplies to requesting military assistance or settling disputes. Your resources are limited, so you’ll need to carefully decide who to help and who to turn away.The game’s management mechanics are straightforward but can be quite challenging. You have to balance your resources—gold, supplies, and military forces—while also keeping your kingdom’s morale high. Every decision has a cost, and sometimes it feels like there’s no right answer, which adds to the game’s sense of tension.In addition to managing your kingdom, you’ll also need to navigate alliances, fend off invaders, and make difficult personal choices that impact your family and your kingdom. The game doesn’t shy away from tough decisions, and the consequences of your actions can be brutal. This can make for a deeply engaging experience, but it can also be frustrating if you’re looking for a more laid-back game.Replayability and LengthYes, Your Grace isn’t a particularly long game, clocking in at around 6 to 10 hours depending on how you play. However, the game’s branching narrative and multiple endings give it a decent amount of replayability. Different choices lead to different outcomes, so there’s an incentive to play through the game more than once to see how things could have turned out differently.That said, the game’s linear structure means that some elements will play out the same way in every playthrough, which might limit its replay value for some players.ConclusionYes, Your Grace is a beautifully crafted game that combines heart-wrenching storytelling with challenging kingdom management mechanics. It’s a game that forces you to make tough decisions and live with the consequences, all while trying to keep your kingdom and family intact. The emotional depth of the story, coupled with the game’s charming art and music, makes it a memorable experience.However, its challenging decisions and sometimes unforgiving consequences might not appeal to everyone, especially if you’re looking for a more relaxing experience. But for those who enjoy narrative-driven games with a focus on choice and consequence, Yes, Your Grace is a game well worth playing.Rating: 8/10Yes, Your Grace offers a heartfelt and challenging experience that stands out in the kingdom management genre, though its difficulty and the weight of its decisions might not be for everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: A fairly interesting resource management game. You are a king tasked with the arduous task of balancing the happiness of your people with the needs of your defense. A hostile army looms just over the horizon, and you must prepare a force to repel them; but at what cost?The core gameplay loop is fairly simple. People under your rule will show up to your court asking for favors. These requests usually take the form of resources, such as food or gold, or assistance provided by one of your agents. Agents can be your general, witch, and hunter, each with their own specialties; the general with combat and organization based tasks, the witch for spiritual or medical related issues,  and the hunter dealing with pests, beasts, or monsters. Agents can also be sent to explore the overworld map, which leads to additional resources, fulfilling quests, and various other matters. The summation of this balancing puts you in a precarious spot when trying to do the right thing and surviving, no matter what it takes. While you manage the daily affairs of your kingdom, your wife and three children will have their own story playing out, requiring you to double as a father. The writing here was done well, and the choices you make will pull at your heart strings in a similar fashion as before. What is right versus what must be done.In terms of the visuals, the games graphics were subtle, but appealing. I have always been a sucker for pixel graphics, and what is shown here gets the job done. The music was a bit lacking overall, but had a few strong moments through the nearly 7 hour long story. My only gripe is that the game is a bit short at 7 hours, at least for my play through. There is potential for replayability based on what I presume are additional endings, but I think it is more along the lines of the Tell Tale's walking dead series; different choices with varying consequences, but ultimately leads to the same ending.Overall, the game does a good job at putting you in the shoes of someone in power, and forces you to make the hard choices. I would recommend giving it a go if you like management sims.

_childDocuments_.review: I have never reviewed a game on steam before, in large part because a game is either successful enough already that I don't think it's worth reviewing, or not good enough to warrant my time. While I don't necessarily think there's any point in writing a love letter to Yes, Your Grace, I certainly think it deserves another positive review. I had only first heard of this game a few days prior to writing this review, and have no real knowledge of its background with crowdfunding or development, all I can speak on is the finished game I picked up during the summer sale for $15 as an effort to get my other purchases over the $5 discount threshold. Two things should be established out of the gate: This isn't really a management game nor is it a choose your own adventure game either. It is also a very short game, with variable replayability. I was expecting the inverse of all of these things to be true when I picked it up, so be forewarned. If you strictly want those things, Yes, Your Grace may not be for you. However, and I can't stress it enough, I found the story it did have to tell compelling and engaging enough for me to not care that my expectations for what it was a as a game were pretty off the mark.The management aspect of gameplay is pretty basic, which admittedly wasn't a bad thing to me once I realized I was playing primarily for the story and wanted to focus on that aspect of the game. It wasn't gripping, but it wasn't unenjoyable, and served to give some depth and context to what exactly the protagonist gets up to as King if nothing else. The decision making, mechanically, doesn't have much impact on the story that is told until close to the end, but it did make me feel more invested in the characters and what happened to them. It made getting invested and attached far easier when I was actively participating in the lives of these characters, even if I wasn't directing the story.The presentation of the game is also worth talking about, at least. The pixel art look gets used a lot, especially by indie games, but I think it's done well enough here that it was enjoyable, The throne room looks really nice, as does most of the castle, and I particularly enjoy the art for the family. The way dialogue is done is probably my favorite parts of the presentation. It gives ideas about tone and voice without putting a specific voice actor into your mind, which I think is good for a game where a certain amount of projection onto King Eryk and his family is important to get invested. It can be a bit weird at times when characters are saying sentences worth of text but only vocalize a few syllables, but it the sounds they do make are well done and add character, even if they can be out of place at times. The music was the least interesting part, to me. It wasn't bad, but it was mostly forgettable, and a few times it seemed a bit thrown in; there's a particular scene with a bear I have in mind for that, and it becomes clear when you see it. The traditional art for the family is absolutely standout though, I very much enjoyed it, and it gave some more depth to the mass of pixels I was trying to relate to. I have never given a ♥♥♥♥ about steam trading cards, but I made an effort to get all of this game's so I could get the high quality art of the characters. Overall, pretty strong presentation, but I wouldn't call it a home run.The story itself is - in my opinion - the thing that takes this game from okay to one of my favorites. There are no spoilers ahead, so there's no need to be wary. The story is fairly quick to get through, which I will bemoan, just because I would have enjoyed more - though the Devs have talked about possibly doing more with the story of Yes, Your Grace, which would be nice. Even so, Yes, Your Grace does a very good job with the time it does have; I beat the game in an afternoon - I got the best ending on my first run, based on some googling, so I'll be speaking mostly in reference to that. I was totally invested in the characters by about half an hour into the three hours it takes to complete. Your mileage might vary on that, but I thought the characters were all very compelling and endearing, even if they fall in line with the tropes you might expect. They're not super complex, but they aren't one-note either, not to mention they're easy to like and they have a lot of personality. I consistently believed that King Eryk was speaking to his wife and his children, or his loyal adviser, or a lord, or a king, or any other minor character. I am admittedly no literary critic, nor am I a good enough writer to give much criticism, but the writing in Yes, Your Grace felt well done and appropriate for the sort of down to earth fairy tale tone the game gave me. The plot itself is very compelling without being overly contrived, but isn't terribly predictable either. The small events that punctuated the large plot points were what helped make things so easy to get invested in for me. Running around the castle to make a gift for my wife not because it was part of the overarching narrative, but because I wanted to get her a gift, was the sort of interaction that really helped sell me on these characters. I do think the game could have used more things like this, but A, it's possible that I simply haven't stumbled across other similar instances, and B, I would also admittedly buy a nobility life sim featuring these characters, so it's not like what's there isn't enough to make it work well. As mentioned, I got the best ending, and feel no real desire to go find the worse ones, so its possible they might not be as well done, but I would doubt that based on my experience at least. Overall, a very concise but compelling story that I'll probably wanna revisit every few years just because it was enjoyable and easy to engage with. I'd highly recommend this game to anyone with $15 and an afternoon to kill. If you're considering watching a movie or a few episodes of a TV show alone or with an SO or what have you, consider playing Yes, Your Grace instead. It's a lot more satisfying and enjoyable with a similar sort of time investment and a story that - as far as video games go - is one of my favorites.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty fun and engaging. If you've ever played the Kongregate game Sort the Court, this is pretty much the same thing but expanded to include more royal court and family drama. If trying to strike a balance between various pools of resources is your thing, you'll like this game.My one complaint so far is that the major events of the story feel incredibly railroaded. No matter how well you do or how well you prepare, certain things WILL happen. As an example, I played the first few weeks and somebody was poisoned. I couldn't save them. A few weeks prior, somebody was selling a mysterious medicine, but I declined it. After finding out someone was poisoned, I reloaded my save and bought the cure. It didn't change the outcome at all.After that, a merchant came by selling a magic chicken. I wanted the chicken to stay in my throne room. The game literally won't let you proceed unless you give the chicken to one of your kids. There's not an option to keep it. As a player, it feels like I don't actually have any control over anything. But the story is interesting and the gameplay loop is fun, so I'll keep playing it anyways.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved this game. THE GOODThe artistic quality to this game had me in awe, and appreciating every little detail in every scene. I loved the variety in sprites, no two characters looked the same, and even their Okami-esque voices/gibberish was unique. I loved the music, it built suspense, felt delightfully medieval and sentimental at times, and other times really felt like great background "thinking" music when I had to pause to consider my choices. I really grew to love the king, and his family... I really sympathized with the situation their kingdom was in, and wanted to take care of it, and everyone in it. This was a great story, which clearly has a linear progression that can't be completely fully swayed one direction or the other, I enjoyed influencing the details and walking the razor's edge with my resources to see how everything would play out in the end. I can't wait for more.THE LESS-GOODI got through it about 75% the first time before I ran out of resources, and my people all rose up and killed me... I get it. Realizing I'd missed out on a really important connection with a certain Lord, I was a little annoyed that there wasn't really a way for me to make gold after the first half of the game finishes, there's really one guy that helps with that an his methods are questionable. In any case, making that one change to my second play through absolutely nailed it, I made just about every decision the same after that, and finished the game with a suitable ending.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a little "choices (don't)matter" game inspired by Paper's Please and a little bit of Frostpunk. Story is simple and gets very lazy in some aspects and simplifies some plots, choices presented to you matter only in terms of resources, almost never in the main storyline - and it's not a big deal anyway, since game is designed in a way it's extremely hard to mess up and actually come unprepared for 2 main events happening in the game you have to be prepared for - and they also have a fixed outcome, no matter how do you deal with them. Some rewards from petitioners don't make sense, and the game leans into that binary choices system - help this guy, another guy gets angry, no way to satisfy both. Also it tries to be "smart" a few times too much with typical "the guy we presented as a better choice was an idiot all along and we gave you not a single mean to predict that, you must be feeling really stupid right now" cliche.In the end you cannot deny this game some charm, i found the characters and different petitioners fun enoguh to finish the game, but if you are looking for a game where you shape the story with your choices - that's just not it. If it looks interesting to you anyway - get in while on a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: "Yes, Your Grace" is, as the Creators claim, a kingdom management game. It isn't. It's a pure storytelling game with RPG (acting and deciding, forget skills and statistics), strategy and adventure (barely, but always) elements. You are sucked into an engaging Shakespeare drama situated in a fictional medieval Slavic kingdom (with strong Polish references). And the story is one of a hell of good writing, really.  But if you want to play this game as an ongoing kingdom management sim with high replayability - forget it, you will be disappointed. The game is sticked mainly to the plot and doesn't provide Crusader Kings 2 experience on a miniscule level where you have full freedom of choosing your path.The game offers you several features, such as audiences during which you deal with current situation in the country, simplified strategy panel in which you can explore your lands and send your agents or invite lords from other lands to consult with them. The game is divided into one-week segments and you have to keep an eye on the situation with your resources (supplies and gold) and people's happiness. With gold and supplies you can keep your kingdom running, use them to help your people, bribe or develop your castle. The decisions taken during the game matter, but they won't stop from occuring key elements of the story, you can only tailor the possible outcomes. Personally I don't have problem with linear stories if they are well-written. And as I said above, this one is pretty well written.Unfortunately, the game has its own problems. The diplomacy and kingdom management from the Throne Room is simple, but enjoyable, but the problem starts when you get off the chair. There is little posibility of interacting with surroundings in your capital and usually your next steps will be only limited to visiting your relatives. There are few cases of interacting with items, but this point-and-click adventure elements barely show up. Finally, even the story and the atmosphere is great, the game can be beat in 7 hours without rushing. There is no endless mode after finishing the story and the replayability is quite low - some elements in the story have to occur and you might be interested only in checking other possible outcomes and unlock missing achievements. Last but not least - the game really differs from the videos presented on Kickstarter and somebody expecting this game could really feel cheated.But even with all these downsides I really enjoyed the game. So, why the hell I don't recommend  this game? The reason is much more trivial. The price. It's too high. And even the storyline can't repay it. At least they could at least add the soundtrack for free. Fortunately I bought it during the -20% sale, but to be honest, it still too high. Wait until the price drops at least 40% or 50%.

_childDocuments_.review: It's tough to review this game because I did enjoy playing it the first time through, so it has value for sure. But on my second playthrough I realized a couple things that leave me feeling letdown. These kind of management game are fun in my opinion, and I especially love branching story paths in games. Sadly many games with branching stories make it appear as if you are making decisions, when in actuality you only have a few choices that don't effect the plot much. This is true with Yes your grace. The main plot in this game is very straight forward and always happens you don't influence it. The only thing your decisions change is which character lives or dies. In my first playthough I was quite bad and had many characters I wanted to live die. I also was bad at managing resources. On my second playthrough I had mastered the resources and could easily by anything I want and chose the best outcomes for my characters. The sad parts are that the best outcomes for the characters are usually that they don't die, we don't truly get to control what happens to them they either do what the game says or they die. And the plot either play out as normal or you lose the game. So after two playthoughs I feel like I have no content left for a third. The story is to unchangable and the choices outcomes are to white and black. I would never want most of the choices, so no reason to play again. Now that the downer stuff is out of the way I do want to leave you with some good stuff. The story is quite good, I liked it alot. and the second playthrough was easy, but it felt good to exert my will on a system I poorly understood before. Also the system of management was quite interesting. I was only let down that some aspects seemed to go underutilized. I didn't need the messenger at all for halve the game at least. The core is quite good though. So the game is good fun for at   least two playthroughs. Some kind of sequal with expanded plot and gameplay built around these mechanics would be good. I would surely try it out. TLDR: Only really fun for two 5 hour playthroughs, A bit let down by the limited choices and outcomes.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't be fooled by the decisions and the story-telling, people, Yes your Grace is actually about managing the ressources of a contry full of edgelordian madman using !You do not get to have the biggest say on the overall story, as it is indeed rolling happily on rails into the next medivial drama town with quite obvious plot-twist tropes, but with , you will always come out on top."Oh no, your Grace, we have only  Supplies left but we need  to survive, how can we possibly do this?!", your subjects will complain to you desperately, like the big crybabies that they are.Lucky for you, you do not immediately devolve into the fetal position at the slightest sign of a problem and can thus solve this and other clearly very complicated, impossible tasks with ease for you provide for your people, you will still never be able to stop the "glass is always half empty"-attidude, which seems to be quite the disease in your kingdom.They will thus simply continue to cry, scream and panic as you shower them in wealth and prosperity.But it is okay, as your  exposes all characters as overly emotinal lunatics, who just revel in the thought of immediate doom, and it is _childDocuments_.review: Okay, my only complaint with this game is that it's somewhat short.Don't get me wrong, there's a fair bit of content in this game, but really only a few scenarios that change the rest of the game. In short, this game is fantastic. The soundtrack is wonderful, and by only complaint on that end is that we didn't hear more of it more often (on that note, please, BUY THE SOUNDTRACK, it is lovely). The pixel art and the voices had me thrown a little bit, and the latter especially took some getting used to, but in the end it had its charm. The game is a choice-based story game with heavy point & click elements with only one setting to speak of--the castle. There is a world outside, sure, but you get the picture via your subjects telling you what's going on over the walls of your castle...or when armies march to your gate and you see them in person (not a spoiler--that's literally the introduction). The world-building was pleasant, and while there is "magic" and maybe (it is very unclear--you'll see why) monsters, most of the stakes are realistic medieval proportions.The story was entertaining and far more stimulating than I honestly expected, which is great. My only qualm was the lack of more options. However, most of the things I wanted to change but couldn't were sort of keystones to the whole narrative, so...I guess I just wish there was more content, and what content existed was good enough to want more. Make deals with lords and fellow kings to strengthen your kingdom, marry off your poor daughters (or don't), help/ignore peasants, and fight to ensure your family and dynasty don't die with you. Have fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: A story of a King facing various troubles, from wild daughters, peasant problems and drug dealing to saving whole kingdom during war. And it is an unexpected gem.The whole gameplay is basicaly about decisions between two choices, but with a longterm and often not really obvious consequences that can matter a lot later in the game. It's similar system to Reigns series, if you made a proper game with a good story out of it. The fun is in not knowing what happens next and dealing with your choices during the story. Many of those choices lead to the tragic events and are emotionaly difficult to choose or accept. Would you force your smart, funny and playful daughter (kind of Arya from GoT) to marry an ally king, even though you know she will never be happy (or worse)? It is (probably) your only chance to save your kingdom after all, but is it really worth it? There may be better options later, but will you risk it? This game is full of choices like this. And it doesn't really lean to forgive you the bad ones.   Yes, Your Grace is sometimes really funny (omg those voices! Aristocracy... The bard !!! And Wojtek! :) ). However, it is even more frequently sad or tragic.  Pixel graphics is really nicely done with a film-like moments and perfectly serves its purpose: to provide a good story. The music and sound is even better for the immersion, with really strong Slavic vibes. I finished the game in approx. 6 hrs with around 2/3 achievements during one run. Developers made really great job here and I'm looking forward to anything they will do in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun inventory balancing game; it reminds me of the old Castles II game I used to play as a kid, and scratches the kingdom management itch that the Reigns card games just weren't quite scratching for me. The pixel art is charming and lovely, and the game is difficult without being impossible, so you feel a real sense of achievement when you manage to win. That said, it should be noted that there's an overarching plot that you have very limited control over. Several times your options as King are basically "Yes/Yes, but". Especially early on, you are crowbared into several decisions that I simply would not have made, and it was particularly frustrating when the plot came back around to chide me for those "choices" that I didn't want to make in the first place. And in the last third of the game you're basically locked into whether you want to be nice to the invaders or nasty to them; the game even *says* at several points that you need to be 100% Nice or 100% Nasty in order to get help from 1 of the 2 available nobles you're courting for help. Not a lot of wiggle room for role-playing. Those issues aside, I enjoyed this game. But I don't think it has any replayability value whatsoever after you've made it to the ending in one piece. You're basically on a single plot-rail the entire time, so the only "choices" you really get to make is how to manage your gold and food supplies. While that affects whether the plot goes well or not, it doesn't really unlock new content, if that makes sense.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: It's a gritty, gut-wrenching journey through the highs and lows of war and revenge.I made the tough call to sacrifice an ally to save my kingdom from barbarians, and it seemed like the right move at the time. But when that ally turned around and betrayed me, killing my daughter and amassing an army of 5,000, I knew I was in deep sh*t.I scrounged for every last resource, but it was a losing battle. My wife and son died, and all that was left was my burning desire for revenge. I didn't give a damn about my castle at that point, I just wanted to put that scumbag in the ground.The siege that followed was brutal, with my 299 men pitted against an army of 5,000. We fought tooth and nail, using every trick in the book to stay alive. It was a battle of attrition, and it seemed like the odds were against us.But I never gave up. I was willing to do whatever it took to see my enemy fall, even if it meant waiting years for the perfect moment to strike. And when I finally got my revenge, it was sweeter than anything I had ever tasted before.If you're looking for a game that will test your mettle and make you question your morals, this is it. Just be prepared to lose everything, including your mind, in the pursuit of victory.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Yes Your Grace is your typical "King hears the peasants" game with the promise that you will have to make tough choices. Your petitioners come with requests for gold/aid/supplies, and you can give it to them, or dismiss them with a handwave. However, instead of needing to make choices, it's instead that you need a strategy guide.Here's why I dislike it: If you're playing BLIND, making your own choices, you will see family members hurt (emotionally or physically) or you will be militarily defeated, or the peasants discontent and kicking you off the throne.If you're playing with a GUIDE though, you are one big happy family, with your army victorious and lands defended, because you know which peasants need to be helped, and which can be dismissed.Therefore, in my book, this game is a big fat thumbs down
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty fantastic, the art design is great, story is great, music is amazing.If you're taking your time you can probably last about 8 hours in a single run, if you're skipping every conversation and ignoring the side stuff, you'll be done in half the time. A lot of this game is in the story, less about the gameplay. The majority is spent building on your kingdom, getting to know the stories of the individuals in your lands and deciding how you will affect their tales. It also relies on you making some tough decisions. Someone's food was stolen by your enemies? Do you give them food that they lost due to your actions or feed your army to prevent some from deserting? A minor lord did something dishonourable but they offer their army if you spare them, what do you do? Your people are asking for gold to rebuild but you need the gold to reinforce your castle. Plenty of decisions to be made.It's great fun and worth a couple of playthroughs, it's best to go in as blind as possible cause there's a few twists, some predictable, some not. Only gripe with the game is that when meeting with people each week, you can't hold off from making a decision until you've spoken to everyone, sometimes I'll send my general to help some guy and realise I needed him for something much more important but I don't get that option again later, huge issue in my opinion.But yeah, game's good, maybe a bit expensive so wait for a sale I guess.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, your Grace is a prime example of how risky kickstarters can be for both backers and developers, After a few years of Rafal dealing with set-back after set-back he's finally managed to publish what I think is a solid, indie game with a very enjoyable, although predictable story.  But it does showcase Rafal's commitment to his projects and although smaller in scope than the intended original target it is nonethleess a solid game. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: I have played this game through a few times now and my overall rating would be that's its OK.  I felt the that the twist and turns in the plot made for an excellent story.  I have always thought a kingdom management game like this would be an awesome game to play. I would have liked to see more options like custom troop/army selection, castle upgrades/expansion, economy upgrades/resource trading with allies etc... and more involved, less busy work when dealing with peasants.  I was EXTREMELY let down by the fact that it doesn't seem that your choices have any real effect on the outcome of the game in regards to what happens with your daughters, big army alliances and trying to solve the kings murder basically the game is going to go one way regardless of your decisions.  I understand this is a start up game company and i would like to see what they come out with next but i would not recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: It is said that a theatrical experience can give you certain feelings and make you become a better citizen, that is at least what the Greek said.I can say that this is the case for Yes, Your Grace. This is a type of game where not only do you have to manage your kingdom but also your decisions have impact in the long term, which makes the game differtent from the other "choose your adventure" kind of game. The story plays out very well and I really felt good being able to save my family but also provide for the poeple in the kingdom, so if you have some time to spare in this wonderful story, or even better, replay it, I would gladly recomment this game
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DRI would behead a certain villain again, because he behaves like Vladimir Putin.Longer Read:I came to play this true Indie Gem due to two facst: 1. I got myself a Steamdeck, 2. I missed to cancel my HumbleBundle Monthly. So I normally I would have sold this on Ebay but because of the Deck, I gave it a shot. And am I glad I did. While this may be a game you only play twice, because after that you know all the alternative story lines, what there is in the form of gameplay, trully shines. Not only is it plain fun to organize the kingdom, furthermore the storytelling really shines. It is charming, heratbreaking and if you know a certain Witcher, very fun.This is just a game to pick up and play in a couple of days and then never play again, but it makes you wanting more of the same.Give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Got a good 7 hours worth of gameplay out of this game. unlikely something to play again unless it's really your thing.The game gives you the illusion of choice while funnelling you down a linear path. I'm not against this kind of story telling at all however it does give the player feeling that his choices don't really matter until it's any important story segments. the second part of the story is the weakest in my opinion as it lacks further dialogue for the kids for quite a while which is sad as the first part of the game is quite fulfilling. the dungeon is under utilised only really being used for a few segments and almost no interaction there. Overall i'm happy with the game as i bought it on discount. I wouldn't buy it for full price.My verdict is to await a discount unless you desperately want to play this. 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Its not a bad game. Finished it in 2 sessions because i wanted to finish the story. No BIG surprises for me in that regard.I actually wish this game would offer even more, because i like the basic construct.But then again...it did cost me 15 euro so i cant expect a big blown up package of content and intertwined systems.So to summarize: The game is fairly priced and entertaining. It did offer no challenge but some minor story twists. It wont stay in my memory for long because in the end its a missed opportunity. But i dont regret to have spent 8 hours on it.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: A game about dealing with your little daughter's obsession with collecting increasingly concerning pets, it's pretty good.On a serious note, the atmosphere is great and the gameplay is simple but engaging. It's not very long, but the playthrough I did had me hooked. Each week in the game you have to make choices about how you allocate your resources and talk to important characters, and every now and then a surprising twist happens. You also get to take part in the daily life of the king's family, and I found the king and his family to be charming, each in their own way.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very much about the story and living with your choices. The writing is so good it will make you:Hate the villainLook for solutionsRegret your choicesWish you could go back and fix things or do them differentlyShocked and surprised at the plot twists.Tips I want to pass on are: You can talk to any person in your throne room, in any order.Trust your daughters.I think the devs should consider adding a story mode without the need to resource manage. So that those that struggle with the game can still experience the story.I really enjoyed this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Great narrative, amazing art, carefully designed... enjoyable all the way through. I don't really have words to express how good it was.You can feel the love and effort the team has put into making this game. Please buy this game to support the developers so they can keep making awesome games like "Yes, your grace".
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: The game isn't as long as I wish it was but still good. It was fun managing my resources and talking with lords to make alliances. I bought it when it was on sale for around 15 dollars and I think that is a more fair price. My only complaint is the story suffers from story telling like Telltale. Replaying it shows most of the choices you make early on don't matter too much. Second half of the story does have key moments that do matter. But don't expect to be having as much fun on the second playthrough. Pretty solid overall, I'd give it a buy/
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: When I first booted this up I thought having to maintain my relationship with my daughters would be a slog, however, the writing / progression of the game is so well done its actually quite charming. When my youngest found her pet snail 'Smudge' and my eldest found a keen interest in sword play after I confined her to the castle due to her sneaking out to get drunk at a wedding, it kinda warmed my cold, black heart.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Finished one play through casually in about 6.5-7 hours. I would like to go and try a few different ending variations. I wasn't quite sure what to expect, and I'm not really sure what to even compare it too. It was cool, I look forward to more from this genre/style and even if they just want to add on more stories to this as DLC.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting for a minute but ultimately kept getting irritated with the story being on rails; might not be fair but I expected more flexibility.    As to the strategy it is more gamble and guess than planning so it doesn't satisfy the trade off of limited resources.  You can run out but you really have no idea 1/2 the time the value of a decision.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Overall great story with a few elements of suprise! Not all choices impact the main story progression, however every choice matters in the end. Loved the artstyle and the character design, every npc felt unique in their own way!I got all the trophies in 15 hours, you could very easily get them wayyy faster that I did. So for that reason I'm not sure if I would have paid full price for this game. However, you should definitely grab it and give it a go if it's on sale!
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: I had a hard time deciding whether to recommend this game or not. The first hours I thought it was kinda boring. I had expected more choices and consequenses, more building the kingdom, more freedom who you want to ally yourself with and so on.In the end though, it grew on me, I found its charm and had fun playing it. The story became funny and intriguing and I got into the classic "One more round" a la Civ mode, and that's always a good thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Not worth the 20 bucks for barely 6 hours of gameplay. If it's ever on sale for like, 5-8 bucks, knock yourself out. For those who want more detail, the following is for you.(2nd time typing this out, steam decided to ♥♥♥♥ on me and delete all my text during my first attempt. Sorry if my thoughts aren't as neatly gathered as they were the first time.)---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------S P O I L E R SSo right out the gate you already have your choices in this choice making game restricted.Its along the lines of "You promised your daughter's hand to some guy, and he's going to march on you unless you deliver"So, since I wasn't given any other context for this, I immediately just decide to go with the demands, I'm a man of my word.So I go along for a while, then I get railroaded into "War time, time to call up my friend the King with the Bling"And I do get more context afterwards, but my character should've already known it.So you go with the "fight the guy option" and you do stuff to build up an army. And despite your efforts, it seems like you were simply destined to lose, but then the game pulls a win out of its ass by just making a mountain explode on your enemies? You get decimated too, but you're still left with some soldiers.So basically your choices were pointless and it was actually all a ruse, this was just a setup to reset you for the 2nd ACTUAL big fight. Surprise surprise though, it doesn't matter either.So things leading up the the 2nd, and final fight goes about as follows.You gather peasantry to fight for you instead now, but they only help you if you did what they asked of you previously, so this is yet another instance, and a big one at that considering you do this the entire game, where your choices don't really matter. Though in the end you don't end up with much either way. Not that it really matters. I'm confident you could do the ending big fight without doing anything really.Only about 5 small things change based on your choices in the end, but they don't really matter either because after the 2nd battle, the game's over. There was supposed to be some level of intrigue, but it doesn't amount to much.The outcomes are either "it was them" and you kill someone for what turns out to be no reason, or the blame automatically shifts to you. Both lead to the same outcome. So it didn't matter either. The final thing is more of an issue I took personally with the game. Your 2nd eldest daughter, they decide to make her a lesbian for no reason. She meets this other girl, and they get to know each other for maybe a month, and she, the 12 year old girl, decides that she's in "love" and you never see her again. I was playing the supportive father here and went with it, but this is the King's own flesh and blood, and this is a medieval setting, that wouldn't have happened. The devs can virtue signal and whatever, that's fine and dandy. I don't really care who's bumping uglies with who, but it's generally unrealistic in this setting and could've been done without. Both choices regarding this character were pretty ♥♥♥♥ really. But they, like most choices in the game, didn't even matter.So my final verdict?game SUCKS i go to BED
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: The best narrative structure you can find in any indie game easily and also beats some AAA games narrative! The story beats are masterfully placed and every decision makes you feel on edge. It really makes you feel under the skin of a king taking very though decisions and even with some humorous dialogue to sooth in the mood. I didn't think we could have any new point & click adventures that can bring something new to the table but Yes, Your Grace proves me wrong.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice game.A game about choices. With wonderful pixel art, a beautiful setting, and charming characters, this game puts the player in the role of King Eyric, who has to deal with all the problems of ruling a kingdom, its peasants, other noble houses, and a beautiful family.The game is not long. The decisions are interesting all the time, and what looks like nothing now can become a problem in the future. It has a very good soundtrack that empowers the emotions in certain moments.If you want to play a beautiful pixel art game, with a low pace, but intriguing and intense, this game suits perfectly for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: The only con I had about this game was that there wasn't any more content after you finished playing.Apart from that, the story is rich and filled with emotion. As a king, you can feel the burden.I'd like to see another game like this, but with the option or mode of continuing to play after the story to see how far and how long you can go. with random events rather than scripted ones.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: I did enjoy the first half hour playing this game. But after realizing the choices I made would not make any difference to the ending, it just became exhausting to repeat the same day over and over again.In the end i gave up reading dialogue patiently and just selected whatever came into my mind first. No way I can loose the war anyway.The battle field part is boring. All I could to is to walk around and select whatever pops up.Don’t recommend this game unless u only wish to kill time by clicking mouse & reading dialogs
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: The game is basically Reigns but embellished with charming pixel art, animations and a story, among a few more mechanics. The game introduces you gradually to the features available, with concise tutorial text windows. Nothing is wasted. The interfaces are functional and lean at the moment.The situations and dilemmas presented to you as king are difficult and sometimes you are put in positions where any choice will inevitably upset someone. This adds some drama to the game, and a bit of realism as choices lead to repercussions.I can certainly see how much more this game could grow. It's a very charming game, the art and music complimenting each other very well. The humour in the interactions you have with people in the game is well-written and quirky.My only criticism is that you often spend a lot of time settling trivial family matters and squabbles between your daughters. It seems like a waste of time when you have important, kingdom-saving duties to perform. I understand the family element is part of the game's design, but to me it feels unnecessary and tedious. For those wanting a more interactive version of Reigns, this is not it... it's half it, and half family drama.Choices become harder the further into the game you get, and there is a mounting sense of tension due to the plot, which is executed in a very organic, non-invasive way. Your adviser who sits by your throne is of great help when you're unsure how to proceed.I recommend this game, but am a bit disappointed that the family soap opera subplot almost overshadows the main story. It would be good to have an option to switch off the family drama stuff, 'cause, you know, deciding what wedding dress your daughter should wear shouldn't really take precedence over a looming barbarian invasion.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty good game.You have to runs your kingdom and make choices in preparation for an enemy invasion. The characters are interesting and some situations can be difficult. The music is very good and the pixel art is great. It reminds me a lot of the final stage of Fable 3, just more fleshed out. It's funny how everyone hates on Peter Molyneux, all the while getting a lot of their ideas from him. The one thing I dislike about this game, which is sadly becoming very prevalent in these "moral choice" story games is that a lot of the choices will have a "twist" in the end. You get it, you save some normal guy on the road from being lynched, but OH-NOOO he's actually an evildoer that eats babies. Your Grace turns this kind of "catch" into an art form and it can be frustrating at times.Other than that, it's a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: "Yes, Your Grace" is a pixel-art kingdom management game (similar to another game called "Sort the Court") where you, as king, receive petitioners who ask for gold, supplies, the expertise of your agents, or even your daughters in marriage. It was short but i enjoyed the Slavic folklore of the game and the very human characters reacting to hard times.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Left-Click SimulatorDialogue options pretend to be a choice, while it makes absolutely no difference on the outcome. The other side will do whatever the one single thing that is in the code. There are some "economic" choices (and I'm being generous here calling it economic) but there is not much of versatility plus they become repetitive. There is never a feeling of negotiation or actual agency over your character.Main story line is railroaded. I read that there are different endings, but at least for the first dozen of weeks of gameplay the outcome is always the same no matter what "choice" you took. Prime example for a i'm-totally-not-a-choice-choice-selection-design. The story and the dialogue themselves are rather dull/cliché.In short. You just sit there and click through a rather dull railroaded dialogue to reduce the lifespan of your mouse. The only achievement I felt was that I didn't do something productive or fun… oh wait… that is not an achievement.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: I was actually very excited to play this game. I liked the play style overall, but there is a very dark story event that happens near the final battle that cannot be controlled, and the story really never redeems itself. I was thoroughly disappointed by the lack of real choices when it came to the main story, particularly Losulia's storyline. I get that her marriage is the main driver of the story, but I wish there would have been a plot twist of some sort to make up for the dark event and the monotony of the final battle. Glad I bought this on a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Summary: I want to recommend this game, but at the end of the day, I don't think I can.  I think it's current price is a bit steep for what it is.  Overall, I think this has a good foundation, some characters are well written, and the soundtrack is good.  However, it seems to lack replayability and doesn't seem like a finished product.Pros: This is one the few games I felt the need to keep playing.  I played the game, beginning to end, in about four hours.  The soundtrack is solid and used very appropriately.  The royal family is fairly well flushed out as characters.Cons: After four hours I've completed the game, and it mostly felt like decisions don't really matter.  It feels like you're forced into very specific path.  Regarding the game itself, the UI can be a bit confusing.  For example, the game doesn't tell you who you have available to send out to towns on the screen in which you send them out to towns.  Furthermore, in the story, there seemed to be references to characters who previously died in the game (by characters who were well aware of their deaths).  I do not view this game as particularly replayable.  At 1/3 of the price for a new AAA game, I'd expect it to either be more replayable or last longer.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Finished after 7 hours, so it is not long game. Anyway I really enjoyed the decision making, seeing that most of them have an impact (more or less) on the game. You have to deal with everyday problems of your kingdom, at the same time take care of your family, manage your army and deal with other lords. _childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: The story is engaging and the characters are captivating (especially the family).I think it's worth the time and money for the amount of entertainment.There were some aspects I didn't like, for example too much guessing and it's hard to track who you talked to and use that information to make more intentional decisions. _childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game with a great story! It's not a challenging skill-based game, but instead an immersive experience on touch decision making and fulfilling kingly duties while balancing those with having to manage  royal family. It is a fun game with many fun references throughout and great music to top it off.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun game, I felt like all my choices mattered in the end. The storyline is good. Only gripe I have is that I am not sure the replayability will be amazing (and I have now completed the game, after 8 hours)Still, I'd say it was totally worth the money to me, thouroughly enjoyed the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: The story of the prince and pauper is a pretty popular one. You know, the one where the young prince wants to swap places with a poor kid who looks just like him so they both get to experience what is it like to live that opposing kind of life. The extremely wealthy and extremely poor type of life. I have always wondered why the prince risks doing it, what could be interesting or intriguing about being dirt poor, or even a better question: what's there to not like about being a literal prince, who's known, feared, obeyed, and respected across the lands?Well, after playing Yes, Your Grace I realized that the burden of rulership, managing a kingdom even when it's a small one, listening to your subjects' complaints and problems, and being the one responsible for finding solutions to one and all aforementioned problems, all the while trying to ensure peace and prosperity and fending off invaders and those that wish ill upon your land is such an incredibly heavy, weary and tiring burden that perhaps the life of a peasant can be very much desired. Much simpler life, where your life isn't worth much, and the lives of others aren't dependant on you and your politics and on how low a knee can you bend in front of every other king whose kingdom, and crown, are bigger than yours.A very creative, and very unique game. Quite moving at times. Well done, and super engaging. I'm not one usually for management types of games but this one was exceptionally special.Was this game about resource management? Or was it about managing family relationships and other kingdoms? I think it was about something more integral, it was about self-management and a test of character... on whose result everything else depends.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: The good :+ Great story+ Decent characters with good development+ Great, but not memorable soundtrack+ While the gameplay mechanism is partially broken, it's still entertainingThe bad :- Choices matter, but only on few choices and mostly on 2nd half of the storyThe ugly :* Partially broken gameplay mechanism, which allows me to reach best ending while being pacifist (most of the times) with bad resource management* Short duration (5 - 7 hours)Yes, Your Grace would be amazing if they expand the world, extend the story and serve major choices with multiple endings. Even so, Yes, Your Grace is still good game and it was fun while it lasted.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece in disguise imo.However the plot needs some leeway to let the player make more personalized and impactful PERSONALIZED decisions.+Needs more items to be found ingame, purchaseable from merchants or otherwise minigames to keep the player interested.a small skill system would do this game good, either with the player or his children to have specific skills that they may gain, Social manipulation, taming, fencing, bowmanship, lockpicking, Thievery etc!The game needs a DLC that allows for your personalized changes to the story, such as choosing not to let your first doughter be sold off for a promise that seems to have no impact what so ever, because the game was never about geting things handed to you, its building everything on your own,  even the player's Ego comes into play and who they are as a person will indicate the result which is what makes this game so amazing.BUT like i said, game needs a DLC , like a Free For All option where you start the game and you may have X amount of Children, X amount of sons or daughters, and have X amount of enemy kings or evildoers in MANY Scenarios try their hands at de-throning you.  Similarly to how "This War of mine" is built, with many many different character combos and stories and possible endings, and many different points of interest.There also needs to be a Random factor where as you may gain a General, Witch or Hunter at any random ingame intervals.Or some other form of DLC related characters in the game, and have the option of having more than one of each but a total not exceeding the maximum so you may personalize your own kingdom!""maybe If we could play as one of the other kings perhaps in a sequel for instance?""Fundimentally i have to say, the only thing that put me off was the fact that the game held your hand wayy to long in the beginning, to get the story going past the point where u have to give away your eldest daughter.Already i had a problem with having no option to weigh my choises. Having different plot or story path's is and has been proven to work Wonderfully!  just look at "The Witcher 1&2" Masterpieces that concieved the best game of 2015 , one of the best gaves ive ever played, HOWEVER having said that, the alternate endings and player choise HEAVILY weighed on me after playing The Witcher 3. i SO Wished they had gone the same path with #3 as they did with 1&2 even if it had taken them an extra 10 years to finish the game, it would have been the best game ever made.anyway..All this and more would make this DIAMOND in the rough into a MASTERPIECE that would be fit for Best game of the year.I will definetly be playing  Yes your grace #2 if they decide to make another one and am heavily interested in seeing whatever this company releases with a keen and interested eye.Thank you so much for this experience, i will be re-visiting this probably within the week.Reccomend this , it was a good 10 hour long experience, i was hooked and played it from start to fininish with maybe one bathroom break.

_childDocuments_.review: This is A LOT better than other indy-ressource-management-games are.The pixel art is pretty good, the sound is as well (unless you dislike pseudo babbling chars). The management aspect works reasonably well (most outcomes do make sense, some are semi-funny and only a few are weird or random) and there are quite a few things to do that go beyond the usual binary decisions.Where this game shines is that it gets better over time. Intially, the characters seem to be on the typical indy/video game level - card boards cutouts at best. (This is normal, mind you, hardly any game offers actual chars.) Over time the main chars do interact with each other in sensible ways though and the story develops like a real, non-game story would - without the usual problems that gameplay brings by breaking the flow/immersion/in-game logic in-between quest/tasks.

Now you have the decision to quickly reload it or just keep failing due to this decision.Some of the quest items are not well described. So you will struggle to understand, what exactly do you have to do.Family Dialogues are kind of weird - there is no logic behind the words of your daughters/wife.Allies requests sometimes also makes no sense - most of the time it feels like they are not well thought and you're just dealing with a child without proper motives.It has great soundtrack, but unfortunately you won't hear it much.

_childDocuments_.review: The problem I have with this game is that the hook to buy it is how much your decisions will affect the plot, when in actuality it's a painfully linear experience. For a single play through, it can be a fun experience. The pixel style is entertaining and I did enjoy a good bit of the writing. But it isn't worth it to play through it a second or third time to pick up the achievements you missed the first time. Most of those are hidden behind the back half of the game, and it just isn't a strong enough title to make it worth that much time to see what the new dialogue would look like.

_childDocuments_.review: This game definitely deserve a positive review. It was an intense experience.So first of all beware, it's not entirely just "king simulator". The whole plot is predetermined and it develops over exactly one year, week by week. Even if the game throws at you *LOTS* of decisions to take you won't be able to influence the main story, but just how the characters will revolve around it, and directly or undirectly, who is going to make it to the end and how "happy" will be (including yourself). There's no RNG involved, the events will occour in the same order in each gameplay, so you can replay it until you get an ending which is satisfing enough for you.The story is good, really good, it's moving, touching, sometimes funny, kind of bittersweet in general, never boring. Sit down (on your throne) and enjoy it.Beware #2, even if never explicit, the story contains some mature content: reference to domestic violence, animal cruelty, psychologic terrorism, extreme religious fanatism, and so on. Again, nothing of those things is displayed "onscreen", I'm just warning you because you WILL face those things so be prepared, it's gonna hurt.In conclusion, buy "Yes, Your Grace" if you think you would enjoy a intruguing medieval story in Game of Thrones style, spiced up by some resource management. If the price is too much, look around for a key from a reseller. If you manage to find it for less that 1€ like I did, just *BUY IT, IT IS WORTH IT*, no further questions.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: An enjoyable story-heavy management game. I could see this being frustrating and unfun if you struggled with the resource management, but I didn't have a very hard time with that aspect on my initial playthrough. If you can strike a balance between morality and pragmatism, things will probably work out for you. I enjoyed that the other members of your family were interesting characters in their own right, and they added a lot of interest to the story for me (especially the youngest daughter! she's great).Also the soundtrack is excellent. Definitely worth a listen.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: This is a review from somebody who got 100% achievements in the game.Supper fun and refreshing game! You take a role of a king. Min maxing your food and gold spending, building your army and sending your agents for quests is a lot of fun. Rule like a fool and your kingdom will stay in ruins. Rule like a king and it doesn't matter what comes your way, you life will be great.Will you get scammed by a travelling merchant, ha ha ha? How do you deal with other lords? Will you marry your daughter off to protect your lands or will you stand alone and fight to the death? Will you save your subjects or let them die? A lot of cool choices.The game offers an intriguing story. I will not spoil it. It's great!The family dynamics are complex and feels real. You act as a king and as a father. Can you keep your family together or will you marry it off to nasty people? Are you a cold hearted person or are you a love caring person? I was legitimately sad making some of the family decisions.The game is fun and interesting to play, I 100% recommend. Well, what's the downside than? Sadly, it's very short.P.S. getting 100% in this game is not difficult, but it will require multiple runs. It might get a bit boring, because you will have to play in a very strict style to get some of the achievements. All and all most of the are easy.

_childDocuments_.review: I am seeing a lot of people state that there is no replayability and the game is very linear. It is short at 6 hours and change for a playthrough (For me) but well worth the price with how invested I became with the story and characters. _childDocuments_.review: Just finished my first playthrough, this is a new favourite of mine. TLDR: the pixel art is gorgeous, the dialogue is immersive and makes you care for the characters, and the plot is captivating. 9.5/10The dialogue made me feel like I was Eryk, and I genuinely cared about the people coming to me for aid and I cared DEEPLY about Aurelea and the girls. If you allow yourself to get immersed in this game, especially on the family side, there's some moments that will truly break your heart and stick with you.The plot is very well handled. Their are little moments inside the plot that I feel could have been ironed out that I can't mention for spoiler reasons, but in my opinion they're so minor that it doesn't ruin anything. Similarly with the gameplay, it's quite repetitive but the game always throws something at you to keep things interesting. There's only a few, small aspects of the gameplay that can get a little too repetitive, but they don't stay for long, minor stuff.I could easily give this game a 9/10, but I honestly think 9.5/10 is more fitting. So much of this game I spent worrying about "my" family. I commend the writers especially for their work with the dialogue and how the plot weaves seamlessly into it. The music is beautiful, the art is beautiful, I love this game. So much so that I wanna keep saying good things about it but I can't find the words to adequately match how I'm feeling.If you're looking for heart wrenching plots and characters that you'll care about then I HIGHLY recommend this game. It's not perfect, but perfection is boring. As I said before, the imperfections don't ruin the experience in anyway.Btw, I CAN NOT wait for Snowfall! The art looks like it's been dialled up to 11 and the fact that we are sticking with Eryk and Aurelea makes me SO happy! I was so worried it would be a sequel that's disconnected from the family in this game. I can't wait and I hope for the best with what Brave At Night have cooked up for the next game.
