_childDocuments_.review: Yes your grace is a cute, little, fun little plot sized game that combines elements of decision making, resource management and attempts to rule a kingdom without dying. Failure can occur through loss of money, food, or just not enough men to field an army! This is absolutely a single player game which is nice for those days where you just want some personal game time. The graphics may not be fancy, the voice lines unintelligible at least to me, and the gameplay slightly repetitive, I still loved playing it! Fair WARNING! You will have to play this game at LEAST TWICE to get all of the achievements. I reloaded dozens of times and found it extremely enjoyable to get the perfect result to a situation. Imagine my annoyance to learn that I, the player and king in the game, would be fooled by some people!I felt real emotions playing this game, I felt hatred towards some characters and love on the first completed playthrough, and disgust with myself on the second for the choices made in order to get the full achievements. This is not even counting the half dozen times I restarted! Just to wash away the bad taste it left me with I intend to play this for a third time for the best possible run.As ruler you will make unsavory choices for the good of the realm, and do it again to protect your small and precious family. Even if you run your funds to the bare minimum!the first 2 segments or arcs of the game were very well done and it was not until the last few weeks did I worry about my odds of success. Unfortunately, I felts as if the messenger bird feature was dropped by the wayside in the latter half of the game as it serves a much reduce role unlike in the first two arcs. The graphics were a comfort to me after seeing all the high graphic games released in 2022. Reminding me that a games does not have to look good to be good! I would give this game a 4 out of 5 rating or an 8.5 out of ten and would recommend this to others. Also if you know of any games similar to this please let me know in the comments. Until then, I have a perfect run to do. Puts on imaginary helmet and yells for Davern! For the family! for Survival. P.S. play this wrong or right I am pretty sure you can end up with the family dead or hating your guts!

_childDocuments_.review: Ultimately, the problem with this game is that it is a resource management and decision making game that doesn't provide you any ways to be proactive in generating resources, and in the end you're reliant upon a lot of guesswork and luck. Heading into the second act of the game, you're left with no way to invest in generating greater resources, while the demands on your resources increase greatly. There's no way to keep all of your agents active at any point in time without going bankrupt, while your petitioners may only be able to be helped by one of these agents. Pick the wrong one to have active that week and you'll suffer a morale drop that's unavoidable, and enough of these will result in your royal lynching.

_childDocuments_.review: Play the gameThis game is good, and as proof of that the 7 hours I have spent playing have been without breaks whatsoever. This game makes you feel like a king, and not in the fun kind of way. Managing family matters as well as the daily needs of your people is difficult and you'd be surprised how which choices will have more significance than at first thought. The  game mixes management with roleplaying aspects that work very well together given the setting. In this game you are the King of Davern, a relatively weak country compared to your neighbors. You'll start off with a crisis in your hands, invaders from a foreign land have come to claim your daughter's hand in marriage (which you promised their leader long ago when he was a mere bandit in order to save your life). To solve the problem you decide to forge an alliance through marriage with the powerful Kingdom of Atana. It all goes downhill from here. It feels like the best parts of Game of Thrones. The moment to moment gameplay  is all about listening to the request of your people and weighing their needs and the needs of the Kingdom (or in some cases, your own). Choices can be tough when you need to think about whether or not you should help a village in need when an army much too strong for your kingdom to defeat is due to arrive. Will you risk running low on resources and failing to buy a much needed boon that will help you in the battle? Then there is the matters of family, will you marry off your daughter to seek a quick way out of your problems or will you stand by her wishes through thick and thin? Sometimes family matters demand important resources that you might need in the battle.In terms of difficulty i'll say this, if you are willing to take risks, you can make everyone you care about happy. You cant satisfy the wishes of all your subject, but you can still help them in many way. In general i didn't feel that it was overly complex, you only really manage two resources and think about how to best use in the long and short term. The game will appeal more to those that enjoy crafting their own stories. The King is yours to control all decisions are made directly by you, you can be cowardly, you can be brave, you can be just, etc. Either way, I feel the characters are well written and in the short moments you get to meet them they are all quite endearing. The story gripped in such a way that at every crucial moment i feared that things wouldn't turn my way despite preparing in every possible way. I don't regret my purchase, and i would buy it again if given the chance

_childDocuments_.review: If you like choose your own adventure books you will like this story.The Pro's-You get to make a lot of choices -Supply & money management are keys to success -it does seem if you make bad choices you will likely not hold at the end. I did hold on my first play through so Thats speculation but it did seem like you could die a couple different ways if you were careless. -It's a decent story and seems to have enough options to please a reasonable morale compass. I personally just execute everyone so that works for me. Cons:-User interface isn't great and sometimes you will be unsure if there is something else you should do prior to ending your turn. -I think some people might find the basic critical thinking aspects a little difficult. Many games now have arrows that point you everywhere, the things to do in this game are not hard but you do have to have some basic logic to point and click in the right places.  ( i am listing this as a con because I don't have much faith in spoonfed gamers,  I did fine) -its a story driven game with choices so not a lot of replay value. If you mess up your first game I suppose thats where that would come in, to have a better or happier ending. I was fine with my choices so no replay for me. All in all if you enjoy choose your own adventure books I  do believe its worth a play through. Hope this helps.

He has no money, he has no army, and he has no supplies.  How the heck did he even manage to become king?  His subjects are brainless idiots who don't know how to chase rabbits from their lettuce patches.  They can't manage to clean up their own messes (in the streets) and have to be told by the king what do do.  Even their love lives are so messed up they have to ask the king for help.  But, they are good at one thing... they know how to give the king a piece of their minds when they are upset with him, and being the weakling that he is, Eryk, just lets them get away with it.This game was frustrating throughout the entire time I played. _childDocuments_.review: Short but sweet. Yes, Your Grace boasts gorgeous visuals and a stellar OST that accompany a very down-to-earth depiction of medieval feudalism.The story of Yes, Your Grace kept me hooked from the get-go and had some very satisfying moments when my planning and spending worked out correctly and allowed me to make all the good decisions I wanted to without negatively impacting on my finances and supplies.If you're looking for a short experience that keeps you engaged for it's six hour playtime (My total playtime, but it might vary from person to person) I would definitely recommend this. _childDocuments_.review: :Played on Game Pass:Choice focused adventure game where you manage your kingdom's gold, supplies, contentment, while trying to protect your family and make alliances with other lords and kings. Decent, often dark story. Looks great, has good music, some well done moments. It can be very trial and error focused, even having a series of events the same day that might require the same agent to deal with it, though the penalty usually isn't that harsh. How difficult the game is will depend on, as is the case with most games like this, how well you understand that playing logically isn't good and you need to play to exploit the games obvious system flaws. In the first war you are preparing for it wants you to gain 1,000 soldiers. The thing is, you can win your battle with less, 1,000 is just the amount needed as one of the checklist items for an achievement/trophy and is around what you should have. The more soldiers you have the more supplies you have to spend each week to upkeep the army so you don't lose some soldiers each week. You can get a lot more soldiers than 1,000 and you spend basically every supply you have or beyond to keep the army at full strength. If you obviously realize that you don't need that many troops and stop supply the army while still doing things to get more soldiers and build more alliances that will supply you with gold and supplies each week, you basically never have to worry about supplies for more than half the game. And if you know how the game is narratively set to work and that you will lose all those soldiers but keep whatever you have of your supplies, then you really don't have to worry about army upkeep.There is no way to speed up days or skip plot events if you need to or want to replay the game. The few more adventure genre like moments can want you to find difficult to notice things in the backgrounds, though these moments are few.An alright playthrough but no real plot deviations that should make you want to play it again, and knowing what will happen would remove any difficulty in your decisions. Everything is done quite well, except for the actual kingdom management that makes up the actual gameplay.Screenshots:

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, this game most likely wont be for everyone. It is about story and strategy rather than gameplay. As far as gameplay goes, it is nothing more than a point and click. As for story, there are many branching paths for each character, making the world feel real. Also, your choices . You can be a nice king, an evil king, or a king who just doesnt say no. Not every strat will work (if your kingdom runs out of supplies, instant game over). Overall, Yes, Your Grace is a magnificent story carried by its incredibly characters, and astonishing artwork
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: A remarkably good game about managing your kingdom while increasingly difficult choices are presented to you, and you can never really make the best choice each time. Though the game isn't quite as difficult as it may suggest (you can beat it pretty easily in a single playthrough without loading saves), the best part is honestly just following the story of this family and what's been happening to them. Not everyone will feel attached to the characters, but if you can let yourself feel for everyone, you'll be gripped by how things twist and turn all while you try to save them--even when you fear you can't.(On that note, it's a great game, but I wouldn't personally recommend it at $20. Grab it on sale!)
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Really wonderfully written and presented - lands somewhere between The Banner Saga, (a non metatextual) Reigns and a Telltale game. Very much a narrative game first and a game-game second, but the mechanical pressure is enough that you feel sufficiently engaged to guide you towards tough narrative decisions. Occaisionally a bit technically janky, both as some options aren't always clear or available (one of agents died towards the end of the game because the game wouldn't let me reascend a staircase to say I didn't want to send them out), and as the strategic management and point-and-click parts of the game rub up against each other, and I'm not a huge fan of the rocky soundtrack, but overall really excited to see what these guys do next!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for July 2022, this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before August 2nd, 2022, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Yes, Your Grace has petitioners who constantly greet you and ask for your favors, which means money and supplies and unless you give them, the entire kingdom loses happiness.  While this sounds like a decision-making game, it’s much more about resource management and trying to manage a kingdom while making your family and guests happy. The problem is I didn’t like the story here.  Yes, Your Grace had this unfortunate habit of allowing players to make choices and then telling the player backstory that would have been useful to know before.  Like when you execute a raider, you then find out that the raider was from a faction you promised a daughter to.  The story just didn’t excite me, and the art style worked in a few scenes, but also pixel art feels almost tired by this point.  Pick this up if you want more of a visual novel with some resource management.  I know people who swear by this game, but I didn’t find it that engaging and I’ll probably be giving it up.   I came into the month hopeful for this one and am leaving it a little disappointed.If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: I completed this game in two sittings, a 45-minute session and the rest of the game in the other (about 4 hours and a half). This game isn't perfect, has a few flaws and has some mechanics that definitely could have been fleshed out more in the end. But honestly? The amount of games that can hold my attention for me to want to actually finish it are dwindling every year and  is another I can add to my list.I'll be honest: my entire life I've clung to this power trip in my head that I'd love to be a king in all its medieval glory. Deciding over matters both trivial and grand, juggling relationships with neighbouring kings and lords for favours when I need them, fill my coffers and chests with all the gold and food you can eat? Sign me up yesterday.  let me live that fantasy for a few hours with a bunch of rewarding storytelling to boot.No, not every event unlocks a chain of grand consequences that shape the rest of the story. Yes, you're bottle-necked into certain events that HAVE to take place in order for the story to continue. But there's plenty of variety regarding the people you can side with, issues you can decide on, peasants you can deny because you're either suspecting them of bull******** you or you just don't like the colour of their shirt that day. Or your General is out shaking pots in random villages for gold to drop out and they can't help that particular villager's raiding bandit problem of the day. It all has SOME consequence; people come back to you reporting on how your choice benefited or negatively impacted their community. Or some guard will drag in some shmuck you handed half your gold to because he said he'd invest it for you but ended up boozing it all away. What you do feels like it matters.In between all this decision-making you get to be a father and husband to your royal family. This part particularly impressed me. I don't know what it is, but conferring with your wife who gives you valuable advice on how to approach certain issues your kingdom is facing just felt so... humane. You felt part of that marriage, you felt that Eryk and Aurelea trusted each other and she helped rule the kingdom as much as you did. You felt that support man. That support of someone who loves you and cares for you but also trusts you to make decisions they might not particularly agree with. Add to that your daughters with wildly different but engaging personalities and you've got a family life that might draw you in as much as it did me.This game genuinely tugged at my heart strings several times. It's got death, betrayal, plot twists, magic, war... and family. Highly recommended. Give it a chance, let it charm you. You'll find it hard not to check on your kingdom that one extra week.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun management game with some choices that are pretty difficult to make (at least for me, a person who struggles with making decisions on the daily), and which carry consequences down the line. The storyline is engaging and compelling and I was impacted more than I thought I would be from a certain...*spoiler* death. I enjoyed the hell out of this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game expecting little better than Fable 3's throne room sequence with slightly more complexity.I was not expecting to be taken on an emotional roller coaster by an endearing pixelated family.It's true what the other reviewers have said. It's short and there really aren't any branching paths—mostly there's only a few key decisions that decide the fate of several people. But the characters are compelling, the story is good, and the game feels challenging.I actually cried at times, for the horrible hardships and heartbreaking moments that this game puts these people through. For that, I recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: This game was amazing. you are king. your kingdom is in turmoil and disaster looms. You only have so many weeks to avert certain destruction and save the lives of your family and your people.  alot of politics, maneuvering... making big, nerve wracking choices... money and resource management constricting your options... all culminating in some very major anxiety and emotional rollercoastering. huge set piece moments that depend on your preparations up until then... the feelings that the game coaxes from you for your family... are intense. every character seems real and you grow to really care about them... or hate them.and all for like, 10 bucks? jeeze man. talk about value. i cried twice.huge recommend. i cant imagine somebody to not recommend this game to... except perhaps to people who have problems with low graphics games, but even then, the graphics are charming and lovingly crafted... buy it. you wont regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Just completed my first playthrough and can't help wondering what my in-game choices say about me as a person. Is this low-key a secret psychological diagnostic tool? Because I deffo prioritized some family members' lives over others, sometimes in ways that even surprised me. Striking game, really. You deserve to play through it. But be careful if you're playing with someone else, because you gonna learn a lot of surprising stuff real quick. Who your *real* friends are.

_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, so I've played through the game fully once now, restarted halfway through at least four times, and I've waited about half a day after finishing the game to make my review. If I had to sum up my opinion TLDR style, Great game, little replay value. As I said, I've replayed from the midpoint four times and there are some features this game could add that would make replaying the game less taxing. The dialogue scenes don't take that much time, but if you've already read through it twice you're just clicking as fast as you can and waiting until the characters finish talking/moving. If there was some feature that allowed the animations to speed up, perhaps a setting that could add into the game that allowed you to click through them fully, it would greatly enhance replay value.Besides that relatively minor gripe - this game is phenomenal. Heart wrenching with twist abound Yes, Your Grace left me genuinely upset to learn that I'd finished playing the game. Every decision you make leaves you uncertain if it was correct, and more often then not you're left staring in shock at the outcome. Ultimately, I believe the developers did a fantastic job, and I hope that either DLC or another game in this vein comes swiftly because I'd like to scratch the itch Yes, Your Grace did again soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Great indie game! Simple traditional dramatic story but very emotional storytelling, you can really feel every character.ca. 10 Hours playtime for one run. Only buy it as you would buy a film, the gameplay is very simple and only some choices matter. If you expect a dungeon crawler roleplaying game or else do not buy this game. In contrast to the last "drama" movies I watched I felt sadness, anger, hatred, and a form of catharsis. Merkfolk is a good band.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing my first playthrough, this game is really something else. It had me thinking what could I have done differently and whether the choices I made were for the best. There were a lot of moments when I was like WTF!? I recommend this game to anyone wanting to be put in a King's shoes and have to rule a kingdom and make hard choices for the benefit of all.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, Your Grace has a very well-executed story; which I personally prioritize over strategic accuracy. It also has stylized and fun graphics, along with fantastic music, making this game just nice to look at and listen to. However, this game poignantly exposes the fact that there are some events in life you just cannot foresee, stop, and/or change - so not the best game to escape from life in. But it just might make you heroic enough to face your very own monsters... who knows?I am also hoping with every fiber of my being for a sequel to this game! Or just some sort of more follow-up. I really want to see more of the family and their adventures; Cedani and her pets, Asalia and Maya . Heck, it could be a hack-and-slash top-down adventure or point-and-click game, and I'd love it - as long as I get me some more Davern family adventure!
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutley amazing!This game has strong story underlined by unusal combination of game mechanics. Funny moments are balanced by hard choices and tough story development, that provides unique connection.I dont like text games, but this on just kept me playing.It has few weaker spots, first half has awsome drive, but management in late stage starts to be a bit repetitive and not that connected to story, as in first half. Also history nerds, like me, will not agree with some details, but that all is just a bit dust on shining armour of this great piece.I will replay it after i forgot the main story a bit.I definitely recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: The game is enjoyable and has some great funny moments. It is difficult to play, but not impossible to get a "good" ending by weighing your choices. I recommend watching a playthrough beforehand, because some of the peasant requests are not what they seem and you miss out a lot if you don't know what they're about. Generally it pays to help out as many people as possible during the first half and become more cautious during the second.I was annoyed by some of the "tragic" twists, you can tell when something is added just for the shock effect but does not help the story, it doesn't even make it more entertaining.- Picking a wedding dress between three impossible options is amusing. - Trying to solve a crime by collecting evidence and questioning suspects is fun.  Basically it is like a movie in which you can not change certain tragedies. This element in the game leaves you with a feeling of frustration because there is no way around it no matter how well you play. However, the hilariousness of the scenarios and being involved in the character's lives makes up for a lot and the game is still recommendable. Even Cedani going through a bunch of animal "agents" is pictured innocently, she's got a plan and never gives up. You cannot be mad at her. Oh and I love the credits song :D
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know I finished the game pretty easy but for a choice matters game, it really felt like my choices didn't matter. Hard to say without the percentages but, the game's not bad just feels like I could just smooth brain through things and get by without much thought. Also really doesn't give me a lot of reason to go through another playthrough except for getting some achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: My only complaint is that you cannot make the most obvious choice in the first few days, which the developer has stated they felt there was no other way to drive the plot forward. Okay. I get it, but it still doesn't please me, and I'd never make the "forced choice," ever.Other than that, a very charming choose your own adventure game.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: The story of this game is the strongest point. You actually feel along with the characters and you care about them. Maybe some plot points are predictable, but this doesn't take away from the great execution. At some points the gameplay can be a bit stale, but it is a very good mean to tell this story. Definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game yesterday and loved it - the story, music and art style are all incredible. Yes, Your Grace left me with lots of emotions and eager for more.I was very conflicted whether to get this game when I saw some of the reviews, but I'm really glad I did. I feel like most of the criticism comes from people not understanding the genre or getting frustrated with bad endings. I would however agree that there is some room for improvement - the game would feel more complete if there were more options on how to respond to situations (even if the outcome was certain death)/more opportunities to influence the story. One thing I personally felt was lacking is the scripting for the 'final villain' - their story wasn't as realistic as the first arc of the game and felt too demonising. Satisfying for a minute or so, but ultimately I think it would have been more impactful to again create a morally grey situation there.To get the best experience for this game you should definitely go in prepared. The game will constantly challenge you and force you to make difficult decisions, so you should take it seriously from the beginning. I personally liked the pressure it put on me and enjoyed navigating the cruel mechanics, but this may not be for everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - Great writing that pulls you in and really gets you invested. Beautiful art. Awesome voice acting and soundtrack. Short (4 hour) play through, but with replayability to go different routes to unlock different endings. Gameplay consists of making choices that affect your kingdom whether it's how you choose to deal with the issues affecting your people, or what you decide is best when it comes to your family members.Great game with a story that really sucked me in. I just completed my first play through at the time of this review (4 hours). I'm not one to replay many games, but there is definitely potential here with different choices you could have made resulting in different endings. The writing was really good as well with a good variety of mini stories for some of the peasants. There was humor as well as deep moments. I really felt for the king and his family.The graphics and visuals of the game were great with very detailed pixel art and animation. The voice acting was awesome as well! I loved hearing all the different voices and each fit very well with the characters. In addition, the soundtrack was great and was able to evoke emotions during many scenes.I really enjoyed this game and would highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: I don't like this game. It's boring and it seems really obvious immediately that I'm not making actual choices. I'm not convinced)I didn't like: That other guy. I really didn't like him.

_childDocuments_.review: The good:- I like the pixel graphics.- Some of the characters are good.- Even though the story had it's stinky moments, in the end i'd say i enjoyed it. It reminded me of Game of Thrones.The bad:- Only mouse buttons are utilized. No fast forwarding or any kind of quality of life features like keyboard shortcuts.- One big immersion breaker was the ritual. I initially agreed to it and was supposed to gather some ingredients. Decided i wouldn't do it and when it was time, the game treated me as if i had gone and gathered the stuff. It told me to hand in the items and Eryk would be like "I'm ready, let's do this". Ritual proceeded but naturally it failed. Why couldn't i just back out? Just wash off the pentagram and proceed with the traditional way. The aftermath of the ritual was underwhelming. No emotion whatsoever from Eryk. One other minor thing i noticed is when one of the daughters cut her hair but afterwards was given to a lord. In the cutscene the daughter reverted to her old, long haired model.- I started losing interest after the first battle. It really didn't feel like my choices mattered that much. It was like the game was holding my hand through these minor events to something bigger that i could not even affect.- Speaking of the battles, i don't know if my preparations for them made any difference or the way i played them out. It felt like i was just auto piloting. It left me craving for strategic turn-based combat. I wanted battles where i had to use my head a little. Battles where i could have actually game over'd.- The archives were executed badly. Pages were too small which resulted in me having to scroll them a lot. Make the pages bigger. Also when viewing a character's backstory, only the name is displayed. Would have made things a lot more clear if there was a picture as well. The faceless people make it a bit harder to tell them apart.- The whole lords and invitations system was kind of stupid. You'd never know if there was any benefit to inviting someone over or if you'd just get a "That's all" dialogue option and then the guest would run off without doing anything.I like the idea behind the game. Too bad it was executed badly. There was not much of a game to experience here. It's basically a visual novel. An incomplete one. I'll give it a 3/10. For the sequel they should improve the gameplay and UI and make choices really matter and have a bigger impact on everything.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: The story's intriguing with meaningful choices. Characters are well defined and the game mechanics are straight forward to figure out yet it's always still difficult to make all of the difficult decisions required of a ruler.  I thought it was going to be a short game but the story is pretty deep, and keeps going, while maintaining interesting drama. It also made me tear up a few times.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Whether I would recommend this would really depend on what price you'd be paying.It is pretty fun but has a lot of downsides:- The graphics are way worse than you'll probably realise from the store page- It's only one days gameplay really- Also there's only one game save / no slots, so your girlfriend sharing your computer is SOL. Starting a new game wipes all saves.- Noone except agents can do anything. Your 300 soldiers can't possibly help with anything. so when three peasants in a day all want your general (so always) you end up with permanent peasant haters (I guess this is intentional to increase difficulty, but you can't even tell people to come back later)- Annoying slow transitions and need to walk to the edge of the screen to move locations feels like it's only there to make the game slower

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful mix of a kingdom simulator and an interactive novel. Yes, Your Grace puts you in charge of a kingdom, one week at a time. The story is very engaging, I couldn't stop playing to find out what was going to happen next week.The UI needs improvements, navigating the castle is a little quirky. The simulation aspects need rebalancing, because the gold and supplies values are very arbitrary from one petitioner to another.

_childDocuments_.review: i absolutely loved this game! im going to go back an play this again and get a different outcome...i just wish there was a litle more to it other then that it was a breath of fresh air to play this game every other game is all the same to me and this was different in my opinion! definitely my type of game!

_childDocuments_.review: Great game with a very interesting concept and execution. The game pretty much boils down to making tough choices, managing resources, and keeping allegiances. All of these factors will affect the story. Can't be very specific about how without spoilers, so the way I would describe it is that the story has a few main plot points that aren't really affected by your choices, however the many details around these plot points are. This is not to say that you don't get agency or that the choices feel inconsequential. On the contrary. Your choices will affect a wide range of things from slight silly details to heavier and permanent consequences.I appreciated the story. I have to admit that being a parent made the decisions that affected the royal family feel very personal, and in cases even relateable. The way the game uses music and sound to convey emotion was very effective too.All in all I really enjoyed this game and have played it through twice already. I'll probably reload some saves to get the rest of the achievements I didn't get from normally roleplaying as two types of kings.

_childDocuments_.review: As a very short description, is a combination of RPG and resource management, with a very capable story. While it offers relatively low* replay value and a playthrough is, again, short*, I totally recommend it.Pros:- exceptional writing (but the dramatism variance is a bit too high, maybe because of needed compression of events in given time)- fully immersive- very good soundtrack- novel (in my experience) approach to gaming concept; it takes the WItcher's concept of choice, but with more layers of impact- coherent universe, even if the details (in terms of lore, let's say), are not abundantCons:- the main one is if you judge it in terms of bang for the buck and you compare with some 50-200$ game which can offer thousands of hours (say, Skyrim or some strategy behemoth). BUT on the other hand is 20something for a very worthile experience. A meal at a cheap restaurant or so, for comparison. Even if this is at the "cons", totally worth it imo- another one is that towards the end is a bit dull and repetitive (won't make it here a spoiler), but the "omg I will not sleep until I see the end"-factor is totally thereAll in all, I would say the game is a showcase, if anything, and a very strong one. On this engine/concept, with enough resources, you could totally have, in time, an alternative which could challenge monuments like Gothic or TeS.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know what I expected going into this, but I feel like I got more than I bargained for.This is a choose-your-own-ending type rpg, with a side of resource management. How do you spend your very limited gold and supplies, so you can sufficiently help your people, while fending off war. And on a more micro scale, how do you be a good parent and spouse? Almost all your choices come with consequences. There is an overarching storyline that doesn't see as much change supposing you survive, but a good number of major characters CAN and WILL die because of your choices, so think through even things that might seem silly to allow at times. The only real critique I have with the gameplay is that there is a diplomatic system that is sort of abandoned in the second half of the game, and I wished that there was a little more going on with that.Without spoiling too much, I am happy that there is also queer representation in the storyline, which is nice to see in games. The plot is relatively well-written and manages to be endearing as well as emotional. You are given a decent amount of moral dilemmas and enemies to feel compassion for, and interactions with your family were actually really sweet at times. I was a little disappointed that , but it was funny that the . The art is pleasant, nothing fantastic, but decent for pixel art. The soundtrack absolutely slaps though and really sets the tone for many portions of the game.No major bugs were encountered in my playthrough, although there were a couple of issues with the names of certain peasant appeals being cut off/poorly labelled. It largely had no effect on my playthrough other than making the recruitment of certain villages for war a little more challenging. There is some replayability in trying to optimise/find out what happens with other choices, but you are largely limited by the downsides of having a mostly linear main plot.Still, not gonna lie, I would buy and play this game all over again if it had better graphics, I'm happy I finally decided to look through my steam library for random things I bought and never played, only to find this gem. Would gladly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: I have never reviewed a game on Steam before, but I had to with this one. Got it on sale, and was expecting it to be a fun little diversion, but oh my gosh, it sucked me right in, and I played it all day until I finished it. I have rarely been so sucked into a story like this one, even though it really was a fairly simple one, and it was filled with so many gut punches. Even though most of the little decisions don't have too terribly large of an impact on the greater story, you still need to do everything very wisely and carefully to ensure that you'll be able to do the important things, and to ensure you keep the support of your people. I really can't recommend this enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: In what world a king would get major lip from an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ little kid who openly threatens him, and would still let him get away with marrying his daughter?That's the kind of unbelievably premise "Yes, Your Grace" has, forcing you to go through the obviously bad choices for dramatic impact, only for it to... not really matter? Imagine playing Fallout: New Vegas, but with most of the plot important decision decided automatically, and the only actual effect of them having is on the post-game cutscenes. Packs less of an impact, right?Add the abundance of optional quests that don't lead to any tough choices due to them literally having very little, and the fact that by the end of the game you're going to end up with plenty of resources, which, again, don't help you in the slightest.I played many Telltale games before, they may be predictable, linear, and simple, but at the very least they don't force me to micromanage for no reason at all.

_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: "Yes, Your Grace" can be summarized as a narrative point-and-click game with some heavy management elements. While the narrative part really impressed me, I have some issues with the management aspect. To put it simply: "Yes, Your Grace is a game of tough choices" is the first thing the game tells your, and it's basically a lie (in absence of further explanation, which the game doesn't provide). All you have to do in order to have a constantly high resource income is to help everyone you can early on, so that you raise your people's morale and, consequently, the taxes they have to pay. Let me take a step back and explain this in more detail.For the first half of the game, everything goes pretty smoothly, mainly because you have a lot of things to take care of. Not only you have to decide whether to help your petitioners by evaluating their requests, but it's also absolutely imperative to make alliances with other lords, weighing the resources their provide and their morality to carefully choose who to stand with. The second half of the game is where you'll feel the ripercussions of early mistakes, since everything is much more straightforward and all you need to do is gather enough resources and have a big enough army to prepare for what's to come. This is where everything will crash into pieces if you didn't understand well enough how to increase your resource income early on and you'll be actually forced to make tough choices as you won't have nearly enough resources to accomodate for everyone's needs.What really bothers me, though, is that it's absolutely clear that you should not end up in this state, and the game's way to tell you this is having your petitioners ask your for something like 25 pieces of gold to repair a damn cart when your  only has about 10 in it (with a 31 weekly cost just to hire agents and an income of roughly 20 gold pieces).I'm not complaining about the game's difficulty, it's just clear that the game doesn't explain well enough how you should handle your economy from the start; rather, it tells you that you'll have to make tough choices (which leads you to believe you should not help everyone and keep a farely safe amount of resources in your deposit) when your only objective should be to have the highest possible taxes and the most income sources.Another thing that's really inconsistent is the amount of morale you gain or lose from some interactions with your petitioners. More often then not you'll find yourself losing 4 points for not paying your weight in gold just to handle some minor problems and gain just 2 for saving a whole village. It wouldn't be a problem if the game told you how much morale you would gain or lose with any interaction, but I also understand that this clearly isn't what the developers had in mind. Problem is: the system's really inconsistent and it's something I hope will be improved in the sequel.That said, I guess you're wondering why the heck I'm actually giving this a positive review.Well, that's because the narrative is really good and really makes you care about the characters, and the first half of the game is very tense and gripping, which is ultimately what keeps the whole game tightly together.Managing your kingdom is not bad per se, but it can be really frustrating if you find yourself with a nearly empty deposit during the second half, since you won't have any choice but to deny any help to most (or any, if you can't even hire agents) of your petitioners with little to no way of actually getting things back together. Despite that, I have to say that I finished the game on a high note and managed to get a really good ending, so you can actually make it through the second half of the story by playing it smart and making every penny count (as I already told you, what really bothers me is the absurd amount of resources petitioners ask for, which ultimately feels like the game is making fun of you, when you're in that situation). If you asked me what I thought of the game before I got halfway through the second part, I would've told you that I was having so much fun, that I was really into the story and that I'd discovered a little gem.Now, I'd tell you that "Yes, Your Grace" is a good game with a very gripping story and a really good blend of different genres and mechanics, however some of them are quite inconsistent and unpredictable, which could lead to some frustration if you don't make certain decisions early on. Thanks to the track pad and the touch screen, it plays really well on the Steam deck.Now that we are done with the analitical bull****, let me say that I'm really looking forward to playing the sequel because this game really got to me in more than a way.I just wanted to take a more analitical and in depth look at it for this review.

_childDocuments_.review: Good idea on paper, but the hazardous consequences of yours choices make it hard to believe that you have choices at all. The story, arts and musics are good, but the gameplay is weak and not rewarding. There is no feeling of accomplishment and I don't know if the gruesomes events happened because of my choices or it is just story telling. I won't play it again even if I wonder what are the differents outcomes, because there is just not enough gameplay to have fun. It's a story. A good story, but just a story.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the best "click adventure" game as I call them, that I've played in an extremely long time. All of your choices actually change things  as you go, and make some things harder or easier based on what you choose.  And the story is good. I wound up just playing through it in one sitting (5.5 hours lmao, it's been a boring day what can I say :P ) And I still feel like I've just finished a really long game. That wierd feeling of sad that its over. But I was content with how it ended for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: It's a visual novel with light point-n-click components. Not much replay value. Can get quite slow. The story was interesting, but the point'n'click elements were few and far between, making it sometimes hard to figure out when you need to go for it and when there's nothing to do. All the gameplay mechanics could have been fleshed out a bit more and been a lot more satisfying. Some mechanics are very unclear - population happiness, for example. What does it do.It takes four hours to click through everything, but there's only half a dozen points where your decisions make a difference. It's alright, not great, but not worth the price, I think.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just a choice based story, where the choices you make affect the ending, not much "kingdom management" or combat or politics. Might or might not be your taste.The price is too steep as the gameplay is too short for me.Completed the game in only around 5 hours, sure you can replay, but im not the type to do that.Only get it on sale, not worth the full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: At £15, and with 13 hours playtime to complete the game from start to finish, I have to say the £1 per hour is worth the experience! A game with great storytelling, compelling characters and that "just one more turn" feeling when you decide to pass over to the next week. The game centres around King Eryk, who you control in deciding matters of the realm. From peasants wanting help with flooding to monsters in the woods, you have to balance their requests for help or payment, with trying to rally local lords and neighbouring kings (and their various want!) to gather the support of their armies. It's not all politics though, and Eryk has to spend time caring for his family (and the cutest damn kid in gaming) as they come to terms with the changing world around them, and how they'll approach their future as princesses.There's a lot of replayability with the various choices and outcomes for the game, with each individual choice having a real impact upon the later stages of the game. There's also plenty of achievements to get, even ones for performing poorly!A stunning story, that deserves a 10/10. I only wish there was more!
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a solid okay especially if it's on sale. I was quite impressed with the sheer amount of written dialogue/quest lines, as all of them appear to be unique and not randomly generated. That being said the game is quite short, with a very unclear view of which choices of yours will ever end up mattering or why they do. The game also has quite beautiful character artwork you can see in banners/credits and it's a shame none of it was utilised in the actual game.There could definitely be minor improvements made as well, for example being able to access the castle map rather than walking to the edge of the screen (and then realising some edges won't take you to the map). Or even the idea of paying resources in advance, which means you have to guess which people will be useful to you for the next segment.Overall, it's okay, I don't regret playing it, and worth picking up on a sale if it seems your style
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: I really do enjoy this game and I'll give it a recommendation any day of the week, but there are some steep negatives. Even though I LOVE Not Tonight.1. Price Point is a bit rough for a 5 hour game, but those 5 hours will be very engaging. I rarely feel a connection to the characters, but throughout I remembered names, locations, and feelings about things. It did feel important.2. The soundtrack really ties the game together, it really is fantastic. But it doesn't have the casualness of Not Tonight.3. I was hoping for at least one callback to swordfighting at the end, I guess I was hoping for a lot, but I still enjoyed it thoroughly.If you want to support an amazing dev with some FANTASTIC Pixel art and an AMAZING soundtrack, buy this game. If you're short on cash, wait for a sale. You won't be disappointed with your purchase. But 20$ can feel steep for some people.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Hello everybody, although I own and play numerous games the last 35 years of my gaming life, it is actually the first time I am compelled to write a review of one.So........ what is actually the reason especially having just  10 hours of playtime?Well..... Being the father of two girls I could not but sympathize with the difficult choices of the main character, the King, during the weeks of his reign.On that regard the game has captivated me. The filling of hopeless choices on the hand and the reward of a daughter's love on the other is what made me love the game.The excessive spending and the need to please the women of your family so as to minimise nagging could not be depicted more realisticly in a game.The plot is so artfully planned to ease you into the role of the King and his problems.What can I say more, buy the game and enjoy the experience.Highly recommended to married man with daughters. Lolololololol
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, definitely a fun RPG story with some replayability in a linear story line with a few different outcomes. My only dislike is the need to rebalance the resource system. You should not have to send agents away for 3 weeks and not get some sort of happiness bonus for it, but suffer -5 happiness to your villagers because you couldn't afford to give someone 23 gold for a damn cow, when you could put the same money towards an entire army. The retainer fees for your agents make it nearly impossible to utilize them without going broke in the end game either. I get having to pick and choose, but it at the end of the day, there should still be a more balanced approach to value of actions.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Not many stories can make me outright furious, but this one managed to accomplish just that. The writing is great, and it had me hooked all the way through. That said, the game REALLY, REALLY should've given me the option to "burn at the stake" instead of "behead." I wanted the poetic justice...Also, the ending is kind of underwhelming, and there's literally 0% replay value if you beat the game the first time through. Feels bad.Worth it, though. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Family man king/sir faints a lot goes on a journey of choices where every major event is on rails and will not change in its outcome. While the main story can be engaging, on repeat playthroughs you will find no choices really matter all that much and some of things you can change are fairly late game 50/50 choices. One positive I will say is the week to week gameplay loop never disappoints you or overwhelms you. Every event/deadline is known for the most part and allows you run your kingdom and resources as you see fit. Looking forward to the sequel if the gameplay story choices have more meaning.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: A good mix of interesting decisions, storytelling and humour! The interface is simple and easy to learn. Great pixel art, music, and the gobbledegook voice-overs grew on me. At times, a little stressful to play, but I think that's just a sign it drew me into the well-imagined world. It's a little disappointing you can't alter some events, but I completely understand that would increase the amount of content required tenfold.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: It's always impressive when a game with this sort of art style proves to be so capable of breathing life into it's cast of characters, so much to the point that you really feel for them. I started playing with a chess mindset, a cold and analytical approach where i tried to make logical decisions set apart from my feelings.  The game quickly wrung that out of me as I was roped into genuinely caring for not only King Eryk's family, but also the subjects of the realm and the soldiers under his command. I did manage to win in the end, but at what cost? The choices i had made weighed heavy on me, the sacrifices King Eryk, I had made felt hollow in the end. I didn't get a happy ending, but i deserved the ending that i got and because of that I have to appreciate Brave At Night's storytelling.If you're on the fence about this game, please take the advice of a stranger and buy it. It's only twenty dollars and is well worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: A game that looked like Not Tonight at first so I was assuming that it's the same concept. _childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game with rich story interesting twists hard choices and best climate. Do not consider this game if you wish to play kingdome management game cause it's not about it. _childDocuments_.review: I put off playing this game way too long, and with the sequel announced it finally pushed me to start! Honestly I really liked the art and mechanics of the game. Pixel art will always be a big draw to me, never get tired of it. The resource managing is pretty difficult, especially with the agents, kinda too miserable sometimes but I get it. The story and writing is where it kinda lost me and I'll go into detail and some spoilers below so here we go:#1 I understand Lorsulia being given away for marriage and are supposed to be emotional driving points, but I felt none of those emotions or connections at all. She is gone 15 minutes into the game, never to be seen again besides a 2 minute scene where she is gone again. Her character "arc" with Ivo was nothing but miserable and weak. And I mean with Dusty...really? Just stupid#2 Asalia is genuinely horribly written, and once again I felt nothing in terms of emotional or story connection. She is written only to be an awful, mean brat and she, to my surprise, stayed that way the whole game. I thought her little character arc with Maya could have been cute, but she just became more bratty and awful. Really? She's 12 or 13 and runs away with nothing, not caring about her family/new baby brother when she knows full well another war is about to happen with them? I was glad to be rid of her#3  Eryk. Oh King Eryk....I really enjoy who we play as, I do. But the way this poor man is written/ the choices you have to make just seem like someone making a tumblr OC just to do torture p*rn. I'm glad we can make him....not so miserable?#4 Ah, finally the good stuff. I LOVED the Queen and Cedani so much. Now here are characters I actually cared about, your wife loves you and only wants the best for you/the family. And Cedani is just a silly kid, with all her agents I wish I could have saved. Great characters, along with Audry and General Stan who I wish had more dialogue. I know it seems like I ragged on the writing and story mostly, but I did truly enjoy the game. I'm hoping that the sequel brings out MUCH more depth with certain characters, along with maybe being able to actually see the kingdom of Davern as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the best story-driven games I have played. Made me feel really immersed and also managed to make me care about each and every character! Feel like it also has replay value, I for sure will give it a second and probably a third go soon!Dont have any negative things to say about this one, so here is a list of things that were exceptionally good:-Soundtrack: Really, really good, felt right in every situation.-Graphic style: I love the atttetion to detail that has gone into every location it seems, even if it is only seen for a short while (trying not to spoiler anyone here)-Decision making: The game just gave me a great overall feel, seeing how my decision from the beginning still had an impact for the rest of the game. Also makes it great for replay!-Achievements: Funny and good achievements, also adds alot of replayvalue (Gotta catch them all!) Long story short: Amazing game, definitely worth it's price, waiting for a second addition already!

_childDocuments_.review: ABSOLUTUTLY  worth it's 12 € in the Halloween sale! _childDocuments_.review: Very nice game. I'm looking forward to its sequel.Replayability is somewhat limited, after two successful playthroughs with opposite playstyles, you may have seen it all. _childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: It was a short but very memorable experience. This game will make you feel like you care about the characters (especially your family) and surprisingly a lot of the npc's you meet during the story, some which you only meet a couple of times. It also puts you in really difficult situations that you don't expect. Like do you risk not helping some of them for the short-term benefit for the long-term negative? Do you prioritize keep upgrades and lord alliances over your people?Overall, a great but short experience. But I this price I think its really worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Well first of I have to say that they've really done a good job with the story line. The soundtrack is amazing and the cutscenes are well written. I truely felt with Eryk during my playthrough. I don't think I will do another playthrough since I botched my first one with the battle. So basically I played twice, but there is not enough replayability, its a set path with a few different choices, although they do have significant changes to the story as a whole but only for his family and close ones.I got it on sale for 13 euro's. In my opinion that is a price worth paying, for the amount of content you do get, I don't think 20 euro's is justified without a sale.Definitly a fun experience for 7 hours. If you do it slow in one try, I'd reckon you'd prolly get 5 hours worth of it, about 4 euro's per hour on the regular price. I'll let you decide if you find that worth for your moneyAll in all, I had a fun time, with felt sorrows and joy, even a little wrath against a character, but you'll discover that yourself.Oh and the way they talk, yea that took some time to get used to, but after 30 minutes it stopped bugging me, it grew on me a bit.I hope I've persuaded some of you to give it a go
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Magnificent.This is one of the few games where you will find yourself truly gnawing at your mind over every single decision you make, and if you play your cards right, only regretting half of them.If you're looking for a tough choices matter style of game, with a well written story with lovable and great characters, in a well designed Game with an awesome soundtrack and artwork, THEN THIS GAME IS FOR YOU, YOUR GRACE
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game, a little bit short but still was very fun to play. The story was very good with many hard decisions, idk if its true but it made me feel like there are many possible outcomes and endings from even small decisions. The music was very annoying to me so i just turned it off. I would give strong 7/10 but i recommend buying it only on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: I found this a frustrating title, but it is still worth a play-through and the price (if you can get it on sale)It did a solid job of building affection between the main cast- but was a bit shallow in regards to the peasant petitioners.The art is really charming and the ui is pretty intuitive.Core game-play loop is relatively fun, but a lack of being able to deeply steer the narrative is frustrating,  The game forces you into a lot of main-plot choices and often does not provide an option for choices you might rather like to to take ((The choices relating to the Marrying off the eldest daughter and how to deal with her abusive husband were hair-pullingly bad.) It also hard resets the story a few times in an effort to restrict pathing and limit the consequences of the choices you do make. Ultimately, many choices do not matter at all and you are just going through the motions to progress the story. Pathing branches a bit more heavily right at the end of the game- but by then it is a little too late and the game felt like it was on a single track with different exit points at the very end. The exception would be who exactly you ended up recruiting to help your cause. Also, the game is a bit too easy.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, Your Grace was a game I thought was heavy on the management and choices. It is for sure but also has a lot of personal story mixed in. Frankly that's not my kind of game when I'm looking for resource management. So if I sound kind of harsh it's because this really just isn't my genre.The choices DO matter and effect the game later on and the management aspect is really easily broken but usually not on a first play through. There is a lot of dead space in this game. I have to walk to the edge of the screen to leave, but not that edge of the screen. I need to walk up stairs and see the animation pan up every single time. I have evidence I need to review but it's literally the same page for each one, spamming Invites until I randomly find someone who knows something or waste my time until I learn the perfect pattern for inviting with pretty much no RNG. The story elements with my character and his family are static on each play through so I'm spamming dialogue to get to the actual choice part because I know it's the same. The point and click matters very very little. It has some relevant plot points but I can count them out on my hands. Truthfully although the pixel art is very pretty and the animations for it are done very well I don't think it matches with the gameplay it wants. The game feels like it's a '2D drawing environment with text overlay' kind of game, with some point and click to justify the pixel art.This game felt a little weird at times. It doesn't feel like I'm a king pretty often. It feels like I'm a quirky guy juggling a wacky family.I bought this on a steep sale and do not regret it. But even for people who enjoy a more story-based, linear ending, love pixel art, and love dipping into several genres, I would recommend around $15 at best.Generic tricks and tips for the interested:-People advocate for themselves when petitioning, keep ti in mind-Allying with Etton easily breaks the games economy. Like, shockingly easily to the point I thought it was bugged. Not that the game is exactly that hard-I would fix everything except the theater for the first few turns as the peoples happiness/contentment really isn't an issue even if you play more neutrally-Pietro needs more than just words to help him
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game. It really sets the mood of how stressful and horrific things were going on for the protagonist. Getting to the end to decide the fate of that little creep who is the antagonist was very satisfying. I will say the little girl and her pets was awesome. I was cracking up over her yelling and the screen shaking in accord...lol
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: It feels more like the game gives you the illusion of choice were almost none of them really matters. Sure there are maybe 2 or 3 choices at the end that has an effect but most is pointless and I also never cared for any of the characters since you have no effect on anything - you are mostly a bystander believing you are in charge.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: This is going to have spoilers. So the game is well made, everything works, it's pretty, I like the characters. But you don't really have any choices and honestly it's annoying. It's so blatantly obvious that Ivo killed his dad, zero option to call him out on it. It's super obvious that Ivo's going to betray you during the battle, zero option to call him out on it. Your daughter warns you three times that Ivo's a piece of ♥♥♥♥. You see that Ivo's a piece of ♥♥♥♥ yourself. Zero option but to trust this guy, cause that's what the story needs. It's infuriating. I liked the game all the way up until this point. I honestly wish that the game was pitched more as an interactive story than a choices matter one.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: I love the art, music, and game play mechanics. The art is especially gorgeous and I was thinking about buying the soundtrack for the game. Despite all of that the story line of the game turned me off to it in just over 30 minutes. The story didn't make much sense to me. Why not just give your daughter to the barbarian king? You can give her to the other king to marry his son if you want, why can't I do that for barbarian king dude? Why was it that when I engaged with the side stories with the kids, I made things worse for myself when talking with friendly king dude who's wife it dying? I don't know any of these peoples names, none of them are interesting to me. I'm pretty sure the developers are using a visual novel style story mechanic, past events trigger future ones and everything that happens is set in stone, i.e. there is no randomness at all. If that's true it means the game can be "solved" with a guide of some kind. If the story was good or if the characters weren't boring then that wouldn't be a problem. I can't help but feel sad for what this game could have been. The art, the music, and game play all feel wasted here. Having a roguelite (or roguelike, I forget the difference) story system and a semirandom, semicustomizable start would have greatly improved the story and made the game into something special. Maybe there's more randomness beyond the first 30 minutes, but by the time I hit that point I just didn't care to continue playing. I alt-f4'd and refunded the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, your grace is a linear story with some coices and consequences.The world, characters, dialogues and story is well written but also kind of short, it takes about 6 to 8 hours for one playthrough. I was able to beat/solve the game on my first attemp, which was suprising for me and kind of disappointing.Based on your decisions the game has supposedly different Endings, though I wouldn't expect too much. ( You'll get pictures/slides with short sentenced explanations how some of your decisions affected the future )However I only heared recently about the game without any deeper, or background information. I was expecting it to have random events or at least outcomes, turns out its all fixed and therefore easy to learn and adept if something goes south. Overall based on my experience with the game and taking the price into consideration I would recommend the game. Its really well crafted and I only experienced one bug that just was just a inconsistance to the story. (SPOILER: The cat appeard on the Wall during a cutscene/event at the wall with some enemys beeing captured, at this point in the story the Cat shouldn't be there)So overall I am just disappointed at the difficulty and linearity, and also the content in the second half of the game, which was rather thin.I would really appreciate it if the devs would expand upon the existing game, be it with different gamemodes ( random events/outcomes ) higher difficulty, more stuff to do or even some kind of priced DLC with more content overall.Bonuspoints: If you are able to understand polish language you'll be suprised by a few really fine tunes/songs at some points in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Got this on a 80% sale and i got to say it was worth it, but anything more than that is way too much for this game.It's fun to make choices that can affect the kingdom, but they choices are really shallow and the so called impact is barely noticeable.Kinda wished they had a chapter/week select so i can redo some choices especially the one to keep the bear.Worth it if it's on a huge sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: I personally do not play many games with lasting consequences because i have a horrible history of save-scumming and going for exactly the ending i wanted. But with "Yes, Your Grace" i found myself to enraptured in the story of this wonderful game. “Yes, your grace” will capture you with it’s wonderful visuals and music while making you take difficult moral choices and you will more than likely find yourself doing a lot of things you honestly don’t want to? But it’s for the better of your kingdom. I cannot stress enough how much i personally absolutely adored the interactions i had with the family and the daughters especially Asalia. I felt Asalia’s story and in general, the character was masterfully done, and in all honesty, I’d love a sequel focused solely on her. The gameplay itself is rather simple, you follow a loop of weeks where you adress the peasants and request the presents of lords and nobles to your kingdom addressing their needs and issues and gaining the support of others or making new enemies. It follows a simple system of managing gold and resources(Food) as well as public favor(All though in my first playthrough i never struggled with the public favor part even in the slightest). While it’s a good functioning system the sheer requirements of certain tasks in comparison to what you’d get out of it were just insane, it was incredibly difficult to consistently meet the demands of my peasants and on some weeks i couldn’t even attend to one of them with all the other things i had to spend gold and or one of the three special units onThe three special units all require upkeep, 9/11/11 gold respectively and all serve a different purpose when it comes to sorting out the issues of the peasants be that clearing wolves or quelling troubles at an in. One way to circumvent having to use them if you’ve used them already and or your planning to use them is with gold…..again. It’s the only major issue i personally can find with the game. Overall I can STRONGLY recommend “Yes, Your Grace” to anyone who wants a relaxing but also a heartwrenching game. Filled with lovable characters, well-written dialogue, and a gorgeous art style and soundtrack. The game is most assuredly going to tug at your hearth a little be that rage, or happiness. Personally I’d rate “Yes, Your grace” a solid 9/10. Despite the issue with some of the currency management and requirements I still sat through my first playthrough in one sitting and enjoyed every second of it it’s a wonderful game and i can only say pick it up now while you can and it’s on sale(As of 09-03-2020)
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: For everything its worth? I'd say the game delivers well with whats given. Despite its story being a little on the short side, there was enough content in it to keep me entertained and engaged so much. The characters were nicely written, and the plot was both interesting, and an overall great experience.There is no endless mode where you keep playing until you meet an unfortunate end like other decision games. But I would probably like to see something like it done here in the future, the game has a good amount of replay-ability despite it only having a story mode. As there's so many choices that you can pick. And each one I can say for certain really has that impact on the story. You will always be engaged during the entire session you play.I can say for certain that I look forward to a possible squeal for this game.I'm not going to lie when I said I bought this during sale. But after experiencing the game? I was considering wanting to buy it at full price. The Developers really put in their effort for this piece. And it shows, from the art, the story, the sounds and music. And while there were somethings that could still get polished, it was overall a great game.10/10 would highly recommend? "Yes, Your Grace."

_childDocuments_.review: The game's story is very engaging with a lot of twists and turns, and did involve some shocking events that I didn't see happening. The managing of resources adds a little difficulty to the game, if you run out of either one the game ends, so you can't help everyone. That said towards the end I fired all my agents and helped nobody and nothing changed.  That brings me to the next part, pretty much nothing you do in the game will change anything. The story will progress forward no matter what, and you can't stray from the path.  The only thing that will change is a few flavor quests and peasants, but nothing that honestly matters. The game is fun for a one playthrough type of gamer, get it on a hefty discount.Also you can either encourage or discourage a lesbian relationship, so that's kinda cool.

_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: The first half of the game was okay. The second half was a slog. There's not a ton of replayability and what little decision making you have to make is limited to, essentially, remembering things told to your character. You make day-to-day decisions for peasants which struggle from a lack of creative choices, and game feedback.The Good-Charming, engaging story-Great writing for all the characters-Touching moments of real empathy-Graphics are cuteThe bad-Battle sequences aren't as rewarding as they should be.-Resource management is kind of fun towards the middle -> end of the game.-The interface is *terrible* about presenting you with invalid options the game knows are invalid while showing to you. "Send your X here" when the game already knows you've used up your X.-Choices when hearing petitioners are too limited.-There's no feedback on what the happiness stat means. Is 100 good? Is 15 good? Who knows!-Interface causes a lot of drudgery walking around in an adventure-like setting, looking for people to talk to. Often times you don't have anyone to speak to and you just want to skip to the next day.-None of the decisions felt very compelling.I wouldn't buy the game for more than 4-5$. Better if you can get it for less. There's little to no replayability unless you're a masochist.

_childDocuments_.review: Picked this up on sale and could not have snagged a better deal.I played through the whole story in about 6 hours and am already thinking about alternative decisions I could have made and whether or not to make them in replays later. Having over a thousand hours in CK2, this is in some ways a microcosm of that game - the personal relationships, alliances with lords, tax and resource management, etc.The music is solid, the graphics simple and fun.But where the game really shines is plot and character development. It has substance I felt like my choices matter. I faced the consequences of them relentlessly. Villages helped or neglected in the early game dictated where I would find support in the late game.I laughed, I clenched my fists in rage, cried in anguish, and let my daughter adopt a bear.

_childDocuments_.review: Decent storytelling game. Writing is fine, characters are solid, and the art style is nice. Gameplay-wise, some things could have been streamlined in the experience. It's also odd that many decisions you make DURING major story events don't have a real impact. All the little decisions add up to affect the day-to-day operations of the kingdom, but a lot of the "story event" stuff is on rails no matter what you decide to do. When your choices DO matter, it's basically just good or bad outcome. For instance, the outcome of the major battle is basically a win or lose but you can't really change the details of the "victory". This issue, some "illusion of choice" dialogue, and knowing the plot after your first run, all greatly reduces replay value.
_childDocuments_.name: Yes, Your Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Yes recommend.  Rivetting.  Beat it in one sitting/ 6 hours for me.  To me its a mash up of adventure games (but with the difficulty ramped down a little relative to 90's era adventure games) with a reasonably difficult strategy/ resource management game.  Interesting characters and intriguing writing.  I wish they would allow you to defer making decisions until you had talked to every supplicant(?) every week, as multiple supplicants would ask for 2 solutions that overlapped, and you could only do both if you picked the correct one by chance the first time. HOWEVER this may have been a CHOICE by the developers that ramps up the difficulty.  If so, its kind of a respectable decision, but it doesn't make sense in the context of a bunch of people making requests of the king that he cant tell them to wait in the corner for a few minutes after asking him for 25% of the treasury.  Only complaint, and its more of a kerfuffle than anything else.  Good humor and writing.  Art style makes me nostalgic for Secrets of Monkey Island.  Good tension and stakes in the story telling.  If you don't like adventure games, strategy/management, or story driven/character driven games, then this is not for you.  If you have ANY interest in either of those genres, I recommend highly.  Decisions seem to matter, but I need to play again to know for sure.  Good day sir!
