_childDocuments_.review: Light/shadow-based games seem kind of getting popular recently, and though I normally love this kind of stuff, nevertheless I just can’t help feeling very conflicted about this game. Don’t get me wrong (as stated in some of my other reviews, I don’t judge this way spontaneously), no, again it really hurts me inside to give this one a negative rating after I finally finished it (even with all achievements). And I definitely don’t want to seem like the nitpicky kind of guy. But in the end I have to stay true to my experience over all the long hours, and the following thoughts are indeed what actually went through my mind when playing this game. I know, it’s kind of complicated to describe it in short, so I guess I have to explain this a bit further, just please stay with me for this.Anyway, I admit the game really starts out tremendously great, the way the shadows are introduced (especially when the 2D effects merge into 3D), the awesome breathtakingly melancholic music all over (fantastic soundtrack), the sensitive dialogs in the beginning. I’m talking about a kind of quality that let me and my wife think, oh my god, this could actually be a candidate for our next favorite indie-game of the year. Seriously, that’s how good it felt for the first hour, no kidding. But the longer I played, I don‘t know, it’s kind of hard to explain, it somehow felt like I COMPLETELY lost the emotional connection to the game. Maybe it was the lost-in-translation English voice-over (if you know The Missing, it’s the same voice-actor, but here she speaks as a child, always weird when an adult speaks one, Clemmy from Walking Dead as a huge exception). Or maybe it was the general under-tone of the game, especially the undecided, sledgehammer-wise psychology (the main topic of the game is a kind of interior struggle after all). Particularly at later chapters the ‘light’ child sounds more like a spoiled brat, while the ‘shadow’ child seems like a self-righteous know-it-all, and honestly, this wasn’t really helping me to connect. This way the message overall relates to, hey girl, if you’re depressed or suffering under self-isolation-issues, just get your act together. And seriously, this is just too simple in my opinion, might even be through-out insulting for people who themselves are suffering under similar afflictions. Apart from that, gameplay-wise there was also definitely too little variation for my taste, it’s always only about lifting boxes here, or pulling levers there, with a lot of trial and error. So my final verdict, for people who expect a decent-to-mediocre narrative puzzle platformer with little variation, and who don’t listen to the story, go ahead, you might enjoy this one. All in all it’s still kind of fair, checkpoints are plenty, and there’s even a clever rewind mechanism. But if you’re a bit more sensitive like me, especially the psychology (which even doesn’t get resolved in the end, like, what the heck happened here anyway), and the arbitrary stereotypic environments (though drawn well) really turned me off in the end. Sorry. Just seems like the devs wanted too much, and at some point didn’t know what to write anymore, so they repeated themselves over and over again (with gameplay AND writing), up to the point at which the main characters just get unsympathetic, and you just want the game to be over. It’s kind of sad, really, because the core of this one actually could have been really good.

_childDocuments_.review: Within the first 10 minutes of play, I fell in love with this game. I had no expectations and was hesitant to take on a 'platformer.' It has elements that reminded me of Limbo (avoiding dark stuff but without the monsters) and Little Nightmares (directing a faceless child through a surreal landscape but without the monsters). I am most reminded of Iris.Fall which also focuses on a child's journey and uses shadow play as part of the game mechanics.For me, Shady Part of Me is better than all three of those, put together. It is a journey of self discovery and overcoming fear to become your true self. The narrative is told through 'self talk' between the child and her shadow (her light and dark sides) and an outer voice that offsets the self doubt and provides encouragement. To be honest, I missed a lot of the narrative because I was so enchanted with the landscapes, the creative puzzles, the music, and the style. As far as platforming goes, I did not struggle. The game is fairly forgiving and has a rewind that lets you re-do a mistake (rather than having you die and start a sequence all over).  Shady Part of Me is broken into many short segments with the puzzles being to get the child and the shadow from entry to exit point. Your game is automatically saved at each exit point. The shadow is navigated through a 2D environment bound by 'edges' of light/dark and the child is navigated through a 3D environment bound by avoiding the light. This makes for some very interesting problem solving as cooperation is required to get both through most of the scenarios. There are 98 birds to find (some light, some dark) as optional collectibles and you have the option of revisiting completed sections to pick up any you may have missed.What I loved most about this game was the diversity of the artwork and how the puzzles changed and had elements added as you proceed through the four major Acts. There are toy trains and airplanes, paper boats, cogs, elevators, and a host of different scenes (a carnival, a hospital, a clock, a theater, etc.). My sense of wonder continued throughout the game. And, by the way, the music is haunting and beautiful to listen to. The voice overs are well done and I may have to replay just to listen to the dialog more closely.The ending was satisfying and heart warming. If childhood was a time of inner struggle for you, the game will have additional meaning and impact.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could pick a "mixed" rating. Some stuff I really liked, but some stuff I really disliked.The visuals are outstanding. Every frame is a work of art, and overall, it's a gorgeous game. However, to me the latter half of the game is relatively plain compared to the incredibly surreal, artistic, and hyper-detailed first half. Things start off very strong, but lose steam over time.As far as the game mechanics go: The interplay of light and shadow allows you to interact in both two and three dimensions, which is a really brilliant idea. It's intuitive and makes for a very fluid gameplay experience the entire way through. Light gets used in clever ways, such as casting shadows from two different switches so they overlap, allowing your shadow-self to pull them both at the same time. I mean come on, that's just awesome. Lots of really neat ideas.Most of the puzzles, sadly, are way too easy -- and the ones that are more involved/detailed are too easily cheesed by the Braid/Prince of Persia-style rewind feature, which feels out of place in a game like this. Temporal manipulations are not required in the puzzle solutions, and you're not outright fighting anyone, and the idea of rewinding time doesn't appear to be an integral aspect of the story... so I'm unclear why this feature exists. I assume it's because some switches/pressure-plates have ambiguous function from the outset, but I think some kind of visual indicators would help circumvent that concern (similar to how Q.U.B.E. 2 or The Witness handle it).At any rate, the rewind feature bails you out of making mistakes, which means you don't have to put as much thought into a tougher puzzle, nor do you have to be careful or plan anything out. You can just start jumping, pulling levers, and pushing buttons without a care, because if you get it wrong and kill your shadow (or yourself), you can just rewind a second or two and try something else. Meanwhile, the boundary conditions feel a little inconsistent. Sometimes you could be just a smidgeon off and get obliterated by the light. Other times you could squeeze your way across a gap that should have probably been fatal. It made strategizing a little less reliable in select cases because it wasn't clear if a particular spot or move was going to kill you or not. But it didn't matter because you could just try it anyway and rewind if it failed.The story is otherwise the weakest part of the game. I'm really not a fan of stories where characters speak in vague terms the whole way through. There's no commitment to any concrete narrative, and the details are left for the player to fill in. By the time you reach the ending of the game, there are more questions raised, and very few answers given. While I have my own speculations and theories as to what the story means, I found the lack of payoff frustrating.There are optional origami collectibles throughout the game that, on the whole, do a good job of adding an element of difficulty to some of the puzzles, but they have no explanation, no mention, no reference, and nothing happens when you collect them all. I'd still recommend Shady Part of Me because I think it's very visually well-done and the core gameplay mechanic is extremely cool. I just wish it had more meat with respect to the story and the puzzles.

_childDocuments_.review: Shady Part of Me is an atmospheric puzzle-platformer. It invites comparisons to games such as Little Nightmares; however, if Little Nightmares is more about platforming and less about puzzles, Shady Part of Me is more about puzzles and less about platforming. The general gameplay involves manipulating a girl and her shadow (?), and using objects around them to solve puzzles to progress both persons through a hostile environment. Overall, I found the art in the game to be quite nice, the music was excellent, and the controls were smooth. The puzzles ranged from straight-forward to being quite difficult/unintuitive, but ultimately solvable with some thought and effort. There are frequent save points and the ability to rewind in time, which I greatly appreciate. The only aspect I didn't particularly enjoy was how much talking there was in between scenes (though it generally happens when you're moving, so it's not like you're stuck waiting for it to finish or anything); it felt like the game could have had 1/5 the amount of dialogue that it did and it would have been better off for it.I highly recommend this game if you have played/enjoyed Little Nightmares and are looking for something that is similar in vibe to that game, or if you generally enjoy puzzle-platforming games. The game took me 6 hours to complete in entirety.

_childDocuments_.review: You switch between a girl moving in a 3D space and her independently moving shadow. The girl does a lot of block pushing while the shadow does a lot of platforming in a 2D space, but both will need to work together to pull switches, solve puzzles, and move forward. There is spoken and written dialog throughout the game. The girl, her shadow, and a third voice will speak to each other and some of their thoughts will be written out on the stage objects and backgrounds. I like the platforming sections of the shadow. I thought the game would be mostly focused on puzzles, but there are some paper birds found throughout the game that take some advanced level platforming to reach sometimes. Other birds are a more advanced puzzle solution than the one needed to progress. The birds only reveal puzzle pieces to images on the level select screens. Each of these screens also helpfully tell you how many of the birds you have collected. This is very helpful to anyone who wants to 100% the game. The game's art style does look very nice.The girl's high pitched voice seemed very out of place at first. I don't think it goes well with the messy-haired girl that looks like she might be out of a horror film. The shadow has a deeper voice, and I think they are supposed to be two personalities of the same person? That would make sense, but the game does not give conclusive answers about who any of the three voices are supposed to be. Most of the game is the three voices arguing with each other over vague concepts when they finally just get over it in the final chapter. Also, that scene in the trailer where the girl pushes over a piece of prop scenery and she dives into the light, that is part of the very end of the game. The ability of the shadow to possess other objects is only done in the last chapter. The game sticks to moving blocks and platforming the entire rest of the game. The puzzles do get difficult, but by the end I was getting tired and wished they could change up the activities more often.The game's characters seem interesting at first, but you never get to know any details of the drama the girl is going through. She may just be fighting extreme shyness. I lost interest in the characters halfway through and was enjoying the gameplay, but that eventually got tiring by the end. The game is about six hours long and has great visual design, but it is not something I will be returning to any time soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: This is a platformer-puzzle game with some really interesting mechanics, and a lot of atmosphere. I'm not going to go too into the plot, as to some extent there's a lot of room for interpretation, and don't want to inadvertently steer anyone else's experience. You play as two characters- a young girl, and her silhouette/shadow self - the ONLY reason I'm saying shadow self here, is that it's not a true shadow and the two are inextricably linked. Both characters have the same aim - to get out. Although they may not always appreciate the other's assistance.Aside from this - the store page does a good job of explaining the plot without spoilers.  The world is a beautiful inked style, and the game mechanics are incredibly well thought out as the young girl must stay in the shadows, and the shadow girl must stay in the light - relatively simple there, until you then consider that the shadow girl is in 2D and the young girl is (almost) 3D - but just as with real light play, what happens in 3D affects 2D as well - and forms the basis for a lot of the puzzles, so it's a really good spatial test at times. The soundtrack is honestly one of the best indie soundtracks I've heard in recent times, and to be quite honest a good few hours of my gameplay is actually just me leaving the soundtrack running because it's super chill and pretty calming. Unfortunately it's not available on Spotify (I looked) but the composer does apparently have it on their Soundcloud, and there's a playlist on YouTube which is now in regular rotation for me. It fits the game so well, with it developing through the narrative helping to create an overall atmosphere that sucks you in. The game is nicely split into four acts - the first - unsurprisingly gets you to grips with the characters, introductions to the mechanics and puzzles, and then three further acts - these make great natural break points if you don't have a whole day to spend on it (I played an act a session) and I'd recommend not rushing through the game - there are collectibles throughout, which give the steam achievements, and none of them are too difficult, but if you rush you may well miss some. I knew quite early on that there were likely to be feels in this game - and whilst it didn't go the way I expected, there were times where I felt quite emotional as recognition of some of the themes contained in the game resonated quite strongly - and there were a couple of moments where I took a break, and at one point there were tears - but I am very much an empathic type so YMMV, but if you know you have that too, might be worth having a tissue on hand or someone to talk about it with. Definitely raised a few hard questions and made me consider some things!If you like a game with an emotional connection, then this is definitely a good one, and a decent length to not be too heavy, but not feel cheated. I'd absolutely recommend this on sale - at full price (currently £12.99) I think I'd still be happy to pay that - at probably 6-8 hours playtime it's cheaper than a trip to the cinema!

_childDocuments_.review: Shady Part of Me impresses with its dreamlike art style and unique blend of 3D and 2D shadow-based puzzles. The hand-drawn visuals and hauntingly beautiful atmosphere perfectly complement the game’s emotional narrative. Its distinctive aesthetic and clever mechanics make it a standout in the puzzle-platformer genre.Rating: ★★★★☆ (4/5)

_childDocuments_.review: There have been times that I've really tried to imagine a mental landscape for therapy and healing yourself, what it would be like... I feel like this game really captured that. It feels like taking a walk inside someone's mind while they work on themselves.I really like the concept of working together *with* yourself as well, guiding each other. The adult version of you that wants to be pragmatic and the child version of you that's still reckless and scared. Loved the dialogue between these two. Reminds me of conversations and arguments I've had with myself.And... the soundtrack is really gorgeous.And... puzzles. I couldn't leave it alone until I got all of the origami. :)

_childDocuments_.review: The game features a little girl, whose name I actually never discovered - she is scared and lonely; seems to be a tad depressed and has a tremendous hatred of the light. Soon after the story begins, we learn that she isn't all alone as her shadow accompanies her – a shadow that can’t survive in darkness.And it must be said that the voice of the little girl is somewhat annoyingly yammer and quite (too?) childlike, all whilst the voice of the shadow seems to be much more sophisticated. Fortunately, it didn't take me very long to get used to the shill voice of the little girl and I persevered to continue playing.Shady Part of Me aims to be one of those tales that won't seem to make much sense at first before becoming increasingly evident as you learn more and progress but, in order to preserve the experience of trying to piece together the narrative on your own, I won't go into too much information about the plot.The main reason I said "trying" is because I'm still unsure if I fully comprehend the story and I'm left with a lot of unanswered questions. For the time being, I can only speculate on what I think the story is about, where we were, etc.The game certainly also tried for an emotional mood, but somewhere along the line the message just got a little lost - It is transparent very early on that the theme is about trauma and therapy, but not more than that - making it unclear what exactly the girl and her shadow are trying to work through. I really wish the tale was just a little less mysterious and the ending provided more clarification.Sadly, it won't take long for me to forget about it, which is unfortunate because I wanted to be more invested in their word. But how can I care about something I don't understand? And yet at the same time; It just serves as a further indication that the narrative had some kind of impact on me regardless,  simply because I occasionally ponder back about it all, at the most unexpected moments – still trying to understand what it all meant. However, where the narrative falls short, it more than makes up for it in terms of visuals, audio, and gameplay. So, let’s dive into that.The sceneries – that are a variety of environments - are represented in a magnificent watercolour palette with the predominant colours being black, grey, white, and off-white. Depending on the location, you may also encounter some red, blue, green, and yellow. It has a suitably gloomy appearance, contributes to the atmosphere-building process, and effectively evokes the emotions of the main character.With moments the game's audio is very peaceful and calming, depending on your actions, it may suddenly become incredibly intense; by increasing the tension and suspense at crucial moments - it made me feel even more immersed. It's impressive to me how well the soundtrack complemented the gameplay and graphics. In my opinion, it was the game's strongest feature; and it is quite unfortunate that we cannot purchase the soundtrack separately to listen to.The puzzle component of the gameplay is represented in 3D, while the platforming component is represented in 2D. To assist and advance, it will be necessary for the player to switch between the two characters while controlling each one separately while cooperating. When they both reach a whirling ring, the level will be finished and you’re good to move on to the next part.The platforming and puzzles are neither the hardest, but some of them did prove to be a little challenging. And I'll admit there have been times when I didn't see it until I finally noticed it, at which point my eye twitched as I wondered how I could have missed that.Death is non-existent, if you fail you simply have to trigger your rewind button and you’re good to retry again.A first look at the gameplay I finished the game in 6.4 hours, but I had to replay it because I missed a few collectable birds and an achievement. The good news is that you can choose your "act," as the game's chapters appear to be termed in this game, and even focus on a specific checkpoint. In addition, there is a sizable illustration that resembles a jigsaw puzzle and lists all the birds you have; A missing puzzle piece simply means a missing collectable. Once you figure out which piece represents which region of the world, which wasn't too difficult, it will be much simpler to go hunt them down and collect them all.This feature is, in my opinion, absolutely heavenly because it prevents you from having to restart the game. So here we are huh, at the end of the review already. Time went by fast, just as in the game – since it wasn’t the longest one, but that’s not a bad thing per se as it didn’t overstay its welcome; and as I indicated before, I didn’t fully comprehend the story and what it all meant. However, I’m ok with that. Who knows one day it might suddenly hit me. I’m still very happy that I got to see that world; to have had the joy to solve the puzzles and use my platforming skills to advance and see the end scene.So, if you can and are willing to overlook that there is a chance you might not fully understand the plot – cause let’s admit, it could be a me thing - and you enjoy puzzle and platform games, then take it into consideration to give this game a shot. Thank you for reading,with love,Tchii I received this game for free; I did not receive any compensation to write this review. The opinions represented here, as well as my experience with the game, are entirely my own and were not influenced in any way.

_childDocuments_.review: A very solid and approachable puzzle platformer. In Shady Part Of Me, you switch between two characters - the shadow can only move freely in 2D and in light, and the girl can only move freely in 3D and in shadow. Together you solve puzzles and make your way through weird environments.The controls are solid, the game's scope is just right and it was a joy to play. The puzzles are overall a bit on the easy side and I did not understand the story fully, but the game does a good job setting the tone and foundation of the gameplay elements and story beats which makes for a nice atmosphere. At a length of about 5 hours, this is a good puzzle snack with some interesting environments and a heartwarming, if slightly cryptic story and I can only recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could recommend this game because I’m sure a lot of work went into it, and on a technical level, it’s a good game. The art style and music are definite highlights, while the puzzles, platforming, and game length are all decent.Unfortunately, where the game falls apart is its story, which is a significant issue since the game is narrative-heavy. The central theme seems to revolve around some form of mental health struggle, but what that struggle is—whether trauma, the challenges of growing up, anxiety, neurodiversity, or something else—is impossible to discern because the writing is so vague. Perhaps this was done intentionally, hoping players would interpret the story through their own life experiences, but even if that’s the case, I think it fails to achieve that goal.There’s also another, more problematic issue with the story, and that is its depiction of therapy and/or the therapist who is supposedly helping and guiding our protagonist through their struggle. The disembodied voice of the "other" never seems to offer the right advice, especially the repeated "try harder" throughout the game, which, in the context of the central theme, is infuriating. The result of this guidance, the supposed goal at the end of the game, struck me as disastrous, to the point where I found it genuinely disturbing. One of the final lines from the protagonist, delivered in a raised voice, is:  My heart sank when I heard that monologue, especially right after Maybe the game is meant to present a nihilistic, depressive view of therapy, where the only way to move forward and get better is to lose all individuality and simply conform. However, I don’t find this perspective acceptable.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: I won't pretend, that I understood "Shady Part of Me". I did not, because there are lots of things left for interpretation and you can interpret it quite differently. Schizophrenia? Autism? Growing up? Accepting your own flaws? Something else?What I can say for sure, is that at some points in the game, I felt a pit in my stomach. It was as if the music, the visuals, some phrase said by one of the characters or even their dialogue... All of those things combined resonated with something deep within.I wish for the game to have a more... "elaborate" ending, but on the other hand, perhaps the subtle feeling of emptiness left by it was meant to be as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Shady Part of Me has captivated us with its stunning artistic direction and its creativity. The puzzles are cleverly constructed and based on an efficient physics engine. The dual gameplay is used to its fullest potential and is constantly renewed with new ideas and elements that will challenge you without being overwhelming. In addition, the sublime soundtrack featuring Hannah Murray certainly won't disappoint.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Out of the shadow-puzzle type games I have played so far, this has been the most creative one. There were some really fun sections, escpecially in the second half where some new mechanics were introduced (I wish those were explored even more, they could make for some satisfyingly mindbogling puzzles).For me the story felt almost dipping into pretentiousness here or there, but it has its emotional strengths, and I appreciate the storytelling through its visuals/mechanics.If the trailer made you interested, then its worth a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Shady Part of Me is a beautiful game about a girl and her shadow dealing with emotional struggles in the girl's dreamworld. You have to solve some interesting puzzles by combining the girl and her shadow's efforts in an attempt to escape. The girl can only walk in darkness, and the shadow can only walk in light, making for an interesting puzzle method. The artwork is cool and the narrator hit it out of the park. The only improvement would be more focus on the story. Whilst there is an idea for the story in the game, it's never really solidified. Non the less, it's an amazing game!15 euros seems a little bit on the high side for this game, but during a sale, it's definitely worth picking up. 7,5 / 10
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Shady Part of Me is a 2-D puzzle platformer that also mixes 2.5-D gameplay.The visual presentation is excellent, which is important to understand what's going on.The story is not explicit. It is about a girl going through some emotional turmoil (as per my interpretation). There is a nice discussion about this in the forum section of the game.You will switch back and forth between the two environments to complete the puzzles. One is the real 3-D world (played as the girl with 2.5-D movements), and another is the 2-D world (played as the shadow of the girl). The puzzles are easy to moderate difficulty-wise and well designed to incorporate both environments.There are collectibles called origamis, which reveal more dialogues, and they also complete a picture art associated with a particular act (plus to unlock achievements). Collecting them adds a nice flavor to the puzzles. Sometimes, you must think outside the box to get them.The game is divided into five parts: the intro and Acts 1 through 4. Each part introduces a new mechanic that makes the puzzles somewhat challenging towards the end. Each part is divided into a number of chapters or sections. You can select any chapter from any act using the select option in the menu.The voice work is decent (and funny at times). The music is top-notch. I felt disappointed that there was no OST release for the game.Some of the sections felt redundant. Those could have been flashed out. The character model is simplistic (covered entirely to be economical, I guess).I played it with an Xbox-gamepad without any issues, and the movement felt smooth. It can be completed in 5 to 6 hours (an extra hour or so to get all the collectibles).I finished the game again on Linux using Proton Experimental without any problems.I recommend getting this at a light discount.My verdict: 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for February 2023, this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before March 7th, 2023, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.A shadow-based platformer.Shady Part of Me has players taking on the role of a shadowy girl and a potentially nameless child.  The entire game is progressing through several platforming levels, with each showing a few short words or voice lines to a large overarching story.  The Platforming mostly deals with using shadows as platforming or avoiding the light depending on the character, and players will have to switch back and forth between them.   There’s also a Time rewind mechanic similar to Braid. This seems like an easy game to like but I found myself getting tired while playing it.  Nothing really interesting happens and while there’s a mystery about the story after a full hour and nothing has been explained yet.  A few of the levels have clever concepts to them, but you’re mostly just walking or jumping through rather common type levels, and while the interactions between the two characters can be good, they also are often mundane.Pick this up if you like platformers, especially if you ever played a game called Contrast.  There are a few interesting art designs and levels, but also a lot of levels that didn’t stand out as much.  A shame because conceptually this is cool, it just wasn’t that exciting to play. If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: A really solid puzzle platformer that is totally worth your time.The only “not good” part of the game is the story, as some people think this is some narrative driven game, but there isn’t really any story to go through. It is more of an abstract “girl going through therapy to fix her mental issues” concept, so don’t expect much. Other than this small problem - the game is one of a high quality.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: A literal interplay of light and darkness with a metaphorical journey of the self, or something.In each level, players will have to alternate between playing as the protagonist in the 3D world or taking control of the shadow in the 2D platformer. The puzzles were simple and so banal I had to look up the word 'ennui' just to find a fitting description for this. Words and sentences popping up on the screen all the time proved a great distraction, the same source of which frustration oft arises, which it unfortunately did. I mean, the walking/jumping onomatopoeia just wouldn't leave you alone. And too many long walks to reach the next level I asked myself whether or when I miss the 'walking simulator' in the game tag. But perhaps they were for the sake of immersion and storytelling. And, to each their own: there are many people enjoying the view along the route. The narration was great, and this is an honest praise. The story itself was rather obscure; people were sharing their take on what it actually was about. My take is that it was about me fighting against my bored and discouraged part in order to finish the game since the game just wouldn't finish itself, and eventually we merged into  which was still as bored and discouraged, yet could manage to complete the game, and threw shade. Lol. Just kidding. But, really, many interesting interpretations on the discussion forum. You can check them out later after you have finished the game (I know you're going to buy it anyway. I mean, one random negative review? Nah, you're not stopping anyone. Believe me, it won't stop me as well).It pains me a bit to rate this game down since many parts of the game is totally creative; the combination of 2D and 3D world, for example. Some puzzles were fantastic and well thought-out. Overall, the game is really not that bad. But it all comes down to this conclusion: "well, I didn't quite enjoy it". And that's that. That's all. If you are a fan of the puzzle platformer thingy and this game looks promising to you, then go ahead and buy it. I mean, no, I'm not going to stop you. Try it for yourself. If you enjoy it, you enjoy it; and if you don't, well, you just don't.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Shady Part of Me is a cur artistic puzzle game about a little girl who stuggles through life. Being afraid of light, or afraid of beeing seen, is one of her issues. As such, she cannot walk through brightly lid areas in the game. Her shadow can only live in the light and there you have a nice twist on the both 2d (shadow) and 3d ('real' world) puzzle elements in this game.Both the girl and her shadow needs to traverse through a quite large amount of small maps and are both controlled independently of eachother. The girl has to walk in shadows, not being able to enter brightly lid areas, while her shadow must walk and jump on shadows cast by the environment. They have to work together to move boxes and turn levers to make the way clear for each other and reach the end of each map. On top of that, there's some dangerous things going on in the shadow world.Puzzles are mostly quite easy, with a few exceptions. The hardest part is getting the optional origamis for several achievements.While the graphics are relatively simple, the whole style of the game is just great. Things flow nicely from one area to another and the maps and layout really fits the narrative. The presentation of the story is a mix of both voice acted and written narrative and they complement each other perfectly. Very well done.One negative point to mention is that the english voice of the girl is weird. It doesn't sound natural at all. It's only a minor complaint though. Other voices are fine and it hardly distracted me from the game itself.While having different mechanics, it's easy to compare this game to Iris Fall. And rightfully so. If you like one, you'll probably like the other as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Man this game was… a lot more than I was expecting. In a very, very good way.This game deals a lot with anxiety and overcoming trauma, though in a vague enough way that I don't think it'd really trigger anyone. The messages in the game were highly relatable and either painful or touching, depending on the message.The gameplay itself felt very creative. You play as two characters - a young girl, and her shadow. Each character can do things to help the other progress - while the shadow is stuck to a 2D world and can only exist in the light, the girl can move in a 3D space and must stick to the shadows. Very creative and made for some fun puzzles! Most of them I was able to figure out pretty easily but I did wind up having to look up 2 near the end.I feel like this story is vague enough that there's a lot of ways to interpret it, but overall, it's a story about finally facing some childhood trauma, accepting that it is part of you, but still realizing you need to move on. For what can be such a sensitive subject, I feel like it was really well done. The vagueness will allow people to relate in ways that a more direct story might not, and I feel like it wasn't really pushing that there is one 'correct' way to heal, which I think a lot of games/media do. It also wasn't a quick 'I've recovered, I'm better' story. The ending, while positive, doesn't say the main character is healed. Just. Working on it. Which is far more realistic than a lot of media handles things.While I loved the game, 100%ing it seems like it might be tedious without a walkthrough. And I was unable to find a text walkthrough, only video, which I personally find far more annoying as it's harder to find the exact parts I need. In order to 100% the game, you need to find all the origami birds, which give motivational phrases upon finding them, and sometimes unique character dialogue. For that reason, I did go for all the ones I could, but there were a few I just never saw and a few I couldn't figure out the puzzles to collect. I did collect over 70 of the 96, though, so pretty good considering my skill level at platformers (very low)!I loved this game a lot more than expected. I'm really glad I decided to pick it up and play it after having had it for a while.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to make a statement about this game because the game doesn't know what to say about itself. The dialogue through the story was vague and meandering and the development of the character(s) cut back on itself in a way that undermined the messaging on the journey. Many of the puzzles were simple, which was fine, but that made the process of moving each character individually through them become tedious, especially when there were long runways that each character had to walk down. There is a way to make them both move at the same time (making the shadow jump while the child moves and switching continuously) but that was pretty annoying.The game was very beautiful, with fantastical sets, and some of the puzzles were exciting and interesting, but when the game concluded I was left disappointed and confused.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: I feel this game is severely underrated. I wasn't expecting much and decided to wait until this game was on sale. Wow am I glad I bought it. I love games such as Limbo, Inside, and Little Nightmares and that is what it felt like to me, but also its own thing. The playing as a shadow and following light rules to figure out puzzles, and playing as the other who had to avoid light was really interesting. There is some dialogue that hints at what it all means and I loved the voices. My only complaint is that the dialogue was often repetitive , saying the same thing over and over in different wording. But you are offered different pieces to the story as you advance through the puzzles. It is not story 'rich' but that is not a complaint, the amount fits the type of game atmosphere and style that was created. The art is great and has the same vibe as the games mentioned above. Controls were easy, puzzles were great only  being head scratchers near the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: this game started really great, like i was really interested but both the gameplay and story repeat and falls apart as times go on and it's just, really not goodspoilers ahead :the gameplay ends up being the same like 2-3 things over and over in various flavour of the same thing, which get boring over like 5-6hthe story is the worst offender tho, bad gameplay will just make me forget a game, that's fine, but how the story is handled feels quite insulting to his subjectThe general subject is about psychology and the general struggle from someone, but it's never clear what it's about, is it about trauma, is it about depression, is it plurality? unclear.But that's not even the main issue because whatever reading you give it it's not good, if you read it about trauma or depression, the message is "therapy will fix you and you should just do better". If you read it about plurality, it's something that has to -and is at the end- "fixed", which is, well, insulting might not be strong enough of a word for that.i'm sure you could read it another way and it'll just ends up feeling just as sanist.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Got it off humble bundle choice.To be honest, when I first saw it, I just saw screenies and was sure I was about to play 20 minutes be pissed off, and leave it.The voice acting was annoying as hell at start, and I was sure it is cheesy af and cringe, little girl waking up and is all whiney, I said to myself ill give it 15 more minutes and I'm throwing this annoying thing away and it looks like so many other games but,after 20 minutes I didn't like the game but the story started to take interesting shape and the visuals were actually pretty good,after another 20 minutes, I was interested in the characters and realized that it is actually on purpose,and 20 minutes after there were actually some cool puzzles that I liked,20 minutes after I started trying to perfect some puzzles and just waiting to see how the story continuesI was "boo 4/10, nice try" to "9/10 good stuff, will recommend" and I'm actually trying to find someone to talk about this game :DThanks, devs for doing it like it is.I tried harder, I mean HARDER, I did it on my own.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: One word, Merveilleux.The soundtrack was beautiful, and I would love if it was released as a DLC.The gameplay mechanics were brilliant, as with the puzzles, which aren't too difficult, but are still entertaining and fun to solve.I played the game in its original language, which is French, so my opinion on this may not matter to many people, but the voice acting was lovely.And of course the wonderful story.However, throughout the game there were many hidden meanings. Which is in no doubt great, it basically forms these types of games and I love the implication of that. Although for someone like me, who won't get the message if you don't literally swing an explanation right before my nose, it was confusing and hard at times to keep up with what is actually happening, who plays what role, what was the backstory, meanings of some of the representations and etc.Nevertheless, the story was truly wonderful to experience and I really enjoyed playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played through Act I of this game so far, but I've really enjoyed it. The mechanics are unique in concept, but easy to understand. I'm excited to play the rest of the game!Edit: After finishing the game, I definitely still recommend it. _childDocuments_.review: Shady Part of Me tells quite a deep, dark story of a traumatic childhood in an easy to swallow way. It shows the process of going through the trauma, then therapy.In a way, it's been theraputic to me, to play, learn this young woman's story and follow along. It's nice to see trauma represented in a way that isn't traumatic.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Love the art style, story telling was enjoyable. This pulled me in and got me hooked.The puzzles are entertaining and expected, not too challenging, but not everything was a cakewalk. I enjoyed the two level of difficulty on some puzzles (one easier solution to progress the story and one more complex solution to get the collectables). It does seem like the story was the main focus, and the puzzles are a pleasant and welcomed gameplay mechanic that enhance the story,
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely write reviews to any games, but this one is a very special one to me. I bought the game on a whim after stumbling across it in the sales. When I watched the trailer I was intrigued though and started the game today only to play through it in one session (with a little bit of help by a walkthrough). It's a platformer with some puzzles in it to advance. I really like the way they made these. The use of different dimensions while still making it simple enough to not require too many explanations is just great here! The puzzles aren't too hard for you to smash in your keyboard out of anger. There are some hard ones in between the easy ones though (took some queues from other gamers, because I just wanted to not stop the flow of the story for too long). "Shady Part of Me" is very forgiving when you fail as it offers you a rewind button (THANK GOD!) Platformers are usually not my cup of tea. I royally suck at those, but just as I loved "Gris" and "The Missing: J.J. Macfield and the Island of Memories" for the overall atmosphere, art and story, I instantly fell in love with "Shady Part of Me". Watching the trailer should already give you a little glimpse into what this game is going to offer to you. I've seen some people complain about how confusing the plot of the game is and well, while I do agree with them that the story isn't completely straightforward with you, I don't think it is too thin to get you properly engaged. The main characters often feel like a half-finished painting - enough there to make out what it could be yet still enough left out for you to turn it into your very own unique work of art. So many lines in the game resonated deep within me (the game comes with voice acting, too btw. - and I just LOVE the voice actors!). One other very noteworthy aspect: THE SOUNDTRACK! Honestly, listen to it, NOW! It's so beautiful. I just can't."I will be the flame. I won't flicker anymore. I will look inside and I won't mind what I see."If you are as most human beings and are currently struggling or have struggled with your life, with fear, anxiety and how to overcome the past for a brighter future, I think this game might be able to become something very special to you as well. Thanks for reading this and I wish you all the best!"I'm so glad that you were able to get there." "I can do this on my own now.""Yes, you can."
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Ok look. I really wanted to enjoy this game. The gameplay was engaging and the art was undeniably beautiful. But as for the story... I originally went in to play this game after hearing that it covered topics of mental health and recovery, but it was clear that the devs put very little research into it beforehand. In the end, it was poorly executed and even outright insulting at times.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game.The puzzles aren't too difficult, but I personally like that.I enjoy being able to take in what's around me.It feels like a combination of the Little Nightmares universe and Limbo, but something else as well that I can't put my finger on. Maybe Bendy and the Dark Revival with Alice in Wonderland?  Maybe Detention? I'm not sure.The graphics are gorgeous, absolutely love them.I'll update this when I finish the game.Update:It's still difficult to understand what the story being told here is, & what the game is trying to say.I unfortunately have to agree, for now at least, with some of the other reviews that this was a lovely concept, but feels a little confusing. If I'm getting it right, then it feels concerning... mental health-wise. (Coming from someone with mental health struggles)Am I not trying hard enough? Do I need to just give up?Am I supposed to trust everyone including people who've hurt me even when I'm not ready to?It is important to be willing to try, listen, breathe, & trust- but it's also good to know to take a break & communicate when something is too much for you or that you need time to be able to trust someone... especially if they've hurt you before.If that's what it's saying I can at least mostly agree, but if it's saying "just do better, smile more, blindly trust people" then... I can't. I can't go along with that.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: From the 2D/3D mechanics to the tranquil soundtrack, this game is a treasure. It tells a subtle story of mental health and what its like to struggle to improve along the way. The artistic style is a simply beautiful and thematic based on the part of the journey the game is alluding to. The puzzles are not overly difficult making this an appealing game for anyone looking to relate or just seeking enjoy to themselves.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Voice of an adult trapped in the shadow of a little girl. This is the basic premise of Shady Part of Me. A premise which lends itself well to very clever puzzle design, where you control two characters. A little girl who moves in 3D space, and a shadow on the wall who platforms in 2D space. In a clinical case of codependency, the girl must manipulate objects in 3D space to create platforms out of their shadows for the shade, while the shade must help cast shadows on the 3D space because the girl can't step into light. This makes for some very clever puzzles, though none that I found frustratingly hard. It helps that there is an instant rewind mechanic, so you don't have to start anything over if you fail. You just rewind a couple seconds.As the backdrop of this shadow play is stunning art design and a touching story, as the characters are having a constant dialogue as you progress. The levels are in a painterly style, and you see them get drawn in as you advance. The story, which is about mental health, never tells you directly what its context is, choosing to work in metaphors instead. I liked this, as it leaves itself up for interpretation, but it might be too vague for some. Especially the ending is left very open-ended, and I too would have liked something more definite, but it wasn't egregious enough to tarry the journey.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Shady Part of Me is a 2D (shadow) and 3D (the girl) puzzle game. Where you follow a little girl and her shadow. The game plays relaxed, the controls are simple and the puzzles aren't too hard, altough some will require some thinking. Visualy the game looks great, it has a bit of an watercolor paint feeling to it. A lot of the map is animated and makes the scene feel more alive.Storywise the game is a little slow with close to no event happing. But that's okey, the game is not about action. The story is about a mental issue, a traumatic event and girl following therapy sessions to help get out of it. What the issue or event really is the game does not say, it stays a bit vague. Perhaps that is to make it fit your own journey a bit more. Even if you never had something 'that' bad.Shady Part of Me is a simple, yet interessting little game.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: I can't remember the last time I played an entire video game in one day. (Didn't happen with Limbo, Portal, Portal 2, or Inside.) This game is just so damn elegant that I couldn't stop. The writing is solid (if obtuse, so that we never get real answers, but that's okay) and the puzzles are beautifully designed. There are checkpoints everywhere, and the rewind function means you never have to run it back too far. The voice acting is good, if not perfect (the girl's voice can be grating at times), and the music is superb. (When the paper boat shows up, oh my goodness.)The one complaint I have is about the kinds of puzzles we get in the final levels. The elegance breaks down in the last parts, and I found myself getting really annoyed. I wish the devs had stuck to the "less is more" approach so effectively used for most of the game. Instead, they kept adding ingredients until the soup tasted kinda nasty. Still, it's a fantastic experience and it's now on my "Best Platformers Ever" shelf, next to Inside and Super Meat Boy.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great short story, a bit more symbolic and allegorical than your typical game. It's basically Sadako, but wholesome and with a fear of light. The shadow acts like a platformer, while the girl acts as if you're in a puzzle setting. The two got together really well. The rewind mechanic helps if you make a mistake. You can rewind as far as you want, too. The puzzles are mindbending, but each mechanic is introduced in a way that's easy to understand... (mostly)The Artstyle is wonderful to watch, from environment to environment.I am not going to spoil anything, because this story is best experienced blind.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Shady Part Of Me is a really beautiful, artsy puzzle game, with wonderful musics, and a moving storyline (especially if you've ever come across self doubt and/or depression). The gameplay is quite basic, made successive puzzles based on light and shadows interactions. They are quite interesting with increasing difficulty, of course.  This game definately deserves to be played, so go ahead : it will be worth your while !
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game but it just didn't meet my expectations. While the game play was kind of cool at first, the puzzles became repetitive and the story was dull, somewhat annoying, and did not make complete sense. The graphics were cool and the 3-D atmosphere was nice but it still wasn't enough to make up for all of the downsides. It was a game that I couldn't wait to end.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely creative puzzles and fun throughout. Never once did I go "oh really? THATS how I was supposed to do it?" or "How was I supposed to figure that out?" yet alot of puzzles still had me scratching my head, trying to figure out how to get through everything.  The Light and Shadow mechanics are varied and interesting, and I never ran into an issue of the game breaking, glitching, or the shadows behaving in a way you wouldnt really expect them to, which is important for a game like this.  This is a very artsy game and alot of the imagery is clearly supposed to be symbolic of stuff, but even if you're like me, and analyzing this stuff isnt your cup of tea, I still think the game has plenty to enjoy.  I got the game on sale but I think this game would've been worth the money even if I did get it for the full price of 20$ CDN.  The puzzles itself were just that good for me, and if you DO enjoy analyzing stories like this, then its a must buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: I have completed my initial playthrough of Shady Part of Me, and while there were many brick shaped holes throughout, the ending hit like a ton of bricks, and whilst it hurts, in the good way, I now have a supply of bricks and can lay them around me in my second playthrough.Conveniently phrased paragraph aside, the game is downright gorgeous, in all regards, from visuals, to audio, the narrative, how that gameplay ties beautifully into the narrative, so on so forth. No gameplay felt forced, and no concept was any I found under developed, aside from a single system involving the Q key that I felt would be nice to have a bit more puzzles involved with it. Upon completion of the game, many things clicked into place, and other things were opened up to understand with another look at previous sections. The story is by no means unfleshed out or with holes that can't be filled in, it is merely a story that requires the player's caring to understand, which is to say, a very good story indeed. I highly recommend this game to anyone looking for a lovely 5 hours or so of a beautiful art piece in every way.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Wow.Just wow.This game is so creative and beautiful and the music is just hits different. The puzzles are quite easy but the story narrative is just amazing. I'm so surprised people haven't yet found this gem of a game yet.Buy it and you will not regret it.plus its 14$,stop tier 3 subbing to pokimane and get this gem
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: I think it's great so far! Obviously beautiful. You play as a shadow of a girl and a "regular" girl and flip between them to solve puzzles. _childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: While it is a short game, it has the perfect length for it's storytelling.The art and character design of this game, suits the narrative and the "situation" of the characters in the story,it illustrates the perspective and fears of the main character. Also, the soundtrack fits the atmosphere, and while it isn't to my taste it delivers what it is intended.The puzzles, they are great, you have to use your head on a few of them, especially if you aim for the Origami pieces, which I welcomed wholeheartedly.Overall, I recommend this game, for it is a short, fun, and interesting game that "explores" a little girl's state of mind.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best puzzle games i've played in a long time!And while i have seen other games of this genre explore the same idea of controlling a character that is just a shadow on the wall, this is certainly the best implementation i have seen of it yet. You have 2 player characters you can take control of.One moves in 3D space - the girl - who can only walk in the shadows, as she's afraid of the light, while her shadow can only move in the light and each puzzle makes use of both characters.And while the puzzles start out pretty simple and easy, they do add new mechanics into the mix as the game progresses.The puzzles are well thought out and have a pleasent difficulty to them. Most of the time the answer will be quite intuitive so you shouldn't expect to get stuck too much, though there's a few headscratchers that'll keep you trying out different ideas until you find the solution.While the game expertly uses it's light and shadow mechanics it can also shine on both the visual and audioside of things just as well.The 3D environments are beautifully crafted with detailed backgrounds, while the 2D-animations of the shadow character are also very well drawn.The music also is fantastic - especially since you have two seperate variations of a song playing depending on whether you are contorlling the girl or her shadow, which is just a beautiful little addition.The story is quite simple and you'll probably be able to guess what it is about pretty quickly, but it is still well presented by the characters' dialogue and underlined by the gameplay.I very highly recommend this game if you have any interest in puzzle games!
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game on multiple levels, and I think it is definitely worth playing if you enjoy an emotional narrative and a light puzzle platformer.  There are very few "timed" maneuvers and the few present I did not find difficult to manage. (And I am not a "twitch" gamer.)A recent highly rated "helpful" negative review said that the puzzles get repetitive.  I didn't find this to be so, at least not enough to suck the joy out of the game.  Up until the very last act, the game is introducing new elements to how puzzles work in every act.  Granted, there's a lot of box pushing and experimenting to figure out how all the elements are going to change the shadows, and it would have helped if what was going to happen had been more obvious.  But I generally found the puzzles engaging and did not find them routine or repetitive near the end.  The puzzles kept getting harder with a steady progression, and the new mechanic for the final act really kept it fresh.  And the rewind mechanism (vs dying and starting over at a checkpoint) makes experimenting very quick and easy.The actress' normal voice is lovely.  The child is... shrill. It took me awhile to get used to it, but it did stop bothering me.  And the reviewer noted above is right, she does get peevish and, well, childish.  Because she's a child, who is angry, and afraid, and just wants to be left alone.  It makes sense that she gets this way when her world view and what she sees as her safe space is challenged.  I felt the writers knew exactly what they were doing all the way through the end.Is this an accurate representation of someone struggling with anxiety or self-doubt?  No.  Is it an intriguing story, as a metaphorical representation of internal struggle?  Yes.  I think that's the important thing to remember... the game is not a representation of a real-world psychological healing process.  It's not meant to be, it's a game.  But as someone who _does_ struggle with some of the anxieties touched upon in the game (people watching me, not wanting to leave my "safe space"), I felt very connected to it.  And I felt seen by someone recognizing my difficulties.There are a lot of subtle touches of symbolism that are easy to overlook.  In the last act, pay attention to where the little girl can never go, but her "shadow" freely does... there's meaning in that.The art is amazing, there is so much detail going on.  The music is beautiful and supports the game very well.  I like how it subtly changes when you switch between the girl and her shadow.(If you have trouble following the written thoughts and knowing who is doing the thinking, pay attention to the fonts... each character uses a different one.  The little girl rarely uses punctuation.)
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: A good game I would recommend, the use of shadows, make for some unique scenery and puzzles. This doesn't save it from the puzzles being a bit too easy to figure out. But the game kept my attention by introducing new mechanics that were easy to understand until the final chapter. In regards to the story, I liked it reminded me a bit of inside and limbo, making not everything clear but leaving enough details to understand of what is going on.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: What a wonderful experience. This is why I consider games to be art.Beautiful art style and graphics, touching story and fun puzzles to solve. The difficulty of the puzzles is just right and you rarely get stuck. _childDocuments_.review: Shady Part of Me is a dreamlike audio-visual masterpiece, which despite its short duration, managed to leave an imprint on my heart forever. Like games that came before it, Shady Part of Me combines simple controls with satisfying puzzles. You control two dimensions; The girl, who exists in the physical 3-dimensional world, and her shadow, whom platforms away in the 2-dimensional world of shadows. By interacting with objects and lights in the 3D space, you create new shadows for the shade to progress forwards. What makes this interesting is how the girl cannot stay in the light, and the shade cannot exist in darkness. Simple, but proves to be very efficient. What grabbed my attention even before buying the game were the visuals. Being a massive fan of the Burtonesque style of impossible structures, gloomy color palettes and the beauty in the abnormal, Shady Part of Me just hit all of the right spots immediately. The landscape and puzzles working together to create mind-bending visuals with the gameplay was such a delight to see every single time. Symbolism oozes from every corner of the world, and the "dreamlike" quality is no joke. The world bends and transforms around you constantly, always keeping you on your toes. The mindscapes are beautifully crafted and sown together to form physical interpretations of psychological concepts and ideas.  Shady Part of Me also nailed the soundscapes along with the visuals. Hannah Murray's performance brought the characters to life, and the soundtrack blew me away the instant it started dancing along with the gameplay. Different levels would have their own themes, where the music would react to your progress, emotional distress and more. For every single piece there are two different versions, for the girl and her shade! Just how amazing is that?! The music, voice acting and visuals work together to immerse you into the world, accepting it as a new reality. It all works to elevate the thought progress when tackling the amazing puzzle designs the game has to offer. The progression of difficulty is very natural. At the start of the game, you're introduced to the weaknesses of both forms in a simple level. The library serves as a great visual anchor to ease into the mind-bending dream illogicality later, and also teaches the basic mechanics in an intuitive way. We also get some glimpses into the character's minds, and some pieces into the larger question of who we are and what we're doing. It's a strong start, and it leans great into what's to come. You're fairly quickly introduced to the rewind mechanic as well. As both forms of our protagonist have their own weaknesses that renders them in a state akin to death, not having to reload a save every time I accidentally turn on the lights is very helpful. Beyond my own stupidity there's also the question of general accessibility taken care of. Slowly, yet surely we dive deeper into the mind, and it shows. Generally the puzzles get more complicated, but there's some story beats and oddities that could bore someone who isn't interested in the story or themes. Every act introduces something new to play with, and I find it a very natural progression; Where you started out as just timing your runs right and walking in the shadows, by the end you are practically bending reality itself to create yourself a shadow bridge. It was always pure pleasure getting to know the new mechanics, and using that knowledge in the later levels to really get a sense of mastery over shadow and light. There are also the collectibles, the origami birds. They also exist in both worlds, and only the respective form of the protagonist is able to pick them up. They don't unlock anything beyond a few steam achievements and in-game puzzle pieces, but their placement made them very enticing to try and pick up. Most were placed somewhere along your route, where they would create an additional puzzle in the same level, just to collect it. With the additional voicelines and another piece towards a completed image puzzle, it was always very satisfying to get one. Not all of them were as interactive, as there were the ones just hidden off to the beaten path between the main game pieces. I managed to collect most of them as well through some simple searching. If you're going the collectivist route, I cannot recommend necturnal's origami guide enough. I don't think I could've ever even stumbled upon a couple of these damn birds. The story and themes of mental health are beautifully woven into the gameplay itself. Text will appear as you walk along, peering into the minds of the characters, sometimes accompanied by a voiceover for the two forms talking to each other. It's a style of storytelling I already fell in love with in my playthough of , and was overjoyed on the implementation done here. Like everything else, this text is often affected by light and shadow, twisting the words into new meaning or perspective. It often hints to an unreliable narrator, and it's done wonderfully with how the story unravels. The girl as a character is naturally written and believable, along with the shade and the  revealed later. It always feels rewarding to get a new peek into the minds of the characters, as they stumble across the themes of self-worth, fears and reflection. It's as promised; Emotional, thought-provoking and dream-like, and I believe the true experience is to experience it yourself. You have to untangle it personally to truly appreciate the message. Overall, I'd recommend this for anybody willing to take an emotional journey with a knack for some mind-bending storytelling and puzzles. The journey won't be long, but it'll be expensive unless you're buying it off of a sale. If you enjoyed games like , you will enjoy Shady Part of Me.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: It's a rather cute game with a tiny bit of lore. I really liked the gameplay, and I find the concept of playing both the little girl and her shadow to complete the riddles very fun. I also really enjoyed the art direction (this completely "paper" style of drawing is what made me want to discover the world of this game), and I liked the music too. So it's a simple game, not stressful, fairly easy and quick to finish but really enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game with an emotional story that I wasn't expecting. The voice acting is wonderful, the ambience is stunning and the mechanics and puzzles are clever and continuously evolving, adding new ways to play and figure them out. Some of the puzzles pushed me to think outside the box, but I never got too frustrated which was nice. The music and lighting is amazing, the characters are intriguing and I couldn't stop playing, always wanting to hear the next part of the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: I love puzzle games. I've played both In My Shadow and this, I like both, but Shady Part of Me is definitely better. The game is more fun, it has really good music, the art is really good. The fact that you control 2 separate characters, instead of just 1 (the shadow not simultaneously moving to the character, like in In My Shadow), makes the game have more potential for puzzles, and slightly harder and more interesting ones.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really beautiful production and even if either the art or music was the only redeeming aspect I still wouldn't be able to dislike it enough to give it a thumb down. I agree with other reviews though, that the story department is lacking and you crave much more development once you experience the incredible quality that the first hour of playtime offers. Instead, the middle part of the game severs the emotional connection that has been established and it misses the chance for a stronger impact at the ending. I would even say that if you removed half of the misleading and repetitive dialogue, it would actually do the game more favour and the ending would make a lot more sense. Anyway the puzzles were fun, the soundtrack was amazing and I would buy it again
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best puzzle platformers I've played. The puzzles kept evolving over time, and many of the in that perfect sweet spot of "I have to stop and think, but I do figure it out shortly and feel clever for it." The only one I got stuck on was the very last puzzle due to a newly introduced mechanic I didn't realize kept your orientation when you stopped using it. And if you're going to get stuck on a puzzle, the last one is the right place so I don't fault it. And as a bonus, I did enjoy the story, which was honestly surprising. with these sorts of games you come in with expectations. They're almost always about a girl with some vague mental illness or trauma coming to some vague terms with it after the world crashes around her, and almost always in the same way. they're an artsy color-by-numbers, and often act like they're revolutionary, looking at you Gris. I thought this one would fall prey to that, seemed to have the "small girl in a imagination world with some vague mental illness" vibe. While that's not neccessarily INACCURATE they legitimately do some new and interesting things with it. nothing revolutionary, but a solid story on solid gameplay is a thumbs up from me!
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: You play as a little girl and her shadow, who must work together to overcome various obstacles and solve puzzles in a surreal and dreamlike world. While the game initially seems reminiscent of other atmospheric puzzle-platformers like Limbo or Inside, but with the lack of horror or any dark atmosphere it feels really different to play.At the start, the puzzles can feel repetitive and unchallenging. The first two hours of this game were a complete drag for me of solving different variations of the same few puzzles over and over again. However, as the game progressed more and the difficulty increased, the puzzles became more imaginative and effectively utilized the mechanics available. I actually started to feel clever for solving them like you should do in any good puzzle game. The narrative got me interested at first but it felt like it was purposefully vague and barely developing, so I completely stopped caring after about an hour. With its amazing artstyle this game is a big disappointment with untapped potential and could have been something much more memorable than it is now.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely simplistic gameplay(can get repetitive), story about mental health(vague and open to interpretation) and one of the most soothing soundtracks I've heard for a long time(soundtrack is probably strongest aspect of game for me). Note that I got this from Humble Bundle and to be honest although I did enjoy this simple and relaxing puzzle platform game I can't justify it for the full Steam price unless you really like the genre. Would wait for at least 75% sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: If you played and enjoyed little nightmares, I would highly recommend this!
