The interactions of light and dark with shadows is definitely unique and felt fun along with the ability to chance orientations, but I won't spoil too much and would hope you all give it a go!
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't call it a captivating game. But it's an interesting one, nonetheless.The art style is beautiful, the gameplay is somewhat ok, the voice acting is.... good except one "half" of the little girl (can't tell if it's the shadow or the real one - I know, shut up) where the voice seems way too high pitch for the atmosphere of the game and the story, I'd say it's slightly above average.Overall, a good game for the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played very many games, the ones I have have been fantastic; but Shady Part of Me was a whole new level. The art was gorgeous, the gameplay was incredibly fluid and inventive (although I have yet to figure out how to get all of the birds), the story was mysterious and ultimately up for interpretation (within reason). I have nothing negative to say about this game, it was a beautiful experience that left me staring at the screen in wonder when it was over. I think this might be my new favorite game!
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this game from the start. The visual style and the creative ideas are impressive. I like the textual integration of the story and the tutorials into the levels. The game mechanics are flawless and it is neither too easy nor frustrating. You can always rewind time to retry. The only downside: The voice acting annoyed me a bit.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: A puzzle game following the recovery journey of a girl suffering from dissociative identity disorder.I was very impressed by the quality and care put into this game. A mixture of 2D platformer and 3D sidescroller the game reminded me a lot of Iris.Fall with its beautiful surreal aesthetic and shadow mechanics.I recommend it if you are interested in playing puzzle games based on light and shadow mechanics. It was a very smart and beautiful game to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best video game if you consider it based on the concept and the story. Shady Part Of Me, the game tells the story of a little girl who has on my guess a split personality where she is talking and following her shade, her shadow and her shadow is even replying to her. It is a puzzle narrative. The challenging levels with exquisite music and visual are mesmerizing on my experience. What I really liked about and I believe others will like about it too is the chapter concept, the voice that is following the girl. It is ordering it in the name of advice. Maybe through this game, we would allow ourselves to peek a bit in a child's mind and heart. Also how the authority is looking at her. Always "Judging". And the line "You've to try harder", "You are not trying hard enough" shows how authoritarian philosophy are there to steal away the innocence of a gentle hard who wishes to play, who wishes to dream big. Every action showed in the game can be interpreted in different layers and I would recommend it to everyone who likes to experience something out of the box.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: It's a decent puzzle game with a nice story. Unfortunately though, I did not enjoy most of the puzzles. They often felt more of a chore than fun and I found myself relieved after each one instead of excited for the next. That said, I actually think the puzzles were mostly well designed and the game had some fun and emotional moments. I'll probably never touch it again once I finish it (almost there) but the experience was not a regret either. Final score : 6/10. Get it if you like puzzle games and don't mind a story that unfolds at a very slow pace.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: I have to say I did not expect much from this. I got it from my boyfriend who just randomly got it somewhere and all he said was "It's similar to Little Nightmare" which we both love. And I was very positively surprised. I completely drowned in the game's atmosphere at the very end. The music is AMAZING. Suddenly my entire mind was occupied with solving all the puzzles, some of them indeed interesting. Thanks to the music part and mysterious story I would definitely recommend. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Shady Part of me is an amazing Puzzler that plays with perspective, light and movement in a way that is very unique, tought provoking, and a joy to experience, with new twists on this simple premise on every puzzle. To top it off, it has fantastic atmosphere, music and narrative, with every single element coming together to form an all around lovely, eerie, and amazing experience. This is a high recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: I was gifted this game a few days ago by a friend who saw it on my wish list. I started playing it yesterday and it captivated me so much that I finished it just today. It was a beautiful and immersive experience as you get used to the light and dark puzzles while trying to piece together the story with the music keeping you relaxed and entertain the whole way. I didn't 100% the game because I wanted to just lean back and enjoy everything.If you're a fan of puzzle games with interesting mechanics, a perplexing story, and beautiful music then I very much reccomend this game for you or a friend who is interested in those things as well.This game will have you solve questions of "How do I get her to the other side?" and have you leave with "How did she get here?" You will enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Impressive atmospheric game with quite unique artstyle, clever puzzles and intuitive gameplay. What really set it apart was the amazing music, really some outstanding stuff I didn't expect (seeing the game was only 2€). Definitely getting my hands on that soundtrack.Not much fed to you storywise, I assumed the kid has mental issues and got better? Ending was bit vague but that's what I figured happened.About 7 hours start to finish, maybe bit more if you want to get all the achievement (I couldn't be bothered as some of the puzzles are a tad annoying - clever but annoying).If you like Little Nightmares, Inside or Limbo (more names escape me atm) then you'll deffo like this, even though it has less action/story but the atmosphere is really dark at times (game is about mental health issues not baby eating fat people on a boat) yet still quite charming.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: These types of games are definitely a guilty pleasure for me. I really enjoyed this one and the puzzles never got too brutal (except maybe a few of the origami collectibles). The platforming is very reasonable as well. It's sorta like Limbo/Inside but a little more chill.The music... It's almost required that you have a decent sound system or headphones with good bass response.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't like the ending much but the rest of the game was absolutely incredible and touching. I have dealt with depression most of my life, many of those thoughts were relatable. It also made me think of someone that I've lost to depression not much time ago, he'd struggle to ask for help and accept it. He's alive though, our relationship didn't make it, lol But I believe he'll heal and find himself just like the MC did. Thank you for this game, I needed it. It has a place in my heart now.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: A relaxing intuitive puzzle.Not the best story, and the psychological message at the end seems less like a resolution, more like the development of an exhausting coping mechanism.  BUT its told well, and its a calming game with a really nice aesthetic. Possible spoiler below?? Its my perspective on one of the narrators by the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the concept but the story was VERY generic and even if it was a story driven game, they didn't give a lot of information that was needed to actually understand the whole storyalso controlling the characters felt wrong more times than I'd like toit was nice 4 hours but I would not pay full price (I did buy it on discount tho)
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Such a remarkable game. It has pretty graphics, beautiful, chill soundtrack which changes smoothly with your shadow or real form, emotional plot(&interactions between shadow, real form and the therapist) to which u can make theories, collectibles: origami birds which make a picture if all collected in a chapter and of course the best one: intruiging puzzles with new mechanics in every chapter,

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really well made game, a decent amount of content, not too hard, but challenging enough puzzles to keep you busy. I really like the rewind feature, it allows you to really deliberate the puzzles and not try and speed through them with irritation, as you never have to restart from the beginning. The story is well incorporated, it is dark and vague and leads the characters well, without the feeling of it being forced. That being said, I still couldn't tell you what the plot is meant to be, but maybe that is the point, it could represent a wide variety of emotional issues, making it feel relateable.The combination of 2D and 3D is really interesting and well made, especially the 2D physics later in the game. I'd love to see a second game, possibly 2 player.

_childDocuments_.review: Cool idea, beautifully made, but very boring to actually play. I'm not sure if there is supposed to be a story. It's all just generic, vague and emotional.You control two characters, a girl and her shadow. They pull levers and push boxes on buttons etc., in order to manipulate light sources and create a path for themselves and the other. However, you don't know what each button or lever will do until you try, and then you accidentally kill the other character, so you have to rewind. This is all very slow and tedious.There is very little puzzling challenge, because you end up doing random things and stumbling upon the solution even though you could have figured it out if you could remember what all the buttons and levers did. There are 98 collectibles, some of which are a bit challenging, but you'll miss some and then the game doesn't tell you which section to redo, just the general chapter.Overall it's very slow and vague, but it looks cool. So play it if you're into this vibe. If you like puzzle games, don't play this.

_childDocuments_.review: Even though Shady part of me is “just” a puzzle game, it had me hooked with its beautiful art style and different levels.SoundtrackThe game has a beautiful soundtrack, that I could listen to for hours on end. It is very relaxing to play this game.The voice acting is also quite cute. I liked the voice acting of (what I assume) Therapist best. It is such a calm and warm voice, so in my opinion a perfect pick!The voices of the protagonist and her shadow are nice too, but I gotta say that I found the protagonist voice at times a tad obnoxious (yes, the protagonist is probably a child, but the whining could get a tiny bit annoying)Game StyleI really like the 2D shadow concept with the 3D Character. It feels quite unique! There were several moments (usually near the end of a scene / act) where the game became a tiny bit cinematic. Especially the “scenes” with music were really cool!Game MechanicsSuper interesting concept of playing two characters at basically the same time! One is afraid of light, the other afraid of darkness. The game can get very challenging, but I am glad that the difficulty varies throughout the game, so it didn’t get too frustrating or too boring. From time to time, it could get difficult to play with a regular keyboard (especially while jumping with the shadow or walking the 3D figure through smaller paths, but nothing too big of the deal, just lagged once or twice). For some puzzles you really have to think outside of the box, and I figured out some puzzles just by sheer luck, but it was fun nonetheless.StoryI felt a little bit disappointed by the story because it is very open to interpretation what the unnamed protagonist is going through. The only thing I was certain off, was that the protagonist was visiting some kind of therapist to adapt to hear fear of light. It was difficult to understand where the fear stems from, why others are judging her (she could be schizophrenic) or why she needs to try harder. There are several unanswered questions; what does she need to train harder? Is her shadow a imaginary friend, a dead sibling/twin, an alternate persona? Is this game about the struggles of growing up? If you like these kinds of games, this might be for you then. For me personally, the story is a tad too weak to be able to stand on its own, but since you are focused on the puzzles anyways, it doesn’t impact the gameplay that much.CharactersThere aren’t many Characters in this game. The protagonist and her shadow, as well as the therapist. You can hear all three of them, but you only ever see the protagonist and her shadow. Other “people” are present as well, in form of some sort of wood mannequins. Apart from the protagonists love for books, not much is known about any of the characters. It is fine, since this game is mainly a puzzle game. But I found it a bit disappointing, since the game advertises itself as an emotional, touching story.SettingThe game takes place in an abstract world, which has insanely cool level designs! It was very fun to play most of the levels. I especially liked the Act 1: Fantasy and one of the levels in Act 1: Trapped (it had a boat scene with insanely cool music, that now lives rent free in my head :) )Overall, I recommend this game, if you are looking for a short game with a cool atmosphere and nice soundtrack to relax to and think outside the boy with challenging puzzles!

_childDocuments_.review: There's a distinction between being "original" and being simply "good." While The Shady Part of Me has garnered acclaim for its innovative approach, it falls short of excellence as a game. It's a decent puzzle-platformer, nothing more.In this game, you control two characters: a girl and her shadow. The girl navigates a 3D environment within shadows, manipulating objects but unable to jump. Conversely, the shadow operates in a 2D plane, capable of jumping but unable to interact with (most) objects directly. Both characters must work together, utilizing their unique abilities to solve puzzles. As you progress, new mechanics are introduced, predominantly for the shadow character, which adds complexity to the puzzles.The narrative remains elusive, leaving much to be desired. The story feels MIA (Missing in action), failing to captivate or engage players beyond the gameplay itself.The sound design and music are serviceable, albeit unremarkable. They provide adequate ambiance but lack the memorable qualities found in truly standout titles.Overall, while The Shady Part of Me offers an original concept, its execution leaves something to be desired. It's worth a playthrough for puzzle enthusiasts seeking a unique experience, but don't expect it to leave a lasting impression. This review was written with the assistance of ChatGPT.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm on the fence.Not 12/10, clearly, more like 5/10.Very tempted to put the thumb down, so call me generous on that one.Yes, the visuals are great. A gorgeous 3D world in sepia and blue, as you can see in the promotion material.What's not so obvious, unfortunately, is that a vandal then committed to write graffiti garbage all over it. The art is pointlessly damaged.Can't say if the culprit had to deface the music after that heinous act. It's very possible; the score goes from bland to slightly unpleasant, however not enough for me to turn it off.I don'r recommend the English voices. It's mostly fine, and I haven't checked other languages, however the chapter with the dispute is hardly bearable, what with the little girl constantly shouting and whining. Obnoxious. I had to take several breaks there.The voices and the graffiti are apparently meant to help telling a story. They fail. They detract.The story itself is nothing to gloat about. The little-girl-in-asylum cliche has long been beaten to death, especially in video games, and the artsy-fartsy route is the laziest to write. Still, it would have worked better in silence, as in show-don't-tell.As for the gameplay, the most important aspect of a game, well, the puzzles are mostly fine.Despite timers, which are balanced by a time-rewind mechanism.Issue #1: the better puzzles are the optional ones, i.e., catching birds as you advance, but you have to see them first. Puzzles are replaced by some hidden-object crap. I missed 15 with my eyes constantly peeled, and the thing is not good enough for me to go back and hunt for them.Issue #2 is the presence of long walking-simulator sections, with nothing to do but walk the distance, twice. Lazy. Cheap. Boring.In conclusion, it is still worth a watch despite the graffiti and the poor story. However, be prepared for some dull, if not annoying moments. It's a rather short game, yet I had to take 7 or 8 breaks before coming back to it. That's not what good games do.

_childDocuments_.review: Shady Part of Me is a puzzle game that I actually enjoyed. For the gameplay mainly though. The clever dichotomy between light and dark and the use of a 2D shadow and 3D player character made for some really fun puzzle solving. And especially so in the later levels with the shadow. The difficulty was perfect for me, too. As someone who isn't into puzzle games that much, I felt each puzzle was appropriately challenged to make me think but not to the extent that I wanted to frustratingly give up. There are additional collectibles to retrieve and these add some challenge. There were a large handful of those that I didn't manage to get so there's is more challenge for those who thrive on that.My biggest gripe with the game is it's story. I felt it was too abstract for me to make sense of it but then again I'm not a fan of abstract things. That being said, it seemed like the character was going through some sort of revelation by the end and the writer(s) wanted to convey some sort of meaning behind it all. I think the abstraction was meant for the player to impart their own conclusions and make it relatable. But I think they tried too hard to make it provocative and detached at the same time that it didn't really pack any punch.I felt by the end completely lost and at the same time a bit annoyed with this character that didn't really seem to do anything to gain this newfound lease on life. Maybe that's just me. That said, it was a wonderful platforming, puzzle game. So I would still recommend it to others if they were interested.As of this writing, Shady Part of Me is in the February 2023 bundle. _childDocuments_.review: Shady Part of Me is a great game, that sets itself apart from other works in the genre with an emotive identity all its own. Classically indie games in this style take a distinctly horror-focused approach to narrative, building up to scares and overwhelming the player with uncomfortable imagery, even when they aren't explicitly a 'horror game'. Shady however is a slower tale, starting with a more quiet sense of nervousness but working into something quite uplifting and triumphant. The puzzle solving suits it well - keeping you invested and complimenting the environment and story nicely - both characters actions helping the other. I really enjoyed this game and strongly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: A game which throws together moody music, an enigmatic but pointless story and profound-sounding put shallow dialogs. You'll have your conflict between the protagonists, which goes like "I like rubberducks!" - "What? How dare you calling this weather nice?", then the phase of consolation and understanding (like "I figure you did some good work." - "That's why beer's best served cold") and - to finish the worn-out trope - the phase of self-awareness and self-empowerment: "Nobody watches us. We are at a stage. They see us how we see us." (this example with it's randomness and inner contradiction is not even made up).In the end, I had no clue where all of this was coming from, no clue what the problem was to begin with, and no clue how it got resolved in the end - and I figure neither had the writers. It's been a while since I've played a game whose story is so incoherent and lackluster at the same time.The puzzles are alright, I guess. Puzzles aren't really my cup of tea, but most of them felt fair, and most of them could be solved with a minute of thinking. At the beginning I tried to collect all available doodads (which made some puzzles harder), but towards the end I just wanted to get it over with.The English voice acting for one character was abysmal, so I switched over to German after half of the game. I understand that both characters are supposed by be voiced by the same person, but they really didn't do themselves a favor with that decision.

_childDocuments_.review: Very artsy, very slow, very boring. All that for 15 bucks. You control a girl in a semi 3D side scrolling space. And you switch to your shadow on a 2D plane. The idea isn't half-bad. Both characters need to help one another out, so both can reach the next checkpoint. Along the way you have "paper birds" to collect for no real reason. Each bird reveals a puzzle piece for the respective chapter, presenting you with a picture, if you can gather enough ... but that's about it.The game is very slow and floaty. The graphics aren't anything to write home about. The music is very ethereal and relaxed. Like a bit of whispy lounge music. The character voice is grating. And the message is apparently clinical depression or sth like that. For a child. Well, okay. It's a sad child. And people are judging her, not believing in her, etc. Probably an orphan. I don't know. I have no desire to see the rest of the story, because the gameplay is simply very simplistic and slow. You walk from left to right, flip a few switches, push some boxes, and wait for the light to go away, so you can pass.I doubt there's much more that will happen. If there is I'm too bored to play a few more hours to find out. I just can't imagine that there's anything amazing coming down the line. If you're just in it for the story and the visual presentation, go for it. But I'd grab it during a sale. And wouldn't expect too much.

_childDocuments_.review: The game concept reminds me of Fireboy and Watergirl and Epistory alike (with the words appearing on the walls and floors). I like the art design, the music is okay (though nothing that stuck to my memory) and the voice actress does her job well.So far so good.The story? Which story?You are thrown right into the prelude of the game and don't get any background info (I would have liked to know: who's the girl, when and where is she?). It's like a confrontation with an emotional struggle but you are kept in the dark (haha, see what I did there?)The game mode is straightforward, move around, jump, avoid the light.There's a lot of waiting:- you have to move both the girl and her shadow, that means, one has to wait while the other is moved.- you have to time your movements in order to avoid the moving lights. Just missed the perfect moment? Then wait something more until the next one appears.- there's no way to fast forward to reduce the waiting time.I wish there was a multiplayer mode, the game would be so much more fun playing with a friend.Like this it's... tiresome and boring. I would have liked to love the game, but I just lost interest.

_childDocuments_.review: In a nutshell: "Take time to let your soul catch up" The developers of Shady part of me took this phrase to a new level, and delivered splendidly.The graphics are somewhat dark, but that actually reflects pretty well the emotional turmoil you will experience whilst playing. And believe me, the turmoil won't derive from neither difficulty, nor stress which is often found in platformer games.Take your time with this game, too. I did, and I can say it certainly is not a piece of art to be played with one sitting. Ponder on it. Think about it. Reflect on it. And get the origamis on your way, don't leave them behind. Leave time to seek them, figure them out, and who knows, maybe your soul will catch up with you in the meantime :)

_childDocuments_.review: [Please note this game does describe themes of childhood trauma, please only play if you are mentally in a good place. Recommend playing with headphones on for a more immersive experience-if you enjoyed Contrast, you may enjoy this game, it is a bit darker and more physiological but it has the shadow aspect seen in Contrast.]What a beautiful and an absolutely incredible game...the storyline, gameplay, mechanics and soundtrack all flowed so well to create this truly amazing game. This was my first time playing "horror" game and I am definitely not a fan of horror but it was definitely a lot more physiological...it felt a little bit like a cosy game in terms of the you could play this game as your own pace and you were able to visit parts of the map again to finish achievements without having to restart it.The puzzle aspect of the game, I did better than expected with this, as I'm not really a fan of games where puzzles are the main mission or genre of the game but I really enjoyed this one; I think as well being able to play as the "shadow" character as well, this definitely helped me feel more comfortable playing a puzzle game, as you were able to switch between two characters and play the game a bit more while you figured the puzzles out.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: I read a negative review about how this story fails to deliver story-wise, as a narrative-driven game, and I agree. It feels like the struggle the girl is going through changes abruptly going from each act to the next, without there being any connection, so they feel very disjointed. The ending doesn't do anything to fix that either and doesn't do anything to answer any questions you might have, outside of how the girl finally decides on how to deal with all her struggles  The reason why I will leave it a recommendation however is that I think that overall, it's not an actually bad game. The music seriously carries it, with BEAUTIFUL soundtracks that really match the atmosphere they're trying to set in each stage. The voice acting is also nice and adds to the experience and the narrative of the story quite smartly. The art style is gorgeous, especially the transition in the starting scene and the watercolor filters. The puzzles were quite fun to solve, not too hard (apart from a couple at the end that need some guess work), not too easy for the most part.So all in all, while at the end of the game, I did feel a bit disappointed with the story, it was a good experience. I would recommend the game on sale (I believe at current time full price is 15 euros which I would say feels little much due to its shortcomings).
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant puzzle game which focuses on atmosphere building and storytelling, even though the story of shadow is a little vague, but it doesn't make it less attractive. It appears to be about the girl's relationship with her shadow, their emotion and weakness.The puzzles are quite intuitive, we can solve them basically following our first impression and thought, but I don't think its ease hurt the fun of gameplay because the graphics, sound and story, all well mixed within the game, when the clues are apparent, I can enjoy other aspects as well. Besides, there are still some interesting designs concerning light and shadow, cooperation between different dimensions. The pace of difficulty change is great, there is no burden or boring moments for me.Minor Problems.1. No restart for current puzzle, rewind is convenient but slow for long operation.2. Character switch is not obvious.3. Voice language other than its local French is not good enough, like English and Chinese.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a situation where I wish there was a neutral option for reviews, since the game isn't , it's just flawedWhile I did enjoy my first playthrough, finishing off the 100% however gave me a better image of the game as a whole- The visuals are nice- The story is very vague, and is left so open that unless you are willing to actively fill in the gaps, you will be left guessing what it was about- The gameplay is fairly slow, it's fine go to through once, but after you've already done a section, repeating it feels annoyingly sluggish- The collectibles are not particularly fun, with many of them hidden completely out of the regular bounds of the camera without even the slightest indication- The game is very short, even with it's slow gameplay you will finish a playthrough in about 2-3 hours- The overall gameplay concept was interesting as well, so it is a shame they didn't explore it muchIf you plan on getting the game I would wait for a saleI likely would've felt ripped off had I paid full price, instead of receiving it for free

_childDocuments_.review: I have a bit of a love/hate with this platformer. It’s an interesting game where you play both a girl and her shadow. The girl can’t stand to be in the light and the shadow can only exist in the light, so you lose if the girl gets trapped in the light or if the shadow gets trapped in shadows (or hits shadowy brambles, or gets squished between shadows). There is clearly a psychological story being told here, however, unlike Gris this one is extremely unclear and is bogged down with dialogue that feels unnecessarily vague and flowery. For the most part I enjoyed the puzzles, but got very irritated as the game dragged on without answering ANY questions. I had no idea what The Shady Part of Me was trying to convey by the end. Even so, it was fun to play through once.

_childDocuments_.review: The art style is unique and attractive. The puzzles, which play with light and shadow in interesting ways, are largely intriguing and vary from pretty easy to a bit harder than average -- I think they miss the sweet spot in terms of difficulty by just a smidge; the puzzles are on average a bit easier than those in comparable games, which is absolutely fine, but if you're like me, you're not likely to feel particularly smart or accomplished after solving them. They're not childishly easy, but nothing struck me as all that challenging, either.The place where the game was lacking for me was in the story, which is very abstract and honestly, to me, pretty much incomprehensible.There are essentially three speaking characters. Two have the voices and attitudes of a grown woman (who appears as a shadow and appears to be afraid of the dark) and a little girl (who appears more fully formed and is afraid of the light). But even though one is clearly adult and one is clearly a child, they both appear to be children of approximately the same size on the screen. It is sort of vaguely suggested that they are maybe two parts of the same person, or that one is a grown version of the other, or that one is the "inner child" of the other ... basically, the game never really says.The third character, meanwhile, is a disembodied male voice (he does not appear on screen) who appears to adopt the role of a really condescending doctor or therapist. The little girl seems to hate him, and honestly I can't really blame her. He's full of platitudes and "encouragement" that comes off more as belligerent criticism. If this game is some sort of meditation on mental illness, as some have suggested, I can't imagine a more useless care giver than the one in this story.Finally, as the story progresses, there are more and more references to being "on stage;" in fact, the story's last act (yes, they are called acts) literally takes place on a proscenium stage with a (mostly silent) audience in the background. So are we using stage fright as a metaphor for fear of revealing your fully-formed self to the general public? Beats me. Maybe. If that's what the story was saying, again, it doesn't say it particularly well.Now, to be fair, I bought this game at 80% off, which means I paid all of three bucks for it. For that price, any competently executed series of puzzles would be more than my money's worth, and so on balance, I'm recommending this game. But play it for the puzzles. The narrative is ... well, kind of a jumbled mess. Maybe I'm just stupid, or maybe the game makes more sense in French, or makes sense if you're taking mind-expanding drugs. To me, it's clear I was told some sort of story, but I have no idea what that story was.

_childDocuments_.review: 2D walking simulators seem to be a whole new genre of their own, are more interesting, and tend to be better than fully 3D ones. Games like Limbo, Little Nightmares, and Inside are perfect examples of this. There is some light platforming, some puzzle solving thrown in, and maybe a little bit of stealth. While none of those had stories that blew me away, they did make up for it in atmosphere and character. Shady Part of Me sadly doesn't accomplish any of those things. The only thing going for it is the dual-character puzzles, and that's about it. There really isn't even a story to speak of. Yourself, your shadow, and some disembodied voice narrate the entire game with cryptic dialogue that really is either open for translation to the player or is entirely meaningless.This game reminds me a lot of Limbo and Lost in Shadow. You play as a little girl in a white dress who is afraid of light, and her shadow (always on the wall) is afraid of darkness. You switch between both to help each other advance. Puzzles involve pushing boxes and pulling switches, and in later levels, your shadow can defy gravity and even take over puppet bodies. Most of the puzzles have that "Aha!" moment, which can be satisfying, but there were a few that really stumped me and took a lot of time just fiddling around until something changed. Most puzzles have you manipulating objects in front of lights to make new shadows, move them, or make them grow or shrink. The real girl can't jump, but your shadow can. This means there is light platforming in the shadow, but nothing complicated.I did find the aspect of two characters to be a bit tedious. Some areas just have you running to the right to stop in the circle to advance to the next area. You then have to switch to the other character and run that full length again. It's not a major problem, but it happens too frequently. I also found the rewind feature to be really handy. This prevents constant deaths and restarts. You can rewind as long as you want, so I have to applaud the developers for making this a frustrating mess. A lot of times your shadow will die or you will get caught in light, and it stops the game, but rewinding allows you to see the error you made and correct it. If you fully died every time and went back to a checkpoint, this game would be unbearably frustrating.Overall, the visuals are great. The sketchbook look and early 20th-century aesthetics are fun, but they're also nothing memorable. We've seen this kind of art style before in other games. That's the biggest takeaway from Shady Part of Me. It does what it does fine. Nothing more, nothing less. It doesn't leave a lasting impression like the above mentioned games. Limbo was gruesome and had a memorable atmosphere. Little Nightmares' ghoulish monsters stood out, and Inside's dystopian world put you on edge. You will spend around five hours in this game and mostly forget about it the next day.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Shady Part is a 2D/3D platformer game featuring three unique characters who communicate with each other: a little girl named Alice, her Shadow, and the Doctor who guides her on her journey in this well-designed game. Without giving away any spoilers, I found the atmosphere, controls, soundtracks, cartoony graphics, and puzzles to be perfect. I would even go so far as to say that this game has one of the best video game soundtracks imaginable. However, I have two minor issues with the game. Firstly, there is no support for macOS, nor is there cloud gaming, as mentioned on SteamDB. Nevertheless, this is not a significant issue for me, so I can overlook it. Secondly, there is a lack of storytelling in the game, if it's fair to say so, because the game doesn't effectively explain what is happening to Alice and other aspects of the plot. I have a couple of theories about this: either Shady Part took the same approach as SUPERHOT and allowed players to form their own theories about the story (which is a positive thing, don't get me wrong), although I'm not entirely sure because in earlier builds, Alice was designed to have schizophrenia. Alternatively, my second theory is that since this game was initially made for a "Game Jam" (if I recall correctly) and took four years of development to release, the developers may have struggled with developing a cohesive story but included elements that could be interpreted as storytelling. I'm not entirely sure which theory is true, but regardless, I've explained why I love this game so much and why it is my all-time favorite video game ever, yet at the same time, I can't help but feel bad because of how underrated it is. Despite its brilliance, it seems to have slipped under the radar for many gamers, which is unfortunate considering the amount of effort and creativity that went into its development. However, I find solace in knowing that those who do discover it are in for a truly memorable experience.A must-have experience for everyone. Can become 2 dollars in discounts. ten out of ten

_childDocuments_.review: This game's music score is by far one of its best qualities, and perfectly carries the melancholic mood on its own. The audio mix and instruments change noticeably when switching characters, and both versions are always exceptionally enjoyable (in and outside the game).Voice overs are a different matter. Mop hair girl is clearly voiced by an adult doing a forced nasally high-pitched impression of a child. So grating it prompted me to switch to French audio, where the actress does a more convincing interpretation. Shadow girl sounds like an adult and thus more natural.The game looks good, with a sort of inky paper vibe and slight color variations throughout giving it a generally monochromatic bent. It features several pretty nice environments, but like the story they seem assembled from common boilerplate parts without a flavor of its own. It wastes no time turning supernatural, with dream-like scenes and impossible situations that still make sense within their context.The main child character must avoid lights as she navigates through the 3D environment, while her detached shadow counterpart must stay within the light on 2D platforms mapped over the world. Very simple controls, walk, jump, pull switches, push crates, etc. Switch between characters to guide them both to safety. Move objects in the real world to affect shadow world, changing perspectives. Rewind time to correct mistakes.Puzzles are divided in small segments with two finish circles for both characters. Few sequences require precise timing and jumps but the experience is decidedly more cerebral than reflexive.It all feels clever, intuitive, and rarely intellectually taxing. There's a decent amount of content and a few new elements over time that prevent the basic concept from going stale.Collect optional origami birds. Quite a few are easy to miss if not explicitly searching for them, and there's no apparent reward for finding them other than a few additional audio quips.Words everywhere contribute to the uneventful story, along with exchanges between the child and her shadow. Overdrawn exposure to the same themes don't really evolve and remain vague, even repetitive, about overcoming inner fears, being hurt by others and trying to fit in, and constantly trying to find the exit. There's a therapist intent on being right and wanting the player to try harder, a host of clichés and abstract symbolism, but never really anything detailed and without significant reveals. Overall, it feels written by someone inexperienced in mental health issues or proper storytelling, despite having a very relatable base.I liked Shady Part of Me for its soundtrack, general mood, reflexive and clever puzzles and would easily recommend it to players looking for a chill time.

_childDocuments_.review: Shady part of me is a pretty good puzzle platformer with creative mechanics, a great artstyle and brilliant voice acting. As is the case with most puzzle platformers you play these games for the namesake of the genre, namely puzzles. Here the shady part of me really delivers with TONS of unique puzzles that use a handfull of innovative mechanics involving shadows and controling two characters at once. There's some real headscratchers in there, but none of them feel unfair or painfully require trial & error. Creativity and thinking outside of the box is needed to progress and is rewarded in many optional collectibles, which push the puzzles that little bit further!The art is great in more ways than one. Not only is great to look at, but it also clearly defines each puzzle and what your options are. Important elements pop out and most of the time you can quickly get an idea of the outlines of a puzzle at first glance. There's many diverse areas and even though the colour pallette is limited, there's still great variety. The accompanying music does the job well enough but doesn't stand out like the visuals do. What does stand out though is the voice acting. It utterly captivated me from start to finish, and while the finale wasn't what i had hoped for i still liked the narrative journey. The story, just like the gameplay, shakes things up enough to remain interesting throughout.Despite all that though, the game's lenght was a bit too long for my liking. i know many people would prefer as many hours of gameplay out of their buck as possible, but for me there's a sweetspot of around 3-4 hours for these types of games. So while shade part of me overstays that by quite a bit, it never managed to lose it's appeal. It's a well made, engaging and polished product that can be played by anyone and should be played by every puzzle enjoyer. It's price is fair and the sales go deep so pick it up whenever you are itching for another puzzler.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Solid puzzle-platformer where you switch between a girl who can move in 3D (but can’t jump) and her shadowy 2D-platforming counterpart. Maybe slightly longer than it needed to be, and the difficulty curve is a bit out of whack (the puzzles steadily ramp up in challenge for the first two acts, then get much easier for a longish stretch before ramping back up again in time for the end), but a strong execution of this concept overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game in 2 sessions and I loved every second of it, the collectables where not neccesary for the end but I collected them for the fun of the challenge of the puzzels. the mechanics are simple but can go deep.the visuals where also very nice, the story can be confusing if you don't pay attention and fill in the blanks. my interpretation of the story might be different than an other person might perceive.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Players control 2 characters: The Girl and her shadow, reminds me of Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons. The game offers a unique puzzle-solving experience with its clever use of light and shadow that can be called as "Puzzles light and shadow", with dual-world gameplay: The Girl exists in a 3D world & her Shadow in a 2D world, it's adding complexity to the puzzles & that is something new for me.Each stage presents its own challenges that I never get bored. I was surprised by the puzzle-solving mechanics in Act 3 and Final Act. The game introduces a rewind time feature, allowing players to help through all situations (so no game over). It took me around 8 hours to finish the game & it's possible to collect items in a single playthrough (the rest is just idling for trading cards).I think the story is open to interpretation. I viewed it as The Girl having a mental illness (possibly a split personality) which is proven by the padded walls in "Trapped Session" and how the world looks like a hospital, inside of it there is a therapy room, the yellow subtitle is sound like a therapist telling The Girl to breathe and trying to persuade her, and the use of "Sessions" instead of stages.At the end of the game, her medicine working, The girl and her shadow become one and The Girl accepted her acceptance. One theme I noticed is The Girl's fear of light. Not just "light", but something else like afraid of being watched by people (spotlight).
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Both soundtrack and especially story are indeed of rare beauty, in lifetime it is rare that I ever felt so understood by any medium. It took me on a wonderful journey of sadness and sorrow with a glimm of hope and light between the darkness. It is something u should take time for and experience on ur own in a quiet place. It is worth the way, it is to become a stunning journey
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: So... this game is something else. Much as I did enjoy it, this is one of those that are a damn bother to write a review for as it'd spoil the whole if one were to discuss the story... So I'll just say that in Shady Part Of Me, you control two characters. A little girl deadly afraid of light and her shadow who needs light to exist. Working together they must solve puzzles in 3D, 2D and even some 2.5D environments to make it to the end of the game. Along the way you must collect origami's (paper birds and their shadows), but getting all of those is very hard. Much like later puzzles. Visually, the game is gorgeous in a sense, but what colour is there is muted and the atmosphere is melancholy. I'd definitely recommend the game though, but . Go and experience it.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really beautiful and has a whole lot of potential, it's creative and the puzzles are done wonderfully, however i just couldn't enjoy it after the first few sections of the game. I'll explain it quickly without any spoilers but basically it feels as if it is trying to be moving and emotional, but is actually very shallow and there's not much to go off if you're looking for the story behind it (very standard in other words). It is boring and repetitive. ((((spoilers ahead)))) It starts of wonderfully, introducing our characters and teaching us how they can work together to complete certain puzzles, and introduces the idea that one can not step on shadows, and the other can not step into light (I don't know if this is true as i haven't looked up any theories into the game or done much research so this is all based off of what i gathered from playing the game, but to me it felt like the shadow was an older version of the human girl, so i'm going to refer to them as the same person). It is very fun for the first little while, but i very quickly felt as if the same message was being pushed over and over again, not just the same story for it could have spent the time slowly revealing more and more about the girl, but it just doesn't? i played this game for 7 and a half hours and i still feel as if i know nothing about this girl.  I have no emotional connection to her at all. In fact i didn't like any of the characters at all. The text on the walls and voice of who i assume to be her therapist is a nice touch, but very quickly it just feels like the same thing over and over just reworded, and you can imagine how boring that is after 7 hours. I was mostly disappointed by the ending, I found myself forcing to play this game to get it over and done with in hope that it would give me something worthwhile at the end, but i didn't. By my understanding the two combined maybe into her modern day self, someone who is no longer afraid of light. Then that was it. no cool ending cut scene, no emotional dialogue... she just walks up to a swing, touches it, then walks out of the cameras view. How disappointing. Apart from that there's not much more i can say about this game, which is the worst part. If someone where to ask me what happened in this game and what it was about, i think i could summarise in a small paragraph. There were emotions in this game, but when they were shown (such as anger) there felt no reason or warning behind them, and just as quickly they disappeared. I'm sure there was more to this game, but with just playing it it is not worth it, and i hate it but i just can't recommend it. It just doesn't give you enough to go off and is extremely repetitive. Sure, give it a go if it's on sale, but if you find yourself in the same position as me and are forcing yourself to finish it, just watch a play through.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: The artistry, atmosphere and ambiance are what sells this game. The gameplay is engaging at first, slips into boredom during Act 2, then picks back up in Acts 3 and 4. The puzzles were reasonably challenging.This game is yet another great example of games as an art form, and for that I give it a recommend. It's definitely something that you can look back on thanks to its unique style.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: I feel somewhat bad giving this a downvote cause objectively, I don't see this as a bad game, but for me, it just doesn't click. Seems to me like a game that should have been two player to alleviate having to control both characters through their own sections and puzzles. and the puzzles themselves, as far as I've played, didn't evolve much to keep the play time interesting. This all could be forgiven if the story kept me engaged, but that too lacks as I'm really just not interested in trauma stories anymore. Call me cold, but it feels to me like if you've seen one, you've seen em all, though that may just be because the narrative in shady is surface level, so there's not really much to delve into and thus make the personal story more interesting.All in all, subpar if you have any real experience playing games like this, but okay if this is a first dive. Maybe it evolved more later on, but I just didn't have the patience to stay for what didn't sell me much to begin with.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: I got this bundled with other games.Not the worst puzzle game that I got the chance to play, not the best.Definitely would give it more of an average rating if I had the option.Shady Part of Me is an indie puzzle game that relies heavily on implying events that took place and leaving a lot to the judgement of the player. It's the type of game where different players are prone to understand the same event in different ways. It explores themes such as mental illness & loneliness. Sadly the writing isn't as clever as I would've liked so it's safe to say the story isn't even the main attraction of this game. We have this 3rd party that chimes in and pushes you to go forward and to be better, do better, he seems to be the voice of a psychologist trying to help you but it feels off. When talking about mental health in general things aren't as black and white as "just do it." This would've been a good occasion to have him offer more background about the girl and the conflicts that take place in her mind. The puzzles themselves start off easy and get moderately difficult later but until the end of the game you keep doing more or less the same types of puzzles, rehashed. Art wise and OST wise this game offers a melancholic feel, the aesthetics are washed out yet warped at times.If you're an aficionado of the genre there's not much for you here, I would feel a bit sorry if I spent 15 euros on this game. If you got it in a bundle or at a sale sure, give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't that good or that bad either.The game mood is quite boring, everything has very slow progress. It doesn’t have any climax moment that gets me excited at all. Some mechanics might look interesting at the beginning when they show up but after that it’s repeated. The ending is quite disappointing, I believe that it has many other ways to present a better ending than this.Anyway, how they design the map and place the bird are quite impressive. They don’t keep it from an unseen location and most of them have a hint that it has a bird nearby. I finished this game without encountering any bugs. The controls when you get rotated in shadow characters are great and make it less confusing. I can feel the effort they put behind the scenes so that is why I can’t dislike this game.If you ask me to recommend a game in this genre, this game might not be in the top list. But if you ask me, is this game worth trying? Definitely yes :)
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Shorter game with fairly easy puzzles, that get a litle tricky at the end. It got a nice, but minimalistic artstyle. The mainattraction here is the music and the voiceacting (english and german), that indirectly tell you a story throughout the game. It also got a little surreal (twisted) surroundings, which are also good.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: A really good puzzle game.  Without spoiling too much, the concept of mixing 2D and 3D is great, and puzzles introduce new mechanics throughout the game, keeping the whole game interesting.  Very good graphics, with a somehow sad mood that fits the game really well.  I liked how some levels have an Escher like design.  Rewind mechanism is just perfect: the game will never punish you for trying something.  The game will take you about 5 hours to finish, with some replayability if you want to find every single secret.  The only aspect I disliked was the voice narration: I ended up lowering the volume as it felt too invasive to me.An awesome game from a young studio.  I can’t wait to see what will come next.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Shady Part of Me is a masterpiece that came out of nowhere. It might not be as entertaining as a AAA for some, but it is an experience, an amazing one.The music, the mood and the graphic style are creating an experience unique to this game.This is definitely not objective, but it's worth a 10/10.Amazing work Douze Dixièmes ! Continuez comme ça !
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Shady Part of Me is a great 2D/3D puzzle platformer that feels like a combination of LIMBO and Little Nightmares.You control two characters: a little girl moving in a 3D environment and her shadow moving on 2D surfaces. In order to solve the puzzles and move forward, the two protagonists have to work together and help each other out.The difficulty curve is good, with the game starting with some pretty easy puzzles (and platforming), which gradually get harder and harder. There is also an extra incentive in the form of origami birds that you can collect throughout the game, but getting them can be quite challenging.I don't want to give any spoilers for the story, but it's pretty good. I like the games that, instead of telling you directly what's happening, make you learn about the story through the environment and the dialogue between the characters.The art direction in this game is superb, and the music complements both the visuals and the situations the characters find themselves in.An easy recommendation for anyone looking for a good puzzle platformer with great visuals and a backstory.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing and for the 2 reasons of it having interesting and fun mechanics whilst having a deeper story underneath as you follow a little girl who's been bullied into the shadows and i didn't play much for the soul purpose that im just not in the mood for this type of game right now but when i am i will be excited to grind it out and get more entangled with the story
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: this game is incredible, its simultaneously whimsical and childlike, while also being deeply profound and haunting, becoming even more so as you progress and piece together whats actually going on. the puzzles are fun, and its really interesting switching between 3D, and 2D styles to interact with objects differently.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Great puzzle game with a narrative that's touches upon a touchy subject. I like games that these types of risk with their story. For me, the most engaging part of the game are the puzzles, which are unique and progressively challenging. The rewind mechanic is a great touch and eases the frustration of getting through some of the later puzzles. The amount of narration was a bit much at times, but I would love to see more puzzle games like this in the future. Definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: I really thought this game had potential to become my #1 favorite story game. The first 30 or so minutes felt one of the most unique gameplay I had ever experienced in a narrative game but soon I realised how repetitive it is. The puzzles are quite simple, only a few are somewhat difficult. Still, the game felt fun throughout the 10 hours I spent on this.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: A Shady Part of Me is a short yet sweet game about internal conflict and outgrowing past traumas. It a mix of 3D and 2D gameplay to show the counterparts of this conflict in a beautiful and atmospheric scenery. The puzzles and platformer aspect of the game are nice and with a good balance of difficulty to keep the game casual and history focus.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Shady Part of Me is a very beautiful and artistic puzzle platformer that reminds me of little nightmares, before I get into the story, the story is extremely vague, so it’s hard to talk about it but basically you play as two girls trying to escape.Okay let’s talk about the likes, the gameplay was very good it is your standard puzzle platformer but with some twists like in the game you can play as a three-dimensional girl and a two-dimensional shadow girl each needing the other helping with puzzles and getting through areas as the shadow girl cannot survive in darkness, while the three-dimensional girl can’t survive in light. I found that to be quite an interesting concept.The puzzles for the game are quite good, very fair and but not overly hard that you'll be stuck hours and hours trying to figure out the answer, I mean maybe you'll be stuck on one or two puzzles but you'll eventually figure it out.The graphics are really beautiful very well detailed with plenty to see and gush at; the 3D world and the 2D world both look really beautiful. The levels for the game are very good, diverse with plenty of unique locations and a lot to see. The atmosphere for the game is very good it's sort of feels like a less scarier version of a little nightmares, this game being more fantasy with little touches of horror then straight up horror like little nightmares had. I like collecting all those little origami birds and getting a picture from it, the pictures were really nice and could make for some nice wallpaper.Okay let’s talk about the dislikes, the story for the game can be very vague I think it's about overcoming mental illness, but I'm not entirely sure. The voice acting for the game is I don't know it’s not that good, I mean no offense to the voice actors they did a good job it's just I feel like they were the wrong kind of people to voice the characters, like take the little 3D girl’s voice she sounds way too screechy and whiny I know she's supposed to be a little kid. But I don't know I feel like they could have gone with a less screechy voice and more like sweet sounding.The narrator for the game also feels like his voice doesn't fit, I mean he sounds good but his dialogue kind of makes him sound like the bad guy, although that could be a narrative point of the game but I'm not entirely sure.Okay then Shady Part of Me is a very beautiful and artistic puzzle platformer that reminds me of little nightmares, it has very good game play, quite good puzzles and really beautiful graphics, so if you're looking for an interesting puzzle platformer with some beautiful graphics and you don't really mind a vague story this game is for you so I definitely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet puzzle game that works a lot with light and shadows. Puzzles were not unfair, mostly the solution is pretty easy to find, or you just have to think outside the box for a minute. The story is some weird psychological stuff about being true to yourself, I didnt pay attention much, but the gameplay is fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: 'Shady Part of Me' is a beautifully drawn puzzle-platform game with an interesting gameplay. Throughout the dreamy story you have to guide a little girl and her shadow, both afraid of the light, through various mazes, puzzles and riddles and get them to work together.I can only recommend this little game, it's been fun to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Beginning half of the game :DSecond half of the game :(Game starts off great but the story falls off hard.  I was fully invested for the first half but I kinda stopped caring towards the end but maybe that's just because the story didn't go in the direction I wanted it to.  Some of the puzzles are a bit repetitive (although I liked how each act kinda had it's own gimmick) and like I said the story falls off but overall the soundtrack and atmosphere are great.  I would only recommend if the game is on sale though, I don't think it is worth $15 unless you only care about the puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece! I'm amazed by the wild imagination the developers have and how they integrated the concept of light and shadow into the game mechanism so perfectly.Core mechanism: Moving the objects in the 3D world to affect their shadow, and control your shadow(technically not, but if I go further, it's gonna be a spoiler) to interact with the shadow of the objects to re-affect the real world, and your purpose is to get the main character(a cute little girl with a mental health problem) and her shadow both to the target point. It really brings up so many interesting ways of puzzle-solving.There are so many "know how" you can use that you already know in real life, like moving the object closer to the light, which makes the shadow bigger and if your shadow is "occasionally" on the object's shadow it'll become an elevator and lifts you to the high platform that you couldn't reach with your own power.Story:I was attracted by the plot until the end, so I would say it's very good, and even though there are only 2 characters (or you can say one), they are portrayed very well, there are not perfect even bad at some points but their attitude to make life better and never give up makes you love them and feel they are so vivid just like a friend.Music:I usually don't care about this part that much, but it's also not bad, it always reflects the little girl's emotions, and makes you feel immersed.The difficulty of levels is just fine, you can easily pass one level and get a sense of achievement. But if you want to challenge yourself more you can try to get the "origami", it's like an extra purpose, you don't need to get it to pass the level, it's just something challenging for hard-core players.I feel it's really a shame that so few people have played and even gotten to know this game, I know people just like to play those templated open-world games because they always seem massive and cost-effective, even most time they just throw it right into the corner of their storage, it's understandable, but I just like these finely designed linear games.I've never felt tired or bored during the whole gameplay, even though the game process is not that long, but who wants and long boring game anyway. It just fits so well, makes you completely immersed, can't stop thinking even after finishing this game.10/10 for definite! Respect to the devs.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic puzzle game. Loved it. In my personal opinion it's even better if you turn down the voice volume to zero and turn off the subtitles so you'll experience the game entirely without narration. The game itself has a very interesting atmosphere that's so much stronger without the narrator and that girl's whiny voice.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: I have nothing but praise for this game. This is an exceptionally polished puzzle platformer, with great art and story. The game beautifully combines 2D and 3D puzzles  in very clever and outstanding ways. All puzzles are doable and the progression is good. As far as I understood, he story is about overcoming trauma/fear/depression. It is something a lot of people can relateThe soundtrack is nice and atmospheric and the voice acting (English) is very well. done. I completed the game in 6.6 hours on the  Steam Deck. So yeah, the game runs flawlessly on the Deck. Again, I have nothing but praise for this game 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Good art style and interesting puzzles and concepts. The difficulty and frustrations are low to average and the puzzles make sense. It reminds me a little of Gris in terms of appearance which I think is a benefit. Voice and story are defiantly not the high point and a little cringe but not enough to not finish the game and enjoy it
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings of "The shady part of me".  It's probably the 3rd or 4th game that I've played that has included these sorts of shadow mechanics but it has a few twists that I don't think I've seen before. Overlaying shadows angles changing shadow orientation and being able to possess dolls are really fun. The issue is that these don't feature very prominently in the game and they aren't really "stretched" in turns of mechanics.The origami birds often feel like you have to get them if you want to experience even a small level of complexity. Some puzzles with them in I feel should have been modified so that the base puzzle was the level of getting the origami birds and then getting the origami birds was even harder (also I'm not super keen on some of them being hidden rather than difficult to get).Most puzzles often don't feel very complex because there is only one way to get through the puzzle so there are actually zero things you need to think about.The music is good and the dialogue and story are serviceable (which quite frankly is a lot better than some games of this style). The voice acting sadly isn't as serviceable with one of the two main voices being really really offputting.I have mixed feelings mainly because there are puzzle elements which I think could be brilliant however they sit (for me) in the realms of "I've seen worse". My lasting feelings are that I hope the developers make another game.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, a nice game, but not a great game.I appreciate the mental health topic, but the presentation here didn't resonate with me.The puzzles are clever and towards the end. I found some to be quite challenging.  I had to look up a clue to three puzzles that I just couldn't figure out.On one of those puzzles, I found a clever solution, however the developer anticipated that solution and included an obstacle in just the right spot that rendered it incorrect.  They didn't have to do that, but they did. I was forced to find their preferred solution. I'd give it a 7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: The game mixes 2D platformer with 3D adventure and explores a cool idea of changing 2D landscape by moving objects in 3D. Some of the puzzles are a bit frustrating in terms of execution, but overall it's a good game and doesn't overstay its welcome: it ends just when you become tired of it. And if you want more, you can spend a bit more time by collecting all hidden origami birds (100% achievements should take you 5-7 hours).
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Story based platformer where you control a 3D person and a shadow. Switching between both to solve puzzles. The story and music do a great job of setting the mood. The story plays out in words and voice lines that appear as you move forward. Really well put together. Can be a little slow if you're not in the mood for that.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: It is difficult for me to put words to my thoughts. This might be because I'm kind of sick right now, but also because an experience like this isn't really something you can speak about easily.This is a wonderful game. It's short, as far as games go, but that doesn't detract from it in the slightest. While I never 100% completed this game, I did finish the story, and that was enough. The story follows two girls. One who can't step into the light, as she is only a shadow, and one who afraid of the light. There are definitely puzzle mechanics in this. It's a puzzle platformer, after all. As you play, you learn more of who these people are, alongside a good twist that I shan't spoil, though it's pretty clear a couple hours in. I think my only gripe is that in the final bit there is a mechanic that sort of spoils some of the old ones, and almost makes one character irrelevant. It was still somewhat puzzling, though, and that's a good thing. All in all, well worth your time to pick up.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: I love the dreamy visuals mixed with darker visuals like in the game "Inside"The story was great, although a little confusing near the end. I loved the manner of story telling where the story was told to you through single sentences and at the same time something else would be written on the walls or hidden somewhere.And lastly, gameplay was just.... CHEF'S KISS!! I love puzzle games and the puzzles in this game are so creative and beautiful to look at as they play out in front of you. Highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Shady part of me, has to be one of the games i'm enjoying the most so far... its super chill with an amount of diverse puzzles to accomplish along your journey with, an amazing storyline which requires quite the attention to fully understand, i love that.Somehow i can resonate with the main characters, based on their fears and also their strengths, trusting in each other until the end.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: I found the artwork to be very unique, and the world was pretty fun. The story was very vague though, and seemed to be about mental illness. The whole game seems to be a therapy session. I was not expecting that before buying it. The puzzles were quite simple, I wish they were a little more challenging seeing how puzzles were a big part of this game. I wasn't really absorbed by the story or the game, my favorite part was the artwork. I liked playing it, but would not play it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this one.   In-game comments became slightly annoying and repetitive (French MUCH less so than English), but not a show-stopper.Switching back and forth between the character and her shadow, each having different reactions to light and shadow, was a lot of fun - AND, it is really nice that the game is divided into many little sections to solve, giving a nice feel of making progress.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: I love the art style of the game and the concept was really fun. The puzzles started out very simple but became very complicated (though still solvable) by the end. I enjoyed the game - but not enough to go back for all the achievements. Very quick too - approx 5 hours to complete the game, though I think you could do it in 3.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Shady Part of Me is a short game with many cool ideas. It features nice puzzle design, unique look, and a surprisingly good soundtrack. The story is interesting and mysterious, and having finished the game, I'm still not quite sure what it was about (in a good way). I'd recommend it for anyone who likes puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not one to put negative reviews on a game and if there were an option for a neutral, I'd mostly say this is more of a "neutral" game for me. The concept is straightforward and so far, I don't find anything challenging about the game. I feel like they could implement more of a challenge to it, but it seems to me that it's more story-based/visual rather than a platformer. I don't even really understand the story line and everything just falls flat. Not sure if there may have been a translation issue of any sort.I'm also not too fond of the voice in the game as it sounds more robotic than it does sound natural. I'm really trying my best to finish the game and some of the music is rather nice-- but the high-pitched voice is the most annoying thing I've ever heard in any game. The quotes are great but again, doesn't seem to correlate with the story line and it seems to be all over the place. You're more busy trying to find the next word to understand the sentence than platforming.Not worth the full price at all and can see this game being $1 in the future.--EDITTrying my absolute best to finish the game to get my money's worth and the only way to enjoy playing this game is by putting the voice acting on mute. LOL.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: is an unusual game in which we control two characters who help each other on their way through different locations.But these characters are a  and can only move in the shadows, and a  who exists only on surfaces that are illuminated by light. This idea was perfectly implemented by the developers.The difficulty of the puzzles is set up well here. They are not difficult, but interestingly made. Here arenas depend on light sources. Therefore, it's not always possible to immediately imagine how the situation will change due to the activation of the handles or the shift of various objects in the arena. The difficulty of the arenas increases towards the end, and to tell the truth, I spied on the passage of two puzzles.About the plot itself, I want to say that it's simple. We have protagonists who met each other and at first they just play in the locations of the girl's house, and later they try to get out somewhere. The story begins to change mood from a joyful journey to a sadder one. I didn't like this change of mood, but this is one of the few negative aspects of the game. So .Separately, I want to praise those who created the musical accompaniment for the locations. Together with interesting-looking decorations, the music gave them their own, different atmosphere.I really liked this game and I  of the usual genres and want variety. This game may surprise you and give you a  of fresh air.

_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: I mostly got this because it supported steam deck, was cheap in a sale and that felt like a good in combo. I came to realise though that this game is really quite beautiful too.On one level it's a platformer. Yet it's also an artistic experiment in story telling. And it pushed the platformer genre forward by being both 2D and 3D simultaneously. At its core the mechanics of a character that needs light to exist and another that's afraid of light is pretty unique. All this whilst actually being fun to play as well. The interplay between the 2D and 3D platformer builds the further through the game you get. This makes for some pretty decent puzzles to solve. The narrative does seem to get repetitive after a while, but the development of the puzzling mechanisms adequately makes up for it. The one thing that seems to be missing and probably prevents this from becoming quite as seminal in its own genre as say portal 2 is the lack of local co-op. I really hope there's a sequel or expansion that develops this potential further.

_childDocuments_.review: Shady Part of Me is a really solid puzzle platformer, but the narrative was convoluted & "fake deep." _childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: I'm on the fence with this one, but have gone for a positive rating because it's clear a lot of love and attention went into the game.To start with the good, the artstyle is fantastic. Each area is really distinct and immersive, whether its the loneliness of the hospital, or the warmth of the forge. I also thought the shadow/light contrast was done really well (with each character having a forbidden element), and the puzzles developed at a good pace as the levels went on. I REALLY liked the rewind function as well, so that instead of being dragged back to a particular checkpoint when you 'failed' you could just zip back time slightly and try again. This allowed freedom to try different puzzle solutions without getting stressed, which I really appreciated.For me, the storyline was what really let this down. Of course this will be very subjective, because it's an emotion/story-based game, but I found the dialogue between the two characters to be very fragmented and confusing. I felt that I wasn't given much context as to why anything was happening. Was the game meant to represent leaving childhood behind? going through therapy? living with autism? I've seen all those suggested on the forums, but for me I found each Act of the game so wildly different to the last that it didn't hang together as a coherent whole. I'm fine with leaving some things up to interpretation, but I didn't feel the game gave me enough to work with, and therefore didn't deliver the same heartfelt punch as something like Gris or Epistory. I also didn't feel the resounding emphasis of 'try harder' and 'act like everyone else' struck the right tone.Overall, a puzzle-game with interesting mechanics and lovely artstyle, but not the emotional heft I was hoping for.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Moderately easy puzzles, I collected 78/98 origamis without trying to find them.
