In the end, it shows that the whole game was about her overcoming her fears but as I have mentioned before I wish that they kept the game a bit longer to explain the story a bit further. Nevertheless, I really liked the game and I would recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Even though the incessant story is rather heavy-handed and upsettingly disingenuous, this is undoubtedly a clever game of bite-sized perspective puzzles.Despite ‘light vs shadow’ and ‘2D vs 3D’ being heavily trodden territory for puzzlers, Shady Part of Me still manages to produce plenty of cunning twists. By the end, the game had introduced and incremented a satisfying mix of concepts in comfortably-sized puzzles that were complicated yet never overwhelming. I'd be remiss not to mention how good the game’s soundtrack is as well. Not only is the music a very pleasant accompaniment for longer stretches of walking, but the music also takes advantage of the concept of playing as two characters and will change slightly as you switch between either perspective. Good use of audio middleware tends to help a game’s music stand out and, considering how often you swap characters, this intuitive addition adds a lot to passive gameplay.In contrast to the thoughtfulness of the gameplay and music, the ever-present story comes across as particularly ‘muddy’ as well as being slightly pretentious, crudely voice-acted, and doing a grossly inadequate job of discussing mental illness. Roughly, the moral of the story is that self-acceptance is achieved through the magic of obeying a horrid therapist and all you need to do to be whole is "try harder". These two recommendations belong more in the comments of a Dark Souls retrospective video than they do in the emotional cinematic platformer that Shady Part of Me wants to be. Upon beating the final chapter, I checked online to make sure I hadn’t gotten the “manipulated by the therapist” route and bad ending for not collecting enough macguffins or something. It’s horrible to imply that masking is the happy ending to anxiety disorders. Coping mechanisms help, but they are not there to inexplicably whisked away harmful behavior. Why on earth would you suggest that working desperately to fit in with society will vanquish the fears that control you? Problems are not solved in the same way that a neurotypical Disney film cures trauma, but Shady Part of Me sure thinks that’s how it all works.After purchasing the game, I’d highly recommend keeping the ‘music’ at 100%, putting ‘voice’ to 0%, and turning off the subtitles. The passive ‘wall words’ are enough to communicate the vague story of self-doubt without the unremarkable dialogue getting in the way of the music or distracting you during an intriguing puzzle.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Shady Part of Me is great. It’s a puzzle-platformer, where you interact with light and shadow. Essentially you’re playing two characters here: the main protagonist, and her shadow. The latter can only operate in the background of the scene, interacting with shadows that form and disappear based on what’s going on in the foreground. It opens up for some fun, brainy puzzles where one world affects the other in pretty big, tangible ways. It only gets more mind-bendy the longer you play too. Especially when the developers start experimenting with perspectives and how shadows interact with surfaces. But it’s never at the cost of complexity or pacing though. In fact, the whole game holds a brisk pace, whooshing you from challenge to challenge. On top of that, you can also rewind time, making failure a natural and streamlined part of the whole process. I’d go so far as to say that Shady actually never discourages you by being difficult. Instead, it’s much more interested in showing you new things, as well as new spins on older concepts. It’s constantly surprising and creative.Recommended, if you enjoy playful, puzzly platformers.

_childDocuments_.review: Shady Part of Me,A game where the player embarks on the story of a conflicted little girl and her shadow. A story well-written as it is "shady" and poetic, forcing the player to reflect on it.The artistic direction of the game is reminiscent of another game: Little Nightmares, albeit less dark in it's overall ambience with intriguing areas shaped by the imagination of a child.Gameplay wise, it is your typical platform game mixed with riddles you're ought to solve by the help of the shadow although some of those riddles can be a little tough for the player to solve thanks to the lack of clarity of some of the level design of the "shadow world". The player is also tasked although it's optional and won't impact anything to find origamis dispersed throughout the game, needless to say by my previous point that some are well-hidden and can lead to som head-scratch.Musically speaking, the soundtrack is really well done with again a reminiscence akin to childhood on some tracks.Overall, a Shady Part of Me was a really good experience with a good artistic design coupled to a well done soundtrack and pretty good riddle/platforming and a well written story.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent puzzles. Switching from 2D to 3D warms up your mind. Music and atmosphere are noir, but soothing at the same time.  Hannah Murray's voice is absolutely fantastic. _childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: At its worst, this game can be a little slow or repetitive, especially early on; the core of the gameplay is a system of light and shadow puzzles that gradually evolve in complexity, but begin very simple. At its best, the game is a magical unfolding pop-up book of dialogue, typography art, transporting visuals, mechanical novelties, and light platforming challenge. What makes it something special is the interplay between those parts and how the evolving mechanics, environment, and narrative reinforce each other. The player's interaction with the world mirrors the shifting conversation between girl and shadow, reinforcing feelings like isolation, confinement, freedom, exploration, and so on.

_childDocuments_.review: Really lovely game. "Contrast" meets "Braid", but more puzzler than platformer. It won't tax your platforming reflexes like those two games; it's more about making you think what approach to take, and is always executed easily once that the thinking part was resolved correctly. Plus you can rewind anytime.The music is fine. In some parts it's truly nice, and it's always at least suitable.The voice-over in English, I've been less impressed by. The whole game is accompanied by a child-voice/adult-voice dialogue of a certain Ms. Hannah Murray, the most prominently credited person of the entire game, whom I'd be supposed to be familiar with if I had watched the Game of Thrones, which I did not, nor plan to. I mean, at times Murray is fine, and conveys well both the woman and the little girl, but other times it's such a hammy delivery that I stop, and blink twice, before proceeding to play.When I will return to replay this game - with a distance of a year or two - I will switch it to French, to see how it all works out in the language of its authors, and a less prominently-credited voice actor. And I will surely return to replay this game because of...... the art. The art, oh my. The art is . It is a gem. The art is all the reason that you need to buy this game and to play it. Plus there are also many good puzzles, some good music and interesting storytelling. Warmly recommended.P.S. if you have kids, say 8+ or so, the game should be great for them too. There's nothing "horrible" in it that would be a reason to not let a kid play it. They won't get the story of course (then again, it's all wrapped up thus that they won't get that there's something they're not getting), but they will enjoy to dive into that art, that surreal flight of imagination, as well as scratch their heads thinking how to proceed past the next puzzle.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: There lives a girl who believes that she can only rely on herself, but there is one that is always close to her side that is willing to help if only she would acknowledge her. In The Shady Part of Me you will take on both characters, a girl lost in her sorrows, and her shadow. They both have a mind of their own, and can do incredible things, but when they work together they might just be able to save the girl from her one glaring fear.You will navigate through the game bouncing between the 3 dimensional world of the girl, and the 2 dimensional world of her shadow. To successfully get through the levels of the game you will have to move objects and activate switches in both worlds. You will also have to keep an eye out for origami birds, it’s not necessary, but I have to admit I enjoyed the challenge of trying to get all of them. I failed to get all of them, but that didn’t stop me from trying. There’s definitely a deep story that will pull at your heartstrings as the game progresses, and you will encounter three main voices that try to untangle the past, and free the girl’s and shadow’s future, and I have to admit that there are times where some of the voices get jumbled up and I couldn’t quite figure out from which perspective it was coming from. That being said, I enjoyed the story from start to finish. There’s definitely a hopelessness, a sense of loss, and the feeling of hiding inside one’s self in the art style. When dealing with the shadow’s 2D world I did enjoy the added challenge of trying to figure which way is up when having to jump from one wall/floor’s shadow to an adjacent one.If you're looking for a challenging platformer that requires you to exist in both 2D and 3D, and you’re ready to take on a story that will frustrate you, make you emotional, and on occasion make you want to scream at the character, then this is a game you’re going to want to check out. I was able to get through the entire game in 5 hours, and I have to say that in terms of the challenge there is no lull so you’re going to get your money’s worth.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Solid puzzle platformer, while idea of light + shadow puzzles isn't anything new, they are executed well. Puzzles surprise you with new things quite regularly, but at points they feel like repeating themselves. Overall puzzle difficulty is still just right and difficult is stable, just a few random spikes in difficulty. Music and Aesthetics are really stylish / beautiful, Shady Part of Me is really beautiful game. Then to negatives... story is really meh, main character voice acting is annoying and sometimes characters are really insufferable, but thankfully the latter point fluctuates on severity.I don't recommend getting the game on full price, but if on decent sale I do recommend it to puzzle game fans, just don't expect an difficult game.

_childDocuments_.review: I knew this game was interesting the way it looked, it's a great simplistic puzzle game, meaning the puzzle aren't that hard most of the time, but are satisfying to complete because of the mechanics. Graphics and design of this game is pretty much a big part of the game, it looks cool. You have yourself, a little girl that looks scared/stressed of something, and your shadow that looks older and more matured, they talk to each other throughout the game and of course solves puzzles together to get somewhere. It's a puzzle game, an easy one, but the mechanics to complete them are fun, and the game looks beautiful, and you also have some surprisingly good voice acting. Chill game.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Shady Part of Me has its drawbacks, but does enough things right to earn a recommendation from me. I'll start by commending the games art style and overall aesthetic which were great. Nothing incredibly flashy, but they matched the puzzle gameplay very well and it was impressive for a game from a small team. The main portion of the game, the puzzles, were unfortunately a mixed bag. You can fit them into three difficulty categories, and each category makes up about a third of the total puzzles in the game:The problem is that the game doesn't start with the easy puzzles and slowly make them more challenging; the game shifts between difficulties at random. You will get a tough puzzle followed by two incredibly easy ones, then another tough puzzle, then another really easy one. It makes the difficulty, and gameplay, disjointed at times.The story was a let-down. There's symbolic imagery throughout the game which hints at the protagonist’s mental state and personal conflicts, but there's no resolution at the end. None of the questions I had were answered, and the ending is abrupt. I also found the voice of the protagonist to be rather annoying. She sounded like an adult putting on an exaggerated high-pitched voice, which I know was the case but It didn't sound natural; a young girl should actually sound like one. The voice acting from the other characters was fine, no complaints there.The music is very well done, and it always fit the atmosphere of the levels. Mixed with the game’s art design, some sections of the game (such as the toy room) were actually quite emotional. At its best, Shady Part Of Me reminded me heavily of the game Braid, which is a great thing.In terms of length, I'd say most people will be able to beat this in 4-5 hours. I collected all of the collectibles too, and that took just under 5 hours for me to do in total. For the price, that's a pretty good length. I also want to say that the option to not only go into any level, but any section as well from the menu was very helpful. It made getting the collectibles I was missing a much easier task, so thanks to the developers for that. My complaints about the puzzles aside, I did enjoy the game. It's a shame the story was such a missed opportunity.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: There are masterpieces, and there are games, Shady Part Of Me features both, exquisite soundtracks, ingenious gameplay with alternating 2D and 3D of the two protagonists of the game, different and enjoyable puzzles to play, and a good story with a magnificent dub. I loved this game and I highly recommend it !!!
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, PLAY THIS GAME FOR THE SOUNDTRACK ALONE! Absolutely fantastic!At first the girl's voice was annoying so I turned the voices off, but later on it grows on you as she grows. I think understand which voice is which:. The shadow girl is the part of you trying to grow (in the light, like a plant), The physical/girl in white is the side of you that just wants to pull back into the comfort zone (the shadows, hence why there are books around a lot. She just wants to crawl inside a book and escape reality), and the narrator/voice over is other people; people on the outside constantly offering advice, or straight-up telling you what to do. I didn't get every metaphor throughout the game (like the whole "we need to close the gap" and "I'll act just like them" during the final act), but I think I got most of them. The dialogue going through the school got me. Narrator: "You need to learn. You need to remember" - White Girl: "WAIT for me to learn. WAIT for me to remember" Just because we're all in the same class doesn't mean we learn in the same way or at the same speed. I always fell behind because I learn visually, not just reading text and figures. Give me a chart, or a visual representation for what you want me to solve. Once I had a tutor do that for me, I caught up no sweat, so that small line of dialogue had me go "Yes!"A couple of weird sentences (in English), such as:- Written on a wall: "Whom do you think I'll listen to?". It's either "Who do you think I'll listen to" or "To whom do you think I'll listen". The sentence used in the game "Whom do you think I'll listen to" is a clash of informal and formal, and it's weird. - Another one was spoken dialogue: the shadow girl said "How much time do I have to wait?". As opposed to what? "How much money do I have to wait"? "How much food"? "Waiting" is only ever used for time, so "How long do I have to wait" is all you need, or "How much more do I have to wait" to emphasise they're taking too long. All in all, a great experience. I really had to use the old noodle for some puzzles which is always welcomed. Just straight platforming gets tiresome sometimes. Great music, nice story and characters, looks good, nice style. I look forward to any future projects. As Chancellor Palpatine said in Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace "We shall watch your career with great interest"
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Shady Part of Me has stunning visuals and ingenious new concepts for puzzles.It is completely driven by visuals and atmosphere (it's not really a "story" story, but if you combine the lore bits you do recieve some kind of journey.)The gameplay itself is as casual as it gets.Neither the short platforming sequences nor the simple puzzles do pose a challenge.Especially the latter is quite sad, since there are so many insanely cool never seen concepts in the mechanics of the shadow movement like changing the size of shadow objects depending on the distance to the lamp or multiple light sources. I really wish, these would have been explored A LOT more.Therefore it is mostly a  and should be treated as such.If you do, the game is quite awesome, even though it may be a little short.

_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly really enjoyed the game. My favorite part was the music. it was spot on and very involving. The puzzles aspect are fun but we're a little bit confusing trying to learn the mechanics as you progress late game (no tips on how things work), however not too awfully difficult. It's a great game, I'd would recommend it to anybody who enjoys solving puzzles and matching timing, similar to Portal. I'd give it a 7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: I was intrigued by the art and the soundtrack in the trailers. I'm a fan of puzzle games so I bought it while it was on sale. I know a lot of people have different on what the story is in this game, but I felt  it stir my own complicated relationship with mental health. I saw it as a story of accepting the help that was given, if only after realizing that you won't get better without it. I'll let you know that if you're very sensitive to mental health topics this game may trigger you if you're not expecting it. That being said, I found it hauntingly beautiful. And even knowing that the ending was going to come sooner than I thought, I was still left surprised and maybe a bit confused before I could process it. The gameplay can be challenging and rewarding when you figure it out, and the rewind feature has saved my butt many times. It was a short game, but I have a feeling it will stay with me for a long time. An excellent game from a very small studio. I look forward to seeing what else they can do.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Wow what an artful game. Looks hand drawn all of it. Music - hauntingly beautiful. Turn the music up, close all other distractions and calmly take in this game. The narrative, subtle tones, dialogues, atmosphere won’t bring you to tears (hopefully) but it will definitely tug at your heartstrings. Its designed to bring you on an emotional journey, so let it. I've never known games could be like this. Almost therapeutic. Maybe deep down all of us are just (2) little girls trying to get out.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Inspired by Iris.Fall and Contrast. Gorgeous unique graphics style, nice and relaxing acoustics, story meh. Puzzles have unique mechanic and some really nice spatial twists. Not too difficult, but two made me pull my hair out. Summary: a pleasant experience, will look out for any other stuff they made.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely beautiful game. Gorgeous art, and some very clever puzzles. I can see why they make such a big deal about Hannah Murray's VA, she does a spectacular job and brings to life some very good writing. Not wishing to give too much away, the tone of the final act was not what I was expecting but it makes for a better more memorable ending.

_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Just a really solid puzzle game. It's creative and beautiful, and I appreciate it when games have a sort of "opt-in" hard mode built into the game, which is the case here with the origami birds you can find in several of the puzzles, but are in no way forced to get. Also did not expect the music to be such a stand out for me, but it's great. I love the subtle differences between the light and dark versions of the songs, and in general thought they were really lovely (albeit melancholic) songs.My only con for this game, is I think the narrative aspect could've been a bit more fleshed out. The fragmented nature of the "story" was working for me for a bit, but then I kind of expected it to get more coherent, and it really doesn't until the very end. Not the worst thing in the world because the story definitely takes a backseat to the puzzles and that's what I expected anyway, but it just left me wanting a bit more. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I just loved the game. It can offer good introspection thanks to all the meaningful quotes we get to read through the game. _childDocuments_.review: In addition to the darkness it have within the story by discussing such sensitive topic like psychological or mental issues and raising awareness about it, Shady Part of Me provide great puzzles and different mechanics in each chapter.It’s unfortunate that the excitement I feel after getting every new mechanic is quickly fades away through repetitiveness of easy puzzles.Other than that, it’s a great game that I enjoyed.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: This is simply wonderful!Even though the setting may seem depressing at the begging, it unfolds beautifully and step by step. The riddles aren't too difficult, even though, towards the end, they do get a bit more challenging.The psychological theme of overcoming and dealing with fears and anxieties is wonderful and may give a subtle insight into such struggles to people who haven't had to tackle these conditions. I simply find the idea of taking a delicate subject like this and transforming it into a game amazing and bold.I'd really like to see even more games of this kind, tackling personal questions and hinting answers paired with riddles, a superb storyline, capturing graphics and complex characters.Go on and give it a try!

_childDocuments_.review: "Try harder...."I played the alpha version of this game at Game Daily Connect in 2019. I told the devs that I was in love with the game and that I couldn't wait for the finished product. My expectations for what this game could be were sky-high, and it still surpassed them.This is a narrative-driven puzzle game with light (HA) platforming elements. You guide a girl and her shadow through imaginative environments that expertly drop hints at the the girl's life and how she views the world. The puzzles, while not overly difficult, require you to get as creative as the visuals to solve them. And that's not mentioning what you have to do if you want to get all the collectibles. You owe it to yourself to play this flawless masterpiece. This game is something that everyone should experience. It's a little short with my playthrough only taking 5 hours total, but it's 5 hours very well spent.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Want a puzzle platformer where you switch between 2D and 3D? Well this is a game to go for, I'd call it Little Nightmares meets Contrast made by a French developer, this is a short one, but it's entertaining.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game why:1: The characters are super designed2: The voices of the avatars are really nice to hear and incredibly cute3: You get to know both characters and their emotional sides. This creates an emotional bond with the characters, which makes the game all the more exciting. I can only recommend it for everyone who likes puzzles and wants to be touched emotionally.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: This game was pretty good. The core concept of moving objects and light sources to manipulate shadows is really interesting and there are many creative twists on the concept throughout the game. It's definitely not very difficult even with getting all collectables, but it's enjoyable nonetheless. The visuals and sound are superb and create an unique atmosphere that's simultaneously dark and bleak, but also calming and comforting. There were actually a few sequences that really impressed me visually, which is amazing for being this studio's first ever game. You tell that some talented people poured their hearts into this game.Really my only complaint is that I couldn't really comprehend the story at all. I mean, I get that the game is taking place inside the girl's imagination or something, but it's all very vague and metaphorical from start to finish. I could pick up pieces of stuff they were alluding to but could never really put them all together into a coherent narrative. I was wondering if there was going to be a moment at the end where they explain everything, but it never came. Considering that the story is such a selling point, the fact that I didn't really understand it should be a problem, but it didn't really diminish my enjoyment of the game. Besides, maybe the story does make sense but I was just too dumb to follow it. That could definitely be it.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: I decided to buy this game because the reviews were pretty good, I enjoy the art style and the music is lovely. The use of switching between the light and dark characters to solve the puzzles was really quite fun. With that being said, most of the puzzles were easy, many were almost brainless, in my opinion. Shady Part of Me uses very simple controls which was nice so that during game play I could read the dialogue- it is also spoken but I watch TV with CC on, I'm "that guy." There were a few times that there were monotonous pages (rooms?) and I just wanted to get to the next one because there was... well... nothing to do. I completed the game in less than 9 hours. Although I didn't get all the origamis, that 9 hours included snack breaks and a few idle periods. All in all, I like it. I'll play it again to get all of the origamis. *spoiler***They make it fairly evident that the girl is in an institute and considering the dialogue she has, mostly with herself, you can make some assumptions as to the diagnosis of the character. But other than that, even after completing it, there's not much information about her or how or why... it's rather anticlimactic. The last act had the hardest puzzles- for sure. That brings me to this- gravity. And maybe this was a user error? Maybe I was just too stupid to realize the last direction the shadow girl "fell" in, set the gravity. BUT I was almost furious with myself in the last act for trying over and over to fall to the correct shadow surface in one part of a puzzle. xD **So... I liked it. Do I recommend it? Sure. The music IS beautiful. It's an interesting game and uses, mostly, minimal strategic thinking. I really would have liked a bit more closure but it was good.
_childDocuments_.name: Shady Part of Me

_childDocuments_.review: Creative ideas and clever use of shadows. The music and the aesthetic was eye and ear-catching, sometimes I just stopped for a while to take in everything. New and interesting mechanics were introduced constantly so the puzzles didn't feel repetitive at all. I was rooting for the girls as they pressed on in this somewhat somber but  beautiful journey. The game was a nice take on the subject of anxiety and personal demons. Completion takes little time, but it's still well worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Shadows have long attracted the musings of curious people, their poetic duality generating wonderful works of art in their honor. Shady Part of Me, a game about this inescapable balance, reveals in playful greyscale the mesmerizing effects of jumping back and forth between realms of light and darkness.Developer Douze Dixiemes has created in Shady Part of Me an innovative and evocative puzzle-platformer that has the player separately control the body and shadow of a little girl through interlocking puzzles of light and shadow.Atmospheric BrillianceFrom the first scene, Shady Part of Me jumps off the screen with its unique style--a dream-like expanse of masterful drawings, all set to an out-of-this-world original soundtrack. There’s a beautiful restraint with the UI, only opting to focus on the little girl’s playful but ominous narration manifest as text across the world. There’s no mini-map, no progression markers, nothing distracting on the screen away from the powerful artistic ambiance.Few games instantly charm like Shady Part of Me does, and in that company it shares with platformer classics like Ori and the Blind Forest, Limbo, Braid or even more artistic adventure games like Journey. Each of these gems are polished to the point of near-perfection where, most importantly, their top-notch aesthetics meld with innovative mechanics.A game made better by the symbiosis of its art and gameplay can only go wrong in places like the main story, but rest assured, Shady Part of Me is no let-down there. Vague enough to keep you guessing and drip-fed at just the right rate, the execution of short-form storytelling here is spot-on.Reorienting PuzzlesAt the core of every great platformer is foundational learning theory: Introduce → Reinforce → Complicate → Reorient. Puzzle mechanics start out easy in low-stakes environments, then they are fully defined by a further challenge. Then, the puzzle demands absolute knowledge and mastery of the mechanic in a high-stakes environment, and once completed that new mechanic reorients the player’s mastery for the rest of the puzzles to come. Shady Part of Me expertly scaffolds its varying degrees of difficulty.Beyond its solid fundamentals, Shady Part of Me proves bold and imaginative. Other platformers in the past like Limbo or Contrast have played around with light and shadow as defining game mechanics, but Shady Part of Me does so with an impressive finesse. Shady Part of Me isn’t an innovative puzzle masterpiece like Portal or Braid because it doesn’t go all out on its zany creativity, but it plays to its strengths with restraint in the puzzle department to let other elements like story and atmosphere get their shine in this short experience.ConclusionShady Part of Me is the definition of short and sweet--its story wraps up well, the puzzles reach a satisfying level of complexity, and the simplicity of the core game loop never gets too old. In a world full of indie platformers and puzzle games, Shady Part of Me stands out among the best of them with its expertly-blended story and mechanics and stunning artistic polish.  Score: 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr a nice, relaxing puzzle gameIt is quite easy and only takes five to seven hours to finish.There is barely any timed action so stress level is one on ten, just because of the slightly creepy atmosphere.Any puzzle game addict will stroll through this game.It seem you're supposed to somewhat guess what the story is really about at some point in the game, but it remains a bit vague.I think it's about .Interesting, but the writing is somewhat repetitive.The graphics are nice, and the dynamic music is pretty cool, although it stays quiet most of the game and the character switching mechanic sometimes makes it harder to appreciate.All in all, still an enjoyable, and very accessible experience.

name: Lake
detailed_description: It's September 1, 1986. You take on the role of forty-something Meredith Weiss, who returns from the big city to her quiet hometown. She exchanges her busy career at a software company to fill in for her dad, the local mail carrier. During her two-week stay in beautiful Providence Oaks, Oregon, she runs into a few familiar faces as well as plenty of new folk. As Meredith, you get to decide who to talk to, who to befriend and perhaps even start a romantic relationship with. Whatever happens, at the end of her stint she'll have to make up her mind: return to her demanding job in the big city, or stay in the town she grew up in? Play Lake and… Escape to a beautiful, rustic environment without cellphones and the Internet. Drive around the lake in your dad's trusty mail truck, or let the auto-pilot do the work. Talk to a range of engaging characters, each with their own personalities and quirks. Choose after-work activities: hang out with your friends, help out your neighbours or stay home and read a book. Experience two weeks of branching story that doesn't shy away from slice-of-life themes. Determine your own story: there are no 'right' or 'wrong' answers or endings, simply what you want to happen.

_childDocuments_.review: this game was a let down for me. It was really cozy and nice at first but then got repetitive. What was the point of knocking on the doors if no one was ever home to get the packages. Cut scenes felt so rushed as well. Felt like there was more coming but would just end so suddenly and never felt enough with the story lines. They just dropped certain characters and left a lot of plot holes and story lines on edge. There was lots of glitches and bugs. Like cars just chilling in the middle of the road doing nothing? and it would cause a huge traffic jam. Not enough animals, characters walking around, or cars even to feel cozy. Many times I would go into the truck to get a package but then there was no package in my hand so I would have to open the truck again. The characters had little to no depth and tbh were kind of annoying. The main character was kind of annoying and the dialogue was really weak too. The romance story line with Robert was honestly so awkward... there was little to no story with his compared to the other girl. He had no range or anything. It was a let down and had me feeling completely empty at the end.

_childDocuments_.review: Simple but sweet game, feels like one of those films you'd put on on a Sunday afternoon.  The main part of the 'game' is you driving around delivering mail, and that's pretty much it.After every day, there are some cut scenes where you can usually have 'conversations' with some of the town folk, giving limited responses etc.Then it's back to driving around the town delivering mail.There is a nice little cameo from Mackenzie Crook at some point if you catch him,If you're after anything action packed for fast paced, even medium paced, this won't be for you, it's a very plodding game, with a fair bit of repetition.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm so in love with this game it's super unique, elegant, spontaneous. A fresh breath of air. _childDocuments_.review: I had been eyeing this game for a long time and when it popped up on a humble bundle I decided to pull the trigger.This game has a huge amount of potential that I hope the makers will consider with the next game they make. With the open world layout they definitely could have gone a different way, and they could keep the main postal route mechanic the same, but I think it would have been way more interesting if you had different quests for each person, and also added mini games that you can do on the weekend when you're off of work, like fishing, community service, etc.The way that they made the game isn't terrible, it just had me wanting more in the best way. I hope that the next game they make will be 10x better than lake since at the core they have an amazing mechanic they can build onto. I loved the story, I loved delivering packages, I loved exploring the town and I really loved how she would talk about her memories during certain aspects, however, it did leave me wanting more so I hope that they decide to make the best sequel ever.Just make sure to manually save on the 13th so you don't have to replay the game 3 times since right now if you have to replay the game, I imagine it would be pretty boring, unless you'd like to drive around delivering mail since as of today, they don't have a free roam version after completing the game. I would highly recommend this game, I would just say get it on sale since its a very short game, but cozy/heartwarming. I'm excited and hopeful for whats next.

_childDocuments_.review: Lake is a low-key game that's great to play when I want to relax, but it's engaging enough to play and beat more than once.No combat. No death.Drive truck, chat, and give mail.That sounds simple, but there's a lot going for Lake: The local characters make dialogues and actions interesting. It's got a homey and charming soundtrack that fits the warm, gentle atmosphere of the game. I'd describe it as early 90's folk rock. The setting immediately appealed to me: a small U.S. Pacific Northwest town in the 1990's. 😍 It's replay-friendly, thanks to "choices matter" game play throughout. It took long enough to beat the game that I felt I got my money's worth, but it was still short enough for more than one play through.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: A great experience, I personally loved this game!It offers one of the best characters in a long time: Meredith Weiss (props to her voice actress). Some great music too! The Lyrics REALLY fit the game and its themes, so great choices on the soundtrack. The game has exceptionally nice character designs, despite not being high polygon. I loved the way the characters models have so much personality without looking either too cartoony or going crazy on the polygons. Also props to some of the animation, Merediths walking animation while holding some different packages where really great. Lastly on the technical side: the driving is suprisingly good for an Indie title.Storywise: I loved it. For me the main reason to play a title like this: your choices do matter. Now I feel this game is more close to real life in the choices it presents to you then most games. It's subjects of reconnection to the place you came from may not appeal to you if you are quite young. I didnt find any "difficult" moral greyzone choices here either, the choices the game presented where about following your heart and defining for Meredith (and yourself): what is home? How do I connect to people. Again I loved this, and think its quite unique in gaming, which usually has only "EPIC/LIFE DEATH/GOODvsEVIL" choices.Some minor Pet peeves: Some of the sound was a bit buggy/missing (like the sound of cars passing by), going "offroad/skyrimming" is not very smooth, but its nothing mayor. Also would recommend having Meredit Whistle a tune while on her rounds/ being able to say hello to passers by. Yes its small stuff and costs time and money to make, but athmosphere was already great in this game, would add to it.Would Highly recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. It's not perfect by any means, but this is the game concept I really like. It's like a next step visual novel. Even though the main focus is supposed to be that you are a mail person delivering mail, and, that I guess is the purpose of the game, there is so much more. Good.-------I love the fact that you can choose differing paths on your journey depending on what choices you make. The choices do not make much of a difference, but, then again, if they did it would not be realistic. But they do make enough of a difference that makes it different every time you play it. I also like the way you can take as long as you like from day to day delivering letters and parcels. There is no time limit in this game. Everyone has real personalities and you really feel like you are engaging with real people in a real village. The ups and downs of friendships are all here. The game is also not very long as to make you get bored but, to me it's a perfect length of about 5 hours per game, (But I always take the long way round when delivering letters as I like to look at the scenery.Bad---Since the update I am finding the game sound is choppy and keeps cutting in and out. I am pleased with the subtitles as sometimes a whole sentence can not be heard. I will have to look into why this is happening as it appears to be my end. It never happened when I played it the first time. Also, I really do wish you could control the "goose" with a game controller as using WASD is very difficult for me and I sway all across the road like a drunk alien. I also wish there were a lot more music tracks in this game. 3 Is nowhere near enough. Especially for a driving game. I tend to put my own music on but it's not the same.  Apart from that I highly recommend this game to people who, like me, like slow paced games where you can take your time and just enjoy the game without having to worry about time limits.  All I want now is Lake 2!
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: This game was absolutely beautiful! Not only was the scenery incredible, but there was so many lovely characters and story involved that made it such a great experience. Also when they say there is no good or bad ending, there truly isn't! Not a single time while I was playing did I regret or feel punished for decisions I had made, even right down to the final choice! Only complaint was it was way too short, will definitely be replaying in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: This is basically a driving simulator with a backstory. The controls are not the easiest to manage to the point that I had to buy this on a console in order to make it work for me. Aside from that: The graphics are wonderful. The pace is slow but not tedious. The story and the choices therein are engaging and you really become attached to the characters. Over all this game is cozy and pleasant.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: This game definitely has potential but it's riddled with so many different issues that the whole experience was ruined for me. The game is just about as fun as it sounds like, you're a what it appears to be a middle aged woman who came back to her hometown to become a temporary delivery driver. I like the story has multiple routes but the story itself isn't very fun or relatable. The gameplay is extremely boring, it has initiatives for exploration but those go ultimately nowhere (there are no collectibles or side quests). The world itself is full of bugs. Also I don't understand why the game has so many different options for FPS optimization when you can literally only play the game at 60 FPS or else the game, if you decide to not cap it, just breaks (mainly delayed/no audio and stuck traffic). The graphics are probably the only good thing about this whole mess. Sadly, the game doesn't support photo mode or has an in-game way how to take proper screenshots.Overall, I'm disappointed with this product, I expected a little more. Some people may find the story interesting but the gameplay is monotonous. I feel like the game would be better off if you could only be picking what the protagonist says.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: I'm about 5 hours in, and honestly just kind of don't care if I finish it.It's a mixed bag.  I was hoping for something similar to Firewatch - one of my favorite games - but this game just doesn't have the draw.  I think the biggest issue is simply that it feels like they went 75% of the way and stopped.Positive:- Voice acting is actually pretty good, considering this is a small studio, kudos.  There wasn't any voice actor that I felt was bad or out of place.  Nice work!- It is relaxing to drive around. It's a nice change of pace from other games- The graphical style of the game is niceNegative:- Graphically the style of this game is good, but it just feels incomplete.  There's areas where there's really rough textures, people warping in/out of existence, and other graphical oddities.  The back of your mail truck looks like the inside of a used yogurt container, and there's no logo on it, just kind of felt more like a generic vehicle than a mail truck.- The main character walks too slow.  If you want to deliver mail in a cul de sac, it can be painful to walk to each house- The music on the radio is (at least to me) horrific and sometimes the radio won't turn off. - I had a hard time connecting with the characters. This could just be me, but I never felt in sync with the main character or the NPC'sI think with time this game has potential, but I'd let it mature a bit before playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: Lake is probably one of the best indie games I've played this year, which is why I give it the Sit Back and Relax reward. Providence Oaks is a charming, peaceful and quiet little town with a great atmosphere which makes delivering mail extremely fun, though I wish some days weren't as tedious and had some more interaction with residents. The main story is okay, there's several different choices you can make throughout the game, but they don't really have that much of an impact on the endings, which are quite similar to each other. I ran in to multiple (not game breaking) bugs like getting stuck after grabbing a parcel from the back of the truck or residents just being stuck in the middle of the road.Overall I did really enjoy the couple of hours I spent playing Lake, it's a rather short game, but I think it's worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: Was feeling kind of burned out by all of the 60+ hour games I have been playing recently, so I wanted a short and chill game to give me a bit of a break. Lake delivered; loved how they essentially made a narrative-driven mail delivery sim. This game is slow-paced which I liked, but I can tell by some other reviews that it wasn't for everyone so keep that in mind. Voice acting was good for the most part. Songs were catchy. Plus there are some romance options for the lead character (both genders, appreciate the inclusive-ness). Takes place in the mid-80's too, so there's some cute dialogue about technology. The FUTURE. Would definitely recommend this game if you are looking for something to chill and vibe to for a few hours. Think it's definitely worth the cost.

_childDocuments_.review: It's fine to be a little clumsy, make mistakes or not know what you're doing. While taking over your Dad's mail rounds back home for two weeks, you get to do things a little differently (if you want to!) There are plenty of people to get to know or reconnect with, each with their own stories, and you can decide how much you want to feature in them. Spending time with different people (and away from your work) is a great chance to re-evaluate your choices. While a lot of your time is spent driving (and taking photos), the highlight for me were the conversations.That said, some of the characters were a bit of a let down for me - the long phone calls with your parents and boss, and Frank's story, didn't really do much for me. But there were plenty of other stories to enjoy.The game really changed for me when I realised that, just like the narrative, you should drive the way you want. So don't fret about driving badly, accidentally bumping into people/buildings, etc - unsurprisingly, fine motor control is not what the game is about. ...I did find the driving controls a little clunky, so this was especially important! I would also recommend checking the control remapping to make things a little easier on yourself for these long drives - you'll be holding the acceleration button for long stretches!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Voice acting is amazing, character models look good, gameplay gets mundane very fast and choices presented as meaningful unfortunately make zero difference.The following detailed review contains spoilers. The first playthrough of Lake is quite enjoyable. You meet some interesting characters and although delivering mail isn't the most exciting thing ever, the balance of the mindless job and the more interesting after-work events makes for an enjoyable game. Throughout the story your dialogue options constitute various choices, and I really enjoyed thinking about my choices and what they might lead to, and what would happen if I chose other options. This was enough to forgive the somewhat empty-feeling town and extremely limited selection of songs on the radio. There are also some fun achievements to unlock as you go, based on what activities you choose to take part in. If you could get all achievements in one playthrough, or if there were achievements for making other choices besides saying yes to everything, this would be a thumbs up review. HOWEVER. Because there are three achievements for three different endings, you have to play through the game again if you want 100%. And this is where I discovered what a disappointment this game really is. Turns out, almost none of your choices matter. Very often, regardless of which dialogue option you choose, NPCs will reply the same way. Oh, you throught Kay wouldn't invite you to the lookout tower if you were always rude to her? Think again. You thought the flick shack would survive if you chose to romance Angie? You're wrong! The only things you have an influence over, are who (if anyone) you romance, and what you do when the story ends. Other than that, Meredith's (and the player's) presence in Providence Oaks makes zero difference, making the entire experience feel pointless. Pros: - The voice-acting is amazing, some of the best I've ever come across actually- Beautiful colors and light- There is a good balance between delivering mail and interacting with NPCs/attending events. - The dynamic minimap which zooms out as you drive faster and zooms in as you slow down to find a mailbox is genious- You can park like an a****** everywhereCons:- The world feels empty and unreal, with too many non-descript, low-poly Sims 2-looking houses, too few NPCs, other drivers on the road which clearly have no mind of their own ++- Turns out delivering the mail is rather mundane- The cats don't go inside/seek cover when it's raining. - The game is pretty heavy-handed about coaxing you into a lesbian relationship and being open about it, despite the story taking place in rural 1980s USA- After the first week there are no achievements left to unlock except the different endings- The "fast" walking speed is incredibly slow- Although you can often choose between multiple dialogue options, a lot of them take you to the same end point. The illusion of choice is not choiceMy game glitched out or something after four days, making it so the "Return to the post office" text was constantly on the screen, and I couldn't turn off my radio. Felt my eyes unfocusing themselves and my soul leaving my body at least thrice.6/10 for the first playthrough, 2/10 for the subsequent ones.

_childDocuments_.review: When Meredith Weiss – a 44-year-old computer programmer with a demanding job and a pushy boss – returns to Providence Oaks in Oregon, the small lake town in which she grew up, she thinks she’s only going to be covering her father’s mail route for two weeks. But actually … no, wait, that’s exactly what does happen. There’s no big twist in this gentle slice-of-life game about driving around a beautiful, entirely unremarkable American environment in a post van. I kept waiting for something a bit Twin Peaks to happen, or for some small-town drama to bubble up into something more exciting, but it never did. You deliver the post, you talk to residents, you gently examine Meredith’s life choices. Once you abandon expectations for some action and sink into the daily rhythm, it’s a relaxing time.Set in 1986, the game keeps things to a very small cast of characters – Meredith’s childhood best friend Kay Evans, the farmer Jack Reynold who’s also local radio DJ, a lumberjack his a name is Robert Harris, the owner Angie Eastman of the new VHS store in town – and the rekindled relationships between them. Supporting actors such as Meredith’s boss and her parents are only ever heard over the telephone.+ Beautiful scenery and mellow music+ Eccentric characters with relatable concerns+ Relaxed and thoughtful atmosphere+ Lovely and distinct visual style+ Gameplay loop of delivering mail is charming and tranquil- Somewhat repetitive gameplay- Linear story- Some cosmetic bugs

_childDocuments_.review: is a slice-of-life, choices-matter story game developed by Netherlands-based developers Gamious and published by White Thorn Games. Released in September 2021, the game provides a lovely bit of escapism from our present times, and shows a lot of promise as a potential format for subsequent games should the developers intend to build upon it. It’s September 1986 and you’re Meredith Weiss, a successful computer programmer from the big city who’s looking for a reprieve from the office culture grind. She has booked off two weeks from work to return to her childhood home of Providence Oaks, a small lakeside town set in the wilderness of Oregon. While there, she volunteers to fulfil her retiring dad’s postal rounds, and through doing so she reconnects with the locals; some from her past, along with a few new faces. Over the next two weeks, she will come to know more about them and possibly, more about herself. The core gameplay loop is the daily delivery of both letters and parcels to the residents of Providence Oaks. To do this you’re provided with a mail van which is your main mode of transportation throughout the game. You can either have the game drive for you, or you can control the vehicle yourself, and using your trusty map you can fulfil your rounds in whatever order you wish and at your own pace. Having used a controller, I can say that the controls are simple and comfortable enough to use repeatedly. The game really delivers on this simple construct, and it provides a really relaxing and straightforward experience, especially after a busy day. Over the course of these rounds you interact with a small but colourful cast of characters who represent the townsfolk, and when doing so you have the opportunity to make dialogue choices and even make a few commitments for events taking place after the main workday, which you keep track of using a journal. Through these interactions and commitments, you can grow closer to the townsfolk, two of whom are romanceable options for Meredith. Despite being identified as a “choices matter” game, I found that there are few moments where the outcomes in dialogue change very much. Nor did I find myself ever particularly pressed for time in terms of the commitments, so there was never any real reason to say no. However, I don’t consider this too terrible of a thing: Lake’s core aim is to provide a relaxing experience, and so it makes sense to avoid too much tension over the course of the game.The writing is nothing groundbreaking, but the story is very pleasant and certainly one worth seeing through to the end. There’s also plenty of great humour sprinkled throughout, and while none of the character’s are particularly deep, there’s enough there for each of them to feel real and appreciable in their own ways.  The game overall is quite short, lasting from 6 ~ 9 hours depending on how long you decide to take in completing your rounds and whether you decide to take any detours along the way, either in the form of just seeing the sites, playing the minigame in the form of an arcade game cabinet in the Diner, and so on. Aside from the three potential endings to the game, there’s not much that changes throughout the course of the playthrough, so there’s not much on offer in terms of replayability. But again, I don’t consider this to the game’s detriment too much: I think it suits the overarching theme - we all must inevitably make a choice, and move on - and reminds us that, like Meredith, we came here for a good time, not a long time. The minimalist, stylised 3D art style of the game is another one of its biggest selling points. You can tell that a lot of effort went into crafting the world of Providence Oaks to make it feel like a believable, small American town, and the character designs are also charming. It really is nice to wander around and appreciate the layout of the town and the appearance of the houses and other little details here and there. The weather effects are also nice. The character models themselves are nice, though the lack of animation makes the cutscenes where character’s talk to one another a little janky. The game also fades to black whenever Meredith leaves the van and enters it, or skips ahead in a cutscene to them entering or exiting places, so it’s clear the developers wanted to avoid some animations. I also encountered a few minor graphical glitches during my playthrough - textures popping in and out, camera going in and out of focus, AI vehicles and townsfolk getting stuck in the terrain. A little immersion-breaking, but nothing too egregious. The sound design and soundtrack for Lake is also very strong. The voice-acting more than makes up for the lack of expression on character’s faces, and the soundtrack - while small and repetitive by the time you reach the end of your playtime - is nevertheless very well-suited to the setting, and adds to the experience. The radio’s songs are especially catchy, and even as I’m writing this review I’m finding myself humming along to them. Occasionally I found that dialogue would cut a bit too early, leading to a very janky conversation between Meredith and whoever she was speaking to, but other than that I didn’t experience anything audibly that was too broken. Lake is a perfectly enjoyable slice-of-life game with some minimal but interesting choices to be made, with a charming yet brief story along with warm visuals and sound design. While there are one or two snags here and there, it’s nothing that has ruined my experience of the game, nor deters me from recommending it heartedly to others. If you need a brief reprieve from the world, this is the game for you. I hope that if they intend to return to this style of game, the developer’s build upon the strong foundations that Lake has given them. I look forward to seeing what they come out with next.

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased this game a few days ago, I had it on my wishlist for quite a while. I finished it in 7,5 to 8 hours. It was a really relaxing and fun game! I felt like playing a chill game that wasn't hard, and this was the perfect game for my mood.It's basically about delivering mail in a van in a small town in Oregon, USA in the 80s, with a cute story line! You can select dialogue options while talking to the residents. You also have the option to romance between two people (a woman and a man, your character is a woman) or you can choose to not romance anyone at all. The town looks really pretty, especially when you drive through the forest/nature or when you're looking out over the lake. You can also turn on the local radio in the van early in the game. The music is kinda country, but I thought it really added to the atmosphere. I enjoyed it even though I don't particularly like country music. I personally loved the game, even if it was a fairly short game. 🥰 My only critique: I wish the dialogue options had more of an impact on the relationships with the residents. Some do with the 2 characters you can choose to start a romance with. And some dialogue options influence how the story ends, no spoilers. You'll see! But when it comes to the rest of the residents, the dialogue choices you make don't really matter. Other than that, I had a lot of fun driving around delivering mail, getting to know the people and following the story!I rate it 9/10! I got it for a cheaper price though, I don't think it's really worth the full €19,99 because it's short and really the only thing you do is drive, deliver mail and talk to people.

_childDocuments_.review: I expected and hoped for a relaxing game and got a boring, underdeveloped mess with a great marketing team. Towards the middle of week two I dreaded playing and just wanted it to be over. I didn't care about the ending anymore. There came a point where I chose the rudest dialogue option every time because I hated everyone, tried to commit grand theft auto and to destroy my surroundings with the truck but sadly it and everything around it is indestructable, so I couldn't even rage properly.Before continuing my rant, I want to say this: The world really is beautiful. It feels cozy and the sun changing during the day added to it. The initial magic fades after some time, but I reckon that's not on the devs. I also loved the minigame in the diner. Let's begin with the indestructable truck as an exampe. Why the mechanic if the truck can't break down? (and why does the mechanic say she can work on the radio in the truck to add more stations? I really drove there trying to get her to do that the day after that dialogue, becuase at that point the 3 songs were already annoying. I would've been fine with license free music ffs.) Also, why the gas station? Why the boat rental? I wanted to get one and go out on the lake so bad. Why the shop with the owner crying about everyone coming in and nobody buying anything, and then I can't buy anything either? Why can't I sit down and get some lunch at the diner? ALSO how is there a movie rental place, and one of my two options every evening is watching TV, YET I CANNOT RENT ANY MOVIES. Don't put all these things in the world just for us to look at them. That doesn't add to the world, it makes me cry about what could've been.And that's the biggest problem I have with this game. It's all talk. (Except with the people on the sidewalk or the people sitting in the diner, you aren't ever able to talk to them.) You truly can't do anything except deliver post and work yourself through the forced boring, flat plot and endless cutscenes and dialogues that you can't even skip. The world / town feels like an empty shell. I became sadder and sadder, more and more coming to the realization that I will not be able to do anything like the above mentioned things ever in the two weeks. Maybe this is just me and I love open world and exploring every little corner too much. Maybe this is just me and I interpreted the game wrong before even buying it. Nonetheless, there's something else. The characters and the delivery. I don't really know how to put it into words but I became so enraged at the fact that you only ever deliver packages and letters to people as a means to trigger an event. Example: the annoying granny.  You meet her daily in the beginning, always talking to her and getting to know her. Then you NEVER deliver anything to her again until in week 2, when she needs a catsitter. That day she conviniently receives something and waits for you, standing next to her letterbox. Why can't she JUST get a letter once in a while? It just made me so angry paired with the fact that nobody other than the five same people open the door for you when ringing their doorbell. It felt like lazy design. At best, Lake feels Early Access. All talk, no exploring, no actual freedom, no interactions, no sprint. It didn't relax me, it enraged me. There's just something off about everything. Lake feels unfinished and very much unpolished.If you're going to buy this, buy it when at least 50% off because at this stage it's worth $10 tops. §20 with 4-6h of playtime and zero replay value is insane. Like I said, they definitely did well on the marketing. I hope they use the money they made with Lake to take their time on the next game. Good luck to them.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: Lake is a story-driven game where you play as a daughter who replaces her father as a postman. All actions take place in a small town around a lake. On your way you will meet many interesting characters and situations. Incredibly beautiful graphics in a stylized low-poly style are my weakness. Silence, calm and comfort, that's what I felt when I started playing this game. In addition, a simple and interesting plot complemented the whole harmony. The work of a postman diluted the gameplay and gave time to think and relax, but not everything was as we would like...The first thing that catches your eye is the  and emotions. This game is built on a deep plot and there is such a huge flaw here. Most of the time the animation is good, the mouth opens in time with the speech, but when the character expresses emotion, it is not visible at all.The second big problem is the . The game has traffic and pedestrians, but they are implemented very poorly. The number of people and cars is extremely small. I understand it's a small city, but they could be increased in the town center. What about the draw distance, it immediately breaks the magical feeling of the game. There are no trees visible on the other side of the lake, only the terrain, although there is vegetation there, if you get close enough. Why you can’t put low-poly LODs of trees or pictures is not clear.There are also minor bugs. For example, the game map for navigation does not match the real world, the roads are different in many places. Sometimes there are visual errors in game locations. And for some reason, the  when we put letters there. The animation of the characters sometimes plays crookedly and we can ring the bell while being two meters away from it. There are many such things and this also has a very negative effect on the gaming experience.The last thing that upset me was the 10 photo limit with the camera and the inability to save those photos. The game has amazing stylized graphics, but . This is the biggest minus!Anyway, I recommend only buying the base game at a discount. I’ll write about the DLC in a separate review, but in short, this is a terribly boring addition, don't buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: I RECOMMEND, BUT WITH HEAVY STIPULATIONS!This is one of the most relaxing and fun games I've ever played and I desperately wish that there was playability after you finish it. It's peaceful and you get REALLY into delivering the mail, but once it's done, it's done.The developers have something special here and I desperately hope that they expand on it; fill in some of the houses, make it possible to keep playing after the end. Anything, really! I do still recommend it, but the 6.1 hrs I have on record was start to finish with it paused on occasion. I reckon I could do it start to finish in about 5hrs. It's totally worth it! But maybe wait until it's on sale as £16 is a lot for such a short amount of gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: A quiet, reflective game. You drive around in your mail truck, listening to the radio and stopping to chat with neighbors while you deliver packages. Throughout the whole game, it's clear the main character is ruminating on her life and what direction she wants to go next, but her thinking is done in such a background way that it gives players the time and space to think about their own lives. This is a game that makes you feel like you're on sabbatical and could do anything you want with your life after it ends.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful game sure to make you take plenty of screenshots, along with having a nice, albeit small, selection of music, some good audio, and some pretty good voice acting.Honestly, this is just a nice chill game to relax and play, the story is also pretty enjoyable, with two interesting endings and a neat third one. (Just neat because you don't get to have any of the love interests join you there.)As for the bad part, the only thing I'd have to put in this section would be the surprising amount of bugs. I wouldn't say it's anything deal-breaking or of the sort, but you do get them a decent amount of times. For example, sometimes the audio cuts out semi-completely, not just the radio, if it were, that'd be fine because it's intentional, as they stated, but also the car sounds. I think this mostly happens near the tunnel, some text that isn't meant to be there when you pull up and leave the camera mode when you get it, sometimes a different sky when reloading a save that didn't have it sunny, there's also some missing audio like the 'guitar song' in the campfire or a voiceline or two. (I think the missing voice line only happened once, though.)Although a pretty major one I had was the day after I had interacted with Lori at the arcade machine, I decided to interact with her again (because Maureene had told me about open mic and was wondering if I'd mention it to Lori) and it just teleported me all the way back to the diner and played the same arcade interaction game of me having beaten her high score that happened the previous day. Obviously, the teleport left my truck behind. Later, I checked reloading the save to see if it'd happen again, and it didn't, so I don't know what was up with that.Now, that was certainly quite a bit, but honestly, I still thoroughly enjoyed my time playing this game. Again, it's more of a chill experience, and the bugs weren't that major except for that rare one.Overall, a beautiful chill experience with a nice story, good voice acting, and beautiful sights.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: Lake is a narrative experience with a chill vibe that doesn't go beyond what it aims to do.  It provides a short, but wholesome experience about the overarching choice to determine your direction in life.  It won't stun on a technical level, but the mechanics perfectly fit the experience.  The game feels more like a shallow river than a huge lake.If you are seeking a simple yet down to earth story with some light dialogue choices, Lake fits the bill.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, this is going to be a hefty and honest one. First of all, do make sure to understand my point; I write this commentary not just as a user, but as a game-designer myself. Therefore, do keep in mind that I want to be honest and professional. Same goes for others. How can I describe "Lake"? Cut corners. This is it. I played a lot of different games; I play-tested various prototypes, demos, and finished products; I also have my share of game creation expereince. This, however, is not a finished and polished product that you can enjoy to the fullest of its own abilities and borders. What I mean is, whenever you'd expect a certain part of the game to deliever an interesting and/or full expereince, you don't get it. Almost every other time, you'd receive an awkward, unnatural mess that really struggles to present a result that is SUPPOSED to be better but just cannot do so just as such. Which is a great shame! To not ramble without a reason and proofs, here is a few things that reallty stood out to me. And would be better to know before you'd buy this game... 1. The game is smooth with animations but plagued with glitches for them. For example, Meredith, the main protagonist, interacting with object through other objects. Or, for example, she'd start the animation sequence much earlier or later from an awkward position, making her float in the air, putting mail outisde of the mail boxes, etc.2. Faces and emotions. Oh, boy... If you're ready to see only emotionless husks of people that awkwardly walk around, trying to interact with each like ABSOLUTELY NORMAL HUMAN BEINGS, then go on. The lip synchronisation is non-existent here, any line of dialogue has more emotion than every character in the game combined, as there is literally no animations for the characters' eyebrows, eyes, or most of the face of that matter... A bit of an uncanny valley, to be completely honest. 3. Optimnization here sometimes forgets about itself. I played with some settings, made the game run smooth on my iron, but even with all that, the background processes were always able to pile up into an inconsistent mess that made my computer smoke any other time. For example, NPC-s driving cars have a real big problem with wayfinding and would inevitably stuck into a column of cars. And they're not gone until the day is finished, mind you! At the end of the shift, when you're returning to the post office, and the line of cars reaches the other end of the street, this somehow makes the game to REEEEEALLY struggle. And believe me, this is not the only thing. Far from it... I just don't want to keep it longer than it already is. 4. The storytelling is another piece of work here. While not having any problem with the vibe (I actually really liked it), the awkward way the characters present the exposition, the situations, and the dialogue... Combining it with the emotionless faces, and all of that looses all its weight and vibe, being unable to emerge you into the experience. 5. The mail work itself. Well, perhaps it was me at the end of the game, loosing my screws with the piling little problems, but the process became tedious at best. The idea of delivery is a real good one, and it is a good relaxing expereince. Additionally, the chance of interacting with more NPC-s, hearing stories, and making decisions were truly the things that drove me further into the game! But, alas, soon it became an absolute slug of an expereince... I was simply anxious to finish with the tasks not even looking forward for the bits of the story that were so disconnected that I was truly amazed by it. 6. The music. I'll be short. DON'T. HAVE. A. RADIO. WITH. ONLY. THREE. SONGS.I can go on for a while, but I'll stop here. Because, regardless of everything, there are good things that I want to tell about the game as well. As I said, the atmosphere is great! The story is interesting! Would've been interesting, if it wasn't delivered by the androids with no knowledge of human's face expressions. The world is cozy. Yes, regardless of evereything, it is nice and really cozy, and I liked it! Now, to conclude, as I said, I have my own expereince with game design.first-hand expereince, as a matter of fact. And every new step that I took in this game, just signaled about cut corners. A lot of marvelous and really cool ideas, not so much quality on the execution. Or, better be said, not enough time for the proper execution with the finished expereince. "Lake" is the game that was made with passion and, it seems, not enough time. "Lake" is the game that you want to love, and it wants to love you by giving you a wholesome experience with  great expostion! How-to-the-ever, it is hard to do in the game's current state. It is unpolished, plagued with little bugs, underdeveloped, and not properly play-tested to the descent level. Think of my review whatever you want, take it with a handful of ssalt, if you may, but it is my honest first-hand expereince. If you're still willing to try the game for yourself, go for it! See, if I'm wrong. The game still deserves the attention for what it tries to be. Best of luck to everyone!
