_childDocuments_.review: Lake is a very special game about coming back to your childhood town and choosing your own path in life, and as someone in University constantly thinking about what I'm going to do for the rest of my life it hit me pretty hard, probably harder than it should have tbh. It provided me with one of the best experiences I've ever had playing a video game, and yet I can't recommend it to everyone. It's a game that unfortunately has some very serious issues, some of which you won't even be aware of until you do a second playthrough of the game. There will be no story spoilers in this review.I absolutely loved my time with Lake. You play as Meredith who is taking a break from her big city life to go work as a postal worker in the small town she grew up in. The task of being a postal worker driving around this small town set on  a beautiful lake was something that grabbed my interest right away. As you carry out your job, you meet both new and familiar characters who you not only build new relationships with, but also repair old relationships. You can also help characters with various tasks if you choose to do so. The more you talk to and help these characters, the more your relationships with them grow. They really did feel like real people to me, and I felt as if the relationships we had were real. As you drive around the town day after day delivering mail, you start to learn the layout. By the end of my time with it, I barely had to use my map to get around. This all creates a very real sense that you really do live in this town. You feel a connection to the people that live there, and to the town itself. You can make choices that affect the outcome of the game and the final moments of the game genuinely made me sad, but in the happiest of ways. I never minded doing the mail delivery and didn't use any fast travel or autopilot because I genuinely loved driving around the town listening to the music, although some more tracks on the radio would've been nice. As beautiful as the lake and setting is, the game is one of the most poorly optimized games I think I've ever played. The game VERY frequently had frame rate issues especially in the forest are, and the amount of trees, buildings, cars, and people just popping in and out of the world or just disappearing entirely was insane. I would be driving down the street and people would just disappear right next to me. It didn't only happen in the open world either, but in cut scenes, characters would just disappear or teleport somewhere else on screen randomly, it was just bizarre.  Speaking of cut scenes, I'm not sure if the animation team just wasn't very good or if it came down to bugginess but there would be times when characters would just not move their lips when talking and the animation at times felt like I was watching animatronics on a theme park ride with how stiff animations were. There were also many many times when during a cut scene parts of the environment would just load in halfway through it. These issues often distracted from the often interesting and engaging conversations happening on screen which was a real shame. Lake presents you with the illusion of choice. You're often given chances to make decisions that in the moment feel like you're actually influencing the conversations you're having but in reality, your input matters very, very little. During my playthrough of the game I thought every choice I made mattered, the game made it seem that way, but the second and third times I loaded up my save at the end of the game to get some achievements I missed, it became very very obvious that no matter what you say, the conversations you have will be exactly the same. This didn't bother me at all during my first playthrough, as I felt I really was influencing the conversations I was having, but going back made it very apparent how little choice I really had. During my first playthough I always selected the options that kept conversations going as I was genuinely interested in talking to them but the second and third times I went back into the game I tried ending conversations early to speed up the process and they just kept talking. I would say something like "Sorry, I have to go now" and the other character would just continue on for 5 more minutes talking. Why even give the player this choice if it doesn't actually do anything? I can imagine someone choosing different options then the ones I picked, and being absolutely baffled and confused as to how these conversations play out because some of them are ridiculous. Overall, if you want a relaxing game with a really nice story, and characters, I think Lake is worth it on a sale. $20 is far too much considering just how many bugs, it has and how poorly optimized it is. If you don't mind the illusion of choice then I think you'll enjoy making your own decisions, however if you're playing this game because you want to truly impact the outcome of your conversations and really meaningfully impact the game, look elsewhere. The ending of this game is pretty decent, and if the themes about reconnecting with where you came from, or choosing your own path in life are ones you want to explore, then this game will be even more enjoyable. _childDocuments_.review: I have a specific category in my Steam library for chilled games, the kind of game I want to play after a stressful or emotional day. This one sits right in that list. It's not a game you'd obsess over and pump a hundred hours into, it's something you play for 30 minutes at a time when you just want to breathe.  Ostensibly it's a game about being a temporary mail worker filling in for 2 weeks at the post office of the town you grew up in but moved away from. Initially that's all you do, deliver post. You can't crash (you can hit objects but nothing happens), can't run anyone down, and can't get hurt. The van is slow, you can't run, there's really no challenge at all. That sounds weird but it's the beauty of the game.  As the days go by you reconnect with old friends from the small town and meet new ones and these relationships are the crux of the game. The dialogue choices, while something of an  of choice, really make you feel a connection to people. The writing and voice acting are fantastic and make the conversations feel joined up. You get a sense of the emotions which so many games fail on. As you engage with people you help them with small tasks, life choices, or just learn about them, and there's even a couple of love interests.I'm a similar age to Meredith and live a similar life. Working in computers after moving away from the sleepy town I grew up in. As such I relate so hard to this story I've find myself questioning if I should move back home and take a nice simple community job!Setting the game in the mid 80s also harks back to the simplicity of the time. With no internet or smartphones, there's a certain peace and isolation to the town. The only interactions are the people you physically meet on your rounds.The game has some flaws: Zooming the map sometimes doesn't work and there's no animation for getting in and out of the van (it just quickly fades to black) which is odd given how much you do this. Also the facial animations are minimal and sometimes the mouth movement bears no resemblance to the words being spoken. The radio has a desperately short playlist and, while the songs are quite fitting for the atmosphere, they grate after a while. The game is also very short. Even taking it at the leisurely pace it's designed to be played, driving your route without fast travel, and filling your days with the optional tasks, you can complete the story in about 4-5 hours. There is some replay value in choosing different conversation options, but this just reveals how little most of the choices actually matter.Overall, I love this game but would only recommend it if you enjoy this kind of relaxing interactive story (it's almost not a game at all).

_childDocuments_.review: You can watch my first impressions review here: Nice, simple game with a simple premise, just driving mail around a sleepy Oregon town. There are plenty of faces, familiar and new to Meredith, to meet and get to know, and the writing doesn't waste your time with lengthy conversations. _childDocuments_.review: Gosh, what a disappointment. I was so excited about this game, which seemed like it would be right up my street...contemplative, with a strong narrative. But it's such a letdown.First of all, the graphics...they're TERRIBLE. The textures in particular are abysmal. There's no bump mapping or displacement mapping, so everything in the game looks flat and dull. We're in a small town surrounded by forests, but the trees are rendered as tapered cylinders with broad-brush lines where the folds in the bark should be. Buildings look flat with one uniform colour all over. The mail van is basically a cube with one chamfer on the edges. And this is with my graphics options within the game set to ULTRA on every setting.The story is cliche-ridden and full of the most awful stereotypes - the crazy cat lady with the tremulous voice acting is really quite offensive, and there's a very odd scene where the main character invites a sixteen-year-old girl over to her house to watch an R-rated horror film. What were the developers thinking?Finally, the subtitles are REALLY bad and are full of terrible grammar. For instance, "Coffee. How could anyone survive without it." That's a question...so it should finish with a question mark, not a full stop. Conversely "I just came home and was wondering if everything worked out alright?" is NOT a question, so it should end in a full stop, NOT a question mark. There's a constant stream of comma splices or "run-on sentences", for instance "You know, I better get some sleep now, my plane leaves early in the morning," or "I hope I can fill his shoes, he hardly ever missed a day", and whoever wrote the subtitles has decided to use the phrase "all right" throughout the entire game when the correct word would be "alright", e.g. "are you all right, madam?"The overall effect is one of shoddy development - on the first day in the game there were literally no other cars on the streets when I delivered a full day's worth of mail, which was spooky. On subsequent days, traffic suddenly appeared, but if I parked on the left side of the road and exited the van to deliver some mail, I would come back two minutes later to find a line of maybe 5-6 vehicles lined up in front of mine - are drivers in Providence Oaks incapable of overtaking? Or did the developers just not have the skills to code that? I think we know the answer.So...on the positive side the original soundtrack is really good, and there's a great choice of modern country songs on the radio when you're driving around. Lake had SUCH potential...it's just a shame to see it delivered with so little panache.

_childDocuments_.review: I've just finished the whole game with some of the possible endings. It's a short game, and I recommend it 100% if A) you are looking for a calming game with wonderful scenery, a strong plot and believable characters, andB) you are good with repetitive tasks.I'm not sure if I would have paid the full price for such a short game, but it's definitely worthwhile if on sale. I bought it at 50% off during the Steam Autumn Sale. This game is so wholesome. Great story and characterisation, and I actually liked all of the voice acting. Driving around this gorgeous lake town is surreal, and I found myself checking out all of the different angles, especially when the mail van was on autopilot. It was quite immersive, and I actually felt as though I took a little holiday when I was playing the game.I really loved the life wisdom delivered through different characters in the story, especially Maureen *spoiler*  *end spoiler*. I thought all of the dialogue was really good as well, and I enjoyed having different options, especially the sassy responses. Also, the different options really helped break up the monotony during subsequent play-throughs.Delivering mail for two straight weeks in-game did get a little bit too repetitive after the first week - but the little surprise cut-scenes you get for selected deliveries makes it really rewarding and worthwhile. And did I mention how calming this job is, in the game? If you're on the fence about buying this game, e.g. not sure if delivering mail for 2 in-game weeks would be too boring for you, I highly recommend trying the free demo first - I thought it was pretty generous and played through two full days - I could go on with day 3 in the demo but I was already smitten so I stopped to buy the game. My saved progress from the demo was transferred to the full game - THANK YOU devs for that nice touch!- If you don't like the voice acting or it's going too slow for you, you can turn on the Skip button for the dialogue in the settings. - During mail routes, I amused myself by looking at the scenery, trying to park perfectly, trying to drive on the correct side of the road, seeing if I could stop the van perfectly next to the mailbox/door, and purposely driving terribly such as reversing all the way until the next destination. - I really appreciated the "Fast Travel"/teleportation spots and autopilot features when they were available, on the map. These options helped to relieve the monotony and made the mail route go a lot faster during moments when I was bored and just wanted to fast-forward to the next scene with the love interest.Now I have to make the agonising decision of whether I want to get the DLC, which isn't on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, however, the playthrough I experienced was a buggy mess that ruined my time with this game.It could've just been me, but I kept getting audio delay that caused continuous lag spikes throughout my playthrough when the audio would catch up to where I was. Not to mention, I wanted to be able to listen to the dialogue, but half of the time, it ended up never playing due to said audio delay. I'm totally fine with reading subtitles, but I wanted to be invested in what the characters were talking about between one another and this bug made that extremely difficult. While I will admit the game is relaxing and cozy, these feelings are attached to a half-baked story with conversations that are, often times, poorly written. I also think the decision-making aspect of this game is terribly designed because, genuinely, there are about two integral decisions that will affect the outcome of your story. Everything else is simply filler - which makes it feel like a waste of time - and it does not matter what you do. This is a relatively short game, about 4 hours of gameplay/story (if you only go for one ending and stay on task for the most part), yet it manages to feel dull, repetitive, and drawn out after about 2 hours.This may be a bit nit-picky considering there was a small developer team, but we seriously couldn't get an animation for getting in and out of the mail truck? The fact that there's a tiny loading screen between entering and exiting the truck gets pretty annoying to deal with when you consider the amount of deliveries you need to do by the end of the game. Also, a two or three song radio playlist? THANK GOD you can shut the radio off - although funny enough, I could not most of the time because of my audio delay bug :D! The developers tried to be cheeky by adding in a small subplot about how the DJ was attempting to add more songs to the city's playlist, but it just comes off as laziness on their part. Lastly, Merideth's running speed is HORRENDOUS. Her "jog" - if you can even call it that - is an ever so slightly faster version of her walk. You're better of saving your finger the trouble from holding down the "sprint" key and just walking to maybe get a few more minutes of enjoyment from the game.Speaking of audio, the lack of sound effects for driving off-road or on bridges is upsetting. Given that the scenery of the game is pretty solid, it is disappointing that minute details like these sound effects are missing. Also, for being a lake town, the fact that the sound of water flowing was absent in areas where it should be kills a lot of the atmosphere that could've been beautiful. They took time to add birds chirping - which, if I might add, breaks the deafening silence when there is an audio delay/glitch - but missed out on these other small ones? It's a shame.On an aside, be prepared to listen to the same dialogue for about an hour straight if you'd like to complete all of the endings of the game for the respective achievements; endings of which give zero gratification.I may have given this game a slight pass if you could hold/interact with the cats... But, you can't even do that...I'm unsure if this bug I mentioned above was solely something on my end or something other players have experienced, but I can most definitely say that it left a sour taste in my mouth regarding my final thoughts of the game. I loved the vibe of the game based on the trailers I had seen, but, ultimately, I was left disappointed by the playthrough I completed. I would say to not let the positive reviews fool you, as most are complimenting it based purely on the fact that it is "relaxing." Only buy this on sale, or skip out on it entirely.

_childDocuments_.review: Here is some harsh criticism and a few reasons of why you might enjoy "Lake."If you're already fond of indiebait such as "Firewatch" and "Gone Home" and have no issues with their narratives then add Lake to your cart for ~6.5 hours of that Cascadia drama, with a town that reminds me of the one in Alan Wake, or Twin Peaks.Take the above, cross "Life is Strange" with less polish and narrative choice with "Death Stranding" sans the heavy Kojima themes and you get this humble story about a mildly autistic woman resolving her midlife crisis. The finest point in my playthrough was going to the movies with the movie store clerk and having to choose between  So the developers are culturally self-aware in this project. What they do with this self-awareness is double down on ideas and matters that are covered in the media they are influenced by.Rather than, say, assimilate directly the social commentary through smoother writing or through player exposure, there is this 50/50 choice of exposition versus experience.  The presentation is heavy handed and offers the subject no cathartic payoff for emotionally engaging with the plot. Think "Disco Elysium" but without Harry.And that is Lake's flaw. It seems to present a tone, or have something profound to say about contemporary connected life that can be observed in the captured historical era of the late Reagan economy, early personal computer, end of the Cold War, "pace" though it has a balancing problem from a writer's perspective. Too direct and formal, it's dry. Hydrated, it's corny.I was born the year the game was set in. Playing as the protagonist and reflecting on my life, the game produced more anxiety and angst about my life than intended in a game that's about delivering mail. For that, I can overlook the narrative faults, disjointed voice acting, and the appearance that conflicts in design were never settled, just melded together. And that showed.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never written a bad review before. I am ALL FOR chill and relaxing games but this one was just a little *toooo* slow for me. I think it would be amazing for other people if truly mindless games are for you. I just couldn't get into it though because this type of mindless just felt TOO slow and like nothing was really happening/getting done.The two biggest things I disliked about the game were the super slow movements and the dialogue:The "sprint" is barely a speed walk at best, which makes delivering packages super slow and tedious. Other animations (like getting out of the truck, getting back in, taking your camera out for a photo, putting the camera away, etc) felt super annoying to constantly do when you have to sit there for a few seconds until the animation/cut is over. I cannot stress enough how slow the game just felt and plays.The dialogue was pretty cringe a lot of the time and prevented me from getting immersed in the world. A lot of it felt predictable in a way. I think the game also felt like it wanted to have these deep conversations and character depth but in the perspective of you JUST moving to town, it all feels fake and unrealistic that all this stuff is happening after being in town for a day or two. And after a few more days, you can already have a girlfriend lol. It felt like there was no buildup or true building of connections.I think the game wanted you to feel like you had a lot of options but the story still felt linear and flat. I think there were only two romance options and it truly felt like the game was heavily pushing you towards one certain individual.There were some bugs that would occur (both auditory and graphically). The game didn't run as well as I would thought it would for smaller game. Not a huge deal, but just nitpicking. Again, I do think that this game could be enjoyed by others. I just personally couldn't get into it primarily because of the dialogue and slowness of the character.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best indie games I have done so far. If you like the Firewatch-style games, with characters reflecting on one's life and one's choices in a 1980's atmosphere, chances are you're going to like this.  A lot of people compare it to Death Stranding as it's essentially just a delivery game. Therefore, if you're expecting much of the gameplay with a crazy scenario that'll make your head flip around with an unforeseen plot twist, you're probably going to be disapointed.The whole point of this game is in the ambiance and the way you reflect on the game. The game makes you feel like you're this character who's coming back to their hometown for a 2-week holiday and you remininsce all the memories created here, enjoy the nature where you grew up, meeting up with people you used to know. If you have moved out of your hometown where you grew up as a kid to work in the city after graduating from university, this game will hit really close to home. The scenary of the game was beautiful, the characters and the level design were all really attractive and made me want to play the game more to get to know the city and the characters more, the scenario and the way you can built up your own story with your own choices gives you freedom to make this character look like you, and the whole chilling while delivering parcels was just awesome. I loved this game and I would recommend it to anyone who liked chilling in Firewatch thinking about life and people who love to visit their hometown in the countryside after moving to the city.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazingly cute slice-of-life game. Overall, it has so much atmosphere, beauty, satisfaction, intrigue. Very much worth the play through; even the grind in order to get the achievements. However, with that said, I do have a few constructive criticisms/gripes:- can't skip cutscenes straight to decisions if you've seen them before; you're forced to rewatch them in full during extra play-throughs- lacks open world elements and immersion - can't interact with most objects or non-story people/animals; can't go off the beaten path, you're limited to your daily delivery route & story-specific dialogue (ex. can't stop in the diner for a coffee or the video rental store for a movie; some hiking trails are blocked off); people walk around outside without umbrellas while it's raining- lacks asset variety/realism inside shops (ex. the shelves in the grocery store contain the exact same assets repeated, rather than organized sections of types like actual grocery/convenience store shelves would be stocked)- NPCs can be very passive aggressive, which can get annoying esp with your limited response options- can't interact with the map while morning radio show is on- won't let you deliver mail while on certain side quests that require you to carry something around, interfering with efficiency- camera view has a bad habit of resetting while driving, forcing constant mouse movements- cars will sometimes bug out either randomly or if you block them, and can cause traffic jams and block sections of roads- the game only contains country music (with exception of the very end which I won't spoil), which really sucks if you despise countryOther than these issues, the game runs very smoothly with beautiful art and a hometown feel to it. Definitely memorable and has replay value after having not played it in a long time. I would absolutely love to see more games in this same style. Performing mail delivery while familiarizing yourself with the town and getting to know the people who live in it is such a rewarding experience. Worth the play for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: Lake is a beautiful game. Not so much in how it looks, it looks fine I guess, but rather it is beautiful for the story it tells and allows you to tell along with it. I think it can best be explained by comparing it to those movies they always show in Christmas, wherein a driven but overworked person returns to their hometown and discover what life is all about. _childDocuments_.review: This game is unique among all the other story-based slice-of-life games I've played because **it treats you like an adult and doesn't provide any easy answers**. As a working adult myself I totally empathized with the MC about all the choices she has to make about her friendships, her family, and her relationships. I also love how the game doesn't judge you for the choices you make, even if that means parting ways with someone you've grown close to.HOWEVER.There are some parts of the game that need significant improvement:1. No Dialogue Skipping?! - Replaying the game is extremely annoying because you have to sit through conversations you've already had.2. Transitions b/w Walking & Driving - The game fades to black every time you go from driving <-> walking. It's jarring and really doesn't help with the atmosphere.3. Relationship Ending with  None of those are game-breaking, but they make a big difference between an enjoyable experience and one that could be considered one of the best story games out there.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve been awaiting the arrival of Lake and it didn’t live up to the hype. From the demo and trailer, it seemed to be a very interactive game where you delivered mails, hang out with your neighbours or explore the lakeside— sadly, the only interactions we got were controlled ones.  There’s no exploring around the place after work, you mostly get two options at home - read a book or watch the TV. You do get some fun hanging out with a few of the characters (if you chose to do so) but again, it’s in a very controlled and limited setting.Some things I liked: The scenery is beautiful and it started off as a very relaxing game. You only get to interact with the characters that’s already established so you can’t randomly go up to a house, knock and expect someone to be there — that made delivering parcels really boring, you just knocked and leave it on the doorstep. I wished we could have mini interactions here and there — being offered drinks or even a senior asking for help with the remote, etc. All in all, if I knew this is what I’ll get, I would have waited for it to be on sale, I don’t think it’s worth the full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved this game. Who thought driving around delivering mail (really - that's it) would be so interesting. Of course, it's the people and the relationships that make the story, as well as the beautiful, relaxing scenery. I really like the premise: returning to your hometown; discovering the things that have changed, and reconnecting with people from the past - or not. I also really appreciated the two choices of romantic leads and was incredibly invested. The witty, playful banter with a "will they, won't they" - wonderful.I also appreciated all the little things that showed this game was aiming to be relaxing. For one, as much as I enjoy games where decisions can have major consequences, I appreciate that (beyond your final decision), your choices mostly affect dialogue and cur scene options; nothing that would make you agonise. Autodrive as an option to get back to the post office was a great way to end the day, being able to just appreciate the scenery, or take a quick break. Importantly as well; time exists, but you are never stressed about the time, as any events you decide to do simply happen after the work day. This game perfectly captures the charm of country life, and did genuinely make me think about my own work-life balance and overworking. Just by delivering the mail and having quick conversations with others, I came to care about these characters, and also really get to know Meredith, and how I think she'd respond (great voice acting there, as well). This game was an absolute delight and very unique - if you're looking for a relaxing game, definitely give this a go.

_childDocuments_.review: Man, I wish I lived here.In "Lake" you play as Meredith Weiss. You take over the job of your father delivering the mail in a small town in Oregon after leaving the big city because of a break.Lake's gameplay is fairly simple. You go to the post office first thing in the morning, deliver mail and packages throughout the day, go back to the post office after delivering all of them, return the truck and go home to do your own thing. Obviously, there's a bit more to it than just that. Another thing you can do are interact with the people in town. This includes helping them by doing a "quest", progressing your "story" or just simply talking to them. However, most of your time will be driving around town delivering packages and mail. Even though I'm not that far into the story yet, I'm still writing this review because I wanted to share some of my thoughts.Lake is a really nice looking game accompanied by beautiful scenery, interesting characters and, overall, alright music. While the gameplay is mostly the same, as far as I'm concerned, it's not too repetitive. Although, not . I can definitely see delivering packages and mail all the time getting repetitive and boring fast. But for now, it isn't. This is mostly because this is a nice looking game and there's a lot to see. The nature, and especially the lake, are the high points of the graphics and art style and give a calming vibe, which the game is trying to do and definitely succeeds in. While driving the delivery truck, you can also listen to the local radio. But other than a couple of songs and the occasional morning announcements when starting the day, that's about it. Now, here are some things that I think could be improved on because this definitely isn't a flawless game.For starters, I really think that this game could've been polished and optimized a bit more. It certainly is a good-looking game, but sometimes the textures are a bit janky.  As well as the movements of the characters and cars are sometimes a bit stiff and robotic. Walking on stairs, for example, has no different animation than just walking vertically, so to say. I've also noticed some cars, kind of, "popping in" while I was driving around delivering mail. The voice actors did a pretty good job overall, in my opinion. But during conversations between the characters, it sounded kind of unnatural. The dialogues don't really flow well. It's as if the voice actors did all their lines separately and the developers went ahead and copy and pasted the corresponding lines one after another. While I assume (and understand) that the lines were  recorded this way, it does result in unnatural sounding conversations which isn't the desired result considering you get options on what to reply and the game lists itself as a "choices matter" kind of game. Another thing I think could be improved on is the number of songs. I think there's about five songs right now (?). That, in itself, isn't that much since you spend most of your time driving. But on top of that, all the songs sound very similar. They're all country-styled. And while it does fit the game, and I like most of them, they get repetitive very fast. I once got the same song three times in a row! One simple thing that would improve on this would be to add little filler pieces in between songs like real radio stations do. Like, "You're listening to..." or, "This next song is called...", etc. I think that would already make it feel much more real and less repetitive.Overall, Lake is a very relaxing, nice-looking, interesting game that, unfortunately, has some small, but noticeable flaws. However, if you look passed these small issues, there's a beautiful game with a nice story and characters in a town that I wish I would live in.A solid 7 for me but if the issues I mentioned were to be fixed, the number would be bumped up to a 7.5 or maybe even an 8.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like casual, cozy games, Lake is worth a shot. I liked the game, but I wish it could be more. Delivering mail is pretty mundane (Obviously), but there weren't many special interactions with neighbors to make up for it. I found myself getting bored with repetitive tasks and just zoning out until I could get to the second part of the day. I wanted more interactions with the town! You haven't been back home in years, surely you should have more loose ends to tie up or people to connect with other than Kay? As far as technical stuff when delivering mail it's pretty annoying getting in and out of the van even though there's no door and you're inches away from the mailbox? I felt like this could have cut so much time off your day. The love interests were so boring. Steve is so...dull. Absolute dingbat. It makes him kinda endearing and his ending was sweet, I just wish you could spend more time connecting with him rather than the apartments. The same goes for Angie. She had such a fun girl next door vibe and I liked that you got the chance to deliver tapes for her and go catch a movie out of town. Still, I just couldn't justify leaving a successful career behind for an unemployed girl who likes cinema.Enough complaining moving on to positives. The game still had a fun nostalgic feel and did a good job connecting you with Meredith. I do, however, wish she and everyone else would blink, but they're endearing nonetheless! I liked driving recklessly around town honking at sad npc cars. Overall, I would recommend it. I mean for 20 dollars it's an okay game. Maybe one day they can add more to it. I would actually like to see this game beefed up.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a short and relaxing game. I thoroughly enjoyed the beautiful scenery, the music and the overall experience of being in a quiet town like Providence Oaks. I do have some thoughts on the controls and some aspects of the gameplay. Like most that I've seen in the review section, I also was bothered with the "walk faster" option which really didn't seem to make enough of a difference from the normal walk speed. I can understand that this game was meant to be enjoyed at a slow pace but if an option like that was made available, I would hope it actually does something. I also had a bit of trouble with the response speed of the controls, I had to click “E” multiple times every time for it to react and that did affect the overall smoothness of my gameplay. There were also some minor issues in details like the lack of collision detection between cars and poles on the streets and parcels and doors as well as people and cars suddenly disappearing in front of you. These are minor but can ultimately affect the big picture.Lastly, I noticed you could “interact” with some objects in the game like benches at certain houses, but with a charming little town like this and its unique locations and people, it would have been great to be able to explore more and interact with them more. This would add on to the interpersonal aspect of the game and help players build a stronger connection with characters within the story and in turn, the town as a whole.I can appreciate Lake for what it is at the moment. I enjoyed it and loved the idea behind the story though it would be great to see some of the issues reflected in the reviews dealt with at some point. I would still recommend this game to anyone who enjoys calm and cozy vibes in games.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: Oh to be a mail carrier in a small town in the late 80's.Lake is a beautiful and relaxing game, though it should be noted that it's very short and quite limited. in terms of replay value as no choices besides the endings require a separate playthrough (even then as long as you save on the 13th you can just replay the last two days of cut scenes and make a separate ending choice for all achievements).All in all this game is lovely if you like relaxing, procedural, slight choice based games. I look forward to the devs future endeavours.  - There is no animation for getting in and out of the postal van, as this is something you do a lot having just a black screen ruins the immersion.  - The songs the game has are lovely and suit the game perfectly, very Gilmore Girls vibes! However, there are so few of them that I think a game where you spend a lot of your time driving really needs more. They address this in the game itself in a short scene, but it still feels like a loss.  - The animation style is really lovely, however the characters have no expression and the voice acting can be really stiff at times. It also feels like the creator really focused on only 1/3 of the ending possibilities as the others, and other conversations, don't feel immersive or impactful based on the choices you make   - I had many instances where I would attempt to get a package from the back of the truck, only for my hands to be empty. Sometimes I would have to repeat the action up to three times.  - Mo disappears mid scene when you are having dinner with Robert.  - When June asks if you'd like something to drink, she gets you one even if you say no.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the atmosphere of the game, it has a lovely artistic style to it. _childDocuments_.review: All and all this is a great game, but there are some cons and some pros. The big cons are that you can't pet the cats and that it is a short game with not a lot of re-playability (there is some, though if you don't mind some repetitiveness). Pros are that it is a gorgeous game! Seriously, this game is very peaceful and so beautiful. An important thing to keep in mind with this game is that it is short, but it really is meant to be played through slow. You're supposed to walk down trails, go sit by the lake, and stare at the cats damning the inability to pet any of them. This is the kind of game that you're supposed to RP with, put yourself into Meredith's shoes for the 8+ hours and reconnect with her childhood home and debate whether you should give up your promising career for something a little more slower pace. At the end of the day, I recommend this game. I enjoyed being Meredith for a bit and trying to figure out what to do with her future, and most of all I loved Providence Oaks. I would live there now honestly, I even tried to find the house I would want (I think I would try to get the church and remodel it, or steal Robert's house).
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: I really love the theme and the atmosphere - even the repetitive country songs coming from the radio.However, there's one major issue in the game:It's WAY too short. There's simply not enough time for any romantic tension to build up, or any other connections for that matter; not with the townspeople nor the town itself. (It doesn't matter if the main character is familiar with them - the player needs to get to know them too in order to immerse into the story.) Plus: if the 2 weeks should be enough for a romance to spark, at least give some options to actually flirt. Not just crack some jokes, help ppl out with their finances and accept a movie or a dinner as a 'thank you'.Anyhow, I do recommend the game. The plot itself hit very close to home, and I had a really chill time playing the game. I just wish it was longer and had more content. The way the game is right now is not worth the price, unfortunately.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: In Lake you play a woman named Meredith while she takes a break from her busy city life and high stress job and returns to the small Oregon lake town she grew up in, Providence Oaks. She temporarily fills a vacancy at the postal office and (re)meets many of its townsfolk.The gameplay is quite simple. You’re in Providence Oaks for 2 weeks and drive around in a postal van delivering mail and packages. Driving is easy enough and the game forces you to a max speed depending on the road you’re driving on. When you reach a delivery spot you then get out of the van, put stuff in the mailbox or you grab a package and ring the doorbell. When you’re not spending time walking or driving, you’ll be spending time socializing. This can happen during or after work and is quite limited and is solely story focused. Most social scenes in the game are just you and another NPC stiffly looking and talking at each other with occasional dialogue options.The story is nothing special but gets the job done. Your character takes a break and spends time as a postal worker. You meet people, sometimes do some stuff for them, get invested in the town and then choose what you want to do. There is only one major choice and there is no high stakes drama going on. It’s a simple story, for a simple town, for a simple game that just wants you to relax for a couple of hours. Which is fine. The graphics of the game are quite good. It’s all very colorful, happy, bright and does a good job of enhancing the beauty of the lake and its surrounding town and forests. It seems that the devs had quite a passion for the location of the game and it shows ingame. Providence Oaks looks beautiful and homely and the atmosphere is done very well. The game almost makes me want to live in a location just like it. The sound of the game is just fine. Neither bad nor exciting. It just gets the job done, however. The music in the game is quite good. Only two songs were composed by the devs and the rest are licensed, though I liked the dev composed song the most. Most songs are fun and fit the setting but it’s a short playlist and eventually you will probably want to turn off the radio in your van.The voice acting is also done decently. Every character had a decent actor behind it, but since there aren’t any situations ingame where a height of emotion is happening, the actors never really get pushed on that regard.This game doesn’t do anything truly bad but there are a few spots that might need some attention.Lake is a really colorful and lovable game. It’s not meant to be deep or evoking. It’s just there for you to have a fun relaxing time in a nice location with a friendly storyline and some decent music. And it also has a couple of easy achievements, if that’s your kind of thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed playing this game through once, but won't be replaying it anytime soon due to unskippable "If you've played it once, you've heard this already" cutscenes. I started it up again and just couldn't deal with it. I liked delivering the mail and exploring the town (though I wish there was a bit more exploring you could do and more photos you could take).I didn't find the game as relaxing as some did, and Meredith's tone of voice sounded like me when I'm working customer service: overly chipper to hide the fact that I can't wait for the conversation to be over. Just not authentic or actually invested in anything that was happening. Only the scenes with Kay were the most believable.I'd recommend watching part of a playthrough to see if this game is for you. As a big fan of "walking sims" with exploration, and looking for a calming game similar to "Eastshade," I set my hopes a little too high. Worthwhile, but not exactly what I wanted.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: What I like:Multiple life choices for the main character of the story. You can choose to be kind, you can also choose to stand up for yourself OR be a bit mean to others.Various characters to interact with, sometimes I miss them during my delivery runs.Music is repetitive, but it gets to you, gives you a true vibe of small town in the middle of nowhere.The view is just breathtaking, wish you could venture out into some of these places in a semi-open world setting.Criticisms:Dialogues from certain characters felt incomplete and their mannerism towards the main protagonist felt off at time. For example, when the main protagonist confessed her feelings to another, it was not really acknowledge and brushed off. It was then picked back up DAYS after the conversation. Something that left a bitter taste, do they really care about the protagonist feelings? It needs that organic feeling.Missed some events such as the photography contest. Maybe its on me for not paying attention but if there are some indication or hints there is such contest I would have surely submitted the photos earlier.Limited interaction with characters that meant a lot to the protagonist. Some days during deliveries, I missed the human interaction with the protagonist best friend, her lover and sometimes the people at the diner. It won't hurt to include more dialogue to make the lonely days felt more bearable. There are days where you took a long trip throughout the town without having a meaningful conversation.However, I am glad I stumble onto this game purely by chance. I love a game where it takes you to another place, escape real life problems and just stay here... in this beautiful small town. I never wanted to leave but sometimes you have to move on. It doesn't hurt to give this one a try, for some it might even change their lives.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: I found the game to be really fun. I think the game is a little too short and the relationships that you could have had in the game fall kinda short but it is something to be expected from a title like this. Do I think the game is worth the $20 price tag, no. I think the game is worth $10 at best so I would grab it when it goes on sale because it is a fun game that is relaxing and just overall chill to play when you kinda just want to escape things in real life.After further reflecting on this game much later, I miss it and have desires to come back and play. I think the calming and laid back aspect of this game makes it amazing. It is so calm and just plain relaxing to sit back and hear the ambiance of the road, nature, and day to day life of most of the residents in this town.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: Lake is a nice game. I bought it for the relaxing aspect and the art direction. The fact that the main character decides to change her life and questions her future resonated in me :)If you accept the game for what it is, a repetitive yet relaxing mail delivery simulator in a charming environment, you will get what you need. The art is nice, driving is relaxing, there is no timing stress nor side quests that you can fail. Nothing crazy, just get the mail and the packages to their recipients, have some interactions with them and go back home when you're done. No ♥♥♥♥♥♥ boss neither.Around the end of the game though, I thought the game could have been a little more interesting with more content. They are only a few people you can interact with, the mail truck never gets damage, some side stories you don't seem to have a lot of control... I even thought at some point: "They could have done a Stardew Valley-like mailman simulator and that would have been glorious"...In summary: this is not a sandbox game, not a realistic car simulator game, and not a very deep visual novel. Just a nice & calm game that depicts a slice of life in the idealized 80s in the USA. And it does it well.PS: Kudos to the developers who mention in the credits that being a package delivery person is way more stressful than what's shown in the game :)

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game a ton. The visuals are great and it has some nice storylines. I'm going to play this game again to explore the other choices that can be made. _childDocuments_.review: A short game, but very sweet. It's an enjoyable experience, living in an idyllic small town by the lake. The gameplay is slow and not very exciting. I found myself wanting to get through mail delivery, or at least the letters, as quickly as possible, so I could activate the cut scenes you get when you drop off packages and meet with people after hours. But I wasn't bored. You just have to sit back and enjoy the relaxed pace. I've lived in plenty of towns like this, and I definitely wanted to stay at the end. It would have been nice to have more than two choices for romantic interests, but I liked both characters, and the others characters were entertaining. The highlight of the game is the dialog, which often made me laugh out loud, and the voice acting was perfect.

There are awkward hugs and even more awkward kisses. Some of the story kinda sucks and I wish it was written better. There's  You can't do anything about it and that is super bogus in my opinion. _childDocuments_.review: Don't play this having expectations.  This game is not like most games where there's a twist or some kind of darker underbelly of events to occur. The game makes you appreciate the small town that this game's world revolves around, and makes you think about a simpler life, focusing only on what's important.  The gameplay can be boring sometimes, but the story does a great job of captivating you... and just like in real life, the choices you have to make are not easy at all.  Would've been nice if there was a little more variety here n there in what you do, but I must say, overall, I enjoyed this game. _childDocuments_.review: If you can imagine Life is Strange or Deadly Premonition without any supernatural elements, murder mysteries, or active gameplay, then you have Lake. I know it sounds like I'm being uncharitable here, but there's a cozy vibe to the relatively low stakes of this game that make it a highly unique experience. You deliver mail to a small lakeside town in 1986 Oregon, meet a cast of quirky supporting characters, and ultimately try to figure out your future. Despite the rough graphics for being an obviously budget title, I think the strong performances and tranquil setting still manage to shine through. Listening to the same 8 catchy tracks on the radio perfectly replicates that sensation of working at a menial job with an unchanging selection of Top 40 songs stuck in your head all day. I'm going WAAAAAAAY down south!Despite only being 5-6 hours long, the mail delivery gameplay really does start to wear out its welcome by the end. I think Lake could have used some more minigames or alternate activities to break up the monotony a little. Still, I enjoyed the experience and would recommend it to anyone who likes pleasant normcore games from time to time.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. But grain of salt, i'm somebody that has 100+ hours in truck driving sims and also enjoyed Dear Esther, the original walking sim. The Dev's own description as "Slice-Of-Life" is spot on, as the whole game is living out 2 weeks of someone getting away from their big city job, for something a little slower pace.I saw someone talking about Firewatch in a discussion on this game and that game is a pretty good comparison to Lake, but maybe with the slight supernatural/mystery element of Firewatch removed. There are a few bugs I came across but nothing game breaking. Just sometimes I had to grab a box from the truck a second time because it didn't register my button press. Had to reload once to get the mini-map to come back up. The worst, which seems to be pretty consistent among bug reports, is getting teleported straight to a delivery location when getting into the truck but the truck doesn't come with you. But the fast travel system brings you and the truck to any point of interest on the map.The game length has been a bit of a touchy subject with a lot of people saying it too short, and wishing there was a free roam option after the story. Personally the length was perfect for me, I don't have the desire to jump into 20, 40, 60 hour games all the time and games I can finish in 2-3 sittings hit my sweet spot. And I totally feel the 6.4 hours this game gave me was worth the price. As far as the free roam mode goes more options are always good, but personally I doubt I would have taken advantage of it. Unless if it had continued conversations with residents, or some change up in how the work days went. But I can imagine some people being able to enjoy another 10-20 hours of just delivering and figuring out the optimum route.Overall I recommend the game as a nice little story, and a relaxing drive around a scenic Lake.

_childDocuments_.review: Lake is a beautiful narrative game that gives you a short glimpse into the lives of several people in an American small town in the 80s. You play a software developer who has returned to her hometown for the first time in 22 years, to take over her dad's job as a postman for two weeks. As such, you will drive around in a (fairly slow) van, deliver letters and parcels to various houses, and possibly reconnect with people who the main character knew from her childhood.The stories are loosely interconnected in the same way as lives between people in a small town are connected, but there is no big mystery or drama, and no overarching plot except for the main character eventually having to decide how to go on with her life. Player agency is limited - three of the relationships can develop in different ways depending on your actions (including two romance options), but all other stories are railroaded, your only options are to either engage with them or ignore them. The game does, however, a pretty good job of not letting you feel these limitations. Most of the dialogue flows naturally even though the NPCs often utter the exact same lines regardless of what you were saying, and your choices often feel impactful even when they aren't. The writing is fairly good, with a generally friendly tone and refreshing doses of humor every now and then, and made me feel for the characters.The game's biggest asset is its atmosphere. Slowly driving through beautiful scenery while listening to a few country/pop tracks can feel very relaxing, especially if you can get in the mindset of the main character, who sees this as a welcome vacation from a stressful day job. That said - if you _can't_ get into this mindset, then these tasks may also feel a bit boring, as there is really nothing to them. You cannot mix up deliveries (the game won't let you), you cannot crash your van (it just stops and/or respawns), you never need to hurry (there is no timer), and you cannot forget deliveries (you can't progress to the next day until your job is done). So in terms of game design, these tasks are just busywork to keep the player occupied in between the conversations that progress the story, which isn't great design in my opinion - but if you just want to escape for a few hours back into a time without cell phones, the Internet, hypermobility, and a global pandemic, then this game is an excellent choice. As a relaxing "feelgood" experience with a wrapping of 80s nostalgia, it works very very well.The game uses a modern, high-quality, low-poly aesthetic that I found very pleasing to look at. Character animations are impressively well done for an indie game, even for animals like the occasional deer in the forest. The soundtrack consists of excellently chosen country and pop tunes, but could have used more than 12 tracks. The voice acting is decent, with a good variety of speakers, though the lip sync is sometimes off.QoL features are, unfortunately, a mixed bag. Rebinding keys is not possible, and the game insists on using WASD for movement, which also makes the placing of the key for opening the map ("M") very inconvenient. A developer said in the forum that they may look into rebinding options, but that was in September 2021 - it's 4 months later now and nothing has happened. On the plus side, the game offers a good selection of graphics options and camera settings, and you can save anywhere outside of cutscenes and conversations. The game also ran stable and very smooth even on the highest settings on my fairly mediocre hardware (1660 Ti, 4-core CPU).I would have preferred more story content and especially a bigger impact of my decisions and actions, but did appreciate the relaxing, wholesome experience a lot. At 20€, the game's asking price is also spot-on for the experience it provides.Special recommendation: If you grew up in the 80s, spend a bit of time looking at the shelves in the video store. Someone obviously had a lot of fun designing all these mock-up video covers. Great attention to detail in that aspect!

_childDocuments_.review: I really really wanted to enjoy this game. The demo was amazing and I was hooked and I was so excited for it to come out.During the demo there was some bugs, which I find to be acceptable; what is not acceptable is when the SAME bugs present in the demo being in the full released. This game isn't early access and should not come out with these bugs present.Bugs I noticed that were in the demo:1. You can hear the car engine EVERYWHERE. You could be in a cutscene and still hear the engine whirring2. Mouth animations not synced with the dialog3. Cars driving in the ground, above the ground, randomly shifting positionsThese are major bugs that should NOT be present in a full release of a game, it takes away from the entire experience. I played through this game in one sitting and I can tell you that halfway through the game it just felt monotonous.The first week of the game is amazing, every day felt like something new was going on, but the second half of the game just felt like waiting until the last day for something to happen. It hit a lull, and extreme lull and it made it almost a chore to play. I loved delivering mail the first week because I was able to speak and hangout with neighbors. The second week is almost nothing. If I can remember correctly, the second week there were days where it felt like all I genuinely was was the mail carrier, not someone who is spending time in my home town. Spoilers: This game wants you to think you can make all of the choices you want. However, you never feel like there are genuine consequences. You can't ask to hangout with the other characters, you are at THEIR beck and call. You cannot ask them to go to the diner with you, maybe get to know them better, you have to wait to get a call from them or hope that you could possibly see them on your route. Lake needed more time. More time to flesh-out characters and choices. More time to polish a game that shouldn't have released in this state. The little things add up. An enjoyable experience can quickly turn into a time waster.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really, really disappointed by Lake.- A lot of bugs. I frequently got stuck in walls. I randomly ended up standing in the lake after a cutscene.- The graphics and animations are not polished. Lip syncing is not good, and driving animations in particular are lacking. For a game where you spend a lot of time driving, I feel there should be more - animations when backing up, checking mirrors, when hitting other cars, or some sort of movement from the driver besides staring blankly ahead.- The radio honestly might have been the worst part. I would rather have no music than a couple songs on repeat.- Characters/storytelling - this might just my opinion, but I found the characters to be a little flat and one-dimensional. Then again, I did not play for long - but the dialogue was lacking and I didn't have interest in getting to know any of them. _childDocuments_.review: This is a charming game about life, decisions, family and friends. You are Meredith, a career woman living in a large town, who comes back to Providence Oaks, your hometown. While delivering the mail in the middle of nowhere, you learn more about the locals, their problems, hobbies and other issues – and can become somehow part of it, depending on your dialogue choices. It is up to the player how to engage with the other people or doing just your job: deliver the mail. They presentation is quite enjoyable, graphics and music are neat. The game itself is very slow paced (but you can use a fast travel option) what fits the whole theme very well. Due to the fact that the game is settled in the 80's there are many references to pop culture in this time, so for older people this is a nice trip to the past, as well. In general I recommend this game but there are some issues:- the game lacks somehow complexity and depth besides dialogues and your job.- for a open world game, there is barely anything to explore (besides beautiful landscape)- the open world is a little bit lifeless: there are only a few cars driving around and few silent people walking the streets- there are a few bugs like invisible walls, stucking in the environment, the tires of your truck appear to be broken while parking ...- the controls feel a little bit clunkyAll in all this feels a little bit like a missed opportunity. On the one hand the lack of depth fits well, because the player is not overwhelmed with points of interests or minigames  like in other games (the usual Ubisoft Open World stuff). On the other hand the empty open world should be more rewarding for exploring. I don't know, maybe you should be able to find some clues about your home town or something like this. But driving around in the forest for, well, nothing, feels a little bit unsatisfying in the end. But I think also that's only me and the game is quite enjoyable nonetheless.

_childDocuments_.review: If I had to describe this game in one word, it would be "journey". You go on different literal journeys every day while delivering mail to the denizens of Providence Oaks, but also a personal journey as you navigate through the tough decision of "Should I stay or should I go?". The main character goes through interpersonal journeys as well, reconnecting with old friends as well as making new connections (romantic or otherwise). The storyline itself is not only interesting and made me play through it in one go, but it felt like I was in a Wes Anderson movie, and the overall small-town vibes are top tier. My problems with this game are minor, however, they're still present. For starters, the graphics can be a bit laggy at times, which make for awkward conversations where neither persons' lips are moving. Also, in the "cutscenes" (conversation blocks between multiple people), the transitions where characters leave and re-enter a scene are almost non-existent, to the point where they just look like random character model cut-and-pastes. Lastly, there's little to no expression in any of the people's faces. I understand that some games benefit from this, but I genuinely think it would add so much more to the experience if I wasn't looking at blank faces while someone was shocked, angry, sad, or overjoyed. That being said, though, I would definitely recommend this game to anyone who likes interactive stories, cozy vibes, choice-based games, and small little lake towns in 1980's Oregon. Overall 7/10 for a great story and interesting characters, but points deducted for glitchy graphics and expressionless faces.

_childDocuments_.review: Thank you for such a beautiful game.The process of reconnecting with old friends from Meredith Weiss' point of view gave me wave after wave of nostalgia. Will I experience this when the time comes for me to reconnect with my old childhood friends? I can only imagine.I already loved this game but the small details made me appreciate it even more. The shadow of the leaves moving in the wind on the street. The way the shadows move when you shine the truck's headlights on the picket fences.As I drove through Lake Rd., I would pan the camera towards the lake because of the wonderful view. The endless asphalt, the pine and birch trees, and even the shadow of electric wires on the road, reminded me of the long drives that my family would take twice in a year. It was similar in a way. We would be driving through the coastal road with the ocean on the left and with the trees on the right.I have also never written a review before. This feels less like a review but more like a show of gratitude to the team.Thank you for letting me realize that though one can get lost in the hustle and bustle of modern life, it is most important that one remember the unexciting yet memorable events of the past.P.S. Will there be a DLC or another game? I have come to love Providence Oaks and its community.

_childDocuments_.review: Lake is a peaceful and relaxing game where you deliver mail and packages in a small Oregon town, that is also the main character's home town. This game asks you the simple question of do you want to continue your hard work or follow your true dreams?I have no complaints on the story or the characters, despite some of the might be a bit stereotypical. The interactions work out in most cases (although some conversations really shows what kind of choice should have been intended, because not all choices match up with the response you get from the NPCs) and in the end you have three big choices to make. I do feel that I wanted more choices to matter, which I guess is the biggest downfall in a game like this.When it comes to gameplay and the technical parts I have no real complaints - the truck handles fine, and there are no issues delivering packages or mail. The map is a good size, even though it feels big it's not too large (or too small for that matter). I had a few bugs with loss of sound, both background, soundtrack and conversations - but those were usually resolved by rebooting the game.In the end, I do want to recommend this game - but perhaps don't expect too much out if and instead let the game take you wherever it goes.

_childDocuments_.review: If you’re in the mood for a leisurely drive through a charming town, delivering mail and packages while soaking in a cozy atmosphere, this game is a perfect match! The visuals are a real treat, creating a warm, inviting environment that, paired with a wonderful soundtrack and fully-voiced dialogues, makes for a truly wholesome experience.What I find particularly endearing is how the game captures everyday moments with such authenticity. For instance, the interactions between Meredith and her boss over the phone reflect the familiar dynamics of a workplace, adding a layer of relatability. As you navigate the town in your mail truck (which, I must admit, I may have bumped into a few things!), Meredith’s little remarks make the journey even more enjoyable. The game’s unhurried pace is ideal for those who want to unwind, offering a gentle and engaging experience.While I did come across a few minor bugs, they were never enough to disrupt the overall experience. A quick return to the title screen usually resolved any issues, and it’s reassuring to know that these small hiccups don’t detract from the overall enjoyment of the game.The story itself is rich and full of warmth, teaching us that there’s always a story to uncover, especially in the routine of delivering mail. From creating small memories and mending relationships to solving problems and offering help, the game beautifully captures these elements. After finishing the game, I felt a deep connection to Meredith and everyone in Providence Oaks, and I’m excited to return. Perhaps I’ll revisit during Christmas to explore the holiday DLC. Driving through the countryside with such a cozy and relaxing vibe truly makes for a joyful experience!

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I genuinely enjoyed my experience with the game. 'Lake' captivated me throughout my entire playthrough, and didn't fail to encapsulate the feeling of living within a small community. The soundtrack is incredible (Last Days of September being my favourite song right now), and I personally found the gameplay - while a tad repetitive - to be a nice breath of fresh air that stands out from other games.However, I simply cannot recommend purchasing this game in the state that it's currently in. While I enjoyed the game very much, there were quite a few flaws that broke my immersion.For starters. the game is INCREDIBLY unoptimized. There are lots of bugs and glitches. From minor things like the voice actor's lines being cut off too early to major things like getting into your mail truck, randomly teleporting half way across the map because a cut scene was spontaneously triggered, and having to walk all the way back to where the truck is. And yes, I walked all the way back.A majority of the time, the cut scenes and dialogue scenes felt like they were made in GoAnimate. Characters would simply snap to a certain positions. In some cases, they would snap out of the frame before the scene even cut to the next frame. You could tell that there wasn't enough time to craft the assets needed during each scene OR program some basic character animation when this game was being developed. Whether it was Robert "opening a letter" or a majority of the driving cut scenes where whoever is driving is simply holding the steering wheel in a neutral position, they felt clunky.What didn't help the clunkiness was how the dialogue was stitched together. There are certain dialogue scenes in the game where it becomes blatant that the dialogue option you chose during that scene held no weight whatsoever as the response of the character you're talking to feels better suited towards one of the other dialogue options.Secondly, the controlling mechanics and pacing for the walking and driving are awful.Meredith walks at an absolute snails pace even while sprinting. Delivering mail takes an egregiously long time due to this. I'm fairly certain my playtime would have been cut in half if her speed was upped a fraction. The amount of times I walked all the way to the house, forgot to bring the package with me, walked all the way back to the truck, picked up the package, and walked all the way back to the house was embarrassing to say the least but was salt rubbed into the wound by Meredith walking at 2km/h.Furthermore, while I wasn't expecting the driving to be on par with that of Grand Theft Auto, it was certainly jarring to me that the mechanics were limited as much as they were. The first few days I was delivering the mail, I had no trouble with the pace of the truck as I was able to soak in the environment of Providence Oaks (which they did a stellar job of crafting might I add). However, as I progressed further and further into the game I found the speed of the truck to be sluggish. As well as this, while I understand the decision for the game to completely ignore when you crash into another car, person, or object, it did break my immersion quite a heavy amount.My final flaw with this game is that the characters are incredibly forgettable. Earlier in my review I mentioned  Robert but in all honesty I had to look up what his name was. The only characters I really remember were Meredith, Frank, and Angie. I can only boil down the rest of the cast as "cat lady," "mechanic girl," "rude motel guy," etc. My personal preference with games like these is when your friendship and relationship with characters carry weight and resonates with the player. There are many examples of games on Steam that do this right (Persona 4 Golden and Stardew Valley are two that stand out) but I don't think Lake really hit the nail on the head with this one, which sucks because I could feel the potential impact that each character fade before my eyes.Usually I don't leave long and detailed reviews like this, but I felt like this game could've been so much more than it is. I'm really hoping the Gamious takes these criticisms into account to make their next endeavour even bigger and better! Again, I enjoyed this game very much and I can't wait to see more games like it. If you get the opportunity to play it, I'd definitely recommend giving it a fair shake. However, for $30 (AUD) I was expecting the final product to have been more polished.

_childDocuments_.review: The idea is great, but sadly there is very little meat on this product.I played the demo for a while, and liked the idea of a relaxing game with multiple choices type of gameplay; but in the end what you get is a short adventure that could be considered a demo product itself, even in its shipped form.I was hoping to see some changes to the game but sadly that didn't happen. Not sure what changed between the demo released in summer and the final game shipped in September, since they look identical- Animations are stiff, graphics is like breath of the wild with some realistic effects; you may like it or not, that is a matter of preferences- Dialogues and choices are really irrelevant (I cheated and watched other "let's play"); this is not "Life Is Strange", let's be clear, and nobody was expecting that from an indie team. The character development, depth or even the overall setup of this little town as you may have in RPG games like Divinity, Pillars of Eternity and similar, but in the end you have the same depth you could find in a nintendo game like Animal Crossing and Harvest moon; or even Stardew Valley:  a cast of very generic people with nothing much to do with them except interact with pre-defined choices. Basically what you do is mostly irrelevant except one choice at the end.- Driving is a big part of this game; and it feels like someone slapped different assets on the Unity driving demo and called the day. There is no first view and internal view of the mail van; there is not even an animation to get in and out of the van, replaced by a fade to black. The driving model is simplistic but that is OK. There are no collisions consequences, there are barely few cars on the road, and in general it feels like driving is there just to prolong this game longevity.- The town is a ghost town; you barely see anyone walking around, stores are empty, nothing really going on. Have you ever been in a small (100 people or less) US town? Probably not, and neither did the devs. Characters are static in their location, they don't move around, nor drive back their home; and same for the "key" characters you talk to. They are there and that's it. If the game was a 2d novel style game, you would not notice the difference.I get that this is an indie game, but there are things we take for granted at this point; and if you promote your game as being an interactive storytelling experience, and slap dialogues on static characters and make everything on rail, then you as consumer start to question why should you buy it. Get the demo; see if this is your thing and buy it if you like the game itself. Don't buy into the idea of what the game want to sell you, but check by yourself if this is what you want to do for few hours, and no incentive to re-play it because the outcomes are 3 I believe, and the main choices that bring you to each of those endings are in 2 occasion.I had high hopes after checking the demo that the game would evolve; but sadly the game is exactly like the demo, so do check the demo and see if that is what you want.I give this a 5 out of 10 mostly because it is super short and most of the game is on rail and what you do has little to no effect on anything except few occasion. Hopefully the devs next game will be more substantial than this one.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, great for the steam deck. Worked fantastically, no lag, and graphics were on high. Gameplay was somewhat smooth. The controls for the car could use some polish. The way it is now, the mail truck will drift left and right on its own. God forbid you tap/hit something, your truck will spin, flip over, or you'll lose control of it for a few seconds. Could really use a run button. I know this is supposed to be kind of a walking simulator but... the walking speed is just too slow, even with the walk faster button. This game tells a very linear story but is masquerading as a game with dialogue choices that matter. In fact, it does not matter. I'm one to chase achievements, especially when they have few enough that I can 100% it. So I played through this twice to get the Workaholic achievement and played the ending three times to get the ending achievements. I can confidently say that your choices in dialogue doesn't really matter. Sure, it unlocks other dialogues for you to experience but... The game will still strong arm you into the direction it wants you to go. The only parts that give you a real choice at all are whether you want to help the residents/Steve (her boss) with their tasks and which of the two romanceable characters you want to romance. Romance in this game is very bare bones. You don't even really feel anything for the two romanceables. The interactions are all pretty shallow. You never really get to know them as people. The most in-depth stuff you will know about them is their name, job, and that one quirky personality they were assigned. In fact, almost every character in this game is shallow and you don't get to know them at all beyond what their relation was to your character before she moved to the big city. With that said, the music in this game is surprisingly really good. It's nothing special. Just some folk(?)/contemporary music off Epidemic Sounds/Music that fit within the theme and setting of the game. However, the way it's implemented into the game, playing off an in-game radio as you deliver mail and go into shops/the diner and the sound mixing for the music to fade or become faint as you walk away from the source of the music was fantastic. There's even a reason for the radio to exist in the game. It isn't one of those, it exists and we don't think too much about it otherwise it breaks immersion kind of thing. Final thoughts: If you want a simple game that doesn't delve too deep into anything and have about 6-10 hours to spare over the weekend or the week, this is a good game to pick up. Despite my opinions of the game, I will recommend it because it's not a bad game. It's a decent game with very low stakes and shallow character interactions and some people really dig that and some people might just need that right now.
