_childDocuments_.review: Lake is a relaxing narrative adventure, that was unfortunately undercooked in the process of making. As much as I love the idea of a "walking simulator" where you're working in the postal service, Lake is seriously lacking in terms of polish on almost every step. Even with all the flaws (read more below), I enjoyed these 4 hours of gameplay. It wasn't something super noteworthy in the long run, but it helped me to chill out in the evening. It's a slice-of-life game so don't expect anything action packed. Meredith, the main protagonist, is temporarily working in the postal service. Besides delivering stuff, we're talking to people from time to time. It's almost always the same few characters, but I don't mind it. It helps to build their personality and gives us another reason to stay in town (if you want). Some people have mini-stories built around them (like reconciliation with our old best friend). Nothing special, but it keeps you going. Writing itself could be better, especially when it comes to our two romantic options, but at least everything was cohesive.Speaking of romantic options - too bland, too short. They are not even bad, but you can't write 10 minutes of "romance" for a 5 hours game and call it a day. It's simply not enough to make you invested in these characters.The gameplay is pretty simple. Deliver letters and packages. Sometimes talk to other people.Alas, the driving portion of the game gets tedious really quickly. It can be relaxing for an hour or two... but almost five? Nah. Maaaybe if the driving would be actually done right. A bar of soap pretending to be a truck was good enough for the authors, I guess.Visually, Lake can be pretty, as long as you're not picky when it comes to details. Non-existent facial animations, textures imposing on each other, ugly models, and much more. It's not awfully bad, but it could definitely be better.Solid voice acting, especially for the main character. The rest of the world could get a little more love though. Sometimes I felt like I'm the only person in the world, because of minimal background sounds.I really liked the music on the radio... but there are only three songs. Listening to the same THREE songs on repeat for almost FIVE hours can destroy your brain.There's a high amount of bugs and glitches of almost every kind: animations glitches - mainly when the protagonist is trying to interact with objects; collision glitches - packages/NPCs/cars glitching into other objects; cars and NPCs have problems with pathfinding; randomly broken voice lines when talking inside the building; textures glitching in the background; it only happened once, but the whole audio in the game was lagging behind and I needed to reload the save to fix the problem. Yeah. There's a lot of it. Fortunately, it's nothing game-breaking, but it definitely can be annoying and immersion breaking.Optimization is also not great, considering the visuals and content of the game. It's not unplayable by any means, but drops from (unstable) 144 to 70 fps shouldn't happen.To sum up. If you're looking for a relaxing game to pass the time, and you're okay with all the issues mentioned above - give Lake a chance. If not, then don't waste your time.

_childDocuments_.review: May or may not have played this through in 1 sitting. Well, 2 if you count that I stopped to eat dinner in the midst. I really enjoyed playing it. It definitely can feel very monotonous at some points, but there's part of me that feels like that's the point in places.The storytelling was good, although I wish there was just more of it, if that makes sense. I'd love to have DLC or something for this at some point that gives more interactions and stories for the different characters in the game.Here are the ratings I would give:Graphics: 9/10Incredibly beautiful scenery, and even the thunderstorms and environmental sounds are both calming and realistic.Sound: 7.5/10There are some places that are a bit buggy with sound. Like the radio continuing to play during conversation scenes, or voices not matching with subtitles on rare occasion. The sound design is great though, other than those few bugs.Story: 7/10Like I said earlier I do think this could be even better if there were just more story lines to it. I'd love to see more interactions with some of the townsfolk. Although maybe I've just not seen it in some circumstances.Gameplay: 8/10Again like I said previously it is monotonous in some spaces. You are delivering mail, though. So it's to be expected. It didn't make me feel bored though, not at all! The only negative thing I'd really say is I wish there was faster walking/speed walking. I think the 'walk faster' button/option is pretty irrelevant when it comes to walking speed. That may just be personal preference though!Overall: 9/10I think this game as well as the developers have super big potential, especially in the 'cozy gaming' market. This game was fun to play, and other than me borderline speed running it haha, I think this could have good replay potential as well! There are definitely multiple endings depending on the choices you make with certain characters. I'd love to see other peoples ending when more people have played this game.Definitely will be on my 'Game Devs to Watch' list from now on!

_childDocuments_.review: Lake is one of those games that makes me wish Steam had a "neutral" rating for reviews, as I'm a bit conflicted about how I feel about the overall game. I leaned a little more positively because I was at least motivated enough to play through to one of the endings.At its core, Lake has two main gameplay elements: "Deliver the mail" and "Talk to people around town." Both parts have their pros and cons.For the first part, delivering mail is very straightforward, as a few random houses on the map require deliveries. It's unsurprisingly repetitive, which is not helped by the fact that both Meredith and the mail truck she drives are very slow. Adding to this, the in-game radio has at most five unique songs, making the mail delivery aspect wear on you quickly. Since this is how you're supposed to advance the story and the gameplay changes very little from day to day, it can be a bit tiring to do 12 times to finish the story.The deliveries are occasionally interrupted by various people on Meredith's route having conversations with her, offering at least 4-5 responses in each situation. This is another area I'm conflicted about because there's a lot of "telling" but not "showing." 95% of the conversations consist of two characters standing still or sitting down with little animation. Characters often stare off-camera with the same neutral facial expression for every conversation. While most of the writing is good, and the voice acting tries to make the conversations sound like believable adult dialogue, the lack of animation is a little jarring.The animation issue is also worsened by weird jump cuts designed to avoid animating certain scenes. For example, one cutscene begins with someone standing on a ledge above Meredith saying, "Hey, come up here and chat with me!" The game then immediately cuts to Meredith standing next to this person on the ledge, with no transition or animation showing her walking up there. This wouldn’t be an issue if it weren’t for the fact that every single cutscene in the game is like this. Fun fact: I was jumpscared during a conversation where she hugged someone because it was the most animation I had seen a character express a couple of hours into the game.Regarding the impact of your choices on the story, that’s also debatable. There are many choices in conversations, but most boil down to "Meredith helps this person with their problem" or "Meredith doesn’t help this person." This leads right up to the ending, where you essentially choose between "Meredith heads back to her old job" or "Meredith decides to stay in her hometown." There is a secret third ending, and while I won’t spoil it, it requires some very specific choices that I don’t think most people will discover without looking up a guide.A few other nitpicks I have:-The weird jump cuts in conversations also affect some side-story beats. For example, one character asks if you’d babysit their kid so they can see a show. If you agree, it shows Meredith walking up to the house, the screen fades to black, and then it cuts to the next day with the character saying, "Hey, thanks for babysitting." There’s no mention of what went on, no references to it later in the game, and Meredith doesn’t talk about anything that happened. It just makes me wonder why I even bothered to agree if the game isn’t going to pretend to care. This happened at least three times in my playthrough.I said yes to every character who requested help later that week. Not a single event intersected, so there was never any dilemma about which character to help.-There’s a character you meet early on who talks to you a lot, then suddenly tries to romance you without much lead-up. If you say no, they disappear for the rest of the game without much fanfare. It's a jarring transition.-There’s a sizable section of the map you’ll never drive on unless you specifically go out of your way to do so. The developers are aware of this, as one of the achievements involves driving to this area.Despite these complaints, I was motivated enough to finish the story, so I’m keeping this at a positive rating. However, I think it's a hard sell at full price, especially given the 4-6 hour length, so I recommend waiting for a sale or getting it during a deal/bundle like I did.

_childDocuments_.review: I sort of wish Steam had a "meh" option.This game is pretty much cookie-cutter female escapism (not that that's a bad thing); it's very much what it looks like on the tin.The town's quite odd. Very strange that it's ostensibly set in the '80s, because there isn't all that much '80s about it (feels more '90s to me!). The radiowaves consist solely of one generic indie singer and her handful of songs which sound more Alannis Morisette than anything else.The characters are all stiffly animated and stare at you with dead eyes. Just about every job in the town seems to be done by a woman - from the girlboss mechanic to the girlboss record store owner. I'm not really criticising this, it's just something I noticed that stood out, and I suppose it lends into what I was saying about this being a cookie-cutter women's story for a female audience (which is fine!).My final gripe would be with how cheap the game feels. I've already mentioned the animations but I can quite readily imagine that those are quite expensive/difficult to get right. But it's more the "little things" are missing that could have made decent touches. Your mail van, for example, doesn't have brake/reverse lights, nor are there any animations for getting in/out of the vehicle (you just teleport). I can't help but feel like they could have licensed some more varied music too.Me being a cynical ♥♥♥♥ aside, the game's relaxing, the scenery is beautiful, and I found my time playing it pretty enjoyable (though I have to admit I didn't finish it). I get the impression that this is a genuine indie title that afforded a new/inexperienced team to be supported in getting the story they wanted to tell out there. And I'm glad they did it! Congratulations and I hope that, next time, they'll make something better.TL;DR - Grab this on sale, and don't go in expecting anything too original.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy... This game angered me so, so much.It's one of these "wholesome games" that hides its short-comings behind a cozy paint. You can't skip dialogues, it's barebone and not really satisfying to play, the content is both minimal and way too stretched out... But, hey, I'm not the target for this game. I was expecting something more fleshed out, more "full", but I should have done my own research.The thing that really angers me is how retrograde this game is. Under its progressive paint, Lake is at best tone-deaf, at worse completely misoginistic.Let's start with the tone-deaf part : Lake is set in a rural American town, in the 80's. Lake also shoehorns a lesbian relationship, which feels... Completely hollow. Has any queer person worked on this game? I doubt that. But the worse thing is this game completely occults the homophobia a lesbian couple would have face in this setting... Honestly, this whole relationship seems like an attemps from the devs to make their game seem more progressive (spoiler: it's not).Now, let's talk about how this game is... Really insulting toward women. Let me summarize it: a brilliant woman in her 40's, a pioneer in computer programming, accepts a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ job in a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ town, where *in real life* she would never have been able to be openly lesbian? The protagonist seems like she never has agency of their own, and she kept being used by a bunch of rednecks. Presenting exploitation as a fantasy is just dangerous, and if I knew this was a faux-woke game, I would have skipped it.So, yeah... This won't work. This game is basically about a good old time where Meredith would never have been able to live happily. It's bigotry covered in wokeness (something, unfortunately, more and more common), and I would have skipped it if I was aware of all these points. I'll make sure to be wary of Gamious' next games.Sorry if my review is not well written and a bit messy. In my defense: I would have written a more polished review if those devs didn't make a game this offensive!

_childDocuments_.review: What a fun ride, playing Meredith who returns home to do something her father once did. Apart from that, in this game we can also learn that socializing is very important to understand each other.Talking about the game, there aren't many problems, but there are some bugs that seem quite annoying, such as characters respawning in cars so they can't walk, making me personally quite afraid that the progress I've made could be lost. Then about several NPCs walking on the streets, again and again it doesn't have much of an impact, but maybe it can be a note for the future. Overall I like it and will probably try playing the newest DLCScore: 7,5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Zen-like experience. Pleasing environments, lovely graphics. Enjoyable gaming experience with a decent storyline and interesting character interactions and dialogue choices. If you've played the demo, and you back up your saves and uninstall the demo before installing the full game, you'll be able to pick up where you left off with the demo which I found helpful.Another great plus is numerous save-game slots (each save game you choose appears in a tree over the past saves. Not sure how MANY save slots there will be, but this is helpful in case you wish to back up a bit and change some of your dialogue choices/responses to see if it changes the storyline a bit). Very few games have multiple save slots anymore, so THANKS DEVS!Relaxing music (sometimes repetitive, but since I enjoy the music I don't mind that one bit). PLus, you can turn off the radio in your postal delivery truck if you choose to.Various graphics setting choices, camera settings, etc. I've played this with a 2-year old Dell PC and have every setting maxed out. PRetty well optimized thus far for me. ALso I"m only using KB/M and driving/walking works quite well.I'm a few days into the game's story and am enjoying the experience so far; how it looks, plays, sounds.Your character is a big-city tech geek who's taking a break from the city (though work seems to keep intruding), and visiting her hometown; helping her dad out with his mail route, so you get to meet interesting townsfolks along the way. Nothing complicated, but a lot of story angles to keep it interesting.One thing I'd have added (and hopefully the DEVS will keep this in mind for patches) is an option to skip to the next dialogue/conversation tree. Frankly I can't think of anything else, currently. Well, OK, two things: perhaps an option to make the walking speed even more quick than the "fast walk" option currently available, which is barely faster than "regular" walking speed. But hey: it's a RELAXING game, not a hack-n-slash. As I mentioned, it's a very chill game and pretty to look at. Worth the money IMHO.

_childDocuments_.review: 🔵Lake is unlike any game I have ever played before, there is no `objective` no targets to aim for or things to unlock, it's just about relaxing and taking time to be you.  🔵The entire game took me about 6.5hrs to complete, but I think there are different endings, so you could play multiple times over to get all achievements.🔵Your character moves to an unfamiliar environment, meets people and shares experiences with those people.  Ultimately the game is about deciding which way you want to go in your life & which direction they want to take regarding the people she meets.🍿 FULL REVIEW : ✔️It's meditative for sure, I feel so relaxed after playing this game and it has a nice mix of humour, some love interests and it's like a feel good movie of the 80's + a decent soundtrack (I think I might have got in touch with my feminine side a few times! lol).🔵There are some adult themes (not graphic) and small use of bad language.🔵Yes I would like to see more added to Lake, more people and families with stories etc.. to interact with, more freedom around the town itself and I especially would like to see the animations improved.✔️Even without any of the wishlist items above, this was a positive experience & one that I enjoyed.🍿 You can watch my LP here: ✔️The background stories are interesting, not sure where they will lead (if anywhere) but like the fact that this perfect little town, isn't quite so perfect after all.✔️Well, well, well...Somebody is on a potential promise, but with whom?  Ménage à trois?✔️Some of the audio tracks are really good, I sing along quite happily.❌Few small audio issues (typing often missing) & often characters mouths don't move when speaking..❌Game crashed once (when I asked Robert to remake his radio announcement).❌Some bugs when getting parcels out of the truck; sometimes won't grab them & other times it does, but the parcel or item is invisible.❌Although walking encourages calmness....ITS A BIT ANNOYING; maybe we could jog a bit if not carrying a parcel?❌Lack of animations a bit of an immersion breaker.  Be nice to see our character climb in and out of the truck instead of fading to black...same applies to most of the encounters.❌Would love to have the freedom of the city, a bit more GTA, allowing us to walk about as we choose (to & from work), shop, speak to other pedestrians.✔️Lake has a meditative quality about it.  Maybe it is the music, maybe it is the stunningly beautiful &  idyllic USA small town vibe or perhaps it is just the people who live there?✔️Lake really does appear to be offering a better life choice, a slower pace of life where people actually take time to get to know each other and actually do care about each other; reminds me of a Britain 35 years ago.✔️Your role as a postal delivery worker involves driving door to door dropping off parcels and mail, but as you get to know the townsfolk you will discover that you are in a unique position to help them and better their lives; but the choice is absolutely yours to make.✔️The Local Radio station is manned by the local Farmer, the local mechanic is just 16 and almost every favourite movie of the 80's is referenced in this game at some stage...so far I am enjoying it immensely.

_childDocuments_.review: What a lovely little game. A wholesome story where you play a character, Meredith, who has gone back to her hometown to take over her dad’s mail delivery job. You spend your day driving around the mailtruck and delivering mail to the correct homes. I love the simplicity of it. There is no urgency, you can take as long as you want delivering the mail and exploring the little lakeside town. Along your way you meet several characters, make choices about how you spend your time, and ultimately, decide whether or not you want to stay in your hometown or head back to the big city.One thing that had put me off this game were the reviews saying how slowly Meredith walks. Honestly, this didn’t bug me as much as I thought it might. Again, there’s no urgency to the game and I enjoyed the slower pace of it. You hardly walk much in the game anyways as you’ve got the truck, and when you do walk, it’s nice to just take in all the scenery.Definitely try this game if you like a slower paced story-rich game. Beautiful graphics and a catchy soundtrack that has been stuck in my head for a week since completing the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok. Where to begin...The game is good but not good enough to pay it full price. The story is simple but effective. The only gripes I would have with it is that it is too short. It could have easily been filled with some really interesting side activities.The world isn't as interactable as I thought it would be and sometimes the animations can be a bit janky. Considering how beautiful the environment is it would have been great if we could have explored the world a bit more. There are way too many areas in the game that are only really used once or twice and then forgotten. I also encountered a bug twice that stopped me from entering the van and the only way to fix it for me to quit the game so that's not great.The controls need some tweaking. It takes too long sometimes for the van to move in the direction I want it too and sometimes the van slows down at really weird points on the road.The townsfolk aren't that interesting to be honest and I don't even remember most of their names. In some cases some of the townsfolk could have been removed from the game and the game would still be the same. I do like the romance options though and I do think the two options are both very different and offer unique experiences.Personally I think the game feels a bit bare bones. I think there is room for improvement to flesh out the game some more. I would have been cool to actually interact with the house you live in by moving around it. It would have been cool to actually go to Mo's  and order something whilst delivering parcels and letters rather than just sitting on the chairs or only going their to push the story. The town could have easily had some stores that we could enter and buy things that we could bring home such as a new dress that we could wear on a date. Maybe a new book. Groceries. An umbrella...There could have been an option to change the appearance of your character, from things like hair to even makeup.With that being said the game is far from a bad game it just does not have enough content in it to justify the full price. However putting that aside I really did enjoy the game. It was really relaxing just driving around town and delivering parcels and letters to people with the view of the lake never too far away.I would recommend this game if you just want something relaxing to pass the time. If you actually want something meaningful and deep this is not the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is RIGHT up my alley now that I'm an older gamer and father of three working full time with very little free days or even hours to spend gaming. And I do recommend purchasing this game, even at full price, for people who love slice-of-life walking simulator light type games.HOWEVER, keep in mind that this game kind of falls a little short when it comes to content. It took me barely 6 hours to play fully and I didn't feel like my choices mattered much to want to go and replay it again. I was very happy with the ending I got, it was exactly what I wanted, but logically it was a very poor decision for the character to choose if it were real life. I don't know, it's hard to explain. It was a fun experience, just... the game felt like there could've been a lot more story added. I don't mean murder or anything, but there was a lot of potential that felt wasted. At first you think you can drive everywhere and explore everything, but then you realize you can only sort of explore... but then you realize not really... actually there's nothing really to explore, and there's nothing really to do except deliver the mail, and that's the problem.I'm kind of not really selling the game am I, hahaha. Sorry, it was still very pretty and very relaxing, just my speed, I guess I just wish it lasted longer and there was more to do. _childDocuments_.review: Or Lake is a mail delivery game, which actually serves to get the main character involved with the inhabitants of the town she left 22 years ago.You, Meredith Weiss, work for a computer company and finished up the final touches to their next software release over Labor Day weekend so that you can fill in for your father delivering mail in Providence Oaks, the small lake community where you grew up in the Pacific Northwest. You left home 22 years ago to go to MIT and haven't been back home since. Your father is normally the backup mail man, but he's on vacation with your mother in Florida.The story takes place in the late 80s, before everyone had a cell phone, back in the VHS days, back with answering machines because you couldn't reach anyone anywhere. The postal truck is left hand drive, instead of the normal right hand drive.The game is full of "handrails" crashing your vehicle doesn't do any damage, you cannot exit your vehicle unless it is not moving, you cannot deliver the wrong mail to the wrong location, all of your "meetings" are set so that they do not conflict.My biggest issue with the game is when you are driving the truck it automatically adjusts your point of view to the default, which is behind the truck and lower down than it should be. This causes you to be unable to see the road at all when it changes elevation. Maintaining a decent view of the road requires you to constantly adjust the view with the mouse.The driving AI occasionally causes traffic jams. I had this occur twice in front of the Post Office at the end of the day and had to drive on the sidewalk to park my mail truck.The mail delivery is a large part of the game, but the main reason for it is to get you to interact with the towns people. There are both a male and a female romantic avenue to pursue. At the end of your two weeks you will need to decide what you are going to do, go back to your old life, stay in Providence Oaks, move on with your romantic interest.This is not a high speed mail delivery game. The mail delivery is to introduce you to the town's people and advance their stories, you decide your path based upon your dialog choices.Intel i7-8086K Coffee Lake 6-Core 4.00GHz CPUCrucial Ballistix Sport AT 2666 MHz DDR4 RAM (16GB x 2)ASUS GeForce RTX 2080 Overclocked 8G GDDR6Or

_childDocuments_.review: Relaxing game of delivering mail and getting involved (or not) in people's problems (such as a sick cat or a protest against a construction project), with three possible endings. There is no challenge to overcome, no time limit, just a vibe for you to enjoy.Sadly, I'm conflicted about this rating. While the game may be a charming, positive indie game, it suffers from quite a few technical issues, so buyer beware. For starters, if you don't limit the game's refresh rate to 60 fps, you may be dealing with severe sound cutoff. Plus, there are lots of instances of insufficient polish. For instance, it won't be long before you start seeing cars floating above the road in the distance or even find some buried up to their windows in the ground (it seems to happen more in the southern part of the map).I've also tried the game on console (PS4 and PS5), and the performance there is rather disappointing, relative to the game's low graphical complexity/fidelity, with both the draw distance and the framerate well below expectations (especially on PS4),

_childDocuments_.review: Set in 1986, Lake is a bite-sized open world adventure about Meredith Weiss, a busy city worker who takes time out to return home and fill in for her dad, the local postman, while he’s out of town.  Played from a third person perspective, Lake is a simple, but lovely game. Across 14 days, you are tasked with delivering letters and packages to the local residents of Providence Oaks. As you go about your rounds, you interact with characters and build relationships with them. Dialogue choices lead to different outcomes and endings.  How will you take to the slow life in Providence Oaks? Perhaps you’ll meet someone and ignore that work you need to do for your city boss. By the end, you may even want to stay. The story is by far the strongest aspect of the game, which is helped by some pretty sold voice acting.  The graphics are gorgeous, Providence Oaks feels real – and reminded me of some of the places I’ve visited when in New England. The attention to detail is also impressive. Special mention has to go to the local video shop on Main Street, that has a large selection of recognisable ‘80s films on the shelves, albeit with slight copyright adaptations – can you guess what film Back to the Present is? Lake is a breath of digital fresh air – and offers a welcome change of pace from the many first-person shooters, bullet hells, and action roguelites on the market at the moment

_childDocuments_.review: A successful woman revisits her childhood town for a stress free break from her big city job in exchange for a couple of weeks casually delivering mail. The location is so beautiful and it’s obvious a lot of thought went into the design, it’s hard to imagine why she left. During her stay she gets to know the locals and generally enjoy the gentler pace of small town life. WIth a name like ‘Lake’ it doesn’t do much to inspire the imagination but it is accurate, there is a lake in this game. Riding on some 80s nostalgia, it’s dialogue heavy game and fits nicely into the category of ‘Walking Sims’, it’s just a shame walking felt excruciatingly slow at first. Posties are some of the fastest walkers I know (absolute calves of steel!), so seeing her waddle slower than what I could after recovering from my broken foot was mildly frustrating to say the least, even if she is a ‘newbie’ to the job. Eventually I was able to melt into a relaxed routine and find optimal routes to minimise the walking.Driving feels smooth though, with no consequences for driving poorly. When I got the keys for the affectionately named ‘Goose’, the first thing I did was drive down the wrong side of the street - it accidentally caused a traffic jam that was still there after I returned from my rounds. Additionally to the driving is a rudimentary ‘fast travel’ system that teleports you to key points in the map and an ‘auto-travel’ option. If the actual driving side of the game doesn’t do anything for you, it’s skippable.Voice and sound occasionally seemed off. Too quiet in parts, or it sounded like it was in a bubble.  That being said I love the soundtrack to this game, it’s super chill and relaxing but it is very limited. The devs seem quite aware to the point a joke was made about it by an NPC. In game you can choose to listen to the ambience or the few songs the local radio has actually access to.Dialogue could be a little cheesy but it’s wholesome and I found myself grinning along. It’s not possible to skip or speed up dialogue, and there choices in-game but they mostly boil down to yes I'll do that or no I won’t, the latter just meaning you’ll miss out on a scene or two. If you’re playing this game for the story you might as well say yes. There are a couple of potential romantic interests which play a key role in the final decision for our protagonist, this is completely optional - you do not have to romance either. I don’t know if I imagined it but the female romance came across as written more in depth.I can’t help but think some of the characters were mildly inspired by those in Twin Peaks, the cat lady in particular but that’s probably wishful thinking… Most were more reminiscent of those found in shows like Northern Exposure or Murder She Wrote (minus the murder part). Quaint, a little bit eccentric, hard working sorts. I grew up surrounded by ‘80s media so this game felt like a small nostalgia trip - especially visiting the rental store, I must have spent at least 20 minutes or so just looking at the poster parodies in there.Although I’m giving ‘Lake’ a thumbs up, I’m happy to acknowledge its flaws and admit this game is definitely not for everyone, at first I wasn’t even sure it was for me. It took its time but the characters really grew and the mellow nature felt like a breath of fresh air. This game really embodies the phrase: ‘Life’s a journey and not a destination, just grab the wheel and enjoy the ride.’

_childDocuments_.review: Well, reviewing this one will have more complexity than I though it would, as I cannot be really objective with that game. What I can say straight away is that this a game for someone stuck on either local or global emigration and kind of torn between the past and future choices. Lake is overall a good-ish game, but very uneven, and close to a real mess on the technical side. I appreciate the fact this is a title made by indie studio, but that does not justify the quality of the technical aspects of the game.As much as the story is slow and relaxed, it isn't anything special - but depending on your perspective it can be good or bad. If you expect something similar to Telltale titles, that's not it. Lake is more likely meant to show you monotony of every day life and attempts of trying to find something special in each day. Removing run button from the game was a good choice that helps the atmosphere of the game, but can annoy the ♥♥♥♥ out of you as well if you are impatient. Luckily there is fast travel option if you don't want to walk or drive around too much.Cultural references are well placed and you can catch yourself getting slightly nostalgic, especially if you have lived in the 80's.Characters are just there as they appear somewhat flat, BUT this is a story of a person visiting home town after being 22 years away. It feels like you expect to be greeted and treated as a guest, but you are just there, kind of ignored, while NPCs go on with their lives. Not too much interaction in a small town. And that actually makes so much sense.Added value is the replayability of the game with several different choices and endings.Music can get boring quickly. Voice acting is acceptable.Technical side is the biggest flaw of the game which feels unpolished, early access at best. You will get crazy with the game having like 5-6 songs on the radio, as it happens that one track can be played 4 times in a row... Or that non-interactive NPCs spawn and disappear randomly... Or that you can see lines of glitched cars stuck on the streets, or driving through signs and garden fences. Or the lights of your car start flickering for no reason. God forbid you try to sidetrack and walk to admire the views. You will get stuck between models, or you will walk on an invisible wall sitting meters in the air above ground, or falling through map flooring. Don't get me started on object collision. This feels so sloppy, untested and simply lazy. What is the weirdest is the spaghetti type of coding/engine used, as Lake sets my CPU ablaze with the temperature levels of 88 Celsius (which can be scary).I am kind of disappointed with the developers since they could have just fixed those small things, rather than hoping that people would ignore them as they focus just on the story. Gameplay wise there there are also visible shortcuts (no animations for certain actions, you just get black screen like with entering/exiting vehicle) and so on. And if gameplay was kept so simple, it shouldn't be that glitchy.Devs could have added more details to make the world more cozy and believable, as there are basically objectives to do and nothing beside it. Sounds quite discouraging right? So how could I rate this game positive?Simply because I decided to play this game after watching a trailer and I had no real expectations of what I will find. And I found myself mirroring the game situation in my real life. And it hit me right in the kokoro. I left my home country in my late 20s, and now in my early 40s I am endlessly rethinking my choices. Which actually are the same as in game: staying where I am, coming back to my home town where things remained the same and changed, at the same time. Or just travel and try someplace new. This games shows very well how people are torn between their past, present and future. How many things we are missing out and how many relations dissolve over time. Nostalgia, wanderlust and melancholy are all present in this game, as it is in life of many of us. And in terms of the game topic and showing that dilemma, Lake simply nails it.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really know what to say about this game. There's an incredible amount of jankiness from the animation to the annoying flickering shadows and the frustratingly slow walking. It has a certain amount of charm though and that kept me playing until the end of the game. The animation is probably the weakest point. The voice acting is great but what you're watching just doesn't match up. Characters stare off into space when chatting and don't have much life to them. There's not even an animation for getting in and out of the van which is something you do many, many times in the game. Walking is so slow that you just try to park your van as close to your target as possible and hope you don't have to make a delivery at the pier.It's not all bad though. The lake is very pretty and the story is nice. It doesn't feel like your decisions carry much weight, more like you're choosing whether you want to take part in an activity or just skip it. There's no conflicts if you want to accept everything offered as I did. It's a relaxing game though and it's nice to drive around without too much to care about.Overall it's hard to recommend unless you're specifically looking for something mind numbing to waste a few hours on. Still, I played to the end and did enjoy it enough to give it a positive rating.EDIT: A couple of weeks after finishing the game I still find myself reflecting on how nice it was to drive around the lake in the sun and how serene the experience felt. Despite its flaws I think this is a game that sticks with you in a good way.

_childDocuments_.review: Heya folks, Shaun here, and I'm back with a new review. In this one, I'm covering an indie adventure game called Lake by Gamious and Whitethorn Games. Big thanks to the developers and publisher for the chance to play and review the game.Lake is super relaxing adventure game that revolves around a woman named Meredith Weiss who returns to her home town after 22 years to work for the postal service to help her father for 2 weeks. During these 2 weeks Meredith delivers mail and meets many new, and old, people. Meredith works a stressful job as a computer programmer and she uses her time in Providence Oaks to ultimately decide what she wants to do with her life from here on. Does she return to her stressful job in the big city, or does she stay in Providence Oaks, or possibly something else entirely? Your choices during these two weeks will determine what Meredith winds up doing but ultimately you can choose any of the 3 options at the end depending on the choice. The game offers a lot of chances to make up for mistaken choices so nothing is set in stone until the end of the game.There are a couple things that I thought could use a little improvement. First are the character animations, they looked a bit stiff when you were walking around. Traffic could be pretty wonky at times as well and there were a couple instances where they were driving way off to the side of the road or they turned really wonkily. I'll also admit that the voice acting took a bit to get used to but once I was, I didn't mind it in the least. These are relatively minor in the grand scheme of things but they were noticeable so I figured I'd mention them.Overall, Lake has been a really fun and relaxing experience and one that I didn't realize I needed. Sometimes it's nice to play games that are slow and don't require much effort and this game has been quite enjoyable in that regard. I admit that it likely won't be something everyone will enjoy, but if you're in the market for a game to play in-between larger games then I gladly recommend Lake. I give Lake an 8 out of 10, very enjoyable game to relax with for a few hours.Until next time folks!My video review:

_childDocuments_.review: Do I recommend it? Yes, why not. This is a fine game with emphasis on fine.The game follows Meredith having to work in the post office covering for her dad and depending on your actions, reconnecting to her past life or just moving on from her past life.For the most part you play as Meredith in a third person view and cut to close-ups of her and other characters for dialogue scenes. You deliver mail in the mornings and can choose to do different activities during the afternoon and the night. The gameplay is fine, nothing extraordinary, you get to drive the mail truck, walk around as Meredith and choose to participate in some activities and how to response to different people. The story is fine, a little cliché but still nice and the characters are likeable for the most part, so all in all, it's an enjoyable game and experience.Now why isn't this game better? Why am I not praising everything about the game?Well, the game can get a little boring, predictable and it's not as emotionally strong as you'd expect it to be. It's fine if you like your games to be "light" and "relaxing" experiences, this has you covered, but I think with just a few minor and maybe not so minor changes, this could have been a much more memorable experience.For starters, the game pauses too much. Not only you have all the cutscenes that change from the classic, high third person view of games like GTA to a more close up camera of the characters that's still kind of boring with mostly just back and forth shots of the characters, but even just getting in and out of the car cuts to black... I mean, they couldn't even animate Meredith getting in the truck?The only thing this game with GTA is probably some elements of the gameplay, and GTA III managed to animate the main character going in and out of the car and have cutscenes play like movies, with different camera shots and effects and they did all that 20 years before Lake. Of course I don't want Lake to be like GTA, the games are very different, but there's no reason to think that just animating Meredith getting in and out of the truck would be making the game "like GTA" or that having the cutscenes with different camera shots, camera angles and other cinematic tricks would be making the game "like GTA".That's my main criticism regarding the gameplay, it's really not bad, it's just, uninspired, basic and kind of boring.My other major criticism is with the cutscenes. I already mentioned how flat most of them look with the way they were "shot" with mostly flat, uninspired camera angles, but my really big criticism of the cutscenes is how bad the characters are at expressing emotions through body language.The voice acting ranges from good to really good, not really going to great or amazing but at least it's not distractingly bad. My only criticism about the voice acting is that some characters sound like they were pulled from a soap opera or a TV show and they feel acted, but it's not too bad, that said, the facial expressions of the characters reacting to everything is always the same. It's a good thing for this game that there wasn't more drama and we didn't see any character crying because that would have been bad. Meredith sometimes sounds excited but doesn't look excited and kind of the same can be said about all the characters.Again with the comparisons, Half-Life 2 came out in 2004 and look at Alyx's body language, it's not just the facial expressions, her body is expressive in many ways. You can tell from just her body language when she's excited, nervous, happy, frustrated, upset and so on and her face was also very expressive and the game came out 17 years ago. Again, this game is nothing like Half-Life 2, but my point is, being able to show a wider range of emotions through body language would have made this game a lot better in terms of relating to the characters and even being attached to them.I'm also not saying you need realistic graphics, I actually like the graphics of the game a lot, they're in a sweet spot of cartoony and realistic and they're really nice, but I just wanted a them to show more emotion and not just in their voices.And my last piece of criticism is that all in all, the game can get kind of boring. The radio station plays like I think 3 songs in a loop and the songs are cute the first time you listen to them but after you've listened them on repeat during the whole game they get annoying. I actually liked the times the people from the town showed up in the radio and I think it's a missed opportunity to not have more of that. Again comparing with GTA, the talk shows in GTA were hilarious and I often preferred to listen to them than the music because of how funny they were. Lake could have done something similar, not to make it funny with hilarious, over-the-top guests, but it would have been a nice way to get to know the town more. Could have had a station or show talking about the town's story, more variety of events happening, people calling to ask for advice... I don't know, so many things that could have made us feel more engaged with the town.I can think of many things they could have made with the game to make it better (in my opinion). Some are the small things like the animations, others could change the game quite a bit but it could have been interesting, like showing the in-game time so if Meredith doesn't deliver something at some time there could be a consequence or if Meredith doesn't meet someone at a set time they get upset and so on. I don't know, the game mostly let's me thinking about its potential more than about the game itself, but maybe that's just me.So my conclusion is, if you're up for a slow, relaxing game with a cute story and likeable characters, sure, play this game. Just don't expect a life-changing narrative experience and groundbreaking gameplay. Like I said, this is the definition of a fine game and nothing more than that.

_childDocuments_.review: I waffled, but in the end decided to give  a thumbs down. I actually did enjoy it quite a bit but, all things considered, it doesn't quite reach its destination.There's something very beautiful and charming about it. This small Oregon town is so lovingly crafted and rendered, with cars parked in the driveways, swings and barbecues in the backyards, wheelbarrows propped against porches, etc. And the core gameplay loop—delivering mail—is very satisfying. The driving controls are just what you expect them to be, and there's no gaminess or unnecessary systems grafted on top. Just be a postal worker. Live the life.But the environment is also too sparse, feeling unfinished. The town ends up being mostly window dressing that allows almost no interaction with its charms. There are invisible walls everywhere, including a hiking path down to the dam—which even has a sign—that is blocked by nothingness.The charm ends up being skin-deep, too. There's just not much depth to the characters and the story. The earnestness and hokeyness of small-town America is dialed up to absurd levels, such that no character feels real anymore. And there's just so little to the story, which you can pretty much figure out entirely in the first few minutes of the game. I really appreciated how gay-friendly it is, but even the potential same-sex relationship felt disappointingly shallow. It's as if in a frantic desire to appear locally authentic the game lost the ability to be authentically human. I found it hard to care about any of these people. Also, it's weird that everyone in this town can follow their dream and not worry about how to make a living. All the houses are perfect.The game feels unfinished in its production polish, too. There are various audio bugs as certain sounds come in and out at random. And animation bugs: once I delivered mail into thin air, and then a pedestrian disappeared while walking. Also, there's just not enough content: you'll hear the same three songs on the radio throughout the whole game. It gets tiresome and also breaks immersion, because that's not how radio works. Luckily the game isn't too long, but towards the end it does feel like you're delivering mail to the same places again and again. Which, I guess is the point, but the game wants you to love your route while doing nothing to endear it to you.What tipped my thumb down was the endgame. You're allowed to save your state freely throughout much of the game, but then the dev decided that you can't save during the last 20 minutes. The consequence is that if you want to see all the endings you will need to repeat those 20 minutes multiple times. Oh, and did I mention?  This felt like a very petty and annoying design choice and it left me with a bad taste.Maybe what disappointed me isn't such a big deal for you. There's definitely a lot to love about  and I'm looking forward to more narrative-driven games from the dev.

_childDocuments_.review: This game falls under the category "I wish Steam had a neutral button". It's not terrible but I'd be lying if I said it was a good game. This game, much like the small town it portrays is shallow and lacking depth. You play a woman who just finished a work project so she takes a break from her "big city" living to do her dad a solid and work his job delivering mail on her vacation time. Okay I can get behind that premise. It gives me the idea, like with most adventure games that I'll face the difficult choice of staying in the small town or returning to Meredith's fast paced lifestyle.  So I think this game wanted to be an adventure game. Think about similar titles featuring small towns like Tell Me Why or Road 96. Yeah you're in a small location where not much happens but then you have to have compelling characters to drive the story forward. The majority of the characters in this game fell flat for me. Out of a town with maybe 10 side characters you interact with, only 3 had any semblance of depth and 2 of them were the main character's love interests. And even those 2 were lukewarm relationships at best. I mean there's so many things the developer could have fleshed out more. I mean you work with a degenerate gambler, there's an old lady living with cats, even an uptight a**hole who plays games while he works at some motel in the boonies. SO much wasted potential. Then there's the mail truck simulator mechanic, which is your main interaction for the majority of the game. You deliver mail everyday. You can take your time and you pretty much can't fail at your job. Everything goes at whatever pace you want, however, there's no incentive for me to do anything else in town because there's nothing else to do. Even when you choose to hang out with the town's residents after work. All side interactions are summed up with a couple lines of dialogue and rarely lead to any new discoveries or information about your hangout buddies. I don't know, it's just if you're going to have an unengaging game maybe litter it with engaging side quests or mini-games? Or something fun so that when I have to make that "ultimate" choice at the end I feel some connection to the town I spent two weeks in? I had high hopes for this after playing the demo but for me this game fell short of all expectations. If you want to go on a fun adventure I suggest you skip this and play something like Road 96 or any title by Dontnod. Or you could deliver mail in real life. I bet that would be more entertaining than this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Follow Meredith Weiss as she returns to her home town after 22 years of living in the city and reconnects with old and new friends. There she will discover Providence Oaks that time flies and things have changed a lot since she left. She will learn to start living life of her own as she approaches her early 40s.Lake is a friendly open world game where you will choose to help or not, be nice or rude to the people you meet along your mail delivery route by the choices given to you during your interaction with the characters.I recommend Lake as it a non-violent, friendly, 80s theme third-person walking simulator where choices matter. The scenery is beautiful, the music is relaxing and the 80s reference is on point especially in the video club store.Here is a glimpse with no commentary:

_childDocuments_.review: Decent game that's pretty chill, but has some bugs and felt unpolished.The atmosphere, soundtrack, and overall feel of this game reminded me a bit of Life is Strange. Small town, interesting people, and (somewhat) choice-driven story. It could really use some polishing, though. Delivering the mail was fun the first few times, but felt like a chore afterwards. The NPCs will form a line of stopped cars in the road for no reason and will sometimes disappear or spawn in right in front of you. The shadows looked very pixelated even at high settings. The story was decent with a few main choices that change the outcome and the ending felt somewhat abrupt. The soundtrack was good, but only had a few songs that were constantly repeated, so I found myself turning the radio off most of the time.Overall, it's a decent game if you enjoy choice-driven stories and want to chill out delivering mail in a small town. I'd have a hard time recommending it at $20, though. I'd wait and get it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: Lake is a gorgeous little game, full of heart and personality. i woudn't take its plotlines and characters too seriously, as there's a certain Hallmark fairytale vibe to the entire thing, but i found myself smiling multiple times while playing both the main and DLC storyline simply due to the charming nature of all the characters and plotlines intertwined in the story of a simple mail route. the gameplay is simple but also fun to drive around in the mail truck and deliver the mail day-by-day, with enough optional events occuring between each day to keep the game interesting to play through. there's quite a lot of choice in each branching storyline and i was impressed by the numerous different places Meredith could end up, although i had to go with Robert as a certified man lover. the romance storylines are hilarious and heartwarming if not taken entirely too seriously -- in reality, if a guy treated me the same way as Robert i'd probably run away from town, but in Lake there's no better place to have a classic trope-y romance. the only frustration i had was with the driving itself; sometimes the car didn't steer properly and i kept having to turn the radio on and off and on and off to stop it from playing randomly. but overall, a very worthwhile game with lots of things to keep one entertained and fantastic replayability value. <3

It gave me the escapism I so desperately needed, and for that I will be forever grateful. It is comforting, wholesome and relaxing as well as being funny and fun. A complete all-rounder, and I will always sing its praises to anyone and everyone. Also, when I first started playing I thought the songs on the radio were lame... Now I have them on my Spotify and play them all the time. They do grow on ya!

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoying this game so far, characters are interesting and it's so relaxing just driving around in a pretty environment. If you enjoy how simple and cozy animal crossing is you will probably enjoy this game. Not to mention the video store owner is super cute. Hope they add to this game eventually

It is super slow paced and relaxed, and it really is a great stress reliever.The choices you make don't affect the ending much, so while some might think it's pointless, I think it's great because you don't get stressed from choices. Controls for driving and just the game in general are quite good (I use mouse and keyboard), interesting dialogues and vantage points, and driving around is just so chill, especially with the radio on. God the music!! The music is amazing and very well curated.It took me over 10 hours to complete the game the first time because I just took my time, and I intend on playing the game again at some point just to experience the driving and its music again.

I had this game on my wishlist forever and the trailer made it seem like it'd be fun and story-rich. Instead, it is a walk/mail delivery simulator with very surface level characters and dialogue. I was completely underwhelmed and had to get his money back. Let's stop excusing games that are mediocre by labeling them as "chill" when in fact they are just lack-luster. Glad other people liked it but damn, I'm not the one.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was so worth the money. It has everything I love in a video game. The relaxing driving, interesting story with choices, beautiful scenery, and much more. Just finished it a couple of days ago and have recommended it to all of my friends. It is the perfect game to play whenever you feel anxious or overstimulated.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: Lake is a very cute litte game. It's entirely unexciting, it's entirely unchallenging and it's... actually a boring game. Actually all that you do is delivering mail. There is no time limit, nothing disturbing ever happens, there ain't no drama, no robberies, no aliens.  Naturally you meet the locals, you learn about their ordinary small-town stories and problems, you make a few decisions that moderately influence the progression and ending of the game, but all in all, that's it. And this is EXACTLY what I wanted from the game. I was aware of what to expect, and that's what I desired. A game to relax. Turn on the PC or Steam Deck in the evening after a long day of work, do my daily mail tour, see what happens next in the story, and then go to bed. And I loved it. It's so calm, so peaceful, so simple. No complicated key combos to learn, no fast reflexes needed. If you are up for a stressless, gentle experience, then this here is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I really this game. It was a calming and peaceful adventure that I didn't have to stress about. There were some glitches with the game that kind of ruined some of the illusion. For example, it spawned me in the middle of the woods while my postal truck was on the other side of the map. _childDocuments_.review: I really thought I was going to love this game. It ended up being one of the most frustrating games I've ever played.First, I agree with the former QA tester who reviewed this game - it's very buggy and needs a lot of fixes. It's also incredibly slow; the walking and driving feel glacial, you can't skip cut scenes and they play out so slowly and unnaturally. And the soundtrack is saccharine Americana (and impossible to turn off in my version of the game - I had to just mute the music)Second, you'll see a lot of people say this game will appeal to "a certain type of person"- I think what they probably mean is middle class, USAmerican or (a very closeted) Northern European and white. There are so many things in this game that are just brushed over as a normal or even nice part of life that for me culturally were massive, massive red flags. I honestly was expecting a left turn into a horror story because it had all the right elements for it, but it turns out it was presenting them totally straight??Finally, I think the main thing that spoiled this game for me is the story. The devs have written such a desperately sad story and I don't think they even realise it. Meredith is a naive and obviously very lonely person, whose good nature and inability to set boundaries is taken advantage of by her work, and then her parents and the people of PO when she's there. I understand that these games are task-driven but this is where a good story / story editor comes in and makes the gameplay elements match up with the story you're trying to tell. Through the entirety of this game there are only 4 times when someone offers Meredith the chance to do something that's actually a fun activity, and only once without her having done a big favour or task for them beforehand (including in the romance storylines). And every single time Meredith has the chance to open up about how she's really feeling to another character, the conversation either gets interrupted or she gets cut off by the character she's trying to open up to. So the mismatch between writing and gameplay presents a set of deeply selfish people who don't truly make the effort to get to know Meredith as she is now, nor do you get the impression that they even really knew the Meredith who was in PO 22 years ago. Especially if you play Meredith as gay, where it's even more evident how isolated she must have been. Good writing would interrogate that - explore the implications to Meredith and Kay's relationship, and Meredith's relationship with the town, if she had grown up gay here and left for 22 years without keeping in touch with anyone at all. Was she in love with Kay at school? Was there something about the town and the people in it that meant she couldn't be herself there? Did nobody ever pick up on it, not even her parents? Even just to show that things are better there now and people have grown and accept her as she is. Instead you get encouraging comments from the town if you are seen with the male love interest and nothing at all even after you've been dating and kissed the female one. Honestly, this game threatened a good time and totally failed to deliver. I will say the easter eggs are cute and the landscape graphics are very nice. But the story is like one of those mobile games where you have to pick between two crappy choices and nothing really happens. It's a skimming stone that skips over what could be a good story and hopes you fill in the blanks yourself. If you enjoy it, good for you I guess but I wouldn't recommend you spend money finding out.

_childDocuments_.review: Simply put if you are looking for action and fast paced stuff then this is not for you.  This is a game that is for relaxing.  Take a break, check out the beautiful scenery, talk with some engaging people and make some life defining choices.  It's not complex, but if you live in the city and can't get out to the countryside to visit your hometown l like me then this provides a nice mental break.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: This little game oozes so much love from the devs, it's hard not to love. It's perhaps janky and a cliché, but the jank and clichés are all in the right places. A late entry, but this game shot up to my favorite games of 2021 instantly.To the lovely devs at Gamious: Keep pouring all that love in these games.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly disappointed. I was looking forward to this game and expected something vastly different than was delivered. Only a few hours of content for way too high a price.I would classify this as an interactive story more than a "game" in any meaningful sense. The story is extremely linear, with little to no player input or choice. At this point, needs vastly more content and updates to be worth the price point.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: Kind of a mixed review here.Just like the story, the mechanics are very stiff and slow. It feels like it takes 5 minutes just to get from your truck to someones front door. You don't really get to interact with people around town. 99% of the time when you deliver something nobody is home.Don't get me wrong though I did enjoy the game. The characters I could interact with were all lovable in their own way. The general story line was very cute. I liked that there were multiple endings to choose from.Overall I'd recommend this to someone if they just wanted a very slow paced, relaxing game
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: Lake is a relaxing and laid back look at what it would be like to be a postal worker for 2 weeks.It's a story about reconnecting with the past and deciding on where you want to go from there.The music is great and fits perfectly with the themes and mood of the story and environment.In addition the beautiful scenery only helps with immersing you in this world.The characters, 90% of them, are believable and likable. Now let's talk problems:- characters being in weird positions during conversations: this only happened during the ending sequences which took away a little out of the emotional moments- the ending sequence was a bit confusing - I don't mean the outcomes, those are pretty obvious - What I mean is that the protagonist says something and then does something different - this is either a bug or a sign of a rush job when it came to the ending- the funny problem - I saw a tanker take flight while coming down a hill LOLThe game also has a little bit of replayability, with 3 different endings and character decisions.Should you buy this game ?Yes, full price, but I would wait a week or two more to give them some more time to fix bugs.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: Lake is just up my street; a tale of a software programmer coming back to their home town for a break and to fill in her fathers postal job.Low octane, drive around, deliver mail, run errands, chat to people, put the radio on, let life happen.  Beautiful.On a technical level, the game is nice; the mechanics are all there and it's a solid piece of work.  Not exceptional, but solid and it all felt good throughout.The sound is good but basic, the songs were a lovely addition and I did enjoy them but (as the protagonist herself alludes to) there aren't that many of them.  Towards the end of the game I did turn the radio off.The story is good and there are lots of clear choices to make, some might not affect the game directly but I did find them having an effect on me (the player) as to other choices I'd make in the game, it was a nice feeling.If you want a slightly repetitive (and I don't mean that as a negative), lovely looking, chilled out gap-year back in our sleepy hometown full of archetypes - then give this a few hours and I think you'll be wondering if you want to leave for the city, or stay for a bit longer.Lovely stuff and really look forward to what the developer does next.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: About a year ago I wrote the following.---------------------I played about an hour of the game and was quite happy to endulge in its relaxing atmosphere. However, there are some nasty sound issues (parts of the audio cutting out intermittently, sometimes footsteps, dialogue, music, ambience; sometimes all at once, sometimes only one or two of those things), which completely ruin the suspension of disbelief. Searching around the forums, the problem has been reported over a year ago and there has not been any update in regards to fixing the issues.I will revise the review if and when I get to play the game proper, as I feel it has potential to be a fun time.---------------------And now, in January 2024, I can happily claim that I revisited the game and no longer experienced any sound issues. Instead I experienced a lovely, cozy, relaxing adventure with some nice music, lovely characters and an overall beautiful vibe. I am 40+ and experienced my share of corporate ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, so the daily routine of delivering mail and helping the town folk was incredibly engaging, relaxing and motivating. It may not be everyone's cup of tea, but for my this was really nice.So I am revising my recommendation from a 'thumbs down due to technical issues' to a solid 'thumbs up'. Good job!
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: You arrive in Providence Oaks where you will work for 2 weeks as a mail delivery gal. The story is good and it has choices that matters. Will you go back to you old life or stay in Providence Oaks? Will you get into any relationships? It's up to you which path to go for. The visuals looks really good too. Its just a really chill and relaxing game where u spend a lot of time delivering mail/packages and talk to the people you meet along the way.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely excellent. The only thing I could improve upon this is I don't want it to end. I'd love the story, which is excellent, to be longer or the ability to deliver much more mail. But still lots of replayability and a very calming and stress free game. Great soundtrack, great graphics, just nailed the care free vibe of the small town life..
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: A very narrative driven game with hardly any gameplay. The voice acting is good, you can make a lot of decisions in dialogs and the character's future. It's a neat little indie game, so adjust your expectations accordingly.The mechanics are pretty much: Go from A to B (i.e. deliver letters and packages) and deal with NPC chatting you up. I also ran into a few minor bugs (character clipping into the terrain, camera clipping into buildings), but nothing serious and no crashes.I'd be interested in the kinds of decisions other players make and how they react to meeting Meredith's friends and acquaintances.The game ran well on my SteamDeck.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautiful and relaxing, like a real lakeside vacation.It doesn't hold up well to multiple play-throughs as even a superficial look behind the game's mechanics reveal just how few of your choices have any affect at all. Most don't even change the very next line of dialogue. This is not as damning as it could be, however, given that a central theme of the game is the importance of putting aside the destination and focusing on the journey - and the journey is gorgeous.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting premise. I think the Life is Strange team might have been able to do something with this idea. But there has to be more to it than what's here. Driving around open worlds is not that fun so a delivery game in that vein is pretty tedious. It would be better if the people you met were engaging but they seem very one note. It's "quaint" but I need something with a bit more grit to it to keep me hooked.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: As a whole, this game is nice. I'd recommend it to someone who likes casual, calm games. But, the story does have a lot of flaws in my opinion.I've noticed some story line/dialogue issues. Some examples:- I chose not to keep the RV, and tell Lori that she can keep it and tinker on it at the shop. Angie shows up at open mic night and tells me that she got the RV from Mickey and June (even though they should have been long gone by the time I gave it to Lori). My two response choices make it seem like I've never heard of the RV before.- I wanted to date Angie during a play through, so I made sure to be as boring and uninterested as possible to Robert (not that we're given too many options). Somehow Maureen still thought that we had a thing and apparently heard that he was into me. (Not sure how that would be possible lol) I figured her dialogue would change to her hearing that Angie was into me, but it didn't.- When Robert wants to make the recording at Jack's place, I chose not to help him. However, during a conversation with Maureen, there's still an option to tell her that I helped him with the recording.The sports betting issue with Frank felt pointless. That would have been a cool angle to the story, but it didn't go very far. Mr. Morgan interrogates you and suspends Frank, all to just leave and have Frank come back like nothing happened.Oh AND- why would there be absolutely no cut scene or at least special dialogue when Meredith has to deliver a chainsaw shaped package to an abandoned house in the woods? That would have been a funny little bonus. (Unless I just haven't been able to trigger it)Overall, the story could definitely use some fine tuning. A lot of the choices during conversations seem pointless, they don't really change anything. And the game ends so quick. I was left a little disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: This game tells a wonderful story about a small town. The core mail delivery gameplay can be seen as slow or repetitive, but this is the type of game where you are encouraged to enjoy those quiet moments in between bigger story points. Lake reminded me a lot of the games "Firewatch" and "The Red Lantern".A small list of grievances I had:-The render distance. In a game about picturesque scenery, seeing rocks and trees pop into existence was a little annoying.-Pedestrians in town will just walk down the center of the street and sometimes cause traffic jams that end up piling 10 cars in a row.-Some sound effects were disproportionately loud (car engines, knocking on doors).-Three hours into my first playthrough, my auto save broke and would only load me onto a black screen. So make sure to manually save every once in a while.Overall I am pretty happy that I bought this game. It's definitely one that I'll replay in a few years to experience the story again.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: Listen, this is not a high-budget game. It's a bit glitchy and there's not a ton of gameplay. But it's charming, and I really do love it. It's a choose-your-own-adventure video game, and that is one of my favorite genres of book! This game isn't for everyone, but it's definitely worth a look. I will certainly be playing through it several more times to find different options! (Also, I have something like 5 hours in the demo that aren't showing up.)
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a completely relaxing game to chill with, this is the game... It is a pretty, scenic game that has a story but you get to choose how the story goes! I have read that there are multiple endings based on your choices, but I haven't finished it nor have I watched game-play to see what those ending are! I am greatly enjoying this game, and not because I received a copy from the devs lol
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: A really sweet and idyllic game. The basic plot of "stay in cozy small town" or "return to big city" is pulled off well, and had a few genuine surprises along the way. Love the use of the mail carrier job to frame the story - as an ex-mail carrier I was very excited to see a game lean into the potential inherent in the job, and it was the perfect framing device for a return to a childhood hometown. Really delighted by a character cameo in the game, and charmed by some of the relationships Meredith can build. I think the art style is nice, and the truck is a delight to drive. (I did successfully flip it once after many attempts, just to see if I could, but overall the game is very forgiving of driving styles that might otherwise get you a citation from a postal inspector, and/or fired.)A few very minor cons:- The game was just slightly too long. Some of the non-plot related deliveries got a little tedious, and the game isn't close enough to a full mail delivery simulator to warrant the number of deliveries that don't even get a little quip from Meredith. I wound up using fast travel during the last few days of the second week, which is generally not a feature I'd ever want in this sort of game.-Steering wheel is on the wrong side of the mail truck.

_childDocuments_.review: Lake's a cute little game that I'd recommend if you can get it on sale (or in a Humblebundle deal, which is where I found it). I absolutely wouldn't recommend it full price though, or even half price. It's about six-seven hours of gameplay if you don't mess up the final ending like I did and have to re-do it.. It's very chill, you roam around a lake in a van delivering letters and packages. I actually really enjoyed driving around with packages, but it did feel very limited. You are delivering to the same places day after day and despite the map being quite small, it doesn't utilise all of it by a long stretch. The pacing is slow, and that was fine, but the mechanics were also slow and that was less so. You have the option to 'run', but your run is a very slightly quicker walk and so you move like a turtle at all times. There was no way to speed up dialogue, even if you've heard it before. I always have subtitles on and prefer to read and click rather than having to wait for people to finish actually talking; that wasn't an option here. It takes several seconds to get out of your van, always on the drivers side, so then you have to slow walk to the mailbox or front door; thankfully you can at least get in the passenger side of the van. And the slice of life aspects were thin. There are technically two romance-able characters, but the game absolutely pushes you towards one. Your dialogue choices don't inspire unique or interesting dialogue. The ending choices felt thin as well; possibly because the game just ends and doesn't actually show you any of the consequences. There were some minor sub-plots that felt more fleshed out than the main narrative and I really wished there were more of them.All in all, this is a relaxing and slow game that's quite enjoyable in it's own little way but is no way near worth retail price. It could have been drastically improved by fully utilising the entire map and by integrating the three endings better with the main narrative, making the dialogue more immersive and with consequences (the Frank narrative line is a good example of how none of your choices really matter) and having more subplots.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: Lake is a refreshing and serene slice of life adventure game where you deliver mail and talk to the locals. To my shock, that's genuinely it. The art direction is gorgeous, even without the highest fidelity assets, and the atmosphere of the Pacific Northwest is nailed here, peaceful and idyllic. The gameplay is procedural and repetitive in the best way possible, the quiet that punctuates the best part of the game, the dialogue and interaction with the other characters. The story and plot are simple as can be, but the well written conversations and excellent voice acting carry it along nicely. I feel the game would've been a bit too slow had it not been so brief, however clocking in at a mere six hours I feel it manages to not overstay its welcome (and for only twenty bucks, that isn't bad dollar/hour value). It's a lovely game, and I had a lovely time with it. It's sweet, it's feel good, it's interesting, and I loved every minute of it. Absolutely recommended.
