_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the game, but I wouldn't recommend it at its current price point, or any at price point it would likely have in the future. I'd give it a "weak yes" if it were free, and a "maybe" in the 1 cent to 3 dollar range. (Disclaimer: I received the game for free).The TL;DR of the matter is that this is a great concept, but a mediocre execution. Playing as a normal 40 year old woman is very refreshing and not something you get to experience often in video games. And the setting and character designs would have meant that you could have very real, human conversations and connections.But when you actually play the game, you'll come to realize that many of your choices don't really matter. The game provides some choices, but they often all lead to the same outcome. To give a fictious example that won't spoil anything, it'd be like if a character asked "So how are you liking the new job?", and you can choose "It's great! I love it!", "Eh, it's okay, I guess" and "I can't wait to be done with it." As a player, you pick "It's great! I love it!" and the NPC will reply "Well, I'm sure it'll grow on you..." which doesn't really make sense as a response to what you said, and seemed like an attempt to have a response that is passably okay no matter which three choices you made.The ending especially didn't make much sense, and it felt like the game go confused about which flags I've set via my dialog choices. To give some spoilery specific, I wanted to  and . This was during a first playthrough, so I didn't know that these were two distinct endings; it just seemed like a win-win situation for everyone: . How it actually played out is  offered to give me a ride to the airport, which I accepted. But then I was suddenly placed in a scene with  This somehow overrode the whole airport thing and I ended up  even though I never actually said I was willing to do this. And then the credits rolled with no explanation of what happened to . Did I just leave him hanging???The characters are charming, and I liked interacting with them, but there just wasn't enough game there to give them the depth they deserve. It's like there's about one paragraph worth of NPC backstories, with a dozen or so NPCs, that you could get through in 20-30 minutes, but the game gets padded out to 6 hours by giving you a driving mini game that doesn't really seem to add much to anything.I suspect there was supposed to be more to the game, but they had to cut a lot of content and ship the game due to running out of budget. Maybe the NPC originally would have given different responses to your dialogue choices, but the dialogue tree got super linearlized due to budget constraints. Maybe delivering packages was supposed to actually "do something", but budget cuts made it so that you always find out nobody's home and you have to keep leaving the packages on your doorstep. Maybe there would have been a whole side quest of helping  instead of the problem just magically going away with no explanation. Maybe you would have actually got to see the , and do a whole minigame around that. Maybe you were supposed to be able to actually go fishing. Maybe, maybe, maybe.I would love to see the developers release a retrospective on all the stuff they wanted to do that they had to cut out. There seems to have been a great game in the dev's mind and imaginations, but sadly what got released only gives us a tiny sliver of it.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't necessarily NOT recommend this game... This is a really enjoyable game to turn your brain off to, but it comes with some major problems. Overall the game feels like it's in alpha. It feels incomplete and very arbitrary. Despite hitting the nail on the head in terms of atmosphere, I would never put this game in the 'Choices Matter' tag since literally none of your dialogue options really matter. Even rude dialogue options will yield the same response from people, and you're able to get all 3 endings just by reloading your last day and choosing the ending you want. This game seemingly does everything wrong, but I did still enjoy the relaxed and casual gameplay, so if that's what you're here for then it might be suitable for you despite its flaws.Some of the errors in the game are just small missed details (like the house with 102 on its mailbox showing up as 202 Lake Rd on the map), but some problems are just from laziness and publishing an unfinished product.- A whole slew of visual glitches: characters laughing and talking with their model not opening their mouth at all, cars glitching halfway underground, cars hovering above the road, character models holding invisible packages in their hands, instructions for the ghostblasters arcade remaining on screen long after you've driven away from the diner- Audio glitch with Angie in her store (midway through the game her dialogue volume became very quiet and then about 3 conversations later it was normal again)- Control glitches: unable to turn the radio off-- which is a huge problem when the game only has 10 songs on its playlist and a horrible shuffle feature. It will repeat the same songs back-to-back sometimes, or play the same 3 songs over and over for a while. Another control glitch was retrieving packages from the trunk. Sometimes it would just close the trunk as if I had pressed F and I would just have to keep trying over and over to interact with E. The ghostblasters arcade game in the diner is also unplayable with how the weapon does not recognize button presses.- Bad movement: Most of the game is spent driving, but the driving mechanics don't feel good. They're not horrible, but not good either. They're just slightly bad but tolerable enough that you adjust to it in time. When you're not driving you're walking, and the walk speed is so slow. You can walk faster, but its a hardly noticeable difference.- When driving, literally 1 second after you stop moving the camera it will automatically adjust the pitch of the camera, sometimes making it impossible to see the road. I literally counted 1 second.- There are no sound effects for driving over a metal bridge, ramming into a telephone pole, etc. Small details that would have made the game feel more finished rather than what it is now, which feels like an alpha release- The game encourages exploration and even gives achievements if you discover some scenic areas, but when I found what looked like a secret hiking trail (with a trail sign and everything) I was met with an invisible wall. This was very unusual given that other hiking trails were really trails, so this left me annoyed and questioning why the developers put a fake trail in at all- While most of the scenery is from individual models of trees, the developers got lazy and used shortcuts too. At the back of the property of 113 Raven Way you can see a levitating 2D facade of trees and shrubbery to make it look like there are more woods behind the cabin. You can walk through this facade and see the mountain and more individual tree models behind it. I wonder why they used this and not just put in a few more models of greenery?By far the BIGGEST flaw of this game is how pointless everything is. Dialogue choices don't matter. Ramming into cars doesn't matter. Driving poorly around police cars, attempting to hit a deer only to have it clip through the van, the mechanic doesn't even need to check up your van. Throughout the game, characters arrange meetings for very specific times, repeating the time and telling you not to be late, when there's not a single clock in the game and you're just magically on time for everything. Using your car horn does nothing, holding up traffic does nothing, ramming into a telephone pole doesn't cause a single mark on the van. Anything and everything you do does not matter, and there are no consequences to your actions at all. It's just a little game of delivering mail where you might choose to do a side quest or two. Or you don't choose that. It literally wouldn't matter.

_childDocuments_.review: Meredith is your high-powered city career woman who comes back to her hometown, Providence Oaks, to do a favor for her father and fill in as the towns mail carrier for two weeks as he and your mom takes a much needed vacation to Florida. Deliver mail and meet old friends and new residents. Kay, the long time best friend, Angie, the movie buff, and Robert, the Lumberjack, as they teach her the true meaning of- wait, is this a hallmark movie?  It isn’t even Christmas! 6-7 hours to complete, Lake is 1980’s atmospheric adventure game with three or four endings and two romanceable characters, Angie and Robert. Recommending Lake is a little difficult for me, because I didn’t like it, hate it, or feel like I gained anything from this. Starting off, people are standoff-ish, blunt, rude, and considering how isolated everyone physically is despite being a town- it’s understandable for them to be a bit prickly since a stranger is delivering their mail- except, you realize it’s not because you’re new, it’s just their entire personality. While a few key characters are friendly, everyone else doesn’t like you and they absolutely will let you know that.  Let’s talk about traffic flow. It’s a small town. You rarely see drivers on the road, but when you do? OH BOY. Traffic jam galore, and what’s causing it? A NPC who forgot to drive causing a chain of multiple cars blocking off entire streets, making delivering mail a bit of a challenge since your walking speed is slower than a grandmother with arms full of groceries. Also, that “relaxing” tag is very deceptive as NPC’s regularly fit themselves in your schedule and making you do something you really should have told them no for. I strongly suggest you just say “I’m Busy!” to everyone you interact with, because in the end, except for a few, your choices throughout the game largely don’t matter. For an example, Kay is your childhood BFF, and aside from doing an emergency side quest for her, I literally told her no for everything and still somehow got her good ending where we reconciled despite, ya know, not ever doing that.  (Do they even have a bad ending?) In conclusion, while Lake is charming in a confusing and unexplainable way, the terrible NPC’s, mediocre graphics, the absolute lie that is the “relaxing” tag, and the weird guilt-trip the game gives you to stay in town while “city life evil, country good” gets banged into your head pushes Lake firmly into my negative list.

_childDocuments_.review: Very boring with cringy dialogue. The main activity in the game is a very basic and boring mailman simulator, and the story isn't anything special either. Just everyday interactions with a bunch of people. There is no "choose your own adventure" there are just some things people ask you to do, and you have the option to tell them "no". I said Yes to basically everything and was done with it within 6,5 hours (it took another almost 1,5 hours to get the other 2 endings because you have to watch an incredibly long cutscene with some dialogue 2 times again to select the other options)On top of litttle and not so interesting gameplay the game isn't very polished either, there are a whole bunch of visual glitches, missing animations (the worst is the absence of an animation to get in and out your car, you do this about 200 times in the game, and every time the game just fades to black and back, but there are also facial animations missing), missing sound effects, and when you play the game too long in a row the audio starts to desynchronise a lot (like 1 to 2 minutes)On the upside: making the final choice does make for a pleasant ending and the game has a nice looking environment and a bunch of background songs that take a while to get repetitive. For €2,- I might've recommended it if you're looking for just a very relaxing game.PS: the lake has nothing to do with anything, kinda lame.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Lake is a very fun and relaxing game with a story. If you just want a cozy game you can take your time with an have fun I recommend.Pros:~Inclusive game: The game allows you to choose to have a romance between a man or woman and though the cast of characters are predominantly white there are a few POC such as Kay and Lori.Amazing visuals and sound: I love taking screenshots in the game. The artstyle of the world is breath taking I love while driving the truck over the dam to just take in the view and just imagine I'm their in real life. You can never go wrong with good visuals and sound.~No time limit: When you play a day in the game it is easy to walk away from your computer without having to suffer any consequences. The day will not be done till you deliver all mail and after you deliver your mail you can drive and explore all you like around the lake.~Able to do all events: Almost everyday when you play their are characters that will ask you to spend time with them after work is over. The great thing the game developers did is they allow us to do all these events without having to choose between one or the other. In one play through you can do all events without having to worry you're going to overlap one event with another.Cons:~5ish hours of gameplay: Now there is roughly 5 hours of gameplay which is a bit short for a $20 game. It would of been better if we had around 8 hours but the 5 hours we do get I say are very good quality.~Bugs and Glitches: To be fair the game just came out and the bugs are minor such as some areas having ground clipping and cut scenes being a bit strange. The only big bug I've discovered while playing is sometimes if you go into the diner you can get glitched behind the counter and you have to stand at the edge of the counter talking to Mo to get out. But this was scary cause I thought I was stuck for good but I'm sure in a update it'll be fix but it's good as a consumer to be aware.Overall rating: 8/10 Blueberry piesConclusion: If you want to pay this game I definitely recommend picking it up. Its fun and nice with a great cast of characters you meet along the way. If the price for gameplay time stresses you then I recommend waiting till its on sale which is okay. But for me the game is replayable cause its just fun talking to the characters and delivering the mail.

_childDocuments_.review: Did I enjoy my time with Lake? Absolutely. It's like a playable Hallmark movie where you can subvert expectations left and right, embodying the heroine Meredith however you please. You even have both straight and queer romance options.The story is worth it and refreshingly unique for an open world game. It's a short six hour jaunt, easily played in one sitting. Most achievements are just a matter of doing sidequests or exploring the map. It's a very relaxed game. That said, this is a janky game - visual glitches, weird choices of lighting (night time looks like they just turned down the default brightness setting), and a near-useless sprint function can hamper things. I even once had the wheels on my truck stop spinning until I restarted the game. Probably the worst part was the radio mute function not always behaving itself, forcing me to listen to country music some in-game days. Nothing separate browser tab with more genuinely relaxing music can't solve!I really like the ideas here, and I'd love to see more games in this style - there's several clever moments I won't spoil - but it does fall short of what it could've been with a bit more polish and focus. A noble experiment worthy of a stronger successor.

_childDocuments_.review: So, sadly I wish I could write a good review for this game, but like Meredith, I just can't lie. When I started, the concept seemed cute and fun, but unfortunately as things went further I found this game to be exceptionally tedious and boring. The concept was so great - a chill, relaxed environment, with a lot of colorful character potential. The problem is that the environment becomes so dull after only a few days in game and the 'colorful' characters are either about as colorful as a newspaper or so rude and obnoxious that I couldn't stand the cutscenes involving them. They were either unlikable or out of place and while I liked Robert I found the relationship so sadly underdeveloped because the game kept trying to force me to hook up with Angie (who I found irritating, forceful and legitimately a little crazy). The language was also exceptionally jarring and unnecessary in a game that was supposed to be so chill (at least two F words for absolutely no reason at all), both from utterly useless NPCs (Matt, the jerky motel clerk who had zero development besides a slightly embarrassing injury and the pothead hippes, who you're forced to interact with in order to randomly be given an RV?))The setting had potential to be fun but there was very little actual attention paid to the details - the 80s time period was completely lost besides a few random movie jokes here and there (Hello?? Where was the fun 80s music?? The wild and crazy 80s outfits??), the random townie NPCs were just walk-bots with no personalities at all (I literally, on purpose, ran into a cop car to see if anything would happen and nothing did) and the ones you could interact with weren't  really much better. You could only go into a place/interact with people when/if you had mail to give them. The mail deliveries themselves got old after the first few days, the music was... awful and repetitive (again... 80s retro time period and you went with easy listening indy-pop?) and good LORD the walking was torture, even at 'top' speed. The game was buggy (I at one point randomly spawned in Robert's yard without my truck, cars were appearing flying in the air or got stuck in the road so traffic backed up through the entire town, I hit random invisible walls, people vanished mid-cutscene, etc.) and ultimately just felt so super unfinished. The characters you could interact with were for the most part a waste of time and energy and no decisions you made or side quests you did had any impact whatsoever, apart from the last one, which really only impacted the final cutscene. Everything really genuinely just felt... pointless. There was a TON of unfinished material or things that just never went anywhere despite the obviously forced choices (Frank's gambling issues, the random metal detector dude, the annoying motel jerk, the bait shop guy, just to name a few).Potential. That's all the game had. Sadly, like most of the people in P.O... it's unrealized potential. And I really hope my refund goes through, because it was absolutely NOT worth a dime.And to clarify, the only reason it took me so long to finish was because I left the game running for 3 hours and because it takes Meredith so long to walk around!

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first time that I reviewed a game as I do not recommend to play it by other players. The main reason why I am thinking like this is that this game is too boring to play when the story is concerned. However, the atmosphere is quite tranquil and chilling. Game mechanics are also too easy to understand. The main problem is that the context of the main story is "happy". Whoever you talk with smiles and there is always a happy atmosphere. In my opinion, the contexts could be reprocessed better For example, something bad might be happen to the main character while delivering the packages and so on... In addition, the context is too linear, which means there are no or few bad events and they do not affect the main story. _childDocuments_.review: Mixed review. First off, the game has frequent audio bugs when played on my high-end desktop PC. I would pause and un-pause the game to fix this. Usually it would work. I don't recall it happening on my Steam Deck but I didn't play it there much. I also didn't see a way to delete save files, and each time you manual save, an additional save is added to the list, creating many built up save files.I like Meredith and thought she was a good character, and I cared about what happened to her. Many/most of the other characters failed to pull me in. It ended up feeling lonely because I didn't feel she ended up with any great friends. (Some of the better characters imo: Meredith, Steve (voice only), Frank, maybe Maureen.) A game like this needs good characters.The radio having only three (?) songs seemed inexcusable. I'm surprised that isn't pointed out in every review. I would usually have it turned off, but the game could use more variety of music in general. Also, something needs to be added to make delivering the mail less monotonous. Yes, some of the calm and relaxation comes from the simplicity of the mail delivery, but sometimes it just felt like something was missing, when it's the same each day. For example, I felt the thunderstorm that finally came near the end of the game set a wonderful mood and ambiance. Still, Meredith didn't seem to make any notice of it.I liked the concept of the game and I enjoy games like this. In the end I felt Lake was good/decent, but not great. With that being said, I would be interested in a sequel if there were significant improvements, better characters for Meredith to meet, and something to make it more interesting. Sorry if this all sounds harsh. Lake is a neat game with a fairly unique concept and I am glad I played it. In my opinion there is a lot of potential and room for improvement though.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not *bad*, but it doesn't feel that good - everything comes with a "however". Hard to explain, but I'll try.6/10.TL;DR: I do recommend it, but it is very flawed. Technical issues (eg: sound and AI), repetitive gameplay loop, and almost every single positive overshadowed by an often bigger negative. I recommend it mostly because I would like to see a second one, but only after a lot of work, mostly on the technical side.Story:- It's easy to flow with and very simple.However:- It can feel forced at times; like at the end when I almost got "kidnapped" by the Lumberjack (long story, too spoilery) which came out of nowhere and ruptured the flow a lot.- The ending choice (SPOILER)  Dialogue & D. options:- It's very serviceable and the options are regular and feel personal enough.- You don't get forced down a dialogue path, and most of the time, you can "back out" of a situation even when neck deep.However:- It feels a little dry. Most of the options carry weight only so far as that dialogue tree, so when you stop talking to the person, it's like you never spoke to them until you meet them again.- Sometimes the dialogue feels a little disjointed. You can go on a "date", then straight-up tell someone you're not interested in them, but they'll keep acting like you've been married for the past 50 years.Characters:- They're great, each feels like an individual, and it's easy to get invested into some of their stories.However:- You can only interact with them either during your rounds (You serious? I'm busy!) or during brief ~5 minute conversations at the end of the day. It just feels a bit confined.World:- I love the lake and how different the places feel. The terrifying cabins, the blissful town, the beautiful campgrounds; it's all really nice.However:- The load distance feels like it was made for the PS1. Looking across the lovely lake to see a barren wasteland knowing it's a lush forest feels like massive wasted potential, and looks plain ugly.- It feels sterile in places. If it's not a named character's house, they will never be in, despite cars on the road and in driveways. Even if it was a simple fade-to-black and some generic "thank you" dialogue, it would add, but there is nothing.Technical side: (more or less all negative)- The AI is terrible at its best. I had a random ~10 car traffic jam in the middle of town; a pedestrian walking in zig-zags in the road; a lorry slam into a cop car, the cop car pushes the lorry out the way, and they both drive on as if nothing happened.- Several bugs and glitches: Finished delivery and I was sent in to orbit; people walking through objects; truck's lights cutting in and out; rain sounds coming and going; dialogue going from mute to space shuttle loud to normal within the same line. There's more, but I'll move on.- Gameplay loop is quite enjoyable; repetitive, but I liked it. That said, it got quite annoying having to deliver to the same ~15 houses/businesses. There's so many places you could go, but you only ever go to the same ones, over and over again.

_childDocuments_.review: When I wishlisted  last December it appeared to me like a  experience without the adventure -- just a relaxing ride in someone else's shoes through a beautiful Oregon forest. Now that I've finished the game, I can confidently say that  delivers in that respect. I could relate very much to Meridith's work related stress, as well as her wish to be a mail man for two weeks, so my connection to the player character couldn't have been stronger. And that's despite the many issues this game has.The game is riddled with imperfections: lacking animations, inconsistent VO, cliché character archetypes, etc. When I started my playthrough, my head was still in playtesting mode, so I've got a whole list of these. But the thing is, the game managed to set my head to relaxation mode all by itself. Even though it's got some rough edges,  still provided the emotions and experience I expected from it, which only goes to show how well the devs managed to focus on the important stuff despite their small scope.And to be really honest, now that I'm writing this review I'm already starting to miss my daily route around the lake. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Lake over promises and under delivers.2.5 hours in and there's little to no story content, just painfully slow pacing and lazy animating. Characters don't have animations so between looking at them then you, the game just snaps them into their second position and it's unsettling. Characters don't even really have expressions even in moments that are 'meant to' be emotional or intense - it makes it feel like there is a huge disconnect between you and the characters you're meant to be 'falling for'.This game is riding the indie wave of 'cozy and cute simulator! so wholesome' but fails to live up to the hype. People like the idea of the game, but not the game itself.In addition, it's poorly optimized and uses about 40% of my CPU when running - I have a high end system. Kind of messed up.Pro: One shortcut - to teleport back to the post office after your run just throw your van into the lake. The game will make you want to do that anyway.

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to describe how I feel about the game. The concept itself, I love. Super laid back game and I really love the art style. I will be happy if there is add on content. I did enjoy the game, however the pros outweigh the cons for me. I do recommend this game but would tell people to wait and see if it goes on sale. _childDocuments_.review: I really, wanted to love this game. I love cozy games , i love dating games , & i  love choice games. However , this game just comes off very . . . surface level.  All of the conversations are super short , so I don't feel like I connected to any of the characters in a way that made me care about the town. Like, sure it's pretty, but 90% of the town is old folks who gamble or hate young people. Then the young people there all want to leave. You have 2 romance options -- Angie and Richard. I went for Angie , simply because I'll probably always pick the LGBTQ option first , && also because Richard was genuinely just . . . boring.  Honestly, I almost considered choosing to stay single and just leave the town. Angie's route falls into the Lesbian Niche of 'we hung out twice in two weeks & now we're basically living together.' I get it, lesbians uhaul joke. Like there was such a chance to have a genuine conversation about LGBTQ issues in the 80s, especially in a small , old folks town. But nope. It's just not there. You can't even talk about her to anyone. Everyone just assumes you're going for Richard. The driving in this game is also unpleasant. Which sucks for a game where you're driving for most of it. The turns take way too long & are so wide. I genuinely just fast traveled anywhere i could to get out of it. Watching the AI hit things in autopilot could be entertaining at times, though. In general, I just think this game feels unfinished. The characters show 0 emotion other than happy , even when the voice actors are clearly upset. The soulless eyes really unnerve me. It's so short and so empty of any real interaction with anyone that i'm kind of glad the games over. Just felt like I was playing for so long with no reward. Again, I love cozy games -- Stardew and Sims and Dating Sims and Animal Crossing are all on my top tier lists. But this was just . . . tedious. I won't be playing it again unless there's like a huge overhaul that makes it even slightly interesting. For what it's worth, though, the monotony and absolute vacancy of life really does simulate small , country , old town life.

_childDocuments_.review: Lake is about a, I assume, middle-aged woman taking a break from her career in a large city. She leaves to visit her hometown and takes over a temporary job as a mail delivery driver. In this game you get to drive around to deliver mail while meeting a lot of different personalities. You are able to give different responses while speaking to people in town, which will change the conversation and their demeanor towards you. I was always nice and helpful during my playthrough and had a very happy and peaceful ending. Lake also offers several endings, depending on decisions you have made throughout the game. Now to the gameplay itself. Lake is one of those games you play at the end of the day to have a relaxing time before going to bed or to just have some peace after a stressful day. Since you deliver mail in this game, it can happen to feel a little repetitive but that is to be expected with this kind of profession. I really enjoyed the interactions and different characters but it felt quiet sometimes, especially when nobody answered the door. I noticed a few times that the game had tiny bugs like not showing the buttons to press or telling me to return to the post office even though I just started my round. It's nothing too distracting though. There is an achievement to go to the church which didn't pop for me at first but was resolved by restarting the game and driving back there. All in all, it's an enjoyable experience for story lovers but a little slow sometimes. I personally loved the game and unlocked all endings by reloading the last checkpoint.

_childDocuments_.review: Lake is not a game you get for a thrilling story or amazing gameplay, it's a comfort game. I bought this game because I was bored, and it did help with my boredom. The scenery is nice and cozy, the characters are pretty well voice acted, and the story isn't terrible although it isn't absolutely stellar. There's some parts where the romantic aspect of the story is just completely forced, and I was actually caught off guard when the "romantic" option came out of no where. (Im not going to say what it is just for spoilers sake). There isn't much interaction with people outside of the forced cut-scenes and I feel the game would benefit greatly with more free roam interactions. Overall, if you have the money to spend, you're very bored, and are looking for a nice singleplayer game to relax to, I would say this game can provide you with at least 5-6 solid hours of enjoyment (for one playthrough that is).

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying the game has been at the top of my wishlist for MONTHS. I REALLY want to recommend this game, and I haven't quite finished it yet, so maybe my review will change. However this game need a lot more work. The release date was heavily rushed. The story is nice and cute and there is LGBTQ+ rep which is also nice, but the bugs truly remove you from the atmosphere. I was going to wait to write my review until I was finished, but the bug I just got makes me not want to even play it again. I was teleported to Robert's cabin on the opposite side of the lake, without my truck, and I cannot describe how little I desire to walk back to it at this point (it is at the post office) and you walk AND RUN at the pace of a slug moving through tar. Not to mention the frequency in which entire dialogs are skipped for no reason. If I could refund this I would. TLDR: Save your money until the bugs are fixed, the game is unenjoyable as-is.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly this is such a simple and cozy game with such pretty scenery. I would definitely recommend it if you need and escape or just some time relaxing. Would love if there were a bit more side quests or just general exploration to do, but even like this it's really good and worth your time. Just a game you need for cozy, rainy autumn afternoons when you feel like drinking you tea and staying in gaming something easy and relaxing.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: (spoiler-free review)Man, I'm torn. I'm a big fan of walking simulators, and Lake is, for all intents and purposes, a GOOD walking simulator. Here's the basics. It's 1986. You play as Meredith, a 40ish year-old woman taking a vacation from work to fill in for her father, who is the mail carrier in Providence Oaks. Providence Oaks happens to be the tiny Oregon town where you grew up before leaving for university and beginning your successful, albiet stressful, career in the blossoming tech field. You essentially rediscover the town while you deliver mail in your trusty mail truck. There's opportunities to make friends, help people out, and maybe even pursue some romance.But here's the thing...Before you can get to all that stuff, you HAVE to deliver the mail. Like, every day. That means you'll be driving all over the town -- every day -- stuffing envelopes in mailboxes and delivering packages to porches. At first, this is relaxing and charming. Maybe even a bit Zen-like! A few hours into the game though, it starts to feel like filler. The town is largely empty, and 90% of the day, you won't talk to anyone while you work. Juuuuust delivering packages to porches and envelopes to mailboxes.Where the game really shines is AFTER you finish your shift for the day. I won't spoil any of the storylines or activities, but I truly enjoyed (almost) all of the interactions with old friends, new residents, and coworkers. Is it a fairly linear storyline? Sure. But it's a good one, with some choices that meaningfully change the ending of the game.Long story short, if you enjoy walking simulators, give this one a shot. Just set your expectations accordingly!
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: Having completed this game I feel like it was definitely worth the buy! Especially if you like slice-of-life games with a little bit of drama thrown in. Though I did feel like the delivering parcels bit was a bit tedious I didn't mind it as much, given that it led to developing the story.My favorite character had to be the writer, given that his accent was hilarious.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: I'm in love with this game and it really saddens me to give it a negative review but the game has a serious audio issue where the sound constantly cuts out and it has really ruined both the immersion and the experience I have tried everything to fix it to no luck i'd be more than happy to give the game a thumbs up if their was some type of fix
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: This game is truly a 10/10. You come to Providence Oaks as a retreat working temporarily as a postal worker, although it may seem like something uneventful, the developers of this game include small side quests, meeting the unique and adorable townspeople and also while enjoying the upmost of beautiful views no matter where you are in this map. The game clings to relaxation, story lines, LGBTQ+ inclusiveness, romance and much more that I believe you should play and experience first hand. What I also appreciate about this game is they represent a woman just trying to figure out where she wants to be in life and i believe they represented it beyond amazing. This game creates a one of a kind experience and I hope to see more like this in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: Lake is a narrative adventure game on par with indie and AA titles like Firewatch, Life is Strange, Night in the Woods, and Gone Home. While it features a novel approach to the story loops of the game (delivering the mail around the small hometown you grew up in), at times, the speed and redundancy made the pacing feel off. While I appreciated many of the story beats, a lot of it felt underedited or that things were cut from the plot(s) that were never amended or updated in the dialogue. The narrative choices you make are also not noted as important or indicated as closing off routes or having an impact on the overall story, but it feels like for the most part, most things are available to you and heavily signposted regardless, which isn't an entirely terrible way of doing this. Still, I felt lost in places, and also the fact that autosaves only happen when you back entirely out of the game meant I had no progress saves when doing a very long playthrough.It also has a weird surreality that hooks into American media in a lot of places for the era, but it doesn't feel like it's made by American developers, in that there's very little commentary on American current events (aside from the Challenger explosion) or pop culture at this time. It is a weird mish-mash of America-seen-through-the-lens-of-other-people, and a quaint amalgam of 80s, 70s, 60s and 50s nostalgia. Still, it wins high aesthetic marks and the setting does a lot to earn its charm.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is extremely simple from what ive played. There doesnt seem to be much to it. It is very slow and has many bugs. Keep in mind that it is an indie game but I was really expecting more from this game tbh.Pros: The characters are pretty coolLove the interactionsThe scenery and graphics are incredibleCons: Very little to do... get in ur truck, deliver and talk to people... go home and thats it.Couple of bugs, like the sound of the truck is constant through every scene.Walking is incredibly slow, runnng and walking is basically the exact same speed.The music for the truck is basically like 2 songs on repeat, but if you dont listen to the radio, all u hear is the sound of the truck.In conclusion, this game is very basic, the storyline is pretty dry and the game gets boring after like 5 minutes of playtime.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a relaxing walking simulator about delivering mail in a beautiful little town. The story is nothing extraordinary but it's nice and I really loved the character interactions. The voice acting is a bit off but OK. The music is nice but it gets repetitive really fast. There are also multiple endings, but only a few of your choices has really an effect and it's easy to play so that it makes an inconsistent story. For example, you could say how you hate this place all the time and yet still choose to stay at the end, or vice versa. There are also some annoying bugs.Overall, I recommend it because of the good atmosphere and nice characters, even though there are some things that can break immersion.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could like this game, and it could have been a lot nicer, if it wasn't for the very repetitive gameplay. The fisherman in this game at a certain point says "there's a fine line between relaxation and boredom"and this game alters between the two. I know that being a mailman/woman is a repetitive job in real life too, but I feel like they could have made this game a bit more interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: I have finally finished the game and so I've decided to edit my review and replace it with a pros and cons list. *PROS*- Beautiful game. The scenery is stunning. Sunrise is so beautiful. The view of the mountain and lake seems real. Love it!- Super cozy. I love the feel of this game. I can relax and just enjoy this small town. - The characters have such unique personalities. - I loved that if you tried to run someone over, the van would slow to a crawl behind them. I loved that!*A LITTLE BIT OF BOTH*- The voice acting for most characters was great, however, a few were pretty cringe and pretty comedic  and not in a good way. It took away from the game.- The soundtrack grew on me but I did expect it to have a bit more oomph. You're in your mail van for most of this game and so the radio is a constant. The rotation of songs was pretty limited and none of the songs really hit me in the feels, you know? It wasn't bad, but, it wasn't amazing, either.*CONS*- The story line feels linear and rushed. You barely have any choices. The romance is either shoved on you without your choice or they play hard to get and then suddenly confessing they'd marry you. We need more context, we need more of the middle. It ruins the game, honestly.- Lack of animations. Not having animations of getting in and out of your van, drinking/eating, food being placed on the counter/table, arm movements, getting out of a booth during a cut scene, FACIAL EXPRESSIONS!!!, etc. It took away from the game. I really wish they delayed the game to get these things taken care of. It just felt choppy and unfinished.- Lack of features in your mail van. - They advertise that after work can choose how you want to spend your evening... but it's so limited that it doesn't even feel like a choice. You always have the option of reading a book at home or watching a show at home. Occasionally you'll have another option depending on things that happened during the day. Why can't I do what I want? Where are the choices? - Outside of the current "mission" that you're on, you have 0 interactive choices. If I want to go talk to XYZ, why can't I? SO LINEAR.- If I hit a cop, he should at least pull me over and tell me to drive more safely or give me a ticket. At the very least, I should get in trouble at work for messing up the mail van!- I could hit a thousand things but no damage to the truck. Why have a mechanic if I don't get to bring my van in to be serviced? The mechanic even states if anything goes wrong, to bring it to them when you first meet them. Why was that not followed through?- The "faster" walking option for Meredith is barely noticeable. I understand why, but, if I'm really not going to get there any faster, I'd prefer to not even have the option.- The fast travel option I feel is unnecessary and out of place.*OVERALL*I am going to still recommend this game because I enjoy it more than I dislike certain elements. I wish they'd address certain things and make some changes. I think it would truly elevate the game so much. 5.5/10. With the way the game is currently, I wouldn't suggest getting it unless it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing cozy game. You play as a postal worker. The developers thought of everyone here: you can drive manually, there's autopilot, fast travel, and an endless mode! The chosen style of graphics ensures that the town is absolutely beautiful, worth driving through again and again.  The residents are charming and not rude initially, merely cold or frank. The dialogue is great for what it is. You have a variety of answers. I enjoyed their quests.Endings were fitting, believable and I loved the one I chose.The DLC is a prequel set during the previous Christmas, offering interesting tidbits of the characters and setting from the main game. I found it worth buying, it being more of the same, with just enough variation to be fresh.All in all, I absolutely loved this game! The only downside is the music. While chosen very well, it is mentioned even in game that the playlist needs more songs. When you get bored of the few there are, just turn the music volume all the way off and play your own alongside the game. I enjoyed it even more that way, it reminded me of recording my own tapes from the radio.Go for a drive!

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't know really what to expect from the game. But it's a quiet and peaceful game where you get to be in the shoes of a mail carrier. It's a small open city where you get to drive around in a truck to deliver the mail inside the town, along the way you get to know the town people and can even develop a romantic intrest (you even can choose if you want a relationship with a male or female)! But it didn't bother me that much because all I wanted and expected from this game was to peacefully deliver mail. My hopes are met and I enjoyed it a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a chill, easy game which is obviously still in the Early Access stage so hopefully a lot more to come. If you're into fast-paced games, this is not the one for you. This is a gentle game, quite slow but pretty and the story is kind. I would like to see more things to do as part of the story line, perhaps having to make choices of what to do each day instead of having one optional activity per day, you have to decide which person to let down. Have interactions that actually alter the story line. The character walks very slowly so I'd like for that to be adjusted too, and when filling a postbox the little flag needs to be raised for authenticity. All in all, it's a fine game, very pretty but with a long way to go to be the great game it can be.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: This was/is such a cozy wholesome little game. It was far too short for me, as I had loads of fun just delivering mail and enjoying the peaceful little town. The romance options did feel a little forced at times, perhaps the result of Meredith's stay being only two weeks long and the game having to make up for that in story? But I did love the different options and choices. I also really enjoyed the 80's vibe. It felt like a warm blanket of nostalgia from the VHS cover parodies in the movie rental store to the arcade game in the diner and even the music having an overall 80's style. The scenery was quite beautiful and I enjoyed many of the characters story lines. It was interesting watching the town change actively in just the two weeks Meredith spent there, and I really hope that more games and stories like this come out in the future. Pick this game up if you like cozy little indie games and 80's vibes. 10/10!

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! It feels nostalgic, like a game I would've enjoyed as a kid. It's cute and relaxing with interesting characters. I think it would be really cool to see some expansions or a sequel of some kind, because I feel like there was more to explore. Kind of like a hallmark movie, but you get to make the choice at the end. Would be nice to be able to interact with more of the items and people. Definitely recommend playing this one.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR I do recommend it, but definitely temper your expectations, and the game is not without its flaws. Has some bugs, story feels very rushed to me, but base game feels just very serene and nice and I would recommend experiencing that (and don't expect too much more). Buy when on sale. 7/10I just finished the game, I thoroughly enjoyed it, I thought it was a really nice and peaceful change of pace. Unfortunately I expected a bit more of a mail delivery game (think Eurotruck simulator, but mail). This is not that. The mail delivery is very simple. Relaxing, but simple. That became obvious pretty fast though, that the game was more about interacting with the NPCs in town. Which is okay.What was less obvious (to me at least) is actually how heavily it starts leaning on those NPCs. I was quite disappointed how the game actually started to revolve around the NPCs, way too fast. I kinda just wanted the chill mail game with the occasional chat, getting to know the NPCs, see their personalities getting fleshed out. At a certain point it feels like it's all about important life choices (that feel very rushed, in my opinion) and .. then the game is just over. So that kind of left a bad aftertaste?But I feel like Gamious really has found something special with this game, if they only just fleshed it out a bit more and (in my opinion) slowed down the story waaaay more (and get rid of some bugs). I want more weeks to spend in Providence Oaks, I wanna take my sweet ass time. I was just starting to get to know the town and learn the routes by heart when the game was over. It's just such a shame.I think the game could easily (!) be an 8/10 or 9/10 even if it had more content, wasn't as rushed story-wise, and just overall was more chill. Right now it feels like it kind of misses the mark with both trying to be very chill but also Important Life Choices. But that might be just me.Either way, I don't regret buying it, but I would heavily recommend buying it on sale, it's not worth 20$ in its current state. It is however worth experiencing, in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Upon the game start, the first thing I've noticed was that the postal truck's wheels were not rotating. And that had set up the mood for the whole playthrough, to be frank.The initial idea is okay, but the gameplay is downright boring. I see what the devs tried to do there — immerse us in country life, allow us to relax while observing nice landscapes and whatnot. What really bugged me, was an obvious lack of attention to detail. Some voice actors doing their job okay, and some are slacking off near the mic. The inability to skip those poorly voiced lines is a bother. Some questlines are narrated properly, and in some, events just happen with no proper foundation or motivation. The playlist is very short, and most of the songs started to annoy me after the first half of the game. What hit the most, was the unclear writing when choosing the ending. That lead to me picking the one I didn't actually want, so I feel I have the reason to point it out. And where the hell is my blueberry pie ffs.

_childDocuments_.review: Saw this game listed in an article maybe a week before it's release. Added it to my wishlist and picked it up without knowing really anything about it, so I guess you could call it an impulse purchase, 22$ seems slightly high for the amount of content here, but i don't regret it. It had a lovely story, great graphics, likeable characters (with the exception of a few, lookin' at you Steve). Lots of people seem to complain about how slow the movement speed is, and I was a bit worried when the game first started, but as it went on I found it really fit the vibe of it. I played for about 6 hours straight, and it felt like 2. Loved every second of it, and in a few weeks time, I'll probably give it another go. I'd recommended it wholeheartedly, though maybe it'd be best to wait for a little bit of a sale if you're on the fence.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like sorting things out and simply enjoying the ambiance of a game you'll really like this. There's no points to accumulate or anything, it's just satisfying. The story is nothing too crazy, but it's well written and the voice acting is on point. My four year old kid really liked having my headset on while we drover around the city, created some irl memory in the process so thanks for the beautiful game. Tips and hints:- I did a "yes to everything" and a "no to everything" run. It was fun to compare how the game progressed both ways.- If you want acheivements, be a little curious...- There are way points on the map to fast travel... I discoverd this in my couple last minutes of gameplay and kinda gratefull I did not noticed before, I enjoy the relaxing travels on the road. But hey, you might prefer speeding things up a bit.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: The writing is just about as lazy as it can get. We're in 1986 Oregon. Is that a place where teenagers say "tight" (slang from the late 90s/early 2000s) and "wicked" (central to Massachusetts)? Every song on the radio sounds like a detergent ad from 2007. Don't get me wrong, I LOVE a good walking simulator with a strong story. But every character interaction in this game is so bereft of anything compelling that I had to put it away. Every piece of dialog is "I'm either committing to this place, or to my product marketing job I've spent 5 minutes max understanding" There's no build-up, there's no moments of emotional surprise. The game is billed as "do whatever you want to do", but your options are to either do the stories or don't... and considering how absolutely tedious every one of these characters are, I decided to take option 3... uninstalling.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: I expected Lake to be a pretty deep and solid story but it's not as deep as I'd hope. The main bulk of the game is to drive around delivering mail and packages around town. While doing that you meet various characters. Depending on the choices you make with them, additional moments and story elements unfold.While the story isn't as thrilling as I'd hoped, Lake is definitely a fun experience and the town is so calm and scenic that it almost feels like a zen-like experience. Sometimes the game can pick up a bit more pace though.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: A very pleasant, relaxing and positive game with a nostalgic mood.The main characters are likable and it’s a pleasure to spend time with them. The gameplay is simple and even a little boring in places, but the situation is saved by the atmosphere and dialogues.The game is like a combination of "Lego Island 2" :D And "Know by heart...", but if the story is told from the perspective of the returning women and not the remaining small town boy. I recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: Lake

_childDocuments_.review: It's 1986 - Meredith Weiss takes a break from her career in the big city to deliver mail in her hometown. How will she experience two weeks in beautiful Providence Oaks, with its iconic lake and quirky community? And what will she do next? It's up to you.

name: Help Will Come Tomorrow
detailed_description: COMING SOON! CHECK OUT OUR OTHER GAMES! AND MORE GAMES! About the Game In an uninhabitable Siberian wilderness, in a wake of the October Revolution, a group of passengers survives the mysterious catastrophe of Trans-Siberian railway train. They must endure in a harsh ice-clad climate until rescue arrives. Facing many dangers, their own weaknesses and, above all, their own prejudice. People from different social classes have to unite and make decisions that often go against their beliefs, either by putting them to the test or by completely breaking them. Will they survive and at what cost is only up to the player. The basic mechanics of the game will focus on the survival of the characters (meeting their needs, gathering resources, expanding the camp, taking care of security, exploring surroundings), but the player will quickly find out that in order to win, he needs much more: to learn the personality of the characters and work out relations between them, mitigating conflicts and taking care of the morale. You may choose to act selfish but it is cooperation that will allow you to win and keep a clear conscience. In Help Will Come Tomorrow you will: • Overcome class animosities between your party members in order to survive in an innovative class relations building system. • Manage scarce resources and stay alive in frosty wilderness of Siberia before help arrives. • Guide 9 unique characters coming from different social origins and grouping in three society classes • Discover intimate stories and past of all party members • Build and expand your own camp to increase the chances of survival • Face dynamically changing weather conditions and unforgiving Siberian wildlife affecting survivors life. • Experience in-game Event system based on characters relations and morale • Immerse yourself in a touching story set in 1917 pre-Bolshevik Imperial Russia

_childDocuments_.review: It is troubling to me that at time of writing the review rated as most helpful includes egregious hyperbole at best and flagrant lies at worst. I want to shed some light on the quality of the game by provide a summary of genuine praises, fair criticisms and unfair criticisms.I STRONGLY encourage anyone just starting out with this game to use the passenger difficulty. Passenger difficulty is lethal enough for just starting out, and you should try to get a good end on the easiest difficulty before even attempting a game on a harder difficulty. At time of writing, only 30% of players have actually gotten to a happy ending, and I know I only was able to because I stumbled upon an exploit.The opening sequence is absolutely beautiful, and introduces you to each of the characters without a single one having to say a word. Insight into each character can come about from this opening sequence, and a lot of care has been put into each panel. The game then opens with gun shots happening in the background as the camera focuses upon a band of four people in various degrees of damage that just managed to escape certain death at the hands of the butchers on the tracks. The terrified survivors lament their fates as a sorrowful woman’s voice accompanied by a somber violin sets the tone. You will be hearing a lot of that singer, and she may be the hidden star of the game.This game has some absolutely amazing character development that is served through multiple different systems that I will list in order of ascending depth. First, while the characters sit around the camp fire, they will say snippets of dialogue. Different characters have different snippets that reveal part of their background (for example, there is a serving girl that is looking for her brother that was lost in the crash. She calls out his name, lamenting that she cannot find him.). Second, each character has a preselected list of traits that may be revealed throughout the game. Playing the game and interacting with different items and actions unlocks the trait. In a beautiful design decision, traits can be either positive or negative, and impact the way mechanics work in intuitive ways (For example, someone with the cook trait has a chance of regaining an action point while cooking). Some traits are exceptionally bad, and the traits you are exposed to is tethered to your difficulty.Third, campfire dialogue. Every night phase you are given a series of topics to choose from to discuss. Talking through these options opens up interesting discussion points and strengthens the bond of your survivors. Usually you can get characters to open up to reveal more about themselves by reading them and having the people they are talking to respond politely to them. Not only do the conversations themselves add depth to characters, but they also allow for the next and even more detailed form of characterization in the game, side quests.Fourth, individual characters have different side quests that impact the camp, survivors, and the items you obtain. For example, there is a British adventurer that left behind his rifle on the train. If it comes up in conversation and the other people are receptive to it, a quest to find his gun appears. Similar quests exist for other characters, including finding lost siblings and other events.Fifth, unique character events. Each character has a collection of unique events that can be either randomly triggered in the morning, or triggered after dialogue during the night. Be warned, not all of these unique events are exactly positive and happy things, characterization can be both positive and negative. However, the characterization is nice, and really adds to the depth of each character.I’m looking at you, Target Practice Event. In the target practice event, your survivors get shot to pieces upon encountering a band of ruffians. In the event they do not even put up a fight. This seems tone deaf to the composition of the party, because soldier characters with rifles and pistols get gunned down without a fight. Events that do not fully take into account the situation at hand are part of the reason that the event avoiding exploit mentioned at the end of the review is worth knowing about. This event does not break the game, however, because it can only be triggered by deliberately moving into a renegade occupied tile.This is probably my biggest gripe with the game. You can only save one game at a time. If you start a new game it overwrites the previous save. I don’t see why any game needs such a limitation. I personally really like to have old saves to go back to of past attempts, especially after I’ve already beaten the game on one save. Even just three or four save slots would nip this criticism right in the bud.The tutorial does an excellent job of introducing the fundamental mechanics, but there are a lot of nuanced and complex interaction that do not get explained. A lot of the learning in this game is on the fly via trial and error. On one level, that is part of the fun, but if you don’t enjoy learning a game that way this game is probably not for you.-This is a lie. Winning the game is a drawn out affair that takes ~25 days of in game time. The earliest you are winning this game is maybe 5 hours in, and that is after having failed your way to success in multiple previous play throughs. If you count having your entire party of survivors die off as “completing the game” then you can get through one playthrough in 1-2 hours. This criticism is about as valid as saying Super Mario Bros should not be played because you can “complete” the game in the first 20 seconds by jumping into a pit.-This criticism is tone deaf to the setting. We are talking about a band of injured wrecked passengers of a train stranded in the middle of the tundra. The 40 tile range provided is the range they can safely navigate to from camp and hope to return to camp safely. -I am astounded someone that played 20+ hours of the game can make this criticism. There is AMPLE character development. Each character starts out as a mystery, and through systems I talked about elsewhere is fleshed out.-The game developers chose to create their game in medias res, which is a valid way of telling a story. The game does not provide extensive background because that would detract from the main focal point of the plot, the gradual development of each of the individual characters thrust into a survival quest not of their choosing. -This is not only not a problem if it were true, but is not true. In this game you are hiding from the band of heavily armed renegades that attacked your train mostly unarmed passenger train. When a bandit moves within one tile of your camp, there is a risk of them finding the camp and the game ending. To counterbalance this you need to keep the fire low and eventually camouflage your campsite. Too much visibility opens up different renegade events. -Something to note is that while the game’s event system can be exceedingly brutal, there is an exploit that renders the event system trivial to cope with. This is because, . If the RNG screws you over, you can quit out of the game and start the entire day over.

_childDocuments_.review: There really isn't much here, despite other reviews. There is very little feedback as to certain mechanics. For example, camp morale was completely empty due to a couple decisions I made at the beginning of a run, and at the end it was completely full, and I saw no difference mechanically. Same for trust, friendship, etc. They're just bars that have a chance to give you a benefit if they're full enough, but other than that seem to do little. If they do have an impact, it's so poorly communicated I wasn't able to tell the difference.There is almost no animation. Even moving characters to a task keeps them in the same position, just shifting them wherever you want. Just feels lazy that they don't even stand up. The UI is also not very intuitive. You end up having to click across the item bar to get to the items you want, and you'll have to do this multiple times to feed, drink, bandage, etc. Often times event dialogue will reference characters by name, and unless you've done a good job committing faces to names, you have no indication of who you're sending to do what.The dialogue is very poorly translated. It's a struggle to understand what the characters are trying to convey sometimes. Near the end of a playthrough one character mentions a child and another character says "COULD IT BE, X???" and up until this point I had no indication of who X was or their relation to any of the characters. Much of the character dialogue is like this, it has a strange tone to it that makes it sound...very much like written characters and less like actual people.There is also very little choice, which unfortunately is somewhat typical of games in this genre. A lot of the time your events are "Choose between A and B". One is good and the other is bad. That's it. I saw maybe 2 other choices that had more options. So, overall between everything I just found the game underwhelming, especially finishing a playthrough and a half in just short of 4 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I liked this game more than I did, the story and aesthetics were really nice, but the mechanics get really old after a while.First, very few item descriptions and every ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ condition has it's own means of curing it that you won't figure out without wasting resources and/or restarting the game. Party getting frostbite, and you try to have them rest in a double shelter with blankets? No, you loser! you need that one specific infirmary upgrade to make warm crompresses to cure the frostbite. You'll probably figure it out after your playthrough collapses. After 6 hours I still don't know how to get characters body temperature up. Rest, campfire and warm clothes sure as hell don't seem to do it.Also, it's one of those colony if idiots games, where in a harsh, hostile environment random characters will just wander alone into the wilderness on day 3 because they don't like the fellow survivor they were 'forced' to build a campfire with.This feels like a traditional Russian game made by software engineers instead of designers, just pile on mechanics, and make the game as hostile and convoluted as possible. The actual gameplay is in figuring the game itself out instead of playing the game.

_childDocuments_.review: is a roguelite resource manager that has a lot of flaws, but somehow engufed me so much I'm currently storming the hardest difficulty—a thing I rarely do in games. As a group of survivors in ~1917 Russia you must navigate your way through multiple stats, negative statuses, and ideological differences, while unlocking events, character backstories and traits that help or harm your situation.The biggest flaws of this game are RNG and negative feedback loops. A single unfortunate event or wrong choice can end your run—or harm it so much it might as well have ended it. While the former is frustrating but typical for roguelites, the latter is exacerbated by the second flaw. See, the systems of this game are interlocked in such a way that losing only makes you lose more: the more negative statuses characters have, the less actions they get, and less actions mean less chances to fix your situation. When a negative condition becomes too strong, a character can downright faint and rob you of any chance to use them... Once again, each of these traits would be fine on its own, but together they create a system that makes it pointless to try and salvage a run if, say, two characters are gone or someone fumbles a crucial action early on.The dialogue is very cool thematically, but functional rather than well-written. The music and visuals are great.Ans yet, despite the flaws,  drew me in. Perhaps the number of items and systems is  so as not to be overwhelming. Perhaps the theme is doing it for me. Perhaps the characters—vivid and well-executed stereotypes—are smart enough with their ideological talks and dark secrets that I'm curious to learn more.I think this game will benefit greatly from additional patching and balancing—patch 1.0.1 already added the much-needed Mushroom Soup and explained some mechanics better. Good luck to the developer in perfecting their game; I'll keep an eye on it (and try to make a Hard run).P.S. Don't be mistaken in thinking this is a clever narrative-driven game. While the bits of narrative it has are interwoven well into the gameplay and the characters are vivid, it's a resource manager first and foremost, not biting commentary on the Russian Revolution.

_childDocuments_.review: Five years ago I played Dead In Bermuda and it was awesome. Since then I can recall about at least 10 more or less similar games, and Help Will Come Tomorrow is one of them.We play as a group of passengers who survived the mysterious catastrophe of Trans-Siberian railway train. Surviving in Siberian wilderness is tough even on easiest difficulty, especially in first few days before you establish your camp.At the same time, if you successfully survived first week, all further adventures are very likely to be easy for you.There's 3 really strong positive things in this game that make it shine:+ Very nice visuals and music+ Good character stories and interesting dialogues between them. These dialogues are well-written and very suitable for that period of time and those characters. A great work here indeed.+ It's good enough for multiple playthroughs, mostly because of different characters and their interactions. A variety of in-game events is not that impressive on the other side.On the other hand there's a few weak (but less important overall) points:- Gameplay/difficulty balance is not really good and has a common for such games "snowball" effect.- Some mechanics are very unclear. I can't understand how some events work even after several playthroughs where I actually tried to figure out how exactly they work.- A bunch of minor bugs that are mostly related to achievements/endings (i.e. I completed game with all characters alive, but didn't receive that achievement). Also, characters exhaustion works weird sometimes.All in all, Help Will Come Tomorrow is a very enjoyable experience with decent replayability. I wish there were more events though. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a misunderstanding. It plays like a visual novel without the actual novel. Some bits of story are interesting and well written, but there's not enough of it to be meaningful. There's no strategy involved, you simply respond to whatever RNG throws at you. There aren't any real choices to make either - you simply choose the thing that lets you continue the game, because the other thing is very obviously bad. "Bad" choices are just that - there aren't any rewards for picking risky options. Overall, it's a little too boring and not enough substance for me to enjoy this game, even though I've tried.

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting concept, but god knows, this game is flawed in so many ways.First of all, game designers didn't know where to stop, adding too many mechanics. The tutorial is overwhelming. But even if you figure everything out, some of them doesn't have much sense, narrative- or gameplay-wise.First of all, the thing with relationship between the survivors. Most of the dialogues are just don't make sense at all and totally unpredictable. Also, I don't think it matters if you a communist or a monarchist when you are freezing in the middle of Siberian taiga. I used to live north from the Arctic Circle, I know. Even in Moscow, when there's wind and frost, and you are wearing decent warm clothes, you are not going to waste your time if you are cold. And these spoiled characters are not fond of working together because they don't know each other too well or do not like one another. That's preposterous! At the same time, it doesn't look like the camp morale is actually affects something.Second, when you are making a makeshift thing, the other survivors hate you. I guess, they believe it is better to freeze to death than to make a temporary shelter when you don't have enough materials. And that's lead us to another game design flaw.You can't use different kinds of the same material to build. Let's say, you need to build a simple cover. For that, you need 8+8 wood, 12 needles and 3 structure. Sticks, branches, split wood, needles and logs provide wood. But you can't mix them. Thus, if you have 7 wood total for each of the material, you won't be able to build the cover. It is even worse with cooking. You have four mushrooms to make a soup but these mushrooms of the same type are split to 2+2 stacks because they have different expiration date and you can't cook them. The funny thing, if you exit the menu for cooking and try that again, they can be available as a stack of 4 mushrooms and this time you can use them.Another thing to mention is random, and for a strategy game it's a very big flaw. You can't make plans because everything is unpredictable. For example, you need a coal to make an upgraded water filter which is the key to survival. You can find a coal near the train, and it make sense. And usually it's there. But sometimes you can search every cell with the train (and it's 7 cells!), and there's nothing. You are screwed. You have wasted 6 out of 12 points (if you are lucky) almost for nothing. The same goes for the rest of resources. And it doesn't matter what difficulty level you are on. Even the passenger level will drive you up the wall.Upgrades of the camp are also stupid. You can make a Fence and upgrade it to get Snares and Marked Path. Snares will provide small animals you can cook. Marked Path unlocks an option of gathering brushwood. The problem is, snares can be empty for days. Even if you upgrade them for Advanced Traps to increase the chance. I needed meat to make a bear trap, and I couldn't get it for a week or so. As for Marked Path, usually you need sticks to build something useful, but characters will be bringing moss, cones, bark and other useless sh★t. Do not forget, every action uses at least 1 point out of 12.Another thing with the points. The balance is awful. You can have up to 3 points for each character. If your characters are thirsty, hungry, freezing, injured or tired, their action points will decrease, and that's a big problem. For example, to build something solo a character should use all his points, 3 out of 3. And some of them has a Lone Wolf Trait. Thus, you can build something for 3 points to get the bonus morale from the trait or spent two points total and lose a lot of morale if you are building with someone. On the top of that, some characters can have Incompetent trait, and they could fail any action, losing points for nothing.Of course, you can use characters who are getting along pretty well with each other but that's rare. Though you can improve their relationship using Fraternization at the camp. The problem is, this action requires 2 points total. Do you think you are going to waste valuable points to make friends when you are in need of resources? Also, some characters can have traits like Distrustful, Braggart or Humbug, and it is almost impossible to be friends with them, especially if there are two characters like that in your camp.The art of the game is decent but cinematics are just plain awful. That's not a big deal at all but it feels like devs didn't care at all about these things. That's an amateur level at the very best.The last but not least. I don't know about the other languages but Russian localization is horrid. For example, your character is bleeding, and the game says to dress the wound. You do that, and nothing happens. You switch to English to learn that you actually need to make a bandage to fix that, and these are two different actions, though I don't believe there's a lot of difference.To sum it up, this game feels strange but okay the first two runs. But every other try you will get irritated due to the random or the balance.
