_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw this game, I was super excited. I expected it to be largely similar to This War of Mine and Day R Survival. It looked like it had an incredible amount of potential, and the basis of the plot, a group of strangers thrown into a survival situation is the pinnacle of survival concepts in my opinion, provided you are able to have a complex story line and character development, with social and moral choices having a major impact on the characters. Help Will Come Tomorrow failed in this aspect, and honestly, you can completely play through this game in about 1-2 hours max. Overall, this game was thrown together hastily, and that is apparent in the lack of quality. This game was a disappointment, it had a great concept, and if Arclight put more time and effort into it, I feel they could have made something incredible, instead, we get a cheap game with a short plot and a base level story line. The first place they fall short is with the general story line. They give no intro to the story, besides a brief clip showing the characters on a train, and it getting blown up. It gives no beginning detail about the October Revolution, the social divisions, and the wars going on in the period. Most survival games, Such as This War of Mine, Distrust,  Day R Survival, the entire Fallout Franchise, and many others, all include a way to give base information, either in the game itself, in the form of an intro movie, or a note with enough information to get a decent understanding, as you progress in the gameplay, through a series of notes or cutscenes meant to give a prologue. The only way to truly understand what is happening in the game is to do outside research on the October Revolution, and what happened. The night discussions give info about individual characters parts in the story, but they completely skip over the part of what the story is. The closest thing I could compare it to is handing someone a spine of a book with the title, and 20 random pages of the book, then expecting them to understand the story. Second, there is the complete lack of character development. The only development we can really see is the change in the Trust, Friendship, and Credit stats, which are pointless mechanics of the game, as the only thing they affect is Morale when you pair up survivors to do tasks together, which only is used for Morale Checks at night if your character has many negative effects. They could have done so much more with this. In This War of Mine, the effects that can happen have major effects. If you kill civilians, your survivors become depressed, and the survivor who did the killing is largely ostracized by the rest of the survivors, with messages shaming and questioning their decisions. This can also lead to infighting, and inability to work. Arclight games just fell short in this concept, and gave a little mechanic to make the game look more appealing and complex, when in reality, the entire character development is almost nonexistent. Also, there is the matter of Traits. No matter what you do with your survivors, there is a very small chance of discovering all of your traits for your characters. I wanted to test this, so I chose the Shatun mode, which has the opportunity to draw out gameplay, and I used this to search for traits. First, I made all characters do Fraternization with each other to find common traits. Then, I took turns having each character do each task, until each survivor had done cooking, building, exploring, hunting, medicine, crafting, etc, and each character had 2 or more traits still undiscovered. I am unsure if it is even possible to discover all traits for a survivor.Third, there is the aspect of detail, and depth to the game. Overall, the game is largely limited. The first place this is seen is in the map size. The entire map is made of about 40 grid spaces, many of which are death traps, where if you enter them, you die from one thing or another. That is miniscule. For a game about survival, there should be a lot more available area for exploration. There are in the middle of the Siberian Wilderness. This wilderness makes up 75% of Russia’s landmass, and encompasses over 13,000,000 Square kilometers. I’m 110% sure they can travel more than 5 grids in any direction without finding civilization and escaping, because if not, why is this a survival game in the first place. In This War of Mine, for exploration, you are able to choose from up to 40 locations to search i think, and each one has a building or multiple building you can search, where each building has dozens of searchable objects with materials. In Day Z, each house has items all over. There needs to be a bigger map, with more in depth searching. Also, character interactions are very limited, and have almost nothing to do with the individual character. When you go hunting, and find a deer, somehow, a military officer with a rifle is unable to shoot a deer, and instead hits a tree. How is a military trained soldier unable to shoot a massive animal? Also, with the Shatun Bear, it’s basically just unable to explore once it starts hunting, because if you encounter it, you have no options, you just die. Finally, we go to NPC enemy interactions, the Renegades. 90% of renegade encounters is just death. Your survivors walk onto their space, and almost every option results in your team dying. This needs to be reworked, because currently, the only way to win is to just sit around and try to avoid the renegades, even if you have multiple soldiers on your exploration team, you can’t do anything. I’d recommend a combat system similar to Forge of Empires, or Day R Survival, where you have a grid setup with obstacles and cover, and proceed in turn based combat, that way actually strategy and gameplay is required, compared to: walking, encounter renegades: Target Practice: your entire team is dead.Overall, I would not recommend Help Will Come Tomorrow, at least not until some major changes and updates are made by Arclight. This game is a very short and low depth experience, and has a lot to be improved upon.

_childDocuments_.review: Game has been out since 2020, isn't getting updates anymore. Still has some bugs. Various portions of activities are ridiculous, for which I'll give an example. You're going to make a delicious roast, requires 4 meat. You have 3 brand new fresh meat, and one meat that's a day old. You can't make it, because all 4 meat aren't at the same stage of freshness. If they were all a day old, or all fresh, you could make the stew. Super frustrating. You can't mix and match materials to build things. You need, let's say, 9 structure components to build a thing. You have component A at 5 structure each, or component B at 4 structure each. You can't use one of each, you must use either 2 A or 3 B. Why is this like this, other than to be annoying?The game could be good. It reminds me of another I've played that is similar and I enjoyed and replayed quite a bit. But the constant stream of irritating minor issues makes it more of an exercise in frustration than a fun and enjoyable challenge. It's close to the 51% mark, but not quite. For me, I'd say 40-45%. Could be good, but it is so annoying on a regular basis.

Day after day of nothing happening - eventually looked it up... sigh. Turns out there is a big, fat ugly bug -- known to the devs -- that glitches the  story event. Like, the very last scripted event before the ending screen. Apparently this game has logging issues - see thread , including dev's suggestion to edit save files to fix it - but not work for me. IDK man, I don't usually get into bugs on my reviews, but this one is ludicrous, and seems like something that should not make it past basic QA. So that's 18 hours down the drain. _childDocuments_.review: When you're born Polish, life will funnel you into one of two paths: of hatred or of despair. Sensitive, artsy people tend to fall into the latter, and that's probably we have so many Polish depression simulators. Frostpunk, This War of Mine, and now this. In a nutshell - this game is Dead in Vinland infused with the essence of Frostpunk and This War of Mine. But it's also much more than that.The atmosphere, the music, the conversation topics, they're all very much in sync and varied enough to keep things interesting. Due to the way the game is designed you -must- have at least one revolutionary (aka communist) and at least one aristocratic (aka conservative old wealth) group member. The theme of the game is overcoming the tensions between the classes to survive, and eventually thrive. It's nothing mind blowing, but it's engaging from start to finish.As for the gameplay - if you're expecting a rehash of Dead in Vinland, this is not it. There is no combat, there are no skills; instead there are perks and action points. The expedition system is also interesting - weighing how much and what loot to bring versus the danger of getting lost in the taiga. The relationships between characters are also quite important, and managing people's happiness and friendship is vital.The survival aspect is pretty great. You have to manage hunger, thirst, fatigue and cold - classics - but also different injuries and illnesses, as well as indigestion or nausea (that's what you get for eating those weird mushrooms and bugs). That way the game pushes you to not rely on the barely edible moss, but actually hunt, fish and cook - and maybe even use herbs to season your dishes to increase morale. I wish more games had this kind of mechanic. (The Long Dark, are you listening? Let me rub greens into that venison!)It's an engaging ride from start to finish. After understanding the mechanics and learning the strengths and weaknesses of my survivors, I had no problem with survival whatsoever (playing on normal difficulty). I'll probably play some more with different endgame scenario and different survivor combination, but for now I'm very satisfied. Check it out! Great time.

_childDocuments_.review: Help Will Come Tomorrow is a roguelike, resource management, survival game.If you want to see a review, the gameplay contents of the game in a short video, then check my video instead of reading this review:The time is 1917, October. Location: Russia. Not the safest place on the Globe. The Great October Socialist Revolution is about to change the tsardom.Chaos is always a friend of criminals. A group of thugs decides to massacre all passengers of the Trans-Siberian railway train while communizing all their possessions. There are a total of 9 different characters in the game. Of these, 4 are randomly selected and available to us at the start. The setup of your survivor squad is different every single time. Each individual has a different social background. Each survivor has its own unique story and randomized traits.The help is coming. Hopefully. Can you survive long enough? Or tomorrow will be the day you give up? Help or Death will come tomorrow? Your actions will decide.The gameplay is resource-management oriented. Collect materials, foods. Craft winter clothes, weapons, build buildings, shelters, and try to survive until some kind of help arrives. Brigands patrolling the area so they can massacre survivors, witnesses, and cut any loose ends. They are not the only enemy, the harsh climate of Siberia, the wilderness, and predators are all against your survival odds.The game is very interesting. Harder difficulty levels offer a hardcore resource management experience. Always hard to decide the real value of a game, as you can get quite decent and long games for the price of this. Because of that, it feels so, that it is perhaps a bit overpriced. You probably not going to finish a whole run in your first playthrough. Completing the game once might take 8-10hours. Art is nice, the game is challenging, so my final conclusion is, that I would recommend the game.Perfection time: 10-20 hours. You can see my perfection time on this review, as it is my played time, ~26 hours. However, i needed to discover and explore all secrets. You don't need to do that anymore, if you don't want. _childDocuments_.review: Help Will Come Tomorrow is the latest in the rather niche strategy-survival genre that reminds me the most of Dead in Bermuda and Dead in Vinland. Its setting is a fresh take and brings along a number of new mechanics that differentiate it from its predecessors while still feeling familiar enough that fans of those will pick it up quickly. I struggled with the overall challenge of surviving Siberia, which is exactly what I was hoping for, but there are difficulty options that you can change to tailor the experience to your liking.Help Will Come Tomorrow begins with your train going off of the rails in the wilds of Siberia under particularly unforgiving circumstances. Civilization is too far for a quick hike to be possible, the temperatures are low enough to be lethal with extended exposure, and the outlaws that derailed the train are still roaming the area. As a matter of fact, they’re so active on the first day that you’ll be hearing their gunfire throughout the day as the other passengers are being gunned down. Your party of four will have to work together to clear enough snow from the small area they are hiding out in to set up a campsite. A fire to keep warm, filter water, and cook food is a must and is needed quickly, though you’ll want to construct as many structures as possible to survive the challenges ahead. A shelter will keep the survivors rested and warm, Palisades will protect the camp from outside threats (human and otherwise), a quarantine post provides sorely needed medical care, and a workshop developed the tools of survival that make many tasks more efficient and less taxing on the survivors. It’s important to note that each of these structures has a number of other actions that can be taken outside of their primary functions, such as being able to fraternize at the campfire to build relationships among party members, and progressing down their development trees will drastically improve your chances to make it out of this experience in one piece.Setting up a functioning camp isn’t the only requirement for survival as you’ll need to put together frequent expeditions to gather the supplies needed to expand its functions and sustain your party. These are where the vast majority of your resources come from, though they carry with them dangers of their own. Getting lost is a very real possibility if you push survivors too far beyond their limits in the wilds, as is getting injured, or simply shot outright by the outlaws.The party of four is randomly selected from the pool of surviving characters at the start of a new game. Each has around half a dozen traits that define their capabilities, what pleases or displeases them, and their general beliefs. These beliefs and personality traits combine with their overall ideology (aristocracy, revolutionary, and neutral) to determine how well they get along with the others by default. Spoiler: it takes quite a bit of work to get the aristocratic army captain to get along with the revolutionary socialist leader. Health, morale, and statuses are more gameplay-oriented features than the narrative traits, but if you let any of them get out of control, you’re likely to lose a companion in one way or another.The characters are easily my favorite part of Help Will Come Tomorrow and they’re written well, though they often share lines when discussions are taking place. You wouldn’t notice this unless you played through multiple times, though this title certainly stands out as one that needs plenty of replay value to stand out as a great experience. I would’ve liked to see unique lines for every member of the party for each scenario that unfolds, not just a ‘primary’ character in the scene who says their unique lines followed by other characters churning out backup lines instead of representing themselves more accurately. I’d also like to see a significantly larger pool of candidates that are drawn from at the start as it currently seems that each playthrough is more defined by the characters that you don’t have than the ones that you do.Help Will Come Tomorrow is a strong showing in the narrative survival-strategy genre that brings some interesting new ideas to the table. I found it to be particularly challenging, which is a huge plus for me, and if there were a few more characters added, along with unique dialogue, I’d be fully satisfied with what’s on offer here thanks to the increased replay value and depth. If you are into the genre, you can’t go wrong with this title; if you’re not, this one is unlikely to convert you. If you end up deciding to get on the train, though, good luck, you’ll need it!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a survival game where you have to gather and manage your resources and build your camp. There are random events and also resources available on the map I think are placed randomly so it gives you some rogue-like feel. Also there are 9 possible characters and each of them can have random skills but I also think some of them have more chance to have skills from certain groups that are connected with their backgrounds. You start the game with 4 characters and you can later rescue or find one more so in order to learn everything about each character you need to play the game at least 2-3 times. And that is good because there are also 3 possible storylines to choose from and they change some random encounters and the weather you will face and your end game goal.I liked that characters belong to different social backgrounds and at the start have their superstitions towards other backgrounds. Some people are nobility and support Tsar and how the things are now while others are revolutionists that want to change the world they live in and there are also people in the middle that don’t strongly support either of the sides. Because of this the more time people spend speaking with each other around the campfire during the day the more they start to like each other and understand others and they also have things they can speak about with others during the night and your choices during that night meetings will change how they feel about others or even trigger some new random events to check on the map. You can check each character friendship and trust towards all other characters and influence it with your actions to make them all work better with each other.The graphic and presentation of the game are nice. I liked how everything looked and even gory things like wounds on characters or having a necrotic hand or losing a foot are presented well. The world presented feels real and each building you can build in your camp and all the loot you can find looks like they belong to the world presented in the game. Also the description combined with graphic makes the random events feel real and important and makes you think what would you do if you were there.I hated that some events have no choices and just makes your people die no mater how many weapons and ammo you have and how good your clothes are. It was also strange that at the end game the same random event was in 6 different places on the map each time resulting in the same description and my people getting killed.The expedition system is strange as it is unclear many times how much action points will your move or search action take and if you will be able to get back to the camp or will your characters get lost in the woods. Simple moving from one area to other area or searching for loot actions take 0-2 action points and you are never 100% sure how much the action will take and random events can also take away some of your action points so you can’t really plan out your moves.The train crashed! Now try to survive in Siberia long enough to be rescued!Rating: 6.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game takes place in Siberian Russia. Domestic terrorists use explosives to derail a train, then attempt to kill any survivors regardless of class or political standing. The gameplay focuses on surviving the harsh environment, wolf/bear attacks, and being found by the renegades. There are three character types based on Russian politics during the early 1917: aristocracy, revolutionary, and neutral. Some characters literally have a "socialist" trait and thus strongly oppose Czar Nikolai II of the Romanovs. There are also several references to the Bolsheviks, though, oddly, Vladimir Lenin is not mentioned. Each character also has a secret, but will only reveal it if their trust in their comrades (fellow survivors) is high enough. Having the characters work together to survive builds up trust, friendship, and credit. The challenge is that there must be an aristocrat and revolutionary in the group, so they don't always get along. ::I recommend it to anyone who enjoys strategy survival games or historical fiction ... or both!

_childDocuments_.review: I've spent a multitude of hours on similar survival and resource management games such as Dead in Vinland and Dead in Bermuda, and this one definitely scratches the same itch. Very challenging, even on normal mode, as you will get an excellent idea of how harsh it is to survive in the Siberian wilderness after surviving a horrific train crash. I've finished one playthrough after several tries, and I'm attempting to get through even one week on difficult mode. If you're not too familiar with this type of game, I would suggest you start on easy. Some salient points:- Fairly replayable, as there are multiple character interactions and random field events- Lovely artwork, clean overall menu layout, but limited poses and animations for the characters- Interesting historical backdrop involving Russian politics during the October Revolution- Diverse cast of personalities, each with the potential to develop helpful or harmful traits, and balanced enough that you can't strongly prefer one or the other.- Dynamic relationship system that involves three parameters: trust, friendship and credit- Brutal and unforgiving events can throw a wrench into your struggling camp (e.g. terrible weather, forced amputations, poisoning)- Antagonists are represented by roaming renegades that need to be eluded- Exploration is always a gamble, due to weather, renegade patrols, dwindling resources and the increasing risk of getting lost.- Gameplay mechanics can be confusing, and you need several playthroughs to figure out how things work.Having fun so far, I'd say it's great value if you appreciate these types of games.

_childDocuments_.review: Fortunately I bought this game in a bundle with "Dead in Vinland" which I would recommend instead.Generally I love the despair-management games, since they challenge Player's intellect and resolve. Not this one.First let's get the good parts outta way to begin with:1. Any cultural and/or historical lore in games is good and welcome;2. Attention to details always pays off. Character condition and clothing are visualized.3. Trait discovery feature is authentic. Standing applause here.4. Procedure-generated starting conditions are cool. Totally unbalanced, unfortunately. Restart-repeat.Done. That's it.Graphics is tolerable, though widescreen support is minimal. Everything's just ugly-stretched.Music is irrelevant, adding negligible immersion. Seems like a persisting placeholder everyone forgot about.Now the bad parts, right?1. Probability — is a joke here. Descriptions provide zero clues to the Player."Has a chance..." means what?1% ?99% ?50/50 ?Whatever.When a good thing procs — the benefits are irrelevant.When a bad thing procs —  it's always a disaster. Yep.Danger level "insignificant" is what now?1% ?17% ?50/50. Yep.Danger level "deadly" is what now?75% ?99% ?50/50. Yep.You can *easily* survive the deadly encounter, and get rekt by an insignificant one.Yep.There's no actual risk-management in this game. "Dead in Vinland" gives you a probability fork at least, so that you can project assumptions. "HWCT" is a blind gamble.Yep.2. Interface is clunky. As an example: you WILL have to go a couple of menu's back to add fuel before cooking. ALWAYS.It's unlearnable. Yep.3. Resources can NOT be combined. You simply can't make a mushroom soup outta mushrooms of different freshness.Deal with it. Yep.4. The tutorial is utterly disgusting. It introduces confusion instead of clarity.Skip it outright to save your braincells.Frankly I don't believe that any game developers understood it yet. Lemme spell it:Never. Steal. My. Focus. Or. Controls. EVER!Tutorial is no excuse to do that either, ye dorks!Why-oh-why it's so hard to understand that it breaks the immersion, eh?Don't you ever play the games you create? Or is it a professional deformation?Phew.5. Game ends when it finally starts to make sense. Needless to say, prematurely.Leaving no desire for replay, despite all the variability.Yep.--Still, it's not a bad game. I just don't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing this game with the latest patches as of 8/18/2020 and I can safely say this is a rather sadistic game. With some more resources available this game could be categorized as Extremely Hard, but I have retried several times and it is easy to see that with the current starting conditions, wounds, etc. there is no winning path. It is not like you run out of luck in game, it is rather you kind of lose at the beginning already and then your only job is to make the gameplay longer until you uninstall it.Also, the artificially added animations and dialog delays everywhere just make you suffer more. I spent 10 hours in 7 games, probably this 10 hour could have been reduced to 2.5 hours.If you know Don't Starve or This War of Mine, this game beats them with its level of hopelessness and insane sadistic randomization.I bought this game for 5 EURs, probably a waste of money, unfortunately I did not buy directly through Steam otherwise I would request a refund. It is sad, because this game has potential, but potential only is not enough these days.A good game should be WINNABLE and this ONLY should depend on the skills of the player. Good example: Frostpunk, which is a rather hard game, and also takes long to play, but with a lot of suffering I won it the first time I played. (And I lost several times later, but each time I was able to track back where I made the bad decision. I did not blame the randomization of resources, each decision of mine affected the unfortunate outcome.)I give thumbs down, but with a sad feeling because I rarely see a potentially good game ruined like this.

_childDocuments_.review: Help Will Come Tomorrow is a squad management game set in the Siberian wilderness around the time of Russia's October Revolution. In the aftermath of a train derailing by bandits, you'll have to manage the needs of your group and explore the surrounding area to ensure that your characters have sufficient food, water, and shelter to survive out in the harsh taiga environment. You'll also need to foster relationships within your band of strangers, who come from various backgrounds and social classes during a time of significant class tensions. Given the revolutionary context of this game, the political views of your characters readily come into play during interactions, particularly during the nightly campfire exchanges.The game has a unique historical setting and a nice art style. Each of the characters is sufficiently differentiated to have a backstory that's worth taking the time to explore. The core gameplay loop is well-polished and engaging, even for those who don't normally play these types of character resource management games. However, after the first playthrough, the novelty of the gameplay does start to wear off, and even though you're presented with new characters, you starting encountering many of the same events all over again, as RNG starts to direct the flow of the game, It also would've been nice for the game to explore some of its historical themes more directly... despite the semi-frequent campfire arguments between the proletariat and bourgeois members of your group, politics tends to take a place on the back burner due to the survival focus of the game.Nonetheless, Help Will Come Tomorrow is fun and well-polished with a unique historical setting. The first playthrough definitely carries a sense of excitement and gravity as your survival story unfolds amidst an unpredictable, snow-blanketed landscape. Wolves lurk in the trees, bears roam the land, and renegades are just around the corner, looking to carry out "shoot and loot on sight" orders from their bandit head honchos. But undoubtedly the most dangerous foe of all, is the freezing wind that makes this landscape such an inhospitable place.

_childDocuments_.review: It was fun in a sort of masochistic, "I enjoy suffering myself and seeing the suffering of these virtual characters"-way. For a while. But when you get an event that completely trashes 3 hours of careful work and management without you having any possibility to do anything about it or save from a previous point, someone in the design team deliberately wanted the players to post bad reviews and/or didn't really think things through.

_childDocuments_.review: is an indie story-based survival simulation where your group of four strangers from different walks of life come together in order to survive. The story takes place in the Siberian wilderness, and the passing through train was attacked, and so the survivors will need to cooperate despite having different beliefs and motivations.The game is heavily story-based, and paying attention to the small details will be important. The group of survivors will have action points to act alone with others in order to carry out different tasks that are important in order for overall survival.The game is fairly easy to understand and there is a very in-depth tutorial that will teach you most of what you need to successfully navigate this game. But you will have to read a lot through that. It's also okay to skip it and understand the game through trial and error.The game comes with three difficulty settings as well, starting on the easiest setting is a good way to become familiar with the game mechanics.Most of the individuals in your group will not trust each other, and certainly they will not like working together. As the player, it's your task to bring them together to see past their differences in order to effectively increase their chances of survival. During the day, you will be assigning them for various jobs, such as upgrading your camp, creating tools, cook, or go out on expeditions. They can also rest, heal, eat, etc. based on the individuals' needs. While out on expeditions, one of two of your group will work on gathering resources, hunt animals, as well as deal with triggered events. It's easy to get lost or face various dangers as well. This is done in a hex-like environment.You will need to take care of the group as they will have hunger, thirst, fatigue, cold, injuries, etc. You will need to manage all of this, while considering the characters' attributes, as some are more tolerant of various conditions/foods/hardship than others. Their individual attributes are revealed as you play, based on the actions taken, and so taking advantage of synergies will help with survival.Each survivor has a set of action points that can be used during the day, end the day/turn when they all reach zero or there is nothing more that you need to do.This then brings about the night sequence, where you have the option to expound on two conversation topics each evening. This allows the individuals to understand each other better and change their opinions of each other. This is very important because these changes bring about better work efficiencies and such when they are tasked to perform actions together.The graphics are well done, the handdrawn artwork and the colors/style are really nice to look at.The music is very nice for the general atmosphere. It fits well overall. The dialogue does not have speech, so you will have to read it all. There's not too much dialogue.This game can be fully played with a mouse.€19.99 is a bit steep for this game. But if you like these kind of games it worth it. There is no regional pricing, so the US price is also $19.99. This is one of those games that's easy to get sucked into for longer sessions because you want to play just one more day. Then one more, then one more. This is a good thing, speaks to the quality of the game and also how engaged the player is with the mechanics of the game.So far I have gone through two runs, the first one lasted 20 days until both expeditions got lost and I couldn't find a solution. The game by default gives me randomized individuals, so the second run had different people. I think I learned from my mistakes, though there are a lot more to learn.If you enjoy surviving simulation games and don't mind the need to reset if you lose and do it all overa gain, this is a muts buy.Score: 8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect for avid fans of games like Dead in Bermuda, Dead in Vinland or even This War of Mine,  is a seemingly simple-looking, 2D survival game where managing your little group of survivors as they try to make the most out of the terrible situation they are in. However, the game is quite challenging to play, even on Easy mode, and it expects you to figure out quite a lot of stuff on your own. Despite the occasionally weird translations, the game also touches on some really hard-hitting and deep topics through your survivors' nightly conversations, and after a while, you do feel some sort of kinship with the characters you're trying to save from the harsh Siberian weather and the thugs who would love to do nothing more than to slaughter them all.Did pretty well for a first run if I say so myself but I didn't make it to the end though :P+ Lots of replayability - the game is difficult to play and due to that, you'll definitely get a lot more hours of playtime out of it as you try different strategies to keep your little group of survivors alive. Game's worth the price.+ Really challenging survival/group management gameplay even on Easy mode.+ A tragic storyline with interesting characters that you can learn more about as you interact with them.+ Besides the occasional weird translations, the storytelling here is really good. The game brings out a lot of hard-hitting topics.- Occasionally weird translations - expect to come across dialogues that don't make much sense- Not much hand-holding... after teaching you the basics, of course. Expect to learn some tough lessons when you lose important members of your group due to one thing or another.As many have said, Help Will Come Tomorrow is just perfect for fans of games like Dead in Bermuda and Dead in Vinland, both of which are games that I've greatly enjoyed playing. The game's truly challenging and although I'd like to think that I did pretty okay for my first playthrough on Easy (since I'm learning the game), I still end up with my entire group dead. That said, if you're not to sort to shy away from a challenge, you don't mind some translation mishaps here and there, and that you do enjoy playing games like the ones mentioned above, then Help Will Come Tomorrow is definitely worth buying and playing!
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: If it were cheaper, I'd recommend it (and almost did). I got it on clearance for $4 and am happy with the purchase. But I wouldn't be if it had been more than $10. The content is just too limited to justify the full price. "This War of Mine," which people have compared this game to, is priced the same, $20. But there is way more content in that game. This game is more similar to the phone app game, "Survive," where the gameplay is just making choices, resource management, and crafting, and that's all there is to the strategy. In "This War of Mine," the strategy depends on the different maps, characters, some gameplay, and dumb luck. In this game, the strategy is basically the same regardless of map or characters. The different characters are different, but it doesn't much affect how you strategize. In addition, "This War of Mine" has the option to make characters, maps, and different starting combinations of characters. There's also a lot more to the gameplay. It has more replay value, so long as one can deal with how depressing the game is. This game is just as depressing, but has more repetitive gameplay. So I think this game is just priced too high. There's more to "TWOM" all around, and it's also a beautiful game in its aesthetics, writing, and story. You get way more bang for your buck with that game.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: There is a certain charm that accompanies every element of a new game called Help Will Come Tomorrow. The game takes place in the historical time that is not often used in games - on the eve of the October Revolution, when bandits attack the train traveling in the taiga and several survivors find themselves in the midst of snowy madness. We will have to save them by correctly distributing resources, fighting off a huge number of dangers, while also trying to maintain humanity within ourselves. Heroes are randomly selected at the beginning of each new game, each of them has its own individual traits and weaknesses that the player will have to work with, and an important role is played by the ability to combine the worldviews of various characters in order to prevent discord in the group of survivors. Gradually revealing the stories of heroes is interesting, you even begin to relate to some quite differently, looking at the situation through their eyes.Survival in the game is very tough, and this is not a joke. Even the average level of complexity makes you suffer incredibly, counting every lump that you can throw in a fire, and by 8-10 days you will begin to howl louder than the pack of wolves attacking your camp. There are just a huge number of dangers, and action points are incredibly small, so you have to spin like crazy, constantly choosing between a bad decision and an even worse one. And it great stimulates the inner sense of danger, delivering a very interesting sensation. I can’t say that the game is fair in everything (often it punishes you only because it can do it), but the brighter the feeling of victory. What I didn’t have was more additional tasks that could diversify the next run. There are many different ways to survive in the game, so each player can find something for himself. Yes, of course, this is not a huge sandbox game, but rather a resilient thing, so you should not expect huge spaces for research from it. But this density allows you to really feel the horror of what is happening, feel the severity of the Siberian frost on your face, and startle from the crack of brushwood under someone’s feet.A difficult but very interesting adventure that throws a serious challenge to the player, but rewards for it in full. Recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: The game is quite addictive (as any other resource management game in my opnion), but honestly too many things annoyed me:1) the game takes place in the Russian wilderness and features Russian characters, but the Russian writing/translation is quite poor (I had to switch to English).2) the discussions that take place at night are somewhat weird, you can't always follow the logic / unclear how answers relate to what's been said.3) it is not possible to combine different resources of the same type, like you need 10 wood, but you can only use branches OR planks - it is not possible to use both. Seems unreasonable.4) game forces the ending on Day 25. I'd like to have an exploration mode, so that one could challenge themselves with how long they could survive.5) sometimes you just get too much to read - a few skippable animations would do wonders to this game.6) the animations that do exist in the game are too vague and boring - couldn't even finish watching the "good ending".All in all too many disappointments for such a small game.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this together with my boyfriend for about 7 hours (on his account). We played a single game from start to finish and got a good ending. Neither of us are planning to ever play it again to get another ending, but if we had ever died and gotten a bad ending, we would've probably restarted. It was enjoyable to play together. Maybe not worth 20€ though, so definitely wait until it's on sale.Firstly, we probably should've played on survival mode instead of normal. That's on us. But the game was quite repetetive and it felt as if we just did the same thing over and over again, not feeling challenged enough - even if I'm completely new to this sort of survival game. Shortly put, it was too easy. Or we were just lucky, considering most people seem to think it was tough. Secondly, the dialogue wasn't exactly rewarding, story-wise the game simply wasn't that interesting. English isn't my first language either, but the translation fell a bit short in this game. And when it came to choosing what the characters said to each other, it was really hard to tell what the outcome would be. Sometimes we would pick what we thought was the most positive, but then the characters got mad at each other. I didn't feel the connection. In the end, we just skipped through almost all of the talking. It was a bit disappointing when we had to amputate a leg but the character artwork didn't change: he still had two legs on screen. Other than that, I really liked the art-style. It felt on-point. I liked the map and the character design was great and gave life to the characters on screen. The characters each have their own personality which actually affects the gameplay. I like that you can build your own group and choose from different characters. So if I were to replay afterall, I could have a different team and a different experience. Finally - yes, I would recommend "Help Will Come Tomorrow". On sale. I have a hard time pointing out what I liked about it, but it is enjoyable and I don't regret buying it. But it definitely isn't the best game experience I've had, and it probably won't be for you either.

_childDocuments_.review: Rather shallow game. I hoped for something like "This War of Mine", but it`s not even close as good as TWoM. I didn`t get the whole relationship thingy in this game, as it seemed to change not much except the morale of the camp.Yea that´s about it.If i had gotten this game for full price i would`ve refunded. You can check it out as long as it is for sale but i would not recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: I completed the entire campaign in about 4-5 hours on a second play through. Your experience may vary depending on difficulty. Additional time was spent achievement hunting through subsequent playthroughs. is a base-survival-story game in the same vein as the acclaimed  - except focused on the intertwining narrative of individuals during the Russian Revolution. While some support the Bolsheviks, others are loyalists who lament the falling of the Tsar and are fleeing. Others still have no allegiance and must contend with the changing world around them. This is the best aspect of HWCT - the narrative. With a random (if you so choose) ensemble of characters, the developers manage to weave a story of discord and survival that is both compelling and historically accurate. As a historian, I always do appreciate when other medium provide historical content whilst still crafting an enjoyable game. Despite a short playtime and only minor replayability if you enjoy learning about the characters,  is a great game to obtain if you can get it at a suitable discount.Pros:* The characters are incredibly well-written - meshing and conflicting depending on the conversations you direct them to have. They all have historical archetypes and will bring up historical events that were happening during the period. You will get to know and understand the characters if you read all their dialogue, and become invested in their stories. I love how well their stories were written, and it is the clear best aspect of HWCT. * The art style is just great, I love the fidelity with which they created their little world. Its pleasant to play and I never was put-off by lazy/poor graphics. The character models also very great, I love how they captured their identities in each of them.* The intro is voice acted nicely and meshes well, however nothing else is voice acted.* The music adequately fit the gameplay but was not very noteworthy. Similarly, the background noises were great at selling the atmosphere of the game.* The gameplay is very intuitive and is not hard to pick up. However, there is still strategy in your decision making and you can always improve, adding another layer of depth despite its accessibility. On the whole, the entire gameplay loop is well-refined to make it weighty and important but never tedious or overly long.* I really like how each individual upgrade to your camp has a visual impact - many games take the lazy route and just tell you that there's been an upgrade, however in HWCT there is always a visual change with each upgrade which is a very nice touch.Cons:* The historical aspects are fundamental to the story. If you're not interested in vicariously understanding the lives of those during the Russian Revolution and are only interested in gameplay, sorry the game does not give you that option. This is not an issue for me, but may be an issue for others.* A complete playthrough is fairly short at 4-5 hours (depending on difficulty). You will probably need to make second run in order to be successful, but it does not change the actual length. There is some replayability, three different scenarios and of course playing with different characters, however if this does not entice you then you'll be left with an overall shorter gameplay time.* Map exploration should have been a bit bigger. Granted, given that each gameplay loop is short, you can't really go too far. However, on the first playthrough you'll already know the entire map thus there's no need to explore further at greater risk to yourself. * I managed to softlock myself in my first playthrough by not completing the end objectives in time. You can avoid this by being more diligent, however there was no indication from the game that I had screwed up and had no way to win afterwards (I survived several more days). This seems like an obvious issues that should have been addressed during development.  fulfills its role as a short but impactful and story driven historical game, with every aspect of the game feeling finished and refined. It's not a perfect game, there's only minor replayability which is only good if you enjoy the historical story - however this can be chalked up to this being the first game from a very small indie studio with a small budget. On the whole however, HWCT is definitely a game to pick up if the story premise interests you.Score: 8.5/10 -> Fantastic, historically accurate, and engaging survival game!

_childDocuments_.review: I first played the demo then bought it.I liked the settings of the game. The historic background, different stories and traits of each character and also their artwork. To acquire random characters each games does increase replayability and difficulties. But then after a few gameplays it gets frustrating. Basically relying on the 4 survivors given will end up in tragic. The 4 will never reach a point where you could feed them well and make progress to upgrade the camp enough, so you most of the time had to sacrifice and suffer.The RNG feels kind of made to annoy you. Bad events always occur. I once tried to upgrade my camp one day and I failed three times in a row. I ended up doing nothing that day and one day wasted is totally fatal.  Player uniqueness and traits does not seem significant enough, or is sometimes irritating. Anna works well with people but will have better chance to fail? She also has the Focused trait but I never get an extra drop of water from the water filter. So these player traits most of the time made the survival more challenging and hopeless instead of allowing me some good division of labor. I might start to prefer that they are all equal and have no difference.  The best I have achieved is 11 days of survival but it also ended in the worst player experience. After a day end I was told my camp is attacked by bandits and they are all dead. A threat that wipes out my whole squad? In this game bandits are close to being invincible. Even a expedition team could result in members getting killed by bandits. It would be very rare to actually defeat a bandit (which I never succeeded). Here I might prefer predators like foxes and bears instead, since without bandits the severe environment is enough to game over players a lot. These animals could be easier to fight and offer some favorable loot like meat. The fatal threats are not well executed. To have your camp surrounded by 3 bandit groups I would rather surrender.

_childDocuments_.review: HWCT is not a very long game, and heavily relies on you replaying it at least once to get most out of it. There are three possible "end game" scenarios out of which one will play, although you can also choose the scenario yourself in case you want to try a specific one. You can also choose the passengers to attempt survival with, although half the fun is not knowing with whom or what kind of personal traits you'll have to deal with. There's also other kinds of random elements like weather, resources, etc. in play, but at its core the game is more about risk management than just getting lucky or farming for resources. Taking care of a small group of detailed, realistic and historical survivors is also nice, since the genre often focuses on just one blank slate player character or a larger community of more heavily randomized survivors which lack personality.

_childDocuments_.review: HWCT is a survival game lite, extremely narrow and linear. It starts with 4 survivors left in the Siberian Taiga who are supposed to be (mostly) Russian, yet their names are spelt with super weird approach to slav naming (Polish, I guess) that makes no sense whatsoever. They're all super miserable and annoying. You get to explore a bit around your camp (Think Neo Scavenger, cut down to just few hex tiles), and upgrade 5 "buildings" in the camp. Actions are turn-based, and in the evening, you get to pick from 2 dialogs that are supposed to inject some story and politics into the game (yet it doesn't matter). Characters even seem to have few ideas about escaping the situation, but this is again, just a window dressing, because there's one way to escape and it's on a timer.So none of this matters. All you have to do is stay alive until game ends. While this idea itself isn't terrible - think Frostpunk for example, but this game doesn't have even 1% of the awe, gameplay or depth of Frostpunk. I wonder why it's on PC at all, everything about it screams "mobile idle clicker game", especially the lack of voice acting, animations and sensible cutscenes - which are absolutely  expensive to do nowadays for even a tiny indie team, especially for so tiny and 2D game. Yet there's none.Meh.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: What you'd survival expert sim game play, interesting characters, but so many game ending events and unclear win conditions that you'll find yourself more frustrated than intrigued.I like this game. The concept is pretty standard but the characters are interesting, especially if you're familiar with pre-revolutionary Russian history. The choices however are unforgiving. For example I had two armed survivors set up an ambush on one renegade and both died. I felt like I had done everything the game would want me to do to have that interaction go as planned, but it didn't and essentially ended my playthrough. There are several other instances like this. Few hints (if any) are given in these situations, which is nice in the sense that it forces you to use your own reasoning, however even logical choices have game ending outcomes. Often times its not even explicitly articulated that your survivors actually died in these interactions.  Win conditions are unclear as well. There is a number of days you are required to complete every quest within. If you don't do this you lose and its not articulated to you when that is, or that those are the specified win conditions.All of this wouldn't be a deal breaker if manual saves were enabled, but I found myself restarting more times than were enjoyable.Might be good if you have more patience than me or enjoy the punishment.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this on sale and very happy with the amount of gameplay I've had out of it, although I would say it's a relatively "shallow" game compared to some other survival/resource management games I've played.I would still recommend it, with the caveat that the English can be a little wonky, the UI is a little clunky, and as other reviews have touched on, there are some odd game mechanic choices (like not being able to combine mushrooms that have different expiration dates). _childDocuments_.review: It's a tentative recommend, because there are some things wrong with this game. The interface doesn't always work right or intuitively (mixing different piles of mushrooms with different expiration dates to make a soup from them is something I still haven't managed despite having beaten the game twice, including on the hardest difficulty). The dialogue after a few playthroughs is 80% stuff you already know. The difficulty can change WILDLY due to RNG. The realism of some survival, crafting and cooking is... questionable (for example, unless you play on the hardest difficulty and turn off the indicators about incoming weather in the game options, you'll probably find a minor hand cut is harder to address than the famous Siberian weather that's supposed to be a constant, deathly threat).And yet, I've spent over 30 hours in HWCT - because, despite those flaws, it's still a good resource management game. It's simple in its principles yet challenging in practice, the gameplay can vary wildly from one playthrough to another (try not finding any clay for a few days...) and at least some of the time there are alternate ways to address particular problems, as well as costs and needs that require careful balancing. What little story and prose there is - is good enough to keep me interested in what's going to happen, and it sometimes manages to convey a glimpse of the tragic situation our characters find themselves in (as well as the petty squabbles they concern themselves with even in the face of death - sadly, one of the most realistic elements of the game). The art is also quite good, I especially love how the eyes of the characters are depicted. Overall, I wouldn't say it's a great or wonderful game, but it's a very good one. I got it on a great discount and I'm 100% satisfied with the value I got for the money - but even at full price, fans of the genre shouldn't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could recommend this game, because I like the genre and it does a lot of things well.  However, there seems to be very little substance beyond mere survival, which is a shame.Help Will Come Tomorrow starts with an intriguing premise - you're a group of survivors with contrasting backgrounds and philosophies who need to work together to overcome resource shortages, bad weather, and villains trying to track down and kill you.  Unfortunately, as the game progresses, the player takes on a reactive, rather than proactive, role in things, which hurts the experience.  What little initiative there is lies in which resources you choose to collect, and the rest is responding to negative events as they occur.The game map has roaming thugs and wildlife, but one thing it's desperately short of is other encounters and events.  You get a mission now and again to explore a cave or search for signs of other survivors or something of the sort, but they're few and far between.  I kept hoping for some goal I could actually pursue beyond the daily routine of collect, consume, and construct, and with rare exception, it was absent.There was some encouragement when I discovered I could engage the roaming thugs voluntarily, but either I have lousy luck, or it's rare to actually be able to succeed.  You get situations where there's one enemy seemingly defenseless, but if you try to attack him, others come and kill you.  The only alternative is to flee, and of course, neither gets you a result you want.  And even if you do kill some of the roving bands, they just seem to pop up again.Overall, I didn't dislike the experience, but it didn't seem like much of a game, and I feel no reason to play it again.  If you like this sort of game, give This War of Mine a shot instead; it's grittier with slightly different mechanics, but a lot of the concepts and feel are the same, and I think it accomplishes much better what Help Will Come Tomorrow tried to.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: Cool survival management game, but has balancing issues.Initially this game is pretty cool and I really wanted to recommend this game. It has nice artwork, yet somewhat limited soundtrack. The story here is intriguing and can be played out with different characters. Although some dialogues repeat themselves even with different characters. But what really matters here is the gameplay. Its both good and bad. The good thing is that it has several elements to it. Resource gathering, base building, group management, dealing with enemies using a combination of the aforementioned. You start off by gathering resources around your base, which you need to manage properly, because they are finite. Need to make sure your party is in good condition, otherwise they wont have the strength to do things. You need to manage their relations, otherwise they will lose morale and the group will collapse. And for the most part it works.However, this game has a few things that dont work well. First thing are the character traits. Your characters can have specific traits. Some are preset, some are random. And if youre not lucky, the random drops can be quite debilitating. Another problem with the characteristics is that you dont know them from the beginning. You need to discover them through actions. And this can rack up some problems, especially in the beginning. On top of that the descriptions for some of them can be quite vague and you might not know exactly what effects they have. This isnt good for a survival management game.But that I could have gotten over. What made me quit my run and decide on a negative review are events. When venturing out outside your camp you may encounter events based on quests, encounters with enemies, animals, etc.Short story - I had a group of well prepared characters die. They were both well armed, I chose the decisions carefully, because I had the event happen to me before. But despite being better prepared I got the exact same text telling me theyre dead as last time. Hours into a campaign I got such a devastating blow. I could still continue with the surviving characters, but how do I know I wont get another surprise at another event?The RNG should be either predictable or manageable. If its neither, then the gameplay becomes a burden.Unfortunately, I have to vote this down.5.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I belong to probably the last generation who could see around people who went thru the first World war and The Revolution, and listened to their stories first-person, although by the time I started school they were quite old. My own granddad was born in 1917, but than, he was  the youngest of 9 siblings... About the game:10/10 for visual design of characters - static pictures do tell the story, from the very Intro to the way they sit around - small details, their poses etc - they all meaning and telling - that Polish (i presume) artist did great jobMusic is good, with there was more variety of soundtracks, but fits well into what you see on screenGame mechanics are simple and easy, saving style is the same as in This war of mine etc - with the beginning of a new day. some people may find it annoying, but it fits the style - if you want to spam saves - you still can, but that's not as game-play was intended... intentions of this game-play are quite clear - to fit the atmosphere, when surprises, good and bad both come at SURPRISE... Writing is good... i would write differently some Russian names and general russian and english texts probably could do with some corrections,  but that`s the only grudge about wringing quality - story writing done very well, both for as literature quality as well as for stories themselves. _childDocuments_.review: Help Will Come Tomorrow is what I described to a friend as being a "survival visual novel". You are put in charge of keeping four survivors alive in the unforgiving wilderness during winter while they are hunted by renegades who want to kill them. Escape might be the final goal, but in order to get there you have to keep everyone alive and (relatively) healthy by foraging for food and supplies, upgrading your shelter, and keeping yourself off of the renegade's radar. Since the 1.0 release Arclight Creations has continued to actively work on the game not just to balance it but also add new "scenarios" with unique endings.The first thing I noticed about this game is how good it looks. The art style, the UI design, all of it is made to grab your attention and it does a great job of that. I know some people have expressed unhappiness with the limited poses of the characters, but honestly given how small the dev team is I'm impressed that the production quality is as high as it is and I'm more than happy to sacrifice a bit of variety because of it.The story is pretty good. The main plot is compelling overall, but the mechanisms with which it's told through can feel repetitive sometimes. Character stories are primarily told through campfire which I enjoyed at first but started to feel tedious near the end of mid-game. I feel like some of the character development could be moved into the map events, which would also give more incentive to use different people in your scouting parties. The devs have, however, added some flavor text to give more context to the renegades and why they were so intent on murdering everyone, which I very much appreciate. They've also included ending texts specific to the fates of the characters, something that serves to give players a more personalized experience.The basic gameplay of foraging for items, upgrading your camp, and taking care of your survivors is fun. The scouting part helps balance the camp part, and I feel like it adds enough variety to keep the camp part from feeling frustrating or monotonous. The events typically only have two choices, but having certain items in your inventory can give you additional options. I still think having more choices and less obvious "good" and "bad" choices would be best, but I'm pretty happy with the way they've been changed.My main beef with the game in my initial review was the difficulty curve and how punishing (and random) the RNG felt. I feel the devs really worked hard to address and fix that issue by giving players more starting options, making the RNG more dependent on various game states, and overall balancing the difficulty to give a better curve. Passenger (aka. easy) mode now  easy, but with enough of a challenge that I need to stay on my toes because mistakes are still costly.Another minor gripe I had was being forced into a random team; that has been addressed by the devs, allowing players to fully customize their starting characters and choose which positions (if any) they want to be random. I would still like to see enough women so that you can roll a women-only team, not just a men-only one--but I understand that it's a big ask, so it's more something to keep in mind if they do DLC and/or for their next game.Ultimately, though, the biggest selling point for me about this game is that the devs are active in the forums and have continued to improve things based on player feedback. They clearly love this game and want all of us to love it, and honestly that  make me like the game more. I look forward to seeing how this game continues to evolve and honestly I would love to see some DLC one day with completely new areas, stories, survivors, and camp options.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: Good game about an interesting time period. People complaining about RNG and difficulty simply aren't paying attention to the mechanics. Once I figured out what I was doing, I won my next 3 games in a row on 2 different end-game scenarios and 2 difficulties (normal and the next hardest) without losing a party member. Though I do think one guy abandoned the party and died on his own. If anything, the game is a little too easy, as the only real challenge and RNG come at the very start of a playthrough. Though I haven't done the  ending, so maybe that one is tougher. The biggest thing to understand (spoilers for those who want to figure it out themselves) is Also, I was kinda worried when I first started playing about how they would portray the different classes/ideologies, but I think they did a good job. The writing is solid (with some shaky translations here and there) and most of the characters have a good amount of depth that comes out through conversation and events, to the point that I haven't even unlocked it all. Though maybe it'd be less interesting to someone that doesn't have an interest in history or the period (Bolshevik Revolution) portrayed. On the negative side, I do agree with another reviewer that mentioned the repeating dialogue/events in multiple playthroughs. It gets to the point where you're just skipping through text that you've already seen. And in terms of gameplay, I don't think it's quite as polished or has the emotional impact of This War of Mine, though it does add things that TWoM doesn't have, like hunting and crafting clothing.

_childDocuments_.review: This game really reminded me (positively) of This War of Mine, another game which I obsessed about for countless hours. It should be noted that this game suffers from the occasional mistranslation or grammatical error which harms the immersion, and that it indeed depends too much on RNG. The interactions between different characters are by far the most interesting part of this game and the events are well-written. Deeper survival mechanics would have been appreciated (for example, breaking down clothes back into its basic components, using herbs or moss for medicine, having a morale boost to being well-fed). Overall a fun diversion for a couple of hours and one I will be returning to from time to time.

_childDocuments_.review: A moody and thoughtful game about working past polarising differences in the face of harsh survival. I was pleasantly surprised by the nuanced dialogues and the non-caricatural representation of class conflict in the turn of the century. Even the more unpleasant characters leave ways to gain insight in where they come from and eventually empathise with them.I'll note that I found the game's difficulty quite harsh and occasionally subject to chance, and so I had to restart a few times and eventually dial it down to easy to finish it. There are plenty of characters and conversations to explore, and secrets to uncover, so restarting did not harm the game's replay value.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished this one at the 7 hour mark, a few runs completed.It's a quiet little game.  If you can pick it up on the cheap (it's awful cheap right now) it's worthwhile.  The save system is forgiving.  Very little broken about it.  Awful opaque about mechanics, but that's the risk of these sorts of games.It's a slow game as well, you end up doing a lot of reading, or risk missing something if you hurry through the convos. _childDocuments_.review: I've always been a big fan of survival games and this one is pretty good. The game, as it is, is very difficult at the start even on Passenger difficulty if you don't know what you're doing or understanding basic mechanics. It is not complex at all once you get the hang of it but the learning curve might be really steep at first. If I may, I'll drop some of my advice:- Always make makeshift buildings, you save on material and you get the same function as building a solid structure,- Try to upgrade first two branches from left to right on the Campfire as soon as possible, you'll need water and cooked food on the daily, considering how much mushrooms you'll find on expeditions, you'll always be able to make some soup,- Get rid of the persistent character statuses like Sick or Bacteria or Strained Leg as soon as possible- Try to specialize your 4-man team into 2 categories: expedition and base building. Characters that work together at first lose morale, but if you buff those characters through Fraternization on the Campfire, they will like working with each other after some time. Characters on expeditions that go together gain more trust into the other character.Good luck, try it out it's a bit slow at the start, and I wish characters are voiced, including narration but it is what it is 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: *DISCLAIMER*:  I like different games than you.It's hard to review this game and the 'Thumbs up' isn't an indicator that it's a great game.  It's not - but it is  It, like so many modern games, has faults, which is indicative of how complex something is.  The more you move away from KISS, the more problems you have.  It does, however, entertain and certainly has high RNG frustration levels, but has an interesting story line and the interaction with the different survivors sets up many different juxtapositions, both in class and political tones.  The loss of a survivor can impact harshly and the discovery of a new survivor may not be a good thing.However, with it's bland animation, strict resource management and harsh RNG, this game is not for the faint of heart.

_childDocuments_.review: This was exactly what I hoped it would be and I really enjoyed this game! It was quite tough at the beginning and took me several attempts to get everyone to survive, but the trial-and-error made it more rewarding when I finally figured out the best strategies. A few things I wish it had:-More quests to do-Alternative endings as it seemed like there was only one way to survive/get rescued (and if you miss the window all your other effort will have been for nothing)-More diversity in the campfire dialogues as those could get repetitive and I found myself skipping over them during multiple play throughs-I also wish there was an epilogue for each character after they get rescued (ex. like This War of Mine)Overall, I consider these pretty minor things and still well worth the price. It is replayable as you can try harder difficulty, different exploring tactics, different characters with different traits to adapt to (/struggle with), etc. I'll definitely be playing more and going for more achievements!

_childDocuments_.review: First impression while playing the demo was quite good. The characters seemed to come up with interesting background stories. The artwork style is almost cute, a contrast to the gloomy situation it is presented in. Although the tutorial was more annoying than helpful with a ton of text, it appeared to be a decent exploration and survival strategy game with a pinch of rpg, so I decided to buy it. Turned out to be a waste of money. Even if you manage to build up a functioning camp and solid structures while keeping the group alive, nourished, and in good relationships, tragedy will happen. The game makes it hard to understand why it all comes to an end without you being able to do anything. Whatever your stats, whatever you equipment, it makes no difference. The railroading to misery leaves no time for encouragement. Characters get shot at while on "safe" terrain, and if chance encounters do not happen to freeze or starve them to death, they lose limbs or just decide (again, without you as the player being able to do anything about it) it would be fun to throw some hallucinogens into the fire to make everyone so trippy they can no longer take care of their basic needs, which is great in the middle of Siberian winter... Game ends with the group getting captured and /or murdered in their sleep, no further explanation, the player can just watch. Game over. Bye. Well, thanks for nothing. I'd never have thought I should end a review with a Homer Simpson quote, but this game deserves it: "You tried your best and failed miserably. The lesson is, never try."

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, so, this game is really confuse a lot at first, even after all those tutorials. There are a lot of stats, items, and each character even have their own set of characteristic to remember, their story, their faction, their skills. It's just too much information at the beginning.But on my second run, everything is just clicked. I suddenly realize it is quiet similar to the good old board game call "Robinson Crusoe". You send your survivors to any action slot you want them to do, and once all the action point are gone you just click end of the turn. Your main goal is to survive the hunger, cold, sickness, etc. A little tip is that try to find the right man for the right job, every characters usually have on skill that when they do something, they have a chance to get action point back. For example, character with cook skill, can have a chance to get action point back after they spend action to cook food. And like most board game, if you get more action, you get more advantage. Still, it's a not an easy game I can say. On one run, I shoot arrows at the thief, they shot me back, everyone die. On another run, I shoot shotgun at the thief, they shot me back, everyone die again... oh, and those rabbits are fleeing real fast, so I don't recommend you to go after them. However, this game have three difficult level for you to choose, I never try the easy one yet, but from what I read it sound like a happy camping time moment, unless you really drag yourself into the danger.In the end, there are pros and cons for this game, and I'm sure that it is not the game for everyone. Luckily, it is suit my type, and I probably will play again tomorrow... so long, and don't shoot those thief back.

_childDocuments_.review: Now, even though I have a "no" recommendation here, I have enjoyed this game and will probably give it a couple of more rounds before I lay off it and maybe never replay it again unless there are some changes.Pros: Environment--good overall presentation and graphics, interesting premise and setting for the game. It maybe feels a little higher-stakes than similar resource management/strategy/survival games.Mechanics--once I got through a couple of sad, major failed save files, I managed to figure out some good strategies that worked and allowed me to finish Passenger mode (easy) with "the good ending," of which there does only seem to be one way to get.Cons:Music--same track on repeat and basically no sound effects, I can't remember hearing any during my 5 game files.Tutorial--maybe the most long-winded tutorial I've encountered in an indie game. I honestly figured things out just by failing a couple of games, so I'd recommend just turning the tutorial off in settings.Repetition--other than stubborn people like myself who keep losing and just have to win--I see no replay value in this game once you've gotten the good ending, unless you're going to bump up the difficulty, which is what I'm trying next. There aren't as many characters as I was hoping there'd be and I just kept getting 33 of the same ones in my party every game (I've played 5 total games). The conversations are the same each time and some events are scheduled and happen on the same day, seemingly to the same character, each time. I can now predict when a certain event will happen and make sure to have the supplies I need to deal with it on hand for afterward.Things I'd like to see changed/added:Character selector--Like I mentioned, I'm pretty bored of getting 3 of the same characters at my starting party every time. I'd like there to be a function to choose your party members, and to change the number you start with (so you can start alone or with just 2, for greater challenge.)Random events--change the events timing so players don't know when they're going to hit, if at all.Multiple endings--choices and such don't hold much meaning when they don't affect gameplay. There is one good ending, otherwise you lose. This would actually be okay if the good ending felt higher-stakes, but once you know what you need to do for it, it's super easy and you can just kind of forget about it until the last couple days of the game. Endless mode/expand game inventory--tying into my criticism of the endings, I wish there were an endless mode. Once you get the hang of things and your camp is kicking ass and you have enough food to feed a tribe of people, it just cuts you off. I wish you could expand, build addition campsites, find more survivors, grow your tents into houses, etc.I think this is a great starter-game for the developer and I see a lot of potential in what they did here. Obviously a lot of time and love went into this, which I respect. However, I do not think it's worth the $20 price tag, as there is virtually no replay value and it is very short (unless you're like me and you'll play it until you, out of spite, get everything perfect.) In short, I think it's more of a form of artistic expression and less of a game. This isn't always a bad thing, but the feeling just doesn't shine through brightly enough to overshadow the shortcomings of the fun-ness of the game aspect.

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game quite immersive and enjoyable to play, with interesting political dialogue that Russian history enthusiasts would enjoy poring over. It's reminiscent of Darkest Dungeon and Don't Starve with its party morale and base management system. The game isn't without its flaws. The expedition risk system is unclear - danger tiers seemed to be random and not related to bandit/Renegade presence. It was also a pain in the ass when resources to keep your characters alive or armed were permanently stuck in high-danger areas (which couldn't be traversed, because you'd need those specific resources to move forward). The RNG mechanic was just a tad too intrusive, which made an effective strategy very difficult and gave the impression that a win would boil down to pure chance.Nonetheless, I'd recommend giving it a shot. I did have a good time playing it!
