_childDocuments_.review: A very enjoyable strategy game with a fair amount of replay-abilty.It is turn-based, (each of your characters has a finite amount of turns/moves they can make each day, e.g cook a meal, create a medicine, go hunting, build a structure) and also has elements of resource-management and crafting. (you need to go foraging to find food ingredients, medicinal ingredients, weapon components; and you are also required to make sure everyone's needs are met, including hunger, warmth, tiredness, morale.)Depending on the choices you make while out on expedition, your characters can be killed or injured, you can lead renegades back to your camp, an additional character can be discovered and brought back to your camp, you can come across a wild animal and attempt to hunt it, or you can chance upon food or weapon components.Camp morale is also a feature of this game; the more acquainted your camp members are, the better they will perform when carrying out tasks together. Each night there is a group get-together around the campfire where you get to choose different topics of conversation, some of which will improve or damage relationships between the camp members; some will provide opportunities to find special items during an expedition.Since there are so many choices available to the player, every game is always that little bit different from the last.I have enjoyed playing it over and over and trying to improve the amount of time that certain moves take me.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite nice “Dead in Vinland/Bermuda” clone, with interesting graphic style, a diverse group of characters and nicely complicated mechanics. Also, it is less unforgiving than those games, and has an option to select a difficulty level! Another praise goes to the developer/publisher for making a demo version available. In fact, it was the thing which induced me to but the full game.While starting a game, apart from the difficulty level, you can choose your characters and scenario (one of the three) or have them randomized.Several people of various trades and social backgrounds are travelling through Siberia on a train when a crash occurs, caused by a bomb set up by some bandits. Next thing they know they are awaking on some forest glade – four people, having almost nothing of value on themselves (well probably apart from some bottles of vodka hidden in one character’s pockets). As in most survival games, you have to provide them with food, beverages, shelter, tools, weapons; you also have to take care of their health. Of course, all of these must be crafted by the characters and in order to do so, they must explore the countryside and gather all they found. There are trees, stones, clay, herbs, mushrooms and other things to be collected, some animals to be hunted (unless the bear scares them away). Also, some useful materials may be found in the trainwreck: metal, ammo, canvas, cigarettes, alcohol, and so on.The map is divided into some 40 hexes with various terrain features: moors, forests, a river, a railway line, hills and caves. These features determine the resources which may be found during exploration – and these resources are not unlimited, so you should treasure them. Five things may be built on your forest glade: a campfire for cooking and heating, a shelter for resting, a palisade for protection, a quarantine point for treating and making medications, and a workshop for skinning of animals and manufacturing of tools, weapons, and other equipment, as well as for raw materials processing, for instance cutting canvas into string or branches into sticks.Every construction may be upgraded to have better effects and offer more actions; also, all of them should be maintained in good conditions. The campfire should be fueled to protect from cold and cook foods, but you should remember about keeping the camp visibility low (the warmer the fire, the higher the visibility; on the other hand, it is lowered by bad weather and there is a palisade upgrade masking your camp too).Oh yes, because they are numerous hazards. Apart from famine, thirst, fatigue, freezing cold, injuries and disease, there are also the bandits chasing the train crash survivors to kill them and some more or less dangerous animals. Your task is to live to see the help coming, but it will occur not before and endgame crisis (for instance, a dire bear hunt).While playing, you have an opportunity to find two more survivors from the train. It may be good because more people means more actions available. Every character has three action points which basically means they may perform three actions per day at maximum. However, APs may be lost in the morning morale check, wasted or recovered, and some actions, especially construction, require two characters or give better results when two persons perform it. But well, having more people in the camp means also you must provide more food and drinks. All characters have numerous traits providing bonuses and/or penalties; for instance, some are more talented in constructing or exploration and resource gathering, while others may fail at construction or be more susceptible to injuries while in the forest. They have also morale, personal likes and dislikes (for instance two people who like each other improve the general camp morale while working together – and vice versa).As for flaws, the rabid bear seems to be indestructible in some gameplays (the developers provided a solution in the forum), and the exploration party has too few options to use their weapons carried in their inventory (for hunting – yes, but less in random encounters with enemies). It is also slightly difficult to tell how the autosave system works and when exactly the game is saved – at the beginning of the day and after critical encounters probably, but I discovered several times that the camp status is different than I remembered.All in all, I found the game really enjoyable, especially for gamers who considered the “Dead” series too difficult or dreary.

_childDocuments_.review: Help is never coming.  The game seems bleak for bleak's sake. If it has an opportunity to punish you via environment during a mission, it will, usually at the cost of a camp-mate. The inventory management is exactly the sort I don't enjoy and find tedious.Trying to pair up characters to perform life-saving tasks is bogged down by pettiness and differences that would either not matter in a desperate survival situation, or would have resulted in the necessary culling to allow everyone else to make it out.  The final nail is the mandatory campfire conversation. Your selection of characters already have bizarrely rigid and one-dimensional personality traits. You're forced to choose characters who have inherent conflict but there's no nuance and each negative trait is like a stick in the spokes of the other characters' bicycle. It's frequently not clear that what sounds like a positive/encouraging remark will generate a negative reaction. By several nights in, my topics had dwindled to nothing but hot-button. The script is so inflexible that even when a pair of characters had supported each other in a task or performed a successful expedition, their campfire convo was a guaranteed morale dumpster fire.I quit this game feeling the real story is that a bunch of people too fractious and petty to cultivate fundamental survival instincts were loaded on a one-way train to Siberia and the army's *true* act of terrorism was creating a derailment that allowed these characters to remain within walking distance of any human settlement. Too encyclopedic a rendition of the revolution.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like strikingly annoying characters being rude to each other while trying to manage their needs, this is the game for you. I mean, two characters can't even work on the same building project for their own survival without hating on each other. It's ridiculous. The art style is nice, the music fine, and some of the mechanics are pretty alright (though a bit clunky in the UI department). Most elements of the game are pretty shallow, however. I think bagging a reindeer with a bow and arrow and cooking it up may have been my favorite experience in the game. My major issue with the game  is the system of random encounters. They are absolutely brutal sometimes. I'm fine with that in some games, but this one takes it way too far, to the point of ending the game. There is often no warning that the game will suddenly end--no ticker that says "the bad guys will find you in__." I was on something like day twelve, everyone healthy, my camp doing awesome, and suddenly the enemy found us and slaughtered everyone without so much as a cut-scene. I was actually enjoying myself until that. When BS moments can happen out of nowhere, it doesn't make me want to invest another couple of hours into the game. Ridiculous. If I could refund it, I would.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a survival game where you have to gather and manage your resources and build your camp. There are random events and also resources available on the map I think are placed randomly so it gives you some rogue-like feel. Also there are 9 possible characters and each of them can have random skills but I also think some of them have more chance to have skills from certain groups that are connected with their backgrounds. You start the game with 4 characters and you can later rescue or find one more so in order to learn everything about each character you need to play the game at least 2-3 times. And that is good because there are also 3 possible storylines to choose from and they change some random encounters and the weather you will face and your end game goal.I liked that characters belong to different social backgrounds and at the start have their superstitions towards other backgrounds. Some people are nobility and support Tsar and how the things are now while others are revolutionists that want to change the world they live in and there are also people in the middle that don’t strongly support either of the sides. Because of this the more time people spend speaking with each other around the campfire during the day the more they start to like each other and understand others and they also have things they can speak about with others during the night and your choices during that night meetings will change how they feel about others or even trigger some new random events to check on the map. You can check each character friendship and trust towards all other characters and influence it with your actions to make them all work better with each other.The graphic and presentation of the game are nice. I liked how everything looked and even gory things like wounds on characters or having a necrotic hand or losing a foot are presented well. The world presented feels real and each building you can build in your camp and all the loot you can find looks like they belong to the world presented in the game. Also the description combined with graphic makes the random events feel real and important and makes you think what would you do if you were there. I hated that some events have no choices and just makes your people die no mater how many weapons and ammo you have and how good your clothes are. It was also strange that at the end game the same random event was in 6 different places on the map each time resulting in the same description and my people getting killed.The expedition system is strange as it is unclear many times how much action points will your move or search action take and if you will be able to get back to the camp or will your characters get lost in the woods. Simple moving from one area to other area or searching for loot actions take 0-2 action points and you are never 100% sure how much the action will take and random events can also take away some of your action points so you can’t really plan out your moves. The train crashed! Now try to survive in Siberia long enough to be rescued!Overall score 6.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: The desperate atmosphere of post-czarist 1917 Russia is amazingly created in every regard. The art, the music, the dialogue... everything just works so well together. Every aspect of this game works to create the feeling a true, and realistic survival scenario set against the historically accurate background of the Bolshevik Revolution and class-warfare. The character interactions are engrossing and show just how viscerally personal each characters ideological allegiance is while also allowing for personal growth borne out of necessity. This game is much less a game than an experience. I strongly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is garbage. Clothes are inefficient, Insulation in sleeping place is inefficient, you have to balance between getting found out and freezing to death. You cannot go directly after the bandits when you have the gun you have to hope event pops up where you can go after them. Also no there are no structures or anything else that allows you to make camp less visible. If you don't grow your camp you are going to die anyway due to cold and other hazards. Character weaknesses are based around rng and loot is rng so you spend lots of time just re-rolling the starting loot and character weaknesses until you actually get forward in the game then down the line one bad throw can destroy your good start completely. There is no comprehensive warning you are going to lose action points next turn due to negative debuffs so you have to memorize what actually matters and what does not. There is probably way to get really good at this game but I would describe it like learning to play an instrument. Game wants you to play in highly specific way there is no room for freedom or ingenuity it is just about knowing what specific actions in specific situations allow you to make an action without spending an action point. Thus you can make more actions in given turn than you should be able to but I would say it is more about learning specific notes than having actual freedom to decide how to solve any given problem. Poorly designed game hides behind a story. What I came out with from this game is diversity is a weakness. If you ever get in to similar situation in real life hope to God people are vaguely on the same page or you will all die. Honestly characters would have had better changes of survival if they just followed the tracks where they came from alone and made a run for it. Would they die? Probably yes but they would actually have better change of succeeding than when they try to stay where they are and try to get people who are not on the same page to work together.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun little game. The writing is lovely, with a couple minor hiccups with typos, characters feel well fleshed out, though after some playthrough you realize many lines are exchangable between characters with similar ideals and backgrounds.It plays very similar to This War Of Mine in the way of management, but much shorter, and focused around more outdoors survival then war living.The gameplay elements are fun and rewarding, especially if you're a survival game fan, and the character dialog each night is very interesting and feels natural. Building up your camp and getting to see it change and become more and more advanced over time feels like something to be proud of as much as it is useful.It does suffer in a couple ways, admittedly. It doesn't have a huge amount of replay value, unless you're moving up to another difficulty- there appears to be 3 end game scinarios which do make up for this a little, and your group is different each time- but they still end up functioning much the same each time.  Still, I could see myself coming back to this a year or so later to relive it even after having completed it once.The game mode I completed was Shatun, or, The Bear, which I would complain some about the game suddenly becoming far too harsh.  When you die in a survival game, you want to feel like it was something you could of done to avoid it- having a better understanding of the world, or maybe if you picked up different supplies beforehand.The Bear, has a % chance to instakill you at any given time during an expedition past a certain point, which is more just irritating then anything else. I tried to bring guns to fend it off, or meat to drop as bait, but unlike most events in this game, there were just no options to defend yourself. Nothing that makes you feel like you even had a chance of effecting your fate.This is not great game design, however is also mostly noneffective as well, due to how easy it is to "cheat death" by just closing and reopening the game. And I'm glad for that, because I think I'd be having a worse time if I couldn't and I wouldn't get to finish this otherwise beautiful and enjoyable little project. Keep up the good work guys!

_childDocuments_.review: My whinging aristocrats were executed after a delicious roast dinner. I fully agree with other reviews that recommend first time players stick to passenger difficulty. There are a range of complicated systems to explore and tinker with, and it's more fun to feel like you're surviving okay before the disasters really strike.If you've enjoyed This War of Mine, or Don't Starve, there are familiar elements here but with a well developed setting and slower pace. Art is fantastic, although some of the characters aren't exactly beloved. You'll find your favourites and a few who you don't mind if they wander off in the woods and never come back to the camp-fire.It only takes a few minutes to get into the rhythm of managing the camp, and is easy to play in small segments if you choose. I don't have hours and hours of free time to devote to gaming anymore, so I appreciate the bite-sized play and emerging story.Next time I'm going to repair my rifle sooner so I can shoot those bandits when they come!
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: Help Will Come Tomorrow is a management game where we play as a group forced to survive in the Siberian wilds. That is one way to describe the game, and it’s accurate because that’s mostly what you’ll be doing. Clear out snowbanks, build shelter, craft tools, gather food and avoid death in all of its forms. That’s the core of this game, and even if you only view it from that perspective it’s still solid, with mechanical features that are varied, interesting and challenging.There is more to this experience, though. While the meat of the game is its mechanics, the spice is its characters. There are nine of them and you can pick four of them for each playthrough. Each of them have their own stories to uncover, their own qualities and flaws that impact gameplay and their own opinions on different topics. Each night they gather around the fire, discussing topics of your choosing. What makes this more interesting is that the game forces you to pick characters of different social classes; some are aristocrats, some are military and some are workers (and mostly socialists, given the time period and setting). Conflicts are thus not uncommon, and it’s up to you to try to mitigate the damage this might cause to morale.But while the interactions between the characters, together with the well-realised setting and political realities, is a clear strength of the game, it’s also a weakness. Not in the existence of it, but in the way that it’s conveyed to us as players. When looking at the management and survival mechanics, they are well described and tutorialised with a clear connection between an action and its effects. Some things are discovered through trial and error, others depend on some sort of randomiser (like hitting a shot while hunting), but they’re all easy to understand. The social mechanics aren’t. The connections between dialogue options and characters’ reactions are pretty vague, and even if you have a grasp of them, the purpose of increasing social meters is not communicated well. Why am I trying to make these people friendly towards each other? The answer, which the game doesn’t tell you, is story. You simply get to know more about a character’s backstory if they trust and are friendly with the rest of the group, which also impacts how much of their ending you get to see. This is a good feature, to be clear; it adds a new challenge to the gameplay, it adds replayability and makes the characters feel a little bit more like people. But when you don’t know exactly how it works, that every social meter with every other character has to be high in order for anything to happen (at least I assume so, I’m not 100% sure myself), then it can feel a bit random and disappointing when you don’t get a special interaction in a run. If the goal and the reward would be better communicated, then I think that the overall experience of hunting for backstories would be more enjoyable.With that said, Help Will Come Tomorrow is still a fine game. It has solid mechanics, varied gameplay and that little bit of extra in the setting and characters to set it apart from the crowd. It’s maybe not as grand as the store description makes it sound like, and the writing has some grammatical flaws. But overall, I had a good time with it and I think you would too.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: A cool little game with many different segments that keep you interested. I'd say it's something worth checking for every fan of this type of games. After around 10 hours of playing I got kind of bored, because it seemed to me that I knew all the mechanics and the characters didn't interested me after playing them one full playthrough. But while it lasted, the game provided some quality fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little survival themed game with decent enough replayability, from a base of decent story and game theory. Definitely keeps you interested in multiple runs as random events are such that no 2 runs are the same. Some events seem downright unfair, but learning the mechanics is part of the game. And using that knowledge in future runs. Difficulty is pretty hard, but also very balanced. Although saying that, if you get screwed by RNG it can ruin a run.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a game I play for long stretches at a time - but since it released I habe downloaded it a few times to enjoy a run or two. It can be really punishing but it's absolutely possible to get a strategy that works for you without failing for dozens of hours or diving deep into guides first.There are a few scenarios that mix up the goals a bit without changing the core loop to much - and even an option to get a random one so that you can't meta-optimize before your characters even know what their big danger will be.Characters have different "alignments" which can cause strain or friendship. as well as some randomized traits. Overall, I can really recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible atmospheric and well-designed - the main gameplay loop is really fun for at least a couple playthroughs. The characters are well-written and interact with the historical context of the game in really interesting ways that adds a lot of flavour. I really enjoyed trying out different character combinations and seeing how it changes the dynamic of the whole group.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: AMAZING! I love this game!!! It's so complex in its management. Not only are you managing the resources you scrounge up, you're also managing the people themselves: their opinions of one another and morale. Each character has the potential to develop traits positive and negative that may effect how they can best be used to help the camp as a whole. And the struggle is real to get the stations of your camp like shelter, fencing, a worktable and fire upgraded enough to sustain yourself comfortably. The artwork is beautiful and the characters are entertaining and engaging to follow. My ONLY issue is that I believe there might be some value lost in translation maybe? The wording in some instances was a little muddled. But ABSOLUTELY worth playing if you enjoy a good story and the challenge of any kind of management game.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great, its has some nice difficulties and some deep character developments. The game has great replay ability, as you cant learn about all the characters in one game. It also has fun scenarios that give you challenges like fighting a bear, or defeating armed robbers (all whilst fighting for basic things like food). So do buy this game, and if you don't your missing out, on this fun game.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very board gamey, which can be nice for some. A lot of the choices you make don't make a difference in the end, and it gets boring after day 10 or so. There seems to also be some limit on resources, like how many animals will get trapped so no reason to check traps once you've caught 3 or so? The mini quests also didn't make sense.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a game just as good as This War of Mine, this isn't it. But if you're looking for a game with similar themes that isn't as difficult or as heartbreaking, then I'd recommend this. I don't think it is as bad as some reviews make out but it can get quite repetitive. Overall it's just okay, it's not a bad game, but I'd recommend buying it on sale. Maybe if I hadn't played This War of Mine first, I would've liked this more.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this review based on two runs on the passenger difficulty, so keep that in mind. I think most of my criticisms will apply, both good and bad.On the whole, I liked this game. It's incredibly atmospheric, and it got me looking into real history (always a solid plus). I got very invested in the game at first, but on my second run I started feeling that the game would do better, if it was expanded. You can really see what the developers were going for, and they did come out the other end with a decent end product. Still, there's room for so much more.Let's get the good stuff out of the way first. As I said, the setting really sucks you in. There's probably no better place for a survival game than the harsh Russian taiga. The characters have interesting backgrounds, and their interactions feel natural for the most part. Furthermore, I loved the art style: it really fit what the game was going for. The gameplay was easy to understand, and at least in the passenger difficulty you can manage your odds of survival well despite the RNG. The division of the gameplay elements made sense, and even in the easiest difficulty there's a fair chance for failure.As for the negative points, the game is just too small in my opinion to really live up to its full potential. The area being explored is somewhat restricted, and you don't have a lot of things to do. That would not necessarily be a problem on its own. A game with more narrative content could make up for the lack of mechanical elements, but despite the decent writing, the story elements feel somewhat superficial. At times they're poorly communicated as well, making you guess what point relates to which character. Not that it mattered much in the passenger difficulty. Camp morale was so easy to keep up that I never felt threatened by a lack of morale. Even the individual morale of characters stayed up most of the time. I recommend the game, but you should probably buy it while it's on sale. Personally, I hope the developers will expand the game in the futre.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: Really, really nice game. Some achievements are "too random" (oh, many, many tries of hunting that elk!), but in everything else... You want harsh survival? Get stranded in Siberia after a train crash.Too easy? Bandits that blew tracks are hunting for survivors.Still too easy? Now there is a bear out there (maybe). Or multi-day snowstorm that will make any foraging impossible.Oh, you managed it? How about plague?...Now this game has atmosphere. And pretty little details that make immersion almost complete.Totally recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: pretty boring game that revolves around the same three screens - Camp, Expedition Map, and Night dialogue, leading to a pretty shallow experience. The game tends to also leave a wealth of things unexplained and also straight up LIE at times leading to a very confusing and mediocre experience (wtf does camp visibility entail? How long/much do ailments last for? What do threat levels entail? Just a bunch of other ♥♥♥♥ left to guesswork as well).And for very likely the worst part of the game - the extremely punishing RNG. Loot is RNG, events are RNG, failure rates are RNG, pretty much almost every "vital" element to survival is RNG. I spent 5 days looking for some materials just to deal with some wounds that, due to RNG, was GIVEN TO ME AT THE START. Couldn't find what I needed to get medicine and care to my chars. and pretty much doomed the run.Faux sense of difficulty due to the excruciating cheapness of RNG along with the (honestly quite boring) shallow gameplay really make the game hard to recommend, and hell I even like This War of Mine; which also unsurprisingly happens to be the superior game.4/10 has some interesting elements but just falls short immensely
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: Serious. Grim. Hard. Enjoyable. . . You will Die, so pick an easy difficulty..The game elegantly has a single set up, and 3 different storylines using 4 of 9 possible survivors.To survive, you must listen at the fire, and choose well..It has surprising replayability.A couple of odd translations and words  is endearing, almost appropriate.I have enjoyed 100 hours of this game, and might spend another 15..4 on medium. (Windx2,Bear,Showdown)Haven't tried Hard..The story and art style is satisfyingly immersive.Each person needs to be kept alive, with constant needs, like 4 Tamagochi's, freezing and starving to death in the snow.Naive story choices, Camp construction inexperience and a set map is why you should start at an easy level..How fast you can press a button is not important.Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: It might be a bit too soon to have solid opinions on this game, but I wanted to write a few things before I get used to it. The game is great, but there's a lot of issues with the UI, yes, you can get used to it, but it's clear that there was almost no though on the UI. Too many menus, too many useless options, a good portion of the time I find myself struggling with the UI, and not the Taiga. That said, after the 3rd game I got more or less used to it, and it's less annoying, and I'm sure that before I get to the 10th hour I'll forget about this feeling of wasting time on the UI.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun little survival game. There's not enough tutorial, so you'll have to play few a through times, but it's easy enough. You have to manage resources, explore the area, and try to not get shot. What's not to like? If you want the fun and expect to win, try the easy setting. If you want the challenge go hard but expect people to die. I picked it up on sale and have enjoyed it for about 25 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice survival game overall. Three scenarios and randomized resource tiles and character traits help keep it fresh for couple of playthroughs. Your mileage may vary but I recommend checking the demo first before buying and probably best bought at some sort of discount (goes down to 70% off on sale).
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun for two or three playthroughs, after that you have seen it all. Some stuff is very powerfull and makes the game way easier, other stuff is completly useless. The Balance is very weird. Its fun but exspect to restart a couple times until you find the one broken thing. Also this game has a huge amount of RNG which some people might dislike, though it didn't annoy me too much.The characters are interesting however their conflicts are sometimes a bit contrived and also have little impact on gameplay.Overall its an okay game, 20$ is maybe a bit too much.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: It is very rare nowadays that I can find a game with a theme and story I enjoy that is learnable within an hour or so and gives at least 10+ hours of entertainment from that point on. I was looking for a good survival game after becoming disenchanted by the fact that in FO4 Horizon I can apparently build a giant town as one man, and was looking for something more realistic, although I liked the hunger and thirst mechanics.Not into multiplayer, the idea of "shot on sight" games like Rust and Scum seemed very unappealing, as I've also heard there is an extremely steep learning curve and I don't like totally starting over after many hours of investment.This game is great! Really scratches a survival itch.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: So at the end of 5.2 hours; I just finished the game with good ending (only 2 loses before that) on easiest difficulty. Good ending is not hard at all, if you ask me. I finished it without losing any of my people as well, 2 achievements at one stone. But let's see;Pros;# Nice graphics# Really good musics on background# Nice story for each character# Resource management is pretty balanced# Has some good buff-debuff system for charactersCons# It's really a short story. Game ended pretty early.# After some point, gaining enough resources, it's just doing same things over and over again# Not much of an outside events from renegades.Conclusion: 7/10I would totally recommend it especially since it's on sale right now. It's a good game with great potential. Hope they'll add more stuff in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: Simple, but fun, Help Will Come Tomorrow is an atmospheric and story-driven survival game. I found myself looking forward to the more story-based evening segments of play, just so I could get a tidbit of this world's characters interacting and more of the setting. I've not yet 'beaten' the game, but I feel like it has its hooks in me enough to say that I feel this game is well worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying this game. My favourite mechanics include the camp building and the character relationships. The different character combinations are excellent and lend great replayability to the game along with the different endings. I anticipate playing many more hours of this game in the future,
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: I personally like this game because of the survival RNG elements. Its not really forgiving and there is always something unexpected and out of my control whenever I play this game. Yeah it maybe kind of visual novelish but I don't find many games featuring the October Revolution which is kind of annoying in my opinion because it is such a significant event that changed Russian history. I hope more developers actually capitalize on the idea of making more historical based games featuring political the horrors of revolutions like this more often because it was never clean or as romantic as it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: Basically a clone of This War of mine without direct control of characters.The problem with this game is that screws you without having any idea what is happening and whether it is a bug (like expedition lost for literally a week)*. Inventory is also not well executed (items in split groups are not automatically combined into bigger stacks for not good reason) making the rather mundane gameplay even worse. It has very low replayability value boring you already on third attempt. I consider it a waste of my time.*EDIT: Out of curiosity, I checked discussions. It turns out this is feature, they are considered dead just not showing it to player until their bodies are discovered. This game was designed for masochists.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: but with cuter graphics and more forgiving gameplay. I'm usually not a fan of resource management games. They end up feeling like I'm controlling a vast space of city/empire/etc and makes it boring to me.  lets me manage 4-5 characters and have them interact with each other over the campfire each night. Wonderful.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: this is the hardest game i've ever experienced in my life took me three day to figure out how to play and survive and this is just the beginning of the nightmare i do love this game but at the same time i hate it so much,but it's good for practicing your reading skill and that's all i can assure you the rest is up to you
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: Needed a bit of a change of pace from first person survival games, and this is a nice fit.Action point based, not real time, so no need to be on constant guard and can take it at your own pace.The stories are quite nice, and you've really got to think to handle the relationships between the survivors so they are not at each other's throats. The survival aspect is not a pushover either, and you have to carefully manage your action points, resources and statuses.I like the graphics, and the music is lovely.Bought it on sale at just over £5, and I feel it's an absolute bargain. I probably would have been happy enough to pay full price with what I've seen so far, and the replayability.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: I just played for my first hour and the game looks really nice, fluid and deep.I'm quite excited to see how hundreds ways for my group to die are hidden in this gem!Feels like pure survival/craft with an extreme setting and impactful choices to make. I really like the dynamics between the characters impacting and being impacted by the actions in the camp but also by the conversation people have during the night and their actual political point of view and personality.Good find, clever game!
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: Great atmosphere, good story and lots of different ways the scenarios can play out. I liked all the characters I played with though have only tried 5 of them so far. The way the game is set up it guarantees a good dynamic cast of characters that have some conflict to overcome through their situation. Surprisingly challenging as well, which is a breath of fresh air for games like this, took me a couple of attempts to get through the end game events. Would be nice to have a codex in the game for some of the nuts and bolts like how long different food lasts before it spoils but it does kind of add to the atmosphere - the characters know as much as about surviving Siberia as you do so you've just got to figure it out. Also, very rarely there's a couple of translation errors but they don't detract from the experience. Very fun game!
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: 3.5 stars out of 5.I really like this game! Got it on sale, like 6.99 and I think it's worth it at that price. Addicting gameplay, makes you think strategicly and a bit of history for history buffs out there. Characters can get a bit repetitive because they're in the same groups, but their backstories are all different. The game is a bit difficult; the whole point is to survive and not get killed by the wilderness, starvation or getting killed by the enemy.My one main complaint? You get random events; sometimes an animal will come in the camp, or icicles will start falling, est. There is this random  event, I think it's random, called Massacre of the innocents. The enemy finds you and kills you, the end. That's. IT. You could be on a roll and you freakin' die! Happened to me many many many times and I don't know how to stop it; maybe my fire's to big and the enemy sees it. If there's a solution please tell me and my rating would go up to like 4 stars. But other than that, it's a great game and highly recommend it :DEDIT: I finally beat the game on easy, don't know about the Massacre of the Innocents if it's something that happens more often in normal and hard mode or what, but it's beatable at least.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game. I'm about 16 hours in and I've probably done most of what I will do with it, but I think that's good value for the price. It's a gripping story with strong characters and interesting strategic choices to be made. The game balance is solid, requiring you to weigh risks vs. gains, physical survival vs. personal and group morale, and heat vs. food vs. risks of being found and killed. The storylines open up more as characters develop stronger relationships and there's a good host of different characters and goals, so there's at least enough replay value to keep me going through two full endings, and I will probably play it at least once more.  Good, thoughtful moral gray areas and reflections on history and society. There's a lot to like!
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy these types of games so my opinion may be biased. It's UI and text based which i enjoy. Its a bit of challenge, i do wish their was more to the game though. I wouldn't pay full price for this game as its lacking in content, characters and stuff to do but on sale for 7 dollars it's a fun little survival game that I do enjoy. I just wish their was more to it, also I feel in games like this it would benefit the players if DEVS would add a narrator to read the long amounts of text, particularly character discussions you could have different voices for them. It would add a lot to the game play and wouldn't add much production time or cost to do.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great game, akin to war of mine.There are some minor issues:- Chat messages don't appear after selecting a topic. Have to click skip.- Placing traps make no sense. I have to wander in certain directions to place traps.- Gave me motion sickness. Not sure if it was the nice bottle of wine I had during the play.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: I love that there are more historical games about Russia and Slavic history and mythology in general. Felt a big lack of them on the market.And about this one?It is beautiful, from the artstyle and soundtrack, that immerse you in this tragic, sensible and touching, I would even say heartwarming story in the harsh and cold atmosphere of the country at the breach of Revolution and inner war, to character and plot development. This game has a unique, but aesthetically and intellectually pleasing vibe.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played on the easy setting, and I have to say - it isn't very easy. It took six tries before something ridiculous didn't some out of nowhere to kill me on the last day. Still, it's engaging and even as low as my frustration tolerance it, I keep coming back. And the replay value is great with all the possible combos of people interacting.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice survival game if you like point-and-click -style adventures! I got to an ending on medium difficulty and it took quite a few deaths and restarts. Overall the game comes with a lot of story to read and decisions to make. The tutorial in the beginning is very helpful for understanding how to play. It's a lot of text but totally worth it if you like this kind of games.Normally I don't write reviews but I wanted to promote this game as I think it should be more popular :) The negative reviews seem to come from players who didn't spend enough time to see the patterns. Buy it on a sale and it's well worth the price. Now go take a walk in Siberia and see if you can find some of that vodka!
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: A fun survival experience crossed with a social study of the Russian Revolution. It’s pleasantly realistic but also strongly dependent on chance. And the odds are always against you. The game lacks a little more objective. The player just wait and wait for some goal to actually pursue beyond the daily routine of collecting, building, hunting, etc, and with rare exception, it was absent.A good game. It definitely have the same vibe as This War of Mine. But not the same quality.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great, story-driven, group survival game. The mechanics are solid and the story is enjoyable, the only thing lacking at the moment is more of a long term, quasi-endless survival mode. While the dwindling resources of the map won't suit a proper endless mode I hope the developer's come up with future modes that take much longer to complete. All in all an excellent atmospheric survival game, worth a good look.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: High replayability and an enjoyable enough game if you enjoy survival/resource management games, but goodness is it tough! Tried it a couple times on normal and died pretty early on, so I dropped down to easy mode to try to get at least a little bit farther along. Even then it took multiple tries and eventually just resetting days (when I got tired of having to play through everything completely over again) to try to manage to get a game end where everyone survives.A lot of the dialogue is repetitive and can get a little tedious, and it's irritating that some of the dialogue that don't appear to be character-based keep appearing when you're further into the game if you don't pick them initially. It makes it harder to try to work your way through everyone's storyline easily. Speaking of storylines, it does appear that one character's story arc might be a little broken-- I've had multiple playthroughs, as I've said, and despite trying just about everything I still . Attempting to look up various guides/discussions hasn't yielded any results beyond other people saying it doesn't appear to exist, so it looks like there's still a couple things that need ironing out . Overall, I did have a good time and plan on going back again after a bit of a break to try to go for all the achievements!
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game. It scratches my itch for games like this. Story driven survival games are hard to come by. Dead in Vinland certainly is one of those types of games. I personally only have problems with the amount of clicking in the UI. I do not mind characters not moving and other things that I have read in the comments. Everyone has their personal taste, I guess. This game certainly is worth giving it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fairly challenging, story deep version of the typical "survival" game.  With multiple characters for replayability, and attention to detail that is impressive! The developers are taking on feedback and changing a lot already after the release, i can see this becoming a really great game with some tweaks.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game.Not so comlex, like "Dead in ..." title. More relaxing, more intuitive.There are no so much numbers, most things are clear whitout calculation or well hinted.Game not so long. For 11 hours I finish it twice. And I very slow player.Good visuals, nice events, characters, that don`t like each other, how it suppose to be. Plot are simple, but very nice.You cannot minmax your characters, but game not about infinite survivng. You just need to pass certain number of days. No need to create ultimate builder or medic. Just relax, survive and have fun with eating moss =)Strongly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: The game comes across as simple, but it is surprisingly complex. The stories of each individual character are well developed and strongly affect pairings that the controller needs to think of compatibility with every task. And even though some characters are well suited to menial tasks such as cooking or crafting, if they are not contributing to credit improving actions, the situation with others worsens.Some issues would be the clarity on major quests that can occur. In the mass amount of information explaining things initially, it's easy to miss that they're time limited. I've also struggled with continuation of other quests. Even with campfire discussion, where a quest activated before, it never did again. An event would occur on its own, but then a huge gap of time has occurred since then and still nothing again.Lastly, after you progress far enough, there are nights where there are no conversation. Unclear if that has to do with character relationships.Other than these two points, I've found no major issues that ruin gameplay for me, and have yet to run into any bugs.I will say I wish there was more than one game save so I could continue different stories.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: So...you see the thumbs up. And there's a reason for that. I mean...to put it simply, this game gives you exactly what you're looking for, it's exactly what you think it's gonna be. Now at first it is gonna throw a whole bunch of information at you and look intimidating and confusing but just be patient, slog through it, and get past the tutorial and into the crux of the game. And on your first playthrough it's not gonna be super easy either btw lol. If you want a more in depth look with more information and actual gameplay then check out the video I put on my youtube channel (link below).But to put it simply.The music is really nice (so are the sound effects)There's no voice actingThe mechanics are a bit confusing at first but once you learn them they're easy.Plenty of choices in this game that really effect the story and gameplay.The survival aspect is very challening but it has a few different difficulty modes just in case you're looking to make it easier or harder for yourself.The art is really nice and pleasant.And...yeah I mean...it's just overall a pretty decent game. Ever play "Dead in Vinland?" This game is a whole heck of a lot like that game but in russia. Right down to the sitting around at night conversing with each other mechanic.I think it's a pretty good game, the price tag matches what you get, and I think that if you're a fan of survival simulation/strategy games then you're gonna love this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: In a uninhabitable Siberian wilderness, in a wake of October Revolution, a group of passengers survives the mysterious catastrophe of Trans-Siberian railway train. They must endure in a harsh ice-clad climate until rescue arrives. Facing many dangers, their own weaknesses and, above all, their own prejudice.
_childDocuments_.name: Help Will Come Tomorrow

name: As Far As The Eye
detailed_description: Wake up, swell up and get up, Sigh. It is time to bring back to me the Pupils scattered throughout the world and to guide them. Do not worry, they will recognize you as soon as they feel your breath on their faces, as soon as they see their woolen clothes spinning, they will understand because they are waiting for you. Caress their feet, carry their bodies, lift their spirit and instill hope and perseverance in them. Do not skimp on the gusts that will make them realize that the road is long and that it must continue, always, As Far As I. You play as the wind guiding the Pupils, a tribe that must reach the center of the world. You’ll have to manage their resources, their buildings, and their lives. Help them grow wiser through agriculture, crafting, scientific and mystical research before the world is submerged. Be careful though, you have to manage your tribe perfectly and make sure they’re not starving or taken by surprise by the waters. The game is a nomadic turn-based city builder. Begin a procedurally generated journey and survive halt after halt, as far as the Eye. Plan the best path for your tribe to take in order to go as far as the Eye. Explore, analyze and search places of interest for long lost treasures on a procedurally generated journey. Harvest, build, stock and leave your halt before the wave engulfs your tribe. Improve your pupils through the job system, your buildings through the improvement system and your whole tribe through Tribe's Knowledge. Survive dire conditions and protect the Pupils against random events. Meet allies, negotiate for resources, recruit new Pupils and more! Make offerings in Sacred Sites or plunder them, but never forget you'll have to bear the consequences of your actions . Live a peaceful adventure as there are no enemies in As Far As The Eye Relive a new adventure each time thanks to our Roguelike tribe system Tune your play session with games modifiers such as game duration, halt size, resources generation and more. Play the campaign to learn about A FATE's traditions and legends. Unlock new tribes and new regions thanks to our Roguelike system. Earn rewards and unlock new stories and fates by reaching the Eye with as many Pupils as you can in this Roguelike resource management game.

short_description: Build a mobile village and travel with your tribe toward the center of the world, called The Eye. This roguelike turn-based resource-management game is made of procedural situations, natural events, skill-trees and hard choices. Ready to move?

_childDocuments_.review: Saw the reviews; bought it anyway. Glad I did, but also understand why this game doesn't have universal appeal to some kinds of players.TL;DR up front: If you like Reus, Faster Than Light, and Monopoly, you'll probably like this game. If you like to reload when you get a really bad dice roll, or keep reloading to reopen the same chest until you get a legendary weapon, or keep playing until your characters become godly and overpowered, you probably will not. There's no saving in the campaign at all (the campaign is sort of like... five short difficult puzzles based around late game mechanics, you can clear the whole thing in an hour if you know what you're doing, otherwise it takes about 3-5 hours). The campaign does not have "save and exit", and you're going to die more than once in the campaign. Also, the campaign is not very fun. Be prepared for these realities. The "Campaign" does teach some later level techniques, but the regular game also has guidance on how to move and generally what to do. If the campaign gets frustrating, skip it entirely and come back to it later. From the reviews it's clear that a lot of people never made it to the actual game and just got frustrated with the campaign.In the regular game you must save when you exit, it saves automatically every turn, and there's only 1 save file. The game is made to be played and finished. This makes it play much like Faster Than Light or Slay the Spire; in 2 hours you either made it to the end of the round or died, so savescumming would be silly, yet the other most popular complaint people seem to have is the lack of multiple save files and ability to reload a couple turns back. You're not meant to play until your group becomes overpowered, and everything doesn't have to be perfect... you're just trying to get to the eye before the world floods, while leaving enough behind for those that come after you.Like Reus, the game is beautiful. It feels like you're lost in a Studio Ghibli film. Like Reus, there's no epic saga where you play the same squad for months and months and get super buff, there's no building a massive base with 10 million of everything, in fact there's even a game mechanic to punish you for taking more than you need from the land. Every "cycle" (aka every game over) has the potential to unlock some new content, but you will always be walking that narrow path of "don't run out of food", "don't take too much food", and "get moving to the next map before the flood comes". Zero "late game domination" occurs.Like Faster than Light, the game is a *little* bit forgiving, but not very, and there's some randomization that can work against you. If you screw up badly enough over the course of 4-5 turns, or get a really rocky start, or pick too hard a path too early on, or decide to open a risk/reward chest and get a bad enough punishment, you'll probably find yourself dying unless you're really good at pulling rabbits (and food/medicine) out of your hat. Sometimes things just don't work out the way you planned. You can screw up and forget to give a unit orders, or send them somewhere to explore and find nothing, and still be totally fine, but if you run completely out of food because you weren't paying attention, you may not be able to get things back on track quickly enough before everyone starves.Like Monopoly (assuming you play 4+ players), you're probably going to lose more times than you're going to win, especially early on, and sometimes it will just feel like you only lost because luck was against you and you kept landing on tax squares and couldn't get all the railroads like you hoped. Better players will usually do better, and you'll reach a point where "bad luck" can be almost entirely avoided with good decisions and caution, but you'll need to get better at knowing what's coming up ahead and when to be cautious and what potential risks may be encountered, which involves losing and learning. And even if you win, no matter how rich you might have been, next time you play you will start with nothing. If you expect to win every time you sit down to play, even as a beginner, you're probably going to get frustrated. If you're OK losing and setting up the board and playing again, the game is a delight.People who find these games frustrating will probably find As Far As The Eye frustrating. People who like these games will probably like As Far As The Eye.I, for one, love this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was incredibly brutal until I discovered the Council building and the Knowledge resource, and then it became an incredibly fair and deep city-building/roguelike/4x game.The biggest problem with the game is there isn't a good reference for how all the mechanics work.  I think it will be better once an online wiki is available.My tips for a winning initial game:Opening:1.  Get 40 wood and build a sawmill.  Assign one of your workers to be a gatherer and gather wood.   Later, when you don't need wood, switch this worker to be a food gatherer and build a fruit hut for 80 (you can do this earlier if you get a 4th worker).  You should have enough rations for this, and the carpenter/fruit gatherer jobs share the first 3 levels.2.  Get 120 wood and build a dispensary.  Assign one of your workers to be a druid and harvest herbs.  IMPORTANT:  Druids generate a ton of Knowledge after they hit level 2, so just keep leveling the druid3.  Have your third worker be a dedicated builder/explorer.  Explore the map and do all of the following:* Find a source of stone, build a quarry for 100 wood, and gather stone until you have 120 stone* Find a source of ore, build a minefor 100 wood, and gather ore until you have 120 ore * Find one packbeast and recruit him5.  Now, you can build the Council auxiliary building.  It has to be built on a plain next to your starting location, so make sure you leave some space!  Build it and click on it and open the tech tree that you never knew existed.6.  Look at the bottom left.  See that technology?  It saves 6 rations/turn for your WHOLE TRIBE.  You want to beeline to this thing as soon as you can.  You need to upgrade your Coucil twice, and it requires some combination of Wool/Wood/Stone/Ore (I don't remember exactly).  Then, this perk costs 900 Knowledge.  Rush this ASAP.7.  The tree on the right hand side is key to managing Vagaries.  You can skip ANY vagary by paying 350/400/500 knowledge (increases as the game goes on).  You can also get earlier and earlier warnings by upgrading this tree, so you can be selective (e.g., you are on a map with no jungles, and the next vagary places disease in jungles)8.  Also prioritize a market and upgrade it to Tier 3.  You need 5 different resources to do this (Knowledge/wood/ore/stone/wool).  Don't be afraid to rotate workers around.  The market is pretty much useless if you don't upgrade it, but it can really save your bacon if you specialize in one/two resources.9.  Mobile buildings are overrated early-on.  You will have plenty of wood; have your woodcutter keep leveling up and SPEND your resources10.  This leads me to...DONT STOCKPILE early on.  If you have harvested enough ore/stone for a tech upgrade, get it and move on.11.  Always get the first upgrade on the fruit hut (-1 harvest time), even on permanent buildings.  Trust me, it's amazing, and will level up your gatherer even faster (gatherers can cost no food per turn when fully upgraded, depending on your build).12.  Select skills that increase knowledge-per-harvest whenever you can (e.g., if you aren't having food problems, have your fruit gatherer take the +Knowledge per turn instead of fruit per turn)13.  In the council building, there are relatively cheap tiers of knowledge that reveal the path costs for both one- and two- paths later.  Use these to plan your routes!  Not all resources are available on every map!Anyhow, all the people who are upset about the randomness of Vagaries and needing too little food probably didn't rush Tier 3 Council.  And yes, the devs should have made it more obvious how critical this building is for early success.  But don't let that turn you off from this game; it's an incredible resource management game, with a relaxing atmosphere and beautiful art.  It is challenging without being crazy 4X (think Stellaris) level deep.  If you think you'd like it, ignore the negative reviews here, give my advice a shot, and enjoy

_childDocuments_.review: *Edited* I'm changing my review from not recommended to recommended as I played this game more. It has a very steep learning curve and I found it almost impossible to actually complete the game at first. In the beginning it was extremely frustrating and disappointing to never be able to finish, because there is no ability to save the game in between stages in case you make a mistake or have bad luck. I almost quit playing because of this and I still think that saves would be a good feature to add. (Note: I'm not a great gamer and just wanted something casual to play) Finally I was able to complete the game, which unlocks other stages. These come with bonus features that make it easier. It feels much more rewarding now and I feel like I actually have a decent chance of completing it when I play. My favorite part of the game is how many skills there are for your characters and how you can really specialize their abilities in different ways. There are lots of options in this game for paths that you take, so you can strategize in different ways each time. I also enjoy the graphics and peaceful music and vibes. So, if you can make it past (what I found to be) the really difficult first part and steep learning curve I think you could really enjoy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a few turns away to win the game, then a rodent event happened and lost a huge amount of resources to it. The result? The wave catched me and my tribe was flooded. The fail was expected. The fun brought by this game was unexpected.As Far As the Eye is a very challenging resource management 4X strategy game and the developers spiced it up. They moved the whole game into the field of roguelike games. Not a common combination for turn based strategy games.If you curious what contents the game offers and how it is look then check out my short video about this game:You will always be short on resources, you will feel that your workers eat too much food while they produce too few resources. In the meantime the wave is coming… It is hard to master the game and easy to fail in it. Understanding the mechanics, react to the deadly events all required if you want to finish a run at least once.Don’t be mad if you can’t do it tho. Custom Game is available so you can adjust the game to the way you want to play it.I enjoyed my time with this game. Water is coming, it could be the story of our world while the ice caps are melting. Kevin Costner would disagree. Roguelike game so replay value is huge, but the game could be uninteresting after you win it a few times.  I believe the visual of the game is very good. Very artistic.. Relaxing and charming soundtracks offered by this game. While there are custom game achievements not available on that mode and the regular gameplay is very challenging. Finishing a run is far from easy.Perfection time: Now this part will be updated at a later point when the game will be listed on my curator. Achievements awarded for unlocking new traits, what then could be on your worker. How to unlock those? Probably awarded for your actions you done during your gameplay and unlocks ONLY once the game was won. Because of this, it will be always hard to predict what unlocked a new trait, therefore 100% achievement will be quite hard and time consuming.

_childDocuments_.review: Short rundown: This game has a great concept, that I love. It has a lot of great gameplay elements to it, and I've been following it for a while expecting it's release.Unfortunately, the game is let down by the developer's conscious decision to rob the player of meaningful decisions through high impact randomness. Ultimately, the game is designed such that you have no ability to predict, mitigate, or play around the random events. Every turn is like playing XCom, except instead of 95% you're looking at 50. Roll well and you succeed, roll poorly and you fail. The frustration is very high, because the random events rob you of your ability as a player to make meaningful goals and achieve them, and give you no opportunity to plan or react around the randomness. You simply have to accept that this game will be affected by a slot machine about once every five minutes. The specific mechanics where this is painfully frustrating are Vagaries, visiting Caravans, and to a lesser extent the explorable random benefit/punishment tiles that profess to be predictable once you progress far enough to have a high level pawn to use.Summary: The random elements in this game are prevalent, high impact, and give you no ability to play with, towards, or around them. This is very frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't review often, but I've been really enjoying this game, and it seems like it's getting quite a few negative reviews with impressions that don't match what I've been experiencing, so I wanted to offer a different perspective.At its core, this game strongly rewards careful planning and familiarity with its systems. The tutorial Campaign doesn't cover everything it should - of the criticisms I've seen, this one is valid. You should probably expect to lose your first game, or at least have a rough time, because you're figuring out the stuff it didn't tell you.However, the other criticisms I've seen a lot of, especially about how easily you can lose to RNG, are a lot less valid, at least once you know what you're doing. I can imagine getting a start with particularly debilitating traits on multiple starting colonists and being unlikely to succeed, but I haven't gotten that bad of a roll there yet, and even if it happens sometimes, it'll probably be obvious immediately and you can restart the run if you want.As for event RNG, it's pretty easy to deal with - you'll always see minor problems coming at least 6 turns in advance, sooner with research, and most of them can be mitigated by making choices: don't have people working the turn an Overwork event pops, or make sure everyone's working though Boredom, and they won't get sick; if important buildings get damaged, either repair them early enough that the next event won't destroy them or make a plan to move on from the loss if it does. In the mid-to-late game, you can use Knowledge Points at the Council building to negate upcoming events - if you don't do it too often, this will let you keep from folding to the particularly bad ones. This doesn't work on the Major event at the end of each level, but you can usually be gone before then if you want to be.Finally, there are complaints about not having enough resources on the map to pay the cost to the next stage - yeah, it happens, but again there's counterplay. You can always see the costs for the next 2 legs, so if you see a good stage ahead, but after it there's only 1 path and it's expensive, consider going somewhere else. It's risk vs reward. If a map is low on a needed resource, the Market can let you trade for it (though the rates are horrid, especially when not upgraded).In my opinion, this game is difficult but ultimately gives the player the tools to deal with the difficulty. If you like building/resource management games where planning well is important, I'd recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Hoo boy, I wanted to like this game. Community management, guiding one's characters and their growth in the quest for survival in a dangerous world? Neat. Mystical auras and enigmatic ruins? Sounds good!So why "wanted to like"? Well, because it screws basically everything up. The community management is extremely cutthroat. If you fail to optimize your tribe's every move (or indeed, frequently, if you succeed to) then your disciples will all run out of food and die in short order. Mission failed, try again.The auras, rather than feeling magical, are simply massive disadvantages. One single aura will reduce all resource gains by 50% in its area until calmed for several turns by a dedicated disciple. You have, like, three of those, by the way. Remember that cutthroat resource economy? Yeah, you're not going to have three turns every twenty to spend soothing auras. But you  won't be able to afford half gather rates. Or none at all, if two auras overlap the spot with the fertile field or wood or ore or whatever you really, really need to get some of. Fun! Oh, but they grant a bonus to production of... one specific resource, within their area, while soothed... which is super useless since you don't ever want ONE resource, you want at least one food resource and then on top of that, three different randomly chosen ones per mobile building out of wood, ore, stone and wool (otherwise you have to pay the wood building costs for each gathering hut, every farm, every quarry, each and every stop of the at least four-or-five-leg journey... which adds up to a lot of wasted time and resources!) and if you have an expert druid then you can permanently soothe the auras, yes. But you won't. You simply will not have one of those expert druids, because you have three people to start with and all of them desperately need to spend the first several hundred turns just building up a basic, basic resource economy which will barely keep them alive once the starting supplies run out.Basic game balance is foreign to this game. With your every move, it seems to say "You searched some ruins? Well, have a massive disadvantage that will wreck this playthrough. Should have  them first with your expert druid, hoo hah! What do you mean you don't have one of those,  must surely have one of those. Haven't we told you how useful they are? What do you mean you're busy trying to scrap together enough food not to die? Screw you! Have some calamities! Oh hey, but a friendly caravan showed up. They'll help you out - for 20 potions! Healing potions, the druid makes them. Well, he used to, then he starved to death. But if you can support a druid, and make 'em gather spices for about fifty turns in a row, and then brew potions for another forty turns or so, you could make this one trade for some random resources or an extra person and mouth to feed from this passing caravan! Doesn't that sound like something you'd be prepared for on day 30 of your long, long journey of needlessly slow character development and desperately trying not to starve (or freeze - the northern tribe gets to ALSO die if they run out of wool, hooh hah! Wanna play as them? They have three people to start with... but those people might have mildly beneficial traits! Yeah! That totally makes up for having yet another constant resource drain that will kill you if ignored! Ha ha haaa, we can design games, could you tell? We never actually played them - we seem bad at them, keep dying, but we assume this is how video games are supposed to work, so here you go! Happy dying!"I mean, sometimes you might get lucky? You make progress, make good decisions, get lucky rolls on various fronts, and for a while you feel like the game isn't terrible. But overall, as a game, unfortunately... it is terrible. It's not fair, every mildly risky move is a dice roll, and so are friendly caravans which may or may not give you what you desperately need to stand a chance at all.It's not fun. You try and try to place buildings as efficiently as possible, assign disciples to never ever rest for a single turn, make the most of what you have, and what do you get? Another weary sigh as the wind (that's you) watches another pack of gormless incompetents starve to death and evaporate into corpse particles because they somehow made it all this way without learning basic survival skills like how to gather, cook food and clothe themselves without ze specific purpose-made buildinks!The potential for a fun game was here, to be sure. It was just completely ignored by whatever goofballs decided to instead hydro-frack the concept for all the frustration, tedium and strange gambley nonsense mechanics they could.Heartily disrecommended.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a huge issue with game mechanics here. I really tried to like this game but it seems like instead of giving you a meaningful challenge, the devs just want the players to randomly suffer. I gave this game more than 3 tries, and around  11.1 hours of gameplay and honestly, no matter how much you plan, prepare and strategize in this game you would loose due to awful bad luck and NOT because of poor planning or bad skill. The "Vagary" mechanic is so unbalanced that you would lose no matter what you do. Imagine acquiring all the necessary resources to progress to the next level AND THEN suddenly a vagary mechanic kicks in where you lose 90% of the required resources to progress to the next level. Now you don't have enough time to gather resources again because you're a few turns away from this flood. I even have this screenshotted so people can see how absurd it is.If it weren't for the very broken vagary mechanic then this game would have been fun. It has a lot of potential but this game is honestly unfair. These "vagary mechanics" don't give the player a challenge to use their skills and think about a solution. It just makes them super frustrated because they appear out of the blue and are out of your control. Another mechanic fast forwards the flood by 20 turns and it stacks. Like I'm uninstalling this game now because this mechanic is highly unbalanced and it wasted my time. It's like using a broken scientific calculator that has a 80% chance of malfunctioning towards the end of your major math exams  -why? just because. that's why.I finished playing all the campaigns. I tried to play the tribes but I honestly even can't get past the first tribe. I don't want to ruin a dev's career by giving them a bad review since they still have the opportunity to change. Please think of ways to balance this mechanic.Players reading this. Expect a broken game mechanic and a lot of frustration during game play.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: This could very easily be an excellent game with just some minor tweaking. All the elements are there, except every time you even get close to getting to the Eye, you end up losing in a way that is completely out of your control and that's what's frustrating about it. You could min/max all day long, hit the last stage, and be (like I was the last time before I quit) trading cereal and spices and wool into a fully upgraded market to desperately try and get enough ore and stone to get out. Even fully upgraded the ratio is 6 to 1! This could be adjusted- make the upgrades scale just a little harder. Or maybe get the halt resources to lean in your favor just a little bit so the resources you need are actually available if you only have one path out. If you're going to give me that few choices, you have to make the resources more forgiving. Maybe just give me more choices! Why is there only one path if you're traveling from one specific place to another specific place? Maybe I can pick between two routes but still end up at the same halt. That would at least give me the illusion of control. There is nothing more frustrating in a game than when you are defeated by a factor out of your control. Give me agency. One unlucky vagary can destroy your game. One time I literally lost a whole pupil to an explore... I have no words for how overtuned that is. Like it was well written as heck (he met his reflection and just followed it through a portal to god knows where), but I honestly ragequit right after. I'm not the sort of person who plays games on easy, but I can't even get past the first campaign...All that said, this game is so beautiful, it's skill system so charming and fun to play with, I just wish you would stop murdering my cute little guys like a monster. Pretty please?I know there is a custom option, but just turning vagaries or food off? That's a different kind of unbalanced, too easy to engage with. Possibly, you need a difficulty slider, my guys. Noobs don't want to play on deity, okay?

_childDocuments_.review: Game looked pretty good.I thought the game was a ressource manager but its actually a crisis management game.Your building is burning; mosquitos in the jungle; all buildings near lakes take damage; all fixed buildings take damage; one of your villagers got sick.... yadda yadda yadda. Thats the game. Every three turns another thing that keeps you from the core gameplay. If you are intrested in this kind of challenge go ahead.Apparently it gets even worse as you mainly unlock more negative events the more you play.Hard pass.Also tutorial takes like two hours, too late to return it.

_childDocuments_.review: The premise of this game is promising, but it's ruined by its frankly terrible UI.
