_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? I don't know, but it certainly is a lovingly crafted turn-based resource-management game. With a prehistoric U-Haul truck (a large dino), you try to guide your tiny tribe to safety to escape the rising sea level. The goal in the game is to reach the Eye, a highland surrounded by mountains. Plan and execute the long journey to the safety of the mountains. I mean, I hope the mountains are safe and the sea won't raise above them as well, in which case you should have built a boat instead of running away.The game takes place on a (random) hexfield map, where you can settle down, send the members of your tribe on different tasks and advance the time by ending your turn. Plays a bit like Civilization. Speed is not of the essence, but efficiency. Think before you make a turn. When you settle down, this is just for a bunch of turns until you reach your objective, then everything will be packed on your trusty dino again and you continue your voyage, hopefully with enough ressources to survive, at least until the next stop in your voyage. Actually, you cannot leave until you have the required resources to reach the next destination. Structures (sawmill, mine, pasture, quary,...) can be built in a permanent or mobile (more expensive) version. Gaining knowledge is important, there is a large technology tree (over 100 traits to improve your tribe members) to be learned. There is no warfare in the game, your tribe is purely pacifist and there are no enemies around, you may only meet friendly tribes (to trade) and creatures (to tame) - but maybe a few natural disasters or obstacles. And some evil ghosts.There are 5 campaigns to be played, on which you will trade with other tribes, cultivate the lands to gain ressources, research knowledge, enlarge your tribe, build structures, explore ancient ruins, communicate with spirits or just offer them some gifts. Choose from 4 (unlocklable) tribes to play, each one living on a different side of the Eye and, from the freezing north to the mild and humid south, in a different biome. You can also chose to play shorter or longer voyages. The devs call their game a roguelike, with a procedureal map and random events. Is everything today called a roguelike? The original Civilization from 1991 was also a roguelike, if I think about it.The scenery, especially the creatures and your characters, look rather alien like. The sound effects are weird and the music is soothing. I saw no bugs and the game worked fine in ultrawidescreen.Unique, lovingly crafted, and *peaceful* roguelike single player strategy game. Collect the ressources you need and lead your small tribe on a long journey to safety.

_childDocuments_.review: DISCLAIMER: I received this product for no cost for the purpose of reviewing. However, this does not affect my views and opinions of the game.As Far As The Eye is; a bunch of different elements combined into a very visually pleasing rouge-like management game. The player takes control of a mobile village moving from one location to another until it reaches "The Eye". Doing so mashes up genres such as base-building and turn-based strategy with a hint of survival and RPG elements mixed in. This, in addition to the FTL-like gameplay, makes for a very interesting, but somehow relaxing, title. --------The aesthetic of the game is very well done. Although there are so many colours and objects placed on the screen at once, the visuals still manage to give off a very calm and relaxing vibe. The animations are also visually pleasing and look great. The theme of the game revolves around nature, and the art and models really reflect that. --------The peaceful sounds and music that is heard while playing the game are also well done. The music fits in with the overall theme of the game, and the small sounds of the wind, movement, and the pupils working are nice. --------Although the game tries to do a lot of things, it does most of those things well enough. There is a lot management involved. The pupils, who are essentially workers, are guided to do specific tasks that the player sets out for them. Whether it be build, explore or gather resources. The "stage" is cleared once the village has a enough of certain resources to continue to the next area. The goal is eventually to get to the final area; The Eye. As the game continues, the player will obtain more pupils. The pupils level up depending on what tasks they are given the most, and can become more efficient at these tasks. They also have a skill tree that the player can use to further shape that pupil. Pupils need food to continue to work, and will also die if they are not fed, or due to other circumstances/events. The player has a certain amount of turns available to them to complete the stage they are in. If they can not complete it in time, the game is over. After finishing an area, the player may choose which area to go to next. The player can not bring everything from the previous area with them, and must choose what they think is important to travel with as they have limited cargo space. Some buildings are also mobile and can be taken along with the village, while others can not.  --------Thanks to the developer for giving me the opportunity to review the title, as well as anyone who took this review into consideration, I hope it helped.

_childDocuments_.review: I was positively surprised.Pros:- Cool worldbuilding. I rarely read flavour-text in games, but I did here. Both the world itself and the culture you play as are interesting.- Loved the nomad theme. Being able to build more expensive versions of buildings that you can bring with you to the next area and taming wild beasts to join your caravan really made it feel like I was on a journey, and not just choosing encounters from a node-map.- With indivudual character levels in every profession, a tech tree, structure upgrades and traits this game had far more strategic depth than I thought.Cons:- Even though there are many different forms of progression, it still feels like every individual researches, upgrades or levels don't affect your survival chances enough. What makes and breakes you are all the small turn-to-turn decisions. In the end, a full run felt less like the typical roguelike experience of gradually specializing and improving a build, and more like a series of disconnected challenges where you hope to clear four in a row.- On the same note, there are quite a few things you have to consider for optimal efficiency that feels more like a chore. Not interrupting pupils mid-action, always gathering each resource with the same pupil to level them up more efficiently, calculating how much space you'll have when you leave and how many resources you can bring with you, always adjust move-targets so that pupils can potentially move their full range into fog, etc.- My first two runs were ended by the random ruin-events. I know you can scout the events once you get high-level druids and I presume that I was just extremely unlucky, but the fact that an event could just remove every piece of a resource from the map when I needed that specific resource to proceed is just bad game-design. In addition, basically all positive effects I've gotten has been useless to me at that point in time (negating damage at a level where I won't be taking any, adding turns when I won't use them, etc). This would be a lot better and much more engaging by simply letting the player choose between a set of three, but the system could probably benefit from a complete overhaul.I am leaving a positive review even if my time with the game thus far has been somewhat frustrating because I really appreciate the unique idea, and intend to play further :)Edit:Okay, lost one more run to RNG. I have victory secured, and then an event adds an additional  victory requirement that is mathematically unachievable due to the scarce resources on the map. Is this really just bad luck?? This turns into a thumbs down for me.

_childDocuments_.review: The 4X strategy combined with a roguelike is definitely interesting, and is worth your time to take a look, but it's hard to say it has a satisfying payoff. The initial pastel colors got old pretty fast, but once I discovered "dark mode" (F5) I switched and it was much more pleasing to the eyes. I encountered no bugs or blips or bloops but I also wasn't deeply engaged either. It seems a cool game for those you like the idea of a 4X strategy mashed with a roguelike, but it ultimately sum of its parts didn't gel for me. I recognize why some people will like this game and that's why I recommend it, but I'm not sure I will come back to it after the time I've already spent.

_childDocuments_.review: Why is everyone complaining about the game when the campaign step by step clearly instructs you about how the game works?  Is it because of the natural disasters?  Is it the Aura effects?  I haven't played a game myself but I've played the campaign and I understand all the mechanics.  When you can see -everything- you're going to need and what the places you're going to have to offer, clearly you can just plan for the future.I'll see how it is after a couple of proper playthroughs of the 'main game' but I fail to understand the issue atm.  I'll obviously change my review if I figure out what this beef with RNG is.Edit: I have played a couple games now and yet I can see everywhere the mistakes I'm personally making.  I didn't have enough rations because I didn't place a pupil near a food source/the caravan too far from pepkins.I would have enough stone if I prepared for it at the last halt.If I had accepted that extra pupil, I would have had another body to help maximize production.But let's be real: you can't prepare for everything so you have to prepare for everything else possible.  And I usually make it out of the starting Halt.I'll continue to update this as I play and if I see no progress I'll start to question the severity of standard game mode.Edit 2: I am making more progress with each and every game.  Founding out I could reset my map by pressing F2 made hunting for good halts and cheap journey requirements significantly easier.  Having just completed my first game that reached 450+ turns total and losing it due to running out of a steady food supply to keep my FIVE pupils sustained, it's becoming more and more clear that the RNG -is in fact- able to be overcome.I'll likely continue this update and with only 4 hours left in the same, I don't know how much it helps to know but... at a pricepoint of 10/15 dollars?  This game is worth the cost of admission.  It's a solid little 4X experience with an amazing aesthetic value, a steep learning curve and very rewarding successes in either pushing forward or amazing trait (positive buff) roll, I've had a good experience for the 20 hours I've sunk into this, failures included.

_childDocuments_.review: if your favorite part of resource management / builder games is starting a new game, then this is perfect! it's like a cuddly cross between Frostpunk and Niche, but with added layers of meta-progression inspired by the roguelike genre. it's definitely an acquired taste for sure, like scotch or anchovies. if you're broken like me though, then this is a real gem!some notes on usability:--navigating around the menus can be cumbersome at times, and most failure states don't have an alert--e.g. when a worker is stuck waiting on resources, or you're running dangerously low on food. --coming from games like Cities Skylines and Oxygen Not Included, I found AFATE's lack of graphs distressing. besides being a lot of fun (i know, i'm broken), the data viz in those games helped me explore the complex systems and learn how they work.--the game is overly reliant on diegetic tells. i love the attention to detail, but without adequate overt messaging to back it up, it took me nearly 4 hours to notice that, for example, the balloons attached to the characters change color to indicate their current status.--while beautiful, the game is not super legible. i often struggled to see where my workers were and which workers were which, or tell the difference between jungle and forest. (again, some data viz would be great here--really miss the color-coded overlays available in most games like this that let you see the status of different units, resources, spaces, etc at a glance!)

Forcing random results taking control of your path and choice away from you.Normally with weird choices like that i would fall back on the story, but its so flighty and garbage they basically pre tell you the story and let you jump into it starting at whatever chapter you want.The writing is terrible, the premise is dumb, all the game play choices i encountered were bad or boring one after another, the music I heard i wanted to instantly mute, the controls some how despite being simple are needlessly clunky with double binds of camera and movement on right mouse click, and the visuals at game play distance look terrible. the only thing that is good in this whole game stepping through the door for the moment i did is the colour palette is pleasant and well unified.Got it in a pack so im only out 4 bucks but uhg, another for the hidden list.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately I can't say that this is a bad game. It's interesting, you start with a few workers, you need to gather resources to advance to the next level meanwhile you need to feed these little s**ts who eat A LOT. One can't produce enough, but if you put two to gather food, you can't gather the other resources you need to advance. Oh and the funny part is that the resources are limited AND the time (the number of turns you have) is ALSO limited. Oh and if it's not enough the dear mother nature also wants to f** you in the a** by sending sickness, storms, fire and other nice things. If you are not the person who spend 10-15 minutes in each turn to optimize the things, you are not a patient one or you get angry very easily, then I don't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Art is beautiful- Concept/lore is special - this + the solid artwork tells me someone put a lot of love into this.- mechanics are creative, I enjoy the way your workers (Pupils) can switch jobs get better. Not the most novel thing in the world, but I've always enjoyed that kind of mechanic!Cons, and the reason I can't recommend this:- way too hard. The tutorial ("Campaign") does a nice job of teaching you the mechanics. What it does NOT prepare you for is the way everything will spontaneously fall apart. I don't know whether the "Vagaries" (negative events) come too often, or what, but at this point I'm uninstalling and writing this review after the 4th or 5th aborted attempted to complete even a single run. In all cases I never made it farther than halfway, and in all cases, things went from "going great" to "complete collapse" in an eyeblink.I can't imagine it's intended to be this hard, given the variety of starting Tribes, but after 5 attempts not even getting halfway, and thus I STILL don't know what you unlock and get to build upon with each completion... _childDocuments_.review: and now onto the short review//Description//As Far as the Eye is a rouge-like turnbased management game. In a world that is flooding, you must guide your Pupils to the Eye or the center of the universe where procedurally generated worlds will give you paths to get to it with a plethora of challenges ahead. Will you reach the promiseland? Or will you perish? //Graphics, Sound & Artstyle//Everything about AFATE is articulated in a very cutesy cartoony style, I love it! the sounds & music only bring the atmoshphere together masking it's difficulty with adorable. //Gameplay//AFATE is a very complex game at first glance, it's deep building mechanics, character wheel and largely RNG worlds seemed intimidating to me at first but after playing  the campaign which acts more like a tutorial I felt I was ready to get to the Eye. Each journey has you controlling a limited amount of Pupils and with every action or harvest they make, levels them up in the perspective field. Everything from foraging, to baking, building, making potions adds exp to their wheel. How you manage each trait is entirely up to strategy and RNG. In some instances you will need a Builder of a certain rank of a Herbalist or another. What you are given in each level can be used to advance in the world before your Turns run out and the flood buries the entire world in a watery grave.//Price//24.99 USD//How many hours estimated//I am about 7 hours into my gameplay, I have only gotten a land away from The Eye on the first campaign. I think about this game at night and reflect on my mistakes, learn from it like you would any good rougelike game. I can estimate me spending well over 35+ hours //Final Thoughts//As Far as the Eye is a very special game I hope is put on more people's radars. It's challenging, it's fun, whether or not you've played games in this genre- the campaign is enough to teach inexperienced players exactly what to do. One of my favorite aspects of the game is deciding what roles my Pupils will have as they also come with one strenght and one weakness; for example- you can have a Pupil that gains 20% more exp from every action they do but their downside could be they are unable to cook/bake. It adds a tantalizing micromanagement that only makes a run that much harder. Study points can also be used to improve your courier to either traverse a new world more easier or add more space to take resources to the next stage. RNG takes a huge role in everything and that could be for better or worse, there are places of interest that can grant you a blessing or a punishment, hexes that are locked and can only be unlocked by blessing a totem of nature to allow you to plow the land and random events usually resulting in something terrible happening to the land or your Pupils. In a playthrough I had nonstop fires that wiped out all jungles i used to cut wood from & was unable to continue other than to trade other resources in Marketplace for wood. It can be frustratingly unfair with no real upside other to add more challenge. AFATE, despite all its bugs & rng mechanics, can be tons of fun. I just wish they would iron out everything sometime during launch week- I am playing the beta so I expect them to anyways One of the worst offenders of the bugs is in campaign missions if you don't follow the text that you can make dissapear and never get back- you wont know what to do exactly despite you having enough resources to proceed to the next land making you restart the mission from the beginning.As far as the Eye certainly seems to be a niche game as I understand some people are not thrilled by RNG especially when the only way to advance sometimes is through a resource that is very limited on a stage. I am still recommending it based on my experience and my admiration for the artstyle plus replayability & my confidence that the devs will iron out the kinks in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: In its current state, this is an early access title. I really wish it would have been released to early access, and the price not quite so high, as I think I would have happily followed it to full release and been happier with the experience.It's very rough around the edges. Within the first 10 minutes of gameplay I was met with typos (the word onward is spelled wrong in one of the first 10 instruction messages) and events that would not trigger (during chapter 2, I was unable to get either pupil to gather resources, I must have taken "too long" to explore, as when I retried I was met with a message event that allowed me to do so, definitely didn't happen the first try and I was hard locked out of progressing). I think that the game does have some fantastic concepts and that the overall theme is well portrayed, but the UI is bland to the point of often being ugly with large SNES looking text boxes for small amounts of left-aligned text, the right click function to access the movement action has no transitional effect it just kind of pops up, characters and other objects overlap each other, and more like this. There are just a multitude of little things that really detract from the experience. And its a big deal with the price, I think if this game was 10 dollars, I wouldn't be so critical, at 5 dollars, I'd probably have stuck with it, but at 22.49 on SALE, I refunded. I may come back to it later but at this point my expectations are set pretty high, and I'd really like some polish to this experience if I'm going to give it a second shot.Side note, only bothering to give such criticism because I think it's worth it, I don't bother to review otherwise. Never fun to not say anything nice so I will say one: the music is excellent, this was nailed and really embodies the experience and two: like I said before with the themes, the aesthetic and immersive qualities attributed to this almost spiritual pilgrimage of the characters is done very, very well. The majority of the graphics are great, and suited nicely to the overall experience. But this is why little things like awful looking text boxes are so jarring. Not, in my opinion, good corners to cut, but lots of potential, so I guess we'll see!

_childDocuments_.review: As Far As The Eye is a handheld (Nintendo Switch)/console game that's seems somewhat out of place for Nintendo Switch due to the complexity of the game... remembering that Nintendo Switch gamers, who this is apparently aimed at, find Pokemon and Super Mario Bros to be extremely complex games.  And complicated this is... which I would normally welcome from any game but the way this is put together doesn't seem to "work", which for me seems like a great shame. One important note is that even though this is an amateur project, it does seem to be sincerely and genuinely made.  I couldn't find any flipped assets, plagiarism or any other kind of insincere actions from the developer, but unfortunately genuine intentions alone are not enough to produce a brilliant PC gaming experience.  In fact it's apparent a lot of work went into this and it's mostly professionally polished. The problem I found with this, aside from the price, which we'll get into later, is just the way it all fits together... or doesn't fit.  It's a bit like Civilization meets Slay the Spire.  And not all mashups are a great idea.  You sort of play a series of short hex based Civ games, but much more complex in many ways as you need to juggle the concept that your civilization (pupils et al) are nomadic, so you need to pack up and move on to the next (procgen) stage.  Just like Slay the Spire, you move between stages and you get punished hard by RNG as you go (a poor desgin decision that will certainly disenfranchise many gamers).  Really for me, while I welcome complexity, the game to me seemed painfully inaccessible... I wasn't motivated to try work out how to play and the tutorial was weak and unengaging.   The UI is cluttered but also badly designed (I have no idea what Switch players thought about this when it arrived on the intended platform).   It's just too hard to get into.  I think the whole game probably needs some re-work by a UI designer or something, but I'm not here to tell developers how to fix things, just tell gamers if things aren't great about a game.Another thing that bugged me, maybe a minor issue, but the colour palette for the game just seemed off.  Like they took sepia tones and oversaturated them to 11.   I kind of got a headache just looking at the map.   I hope that's not just me but it seems weird.   Civ V never gave me a headache like that. Another upside, the game does feature customisable controls and resolution, so at least some of the basic, minimum requirements have been met.  Unfortunately there's a number of other technical defects and shortcomings which contribute to the game being difficult to recommend to gamers.The game assets are far from bleeding edge, with lowish polygon counts and somewhat low resolution textures, making this look like it's at least 10 years old.  It's unclear why the developers weren't able to arrange high quality, high polygon count contemporary assets for the game, and also irrelevant... what matters is that this looks poor in comparison to more professionally produced games as a result of their decisions.Because this is designed for handheld/portable gaming appliances, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the low power handheld gaming appliances that the game was designed for.  These are unfortunate compromises and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was a second thought for the mobile game developers.  The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for low power handhelds forces upon a game.  While this might run well on a Steam Deck, we must remember the vast majority of gamers here are gaming on PC.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.So, should you buy this game?  Is this one of the best of the 100,000+ games on Steam?As Far As The Eye has the total ripoff price of $25 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.For comparison, the $25 asking price for this game could get you games like "Yakuza Kiwami", "The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt" or "Final Fantasy XIV Online".  Hundreds of quality, professionally made games like those are frequently on sale cheaper than this.Unfortunately Steam reviewers aren't presented with a "Maybe" option... if they did, that's what I'd choose.  This isn't a completely bad game, but it's also not one of the best.  As always, if you read my review and you can overlook the negatives I've called out, or they just aren't important to you, then by all means go ahead and buy this.

_childDocuments_.review: Do not get this as your first resource-management game.If you were in love with The Settlers 4 on iPhones back in the day, then this is it, but turn-based instead of an RTS, and the only "enemies" here are RNG, and the amount of turns left. It's an interesting mix of alarming resource management where every turn counts, dressed up in a calm "narrative" with simple graphics that fit its style. Hard to get into, but appealing for players who are willing to take the time to learn how everything works (I recommend doing this through the "play" function; the "campaign" is sort of a tutorial that might get boring). This game has its own flow, and even if prior experience in resource management games might help you get a general understanding, this game forces you to think differently to lean how to prioritise your moves with its harsh RNG.Someone mentioned that if you re-roll or reload saves to get a better outcome, this isn't for you. That is absolutely correct.

At some point, you are not able to harvest the needed ressources to move on. Some maps are generated without the needed resources to cross it, and it makes you start again and again praying that luck will help you to have what you need. But as failure makes your full colony die, it means you need to restart from scratch. Bringing some balance to the game would make it a great one (check that at maps generation it is possible to win; allow at least to use the market to compensate your ignorance about what you should have brought with you), but it seems this won't happen. Conclusion: you cannot rely on you abilities only to complete some runs. No more updates, whereas, if you are hooked, you will crave for it... I don't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: A very aesthetically pleasing little game and a solid city-builder. There are some mechanical issues - most notably, it feels really quite awkward that you're incentivized to collect as many resources as possible before leaving a zone (to gain XP on your dudes, which can be hugely valuable), but you're also penalised for gathering things you can't carry with you. The game can also be deceptively punishing at times, with negative events being very swingy - sometimes they'll absolutely hammer you, other times they'll do literally nothing (e.g. 'dudes crossing jungles become ill' - awful in a jungle biome, entirely irrelevant if you've deforested the map, and the game seems to make no attempt to weight one way or another).That said, while there are some issues, the game is relaxing enough and sufficiently stylistically pleasing to be worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to love this game so much, but honestly it just is an excercise in rage and frustration.  You'll move to an area where the objective to move forward will require a resource that doesn't exist in your area....guess your run is pretty doomed unless you can trade a TON of stuff to get it yourself.  You've gone down a path only to discover that later paths you couldn't see earlier need a ton of food/meat/grain?  You're basically screwed as those resources are constantly going down a ton as your villagers eat like locusts.  You've finally got a run where everything seems to be going perfectly?  A random bug will appear like your villagers dying of Hunger while they have over 200 rations in the camp.  Pity there's no way to save mid-run so all your progress is lost!  I want to like this game so much, its charming and cute and could be an interesting puzzle.  But dang does it just feel like bashing your head against a wall till the stars align and you get a doable run.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent game to advance your skills in management and dealing with crisis. Some vagaries are brutal and even those that arent can send you off course for enough turns for the next catastrophe to finish you off. I like the fact that if you remain focused you can develop your worker's skills and make it to THE EYE without too much stress. Besides being focused the game also requires you to understand the mechanics to produce surplus and that alone can take a few playthroughs.The graphics and sound wildly depends on your preferences. I must admit that for a small production the graphics are interesting, the music is calming and peaceful and the sound effects intriguing eventhough quite few (I think this was done intentionally). Overall, the game succeeds to transfer you into its own fantasy world.All in all, this is a medium (first column of difficulty) to hard (second column) game that will challenge, entertain and infuriate you in equal measure. If you are very nervous dont play this, as the moment when you have achieved your goals in the final turn and THE FLOOD simply washes the last half and up to four hours of play will drive you mad (this happened to me 8 times, I wonder if its excellent game design or my tremendous luck). I do reccomend it for ORIGINALITY, GOOD DEVELOPMENT, FUN GAMEPLAY (outrageous too), ADDICTIVE RPG ELEMENTS, REPLAYABILITY, ARTWORK.

_childDocuments_.review: Why I think this game's brilliant: - adds clear goals to what could be considered a turn based city builder - just recently I was reflecting on what I think good city builder games needed and it was clear win conditions.  This essentially has that - short halts (levels) means you can complete one in 20 mins which is a nice game lengthWhy I tear my hair out playing it: - random events can sometimes do you over (required resource not present enough in halt, random increased resources required for next halt, etc) - hard, but while I struggle with games without difficulty levels as I'm not that great, I've been able to get the hang of this ... key issue is no save spamming is possible - which I don't normally do - if you do, this will frustrate you.Overall: yeah, worth it, i reckon.  8/10. _childDocuments_.review: As Far As The Eye (or A FATE) is a cute resource managing game with a unique conceptYou're tasked to guide your tribe on a journey to the safe centre before floodwaters consume the land.Your small number of settlers have to move from 'halt' to 'halt' gathering resources to survive, build and move onward. There's a short campaign that acts as a tutorial which mostly explains the basics but the meat and potatoes is in the sandbox where you take a tribe (one from each of the four cardinal directions) on either a long or short trek.Definitely something that i'd like to see a sequel to.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game for those that like to replay scenarios, select different paths and try new approach. Great clear goals for each of the steps and you can choose paths to fit better your play style. I have been really looking for exactly this kind of game for a long long time. - Good tutorial that teaches basics, but does not reveal all, so even main game still has a lot of new things to discover. - Really love the balance/harmony focus - if you plunder, remove resources or leave "trash" behind, it affects not only final score, but also next steps in scenario by making them more difficult. So it's not about stockpiling to as much as you can, but really gathering only the stuff you need long term and planning many steps ahead. - Even on easy you can mess up, like focus on building and realize you have no food. No saves to go back to to avoid consequences (just this turn save), just start again and learn from mistakes. So much as real life!- Unlimited time, so perfect if you want to relax and not stress you need to pause or something will happen. - Packing puzzle - I had to remind myself to check more often if I don't make too much stuff and cannot take it with me and that I cannot spend an hour trying to pack everything perfectly and not have empty spaces. Real challenge there for hoarder players like me :)- Gentle music, and sounds that remind you about things.Small issues (personally for me, but lesson learned) - didn't find a good system yet to be able to recognize who specializes in what. Ribbons are fine but hard to see and easy to forget. So I ended up checking what is everyone doing and if they should be doing that or not, as it happened that I assigned them wrong. I didn't want to name them builder and so on. But, this is something to get used to and train memory too. And no warnings that this action will make them drop/loose item. And apparently trying to tell them no to go via specific hex but still go home to deliver, makes them drop stuff. Bit annoying if you want them to avoid mosquitoes by going around. So just no clicking around unless you know what you want to do.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: Cute. But that's all.It takes a lot of effort to learn this game, but it is not fun once you learned it. The game is very repetitive despite of its complicated system. And you can't really strategize when the game just hit you with an additional requirement of 750 of something you don't have in storage when there are 50 turns until the flood.And for some reason the game gives you achievements for unlocking stuffs
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: This is an fun roguelight colony/resource management sim. It's quick to learn but rewards thoughtful and creative play. It's a little light on variety of strategies that can be effective, and sometimes it's randomness can be frustrating (for example when you select a particular path only to find that you need a type & quantity of resources not available along that path), but there is a lot of strategy there to have fun with and figuring out how to get out of binds is what this type of game is all about. The pleasant soundtrack, cute graphics, and overall chill vibe blunt a lot (but not all) of the no-save, permadeath frustrations inherit in a game like this.It's a game I may put 100 hours into, but I'm unlikely to sink 100s. If you like the Civilization series or city colony building games, give it a try, especially if you can get it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: How can a game give such a big calming and chill vibes with this magnificent graphics and yet be so difficult?Even though I really love the idea of the game, I simply cannot give it a positive review as the difficulty makes it nearly impossible to get to the Eye and not die out of hunger, thunder or other occurrences. This should be truly adjusted accordingly, so the player does not have a constant feeling of demotivation and hopelessness.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: This is fun yet challenging little game. Sometimes you get good luck with locations, goals, and little dudes, and sometimes you can be having a very good run fall apart. I wish there was a way to upgrade things in between runs to keep some sort of progress but that could become too strong too fast. Very chill vibe and you can play at your own pace. Would recommend for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished with the tutorial at 4 hours (I died in tutorial). The tutorial was very well paced. The Creatures are cute and the animation is done well.This game is serious stuff. I tried my first game and I did so poorly I couldn't even stand to continue.10/10 would recommend for lovers of resource management games.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very fun game... when it works. _childDocuments_.review: Beautiful character and feature designs.   Even once you learn this game well it has a lot of replay value because of all the unique scenarios you find yourself in.  It isn't easy but rather than be discouraged when you fail, trying again feels like a fresh challenge I look forward too rather than a letdown I lost my last progress.

_childDocuments_.review: i love the design and the game play is quite unique, having lots of options and diversity, upgrades ectr. you can see theres lots of love to detail.HOWEVER!, having played lots of strategy/management/builder games, i find this game incredibly difficult to play! the interval of catastrophes is mortifying, the time pressure is stressing and i don't consider it fun, dying all the time without actually getting a good grip on properly upgrading/building your beast or pupils.the hexagons in total (even tho incredibly beautiful and detailed) seem quite cluttered, maybe making them somehow bigger or the resources smaller might help.overall its a beautiful game and id really love to play it, if there would somehow be an option for "easy". playing like this is just incredibly stressy.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! It's genuinely really cute and fun. My only problem is just how hard it is. I have played it for 11 hours and only managed to actually get to the eye once on a custom game and I love resource management games. It also can crush all of your hard work if you get to a place that does not have the resource that is necessary in the required amounts. But I do highly recommend the game!
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: As Far as The Eye is a very calming TBS strategy. Don’t get me wrong, it has a sense of urgency because you are racing against the clock and you not only have to support your tribe and gather necessary resources to advance to next location, but you also need to forward plan given the variety of locations you may need to complete before getting ‘home’. Despite this, the game aesthetics, music and animations are very relaxing. This is where the deception is, it relaxes you so much that you may miss important events or not pay close attention to resource management and well, lose.The only negative about the game is that it is slow paced and I often found myself a little bored after setting my base of operations and setting my resource managing approach. score 6.5/10 – calming and slow, but yet challenging at times TBS resource manager game.For more reviews and recommendations follow me as a curator at
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely game to have a relaxing game night. The graphics are nicely done and cute. The objectives are sometimes a bit random which make planning important maybe even very hard from time to time. The implementation of vagaries and traits for the pupils/characters is super nice. Recommend for a relaxing evening of fun gaming.Bonus: the music is super nice
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very fun game if you like strategy and adventure! One thing I love about this game is the jobs. All of the characters have the same jobs but the more they do them the better they get at them! That means that you could have one pupil (in-game villager name) do the cooking,one do the gathering, and one do the hunting/farming! This game has much growing room. So if you don't like how it is right now you might like it better If/when they update it!
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty hard to find a game that is genuinely challenging and fun every play though, but this is one of them. The campaign is short and to the point, showing you what you need to play the game. The actual game requires you balance planning ahead with over-exploiting resources or staying on a map too long, and provides a few different modes for different challenges. The game play actually feels well thought out and unique; I'd say definitely worth getting this one.

However, I played for 6 hours straight in the blink of an eye, and I realised people are probably just sad because they lost a couple of times (which I also did). _childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: AFATE is a tricky one for me to review and recommend. On one hand, there are definitely bugs, improvements to clarity and QoL which could be made, and the consensus that the development team is no longer working on it. While I wouldn't pay full price for this game in its' current state, I do absolutely enjoy the time I spend playing it. Sometimes RNG screws you over, sometimes it doesn't, but it still almost always feels like I have at least a fighting chance each run. While there are definitely some balance issues that CAN cause you to just helplessly go through your turns knowing that you won't survive that "level", I don't run into it too often. It's a gorgeous game with a very relaxing atmosphere... I just wish it were either more fleshed out or cheaper for having been abandoned.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great little game. Love the idea of a bite-size city builder/resource management sim that doesn't have to take over your life for a single 50-hour playthrough. Also a nice re-purposing of the "Slay the Spire" style branching paths procedurally generated map for each run. And it's all wound into a nice story that really fits the mechanics and theme. Well done to the developers. Really like this one; holds up much better than Banners of Ruin.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: It's a different kind of resource management sim where you play the wind instructing a bunch of "pupils". It's incredibly complex despite how it looks. The art is incredible and I love the character designs. I think it's a very clever game with interesting mechanics. The game itself is difficult - I haven't yet won a single game outside of the Campaign - but very fun. I keep wanting to come back and redo the matches to see if I could fare better the next time. I would highly recommend this.Updated review after playing more than 13 hours... I've played over 13 hours of this game and I haven't won a single game... It took me so many tries to get the campaigns done as well. I almost always get to halt 3 of 4 and die because there's just too many resources to get and not enough pupils or food to get them all... Since the maps are randomly generated, sometimes I find that there aren't enough resources in the halt for the required amount! The RNG is brutal and the unwinnable a lot of the times. The crazy thing is how I keep trying over and over with hopes that maybe this time I'll win... No such luck yet.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: I started playing this game as if it was some sort of rogue-like turn based rts. I could not be more wrong and that stressed me out.The moment when I start chilling, focusing on small tasks and just gathering enough for the travel to the next node along the path and the health of my caravan was when I started enjoying the game.Don't get me wrong, the game is challenging, but not in a sense that you must min-max everything or that you must be Creed's Tactical Genius.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun little game. I conveys its atmosphere very well and makes for a fun afternoon playthrough. I do have some issues with it which shall follow:It excels at 4-6 Colonists and kinda falls apart beyond that, since the objectives become trivial. I originally couldn't understand why it doesn't have an endless mode, but that is probably the reason. Sadly there are also many sytems that seem superfluos, namely the council and the workshop. _childDocuments_.review: It is a surprisingly addictive game with a pleasant mix of city building, survival, rougelike and RPG mechanics. While all the pupils can work in any field, you should level up and customize their skill sets to maximize their potential according to their traits. It is also a management game: your survival is at risk if you don't have enough resources and you will be punished for wasting resources.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: Quite a unique strategy game, plays like turn-based Settlers with rogue-like and survival elements. It looks cute, but it'll kick your ass - it's *very* challenging if you play it as it is designed. There is a "custom game" option which lets you turn off some of the more difficult mechanics, so you can use that for a milder learning curve. But if you play with everything enabled it's quite elaborate and requires you to understand and master a lot of different mechanics.What brings the game down in my opinion is the lack of consistency - the difference in difficulty between runs can be very big, because of the intersection of a lot of random and procedural mechanics. Generally, with good management and foresight you can overcome anything, but sometimes it's just down right unfair. Also I feel like the replayability could have been higher.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: This game is solid, and surprisingly difficult (at least in my opinion).It has a peaceful, calm and gentle aesthetic and vibe which lull'd me into a false sense of security. It took me until my fifth try to complete a game on the most basic settings. I wasn't able to beat the 4th campaign mission yet either, though I may try again.The premise is simple enough: you are a disembodied divine influence called "The Sigh," almost a benevolent wind god. Every so often, the world is flooded and its residents, pupils, must flee to the only place safe from the flood - The Eye.The gameplay is  a resource and villager management game with exploration and risk-reward components. You control a caravan of pupils on their way to the sigh, but the trip takes place in parts called "halts," which are effectively maps of varying sizes and biomes where you set up to gather resources needed to make progress on your journey. Going from one halt to the next has certain requirements, like resources or pupils leveled up in certain professions. While it sounds simple, there is a lot of nuance. Balancing the constant demands on wood, food, housing, medicine and other resources is more challenging that it first appears. Also, your final score (and extra challenges along the way) are impacted by how much you waste. Your storage going from halt to halt is limited, you can expand it in a number of ways but these are fairly costly and sometimes complicated.The other big challenge is that, in addition to the time limit on each halt before the flood catches up and overtakes you (killing everyone, or 'returning them to the sigh' more kindly as they put it), there are auras and vagaries. Auras are places that restrict your ability to collect resources unless you 'calm' them. Calming them, except with a specialized character, is temporary and has to be repeated. Vagaries are random events that do all sorts of bad things; minor vagaries come up many times, and have usually very specific moderate effects that can sometimes be avoided. Major vagaries, though, are often the real challenge. Say you have 200 turns 'til your halt floods - well, probably 30 or so turns before that, a major vagary will kick in. These also run the gammut in variety of effects, but most are pretty damning. In some cases, if you don't leave before they kick in you may die from them fairly quickly.All in all, I give it a solid thumbs up, with the caveat that it may not be quite as easy or relaxed as it appears.EDIT: I went back and retried the final campaign mission after having beaten one playthrough with the first unlocked tribe (presumably the easiest) - it was much easier to complete with the knowledge I gained from that success, and the many failures that enabled it. 9 / 10
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

It's very hard to tell what's going on and what each of your characters is doing. Important actions are buried in different kinds of menus. _childDocuments_.review: I played roughly 27 hours, and from my in game experience this game is HARD AF, and not in a fun way.My biggest problem comes from the random quirks, the positive quirks are meh, but the negatives one are just straight out crippling, I can't even get rid of that one pupil who had like 4 bad quirks on them.Resource managing is also hard in this game, basically you need EVERY resource to just be able to build and get that one building. When you are unlucky, that iron you need might be ten tiles away from the tile you settled, and to be able to get that iron 20 turns had already passed.And why is stone an iron needs different building, this makes absolutely zero sense.The world effects are also kinda meh, all bad no good, most of the time it doesn't even matter. If you are paying attention, most of the events can be easily avoided by make you pupil taking a rest or go to other tiles for a round. It just so uninspiring and boring, all and all just another strategy the devs make to waste your turns, might as well make every event into rising waters.And please make the pupils animation faster, or just give us an option to cancel their transform animation, I felt like spending so much time just waiting them for them to change their clothes.Last but not least, the UI is just... HORRIBLE, why is there no easy way to checkout what are my pupils stat and what are they doing at the moment? Why do I always have to check on them one by one? Is this some kind of statement? I kinda feel like tons of 4X game already master the art of relaying information, games like civ 6 has tons of resource and stuff to manage and its still doing a better job then this game.There are still some great things going on though, the art and music are pretty good. I really thought I will have a good time playing this at first, but for me it quickly become just a rage playing game, I try to quit it but my frail ego needs to beat this damn thing, its even worse than Dark Souls cause  those pupils just NEED to change those masks and costumes and you can NOT skip them or you might get their lazy ass rest for one turn
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: Not for the faint of heart.The Tutorials aren't the best and it is possible to fail them easily (took me 4 attempts at Tutorial 4 but I managed 1-3 and 5 on my first go).I've seen comments on the 2nd tutorial that you run out of stone before you gather the 100 needed to progress.  Don't panic!  The character that mines the last of the stone will hold it in their hands for a turn or 2 while walking back to the quarry.  As long as you leave the character alone, it will take the resources back to base.  Tip for the whole game, not just the tutorial: if a character is "Returning Resources" DO NOT give them any instructions.  This is said in tutorial 1 but is easily missed.  This is especially true for rare resources (like the Rhinofallows).A FATE is tricky to learn, difficult to master and impossible to predict.  For example, more than once I've said to myself, "it will take me exactly 15 turns to get enough fish to progress," only for a vagary (minor negative event) to come along and stop my fisher(s) from working for 10 turns, thus taking 25 turns when I only had 24 available.9/10, my failures are my own, normally I've gotten too greedy, too impaitent or took my eye off the ball and didn't leave enough time to plan.  3/10 I've failed due to chance.  And yes, those numbers are correct.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I got the came through Humble, so far cheaper than the normal purchase price on steam. For that price, I 100% recommend the game. For the normal purchase price, you have to know what you're getting into, but for certain gamers could still be worth it.It's a roguelike cross between Civ, and FTL. It is HARD, but once you've completed the "Campaign" (really just a poorly named tutorial) and take a few stabs at the normal game, you start to get the hang of resource management/prioritization, and route planning. There is a lot of replayability, with all the different ways each playthrough can go, you have to learn to adapt to all the different biomes, vaguaries, positive and negative traits, etc. It can be very rewarding to complete the game in the face of some of these adversities.That said, I agree with some of the negative reviews that the UI and interface need some QOL improvements. I didn't find these issues as game-breaking as most reviewers seem to paint them though. If you like the game, you'll like it in spite of these issues. If you dislike the game, fixing these probably won't change the game enough to swing your vote. Given that the game has been out for a year now, I wouldn't anticipate these fixes ever coming, unfortunately.TLDR: If you like roguelikes, and FTL/Civilization, get the game on sale or through humble.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: As Far As The Eye short review: Agricola meets FTL with Miyazaki aesthetics.There aren't many computer games I feel the urge to tell people about. But this game... this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game. It is precision aimed to target me, specifically, as its market. Since picking it up 3/4 days ago, Steam tells me I have sunk almost 24 hours into it already. The first night, I was up until 7.30am the next day. It has sunk its claws into my brain and it will not. let. go.It is a resource management/action economy game about cute little spirits going on a migration across their little spirit world to evade a flood. Depending on tribe, you'll have slightly different start and play conditions, but you have to feed your little people, they level up in skill efficiency the more they do of a particular role (of which there are like 7 main roles and a number of specialisations off that), and you always need more of everything.With the 24 hour playtime, I've managed to win just 3 times - on easy maps. Starvation or flooding are constant pressures, with random events sometimes popping up in the last few turns of a go completely skewing your chances - but even then, they don't feel particularly unfair, 'cos there is so much replay with procedurally generated maps, randomised starting traits, and different objectives at each map on how to proceed.Even the inventory mini-game is enjoyable! You have a finite amount of space to carry resources into the next map, and each of the resources take a different shape for fitting together. You can spend some of your resources to upgrade the amount you can carry, at the opportunity cost of not being able to make your caravan more efficient in other ways, or to save those resources in case of needing them for objectives, or to spend on expensive tribe-wide upgrades... Some of the buildings you need to harvest resources can be carried as well, and they're all irritating, irregular shapes that need to be worked around. But there is an INCREDIBLE sense of satisfaction in getting the inventory screen 100% efficiently packed.Yeah, so, if all of that sounds like the exact thing that will consume you completely, all I can say is: BE WARNED. It turns out that people need sleep.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: fun but this is too hard for my small brainEdit: Ya know, after the 5 tutorial campaigns, I've spent 4 more hours trying to beat what's after that. It's actually disappointing of how many times I've almost made it to the eye, yet there I am losing everything I built up because of some stupid RNG causation.I still remember my first attempt where Auras spawned right next to each other and I couldn't manage simultaneously soothing them, collecting resources, and keeping my little guys fed for the night. I really loved everything in the game except playing the game itself. The character designs, cutesy little buildings that I create, the creatures and dungeons... but just playing the game takes a lot of worthless perseverance and that wasn't what I was looking for when I bought the game.tl;dr: I liked how the game looks, playing it through my 8.7 hours (as of writing this) was more of a time waster more than anything. I feel as if I'm just stupid and that I'm not comprehending anything, but other reviews seem to solidify that maybe I'm not stupid. It would take someone who is a very smart tactition to maybe beat this game (spoiler alert, I'm not that guy).It's like Loki trying to fix all the alternate timelines that branch off the sacred timeline, you can't. It's impossible, and im pretty sure that's what developing this game felt like to the developers.
