_childDocuments_.review: Watch some playthrough, make sure you know what you're getting into. As long as you come in prepared this is pretty great, like a nonviolent distilled version of the early turns of civilization mixed with ftl. Got this through humble so can't comment on price/value but I'm enjoying it and thought I'd throw in a positive review.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: A randomly generated journey game where you travel from location to location, gathering enough resources so that your tribe can journey to a safe location called the Eye before an apocalyptic flood overtakes the planet. Your characters will level up on your journey and specialize in certain roles, you can build buildings to speed up collection or collect or make things you couldn't otherwise, and you can trade and interact with ancient ruins. It's a neat idea, but it's missing something that is making it difficult for me to get into. The transition from beating the tutorial missions into a full playthrough requires you to come to grips with the higher tiers of food and resource production, and something about the interface and managing your little tribesman is such a headache that I'm not really interested in investing the time I'd need to do that. Basically it feels like good ideas, messily implemented.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game. Really nice artstyle and music. The mechanics are unique and challenging, It is an easy to learn - hard to master kind of game. The tutorial does a good job of explaining the basics, and I found it fun to explore strategies by myself after that.As some people have said, it can be "unfair", for example sometimes there's just not enough resources on the map of the kind you need to proceed. It doesn't happen very often tho, and most of the time you can prevent it by good planning. While the balancing can be unforgiving it doesn't ruin the game for me.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: You have a tribe of a few workers and you have to bring them through couple of halts (nodes) to the end of their journey for which you need resources. You need to consider the biomes of the nodes, and plan your workers' skills. It also has beautiful graphics, and calming sounds. What I particularly like about this game is how short one game lasts for a resource management game. Instead of long-term planning and playing for tens of hours, you get a quick game of optimization and resource management, one run lasts about ~1 hour for me. Game runs really well on Linux, I personally had no problems running it on two machines.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game! The graphics, music, and narrative make it FEEL like a "cozy game" but it's way more challenging than expected.Every time I lost a run, I was excited to try again immediately. Every time you play, it's a different experience. You could get bad or lucky rolls (in terms of the map, character traits, random events, etc)--which makes it super addicting. Gameplay aside, this game is just so beautiful and immersive.I ran into a couple tutorial bugs (had to restart once because of a stuck prompt), but other than that, it's been smooth. I'm sad it seems like a short game.. I'll probably finish all the challenges this weekend. I want MORE. :) Highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: A FATE is a pretty roguelike where you guide a nomadic tribe away from the rising water. The basic mechanisms are easy to get, but gathering food and the resources you need is a hard and fun challenge. However, its greatest downside is the severely punishing random events that much too often cripple you beyond repair - at which point you lose, not because you didn't git gud, but because random disasters are too punishing. I recommend it, as it's fun, interesting and hard, but you'll have to consider how disappointed you'll be when your tribe dies because of randomness, especially on a long journey.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: 1) There's a lot to like about this game! It's a cute world with nice, but simple backstory. The traveling caravan mechanic works very well. The game has a pretty unique feel and flavor. In the world of so many ripoffs and copycats, this stands out!2) This really feels to me like a spiritual successor to FTL (Faster Than Light). This means it's HARD! And you're often at the mercy of RNG. It doesn't mean the game is random, it just means if you don't know how to adapt (or how to prepare), you're going to have a bad time. Again and again. Until you get better. (I'm nowhere near as good as I'd like to be yet.)3) Even though this game is not Early Access, I'd say by its quality that it should be so. If you come in with that expectation, you won't be surprised. (E.g. Buggy UI on Mac OS X basically forces you to play in a windowed mode. The tutorial sometimes gets into weird states.)But yeah, this game is pretty hard. There was one training mission I have failed a few times. But it's satisfying to go back to it and optimize your build orders + resource priority until you get it right (and with time to spare!).On the first "real" mission, I failed because I ended up in a canyon with low forest (that quickly got destroyed by fires) and 2 out of 3 available fish sources were "golden" which meant I couldn't use them. (Devs, if you're reading it, I'd make the golden resources still usable as normal.) So I couldn't collect the required amount of fish (and I couldn't try to go to another halt, since that would require constructing things with wood). Anyway, now I know to be careful about these things in the canyon.I hope as I get better at the game, I'll get more fun out of adapting to various situations + exploring different strategies. (Just like with FTL.)My top asks from devs right now:1. Fix UI problems with Mac OS2. When you travel to the next place and arrange your resources, save that placement even if you decide not to travel. And also reuse item placement when you travel from the next halt onwards.3. Sometimes a halt simply doesn't have enough resources to do one of the paths. This should be fixed.4. It's hard to remember all the different halt types (e.g. that canyon doesn't have many forests). It would be nice if when you hover over a halt it showed the amount of resources that will be there (even if it's approximate or a range).5. The map doesn't always reflect the game state. E.g. during Earthquake, the birds are still around making you think you can hunt them.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very tentative yes. Yes, dying due to a single mistake is part of a roguelike. But fighting the UI and the controls isn't, and neither are presenting false choices.The terrain types aren't balanced; there's not really much point in the branching map when there's almost always a clear path to the finish that is dictated purely by food supply. Even with an assload of upgrades there is only so much food you can take with you. The late game is nonexistent; it's either "did I pick the route that lets me skip halts" or "am I stuck somewhere without food and just lose?"It's a very unique game but for your own sanity don't play it on the higher difficulties.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: This game can be incredibly difficult as far as food management at times. You forget about it for a moment and you're dead, even if you've invested 45 minutes into these kiddos. That aside, it is an incredibly fun game if you like survival elements or strategy games. There isn't a whole lot of content, it feels like, but it seriously takes a lot of time to complete each milestone and unlock the next tier. Its a very cute game with a nice atmosphere. I'm dumb af, so most probably won't have as much trouble as I.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: Its cute and challenging, occasionally a bit frustrating. Theres something slightly off in the mechanics that hinders game play, but I cant put my finger on it. Its not incredible but I am having fun and I would purchase again. One thing that I would change is the ability to restart with the same pupils (if defeated restart the journey with the same pupils, but new map).
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: Very unforgiving game. Maybe I'm not playing enough ressource planning games to finesse my way through this one but i found myself frustrated at the randomness of it all almost everytime i played. Sometimes the generated maps don't even have enough resources for you to level up a certain skill you need to progress, or theres a vagrancy that wrecks your entire progress last minute. Both situations are essentially softlocks and both happened multiple times. Also if you don't dedicate one unit to constantly produce food you're also not gonna go far. So that little pupil is for the most part useless. As long as the vagrancies and resource spawning don't get balanced I can't really recommend this one.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: I probably won't be playing this game much, I gave it a few hours and I did really enjoy the game play and the pacing, so much so that I decided not to ask for a refund so I can support its makers. However, it just isn't really my type of game. You won't like this game if you like other rogue-lite casual games like Spiral and FTL. You WILL like this game if you are interested in something more casual and imaginative, with a touch of strategy that might be more challenging than initially thought. If you're considering, I urge you to at least try it and play through the first few 'tutorials'. This game was clearly made with love and it shows.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun little game. Your goal is to guide spirits (or pupils) across a map to The Eye, where they can be safe from the rising waters. You stay in areas (or halts) and manage your resources on this map, such as collecting stone, wood, spices and food. Your pupils can level up and become more competent in certain tasks. To get to the next halt, a list of resources are required. To move between each halt you choose what resources to bring by packing it on your caravan. However, if you leave resources behind then the amount of bad events (e.g. buildings being damaged or resources being reduced) increases. So you have to be mindful to only take what you need. Rinse and repeat until you get to the eye.My only bugbear with it at the moment is sometimes the randomness is too random. For example, I managed to travel to a halt and I looked at the requirement of the next (and only) halt to find I needed 900 spices. I load up the map I was on and found that only 250 spices were in the wild. I could trade for spices but required a large amount of another source. I noticed there were an abundance of fishes, so I set 4 pupils to fishing and 2 on keeping the tribe alive with food. I spent 100 turns (most of the halt duration) buying spices (I gained about 500) and I never managed to get it. So I felt like I was set up to fail from that point.I'm a spiritual person and I found I enjoyed the spiritual aspect of it. You play the role of the wind whispering suggestions into your pupils, who are also spirits that morph when performing certain jobs.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: Although this game is fun and challenging, it is repetitious.  I realize that in a custom game you can tweak the setup, but overall it is generally the same. The environments you create are different as the amount of pupils you want in your caravan, but know that a caravan can only house 3 workers and then you have to build a camp. The amount of jumps you create until you get to the eye are different and random benefits or disasters along the way are interesting but overall you strive for the same goal-to get to the eye. After a while, there was no other goal, no additional quests, so I decided at that point, to stop playing. But, for a while it was interesting. I did enjoy and finish the campaign.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine an FTL like race to the end where each encounter is a quick game of civilization with a dash of resident evil style inventory management that ensures you're never too comfortable in your race. At time of writing there are patches rolling out for balance, which are sorely needed. You can make relatively informed decisions of upcoming encounters well in advance but there are a few random events that can force you into a no win scenario. One screw up can destroy the house of cards that is your caravan and most of them won't land in your hat. For what it's worth I never found a loss frustrating enough to stop, and it's quite easy to reload and try again.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game, but I can't recommend it.  It's simply too easy to starve to death by mistake.  The amount of food you have remaining is not always obvious. It becomes obvious once you start taking starvation damage, but by then it's often too late. Give me an 'X turns of food in stock' indicator that's clearly visible, or maybe just make it so that I can see what my guys are doing (and whether the kitchen actually has ingredients and fuel available) without having to click on each of them, and I'll happily recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: The game is gorgeous, has a novel concept, and a good game system, but it's stupidly difficult for no good reason. There's no ability to change difficulty settings, and if you don't understand some core mechanic (which I clearly haven't yet figured out after almost 12 hrs of gameplay) you just die over and over and over. This game is marketed as "relaxing," because the devs want to laugh at your pain. Do not buy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: Adorable resource management game that will kick your ass if you don't plan ahead and watch the food number like a toddler heading for a wall socket. I love getting my characters better at better at their skills until they can chop hella trees, build amazing buildings in zero time, save everyone from starvation in a frenzied cooking spree, but if you take your eye off the food number, don't notice a bad vaguery, or don't pay attention to the road ahead, you will die. This game can be frustrating, but it's wonderful when you make it through. There's unfortunately some things that are unclear in the UI or never spelled out that you end up figuring out only through failed journeys. Despite that, I'm still a fan.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: Great Game tons of fun!!!!  Amazing design, beautiful, so much fun!!!  I love how the different paths work and how the different resources are all connected ect.A few suggestions:Please fix up the UI.  I am constantly sending the wrong guy to do tasks.  which guy is highlighted is hard to see and their paths are also hard to see.  Also, after selecting a guy from the trades menu then leaving the menu, I can’t see who is actually highlighted.I would also love to see a flip of the trades leveling path.  For example, in the fishing path, the net power is neat and fun and I want to get it and try it out, but it takes so long to get there that I barely get to try it out on a long campaign.  Putting the fun powers at level 4 could be a lot more fun.Adding another path for the druid, it can have extra knowledge, healing, faster potion making, and the ability to harvest without a building.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: Typically I do not play turned based games but I got this one as a birthday gift. I had it on my wishlist for a while just because I loved the way it looked. I am not disappointed. It is beautifully created and the attention to detail is on point.  Don't get me wrong, it isn't just a game that looks pretty and has chill, relaxing music; it is still a strategy game that takes planning.   If you want a chill feeling game that still provides a challenge, I would recommend this game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: I received this game as a gift. It's actually not my kind of game but I always pay my respects when someone offers me a game.This is quite a relaxing game, especially the campaign which is a glorified tutorial and the four "missions" on what seems to be Normal mode difficulty.The graphics are simple and colorful, the music is quite soothing and hearing the Sigh whispering to your Pupils is quite enjoyable.These elements along the turn based game design makes for a peaceful setting, which is enjoyable.Until you realise that this game isn't as friendly as it first seems. As soon as you get out of the campaign, you realise how much of a tutorial it was. Now you have to deal with pupils that have flaws, the random events are quite punishing and the random generations of the tiles will show you what true despair is at times.While the randomisation of each mission, team members, tiles, and events are all great at making the game experience last forever, it will mostly screw you over when you enter what seems to be Hard Mode.You can always play Normal mode, or setup your own custom game still using the random generation, which makes for an enjoyable experience. But getting into a harder difficulty you'll realise that the base you start with often has something bad, special rules for this difficulty only.The smallest mistake, the tiniest oversight will make you waste a turn. In this desperate setup it will make the difference between victory and defeat.Even when facing such difficulty the game is still fun it even gets thrilling, but extremely frustrating in this area where the game isn't bug free. Under special circumstances, your pupils may waste a turn waiting for no reason while they should be able to run. Sometimes having too many bonuses on harvesting speed can result in slower harvesting. All the pupils look alike, and sometimes the randomly generated name is the same as one pupil you already have in your team.Not a big deal, until the flow of your plan gets disrupted by the game auto-selecting another pupil which stopped working. All fine except the camera doesn't pan toward it on its own, so it's your job to pay attention to that and many many other things which will come your way.All missions were first relaxing, then challenging, and lastly rewarding. Except the very last one.That one is not only the hardest you might get but also extremely frustrating,  I'd say this is the only mission where I thought I couldn't win if I wasn't given a good team from the start. But it would be harsh to judge the whole game based on that one mission...Even if you will spend alot of hours on it.I think I would recommend it as a curious experience to share around. It's really strange that this game can both be extremely relaxing and suddenly quite stressful, where all hell break lose. I dig the contrast it offers there. The fact I usually dislike this genre and still wanted to recommend it should give you a hint.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: There's not a lot of between-run progression here, but the idea of a civilization-builder roguelike is great, the implementation keeps me coming back for more runs, and the graphic design is absolutely adorable.Nominated for the "sit back and chill" award, because the style and the whisper of wind are both going for it, and as long as you set yourself up well in the first map, cleaning up and moving on to the end of the journey can be very relaxing.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: Overall good game. A Couple of bugs here and there but nothing game breaking.Hard difficulty but the new update made it much more newbie friendly while keeping the same level of difficulty. If you like strategy and games and turn based game, this game is for you otherwise forge yourself an opinion first by watching streams or videos because this game is not for everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: Leading with the likes: It's a rogue like that has meaningful decisions and often requires adaptable strategies. It is difficult to just use one strategy and try to win each game and the changes to each map and requirement can make it challenging.  It is aesthetically pleasing, the maps are gorgeous and the music and sounds really match the artistic feel of the game.Dislikes: Sometimes the vagaries can be absolutely damning to a run and make it quite literally impossible. It feels frustrating to reach the final level only to get a 'damaged path' where there are literally not enough resources on the map to complete it in time. Similarly some of the negative traits are really just unplayable. Particularly those that cost a character health every turn it basically just means you'll be down one player.   The last thing would be that there is no long term progression, even if it is a rogue like. The only meaningful long term progression is unlocking more randomly rolled traits. It would be nice if there was something more long term, and also more options than just the four paths long/short.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: This one is total gem. A really hard strategy survival sim which is definitely not for faint hearts. You got 3 nature loving pupils and a caravan at the beginning. Music is cool, graphics are cute, sound effects are chill, but that's just an illusion. You got limited turn, unforgiving maps and RNG based harsh events to survive. Your pupils gains experience through actions and there's no limit what they can become. While their values getting higher and higher their loss will be that much painful too. Maps are roguelite it's random every time so you repeat value is great. But due to RNG you may get some terrible terrible map and events and miserably fail at your last map before the eye. Every turn is precious and every precaution you plan may save your entire run in next maps. Honestly i played few hundreds of strategy, sim etc. titles but this one can easily force it's way to top 3 hardest one i ever played. It feels like roguelite-darksouls of strategy games.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: I love where this game is going. The art, style, acoustics, and function are great, especially considering how fresh of a game it is from a small indie developer. Unfortunately there are some balance issues to work out, but I still found myself addicted and Unexpected Studios seem to be very responsive to feedback and have already started working on balance.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: I don't want to repeat other review's comment about aesthetic aspect of the game.  They are great but UI has quite a few issues.  There are many other quality of life changes the game can use either, but the biggest problem really falls on game balance.  However if devs can listen to community feedbacks and fix these issues in the next few patches, this game will be in a very good spot.  I'm even looking forward to the DLC already.A few tips for those who are struggling:1.  Like another comment said, rush Council as soon as possible.  You can reduce your ration cost by 6 per turn by purchasing the One For All Council option (bottom left), it will significantly help you.2. Consider dedicate a Pupil to a Harvest Hut and upgrade it.  The upgrade reduce harvest cycle by a turn, which is roughly a 33% increase in efficiency.  This can help a lot to alleviate early game food pressure.3.  Try roll up a Pupil with Agile trait if you are really struggling with the game.  -1 Turn to any harvest activity is simply too powerful.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: While some of the comments I've seen on this are valid (the tutorial/campaign doesn't include several key elements), a lot seem to have been fixed since I bought this game and I'm really enjoying it. Although RNGs are annoying, they are not debilitating and tbh just make the game more interesting- without them it'd be pretty predictable. I like the different modes you can unlock, letting you choose how you want to play, and while I lose quite a lot, it doesn't seem an unfair amount- roughly 2/3 goes and that is mainly due to bad planning on my part rather than the game. I love the graphics and find the gameplay a good balance of luck and preparation so overall like this game!
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this is an adorable roguelite centered on resource & time management and character specialization. The general concept of the game being that you have X turns on the map until you lose and need Y materials to continue traveling. So you send your shapeshifter animals to various resource node to gather/harvest/mine, construct buildings, try to level your people up in professions, and save up enough resources to go to another map. Rinse and repeat until you reach the last spot on the map. This is broken up by major and minor vagaries... which are RNG bad stuff like "after 5 turns, anyone working as a cook will get ill" or "lighting strikes three spots" which sets fires & harms buildings. The major issues with the game come from randomized map resources and not being able to plan far enough ahead sometimes.... which might make you feel like you were set up for failure from the start. You may think a spot will be good to travel to but then find out none of the resources you need are there or there's only one forest but you need the wood to cook so you don't starve. And so on. But its a roguelite.... so you lose, maybe unlock some more traits, and try again.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting game. But once you figure out what to do it becomes easy to win any game. Though there are a lot of aspects to the game that can ruin your run even if you thought it was in your grasp. Like missing some vagaries etc. Knowing that you can remove some vagaries might help. But you gotta explore the game and know what tools are at your disposal to make it more favorable for you.SPOILER ALERT. TIPS to help you win. If you happen to lose all the time, try figuring out how to support your pupils need. 1 cook, one fish/meat trapper - this should be enough to feed 5-7 pupils. Also try to reach lvl 3 gatherer with all pupils. That helps reduce food consumption. So the rest of the pupils can gather resources required to reach next halt. Also don't instantly go to next halt if you have already met the requirements. Check what is needed for the next halt and try to gather some (or all resources if possible). That way you have more options to go around if new halt doesn't have enough resources to go to the next one.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: I don't have a ton of experience playing civilization building turn based games but this game is really cute visually and the audio is so nice.This game seems fairly basic at first glance but there's so much more than even the campaign mode tells you about. At the time of writing this I have just under 7 hours into the game but I'm excited to keep playing and experience more things. It feels like it will be a real challenge at times, especially because I can't resist the allure of the ruins regardless of if I have a druid on my team or not.I did receive this game for free as a content creator but was not asked or required to provide a review.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: A Wonderfully charming yet challenging town builder, it is great to see each villager growing and changing their forms. The unique twist of being forced to pack up your town and go on the move presents a number of interesting decisions such as whether to build cheap structures that will be left behind when you move on or go to the effort of collecting advanced resources to build buildings that can be packed away into the caravan. the constant demand for food forces you to make tough decisions while the approaching water means you can never stay long enough to become comfortable.The game is well polished with a lot of replayability, i could relate it a far more upbeat Frostpunk, definitely worth checking out and supporting.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: Like other folks have mentioned this is a deceptively difficult game that will ask you to fail in order to learn. Planning is key. Placement is key. Timing is key. And you'll need a little luck as well. It's super rewarding though, and such beautiful execution with really interesting mechanics (a little 4x, but without combat, and major resource management with unique skill trees)  and a somehow-adorable take on an impending disaster. I have found it difficult to put down. Would've loved a cut scene or two during transitions. 10/10 would run out of food while looking for herbs again.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: I would suggest holding off on this game for a bit. The balance seems really bad with its vagaries and halt costs. On the easiest difficulty, I was locked into a path that had almost no stone or minerals, then asked me to get 200 more than each resource was on that halt. They allow you to build a market place to trade for resources you don't have, but the RNG events broke so many buildings I didn't have the resources to get that set up either. The devs said it's based on a background karma mechanic, I saw this in another review and so was very careful not to exhaust resources and generally be greedy in any way. Didn't matter. Obscure mechanics and bad RNG make strategy in this game an exercise in frustration.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: The game was a little too difficult at first but the recent update has helped a lot with some balancing issues! It's a really fun strategy game, similar to games like Niche, minus the whole genes and genetics aspect and with more focus on class/skill building. Each game can turn out very different based on the map and traits of your pupils. I can still see some areas that the game could improve upon but overall I do generally enjoy the game and would recommend to others!
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: Challenging but fair. Its like Into the Breach and Settler's of Catan had a baby, and that baby grew up to have a kid with FrostPunk. This is that third generation game. It has a very light atmosphere with everything being light cheerful colors and dialog, in a game with no combat... and the stark contrast with how many of my workers die of sickness and starvation.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: First things first: I received this game for free to review. However, like many of my reviews, if a game is bad, it's bad.This is not one of those games. As Far As The Eye is a surprisingly complex turn-based strategy game. With a progress style similar to Slay the Spire, choices you make in tech trees early on can greatly effect your ability to push your caravan forward. There are also choices regarding how many (and what type of) resources you carry from location to location. All these decisions culminated in my games ending early do to starvation, or death from the various events.Overall, AFatE has been an enjoyable game to play. I found very few bugs early on and the learning curve is a little steep at first, but not difficult to get the hang. Overall, I would say if you love strategy games and also have an interest in rogue-likes, AFatE is a DEFINITE purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent premise, the interface needs a little work but the devs put out a respectable patch after one week and have promised more, so I'm comfortable recommending it. The difficulty/RNG complaints in other reviews were overblown before the patch, and the patch has removed the most notorious lowroll situations anyway.@Devs: you won't need massive tutorials if the interface is good enough. Tooltips especially. Show us more of the hidden numbers (exp bars, expected action yields, etc) and we'll figure it out ourselves. Being able to move units without ending turn is a big QoL improvement that every conventional 4x has, sure it shouldn't be allowed during a task, but there's no reason free roaming can't have the usual 4x movement interface.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR; love the artwork and soothing gameplay, game feels like work instead of play because of gather/fetch/grind, randomness that gets you stuck killed it for me.I would love to give this game a thumbs up.I Got the game because i am a big fan of roguelikes and i triggered on the artwork.As much as I want to like this game, it mainly feels like work, fetch and grind. Which is fine If that would have been mixed with a sense of progression, but here comes the  point I got frustrated with in this game; the randomness of events/vagaries that come up. To give you an extreme example; You almost got enough resources gathered to move on, vagary happens, all of a sudden you need more resources of a kind, which the current land does not provide.Now, from doing well, all of a sudden you are stuck with no way out.. This happened to me during three successive playsessions. Now im done.The only way out of this specific example I see is building a market (if you have a pack animal) and trading some other resource 5:1. But that never worked in time..
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: As Far as the Eye is a sweet yet challenging strategy game. My experience has been enjoyable so far. To discover the path to victory via trial and error gives the game a roguelike vibe that may feel daunting to some.  I find the harmony mechanic quite interesting, I like a game with underlying messages.I don't know if devs read positive reviews as I've seen them answer to negative ones I'll give this one a try :
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: I fell in love only 30 minutes in. The game is pretty hard to get used to your first try, plus for a lot of people its just hard in general. But I fully recommend playing even if doesn't seem like the type of game you'd play. I didn't even realize a whole hour passed, I honestly love this game A LOT.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: Please add save&load. I left a place with 10 students and no resources because I click leave by mistake before I can sort the backpack. And there's no way I can feed them in a brand new stage with 10 students and no resources. Now I have to give up the game which I spent more than 10 hours and start again.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent game, in my opinion at least. I love rogue likes, and I love resource management, so this game is perfect for me. They just released an update cause a lot of people were having issue with certain RNG based mechanics in the game. I had no issues prior, but the game certainly is more fair, but can still be just as challenging. I highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: Very pleasant game !From the Title menu to the maps, the visuals and the musics / sounds, will put you in a new universe.As a non-try harder player, I was quite worried about not enjoying this game as the difficulty is everywhere (and that's not a bad thing, I enjoyed being challenged by the tutorial).But thanks to the campaign (I took my time to read and to think about my actions), I started learning the game and  enjoying it straight from the campaign.I also like the concept of mixing the building/management ressources game with a rogue-like.The normal games being a bit to difficult for me (still having trouble managing my food and not destroying the map), I'm currently playing custom games with my own parameters (mainly without food :P).It's really great to be able to do that, even if the game is planned to be difficult, and to discover a chill and contemplative way of playing.I will, for sure, keep playing for many hours.Congratulations to the team, I really enjoy playing your game !
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: Very unique game, may not please to everyone, but for who likes this specific gameplay it must be a very good game.You have to take your time, read, don't rush the turns, or you will lose without any understanding of what happened. The design is very beautiful, the sounds too, but don't underestimate this cute game: the gameplay is complex :p
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: first had thank you for letting me try out the game early. The first week I was hooked. I came home with my mind fixated on getting to the eye. It brought back the joy of the Oregon trail with a twist; more interaction with it being turned based and having to keep an eye on everyone. 12 hours in and well.. I still havent made it to the eye. It is a hard one even when you are one slot away. It makes you think and reevaluate your choices. I like how the pupils have their own needs/wants/attributes that can make them a good villager or not.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game only because I feel the early access is still present and I'll be forgiving while the game, on the other hand, is not. While the game is aesthetically pleasing with the graphics and soundtrack, it is so brutal. I barely got through the tutorial before being soul crushingly destroyed by the AI. The tutorial gave you very minimal basics (movements, general crafting, how to navigate the map, the goals) but I feel it missed a lot of important parts you won't identify until you spend hours of trial and error. Sorry, but the tutorial should prepare the user for the full game, not destroy the experience before they begin. I couldn't figure out 'auras' for the life of me and then as I was being blocked by those for an entire section, the new negative impact events rolled in and demolished my team. Food is running out faster than you can explore a section in the hopes to get the mats for building the cook station and then the food to cook. The game has a wonderful concept for strategy but it is unforgiving with the pace, negative events that overpower the positive ones and a very steep learning curve within the tutorial before even playing the full game. I hope they work on improving this in updates. If they can, this game would be an excellent strategy game. 7/10 rating - needs to improve the tutorial so you can play the full game without spending hours figuring out how it works to enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: In this video I take a look at As Far As The Eye, a survival strategy game.A very nicely made game that easily entertains. It's easy to loose an hour or two playing "As Far As The Eye" but it's quite an unforgiving title. My first two attempts I tried focusing on the required resources using the remaining time to stock food but both times my workers starved to death. I suppose the opposite approach might be best. The goal is to complete the journey one stage at a time. Each stage requires it's own resources to pass and there are lots of random events, encounters, and exploration. Take a look.Watch the video to see what the game is like...Check'n Games Video Curation, providing you with as many Let's Play's as we can.Thanks for watching. Please like comment and subscribe.
_childDocuments_.name: As Far As The Eye

_childDocuments_.review: Great indy game, the art is beautiful, even if the legibility could be improved. The music is adding a lot to the chill atmosphere.But, don't get fouled ! That game is hard, and could feel unfair and random in the beginning. However, after a few hours, you will start to realize that you have a some ways to mitigate the randomness. _childDocuments_.review: Many reviews complain about the current rng. Although it can be frustrating at times, after a couple runs I was able to reach the eye without much problem. _childDocuments_.review: ****STILL NEEDS BALANCING:Picked up this game after seeing it on the store page and watching a few Twitch streams. Reviews are not wrong - this game is super unique, beautiful and gives me a very Northgard/Frost Punk/Civ sort of management feel. However, this game event on the first "tribe" is very difficult and is mostly due to random events. I feel the game needs further balancing; perhaps increasing the time before the tide comes on each halt, maybe less overall events, or mixing them with some positive events for the minor ones or having them occur progressively more towards the end? I have learned that rushing the Council mobile building allows you to spend Knowledge points to predict/avoid the minor events but these start right from the first halt.Another note is the "campaign" which appears to largely be an adorable tutorial is unfunctional - the goal on the map required me to get stone (or iron, cannot recall which one) to move the next Halt, however the tutorial led me to get the opposite and then I was unable to proceed. REALLY looking forward to this game once some tweeks have been made!

_childDocuments_.review: As Far As The Eye is a gorgeous turn-based resource management game where you navigate your caravan and "pupils" (workers) through a series of randomly generated maps, finally arriving at The Eye to complete your journey. Sound simple? I have yet to make it past the second "Halt" (map) due to the brutal difficulty of this game. In order to make it out alive, you have to balance resource gathering and building structures with a never-ending onslaught of random negative events that poison your meeples and destroy your buildings. If you are a fan of steep intellectual challenges of the worker variety, this game is for you! I like it enough to keep playing, but honestly find myself wondering if the developers actually play-tested their own creation before unleashing pain upon the world... My only complaints, aside from getting smacked-down by nature every time I play, are some minor glitches with the tutorial system, odd English typos and grammar problems in the descriptive text and a skill tree system that could use a bit of UX polish. Overall, As Far As They Eye is an enticing, pretty little hex-based indie that will keep you screaming at your monitor for weeks on end.

_childDocuments_.review: Too many people complaining about the bad RNGs of either pupil's negative traits and/or the punishing vagaries without knowing there's a workaround to deal with these things. Negative traits can be removed by visiting Remains and there's a building to mitigate and prevent disasters. I had a pupil that always gets -5 health everytime they harvest anything. You know what I did? Make them a Druid or Conctruction worker, and let the other pupils do the harvesting. I got lucky and found the said Remains that removed the trait, but even if it's not removed I could always make potions for the pupil to recover while at the same time leveling the Druid's exp."Minor" Vagaries despite minor can be pretty lethal such as the lightning bolts that can destroy buildings with one strike. Doesn't always hit your things, but when it does, it's tough to get back up. These small Vagaries however can be avoided by making the Council building provided you have the bull and the materials. You can spend Knowledge Points to reduce damage from Vagaries, remove an upcoming one and even make Auras to be less threatening. The devs should've make a tutorial on this because I almost finished the first playthrough but just realized this building existed lmaoPersonally, the only thing that bugs me is there's no undo button. When I had a second thought about assigning my pupils, I can't go back and they already left whatever they're previously doing. It's not a major problem, it just means I have to plan carefully before making any wrong movements.If you don't fancy all these RNG stuff, you can always make a custom campaign, start out easy, try things out and get to feel the game. I only scratched the surface so this is all I currently know. One thing I know for sure? I like the game so far.

_childDocuments_.review: After nearly seven hours and a bunch of tries, I finally managed to reach the Eye with the West Tribe (my last full run took me about 3h I’d say). The game is not easy, not at all, but the challenge is really fun!You have a Campaign to familiarize you with some game mechanics but be aware it’s not some random tutorial. If you do not think wisely, you will lose. Never forget about feeding your Pupils Be aware that even if the soundtrack and the design look relaxing, the game is not a cakewalk.EDIT: Two years later, I do not recommend buying this game. At least wait a Steam Sale. Sadly the studio did not continue to support the game. Even if I think the core mechanics are good, bugs and flaws are still present throughout the game.

name: In Sound Mind
detailed_description: As you awake in the corridors of an inexplicable building, you find the environment takes on a life of its own and leads you to discover a series of victims, all exposed to the same experimental chemical. In your search for answers, bizarre visions emerge and introduce a host of imposing horrors…and a cat named Tonia. From the creators of the cult classic Nightmare House 2 comes In Sound Mind, a witty first-person psychological horror with frenetic puzzles and unique boss fights. Traverse a series of unsettling memories as you journey within the inner workings of the one place you can’t seem to escape—your own mind. A new survival horror experience from the creators of the legendary Nightmare House 2. We Create Stuff, the team behind one of highest-rated mods of all time returns with an unexpected spin on the horror genre. Experience a series of haunting memories. Journey through a progression of unsettling stories, each with unique puzzles, mechanics, weapons, and boss fights. Overcome a cast of terrors. Confront those who stalk you in a series of daunting boss fights and learn how to defeat them by solving mind-bending puzzles. An eerie soundtrack by The Living Tombstone. The internet icon lends his distinct sound to this next generation psychological thriller, with a distinctive song for each story. Unexpect the expected. Explore an imaginative and disorienting narrative, featuring sentient mannequins, a feline companion, and much more. And yes, you can pet the cat.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game. Well structured. Solid blend of spooky, goofy, and eerie. If I had to compare it thematically to something, I'm thinking The X-Files would probably be the closest in terms of tone in that it has a serious/spooky core plot with some irreverent moments thrown in to break things up. Puzzles are not overly obtuse and pacing and presentation seemed pretty good. Having songs made up for each of the tapes/levels was a nice addition. Definitely worth checking out. Also, you can pet the cat, 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't yet completed the game but I just have to give my two cents; this game is brilliant! I've been hooked and playing well into the night, which only enhances the atmosphere. A truly spooky experience that delves deep into the pits of mental health, using horror as the medium to the tell the story of a therapist with seriously damaged patients. I adore this game, and it breaks my heart that it isn't better known since it's so so clear that nothing but absolute passion went into making it. I really wish these devs nothing but success.

_childDocuments_.review: Really good game! Your character is a therapist who is down on his luck himself. He can't seem to help his patients and it's wearing on him. You explore the histories you've had with your patients and uncover something greater. In Sound Mind is a bit of an everything-genre game, but it's primarily story-rich and platformer/puzzle. It's hard to describe what is great about In Sound Mind, but it's just fun and interesting through and through. New story developments and level designs keep coming. In Sound Mind has a serious story at its core, but it never felt like a slog because the levels were all unique and enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: When your therapist needs a therapist, That’s the story of in sound mind.A game where you take a journey into the minds of your patients and see things from the perspective of both parties. Watch the struggles your patients have while dealing with your own insecurities made this games story quite enjoyable. The game was quite long and took me 20hrs to complete and that was looking and doing everything the game has to offer as well as dying a bunch of times. The combat was decent enough and offers the players a good selection of weapons to choose from. Some of the combat felt a bit cheap with certain enemies being bullet sponges where even the best weapons felt weak against them. This is felt the most when 4 enemies spawn in small hallways filled with toxic gasses and you run out of ammo while trying not to die from stepping on poison puddles.The maps are very large and takes a decent amount of time to complete them. They are filled with all sorts of puzzles, collectibles, and character upgrades and is worthwhile to check every corner for everything. Once you complete a map you are free to roam it for anything you have missed so you don’t have to feel pressured to get everything right then and there. You can also revisit areas at any time.Things I liked - the story and characters. Good selection of weapons. Large maps.Things I didn’t really like - bullet sponge enemies. Sometimes puzzles got annoying only to have to solve another puzzle directly after.This was definitely an underrated game that deserves more attention and maybe we will see a sequel for it in the future.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Well, it's complex. It's a higly metaphorical game. The gameplay it's rather simple and easy to understand. The overall story is quite long and, apart from a few errors in jungian psychology interpretation, this portrays an interesting and realistic internal struggle of a therapist with his shadow. This theme is very important to me, so i'll give it a 9/10. But if you mainly care about gameplay, this will probably bore you.

_childDocuments_.review: I have just finished the game and I cannot recommend it.  I've read the glowing reviews and I disagree on almost all points. I will be brief and break it down into Story, Gameplay, Music and Graphics.The story in my view is very weak. It's not captivating, I don't care about any of the characters. I understand what the creators were going for but this seems like a very unpolished draft so for me it's maybe 2 or 3 out of 10 but no higher.Gameplay is ok but I also had a few FPS issues and switching the items can be very annoying. Usually the item I need always ends up being last, maybe a pocket light would have at least removed one item from the inventory and made it permanent like in Silent Hill 3. But I also suppose that the puzzles fit in this category and while many again gave glowing reviews stating that the puzzles were original and unique, in reality it's far from it. It almost feels like they were forced into the game. Not a fan. So all in all it's 5/10The music I felt was nothing special, more or less what you'd expect. I'm not even sure what rating to give it, maybe 3/10Finally the graphics. This is probably the only redeeming factor. Again, I wouldn't say it's great but it's alright, a bit repetitive. I think it's the same models used over and over to populate maps. Maybe 6/10Overall my score is 16/40. There are far far better choices if you want a psychological horror experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Its spooky at first, has good variety in terms of characters/environments, compelling story, good humor. Cons: I feel like it turns into an action adventure game at the last quarter of the game, I dont like how when the main character saves the villains by just saying "Its not your fault" and then they are magically healed, I feel it needs to be more fleshed out. Enemies need more variety and a redesign, they feel very generic and boring. Hard Difficulty is not hard at all. Some smaller issues I faced: The 2nd boss's animations are very janky, Autosaves can be inconsistent at times. Small note: The gameplay mechanic in the first chapter is a cool concept that adds a lot to the fun factor of the game, but the mechanics that come after arent as good. All in all, In sound mind is a decent game but has a lot of room for improvement. I'm interested in seeing what the game devs are going to do in the next installment.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. The amount of exploration and puzzles peaked my interest enough to finish it. You can set the level of difficulty in the beginning so you can enjoy the story or you can focus more on the challenge. I wouldn't really say this game is "horror" but more so a thriller. A few jump scares here and there but nothing where I was screaming. Although Agent Rainbow was a little freaky looking.I was absolutely astonished by the character design in each episode for each patient. My favorites being Max and Lucas' characters.Mechanics of this game was both simple and tricky. I kind of wish there was a better way to toggle your weapon inventory other than with the scroll wheel. Half the time I'm zipping through the wheel trying to get a hold of the weapon I want and it gets frustrating when I'm trying to run around  as quickly as I can while also being attacked. Nothing too major though.The sound design was incredible. There was so much ambient noise that fit in so well to create this haunting atmosphere. The bonus of the vinyl record songs were neat too.The cat, Tonia, was so cute but also the story behind what happened to her was pretty sad.Overall I highly recommend this game regardless if it was on sale or not. It seemed like there may be a sequel to this but if it does happen, I'm all for it.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: An outstanding indie game, a rare type of horror that's both emotional, funny, and spooky. In Sound Mind features a really really good story, great characters, a great atmosphere, and a fantastic soundtrack, also has little to no bugs. There were times where I was fighting back tears on this one. Darn it this game really does pull your heart strings. I also like the antagonist, such a cool dude.And lastly, you can pet the cat. so 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: for an indie studio its a decent title but the ending left me annoyed.solid art direction, fairly decent polish and not much cheese, runs decently for a unity game and an interesting premise for the most part, but the gun handling was mediocre, "normal" difficulty is grotesquely easy given my normal videogame incompetence, and most of the puzzles felt very... handhold-ey? very few of them did i have to think about for more than a few seconds. the game does  do subtlety plot-wise and constantly beat you over the head that yes! you use a Tool You Earned Earlier to solve this puzzle and it felt vaguely insulting to my intelligence at points, which normally isn't a problem, but this is the first game i managed to 100% in one run with no walkthrough, so. yeah.i dont regret playing it and it kept my room very toasty from the hilarious gpu load, but i dont think i can recommend it

_childDocuments_.review: The absolute passion and soul poured into this game is unmatched and it's criminal that this didn't release to bigger success. The best way I can possibly describe it is like a sourcemod from an alternate universe where the developers had budgets, which should be no surprise considering who made it. If you've played nightmare house 2 or underhell you'll immediately understand, the game contains some tricky hl2 style platforming and the character controls extremely similar to Gordon, the only thing missing is the crouch jump. Otherwise I mean, it's a fantastic game. Story has a very interesting concept and the voice acting is really good, puzzles are decent and the setpieces are truly phenomenal- like the spooky mannequins that move when you're not looking but they actually help you this time. General combat is fairly mediocre with only a few enemy types, but it doesn't detract much. I also like how the big bad in each level, you know, the enemy you can't kill always has some weakness you can use to temporarily disable them so they get in your way less.The weakest part would have to be the old factory, which contains an annoying building crawl searching for keys and an ABOMINABLE conveyor belt puzzle you have to solve while the big bad chases you around in a confined space. Generally, if you're expecting something really hardcore scary like Amnesia you might be disappointed, it's more of an adventure game with horror aesthetics sort of like Alan Wake. Honestly I prefer these, the gameplay has a lot more room to breathe when the developer isn't constantly trying to freak you out with unkillable stalkers and sanity management systems.The best part by far in my opinion is something small, it's how every note you pick up is unique. It's not just a text popup like most games. Every character has different handwriting just like real life. Agent Rainbow, the main villain, writes in big scratchy oil slick text which gives him even more personality. It really is minor, but it shows a level of care you don't see too often.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game after following the Nightmare House game they are currently making/releasing. I have to say that I am blown away by this game and how fun it is. This game is so intriguing that it sucks you into the story and gets you vested in what happens. It has so many cool mechanics like the broken mirror that just add to the lore of the story. The way that all the different stories are connected is so cool that you just want to keep going to figure out more of the story.I would absolutely recommend this game to anyone that loves really intricate stories with some really amazing level designs. This game is now in my all time favorite list so huge shout out to these developers and the amazing game they have created here!
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to love this game. It's visually amazing and the metaphors while a bit stretched are well represented. Every gameplay mechanic worked well on its own and the design was intuitive. The extra in the game was to much though. So much FPS parkour, added boss encounters and overstretched level designs with so much backtracking, You could have cut 30% of the game out and had it be an intense tight experience. The worst part was all my saves corrupting and the game refusing to allow me to interact with the final boss fight. I was 2 tapes from done as well. Combined with the other minor technical glitches it was equally frustrating as it was fun to play.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: Finished "In Sound Mind" today.You know how when you finish some stories you can feel... Maybe not exactly "catharsis", but some sort of "cleansing relief", I guess. Well, this game has this. Even more - it has 4 such stories inside of it, which you will experience as you finish the puzzles. And fights. Not sure if they were really necessary in a game like this, but they surely can spice things up.It also sends an important message, that psychotherapy is... Well, "important". That it can help. Yes, it may be more difficult in some cases, but it still can be helpful. It can literally change your life. And if not that - at least, it can make things a bit easier.But an even more important feature of this game is... Ability to pet the cat. In fact, if you do not pet Tonia enough to annoy her - you're not playing this game right.Don't wait for a discount - totally worth full price.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: It doesn't take long to appreciate the smooth handling controls and colorful environment.  The main plot is thoroughly put together, even though I wasn't a big fan of it, I could see many people resonating with this type of psychological story. Overall, it's been quite enjoyable to play and easily recommendable.  | 3.5/5 |
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: This effing game. Snapshot description: FPS surreal modern horror fantasy, good voice acting, lite firearm/melee combat, mostly exploration and puzzle solve with even some lite metriodvania elements (Get new tool/ability, go back to a section to unlock new section)The production value is fairly good though there are some small and infrequent issues for me regarding the jumping, crouching, and walking backwards that doesn't give it perfect scores.Well worth the money with a decent story and mystery at it's core where you will be going to new themed maps surrounding the psychology of specific characters. While it's not my cup of tea, they cared about the soundtrack and it's pro.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: I finished the game, "In Sound Mind." Wow. I wanted to try a new game in 2023, so I just went to a website and get 5 randoms keys. This game was one of them.First and foremost, I'm a wussy when it comes to horror games. But, I already spent my money, so I have to give it a try. As I go deep into the game, I was LOCKED IN. The story, the levels, the characters, and the gameplay! The game plays identically to Half-Life.I found myself a gold mine game that I dug up. And I'm so glad I got to play this game. A truly 10/10 experience.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: In Sound Mind was an amazing game. New mechanics I've never seen before, amazing world building, unique and memorable characters, and by far one of the best stories I have ever played. This game had the perfect balance of horror, combat, and puzzles. I enjoyed every last minute of this game. 10/10 game!
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: Overwhelmingly positive...hmmmm, well I guess people liked this game. I finished the game and here are my thoughts.I will address some things developers put in game description - This game is not survival horror, most of the things wrong in this game a horrific but survival with tons of ammo and supplies doesn't work, I played on hard an didn't have any problem in battles, I will not get into is this a horror game debate because it is highly subjective, - Unexpected spin on the horror genre - Well I would have to say this is a good joke, this game has nothing original to show, it is a Outlast - Amnesia hybrid that in 1 chapter pays homage to the great game Alan Wake. When I finished this game I was trying to think of a train wreck of a game to compare this game to and I can say only Amnesia Rebirth came to my mind. Now, I don't play many modern horror games because they are not good, I got this one in a bundle and just tried it, I regret it . - Confront those who stalk you in a series of daunting boss fights and learn how to defeat them by solving mind-bending puzzles. OMG they wrote that, most of the bosses are awful, there are some good optional puzzles but mind bending not a chance.I will stop here because I could get through more of the things they throbbed in game description.The game is everything I despise about modern game, it looks good, it sounds good but everything else is awful. The story, writing, repetitive quests, backtracking, tons of collectibles etc. Now you tell me if this sounds like a horror survival game.The thing that bothered me the most is how this game tackles mental health issues, at times is is borderline immature and offensive. It is irresponsible and I think they should've not based their game around this thematic.The only chapter I liked was Alan Wake homage, it was the only chapter I cared for the person I was trying to save and that is because that chapter was well written, it had structure which I can't say for the other chapters.All in all an awful AAA like game that has 0 survival horror elements, generally bad writing, bad combat, awful boss fights, tons of backtracking.... overwhelmingly positive my a** !
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: The tone of this game is all over the place. Voice acting for the villain sounds like he's suited for a cartoon and not a horror game. You encounter the first enemy and jarring techno music plays. There's a constant generic "spooky" theme that plays in the background that doesn't allow you to take in any of the atmosphere. I can appreciate the technical work that went into this, but besides being poorly optimized it's just not very engaging.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: It is good... very clear on where to go most of the time, story is overall good.. in fact, "most" of the game is just good.Horror element is very light, it's spookiness isn't jump scare heavy, so that is respectable, its mostly just seeing things in the corner of your vision or maybe a wall will move... it was so subtle at times that it honestly just felt like I was being gaslit constantly, i did have a few times where I was honestly questioning my own sanity... which kinda immersed me quite a lot.Combat and stealth is pretty rough, you are easily given enough resources to end both of the weak points of the game relatively quickly however, so no biggy there.Found 1 bug in the 10 hour playthrough that stopped a side objective door opening, easily fixed by reloading the save.Direction and puzzles are intuitive, I found myself spending a few minutes at most with any puzzle, it made me feel smart.. talking of feeling smart, I was able to piece together stuff before they happened relatively easily, there wasnt too many rug pulls with the general plot, this game allows your brain to have serotonin, it was kinda fun to listen and read stuff and be able to pick out key things, knowing what mental disorders patients had and what these patients went through just by environmental story telling.Talking of story telling, Stories of all the characters/patients is... pretty gloomy, and worryingly relatable, due to experiencing nearly all of these disorders first hand... I can say most of it is pretty accurate when it comes to the mental illness side of things.Songs... Brilliant, I've listened to them since the Living tombstone released the OSTs... nothing more needed to be said.Is it worth it? Yeah, I'd recommend. Definitely an experience.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best hidden gems of 2023. While not as deep as the psychological aspects of games like Persona, Silent Hill, or Soma - it still has some meat and potatoes to offer on that front as it let's you eat the meal one bite at a time until you realize just how big the course is. Great artwork and vivid designs. Solid soundtrack. Alot of great voice acting.And if that's your type of treat - I'd pay the full 35usd for it tbh
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: Great indie horror game with the emphasis and polish in all the right places for me.Excellent level design and traversal with really satisfying puzzles and good environment variety.New mechanics and tools are added regularly making sure the game stays fresh. Resource management also feels really well balanced where you are always have what you need to make it through tough situations but still feeding the need to search well and play carefully.Exploration is really the strong draw of this game with each level being super satisfying, creative and immersive to poke around in and figure out. On the downside, while the levels are designed very well, the visuals are a bit mixed. Not the worst but definitely not cutting edge. The gun combat is also a bit janky but it isnt a huge part of the game. These drawbacks however were not enough to stop me from enjoying the game and looking forward to what this team does next.

_childDocuments_.review: I love game lore, with any game. This game was right down my alley with the amazing story line, it was different from any other game I've played, and it was so much fun to play. I'm posting this review on my second play through of the game, the second time was even more fun than the first. Definitely worth playing if you're looking for something with puzzles, story line and some thrills.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best game I played in a year, and I play a lot of different ones in various genres. Calling it a horror adventure would be an understatement since In Sound Mind merges so many gameplay elements together. Sometimes it reminds about Half-Life, sometimes about Alan Wake,  sometimes about Psychonauts, sometimes about Resident Evil (the new ones, 7 and 8), sometimes about Thief, it also has elements of metroidvanias, some interesting puzzles, and tons of cleverly hidden secrets.It also contains a lot of shooter and action scenes, and while it has only three different common enemies and a limited selection of weapons, great boss fights and solid level design makes up for a lack of variety in "shoot things up" department. It's really hard to explain what In Sound Mind is without spoiling the setting or the story, which both are great.As well as the game's OST which has ambient tracks and several amazing songs with vocals representing various musical genres. Seriously, soundtrack here is on par with what Supergiant Games does, and it alone is a good reason to play the game.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: great game!  not many horror games allow combat for good reason, its hard to be scared when you can gun down whatever is chasing you. However this game implements combat without it ruining the atmosphere of the game. This game also throws little curve balls like things moving around when you are not looking, which creates an awesome atmosphere. Major points for style!
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: That was a really good game, much longer than I originally thought but in a good way.Great story, some cool environments, a good mix of the rare jump scare, but mostly just interesting puzzles with some creepiness and uneasesness tossed in. Combat isn't too difficult and felt almost optional by the end, but FPS skills were a surprisingly large part of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: Starts off really strong but seemed to get weaker as it went along. I found myself getting bored with the repetitive game play. I felt like it just went on for far too long but all in all I don't regret finishing the game. Good story, strong spooks in the first 2 hours but everything else is average.Not sure my opinion would be the same if I had not gotten this from Humble Bundle.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: The level design is very well done. There is a linear progression in levels, but it doesn't feel limiting as it promotes exploration by having both a large open-like world and by rewarding it with useful items. The puzzles in the game are very intuitive. I have felt stumped on many of them, but never to the point where the solution feels ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ or impossible. It is very rewarding to figure out how to progress the game.It is an overall incredible experience; defining it as just a game doesn't do it justice. It hits all the marks of a good production: great soundtrack, great story, and great characters and character development. 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that did a good job of tugging at my feelings and making me feel invested in finding resolution by completing it.The story keeps you engaged, and the gameplay mechanics mesh well with the narrative. _childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: I... don't know how to move on after this. I don't even remember how I found this game, I expected nothing and was gifted so many hours yelling at my screen out of horror. I don't like horror games. I really don't. I usually rage quit them. But this gem was different, I couldn't look away. ( Bec mannequins! DUH! )  This game has the perfect final boss. Non repetitive combat, great sense of humor. I don't know how many times I started yelling out of horror then started laughing bec I saw the joke right after. I would  have change the writing a bit  But it's not bad the way it is. Imma miss the mannequins and the only 3 pets I can get every time from Tonia. Talking with her was precious.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: A really cool game with very nice atmosphere.The story(s) are amazing and hit really hard.The puzzles are also very well done, they arnt "if i didnt look that up id never even quessed that" hard, but they arnt a cakewalk either with bonus point to the fact that theres an mechanic, that tells you that theres a secret somewhere, that also doesnt make it easier to solve.Its kind of a short game and the combat is generally pretty easy, even on the hardest difficulty, which i generally dont like at all, but the progression combined with the constant feeding of story always keept my interest high.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant story driven game. I was surprised with how unique the story was for this game and got sucked into it. Each level does something unique and keeps the game feeling fresh. The only gripe I had was, even on hard mode, it always felt like I had a maxed out inventory of ammo/items. It would have been nice to have to conserve my resources a bit more.Seriously though, this game has a lot of charm and stands out in an ocean of generic horror games. 10/10 for the mannequins alone, they're real bros.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely beautiful game!Some unique mechanics, great level design, charismatic characters, great sound and music.My only problem is some kind of bug with collectible achievement in Max's tape. I'm absolutely sure that i grabbed all 12. Double checked that level with a guide video later on. And also mirror shows nothing. But it still says that 1 pill left. Sad, but not a big deal.Would definitely recommend the game to anyone who enjoys weird horror with Lovecraftian vibes :)
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: What an unexpectedly enjoyable game. The story is actually interesting and drive the engagement through the game. The music is one part that really stands out as phenomenal, especially the character based vinyl records. The puzzles can be tedious at times, but this would be the first puzzle game where all puzzles are top shelf all the time, most of the time you are just applying tool X to problem Y, but the progressive unlocking of items does give a good sense of progression through the game.The enemies are very lackluster, adding little than occasional jump-scares, but didn't bother me too much.Level design is very good, most levels are very big and open, making traversal a pain, especially when you are backtracking to grab pills (collectibles) that you missed.All in all I can recommend this game, even outside of a sale, I believe the 30€ price tag is well deserved.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: A great mix of psychological horror, puzzles, and sound design. While playing I always wondered what the full picture was, the story telling was amazing, using both what you see in the world as well as paper clippings and what the voice actors say. All in all I had a great time playing In Sound Mind!

_childDocuments_.review: An esoteric thriller is how i would characterize the game in the end. A story, an imagery involved both create a rare thing i have only seen in previous work that was made with help of the team We Create Stuff - Underhell and Nightmare house 2.But those two were mods. This? This is a masterpiece of storytelling and imagery i have come to love through the playthrough. it took me time - not as much as it lists me playing, given i left it on for a bit as i did other stuff, but more than enough for it's price. I look forward to what will We create Stuff pursue next.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished this game this morning, I have to say it was a pretty fun interesting game, I definitely recommend it. There was some parts of the game that were annoying to me but thats mostly just because of my poor memory and not fully understanding some puzzle/platforming sections and not remembering paths.
