_childDocuments_.review: 3 hours in review: This game, let me tell you, this game is heavy and I am loving every second of the experience. This game is not afraid to tackle topics regarding mental health and is trying its best to give awareness of the topic, while keeping things entertaining in a heavy way. You are able to defend yourself, albeit the game still feels like a walking sim; however, this is okay with me, and I am not a fan at all of walking sims. So far, the game play is heavily focused on puzzles and luckily they are not difficult. I haven't had the need to search for an answer to these, yet, which is quite nice and refreshing. This game is reaching top 5 for me at the moment and I will update once I finish the game. I really hope this game sticks the landing at the end b/c so far I am enjoying the ride. Edit: Finished the game and this story stuck the landing. Incredible all the way around. 9/10 - Puzzles get boring towards the end, but nice enough that I didn't require a Youtube video. I was able to figure them out on my own w/o any hand holding, which was refreshing.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: Great adventure filled with impressive moments that show the effort of a smart production team. This game caught me since the first minute and had me hooked for the whole ride. The story has a good pacing and is a bit convoluted in an interesting way, yet comprehensive enough to keep the player invested. The game concept consists of 4 big areas connected to a main one, where each area represents the psyche of a former patient, each having to struggle with their own set of mental disorders. This adds to the aesthetics and eerie feel of each area and the construction of the puzzles.Fighting feels somewhat rigid and clunky but from an artistic viewpoint, it puts you in the shoes of the therapist, who lacks combat skills but is trying to survive. A definite hit with a big thumbs up
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good mix of horror, adventure, metroidvania, puzzle, platformer and shooter, maybe a bit of survival horror too. So yeah, it mixes a lot, but I'd say it's mostly an adventure. That gives the game quite a lot of variety.  It's a pretty lengthy game which very likely take you over 10 hours to beat it. And the game quality is pretty high, so the quite high price is definitly justified.The game consists of a hub level, 4 main levels plus a last shorter "boss"-level. In all of those you have some sort of nemesis enemy who is often after you and you can't kill him but usually you can make him flee for some time. Only at the end of the level, you can "kill" him. They are mostly quite different, just as the different leves are. Tho I have to say it can get quite annoying having to deal with those nemesis all the time, especially in the third level which I actually didn't like at all. But all the others are pretty good.Let's talk a bit about some of those different genres the game tries to mix:-horror: it's actually not a lot of horror, and I'd say most of it is in the first large level. If you are one of those who don't like horror games bc they are too afraid: don't worry you can play this one-adventure: you walk around a lot, listen to dialogues or read notes, story takes a big part-metroidvania: it has exactly one aspect of those but a pretty big one: you find new equipement during the game which you can use to open previous closed areas. But thank god no respawning enemies like in a lot of metroidvanias which I hate bc of that.-puzzle: there are quite a few of them in every level, some of them are optional for collectibles. Most of the puzzles are rather easy item puzzles, like just find a key; sometimes it's not that clear where to go or what to do next tho.-platformer: don't worry, there aren't a lot of those sections and they aren't hard. I actually didn't mind them.-shooter: you often face enemies which also definitly give a horror vibe, just for the first one you have to sneak around but all the others (except the nemesis) you can kill. Sadly there are just very few weapons. () Gunplay is pretty fun tho.-survival horror: just mention this here bc mainly of the feeling of it: it's often a horror atmosphere (even tho not very spooky), have to do some puzzles and kill enemies with your limited ressources, especially early in the game. Tho I'd say after maybe one or two levels I was pretty much always stocked up on ammo. Also there is no limited inventory, except of course for ammo which you can only carry a certain amount.-"RPG": I didn't mention this before, bc it's defintily not an RPG but your character has 4 different stats: speed, health, stealth and stamina which you can increase by finding pills. Tho you can't choose which one gets increased, it's predetermined. I found this mechanic to be quite unnecessary. First of all those increase by a very small amout and the stealth stat seem useless to me bc it's really not a stealth game. You can't realistically sneak around the enemies. There is either simply no way of doing or you have to kill them bc you have to do puzzles in that erea.So this is an easy recommend, even tho sometimes the game felt a bit too long for me, especially during the third level which I didn't like. And the nemesis can get a bit annoying at some point. I'd say you prob shouldn't buy this if you want a shooter (nor the other genres) tho, you should rather see this as an adventure and a pretty unique one with a high overall variety.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy horror games in any way shape or form you should grab this one. Not only does In Sound mind have some good spooks, it has an intriguing story that unfolds well. The exploration is useful and immersive in that the more you play the more you can explore. The bosses were absolutely amazing. Each one had their own significant reason to be how they were, not to mention the design was *chef's kiss*. The music of In Sound Mind really added to the narrative and was simply pleasant to listen to. The humor was nicely placed as well~That said, having to fight monsters progressively more as the story plays through wasn't my all-time favorite part.. Don't get me wrong, the challenge was good, but I really wanted to focus on finding all the details I could and the monsters took away from that a bit. There is an easier mode, so it seems the devs made it possible for a less combative game, I just wanted to play normal as intended for my first play-through.In Sound Mind is easily one of the most captivating games I've played, and well worth it for anyone who likes horror and story games alike!

_childDocuments_.review: Quick disclaimer, this is not a jumpscare game at all. The ambient is tense and dreadful, and there's a trickster-like character that likes to sneak up on you, but there are no cheap jumpscares and the game let's you explore leisurely most of the time. With that said, I have to say this is one of the best psychological horror games I've played, if maybe a bit easy compared to what I expected. Especially I feel like the main antagonists should be a bit more difficult to get rid of. Each has its own gimmick, which once you understand it's just a matter of using the right tool to quickly send them away. If then you would have to hide or do another especial action to actually get a respite it would be more balanced, but basically you're not in much danger unless you stumble to find the proper item (and even then, you get a couple of hits that can be easily healed).All in all a great experience, great horror vibes and great story, which is what I look for in these kinds of games

_childDocuments_.review: -Extremely well produced soundtrack. It heightened the tension as needed and managed to fit in every scenario perfectly. I think I'm addicted to the dynamic theme that plays when enemies are present.-The storyline and it's characters are extremely well written and will keep you hooked throughout the game. Not to mention there's a couple of tear jerker moments here n' there. The cat in particular breaks the 4th wall constantly and it's always a joy hearing what she'll say next.-The game manages to introduce complete piece of sh*t human beings and you'll still end up feeling sympathy for them at the end of the level.-The first half of the game is very reminiscent of old school survival horror with some great memorable moments such as the mannequins in the Mall Level.-The atmosphere is top notch and unique for every level in the game. The levels themselves are very different from one another, each with their own unique location.-Combat is tense and feels just like how it should feel in a survival horror game. You won't be running around blasting fools with Assault Rifles and Rocket Launchers on this one... You'll instead be constantly considering if you should save those precious handgun bullets or use them accordingly. Either that, or panicking and wasting all those precious bullets because enemies are fast as hell!-The main antagonist occasionally appears in a level and randomly chases you until he's up in your face. It's a super simple scare but one that got me good multiple times.-Mostly unique and enjoyable boss fights, with a few exceptions. The final boss fight is pretty challenging and you'll feel a sense of pride and accomplishment once you overcome it, especially on Hard Difficulty.-A cliffhanger ending which still manages to feel satisfying after what you've been through.-Lack of direction, which is visible ever since the first level. Levels often lack proper direction and will cause you to frustratingly wander around until you hopefully come across to where you should be. The Mall level and the Forest level are the biggest offenders of this, they'll start off strongly but completely obliterate the pacing by causing you to backtrack in a maze-like area and get lost in the process. -A few boss fights are unnecessarily annoying and frustrating. The train level with the metal briefcase comes to mind. If you're playing on Hard, you have to constantly follow a briefcase as you're required to change it's directions multiple times in an on-rails scenario... Which would be fine n' all IF YOU WEREN'T BEING CHASED BY A SUPER AGGRESSIVE INVINCIBLE BIG FELLA WHILE DOING SO! Whoever designed that mission clearly just wanted to introduce a time-waster and artificially prolong the length of the game by causing you to restart over and over.-The protagonist is a little on the dull side. He speaks over almost everything that you interact with in the game with a very moody and lifeless voice. I would've rather had him silently project his thoughts of the interaction with a text on the screen, just like older survival horror games. It takes you out of the experience a little when you're being chased by monsters and your dude robotically says "it's blocked from the other side" as he tries to open a door. On the same token, his "session discussions" dialogue is much better in comparison and for some reasons, he reminds me of Harry Mason during certain lines.-No in-game map system. Every classic survival horror title had a map system and it was super useful for players who were stuck. In this game, you get none of that, you only get pre-placed maps which are nearly useless. This contributes to "lack of direction" as if you're trying to find a particular room, especially in the mall level, you either wander around for 20 minutes or open up a walkthrough.-The game tries to tell you that "stealth is an available option". This is a lie 99% of the time as enemies are extremely twitchy and will spot you the nanosecond they see a pixel of you. Just make sure you got some handgun bullets and get ready for a fight everytime there's enemies in the level.-The optimization is wonky and sometimes unstable. While I didn't mind it as much as others, for the graphics that this game has, framerates dip A LOT on a system that should otherwise be able to run it stable at 60 FPS.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: God, this is such a good game. In light of all the trendy modern horror game releases I am so happy to find something like this game, something that has so much passion in it. This game focuses and polishes all of its aspects: gameplay, exploration, horror, atmosphere, music and plot. Oh, the plot and the music of this game are worthy of a separate mention and applause. The absolute feeling of defeat(?) you experience while listening to the vinyl records after completing a chapter is indescribable, even though you have just beaten a huge and challenging portion of the game, the context and things you have learned about your patients, the connection you have formed with them, all of that really falls down on you at once while listenig to these records and realising what role you have played (or rather, should have played) in their lives - you have failed. And you can not change anything about it... but you can prevent those things from happening again. Maybe?

_childDocuments_.review: Personally I really enjoyed and loved this game, the concepts, details and characters were very well done. _childDocuments_.review: Shoutout to the mannequin who'd helped me. I don't have problems with the game nor the monsters, I just hate when those alien with glowing eyes showed up and this spooky detective playing around with me all the time, they are so annoying -_-The game looks scary? It is. But the more you play, the more you'll enjoy it. Honestly, it's an incredible experience. Players play as the therapist who will journey through their patients' minds, whether it's their problems, traumas, or fears, and try to help them find peace. Stories are divided into 5 chapters with a tape as the session. Each chapter is unique, with its own theme and its own monster/final boss. The characters are interesting, the environments are well-designed, and I was moved by the story in Chapter 1 and Chapter 3.Gameplay mechanics were challenging, there are 'frenetic' puzzles to solve, players will encounter aliens (you can either fight them or go stealth). There are also useful items and weapons to bang the aliens. Exploration is a must for me in this game, just in case I collect something like notes or documents to expand on the story. Use the mirror shard all the time, believe me.

_childDocuments_.review: It's worth it. And don't thank me--thank the dev team who did such an awesome job creating this masterpiece!! :] This game is in my top 3 favorites all time, it satisfied an itch I didn't know I had and left me both uplifted and wanting more! Also, Atmosphere: 10/10Music: 11/10Story: 11/10Combat: 9/10Flow: 10/10Puzzles: 10/10Voice Acting: 10/10 blew me away! I  recommend it.I was expecting something out of the ordinary and exceptional, but WOW it  exceeded that! The Atmosphere:The creators made every effort to make the Desmond's surreal world an immersive place. I was always on edge about what was going to happen next and loved every minute of it! I never knew exactly what new twist the creators were going to throw in. As far as the sound design goes, I can't even describe how much I loved it. The sounds always added all the perfect touches to every scenario and made the story/combat/puzzles/etc. better. The scares are soo well done and the game really ramped up my adrenaline with the excitement, fear, and mystery! The Music:As a fellow composer/singer, the music is +S Tier. Period. Not only are the vocals amazing for each of the scores, but the melodies are catchy and memorable, the lyrics are relatable and powerful, and the performance (voice and instrument) is simply exceptional. I wish there was more music like this!! I am blown away the talent of the composers and voices :] The Story:I LOVE THE STORY. I was anxiously engaged the entirety of the game. Along the way, you'll learn a few things (if you're paying attention). I felt like there were very distinct morals throughout that made me feel uplifted and hopeful. It was quite refreshing in contrast to the crazy world we've got today :]. READ AS MUCH AS YOU CAN!!! If you can read something, read it and actually READ it. It is immensely satisfying how the creators came up with a story and a world that come seamlessly together by the end. It's amazing.The Combat:The combat is nice and fast-paced, with elements of stealth and creativity. I felt like the movement/pathfinding of the adversaries was sometimes a bit janky (take that with a grain of salt though, because I am not running on the beefiest of PCs). The combat was smooth and enough of a challenge that it was fun. The amount of ammunition around was balanced in favor of having extra, especially if you have good aim. Though I admit there were a few times I got low, but I don't think I ever ran out of stuff to use to fight. I'm glad the focus was more on the story instead of the combat, though the combat fit well and was enjoyable.The Flow:The whole game flew by (it took me around 15 hours, though I tried really hard to find EVERY secret). Each of the scenarios flowed seamlessly into the next, and the objectives did a good job of guiding you to what was needed next. (Go into your inventory to see relevant objectives) The path forward was usually self-explanatory, or found without too much exploration. Don't stop looking around... like a wise man once said, "There's always another secret..." :]The Puzzles:I LOVE PUZZLES. I am a sucker for good puzzles. I really enjoyed each puzzle (no 2 puzzles were ever the same), they each were just the right amount of challenging (I would've been happy if they were more challenging, though they were great either way) and very creative. This is where I had that itch scratched, I look forward to playing this again in the future especially because of the story and puzzles. The Voice Acting:I ABSOLUTELY LOVE THE VOICES!! I have done some voice acting myself and have listened countless hours of others do voice overs/narration/voice acting/etc. These voice actors the dev team picked did an amazing job both telling the story and making it feel real. I was pleasantly surprised by the caliber of performance and blown away by the amazing job they all did. To the dev team, thank you so much for creating this masterpiece! I can't express how much I love and would recommend !! I don't know where I'd submit an application, but you're ever looking for another alpha/beta-tester I'd be honored to test/give feedback and review!

_childDocuments_.review: This game I would highly recommend, as I feel it was worth the wait.The mechanics of this game were amazing, introducing either a new weapon, tool, or mechanic each level. This game also was lighter on horror for some things, but held intensity and suspense, which I honestly like for a decent amount of horror games now, moving towards that, instead of just relying on jump scares for the scary factor.On top of that, this story was amazing, along with every monster. I also liked the subject it covered, with the name of the game sort of giving away what the subject of the game will be, but it still did it wonderfully.For this next part, it talks about the game. I would highly suggest you don't read the spoiler, until you've played the game yourself. As you can probably tell by the spoiler, you can probably understand what I like about each character. Also,the music I absolutely enjoy, it's not scary normally, but helps set the situation or scene, and the original work from The Living Tombstone (which is how I found out about this game), I also really enjoy.To finalize the good part of this review, you can pet the cat, and there's an achievement for it too, which by far, makes it the best game of the year, maybe ever.------------------------------------------------------------Now for the bad part, which won't be long.The only real complaints I can have about the game, is that sometimes frames would drop and lag would be an issue, so trying to optimize it would be helpful. Another, but I see the Devs trying their hardest at this, and that is bugs, but they try their best to fix them. Other than that, I really liked this game and what it had.

I would like to praise is the pacing, right when I said "huh this thing hasnt showed up in a while" they showed up right when they needed to, obviously the perfect game doesn't exist but honestly I would put the quality of this game up there with titles like half-life 2, despite the genre differencesThis is a great game to play at the time of writing this review too (2023), so many indie horror games are so focused on being "the next big thing" but seem to forget about the most important of them all: being a good game, it's sad this game doesn't have much attention though, I would love to see like more advertising for this game because it feels like no one knows about it, it deserves the attention for prioritizing being a good game first, very underratedThis game thankfully doesnt fall into this trap and Im happy to say I can just feel the passion put into this, great mix of a tiny little humor lines here and there, and references tooThe combat in this game is amazing too, you actually have to hit your shots, otherwise you could be left without any ammo, which is what happened to me, once I realized I had to be accurate though I saw my ammo was almost always at max because _childDocuments_.review: Went into it without any expectations since i got it via the Humble Choice Bundle. Excellent game in way too many aspects.Good: It tries to avoid cheap jump-scare mechanics and generates its spooky yet interesting atmosphere through interesting, very well thought out level design and puzzles. The worlds you visit in this game all have their own theme to it - in the end i found all of them to be quite engaging and interesting. The voice acting and overall writing was superb, most things happening in the games universe are explained through voice snippets and things to read you find throughout the levels. The game can also be quite emotional at times, but somehow it masterfully mixes it up with a general horror atmosphere baseline adding some mild comedy here and there without it being too distracting.Neutral: The enemies you encounter () don't really suit the game in my opinion. The general idea behind this type of enemy is great and theme fitting, but they definitely feel like an unnecessary filler for this otherwise great game that already tells the story well enough without enemy encounters. At best they feel annoying, at worst they pulled me right out of the otherwise great atmosphere and i kind of wished for a difficulty level or game-mode that just doesn't include them.I really don't know how this isn't more popular, it's definitely playing in the same leagues as other more well known AAA horror games out there.Hoping for more from this studio!

_childDocuments_.review: My god, what a wonderful experience. I had no expectations going into In Sound Mind. It was a game I assumed was just another spoopy aesthetic walking sim. But quickly showed me just how wrong that was.  To start, it was quickly shown that this was closer to that of Resident Evil or Silent Hill. And very much for the best. Delightfully Puzzle heavy, with a combat system that does the job right enough. And an atmosphere that walks the fine line between spooky and campy wonderfully. Exploring the building, finding upgrades and gear as well as the next area, while taking on monsters and Agent Rainbow's delightfully campy and sometimes unnerving act, than proceeding to a themed zone, finding new gear to work out puzzles with and defeat the pursuer of the level made for a game play loop that kept me very much excited to keep going to discover more! The gear was another very good aspect. Weapons and tools more often than not had multiple uses. The melee weapon of the game, a thick shard of a mirror for example acting as a board breaker, a tape cutter, and a way to see things that are hidden. Both for puzzles and for collectibles. Each item feels extremely important  and you'll often find a use for it even extremely late into the game.  The bosses all tend to feel interesting, although barring the lighthouse bulb, all bosses are some flavor of puzzle boss, and the weapons are generally geared for dispatching the various Ink Blot enemies that infest the worlds. Only three major enemy types, all of which are generally easy to take care of with practice. You'll be more threatened by the environment and the bosses than any Ink Blot.  The level variety was decent given the small scope of the game. All levels taking place in one of the corners of Milton Haven, the town our protagonist lives in. And these four levels can even be seen from the roof tops telescope. Giving the city a sense of scale in spite of the method of reaching levels.  Each level seems to work with a different theme of horror that is capped with the pursuing boss. The sobbing masked Watcher, the screaming Shade, the perpetually enraged Bull, and the aggressively paranoid Flash. with clear weaknesses that must be exploited to avoid them until you have the means of defeating them.  The length of each level ultimately doesn't over stay its welcome, and the puzzles aren't exactly brain scratchers, Unless your reaching for full completion and or miss something you will make it through the game around the 12 hour mark. The characters are definitely one of the highlights of the story, with Desmond's interactions with Tonia, his cat, who can talk in this strange world being a strong tension breaker for the anxiety of the buildings dark halls, the aforementioned levels and Rainbows taunting and random appearances throughout. Agent Rainbow is the overarching villain of this hellhole, who takes complete delight in taunting and threatening Desmond at each corner, all well doing the best and most intimidating Freddy Krueger impression he can muster. He's frankly not as scary as he'd like to be, but he has his moments where he can genuinely unsettle an unsuspecting player, and the threat of him randomly showing his face or warping the layout of the building its enough to make his presence felt at all times. And his taunting makes the finale all the more effective and satisfying to reach. One complaint that I had heard and I agree with, the stat boosting pills found throughout the levels don't really particularly effect the game in any meaningful way. 6 boosts of Speed, Health, Stamina and... Stealth? Which ultimately feel unnecessary and generally only there to fill the role as rewards. The gains are either limitedly tangible at best, with the health and speed boost, or completely worthless with the stealth boost that really never is needed in the face of just running at top speed. Finally, the music, and of course, this is Living Tomestone. Someone I've enjoyed long before this game, and am happy to find brought there talents to this game! It really adds to the game to hear music with that familiar LT touch to it. Be it threatening boss warning music, or the delightful record themes of each boss, or even the hidden chiptunes and acoustic renditions of LT's library on the guitar in Desmond's room. I am blown away that this is the first game this studio has put to store, the quality is very much there. And I am very much looking forward to the dev's next project. I personally want to know more about the world of In Sound Mind.

_childDocuments_.review: All in all, In Sound Mind was a pretty average game. The gameplay is immensely generic, and it's incredibly easy to just kite enemies and bop them on the head. It's like someone did an FPS tutorial in Unity and decided that no change from that was needed. You could win almost the entire game with your first melee weapon. Despite the horror tag, I wouldn't remotely classify this as a horror game - more of a drama/suspense mystery. The voice acting ranges from bad to OK, and the antagonist quickly identifies himself as generic, annoying, and without depth. After two phone calls I was hanging up halfway through almost every time. That said, the story's pretty awesome. It's a great concept, and is fleshed out and introduced organically, by connected characters whose stories pull you in and help you see those threads. If I get a chance to do another RP campaign, I feel like the story here lends itself to something like that really well. All in all, it's worth a play. But it's not even remotely worth the price tag ($35 at review time). I'd pay $10 at the absolute most for this game, and that's being generous. Even taking into account its strengths, there's better horror games, better stories, better shooters, and better mysteries out there, and most of them are cheaper.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty darn fun little adventure game- emphasis on the adventure part of it. It does a pretty good job of keeping you on your toes throughout the game, although it feels like you can get comfortable quickly. I appreciate the sort of lighthearted moments the game has intertwined with much heavier topics. Because of this, a certain someone ended up being a lot funnier as time went on, even during tense moments. I can't say that's a bad thing, I've had a lot of laughs during certain moments and I'm glad for it.The game's strength really comes from the level design and pacing. You're introduced to new progression mechanics at a good pace, and the game does a great job of introducing things to keep in mind for later. You're on your toes a lot of the time when you're going through new areas because the game always throws new stuff at you to keep you hooked. It's got humorous moments intertwined with more serious ones. My one small complaint in this department is in the basic enemies. Many can't seem to figure their way out around objects, and boxes are their worst enemies. The game would definitely be more stressful if the enemies could jump after you onto most objects, or if combat was restricted to areas where you can't get on higher ground. The more unique enemies though? Really cool, and fun to work around.The voice acting felt pretty good like the actors were really giving their all. There were a few rough moments I think but overall I think everyone did a good job. The music's also pretty alright, no complaints there. The little 8-bit tunes also make for fun little easter eggs.I appreciate being able to replay story sections. However, I wish the game gave you an option of whether or not you wanted to start from the beginning when you do so since you're not able to access old saves (as far as I know) and the game only autosaves. It's somewhat frustrating having to replay the entire story of a section when you want to go back to collect any pills you miss. It's just a little frustrating- there won't be anything new, you're just quickly going through the story as soon as possible so it reduces the process down to busy work. However, that's certainly no dealbreaker and I still recommend the game.Just know that if you're playing on Normal, you'll have a pretty easy time if you're someone who explores every nook and cranny.

_childDocuments_.review: In Sound Mind is a beautifully well put together game. With gorgeous visuals and a real heart tugging story, this game takes the horror genre and manages to make an actually compelling game with it that isn't just another walking simulator. Often I find myself returning to this game to 100% it and I plan to. There's a lot of collectible items and the game makes it really easy to return to previous areas by doing a hub world thing that connects the rest of the environments. Each level is unique and feels different and the way the game handles mental health and certain conditions is with a lot of dignity.It can get icky when you try to create your big boss monsters based off of mental health and illness, so it's good that it didn't just portray these people as monsters, but it portrayed them as human. I avoid going into spoilers here, but know the stories of each of these characters is well thought out and beautifully told by having these environments feel like real demented versions of their realities. The ending is probably the weakest part but isn't without it's merits. I won't touch on what happens in the ending, but it begins to become a little generic and corny for my liking especially with how the rest of the story portrays itself. (And it's only a small portion of the game so I wouldn't worry about it)Ultimately this game has a gripping story, gorgeous graphics, and a beautiful soundtrack along with it. This game is truly one that begs to be played and I'm shocked it isn't more popular. It's likely because when this game released that was the peak of 'mascot' horror with the likes of Poppy Playtime and FNaF SB. This game also doesn't overly on gore or jump-scares and uses the story to scare you or make you feel uneasy. This game will keep you invested all the way through by having a constant ever evolving story-line and you'll soon begin to question your own sanity. I'd recommend this game to anyone who's looking for a really good psychological horror game.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally got around to finishing this and I have to say.  This is my GOTY for the horror genre, first off the visuals are top tier and you can tell they really put alot of effort into creating a beautiful game.  With wonderful looking environments and set pieces throughout it all.  Secondly the gameplay is solid overall, there is enough variety within each location and I like how the weapons were handled.  There is normally two to three ways you can handle the enemies in this game that includes also just blasting them with firepower, I think it's very well done once you figure out some of those methods.  Additionally the game doesn't throw too much at once to confuse the player, normally letting the player just soak in the surroundings before getting you to deal with the threat.  Thirdly the game has a great story with characters that I can understand and connect with their struggles.  I can believe the issues the characters were having in the story and the problems that happened to them.  Lastly the music in this game is top notch, The Living Tombstone did a great job on creating unique sounding tracks for each area of the game and his work has helped made this game more emotional at set pieces.  I hope the team behind this game gets the praise they deserve for delivering us a wonderful horror game that I will gladly replay to enjoy once again.If I had to give an score, I would give it an solid 8.5/10.  It has very few things I can nitpick about but if I have to nitpick to find issues then that means the developers has done a very good job in ensuring the game is fun and engaging.

_childDocuments_.review: (this may seem disjointed and frenetic but and that is because i finished the game an hour ago and wanted to get my thoughts down) I consider myself a fan of horror games I collect them, I play them, I listen to their soundtracks but very few of them I would consider a straight 10/10. Amnesia The Dark Descent, Soma, Observer, Outlast 1&2, The Evil Within 1&2, these are all what I would consider very good horror games but so far none of them have gained a rating of 10/10. I won’t be going into the core gameplay (items, weapons, enemies, pills) but I will be going into the overall quality of the game and how it played based on my own experiences.    the overall quality was very pleasant on the eyes and the environments did not get boring to walk though, In Sound mind genuinely impressed me on a myriad of technical levels such as the soundtrack (The sound design in this game is beyond impressive), the main enemies design's, the puzzles, the level and map design and many MANY more examples.  This game hit the head on the nail for me in so many ways that its hard to put into words. The average playthroughs runtime last about 7-9 hours but it took me 16 hours to complete my first because I wanted to make sure I saw and heard everything I could about the game because it was that good, I never grew bored of the levels or the enemies or the music even the combat (which people complain about) is entirely optional as sneaking is always an option and is usually the better option if you want to save resources.   The games soundtrack and music were produced by The Living Tombstone who is an exceptional artist and playing through the game it is apparent from the beginning to the end that choosing them was the correct choice as the Soundtrack is stunning, the boss themes are 10/10, the quiet atmospheric themes are 10/10, the Vinyl Disks are an easy 10/10. It is my opinion that horror games universally have better music opposed to other genres and that notion is reinforced by this title  I don’t consider myself a person that Is easy to scare/startle but this game ended up doing both in impressive ways that cannot be read and understood. The game has an impressive and stunning ominous atmosphere to it that added and even accelerated the feeling of the game.  I constantly had an interest in the story and the directions it was taking, it felt as though you were unraveling a mystery that had an unfathomable answer until it was no longer unfathomable and everything fell into place. The best parts of the story to me were discovering things about patients through their tapes, the psychology of them were extremely entertaining to read and listen to.  The game gives you as much of the puzzle as you need at any one time. While there isn’t much replay ability (such as extra unlockable’s or secret weapons) to the game it was interesting enough that I could easily play through this game another time, unfortunately there is no difficulty higher than Hard which Is what my first playthrough was on (and my personal recommended difficulty). Granted this game may not be A 10/10 for everyone (it may not even be to other people’s taste) to me it was the easiest 10/10 of any game I’ve played to this day. In short, the only way to truly know if its for you is to try it, the game is 100% worth the sale price and I am going to be keeping a keen eye on the developer’s future project

_childDocuments_.review: When it comes to psychological horror, this game does exactly what you want it to do.  It was truly an amazing experience for me, and did change my outlook on some things. It makes you think about your own life experiences, and what others are struggling with. How people break and how others pretend to manage. What people are willing to do when they are on the verge of falling into a void, looking at themselves in the mirror and questioning what it really is worth, and why it is worth it. This game makes you feel paranoid. Scared. Yet eager to see what's next. It is meant to drag you down a dark corridor you didn't even think of entering. In perspective, you as the therapist (Desmond Wales), have to figure out what happened to your patients. Why they're all gone.  I personally loved every single tape, the unique stories (even Agent Rainbow's). Every patient is valued to you. They are all different. They all struggled in their own way. What's unique is that each patient has their own song in-game, and each song connects with their story. Each patient has a color associated with their name, their case, their life. The color is represented in their story and map, and is beautifully aesthetically pleasing. The two ones that I loved the most were Virginia's and Max's because of the anger and the sadness. The dread. All the meanwhile, you have Agent Rainbow following you around, (he is an outstanding villain) and he voices your doubts, your fears, your worries. He is a part of you.  I would also do anything to experience this game for the first time again. Turning around and seeing something that wasn't there before, yet it disappears again just to mess with you. I will replay anytime. It is one of those games that you could come back to in 3 years and experience something different each time. It is truly  underrated. I thank my friend for recommending me this game, you truly did me a favor.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ incredible. It may have just entered my top ten horror games of all time, pretty impressive for a game that isn't even that scary. In sound mind is a psychological horror game and is the debut of indie dev team we create stuff, if this is their first game I cannot wait to see what they do in the future. What this game consists of is puzzles, light combat and platforming, interesting bosses, banging music and a deeply atmospheric story filled with twists and turns. We play as Desmond Wales, a Psychiatrist living in small town Milton Haven and residing in an old apartment block, we start our journey waking up in the basement with no clue what is going on, what unfolds is an unforgettable journey through the mind and what horrors lurk in our own psyche. I tend to compare games quite a bit and this is no exception, I found the gameplay in line with the first half of resi 7, each level is a robik's cube that needs solving, much like the house in RE7. In terms of tone I found this game reminded me strongly of Allen Wake with sprinkles of SH4: The room. Whilst this game isn't very gore heavy or reliant on shock it does have plenty of jump scares and very clever uses of fear and darkness. I am also trying to avoid comparing this game to amnesia/outlast just because that's obvious and in this case I don't think accurate other than they are horror games in first person and light is important, as mentioned this game is more Allan wake than amnesia. Pros Amazing level design, for a game without a map system I never found myself getting lost. Puzzles aren't complex but they do sometimes require out of the box thinking and environmental manipulation, it felt incredible finding shortcuts and secrets and areas looped back into each other, it's very clear the devs understand what make a good level and I was rarely lost or stuck knowing what to do next. I struggle to pick a favourite level as they all have such strengths and they all play so differently whilst also taking place in radically different settings. Even the hub is jam packed with secrets! As mentioned above this game oozes atmosphere and has some really clever jumpsacres and moments that really surprised me with how much they scared me, the devs really get what makes a good horror game and I love that there is no blood or corpses or any shock horror. Just good old fashioned level design and set pieces that really are imaginative. This game also has a sense of humor that is not cringe, how they make that work in a horror game is a stroke of genius. Music is 10/10, I know it's subjective but I love when games have orginal music made for them and bonus points for vocal tracks. Story was surprisingly good and even evoked some emotion in me, I think that may be due to the themes of the game hitting a bit too close to home but to say how and why would be spoilers.Cons Combat is jank and controls in general aren't amazing, I played this on a controller and sprinting requires you to keep the stick held down all the time which annoyed me but the biggest issue is Gunplay, it's bad but personally it's serviceable. Look I've played call of cthulhu and that game possibly has the worst fps combat I've ever experienced so anything is better than that. It begs the question 'would this game be better without combat' and to answer that I would say no. Stealth is an option but really combat not only opens up options for puzzles but also stops this game falling into the amnesia clone trap. Personally I'm happy it had combat its just my biggest and only complaint and I hope we see it vastly improved in the future. Conclusion To finish this I want to add that I played this on a whim, got it in a bundle and had no idea wtf it was but seeing it was a horror game added it to my October list (every year in October I try and play exclusively horror games.) I'm so so so glad I gave this game a chance and now I hope you do to. Now get your head screwed on for a moderate fee.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this a bad game? No. Is it a good survival horror game? No, the horror is weak and the survival is weaker.  What this game actually is, is B- Psychonauts, and that is way better anyways. It's a linear game with neat levels designed around a character's issues, and can secret hunt in the level for more lore and goodies. It has special spookies for each level with their own mechanic but they aren't anything special. I did not care for the dialogue, but I did like the overall plot , and they did a very good job with the level design and atmosphere of the game. It had some real funny bits too, honestly probably should have leaned on that more.Horror is subjective but having the evil bad guy call me every 20 feet and taunt me in ways that double as hints didn't do it for me. The enemies are generally not enough of a threat to be scary, and design wise they are blobs with big shoot-me targets for heads. There are some trap sections that are tense but most are solved in about 10 seconds. Survival wise, you have limited HP, ammo, etc and that is tense for about an hour or two. Eventually you figure out that because the game requires resources for puzzles, you will be drip fed resources constantly to ensure you can do puzzles. I only died twice in 10 hours on normal, and it could have very easily been deathless if I was less hasty.Overall: not bad. I paid $3.50, I don't know about $35.

_childDocuments_.review: I just wrapped this game up, and I have a few praises and criticisms. Overall, despite these, I would still recommend this game. It has a lot of interesting elements, but there are a lot of unrefined issues that I wish would get resolved or overhauled. These are covered in the lists below:Praises:- Graphics are pretty good. - The environmental effects are awesome as well as the way that certain attacks appear by mobs and bosses.- The gameplay mechanisms are decent but the way they play out to create a sense of panic and intensity during certain events are great. You really get a sense of a dynamic environment while you're playing.- The voice acting is decent, but could be a little less melodramatic, and I feel that comes down to the writing, not the performances. The voice performances are great.- There are some really interesting features in this game that I loved. Looking into a mirror to see 'otherworldly' clues and items was awesome. I really liked some of the temporal effects. The idea of things changing as you looked away was stellar.  The call back to that at the end level was a nice surprise and I got that achievement.- The plot is very intriguing.- There are definitely some nods and easter eggs that are entertaining. You can tell that the game had some solid inspirations.- The fact that there are a variety of mechanisms to accomplish the goals of the levels does keep you interested throughout the game. The game doesn't rely on just button pushing or switch flipping. The variety of interactions and tools was definitely well thought out and implemented well. - That the game focused heavily on mental health was good, but the melodrama of the portrayals was a juxtaposition of what I feel like design was trying to accomplish. It was somewhat distracting from the overall message, but I appreciate what they were trying to do.- There is a *lot of lore* so if you're into games with that this is a huge plus.Criticisms:- By the time you get to the level with the shade/puddle, the 'avoid the boss' mechanism is tiring/exhausting. This is the #1 negative feature of this game.- Level design doesn't have a lot of context clues to indicate where you're going. The levels rely on signs, rather than varied environmental design to let you know you're in a different area and that is one of the roughest things about them. It's easy to forget where you are even though there are maps available and the navigation is not very clear. There are some aspects of level design that are great and rewarding but boy, is there is a ton that is just a slog.- I wish the plot had been fleshed out more. Overall it kind of follows a path but then it becomes a little muddled at the end with too many directions being established in the last acts. - The gunplay is weak. If you're going to make enemies that have multiple health bars/defensive capabilities/aggressive strategies, you cannot handicap the player with poor shooting implementation. Don't make the game hard by just making weapon interaction not as good. If your goal is to create a panic state and force the player to be nervous in combat, make them at least fully capable of taking them down *if they're a good player*. - If you are concerned that you've made a game that is too easy when you make weapons accurate, then rethink how you've programmed your AI to interact in combat. Maybe throw in more enemies so that if the player is too good they'll have the capability to feel only "slightly" overwhelmed instead of just straight up bullied because of weaker FPS mechanics.- I am not sure if the fact that there are some unresolved plot elements is supposed to be a metanarrative or not. Did the game just wrap up early without exploring some of the themes established?This is one of those games that has a strong art inspiration and is clearly trying to communicate something to the player. The character design is good, and the desire to tell a story is strong. The controls are a little lackluster, but I feel like you should still buy and play this game to support the team that developed it. I think that future projects of theirs could be more refined and end up being really solid titles.Even though I'd give this game about a 75-80% (C+ to B-ish territory) I think it's still worth your time. I don't at all feel bad that I paid for this title, and you should give it a go as well. I think the developers deserve to be supported and the game is worth your while.

_childDocuments_.review: At it's core, it feels a bit like Alana Wake, except you know, good. It's good enough where it transcends being a horror game. Modern horror is goes after one singular experience, I'm thinking Outlast or Soma where you just run and hide. Here we have combat, running and hiding, puzzles, exploration, upgrades. It's a full game and it's wonderful. It's scary enough early on until you figure out the gist of it at which point I would call it more tense than outright scary. There is so much love and craft put it, clever details and game play crafted with what the player has in their head and what they expected. I'll say it again; I'm impressed. Where it lags is the technical side. Most of the game looks like it was store bought assets and I was a bit surprised to find out a studio (albeit a small one) was behind this. Granted, there is some production value in some other areas-- I was floored by the hidding music. Like really, there are some genuine good songs in this game that are hidding as secrets. Back on point, I even had some slow down and some weird technical issues. It was annoying but the game was good enough where it didn't ruin the experience. Overall, this is one of my favorite horror games now. If you are into that genre, 100% play this. And even if you're not and like more old school feeling games like Half Life, I would also recommend this if you can handle some extra stress. 7/10. (It would be an 8/10 without the technical issues which others may not have).

I would suppose that would be originality, but I digressOut of what I've played so far, this game is absolutely amazing, It strikes an absolutely great balance between horror and wit. it expects the player well, and indeed it sets up it's scares just as well.I would absolutely recommend this game to just about anyone, because so far from what I've seen, the story is emotional and makes a solid, and effective commentary on psychological issues and does a good job on taking on such a difficult to explain thing in it's own medium. Throughout the story, the game has a tasteful variety of bits, whether emotional, witty, relieving, etc, It does it masterfully. On top of this, is unique and fun game machanics that makes me actually think™.I'll cut to the chase- If you want a game with great charm and personality, this is the one for you. notice how I didn't mention horror game- While the game is indeed scary sometimes, I think it's more of a well rounded experience and story that I don't see often. _childDocuments_.review: I've been enjoying the game so far, it's a great Psychological action adventure horror game, you are a psychiatrist playing through the story of your patients, each story with its unique mechanics and enemies. _childDocuments_.review: This is a game that tries several things at once, and actually suceedds!Intriguing story, psychological horror, shooting, puzzles, in game mechanics - all very well done.You are a psychologist, whos last 5 patients ended up dead/suicided. You yourself end up stuck in some pseudo reality (in your own mind), and try to figure out how that came to be. Each case is about a certain patient, and offers its own reality to delve into and find your way through. Each patient has its own mechanic/item, which after that episode, continues to be useful and part of puzzle solving. The shooting part is very basic: you just shoot enemies with any of your weapons till dead. There's a few variants, but this is not the focus of the game. It's more like a short intermezzo between puzzles and exploration.Puzzles are very well done. Not too hard, but require some thinking and using items you've gathered so far.This game has been a very positive surprise for me, and it has NOT turned into one of those games, where you just hope for a quick end after about 10 hours. You're always curious about what's up next, what your next patient is about and also the resolution of the story.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot believe I bought this on sale for $3. I feel like I stole it! Though, to be fair, I'm wary of not being able to finish horror games, so I generally avoid them. Without such a steep cut minimizing the risk I wouldn't get very far before quitting, I might not have gone for it at all.In Sound Mind has thrills and chills, an engaging story, varied gameplay, a surprisingly great soundtrack for the genre, and a wonderful atmosphere. The game is always changing and evolving, adding new elements at every turn. There are plenty of secrets to discover and background lore documents to find between story sections as well.The game isn't flawless, of course. The gameplay is maybe TOO varied, often feeling unfocused (are we a platformer, puzzler, shooter, walking sim?). The sprint function is finicky at best, I wish a different button or maybe a 'tap button to turn on sprint' mode could have been utilized. Switching between items is a drag, too. Those looking for a straight up horror experience may disappointed after Tape 1, at which point the scare factor declines rapidly (I also think most of the game's best ideas get used in Tape 1, but your mileage may vary on that), but honestly I feel stingy complaining.In Sound Mind is a fantastic experience that I haven't seen anywhere else. Would have been worth it at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: This is EXACTLY what I want in a horror game: no gore, all ambiance and mood. This game has a really excellent story with surprisingly heartfelt moments, and it's not afraid to tackle some tough but thoughtfully handled issues surrounding mental health. The gameplay is fun and challenging with well designed puzzles and unique mechanics from tape to tape so it always feels fresh and interesting. And the pacing was just perfect, both in terms of story beats and in terms of scare factor. I constantly found myself waiting for the scary moment, and it would never come, and then right as I let my guard down, WHAM the perfect nudge of scary to get you right back on the edge of your seat. The game was also surprisingly vibrant and colorful in many places, something I don't feel you see very often in the genre, and it's all tied together with a great soundtrack.If I had any complaint it's the lack of weapon/item wheel. Having to frantically flip between items to find the one you need does add to your anxiety in a tense moment, but later in the game when you have 7-8 items it becomes more tedious than game enhancing. All in all I strongly recommend this game to any fans of the psychological horror genre.

_childDocuments_.review: In Sound Mind is a fairly lengthy survival horror adventure that focuses on the adventure side of things. It's got great writing, a good (if a bit hackneyed) plot, great exploration, imaginative and cool ideas, lovely music, tons of ambience, and a goofy sense of humor. You play as Desmond Wales, a psychologist who wakes up in the basement of a run-down apartment building in an abandoned, flooded town. As you set out to explore your environs you run into some monsters, find a way to enter the minds of four of your patients, discover a conspiracy, and gain tools which in turn allow you to explore further. At its heart the game is a first-person survival horror game - combat is very manageable on Normal difficulty, with the scarce resources the genre demands well managed to give some urgency but never annoy too much... at least until very late in the game. The environments you explore are varied and interesting, with some jumping puzzles and a lot of secrets and information to dig out; Each one of the patients’ worlds focuses on a set of mechanics which make them fairly distinct and gives them a lot of personality, with puzzles mostly being of the traversal variety, and some basic inventory puzzles thrown into the mix. Each world also has an unbeatable 'boss' that pesters you throughout the level making you run through gauntlets of relentless attacks (some of which need to be harnessed to progress) until you face him at the end of the level; All of which are great fun and very imaginative. (Note - these bosses may make looking for secrets a bit annoying, but be aware that you can wait until you get rid of them and finish up exploring at your own leisure before you finish each world.) The tools/weapons you grab range from boring (guns) to weird and inventive (my favorite being a mirror shard that serves as a knife but can also highlight secrets behind you when you raise it to your eyes.) Is it scary? Well, not really - it's not really going for horror or discomfort. It's a more of a horror-themed adventure with a few jump-scares, focusing on cool moments and ideas - and a very healthy, very goofy sense of humor. And while there’s not a lot here that hasn’t been seen before in other games, it’s willing to shake things up quite a bit every so often, giving the whole thing a pleasing sense of variety which again feeds into that sense of being on a grand adventure. The story is very well written, coherent and wraps up nicely. It leans a bit too much on pop-psychology, but has a thematic heft that’s rare in gaming and not a little warmth to it; I loved, for example, .Technically we’re talking about a mid-budget game built in Unity, with all that entails – a certain blocky, murky look, which is well-hidden by genre conventions. Within its constraints it’s a good-looking game, with some striking designs and very moody imagery. The only real problems I ran into was some poorly placed checkpoints, and one bug where a trigger didn’t fire, leaving me locked out of an area (resolved by reloading, but due to the checkpoint issue mentioned above, it meant I had to replay the whole section.) Other than that, In Sound Mind is a great indie game and I’d recommend it without hesitation.

_childDocuments_.review: A game about a therapist starting to lose his mind, so he goes through the recordings of his patients, who showed similar symptomes, and tries to solve the mystery of what's going on with him and what happened to them.Not entirely sure what to say about this game so I'm just gonna keep it simple.The atmosphere is pretty good, mysterious but not particularily spooky. Music works just fine, it serves great as atmospheric noise and intensifies the moments when needed.Difficulty curve is good, it teaches you how to use each new piece of equipment you get as soon as you collect it and new enemies indicate game just got more serious, but they can be beaten without too much problem if you remember about all your tools. I think I was playing on hard difficulty and still didn't have that much trouble beating it, though there were parts where I had to scrape for health.Chasers aren't too annoying, aside from the last one who has ranged attack, allowing him to start shooting you from across the map if he spots you, and he's not that easy to knock out, so it's always better to just seek cover until he leaves.Every tool that isn't a gun has multiple uses, which was very nice to see. Gas mask is an exception, which was a bit underused imo.Game has a slew of collectibles (mostly in form of pills collecting 3 of upgrades your stats), but with item you get very early on and by putting a bit of thought and trial into it it's quite doable to collect everything without needing a guide.Overall the story was interesting and from technical point of view the game was very well put together. It had a few tense moments, but it didn't quite got me as a horror game. Still I'd seriously recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: "In Sound Mind" is quite a complex game in which you, as a former therapist, get to the bottom of the deaths of some of your patients. Did your treatment really drive to them death - or is there more to it than that.That's what you have to find out in this puzzle and exploration game that defines itself as a horror game, but isn't, because there is never any scare, panic or fear. In fact I was very annoyed by the monsters that appeared unnecessarily. And what's with the nonsense with the boss fights? Unfortunately, there is a clear point deduction for this.Otherwise there are levels per patient with huge, varied areas to explore. The puzzles are very good and the surreal, mysterious basic story is conveyed quite well. Additionally the game mechanics are very cleverly expanded with more tools each level, which is very motivating.

_childDocuments_.review: Not even in my weirdest moment I would though that my favorite game I've played this year so far would be a horror game, a genre I don't really play much and don't care about, but here we are.In Sound Mind completely shattered all my expectations out of the water, it is excellent on every single regard, it's 6:00 AM now, and as I write this review, I really don't know what else to say, but I will try:This game is a perfect experience, the charm, the details, so many little things that made me smile or left me horrified (For example the Chandelier of the main hall after tape 3, that was G E N I U S). The scares are earned, there are no cheaply gory jumpscare, it is so much more, the dread lies elsewhere, the atmosphere is dense, palpable, even funny at some times, the story is really (REALLY) well written, well explained, it has substance, and it is very sad... The style, graphics, soundtrack, gameplay, and the characters, OHHH the characters!The only flaw this game has is some FPS drops on intense scenes, but nothing drastic, just some noticeable drops.Believe me, as someone who does not play this kind of game regularly, if you are on the fence about this one, just go for it. Definitely one of my favorites now.Thank you WCS, after this game, I will definitely stick around to see what comes next <3*edit: Oh yea, there's a cat, and you can pet it :)

_childDocuments_.review: I both love and hate horror. On the face of things, I love it. But I hate that 90% of horror games on Steam feel exactly the same, so I mostly stopped playing them out of cynicism.I didn't have that problem with this one. The story is one you've heard before if you've played a lot of horror games. Without giving too much away, the story has some strong elements from Deadly Premonition. But it isn't the story that makes this game unique. It's the way it's told.And that's all that matters in the end. Looking for a unique story is borderline impossible. We've been telling stories for millennia. But still finding a new way to tell a story is incredible. And this one had me hooked from beginning to end. So much that I finished the game in one 17+ hour sitting. I loved that the creepy mannequins weren't bad guys (can't say more without giving a lot away). I loved that all but 2 of the voice actors did their own characters' theme songs. I loved the color palette, even if it suggested this game should've had 3 more levels. Instead, you wind up loving it so much that you start assigning the colors to characters that didn't get a level. Which isn't hard to do if you're playing with subtitles.I've been burnt out on horror. But this game made me feel refreshed. I hope to find others like it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very unique, well written story. While it holds up as a horror game from obvious jumpscares to horror themes, and even with quiet unexpected moments that are actually far more terrifying, it is really a much more startling story that can push buttons and get super uncomfy at places.  The game touches on some very serious subjects and heavy themes, and verges into not always well  handled detailed examinations of various mental heath issues and trauma. Overall the story is unique and refreshing, and plays around the edges of conspiracy theory and psychological studies in reasonably clever ways. The sound engineering and musical score are fantastic - the music has a great range and really fits the game all the way through - it's nice to find a game where the music adds, enhances and holds up the story and never interferes with it.  Really impressive work on the sound.The story goes in and out of various levels, or chapters, and each one is it's own section of story, which plays nicely.  There are puzzles wound throughout the game from progression steps to combat techniques - if you like having to figure things out you'll enjoy this.  Some of them will be fairly obviously fast enough but a few will take a bit of figuring out.  The puzzles are good and reasonably unique and challenging in an averagely fair way - but they are all fun to solve and play with. I enjoyed the puzzle and story aspects of this game quite a lot.The generic enemies are pretty much the same throughout the entire game, and they're not very challenging - a fact that is sometimes made up for with numbers or physical impediments, but they're not offensive either - they just don't add much to the story or gameplay.  The chapter subjects, or bosses, are each very unique and interesting and present some clever non-standard ways to require to deal with them.  Some of the bosses were quite fun.My one real complaint with this game came with the final level boss fight.  Without laying out spoilers, I felt that the level design was poorly planned out.  The mechanics came out of left field - while all the tools  you had become accustomed to throughout the game were still there and functioning the same, all the environmental rules changed in ways that made little to no sense to the rest of the game.  While suitably difficult as a boss fight for its place in the game, it was nevertheless jarring and more distracting from what i expected to be a great culmination of story whittled down to annoying physics, platforming, and touchy timing that just felt out of place with the rest of the gameplay.  In my opinion, the style and design of the final encounters detracted from the game more than it added, and given some of the very clever boss mechanics used throughout the game, I think it felt rushed and underthought and could have been done a lot better.  Frankly it felt like somebody in the side office just "wanted more shooting and mayhem  in there" before it was over.Overall I highly recommend this game. It is refreshing, unique, enjoyable and overall completely worth the cost and time to play.  I intend to go back and get everything I missed first time though. Definitely don't pass this up.

_childDocuments_.review: In Sound Mind is a first-person horror adventure following a counselor named Desmond Wales, a man forced to face himself and also relive the trauma his patients have been suffering through. It has a compelling story and characters but suffers from poor optimization and tedious combat sequences. All in all, it can be a fun experience that deserves a chance.    Desmond Wales wakes up in an unfamiliar place with no recollection of the events prior. Trapped in this nightmare, he soon realizes that there is no way out, and his only salvation is to revisit old tape recordings of patients he had treated before as a counselor. Guided by his loyal cat, Tonia, he begins to unravel a series of interconnected stories, and also brings peace to the souls of his tormented clients ensnared by their demons. The story is the strongest point, and it keeps you engaged throughout the entire journey. I thought going inside the memories of your patients and relieving each counseling session while a gigantic tape is rolling in the background is fairly unique, and is a nice touch of detail. Lore is strewn about in each locale, sometimes hidden, but mostly in obvious places, and they contain pieces of events that will play out later. It's a great way of introducing foreshadowing without making it too overt. Even though it covers a variety of sensitive topics like self-harm, PTSD, and depression, they are handled with tact and respect. I think it’s tough covering cases of mental health issues without it becoming distasteful, but the developers did a good job in conveying these issues and not going overboard with them. As someone with a background in mental health, I appreciate it. Overall, I am not disappointed with the big reveal at the end and look forward to more additions in the future.The combat is fairly standard. You shoot enemies on the head or body and occasionally aim at explosive barrels for AOE damage capable of whittling down mobs if positioned correctly. Resources are plenty at normal difficulty, so I never had to worry about conserving ammo or food items, which act as healing curatives. You have a small arsenal at your disposal, from a shotgun to a pistol, and fighting non-boss enemies is as generic as they come. You can either run away, sneak around or face them head-on. I flee when I can because fighting becomes tedious, and you don’t gain anything significant, so it feels like a waste of time. These lightbulb head monsters materialize everywhere, with variations who spit or charge at you scattered in each story chapter. They are unique, clever, and it only takes common sense to solve them. For example, one of my favorite ones is to figure out the meaning of a clue concerning a “red light”, and upon closer inspection, there’s a TV emitting red light. The usage of visual and audio cues is a great way of inserting clues in without breaking immersion. Even the bosses require you to work out a puzzle to beat them, and while they aren’t a challenge, I do like the setup leading to the climatic defeat. Desmond has a good collection of gadgets to choose from as you progress in the story. From a pill that can act as a grenade and also as a health potion, to a knife mirror capable of displaying secrets hidden from the naked eye, you can use these items to solve puzzles and fend off the opposition. However, the inventory UI infuriating since switching around equipment can be a hassle, especially if you are using a controller because you can’t assign specific weapons to buttons like you can with a mouse and keyboard. Another nitpick I have is that the character has two hands, but can only use one gadget at a time. I would have preferred if the flashlight was accessible at all times while having a weapon or gadget on the other hand. It can be cumbersome when I need illumination at certain places, but I can’t equip my torch at the same time because I have to replace it with another item to complete the task.I was a bit disappointed in the action to horror ratio considering I felt as though it tilted more towards the former. While this isn’t usually a bad thing, the action sequences are where this game falters, and it’s customarily accompanied by laborious fighting encounters. They’re not difficult, per se, but enemies can ruin the great atmosphere it was trying to build up.  In one instance, I was soaking up the tension as my anxiety peaked, then out-of-place battle music crops up alongside these awkward looking enemies. The sense of dread and paranoia was apparent in only a couple of memories where the atmosphere was allowed to develop and unnerve you rather than inserting monsters in just to be a hindrance. To be honest, the game could have flourished more without the combat and replaced it with a system where the psychological horror aspect is more emphasized or utilize the variety of gadgets given to you in each location. For context, my specs are RTX 2070 Super, i7 4790S, 12 GB RAM. Playing at 1080p For the most part, the graphics are beautiful to gaze at, and you can tell how much the developers spent time designing each location. From ships banked forever at the coastline to whalebones jutting out from the sandy beaches, every level is detailed and corresponds to a client’s distorted memories.The optimization on the other hand is atrocious. Every time enemies appear, the frame rate tanks, hovering around the 30’s - 40’s, even lower around bigger opponents. I think this is why I dread enemy encounters because of how awful the FPS becomes. Decreasing settings and the resolution doesn’t improve it significantly. There were also several times where I fell into the world unexpectedly. Good thing the checkpoint was close by.With 16 hours to its belt, it is a good-sized adventure with an awesome story to enjoy. I love Desmond and his clients and would like to see a continuation of their story. It is hindered by its optimization issue, combat, and enemies, and hopefully, they will be addressed in later installments. ...If you have some time, check out my video of In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: At this point, most people who are going to play this game probably already have, but here's my two cents.In Sound Mind is an awesome experience. It's got atmosphere in spades, decent combat, and a compelling story. Is it incredibly original? That's not really for me to say, I think, but it's certainly an interesting concept with the way it all comes together at the end. I was determined to complete the game even after I experienced a bug that forced me to repeat a portion of one of the levels several times. (Very frustrating) Is it perfect, no, but no game is. The combat is a little clunky, and puzzles can be a little obtuse at times, but it's easy to move past the game's flaws to just enjoy the process.I'm actually anxious to try playing the game on the hardest difficulty just to see what it's like, and to experience the game again already knowing the puzzles and the story. In all honesty, I haven't completed the game yet, as you can tell from my achievements, assuming you read this before I complete it, but I felt a need to write a review. I always like to give a positive review to a game that I feel deserves it, and In Sound Mind certainly deserves it.I highly recommend giving this game a try if you like a nice, atmospheric game with some horror, shooter, and puzzle aspects along with it, you should definitely check out this game. Shoot, the music alone is almost reason enough to check it out.

_childDocuments_.review: This was on and off my wish list for awhile because I didn't much know about what this game was.  I thought it was just another over saturated horror walking simulator with some scripted, one time shooting sections, but after playing it I was completely wrong.  I finally decided to get this since I saw it on sale for 90% which was about the price of a candy bar and saw the reviews saying overwhelmingly positive and found they are right.  This is not a walking horror game, although it has horror elements, but more of a first-person, psychological horror, puzzle platformer with shooting elements and quite a few lighthearted weird moments ( freaky mannequins are actually helpful in this game).  The game play is simple yet challenging in some parts but not too hard to cause frustration ad the puzzles are complex yet simple in their mechanics and can be solved easily when you realize what is needed.  The levels are huge and each area feels different and unique without feeling like you seen the same thing over and over. The physics and destruction of set pieces are well done and makes action sequences feel more exhilarating.  It always feels like there is something new that needs to be done and all the bosses in each level are distinct memorable.  The game is well optimized and I did not experience any glitches or freezes and there was no graphical errors even with settings set to ultra.  The developers seem to really care about their customers on this game and I am hoping they do a sequel. I seriously recommend  giving this game a try.

I WANT more!!!Replaying the game will not give me the same level of satisfaction as MORE content would give.I can't wait to see what else you people come up with next.To the devs: Thanks for one heck of an amazing game.Nitpiciking:} Jumping could use a bit more tweaking. A standard jump SLOWS you down.Sprint-jumping feels satisfying, yet sometimes it feels as if though one is about to overshoot.} Combat felt more like a last minute tacked on feature just to move away from "walking simulator".} End combat against the BBEG was WEIRD. As is, was VERY annoying to use, but still fun too.} I'm sad we didn't get to see "shifting walls" or rooms as often as we did. _childDocuments_.review: Summery: In Sound Mind is a story-driven psychological survival horror game with puzzle elements. You are playing as Desmond, a Psychiatrist, in an odd building that seems to be in a city surrounded by odd water. As you make your way through, you find the only way to get out of here is by recalling what your patients have gone through.Pros: A very solid story with a good, slow ramp up to unraveling the mystery. Solid controls and fun gameplay keeps it engaging. Some extremely unique mechanics and experimental ideas. Suburb level design that keeps you guessing where it'll go next. The soundtrack is amazing! Sound design is amazing! And overflowing visual creativity that I can't help but think of a more grounded version of Psychonauts or something similar. Cons: Feels a little too generous with resources for a survival horror, making resources less of an issue than most in the genre. The occasional "im not sure where to go next" does occur, albeit rarely.Overall: This is a very solid gaming experience. it's a very short game and very small, so this is one of those "the experience over the time" kind of deals. As you see, i played this for 14 hours and got basically everything except some highly situational and specific achievements that one would likely do for the achievements. This is well worth it, in my opinion. I got it from Humble Bundle, but would have paid full price knowing what this game is now.
