_childDocuments_.review: I love immersion, don't misconstrued immersion for realism. Two completely different things in my eyes. Immersion to me means believably. Does this world feel real.This is often a box ticked easily by open world games, you see a mountain and most likely you can climb it, windows work because there's actually a world outside, npc go home at night and work during the day etc etc. Simple things that make a world feel real.The setting of this game is an apartment complex with mini "worlds" breaking things up every now and again. The apartment complex from the second I started this game has blown my immersion expectations out of the water. First thing i did when our boy wakes up in the basement was to look for a window and I wasn't disappointed. Even starfield doesn't entertain working windows for the most part or Hogwarts legacy but this game does and it's not boring outside. A half sunken city, we are surrounded by an ocean and a deeply unsettling night that just doesn't look right. This instantly made the game feel huge to me, I wasn't just in an apartment, I was part of a ruined world. The devs clearly cared and paid attention even to the things a player might not focus on and just see in their peripherals, that's immersion.This game reminds me of RE 7 which is as big a compliment I can give it, a small world that feels huge thanks to minute attention to detail, constant world building and a sound design that will have your ears crying tears of joy. The ambience in this title is honestly peak, from the gentle sound of waves in that basement cluing in the player to the situation before you even look out a window to the vast silence of an abandoned supermarket only broken by the wind and various 24/7 on electronics humming.This game has performance issues sadly, stutters and drops frames like nobodies business but it is just so good I don't care. Easily making my favourite horror games list and will be keeping an eye on these devs

_childDocuments_.review: This was an excellent game that truly highlights the best of "Indie" horror game development. I would gladly play another game of this style, and will be excited for whatever We Create Stuff does next!

_childDocuments_.review: Never written a review so hear me out. (AKA, i have no idea what im talking about) /small spoilers kinda?/As a psych nerd I've been waiting for a game that scratched this itch, a fight through broken minds mixed with a sci-fi supernatural horror shooter has got to be the most niche idea that i never expected to come to fruition but this game delivered so hard and not to repeat myself too much but its what i've been looking for more of ever since since bioshock, outlast, Hunt; Showdown and Metal Gear when it started to get into creepy nano tech and parasite experiments.One of the best games I have ever bought for under five bucks and probably one of my top ten favorites at least. I see negative reviews that it wasn't scary enough for some, but basing your entire review on how scary the game was is ignorant to all of the other beautiful factors that makes this game so great. Everything from the music, art style, puzzles, and those damn pills i still have yet to find all of was amazing and it makes me want to run through and do it all again. I also frequently find myself putting the OS on repeat on my spotify (favoring some songs over others).Also some reviews said that the game tried to appeal to too many types of genres and it fell short, but i'd argue that no mechanic felt out of place for a man fighting the complexities of his and others minds, it wasn't trying to appeal to everyone, it was trying to push a narrative that felt fun and interesting, an initiative that I admire and wish more games would take.I didn't mean for this to turn into an attack on negative reviews, I believe any good game should have negative reviews otherwise somebody is lying and again I have no idea what i'm talking about. I love this game 100% recommend at least giving it a shot for whatever price you can manage (I waited for a sale). Almost makes me want to go back to therapy, but I've got that padded room and grippy sock life to live.9.3/10 only wish it was longer, also cute cat and fruity antagonist.

I recommend it highly.My primary criticism is that many of the maps are very large, and there's no in-game map, beyond the stationary maps you find mounted on walls. _childDocuments_.review: It was an extremely interesting experience but i'll leave here 5 things to keep in mind:- Altough it has combat (while not needing it), the gameplay, asthetic, music and map design are absolutely superb;- The story has great twists and turns that will keep you wishing to pursue the adventure to uncover it's secrets;- The puzzles are extremely simple and straight-forward;- While not mandatory i recommend going for the collectibles, not some are really helpfull, but you can also find some vinyls with absolutely magnificent songs (Me and the Boys was definitly my favourite);- Tell me whatever you like, this is not exactly a horror game.... you can't trick me like that, it's a concert, with humor and horror stories. _childDocuments_.review: 7/10 One of the better walking sims I've played.A surprisingly engaging walking simulator that combines good graphics and ambience with a spattering of puzzles, combat and platforming. The story is nothing special: tried and true horror elements culminating in an entirely predictable ending. However, the journey itself is generally enjoyable: each area has unique puzzles and a well-thought out boss battle. The only downsides are that your main character constantly talks to himself for no reason what-so-ever while the antagonist keeps calling on the phone to issue lame, over-the-top, entirely empty threats which often detract from the otherwise excellent horror elements. Fortunately, you can hang up on him (or not even answer the phone), and I strongly advise even first time players to do just that.Despite its flaws, all in all, this one is well worth the full asking price, but feel free to get it at discount if you're on the fence.

_childDocuments_.review: I typically don't play horror games, but this game was recommended to me by a friend and I could not just say no.The Sound Mind is a horror game in which you play as a Psychiatrist trying to save your patients from their own darkness and a mysterious fedora wearing govermant-man who's trying to kill you. The game mixes elements of horror, humor, psychology, philosophy and MUSIC - as expected from a game about psychology and mental wellness. The music in this game is SICK, and definitely worth a listening to!The game takes few elements from typical horror tropes and turns them upside down, giving you a pleasant surprise of a not so typical horror game, thus making it unique.You can tell that the developeres did their homework, and knew their materials and how psychology works. If you ever been to a psychologist, or dealt with personal issues that you had to battle, you will most likely relate to many elements in this game. The ending of the game is very fitting of the theme, and the conclusion of how life just is. (No worries, I will not spoil it!)In fact, this game got way too personal for me as I went (and still going as of now) through similar journey trying to fight my own demons. _childDocuments_.review: I was pleasantly surprised by how much I enjoyed this game I wanted to give it a review. I bought it in a sale sometime last year based on reviews at the time and have just gotten around to playing it through. What I think works well in this game is it has solid pacing. Each level has a unique main threat that pursues you throughout and you are given a new tool/weapon to deal with it and solve puzzles. The puzzles are not that difficult, nor are they overly simple. They don't exactly hold your hand with quest markers cluttering the screen but instead allow you to gleam points of interest with a neat item you receive early on. The new tools you obtain also allow you to open new areas and secrets in the apartment hub you return to between levels.The story is a mystery with each level being like a nightmare based around the main character's patient's issues and anxieties. As you get further in you discover how they are all linked to a larger conspiracy. I felt pulled in by each patient's story and was satisfied by how they ended.The combat is serviceable, breaking up the puzzle solving on the buildup to each level's boss.Have to mention some good quality of life features. You can replay any level from the hub. After beating each level's boss you can remain in the level and backtrack to hunt for secret collectables that increase certain stats. You can grab them while you progress through the level normally but it's nice to know that you won't by locked out of them by progressing too far.Overall a solid game with some great ideas and variety without much padding.

_childDocuments_.review: NO SPOILERSI had been waiting for this ever since the first teaser in 2019.Knowing that The Living Tombstone was making a soundtrack for a game AND it actually looked interesting got me very, very intriqued.The next year when i played the demo i definitely enjoyed it but found it slightly hard to get fully into, some things just felt off and the soundtrack wasnt the most mindblowing thing i had ever heard. Despite that the song A Doll´s House kept my hopes very high as i absolutely adore that song.As time went by and more trailers came out i definitely found myself very hyped especially with the "One Week" trailer and Here Comes A Savior theme song.Now that its out i played the whole thing in just two sittings, then getting all collectibles on a third, and i can easily say i love this game.An insanely good story that actually made me wanna find pieces of text around the levels, characters i genuinely related to and wanted to help, and an ending that hit very close to home.Puzzle games might be the genre im worst at but i loved the puzzles they were super fun and definitely very satisfying to complete i constantly felt like i was accomplishing something.While the individual textures on objects and surfaces might not be AAA tier, the game looks spectacular with its brilliant use of colour and lighting. Theres some truly unique set pieces where i had to stop and just look at it.The complete soundtrack feels so much more finished with some awesome tracks, it can go from creepy and eerie, Intense or just straight up head banging. The vinyl songs you found are all so wonderful and adds so much more depth to each character even if they can feel a little bit exposition heavy in the lyrics. "Bottom Of The Pit" in particular speaks to me and im kinda obsessed with it at the moment.Genuinely one of the most note worthy soundtracks ive ever heard.The things i felt was off during the demo; things like some kinda cheesy dialogue, sometimes over the top voice acting, big maze like areas and other things ended up feeling so purposful and deliberate and made the whole game so much more interesting than most other games right now, its a huge mix of nostalgia for older horror games while adding so much new to the table.Enemy designs are so creative and interesting, levels were fun to explore, collectibles are fun to get and mostly all super useful and the whole thing just left me wanting more which is the best piece of criticsm you could give a game in my opinion.Theres a couple bugs and frame rate issues here and there but overall a very polished package that i would recommend to everyone. Atleast check out the original songs on The Living Tombstones channel if you have the time as they´re genuinely amazingvery very good 9,5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Very solid experience all around. Story and vibes are the key standouts here. A lot of really excellent moments where they effectively pull the carpet out from under you.My two complaints: the first person platforming is really not good. I think that is a common enough problem, but there is more of it than I was expecting. (It's funny because when the gunplay is a little clumsy, it really helps it to feel like a horror game. When I'm struggling to jump over a puddle, I'm just annoyed. Weird, where those lines get drawn.)Light spoilers? Some plot details get relegated to an epilogue, and the whole climax really would have hit harder if they had been introduced earlier. It was not a huge issue because I felt like the stories of the individual levels were a lot more engaging than the overall plot anyway. But still.

_childDocuments_.review: WARNING: SPOILERS AHEAD!NB: I'm writing this review from as someone who has been in the mental health system for years now, and I will be bringing that perspective with me as I write this.Is "In Sound Mind" one of the greatest horror games ever, worthy of being spoken of in the same breath as Silent Hill? Yes. Does it have one of the greatest horror antagonists of all times, engaging and enthralling throughout the entire game? Yes. Does it have some of the best puzzles, atmosphere, music, and level design I've ever seen in a horror game? Yes. Would I recommend it, both at full price and at discount? Yes.But, because I love this game, I want to elaborate on what I feel are its problems. These are just my own opinions that I am presenting here in case the developers or anybody else are interested in hearing them. I recognize that the developers have their own artistic vision for what they wanted to do for this game, and I don't want to invalidate that in any way.So. What is my problem with this game?The main story. Virtually all of it. Yes, a game that I just spent an entire paragraph praising has, in my opinion, a very poorly managed main story, and this results in the personal stories of the four patients suffering as a result.Virginia's story is the best one in the entire game, and there is a very good reason for this: Her entire story is almost virtually all about her. It's not about the Meyer Corporation. It's not about the Central Intelligence Bureau. It's not about Agent Rainbow. It's about her. It's about her past, her thoughts, her feelings, her problems, and the way that Desmond tried to help her.Compare this to the other stories. In Allen's, we spend more time learning about the crash of the Thanatos than we do about him. In Max's, we spend more time learning about the manufacture of Agent Rainbow than we do about him. In Lucas', we spend more time learning about the government cover-up than we do about him. It's all about the evil Meyer corporation, the evil government, and the evil Agent Rainbow.Now, again, I want to emphasize that I respect the developer's artistic vision, but I'd like to elaborate on how I feel each of the character's personal stories could have been improved.Allen has a crippling fear of the dark, seems to be afflicted with Cluster A personality disorders - resulting in paranoia, mild hallucinations, and delusions - and seems to feel conflicted over his mental health issues: Rather than being troubled over his conditions, he seems to relish in them and find an unhealthy sort of enjoyment in them, which is potentially a coping mechanism that he's developed over his life to help handle his issues.Unfortunately, the outro of Allen's story is all about the CIB agents poking around his house, rather than about Allen's issues. Instead of sacrificing Allen's personal story to the main plot, I feel like Allen should have had the chance to elaborate on the feelings he has surrounding his mental health."Doc, I know this ain't healthy. I know it ain't right to like... Well, to like bein' crazy. But I worry what it might be like if I *didn't* like bein' crazy. If I had to accept that I've been ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up and sick for my entire life. That I *am* weird. You said that you can help me, right, Doc? So please, help me get better. Help pull me out of this darkness."Max has severe anger issues, and clues littered throughout suggest that these are inherited from his father. But, again, the outro of Max's story is more about the Meyer corporation than it is about Max. Once more, I feel like Max should have had the chance to elaborate on his feelings."You think I like bein' angry, Doc? Who the ♥♥♥♥ likes bein' angry?! But I just don't know any other way to be, is all. Guys like me, we're supposed to be big, tough, and mad all the time. We're supposed to hit things, get angry, and scream. That's what I been taught my whole life. But I know bein' like that hurts the people I care about. It hurts my wife. It hurts my daughter. And I don't wanna hurt them, Doc. I wanna be a good husband. I wanna be a good father. Help me be a good father, Doc?"Lucas' is, unfortunately, explicitly tied to the main Agent Rainbow plot. He served in an undefined war (Vietnam, likely) where he and his entire squad were exposed to Agent Rainbow, leaving Lucas as the only survivor. Coming out of the war, Lucas has spent his entire life searching for answers to what happened to him back then, all while simultaneously dealing with the PTSD that one normally gets from serving in an armed conflict and seeing one's friends be brutally killed. Even so, I feel that there are still ways to focus on the personal character drama of Lucas, even with him being directly involved in the main plot."I do worry about it sometimes. That I really am just crazy. That this stuff with Agent Rainbow, the Meyer corporation, the government, that none of it is real. That maybe I'm just looking for a way to explain what happened to me back during the war. That I'm just looking for an explanation for what happened to me, and to my friends. And that I'm making up this grand conspiracy to help me understand it all."Now, here's the part where I stop being polite and nice with my critique.This game has fallen for the common misconception about Jung's collective unconscious that has been perpetuated throughout popular culture, including... Well, including pieces of media such as this. The collective unconscious isn't this supernatural thing that psychically connects everyone; that would instead be the noosphere, which the collective unconscious is often confused for. Instead, the collective unconscious is related to human instincts, and is the way that commonalities across humanity result in commonalities across our unconscious experiences. It isn't "Everybody's unconscious minds are psychically connected." Again, that's the noosphere.It is shocking to me that the developers managed to misunderstand Jung's collective unconscious so badly, especially when they have a fairly good understanding of the Jungian shadow. Honestly? Everything related to psychic powers should have been thrown out the window. Just let Agent Rainbow be an experimental bioweapon that got out of hand and affected the people of Milton Haven. There's no need to add psychic powers on top of it.I have nowhere else to put this, so, here it is: One thing that I noticed at the end of Virginia's story that put me off slightly was that Desmond remarked that Virginia would "never have done this [her suicide in Homa-Mart] on her own". Really? A young girl who had remarkably severe mental health issues even before exposure to Agent Rainbow wouldn't have committed suicide? I feel like it would have been better for something like: "Virginia and I were making so much progress. She was improving so much. But then... Something happened. Something shattered it all. And I'm going to find out what it was." The same could be done for Allen and Max. "Allen was so close to overcoming his fears, so close to becoming better. But then something drove him right back into that pit." And then, for Max: "Max was finally improving. He was understanding his anger, and where it came from. He was calming down. But then something revved him right back up into full throttle." So, to summarize, here are my personal issues with the game: The personal dramas and stories of the four patients are compromised by the existence of the main plot, which itself is muddled by silliness about psychic nonsense and horrible misunderstandings of Jungian theory. More time should have been spent developing the characters and exploring their issues, and less time should have been spent hammering in how evil the Mayer corporation and the government is. Again, though, I would still recommend the game, and give it a B+ rating....also, I recently lost a cat of 21 years. So the Tonia stuff hit me real hard. So, good on the devs for that.

_childDocuments_.review: Every so often a game will come around that I don't want to stop playing until the end. Typically, I have no problem switching between a couple games every few hours or days as I get my fill of it and need to play something else. In Sound Mind is one of those games that got me invested right from the start and I couldn't put it down until I figured out what was happening in the small town of Milton Haven.You are Desmond Wales, a therapist whose patients are having mental crises and in some cases dying. You start the game by waking up in a dark basement floor of an apartment building that seems to be a manifestation of your mind. In this building, a few of the doors in the apartment building are actually gateways to the homes of your patients like Virginia, Allen, Max, and Lucas. As you enter their homes you are able to find a tape of their therapy sessions with you. When you bring these tapes back to your office, you can turn back time and experience their breaking points. These tapes become explorable levels in which you try to figure out what has happened to your patients. As you progress, you end up discovering that your patients actually are linked in a way that you never imagined.Each area, including the apartment building, have secret areas and have interesting puzzles that must be solved in order to fully explore and understand each character's motivations and emotions. There is a nice variety of puzzles that involve using several tools that you unlock through the play through. As you unlock these tools more of the apartment building opens and you can reach new locations. A few examples of these tools are a shard of a mirror, which you can use to see hidden notes and objects, and a flare gun that allows you to pass thick shadows.Once you reach the end of these areas there is a boss fight which involves using the items you have unlocked to solve these battles which are mostly puzzle based fights. While there are weapons such as pistols and shotguns, they are mostly used to destroy lesser enemies. These enemies have weak points, such as shooting the glowing light on their head for a quick kill. The boss fights are usually fast paced and there is plenty of action to balance out the searching and navigation portions of the adventure. The puzzles remind me of Resident Evil, such as collecting medallions to put into a lock, or twisting valves so fluid will come out the other side of a pipe. Most are simple but some can provide a decent challenge.There are plenty of notes to provide lore and items scattered around the levels such as healing items, ammunition, and pills. These pills are used to permanently increase certain passive stats like how stealthy you are and your max health. I found it fun to search high and low for all the pills in each level and quite a few of them are well hidden and require the use of your tools to find them.The game's environments are really well done. You will investigate different locales such as a lighthouse, a quarry, and a factory to name a few. These levels take about 2-3 hours to fully search and unlock all the secrets. The best way I could describe the story without spoiling anything is to say it's as if David Lynch filmed an episode of X-Files. Plenty of conspiracy and paranormal events fill the 10-13 hour play through. There are also a lot of dark ideas that are explored in "In Sound Mind" such as suicide, PTSD, and domestic violence. I didn't feel as if they were portrayed in a joking way and that these elements were treated with respect and not taken lightly.One of my favorite aspects of the game was that after each level, you can go back to the room of the patient and try to find their secret vinyl album. If you find the album, you can take it back to your office and listen to it on your record player. Each song is sung by the patient and gives a retelling of their story. Each of the songs were really well done and it added an element of sadness on top of their already sad story. All together, the music fit the game perfectly as well, not just with these musical selections.There is a lot to like about In Sound Mind! When thinking back on my experience with the game I would say that the downsides are relatively few. Some of the levels felt like they dragged on and sometimes secrets would be obvious but getting access to them took measures that felt unnecessary. For instance, I could have sworn I knew the way to unlock a secret and it made logical sense but executing it wouldn't work. Also there were some elements of platforming which people may have an issue with since the game is in first person.Overall, In Sound Mind is a gem. If you are looking for a psychological horror game with creepy Twin Peaks and X-Files vibes then I would definitely consider giving In Sound Mind a chance! You can even download the demo to get a feel for the game as well which is great if you are on the fence. You won't be disappointed!

_childDocuments_.review: In Sound Mind is one of the better psychological horror romps of the year, considering the sheer lack of its kind of late. It is unfortunately short, albeit only around 12-16 hours on average. But the condensed story and tight cast make up for the game's quick runtime. The horror aspect of In Sound Mind relies on the environmental. psychological, and jumpscare aspects. Eventually, these all wear out as the chapters progress further, and it slowly switches to a puzzle-mystery and survival run as Desmond Wales uncover more of the story. Explore enough of every location, and lore drops are aplenty. The game's unique approach allows you to experience the story of every character, and still be able to keep up with the game's overarching narrative. Combat is probably the game's weakest aspect, but by no means a deterrent to decent gameplay. Save for the last tape, most of the combat in-game don't really scale. Desmond will only encounter at least 3-4 types of grunts/inkblots. Bullet economy isn't even a problem, since ammo is littered everywhere, even in hard mode. What's impressive, on the other hand, is how the game is able to incorporate level boss mechanics into puzzle solving (case in point: luring the shade to specific objects to melt away a new path, or having to lure the bull to destroy barricades). If nothing else, In Sound Mind is one of the rare few games where you can pet the cat as frequently as you want. That alone is enough to recommend this game. PROTIPS: - The shotgun is easily missable, since it's optional. Once you get the flare gun on the 2nd tape, head to the 1st floor lobby of the main building and head on to Ventilations. Shoot the dark puff of smoke with a flare and find the shotgun hanging inside the vent. It's unreachable, but there's a breakable board holding it up. Break that, and head to the basement. Take the stairs on the left after exiting the elevator, shoot any dark puffs with your flare, and retrieve the Shotgun. - If you're missing 4 pills in the main building, it might be the vending machine. Remember to interact with the vending machine on the 1st floor near the stairs to the main lobby. Only after interacting with it will the Homa Mart Coins spawn throughout the building. - In Lucas's Tape, don't leave the church until you've found a freshly made grave. You'll find a vinyl there.- Always return to your patients' apartments after finishing their tapes. The new weapons/items you get will always unlock a new area or chest where their vinyls are found. The Audiophile achievement won't appear if you don't display the vinyls on the shelf beside your record player. - You might find a pen and paper in the Homa Mart level, but is entirely useless throughout the level. It's only used for an achievement "Turn that Frown Upside Dow" by interacting with a mannequin's face with the item.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic horror FPS with a great balance of gameplay and storytelling.  You essentially take on the role of a psychiatrist who is trying to figure out what is going on with the world around him.  Without giving too much away, this "world" slowly reveals itself as you progress through the game and play through each of your "patients" experiences.  The level design for each "patient" is unique with a myriad of puzzles strewn about.  There is very little repetitiveness and it always feels "fresh" when you begin a new chapter.  The story narration and voice overs and crisp and clear.  The bosses for each chapter are done extremely well as they present very different challenges to the player.  The only critique I can think of is that the variety of non-boss enemies is a bit lacking (I believe there are only 3 types in the game).  The story itself is excellent and it does leave room for a sequel which I'm crossing my fingers for.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Old fashioned 1st person shooter with small but interesting extra mechanics to keep things fresh. Enemies are redundant but the game is short enough so it won't get old. The game is about 13 hours if you rush it. Bonus points for letting me pet the cat.Story: As therapist Desmond Wales, you awake in an apartment complex with no real idea how you got there and what is happening. This area will serve as your hub between levels and you will unlock more areas as you gain access thanks to gear brought back from levels. You will quickly realise that you will be revisiting places and events of your past patients and that there is something weird linking them all, and you. There's also some weird creep, let's call him Agent Rainbow, following around, he's a weirdo.I personally felt that the story was a bit loose, as in it had a tendency to take a back seat, but the swiftness was appreciated; by that I mean that it didn't beat around the bush and everything progressed quickly. That is something a lot of recent games lack.Gameplay: It plays like any old school shooter: Half Life, L4D, Halo, name it. The main difference from regular shooters is that they added a few items which are often directly linked to progression, for instance, you will quickly find a mirror shard which allows you to cut through tape and break planks, of course, but when held up with the right click, you can see behind you and light up objectives and item pick ups. Is it awkward? Yes. Is it kinda cool? Up to you to decide. I found it both awkward and kinda cool.Very limited weapons selection but they get the job done. The combat isn't constant, you will be spending about as much time exploring, solving puzzles and fighting. It was a good balance, at least to me.Exploration is strongly recommended as a lot of items are somewhat hidden, and some grant you permanent buffs to health, stealth (wtf is that anyway, never had to use it in this game), stamina and speed.Item pick ups include every necessity; ammo, health and consumables. They aren't rare, but that doesn't mean to go shooting willy nilly. To me, the puzzles were simple and satisfying.It's important to know that when you find and read a note, the game doesn't pause, so put away (or turn off) that flashlight and make sure you're outta combat before taking your sweet time reading those.The game does NOT have a manual save, it's 100% autosaves. I hope your better half isn't the type to declare when you're ready to stop playing.Graphics: Nothing amazing here, but it was fine for me. I had some slowdowns and I could never tell why. Maybe for area loading? But it didn't make sense as it was just jumping down a platform or entering a hallway... Anyway, it didn't impede me in any way, it was just weird.Audio: While there are 8 bit tracks and a couple of Vinyls (The Vinyls were pretty good) to find and play at Desmond's Office, I didn't find the overall in-game tracks to be amazing, they just got the job done. The sound effects were average at best. The voice actors were the better part of the experience. All in all, and of course this is just my personal opinion, I found ''In sound Mind'' to be a good game, especially if you get it on sales.... but it won't be one of those memorable ones.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very well thought-out game for an indie dev, a clear vision and lots of love was put into this one. I would describe it as a horror-themed narrative-driven action/adventure game.Decent voice acting, puzzles, some stealth and action sequences, a lovecraftian influence throughout the story, and quite a bit of originality overall. No cheap jumpscares yet atmospheric with its interesting environments, every level is different enough and features some sort of "boss" you need to defeat with different mechanics each time.It has an actual story, a small hub world connecting the levels that has you backtracking with some metroidvania elements, secret areas, even collectibles in the form of vinyl records containing songs pertaining to the story of the level you find them in.Looking forward to future releases from this team, keep it up!

_childDocuments_.review: A hidden gem.I've never really heard anything about this game till about a year ago when i stumbled upon it by clicking through a Steam discovery queue. It looked interesting so i've whishlisted and forgot about it. During this years Summer Sale Event it was available for a couple of bucks, so i thought "eh, why not". Long Story short: The reviewscore is well deserved. The game shines in its storytelling, setting and atmosphere, albeit i wouldn't call it a horror game in the classical sense. Its more surreal and psychological as it is gory. Do not expect Silent Hill or something like that.You play as Desmond a psychologist, one day waking up in a crumbling, distorted world, challenging your own sanity. You relive the trauma and death of your patients in a bizarre, twisted projection of reality while trying to unravel what lead to their shared demise and ultimately prevent your own; all while a mysterious shadowy figure tries to break you physically and mentally. While doing so, you are being hunted by diffuse shadow beings, originating from a strange mist oozing into the reality you are trapped in by what seems to be a unknown chemical slowly consuming the world around you. Also, you can talk to your cat. In terms of gameplay, In Sound Mind is a first person story rich horror puzzle game. The game features multiple types of weapons as well as a combat system, but that is not where its focus lies. Do not expect a horror shooter. If your a decent FPS player, you can rush through the gunplay sections without breaking a sweat. Most weapons are actually used to solve puzzles or provide specific abilities used throughout the course of the game. For example, the Mirror Shard (your "knife") lets you see into different realities, showing you things that are hidden in this one. The puzzles however are engaging and sometimes require some out of the box thinking. They don't feel forced but instead blend perfectly into the games twisted atmosphere. The level design is very unique. Every patient plays differently, very much resembling the kind of mental illness they were suffering before their death. The soundtrack underlines the bizarre strangeness of the world perfectly. Imho, the game is worth its pricetag although you can get if fairly cheap in current sales. Give it a try, you most certainly won't regret it. And if you do so, give a high five to Dave for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Title: In Sound Mind: A Haunting Psychological ThrillerRating: ★★★★☆In Sound Mind, developed by We Create Stuff, offers a chilling and mind-bending journey into the depths of the human psyche. This psychological thriller delivers a unique blend of horror, mystery, and puzzle-solving that will keep players on the edge of their seats.One of the standout features of In Sound Mind is its atmospheric and hauntingly beautiful environments. From abandoned hospitals to eerie mansions, each location is meticulously crafted to create an unsettling and immersive atmosphere. The attention to detail is remarkable, with eerie lighting, disturbing audio cues, and subtle visual cues that constantly keep players on their toes.The gameplay mechanics of In Sound Mind are centered around solving puzzles and unraveling the game's intricate narrative. The puzzles range from cleverly designed brain teasers to tense stealth sequences, providing a good balance of challenge and variety. The game also incorporates psychological twists, blurring the line between reality and the protagonist's own sanity, which adds an extra layer of intrigue to the overall experience.

_childDocuments_.review: So this game hits a lot of high points that are amazing. The middle section kinda breaks down a bit, but by the end, it all comes back together to still be an overall solid horror experience. This is from the perspective of someone who plays a LOT of horror games. This is also going to be spoiler free aside from very generalized comments about how a chapter feels. Pros: Horror - The horror elements are solid! Hooray! Not really and shrilly loud jump scares, good atmosphere, well thought out tension and mind tricks too. There's even a little bit of humor sprinkled in there to balance out the spoops. Story - The story is pretty straight forward. You're a therapist, your patients have been dying and you're listening to their recorded sessions as a way to kind of relive and investigate what happened, but in a really trippy way. There's some parts that don't really make sense, but more on that later. Visuals - Holy crap. There's some sections that are super trippy and psychological that I just looooove. My mind was blown at just the imagination the game devs have as well as the nice attention to detail. It was never disappointing. Length - I don't like to advocate or complain about a game's length, because really the experience is what makes it. I've paid $60 for 5 hour experiences that were incredible and I've paid $20 for literal hundreds of hours I'll never get back and I still like it, however, horror tends to have a problem where around the 4 hour mark, it gets stale. You recognize the enemy AI or the jump scares or whatever mechanics it has and it becomes dull and predictable. In Sound Mind does this a tiny bit, but it's never as bad as each tape introduces a different mechanic that kinda keeps it a little bit fresh. Gameplay - Also worth noting, I usually hate combat in indie horror. Combat and horror are difficult enough to do and very few do both well. In Sound Mind does a pretty good job of balancing it all out. The combat is good enough, but not super involved. There's a couple of cons within this that I'll get into. Cons: Combat - Okay I know I just said it was balanced, BUT for whatever reason, a lot of horror games just toss a LOT of combat towards the last quarter of the game and In Sound Mind is no different. The last section was just me mindlessly shooting things and the combat is just good enough to be okay, but not good enough to be a good combat game if that makes sense. Story - This was also a pro, BUT some parts were weird to think about. Like we seem surprised or enlightened by whats on the tapes of our own sessions...but we were there. We should already know this information. I get that it's to review the case or because it's the upside-down or whatever we're a bit hazy on details, but it never really feels like that's why we don't remember anything. Pacing - The first chapter of the game is phenomenal. Amazing. Bravo. Loved the atmosphere, the story, the scares, everything. Top notch. Unfortunately this section was the free demo which was INCREDIBLY generous that the demo was an entire chapter and the best part, but it's all (mostly) downhill from here. The third chapter in particular was VERY long winded and the boss was very cool looking, however it did last far too long and it was very buggy for me. I couldn't tell if what I was doing was registering correctly and once I had beaten the boss, I was running around to find ammo, but once the boss was down, all these invisible walls went up and prevented me from approaching the boss. I had to restart and goodness that was awful. The last chapter is also pretty long winded and very repetitive. I found myself happy to reach the end to be done with it and not wanting more, which isn't a great place to leave it right? Missable objects - Super specific, but I did miss the 2nd weapon and I went onto the next chapter and was constantly running low on ammo. I realized it would've been a LOT easier if I had picked up the 2nd weapon before I went in, but I just happened to miss it....due mostly to my own ADD. But still. TLDR; Okay so this game is great. The first chapter is by far one of the best horror experiences I've played. The third chapter I actually actively hated, and the final area was just okay. Overall though, this is absolutely worth the purchase and I had fun with it and if you see my track record with horror game reviews, I'm not often impressed with horror games. (Mostly due to my own desensitization to horror) so I can safely recommend this to anyone looking for a solid experience.

_childDocuments_.review: If there's one thing I could say negative about In Sound Mind, it's that it's not particularly scary for a horror game. It has elements that would normally provide that kind of tension, like each stage featuring a (very cool) main threat that can't be killed and frequently comes after you, but the means of dispensing with them are always close at hand so you rarely feel like you're actually being "chased". There's a stealth system that you can upgrade through collectibles, but it's almost never necessary; the maps' open nature means sneaking by common enemies isn't really worth it, because you never know if you're just going to have to sneak past them again on your way back, and even on Hard there's always enough ammo that it seems like you're expected to just fight (which is admittedly fun enough to not be a problem).The reason I don't hold any of that against the game is because it doesn't rely on that one trick, either; the full length clocked in at around 13 hours for me, and in that time it dished out heavy doses of comedy, tragedy, and intrigue enough that I stopped caring very early on about getting my Halloween frights and just wanted to see where it all went. It's not very subtle, but it's heartfelt enough to power through it. It's not very hard, but it's creative enough that I didn't care. The story is backed up by both a full voice cast and a great soundtrack from The Living Tombstone, and the puzzles are exactly what I would expect from developers who were previously known for their contributions to the golden age of Half Life 2 horror mods. The people who know what I'm talking about (shoutout to the real ones) will feel right at home here.

_childDocuments_.review: The thing I really liked about this game is its story. It isn't your typical "stuck in your own mind" scenario. The gameplay is fairly decent, each section of the game introduces new mechanics and there are a lot of really good moments. The music is also good. In addition to standart soundtrack there are also music records scattered around in the game, one for each important character, that contain songs sung by said characters. The one thing I did not like was platforming - for some reason, the length of your jump is tied to your framerate, and the game isn't that well optimised(and to be honest my computer isn't that great). So I really stuggled at the platforming sections, of which there are many. Overall, I do recommend you to play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Having finished the game and completed 71% of its achievements I must say it is definitely not worthy its reviews. The game is definitely not scary or intimidating, the puzzles can be clever sometimes but the level design is very boring and you will feel like you want to "skip the levels" because it can be really, really monotonous. The theme of the game is interesting, the struggle of the characters can be relatable in part and feels humane. However it is not enough to make up for the shortcomings during gameplay. It has its own charm but it fails terribly at doing what it is marketed to do both as a horror / scary / psychological thriller. The insight into the topics feels childish at times, even, taken with levity and ingenuity, a very pompous perspective on things that are actually way more grave than the game tries to portray. BIG SPOILER: . If you want to play this be wary that you are buying a "FPS puzzle shooter" with very small, childlike in nature insights into the frailties of the human psyche. Again, it is a FPS. Not a groundbreaking game in the horror genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I regret buying this on sale. This game has so much love and soul in it.Every once in a while, you stumble upon a hidden gem that blows you away. This is one of those cases. I'll divide this review into three parts: open info, spoiler info and super-spoilers. Read the spoilers if you want to know a bit more of what's happening. Read the super-spoiler if you've already beaten the game. That being said, I recommend that you stop reading RIGHT NOW and go in blind. Hey, if you hate it, there's a refund button, right? But you won't.Ok, so let me preface this. I've played a lot of horror games in my life. One of my favorite genres, honestly. This allowed me at a certain point to gain eyesight to differentiate between horror games and horror-themed games. What's a horror game? Think Silent Hill 1-4. What's horror-themed? Think Resident Evil post 3, Killing Floor, Dead by Daylight, Alan Wake. Nothing wrong with that, I do like horror-themed games as much as I like horror games. One aims to scare you, the other puts you in a setting that the character might find unsettling.I would classify "In Sound Mind" as a Horror-themed Psychological Thriller. Think Eternal Darkness. It's not scary. I mean, I don't know you. It might be scary for you. But if you play a lot of horror games, don't expect to be scared.This game is about a character finding themselves in an unsettling situation.So, why is this game Overwhelmingly Positive? For so many good reasons. It's sort of an intersection of many gaming influences. I got strong vibes of Alan Wake, Half-Life 2, Resident Evil 7-ish, Someday You'll Return, The Medium, The Evil Within and I'm sure some other major things I've missed. The developers are clearly very well-versed in gaming culture, or, rather, the cultural and design heritage of gaming, and it shows. They not only understand it, they build upon it.Broad strokes? You're in a building full of puzzles trying to progress the story. Slight metroidvania vibes par for the course for horror games. I've played on Hard and it's not hard, but I am very experienced, so perhaps you'll have a different experience. The puzzles are great. They are varied, immersive, innovative and fun to solve. It's surprisingly lengthy, but not in the way that overstays its welcome. It's just a quality game with lots of content that is all great and varied. I was excited to do every side activity you could find.One really smart and welcome gameplay decision: fairly early you get an item that allows you to find collectibles. Thank you, devs!The music in this game is astonishing. Especially the songs you hear that you get as a reward for doing major things in the story. I often default to gaming while having a video on another monitor, but, credit where it's due, this game had all of my attention all the time. When I got another song to listen to, I was excited to go and listen to it.Visuals? Technically speaking, it's not that impressive. It's ok, it's not ugly, but nothing to write home about. However, the developers use special effects, shadows, direction to great effect. I've caught myself just basking in the beauty numerous times during my time with this game. There are clearly, no offense, narcissists in the dev team who truly, fully, deeply understand beauty. I was thinking, "I wish I saw this in VR".I won't touch upon the story in this section, but it's really, really good. Now, characters are all interesting, not deep per se, but well-written and compelling. Good writing, good dialogue. One character stands out: the antagonist. That guy adds so much to the experience. He keeps trolling, mocking, harassing you with phone calls and showing up and I was always looking forward to our next meeting. What a character. So much charisma. They hit the nail on the head there.But, as any good horror(-themed) games, this one also excels in humour. The see-saw of humour and tension is perfect. On that note, this is one of the few games that got me by jump-scaring me with a still object. And then subverting that jump-scare instantly to the point I felt genuinely impressed and warm inside.Downsides? The combat isn't anything to write home about. It works, it's not annoying, it's passable. However, the gameplay is stellar. I didn't bring up Half-Life 2 for nothing. There are some seriously talented game designers on the dev team. There are so many creative gaming situation here that don't really repeat or overstay their welcome. It's a REALLY FUN game to play. I felt younger playing In Sound Mind because it made me feel the joy of gaming I usually felt back in my teen years. Valve should really look into hiring these people. They are that good.I also wish there were Dualshock/Dualsense icon input images, but it's a moot point, I ended up using KB/M for the game anyway.There is a cat you can pet regularly.Techincal side of things, no problems. No crashes, no lag, no stutter, nothing. It just runs smoothly.Spoilers starting. I'm going to describe the gameplay loop and try not to touch too much upon the story. Super-spoilers. Read this only if you have beaten the game: Do a sequel or make more games! 9.5/10 DESPITE technical issues. Also, the developers really, really respect and love cats. They deserve your money.Achievements: Easily doable in 15 hours, not sure if there are missables, but you can replay sections. Good achievement design overall.Edit: This game desrves a BAFTA award. Went straight to my favorites on Steam. Also, if you complete it, there is an amazing animation music video you unlock. This game is so good.

_childDocuments_.review: To be perfectly honest, I got this game on a whim. I wasn't sure exactly what it would be, but I saw The Living Tombstone was part of the project and thought, "What the hell."At first, just after loading it, I was certain I knew what it was. It was one of those meme-tastic sarcastic quasi-games that smacks of low budget and low effort. The idea persisted for perhaps the first half hour of the game. About the time I got the elevator to work. I figured I had it pegged and the game was pretty much over. After all, at that point it was overly simplistic, had a few jump-ish scares and had a good atmosphere.Little did I know that was just the intro. Once you start finding and reading the notes, then you find your first tape, you start to realize there is a LOT more going on than was apparent with the simple intro video, the typical locked in a basement get yourself out game. The thread of a plot was picked carefully between exposition, atmosphere, and a cat. Cat-a-Tonia, who, as you progress you begin to understand how clever her inclusion actually IS in the game. No, I won't give away any more than that.As you play, you begin to connect the dots. Each time you leave a tape, you understand a little more of the story NOT being told while you are hearing the story that IS being told. Big pharma drug experiment. A massive F up. Government cover up. Tainted water. Four separate stories come together in the subtle details until you finally by the fourth tape get a really good understanding of WHY, WHO, and WHAT. Maybe even part of the how. Then the climax. Things are close to what you might have guessed by this point and you are confronted with an enemy who has dogged you from the shadows from the beginning. Cue a boss fight that has no actual player on boss violence but still gives a satisfying and decisive victory.While not on the level of SOMA for twists that make you think LONG after the credits roll, it still leaves you with more to think about than you might have believed from a game that starts so simply. There is a much more powerful story with deep emotional notes throughout than you might ever possibly consider just from the store page, the artwork, and the like. This game deserves to be played, deserves to be thought about after you tease out the last hidden achievement. Is it perfect? No. There are clipping and pacing issues here and there. Once I jumped and clipped through the level and had to start over again, but only once and I could not repeat it. The apartments serve as a hub world with its own exploration to do, but it lacks the pacing of the levels. Not a big quibble, but it feels overly empty by the third visit.I got quite frustrated by Lucas's tape. Not only did you have the story and its achievements, the level was huge and sprawling with multiple crisscrossing and doubling back pathways, but it added on top of the pills you were looking for also his segments of the session tapes to find. I think that brought the collectibles up to something like 22 or 24 on a level already made difficult by the back and forth, the lack of a player oriented map, and a machine hounding you when you're out in the open. None of the pills seemed to have a terribly large effect on our protagonist, save the health pills. You still run out of endurance VERY quickly when sprinting about, your regular movement speed doesn't seem to increase too dramatically and stealth is pretty much a joke. Things see you far too easily and you might as well just run from the bosses. None can be killed or even stunned long until their final sequence. That's not a huge issue. having a stalker in every level works, especially how they tie in to their stories, but it does make for a couple of save-reloads that you wind up just rolling your eyes over.Do not mistake me, though. This is a well done game. Every part of it works, just some parts a little better than others.Absolutely worth playing through, at least as many times as needed to get the achievements. And it seems like there will be a second game. You'll understand when you get there...

_childDocuments_.review: Some things I liked about the game:- The gameplay is very solid, it doesn't do a whole lot new but it does have some unique ideas that keep it fresh- The level design is very solid, I felt like each level was engaging the whole way through, and each level was different enough that it didn't get old.- The aesthetic is super good, I really like the look of the game and I like how different each level feels with their aesthetics- The soundtrack works really well, and each level's tracks really compliments the vibe- There are puzzles, and I think it does a pretty good job with them. Each level has different puzzles that use tools you already have, along with a tool you find in that specific level, and they're all relatively simple but are varied enough that they don't get old.- The story is Really well crafted. You're not told much at first, but over time it unravels to you, and it actually reveals itself to be a lot bigger than what you'd initially think. It's very interesting, and it also manages to get you invested in the characters        Things i was 'Eh' on:- The combat is alright, guns feel good to use and it can be fun. However, the enemies are very bare bones. There's literally only three types of enemies in the entire game, aside from the big boss of the level, and they work fine but I feel like they could've been fleshed out more, especially for this kind of game- This is considered a horror game, but I wouldn't really call it that. It's more like an action game with horror elements. I'm not bothered by it personally but it is something to noteOverall, I really liked this game. You can tell that there was a lot of love and care put into it, and I certainly would recommend it to anyone who's into linear narrative driven games with a fair bit of exploration.

_childDocuments_.review: I think the best thing about this game is that Desmond is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ therapist.You see him constantly fail to relate to his patients, watch them pull back as he fails to reach out and understand their problems at a personal level.He sucks, and it's great, and I don't think the story would've worked otherwise. There were other factors at play he was ignorant to sure but didn't change how real it felt that he sucked (justified in his backstory too).Gameplay wise it's a unique take on survival horror, where it feels like they had a ton of inventive ideas for setpieces but also do a great job bridging them together with cohesive mechanics. It's very approachable, and pain free- puzzles are just complicated enough, ammo and health are abundant enough. The set of items you get all feel reasonable (power-level wise and narratively), unique, grounded to specific characters, and applicable to different scenarios. I'm in line with others saying this is light on horror for sure but there are moments that are unnerving to the point you're afraid. They mix you up with unexpected scares enough it feels like you can't be sure you're safe or what's going to happen as tension builds in a dark room.SPOILERSMain negative; sometimes the tone is a little much. The quirkiness usually works but occasionally I was rolling my eyes or struggling to feel the moment.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: In short: Amazingly inventive survival horror crammed with brilliant touches.Similar games: Outlast 2; Evil Within 2.Is it scary?: There are some truly tense moments throughout, but overall, story and atmosphere are prioritised over scaring you and you will often be fighting hard just to survive. There are some jumpscares (most of them will get you). Don't look back...Plot: Psychiatrist Dr Desmond Wales struggles with guilt over the deaths of several of his clients. Does he suck as a therapist, or was something more going on? Both angles are explored, but as the story unfolds, it seems that there are links between each death, and Desmond may be suffering the same fate.PROS Where can I start, this is one of my favourite games of all time and if there's a sequel coming, I'm down for it. I would compare it to the criminally underrated Evil Within 2, as it deals with sanity and reality, but gives you the ability to fight back. It's not as scary as EW2, but your character improves as you find medications and there are several weapons, including a radio. Yes, you can kill the monsters with a radio, which is cool. Your best friend in the game is a talking cat. Computer game logic, right? Except it works so beautifully. She's funny and reassuring. SPOILER: When I played a record and left the room, cancelling the song part way though, she went "NOOO!" because she was enjoying it!Huge, huge kudos to whoever designed the creepy mannequins. I am dying to talk about these, but they are certainly one of the high points of the game.I love the graphical style. The landscapes are beautifully creepy with a number of standout moments, including a ruined supermarket haunted by a girl who hates her reflection, a forest patrolled by an insane military giant and a beach swept by the evil light of a lighthouse. The stealth in this game is well implemented, so being spotted is not a death sentence.The "villains" are all good - the first villain being especially memorable, but the game doesn't peak early. One of them was maybe a bit annoying, but the rest were so much fun to work around, hiding from plasma bolts and monstrous engines... look, just play it, it's worth it.The music felt a bit of a letdown early on until I realised that this wasn't a "terrorise them at all costs" game, and it does improve significantly. So while it never becomes Aubrey Hodge's PSX Doom soundtrack, it begins to really suit the tone of the game. The songs (if you can find them) tend to be cheesy, but if you think about it, severe mental illness isn't pretty, it isn't poetic, and these are ordinary people, not the world's greatest lyricists, so even this is a win. If you beat the game, watch the video unlocked on the main menu, it's brilliant, the whole game in a nutshell.CONSHonestly, for an indie game which I got on Humble Bundle, I feel a traitor by suggesting this game has any flaws. I'd say a couple of sections can be frustrating if you don't know where to go (the forest and the irritating final confrontation in particular), but almost every location presents you with a map that's easy to use. Let's put it this way. I have severe ADHD which has been worsened by long Covid. My attention span is so bad I can barely sit and wrap Christmas presents. I give up on games because I can't get organised to play them. In Sound Mind is the first game I've finished in two years. I looked forward to playing it every night. I bore my best friend and GF by going on about it. (Neither of them will get it because they're grinches of gaming.) My heart is heavy since finishing it. I loved almost every minute of this game and thank the devs for blessing us with it. NOW GO FORTH AND IGNORE MY FUTURE REVIEWS TOO!

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic psychological horror FPS that is a love song to Half-Life in a psychologist perspective, In Sound Mind is a great sub-20 hour game to sink your time into that I would highly recommend. With 4 unique levels that have their own puzzle mechanics that continually building on each other as you progress further while also being useful in exploration in said levels to provide lore within the story to piece together fractured parts of a whole story to the player, which again, is very reminiscent of how Half-Life used its puzzle mechanics and tools within its story.Outside of the many positives, the cons are very few and far between. The main two I can bring up is the very basic FPS that isn't too accurate (this however is only applicable in the hard mode; on normal/easy, it isn't too difficult) and the some of the later puzzles being a bit odd (IMO mostly the star puzzles in the 4th tape as there is only 1 hint on the solutions, but it isn't necessarily very "clear" that its a hint unless you look an explanation).8.5/10: Great psychological horror game with an interesting story and unique puzzles, definitely worth playing for its experience.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first found this game, I assumed it would be just a short horror indie game. I went into this game practically blind, having not read any reviews or watched any game-play videos. I finished playing this game a few minutes ago and immediately wanted to write a review of my experience. As I'm writing this, I'm listening to the OST. I love it when a game makes you feel something -- some emotion that just grabs your heart or punches you in the gut. In Sound Mind (ISM) does all of that. There are intricate puzzles that really make you think, look around, and jump atop of objects you'd never think to jump upon. The plot of the game is so interwoven with mystery and scary bits that you want to keep pushing forward to discover the underlying cause of what exactly is going on -- with YOU and your patients. I LOVE LOVE LOVE the fact that there are collectibles in-game. I love the fact that you actually have to work to find them. I admire the level of detail the in-game documents and artwork contain. Everything is connected and, one way or another, you'll find a way to reach every objective. And the ending... GOD, that ENDING. The ending makes me want to see what happens next. I want to at least read a short story about it. This game was perfect in my opinion. 10/10, all the way. This game is currently in my TOP 10 indie game list. FANTASTIC!

_childDocuments_.review: This first person horror/mystery game is really great. It is in the same vein as games like Amnesia, Layers of Fear and The Beast Inside, so if you like those types of games I highly recommend this one.I can also note that this game is quite long for this genre. I played through the game on normal, and didn't bother getting all the collectibles and achievements, and it took me about 12 hours to play through. This actually makes it the longest first person horror game I've played (and I've played quite a few), followed by Outlast 2 and SOMA. So you're getting a lot of (good) content for your money.The story in this game is really good and interesting, and you learn more and more as you play through the chapters. There are a lot of hidden notes scattered throughout the world, that paints a picture of the interesting world you're in. The therapy session recordings also paint a picture of the characters in the game.There are collectibles in this game in the form of pills that increase your stats. The game kindly tells you how many pills are left to find in each level. So for the completionist out there, you have that to do! There are of course several steam achievements as well if you are into that stuff.The game is visually quite good, it runs on Unreal engine and the developers did a really good job on the graphics overall. I can also mention that my computer is a bit old by now, but this game runs just fine on decent settings, so I would say that the game is pretty optimized as well. The atmosphere and sound design is really great, and the fact that they have several chapters to build different worlds in (which they do) add to the immersion.As far as complaints go, I have to try a bit hard to find any. I didn't personally find any bugs or quirks in the game. Perhaps the fact that monsters can't open doors, so in the first chapter it's quite easy to escape from monsters by just closing the door behind you. Maybe it's a feature, not a bug, not sure :) I also think that the game changes into more of an action/mystery towards the end rather than a horror. There are some great adrenaline fueled segments by the end, but not much of the horror atmosphere, I think. Not a complaint really, just an observation, I still liked it.Oh, and the music in this game is amazing as well, with several songs with lyrics you can find music discs for and listen in your office. A small detail that really adds to the atmosphere.So honestly, I don't really have any complaints at all, I really liked playing through this game. I would rate it almost as high as the top tier games like SOMA and Amnesia, so I hope that this game gets some well deserved attention. So I highly recommend this game to anyone who is a fan of this genre, hopefully we will see more good stuff from this developer.

_childDocuments_.review: So I went into this expecting some kind of Eldritch/cosmic horror detective game, but the most accurate way I feel I can describe it after nine hours of playtime is  If that sounds appealing to you, then by all means, pick it up (At a discount). _childDocuments_.review: I hate horror games. I hate being jumpscared for no reason. I hate screamers and I hate the dumb ""scary"" things that every horror game on the planet likes to put in not because it's actually scary on any deeper level, but because it's easy and it gets youtubers to jump in their seat.This is not one of those games.The story is intriguing, the music is absolutely captivating, the puzzles and gameplay challenges are unique and interesting, but, above all, the environments in this game are PHENOMENAL. This could be a walking simulator with zero gameplay and it would still be worth it just for the sights alone! The game doesn't try too hard to be scary. And that's a GOOD THING. Its atmosphere and audio tracks are perfect for making you slightly uneasy, but not enough to the point that a whimp like myself would stop playing. The game also doesn't try too hard to be difficult. Again, it's a GOOD THING. The gameplay challenges are there to engage you and to provide meaningful interactivity with the beautiful (and creepy) worlds you visit, not to obstruct your path.I was very shocked to discover that this game is so unpopular with let's players. And that made me come to the unfortunate realization about why games like these are rare. They aren't going to make ♥♥♥♥♥♥ youtubers jump and scream and make thumbnail faces, so they fall into obscurity.Don't let this game pass you by, it really is a gem in the rough and cringy world of horror games.

_childDocuments_.review: In Sound Mind is a great game with a little something for everyone. FPS, puzzle-solving, etc and bundled up into a nice knit story filled with a pleasant mixture of comedy and horror, and when the game takes its time to accurately and respectfully portray the struggles the main characters go through, it does so with tact and reverence. The places in the game are large and even gorgeous, all the while maintaining that eerie feeling of dread. However, as genius as the game's story, setting(s), characters, and FPS-elements and puzzle-solving elements are, there lies one hindrance to the game as a whole. The gameplay. Trying to play this game at times was like trying to walk through a pond of sludge, with lag every time you look into the mirror shard, and even just lag when you are trying to traverse the levels or even if you encounter action-heavy scenes or asset-heavy parts of a level (i.e Thanatos' ship) This results in more frustration rather than enjoyment as it effects the FPS and in some instances the puzzle-solving. One nitpick I have is the final tape, where you have to jump across rocks to get to the final boss. In this tape, the rocks seem too spread out, resulting in many deaths. This, however, I will not hold against the game as it must simply be due to difficulty.In Sound Mind is a great game with interesting combinations of different genres, all while managing to stay respectful about the topics it brings up. But, the poor performance really hurts the game in terms of quality and enjoyability. It is my wishes for the devs to release patches for the issue of lag so that others like me can enjoy this game all its full potential.

_childDocuments_.review: Very original, surrealistic game that isn't too heavy to enjoy. That said there are some rough edges that need smoothing.It's uncommon to see such a unique game, that is enjoyable to play, and feels like a complete thought.It's also worth mentioning that while the effects / graphics are not AAA-grade, they have a unique feel (such as the look of the chemicals, how the side effects of the chemicals look when exposed to them, and how things look through the mirror as examples).That said, this game doesn't feel very play tested, I'll give some examples:1) I never finished the Rainbow Tape / final stage because I couldn't jump far enough from rock to rock. I presume this means I would need to replay levels to find more pills / power up. If I speedran this game, I would understand - but I didn't. I took my time, searched pretty thoroughly around levels and still came up short on enough pills to jump across all the rocks (apparently). Each level is quite a commitment, so to think I might have to replay a few levels to find enough pills is just daunting, no thanks.2) The electric grid puzzle was messy and confusing. Based on old YouTube videos, this puzzle was redone with the 1.05 release, but the redo isn't any better.3) Ammo balance could be kinder in the facility where lure pills are first created.4) Every load screen should be an auto-save. More auto-saves in general since you can't manually save.I'm really looking forward to seeing what the developers come up with in the future, but it's a shame I couldn't finish this game without going back and collecting a ton of pills just so I could jump an inch further.

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts as a Horror Game! One of the best things I have played in a loooong time!Gameplay:It's your standard puzzle/shooter type cycle, but you will get new abilities throughout the game that are very unique and interesting to use. The game consists of a hub world and 4 open levels that you go through. It perfectly strikes the balance between letting the player explore and discover at their own pace, but also places you in scripted events and pushes the pace when it needs to. Rarely have I felt so immersed because the game always knew when to be more tight, and when it had to let loose more. If you don't expect the shooting-aspect to be on par with something like doom I have no complaints here.Story:One of the best in a while. My first sentence sums it up perfectly, you are a therapist that rediscovers his and his patients past by exploring past events in your/their mind, and it does a perfect job at creating individual stories for each character, as well as an overarching plot that keeps you invested. And just like Psychonauts, it merges some of the story aspects with gameplay, enemy- and world-design, and I love it!!! Honestly nowadays it already makes me smile when I see things presented to you in the beginning or as a minor thing, become more important or get reincorporated later on. The dialogue is well written, reading notes is very rewarding, and the voice acting is top notch!Minor issues:The game crashed on me a couple of times, but that could just as well be my rig. Honestly the only real bad thing about the game is, that you can revisit all the levels to go back for collectibles... BUT you have to replay the entire level for that, which feels really dumb when all the levels are built on you backtracking and unlocking shortcuts, so when I first wanted to go back for something I was very disappointed to find that I had to go through 0.5-1 hour of gameplay again just to reach that part of the level, although after I had finished it the first time, I unlocked a shortcut that made the area reachable within 5 minutes of the start of the level. Just... why?Verdict:Highly recommended! One of the best horror/puzzle/story games you will ever come across. With a game time of 14 hours without chasing achievements it is well worth the price!

_childDocuments_.review: In Sound Mind is a horror puzzle game, emphasis on the puzzles, with excellent atmosphere, smooth controls and minimal bugs. Given that I am an avid lover of horror games, I was surprised that I didn't find this until it appeared in a bundle, but I'm glad it did.On the horror side of things, I wouldn't say this game is scary, but it is spooky. Enemies can be fought, fairly easily at that, but the emphasis of ISM is exploration and puzzle solving, so this works well. Think Resident Evil, but not as scary, with easier combat, but much the same sort of puzzles.It's refreshing in 2022 to see a game complete, and well made, in both its software integrity and game design. Never once did I get stuck in level geometry, never did I find myself unable to get collectibles after a certain point, and never once did I feel the need to look up a guide. New mechanics and items are sprinkled in at just the right frequency, and the aforementioned mechanics are generally interesting and simple, fit the theme, and don't feel shoehorned in. As icing on the cake, ISM features voice acting, which is surprisingly polished for an indie game, as well as music of equally surprising quality. (Not to mention 6 singles.)You will see that I've played ISM for 14 hours, and that is about how long it took me to complete the game, given that I backtracked to retrieve all the collectibles and achievements. This is a relatively short runtime, of course, but a longer runtime would do ISM a disservice. The game is whole and complete as it is, polished and cohesive in both gameplay and identity, and that is a regrettably rare thing in this the year of our Lord 2022.
