_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - This game is criminally underrated (not by the reviews, but by popularity). It isn't particularly scary, but it does a good job with atmosphere for each area you visit. The combat is...a thing that you do. The puzzles require some brain work to figure out. The soundtrack is really good. The story actually surprised me with the directions it took, I thoroughly enjoyed it. It won't blow your mind, but I think if you're looking for a good adventure/horror game, this is definitely one to look at. It's DEFINITELY worth it on sale, I'd even say at full price it makes the mark. This game really surprised me. I picked it up on sale randomly because of all of the positive reviews, and I was itching for a new horror game to play. While this game may not deliver many (if any) scares, it does carry the atmosphere very well. I wouldn't compare it to a Resident Evil or Silent Hill game, but moreso just solid game design that ensures each area matches the themes of what's going on.The story takes some twists and turns, but doesn't get too crazy or go off the tracks. I, personally, enjoyed the ride. It didn't blow my mind or pull any "WHAT?!"'s out of me, it was just a solid enjoyable story. Each section kept me intrigued to see how it would play out, and I kept wanting more on what the heck is going on. Overall, you start off knowing pretty much nothing, but are drip-fed the story as you play. Some of it you have to piece together yourself, but most of it is given to you straight forward at various points throughout the game. The characters, I actually really liked learning about and see developed throughout the game. They each carry their own personality, even Desmond (the main character). The villain reminds me a lot of Pete from Mickey Mouse, and I'm not sure why. He has fun with everything, and he does things to minorly inconvenience you, and then at times straight up tries to kill you. Overall, again, nothing that will blow your mind, but they did a great job writing each character, and I enjoyed getting to learn more about them.The gameplay, overall, is solid. The one drawback I found with this game was the combat. When you engage enemies, it does feel janky, and not in a good way. I think it was the only part of the game I wasn't really looking forward to, minus the bosses. They, for the most part, were done well. The game has you solve various puzzles that do require some thought to complete them. You don't get the answer to every single one put in your face (though some do), but you still have to figure out the application of the information given, or just figure out the puzzle altogether. There is some exploration elements to the game if you feel so inclined with various rewards in the form of stat boosters and resources (batteries, ammo, etc...). The game is played in sections and each map is fully explorable on its own. It plays out like a metroidvania as well requiring special tools to get access to different areas. The game also leaves plenty to look for and figure out as you explore. There may be an item behind a window with no access to the room, so you have to figure out how to get in there. It doesn't get to complicated but again, does require some thought.I also never felt that the game overstayed its welcome. Clocking in at just under 12 hours worked well for me, and I did do a decent amount of exploring. It kept each section the right size, and still kept me wanting to see it through to the end.The graphics are fine. I enjoyed the artistic direction they took, for sure. The graphics won't blow your mind though, but they aren't bad either.The soundtrack is REALLY well done. They really made it enhance the atmosphere, and certain songs you can find also add to the development of the story and characters.Overall, I hadn't heard of this game until it was on a random sale, bought it, and am upset that it's not better known. The dev team, We Create Stuff, really created something special here, and I hope that we get to see more from this universe by them!

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever wanted to pay $30 for a panic attack? Well now you can with "In Sound Mind"! There are times you will watch a movie trailer and unmistakably feel you have just seen the entire movie. More often than not, going into something without any preconceived ideas of what is at hand is often the better route when seeing a movie, watching a new show, or playing a video game. In Sound Mind is one of those games where you want to go into it understanding its conceptual ambitions. I bought this game on a whim because it checked off several of my favorite game themes, horror with a literal psychological and therapeutic theme. Going into it I had thought it would be a fight-less horror genre walking-scape game much like SOMA or Outlast. Throughout the games 5 scenarios there were times that I felt its aggressive gun and fight scenes were too frequent, demanding and out of place for this game. But after my expectation abated that this game had FPS elements I was able to enjoy it far more. I am not qualified enough to weigh in on the games accuracy regarding mental disorders but this game feels like its potrail is realistic, grounded, and without underhanded ridicule. It does not paint mental illnesses as something that is someones fault, or without potential help and treatment. To even the untrained eye the game delves into topics such as obsessive compulsive behavior, anxiety, depression, suicidal idealizations, post traumatic stress, paranoia, fear of people, body dysmorphia etc. but they certainly felt respectful which is the true element to this games overwhelming sense of dread. It is not without its jump-scares, but as far as jump-scares go they feel tame and not without a purpose. These are often relegated to doing a 180 and there being an inexplicable appearance of a mannequin or the sudden appearance of a swarthy dandy dressed man with a gravelly voice. These and a few other examples are still are not as scary as the strange paranoia you feel as this game takes a grip on you and you try and shake away the feeling this game was somehow made with you in mind. While I found it sometimes to terrifying to endure, it was too alluring to stay away for long. While playing In Sound Mind, I was often at odds of whether or not a game of such serious topics makes for a worthwhile game. Sometimes games make you do despicable acts for the sake of tone or making an impression on its players. Things along the lines of 'No Russian' from Call of Duty. Then there are of course heavy topics featured in games before this such as I Am Setsuna or Hellblade: Senuas Sacrifice. Despite their often challenging nature, they were at least games that you felt you had fun playing. I am still uncertain if In Sound Mind makes for an actual fun game or if its just an exercise in learning how much tension is too much tension?In Sound Mind has an ingenious method of information collection though use of invisible objects and magic lenses. While the game certainly mastered how mirrors work in video games, these tropes are basically a fresh coat of polish on old tricks long pulled out of their hat. However, I easily forgive that simply for its outstanding finale. For a game that I felt was overly action oriented at times, its ending pulled it together very nicely. It is neither a bullet sponge or wimpy cop-out. It is heartfelt, meaningful, and all too rare for a game I just accused of being redundant.Give this game a chance, knowing what to expect will in my opinion make for a far greater experience. I give In Sound Mind an: 8/10 on the spookies, 7/10 on the overall experience, but a 10/10 for its exceptional ambition and unforgettable ending.Oh, and you can pet the cat. 11/10.

_childDocuments_.review: ISM's a beautiful, charming, and excitement filled adventure worth not only every penny, but every second.I (as well as all of my friends) have fallen in love with it- not a day goes by that we don't discuss the characters in specific, who've captured our hearts. The game has a multitude of mechanics ranging from the usual flashlight to pills or even radio controls, a genuinely beautiful soundtrack, but most evidently to me personally, a wonderful take on mental illness and how it affects not only those struggling but the world as they view it. I myself am in school to be a therapist, which is why I initially decided to buy the game out of curiosity when i heard the main character had the profession I was hoping to go into. I admit to my nervousness: its not uncommon to see major mischaracterization in regards to those struggling with their mental health, but i was blown away by how they not only chose to speak on but show it to us through the environments that are meant to represent the minds of the four other major characters. There was no babying them, or villanizing them- just a genuine look into the minds of people struggling. I've played through the game two or three times over spans of weeks, each time with my friends in tow. I've got all the achievements, all the vinyls, all the pills. If you take anything away from this, its this: if nothing else, play for the experience of getting to know these characters. I love them so dearly

_childDocuments_.review: In Sound Mind is a prime example of what indie gaming represents. It is a fountain of fresh and original ideas, while also lacking polish being incohesive and overstaying its welcome at some parts. The horror atmosphere is well done, the game can be creepy without relying on jumpscares (and the few of them present are very well placed to moments when they are least expected). I would even go as far as to say that this is more of an adventure with the elements of psychological horror. The puzzles were the best aspect of the game for me. They are intuitive, but not overly simple, and interact perfectly with the environment. Nothing of what you do feels pointless or random (from which many games, especially horror games, usually suffer). I also applaud clever use of the arsenal/tools player acquires throughout the game. The combat itself was unfortunately not that good, controls are a bit wonky and some parts of the game were too long to the point of being tiring. What was also quite unfortunate for me, is that I was very hooked into the story, but the game progressively killed it. Without going into spoilers, the plot deals with mental illnesses and the depiction of them is terrifyingly accurate, but then some twist tries to blend into the plot and it does not work for the narrative's favour. Despite the typical downsides of an indie game, its high points are something to behold, and the dev team have clearly shown they are very talented and can create unique experience. That is a great premise for (hopefully) their next game. Until then, I can recommend all indie players to give this game a try, others may want to wait for some discount before hooking it up.High points:✅ Original setting and horror atmosphere✅ Clever puzzles, good interaction with the environment✅ Good sounds, fitting musicNeutral:🟡 Story (at first good, but goes over the top in the end)🟡 Surprisingly good visuals for an indie game, but that also brings technical issues (high hardware requirements, FPS drops, microstutters)🟡 Surprisingly good amount of content, but some parts are too long and tiring as a resultLow points:❌ Combat, controls, physics❌ Abysmal autosave in puzzle segments (you cannot save manually and the games forces you to repeat some parts when leaving)Something more that should be mentioned before giving final mark: huge thumbs up for the native ultrawide support (something even AAA publishers repeatedly fail to do) and for direct encouragement of use of all the material in live streaming! This sets a good precedent.

And hey, no DLC so it's not like they are trying to milk this game of money like every triple A title out there, even though this feels like this was made by a triple A dev team.

_childDocuments_.review: *spoilers maybe*Excellent game. Soundtrack was great (especially the records...an insanely cool detail), visuals were satisfactory, gameplay was easy to get used to. There are a lot of moments that are silly enough just to get the tension off and make it not feel like a horror game, though it always pulls you right back into the grit of it. Really enjoyed that every area had its own look/feel and associated boss, with new mechanic. Every chapter felt fresh!Story is written very well---even if you figure out some beats early, it leaves just enough out that you have to wait to put all the pieces together. Not insanely original, but extremely satisfying with its pacing. Mr. Rainbow is also extremely compelling! Threatening you, but at the same time giving you not-so-subtle hints... definitely a favorite.Complaints; Feels like too much combat, and the combat isn't particularly fun/engaging after the first time. If the direct gun-combat was reduced and more emphasis placed on stealth, it'd be a lot more fun and would give a better horror feel. You can tell you're in a horror game, but it almost feels like a regular fps during combat sequences. The sprint mechanic kinda sucks ass, even maxed out. Made every Lucas chase feel miserable.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: I thought this was a decent game but not scary at all, psychological or otherwise. It's like survival horror for people who don't like horror. Unless you are afraid of the dark (in a game) or afraid of some monsters that are not particularly grotesque and don't do much worse than scream and charge at you occasionally (in a way that barely qualifies as a jumpscare) you'll probably be fine even if you hate scary games. Overall the game is pretty fun and has the typical survival horror mechanics like puzzles, managing limited health and ammo, and fights that are difficult to win with without taking damage and wasting ammo (due to the way the enemies move). It looks pretty good and the various environments are engaging and well done. I did think the story was a bit silly though. Overall I give it 6.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: This game was phenomenal, from start to finish.Let's start with the story.I'll keep this spoiler free, it is very strong but a little convoluted in places. It explains itself well and sitting through each chapter was delightful while not being to challenging on the game play front.The soundtrackThis is such a beautifully composed game, the ambient music, the boss music, the bonus music tracks all of it fits the setting and theme so well while also bring it's own personality to the mix.The game-play.This is where I talk a little about the technical and I will say this game can be relatively optimised, I've had stuttering and frame drop issues in some spots but nothing unplayable, a majority of the game ran at 70fps solid on all medium with a RTX 2060, Intel Core i5-10600k and 32gb of 3200mghz of ram.Final thoughts.I played this game on a whim, It was pot luck this game was chosen to be played during one of my nightly "hey friend pick a random game from my games list for me to play" and my god what an amazing choice they made.This game is hands down a top 10 for me.I am happy to give it a solid 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game and exactly what it advertises itself as. Also, it is good to see the characters that have a mental illness being treated empathetically.On an extra note, although the screenshots do a good job of showing how creative the art direction can get, it is even better on the actual game! Environments are consistent with the themes of the levels, which can go wild sometimes.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: I had to force myself everyday to stop playing it.It looks very nice, very good puzzles, great boss fights, and at times very challenging.Story is great, some moments are just epic, scenarios were very different from each other. Weapons serve not only to kill enemies, but also as tools to complete the puzzles.Exploration is a 10. I see it as a metroidvania kind of, it's a game where you need to collect new items/tools to access some parts of previously visited (and blocked) areas (i.e. you may encounter black smoke blocking an item, and the flare gun which disperses said smoke, is obtained in a later level)Only thing lacking was grunt enemy variety (only 3 types iirc)Gonna rest for like 2 weeks, and then replay it.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: It is such a great game. I already played it on  Epic because it was free for a week but damn, i love this game so much I had to buy it on Steam and get all Achievments. The Story is rfeally sad and interessting, gameplay is fun imo and the music is just on point. I didn´t even realize that I know the guys who made the music for this game, The Living Tombstones. This game is definetly  less horror and more story and puzzle game but it´s so good. i really wish that the game had more fans and that the whole world would know about it, my personal ranking is that this game is on one level with undertale. And I played Undertale like 8 times until now
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: In Sound Mind is a psychological horror game (but actually it's a Tonia petting simulator) with some Alan Wake vibes.+ Good story(especially for an indie game)+ Great level design (all six levels are different from each other)+ Decent and unique boss fights+ Great original soundtrack+ Some unexpected jumpscares+ Tonia...- Some of the levels were pretty big so you can get lost- A bit laggy sometimes (my pc is old)- You can only pet Tonia a limited number of times ;(In Sound Mind is a great hidden gem and everyone should buy it especially at this cheap price.For those who don't know this is Tonia:
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of both horror and puzzle games, I did enjoy this though I'm not as head over heels for the game as other reviewers. The horror of the game is perfect, with no cheesy and low brow jumpscares and just a good amount of creepiness. The puzzles aren't really puzzles moreso than "go find this to get here" type gameplay - nothing like The Witness, Talos Principle, etc. Just more of exploring and getting through the story. Outside of the bosses the enemy variety isn't anything special with only 3 types (close combat, range, and large) and present no real challenge. I was really hooked on the game and story at first, but personally for me it dragged on a little bit in the end. Technically, the graphics are fairly good, with well done environments and sound is on point. I did experience 3 crashes which is a somewhat rare thing that happens to me. I got this on sale and would definitely recommend the game at a discount if you're looking for something a little different.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: This is just what I was looking for. Creepy atmosphere, a story with some mystery behind it, but most importantly, lots of puzzles and puzzle items. I recommend playing on hard as there is lots of ammo and batteries on normal. Just when I thought I had played thru every decent scary game in existence, I found this. This game feels like silent hill but plays more like Amnesia. It is not completely linear, there is quite a bit of backtracking which I do like. You spend a fair amount of time in each area switching fuse boxes, reading scattered notes with hints. We need more games like this
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: Game is awesome, original and it's really a lot of fun to play. The story is very involved and told in an interesting way. The best part of the game are the different stories, each has its own very different enthronements, characters and playing style.  And after each story you return to your office to your little cat, Tonia. And you can pet her and she talks to you! How good is that! You should play this game just so you can meet Tonia.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible experience from a fledgling studio with so much damn potential its crazy.I loved every bit of this game, with its elements of horror, action and adventure, definitely inspired by games like Alan Wake, The Evil Within, Silent Hill, Resident Evil and hell even Psychonauts. From its unique worlds and bosses, fully fleshed out in the minds of protagonist, Desmond's patients, to its supremely crafted puzzles. The game is so much more than your average indie horror. There's no dipping your toe in with this title, its full acid drop into the bottom of the abyss and its gorgeous.Not to mention the soundtrack is peak. I also have much love for both Tonia the cat and the mannequin friends that accompany you along the way.Without a doubt, one of my favorite games of all time. My friends will have hell to pay trying to shut me up when I talk about this game because to me, it was perfect. Can't wait for more from We Make Games. The name of the studio is incredibly apropos, cause they SURE AS HELL DO.10/10 - A Classic that will stay with me for a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: I can't believe I sat on this game for so long. Turns out this was a great play! I didn't realize how long it was going to be. I spent a total of 14 hours on the game and loved every moment. The plot was inspiring. the freaking JUMPSCARES almost gave me a heart attack. I enjoyed the boss battles and how they correlated to each patient, very creative. I would love to see a squeal to this game.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: In Sound Mind - a game in which everything is done with soul, but modestly.The main feature of the game is the disclosure of the psychological trauma of patients. Each patient is a fairly large level with a set of puzzles and a boss.Puzzles are interesting, but closer to the middle of the game, their concentration exceeds all reasonable limits, even skirmishes with ordinary enemies do not help to relax.Plot hooks work as they should, you, like the main character, want to know what is happening here.With all its budget, the game looks decent, some locations just want to be done in order to shoot from all angles.The game lacks only cut-scenes and a variety of ordinary opponents (there are two types of them, but they look the same :D).Optimization is suffocating. The transition from one part of the location to another is accompanied by an unpleasant frieze, during especially loaded scenes the FPS flies up and down.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: Mind bendingly awesome. This game is like a psychedelic trip but exploring other people's minds, like, literally...I guess it would be similar to ayahuasca more than anything else, because it becomes downright terrifying at times. You can really feel a connection between the protagonist and his patients. He essentially explores their mind, which each of them is like a series of complicated puzzles similar to Riven or Myst but there's free movement and also horror elements...they are like restless souls. You have to solve the puzzles to make them feel at peace. I haven't gone through all the stories yet, but I got through the second person's mind. It was exhilarating...this is so...phew. I gotta catch my breath. Oh, there's a kitty cat in the game, so that's nice as well. :)This is a really cool concept. Blown away so far.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: Whoo boy...we are going on a trip hereI'm going to preface this by saying that i think my review will be entirely personal.This game is a more adult/gritty version of psychonauts. It lacks the polish and feel of a double-fine production however I would not discount it on those grounds.This game is a gem. To get my point across i feel that i need to make criticism however small.The stealth mechanic is entirely useless, more or less along with the pill/stat mechanic. the enemies are basicThat is all for criticism.This game obviously had love in it, each level makes use full use of the idea of going into a persons mental head space beautifully. I'm not going to spoil it but tape 3-4 are particularly moving. So many games have absolutely whiffed when it comes to mental health...I'm looking at you Sejuna. This one makes every scenario feel lived in and understandable, all the right decisions are made in my opinion to tell the story and give the smoothest game play experience.The audio is a thing of beauty, listen to the vinyls...its a mood in of itselfWere i to make any observation it would be that the story kind of detracts from the individual journey of the patients but i also cannot see how the game would exist without it. I understand that this review is probably a difficult read. please re read after finishing a playthrough.9/10- Patience and grace

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute masterpiece of a game.As the many (non-meme) reviews explain here, the game is a wonderfully paced puzzle story-rich horror game that delves into the human psyche in the most enigmatic, artistically beautiful way. _childDocuments_.review: Cool horror/puzzle adventure game by the folks at We Make Stuff. Gameplay is reminiscent of old school Half-Life mixed in with Silent Hill -- more focus is given to atmosphere, exploration and puzzles than to gunplay or jump scares. The music is great and the story is quite engaging. Had a few frame rate issues (game slogs down every once in a while, which is frustrating, considering the graphics aren't all that) but nothing game breaking. Would recommend to anyone who enjoys survival horror games.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: In Sound Mind is a game with a fantastic story that is, while not perfect, a full and immersive experience. You play Desmond Wales, a psychologist reviewing his patient's cases as he himself is being driven to insanity by a mysterious force. Every single case is represented by a tape, where you play through the distorted versions of their memories and experiences.The pros:- Phenomenal story- Great horror elements, no cheap jumpscares- Great puzzles- One of the few games to tackle the subject of mental health well- Plenty to collect for those looking to 100%- Soundtrack by The Living Tombstone- Adorable catThe cons:- Mixing multiple gameplay genres causes it to miss the mark on some of them- Horror aspects are hit-or-miss, with some chapters excelling at being scary and others being more action-focused, similar to Resident Evil (if you enjoy this then this may be a plus, I personally was expecting more horror)- Overall, the game is a fantastic experience that I would recommend to anyone who is looking for a deeper experience with some horror elements and enjoys singleplayer shooters, puzzle games, or platforming, since this game has elements of all three. I found that the platforming was the least exciting of the three, with the shooter and puzzle elements shining the brightest and the platforming personally being relatively frustrating. However, it ultimately did not detract from the experience enough for me to come even close to not recommending this game. Go forth, and remember, Desmond: YOU are In Sound Mind.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: I was tempted to turn the game off with the introductory line of the game's main antagonist, but I'm amazed that they were able to pull a twist on such a groan inducing line. The game isn't particularly scary, and is more in the Resident evil line of Survival Horror where it has a few spooky sections, but you're filling baddies with lead, or solving puzzles for most of the game's run time. The writing, which gave a extremely bad impression from that opening line. Is actually pretty clever. I'm going to start spoiling the games story, but the protagonist accidentally killed his cat, and the antagonist is supposed to be his "Shadow" animated by "Rainbow" the substance that is the games central focus. The game is broken down into "Tapes" which are the levels in addition to the hub level that is the apartment. Going through the different patients the protagonist had, and trying to work through the mystery of how they connect. While unraveling the mystery the protagonist is shown to have been wrong about each one of his patients, having totally dropped the ball. The least bad screw up was the first level, where you can in part say he had no way of knowing that she'd end up exposed to the stuff. So he pushed her a little to hard, and she had a extra helping hand with Rainbow. The second, and third level, he has contempt for the guy, the levels, which are his unconscious minds assessment of his case, what he thinks about them. Completely dismissing the guy getting burned alive by spooks as a suicide. Has him completely missing really obvious hints that he's talking with another one of his patients, and planning to go commit crimes with him. So you'd think, with the all of the levels being him dropping the ball, and his harsh judgement of his patients missing a huge disaster, and getting most of them killed. The dude even having killed his own cat with his hubris, that the game would be rounding out with the ghost cat telling him "You dumby, you still don't get it. You weren't supposed to accept your flaws, and give a brave boy speech about how you were making progress with them. Your flaw was pride, you literally killed me because you thought you were so clever. You don't know anything." Instead, they double down on the whole "Savior" idea for the character, to the point of literally calling his song, which are basically the wrap ups of the character's story, that. Now, because the rest of the game up until that point was good. I am choosing to go with the notion that the whole "my legs seem to move without me" line, and the screen going black when you're hearing Lucas's lines when he rescues the protagonist as Rainbow having won. I won't let the last hour spoil what was otherwise a fun game though, I had a good time in spite of things not being wrapped up neatly.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: There is so much love and attention put into this game, and it shows through the shear amount of detail, strong visuals, and amazing story telling. For people like me who love a linear story experience (and maybe have an inkling for 100% completion), I highly recommend this game. It touches on the topic of mental health, yet retains lightheartedness through the personality within the characters, the moments of comedic relief, and the few subtle references to outside media. It has some truly scary moments, as well as utilizes unique mechanics that blew my mind.Love the concept behind this game - love everything about it! So glad it got recommended to me.Not to mention I have been a long-time fan of The Living Tombstone. Not only does seeing their work in an amazing project such as this bring me great joy, but having listened to the soundtrack before playing the game, and getting to see the context behind the songs unfold as I play, is an extra plus in my book.

_childDocuments_.review: In terms of bugs, the experience was decent, aside from routine collision glitches and visual disturbances like rocks being placed on the air. Instead, I've had unwarranted performance issues, 5-20 frame drops in many places on Ultra settings with TAA. Knocking them down a notch helped, albeit partially. I've heard the stuttering could also be tied to the in-game Vsync, but turning it off did nothing for me. Granted that I ran more demanding and technically impressive games on my rig without a hitch, I think it's someone's amateur hands slightly breaking the engine rather than a natural occurrence. Reprehensible, but tolerable.It's a pet peeve of mine, a nitpick... but why are the fonts so bad? What are they, Comic Sans and Arial? I'm not a specialist on the matter, but certainly I saw these fonts regularly outside of the game, and their use here isn't commendable at all. Some plaques, for example, are cheaply gilded and smeared with those basic postcard filters. The placeholder vibe is real and stylistically contrasts with the game's unhinged, fun identity. It seems like the decor was outsourced to someone with a fake designer's resume, or several such people, since similar objects are often decorated in differently distasteful manners.The sound design is okay and the music is fantastic, featuring a couple of apocalyptic Western tracks that got me good. The graphics aren't as ideal. Object models and texture work are inconsistent in quality, I often encountered highly-detailed assets next to some muddled mess. The lighting, however, looks hand-crafted, and great elemental effects add to the surreal picture. Then, a pinch of Half-Life and Bioshock for shooting and environments, on top of other influences, evoke a sense of familiarity. The problem is that all of it appears cartoonish in more ways than one, which is bad for the horror factor.The story has its neat beats, but the weak delivery has failed to oppress me psychologically. Also weak is Desmond Wales, our protagonist and a therapist who attempts to solve a sinister mental mystery by travelling through the worlds of his former patients whose disorders are represented in the forms of demons and perils. The game's tongue-in-cheek disposition in the face of grim circumstances reminded me of Evil Dead and The Darkness. Although, our hero isn't as passionate as Jackie Estacado or witty like Ash, he's bland in comparison to anyone whom I'd call a real character, and should rather be equated with Ethan Winters of Resident Evil fame. His patients, fortunately, are relatively well-written, and the game does its best to make you sympathize with them.I saw myself in each one of the poor sods, and this is, in part, how a regular insane asylum works its magic, too. But just like in real life, other people's mental problems are alien to most of us, one can't relate to everyone. Naturally, in this regard, the villain is the hardest pill to swallow. Before the game even starts, he proclaims: "They say curiosity killed the cat. I killed the cat. Curiosity only brought her to me." Way to establish his malice early on and make me instantly hate the bastard! He's a cackling Freddy Krueger type. A sicko, for sure, but I loved the taunts he spewed during the frequent calls on random phones scattered across the game. And his cheeky memos gave me a few chuckles.The premise was strong and promised to reveal a gruesome and terrifying ride within. Soon, the vibes changed from the good titles I've mentioned to Goosebumps with shallow Lynchian undertones. I assumed the 80's horror potential that wasn't there, to begin with. But assumptions be damned! More importantly, the game delivered on the volatile sense of adventure, a property modern formulaic horror scene lacks. This alone puts ISM on a pedestal. A flimsy one, but to be reckoned with when making a game in this genre. It doesn't have to be a predictable Slenderman or Amnesia bootleg. Here's an example showing that you can have a couple of compelling sci-fi ideas as well as an array of gameplay mechanics in a spooky flick, and it would sell.For an indie horror, the assortment of equipment is staggering. Your arsenal includes a mirror shard to reflect ghosts and look for hidden traces of various utility, a radio to solve radio-based puzzles as well as to stun colossi, a few guns with decent gunplay to boot, speed pills, and a flashlight. All of the items you carry have multiple uses, and the gameplay is weaved around juggling them to your benefit. Given the lineup of fun predicaments, it's a delightful endeavor. When it comes to survival, ISM pretends your resources are limited, but I haven't felt any scarcity, even though I played on Hard.Exploring for abundant resources could get old fast, but all the crazy jams and stat-upgrading pills are worth seeking out. The effect of each pill is negligible, but the buffs stack, making finding them a good incentive, and an even better allegory. The levels are moderate in scale and typically open-ended. To an extent, of course, don't expect anything deep or complex, I wouldn't call ISM an Immersive Sim. But its design gives just enough room for exploration, breathtaking chases, secret-hunting, and an arrayy of SAW-like (kinda) traps. All the while, they kept maps concise, cut into easily memorized chunks or set pieces, so you won't get lost.There's stealth for some reason, but I forgot about it completely. Taking enemies head-on had me killed quite a few times, which I consider a positive, even though frame drops often played their annoying role. None of the inkblots seemed scary regardless, no matter how gigantic they got. In that last Prey game, blobs at least had gimmicks like pretending to be objects or setting the player on fire, making them more interesting. But not that frightening still. If cartoon shadowy figures were fearsome, then Heart of Darkness must've been the apogee of horror. Yeah, a joke about a game 3 people remember.So, as I've mentioned a 'couple' of times, I wasn't terrified at any point, but boy, does this game provide excitement! In one of the reviews, someone called it a thriller, and I couldn't agree more. While the cloud castles of my initial expectations crumbled, I'd say the agitation of running away from The Bull train or climbing a crushing crane compensated for that loss. All in all, the bosses are distinctive, the panic-inducing encounter design is superb, and platforming trials in the form of challenging hazard courses are surprisingly well-realized for a first-person game.In Sound Mind isn't something completely fresh, but it's exploratory with its time-tested fragments. Frankly, the game doesn't excel in any of these fragments, but I can look past an occasional 'fuse abuse' and other flaws, because its inventive gear, enemy-based tricks, and Metroidvania elements were combined in a clever way, allowing the tired tropes to bloom once more. Apparently, the combination doesn't have to be sophisticated to get appreciated by the public! Fold things differently for a change, and with some luck, win people's hearts.I wouldn't call the game brilliant, but its unpredictable thrills are leagues above the low ceiling that has become the standard template for 'stealth horrors' today. Take a hint, you cautious indies, transforming into cowardly mini-corporations incapable of taking risks, is exactly what people never wanted to see from your lot. The market is severe, but it's short-sighted to sit with its shell strenuously pressed against your bleeding ear, paralyzed like the UN at the sight of a genocide. People forgive the flawed, but nobody respects the faint-hearted. Can't wait for the inevitable sequel!My curator

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, you look like hell, friend!  A tough day and some mental strain starting to get to you? Just take a quick pill here and chill with the rest of us through this review. And don't fret about the trippy chemical gas. Its all good here. *tips suspicious gooey hat*GAME-PLAY: 10/10In Sound Mind plays itself as a psychological-horror with that lovely first-person shooter mentality. There is no clear hiding of the Half-Life inspirations around this game and the team behind In Sound Mind LITERALLY have their background tied to the GoldSource engine starting back in their early titles like Nightmare House 1 & 2 (they are both FREE mods to Half-Life 2 that I would HIGHLY RECOMMEND checking out). That all said, the game does truly a wonderful job on presenting a really straightforward and yet odd way to tackle the game. Shooting bits are what you expect, but the psychedelic and the horror elements are handled so well I don't think I've played something so satisfying since the FEAR 1 and its truly amazing atmosphere/world. I love the immense care to this game's design making everything feel so consistently fresh/wild/scary all the time.GRAPHICS : 10/10As this game does hint well to the heralds of Half-Life 2 visuals, I will still argue they made this game and style their own. Weapons, items and etc feel familiar, but they level of polish put to them is so uniquely spun, you never are taken away from the game. I really have to profoundly cheer on this game's visual design towards the environments, worlds and the ??? that you visit during your journey. They know how to play creatively to make every place you visit feel that much more special and memorable. Twisting visuals, keeping the uncomfortable feel of the horror and good WOW how I love enemies and bosses in this game. Trust me, you'll be massively impressed. <3CONTROLS : 10/10Did this up with the ole keyboard and mouse and it felt absolutely comfortable and just like home. Nothing was slow or problematic. Always felt the game was responsive to me and nothing that took control out from my hands. Flawless. SOUND/MUSIC : 100/10I have to really congratulate how DEDICATED they went with the music here. The feel of horror and its music was one thing, but they even managed to the The Living Tombstone to design some of the tracks in the game WOW, do you notice/adore them. I won't spoil more then that, but just music alone felt creepy, isolating, haunting, quiet and even sometimes peaceful where its needed to be. Nothing but praise. *nods*The other reason I've cranked up the rating for the game via sound/music is strictly because of the SENSATIONAL voice work to this game. This carries the game so well with the voice acting being done so varied, uniquely and downright impressive from every talent's mouth. The amount too is just perfect. Nothing that overloads you, but always keeps you going and further rounds out the characters to such a wonderful degree. I really, really love the characters in this game. You too, Tonia. <3WRITING/DESIGN/PUZZLES : 10/10This is quite a widespread topic, but I think all three elements are so wonderfully connected. The game is horror themed, but there are puzzles and mysteries to be had! Shocker, right? But more then that is how everything is executed. You are heavily rewarded when exploring and you ARE encouraged to explore. Everything feels like such a mystery you can't help but unwrap like a curious detective. The developers know this as they make sure you revisit old areas and find some truly amazing/shocking things when doing so. Some even flesh out the characters even more and some really mess you up in the best way. The devs here deserve so much praise for these elements alone (and even stuff I won't dare spoil to you),STORY : 10/10I think I will leave this as limited a possible. You wake up in a confused state and you have to put the pieces back of who you are and why you are here. Sounds simple and not very enthralling? Perhaps! But I think you might not be In Sound Mind to agree just yet. *insert massive grin here*COST : 10/10PLEASE BUY THIS GAME. The cost is horrendously cheap for the experience you get out of it. This is a massive steal for the quality/music/story/love that I've seen in a long time put into a game. Worth every penny and more.AGE RANGE : TEEN/ADULTSIn Sound Mind is clearly set for a more mature audience. If the use of guns and violence already didn't tip you off about that, it does deal with heavy themes of psychology and mental health. This isn't a game littered with endless emotional drama, but it carries a notable tone about the conditions and struggles of people dealing with their own demons. Its perfectly balanced with the horror to keep you intrigued and I love it for that.TLDR : 10/10In Sound Mind is the prime example of a quality horror game with psychological elements to carry itself. Along with insanely clever design, love and genuine polish I've not seen in a long time, this game is a wonderful gem to behold. Zero regrets and PLEASE BUY IT. o0oOverall Score : 10/10If it was not clear enough, In Sound Mind provides one of the best experiences I've had with the realm of shooter, horror and psychological elements ALL done so respectfully and with masterful polish. The devs have shown their roots here connecting a great story, wonderful mystery and that idea of horror to push something truly one-of-a-kind to a player. Much like Pyschonauts, you feel great curiosity, horror, humour, danger and something you cannot explain to others when describing the game. I hold tightly to this game and everything behind it. And added to that is some incredible tunes/character to back it up. Don't forget to give a high five to a good friend of mine and always leave room to pet the cat. Even if she can be a bit snarky. ^=^

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR:Wow. 10/10 game - it's just... wow. The game play is a mix of Resident Evil and Silent Hill, and the story hits really close home. Achievements are fun to get for the most part, and each boss is radically different.Also: You get to pet a cat, so really it's an 11/10.---All the words: In sound Mind is a GOTY that never got recognized as such. The story is captivating, the game play is easy, and the boss fights are all different, and I /love/ that. Instead of the same rinse and repeat for each encounter, it all revolves around the item you get for the level, and it's so cool the way that items are useful in a pyramid order. Nothing ever becomes obsolete, so you never feel like you wasted any time.The puzzles are so easy that if you can't figure them out, you're over-thinking it. That was me in the stupid Hom-a-mart store. I am stupid, stupid, stupid for not figuring out how to get through the first set of doors. I finally understood after I stood there like a dunce and really thought about the clue they offered.If you are sensitive like I am and enjoy emotional connections to characters - look no further.Virginia is relatable for those of us with childhood issues.Allen is relatable to those of us who feel like outsiders.Max is relatable to those of us who are parents or children who had to watch their parents separate.Lucas is relatable to those of us who went through a military experience, or people with PTSD in general.As someone who could grasp onto each of them, I can relate to each mental condition they are "diagnosed" with. Anxiety was wonderfully presented, and the PTSD sections made me want to cry because of how 'real' it felt to me to have to drop everything to do calming techniques over a sound or item that reminds us of our terrors. Lots of hidden lore - lots of stuff to enjoy and hunt for - and great voice acting! Not to mention the soundtrack which is done by the great Living Tombstone. The graphics are nice, too - and I love the way things stand out in the darkness, unlike most horror games that make it impossible to see.  Being dark doesn't equal scary, it just equals frustration, and this dev team definitely understands that.I am now replaying it with my almost 9 year old daughter who loves the horror genre. She is so smart and realized already with Virginia that I have the same issues as her when I go out. To me, that signals these writers did EVERYTHING right. When a kid can realize what they are trying to convey - they did a dang good job.A two year old game that DOESN'T feel dated. The only problem is that is leaves on a cliff-hanger, and there are no announcements to make a sequel as of yet.You still get a good, solid ending - but it also leaves you lacking a bit because you want to know what happens to the over-all background of the world.Play it, play it, play it - you won't regret it! It is SO good!

_childDocuments_.review: In Sound Mind's controller support fails to fit its gameplay. Controller users are hampered by sluggish camera movement (even with the sensitivity turned all the way up) to the point where combat and platforming become very frustrating, and even, broken. Thankfully, this aspect can be fixed with Steam Input by mapping the right stick to joystick mouse.Controller mappings are far from ideal, too. Reload is B instead of X. Sprint is on clicking the left stick, and you often need to use it for the plethora of horrible first person jumping (sprint can be set to a toggle, but still feels bad). Item swapping is on various buttons, but controller mappings aren't actually in the remapping options, so you can't unset any of them, and changing buttons in game will still activate both the new mapping and the unchangeable swapping. Items themselves are in a linear list instead of the obviously vastly more sensible radial menu format, so if you need to quickly access a weapon from some other item not directly next to it, enjoy frantically pressing the item swap button multiple times.Aside from control issues, I didn't get much enjoyment out of the game. Its spookiness and story are pretty flat, and various gameplay aspects made playing more annoying than fun. The areas you traverse aren't linear, and although they clearly made maps for the game, since occasionally you'll see one around, you aren't given easy access to one. I'm not bad at keeping track of where I am and have been, but still found it confusing, especially since, being a horror game, your surroundings change sometimes. You're constantly hassled with damage, from environment hazards, enemies, and bosses. Supplies are plentiful, but health comes in small amounts, and I always felt harassed and near death. Checkpoints are your only true saves, and it's hard to tell when an autosave is a checkpoint. There's a cat indicator for autosaving, but sometimes when I would quit after seeing it, I'd be farther back on continuing. Always fun to repeat progress because the game forces a bad save system. The main character says dumb things when examining objects, eating food, and picking up supplies they're full on, and it's very grating.I did like one of the songs, and while it made me want to appreciate more of what they were going for, it was impossible to escape how irritating to interact with the game actually was.

_childDocuments_.review: ISM actively uses reflection mechanic, where you use a broken piece of a mirror. When it's held, you spot everything hidden i.e. entrances, cables and items. This quickly becomes your №1 gear, since it shows more than just consumables - it reveals enemies and keeps some away, shows safe paths and etc-etc!Each area unique, has a memorable boss who chases your around the map, forcing to progress, explore and gradually adds more equipment into use. That mirror shard from the first chapter? Combine with a flashlight to pick up eerie keys. Try the radio to unlock fences and shoot flares to clear out dark clogs. What's even better - you'll need these to fight bosses.But before you reach battle arenas, be ready to navigate through dark warehouses, survive a lockdown in a freezer and make a mannequin friend, dodge lethal rams in a train station and experience so many more unforgettable episodes.I have to mention this guy. Sneaks on you. Peaks around a corner. Jokes about fear. Constantly calls you. Even poses for a photo! And then starts throwing explosive objects at you. Thanks! In Sound Mind is an absolute gem! Had a blast playing it. Enjoyed its story, flawless and well balanced combat/explore moments. And what a treat you get for completing each chapter! Such great songs!

_childDocuments_.review: In Sound Mind is one of those games that seemingly takes place in your mind -- starting off somewhat grounded, and ending up more like a fever dream. With minute details along the way that change and shift, reflecting your state of mind.You play as Desmond, a therapist who’s haunted by his former patients. Each one represents a portion of the game; each chapter with a unique location and gameplay hook. Every level is an extension of their respective master, giving the developers impetus to focus on how it all  as much as how well it . It also means you’ll see environments full of details that feel significant, not just the result of a haphazard prop department.As far as I’m concerned, In Sound Mind is an Instant classic. It’s light hearted. It’s funny. It’s poignant. It’s a game that hasn’t forgotten that it has to be  to play -- not just . It’s not about giving you a hard time either, or inflating odds in the name of challenge. You’re far from helpless.The big thing for me here is just its design sensibilities. It feels like a game from the early 2000s. Forget the dark, oppressive nature of Visage and all your Silent Hills. In Sound Mind handles like a game that empowers you, with perfectly balanced combat and accentuated scares scattered throughout. It handles well. It feels smooth. Intent just translates into action really well.More importantly though, it’s about the adventure. It reminds me a lot about The Beast Within in that sense. It’s about discovering the gimmicks, and the gameplay. Coming full circle with mechanisms that are clearly hinted at and systematically fed to you as the story develops. It plays with your expectations as much as it tries to unnerve you. Scares are often unceremonious and hilarious; borderline harassment. And the way it toys with perspective and perception makes you constantly do double takes and question yourself. It’s great at giving you that feeling that something is off.I adore it.Highly recommended to just about anyone who loves first person action games, and can stomach some great puzzles and good scares.

_childDocuments_.review: is a really solid high-concept horror/puzzle/adventure game by Tel Aviv-based studio We Create Stuff, previously best known for making horror mods of .  A lot of that genesis is intact in ; although nominally a horror game, it is in practice a linear first-person shooter title with some deceptively excellent puzzle gameplay.  Unfortunately, the shooting design is not nearly as competent as the execution of the puzzles, with sluggish controls, 3 weapons, and only 3 enemy types (that can be killed by shooting, anyway), but the puzzles alone are enough to carry the whole experience.The framework of  is a bit of a riff on ,  and a 'pursuer' horror game like  or .  As the protagonist - psychotherapist Desmond Wales - explores an abandoned, surreal city trying to figure out why his patients keep dying, he is haunted by the vengeful spirits of those selfsame patients who often have a very cool character design and thematic power emblematic of their diagnosis.  In addition to the more boring, standard enemy types, these tragic pursuers chase Desmond around the map, undeterred by weapons fire.Where the game does something interesting compared to your  or  is that Desmond frequently has to use the pursuer within the title's puzzle game loop, paying attention to the capabilities of each pursuer and goading them in to puzzle objects.  One monster, a man who was terribly afraid of the dark, takes the form of a black hole that objects can be swallowed up by, a bit like a  tunnel, and so the player can goad the monster to lower platforms or level elements with this ability.  Another monster, a man with rage problems, takes the form of a metal behemoth that charges the player in a straight line, and can be used to knock down doors or press buttons.  The depth of interactions between the pursuer and level geometry for the purposes of puzzle-platforming gameplay can get truly ingenious, without ever becoming frustrating; I felt that the puzzles were perfectly paced, and the perverse incentive to constantly stay close to the monster was a clever way to keep the player on-edge even if I never found the game unbearably scary.Yes,  would be the word I'd use to describe : it's consistently clever in its design, and always delights with new puzzles and gameplay conceits paced excellently throughout its ~8 hour length.  It's my hope that the great promise the team showed in this game is capitalized on in a sequel, one with less concessions to obligatory first-person shooter tropes and leaning even harder on the psychedelic puzzle gameplay that We Create Stuff clearly has an underutilized knack for.Bravo!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty unique game, with some fresh ideas. It is essentially an adventure / puzzle game primarily.It is heavily story-driven, with heavy themes of emotional and mental health, which is where the entire "psychological horror" aspect of the game is. It has some creepy moments, but in essence, it's not really a horror game. It has very little in the way of regular combat and regular enemies for that matter, so it's not a shooter either. Of all the items you will have in the game, merely two of them are real weapons.The strongest points in the game are the really creative and innovative boss fights and puzzles, exploration, and an authentic atmosphere and setting. Play it if you're looking for something new and fresh with some cool ideas.

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles aren't incredibly difficult, but you will probably spend a ton of time wandering if you happen to miss some clue as to where to go next. And honestly, even that part of the game is awesome as the worlds are amazing. But, often there is no clue as to where to go next. So you might just get flat out stuck until you do happen to see that little thing you kept missing. Those reviews that state the game turns into a first-person shooter I feel might have rushed things or didn't quite observe as much as they could have. Sure, you can use the brute-force solution of 'shoot guy in face until dead', but the game offers a lot more clever ways of removing enemies without bullets (or with fewer bullets). If you stop and 'reflect' before shooting, maybe some things will stand out. Also, if you don't explore more....you might also miss something that will also make combat easier.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm about ~3 hours into this game, and I am absolutely loving it. I've played a lot of psychological horror games, and this one has been creepy and satisfying in a way that is very rare. It has a thick atmosphere of devastating solitude, guilt, and surrealism, broken up by terrifying combat. (But with difficulty settings make this game more accessible.) The burning hot neon aesthetic is (as far as I know) a unique artistic choice in this genre. This game has presented me with a handful of moments I expect I will never forget.The game has the common trope of "mental illness turns people into monsters". I've got my fingers crossed that they stick the landing with a more nuanced message before the end of the game. If they achieve that, this game may unseat Silent Hill 2 as my favorite horror game evar.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the negative review, I do think this is a decent 6/10 game and that there's genuine effort put into it. If it's on sale then it's worth a playthrough. _childDocuments_.review: I found this to be such a beautiful game and highly recommend it to people that want a good story about mental health traumas that is built in slight horror elements. Where do I begin? I went into this knowing nothing during the steam summer festival awhile back with the demo. Thinking it was going to be a full on horror game, I found myself pleasantly surprised that I wasn't overwhelmed by the horror and instead was invested in the story. Come full release my friend got it for me, but it was put on hold for many months. Finally I have finished it and I loved the experience.The gameplay is akin to a horror game with metroidvania elements. Each story gives you a new "weapon" that is integral during said story. As you are introduced to the new elements, you will still be greeted by old elements so it never feels stale. I thoroughly enjoyed each tool and the different mechanics that they added. You also are equipped with a couple of guns to fend off shadow-like enemies at times. Finally, each story introduces a new "boss" enemy that changes the way you need to play the game (sneaking, using a mirror all the time, guns a blazing) which adds variety and kept me from getting bored. Granted there were a couple of boss fights and areas that I wish were fleshed out a little more but that is to be expected.Then we come to the story that won't be for everyone as it revolves around trauma and the mental health struggles that come with it. I noticed some arguing that it wasn't written very well from that standpoint but I never noticed an issue while playing. I constantly felt the emotion and struggle that each character had been through, and how it had turned them into the monster they are. Beating levels was always bitter sweet. And to have my trusty adorable talking cat at my side through it all, made me want to see it through to the end...no matter how sad it may become. Being that I felt connected to these characters from my own trauma may have also made me a little biased.However, I found it to be a wonderful game with an interesting take on trauma and I hope it gets the popularity that it deserves! 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 In Sound Mind is perfect, no cap, like the youth says. Go buy this game. Cons? One... dialogue was kind of cheesy a couple times. End of review.For real, though. I can't go deep into it without spoiling this wonderful experience of a game and I have to bite my hands as I type this cause I'm at the verge of geeking out all over it. The story is brilliant. The music is masterful. The levels are incredibly detailed and the ambience is sublime.I knew I was in for a treat when the title had such a grandiose presentation shortly after the game begins. We Create Stuff, the creators of Nightmare House 2, have proven once again that they not only have passion to show in their projects, but a brilliant knack at psychological horror. And having music be a heavily important part of the experience was a stroke of genius! I'm not talking just about ambient music, I'm talking about a meaty and mesmerizing dedicated soundtrack made by The Living Tombstone.For a story that features pretty dark psychological issues, it also has moments of subtle humor that let the tension ease off before building back up as the plot thickens all the way to an epic conclusion.In the sea of trash that is modern gaming, In Sound Mind is a paradisiacal island that not only honors the past, but also endears you for a future where people still have passion.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start this by saying that this one was hell of a journey, one that made feel emotions no other video game did in my 25 years of being alive.Won't spoil the game too much, but you play as Desmond Wales, a therapist that finds himself trapped inside of a strange hotel? The whole place is creepy and you have one mission, find out what's going on and leave this place alive, preferably.But this is where the twist came, to actually do that, you'll have to go and experience your patients traumas, something that many would find similar to their lives. I won't lie, the second patient story made me cry, but that's a-ok.The horror element is beautifully shown by We Create Stuff throughout the story, the audio and the environment rather than cheap jumpscares.Speaking of audio, the soundtrack is amazing and I highly recommend everyone to try and find all vinyls inside the game to listen to it.Bugs? Hehe, I haven't personally encounter any, despite my laptop being quite old and the game not running as well as I would have loved it to run.To end this review, I'll say it once more, this is not a simply horror game, no, this is one hell of an experience that would one way or the other touch you feelings like no other game.

_childDocuments_.review: I like almost everything about this game. It's a really different way of doing psychological horror that I haven't experienced before. There are some jump scares but they're usually done with the game's odd sense of humor where I didn't mind it. It's strange for this kind of game to have the occasional fart joke but it breaks up the tension and darkness of the main story well. It plays almost like half life in some sections which is unusual, but welcome, for this genre. Exploration is encouraged and there are puzzles around every corner.The only real issue are some serious optimization issues. With a 3080 I was having drops in some areas from 100fps to the 40s. If the framerate could be stabilized this would be a unique gem in the horror genre.

Most of the game, like around 90% of it is just bad. Bad game-play with its janky gun-play, bad horror when it comes to all it's scares. The game's story can be bogged down to a simple "government am bad cuz MKultra is real," seeing the game get overwhelming positive reviews is mind boggling to me. Seriously, both the tags "Horror" and "Psychological Horror" being used here is an insult to actual horror games, even as a comedy this game falls flat on its face, there is no horror or spooks. In Sound Mind is a game made for youtubers and streamers to play to for an audience of children, the "villain" reeks of "I'm quirky lol." He literally tip toes around corners on more than one occasion, hell, whenever he's on screen it makes me eye roll so bad that my eyes rolled back into my skull.Honestly, the only redeeming thing about the game is the mannequins, and I'm sure the developers know this, considering, they marketed the hell out of them and their section in the trailers, art, and animation. _childDocuments_.review: This is like Alan Wake and INFRA had a baby. I love a good mystery. It's psychological horror with mental health at its center, which has been treated with care and respect. Such a great and smart game, an overlooked gem on a platform with 82,500+ titles and it's better than any Amnesia game I've played. A fun mix of mechanics and often very funny, which I wasn't expecting. Just a heads up, there are jump scares here, sorta, the flashlight runs out of batteries, but guns run out of bullets, so get over it and the game has autosaves only, which only annoyed me with a couple of achievements. It has great original songs, professional voice acting and developers just making magic with the Unity engine. No showboating, it's substance over looks. While it's not going to impress anyone with its graphics, it actually reminds me of Source mods, there's more intelligent design here than in most triple A games and for half the price. Whether you get it for 30 money, 3 money or get it as a gift, just make sure you play it. In Sound Mind isn't for backlog padding, this deserves way more attention than it has gotten so far. I'll be voting for it in the Steam Awards, in whatever category I'm allowed to.

_childDocuments_.review: Great psychological horror indie game with a strong story-line, extremely well produced soundtrack, memorable tense moments and enjoyable combat mechanics. The first half of the game is very reminiscent of old school survival horror while the second half is more like a psychological thriller. Each level (six in total) are very different from one another and features a terrifying spirit that you must tame. The creature designs are creepy with one in particular being very unique in its ability as it chases you. The puzzle elements are tricky but never difficult if you take your time to look and listen carefully as the solutions are usually next to you either within a note or in a reflection. The only negative is having no in-game map system but instead having an useless pre-placed map at certain locations. The game can be beaten within 10 to 15 hours depending if you are going for all the hidden collectibles. Very enjoyable experience and looking forward to the sequel. [8.5/10]
