_childDocuments_.review: Finally getting around to finishing this a year after release. It's a solid experience...and, by the end, it surprisingly pulled on my heartstrings a bit (but that's probably because I just adore cats, and my own lovey died of old age just a little while ago, and the end of this game involves...well, no spoilers). "You're a pretty cool cat." "Yeah, I know."The structure of the game (the way the chapters are presented--or rather, the way you activate each chapter) overall is interesting--with an "otherworld" office belonging to the protagonist therapist Desmond (where he treats his patients and also where his snow white, talking cat Tonia [short for Cat-a-Tonia...har, har] hangs out). It's a "hub" of sorts which separates the chapters. You explore the real world digs (apartment, home, cabin) of each therapy patient first, but then you plunge into an "other" reality where the real action gameplay begins. At that point, it's a mix of mystery/detective collect-a-thon and kind-of-shooty mid-range horror. It's got atmosphere, a mix of locations that are tied to (and flesh out) each patient's case (from a lighthouse with a wrecked shipyard to a haunted Walmart-like department store and a sprawling train yard, all of it on the standard side for the most part). The big picture mystery (which ties together each patient's case) surprisingly involves a kind of government / big corporate cover-up that all Desmond's patients were connected to in some way--honestly, this "evil corp" aspect of the story gave me Umbrella-esque vibes.The enemies are two-legged "inkblot" monsters of several types (following through on the therapist theme). I guess you might say they are distant relatives of the Typhon mimics in Arkane's 2017 version of Prey? (Yes, I also played the original Prey way back in 2006 on my whining, overheating Xbox 360, and it was awesome, and I feel obliged to make that claim here...so...alright then.) The AI in general is very straightforward--the inkblots shamble around and patrol an area, but once they spot you they simply run at you full speed. The shooting is...okay. It's not broken, but it's not a strength either. Weapons are not amazing or interesting (pistol, shotgun, flare gun), but they all work and have an appropriate heft. There is an interesting reflection-type mini-game involving a mirror shard which you can gaze into (behind you) to see various collectibles and answers to puzzles. Personally, I found it a bit annoying trying to navigate backwards while looking into the mirror shard, but it ends up not really being entirely necessary--I forgot about using it at all after a while.I'm an elitist when it comes to music (sorry, not sorry--I've had four CDs published nationally over my many years with some tracks used on HBO TV shows and some indie films), and this game includes music by The Living Tombstone (I'm not familiar), and it's...not all that great. Some of the collectibles are actually vinyl records which you can take back to your office hub, and you can listen to an entire 3- or 4-minute track while you pet your cat. (Damn, come to think of it, one of my tracks was pressed to white-label vinyl too by LTJ Bukem's Good Looking label a decade ago--hell, I need to dig that out, dust off my turntable, and listen to it again...it's been a while.) Anyway, the record-spinning component in the game is an interesting idea (and I know it's been done before--wasn't there something like this in one of new Wolfenstein games?), but the problem here: The songs are...eh...not all that great. Some of them are fine, but the lyrics for most of them are...well, they sound like they've been written for an aggro teen or someone like that...kind of cloying, sentimental, obvious...tiresome. As an ancient 57-year-old dude, I guess I just wasn't the audience. Production values are good though. All in all, the game feels like a proper adventure, honestly. I know my playtime says 26+ hours, but I'm glacially slow at playing games in general. There's no way a normal person at normal speed would need even half that amount of time to finish this title. The end hints strongly at a sequel (that may be...co-op?), and I imagine a sequel will happen considering this title was reviewed pretty favorably by the press and players alike. I'd play a part two "fur" sure. The devs just better bring back Tonia, dammit!
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: You can pet the cat.On a more serious note however, the game is more or less a Stranger Things-esque immersive sim. The story, soundtrack, & visual style are definitely the best parts about the game. As for the bad, the game's technical performance is really poor to be frank. I have a beastly PC, yet I get constant frame jitters. Altogether, highly recommend this game. You might need to use a guide if you get lost in a few parts, but you can usually figure stuff out on your own if you just have a little patience.Pick this one up for ~$15 or less & I am sure you'll be satisfied with it if the game sounds interesting to you.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: I don't often write reviews.  But I need to express how much I recommend this game.  It subverts just enough genre expectations to make it very tense, and the atmosphere is amazingly well put together.  The devs could have padded it out and added a bunch of unnecessary stuff, but the game has a decent length as is, and gets through its story expertly. There is also a cat, whom you can pet.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: Beautifully crafted game. Where it lacks in horror, it more than makes up for in its atmosphere, soundtrack, and its storyline. Speaking of, this game's true richness lies is in how story based it is, so if that is not your thing, probably not the game for you. But this got me back into games again, and I even bought it for a few friends. 10/10 reccomend. I don't even regularly leave reviews but this one needed it.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: Good game with some cool mechanics, locations and funny gimmicks, that also has an interesting and unique story with fun characters. The voice acting and writing are also well done. Never heard of The Living Tombstone but they made some cool and fitting songs for this game.However, some gameplay mechanics and sequences felt a bit clunky, repetitive and/or out of place (especially some specific parkour sequences and ).  also seemed a bit unoriginal and repetitive, featuring only some boring parkour and shooting (the build up was cool though). Finally, I had a very annoying bug that caused me to get stuck in some strange invisible barriers in multiple locations and chapters. It prevented me from moving and jumping, which resulted in my death during parts like the . I had to noclip to get out of them. But besides these points, you can tell that the developers put a lot of time and effort into this game. It is really fun and one of a kind! All in all, the positives outweigh the negatives, so I would recommend it! If you are contemplating on buying it on sale for only 3 euros. DO IT! It is worth more than that. PS: It is not a scary game, but it is also not really meant to be one.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely solid psychological horror game. Great story, great level design, great atmosphere, good puzzles, and good combat make for an all around great experience. Some may not be able to justify the price since the game has only four levels, a hub world, and a final boss level, giving you about 10-15 hours of playtime. But if you can put down the money or wait for a sale definitely pick it up
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: SUCH a good horror puzzle game, had so much fun with this game, and probably will never find a new game that holds up to this level of polish. I did have a few issues tho; The FPS on this game on linux is usually fine, but Tape 2 and Tape 3 really stress test your system(15FPS average on Tape 2). Also the puzzle in Tape 3 got me for a while but otherwise they're perfect.Friend bought me the game
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this was a surprisingly well put together action horror game.  It definitely starts more on the horror side, but by the end is a full action game with strong feels of Half-Life.  There are a few legitimately new ideas in here, and overall I found the game well put together and fun to explore/navigate through.  Also, the level design is pretty impressively nested with hidden secrets and reasons to loop back for a game of this scale.The game holistically is set up in 4 acts, with a hub world somewhat connecting all of them.  Each of the worlds has a pretty unique flavor and gimmick associated with it, so the gameplay keeps changing as you move forward.  Finally, you can pet a cat.  So yeah, if the game looks up your alley you'll definitely have a good time.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: Really solid game. A weird blend of horror, comedy and metroidvania-like progression. Can be a bit scary at the beginning. It's very formulaic in its design but they manage to still have a lot of environment and gameplay variety. Each level having its own gameplay mechanic is cool but I think some of the ideas are better than others. The first level is perfect imo. Having to use a piece of a mirror to scare the monster and find objects is genius. The other levels are good but feel less polished or underdeveloped. A lot of good moments and the game doesn't take itself too seriously. You can tell it was made with love.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: In Sound Mind was an awesome experience. The game really only limited my experience with the technical aspects. I wish the game performed better and had a more unique art approach.However, the game's mechanics were stellar. The ideas when implementing new items/abilities were really exciting and intertwined with the story really well. Nothing in the story was overdone, and like the gameplay, the story was creative and fun.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: FANTASTIC GAME!!!!I bought this on sale for 4 bucks. Once I started playing I instantly fell in love with it! The perfect mix of combat, parkour, and storytelling had me on edge throughout the whole thing. I liked the game so much that I went so far as to obtain all of the achievements! Anyways, if you are looking for a game to play if you are bored I 100% recommend this game. Also, if you are like me and love that feeling of satisfaction of getting every single achievement and not spending years to do it then this is the game for you. Huge props to the game's developers for creating such an amazingly fun and action-packed game with a solid story.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible story is 8/10 there's some that i don't like, Gameplay is fun!!! Soundtracks is out of this world well because Tombstone made it idk what to expect tbh. Apparently there's some cliffhanger at the end. I defo wanna see it but i think its complete by itself i love every part of the games.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: Not sure how I can across In Sound Mind as I don't ever remember playing a demo for it. Chances are I picked it up based on ratings or very good reviews and took and chance and purchased it. Well I'm sure glad I did. I think this might be the 'bigger" (as in a long play) game I'm looking for. At the start I was a bit overwhelmed at the initial space that could be searched but turns out it's manageable and so far the game is interesting, and has me chomping at the bit to figure out just what is going on. Definitely interesting, fun, but really can't say more because I'm still in the beginning stages having just played Victoria's tape and currently slogging through the torn up Homa Mart. Anyways, will post more later on as I progress, if I can.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: Short version - absolute banger.When I was a kid I played Nightmare House 2 and there was something special about it even back then.I had this game laying around for a while, got it as soon as I learned the developers of the mod made their own full game and I am really sorry it took me so long to get around to play it.This again, is something really special. Hard to put my finger on what exactly makes it such an amazing experience, but I know that the game has so much soul and love put into it.Just play it, you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: Bad frame rates. My guess is that the "hold up mirror knife and have truesight of what's behind you" mechanic isn't very well optimized. I lost interest after finishing the 2nd chapter because the combat is tedious and has ammo starvation and the big monster won't stop loudly harassing you while you're trying to solve the puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: Quite a good game with great atmosphere and decent sound design. On top of that, it can get pretty spooky too in certain moments, even giving me some Layers of Fear vibes at times. The narrative design befits the genre - you unravel what is going on with the main protagonist and other characters through tapes, notes, and scarce bits of dialogue with the one who I presume is the main antagonist, and hence, the final boss to defeat. Beat two bosses but, unfortunately, did not feel invested enough in the story to keep going at the time of playing. Otherwise, can definitely recommend to at least give it a go.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: This was a game I didn't expect to enjoy as much as I had. I originally found it because I was recently shown music by The Living Tombstone and found out they did the soundtrack for this.Overall I have been impressed by the story. And for a horror game, they only have a few jump scares and they're good payoff ones at that! Then you have moments where something changes when you look away (I loved "Dave" btw!. Otherwise, the game is great at keeping tension. As for music, the thing that brought me here, the first tape I think is the best, though they're all good in their own right. But having such a melody to play with and the Watchers, it all just went together. I do wish the soundtrack song and the level song could be more alike but I know that can't work perfectly all the time.Play this game if you're a fan of psychological horror and enjoy a great soundtrack. It's worth the price of admission.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great.  Extremely story-rich and puzzles to keep you engaged all along the way - but not too many puzzles to the point of frustration that tempts you to lookup solutions online.  A unique story full of twists and turns, great voice acting, and really fun game mechanics and concepts all wrapped up into one.  I picked this game up on sale for $5 but would have been okay with paying $20 for it.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: Loving it so far, very unique, original, and overall just fun. It knows what it is and doesn't take itself 100% seriously. There's a lot of comedy in the game and it balances superbly with the darker themes. The amount of charm and wit the writing displays (while knowingly camp at times, I mean listen to the main villain) is definitely cohesive and interesting to explore, and the story and environments so far are equally well thought-out and put together. There's tons of hidden collectables that I've really enjoyed rooting around for, the tapes requiring no backtracking to get all of them if you've a keen eye. The music and sound design, while not always feeling thematically appropriate, is also very well implemented. I don't recall running into any bugs either, save for a weird world rendering flicker synchronised to a flashing light bulb after the  Neither bug was game-breaking as I'd already finished the tape. Also seems to be decently optimised - I don't have an amazing PC but I've seen no stutters, crashes or framedrops as of yet.As a long time fan of the Nightmare House series, it's super fun to see the amount of easter eggs and callbacks; this game overall feels like an incredibly natural progression from its origins and I've quickly fallen in love with it. So far it's just a fun game world to explore and it's one that you can tell is full of passion. Let's hope it finishes strong. I just wanted to review it now to mention the warm feeling in my heart I got when I saw the NH2 mannequin model on the ship.Oh I should mention cons too. The only thing I really don't care for in the game is the weapon combat - it's very unfocused and under developed. It's much better when you can combat the enemies with the environment (distracting them with a loud sound, in one instance shining a light at an enemy) but times like that are few and far between. When spotted enemies just bumrush me and I end up wasting ammo not being able to land a hit off on what appears to be a critical hit, though there's not great visual indication that my weapons are being effective or not.Definitely worth your time! Excited to hop back into it again soon.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

_childDocuments_.review: From the creators of cult classic Nightmare House 2, comes an imaginative psychological horror experience that challenges your expectations and ushers you through the deepest corners of your mind. As you awake in the corridors of an inexplicable building, you find the environment takes on a life of its own and leads you to discover a series of victims, all exposed to the same experimental therapy. In your search for answers, bizarre visions emerge and introduce a host of imposing horrors. With your sanity in question, you have no choice but to rely on your instinct…and a cat named Tonia. In Sound Mind is a witty first-person psychological horror with frenetic puzzles, unique boss fights, and original music by The Living Tombstone. Explore and fight through a series of unsettling memories as you journey within the inner workings of the one place you can’t seem to escape—your own mind.
_childDocuments_.name: In Sound Mind

name: Infini
detailed_description: Challenge your mind in a psychedelic journey of puzzles and meaningful encounters with Time, Poetry, Memory, Technology, War and Fatality. As Hope drifts deeper into Infinity, the real world begins to suffer from his absence. There doesn’t seem to be any way out, and Hope is by nature doomed to carry on. Master the innovative camera manipulation mechanic to unlock new areas. Each world harbors new abilities, themes, and opportunities to explore the multiverse and meet bizarre personalities who can be helpful allies or deceitful foes. Infini Key Features : ● Discover a unique, mind-bending and varied gameplay ● Immerse yourself in a rich emotional story ● Easy to learn but increasingly challenging ● At least 8 hours of gameplay across 100+ levels and 10 diverse worlds ● Experience original imagery and a soundtrack of over 20 songs ● Feel the void of Infinity! DEVELOPED BY Barnaque “We are always striving to push limits and break boundaries with our narratives, gameplay and music. Our goal with Infini is to throw you into an unknown world of surprise.” - David Martin and Emeric Morin from the Montreal-based indie studio. PUBLISHED BY Nakana.io “We gather games that share a strong experience to remember. With Infini we are excited to present a title that manages to be both unique and captivating in all its aspects: gameplay, art and story.” - Mikaël Bourget, founder of the publishing label.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow.(I have finished the game with a 100% completion)This game is a true gem.The visual, the audio and the gameplay are all extremely unique. I had all three aspects blow me away at multiple part of the game.Highly recommended for anyone who loves puzzle game or would like to experience a game like you've never seen before.
_childDocuments_.name: Infini

_childDocuments_.review: I’m still not done with the game. I’m probably half way through and I plan on updating my review when I’m done. Infini is a puzzle game with a simple initial idea: you’re are constantly falling and when you reach the end of the screen, you just reappear on the other side. From that simple idea, the team behind Infini did craft a lot of puzzles where the rules change (having the ability to fly upward, changing direction from up and down to left and right, using a jetpack (!) to go fast enough to break through obstacles, pushing beach balls to destroy other kind of obstacle, etc.). Those variations on the initial idea keep the game fresh and interesting and, for me, challenging.  I will update more in the future, but for now, I’m enjoying the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Infini

_childDocuments_.review: I've had a blast playing this game so far and just couldn't put it down. The game starts very simple, but rapidly becomes a mind-binding puzzle with all the added mechanics. Even requires a bit of skills at the end to properly queue every actions. The universe is very interesting and the story keeps you engaged with each different chapters. Definitely recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Infini

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most unique and fun games I've ever played. It has this surreal aspect of the works of Alejandro Jodorowsky. The level design is what really makes this game special. Every level explores a unique combination of mechanics. A lot of them really make you think outside the box, experiment, and just keep trying different things. An overlooked masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: Infini

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game I still think about even months after I've beaten it. Don't let its crude aesthetics put you off what is in my opinion of the most bizarre and interesting puzzle games I've played yet.Infini does a good job of introducing a new gameplay mechanic each stage so you won't feel like you're playing a repetitive game. The puzzles require you to stretch your brain a bit but its not too hard and the length felt appropriate for the price tag. The music and artstyle took some getting used to but it absolutely fits the themes the game conveys. When I would get stuck on a level the thing that kept pushing me forward was always the story. I wanted to see what could possibly happen next and I truly enjoyed finding out about the hidden lore in the game. I'd recommend Infini to anyone, but words can't express how amazing and thought provoking the game is. Give it a chance you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Infini

_childDocuments_.review: I'm finding it hard to describe how I feel about Infini. The soundtrack, themes, art, and gameplay are phenomenal. The game's mind boggling puzzles and difficulty had made the last slog an insufferable experienced I felt happy to have gone through when it was over. I'll warn your mental well-being, but I'd recommend the experience of Infini to nearly anyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Infini

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best game i've ever played. I've played it quite a bit in some event already and i've only begun to play the real deal, but it got me hooked right from the beginning of the game. The characters, the story line, the puzzles, everything is really well made and with great care. Love the developers too, they are really nice!
_childDocuments_.name: Infini

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this game is... weird, sad, ugly and beautiful.It's a really weird beast, but a beast I'd recommend to people interested in deep philosophical and symbolic stories.Everything about this game, the art style, the music, the puzzles, is strange and slightly disturbing, but it fits perfectly with the game's story. It's a great example of a game that tries to make you feel the main character's emotions through the game's design.It's not an easy game, some of the puzzles are pretty difficult, not only in terms of puzzle solving, but also in terms of the dexterity required to solve them. Your character is falling most of the time and you often need to move quickly to get where you want to go.I've completed about 60% of the game in a little over 3 hours, which, with the levels being more and more difficult, is in line with the "at least 8 hours of gameplay" promised by the developers.
_childDocuments_.name: Infini

_childDocuments_.review: Infini is a nice trip, as someone wrote - acid trip. At first glance, it is totally strange, not entirely accessible and not quite pretty. But above all it is one of the most interesting logic games on the market. The puzzles are demanding but satisfying and fair. Mechanics are used in an interesting way, which is often a weak point of such games that can be very repetitive - infini surprises with every level. Story is very philosophical and thought-provoking, but like visual site it's not easy to digest. If you are fans of interesting and intriguing games then absolutely try Infini, don't let the not-so-pleasant environment reject you.
_childDocuments_.name: Infini

_childDocuments_.review: Lose yourself in Infinity… but never lose Hope. Try to escape a world of never-ending puzzles and oddities.
_childDocuments_.name: Infini

name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders
detailed_description: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders brings the 2004 cult action-strategy hybrid hit to PC. Take up arms and lead massive fantasy armies from the front lines. Experience an epic scale medieval warfare!! Conquer your foes with sword and sorcery, steel and strategy! Enhanced for modern PCs. - Full controller support (we recommend using a gamepad for the optimal experience) plus an all-new mouse & keyboard mode. - Revisit classic battlefields in widescreen HD. - The thundering guitar soundtrack returns. Metal heavier than any knight’s plate! Adapt and survive on an ever-changing battlefield. - Charge with the sun at your cavalry’s backs to blind your targets. - Burn your enemy out of forests, or hide behind dense walls of smoke. - Claim the high ground and crush your foes in the valleys below. - High winds blow smoke and deflect arrows, and rain douses flame. - Watch the skies; falling aerial units can make an impression on infantry. - Close ranks in melee, and scatter your troops as artillery rains down. Hack and slash through armies as a powerful hero. - Become a master of arms as you directly control one of four legendary heroes. - Master each hero’s special attacks and combos and wreak havoc on your foes. - Change the tide of battle. Cut down officers and watch their ranks crumble. - Call on allied heroes to assist you in battle, each with their own unique skills & spells. - One warrior can’t win the war. Command your troops from the tactical map as you fight. Reforge your soldiers in the fires of war: - Watch the campaign unfold across a 3D world map, and lead your troops across it. - Spend the spoils of war on upgrading and customizing your troops. - Level up your units, equip them or change their class to fit your strategy. - Assign powerful special abilities and spells to your troops to call upon in battle. - Fill your army with spectacular special units including airships and giant monsters. Your armies stand ready and await orders, commander.

_childDocuments_.review: Shock and Awe. Could not believe my eyes when i seen this title (re-incarnated) sitting in the steam store. This game is LEGENDARY beyond reason... If you've played it 15 years back you know what i'm talking about. If your 15 years old, go steal 20$ from your parents, play this game. It is a true (one of a kind). The standard. Bar None. Has held a wicked reputation for over a decade... WE'VE ALL SAID WE MISSED IT, AND ITS BACK!!!! K.U.F. YOUTUBERS REJOICE!!! SEND WORD TO THE MASSES!!! The game is OUTSTANDING, period. -Minus multiplayer? oh well go play KUF2 if that's what you want. DEVS DESERVE A STANDING OVATION; CONTROLLER SUPPORT MENU, NO LOOT BOXES, NO B.S. Even if KUF2 didn't do as well as desired; The Presence of THIS game ...could possibly mean-? Will the DEV's break the magic seals and AWAKEN THE ANCIENT DEMONS..!?!?!? Will CIRCLE OF DOOM come-- Kicking/Roaring/screaming back to life?!? The new-world could not possibly be ready for that yet... They are NOT PREPARED... Time will tell. For now, buckle up kids: You've never slain bodies; till' you've slain bodies in KINGDOM UNDER FIRE! Just remember CRITICS: RE-RELEASE. NOT BRAND NEW. Have well over 3000 hours in this and circle of doom, (XBOX). Replay value?.. YES!! RE-PAY VALUE? YES!! Worth the wait, Worth 20$, worth everything the game is, was, and meant to be.. THEY DON'T MAKE GAMES AS GREAT AS THESE ANYMORE. SOLID BUY. FULL SEND.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR European High Fantasy Dynasty Warriors with RTS Elements (works surprisingly well), game works, locked to 30fps, no initial glaring issues, just as though you were playing an Xbox game that was released on PC like.... 15 years ago or so. Also, pretty savage metal soundtrack too.Well, hopped in and did the first missions. Its as you remember, if you've played it on Xbox. Feels a BIT like... almost like its emulated. There isn't much changed as far as I can remember/tell. 30fps lock, but, didn't seem to be messing with my refresh at all, so it looked and ran smoothly. Using a Controller, though there are KB&M Controls (can't speak to them though, not a game I'd really suggest using them on). There isn't anything special here, aside from, well, an accessible and fully functional way to play Kingdom Under Fire. If thats what you're looking for, then this is what you want.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: Literally my favourite game of all time. An original take on the high fantasy genre, intense mix of hack and slash and rts gameplay with a lot of awesome rpg features, and FOUR 10-12 mission long campaigns, each one more awesome than the last. Buy this game. Buy it five times, spend all the money you would've spent on whatever BS modern AAA title just came out and buy this game instead. You will never regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: This is the only game that has ever combined RTS, RPG, and an active battle system in a way that works fluidly. There is nothing like the thrill of taking on a hoard of enemies and winning through meaningful tactics like use of terrain, direction of sunlight, and flanking as well as through frantic swordplay. It's a battle system that rewards strategic thinking, and forces you into situations that require flexibility in your tactics. You can't turtle or dive your way through every mission. The player-controlled unit is powerful, but it can't win the day for you with brute strength on its own. I wish they had given the graphics an overhaul for this version, but in the heat of battle you won't notice it's a little blocky. Overall, a ground-breaking game that deserves a place of honor on any gamer's shelf!
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: Kingdom Under Fire is one of those games that's basically the definition of a "hidden gem" because it never really found that strong of an audience when it first released all the way back on the original Xbox, but it did a lot of interesting things that made it either better than or at least different enough from its peers to be genuinely interesting.Basically, it does Dynasty Warriors better than Dynasty Warriors, in my opinion, by expanding the tactical elements into something meaningful. A cross between hack and slash and Total War, you take control of a heroic lead character who is completely OP, but you lead a small number of units of men from the front on what are usually rather open battle maps. You can direct these units into advantageous tactical positions in ways that actually matter, but when your main unit meets with the enemy, you take direct control of your hero and hack n'slash the enemy to death in a relatively simple real-time combat system. The result is actually something very dynamic, as it addresses the potential downsides people might find with two very different genres. For the hack n'slash crowd, the tactical elements  matter more than you would expect and give you something that you actually need to think about critically rather than hitting endless button combos, while for the tactics crowd you get a dose of twitch action that livens up your tactical decisions by putting you directly into the action. It's a hybrid combo that probably won't be suited to any purist's tastes for either genre, but is interesting and different enough that it ends up engaging for fans of either genre looking for something a bit different from the norm.What's more surprising is that it actually has a rather good story. Though it's not delivered perfectly, with rather simple cutscenes even by the standards of the time and uneven voice acting, the overall plot and characters are well written, delving into a fantasy world that approaches Warhammer levels in its grimdarkness while being somehow grittier and at least as brutal (thanks in no small part to the soundtrack, which completely eschews standard fantasy fare for heavy metal constantly thrashing in the background).I wouldn't say this port is perfect, but it works well enough and frankly, it's surprising that this game was rescued from the archives of lost media island to be re-released onto steam 15 years after its debut. Worth your time if you want to try something a bit different and you're not afraid of some outdated graphics.

_childDocuments_.review: I missed Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders the first time around completely and I’d somehow never even heard of it when I came across news of its Steam release. At first glance, I got a Dynasty Warriors vibe from it though after getting my hands on it I’ve discovered that it’s much heavier on the strategy and somewhat lighter on the hack-and-slash. To be honest, it’s quite a bit different than anything that I’ve played before and feels like a combination of Dynasty Warriors and a simplified Total War game that somehow works.Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders tells the story of a war that has broken out in a familiar, but unique, fantasy world. Humans, orcs, elves, and a handful of other staples of the genre show their faces here in a way that pays their respects to their inspirations while showing us something new. There are heavily armed and armored knights, beefy ogres, terrifying dragons in the sky, and mortars on the ground. You’ll choose one of four factions and play their hero as you battle through their involvement in the events to come. Don’t expect any real narrative choice though; your heroes and units are yours to build and customize as you please but the entire experience consists of moving from one battle on the map to the next with brief intermissions where you can spend experience and gold to upgrade your forces and engage in some setting-building conversation. Scenarios are predetermined and the story itself is as linear as can be.The audio and visuals are decent enough, though as with most games released in the early 2000s, they’re certainly outdated when compared to today’s standards. Some aspects are fantastic, like the inclusion of an archer in the unit running up and down your line lighting arrows with a torch when you order a volley of fire arrows. Others aren’t as impressive, such as how some characters seem to be chewing like a cow while they speak. The overall graphics and art style do well enough to immerse you in the atmosphere though they’re certainly a long shot from what you probably prefer in an action game at this point.The metal soundtrack surprised me, initially by its existence, and then by how well it fits in with and creates intensity with the game every step of the way. I used to consider myself a purist of sorts and preferred music that might exist in the setting itself, but I can say that I’ve been converted more and more by the excellent use of modern music that has been adapted into titles where you wouldn’t necessarily expect it at first.Combat is the primary, almost single-minded focus of Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders, and as your army grows, your ability to manage it just as well. The first few scenarios feel a bit Dynasty Warriors as you control one unit, so the required tactical thinking is minimal, but each new unit broadens your control over the battlefield. You’ll never be overwhelmed by the number of units that you’re tasked with commanding and swapping between them to issue orders quickly becomes second nature.The wide variety of units on a single class tree immediately interested me. It starts simple enough with basic units, but as these units gain experience they’ll be able to evolve into more powerful, faction-specific types. These upgrades come with a sleek new look, some stat buffs, the potential for new equipment options, and maybe even some new abilities.Although buying new equipment for your heroes is exciting and can help you tailor your efficiency that much more, the special abilities of your units take front and center and there’s plenty of variety. For example, archers can set their arrows on fire to rain flame down on their enemies, doing catastrophic damage under the right circumstances. Alternatively, sappers can detect and disarm enemy traps, set their own, and even interact with the environment to turn the tide of battle in your favor.Outside of these, there are a few additional tactics that you can employ to overcome your foes. The sun itself stands out as the most unique as it can be a friend or foe at any given time. You’ll always want to prioritize positioning your units so that it is at their back and use it against your enemy whenever possible; a blinded soldier is one that can’t fight to their fullest. I found this particularly innovative as most games entirely ignore this element of tactical combat that has played a huge role throughout history.There are a couple of issues that I have that you’re sure to face if you spend any real time with this title, some of which are unforgivable, others which are simply the standard for the era that it was released in. The more frustrating of the two is that battles can be quite long, well over half an hour depending on the situation. This wouldn’t normally be a problem other than that there are no autosaves and they tend to be more or less the same each time you play thanks to the linear nature of the game. The second problem ties directly into this first as there are times when unit reactions to your orders simply don’t make much sense. You might give an order for a unit to move to a specific location and they’ll walk forward forty yards before starting to turn in the direction that they need to be going in. This may very well get them and the rest of your forces annihilated in some missions where stealth is key, putting you in a position where Issue #1 becomes a serious problem. That said, the latter issue tends to be relatively rare and although it interfered with my enjoyment of the game a few times, I had a good experience overall.Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders is a strategy RPG that I would’ve loved if I’d played it on its release. I can’t say that I have that same level of enthusiasm for it in 2020 when there are so many fantastic titles available, though there’s still plenty of fun to be had here if the concept interests you. As long as you can embrace its corny dialogue, accept its flaws when it comes to the combat not being all that realistic, and embrace its outdated visuals and audio, there’s a solid game here that still manages to feel unique and innovative to this day.Original Review:

_childDocuments_.review: This was one of my favourite games from my childhood. I haven't played it in, what, 20 years? 19 or 18 years? I'm not sure. I had forgotten it exists until I saw it randomly in the steam store. I bought it and played it all night. It's exactly how I remember, and it's just as fun as it was in my memory. I think this game stands up surprisingly well - one of the best games from the 360 era. The gameplay mechanics feel surprisingly modern for its age. It's a hack and slash game merged together with an RTS, with RPG elements thrown in for good measure. You command a small army when outside of battles by directing your troop units which consists of melee units, archers, spearmen, cavalry, artillery. You can upgrade these units with a skill tree, so basic swordsmen can be upgraded to knights, etc. As for the RPG elements: when you enter battle you directly control your commander, and after a level, you can buy new weapons for the commander, upgrade their stats, and choose different abilities, such as healing spells, lightning spells, and special attacks. The story is also great. It's kind of basic - about a crusade against evil dark elves (who I think are based off of DnD Drow) and orcs), but the characters are fantastic, and it's the way the story is told that makes it so interesting. It's very loose and rough, just like the music.THE MUSIC. The music is incredible. The entire soundtrack is heavy metal, and it just fits the vibe perfectly as you run around a battlefield as the beefiest dude in the world with a gigantic claymore, a scantily clad dark-elf in a gstring, or a bodybuilder demon. It might sound childish, and that's because it is, but it's self-aware of its childishness, and it leans into it. It intentionally tries to be as cool and hardcore as possible, which makes it very endearing and fun. It feels like riding a jet ski while slamming a tinny.The graphics hold up to this day - another surprise to me. And the aesthetic is wonderful. I seriously wonder whether Demon's/Dark Souls was influenced by this game, because to me, it has a strong Souls aesthetic. And this came out well before Demon's Souls.Overall, fantastic game from 20 years ago that holds up surprisingly well. It's a fun mix of a number of genres that is entirely unique, I haven't seen a game like it since, and the story is very entertaining.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a bare-bones port with 4K support and locked at 30fps, but the game itself is fantastic and it's great to see all the additional details from the higher resolution.The controls and interface have a little bit of a learning curve, and feel slightly awkward at first, but once you are acclimated, the brilliance of the game really shines through. The transition between strategic commands and hack and slash is absolutely seamless, and it was a major accomplishment to design an interface that allowed a game of this complexity to be played on a gamepad.The hack and slash action is still fun. Plenty of games since have had deeper movesets, but there is a certain visceral weight to both the moves and enemies that a lot of more modern games have not duplicated. It just feels . . . solid. Like Rupert's delts. Tactically, the game rewards you for good decisions in an impactful way. For example, archers can't shoot as well if they are facing the sun or trees, and if you flank an enemy, you get extra SP (which allows you to do more super moves and kill the enemy even faster). This is the rare game that fuses two genres and actually does both of them well.The story and characters are also very entertaining. Voice acting is generally bad, but often in a way that it's actually so bad that it's good. In summary, this game is not just a nostalgia trip for people who enjoyed it before, it's a legitimately good game that has held up over time very well, and the innovative control scheme (particularly with how you can seamlessly set multiple waypoints on the minimap) is something that other games have not duplicated. Even 15+ years later, this is still arguably the best game of its type.

_childDocuments_.review: KUF Crusaders is essentially an rts mixed with 3rd person hack and slash gameplay.As far as I know, KUF is quite unique in how it plays, as the only game I've played having similar ideas is maybe Brutal Legend, but even then, they're very different in execution.In the meat of the game, you are given 5 slots, give or take, to pick whatever troop you have in your army to take on missions, with each mission throwing different scenarios, enemy unit compositions, and tactics. Each unit has specific roles and counters they fulfill, so you can get caught off guard by different enemies and situations that you'll have to think to get out of.When in a mission, you switch between each unit you control and give them their orders individually (though there is a very basic and limited way to command all simultaneously) with your hero's unit being unique.When in melee combat as your hero's infantry, you take direct control of your hero in the middle of the battle yourself- you aren't a Dynasty Warriorsesque lawn mower, but your main unit has the edge that is your hero being there.There are four different campaigns, one for each hero, each being their perspective of an overall story that (though I might be biased) I think is good to at least average.You can play 2 campaigns immediately, the easy one being a bit more railroaded as a tutorial campaign that explains mechanics and how everything started, with the normal still teaching you but giving a bit more freedom (normal is required to unlock the last 2 campaigns).But the game really shines in the two hard campaigns- the hard campaigns give optional extra missions to complete, scale the battles drastically, makes use of all the units available for both armies, and gives you the actual main conflict of the game.The voice acting is really all over the place. There are some downright awful performances, to some that are at surprisingly good. Also, the word "pope" is completely cut out, because they thought it'd be controversial back then.The soundtrack also really gives this series its character-very intense heavy metal music to accompany the fighting, and it sets the tone of whether a battle is getting climactic or desperate very well.The controls were made for the og Xbox, so the keyboard and mouse take some fiddling to figure out- you can use the '~ key at anytime however to see the current controls. Once I learned them however, its totally doable, but you would be better off using a controller if you have one.The UI, artwork, and fonts are clearly exactly as they used to be, showing its age as they are all low res. Devs have already stated that they'll look into fixing that however. Autosaves aren't a thing in this 2004 Xbox game.There are a few bugs that weren't in the original: transparent lines around some textures, repeating/wrong contextual dialogue from your troop commands, some particles effects being squares; major bugs causing crashes have already been patched, with only minor non gameplay bugs being around from what I've seen and read.Game is capped at 30fps, possibly being tied to the gameplay, though devs have already said it'll be looked into.Devs have also posted about the game having modding support, and after fiddling with it myself, the game seems simple to mod/edit, so fixes to these issues are guaranteed, official or unofficial.I hope this port is successful, so they'll port this game's sequel, KUF Heroes. Heroes has 7 campaigns, each one being a playable character of the cast already in Crusaders, also telling the same war from their perspective.Overall, this was genuinely one of my favorite games as a kid, and though visually in some places it has aged poorly, I wholeheartedly recommend it, as there are very few games with massive battles around that aren't you just steamrolling massive hordes of enemies all by yourself! More games should take this gameplay formula and really refine it!

_childDocuments_.review: If you're able to look past its awkward and rushed translation, the rust and crust around the game's age, and the frankly embarrassing way the game outfits its dark elves, you will find a rewarding blend of action and tactical games and an even more surprisingly refreshing take on well worn high fantasy tropes.Right off the bat, this game sets up expectations for a very stereotypical world of elves, orc, giant scorpions, and other familiar fantasy fauna, but over time will pull the rug out from under you. Its willingness to humanize its orcs as well as its willingness to criticize power structures is especially refreshing for a piece of media from nearly two decades ago. Not all of it is flawlessly executed, of course, especially in regards to its translation from Korean. There are occasional wordings and phrases that just don't make much sense and you get a lot of moments like that from the very start. Its writing is still heavy-handed in an extremely video game sort of way, and I find the constant bickering between the characters of Lucretia's campaign to be especially bothersome and unnecessarily vitriolic. The plot also moves at a particularly glacial pace, one could say that the game doesn't "really begin" until the third and fourth campaigns, with the first two being more of an opportunity for tutorialization and world building. But everything wraps up in a way that is compelling, exciting, and far more thought-provoking than one would expect from a game like this.On a mechanical level, KuF:TC offers a simple tactical game and simple hack-and-slash combat that when combined manages to become more than the sum of its parts as you quickly find yourself bouncing between ordering your troops and personally slashing through hoards of enemies en mass. The 'lower-to the ground' perspective over more traditional strategy games gives you a much more direct and personable feeling, allowing you to see your troops as more than just dots on a map as you aim to protect them and take advantage of their strengths and weaknesses. Though you may come to find that this game does not have a particularly gentle difficulty curve. This game will demand a lot from you in terms of multitasking, situational awareness, and even a small degree of lateral thinking. Particularly in the third and fourth campaigns you will be put into situations that seem absolutely impossible at first glance. But if you're willing to persevere, you will find a rewarding and replayable experience.On top of that, there is an, admittedly small, degree of unit customization that lets you further connect with your troops. Experience and gold can be used to tailor your troops for the mission at hand, and success in the campaign will hinge on knowing what kinds of troops to take and keeping them properly equipped. It's all fairly simple, but offers a lot of small joys.The music, while not particularly memorable on its own, does help the overall experience stand out from the crowd of high-fantasy strategy games. Rather than relying on an orchestral score, we are instead presented with a more hard rock soundtrack that aims to be more high-energy rather than grandiose. It's smaller, more intimate, louder, and more aggressive; and as a result fits the tone of the gameplay almost perfectly.There are many aspects that are flawed, like its slapdash translation or sudden difficulty spikes. Some aspects that I find particularly troubling, particularly its portrayal and treatment of women. But there are many positives that make up for these shortcomings if you are able to look past those negatives. There really are a lot of great ideas to be found in this game and I ultimately do recommend taking a look if you are interested at all.

_childDocuments_.review: A classic. Shame this isn't a remaster. I would definitely buy Kingdom Under Fire: Heros for around the same price. There are four campaigns which I think can take about 10 hours of play time each (I'll edit this review with the final time when all are done).Pros:          a)  Classic game, gives me a feeling of nostalgia.          b)  Very few strategy games that allow you switch between third person strategy and first person combat like this game. Also the very game that got me into strategy games to begin with.         c)  I find the story to be interesting and the character development/banter enjoyable.          d)  The musics heavy metal rifts are awesome and well timed. Cons (more like nitpicking):             a)  It hasn't aged THAT well, but it's not a complete eyesore to play.           b)  The music/audio sounds damaged occasionally. For example: Battle music, dialog, and other sounds might be going on, but the battle music sounds like it's 'clipping'. It's a pretty noticeable sound so I don't think it was ever in the classic xbox version.Final Thoughts:                        While I'm not that keen on multiplayer for Kingdom Under Fire 2, I really enjoyed the single player experience in Kingdom Under Fire: Crusaders and Kingdom Under Fire: Heros. I hope with people buying Crusaders and (hopefully) buying Kingdom Under Fire: Heros in the future, the developer Blueside will be incentivized to make another single player focused Kingdom Under Fire game (even if it's a reboot). _childDocuments_.review: Game of Thrones mixed with Berserk. Don't compare this to Dynasty Warriors because it's not, not even close. Welcome to Bersia, welcome to the third war of heroes.This game will break you, it's not easy and you will become frustrated but never unfairly so. KUF is designed to generously reward those who master its blend of RTS and RPG elements. If you think you're up for a challenge, prepare to be rewarded with one of the most thought provoking, compelling works of gaming fiction ever released. The combat is an adrenaline rush of intense action coupled with strategy that requires quick, decisive decision making and critical thinking. Behind all this is a ferocious, passionate score that pulls you right into the middle of the conflict, and you'll quickly feel immersed in just how much is at stake for the four heroes of the campaign.Play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: About 17 hours of gameplay in PC, some hundreds of gameplay in the original Xbox. This is mostly a review for those who have NEVER played KUF... I'm pretty sure if you played it before, you remember the awesomeness of the game.At release, for PC, it had some bugs but most of them that made some missions impossible to finish are gone now.IF you've never tried KUF, definitely should give it a go.The game is a mix between a tactical game and a hack and slash. But that's also what makes it so fun. Some missions can only be successful by proper management of your commander's troop while others you need to use your tactical abilities to move certain troops for it to succeed. It ain't one of those games where you can just go around mindlessly on your commander hacking and slashing enemies left to right to win every single mission.The soundtrack is amazing, 10/10The controls for computer suck unless you remap 5/10The controls with a controller connected are 100% fine which is what should be expected since this was a port to pc so I guess 10/10? _childDocuments_.review: If you've played KuF Crusaders before, this is literally just the same game but ported onto PC, there were a few crash inducing bugs at launch but those have been patched so you'll be able to enjoy the game just as it was on the Xbox HUGE.As for players who haven't played KuF Crusaders, the game is set in a pretty generic European high fantasy world and mixes some basic action gameplay with some really awkward real time strategy controls. As far as graphics go the game looks pretty ugly most of the time, the sound just straight up dies sometimes, the framerate is locked to 30 (but hey one dev said he would maybe fix this so there you go), the voice acting is all over the place and even after all these years they still haven't fixed some of the silly grammar that's going on in the tavern dialogue.Despite all of these flaws I still consider KuF a really worth while game because you just won't be able to get the experience  this game offers anywhere else, the mix of action and RTS is pretty fun, the music is extremely over the top and sell the setting as unique, the characters and their interactions are fun,the setting is gritty but knows not to take itself too seriously and some of the game's strategy related mechanics are extremely fun and do things that more popular strategy/tactics series like Total War still haven't bothered implementing like fighting with the sun at your back for an advantage on the battlefield, or burning out forests to force your enemies into fighting in the open ground.KuF Crusaders is greater than the sum of its parts, you're bound to appreciate it either as an unique experience or as a fun ride through the video game equivalent of a B List Action movie.

_childDocuments_.review: Real time strategy meets hack and slash with an RPG sauce thrown into the mix.When controlling your troops it's an RTS but, when the waves clash hard, the camera shifts and you're in full control of the main character, Dynasty Warriors style. With each victory you earn gold and experience and, when out of battle, you spend your time customizing, managing and upgrading your troops in the barracks.The game delivers an interesting story full of political intrigue and supernatural bits and, despite being a fantasy title, it has a realistic feel to the whole thing. Voice-acting is far from ridiculous, despite what some say, and the entire soundtrack is metal as ♥♥♥♥. Literally.The game offers four campaigns, each interconnected. 40+ missions that will net you, at least, 20 hours of play-time. Give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Kingdom Under Fire is a game about a kingdom. That is under fire.Its been fifty years since the Second Great War of Heroes. A village on the border of the kingdom of Hironeiden is attacked by Orcs. In response, Hironeiden  declares war on the evil nation of Vellond, where all the orcs and dark elves and vampires and other stinky idiots live. Of course, things are never that simple, and soon a plot of intrigue, betrayal, and other fun stuff unfolds. So, my Steam time for this is short, but don't worry, I play this game like, once a year. I got this game on a whim after watching Greg Kasavin's review of it back in 2004. You can watch it here:Kingdom Under Fire is a weird, but neat game, where its half commanding armies and half slapping people around with hack and slash gameplay. You have a choice of four characters, but two of them don't unlock until you've beaten the normal campaign. I recommend playing them all, since they all have stories that intertwine. Gerald is usually everyone's first campaign, a commander in the Hironeiden army, Gerald is a human warrior who can win fights by back-handing ogres in the mouth. Like, legit one of his attacks is a back hand. Lucretia is a dark elf commander in the Vellond border guards, she fights with two swords and has a more complicated move list, as well as making me bashful when I look at her.Kendal and Regnier are also there. Kendall fights with a mace as well as a warhammer so he can kill you twice as fast. In the name of god, you see. Regnier is an evil, mountain of a man who is rocking the cod piece and glistening man muscles. Also, he has a big sword and kind of tools on anyone that tris to fight him.The Human armies and the Dark Legion have similar army compositions, with a few differences. Humans rely on technology more while the Dark Legions tend to bring giant monsters and wyverns to the fight. Its kind of weird to think that this was a console exclusive sequel to a PC RTS.Controlling your armies is easy, you choose where they move and who they attack with the left analog stick or the mouse. But when fighting starts, you take control of your hero and play it like a hack and slash. You have an assortment of moves, with some characters being slightly more complicated than others, but its never anything too difficult. Each campaign goes through a handful of story missions. After each mission you collect experience and gold which you can use to upgrade your units and buy new equipment for your hero and soldiers. You take your regiments from one battle to another, and what units you can use are tied to your heroes stats.For instance, you have to increase certain stats to upgrade a unit from, lets say, infantry to heavy infantry, or heavy infantry to knights, etc.Each hero is also accompanied by two captain characters in your main unit. These two are story-characters that help you in battle as well as use special attacks in exchange for the combat points you build up in battle. These characters are unique, and are fully voiced. Ellen and Rupert are my particular favorites, but everyone stands out. Like Cirith in Lucretia's campaign. And who could forget Kendal's companions: Old man and...Boy with bowl cut. On top of upgrading your units, you can also hire mercenaries to fill out rolls you need covered. It doesn't really come into play until later campaigns, when you start deploying 3-4 units at any given time. But its a nice option if you want to bring more Calvary or infantry to particularly hard missions. There's also fairly decent unit customization, since it goes off the stats of whoever is commanding the unit. You can have a archer unit that heals, or Calvary that can cast meteor.Driveby meteor.Oh yeah, and there's magic in the game. There use to be multiplayer on Xbox live, but I guess they didn't want to bring that over. It only took them sixteen years to port this game to PC. Wow, a little quick to the draw there, huh fellas? The game runs great on PC, and its probably the definitive way to play now, but don't be mistaken, its a straight port. They even say “Press the black and white button” during tutorial messages. I didn't have any problems playing the game, but there was a glitch with mission 6 for Gerald's campaign that was patched out by the time I'm writing this review.KUF: The Crusaders is one of my favorite games of all time. I talk about it every year during my “Game of the Year” threads on my curator. I love it a lot, I first thought that it might be nostalgia, but no I still think its great.Some missions are complete ball busters, however, especially with the later Kendal missions and flat out the first mission for Regnier. Oh, and funny thing. The word “Pope” is censored. They changed the subtitle to “Patriarch” and just flat out muted the word. You can hear them say it sometimes though, since the mute wasn't 100% accurate. Its like: “The P—pe wants to speak with you.” I don't know, I always found that funny.Kingdom Under Fire: The Religious guys gets 9 funny English voice lines out of 10. Takeout coffee cups are not recyclable.

_childDocuments_.review: MandaloreGaming "I'm sure this was somebody's dream game" Me, he was talking about me. This was one of my top 5 favorite games on the original xbox, and 16 years later, out of NOWHERE, it gets ported to the PC. Blew my mind! Anyways, if you want an in-depth look at the game, I recommend checking out Mando's review of it. But I'll give my short hand thoughts on it. Why play this game? Because there is nothing else like it, including from its own franchise. The mix of RTS and hack n' slash is amazing. Great RPG elements of leveling up your units, equipment, and what units to take into each battle. Great Metal music. The story and characters are interesting, just poorly told. Also, there are a few mods like better textures, rebalance exp, and bring more units into battle that make this game better.TLDR: There are plenty of things wrong about this game, but you should play it because it's unique. And this is a controller game.

_childDocuments_.review: Suffice it to say, when I saw this game pop up in Steam's store, my heart skipped a beat as I thought this old gem would suffer the fate of digital oblivion due to being an original Xbox exclusive. Kingdom Under Fire: Crusades is one of those hidden gems you come across without really expecting them. While the cover art and theme might appear generic at first glance, the game is truly unique and has a strategic depth to its gameplay that arguably comes close to the realtime battle modes of other strategy games like the Total War series. Which is doubly surprising when you consider it's a good strategy game on console, something that is a rarity to say the least.You lead your army as its hero on a ground level, commanding from between 1 unit to 4 units + 2 support units. You can enter hack and slash mode on your main hero, enhancing their units combat effectiveness, but given the complexity of the gameplay you'll often find yourself spending half of the time or more managing your different units, archers, cavalry artillery, abilities and spells to support your main unit. Things like unit elevation, flanking, direction and even weather effects like sharp sunlight can have a decisive impact on the outcome of battles and affect the ways you approach different situations.This game has been compared to games like Dynasty Warriors, however the hero's relative strength is a lot weaker in this game, where proper army and unit management is a lot more important, forcing you to properly divide your attention between your hero and your army.There are four campaigns in total. The first two are more linear and story focused, limiting the player's options slightly. The game truly opens up in Kendal and Regnier's campaigns, allowing for far greater customization and freedom in how you choose to equip for and approach different missions. The difficulty is also racked up a lot. The focus on the story is diminished, which might not be too bad, for while the game has some fun character interactions and interesting intrigue, the overral story itself is average.The graphics are obviously old, but were very good for their time, and have aged surprisingly well. And while it has been mentioned a thousand times, the high-powered music track is a blast and perfectly matches the frantic and chaotic battles you'll invariably end up throwing yourself right in the middle of, and even has variations that fits the different races and factions, like amping up the volume and hard rock when playing as Regnier, or adding a more warped and discordant soundtrack when playing as the devious dark elves.The main downside is that this is a port, and you will expect to spend some time adjusting the keybindings to suit your preferences when you first start the game unless you have a controller. There are also some issues with minimizing the game window during play on Windows 10, making alt-tabbing difficult in my own experience.Overral, I would really recommend that you give this game a shot. If only for the fact it's one of the few genuinely good console strategy games out there.

_childDocuments_.review: Never thought I'd see KuF Crusaders playable on PC, one of my all time favourite games, I even kept my OG Xbox and 360 exclusively for Crusaders and Heroes, they can finally rest now that Blueside finally brought it to PC.I was overjoyed with the first announcement and trailer of KuF 2 but my heart sunk when I learned it would be an MMO and was especially disappointed after playing it and witnessing how bland it is, I really wish they had expanded this fantastic mix of RTS/Action RPG and just rolled out more campaigns like these. I have alot of nostalgia for this game and Heroes but the HD treatment is exactly what this game needs, it's still amazing after all these years, how no one else picked up on this genre is beyond me. Awesome real time fantasy battles leading armies of Humans, Elves, Dark Elves and Orcs, Mercenary bands, with tons of diverse troop types and roles to play, Good replayability but it lacks a custom battle mode like Heroes had, having custom battles would add so much to an already epic game. Something as simple as dialogue and storyline makes me love these characters, the voice acting is by no means the best but still leagues better than KUF2's cheap mmo speech boxes, which only add to a feeling of emptiness. These campaigns are so damn good that I've lost count on how many times I've played them, the troops customization, diversity of units, officers and companions add so much replayability.The soundtrack is legendary, "Metal heavier than any knight’s plate!" indeed, each song fits the scene and battle like a glove and I can stop listening to it, makes smashing your horde of Orcs against an enemy line so unique. Controls on keyboard aren't great, but that was to be expected for such an old game built for a console, playing with a 360 controller is pretty smooth though. It is absolutely worth it picking this up, the graphics are obviously old but the models still hold fantasticly well for their time but of course most RTS fans are fine with worse graphics if the gameplay makes up for it, and boy does blows this blow the scale.Let's hope Blueside gives us Heroes too!

Yet, if you enjoyed Heroes, you'll enjoy this for sure.If you've never played either of these games, let me sum it up. It's an action strategy game. So if you want to feel awesome while slashing through waves of enemies, and having to control an army at your back, then this game is gonna scratch that itch.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a faithful port of the original Xbox game, no mess or fuss or extra features and entirely bug-free on my playthrough. It is missing the two mini-games you can unlock in the original but everything else is exactly the same. For someone like me who was looking to relive the awesome experience I had as a child, it was everything I wanted.If you are new to the game or the series, know that the graphics have not aged particularly well and it was entirely designed to be played on a gamepad rather than keyboard and mouse. But if you can look past those things then you will find a true gem. It's so incredibly rare to find a game that blends RTS and RPG like the KUF series does, and it does it very well.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, this game is ported to PC. Throughout the years I would occasionally get out the XBox and play through this and Heroes. Never got boring for me, though I did miss multiplayer a lot. Now that we've got it on PC, I was psyched! It's still at 30 fps but I don't really see that as a problem, especially because the logic behind the game is tied to the frames. The 4k and the fact that we're on PC now makes the game run great and there are no hiccups like the original. I'm a bit sad that there's no multiplayer support, but I'm hoping that this game doing well will prompt them to either update this with more PC centric updates or release Heroes with multiplayer and other QoL improvements as well. Honestly KuF 2 was a downgrade for me and I am hoping for a real KuF game soon. Here's hoping this kindles the fire!Highly recommend, you get a lot for 20 dollars here, and there's a good chance Heroes will also be ported if this does well enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Its really janky, ugly, with poor controls, and often feels like a game being played in a garbage emulator. There's no AA. Its locked at 30 FPS. Things like tree leaves, fur, and other 2D assets on 3D models have white outlines around it. The sound effects, namely the marching sounds stacks, leading to an horrrrrid peaking of audio. The officer unique heal assist causes crashes. Its a technical mess.However, its an O.G. Xbox title trying to do something different on a low budget. You'll often times be pulled in by the banter of characters, the (short looped) energetic metal music, and the surprising depth in the forming and running of your army in battle. Despite some regarding it as a dynasty warriors-like game, that is quite surface level. You need to manage where and what your units are doing. Its more akin to a Total War game in that regard. Even then you have to manage a limited shared pool of EXP and Gold across all your units. Its an RTS/RPG before being a hack-n-slash.There's really nothing quite like it. Now I'm waiting for the sequel to arrive on PC. Hopefully with better porting polish.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that no matter what annoys you about it you'll be back for more. Great story, great build up, great climax, great art, great characters, great writing, great mechanics, great balance, great detail and just a great time. 4 campaigns: Easy, Medium, Hard and Very Hard and they are all unique yet similar, must complete the first campaign to unlock second so on so fourth, first campaign is basically a tutorial but you don't realise until you get to the last campaign and even then first campaign is still worth replaying again.This game had me philosophizing about race and righteousness as a child quite a lot, You play as either a human captain, a dark elf commander, human general and a demon lord and it's actually the demon lord who has the most humanity out of them all. Whilst the human captain (Gerald) two officers are both either logical or illogical they are both commanded through authority and a constantly reminded sense of hierarchy. The Dark Elf commander (Lucretia) two officers are all constantly fighting with each other and demonstrate absolutely no trust.The human general (Kendal) two officers are either a completely religious fanatic child or a completely free thinking gold seeking mercenary.The demon lord (Regnier) two officers are both completely loyal through respect.Really interesting dynamics with the characters.The only complaint I have about the games balance is that the Regnier campaign should have been called "very Hard" but instead it's called "Hard".

_childDocuments_.review: Dont Buy, It's Broken:There are 4 main Campaigns; Geralds, Lucretcia, Kendall, and Reigner. You have to beat Lucretcia's campaign to unlock Kendalls and Reigners. I beat Lucretcia's campaign, and then stopped playing for the day. The next day, I tried to play Kendals campaign, and the game said "you have to beat Lucretcia's campaign. Confused, i reloaded my last save of Lucretcia's, beat it again, and then went right into a New Game and started Kendals Campaign. _childDocuments_.review: I was a fan of this series over 15 years ago and I'm still a fan of it now with this PC release. It's pretty much just a direct port for PC so if you're planning on playing this game with mouse and keyboard the controls will probably feel even more wonky than it already does on controller. But other than the outdated controls and RTS gameplay for console, this game has always had a certain charm to it. Sophisticated mechanics like receiving a damage penalty for archers when they shoot at enemies in the direction of sunlight and setting a spot on fire making enemies retreat from that location. Overall the gameplay is a RTS during battles with hack and slash action controlling your hero's troop similar to the Dynasty Warriors series. It has a linear story and mild RPG elements with upgrading your troops outside of battles, with the troops also having a job system similar to Final Fantasy Tactics but not nearly as in depth. There's also a fair bit of content in the game with 4 campaigns to choose from, with 2 out of the 4 needing to be unlocked by first completing Lucretia's story. I gladly dropped the $20 for my love of the game to go through another playthrough and with the amount of content in this game I'd say $20 is a fair price. If I remember correctly there's probably around 20 hours of gameplay and looking at  that looks to be correct.I truly believe this is a great series and would love to have Kingdom Under Fire: Heroes ported to PC as well since it's not backwards compatible with the Xbox 360 like Crusaders was. However disregard Kingdom Under Fire 2 and Kingdom Under Fire: Circle of Doom because both of those games are dumpster fires that should have been apart of this series, but that's for another time and for a different review.

_childDocuments_.review: Both the tactical gameplay and hack and slash gameplay elements are well-executed and significant. Unit maneuvering is important and tactical use of spells determines victory or defeat. The hack and slash gameplay involves a decent amount of unique combos and movesets for each character.Furthermore, the unit customization and upgrading has some surprising depth and variety to it for a real-time tactics game. It has a RPG-like feel to it and is rewarding and addictive.The story and dialogues are not anything deep or complex, but still very enjoyable. From the two campaigns (out of four) I've been playing through so far, each has a very different feel and cast of characters. The stories involve a good amount of intrigue and character conflict that's simple but effective and believable.The character and unit designs and in-game character artwork are top-notch.The voice acting ranges from good to great for the main characters, but unit voice acting is quite poor overall.The PC port is locked to 30 FPS but it's well-optimized and uses minimal resources. The KB+M controls make it obvious that it's a console original game, but they nonetheless work well, though the camera control is flawed.

_childDocuments_.review: An aged but still functional niche game once found in Xbox, The Crusaders gameplay has balancing notes found with being the first of the series: Two major factions have strengths in different fields and require familiarizing both to understand appropriate equipment, skill, and class counters. Humans, Dark Elves, Orcs, monsters, fliers, and siege equipment.Deploying group classes appear fine until facing increasingly difficult odds where the enemy forces are larger and carrying more powerful backline support. Only the leader allows direct control in combat, which is a challenge when micromanaging groups to avoid unintentional engagements.As what was noted being originally an Xbox, a controller offers a better experience, though mouse and keyboard commands have a hotkey for key map reference to acclimate.The Crusaders is recommended for those who have a score to settle from the olden days of Xbox like I have, want to understand the game's mechanics first before playing Kingdom Under Fire Heroes, or want something that is an experiment between mechanics familiar with Dynasty Warriors (in the first Xbox generation) and Total War, in a fantasy setting that has some familiarity to examples like Warhammer.
