_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely awesome game. I definitely recommend you pick this up. It's fully worth the $20. Yes, it runs at 30 FPS, but it runs well and stays consistent. I bet there's some animations or something time related that bugs horribly at 60 FPS due to the games's design that made them decide to lock it at 30 FPS, so it's no worry to me. The combat is simple but that's good for a musou-like game. Also, battles feels much more like a real battle unlike dynasty warriors because everyone on the field is constantly contributing to the fight, which I'm guessing happens because the troops to not have individual health, but instead your units health is tied to YOUR health, which is actually a really great idea. The writing and story is great too, and the voice acting is actually pretty decent to. And the graphics are nice for a xbox era game. I can't tell you how awesome I felt the first time I ordered my archers to shoot flaming arrows into a forest that enemy troops were coming through, just to light the forest (and the enemy) on fire!P.S: When I say "musou-like game" I don't mean this game is truly musou style. There are actually quite a bit of differences from this game and musou games, it's just in a VERY similar style.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: I had been waiting for this game a long ago, and its awesome. Great mechanics and music. Also you need a bit of strategy to beat any mission, is not too hard compare to KUF: Heroes, but is a really good game. Also, have in mind that is a port not a remaster or remake, some texture have been improve but don't spect too much of visual. But the great mechanis that it posses makes it a really enjoyable game
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: I remember playing this game and it's sequel as a teenager, on the original XBox, and being continually aggravated that it never made the backwards compatibility lists on the 360. Revisiting Crusaders, finally ported to modern devices... oh god is it cringy. The metal theme is silly and over the top in the not great sort of way, the dialog is poor, and the voice delivery is *so much worse*. And yet, in the 15+ years since, I don't think I have ever seen anything that hit the same appealing gameplay formula quite like it. Real-time tactics from within the chaotic thick of things is just so delicious, and it's worth risking rolling my eyes out of their sockets to get a taste of it.There's a number of things that could stand to be modernized, sure, but I think the only one that's truly egregious to modern eyes, for me at least, is a lack of in-mission checkpoints. Some of them can run quite long, with some kind of irritating bonus failure conditions that can be rather finicky; it's a bit more annoying to have to redo the first half hour of rote easy stuff now that I'm older and have more limited playtime. Still, if you think you have the patience for that, this title remains a gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing classic RTS/Hack and Slash from 2004, with gameplay and graphics way ahead of its time. The unique part about this game is that you actually get to fight in the battles with your soldiers as the Heroes- Gerald- Kendal- Lucretia- RegnierYou command three different Races, Humans, Dark Elves and Orcs in 4 different campaigns, Gerald and Kendal are the human campaigns, Lucretia and Regnier and the Dark Elf and Orc Campaigns. Ive finished Geralds and gotten almost all the way through Lucretias Campaign in about 12 hours of play time so the game definitely has a decent money to gameplay ratio.looks great on my 1440p monitor and havent had any crashes or performance issues at all.Great game to replay and feel nostalgic or pick up and try out if you want to play something on the couch or in bed with a controller
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: (True Story) For several years, after loosing my original xbox with my physical copies of Kingdom Under Fire The Crusaders, Heroes and circle of doom, I've been literally dreaming about playing this game again, just to wake up, and realize that I still no longer have the games... so this is really a dream come true. (THANKS PORTABILITY TEAM)This game was really ahead of it's time, with it's game mechanics, the intense strategy/action oriented gameplay, the lore, God I  can't express how much I love this game.I just hope someday, somehow, we get to play Kingdom under fire heroes on steam, I really don't care about multiplayer (which would be nice to have though) but really, i'd give anything to play that campaing again, to have the custom battle game mode for replayablility again, pls guys make it happen, I´ll buy it the very instant it goes up on the store. (Sorry for my bad english, I just wanted to express my gratitude to the portability team and my love for this game)
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: I really miss games having good story.  I paid full price to get this one as it does have a very good story.  But it is old and was originaly made for the first xbox.  Ports often have problems, but the guys behind this have been working hard to fix the bugs.  So far very frequent bugfixes are released.  I hope you enjoy it as much as I had in the past and now will again.  Game play was meant to be played with a controler and I think you should do it that way.  You will play as a general leading troops, devising on the go strategies to take the battlefield.  As a general you wont just be watching, but will also jump in with a sword and duke it out.  If you can kill an enemy bands leader they will be knocked out, meaning your sword fighting can be a major plus to your side.  Of course you don't have to play for the good guys, try being a general for the dark elves.  The elves are easy on the eyes after all.I never understood why they censored the word Patriarch, but it was like that back on xbox and still in this version.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: SO I have reserved my Review only because I wanted to complete everything and dear god is it worth it. The game is almost exactly the same. Obviously there is gonna  be some serious porting issues from xbox to pc especially on older exclusive games. However this is the early 2ks best out of nowhere game. None of the early "we are changing the game" games came even close. When this game came out the crits panned the ♥♥♥♥ outta of it for its "Lack luster" Tutorial and its difficulty spikes...once more However that is what makes this game so amazing. It dares you to come and try to master both the RTS aspect, the RPG aspect, AND the hack and slack Aspect. Each Character is unique and beyond amazing with compelling reasons why they are doing what they are doing. The story, the mythos, the set up at the end is amazing. I want a PROPER sequel to the Heroes.The game does suffer from awful early 2k dialogue and actually paying attention to whats being said even in the tutorials. if you don't the game will punish you and its a hard lesson to learn. I will always come back to play this game it was my childhood and is still an amazing game.To the bad port people I will simply state the game is finally being seen and able to play without paying major money and having a old school xbox be happy we still have it. I thought this game was lost to time and I was seriously the only one who remember it.If you are considering buying it do. The hours apon hours you will spend returning wondering if you can save certain units or if this mix up of powers on that unit will work better. You owe it to yourself if you have never played this serious gem to buy it. I don't like pushing people to buy but we need a proper sequel and for those who know CIRCLE DOESNT COUNT!!!Just saying.Do it for yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: I remember playing this game WAY back in my teenage years (I was maybe 11). This game was absolutely mind blowing for me. I've always loved medieval/fantasy style settings and have always been more keen on those types of games. I had never truly messed with RTS, but this game is definitely in one of my top five games of all time. (It also inspired me to write some fantasy work of my own!)Very fun and a bit challenging on your first ever playthrough through all of the campaigns. My only gripe with the game is the voice acting for most of the characters is God awful. That said, I still absolutely love this game. And I want Heroes and Circle of Doom ported to Steam as well! This entire franchise never got enough credit for how awesome it was (although CoD was a bit of a let down, still want to see it back again). Would very much recommend to everyone!
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: Played this game back when it was on OG Xbox, completed all campaigns. Loved everything about it, especially the soundtrack. If there was one game I would recommend to all friends/family/people, it would be this one. Very unique mix of ARPG, RTS, and hack'n'slash. Sure, graphics are a bit dated since the game is going on 20 years old (Came out in 2004*) but as far as I recall everything is voice acted despite the majority of text actually showing up on-screen. Strongly recommend using a controller/gamepad to play though since the M+KB controls are a bit wonky.My only gripes about the game are as follows:-Volume levels seem to be imbalanced (SFX tend to wash out dialogue)-Volume of the game is generally high (I turned everything down next to off and still had to reduce the game volume in the Sound Mixer to around 15-20%)-Game doesn't stay paused when alt-tabbing (Acts wonky with alt-tab in general, probably due to the M+KB controls being on even when using a gamepad)-Game crashes when stopping a screen share through Discord (Not sure if it happens when streaming to Twitch or something else.)Main tip for playing: Save often
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: Cult Classic for sure! This game is exactly as good as I remember it being. A solid 8/10. The story and gameplay are both pretty good. The combat and strategies are generally engaging and challenging-- It does have a few difficulty spikes and a bad mission or two spread over the 4 campaigns but well worth the 50 hours I put in. Immediately adding it to my iteration of that list of games we all have that we keep coming back to again and again instead of playing those 12 games we got on sale in 2017.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: A blast from the past that I didn't realise how much I wanted.Big part of my love probably comes from nostalgia, but it's also a pleasant blend of hack and slash combat, with real time strategy. Getting to build up custom units with gear and leaders is a ton of fun.The story is not terribly deep or engaging, with a heavy focus on fairly standard characters that are done well. It's a unique experience that feels like a labour of love.The soundtrack is 18 flavours of guitar wankery. Some of it is great, others not, might not be for everyone.I love it, was so giddy to see it getting a PC release, overjoyed that it's a reasonable price, look forward to getting the new game once I have the hardware to run it.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: A gem from the past and a decent port to pc. Great gameplay, varied missions, many hours of game content (spread across 4 campaigns). Satisfying progression through upgrade / rpg mechanics (you can upgrade / customize your troops and your hero).The only nuisance is that it takes some time to get used to the controls (hint: press the tilde key / button below escape to view controls regularly and memorize them).
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: I'm glad you could configure the keybindings on the mouse and keyboard because the default setting were pretty terrible in my opinion, but that said, i played this game back on the original xbox so i just used an xbox 360 controller and it worked like a charm. FINALLY i could open the mini-map in game and not have the game crash on me. I had to complete all 4 campaigns without using the mini-map on the original xbox and let me say it was a bloody challenge haha. So far just completed Gerald's campaign but so far the game is brilliant. A few issues tho:-Some of the voice acting cuts off or plays too late/early-Sound effect when a huge amount of troops moving sounds like its just static-When you have a fire aspect weapon on your hero some of the sound effects when the fire triggers sounds like a chair squeaking.But other than those issues its a solid port, a great one at that, and with the added save slots (original was 15, but now its like 100) you can save every single mission if you desire.I rate a solid 9/10, 10/10 if those issues were fixed : )IT GUD MUST BUY
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: Classic game, remember playing as a kid on my original Xbox, still so much fun, brings back all the memories. Remember it mainly because of the amazing gameplay style that I've never had before in any other game. You command your troops from a third person view, then when you go into combat fighting against another horde of troops, you control your hero slashing through the enemy.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: The port works. If you've played this before that's really all you need to know. If you haven't played it before then the game itself is not only excellent but almost completely unique. It is an incredibly challenging game, however, and the English voice work can be quite awful for some of the characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: Okay.... where can I start.... I started playing this when I was around 8 or 9 years old. This game is still a blast from the past and definitely in my top 3 favorite RTS/Slash games. Runs very smooth and So far no bugs. I am very happy they brought it back and I will gladly play this again and again. Hopefully in the future they make games like this again and at the very least ass Kingdom under fire Heroes and Multiplayer on here! 10/10 worth the $20.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: Some part of me knew this gem would find its way here someday. One of those titles i wish i could unlearn and replay fresh. An RTS player's dream. Great replay value but the real business is multiplayer which unfortunately isn't available here. Not sure if there are plans but would gladly pay a little extra for the feature's return. Still a great buy. 22 hours in I've completed all 4 campaigns but that doesn't mean i cant restart and try different troop combos ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent port of an excellent Xbox game. The graphics might look dated, but the unique gameplay stands the test of time. The perfect blend of strategy and action, wrapped up in an interesting story with great characters. Don't miss this one.Please bring Heroes to PC next! EDIT: Heroes is coming to Steam! So excited!
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: It is a great game. Since I played Kessen 2 and 3, I never had the opportunity to see a game that satisfies what they embodied. Tactical RTS battles with hack and slash and cinematic story with interesting characters whose relations develop in the course of the narrative, I particularly liked the rivalries between the elven commander and her overseer. The characters are well developed (though I maybe the only one in this gaming world that misses Kessen 1 and 2 for not allowing you to interfere with the development of your officers' skills) The story is captivating here, the special abilities spectacular and I really love the characters. They are very complex and they can be unpredictable (not totally subject to choice matters arithmetic systems. A gem from the happy old days.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: I've have never seen anything like this game before, this was true when it came out on the original X-Box and it still is. A hybrid of RTS/RPG and third-person hack'n slash, it really is unlike anything I've ever played. The controls take some getting used to, but it's nothing too complicated and in this version you can use the mouse and keyboard to bypass some limitations of the controller. It's a challenging game, one I've never managed to finish unfortunately, mostly due too my own lack of skill at strategy games, but it's a good game, one I think more people should play.P.S.: If you're unsure because you played Kingdom Under Fire 2, don't be, that game has little to do with this one. KUF 2 is an MMO with some elements of previous KUF games in it. Don't be fooled, Kingdom Under Fire: Crusaders is the real sh*t.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished all four campaigns of my childhood favourite game. What a blast from the past there isn't anything quite like this game, (apart from Dynasty warriors). The story is great something about it feels so retro, atmosphere and the music are god tier. Some sound effect from this game are perfect some seem phoned in you can hear it here and there. The overall polish of each mission feels so hand crafted in the first two campaign. Regnier campaign feels like its just "Hulk Smash" but its still fun. The game overall is an experience of some of the best the original Xbox had to offer in terms of ground breaking gameplay which its all about. I still can't believe how fast you need to make decisions in this game its nuts and makes it so gripping.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorites of all time, finally released on steam. Its the same game we all know and love, no remaster just a port (including the bugs, completely forgot how they seemingly censored "Patriarch" to just "The Puh"). Multiplayer is absent at the time of this review, but lets be real it was a bit of a ♥♥♥♥ show anyway. Here's to hoping this means Heroes isn't too far behind!
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: This game is has aged stupidly well. It's just as fun (if not more so) than when it was released on the original Xbox way back in 2004. The controls make a lot of sense and handle really nicely (at least using a controller).Be warned though, there is no replay function. You beat a level and that's the only time you'll get to play it. So how you spend your gold and how you allocate the exp earned to which characters at base is as important if not more than the decisions you make on the field in determining your success.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: Never played any of the previous games (except the KUF2 free trial, which wasn't good) until now so I don't have nostalgia going into this PC release and I can still say that the game totally holds up despite being 16 years old. Controls are a bit clunky bit I can look past that given the game's age.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: KUF: The Crusaders and KUF: Heroes are easily two of my favorite games of all time. Unfortunately there hasn't been a good way to play them anymore without having an OG Fat Xbox, which are getting increasingly tough to get your hands these days.Essentially combine the hack and slash action of the Dynasty Warriors series, mesh it with the battles of the Total War series, add in the unit development tree/skills for added RPG-lite depth, throw in a slamming metal sound track and you have one powerhouse of a game.The hack and slash action feels a bit stiffer than modern games but I'd say for a 16 year old game, it aged pretty nicely.My largest gripe is that Blueside didn't include the old PvP mode, which had me spending TONS of hours on the game around original release.I strongly recommend checking Kingdom Under Fire: Crusaders out!Hopefully it'll get enough support that Blueside either patches the multiplayer in, or better yet, port KUF: Heroes in the same fashion and include the online play.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: A true blast from the past, while nostalgia is carrying this game for me sofar,  it still is a great game, the graphics are a bit dated, and the controls are REALLY dated. However taking into account that this is an original xbox title, the game is very much worth it. Though it is pretty niche for 20$
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: This has stood for over 15 years as, in my personal opinion, the best 'RTS' game ever released on console. You really need to play this game with a controller if you're to really enjoy it. The graphics won't blow you out of the water, but they haven't aged too terribly either. The soundtrack isn't huge, but is a work of genius nonetheless, who would have thought before this game that "Medieval Fantasy Warfare" and "Heavy Metal" would mix so well.This release has done very little to change or improve on the original 2004 game besides add widescreen and sharpen up the visuals a little. I wouldn't have asked for much more than that considering it took Blueside over 15 years to do even that much. Multiplayer is unfortunately non-functioning at the moment, but then again, I didn't keep the original Xbox and Kingdom Under Fire disc's in my library so I could play the multiplayer. The story and gameplay are good enough themselves to warrant a return for me. Maybe you will feel the same way.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: Good working port. They just released a patch to fix some crashes but I've yet to crash a single time playing so far. Partially through Lucretia's campaign currently. My nostalgia for this game was strong, and 12 year old me remembers an epic story with so many unit choices it boggled the mind. 21 year old me is pleasantly surprised at how well this game holds up and how much more depth goes into it than I remembered from my childhood. Well worth it, a real shame we haven't seen any similar games since.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: So at 16 hours in I have beat the two easy Campaigns and Kendall's hard Campaign. I love every second of it, like back when I was a kid. Still just as good.It is a cool mix of dynasty warriors hack and slash but real time troop movement is super important like total war. Linear campaign so you cant grind up EXP and money,I would love some PVP which I never got to do as a kid, but that is sadly not an option.The first two campaigns are absolutely necassary to get used to the controls and units, but they do get boring and are not particularly challenging once you get into the swing of it. You will be absolutely thankful for the practice before you get into the absolutely vicious Hard Campaigns. the two races are different enough to both have their own challenges, and you will need to vary strategy. you cant just have an unbeatable army comp that walks through a campaign.the controls are probably the worst part of the game (mouse and keyboard) and it tooks some serious time to get comfortable. (" ` " key is your friend and cheat sheet until you get used to it) also knowing that you can use shift to que up your movements is especially useful with cavalry.I did also have a problem with crashing on Lucrecia's last level of the campaign, so I just went counter clockwise around the map instead of clockwise.seriously. great game, I was glad to see it come back as I was literally looking for an emlator for this game a month and a half ago. I was willing to pay for a working copy.soundtrack is great!Geralds constant chewing is stupid, but for a 16 year old game, I will get over it.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: Great game that can really make you clench sometimes when it looks grim but if you stay cool, its all gravy. Game has four campaigns that all take place at the same time and explains different points of view from the different factions. You unlock the two last campaigns by beating lucretias campaign (which has its own set of challenges) which gives you two badasses to play with and almost always large scale battles. The battles are incredibly satisfying and the game is just plain fun. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: I had this game back on the original Xbox, and I've easily completed it about 4-5 times, not to mention the countless hours replaying the demo on the disk i got, setting silly challenges for myself, like highest kill count, no survivors and no losses.I can easily recommend the game because its a staple game in my childhood, like Battlefront 2, Halo CE and KOTOR 1 and 2. Some people may not like it, but i enjoyed the levelling up of skills and units, the way you can customize your armies (Albeit its only weapons and armour for most) and the way you can strategize, whether its micromanaging a Cavalry charge or sending 3 infantry squads in at a time.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite games as a kid has finally made it to steam, and I was thrilled to jump back into it. Sure, there are a few bugs here and there that need to be worked out, but the game play is still rock solid, and the soundtrack is as awesomely heavy as I remember. 10/10 would absolutely recommend this blast from the past.Now please for the love of the Ecclesian Patriarch add Heroes.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game back in the day for X-box and was delighted to see it ported over to Steam. The RTS elements are still there and while it feels a bit odd to hack and slash with a mouse rather that the satisfaction of a controller the game is still so much fun. There is something So special about calling down a meteor storm on an lvl 25 Heavy Infantry enemy before you send  your own Infantry against them. Using your Calvary to rack up SP and then having your archers pick off any survivors. I've missed this Game and am SO glad its on Steam.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: What a blast from my past as soon as i saw this it was sold. Its old and a little klunky but still plays as well as it back in its hay day. I loved this game and being able to play lucretia again was mucho es bueno. Starts up smoothly, combat is fun, story line is good. its a great nostalgia trip hope it gets a revamp in time. Glad I bought this gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: I came across this by chance. I have been hoping for a port to PC ever since I touched this game 16 years ago on my friends XBOX. In the past, I have even considered buying an old console just for this game.I am halfway through Gerald's campaign and so far it has been an identical experience to the original game, except for the higher res graphics. Very Smooth, no crashes. The game is maxed at 30 fps.Thank you so much for bringing this back.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: I've been dying to play this game for YEARS.Now that I have it, I love it even more than before. If you love RTS games and you want to know one of the very best ever, then you better buy this underrated gem! The characters are great, the story is very interesting, the gameplay is complex, and the difficulty can be very demanding, especially if you get greedy or overconfident. Overall, it's a challenging, but incredibly satisfactory experience that will challenge the most strategic minds. Finally, if this game is the equivalent of Leonardo DaVinci's "Last Supper", its sequel, KINGDOM UNDER FIRE: HEROES, is the "Monalisa".I truly hope they release for PC too.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite games as a kid, and except for the terrible voice acting, it still holds up. Despite it being such an old game  the battles remain impressive, chaotic spectacles, and the strategy layer has a suitable amount of depth. Overall its an experience I haven't really had in any other game since its release, and its nice to be able to scratch that itch again.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: Great game at a great price.I initially bought this title when it was first released for the original Xbox. I loved it then, I love it now. It's a fantastic RST/Hack and slash mix.It's a worth a try if you can get over the dated graphics, though this PC port has improved things, and made it a lot more accessible for years to come.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just such a masterpiece to me. The sound track is awesome and the RTS gameplay is really addicting. Upgrading and equipping troops, and also the job system, allows for a lot of creativity in builds - so it has a really high replay value too. Definitely worth it for the price tag, a must have in any RTS lovers collection.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ does this bring back memories.I played this game with my cousin on the original xbox back in 2005-06. I never beat it nor even came close to beating it. Since for a young kid this game was just to tough. Now however, that I am an adult this game should be a breeze.I was wrong. This game kicks you  in the balls until you love it. Even with the easier of the two starting characters (Geralt) the game ramps up the punches around level 4. This game holds your hand rather well while teaching you the basics of the game, and showing more advance moves slowly but surely.Now the story of the game (at least on the surface) is the typical good vs evil trope. However, with the voice acting and the written dialogue it's well executed and feels fairly believable. I have a strong liking for each of the main playable and the officers that accompany them. They all play off of each other, and it never feels forced.The music just kicks ass. The soundtrack to this game is off the charts.So with great combat, great story, and great music what's wrong with it then? Well this came out in 2004 and it shows. The very first opening screen shows this. The textures are terrible. The models themselves look good, other than the faces. If you can get past that, it starts to look alright. Nothing great, but you can see where the overall art style of the game shines.My last complaint is while the hack'n'slash combat is great, the RTS controls feel terrible at times. I do use a gamepad as the game was designed for one, but sometimes trying to move troops a few more feet away, or closer is like wrestling a f*cking ogre! It's also hard because there is no top down view. Now there is a minimap that allows you to be more prieces but even with the mini map, it only helps so much.If you want a great story, some good fun hack'n'slash style combat. Don't mind wrestling with the camera or looking at ugly textures, then I highly recommend this game! For only $20 isn't to bad. If you are really hesitant at least wait for it to go on sale, but it's a fantastic game overall and a damn good port of the original game!
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: You know how you see a game that makes you fill with nostalgia, but then when you buy and start playing that classic gem and realize that the game play does not hold up to todays standards?Guess what? This is not one of those games!Originally released in 2004 for the original Xbox (man, i feel old) Kingdom under fire: The Crusaders was the first installment of the franchise. I will admit that the graphics are rough, but they are serviceable and I had no issues playing through this game. It holds up really well and I think is well worth the price for a decent port of a great game!
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: I was positively surprised how good they managed to make the game look. Gonna be a blast playing through all the campaigns again. Blueside please remaster KUF: Heroes aswell. And while you're at it, make these games moddable and you will find out they will take a life of their own. The community can develop this series in to an even better masterpiece than it already is. The gameplay is 10/10, you just need to give us the tools to expand on the experience. (If it's even possible to mod such an old game?)
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders

_childDocuments_.review: I'm usually not that big into RTS but this Game does it so well, combining RTS Elements with Hack and Slash and RPG.It's a very unique title even to this day.I remember randomly picking up this one and KuF:Heroes some time after they released, not knowing what I was getting myself into.Me and a friend then spent weeks on end playing these games.The graphics are obviously dated for a game released in 2004. Back then the graphics were really nice though.The controls require some time to get used to, it can feel a little bit clunky at times, but when you've figured it out it feels really nice.I also strongly recommend using a controller to play this.The game is sporting a Metal soundtrack during the battles and it is really fitting. I'm a fan of metal and so I really love the soundtrack in this game. It's proper heavy, although it can become repetitive when playing long sessions.I bought this steam version for 20€ at the release date and I still feel it's fully worth it, considering that besides using an emulator there is no other way to get this kind of gameplay on PC.Definite pick up if it ever goes on sale.Now I really do hope they will also release KuF:Heroes eventually.

_childDocuments_.review: I believe with the current playtime I have the right to say some things regarding the game-state.It is fully playable, but really iffy. Controlling with an Keyboard is pain and not every Controller is accepted and requires an 3rd party software to circumvent. There are some start-up issues for some players, which I personally haven't encountered. Those people often times also have the problem that the game wont save your progress after you finish an Campaign, although there are some simple fixes for the latter. There are some small scripting problems, like the black boxes that appear during a cutscene not loading in correctly as they should be. Some players also have reported some stuff like "Immortal Enemies", but that one is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and not really true. Overall you won't experience anything game-breaking and it's on a very similar level to the XBOX version.A huge difference to the XBOX version is that most files can be loaded in loosely now. This makes not only graphic mods an possibility, but also some other good stuff. You can consider this as an indirect modding support, with an basic coding structure provided by one Developer. However apart from some file structure, the community was left on it's own accord to figure stuff out. Speaking of mods, there are some available on the Steam Guide section and Nexusmods.To sum it up, this version is pretty close to the XBOX version. The only new thing it has is the widescreen support and loose file support, other than that this port is pretty much a cash grab and is now abandonware. Still, it is much better than the broken Heroes port and fully playable at least. Since it's pretty close to the XBOX version, stuff like 60fps, newer file formats and other stuff is not available and wont be from Blueside.People that are here for the nostalgia wont be that much disappointed, albeit there is no Multiplayer available. People that never played it before should look at an let's play video before buying. In both cases I recommend buying this at an discount, as this port is not worth the full price for what it is.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine you're a military hero in the Middle Ages, gallantly striking down the enemy and commanding friendly forces. Set 50 years after the events of Kingdom Under Fire, The Crusaders lets you lead hundreds of troops into war, while managing resources, augmenting your forces, and developing your combat strategies. You can choose to play as one of two races, Humans or Dark Legions, and you can select one of several character types within each race. While moving across the continent, you can stop by castles, gain endorsements from feudal lords, hire mercenaries, replenish or change equipment, and more.

name: Astria Ascending
detailed_description: More from us About the Game Explore the vast and beautiful world of Orcanon Visit five different cities populated by unique creatures and solve more than 20 dangerous dungeons. With over 50 hours of game-play and a range of fun mini-games - including shoot ‘em ups, an original fantasy-themed card game and challenging environmental puzzles. A grand tale of fate and sacrifice Immerse yourself in a fascinating narrative rife with betrayal, sacrifice and terrors. A story based around adult characters, Astria Ascending offers a more mature experience and extensive dialog. A rewarding turn-based combat system Fight over 200 different monsters in captivating, turn-based combat. Collect and summon legendary beasts into the fight and build up your power to wield legendary Cosmo Breaks. Meet an unforgettable cast of characters Pick from eight customizable characters spanning a range of fantastical races and skills, and assemble a heroic team that must sacrifice everything to save the world. With 20 classes to choose from and an array of unique skills to command, their fates are doomed, but the world is not. A hand-drawn adventure crafted with skill and passion From a team featuring developers from Final Fantasy, Nier Automata and Bravely Default, Astria Ascending includes full voice acting in Japanese and English, a traditionally animated, fully hand-drawn 2D world and a dynamic weather system.

_childDocuments_.review: In summary: I really don't understand the negative reviews of this game.The game is really interesting, and quite different from the vast majority of recent j-RPGs, and maybe that's the problem. They evaluate the game for what it is NOT intended to be.The game's story is simple, it's not a cliché, the plots are "reasons", but it provides an interesting adventure and far from being boring, the game basically sets up a scenario where the story will unfold sufficiently.Combat is probably the most interesting part of the game. Allows you to customize your characters by giving a "I made it" feel as you progress in building each of them. Mages, warriors, support, healer, all have their uses.Yes, the game doesn't have great quality of life features, and I think that's intentional. You don't have access to ALL of an enemy's vulnerabilities right away, you need to memorize or recognize every new enemy you encounter. You need to equip your characters item by item, but each has unique artwork and it feels like each piece of equipment has been thought through. After playing the beginning of the game (I have just over 8 hours, I think), the feeling I have is of a game that was made with the intention of being beautiful AND challenging.Yes, common enemies can destroy you if you are careless. Bosses are going to be troublesome. You will need to plan your characters and party in order to enter combat. If it's difficult, you'll need to stop and farm a little. But the game? He's fun and cute, could it be better done? Could, but little.Yes, the game could have better customization of video settings (for me it's great, but it's my monitor that conveniently fits the game's resolution), or it could have better mouse and keyboard support, but they patched it on day 1 and if this is really a nuisance, refund the game, but the game itself will fulfill its purpose.Ps.: The game has many sidequests. And thats a good thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Astria Ascending

_childDocuments_.review: Where oh where to begin....This game has a ton of potential, however there are many game design choices that leave you with a time sink that is not very fulfilling.Let's start with the good:Different class variations to play with.Combat rewards you when you match weaknesses.Exploratory gameplay becomes quite fun in late-game dungeons. Jumping around and solving a few puzzles is fun!The token minigame is a nice side game (until it forces you to 100% random your tokens vs a max difficulty opponent)You can save ANYWHERE! (This is important to tolerate many of the cons)Now the downsides:It feels like a lot of design decisions were made by a 6th grader that thought it would be funny to punish you for normal choices.You can accept a few bonus monster hunts, most that you can look for early will waste your party until later in the game.Dungeon maps are not easy to read. I mostly had no issues though. They served their purpose.Quests feel mostly pointless, with nothing pointing you in the correct directionThere are actually chests later in the game with equipment that seems to be for the base classes only. Since you would never gimp yourself in such a way this really makes no sense.Combat:There is a slash you can use to start a fight. It. Does. Nothing.Enemies are almost always faster than you, and will get a full turn smacking your party before you get to move.There is a steep penalty for hitting a resist/null/absorb attribute, which wouldn't be much of a problem except:Some enemies have no weakness.Some enemies cannot be scanned for weakness. (enable the setting to check weaknesses on skill target to get past this)Some party member skills always include a physical attack, leaving some of your party members useless for a very long time.(if they are resistant to physical you wasted the attack)And then, many skills feel useless, and every skill you unlock becomes part of an ever growing list per character.Progression:SP and stat orb farming requires tricks to get you what you need, as you need both to progress through class treeswhen you choose extra classes, you don't get to see what you will get until you select.Story:Story is not really fleshed out, and most of what is happening is implied for you to come to conclusions on your own.And then there are bugs...many many bugs.From some missing cutscenes, to voiceline mistakes in combat, to a game blocking bug that required a reload to resolveAs long as you abuse the system where possible, you can make your way through and enjoy it for what it is: a B-game that can scratch an itch.If you want something more fulfilling, There are plenty of other games that do a much better job.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally write reviews, but I don't understand the abundance of negative reviews at all - I think this game's dope asf. For context, I just beat the third? temple (desert area), and so far I've been really enjoying this game. The music is wonderful and the world is absolutely gorgeous as others have said. One of my gripes, however, would be that thus far the characters feel a little bland dialogue-wise - the character designs themselves are great though.I'm a big fan of more old-school games like FF6 and so far I've enjoyed the foray into something similar (albeit updated graphically...praise the lord). I have the Japanese voices on (even though I don't understand it, I just prefer the voice acting) with English text. The game itself is very challenging, which is something I crave - I like actually having to strategise and switch my characters around based on enemy vulnerabilities; there is an option I turned on which lets me see the enemy weaknesses relative to whatever attack/spell I'm targeting them with (obviously this mitigates the "challenge" aspect of the game, but I prefer it). The job/class system is looks good and feels good too and I'm happily experimenting with it rn. I also like the dungeon/metroidvania aspects of the game and although it's not overly complicated, it flows well. Minor "inconveniences" like not having a buy-and-equip button or having to go to town briefly for MP regeneration (as others have mentioned) seem absolutely trivial to me, but to each their own. Overall, I'm very glad I bought it (having a blast taking my time and loving it) and I hope others aren't dissuaded by some of the negative reviews on here - just make sure you know what you're in for before you buy!

_childDocuments_.review: I am actually pretty torn between yes and no when it comes to recommending this game..This game is a very classical JRPG kind of game. I am talking about Job system, Turn based battle, and quite a cliche save the world kind of plot right from the start.Battle in Astria Ascending is quite challenging. Often times, the boss have a pretty large HP pool and you have to poke around to find what their weaknesses are. The only punishment you get from being wrong is that you are somewhat loses the ability to boost your attacks up to 200%, which is not that harsh since you are still poking at it anyway.Normal battle though.. these can be brutal. Early in the games, you will encounter a squad of enemies.. WHO CAN STUN YOUR WHOLE PARTY for 3 whole turns! it is almost as if the player are expected to equip stun break ring for the whole party... just because they are steal-able quite early in the game too. but thats now how you balance a game.Battle formation have no meaning whatsoever. its pretty much a 1 lane formation shaped like a diamond. Mage at the back and Tank at the front does not have any difference in the chance of being hit at all. that means Tanking relies on "taunt" and "provoke" skills, and hope they works. but keep in mind.. many enemies have hit all skills.. they are very common from normal battle to boss battlesBattle are also a little on the slow side. often times enemies have certain weakness, that often only 1 of your party members can take advantage of (im looking at the black mage... and effectively you only get 1 of them.. unless you want to sacrifice your only viable tank... to be the second black mage) and often times, your other party member cant effectively attack either, because of how the focus system works... hit their resistance, and you suffer focus penalty..Job system can be fun.. BUT NOT IN THIS GAME. first of all, ideally you want a generic starting job, and as character progress and develop (both statwise and plotwise), they should then gain access to a more unique end game jobs which depicts their own uniqueness, strength, and role.. both as a character in a plot, and as a party member.. in Astria Ascending though... guess what? your beginning job is the most unique job each character can get, as in all 8 have different starting jobs, and as you progress, you unlock Main Jobs, Sub Jobs, and Support Jobs in that order. These jobs are from a pool of 12, and each character are assigned (YES, ASSIGNED, by the devs) 3 jobs that then, as a player you can choose which of those 3 shall be the main, sub, and support. This is basically character progression into uniqueness.... in reverse.. as they lose their uniqueness as they advance jobsoh.. and did I mention.. the job choice... ARE IRREVERSIBLE.. they are permanent and you cannot change them! Main job also alter your: appearance, equipment, and main skill sets..Plotwise, the game have pretty cliche plot with cheesy names (Harmelons... cmon... Harmelons??). you get thrown into an interesting conflict right away... but then the conflict pattern repeats for 4 times.. its like creativity is pretty dead there. oh and after 4 repeats, basically the game just tells you, we told you where to go 4 times, now you can go 8 more times to the rest of the temple at your leisure... with mini stories in each temple.. just because it would be extra bad if there are no stories insideThere is no such thing as new party member, you get all 8 Party members right from the start and get to know all of them, and their strength and role in the party. so do not expect the excitement of having a new party member, you get all of them straight awayLoading Screen is sometimes VERY LONG. this really brings back the nostalgia of playing PS1 gamesas i am writing this, I also notice that there is a weird bug when exploring where I should be going somewhere but suddenly i am teleported to another place when changing screen. this happens to me twice in my 20 hours gameplay, but i cant really pinpoint whyIn the end, I really dont know if I like this game or not.. i love the difficult battle, but the job system does not help. the cliche naming also does not help. The Cliche plot makes it even worse...

_childDocuments_.review: Tl;dr - at this point, i don't recommend it.This review is written at the desert area at chapter 3.The hand-drawn style is great. The whole characters with different sprite classes, and even their enemies have distinct appearance. This was one of the biggest reason why i followed this game from a long time. BUT then, the gameplay disappoint me.At first, i thought this game is inspired by Valkyrie Profile (with 4 diamond lineup, photon/crystal freeze enemies, and so on). But it's not the same. The positional lineup? enemies can still hit your DPS (mage) protected on the back side of your formation, unlike Valkyrie Profile. The tag system doesn't work well. At first, i thought the tag will work like FFX, where you can tag, and go right away taking action. No, in this game, you'd waste your turn. Which is okay and flexible enough, IF the enemies are not so badly designed.On early chapters, the enemies are balanced. Couple of weird placed enemies, but nothing too serious. And then i reached chapter 3. There are 2 types of enemy-groups that made me think, this game is not well-designed.1. 7 (seven) enemies that have quite high speed, and heavy hitting insects. You'd think, "ah, it's not too bad right?" Yes, it's not that bad IF you can protect your Damage dealer. Like i said earlier, position don't matter. Even if you put your nuker on the back, the enemies can still attack you repeatedly. Most of the time, i had to spam revive item while killing and reducing the numbers of those enemies. Is this the intended way of playing by the devs?2. 2 knights type enemies that's invulnerable against physical damage. You'd think, "just do magic damage then" Yes, but that's not the problem. In this game, you can get stunned whole-party 4 turns in a row from those knights. What's that? i should wear stun-proof accessory? Yeah, it cost 10k a piece.Job system looks cool, with using constellation as the progression system (similar to FFX Grid.. or skyrim i guess). Your character will change the appearance based on the job. As i said, the art style is the best aspect of the game. But, the execution is lacking. You can't see the preview of the class, usable equipments, and so on. (Think of it like highlight of your class). They have none. So either you have to accept and job change to said class, and if you don't like it, load to your previous saves.Well, they have way to check what skills/ nodes from specific class, by opening the journal/ compendium. Hopefully this will change.I could go on more detail, but i guess from these points, they're enough to show that i don't recommend the game. Good concept, great arts, bad execution. Hopefully the devs will improve the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Im going to give this a positive rating out of the kindness of my heart; because this game really isnt the worst... it just has some really bad pacing issues and lacks basic quality of life improvements imo.First things first. Its basically an ideological mashup of bravely default and octopath traveler; but seems to miss slightly on what made those two game's respective mechanics 'fun' and 'engaging'. The boost mechanic from bravely default is here but its a bit hampered in its implementation. Exploiting weakness or defaulting will increase your potential brave activation rate (up to 4x or 200%) which does increase all the various mechanics of the skill you're about to use (steal chance etc too); but it doesnt let you take more actions in a single turn. It's got a roster of characters all with somewhat unique reasons to use some over others (especially for various combat situations) a-la octopath traveler; but the game just starts you with all characters--rather than making 'unlocking' them or 'finding' them part of the story.'Ok cool; so you start with your full team and the brave mechanic is gimped but that doesnt sound all bad,' I psychically hear you thinking.  Well; now we get to turn to the brutal pacing of the quest / battle system. Let me start with; *you can change the difficulty of the battle system. Very easy is what you should be playing on when you're attempting to farm for exp / sp / items / etc.* There's no downside to changing difficulty; and normal / hard appear to be balanced for INSANE levels of grinding. Quests are an absolute chore and incredibly uninspired and annoying to complete. Drop rates from mobs are abysmal etc.The game also seems to assume that you are going to grind for hours on end; as you never really generate more than 1-6 SP per battle (even at the end of the game). But to that end; the balance / pacing seems to be off--since you're rewarded the same SP for farming level 1 areas as you are level 50 areas.So while the game seems to be set up to be extremely trollish to the player; it equally gives you all the tools to handle even the hardest of its wonky difficulty choices (*should you choose to invest an ungodly amount of time farming).I should also mention that this game has a good amount of crashes, soft locks, hard locks, etc. I've had to quit out or reload multiple times (and lost lots of progress multiple times) due to random bugs. There is also VERY MINIMAL quality of life improvements with this game. No auto combat; no speed up function; no animation skips; no nothing. If you arent used to playing RPGs circa 1996; you're probably not going to have the patience for this one.Also this game is the furthest thing from emotional and mature. Schizophrenic; maybe, but not emotional and mature.

_childDocuments_.review: + indepth skill and job system+ sympathic characters+ good 2D animations+ good OST+ lightweight story+ beautiful handdrawn background+ easy to learn figthing system+ dynamic dialogue reactions from characters+/- feels somehow too many characters for a specific focus- minor technical issues (FPS breakdown from 144 to 50 while screen switching etc., audio missmatch: when you choose japanese dialogue and some skills have still english dialogues)- some things are not properly explained- some missing tutorials- suffers from too many characters imho- some jobs a pretty much useless- long drawn story- some poor design choices in skill system (+ not explained)- shallow fighting system (missing some OMMPH! in combat)- game suffers from very high difficulty level (normal = hard, easy = normal etc.)- pretty annoying design choices in story- enemies can get pretty nasty (one hit kills in normal)- pretty much slow progression in skills- some choices by the player tend to get wrong if not informed (some choices are not reversible in skills + not explained)- flow of combat stays pretty much the same In conclusion, the game just tortured me at the middle of it. Dungeons begin to get longer and more boring. The pacing is just isnt there. the game wanted to be so much more. But stopped in the middle of it. I really like Super Neptunia from the devs. But this game really executed me in the later half. 50/100 not very likeable.

_childDocuments_.review: Grain of salt on some topics below - I have NOT cleared a single playthrough at the time of this post. I've also left the game on several times while doing other things - padding the hours some (e.g., like while I'm writing this review to do a little bit of bug checking.).Some things I liked:* Assembling a party of four out of the eight, with a base class, eventually choosing from a second job with its abilities and passives, then with further progression - a sub job and support job.* Customizing the character's stats whether they get more HP vs. MP, more Agility vs. Accuracy vs. Evade vs. Luck, or more Strength vs. Magic vs. Defense vs. Magic Defense.* The character and background art.* Some of the music tracks, though I couldn't hum any if I was on the spot.* Some of the exploration and puzzles in the latter half of the game. Not the rewards or outcome, but just the process of it.* I like the possibilities of where the job system and character customization could have come in.e.g., making a character into a buffing job like the Harnesser and will have them spend more time buffing and using items? They don't need Attack, Magic, or Accuracy anymore. Or helping your melee/tank Captain become a Black Mage by equipping the passive that increases Magic by 30%, but reduces Strength by 30% - then ensuring her future investments help with sustaining the cast, dealing damage, and hitting the target accurately OR earlier in the turn. Or perhaps having a White Mage or other healer who intentionally acts late in the round to patch up any allies, but ensuring that this healer is resistant to silence, stun, or confusion - and deciding which one you'll risk. etc.Alternatively, if you're playing on a lower difficulty and/or discover game breaking combinations early on, you just AoE all enemies at the beginning of the round and do that until it's boss time. Even on Hard difficulty if too optimized. Short of chests with a Surprise Attack, should be able to clear most combat comfortably.Many abilities, some classes, and some gameplay systems could have used some love.========And then a host of things that I didn't like and/or thought needed more polish. Issues below tried across 3 computers:* Bright background on main menu and menus without a dark mode equivalent.* Audio abruptly cutting off intermittently for 0.5~1 second every so often.* Idle time during combat could be sped up. Debuffs and misses tend to have 0.5~3 seconds of nothing happening. With 2~8 enemies, multiple rounds, and encounters throughout the game - this is a lot of time that adds up with nothing happening.* Bugs in the game such as NPCs in Chapter 5 being able to disable the player's movement and menus unless you start a mini-game with them, then escape out. This impacted both the controller and keyboard/mouse. And if you speak to an NPC that doesn't have the mini-game, you have to force quit out of the game.* Largely uneven voice acting. Several of the main cast are on the better side. Some characters who are emotive get marred with poor voice direction and/or no retakes. Many voices don't match up and most are low energy and disengaging.* Uneven audio volume where in-game voices are unaffected, e.g., voice volume at 100%, music volume at 30% - many sequences have the voices blend / blur into the music.* One environment in the game overrides Controller Vibration Off settings and is pretty annoying. It's a mechanic to warn the player of a timed hazard, but as a workaround - the player can go into the menu to reset the time on the hazard.* Many of the vertical menus have inconsistent wraparounds, e.g., if you have 2~5 items, you can wraparound from the bottom to the top, but not the top to the bottom. Once you have 6 items, you can wraparound in either direction. This behavior occurs in several other vertical menus.* Incorrect UI glyphs displayed such as showing the analog stick, but requiring the D-Pad or showing the analog stick, but requiring a face button to perform an action.* Inconsistent mouse navigation - e.g., you can't click on a choice in most in-game menus, you mouse wheel down to it - then click to confirm whatever has focused - but then the store menus, you have to click directly on the Buy or Sell and can't use the mouse wheel.* Missing UI legend - e.g., in the item shop, if you want to use the filters, for controller - you use your R1/L1 / Bumper equivalents. For keyboard/mouse, you need to press Tab or Shift + Tab (default Steam overlay), but in either case, the input legend is not indicated across the bottom with the other possible actions.* Some puzzles midway through the game and onward do not have apparent answers on where the solution is supposed to go. e.g., you have two identical blocks and two empty "block sockets". You place the blocks in the sockets, nothing happens. Visually, the blocks and sockets are designed and colored the same. OR another puzzle where the block socket isn't marked and you just keep moving pieces until you can't move them anymore to see if you can brick the game.* Side quests and treasure chests tend to have subjectively unfulfilling rewards compared to what you can just buy in the store. e.g., defeat 5 specific enemies in location A, then 10 enemies in location B, to receive 500 lums as a reward. Which is about 1/4 or less of what you get just from defeating the enemies required for the quest. Or you solve components of a puzzle and find a chest out of the way only to pickup a duplicate piece of gear.* The item list could have used a Sort by New in case the UI glitches out and opening a chest doesn't actually display the toast notification of what dropped.* Combat sound effects are generally lacking in OOMPH! Did your mighty Guardian just leap in the air and slam an axe down on four enemies at one time? The sound effect of these enemies dying sound like I flicked four of fingers against a piece of paper.* Exploration hit boxes need work such as slashing your sword through an enemy and the battle not initiating or firing off a ring too close to a target - resulting in no action. The former, if you're running forward, thinking you're going to get into combat and keep running - you might end up with the enemy doing a Surprise Attack (without the necessary passive to prevent it).Neutral / lukewarm:* I wasn't very attached to the story. Overall, not interested in it - but was hoping talking to every NPC between chapters and doing the side quests would help with world lore - but not enough for me to be invested in the story and characters more.* Didn't like the flying mini-game.* Stat Orbs are in shorter supply early on and this can hurt developing and exploring your 8 party members. As much as I wanted to spread myself thin, some of the characters were pretty unlikeable early on to me, so it helped narrow the party down to 4 and focus on them. Still didn't have enough stat orbs at times and ended up sitting on hundreds at one point, 1000+ SP waiting for a stat orb to progress.=======I'll still play the game to the credits and see if there's anything else afterwards. But as I'm exploring some of these locations, I'm unfortunately caring less and less about the story, the combat, and replaying the game with a different combination of jobs.

_childDocuments_.review: This game got a lot of (likely deserved) flak for being a buggy unplayable mess on release.  I played a little less than a year after launch and while it still had some issues, I experienced nothing game-breaking.  What you get here is a classic turn-based style RPG with some interesting mechanics revolving around exploiting weaknesses.  The story is pretty bland, I found myself largely uninterested before even reaching the halfway point.  Musically the game is fantastic, however the major bug I encountered was most areas would stop playing any BGM after getting into a battle.There is a skill system in place where your characters select from a limited set of jobs; the order you pick these will determine which skills you can learn.  There are some cool synergies here, though the biggest problem is you'll likely want to do a little research before selecting as these decisions are permanent and you can't respec later.  Side quests are bland and for the most part unrewarding.  While I did enjoy my time with this game, my main complaint stems from where most of the difficulty comes from: turn initiative.  Even on normal difficulty, in most battles after the early game (even where you are not ambushed) all the enemies will take turns before anybody in your party.  This means sometimes you'll be wiped out or damn near wiped out before you ever even get a turn.  Difficulty can be tweaked at any time.If you enjoy turn based RPGs, I would still recommend this game.  It's not the best of the bunch but it shows a lot of promise.  The devs previous game, Super Neptunia RPG, was not my cup of tea at all.  This was a major step in the right direction, and with improvement like that I'm sure the next game will be a knockout.

_childDocuments_.review: Astria Ascending is a classic JRPG developed by Artisan Studios and published by Dear Villagers. It's chock full of pedigree, boasting an amazing score by Hitoshi Sakimoto from FFXII, narrative from FFVII remake's Kazushige Nojima and simply stunning art from CyDesignation's Akihiko Yoshida and Hideo Minaba, who have previously worked on both FF and NieR. That's a powerhouse of talent!As soon as you launch the game you can see and feel the painstaking care and attention to detail that's been poured into this title over the last three years. Gorgeous is a word I've no doubt every review will probably have in it's first paragraph, rightly so as the artwork is simply beautiful. Hand drawn and animated characters, stunning backdrops and incredible character design are at it's core and run through the entirety of the game.In Astria Ascending you take control of 8 Demigods. The demigods are chosen from the races of Orcanon to protect the balance and harmony of the world that is constantly under threat from "the noise".The demigods are in effect, a sort of cross between fantasy superheroes and the replicants from Blade Runner; when appointed a demigod, they also have their lifespan reduced to 3 years, after that they're gone.....lost in time, like tears in the rain....We join the story during the party's final three months of their lifespan.The noise? Far from being an 80's punk ensemble from Nottingham, are creatures who sole purpose is to disrupt the harmony between the races of Orcanon. This tenuous Harmony is held intact partly as the result of the magical effects of a fruit called Harmelon and policing by the demigods.Each character has their own story, explored across five cities, twenty-five dungeons and around thirty hours of gameplay. Along with the main story quest, there are a range of side quests and mini-games. The game is played out completely in 2D.... Did I mention it's gorgeous??Exploration of the cities, dungeons and various location environments is done by your party leader avatar, they can interact, initiate conversation, jump, slash and execute a ranged attack. I found this vaguely reminiscent of Atlus' Odin Sphere both in it's execution and art style.As is standard in JRPG's contact with a monster initiates combat. Rather than stumblingly into creatures, you could also choose to use your ranged attack to stun the creature and avoid it, or slash attack to initiate combat with advantage.Once combat is initiated it is a very classic turn-based structure, with your party on one side of the screen and the enemy on the other. Only four of your party can actively engage in combat, but you can swap party members in and out, from your full compliment, as the fight progresses (at the cost of their action for that turn).The in game menus are extensive and offer a wide variety of options and customization to make the game as challenging or accessible as you like.This is also where you access your party management screens and individual character development. Skill and job trees are enormous offering tremendous scope of how you want to build each character's abilities, passives and class skills.The audio for the game has also been masterfully created. The musical score is fantastic and compliments the different locations, perfectly while switching up the tempo for party combat. The characters have all been fully voiced as well, so talking to NPCs, as well as listening to party interactions adds another level of polish and immersion to an already fantastic title.You can choose between Japanese voice acting or English. The quality of the Japanese voice acting, in my opinion, is far better than the English so I kept it set to Japanese with English subtitles.I played the game exclusively using a controller and found it easy to use with the interface, intuitive and comfortable for longer gaming sessions. The more casual pace of a jrpg, lends itself perfectly to reclining in a comfortable chair with a gamepad, as opposed to being hunched over a mouse and keyboard.While I could see some people off put by the 2D approach and classic JRPG turn based combat; those people are quite simply buffoons, philistines and completely wrong.Astria Ascending is exactly how a jrpg should be made, it's like a comfortable blanket that smells of home and a warm cup of tea. A game bursting full of fantastic narrative, stunning artwork, incredible music, character design, lore and a comfortable familiarity.It's doesn't innovate or try anything new, it's just a fantastic example of a classic JRPG and an excellent adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like somebody came into the office with their mother's best recipe, but then dropped the ball. There is a skeleton of a game here that could have been fantastic but upon building upon it could not meet their aspirations. There is a "job" system, but it's basically just gated skills, if you don't select 'the' class path you're completely handicapping yourself. There are no reset options and there is lacking massive information. When you first look at the classes, you'll see "end cap" skills that feel like you're basically selecting the class based on these end cap skills. However, the game doesn't tell you that these Silver outlined skill nodes are not accessible during the game (post game content only, and specific rules to it)To top off that aspect, there are tonnes of bugs and issues (Ensure the golden rule, keep multiple different save files). I've been soft locked out of multiple side quests due to these bugs and have to just give up on them, one of which is a quest to be able to get a subjob.This game had so much information/feedback to pull from, and decided to disregard all Quality of life aspects generated over time from other games (5 second example.. when you buy items from the shop, you can't equip them right there)I hate that this game is getting bad reviews, I want JRPGs to thrive so developers will keep trying them, but I would like to give a realistic view into this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The hand drawn art style is what initially attracted me to the game. I am also a fan of JRPGs in general.Let's start with some positive points. The in-game art style is still very nice and I like the customization available to your party. Every character has three classes to choose from (though some classes overlap between characters) which adds some nice diversity and lets you build your team how you would like. Combat also has a nice feel to it as you exploit enemy weaknesses to build focus points which can then be used to empower another attack by up to 200%.And now for the the bad. The story is god awful. Like not even laughably bad, just straight up awful. For the first half of the game, your party simply reacts to events, barely showing any initiative. Things will happen for no logical reason and for some reason, almost everyone's family members get involved to the point where you think there has to be some story reason for this, but none ever appears.Next, the characters. There is not a single likable character among the cast with the exception of maybe one or two characters who are tolerable at best. The main reason for this is that nearly every party member is racist. Does the game use this as a learning moment to show that ultimately, the party members are all equal or that they must put aside their differences for the greater good? Nope, they're just straight up racist. This is especially bewildering to see when the target of their racism is often their youngest party member, a 13 year old kid.Lastly, game play balance. While the combat itself has a nice flow to it, the balance is a mess. I played the game on only normal, but enemies early in the game can still wipe out your team, gaining access to AoE moves well before you do. In fact, enemies often do so much damage that you won't even have a chance to heal, resulting in needing to use multiple revive items per over world battle. But it's okay because if you pick Alchemist and use distillate, you can generate infinite money for infinite items which includes full party heals, full party revives, and full party status recoveries that devalue any other healing class. Or the fact that Hunter has access to Gunner, which randomly does 1 to 10 hits meaning you have a 90% chance of doing at least double the damage of a normal attack.Actually, while we're here, let's have a speed run of minor grievances:At its core, this game has a competent skeleton. A good game could be made with what is here, but it's currently lacking in organs, flesh, and skin, as well as a thick layer of polish and sheen. As it is though, I honestly wouldn't recommend Astria Ascending.

_childDocuments_.review: I was hesitant about buying this game because of many reviews. The best advice i offer is that if you are a fan of JPRG, you must try it yourself. If YOU are in the same ship, please read all...Ok, thanks. Overall is a tad of many classics, and maybe that´s the problem with many reviews: they automatically expect or compare this to all of them labelling it "not a classic". Gameplay wise It has the "charge" mechanic, all the spells and conditions, invocations and the swap character in the middle of the battle; in the many hours i have played haven't gotten tired of, it reminds a little of Octopath. The only grip if you can say so is some spikes in difficulty, but amazingly you can customize the random encounters from a menu (if you don't want random, if you want the enemies to respawn or not in a dungeon) you can always grind like in most rpg and rethink the strategy for that lost battle, dungeon or boss. Leveling is a mix between FFX and FFXII (zodiac signs included) where you "unlock" orbs that grant more points, attributes or actions. You can choose different jobs, each character having the initial, principal, secondary and support.The side game that uses cards (whatever they are called here) is just another version of FFVIII card game.The ART is AMAZING, of course this is in my opinion, but even if i really enjoyed the art in Octopath i like when the proportions are equal between non-battle and party-enemies in battle. Also i love the art in games where it looks like a drawing moving, most agree this along the gameplay to be the strongest points of the game, even with all that crap of QoL many people argue (yes you can't equip or try equipment at stores, and makes you lose track specially when you change job, but come one, didn't you play some of the classics you claim to love?).About the story: I won't argue that there isn't enough development on the character part, you see a flashback with the story here and there and that's it. I don't think that's enough to put it down, effectively, the story of each character could be cliche (exactly like most games) is what you expect of the genre. It's different and I like it, from the beginning you have your party assembled, i know many people would have prefered to play all those back stories and conform the party but it´s a fresh change for once. The grand scene is the same as always, with you playing the protectors of peace with the twist of the likes of FFXIII and X introduced from the start, you will finish your time soon after doing your job and "ascend" (die). I didn´t find it so confusing as many try to put it (if you played FFXIII and sequels this is clear as water and well encompased in comparison). Its light and delivers what it must. I say all this even when i hate to read it on other reviews, its not a "bad" story, but you cant expect a persona kind of development or a Darth Revan plot twist (oops that's not JRPG). Try it, why not take the 4 warriors of light approach on this one.Now with the gripe gun out (the things i consider should have been different):- The map: I mean the one in dungeons, that's a dissaster. When you begin to understand it, it becomes like an ugly dog, its ugly but for some reason you have learned to love him. It has no marker of where you are, i don´t like opening my map every 10 seconds to make logic of it. At least you can fast travel and save/load without any restrictions.- The pc configuration. I wanted it on ps5 but for some reason (yeah right) on steam in my country it was at 1/4 the price of the psstore... it has been reaaaaally worth every penny. The thing is performance on some dungeons (sewers im looking at you) really lags. There are no options like in most pc game where you can configure it. I solved it lowering the resolution on my pc (i was playing it connected to my 4k tv with 4k resolution, when i went to 1080 no more lag). That is a truly QoL.
