_childDocuments_.review: I debated whether or not I wanted to write a review for Astria Ascending.  But since I hit the recommend button I felt it was appropriate to explain why.  ****Slight Spoilers Below****How to begin?  Astria Ascending isn't a good game.  It is an average game in almost all respects.  There were plenty of bugs I encountered at various points throughout my playtime.  I had to reset my game about six times due to various soft lock issues.  There were text bugs and some quests which wouldn't finish if I had another quest with the same NPC currently active.  You would need to finish the other quest first.Story: The second worst aspect of this game.  The story is without a doubt below average fare.  Your team of Demi-gods, in my opinion, were generally wrong in everything they did.  Sure there is a bigger threat that must be dealt with at the end, but generally everything you stood for felt backwards.  The game preached anti-individualism and favored solidarity and harmony no matter the cost. Being unique is seen as problematic and must be dealt with in a harsh way.Gameplay: The Gameplay of Astria Ascending is its greatest asset and also one of its hindrances.  Battles can feel unfair, even regular encounters, due to how status effects work and turn order.  You can mitigate these issues later in the game with accessories and stat increases, but when it happens it is very frustrating. With that aside, once you get a grasp of how the battle system works, it can be pretty fun exploiting weaknesses and swapping characters to develop strategies.Game Design: I'm not sure where to put this, but the map design is the worst aspect of this game by a mile.  Early on it isn't so bad.  However, after the halfway point it becomes nearly unbearable.  It is awful and I don't understand who decided to do it this way. The map doesn't tell you where you are in a room, even if the room is huge and has multiple doors you can enter and exit.  It just isn't intuitive and often hurts your experience.  You're better off just memorizing a dungeon.  BAD.  Gear progression is nearly as puzzling as the map design.  Obtaining base job gear in the last two dungeons of the game when you can't even equip them makes no sense.  Were the designers suggesting you should go the entire game without choosing a main job?  Challenge runs maybe.  Music: A highlight of the game.  Some very good tracks which you will hum after exiting the game and a few poor ones.  Unfortunately some songs were hurt by dungeon frustrations and backtracking.Visuals: This will probably be hit or miss for many people, but I really liked the art style.  I looked forward to seeing the art design of every zone and the unique characters you encounter throughout your journey.Accessibility:  Lots of options to choose from to customize your difficulty level.  If you don't want to spend time figuring out enemy weaknesses and want to have it laid out for you?  There is an option.  Want full EXP for party members not participating in battles?  That is there too.  Want monsters to respawn or not respawn in dungeons?  That is also an option.  Very good job in this respect!If you are considering this game you need to realize there are many faults in its design and story, but if you can pick this up for $20-$25 or less it may be worth your money.  I hope this was of some help to someone out there.

_childDocuments_.review: I refrained from buying this game last year because of the mixed reviews. I don't regret my decision simply because I haven't encountered a single bug. I assume that has to do with the patches before I bought this game. I don't know if there is a difficulty selection. I didn't see one when I started the game. But, it feels like it's on hard mode. This game is unforgiving to gamers that don't understand how to play the way developers want you to play. If you're familiar with Final Fantasy games, the strategy tactics are similar. The tactics are always changing depending on the enemies. Regular enemies will be hard to defeat if you don't know what you're doing. Even when you do know what you're doing, if your characters are under-developed, expect to get obliterated from a surprise attack. Like most JRPG, expect to do some exp grinding to have an easier time fighting enemies. You will encounter difficult enemies before you even get to the boss chapter. So, if you're having trouble defeating them, you're not ready for the boss. As for ability upgrades, you use Special Points. They are earned by killing enemies. It's a 1:1 ratio. Kill 1 enemy to get 1 SP. The good thing is that you can kill lower level enemies to farm SP. The bad thing is that upgrades require so much SP that you're farming for hours. The benefit about farming is that you'll earn coin too. You will need a lot of coin to stock up on potions and ethers for those harder fights. Literally by Chapter 2, the devs are throwing you in the deep end. I imagine this must be why only 30% of players on Steam have progressed past Chapter 2. It's understandable if you don't want to commit all that time to just farming. But that's no different from any other JRPG. One thing I absolutely love is the instant travel. You can pull up your map and go to any previous destinations you've been too. I hate it when games use a travel point or when there is none. I just want to get to where I'm going. So, THANK YOU developers for making it this easy for us. As for visuals, it's gorgeous. I love the art style of this game. It's in 2D but still it looks beautiful. In the very beginning of this game, they don't hide the fact that there is jiggle physics. You will see bouncing cleavage and thunder thighs. It's simply there for eye appeal, nothing more, which is great. Think of the game, Magna Carta. That artist loved to draw his female characters with the most unrealistic but visually appealing bodies. As for the story, it's very linear. Nothing fancy which I like. Not every story has to be complex. The characters make it known that they don't get along with each other. At first, it didn't make sense because they're a team. But, if you look at it from the perspective of what their world use to be, it makes sense why they don't get along with each other. Maybe it comes off as forced and that's why it feels awkward. I don't like that there aren't short keys for characters during a battle. It's annoying having to go thru the list of abilities every time I want to cast a spell. The battles aren't timed which I like. But having short keys can make battles go by much quicker. It's a useful tool since they expect us to grind in this game. Regardless, I am enjoying this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I passed on this game early on due to the mixed reviews. I recently tried it on Game Pass and enjoyed it enough to buy a copy here to support the developers.I feel kinda bad for this game. It definitely does not deserve to have such a low rating, but I can see why it's not for everyone. I guess it used to be pretty buggy and it took a while for them to fix things. I only ran into one minor bug once.The good:- The art and music are both great.- The developers seem to have taken inspiration from older JRPGs when it comes to gameplay and art style.- The job system allows you to highly customize your party members. - Fun variety of dungeon mechanics- Ability to save the game and adjust difficulty anywhere.Not necessarily good or bad:- The game is not easy, even on normal. However, the ability the change difficulty any time should make this not really matter. The difficulty lovers and the easy-going people can both have it their way.The bad:- I played on normal, and the difficulty at times made me feel like I needed to save before every encounter. One battle can go fine and the next can wipe the entire party on the first turn.- Sometimes there will be a boss and then another boss two feet later with no indication. There was one part where I killed a boss and decided I'd look around the room a bit afterwards. Ran right into another boss without the chance to refill my MP.- I had a lot of times where enemies focus targeted one party member. I don't know if this was just bad luck or if it's intended, but it was annoying.- In my opinion, there wasn't quite enough explained in the story and the ending was lackluster.Overall, I enjoyed this game. It's a shame it had so many problems at launch.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh Astria Ascending, where do I begin? I would like to swear to show my immense displeasure but alas, I'm limited to the polite vagaries of language. So instead let me sum up in section why I truly, truly despise this game.Plot: In the land of harmony, people eat harmelons to barely suppress their active hate for each other. Eight people protect this barely existent harmony and will die in three years. Except the plot sort of falls apart because the harmony barely exists as it is and you often find that the people themselves may as well not eat the harmelon for all the good it does. I won't go into details because of spoilers (not that I give a care) but the plot is as thin as one-ply toilet paper on a good day. Characterization: Meet our lovely heroes! Ulan: Ms.Generic Party Leader, Kress: Stoic Dragon Person, Kaydin: Warrior with a barely tangential past with one of the villains, Eko, the games punching bag for reasons, Dagmar who may as well be emotionally dead, Arpajo: One of the least likable party members I've seen in gaming and this counts the entire crew of this game too. , Alek: A Simp for Goddess Yuno who could be compared to a Vtuber fan who spent superchat money and Alassia: Whose sort of likable and maybe the only level headed person in the party. Sprinkle so much hypocrisy that it spoils the dish and you have a pasta that while it may look appetizing is soggy and barely edible. Gameplay: Basically a mix of platforming and Bravely default. It's ok, its not horrible but several dungeons aren't designed well and the noises are a chore to kill due to an ever shifting array of weaknesses. Also, the side quests in this game have a major flaw in that there are no map icons whatsoever to point you to where you need to go. I had to google most of the locations for sidequests and even then the amount of information was so limited that I had to guess in most places. Plus when you aren't searching for a red glowing ball in a haystack you have quests where you have to kill 10 herpderps in the flerpherp isles for 5000 money and a weapon that will probably suck compared to what you are actively using. You can also try hunts which suffer from the same issues as the sidequests with the bonus of requiring random weather patterns to even spawn. I used podcasts to get through this game because after the amount of time I spent trying to decipher what I needed to do plus the amount of time needed to get through sidequests, I was dangerously close to putting this game down. Oh, also hope you like rail-shooters, because this game dips into that puddle for a moment and then forgets about it like it never happened. Jster: Probably the one positive to this game. It's well designed and mostly fair, except for the random rule opponents that pop up every now and then. This could probably be spun off and do decently, its no Gwent but its not horrible. Verdict: I could say much more about how much this game irks me but I think I covered enough. It's a shame too because the art style is good and the enemy designers feel wasted on a game of this scale. This game is a nightmare for completionists because of all the glitches and sidequests. I wanted to like this game, but I can't stand hypocrites and I can't stand games that have more holes than swiss cheese. I beat this game but you don't have to. Save yourself and buy something much better made.

_childDocuments_.review: After 20 hours played I can finally give a proper review and sadly its not a good one.The pacing of the story is extremely slow, boring and uninteresting. It all revolves around the 8 characters who are called Demi-gods but there is no introduction towards them at all so you never feel attached towards any of their stories and on top of that somehow the game manages to make each of every one of them annoying as heck.The combat gameplay is pretty fun, standard jrpg turn based combat with class and subclass development. However the UI is filled with so many bugs it becomes extremely frustrating to just select a single spell from a list that keeps scrolling away and bugging every time. The pacing of the combat is also extremely slow and some animations take up to 10 seconds and I'm not exaggerating. J-Ster minigame is heavily inspired by the FF8 Triple Triad except they somehow managed to make it so easy that after you get a certain amount of medals is just impossible to lose, so it becomes a minigame of finding the right people to win new medals from. Aesthetics and art of the game are extremely good and I'm in love with them, however the OST and SFX of the game is very mediocre trending to poor. The characters have limited voice sets so whenever you use resurrection for example the Fish will only say "Pichi pichi" twice, first when casting then when ressing, which makes no sense. Another example is when characters make a critical they say a line, but when they get struck by a critical strike they also say the same line because they have no lines for harmth.Finally the maps are interesting to explore but in general they feel quite short and not very immersing. The way they are planned in 2D feels more like exploring a metroidvania without any difficulty and there is no puzzles or challenging trials, its just walking and jumping around.All in all I think its a 5/10 game, get it on a good sale and enjoy it for what it is but don't expect anything great.

_childDocuments_.review: Tl;DR This game was a lot of fun from the start to finish. Despite some issues it does have. Solid 3/5 B rate Game. If you like JRPG's such as FFX or Bravely Default you will enjoy this game for the most part. Long part of the Review now. In the 48 hours of my first time playing this game I had a good time from start to finish. You start off with your full Party right from the start. 8 unique characters all with familiar Jobs and classes to any seasoned JRPG fan. As well as a plethora of character identities that offer a sense of diversity in the team. This game does many things right as well as a few things wrong that will be brought up in this review. Things done Right.From the start of the game you have all 8 party members all with different things to offer for party synergy. You can swap each member out as needed from the start, so unlike other JRPGs where the main character has to be present at all times this game does not necessarily have a main protag. Instead however each party member shares a spot in the story. When it comes to combat Astria Ascending does a few things that other games don’t do as well. First is the Focus gage, this is an in-combat system that allows you to empower one's next ability or skill. Allowing you do do more damage or even elongating a skill that buffs the team for a few extra turns. This makes for interesting meta gaming where you have to match the element with the enemies to make quick work of them in a fight. Figuring out an enemy's weakness generates 2 focus points up to a reserve of 10. Additionally if you hit an enemies defensive spot you will lose focus points down to a negative 10. So it balances out. The focus points are also used for summoning astray to help you in battle. There are more ways to generate focus points which are tied to the job system, specifically the chronomancer. The second thing that Astria does, that is just great quality of life, is the ability to swap out any number of party members on the field for the ones on the bench. The kicker is that this ability can be used by any of the party members and it only uses up one of their turns. Which is just a great quality of life for these types of games. If you mess up a fight and you forgot a healer, no worries just use a turn to swap them in for the fight and you are all set. Just perfect for when you need a specific thing and your party is not well equipped for it. The last thing of note is the job system. After every dungeon you get 2 job spheres that can be used on 2 party members to unlock a new job for them. This does not override their base job in any way and it just gives you additional abilities for them to learn. NOTE: Selecting a new main job will change their weapon type and will often change their armor type depending. That being said, each of the 8 characters can learn 1 of 3 jobs offered to them per sphere. And if you complete all the dungeons and obtain all the job spheres each of the party members can in fact learn all 3 jobs offered to them. However, Depending on if it is a main, sub, or support job will change the abilities offered by the class. Something I wish I knew going into the game. When you choose a Main job, you get access to all the abilities the job offers, all the skills, all the support abilities and all the raw stat increases. A sub job will only allow you to learn the abilities for the job, and the support job will only offer the support abilities for the job. Looking back at it now, I'm sure it was explained somewhere but I skipped the prompt. Things Done Wrong. One of the first things you will notice when it comes to Astria is the brutal jump in difficulty spikes. I am not sure what the call for such harsh spikes in power creep but i felt it going into the first dungeon almost immediately. I certainly had to grind for a bit until I felt capable of handling the boss near the end. If you pick up this game, just know that grinding for a few hours here and there will be necessary for finishing the game. If you have a hard time you can turn the difficulty down to very easy. No shame in that. Secondly, the game lacks a turn bar. Agility is the stat that determines whose turn it is and in what order. But the lack of a turn bar really hinders this game's fun factor. In the early game, being able to know whose turn is next could have really helped with things like eliminating threats or who to buff for an empowered attack. Just a slight Nit-pick though. This does not outright ruin the experience, just feels a bit off when it is not present. Next on the list of things that this game did not do well, is the side quests. I had such a horrible time trying to decipher the cryptic messages for the side quests. There is no Marker on the map, there is nothing to tell you where to go exactly. I had a quest that literally says, get a strawberry, and i have no idea where the ♥♥♥♥ that is or what enemy drops it. Plenty of them are also out right just bugged. One of my quests says to explore a dungeon, and i ran through that dungeon for hours killing every mob and scanning every room up and down trying to allocate the item i need to click on but it just was not happening for me. The quests and side quests need to be better optimized and bug fixed. Because at this point I gave up on the side quests with only like 6 left to do. That being said, the game was a lot of fun to play and there is replay value in the job system that allows you to try new and different build combinations. Most of my game was spent using Kress as a Dark Knight, Kaiden as a Hunter, Dagmar as a Black Mage [], and Ulan as Harnesser. I will be looking forward to future play though, not anytime soon though. Hopefully when they fix some of the bugs I encountered and the soft locks in some of the dungeons.

_childDocuments_.review: Astria Ascending is an oldschool style JPRG with gorgeous art, beautiful score, and appealing combat. The game is splendidly crafted with lots of charm, having people who previous worked on JRPGs like various Final Fantasy games and Nier Automata, altogether to make solid work out of this.In the world of Orcanon which is full of devastating beings called Noises, play as a group of eight Demigods in their journey of vanquishing them all to save the world. Encountering them commences turn-based combat where four of the demigods at a time battle against a few random creatures and monsters. Along with the main storyline and turn-based combat are a mix of platforming and exploration for unlocking abilities and customisable equipment. There is also variable difficulty of puzzle solving and minigames like ‘J-Ster’ when enough tokens are earned. While the combat is mostly nothing out of the norm when it comes to JRPGs, it is still satisfying to play as you control multiple demigods each with their own unique strengths and abilities. There is a little twist to it where if your character hits an enemy’s weak point, you receive these focus points that can be used for additional damage. Even with the extensive gameplay the game is quite diverse with many characters to choose and swap between, levelling them up, and play along with lots of customizations and classes to keep the game enjoyable.I do quite like the art and designs within the game, which is beautifully and creatively hand drawn. It is full of vibrant characters and backgrounds that are exciting to encounter and visit. Characters and backgrounds are well detailed though occasionally characters are just standing in a weird position. The demigods themselves are all unique and full of colour including human and anthropomorphic beasts amongst others. The kinds of enemies that are fought are also vast, starting off being more standard with rats and robots, and later getting more bizarre with tree people, beasts and monsters with compelling designs.Throughout the game is voice acting in both English and Japanese. While it is decent in English, having the Japanese voice acting on is the superior and more enjoyable way to play. Dialogue being accompanied by voice acting a lot of the time does makes it fun to read and listen to, whether it be crucial to the plot or just random casual talk. With the large number of characters and NPCs to talk to, it makes the game quite immersive. The score is also superb to listen to with the variable tone and tempo that there are, including slower and somber music to instrumentals having faster tempo in more thrilling sequences. All in all, the soundtrack itself is worth buying to listen to.Though the game is playable with keyboard and mouse, being a JRPG I was playing it with a controller which I found comfortable to play with in terms of both the controls and interface. This is because overall the game is not too complex so it can be easily played sitting back casually with a controller as opposed to sitting and playing with keyboard and mouse. The game is a bit expensive but due to the length of the game and the entertainment it provides, the price is rather fair. I would recommend it mainly to those who are into JRPG games, otherwise to check it out when it is on sale. Overall Astria Ascending is a solid JRPG with a lot of fun and fascinating characters and absorbing world to explore.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm glad that I looked past the decidedly mixed reviews, as Astria Ascending is a pretty fun JRPG with platforming exploration. There might have been some nasty bugs on launch, but at this point, I didn't run into anything that mattered. The dialogue is weak and the voice acting and direction is laughable, but the Octopath Traveler-like combat with class options and skill boards is very welcome. Sure, there are a few places that require some minor leveling to proceed, but you often gain needed strength very quickly. If things become too much of a slog, there are quality of life options in the settings and many of the later game areas are entirely avoidable if you so choose. It's far from perfect, but it's worth a play on deep sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a really good addition to the JRPG genre. Combat doesn't feel clunky and not overly complex. Graphics is certainly good, the cities, the characters and the effects used in battle. I just don't like how other characters feet are drawn but that's for a few characters. What really interest me is the job system. You can really customize them in many ways and so far none of the classes feels the same nor repetitive. Imagine your tank becoming a black mage and it freaking works well LOL. From what I have seen so far, the are about lack of optimization, keybind customization and some about game being somewhat hard. About the lack of optimization yes there's currently none but graphics are beautiful and it's running smoothly in my pc and had no issues regarding performance so far. Same for keybind customization, currently there is none but for me easily disregarded. Now for the game being somewhat hard, all I can say is read your characters skills and even at hard difficulty its really easy.About bugs, yes there are few but as I discover more bugs, I am inclined to say that there are too many bugs, not game breaking but enough to make you ask if QAs did really do their job. You'll have those lock abilities on your job's tree and can unlock them later. Most that I tested are either not working correctly with their description or doing something else. I suggest that you save first before you use that crest that unlocks these abilities since you only get ONE (so far I have just gotten one.)Lastly there are really some QOL features that are missing on this game that dampens the mood. The map dungeon is terrible ESPECIALLY when doing quest. Map dungeon do not have an indicator where the quest objective is and you have to carefully look so to what is interact able throughout the dungeon, as a result questing in this game is really a pain but not all quest are like that. Leveling also can be a pain since it does not have a way to turn off or modify skill list making you scroll thru a bunch of skills while leveling since some DPS job combination have A LOT of skills.There is also no job change option so think carefully before deciding since you get the whole tree of the class as your MAIN JOB, you only get active skills for your SUB JOB and you only get support nodes (these are the abilities that you can equip) for your SUPPORT JOB.It can be a frustrating experience sometimes but if you can get past these things (hopefully they will address this since their discord have a suggestion tab dedicated for these) it's really a good game.If you're for the story then you'll be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: A really solid JRPG.Is it the best JRPG of all time ? Really not.The dialog is sometimes a bit awkward and the pacing of the game in general is quite slow (both during dialogs and in combat).If you don't mind taking things slowly and you like engaging turn based combat in a beautiful art style and with good music this game is for you.Most critics are way too harsh with this game. If your expectations are kept in check and you know what you are getting into you will have a good time. It is not a huge budget AAA title despite the excellent visuals. It's a small indie title with a small budget that lacks polish. We need more games like that. I will happily support Artisan Studio if they keep producing games like that (hopefully with higher polish and better execution though).

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I enjoyed myself overall. Not a perfect game, obviously, but I think it might be hard for me to say it's only "mediocre." I would probably give it a hard 6, maybe soft 7 out of 10, leaning toward 7 because basically anything under 7 seems to be regarded as trash.The game looks good, combat is challenging but enjoyable based on the system that is present and how customization is handled. The story and much of the game can be summed up in one word: concise. Dialogue and explanation of the story is short and to the point. Even most of the main quest events are without filler (like being in a room/house and needing to look for something. It's a side-scroller, so... it's right there). The big names that helped create this game have their influence on display with the music and gameplay and make the experience enjoyable. Unfortunately, perhaps due to the budget or otherwise, some achievements are bugged so if that's a problem for you, maybe wait for a patch. Otherwise, the game is worth the price tag, and gets better once the world opens up, going from pretty simple, introductory dungeons to more complicated puzzle-filled ones.Plus, jiggle physics and thunder thighs.

_childDocuments_.review: Astria Ascending sets out to provide a  with beautiful aesthetics and nails it: which is unfortunate, because so many negative reviews boil down to 'damn, this game gave me a classic JRPG experience!'Despite throwing you into the world with a huge party and little context, it doesn't feel overwhelming. The world and story are gradually established through dialog and quickly bring the player up to speed without relying on huge info dumps.Combat is simple, which is great, given the size of the party. Starting off with two abilities each makes it easy to get acquainted with each character's combat capabilities and specializations. The entire party gains EXP and SP, allowing you to level the entire cast evenly and bring out characters specialized for different situations.I played on Hard difficulty, and despite finding it frustrating at certain points (especially early on, when you have limited options available), I still found that it provided an enjoyable challenge.There are some rough edges that could use quality of life improvements, but nothing that really ruins the game. You have to purchase and equip items separately, but you only do this once every 3-4 hours at most. Combat against large groups can be a bit slow with waiting for long animations to play out. Having MP restored when walking over a teleporter would be nice, but teleporting to town is a very minor inconvenience.Overall, this is a great game reminiscent of a SNES or PSX-era classic.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty much what I expected from jRPG. I can guess from where some people have their bad opinions, but I believe that this game is good as it is. There are some things that could be told earlier in the game about the mechanics, or life/time saver improvements. They can be implemented in the future, but they do not have to. My expectation of this game before the release was exactly like it is right now. Sometimes clunky, a beautiful game where you need to micromanage your characters and prepare (or do some grinding) before facing a boss. For example, act III, sometimes you met there a group of 8 monsters with high AGI (they start their turn pretty fast) and have high resistances for nearly everything. Simply put, pain. But after some farm and getting proper skills to manage them, I find them a pretty nice place to farm. A run where I kill 2 groups of monsters (those 8 can spawn there, but they do not have to) within 1 min, can give me from 6 to 16 SP. (Probably there are better places, but this gives me the most fun and probably I am not aware of others)

_childDocuments_.review: Hmm.  First impressions.  It's OK.  It's reminds me of a Vanillaware game, though it's production values are not up to that level.  Day 1 KB/M patch (seriously? you're releasing on PC, it should have been implemented already).  And, the implementation isn't very good.  Just use a controller.Graphically, the art is pretty good, but the animations, like moving around (which is pretty central to the game) are not smooth, a little disappointing especially for a game that relies on its presentation.The game itself is kind of a mash up of 2D RPG combat with platformer movement.  Enemies are visible on the screen and walk up to them to start the turn based battles.  You can also gain preemptive attacks by 'slashing' (a la Shin Megami Tensei IV) before you run into them.Battles seem to be played out in some random order, there are no turn indicators.  You can also swap out characters during battle, which is cool, but you lose that characters turn.Combat is somewhat akin to Octopath traveler, where throughout the battle, you can gain charges that make your attacks stronger.  These charges are global which max out at 9 and any members can use up to 4 or 5 to increase their attacks.Also, during battles, you always seem to be on the right, even if you initiate attacks from the left.  This is minor and I know most games do this.  It just feels more jarring here.Sound effects feel pretty small.  English VA decent.  Japanese VA is good.When using Japanese Language, the characters will sometimes still randomly speak English when not in combat.Music is decent enough.No 32:9 supportThere also does not seem to be a way to Load a save when you start up.  You have to start the game like you're starting a new game, then load.  This is not acceptable.  *looks like it was fixedThere are no settings...oOWatching the broadcast, there seems to be some possible card game mechanic... (honestly, I'm a little tired of card games)Oddities:Ether restores mana (per usual)Omni ether restores party HP (?)Again, it's OK.  A thumbs up for me would be better than 70% (passing).  That said, it's a tentative thumbs up.  Not sure if it's worth $35.  Half off, probably.

_childDocuments_.review: Every decision about this game's design is horribly flawed. It's like someone who never played a game was given pieces stolen from good titles in the past and was forced to glue them together in a room with someone holding a gun to their head.There is no polish. Music consistently breaks in at least three different ways, jumping janks out visually on a consistent basis. The mishmash sorceror's ring/Valkyrie freezing does nothing for the player. The sword swipe outside combat does nothing. There is no balance consideration and grinding is mega grindy. The story isn't a story, it's an outline someone didn't finish writing. I could go on for ages, just... don't support these devs, this is obscene.
_childDocuments_.name: Astria Ascending

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad game but tries to do too much and too little at the same time. A card game, boring side quest, skill trees, jobs, and more. The story was ok, but the delivery and lack of character development made it bland. The voice acting was forgettable. It's a grind fest and felt like a chore. Boss after boss and transformations after transformation. The game had a lot of potential but falls short.

_childDocuments_.name: Astria Ascending

_childDocuments_.review: I like the idea of the game, but i cant help but feel devs run out of money at some point so they had to wrap it up without polish. My main issue would be with boring unlikable charaters in party. They dont have any introduction, there are too many of them, and honestly they look bad visually. Second, whats wrong with painfully slow combat animation? It should be 20-30% faster at least.Art style in general is to my liking, but i dont think i met a single character that i thought 'hey it looks cool'. Barely passable at best.  And then there are some weird design choices. I understand its hard to come up with something original, but a kid with fishtank on a head, some horse-like looking lizard, weird bird-person and also two old dudes in your party... Oh right there is a cat-like race, but instead of sexy kitty girl you get some grumpy cat-man thet looks more like a bear, as party member.Rememberr moogles from Final Fantasy series? Well here we get some creepy weird flying imps in clown hats with annoying voices and manner of speech.Level design pretty bland after first two areas, Canyon and Steppes looks identical. And devs, why  could you put normal mob models on a map instead of boring blue orbs?On a positive side of things, combat is great. Debuffs are meaningfull, some thinking is required, and some boss fights are pretty interesting. Also gear and leveling system interesting enough. Resistances are more important than simple increase to defence. That is bread and butter of the game and that is also why i'm so disappointed in game's many flaws.And one final thing, the person who came up with the map system in this game should never ever work in game industry.

_childDocuments_.review: Listen, I want to like it.  It has a really fascinating core concept (this idea that you get to have super powers for three years so you can defend the world, but then you die) and it even has a female protagonist.  It's turn-based combat.  You'd think I'd be all over this like a sticky bun, but I just can't play it for more than an hour.The art style is so over the top in places that I can't take the world or characters seriously.  I don't know what you call this kind of exaggerated style, but it just looks like something for very young children.  The women's proportions are crazy (not in a sexy way, which would be fine) and the cute characters are so cutesy that they don't look real.  From a gameplay perspective, there are way too many characters with similar abilities unlocked right away, which makes strategy difficult, and the enemies are very spongy.  It's not for me.  But it's clearly a labor of love and it probably is exactly someone else's jam.

_childDocuments_.review: It's crap. There are some cool things, like the class systems and builds and basic mechanics. But the game faceplants in a lot of ways. There's a lot of QoL things we've had in RPGs for a long time now (like being able to equip weapons directly from the store!) no present in this game. The worst part is the story, which dumps a whole group of eight characters on you at once, expects you to absorb a ton of concepts and then moves away. There's fish people everyone's racist against that eat a fruit to survive on land but apparently it's also a sin to not eat it? This is treated like an important thing but it's never explained. None of the characters have any kind of chemistry and the US voice acting is clear, and fine, but they're clearly missing some direction during different lines. Thedre are some things I liked a lot, but its all in a confusing, slightly buggy mess. It just feels bad

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Now that I've finished the game and post game dungeon, I do not recommend this game.Not even on sale. Do not buy.1. By mid to end game, you can basically use 4 characters and ignore the rest. 2. The confusing map and lack of quest objective markers makes this game extremely frustrating. 3. Bugged quests, achievements not registering. -------------------------------------Pros:1. Great art style2. Classic turned based RPG with various classes and skills to learn.3. You start off with all the characters and each have their own skills that will allow you to swap in and out to use their speciality.4. Normal difficulty is just right. Gameplay is not very complicated. 5. You are able to select which stat to upgrade in specific skill tree nodes. 6. Has a token(card) game that is somewhat challenging. To earn cards, beat NPCs or get rare drop from battles. 7. Has a side scrolling shoot-em-up sections.8. Can save anywhere. CONS: 1. No ability to speed up text, speed up game. 2. Dungeon mapping is not very helpful. You will constantly be opening the map to make sure you entered the correct door. 3. There are some overlapping of job classes later one which will make some characters obsolete. 4. Limit breaks (cosmo breaks) are pretty underwhelming.

name: Giraffe and Annika
detailed_description: New DLC Available About the Game Join the cat-eared heroine Annika on her adventures in the mysterious island of Spica! Tasked by the young boy Giraffe, she sets off to find pieces of the stars. Solve the islands hidden mysteries! Adventure! Explore the mysterious Island of Spica! Uncover hidden secrets on the island! Rhythm! Defeat bosses with the beat! Synchronize your attacks to the music to overcome challenges! Comic! See the world of Giraffe & Annika brought to life in beautiful, manga-inspired style! Dungeons! Challenge five unique dungeons on the island to recover the star fragments and help recover Annika's memories! Collectibles! Find cute cat collectibles hidden all over the island! Expand your gallery and unlock prizes! Annika awoke from a strange dream to find herself stranded on the mysterious 'Spica Island'! Upon exploring, she meets a boy named Giraffe, who seems to know her yet she can't remember him at all. Giraffe tasks Annika with finding three special star fragments on the island - Only then will she be able to unravel the mystery! While searching for the fragments, Annika meets Lily, the Witch of the Mysterious Forest! After winning a battle with Lily, Annika uncovers the star fragments and absorbs it into herself. What strange visions will the star fragment grant her? Help Annika as she explores the island in search of the star fragments and her lost memories! What awaits our feline adventurer on this island of secrets?! Annika Annika has lost her memory... But even with such hardship before her the carefree and gentle Anika, along with her little bluebird companion Pipi, go on the adventure of a lifetime in order to discover herself! Giraffe A strange denizen of the island, Giraffe has given Annika her quest to find the missing star fragments. Though he makes a lot of demands, he seems gentle and calm. And perhaps he knows more about the island than he's told Annika... Lily A wily witch that loves to cause trouble for Annika on her quest! She's bossy and loud, but that's what people love about her! She seems to be related to Annika's past, somehow...

_childDocuments_.review: Giraffe and Annika. This is a 3D rhythm puzzle adventure by atelier mimina. At the time of the first announcement, the publisher was UNTIES, but it appears that the publisher was later changed to PLAYISM. The background of this game is about Anika, the girl with cat ears. One day, she woke up and found herself on the mysterious starlight island(Spica). What adventure is waiting for her?In-game 3D and 2D graphics are in the right balance. This game uses Unreal Engine 4, which has a pretty good 3D character design. It's not awkward, it also goes well with 2D graphics. This allows players to venture more immersed in the game world. Story progress is delivered in a comic book(Manga) format with hand-drawn 2D graphics. It gives you the impression that you are watching and playing an animation movie game.The game mood is like a comfortable fantasy fairy tale overall. The game delivers heartwarming things to the player. You are adventurous with a young girl full of curiosity. She is interested in everything and is always alive. As she explores the five worlds, she recovers her memories gradually. The game progress is somewhat linear but not boring. And the puzzles and rhythm difficulty gradually increases. The game itself is not well optimized, but it does not spoil the gameplay. The soundtrack goes well with the rhythm game, and the quality is good overall.Giraffe and Annika. This is a pretty interesting 3D platformer that anyone can enjoy easily. Despite some glitches, this game pleases the player. The cat ears girl, Annika is pretty cute and the adventure with her is fun. The game is designed to start with something small and experience more and more. If you are looking for a fairy tale adventure, this game is for you. Recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Giraffe and Annika

_childDocuments_.review: A really cute mash-up between 3D platformer and rhythm game. Featurewise it's nothing special, but the artstyle and comic sequences are pretty cute and well made. The music is fitting and I haven't encountered any bugs or problems during the time I've played. Also you play as a catgirl which is already amazing on its own.EDIT:Okay now that I have finished the story, this was an amazing game to experience. I loved every single second of Giraffe and Annika. Without spoiling the ending, it was very bittersweet and made me cry, but It also wrapped up the game very nicely. I just wish the game was a bit longer than about 5 hours if I'm being honest.
_childDocuments_.name: Giraffe and Annika

_childDocuments_.review: Been waiting a pretty long time to play this and my first couple hours have been very enjoyable so far.  I got basically what I expected.The trailer says it all- you're a cute catgirl running around a scenic island either fetching stuff, checking out objects, or running around in dungeons with rhythm game boss fights.  The atmosphere is really serene and the music is too. It nails the vibe it's going for, which is an innocent, fairly low pressure adventure with a lot of fine details and wholesome moments to bring it all to life. You find collectibles, unlock art and costumes, gain abilities and items that let you progress--all very familiar elements executed without much friction. It's all in the small details and moments of character interaction that keep you interested in seeing what else is around the corner. Gameplay is mostly simple adventuring, but the rhythm game boss fights are what separates this game from the rest. I've done 3 of them so far, on normal and hard difficulty.  It might feel a bit strange at first, but the trick is to hit the button when the circle lights up and not when it looks like she's soonest able to hit the "notes" with her staff.  After a few tries, you won't really need to look and can do it on intuition. The songs are each a step of difficulty up above the previous--hard mode on the 3rd song was pretty tricky!  So far, they've been pretty memorable and I can tell I'm gonna be sad there's only 5 songs in the end. The secret sauce here is that the main developer worked on Gitaroo Man (PS2), Gitaroo Man Live (PSP), Osu Tatake Ouendan 1+2 (DS), and Elite Beat Agents (DS.)  And the music composer worked on Gitaroo Man and Gitaroo Man Live as well. He also founded Sonica Instruments, music software for Japanese instruments like taiko drums, shamisen, etc.  That's pretty good pedigree for the rhythm action sections! They definitely have that cinematic vibe that all the games mentioned above have, albeit not as crazy since this is a two person team vs. the huge teams those games had.Edit: This was a paragraph about some graphics issues that needed patching, but they knocked that out within 24 hours of the game coming out with patch 1.01. Yay!TL;DR - wholesome and comfy adventure, rhythm game boss fights that elevate the whole experience quite a bit thanks to developer pedigree, and had some day 1 issues that got patched.  Despite the issues, I give it a 914 out of 10.
_childDocuments_.name: Giraffe and Annika

_childDocuments_.review: Fun enough to play for the most part, but do be aware that the game can be a bit annoying. Sometimes when doing the rhythm game fights, you'll have it where you won't go all the way, but will instead stop partway. Another issue with fights is timing as the way the fights are set up make timing harder to judge - the fights would work better in first person VR view than third person flat screen view. Even then, there is a reason why rhythm games typically use linear paths.  Also, same color lights as the background does not help. These factors and a few others combined (such as being unable to pause mid-song (if you pause, you have to restart from the beginning)) can really make the fights annoying.Also note that the game is full of invisible walls. Annoying to die because there was an invisible wall when logically, you should have made a jump, but in reality, you can't make the jump because of an invisible wall. Similarly, later areas have falling tiles and this can be frustrating as sometimes a tile will fall before you've stepped on it because you landed close to it.You'll most likely run two or more saves, splitting first at the point of no return - there is a semi-hidden questline that must be completed before this point, but this can take some time, so you may wish to do this questline separately if you are not confident in your time.The next point where you might want to make a separate save is right after the point of no return. This is a good point to save as this can be another point where you may end up taking more time than intended.Finally, you can also make a final separate save after obtaining the final chest related picture (#30) as there is a save point shortly after. This lets you choose to backtrack and complete everything on one save file and rush the ending on the other. This will allow you to minimize the amount of replaying needed. (You can also set your date to Dec 24 before starting the game to further minimize replaying). The story is mostly predictable and several clues are given to you right at the start, but that isn't necessarily a bad thing.The music is fine, especially in the important parts.A bit of a jarring issue is that the first cutscene uses both 2d and 3d in one panel, so it looks somewhat off.
_childDocuments_.name: Giraffe and Annika

_childDocuments_.review: Not too bad! I do have a couple problems though. It's a game that really holds your hand through the course of its run; it's way too easy to heal yourself, and dying doesn't even really have any consequences. It's also a little unpolished - some of the lighting can look rough and the physics feel kinda clunky. Also some technical hiccups, the biggest one being I've saved my game at the last save spot and can't seem to get back to the main hub world to finish up any of the small stuff like collecting the meowsterpieces, I'm just forced into finishing the game. And a couple other nitpicks, like the boats going too slow, and also I wish there was a button that just let you store food in your bag rather than having to go through the dialogue box each time. But one thing I love about indie games is you can tell when they're a product of love. I can see the effort and charm they tried to put in. I think the story is lovely. The environment is endearing. The rhythm tap bosses are fun. Annika and Lilly are cute. I can tell the devs tried, and I appreciate it. It held me through to the end just fine.
_childDocuments_.name: Giraffe and Annika

_childDocuments_.review: pretty cute, if slightly janky adventure that isn't going to blow anyone out of the water in terms of features, but is enjoyable and cute enough to warrant a try for those interested.The story is a bit confusing, it's all told in Manga cutscenes, and then some cutscenes in game as well.I haven't obtained an attack, but after about an hour - I got a jump move ( lol )Some plot involving collecting magical crystals - and a few dungeons spattered throughout - and that's the jist of Giraffe and Annika.\The main take away is everythign is CUTE!the enemes, the uI, the characters - all flipping adorable.The one VERY standout feature is how battles play out.They're rhythm games, lol.You can see one on the store page, it's a simple setup- but fun nonetheless.The price seems a bit steep, but after messing around with the game pre-release and post rel;ease, it's evident a lot of love and effort went into this.  ( they couldve just slapped the 3D anime ARGG asset pack, but this is UNreal Engine ) Recommended if you want a light hearted romp through famialiar territory with a music game twist for combat.If you have young kids, this might be perfect for them, the difficulty isn't outrageous, the puzzles are not simple, but easy enough for most people to figure out.Got a duaghter that likesd cute things and games? This might be for her.

_childDocuments_.review: Giraffe is a fun game in general but the control become annoying around the ending. The story is interesting but not entirely for children. The graphics are good. I really loved all the 2d illustrations that told the story. The music rhythm fight isn't so great. I mean, even on easy it unforgiving on the timing. The music is great however. The control is something bad at time. The jumping isn't precise. Which became very bad in the last 2 levels. Swimming is slow and fuzzy. I wasn't always impress with some level designs, very unequal. I like the collecting stuff. I give it a 68%. A game for children and maybe a bit for adult. Sadly the controls are missing at times, but overall enjoyable for the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Giraffe and Annika

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really fun. It helped me understand the importance of simple games that focus on specific ideas and don't branch out with an overwhelming amount of things.I like little details like when you learn how to jump, your character alternates which posture they shift their legs and arms to almost like a big jump skip motion. It's cute. Also finding the cute cat drawn art is adorable and very important. The music is nice and it feels good just going back into a game where you know the setting is calm and it won't require too much but still delivers an enjoyable experience for a short time. Games like this are important. I loved running around the island and looking at the sky and moon and anything that's floating and the ocean and watching the time of day change. Also the way you interact with things is adorable like being able to make your character just play on a bongo drum just watching them do it as a random interaction. And seeing the small bird follow you and giraffe around to new areas. Very cute game.It's important to have simple ideas to make cute things possible.
_childDocuments_.name: Giraffe and Annika

_childDocuments_.review: Adorable little game that I thoroughly enjoyed.The story is cute, and the twist at the end was a good touch. The characters are all cute as well.The gameplay was mildly frustrating at times, but nothing that would have caused me to stop playing. The game is largely a platformer with rhythm boss fights. The platforming was a bit awkward at times but nothing game-breaking. The timing of the rhythm segments took me some time to get used to, though maybe I should’ve adjusted the settings instead of leaving on default and that might have helped.Still none of the above issues would stop me recommending the game.It is fairly short and sweet (my first play though blind running about and backtracking a lot took ~6.5hours), but I enjoyed the time and thought it was 100% worth the price tag.Overall I would recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Giraffe and Annika

_childDocuments_.review: Really cute and heartwarming little game mostly about exploring, collecting stuff and interacting with things.The rhythmic boss battles are quite enjoyable and get pretty hard at the end on the hard difficulty.The story is simple at first, but gets quite interesting after a certain point, where you finally start getting some answers about what's going on.The comic cutscenes have a cute art and have a lot of funny moments, the character sprites in dialogue boxes look great too.Oh and I really love the music, fits the game and the mood perfectly.As for the negatives, the most obvious would be the lower quality compared to other games when it comes to certain stuff, like animations of secondary characters or enemies, overall clunkyness (everything feels kinda floaty) and other minor issues.Overall I really enjoyed it.
_childDocuments_.name: Giraffe and Annika

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: adorable and worth every penny!More details:While from graphical/technological point of view, it's not perfect (still pretty nicely done though), I simply loved the game!Presentation, artwork and storytelling are really great, and overall it makes a very relaxing and adorable experience.Collecting stuff was nice and not overdone (like in some other games where you have to collect like 100 items with no or little clues of where to find them), and the rewards were really cute.The rhythm-game was a lot of fun (I'm usually not that much into such games), and even encouraged me to squeeze out a few more points to get all bonus-pictures (and here again the developping studio didn't overdo it, it was manageabledoable in a reasonable time while still being challenging), and I simply loved to look at the cute characters dance (and with increased emotional aspects in the storytelling and athmosphere, I almost needed a tissue - *almost* xD)I loved pretty much every aspect of the game and hope to see more like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Giraffe and Annika

_childDocuments_.review: Been awhile since i am so hooked up on a game and spammed the snapshot key like crazy.This game is relaxing and fun as well as on the right level of challenging. Although the game said it's a rhythm game, it's not really just that, because there's only 5 music track with 5 rhythm battle that works more like a tennis game. The game itself is more like an explore type 3D platformer. Everything is balanced on the casual side so it's not stressful playing any of the challenges in this game even when some part of it does look like Tomb Raider. XDEverything about this game is built full of love and care from its devs, from the graphic to the story to the balance of the mechanism to every single tiny details. So it's really hard not to love this game. Strongly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: I was surprised about how deep the story was, and i really wish i picked this up when it released. The gameplay has everything that i love: Story, exploration, small puzzles, platforming, secrets, and even rhythm. It took me about 5 hours to beat the game, but some of that time was spent working on the extras as i played. Once i beat the game i worked on full completion which is where the rest of my playtime went in to. The only slight problem i had was the controls can be a bit strange at some times, and also i needed to switch to mouse on the final two minecart minigames. _childDocuments_.name: Giraffe and Annika

_childDocuments_.review: A short, but very enjoyable adventure. This isn't a triple-A game, but you can tell that a lot of love went into its creation. Expect to finish the story in under 10 hours, but I'll definitely be playing again. Very satisfied with the experience, and I'm just a little sad that there isn't a new game+, or a way to continue exploring after the credits (you just have to save before finishing the final dungeon as a compromise).The only other thing besides the delightful art that's worth mentioning, is that the boss battles are a simple but pretty entertaining rhythm game, which was a nice surprise.
_childDocuments_.name: Giraffe and Annika

_childDocuments_.review: This is a charming little gem of a game, and I'd strongly recommend it to anybody who's looking for a relaxing, heartwarming experience.Annika wakes up on a mysterious island without any memories, and from there, the goal of the game is to explore the island to figure out who you are and solve its mysteries.  Most of the gameplay is exactly that: exploring the island, talking to NPCs, and solving puzzles.  There are a handful of battles that play out as rhythm game segments, but otherwise there is no combat.  Aside from a couple of platforming segments that took me a few tries, it's an easy game, and that's fine; the atmosphere generated by the music and graphics is comfy and will make you want to just hang out and have a good time with these characters.The worst part of the game is that it's short; it took me about 6 hours to beat it, and I could see myself replaying it to find some items I missed, which I suspect would take me maybe another 4 hours.  Still, I'd rather have a game that leaves me wanting more than one that overstays its welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: Giraffe and Annika

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game because it is so cute...Unfortunately it is also quite boring. Mainly I walked around, did some simple tasks like collect wodden logs or find rabbits... At least your girl gets some additional abilities when you clear a dungeon...The first dungeon had some ghosts, I believe you just have to avoid them, since I was not able to fight. Then there is a rhythm game as boss fight. Did not like that at all...Dialogs are done as comic strips, did not like that at all...
_childDocuments_.name: Giraffe and Annika

_childDocuments_.review: A cute little game with a nice, wholesome story. The boss fights being rhythm based was different and refreshing, the songs were nice too. Now what I was not expecting was for the story to make me cry at the end. Apparently I did not learn my lesson as a kid with The Dog Island on the Wii that wholesome cute games can have strong stories that just make you break out in tears, especially at the end. The ending was beautiful. I recommend giving this little game a chance.
_childDocuments_.name: Giraffe and Annika

_childDocuments_.review: This game is objectively flawed, but personally one of my absolute favorites.A major highlight is its soundtrack - Tomohiro Harada (TOMZUIN H, also worked on Gitaroo Man's soundtrack) has simply done incredible work composing and arranging a soundtrack that gives a sense of 'home' and 'adventure', that goes along so well with the game design of Annika learning about the island of Spica.The clarinet and flute in particular gives the game's soundtrack a unique identity, and sounds very warm in harmony with piano and percussion.While there are flaws to find with both visuals and gameplay, I feel they work well together and gives the game a specific atmosphere and feel. The quickened day-night cycle lets the island of Spica feel more alive while adding to the dreamy, timeless influence on the narrative.This is one of the few games where finding collectibles and secrets feel more engaging and less of a chore, and rewards you multiple times for engaging with it! The rhythm stages also function really well as a reward for completing each 'world' and are among the many highlights of the game.The narrative reveal at the end is also very sweet and goes along with several plot points that the game introduces along the way.A wonderful world.
_childDocuments_.name: Giraffe and Annika

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun charming little game.  The characters were adorable, the story was heartwarming and the soundtrack was amazing!  That being said there were still a few things that disappointed me one being that the 5 bosses in the dungeons were the only rhythm game elements.  I thought the rhythm game element would encompass the game more.  The game really is pretty straightforward with the rhythm games being the only difficult part in terms of S ranking so adding more would definitely up the difficulty as well.  Also I am not a fan of the game not giving a warning that hey you won't be able to go back to finish any small achievements once you reach a certain point so be sure to not overwrite your existing saves since that was my saving grace (otherwise you will have to play a completely new game).  Lastly I am not a fan of games that has a speedrun as one of the achievements since I do not like rushing through games and prefer to take my time and explore every nook and cranny.  Sure I could play the game again from start to finish but I did not enjoy it that much to feel like spending time doing that.  I would still say the pros outweighed the cons for me and would recommend it to any casual gamer to pick up on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Giraffe and Annika

_childDocuments_.review: This is by far the best game I have had the pleasure to play in quite some time.The gameplay reminded me of a game called "Catz 2" for the PS2, which is very nostalgic for me, and I am so happy that I found something similar.I thoroughly enjoyed every second of this game, and I really hope to see more games like this in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Giraffe and Annika

_childDocuments_.review: It's okay for a game about drowning. I died probably a thousand times playing through the story, and can remember almost every individual instance that didn't involve drowning in shallow water because I couldn't find an object or surface to climb onto. Most of the non-drowning deaths were memorable in how brutal they were as game concepts, like being immolated when straying too close to insta-kill volumes like fire or crushed to death by falling boulders. So...definitely not a kids game?In fact, I really grapple with the question of who I would recommend this game . Not to kids, it's too difficult. Not to srs gamerz, it isn't difficult enough. Not to rhythm gamers because there isn't enough of that content. Not to adventure gamers because there are no requisite adventure features like quest logs, maps, or a compass. Not to achievement hunters because the achievements are actual ("beat the game within 4.5 hours") burning ("cleared every hard rhythm game on S rank") garbage (wait until Dec. 24 or 25 for a Christmas achievement!). There's also no combat, which is a plus for me, but... not being able to fight back isn't fun either?But everything is done pretty well! Great animations, good textures and level design that felt believable, nice sounds and music, cool and varied environmental effects, challenging-but-not-annoying collectibles, a good variety of gameplay modes. But removing standard core gameplay features (jump, swim, run) for the sake of making them the exclusive story-progression rewards left a sour taste in my mouth. Then of course the time-gating which seemed only to pay off the bananas-fast day/night cycle was one of my central frustrations with actually playing the game.I was worried when I bought this game that it would feel "cheap" and rigid, but it didn't. The world felt right and I don't regret buying it, but except to myself I still don't know who to recommend this game to.
_childDocuments_.name: Giraffe and Annika

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful little exploration game that takes place on an island with plenty of vibrant characters. The island overworld consists of finding items and exploring as you interact with the citizens. There are several dungeons that rely more on platforming, and they each end with a rhythm game boss fight. The rhythm game fights were really unique, and you can replay them anytime on any difficulty to go for S ranks. Story segments are told through cute manga panels and showcase the detailed character designs. If you don't smile while playing this you have no heart.Also one of the dudes worked on Gitaroo Man
_childDocuments_.name: Giraffe and Annika

_childDocuments_.review: The adventure was fun. Exploration was necessary and fulfilling since the map was very gorgeous (especially White World). The rhythm games were perfectly sized, not too long and not too short, and the tracks were a banger. The story was nice, although the ending was a little confusing.There are some negative miniature details that would probably put people off, such as the walking animation for the bird character, no journal with objectives in case you forgot what to do, and no map either (although I'm fine with it because the area is perfectly fun-sized). It's a slightly weird game, but I enjoyed it a lot because of it. 9/10Edit: Updated for badge

Excellent graphics, controls, music, story, and very fun to play.  The graphics/game remind me of Breath of the Wild mixed with other JRPG elements. _childDocuments_.review: This is the type of game I'd love to see accepted more openly by folk, a very laid-back and ambitious c-tier indie game by a very small Japanese group. A very short adventure across an island inhabited by cute characters, and a story that packs a surprising amount of heat. Exploring this island was a genuine joy. Absolutely wonderful, I wouldn't be surprised if this remains in the top-5 spot on my favourite games from this year.
_childDocuments_.name: Giraffe and Annika

_childDocuments_.review: Had high hopes for this, but the dance sections are irritating and rather unresponsive - probably because there is little in the way of feedback - plus, the 3D view doesn't help.  In addition, Annika seems to have an aversion to responding to long sequences in quick succession.Some of the missions are downright boring (and some are extremely easy to get lost).  Trying to surface out of water rarely works and you end up drowning.You can only talk to characters at a set distance - get to close and it won't work...To top it all off, if you want to get to the end stage to need at least a total of 9 meowstapieces - which could require searching for them.
_childDocuments_.name: Giraffe and Annika

_childDocuments_.review: I was looking forward to giving this a positive review along the lines of "This is the game I wish  was" but the latter half of the game left a pretty bad taste in my mouth. This is yet another on my list of "if I could give this a sideways thumb I would".The game is pleasant enough for what it is. It feels like it was made with a younger audience in mind and I mean that respectfully. The exploration and platforming is a little jank but aside from one or two sections in the final dungeon it works. Collectables aren't overly fiddly either and there's just the right amount of them to not feel like padding or busywork. Its nice to look at at listen to and the characters are cute.Unfortunately the rhythm game sections really bring the game down. I don't know if I just couldn't figure out the right "calibration" setting, or because I was using Steam Input with a DualSense, but from the third fight onwards I was fighting the controls more than the witch. The final boss was unplayable on anything above Easy, even when I bit the bullet and tried with my keyboard. This wasn't helped by the story going from "serviceable, but entertaining" to "???" about halfway through as well. I see what they were going for but it kinda stumbled the landing.All in all it averages out to something... on the better side of mediocre, I suppose? If you want a chill low-concentration thing to putter around in between bigger games or something for a daughter that loves cats and this is on a good sale you could do worse, but the flaws scratch enough to take it from like, a 7 to a 5.
_childDocuments_.name: Giraffe and Annika

_childDocuments_.review: Mark Twain once said, “there is no such thing as a new idea.” That anything original by today’s standard is more of the right combination of pre-existing ideas. Many video games these days are not much different in that regard. We see a mixture of many genres with quite a bit of success like Borderlands, a looter shooter that has adopted some aspects of RPGs into its primarily FPS gameplay, or Dead Cells which has beautifully woven together Metroidvania and rogue-like style of games. This is the direction that I had presumed that Giraffe and Annika are going for. I was wrong, dead wrong. Either that or something went off the rail so much that it strayed from the original intent. Giraffe and Annika, despite its effort to give a cute and soothing experience, comes off as frustrating due to the unsuccessful mash-up of genres or lack-thereof further weighted down by many rough edges of unpolishedness. for full review.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the game and it's definitely more than a cozy little title. It's beautiful, of course, cozy, relaxing, and fun to play. Music is pretty, as well as the characters designs. The thing I liked the most was the little exploration you're allowed to do, with special focus on the swimming mechanic through medium to big banks of water. Playable character stucks here and there, small bugs here and there, and the final boss battles stages offered a challenge for those who decide to take them in the hardest level of difficulty. The only negative aspect of this review lies on that one guy from the development team who was in charge of the render modeling of characters, at least for the playable character, a little girl, and the sailor school costume. I cannot get into details nor elaborate because it's a gross topic but I know more than one out there, including such employee, knows exactly what I'm referring to.All in all, I recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I experienced happiness, then sadness and frustration. Annika is very cheerful and cute and it brings a smile to my face every time she interacts with things, or even stand idle. The puzzles are nice, and collectibles are challenging to collect and complete but not so hard that you feel like giving up. The whole journey was a lovely story and experience, right till the end, then that's where sadness and frustration came in... cuz I suck at the rhythm game and can't 100% all achievements :') But to the developers, I salute making a fun & unique game that's family friendly (non-violent) but also at the same time adults can enjoy (if you like cute stuff). Definitely a hidden & underrated gem that everyone who loves cute anime-ish characters should play!
_childDocuments_.name: Giraffe and Annika

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so CUTE! I thought the story was wonderful and very moving, I may or may not have cried at the end... It's quite a short game, I was able to beat it in about 8 1/2 hours, so if you're looking for something you can beat over the weekend, it's a perfect length. The gameplay was not difficult at all, though I was having odd issues with the left click sometimes not registering, which made for some frustrating attempts at the later rhythm game fights. My friend playing it on controller said they were having the same problem. Thankfully the game lets players try again on easy mode, which was doable even with the dropped inputs.The true strength of this game IMO is the music, which was wonderful throughout, reminiscient of Joe Hisaishi, complementing the game's beautiful visual style, which very much looks inspired by Studio Ghibli.Highly recommended if you're looking for a cute anime game experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Giraffe and Annika

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly did not know what to expect from this when I started playing it, what I thought I was getting was "rhythm game with cute cat girl" ... what I got, "rhythm game with cute cat girl, platforming dungeons and an emotional story".This game was really good, I love seeing smaller games like this that don't try to go crazy as hell with looks, and care more about telling the story or making it fun.Music was nice, game play fun, story well told, game looks fine for it's style, and I left with a bag of feelings I need to go play DOOM to remove ;p
_childDocuments_.name: Giraffe and Annika

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this game actually surprised me with its story ! I was going in expecting nothing more than just a cozy cute adventure, something along the lines of Here Comes Niko, but I ended up tearing up a bit at the end ;w;The game still is really cute and sweet and pretty fun when it comes to exploring and getting to collect stuff and unlock new areas. Got a bunch of comic-cutscenes that I liked a lot and I found most of the OST quite lovely. I do have to warn that platforming (which luckily there isn't a lot of) and rhythm games (which there are even less of) are REALLY janky and take a lot of getting used to. For me personally it didn't make the experience so bad that I'd recommend against playing this game, but I still feel its important to mention that. If you buy this game on sale then it's definitely worth the price !!Lastly can I just say that it's absolutely hilarious how you get to blow up gigantic rocks by shooting at them with a shotgun??

_childDocuments_.review: Giraffe and Annika tells a rather interesting and emotional story through the use of a comic book and in-game events.Devs really put in effort in this one and it shows. The world is adorable and easy to navigate in, the soundtracks are nice, gameplay (while casual and not punishing players much at all for mistakes) is fun, and the rhythm mechanic for boss fights was a nice change of pace from the usual RPG formats.I'm not going to spoil the story here, but I can say it left me feeling a little emotional afterwards, in a good way. It left a sad but ultimately a happy impression on me.I encountered a couple of minor glitches, like Annika getting stuck at one point and a quest dialogue not disappearing when I clicked close at first. The day/night cycle also feels a bit too short so NPC's will run home before I had a chance to finish their quests and soundtracks will switch rather often. Other than that, the game is very solid.

_childDocuments_.review: The good!this game is beautiful and really cute! the majority of the experience was relaxing and the gimmicks of each new dungeon kept its fresh until the end.it ran smoothly and i did not encounter any glitches.the the stuff to collect were a nice touch not only giving some incentive to explore. but also as a bonus unlock a few things.the badthis is completely subjective but the last stage was a little stressful. in a game which was cute and relaxing up to that point. it was surprising.the final (5th) outfit you unlock from the cat pictures person. i was hoping it would have a bonus abilty. like improving dash duration and how fast it recovers.especially after the amazing effect of the 4th and best outfit :)Overalli highly recommend this game to people who just like cute and (mostly) relaxing games.i had a fantastic time! thank you for this!

_childDocuments_.review: A very sweet and charming adventure with a heartwarming story. The island of Spica is full of personality and is a delight to explore, and the dynamic day and night cycle is a really nice touch that plays into more of the puzzles than I expected. The rhythm battle boss fights are the most exciting sections, as the puzzles are quite simple and the platforming is very forgiving, but I enjoyed all of it. While the game is a little rough around the edges with its weird PS1-era collision on objects, I still felt compelled to finish the story and even do a little extra exploring for the "Meowsterpieces", collectable artwork that can really only be described as feline fanart, though none of it is related to the world of Giraffe and Annika oddly enough. I played the game with an Xbox 360 controller which the game has native bindings for, though the camera and movement feel like they would work well on a keyboard and mouse setup. It's rather short, but it doesn't overstay its welcome, giving you just enough new abilities to add variety without making things confusing. That said, I would love to see a sequel with more to do and hopefully tighter mechanics. I would definitely recommend this to anyone who can put up with a little jank, and is a fan of Studio Ghibli, 3D platformers, and adventure games.
_childDocuments_.name: Giraffe and Annika

The further I got in the game the more intrigued I became with finishing it and figuring out what is happening! I would absolutely recommend this game to anyone! Bit of a spoiler here....The game is called Giraffe and Annika. But once you play through the game the name means so much more!!! The name Giraffe makes so much sense lol!

The rhythm game parts are also pretty challenging if you are aiming for S-ranking which I really enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: Lovable, cat-eared Annika sets off on a grand quest on the Island of Spica! 3D adventure & rhythm action genres mesh in the lush, pastoral and beautiful manga-inspired world of Giraffe and Annika.
