_childDocuments_.review: May 26th 2024 - I just wanted to say what a tragedy that this game was ever dropped by DMM. Whatever the reason, the structural design, mechanics and especially visual appeal of this game is utterly brilliant and "Stationflow" remains one of the very few that I have played which is both tremendous fun to play and, despite the issues covered elsewhere here, so totally engrossing. The knowledge that this game is now no longer supported, does not prevent me from experiencing even now a regular surge of affectionate longing to be immersed once again in this game. I do very sincerely miss it, as I said, even today, which underlines, for me at least, the tragedy of its untimely abandonment. Having enjoyed so many pleasurable hours and for such a reasonable price tag too, I shall never be able to hate DMM. I know they will have their own legitimate reasons for leaving the scene, but that cannot prevent me from feeling so profoundly disappointed that they have failed to persevere with this title and so very sad to think of the massive amount of money they have probably turned their back on here. For I remain convinced that today, in light of the massive expansion in popularity of base building, puzzle-orientated  mechanical/social engineering titles "Stationflow" could easily experience a resurgence of popularity and massive sales if only the Developers would return and set about addressing, assuming they are "fixable" some of the issues raised and refining some of the game play to make it even more fun to play.Anyway, I'm neither a masochist nor a sadist, so I'll cease flogging this poor old dead horse any more. What a shame this had to happen to this extremely potential masterpiece of creative game play.===================================================================================== It's a brilliant game with bags of potential and significant Workshop support from good people who have taken time to provide additional station layouts to challenge us and expand our experience and enjoyment.I've changed my rating from recommend to not recommend, purely because as mentioned in other negative reviews here, there exist some pretty integral flaws in the design and functionality of some pretty core game play, elevator behaviour and signage arrangement to name two, which really do need and, I would think, should be able to be corrected.However, the Developer(s), for whatever reason, seem to have gone awol and there has been absolutely no communication or activity from them for a considerable time now, especially given the justifiable issues raised.Shame because it's a refreshing niche they've found here and game play can become pretty addictive, despite the frustrations. Until the Dev(s) resurfaces I feel unable, in good conscience, to recommend this title to anyone else at this time.
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: Quirky and addictive railway station simulator. Impressive work for a single developer. Stable on my machine- i5/gtx1065/16G - but gets a bit choppy with more than 3000 agents on the screen at once. AI pathfinding is OK and you will have to work at getting things flowing smoothly. Pay attention when you walk around your local transport centre and pick up some useful tips!. As in real life it does not seem possible to keep everybody happy all the time.  Minor annoyances.  Clicking on a station improvement could tell how often it has been used, how much money it has made or lost, and percentage utilisation--but for now, we have to guess. Game gets somewhat dull towards the end once you have finally refined your station layout and have nothing to do but watch it run.  Maybe not for everybody but good value if you like this type of logistics simulator.  I have enjoyed my time with StationFlow and recommend it to others
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: STATIONflow is an excellent management game that has all the hallmarks of a classic of the genre. It's very simple to pick up and learn how to play, but gets more complex pretty quickly without ever feeling overwhelming. Once you get into the zone of building, it's hard to put the game down! It's a fun challenge to fit together your station like a jigsaw, and make sure you've left enough space for future expansion. The graphics and sounds are simple but effective, and the UI is very easy to use and read. It would be nice if 'angry' passengers had their 'problem' button above their heads permanently, though, rather than just for a second or two - with lots of passengers it can be quite hard to narrow down which one is having an issue. There's also a lot of content in there, with many different difficulty options and quite a few built-in maps, with the option to even create your own. It also has one of the best path-building mechanics I've seen in this type of game - it's super easy to put together corridors and plazas to the exact shape you want.On the downside, the passenger AI can get a little confused at times. Sometimes that'll be because you haven't signposted locations correctly, but equally I've seen many passengers at completely unexpected areas of the station without any indication (via their needs) of how they got there. It would be great if there was a path showing where they'd come from and where they're going as it would help to narrow down problems you've created. Some kind of overlay showing the busiest areas of the station - so that you could think about creating shortcuts etc. - would be fantastic too.Overall, this is a wonderful little game that I've had a blast playing. Hopefully there will be further updates and expansions in future. I'd also like to see the developer use this template in other settings - an airport, a shopping mall, that kind of thing. If you're into management/building games, definitely pick this up - it's well worth it :)
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: This game practically feels like it was made for me: Design the layout of a subway station, and then evolve that layout as additional lines and connections are added. I've wanted a game like this ever since I walked through the Harvard Square subway station. Traffic is modeled in a very interesting way, and in almost all cases where my riders get upset, it's because I built a bad sign, or failed to build one where one was needed.The different scenarios (layouts) are interesting and present different challenges. The editor makes doing complex, multi-level designs relatively easy. I wish the pacing were a little bit faster... there are a few days that go by with no new connections to make and no new services to provide (and even the services aren't quite as interesting). Most of the time between things to add, I end up having to fix up my connections or add more efficient routes... but there's still a little more time than needed.
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: People are sometimes to slow to get to their destination without getting annoyed, the worst are the elderly and those tourists. And if you forget signage, then they get all in a huff that they don't know how to navigate.Anyways, then I booted up StationFlow, and found that it modeled people quite well. Jokes aside, very good logistics and modeling game of a metro station, and it gives you a ton of overlays to make sure you know where people are moving. A couple snapping issues on the paths, but once you have it happen once, you know to check the sides for the blue dashes. While a random map would be nice, the game instead provides a comprehensive level editor, which makes up for it and more, even if the terminals don't snap.Overall, an incredibly enjoyable game, the time I have spent so far has only been on the tutorial level. Could have longevity issues, but has the aforementioned level editor and difficulty settings should mean this game lasts for a while longer.
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr STATIONflow is a wonderful game about routing visitors through an ever-growing subway system. The more optimal your routes and the better you meet their needs, the happier your visitors are, and the higher your rewards. Excellent building tools and excellent overlays for planning out your routes, and figuring out what is broken and where. I have played 101 hours in 7 days making it a very worthwhile investment. Devs are active in the forums, quashing any bugs we find very quickly. /tl;drIt starts easy. You have 5 entrances to your subway system and 1 train platform. Build walkways. stairs and signposts to connect it all up. The faster you can get visitors through your system, the happier they are. The happier your visitors are, the higher your cash reward and experience gained at the end of the day. Seems pretty easy, pretty basic.Then you level up, and another train platform and another 5 entrances open, and you have to think how to connect all the new stuff to your existing system.Then you start attracting different types of visitors. Tourists have no idea where they are going, so they need information boards. Elderly can't use the stairs, so you'll need to build escalators throughout. Disabled can't use stairs or escalators, so you'll need to add elevators.And your visitors start having needs, so you're going to need to build vending machines, then bathrooms, ticket offices, cafes...All the while you are using amazing overlays to watch everything that's happening, and fix any issues that arise. Select the Happiness overlay to highlight anyone who is unhappy. Click that person and a frame pops up with all their info: their origin, their destination, their traits and their needs. Hmmm, looks like this guy couldn't find food between Exit A1 and Train P2. Clicking the origin or destination on the visitor's frame will jump the map to that location so you can get a quick view of his path. Hmm, looks like he should be near a cafe between those two points. Jump to A1. Bring up the pathing overlay and select P2 and you see which signs he followed and where they led him. Oh, I see. He couldn't actually see the cafe from there. Let me add a sign so all future people taking that route know there is a cafe around the corner.So it starts simple, and slowly gives you more and more to deal with. The difficulty increases at a nice pace, and you alternate between building new stuff and optimizing paths to your existing stuff. For anyone who loves building and optimizing, and having great tools to help you do both, this is a must-buy.Minor complaints:1. My crappy old AMD FX-8350 Black struggles if I play in double or triple speed once the subway gets full-size, but plays fine in normal speed. It probably plays better on a strong single-core proc.2. You can't disable the various types of snapping while you are building, so it can be difficult to get pieces to attach in places that are asymmetrical. That's probably a big pro for some people though :)
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: Been lost in Tokyo Station irl I must say this game finally tells me how I was came to that place.  I can't believe I have spent 7 hours in putting up roads and updating signs when each exits turns up. This game, generally isn't that difficult as imagined but is definitely challenging when you bumped into   "how to make this better" situation .
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: I like it a lot so far. The aspects I enjoy most are the planning and optimization as well as the challenge of redesigning present structures to accommodate for new requirements.Still, I have a few gripes with the game.There is a bug where escalators detach and move away from their intended position which seems to be only cosmetic but it's pretty obvious, so I think it'll be fixed relatively soon.I would like the game to use my hardware more efficiently. With ca. 2k Passengers in the station on speed 2, the game stutters a lot with only one CPU core being maxed out and the others still idling. In the day and age of consumer CPUs with a minimum of 6 cores, this is just sub-par. Sadly, this is quite unlikely to be fixed this late in development, so I suppose it isn't really possible to build a very high volume station with < 3k passengers and still have the game playable, maybe even at default speed.
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: STATIONflow is one of those games where you sit down to solve a simple problem for an hour or so, and before you know it, it's 4 AM and you've only just started optimizing the flow of travelers through your station. Well worth the asking price for a seemingly simple game with an interesting amount of depth to it.
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible.  Might be one of the best simulations I've ever played, definitely the best since Cities:Skylines.  It's like Mini-Metro++ DX Hyper Extreme Championship Edition.  I wish I didn't have to go to sleep.  I will be dreaming about this game tonight (and likely for many more nights to come).
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little puzzler that appears simple at first and even on the first world, starts to grow more complex as you "level up" and need to include different facilities and connections. Simple poly graphics help to give it a clean look, although maybe the option to show a textured view of your creation would be nice, and heatmaps of where people are getting stuck or where the throughput is highest perhaps.Couple of minor issues with people who don't seem to follow signs right in front of their faces, or people entering the station through an entrance and wanting to leave via another street entrance, or even the same one - weird behaviour. I'm sure it'll get fixed.
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: STATIONflow is a game developed and published by DMM GAMESThe game offers some nice graphics, although some ugly glitches here and there, it is pleasant all the sameSTATIONflow overall, however, is a fun game to play, and it does get boring if being played for a long time, but is a very good simulation game and to play in short bursts!
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: It is surprisingly fun to build a station, own your choices and rebuild as the flows grow. Finances in the game are little bit flat and could use some depth and more dynamism - currently quality inspection awards are dominating the income stream which makes sense on some level. But on another level it leaves hunger for more, especially given how fun passengers are and how satisfying it is to satisfy their needs. Do try it!
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! As your station and the passenger flows get bigger and bigger it gets more and more challenging to keep everything running efficiently. But when it does the endless flows of passengers are quite mesmerizing to look at. Very clean and abstract shapes yet very recognizable.Did you open up a new platform? Then don't forget to update all the signage or people won't be able to find it and get angry. And they have a funny way of letting you know ;)
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: If you like any building games, you should play this one. It's optimized for people who like to optimize.Something this game does really well is the progression mechanic, which avoids the thing in some other games where you just get exponentially more money as you scale and the difficulty goes away. It isn't perfect, but it is fun.
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: Very pretty, very easy to operate, very addictive!The open ended planning makes STATIONflow a designer's dream.One con, but only one, is the lacking geometry tools that the design minded players would demand. It is not a detriment to the game, just annoying when walkways and stairs can't be perfectly centred on a platform, for example.A toolchest of customised blocks of assets to drop in would be nice too, but if not managed well this can be more annoying than always building from scratch.Would play again, 7/5.
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: An addicting metro simulator with a nice minimalist aesthetic. Easy to learn with steadily increasing challenge of more commuters traveling to their needed destinations. Would be nice to see an overall stat screen of how certain buildings (restaurants, bathrooms, info, atm, etc) compare to the rest of the station. Perhaps after the budget screen shows up at the end of each stage.Overall this is definitely an easy recommendation if one enjoys Mini Metro and simulation games.
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: Review after 20h playtime at level 24the good things:-the minimalist design helps the player stay focused on the routes each passenger can take-since the passengers aren't fully animated they traverse the map fairly quickly, which can make even 700 seem quite a bit when looking over the map-the passengers have different walking speeds-they clearly emote when you have forgotten a info on a sign- you are forced to design for elderly and disabled peoplethe bad things:1. the stores and utilities you can place in your station is fairly limited and feel unenjoyable (toilets, restaurant, atms & bank, info point, self service ticketing...)no electronics stores, cafes, bakeries etc. pp2. you can't clone items or surfaces3. there is no greenery to fill empty spaces and or benches where people can sit, to seperate traffic flows -> you have to leave gaps or rather erect new corridors if you intend to manage your passengers this way4. in planning mode, you can't group and move objects together5. very annoying -> you can't color code areas, which results in that you have to touch up EVERY sign since the game already gives the predetemined exits letters AND colors. More useful would be a system that determines the level (1/2/3/4...)of the exit and I color code the area (A- blue, B - green, C pink... etc), this way when a new exits pops up with a new line, I don't have to go through all cardinal directions and touch up the signs to show there is a new series of exits F or G, which if absolutely irrelevant for the player...6. Obstacles aren't a thing, the only obstacles you get are giant rocks in the ground and a river in one map...7. personally I don't like that we only get one type of escalator, I would wish for one with a tiny bit steeper angle 8. When placing a ground tile, you can't rearrange the four end points, when you all rotate their position by 90° it seems to fail9. There floor tiles come with only 4 adressable points to change the angle, which since you can't clone objects, covering area is very tedious, especially if you don't want just squares and rectangles (the hexagon surface has a similar problem to 8.)...10. after the first 15 levels it doesn't feel like game has an challenge left for youFun for about 15h, would give it a score of 7.2/10 currently
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: Addicting game, quite a bit of stuff to keep on top of and keeps you thinking how to make the station layout better which are the biggest things about these games right? So yeah it's highly recommended if you like these types of games. But it's seems too easy imo, I've not checked other maps or difficulty sliders other than the default though. It just gives you too much time between it adding more platforms and entrances for you to watch, there should be new platforms or entrances daily so you barely get time to handle the previous additions before it suddenly chucks on more things for you to juggle. Instead it adds platforms or whatever, then you quickly edit the station to handle them and fix any problems, then you still have a few days before it adds more of them. Money isn't a problem either, I've not looked at my money once because it just keeps going up by huge amounts, this can be changed in the difficulty though. BUT the difficulty settings can't be changed mid save so I'd have to scrap my 4 hour station and start again with harder money options or whatever.Basically it's a great game but it seems like im playing in sandbox mode sometimes because money and time isn't an issue really. The other maps and settings might fix that though. I want to be worried about looosingggg.
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: Unbelievably good, and very impressive addictiveness/replayability for an indie 1.0.0 early release. I'm a huge fan of transportation and tycoon games, and while I enjoyed Overcrowd it didn't quite scratch the "itch". Here comes STATIONflow, where the goal is to shepherd passenger from trains to exits and vice-versa. Build concourses, corridors, stairs, escalators, elevators, complete with signs so passengers don't find themselves lost. Different passengers have different characteristics; commuters walk fast and know where they're going; tourists are slow and misread signs; elderly people are very slow and cannot take stairs. It's all brilliant with simplicity, and the progressive extension of the station with new exits and platforms leads the player to build a multilayered ant farm, organically reproducing the layout and structure of real world subway stations. Amazing stuff!
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: This hidden gem is a management game that successfully walks the line between zen relaxation and chaotic scrambling as the game introduces new challenging mechanics. It also avoids the pitfall of having only one true solution to its puzzles, another challenge for management games. I don't know what motivated DMM Games to leap into such a different genre of game, but I hope they stick with management as I have no interest in Anime dating sims.
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: Great idea, this game has huge potential! I had a lot of fun for a couple days and look forward to additional levels and challenges. Potential developments:- Platform construction: More control about where exactly new platforms are built (for example, level, entry point and exit point on map are defined, exact position and layout can be defined by the user)- Introduce curved platforms- More shops and infrastructure (people go to train stations for shopping)- Differ between public sections (accessible for people just walking through the session or going to shops and restaurants) and transportation section (where people need a ticket)- Add need of renovation (depending on infrastructure type, size etc. renovation is needed every x days)A huge pain, and the only downside of the game, is the massive micro-management when adding new directions to signs. Especially after adding new platforms, this is too much. A way of avoiding this might be adding a tool for "auto-updating specific goals to all or a certain group of signs" and simply base this on distance (nearest ways). That way, the player then just adapts signs where he wants to lead visitors through other ways.Keep going, nice work!
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: Really nice flow efficiency/optimisation game.Early access atm means theres only the one map available at the moment. and the level progression is very same-y. Level up, you get another 1 platform and 5 exits.If the developers get sensible randomisation working in this for map generation, this will be one of those games you can keep coming back to forever.
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: I love planning/design/logistics games and this one shows a lot of promise. The difficulty is well balanced making a progressively more complex and challenging game. I appreciate being given time to solve problems little by little without fear of losing the level or going bankrupt. It's easy to lose a lot of hours chasing passengers and fixing problems! Controls are intuitive and easy to learn.Occasionally have issues with reading coloured text on a coloured background for entrance numbers and info boxes can obscure objects you're trying to interact with requiring you to swing the camera around to a better angle, particularly in the building phase.
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: Fun unique "tycoon" style game. Really enjoyed making my own metro station! Plus as you play you get more and more to build. I am at level 20 and it seems like there aren't new buildings after that which is a bummer. Overall still a lot of fun, love seeing crowds of people walk around through the station.
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: i purchased this game thanks to the 'lets play' series by Sampstra Games.  while this is an early access review, i think that the developers have been able to demonstrate proof of concept, as well as show a development road map for the future.  so far i've had a lot of fun and look forward to watching the development cycle of this game.
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing! I love the idea and execution, nice graphic choice ads a bit of charm to this game.Even though I recommend this game, I must say to not buy it yet for multiple reasons. Wait until alpha/beta ends.1. Game is poorly optimized (CPU bound) - In the beginning, there are no issues at all, but once you reach the current end game with 8-10 stations game starts to get choppy. This is especially seen when building. This is most likely due to how pathfinding works in this game and a need to rebuild the whole map. I wish to keep building onto the map but its lagging more and more.   (Recommendation for developers - Develop your own A* for pathfinding and divide the whole map into chunks. If you would still need to rebuild navmesh, it will be much faster to rebuild just a small part. Also do not calculate paths for all agents at all times, do it X agents per frame and disable agents until it reaches the destination or collides with something)2. There is only one map - Developer said that there will be more maps (random possibly) after release3. UI gets in a way of the game, especially signs - This is annoying since you can have multiple stairs next to a sign or two where all needs to have 5 stations directions, 4 exits and all amenities. This view should be contextual, also some tool where you add the same signs in the area, or UI is smart and merges all neighbor's signs.4. There is no "overview/statistics" of your station - Your passengers complain about the lack of X, so you see details of this given guest and let's say he wanted to get from D1 to D4, but he is on the other side of the station! Nowhere near D exit... At the summary screen, you see that you lack medical buildings. But you have no idea whether its lack in capacity or signs are misleading, or passengers are dumb.5. There is not a measurement tool. - If you want to find the closest exit to a given sign you better have good eyeballing skills or else your guests will be complaining about the long time spent on stations.6. After 10 hours there is nothing more to the game, new maps would solve part of this equation but stuff like research trees, multiple stations to manage, more "needs" like benches or cleanliness7. And last, balance. The game currently is not balanced and the difficulty is progressively easier as you play, there is no challenge after 10 exits and you pretty mutch play sandbox with extra steps.Overall if you can stand all of the above issues you have around 10 hours of solid gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: Really great game for those who like efficiency and optimization. I've logged 11 hours so far and will surely play more.The game runs well, is very stable and no bugs so far.Tip: go easy on the signs- they'll drive you mad as the game adds more entries/platforms and you have to go around updating all 200 of them to include them.
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! It's so much fun and so rewarding to design for efficient passenger flows. I can see the game still needs polishing but already I find it difficult to stop and I long for more whenever I do. What a great game. I'm already dreaming of expansions in which I can design flows for indoor or outdoor events. Enough for now, I've got to get back to tinkering with my station.
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: For an early access game, it's looking pretty good, and I'm looking forward to the final product. Recommendations for the developer:First, some of the mechanics aren't intuitive. For example, can I stack an elevator on more than two levels? One would think, or you'd have a very inefficient stacked elevator system. I know this game is still receiving ongoing updates, and it would be great if you could focus on mechanics like that.Second, I would LOVE if more than one map became available. That would greatly enhance replayability.That said, this game is looking pretty great. I highly recommend for anyone who likes to devote a couple hours at a time to perfecting the art of commuting and figuring out just how many cafe seats you need to meet commuter demand.
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game!!  It's in early access, and so far I haven't had any lag, and I've had no crashes which is a plus.I think however there may be pathfinding issues, unless those are intentional I'm not sure.  And the only other issue I'm having is how fast you upgrade.  It seems to move at a fast pace which I like taking my time, being able to watch what's going on and then upgrade.  I feel like I'm being rushed as I'm playing.  Anyway,  I'm sure the more the game progresses the better it will get.  I love the concept of it all, and I totally recommend this to anyone who might be on the fence about getting it, THIS game is worth getting for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: Great game alltogether, starts really easy and relaxinf with some relaxing music, but rather quickly difficulty rises, and (at least for me) by reaching lvl 10 i start feeling how my brain melts a little with all that planning of effective ways to make a way for all those people and with all those additional restrictions.Definetly worth a try.
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: Great idea for a game. It's got that 'Early Access Feel' to it but that's to be expected. The tutorial is good although additional hints may be required before final release. It feels a little easy at the moment, and without knowing how many levels there are i'm not sure how far into the game I've got already. It may be good to consider some form of progression system. I've also accrued lots of money yet despite this I've got the option to take out loans... can't see the need for a loan if you're playing well.Looking forward to seeing how this develops.
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: StationFlow is a very satisfying and well-done traffic management game - bravo to the creators, I'm an instant fan. The game combines elements of 3D puzzles, planning & strategy, traffic management, simulation, and (to a small extent) tycoon genres.Looking forward to see what improvements the creators make to the already great early access release. See the discussions page for my suggestions on how to make the game even better!
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that fills a niche and I'm loving it! It feels a bit like Software Inc. but for metro stations. Two things that I'm missing are:- A way to rotate objects via the keyboard (perhaps m and n like in Transport Fever).- Data views; it's all fine and dandy seeing people move around but we need some data views to see where the pain points are.Special note: I love that this game has wheelchair users in it! One of those little touches that shows that the dev(s) care about everyone.Keep it up!
_childDocuments_.name: STATIONflow

_childDocuments_.review: STATIONflow is a game about controlling the flow of thousands of passengers by building and managing an efficient underground train station.

name: The Artful Escape
detailed_description: On the eve of his first performance, Francis Vendetti struggles with the legacy of a dead folk legend and the cosmic wanderings of his own imagination. In an attempt to escape the musical legacy of his uncle, a teenage guitar prodigy embarks on a psychedelic journey to inspire his new stage persona, searching for who he isn’t in an adventure spanning stolen opera houses, melodic alien landscapes, and the impossible depths of the Cosmic Extraordinary . Starring voice performances by Michael Johnston, Caroline Kinley, Lena Headey, Jason Schwartzman, Mark Strong, and Carl Weathers. KEY FEATURES: * A story about great expectations, towering legacies, aliens, folk music, guitar solos, making stuff up, and living your dreams like memories. * Musical jams. They’re visceral. They traverse dimensions. * Craft your own stage persona from the sci-fi beginnings of your backstory to the trim on your moonboots. * Converse, consult and chill with all manner of beings: disenchanted publicans, nostalgic villagers, lumbering alien wildlife, and reality-defying behemoths. * Shred, soar and dance across the multiverse. Traverse landscapes made of sound -- composed by your movement -- as if the world itself were an instrument.

_childDocuments_.review: I ignored this title multiple times but it kept popping up. 'Too musical, too artsy, too colorful - too much of a psychedelic cup of tea for my taste', - I thought. But initially, I gave in. Two points made the difference: 1) Annapurna Interactive - BEASTS and BEST in this industry. They publish excellent, amazing titles or at least very good ones. 2) Line of dialogue from the trailer:  I repeated those words in my head and it clicked. Gut feeling or something? Not sure, but I was intrigued. Wishlisted. Dunzo. Oh, and it's hard to ignore a company named 'Beethoven & Dinosaur', right?Queen, 70-80s music, Firewatch game (great outdoors, folk music in the background, Colorado) and, unsurprisingly perhaps, Bill & Ted's Excellent Adventure movie (1989).  filled with references and inspirations, from David Bowie to Stanley Kubrick and Wes Anderson. I felt The Matrix and Marvel (Guardians of the Galaxy) influence. I'm sure there's more to it.Oh, and the weirdest thing, for me anyway. The first character you meet, a girl (with my *click-bait* line), was named EXACTLY like the first girl I fell in love with, as a kid. What are the odds? Her name is uncommon so I was a bit bewildered. But hey, enough indulging around my fantasies - let's dive deep into mechanics and story.  That's how Johnny Galvatron, main developer, described the core gameplay of . I can hear your 'huh?' in the background so allow me to explain how I experienced it: a sweet cocktail of walking (or, rather running) sim + simple, forgiving platforming + rhythms elements from Guitar Hero games. Remember those? Where you had to carefully, in precise order and harmony, connect buttons to emulate the tunes of famous bands and musicians? Same mechanic applies, but in a more simplistic, primitive, and non-punishing way. You follow the sequence of notes, but you are free to maintain your own rhythm if that makes any sense? Notably, music  the main essence of the game. It's the heart & soul, as well as the language you use to speak, jam, and interact with environment. It's your sword and shield and Nietzsche's words come to mind: 'Without music, life would be a mistake'. And all the inhabitants & cosmic creatures you'll meet live accordingly to that motto. Party on, dude!   How does it feel to play tho? In short: peculiar!'We wanted the shredding of the game to feel powerful and effortless, the same way some games depict a mastery of combat' quote by Johnny G. - and I would apply this to entire gameplay. It feels immersive and rewarding - your character is a guitar prodigy after all. Strumming, wailing, shredding, and even twinkling - yes, I collected all the words I know about guitars! Jokes aside, it feels satisfying. Simplicity is a strength here, unless, of course, you want to play some Dark Souls-type of rhythmic game. : if you're lookin' for some hard-core platform mechanics, challenges, and/or 100+ tune sequences to strum your fingers off, you may want to look the other way. There's one button to use your guitar (you can use more sometimes, but game won't tell you this, so experiment) + boss jams sessions. They can get a lil intense, but that's about it. If you want to suffer, truly - play 'Crypt of the NecroDancer' instead.  is more about EXPERIENCE, than gameplay. It may or may not resonate with your gaming soul (or preferences).  What about visuals? Just take a look at screenshots! The game is made in 2D, but hot damn, it's the most marvelous, majestic, phantasmagorical, and fabulous 2-D in your life! Once you get out of the base location, the stuff gets . I was 'WOAH-ing' in unison with the main hero: locations, vistas, all the impossible creatures - my jaw was permanently at the floor through the entire game! And in combination with the soundtrack, which is ever-present, and your own jammin' it's like a magical candy you cannot stop eating. I think, my brain produced more dopamine during those 5-6 hours of playing than through the entire week - every cell of my body was literally vibing in coherence. It's just that good.But it wouldn't be THAT good without the third ingredient - . And the art of telling this story to the audience.The writing in this game is sharp and exceptional. Poetic dialogue will easily capture your attention and cast of professional actors - we're talking Hollywood-big - made the game feel like top-quality interactive movie where you happened to be the main hero.Remember that line that sold me the game? ? The more you play, the more you realize that the entire game is a literal . You can customize many elements of your stage persona, such as name, home, backstory, special event, and even appearance! From socks to haircut - I spent an HOUR crafting a Star-Lord costume! Stage name goes first, naturally, and it's unleashed my inner joy! It's of two parts: 1) predetermined adjective 2) type whatever word/name you wish. Scrolling through peculiarity of pre-set variants (some of them are so far out!) the word *PURPOSE* pops up and it lights up my brain like it's Christmas already. Being madly in love with Loki Disney+ tv series, () it immediately clicked. Glorious Purpose is my stage name! Best part? Your character would say your name out loud multiple times during the game. Every time I'd hear  every fiber of my body would scream in ethereal joy!  ***You ever had a feeling that some game was made just for you or that it speaks directly to your inner kid, who was craving attention since forever and you've always ignored him? And all of sudden you've connected to this kid again? Well, this is a slight understatement of how I feel about . Music, visuals, Shakespearean-like dialogue.. it's mesmerizing and all, but there's something more about this game. The existential crisis main hero experienced spoke volumes to the one I'm going through, making me question everything. To own who I am, to have the courage to stand my ground. Delightful. Gloriously purposeful.: You've heard of 'video games are a form of art' thing-y? I always doubted it, but  might just be that piece of art we all need. To discover who we are not, and to go on a journey to become someone else. Entirely.Worthy to mention:-- One of the characters looks like Morgan Freeman and is voiced by Carl Weathers (Greef Karga, The Mandalorian)-- Johnson Vendetti, legendary uncle of the character you play, is based on folk music legend Bob Dylan-- You can turn audio settings up to 11, instead of the common 10. 11/11!-- You can ride a GIANT turtle while jammin' on their shell-- You can pet a dog!To wrap this 'essay' up: Johnny Galvatron, Beethoven & Dinosaur team - thank you SO very much! Couple of musicians from Melbourne made a top-quality video game, that is actually so good, that I honestly want a sequel, prequel, or any kind of -quel! I just want to experience this musical mischief for the first time ever, again. It's one of my fav games now. GOTY material even.To the wonderful few who're still reading - so much LOVE for you! ~ Appreciate your time and attention! Go discover your glorious purpose and be excellent to each other. ~PS: In the trailer, main character was rollin' down the hill on a skateboard, but the feature was cut off before the release. Make it happen, Johnny G! Skateboard and Jam!PPS: My GOTY. Miss you Francis ~

_childDocuments_.review: The Artful Escape is a mind-bending adventure containing platforming and memory elements.Francis Vendetti, the nephew of famous folk singer Johnson Vendetti, is about to perform in his first concert. The townsfolk of Calypso have long been looking forward to hearing Francis play his uncle’s greatest hits.On the eve of the concert, Francis encounters a girl called Violetta who senses that he is having an identity crisis. Does Francis really want to live in the shadows of his uncle or does he want to emerge and forge his own destiny? Violetta summons Lightman, the greatest guitar player in the Universe, and together they embark on a psychedelic trip through the cosmos, meeting strange alien life forms and visiting faraway planets to share their musical vision.It felt like a mixture of Bill and Ted, The Beatles’ Yellow Submarine and Monty Python rolled into one. The production value was immense with wonderful voice acting and incredible visuals. It was an assault on the senses for five hours and never let up. Wielding his mighty holographic electric guitar, Francis is able to literally light up environments with his playing. Animals emerge from holes; lights get brighter; and alien life forms dance as he slides down slopes and jumps over chasms whilst playing. His music is a catalyst for hope and regeneration and it is wonderful to watch. I would recommend playing guitar as much as possible as it can produce some interesting spectacles in the background. Unfortunately, it does make the platforming a little more cumbersome, as you must hold down a controller button, and sometimes playing riffs interferes with the ambient music in the background; Sometimes it compliments it and other times it clashes.The platforming elements are very easy and won’t challenge. On occasion you will die, but the respawn is so generous that it keeps the intensity high and never causes frustration. The platforming elements are purely there as a vehicle to break up narrative sections of the game.There is an array of characters to meet, and they are all incredibly original and imaginative. The main characters are noticeably performed by some famous actors, and although this doesn’t always guarantee success, in this case it is done superbly.The dialogue is not only inciteful but it is marvelously witty. I laughed out loud on a few occasions and felt like I had a smile on my face throughout the game. It is full of little touches of genius and clever exchanges.The story is quite deep and meaningful for such a zany production. There are moments of drama, regret, and emotion, and the characters are well developed for such a short excursion. It has all the ingredients to make a decent story, and embellished with the spectacular visuals and sound, it produces a memorable experience.There is an element of memory recall in the gameplay, much like Simple Simon, where you have to repeat sequences. This may stump younger players as it can be quick and relatively difficult, but if you make a mistake, it is very generous in giving you another go, until eventually you will succeed.The gameplay involves platforming, memory recall, narrative and dialogue exchanges.The Artful Escape is essentially a narrative driven adventure but the story is broken up with the following mechanics.There are platforming sections, usually on the way to meet a character or find a mysterious place. Francis can jump, double jump and perform a slight hover whilst trying to leap over chasms. They are generally easy to navigate and rarely will you need more than a single jump. Larger gaps may require you to use a double jump and then a hang to make it. You also slide down slopes, gathering momentum and you can jump higher if you bounce on certain objects, like mushrooms.Whilst performing platforming you can play your guitar which grabs the attention of the local inhabitants and brings the environments to life.During your quest to find yourself, you will encounter creatures that challenge you to guitar showdowns, where you have to repeat the riffs that the creature performs.Using your controller or keyboard you have to use five different buttons and match their sequence. Sometimes, there will be two notes played together and even three notes simultaneously.The intensity and the longevity of the sequences increase until they are defeated.Behind the musical extravaganza is a wonderful story and often you will converse with weird and eccentric creatures.Luckily, they all speak your language and you are given dialogue options to respond. The choices don’t really matter though so pick the funniest ones and don’t worry about the consequences.I'm not usually bothered about designing my character but there is a fun and creative opportunity to redesign your look with a vast array of different clothing items and accessories, as well as your hair and makeup.Visuals are nothing short of spectacular with explosions of color everywhere. Characters are incredibly imaginatively drawn and there are copious amounts of opportunities for screenshots.The environments, locations and buildings are wonderfully crafted with a futuristic feel and cosmic attitude.A music game wouldn’t be any good without good sound design and this game has it all. Amazing voice acting from every character, with some household names performing voiceovers, and an outburst of guitar riffs and musical compositions that are relentless.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those few art experience kinda games that swing well above its weight class. Think GRIS, Hellblade, Outer Wilds. The big difference that I think is the main reason that Artful Escape doesn't have nearly as much recognition as it deserves, is that I loved my time with it, but if you aren't looking for something that *is* a walking sim, I might pass on this. Don't pass just yet, though.Calling this a walking sim is extraordinarily reductive and disrespectful to the effort that went into making a gorgeous experience.Lets start with the 2 biggest wins, audio and visuals. First and foremost, stop reading for half a second and go up to look at the game's description to read the voice acting cast. Yep, that is Carl ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Weathers. Thankfully in the last few years good voice acting is becoming more common place, but this is a rare instance of phenomenal voice acting. It helps tremendously that the voice cast had a lot of really solid material to work with too, as the writing chops on display by this team's writers room is impressive to say the least. All of the dialogue is perfectly oblique in a way that suits the very acid trip-like story going on.Which brings me to the next dub, visuals. There was no portion of this game that wasn't gorgeous. Seriously, even the "boring" parts are still wonderfully realized, and I think that by focusing less on the character models by making them side scrolling and very puppet like in their animation, the team was able to focus on putting those characters in an obscenely beautiful world. Well, a lot of worlds, the whole game is very out there (as in space).The cover art for this game is actually surprisingly on point with showing exactly whats in store for you. The Artful Escape is the story of a young artist reaching through the expectations set of them to find what they want to be, and it takes place in the middle of this epic sci-fi rock opera. Lasers, light shows and a guitar soundtrack that Steve Vai and Joe Satriana would be proud of. The screenshots and even trailers for this game do not do justice to the truly zany 5-ish hour experience of having to put on the best show in the galaxy and let loose some sick riffs on your magical electric guitar.The sad part is that this game really is, as one other reviewer put it "closer to simon says than Guitar Hero".Thats where it probably loses a lot of people. It didn't really detract from my experience, I was more enamored with the visuals and music going on than looking for challenging rhythm game gameplay, but again, if that is what you expect going in, I totally understand how you might be frustrated.Marketing for a game like this has to be a nightmare for Annapurna because its so weird and different from so many things out there, and its difficult to say "just trust me bro" about a game, but that seriously is the best thing I can say to people who are really on the fence.I review tons of games, I play tons of games and have quite a bit of experience with both amazing, must play and absolute dumpster fire games. This is pretty up there as an experience, and if you treat it as an experience instead of a game I think you'll find a lot of fun here.And come on now, its Carl ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Weathers, what else do you need??Thats all, thanks for reading, and be sure to follow my curator page for more reviews.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This game is definitely more of an experience than a game. If you prefer more gameplay oriented games, then this might not be your cup of tea, but if you like beautiful visuals, a fun and engaging story, and good adventure vibes, buy it right now without any hesitation. Even if you do prefer more gameplay oriented games, I would still recommend getting this game 'cause hey, it doesn't hurt to try something new. Anyways, I'm off for another tour of the Cosmic Extraordinary, I hope I see you in Calypso when I get back :)

_childDocuments_.review: I play Guitar, I compose Music, I am a lifelong Gamer, I love weird stuff and I own a Masters-Degree in Media-Design. None of these facts makes me especially able to judge this Game, but they seemed to yell at me, that i should absolutely love it. Yet I feel compelled, to not only write a review, but the first negative Steam review i have ever written, about how much i hated it. First and foremost the thing most other critics have pointed out: The Gameplay is practically nonexistent! This is often the Case in "Playable Story Games", but i feel it's outright damning for a Game about the "Freedom of Artistic Expression". The Story tries it's hardest to drive the point of "Making the Music you wanna make" into your brain, only to then go on, to limit musical expression to "Hold X to shred Guitar" and "Play Simon Says", while also omitting any rhythmic Element from the music it forces you to play.As everything is supposedly about music and composition, there is a whole other harmonic can of worms to be opened. There's a main crux with the way the game wants you to "Play the music by holding X" at any time. Because when you do, random, generic pentatonic licks will sound layered over the background instrumentals. The Issues with this are that A: Pentatonic licks that sound good with everything will also sound incredibly generic, no matter what you do and B: within the 1st Minute of Playtime you know all the games music.The Story is what you would expect and while it's servicable, it's also extremely predictable and overloaden nonsense at times, to the point where all i could feel was: "Whatever, Man". While the story does suggest a development in terms of Genre and certain harmonical epiphanies of the main character, the music just stays mostly the same for the entire Game. Your Character is a "Shred God" From Minute One anyway, yet somehow needs some elaborate Stage Persona and convince cosmic beeings that he is great by stacking random Electric Lead Wankery on Top of each other, mimicking what they show him? Give me a break and go gently ♥♥♥♥ yourself. Don't get me wrong: The Visuals and Designs are absolutely fantastic, but this means that the whole Game ultimately feels like a bunch of Painters made a Game about Guitar-Playing and were shocked that neither the Game nor the Guitar Playing ended up beeing Fun or even sensible. It's baffeling how a Game about making Music Ends up beeing a purely visual spectacle and pathetic on the musical surface. Yakuza's Karaoke Singing has more musicality than this Game. And don't get me started on how the Lipsync is extremely bad and the Hand/Finger Movement not even remotely has anthying to do with the audible Guitar Playing.To get back to my Introductory Statements: I am probably mostly infuirated at the wasted Potential of this one, as well as the amount of time the game was forcing me to "Press X to continue", while beeing utterly pretentious about beeing Art at the same time. This piece of Media is still gorgeous to look at, but it felt abusive to play. All underlined by the absurd decision to have to Press A after EVERY. SPOKEN. PIECE. OF. DIALOGUE. So the "Press X to continue" Gameplay gets hammered into your mind even more so. It ends up beeing either "Press X to continue Dialogue to get to playing Music" or "Press X to continue playing Music to get to the section where you can press X to dialogue".Watch a playthrough on Youtube and you will have more Fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Does music make you feel good? Do you like epic guitar solos? Are you the type of person who gets goosebumps when music swells to a fantastical high? This is probably an experience for you.If you want some mad Ziggy Stardust vibes, a good cast of characters, great voice acting, a captivating art style and to feel really bloody good. Just buy it. _childDocuments_.review: The art in this game is really beautiful as is the music. It kept me entertained and I couldn't wait to see what the next areas had to offer. Unfortunately the game just wasn't really fun in the end. The platforming is almost non existent. I wish the gameplay had more to it than a Simon Says minigame/holding right on the analog stick and holding X while pressing A every now and then to clear a small gap. The movement feels clunky and I wish there was a dedicated run button instead of having to wait for the character to speed up. A lot of the game has you talking to various NPCs that reveal a little more of the plot as you meet new characters. The problem is a lot of the dialogue is broken up since it has you press A to continue a conversation so it ends up spoken unnaturally. Not to mention the cadence of delivery. I feel like there really isn't much left for replay value either. I don't see a reason to try the other "choices" the game prompted but maybe it does change the experience in some way. The reason I'm giving this game a negative review is because there's a segment maybe a little past halfway thru the game where you meet a character that absolutely blasts your speakers with rage screaming dialogue at least 3 or 4 times. Ah yes, the pinnacle of comedy. Peaking volume. This isn't a YouTube poop. This ruined my experience since I was having to lower the volume over and over in order not to damage my ears or my sound system. This game is carried by the music and art. While it is enjoyable to an extent -- the dialogue and gameplay just ruins it for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, one of the most pure and beautiful experiences I've ever had while playing a game.  That sounds like the  hyperbole of someone who just finished something cool.  It's not.  I'm a musician - this speaks to me on such a deep level that I still feel it in my stomach.  That's the thing though - this isn't just about musicians - this is about everyone who is unsure about themselves and whether they can meet the expectations set before them.The musical gameplay - perfect.  I know how it works mechanically, musically, how the sausage is made - but man oh man does it still feel absolutely amazing to play.  It was exactly as complicated and challenging as it needed to be - just - pure.The game warns you that you should play it on a controller, and I didn't.  I played it on keyboard and found some of the "challenge" sections a bit clunky - but that's on me.  I can see exactly how this would feel better on a controller, and I highly suggest you follow the game's advice on this one.Truly beautiful story / game, and I can't wait to pick this one up again in a year or two and remember what this feeling was like.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: The Artful EscapeThis game is about a teenage guitar player who is forced to step into his dead uncles footsteps who was a folk legend. The teenager struggles with his sounds and ends up going on a psychedelic journey to find his new stage performance and find out which sounds he doesn't like.This game is incredibly gorgeous! It has overwhelmingly, beautiful and extreme vibrant colors you just can't look away. The music they used for the guitar riffs and everything around it is amazing!The game is a side scroll visual novel. During the game you come across people you have to have an epic guitar battle with.Only a handful of games have been able to REALLY grab my attention for a very long time in a row. Therefor I finished this game in 6 - 7 hours in one go. I just wasn't able to stop, I had to keep going, i had to finish it. This game got me HOOKED big time! I had to get up at 5:30am in the morning but finished the game far past midnight. Absolutely no regrets whatsoever! Lack of sleep was completely worth it.This game only has 12 achievements and most of them are story based so unmissable. There are a few who you can mis on your first run but seriously, having to play this for a second time would not be a bad thing at all! You could if you don't want too, read into the achievements then you'll know at which parts you need to do a little thing to get it.This game is a 10/10 all the way.The story, the art, the humor, the everything!

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, I played this game completely in VR using the totally free UEVR mod by Praydog. You do have to use scene compatibility though in the compatibility tab of UEVR, otherwise you'll  get a double image. Also, it is important to know that barring a specific fix for this game, it does have a major issue: the text in VR displays in a double image. Perhaps there is a way to fix that within UEVR, but if not, there will need to be a modded fix for the game so that the text is clearly visible. Unfortunately for me, the text was always a double image and so it was difficult to read. However, you can close one eye and it'll be readable on either the left or right lens of your VR headset. There are also some other minor issues, like some reflections in the corners, or blocked off parts in the edge of your sight, but these are minor annoyances. The text is the big problem because there is almost always text in this game, with no setting to turn off text or subtitles. There is also black text on backgrounds that make it barely visible.The game looks great in VR. In fact, as soon as you leave the town, the game starts looking like it was meant for VR. At first it looks like a theater showing of a 2.5 3 dimensional game. If you look to the side or up and down, you'll see the entire off-stage production, which will have many graphical oddities. However, simply looking straight will have you enjoying what was meant to be seen through the camera. After leaving town though, this stops being an issue for the most part as most of the game is rendered in 3D. There's a lot more 3D depth than you'd think by seeing the store page video. After playing this in VR, I have no desire to ever play this in 2D (pancake mode). I hope the dev considers adding official VR support. Really most of what would need to be fixed is the text that doesn't display correctly in VR. Maybe a bit better optimization as well. Although I was getting mostly 90 fps, I did experience a few drops on my RTX 3080.

_childDocuments_.review: The recommendations made me buy it.I will recommend you re-consider that choice. I am very disappointed. I have played it for about 2,5 hours and I have not made a single decision yet except my "new name" as an artist. I do realise that this game is extremely beautiful, but there is zero gameplay besides a few "guitar chords" chich is pressing q, w, e, a, and d in a very simple order. No deep conversations, no quests, no decisions, no exploration.I missed, if it was even mentioned, that this is a visual novel that requires for you to run in certain directions a lot, thus I am immensly disappointed that I spent my money on this. I do not mind very slow pased indie games, but I do not want to feel bored. If you do not mind "playing" visual novels, then you might absolutely love this, it is beyond gorgeous.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: There are few games I fall in love with the moment I start playing them. The Artful Escape was one of those games. For some reason, the extraordinarily beautiful game, only able to be described as hipster-esquè in a self aware fashion, is absolutely perfect.The soundtrack, whether you are using your guitar or not, is mesmerizing, the plot is beautiful and it is a coming-of-age and coming-to-terms story unlike one I have seen in a game in years. It truly is a masterpiece of a game, which deserves no less than a whole-hearted critique.Good for achievement hunters, time to complete: 3-4 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: I felt this game irregular.There are 3 different type of gaming in it:1. musical jams (reproduce musics with buttons): nice parts, no too hard;2. meet and talk parts: a little boring, especially because the dialog choices have zero effect on the story;3. the run/platform sequences: THE BEST PART OF THE GAME! It's definitively not hard, no dangers, no challenge, but it's beautiful, pleasant, like a dream: floating among the clouds in the space under a space battle, sliding in a snowy forest full of weird alien creatures that wake up with your music, crossing a futuristic strange city to escape from the anti-music police... I love these levels, also they are not a lot (about 5). But the game deserves to be played just because of them!
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10 I don't if there is anyone I know that I could recommend this game toPros:Its visually very beautiful, the voice acting is solid, and some of the dialogue is really good. Its a very unique experience playing it, mostly due to the visuals. Cons:In some other aspects it lacks greatly. The gameplay mostly consists of a "platforming" section or a simon says game. The platforming gave some downwards slopes you slide on and pads you double jump to. I thought it would get cooler, maybe slopes would start to connect more in increasing difficulty, maybe some way to use the guitar for interesting movement options. Just anything other than a couple slopes, and some jumping up ledges in every single area. You can play your guitar (holding down one button) to make the background set off triggers, which really does look visually amazing, but you quickly get sick of hearing the same guitar solo repeated over and over as you play. The second aspect is what I saw as the boss fights. After a platforming section you go against one. It consists of essentially simon says. You have 5 buttons that each play a different note, and you just follow the same pattern of 5 buttons as the boss you go against. It is really cool how they visually worked it in all together, but the gameplay is dreadful. The string of notes is only ever 5 long at a time. So you sit, wait for the boss to show 3-5 buttons get hit, and you repeat the pattern. Thats every single boss fight. The "increase" of difficulty is the fact you must hit multiple buttons at once now "A+B", but since it is only a string of 5 notes it is still just not entertaining to play. There is no time limit or rythm required to how you hit the buttons either, its so simple that its extremely disappointing. Both main aspects of the game, platforming and "boss" fights both suffer from being simple and staying simple all the way till the end. It almost feels like an afterthought, its a lot of lost potential.The last portion of the gaming is talking to others. There are options on what you say in the game. Sometimes the options have 0 affect on anything, or is utter nonsense answers to a nonsense question. Other times someone says something that really connects. Its a mixed bag, I was speed reading through most parts and in rare moments reflected on others. It took me around 3 hours to beat.I wouldn't touch this game if you are looking for a game that isn't just a visual experience with silly but sometimes intrapersonal story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: The good- Artistic visuals with vivid colors and psychedelic aesthetics. The combination of 3d background and 2d characters is unique. Its world is a surreal, crazy mix of fast moving elements and imaginary creatures.- Nice direction. Very cinematic platforming sequences with all kinds of things happening at the background while you're moving. Lights, particles, creatures, everything is dancing synchronized to your moves. - Great, expressive voice acting performances. They give some life to the dull characters.- Trippy, colorful creatures designed with lots of imagination. - Good sense of humor and some nice surreal dialogues. The answers you can give are hilarious.- It refers to an attempt a self discovering. A personal, emotional story of struggling to do things you love while breaking free of people's expectations on you.- It's a clever addition to let you at some point customize your character. It makes him more personal to you and symbolizes his rebirth. The creation of a new self.- It wants to be more of a sensory experience than telling a definite series of events and that's what makes it unique. Although, I'm not sure it succeeds to wake up your senses.The bad- It lacks a purpose, something to motivate you keep playing. There is no challenge at the gameplay and the story doesn't really evolves. You just walk from left to right watching gorgeous visuals. In other games like this, the environment has a role to play like telling stories or creating further thoughts. Here, everything seems random, like the developers just put beautiful designs together without having to support a specific idea. It feels shallow and ends up being just a showcase of impressive visuals.- Uninspiring gameplay. It's a game about music so I expected it to have bigger impact on the gameplay either by synthesizing creative sounds and songs or through more complex rhythmic skill challenges. Instead, you get some boring, slow, repetitive combinations of the same five notes through the entire game. Also sometimes it makes no sense at all to impress or beat your enemies with patterns that they showed you to play.- Dull characters with shallow personalities. It's hard to love them or attach emotionally to them. - Clunky animations. It's like they were made in Flash or some other obsolete program. Also, some guitar moves look excessive and silly.- Short duration. Everything happens too fast. Each character and place doesn't get the time to establish inside your mind. At the end their names tell you nothing at all.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: To write a review hitting all the points you want press shift.Right away, if you watched the trailer and gotten the impression that this is a platformer. It isn't. While there is some light platforming, but it's seldom more then pressing right and double/jumping at the right moment. Wailing on your guitar while doing so is optional but recommended. There's no diverging paths besides, it's basically all on rails, and once in a while you get to pads you need to activate or jump pads needed to jump over stuff.And while this might sound like a bad thing, it really isn't. If you'd need to concentrate or even look on when and where to jump you'd probably don't have as much time admiring the beautiful scenery you run or slide through, much of it reacting to your guitar playing... thus it being recommended. And in the rare case where you mess up a jump, the check points are pretty forgiving and you'll get spawned back into the level just a screen or so before.The only other somewhat action-y game mechanic is Simon Shreds... this one, while a sometimes somewhat jarring pause to the running and jumping around, is a feast for the ears. This one dials the music up to 11. The later segments of this also might be somewhat challenging if your short term memory is crap... or you're inebriated as I was. ;)When not running from one side of the level to the other you either get to "free roam" in 3 small-ish areas and have some light interaction with your surroundings and characters that span from relatively normal to really weird, but there's no puzzles or anything like that. The comments and dialogs are written well enough, the voice acting is nice and fits even beside the big names. Sprinkled in are some short multiple choice segments where you create the back story for your newly born Rock-Star alter ego full of puns and references to bands and other media, as well as a shopping trip to an 80ties mall for the appropriate attire. And this might be the thing where your mileage may vary. Depending on your age and what music, movies, and books you consumed some or all of this might go straight over your head where others get that sweet nostalgia hit. Personally, as someone watching Bill & Ted, Waynes World, and Spinal Tap, listening to Rock and Metal, and deep into Sci-Fi this was awesome and I'm kinda sad that a replay won't give me the same satisfaction again.And while speaking of replaying... there's really no reason. Maybe in a couple of years when memories gotten foggy. There are 3 or 4 achievements that are missable but easy to figure out how to by their name and you can go straight to the corresponding stage via the chapter select in the pause menu. The whole game only takes 3½ hours even with looking at and speaking with everything.Don't get this for the platforming, or the adventure, or action... who really gives a game like this these tags!?Get this for the visual and audible experience. Get this for the neat little, 4 hour, story.And if the price of admission for 4 hours is too high for you wait for a sale or get XBGP.P.S. This edit is for some silly badge... please ignore. ;)

_childDocuments_.review: Admittedly, I bought this game and left it to sit in my library for the longest time. And as of last night, I can't recall a time that I've been more upset with myself about something. Because this game? oh man...The Artful Escape has it all. Beautifully crafted fantastic worlds, characters, music and dialogue perfectly intertwined with a very grounded story about finding yourself. Its rare to find something that your mind knows is fiction, but its masterful execution warmly invites you to a very real place. For the entire play-through I was in a trance. I count myself lucky being able to enjoy this work of art and to have gotten to know the creatures within. In short: ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ crazy, and I cried my eyes out. 10's across the board.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: A trippy journey through Impostor Syndrome, identity and music.Needless to say, this game isn’t for everyone. At first glance, it might look and feel like a simple quirky story based “sidescroller’’, but it sure isn’t.The gameplay is simplistic, and if you’re going to this game wanting a super duper complicated rhythm based game, then you will be a bit disappointed. Nevertheless that’s not what I'm here to babble about. Control wise, I do not own a controller, so all I did was change the input of some keys and I’ve managed to play it smoothly.It looks stunning and artistically distinct from most games I’ve played, the designs and colors used pass this idea of, not joking- an acid trip. From the aesthetic, to the visuals, to the music, from top to bottom this game reeks of a passion project, and you can feel and see it clearly in its entirety.Now, I won’t spoil much, but the story hits close to home when it comes to Impostor Syndrome and Personal Identity. It is a journey and I highly recommend playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: A "must have" pearl in your game library!You are Francis Vendetti, nephew of the deceased folk music legend, Johnson Vendetti. Before your first public concert you embark on a journey to the stars. In the tradition of the classic Hero's Journey you´ll grow from a reluctant earth weakling to the guitar god of a whole universe. According to Johnny Galvatron, lead guitarist of the band "The Galvatrons", who conceived this game, the character of Francis is based on David Bowie/Ziggy Stardust. Experience a wacky, psychedelic mix of the "Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy", "Bill & Ted's Excellent Adventure", "Back to the Future" and a pot full of acid.The Artful Escape is a platform game in which you control Francis by moving him through different landscapes imbued with sound and stunning visuals, the sound and art design is fantastic. Besides running and jumping, Francis has a guitar that he can play to achieve different effects in the environment, jamming with all the creatures on his way. There are some boss characters you´ll easily defeat or, better said, convince of your talent by "just" replaying simply kept sequences of sound. Finally there are some well-staged conversations  to underline the already fantastic atmosphere.Gentle as a kitten, even with my old potatoe I never encountered any problems whatsoever!Ryzen 5 2600 @ 3,9GHzMSI GTX1060 Gaming X 6GBDDR 4 16GBThe Artful Escape is one of those games you´ll probably never forget and a great example of what the medium "video game" is capable of. A good game doesn't have to be open world and contain hundreds of quests - quality over quantity. It´s unique without serving clichés, sound and visuals are bombastic and with about 3-4 hours to finish just the right thing for one session. The price is ok, although I didn't pay a single cent for it because it was a gift from a friend, which makes it even more precious to me. I had a ton of fun exploring those beautifully animated worlds and their freaky inhabitants. The story is good but not the star of this journey, you are!
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I have grinned this much in playing a video game in a LONG time.  The art is gorgeous, the music is wonderful, and the story just makes you feel so badly for poor Francis.  There are little touches and eggs everywhere, and I will have to play through again to catch more of them.  The only thing I could complain about is that the movement is so fast, that the art goes flying by.  There were a few times I just stopped and stood still so that I could look at the gorgeous feast for the eyes.  I am super sad though, for the last concert there was so much going on, but I wasn't able to watch it all, simply because I was (ironically) playing the game.  Guess that is secondary excuse to just go back and play the game again!The game is short (as of writing this I played 5 hours), and not terribly complicated.  It is very relaxing actually.  The only issue I had at all was in one part jumping though a window.  It took me almost ten minutes of repeat repeat repeat, until I could get through that darn window!  Aside from that one spot, the game was a very relaxing play, allowing you to just sit back and enjoy the art.  It really was a very nicely done, artful escape.
