_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is atrocious. The music becomes relentless in it's stagnant, stale, boring, unchanging fervor. For a title that is about 'artfully escaping' from people expect you to be as a musician, it doesn't at all let YOU have ANY creative freedom on the music in this game. It doesn't allow YOU to do what the player is desperately trying to do which is the change the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ music in any way shape or form. It's ironic in a bad way. There was a lot of anticipation surrounding this game but it disappoints. The gameplay consists of holding left, as you always ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ do in 2d games (only Night In The Woods goes from right to left in a very subtle way that shows that the main character is going back in time, back from University, dropping out because of mental health issues and wanting to go back to their childhood) and holding X/Square. In a game that is all about escaping into different dimensions and flying through countless gorgeous worlds while putting on an incredible performance with your guitar while doing so, you have NO creative freedom whatsoever over what the music does, what YOU do, or the choices that it makes you choose which don't amount to anything different, all choices result in the same guitar playing that gets mind-numbing way faster than you'd initially think. You just hold right and hold another button, the whole game... save a few times where you can go around and talk to people. And only after 2 hours of this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ "gameplay" I dreaded holding down that button to hear the same ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ guitar soloing the same exact way over and over and over. But you have to in order to make the incredible visuals interact with your music and do all manner of extraordinary breathtaking beautiful things. The numb boring gameplay is only broken up by ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ SIMON SAYS moments... It's literally Simon Says, it's so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ stupid and too ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ easy. And in a game about music, you'd expect the rythym of the Simon Says moments to be important... whelp, it's not. They even tell you "USE YOUR OWN RYTHYM." In other words, it doesn't matter how much you suck, which makes every Simon Says part suck. Not even a challenge for a toddler... great ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ gameplay... This is not a "Rythym" game at all like you'd expect. This game is a spectacle. There is really no reason at all to buy this game because you can just watch someone else "play" it on youtube or Twitch. The gameplay is so weak that it's downright stupid to buy this game when you can see the gorgeous spectacles and hear monotonous "shredding" of the main character. The music is all gorgeous at first but once you get into the main "gameplay" loop... it becomes immensely stale, stagnant and boring. Questions:This was such a huge missed opportunity. Why can't you change how the music in any way? That alone would have made up for so much of the boring stale "shredding" that you HAVE to do. Why can't you change the key of music your playing in? Why can't you at least change the chords that you are soloing in? Why can't you change the tempo? WHY IS THERE NO RHYTHM COMPONENT!? Why is there no challenging gameplay whatsoever? Why couldn't you have at least controlled the rate at which you were "shredding" from really slow to really high? Why the ♥♥♥♥ didn't they do ANYTHING interesting or creative at all with the Simon Says parts?? WHY COULD YOU NOT CONTROL EFFECTS LIKE REVERB, ECHO, WAH, WHAMMY PEDAL AND/OR BAR, CHORUS, TREMOLO, ETC... If they at least had that, it would have brought an entire new level of interactivity to the game even if the entire game still had the same horribly lacking level of interactivity and challenge in many other ways. Even Ocarina of Time included vibrato AND bending of the pitch up or down when you were playing the Ocarina... How did The Artful Escape not take any note of any of the interesting elements of music in games prior to it? Who the hell was in charge of the decision to make this the most boring music game of all time? Why don't you at least have to press those Simon Says buttons at certain points during each running/sliding stage? Why can't you do back-flips, front-flips and other tricks when you are in the air? Why can't you change the tone and volume of your guitar? This is in outer space and other dimensions so why can't we do cool things like teleport, fire lasers out the guitar corresponding to what notes we're playing, etc.? Why are there only 5 Simon Says buttons? There's a lot more than 5 buttons on a controller, and especially a keyboard. Why isn't there a key-tar? Why can't you mess around with one of those? Why isn't there a drumset you can attach to yourself, or a harmonica, why don't you ever sing??? Why can't you change your instruments at will with a button or whatever? Even Majora's Mask had different instruments you could play. This is a different dimension/s, why isn't electricity shooting out and shocking and grabbing everything near you and explodes outward as you make a full chord. Why don't you have Portuguese Man O' Wars as shoes zapping things and snatching fish while you get to walk on water and your music causes waves to emanate from you? Why don't you get to walk along the rings of Saturn and discover than certain notes resonate to the rings and moves them? And why isn't that a puzzle that you need to solve? WHY ISN'T ANYTHING A PUZZLE YOU NEED TO SOLVE!? I could go on for a long time about what this game could have been, but I think you get the picture. There is just nothing here.Annapurna Interactive produces THE BEST Indie games, and they make the BEST games with music in them "Journey" and "Sayonara Wild Heart" are among the best music/video game combinations, "Gorogoa" even. But this game baffles me. I've got to say this is one of the weakest titles and certainly the most deceptive title Annapurna has ever produced. Huge disappointment. There's just nothing here beyond the incredible imagery, which clearly the developers were laser-focused on, when instead they should have been making one of the best interactive music games there is... Huge missed opportunity. It's almost like the developers had no idea what makes a video game interesting. I am returning this without a second thought and am going to watch the rest on Youtube to see if the music gets any better or if it just continues being a nongame that has a relentless assault of the same exact style of "shredding" which gets stale after 5 minutes, but I endured 2 hours of it...  and a complete absence of even the SLIGHTEST challenging gameplay. If you want a game the has music at it's center and actually has gameplay and puzzles, try FRACT. Or endure this game for as long as you can, and then put the music on mute after you inevitably get sick of it and put on your own music and pretend that's what the guy is playing.

_childDocuments_.review: A game so good i got it with Game Pass and immediately bought a copy on Steam to support the dev's.Whilst there is some truth in reviews that point out the gameplay is extremely simplistic platforming interspersed with some 'Simon Says' rythm action elements, that really does miss the point of Escape entirely.What you get for well under £20 (or your equivalent) is a stunning, lusciously colourful and visually hypnotic romp through a psychedelic landscape which you influence through playing your guitar. The plot is witty and engaging, drawing you into the incredible universe as seen through the eyes of a hero we can pretty much all empathise with... assuming guitar shredding psychedelia is your bag.The 4-5 hours here are so vivid, trippy and entertaining as to make the last two awful years of real world misery seem like a bad memory. This is a trip worth taking and one i guarantee will distract you completely throughout. Do yourself a favour and grab this kaleidoscopic, hypnotic, audio-visual experience!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is something alright. What a journey and, above all, what a trip. Literally and figuratively. Where do I even begin?What starts off as a down to earth adventure quickly transforms into intergalactic space opera of epic proportions. The general story is one that most of us will be able to relate to: finding your own identity when faced with towering expectations. In this case it’s following in your uncle’s footsteps, who has passed away and was a musical prodigy in his hometown, where you character, Francis Vendetti, also resides. After a brief introduction in and of your hometown you’ll be going on a colorful, psychedelic, fantastical musical journey all across the cosmos.The game plays out like a 2D platformer and early on you’ll gain access to a spaceship that will act as some sort of hub for your musical trek. Don’t expect the ability to choose a destination; the game plays out in an entirely linear fashion. It’s just another part of the story.Since this is a game focused entirely on music and telling its story there are no enemies or real obstacles to be found here. Francis can be directed to the left and the right and he can jump. He can also initiate a conversation and play his guitar. And that’s all you will do. Yup, the gameplay is quite limited indeed. Now, the game isn’t super long so all in all you’ll be playing it for only a couple of hours so it’s not that bad in the end. I will say this, though: this game should really be played for the story and the experience itself. I’ve seen nothing like this before, not in this way. And that’s a huge compliment.Whenever you arrive on a planet you’ll mostly walk in a straight line, right to the objective. The road towards the objective is usually laid out like a music track, though. Sometimes jumping on an obstacle may emit a sound. And you can optionally strum your guitar whenever you feel like it. But it’s always worth it; the whole environment will literally light up and come alive. It’s a true sight to behold.At the end of each area is usually a music stage and a boss fight - if you could even call them that - where you have to mimic the musical button presses as shown in the creature’s appearance (yes, they are part of their bodies). Failing isn’t an option apparently, as pressing the wrong input will have the boss just repeat them without any consequences. This feels both nice and weird; on one hand you want the story to move forward, but on the other hand you’re supposed to be a musical prodigy.You can also die, but you’ll almost instantly respawn usually just a few meters away. It won’t happen often, but the unnoticeable checkpoints are generally placed.About halfway through you’ll gain the ability to change your outfit. Despite being such a short game I was impressed by the massive amount of clothes I was able to pick to dress up my character. Think of glasses, make-up, pants, jackets, you name it. When I thought I had checked everything the game gave me even more options. Impressive and it shows the developers were adamant on letting you choose your own story. Because even though the story is the same for everyone, there are different choices to be made from time to time. Think of your home planet (from which I could also choose an insane amount) and your backstory, for example. When you first start the game you can already tell that a lot of love and care was put in the game, but this shows they went above and beyond in order to tell their story in its totality. Amazing.With the exception of one bug right at the start (I jumped and got stuck in the environment) I didn’t experience any bugs or issues.Playing through the game should take around four hours.Graphically the game reminded me a whole lot of the Zoink (developer) games, especially the creature and level designs. But ten times more intense if we’re speaking about colors and vibrancy. The colors pop off the screen, it’s pure eye candy. Besides the gorgeous artistic style everything is superbly animated with lots of character.The voice acting is pretty much of the same quality. Everyone sounds spot on and the famous actors like Lena Headey (Game of Thrones) and Carl Weathers (Predator, Arrested Development (‘Baby, you’ve got a stew going’) give a nuanced, yet fitting performance.There aren’t many sounds, but what’s there sounds good. As for the music; it’s pretty much perfect. Guitar solos and jamming with bosses and gates/portals(?) all sound terrific. The music is supposed to be one of the best parts of the game, and rightfully so, and in doesn’t disappoint in that regard.The Artful Escape is art, let there be no doubt about it. Its colorful, vibrant and psychedelic visuals are among the best I’ve ever seen and, for reference, I’ve seen and played thousands of games. Very rarely have I seen one with art this detailed, lovingly created and with such care. But, and there’s a big but here, I wouldn’t recommend it as a game. Behind all the glamour is a really basic game, you see. If you’re looking for something artsy, however, then grab it right away. And if you can look past the fact that it’s more of an experience and not so much a game then you should play it as well, obviously. If you can’t do that or want something a little more interactive then you should find yourself a different game to play. No matter how you slice it, though, it’s always your own choice. And you could always buy it and refund it if you don’t care for it. But it’s an experience alright.

_childDocuments_.review: Every once in a while, a game comes along that wasn't made with the intentions of making big money or selling dlc or even being on the front page of Steam for that matter.Sometimes games are made with absolute heart and soul, trying to spread the message of finding yourself or getting lost in a world that makes you take a step back from your own life for a moment.I can't begin to tell you how beautiful, how stunning, how thought invoking this game really was. I started it and could not put it down. It's not a long game. It's not trying to compete for longest play time. It's trying to send a message. I'm totally fine with that.I think you'll find yourself wanting to rock out and take tons of screenshots because it's hard to describe what it feels like to just jam on an alien planet in the Infinite Universe.So buy this game. It's the zen you need. It's a breath of fresh air from all the games out there trying to be a live service.

_childDocuments_.review: This is what "walking simulators" are supposed to be. There's no challenge here, just bumps on the road, and the gameplay is there to fill you with feels. _childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: The Artful Escape is mostly walking simulator through some interesting locations with the ability to do guitar wails and a very basic rhythm game mechanic at performances. Story-wise it's a nonsensical journey of a young artist struggling to find/embrace his stage persona and break free of his famous relative.I beat the entire game in 3 hours and felt like it dragged on even in that time. While an interesting experience, I can't recommend it. It would have been nice to have variety in the music, more depth to the game play and for me the nonsensical presentation of the story, while probably intended as comedic, fell flat. It's worth seeing this once but I would not spend much money on this again as the value isn't really there.You can tell the developers really enjoyed this but just didn't translate into a fun game for me.

_childDocuments_.review: The Artful Escape, a game that rather feels like a psychedelic 70's fever dream caused by an overdosis of '' e d i b l e s '' after watching sci-fi movies on a saturday evening, a delusional journey lost on the wonders of the universei'd be fun if i were exaggerating but i ain't even Putting aside it's stunning, wondrous artstyle - which it's sustained from start to finish, an impeccable voice acting and an outstanding soundtrack,  we got a 2d platformer / exploration with some respective stage  ''bosses'',played as stage performances that can be summarize in a musical Simon-says gameI was absolutely hooked in from the first glance i took to its visuals and symphony, then slowy got into a pretty well directed and enjoyable storyat times i would just stop for a moment to shred the guitar and hear the chords blend into the symphonious ambience and colors on the landscapeswould i recommend this game? for a lucid, trippy yet splendid experience, absolutely

_childDocuments_.review: The Artful Escape is a shining example of video games as art. This is an immersive experience that is focused on interacting with its beautiful environments while enjoying a stellar and atmospheric soundtrack. It's also a story that is focused on the protagonist getting out of his uncle's shadow and finding his own identity. You'll travel from the quaint town of Calypso, through the cosmic extraordinary and all the way out to the far end of the cosmos in your quest for rock 'n' roll glory.  The Artful Escape is a love letter to Rock 'n' Roll and is a fun and creative adventure best experienced in a dark room with headphones to maximize your immersion. If you're looking for a challenge, you'll have to look elsewhere. You can do no wrong in this game - a failed platforming section can be repeated as many times as you need, and you'll be right in front of the last jump you missed. There are no enemies to fight; instead, there are intergalactic VIPs you have to impress with your performance by following a series of inputs using the musical key, conveniently displayed on the head or face of every being you come across but always in a clever way. It's impossible to fail; a missed note will simply be repeated until you get it right. all the while your playing will be accompanied by the greatest laser light show in the universe. This is a quick game. You can finish it in about 4-5 hours. However, you may want to play more than once - you can make several choices during the gameplay that will affect your character and it can be fun to see how the other characters react to your choices. Overall I would recommend this game to anyone who wants to enjoy a relaxing experience that is a feast for the eyes and ears. A must play for any fans of rock music and lovers or stories of self-discovery, as well as anyone who would like a different experience with a video game that diverts from the common action and sports titles we play most of the time.

Maybe I should gift it to a friend and watch them play through..Edit: I played through it again and enjoyed it again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely ever leave game reviews, but I think I owe it to the team behind this game. This was such a fun ride. I will be telling all my friends who are into music, art, and the weird and unusual about this one. Psychedelic. Artsy. Unique. Eyegasm. Full of heart. Would recommend 10/10. It's a "game" we all need right now after a rough year. It's more of eye candy with insanely creative story line with jumping, wailing a guitar, and power-sliding. Get this game right now, you will not regret it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This is a neat diversion if you are looking for a visual distraction that won't demand too much of you for your time. I'd describe it as lite platformer with rhythm game elements which don't really require a lot of precision or skill to pass through. There is a lot of dialogue which is okay if you like text. It's kinda low-tier as far as Annupurna titles go, still it has a solid presentation and general quality consistent with the brand, as far as the publisher goes and if you have expectations based on their other offerings. It's a guitar-centric fantasy adventure that really only has one modality but it it is a pleasing one. I enjoyed Sayanora Wild Hearts a little more and although the experience delivered is different, I would put these in a similar box, of audio-visual eye candy with an emotional hook that may actually deeply appeal to its intended audience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This has been one of my most enjoyable gaming experiences in some time. While the gameplay never really exceeds basic platforming and rhythm action, the story, characters, music and visuals take these simple mechanics and turn the whole thing into a spectacle of cosmic proportions.This is a narrative adventure with strong writing, excellent performances and an abundance of both profundity and levity. This is also a love letter to the guitar, to music and to the artistic spirit in general. It's a very singular experience that may not resonate with everyone, but for those for whom this is their jam, oh boy will they both rock and be rocked hard. Personally this was a fully immersive audio visual overload that had the hairs on my arms standing on end for the entirety of my play through. Frissoning my little socks off I was. Anyone who has ever played guitar even casually, (but secretly harboured notions of rock godhood) will love this. The feeling of performance is somehow distilled into a few button presses, and any recovering Rock Band addict will feel right at home.Influences abound: Yellow Submarine meets Bill & Ted, Guitar Hero by way of Inside Llewyn Davis. A soundtrack that channels both Bob Dylan and Joe Satriani, an art style and sense of humour and whimsy reminiscent of Broken Age and Psychonauts. That's lots of yes from me.  Oh and the creative director behind the game is called Johnny Galvatron; some say he is the child of the Glamourgonn.Grab your axe, shred some intergalactic licks and unleash your inner Ziggy Stardust if only for a few hours.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: First off: this game is light on game-play and light on challenge. If that's the start and end of your interests, then pass on this. However, if you're looking for a good story with amazing visuals and fantastic music, this is going to be your jam. Some will compare this to a visual novel, and they're not entirely wrong. However, that comparison also does this game a disservice as it is much more interesting that that. It's an experience that is definitely not for everyone, but for those looking for something new that will grab your brain-stem and not let go, consider this little gem of a game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the most gorgeous game I have ever played, every rendered frame looks simply amazing.It's a simple game: run around with some basic jumping while pressing X to wail. There are no frustrating or challenging gameplay elements, just a wonderful experience where you feel like a real guitar hero with every step you take.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: I'm in awe with the visuals and the soundtrack. Every frame is an art piece and every second a harmony. The art direction is wild ! This game has some of the craziest character and environment design ever. And the characters themselves are charming and very enjoyable. The story is interesting and is portrayed very well. Not a single dull moment in throughout my playthrough. Onto gameplay- it's soothing and simple, a perfect sit-back-and-relax kinda game. Despite being very short, I can see myself replaying this multiple times. I thank a certain mango for gifting me this gem. And I hope many others too get to experience this wonder.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: A musical and colorful coming-of-age game with dreamlike art design and some funny parts in the story, which is suitable for players who are NOT looking for a big challenge at a certain time. The Artful Escape is a visual and sound design work of art to play. Dialogues are quite well written, with some quirky humor and the voice actors have done a great job as well.If you're looking for your next action shooter or horror adventure game, keep surfing, there are always waves just waiting for you. If you've studied art, call yourself some kind of musician and have loved playing video games all your life, but as a person you're more of a pessimist and a grump, do whatever you want, you're lost anyway. But if you're one those open-minded ones, down for a different experience than usual, then the game can also be an Artfulf Escape for you as it was for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic. I first chose this game for it's detailed and original aesthetic, seemed like an ufo coming to Steam - and it is - before being blown away by the music and whole of the game / concept.The gameplay is quite simple from what I've experienced so far: some easy platforming phases where you can shred on your luminous star-shaped guitar, alternating with music you "play" more in depth on it, using just 5 buttons.But the true interest of "The Artful Esacpe" is really the whole trippy vibe and beautiful space rock music, evoking nostalgia of times when musicians actually used instruments :))Such as the beautiful graphics of the game serve excellently right it's uplifting purpose: you'll have no time to cry in front of that, may it be for it's beauty or if you might feel down or emotioned, you'll surely be smiling like an idiot all the way, of pure joy. Simply awesome.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, I bought the game in the sale, the artwork intrigued me. But the musical theme and the trailers really won me over. And then I started playing... Please, please, please... Promise me (and the game devs) one thing: Just start to play, and emerge yourself without any expectations. It. Will. Blow. Your Mind.A trip of a lifetime.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: I'm very torn with this one.Visually, it's almost like a movie. Musically, it gets repetitive quickly. For me personally, the gameplay is very lacking. This game really requires no skill or anything, not even rhythm, at all. You can just lean back and continually press buttons to move on. The topics of the character and the conversations are interesting. But nothing new or very deep or philosophically advanced.I must say I'm a bit bored, but I'll continue, maybe it gets better near the end.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: The Artful Escape is a hard game to review. It's quite possibly one of my favourite games of all time, but at the same time, it didn't really feel like a game. It feels more like an experience, and a brilliant experience at that.The game is presented as a simple platformer but is less focused on platforming and more focused on rhythm-esque sequences and character dialogue.If you're looking for a mechanically complex/gameplay centric experience then this probably isn't for you.If you're looking for a compelling narrative, following a character as he finds his musical identity and meets strange individuals along the way, then I believe you will thoroughly enjoy this.To top it all off, both the soundtrack and art style are incredible.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Yet another game that falls victim to the black and white Yes/No recommendation.There is a lot to like in the game. It is well voice acted, the visuals are cool. The music is great. But can I recommend the game to buy? No. It is barely even a game, the platforming is basic, the music sections are basic and imo don't sound amazing compared to the pre-recorded music. I would recommend watching a lets play for this game. Or play it from a friend's library, but not to buy.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: What a show! Beautiful power metal at its finest, destroyed my blues and lifted me into a higher plane. Felt like the best of magical 80s and 90s movies rolled together in one. You know Bill and Ted's adventures? Well imagine playing a Bill and Ted movie. If you want something chill to relax to, but also want a bit of spice and good music, do not miss this gem.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This is a charming game carried by a tight story, quirky dialogue and excellent voice acting. The art design also helps to elevate the whole experience. The gameplay is extremely simple and is ideal for a younger audience. The integration of the music into the game felt like the weak link here. The music mini-game often felt awkward and unintuitive. I would have liked more options for jamming out in the game's platforming sections. The ability to trigger different notes using the face buttons would have been far more enjoyable than simply holding a single button the whole time. Finally with music being such a huge feature of the game I felt underwhelmed by the variety of genres on offer. Most of the music set pieces are pretty much the same. Likewise the guitar solos during traversal are pretty dull and don't integrate with the background music. Each solo sounds kind of like the guitar salesman in the showroom who just cranks the same showy licks every time but lacks musicality.With that aside the game was still tremendously enjoyable and it is great to see such a quality game produced in Melbourne.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: I waited for this game for more than 6 years, back to their Kickstarter in 2015. It exceeded my expectation. It has not much gameplay, but its purpose is to tell a short story with amazing visuals you will remember a long time. As a pop music fan, it's everything I ever wanted this game to be. It looks wonderful, and takes you to an amazing ride and makes you think of what it takes to grow a stage persona. It's such a unique topic for a video game, and it has never been made before. Thank you for this game, developers.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Even though the gameplay can be simplified to the most basic of platforming and on occasion an over-glorified Simon Says, the artstyle of this game is truly beautiful.It's one of those games that's more akin to an interactive movie if that makes sense, so if that's something you're ok with chances are you'll love this game.Also I've seen people complaining about a bug that softlocks you out of the game early on? I didn't run into so either they've patched it or I was just lucky? Either way I'd say look that up before buying cause I'm not completely sure.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: I played a demo of the Artful Escape at E3 2017 and thought it showed a lot of promise: a cinematic-ish platformer with beautiful backgrounds and themed around music. Very cool. It took 4 years after that event to come out, and I can confirm that it's still a cinematic-ish platformer with beautiful background and themed around music. If 3 hours of great art is your jam, then check it out.But I have a bone to pick, and that bone extends through both the mechanics of the game and the story. Let's start with the mechanics. This is a platformer where you run and jump, and the only other button you have is to push a button to play your guitar. This is a challenging thing to do -- have a composer come in and write music for playing guitar over any point of the background music in any segment of the game.  did this, and I know how difficult it was for the many, many talented composers and session musicians who worked to make that happen. So, with all due respect, what the hell happened here? When you play your guitar here, it's just random noodling. Your character doesn't play riffs, it's just a sequence of unrelated chords and notes, like a random number generator is spitting out bites of music. Very strange. Then you get to the end-of-level "boss" segments, which play out like the classic duelling banjos via a Simon Says mechanics. Again, great idea. But... the music you play is also just noodling. There's nothing resembling the structure of an actual song. Even the game's very ending, where you finally take the stage in the "real world" and blow the room away... it's just a 13 year old metal head's idea of music: rapid arpeggios all over the guitar. Playing notes fast is technically interesting, but it's not musically interesting. All the great players of this style know how to build together chord and note progressions that tell a sonic and emotional story.Which brings me to the story. You play as Francis Vendetti, nephew of a famous Bob Dylan-esque folk singer. You have to take the stage, but you feel like a fraud. Your heart is not in folk music, you instead want to play 70s inflected space themed progressive rock. This, again, is something a teenager would think. Genres of music are not in opposition to each other, they aren't things you need to rank. It is possible to play at the intersection of genres. Nirvana played folk music even though they were a grunge band. No guitarist, no matter what their primary genre, would ever deny Django Reinhardt's virtuosity. I have never met a musician that doesn't listen to, play, and write music broadly. The game takes visual inspiration for the folk artist from Bob Dylan. Bob Dylan played folk, but not just folk. Same with Neil Young or Merle Haggard. Country, roots, rock and roll. They played broadly. Eric Clapton is probably the world's most famous rock blues guitarist, and he put out an MTV Unplugged album as well. Folk is barely even a genre, it's a tradition. The idea that Taylor Swift, John Prine, Paul Simon, and Willie Nelson are playing the same genre might be a marketing convenience, but it's not in any sense true. The entire juxtaposition of folk and rock in this game makes absolutely no sense and there's no way that the character knows enough about music to consider playing professionally but is so ignorant that he is in his head about this. Made worse, this is a world that imagines folk as a commercially successful and vibrant route to fame and electronic rock as obscure and underground? Bizarre.What is this game saying about identity? Throw off the shackles of expectation and be who you really are. Nice moral, so why does it have you do that by inventing a stage persona, having a makeover (I sensibly made my character look like Buddy Holly), and playing derivative commercial pap. Rick Wakeman broke new ground, The Flaming Lips broke new ground, the character in this game is following in footsteps whether he's playing folk or rock or anything else. It feels like the artists who made this game remember thinking Kiss or David Bowie qua Ziggy Stardust were cool, that having a stage character that's a separate person from who you are is the hallmark of musical maturity. But these were inventions of marketing as much as they were true and authentic perspectives (by the way, Bowie wandered from genre to genre too, no one would have pigeonholed him as a glam rocker).A smarter game would problematize this by introducing these ideas and then showing them to be false. But this game seems to think they aren't false. It troubles me that this is a game about music: the act of making it, discovering your voice as a performer and songwriter, how music impacts audiences and the world, and neither the mechanics nor the writing reveal any understanding of music in the slightest. How about this: stop paying celebrity voice actors (thank god they got Lena Headey for 3 lines and Carl Weathers for 15) and spend the money on hiring actual musicians?
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: I've been getting bored with games recently I haven't found any games that have really given me that spark that good games give you. This game was a breath of fresh air. The art on this game is insanity. Talk about intense visual and borderline psychedelic experiences. The feel of the game is just so pleasant I loved every second of it and I'll probably replay this game because I loved the art so much. While it doesn't offer much when it comes to game play besides some platforming, rhythm games and having fairly straight forward conversations, the games makes up for that and sets itself above just a walking sim. Just the raw emotion and passion I felt while I played this game has left me utterly speechless. While the story isn't crazy in a narrative sense, the game is just perfect and much like the message it creates, it doesn't try to push itself to be something it isn't. And for that I'd say its perfect and I'll be adding this game to my favorites,
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: As someone, who just started learning the guitar, this game is just pure joy! Normally, these genre isn't my cup of tea, but this journey just impressed me. The Sound ist fullfilling, the graphics are lovely and enjoyable, the story is, for me as a starter in playing the guitar, pure motivation. I like so say thank you for this ride, i really enjoyed it and i will join the journey again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: For quite a while now, I'd missed that feeling of being fully convinced by a game. There was always something that left a bit of an unpleasant aftertaste, or there was nothing really wrong but I just didn't quite  it. Some of the games I loved at first, but got kind of tired of them towards the end. Might well be because I haven't exactly had a good year. But THIS game - there were a few things that bothered me a bit, I mean, even starting with the fact that I hate platformers. But all those things felt insignificant, because 95% of the time this game genuinely made me feel good and enjoy myself, and it left me glowing. The stunning visuals and the awesome soundtrack and voice-over have been mentioned a lot, and I'll have to mention them again. Also, from the way the initial menu screen turns into the game and the menu song is repeated as a background theme in later scenes, to the way the fantastical environments and creatures react to your guitar-shredding, this game is amazingly well executed. If you can get behind the idea of playing a game for the amazing art and  and this one looks interesting to you, this is very likely to be an absolute treat. The gameplay is light and forgiving so as not to be in the way. There's a lot of talk about how much danger you're in, but the worst thing that can happen is that you miss a jump and are transported back a short distance. As much as I suck at platforming, there was only one sequence that I found tricky and frustrating.  The music minigames show you the buttons you need to press, so it's more of a short-term memory thing which you can retry without any consequences. You could basically play this music game even if you're deaf - and it would probably still be a good experience to just move from one positively gorgeous space landscape into the next. The story about breaking free from other people's expectations and finding your identity wasn't particularly deep, but apparently a lot of people found it both meaningful and helpful, and it did touch me at times. My negatives: The  development towards the end seemed a bit off. It was annoying that there's no manual save, only checkpoints - and it wasn't even obvious to me what counted as checkpoints. I almost got cramps in my fingers from constantly pressing down the same keys. The minigames were obviously made for gamepads and a bit confusing to do on a keyboard. But as I said, these negatives didn't keep me from having a lot of fun with this game. They are probably already balanced out by the fact that I got to name my character The Terrible Buttonmasher (which says absolutely nothing about my talent for the music minigame!) and it cracked me up every time the name appeared in-game.TL;DR: 11/11 would jam with the Glamourgonn again* * * If you like chill and story-driven games, check out my curator . You're also welcome to join the .
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: The Artful Escape is a wild, trippy ride where you play as Francis Vendetti, a kid trying to dodge his folk singer legacy by ripping through the universe with epic guitar solos. The gameplay’s super chill, but that’s not really the vibe here, it’s all about the crazy visuals, killer music, and figuring out who you actually want to be. With a quirky cast and a whole intergalactic rock vibe, it’s more like a cosmic jam session than a tough game. Perfect for anyone into music, wild visuals, or just a really cool escape.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay is flat: platforming to the extent of holding buttons and performing basic combos; basic Simon-says pattern copying.But you're not really playing it for that reason. It's more for the visual and audio experience. The music for the environments is intended to give a sense of awe, which it does- as long as you're not spamming your guitar. And the art design is absolutely delightful, very colourful and creative. Definitely an escape from normalcy. Interesting choices available for character creation in the late-ish game.The story is alright, and it's nice that it reflects some of your dialogue choices. Definitely heavy-handed on the "be yourself" as long as yourself is quirky.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: i played this mostly on an afternoon when I didnt have any internet and it was so fun and nice to experience the joy and wonder that is this game in pretty much one sitting. the gameplay is admittedly not very deep but the excellent narrative, interesting characters, gorgeous views, stunning visuals and electric soundtrack more than make up for it
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Alter your consciousness and take a trip to the Cosmic Extraordinary!This game is an absolute gem.  It all seems pretty straight forward at first, an aimless walk about into the oddities of the universe.  However, the music in the game and the environmental vibes are amazingly reactive.  If you catch the beats, feel the flow, and take the time to jam the world around you reacts in amazing and often surprising ways.It truly is an experience where the journey is just as important as the destination.  If you play with a gamer mindset you will miss the forest for the trees.  Take of that hat and put on a pair of shades.  Play this game like an instrument and it will play right back with you.Listen to Lightman, take your time and don't miss your cue! 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: A game that isn't afraid of being short.More of an example of how a video game can be the Trojan Horse in which you hide a movie, so y'know, if anyone feels like making Jodorowsky's Dune, then consider sneaking it by in a video game.Visually awesome, conceptually fun, some laughs along the way.Gameplay is where it falls down though. Nothing you do seems to have any consequences, which is a good thing in some ways, as the "music key" was counter-intuitive for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: I lost count of how many times I became speechless over the course of my playthrough. I always love a good Annapurna game, but this one is truly special. It's a feast for the senses that will rock you to your core. Especially being a creative, the narrative hit me like a dump truck too. Beethoven & Dinosaur set quite a high bar for themselves, but I can't wait to see them clear it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: A great and very creative experience. The game doesn't really give the player a lot of traditional gameplay, but the music, the visuals and the story is unique and powerful, successfully creating a space musical. Would recommend to anyone who is looking for something more along the lines of a ride for your senses rather than technically advanced gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: very visually pleasing and fun game! enjoyed the simon-says style 'battle' system, and it was a lot easier to do than it first seems. story isn't amazing but it's good enough to get you through! i'd say taking story and length into consideration, the 15$ sale price is perfect.complaints are mostly on gameplay; sometimes its unclear when you NEED to play guitar while walking to get environmental effects, and playing guitar felt like it'd make the platforming hard. a few times it was unclear what couldn't be platformed to and i'd jump to my death, or i'd jump on a bounce-pad but i wouldn't hit it at exactly the right time or angle and not get boosted. not detrimental to the overall game but definitely annoying.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely GORGEOUS!!! The music and the visuals are straight out of a psychedelic rock album, in the best way possible. The gameplay is simple, but by no means is that a bad thing. It feels great! I feel like the story and the gameplay clash a bit, especially during certain rhythm game segments, but the overall message the game gives is really great, and most of the mechanics add to it even further. It's a good time!
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably my new favorite game. Its breathtakingly beautiful and kinda insane in a very good way. The story is really great because while having a predictable structure it is made completely unpredictable by it's characters and the world around them. It also really feels like you're creating this stage persona for the kid with tons of customizable options that come naturally as the story progresses. My only complaint would be that its a bit short (I finished my first play through in 4.7 hours with only 3 achievements uncompleted), but i do want to replay it and try out other choices which doesn't happen often. Anyway the point is give this game a try it is really something you should experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Game was beautiful, I love the art style and the colours throughout the game. The story of being a musician overshadowed by your famous relative really sets the tone as you explore to find yourself. Overall short but unique game that I would love to play again in the future just to hear the music and adore the art. So much fun!
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a short game but a game you will never forget. Being able to bring the player into a world that is extremely psychedelic and incredible. And the fight against him trembling thoughts and friends who want him to become something he doesn't want to be. If you have 15 euros over. Buy this. Short but really good
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful animation, avatar customization, and concept. The dialogue flowed so well it felt alive (no pauses between clicks). However, I do agree with the others that I wish it had more gameplay as 90% of the game is just running holding one button. And it repeats riffs to the point of a headache. You have to jam to interact with the beautiful landscape, but it doesn't change up for long stretches of the map and drones on. It would have been perfect if they gave us more musical control or changed up the jams somewhat. Recommend for psychedelic enjoyment, not if you're looking for a game with lots of replayability.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Needs some attention to transitions and how the music is weaved into the game. But the game surprised me, moved me, and impressed me, giving me a window into a wonderful vision of a music epic I have never seen before. It was definitely awesome. Definitely a recommended game. Also one that I hope you go in blind to get the most out of it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: More of an experience than a game itself, as gameplay is very limited. Move forward, jump and press the right buttons when in a "guitar challenge", there is not much more to do. Great visuals, interesting and funny storyline. I liked it and had a blast playing through it with a bunch of stoned friends. Worth it for the price asked (15.-).
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Listen,Do you remember picking up and playing guitar hero for the first time?Do you remember that feeling when you played a song you've never heard before for the first time and just falling in love with it? That feeling when you 100% it for the first time?Completing it on hard or expert even? Hold all that and imagine....Imagine if Tenacious D decided to make a game, where Spiderman gets abducted instead of Quill.But instead of becoming a ravager, he falls in love with the music from his world and decides to become a musician within this one.Touring and exploring a Guardians of the Galaxy/Rick & Morty esq universe. With some of the most incredible art direction that could only come from the combined minds of Tim Schafer, Tim Burton wrapped together in a Kubo and the six strings sort of manner with a dash of Hayao MiyazakiThat might be, this game.Sure the, "gameplay mechanics" aren't incredible per say. But that's not what you're here for are you?You're here for an experience and this... This is that experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This game blew my mind almost every 5 minutes. It's story is one that I think almost everyone needs to hear, needs to experience and needs to understand. Using the medium of music is perfect for a story of finding out who you are, not living up to what everyone thinks you should be and carving your own path, as music is probably the most expressive and personal art form there is, and this game pulled it off masterfully. This was a 10/10 journey that nothing else can even dream of rivaling, and taught me many things along the way, made me reflect on my own life, and brought me to tears along the way. I couldn't have asked for a better awakening.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Most triumphant!Out-of-this-world art & sound design, alongside a story of redefining oneself via encounter with the sublime, intertwine to create an experience that is wonderfully reminiscent of the profound experience of psychedelic self-discovery.The gameplay is simple, and there's no meaningful penalty for failure. Play for the vibes... play for the metamorphosis... play for the Glamourgonn!
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: The voice cast is stellar! Lena Headey, Carl Weathers, Mark Strong and Jason SchwartzmanStunningly gorgeous visuals and fun to play. This is a quick game, but it has a lot of heart - I feel like a lot of love went into making this. I was expecting it to be more difficult, but it was mostly running through beautiful alien landscapes, holding down the X button and occasionally playing a Simon-type follow along.  Aside from a few "G-d---its" in the dialogue options, there was no reason that I could see that this wouldn't be a great game for older kids (as there doesn't seem to be any penalty for getting things wrong or falling off a cliff), though I think teenagers might have been the target audience. I might be a few decades older than a rebellious teen now, but I like to support games that are trying something different, unusual, and cheeky.  My favorite part of the game was the Closet Mall :D I was able to approximate a Life on Mars - Bowie look, and I loved trying on a bunch of virtual Rock Star outfits. If you're looking for crazy skill based game play, this might not be for you... but if you're looking for an artful escape for a few hours - you might like this psychedelic ride ♥ Now I'm off for my Victory Lap. ♥
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: I despite the short amount of time over a single sitting it took to finish this game, it didn't feel like a small game. This Psychedelic Rock Opera for the Stars, despite not being much in the gameplay department, felt like so much fun based around the vibes and character of the game. Definitely worth checking out.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful art style and sound design.  Story is very well told, yet not entirely linear in an open ended sense and the message is something anyone of any age can learn from.  Sound track is wonderful and the game is fun top to bottom.  A must play yet sad I cannot experience it again so I shall quote my favorite character "I am overcome with sorrow!"
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: A musical saga of self-discovery, with stunning attention to detail, a star-studded cast, and supersonic shredding.A journey, a trip, a moment, a message; an artful escape.Thankyou, Beethoven & Dinosaur. I'll remember this for the rest of my days.- The Maniacal Marowi, from Worblewerd, soloist of the first intergalactic transmission.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed every minute of this game, a huge smile plastered across my face the whole way, and tears welling up at the end. I struggle to find the words to describe it, but fortunately better wordsmiths than I have already done that;"Psychedelic perfection. The Artful Escape is a game full of surprisingly deep messages about what it means to be authentic, to make impactful art, and to prove others' expectations of us wrong." - Wired"An unforgettable psychedelic journey of self-discovery across the cosmos" - CNET"A tour de force of light and sound, The Artful Escape is unlike anything else you've played." - GameSpew"Truly quite the visual trip. It's best approached as a series of multi-coloured dreamscapes / spectacular album covers. Hard to do it justice - in motion, it's a thing of beauty with a booming soundtrack to match." - Stephen McNeice"The Artful Escape is one of the most captivating games I have ever played. Stunning in every scene, poetic dialogue and a soundtrack that makes this a truly unique experience." - Samuel Bateman"A wondrous trip down the rabbit hole." - Dexerto"The Most Beautiful Indie Game of 2021" - Forbes"10/10; This one's a no-brainer; you absolutely, positively have no reason to miss it." - Strevivor"The Artful Escape is my Game of the Year so far. A cinematic wonderland of color, sound, and emotion unlike anything I've ever experienced." - Tim Gettys"A psychedelic trip through a glam-rock wonderland, an utter visual delight." - Explosion Network"The Artful Escape is a space opera about legacy, self-discovery, and identity. The world-building and creativity are beyond anything I've seen in a game... and it gets even wilder as you go on." - Checkpoint Gaming"The Artful Escape is a beautiful symphony of sight and sound that kept me completely enraptured for every single step of the adventure. It’s unlike anything I’ve ever played before, and I absolutely love it for that." - Marty Silvia"Like conducting a psychedelic alien orchestra set to acid rock. Breathtaking visuals, sonic bliss, and Carl Weathers. The Artful Escape should be on your radar." - GamesRadar+"Annapurna is back with one of the best games of the year; The Artful Escape is a surprise contender for GOTY and everyone needs to go and play it." - "The Artful Escape plays like a psychedelic jam band and tells a story like someone spiked Wes Anderson's Darjeeling tea with a few drops of acid." - "Another indie gaming debut has been given the stage by Annapurna Interactive, and 'The Artful Escape' may be one of its greatest-ever releases." - GameTripperUKMy one fairly small complaint is that the gameplay isn't  engaging, relatively speaking. It's primarily a story-driven game, no doubt, but that isn't to say your inputs don't matter or don't feel important, or that you'll ever be the least bit bored. The gameplay may be light, but the experience is big.So go play it. It's best played in one sitting, if you can (about five hours), with a good sound system or headphones. Trust me.Oh, and you can pet the dog.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: A story about a boy dealing with identity problems living in the shadows of his uncle while trying to become an artist of his own.The artstyle is fantastic and the music is great, aswell as you can (and should) add your own music by running around playing your guitar, it affect the landscape and it is just such a nice laid back game that is just "run to the right" most of the time.I 100% enjoyed the game though it is short, between 3-4 hours I would say if you just rush through it, but with some exploring and talking to everyone it can be more like 4-5 hours.10/10 - do recommend, the music like I said is great, the artstyle is gorgeous, you are now the artist of your story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Charming story with a good message; great scenery, good voice acting, good music, this was a very nice game that captivated me from the very start. It's a narrative game though, so don't expect too much gameplay. It has some light platforming and simon says minigames in the style of Wandersong. If Wandersong was your thing, you might enjoy this too. I know I did.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: If you had told me a month ago that I would soon be playing the most visually appealing game I had ever seen, I would have said "Who are you?  How did you get in here?  I'm calling the cops!"But you know something?  You were right.  I'm sorry I had you arrested.The Artful Escape is mostly a walk through a trippy neon art gallery, only you're playing a guitar the whole time.  Toss in a dash of humor, and a story about losing yourself to find yourself, or even someone else, and you've got a winner on your hands.Somehow I missed this one when it came out, or I would have been voting for it in multiple categories in the awards.  It's just that cool.  No stress, you can't ever really lose, just a really fun trip down memory lane, even though those memories haven't happened yet, and are in space, and have a laser light show. Elegant Otter is the commander of the Heavy Metal Light Brigade, and is a .
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: A very unique, master-class demonstration of the phrase "more than the sum of its parts".Is it a combination of the "Simon Says" toy, mild platforming, and constantly holding down the Shift button to riff random space-rock?Sure, in the same way that a fine piece of art is just some colored gunk smeared on a grubby piece of cloth.It's pretty to look at, and my gawd, is it gorgeous to listen to.It's... FUN, and though it only took me 5 hrs to finish, it  a lot longer to me.It's forgiving, if you have clumsy fingers like me, but I felt like a  when I nailed several sequences in a row.It's even forgiving of goofed simon-says bits, as each checkpoint only sets you back 4-5 chords.It's friggin' , in all the right ways.The only criticisms I have are on the platforming - "died" on several a blind jumps, when I couldn't tell if I needed a double-jump or a double-jump-and-dash.  You respawn just before tho, so it's not a huge issue.Oh, and I found it easier to nail the Simon-says bits when I remapped those controls to use both WASD and Left/Right/Up - YMMV.So.. TL;DR?  If you like music and wanna pretend you're an up-and-coming rock-guitar player, get it.  Get it on sale if you want, but I'd say it's worth $20 if you can't wait to play.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a huge masterpiece music video. A mixture of "The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy" and your favorite rock concert with all these AWESOME guitar riffs and solos.The game has no hard battle or puzzle mechanic. It's not for challenge, it's for soul.Start of the game was a bit dull, but it changes pretty fast and after that it's really hard to stop playing it.I love it! It's a real Artful Escape!5 stars for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Despite being a small project, this interactive experience packs a ton of visual and musical extravaganza to behold! Yes, experience, since interactivity is indeed kept to a minimum. Maybe some sort of arcade system would have spiced things up, but I recognize that it would have also distracted the viewer from the artistic presentation. The mixing of alien hyper-chromatic landscapes and vast epic guitar shredding sets the right tone for an outer-world trip filled with curious creatures and very well executed animations. I have to say, the music is probably too generic and nothing really sticks at the end, but the cool characters definetly leave a mark, teaching how the most difficult yet fundamental lesson for an artist is learn to believe in himself.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: A short but sweet game. The mechanics are not that interesting, but I would also not categorize it as a game. It's an experience that uses game mechanics to help the story along. It makes you  feel like an epic rockstar.Just play the game with headphones in fullscreen, and allow yourself to be immersed by it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: imagine the most amazing painting you ever saw... and then the guy who made it talks about how terrible it is, and how great his other work is, but its just the same quality over and over until you're sick of the style of art. that is this game. its reeeeealy pretty. buts besides Simon says that's it, and it gets old fast because its just 100% all the time, no down time to stew on something, no break, an infinite climax makes you sick of climax.my """favorite""" part is the fact they keep talking about how the town the game starts in is dying, like they force it down your throat. and it looks like a paradise. the biggest issue should be the housing prices, i mean the """dying""" town looks like every coffee shop hipsters wet dream.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most beautiful games I've ever played, given that im currently going through some existencial crisis and trying to fit in society...then this game comes and changes everything, makes you see things in a way you didnt think about. Even if its a very small (5 hours first playthrough), I can say that this is my favourite game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty nifty experience with really striking visuals and a narrative about finding your own identity that resonated pretty well with me and a friend who are both very transing our genders (love too find trans narratives in media now) and it's a pretty relaxed experience overall in a pleasant way. Yeah, the guitar playing could be more... fleshed out, the platforming could be more complex, but... how simple things are gives you more time to focus on the spectacle and I think that was the right decision.If I could gripe minorly, I wish the clothes changing option came sooner than two-thirds of the way through the game, 'cause like... wow I could've used that sooner. And for as big a focus on music as this game has, the music itself is... nothing special? I dunno, the ambient shred guitar style (get a lot of Steve Vai vibes in particular) is... neat for a bit, but that's like... all the game has, no actual tunes or compositions, and I'm not wild about equating shred to talent or creativity considering how bland and samey a lot of guitar work like that tends to sound, but that's the music nerd in me speaking blah blah blah it was a pretty cool experience and I'm glad to have had it, yeah.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Best trip you can have without drugs!Not a dull moment, utter art explosion, sincere, funny writing and a wonderful message of free expression and self realization.It is not a walking sim, some people just calls everything a walking sim. Gameplay consists of dialouge choices, light platforming and Simon-Says-musical-numbers. I struggled with several bossfights/performances so I wouldn't say it's completely devoid of challenge (at least if you struggle to remember patterns and also then have trouble with new patterns following), even though it is straight forward and you'll get infinite chances.Best played with controller for sure, keyboard is a bit clunky, but it works.I'm not a fan of wailing electric guitars myself but I still enjoyed the heck out of this!
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: It's just kind of a vibe, if the vibe were any less good then it would ultimately be pretty boring. The music, the art design, the wackiness, and the simple yet really meaningful story all combine together to keep you distracted from the fact you are pretty much just holding forward and the button that makes you play sick guitar solos. In that way it is a testament to how good the rest of the game is that I didn't give a ♥♥♥♥ and just marveled at the ride. Far out.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: YAWN!  All these great graphics and voiceover artists and this wonderful cosmic music... and ABSOLUTELY ZERO challenge to the gameplay.  Go one direction... tirelessly... holding down the guitar... and jump over holes/pits.  THAT's IT!  That's the entire "game" aspect of this "visual novel."   Over and Over and Over.I was quite disappointed as this is a prime example of 'style-over-substance."  A lot of missed opportunity to make the "Repeat After Me" button pushing aspect more challenging... or to add a small rhythm game during performance parts... HELL... ANYTHING other than the pre-school gameplay demonstrated here.  Almost like they HAD to put controller functions into this graphic novel or they wouldn't be able to sell it as a 'game.'What pisses me off the most is that the game deals with more mature themes like death, and popularity... living in the shadow of a popular family member, etc... but has the play-style that wouldn't challenge a 6 year old.  Just a huge, dis-appointing gap between the artistic approach and the game design.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: If you've read the reviews you know what you're getting here. Beautiful artistic design, gorgeous sound and very little game-play. Oh yeah, not much game-play at all, limited to the most basic of button prompts and platforming. But that's not the point of this 'game'. The point is to experience a vibrant visual/musical display while engaging with a somewhat peculiar story. And peculiar it is! But that doesn't detract from the great performances from a great cast that works around a plot that can be compared to the likes of Hitchhikers Guide to the Galaxy.I won't go on much as the lack of challenging game-play made me disengage half way through. However! If the concept does peak your interest, then it is well worth the $28.85AUD as there isn't another indie game like this one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game, in fact one of the best games I have ever played. But there're serious bugs with the keyboard control that just make the whole game unplayable. I just got stuck at one chapter due to a bug, and there's no way to solve the problem or keep playing. It's such a shame because the music and art design of the game is absolutely amazing. So PLEASE FIX IT!
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: I really love artsy walking simulators, I appreciate any game that tries to take you on a journey, but this game for some reason couldn't do it for me no matter how hard it tries. I think the art is superb and imaginative, but all the other departments don't elevate it at all so it stays as a beautiful world that you see from afar instead of immersive experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to enjoy in The Artful Escape, but unfortunately you're left with the bittersweet feeling that this game could have been so much more if some of the creativity put in the story and in the design of the characters and locations were also implemented in a more interesting gameplay, which instead is quite lacking, particularly in the left to right sections where you just keep the same two buttons pressed the whole time. The jams are fun, but few and short.I usually appreciate even games that feature maybe little gameplay and are more like interactive experiences, and The Artful Escape is an amazing one, with gorgeous art and music and a compelling story, but, having just finished the game, the feeling of it being a missed opportunity to be more fun to play is prominent unfortunately
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: "Sports... pretty much the opposite of Story." -- Rick SanchezThis is less a game and more a story told with interactive elements, and I for one greatly prefer the games which don't try to squeeze in challenges when that isn't the point. Artful Escape fumbles this a bit with jumping challenges that break the flow and "boss fights" that ask for button prompts different from the rest of the game. However... who cares?Despite never quite achieving the kind of freedom the story-line wants, there's moment of actual JOY in this game. When Francis flies through the air, hitting a high F chrord on a guitar made of light with colorful alien landscapes flying behind him and he shouts, "WhoooOOOOOO!!!" I f@#$%ing FEEL it!  You can tell the composers and programmers are not separate teams, but multi-talented people synergizing their crafts, and the end result is...The second level has a segment where you can use all the buttons to jam improv on the guitar, and it's less Parappa on Cool mode and much more Guitar Hero. The point of those games is the vicarious thrill of creating a persona and simulating the joy of creating your own music. And for just a moment, I felt like I was also making the game. Creating it while playing it.These are the moments that make it work. The dialogue is kinda slack and there are a few eye-rolling cliches (bear in mind, this rated E-for-Everyone ;) but the execution is spot on right where it needs to be. The Game industry is starting to resemble the Music industry in a lot of ways, and to me The Artful Escape is the perfect embodiment of the best parts of that. [★★☆] If you like what you see, you'll love what you do.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: The Artful Escape is a gorgeous 2D platformer that is awfully uninspired. Everything besides the graphics are half baked at best. The story, while cute, is extremely cliche and never held my interest. The meaning is admirable. It is about a boy who is trapped in the shadow of his famous folk singer uncle. He has expectations to follow in his uncle’s footsteps by becoming his own folk musician as it is what he was “meant” to be. Of course he doesn’t like doing this and instead loves psychedelic rock. Throughout the game, the main character begins to come into his own and is eventually able to shed off the daunting shadow of his uncle’s legacy. It is a heartwarming story, but it is nevertheless a boring one. It is a back and forth between set pieces that never feels like a cohesive story. It doesn’t help that the story is so on the nose and predictable. The story is its message… that you should be whatever you want and not worry what other people think. Everything that happens contriburtes to that single belief, with nothing in-between. The gameplay is also lazy. The platforming has zero obstacle as you essentially just move you analog stick to the right. The guitar minigames are also boring. I would have enjoyed something akin to Guitar Hero, but instead we are left with a memory game which you repeat the notes of the boss you are fighting. It almost makes you wonder why the bosses are so impressed with your performances as you essentially just copy them. For being a music game, I didn’t find the music to be anything special. Certain songs were good, but they eventually all started to blend together. I’m not super into the genre, so this probably influences my decision, but the music definitely felt samey fast. As I stated, the game is beautiful and that deserves to be commended. When I first opened the game I was blown away and thought I was in for a truely special experience. Instead I was left with a game I felt was rather boring. 3/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: For the lack of interactivity this game generally has, I wish it had even less of it because holding a button to make the character do the same guitar loop all over again feels like an instant on-demand take on Chinese water torture. That made the experience so much more grating than it surely deserves to be, and it underscores the arduous repetition of much of the game's content.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: The Artful Escape is very aptly named. It is of the most visually creative videogames I have played. Do not expect interesting gameplay, as such as other Annapurna Games, The Artful Escape is more of an experience than a traditional videogame. In this case, it is a visually and musically very pleasing, trippy and weird experience in a good way. The gameplay is not deeper than shown in trailers. I only wish it was longer. The videogames industry needs more creative games (indie or not) like The Artful Escape. Please do more like this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only an hour into this game, but I think I have finally found " my " game! Visually stunning sound is fantastic. _childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This is literally the best game I've played in the last few years. A cosmic psychedelic rock opera filled with electrical energy, lasers, bursts of colors, and incredible staging. It started out as Night in the Woods and evolved into something absolutely incomparable.Highly recommend to anyone who let Glamourgonn inside and jammed with it like never before.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of my favorite games of all time.It is like a space rock opera game where you shread your way through a cosmic journey of self-discovery. It is a story telling platformer game with music playing & skateboarding mini games. Overall it is quite easy game to play with beautiful art style colours and one hell of a soundtrack.
