_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: fantastic art, great technical work with the audio, and that's it.story isn't terribly interesting and the "interactive bits" boil down to a basic side-scroller & "Simon Says". i was ready for this to end after the first 90 minutes.appreciate what they reached for, but can't help but feel like the mark was missed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Visually stunning, though of little substance. No real skill required to play, short of basic platforming and Simon Says-ing. Which would be okay, if it left a sense of satisfaction. I've played games requiring less coordination than even this, but some of those had meaningful choices and a story that stuck with me beyond the time I spent playing the game. This... is not one of them. If you like to be railroaded on a set course while assaulted on all sides by colour and sound as you make nonsensical choices that have little effect on the outcome, this is the game for you. Unfortunately, it was not the game for me. Kudos to the art and sound department, though.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: I would wait for a sale, less then $10 for sure. I finished it because its short. Graphics are amazing, store is boring, game play does not do much to keep you engaged. This game has about 1 hour worth of great moments. Followed by 3 hours of numbness. Its worth experiencing, but don't pay full price like I did.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: at first i thought this game would offer nothing special but after watching the ign review i bought it and gave it a shot. 4 hours later i was left with the biggest grin and throughout my play through i couldnt believe what i was seeing. amazing visuals, awesome sound design, insane rifts and crazy colors everywhere. truley one of the best games ive played in a while and it actually made me want to write a review. best 4.5 hours ever. get this game you wont regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: I have to say this first. Musically and visually this is an amazing experience. As a game though, it is very boring. It feels like it is a glorified walking simulator.What you do gameplay wise is just walk right, hold a button to shred the guitar and jump. There is also very few "boss fights" where you are jamming with someone else. Which is very cool, but they are way too short in my opinion. Think the longest lasted around 5 minutes (in which most of it were spent moving left and right to walk on different platforms to stand on).Overall as an experience I would rate it positive, but as a game I will rate it negative, mostly because of the things said above.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This game is boring as hell, while playing I kept thinking when it is gonna end. I don't understand why people are liking this game. There is no game play to it, not fun at all. Graphically I cannot look closely to it, everything are 2D sticked into 3D space, and I can hardly appreciate it. I do not think making everything lid up and sparkling on my screen is beautiful. The animation and facial movement is really repetitive, feels cheap as ♥♥♥♥. I cannot complain enough about this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: THIS GAME IS THE MOST FULFILLING GAME I HAVE EVER HAD THE EXTREME PLEASURE OF PLAYING!  I absolutely love rhythm games and this game amazed me beyond the trailers and gameplay videos.  I don't have enough words in the english language to describe how I felt playing this game.  There were moments where I almost teared up because of how beautiful the sounds and visuals were.  I would gladly offer my time to help test the sequel or a sequel for this game.  The people and Beethoven and Dinosaur are legends in their own right.  If you own a PC, you owe it to yourself to play this masterpiece. 20/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: An exciting and electric escape into a psychedelic sci fi musical experience. This game had those coming of age story vibes like a Disney or Dreamworks movie. An inspiring game for any budding musicians or anyone trying to become something more than themselves. The whole game is shredding psychedlic electro rock with very beautiful and vibrant visuals throughout. The concepts of the worlds, the characters and the lingo is very far out and gives that very strong 80s electro retro rock wave. More of a story game. There wasnt much difficulty other than inputting commands to shred your guitar and run and jump across the creative worlds. I had fun playing this although it can get a bit monotonous at times but the weird and wonderful art and sci fi plot makes up for it. Definitely a game for the mushroom heads and stoners to dive into!
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: The Artful Escape is a true Feast for the Senses...I loved every second of this game. The world is created to be explored with both eyes and ears. It is not a complicated platformer adventure as it's intended to be an exploration game so do not expect some crazy boss battles and enemy creatures.I did receive the game for review purposes but this did not affect my opinion on the game. I give this game a must experience as it offers something truly unique that you will not find anywhere out there. Enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: , what a game, easily dismissible as a beautifully realized musical adventure (I have more screenshots of this game than any other put together) however a little naive and dumb.However, it could also lend itself well to interpretations of much deeper stuff, so it's a tossup.The opening and first trip are some of the most amazing setups and setpieces I've seen in media, from pacing, to meaning, to sheer awesomeness.Here’s the short of it:You play as a guy whose uncle is considered the best artist in the genre, so the shadow of his success looms over and indirectly decides how's the life of our protagonist will play out in order to catch even a glimmer of what a person he once was.However, our character is meant for much more, often spacing out, wanting to break free from this, until he has a fateful encounter with an alien willing to spirit him away in an adventure that's going to make him realize who he is.The remaining 2/3 of the game feels like it's trying to steal the thunder of an amazing first act only halfway succeeding, but even halfway is enough to make it a great experience, it only leaves a but of sour taste after such a great "intro".While adding to the style, the weird 2.5d aesthetic in motion often looks weird and many times restrained in their movements.Creature design starts off strong and despite travelling to the end of the galaxies, this design almost never changes.I would have liked more an adventure where it was more of a "secret life" kind of deal, where one persona the character built would want to keep the other hidden, as well as more complex themes, but that's just me never having enough.So yes, it's a relatively short experience but that's what it is, an experience, and one everyone should play for themselves.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Here's the thing. It's stylish as f**k, has some great writing, is a visual buffet....BUTAs a game, it's "hold one direction, occasionally press button" writ large.If you're able to let style win over substance for a few hours, it's worth. If you want something a bit more reflex-y...look elsewhere. HOWEVER. If you've got a "normie" family member/friend that you're trying to get into gaming, I'd use this as a gateway.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: The art and story are amazing and I'd love to dive deeper into this world. Unfortunately the actual gameplay is very very repetitive and boring. After 10 hours I was really hoping the game might open up, but even the art and story aren't deep enough to keep me interested in continuing the game. The mechanics of gameplay are so simple and repetitive it really feels unfinished. I'd much rather they cut the long sidescrolling scenes and just make this a beautiful short film or something.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This game is everything that is wrong with the modern games industry summed up into one package. It has absolutely stunning visuals, a beautifully touching story, and absolutely no gameplay whatsoever. Like they literally could've just made this into a movie and it would have been just as effective, if not moreso. Yet somehow it is beloved by critics who have stomped better games than this into the dirt for lesser issues. I don't get it, but I'm assuming mind control is involved.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This game is seriously not fun. I bought it mainly because it was on yahtzee's top 5 and it has a "Very Positive" reviews on steam.  Frankly, this game sucks.  The sound track is annoying with the main music being this terrible Bob Dylan-esk folk music, with blaring rock guitars thrown in every now and then. (and I am a guy who loves Death Metal..) The main character animation looks like a smoother version of qwop and the story was is pretty lame.  I had high hopes, was disappointed.   I played for an hour, then asked for a refund.  Save your money.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say, walking sim "games" are really hit and miss. Sometimes with games like Stanley Parable and Edith Finch, you feel richer for the experience. With this game though? Well, I played it high off my ass like I think you were intended to and still didn't enjoy it. Despite being something like 3-4 hours, I dropped it 2 hours in. I just didn't care for it. The story wasn't going anywhere and the setting, despite being a fantastical outer space, was highly underutilized. The gameplay is by and large nonexistent: the sections with platforming have zero challenge or interactivity (outside of pointless "free-styling" with a guitar), and the Simon Says boss mini-games are boring. This would have been better off as an interactive novel, but that would only highlight the fact that there is no story either. I like the protagonist but it's not clear how in his journey he's actually evolving into a new persona, which is the whole point of the story. So not only do the gameplay and story not mesh well, but more importantly it legitimately feels like neither one had any thought put into them. This whole game feels pointless.Some of the backgrounds look nice but a lot of times they come off as garish, especially since sometimes there's just a few colors used extensively throughout a scene; someone really went crazy with the purples and blues. I was really trying hard to power through it since I don't like leaving games undone, but if I'm constantly looking at the chapter select screen to measure my progress, impatiently hoping it'll be over soon, only to dread that I'm barely halfway done, then there's a problem. I can usually look past a lot of these missteps if the story is engaging enough to make me want to keep playing. But it wasn't, it was absurdly nonsensical and boring. The funny thing is I could easily have spent an hour finishing the game but didn't, I wrote this review instead. That's how tedious this crap is, that ranting about it is more fun than playing it. I could only play this game in 15 minute intervals because anything else was straining. I only heard about this game from Zero Punctuation but to be honest the more I watch it the more I realize my taste and Yahtzee's taste are basically nothing alike.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This was largely a fun game - it falls more into a bit of 'an experience' rather than actually a game but what was there I enjoyed. Turn off for most would be the fact that the 'gameplay' is largely just run to the right and occasionally jump interspersed with somelow stakes Simon Says segments. That sounds like a poor experience in words but otherwise the charm and story behind it carried it through for the relatively short run time - it's more middling than not unfortunately but I'd give it around a 6.5/10 so nice if you just want to while away an evening or two or want something in between more intense games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Annapurna really has a knack for uncovering strong concepts and providing unique, original experiences (I still haven't recovered from the impact of What Remains of Edith Finch). Once again, simple gameplay mechanics are used to tell a rich and surprising story—nothing like what I expected after watching the trailers, and I was pleasantly surprised by the twists in the narrative!This is primarily a contemplative, narrative-driven experience, but I found the story incredibly cool. The art direction and visual ideas unfold rapidly, making you eager to see the game through to the end and impatient for the next creation from Beethoven & Dinosaur. The trailers for their upcoming game Mixtape look exciting! Oh, and Jason Schwartzman voices an alien in this game. What else can I say?
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Still sitting here in shock over this game. This is hands down one of the most beautifully illustrated games I've ever played. The music, the colors, the actual characters all point to just masters of their craft.The story was a little confusing at the beginning, but at the end, it all comes together anyways and you understand the whole point of the journey. The experience of playing this game was something I LOVED. It had a plot, it had creativity, and overall, 9/10. Could not recommend enough.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Not really quite sure what to make of this game. The writing was uneven, the gameplay was middling and overall nothing stood out that much... And yet, this game has heart. It has vision. It might not be amazing vision but it is pure.And in a world of derivative, boring, cookie-cutter games that's gotta count for something. It is an audio-visual spectacle and it is rather short so I don't feel bad for the time spent. If you're looking for an intergalactic rock ballad - well, I have just the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: A nice little game reminding me of GRIS and in that way, it is not for everyone. That is to say : the emphasis is put on the artistic direction and a strong theme, alongside little to no gameplay. I liked very much the themes concerned (identity, social pressure) and the way the game manages to bring the notion of emotion which music can bring. Besides, the very basical gameplay and the lack of challenge prevents it to be as great as GRIS for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game purely on the basis of having watched the trailer for 'Mixtape' and being in awe of its style and music. I was flawed by how beautiful this game is, wondering around Calypso in the beginning I just kept taking my time, often retreading my steps just enjoying the backdrop and characters, then the game goes off the rails and I was happy to go along for the ride. Being a rock fan I very much enjoy the soundtrack and I like the guitar mini games although admittedly I tend to mess a lot of them up, much to the dismay of onlookers. I'm nearly 3 hours in and I cant wait to see where this goes.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: The Artful Escape is a colorful, vibrant and can be quite bizzare/alien-ish in its design when you explore other planets. The story is meaningful however implementation wise.For that, the story falls flat, the game does not have much replayability value. Would have been nice if they could make every choice with different outcomes/different endings. Example: what do we with lightman? Do we have options to talk to violetta at the end of the journey? Can we interact/decide the fate of the town/as captain of this ship? Does the game allow you to choose your finale; we go rock/can we still stick with folk song - why not?As for controls, on the pc, it took a while to get used to the 5 keys and combos. nothing infuriating or finger entangling crap experience.The game only offers you room for creativity and freedom when it comes to customizing your characters visually. Overall, I feel this product is very limited/restrictive and probably suitable for young audience to spark their creativity or interest in music. For those looking for a more open/to express yourself freely, will find it very disappointing with the direction of this game. For those who are looking for something different and just want to experience a simple story, will be dazzled by its vibrant colors and art style, rock tunes and some funny dialogues.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: The Artful Escape isn't so much a game as an experience, a game-sized cinematic spacey dream sequence symphonic opera wailing guitar solo hallucination adventure. That's a word salad, but that sums up what the game is like. If you want to experience some symphonic guitar and metaphoric rambling dialogue, this is your game. This is one of those games that doesn't last long, but all the time it does last is really high quality.Mechanically, it's got some 2D traversing (not really platforming) and some Simon-Says. It's all pretty easy and very linear.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Don't know if this review will work because the game is from my family library. But it's an incredibly personal tale about finding one's identity (as an artist? As a person?), going from straight-faced (but still beautiful!) folk music, to epic, sci-fi guitar rock (and I'm only a few hours in, such has it inspired me to write a review). Both genres I love, and I could see elements of my own artistic journey in the writing. This is a game less about game design, and everything about playable narrative and art. It’s vastly creative, imaginative, immaculate and beautiful.Anyway, enough blathering, I've got a musical sci-fi space opera to get back to! I also didn't expect the free-form guitar playing it has just introduced - Space Channel 5 Simon Says is great, but I have a feeling I'm gonna be able to improv my way to superstardom too. Bring on Mixtape!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: The Artful Escape is a whimsical adventure of self-discovery and self-determinization, told through the lens of a musician living in the shadow of a famous relative and having to adhere with the expectations set for him. While light on gameplay, the four hours it took me to get through this game were great, with incredibly dense environments to traverse through, all of which were reactive to music I played, gorgeous art direction, and excellent voice acting. The soundtrack of this game is phenomenal, with a range of genres on display, and the story was well-written and well-told. I thoroughly enjoyed my time with this game, and recommend it to anyone with a deep love of music.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: I dont really review games on steam often but wow, this is an amazing experience! Very beautiful game, has a lot of heart and the art and music are top notch! The guitar simon says segments are hit and miss and you're not allowed to hit notes too fast or else it just doesnt count for some reason, but aside from that everything else is simple but amazing
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever asked yourself: "what is my purpose?"And if you have asked so, continued on the barrage with: "what sets my purpose apart from others?", "have I learned enough to know and perfect my purpose?", "can my purpose ever be something unique?"After sieging yourself like that with the questions, if you have came out alive but light gone from your eyes:This game will fill your eyes back with flames of ever burning sun.You will be the next star, if you know how to take your lesson, like you know how to question.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a rhythm/music game, and while it has platformer sections, I consider it more of an interactive narrative experience, with the way the platformer sections and music are designed lending itself to the emotions of the story. It's almost more if you could play a musical, and I recommend it for that feeling, the narrative themes, and the solidly eclectic art style.

_childDocuments_.review: For this review, we’re going to need to set some ground rules. The first of these is that the author is dead, and in engaging with this game, we killed that author together. The moment a story leaves its creator’s head, that creator is dead to it, serving only as an egg from which something independent emerged. The media is not some fluffy baby goose, sitting in terror as its author-mother hisses at passers-by. It emerges, fully formed, from Zeus’ thigh, prepared to be marveled at for what it is, not for its origins, but for itself and itself alone.The second is that there are many readings of any given piece of media. Their validity is determined not by what they are, but by how well they are supported by the text. My reading may not be your reading, but it is no less valid. And third, trans rights are human rights.Let’s go.The Artful Escape is an adventure game. The player plays as Francis Vendetti, a young guitar player and nephew of the local hero and famous folk singer, Johnson Vendetti. While he has undeniable talent with the guitar, Francis is constantly expected to live up to his uncle’s reputation, following in his uncle’s footsteps and becoming a folk singer. As Francis prepares for his very first public show, he gets the chance to explore other avenues and identities, and to truly decide who and what he could be once free from the weight of others’ expectations and the identities they have assigned him. The Artful Escape’s story, fundamentally, is about self-discovery and becoming who we believe we are meant to be. However, I’d also argue that, more than simply being a game about self-discovery, the Artful Escape is also a narrative about trans identity and an expression of trans joy.The Artful Escape focuses on the ideas of engaging and forging one’s own identity throughout the game. It’s not a unique theme - and indeed, the fact that the protagonist is 17 means this in some ways feels like a young adult game more than anything, and young adults focus very much on forging their identities - but its particular expression here caught my eye. Francis is continuously faced with opportunities to remake every element of himself, from his past to his look to his future, and choose to create not just a musical identity, but an entirely new being to become. By the end of the game, Francis has ceased to be, replaced by whatever persona he has created for himself along the way. He is no longer trapped in an identity he knows was wrong for him, but is instead embracing and in turn embraced by something that better reflects who he actually is. Francis’ fear about the people of Calypso finding out who he is also mirrors the fear felt by many LGBTQ+ - and trans people specifically - around coming out of the closet and the repercussions they’ll face if they do come out. While I am not trans, I am queer, and have several trans friends. That fear of being seen by those who know you, and the experimentation with identity in a safer space resonates. When Francis tries on a new name and new outfit that more accurately reflects him, I am cheering him on, not just for him, but for all the people who do the same, and don’t necessarily have the chance to become who they are in a public way. It’s the sheer joy of self-discovery and the absolute joy in resolving the paradox of identity that makes the Artful Escape a thing of beauty, though. We live in a world that increasingly and dangerously politicises identity, especially that of LGBTQ+ people, and most especially trans identities. The common mainstream narrative of trans identity is an identity of struggle, sorrow, and pain. Indeed, the most common defenses of things like gender-affirming care are framed in terms of suicide rates of people who do not have access to this care, of pain caused through dysphoria, of broken homes, and people abandoned. The narrative of the trans experience we hear most often is one of opposition and mitigation, and while gender-affirming care is a positive within this context, it is still a positive that serves to mitigate the negatives of being trans. Trans identity, in this context, is a hardship that must be survived, endured, and mitigated.The Artful Escape doesn’t frame being caught in an assigned identity in this way, and I love it for that. It is a game about joy, about forging who we are, and the joy that stems from being liberated from an assigned identity. It’s about the joy of creating a found family and choosing where we’re from instead of having it forced upon us. It’s about the colour and music that come when given the freedom to be who we are, and it’s wonderful. My love of the Artful Escape is, admittedly, stemming from what the game is rather than how well it works as a game. As a game, it has its flaws. Much of it feels more like a walking simulator than an adventure game, which is fine. I found its keyboard controls to be sticky and clunky, and its music sections are all too brief. However, these mechanical flaws are far, far outweighed by the bombasity of the game itself. Its art and music are incredible, evoking a version of outer space that is as joyous and alive as the narrative itself. It’s a world I wanted to explore every inch of, just to see what music awaited me, and what wonderful creature I might see next. This is coupled with writing that is an effective blend of Python-esque humour and something like Wallace and Gromit, where characters take themselves seriously, while also softly acknowledging the absurdity of the world around them. When combined, the art, music, and writing just accentuate the sheer joy of the character, creating an experience that just leaves the player with a massive smile. I loved the Artful Escape. It’s a game about joy, about authenticity, and about the pride in being who we are. It is amazing.If you enjoyed this review, please check out the  as well as  Thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: "A psychedelic journey about finding yourself as well as finding dope ass planets to jam across. What a phenomenal game, thank you Beethoven & Dinosaur." - me, stoned, 3 minutes after beating the game.Upon reflection, this game really IS phenomenal. It's artistic direction and overall message to the player is both heartwarming and sick af. It's not a very long game, but it sticks with you. I'll be due for a replay at some point and I just know I'll enjoy it just as much. Highly recommend to anyone even slightly interested in a simple, albeit trippy, journey with pretty cool guitar shredding (even though it's some simple ass button prompts)
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: As a metaphor for or meditation on the nature of artistic identity and inspiration, it works. There are moments when the raw creative joy of making music, or art generally, peeks through the otherwise simple mechanics of pressing one, two, or three buttons "when you're ready" (ad infinitum).As a game, though, it leaves much to be desired; the platforming is floaty and sticky, the musical jams incredibly basic and short, and the exploration of the sets a bit tedious and one-note. To my taste, the writing is also a bit self-important and pretentious at times (a Colorado town filled with Bob-Dylan-loving hipsters) - a sort of twee, sense-making through nonsense schtick - but I'll admit it ties together neatly when it comes full circle to its campy, earthy conclusion; in other words, when it takes itself less seriously or grounds itself.If you're interested in music, metaphysical takes on the nature of making art, or interested in an alternative media take on Ziggy Stardust, you might have a fun, if brief, trip.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: The Artful Escape could be called an interactive music video. A very long music video, relatively. Its main strengths are: beautiful visuals, very nice electric guitars, simple but quite enjoyable story and - this one is the most important - psychedelic sci-fi aesthetics.If you're looking for a rhythm game, look elsewhere. While the game has (few and short) segments where you need to push the right buttons in the right order to produce sounds, they - similarly to sections where you run to the right while jumping over things - pose no challenge at all. The game is just super easy and even if you mess up, you're not punished in any way.But that's clearly not the point of this game. You play it for amazing views and music. And it's very fun for what it is. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: A pleasant enough experience, with somewhat thin gameplay consisting of simple platforming, occasional sequence-matching challenges and some freestyle segments where you can just play whatever notes you like while.The art is very nice, with a good range of colors on display - at first, you're on Earth, enjoying relatively grounded natural beauty. A little later on, things get wild, weird and wonderful. It's nice to see real imagination, artists being genuinely creative. Some may find it a bit much, or find themselves desensitized to this kind of visual feast by similar games - or by this game in itself, toward the end.The story exists largely to facilitate your character's personal journey. You have several opportunities to tailor this evolutionary trip to your liking, but as is inevitable, there are some limitations and your character has an overall vibe he's leaning toward. Still, there's a good amount of customization options available once you get to somewhere around the halfway point of the game.As a creative work and enjoyable narrative experience, I'd give it a recommendation, but be aware: This is not a particularly cost-effective game in terms of play hours to price. I'd argue it still has merit as a distinctive and enjoyable time to be had, just don't expect to be playing it for weeks on end. It's a fun-sized bite of gorgeous goodness.Recommended overall, but maybe wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an epic journey that I keep coming back to. Fantastic psychedelic visuals, great music, and an original story about a musician finding his own, authentic sound while dealing with the expectations of others.Not a game in the traditional sense, if you’re looking for a lot of gameplay and action. Let the story and the protagonist’s transformation draw you in and go on this trip through space and sound.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: A little on the short side (5 hours), but overall a fantastic experience. Reminded me of a higher production, musical version of Limbo or Inside; where the gameplay is simple but the atmosphere and environmental story telling is incredible. I wish the bosses had longer simon says sequences that were a bit more challenging, but outside of that the game has an identity and never strays from it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute Masterpiece! Yes, the gameplay is super simplistic but if you enjoy meaningful and inspiring indie titles that don't play by the rules you will simply not care. It is gorgeous in art and sound. It is masterfully crafted and most importantly... it will touch your heart and will either spark something that you might have lost or breathe life into your soul like it did for me. Please do yourself a favor and play it! Oh and since you are here I wonder... have you ever considered becoming someone else entirely?
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most visually and auditorily stunning games I've ever played. The art direction and sound design were definitely the stars of the show. It was a treat to experience.This is mostly a story-driven experience, so the gameplay itself is a bit simple. The platforming is extremely easy and the musical sections are very uninvolved. It seems like this was meant to be a chill experience in the vain of games like Journey or ABZU, so none of these things really detract from the experience.The voice acting is also excellent thanks to the talented and experienced cast of actors.

It is an experience for sure, not one for everyone, with 0 repalayability outside of changing words 20 is steep.  Get it on sale, rock on
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: A unique music-focused narrative game with arthouse vibes that I should love in theory. Beautiful visuals and music. The gameplay swaps between story beats, simple platforming, and rhythm game button tapping to the music. Maybe I wasn't in the right mood, but for me none of these game elements stood out enough. I liked the soul of the story, but the somewhat pretentious presentation kept me too distant to be truly invested. Mixed feelings on this one. Would recommend if you're really into this kind of thing, otherwise not really a must-play in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Played this game tripping sack and it was the perfect length where I was on the come down as the game ended. Fabulous story, and I don't think I've ever played a game with this art style before personally. The lighting in the game is incredible and the way the environment works in the game had me shredding as often as I could. I really liked how the game isn't that challenging. Not that challenge is bad, but it isn't required for a character to grow. You follow along the protagonist, and see him deal with his own, interpersonal, challenges. This is more an interactive visual/audio masterpiece than a video game, and I hope you experience it for yourself.SignedThe Almighty Cringe

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a majestic masterpiece of sci-fi space psychedelia guitar riffs of the hands forged by titans themselves of rock' n' roll. With the visuals of what any and every space explorer, wrapped with the inspiration of becoming who you want to be. Such a one in a life time experience that i wish i could forget to experience fresh again. I highly recommend this game to anyone wanting an escape or even just a place for the moment, this is the game. Well worth the play.

_childDocuments_.review: The Artful Escape : By Triple FIn the vast and diverse realm of video games, it's a rare gem that manages to seamlessly blend visual artistry, musical prowess, and heartfelt storytelling. "The Artful Escape," developed by Beethoven & Dinosaur and published by Annapurna Interactive, is one such gem that pushes the boundaries of what a video game can be. With its kaleidoscopic visuals, mind-bending narrative, and ethereal musical score, it crafts an experience that feels more like a surreal dream than a traditional game.From the moment you step into the world of "The Artful Escape," it's evident that you're about to embark on an otherworldly adventure. The game's visuals are a mesmerizing fusion of hand-painted landscapes, neon-infused sci-fi realms, and surreal cosmic vistas. Each environment feels meticulously crafted, inviting players to immerse themselves in a visual tapestry that's as much a work of art as it is a gaming backdrop. The sheer diversity of the worlds you traverse keeps the experience feeling fresh and continually awe-inspiring.At its core, "The Artful Escape" is a story of self-discovery and creative liberation. Players assume the role of Francis Vendetti, a teenage folk musician burdened by his family's musical legacy. The game takes a delightful twist when Francis embarks on a fantastical journey through alternate dimensions, assuming a new persona that enables him to explore the uncharted territories of his own imagination. The narrative dances between reality and fantasy, grappling with themes of identity, artistic expression, and the struggle to find one's place in a world of expectations.Music isn't just an accompaniment in "The Artful Escape"; it's the very soul of the game. The original soundtrack, composed by Johnny Galvatron, is a sonic marvel that seamlessly melds genres, mirroring the game's boundary-breaking ethos. The music evolves as Francis' journey unfolds, embracing everything from folk and rock to synth-infused psychedelia. Each musical piece complements the visual splendor, creating an immersive experience where the line between sound and imagery blurs into a symphony of emotions.While "The Artful Escape" leans more towards interactive storytelling than traditional game-play mechanics, it strikes a harmonious balance between exploration, dialogue choices, and occasional rhythm-based sequences. This balance keeps players engaged without overshadowing the game's primary focus – the journey itself. The interactive moments serve as conduits for narrative progression, allowing players to shape Francis' responses and decisions, making the experience feel uniquely personal.All in all, "The Artful Escape" is a breathtaking testament to the power of creative expression and the boundless potential of interactive storytelling. It defies conventional definitions, transcending the labels of 'game' and 'art' to become a transformative experience. With its evocative visuals, mind-bending narrative, and a soundtrack that resonates deep within, this game invites players to step into the shoes of a young musician searching for his true self. In doing so, it compels us all to explore the uncharted dimensions of our own imagination.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game with pretty high expectations, considering I have played a few other Annapurna titles and thought they were great. No joke, this game came out well above my already high expectations. IT MADE ME FEEL LIKE A KID AGAIN! A little cheesy, but so heartfelt and smile-inducing. I haven't felt like this from a game in a VERY LONG TIME>>> buy it and enjoy the story and the feels.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is pretty simple: a sidescroller with some simon-says to play the guitar. But it's visually stunning, the story is gripping, the voice acting is fantastic, and even the silly way the guitar playing affects the environment as you move along is fun and engaging. Save the world with your guitar.

_childDocuments_.review: The Artful Escape is a rock opera masquerading as a musical platforming game from the Australian development studio Beethoven & Dinosaur. The Artful Escape follows Francis Vendetti, a teenage guitar prodigy bristling under others' expectations. An improbable encounter catapults him into a universe-spanning, mind-expanding adventure. Francis sheds his past and discovers who he wants to be.The gameplay shifts between three loops. The first is exploration and conversations with NPCs. The second is light platforming. The third is playing music by copying button presses, emulating playing different notes.However, the gameplay is almost unimportant. It is more something to do while gawking at the supersaturated visuals and basking in the music. Holding "X" on the controller allows Francis to improvise on the guitar ("shred") as he runs, leaps and slides through alien landscapes. I could not wipe the grin off my face from the sheer joy and spectacle. The Artful Escape's universe has a Douglas Adams-like absurdity and comedy. For example, Francis Vendetti flies a warp turtle through the cosmic extraordinary to a starship called The Galactic Lung. He visits the Hyperion Wailzone, where the danger level is "dolphin". The game's music is a love letter to the 1980s, particularly psychedelic rock. Much of the inspiration and music come from Johnny Galvatron, one of the developers. He fronted the band "The Galvatrons" in Australia and the UK in the late 2000s. The Artful Escape is part celebration, parody and critique of the music industry.Unfortunately, The Artful Escape is short, taking about five hours to finish. Those looking for challenges or meaningful choices will be disappointed. Sometimes holding "X" while jumping or moving is awkward.However, The Artful Escape is bursting with spectacle, absurdity and glee. Its message is hopeful and empowering. It is a fairy tale for the rock era, a monument to the joy of music and self-actualization.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: It's a game where at any time you can pull out a Glowing Neon Guitar and Shred.The vast majority of the "Serious" Dialogue is way too on the nose and it sounds like audio from a Therapy TV show, and all of the other Dialogue sounds like an AI tried to write a Terry Pratchett Sci-fi book, but it juxtaposes nicely with the Therapy TV show stuff, so it comes off much better.Gameplay is a simplistic Platformer with occasional Simon Says mini games, which is unfortunate, but it's hard to be bothered by it when the entire game is an utter delight of sights and sounds. It's somewhat short but not unreasonably priced, only had one major crash, and I enjoyed myself from start to finish.I am The Wonderous Delusion.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: It’s like if someone story boarded while on acid and someone else made a game out of it without compromising the vision.The game is a trip of unique sounds, visuals, and weird story about a far away place of aliens, concerts, music, a lung spaceship, and a giant killer moth. It’s also about a guy in not Portland trying to fill the shoes of not Bob Dylan while he really wants to rock. The setup makes you think it’s going to be a normal “believe in yourself plot” which it ultimately is but the journey is spread out with this insanity which kinda works to force this uncomfortable kid to evolve and take responsibility for this new persona. The gameplay is weak as you basically hold right. There is platforming and simon says music playing which you can fail but it’s ultimately a walking simulator (with minor adventure game story elements). I think this could have been a trip of continuous platforming while you wail away at guitar solos but overall, it’s a walking sim which you may or may not like. I thought it was fun to just wail and walk with beautiful music playing and the environment reactingOverall, the story, visuals, and environment has to carry it and while it's weird and trippy, the overarching message is just an artist being weird and trying to find themselves. It’s a bit hokey but I had fun with it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome! Especially if you like some trippy stuff, deep conversations and beautiful artwork, you should try this game.More than once I asked myself what kind of drugs the devs took :D, but it's fantastic. I wished there would have been more (and bit more complexe) Simon Says stages because I really love Simon Says and was evry happy having such stuff in a game but ofc you can't have everything. :D
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: I truly love everything about this game. The visuals, the story, characters and mainly the sound blew me away with the quality and care the creators put into The Artful Escape. I really like guitars and maybe that helped me to fell for this game, but I honestly think that everyone who likes music and sci-fi will be blown away. Play the game and you will probably end up buying the soundtrack as well to keep something from that oddly amaizing trip through the universe of weird creatures and loud guitar shredding.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: I picked up The Artful Escape from Fanatical during a sale in summer 2022.  It had been on my wishlist for some time and the sale price was quite good.The game has excellent,- Visual Style- Music- Narrative and Storytelling- CreativityThe middle ground,- Gameplay Mechanics are simple.- Limited Exploration, linear path with no side paths or hidden areas.The game doesn’t have any bad points.As there are no different paths to take, once you finish the game there isn’t anything to bring you back in.  Maybe replay it down the road.To leisurely complete the game along with all the achievements (some are missable), it is about 6-7 hours.Highly recommended, especially on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This is an experience unlike any I have ever had in over a decade.  And I mean that literally.This is not a 'game'.  This is an 'EXPERIENCE'.If any of this aesthetic interests you, the open yourself to it and walk it's paths.  Allow it to sing within your bones and illuminate your mind until you blossom as a new being!I have not felt this level of awe and child-like wonderment since before my age had a second digit.  I didn't know I still  feel such joy anymore.May your journey speak to you as mine spoke to me.

_childDocuments_.review: There aren't many games out there that make you "think". I'm not talking about Myst, or any puzzle aspects. This game makes you question your existence. It challenges you with a narrative that opens your "minds-eye" and really makes you ponder who you're trying to impress during your life. I would play this again if able, I loved it. It was truly an amazing experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so beautiful it's physically painful. Wildly imaginative and grand in scale, it's a delight to look at and a blast to play. The linear story stays engaging by offering the player many options to build their own persona, allowing for a great deal of personal connection with Francis Vendetti and the game itself. As an artistic person trapped in their small hometown, the themes of the story hit me like a ton of bricks. I don't think I'd played for half an hour before I realized that this is my new favorite game. By like, a lot. I wish I could convey to you through the wholly inadequate medium of language how mind-blowingly, earth-shatteringly great this game is. If you love art, music, self-discovery, and stories of human triumph, then this one's for you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: this is one of my favorite games. the gameplay isn't really complicated. it is just pressing a button and running in one direction. altough the game is so simple it is really enjoyable with the awesome music and the great art style. the story is about a young men questioning who he wants to be. the game is filled with funny creatures and a great sense of humor. if you like the music from the trailer and enjoy a more simple gameplay then this is your game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of fun jumping, sliding, and launching around absolutely beautiful scenery and creative aliens while jamming on the guitar. My wife and I alternated playing different parts of it. The first 10 minutes are just about building up the story, which is a little slow, but it gets more fun after that. We finished it over the course of two days. Took about 5 hours total. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished this game, I am a multi-instrumental musician, but primary in guitar. I was moved to tears by the phenomenal music and the powerful message on the importance of confidence, courage, and finding oneself. An amazing game with a story that will leave you with a profound personal revelation.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: It's really difficult for me to give a thumbs down to this game because I think this is a great game in some aspects and there were also moments in the game that I enjoyed it, but since I've refunded it, it made no sense for me to recommend it.As anybody can see, it is just delightful to look at this game, the visual is great and what has fascinated me the most was the sound design of this game, it is superb! but unfortunately on the other hand, the gameplay is lacking, it could be just because they tried to make this game as relaxing as possible and it kind of turned into a walking simulator. the story is also not interesting enough (at least wasn't for me). those two reason made this game boring and repetitive after a while and despite very enjoyable arts and music I had to refund it.But regardless, I advise you to at least try this game and see if it is for you or not.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: My "recommend" comes with a couple of significant caveats. You may be annoyed if you spend more than $7 on this.This is an EXTREMELY short game (and I generally take ages to finish a game). The path is strictly linear and there are no collectables or any other reason to explore the environment. Achievements are attained through playing the game (and 99% of them take no effort).The gameplay aspects of this are pretty weak. It would call itself a rhythm game, but it's not, since timing is irrelevant.The music borders on repetitive, but if you're into it, that won't be an issue.I know i appear to have a lot of negative opinions about this game, and you may be wondering why I would then recommend it. It's because I've never played anything that looked, sounded, or felt like this. Even with as little as I was doing, my mouth was stunned open by the beauty of everything happening.As a game it may be a little disappointing and leave you wanting more (or wishing there was less of it), but as an experience? ...imagine Laser Floyd was a videogame. Alter appropriately and enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: A masterpiece driven by visuals, music and a deeply rooted narrative. To call this a game would be slightly unfair as this experience is more directed towards telling a story. In terms of actual playability, this game offers little, that come in the form of a memory game. But in terms of an experience this game delivers some of the best music and visuals to ever come from an indie game.The game features a space age, vaporwave, psychedelia driven art-style combined with a heavily emphasized dichotomy between small town and comforting folk music versus the infinite and exploratory but risky realm of space rock. As the protagonist of this game, you will be taken on a journey beyond reality as you grow and come of age to rid yourself of your past weights and build your persona as the best guitarist in the galaxy. Through the plot you'll come across various characters who will share equal parts whim and wisdom and help you find yourself in the process.I will not be enlisting pros or cons for this game as this game is so indie that it is more of an experience than a game. You really won't find yourself stressing out over losing lives, or over a Game Over screen. Instead, you'll be controlling the main character through a beautifully handcrafted (and 2D platformed?) world unravelling the story gradually and falling in love with the characters and the music in the process.I would recommend this game to anyone with a tiny bit of patience and an interest in music and/or art. This game is a must experience for artists who are struggling with their identity or looking for inspiration. It is a breath of fresh air into the art-blocked mind and has the potential to reignite the creative spark that may have diminished.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful, short little game with a really fun and even somewhat inspiring story about a musician trying to escape from under his much-more-succesful uncle's shadow; very minimal gameplay, that can be summed up as half extremely-basic-platformer, and half Simon-says; a really fun soundtrack, and genuinely stunning graphics.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: I believe video games are art, and I believe the people that make video games are artists. This is a work of art, and it's one of the most beautiful video game experiences I've ever had, both visually and musically. It is also a deeply personal story about an artist discovering their true self, and the love that was poured into this game to tell this story is apparent from the start. Simply put, it's beautiful in every respect.Don't come into this game expecting deep gameplay, though. It's interactive fiction with a smidge of 2D platforming and musically-themed minigames, but that's fine, that's not the point of the game. Again, this is a work of art in the medium of a video game.If you're an artist of any variety, especially if you're young and still in the early stages of your life's journey, you need to play this game. Even if you're not, though, this is a beautiful story that's definitely worth experiencing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This is a heartwarmingly beautiful 2D adventure game--a touching depiction of adolescent wonder and angst, playing as a Buddy Holly lookalike blooming into an artist of your own styling, and meeting likable, well-written characters along the way.On your journey, there are a few platforming and rhythm section, and these can get a little annoying when playing with mouse and keyboard (or just keyboard, in this case). Other than these unnecessarily floaty sections, this isn't a hard game. However, that also means *not frustrating*. And I can forgive the lack of strong gameplay in exchange for a story that really spoke to me, to the point where I had tears in my eyes at the end of this emotional journey. Voice acting is quality, with the lead characters all giving a strong performance. In the marketing, a lot of focus was put on the non-gaming actors such as Lena Heady and Carl Weathers, but the final boss is voiced by Courtney Taylor, and she blows it out of the park!If you yourself are artistically inclined, this will be a very recognisable tale, and it is fun to see it done in this creative a way.It's also worth it for the music. I genuinely sat in the main menu for minutes, listening to the gorgeous folk music, and all the way through the end credits for dat 80's electro groove!FINAL SCORE: 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough one. I didn't enjoy playing this game, the mechanics are way too simple and repetitive. However, I did enjoy looking at this game, a lot. And listening to it as well. It's one of the most original and beautifully designed games I've ever set my eyes on. So I'd recommend you to look at it as a work of art, not as a game in the traditional sense, and just make the most out of this trippy ride.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This game definitely has its pros and cons. One pro is the visuals. They're unlike any other game I've ever played. The voice acting is also very good. The con for me is that I didn't realize until after I bought it that it's best played with a game pad. Well, I don't have a game pad and playing with a keyboard is a bit of a b**ch. I've played for about 5 1/2 hours and now I'm stuck because I can't for the life of me find any info on how to dash using a keyboard. And until our hero is able to dash, this game isn't going to progress any further. Very frustrating and sad. So, bottom line- if you have a game pad but don't want a lot of complicated game play, then yes, I would recommend. Otherwise.... eh. I don't really know if it's worth it or not.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This was less of a game and more of an experience. Sure, there are game-like elements: you run, you jump, you do memory puzzles. But the heart of the game is Francis's journey, his quest to discover how to be true to himself.That might not be enough to hold a game together, but THE ARTFUL ESCAPE sets this journey in a psychedelic galactic environment that is beautiful to look at and exciting to explore. Leaping through the air in a glittery bodysuit, surrounded by an alien landscape, wailing on an electric guitar was the game experience I didn't know I needed.The end of the game brings the journey to a satisfying conclusion, one I look forward to playing again (no doubt wishing I could feel it again for the first time).Pros:-gorgeous art and captivating environments-fun guitar-playing interface-great, satisfying story-memorable characters-excellent character customization about halfway throughCons:-only about 3 hours-not many challenges - mostly just exploration-but get it anyway
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Insane. Amazing. Overwhelming in every good way. Scott Pilgrim vibes if you like that. If this was a book it'd be my favourite book, if it was a movie it'd be my favourite movie, but neither of those mediums can deliver what this did as a video game; And as a video game it has made my hall of fame. The story, the visuals, the sound design and voice acting, all of it is a 10.Ridiculously fun. Inspired and inspiring. It's a short 4-5 hour game and it's next on your list. Enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: The Artful Escape is a visual and auditory feast. You don't play it so much as experience it. If I had to try confine this game to a specific category I might say it's something like a walking sim or an interactive visual novel, but that would be doing it a disservice. Story: Think Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy if it were retold as a psychedelic rock opera. Beneath all the bells and whistles though are simple universal human truths and experiences. Through the eyes of Francis Vendetti, the nephew of an uber-famous Bob Dylan clone (and a gifted guitarist in his own right), we are treated to an exploration of Imposter Syndrome and the ways in which we sabotage ourselves. As that old Roosevelt quote goes, "Comparison is the thief of joy"- or something like that. I'm not American, I don't know. Outside of Francis's small little Bob Dylan clone-obsessed town there is a big wide multiverse for the taking, just aching for some half-decent music. Gameplay: You navigate the game platform-style, with the ability to shred your guitar to gain extra jumping power and awesome integalactic vibes. Sometimes there are simple memory puzzles where you have to copy music notes in a certain order - nothing too crazy unless you have the attention span of a gnat like myself. I wasn't focusing on gameplay anyway, It's just a vehicle to look at all the pretty landscapes. Visuals: The artwork is the crown jewel of this game. Every wondrous gloriously-detailed scene is infused with obvious love from the game's creators. The art direction is impeccable. I'm a sucker for gorgeous artwork and impressed with the sheer number of highly original scenes and creatures the creators were able to come up with. Sound: Glorious guitar riffs and solos accompany the visual extravaganza without ever sounding repetitive. The theme of the game is music, so this is fitting.Play this game to experience something beautiful and creative. It's something to be enjoyed at a leisurely pace. Don't play it if you're more into the gameplay side of things.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: The Artful Escape is a psychodelic narrative experience with nice artistic designs and a touching story. Although it can feel more as an experience than a game. As the game is mostly a walking simulator with little to no gameplay. But I really liked the vibes and the adventurous feeling of the Artful Escape.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: The Artful Escape isn't much of a game, more of an interactive experience, as the gameplay elements aren't really there, but that aside, it's incredible. The visuals, audio, And story are all beautifully done, and are some of the best I've seen.The story in particular is great, as at it's surface level is a feel good story about a musician finding his inner Ziggy Stardust and playing what he wants instead of what he's expected to; but when you look a little deeper, it's a game with strong allegories to gender and sexual identity. As someone who has struggled with both, the game hit a whole different level in terms of impact, and if you have experienced or are experiencing any of those, you should give it a try as well.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: For starters, I wouldn't necessarily say that Videogame is the right medium for this creative endeavor as the gaming aspect is pretty rudimentary. That out of the way it is a creative endeavor anyone who likes guitars and rock music, a heartwarming story with memorable characters or simply a stunning audiovisual experience should enjoy. I know I did. Said from it basically being nothing more than quicktime events (which I hate) and some pretty dull platforming there's nothing to the game in terms of mechanics. It maybe could've been a TV Series or a movie (god how I would love such a thing) but since we got a game that's what everyone should check out and be amazed by. You'll not have seen or played anything like it. :-)
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: The Artful Escape is a true gem. It’s probably the most beautiful and gorgeous game I’ve ever played. There are no deep or complex game mechanics, it’s more a walking simulator or mostly sliding down hills while jamming simulator, which is extremely satisfying.The voice acting is the best I ever experienced in a video game. The soundtrack is great, starting with some echoing folk music in the little town of Calypso, up to solo jams through the trippy Cosmic Extraordinary. It was a very enjoyable experience following the story of young artist Francis Vendetti, who stands in the shadow of his uncle, a legendary folk guitarist, while trying to find his true self on his journey through stunning alien worlds.The Artful Escape is an easy recommendable Masterpiece!
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: The art style of the game is good, but the repetitive gameplay and the games of simon says do not justify a recommendation. The story sounds promising, but doesn't particularly hold up well in my opinion. You follow a young folk artist trying to figure out who he is in the world due to being in the shadow of his uncle's legacy. For me, it didn't grip me enough to stay engaged. I was engaged for about the first half an hour, just after  and then I drifted off. A story like this must be engaging enough to balance out the gameplay you are provided with. Take Telltale games for example. The Walking Dead S1 is a very basic point-and-click as well as a major QTE lover, but the story is so gripping that the gameplay didn't need to be better. It could just be that this game doesn't have my taste for a story.I don't think it is a terrible game, I just think it lacks what a game of its genre needs. If you're a big fan of music, this game provides a lot to make you happy.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: The Artful Escape is a really enjoyable and fun game overall, with a really good story, and relatively good gameplay. I do wish that the game was longer in length of time, and I do wish that the game evolved its gameplay more, but other than that, I really liked the game overall, I loved the soundtrack and visual style, and this is an 8/10 game for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Not only loving the look and style of the game, I also really loved Francis as a character. While some of the guitar moves went a little too fast to keep up with, it's nice to get multiple tries without any repercussions. It would have been nice to eventually meet Johnson in the end, him telling Francis that he did a good job or something of the sort in the other realm. Some of the walking scenes felt unnecessary but watching the look of the game change was nice either way. I loved the style options & worlds you could choose from. Overall loved this game and would recommend to others! :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: A musical story about a boy finding his place in the world, across a grand universe with beautiful locations and set pieces, and an absolutely fantastic finale. Voice acting and soundtrack are top notch. This game feels incredibly cinematic. Not much gameplay mechanics besides playing the guitar, though. A very enjoyable journey overall!
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: A gorgeous psychedelic trip that'll take only one play session to finish. Not super hard in terms of gameplay (lots of running, and also quite a few jam sessions that play out a bit like a game of Simon), but definitely an experience I spent mashing the screenshot key in several spots.
