_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute masterpiece. The score was phenomenal, the artistry was grander than anything I could've anticipated, truly taking you through alien worlds and exploring the unknown. The games story within itself is well crafted and punches you in the gut with emotional turmoil. They go over topics a lot of artist, and hell, everyday people struggle with, like trying to figure out who you are. All in all an amazing game, one I played all the way through first sitting(it takes 4-5hrs to complete). It truly was a passion project turned out of this world experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: A visually artistic coming-of-age story about a young lad standing in the shadow of expectations. Emphasis on the word "story" as there is little gameplay and no fail-states, but also as it is a very strong and emotional narrative with an elegant climactic ending.Is it worth the full price? I don't think so. It's not to muddy the developers beautiful efforts, but as the end-user digesting the experience; it's just too short and without challenge. For the same value you get ~1 month of Netflix if you just want to sit back and relax. That said: It IS a journey worth experiencing!NB:It is not a rhythm game although it could look like one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: A nice feel good game. The gameplay is a little light, it's mostly just hold right and some very forgiving Simon Says, but the story with solid voice acting help carry things along. The stand out is for sure the visuals, as there are a lot of really cool psychedelic sequences that are just kind of fun to watch unfold. It's not the longest game in the world at about 4 hours but any longer than that would've outstayed it's welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Explosive and beautiful visuals in this game, its like a big acid trip to discover who is Francis Vendetti. The music of course is amazing, the storytelling is very good regarding legacy and the search of identity for an artist. Good cast for the voice actors too. On the cons side, I would say the musical gameplay could've been more deep. Its quickly redundant.A good experience I would recommend, especially if you're sensitive to visual arts and music
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: What a great simple game. The game design is very forgiven and you don't get frustrated when you miss a note. Following a flow design philosophy, like Journey and Abzu, The Artful Escape impressed me with it's gorgeous visuals, amazing score, and well crafted narrative. Perfect game to relax and enjoy a great work of interactive art.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't a game. It's an EXPERIENCE. And that's AWESOME. Try it and get blown away. I'm not sure I've ever watched anything with my eyes so wide in my life. The music is mind blowing! However, don't get it with the soundtrack unless you want it without the sweet sweet guitar jams, which is such a tragic blow to it's incredible effervescence.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: You know what... this is one of those games that you just chill with.. not a lot of gameplay, I would call it a glorified Simon Says ... BUT... it's a cool story, great graphics, everything is pretty! great music and it just sucks u in and u want to move in the different levels and discover what weird thing you are going to play music with next. I would recommend :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: I first saw a friend of mine streaming this game. My first impression wasn't too positive - nice graphics and music, but what about the game?The further she got into the game, the more I starting admiring it. So much so that I bought it. Then when I wanted to stream it, I found out the game did not see my controller (on Linux, which is not officially supported, so I can't really blame the developers too much). I wanted to play it though, so I decided to buy it on the Switch too.I played and streamed it and loved it. Yes, this is a (shortish) game, but most of all it is probably the most amazing experience I have ever had in 40+ years of gaming.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible experience.The Artful Escape tells the story of Francis, a young artist who's supposed to play a concert in honour of his late uncle - a legendary folk musician.This is a coming of age story and the story about a musician trying to find himself and who he wants to be on the stage. You'll be creating a stage persona for yourself, something like your own Ziggy Stardust.All this is told through absolutely stunning visuals and soundscapes - majestic snowy mountains on alien planets, a glass road leading you through the cosmos or a radiant desert landscape all are your stage to perform your music on.Put simply, the Artful Escape is a simple sidescroller, but instead of simply running and jumping you are simultaneously playing your own rock-opera.As you run, jump, slide and slam down you're playing different parts of melodies as you progress through a level, creating your own one of a kind sound.In between there'll be segments where you'll be able to freely play notes, creating your own unique little song while you fly through stunning vistas.All in all, this was one of the most unique titles i've played in a long time and highly recommend to anyone with any interest in (rock)-music and artful experiences.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: The music and art style are captivating, the story is bog standard living in ancestor's shadow, but let me tell you, I haven't finished a game the same day I bought it in over 10 years. If you're even thinking this game might be for you, I implore you get this, it's something like none other I've experienced in a LONG time!
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so I would have to give this game a solid 6.5/10. It was a really enjoyable experience, but there were a few big things that stop it from being stellar.I absolutely loved the visuals. The psychedelic space aesthetic is just awe-inspiring at times. The overall art direction is absolutely fantastic.The music is alright. I really like most of it, but the "shred" mechanic just lacks any sort of subtlety, and turns everything into a mindless guitar solo with no coherent melody. I understand the limitations of having to be able to shred anywhere at anytime and how that might affect things creatively, but I would much rather have the player fade in and out of a well thought-out melody or lead line rather than the shredding. The only other complaint I have about the music is that it's a little bland, with nothing particularly interesting happening.The main problem I have with this game is the gameplay, or lack thereof. There are a few Simon Says sequences dotted about, which don't feel particularly musical, and feel challenging in the wrong way. I don't feel like this game would work if it was incredibly challenging, so I understand the reluctance to include a lot of gameplay, but some sort of minigame that feels somewhat musical would be appreciated. I'm picturing dodging notes on a fretboard, or something else to that effect. I also felt that the minigames broke the flow of the music too easily. This is a game that lives and dies on the rising and falling spectacle, so stopping in the middle of a climactic moment because you missed a note only to start again a second before breaks that apart. I know gameplay has to have failure conditions, but I would prefer something that either keeps things rising, or resets to the start to begin building up again.A lot of these nitpicks might be because I'm a guitarist myself, and I feel like this could've been a game specifically directed at me, but all of these things just put me slightly off.So overall I enjoyed the experience, but I feel like it's overshadowed by what it could've been.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not a game. It's a true experience! It can be done in at least 4 hours or so, but that's not what should matter. This is a trip beyond your wildest imaginations! If you love a roller coaster of rock and sound, I recommend this. If you're wanting more game in this, you'll be left disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: A 21st Century psychedelic odyssey with creative themes that resonate. Flat out one of the most gorgeous titles I've ever played. The art direction is just off the scale - from I believe an art  team of 5 people! Annapurna always publish interesting titles - but be aware this is more an extended interactive feature (or "trip") than a game, with about a 4 hour run time.  BUT it's a sonic and visual journey like no other - in equal measures astonishing, surprising, delightful and grin inducing.If anything the game play is actually the weakest point - and personally not being under the influence a couple of the later levels seemed a little longer than necessary - but this is maybe because I loved it so much I played it through it 2 sittings. Indeed I had it on Game Pass AND still bought it on Steam so I could own it - to marvel at it in the future.If you ever wanted to be Bill, Ted, or Bowie,  live inside a Roger Dean album cover with Terry Gilliam & the cast of Yellow Submarine, whilst shredding epic Floyd guitar solos - then Rockstars your boat has come in!In an age where they're renting dull blockbuster movies for 15 quid - if you think it sounds good -  just buy it already.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: graphics is fabplot is confusingdifficulty is nullthe artful escape is more like a picture book than a video game.i love what the dev did with the game,had great time playing it.you get to run in pretty places,pretend to play guitar and be a confused teenager.sadly the game is short(you may finish playing this game in 4 hrs top) i think its slightly not worth the price.if its not on sale,its better if you dont buy it just add it to your wishlist.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: 'Meh',  only recommended on deep sale.Both the soundtrack and game play is not nearly as varied as I expected.  The music is *fine*, but very repetitive, the voice acting is *fine* if a bit uninspired.  The gameplay is very simple, some extremely simple platforming and very mildly challenging games of 'Simon Says'.I give it a B- to a C+, there are better games in this genre I'd play before this one:Sayonara Wild HeartsJust Shapes & BeatsThumper
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Wow.I am so grateful to have eyes and ears and be able to experience this.... sensation. What a game. What. A. Game.To put this into words that would be slightly more useful to potential buyers: this is not an action game or a platformer. There's no score, no timer, no enemies. Someone else said that this is a "four hour progressive rock music video" and I guess that's pretty accurate. I don't think you can lose it, and unless you're in it for the show, there's no reason to replay it. But if you ARE in it for a show, oh boy, "prepare for a show that you will remember for the rest of your lives".
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: I really do not know where to start with game. This game was an offhand purchase when I first found it on sale on steam, but I could not be happier with my purchase. If I were to buy this game again, I would do so for the full price. I will say, this isn't not so much of a game, but a interactive movie. So, if that is not something you would like I would stray away. In order to make it seem like I am not just praising the game nonstop, here are some pros and cons of this game:Cons: - Interactive movie (this can be seen as both pro or con) - Game is not hard at all (there are no difficulty settings either) - Game is pretty short (took me 4.5 hours to beat, but you could beat this in about 2 hours)Pros: - BANGER OST - Really stylized and beautiful scenery and characters - Unique mechanics - Amazing voice acting and writing - Great coming of age storyIn short, this game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome. Please, if you have some money and 2 hours to spend. Try this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: A journey of a young folk musician finding himself. You will go on a pychedelic journey through space on the cosmic lung, answer questions about your home the cosmic extraordinaire on Stargordon's talk show and face the evil fashionista atop the rare warp turtle. If you don't have the wail of the electric guitar in your veins and the soul of an artist in your heart then go now! This show is not for you kid! But if you stay, prepare for a wild ride of self discovery that you won't forget for a long tim!
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous graphics, stunning visual effects, great music and sound design. The gameplay is a bit underwhelming, as is the storyline. There is no real exploration or puzzles to be solved, resulting in a pretty linear experience that falls short of other similar titles like Night In The Woods. Grab it on sale and enjoy the amazing art that this game delivers.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: A 2d platformer with some Simon Says type music challenges. Like a lot of AnnaPurna games, it's more pretty/impressive than it is fun to play, which is a shame.+ Really interesting visual style and design.+ Sliding downhill in an alien desert, riffing on your hologram guitar is pretty epic!+ Some incredibly imaginative characters and environments.+ You can design some awesome clothing to wear (even if the color buttons are oddly placed)- The 2D platforming is incredibly basic.- The riffing is cool, but doesn't seem to fit the music perfectly.- 21:9 is VER- - Even letterboxing would have been better.- The "loading screen" was cool the first time, but not the second, or the 10th.- Horrible/impossible button combinations (like X, Y and B at the same time!)It's hard to recommend. The visuals and music are incredibly unique, but the gameplay drags it down much more than I'd like to admit. I don't know. I will say yes because more games like this should be made, but also should be made better.It's very flawed gameplay wise, but still an enjoyable journey.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly wasn't sure what to expect exactly when I bought this game, drawn in by the visual style and the promise of a decent soundtrack. In my opinion, this game was well worth going in pretty much blind. The vibrancy of the world and the music of the game were amazing! I can't wait to see what the creators do next.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: The art direction is incredible, every environment packed with detail and vibrant colors. The story is fun and made me think, which is always a plus. Gameplay is simple but fun, doesn't rush you, although the shredding got annoying after a while, blending with the bg music. Still, this game is near perfect in my eyes. Highly recommend, especially to fans of music.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended depending on what you're in the mood for.If you want short narrative with a good story and vibrant, psychedelic imagery then go for it.However, there is almost no gameplay beyond some really basic platforming, so if you're in the mood for a challenge then this isn't it.Regardless, worth a playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: It was a solid experience. The music and art style is definitely what makes this game worth getting. The gameplay was simple and can get a bit boring at times when all you really have to do is move right. I actually enjoyed the story quite a bit. I was going into it thinking the story was going to be the worst part, the ending especially got to me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: The game grabbed me right away with its unique presentation and its intriguing premise. It took me 4 hours to complete and I totally enjoyed my journey in this luxuriant universe. It's really a joke this game lost to Death Loop in the art direction category. The visuals are nothing short of spectacular, literally out of this world. So, yes it's more an "experience" than a "game" and I wished there were more rhythm mini-games, but, as the Glamourgonn would put it, I was entertained.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: The Artful Escape is a game developed by Beethoven and Dinosaur and published by Annapurna InteractiveThe game offers some nice graphics and environments, although some ugly glitches here and there, it is pleasant all the same and has a really great aesthetic and some equally amazing music and compositions which complement the fantastic visuals so wellThe Artful Escape overall, however, is a fun game to play, and it does get boring if being played for a long time, but is a fantastic story rich, adventure game and to play in short bursts
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: A great journey that is flawed but is carried by its amazing art style and music. The main game play is walking, choosing dialogue choices and doing a match the colours guitar mini game. The walking is a aspect that would annoy me in most games but because the visuals are amazing i liked walking in these new places everytime, it felt like an adventure. The dialogue choices seem like an aspect that was just added at for the sake of having one, in most situations. However the devs found clever ways to use this system, there's many choices that have funny choices that have an impact later in the game that you don't realize. The matching colours mini game is fairly simple once you get the hang of it, the game is fine itself since the visuals and the music make it seem so grand that its impossible not to have fun. But when this part fails the game gets boring, i would have put in another mini game to up the difficulty level near the end, so you have to handle both minigames when fighting bosses. The story is fairly simple and reminds me of a pixar or disney animated movie plot, it could have been much more serious and it comes super close to hitting those real life relatable moments but in the end it feels distant, like it would only relate to people who had famous parents. In the end i would probably rate this game a 7/10. Give it a shot if you want to play an interesting game that has amazing visuals, music, and powerful moments.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: What a beautiful game.The visuals are absolutely stunning and the soundtrack and gameplay make it even more entrancing. I can only reccomend this game, it's so fun and so stunning. A story that I'm sure many can relate to in some way. A perfect action game for anyone who doesn't like usual action games!
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing soundtrack, interesting environments and character design, and a compelling story make this game a very enjoyable and memorable experience.The gameplay however is lacking with the majority of the gameplay simply being moving right and jumping (very little to do with any kind of jumping puzzle), then a memory puzzle for the few encounters in the game.I didn't feel this detracted from the overall experience of the game, it just added very little to the experience and something that could be improved on for future titles from Beethoven & Dinosaur.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: "The Artful Escape" lets us play as a young singer-songwriter who feels pressured into pursuing a career as a folk singer due to his famour (but dead) uncle of Bob-Dylan-like stardom. Still, secretly the young man would much rather be a 80s-hair-metal guitarist shredding his axe to neon-coloured pyro effects on stage. How he manages to reach this goal during the game involves alien abduction, a gigantic cosmic lung, a turtle traveling at warp speed and a shopping mall inside a closet inside a flying ship above a glittering desert around a very beige city.One half of the core gameplay is a Jump'n'Run. But while jumping and running, you also carry an electric guitar with you that is at the heart of the other half of the game's mechanics: A music game. You can use the guitar to shred wailing solos along to the background music - and by doing so, you illuminate the world around you. At certain points in the game you will be challenged to jam sessions - in which you will have to synchronize your guitar melodies to the tune your (mostly alien) musical partners by following certain button patterns. Both the Jump'n'Run and the music game part of "The Artful Escape" are very, very easy, which could be considered the game's major weakness if you're all about adrenaline and challenge. Still, considering the unique (and very, very colourful) art style of the game, you will likely find yourself glad that most of the time you'll have a hand free to take screenshots while playing. And quite probably lots of them. The game revels in neon-coloured absurdities, bizarre characters and glittering space monsters speaking to you in saxophone phrases.To say that "The Artful Escape" is pretty trippy would be quite an understatement. It is a huge, intergalactic trip across the boundaries of time, space and quirky humor back into the heart of the 80s. And even though this journey will take you only a few hours, it will leave you with more than a few dear memories.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: I really had fun playing this game. If it looks interesting to you, you'd probably like it. It has a lot of heart and the much of the designs and visuals were amazing. I'm glad I played it.A few points to consider however: 1) I beat this game in about 5 hours. Although it was an enjoyable experience, that's not a whole lot of gameplay. You might consider waiting for this to be on sale.2) It's incredibly easy. There are purely cosmetic choices to be made and a story to engage with, but no real challenge at all. There is no difficulty setting, which is a shame because this drops its replayability to pretty much zero.3) The music is nice but not exceptional. The main gameplay mechanics are not very engaging. You run around and explore lush environments (which is nice the first time) but the 'jump and strum guitar' bit gets a little tedious, even with the interesting scenery. I wish the music mechanic let you do more.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: At times the Artful Escape felt like it was less of a game and more of an experience.   However, that's by no means a criticism.  I've played other video games like this with minimalist gameplay that try to be an audio-visual feast for the senses (e.g. Journey, Abzu), but I can honestly say this is the first time that approach has ever actually clicked with me.  The gameplay is serviceable enough.  You'll spend a fair amount of time sprinting and jumping around, interacting with folks, exhausting dialogue trees, and playing a Simon-says style mini-game with your guitar.   The Artful Escape really isn't about that though.  It's about sending you on a journey, and evoking a strong emotional response.  For me that response was pure delight.  From the scenic introduction to the bombastic ending credits, I was blown away by this game's presentation.  and it's not just the visuals and score that make the game great; the fever dream like plot and fun, endearing characters kept the controller glued to my hands just to see what would happen next. Without giving too much away, this game follows the mind-bending journey of a young folk musician who decides to step out of the shadow of his famous uncle by becoming his own person, reinventing himself as a glam-rock god.  On his quest to craft a Ziggy Stardust-like persona for himself, he ends up reaching for the stars . . . literally and figuratively.  To say any more would be doing the game a disservice.  Just know that the Artful Escape is a journey that's well worth taking.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: A truly lovely game. You'll know if you will love it or not as soon as you play the first 5 minutes. It lays itself bare and honest with you from the very start. It's not a very long game, however it ignites your audiovisual senses 100% from start to finish. Part of me wishes it was longer, but I feel it would have diluted the experience had it been longer.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game and I enjoyed every minute of this wonderfully surreal and psychedelic tale of a young man called Francis trying to find himself while being overshadowed by the fame of his legendary dead uncle... The only problem was, once I'd unlocked the ability to start changing him into his new persona through the use of the character editor, giving him his new name and altering his style to suit... it was over.Great game. Fantastic story. Too short. Didn't really get the time to enjoy Francis's new life.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a cross between a side scroller, the Hasbro toy "Simon" and the Beatles movie The Yellow Submarine.It's pretty simple.  You mostly go from left to right.  When a game just has you going from left to right, how do you keep it from being boring?  By having the most amazing scenery.  Never did I regret going right.  Oftentimes I would go left, just to look again at something I almost missed during my first fly by.At one point in the game, your character hears "An artist is someone who gives people something they could NEVER have imagined".  How meta.  That's the game!  Something I could never have imagined, but I definitely enjoyed the journey.I'm not here to describe the game, the controls, the difficulty.  I'm here to tell you if I think the game is worth $20 bucks.  The visuals, the audio, the music, the amazing voice acting, the remarkable cast!  Yes!  This is worth 20 dollars of your money and how few hours you manage to get out of it.It has ... shrubbery.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: A really beautiful game which despite the short play time I will play again just for the sheer joy of it. The visuals, psychedelia, music, animation, and characters are awesome. My only gripe is a couple bugs I encountered, one of which was basically gamebreaking at the time. (In a music 'battle' I had to press three keys and they would not register, even after restarting. Remapping the keys was the answer for me!) Otherwise a masterpiece of a game about the beauty of art to free you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This is a relaxing game that is more about the journey of your character than the gameplay. It’s short and can be completed in a few hours, but I took my time and completed it over a few days. It can be a bit weird at times with the characters and art, but that makes it unique! If you want a game with less gameplay but more story and exciting visuals, then this is for you. I highly recommend this game for how unique it is.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: The best thing about this game are those sequences where you're just moving forward, holding x, and staring in awe at the amazing visuals and stellar audio. They're spaced apart by some simon says style memory games, and dialogue sections, but really the focus is the audiovisual experiences. Also those characters and monsters are amazing, whoever did them did a really great job ;?)
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an experience that I fell in love with. It is Annapurna so the art and music are unparalleled. The gameplay is relaxed, a very easy sidescroller/jumper with minimal "Simon" style challenges; the game is almost more of an interactive movie. In other instances I would say that as a criticism, here I mean it as praise. Stop worrying about difficulty settings and just let The Artful Escape overwhelm your senses and draw you in.My only complaint: it is painfully short.For now, I'm off to buy the soundtrack!
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: I'm truely thankful to this game, since it opened my eyes to a new chapter of my life.There's a sentence and an arc in this game that truely resonated with me.After I played this, I started to become myself, to work on myself, so I can be, who I want to be, and not, who others told me, I needed to be.Gameplay wise this is really simple, it's about the visuals, the characters and the music, not about the gameplay. Maybe it is less of a game and more of an experience.For me, at least, it changed my life to the better. I'm deeply thankful this game existed within my lifetime.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: I thought I wasn't going to enjoy The Artful Escape' in the first few minutes... and then it took off. While the limited gameplay mechanics might be a deter for some people, it isn't something that bothered me. I enjoyed it similarly to how I enjoyed games like Journey- the creative use of visuals and  composition are phenomenal and breath-taking. The experience *couldn't* be a movie- it was designed to be a walked through first hand. What I enjoyed about the Artful Escape in particular was it's use of absurd iconography and language. It manages to recreate a world that pops right off an 80's space opera rock cover, with music ultimately guiding the experience. It's enjoyable and fun and weird!! Very weird...And there is a lesson to be taken from it- whether or not it resonates with you may depend on where you are in your creative journey. If you find yourself struggling to find your identity and/or feeling suffocated by clout, this might be perfect for you. Otherwise, the story is just an innocent function supplementary to the experience. It does what it has to do to keep the train moving. All in all, it was a fun time. There is one line that'll stick with me:"Play as if your dreams are memories."
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: First things first, this is less of a game and more of an interactive experience, so you won't be doing too much in that department. That being said, the game is a feast for the eyes and ears, and brings you to fantastic places. If you are looking for an interactive rock opera that takes you to the furthest reaches of space, this is it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: The Artful Escape is nearly impossible to explain; almost like reviewing a music video or a live concert.  The game starts off a bit slow; at least compared to what’s coming, as you explore your home town and talk to anyone who will talk back.  Things really start to shred once you step through Lightman’s doorway and enter the Cosmic Extraordinary.  Here you find yourself on a massive spaceship with a live theater, disco, nightclub, and other areas to explore.  From this hub you will branch off into otherworldly adventures on strange planets and landscapes ripped straight from album cover art inspired by Boston, ELO, and Asia.  You will gradually learn the history of the cosmos while interacting with indigenous life, always trying to get back to your ship so you can do it all again.Gameplay isn’t terribly difficult or even that challenging.  You explore these scrolling worlds much like any other platformer by running and jumping.  You can use your guitar to extend jumps by shredding a quick solo or just hold down the X button for a continuous jam that blends seamlessly into the main soundtrack while often lighting up various parts of the level as you pass through.  There are numerous moments, both in level traversal as well as significant encounters and even boss fights where you will get to play a classic game of Simon using a few buttons on the controller to mimic the sounds and colors presented to you.  These moments are made even more interesting by the way the game integrates the button layout into actual creature designs; eyes and other orifices.The Artful Escape is here to celebrate some fantastic music and visuals while creating a relaxing journey that flows with the music and tells a fun quirky story about a boy who is trying to find his spot in the Cosmic Extraordinary.Read the full review at  Check out our live gameplay series on YouTube - More Steam reviews on our Curator page -
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Let's make it clear. It is not a game based on mechanics, it is an interactive experience based only on its audiovisual brilliance. If you like games with extraordinary beautiful scenery combined with feelings of awe and wonder, electric guitar sequences and space ambient music, this space adventure is for you. After the guitar started playing, I just knew this game was gonna destroy me in the most emotional way possible and I would give double the money to re-live this 4.5 hour experience for the first time.!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Oh. My. God.This game hit close to home for me, so obviously I'm a little biased on this front, but I'll try to address the important bits.First and foremost. This is NOT a game for its gameplay. To me, the gameplay was secondary. The game is more of an experience than anything.The music and background visuals are absolutely breathtaking. The character models were doll-like, but that's okay, because it's not the focus of the game itself.Voice acting was good, but lots of lines were reused. Again, not a bad thing.But holy crap. For five hours of playtime, this game was really something. I'd like to thank the developers for the experience this game put me through. I loved absolutely every second I spent playing this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absurdly gorgeous. From the opening scene you just know you're in for something special. For my entire 3+ hour playthrough, I was consistently dazzled - there's so much going on onscreen that I want to play the game again just to take more of it in. The colors are vibrant, the environments are unique, the creatures and characters are fantastical. Games like this can often quickly fall into "style over substance" territory and suffer for it, but I found that the art, music, and story were so good that the fact that the gameplay is very light didn't bother me.The Artful Escape is a visual and sonic treat with an engaging, humorous, and heartfelt story. The gameplay is basic, but just enough to keep you interested and not feel like you're playing a walking simulator. The game is short, but it's as long as it needs to be and I can see myself replaying it for the spectacle alone.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this game, the art style, music, and story are everything you expect from a game being published by Annapurna.Only drawbacks I can think of is a lack of difficulty setting, and the odd way the story sort of abruptly changes your perspective on Lightman.Also wish I wasn't too late for that show at the end, that was sort of anti climactic way of going about the entire conclusion.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: A stellar game that plays like you're gliding through a David Bowie album presented in the style of Yellow Submarine. It's about overcoming the expectations of others, struggling with imposter syndrome, and of building your own identity. More about psychedelic imagery and ~vibes~ than pure technical gameplay. Don't come to this game for exceptional difficulty or a skill to master, but for an experience.If that doesn't sell you, there's a dedicated "Play Guitar" button that you can hammer down for nearly the entire game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: Actually bought this game with the intention to refund.Seriously, wtf was I thinking right?! This game is gorgeous! It has guitar solo's, great artwork, Comedy, Guitar solo's, amazing story-driven, music and guitar solo's! I'm really blown away with the artwork and the great soundtrack. This is the kinda game when you're a musician (or not and just love music-games) that takes your mind away.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: The Artful Escape starts out as a Night-in-the-Woods esque nostalgia walk, but very quickly goes off the rails and evolves into a fantastically trippy interstellar adventure. The gameplay is relatively straightforward, and is more of an experience than a challenge, but is enough to stay engaged through mindblowing visual after mindblowing visual. Seriously, the art direction is incredibly creative and unique. A decent coming-of-age tale and a prime example of Games As Art, with a triumphant set of successive climaxes. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: The Artful Escape is a story about legacies, finding yourself, change and transition that presents itself in such an ingenious way that all can absolutely enjoy it. Gliding across the cosmos, playing electric guitar in unknown lands, and eventually vanquishing a divine complication with intricate audio design and superb music to accompany – it’s perplexing how captivating this interstellar adventure is. Inviting players on a musical journey through cosmic realms and challenging introspection, The Artful Escape is a masterpiece.Full review at
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably one of the weirdest games I have ever played. The range of different genres of music was a real treat would happily just sit and listen to the soundtrack for hours. The Art work specifically the background was beautiful top job. However a little lack luster in animation and quite easy gameplay I did find the story interesting but was really the music and art that made me engaged.Was a real treat to play very much a casual game that you can enjoy just relaxing without having the stress of many consequences.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: I've been really excited for this game since I saw it teased here in there in Indie Showcases. I was not disappointed. This game is trippy, weird, and wonderful. It makes you feel like Major Tom in Space Oddity. I had no idea where the game was going and really loved where it ended up. It sounds, looks, and feels fantastic to play. While it's not my favorite Annapurna game, it's certainly a good one. Better then some of the others for sure.Edit: I guess I should add since there's some negative reviews that the gameplay is a little bit repetitive and easy, but to me, this game is more about the story it tells then having gripping gameplay. (If that sounds more interesting, try Sayonara Wild Hearts for a game heavy on the music but with great gameplay.) I found the movement pretty fun and liked seeing how fast I could go and while the Simon Says segments were not that difficult, I really liked how they were duets and how they sounded.Overall I still really recommend this game but if you're going into it expecting the best gameplay ever you'll be sorely disappointed.  If you like things like Wandersong or Edith Finch where the game is merely a medium for the story then you'll probably like The Artful Escape.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

_childDocuments_.review: The Artful Escape of Francis Vendetti is a video game about great expectations, famous folk singers, lingering shadows, space Gods, hallucinogens, individuality, reptile shops, and wild imaginations. It's an action, adventure, exploration, narrative driven, musical-laser-light-battle kind of game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Artful Escape

name: Hindsight
detailed_description: What if the physical objects of everyday life, the possessions we hold close, were actual windows to the past? Peer into distant memories and unseen futures in Hindsight. From the creator of Prune, Hindsight is a narrative exploration game spanning the entirety of a woman's life, from birth to present day, as she tries to make sense of it all. Revisit her childhood home, sort through personal belongings, and step through windows to memories frozen in time. Hindsight asks you to slow down and pay attention to the little things left behind. Piece these things together and shift your viewpoint until you find just the right perspective to pull you deeper into the past. Long forgotten memories and dreams cascade into one another. Linger as long as you wish, but sooner or later you must come back to the present. What will you take with you? And what will you leave behind?

_childDocuments_.review: Another beautiful game from Annapurna that reminded me a lot of  and . It has a thoughtful well-written story that will resonate with a lot of people. Its core mechanic of diving into objects to explore memories is absorbing and immersive, and the soundtrack is successful at evoking empathy. _childDocuments_.review: With so many story driven interactive experiences and story exploration titles around nowadays videogames are covering many topics and themes in various ways. Hindsight takes a form of something like an interactive photo album with a really cool visual style and a story about loss and grief. But for how pretty it is, playing it isn’t particularly enjoyable.This title was clearly developed for a touch screen control and I wouldn’t be surprised if there it feels somewhat more enjoyable to play. With a mouse, however, it is often a rather frustrating experience even if you crank up the camera movement at least by a quarter up. You see – the gameplay process of Hindsight is you flying through small freeze frame-like scenes with the ability to rotate the camera around. And when I say the ability, i mean the requirement, because to progress to the next scene you have to find a particular hotspot to click. And that hotspot can sometimes only exist when you rotate the camera to a certain angle. This looks cool, but in practical terms means that to “turn the page” you have to drag your mouse around until you find an angle that the developers consider correct that let’s you proceed further. And while in some cases that angle is visually tied to the perspective of the scene, most of the time it seems completely arbitrary and existing just so players have “stuff to do” because “it’s a videogame you see”.When not being frustrating to go through, the title tells a story well enough, but here I feel that it might click for some and not for others. For me, for example, it didn’t – partially because the whole narrative is very “being stuck in the past is good”, partially because it speaks of very “growing up in US” experiences that are entirely alien to me. But I could easily see others liking the story and connecting with what it’s going for. And it is told in a nice and stylish way.If Hindsight didn’t try so desperately to add interactivity for the sake of interactivity, I feel that I would’ve enjoyed it more. And even though I didn’t connect with the story at all, it would’ve at least led to a far more enjoyable experience through someone’s life with pretty visuals.

Nice art, nice voice acting, really touching story of loss and reflection.Also, if you finish this in under 2 hours, don't be one of those jerkfaces who refunds!

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a beautifully made thoughtful story.  I ugly cried through the entire thing.  This story captures so many aspects of grief so well.  Having lost my own mom last year and having to go through all her things... I saw so many of my own thoughts, my own feelings, reflected in this game.  There is some comfort in knowing others understand your grief, in seeing your experiences understood.  If you've gone through a deep loss, this is a very heavy game, but I think you'll find echoes of your own loss in it.It's clear Hindsight was developed with a lot of love, and I deeply appreciate the creators sharing this with others.

_childDocuments_.review: I am obviously not the type who plays games like this. I am a bear. I do bear things, like mauling people, liberating picnic baskets and sometimes breaking into cars because people leave Mars bars in them, and no, don't start joking how this is unbearable. No, I'm not the one who ruined that woman's canoe in that one viral video. How dare you. Anyway. I wouldn't call this a game. It's an interactive story. Took me 3 hours to finish.And let me tell you...The game is gorgeous, the art style just fits. The story? Well...There are too many moments in this where I thought "Who the hell was reading my mind and stealing some elements of my past when writing this?"The one scene where protagonist talks about college. I almost threw my banana at the screen. No, that's not a euphemism. I mean a real banana. I just went "get out of my head!" Because that's literally me back in 1995.There are these moments where I could see myself as the protagonist. That is brilliant, but also a wee bit scary. And the mechanics? What they do with the camera, how it reveals the next scene, crafty and smart. I love it. Sometimes it makes you feel like you're in a David Lynch movie.I bought this on the recommendation of a Twitter acqaintance and she said I won't regret it. She was right. I did not regret this. Yes, it's short at 2-3 hours, but 100% worth the price IMHO, since the experience is spot on.Going to buy the soundtrack, too, because it's fantastic.

_childDocuments_.review: You can tell the dev(s) who made this game really wanted it to be impactful and emotional, but man was this ever a miss for me. I love games like these, point and click cozy games. But therein lies my issues with this game. When you make a point and click game, whereas there is very little interaction, its totally fine, but it does mean your message/story needs to be super interesting or rich. You need to have something important to say, otherwise the point and clicking gets to be a tad boring very quickly.This game half of the time, seemed to have nothing to say at all, much less something important. In fact, the message for me was the complete opposite. I also think the creators of the game meant for it to read like a letter, but it came off feeling long winded and often had unnecessary sentences that felt like they were just there to fluff up the story and add an extra picture to have stuff to click on (maybe to get over that 2 hour mark for steam refunds?). The character would hold up something as inane as an oven mitt and be like "you always loved this oven mitt ever since you baked cookies that one time". It left me resenting the narration as I kept feeling like I wanted to rush through the game to get to whatever point or message the story was struggling to get to.And OH BOY the message was just...well it was bad. Like really in my humble opinion, it was toxic. Pretty much it was 'if your parent wasn't great, it was probably your fault or their ♥♥♥♥♥♥ actions were because they wanted what was best for you.If your parent is strict or overbearing or neglectful, apparently according to this game, you just didn't understand your parent and they are super complex and misunderstood and you didn't understand this because you were a stupid kid busy with childhood and not paying attention. This is a super unhealthy message to people who actually dealt with parents like this (or worse for some of us) growing up or who have a strained relationship with their parent(s).  If you dealt with a neglectful, strict, abusive, or overbearing parent. It was not your fault, nor was it your job as a YOUNG CHILD to live up to your parents or anyone else's expectations. You didn't ask to be born, your parents made that important decision a long time ago for you. And if they weren't supportive, were abusive or hurtful, weren't emotionally available or loving, or just were too busy to 'deal with you' or raise you, that means that they did a piss poor job being a parent. End of story. It isn't a child's job to EARN a parents respect or praise. And as a parent, expecting a young developing mind to do everything perfectly and to such high standards doesn't create a more successful or better adult, it just breeds confidence issues and fear later on in life. And neglecting or being unavailable to your kid doesn't make them independent, it makes them lonely and not trusting as an adult.This game would have you listen to a couple of hours (if you rush through) of game play of the main character narrating why the present point in time is completely THEIR FAULT (their words) and how they should have tried harder or looked closer to understand their, to be honest, ♥♥♥♥♥♥ parent.Spoilerinos ahead (skip to get to TL;DR if needed):So the game starts off with the main characters birth. You don't know your name (why this is annoying in a bit), and you're panning the camera around to find a hidden next picture. This is the main mechanic of the game, and though it isn't totally awful, it does get repetitive and often clunky sometimes (also more on this in a bit). So that's all you need to understand how the game works. Now I'm going to do you the courtesy of respecting your time, something that the devs didn't seem to think was important while creating this game. Here we go. You ready?Young girl has parents. Dad's nice, Mom is strict. Girl grows up into teen, Strict mom is strict about all things and is unfun. Nice Dad is super fun. Girl teen applies and gets into college. Dad dies. Everyone super sad. Strict Mom becomes even more unfun. Teenage girl grows into woman, leaves college. Still sad about dead dad. Gets a job, earns living. Much success, owns their own business. Mom dies. Woman sad. Somehow blames HERSELF???? for the mom being a strict and sometimes neglectful overbearing parent?!? Somehow the final message is that SHE (the child into an adult) should have tried MORE to understand her boar of a mother?!? (main character actually says this)Woman now super success, goes to Japan to understand super sucky mom's past. Keeps only some things from dead moms house to remember the suck-tastic memories of childhood.the end.there are some annoying bits in there. Like without you knowing the main characters name you somehow need to solve a puzzle with fridge magnets spelling out their name...yea idk. Or like the main mechanic being super annoying when you are looking for that one 'window' to the next point and click picture and its a small pencil or doorknob or something. In those moments the games momentum is interrupted and the already winded story is paused until you find the one angle or small window it needs to continue talking. And to be honest it's just...awful.TL;DR Story was a luke warm 2.5 out of 10Game Mechanics were 4.5 out of 10Message was a 0 out of 10 for meSo probably skip this title (or if you are really that curious go watch a play through or something) and uh...hug your kids or something...I don't know.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an interactive poem: a game that speaks to the player's soul by transporting them through the mind of a protagonist exploring their memories. I really enjoy this type of game (narrative-heavy with minimal gameplay) and this is a delightfully unique game amongst all the rest. You're given the ability to see the protagonist's memories in any angle your heart desires, and the game is very clear that we see our memories differently over time. Time, and memory, are the poetic elements in this game.A lot of the narrative is conveyed visually with audio (words and music) helping make sense of what you're seeing. I found myself quite moved throughout the story as more and more of the protagonists' memories were given context. The subject matter might be partly why I was moved so strongly as it deals with how a person deals with grief, the parts of life that we all face eventually but would love to do without. Because of this, I saw a lot of myself in the protagonist. As the story winded down towards a conclusion I couldn't help but cry, not that this game is necessarily sad, more-so that it's just deeply human. It's a truly beautiful story.I'd recommend this, especially if you're looking for a 2-ish hour long story that's more intimate than a film. The story's definitely worth your time.edit: minor grammar fixes.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is brilliant. It manages to do so much. It talks about generational trauma. It talks about death, loss, coping. It does what it needs to do, which is to be emotionally immersive. Many games are physically immersive, where you perform actions as an extension of yourself, but this game creates immersion by embodying your actions and emotionsin the role of the main character.It does what it needs to do, which is evoke an emotion through connection, without more mechanics.I'm all for pushing the envelope, but at the end of the day, game devs are storytellers and we can achieve a level of immersion that film and TV cannot, because we engage the user in the action. And we can do it without needing to create new mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the idea of this visual novel. The return to a childhood home to reinterpret childhood memories as an adult is an emotionally evocative theme. Using the rooms and objects in them is a great structure for reflection (literally, in the case of this game). But the writing was dreary and overly concerned with its supposed deep insight. There was little light or humor or life here--it was just unrelentingly sad. The writers missed a chance for player-created meaning in one of the final scenes that might have allowed some player introspection as well. The objects the player chose at the end of every chapter could have been meaningful for how the protagonist tells her own story at the end, but they weren't.

_childDocuments_.review: I sobbed :c This game reminded me of the short story The Paper Menagerie by Ken Liu (which I broadly suggest people read, but in particular if you play this game and enjoy it).Hindsight is a narrative-based point & click exploration game that focuses on a woman reflecting back on her life, and more specifically, her relationship to her mother. The story was a bit slow to become engaging, but the atmosphere/style of the game + the core gameplay mechanic kept me interested. And then I found myself being welcomed with a gut punch for the last ~25% of the game. There are some really interesting motifs sprinkled throughout the game that I suspect more attentive people will appreciate. The game explores themes such as familial love, misunderstandings related to displays of affection (e.g. the demonstration of care from a parent to a child that doesn't register as such for the child until they are old enough to understand it better), memory distortions from childhood to adulthood, grief, loss, finding one's way in life, personal meaning attributed to items, etc and does so in a thoughtful and relatable way, all the while being contained in a game that takes ~2 hours to complete. If you enjoy narrative games and can appreciate a slow burn with a strong payoff, then this is worth a playthrough. That said, given its length and limited replayability, I suggest waiting to buy it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Although I found the narration sometimes a bit on the nose and the navigation mechanic a tad gimmicky, I really enjoyed those 2 hours spent in Hindsight. The theme of the story (a daughter coming to terms with her mother's death while emptying her house) is original and interesting, some scenes are really beautiful and it's a memorable experience. There should be more games like this one, that you can play through in an evening and that stay with you for quite a long time afterwards.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first time I've felt compelled to write a review for a game. I should work on improving that, but I hope this serves as a testament of how much I enjoyed this. It's just a very, very touching narrative, woven together in such a poignant way it was almost hard to continue at times. Hard to face. But I had to. It's difficult to write this because there's so much I want to say, but I don't want to spoil the story. I guess I'll say that this is a story not just about grief but about the hard part of grief. And yet, it is kind. The kindest way such a hard message could be delivered. Gameplay-wise, the game is beautiful visually and the gameplay is very intuitive. Very enjoyable. I can't really comment on the gameplay much more beyond that, but if you love stories and writing, I really recommend you play this. Really wonderful showcase on writing about difficult topics (game credits Emma Kidwell as the writer so, if they are reading this, thank you and also damn you for reminding me I'm a cry baby).Really really recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Hindsight is a narrative-driven game that deals with themes of loss, particularly the experience of returning home. It’s hard not to draw comparisons to What Remains of Edith Finch, but here the focus is entirely on emotions, memories, and the exploration of family values, rather than using these themes as a backdrop for a series of magical stories like in The Life and Times of Scrooge McDuck.The narration can sometimes be a bit heavy-handed and could have been written with a subtler touch, but the themes of memory, nostalgia, and the difficulties of communication are always among my favorites.Although the genre is referred to as ‘walking simulator,’ there’s no actual walking involved here. Instead, scenes are observed from predetermined viewpoints, and the transitions are beautifully crafted animations that play with perspectives and significant objects from the protagonist’s past and present life, as well as the unconscious connections our memories constantly make.Unfortunately, the game was released simultaneously on mobile and PC, and on Steam, it feels like a poorly done mobile port. The controls are clunky, there’s an odd, almost nauseating lag, and the gameplay relies on simple rotating movements and tapping on predetermined areas, which can sometimes be hard to spot. This is a stark contrast to the more traditional gameplay of Edith Finch, which, with its free exploration and numerous interactions, provided a much deeper sense of immersion — something I believe is a key strength of video games compared to other visual arts.A rare miss for Annapurna. I’d recommend playing it on a tablet with someone who’s not a regular gamer.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is 7 euros on 50% sale, which is too much for what you get.I like the genre, the art-style and what the game tries to do, but it is too little content for the price.It is actually a 1-hour, linear, slow-paced. narrated game which is stretched to a 2-hour game by the find-the-next-thing-to-click-from-just-the-right-angle mechanic which breaks immersion into the story.Would recommend if the game were ~3 euros and if you don't mind wasting your time spinning the view-angle around half the time.Pro-tip: Play at 16:9 display ratio. At times it was obvious that the game was developed for 16:9 display, which made the arrange-the-table task frustrating to control on 21:9 display. Also some next-thing-to-click locations are on the upper boundary of your view-control, which would be much easier to find on 16:9.

_childDocuments_.review: I do recommend this game. I dont think its really worth $15 but if you catch it on a good sale, I do think it is worth playing.On that note, there are a few things that I believe lower this game's rankings in my mind.1. The "gameplay" feels more like a chore than anything else. Implementing a unique gameplay mechanic into a game of this genre is tough to do well. From a technical standpoint I do admire the core gameplay mechanic, but after some time it feels slow to move the camera and slow when you travel from spot to spot, and all this for seemingly no reason other than that it makes the game "more game-y". I think this game could learn a lot from Before Your Eyes' gameplay and how it immerses the player into the game more rather than how the mechanic in Hindsight seems to make things worse.2. The writing isnt great. Its not easy to feel attached to the main character. Hindsight would benefit from using more of a show dont tell writing format. Additionally, giving us better reason to care about the characters would give the story a better emotional kick. Having said that, I do recognize that one of the core takeaways of the story is . 3. One more thing for the writing is the tone. The tone felt pretty constant, which isnt necessarily bad, but it makes it a little challenging to stay engaged. Im not sure how to describe it perfectly here, but there are quite a few parts that I think could use a change in tone, and music choice to make the deeper parts stand out more.Anyways, thats about it

_childDocuments_.review: Hindsight is a visual novel involving a contemplative walk-through of the past of the protagonist. The way the story is propelled forward is through the movement of the camera within the scene and connecting pieces in the scenery to make a full object. This will then involve the protagonist revealing more of their past as the scene moves to flashback and to the present day as the protagonist thinks more on her relationship with her parents. Hindsight tells a heartfelt story with complicated emotions about how best to come to terms with past relationships. It has a nice, simple art style and a mood that fits well with the story being told. Worth the couple hours of gameplay, though the price is hard to argue for.7/10

name: GRIME
detailed_description: Parting Shade - Face the grueling platforming challenges of the Abandoned Opus, a new Area which lies at the top of the Weeping Cavity. Tinge of Terror - NG+ Mode added, along with Major modifications to existing Bosses, and an entirely New Boss, Music & Weapons. Colors of Rot - Explore Childbed, a massive new interconnected Area. As well as 3 New Bosses, New Music, New Abilities, New Weapons Traits and more. Feedback Patch - New systems added: Armor stats & Respec. Additional Nervepasses & Weapons. Removed Missables, re-balancing and more. Destroy... Absorb... Grow... GRIME is a fast and unforgiving Action-Adventure RPG in which you crush your foes with living weapons that mutate form and function, and then consume their remains with a black hole to strengthen your vessel as you break apart a world of anatomical horror and intrigue. An unusual material collapses in on itself, the world shudders and contracts, and suddenly you are squeezed into existence. What awaits you is a world unknown, alien in its own familiarity, and you must survive what terrors you face. Explore your surreal surroundings, absorb the many enemies you encounter, and use their own traits against them as you let yourself become far more than you once were. GRIME lets you play to your preference, upgrading only those traits you feel most suited to your unique style. You’ll find there is more than one way to break open an enemy as you move through a variety of evocative environments, meet their inhabitants, and discover the source of their madness. • Eye-Popping Surrealism - Uncover mysterious secrets in weeping caves and face-covered deserts. Meet otherworldly characters in distinct civilizations across an organic, interconnected world - all rendered in unearthly 3D. Face foes born of the world itself, and swallow them whole. • Death-Defying Combat - Punish enemies by parrying their attacks, smash them from the ground or even airborne, and absorb them to grow your strength as you wage war on a living world. • Living Weapons - Seamlessly swap weapons made of living creatures that mutate form during combat, from clawing swords to centipede whips. • Unique Skill Progression - Hunt down and absorb challenging monsters to improve your skills and bring true customization to your play style. • Challenge Menacing Bosses - Defeat creatures dozens of times your size. Adapt to their strategies, withstand their assault, and consume them to gain game-changing abilities that affect both combat and traversal. • Colors of Rot - Discover new abilities, new weapons, and new enemies that are champing at the bit just to get a piece of you. _childDocuments_.review: After about 4 hours of trying to get into the game, I decided to stop as I was having no fun and felt exhausted. The reason for that is "tedious". Everything you do in Grime feels very slow and exhausting. This might fit the design and theme but gameplay wise it's just very off-putting. Let me tell you why.Navigating areas is extremely time consuming, as the checkpoints are very rare, there are a lot of traps that kill you in 1-3 hits, same goes for enemies, and the whole beacon system. I have absolutely no idea, why you have to implement a system, that adds absolutely nothing but more time spent on the game. You basically don't see the map unless you activate said beacons, but even then, only the already visited areas are revealed, which means you have to backtrack and see if you missed something. As I said before, movement and platforming is tedious, so it doesn't feel "good" to explore areas. Hidden loot is not worth getting most of the time, as it mostly consists of consumables, that you will most likely never use. (I only found about 20% of the consumables useful).The whole healing system revolves around parrying and my god, to the devs love their parrying. To be able to heal for example, you have to parry enemies, which sounds ok BUT once you are at low health, with no enemies nearby, in a hard to navigate area with traps, you will most certainly end up dead. Paired with the before mentioned low number of checkpoints, it is so absolutely frustrating to die deep in a new area with no map visible. On top of that, you can only hold one healing charge.Your stamina runs out extremely fast and is required for basically everything (except parrying). So trying to get more than 1-2 hits in is not possible, especially during boss fights, since you need to dodge every other second. Oh and speaking of dodging, bosses kill you in 4-6 hits with badly telegraphed attacks while being damage sponges.There are other flaws in the game desing in my opinion, but these points really stood out in my opinion. Some other honorable mentions are the whole "Ardor" system, which I am not going into, useless weapons and armor (to a point where it feels bad unlocking new stuff, since you're never going to use it, due to the gear being bad or simply not usable at all because of stat restrictions.I really loved the design, the gritty and dark atmosphere, but if a game feels more like work than an actual game, there's just something wrong with it.Now while I wouldn't recommend the game, I would suggest giving it a shot because there are certainly a lot of people enjoying it, judging by the reviews. So by all means, go ahead, jump into the game for 1-2 hours and if you don't like it, get a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I'm somewhat on edge with recommending this or not.  The basic mechanics feel pretty good, and the premise of absorbing your enemies to grow is extremely interesting.  The animation canceling into parrying really reinforces it as the primary mechanic, and is so responsive that it can even feel a bit jarring.  Some of the weapons feel great, and a few of the upgrades are pretty interesting.  I can absolutely see potential in the game and really hope that it continues to grow.The biggest problem with the game is that overall its just a bit too slow, most of the bosses feel easy and the biggest problems you'll likely run into with them is extremely glitchy hitboxes, getting stuck in animations, or just running out of your exceedingly small stamina bar.  The armor pickups feel disappointing because they don't change the game at all and are entirely cosmetic, a lot of the weapons feel like the same animation, and without the ability to try weapons before you spec into them or respec at all (apparently its coming at some point) you can spend hours pushing points into a stat to try out a weapon just to find it boring and sticking you with a stat you don't want.TLDR: I think a lot of these problems can be fixed with updates, but I'm worried the game is hamstrung by a few of its core concepts and is ultimately the reason I don't recommend the game to others.  I think it just slightly missed the mark, and while its fun and has a really interesting concept... it just feels a bit like a beta release.

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderfully unique setting and combat mechanics, but tons of bugs, poor optimisation, sloppy controls and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ surprise moments really take away from the overall experience. Hopefully the game will patch out most of its technical problems, especially wonky geometry.Two things I want to specifically adress. First, I particularly despise the fact that the map is almost always absent. Areas are constructed in such a way, that you will explore nearly the entirety of a location before getting a chance to see its map. And the amount of detail on it is inexcusably low. Second, the amount of damage you receive from environmental hazards while platforming is so much you'll die in three hits, five if you have healing. Combined with how long some of these sections are, the game quickly goes from annoying to rage-inducing in them.Don't take me wrong, I like the game, it certainly is another addition to all the great metroidvanias of present time, but I wish the game was more fair to the player. Oh, also, there is fall damage in this platformer game. Yes, its combat focused. No, that doesn't change the fact that platformers shouldn't do that.

_childDocuments_.review: Hollow Knight's release in 2017 marked a turning point in the Metroid-like genre. Since then, the popularity of Metroid-likes that also try to be Souls-likes has risen, and while a lot of them are great, many don't nail the feeling of exploration that Hollow Knight had. Grime is not one of these games. In fact, I haven't felt so thrilled exploring a Metroid-like game world since I played Hollow Knight some years ago.To start, there's the atmosphere. The 3D graphics and the lighting, coupled with the unique environments mildly inspired by body horror aesthetics make for a disturbing trip into the unsettling caverns of a world made of rock. The level design is amazing, secrets are everywhere, and the game makes sure that the better ones are not easy to reach. In addition, there are entire areas, along with bosses, that are completely optional. And while exploring the game is partly why I consider it so good, I'd wager speed-running it is just as fun. This is mostly because of the snappy controls and fun movement options revolving (no pun intended) around the black hole that you have for a head. I was almost disappointed that there wasn't a secret superhard platforming challenge, because the game sure does have a huge focus on tough platforming. And tough combat, of course.Showing its Dark Souls inspiration, the main combat mechanic is parrying your enemies in order to absorb huge chunks of your health, which also allows you to heal. Couple this with great weapons, each one with unique special attacks that all feel weighty, and both the regular enemies and the huge bosses are a treat to fight. And most enemies reward you with a specific trait that you can acquire to fit your playstyle better.Oh, and speaking of Darks Souls inspiration, yes, this game has very unique lore that will take a lot of analyzing to decipher.For how much I praised this game, I do have a couple of negative points. One is fall damage, and while the devs have addressed it and it is an integral part of gameplay, 2D and fall damage just don't get along. Even less in a game where the focus is exploration and there's a lot of verticality. The other is the map system: they tried going for a Cornifer-kinda vibe, but instead of fully revealing the map, reaching a beacon only reveals what you've explored so far in a new area. The problem is that until you reach it, that map is completely blank. The result? Backtracking to areas that you've already explored without realizing, because your map shows them as unexplored, and if you miss a required path in an area where you haven't found the map, good luck finding where to go. I think it's great that they tried something different, but in a genre where looking at the map is key to progressing, it was not a good idea.Regardless of these two problems, I loved the game. I was sure I'd enjoy it, but I didn't expect it to be so good. If you like Dark Souls, Hollow Knight and exploration-based Metroid-likes, definitely don't sleep on this one. While it sure won't mark a turning point as Hollow Knight did, I hope it is remembered as one of the best in this style of game.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who is currently on NG+12 I feel it's finally time to give a review to the game I've had the pleasure of reliving over and over again. Quick note regarding the story:I feel that the game is best experienced blind without any major spoilers regarding the story. You are unlikely to find every little lore bit on the first go around, but figuring out the finer details of this usually grotesque and sometimes beautiful world is satisfying on a meta level I haven't seen in many other games. Don't expect Grime's most important nuances to be found in text. The developers respect you more than that so use your head.  Platforming in this game is smooth and deliberate. Deliberate is defined in contrast to standard 2D platformer fair, which is where you have so much air mobility mistakes hardly matter. When you make a jump the outcome is controllable and predictable despite what some people somehow think. Jump strafing attacks is very viable and easy to do, and are a readily available means of dodging a wide variety of attacks. There is a clear input distinction between short and long jumps for easy precision. Classic movement resource management applies during later platforming segments, and the game will make sure you understand it. The developers even added an accessibility ability for those who found the base game platforming to be too difficult, but don't expect everything to be so easy... (I love the Parting Shade update gimme that and more in Grime 2) Grime combat is methodical. You won't be mashing buttons like your typical Metroidvania, and every decision you make actually does matter. The game starts off slow and teaches you the ropes. Parrying in Grime is literally the only way to progress past the first area, which is a very subtle way of telling you to practice it. Regular enemies have react-able patterns with a large game-play incentive to learn them. Absorbing enemies via the parry unlocks traits which you can invest in, and further specialize in along your journey. Hitboxes are very tight and enemy attack animations have significant weight behind them. Micro such as the previously mentioned jump strafing relies on precise hitboxes, fluid aerial movement, and for it to feel satisfying enemy encounters must take advantage of said movement system. If you're used to the leeway that other "difficult" games afforded you, this will either feel clunky or refreshing. Grime has many weapons with quite the variety of play-styles to choose from. You have your usual str/dex split, but I actually think the weapons themselves are what you should focus on. Find something cool and just set your stats accordingly. The longer the animation the more damage it usually deals. Pretty simple and timeless philosophy. You can of course make every weapon work, but if you're having a hard time there are easier weapons than others. Healing is far less plentiful than what you're probably used to. Parrying enemies with certain health bars gives you the resource to heal, along with an optional hidden potion system to tie you over. Please just learn to parry regular enemies. There are even traits that increase the parry frames and decrease damage taken if you miss.  . I can't tell you how many 3 move bosses I've fought over the years in Metroidvanias, and if you're like me this will be a very exciting experience. These bosses have layers. Thoughtfully weaved layers of area denial, forced platforming, and complex interactive states that allow for an extreme amount of depth. There are several bosses on this roster that could literally be final bosses in other metroidvanias, that's the scale of set-piece we are talking about here. Don't even get me started on the OST. To be brief (wall of text ikr) I will say Alex Roe outdid himself on this one. NG+ actually changes every boss fight for the better. I can't quite go into detail without listing every change and therefore spoiling the entire game. But I can certainly say I'm looking forward to seeing further mixups and shenanigans in Grime 2. Also there's a superboss. Man this game just has everything. Actually done with that wall of text? This will be relatively brief compared to that due to the spoiler-heavy nature of this topic. In short: the game isn't afraid to hide things from you, and there is alot of cool stuff to find. Weapons, armor, and a fair share of bosses aren't found in readily accessible places. There is plenty of backtracking around if you're up for it. Just make sure to look around first since they're pretty well hidden.  No lag during boss fights thankfully but... there are some performance issues, though I think people forget that this game has 3D assets translated onto a 2D platforming environment. And it's a really good looking environment at that. These aren't exactly sprites we're talking about here. However I would love to see further optimization in the sequel given what looks to be an increased emphasis on locale diversity.People play this game like it's a Souls-like and complain that they're constantly out of stamina. Here's a tip: play this game like it's old Monster Hunter. Translation: the vertical axis exists and you should use it. Let's not have another "nerf Radahn" situation.I want more Dreamborn armor sets just patch it into the game gimme a reason to go to NG+20 I dare you :)
