_childDocuments_.review: Falling from a broken sky, you crash onto a world of misbegotten amalgams. You have but one purpose. To destroy... to absorb... to GROW. Nothing can stop you. Go forth and do what you were created to do.Traverse a strange and anatomically twisted world of flesh and stone. One intertwined with the other. Where the inhabitants of this world are stone, the environments are made of flesh. Guts and viscera create an eerie landscape that is downright beautiful. Uncover the secrets beneath a broken sky and you will find yourself stopping often to take in the breath-taking scenery. This game is absolutely gorgeous. Each new area I discovered had its own captivating landscape, often making me proclaim its beauty aloud.The story follows suit of many modern Metroidvanias; there is little. To me, this is not a fault but a positive. It tells the story in my favorite way, through the exploration of the world and its inhabitants, gaining items and through the dialogue. It has a very visual story. The way the environments and the creatures look tells you a lot about this strange, creepy place.The combat relies heavily on a parry/absorb system. Not only can the parry repel and damage an enemy, but when you successfully absorb it gives you Breath which is then used as a self heal. I love the way this mechanic is implemented. The parry is absolutely mandatory and by adding a self heal it rewards the players for utilizing it. As for weapons, there is a multitude of tools of death to find and choose from with various attack speeds and patterns. Each weapon has the ability to drastically change your playstyle and can be upgraded. The game is a sort of pseudo RPG, allowing you to gain points through killing certain prey and spend them on passive skills.The boss fights were fantastic. Learn attack pattern. See new pattern. Die. Repeat. Even when I would be hitting my head against the wall on a boss, it always felt fair. Never was I frustrated or saying how much I f*****g hated the game (which is common for me on frustrating fights) because it ALWAYS. FELT. FAIR. Every death was my fault and I knew I just had to play better. The game pushes you to master the mechanics and only then can you proceed. In this regard, the game reminded me of Unto the End. Every enemy has the ability to end you.With every good game, there is good sound design and a good score. The OST for GRIME was done by Alex Roe, who perfectly matches the music to the world. My favorite track is The Whispering Mothers as it makes you see this boss fight as a sort of beautiful dance.The only complaint I can even give is the lack of a New Game + option. Upon game completion, I went through and explored any areas I missed but found myself wishing I could fight all of the bosses again. I would love to start a new save with all of my current abilities and fight through the world again with properly scaled enemies. Dive into this world black hole first and absorb everything that crosses your path. Be patient and use all of the game mechanics and be sure to stop and smell the flowers, just be careful which ones you smell.

_childDocuments_.review: GRIME is an underrated gem of the metroidvania genre. This game just oozes passion and creativity, and the attention to detail on almost every aspect of its components is worthy of praise. Let's look at them individually:COMBAT: The cornerstone of the gameplay. The combat of GRIME takes heavy inspiration from Souls-like games, only on a 2D plane. The movements of your character are slow and deliberate, they feel heavy and powerful. You can parry enemy attacks, and the parry is a very important and powerful part of your toolkit because it is one of two defensive options, the other being a dash that can go through enemies and certain hazards. You are limited, however, by a stamina bar that depletes on every action you take and takes a little while to refill. This makes combat very intense and the moment-to-moment gameplay requires focus and skill, because this is one HARD game. The enemies hit very hard and some of their placement is very tricky. The bosses are noteworthyfor their design, difficulty and intensity of their encounters, these big enemies will really test you and you better be well prepared for them. This leads me to my next point:PROGRESSION: GRIME is a very open-ended game, and true to its metroidvania nature, backtracking and exploration are very important parts of the whole experience. Fortunately, for those who like to get straight to the point we have markers on the map that give us a rough location of our next objective, so we never get lost. Speaking of the map, the design is very interesting: each time you enter a new area you will wander around in the dark until you find a "beacon", which will uncover the parts you have explored so far and will continue to update as you progress until the next big area. This adds a layer of difficulty because the level design is very labyrinth-like and the platform can be quite complicated (but very fun) and branching paths are aplenty. For fans of the genre though, this system can be quite interesting and challenging. For those of us who take the time to explore and remember the inaccessible parts of the map for later, we will be rewarded with plentiful goodies: armor sets, new weapons with unique movesets, upgrade items, consumables that will give us an edge on combat, fast-travel points and optional mini-bosses who are a reward in and of themselves since the combat is so gratifying. We can use all these tools to better equip ourselves, and we will also spend "mass", this game's currency and EXP system, all in one. We collect mass when we defeat enemies or use certain items, and we spend mass to level up each of our stats individually. Each weapon is unique and different, and none of them feels useless, not even the starting ones. This is because each weapon scales with some of our stats differently, so we can pick and choose which build we go for depending on our playstyle.ARTISTRY: GRIME is a strikingly beautiful game. Being 2D, a lot of emphasis was put on the backgrounds and each area feels very distinct and memorable, despite the very strong stone theme in almost all of them. This is a very unique artistic choice in GRIME, everything is rocks and stones. And hands. Lots and lots of hands. It makes for a very bleak and desolate atmosphere, but it is very fitting since we are an antropomorphic black hole devouring everything, after all. Even still, the game can fill with very pretty colors and striking landscapes, and the experience is enhanced by the sound design. The sounds are very fitting for the creatures we find and are quite satisfying, and the music is very low-key, ominous and minimalistic, but it knows how and when to rise in orchestral crescendos to accentuate the most important parts of our journey. A journey that is very, very obscure in its purpose and goal. Our character is silent and the NPCs talk in a very confusing and obtuse way. It doesn't help that a LOT of this game's terminology is not at all intuitive and the writers really seem to like to make up words or use complicated terms with little to no context to sound ominous and menacing. Still, near the end of the game a lot of lore just clicks and makes a little more sense, but it will no doubt leave you with plenty of questions. Mysteries abound, but replaying the game on the NG+ mode (which boasts new enemies, improved bosses and new upgrades) and paying attention to all the lore will undercover a very deep, existential and depressing story about the illness of the body, the illness of the mind and the inescapable fear of the void. It is a very, VERY slow burn, but oh so worth it.DEV SUPPORT & DLC: This game was released in 2021 and it still gets a lot of support from its devs, with already 3 FREE DLCs and one more coming before the sequel. From what I've seen, GRIME's devs take player feedback seriously and have made strides to improve the game since its release. Their level of dedication to making a new and polished game, with so much passion, deserves to be recognized.CONCLUSION: If you're a fan of either metroidvanias, soulslikes or just hard games, you will enjoy GRIME. If you (like me) are a fan on all three, you will LOVE GRIME. Support the devs and buy this game, it deserves a lot more recognition. And look forward to the 4th DLC and the sequel!

_childDocuments_.review: F*cking delicious...I liked everything about it and now I'm so incredibly impressed.. Ahhrgh! It's so difficult to explain. Still i'll try:Firstly, I'd never imagine I could get a game that'd be capable to make me feel like a real dodger. Like glass but unstoppable thing. So that there'd be no combo or situation you managed but ran out your stamina.Ohhhh... that was the best one. There's no words to describe that experience... And graphics (words ain't even needed).And story.The story needs a separate mention. It made me cry some times. _childDocuments_.review: This is a 51% YES review, because I really like the game and want to support the developers.That said, this game is DIFFICULT and for all the wrong reasons.Over all my years I've never come across an art style like this, the whole presentation is gorgeous.The rock theme is refreshing, the body metaphors are wonderful gruesome, the story something different and unique.Truly a piece of Art and a real diamond in the rough.That said, the price for all that eye candy is the game DEMANDING perfection from you, while having quite some flaws itself.The overall gameplay is solid, you need to get your mechanics straight and then it's really fun.I'm surprised there is not more speedrunning, it certainly looks like the game is made for it.Small secrets to find, enemy variation, some platforming puzzles, the abstrusity, top notch.As I said though, the game is difficult. But more often from janky game behavior than challenge.- Enemies can stun-lock you(Because you missing the Force to do anything and it will only regenerate after like 2 seconds)- You constantly grab ledges that you don't want to(Because the game is very lenient with ledge hit-boxes for some reason and there is no additional input to actively choose to grab on)- Sometimes the game has micro-lags that disturb your flow, but also inputs are simply dropped from time to time(Devastating in the context of precision this game often requires)- Health does not matter when fighting bosses, they will often just one-hit you as result of even one mistake(In addition you might have to walk a short distance to get back to the boss)- Consumables are mostly underwhelming and barely useful- The "rat fang" environment hazards need such precision that I had look up how it works, because I thought I'm missing an ability to pass them and got stuck- A bit lacking in terms of quality of life and player comfort(Zone teleporters are somewhat far, on-death teleport to the last checkpoint, not the closest, no proper item activation in the menu, etc.)- Some areas are quite dark and you don't get anything for lightingCuriously enough, the first few items you get are extremely solid and kind of makes other equipment obsolete, if not for looks.Also the stated issues get worse with the dlc content, as that content is even more demanding.Bosses want you dancing and it feels like you are forced into EXACTLY the pattern they want, there is no deviation.I really want to enjoy this game, and I mostly do, as it is packed with charm, but it is truly a rough ride.The core definition of pure, raw potential and an experience worth trying.Tons of appreciation for taking a different take on the design than the usual worn out (high-) fantasy or classic sci-fi.Grimes presentation is just: *chef's kiss*.

_childDocuments_.review: I quite enjoyed this game. The boss fights were fun and unique, the style of the art was right up my alley and it was a solid metroidvania. _childDocuments_.review: There's a few things I don't like about it, but the world and the gameplay makes up for it! Super fun and addictive- definitely a challenging game that relies mostly on dodging at the right time, managing your stamina and upgrading your skills and weaponsMy only few complaints are the travel system and the weapon upgrades. Travel wise, it takes a while to get from one side of the map to the other and the fast travel points are... kinda out of the way.The weapons look cool, although I keep coming back to the first weapon in the game- the axe. It's fast, does good damage and it's special attack does more damage then most of the slow weapons special and normal attacks. Might be just me, but at a glance it's too good to pass up... the other weapons do have some advantages that you can only really get from using them- I just started forcing myself to use the other weapons. I don't know if upgrading them is a good idea or not, as the upgrade materials seem to be limitedHowever, they're pretty minor points- love the game in general. It's fun, got an interesting world design and concept (LIving rocks- super cool)- I would definitely recommend this game! It's like a Metroidvania had a baby with darksouls. It has a little of the feeling from each game type

_childDocuments_.review: Grime is excellent. Very reminiscent of Hollow Knight while maintaining its own  very distinct identity. When I bought this I was expecting a classic low-budget souls-like metroidvania, but I was constantly impressed by the effort and finesse that was put into making this game the lovely experience that it is.I was most impressed by the quality of the soundtrack: the main menu isn't usually where I expect to be slammed with the big bass strings and Gregorian chanting that I'd expect from a Warhammer 40k title. It sets the stage for what's to come both gameplay-wise and for the rest of the marvellous OST.I highly recommend Grime. Try it.

_childDocuments_.review: A SoulsVania GemI've played my share of Soulslike games lately. Along with Roguelike, this genre is trending: we see much more games like these or even games that didn't even have the genre are being adapted into some kind of Soulslike (Darksiders 3 and Jedi Fallen Order just to name a couple).Grime isn't the only MetroidVania with a Souls feel at all. If you haven't played Hollow Knight, do yourself a favor and play that game first. Grime is an action 2D game. It's a hard game, you'll die a lot. However unlike Dark Souls, you never have to worry about losing your hardworked currency. That means you don't quite have to worry about dying because you can still spend the mass you've earned.While exploration is not punished, it's only encouraged as long as you're continuing the story because unlike Metroid games, you are not really forced story-wise to re-explore previous areas. Also, while there are a lot of perks and weapons you're aren't really able to try a lot because you need to spend limited resources to refund your ability points. For this reason, I just kept the first weapon as my main.Apart from these few minor cons, Grime is a great game. Boss and mini-boss fights are amazing. They are quite different from one another and very satisfying. Parrying is not only encouraged but mandatory if you want to beat the game. Even though the timing for parrying is forgiving, you still definitely have to get good to succeed in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: GRIME

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent metroidvania / soulslike, easily recommended. I've played like a dozen+ of these games since the pandemic and this one is right up there with some of the big titles.Pros:- Very well designed and satisfying bosses, far above average. You go into them getting obliterated but come out mastering them and feeling like a champ.- Off beat lore and atmospheric, some really cool backgrounds and music at times- The combat feels smooth and methodical, the parrying is generous and fun to use- Character builds via traits you absorb from defeating enemies. There are armor sets with stat boosts and trait bonuses. The weapon selection is fairly large and each one has its own stats and special move.- Levels are hand crafted, generally well designed and fun to explore- Difficulty is quite hard but fair.- Some great platforming challenges / puzzles. They might get on the hard side for people who aren't good at that sort of thing, but I enjoyed it.- Responsive devs that seem to be actively improving and working on the game with community feedbackCons:- One area in particular (like middle of the palace) could maybe use a checkpoint- There was the odd bug surrounding ladders and grabbing ledges, but nothing too severeWishlist:- Ability to try out weapons before investing in them- Boss rush mode and/or a way to rematch bossesThere have been patches since the criticisms on release, and in my playthrough the checkpoint and fast travel spacings are almost entirely fine now. I didn't run into any show stopping bugs and they're adding sprinting in a future patch to ease up traveling even further.Anyway, if you liked games like Blasphemous or this genre in general you should check Grime out. It has a sweet atmosphere, fun platforming, and very fun and memorable boss battles.

_childDocuments_.review: My first Metroidvania, and my god is it amazing. There was only one boss fight that really me awhile to beat, but man are the boss fights themselves incredible. _childDocuments_.review: The teeth. I'm not recommending the game solely for the teeth. One of the worst and terrible examples of game design I have ever seen in my life. First time you see them, you will try attacking, no luck. Then jumping. They will kill you over and over.  You decide "Well this is a metroidvania game. I must need an item!" you'll search, find nothing. Then look it up on a wiki...Yes you ARE supposed to jump through the teeth to progress the game. In a very imprecise, nigh perfect, way. There was no way to indicate how. Horrible game design. And now that you know.. it's very inconsistent.  And you need to jump through multiple times. And it feels more like a coin flip if you don't do this awkward, near perfect pixel jump.And SO Much of this game explains no mechanics. Purple doors? run through them with sprint. Will we tell you? No. Spikes? Dash through them. Will we tell you or show an example? No.  Final boss. Killed. Finally. Good battle. Oh! An escape sequence! Slipped and die.. redo the boss because F*ck you. I mean, whoever made this game needs to take some basic courses in game design!

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely beautiful Souls Like metroidvania platformer. These developers are also incredibly communicative and so much love and care was invested in their game, a realy rare thing to see in this world of cashing in and forget about it mentality.Or maybe they just love their fans. who the hell wouldn't love us. We're awesome!-Visuals: STUNNING, beutiful landscapes and very clever artistic and environmental storytelling without being a smartass. The game does pull it's weight with great style.-Difficulty: a VERY comfortable middle ground for experienced players, might be a bit difficult for new players to the genre, but certainly not among the most difficult or irritating game. It hits the perfect balance for me when it comes to difficulty.-Level design: FANTASTIC. The exploration feels wonderful, so many small secrets and shortcuts hidden here and there, even if generally most aren't a huge game changer, it feels so nice to discover the map gradually, and it is really well built and different areas are masterfully interconnected.-some minus points: you are not able to try out the weapons and their moveset before investing points in their respective attribute requirements. I wish we would be able to use them (inefficiently with low damage) to try them out before committing precious points just to check out a weapon.Looking forward for future projects of these developers, they are people worth following to see what they might do nextand Yes, totally worth the full price. In case you are wondering.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely astonishing game. You get thrown into an unknown world full with weird creatures and living terrain. You don't know anything about your past or what you're doing there, all you know is that you need to consume to get stronger. Over time you unlock new abilities that help you advance so that you can take on bosses.Grime is a fun and difficult Souls-Like. It looks amazing and the exploration is very exciting. You get to meet many strange NPCs, each with their own personality, from admiring you to hating you. The world is a dark and unforgiving place, and they convey it pretty well.I can definitely recommend it too all the Souls-Like enjoyers. It became one of my most favorite ones.

_childDocuments_.review: You judge a few things when playing a metroidvania.Lore. It's philosophically intriguing as how the atmosphere is created. We have several distinctive key characters that contribute to the main plot progressing. Very well written.Exploration. Very terrible experience as many scenes look similar, that makes its map revealing system annoying and frustrating. You want some backtracking? There's nearly no fast travel here. Seriously?Combat and platforming. It's mediocre. Everything feels squishy. Parrying is easy and forgiving. It's nicely blended into the combat and character building systems. Character progressing. What I see is this game copies how those rpgs create many character builds and weapons and styles. But sadly it's a failure. Weapons are very unbalanced so are enemy stats. Player stats feel like none. You are expected to make zero mistake in late game. Be prepared. I suggest an overhaul to numbers in general.It's a good game. Endeavors are respected.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE:  In the off-chance that someone might read this - there have been several fantastic updates to the game that address many of the gripes in my original review.  While a few won't change simply because they are core design elements of the game, I'm going to upgrade my review to 8/10.  This game was a great game, and now it's even better.  ORIGINAL REVIEW:  As many others have said, the game is obnoxious.  It's not difficult.  Every boss I've fought so far has been killed in a couple attempts.  Navigating the areas, can be a lot of fun. However, 90% of your deaths will be getting to the boss.  The mapping system is crap.  Map visibility is locked behind finding pillars that are (sometimes) placed in locations that make no sense.  I've fought through an area and killed the boss without ever discovering the map unlock for the area.  It's really, really dumb.  The game is littered with obnoxious and pointless annoyances that don't add difficulty, they just ruin the enjoyment of what would've been one of the best Metroidvanias I've played in a while. The art style is wonderful - just look at the screenshots. Animation is buttery smooth. Audio is well above average. The combat is great most of the time, but can be hindered by sloppy controls. For example, your character can get stuck on walls, ladders, and enemies. I've been killed on a ladder, only to spawn on the ladder and immediately fall, then respawn, then fall to my death in an infinite death loop. If you attempt to grab a ladder while standing on a moving platform, your character will bug out, slide off the ladder, then get stuck on the ground in the ladder-climbing animation. Hidden paths will obscure enemies that will remain hidden and then magically pounce on you the instant the hidden path opens up.  This is a perfect example of annoying game design that doesn't add difficulty. Floating enemies will inexplicably zoom in front of you and block your path as you make a jump, causing you to fall to your death. Enemies charging up an "unblockable" attack will inexplicably turn around  and hit you as you dash through them. The hit register can be bizarre as well, where moving closer to enemies will cause your attacks to miss, yet moving out of range will cause them to hit.Bad things aside, the game really is awesome. It reminds me a little of Shadow of the Beast. The world is so imaginative, it's worth the play through just to experience the world they've built. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: I don't generally like souls-like games because I find them a bit too slow and unforgiving however, Grime's combat and movement feels fluid and fast, the former depending on your weapon choice, and the penalty for dying isn't as severe (although there is still a penalty). It also has RPG elements in that you can gain skills by absorbing particular enemy types and you can upgrade your stats (Health, Strength, Dexterity etc.) by using "souls", these same souls can also be used to purchase items in the shop.If I had one complaint, which is a very shallow one, it would be the "skins". They don't seem to add anything in terms of stats, so far at least, and I think they look quite unattractive and bland. It'd be nice if they had more texture and colour :)I played the demo a week or so ago and purchased it as soon as it was released and I honestly couldn't be happier. It's the metroidvania RPG hybrid I've been looking for. Thanks devs! :D

_childDocuments_.review: This game is slow, slow attacks, slow movement speed, slow progression. Way too much backtracking due to the ability to teleport between save points is locked behind a hidden boss. Double jump and air dash are among the last abilities you unlock meaning you will spend most game-play seeing secrets that you just cant get into in every single named area for 90% of the game. Almost all bosses are surprisingly easy due to the parry system the difficult bosses are just the ones that the devs decided to cover in you cant parry this paint making some builds really difficult to use. Almost all the hunt points are really underwhelming except for the ones that give you extra stamina on perfect dodges and parries and the ones that allow you to regain healing charges on things other than parries. Too be honest this game can be enjoyable for some but to me this game is a horridly mediocre metroidvania attempt and i cant really recommend it at full price maybe wait for a sale

_childDocuments_.review: A really fantastic Metroidvania. The graphics are beautiful, the story is dark, the world quite expansive, and the controls are well polished.I was completely hooked from the first boss encounter – the fight had a very satisfying rhythm to it, one that took me a couple attempts to get into, but once it clicked, it was so rewarding. And the same thing can be said of most other bosses in the game.There's also plenty of secrets to discover, with just enough clues to make it possible for you to spot them on your own, without feeling like they are too obvious.And the music is a perfect complement to the graphic design. Although, this is one area where I feel like the game deserves some criticism – when the music plays, it really accentuates the atmosphere, but there are just way too many places where there just isn't any. You just suddenly realize that the game is awfully quiet, because there are areas without any background music at all. Either way, this is a fairly minor annoyance.I have now played through the game three times, and I can't wait for the final DLC to be out so I get to experience it once again.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game up until the point that the gameplay became so tediously punishing that it was no longer fun to play. I do think it's a good game, and would reccomend it, but only with some caveats.I'm a souls player but not much of a metroidvania player, so I'm going to give the benefit of the doubt to the game and say that my issues are because I'm not used to metroidvanias?Pros: -Very good souls combat-Fun movement mechanics-Unique upgrade mechanics-Gorgeous visuals and unique enemies-Fun parrying/heal mechanicCons:-Waaaay too much backtracking and repetitious platforming-No bonfire fast travel system-Annoying boss designs that can 2-shot you but take forever to kill and have multiple phases-Not enough ways to healUltimately the boss fights are what ruined the game for me. When a boss fight starts to feel like a precision platforming session (eg, mess up once and you start over) I can only stand to slog it out for so long before it's not fun anymore.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing Game. Really enjoyed my time with this one and looking forward to new content they shall bring.Art style is awesome. Many left in Awe moments so to say. Backgrounds/Skyboxes are well doneCombat is smooth and you feel powerful when you find and upgrade many of the weapons. Just make sure you hit many walls and floors as you explore as there is a lot to be discovered and many of the places are not obvious that it leads to a Secret path/chamber.Outfits are unique and offer cool benefits when trying to optimise your build.Boss battles are fun and the OST of the game was a joy to listen too. _childDocuments_.review: DEFINITELY A BUY  if you are into Dark souls stamina system and combat system with a blend unique world like hollow knight. Only difference here is the world is GRIM and dark. Pretty underrated game. To me this is as close as it gets to playing another hollow knight kind of game. unique world filled with cute enemies. Combat - those that have not played dark souls or any stamina related combat game will have a harder time and might rage quit. But if you understand to not USED ALL THE STAMINA and reserve some for dodging always. then the fight wont be hard.World/map - BEAUTIFUL and pay attention to the background of the world to finding key areas. You can thank me later.Platforming- pretty decent platforming. Easier than hollow knight.   Leveling - It's pretty nice to not lose your EXP when you die. this makes the game way less frustrating. Boss - So far no bugs. All boss pretty good design. you will have some retry, Difficulty depends on your choice of weapon  that you use against each boss. Mobs - when you first encounter a new monster dont go in and try to deflect/parry. YOU WILL REGRET IT. Study it first dont be like me. LOL always remember if your not confident in that enemy you can dodge first. dodging is easier. Weapons - only a few good one. That you can totally destroy enemy with, alot of meh weapons sadly. my favourite weapon is a boss weapon. when you click on that special attack, if you time it before the enemy lands an attack on you. you will activate the skill where you dodge that attack leap up and slam the ground for BIG DMG. I wish other metroidvania has weapons like this lol.Bugs - stuck while dashing here and there. happens but not too often that I would rage quit.Feedback - some area too dark. i was finding an item for light source. in the end I used the lantern weapon to light my way lol. kinda sad. that there is no light skills. OVERALL superb metroidvania game.

_childDocuments_.review: I will keep my current review of the game as a reminder of what the game WAS; compared to how it is now.Better.The devs seems to have taken to heart some of the major flaws the game had and have ironed out alot of the gripes i had previously, combat feels more focused, cheap deaths still happen but not as frequently (weeping giant STILL comes to mind with no telegraphed attacks!) and some of the quality of life upgrades help it out alot.  I can safely say now that i beat it, its worth checking out in its more polished and refined state.---Very jank movement, your character feels like not just a rock but a boulder trying to roll through sludge, your 'force' (energy meter) will be your biggest enemy next to the controls, and enemys dont have fluid attack patterns, sometimes not even doing a proper telegraph. Also, this game has glitches that WILL frustrate you: Dodging into invisible walls that werent there before; jumps you sometimes can make and other times you cant;  momentum pads not giving you full height (again, at times), enemy's hitboxes being WAY bigger than what they even telegraphed, letting you get hit when you werent even near them. Also im feeling that if you get hit, your 'force' also takes damage as ive found my energy just GONE when i get plumbed by 2 or more enemys.I bought this as a bundle...and honestly, i like the OTHER game i got better than this one, it may not be the better in graphic, but its combat and 'jank' actually had fluidity and made it much more enjoyable.One final issue i have is with this games 'parry' mechanic; did you know you can use it to strip armor/shields?I SURE DIDENT!I had to learn it from trial and error; but it only works on SOME enemys.  This mechanic was not brought up or better explained.  I only found out about it when trying to fight a giant crab-jaw monster, and could only do pitiful damage to it, turns out his claws were blocking my attacks.  How do you stop this?  Use the parry mechanic to strip off the claw armor.This is effectively saying "oh, you'll figure that out eventually' when this is APPARENTLY a very crucial game mechanic that isent even hinted at.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the indie gems, ranking up there with Hollow Knight or Ori and the Blind Forest.Incredible artstyle merged with responsive, challenging combat. The world of Grime lures you in with just how unique its... geode aesthethic shines, then has you battle through dangerous foes a la the seemingly obligatory Dark Souls reference.Speaking of Souls, Grime thankfully leans away from the Dark Souls 2 school of game design, where there is prevalent spam and an obsession with ambushing you around every other corner. I'd describe pretty much all of Grime as very 'fair' difficulty.It has its fair share of annoyances here and there, as well as some bugs. I got stuck in the walls a few times myself and I have had some of the friendly NPCs seemingly warp around at random, spouting no longer relevant story beats as if they had been moved out of time.And while such errors are irritating, they do not take away from the whole in any meaningful regard. It is an absolute delight, and it is a game that should not be missed.

This game is weird, really weird, but not in a bad sense.The aesthetics are strange and amazing, borderline body horror in some ways, so if you find hands, teeth and other body parts jutting out walls disturbing, you've been warned.The music is fantastic, but unfortunately absent in some areas. Some of the more difficult areas can be frustrating to run through over and over, and there is quite a bit of backtracking, these two points were the only negatives personaly. Overall a really good game.

_childDocuments_.review: Simply put, a must-play for any fans of Souls-likes OR Metroidvanias. The combination Souls-like + Metroidvania genre has been growing a lot lately, but this is one of the few that hits all of the marks for me personally. Judging it just as a game on its own: the art style is a great mix of beautiful and (duh) grimy. You've got your classic caves and deserts, elaborate palaces, and without spoiling any endgame areas some truly awe-inspiring art. Everything from the environments to your character to your equipment all reflects this, with weapons being living objects and transforming based on your attacks in some cases. The soundtrack and the score are both incredible, with the boss soundtrack done by Alex Roe, a very well-known member of the Souls community, who's even collaborated with the likes of Yuka Kitamura herself (Dark Souls 2/3, Bloodborne, Sekiro, Elden Ring).As a Souls-like, the combat gets the "tough but fair" thing down: bosses are challenging at first but with very well-telegraphed attacks, patterns, and once you've mastered them, you'll get in a rhythm of dancing around while wrecking their health bar. The parry system is fairly forgiving, especially if you're used to the relatively tight windows of most Souls-likes, and the game does a great job of showing you what exactly can and cannot be parried. That being said, parrying is massively important, in both regular encounters and bosses. It deals damage, it gives you your healing charges, and can be upgraded to provide additional benefits on top of those two. If you don't have those "twitch" reflexes, the game will be significantly harder, but again it's definitely something you can get better at through learning enemy patterns, and checkpoints are always generous. Boss runbacks in particular are VERY short, usually about one or two screens.As a Metroidvania, it's tons of fun and has all the usual beats. Great platforming, including some palm-sweat-inducing "challenge" areas. Throws upgrades at you at a good speed so you always have something new to play with. Backtracking is kept to a minimum and the game makes a pretty clear "point of no return" if you want to go back and get everything you missed. The developers have also teased a "dash" upgrade that will make this faster in a future update, with other content to come as well. Also because this has been a trend in some games of this genre: yes, there is a map.As for what makes it unique, there are two progression systems. You have your standard RPG fare strength, dex, magic, health, stamina. But you also have passive abilities that you get from consuming enemies (you are a sentient black hole thing, after all). These range from "just ok" to "must have" and fortunately the cost of re-speccing isn't too bad. That being said, you won't exactly be swimming in the token needed, so it's not something you can do trivially without cheating. This does somewhat discourage experimentation, but generally you can figure out pretty quickly which upgrades are worth the investment based on your playstyle.Overall, 100% worth a buy even at full price. A 100% playthrough took me ~13 hours, and I enjoyed every minute. If you like Metroidvanias and can stand to play one that's a bit on the "hard but fair" side, you won't regret picking up Grime.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely gorgeous and unsettling metroidvania. Loved the art, the world and the actual moment to moment combat was fantastic. Boss fights in particular were amazing (and amazingly brutal). .EDIT: The beacon map thing, fast travel and a number of other things were apparently fixed or improved on the day that I posted this review. So two major patches fixing frustrations and bugs in under week!It's not perfect, unfortunately, as a lot of the platforming in certain areas is not especially polished and the actual level design can be extremely hit-or-miss depending on the area. I certainly wasn't a fan of activating a (usually hidden or far-in) beacon to begin loading the map, as it made some areas especially difficult. I realized I ended up missing quite a bit of content as a result of rushing in too far into a level in hopes of finding the beacon. The rush of crushing the area boss often made up for the earlier level's frustration, and at the very least the visual rewards of progression were more than enough to keep me moving forwards. Fortunately the devs are actively engaged with the community and adding fixes for frustrating issues. So I'm optimistic for the future and any dlc/sequel that comes out.At the price point it's at, it's definitely worth checking out if you're a fan of the genre and looking for a hefty challenge  (♥♥♥♥ you Shapely Sidus), and the devs are doing a great job of addressing complaints. Fingers crossed for DLC!

_childDocuments_.review: Hits an itch for both metroidvanians and souls-like games. The themes are dark and compelling. Not quite as compelling as competitor games like Hollow Knight but that may be because it is vastly more alien. Yeah, things are shaped like humans but the underlying feeling is anything but familiar. Combat is tight and well designed around understanding your opponent's move sets. Yes, the character gets stronger the more you level up but that isn't what wins you the boss battle. That takes learning their telegraphs and mastering parry and dodge, just like a souls-like. The most leveling gets you is access to better equipment. The only criticism I have about combat is that a few of the prey-abilities seem pretty necessary to unlock to have a real chance at killing a few bosses and the orbs to reset things like that are few and far between.Exploration is laid out relatively well although there is some glitchiness in some of the platforming. I have had the character stuck on a wall more than a few times. Some encounters and map layouts have had me irked but not because they are unfair but rather irked in a good way. Like getting frustrated by a tough, but fair, challenge. Unlockables are mostly based on finding weapons and new enemies to learn abilities from. Some are quite rare with my favorite ability coming from an enemy that there is maybe 3 of in the entire game. Some more variety in things to find while exploring here would be nice. It may be thematic but having armor be purely cosmetic is a bit of a let down.Finally, art direction is great. I get the impression of minds long disconnected from their former humanity trying to remember what being a human was all about. We get themes of beauty, life, killing, and reshaping ourselves to become "acceptable". I haven't finished the game yet at about 20 hours of game play (I often have to pause and walk away for hours at a time due to real life stuff so my hours played is a bit inflated) but I am compelled to finish it mostly based on how well executed the art direction is, followed closely by its combat system.

_childDocuments_.review: A solid 2D indie souls-like with a distinct art direction and (mostly) fun design choices. Draws a lot of aesthetic notes from Bloodborne, moreso than Dark Souls, but injects enough of its own direction to avoid feeling uninspired. There are a few too many tedious bits (long run backs, bosses with too much health, overly sparse healing at the start), and the level of polish is very inconsistent throughout (especially the attack animations). Still, there are some incredible boss fights (aided by music that punches way above its pay grade), and the moment to moment platforming becomes fun and smooth once you unlock the Pull ability. As someone who found Elden Ring excessively large, I also appreciated the game's focused scope. Before NG+, Weapons max out at +6, upgrade materials are plentiful, and the highest stat requirement for any weapon is 30. It feels much more like Dark Souls 1 or Bloodborne in this regard, and is much better off for it.I would recommend it to those with patience, a preference for slower, methodical combat, and a taste for the uniquely grotesque aesthetic. As a bonus, the developers are clearly passionate about the game and put out 4 totally free, substantial updates that show they listen to the community. Definitely excited to see more from them in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: A great game that's sadly let down with some technical issues.So I'm not great at souls-likes. I'll start off fully acknowledging that. I still managed to beat the game, but barely. I tried NG+. Nope, not for me.The main reason I'm leaving this review is in hopes that the developers focus on fixing the more technical problems. The biggest of which is that if you click outside of the window, there's a 50/50 chance your controller will just lose all interest in working until you either restart or unless you go into the Steam Overlay while the game is open, disable steam input, go back into the game, then go back into Steam Overlay, re-enable steam input and then your controller will work.That'd be fine if this was a game that didn't have a sprawling map you may need to check up on stuff outside of the game if you want to 100% it. But it's a metroidvania you can't use a map for unless you want to spend a ton of time fixing the controller bug that should not be in the game to start with. _childDocuments_.review: I tried the demo but after purchasing the full game, sadly I am disappointed. for context, I love soulsgames and also finished some challenge runs in dark souls, so I am not thrown off by the soulslike components of the game.there is way too much backtracking and the checkpoints are way too far apart. This game sometimes nailed the Dark Souls 1-moments of unlocking shortcuts to a previous checkpoint, making your life easier but this is rather the exception. Often times I found myself running through already explored areas just to get back to the mainhub of the world, focussing on not dying because I would have to restart from my last checkpoint. Steam states that I have ~8 hours in this game and I don't think I'm exaggerating when I say that probably 3 hours out it was just braindead running around. you get an errand from the mainhub sending you through the world where you discover that you are lacking a skill and run back through the world hoping to find the skill somewhere else. you return eventually and the next quest repeats the procedure.Encountering new enemies is rewarding by absorbing them and unlocking new traits but after this they become just an obstacle in your way running through the world. They give very little experience, leveling up feels like it hardly changes anything and the absorbing/parrying skill becomes obsolete later on.This made world exploration a massive pain to me, I found myself at a late game boss severly underleveled and under equipped but at no point in the game I felt encouraged to actively explore since it would have meant having to backtrack to the checkpoint for 10 to 20 minutes. apparently you unlock some form of fast travel near the end but by then it completely misses the point of making your quality of life in the game better. I also want to mention the dash ability. It is so annoying that you cannot speedjump and continue running when encountering a change of height in the terrain, always having to start over running up.So I am stuck with this boss I can't beat. My options are to backtrack through challenging jumping parts of the game not just straight ahead, farming and exploring just hoping to become actually stronger and then walking back to the boss. this would probably take another 4 to 5 hours, my estimation. or I could bruteforce my way in the hopes to kill him eventually. neither options are fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty great metroidvania, definitely takes a lot of inspiration from Hollow Knight (sometimes a little too closely, more on that later).Pros:- Extremely unique aesthetic and setting, this was the main draw of the game for me. I haven't seen anything quite like it.- Great visuals; character models all look great, varied enemy designs, awesome backgrounds, lots of cool animations. It can be a bit too dark (as in the amount of light) sometimes. - Plenty of fun NPCs, the game has a very dry, morbid sense of humor with how it treats a lot of these npcs as well. - Awesome soundtrack, has a great mix of orchestral pieces for bosses and ambient music for levels- Boss lineup is pretty solid all around, there are times when it can be hard to tell what is actually happening during a boss fight, but overall the bosses have very fair telegraphs and the difficulty curve is steady throughout, no random spikes in difficulty (looking at you Elden Ring). - Great weapon, armor and skill variety, plenty of replay value in different builds. - Most importantly, you can overlay owned armor sets cosmetically on the set you are actually using for stats. More games need to do this. Cons:- The game doesn't properly gate some areas based on your current movement abilities. There are several places where you have the ability to traverse partway across a platforming gate, but not ALL the way, and then there is no way to return from where you came, so you get softlocked and have to either use an item to return to a checkpoint or self destruct. - The checkpoints and fast travel stations are spread a little too far apart in my opinion. This is remedied later on in the game when you get the ability to teleport between checkpoints, but before that (and while exploring a new area), dying while exploring can sometimes mean repeating 15 or even 20 minutes of travel time. - The game likes to throw a lot of blind platforming at you, requiring you to make downward jumps to platforms below you that you can't see on screen. Couple this with the choice to include fall damage, and you get some pretty unsatisfying exploration. There also seems to be a height threshold where the fall damage also respawns you back your previous platform. Normally you can use an air dash to avoid fall damage, but beyond this threshold you still suffer the damage and are respawned, which feels like a very awkward and unimmersive way to gate travel progress. This is slightly remedied by an ability gained through DLC, but I can't include that as an excuse since not all players will have access to that ability. - The platforming controls glitch out too often for how demanding some of the platforming challenges are. I've consistently run into a few platforming glitches that cause the player to uncontrollably float into killzones or get stuck inside platforms. Normally I would be more willing to forgive this but it's extremely frustrating when going through the many precise platforming sections the game has. Nothing was more aggravating than the new platforming gauntlet in that was recently added in DLC. It took me 2 hours to complete and probably 30 mins of the time was due to deaths caused by these glitches. This section of the game was clearly an homage to the Path of Pain in Hollow Knight, but the difference is that HK has polished the controls enough that any failure is completely down to player skill, this isn't the case in Grime's platforming challenges and frankly, I've never understood why these games where the focus is exploration, feel the need to include these grueling platforming challenges that require hours of trial and error to complete. Overall I think Grime is a great game, and one of the better entries in the genre. If you enjoyed Hollow Knight and also like a focus on parrying like in Sekiro, then you'll like this game. I am looking forward to the sequel and hope that the devs look into some of the issues I've listed here (if they even get to read this).

_childDocuments_.review: Despite my obsession with Souls-like games, I am usually not a fan of 2D Souls-likes. I think GRIME absolutely nails it though. The combat is weighty but the dodge move is fast. But dodging too much will drain your stamina and leave you vulnerable. Enemy attacks hit hard but are well-telegraphed, so you always have a chance to parry or dodge. Taking damage does not cause your character to be knocked back/ragdoll. The traversal/combat unlocks are fleshed out and are unlocked at a decent pace. There is some decently tough but satisfying platforming here as well. The story is typical Souls-fare (formerly great kingdom is now broken and going through Armageddon/plague/Ragnarok/no more free coffee in the break room, etc.)I highly recommend this game to fans of Metroidvanias/Souls-like games.

_childDocuments_.review: TL DR: If you like Souls games, Ori and Metroidvanias, you'll definitely like this game.Some pros & cons in more detail:PROS:- combat is responsive and the control scheme makes sense, except for one move you do with the right analog stick, which should have its directional input reversed IMO (I'm vague here to avoid spoilers)- graphics and music are good- story is atmospheric, but also (too) cryptic (same as Souls games)- lots of things to discover for completionists, great value for money (takes about 20+ hours to finish the game if you don't explore, 30+ otherwise)CONS:- follows Souls formula to a fault, with all its... faults- stressful platforming segments later on, which I did not enjoy most of the time- fast travel is very limited, which harms the joy of exploration- enemy attack patterns are too hard to predict, because their weapon swing animations don't feel realistic- weapons above speed "fast" are a frustrating gamble, because bosses and even normal mob attacks that start AFTER you press attack will still interrupt you. Likewise, the animation lock of your attack will often make it feel like you pressed a skill and nothing happened if you're using weapons of "average" speed and slowerOverall, the game has a clear vision, very few bugs and it feels complete. I would have liked to see the creators deviate more from the Souls formula, because it doesn't always work (in a 2D environment), and I definitely would have made the platforming sections less input-heavy and tight. Still, it's a good product that's worth the money 100%.

_childDocuments_.review: it's very like dark souls. except the only consequence for death is having to run back to wherever you were. you don't lose much of anything. you do lose ardor on death; ardor is like a combo meter that increases the amount of Mass (souls) you get from enemies. it doesn't apply to minibosses or bosses, though, so I don't really understand what makes it so valuable.the absorb (parry) window is absolutely enormous; highly recommend parrying everything that isn't red. there have been multiple times i've successfully absorbed a few frames after getting hit, which seems silly to me.it's got a bit of a castlevania vibe, too. you absorb (some) enemies and get skills related to them, and there are plenty of interesting movement abilities that let you access secrets and new areas and such.otherwise, it has all your favorite mechanics from the DS series:- hitstun from enemy attacks leading into getting combo'd to death? check.- getting surprised by offscreen attacks that kill you? check.- the physical pain you feel on death, realizing how much ♥♥♥♥ you have to get through again? check.- feeling completely lost? check.- not being able to teleport between bonfires? check.- mimics and breakable walls? check.- finding a cool new weapon you can't use? check. (you can respec, though it's fairly expensive)- getting frustrated and turning the game off for the day, then turning it back on 3 hours later? check.it's a fun game; i just wish some of the dark souls slowness/jank wasn't around. and you really ought to lose your Mass on death. that said, it feels really good to move around, especially as you unlock more movement abilities; it's very much like Hollow Knight in that aspect.if you go into it expecting 2D dark souls, i think you'll like it. i'm only a few bosses in but it's honestly great so far.

_childDocuments_.review: Grime is one of the first castlevania like games that I played and stuck with to finish. New abilities are gained from consuming bosses that let you traverse new areas and unlock hidden paths from backtracking to visited areas. Although the fast travel system gets unlocked midway through and behind hidden paths, backtracking isn't too bad due the areas being smaller and the enemies being easily passable if you want to. The game can be fairly quiet with the main music only playing when fighting bosses. The story was interesting, centering around the stone people and their strive for becoming "perfect", while you're this being running around figuring out what you are yourself. _childDocuments_.review: First things first, this game is my game of the year at the moment. Hands down. No contest. Easy.I haven't been blown away by a game since, I think, NieR: Ataumota. There are some current bugs due to patch issues they weren't anticipating, but nevertheless, my first run through had zero bugs.NOW! What I love about this game most, is the fact that this is the first game I've really looked at as a piece of art. I recognize that all games are forms of art with all the different processes that go into making them. But I usually look at them as different art pieces mashed into a gallery of sorts. Grime on the other hand, is one whole piece of art. Every aspect of the game is so well done and naturally blends together so well. The music, the art, the animations, the lore. _childDocuments_.review: A weak "yes" from me.If you like the Metroidvanias and don't mind souls-likes I think it's a game you'll enjoy. I also think, you'll forget it as soon as you drop it and never never come back to it even if you remember it. As a package it's okay, but it doesn't do anything different or better than other similar games. Exploration is what makes or kills metroidvanias and I'm happy to report it's there and It is rewarding. Most items being useless (and some equipment being stat-gated rendering it useless) diminishes how rewarding your finds are. With that said most equipment and upgrade materials are only found by exploring, which is probably the best decision this game could have made to reward exploration. You also find regular enemies (unlock skills when absorbed) and elite enemies (give skill points when killed).Negative (with a spoiler): Some of the timed platforming sections soured my exploration experience. The worst offender (for me) has you pull a platform you're riding along a wire (it takes getting used to). The path is usually littered with traps that damage you and then reset you to the very start. Obviously damage eventually kills you and has you have to run from a checkpoint.Keep in mind this was the worst offender, not the only one.Combat is a standard 2D melee metroidvania, but with souls-like pacing and stamina restrictions. 2 things set it apart (kind of) and those are parry (absorb) and weapon special attacks. Enemies also have unblockable attacks and become pullable at specific moments (gimmick, really).Parry mechanic (absorb) is the focus of this game and you are more or less forced to use it. You absorb (and counterattack) most attacks including projectiles if an enemy is "Vulnerable" (healthbar is not greyed out). If an enemy is not vulnerable you only repel the attack (you take no damage, enemy no or low damage). Absorbing does multiple things besides parrying: refills healing resource, rips off parts of some enemies (prevents them from using certain moves) and unlocks skills when each enemy is absorb-killed enough times.Most weapons start out feeling identical to each other, with only real difference being their attack speed. Range/reach is also a factor, but less noticeable. As you get access to more weapons you'll notice each weapon has special attack/effect associated with it. Some special skills are strong and some are very useful (without just being strong), and some are outright bad as they are weak AND leave you defenseless with weird animations or long windups. Most of them are fun to try, but this wouldn't be a souls-like if weapons didn't have stat requirements that heavily discourage trying all of them.You use stamina to attack, jump, dash and counter attack. I feel like this game doesn't benefit from having stamina. Your character animations are not slow and deliberate and those of enemies are. Almost every time I ran out of stamina, the enemy was stuck in their animation giving me plenty of time to recover stamina. On one hand it makes it an easier souls-like. On the other hand I spend like half the combat time standing around (not moving or evading) waiting for stamina to recover. It just feels like a waste of time, since stamina management is not a big thing.Some fights need to be learned and stamina needs to carefully managed, but that's a few elites (not all) and bosses.It has great(10/10) features, but progression overall lacks the game-changing impact. Most noticeable progression (skills) effectively removes some of the clunkyness souls-like stamina limitations create. It's noticeable, but it's not exciting. Character progression comes in 4 forms: Stats, passive skills, boss skills and equipment. I will skip boss skills, because minor spoilers and generally speaking they are not very interesting.Obviously you have your souls-like stats where you choose between Health, Stamina and 3 weapon-specific stats. After each upgrade every other stat costs more. As is customary with souls-likes these make so little difference that you will only feel it if you compare performance after increments of 10, not the single points you allocate throughout your play-through. I personally hate this stat system, precisely because it locks me out of trying/playing different weapons while making progress virtually invisible.I think this is one of the better features in game. You have to absorb-kill enemies to unlock their skills then you have to kill stronger enemies to get skill points (finite amount). These 2 points alone add to exploration feeling rewarding and skills feel valuable. It also has other hidden benefit of teaching you to counter-attack almost every enemy in game.Skills themselves give you increased stats (BOOOOORIIIIIING) or a passive effect you can trigger after action. To give you one example, as I mentioned stamina management wastes a lot of your time, which often lead me to jumping over enemies instead of dodging (uses less stamina). One passive skill leaves a clone after dodge and if that clone gets attacked you get some stamina back. It's a little thing that mitigates a tiny bit of a problem, and in turn feels rewarding from progression point of view.Armors give a percentange bonus to specific stats and full sets empower passive skill you got from monster.Weapons have attack speed, stagger and special attack. Once you pick your weapon your stats and armors are sort of built around that.I feel like this is a lost opportunity. Devs clearly put some time into designing special attack and I will only try like half of them at best and even if I like them, I can only realistically use about 1/3 of them without losing damage. I don't feel like this game is the kind of gold-tier game that people will be replaying to try out weapons. It's an amazing supplement to the game, but not a driving reason to play it.Most storytelling is environmental storytelling and a little bit of dialogue which sets up the context to give you a better grasp on things. It's one of those games where it seems like nothing is going on, but then some story point shifts your perspective and you realize just how much was going on, but you just didn't notice.I enjoy this kind of story-telling in games for 2 reason. It's non-intrusive (not a fan of lengthy cutscenes or dialogs when the story can be told in 1 paragraph) and preserves the mystery.I think it's worth trying, even if I would recommend a whole bunch of other games before this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start with what I liked:  - the hunt aspect: I enjoyed the idea of hunting for enemies to absorb to get new passive bonuses and then spend points in them.- I liked the music: atmospheric at time and rightly epic during some bosses.- I see you dead cells inspirationNow what I disliked:- I did not particularly enjoy the asthetic. Many areas just look more of the same. (Some of the  outside backgrounds were breathtaking tough)- I did not like most of the enemies movesets: turning mid animation to deck you in the shnaws after dashing behind them, or punishing you for parrying or pulling them with hard to avoid attacks, or spamming moves that oneshot you. Bosses more frustrating to fight than anything else (shapely Fidus and Misbegotten Amalgam are special offenders)- Did not like the level design. Traps and enemy placement seems to be designed to be as obnoxious as possible. I especially hated the last 2 areas of the game, no enemies, just frustrating platforming. At least Hollow Knight's path of pain was optional.  -  - Doublejump is given at the end of the game and is only useful for 2 things: 2 hellish and unfun platforming section + final boss, and backtracking. On top of it, it feels aweful and slugish. The doublejump actually slows you down and is slow to activate.- Cosmetic only armor is a missed opportunity IMO.- The ability to backtrack to any checkpoint is given by the final boss (yeah I looked it up). So if you feel underpowered and want to do some hunting before tackling the final boss, you gotta go around the map on foot through all those boring and annoying levels, the long way around.-Missables: I hate missables. I'm the kind of gamer that likes to run around find what I can and come back later to 100% the areas once I got some better movement abilities like double-jump. So I got really frustrated when some opportunities simply disappeared without warning after certain points in the main story.- Healing way is to sparse. The game gives a mechanic where if you parry (absorb) enemies, you can breath that you can use to heal (think hollow knight heal). But the more you advance, the less frequent parriable enemies become. You can only deflect them, therefore later in game you can no longer rely on parries to get more healing, you have to rely on items that recover your breath meter, but items have to be used during the action (like healing) so if you need more breath, you need to spend time to use breath item AND spend time to heal, all the while enemies are trying to kill you. Now don't get me wrong, I enjoy challenging game play: I played and enjoyed 'Souls' games. adored Salt & Sanctuary as well as Vigil the Longest Night. But sadly, as much as I wanted to, I could not fall in love with this game. Though I'm planning to finish it (at the last boss currently). I ended up using cheat engine to even the odds (I got tired of getting oneshot by spongy enemies)Dear devs. please don't take it too personally. I know you put a lot of effort and love in your game and it shows (despite my above rambling). I expect much more positive reviews than bad and this is just my take.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game is pretty underrated, and I know why because i thought the same thing.Another metroidvania with the same gimmicky progression with a double jump and grappling hooks and whatever.It is also edgy like Dark Souls but more dull and gray.Well the thing is this game has many unique ideas, visually and gameplay-wise, but it executes them in such a humble and professional manner that it goes unseen.First of all, It is very subtle with its designs. They've gone and made everything stone, and that may remind you of boring concrete at first, but literally everything is stone. Your body, the creatures and the whole environment, which is actually equal to a human living in a world of flesh, and it is aware of this concept, that's the intended lore. I only wish it had more armor designs. But weapon designs are top notch. This game mainly revolves around parries. I know a "parry mechanic", wow, how original, you have also a light and heavy attack, how inspirational, right? The thing is this game's gameplay is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ crisp. It is so slick that AAA games on the market could eat ♥♥♥♥. The enemies' animations are so in-line with your character that you can dance around every attack of the enemy without waiting for an opening. And that is not something you can see with your eyes in a 2D game, but you feel it when you're playing the game. is also slick af, because this game has good movement overall. But it also comes with a unique ability . It might not be as fancy and gaudy as some other games where you have triple dashes, teleports and a rocket in your ass, but it comes up with creative platforming puzzles to be solved. Other interesting thing with this game is that you need to parry-kill your enemies a set number of times to get their special skills. To be fair I would like them to be more animated. Usually they are passives that cater to specific playstyles. They also feel disconnected with the attribute system, which is only good for health,stamina or weapon scaling attributes Strength/Dexterity/Resonance, which are just a requirement to lock weapons away from your use. Don't get me wrong, the weapons are good and the passive skills are useful, but if I were the devs I would take Nioh 2 as a closer example. I think Ender Lilies also does a similar thing where you get the skills of your enemies. I do not mean it should be a projection of the enemy model performing an attack specifically, but it would be nice to get a new move that your character can perform, like ramming move you get from the Stag enemy, or a grapple move from cannibalistic monsters, as well as projectiles which could be tied to the stamina as mana, so if you wanted to make a sorcery build you would pick stamina and resonance for your character, and so on... is my only real complaint. That part is literally a boring cave, a textbook journey into the underworld and the rebirth of the protagonist, which opens into a fun world of the living. You have to be patient and wait for it. The first 15 minutes of the game you are bullying inept tutorial enemies, and the game forces you to use the parry, which is fair because it is absolutely the most essential part of the game, but it holds you in that gray starting cave long enough to be bored. If there is something they've done differently, it is the tutorial, I would rather be thrown into the world and figure out that if I use the parry mechanic things become way easier. I think the tutorial's problem is that it is done too correctly, which becomes handholdy and humbles itself in front of the newcoming player that it veils the sense of exploration that opens up to you later in the game. I firmly believe this game didn't get the attention it deserves solely because its presentation. It is humble, if that's the right word. It is gross in a nice way, and its difficulty is on a very nice curve. It is so professional that it lacks the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ which makes some other things sell very well. But it is such a good game.

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah it's good.I dunno, man. This is one of those games I find it hard to say much interesting about. It has that paralysing quality where every time I try to complain about the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ story, I find myself qualifying with its strengths like the fantastic combat, and every time I try to praise it, I wind up complaining about the never ending backtracking.Grime, as a game, really wants you to put the work in, and the issue with that is that the people who love an unreasonable challenge will love it, and people like me will hack the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ for as long as we can stomach it and then finish our play time with the phrase "♥♥♥♥ it, that'll do." Which isn't exactly high praise. I made it to the final boss at which point I looked down the barrel of the 8 hour grind sesh I would have to do to stand half a chance and decided I would sate my desire to see the end credits scene by watching the opening to star wars after smearing my monitor with animal guts and gravel.The combat is smooth as hell. It reminds me of Salt and Sanctuary in some good ways, with the addition of a well implemented parry to make it even more fresh. That being said, the bone vulture ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ can suck my fat ♥♥♥♥.The environment design is lovely and filled with the kind of body horror and grotesquery that really cheers me up. So that's a big tick for scenery porn, albeit the kind of German scat porn where everything is teeth and disembodied stone guts. Even so, the warp points are waaay the ♥♥♥♥ too far apart and you don't unlock the ability to warp between benches until waaay too late.Boss design is fun, boss health bars are way too long. Movement feels great, double jump is unlocked too late. learning traits by spending hunt points is fun, hunt points are far too limited to really make the most of the mechanic.You see my dilemma? I guess my final word on Grime is that I'll toss it off with one hand and smack it in the face with the other. If you're into that, check it out, if you're into something a little more vanilla, I can't recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: GRIME is a Souls-Like Metroidvania, and maybe one of the most forgiving of its kind. There are consumables that can buff you for any fight, armor that can be mixed and matched to great effect, upgradeable weapons, and unique upgrades that come from taking the time to learn and counter each enemy you face. When you die, you may lose some of your momentum, but you never lose your "souls," the currency that lets you enhance your stats, meaning you continue to grow stronger and stronger no matter what.Honestly, it's an underrated gem with passionate developers. Since release, the developers have been putting out large DLC sized  that continue to build more and more on the game. I only just picked it up, but its so clear where the devs put love and care into building their game. They've crafted a story with themes of destruction and optimism, overcoming enemies and even yourself, and deciding what role you will play in something that should be inevitable. The art direction is fantastic, with distinct enemy designs and area environments that are stunning. From top to bottom, this game is a great time, and one that I'd recommend playing through again right after you finish it the first time. If Metroidvanias are up your alley, with the backtracking and exploration that comes with the genre, then it's a must-play.

_childDocuments_.review: I've only just beaten the first boss, but can already tell this game is worth your time.At the surface, GRIME is just another 2D soulslike (which isn't a bad thing btw), but it's more like a Metroidvania with it's heavy emphasis on exploration, shortcuts and new abilities for both traversal AND combat. The main gimmick of the game revolves around the parry system / perfect-block. If timed correctly, you can block an attack and even absorb the enemy attacking you, unlocking their abilities for yourself to purchase.If you die, you don't seem to lose your XP, but you will have to travel back to where you died. After the first boss, you earn a multiplier that goes away if you get hit, so that's where the "punishment" aspect of the game comes into play.Even though I didn't play very long, I still managed to find a couple pieces of armor and weapons to choose from, so you're definitely rewarded for exploring.I'll update my review whenever I find more time to play through it, but if you enjoyed Blasphemous, Salt and Sanctuary or Hollow Knight, I think you'll dig GRIME.

_childDocuments_.review: Let it be known, this game is not Hollow Knight. This is not a small, concise world, it feels sprawling, lengthy, even if the map isn't as big as one might at first believe, the world feels so much vaster than it actually is. This is a game where foot travel is expected, and encouraged. It's not a bad thing though, to encourage people to walk to where they want to go, especially since it feels like the arduous feeling going back to find secrets has is intentional. I recommend this game to people who enjoy sprawling spaces rather than intricate ones, who want to dig deep in order to figure what's really going on.

_childDocuments_.review: Entire game is fun except Misbegotten Amalgam. Dying despite having hitpoints remaining, the Vase trait resurrecting me into the pit below the ground height on loop, poor visibility on the eye pull cue.Otherwise a relatively fun take on the genre with a decent difficulty curve. Visual design is on point with a wide array of zones that each feel distinct, with a very atmospheric soundtrack that helps really sell the setting.Force regeneration is downright torture for a majority of the game and didn't feel reasonable until investing into Rank 3 of the Force Regeneration speed trait, which really hampers the dodge and parry focus for a majority of the play through.Armour could do with feeling more unique, as they mostly have identical stat amounts, but distributed differently and with a new amplified trait. The ones that don't amplify a trait are notably many times more powerful than the majority, but thankfully cosmetic slots exist.With a bit more combat polish, this could have been up there with Hollow Knight, but its still a solid game in its own right.Edited after NG+: The new boss needs optimisation work but otherwise a great job of making it a similar but different experience.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent metroidvania with a very methodical approach to combat. Gameplay and controls feels great and thats good considering the amount of platforming here is comparable to Hollow Knight or Guacamelee.The combat is about learning attack patterns and managing your force bar, making the boss fights very engaging and some of the best i played in the genre. That said, i found the combat to be a little bit too passive for regular mobs, you have two options: 1. land a few attacks and withdraw until you replenish your force or 2. sit and wait to use your absorb mechanic multiple times. Early, the punishment for playing aggressively is too high, making common encounters a chore.The visuals and music successfully creates a world that matches the tone of the characters and the narrative. Sadly, as a consequence of the cohesive dry tone, some areas blend too much and a lot of the music is forgettable (except boss music that is epic).I can't put Grime at the same tier than HK or Blasphemous in part for the issues metioned above and for some design choices that i found annoying or straight bad: fall damage, undertuned force bar for non-boss encounters, having to equip non-combat consumables to use them, mostly useless combat consumables, having limited resources to respec forcing you to check a guide so you don´t end stuck with a build you don't like.TLDR: this is one is great, just a notch below the bests
