_childDocuments_.review: When developers think 'souls-Like', they often fall into the pit of making their game uncomfortably hard. Grime, however, seems to understand that it's a balance of mechanics and reward. And for a first try, they hit it out of the park. The blend of DS challenge in a Metroidvania game can be a little rough, but they obviously put a lot of effort into making the experience as seamless as possible.Combat is what you would expect in a 2D game of this type. There is no blocking an attack; instead you have a parry/absorb mechanic that you are pretty much required to Master if you plan on proceeding. Triggering it at just the right time can negate the enemies' attack, opening them up for a counterattack. If their health is low enough (shown by a helpful line on their health bar), you instead absorb them for an instant kill. This second half is vital for proceeding: The only way to regain health is with 'breath'. At the start you only carry a single charge, which does about 30% of your health bar on use. Refilling it is done by absorbing enemies.The second benefit of absorbing is the Hunt system. A fair portion of the enemies in the game will give you a new skill when you absorb enough of them. Certain special enemies will give you a point to put into that skill when defeated. These can range from simple attack/health buffs, to small benefits that give you an edge in the fight. Each one of these Traits are tiered, letting you allot more points for a larger benefit. While it's tempting to drop points early on, you can end up locking yourself with them for the whole game. The materials required to respec are easily the most rare items in the game, and using them only resets a single perk tier. Which, for their rarity, feels like an oversight on the developers. For something so rare it should reset all of that perks.Where this game shines brightest is the world of Grime. Another aspect of Dark Souls they manages to replicate wonderfully is the sense of a broken and aged world, where every being you encounter shines just a tiny light on a grand story. Lore hounds will delight in piecing together everything from the snippets attached to items and enemy descriptions.The World itself is massive and loaded with secrets. exploration almost always reaps rewards. And you will stumble across more than a few of these, as there is little more than an icon in a blank map to identify your next story goal. It's easy to get lost and stumble across an entirely optional area (and boss) in your efforts to find the correct route. In classic metroidvania fashion, defeating certain bosses will unlock new abilities, which in turn let you reach previously unexplored regions. A fair portion of these are jumping puzzles, which can range from simple to rage-quit levels of frustrating as you need to perfectly time each jump and dash. Death can be the most frustrating part by far, Checkpoints are a little sparse, and often your last checkpoint is far away and you find yourself having to fight through multiple encounters just to get back where you were. Like Dark Souls, you'll become a paragon of skill simply by the repeated efforts to progress further the next attempt.... Or you earn enough levels to basically one-shot even the most Tanky or enemies.I can't recommend this game enough, for all it's flaws. it's beautiful yet horrifying art style and world will draw you in. But the learning curve and mechanics will swiftly frustrate many.Post-completion Edit: I finished the game only missing two achievements in just under 25 hours. Going back in to knock out the remaining achievements means another hour or two, which gives this game a suitable value for it's cost.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok the game was in my head now for two days after i finished it and now i thought "ok lets write a review".First things first and i already wrote that on so many other reviews i did SADLY theres still no neutral review option on steam so we always have to choose between "positive" and "negative" which is kinda dumb IMO steam review options are soooo behind it needs a big overhaul again IMO... Lets go to the review now!When i say "end of the game" or the term "of the game" i mean the main mission / story missions / campaign obviously just as a side note!Where / how should i start.... lets rip the band-aid at the start... as a "Game" grime was a failure for me... why? because its not a game till u reach like the last 10% of the game which was sad and bad game design like the best example: you get the double jumpe for the last LITERALLY last 5% of the game and for optional areas and the mid air dash after like 50-60% of the game and you know why? ATL (artificial time lenghtner) backtracking A LOT OF BACKTRACKING would the developers decided to give u these two things around 15-25% into the game it wouldve been SO MUCH better!You will find so many hidden caves / connections or lets call it "secrets" where u just cant do anything bcs u dont have those two skills... and thats annoying as ♥♥♥♥ to always find smth or to stand in front of smth u cant reach or interact with. I know thats the game design behind those metroidvania style games but in most of them u have the double jump or mid air dash from the get go (or u learn them very quickly) which makes the gameplay already thousand times better. To get a new ability to reach certain points or interact with smth in the world is nothing new to me iam a 90s kid and i come from games like DMC, GOW, Darksiders etc. in those games its atleast almost always a story relevant thing but damn in grime its just idk again dumb bad game design... or again you just get it to late...Now to the combat its pretty simple and when i say that i mean it! Its basically a Souls-like thats why it got the tag for it i guess! (bonfireish "runestones" thingys and smth like souls are there too) You have a parry / block you have a dodge / dash and you have your normal attacks and a heavy attack AND you have stamina so the whole game is always about attack X times -> dodge or parry -> recover stamina repeat thats it. The combat gets a "bit" more "complex" later but to late as you see theres a pattern the game just needs too long to be a "game" as i already mentioned above! Now the best and worst part of the game... the exploration you ask now why best and worst part? bcs the exploration was fun especially after u are able to reach everything and being able to interact with everything which is possible at and again after u reached the last 5% of the game theres the pattern again to late... the funny thing ist there are smth between 4-7 areas in the game which are completly optional which is totally fine i love exploring but i was only able to fully explore them and yes i know iam repeating myself at the end of the game! The game hast two fast travel options one of them is basically just for the world design IMO and the other is fast traveling between your Runestones (bonfires) which you get ehm yea at the end of the game... And now the inventory / consumables / gear / stats oh man.... literally 90% of the items in the game are lets say "useless" especially bcs of the fact that you find them after who wouldve thought that you reached the end of the game... I literally finished the whole game with the starting weapon and another greatswordish thing i found after an hour or smth the only reason i used the greatsword was for certain enemies but i literally used the starting weapon to fight (which i upgraded to max lvl kinda fast) for 95% of the game you ask now why? bcs as i already mentioned its Souls-like so you have stuff like "Health - Strenght - Dexterity - Force <-(which is basically stamina) Resonance <- (for abilities and the parry) so you are not able to use 90% of the weapons properly bcs u are missing the required stats hell even at the end of the game i had almost every stat above 20 except for dexterity and i was still not able to use 50% of the weapons roster properly...? and no those werent all weapons who need it more dexterity... Now the Armor you have a Chest, Arms and Legs slot when you wear three parts of the same gear you get a set bonus well what can i say most of the full sets iam sry but it is how it is you find to late... me personally i ran around for 60% of the game with the same set sometimes i swapped one part here and there and at the end i found a really good set which gave me % dmg reduction and i basically used that only for one side boss and the last main boss but its not like you need that i just like to be tanky in games i always play tank :D so thats a me thing. Ah the consumables well i used some of them but literally just as a joke just to see how much a difference they make or if it changes anything but yeah kinda useless IMO.Sooo why was the game stucked in my head for two days? bcs the music, art, world design are top notch and the story was really nice! The story is kinda tricky its a lot about interpretation and you have to pay attention theres no voice acting its all told through text and world design!So yeah as i already mentioned at the beginning as a "game" Grime was a failure IMO but as an experience / adventure its nice! Would i try to wrap up the game with some few words i would say: to late, to simple, and wasted potential! _childDocuments_.review: In brief, this is an excellent and inventive metroidvania, and one that (maybe?) touches on aspects of Hebrew mythology, with a little bit of earth science thrown in for nerds. I do love the rock/mineral/earth aesthetic. The combat is satisfying, the world is interesting enough to keep you hooked, and the progression is well-timed - until it isn't.And this brings me to my only real gripe with the game. While the movement and control is fluid for the most part, it can be janky at times. The pacing of the game is very good until the final part, minor spoilers, where you face the greatest enemy of all - the sometimes janky controls and glitchy platforming. There is a part at the end which is entirely platforming, and I actually found this the most boring, frustrating and difficult part of the game. Some was due to my lack of skill, but a lot of the time, I had to repeat entire, long, drawn out, far from save point, sections of the game due to glitches in platforming. This really cheapened an otherwise excellent experience, but frustrated me to the point that by the final, final boss, I was completely tired of the game and decided to watch the endings on youtube. Disappointing, but I knew when I'd had enough, and just wanted to be done with it.Maybe a lesson for Grime 2, if you've got a fight called 'The final performance' and it's ramping up to the end, don't slow players down with a frustratingly difficult and obtuse platforming section to make way for exposition...

_childDocuments_.review: The good and the bad (but mostly bad).The good: -The parry system is pretty cool.  It's kind of like Surge 2 where you're heavily rewarded for parries.-The art style is nice.The bad: Almost everything else.-Almost everything I'm about to list artificially makes the game take longer to complete for zero benefit.  This game is full of decisions where they just thought "how can we pad the game playtime without actually making it more interesting or better?"-First and foremost, they put a stamina bar in a metroidvania.  That's a cardinal sin.  I don't know how that got past the discussion phase much less into alpha release.  Stamina bars only exist to slow down gameplay and have no place in a metroidvania.  It is NEVER interesting to stand still doing nothing waiting to regen stamina.  That's like rule zero of this genre.-The map system is beyond awful.  If you thought Hollow Knight was bad by making you find an NPC 70% of the way through in order to have a map of the area, this is worse.  It's like that but it doesn't even reveal the area, it just lets you BEGIN to map it.  Most of the map nodes are 90% through the areas as well, so by the time you find it it's almost pointless.  Worst mapping sytem in a metroidvania I have ever seen.-The progression for ability gates is awful.  You don't get double jump until the second to last boss and you don't get checkpoint warping at all unless you do a secret boss.  Combined with the above mentioned awful map system, it is hard to impossible to finish this game blind playthrough because there's no indication of what you are missing or where to find it.-The NG+ is the worst type of Nintendo hard I have seen since it was an actual thing in old school Nintendo games.  Remember that parry/deflect system that I said was the only reason to play this over games like Hollow Knight and Ori?  I counted 32 consecutive unparriable attacks from a trash mob in the NG+ run.  They all but delete the parry button because EVERYTHING spams unparriable attacks in NG+.  It sucks any and all joy out of the game real fast.-The level design.  ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, it's like they took a normal game and just stretched every hallway to be 10 times longer than it should be just so you spend more time (slowly) walking back through the map to try and find the progression token you are missing to complete the game.  There's no reason to stretch every platform like this except to waste the players time.But yeah, the art is nice.

_childDocuments_.review: Nah.Grime is mix of Metroidvania and Dark Souls, with a difficulty that keeps climbing, to a level I'm personnally not interested in.If that was the only issue, I could reccommend it to hardcore fans of the genre, but let's be real, the game is also awfully mid. This has the typical riddle storytelling of the more blatant Souls rip-offs, so you never know, it may make sense or get interesting down the line, but with 4 bosses left, for me it isn't.Gameplay is mid, everything is competently executed, but the more elaborate plateforming could have been more fluid.Now the big no no, which you have probably heard of if you looked into the game, is QOL features.The map is blank until you find a beacon in each area, but until then I hope you like running blind. A lot.Then teleportation between areas do exist but are so rare that you will probably have to take painfully long slogs between two important locations, just because it's apparently fun.Grime is mid. It could interest some very specific players, it does what it does relatively well, but at the end of the day it's not enough to make it more than 'oh, it's the super hard Metroidvania with body horror'.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastically creative game! The world and lore is so unique! I've honestly never seen anything like this. I can't even think of another anything that I could liken it to. It's that original. I don't want to spoil anything, but gone is your standard grimdark fantasy world so common in soulslikes. I couldn't wait to visit new areas just to see the next part of this intriguing world.The gameplay is your standard souls-like / metroidvania mix, but the character building is a lot of fun. After absorbing certain enemies enough times, you are able to put upgrade points in the skills they unlock. In this way you can fine tune your character to the play style you most favor. The combat itself is a bit more like Sekiro than Dark Souls though, since there is an emphasis on parrying attacks.I enjoyed the soundtrack and sound effects too. They compliment the game well. Not much more to say here, though I will probably end up buying the soundtrack once I get around to it. I'd like to use it for my D&D games! Especially the ambient tracks.My only legit beef with this game is it has some pretty serious performance problems. I don't know if this is because of Unity, but even at the lowest setting my i7 7700k RTX 2080 computer CONSTANTLY dipped into 20 fps territory. With that said, the game was so good, I just dealt with it. It doesn't seem like everyone is having the same trouble I had, but that's the nature of Unity engine games I suppose. It's not a deal killer, but I can only imagine how much greater this game could have been if I figured out some way to maintain a consistent 60fps. So all and all, even with the performance issues, I still strongly recommend this game.Edit: I'm replaying the game again now that Colors of Rot DLC has released. I have a new computer that's decently more powerful and I haven't come across even a small performance problem. I'm sure my beefier CPU has a lot to do with it. The performance issues was probably because of my aging computer. Also though, the devs have put A LOT more work into their game since my first play though, polishing their masterpiece even further. So on top of my better computer, they worked to smooth out any rough edges the game may have once had, including making it run better. Edit 2: Just finished my final play through including the final DLC. I'm going to miss this world. Great job guys. One day I would love to see a developers commentary from all of you. I really need to know what you were all thinking when you came up with this twisted masterpiece!TL;DR: BUY THIS GAME! IT's A MASTERPIECE! Can't wait for the next one!

_childDocuments_.review: Grime is super good!  The art style is super cool with its weird creature and world designs, the music is great, and the combat is super fun.  There's lots of weapons to find and use, lots of different kinds of enemies, and other stuff to find.  The bosses were all really fun to fight.  I haven't fought/found every one, but all the ones I did and the main ones had fun movesets and actually felt pretty fair.  Once I got the hang of what they were doing, my deaths never felt cheap.  I love this game, and can't wait to replay it again at some point!The game can be pretty tough at times, especially when you're first starting out.  Sometimes the map can feel confusing, and it's not hard to miss checkpoints altogether.  If you're up for a challenge, and have some patience, then you'll have a great time with Grime.  Also, a lot of the combat revolves around parrying, so the game might be a pass if you're not into that, but the parry mechanic is really well implemented, and honestly a ton of fun to use.  You can get through a lot of the game and defeat a lot of enemies by just parrying.  You can kill them with it, and even get health back, so if you get the timing right you'll be doing great!

_childDocuments_.review: Tough to know where to start!  The combat - it's like a greatest hits of modern combat mechanics.  You've got your Souls foundation with dodge/endurance. From there, things go off into the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ stratosphere.  Do you want to tinker with a billion buffs, managing their various cooldowns and conditions to do insane damage per hit with a weapon that has a 5 second heavy attack animation?  You can do that.  Do you want to go a more Nioh route and mess with endurance refreshes from dodges and parries?  That too. How about  using the lantern to dance around enemies, stacking up 30 detonations on them, then hitting heavy attack, and exploding them? Sure. It's best to start the game doing your best to parry parry parry everything.  Put yourself in terrible situations and parry out of them. It'll happen whether you like it or not, really.  But the parry is your key to maximum enjoyment no matter your build. The weapons play a bit like simpler trick weapons from Bloodborne-- all of them are cool, few are redundant, and all can be built around.  Fight/Enemy designs - they can be a bit tanky and some of the fight set ups can really grind on you while you're trying to advance.  But every enemy tests various aspects of combat and keeps you on your toes most of the game.  There were no popcorn guys who just take one hit.  Enemies have all kinds of combinations of traits and tricks to take them down. You'll really feel it when you're running through an area fighting a new set of enemies, then are confronted with some guys you haven't fought in an hour or two.  Time to scramble and remember their timing for parries!Exploration/Platforming - here's where the whole "experience" comes together.  The platforming is some of the toughest in a metroidvania/souls-ish game and you're gonna be dying left and right.  You're gonna be making some really long treks and might end up stranded/lost a lot.  But this game's environment really puts you in a trance so you don't really even think about it. The map is always full of spots to explore and surprise short-cuts and wrap-around spots to keep things moving along.  It's also all just so...cool and unique that it's no problem to go off on your own adventure just to see what pops up. That's a great way to run into mini-bosses, alternate entrances to areas, weird side hidden paths with weapons, and tons of mats to upgrade your weapons.  It's basically always rewarding to explore!  Even at the final boss, there's plenty more I can do, with 25 hours on the in-game timer too.The bad - there's some stuff to complain about, like any game.  Ladders were a bit weird for me throughout - keep in mind a lot of times its easier just to dash off then jump. The difficulty could be pretty crazy at times--I guess this is the part where I go "hey even for me a Souls fan!" but no, it's hard, even for me, the Ninja Gaiden Black and Ninja Gaiden 2 (360) on Master Ninja difficulty fan. So this game is yes actually very really not just some iframe timing not just a single parry but damn the whole damn experience-- it's hard!  That's not for everyone.  I loved it. It's going to make people bounce a lot. But remember - it's still got very thick Souls roots.  That means there are items galore to help you.  Don't be like me and keep health at 5 to the end of the game.I'll just conclude since I'm writing too much - This game is being slept on a little maybe, but I think the final few patches are gonna make it an undeniable classic. Maybe it'll take a game pass release - I hope for the best for this team.  They put together an amazing game and if you check the forums, you can see they polished with tons of feedback and discussion.

_childDocuments_.review: This game made me go "wtf" several times which is pretty good for a metroidvania. This game definitely leans more toward the "vania" side of things with its focus on combat and skill customization. The world is beautifully laid out; despite being themed on various grotesque representations of anatomy it is very believable and has many cool surprises hidden throughout.The main two mechanics of parrying with your head and pulling ledges/enemies works flawlessly and makes for a unique experience. Combat is fluid and bosses have many different ways of dealing with them, allowing for lots of customization and weapon choices.Music is incredible, ranging from moody atmospheric pieces to epic boss themes (and that one theme in that one city, if you know you know). Very captivating, could not put down once I started.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best metroidvanias ever made that deserves Hollow Knight levels of praise and recognition. I don't know how it was on release, but the current "Definitive Edition" is amazing. From what I read they added A LOT of content for a bargain price of NOTHING.Artstyle is stunning and very original, I often stopped to marvel at the environments or was bewildered by the character designs. After 30 years of gaming its not often I see any visual design that is truly original, but GRIME somehow managed to surprise me at every turn. The artstyle alone makes GRIME worth a playthrough.Gameplay wise its smooth and very well designed. Core mechanic of absorbing enemy attacks is a lot of fun and quickly becomes an a reflex. There are many other abilities you'll unlock, mostly they are staples of metroidvania genres, but there are some standouts that I won't spoil here. GRIME isn't as hand-holdy as some metroidvanias and I was lost at times, but never in an annoying way. Even when I felt directionless it was a joy to just explore the stunning world of GRIME. There are many secrets to find, several tricky platforming sections and some well hidden optional bosses that will put your combat skills to the test. Similiar to Hollow Knight, GRIME has its own Path of Pain in the form of Abandoned Opus - an endgame platforming challenge that absolutely requires you obtain and master all movement abilities. I wouldn't say its as hard as Path of Pain, but it was a nice challenge.GRIME is a must play for anyone even remotely insterested in metroidvanias. I place it way above Ori series and on the same level as Hollow Knight. Its so strange that GRIME has nowhere near as much recognition as Hollow Knight or Ori, but it seems developers had enough success to warrant a sequel (trailer looks awesome). GRIME 2 in 2025? Get hyped!

_childDocuments_.review: I'd had GRIME on my wishlist for about a year, and I'm really glad I finally decided to dig in! GRIME is everything I was hoping it would be.The world is fascinating to explore. It oozes aesthetic and ambience...seriously! There are *very* few games that succeed at constructing such a palpable atmosphere, and that have such powerful soundtracks to go alongside them. The endgame areas were just astonishingly beautiful.Area variety and interconnectedness are pretty good, with several paths to explore at any given time and some well-placed shortcuts that loop areas back on themselves (the closest match I can think of is Firelink Shrine in Dark Souls 1). The main thing I would offer as constructive criticism is that save points were sometimes a bit too far apart for my liking (note: I'm playing after the CoR DLC, which I heard increased the frequency of some checkpoints). For the most part things were okay, but there were a few instances where checkpoints (or shortcuts) required frustratingly long gauntlets. Minor nitpick about the world design: to the best of my knowledge, while there are a few optional bosses and/or areas, the sequence of bosses required to beat the game is fixed. Although you can take different routes through the interconnected world to get between the mandatory bosses, you ultimately don't seem to have a choice about the order in which you fight them. This isn't a big deal, but is something that I would expect an MV of this calibre to have.Combat feels solid and satisfying. The absorb (parry) is fun to use, and takes on a whole new meaning when paired with the trait that causes stamina recovery (I think that trait should be mandatory to unlock by default!). Timing is also pretty forgiving on the parry, and bosses/enemies telegraph their parryable attacks super well in my opinion. The pull mechanic feels unique and was designed into the bosses in a very satisfying manner (love yanking them to the ground when they're in mid-air!). The boss quality is exceptionally high, with great movesets, soundtracks, and arena settings. There are a few tricky ones, but they are possible to master. Enemies are well-designed too, rarely feeling unfair to fight.Movement feels fluid and the abilities are satisfying to use. There's some decently-intense platforming in later parts of the game, but nothing that took me more than a couple of tries. Platforming is fun to execute and the challenges are well-matched to the mechanics.All in all, a very solid MV experience. Would recommend to any enjoyer of the genre who is not afraid of some real boss fights, and who can tolerate a few instances where checkpoints are far apart.

_childDocuments_.review: Grime is a Souls inspired Metroidvania that takes the wrong lessons from Souls. Combat is slow and ponderous, but also hard to read with unintuitive hitboxes and weirdly paced animations. The story is pretty original, but has a strong "find and replace" problem when it comes to terms cribbed from Dark Souls. Platforming feels clunky and imprecise. Overall this is a game where the two things you do the most (platforming and combat) feel unpolished and unsatisfying. This ruins the other elements, like exploration and lore hunting, which are otherwise decent enough.

_childDocuments_.review: With just under 40 hours logged on this game, I have completed everything all the way through the most recent January 2024 major patch update. Grime, to me, falls somewhere between a souls-like and a metroidvania, but doesn't entirely latch onto either categorization completely.TLDR, if you like souls-like or metroidvania type games, it's decently probable you'll find yourself enjoying Grime if you give it a shot.This game is challenging but in a rewarding way that makes you get that good rush of adrenaline when you're in the throes of a major boss fight, and that surge of relief and exhilaration when you finally beat those bosses. The overall mechanics and feel of the game are likely to be a little clunkier or slower than your average game in the same genre, but I think that adds to the aesthetic and concept of the game's narrative. Movement and combat mechanics take a little getting used to, but it is in no means a negative aspect of the game.The character building is great, from leveling in certain stats to focusing on certain traits to power up, all the way to what weapons and armors you choose to use in certain situations.Enemy designs are absolutely fantastic. I found myself enjoying every new encounter (especially bosses) extremely thoroughly, and often thought to myself the boss fights in this game are some of the most fun ones I've faced in quite awhile (and if you play through a NG+ file, you get to relearn regular enemy and boss behaviors alike).If you're someone who enjoys the lore aspects in games like Dark Souls, Elden Ring, Hollow Knight, or Blasphemous, you'll love the story narrative and little tidbits of info you pick up throughout the game. The storytelling leads you in a pretty clear direction, but only feeds you snippets of pertinent information at a time, allowing you to focus on the main story progression or to go out and explore different areas of the map and see what you can discover.All said and done, I think Grime is an exceptional game with a lot of ingenuity and creativity poured into it. The devs clearly stuck with it as they have put our 4 major updates since the game's release, adding new content and fixing or revamping old content. Games of this variety tend to take inspiration from other predecessors, but I didn't feel like it preyed heavily on any game in particular and did a great job standing out as its own unique take on the genre. Grime gets a big recommend from me.

_childDocuments_.review: So I was really excited when I began playing this game and for quite a ways in too. This game is very bizarre and unique visually, the lore is also weird. All good stuff.The game felt lacking in a bit of polish here and there but nothing major. And it felt like it was trying to learn the RIGHT lessons from Dark Souls - to make the game difficult but not annoy you. Make it fun to keep pushing against a challenge. It was doing this with lots of well placed checkpoints and shortcuts, well designed telegraphs and nothing that felt like a ridiculous hitbox. Furthermore the platforming that felt deceptively simple at first, became more complex the more abilities were handed to me, helping the game stand out. It had side paths with tricky enemies that rewarded me with neat finds like weapons or cosmetics. It was just doing super well.And then I got to an area called the Palace and it was like the game gave up being itself and started going down a Dark Souls checklist. Enemies shooting me with projectiles (which you can't parry unlike earlier ones in the game) from areas I can't reach while having to fight multiple enemies. Cheap shot traps, short cuts being slow elevators that I have to wait around on after every death, contrasting horribly with the well placed checkpoints and breakable one way tunnels from earlier in the game.What's worse is this games healing system - a gradual heal charged by a bar you fill up by parrying enemies, is not at all suitable to a Dark Souls boiler plate area - not that you ever get to use it in the palace area because all the enemies have stone health bars meaning you can only repel, not absorb (which in the game's terms means you can't fill your healbar off them).The platforming went from fun zippy stuff to irritating platform pulling, with platforms that go back to the beginning of a rail if you stray too far, forcing you to backtrack and start over.The game also has some of the more limited and slow recovering stamina among souls likes. Which the game felt built around until this area's boss.The boss of the area is a flailing mess. Since this is a 2D game, you can't always dodge via repositioning, this boss is designed to make SURE you can't. For one of it's phases you need to hold onto 3 dodges worth of stamina to deal with one of its long winded combos. Not to mention the boss has awful frame drops during one or two of it's attacks, making it frustrating to time dodges during those attacks. Some of the limited stamina issues can be dealt with using certain abilities (like recharge on repel) if you have them, but only when the boss is performing attacks that allow you to, and the boss more or less stops doing any relevant attacks after the first phase - even though its the second where you need all that dodging stamina. The whole area and its boss just seems to clash with the games systems, it doesn't feel made for it.I wanted to push through and see if the rest of the game stopped going down a boiler plate Dark Souls checklist unsuited to it and went back to doing its own thing but I'm just not having fun anymore and chose to stop. I'd at least recommend waiting until this game gets more polish to address the awful frame drops and the stamina balance issues.

_childDocuments_.review: When I started I liked it, but the further on it went the less interested I became. It’s not a bad game, there’s some interesting mythology and bosses. The world and sound are both great, It’s one of the few souls likes to get the ‘tough but fair’ ratio right. Where it falls down is the weapons/armour/upgrades. Armour seems to have no defensive value, it’s just cosmetic. And it seemed no matter how many points I invested in my character his stats only marginally improved. Especially damage, I might have been using the wrong weapon (got confused by the stats) for my build, but at level sixty I was expecting to do a lot more damage. It’s a game I will come back and finish but for now, I’ve had enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Worldbuilding and aesthetics are the ONLY two things this game did right. Combat is stale at best, weapons are extremely similar and boring, the parry system is nice but it is not worth using for anything other than healing, it does not stun the enemy and only deals some damage if you put a lot of resources into a specific trinket/perk. A lot of enemies are specifically designed to be ANNOYING, not challenging, but strictly ANNOYING. Map design is HORRIBLE. All locations are basically corridors with 15 branching paths that lead to dead ends and useless loot. Maps are not "Intertwined" or connected, like in HK or Dark Souls, most of the shortcuts you unlock are literally useless and do not serve any purpose. The placement of beacons that allow you to view the map is absolutely DERANGED. I had to wander through the first four locations without any sense of direction because you literally have to walk through an entire location to find a beacon that becomes essentially useless since you already walked the same path 10 times and memorized everything on your own. Fast travel is locked to specific locations that you have to unlock. Why can't we just teleport between previously unlocked checkpoints? Probably because the developers wanted this game to be as tedious and annoying as possible. And believe me, they succeeded in it. The name of this game perfectly encapsulates all its features - this game is gross, dirty and filthy.

_childDocuments_.review: Great metroidvania which isn't as punishing as one might think. You respawn with full healing and leave a bloodstain behind like in a soulslike but you don't lose any currency on death, only a multiplier on currency gain, which you can easily ignore.Very memorable artstyle with surprisingly good production values. Nice mix of cosmic horror, body horror, artisanship and existential crisis. It has a good amount of content with some replay value in replayable boss battles and multiple NG+ modes. It has a LOT of secrets, which may cause you to miss quite a few pieces of gear and items but there is nothing you can permanently miss and there is a trait that helps slightly.There is lots and lots of platforming, optional and necessary, and almost all of it is great, with some singular points that can be frustrating.The game also has a lot of backtracking, which can be really frustrating at points. The game provides shortcuts but the games bonfires can be a bit sparse and fast travel points are seperate from bonfires. Two optional but rather difficult bosses drop convenient mobility abilities, with the   rewarding you with the ability to warp between bonfires. If you plan on 100% the game I HIGHLY recommend using map markers at all times and trying to get to the end quickly, since all abilities are insanely useful and mostly necessary. After beating the game you start NG+ manually, so no problems there. And there are some great maps out there for completionists. In case you want a direct link:  . These were not created by me and obviously contain spoilers. Very accurate though.Definitely recommended, I had a good bit of fun with the game.

_childDocuments_.review: GRIME is a game graced by an absolutely inspired and captivating artistic vision. The world feels inspired by Giger and Beksinski, but it absolutely commits to its "rock" theme in a way that reminded me of Land of the Lustrous. Overall, it's absolutely enthralling aesthetically, and this is by far the game's biggest strength. Some vistas are breathtaking, and I'm almost tempted to say that it's worth it to get to the very end for the game for the visuals of that particular scene alone. It's a game with serious personality and charm. It is also accompanied by a solid OST, a bit on the moodier and ambient side for exploration, but epic and quite memorable for boss fights.Regarding the gameplay, GRIME is fantastic in some areas, while a bit lacking in others (overall, though, I'd say it's great). It is also going through an improvement process, so keep that in mind. The combat wants to recapture the soulslike formula and it does so on a 2D plane successfully enough, as far as I'm concerned. The feel of the combat is satisfying, especially thanks to the focus on the parry and how it incorporates a certain ability from the mid game onwards. Boss fights are especially satisfying and demanding. Platforming is also generally good, and the later advanced challenges that require chaining together the movement abilities were cool.I'll insist on the cons of the game a bit more in this section, because I want this review to also serve as feedback for the ongoing work of the devs. They don't outweight the positive at all, at least for me. Exploration has room for improvement. Areas are interesting and there are a lot of secrets to find, but often rewards aren't particularly exciting. Nothing is useless, per se, but some consumables that the game treated as "rare rewards" were not worthy of such secrecy for me. It might just be my personal preference. Other rewards, like the cosmetic armors, I really enjoyed. Map navigability is another issue. The game uses a beacon system that reveals the map for a certain area only when you find the corresponding beacon; the problem is that sometimes these beacons are pretty far into the area and you'll have to stumble a lot before you find them. Personally, I found it only really problematic in Feaster's Lair, because the area is maze-y and the beacon is after the boss, but your mileage may vary. Also, some areas (especially a certain late game one) have a number of annoying "mini points of no-return", in the sense that sometimes you go somewhere and you're not able to go back the same way, so you have to take a really long and annoying detour to get to where you were before. It can be rectified with a consumable that takes you to your last save point, but I feel that it would just be better to have a reasonable way to get back to a certain point if one goes the "wrong way" while exploring. The fast travel system, as far as I'm concerned is perfectly serviceable now, with reasonably placed Nervepasses and elevators. You can go everywhere pretty much hassle-free. The other important negative is a general lack of polish, as there are a lot of (mostly minor) glitches related to graphics, animations and collisions. The devs are actively working to patch the game though, so consider that. I'll update my review to rectify this when things are more ironed out.Overall, even if it seems like it needed a bit more time in the oven, GRIME is a solid, unique metroidvania/soulslike that's absolutely worth trying. I'd recommend to buy this now anyway to show support to the devs if you like the genre, just keep an eye on the ongoing patching process.

_childDocuments_.review: True to the words of the developer, this is an indie masterpiece indeed made with love! A definite treat for old school Metroidvania/souls like players or simply those who seek a fair test of skills, RPG tactics and most importantly patience. The bosses are as challenging as they appear and the platforming can really test your reflexes and patience.Once through the many choke points of difficulty lies a a satisfying journey to master!Cons would be a few minor bugs and few imbalances in platforming sections that may complicate things, but easily forgiven with a bit of patience and muscle memory.

_childDocuments_.review: Souls-like Metroidvania with very clunky controls and movement. Pretty unique artstyle but looks better in stills than in motion. There is a bit of Iitem-Lore and some End of the World dystopia going on, though things are mostly spoken out by NPCs. The game enforces heavily a "be good at parry or you are not gonna have fun" gameplay, which isnt the most enjoyable playstyle for everyone. Bosses and normal mobs are all about dodging unblockable and parrying normal attacks. Enemy attacks vary between well telegraphed with nonsensical mid motion halts/delays and instant attacks where you have to see the first few frames to prepare the parry. Especially later bosses are mostly unblockable and non-marked unblockable attack flurries.There is currently only a very resource limited way to test out new weapons, since they are stats-bound (said stats can be reseted via a rare item) Same goes for passive abilities, which can be slotted via "Hunting Points", which also are semi permanently slotted once attributed. Making weapon and playstyle-testing resource limited  is a fun-blocker imo, though as already mentioned, the only working playstyle is "Dodge and Parry". Movement and map navigation in this game are somewhat of a nightmare. Most of the time you are underground, relying on an area map that even if unlocked, only shows area parts you have visited. Teleportation points are far to few and tedious walking (especially for bosses) are the norm. I swear, most of my 26 hours were spent trying to navigate back to bosses in 4-5 minute walks.All in all I cannot recommend this game yet, since there are far and wide better metroidvanias/soulslike on the market that are more fun. Try to find a good lets play of this game an see if this satisfies your curiosity.Update: Finally beat the last boss and the last super boring platform passage, kthxbye uninstalled. Will have a look again once they did their seemingly last patch. Jesus, what a frustrating and unsatisfying game.

It is possible to beat, but the hours of trying is better spent elsewhere.So go in with the expectation that you will get frustrated at times and you can have a mostly good time.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a Metroidvania I enjoyed playing.In summary you are a parry god that descended on this world and now you have to parry your way back up.I have to say did not understand the story due to small brain, I'll have to watch a video summarizing it and explaining all the symbolism. The music is great but I believe it's not showcased enough.While this game has a stat build and weapon upgrade system, I did not bother using them. I upgraded my stats obviously, but only used and upgraded the first weapon. The hunt point system is unique, but there aren't nearly enough hunt points to be gained, making most upgrades irrelevant. Where this game truly shines is the boss fights. Definitely among the best I've seen in a Metroidvania, if not the best. They make maximum use of the movement mechanics and are unique and exhilarating. By the look of the level design, it is clear that the devs wanted to focus on movement-mechanic skill based puzzles. There are entire areas devoid of normal enemies and the game says goodbye to you with a final jumping puzzle after the final boss fight (named "the peak of creation" no less, if that is not symbolism I don't know what is). Really if the game was just jumping puzzles with more bosses (both of those things rely on movement-mechanic skill rather on the RPG elements), no mobs and less exploration, I would have possibly been content with this game. Although it is hard to tell if it would have been a better game this way.

_childDocuments_.review: Update 2: Despite numerous complaints about the tedium of exploration, backtracking, fast travel, and checkpoints in general, they seem intent on doubling down on it. They've announced NG+ will let you keep everything EXCEPT the movement upgrades (air dash, double jump, etc.) which means . They apparently intend for the game to just pointlessly consume hours of you doing nothing, for no reason. Empty rooms, shallow rewards, poor checkpoint placement, etc. are a real issue and doubling down on how long it takes to get through those is just more bad design. I have played metroidvanias with no fast travel and they are faster to backtrack and navigate than GRIME, it's that bad at this.I will add, as I mentioned this elsewhere - if you don't play very many games, and don't mind games that just add tedium for the sake of making themselves longer, you could still enjoy this game. I like challenge, I do not like tedium, and this game is 75% tedium and 25% challenge so unless they revisit their bad designs it will never be fun for me.Update: I've (clearly) played more of it since the review, but unfortunately everything I found wrong in the first 3 hours just carries into the next 3 but often times worse. The amount of auto-scrolling (or waiting for timed cycles) navigating you should have to do between tricky platforming or combat sections and a checkpoint is 0, but I've counted 3 distinct instances so far. There are other issues that weren't around earlier as well - one of the major "challenges" in a number of rooms are ranged enemies attacking you from offscreen, sometimes with attacks you can parry but not always, and I can't recall any game where enemies attacking you offscreen was considered a good thing. Speaking of offscreen, there are a number of rooms where in a normal metroidvania with, y'know, checkpoints, they wouldn't be a big design concern, or if you were in a 3D souls game where you could actually SEE what was going on. But in this game, you get the worst of both worlds, where you can get into a platforming section for a stashed away item that isn't worth it and costs you a death because the way to get back out is not only not obvious, but nearly pixel-perfect. And once you go in that's the only (visible) way out (maybe I couldn't find another way?). Once again, a good chunk of my next 3 hours were spent backtracking either through empty corridors or just boring corridors to get back to where I died, either through a boss fight I didn't see coming (because some boss fights pending are obvious, others are completely not), or an ambush you literally fall into, or just glitchy pathing (I've gotten stuck in a number of walls, corners, had enemies just warp across the screen, etc.)A lot of this stuff can be fixed with patches but aside from bugs (which I would expect in nearly any game to pop up eventually, especially when I'm sometimes pushing it), all of these are poor game design elements that were literally solved in some cases decades ago. It feels like the game would be so much better if they'd had fans of either major genre here actually play the game in testing at some point, who weren't involved in QA or designing it. Or maybe they did and just didn't listen to them, since all the complaints are echoed even across many of the positive reviews.It's really a shame, it speaks to the quality of the world and the gameplay that I tried to push through what is really just poorly designed backbone systems, but at this point I really can't anymore. The platforming is becoming more and more tedious and you often have to go through multiple rooms of that at sometimes slow speeds to retry anything. I'll keep an eye on the patches but I don't honestly expect them to fix this. If this game was their vision than the fixes go too much against that and I don't see it happening for them to just add a bunch of checkpoints that would be necessary for the game to both flow well and not waste your time. I just finished Hellpoint before playing this and that game has some issues as well but it (nor any souls game I've played) comes close to the gaps in checkpoints or the time spent retreading the same spaces slowly over and over again.Original review:I still have a way to go, and I will probably keep trying, but this game really is ruined by some bad design choices. It is fun, but doesn't want you to enjoy it. ANY game that has dedicated fast travel "rooms" instead of using checkpoints (either in addition to or instead of) is just doing it wrong, end of story. There's even really obviously a ton of menu space in the checkpoints that would enable this. They have added some fast travel points but after almost 3 hours I have found exactly 2, and they are so scattered that it makes no sense to even backtrack at this point (or probably ever) just because of the time involved to explore around, compounded with being a metroidvania meaning you may not even be able to access everywhere.Secondly, the checkpoints themselves - they are pretty far apart even for a souls game, but for a metroidvania they are criminally far apart. If you die most of your time will be spent backtracking through empty areas because the checkpoints are far and in many places there are not shortcuts to unlock. One boss battle is preceded by an unskippable 30-60 second walk every time you die, for no reason.Dying in this game is actually not punishing, by souls standards, but it costs you an immense amount of time in backtracking even if you skip every enemy. That alone would be a problem but it's also still a 2D platformer with insta-death falls and traps all of the place, a misstep into which can cost you minutes each time which adds up. It shows I have 2.7 hours and I would be willing to bet that .7 is just from me walking back to where I died, and I have only died like 6 or 7 times.It has an extremely soulslike level system - you put "mass" into whatever you want of the 5 stats, and it increases cost each time. And just like souls, you have no concept of what you might enjoy using down the road. Normally in a metroidvania, you are always excited to spent upgrade points etc. when you get them, but here you feel like just barely spending what you need to get by because you have no idea if you'll have wasted dozens of levels and hours of XP down the road (they have said they are working on a way to respec but the existing system for "perks" I guess cost resources which are rare so I'm not optimistic). It basically tries to shove a souls-like game into a traditional metroidvania vessel but without considering the balance of systems or what that might mean. If you like souls games a LOT you might be able to get over the shortcomings that are introduced here by, if you like metroidvanias I would honestly skip it as it's a TERRIBLE metroidvania. It's a souls game with bad design but an interesting world and fairly fun combat.If they add fast travel to all checkpoints, and double (or more) the amount of them, and add a friendly respec system, I could really see it being a lot more fun to engage with, but as it stands now I just don't know why you would get this over a different game of either genre. It tries to merge the two without actually trying to merge the two, and they just conflict with each other in a number of ways. It's a shame because there's a lot to like here but the game doesn't want to let you.

_childDocuments_.review: Grime is a very unforgiving game. It has a "get it right or die" kind of attitude, and this will leave you dying to enemies on most initial encounters. This very much goes for the bosses, who in my experience, can kill you near instantly if you don't know their moves. The speed at which you burn through your stamina bar (or 'Force' as the game calls it), along with it's slow recovery adds to the difficulty, and will often leave you seeking space as opposed to fighting the boss itself. However, having said that, their AI is easily manipulable to give you a MOSTLY consistent fight once you've learnt said moves. I say MOSTLY, because even the slightest mess up is capable of ending you instantly. This direction the game has can be very satisfying when you manage to pull it off, but until then will leave you pulling your hair out in frustration.The game has its fair share of bugs that the devs are currently working to clear up. There are plenty of small bugs, including attack hitboxes sometimes being significantly larger than they appear. The most notable glitch I had was my left joystick seemingly stopped working and I couldn't move until I relaunched the game. Some of the abilities you get can also be a bit dodgy, semi-regularly not activating and often resulting in your death.Having said all that, playing Grime was a great experience and a metroidvania I'm glad to have in my collection. If you're concerned about the bugs, give the devs some time to iron them out and come back to it later, they have been working hard and putting out regular patches. The difficulty can be dissuasive to some people, but if you're willing to push through it, the game is very satisfying to beat.

_childDocuments_.review: Very well made metroidvania with souls-like games elements, probably closest thing to Silksong we have right know. It ticks every boxes of this genre - interconected world, collecting power ups, revisitng previous areas for serching of missing items, combat, difficult bosses. I spend 50 hours doing 100% achievements, and it was only 2 playtrough, so if you looking for longer game with a lot of content this is definitely for youStory - you are little black hole traveling through dying space giant. And you have ability to S U C C. Overall i found premise of Grime very similar to Hollow Knight and Dark Souls. You are a being on a quest to end world/era of a place that doesnt want to move on and accept change. And probably you are not a good guy. Rock... Thing. Anyway, as per usual, this is not a Planescape Torment level of storytelling, you dont need understand plot or even pay attention to enjoy game. Everything is vogue and foggy, some worldbuilding is hidden in item description, Npc talks in weird way, you know the drill. Mechanics: combat is build around three major things: ability to parry/absorb enemies; managing stamina and proper timing. Especialy stamina is a big thing - even with high number putting in stat and having full developed traits i still struggle to perform many attacks. And jumping or dodging also consume it. So dont charge, dont go berserk, be patient, you cannot brute force this game. Many enemies also have this nasty habit of having delayed attacks. Monster can swing at you, and you think they finish animation but suddenly BANG! Fallow up attack hits you right in face. Or hole. Developing character is a mix of dark souls, metroidvania and some unique mechanics. First you have your standard metroidvania stuff - you explore world, looking for upgrades like air dash, double jump, pull object etc. But you also have levels, stats and point distribution. Nothing extraodrinary here - rise health for more hit points, rise force for more stamina... Weapons have scalling stats, so slow and heavy hitting hammer is tied to strengh, double knives to dextrenity, Resonance fo you S U C C mechanics. On top of that game also have traits, with are gained by absorbing enemies using parry. This can add some new abilities, like damaging enemies during dash, or better healing. Speaking of healing, you have only max three heals, with are refiled by using parry. As you can see, gameplay is build around it and if you are unsure about you skills, dont worry, hitboxes and parry windows are pretty generous, even dodging scrub like you can handle it.The real king of this game is exploration. Every area have alternate path, hidden rooms, collectibles, armor to pick up or weapons to find. Some level have even three entrance points. Everything is labirynthian and i feel same joy of being lost I felt when I played Hollow Knight. Grime even have Path of pain look a like area, so if you like to suffer you have found right place.Grime can be hard. Some bosses like misbigotten amalgam or Dreamborn Terror took me atleast 40 tries to beat, Add to this lack of healing, checkpoints usually two per area, looking for windows of oportunity in combat or exploration puzzles - there is a lot of jumping or dashing gauntlest - and there is a big oportunity for loosing temper and rage. I recomend grinding some exp for time and putting a lot to Force stats, it will be easier to managae pain.After beating game once go for NG+. Unlike in other games, Grime is not going simplest of path by adding just some numbers to enemies stats. No, here you have full new experience. Common enemies have diffrent attacks now, bosses have aditional stages, there is one aviable only in NG+, you keep all your movement abilities so you can brake sequence, there is new resources to collect, new weapons, armors, extra upgrades are a thing. Yeah, devs did a excelent job with this mode.Critique. Yeah, there is some. First - camera. It could go lower when i try look what is below my character. I was constantly forced to jump almost blindly because I didnt know what is below, many times i lost hitpoints thanks to that. Some areas are to dark. I understand that devs wants keep us alerted during exploration, but is not fun when i cant see enemies attacks. Few times my characters - after failed jump - spawn under spikes or on verge instakilling vines. Once i was stun locked to death because of that. I also dont like when in boss fight you have this littlle jumping section. Mainly talking about Dreamborn terror. Imagine doing a perfect no damage two phases of boss fight just to die to jumping section. Not fun. And it happens several times. So yeah. Thats all folks. Hope we have Grime 2 soon.

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard the write a purely objective review as everyone's definition of objectivity is different. I will tell you right off the bat that GRIME's story and world building is inspired and unique. Most of the bosses and mini-bosses are well designed and exciting to fight. However, everything else falls short in my opinion. There's a reason why souls-like is the second genre tag after metroidvania. It borrows extremely heavily from the souls series. If this is your cup of tea, you might really enjoy it. But I've noticed that, more often than not, these two genres are very hard to combine properly. GRIME is one such attempt and unfortunately I think it has missed the mark in all the places that really matter. Let me explain why.The environments are unnecessarily maze-like and quite bland. Although such areas are often found in the souls-series, they are never without purpose and are always fun to explore. On the flip side, metroidvanias  have bland, pointless areas as exploring them is part of the appeal of this genre. The trademark inaccessible areas aren't well telegraphed in GRIME - they are more like the hidden walls from Dark Souls, which results in you either missing them completely or forgetting about them entirely in the future. At the end of the day, 80% of each level is just a maze serving as "filler" of sorts while you frantically search for the next bonfi- I mean .Unfortunately, GRIME's combat is generic and repetitive - it lacks the variety that most other metroidvanias have. There aren't any cool powers, abilities or weapon varieties on display - weapons simply have a light attack, heavy attack and a special attack (read: weapon art). Keep in mind that I have not completed the game and therefore I am yet to see all of the abilities you can unlock. However, I can assure you the game was quite boring during the first 7 hours that I played, which I firmly believe can not be justified.There's not much more I can say. Everything else is fine - the music, the UI, the bits of story and worldbuilding I experienced. Level design and combat though are key attributes of souls-likes and metroidvanias. If they are flawed, you have missed the mark. As such, I do not really recommend GRIME.
_childDocuments_.name: GRIME

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved the demo and bought this game on release, It's sadly a purchase I regret.Game starts off really well, has some incredibly weird atmosphere and good music. The world building is nicely done and you don't get an overly long intro or any hand holding tutorials.Combat is simplistic but it does the job, you parry enemies to regain potential healing charges which is a system that becomes obsolete a bit later as the game goes into " Sorry, no fun allowed " territory.I love the "Hunt" system in this game, where you unlock some passive/talents with points gathered from killing a set number of enemies or mini bosses.The 2nd half of the game slowly started to wear me down mentally, Most secrets I found were some needlessly precise and slightly janky platforming (One instance being a platform I had to guide through a maze, only to find out I couldn't stand on it until i quit and reloaded my game) and the rewards were never worth it, causing me to quickly become annoyed with the concept of exploring.Checkpoints are far in between and fast travel is basically pointless, or obtained at a point where it's borderline irrelevant.  If i wanted to upgrade my weapon near the end of the game, I would have to navigate all the way back to the main hub, and then back. This is not fun or exciting.Bosses get glitchier, with dodgier hitboxes and enemy placement becomes an exercise in frustration.  Similar games in the genre have comparable enemy placements but aren't as punishing about it or give you faster movement options to at least get back to where you died. Not being able to use items from your inventory but being required to assign them to your dpad is also something i'm not a fan of (For example for the gaining of XP based items) I did NOT finish this game, I made it to the last  stretch before deciding I am just flat out not having any fun since the middle point of the game. There's incredible amounts of potential here, but it just completely misses the mark for me where the amount of frustration quickly overtakes the initial excitement I had when launching this game. I have no desire to go back and finish it and I cannot fully recommend it at this state, I do look forward to whatever the development team comes up with next.I give this a "Definitely a videogame"  out of 10Edit :I finished the game, I highly respect the devs for continuing to adres and respond to the flaws in the way they do. The last update has fixed some of the issues I have with it but not all. I do have a tendency to break games and this wasn't an exception but there was nothing game breaking, I have probably missed my calling as a Q A tester. At this point certainly, I would say that it's a game that is worth at least giving a try if the art style is pleasing to you, especially as problems get resolved.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really fun. Though combat can be quite hard, because the game incentivises repelling/absorbing enemies' attacks. You could gain new abilities, recover stamina/health with successful repel/absorb. However, that would also put you at higher risk of dying if you fail repelling/absorbing, which happen quite often until you memorise their attack patterns and timing.Also, the game sort of shifted into platforming later in the game (that requires many trials-and-errors) especially after you get double-jump ability. But platforming sections are relatively short comparing to the rest of the game. Even though you are not good at platforming (which I also am not), they could be completed in less than an hour.I wish it would have more late-game contents though. By the time you acquired all abilities that are super useful for exploration, it's almost the end of the game. And you probably have already explored like ~95% at that point.I need to warn about achievements if you plan to 100% the game. There are some missable achievements if you progress too far into the game. Some enemies won't spawn late-game, and there is an ability that you need to gain from defeating an optional enemy in order to complete achievements. Since this game auto-saves, you would have to re-play the whole game if you missed them. To not spoil too much, I would recommend to explore as much as you could before continue pass Beyond the Barrier.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I have been curious about Grime since launch, and I am glad I bought it.While not transcendent, Grime is a competent and enjoyable metroidvania with some soulslike elements and a difficulty level that I found "just right".  It's also anything but grimy; the aesthetic is more otherworldly, with lots of polished metal, living rock, and molded clay.  This seems to be a dedicated developer worth supporting, and the publisher has had a very good track record lately.  The effort put into the game really shows, and it is currently getting frequent updates, tweaks, and patches to further polish the experience.I did have trouble following Grime's story, as it leaves a lot open to interpretation and little is explicitly stated, but the general gist is that you are a silent "Perfect" being in a world full of imperfections.  Your overall goal is to reach the world's peak, but you have interactions along the way that make you question your character's purpose and motives.  The story gets the job done, but I would have preferred a clearer, more cohesive narrative.Grime's combat is brutal and punishing, but fun.  Combat is smooth and quick but hefty, with really satisfying sound design that can only be described as "bouldery".  While there are a variety of unique weapons that all have different timings and patterns to learn, the real ticket to success is mastering perfect dodges, which can deal minor damage and restore stamina with the right perks, and perfect counters, which deal massive damage.  Properly timed counters also allow you to absorb bits of enemies, or sometimes the entire enemy itself.  This is your primary method of learning new abilities - absorbing bosses gives you additional skills that make exploration easier, while absorbing regular enemies unlocks new passive perks such as faster stamina regen or increased backstab damage.There's a lot of pure platforming in Grime, as well (and a LOT of very punishing fall damage). For the most part, the control is smooth and responsive, although I definitely had some minor issues.  In particular, there seems to be an issue where you jump several feet up a ladder when you intend to leap off sideways, and I also found the "sweet spot" for dodge-dashing through small wall gaps to be a tad small.  In fact, other than bosses, no enemies at all appear in Grime's final four areas.  There's a fair bit of backtracking, as well, due to a combination of factors.  First, the map for each area is hidden until you find a specific crystal within the area, so it is fairly easy to get lost if you are not paying attention.  Second, checkpoints are pretty few and far between, so death will set you back a ways.  Third, there are very few fast-travel points; though a very late-game upgrade mitigates this a little bit by allowing you to warp between checkpoints as well.All in all, I enjoyed my time with Grime.  It's worth checking out.

_childDocuments_.review: When dealing with the world setting of "creation" and "the essence of being", there's a certain amount of color that comes to mind. GRIME, in strict adherence to its name, decides to take a more opposite approach, instead interpreting nebulaic colouration as a sort of muddy greenish purple, and spreading this interpretation through generally every corner of its fairly samey looking world. Though I can't say that the true breadth of design potential for "rock people" is likely that large, I'm somewhat disappointed that I found myself bored by the designs in a game with literally limitless options. The story fares a little bit better, with a mostly interesting premise, but it's something of an Atlas situation in that the weight of the main plotpoint holds down the entire experience with a now-tropified "cycle" understanding of the lore that has mostly prevented long-lasting development, outside of a single character, from persisting. Combat-wise, GRIME is middling, with a decent grip on enjoyable movement but strange, clunky animations and occasionally poor hitboxes. Questionable pathing can route the player through DLC bosses far above the skill level required at the time, and the fairly stingy upgrade materials makes the surprising amount of weapon options mostly an early-game faux pas. World pathing and backtracking isn't so bad if you're paying attention, though the lack of a true fast travel (as most metroids decide to go with) makes for uncomfortable layaways in the middle of who-knows-where since you could really use an upgrade, but it's a mile and a half back to the sole blacksmith. The Absorb mechanic is interesting and parries are... at least fun (though the overall sound design of the game may be its worst quality), but armor requiring the full set for any benefits kills true mix and match build development in lieu of wearing whatever gives a buff. Despite all these complaints, I still found GRIME at least pleasant, with some parkour sections utilizing the snappy (and mildly imprecise) blink to be the best moments. In the big picture, GRIME's half-decent, even if there's a little mud on the lens.

_childDocuments_.review: Game continually crashes about once an hour. 5950x, 3090, 32 GB of RAM. Despite this, powered through and completed the game. Game relies on a mechanic similar to Dark Souls parrying for making significant progress in boss battles. While this sounds like a cool feature, that's the only mechanic to make any significant progress on bosses, otherwise imagine fighting DS3 Yhorm levels of health on most bosses with a single Estus flask, a dagger, and being able to parry halfway through that health bar. At one point, a critical boss can ONLY be parried to complete, which can be super frustrating for those without. Hitboxes for boss and enemy attacks are also WAY larger than the model's attack, and can result in many frustrating deaths as well. Game's map is also a hugely missed opportunity, with the layout being a hodge-podge of separate zones that, in the grand scheme of the plot, don't make sense. Had some consideration been put into the map design, there's a fairly obvious scheme that would have made a much better fit, and really helped sell the story at the end (without spoiling). The plot had potentially to be interesting, but much of the plot in the platform gauntlet section sort of throws things off the rails.Platforming is serviceable, although the camera doesn't condone to getting a good view of some sections in the platforming gauntlet section, leading to a fairly healthy amount of padding the length of the game, as you are going to die many, many times before trial and error rote memorization of the layout of the section. While for a challenge location akin to Hollow Knight's White Castle, this would be fine, but this is a required section in the game that needs to be completed to progress.I like challenging games that can be engaging, with certain areas really ramping up, but this was trudging through genuine grime. It's a shame, as the game does have a lot of potential and a lot of love put into it. I don't get the hype though.

_childDocuments_.review: No pros vs. cons here. Just some general info. Wether this info seems like a pro or a con is for anyone to decide.First off, it appears that at release the game had some major flaws and QoL mishaps.However a lot of those seem to have been taken care off making the experience more then acceptable.- Potential flaws I encountered.   - The game may forget to load the UI for no reason ( rest at a surrogate and it get's restored )   - You may lose your hitbox making you invuln. ( I mean, is that really that bad :3 ) °° this might also be intended near end game, not sure...You are a black hole that for some reason finds itself at the bottom of the world. Make your way to the top of the world by any means available. Luckily as a black hole you kinda "suck".... how convenient !It looks like a metroid vania, it plays like one, it must be one :)This also means : - Sneaky hidden rooms ( and some of them are very well hidden ) - Missable items - Backtracking - You name it°° Important note °°Even though the bait tags reffer to this as soul-like... it isn't, it's not even souls-liTe...Sure it has a dodge and a parry and it has all the basics in place. These are universal concepts though, Fromsoft didn't invent them nor owns them.The main reason i won't put it in that category is "SPEED" and "GAMEFLOW".This game is rather SLOW paced. It forces you to read the telegrpahed move and act accordingly with one of a couple of available mechanics. Parrying being the main mechanic. Experience may vary, but I stood still for a lot of things just waiting to propperly react to the next big thing.Yes ! You can brute force your way trough it not using the mechanics given or performing the correct action on the telegrpahed prompt. Allthough I wouldn't recommend it. They really REALLY want you to react to ongoing situations contrary to mindless attacking.°° I know, this all still sound very souls-like... untill you are in it and you'll come to the conclusion it kinda isn't. Just don't overexpect the wrong things, It doesn't need to be a Souls to be good after all !!- The mechanics themselves: - Press a button to attack, press another button to heavy attack ( or charge an attack if available ). Attacking mid air gives a jump attack. - Dodge to evade all damage if need be - A pull move to be used on specific situations based on telegraphing - A backstep ( hardly ever used it ) - A parry / deflect.I want to say that this last one is your main move. When timed correctly it WILL negate all damage ( excluding non blockable moves ofc ) and stagger the enemy.Along side some more unique features.More on this wonderfull parry system. As a black hole you obv suck all gravity and matter towards you. Or in other words, you "absorb" the enemy itself once a treshold on their hp bar is breached.This absorption opens the game to a plethora of playstyles. Whever you absorb an enemy enough times you "inheret" an ability. This ability ( mostly passives ) come in a wide variety ranging from extra damage to better survivability, whatever suits you best.Furthermore certain enemies are concidered mini bosses, they come with a specific set of unique moves that require a more sophisticated approach. when defeating these you earn a "hunt point".Thse hunt points will allow you to adapt the unique abilities ( traits ) to your character°° Respecs are in place if need beAll of this ofc is mainly a reward for thorough exploration and can be missed !!Put alongside that a decent amount of weapons with different playstyles to themselves and combine it with a specific trait build and you can get stuff done............ YES .............Yet never ever unfair ( excluding jumping bits... that's just annoying at times for no good reason :p )I get why some say it's "hard". Early on ( and for most of the game ) you pretty much get 2 shot accros the board. ( Assuming you missdodge, misspary etc ofc )On top of that the healing is tricky. Healing is tied into your absorb ( or later on specific traits that will allow some other means ). This howeve means you need to take a risk to get the reward of a heal.No risk taking might avoid damage, but when damage is taken you WILL HAVE NO HEAL, "sucks" to be you !If however you take the risk to deflect or absorb what would be instant death, you will end up with a heal you might need later on.The risk-reward is heavy in this game and it certainly starts out as such. Expect your first 5 ish hours to be " I have no heals, I don't want to die ! Scared to take the parry, i'm so far away from my checkpoint ! AAAgh ! "Rest assured, if you make it passed that point where the game gives options.... you'll be doing better, you just need to get there first and this might be offputting early on.AND YES IT HAS FAST TRAVEL... it is however also locked away behind that first 4-5 hour mark !!!You should, it's a small team project that clearly shows their love and care for it. The game ( excluding some minor misshaps ) plays smoothly and is never unfair ( even though sometimes it might feel like it ).If unsure, get it on a sale and I don't think you can go wrong with this.Just don't overexpect it as a souls-like... that sadly won't do!

_childDocuments_.review: It's very similar to Hollow Knight but with some changed mechanics like:- you don't lose currency on death if you don't retrieve the body, only the Ardor - you can change items and use one-time items- you can level up stuffA very enjoyable experience. At first it felt really clunky to play (also similar to Hollow Knight until Greenpath <3) and I very often struggled thinking I'm not working against the enemies and puzzles here but against the controls and the game. It made me put the game off for a while and I started googling "when does Grime get good?". I decided to power through it and once you get a certain upgrade from a certain boss (it is the first enemy that you get a quest to kill and is marked on map, I'd suggest doing it asap to start having fun) the game becomes so much more smooth and entertaining.Overall a very cool, beautiful game with a lot of creativity put into it.
