_childDocuments_.review: Excellent metroidvania, one of the better entries in the genre! The progression feels nice, the world is chok full of secrets, the setting is fun, and the boss fights are both incredibly difficult and incredibly satisfying to defeat. Grime has been described as a souls-like - I think that's going a tad far, as this game is not nearly as punishing when you die, but the difficulty is there.There is well over 20 hours of content in this game, so you will get a reasonable value as well. There is some replayability with alternate weapons, but I suspect most will do a single playthrough. Great game overall, highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since I played Blasphemous, I have developed at least a small appreciation for Souls-likes and was interested enough to try this game out. It is challenging, as you would expect from a game like this, but I still had fun getting through it. There were a few bosses and platforming sections that I thought were not very well-designed, but I'm sure people who are more familiar with this game style are more accepting of those types of things.If there is one thing I would complain about, it's the game's loot. On one hand, I appreciate the fact that the game has a large amount of loot to collect, with the intention of allowing the player to experiment and find a set of equipment that they like. However, I really think the main essence of this game simply boils down to, "hit the enemy without getting hit". Because of that, I felt very little motivation to actually try much of the game's loot and ended up using some early-game weapons and armor for the entirety of the playthrough. However, if you are willing to take the time to experiment with other items, you might enjoy more of the game's items than I did.Overall, not a bad game if you like Souls-likes, with a bonus if you are also a fan of Metroidvanias.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing and gorgeous, can't imagine a more fitting style for a story like this. Everything has a ''raw'' feeling to it. Combat is fun, however once you get used to the parry mechanic the game becomes a little easy, there were exactly 3 bosses that took me more than 1 or 2 tries, those were amazing. Rest of the bosses wasn't much of a challenge, but I don't think they were going for an extremely difficult game anyway - seeing as a lot, if not all, bosses had checkpoints right before them.From the visual, sound and combat side I have no complains really, just fun through and through. Platforming was mostly just a pain in the ass, the fact that platforming puzzles aren't synced sometimes results in you standing and waiting for the right time and that sometimes takes 10-20 seconds of you doing nothing. Sometimes your character tries to grab onto moving platforms and just falls through.  I wish  would be an earlier unlock (I know the levels would have to be adjusted but platforming games just generally feel better if you have more movement options to me).There is not a lot of fast travel points  and the rewards never felt inspiring enough for me to try and find everything and go back to all of the previously inaccessible areas I found (this comes from the game's difficulty as well, a lot of loot are consumables, which most of the time I just didn't need, some of them I never used once. If it's not consumables it's weapon upgrade material, by the end of the game I had enough to fully upgrade 3 or 4 weapons, maybe more - I only used 2 of them that I liked the most) The set bonuses were a cool idea though! I'd recommend the game, it's not too difficult. It's pretty and soundtrack is amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best Metroidvania games I ever played. Something you really should give a try!The story and lore is much more observative, so if you pay attention and try to understand the world you will definitely be pulled in. There is barely any fat on the overall flow of the gameplay, only very rarely small things might happen, like getting stuck on geometry, mid-air automatic ledge-grabbing or exploiting the enemy AI. At the same time these things are something you have to provoke a little bit.The atmosphere and the music is super unique, the characters leave room for interpretation which in this game is a great. The boss fights are ridiculously fun and challenging, rememberable and all have their own special attacks. Enemy placement and choice is sometimes really something you have to chew through, but areas with such encounters are almost always tied to something of worth. The backtracking doesn't feel too tedious because you can navigate fairly quickly through everything, which makes repeatedly dying not as bad as in other games.A very great game I will always recommend to a metroidvania fan.

_childDocuments_.review: In the vast sea of ignorant metroidvanias and soulslikes there is a shining black beacon of violet excellence. One worthy to join the pantheon of passionately well crafted 2D action exploration games such as Hollow Knight, Blasphemous and Ender Lilies.From the very start you are birthed into this dying world of rock and root you are forced to survive on your most primeval talent, the most core thing that identify you as a black hole that pulls rubble together to form a humanoid vessel. The ability to consume, or "Absorb" as they call it. And every enemy is noted as Prey for a reason.The Absorb is a parry by other name but with a layer of mechanics to it. Once you've consumed enough prey of the same kin as tracked you will inherit the potential of a new passive power you can spend blood ichors to make your build with. It's up to you how to build your character and while respects are limited there's enough to try a few different abilities as your combination to play the game with.Each area is not like the other. Before you enter the golden halls of the Carven you most endure the more savage nature of life of the ferocious wilds. The Weeping Cavern is filled with eyes in the walls and water dripping from the stalagmites. A place of lamentation where people of rock succumb to the Old Pain. For they are made of stone and not flesh, like no living being should be and thus live in agony in mere existence.The Feaster's Lair, a place where the most ravenous beasts lie is filled with teeth and bile. If the teeth don't break you the gastric acid will wear you down.In the Unformed Desert, formed by Hands and bones, the Broken Sky makes its appearance where stone falls from the sky. The world has story of untold quakes ago. It is a worn, beaten world. And your birth into it was not a thing of chance. As you explore the world of Grime you will learn about old contempt, envy and adoration of what you are.The developers spared no expenses in making creative weapons. Although you start by finding an axe that on its special attack extends itself for a heavier downward swing. You soon find a sword that will break small shards off itself when hitting something, be it enemies or a lying rock. A sword that's a large broken rock slab that can reform itself to its whole shape for a larger weapon swing.Even with the game's main flaw being how long it takes for the fast travel to be unlocked (the Nervepass is subpar. To travel between surrogates you need to find a boss roughly 60-70%'ish through the game on a normal run) the game is still a treat of an experience. Travelling back to previous areas when you've unlocked new mobility options often rewards you with something, sometimes even completely new areas worth of minibosses and weapons.At this point, in the afterglow of a 20hour playthrough experience. I look back fondly at the game I conquered. Knowing there is still content to come to the game in at least one more large update. My faith and goodwill in the developers leaves me both wanting and excited to see what else they will add to this already well completed game.It's not every day we get to play a game so complete in both presentation and content in modern gaming development. In an era of seasonpasses, battlepasses and unfinished promises of half a decade long 'Early Access' titles. Like a marble statue from ancient Rome this game too will survive the passage of time and whether you bought this in 2021 or in 2031 it will be one of those games that will leave you with an impression. Of an interesting but cruel world, giving you just enough story to understand what cog in the grand scheme of fates you are yet leaving you wanting more of this brutal, unrefined realm's tales to be told.GRIME gets nothing short but my highest recommendation. Whether it is your first or 10th Metroidvania game this one is worth adding to the collection. And I hope, with all my heart that after reading this love letter to this game and its developers that you too will find it in you to give this game an honest chance to encapsulate you too.The game can be brutal, the bosses can feel unfair. But is that not a reflection of the world itself? And the most brutal, the most unfair of them all in this reckless realm, is you."You know what it is you're doing. You've been doing it since you first came into this world."

_childDocuments_.review: Spectacular art design and a wonderful ambiguity in the narrative elements can't really make up for a very disappointing combat system.  There's a thing going on in indie games where everyone wants to keep iterating on the souls formula, but there's simply no reason to keep iterating Soulslikes just like there's not much reason to iterate on FPS design.  It's been pretty perfected.  Grime wants to use the Mortal Shell parry to heal mechanic but, unlike Mortal Shell, you don't....heal on parry.  You get a resource when a parry kills an enemy.  So killing 3 or 4 enemies with the parry gives you one heal.  The second ever game in the genre basically perfected the healing system in these games.  There's no real reason to push it anywhere else and if you're going to mess with a core staple of the design it better feel revalatory and spotless.  That's not the case with grime.  IT feels frustrating.  There's no real reason (beyond an interesting narrative idea) to make healing require a parry.  Especially when enemies are sometimes sparse and many have chunky health bars, very poor telegraphs and unparryable attacks they can spam.Want to know the best 2D souls like?  Salt and Sanctuary.  Know why?  Because it didn't think it needed to reinvent the wheel.  It kept what works.Beyond that movement is sluggish and slow.  There's no sprint.  Jumping and traversal is average at best.Finally the Metroidvania elements aren't particularly well done.  Not terribly done, but not great.  Underwhelming would be the best way to describe them.SO you're left with a game that's not a top tier Metroidvania (this isn't Hollow Knight or Ori or Bloodstained) combined with a not very enjoyable 2D soulslike (this isn't Salt and Sanctuary or Vigil) with stunning art, music and narrative elements.  But when the best core of your game is it's visuals and music and exploration you want to make the game not frustrating. Frustrating combat design only works when those systems are spotless and tight.  Hollow Knight is frustrating but it's an absolute joy to play because it feels so good and it's platforming and combat is just rock solid.  Salt and Sanctuary is frustrating but combat just feels great there. Ori can be frustrating but it's platforming is smooth as silk.  You're not getting that here.I wish there was a choice between yes and no in these reviews because the quality of the art, music and atmosphere is so wonderful that it is perhaps worth playing for that, but people who play Metroidvania's and Soulslikes come for super tight gameplay first and foremost and on those fronts Grime simply ins't good enough.The developers deserve praise for a totally unique world but it just doesn't feel good to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Brutal combat, haunting world design, existential and occasionally funny dialogue... GRIME is just an all-around fascinating if occasionally frustrating take on metroidvanias, a genre both beloved and bemoaned for its ball-busting boss fights and backtracking. GRIME certainly checked both of those boxes when it launched in August last year, and now it gets a free DLC, Colors of Rot, which adds new weapons, abilities, and music for you to love... and new enemies, bosses, and environmental hazards for you to loathe. But before diving headfirst into my spoiler-free thoughts on the new content, let’s presume you—like I, until last week—have either never played GRIME or could at least benefit from a brief refresher.  As protagonists go, GRIME follows in the soulsy-footsteps of former metroidvanias in giving you control of a mute brute who seems perfectly content to destroy slash absorb everything in sight with nary a second or maybe even first thought. This genre dynamic is not lost on the strange, cryptic, and quirky denizens of Grimeland (and, no, that’s not the world’s real name), as they will either worship or despise you for your destructive ambitions and literally chiseled bod.  In my opinion, GRIME’s plot is a little too one-dimensional to call a strength, though that’s not to say it’s an uninteresting journey, as the game’s well-constructed and unsettling world is drenched in tragic, fascinating lore. GRIME’s characters, meanwhile, inject much-needed life into this strange and unforgiving realm, but there are only a handful of them and they’re rarely on-screen. When they are, they deliver interesting text-based dialogue that flirts with the philosophical, but, again, there’s not much of it to go around. What there is much of, is combat...  GRIME’s stamina-based combat is as intricate and infuriating as genre fans would expect. You’re given well-over a dozen melee weapons, some of them living, and they vary considerably in terms of range and attack speed. GRIME boy (again, not the real name) rounds out this violent armament with a number of ranged items and buffs, though your most useful attack isn’t an attack at all but rather an enemy absorbing parry that grants you Breath—the resource used to heal—as well as Mass—the game's currency. Finally, the more you hurt without getting hurt, the more Ardor you’ll gain, which grants you more Mass on kills, but who are we kidding? This game never stops hurting you. Which must make me a masochist, because I thoroughly enjoyed GRIME’s intense combat, even if it felt like some fights were moreso against the stingy stamina bar than anything else. The game’s non-combat platforming sections, meanwhile, are a nice change of pace, though that’s not to say they’re simple—far from it, as these sequences will demand increasingly more from you as you steadily accrue more movement-based abilities. How? By killing bosses, of course! GRIME has some of the best and hardest boss fights I have ever seen in a 2D game—their designs are intriguing, their multi-stage movesets are daunting, and mastering each is a deeply rewarding experience. Such a shame, then, that GRIME’s clunky, unhelpful UI and dubious playability often spoil the fun: inconsistent hit boxes, tedious world traversal design decisions, an absurdly punishing respec penalty that discourages experimentation, and the occasional game-breaking bug were all things I would’ve expected to see cleaned up in the Colors of Rot release. That said, the DLC’s ominous new area, “Childbed,” is seamlessly integrated into the main game’s story and world, and it adds several new hours of value to an already reasonably priced title, not to mention gives players the ability to fight old bosses after beating the game. In other words, faults considered, there’s never been a better time to GRIME.  Finally, a few words on style. While some textures lack detail and some animations are painfully jumpy, I still enjoyed GRIME’s surreal visual presentation—the environments are memorable, the color palette is fresh, the lighting is occasionally stellar, and I’ve just never seen anything quite like it. That's not quite the case for the game’s music, however—while very well done and by no means a weakness, I’m just personally getting tired of frantic choirs in hard games, feels a bit cliched at this point. Luckily, GRIME’s sound design does more to create a sense of individual identity, as the game is dripping in an alien sonic ambience.  After averaging up our micrometrics, GRIME and its new DLC get an aggregate MEGA score of 3.43/5 (full scores, from “Plot” to “Sound,” available in the video) and are well-worth your time. Thanks so much for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: This is 100% a Metroidvania, its one large interconnected map with gated progression requiring movement and other upgrades, with tons of backtracking and looping back and hidden optional content. I highly recommend this game, the bosses are the best in a Metroidvania since Hollow Knight so far.Okay so here goes the main review after finishing the game. Light Spoilers ahead.This is a metroidvania. You gain upgrades to movement which then allows you to further progress or backtrack and explore the open map. Abilities are guarded by bosses or elite enemies.The combat in this game is more comparable to bloodborne than dark souls. Your dodge is very fast and so are most attacks. Enemies are designed and animated very well, their attacks all seem fair. There are a large number of weapons: although they still fall into distinct classes, most have a special move that is unique. The game also makes use of a VERY forgiving parry called absorb, you are required to use it at some parts for progression, but it does not take frame perfect reaction, it has a very generous amount of time. Absorbing is also how you heal, it is a play off of hollow knights heal system, where you need to damage enemies to heal, but instead of just striking them, you have to absorb their attack to gain the energy needed to perform a heal.The bosses are few in number but very well designed, all seem fair and challenging. There is also a number of sub bosses, as well as unique elite enemies, giving plenty of variety, however in the age of Hollow Knight, the actual amount of main bosses seems pitifully small, and is my one main complaint.Exploration is rewarded very well, I never found something I didn't want like the bones from blasphemous or something, and the environments are all fun AND breezy to backtrack through.Overall I give this game a 8/10 and HIGHLY recommend this game to any fan of the metroidvania genre. This will go down as one of the GREATS.

Has an interesting and slightly creepy world/atmosphere, above average combat, good boss design, interconnected world (staple of metroidvania genre game), non-linear progression, lots of secrets (mainly items though, and armour sets which are cosmetic so kinda lame), and same sound as dark souls when you reach a new area so its basically 2d dark souls tbh.

_childDocuments_.review: A nice and climatic platformer/rpg/soulslike game. You'll often die and in a frustrating way, but you'll want another round each time. The setting is pleasantly mysterious, the combat is difficult and fun (maybe a bit too repetitive) and graphics are nice enough not to interfere with the gameplay (although not extraordinary in any way in my opinion). A fun game whether you have 15 minutes or an hour to play
_childDocuments_.name: GRIME

_childDocuments_.review: Good metrioidvania, great tone, art, and story, but not so good of a souls-like.+ Good, if not great story+ Great tone+ Stunning world design and character design+ Great platforming, quite a bit of variety= Combat exists- Weapons do 2 things, and almost no weapon variety, should have not bothered with multiple weapons- Stats were a mistake, you can't respec so you're pretty much forced into 1 build or risk soft-locking (frustration is a way to soft lock)- Doesn't utilize metroidvania backtracking enough- The map is waaaaay too sprawling with not enough in it. It feels probably 4 times as wide as it is tall, with huge chunks of the map being completely empty, with incredibly few metroidvania backtracking opportunities, if you can even remember where they are (spoiler, you can't)* There is no respec right now, so skill points are permanent. Personally I think an NPC with limited respecs should be good for this* Removing perks requires a resource that appears to be limited in supply, which can be a problem when you have some perks that are required for specific sections, or if you need to switch from farming to dps or tank builds* Pretty much all the strength weapons are too slow to actually be useful in a twitchy platformer, and also not even particularly strong when you compare their dps to dex weaponsAt one point I soft-locked myself by using strength weapons. I thought it would be fun, because in Dark Souls I love running around with a huge sword and one-hitting everything I see. It really feels like the developers on this team , because in this game, it made everything . So much harder, in fact, that I couldn't beat a particular boss after almost 50 attempts. I couldn't dodge enough to avoid attacks, and the healing options were too limited to sustain me through the fight (and this is with almost every skill point in Health). Again, this is a build that I have done in Darks Souls countless times, and it's basically "you get to play as a truck" mode.My character being unable to dash enough in the fight, combined with strength weapons taking so long to attack that against this particular boss means that you basically get 1 attack every 10 seconds, and always trade because the punish window is too small.I decided to restart the game because there was no respec, and I literally couldn't progress. Got back to where I was on a dex build in about 2.5 hours, and it originally took me almost 8 hours on a strength build.The funniest thing was, I was doing  with dex weapons, which attacks about 5 times faster. I started  enemies that would take me 3-4 seconds each with the best strength weapon in the game.Ended up beating the game with dex weapon that has an ability that increases its damage, and straight-up beat the game in less time than it took me to get about halfway through on a strength build.Pretty much nothing but dex is good right now, and without being able to respec you can't even try the other weapons out. I had probably 20 weapons at the end of the game, and could have bought probably another 10, and I only used 3 at all during the game. 1 was decent, and carried me until I got a straight-up upgrade to my main weapon, and the other weapon was a token weapon that allows you to break the floors in specific sections. So, really 1 weapon the whole game.However, none of the weapons I found looked any good, because they had pretty bad stats compared to one of 2-3 weapons with an A in scaling. That, and since I only put points into dex I couldn't try the weapon out anyway.If I wanted to try out a weapon, I would have to  just to be able to try it out, on top of the fact that the . As a result, expect to pick 1 weapon, and maybe an upgrade to the weapon when you unlock it, and don't ever expect to be able to use a different one. You're pretty much locked in.Weapon variety and lack of respec completely kills the spirit of experimentation in this game, to the point where , or to , because with the exception of hitting the floor with a few weapons, weapons in this game  and are .I honestly cannot fathom how you could fumble weapons this hard; there were so many ways from a design standpoint to completely avoid this problem, many of which could easily pair very well with a metroidvania. Instead of avoiding the problem through design altogether, this game doesn't even mitigate the problems. It just leaves in a broken, pointless weapon system that it stole from Dark Souls without a second thought. It's poorly thought out stuff like this that really makes "inspired by [Dark Souls]" a derogatory term these days.The things in this game that feel most like Dark Souls from a mechanical standpoint, the stats and weapon system, are easily the worst part of this game, and in my opinion was a mistake to waste time on implementation if it's not going to be designed well. You could have stopped at design time when your design team came back with "there's 50 weapons but only 2 are good, and all upgrades do is make them stronger, no actual effects other than damage".Would have just been better to slowly upgrade 1 weapon like metroid than effectively make me use 1 boring weapon for 8+ hours with .Ultimately, I think this game is going to mostly go under the radar when it could have been a hit because it tried to mimic Dark Souls and while it clearly has its own identity, it doesn't shine because it's too focused on copying another game that has mechanics that are for a completely different type of game with completely different mechanical needs, and it doesn't gel very well.I think I'll remember this game in the years to come for its story and world design, but probably never come back, because mechanically I will remember it as "another game that tried to clone dark souls wrong", when it could have actually broken ground.The more I write this review, the more I look back and think "this particular problem that stems from the cloned Dark Souls mechanics could have been fixed with X from a metroidvania and would have been better for it".

_childDocuments_.review: Grime is an exceptional Metroidvania-style title. The game's strongest attributes include its intricately designed world, immersive atmosphere, and extensive exploration opportunities. Players can uncover a multitude of secrets scattered throughout the game. Moreover, the boss battles are both intriguing and diverse, offering a unique challenge.However, the game is not without its drawbacks, primarily technical issues. Initially, I suspected these problems were unique to my PC setup, specifically with my RTX 3070. However, after experiencing similar issues on the PS5 version, it appears these are inherent flaws within the game. Notably, there is occasional stuttering, occurring even when the frame rate is well above 90 FPS. Additionally, the game's fast travel system becomes available only in the later stages, leading to considerable backtracking, which might detract from the overall gaming experience.
_childDocuments_.name: GRIME

_childDocuments_.review: GRIME is an incredibly beautiful work of art. Every aspect of its presentation is downright inspired, from the world, to the character design, to the architecture, to the sound. Every single time I entered a new area, I found myself thinking, "Wow. This is the peak, they can't possibly top this." And every time, I'm proven wrong by the sheer level of artistry and passion and beauty and creativity that seeps into every inch of this game.The lone exception to this would be the gameplay - it's a bit of a cosmic gumbo of metroidvania and souls-like, with an emphasis on a parrying mechanic that's intensely satisfying to land. Aside from that, though, what you're getting is exactly what you'd expect from that description. At its worst, it's only decent, and at its best, GRIME's gameplay holds up with the rest of its absolutely inspired aesthetic. 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: GRIME

_childDocuments_.review: I guess they really stuck with the theme because playing the game feels like walking through waist deep mud.It feels like ♥♥♥♥ to play. Every animation takes 5h to complete (including the dash which is criminal imo) and attacking and dashing takes stamina so theres pretty much no way to be aggressive, the stat improvements, abilities and armour barely make a difference, they feel insignificant. It's a shame because the art direction worldbuilding and story seem really interesting.if you're looking for a challenging parry oriented metroidvania with controls that actually feel responsive then check out "nine sols"
_childDocuments_.name: GRIME

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great Souls-Like metroidvania with a heavy emphasis on countering attacks. The environments are varied enough to keep things interesting. The boss battles are really exciting and you really have to learn the attacks to get through the fight. What initially starts out as an impossible struggle will be a well choreographed dance by the time you overcome the challenge. The platforming sections can be extremely difficult when trying to navigate the world to progress, but well planned character leveling and weapon/skill upgrades will see you through to victory!Definitely give this game a playthrough!

_childDocuments_.review: Constant and often patches and updates and devs interaction with the fanbase is comendable and refreshing to see. You can clearly see a lot of love went and is still going into this project. This only adds more value to a game that on it's own is a very good indie "soulslike" with excelent gameplay, world and atmosphere.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent souls-like Metroidvania game shining in every aspect possible.The artstyle is grotesque and unique, especially the combination of inanimate stone and humanly, fleshy shapes. The art direction also left me in awe, each region with its own otherwordly special theme that goes beyond classic tropes like "lava level" or "ice biom". At times the environment feels claustrophobic and oppressive, at other times vast and majestic, just as they need and intend to be. Each new area feels wondrous and menacing, as , fitting a setting where the world is brimming with predators and danger. The music and sound design are also top notch. The lore is well written, yet cryptic and in huge parts hidden in item descriptions. It neatly weaves together enemy-, area-, and world design with its game mechanics, story progress and secrets.The gameplay is tight, enemies and bosses are in classic souls-like fashion: unforgiving but fair with clearly telegraphed attacks and openings. I fell in love with the game's heavy focus on parrying, as this is my favorite playstyle in other souls-likes as well (but I can see how other people won't like that aspect, but if you do, this game is perfect for it).The developers deeply care for community feedback. They quickly reply to bug reports after a new update is out and even changed or improved game mechanics (no missable achievements, better telegraphing for unparryable attacks and interruptable movements). Not to mention, they added two FREE huge DLCs and a third is to come while they also started developing the second entry of GRIME.There are only two minor critic points: The game did not get me to change my starter weapon permanently (but I experimented with other weapons, which sometimes lead to completely new playstyles) and the timing for unlocking fast travel was set a bit late.Overall, the game experience was easily a 9/10, which I currently can only say for five games out of my >170 played games on steam.Addendum:For the people who are unsure how they feel about the parry mechanic or the difficulty in general: Please play the demo before you buy the game and leave a negative review. You also would not buy a pepperoni for dinner when you can't stand spicy food and then start complaining your mouth burns, would you.

_childDocuments_.review: Setting, gameplay and design is great. Stamina bar and constant bugs are annoying as hell. In its current state there are waaay too many glitches to justify buying at full price. I have just spent the last 10 mins trying to complete a puzzle that uses a moving platform, not knowing that the game has only made the moving platform appear to exist, I just fell through it.There has also been more than 5 occasions where I fall too far and get teleported back to where I was just standing, only for my character to just repeatedly fall, teleport, fall, teleport, until he fell and died.When deflecting spikes my character has repeatedly done a David Bowie and just shot off into space, then fell back down to earth and died to whatever random crap was there as I couldn't see it.There are lots of other glitches I've encountered that caused smaller problems as well.I know the game is a new release but it is frustrating as hell every time I have to redo a section because the game wasn't ironed out properly instead of learning from my own mistakes.As I said, great game. Please fix the bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing Hollow Knight I thought I wouldn’t dive into another souls-like metroidvania again because I was mad at myself about skills. However, the art style of GRIME caught my eye as it is both amazing and bizarre in a way, and reminded me of claymation games like The Neverhood and Don't Open the Doors!. Eventually, I installed it and had a good time playing  and stopped right before I started getting mad at myself again.What I enjoyed most is the rhythm of fighting, although you don’t necessarily have to eliminate enemies. Much of the time player is asked to travel long distances, so the best strategy is to avoid encounters by landing in precise spots - since the teleport portals are somewhat limited, this game does feel like a parkour game. Leveling up isn’t too difficult, I mostly add points in health, which unfortunately made some new weapons unusable. The death penalty isn’t too harsh, and the respawn point is not far from the area bosses.That said, the game isn’t without bugs. Once when I mashed the space key at a corner, it glitched me out of the map and eventually dropped me into a lower floor with an open space. As I wandered around, I encountered an incredibly giant and powerful enemy, clearly a boss, and lasted less than half a minute against it. It was actually fun to see it because I wouldn’t have had the chance in my regular gameplay.I recommend this game to anyone who enjoyed Hollow Knight and is up for a challenge. If you’re more interested in other elements, I’d suggest waiting for a discount.
_childDocuments_.name: GRIME

_childDocuments_.review: About 4 hours of play and I'm loving this game so far. Metroidvania with Dark Souls elements, though it's a bit more on the Bloodborne side with countering mechanics. Healing is like Hollow Knight but to get your charge up you have to counter/absorb enemies, so it's a bit more difficult.There's still lots to see and learn but the controls are tight, the look of the game is really cool and I'm looking forward to see what it throws at me next.
_childDocuments_.name: GRIME

_childDocuments_.review: This is so far my favorite metroidvania and one of my favorite 2d games . But before gushing about it , here are some complaints . -The map is legit terrible . Granted you have an ability that helps you indicate secret walls , but the lack of indication would make a completionist ( that i am not ) cry . It's not all bad since you do leave a trail even after death , so it isn't often i willget lost . -Vulture in ng+ sucks , it is my only bad boss experience of the game . -In the middle of ng+ , you get so much stat that most of the middle to endgame boss become pretty trivial . Which brings to the point of the upgrade system being pretty primitive . Like once you upgrade your stats for a specific weapon , there is no reason to not boost your force and hp . So kinda wish there was an incenstive to not do so . Now the negatives out of the way , man this game rocks . Aside from that one ng+ boss , the other bosses and mini bosses have been a blast , and i have never seen a game that is that consistent about this side of game design . I also love the platforming of this game . Very little of it is based on cycle which thank you , because prince of persia lost crown could learn a thing or two about it . So most of the time you are doing the platforming instead of waiting the platforms to play for you . So yeah game rocks , highly highly recommend if you love 2d parry focus games like nine sols or lost crown . I promise you'll have a blast .

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Great art, fun combat, unique story, a little buggy at times.Q: Is it fun?A: Yes. Combat, movement, and mechanics are very satisfying.Q: Is there replayability?A: Kinda. Level design is designed to be branching paths (metroidvania) and some things can be missed. Also, different weapons and builds to try out would be difficult or impossible to do in one run.Q: Is it worth the price?A: Yes. One play-through is about 12 - 15 hours. Could be longer if you try multiple builds or search all nooks and crannys.The ogre creamed 9.5 out of 10 times with this one.
_childDocuments_.name: GRIME

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great souls-like/metroidvania, with amazing platforming, exploration and combat, which is rare since most games focus on one or two of those aspects but Grime actually nails all 3. Refreshing lack of handholding too! If only the technical side was more polished, it still stutters and hitches like crazy on a reasonably powerful pc, and some minor bugs and glitches do remain. Playable, sure, but not pleasing to see in motion. If they ever manage to make it run smoothly we'll be talking about a Hollow Knight tier classic here.
_childDocuments_.name: GRIME

_childDocuments_.review: Really recommend this game to anyone who likes metroidvanias. Devs cleary were inspired by the best games like hollow knight, dead cells and dark souls. The game has a very interesting parry mechanic that helps not only with combat and bosses but also with player progression. And while character stats progress is simple it is very satisfying to meet the needed requirements for a new weapon you just found. Speaking of weapons there is a lot of them ranging from slow big to fast dps. Replayability is also a factor, you can try very different builds in multiple playthroughs.The games atmosphere and soundtracks are such a vibe.Really happy for the devs, plus one to the great metroidavnia games.
_childDocuments_.name: GRIME

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant art style, tremendous build diversity, smart evolution of traditional "souls-like" game mechanics, spectacular boss fights, and so, so,  many secret rooms. The problem with making difficult games is that you have to balance challenging the player with respecting their time. "Souls-like" games are infamous for often being unnecessarily punishing in their attempts to beat down the player, but GRIME leaves that job to the enemies. There's no currency or experience loss on death, boss runback distance is short, corpse retrieval is not required and can actually AID you in fights, your map tracks your steps so you're never completely blind, you unlock two types of teleport abilities, and doing lots of side exploration will reward you with additional healing capacity. I love it. This game  to kill you and it rewards skillful play immensely - but it doesn't want to leave you stuck up against a wall. Easily one of my favorite games of its kind, and earns a thumbs-up without any hesitation.
_childDocuments_.name: GRIME

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant game with great variety and versatility in both enemy design and Character building. It is mechanically fun and  flexible depending on how you choose to approach sections and bosses. The bosses themselves are also very well designed both visually and mechanically, they have a great balance of difficulty without feeling cheap when they beat you.
_childDocuments_.name: GRIME

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic metroidvania with a surreal aesthetic and an amazing soundtrack. The progression felt well paced, the upgrades had impact with combat and exploration. The world takes a bit to understand but the general look and feel makes the game worth exploring further and further. My only issue is that the weapons didn't have a satisfying feel to it. The Parrying and Pull system in fights does make up for that. All in all I think if you enjoy metroidvanias I would highly recommend this one.
_childDocuments_.name: GRIME

_childDocuments_.review: I can easily remember plenty of quirky and unique characters whose 'heads' are part of their identity. A detective with a brain inside a jar for a head, A scientist whose upper half of his head is the entire body of a monkey, Siren Head, just to name a few. In "GRIME" your head is literally a black hole.To be fair YOU are a black hole. The rest of your body is made from dust and stones merged together to survive the unknown world you need to devour, little by little. You are very weak so you need to get stronger by destroying everything in your path.The world in question is a real mystery and in a state that someone could describe as 'hopeless'. Everything is in ruins and every living creature is doing their best to barely continue their lifes or trying to make the world even worse. Especially for you. A beautiful destroyed dangerous world just for your 'eyes'.The first rule you must know to survive and to determine if you will like the game or not: Parry is the king. If you can easily time the attacks of your enemies so you can parry them, you will feel right at home. If not, I highly suggest you refund the game.Obviously the game is not only about parrying, but a very important aspect of it is getting new abilities and making your journey much easier.If you are still with me, you will have the pleasure of using a big variety of weapons, nearly unique from each other, and satisfying combat overcoming different colorful enemies and bosses.The classic formula of a metroidvania game is present here: A lot of exploring, getting new powers and finding secrets. Sadly traversing in different areas back and forth is a bit more time consuming. Without saying much, only near the end does it become 'normal'.Finally I need to mention the platforming. At the beginning it was not so bad. However you get so many different moves to literally master to continue exploring. I dare to say it becomes the only reason I was ready to scream after failing a specific combination of jumps/dashes to reach a cliff.I think I said enough details to make a decision if you want to try "GRIME". I hope you do even with the specific play style you must follow.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: GRIME

_childDocuments_.review: Great Metroidvania Type game with tons of different weapons and armor sets to use. Bosses prove to be relatively challenge and are well designed with great themes. The one thing I think that holds this game back a little bit is how reliant the game mechanics are on the player parrying enemies but the Devs are listening to player feedback and implementing new perk options and buffing others to allow the player to approach encounters differently than just relying on parrying to heal and avoid damage. The one biggest positive I noticed is how involved the devs are with the players on steam discussions and quick they are to respond to bug reports and also help players work around possible lockouts the player might miss huge positive on the devs part I can really tell they care and love this game and want players to feel the same.
_childDocuments_.name: GRIME

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Grime is a contrived mess with some good ideas, but ultimately tries to equate annoyance with difficulty and challenge. If you want a quality 2D metroidvenia, try Blasphemous, Ender Lilies, Salt and Sanctuary, and Vigil: The Longest Night.Boses:* The bosses range from boring (Amalgam) to extremely annoying (Vulture). Utter chaos during some of the encounters is equated to difficulty and challenge, but ultimately comes off as annoyance.Enemies:The developers have intentionally situated certain enemies in places to maximally annoy the player.* Since the player cannot shoot, s/he is supposed to absorb and return the enemy's projectiles. Fine, but what about those annoying burning needle throwers? Those projectiles cannot be absorbed and the enemy cannot be reached to be killed. The player is bombarded mercilessly while fighting other enemies, avoiding spikes coming from the ceiling, and running over crumbling floor, all at the same time. Annoying!* Another class of enemies can target the player from half a level away, and are placed in areas accessible only after acquiring a particular skill. This makes traversing the area hell. Annoying!Skills:* Respeccing is not encouraged in this game. Trying out a new build requires a completely new run, going though the same annoying slog.Levels:* Entering a new level or a "room" does not reveal it on the map. The player is forced to run around blind, trying to find the pylon that reveals the area. Once you die, you have to retrace your steps going blind, which is annoying.* The developers decided that adding platforms that ultimately drop you to your death without letting you see what's below you is challenging, but again, comes off as annoying.Weapons:* Most of the weapons are useless. They either consume too much focus, do very little damage, or are too slow.Transportation:* The transportation network is very sparse, roughly one entry/exit point per three areas. This causes the player to re-traverse whole areas just to get from point A to point B, which is very annoying. I don't see why the obelisks cannot be part of the transportation network...
_childDocuments_.name: GRIME

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a beautiful spectacle through and through. I've never been more dumbfounded by tailored grim, delightful and bizarre art. From the mobs to the bosses and environment to the backdrop, this game is such a challenging and exhilarating  experience. In addition, the soundtrack fits so perfect with the ambiance and flows perfectly between areas. The unique characters you meet along the way, weather menacing, deranged or endearing, are so unfamiliar that you truly feel that you're enveloped in a undiscovered universe. The story in it of it self is intriguing and conveyed through the mouths of sickened creatures leaving it for interpretation. If you love side-scrolling Action-Adventure RPG's I highly recommend you treat yourself to this demented, beautiful wonderland.
_childDocuments_.name: GRIME

_childDocuments_.review: I might have to take a break from metroidvanias until they outgrow their obsession with dark souls. Grime has an interesting and unique concept of having your character absorb and reflect attacks as their main attack. However almost immediately someone gives you a huge club to beat the crap out of everything with. This squandering of such an interesting mechanic feels indicative of the problems of the game.The visual world of the game is unusual and beautiful to look at, but because of the overly slow soulsborn style mechanics, it's certainly not very fun to play.
_childDocuments_.name: GRIME

_childDocuments_.review: "Easy Recommend. This hits all the Metroidvania boxes for me:1. Large map with tons of secrets.2. Excellent combat that always feels great (with a few bugs).3. Very interesting world and lore that puts the responsibility on the player to dissect it.4. Developers that clearly care about their community with full-blown free DLC that adds a lot to the overall experience.5. Weapon variety and weapon arts are actually the best in the genre. So much variety! And every single one feels great!6. The art and music are 10/10 supreme.Some things for improvement:1. The platforming at times is hit or miss for me. On one hand, it aims to do a lot, but I personally don't know if it succeeds in a few areas. Not so bad that I was put off, but definitely janky enough for me to get annoyed. Example: Colors of Rot update added these electric tiles that are quite unforgiving.2. The map could use some missing elements like shop locations and when warping, it would be nice to see physically on the map where I'm heading instead of having to remember the surrogate location names. I took a year off from playing, and it was impossible to navigate based solely on the names and little title cards.3. I love the art, but there are a lot of repeat platforms that can take me out of the otherwise awe-striking environment. It doesn't always blend well.4. Maybe the stamina system needs to be reworked a tiny bit? I find that fast weapons overall are better because they consume less of it, while slow weapons consume the whole bar after like 2 swings. Maybe having a base stamina absorption for all weapons would feel better. Logically, it makes sense, I just don't feel incentivized to use the slow weapons as much as the fast/very fat ones.I primarily play Metroidvanias and rogue-type games, and this one is certainly a hidden gem that frustrates me that not enough people have heard of. 9/10. Thank you, Clover Bite!"
_childDocuments_.name: GRIME

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best souls-like/metroidvania I played so far. It's not flawless but gameplay and mechanics are well crafted.Combat is very good with a lot of variety. Attacks and parry mechanic feels very good and satisfying. Enemy variety enough and enemies didn't felt overused. Boss design and mechanics are good and I enjoyed them all. Platforming and level design are one of the best I played and its actually fun to navigate through the level. Lore and story has depth and it could be interesting if you pay attention to dialogs.Although it has a unique artstyle and it's well suited for the story it want to tell, I understand it might not be for every one but in it's defense it gets more interesting further in the game. Music is well done and fits the atmospheres, also its memorable which is a good point.If you are fan of this type of games, definitely try it out.
_childDocuments_.name: GRIME

_childDocuments_.review: Nice visual style and bosses were decent.  That's where ithe good points end.  It's very punishing.  The map isn't good, there's no real indicator where to go, exploration itself tries to kill you, combat is bad and puts focus on parries if you want to ever heal.  Skills I encountered seemed ok, weapons ok (but you need to switch them to handle many enemies, you cant just be good with your favorite).The problem is that you cant get anywhere without a fight (sometimes dropped right on your head out of nowhere) or some sort of very precise timing of jumps/movement.  As you learn to fight and move you lose life.. alot.  When you die you lose a portion of the materials you need to skill up.  So... better get good or youre not going anywhere.  You get one big heal between checkpoints, and if you want it after that you need to parry.. which is risky... multiple times before you can heal again.  You do not have a lot of life to lose.  2 or 3 mistakes, often in quick succession, can end you.  You can also end up in a bad position with no way out and you're dead if you haven't mastered combat.This is not a metroidvania designed to be enjoyable to play.  You need to be good and methodical with everything you do very quickly.  There is almost no learning curve to help you.  It's just one big wall of punishment.I don't have the time to invest into this game.  It's just painful dying so much and having no idea where I'm even going or why.  It became unpleasant.  I don't play games to be annoyed and frustrated and abused by punishing design.  If you are, great get this.  For everyone else, I highly suggest passing on Grime.
_childDocuments_.name: GRIME

_childDocuments_.review: I want to love this game but cannot. My review will be biased as a heavy player of Dark Souls series as well as Hollow Knight.This souls-like game (unfortunately) picks up a lot of misconceptions about what make Dark Souls Dark Souls. Yes, you collect mass from enemies to grow and lose them on death, when you respawn from a monument-ish structure, leaving a broken vessel on the spot of death. You got a large variety of weapons and seem truly to offer different combat styles, and the weapons can scale with strength / dexterity / w.e which you cannot possible max out all of them at least not in early game... the list goes on, and these are not bad features. However, in Dark Souls every single piece of game mechanics and concepts has been created to collectively tell a coherent story, while leaving room for interpretation from each individual player. They are not there just to make the player suffer (although they do make the player suffer). In contrast, everything in this game seems to have been designed just so that it looks like.. well, Dark Souls. In that the game succeeded, but as a player I expect more from souls-like games than just being souls-like on a mechanics level.As for the metroidvania part, the control and movement feels clunky enough to make exploration practically not enjoyable. Unnecessary hidden paths, no soundtrack at least not before the 1st boss, plain world design (yes I see nothing but rocks everywhere 1 whole hour in), and not one interesting character yet to have met.The combat system heavily relies on parry mechanism. Sadly parry is just too easy, and upon successful parry the player gets absolutely no reward in terms of visual and sound effects. To make it worse you are forced to watch several seconds of bland animation while the character 'absorbs' the enemy. This soon becomes painful. I don't know what else to say about it. Core mechanism of an action game, made painful to trigger, only as a way (and the only way) to grind (grind!) for upgradable traits? I don't know what I'm doing.By no means is this a bad game and the team has apparently made a lot of efforts in making it. That said, I cannot recommend a game that simply offers nothing enjoyable to me as a player in the first hour of playtime.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely stunning, rich, and challenging metroidvania.I was more than a little biased when picking this out game from the big list of dark-gritty-difficult metroidvanias out there (), but I'm extremely glad this is the one I chose. The combat is challenging and moldable to different playstyles, the platforming (which plays a big role in exploration as well as normal progression through the game) is varied and rewarding, the worldmap is vast yet varied, the boss battles (as well as a few particularly cunning enemies) drive you to keep getting better and better, secrets litter every corner of the map and constantly keep you on your toes, and character death never pushes you too far back. A few particular great gameplay choices, such as watching the worldmap and its inhabitants change as you progress through it or facing the same boss in a different form and location, push you even further into the gritty world the game takes place in.But there are two suits that stand out even further than all the rest - the first being the post-game: it's fairly common for these types of games to have some form of new game+, but Grime's is handled perfectly - You can train skills and upgrade weapons even further than before. Enemies don't just hit harder, some have altogether different attack patterns from the base game. Boss fights add new attacks and moves to their fights, and some have whole new phases (). Even some of the environmental challenges are more difficult, to test your skill at controlling your growing character. All these together make it well worth at least one additional runthrough of the game (which is enough to collect all achievements, if you're paying enough attention).However, the greatest pull of the game () is the art direction: every model oozes thought and care, the environments are bleak yet never dull or boring, enemies are varied yet immediately recognizable. Several bosses () are some of my favorite character designs of all time.Another surprisingly great part of the game is the plot: while it isn't the most original, its strength lies in the fact that it doesn't hinder the gameplay - the premise, once you catch on, is extremely simple, and you can breeze through the entire game without paying any attention to what the characters are saying and get a general idea of what's happening. Diving into the lore, which I do recommend, is rewarding, but isn't necessary to understand or enjoy the game ().Overall, a truly fantastic experience. True, there are a few minor kinks and quality of life issues that could use fixing, and I found a few minor graphical bugs during my playthroughs, but nothing that takes away from the experience as a whole. Definitely recommended for anyone on the lookout for challenging metroidvanias with good replay value, with new content still being added and expanded, or anyone looking to support small, lesser-known indie teams from small, lesser-known countries.

_childDocuments_.review: So I love metroidvanias, and I've played a fair amount of difficult or souls-like metroidvanias at a high level. For reference I've beat Hollow Knight, Ender Lilies, Afterimage, Rabi-Ribi, Blasphemous True Ending (1 and 2), and many more.  (shouldn't have to qualify this because less skilled or experienced gamers opinions are still valid and important but some of y'all are just huge snobs) So give me the jester award all you want, but I can't recommend this game to anyone who wants to have a good time. There are some excellent ideas, I loved the beginning and the Demo reeled me in when I tried it a while ago. Atmospheric, cool boss design, challenging combat. But way too unpolished and anti-fun. If you worship at the feet of purposely punishing souls-like games....then you might overlook the issues I present here. If you aren't a souls-like simp, then I would heed my words and save your money. CONS: Platforming/movement - sorry but the movement is too glitchy. I got stuck in walls and platforms way too many times for a game that has been out this long. So many platforms that are lower than your character's head you for some reason cannot jump up to, yet there are platforms above your head your character can grasp onto. Hitboxes for movement/grapple are completely irrelevant as you can be within range and the grapple won't go through, where as some bosses were pullable from WAY outside of the visible grappling range. Very very messy hitboxes which is not good when what we see is what we are supposed to work with. Healing is painfully slow, and then after you safely finish the healing animation you still have to slowly wait for the health bar to go up. You have no iframes after taking damage so in many boss fights you can die in 2 hits which buffs the bosses difficulty up imo very cheaply rather than just making it challenging but playable. I beat all of the bosses except NG plus bosses, and the last 2 in game bosses. So I was good at it.....it just stopped being fun when you realized it is designed to be tedious and stressful rather than exciting and fun. Combat - the combat starts promising when you master the parry system, only to punish you later by forcing you to "dodge dodge dodge hit.....repeat" when you can no longer parry enemy attacks. Really tedious and unfun which is a shame because the beginning of the game was cool and fun. (I am talking about the first couple biomes....not just the demo area). World design - the game is very linear to the point where there are no abilities or major game items that you get from backtracking. Making backtracking completely irrelevant in my opinion is a huge failure to engage players throughout the MV experience. Backtracking only yields items that are peppered throughout the entire game very much like Metroid Rockets. There was one biome with a different color scheme but everything else is so very very dimly lit to the point where it's not atmospheric....it just hurts your eyes and you can't appreciate the wonderful design. I love dark atmosphere but we need to be able to see where we are going if there are death pits or hidden enemies that can one shot us. After the beginning of the game, too often you are punished for moving forward by being hit with unparryable weapons without even having a chance to know where the attack is coming from...and then it eats through your health bar and you die. Balance - Enemies, traps, etc. do way way way too much damage at all points in the game. If you want to make your game so souls-like, the character needs to be able to respond quickly and fluidly. There were so many times where my character was attacked after dashing through an enemy or boss, or dashed right next to an enemy and remained on the same side instead of dashing through. Bizarrely unpolished for a game with so much acclaim. Y'all deserve to have higher standards for products you pay for. Scaling/Upgrades - Upgrades are very limited in their effect and seem to do little to your character, plus not being able to upgrade freely (you have a certain amount of rebuilds allotted) discourages exploring different builds/upgrades. If I am required to experiment with different builds for different areas or bosses, please do not limit my ability to do so. That's just not fun....and instead of making us explore your game we are paralyzed with uncertainty lest we lose all of our rebuilding items and end up stuck with a bad build. What is the point of that other than trying to make the game not fun? Really....someone tell me? Are games not for fun anymore? I have 2 bosses left and I don't even want to finish the game because the final parts of the game seem very underpolished compared to the demo portion of the game and first two biomes. I absolutely could beat this.....but the game doesn't match its' demands for responsiveness and polish with..........responsiveness and polish. Spoiler alert as well - but the last 2 biomes are platforming only biomes and.......as someone who loves platformer games as well even I have zero interest because I already know how bad and glitchy it's going to be and I'd rather learn Path of Pain with no crystal dash or something more casual. I see that the developers have addressed SOME of the issues people have brought up, but they have done nothing to acknowledge the sluggish slipperyness of the main character, or how unbalanced and glitchy the last few bosses can be. The RNG is allowed to generate a lot of no win scenarios....which to me is just anti fun. There is also SO MUCH lag and eaten input in the late game fights and biomes, that my partner was actually able to see that the stamina bar regenerates slower during boss fights and combat than it does when my character is near a save with no enemies. That is not good, as my computer was even able to run Ori or 3d platformer games......so this should not be happening to this degree. Not optimized. PROS: Story/lore - This story and the characters and concepts behind the lore are so dope. Honestly so cool, developers I hope you don't let Grime 2 be this jank in terms of the gameplay experience because you know how to create atmosphere and tell a story without being overbearing. Really cool. Design - The body horror enemy/character design is so cool and original. I was rooting for the game because of how stunning it is. Truly excellent. I hope you the developers can get the sequel to be more responsive and polished because their ability to create enemies and bosses that are unique and interesting is unquestionable. Music - I am not a huge fan of the music but it is good and it is atmospheric.....just not to my personal taste but beautifully rendered and it does seem to match the game. Sound design overall is excellent, I just personally wouldn't recognize or necessarily want to hear the music outside of the game. Doesn't mean it's not excellent, just not to my taste. I still think it's a strong point of the game. Overall message to the developers - please please make sure that if you want the challenge of the game to require responsiveness and precision from the player.....that your movement/world design/controls are equally responsive and precise. I have been frustrated playing other souls like games but pushed on because i knew it was me. I can tell that is not the case here and it's a shame because there is some super cool stuff happening in this game. But I have to quit here.....I don't want to play it anymore and I would hope that disappoints y'all as much as it disappoints me. I would recommend having some of your QA team for Grime 2 not worship at the temple of dark souls, because I want it to be an even bigger success and a knockout beginning to end.

_childDocuments_.review: Dark Souls and Castlevania had a baby and named it Hollow Knight.  Then, Hollow Knight coupled with daddy Dark Souls and made Grime.  Grime is more similar to Dark Souls in its creepy environments, weird, semi-humanoid enemies, and opaque storytelling.  But it takes challenging platforming and slick 2D from Hollow Knight.  Death is a bit more forgiving than both games since you retain your “souls” after death and can upgrade your character.  This does reduce the overall stress of the game, although I certainly died a lot.  It also has that famous mid-game boss difficulty spike that Dark Souls made famous.  So while it has its roots in a tried and tested gaming formula, it is a beauty to play.  The developers clearly put their hearts and souls (pun intended) into the game.  The level and enemy design is spectacular.  And there is a story (perhaps metaphor is a better word for it) that does become relatively apparent by the end of the game.  The graphics are stellar and reflect the story that is being told.It is difficult – that’s for sure.  There is a parry mechanic that is crucial to survival, and a lot of deaths are spent learning to anticipate enemy moves.  Most moves are sufficiently telegraphed, however; and I never rage-quit over an unfair death.  BIG thumbs-ups from me – highly recommended, particularly for fans of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Great soulslike metroidvania game. 9/10 Pros:Unique aestheticIt might be a bit repetitive exploring caves, but the areas are still pretty varied.Amazing bossesThere's not really any bad bosses in the game. Each one has fun mechanics and good music.Cool weapons and mechanicsThe combat is weighty and satisfying, and the weapons feel unique and good to use.I like the hunt point trait system too. After you absorb enough of an enemy, you unlock a trait you can put points into. You get these points from defeating stronger enemies in the world.Devs listen to feedbackThere's so many things that they added and changed that made the game so much better. Armor now gives stat and trait buffs, more fast travel points, fast travel can now be earned way earlier in the game, buffed str weapons, added respeccing stats, some bosses have been reworked, as well as the whole free dlc update.Potential cons:None of these really bothered me that much, but they're something to keep in mind.Late game pacingThe late game areas are mostly just platforming and lore/story exposition with little to no enemies and linear.The game doesn't hold your handThere's some minor mechanics that the game doesn't directly tell you, but you should be able to figure it out yourself at some point. It's also easy to get lost, and it has the hollow knight map system, you need to get the beacon to get the map, which people might not like.This isn't really a con, but the combat is pretty stamina management focused, and you generally want to be parrying a lot, and can't spam dash a bunch.

_childDocuments_.review: Top tier metroidvania. Should be up in the pantheon of the greats.I can't stress enough how good the boss design is. The fights were soooo good. My only complaint is that there aren't more of them. Combat is incredibly fair. Never feel like I died to something I couldn't do something about. No cheap hidden instakill traps laid by the devs just to annoy you, no enemy ganks for the luls of your death, heck Grime is super generous in general despite being fairly tough. Not losing  mass when dying is nice.The platforming challenges are actually challenges, but respect your time. None of that "oopsie ya didn't pixel perfect that jump, now fall all the way to the beginning and start over!" Nearly all of them have safe checkpoints throughout and are satisfying to complete. I will complain that maaaaaybe some aspects could be more generous (specifically hitboxes of the green bubble jump things and dashing through wall cracks) but nothing is impossible. It's a biiiiiit slow to start, I popped in and played like 15-20 min at a time for the first few sessions, but got hooked around after the second boss. Stick with it til then if you're on the fence. By the end I was completing everything just because I didn't want the game to end.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd give it an overall 7/10.The first half I truly enjoyed, I really liked the combat, the build diversity, the parry mechanic, the bosses, the minor platforming, it was all great fun.However the last half of the game kind of soured the experience. Way too many tedious platforms sections that felt as if they were designed to make you fail over and over, especially since ladders in this game are so poorly designed and for some reason the character glues himself to them, making it very challenging to jump from them (as holding left or right just forces him to climb up or down), combat enemies around them, and navigate between them when obstructions are present, seriously they almost made me want to stop playing altogether. Besides that.. the combat just started to get very stale, and once you get the parry timings down (which is very easy), basic enemies don't really pose a challenge. And with the way healing works, they can only make the bosses so strong since heals are so limited, making the last half of the bosses very easy (atleast for me).I don't know.. I feel very torn on this game, since I feel like it HAS SO MUCH POTENTIAL, but just so many things felt bland and stale the more I played it.TLDR;First half of the game I'd give a 8/10 - 9/10.. last half I can't really go higher than a 5/10 - 6/10. Will keep my eyes peeled for future projects from the developers, as they definitely have a lot of potential.

_childDocuments_.review: So its PRO CONS list time. Pros --Looks good most of the time-Story seems fine haven't finished it-platforming is solid and even really cool and interesting with good platform puzzles and gauntlets -Bosses look great and often have good move sets with good clear windows of attack and Parrying Cons--Some platforming areas feel nearly impossible without sufficient Force levels-Encountered many minor bugs - getting stuck in things, getting sent back to checkpoints without dying, dashing in place, effects becoming invisible -Game does not respect your time, everything feels like it takes too long, and will make you repeat huge areas and backtrack huge areas.-fighting everything except the bosses feels awful and unbalanced-weapon selection is a facade, with faster weapons out classing slow weapons by miles-leveling feels pointless outside of Force, and base weapon holding requirements-Your damage is always too low making fighting feel like a slog even with no points in anything except damage and high levels of weapon upgrades.-game focuses on parrying heavily, but than adds piles of enemies who you cannot parry for full effect or not at all. -Enemies track your movement with attacks in a bad way-map layout and navigation is HORRIBLE its disgusting how bad it feels to back track through areas. _childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for June 2023, and this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before July 4th, 2023, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.A 2d Souls-like game with a push for parrying. GRIME starts differently than most souls-like, instead of knocking down the first few enemies with your weapon, GRIME has players practice parrying.  GRIME has a really interesting mechanic with its parry that lets players take abilities based on enemies.  It’s just one of many ways GRIME stands out.  In addition to a Souls-like, this is also a bit of a Metroidvania, at least according to how many times I’ve seen it on that subreddit.  So far it’s a typical side scroller but I imagine players will unlock more abilities over time. The game is also pretty hard as you would expect, though I was able to get to the first boss and take him down in a pretty epic fight.   There’s also no real penalty so far for dying, so players can grind up points to level up abilities pretty easily.  There’s an interesting style to the game as well, and some people might be turned off by it, but it’s an intriguing game so far. Pick this up if you like a decent challenge, interesting monsters, and a very solid Metroidvania.   It’s an odd beginning and the characters are weird, but there’s also an interesting boss design and the map has a lot of nooks and crannies to explore.  This is a surprisingly good game, and I’m glad I finally got a chance to check it out. It also just added a new free DLC which adds a new game plus an additional boss, so that would be worth checking out as well.If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: Let’s just get to the brass tacks. Beautiful aesthetics and concept but the mechanical movement of the player character feels like walking through mud. I have unlocked some movement upgrades, air dash and sprint, but combat and movement don’t feel any different. I agree with other reviews indicating a ‘clunky’ feel to the game. Climbing ladders, getting stuck on them when you don’t intend to use them, janky platforming, ridiculous traps that simply make getting around a chore, rather than enjoyable. In other true platforming games, Ori or Hollow Knight, getting around is fun. GRIME makes it an arduous task, especially when you get one-shotted even after 10+ health point upgrades. Which brings me to the next issue of combat. This game is difficult, but is beyond just gitting gud. I’ve played, beaten, and enjoyed games like Sekiro, Elden Ring, Hollow Knight and other very difficult games. Every time I died or encountered a difficult section without progressing in any of the aforementioned titles, I felt like I deserved it. I wasn’t doing something right. It felt like a challenge, but felt right. in GRIME I am now over level 40 and I feel no more powerful than when I first started. My sprint or air dash are useless, I keep getting one shotted by normal mobs then respawning halfway across the map only to get one shotted again. The game is punishing, but not in the same way Sekiro is, not the way Hollow Knight is – it just feels punitive and, again, like a task. TLDR: Needs refinement. Overall clunky movement, combat feels oddly unfair compared to other difficult games, traps and obstacles on the map crush your health even after multiple skill point upgrades.

_childDocuments_.review: For a metroidvania it has a very souls-like combat system with light and heavy attacks as well as parrying. You are given the option of switching between two weapons already selected previously. On top of that, the game has a lot of "resine" type weapon buffs consumable items which can be equipped in 4 slots.  Perhaps the most influensial of all the souls-like mechanics Grime has is stamina. it is consumed when sprinting, attacking and jumping while its conditions for replenishing vary based on what traits (charms) one has progressed.  Healing is done either using "Breath", a mana-like bar or through estus-like items that regenerate upon visiting a bonfire (surrogate)  Parrying is going to be your most used form of both defence and offence. Not all attacks can be parried. Any attack that has the weapon or the enemy glowing red is non parry-able. Moreover, any red health bar an enemy might have is instantly shredded after a successful parry.  Traits (much like charms in Hollow Knight or prayer beads in Blasphemous) are your main source of variation when it comes to combat. Traits are gained whenever an enemy is consumed (killed via parrying) a number of times and then unlocked using hunt points which you get from miniboss type enemies. Traits offer really enjoyable ways of making you more powerful. For example stamina regeneration upon pulling an enemy or parrying their attack.  As a souls like it offers a levelling system, a very lenient at that. I got near to lvl 100 just by playing and paying no mind about "souls". "Souls" are not lost upon dying but instead a shadow clone is left behind which holds your "Ardor": a stat that increases the more enemies you absorb and sometimes decreases upon taking damage. Its main purpose is to increase the amount of souls gained.  There is a plethora of both weapons and armour sets with weapons having a variety of possible strong attacks and types which I won't mention here. Armour sets offer trait buffs when worn in full  My main enjoyment of the game came from the bosses. Most weren't particularly challenging (With a few exceptions like  but between parrying and pulling your enemy you feel like an unstoppable force of destruction  There is a wide variety of enemies with different timings on their parries and after-parry behaviour  For a game so focused on combat one might expect that the movement isn't the most fluid but that is not the case (at least now). Akhlan's movements feel fluid and intuitive making the platforming fun. Said platforming isn't particularly difficult either  As many other metroidvanias, Grime has a platforming challenge. Much in the style of HK's Path of Pain, it's a linear platforming section of increased difficulty compared to the rest of the game. That being said, it is not all that challenging. My personal gripe with it is that the way forward is often hidden behind hidden walls or floors that are not given away by their surroundings  The plot (as in most soulslike games) is left intentionally vague and left to be pieced together by the player. I haven't spent much time on it and so don't know anything more than .  The art direction feels spot on with a lot of originality in my opinion, mixing body-horror with a cosmic feelIf you enjoy metroidvanias and souls-likes then you will most likely enjoy Grime as well. 100% the game is also not particularly difficult.

_childDocuments_.review: Great visuals. Great gameplay. Fantastic enemy design - a cosmic horror / Lovecraftian influence, perhaps? Alex Roe did the music, so it's fitting and haunting. Story so far seems like it will evolve well - we really don't know who we are or why we are here, but neither do the enemies, it seems.In my hour playthrough of the game so far, there are three weapons to choose from. You must make use of a parry mechanic to gain health, which is not as complex as it seems. Having said that, failing to connect this parry this is how I've died each time so far. Minimal penalty for death. The two checkpoints I've found so far are fairly far apart, but that's where the difficulty partly comes in and that's what I love.My major performance issues, although I did have some stuttering and frame drops at times. No bugs or glitches. No crashes.Finally, my main gripe with the game so far is the inventory / menu interface.
