_childDocuments_.review: Grime is not subtle about its influences and that does the game a lot of favors. It's a great take on a winning formula. If you like this genre, you will like this game.Overall, Grime is very respectful of your time. They've shaved off many of the typical frustrations that come with this genre. Your currency is not lost on death. There's always a very quick shortcut between spawn points and boss battles. Backtracking is largely optional, and grinding is completely unnecessary.The boss battles, particularly the optional ones, are a total blast, and there are some really thrilling platforming sections.The world is genuinely interesting to explore, and I was consistently thrilled by the big reveals. My only real complaint is the lack of NG+ mode, which apparently is already in the works!

_childDocuments_.review: You know, people will say "its not a metroidvania it's a soulslike" and "it's not a soulslike it's a metroidvania!" but lets be honest, the only tangible difference that I've been able to see between the two genres seems to be whether the worldspace is 3d or not. If dark souls was 2d, it would be a metroidvania, if castlevania was 3d, it would be a soulslike, the two genres are so nearly identical, and this game only proves it further, it has aspects of "soulslikes" with a tight combat system, a dodge, and a stamina bar, but it also has aspects of "metroidvanias", where full exploration of an area is gated behind unlockable platforming upgrades, it's neither, it's both, I'd even go so far as to call it a "Soulsvania!" But, either way, it's downright awesome. This game plays great, the bosses are fun, the story is totally unique, the world is interesting, the platforming is great, the combat is tight, everything feels GOOD, period, The games I'd call closest to it are Hollow Knight, Ori, and Salt and Sanctuary, so if you like any of those games, or anything you'd call "similar", you probably wanna pick this game up. It's hella fun.

_childDocuments_.review: (Note: This review was done after playing through the main game, including the Colors of Rot update. The "Extra Content" tab reveals there's a third major update planned)- At first, the game is a visual feast. Light glistening off of slick cave floors. A strange but eerily cool-looking protagonist. Twisted, grotesque enemies and towering Lovecraftian monsters lurk around every corner, but you have monstrous crushing weapons and iridescent armor to protect yourself- These initial impressions slowly fade. By-and-large, the looks of the enemies and gear stay consistently good, but boss design reuse and the omnipresence of cave environments get a little stale by hour 15. "Oh, I've gone through blue cave and pink cave, but now I need to go through green cave to get to slightly greener cave." Or, "Oh cool, a second 4-armed rock monster with different attack sequencing. I bet the final boss won't have a phase like that"- Gripes aside, the visual design did leave a very good impression. It's eerie, brooding, and mysterious. I kept coming back for more- The music is what you'd expect given the Lovecraftian and Souls-like influences. Ominous, sweeping orchestral and choral arrangements punctuated by sparse, austere pieces- There's some meat on the bones lore-wise, but not as intricately woven as other similar games. Overtly, the story is about your character bringing about the end of the world, but there's slightly more to it than that if you pay attention to the NPCs and item descriptions- Expect to see plenty of genre tropes about death/rebirth and destruction/creation- But all of that hardly matters because there's cool weapons to find and difficult bosses to kill them with- Weapon variety is honestly very impressive as are the corresponding move sets. You've got stuff like tooth fists with projectile attacks, centipede whips with AOE, and axes that literally chew through enemies- Armor designs are similarly excellent. Sure, eating an entire city after putting on a theater performance is cool, but it's even better if you're dressed in glowing mother of pearl armor while doing it- The moment-to-moment gameplay feels fantastic. In combat, attacking feels fluid and natural. Small weapons like dual daggers feel speedy and spammable, but heavy attacks with giant hammers feel weighty and crushing. Dodging also feels very fair, though I feel like a few more invincibility frames would have saved me a dozen or so deaths- Platforming is also excellent. As you'd expect from a metroidvania, you unlock ways to traverse the environment as you go, but Grime has a cool way of making you string them together into some of the most difficult platforming sections I've had the pleasure of completing- While I was disappointed by some of the reused environments and copy/paste bosses, the game has a lot going for it. It looks incredible and presents players with a tough but ultimately satisfying challenge. That was more than enough to impress me- Mix the platforming of Ori with the combat of Blasphemous, and you'll get an idea of what it feels like to play- I played the game entirely on Steam Deck and swapped the left stick and d-pad in the layout settings. 2D platformers just feel more natural without an analog stick. Performance-wise, I did unfortunately experience some occasional framiness, but it was mostly fine. Ran well otherwise- . If you're a fan of the genre and love a challenge, you owe it to yourself to give this one a try. Looking forward to seeing more from this developer, because this was a really impressive first release

_childDocuments_.review: I have gotten to the final boss, but wanted to write this review before I know how this game ends.Pros:-World building is beautiful and natural. -The scenery adds to the lore.-Leaves lore up for much interpretation, allowing fun chats within the community.-Pull and Absorb mechanics, their interactions in platforming AND fighting, add a pleasant variety to the way you can defeat various challenges.-At points the platforming feels like a boss fight all its own. Mechanics are design well enough to require multiple attempts to overcome, but never feel cheap.-Sound adds to the experience, music is intentional and the absence of it in set scenes helps add weight to the moment. -HK easter eggs! Praise the servant needle!- Leveling and weapon upgrade are limited. Making your choices feel more impact full, and promoting multiple play throughs.Cons:- Glitches into more than a few walls at very frustrating moments. Don't dash to wall when teeth close. _childDocuments_.review: Grime is good but my opinion on it is weird, let me explain.First of all, I just wanna state how amazing the game is artistically. Both visually and lorewise, this game gets a 10/10 from me. It delves into a similar type of cosmic horror theme as H.P. Lovecraft does so if you like his work, this might scratch that itch.Let me get it out of that way that, yes, this game is clunky. The combat feels either weightless or it feels like its taking place in a waist high pool of water. The combat isn't bad, but the flow is often unsatisfactory. That's not to say there aren't any fights with amazing flow, cuz there are. My two favorite bosses, namely The final performance and Dreamborn terror have a really good flow and feel really good to fight against. The weapons are all cool. I don't think there is a single weapon i find boring which is obviously a huge win. I do however feel like the game is too easy. During my first playthrough of the game, not a single boss took me over 30 min to beat, same goes for ng+ (with the new movesets and whatnot). I play a LOT of metroidvanias so without sounding like a prick, I may have an easier time than others.All in all, do I recommend it? Yes. It tells a beautiful tale and at the end of the day, its a wonderful looking, fairly tight feeling metroidvania with great platforming and awesome looking bosses, and that's all that really matters.

_childDocuments_.review: This game gets what makes this genre fun and intriguing.The artstyle, story and music are all woven togheter in a weird dreamy cosmic horror vibe.The combat is varied with lots of different weapons that each feel unique, but the best feature is the parry done with your black hole head, capable of absorbing enemies and their traits.I absolutely fell in love with the the freedom of movement and traversal you gain once you unlock all abilities.

_childDocuments_.review: Grime has some really great and equally bad elements in every aspect:- Even though there are some creative platforming segments, the movement usually feels clunky and unresponsive, especially when it comes to grabbing ledges and ladders.- The level design and interconnectivity of the world is mostly good, but areas like Gloomnest and Garden are an absolute slog to go through because of frustrating enemy design and placements.- At first, the only way to teleport is through gates that are placed very sparingly, but by the mid point you get the ability to teleport between any checkpoints, rendering the whole gate mechanic completely obsolete, which leaves me to question why the developers bothered to put it in the first place.- The music and sound design are great, but the music kept cutting out randomly when it felt like it should've kept going. This ruined my immersion as it happened every time I was really getting into the atmosphere.- Bosses leave a lot to be desired. They are fine, but never feel like they reach their full potential. I didn't really feel any tension fighting most of them, which is not a good sign for this type of game. Final boss was especially disappointing.- Leveling up and upgrade mechanics don't feel properly balanced. Weapons are extremely easy to upgrade fully, which I actually really like since it promoted experimentation, but on the flipside leveling up stats doesn't feel like it does anything. The unique upgrades you get from parrying enemies is a great mechanic, but again it feels like there either should've been less upgrades in general or more materials for upgrading. It never felt like I was truly improving my character.- The setting and aesthetic are excellent. Probably the best and most unique thing about the game. As in other similar games, the story is hard to decipher, but from what I understood I think it is pretty intriguing.- By the end of the game I was ready for to be over. For games of this style I always strive to 100% it and see most of what the game offers, but for this one I didn't have that urge to backtrack and explore every nook and cranny I missed like I had in Hollow Knight or Blasphemous.As a whole Grime is a solid metroidvania, but it is plagued with too many issues to call it more than that or for me to come back to.

_childDocuments_.review: Im really enjoying this game so far, So far I have killed 3 main bosses a number of hidden mini bosses and have explored many areas. Fast travel points are very, very rare to come across. So far, I have only unlocked 3 fast travel points and I have explored more than 8 different areas of the game. _childDocuments_.review: The game is phenomenal. It looks great, the bosses are fun (for the most part) and the combat is... passable, and the level up mechanic is well implemented.The worst part about the game from a gameplay standpoint is how you heal, or rather, how you get the heal juice.To get the ability to heal, you must parry. This is a good concept on paper, but in execution it's abhorrent. For one, you can't parry a good majority of the bosses, thus resulting in no consistent, reliable healing. Two, you must parry a certain number of times to get enough juice to heal.It would be to the game's benefit if the healing acted more like Hollow Knight's: you get heal juice simply from dealing melee damage.Another thing, although I personally am not very far into NG+, it seems very unfair. _childDocuments_.review: ***NOTE: I did read all the patch notes from right before the new free DLC and the free DLC notes themselves, and I gotta say, I probably wouldn't be singing it's praises had I played before the free DLC. They added so much well-done stuff like new enemies and a huge new area which is all fantastic, but it's the QoL changes that really make this game shine even more. They changed so many of the issues brought to light by the community, that I actually think it's fair to dismiss all reviews prior to the Color of Rot DLC that released this month (Dec of 2022), because the complaints have most likely been fixed or at least modified, and it's effectively a different game at this point***I've been playing offline, so I'm at about 10 hours in, have a few hours left to go I believe EDIT: finished the game with 13 hours in and about 95% map completion. I play most games I can find in this genre, that of side-scrolling souls or Metroidvania games. Honestly, this is one of the best, and I don't say that lightly.Positives:- Movement is very good. The game just feels great to play, a solid mixture of slower Souls-like combat and more fluid movement abilities found in games like HK, Ori, Blasphemous, etc...though it takes a few hours to start feeling the fluid movement. By mid-end game, you're sprinting and jumping and dashing and grappling all over the place and it feels great!- Combat is more akin to Souls than most others in this genre; think Salt and Sanctuary rather than Hollow Knight. Very focused on timings and stamina management, which I personally like a lot. Also, weapon design is sick- Level design is fantastic. Tons of interconnecting paths and shortcuts, and the atmosphere is always top notch. Plenty of ways to break intended sequence, though not as much as say, Super Metroid or HK. Lots of secrets to find, and plenty of backtracking rewards such as new armor sets and weapons.- Mid to late game platforming feels great. Plenty of movement abilities that make traversing the world feel really good and offers plenty of fun platforming challenges that actually get quite hard near the end. This is a pro for me, but it may not be for you, if you don't like challenging platforming.- Enemy design is great, LOTS of totally unique enemies, not re-skins, and they're all very well designed both in looks and in move set.- The Prey system for traits is freaking sweet. The traits are usually very meaningful too, most are not "gain X percent damage", but are rather things that actually change the combat in fairly significant ways, which is great.I don't know if I really have any major negatives to be honest, but some minor ones: - When I first started the game, there was a bug with the controller but they fixed it in literally 2 days. At the time of this writing, they have already released two patches for the free DLC update that fixed a ton of issues and 10 hours in, I haven't encountered any bugs after the first patch; still, there may be some minor ones in the coming weeks that they're sure to fix quickly so be aware and read forums before purchasing.- I think there's a few spots where enemies pop out at you and they're hidden in the environment so it feels a little cheap but it's not often.- Some of the rewards for platforming or backtracking challenges are a bit lame, like usable items that I'm guessing most people don't use. I would say 70% of the rewards are good like armor or weapons, but considering the challenge on some of these parts, I wish it was more like 95%. This is a minor issue though, as I find the platforming challenges to be fun, so my time wasn't wasted regardless.-  A few traps in the game have hitboxes that are hard to judge, but you don't encounter them often outside of one area.- Map is generally fine, and they let you place a few markers, but I think it would be beneficial to mark vendors on the map as well.- I don't care that much about the story, but your mileage may vary, as I generally don't care about the story in these types of games, it's all about the gameplay for me.Maybe this game was just made for people like me who love all the systems they implemented, slower, methodical combat, fluid movement, lots of parrying in combat, interesting enemy design...all things I love to death. It just happens to do them all very well. If you read my other reviews, you will see that I try to be as fair and objective as I can, and I am not afraid to explain my concerns with a game, so me giving this game a 9/10 is quite an impressive accomplishment for the devs.I will be recommending this game in the same breath as Salt and Sanctuary and Blasphemous, and might just mention this one first.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of consistency issues, especially with hitboxes and parry windows. The parry mechanic plays a huge role in combat, but the parry window varies wildly between enemies. Some windows are large, others are tiny, and they can happen at different points in the enemy’s attack animation—sometimes at the start, sometimes right before you’re hit, and in rare cases, even a few frames after the attack connects.Enemies also have inconsistencies with the hitbox and shockwave effects of their attacks. Sometimes, you’ll be standing inside the dust from a shockwave and not take any damage, while other times you’ll be outside it and still get hit. I think this explains why some attacks don’t visually touch your character but still land.In this game, your strength comes from your skill. The character is very fragile, healing is limited, and there’s little room for error. So when a core mechanic like parrying is poorly implemented, it really drags down the gameplay experience.Another big issue is the beacon system. I struggle with navigating 2D games, but even so, I end up mentally mapping the whole area before I even find a beacon. By the time I reach it, I’ve already explored everything

_childDocuments_.review: This is a spoiler-free review. I will only touch on information that is gathered during the prologue and tutorial section of the game.GRIME is a brutal 2D side-scrolling platformer with clear inspirations from games such as Hollow Knight, Dark Souls and Castlevania to name a few. The grim aesthetic of the world ,coupled with the overall feeling of self-loathing and hatred, that emanates from every facet from start to end. Many have called this game “a hidden gem", but does it live up to the hype?GRIME takes place in a world that is being torn to pieces by unstable energies. A power known as Breath gives birth to new life, but is unable to create everyone equal due to its instability. The creatures are born ugly and malformed, and it is through this force that your character enters the story.You play as The Chiselled One, a perfect creation surrounded by misshapen creatures, born with a black hole for a head. The character soon becomes aware that their only purpose in this world is to consume life. Inhabitants of this world, known as Prey, will make it easy for you as they hate you with every fibre of their being, and will continue to try and kill you until the very end of the game.As the character you will use the power of the black hole to tear your enemies asunder and consume their essence. You can also use it to absorb Breath from their broken bodies to regenerate from your injuries, through this the story begins to unravel and your destiny is revealed. GRIME is unique in its combat. Swinging your weapon blindly will only lead to you dying and having to respawn at the nearest checkpoint, which could be 10-15 minutes away. GRIME forces you to play defensively as your main ability in the game is to parry enemy attacks and use the counterattack to absorb them into yourself. You do have the ability to go on the offensive too, however it’s just not as useful as playing it slowly and cautiously. Many of the inhabitants can be overwhelmed with brute strength, but it's a good idea to become familiar with the parry mechanic as soon as you can. You have two major resources to manage in combat: Health (when emptied you die) and Force which is used as stamina to maneuver through the battlefield. I like that more and more platformers are folding in more RPG-related gameplay mechanics, as it helps to add a unique aspect to every player's experience; GRIME does this excellently, providing a plethora of weapon choices as well as different armour sets, which must first be located out in the wilderness. Equipping multiple pieces from the same set also gives your character an additional boon on top of the individual piece bonuses, so it’s worth exploring to find both weapons and armour as soon as you can. The developers put a lot of heart into designing the world, it's apparent from the moment you start the game that each zone has been dutifully crafted to be not only aesthetically pleasing but also fun to explore. With the selection of armour and weapons, comes far more thought-provoking choices in your individuality. Your character has a small repertoire of options open to him at the start of the game, but as you progress through the game world and meet bigger and stronger foes, you will absorb them and with that, all of their knowledge. You will attain vast amounts of potential skill choices from the endeavour.  I don’t get to say this enough in modern gaming, so I will relish this moment. The boss fights are sublime. Not only do they break the mindset that bosses need to be giant damage sponges, but they have added interesting and fun mechanics to coincide with the experience. Several of the bosses had me pause for a second to appreciate how intuitive their design was. I went against my better judgement upon launching the game and attempted to use a keyboard and mouse. That was a huge mistake, as the controls are clunky and delayed at the best of times. Immediately I switched to the controller, which remedied a lot of the issues I was having, but not all of them. Movement is sluggish, heavy and does not feel responsive. A concern. As many of the fights require quick reaction times. GRIME is set in a sprawling world, so being able to traverse it quickly and with ease is crucial to an enjoyable experience. The developers added an ingenious method of fast travel, in the form of “Nervepasses”, which act as fast travel stations. The only concern with this mode of transport is that the stations aren’t in beneficial locations that you are likely to return to at all. Often they are at the end of an expansive boss room, still entailing you to run long distances to get to where you need to go. In the current generation of games of this style, items seem to be critical to your experience. They can give you a quick boost that could save your life and defeat that boss you have been stuck fighting. GRIME does deliver this minimally but suffers from item usefulness in certain situations.GRIME is an undeniably gorgeous game filled to the brim with fine details and beautifully designed textures, from interactive particles and clothing physics to atmospheric features such as light blooming. Unfortunately, that is where the positives end. It is littered with game-breaking graphical bugs to the point where I couldn't finish the game. During the final boss fight, the character would get stuck in the combat platform and the only way to fix it would be to exit the game and restart. I tried this seven times and got stuck every single time.With that being said, the audio in this game is on another level. It is such a grandiose experience that it captivates from the second you start playing, where every step feels heavy and realistic, with the melodic soundtrack playing in the background to perfectly carry you from one emotion to the next.Motherboard: Z490 Vision-DRAM: 32GBCPU: i9 10900KA 3.70GHzGPU: MSI Ventus RTX 3080GRIME at Ultra settings with motion blur disabled, sat at a comfortable 60 FPS capped. Loads of bugs, both gameplay and graphical, don’t be surprised if you experience them. Plenty of game-breaking ones as well, getting stuck in the world, game crashing and unexpected graphical tearing that stops forward progression just to name a few.I loved playing GRIME, it became a serious obsession for the last couple of days (Roughly 10 hours of playtime to reach the endgame). So it truly pains me to give this such a terribly negative review. If you cannot finish a game, you can’t truly say you’ve played it. GRIME is a beautiful game, absolutely teeming with personality and character, but the profound quantity of bugs and glitches is beyond acceptable for a game of this value. Wait for this game to be patched before you invest your hard-earned money if it ever does at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Admittedly, I was not even aware of  existence a few days ago. Nevertheless, it immediately caught my interest once I browsed through its screenshots, as its dark yet beautiful visuals and the premise of delivering a surrealistic environment filled with bones and entrails was captivating enough for me. Plus, I have not played a good Metroidvania in a while, so this one seemed like the right title to satisfy my hunger for it. Surprisingly, it was way better than I expected.Let us start from the beginning, though, or rather even earlier than that, this time. By that, I mean the main menu itself. What is so interesting there? Its music reminded me of some of the orchestral compositions from the  series, to which I listen at times to this very day. That is a great first impression, I would say; luckily, it manages to keep that quality for the whole playthrough, and I have nothing but praise for the soundtrack.When you actually start the game, a confusing intro awaits and leaves you with the impression that you are just a weakling in a cave whose goal is to kill other creatures, absorb them and grow. You do not even have a weapon at the start, so you have to rely on the parry system, which happens to be one of the most crucial mechanics. Why? It replenishes your so-called Breath bar that is present instead of healing potions. Once filled up, you can use it to slowly heal yourself; this forces you to be more aggressive during the combat, and that is right up my alley.Do not be afraid, though! You will get your weapon soon enough. There is a sheer variety of those, from light, fast swords to heavy hammers, but all of them are melee-based. Sure, they have their combos and special moves, making them useful for different situations. Also, they seem to be of biological origin, as their form mutates at times. However, there are no other combat styles, such as magic. Even the role-playing mechanics and statistics are simplistic, so you will not find yourself creating distinctive builds. That is my only gripe with this title, as it does not offer enough replayability.Even though it lacks in that area, it makes up for it with its beautifully crafted interconnected environment, gripping lore and diverse enemies and bosses, which create an unforgettable experience. I cared less about the abovementioned shortcomings the more I played, and I became fully immersed in this world. does not focus much on the narrative at first but prefers to unveil its secrets slowly, so you only get tiny bits of a story at the start. Nevertheless, it works brilliantly, and I was left in awe once I witnessed how this universe actually works. The great thing is that its simple premise stays that way without getting too complicated for its own good. It is a bit difficult to describe its premise without spoiling it, so all I will say is that it revolves around the possible end of the world and how its inhabitants react to it. That might not sound original, but I enjoyed it nonetheless.What I adored even more was the overall design of the whole map. It might seem linear at the beginning, but at the end, you will witness how interconnected it is and that there are several shortcuts to find, which are crucial, as there are only a few checkpoints. Apart from that, its overall visuals make galavanting through it intriguing and even creepy at times. There might be a biological mass observing your every movement, and you might even hear it breathing at times. These surreal and anatomical aspects are not just used visually but also gameplay-wise. Due to that, it is important to pay attention to your surroundings, as those large teeth might be a deadly trap that will crush you within seconds. Or perhaps some of those lovely flowers hide an enemy within them, hoping to lure you in. I loved that, as it gave me the feeling of being in constant danger.There are also secrets lying around. Thus, exploring the environment is worth it for finding consumable items, such as boosts for your weapons’ damage or beacons that reveal your progress on the map. Apart from that, there are optional stronger foes scattered around; defeating them grants you with so-called Hunt points. You can use those for unlocking helpful bonuses, such as dealing more damage while having lower health or leaving an echo behind you after dashing, damaging the enemies who touch it. Beware that you cannot activate all of those at once, so you have to think about which ones are suitable for your playstyle. Oh, and some of those monsters even influence the environment a bit. For example, one of the creatures puts its tail into the ground, which proceeds to emerge at your latest location, forcing you to be in constant movement until you kill it.The platforming sections happen to be a significant part, as well. While they are pretty simple at first, once you get access to dash, double jump and porting at orbs, the environmental obstacles will become much harder to deal with; plus, it allows you to get to before unreachable parts and obtain those sweet rewards. Moreover, it changes the gameplay’s pace drastically, as you will suddenly become very agile, and the game will force you to deal with several traps and aggressive foes while you are trying to pull a platform towards you; also, if you are smart enough, you can use those traps to your advantage in combat. Luckily, the movement and controls are responsive and smooth, and I have never felt that I would die unfairly but rather because of my own mistakes.Due to all that I mentioned, the combat is enjoyable despite being simple. Its varied enemies and bosses will always try to surprise you, and I must especially praise the boss fights, as some of them are truly great and incredibly creative, both visual and gameplay-wise. Several of them even have the abovementioned platforming sections that spice these encounters a lot. And I must admit that I had difficulties with beating a few bosses here and there, especially with the last one, who almost pushed me to my limits. That is a positive thing to say, though, as it felt like a combination of the obstacles I had dealt with throughout my playthrough, making my frustration entertaining.All in all, I can safely recommend  to fans of Metroidvanias, as well as to those who lust for a challenging title. Even though I would prefer a bit more complex combat system, every other aspect makes up for it, creating a thrilling fourteenth-hour long adventure to overcome. Honestly, I did not expect that I would be surprised that much, but here I stand corrected.
_childDocuments_.name: GRIME

_childDocuments_.review: This game goes on the list of games that stands shoulder to shoulder with some of the greats.I commend the developers for continuing to update and patch the game. I know that the console versions, Switch especially, may have outstanding bugs, but I have full belief that the developers will work on fixing what the last dlc of the game broke. I did not have a bug during gameplay that caused frustration or detracted from the experience.So, where do I even begin with this amazing game? It's advertised as a metroidvania and it succeeds in having a diverse world full of secrets. It uses combat mechanics and staples that Dark Souls popularized as a transparent suit and tie, but instead of copying outright, it expands upon those systems and encourages extremely aggressive play. The parry-riposte centric gameplay is a nice change of pace from games that force you to constantly roll or dash through enemies... I greatly appreciate being able to pace the momentum of a fight if I have the skill for it.This game is contender for the most unique play style weapons in a metroidvania to me. Every weapon I picked up had a fabulous new special attack to play around with that changed up how I interact with enemies and bosses. Lanterns bring a whole new play style that accentuates interacting with bosses in ways that aren't just slapping them silly if used with a weapon that benefits from lantern stacks in the offhand.The prey system reminds me of the Sorrow  line of Castlevania games a lot. Killing certain enemies through parries enough times unlocks an ability related to their form that you can then use to complement your build. With an old update that swapped two preys around, managing early stamina is quite easy- just invest into the parrying returns force prey that you can get directly at the start of the game. One point should be enough.The bosses in this game are cinematic masterpieces. They are so well animated that watching the game in motion truly makes the world seem like a living art piece. Getting to a boss always feels like a sweet reward at the end of every unique area, the cherry on top of all the sweet loot you've picked up along the way. It's worth noting that this is one of the only metroidvanias out there where NG+ actually does something unique to the game world. Every single enemy and boss has new attack patterns or even phases, greatly mixing up every single encounter you'll have through the world on the second playthrough. The addition of mechanics that didn't exist in the first playthrough like Breathearts and Sanguine Ichor add further ways to carve out a build in your own unique way. The NG+ exclusive boss is an ABSOLUTE SPECTACLE, and it is worth doing a second playthrough alone.If the developers read this, please add the Dreamborn Nightmare's weapon into the game. Maybe as a reward for going through ALL NG+ rewards of it. I know, I know- you said you were done. ...But you can't just be done!!! Not until I have the ability to use that kickass weapon in the game!!!

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, but I sadly can’t give it a favorable review. I enjoyed it at the beginning and I liked the challenge, but the more you play the more tedious and frustrating Grime becomes. It doesn’t respect the player’s time – it doesn’t have a proper teleportation system and checkpoints are too sparse, which really puts a damper on exploration. I gave up close to the end as the game started feeling too much like a chore.
_childDocuments_.name: GRIME

_childDocuments_.review: Just... WOW. After more than thirty hours playing the game, I have just finished my first playthrough. And I say first because I know I will be playing more times. Got the most basic ending, and there were several points during my journey where I knew I could have done different (one of them very early on). Not only because of the story: as many other reviewers have mentioned there is a very wide array of weapons, armour sets and abilities to try. You can change at any point, but I like sticking with one combination.This is quite possibly the best metroidvania/action exploration game I have ever played, and I'm an enthusiast of this genre so it's hard to live up to my tastes after so many permutations and variations on the theme. The design of monsters, NPCs and areas, the soundtrack, the challenging but fair gameplay (although I have to admit there were several times when the platforming got a little too annoying or frustrating for me), the intriguing and obscure storyline/lore and the VERY satisfying exploration make it truly spectacular on every category I can think of. By the way, the blend of traditional metroidvania and the more modern soulslike elements is done masterfully too.So all in all a big thumbs up and now I'm eagerly awaiting Grime 2 with bated breath.
_childDocuments_.name: GRIME

_childDocuments_.review: GRIME is Game of the Year.I haven't been floored by a game like this since Cuphead. There's a level of polish here in the visuals, soundtrack and combat that shouldn't be possible from a studio doing this for the first time, but Clover Bite (and Alex Roe, shoutout to the composer) have made a real name for themselves with what I can only describe as a masterpiece of game design. GRIME perfectly straddles that line of "tough-but-fair", a line that many games attempt to draw but fail miserably at. The boss fights are difficult, but I ended up fighting each one in one sitting until I finally beat them. The game is that polished and that addicting. The sweeping orchestra and choir of the score, the intricate, entertaining character designs and interactions, the boss fights that reward you for going back in and trying time and time again until you get the satisfaction of seeing "GREAT PREY CRUSHED" splayed across your screen, all of it makes for an immensely gripping experience that I could go back and play time and time again. I could talk about this game for hours on end, but I'll leave it at this for now: I'm so excited for more GRIME content and to see what else Clover Bite has to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: GRIME

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is the first steam review I've ever bothered to leave here and I'm leaving it because I felt it was really deserved. I've always been a huge fan of metriodvania style games, and nearly a year ago Grime came onto my radar. Unfortunately, my computer at the time was a potato and could barely run the demo so I moved on with my life until this month. I finally got my new rig set up, saw the demo still in my game library and figured, "hell, I'll give it a try." I was enormously pleased to see this game had been getting free content updates in the time since I first tried it. I haven't heard much chatter about Grime at all since it's launch and the fact that the developers have been passionately chipping away at improving their art with community feedback put this at the top of my list. I must say, wow, really excellent job guys. The premise and concept of the world and it's characters had me interested from the get go. The little hints at the nature of my player character and it's meta narrative in relation to myself, the player, was handled with a clear understanding of the subtly necessary to pull off this FromSoftware-style world that rewards exploration, community discussion, and careful personal consideration not only of the small bits of lore text littered throughout the game, but of the mechanics that embody and support the lore. The gameplay itself felt really responsive and considered, and I felt I had a pretty consistent level of challenge throughout. There was no boss I cleared first try, learning their pattern was a must, and nothing felt like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. I loved pushing the boundaries of exploration at every turn and barely getting myself to a checkpoint with little health and most resources spent. The platforming maintained a comparable level of difficulty to the combat throughout most of the game as well and I enjoyed the challenge. I look forward to seeing how much sequence breaking is available for a 2nd playthrough, usually my go to 2nd playthrough objective in games like these.Great job, I so look forward to whatever these developers do next!
_childDocuments_.name: GRIME

_childDocuments_.review: If you like dark souls and metroidvania games, this one is nearly a no brainer. The game is good: solid, unforgiving combat, good level progression, woefully beatifull and unique world building and fitting soundtrack. It has amazingly designed boss fights that are trully a sight to behold and play... overall excellent game. The only drawback i get from my playthrough is severe however: the game features an insane amount of secret rooms and hard to get places, most of which can only be accesed after attaining certain powerups, mixed with a platforming style that is good enough but can feel really obnoxious every now and then. Because of this two combined, backtracking is really time consuming and very slow and frustrating, also, very convoluted map design. Other than this nitpicking, go for it.
_childDocuments_.name: GRIME

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent game, and my favorite metroidvania since Hollow Knight (which is my favorite game of all time). Grime gets a lot of things right - the combat is satisfying, the hunt and absorb mechanics are unique, the art direction is incredible, and lastly the boss fights are a rush. The game does feel a bit unpolished sometimes - it's hard to pinpoint it, but it lacks the finesse you feel playing Hollow Knight or Ori. Overall, if you're a fan of metroidvanias, you'll love this game. Definitely looking forward to Clover Bite's next release.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like souls-like and Metroidvanias its pretty simple, this game is great and you'll love it. Responsive controls, cool abilities that add to to mobility and give you more options in combat, an expansive list of weapons and armor, and a fun trait system. The enemy variety was large enough that I felt like I never ran out of new things to fight. Plus the bosses, for the most part, were always a challenging yet rewarding experience, not to mention looked incredible.  If you need a bit more selling, the game has some of the most beautiful set pieces and background I've seen in a game in a while. The music was fantastic. Despite all the good i have to say about the game there is a little bit of jank every now and then, that i would be remiss to ignore. Certain attacks can feel cheap at time, with little to no time to react, yet it was over shadowed by the fun i found the rest of the time. All in all incredible, since 100%ing the game i wish there was more i could do. totally recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Good value for money metroidvania souls-like at times hardcore platformer.Grime has disturbing visuals, a barely comprehensible "plot", competent combat and mostly solid foundations.There's a good variety of weapons, but the play style will remain largely the same: You attack in 2D, mostly from melee range. You have different attacks, but this core concept never changes. There is no ranged class, no magic to speak of.Enemy design is LARGELY alright. There are a few really stupid ones, especially in combination, i.e. "kill rooms".The level design is mostly fine as well, though I am so not a fan of having to find a "map marker" first, before the parts you've explored actually get revealed. This is needless frustration, especially when you come back to the game after a little while and are hopelessly lost. Even with the updates that leave little "lines/dots" on the blank map this is my biggest gripe about the game.My 2nd big gripe is the way healing works, because essentially it doesn't. At least in the beginning you're given ONE healing charge. The only way to refill that charge is to "parry" enemies. Parrying is an essential part of the game (until it isn't, of course, because inconsistency is so much fun...) and you NEED to learn it. Otherwise don't bother playing. It's technically possible to get to the final boss without parrying once I think, but that would be prime material for a challenge run. Parrying, for the most part, is relatively easy as well. Only some enemies (see above) have really stupid attacks that are a pain to parry. After 4 successful parries (absorbs) you can heal one more time. A parry will automatically consume all the red health of an enemy, so it's just worth doing, but there's always a risk, of course.Later on in the game you get more healing options, especially once the traits kick in and you get health back with every parry/absorb. But until that point ... it's a slog. Exploration is fine for the most part, but I always hate it when games present you with "death drops" you just can't see. Because half of the time you HAVE to go down there, but good luck figuring out where exactly to drop without dying.The aforementioned traits are basically your skill tree. You defeat strong enemies to get points, you absorb enemies to unlock said traits, then you invest them ... and you can also refund them. To an extent at least. The good news is that this offers some much needed flexibility. The bad news is that your traits can be absolutely worthless in many circumstances. For the final boss I just respecced, because there was no way (that I could discern) to parry him and thus heal some life back.The equipment mechanic ties in seamlessly with this system. There are 3 items you can equip. Only the set will give you the corresponding bonus for specific traits. If you've not invested points in a trait, there's no need to wear that armor set, but you can set them as cosmetics, which is nice.Now, the real highlight of Grime are the bosses. It's one of the few 2D games these days with almost perfect boss design (with some exceptions). Pretty much every boss has a varied, but mostly fair move set. To defeat them, all you have to do is learn that moveset and react appropriately. With some bosses they went a bit overboard with the effects and things that happen simultaneously. And I would be lying if I didn't curse the devs a few times, but ultimately even I was able to get through every boss in the game without cheating (NG+ excluded), and I'm really not that good. A big part of that is also weapon choice. Some weapons are dope for fighting regular enemies, but they suck ass vs many bosses. Either they're too slow, don't deal enough damage or cost too much stamina. And stamina cost is a BIG factor in this game.Once you're done there's NG+ to explore with new and improved enemies and bosses apparently, but I don't have the stomach for that. At least not right now. I just mention it, because the updates are all free and give you more play time. A first play through should be between 10 to 20 hours, depending on how much you explore or how often you fail. I think I beat every boss in under 10 tries, so your mileage may of course vary. As with every other souls-like, you can "farm" here as well to get a bit stronger. And at least you don't lose all your hard-earned stuff when you die ... only your multiplier.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated review (as of 14 Aug 2021 Patch):I've decided to switch my review to a recommended, as the dev appears to be really striving to adjust the kinds of things that are a severe detriment to the game, and is listening to community feedback on it.  Even if it takes another patch or two, I think this will end up a great game.Warning for potential buyers though - there is a lot of frustration to be had currently in the game, but even if this is all addressed it will still be frustrating (but the good kind of frustrating), and it will still be hard.  So if you like hard games with plenty to challenge you, this might be your jam.Similarly, if you are a fan of metroidvanias, I think this will be worth your time.Original Review and Update 01:Soulless.______Update:After re-starting, and putting in a fair bit more time into the game, I still cannot recommend it at present.  If they can tighten up the controls, deal with the glitches, deal with the enemy tracking, deal with the hitboxes, deal with the bugs and stuttering, and sort out the balancing a bit I'd recommend it.There is a spark of something special in here for sure, but absolutely nothing about the game's narrative or atmosphere drew me in at all.  Nothing made me care about progressing further at any point.  There were more maddening moments that made me want to quit because of awful controls and mean design than there were maddening moments that made me want to git gud.  A huge amount of the time I felt robbed by encounters, troll-traps, pitch-black areas, pitfalls, etc., rather than feel like it was just me being crap.For context, I'm a huge fan of metroidvanias, a huge fan of Soulsborne games, and I like a good challenge all around.  I don't mind having my skills put to the test, and there are times when I just keep getting beaten in many games and I don't seem to be getting further in them but I still really enjoy myself.  This game doesn't have that vibe for me.The point where I've decided to stop playing for time's sake is the "FP" boss fight.  I like the idea, but the execution coupled with the hit points and the clunky controls just make it feel like a cheap attempt to really wall off the end of the game.  It should be difficult, but this whole fight (along with the controls) needs tightening up and re-balancing.Other areas which really need looking at are the armour and weapons, and the stats.  I honestly never really noticed any difference as I went through the game when it came to the impact my stats had on performance.  So why on earth have you walled off the weapons and not put in a re-spec ability?  There's no benefit to any of the armour, so why not make the weapons the same way?  Otherwise you're stuck, and if you opted to level the way I did on my initial blind attempt, you'll end up either having to grind (not a chance I'm doing that in a game I don't really enjoy), or restart.  That really sucks, and removes the drive to hunt down new weapons and armour as you can't use 90% of the weapons and the armour does absolutely nothing except look "interesting".I'm not going to keep harping on about all the negatives, as if the things I've mentioned above are addressed it would become a recommended game.  The biggest thing I think the game has in its favour is the art style.  The visuals remind me of things like the old tv show Lexxx, and the old game Planescape Torment.  It is a cool setting, and even if the story did absolutely nothing for me it might for other people.  I think it may have done more for me had all the other issues not been present that constantly took me out of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: First game ever I wanted to finish, and actually did on NG+You can beat the whole game just parrying attacks.Parrying in Grime is extremely satisfying. Like biting a cold watermelon on a hot ass day: crunchy, explosive, full of intense flavor of victory and dopamine pumps.Game feels alive and truly makes you feel like an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ (or a god, which are practically the same thing) once you realize what's going on. Wish they'd give you teleporting much sooner. Thank you for that. Map is not the best, but also not the complete bafoonery of hollow knight. But which metrodvania has a perfect map?Sidenote: Why you gotta make this ♥♥♥♥ cryptic? It's a MAP!  I want maximum zoom level of Google maps style map in metrodvanias. When will we see a developer so confident in their game that map will give players full and unobstructed view of the world? Binding of isaac has a better ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ map than most metrodvanias 🤣No way to experiment and play with all the weapons as respec is very rare and expensive. Why don't devs just chill on this in general?Best idea since grappling hook -- cosmetics gear! Pick one set of gear for stats, and also wear whatever you want for the looks. Please make this mandatory in all games. Open paths sometimes lead you to places where you have no business being at, but I look at it as more of a "natural" wall rather than an "ability" wall. Don't know why I used quotation marks there.Music balance could have been much better. Sometimes it feels like the tracks and audio were just thrown like vegetables into a salad. Hopefully for grime 2 they will find a person with skillful ears to master it. Because this OST slaps.I played Grime last year when all the content came out, zero issues with performance. Just finished Prince of the Persia the Lost Crown. Grime is much better, smarter, tighter, more alive and challenging. Also black hole for your head.Final boss Sophie's choice fork is wonderful. I wonder how many people carried on with what's offered.

_childDocuments_.review: Just defeated the final boss and saw last moments of the game.Those are literally stunning and gorgeous. I'm glad I beat the game to witness that. Developers did really good job on that one and the game altogether, epecially, as i get it, there are only 3 of them.Grime rightfully takes it's well-dserved place in the row of the best modern post-Hollow Kinght metroidvanias.It is definitely most difficult of them all (not including Hollow knight itself) and has the best visual component.Especially I want to mark out the bosses. What is a good boss? He has to:1) be good looking (understand this as you will)2) be close to a bonfire3) have decent number of attacks4) those attacks must be very well telegraphed, so player can learn and realise every time, where  his mistakes take place, so he could get good5) Damage and health should be on the level, where you can neither face tank him, nor is he a bullet sponge.All those properties Grime's bosses do possess, but there are also 3 ''real deal bosses'', who don't mess around, and will take out of you all your wit, skill and patience, and reward you at the end with a solid dophamine shot, called ''omfg i did it''.Of course, there always are things, that can be better. Devs are very active on this forum, reacting pronto to people's issues, making the game better as i write this.So, if you are a metroidvania fan, or up to a rewarding challenge - this one is sure for you

name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale
detailed_description: Chicory: A Colorful Tale is a top-down adventure game in a coloring book world where you can draw on anything. Use your painting powers to explore new places, solve puzzles, help your friends, and change the world! Something terrible happened. Chicory, superstar artist and wielder of the Brush , is missing, and all the color in the land vanished with her. It’s up to you, Chicory’s number one fan, to pick up the Brush and fill in for her. It’s a big job… but you’re ready for it! Probably! Explore the Picnic Province, and paint on anything! Solve puzzles and manipulate the environment with paint. Unlock new paint abilities and use them to reach new places. Dress up how you want with collectible clothes, plants, and furniture. Discover a world full of 100+ animal characters. Experience 10+ hours of gameplay and dozens of side quests including mail delivery, art classes, photo taking, and more. Play with your friends and paint together in local co-op! Featuring audio design by Em Halberstadt and A Shell in the Pit (Untitled Goose Game, Night in the Woods) And an original soundtrack by Lena Raine ! (Celeste, Minecraft)

_childDocuments_.review: A truly heartwarming experience. The characters are very sweet, and I found some of the struggles from the characters relatable. The world is fun to interact with, it is larger than it seems, and hides multiple secrets. I enjoyed collecting everything from the game. The puzzles themselves are not mindblowing, but just enough that you can pretty quick know what you have to do without becoming tedious at all.The only part I found a bit frustrating was completing all the art classes to get one of the achievements. Some were fun, but there were too many for my taste. But they are optional for the main story, so not really a complaint :)

_childDocuments_.review: I first wanted to play this game because I liked the idea of being able to colour the environments the way you want + I really liked the artstyle. I wasn't prepared for the game to resonate so much with me when it started tackling the problems the characters where going through... It's something I tend to struggle with, so seeing a game adressing this issue helped me empathize even more with the characters, be it Chicory or the MC.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty much everything I could've hoped for!!! Relaxing, fun, creative, and interesting from start to finish. The music and sound design are spectacular and set the mood very well, the characters and writing are charming and memorable, and the game explores so many cool concepts and mechanics. And of course the whole concept of being able to paint the world around you is pretty unique and satisfying on its own! The base Zelda-like design is also executed perfectly, and the boss fights really caught me off guard.The only thing I would warn someone looking to pick this up is to not expect a difficult game. There are some interesting puzzles and getting to some areas requires thinking, and there's tons to explore and secrets to find, but most of the enjoyment I got out of this game was from interacting with the characters and drawing stuff around the world. If you're okay with that, then GET THIS GAME!Thank you to the devs for all their hard work and for putting this out into the world.P.S. This isn't related to the game itself, but the Kickstarter was super well-done. It's really hard to run a good Kickstarter campaign, but Greg and the team were always on top of communicating progress and answering people's questions! I'm very glad to have backed this.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Chicory was a really sweet, enjoyable game! The painting was a little tedious to me at first but after unlocking other brush styles/ways of coloring it got a lot more fun. The world was super fun to explore and the story was really lovely. If you play, I highly suggest exhausting all dialogue with all characters; they had a lot of insightful stuff to say. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: I 100 percented this game and I did enjoy it! I liked the food theme, the unlocking of all the little clothes and brushes, it was fun! My favorite part has to be how focused the game is on letting you play how you want. You can skip every cutscene if you want, which is standard, but you can also completely skip the boss battles and be fine and get to continue the story. I really liked that! I personally played the battles, though I did change in the settings how many hits it would take to down me (you can make it harder or literally baby proof yourself so you can just focus on having fun and the battle dialogue!) The characters were so cute, and I found myself really enjoying the art classes. I will say painting the world itself was sometimes tedious, mostly because it is literally impossible to make things exactly how you want, like fill in every speck of white, or make everything the color you want. Like if you choose green grass and a red flower, sometimes the flower will leave a detached red dot on the grass, which is frustrating, and goes for furniture inside too.  It's also hard to adjust to having such a small color pallet in each area but honestly I got used to it, and they do change that a bit as you progress.My favorite thing to color was the caves though, the paint glows so nice and it made the rest of the paint pale in comparison. But overall yeah fun game!
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: This game has really touched me in a profound way. I wasn't sold on the coloring aspect through much of the game, but the mechanics are tight and the puzzles are numerous and clever. A lot of love was involved when developing the layout so that you can keep going back to previous places to utilize your newly unlocked skills. It 100% has the gameplay to make a fun game (there may be some missed opportunities using the brush, andd different colors) but the story is what takes it to the next level where I actively want to recommend this game to friends and family.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed a lot of aspects of this game. The music by Lena Raine (Celeste) is fantastic. The gameplay was relaxing, but engaging. While painting everything is completely optional, there are a lot of tricks and tools the game provides to prevent it from becoming tedious. Plus, it's a nice way to make the world feel like it's something you're invested in - especially since characters will occasionally stop by and admire your work. The story is very charming and shared a lot of themes with the creators' previous game, Wandersong.Highly recommend if you like relaxing games with great writing.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Chicory is the perfect heart-wrenching game if you are an artist. It touches on a lot of anxieties and stresses that I think a lot of artists can relate to. Gameplay-wise, it's super fun! It teaches each new mechanic well. The art classes are a little tedious for 100%-ing, but are interesting and rewarding to listen to the students discuss and also explore art techniques. I've played this probably 3 times over now and only just finished it 100% but all the little side quests and storylines make it worth it :) (also fashion and decorating my house)
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game overall; aesthetics were spectacular. Exploring the overworld made me want to play Stardew Valley lol. Puzzles were all quite clever too. Never a dull moment in the exploration.The boss fights were a little hit-and-miss (though the techniques themselves tended to be quite clever), and the way hitpoints (didn't really seem to) work made me feel like I was basically just invincible, which worked against the fun of the fight a bit.The themes of the game were spectacular as well; I thought the central message got a little sloppily communicated in the endgame, but overall I think it all worked out just fine. I also appreciated the diverse character personalities (shoutout to the wonderful jab at capitalism lol).In the end, I would strongly recommend this game for anyone looking for a charming puzzle-based adventure game to fill their weekend with; I look forward to pursuing full completion in this game, as well as seeing what other creations the makers have in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: This game handles the themes of creation and depression with the peacefulness of a coloring book, the whimsy of a Paper Mario game, and a sincerity that only the Celeste and Wandersong team can achieve. While its mix of gameplay styles may not satisfy everyone, Chicory's commitment to self-expression and affirmation can make this a wonderful experience for almost anybody. Send this to your artist friends, your creative friends, your anxious friends, and maybe remind them how much they mean to you.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: I love love love this game and have completed it 3 times so far. It has a lovely and endearing art style, cool sound effects, and beautiful music. It has a relatable story and an important message, even if you don't consider yourself to be an "artist" I still highly recommend you give it a try. It's AMAZING! at least in my eyes
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: This is it. MY perfect game. Something I never knew I wanted, but I'm so happy I got.Something that entered my radar not too long ago and left me utterly enthralled.It's not just a coloring book. It's a coloring book for the SOUL.This game is a love letter to all the creatives out there that struggle with "wielding" their own creative energies.To all the people that are left misunderstood, thrusted into rigid systems and power structures with little care for their well-being. This is a game with and for GAY ANIMALS. I feel utterly seen, and I never want to leave this world. I don't think there's been a game that's done this to me before or since.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Between a deep and touching story, not-too-difficult-to-find collectables, and strong game mechanics, Chicory is perhaps a perfect game. Everything you experience was obviously loved by the creators and time and effort was put into each detail. This may have become my new favorite game (at least sharing the podium with Portal). If you like coloring, puzzles, cute characters, and a game that wants its players to succeed, I recommend picking this one up.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably one of the cutest, most charming games I've ever played, with such an important message for any creatives out there... The characters feel fleshed out and have personality, from the main characters to that one mouse that keeps getting lost. The mechanics are easy to understand and I made myself laugh at just how bad I was at colouring, despite all the NPCs telling me otherwise. This game is oozing with personality and charm and it's easy to see just how much love went into the entire experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

Highly recommended.
