_childDocuments_.review: While charming and light in nature, the gameplay loop is tedious to the point of monotony. Solve some puzzles using your abilities, fight a boss by dodging its attacks while painting it with a brush and then have a conversation with an NPC, rinse and repeat. The collecting is cynical in the extreme with items gathered for the reward of getting more items that have no use to the player other than to exist. I get it, Chicory is a game about art and celebrates creativity, but not for its own sake!There are better, more entertaining action adventure games out there, don't buy this.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, where do I start? I cannot begin to describe how special I found this game. I really didn't expect that much of it, I just thought the mechanics and art style were cool. What I didn't know was how touching the story would be, and how much it would have an impact on me as an artist. It talks about heavily about imposter syndrome and doubting yourself as an artist, and a person. Chicory's struggles can be heavily related to, and I found the dialogue between characters really sweet and touching (and sometimes funny!). There's such a charm to the world and how it is introduced to the player, I love that you can make the world look however you like and just go crazy with it, including the menu screen.The mechanics were really fun and the puzzles were not too difficult. Sometimes I needed a few hints but I also think i'm just bad lol. The boss fights helped break up the calmness and I like that you don't really fail should you get hit too many times because again, I'm bad. The music is a huge plus! The song that you (I called her Katsu) and Chicory sing at the top of the mountain is so sweet, I loved its reprise at the end of the game. I also loved that if you 100% the game, you can read little messages from the devs, it was a really nice way to finish the game. Overall, if you're thinking of picking this up, you absolutely should. This game had me laughing, smiling and crying. It really was such a joyful experience, thank you to the devs for making it <3

The soundtrack was phenomenal, I would be able to sit in the menu for hours listening purely to the soundtrack.The boss fights were simplistic in the terms of being easy, although every boss that you faced was always different and introduced new mechanics.The story is an absolute eye-opener, with a heartwarming story. _childDocuments_.review: An actually incredible game. The gameplay is fun and so unique, the whole world is literally a coloring book for you to fill in and the game gives you a reason to with multiple different powers that let you traverse and pick up collectibles and talk to people. The music is incredible, made by Lena Raine, the same person who made the soundtrack for Celeste and loads of other things; overall a very talented composer who manages to get the mood perfect in every soundtrack she's worked on, and this is no exception. The game is also very accessible, it's a simple and easy game with fun puzzles, and the game encourages you to embrace your artistic flare even if you aren't necessarily good at art or drawing; that's even a main concept for the story of the game. Speaking of the story, I won't get into any spoilers, but the story is probably the best part of the game. I personally adored the drawing gameplay, but the story is so intricate, meaningful, and touches on a lot of deeper topics that more things should talk about and does so in such an excellent way. It's also very clear that the team who worked on this cared so much about the story and getting the whole game absolutely perfect in its own imperfect way. I would say this might be one of my favorite stories in a game that I have played, probably ever, the characters are unique and both add to the story and feel like people with their own struggles rather than set pieces in an environment, i could talk for a while on this but I really shouldn't, just play the game yourself.Coming out of this game after 100%ing it, I can safely say this is one of my favorite games to have played through and experienced, though it does feel like it doesn't have that much replayability after 100% as you've seen everything and this is a very story-based game, but this game doesn't need infinite content, that's part of why the game is so good, it doesn't outstay its welcome, it stays long enough to allow you to experience it and enjoy it, but not too long to make it feel old or boring. So yeah, this game is great, would go out of my way to experience the story again if possible. Also if you enjoyed this game, you should play Wandersong, it was made by some of the people who made this game and is good in very similar ways, that game is also one of my favorite games but it's so hidden and I think more people should experience it.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Oh heck yes do I recommend this game. It didn't catch me for a while at first, and I sort of blame that on playing the demo earlier. Once I delved a bit deeper I was hooked. Much like their previous game wandersong, its a less cut and dry adventure, with some incrediblyt touching moments. Its full of humor, sadness, and a swathe of emotions in between. One of my favorite mechanics (also in wandersong), is that your core controls are available when in conversation. Want to decorate the pizza shop while the owner complains about a lack of business? Go ahead! It really keeps the story moving a long without being disruptive. Another standout is the incredible music. Take a look at "Chicory: The Sounds of Picnic Provence" on bandcamp. Lena Raine is remarkable at subtly shifting a tone to paint a broader aural picture.Just go play it. There are surprises at every turn.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Chicory is a coloring book/puzzle/adventure game where you have to color in the world around you. A simple concept that is very creative and well-executed!The game makes some clever design choices that limit what you can create (the biggest one being that each area only has 4 available colors). Those choices encourage you to be creative with your options without being discouraged by what you can or can't do. I'm not an artist, but even I have been able to create color palettes and art pieces that I'm proud of. And that's what Chicory is all about. Showing you that you don't have to be the best to be good enough. Sometimes, just putting in the work and being genuine is what really counts. This ties in with the story's themes of artist's block and imposter's syndrome, and I adore anything that uses game mechanics to make the player feel what the characters are feeling. Also this game has the car frog from Mother 3 in it. what more do you need?

_childDocuments_.review: Chicory: A Colorful Tale will unleash your sense of creativity in ways you never thought possible, and along the way carry you through an endearing tale of self-discovery.  I’m going to give you three reasons why you need to play Chicory.Watch my 7 minute review here: 1-The writing and character development are hands down some of the best I have ever had the pleasure of experiencing.  And I’m going to say something that might offend you, but it rivals Undertale.  Chicory utilizes some very similar textual styles to Undertale, in that each character, no matter how many you encounter in the world, has its own distinct voice, communicated through text cadence, font style, vocabulary, and so on.2-Chicory is a closet metroidvania, and it’s something I truly did not expect.  I came into Chicory expecting a strong narrative focus, lots of dialogue and exploration, but not nearly as much as there is here.  So what makes this a metroidvania?  Well, to be fair, it’s not a pure metroidvania since it’s not 2D, but it does have an expanding and discoverable world, with certain areas being gated until new powers are granted.  As the world expands and you discover more of Picnic Province, with it’s charming area names like Teatime Meadows, Sips River, Elevenses, and so on, you’ll also discover some mysterious ways of getting around, either spotting narrow gaps in walls, cracks to be exploited, twisting vines going up and down cliffs, but until you’ve reached certain points in the game, these areas are gated.3-Incredible sound design.  As Lena Raine does, she has crafted a charming soundtrack in Chicory, one that changes gradually as you move through the world, but one that always remains lovely, whimsical, and most of all catchy.  Within an hour or two, I found myself humming along to the music, even when I stepped away from the game to grab more tea, and it hit me in those moments just how quickly the soundtrack was making an impression on me.There are my three reasons why you need to play Chicory, and I didn’t even get to talk about all the awesome collectibles you can find and wear, how you can color them and every character, building, tree and plant you encounter, and so much more.  Chicory is a masterpiece, whose individual strokes of genius compound to create a sight to behold, a feast for the eyes and ears, and one that I imagine will be held as a standard for creativity and storytelling for years to come.

_childDocuments_.review: Chicory: A Colorful Tale is a fun and charming top-down adventure game from indie developer Greg Lobanov. It’s a classic “don’t judge a book by its cover” scenario in that the visual styling may be simple, but the story features a multilayered depth. It tackles very important topics of mental health that I’m sure we can all resonate with. If nothing else, it’s a great opportunity to learn about how others might be feeling beneath the surface. This is all wrapped up in a therapeutic and fun colouring game with a powerful soundtrack. The initial premise this fairly simple you take on the mantle of the Wielder and, with the power of the Brush, bring colour back to the world. As you traverse the province of Picnic, you’ll meet friends, family, and neighbours. Taking on challenging puzzles as you explore the mysteries behind the corruption. Oh, and there’s a bunch of Earthbound references for good measure. Don’t be fooled by the charming art style as Chicory: A Colorful Tale contains a depth and challenge that might come as a surprise.The dominant theme running throughout the story and interactions with its characters centre around mental health. As the Wielder, you bring back colour to the world and there’s a lot of worried residents to reassure. The world suddenly becoming void of all colour would be a shock to anyone. With the rightful Wielder’s whereabouts currently unknown, you take a lot of flak from residents. A lot of the interactions you have with people are tough. Their ability to cope with the sudden loss of colour has shaken them mentally. You listen, learn and help in whatever way they ask. Most of the time, that means progressing with the game. Not everyone is so dour, however, some are just happy to get back on with life colour or not. While there’s a wide spectrum of characters to interact with and most of the interactions can be very impactful. There’s an unfortunate downside in that there can be too much dialogue. It’s praiseworthy to have every interaction be unique throughout the game, but the meaningful moments of dialogue happen only a few times per character. The rest is made up of endless waffling. What makes it unfortunate is you need to exhaust all dialogue scenarios to either progress or obtain items needed for perfect completion. Thankfully, the impactful moments between characters really stay with you. One of the best examples of this, and without giving away too much, is a beautiful lesbian relationship that blossoms between two characters. One character that’s more important to the story than any other is the titular Chicory. Every interaction with Chicory is a learning moment. Her grappling with mental health is sometimes hard to watch. She is an anxious, self-deprecating mess with imposter syndrome that can’t believe in the esteem of which the people hold her. The player character is no stranger to thoughts of self-doubt and together the two travel a gamut of emotional highs and lows. It is through these difficulties do they learn of each other, the good and the bad, and become more than the strangers they started as.The premise of Chicory: A Colorful Tale is a simple one. The world has lost its colour everything is now black and white, an empty canvas if you will. With brush in hand colouring, every inch of the world is completely up to the player. The early stages of the game won’t require much painting to proceed. But progression soon becomes dependent on abilities you unlock and will necessitate painting more aspects of each screen to activate. To make it easier and less time-consuming in the late game, it’s worth painting as much as possible as you progress. Luckily, you don’t need to possess the skills of a master painter to complete the game. As you can quickly and easily fill an entire screen with little effort. But those that are not artistically challenged will find a lot to like here. There’s a variety of different brush packs to unlock, even creating your own alongside custom colour palettes. The world truly is your canvas and there’s no limit to your imagination. You can even bring in a second player and by working together, bring a little joy to Picnic.The gameplay is reminiscent of Concrete Genie but without the motion controls. The implementation is very different, however, and never truly felt streamlined throughout the game. It’s clearly geared toward mouse and keyboard use where you can easily paint with the mouse swiftly and with precision. However, the movement of the character is better on a controller. There’s a trade-off no matter which control scheme you decide to use. There’s another stark difference, and that’s in the overly white colour palette of Chicory: A Colorful Tale. It’s like a charming colouring book, but when applied to screens there’s a very serious risk of eyestrain. Thankfully, the developer has considered this with an Eyestrain Helper option located in the menu. Do your eyes and head a favour and turn this on if you’re planning to play for an extended period. It works the same as phones and tablets by adding a warmer tint to the screen. Lena Raine’s composition is a perfect accompaniment to the gameplay. The music in every area of Picnic is unique. It’s worth taking a few moments when entering a new area to let the music take you on a journey. There’s so much depth to be found within the music choices and when they appear within the game. The music accompanying the challenging yet not impossible boss battles is intense and a major departure from the soothing upbeat and sombre tones of the towns. Without this soundtrack, I don’t know if the game would have had the same level of impact.Chicory: A Colorful Tale perfectly embraces the “don’t judge a book by its cover” metaphorical phrase. It lulls you into a false sense of security with its charmingly simple visuals and cute anthropomorphic characters. The depth found within its story is unexpected, surprising, and frankly wonderful storytelling. The focus on mental health is eye-opening, self-affirming and a great opportunity to learn. This is all wrapped up in a therapeutic and fun colouring game with a powerful soundtrack.(Originally Published on )

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a tale of a whimsical adventure filled with creativity, laughter, and a touch of intoxication. It was me, the daring artist, and my cunning puzzle-loving companion, embarking on a tipsy journey through the enchanting world of Chicory!As I found myself lost in Chicory's initially plain world, the atmosphere grew more delightful by the sip. With each brushstroke, guided not only by imagination but also by the refreshing beverage in my hand, it was as if drink and art became dancing partners.Amidst laughter and refilling our glasses, my companion showcased her boozed-enhanced intellect by mastering Chicory's intricate challenges and landscapes with ease. I marvelled at her ability to solve each mind-boggling puzzle and navigate us to the next section, raising our glasses in celebration with every triumph.Sometimes, amid the giggles and banter, we overlooked clues or got lost, but in the end this just gave me extra time to add more and more layers, colour and beauty into our world.As our escapades in Chicory came to a close, we stepped back to admire our intoxicating masterpiece - a canvas adorned with ridiculous colours, terrible patterns, and missed sections. But it was the most hilarious representation of our fun and the good times we had together playing this game. If ever you find yourself embarking on an artistic adventure, armed with paintbrushes, a great friend and a hint of liquid inspiration, I highly recommend Chicory. Raise your glasses to the artist within you both and enjoy the masterpiece that unfolds!

_childDocuments_.review: .So, I've played Wandersong before, and seeing as it is one of my top favorite story-based game of ALL time, and Night in the Woods being in the top 3, I had to play this. Chicory is developed by Greg Lobanov as the lead developer with help from Lena Reine's (Celeste) Music and AShellInThePit's Em Halberstadt's Sound Design (Night in the Woods), which means Chicory is the spiritual sequel to basically a lot of those games. Having played all 3 games, I can say there are some influences in the themes explored, along with some references and other similarities such as . Chicory is still a unique experience, and I applaud Greg for being able to come out with yet another amazing game that could stand on equal grounds with Wandersong, although I still prefer the latter.It's important to note that this is mainly a . From a plot standpoint, the premise is interesting, and the story kept me hooked up until the very end, with a surprising twist right near the end that calls back to 2 other plot points about "Wielder" history that already gets said during earlier parts of the game. There's a lot of thought put into the writing of the main plot, and it really shows. There's also a heartfelt conversation with a family member about "" that really resonates with me personally AND also in-game, because I've been drawing every single place with detail and at that point and I felt a bit exhausted. Overall, it explores important themes regarding mental health and self identity as shown in the trailer, and I think everyone would find it a worthy experience.That being said, I found the overall cast slightly weaker and less endearing than , especially in the beginning. There's no particularly important recurring side-character that feel memorable like the Pirate or the Mask in Wandersong. Some of these characters could literally say each other's lines and it wouldn't feel off by far, save for Blackberry, Cardamom and Chicory herself. I understand that character writing is not that easy, but in this regard, I would like to recommend you all to still play Wandersong first if you care about characters more than gameplay., often for secret-collecting purposes. The abilities do feel pretty cool to use, levelling up always feels like an amazing reward everytime, and  for example gives a real sense of reward for me who has been painting every single thing neatly since the beginning of the game. I can say most of the abilities to incentivize the player to paint everything, and since you're a wielder, it fits., with varied things such as flower platforms that grow when painted, doors that open when you draw specific patterns found somewhere else, and those flinger flowers that launch nearby player to certain places when painted. The puzzles themselves are not too hard that I have to look for a guide on anything, it's well balanced. It's nicely crafted and the different puzzle types according to area makes the whole thing less boring. In this aspect, it is similar to Wandersong too., with scattered phonebooths almost everytime a new hint is available. You can get soft hints and direct-spoonfed hints on a lot of occasions during puzzle segments, and the option to "know less" being there is extremely valuable., there's a lot of options such as making the game slightly easier on boss fights, turning off paint sounds that might be triggering to some people, a different more readable font, less screen shake or screen flash, you get the idea. There's also an optional "content warnings" toggle that shows pop-ups whenever things are going to go certain ways that might be triggering to people, and in that regard, I can feel that the developers care a lot about the player. I've played with content warnings on despite not actually needing it just to see how they do it, and they show it appropriately; not too often that you'd feel annoyed, but they're there everytime they need to be in my opinion., and I dare say is one of the strongest points of the game other than the plot.  The sound design is also very nice. In comparison, the art is not spectacularly spec-demanding that makes it hard to run the game, but it is quite charming in it's own way since it's reminiscent of coloring books and fits the theme and premise of the game about painting the world and being the wielder. It's also still quite intricate and that's the plus. The coloring is left up to the player , although the object-coloring system is a bit wonky sometimes when you can't really color some things easily due to other objects being nearby and the game causing you to auto-lock to those instead. I wish there was an option to use certain buttons to basically "scroll" through nearby objects before we could click and paint them for more specific coloring.And into criticism territory, . While I do know the amount and size of the "paint pixels" in the game and I'm fine with it being as it is (smallest pixel being when you lightly tap left click on any surface), I wish drawing while zoomed lets us consistently paint smaller when held down, since I'm sure the smallest brush size is atleast 5-pixel width when held down and zooming in doesn't seem to change that size. I want brush sizes to adapt with whether or not we're drawing while zoomed in. But again, part of the charm of the entire game is the implied fact that Pizza (or whoever you named the protagonist dog) is not an amazing drawer, so living with small mistakes and imperfections isn't the end of the world, and any casual gamers without any drawing skills would feel at home.And finally, about secrets and collectibles, I found many of the outfits and customization in-game great, with additional fun collectibles such as decoration items that you can place in a lot of places as additional paintable objects. There's also some amazing secret  in game that lets you do many things, such as painting with a certain intricate texture, basically stamping symbols, and other amazing things I won't spoil. All these secret and additional stuff is what makes this game go from roughly 10/15 hours of plot content to 30 hours of fun, along with the fact that you might try painting the whole world like I did, as you should.Final score:

The concept is wonderful and coloring the trees and land is good fun, but I found the game failed to capitalize much on the primary mechanic of painting. A citizen tells you "paint my house!" and then you just blob it with red and your done. Maybe they'll tell you to add some yellow. You can design a donut that hangs on the wall of a donut shop, but as soon as its complete you leave the room and never see it again. The game floods you with a metric buttload of cosmetics around every corner, but your character can only wear a hat and shirt, and so each piece feels vapid and empty as if you just equip whatever you find you'll rarely wear a piece for more than two minutes. Inside the dungeons, the paintbrush felt like it was simply a proxy for bopping things with your weapon or flipping a switch, with level design that is otherwise identical to what has existed for decades. Also, the promise of coop fell very short when you realize that player 1 controls both the character and the brush but the second player can only control a brush. Player 2 feels like a vestigial cursor rather than an actual player 2. I do really like how the game is basically a giant coloring book and your work is fully saved screen to screen, allowing if you wish the chance to collage in the whole map in what I'm sure are some really interesting and novel ways.

_childDocuments_.review: i backed this game in 2019 as soon as i could when it was first revealed as drawdog: you play as a dog wielding a paint brush. i mean come on, that's the best sales pitch i've ever heard for any one video game.at the beginning of 2020, i made a new years resolution draw every single day, before life as we knew it would change thanks to the pandemic. i kept at it every day though, without fail (to this day still, as i'm writing this!). but it wasn't without its own trials and tribulations; mental health came into focus, i had newfound feelings of self-doubt, imposter syndrome, and wondering why i ever wanted to pursue art (and asking myself: do i  want this?). it definitely got easier as time went on, but i continued having those thoughts.but then, chicory finally came out, and the experience of playing it...validated my own personal journey with art.the beginning lured me in with its charm. wielding the brush filled me almost with child-like wonder and excitement, painting stuff in wanton disregard of literally anything (because who cares paint everything!!). mechanically, the game plays out like a zelda game crossed with mario paint. as you progress in the game, you get access to new abilities to help you solve puzzles and gain access to new areas; the puzzles are nicely designed and paced out well! and if you get really into it, you start paying more attention to details you didn't use to before, eventually imparting your artistic sensibilities into the game's environments.all of which is to say, i  adore this game (it might even be my most favourite game ever?? heck). it's narrative and gameplay resonated with me so strongly as an artist. this game neatly summarized my own experiences with becoming an artist in such an adorable package. while the unexpected punches the game throws at you felt...too real at times, it's also quick to remind you to be kind to yourself, in the face of any challenges that we might encounter. we do our best, and often times, our best is good enough to keep going.also this game makes at least several jokes about butts. 12/10

_childDocuments_.review: A heartfelt and comfortable journey though the creative process, and dealing with the very real hardships it brings to call yourself and artist and aspire to heights that seem unreachable, even and especially for those who say they arn't creative, let this game point you in a new direction. _childDocuments_.review: Before I begin, let me preface this review by saying the extent of my artistic ability is drawing random things in Microsoft Paint as well as basic vector graphics in Inkscape.I went into this game expecting a small $20 Microsoft Paint clone. What I got was an adventure that basically made me almost cry, like the endings to OneShot, Beacon Pines and the like; with painting elements mixed in.Without even trying, you can beat the game in about six hours if you skip over all the extra side quests, but would you really want to? You could spend hours just perfecting every single detail on the map, it's like a virtual coloring book! The characters are lively, they have their own unique twists, and most of them are named after food! (hell, even you're named after food if you want to!) The music in this game is top notch, as well; being composed by the same person that did the soundtracks for Celeste and a couple Minecraft updates (cheers, Lena).So, overall, get the game. Buy it now. Even if you think you have no artistic ability in you (like me), pick it up and try it. You never know what will come out on the canvas.

_childDocuments_.review: It was a little hard to tell whether or not I'd like this game before trying it because of how vague a lot of the reviews for it are, but I'm glad that I did.Chicory is a great game with a compelling story and a lot of very interesting and unique paint-based mechanics. The puzzles are never particularly challenging or overwhelming, even when finding the most hidden secret treasures, but they're always a lot of fun, and there are a lot of them throughout the game. Each area has its own unique set of obstacles used to their fullest, on top of your character's skill-set expanding over the course of the game.The game is short (~4-6 hours) if you just play it to completion, but there's a lot of additional playtime from the optional task of coloring in each new screen you enter, which can be very relaxing.The story is a simple but very well done one about not knowing who you're supposed to be and what you want to do, and about being a good friend to people. It gets intense at times, which make for some of my favorite moments in the game, like the visually and audibly incredible boss fights, but it rarely lasts long.My only complaint is that after the end of the game most characters have very little more to say or do, including major ones. After the game, you get attached to them, so it's tough to have them suddenly stop talking to you forever!

_childDocuments_.review: Chicory: A Colorful Tale truly is a hidden gem; words can't even begin to describe how wonderful this game is. When I first bought it, I only expected it to be an adorable coloring game I could play to destress or ease my anxiety, but Chicory was more than this. It went above and beyond my expectations in every possible way. The game combines so many elements into one game: boss/fighting mechanics; simple platforming; and puzzles all while being a coloring game. Gameplay also is unique and the way you wield the paintbrush is so versatile and fun.The game's aesthetics is cozy - the art is simple but the hand-drawn visuals contribute so much to the overall atmosphere of the game and fits so well. I love the artistic freedom you have to customize so many aspects of the game ranging from your clothes (character design) to environment. You literally get to shape and mold how you want Picnic to look like (given early on you have a set of presets to choose from depending on the area). However, what makes Chicory: A Colorful Tale such a memorable game is the simple, yet so meaningful story and message it conveys alongside with the beautiful original soundtrack. As someone who struggles with mental health, I constantly allow myself to fall down the rabbit hole of self-hatred while creating unrealistic expectations that I often fail to meet. Chicory reminds me that these moments of self-doubt and anxiety exist in all of us, but may manifest differently as we all have unique experiences. It's okay to not be okay; self-acceptance and asking for help often goes a really long way. The story's dialogue feels like a conversation between friends and flows so naturally, nothing ever feels forced and so many quotes throughout the game resonate so well with me. The way the game discusses depression through such a simple yet powerful means is extraordinary; the artistic symbolism throughout the game is riveting.You can tell that the developers put so much care and heart into making this game. The original soundtrack is beautiful and features a wide range - different boss battles and areas of the world have its own music. My favorite one is 'Probably Ancient Evil' - I find myself listening to it outside of the game (it's so good). I most definitely would suggest this game to anyone, you don't need to be an artist or someone who enjoys drawing or painting to get the full experience out of the game. The game is so unique, I can't think of any other games that might be similar and wish it got more traction for how beautifully crafted it is. I truly adore this game so much and it definitely has made it to my list of favorite games of all time（＾・ω・＾❁）
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Chicory is an absolute delight. I was expecting a reasonably short, cute enough indie title to pass the time with, instead I got a surprisingly expansive adventure with an emotional, moving narrative and many charming and memorable characters. The game mechanics work fantastically, and the soundtrack from the legendary Lena Raine is obviously wonderful.I thought I might struggle in parts with my own lack of artistic ability, but the game never expects you to produce anything of high quality, and the drawing tools the game gives you very cleverly disallow a level of precision that might otherwise have triggered my perfectionist anxiety.I love this game. Quite a lot. I'm really excited to see what Greg Lobanov does next.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to admit, I feel odd. This is the second, seemingly perfect game for me, and I get big disappointment. I'm halfway through the game, but I will put the game aside.Huh. Where to start. The core gameplay has a colorizing mechanic. And I feel it's simply sabotaging me. I have to take in small portions because it's clunky. I could write more details, but then this would be a long review.If you put this aside, you have color limitations. I understand there are certain regions in the game, but why do I have 2 blues in one zone and barely see the difference, while in the other zone, it's the same situation with oranges. If the game tries to boost your creativity and motivate you to make it colorful, then you should be able to rearrange the color palettes or have better ones.Oh yea, I didn't mention this game is a puzzle game, but you can see in the screenshots. However, when the game gave me a maze of "connect this with that" megapuzzles, I just got annoyed. I was okay with some puzzles, but this is too much.According to a walkthrough, I played the first half of the game. Yes, I was checking where I was in the story because I started to be seriously bored.The main character is clingy. I seriously felt sorry for Chicory, the main character is like a stalker or a weirdo and annoys Chicory. The main character's behaviour irritates me and doesn't give much space to the poor bunny. At least the second half changes this situation in a better way.I know what the main topic of the game is. But it was hard to pay attention to the details because there is just too much "yap yap" from the main character. The game's title is "Chicory", but you won't know much about that bunny in the first half because NPC-s are just rumoring everywhere, and it's like a real life mysterious celebrity that no one really knows or understands. Well, I guess the story is using the idea of having an emotional catharsis and a slow-building friendship.People were complaining, as even if you paint the whole screen the same color, you get the same "empty" phrases from NPC-s. But I really liked when, I painted enough, some characters from other regions showed up and said some nice things.I also like the art class mini challenges, the decorating requests, and the obviously scripted but kind reactions. The mailing minigame and the photo-remake one are enjoyable too.The boss fights are cool, and I am happy you have a lot of difficulty options in the menu, because I didn't bump into a game over screen (it breaks the focus with a "Hello Loser") just because I died. So I would say it's very friendly for casual players.The hint system is funny, I really liked it.Yes, I know it's a thumbs down. No mistake. The game more often frustrates than relaxes me. I have here the thing, that I call "Spiritfarer issue". Spiritfarer is also an overwhelmingly positive game. Both games won awards too. And I think both games feel like a chore to play and have story elements that I really dislike.When I started that game, it was harder to continue. To be honest, I feel the same here too. The only difference is that here you can push the main story, at least (by ignoring everything else).However, I believe this game was made with kindness and good intentions. I can see the positive things in it, I can see myself finish it maybe another time in small portions, but it has too many flaws. But hey, this is me! I highly recommend seeing videos about it before you buy it. And hey, if you like what you see, don't let me hold you back! A whole world is waiting for you to make it colorful.

_childDocuments_.review: Everybody can be an artist?I’m not sure if that’s the core message of Chicory… or maybe I’m deceiving you to avoid spoilers. The fact of the matter is that this game has . Over the years I grew tired with slew of pretentious games that fool you into buying their cookie-cutter, puddle-deep explanations of grander themes. However I do think that this time it is a little different…While it doesn’t stick the landing in all places, it does a genuine job of presenting a true, universal problem and trying to figure out possible solutions. Story in multiple moments is truly heart-touching with multiple outstanding scenes either hitting too close to home or just being emotional rollercoasters. This is truly a story about creativity and for people striving to use it and struggling with things that might come from it.Creativity also something that comes to mind then it comes to world design. Chicory is mostly a 2D environmental puzzle game with heavy emphasis on exploration. While puzzles are fine enough and don’t distract much by being too overbearing, difficult or boring, it’s the exploration aspect that deserves a lot of praise. Not only there are tons of treasures to find, but also world of Chicory is a genuinely interesting place to visit. It is full of curious places, regions and NPCs to meet with diagetic sidequests and stuff to do. And that despite being mostly monochrome (before you show up), filled with antropomorthic animals and in isometric 2D.I had a genuinely good time with going through the game for full completion, but I feel like some places could use a tiny bit of improvement. While 95% of dialogue in the game is pretty great, some of the scenes and NPC encounters feel like they don’t match to overall quality? Some of that strange dialogue can make characters suddenly unsympathetic for a short while or throw a quip that doesn’t fit the game’s world and tone. While I’m thankful those aren’t a common occurrence, I do wonder how they ended up in the game.There are also few other minor pointers for improvement (world painting mechanics could be utilized more, some sidequests could be improved story wise) but what definitely doesn’t need any tweaks is the soundtrack and overall presentation. Graphics and animations are good enough, but game’s OST is really full of distinctive leitmotifs and emotional delivery that steals a lot of scenes alone. Wielder’s theme is one of my favorites here and fills me with joy every time I hear it.I’m so enamored with that song that I could end this review with lyrics from it, but I do need a proper conclusion for you do know if the game is worth your time. Chicory is not a gameplay powerhouse. If you look for gripping gameplay, you need to look elsewhere. But if you feel like there is that creative spark inside you and you are mostly interested in stories and journeys, I can safely tell you to hop right in for a meaningful experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: I went in expecting a funny coloring game; got a heartfelt story about artistic expression, impostor syndrome, and how to deal with expectations from not only others but yourself as well. I usually rush through when finishing up achievements for a game but I ended up really trying my best during the optional art classes. Then spent a couple hours drawing a giant amogus across the whole map.Also shoutouts to Lena Raine for nothing but bangers yet again.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: What an enjoyable little experience this was.First of all know that my drawing and coloring skills can barely manage stick figures, so i wasn't going into this knowing at all what i was doing, and the art i did create in the game to 100% it was terrible but i still had a blast throughout the entire game.So please don't get discouraged from buying it just because you suck at drawing. Nothing in game is going to prevent you from playing it just because you suck. It's a lot more of a puzzle narrative game about overcoming self doubt and learning to love your art and yourself. I really enjoyed the whole thing, the artstyle was cute and the music was very soothing. I found all the characters to be likable and interesting to listen to.Some minor issues i had with the game:I found the platforming to be kinda clunky in some areas and i didn't really like the cloud parkour.. It had some weird framerate issues sometimes when i booted it up but it was very rare. felt like the boss fights was too samey? Might be because there is so few of them and also i have no idea if there is a fail state for boss fights cause i never got it even when i sucked. Would have enjoyed having access to a smaller brush size and more variety in colors at the time, but that's just me not really an issue. Overall i would recommend this game to anyone who enjoys puzzle narrative focused games with a lot of character moments. Fun game!
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Puzzle adventure action game. You use a keyboard to control the movement and the mouse to do the action, such as painting and combatting. It has an outstanding concept and a fun boss-fighting design. Easy difficulty boss fight, easy to medium difficulty for map exploring. Though most of the dialogue from NPCs are light-heart to read, surprisingly, some contain very interesting subjects from LGBT equal right to the philosophical debate about capitalism. There were secrets, collectibles, and many side quests in the game. The only tiny issue that troubled me was the map detail, that quite hard to navigate.It took me 15 hours to complete the game with 92% map clear and nearly finished all side quests. Recommended for those who want to enjoy an action-adventure with an innovative fighting mechanic.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of both Celeste and Wandersong I can say this game is super cute and very charming, from the music and the minimalist visuals, it leaves a lot of room for creativity with the mechanics of the brush. Worth the play and I never expected this game to have such a deep *albeit small* story connected with it. Worthwhile to play and I will def 100% it when I get the chance.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: First: the coloring is soooooo satisfying!Chicory has all the aspects of a great Zelda-ish adventure game: exploring, solving puzzles, finding secrets, helping people. But the entire time you're also painting and doodling and coloring and drawing on absolutely everything.It's genius. While you're talking to an NPC, you can splash color on them then draw hearts (and/or d**ks) all over their living room. The coloring interface is so smooth and easy, so you can fill a screen with color as you walk through it without having to stop. The limited palette and tools (you can customize them later) and the way color pops into objects makes it look cool even if you have no art skills whatsoever.And every part of this game is just as playful and whimsical and good!!There are super tricky environmental puzzles and hard to reach places that I scratched my head over for ages before figuring them out. Memorable boss battles and big narrative moments (sob sob!). Hundreds of NPCs to talk to with adorable and sincere lives that are sometimes sad and sometimes hopeful. Tons of extra optional content and stuff to collect and decorate with.I was a beta tester (many more hours than whatever it says here) but I still haven't found half of it all.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Oh this is SUCH A COOL GAME! Even though it deals with artists that get into a depression because they think they're never quite good enough (if you read this, maybe you've been there?), I LOVE how they handle this topic, it's so well done and clever! I love the humour, the art style, the colors, the weird story, the boss fights (that are quite forgiving - after all, it's about the story), Highly recommended!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: It was wonderful how creative I could be throughout the game, for example painting all the plants and buildings with new colors! I was able to fully immerse myself in the story and wander around the map exploring all the different places and meeting some cute characters along the way.The various puzzles and main boss fights also made the game interesting. If, for some reason, you didn't know what to do next, you could always call your parents at home and they would help you by giving you advice about the game. For this reason, it is absolutely certain that the game is suitable for all types of players.I can really recommend this game if you like casual, creative and cute games, this was 100% worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Cool Ideas, but in practice is mostly a boring slog to play since it boils down to just waggling your mouse all over the screen turning it into a single color ugly mess with no actual motivation to color things properly or make anything look good. It ends up feeling like old Wii games that ham-fisted franticly waggling the Wii-mote as a game mechanic to make it 'unique' but just turned the game into a chore without adding anything to the experiece.Whilst also being filled with dialog window after dialog window, that you're encouraged to repeatedly talk to the same NPCs over and over, of uninteresting text seemingly extracted from a teenager's text messages.There might be a case of 'but you didn't even get to the good parts hours in where everything comes together', and I'd say that if it takes that long for a game to click and get interesting it's just bad design.Definitely not a game for me and probably wouldn't recommend it to a friend unless they had kids that they wanted a simple game for maybe.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: this game is SOULFUL. what does that mean? i don't know! but it's very cathartic to swing a big ol brush around.  you fill in the world as you go, and you leave your own sort of mark on the places you've been. you remember 'hey, i done did paintered that.' when you pass by again.i definitely recommend taking your time to do so, too. i think you're technically allowed to just... not paint anything, and just rush to the story bits, but i don't think that's nearly as fun a way to experience the game as painting as you go. if you're looking for something more peaceful, this game is a nice change of pace.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10What's great about this game:- Great story, relatable characters- Fun & creative puzzles- Great quality of life features, the game takes extra care to put in features that might frustrates players over trivial things.- Very polished, no bugs encountered at all during my playthroughWhat's not so great about this game- Predetermined color choices for each area. Kinda a bummer when you want to color an area but you don't have any color that matches it.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: This is so so much fun. I love that you are given a colour pallet in each area and can freely decorate. it forces you to get really fun and free with colouring different areas. I love that you get more tools and textures as you go so you can come back and add to areas but you don't need to redo areas. The glow in the dark caves are really satisfying and so fun. You don't have to be an artist to have fun and be creative in this little game, I love its cute humour. I really highly recommend this game. The puzzles are fun and interactive and I don't find the game too hard or challenging, really is relaxing. I'm Obsessed.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: The good:+ Great story+ Suprisingly decent world building+ Lovely character+ Good soundtrack+ You LITERALLY can paint on everything, which suprisingly fun+ Out of the box gameplay mechanism+ Challanging puzzle, although few feels annoying+ Epic boss fight+ Some anti-frustration featuresThe bad:- No tracker or note for side questThe ugly:* Very few object have lower resolution, which is noticeable on 2K monitor* I wish main/secondary character is fully voiced (not really ugly point)Although i'm not artist or work on creative field, i enjoyed this game more than i thought. The developer have come a long way since Wandersong. Try it and you might be surprised.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: It took a while to get to the point where I felt I could write this review even after reaching 100% completion.I knew before I played that there was going to be an uplifting emotional journey involved and that no matter what I wouldn't really be able to screw up. The team that made this game makes games that reward exploration and creativity. I did not know that by the end of the game I would have a really deep, emotional, reaction to feeling like I maybe kind of finally understand what it feels like to make good art.My art isn't good. I have never managed more than a stick figure or the default brown rectangle tree with green circles for leaves. But I 100% completed this game. 20 hours (not the fastest by a long shot) and that includes all the 'drawing classes' that don't really teach you anything about drawing but absolutely teach you about feeling good for trying.I stream video games when I can but I didn't stream this game. I didn't want anyone to see me try to draw. Now I deeply regret it. I want people to see the weird things I drew off of vague prompts with the tools the game gives you. I want to see what other people did. Looking back at the drawings I made.. I actually think I improved over the course of the game.Anyway. This is a great game. It's heart is about doing what you can every day to live. It doesn't ask for people to do more than that. Just live and find what joy you can. Help each other when you can and be kind enough to yourself to allow others to help you too. People who played Wandersong will love it.As for game play, the puzzles are challenging enough to be entertaining and don't get too repetitive or challenging to the point that you feel bored or roadblocked. The hint system is fantastic and placed where players may need a little help. Mom does a great job of pointing you toward a solution without giving it away. Dad gives some specific directions that may be very helpful for younger players or for when you can't find that last hidden present.I would recommend this game to anyone, everyone, and be fairly sure that they'll get at least a little something out of it if not the full 20 hour experience. Assuming they are willing to give it a real try.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: play chicoryplay chicoryplay, and i cannot emphasize this enough, chicorygreg lobanov makes games the way they were meant to be made. at least in line with my tastes. like i hate when stuff turns into just a List Of Qualities but this game is all ive been thinking about for days and days now and i still cant form coherent thoughts about it so the raw materials are as such:-completely enamored with the world, not just with the worldbuilding which is super adorable, or with the overal world/level design which is extremely good (its more ambitious then the linearity of wandersong while also being so satisfactorily compact that i barely felt the desire to use the fast travel), but, god. the way it makes u feel so intertwined with it via yr coloring (i colored every single screen cuz im That ♥♥♥♥♥ ig), but also the way that every area has so much care taken with the Ambience, even if u splat colors everywhere itll have a fitting palate, and even if u leave it as black and white as possible, the lena raines incredible career-best score still sells the atmosphere. its unfair that dinner and teatime meadows r right next to eachother, flipping back and forth between two of my fave pieces of video game music + general Area Vibes ive encountered in a while. i ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love existing in the world which is way even tho i beat the game a few days ago, with a very completionist playthrough, im still wandering around the world postgame just to find the last few stray things and like, Feel There-greg's games have gotten a lot of praise for being Emotional and Charming and Wholesome™ (have kinda come to loathe that term but i cant deny the gravitational pull that stuff it gets applied to has on me) but theres always a lot more then just good vibes and post-undertale-earthbound-revival quirkiness punctuated with occasional emotional darkness (tho even the darkest moments still remain as approachable as a well-written childrens cartoon, in presentation if not in subject matter). theres a real thematic consideration in the emotions being explored, a refusal to not extend sympathy to any character (even wandersong's audrey redheart is well considered as an actual person, even if she also represents complete and utter opposition to the game's ideology), and a dedication more then anything to the questioning and subversion and rejection of dominant narratives. thats rly the Big Thing that connects wandersong and chicory, tho their character's emotional journeys are certainly distinct (the protagonist and chicory's dynamic and development has more then a few parallels to that of the bard and miriam, often in striking contrast or role reversal)-between this and art sqool, maybe indie games are the thing thatll make me _childDocuments_.review: A couple of years ago I saw the first teasers of the “Drawdog” game on twitter and it looked really neat. The project regularly popped up somewhere on my timeline, consistently looking more enticing until finally it changed the title to the current Chicory: A Colorful Tale and then finally, and very recently, got released. Despite me not liking the previous title from the developer, Wandersong, all that much it was a promising game with lots of heart, so I was hoping that Chicory will be better. It turned out to be more than that.Mechanically, Chicory plays as a top down Legend of Zelda entry, with focus on exploration and puzzles and no combat outside of several boss battles. Though even there you don’t get a fail state, instead being able to continue immediately if you “fail”. However, the main way of interaction with the world is not a sword, a shield or a bow. It’s a magic brush that lets you paint the world as you see fit. Everything in this world can be painted by you. …well, technically there are limitations, but they’re minor or puzzle-related. Either way – the brush, that you can use at almost any point, is your main tool to solve puzzles, to fight bosses, to help people and to just have fun expressing yourself.Which is central to the story of the game that shows us the world that suddenly became devoid of colour. And the wielders of the magic brush, who must paint the world with colour anew. This world is full of adorable characters, full of personality, many side stories and side quests, fun locations and lots of really heartwarming dialogue. And the journey the player takes is a journey of self discovery and hope. This game is so damn wholesome it’s impossible to not smile for the most of it.Sure, this game has some weaker elements. For one, just like Wandersong before it, there are several sequences which last for longer than they should, crossing that line from “this is fun” to “can it stop now” and “am I doing things correctly, is something happening?” Which, unfortunately also just like Wandersong, extends to the final boss fight and some of the final moments. Hopefully, this is something the developer will figure out eventually. Among many many superbly written moments of characters “getting real” and talking about their views and issues, there were two that stood out as being shockingly poor done in contrast to everything else. And I’d say that one particular puzzle concept that came around the midpoint of the game was rather frustrating and finicky more than anything. But luckily it was not reused and with the amount of fresh ideas the game had, it never got stale.Since it is a more exploration and experience kind of game, where gameplay is very simple (but shockingly engaging), it’s hard to find more words about the game. Despite being overwhelmed by joy of playing it and wanting to share it with the world. The soundtrack is good, the visual design and lots of fun little details are stellar. There are so many fun reactions and variations to how you play. And so many different ways you can experience this, otherwise mostly linear and narrative focused, game. Because it allows the players to put their personality in it on such a low level of colouring the world and the characters.I loved this game. It feels like a lot of the ideas and concepts from Wandersong revisited, but improved by a lot. It is lovely, it is delightful, it is heartening. I simply cannot recommend Chicory: A Colorful Tale enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: A wholesome take on the Zelda formula that also touches on the struggles of depression and evaluating self-worth. The characters all around make for a great universe, while also offering fun side quests and dialogue to explore. The idea of painting everything makes for fun things to accomplish while moving the story forward.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Do you play Night In The Woods or Wandersong? If you love/like both or either of them like me, you'll love this one. Don't overlook this, This game is such an amazing charming art-loving game yet it somehow manages to pull off a wonderful twist and creativeness.Worth the full price if you enjoy artistic casual game with lovable cast of characters, story and old-school Zelda puzzling.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: At this point it's become a common trope to have an indie game that does a spin on a retro game while layering in themes of depression, but it's hard not like what's on display in Chicory: a color book world that lost all color and tasks you with solving Zelda style puzzles with a paint brush. I was constantly reminded of Celeste not just due to the composer but from the way the plot and encounters ramp up in intensity. Chicory was a fun game to go through at a relaxed pace stopping to color in and out of the lines.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: I've never made a recommendation for a game until this moment but I had to for this game!! I knew I wanted to play this game as soon as I saw the trailer for it. :) It is SO beautiful - the music, the art, the story, everything! There are also content warnings that you can turn on from the settings, which is something I don't see very often but should be in every game, in my opinion. A really excellent experience through and through. HIGHLY recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Essentially, this game is a coloring-book inspired game that also has an amazing story and unique pacing.This game is expertly hand-crafted in every screen, has some amazing story telling, and never slacks in the in-between. It works amazingly as a casual game, but it does mostly lack a post-game competitive kind of content.But nonetheless, it is still worth the money to go pick it up, as it will be some of the best 20 hours you can get. If you want to see a general idea of what this game is about, watching the first or maybe second chapters on YouTube should generally give you an idea of if you will like the game or not. The casual gameplay isn't for everyone, but that doesn't mean that you should turn it away without at least giving it a chance. 8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: The few links it had to Celeste were enough for me to give it a shot, and it didn't disappoint. Chicory is an absolute bliss of a time, combining mechanics with visuals and narrative in perfect harmony to tell a story about self expression, expectations and anxiety, all the while delivering all the stops in wholesomeness, humor, charm, and fun puzzles. I loved all the characters both important and secondary, and the completionist aspect is so relaxed that I went for it despite never giving games such honor.My stronger critisisms of the game are as follow:1. The story is a bit wordy. Now, generally I digged it a lot, but I won't pretend like at some point there were just too many long monologues. Celeste, in my opinion, struck a better balance between showing emotions through gameplay and imagery and flat out telling you stuff. Here, not so much.2. The bosses are a big let down. For what are essentially the story's biggest emotional points, they feel so aimless and lacking in strategy. The only one I found specially memorable was the evil protagonist one, where you mirror the brush to hit it.These are small elements of a larger whole, a whole which I thoroughly liked. It's so nice to have a game so open to explore these ideas and in such a welcoming manner. This is what I mean when I say games are an artform.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Expect to release your creative side in a entire game that's a coloring book. As you progress not only will your skill as an artist but so will your tools as you learn how to express yourself in the world of Chicory. There are head scratching puzzles, npc back stories, and bosses that are as creative and thrilling as Undertale. In the game the drawing is almost half pixel art and half normal drawing which has actually helped a amateur like me create beautiful paintings. As someone who has gamed for a good portion of my life, im confidant to say this is now my number one favorite game that I have played. Lastly, Lena Raine, the same composer for Celeste, has stolen my heart with her amazing music. For short: Chicory has amazing music and lets you express your artistic side while exploring.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: A game that warms my cold,dead heart. It's been a long time that a game has put a smile on my face as much as Chicory: A Colorful Tale has. Best game that I have played all year. Incredible music, fun puzzles, heartwarming dialogue, calm-inducing coloring...the list just goes on and on. The game is just a breath of fresh air for me. 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: This was a delightful surprise. I expected a painting toy with a thin layer of structure but got a very satisfying, varied, personality filled game packed with little details, incredible music and sound design, wonderful writing, achingly cute characters, and a very cohesive and relatable storyline that perfectly hits the sweet spot of all ages appeal while telling a surprisingly mature story that anyone who has ever aspired to something can relate to. I had mixed feelings about Wandersong, their prior game, but I don't about Chicory. A game has not made me "awww!" aloud as many times as this. Come for the "pat head rub tummy zelda" gameplay, stay for the long hugs and juicy wet sounds.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Who would have thought that a painting brush coupled with a metroidvania would result in such an amazing experience? Chicory is a labour of love and creativity that shines through and trough. The soundtrack is a banger too, but then again that's no surprise when Lena Raine is the one behind it!Even with my extremely limited ability to draw, this game made me feel like an artist. And that's honestly the biggest praise I can give it.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a person to do reviews or even call myself a good steam reviewer, but I have to say this one of the best games I've ever played.It's been very long ever since a game made feel sad, happy, relaxed, frustated, scared, all bundled up in an experience that you can easily prolong to over 15 hours by just exploring every possibility.- exploration is well rewarding, especially when you unlock new abilites- The game is always ready to give you a tip, even the solution if you think the puzzles are difficult,- Possibly all characters and NPCs in this game are fleshed out, - The boss fights are amazing along with their mechanics- The sound design and the music are incredible- The themes of depression and even anxiety are incredibly well portrayed.Overall, I dont have enough words to describe it, I felt happy during my entire playthrough and to think that it all came from the simple ability of allowing you to do and paint however you wish, like a paintbook but without the numbers that tell you which colors should be whereAt the end, its an experience that just can't be described but only understood by playing andI can safely say, this was my first game bought off sale and it was worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: I am unbelievably in love with this game!! If you're any type of creative person, you need to play this right now. The world, characters, story, and mechanics of this game all feel so cozy, playful and unique. The map is decently sized, which really daunted me when I first started the game since I needed to fill SO MUCH. But taking up that challenge just made the story so much more compelling! I would spend so long on some screens and then scribble another screen in lazily and look back on it thinking "that looks very bad!" And suddenly, a character pops up and tells me that they love what I did, and my little perfectionist artist heart crumbles. I really need a reminder sometime that someone is always admiring what you are creating, no matter how good or bad you think it is- and this game is that reminder and so much more. Did I mention how good the music is??? If you're considering this game in any way, DO IT!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: This game may actually be my favorite 2D Zelda game of all time.I knew going into it that the music by Lena Rain (who did Celeste's music) would be great. It is. I knew the game would be wholesome and adorable since it's by the designer from Wandersong. And it is. What I didn't expect was just how fun and interesting the paint-based gameplay would be. The puzzles constantly make you feel super smart, and the abilities you gain are all super fun to play with. When I first heard about the idea, I didn't think there would be all that many interesting puzzles and mechanics based on painting, but wow was I wrong. The puzzles and mechanics never get old, and there are an absolute ton of creative ideas being introduced all the way to the end of the game.And I certainly didn't predict how incredibly deep and personal the story and overall theme would be. The characters, writing, and plot of this game are astoundingly well done, and they turn a fantastic cozy 2D Zelda game into a truly unique and wonderful experience.I guess what I'm saying is, Chicory does for 2D Zelda games what Celeste did for platformers. It takes the base concept, turns the gameplay, music, and charm up to 11, and interweaves incredibly deep and emotional threads into every aspect of the game.I cannot recommend Chicory enough. I did back it on Kickstarter, which is how I got an advanced copy, but the game is better than I ever dreamed it could be. If you like cozy games about discussing feelings and helping people, or you like 2D Zelda games with innovative puzzles and hundreds of collectibles, or you just want to draw butts on everyone you meet, you need to get Chicory.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful, relaxing experience with a surprising amount of content. Between painting *whatever*, reproducing specific paintings, painting prompts, exploring the map, and finding secrets, I'm still not quite finished - even if I've technically beaten the game.The music is incredible, as to be expected of Lena Raine, and the writing was, to me, just the right combination of lighthearted and serious.4.5 paint-stained paws out of 5.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely heartwarming story paired with a beautiful soundtrack by Lena Raine. Gameplay isn't particularly challenging but that doesn't detract from the game at all. Feel like stopping and painting a whole screen? Feel free. Want to continue the story and ignore all the painting? Be my guest. Just want to explore or do challenges? Lots of those. It's a game filled with love for both the game and art itself and those feelings are so clear I just can't help but enjoy every little detail in it. Brought back a childlike love for art and jumping head first into creative tasks which I hadn't felt in many years. Easily one of the best relaxing games I have ever played and might just be my favourite game of all time once I finish all the painting classes. 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: I've ruined an important cutscene because it took me to a room in which I drew an amogus hours earlier. Best game, hands down.Joking aside (although that *did* happen), Chicory is a beautiful game that tackles important topics, with believable characters and an incredible soundtrack. It was a very positive experience, that'll I'll remember for a long time.If you want a game to give you the feelies and goosebumps of your life, play Chicory.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: This game was an absolutely amazing experience, and I'd highly recommend it even if you aren't an artist. In fact, I might even say that's more a reason to play. Your creativity is not only used, but given great encouragement as you explore the world. Every screen is something to enjoy and interact with, and I found myself playing long into the night just relaxing and bringing color to the environment. My enjoyment pushed me to complete the game 100%, and I can say confidently that it was worth every moment. Huge props to the developers , you've really made something beautiful.
_childDocuments_.name: Chicory: A Colorful Tale

_childDocuments_.review: GOOSHH THIS GAME IS SOO AGGHGHHGH. Absolutely one of my best experiences with games in a loooong while. I just can't put in words how much comfort this game gives me.The music was ABSOLUTELY STUNNING. It fits so well to the whole game and I would just stop sometimes to contemplate the songs because they are just that good.The whole idea of the game is sooo well done, like you could totally mess up with the idea of painting the game itself, but the team absolutely NAILED IT. It's easy enough to be minimalism, but also complex enough to add as much details as your heart desires. Of course there were times which I was bored, because painting the whole world map is very energy draining, but that's just what you would expect for such task, and even then, You can do many other things in the game instead of just painting.Gosh the story and the whole gameplay are sooooo perfect. I love all character interactions and the story itself is so catching and mysterious, but also simple. I love specially Chicory beacause of her deepness as a character and how I relate to her. That is another really good point, which is the fact that this game is so comfortable and cozy and filled with good lessons about relationships, mental health, self care, and just life in general. I've been really needing many things I've heard from npcs in this game and so many little cute thoughful details that spread love in my heart. I've been really lonely and needing someone to care about me lately, and even tho I still don't have such thing, this game kinda feels like this, or this place I could go and just stay there and nothing is wrong because everything and everyone is so respectful and kind.AND OMG THE BOSS BATTLES, where do I even begin! When I was fighting the first boss battle I thought that it would not really fit the game, but as the story progressed and I fought other ones, this became one of my favorite things in it! It really feels epic to splash paint around in a fight as if you were some kind of magic painter (Which is true but you get what I mean). Every single boss fight surprised me in a way, it was never what I was expecting, but even better. I also love every single of the 4 missions before fighting the last boss fight which you do with Chicory. Gosh those hit me so hard because they were nothing that I was expecting, specially the mountain one which I was concerned on how they would fit a song mini game but it went SO WELL and I LOVE IT SO MUCH. Also the painting you do of yourself to put in the tower, that scene of the island hit me so hard I almost cried legit. There were many times I almost cried in this game, specially when Chicory does a painting of you, I found that SOOOO ADORABLEE. I also love the puzzles and how they really get interesting and not boring! I'm used to not really like puzzles in these kinds of games, but they just nailed it in this one perfectly, mwah!I also love the options of pronoums in the beggining. I haven't seen many games include these options, specially non binary ones which is a big 1 up (even tho I'm not non binary myself). I also love how your favorite food becomes your name and actually every character name is the name of a food haha.Also there are many things that painting the world taught me, including that I do draw but I very rarely put colors in my drawings, but this game expanded my creativity a lot in relation to that and I might start painting my drawings from now on!This is such an original game and I can feel how much love the people behind it put into it. Definately one of the games I'll keep in my heart forever. And in a bad day(or just any regular day) I can come back and continue painting the world and adding little details to make it more beautiful. The ending is so beautiful and its message, gosh I just can't describe what I feel, it's so intense.I wish I could say much more, and I definately would, but my memory is kinda bad and I can't mention everything here rn(also because of spoilers), so do I recommend this game? YESSS OF COURSE WITH NO DOUBT AT ALLLL. The only thing I would tell people before anything is that you reaaaaalllly gotta be into painting because this game is gonna abuse of that haha. Well that's all, thanks for the experience, and thanks for reading this if you did it to the end. Gonna be playing this for a long while yet.       :)                         ~ Thank you so much Arth for sharing me this masterpiece ilu <3

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has always been too scared of not being good enough to create art, this game has spoken to me in a way no other has in my entire lifetime, especially because I purchased and started playing it while going through my last year of high school, right as I was getting my first art classes since kindergarten, and believe me, it was hard to convince myself I was worthy of trying, and I highly doubt I would have managed to do so had I not found this game, with all of its ups and downs, touching on mental health, depression, and some of the struggles people face when trying to create something, without being boring or overwhelming for the player, and all of this happens through the eyes of a little dog called Pizza (in my case hamburger =D ) that's just trying to not let Chicory down. I won't spoil the story for anyone who has yet to play this game. Still, if it helps, this experience brought me laughter, excitement, and fear and even made tears roll down my face during some of the darker segments of it, out of all of the games I've played, I'd say this one has an uncanny ability to transmit strong emotions that is on par with that of Undertale or Omori.The game itself is incredibly fun with all of its different game mechanics and keeps itself refreshing by introducing more complex ones as it progresses, while at the same time, it allows the player incredible freedom on the play-style they choose to use, ranging from the super-efficient one that can't wait to get all of the achievements as fast as possible by just drawing a few calculated lines here and there, all the way to the details-oriented player that wishes to fill in every single corner of the map in a thoughtful arrangement of colors, I personally was trying to get things to look nice without overthinking too much. Another thing that I found absolutely superb in the game is the overall art style and music, which was composed by Lena Raine, and does an excellent job of being meaningful while blending in with the game in such a way that it becomes one with the landscape rather than being "on top" of it, if that makes any sense.soundtrack 10/10art 10/10gameplay 10/10Thanks to everyone who worked on this masterpiece, you changed my life.
