_childDocuments_.review: As an avid roguelike gamer I was instantly drawn to Curse of the Dead Gods. I will admit I was not enthusiastic after my first few runs but once you get your first good run and realize how to optimize your play style to your load out it just feels REALLY GOOD. I am not done the game but I know it won't take me too much longer to get through all the content. Thank goodness for the refreshing daily one chance dungeons that load, reminds me a lot of Binding of Issac. Would really love if you added the option to play them again for practice and not rewards, some of them are really challenging but fun, so if you fail early on in your run you don't get to try again.Make more content! _childDocuments_.review: You play a guy in a big underground dungeon going from room to room fighting monsters and collecting treasure. It's one of those dodge roll roguelite games like Hades, with a light mechanic where you need to keep torches lit or monsters on fire to see traps and avoid taking extra damage. As you progress, you also acquire curses which make your life harder in a variety of ways. Oh and when you finish a run you can get upgrades you carry over to make the next run easier. Die and grind is a gameplay loop that I just find tiresome anymore and there wasn't anything new or interesting about this game compared to the others of its breed I've played.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: Curse of the Dead Gods is both a very competent game, but also an increasingly repetitive and difficult game. The rewards you can unlock start becoming harder and harder to collect as the costs begin to increase. There's 0 dialogue whatsoever and the story is largely hidden away in the flavor texts. There's no epic music to pump up some of the moments you encounter within the game and no real incentive to keep going for me.Play this game if you want to play some absolutely dark and soul crushing with intense repetition. But please do not get this game if you're interested in the story or dialogue, because to be honest. You will not get it here.

_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: Not a particularly fun loop to me.  There's a lot of interesting things here but none of them land except the art.  The combat feels clunky and uninspired, with a strange mechanic for stamina that seems interesting at first but turns into just a further way to punish your character over executing a roll or a combo.  Everything in the game hurts you, there's traps, enemies, healing yourself, simply progressing, getting upgrades during runs, it feels needless a lot of the time. And even when you do make a good run, the rewards don't feel like rewards or character progression, they just kind of fall flat.  Also there's a light mechanic that feels underutilized or maybe just poorly utilized?  Even if you light a torch in a room, there are so many enemy moves, traps, etc that will either put that light out right away or completely destroy the light source.  The point was supposed to take less damage in light, but the way it's set up it's typically more effective to completely ignore it, making me question why it's in the game at all.If you're a huge fan of this style of game with the top down combat, you might get more out of this than I did for sure.  But if I want to punish myself needlessly I'll go play Darkest Dungeon, and if I want to get some randomized rooms to kill baddies in there are better games out there like Gungeon and many others.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: Had this game on PS4 before I swapped to PC and re-bought it because it's so good. Each temple has it's own charm and flair, and the Eagle temple in particular is really punishing on higher tiers and difficulties. Each weapon has it's own perk and they all have their niche. You can get certain roles where you essentially turn into God, Thanos-snapping mobs away with one combo or even one or two swings. The movement and stamina management system is amazing, and it feels absolutely incredible mowing down mobs in front of you with high power weapons.Some critiques: Certain curses dont feel like curses at all, and some can be mitigated with a single weapon or relic. For example Bloodlust. It prevents you from gaining gold upon killing enemies, and instead heals you. Firstly that "curse" isn't even bad at all, especially if you've been getting kicked around recently in the dungeon. Secondly there is a relic you can buy that turns excess healing into gold. In runs with Bloodlust and this relic (I forget what it's called), I regularly end up with north of 50,000 gold. It's genuinely insane that this is considered a "curse". Some weapons just don't hit the mark. After a few runs I realized there is a meta involving whips, claws, daggers, and certain swords. Everything else is forgettable and/or just straight up unusable at higher levels. Specifically pistols scale absolutely terribly between tiers of dungeons.  8/10, great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: it's like hades but better,There are no cutscenes, no story shoved down your throat, no voice acting, not even dialogue.You do the tutorial and the game is yours to play with, offering a very addictive and challenging roguelike action loop.Unlike hades, this game has a proper difficulty curve, and you are not left grinding for upgrades - most of the time you die it will be because you messed up, not because you didn't get a good upgrade or haven't unlocked something yet.If you disliked the forced story and mind numbing grind of hades but enjoyed its core combat, this is definitely the game for you

Itemization and weapon design is bad. Like really bad. The economic stuff is great.While I'd recommend this I'd get it on sale, which I did, so great stuff. _childDocuments_.review: This game is solidly fun and brings back the feeling of being in an arcade with just 1 quarter. I've made it through to a champion without taking any damage, and I've also gone into a room with full health and died.  The mechanics are there to do well or to smash your face into the wall.  It is all about timing, positioning, and understanding the abilities of each of the enemies. I would like a little more variety in monster types, and once I've made it further in the game I'd like to be able to start from the higher levels, instead of trudging through the low level monsters as I work to practice on some of the more challenging ones.  The daily challenges could use a little more detail as well, but I certainly like the fact they are there - it adds a good deal of replayability.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing 10 hours of the game and grasping all the main mechanics of the game I would rather recommend it. Here are some pros and cons:PROS:- Good cell shading graphics;- Engaging yet challenging combat, with dodge and parry system, where it is required to fight smart rather carelessly button smashing;- Healthy variety of weapons and items (relics);- Interesting and innovative corruption and curses system, where with each full corruption meter you gain one punishment and positive passive skill; - Setting. North American mythology, that I personally like;CONS:- No story or plot whatsoever. You are just a random guy exploring the underground temple;- Visually non customizable character. I wish they had an option where you could change the appearance of the main character, and use various costumes.- Though randomly generated, yet still small variety of rooms/levels. Patterns of the rooms often repeated.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: While I will probably play this game from time to time still to get my rogue-like fix , this game lacks the charm and player creativity that so many others of the genre possess. There is a great combat system there to be sure but it ultimately becomes part of the problem as the slower methodical gameplay makes the lack of  items, enemy variety, and interesting bosses stand out that much more. On top of that the curses initially sounded terrifying but most of the time could be ignored or end up a buff more so than a hinderance so it felt thematically incongruent. TL;DR Ultimately this game just ends up feeling like it doesn't know what it wants to be.

_childDocuments_.review: I play this type of game a lot. But this one somehow bores me already. I can't really tell why, I'd have to play more to really make it out.It has interesting mechanics like that you have a secondary currency namely your "blood" which is more like your sanity and when a threshold is reached, you will get afflicked with a curse that has multiple stages and (not only) detrimental effects that last for the remainder of the run. This mechanic has so much potential especially in combination with the lighting mechanic (darkness has an effect on gameplay). Yet I find myself playing in the exact same way with or without the curses when they actually should make me play differntly somehow?The main issue is though, that I find the main mechanic, which is the combat, utterly uninteresting. And yet again I can't really tell why. There is interesting stuff here, in theory. You have 3 differnt weapon types. Main, secondary and a two handed wepon. All of which you need to unlock by equipping a weapon of that type. Yet those weapons are not always really of the same type. At least categorized by their behaviour. Your secondary could be a melee or ranged weapon for instance. Same probably also goes for the main and two handed weapon slots, but I haven't experienced that yet. Point being there is a lot of variety of playstyles in here. Some weapons even syngergize with a specific weapon category of this one is equipped in a certain slot.Now that I think about it, the swapping between the different weapons is also an issue for me. It always feels clunky like the rest of the combat. You can charge your weapons as well, but you can't attack with one and then instantly charge the other weapon. Which you would assue you can. But you have to push the button to swap and then release and push again zu charge. Which I find strange and unintuitive.Anyway I will test more and refine the review later, but for now I wouldn't recommend it to anyone.

Map similar to slay the spire - good feel of level progressionIn early access but feels extremely polished, have not experienced any bugs playing the game as intendedWeapon upgrades are compared side to side for convenience No heavy reading, some flavor text short enough to read, not long enough to feel like a choreNo extreme back tracking, game prevents you going back most of the timeSoundtrack suits gameplayCons:Single player, would be amazing with at least 1 other Lan player (online would be good but couch isn't the end of the world)Could have a quick tutorial/ when using something for the first time have an indicator as to what does what (when sacrificing blood, it doesn't take from your hp but adds to your corruption)Currently the same starting weapons all the time, would be fun for different explorers either through gameplay unlock or easter eggCould have a few different animations for cutscenesCould have a greater selection of enemies (but too many at one time makes it difficult when learning attack patterns)This is the type of game where you can play for hours, forget about it for a year and come back to it and experience the same fun as when you first played it.

_childDocuments_.review: The grim setting of this game is realized beatifully and the snappy animations make it feel great to play. _childDocuments_.review: Got this game on sale in September 2022 and played for a long time. Got hooked from the start on the game and had a great time. I would argue that  is one of my favourite games and I have this game of the back of my head at times. It's a shame this game doesn't have any dialogue while progressing and and story-based cutscenes or something of that kind but regardless, this game is something I will definitely remember for a very long time after I will finally beat it.Whenever I see some posts about "recommended rougelike" I never see this game getting a mention whatsoever and it's a shame because this game is very well made and is one of the best games of it's genre out there in my opinion. _childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game, but it just doesn't work.I think the main issue is that while other games create obstacles for you to overcome, Curse of the Dead Gods punishes you instead of rewarding you. So instead of obstacles that you need your Rogue-lite upgrades to power past the game just punishes you more and more the longer you play.This is actively anti-fun game design at its core. Punishing players for playing your game makes no sense. Playing longer should reward you with more and more broken things and more fun combos but in this game it just stacks curses and with the extremely limited ways to heal it just makes the experience stressful and unfun the longer a run goes.The game doesn't balance risk with reward at all, it doesn't even remotely try to. The game has frustrating hit boxes and enemy groupings that just ruin the flow of runs and then gets to hide behind "well its a rogue-lite so just try again, losing is part of the genre!" but then doesn't give you any permanent upgrades besides better starting gear. Having better starting gear only offsets the punishment mechanics and doesn't feel like you built anything, it just feels like you started stronger so you can be strong enough when you get to the end to fight through all the BS that weakens you. Overall I think the game is fun, the weapons are samey but I had a lot of fun, until I realized my time was just being toyed with and that the game is ultimately RNG dependent on if you win or not. I really really want to recommend this and keep enjoying the game for myself but I just can't as the core game design won't let me.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: Great game here.  This game got me into roguelikes.  The curses aren't all negative, some just make you switch your strategy, which makes each run just a tad different.  There are daily events that change the way your run will go, although you can only run them once a day and each day they change.  My favorite part is probably the environmental factors: luring the enemies into the temple traps, drifting between light and dark, manipulating enemies to break a wall if I cant do it myself, it's all very interactive and makes for a very fun time!If I had to pick a CON for the game, it might be the RNG factor.  I don't play a lot of roguelikes but as I understand it, you play a run 'til you die, then spend points (or something similar) to boost the power of your character.  This game, you unlock more choices for starting weapons and more choices for weapons to spawn during the run, but completing runs doesn't take away bad choices it only adds good ones.  This means that you can have 50+ hours in the game and still have runs that are crazy difficult because RNG says so (this does not happen too often but still).  So your character doesn't get stronger perse, you just unlock more tools for him to use, but you're never guaranteed any one specific tool. _childDocuments_.review: So I bought this game because it seemed very stylized, with a strong sense of what it was, and it was different enough from Hades to be worth it. All of these things were true, and it is indeed extremely fun and challenging. However, this is a true roguelite experience, and until you get good (and ideally get some upgrades) you're gonna die. A lot. And it's almost always gonna be your fault. You're gonna miss one too many parries, or dodge into a trap or get surrounded because you didn't dispatch the weaker enemies fast enough, and you're gonna bite it on a promising run. You're gonna get frustrated close the game and go do something else. And then, a little while later, you're gonna boot it back up and do it all over again. I guess that's the "Souls-like" aspect. If that's not a deal breaker, absolutely pick this up.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing and has one of the best combat mechanics out there for a Rogue-Lite. I've read the negative reviews and I would like to address them here. The fights feel like frantic duels in the deepest bowels of the earth. _childDocuments_.review: This is an action based roguelite game that’s all about exploring deadly rooms, defeating enemies, upgrading your skills and weapons all while making difficult decisions all around an interesting curse system that will plague you throughout every run. First of all, is it worth playing, is it worth your time? If you’ve spent hours into other roguelikes such as The Binding of Isaac, Slay The Spire, and Enter The Gungeon, then yes. This is an easy pick up. Though barely released on Steam in early access, it has a lot of positive reviews and it’s well deserved. This game just feels polished, fun, and definitely challenging. Not sure if there’s much a story right beyond that you’re a sort of treasure hunter who wants to dive deeper and deeper into various temples all for untold riches, eternal life, and divine powers. It doesn’t bog you down with narratives or any character development as of yet. They could change it up in the future, but right now it’s all about the gameplay. And WOW, this game takes the best of a lot of popular roguelikes and meshes it up all while putting it’s own twist on it and makes it all feel fresh. Let me give you a summary of what each run potentially looks like and then go deeper into the mechanics of things. This is a game where you’ll be dying and starting over a lot. Unlock new things to aid you in future runs. It’s all about learning the mechanics and patterns of enemies. You start in a base room where you can upgrade and customize your character via feats that you can permanently unlock to swap in and out at your leisure before runs; with restrictions of course. The better and further you get in runs will then provide you with the permanent currency needed to unlock the nodes. You then enter the next room and a map pops up, if you’re familiar with Slay The Spire, it’s pretty much exactly like that map. You can see every level you’re going to come across. You’ll plan your route and deviate accordingly depending on what you want and need. There are Gold Rooms, which usually have you fighting enemies, dodging traps, and collecting treasure. Weapons rooms which after clearing the level you can choose to purchase new equipment, relic rooms which pretty much the same thing except for status and effect enhancements like better damage with fire attacks or increase gold find. Then there’s the question mark rooms which can be anything from free loot to time challenge battles where you have to clear the group of enemies before time runs out to get massive treasure. Though this all sounds pretty standard for roguelike games, it’s the curse system that applies to almost everything you do that changes things up immensely. Everytime you enter a new floor, get hit by enemies, and heal at a shrine you gain a certain amount of curse. Even when purchasing new equipment and relics at treasure shrines you can forgo using gold and instead get the benefits in exchange for increasing your curse bar. There are currently five stages of curses that stack throughout your run. Once it hits one of the thresholds you get a random effect that sometimes messes with you, the environment, or even the mechanics of the game. For example, there are some curses that when hit, makes your character hallucinate, meaning the UI completely disappears for a bit while there’s a sort of filter on the screen. It makes it hard to tell how much damage you’ve taken. There’s another curse where instead of gold being found in pots, it’s replaced by blood. It heals you but at the same time it continues to build curse if you choose to pick them up. It’s a fun risk reward system where one run you can decide to skip everything that builds curse and try to play clean, another run you can say f it and grab every stat buff and legendary weapon you come across and hope you don’t roll bad curses. There was one run where I had two curses that really synergied together to mess with me. One made some torches and braziers have a purple darkness flame that would block all light entering it, the other curse made it so enemies would disappear in the dark and only reveal themselves in light or about when they’re about to attack. It’s rough but every run feels very different. The game is recommended to be played with a pad. I used a PS4 controller but the buttons were mapped out for Xbox so it’s safe to assume that control works as well. You have a lot of means of offensive and defensive options that drastically change throughout the run. For starters, you always enter with a torch, machete, and pistol. The torch can attack enemies lighting them aflame but it’s mostly used to reveal the room layout and to see traps and enemies better. The machete like most weapons you can exchange it for has combos when mashing down attack and a charge strike. Your secondary weapon, in this case the pistol, is very versatile, you can attack from far away, time your aim to get perfect strikes, and if you interrupt your main weapon combo with your secondary you get another type of attack. For example interrupting with the pistol you get a shotgun type of blast which has AOE and can stun. If you use a shield it bashes and pushes away enemies and so on. If you’re lucky alongside all these weapons you can add a two-handed weapon like a greatsword, hammer, spear, and more. These take up stamina whenever you swing with them. Speaking of stamina, this game’s combat system rewards timing, reaction, and planning out our next move. Certain actions like rolling, countering, and even finishing combos with your main weapon and attacking with your secondary uses up stamina. Without you can’t perform those actions and will usually leave you in a very vulnerable state. You can gain stamina back by waiting it out or doing a counter or perfect dodge. In short, the combat is slow and methodical while at the same time fast when you decide it is. Go guns blazing countering everything to regain stamina, or wait for whiff and punishes maintaining your stamina for dodges if you need to. Even though Curse of the  Gods is Early Access, it feels very polished and they have a roadmap for future content. There’s a lot of new temples to be added, difficulties, weapons, and so on. I look forward to revisiting this game every now and then. It’s a great pick up and an easy recommendation for those who enjoy roguelikes. This one’s good, guys. I was not paid to promote or write a review. All thoughts are solely my own. Thanks!

_childDocuments_.review: It's decent enough where I'll keep playing until I've beaten it 100% but is it worth it? Eh. The designer behind the stamina system never play-tested their own game because WOW is it the most counterproductive thing I've seen in a game. Basically, when you attack stamina is consumed. When you dodge, stamina is also consumed so you're punished if you attack a lot and punished if you dodge a lot. Sounds fair on paper but the result is that you just have to turtle. A 2 minute boss fight is turned into 6 because instead of getting a full combo off after dodging all of their moves, you get to tap them twice and go back to running away. Very boring loop.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this after watching Haelian (Hades streamer) play it. I've been playing rouguelikes for a very long time now. Whenever one comes out with potential I usually get it. They either have that replay-ability factor, or they don't and are good for only a few hours. This game has it. At the time of this review I only have a few hours in, but the depth is obvious. All the the different systems work well, my favorite probably being managing the balance of health, gold, and corruption. The fighting mechanics are top notch, reminding me of a less twitchy, more deliberate Hades with some soulslike mechanics for good measure. You can take it very slow and easy, taking advantage of the enemy attack telegraphs to dodge and parry your way out of rooms without taking damage. Once you get better, you will start chasing larger and larger greed kill combo's, making combat more hectic and rewarding for the risks you take. None of the enemies feel particularly broken and have clear attack patterns that can be mastered over time. This risk/reward system of fighting slow for safety or fast and loose for gold means you won't get bored as you begin to "get good". About getting good. The only negative reviews I've seen have been about the difficulty or managing corruption. Don't listen to these people. They want a game that is easy start to finish and you shouldn't rely on their reviews of a hard action roguelike. That is, unless you are like them and want a super easy game. If you are on the fence, and enjoy roguelikes but aren't sure if there is enough content, throw down and purchase this already great game with more to come. This feels like a full release with the bugs worked out, and it's still in early access. You won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Curse of the Dead Gods : By Triple F"Curse of the Dead Gods" isn't just your average type of game; it's a mesmerizing journey into the depths of an ancient and malevolent world that beckons you to unravel its secrets. From the moment you step foot into its foreboding corridors to the heart-pounding battles against eldritch horrors, this game ensnares you with an unrelenting grip, refusing to release its hold even after you've turned off your screen.The game's atmospheric prowess is nothing short of breathtaking. The dimly lit chambers exude an eerie aura that seems to seep through the screen, immersing you in a foreboding ambiance that raises the hair on the back of your neck. As you traverse through temples of both mundane and supernatural origins, you can almost taste the oppressive tension that hangs in the air, a testament to the game's brilliant art direction and sound design.But what truly sets "Curse of the Dead Gods" apart is its innovative mechanics. The risk-reward system, where you push your luck by choosing to press forward or retreat to secure your progress, mirrors the psychological tightrope walk between greed and caution. This constant decision-making injects an adrenaline-fueled excitement into every step you take, as you weigh the potential rewards against the lurking horrors that could snatch it all away.The combat is a mesmerizing dance of reflexes and strategy. The swift clashes against grotesque enemies require quick thinking and split-second timing, all while managing your stamina and resources. Each weapon feels distinct, and the ability to dual-wield them leads to a satisfying array of play-styles, from the brutal efficiency of a sword and shield combo to the reckless onslaught of dual pistols. Every encounter is a deadly puzzle, a ballet of blades that keeps you on the edge of your seat.Furthermore, the Curse system is a masterstroke of innovation. As you delve deeper into the temple, you'll succumb to an increasing number of curses, each with unique drawbacks that demand adaptation and creativity. This ingenious mechanic forces you to reevaluate your strategy continually, offering an ever-evolving experience that defies monotony.The visual aesthetics are a testament to the artistry of the developers. The eldritch abominations that lurk in the shadows are both captivating and repulsive, their twisted forms etching themselves into your memory. The intricate detailing of the environments reveals a world rich with lore, leaving you hungry to uncover every scrap of its hidden history."Curse of the Dead Gods" isn't a game that holds your hand; it's a game that sharpens your instincts and challenges your resolve. The learning curve is as steep as the temple's treacherous stairs, but with each defeat comes a nugget of wisdom that propels you forward. It's in those moments of self-discovery that the game truly shines, as you emerge from the abyss of failure, stronger and more determined than before.All in all, "Curse of the Dead Gods" is a haunting masterpiece that transcends the boundaries of traditional gaming. It's a symphony of fear and fascination, a dance of light and shadow that etches its mark on your very soul. With its gripping atmosphere, innovative mechanics, and relentless challenge, this game stands as a testament to the boundless potential of indie game development. If you're prepared to confront your fears and venture into the abyss, "Curse of the Dead Gods" awaits, ready to devour your senses and leave you spellbound.

_childDocuments_.review: While I don't write many reviews, I still do sometimes for games I love as much as I hate.Curse of the dead gods is that kind of game.First things first: Curse of the dead gods is a top-down roguelike where you scour an old Maya/Inca pyramid in order to find a way out. If you've played or seen Hades, it's the exact same kind of game. You choose a room, defeat its monsters and traps, acquire some loot or buff and then, at the end, a boss is there, waiting for you. After a run, you'll have collected some tokens to unlock weapons to find or blessings to equip.Pretty classic design and pretty well executed to boot, hence the recommendation. On top of classic mechanics, you also have a light and darkness gimmick that's quite clever. While in the dark, you take more damage and can't see traps, but some buffs give you more damage in the dark.Combat comes with three different weapons, assigned to three different buttons. One main weapon, one secondary and one two-handed. Your character has five stamina points that deplete when rolling, doing a combo with your main weapon or attacking with your secondary or two-handed weapon. Stamina points regen after a short while when not dodging or attacking. There's also a parry that will negate an attack, stun the ennemy, refund two stamina points AND weaken the ennemy's defenses, meaning you'll deal more damage for a short duration.As you can see (well, read), it's a game with a fair amount of mechanics and combat is pretty fun.So why do I also hate it? Because, beyond its solid basics, the game falls a bit short.While combat is fun, it's also plagued with an unreliable dodge. Not that this is entirely subjective, as I am not sure it is a shared point of view. But it's often happened that I hit dodge right before an attack and my character won't move, even though I am neither animation-locked nor out of stamina. Some attacks will also hit juuuust a tad before the hit actually reaches you. Sometimes, you'll even get hit mid-roll (confirmed this thanks to the slight freeze some shields provoke with their auto-parry, while my character is in roll animation). There are also some beam attacks that try to follow and catch you at a somewhat outrunable pace. Aaaand sometimes that very same beam goes from 10 to 200 mph all of a sudden. And beams are multihit attacks that stunlock you, meaning that they hit you for the entire duration.While that's on the buggy side of things, some design choices also come to ruin the fun. Dodges have a very short delay between them, but when multiple ennemies hit not quite at the same time, you can have no other choice but to get hit. As far as I can tell, you also can't dodge attacks that create zones on the ground (cursed circles, explosive barrels explosions), which can sometime appear right where you decided to dodge.RNG can get you good, not only in combat, but also when it comes to powering up. Hitting harder will come from your weapon's effects, its affixes (+30% to fire damage, for example) and the relics you find throughout your run (more damage to crits, more damage from fire, etc). While you can improve the basic damage of weapons, their affixes will never improve and you can't improve relics. This means that getting stronger is a game of luck. Either you drop exactly the relics for the build you had in mind or you make do with whatever you find.Finally, while I don't have much criticism against common ennemies and champions (the "lesser" bosses of a run), I do find the last bosses of each temple, as well as the final boss, to be a bit overtuned. Spoiler alert, there's a "check" before the final boss. If you didn't save a quite large amount of gold, you'll take damage, have your best relics destroyed and your weapons will lose a level, and therefore in power. Just before the final and brutal boss.While I have other minor criticism to make, those are the most important to me and they tend to ruin the fun in my opinion (which is my own, and not an objective statement).In the end, I recommend this game for its art direction, overall good combat and fun mechanics (light and dark, using traps to kill monsters, many weapons to use). Plus, the price is decent for its quality. But, the more I play, the more I get annoyed at some designs and the game can be pretty unfair sometimes, which can end a run prematurely.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a Rogue like with high potentialIt's very punishing, and might want to lower this a bit once the game has all it's features to let players ease into it, such as slay the spire, where you get full HP after beating the floor boss could be a good start. Right now, it doesn't have a lot of content. playing for a few hours, you will find the same floors, the same mobs, the same secrets.I would like more opitmisation choices for restarts, such as choosing the type of your starting weapons and alike (see dead cells)Hope the game keeps getting updates, i'll check it out more down the line i think.Also, ran into a few performance issues,  bad fps drops and the sort. hopefully these gets focused on, because its veeery frustrating in a gaem like this that forces milisecond time reactions from you.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: it's pretty good so far... i just beat the first exploration map. There's not much enemy variety but i guess it's not a problem for now.Regarding to people comparing it to Hades, i'd say it's mostly because of the aesthetics, everything else is pretty different, specially the combat system which relies on a stamina bar, so you need to manage it pretty well. The combat style is way more based on parrying enemies to compensate the stamina and attacking in the right time. If you do something wrong you get punished, specially by the ranged enemies which inflicts you curse.The curse bar it's a nice add to the game, the curses can be used in your favor, but they always have a disadvantage too (for example, there's a curse where you don't find coins in the chest, instead of that you'll find blood, it fills your health but also inflicts you curse). So managing this bar is a pretty important too.There are a bunch of weapons, 3 types (that i've seen so far): one handed melee, one handed ranged and two handed weapons (melee). you can equip them all together, but you can just combine combos with one handed weapons.Relics are mostly focused on passive stats like more damage, more coins etc. The map system is pretty similar to Slay The Spire. I'm really enjoying it so far, hope the devs keep it up with major updates.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: Played in beta, didn't really like it that much.Played again at release, felt way better, although I can't pinpoint why. The fighting just got a tad smoother,or maybe it's just that I only ever use Claws as my main hand weapon.Anyway, it's well polished, entry with short runs is easy, after you beat the endboss the first time the hard runs begin.It doesn't beat Hades, but it's a nice change for in between.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who is new to this genre of games, I can say that my experience playing this game for four hours and defeating the first four bosses has been both challenging and enjoyable the game-play is addictive and kept me engaged throughout.Overall, I highly recommend this game to anyone looking for a fun and challenging gaming experience
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: This is a solid rogue action game with an art style similar to Darkest Dungeon. it is a fast paced run through various dungeon levels, with 3 styles of dungeons for one of 3 gods represented by Eagle, Jaguar, and Serpent gods. The Aztec aesthetic to this game is a very nice touch.  there are weapon to unlock and favors to earn and trinkets you can wear to up your stats even further. you can also offer  either blood or gold at various shrines through the dungeon to get anew weapon, trinket, or stat boost.  As you progress, you will discover various monsters and traps of various types which can harm you OR your enemies, so use those wisely when you come across a room with mobs that also have traps. Lots of play time and a decent replay-ability factor but nothing to write home about. All this said, it is a good game-but not full price good. Wait for this game to go on sale before buying it. Why?  Because it dropped the ball on the plot. Oh the basic theme is there, and you can find out bits and pieces as to what is actually going on as you defeat a certain amount of a certain monster to learn more about it.  However-there is no narration, no overall plot, no story-and this game DEFINITELY feels lacking without it.  There was a lot of potential here story wise but they simply dropped the ball on that, Perhaps if there is a sequel they will actually bother giving it an actual story or at least invest in some narration.Summary: This is a decent rogue action game, but get it on sale. Graphic and play wise it is fine but in a field with so many other similar rogue games that have a coherent story line and narration, it is not worth buying at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: "Greed" kills, great combat feel, an Aztec temple theme, light mechanics, and the growing chaotic effects of "curses" all help to make this game stand out from other roguelikes. There aren't any ground-breaking mechanics and it suffers from repetitive gameplay like most other roguelikes, but it's definitely better than most.Don't expect to be surprised, but expect to be impressed.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: I stopped playing in april of 2021, but there was a few updates after that. I stopped playing because the movement is clunky and not very fun. Coming back after the final update, nothing's changed.According to other reviews (Even the positive ones!), there isn't much variation between runs. Safe bet to skip unless you like really easy roguelikes with no variation.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: A fun arcade-y game.  The comparisons to Hades are legitimate in that the controls and game play feel similar enough to satisfy someone missing that game for awhile, though a story is nearly non-existent.  It's well designed for what it offers, but my one caveat is that the light/dark mechanic is more annoying than interesting. Fortunately it can be minimised by avoiding powers that focus too much on it
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: Great combination of action RPG dungeon crawler and roguelite with an interesting system for gaining upgrades and rewards that almost feels like a monkey's paw at times. Feels like if Darkest Dungeon were an action RPG. HIGHLY recommend playing with a controller, as combos necessary to higher level play are nigh impossible on M&K due to the way the game is designed. Trust me.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to love this game but there are too many major flaws to recommend. They say there are roll-frames, there arent, its a parry in roll form. Not a problem if the parry and roll (more like a dodge parry) were solid, tight mechanics. However, its kinda hit or miss even when you swear your timing is right. Also, the enemies can have attacks where they disappear without warning and just strike from behind. there should just be a better telegraph for a lot of the enemies' attacks. If this was early access and the game was still being worked on, i wouldnt be so critical of these minor details, but because this is the final iteration of the game, what i see is what i get. all this just makes for a clunky frustrating experience and just makes me want to play a game with tighter mechanics like one of the Hades. BTW, i love the difficulty, the traps, the art style, curse mechanic, i even love the roguelite genre and frustrating games like the dark souls franchise. however, the mechanics are off and feel like it should be noted
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: Story is kinda nonexistent unless your  willing to read codex entries, everything else is top notch, combat is satisfying with a ton of different weapons and artifacts to combine, cool corruption system than gives u curses who can help ur run or make it harder depending of your play style, beautiful visuals, good soundrecommended for fans of roguelike and action
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: the design philosophy behind this game is amazing.most rogue likes punish you for your mistakes, making loosing all your hard work/run/what ever a bit sad as each mistake builds on the last to become a cycle of defeat.this one rewards you with it's amazing curse system, which are both bane and boon at the same time, with curses like loosing gold for every hit you take, but overall damage is reduced, leading to some really great gameplay choices (especially when there's multiple curses in play - some of which you want to keep!) you are rewarded for dodging TOWARD the danger with the roll systemyou're rewarded for achieving a split second weapon parry by weakening the enemy - but missing this precise timing means you take a potentially nasty hit.the weapons are quite diverse (though a few do shine quite brightly compared to the others) and allow for very different play styles and each hit feels like it packs a punch.The developer clearly took everything about the rogue like genre and turned it on it's head -I really can't praise this game enough!
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: The game is beautiful, no doubt about that.. but the combat is brutal.. and unforgiving.and they don't ease you into it either.. no explanation about anything, your just tossed into a map with first enemies that can lunge from halfway across the map and chunk your health away very very quickly.once you learn the parry mechanic is doesn't make things any easier.. as you can only parry 1 enemy at a time, and they attack in droves. with ranged casters nuking you from afar, trying to position yourself to get a good parry off will very quickly deplete your stamina and leave you unable to attack.the fact attacks are tied to your stamina is very stupid, you can either dodge. or attack.. not bothI played it for about 2 hours and I have to say this needs ALOT of tweaks to welcome new people to the ARPG genre.I cannot reccomend this game as it stands now.. for only 20$ I mean that's not a lot, but is 20$ worth the frusteration? I don't know.. not feeling it so far. well see how it pans out over time.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great, and it is a full game despite being early access. difficult with a rewarding combat system where you can really learn what your favorite weapon combos are and the havens (healing shrines) are placed in a fair enough way that your run isn't doomed if you sustain a lot of damage from the boss. There is easily 15-20 hours worth of content (or even longer if you're bad). This game is easily worth $25 as is.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: This game is tough to use cheese strategies, it comes down to timing and planning with parry and dodge, and  a serious large heap of luck on each run. controls are a bit difficult to get used to at the start in my opinion, the map is all set on top down diagonals but the controls move you in true WASD straights so you are always toggling between 2 directions to achieve smoother movement. I definitely agree with the developer that a controller with thumbsticks is recommended for this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: As part of the apparent 1% of the people who finished this game; it itself is like the curse mechanics of the game:+VERY NICE TO GET INTO-VERY HARD TO RECOMMENDList of curses__________+No characters that flirt with the main characters or constantly quip at each other.-No character interaction whatsoever. Paper thin plot that is only in 1 page long journal entries.+Once you have discovered an item combo that can mow through enemies you're set to win.-YOU HAVE NO CONTROL OVER THE ITEMS YOU RECEIVE. Even if you boost your perception (Luck) it has no effect what type of items appear.+The game has a course that gradually increases in difficulty, as to help people get into the game.-No training room where you can test mechanics like parrying after the initial tutorial.+The game has boss fights that are unique, memorable and exciting to fight.-The Dark avatar of the serpent is just a DPS check. You probably can't defeat it initially unless you have proper damage items.FINAL CURSE:+The final boss is exhilarating and tests your planning and resource management, overall a great conclusion to the game.-After you feel good after defeating it; the game pads itself by asking you to do it 3 MORE TIMES UNTIL YOU GET THE END CREDITS.-------I like the design, I like the combat mostly, but 70% OF THE GAME IS UP TO LUCK. This makes it hard to recommend to people looking for something that purely tests your skill.A well made game bogged by bad decisions in its final release, the daily quest mechanic is baffling for a rogue-like game. Best of luck to this studio as the team has potential and talent.

_childDocuments_.review: Curse of the Dead Gods, developed by Passtech Games and published by Focus Home Interactive, is an action-packed roguelike dungeon crawler with a dedicated following since its release on PC. With its challenging gameplay, intricate mechanics, and dark atmospheric setting, it's no wonder this title has captured many new fans. While this game doesn't feature a traditional narrative, it does offer a rich and intriguing lore that players can uncover through exploration and item descriptions. The game's world is steeped in mystery, with ancient gods, cursed relics, and forgotten civilisations all playing a role in the player's journey. This approach to storytelling is reminiscent of games like Dark Souls, where the narrative is woven into the fabric of the game world itself, rewarding players who take the time to delve into its secrets.At its core, Curse of the Dead Gods is a roguelike dungeon crawler, tasking players through procedurally generated temples filled with traps, enemies, and treasure. The game's combat system is both fluid and punishing, requiring players to master a variety of weapons and abilities to survive the onslaught of foes that stand in their way. The curse system further amplifies the game's difficulty, which adds a layer of risk and reward to each run, forcing players to weigh the benefits of acquiring powerful relics against the potential consequences of accumulating curses.The game features a variety of mechanics and systems that work together to create a deep and engaging gameplay experience. The game's combat system is a standout, with various weapons and abilities catering to different playstyles. Players can wield swords, spears, and bows with unique move sets and properties. Additionally, players can acquire powerful relics that grant them new abilities or enhance their existing ones, allowing for much customisation and experimentation.The game's curse system is another key aspect of its design, as players accumulate curse points by acquiring relics, taking damage, or performing specific actions. Once a player's curse meter is full, they will be afflicted with a random curse, ranging from minor inconveniences to game-changing debuffs. This adds an element of risk and reward to the gameplay, as players must weigh the benefits of acquiring powerful relics against the potential consequences of accumulating curses.The game's procedural generation ensures that no two runs are the same. Each temple offers a unique layout, enemy placement, and treasure distribution. This keeps the gameplay fresh and engaging, as players must adapt to new challenges and opportunities with each run.One of the standout features is its unique light and darkness mechanic. Players must carefully manage their torch, as standing in the darkness increases the damage they take and reduces their vision. This adds a strategic element to the gameplay, as players must decide when to risk venturing into the darkness to see the temple's ruins or suffer from the unseen.Curse of the Dead Gods boasts a dark and atmospheric visual style, with detailed environments and enemy designs that evoke a sense of dread and danger. The game's use of lighting is awe-inspiring, as the flickering torchlight casts eerie shadows on the walls and highlights the intricate details of the game's various traps and hazards.The sound design is equally immersive, with haunting ambient music and bone-chilling sound effects that perfectly complement the game's oppressive atmosphere. The clang of weapons, the growls of enemies, and the creaking of ancient temple doors all draw players deeper into the game's world.Curse of the Dead Gods is a challenging and rewarding roguelike dungeon crawler that offers a deep and engaging gameplay experience. With its unique light and darkness mechanic, intricate progression system, and immersive graphics and sound design, it's a title that stands out in a crowded genre. While its difficulty and reliance on RNG may be off-putting to some, those willing to embrace the challenge and delve into the game's dark and mysterious world will find a rewarding and addictive experience well worth the investment.

Even if this game was abandoned tomorrow by the dev team, it'd be worth the money. _childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: I laughed at the reviewer who called this "Hades 2.0". There is no story, no engaging characters, no voice-acting beyond monsters screaming, and the music and sound effects are repetitive nothings. Neither the dodge mechanic nor the enemies' attack patterns for parrying are consistent. Get ready to get hit by attacks through obstacles, dodging, and parries. If you don't RNG yourself the weapons that the game likes at the start of a run, you're SOL. The only interesting thing about the game is its art.2/5 stars.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not Hades 2.0, and unfortunately that's why it's significantly underrated, as many rogue-lite newcomers don't accept anything else and approach the game with false expectations.In fact, Curse of the Dead Gods is one of the best rogue-lites I've ever played and the combat system is just brilliant.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: Steam Deck homies, do not miss this! Great game, great performance!Amazing surprise of a game with very satisfying skill-based combat and new and interesting mechanics. The whole game is just pure combat. No narrative, no cutscenes, no unnecessary bs. Get on, do a run and see how far you can get. It is not a full-length rougelite like Hades (with which it has things in common), levels are split into tiers and different temples, each of which you have to complete in one go, you can pick out of many levels and temporary events with different modifications (updated each week) and your "build" will be tied to that run.You keep couple of currencies between runs which allow you to make your subsequent runs better.For those who heard "it is just like Hades" - it is not! It is a different game that has some similarities with Hades, but Hades is a narrative, dialog heavy game, where the wonderful combat is tightly connected to that and feels more "hack'n'slashy". It also has different progression structure. In Curse, combat is much slower, weightier with a type of dodge stamina, and feels similar to the Souls games. This game is all about this combat and is a "get on, do a run, leave" kind of game. There's nothing here besides this combat. And this combat is great, easy to learn, difficult to master. And build/weapon diversity is great as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: Been watching this game since it hit Steam in EA, was waiting on more content and consumer reviews. This game doesn't disappoint, the temple runs are engaging and thoughtful. I love how much decision making this game allows with with the in-temple run shrine shops. Making the choice on what items and how much gold/blood/corruption I'm willing to sacrifice. These devs have quite the little gem and I cant wait to see what they add in the future. If you like Hades and Binding of Isaac, you'll love this. Fair warning, it does play a bit slower than Hades but you don't notice it.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first Rogue-like game to completely suck me in. The enemies are varied, there are tons of weapons, and the progression through getting crystal skulls and jade rings is very entertaining. There are so many different synergies with different blessings to choose from, and I have already found quite a few weapon combos that work very well for me. All of the 3 temples have a distinct feel to them (being based on 3 elements: fire, poison, and electricity) that all have different enemy types that compliment them each respectively. I highly recommend this game to anyone, as I have never fully dived into a Rogue-like game like this until I gave this game a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Take the fluid combat and weapon variety of Enter the Gungeon, add in a dash of Slay the Spire level picking and pathing, and add in a healthy touch of Spelunky/Indiana Jones cultures for level design and artistic motifs/aesthetic and you have this gem of a game. It may only be Early Access but it shows incredible polish and potential ahead. Ingenious mechanics and skillful combat make Curse of the Dead Gods a game to pick up if you are interested from the sounds of it so far or if you are way to keep your eye on it as it develops. _childDocuments_.review: It really is a fun game at the start with some interesting mechanics for fighting and dealing with the environment. Movement with a game controller feels fluid, dynamic, and well designed. Combat is also fairly fluid and enjoyable with many monsters / bosses using interesting mechanics that can be dodged or parried.Areas for improvement:* The enhancements available at the start of a run seem lackluster. There is the ability to "unlock" weapons to acquire in future runs, similar to Dead Cells, but is limited to weapons and only a few of each type (including a cursed weapon). Favors (let you re-roll loot pools) have little value.* There's only a few weapons and weapon combinations that seem to work well in the dungeons. Expect to master claws and swords because those are the best. Slow / 2H weapons are occasionally viable but extremely situational due to massive stamina drain and enemy reaction time.* Progression is not fun. Each time you defeat a boss for the first time, you're sent back to the beginning. There is no way to progress further in that run. It sucks to get a good run with good RNG and then be told "go back to the beginning" for no reason.* Each run is distilled down to collecting skulls and rings (the only items that persist across runs). A few of these drop from enemies while exploring, more of them drop from bosses and champions, and that's about it. The rest of the run doesn't have any lasting impacts on character progression. This feels very limited.* Almost all of your skulls will be used to buy upgrades to the weapon tables, which end up giving you more choices and better odds for rare / cursed weapons. No other attributes can be improved outside of purchasing 1 of 3 enhancement slots that give minor boons for a run, such as +5 Perception.* Many folks point out a lack of story. The Codex is helpful here, but beyond that, it would be nice to have any sort of clue as to why I should care about this guy entering a tomb over and over again. :)

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this after it left Early Access because I loved the art style, the gameplay looked close to Hades, and everything looked very polished (for the asking price). Overall I was correct in my assessment and was initially pleased with my purchase. Sadly, the longer I played, the more flaws became prevalent, and the less I wanted to play. I took a break from it to wait for patches and there have been some good QoL updates since then. However it wasn't enough to fix the main problems I had with the game: poor difficulty scaling, tedious boss fights, and poor resource management. Initially this would've been a cautious recommendation but now I am disappointed to say I can't recommend it.If the aesthetics of Curse of the Dead Gods are enough to sell you as a casual gamer, then this might be worth it for you. There's a lot of detail put into real-time lighting, environmental effects and traps, enemy animations, punchy sound effects, and a great atmospheric soundtrack. I wish all of this was packaged into a better game; I'd love to support games with more Western art styles with all the anime and faux-anime games flooding the market. Unfortunately, the rest of the game is your typical amalgam of  repurposed game design ideas from other popular indie games. It's yet another rogue-lite with no save system, a floor selection chart like Slay the Spire, combat like a slower-paced Hades, bullet sponge bosses like Gungeon, and stacking sanity debuffs that feels similar to Darkest Dungeon. Player movement and attack animations feel like they were programmed by someone who doesn't play video games. Animations will often lock you in place or in a direction: rolling can't be cancelled or redirected, melee attacks lock your movement into the animation, and attacks have to finish their animation to deal damage. This sounds like nitpicking but these problems add up and make the game feel clunky, dated, and console-ish. All of this is also weighed down by the stamina system which is consumed by anything you do besides basic attacks. Charged attacks, heavy weapon attacks, and dodging all consume a stamina point and you only have five by default. This means if you run out of stamina during a fight, you can't dodge. Perfectly dodging or parrying an enemy attack will restore stamina but you have to do this so much that it slows down the combat. The parry window is also so narrow that it's not worth the risk of taking damage or wasting a weapon slot on a shield.Speaking of damage, you might as well not have a health bar outside of boss fights. Default health is fine on paper for normal fights but the invincibility window is too small for all of the rapidly attacking enemies and AoE attacks that are throw at you. Enemies will quickly chew through your health if you miss a dodge, effectively ending a run because of a bad room. Early on, the damage and healing scaling is manageable but later on (in the meat the of the game) healing is too infrequent at tier 3 & 4, with an average of one healing floor between each boss. For comparison, this is roughly the equivalent of one campfire between bosses in Slay the Spire. Many enemies also deal corruption damage which can lead to difficult-to-remove stacking modifiers, with the final curse just being a constant DoT that eventually drops you to 1 HP. Every floor will add 20 corruption no matter what, with the default max being 100. This also isn't a huge deal until the last tier where it increased to 30 per floor, basically pigeon-holing you into boss rush mode to remove curses between the actual boss fights. The visible issues with corruption and curses are only part of the difficulty scaling problems. Tier 1 feels like a tutorial for each boss's zones and made me wonder if the whole game was going to be a cake walk. Tier 2 is a huge leap in difficulty but is manageable with some skilled movements and knowledge of mechanics. Tier 3 will really make you sweat but can eventually be defeated. Tier 4 feels like some kind of sadistic joke, where everything and the kitchen sink from the previous tiers combined is thrown at you, and yet they also felt the need to add more bosses and more corruption stacking too.Sadly I can not recommend Curse of the Dead Gods. I really wanted to like this game but the only really original concept it has going are the aesthetics. Like the design philosophy of grabbing everything they could think of from other popular indie rogue-lites, you can feel the bad design choices from their amalgamation congeal into a frustrating, padded concoction of pain. This is yet another indie game that you might enjoy if you plan on never beating it; personally I am tired of buying games that are clearly a handful of hours of content padded by randomization, permadeath, and absurd difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: I like the game. I like the pacing and how it's slower and more methodical than Hades. The art is great. The combat is fun and responsive. You start by having to beat 1 boss at a time. Then two at a time. And I'm presuming it will eventually be 3. (I'm not that far in).Some improvements I hope get implemented. A little bit more monster diversity. It's good right now, but even a few more or some more varients  would be great. I'm not sure because I haven't beat it but it looks like there are only a handful of different bosses, and you know which ones you are going to fight ahead of time. It would be awesome to see these expanded upon. IE instead of 1 boss per "path" maybe a random of 2-3. That would go a long way because the boss fight's are actually great. This would bring some more diversity to runs and have more of that WOW factor when you first fight a boss.All in all, it's good. For sure worth $20. (I got it 10% off at just under $20). _childDocuments_.review: It's a nice little roguelike in EA. It shows promise, both in the core gameplay and the upcoming content. I have a few grips with it, like the sheer ammount of health damage and curse damage the enemies can do (especially compared to the ammount of health you can get back), rendering some runs pretty much outright unwinnable. The bosses are quite alright, a bit frustrating at first with the sheer damage they can do in a few seconds while you're still learning the patterns, which means all your hard work to get there ends in about 3 seconds, but once you get there with enough health to get a grasp of the patterns, they become fairly simple, provided you don't make any mistake as they are punished a tad bit much.I've played harder games, but this game is fairly challenging, no mistake about it. If you're not into games that beat you up until you master them, this likely won't be for you. That being said, despite the simple moveset of the enemies, bosses, AND yourself, the game is pretty satisfying to play. You're equipped with a torch in the first slot which allows you to spot traps, a primary weapon in the second slot, a secondary weapon in the third slot, and a double handed weapon in the last slot. The second and third slot are used together, so in total, you have three "stances". The moveset consists of one combo, one charged attack per weapon. Just a charged attack for ranged weapons. And a combo combining both your primary and secondary. The enemies usually have one to two patterns, whereas the bosses have about three. No complex patterns, but satisfying nonetheless. You need that simplicity because the game offers you two very different ways to tackle your defensive strategy: Dodging, which is a fairly safe and efficient way to dodge, it's the standard way. It does give you an iframe and although it's a bit inconsistent, there's rarely ever a situation where dodging is not feasible. One of the exceptions is when you're out of stamina, which is used to perform most actions above. Your alternate defensive strategy is much more powerful, doesn't consume stamina, and is quite difficult to perform: Parry. It behaves as you'd expect, though you need to parry every single incoming hit individually, it has a very short frame of active parrying, and it inflicts a debuff on most enemies which makes them take more damage. It's a skilled approach to the game that WILL require practice in order to be pulled off in such a way that you gain anything positive out of it.Your goal is to go through a temple riddled with traps, enemies and chests to loot, as you choose which type of rooms to progress to with the limited paths you're provided depending on where you go... All of this to ultimately kill the last boss of the run. Well yeah, it's a roguelike. I'm sure there'll be a bit more lore as the game leaves EA, though.Many parallels can be drawn to other roguelikes such as Hades, Dead Cells, Slay The Spire, and so on... but they are only superficial. This game implements mechanics seen in a ton of different roguelikes while making them its own, which is appreciated. There's a very Soulslike approach to combat aswell.The game puts a lot of attention into small details that matter, like the ambiance, the animations, the sound design, the ability to move freely during certain attacks which can be used as a clever way to dodge, the way you can use enemies to light up torches, push them into traps, and so much more. The sound, music, art are all pretty well made, and the dark atmosphere of the game is very enjoyable, you do feel like you're stuck in an unforgiving temple where the shadows are out to get you. Which they might be more than i let on. The game has a clever mechanic of curses that can give you mostly negative modifiers if you get enough curse damage, so as to force you to have a strategy. Curse damage is obtained by getting hit by certain attacks/enemies, just for entering a room, aswell as an alternate currency for altars that can give you buffs, passive items, weapons, etc... when you don't have enough golds. Get enough curse damage, and you get... a curse, which will usually make your run a tad bit harder. Get 5 curses, and you get an uncleansable curse that will spell doom for you, trust me on that one.Overall it makes me want to play it more than once, and that's a good sign for a roguelike/lite.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: I've played just a bit more and what I state below remains the same, but with a caveat.After doing four full runs, I now firmly believe the devs are fully aware the game isn't as sharp in its handling as other roguelikes and have simply chose to let it be that way.Why else would they make you an absolute TANK?I'm used to having to dodge/parry perfectly in these games to avoid enemy attacks because every hit is extremely punishing and draws you closer to an untimely end. Your character is nimble and the tells are very clear so that you're forced to plan tactics to separate enemies and pick them off one by one as best as you can.Curse of the Dead Gods ignores this principle and instead makes you an unstoppable force of nature. There's been times where I've cleared an entire room without dodging because enemies die in a few strikes and it's more effective to just rush them and attack while fully taking any hits because they barely sting. The only thing you have to watch out for are traps.This is true even with bosses: they're sort of imaginative for the first 2 minutes, but then you realise they're just sponges with simple patterns. I fought K'ax taca and tanked nearly 1400 damage because I accumulated 2100HP easily and could just ignore his attacks and hit him straight until he fell.It's a shame because the game is gorgeous in every way, but I honestly don't recommend it over any other roguelike.----I've only played a little bit so far, but it's already a bit of a tough choice.Roguelikes depend almost entirely on their gameplay and this game's is... not that great. The controls are not as responsive as they should and a lot of the cues (when an enemy attacks or when a trap activates) are so poorly communicated that it only makes it even more difficult to play flawlessly.Everything else, from the aesthetics to the curse system or the upgrades range from fine to excellent, but the combat itself (the core of the game) could be a lot better. If you have to choose, go buy Hades or Dead Cells first, they're much more apt options for this particular genre.----

_childDocuments_.review: Curse of the dead gods has a lot of things going for it. A wide variety of weapon types, a uniquely interesting art style, and combat that feels generally solid. I wanted to give this a meh review because although I had fun playing for the few hours I did, I honestly just don't feel like the progression system feels very rewarding. Instead of the structure of most roguelikes, such as Hades or Enter the gungeon, where you have to make it through 4-5 biomes, beating bosses and eventually reaching the end, this game instead has you beat a boss, then beat it again on another run followed by another boss, then that same thing but with a third boss added on. This is repeated across 3 different biome types, each with their own sets of traps and enemies. I think the variety between the 3 biomes works, but extending the next run's length after a victory doesn't feel very rewarding and makes it seem like much more of a chore. One of the main ideas behind this choice of design I'd assume is that it forces you to think about handling your curse meter much more. But honestly the game is quite lacking in this department as well. The curses all generally seem pretty weak with few exceptions and so don't feel like much of a threat. However, the 5th and final curse can often be quite brutal and has the complete opposite effect. One I got was constant reduction of health per second which quickly ended my run and didn't really give me much of a chance of winning at all. All in all, it doesn't feel quite balanced or well paced nor does it particularly stand out as groundbreaking in any area to keep me wanting to push forward. I think one of the big changes that could be made is getting rid of the runs with only the first/second bosses in them, allowing for more satisfying and less dragged out wins, but the game also seems designed partially around this grindy system with its unlocks so it would certainly take some work. But if you just want to try something new out and it looks fun, give it a shot as there is some enjoyment to be had, especially if it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Hot damn, what a ride. I tried this out during early access and put a good 80 hours into it. The art style is sublime, the animations are crisp and clear, the sound effects are solid and the overall look and feel just oozes style. I struggled immensely to beat the final boss of the first temple (fire) as the game was absurdly difficult at that time and that was the extent of the content. I put it down for a while after that, feeling quite proud of myself and excited for what they'd come up with later.I picked it up again a while after it released and at the time I was pretty soured by how much easier they'd made it with starting weapon loadouts, being able to trash items for permanent buffs/money, and a bunch of new weapons and affixes that far exceeded the rest. I was blazing my way through the new content without a care in the world ... until I beat the 'final boss' only to discover there was even *more* difficult content waiting for me. At that point, the game finally felt like it originally had again and I enjoyed it immensely. You really have to get to grips with timings of enemy attacks, because the higher difficulties are much less forgiving. You'll start to pray you find certain artifacts that increase your survivability, but since you can't rely on those appearing, sometimes you have to push on and give the next encounter the old college try until eventually you fail, learn, and try again. Put the game down, take a breather and come back refreshed again later. Once you've got it down, previously difficult encounters become a walk in the park (although the final boss of the lightning temple was my personal nemesis, always giving me grief). It does a decent job of giving you that 'making do with what you get' feeling of the best roguelites, and while I do think those mechanics could be improved in a handful of ways, they weren't dealbreakers for me. Some weapons and effect combos are clearly head and shoulders above the rest, so its a bit of a shame its so easy to cheese the starting weapon loadouts to find something 'viable' (aka that pumps out massive damage even without upgrades), but amazing weapon set or not, you still won't get far unless you learn patience and read attack animations properly, so its somewhat forgivable.It was a joy to work through to finally beating it and I'm looking forward to starting a new save somewhere down the line and seeing how far I can get with the fewest amount of meta-progression upgrades unlocked (if any). If you like Roguelites, and Stamina/Dodge/Parry-based Combat, this game is absolutely worth the price of admission.

_childDocuments_.review: Couple things to get out of the way first: this game is not a Hades clone and shares very few similarities with Hades, and this game is absolutely amazing and you should buy it right now. This game is a perfectly executed combination of a number of previous ideas meshed flawlessly to create a game that is truly greater than the sum of its parts; it takes a weighty, Dark Souls style combat combines it with a Slay The Spire style mapping system, adds a Darkest Dungeon type light and corruption mechanic, and combines all that with an almost X-Com style resource balancing metagame to give a top-tier rogue-lite experience.The combat in this game is sublime, and its clear that a lot of time and effort went into perfecting the balance and feel of the experience. Enemy attacks are clear and avoidable, stamina management is hugely important, and each weapon type has a unique style and feel to it that completely changes the way you play the game. There are about 15 different weapon types split between Primary/Secondary (that combo off of each other depending on what you have in each slot) and a Two-Handed Weapon. Generally the primary weapons are faster and allow more mobility and stamina reserve at the cost of damage, while the Two-Handers consume stamina when used but do more damage and can stun enemies. For the metagame, you will be juggling several important resources as you make your way through increasingly difficult and complex temples. First is your corruption, which you naturally gain as you go through the temple and can be inflicted by enemies. As you accumulate more and more, you start to get corruption debuffs that will change the way you play. It is very important you not get too many of these as if you get too many you will receive a final, utterly debilitating curse that really hurts your changes. You will also accumulate gold, which you can spend to purchase upgrades through your run or alternatively you can trade corruption to get the upgrades - balancing these things is very important.Along each journey you will have to balance these two currencies (gold/corruption) to make sure you have the damage, healing, and stats that you need to make it to the end. One thing that I really enjoy about the style of this game is that the progression becomes more of a calculating balancing of things you need to succeed, and the risk you're willing to take on; you really need to plan ahead to optimize your run. It is less about finding a "broken" character build to create a very powerful run, and more about surviving by making good choices. The best part of this all is the subtle design choices that totally magnify how you play you play the game. There's a lighting mechanic that impacts your damage and how much you take, there's a high combat skill ceiling on the combat with a parry mechanic and rewards for timing dodges perfectly, there's a basic elemental system where weapons can have elements that give certain bonuses, there's a long term progression system with perks, each weapon has a sub-type that dramatically changes how you use it, There are so many small things that work perfectly to make this game so much better than it would have been and I can't even list them all.This game might be my favorite rogue-lite every and it is in danger of being a serious contender as one of my favorite games. Buy this game.
