_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: 7/10A challenging Roguelike that has a great atmosphere and a growing challenge of Curses during your run, but lacking in some areas of diversity.Thoughts:I bought this game a while ago but only started to really play it recently. In my runs I found there is a lot to enjoy but there are certainly some grievances that I came to foster as well. I'll break them down into Pros & Cons. Pros:Visuals -It is a very simplistic cartoony style in Curse of the Dead Gods, but with the color palette chosen and the lighting effects (and how lighting can actually be a major influence in your run) it makes for an immersive and visually impressive delve into the depths.Gameplay-Curse of the Dead Gods is fairly punishing for making mistakes, but all mistakes can be avoided. I still have not cleared the Jaguar and Snake temples, only the Eagle. But I can say all the mistakes are my own, it doesn't ever feel like I've been cheated by the game in my failures.Enemy Variety -No temple feels the same, there aren't too many types of enemy in each temple, but no champion or boss fight nor their minions feels the same. Each has their own attack patterns or effects and take different timing or approaches to handle them and prevail.Sounds Effects & Ambience -I am unsure if there is even music for most of Curse of the Dead Gods, only in champion/boss fights do I noticeably hear them. But the impact noises of your weapons and enemy attacks, the sounds of traps and the ambient sounds of the temples are all very resounding and immersive, you can feel when you dodge, land a hit, parry or are struck or at least attacked (as enemy attacks have sound effects as well even if they miss).Pros & Cons:Curses -You will always incur some form of curse in your runs, to this games credit there is a large plethora of them that can change up how it goes. However there doesn't seem to be any kind of filter based on how cursed you are to which curse you get. Some curses are harmless, or can be ignored, and can even inadvertently help you. Other curses if you have the bad luck of getting them early can completely destroy your run. You can only remove a curse by defeating one of the champions, and offering a cursed items to the Gods (but they have an extremely low drop chance so this is a rare occurrence). It would be better if some of the more damaging curses were reserved for being cursed a third or fourth time, rather than the chance of getting them as your first curse.Cons:Weapon Diversity & Feel -In a much smaller roguelike like this one, it is important that there either be a large variety of weapons, or that the weapons feel significantly different to use. Curse of the Dead Gods only has 13 weapon types broken up into 3 categories (main hand, off-hand, & two-handed weapon slot). There are variations on each weapon with their affixes, but they function exactly the same, more on the affixes in the next point.13 seems like a decent amount of weaponry right? But when some of them feel terrible to use, or feel exactly the same as another weapon type it ends up at a much smaller number. For instance swords and maces, one handed swords and one handed maces function exactly the same with the exception of the charge attack; and even worse two handed swords and two handed maces don't even have a difference in their charge attack, two skins, same function. So at that point it only matters what affixes they have and damage they deal.Throwing Weapons, the only main hand ranged weapon, have a terrible range. Which makes most of them (except for the one type with longer range and the chromatic daggers) come up short compared to other main handed weapons. They should reach much further being a ranged weapon, currently they reach about as far as a two handed spear, countless times I have dodged an attack and tried to return fire only to come up short with this subpar weapon. Their charge attack, only throws knives in four directions, it would work much better as a frontal cone or six point attack rather than a four point compass.Pistols are awful; each shot takes one stamina (the same cost of two handed weapons, which have much more effect), most don't do that much damage, and their only combo (Most offhands have two) is just a cone knockback which doesn't work well with most main weapons outside of the throwing dagger.Weapon affixes -With weapon diversity coming up short you would think the affixes could compensate, however, there are some dead affixes and others that are just a lot weaker than their counterparts.Fire damage for instance is the worst of the elemental affixes, unless affected by a flame trap, enemies take little damage from the passive damage from being on fire. The Lightning and Poison affixes are just better hands down.There is also a common affix, or at least it keeps trying to be pushed in my runs, of dealing more damage when behind enemies. This is a dead affix, only the Charge attack of the claw will reliably place you behind enemies, otherwise with stuns only lasting a split second and you being your enemies only focus, you can't ever really take advantage of this as they are always facing you.Overall Curse of the Dead Gods is a fine game, definitely worth the purchase and your time. There are just some things that could be patched to function differently to make your weapon choices more varied and their different combinations more prominent in how one functions differently than the other.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, a challenging rogue like. Just when you think you have it all figured out, it gets harder. When you think you FINALLY beaten the last boss.. it says, "Oh, was that too easy Sissy-Boy! Let's START THE REAL GAME!" At night.. when I sleep.. I hear the game.. laughing.. laughing at me... In summary.. plenty of content and worth the $20 at full price!
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: So far, so good. I discovered the rogue-like genre with Hades, so ill compare it to the only other one I know. I was was looking for a new one, and Curse of the dead gods seems to do the tricks for now. The game doesnt have that much weapon/skills variety, but it does bring some cool stuffs to the table, such as the curses, the endurance system and parry/roll for an example,The gameplay itself is slower, but requires more focus in my opinion than Hades. Difficulty wise I cant tell yet, since i am only at the beginning, but it will surely be a challenging game.I will edit my review when ill have more hours into the game, but at the moment I strongly suggest it.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to say it, but this is not good (or fun) yet. There is not enough here to make it interesting beyond the first run. The same RNG maps, weapons and baddies. It gets dull real quick. The combat is a drag and is not enjoyable at all. And it is too difficult by default. A rougelike does not have to be punishing, look at Dead Cell. I hope this gets there, but it is not yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: The combat is by far my favorite thing. It is so incredibly rewarding once you get the hang of mixing in weapon swapping and parrying to your rotations. The itemization is also really satisfying as there are a lot of things you need to consider balancing; needing hp restore and corruption management is just as important as damage and health, etc.As someone who has been playing for a long time my only complaint is that the universal currency shared between all the unlocks (blue skulls) should be more diversified. I haven't had a chance to play with a lot of the blessings you select in the lobby because I prioritized unlocking the weapon altars and increasing the rarities of the offerings. The green rings used for different weapon specialties I think is fine cuz it really pushes you to complete the more difficult temple explorations, however, everything else being tied to the blues, which you also don't get many of per run (especially if you don't kill a boss) really stifles progression and can make you feel like you are playing the same game for a long time.Overall though, if you like fast paced arpg-esque combat that rewards good reflexes and timing, and you dig the cool dead/aztec aesthetic, I can't recommend this game enough! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked diablo Ii lord of destruction and played since .08 and have been messing with games like POE to itch the scratch, THIS IS IT. THIS IS THE GAKE IVE BEEN WAITING FOR! Insane replayability with super core fundamentals. Relics and gear make builds and you know what you want. Game is extremely difficult but fun. I started after patch where things seemed a little too easy before reading patchnotes. Game is at a perfect spot right now if you as me
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: Curse of the Dead Gods is a modern roguelite following in the footsteps of Rogue Legacy, where progress can be made between deaths. Progression during game feels inspired by Slay the Spire, where you choose from a couple different types of rooms to move into.Combat rewards fast fingers and twitch reflexes, like a 2D isometric Dark Souls. Rushing in will only get you killed, and quickly, but with smart tactics and using the terrain, traps, and layout of the map to your advantage, even waves of foes can be taken down. Healing is few and far between, so evasion is important.I can see the potential in CoDG already, and I think I can get the same kind of enjoyment from it as I did from Rogue Legacy. With it being in early access, only time will tell. Right now? I'd say it's worth the grab.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: Curse of the Dead Gods is a very solid action roguelike; if you're a fan of the genre you will definitely enjoy this game. The art style is wonderfully dark & moody. The combat is fast-paced, weighty, & satisfying. There is a lot of variety to be had in building your character for each run, based on many weapon combinations as well as the light/dark mechanic & the risk/reward system which allows you to take negative curses to make your character stronger. The game is fairly difficult but not too frustrating, especially for veterans of the genre. Make sure to use a controller rather than your keyboard!The only negative thing I can think to mention is the lack of variety in room layouts, enemies, & bosses. You will be fighting the same enemies over & over again in the same scenery, especially in the latter half of the game. If there were more bosses & enemy types to mix things up a bit, the game would stay fresh & exciting for a lot longer.Overall I'd recommend Curse of the Dead Gods to any fan of action roguelikes.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: Its really fun. The weapons system is pretty similar to dead cells, at least in some aspects. The system with the energy points (i forgot what they were called) is new for me and kinda makes it harder for someone like me who is used to hades where you can basically spam dodges without really being punished for it. In my opinion thats not a bad thing though as it just takes some time getting used to it.The curses put a nice twist to it and also add a lot of replayability. The games artstyle is great and fits the vibe of the game very well. Same goes for the music.I did not come across any bugs or glitches yet.Overall Curse of the Dead Gods is a great and fun roguelite and thus i recommend it to everyone who is a fan of the genre. However, i wouldnt recommend people who never played roguelites before to pick this game as your first roguelite as its pretty hard compared to other games like Hades for example.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: Not sure about another review I saw.  0 framerate issues with 2080 TI RTX.   So far I'm really enjoying this game.   I hope to see more enemies in the future but thus far it is very very good.  Spent about 4 hours to beat the second plot.  The gameplay is much more direct and less button mashing vs Haydes for example.  Timing is way more important as well as managing your stamina meter.  There are also many traps etc that you must avoid but can as well use them against your enemies.  (BTW not knocking Haydes just trying to note the differences I love them both)
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: This is a simple roguelite with an Aztec\Mayan mythology setting (which is almost the only reason I bothered to review this, I appreciate original setting or themes). The gameplay focuses over dodging and perfect parrying to get you more advantages and survivability. Combat is fast and the rooms are small. The main gimmick is that you get curses the more you get forward, reaching a breaking point to the last when health keeps going down until 1 hp. The curses are double edged knives, many have advantages more than disadvantages. Also you can trade your hp for upgrades and weapons, making it a trade every time you need to improve your chances.There is also a lot around keeping the lights on since if you are in darkness you take more damage, and this is also something kept in consideration over curses and advantages.Not the most interesting or complicated roguelite I’ve seen but it’s ok if you get it for cheap and you need something new to add to your menu.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: Very high risk/ high reward style of gameplay. Playing overly cautious can hurt you in the long run, it's worth being reckless at first and bombing a few runs just to get a handle of how it can help you when you inevitably get better at the combat. There isn't a whole lot to the game right now, but what is there is already extremely polished and well executed. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: It's a seriously fun and challenging game.I'm not super good at games like this, so even defeating the Medium challenge at first was pretty difficult (you have to beat the short campaign, then medium, then long in order to unlock the next set). The end of each section has a boss to beat, and just making it to each one to then just start learning how to fight it can be tough!I've started to get a better feel at what works and what doesn't, or how to roll with what the game gives you. It was a supremely rewarding feeling to beat the Long run, which ends with the actual "Boss" of that Temple (currently only the "Jaguar" temple is unlocked, with another temple in beta branch).Each run you collect 'skulls', which drop occasionally from regular enemies, but a bunch will drop from each mini-boss and boss. These let you buy blessings (you can equip up to 3) that give a unique benefit, as well as divine re-rolls (you can swap the items in the shrines during a run for each divine unlock), so there is some permanent progress between attempts.At the moment, it's got some lack of variety for the available rooms, which they hopefully will improve on. You'll definitely notice that you're in one of the dozen or so layouts within each section of the temple. Of course, that also helps you be successful since you know what to do.The "Corruption" mechanic is pretty unique. Going through the door to each next room adds to corruption, at and every 100 (or 120 with a blessing) corruption, it resets to 0 and you get cursed, which adds a modifier to you that can both hinder and help - for instance, you'll do extra damage while in a lighted area, but taking damage will send a pulse of darkness out that extinguishes light."Greed" also rewards you for chaining kills without taking any damage, and it increases the gold you get from defeated enemies, which can be spent on weapons, stats, or relics at shrines along the way. The map allows you to choose what section you go to next, which will tell you what you'll find there (unless it's a ?), although not all paths connect.Really looking forward to more updates. They're planning for at least 3 full temples, they've just added stat tracking and a bestiary in-game. I'm sure there's even more cool stuff coming. I usually find myself popping off a run a day just for kicks. I've got further to go to beat the hardest challenges.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: Hades clone with less story and more punishing boons. People complain game is hard but i think combat is way easier than hades. Not much replayability but there is different bosses. No cosmetics to unlock or characters to interact with just straight up no nonsense dungeon crawler. Its good just short. Instead of unlocking cosmetics for late game you are unlocking perks and weapons.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: It's a decent roguelike with a serious difficulty spike here and there. After 30+ hours I haven't seen the true ending yet. The combat is very fluid and you get those 'just one more run' cravings all the time. Yes, it's somewhat unpolished. Yes, there's almost nothing spectacular in the game except the core gameplay loop. But the loop more than compensates for it. If you invest time to git 'somewhat' gud of course.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: For me this game is on a weird threshold between "fun to play" and "why do i even bother playing?". Unfortunately steam only let's me recommend or don't recommend. Otherwise it's 3/5 for me.An action roguelite comparable to Hades. It is challenging but overall fair i think. The combat is fast-paced and the controls work well imo. Graphics are nice and sound is servicable but unremarkable. There isn't much of a story beside what the title and intro give you.During the first few runs the game is pretty forgiving; getting hit doesn't give you too much damage and failures can be attributed to you not knowing attack-patterns or mismanaging your ressources which is expected of a roguelite. In terms of ressources you need to manage health, stamina for some of your attacks and dodging, corruption which gives you curses after reaching certain corruption levels that are double-edged sword passives and gold to buy weapons, weapon-upgrades and relics for passive effects. Especially in later stages you meet enemies that kinda delay some attacks which can be quite annoying and those attacks paired with traps and AOE attacks can take a lot of speed out of the game to a point where it feels like you're more dodging and waiting for a moment to attack then necessary. Most of the time i got hit it was because i wasn't careful enough or positioned badly though often it felt like the game cheated a hit out of me and especially when you're on hard mode even single hits cost you dearly. Other people commented that they felt somewhat inhibited by the stamina system but thats part of the difficulty imo though I think it makes some playstyles less attractive. That being said since you can parry most attacks which doesn't cost but restores stamina you can get by with excessive parrying though that takes better timing than dodging. If you feel like you're not good enough but still want to finish the game you can activate an assist-mode that turns off achievements and "marks" your save file as an assissted file xDProgress feels also kind of slow since it comes mostly from you getting better while aside from three perks most roguelite-typical permanent upgrades don't feel very impactful since it's mostly new weapon unlocks and among weapon types there isn't much variation in playstyle. That also means that the game gets stale very quickly since you're mostly looking for the same stats and weapons while there are only a few different types of rooms to clear and bosses are always the same. What i especially disliked was that the "early" game made you decide how many bosses you want to attempt during your runs which can keep runs short if you're short on time but why not give the option of going on if you're on a good run or leaving after a boss if it's not going well? Seems to stretch the game unnecessarily...Overall the game is alright but for me a little short of being good. Combat is fast-paced and fun but gets stale quickly and progress depends on you getting better while the game gets progressively harder without offering much of a hook to keep you playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoying the hell out of this game. My one issue is that the block mechanic seems to be a touch too frame perfect. I am definitely improving at this significantly but it took me like 8 hours to get the first boss. Just make blocking last like one more frame and it wont feel like you get unfairly ganked even when making strong plays.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: I love ancient temples, Indiana Jones themes, isometrics and roguelites.  This game is almost as if it was built for me.  Those things alone would have made me plays this game for 30 hours at least.  But now that the novelty of that has run out, I find more mild annoyance with this game than love of the game.  Some people compare it to Hades, but that's like comparing a hydrogen bomb to a coughing baby.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: Another good roguelite game, but this one doesn't make you feel overpowered after new runs. This game like Dead Cells, but way slower and tacticalNo lore or story provided, it's just simple isometric action roguelike, so i advise you to play this game by listening something on the background like i didGame doesn't require that much skill or focusing, it's just all about weapons, some of them good, some of them bad, play more runs and hope for good RNG, which is actually controllableThis game made technically very good, has potential for DLC's, so you rly can buy and play it, especially if you like this genre
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: This game has some of the finest combat I've ever seen. It's methodical, predictable and very difficult, but more than that, it feels *fluid*. Every weapon has had love poured into its moveset and you're constantly finding rewarding synergies, combos and strategies to use them better.Like the dark souls stamina bar, the stamina points in this game give you the ability to both attack and defend, and managing them is a large portion of the combat experience. The game is utterly transparent about its mechanics -- there is a stat for health, a stat for damage, and a stat for magic find (a genius idea in a roguelike, where magic find can be the tactically correct thing to do sometimes). There are plenty of more complex interactions, and the game very clearly spells them all out for you in the menu if you're curious -- no guesswork. It's refreshingly simple and open with an incredible amount of depth built in.Simply the best.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely worth $5, not sure about much more than that. Fun rogue-like with pretty good combat and an interesting mechanic in the light/dark.But after about an hour you'll pick things up and not move much farther. I was able to beat the 2nd and 3rd bosses on my first try once I got the game play loop figured out and began to spam the bomb secondary weapon. But if this was really made by a single developer than kudos, it looks good and plays well. Just a bit minimal.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: I have been enjoying this game immensely even with the high difficulty of getting used to everything going on. aka balancing gold, curse, health, and stats. So far able to consistently get to the second boss on a medium floor. Great combat and quite fluid. One issue that has been consistent however, the game tends to crash frequently whenever my controller disconnects. other than that no issues! Love it
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: Fun roguelike with high skill ceiling action in the same vein as Hades, Dead Cells, Rogue Legacy, and similar. Assist Mode allows for adjustments that make the game more accessible. I played with improved parry window, which made the game significantly more fun to me. I can easily imagine any of the available settings doing the same for other players.The game features 3 distinct biomes and Slay the Spire inspired navigation. Environments are beautiful and well made, but patterns in the random generation are quickly spotted, which leads to stages feeling samey after extended play. This doesn't detract from the gameplay, but is worth noting.The game's biggest problem is an uninteresting meta progression. Meta currencies can be spent to unlock new weapons and improve loadouts, but very few feel worth unlocking. As a result, the game doesn't have the same longevity provided by similar roguelikes.With that said, I'd still fire up this game, rather than any of the other games competing for my attention, if I have 30 minutes to burn. A very enjoyable experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: great game though the weapon system feels a little unbalanced. get big sword or hammer and swing til you win but damn is it fun and despite breezing through the first 5 "levels" i hit a road block and is now proving to be quite challenging. hoping there is some good end game content after the pantheon as that is rapidly approaching!
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: Curse of the dead gods is an incredible game. Extremely well made with satisfying combat, interesting enemies, and unique mechanics that make it stand out from other roguelike titles. The curse mechanic helps keep things interesting and forces you to adapt your play style in unique ways on every run. The game can be challenging, so don't come here looking for a casual walk in the park. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: This should have been called Dark Hades Souls.Jokes aside, I liked it more than Hades (even though Hades is a 10/10 game), because it is mostly skill-based, you don't need to grind for ingame currencies to progress. There is no story here, so your main motivation to keep playing is increasing difficulty and satisfying combat.The game is brutal at times (the reveal of the final boss is rage-inducing the first time you get there). However, most of the enemies are well designed with clear and well-telegraphed attacks, so it's all about you learning their patterns. It took me around 20 hours to finish base temples, and than around 50 hours to finish hard-mode temples - they basically expect you to play perfectly, dodging almost every attack and stacking optimal relics+weapons. For those who want 100% achievements - do not buy, one of the achievements is way too difficult to get, you'll need to learn every boss move and defeat them without getting hit 10 times each.Curses are a very interesting mechanic for a roguelike, they seem as penalties at first, but soon you learn that some of them are actually quite helpful, and use this to your advantage.Anyway, it's great, I hope they make a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: I've been thinking for a long time what rating to put on the game. On the one hand, quite an interesting gameplay, smooth animations, a well-balanced level of difficulty (make you suffer, but not burn your chair). But after playing for a week, there is a feeling that the game was abandoned halfway. The absolute absence of a plot, a monotonous soundtrack, there is no sense of progress during the game.4/10, only if you are a fan of this genre of games.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: TL'DR: A perfect grand slam, double thrust to perfect dagger evade proccing crits into a perfect dodge in the light while your enemies are on fire and .... sadly very little reward for your efforts   The tragic story of wishing there was a middle ground of recommendation. I've opted to give the thumbs up and trash talk here, because in the end I've had a lot of fun with this and maybe I'll have a further change of heart down the line (though I doubt).Combat system (which has it's moments of glory) and the tacking on of more and harder enemies eventually turns to frustration and feeling like battling out of the duldrums. I'm decent enough at these types of games; and here, once you're into the 3rd tier temples, it's just not that fun. This sucks because that's when the game starts looking cool. It's where you start having enough enemies to justify the way too frequent micro-pauses both in and out of combat (waiting for the door animation, waiting for the corruption animation, waiting for stamina to not be gone, waiting for enemies to make moves, waiting... yeah?). And then when there are tons of enemies instead of the 3 or 4 per room you get early on, they are all elite. They behave quite differently and have loads more health while your own weapons which you attempt to upgrade basically start to feel like shooting spitballs at rocks. As well I'd wager more than half of the games mechanics are pure fluff. It looks like there are many weapons and bits of gear, but for the most part all the affixes don't amount to much of anything and the gear is interchangeable. Once it's all cooking with gas even if you get lucky enough (and it's basically pure luck, but not like Isaac or Hades where there is also curiosity) and manage to match all the elements to buff each other and your runs play style.... it doesn't feel like it matters. At all. Those +10s if; +20s whens; Perfect x triggers y? The numbers are too small to notice. A perfect grand slam, double thrust to perfect dagger evade proccing crits into a perfect dodge in the light while your enemies are on fire and .... sadly very little reward for your efforts.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: Already a pretty fun game. The gameplay is extremely good and satisfying. You can feel the weapons, rolls are tight and parries are rewarding. Everything has just the right speed so the gameplay isn't too frenetic and you have always control of your character. Every death is your flaw just like in Dark Souls. Sometimes the RNG can frick you over with a really unlucky drops but that's part of the game + you have so many options how to minimize RNG. It's up to you. As I said the game is already a pretty fun thing to play but we shall wait for what lies ahead. I'm not very sure what the plans are for the future but currently there are 4 dungeons you can play (starting with only one unlocked) and only couple tilesets and enemies. Weapons have random affixes making them fun to loot and the graphics are sweet but I honestly hope we're going to see more modes, more tilesets, more enemies and more of everything in general. As of now this is a careful recommendation - the gameplay is amazing but the content probably won't entertain you for more than 10 hours. If the development goes in the right direction this might honestly be one of the best isometric action rpg games ever created.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun top down action game here. Love the rogue-like elements as well. Highly recommend if this looks cool to you.Update:There is a full games worth of content here. I want to stress this. Whats great about this rogue-like is that path choice matters and all choices make you stronger. I feel like I have a few favorites locations at certain points of run I lean towards. Ex going for early weapon. But every choice allows you to become stronger in the end. Really enjoyed this one. I want more, can't wait for 3rd temple to unlock.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: It's quite a different take on rogue-like genre, it's more of you choosing what exploration you want to take. It starts of pretty easy, so you have time to learn how the game works and prepare for each boss, and I think that's quite neat, though some people might consider it repetative. I loved the mechanic of curses, which don't just nerf you down completely but actually balance it in a fun way. What I had issues with is the difficulty spike once you get further, which eventually made me quit the game. I have to say that even though I was failing many times, it still felt fun and I always could tell what my mistake was, so I think it's fair.Good game, bought it on sale, worth the buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: Already a solid 8/10, really curious where this games going to go after Early Access.First saw this from Pat's stream ( @PatStaresAt ) and was really drawn in from the art design and the overall presentation - what I wasn't expecting was how amazing the game feels to actually play. While its challenging and engaging past the initial challenge, the game expects you to achieve a comfortable level of mastery of its very forgiving controls. The ebb and flow of the health / gold / curse mechanics seems pretty compelling and I'm curious to see how deep those difference go.Pick this up if you're in for a great dungeon crawling good time with an aesthetic that evokes Darkest Dungeon and Incan Cult Horror.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: Im no fan of DeadCells and about the 300 other  16bit pixelated indie side scrollers that followed after that; but I am loving this game.The light (torch) mechanic is a nice touch.And the curse(s) mechanic to pay for upgrades is  a fun way.Only negative remarks is that:random curses and gear appearing can lead to a great run or a short run (but everyone should be used to that one)no story or npcs. It would be nice if a story and NPCs to appear.The theme is Aztec gods. I would much have preferred a mad/evil ancient western spire. But that would only be a cosmetic difference.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: The people who have the platinum trophy for this game should probably get a psychiatric assessment...The people who have just finished this thing should probably, at the very least get therapy...Finishing this game was the most harrowing experience I have had playing any video game. Dark souls and even sekiro don't hold a candle to this. 30-40 minutes of progress can be lost in a split second on the final difficulties. I actually caught myself chuckling like a mad man when I died. I would recommend this game for the lower temple runs, but to those that seek the higher temple runs.... only despair and madness await you.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: It's kinda... meh?Everything in the game is designed to ♥♥♥♥ you over while giving very little reward at the same time.  Even completing the room punishes you. It doesn't exactly make the game more difficult, it's just annoying, you know?Relics/powers/boosts feel the same - "+10% damage from heavy weapons", oof, okay, very exciting.Music is very repetitive and forgettable, and they've got balls to sell it? Good one.Performance is kinda wonky, FPS constantly jumps between 72 and 144 FPS which leads to a noticeable jitter all the time, very annoying.There's also no story what-so-ever, soooo... can't recommend, nope.
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: First few hours are fun but that's it. At the moment I would even say its false advertising:'Dozens of enemies' - there are like 4 different enemies in the whole game'30 curses' - In 12 hours of playtime I have seen 5-6 curses and 1 final curse (literally 1 final curse in the game...) '11 fighting styles' - feels like best case 4, every weapon feels the same, its either a main hand sword/mace or thrown, secondary is either a shield/gun and you got a two hand weapon that is either sword/mace or a bow. If you've seen it all get this on sale and enjoy for a few hours, if not buy Hades and enjoy for a couple hundred hours.I really wanted this one to be good but it's not.Disappointment / 10
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review: Great game so far, I feel like there's a lot of content to go through in its current state, which I think is alpha. There is also persistence, you can unlock things to help you permanently allowing some satisfaction even if you die, as long as you collect the currency used to unlock those things. I like this way more than deadcells, it borrows the travel system from slay the spire, which is awesome / dynamic (changes every time you play) and the weapons are randomized with cool status effects, there are relics that give passive buffs like 10% extra sword damage or mace damage, and there is a good variety of weapons. 15 ham sandwiches out of 17
_childDocuments_.name: Curse of the Dead Gods

_childDocuments_.review:
You seek untold riches, eternal life, divine powers -- it leads to this accursed temple, a seemingly-infinite labyrinth of bottomless pits, deadly traps, and monsters.

Your greed will lead you to death, but that is not an escape. Rise to fight again. Delve deeper again. Defy the malignant deities that linger in this place. Battle through hordes of enemies in dark, cavernous passages filled with traps and secrets of all sorts -- fire-spewing statues, explosives, hidden spikes, and worse.

Collect mystical Relics and an arsenal of weapons to make yourself unstoppable. Corruption builds in you with every step -- encourage or ignore it, but each powerful curse can be a double-edged sword.

name: Griefhelm
detailed_description: Check out my new game About the Game Griefhelm is an award-winning party game with lethal medieval weaponry. Skewer your friends, deflect their blows, and push your advantage in fast-paced duels. Clash and clang it out in couch co-op or online multiplayer. Find some friends and cut off their heads! Practice your skills with a challenging, replayable campaign as you uncover the secrets (and the loot) of this strange land. Then battle your own way with or against your friends locally or online. There is no rest for the worthy. Keep your head attached to your neck and claim your eternal reward! Features: Master 4-player online combat! Slay on the same couch with up to 4 people in local multiplayer. Unlock weapons and armor in a lunch-break length campaign, designed to be repeated with new challenges each time. Visually striking art style and hand crafted environments bring the world of Griefhelm to life. Oh, my children! Let not your hearts burn within you! For your suffering and anguish shall be made into that which is perfect, incorruptible and true. Go now. Prove yourself worthy of Griefhelm.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has expanded drasitcally on the tried and true formula of both Nidhogg 1 & 2, with a variety of maps, weapons, and armor to unlock which will keep you busy for hours to come. The AI, although occasionally buggy, offers lots of singleplayer content along with the online multiplayer & the local aswell. This is a great game if you're willing to overlook the occasional bugs (albeit not gamebreaking) until the developers iron them out. Graphics are a solid 7.5/10, the combat is a 8/10, replayability is a 8.5/10, and the variety of weapons/maps/armor is a 9/10. Would definitely recommend if you're looking for something to keep you occupied for some time if that be alone or with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: 🔹 takes its cue from some renowned niches in gaming like , and the . It emphasizes on a methodical action as there's a fine line between death and glory in this game. You are in the boots of a medieval knight who fights his way through a branching campaign You traverse from node to node through a set of stages, each challenging you with a leader battle at the end before progressing to the next location. Despite its flaws, The game is an amazing effort for a project made by a single person.Mechanics are fairly easy to pick up and play but overcoming the learning curve presents an excruciating difficulty spike since the tutorial barely covers the more advanced footwork and swordplay. The final boss is a lot faster than normal enemies and also wields a much bigger swords than the likes players have access to, making him unfairly challenging. That being said, I haven't been able to beat the final boss by the time of reviewing the game. Both attacking and parrying are based on high, middle, and low stances. If you're holding your sword high, for example, any incoming attack from that stance will be blocked and can be utilized to do a riposte, shove, or a chain of blows. Talking about chained attacks,  rewards well-timed blows with more speed for the next swing and punishes those who mindlessly mash the keys. This creates a high skill ceiling that can't be easily mastered but becomes enjoyable over time. I must admit there's an unspeakable satisfaction in lunging your weapon at the enemies no matter how unskillful or unplanned your move was.In  timing your attacks are more important than wielding effective weaponry. It turns out getting up close and personal with your opponent while holding a big battleaxe or a spear is a sure way to take a dirt nap. On the other hand, short swords or maces must be swung face to face or enemies find an opening to strike back. But the swordplay can be a bit clunky. Sometimes the tip of your weapon might gently touch your foe and happens to be a death blow while at other times, a perfectly calculated swing might just slip through and signs your death warrant.As for now,  has only three modes to choose from. In the Horde, you'll face several enemies at once, increasing in number and strength as waves pass. Skirmish tests out your skills in a best-of-five one-on-one battle. Tug of War tests out your patience in a fight over territory. This mode is the most intense one out of three as there's room for only a few mistakes. Tug of War battles can be a drag since enemies respawn more quickly compared to you, not giving you enough time to progress much further.When checking out updates and changelogs of the game, I noticed that AI has been tweaked in some ways since the release but still it doesn't behave accordingly to the difficulty level of a mission. This makes a brutal difficulty gap going from cadet to expert and master. It happened a handful of times during the campaign that enemies on the cadet difficulty or lower managed to string several moves into one unblockable combo and kill me immediately. Au contraire, they stood still so I can take my time killing them on the master difficulty.Is non-existent so far, both in single-player and multiplayer. I'm hoping future updates can bring more life to the game. The only sense of progression that could be given is the occasional better weapons and armors you obtain from certain missions throughout the campaign and encounters. Additionally, each mission rewards you with a single-use perk. Once they're equipped for a mission, they'll be consumed right at the start of it. These perks may offer extra lives, leeching health out of enemies to fighting on horseback and so on. But when you develop a good sense of how the game works, the advantages you get from them become so insignificant that you can pretty much ignore them from start to finish.Public sessions are already dead. I've been trying to find random people to play with over the course of two weeks but I had no luck. However, the means to play co-op are so varied that make up for the lack of players. Your options are online co-op, steam remote play, and couch co-op to ensure your fun along with your friends.Stages in  might be one-dimensional but the intelligent use of a dynamic background added a nice level of immersion to both visuals and the gameplay. The ethereal vibe with the fog and heavy white saturation makes the game really stand out. However, not all maps are so colorful and bright. The crypts and campsite, both taking place in the dark, utilize the shadows and lighting effects to create unique sceneries and spice up the fights.As you may have expected, medieval and epic soundtracks are all over the game. Perfectly intensifying the battles as your opponents wail death-cry when your sword meets their flesh (yes, they scream out loud when struck). However, some of these tracks give more of a Japanese/samurai vibe than the European crusades. Moreover, I liked the weird poetry given in texts between campaign stages that vaguely represent the chivalrous conducts of medieval knights.🔹🔹Specs: GTX1050 2GB - Athlon II X4 645 - 8GB DDR3 RAMThe game runs with all settings maxed out using about 60% of VRAM at 1050p 60hz.🔹🔹🔹 is promising and fun but I've put in a dozen hours, nigh beating the campaign and thoroughly trying the other game modes. At this point, it's worn thin for me. Combat is at the center of the focus here and proves to be tense and enjoyable at the same time, without rigorously pushing you to take on the complicated depth of newer fighting games. Although, it could use more polishing.You can see and feel the empty places of some of the intended necessities for the game but how long it takes until they're in action? Lack of progression is somewhat off-putting and I think time is the only thing this game can't afford to lose as it's already being abandoned by players. Pick it up on a steep sale as $20 isn't justified for the content it offers for now.

_childDocuments_.review: I retract my good review. It is a mediocre game. The mechanics are good but there are so many little things that piss me off. -The battle modes are so one sided, you can wipe multiple teams of enemies while being stuck in the same spot, due to the fact that they infinitely respawn on horses which means they have double the health. You team being wiped means the end of the level, regardless of wether you hit those fake "checkpoints" that just respawn your allies if they're dead, it doesn't even heal you or give you a slight buff. The mode rewards you for sprinting past everyone and getting to the end to stop the respawns.  -The weapons of your allies in these battle modes fully determine if you'll be able to beat it or not, since if the game decides to give all your allies short swords, you'll get speared by the crowds. -The camp and tent levels, as well as the last level (this really made me mad) have lighting done by a 5 year old with down syndrome. you can see maybe every couple of feet, and god forbid you want to be able to see the giant sword or two-hit hammer they're swinging at you. -Weapons aren't different. There's 2 really good ones, the mace and the hammer since they do extra damage and (for some monkey reason) are just as fast if not faster than the other weapons, the mace being swung by the enemies like its made out of styrofoam. -The combat is decent, but spamming the guardbreak button after every hit beats any sort of tactics, since the hitstun is long enough, especially if the enemy gets lucky and gets the kick guardbreak animation, almost doubling its range.

_childDocuments_.review: Review changed to positive: +The developer is active with the community. +Lots of great changes since last review.This game - oh so almost - scratches an itch that I've been having since the first Bushido Blade. I got this game at 10% off which came out to just over $20 CAD. If this game had a deeper sale or (even better) was slightly improved - I might be recommending it now.The game recommends a gamepad but does NOT bring out its full potential. It has a great basic idea where the right analog stick determines the stance of your knight... but with only three options: high, medium, or low. They missed a great opportunity to incorporate defensive/offensive by not utilising the X axis on the stick. This means there are only three attacks which feels so limited. They way the training is done makes it FEEL like you will eventually learn more - but no. There could be at least 6 basic attacks (7 if they let you attack without moving the stick). Just look online to see how many stances there were in medieval sword arts.The jump feels awkward. These guys are in full armour but they can just bunny-hop around the screen.It feels like the weapons, despite having different animations, act alike.I'll play this for a bit more - but I think without some small additions, it is a game that will get old fast. It reaches for an itch and almost scratches it - but just barely misses the mark. Patch 1.1 was released recently - I have some hope that they might add a few more things to the game. I do enjoy the game - but I can't commit to recommending it as it is (state and price).Wait for a decent sale - or wait to see if they patch beyond 1.1.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is interesting, reminds me of Nidhogg (enough so that I thought it was directly inspired by it) but with a nicer graphic style, beautiful backgrounds and a nice diverse set of weapons. Unfortunately, unlike Nidhogg, the gameplay is clunky and needs some serious tweaks. _childDocuments_.review: Bought on Winter Sale for $8It's fun, it's medieval Nidhogg in every way. High/Mid/Low block/attack system, plus checking, kicking, dashing, and turning around. I'm super excited to try the local multiplayer after playing the campaign last night because....The campaign is scripted-ly difficult, featuring horseback riders that you *cannot* block. I've also parried a move in the campaign to get parried IMMEDIATELY back by the "Expert" CPU to then kill me and take another one of my precious lives. Parries are meant to be a 1-way deal, not "well I parry your parry!"The shove works fine, the feints work fine, footwork, dashing, I'm excited to get to play this with friends at a party tonight, but the single-player is beyond aggravating. I got it on sale for $8, worth it just for a more authentic Nidhogg kind of dueling game, but only with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: Clearly inspired by 2014's Nidhogg, Griefhelm is a more serious alternative created by Johnny Dale Lonack and published by .Being serious doesn't mean that is not as fun. The game builds over the original roots by presenting a medieval setting under strong production values, gorgeous graphics, accessible but deep gameplay mechanics and an array of game modes that includes online duels, campaign, online and horde mode; where countless opponents will test your skills in battle. There is a limited but fun customization of our warriors where you choose different accessories and different weapons to bring the gore to your enemies. Griefhelm could become 2020's biggest surprise. The potential is there but it definitely needs more work.At the time, there are bugs here and there that affect the experience. Some physics are a little bit loose, the online capabilities are a little bit buggy and on the graphical settings a V-Sync option it's tremendously needed as well as an option to control the amount of blur that feels too extra in what should be a more grim game. The campaign feels a little bit shallow in comparison to the game's strong suit that is the Local Couch Mode, where you can set up a 4 Way Dance with your friends and it's where really the game shines.The developer set up a post-launch road map, where most of what seems to be missing will be introduced, including Steam Achievements, more weapons, and improvements on campaign mode and multiplayer lobby. I wish the game's stages are also improved and can provide more variety in how they impact the gameplay more than just being eye candy. I am really pleased with my time spent with Griefhelm and I strongly believe that the game is worth the money for the local couch mode alone, even with the technical glitches and shortcomings that seem to be caused by a last minute upgrade on the game's engine. I trust in the vision of the developer. As a fan of Bushido Blade and Nidhogg I don't think there are too many of these games out there so the proposal feels fresh and I am convinced that the game will become a strong contender for the best in the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: The comments are right: immediately recoginzable influences are Nidhogg-styled gameplay mixed with Mordhau's style and a higher level of complexity in combat. This results in a truly awesome combination.Only played Versus-mode with some friends so far, but we already had a blast with it. Fighting is stylish and there is a lot of room to grow and get better. Running towards your adversary hacking and slashing like in Nidhogg will only get you killed fast.We liked the implementation of unlocking items even during party play: after a few rounds of Versus, the player with the most kills total gets to fight against an NPC, unlocking new stages, weapons and armor upon victory.The stages we played so far are all very nicely designed and fun to play in. Each has a small detail that makes it unique, like the Crypts, where you battle through darkness from light source to light source.The weapons feel different in their handling, having different range and speed, and it's cool to make your own knight, especially after unlocking some gear. I got this game on sale, and would deem it worthy of every cent. Full price is slightly too high imho. Around ten bucks is perfect.

_childDocuments_.review: This has quickly become one of my favorite games ever. The combat is so simplistic, yet unpredictable and complex, which makes every battle tense and endlessly entertaining! It's comparable to titles such as , , , and a little bit of  in there, too. The physics are super brutal and quite funny, at times! I love impaling someone with a spear and then flinging them off, or watching how flails actually hook around some weapons when they clash! It's amazingly satisfying.The aesthetic is top notch and blends very well with the eerie music that makes for makes for a great atmosphere. The theme that plays when you are approached by an adversary is very tense, especially! The maps are varied and have very interesting elements, such as limited visibility with reliance on light and shadows and some interactive environments. The content and replay value is expansive, having not only a rogue-lite, randomized campaign, but also a fully tweakable encounter mode where you can make your own unique battles with bots! One on one jousts with spears is very fun! I have yet to try the multiplayer component, but I am sure it'll be great.All and all, this game is a gem! You can tell lots of love went into it, and the dev is a very nice and responsive sort, seeing from his posts in the forums, as well as my own brief conversations with him!  recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: While i cannot agree with the game being ready for a full release (it should have been version 0.8 or something like that), Griefhelm is a masterpiece in the making with an extremely active group of developers that constantly interact with the community in discord. Make no mistakes - Griefhelm is HARD. Ever heard of Nidhogg? Griefhelm is harder, and it's single player gameplay is rogue-lite - meaning it's a very difficult game with a sharp learning curve. Gameplay is quick, brutal and satisfying, like a lunch break-sized Mordhau. A brutal game of rock, paper, scissors, Griefhelm features intelligent, fast-paced dueling behind gorgeous visuals in minimalistic levels.I believe in the developers' abilities to fix, improve and polish the game. It could probably have used another couple months in development before full release, but the devs are nowhere near done with working on it and we, the community, are welcome to contribute to the game's growth.For the most part when it comes to issues, the AI can make some frustrating decisions from time to time. Later in the game they outright cheat - breaking the rules of combat, animation canceling, straight up ignoring staggering and striking directly through your block. I hope it will be fixed soon. Occasionally they might ignore a shove, or strike you through your block. But otherwise, the game handles like a dream - in PVP it feels decently balanced and although skill intensive, also accessible to beginners. Everything happens very quickly and matches rarely drag on - you could easily play several rounds with a friend during a lunch break, for example.I highly suggest you give the free demo a try and see what you think of the game. You get access to the main gameplay loop of Griefhelm, letting you see exactly what you are getting yourself into. If you like what you see, please support the developers to help them keep up their work - their passion in the project is contagious and if nothing else they deserve to be given a chance to show what they can do. Griefhelm has the potential to become something amazing - and the developers actively welcome and encourage us to be part of the process. They are doing all the heavy lifting, but this is still a team effort. No matter how this turns out, it's an adventure i will look back on with nostalgia in ten years from now. You can be part of that too, if you want to.

_childDocuments_.review: Given the hype through its showcase during the Steam Summer Games Fest, I was eager to dive into this side-scrolling combat game. Upon playing, its apparent that the developers went to extreme measures to ensure that the replayability and graphics were up to par with other competing titles. The ability to hop right back into the fight after a bloodthirsting, yet gratifying, battle with little-to-no downtime is incredible. Not to mention, the lighting effects and shaders are among some of the best I've seen. Evidently, through the numerous updates that were already implemented, this is a team that listens to their community and utilizes its critiques. I'm super stoked for the future of this game and would recommend it to anyone that enjoys true to life combat and convincing medieval details.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game for anyone looking to stretch their strategic reflexes. The campaign, gamemodes, and multiplayer are all interesting and will get you your money's worth out of the game. However, the depth of the combat system is what will keep you engaged and having fun the entire time. It's definitely the defining feature of the game, and is overflowing with polish. The combat feels very fair, with each blow, parry, and feint giving you openings and leaving you open to attacks from others. Another fun, unique feature is the ability to customize your knight's armor and weapons. Each piece of armor has unique stats, but more importantly, each weapon plays completely differently. There is no other 'class' besides being a brave and daring knight, but that one knight has a multitude of options when approaching any combat scenario. The campaign is fairly challenging, and half of the fun is finding quirks to exploit in the enemy AI. It features unique mechanics such as earning gear for your knight and single-use perks giving different advantages for a battle. There was obviously a lot of thought put into the campaign's node system and how it tells the narrative of a knight fighting to regain forgotten honor. It gives each battle unique context and drives the game's feeling of worthiness and chivalry. Atmosphere is an important part of any game, and this one gets it right. The art style is clean and consistent, and all of the maps are beautiful battlegrounds with their own unique properties and pretty views. I highly recommend this game to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a  surprisingly small fanbase for what I consider to be the best version and evolution of the massive side scrolling VS game, Nidhog. Griefhelm has fantastic combat, great additions to the system, and can be a true treat for a party. With up to four players, even using AI, it can get really strategic and visually spectacular! There definitely is some jank, I believe due to the single man development. For example, why have 16 weapon slots when there are only 8 in the game? Why have the font and UI generally be ugly and hard to read? Those are things teams usually work out, but I can understand falling to the wayside if the single dev isn't very passionate about those particular pieces of the puzzle. I'd also say a huge amount of time was put into a single player "campaign", when in my mind, this type of game is inherently boring playing exclusively against AI. Either way, Griefhelm is a great success in it's core gameplay concepts and is a real treat to play. It seems like it's completed in it's development lifecycle, so here's hoping the best for the developer on their future projects!

_childDocuments_.review: Griefhelm is a fun little action game in a pseudo-medieval setting, which I discovered recently and fell in love with. It offers lots of cosutmization and weapons, a singleplayer campaign, singleplayer and multiplayer costum fights called "encounters" which you can design the way you want by chosing your equipment, the enemy's equipment, different rule sets, the stage/level/map and the exact gamemode: skirmish=duel, battle=capture waypoints, tug-of-war=push the enemy back by killing him and running towards the end of the stage/level and more! (In-depth review below)-Controls & comabat: The player has three possible control-setups and can set the keybindings to his liking (via the "input") menu: gamepad, keyboard only or keyboard + mouse.If you use keyboard and mouse, like I do, your character moves with WASD, choses (defensive) stances by holding the right mouse button and moving the mouse and attacks by pressing the left mouse button. This system is easy to learn (in the "general" settings menu the player can TURN ON a "tutor" which a HUD element showing your curretn defensive and offensive stance), yet hard to master with every single weapon (yes, there are numerous weapons in this game!). Simply said: it is a directional combat system, but easier than Mount & Blade's, Kingdom Come's or Mordhau's directional combat system is. It reward smart backwards steps to evade the enemy's strike and fast forward steps combined with attacks, but punishes "hack n slash" approaches - I LOVE IT!- costumization/armour: the game offers several body armour sets which cover torso, arms, shoulders, legs all in one + seperate helmets + seperate plumes on top of the helmet. You unlock these things during your campaign(s). Colours are selectable in the "encouter mode" or "multiplayer" mode, in which you can equipt every armour/helmet/plume/weapon you collected in the campaign mode. During the campaign your default colour is black and white. By the way: the game offers a sallet and a hounskull! Awesome! In general, the high and late medieval equipment is historically accurate - at least more accurate than it was in Dark Souls or similar games with a dark pseudo-medieval setting. I appreciate this.HINT for people wanting to UNLOCK EVERY ITEM FASTLY: Be aware that not all is unlockable in one campaign-playthrough so, if there is a sepcific weapon/helmet/armour you want to unlock, you should look at the first stages/"nodes" available to you and see whether they drop the desired item. If they do, fight your way through the stages/nodes leading to the one stage/node which contains the desired item as a reward, beat it and equip the item - then quit the current campaign (Esc, then click on "Quit") and select "New" instead of "continue". THIS RESETS the stages/nodes and REWARDS/COLLECTABLE ITEMS on the MAP, but YOUR CHARACTER of course KEEPS what you ALREADY unlocked in passed campaigns.- weapons: fast two-handed sword (starting weapon), slow but very long two-handed sword (Flamberg/Landsknecht sword), super fast one-handed sword, one-handed mace, two-handed warhammer, pole-axe... oh and a rondell dagger* everyone can use by pressing Z on the keyboard.*a late medieval dagger used to kill full-plated knights lying on the ground though the eyeslids in their helmet. Nice little detail, isn't it?- Is it a pure side scroller? No, you can turn the direction your character faces and thus run back and forth the way you like, which sets it apart from classic "push forward, never go back" side scrollers. If by "side scroller" you mean a "2-D" level design, then yes it is. - Are there horses? Yes, there are, but most of the time you fight on foot which is typical for late medieval combat, especially duels (look at historical sources like manuscript paintings, altar paintings depicting battles, Fechtbuecher showing duels in plate amour etc.). In-game horses on the enemies side are an easy target, because the NPCs don't use their speed to land one hard and fast strike, while you being the smart all-mighty player use the speed and only land one strike at a time, then ride away, turn, ride again towards/through the enemy while striking again one time and so on.Historical note: Horses tended to be used during jousts (free-time activity) to show off one's status, to travel and on big plain/flat battlefields, but even such battlefields the tactics tended towards heavily armoured infantry beating knightly cavalry regularly since 1360, roughly spoken. On hills or uneven battlefields horses were not as awesome as some movies make us modern viewers think... If you want all the advantages and disadavantages play one of the Mount & Blade games. It a has MOUNTS and BLADES. Long story short: This game here is focused on simplified yet realistic dueling and offers costumization, two singleplayer modes (campaign and encounter with its various sub-categories)

_childDocuments_.review: is a 2D sword-duelling game with incredibly atmospheric graphics, hardcore progression, and a brutal, Dark Souls-like difficulty. The game really doesn't pull any punches when it comes to missing a parry or getting hit by a riposte and most of the time, a single good blow can kill you *snaps finger* just like that. There are some strategy involved too, where you will have to decide whether to spend the perks you've earned on a single, more challenging match or saving it for later. P/S: Didn't get to put a lot of time into the game mainly because I tried playing the game using the keyboard and mouse, and it's really hard to get used to the controls. I simply have to give up. That said, the game did mention that it's best played using a gamepad  so the game isn't at fault here.+ Atmospheric 2D graphics+ Multiple game modes including duels (boss fights included), skirmishes, tug-of-war, and horde mode where you'll need to stand your ground and take on enemies that attack you in waves.+ Has campaign + multiplayer mode+ Very fun to play in co-op. + Hardcore progression - Limited lives and if all are extinguished, you have to start all over. Has some perks and equipment that can be equipped for specific matches. Can choose your own path of progression depending on the reward you want or the difficulty of the enemy you face.+ Cool swordplay with amazing animations that correspond with your attacks. Slicing at someone's leg will cut their leg off; same thing applies to heads. * When the game says it's "best played with a gamepad", it really means it. I struggled with the keyboard and mouse, especially when parrying and dealing blows, when I'm playing the game. * Slow-paced combat with deliberate blows and attack combos - rushing in Rambo-style or using basic hack-and-slash will just get you killed! It's all about timing and anticipating your opponent's moves. That said, I'm not a fan of its much slower combat and this is entirely a personal preference.* The game is most definitely replayable but how much "replayable" it is is subjected to your own preference. - Controls aren't as tight as I'd expect. There are times when I right-clicked to parry or left click to attack, and my character just stand there afk. But note that this might only be happening because I was using the keyboard and mouse to play.- The bunny hopping thing which the devs will be addressing in an upcoming patch.- Slow animations, especially when a combo is triggered. I've taken a sword in the gut or in the head way too many times because of this, and currently, I don't think there's a way to cancel animations mid-swing. Might be wrong here.- Very high skill ceiling - Getting owned in Cadet mode... lol. Might be good if there's an easier game mode option for midcore gamers like me who isn't too familiar with the style of swordplay but was attracted to try the game out because of the visuals and medieval-based combat.- Some reviewers mentioned about the lack of players for multiplayer matches and although I didn't try multiplayer - I'm already getting my ass beaten enough times by the AI - this is something that plagues many indie games, so it's not surprising to know that Griefhelm is encountering the same issues. - Can be a bit costly unless you plan on replaying the game.- Maybe refund the perks used if a player failed a level? Seems like losing a life is punishment enough for failing a level.Personally, despite the cool artistic graphics, amazing swordplay, and fun co-op play, I can't recommend Griefhelm as a midcore gamer mainly because of how hard it is, which is further made worse with me playing using the keyboard and mouse as I don't have a gamepad to use . However, for hardcore gamers who loves For Honor-style games (the swordplay and the aesthetics, albeit in 2D) and are out looking for a challenge, Griefhelm is definitely a game they might want to check out. The devs are also actively patching the game up based on feedback and making the game better, so the game can only get better from here.

_childDocuments_.review: This is essentially a themed and deeper version of Nidhogg. If you haven't played it, it's essentially a boiled down arena fighter, with a simple but deceptively in dept stance-based combat system. The campaign is roguelike styled, and rather raw, with only flavor text in place of a story. Progression and cosmetics are locked to 'Encounters', which is basically an arcade mode. Unforunately, the progression is locked behind RNG,Despite all those negatives, the core gameplay is *mint*. You can strike from three stances and shove, while your defence is automatic if you match the stance. What makes griefhelm special is that the transition between said stances are completely smooth, allowing a battle to flow between offence and defence more than the vast majority of weapon-based melee combat games.I define a quality melee combat system by asking the simple question: can a newbie possibly beat an absolute monster at the game? Most weapons are two shot kills, so it is very possible.But probably not.So yes, its a worthy collection for anyone who is a lover of a good ol sword duel. The playerbase is small, but I hope it grows. The devs keep in close contact with the playerbase, and seem to be on top of potential issues.

_childDocuments_.review: Griefhelm is a great game to pick up and play with a group of friends! Combat is fun and complex, which can allow for people to play casually or spend time mastering the gameplay. The controls feel great, and landing blows on enemies is super satisfying. Not to mention, the visuals for Griefhelm are gorgeous. By combining your movement in combat and the aesthetics of each map, you get something that feels very cinematic. The single player campaign is great, but the online multiplayer is definitely the way to play the game. There is a variety of different cosmetics you can acquire to customize your fighter, and tons of different weapons to try out and maps to play on. If you like games like Nidhogg and Mordhau, or if you're just looking for a great game to battle it out with you friends in, I highly recommend Griefhelm!

_childDocuments_.review: Mordhau but 2D and with a singleplayer/co-op campaign.Definitely something to play if you enjoy games like Chivalry: Medieval Warfare, or Mordhau.The game is kind of low population right now in the multiplayer, but that's why I think you should play it. We need to keep this game alive.As for the gameplay, it has a few different modes. The most prominent is Tug-of-War, where you're playing Nidhogg and fighting to the end of the level, against a single opponent that respawns.There's Skirmish, which are 1v1s, first to three wins is the victor.There's Horde, fighting a bunch of enemies that spawn in randomly.And Battle, where you lead a group of soldiers to battle and take over objectives.The game consists of three attack angles, overhead, stabs, and underhands. You also have jabs/kicks to throw your opponent off, parries and ripostes, as well as the ability to dodge. It's simple until you start chaining those mechanics together.Definitely replayable and fun.

_childDocuments_.review: We wrote a critique of Griefhelm. Here is a select quote from the critique:"If you’re looking for a game that is somewhat similar to Nidhogg and find its art style off-putting, Griefhelm might scratch that itch. However, it comes at a cost. It is slower and more unwieldy than Nidhogg, with more awkward controls. Combat feels inconsistent. Its maps are wholly uninteresting, consisting largely of flat stretches of land. What’s more, its campaign feels patched together from other parts of the game and inexplicably keeps one of the more interesting systems, perks, to itself, not allowing players to make use of it in custom lobbies. The most egregious problem, however, is that the AI is extremely exploitable, easily falling victim to simplistic tactics. Despite all of its problems, you may yet find enjoyment here, as the core that its combat system is based on is a proven winning formula, but it just made me wish that I was playing Nidhogg instead."You can find the full critique, complete with awesome ultrawide screenshots, here:

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent 2D Mordhau/Bannerlord for local co-op. I was expecting nothing, and I'm blown away. This is REALLY fun with a friend. Any couch co-op game has to be extremely accessible and immediately engaging. Packaging a satisfying sword-play experience into the co-op package is no easy task. This game NAILS IT. The parries, ripostes, feints...they're all here and very accessible with a controller. Advancing and retreating, combos, and...beheading...it's all baked into the game-play. Would you like to decapitate your foe while charging on a horse? Yes. How about setting an opponent ablaze with one fell-swoop from a flaming sword? Yasss. The campaign mode has momentum and danger to it. You aren't just hacking and slashing; it feels dangerous and thrilling. You can gamble your perks on challenging matches and gain momentum or suffer agonizing setbacks. You and a friend can fight with your backs against each other against hordes of enemies.... or you can charge together in a well-timed combination attack. You will feel the tide of battle turning in certain matches... you can feel fear and retreat...or advance with the foolish hubris of a gladiator.10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Griefhelm is a tactical dueling game set during medieval times, so no laser guns people, just big swords and shields.Unlike your typical beat em up, there is no 100 hit combo, or coming back after being hit 50 times, Griefhelm takes a realistic approach in that a few hits and you are dead, and the same with your enemies. They attack you, you deflect or defend their blows and when you see an opening you take your chance to strike.This is a 2D fighting game, but with very striking graphics, the backgrounds are beautiful and the characters look great. You progress through the game by choosing different routes on a map, different locations will give different benefits, you have 5 "lives" and no saves as such, in other words you cant keep trying to beat an opponent by loading up a save point. And yes you can kill an opponent with just one hit. You have three ways of attacking, low, mid and high attacks. If using a gamepad, as I did, you use the right stick to choose your attack, but this position will also decide how you will defend, if you match the attack of your opponent with your defensive position you will parry their attack which allows you to then go in for the kill.Trust me hack and slash won't work here outside of the first level. You can't luck your way through this game, there is a specific way to attack and defend and for you to progress you have to follow that way. And this means a steep learning curve.There are multiple weapons to collect, each are different, but are controlled in basically the same way.As you play through the story you will encounter different styles of fight, from one on one, to "tug of war" which has nothing to do with pulling a rope, you beat opponents and get closer to their side of the screen and once you have beaten enough you will win that level, you will lose if they push you back far enough. There is also a horde mode, and of course you will have your fair share of bosses to beat.There is also multiplayer mode, but I have not been able to play that.The GoodGraphically impressive.The BadI was hoping for more of a medieval beatem up, so for me this game was a bit limited in what it offered.SummaryJust didn't quite offer enough for me as a whole, and although it tries to add longevity with different weapons, armour and so on, it just wasn't quite enough.I score this game 5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Good concept but terrible execution. The game looks great for the price and sounds great. the problem is the learning curve. _childDocuments_.review: 9/10I don't care what the other reviewers say onlineThe video game industry is so pretentious, they don't know a good game when they see oneThis is an un-pretentious medieval combat gameNo Dungeons and Dragons BS with the "RPG story-rich adventure", just shut up and fight like how games used to beThere are many comparisons to Nidhogg but Griefhelm is better, because of the control schemeI actually fence with greatsword in real life, and while this does almost nothing to evoke the same precautions, methods, techniques, etc. it's a very good fighting game in medieval settingUnlike other sword games, it involves skill rather than mindlessly smashing the button, and while that skill isn't a true analogue to fencing, it's still the best I've ever seenComplaints:This game lacks a medium difficulty, unless you turn the damage multiplier down to 0.25, bosses are too hard0.25 Is the sweet spot for medium difficultyMost of the stages are a strange eyesore, too much stuff in the way of the characters, poor optimization and lags sometimesThere are 3 stages I play the most of because they're the least distracting to look atI almost think this game should've been made with high-contrast pixelated graphics instead, it would make it easier to judge the spacing, run smoother, etc.Improvements:In Battle mode, sometimes I die because the view suddenly jumps across the screen to re-center on new enemiesThe montante should be able to hit like 2-3 times on each attackThere only seems to be 1 AI style, if you've beat one enemy you've beat them allNo shieldsThis is a 9/10 game with few and minor blemishes, and absolutely one of my all-time favouritesI don't know who made it but you are so coolI want to see what comes next
