_childDocuments_.review: "It's a Nidhogg roguelite" would be the easiest way to describe the gameplay. Same combat system, same tug-o-war style gameplay, same premise. There are some key differences though. For one, the gameplay is much slower than Nidhogg. It takes a bit longer to change stances, you don't run as fast, and really your character just feels sluggish by comparison.However that's the only thing I feel is worse than Nidhogg, as every other aspect seems improved upon. It's easier to react to your opponents moves, there's different weapon and armor types to suit your play style, the roguelite aspect is fun and challenging (unless you unlock the spear which I would consider to be the first "op weapon" you can get), and the graphics and art style is killer. So overall, this is definitely worth the price of admission.

_childDocuments_.review: Its good, if you have played For Honor and Nidhogg(1 or 2) its basically a combination of both. Distance and timing is key. I used controller as that is what is recommended, in order to attack you must pick either high, middle or low using the joystick and the right trigger to initiate the attack. Same goes for the guard though I found it easier to simply move in and out of distance to attack and defend rather than try to read the AI.Also. the AI... well it has its moments of being smart, in between stabbing its ally in the back(yes 1v2 is a possibility, so is 2v1 and 2v2 as well) and jumping to its death in an arena with pits to jump over.... hilarious, but loses its charm after 15mins in the same game where the mechanics arent really built for jumping(which honestly feels like it was just kinda shoehorned in). I may sound like Im trashing it but I really did enjoy it, If you like Nidhogg or For Honor you may very well like this little gem.

In a game like this, it doesn't make much sense to be unable to see your character at times, especially when the AI still knows how to fight behind foreground. With those two issues being said though, it is overall a great game, 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to love this game but it's just way too unpolished to be really enjoyable right now. A lot of animations can be unreadable (namely stabs, which have almost no indicator for when they're in active damage frames or recovery, along with the 1 handed sword, whose windups for all 3 attack directions look nearly identical), your armor stat resets to standard whenever you die in a tug-of-war match (this has been fixed actually :D), bash is way too powerful, online is seemingly totally dead on launch, and the game is about $5 more than could possibly be justifiable. Still, I think this game absolutely has the potential to be fantastic, and that's why I'm recommending it. I really don't want to see a game as unique as this in a genre as niche as nidhogg-likes die on the vine. with some touch ups and a bigger community this could be great. The atmosphere really reminds me almost of a cross between Shadow of the Colossus' wordless worldbuilding with Dark Souls' almost poetic descriptions and fractured story. It's simultaneously a serious, moody game about an ancient order interrupted by needless war fought by knights who know no better, and also a splitscreen party game to play with friends. I really hope it gets the love it deserves.

_childDocuments_.review: 2D Sidescroller Nidhogg/Mordhau-like.Made by a tiny dev team I believe it was basically a tech demo made for a competition that has been expanded on.Current Features: -Campaign Mode-Horde Mode-Co-op Vs. AI-Local Co-op-Custom Matchmaking-Online MatchmakingVisually the game features a dreamy dark aesthetic as you trudge across various encounters in biomes ranging from a stony keep to a dark crypt or the far reaches of the arctic. The stages are relatively simple with minor environmental effects  such as sliding on ice sheets, or being obscured by tall grass changing things up between areas. Graphics are decent but optimization is a bit lacking.The gameplay has a fair amount of depth featuring a stance based attack/block system. Match your opponents stance to block their attack and there are three stances. This results in a basic rock-paper-scissors match but is mixed up by adding shoves/kicks and a counter to said attacks. There are even more advanced techniques involving attacking from a neutral stance, feinting your stance only to attack from a different angle, and the "morph attack" ala-Mordhau. You're able to start an attack in one stance and quickly cancel it into a different angle. So overall I would say the basic mechanics have a surprising amount of depth.The equipment you can use in every game mode has to first be unlocked through the campaign by looting it from foes and using either a perk that will unlock your current equipment set, or by completing the campaign. At first this can be pretty daunting as the campaign can be unforgiving to a new player with just basic armor and a longsword. Encounters and rewards are randomized each playthrough meaning you are faced with choices involving risk vs. reward. There are some runs where you have to plan your route in order to get a specific piece of gear and the perk to unlock it permanently, and others where you may want more lives or map vision for route planning. Both you and the NPCs you encounter in the campaign use the stats of your equipment unlike multiplayer where only weapon animations/speed affect balance. At first this hinders you severely as you'll eventually encounter a situation where an enemy kill you in one hit, but you have to hit them three times. That can be really frustrating, but on the other hand you can unlock armor and equipment that will make these enemies seem trivial in later runs. I enjoyed the campaign more once I had unlocked different gear to experiment with but getting killed by a mini-boss about eight times halfway through the campaign was demoralizing, I'll admit.Online matchmaking was fun though it requires a very good connection or lag will actually mess with hitboxes and collision. I had some frustration in free for all matches given that sometimes you will spawn in sandwiched between people though that really depends on who you're playing with. Skirmishes are the 2v2 team battles which are a slightly less chaotic way to test your skills. Horde mode is a wave survival mode where you and your teammates will fend off waves of randomly equipped enemy AI closing in from each side. You can play each gamemode in local co-op or in solo encounters as well as create custom online lobbies with adjusted damage, and unlockable stages.Some sort of ranked system would be interesting I'm sure to many people as well as making a more official "clan system" rather than just a preferred color.There's a decent amount of replayability with the unlockable gear and stages. I could see the current campaign becoming a bit boring once you've unlocked most of the available gear, as well as some encounters are able to be cheesed by running past your opponent. There are planned updates and fixes so I'm optimistic that the game will be even better come the EOY.Overall I would say the current state is a solid 7-8/10. More optimization and content is planned to release about every month, so I will update as the state of the game changes.TL;DR A decent semi-realistic medieval combat game that plays a bit like a sidescroller Mordhau. Branching paths and random rewards in a campaign add a degree of replayability. Unlockable gear including weapons, helms, armor, and plumage with more planned. Features Local and Online co-op/PVP

_childDocuments_.review: edit: vsync has been added!First off i would recommend this if you plan to just play with friends. Otherwise no. I played the demo a ton with 3 freinds on local coop and I really liked it, but so far with the release build I'm just left frustrated. The nidhogg esque mode got changed from 1HK attacks to 2 hits which seems like something minor but totally ruins the mode. Controls feel unresponsive during combat, especially after parrying. AI can be insanely hard for seemingly no reason. the neat idea of blocking visibilty using the map in the foreground looks great but is simply infuriating. The camera in general jerks around a ton when teammates or enemies spawn which got me killed constantly. Some weapons are very difficult to read like the spear which was just as broken in the demo. Worst of all for some reason you have to unlock all the weapons in a super smash bros challenger approaching design. Which is very frustrating when all of the above comes into play.But by far the biggest and most annoying problem is no option for v sync. Massive screen tears on my gaming laptop. IMO this needs a fix asap.I expected more on release. Visually it's much nicer than the demo by miles but gameplay just feels clunky. I'm sticking around because this game has insane potential to be an incredible party game but currently if you plan on playing alone just don't bother. i wouldn't recommend unless you're playing with humans and even then over the internet latency is finnicky.

name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit
detailed_description: Quotes With beautiful graphics and a fascinating story, Crowns and Pawns is looking like it will be an excellent point and click adventure. - Charles Cecil (creator of the Broken Sword series) Crowns and Pawns is groovy. I dig it. - Bill Tiller (artist of The Curse of Monkey Island) About the Game Legends of the past come back to life in this charming European mystery point-and-click adventure. Crowns and Pawns , a modern-day detective point&click adventure, inspired by classics such as Broken Sword, The Curse of Monkey Island, Still Life, Syberia and others. The game highlights the less explored history of Europe to the world of adventurers. Experience the legendary stories of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, bring to light the conspiracy of the villainous branch of the KGB, solve puzzles and follow hints to reveal the secrets of the King who was never crowned. The story follows a girl from Chicago, Milda, who unexpectedly receives an inheritance from her grandfather – a house in Lithuania. She sets off to Europe, but upon arrival she is threatened by an unknown man, demanding that she gives up her inheritance. Determined and intrigued by the mystery, she explores the run-down house, discovering old documents and clues dating back to the 15th century. Before long, Milda gets dragged into a dangerous search for a long-lost mysterious relic with a curse... A blend of history and myths set in a modern world, featuring real life locations all around Europe. Crowns and Pawns is led by the art director of the highly acclaimed fan-adventure Broken Sword 2.5. Classic point-and-click puzzles that involve finding items hidden in beautiful environments, creatively combining the contents of your inventory, interesting dialogue choices, and more! Feel like a detective uncovering the conspiracy behind a cursed relic. Beautiful hand painted art that comes to life with a touch of modern graphics features. A world that reacts to your decisions. Change the looks of the main character to solve puzzles (or for fun!). Fully voiced dialogue. Music written by the award winning composer Daniel Pharos (A New Beginning, Memoria, Blackguards). A control scheme perfectly adapted for the best possible experience with both a mouse and a gamepad. The mystery detective point&click adventure is brought to you by the award-winning indie game development studio Tag of Joy . Partly funded by:

_childDocuments_.review: Crowns and Pawns is a new point&click adventure game from a small studio from a small country. And guess what? It's good. It offers traditional point&click gameplay, beautiful graphics and challenging yet logical puzzles.You play as Milda, a Lithuanian girl living in Chicago. Suddenly she receives a message from Lithuania that her grandpa died and she inherited his house. So she needs to travel to Lithuania to get the house and sign some papers, otherwise the house will be sold in an auction in two weeks. And here's where Milda's journey begins.If you played the demo you probably know that something happens when Milda arrives to Lithuania and visits the house. There was a break in and suddenly it becomes a mystery story where Milda tries to uncover the truth about her grandpa and his secrets.The story in Crown and Pawns is great. It feels completely fresh, something you have never heard before. Not because it's complicated or anything but because it is based on Lithuanian history and no one outside of Lithuania know that probably. You learn about Lithuanian heritage, historical figures, lithuanian jewish community, KGB, soviet occupation and even about pagans. There's a lot of names, dates, characters both real and mythical mentioned through the game. The story is tied to history a lot.It also represents Lithuanian architecture and areas in the game are real places in real life which are recreated very nicely. Churches, Vilnius university, it warms my heart seeing those places in a game.Gameplay is standard point&click style. The game was inspired by Broken Sword series and you can really feel that Broken Sword vibe here. The artistic style is similar, the story is similar too in a way (digging in the past, looking for mysterious artifact, religious figures, etc.) and everything else is done in a  similar style.But developers probably wanted to add something fresh to the genre. We all know the genre is barely alive. I am a fan of the genre since 1998 maybe and I still play these games. So it has two features which were absent from such games (or maybe I never played the one).First, you can customize the main character's appearance. You can change Milda's haircut, shirt, pants, shoes and also bracelet, earrings and necklace. This seems like unimportant feature but it's nice to have it.Second, you can actually choose who Milda is in her life, like her profession. This will give you a certain item and depending on your choice it will have impact on solving some puzzles in different ways. This feature is simply amazing and shows that after decades of barely changing gameplay of the genre you still can find new features to add to make it fresh.As always you'll need to talk with people, go through dialogue options to solve puzzles or learn important information. There also are optional dialogue choices which could lead to some funny moments. Speaking of funny – jokes in this game are awesome. I can't remember when was the last time I had such a good laugh. Although at least one joke is made for Lithuanian players only. But hey, if someone is really enjoying this game maybe they will google the answer considering fridge content.Puzzles are pretty tough sometimes but in the end they are logical. Unlike in many other games of the genre where some puzzles just make zero sense (looking at you Runaway) here everything makes sense and is well thought. You just need to pay attention to everything, every little detail. Most importantly never give up. The game isn't long, don't go looking for a walkthrough, just use your brain. If you're tired just take a break. You'll need to use items, examine them, combine them. On top of that you have your phone so you can call people or text them. There are also objectives/clues on your phone which you can combine.Graphically the game looks very pretty. Especially the main character, Milda is a very pretty young lady. Characters even have some facial expressions. Each character is well made and none of them feel generic. Each of them has a character and looks unique.Character models are very well done. Usually I prefer 2D characters but in this game 3D characters actually look good.Environments are nice drawn and are work of art but I wish they would be a bit higher resolution. It all looks perfectly fine until camera zooms in for the dialogue. It's when you start seeing the blurry image.Performance should be fine. Doesn't look like a demanding game and i'm playing on 5800x, rtx3080, 32GB so obviously I have zero problems. Game should be potato friendly.One thing I didn't like is that you have zero graphics options. Of course they're not needed except at least one – windowed mode/resolution change. Come on guys it's 2022, that's not acceptable.One thing I didn't expect from a tiny studio making a niche game was voice acting. It adds so much ot the game and the best part is that the voice acting is good. The characters sound good and voiced dialogues makes the game more lively.Music maybe isn't very remarkable. _childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? Looking at the key art and the title this game mislead me to believe it is a casual adventure. Or a hidden object game. Or even a time management game. It isn't. It is a hardcore classic point and click adventure. A dozen hotspots in every screen, a dozen things in your inventory, different locations you can visit, differnt people you can talk to. Add a phone with some people you can call or message, and a notes app on the phone to draw conclusions and you get quite a lot of possible things to try at any time. And as usual, things are not easy - there are some poisonous vines in your way, you can't just trample over them, burn them, sneak past them, no, you need the right tool to cut them. And of course this tool needs to be repaired first and needs spare parts. To find those spare parts, you need technical equipment... which of course also needs to be repaired before you can use it. I think you get the point - there are long puzzle chains to solve on every step before you can advance. Fortunately the puzzles mostly have clues and some even make sense. Some puzzles are timed, you have to do the right thing at the right time. Fail, and you can try again, but it might take a minute to prepare everything again. Additionally, there are some mini games, like a slider puzzle or a fuse box to repair.The story is classic - a young woman from the States travels to her family roots in Eastern Europe after her uncle had passed away, and quickly is on the trail of her lost father and medieval stuff of enormous power. You choose her profession at the start of the game (out of three), and this actually has an impact on your inventory and some puzzles. She is helped by a local friend who seems to like her but is too stupid to bring her into his bed (so she sleeps on his couch). Other people are often unhelpful (like the cleaning lady with the broomstick) or even downright dangerous, seems they are also after the medieval stuff. So, this is kind of a mystery thriller inspired by the novels of Dan Brown (Da Vinci Code). Or at least inspired by the Broken Sword games.Technically, there is not much to complain. Save anywhere. Loading times are very fast. Double click to fast exit, press the middle mouse button to show all hotspots - better than the usual press "SPACE". Left click to interact, right click to examine things... although the right click most of the time doesn't work. I always have to right click more than once before the game gives me a description. The visual presentation may look like a casual game, but it is actually well drawn. The size of your character scales down when she walks away from the front of the scene. You can dress her up like you want (actually, finding the correct dress for the occasion is one of the first puzzles), but just what she wears, you cannot change her gender, breast size or skin color. Not even her hat. The game is fully voiced (in good quality).Point and click adventure, classic style. Lots of puzzles. Nice.

_childDocuments_.review: As stated above, if you are a fan of the genre you’re going to appreciate this game for the uniqueness it brings and you will be able to look past the smaller faults the game has, as they are more common for games of this type.Starting off with the negatives, because people tend to remember the last pieces of information more.Puzzle solving and trial and error gameplay feels… really weird during . If you are being chased or in some kind of imminent danger, it has always felt really odd to me when you have the time to try over and over again until you get it just right.  not only are those kinds of scenes relatively scarce in this game, it is sadly very common for the genre too. It relies more on the mystery than scooter chases like on the cover.Sometimes it is important you do something in an annoying order. Like you need to have inspected a picture in a book or an item before you are able to talk to a character about it or combine something.  Even if you have seen and understood the connection.The antagonists are very forgettable. As are most side characters.I don’t like the “be quiet in a library” comments… This might be a personal thing, but in many modern libraries today, unless you are in a designated ‘quiet zone’ libraries serve as public and cultural meeting places, and they are not meant to be quiet all around. So, it annoys me whenever I see media that keeps portraying libraries (or museums) as they were in the twentieth century. The main character is extremely likable, which is great, since she is the one you spend the whole game with. You are also able to alter her in slight ways to make her more your own, such as picking between three different backgrounds (that affects at least one of the puzzles) and changing her style multiple times throughout the game.A couple of memorable side characters that brightens up the story. Luckily your character’s best friend Dana is among them, the two others I will probably remember fondly (or for the love-to-hate) is investor-douchebag and the amazing Lithuanian hockey-fan With the setting being in the modern world, I appreciate it being in a region of the world, which isn’t so often the focus. It isn’t just cosmetic either, rather the region’s history, language, and religions become integral to the mystery aspect.The far majority of puzzles are logical, and once you figure out the solution it sorta makes sense. (Which isn’t always the case in games like this. Oh the horror where you have to make so many mental leaps of how it makes sense to inflate a rubber duck ring so it can be used in combination with two other random things to grab a third item before it deflates. :P)The game also has a very pleasing art style, which is definitely a big plus.

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game kind of mixed bag, it does some things right and for cheaper AA game it is fine, but I really wish they did more with all the mechanics they put into it. I say once because second time you have to change the look it is done automatically and not vie mechanic. And it really didn't feel like environment is reacting to outside of that. And it has quite a bit of that with rest of mechanics as well. Another thing that kind of bothered me were some of the timed puzzles. Not necessarily the timing itself, but just time penalty if you fail. Since you need to go through dialogue again and again. And sometimes it is not obvious that you need to set things, like turning object multiple times, which can be quite pain. Like early and less spoilery example, though also least offensive, is one where you can get coins from another character, you need those coins like three times, if you get everything right and you need to ask that character for new coins, because every time you use them, they are out of the inventory, adding just whole traveling back and forth, plus then add up all failed timed events because you didn't do everything out. Instead of just getting pile of coins, and just having them there to redo things. Though the worst case is with librarian for sure and that thing you need to know to turn few times... _childDocuments_.review: The puzzles are reasonable logical and mostly well done. They are certainly on harder end of the point and click genre, and some are even trial and error based. Nevertheless I don't think you'll need a guide if you have enough experience in this genre. You just need to pay close attention to every detail. However there is one particular exception (), that can end up being a trial and error torment. At least I gave up on this one puzzle and looked for hints online.The story is very enjoyable and sprinkled with well fitting history bits. While investigating your grandfather's mysterious past, you stumble more and more into a true adventure about the name giving crown. Later on you'll even encounter ancient mechanisms, evil villains and some surprising twists. All of this isn't overly drawn out and fairly well paced. A tpyical playthrough should be around 6-8 hours.The voice over and music are great and the visuals are really good as well. There is only one minor thing to criticize about the latter. When the game zooms into a scene, e.g. for a dialog, a higher res background would have been nice in some places.Overall I can recommend this game to any adventure fan. Just be ready to ignore the above mentioned puzzle and enjoy an otherwise fine game. Also thanks Tag of Joy for the native Linux version which worked perfectly for me.Played on Manjaro Linux (Kernel 5.17.9, Mesa 22.0.4) with an AMD Ryzen 5900X, an AMD RX 5700 XT and 32GB RAM.

_childDocuments_.review: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit is an ambitious but decent classic point and click adventure game inspired by Broken Sword that does not quite reach the quality of its influence.👍 +The protagonist had quite a lot of charm.+Voice acting+Puzzles were neither extremely obtuse nor extremely easy, perfect difficulty.👎-Main story is filled with plot holes and the ending was rushed.-Backgrounds are not that interesting and too few.-Lacks danger, intrigue. The story follows the steps of Milda, a young woman who receives a letter that her grandfather died and she inherited his house in Lithuania. So she decides to go there where things get a bit interesting. As you expect it's your typical "he died in mysterious circumstances and I found some super secret treasure hidden for political reasons" type of story.It has Broken Sword/Indiana Jones written all over it but sadly it does not actually do anything unique to stand on its own. Worse, it lacks what's most important in these type of stories, intrigue and danger. Instead it goes for a goofy, comedy type of mystery adventure where the villains are just caricatures or complete idiots. The main story isn't bad but just lacks any oomph so to say, everything you discover is just not masterfully crafted, but instead it's comically convenient. I have no issues with comedy and light stories but it sadly has become the norm nowadays. Broken Sword also had comedy but the serious side was not as goofy. You truly felt the danger there. It had impact. Sadly the ending in Crowns and Pawns emphasizes this even more as you approach the final parts you can clearly see, it's highly lacking and it just ends not giving you closure or at least some form of intrigue to the mystery of the crown or to its background, worse, not even to some of the main characters you met and the final confrontation is just stupid. Overall the story is just okay, it's not as bad as I make it out to be but the potential it had was incredible and it just failed on that aspect. Story rating: 7/10So how are the puzzles in the game? Well suffice to say, I enjoyed them even if I got stuck on some for being stupid. If you haven't played classic point and click adventure games, the short version is, you find objects around the levels and you have to combine them in your inventory and/or with the persons or objects in the environment to progress the story. Crowns and Pawns comes with some small variation to some of the puzzles. What I mean by that at the start of the game Milda can have other jobs which will change how maybe one or two puzzles in the game get solved. You can also customize the appearence of the character which also involves a puzzle or two. It's cool but they could've done so much more with this. Again, I stress, the potential in this game was enourmous, you see a ton of creative ideas and they just end prematurely. Still, as far as adventures go, Crowns and Pawns at least tried to do something better than recent examples and the puzzles really made me think which I liked. Gameplay rating: 7.5/10Voice acting is pretty damn good. Milda has a charming actor, and I genuinely laughed several times. The supporting characters also do a pretty good job voicing their characters. The soundtrack, although not very memorable, it does what it sets to do and is quite pleasant and fitting with what's happening in the background. As for all the other sound effects, all was good, nothing out of the ordinary here. Audio rating: 8/10First the good, game runs great, had no issues with performance, and besides one or two crashes, I had no other problems bug wise. The not so good thing which kinda dissapointed me were the backgrounds. The characters themselves are ok but the game really needs some anti-aliasing. The backgrounds and the places you visit though? Not as good as I hoped they would be. They're all mostly static and just lack a lot of details. For someone who visits a lot of historical cities, the places were just eh and kinda few. Graphics, performance and tech analysis score: 7/10Overall Crowns and Pawns is a fine adventure game that had the potential to be something greater than Broken Sword but alas, it prefers to remain in its shadow. If you're not a fan of the genre, not sure this game will change your mind but if you are, theres no reason not to buy it and support indie devs.

_childDocuments_.review: (Follow  for more reviews like this)Crowns and Pawns is a pretty decent adventure game in classic Lucas Arts style, with a few unique features and one extremely annoying puzzle of the type I hoped adventure game devs left behind two decades ago.You play a Milda, a young woman of Lithuanian ancestry, who receives a letter informing her of her grandfather's death. She inherits his old house in Lithuania and decides to journey there and check it out. Of course, things aren't as simple as they appear, and as she collects cryptic notes left by her deceased grandfather, she's pulled into a treasure hunt for the crown of Mindaugas, the first and only king of Lithuania.The story is classic adventure fare inspired by Indiana Jones and Broken Sword. If you played those games, you know what to expect. It's told in a lighthearted tone, but not as joke-driven as Lucas Arts games. While the story is fictional and contains a few fantasy elements, the game mixes it with some actual history for great effect. If you're familiar with Lithuanian history, you'll enjoy catching the references, if not, you'll get to learn something!Gameplay is classic point & click fare: collect items, use them to solve puzzles, talk to NPCs, etc. The puzzles are mostly logical and can easily be solved on your own, without the need for a walkthrough. I only had to look up hints for two of them: one is entirely based on trial and error (figure out the weight of an object without any hints), and another is an annoying action sequence. Action sequences in adventure games have been tried many times, but rarely work. Here, it fails spectacularly. During a bike chase, you have to perform specific actions at specific moments by clicking on specific spots in the scene. It's not fun, but with the help of a walkthrough you can get through it easily enough. This is honestly the worst action sequence in a point & click I've seen yet, and I've seen many.The game's most unique feature for the genre is the wardrobe. You can assemble your outfit from a variety of different clothes, and you can even change your haircut, with various options ranging from a short pixie to a braided bun. One early puzzle requires you to choose the right outfit to make an impression on a certain character, so it's more than just a cosmetic feature, which is nice.Another uncommon (but not unheard of) feature is that you can choose your profession in the intro - photographer, programmer, or psychologist - and one puzzle in the mid-game has a different solution depending on your profession, adding a bit of replay value.Overall, it's a solid entry into the point & click adventure genre, and I can recommend it for its unique features and charming treasure hunt story. The puzzles are just the right difficulty to make you think without getting stumped. The only bad thing in the game is that action sequence... but considering the quality of the rest, it doesn't impact the game's enjoyment overly much.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this game for a while and - unsurprisingly - not only does it not disappoint, it exceeded my expectations!A very well-crafted, polished experience, featuring an instantly likeable main character, a lovely atmosphere throughout, and stunning graphics. I want to take a moment and commend these guys on the graphics, because they really, really shine - especially for a small indie team. A combination of skillfully modeled 3D characters - not too realistic, not exaggeratedly cartoony - and hand-painted environments that just pop out of the screen. The use of color is tremendous - I let out an audible "WOW" entering an Orthodox church in the game. There's a subtle parallax scroll when you pan through the screen with your mouse; attention has been given to small details that do take a lot of work, like pigeons (3D pigeons! 😄), vegetation waving in the wind, planes streaking across the evening sky... This game builds a world I'd gladly move into.And speaking of places, probably my favorite aspect of Crowns and Pawns is the local color. This isn't an edutainment title - far from it - but you'll learn a bunch of stuff about Lithuania which you probably had no idea about (I know I didn't!). I love how effective and beautifully integrated into the story this element is, and I wish more games drew inspiration from where the devs are located. It makes for an ineffable feeling of authenticity that is hard to come by otherwise. Adventure game players usually complain about modern games' puzzles being too easy or hand-hold-y - definitely not the case here. Even the very first puzzle in the game had me scratching my head. If you enjoy a challenge, albeit a fair one, you'll be happy with the brain teasers Crowns and Pawns throws at you.What else is there to say? I can't wait to jump back in. This game took a while to make, and it shows - everything from the way godrays affect your character, to the lovely music, to the sleek UI shows the work, attention and love that these guys and girls have poured into the project.If you're a fan of Broken Sword-style conspiracy mysteries - buy this game immediately. If you're a fan of adventure games in general - same advice. It's one of the best titles the genre has seen recently. tl;dr: BUY THIS GAME NOW, what are you waiting for?

_childDocuments_.review: Kind of a short P&C-Adventure but while playing you can feel the love and passion the devs put into this little gem.Sometimes I needed to look into the "discussions" where players and also the devs gave hints (some more ingame hints in the style of "maybe I could" after a few tries would've been appreciated).Also (2x) I looked at a walkthrough (e.g. hockeygame) because one NPC-hint was so fast that I couldn't remember it.Actions sometimes take too long: Walking, using things from inventory or if you click on NPCs: waiting for their animation to finish before they talk with you.Really enjoyed the art-style and voice-acting.The story is unique and gives some insights about Lithuania's past. The main- (and side) character(s) are relatable (I like it when you can choose between a rational and a "dumb" answer to have a laugh^^) Funny moment was when I called someone who was standing right next to me. I was asked why I am calling :DOverall a solid 7,5 / 10 pointsReminds me somehow of the Ankh-Adventures. Not perfect but still fun.There are a few things that need to be improved (and I am sure they will) for hopefully a next game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game in its current form is a whole lot of mixed quality- but that being said, the developer seems truly interested in making quality of life adjustments to iron that out with time, so I'm hoping eventually I change my vote from a hesitant thumbs up, to a confident thumbs up.The story is solid, about what you would expect from a typical adventure game and nothing more. The puzzle design ranges from good to the usual issues you find in adventure games- some clever things that feel good to piece together, and some puzzles that are just pure tedium by design. That being said, it does sound like the developer has already adjusted some puzzles, so here's hoping with time they'll clean up a few more.The game features some fantastic voice acting, bringing life to even some more awkward lines. And it's got some truly unique ideas too- I don't think I've ever seen an adventure game that has character customization, nor that lets you choose a 'class' up front that changes how you solve puzzles throughout the game. Neither of these additions are executed perfectly of course , but they're definitely welcome additions to a genre that could use some changes.The humor often lands when it's supposed to, once again given energy by the excellent voice acting, and the art design has some truly beautiful backgrounds (not that the first two screens you're presented with would give you that notion). The music actually does a pretty good job of matching the tone for the style of game, although I have to admit the first two background songs hurt my ears so much that I stopped playing the game the first time I booted it up within minutes.The facial animations range from ok, to, actually quite good- Dana's glare when I kept asking her for money will actually stick with me for a while. And there truly are some unique puzzle/scenario designs at play here (the hockey game) that makes me optimistic that te studio will be able to continue to bring unique ideas to the genre.Overall, I think I would say it was worth the play through, and worth the money (about 6 hours of playtime for a single run through), but it's not a smooth ride throughout, just yet.

_childDocuments_.review: (Mild recommend - read on)This is a charming, albeit short game which suffers from somewhat glossy character graphics and occasionally obtuse puzzles.The story is good, but not very substantial. People who have played games like Broken Sword or Gabriel Knight will recognize the mixing of factual and fictional historical events into the story. Unfortunately the game is too short to fully utilize this storytelling, and the results are not quite as gripping or epic as it could've been. The conclusion also felt a bit rushed, and I saw the contours of a puzzle that may have been scrapped before release.The puzzles are for the most part good, and more difficult than many other modern point and click games. This is a good thing, and something for the developers to continue in future games. Many of them are very clever and quite unique, and felt very logical in the story setting. There are however at least three timed puzzles, where - if you fail - you'll need to repeat a number of cumbersome steps to try again - every single time. Sometimes including a good amount of trial and error to figure out the correct solution.As mentioned, the characters are a bit glossy and cartoonish. This may be a personal taste, but felt a little bit out of place in the story. The background and scenes are gorgeous, however.Some segments consists of fairly long exchanges that aren't really skipable and contributed too little to the story.All in all: A very charming game, and definitely not a bad successor to the Broken Sword series. It's however only a mild recommend due to the short length and somewhat disappointing conclusion.

_childDocuments_.review: Crowns and Pawns is a decent little adventure game. If you are looking for a cozy point and click for a weekend playthrough, this mostly fits the bill. The puzzles are logical, the story progresses at a good clip and the main character is resourceful and witty. You get to go on a treasure hunt around Europe, visiting lovingly-drawn locations and thwarting the sinister machinations of a gun-toting bad guy. What more could you want?The game has its flaws, unfortunately. While the voice acting is solid, it's really jarring that almost all the actors are American when almost all the characters are European. It would have added a lot to the immersion if the voices had sounded more European. Also the text message scripting is an embarrassment. For a game set in the modern smartphone era, there is no excuse for having full-grown adults text each other like they are 13 year olds on AOL Instant Messenger. The ending feels rushed and has some logic gaps. The story doesn't come to a satisfying resolution, and it fades out with the main character cracking wise with the creepy, awkward sidekick who won't take a hint, instead of her best friend or family members.But up until the last chapter, it's a pretty fun romp through Europe, following clues and finding secret passages and all that good stuff. Well worth it for adventure game fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit

_childDocuments_.review: I had a good time with this game! The voice acting is pretty good, the puzzles are challenging enough, the visuals are stunning and the story is solid. I also liked all these little easter eggs - the developers obviously love the adventure genre!A few scenes killed the flow, though. There are moments where Milda has to repeat actions all over again (e.g. In the library). In addition, I don't understand why they didn't include the option to let Milda run with a double-click. I also feel like this game should've been longer. Some arcs fell short and therefore this game was overall lacking in depth (compared to Broken Sword and Syberia). And what I really don't understand are these "zoom-in" attempts during dialogue - the background looks so bad in these scenes and it really destroys the good atmosphere of the game (maybe a patch can fix this). Lastly: The ending is very abrupt - a common trope in point and click games.All in all, a nice little p&c adventure game. I will definitely play this again some time. Big fan of this genre!

_childDocuments_.review: I am part of the generation that grew up with the traditional point and click adventure games like »Sam and Max: Hit the Road«, »The Day of the Tentacle«, »Monkey Island«, and »Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis«. Certainly my all-time favourite among all adventure games is »Broken Sword«. Its atmosphere just perfectly catches the feeling of beautiful summer days in the 1990s – warm light, interesting and deep conversations, a glimpse of tension in the air, the desire to simply dwell a little in this cozy place and to imbrue yourself with the pinnacle of all positive emotions.What I have assumed to be lost in the maelstrom of time and buried by the severities of everyday life has been revived by »Crowns and Pawns«. If you love the »Broken Sword« games – that is the comparison I hear most often and it fits so well –, you will by no means be disappointed by »Crowns and Pawns«, as it achieves every single point I have noted in my introduction of this review. Each scene is designed with love in a very appealing art style. The people you converse with are charming with extraordinarily well fitting voices and a subtle sense of humor. At no point of the story I had the feeling of lacking plausibility; only one puzzle took me quite some time to solve, but in general they are all very well balanced and are purely logic-based without any guessing or combining items in an absurd way. This kind of puzzle design allows you to enjoy the story and won’t shackle you too long to a scene and thus make you forget why exactly you want to achieve something specific.There is one aspect I want to emphasize: Tag of Joy, the developers, support Linux users. This is no matter of course, especially with Steam’s Proton making it attractive to put other platforms aside and rely on that instead. So I want to honour this effort by mentioning it explicitly in my review. The Linux version plays very well; I encountered no crashes, no bugs, no corrupted save files. The immersion was perfect from the beginning to the end and not torn asunder by technical issues.My first playthrough took me roughly 10 hours, which is the playtime that most people I know have on their record, so I consider this the average experience without skipping dialogues and rushing through the scenes just for the sake of finishing the game. I enjoyed every minute and can say that »Crowns and Pawns« is absolutely worth its price. There is no reason to wait for a discount. The developers deserve to be supported for keeping the genre alive – or stated more accurately: reviving it. I am very much looking forward to more games with great captivating stories by the developers. Thank you so very much for this trip to the past in the garments of the present. It is my personal story game of the year.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of people will tell you this game definitely has some Broken Sword in its DNA. Well, let me tell you as (apparently) one of the few people who tried to get into Broken Sword and just couldn't for whatever reason, this game is really enjoyable. I'm a big sucker for good voice acting and likable characters, and this game definitely delivers in that regard. A lot of genuinely funny moments. And touches like the protagonist texting her friend back home or the dress-up mechanic (that actually has in-game purpose) make it feel very warm. Plus, all of the locations are vibrant and gorgeous to look at. As there always are, there were a couple puzzles I spent way too long trying to figure out - but despite my frustration, I wasn't offended. I was just relieved I found a way to keep the story going.

_childDocuments_.review: I was very excited about this game after playing the demo and quickly added it to my wishlist! I purchased this the day after it was released for a 10% discount (17.99 USD). I enjoyed the references , the options for customization, and the multitude of things that could be clicked for the main character to view or express thoughts on. Regarding the story, I did not enjoy the main character's closest relationships. I felt they were forced, and I found one of them quite annoying. The side characters were more interesting to me, so I did not enjoy some of the puzzle solutions where the game forced scenarios to the detriment of some of these characters. As the game went on, more and more of the puzzles became trial and error for me. Quite a few of them seemed to be time-locked, or I had to do something specific beforehand, even though what I used or did should have worked. This was somewhat frustrating, but taking a break from the game and coming back much later on usually helped. For my first complete playthrough, it took me around 65 minutes to reach the point where the demo concluded, and I finished the game in 13.8 hours (there was a puzzle that I was stuck on for around 7 hours), with subsequent playthroughs being approximately 4 to 6 hours each. My playtime is not representative of how long it takes to complete the game, and I admittedly played this one distractedly. I often try to solve this type of game without guides for the first playthrough and sometimes even take a nap in the middle to refresh my brain! There were times that I accidentally left the game on while I was eating, napping, or just away doing other tasks. If I posted this review after my first playthrough, I probably would not have recommended this. Taking breaks in between and knowing how the puzzles worked without having to do as much trial and error (I still did some because my breaks lasted for months, and I did not remember everything perfectly) made the subsequent playthroughs more enjoyable. I did read that they rebalanced some of the puzzles after I finished my first playthrough, but I could not tell which ones changed and how they changed since the solutions seemed the same to me. Something that would greatly improve this game is . Many characters kept repeating their animations when talking to them again. It was nice at first, but it took up quite some time, especially when going back to them while on the trail of a clue.I do not recommend this to those who prefer more logic-based games or to those who dislike time or activity-locked mechanisms that may result in trial and error. For players like me who are not into excessive trial and error but may still appreciate the game's puzzles and ambience, or if you tend to solve this type of game quickly, I recommend getting it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Thumbs up if you like this kind of game, thumbs down if you are new to the genre it's not the easiest one I have played. My biggest complain without spoiling anything is that there is a mechanic that require you to pull things out of the inventory and use them in a timely fashion. _childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the most nicely presented modern point and click games I've played that still retains the feel of the classics. I like that the game doesn't resort to paying homage to the genre simply by using pixel art to mimic the old feel, but rather does so via the gameplay, the sense of adventure and discovery, the gorgeous locations and fun conversations between characters.- Gorgeous locations across Europe, the art is just sublime- Really good believable voice-acting and good soundtrack- Characters and friendships were really believable and sweet, and the control you have to both choose your main character's profession and to change their outfit made me feel more invested in the character. Really nice and new for a point and click adventure to have this kind of customisation, and I'd love to see more of it.- The puzzles were just right for me personally, usually requiring a few steps or a chain of thinking, but mostly logical and I didn't get frustrated by any moon-logic here. There were actually some subtle hints in dialogue and item descriptions that when you realised to pay attention really helped, and even when I got stuck for a while it was satisfying to make the connection.- Interesting story with a few twists and turns and it was neat to see Lithuanian history as the main theme of the game as it seemed really original and not something that is out there already in a game that I know of.- Only one place in the game really bugged me which I won't spoil but there was a puzzle that relied on dexterity and basically clicking the right place at the right time, it was a little frustrating as to me it doesn't go in line with the relaxed nature of a point and click game which is more about pondering solutions, than dexterity skills. But this was very minor in my enjoyment of the overall game.9/10, really hoping for a sequel!!

_childDocuments_.review: **NOTE:** This review is part of my steam curator review and is the extended version. Check my steam curator page at  . Follow appreciated!—	Have you ever seen a game that at first glance interests you, however upon a closer look it's part of a completely different genre than which you are used to, making you hesitant to try it out? This is that game for me. I was never really into Point and Click games. Still, the artstyle of this game somehow drew me closer making me wonder if I've been too harsh to Point and Click games. It most likely also has to do with the fact that the moment I saw the game's artstyle it made me think of Detective Pikachu on the Nintendo 3DS, and transformed me back to last summer. Having been one of my favorite game (and movie!), I just had to relive the moment by playing this game!As already mentioned (sorry! One last time), this game has an amazing artstyle! The perfect brightness of the colors that perfectly blend in with the occasional darker segments of the game are something you rarely see in games. If I had to compare it to something I would say the use of color is similar to that in a happy kids game. The graphics are also beautifully sharp. Of Course if you zoom in too close they get sort of pixelated, but with that amount of zoom you can't play the game properly anyway. What also really got me is that the game features fully spoken dialogue. Every action, every NPC, every choice (yes, you have choices in the dialogue you  speak), is brought to life by the developers decision to implement dialogue for everything there's to offer in this game! It really makes the player feel as if they aren't just playing ‘someones’ game, but are in the game ‘themselve’. It's one of those things where you have to experience it yourself to fully understand and appreciate it. Oh, and don't worry about the storyline! I have rarely played games which get the suspense up to a plot done correctly. Instead of somehow emerging in the middle of the plot, just for there to be a bigger plot, this game does it the traditional way by immersing you in a preplot which slowly builds up suspense (the good thriller book way). The story is an amazing crafted story which keeps players thrilled to the very end. Lastly, after having focused on the games art and story, now comes the most important part of all my reviews: Is the game worth the price? Well, let's discuss, shall we? While the price may seem steep to some, it's cheap when one compares it to the amount of playtime and story they are getting. Maybe I'm just bad at puzzles, but I could never never have completed this game in the minimum completion hours of 4 (according to Howlongtobeat). It took me almost 7! Further, as the game bases itself on semi accurate history in real locations, this is a perfect opportunity to learn while gaming! A lot of the things In this game, I would have never even thought of searching up, and yet here I am knowing about Lithuanian history (well sort of). You rarely find such games nowadays. All in all, I would say that based on all the aforementioned reasons, that this game is worth its price for the enjoyment and knowledge it brings. Good luck, upcoming adventurer!

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game after 8.4 hours and i loved every second of it. _childDocuments_.review: The graphics are nice, but an ancient computer might struggle a little in scenes with lighting effects even after the developers added the ability to change resolutions.Some people welcome dialogue options in games, but here some options might make the player miss a joke or two while ultimately leading to the same response. Similarly, choice of profession seems to only affect a couple dialogue lines and one puzzle in the whole game.There seems to be no running implemented, and, to my knowledge, animations cannot be skipped. Milda walks pretty slowly towards interactive spots, but at least there is instant teleport to location exit by double-clicking on it.There are almost no funny comments for combining wrong items. A couple of objects could only be picked up once Milda realized she needed them. This is not expressly stated, so those objects can easily be forgotten if the game is played in multiple sessions over a period of several days or weeks. The sound puzzle during a hockey match can only be solved by having saved during the second period of the match, unless one is blessed with sound memory in every sense of the word. Small hint for the scooter chase puzzle: it is not supposed to be played quite like the duels in Full Throttle. Overall, the puzzles are not too difficult, but, since some of them necessitate trial-and-error, I recommend having a guide handy.In general, it appears some things were cut from the game. Some characters could have had more of an arc, instead of coming across as insensitive sociopaths. The ending feels abrupt; the final room felt like there was supposed to be a puzzle involved with it, but it turns out to only serve as the backdrop for the final conversation with the villain and a cut-scene.Lastly, there are achievements for finishing the game choosing other professions - so three times altogether. I understand replays do not take as long once all the solutions have been worked out, but, since professions are only used for one puzzle, would it not be better to ask players to solve that one puzzle in three ways to be awarded the achievements? Imagine a D&D game having an achievement for playing through almost exactly the same campaign picking each class and dual-class combo - definitely not everyone's cup of tea.Ultimately, it is a decent first effort which, regrettably, can only be recommended if one has run out of classics to play, and does not mind putting up with the shortcomings to express support for the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. Point and Click is my favorite genre; I love to snuggle up and bang my head against puzzles.Most of the puzzles in this game were decent, but none of them really gave me an "aha" moment that marks the great point and click games like Monkey Island. A few of the puzzles were timing puzzles; twice this has the unfortunate effect of leading me to believe that the reason I wasn't solving the puzzle was that my timing was off when in reality I was missing a step in one of them (the balloon puzzle) and attempting to solve a puzzle that I wasn't ready to solve yet (the library cat puzzle) for another. Ultimately, I had to consult a walkthru to solve both puzzles. There was at least one other puzzle involving some cubes that was insufficiently clued (unless I missed something) and seemed to rely on trial and error. This got old *fast* because it took so long to try a solution and get the feedback. After four failed attempts I ran out of patience and had a walkthru open to find the correct combination. One of the final puzzles was insufficiently clued to progress (the shadow puzzle), and it turned out that I had solved it but had expected to get some reaction from the game, so I spent several extra minutes on it before turning to the walkthru and discovering that I had solved it and had just assumed that I had been wrong. Unfortunately, the story also just lacked interest. The characters failed to draw me in or make me care for their success and well-being. I could have quit the game halfway through and never really given it a second thought.I'm an impatient player: I tend to read the dialogue rather than give the characters the time to say it, especially if I'm not all that interested in what they're saying. In this game, I was constantly clicking to get them to hurry up and talk so that I could get back to the puzzles. So one thing that really irritated me was the random phone texts from the character's roommate in America asking for updates. I was forced to pause for what a ridiculously long time to read several lines of cellphone text dialogue and choose cheeky responses. But none of the responses seemed to relate to the game other than to recap what had happened so far. And this was especially annoying since it had literally all just happened to me. Being forced to choose dialogue for the sake of a cheeky text conversation that didn't affect the gameplay was irritating, especially since I couldn't seem to click past it all to speed it up.The game does feature a fun and quirky main character and some of the dialogue options were pretty fun. The humor just couldn't quite lift the game enough to save it for me. I do hope that the developers give it another go, though. There is some potential in the creativity of the premise and the puzzles, and I genuinely enjoyed learning about Lithuania. I feel bad not recommending this game because the game isn't poorly written or problematic and the company clearly put a lot of work into creating it. But I wanted to give an honest review for anyone else who is searching for a good point and click. I got this game on sale for half off and would probably only recommend purchasing it if it were even a bit cheaper than that.

_childDocuments_.review: Read this review and others “Dana do you have some coins?” By the way… Dana, do you have some coins for a trip to Europe?Who has never asked his friends for coins, throw the first rock. Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit is the adventure presented by the studio’s hand, Tag of Joy, which unfolds entirely through Point & Click mechanics.Milda, the main character who lives in Chicago, can come from one of three different professional backgrounds that will be chosen by the player at the beginning of the plot. Even in this aspect of choosing small details of the character, shows all the attention and affection for the main character. This is actually an aspect that at a certain point, can work as a conclusion for a puzzle. The fact that Milda brings with her camera allowing her to photograph all kinds of objects, landscapes, or even people has no direct impact on the story. However, it is also a fundamental piece to a certain extent. Eureka!It all starts when Milda receives a letter informing her of her grandfather’s disappearance. The letter also informs her that she has inherited her ancestor’s house and has about two weeks to travel to Europe, specifically Lithuania, to demonstrate her interest in keeping the house. Well, so far so good, except for the fact that she doesn’t have the money for this big trip. This is where her best friend Dana comes in. A painter budding to the life of an artist and with ideas of putting her name in the history of Alfred’s gallery. Friendship is a very explored point, or this is not one of the pillars that support the conclusion of all the plot and suspense present in this title. If you listen carefully, you can hear, deep in the background, the music “You got a friend in me”. Or maybe it was just my imagination.Upon arriving in Lithuania, Milda finds the house turned inside out as if someone was looking for something. “The plot thickens” when Milda discovers a hidden message from her grandfather, for her, about some king, knight, and crowns? Hence the name Crowns and Pawns.Like any young adult today, Milda will rely on her cell phone to help her unravel this intrigue. All the clues that are discovered will be displayed on her cell phone with the possibility of crossing them to reach the desired objective. This mechanic works quite well, it is only necessary to have bases to support the choices, or to spend a little time testing all the options provided.Point & Click titles are sometimes frustrating, mostly because of small details that can go unnoticed to the player’s eye, moments of trial and error, or actions that don’t make much sense. Crowns and Pawns is no exception to this rule, but it doesn’t become so frustrating that it makes me lose my hair. I mean, who uses a shovel on a brick floor? Without having any button designated for “hint” the conversation with Joris, her other good friend, can help point the way, without ever presenting how to get to the goal. Leaving all the “dirty” work open to the player.Definitely, the graphic aspect was also something that drew a lot of attention. A mix of 2D background with characters and small 3D elements transcribe a very pleasant sensation to the eye. It’s a treat to take in the sights of Lithuania’s cities, or through the picturesque alleys of Italy with the much-acclaimed Scooters. It would be wrong to visit Italy and not drive a Vespa, right?The sound is also a plus, with a varied and satisfying soundtrack. All the characters have excellent voice acting, managing to perfectly convey their personality traits to the listener. The chemistry between characters is hat’s off, even if the interactions are done via cell phone message. They managed to get a few laughs out of me.This is a small title in terms of story longevity. Of course, each player will have their own pace of solving puzzles, but it is effectively a game with a duration of about 4/5 hours.Although as previously stated Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit is a short title, it is quite fun for fans of the genre. The puzzles are somewhat logical, the characters are quite fun and with enough juice to drink throughout the adventure and the mix between history and fictional intrigue is genuinely captivating. It trapped me and kept me invested until the last second.“Hey, you reading this review, do you have some coins?”

_childDocuments_.review: I mean I love adventure games…but in this day and age most adventure games really require far more player agency/choice.  This is an extremely linear game for a game being made in 2022.  So first you have to prepare yourself for that.  On the plus side you do get a lot of character customize options, but these shortly become meaningless.  Overall the story of this game is just absurdly mediocre.  It’s basically a worse version of Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade right down to the ending.  It’s so uninspired.  I feel player choice is even more drastically critical if your overall narrative is just a rehash of a far better narrative.  Broken Sword 5 suffers from the same issues.  It does it better than this game sort of…but neither are games I’d recommend. Overall, I’m just sorely disappointed in this game.  It has a lot to like, but the story is just so terrible and pointless.  Even worse it’s just not worth the price.  This is a ludicrously short game.  It takes about 5hrs.  It literally feels unfinished.  The game has interesting characters.  The main character, Milda, is great.  Everything about her is fun, the voice actress just crushed it.  Shes a fun character that I want more of.  Even the side characters are fun like the insane cleaning lady or the super excited hockey fan.  At just 5 hours though…you just don’t get enough time with these people.  If this was a 12-15hr game with a similar predictable dull story, but I got to have more of these characters bantering back and forth and going on fun adventures, then I probably would be recommending this game.  Instead events happen at such a breakneck speed it just feels unfinished, like the original outline was larger, but then had to cut a lot of stuff out.  The fact you never find out what happened with your father despite this apparently being a major part of the story is a pretty good indication that this game is just unfinished.  The final room looks like it literally has a puzzle which is then just skipped.While the areas you explore are nicely done and interesting…the puzzles can be pretty arduous…not in the difficulty of solving them, instead it’s once you know the solution it can take a long time to accomplish this solution.  The library puzzle was exhausting to click just perfectly that it took a while after I figured out the solution.  Quite a few puzzles are this way.  Still as far as adventure games go, these are much better puzzles than most.    Sigh, there just isn’t much to say about this game.  It’s not the worst adventure game ever made, but it’s just way too short with a mediocre story.  I certainly wish this developer would make a new game with this character which is a proper 12-15hr game with choices and a drastically more interesting story, maybe try a murder mystery adventure game instead considering the characters are the strongest part of this game so it would be far better to focus on this strength in a story that can benefit from it like a murder mystery.  Until then, don’t bother, there are much better classic style adventure games like Unavowed or Technobabylon or more modern adventure games like Detroit Become Human or Elsinore.
