_childDocuments_.review: I've started playing "Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit".This is a light and colourful game with beautiful backgrounds, a movie or good TV show quality soundtrack, and a fun to play with main character whose outfit you can even customise. One puzzle I encountered even involved putting together the right pieces of clothing.I'm Milda Kovas, freelance photographer (I chose that profession from three options at the start of the game) and I just inherited a house from my grandfather in Lithuania. Once there, I discover some people are after a secret gramps seemed to've been hiding, so of course I want to go after it myself first!The game takes elements from "Broken Sword" and "Secret Files" to build a mystery drenched in history. I've encountered a couple of logic puzzles but the others are mostly inventory based. There is some level of interactivity added to interaction of NPC's by offering multiple ways to respond in conversations (not only in person but also by phone; calls ánd text messages), building your version of Milda's personality along the way.Your phone also has a "notes" option where Milda keeps track of major clues, and you can combine them to make progress.The quality of the game is top notch, it's everything what I expected, 5 hours into the game I encountered some doozies of puzzles, like trying to get my hands on a librarian's password, catching a cat, juggling metal cubes, and finally a good use of the in-game notes system to find three particular churches in the city of Vilnius, Lithuania.Finished "Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit" in 7 hours!I'm actually surprised I already finished it, because I was expecting a bit more puzzling in the end...After a little bit of comparing notes, which in my opinion is very underused in this game, I found my way to the finale. First I had to traverse a cave system in pretty much the same way one particular pirate wannabe finds his way in one particular island forest. Then what looked like the puzzle of all puzzles welcomed me at the final showdown, only... I didn't have to do anything. I got some kind of Indy and Elsa, Gabriel and Malia moment but that was it.I assume it has to do with the profession I chose at the start of the game (the photographer) and that this choice influences the puzzles you get. Perhaps one of the other professions really does have to do more in this finale, I don't know. I hope so, otherwise, that entire room seems like too much needless work from the art department.Anyway, I did enjoy this game very much. There were some tricky puzzles, not that traditional, but nothing all too hard. The only thing that really set me back somewhat was one small instance of pixel hunting. I had to look up where exactly to find one particular item I needed. Turns out it was in plain sight, I just didn't see it and Milda hadn't made a comment about it before. In my view you could only be led there by an assumption. All the regular puzzles were pretty much on the light side, and the game ended too sudden in my view, but it was very funny and certainly enjoyable! And who knows, some day I might play it again, choosing a different profession that time...
_childDocuments_.name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit

_childDocuments_.review: It's a charming 3D point-and-click adventure gem and if you enjoyed the likes of Secret Files or Lost Horizon (or classics like Syberia and the Broken Sword series, both of which this game explicitly references) then you'll really like this too. I see some reviews complaining about tough puzzles but I found nothing that seems remotely out of the ordinary for the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit

_childDocuments_.review: It´s a charming adventure game with some literal problems with the riddles design. There´s potential to be great but it´s just delightful. Great voice acting, beautiful graphics and sound design (the ost is joyful) but some of the puzzles are way convoluted (library, hockey or scooter, for instance). nevertheless, I liked the game a lot. Milda is such a lovely character...
_childDocuments_.name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable game.  A couple of times I was lost as to what to do next.  One was related to not understanding something to do with the inventory and another was not talking to a character again to find a new topic had appeared.  I wasn't a big fan of the scooter chase and had to watch a walkthru to see what I needed to do. But I thought the game was fun, the voice acting was good and the story was interesting.  Worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit

_childDocuments_.review: I will start with my conclusion: In overall I was satisfied with the game. If you enjoy adventure games you might consider a buy. But buy it at a discount!Pro: I liked the story and the unusual setting. The writing was enjoyable the voice acting good. What I really enjoyed where those dialogue options that didn't matter for the story but let you roleplay your character as you like. The puzzle where logical and on the easier side, but that was what I was in mood for. Grafics where good (lightly cartoonish 3D-models). I really enjoyed my time.Cons: However the game is really short. Maybe 5 - 7 hours play time. In my case it was one afternoon. And while my PC runs heavy 3D games easily my fans worked like crazy while playing this game without any visible reasons for that. So I guess with the next game developers should take more care with optimization.
_childDocuments_.name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit

_childDocuments_.review: A game in the style of the 'Secret Files Tunguska' (2006 ff.) series or the 'The Legend of Crystal Valley' game with a serious plot which involves investigation and conspiracies, only that it has a very special visual style (painting-like backgrounds and a bit cartoonic characters).And that is already one of the best ingredient of the game, the artwork. Every location looks inviting, and characters fit well into the scenes.Soundtrack is fine - although sometimes one has some action music where there is not much action in the scene, which feels a bit off.The story told is not one which would win a price, it's interwoven a bit with the amount of historical information one gets to know during the game, but yet entertaining.The puzzles are a bit ... mostly classical point-and-click-adventure puzzles, sometimes connected to the character wardrobe, and mostly fair. Hints for puzzles in the game are very sparsely scattered so that it is easy to get stuck at one or the other point in the game and to get in need for a hint from a walkthrough.To sum it up: An entertaining piece of artwork which is fun to play, even if it's not a star on the adventure games landscape.
_childDocuments_.name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit

_childDocuments_.review: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit is a great game! I play a LOT of point-and-click adventure games, and this is one of the best I've played in a long time. The puzzles are excellent -- well designed, some are difficult, but you can think your way through all of them. The voice acting was fantastic. The general gameplay was well-done, with a few clever bits. Plus, it was actually funny (not just "make a pop culture reference" funny). Plus, I learned a lot about Lithuania -- I may have to visit now! If you're looking for a good point and click experience, this is definitely worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit

_childDocuments_.review: Really well polished old-school-style adventure game. I love a good inventory management game and this one does not disappoint. The voice acting is superb, along with the score which supports a beautiful artscape that you will fall in love with. Love the fact the game spends time in Lithuania and if the game would ever have a sequel to explore more of this region and its history would be amazing. Story was very engaging with some twists and turns thrown in, and not everything answered but that's ok (again for a sequel to do that). Overall a lovely mystery that you can play at your own pace and very cosy for those of us who've played many adventure games of times gone by
_childDocuments_.name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a neutral button. I really like puzzles. NYT crossword every day, big point and click gamer, stack of board games in the house. I had to look up some guides to figure out the solutions to a lot of the puzzles. Not because they were difficult conceptually, but because the game fails to lead you to the answers it wants you to come to. The book, I don't think, adequately explained the orientation of the statues. The cat was weird because why on earth would you do that to the bagel? The story was interesting but the puzzling was dull and slow and sometimes nonsensical.
_childDocuments_.name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit

_childDocuments_.review: Crowns and Pawns is a delight. It does a great job of capturing the "menace to society" energy that I always enjoy in an adventure game protagonist, and the puzzles, though occasionally esoteric enough to be frustrating (there's a sound based one late in the game that was particularly bad), are by and large reasonable, and strike a good balance between being tricky without being maddening or impossible. The story is a great deal of fun. This game was crafted by people who love old school adventure games, and it shows, as you engage in a globe-trotting adventure of lost relics and international intrigue. Milda is an entertaining protagonist, and the plot knows exactly how seriously to take itself. If you're a fan of adventure games, definitely treat yourself to this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit

_childDocuments_.review: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit is a very interesting adventure game that takes us to the Republic of Lithuania. The main character, Milda, is here building a house for his grandfather, who just died. She learns everything from the letter that was delivered to her at the beginning of the story. So the journey and one great adventure can begin!The game has amazing graphics, despite some small things that don't quite fit visually. There is also nothing to complain about in terms of music. The soundtrack does have a main theme, which about half of the subplots stick to, but I can't say that it interfered with me in any way. On the contrary, I always looked forward to those certain tones.The puzzles are more or less common, some are original and others are based on the time window when you had to complete the given procedure. Unfortunately, there were also a few puzzles that had a precisely ordered procedure, despite the fact that a different order in the solution would not have led to any irregularities.Mechanically, the game lacks the principle of "teleports." That is the immediate movement of the character after double-clicking. In a few rare cases, this mechanic is there (clicking on items that move you to another location). The advantage is that you can use the spacebar to display usable items.Crowns and Pawns was a nice surprise for me. There are still flies to catch, but I would be happy for a sequel with a new adventure and the same main characters.My rating: 8.2/10
_childDocuments_.name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit

_childDocuments_.review: I've been an adventure gamer since the Lucasarts days.  I was pleasantly surprised by this game.  I enjoyed it way more than many other modern attempts at the genre.   Still, its  has some tiny annoyances, and some may find it a bit short.  But it has a lot going for it too: it's plot is based on history, and it feels smart - yet it doesn't overwhelm the player with exposition.  Most puzzles feel logical (ie. no cockraches needed to fix an electronic circuit, hear me Broken Sword?)  Puzzles can be solved in different ways, depending on which profession you select for the main character at the beginning of the game - this also means there's a lot of replay value. Graphics are bright and colorful, and voice acting is good and funny.  The ending comes at you swiftly and quickly, and leaves you wanting a bit more.  There are a few unresolved plot lines left, and a lot of questions remain unanswered.  Overall, a great package.  Here's hoping the developers are thinking about a sequel! I would gladly support it.
_childDocuments_.name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit

_childDocuments_.review: I first time tried this game for few minutes at Game-On-Comincon, I thought I liked it to play all, so my experience is that I really liked the graphics, the historic facts about Lithuania which I didn't even knew myself, more interesting information, but one thing I really disliked that there was no hints at all! I got stuck on some places for a long period of time, trying to figure out what to do and why i came here, because there is so much information, that I forgot what I need to do next.. In other hand there was a lot of really funny dialogues.
_childDocuments_.name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice, old-style point & click adventure game with strong hints of Broken Sword!Very recommended for people who like this series. The end felt a bit rushed and like a bit of cut content and some design choices felt a bit forced (do we really need to change costumes in adventure games?) but overall it was very good. Some jokes fell flat but the voice acting cast is very good and made most of it work.I can absolutely see this developing into a long-running series like Broken Sword which was a clear inspiration for this.It's not too challenging in most parts but some puzzles had me reaching for a guide. Sometimes things became obvious after but one or two puzzles I never figured out...
_childDocuments_.name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit

_childDocuments_.review: Crown and Pawns is a  solid point and click game that could be compared to the likes of the Monkey Island series, with the graphics and story to boot. It was a nice change on the standard traditional point and click adventure, with a nice Indiana Jones twist. I appreciate the modern day element to it, though the whole texting element seemed kind of irrelevant, all in all though a solid game for a decent length adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit

_childDocuments_.review: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit is traditional point and click adventure with modern setting and graphically more modern than most of the retro stuff.There are some frustrating puzzles. One involves long animation and after that  limited time to do anything. Another involves guessing. Most of the puzzles are not bad though.Puzzles that are somewhere in the middle are ones involving studying and researching. Some of it is quite straightforward, but sometimes you might forget relevant clue and get quite confused.What shines though, is the presentation and sense of humor. Graphics are combination of 3D and 2D and look quite nice. Voice acting fits quite good into the game. Just right amount of quirkiness to keep things interesting.Plot is good enough to keep things interesting, but in the long term it might not be memorable.If you're fan of traditional point and click games, this is worth trying out. For the first timers it might be too frustrating.PS: for the achievement hunters there's some annoyance. Getting all of the achievements requires three playthoughs and while there's some unique things based on the chosen profession, completing the game three times might be bit too much grinding
_childDocuments_.name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit

_childDocuments_.review: Crowns and Pawns is a decent point and click adventure game; though not without some flaws. By far, the voice acting is the best part of the game; all the characters are certainly well voiced; the main character in particular. She can also wear a number of different outfits and hairstyles, which I thought was a cute touch. Some of the puzzles are enjoyable and for the most part aren't very difficult, though its certainly possible to get stuck in a spot or two.The weakest part of the game is in the story; a young woman travels to Lithuania in search of an ancient crown with magical powers. A typical story told far too many times and simply lacks imagination; there isn't a whole of intrigue or any real plot twists. You're really just trying to get from point A to B to C and so on.Overall, I did enjoy the game but it isn't particularly groundbreaking. If you're itching for a new point and click adventure; there are certainly worse options out there, but don't expect to be sucked into anything grand.
_childDocuments_.name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit

_childDocuments_.review: Good game overallPros:-One of the (if not the) first decent graphics game related to Lithuania-Real world Vilnius map and somewhat accurately pictured places-Attractive, light and bright visuals, suitable for all age groups-Positively neutral soundtrack, matches quest game genre-Story includes historical persons-I liked the minigamesCons:--Too short for full price - expected more content
_childDocuments_.name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit

_childDocuments_.review: One of the titles that reiterate how the point-and-click glory days are back, baby! It even directly references one of the other recent examples of the genre, Gibbous: there, it was Romanian developers telling a story about a second-generation expat coming back home, here it's Lithuania's turn. It's clearly reminiscent of Broken Sword and kind of short (a second playthrough skipping the dialogues takes about two hours), but the story is good, the historical details are well-researched, the places and dialogues feel real, the puzzles are grounded, the voice acting is top-notch, the characters are solid and the protagonist is adorable.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful point-and-click adventure game. The puzzles are a bit complex at times in this one (I had to google what to do several times, but I don't mind that) so they can be challenging at times because it's not always clear what to do (once you do figure it out one way or another though it does make sense). I love when these point-and-click adventure games come out. I enjoy the 3D art style of this game. You can customize your main character and even choose what to say (it's more fun, not "decision breaking" of what you choose to say). The jokes in this game were good and clever to me. I hope to see this turn into a series, but above all else Tag of Joy to keep making point and click adventure games.And now, for a while, I'm going to go around town and scream "ATTACKERS FAIL, GOALIE WILL PREVAIL!". Buy this game and support these wonderful people making these types of games. And you will know exactly what I mean by that quote above when you play the game for yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit

_childDocuments_.review: Great for those who like point-and-click, adventure, puzzle solving. There were a few parts that were incredibly challenging. One was extra frustrating just because of the timing (scooters), but overall this was a great game. GREAT GRAPHICS. Loved the way she walked, options to change her outfit/hair. Wish double-clicking could get her to walk faster (though she doesn't necessarily walk slow). Good voices, I kept the music off (never like playing with music). Wish games would offer ambiance, weather, or season choice (that would be fun and different). Liked Tamara's New York/New Jersey accent. At the beginning of the game you get to choose your profession (photographer, and two others... pharmacist?...and.... can't remember.) _childDocuments_.review: My only complaint:  that the game wasn't longer.  I thoroughly enjoyed playing it, and hope the devs make another!  And maaaaaybe that there was a "love connection", but it's ok...I still had a fondness for the characters' relationship even if it stayed pretty much platonic.  Awesome game, didn't want it to end. _childDocuments_.name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best point-and-click adventures I have played. In my opinion, what distinguishes it from other games of such type, is, first and foremost, clever and interesting puzzles, many of them needing out of the box thinking. Second, the atmosphere of Vilnius, New York and other cities you visit along the way (don't want to spoil anything) is joyous, sunny and colorful - something that gloomier point-and-click adventures tend to lack these days. Since the game takes place in historically and geographically accurate places, these are spots that you can visit in real life. I also must say I enjoyed the quirky, memorable cast of characters Milda encounters (her sarcastic yet friendly dialogues with Dana are simple priceless!) and various bits of historical trivia I got introduced to. Do recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, well written story, with a gorgeous art style and a fabulous lead character. Milda's VA is probably the highlight of the game, but all the voice work is on point. However, for me there was considerable frustration in some of the puzzles. I didn't have problems with the likes of Norco or Kathy Rain, but this one caused much swearing during the mid-game locations. Overall, a positive experience though.
_childDocuments_.name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game to be decent. Seems pretty clear that we might get a sequel tough. The characters was mostly fine and decent and so was the ending. The story was overall good. The setting and the places you visit was also good and varied enough. Even if i found some of the puzzles a little weird , but then again i am bad at these types of games. _childDocuments_.name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit

_childDocuments_.review: Point and click is not the mainstay of gaming that it once was. For a small studio to take a punt on the genre in 2022 is brave, but it pays off. The passion for point and click classics shines through, while a few modern ideas remove some of the frustrations that usually go hand in hand with games of this type.I really enjoyed the art style (although it does suffer when zoomed in). It would also be nice if the ancillary characters had more to say. Almost everything they have to say is salient to the plot or current puzzle.Based on the quality of the development, it would be great to see what the team could do with a lesser known classic like ToonStruck or a spiritual successor thereof.
_childDocuments_.name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit

_childDocuments_.review: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit is a refreshing return to the glory days of point-and-click adventure games.  The story is pretty basic, almost cliché at this point, where we meet up with Milda who lives in Chicago, but after inheriting an old house in Lithuania, sets off to Europe to claim her new home and triggers a surprising epic adventure.  Her grandfather’s house is loaded with clues all leading to some 15th century relic that will have you exploring all sorts of real-world European locales, solving puzzles, and avoiding a dangerous foe.Ready the full review at Watch the first two hours of the game at More Steam reviews on our Curator page -

_childDocuments_.review: what a fun point and click adventure game ala da vinici code/Indiana Jones or more similar like a broken sword game- it even has a goat. it can be a little a frustrating at times , but so worth it for the old school type of puzzles!. great voice acting and writing .the art direction great too very painterly and full of vibrant color. Your dialog and even some choices matter? or at the very least with get you specific to that choice's responses, it so cool! like for example a certain character will recognize if they see you  wearing there old shirt(kept vague to prevent spoilers) .honestly i played through to credits and I'm still thinking is there still something i could go back and do ? maybe get the rest of the achievements .great game i recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit

_childDocuments_.review: I'm usually an avid fan of 2D art for point & click adventure games, but here the 3D works really nicely; the characters are well designed and nicely animated, and the character customisation is a nice touch - in a couple of places it even plays into the plot. The dialog is lighthearted and occasionally honestly funny, and the voice actors do a great job delivering it, especially the protagonist.The plot is pretty interesting - set in modern times but explores a story set over several centuries of Lithuanian (and European) history - but towards the end it feels a little rushed; I would be happy to keep exploring more and delve deeper into the mysteries of the past and the protagonist's story.The puzzles are decent - some quite clever, some a bit strange and potentially frustrating, because the game doesn't often provide helpful feedback to incorrect-but-on-the-right-track attempts. Another cause for frustration is that some characters have quite tedious animation sequences before or during their dialog, so chatting with them again and again can become a little tiresome.Overall it's a nice little indie game that I enjoyed for a good few hours. If you tend to get impatient I would keep a walkthrough guide handy so you can always skip trying things over and over again.
_childDocuments_.name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit

_childDocuments_.review: A very nice P&C adventure that captures the spirit of its role model Broken Sword. Thanks to tricky puzzles and excellent speakers, the game even feels very high-quality - but unfortunately you can tell that the ending was completed relatively hastily (a puzzle is even obviously missing shortly before the end).Nevertheless, a full recommendation and the hope for a successor that gives answers to the unanswered questions in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit

_childDocuments_.review: Personally, I really like this game. I love that you can dress up the MC and how her profession changes the puzzles slightly. The graphic also look charming and well done. The MC is fun though other characters are fairly simple and sort of dull. The story has a nice hook but becomes straightforward real quick with one or two twists. (Not a bad thing, btw.) The villain is boring and you’ll notice him immediately. (No, seriously. As soon as he’s on screen you’ll know who the main villain is.) The puzzles  are okay, except for two that can get annoying. All in all, I recommend playing for those who like point and click adventures.
_childDocuments_.name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit

_childDocuments_.review: All in all an enjoyable experience. I liked the characters and most of the puzzles could be figured out without a walkthrough. The graphics were clear and bright and the story was plausible. The only thing I did not care for were the challenges where the player had to be quick with actions. Maybe it was a lack of adroitness on my part, or a lagging Macintosh mouse, but two challenges in particular took me waaaay too long to successfully complete. Otherwise, highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished Crowns and Pawns.It was decent-ish. **Good**Traditional Adventure with some decent additions like being able to customise your characters look which plays into a couple of the puzzles.You choose her profession and dialogues have options on how to respond etc They change depending on your profession allowing for replayingDecent graphics I liked the idea that it was about Lithuania so could learn more about the history of a country I know nothing about **Bad**Its' short (about 8 hours - longer if you struggle with some of the puzzles) and felt unfinished. _childDocuments_.review: Great story and nice puzzle! It really brought me back to my Broken Sword obsession years. There are of course some more modern sensibilities injected in the formula: like outfit customization that come into play in some puzzles and even a career choice that changes one puzzle. It made me want more of these kind of changes and some kind of epilogue where you see Dana's paintings of our adventures!
_childDocuments_.name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit

_childDocuments_.review: classic style point & click adventure which ticks all of the right boxes for a fan of the genre. graphics are excellent, so are music and voicing. the story is on par with the best adventure games out there. humor is top notch, language is in tune with contemporary youth, which helps with immersion, since the protagonist and her friends are young peeps. in fact all of the characters talk and behave like you'd expect from them. there are neat references/nods to other great games of the genre and you get a slice of lithuania, its culture and history. the puzzle design doesn't disappoint (except the mailbox puzzle could have been explained better), some of the puzzles were proper head-scratchers, which is not a bad thing at all in my book. such were the 80's & 90's classics after all. all in all a great game and a proper P&C adventure experience i'm glad i didn't miss.
_childDocuments_.name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit

_childDocuments_.review: Crowns and Pawns is a broken sword type of adventuregame set in eastern europe. It features a very engaging and interesting storyline, acted out by a nicely done cast of interesting characters which perfectly fit the narrative. It's presented in a fairly typical 2.5D-style, but is very well done with livid animations and palette. The great visuals and professional voice-overs makes for a pleasant audio-visual experience, and the whole game just oozes of tender loving care towards the end product.My only gripe with this game is that the puzzles are hit and miss. Most are well designed and fun to work through, but others feels like arbitrary obstructions for the player to suffer through before resuming the game.I enjoyed and certainly recommend this game, but more than anything I sincerely hope for the developers to get funding for new games. They are a very talented team and deserve to hone their skills to make even greater games in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit

_childDocuments_.review: It's direct sequel should focus more on uncovering Milda's family secrets, while choosing between 1 of 3 career paths should always affect more than 1 significant in game self-transaction. Items should automatically be self-removed from inventory when no longer needed for any scene, cutscenes such as travelling from 1 map to another should be skippable, texting by phone should be removed; since it needlessly took way too long for both sides to respond, self-interactive animation between characters should show clear visible items when they actually receive, or use them; than just miming it with thin air, and there should be more self-hints as what to do next when stumped; when asking a particular character what should I be doing?

_childDocuments_.review: Has all the charm of an old school point and click, One of my favourite genres and a worthy entry.Some puzzles can be a little convoluted, requiring unnecessary back tracking for literally 10 seconds of work (thinking of 2 instances near the start). The first segment of the game has both of these "problems" and I feel the game gets much better once you get to lithuania.I'd love to see more from the company, they have a lot of potential!

Maybe being still on the easy side.There are some action/timing scenes for what I am not so sure that they fit in this genre of games.Nice Voice acting, funny dialogues,  brilliant backgrounds and good character writing. Very polished game, could not seeany glitches or similar annoyances.Already waiting for sequel or other adventures by this ream. Love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Crowns and Pawns: Kingdom of Deceit

_childDocuments_.review: Nice game, especially in a bad time for point-n-click's. Being a huge fan of the genre, I was very disappointed of some of the games released lately. They were either way too short or too easy, most of them both. They just felt like clicking through a short story.Therefore, I was very happy to read the first reviews of this game regarding the puzzles, and I bought it right away. Right from the start, I was very happy with the first puzzles. I like it, when puzzles have a more or less obvious solution where you basically know what you have to do, but the solution isn't as straightforward as it looks like and you have to work for it. Guybrush-enthusiasts know what I'm talking about. This game has those puzzles. Sometimes you're just stuck for a while and have to think about the solution. Graphics are very nice.So much for the parts i really liked. But since i played A LOT of those games, I think there still weren't enough puzzles, and there should have been some harder ones. Personally, I think there should be a good balance between easy, medium, hard and very hard puzzles. This game is missing the last two - maybe you could say there are some puzzles that are in the upper medium or even in the lower hard area. Don't get me wrong, I really enjoyed the puzzles. Like I said, they were very decent, especially compared to the latest bigger releases. I'm saying this, because from reviews of other games I read, I get that some people find that to be a good thing. Also, if you are rather new to the genre, having started and enjoyed games like gibbous, you might consider this game for a little more challenge. But if you're the old-school monkey-island-player (which i compare every game in the genre to), this might not be a real challenge to you, but still an enjoyable game.Even though this game wasn't really too short, it could have been longer. The story was very straight-forward. What happened to those middle parts where you could visit a lot of locations and had to solve side quests you had to solve? This game has it, but a "light version" of it. This is sad, because the game has the potential for that. Another sad thing is, that the game has a lot of likable characters, that could be interesting, but aren't. That's the part where the side quests could come in. You should have to work the characters more to get what you want and make them more memorable. You know you've created such a character when you can let her or him reappear in the second part, like a skull or a tentacle. ;) Again, the characters all had the potential to make the game longer and with some harder puzzles.Also, the ending was a bit abrupt. It was missing a final puzzle. OK, that was a lot of complaining, but after all, i really enjoyed the game. The story is interesting enough and it's "family-friendly funny" (Not as funny as a lot of the classics, though). But most importantly, I didn't feel like sitting in front of my screen, just watching a story. I had to do my playing and it's a good game worth it's time. After all, it is a good game. I just think if could have done the things mentioned above better and then would have been a great game. Maybe a second part will deal with that? I would play it.

name: Mini Motorways
detailed_description: Have you ever been stuck in traffic and wished you could do something to fix it? In Mini Motorways, the city’s traffic problems are in your hands. From the makers of Mini Metro, Mini Motorways is a game about drawing the roads that drive a growing city. Build a road network, one road at a time, to create a bustling metropolis. Redesign your city to keep the traffic flowing, and carefully manage upgrades to meet the changing demands. How long can you keep the cities of the world moving? Key Features Draw roads in dynamic cities that grow and change - every game is unique! Explore stunning maps inspired by cities all around the world. Choose from a variety of upgrades to meet the demands of your ever-expanding road network: highways, roundabouts, and more! Stress-free Endless Mode offers you a relaxing gameplay experience, plus you can continue building your city after Game Over. Tackle our Expert Mode, which features twists such as permanent roads and limited upgrades for the ultimate challenge. Select different colour palettes on every map including colourblind and night modes. Relax to a responsive soundtrack from Disasterpeace that grows along with your city. Unlock new maps and achievements as you achieve mastery. Export GIFs of your city layouts to share with your friends. Compete against other players in Daily and Weekly Challenges.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun and challenges you to think ahead and think differently. In the early game, there is plenty of breathing room for occasional mistakes or readjustments, but the late game difficulty ramps up exponentially as more and more precision is required.Unfortunately, the game has some poor pathfinding behaviors as well as a few noticeable bugs, e.g.:- Shops spawning when no houses of the same color have spawned (see screenshots).- Replacing an intersection with a roundabout results in cars freezing and doing nothing (see screenshots).- Stoplights change too rapidly and are barely functional.- Cars always take the *shortest route*, not the fastest route (I thought I was building motorways for a reason?).It also suffers from a few UI problems:- If you accidentally delete a motorway (and don't have a spare sitting around handy) there is *no way* to undo. You have to wait for every car to finish using it. In the late game, this can be a game-ending mistake.- The motorways cannot be made transparent and must clicked and dragged like rubber bands (hint!) in order to peep behind them.- Once the map gets large, it's hard to notice when houses spawn, and they may do so facing the wrong road, causing the cars to immediately embark on the stupidest, most scenic route possible around the map. If only there was an option to have the game pause (or slow down) when houses spawn so I could orient them correctly, instead of this reflex requirement.Overall, I felt forced to give a negative review to highlight these frustrations I've experienced with the late game here. And while I have no doubt that any casual player would enjoy it - I feel strongly that a strategy game should challenge you to think ahead / outside the box and tackle mounting obstacles, *not* force you to handle inconsistent behaviors, and punish you for 'misclicking' something in the UI.Also, I wish I could replace the trees );

_childDocuments_.review: The game has potential but in my opinion it doesn't offer significant levels of strategic depth in its current state. Given the randomness of spawns, you can't put a significant level of strategy into futureproofing your designs, nor does the game provide for enough resources to build robust infrastructure early that would benefit you down the line. When you do get into the later game, you generally don't have enough resources or time to overhaul your designs.As a result, I feel like every round develops the same way; you build a lot of direct routes because that's all you can do with limited resources and the game ends when you get some bad spawns that make it difficult for you to account for in your design.One pretty easy change that I think the game would benefit from is giving you more advanced notice about spawns (e.g. you'll see all spawns as grayed-out modules X weeks before they land in the same way that a city would know about new construction well ahead of time). That would allow you to juggle immediate needs with some short/long term planning rather than only juggling immediate needs.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: It's simple and fun traffic "simulator", for a while.This game is about minimalism, in artwork, and in mechanics. You aren't trying to build a mega-city, rather put together a functioning road system on a small map. There's no real winning, you just try to do better each time. As you play, more maps will unlock. Surprisingly, small alterations in the map create different challenges.For the price point this is okay, but it loses its appeal fast. There's no real depth to the gameplay, and after several iterations you realize you can't make a huge difference in the outcome, especially due to randomness.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little game, pretty straightforward enough in gameplay, quick to get into, pleasing simplistic graphical design, lovely audio design with the blips and bloops and time distortion.I feel like it would benefit from additional features like a sandbox/god mode, workshop support for player-made levels, or at the very least procedurally generated levels.Aside from that, for the gameplay in its current form, I have one gripe, and it's a pretty big one at that;The visitor demand for the buildings is in no way programmatically related to the number of houses.This means that, on a few occasions, the game-ending condition is outside of the players control, literally impossible to satisfy the demand.Sometimes a building can have a demand that is so high, cars cannot possibly arrive at it fast enough. Or not enough houses for a particular colour are able to spawn and meet the demand.There's no ensured balance of colour distribution in any given game, as each level is human-made*, and so it is pre-defined where buildings of particular colours can spawn. The starting zone is positioned randomly around the middle-ish of the map area, and since player-placed roads may cover potential spawn places for any given colour, and the player can't really tell exactly where those areas are (unless they play it a lot and record spawn rates and such across 100s of games), it's possible that not enough houses of a colour will be able to spawn, while the demand just keeps rising unrealistically.I've had conditions where it's just one colour of house and one colour of building, and there wasn't enough space for it to spawn more houses and more buildings, so the demand was all on the one building, and not enough houses could satisfy it, even with all the road going directly to it.So it's clear the supply/demand mechanic, which is like the main mechanic in the game, is not  programmatically balanced at all. I feel like this is quite an oversight, and surprised nobody caught it during play-testing.So, essentially, it's really down to chance whether a run is gonna be doomed to fail due to map design and start conditions, or player fault.I've had quite a few occasions where the loss conditions were no fault of my own, and I'm getting pretty tired of it, it's making the game a lot less fun for me tbh.* from my understanding based on the  the devs postedP.S. The developers/publishers appear to be greedy selfish A-Holes, Bullying a solo developer who developed their own game, inspired by this and others, into removing it from steam because of baseless legal claims.

_childDocuments_.review: A video review of this game is . Alternatively, here is a text version of my thoughts:Mini Motorways is the successor to Mini Metro, both being very minimalist city traffic management simulators. And really, there's nothing quite like a game that embraces simplicity as a core tenet, because it's nice to see something easy to pick up and play. The thing is, like Mini Metro, this game has some very fundamental flaws that really hurt the experience. At one point, you will lose control of your situation, and watch as everything burns down around you.Do you want to play Mini Motorways and win? The city already segregates people by one of a few colours, why not maximize your racial disparity and segregate your city as much as you can? Have only a few houses go exclusively to a business. Minimize cars sharing roads. If possible, have only one colour use one road. Buy those 30 road tiles instead of traffic lights. Motorways aren't gamebreaking, but they're effective bridges over everything.But then the game just starts spewing buildings faster than you can handle, you run out of road, they start being in VERY inconvenient areas, and you lose with 1800 points because of it. You're going to suffocate in traffic from all the leaded gasoline because of the game's intentional "ha ha time to fail" design, and there's nothing you can do about it.And yet, it's one of the most addictive games you can play, but it's the good kind of addictive. Unlike other games, I can just leave and not worry about it. It's simple to get in, it eases you in nice, and then starts ramping up the paranoia and anxiety for a good 15-20 minutes and then the game's over.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: As far as simulation concepts that get boiled down into pretty and well-designed game mechanics, the only other game I can think of besides Mini Motorways is its predecessor, Mini Metro. This is low-complexity with seemingly few mechanics that can quickly turn into a city planning nightmare. With the beautiful synth soundtrack, though, that is tuned to the beats of your traffic, Mini Motorways always fits that balance between chill and stressful in its game. The devs also stepped up all of the game juice in graphics, art, and sound. Highly recommended for the busy gamer looking for games that can be played in one-offs. Also there are a ton of city maps with more being added all the time.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let it fool you; you're actually getting  games.One is stress-free, charming game that lasts around 10 minutes. You get sucked in by the music, lulled in by a false sense of peace and zen that the beautiful pastel colours and relaxing ambient music create.Then... Nothing prepares your for what comes next. It becomes the most unforgiving sim I have ever played. Gone is the soft, ambient music, replaced by the horns of the cars that never got to work. They haunt me at night. Let your attention drift even for a moment, and it becomes a beautiful mess of colours. _childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: A game with a simple premise. Make use of your ever dwindling resources to construct a motorway system that can transport the ever increasing traffic that inhabits the miniature island. What a grand concept that is easily understood, no? You think so, don’t you. You know nothing. The true motive is to lull you into a false feeling of safety, security and control. Once you are hooked, you are now a slave to the game and it’s machinations. You cannot stop. You will never quit. You will become like the cars that inhabit the world you helped create. Stasis. Agony. Despair. Unending anguish. Your spirit will have been crushed under the tire of capitalism, and it’s ever churning, unrelenting wheels. There will have been no point to your struggle. You will have wasted precious hours, days or hell, even months trying to achieve a mere fraction of the goal you had set. This, my friend, is the meaning of life.What are these miniature automobiles? Such a frivolous creation, serving no more than a cosmetic purpose. We are witnessing the decay of society as the populace slowly succumbs to the trappings of capitalistic greed. While their pockets overflow with currency they can scarcely find a way to spend, they instead take to the construction of miniature highways that exist for naught but their twisted pleasure. Truly, a disgusting display of conspicuous consumption, that would have the late Karl Marx turning in his proverbial grave.The urban hellscape is not as terrifying as some may think. Yes, it is rather daunting, especially when the driver is faced with the conundrum of either taking an alleyway to save time, only to get stuck in a dead-end with no escape, a fate worse than a lifetime of being an office worker. Though this could be avoided, if more people were willing to listen to the voices of the schizophrenic, instead of dismissing them as lunatics, due to the fact they are not willing to adhere to the oppressive systems that are currently in place.You have been tasked with solving a seemingly impossible dilemma that only the mentally unstable can achieve. For you must figure out the optimal method of getting all these automobiles to their destination without causing widespread pandemonium. Yes, this is a herculean task, which can lead, and often does, to the onset of mania, followed by a bout of depression, but this is where the fun begins. For it is only when you are pushed to the absolute brink of (in)sanity, that your greatest potential is realized and your greatest creations become a reality. Why continue the facade of a well adjusted being, when the voices within your head, offer a far more tantalising proposition. Join us, they whisper, and you will be freed from the shackles of a mundane and boring office life, and with it all your problems disappear. No longer will you be confined to your prison cell, you will instead live within a reality of your own making. The walls of your home will be demolished and the only remaining structure will be your imagination. Only then will you truly be freed from the oppressive social conventions and archaic societal norms that once held you hostage.With each passing traffic jam, you are further pushed into the depths of madness. The traffic is a symptom of a much broader issue. the roads in the cities of the Mini Motorways realm of existence are far too narrow to accommodate the sheer volume of drivers on the road. Not to mention the fact that it's extremely difficult to maneuver with the amount of vehicles present, especially when trying to shift lanes. An individual will find that what he or she is creating is no mere road but a highway to purgatory. A road paved, not with materials such as rock or brick, but paved with the tears of men and the souls of the lost. A road that leads only to one place, the fiery den where the damned reside in perpetuity.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: It's a decent game. Has an interesting simplistic art-style and soundtrack. It is fun for a few hours, but eventually gets pretty repetitive. Considering how simplistic the game is, and the fact that the game is literally about tracking numbers, you'd think they'd be able to track achievements properly. After successfully completing a weekly challenge, it sometimes just doesn't increment the number.I've looked online and from the sounds of it, many other people are having this issue as well.It is a good game, but I just don't understand how these achievements are so broken.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this game but only for a short time. This is the kind of game that gets less enjoyable the better you understand it. At least that is what happened to me.Once you have a little experience you realize that the best strategy is to keep everything separated as much as possible. Always connect a bunch of houses with a destination and avoid intersections at all costs. So essentially you are doing the opposite of designing an actual believable city. You are designing a bunch of segregated communities that never interact with each other. You can of course try to have something that more closely resembles an actual city but you will not be able to enjoy it for very long before it's game over.I think the main problem lies in the objective itself.1. It's your job to supply destinations with customers, not the other way around. If a destination doesn't get enough customers, you lose.2. Only cars of matching color can go to a specific destination.3. Spawning of houses and destinations seems fairly random.The result of that is that you will inevitably get a destination spawning on the opposite end of the map from where its target demographic lives. And now you have to somehow find a way to get those people over there and fast. The business doesn't get punished for building in a stupid place, you do. And the only way to resolve this situation is by building a direct connection, again without coming into contact with any other traffic, or the cars will simply be too slow and the business dies and you lose.TL;DR:The game is challenging. There are ways to succeed and if you just want a puzzle to solve, you might enjoy it.But if you want some of the aesthetics of actual traffic and an actual city with intersections and actual OPTIONS for your citizens, this game will punish you for that.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: Like Mini Metro, I absolutely love the sort of relaxed, zen-like gameplay, right until things get hectic.The road building mechanic (if done right) gives you some level of control over the game, unlike in Mini Metro, where you could only react to stations popping up all over the place.However, here you have no direct control over the actual traffic-flow itself, which is the really challenging part, since you can't simply reassign cars / trains to service overcrowded destination like you could in Mini Metro and it's therfore way easier to have lost the game before you even realise it.But overall it is a much more tactical successor to Mini Metro and I love it.

Everything else about the game is great, but this design choice ruins it as a simulator. It's still a decent puzzle game though.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game  This game is all about organizing road in a growing road network. _childDocuments_.review: A very simple title from game design perspective - the map spawns color coded houses, that each has 2 cars which need to collect "orders" from destination of the same color code. To do that you connect them with road tiles. It starts all nice and simple and after around 15-20 minutes you are looking at a road spaghetti trying to figure out how you got there.The challenge is in resource scarcity. Your main resource is road tiles, which can be upgraded with traffic lights, roundabouts, bridges, tunnels and highways. You earn these resources by advancing in time.Each run ends with you losing to the ever increasing traffic jams in your city and there are different milestones to how far can you get on each map.The game provides lot's of content, an abundance of maps, challenges and achievements. It's great for short wind-down gaming sessions after a hard working day. Helps to clear your mind.I see myself playing this for quite some time ahead. A strong recommend if you have gotten this far.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite this game's pros, it's many cons keep me from recommending it.PROS:- Cohesive simplistic appealing art style- Sound design fits the style and flows with gameplay- Good game concept- Immediately addictingCONS:- Road building; For the most part road building is functionally easy to grasp and master, however when it comes to gameplay it has a big critical failure. So, if I want to modify my existing roads and I don't have any road pieces I can subtract roads in order to gain them back to be placed elsewhere, right? In a traffic management game this would seem pretty critical because conditions can quickly change and you need to optimize your roads to keep traffic flowing. HOWEVER, in this game, when you delete a piece it doesn't immediately return the piece to your inventory because its waiting for cars to finish their route across it... So you can either wait 4 days for the cars to eventually all finish their routes, meanwhile your cars elsewhere are unable to get to their critical locations for lack of pieces, OR you can do nothing and wait 3 days until a new week when you're given extra road pieces. You can't even undo erasing a road. If you try to draw it back on it tells you you don't have enough pieces. It's BS, man. This may be by design but If it is I'd say it was a bad idea. - Win State; When your game ends, it ends because you failed. You're struggling to keep up as long as you can until you lose to the game's procedural building generation and increased traffic congestion. Combined with being unable to modify and optimize roads and you're at the mercy of the game.- Variation; Each map of the game is quite basically the same as all other maps. The only differences is a lake slightly in a different position, or a river that cuts across horizontally instead of vertically. Throughout the levels there isn't an introduction of new abilities or mechanics. It's just the same thing at the same difficulty level for the entirety of the game. You can experience it all in a few hours.  FINAL THOUGHTSI think the fundamental flaw here is not giving players enough creative freedom to modify their cities traffic flow to a meaningful degree, and in a game with randomized procedural building generation and limited supplies, you can never plan your cities ahead and prepare for all scenarios. For these reasons I struggled to find meaningful enjoyment out of it. Others may not find these issues break their experience and that's fine. You will know if you like it in an hour or two.

_childDocuments_.review: Mini Motorways is a light little logistics game about getting cars to businesses as efficiently as possible by building roads, bridges, tunnels, overpasses, and roundabouts (and, rarely, traffic lights). It has about a dozen maps with unique terrain and spawn tendancies, along with RNG spawns of each house and business to keep the puzzle unsolved. I've been replaying maps just for the fun of it, but by the time I get all the achievements, I'll probably have 30-35 hours played. Absolutely solid game and a very fair price.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Mini Metro (got 100% achievements and many hours played), but I cannot recommend this title in its current state. I'm sure developers will improve most of the issues, but for now the list of inconveniences is way to long:- Traffic lights are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.- Roundabouts aren't much better.- There is no way to build elevated roads for overpasses, we are forced to intersect roads.- There are two strategies to get a good score: build ugly city with separated roads and highways, or block the spawn of houses by placing empty roads.- Houses spawn at super random interval and locations, leading to whole neighbourhoods left without roads because we don't need to connect them- Upgrades are also super random, and sometimes you can get owned by getting 6 bridges and nothing else.- Entry points to the buildings are also random and there's no way to adjust how cars will reach the parking zone, leading to ridiculous situations and zigzags.- Timeou timer when building is full is reduced when car arrives, but the amount it is reduced is so small that it grow even more before the car can even leave the parking zone.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of Mini Metro, I had high expectations for its sequel, Mini Motorways. Thankfully, the game delivers!If you're looking for a relaxing, puzzle-lite game Mini Motorways is definitely one to try. The premise is simple enough: Houses spawn in random spots, and you connect them with roads to shops of the same color using a limited number road tiles.Of course, things never stay too simple, and you'll soon have to manage traffic flows, roundabout/rotary intersections and freeways to juggle the ever-mounting chaos of criss-crossing vehicles.Terrain such as rivers and mountains also complicate things, with options to deal with them (such as bridges and tunnels) being in very limited supply, so you'll need to take care in optimizing your roads as much as possible while houses and shops continue to pop up all around. It ends up a little chaotic, but in a fun way.If you've played Mini Metro, Mini Motorways will be immediately familiar and comfortable. If not, it's a great place to jump in.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't about "beating" the different "levels".  It's about doing the best you can with what you're given.  It's almost roguelike.  It's about the highest score you can get.  I love this game and it's not even close to being on my top 10 list of best video games.  It's just...what it is.  It doesn't try to be anything other than simple and challenging.  Oh, and it has a dark mode, which I love.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: It's just not as fun I hoped it would be. As a fan of Mini Metro I thought this would be right up my ally. But I feel there are too many detractors that push it into the "don't recommend" category. Some of them are:I really wanted to like this game, but just couldn't. It felt like my decisions, effort and skill were only tangentially affecting the game's outcome, and so it all feels meaningless. I enjoy games where I feel good about being clever, or feel bad about being so stupid, and wanting to do better next time. Not games where I reach the failure condition and ask myself why it happened, not be sure how I could have done it better, and not really wanting to try again because even if I succeeded the game offers no real progression, so what's the point?

_childDocuments_.review: The game is only a high score game, with around 8 levels and that's it. -- That wouldn't be so terrible if it wasn't crazy buggy also. -- I've watched cars on an isolated road with no traffic just stop in the middle of the road -- for no reason -- no other roads intersected with it, nothing -- they just stopped and refused to drive to their destination, and lost because of this. -- So you can have a really good run that you've spent an hour on, trying to climb the leader boards, and the game just glitches out and you lose. -- It's super annoying and it really needs to have its bugs fixed, and for it to have more than 8 levels as well.  Possibly they should add additional goals like to progress the story or something. -- Also the game over screen is just dumb. -- "Your city had a single traffic jam so it was shut down after 92 days".  Like, really?  That's how traffic jams work? -- I had no idea! * eye roll *
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: One of the big problems with this game is skill, and thinking things through will only carry you so far. Luck will have to get you the rest of the way.Sometimes buildings spawn across a river, and the game refuses to give you a bridge, so you just automatically lose. Sometimes a building will spawn way off in a corner of the map, with the associated houses in the opposite, both out of the way of your current road network, so it's impossible to have enough tiles to hook them both up, so you just lose. Sometimes you'll build a side street to ease congestion, but the AI is just not smart enough to use it, despite it obviously being a shorter route for them, and they gridlock the rest of the system, so you just lose.It's a really fun concept that unfortunately isn't really fleshed out enough. Where's one way roads, or no left turns intersections? Why do highways only have one on, and one off ramp?tl;dr It's not as good as mini metro.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: Easy to learn, hard to master; a simple game that will entertain for hours as you perfect your strategies and amass higher scores, to only find that you will never get that god RNG you need to come close to first place on leader boards. _childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: I'll admit it! I'm addicted to this, and it's sibling Mini Metro. Highly recommended & a lot of fun. Game takes about 15 to 20 mins, I'm only starting so not that good yet, but the replay value & (more importantly) the compulsion to try and better your score keeps you coming back again, and again.  It's as relaxing as it is frustrating, which all adds up to a lot of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not normally a puzzle game kind of guy, but something about Mini Motorways really just sucks me in. The minimalistic art style and the mellow but surprisingly communicative soundscape are both calming and beautiful. This is good, because underneath its soothing exterior the game is a seething hate machine that will do its best to drive you mad.Would I recommend Mini Motorways? Absolutely! It's very enjoyable, and once you learn the basics it becomes an interesting puzzle that is very satisfying to watch unfold.You are presented with problems, offered limited time and tools to solve them, and then get to watch what you've built come to life and troubleshoot any inefficiencies. Sometimes you have to accept a less than optimal solution because of minimal resources or time demands. Sometimes you have to go back and restructure something you built poorly earlier that is now causing you trouble in a more mature city. Mini Motorways feels a lot like working through a coding/design project in some ways and will either teach you useful lessons in iterative design, or will harness your existing knowledge. My biggest complaint is probably the terminal nature of the difficulty. I'd love to be able to build larger cities before the demand outstrips realistic supply. Bigger or procedurally generated maps that allowed for a pseudo-endless mode would be a lot of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little game I would describe as a roguelite puzzle-strategy game where you must use roads, bridges and other features to connect coloured industries with their respectively coloured houses. Fun, challenging and stylish, although the game does feel a bit repetitive after a short while and it doesn't keep its wow effect as long as Mini Metro did, at least for me. Best advice I found for this game: - Keep colors as separated as you can, with each their own route when possible- Don't be afraid to place long winding roads, especially to keep colored routes separated- Don't connect all the houses; 4 for a developed industry is usually enough8/10 Good brain exercise

You have to know them and notice it quite fast so you can remedy it. 2 Examples would be when you place a stoplight immediately on the entrance of a shop can cause a deadlock, or rerouting a motorway can rarely disconnect all the houses to the destination despite it being connected.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game for $10. Chill builder. Game slowly ads the residential and commercial structures... and you have to build the roadways to get them there. Blue residents to blue commerce, yellow to yellow, etc..... Easy to grasp... not so easy to master. Glad I pulled the trigger. I am enjoying. Tho know there are no saves! _childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: Simple yet challenging puzzle involving the simple concept of getting vehicles to a destination and taking passengers back. However for all its simplicity the tension, pressure and challenge ramps up quickly as traffic becomes a nightmare over time. The base game progression is good and slowly introduces new elements to ramp up the challenges for the different cities from bridges, tunnels and highways and the additional challenges each give a new way and dimension to each game you play. Add on the weekly and daily challenges the game will have a surprising shelf life to keep it fresh. The span of time for each game is nice enough to not be overly long and short enough to do in between your free time, making it ideal when you burn out from other longer game campaigns and just want a break. Though you may be lulled to have that one more turn feeling now and then after completing a super satisfying run.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: [INTP review]THIS IS SO GOOD. I liked Mini Metro quite a bit, but Motorways is EVEN BETTER, for my brain at least. The increased creativity and freedom to problem solve, mixed with needing to account for the pathfinding of the cars multiplies the mental challenge, and therefor fun! Compared to Metro, I feel there is more terrain and environmental factors to factor in, and you're likely to be finding hidden depth for dozens and dozens of play-throughs on any individual level.If you're interested in a dynamic puzzle game with high re-playability and non-linear strategic thinking, get this now. It's even more fun when you try to beat your friend list's score! >:DDownsides are: Almost TOO addicting... I wish there more insight into car decision making... and it starts to feel a LIIIIIITTLE unfair w/ the amount of packages to pick up from small round buildings with TEENY TINY parking lots and only 1 entrance. But, the game has to end eventually and that's primarily an issue only with the end game when you're barely staving off death anyway, so it's likely intentional.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: So far this is a cautious recommend with a big disclaimer. This is based solely on how well Dinosaur Polo Club have previously supported Mini Metro with free updates.I wouldn't recommend the game in its current state but I would recommend it if you plan to revisit the game in a few months to a year's time. Maybe in two years there will be support for custom mods and Steam Workshop, something which definitely extended the shelf life of the previous game massively.If you're familiar with Mini Metro, you'll (almost) feel right at home. One of Mini Motorways' biggest problems is the lack of variety in its gameplay compared to its predecessor.A sequel like this needs to be far more than just a "barebones car-themed Mini Metro", which is what this game currently feels like.Upgrades definitely vary in terms of usefulness, with tunnels & bridges becoming mandatory to cross certain impassible terrain, highways becoming a damn near necessity, roundabouts being god-tier for controlling junctions and traffic lights just outright being garbage tier because you can't set their frequency nor sync them with other sets of lights.More balance and/or a better variety in terms of road upgrades (i.e. one-way streets, dual carriageways, better traffic light synchronisation, overpasses & underpasses) would improve the game a lot.Another way to spice up the gameplay is to do what Mini Metro did with stations. Have houses and buildings randomly change colour, representing either a resident's change in preferences or a change of building ownership.MM's biggest flaw comes in its (lack of) Endless Mode, which was a low-stress and more realistic gameplay option back in Mini Metro that didn't punish you with a game over if there's too much traffic, or if (in this game's case) the motorist AI bugs out and you end up with a mile long traffic jam where nobody can move anywhere resulting in a frustrating-as-hell game over.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very much one of those hit or miss games. That being said, I really like this game, and can recommend it to anyone who wants to give their brains a workout or just relax and have fun while eating some popcorn. _childDocuments_.review: Pros:++ Good graphics++ Good UI++ Good sound design++ Easy to pickup and play for kidsCons:-- Passive feel game play (Note: this is how the game is designed)-- Lacks depth and control; the game has potential to be more fun-- You may get bored after only a few hours of playing This is not a city building game. TLDR: Different color buildings pop up randomly on the map and they have to be connected with the same color houses so the cars from the houses get to the buildings before the buildings timer expires. You do not control where the houses or the buildings pop up. You only control how the roads are connected between them. The game is fun at first, but I started losing interest in it when I realized that all you're doing is just REACTING to where the building and houses spawn and how to connect them. Basically, you are constantly rebuilding the roadways, so it got old for me quick. However, this is the design of the game; to force you link houses and buildings together when they are not ideally placed on the map. I personally wanted a bit more ACTIVE control in the game, like a way to relocate houses or buildings or even zone places where only buildings or houses can appear as way to implement strategy.In the end, this game is challenging and well made, but it's very simple. Honestly, the game looks like it was focused for a smart phone or tablet touch screen due to the simplistic user interface and game play. If you want a game to keep you busy on a plane or keep a kid entertained for a few hours, than I would recommend it for that. If you are looking for a city simulation game, this is just a simple traffic simulator, not a building game.

If you love a puzzler that finds its stride in changing the small things while keeping its core components the same, this is your jam.

_childDocuments_.review: After less than 3 hours, I've unlocked and gotten 200-400 travelers on every available map. So, this game is a bit easier than Mini Metro and arguably short on content. On the other hand, I don't know if I've ever been sucked into Mini Metro for a two-and-a-half hour session, and I've got plenty of achievements left to get.
