I would appreciate shapes/numbers or something else that we can use to tell that houses and destinations belong together. Perhaps a hover that shows the color?
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: A good, chill game to pass your time that can get quite a bit hard later on. The art-style is very calming and pleasing to look at, and it also includes night mode! There are quite a lot of levels, each having their own theme and aesthetic to them and some even bring new obstacles and options to deal with said obstacles.The game is updated with weekly and daily challenges which keep the experience fresh even after you've finished it for good. The only gripe that I have with this game are the traffic lights, they're practically useless. Recent patches have tried fixing them, but compared to other options to deal with the traffic, I just didn't find much use for them. Still it's a pretty enjoyable game!
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun game. This is also an infuriating game. Right when you think youve got it all down and your metropolis is flowing harmoniously 5 stores will spawn at once on straight roads, intersections, and already developed store entrances. Houses will spawn across the entire map from the color store they are associated or in random spots along already established roads. This results in inevitable traffic pile up 30 to 45 minutes in the game. When I say inevitable I mean this happens 100 percent of the time. Unless you meticulously exploit the seemingly malicious spawn algorithm by wasting your few roads to block it precog style you will fail just when things are getting fun every time. The game should not force me to be wasteful simply to make it playable after an hour in one map. I understand that the goal is designed around score, but the fun for me isnt in the score its in the design, mechanics and the feasible if difficult challenge of developing a road network. The mechanisms in this game that force the game to come to a close, not as a result of the players choices or intellect, but as a result of the sheer and infeasible nature of an exponential ramping logistic strain make it more infuriating than it is fun to play. I may change my mind in future if some of the mobile focused design gets removed/more freedom in the game mode gets added but as of now I can not recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-Very addicting, intensely engaging, simple short and sweet, beautiful.-For anyone who likes management sims and also has a life.Cons:-The music is unbearable, the constant popping and low frequency humming is a violent assault on the ears. -A ENORMOUS AMOUNT OF RNG, every round lives and dies by RNG at the moment there is only so much the player can control and this saps a lot of the really fun puzzle and planning aspect out of the game. Improvements:-A custom mode where the player can go in and create their own maps, or custom build a ideal city.-roundabout's and traffic lights are entirely useless, and there is a very limited selection of construction devices.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: Is your ass puckered tight? Does stress induce massive amounts of dopamine into your system? Do you like to feel both upset and worthless whilst being robbed for all that you love?Welcome to Mini-Motorways.What you'll find in this game is a large rod firmly up your rear end whilst you try - in vain - to survive an onslaught of hungry citizens just trying to feed their children. You build their roads. The only issue? That ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ yellow house in your sea of red houses that wants to go to Narnia with their third son and his extended family on a Wednesday in the middle of rush hour.You might say: "What a fun challenge, there must be some satisfaction in this!"No. There is not. There is no homeowners' association. There is no God. And there is no way in hell that your colors will ever want to be in their own neighborhoods. No. They want to go to their yellow bank across the Pacific. Yesterday. And they didn't leave till this morning.No. They will absolutely put their only grocery store on the other-side of Mt. TooBigForYourTunnels for you to EVER connect properly.No. The intersections and turnabouts will absolutely not lower traffic density. In fact, they will increase it.Godspeed fellow infrastructure enthusiasts, because this is Portland on a Monday morning with I-5 under construction.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little game to kill some time. At first it seems basic and simple but as you get into it you gotta think. Where do i place this road, bridge, light, or even roundabout?! Great little time killer with high replayability. Your objective will stay the same, but how you will be able to do it will change. No two play-throughs will end out the same way.So yes, i would recommend this game to others!(I plan to also grab the other game "Mini Metro" and make a review on that so keep an eye out!)
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: Props:- Relaxing- can be easy and can be hard at the same time- Sounds effects are on point- Visually appealing Cons:- hard to master (can be good too)- They need to add custom map and more road type, car type, etc..- frustrating sometimes when a house pops in the middle of nowhere :(Overall: 8.5/10 A good relaxing strategy/casual game. Would recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: This game is AMAZING, and I know I say that for most of the games I reviewed but this one is so unique. The way that this game is made is so simple and yet so complex, and I love it! Every time you play it, it starts of as a chill game where you just connect the houses with the right buildings, but it ends with sheer panic of where am I gonna put this roundabout, where am I gonna put this bridge, how did that junction get clogged, WhY iS tHaT tImEr GoInG uP sO fAsT!?!?!?!? And in that moment it ends, as you start to calm down you get to see the beautiful mess of roads you made trough all that carnage that was going around you. There are different city's you can unlock and play and there are more to come as well, there are also daily and weekly challenges you can play, in witch you get unlimited of something you can always use or that some buildings always spawn as the level 2, or both at the same time, so its really interesting trying out new ones every day and week. The game is cheap and a LOT OF FUN so you should check it out, the people that made Mini Motorways also have a different game on a similar style, its a bit older then this one and its called Mini Metro. You do the same thing in Mini Metro as in Mini Motorways just with passengers and trains, and at the end of a run it actually looks like real metro map, I still haven't played it but would like to since it seems like a bunch of fun too. Anyways, love the game, the style, the concept, everything 10/10!If anyone read all of this, I am so sorry, and also congratulations you have made it to the end, I just go on a ranting spree when writing these, but that is because the games I review are SO GOOD!

_childDocuments_.review: Night mode and colorblind mode!  It's great to see a developer adding options for people with eyes that don't work quite right.  Gameplay is simple but complex. _childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: I saw this game only a couple weeks ago and knew I would like it.  It looks simple at first glance but once you start to play you slowly start to realize that it is deceptively difficult to say the least. All I have to do is connect roads on this tiny little grid, pshh, piece of cake....and 10 minutes later OMG WTF STOP HONKING I DON'T HAVE ANY ROAD TILES OR ROUNDABOUTS AND IT IS ONLY FRIDAY, SUNDAY IS A LONG WAY AWAY!The levels all start off very small (I think I counted it to be ~8x12 on most levels.  But as you go, it very slyly zooms you out a little bit and the next thing you know it's 30x40 and we are in the above "Friday" situation all over again.  The game also requires the player to be very proactive or extremely forward thinking with how they want to plan the city.  Although trying to plan the city far in advance seems to come back to bite you as the spawns for pins and houses can be pretty awful sometimes.  It seems best to have a plan but not be too rigorous.  If it works, great, if not, just try and keep a general idea of how you want things to go from there on.About being proactive, you absolutely need to find traffic jams/pinch points long before they become a hindrance to traffic and if you are at ~200 pins and a shop gets a timer, you are done.  There is almost no way to fix this unless you have a highway that you can connect a subdivision of the color needed right to the timer.  But if you had a free Highway, you should have never gotten the timer in the first place.Overall an extremely fun game and a great deal for the price.  It reminds me of the physical game Rush Hour but much more complex and instead of trying to unblock a single car you have to deal with unblocking a whole city that you designed to be this way.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: This review is specially made for those who like to get all the achievements in games.Gameplay spoilers ahead.Mini Motorways is a sequel to mini metro and also a minimalist 2D puzzle game where you need to create an effective road network connecting homes to buildings of the same color using roads in the path and shape of your choosing but also bridges, tunnels and motorways (shortcut roads that go over everything) to reach areas that otherwise would be inaccessible. There’s also some resources that can be used to manage the traffic better like roundabouts and traffic lights.When compared to its predecessor, the gameplay is more complex and satisfying: the design and shape of the roads matter a lot and there is no way to quick-fix mistakes you made because you have to wait for the cars to get back home to get the resources you spent. On the other hand, RNG can screw your planning, specially if you don’t take precautions.There are several different cities and maps available and a classic and expert mode, but also a challenge mode that offers new ways of playing those maps by adding game modifiers that either restrict the use of certain resources or make them infinite. These modifiers are also present in the week and daily challengesAs mentioned, the graphics and interface look minimalist like mini metro, but now we have more complex designs for the houses and buildings, instead of just a simple geometric shape. There are also 3 different graphic options for each city: white, dark and colored backgrounds, and personally I prefer the colored ones.The sound effects still work well but for some reason the ambient music in some cities is very annoying, specially when the game is paused, and the sounds keep looping resembling a broken refrigerator. My suggestion is going to options and reducing the sound to the sound cues you get when a new building or house pops up or the timer starts ticking. As mentioned the gameplay is more complex and road design matters a lot. There are some basic tips you need to follow to be able to reach the 2000 score needed for the hardest achievements, here are a few: SPOILERS.  115 Achievements. Took me around +40 hours, without quitting maps when I got the achievements and playing each map to the highest score I could reach. I remember getting 4000 and a daily challenge and above 2000 on an expert map. Medium, but depends on the mode and city you’re playing. Getting 2000 trips or better requires luck and skill. Medium to hard. The game felt easier than Mini metro, while getting a 2000 score requires an effective road system, you don’t have to worry about the constraints Mini Metro had. Some challenge maps are also easier than the classic mode on some cities. I got the other lower score achievements on the first try, even on expert mode. There are also some grindy achievements that will be partially completed by playing normally, like using 100 lights, 100 roundabouts, etc.. that can be completed in a challenge map where that resource is infinite and using a lot of them there. Note: Tunnels only seem to be counted when the game ends and if they have an entrance and exit, making small round tunnels seemed to work when I wanted to get the few I was missing.    It’s a great sequel and a better 2D puzzle game than mini metro, offering more gameplay options with its new modifiers. The maps look a bit better and the destinations are no longer just a geometric shape. Requires some luck, and good planning and road design to reach the 2000 scores needed to 100% the game, so you’ll need some patience and practice.

_childDocuments_.review: Mini Motorways is a colorful and wonderfully engaging game! It seems simple (connect your houses to the storefronts and have the cars pick up the pins) but it becomes much more complicated than that as your game progresses! You must find ways to manage the traffic that arises from the network you create. However, spawn locations of buildings is random, as are the upgrades you receive each week. Road tiles quickly become limited, and the puzzle element really comes into play when trying to figure out how to best use the space in front of you. While this game can be stressful at times, I would say the overall experience is fairly casual. There are multiple speeds at which you can play, and you can pause freely to evaluate your situation (or walk away for a little while). Definitely recommended! Good luck with your road designing endeavors!

I'm not sure it should be easier, but I would love some more visual feedback about how long it's going to take for everyone using it to be done, so that I can guess if it's worth trying- Roundabout placement is a bit fiddly, especially with regards to already existing roads in the vicinity- Traffic lights seem to be basically useless at the moment (especially on T junctions), and that's a shameAlso, I would like a few small additional features (like a bulldozer upgrade that allows you to delete a single house?) to create a bit more variety, even though the weekly challenges already help a lot :)Everything considered, very well worth buying at it's current price!

_childDocuments_.review: ok, i write a positive review.originally i wrote a negative review, then removed it, now this. i'll explain.my original negative review was about the fact the devs announce this game as "a strategy simulation game about designing the road map for a growing city" io "to create a bustling metropolis", which is bollocks !this game has nothing to do with any kind of a simulation or city builder or traffic manager. i must know since i play such games since over two decades. that description is only about the game's skin, not its gameplay. but maybe the devs don't even know what they made, would be not the first humans not realising the treasure they created.but the claim, this to be a strategic game is absolutely correct. it is an abstract strategy game, similar to such classics as chess, though more dynamic & the opponent is the devs' AI. so if the devs want to expand on the basic idea, a multiplayer would be possible, where one player has the position of connecting supply with demand while the other tries to make such connections impossible.but back to the review.i removed the originally negative review cause the game offers a strong enough strategy content to keep me interested now for over 350 hours, despite some quite glaring gameplay solutions not far from being just bugs (roundabout/motorway scrapping delay) & rather questionable music & sound choices. it's a pity the devs don't let the game just shine as an abstract strategy game, cause the need for the ability to think properly was never more needed than nowadays.& that's also why i decided now to write a positive review. the game can serve as a quite interesting tool for complex thinking, reasoning & cognition beyond just the game itself.so, buy the game if you want a tool for thinking, especially under pressure. the pressure being not really time, since the game has a pause button, but the pressure of space, AI hostility, opposing goals, limiting conditions, your impatience, outright panic & just your stubborn lack of attention to detail.in short features description : the game has so far a handful of predetermined maps, no randomly generated maps, weekly & daily challenges with randomly changing limiting conditions & the newest feature, few additional challenges with (again) limiting conditions for every of the present maps.would the devs finally drop that "simulation city builder traffic manager" nonsense i would highly recommend the game, with it it's - buy at your own discretion.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly it's just not fun. Starting off the first couple of minutes are nice, but it ramps up insanely fast. And relies not only on having good skill but also incredible luck to get a good score.Especially when it comes to blocking. Part of the fun of this game is the fact that malls and houses spawn (somewhat) randomly. But the first step to ensuring you get a good score is to use extra roads to block off sections of the map to prevent that. Even after that there's a lot of strategy involved in exactly how you structure your intersections, because that surprisingly makes a HUGE difference in how fast traffic moves.And then, even if you are an absolute master, a huge part of it is just down to luck. Have a mall spawn in a bad location? Might as well restart, you aren't gonna get a high score. And for the upgrades? Only thing worth using is motorways. Traffic lights and roundabouts are both worse than just using a normal intersection. So if you don't get a few motorways early on then, again, might as well restart.And if you do master it and get incredibly lucky with the spawns? Well, after a certain point it just becomes a waiting game. Once the map is full and traffic is stable, nothing happens. You can let it run until you get bored and rack up an immense high score. Short of running into a traffic bug or hitting the cap of 400 weeks nothing will ever end your run.It could work as a casual city-builder, but it's got far too much of a strategy/puzzle element to it. And it could work as a strategy/puzzle game, but the sheer amount of luck necessary to get a whole map with nothing spawning in a bad location and no useless road upgrades is insane (and no amount of skill will make up for it). It tries to be both and fails miserably at being either.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is fun, relaxing, and beautiful. Would definitely recommend.Some annoyances:- When things start to go south, there's not nearly enough time to actually do much about it, and the game doesn't have enough feedback before things go wrong. It's often quite tricky to tell what exactly the issue is.- Rebuilding roads and motorways can be quite annoying, because you have to wait until the previous cars on the road are all done. When you build a motorway and immediately want move it, you still have to wait (even when paused) sometimes. I suppose this is to prevent exploiting the roads available, but I think the frustration of having to wait for roads to become available is much worse.- Roundabouts can be very tricky to place sometimes, since they require a lot of space, making their usefulness more limited.- Stop lights aren't particularly useful, almost to the point where I basically never use them. Either that, or their effect is far too subtle. It's also not very well explained in the tutorial.- The game tries a bit too hard to deliberately throw you off balance, with some building placements being ridiculously far out of reach. I think this detracts from the enjoyment of the game a bit. It's fine to add some challenge here and there, but I think at the moment it's a bit too aggressive. This is especially annoying when you don't have the bridges or motorways available to connect the buildings, which mostly just means I have to wait til Sunday.- AI could be a little more sophisticated. Right now they seem to just take the shortest path possible, I wish they had some way of also finding less congested paths for their destination, so side roads could be used to alleviate traffic.That's just some feedback. Overall I think the game is great and comes highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: This is a lot of fun. The game mechanics are very easy to learn but there are a lot of intricacies built into the game. My only criticism is there should be some in-game tutorial and/or mechanic that teaches you how traffic lights, round-abouts and other upgrades work. They're not as intuitive as one might expect them to be.A worthy sequel to Mini Metro. Highly recommended!BONUS: There are no micro-transactions or non-fungible tokens (NFTs) in this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: It's good clean fun, much like Mini Metro. I wish there was a way to define traffic rules for the cars to follow, though, because often you fall victim to cars just being too dumb. And although I like the game overall, I do feel a bit dirty building streets for cars, compared to building public transport...
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 27.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ing minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: It's an abstract puzzle game with the illusion of constructive play and the illusion of a road builder. Pretty looking but pretty shallow.It entertains for just enough hours beyond the refund window to justify its cheap price after which you quickly realise its shortcomings. Those being aggressively bad AI building placement and a poorly modelled set of tools to deal with it.For the hours I got out of it about 75% of those hours were spent trying to overcome the frustrating game design by painting in spare road to block bad building placement. After that it's deeply into annoying anti-game territory which I did not find fun, becoming adversarial rather than constructive play.Perhaps with extra game modes it will improve (I saw the recent update news, that's why updating my review) and if it doesn't improve I got just about my money's worth in entertainment. Hardly an endorsement.I wouldn't buy another Dino PC Mini game based on this experience and I cannot recommend it. It's fun while the fun lasts but that fun dries up far too quickly.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: I refunded it. It feels like a 100% RNG based game, set around making the RNG as aggravating as humanly possible. And the only skill that could be ever found in it is based around learning the games BS and working around it's illogical RNG and trying to manage and manipulate that. Which is trying to be aggravating. It's like taking all the fun out of a city sim game. By boiling it down to nothing. And making it even more of a pain in the ass. Not for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game in its current state. The game has excellent audio-visual design, and it is satisfying and tactile to play. However, there are some fatal flaws in its design that render it a chore to play. The way to win in this game is so counter-intuitive and unsatisfying that it ruins the gameplay. The ideal way to play is to segregate your roads by the colour of buildings - that means NO intersections or roundabouts whatsoever, just segregated roads that are not at all connected. Any actual road network will slow traffic to the point that it's difficult to get over 1000 points. You can also cheese the game by laying down unused road in empty space, preventing the game from spawning new buildings. Doing this, the game is essentially over, and you can rack up points without doing anything, rendering the leaderboards and scoring system useless. Everything else in the game is great, it's just a shame that the mechanics discourage actually building a road network. It's a puzzle where the solution is extremely unsatisfying, rewarding cheap and cheesy play over ingenuity and smart planning. I would recommend if you don't care about the scoring system or the traffic ruining your city, and are in the mood for a chill road simulator.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: This game is quite relaxing for a little while until it gets to the 'stressful' stage when you really need to think. Its a good game, I recommend it, but the price could be lowered, maybe something in the range of 7-10 dollars but other than that, well done, this game has given me quite a lot of joy.Kind regards - fexfox63
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: Although I'm recommending this game, there are a number of important caveats to know. First of all, houses can spawn randomly. So you could have a highway going and all of a sudden traffic backs up because a house spawn in the middle. The later you go, the more you will encounter this issue. Second, you can not adjust the entrance of the business. This means sometimes you will have the most ridiculously windy road going around the place just to reach the entrance. Lastly, roads can not stack and every intersection is a ridiculous mess given the lack of basic traffic management tools such as one way streets and stop signs (i.e. prioritization).Everything above means that there is a difficulty cliff around 1250 points that hits very hard. Not too much you can do at a certain point since the map is just too filled up.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked mini metro, buy this gameIf you didn't like mini metro, I don't want to be friends with you, but buy this game anywayIf you never played mini metro, buy this and that in the bundle togetherIf you have never heard of mini metro or mini motorways, imagine halfway between factorio and cities:skylines, and then once you're done imagining, still buy them both
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun however its more luck than anything getting past a few thousand points seeing as once you have a high volume of traffic its effectively impossible to remove the roads before a shop overloads. I enjoy seeing where I place on the leader boards however most of the scores on there are hacked. A bunch of people with 2,000,000+ score. Its fun to pass some time. The art and sound style is cool. Try it out if you don't like it you can always return it.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: Mini Motorways seems to be a simple game when you start playing it but then learn over a few hours that there is so much more going on underneath the surface that makes you want to keep coming back for more. I have put almost 25 hours into this game so far and I am not bored of it yet. Over many plays, you learn strategies that will help you get more and more points and keep trying to up your previous best and work your way up the leader board that it becomes addictive. The daily challenges are hard and only having one chance to get the best score makes it a little more stressful than the regular levels. There is also a weekly challenge that allows for multiple attempts to try to get the highest score possible as well. Both of these challenges have a couple of new rules added to them that changes the gameplay. Such as, not being able to remove trees or not having bridges to go over water. Each rule changes the base game in a way that makes you have to think of a new way to solve that problem.I really enjoy this game and anyone who likes puzzle games or enjoyed Mini Metro would like this game as well. It is so different from Mini Metro but has almost the same feel to it since you are transporting people from one location to another.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little simple puzzle game.I wish there was a mode where the mechanics allowed you to place the buildings or houses instead of being rando-placed on the map.The difficulty is not how well you design your city, because when you start nearing 4 digit trips the speed of the buildings generating supply is ridiculously fast and literally impossible to keep up.  Even more strange is cars start grid locking for no reason I can tell where they will not move out of the buildings causing weird backups.  Not a fan of that (disguising difficulty with faster timers), but regardless its still fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I haven't had a game make me focused and engaged with one thing for so long in such a long time. It's so "simple" yet super entertaining. Red houses have red cars that drive to red....supermarkets and blue houses have blue cars that drive to blue...???supermarkets???Still haven't figured out why I once saw a red car leaving a yellow house...very suspicious I gotta say.Anyways if you are young minded enough to get excited over coloured houses and cars driving about this is a game for you. But watch out there might be random supermarkets spawning somewhere on the map at any point in the game and if you miss them it's basically game over :)

_childDocuments_.review: Super relaxing and quite a simple, beautiful game, I think the highest score I've gotten so far is 2,300, it does not lack on the difficulty factor.The only thing that slightly bugs me is that it seems that all the cars take the optimal route to their location, and while this is sufficient for most situations, when traffic gets extremely clogged, it would be a blessing to be able to redirect some of that into back roads, though I can understand the difficult of adding a feature like this without making it much more complex

_childDocuments_.review: Mid tbh. Car AI noticeably stupid. The organic music walks over the line into creepy instead of cute. The challenges boil down to a handful of mutators; "no bridges", "random upgrades", etc. with no unique conceits - they feel tacked on. Destination placement on a fraction of maps is out of tune, upping the challenge arbitrarily; not insurmountable, but the tactics required are sweaty and unseemly with the zen aesthetic.The biggest flaw is in the core gameplay: since cars/destinations are permanently color-coded you're incentivized to  colors into their own loops. It's inauthentic to the core theme. Instead of a traffic network connecting the whole city, you're better off jumping through hoops to guarantee isolation.Mini Motorways takes after its predecessor Mini Metro with perfect visuals, but the similarities end there. Metro had a better name, its organic music didn't enter the uncanny valley, there weren't trap upgrades(roundabout), connecting far-flung destinations was integral, and its challenges were unique & actually . I was really wanting another Mini Metro, but this ain't it.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played more hours of this game than I'd like to admit. It's so simple, yet addictive. _childDocuments_.review: I loved Mini Metro. Mini Metro provided ways recover from pretty bad situations, and to learn from them, even in the same session. The end of the game was fun, triaging, micromanaging, replanning, moving a train to an overflowing platform, moving carriages around, etc..Mini Motorways is not like that. Things start painfully slow, then there is a plateau, then everything goes south, and there is usually no way to recover. Or maybe I just haven't figured out the game yet. Mini Metro was a relaxing experience, and the endgame was fun.I can't say the same about Mini Motorways. I usually just end up feeling frustrated.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE:I can't recommend this game anymore. Every time I play it, it gets more annoying. Please do check the other negative reviews to see all the questionable design decisions this game has.ORIGINAL REVIEW:Visually, it's much more better than Mini Metro. The art is more detailed, it's got shadows... In that aspect, the game is quite cool, while still keeping the same minimalistic and flat design.This time the game gives you a lot more freedom to place wherever you want (because, of course, they're roads), and the gameplays itself feels much more dynamic than Mini Metro.As for the performance, it runs  in my 2015 MacBook Pro at 2560x1440, with an approximate average of 40 fps during a game, but in my two-year old PC with GTX 1650 at 1080p works like a charm, being pretty stable at 144 fps.The only bad thing about this game that I found pretty annoying, is the controls. They're not awesome. Do not expect, for example, to quickly drag a traffic light into a road, because if your mouse was 1px away from the traffic light icon, you'll be placing roads instead. In this area, they defintely haven't improved. I've got Mini Metro in my Nintendo Switch and the controls were also quite annoying.There are things like these that kind of ruin the fun of the game sometimes, but it's just for a brief moment. The game is definitely worth the 8,19€ (although it was a gift from a friend).

_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: This is actually a more compelling city building concept than more complicated games. Basically by placing roads/bridges/tunnels with traffic lights/circles you have to compete against computer, which is randomly placing more homes and workplaces on geographic locations on the map. Eventually, a workplace will get filled up due to a traffic jam somewhere. Due to the ambiance and simplicity of the game, it is a meditative experience.. as the traffic increases attention is required. Thanks to the simplicity, it also doesn't feel like a big mental investment in the cities that are built, as you start over more frequently. Yet it retains replay-ability and infinite puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely delightful! _childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: Get your thinking hat on, as it's about to get jam packed! TBH this game is a tad mind numbing when you're trying to find the best route, but it is actually fairly pleasant when you finally figure out the gist of the games' tactics. I'd certainly recommend having a motorway handy for the sneaky cross city placements of the buildings, and often roundabouts are good to create a block of free space where your joining roads have become congested. I'm yet to fully figure out the tips and tricks to Mini Motorways, but again.. it's been a pleasant mind puzzling game.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: Mini Motorways is a brilliant little game, although I've only sunk 4h00 playtime it's enough for me to see how strategic yet simple this game is. You start with a couple of houses and one commercial building that you'll need to connect via roads, motorways, bridges and tunnels with the help of traffic lights and roundabouts. Gradually the camera pans out to expand the map and in turn more houses and commercial buildings spawn and before you know it you have a sprawling city with traffic building and horns beeping, but keep an eye on those pins! This is for sure a game where you can  - so vote! (My nomination for the 2021 Steam Awards)

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little strategy game, were you have to manage the traffic of a growing city. The ramp up of each level is a blast, as it goes from nice and relaxing to ohh ^%& "why did that building pop up there, let me redesign my perfect road system." _childDocuments_.review: Decent game, but not as great as the rating implies.As a kind-of-a-sequel to Mini Metro, it is, effectively, a step down in several aspects.First, the decision to bring in a grid seems to have been wrong. The spatial positioning aspect haven't added that much, but its limitations are stifling: it means that, as the game field is being filled, you have less and less room to rebuild. By midgame your road configuration is mostly set in stone, and you just don't have much to do, just add stuff and wait for the end.Second, game dynamics seem to have been mishandled. Sure, train teleporting & 'ghostlining' in Mini Metro was, in a way, wrong, but getting rid of effectively everything you could do on the fly (yes, you can maneuver with a spare motorway, but it's painfully slow: it's like a Mini Metro line wouldn't become available upon its cancellation immediately, but rather would be locked till the train returns to the original station) doesn't seem to be right either. Third, crossroads outright don't work (even with roundabouts or traffic lights they clog up traffic horribly). Basically, you want your roads not to cross, ever. Good scores are attained when RNG allows you to get close to using separate (insert your favorite joke about segregation here) access roads for every destination, otherwise, your run is botched. This seems to be the reason why the game just doesn't feel like a real city.Fourth, reward balance is just horrible. Basically, you want as many motorways as possible, their number is probably the most important factor in your score. Tunnels are a second priority (rarely, you could even want a tunnel over a motorway), bridges are a third (same for bridge vs. tunnel). Traffic lights, though, are weak (they sometimes allow you to somewhat unscrew your traffic when RNG forces you to cross your roads), and roundabouts seem to be hardly ever needed (strictly never after the midgame).Fifth, the game is extremely random-dependent. Badly positioned destinations? Restart, later spawns will just make the situation worse. Not enough motorways? Restart, your transport capacity is crippled. The result of it is that I played Munich map something like ten times in a row, never passing 2k score mark, then suddenly attained top-200 (out of hundreds of thousands of players), changing literally nothing about my playstyle. Most of the time spent on that amounted to just waiting.All of this doesn't mean that Mini Motorways is bad or anything. When approached as an abstract puzzle, it's mostly fun, it's just not as awesome, consistent or replayable as Mini Metro was.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a perfect arcade puzzler for when you have 10-30 minutes to listen to a podcast. Mini-Motorways is nearly perfect for what it is. Shops spawn and house pawn. You link them together with roads. The longer the game goes on, the more colors spawn. More colors means more competing traffic. You use special road units on a tight unlock schedule to manage intense traffic jams. And that's all there is to it. There's no fluff here. No story, no objectives, no bonus goals. You connect yellow house to yellow store and see how many cars you can get to yellow store before a traffic jam shuts down the city. That's it. The art style is minimal and the colors make it easy to keep track of everything going on. The sound track is dynamic and changes based on what you're seeing on screen. It just works. And it's really fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Mini Metro is one of my favorite games of all time design-wise, so I was quite excited to see another entry in the series, particularly one with similarly warm reviews. I have 112 hours in that, have 100%'d the game through its repeated updates, and I'm in the top few percent of the leaderboard for every map, including a few top-500 and top-1000 positions. I did this all without needing more than a passing glance at guides and other people's strategies and recommendations, as I found that the vast majority of the game's intricacies can be easily understood just by observing and thinking through the effects of various gameplay decisions that you have available.Unfortunately, in its current state, I've found that in Mini Motorways there are more things I find frustrating than ones which I find fun. Whereas Mini Metro scores top marks for elegant and intuitive gameplay, I really feel that Mini Motorways falls quite short of that. The very action of the transportation itself feels so much less elegant across the board, from how cars are shown to arrive and then immediately leave, to how roads are drawn a bit weirdly when in more complex orientations, to punishingly high variance in RNG, and because of its minimalist presentation it's often difficult to tell at a glance where a car is going (in a crowded network) unless you follow it along the entire way. It just feels so messy compared to Mini Metro, where things are fairly clear and the player remains in control of outcomes even when gameplay gets hectic.The effect and thresholds for specific road angles affecting speed has often felt unclear without checking (and also follows nothing close to real-world physics, with cars able to navigate near-hairpin turns at speed(!)). Despite there being only eight possible directions that a road can be built, the way which a road is drawn makes the direction at times ambiguous at a glance, requiring double-checking against the layout grid (which is not shown by default, and cannot be enabled to be always-shown).Motorways (elevated high speed road bridges)  vision below them, which is needlessly frustrating if they block off line of sight to important parts of your network. You can adjust how an individual motorway is positioned, but doing so will have a gameplay impact and so you may have to trade a bit of travel speed for visibility. Not being able to e.g. hover over to see underneath (with partial transparency applied to the motorway) is mind boggling to me, and seems like such an enormous oversight for usability. With only three hours I've already had multiple times where a motorway blocked vision of key areas, making it needlessly difficult to connect roads, check pin counts (travel demand indicators), and monitor local traffic underneath those areas. [while writing this review I leafed through some of the game's recent patches and noticed that a July 8, 2022 patch makes motorways transparent while the game is paused, which does help for some of these issues.]While I'm totally okay with there being a degree of randomisation in where things spawn, the variance between good and bad spawns here feels comparatively enormous. The "destination" blocks are prefab, and have preset entry/exit paths for cars which you can't adjust. This means that if you get a destination that spawns with an entrance/exit up against an existing high-traffic area, your run might be screwed as good traffic management may simply not be possible for that location. If an entry/exit spawns on the opposite side of where you need it to be, you'll have to pay a large travel time penalty for possibly the rest of the game, i.e., you may also screwed. If you get a spawn that doesn't have enough space to optimise, you might be screwed. And this didn't just feel like a late-game issue, it felt like an all-game issue but one where the extent of the the effects are most obvious in the late game - but which are silently congesting your road network the entire time.Traffic lights are only a step or two above useless for manyjunction types (although based on what I've read, this is a side effect of some of the patches), and so are something of a choice-trap for the player.Placing roundabouts requires large areas to be free of buildings and other blocking elements due to their size, but random building spawns mean you'll more often than not be lacking enough free space where and when you need roundabouts to be placed. It's difficult to get ahead of it by simply pre-placing roundabouts before they're needed because of the aforementioned random spawns - as often as not you'll end up with a wasted roundabout if you try to place it before the area around it has developed enough to really need it.To mitigate or avoid some of the above random-spawn-issues, Mini Motorways unfortunately currently has a gameplay incentive that I would describe as "perverse". Because buildings can't spawn on road, you can block off large sections of the map to heavily manipulate the randomised spawns by just sticking down huge amounts of dead-end, useless road. You block off areas around key junctions to keep them free for future roundabouts. You block off entire islands if you don't like where they are and don't want to allocate bridges to servicing them. You block off outlying areas that would have higher than average travel time. Yes, you absolutely  opt to not do this as the player, but then you just go back to getting remarkably screwed by bad rng with a frequency which I think is simply too high. I find it to be a very dumb and tedious mechanic, so it's frustrating that it's a meta one.In a way it feels unfair of me to give this a thumbs down, as Mini Motorways is probably overall still something like a 6/10 or 7/10 game for me, which isn't normally enough to warrant a long whiny review full of almost nothing but complaints. It's just that in my experience it compares surprisingly unfavorably to Mini Metro despite fulfilling a similar gameplay niche such that I find it very difficult to recommend it instead of just hopping back on Mini Metro instead. The comparative novelty found in Mini Motorway's gameplay as a veteran Mini Metro player has in no way made up for what I perceive to be significant and ongoing flaws in its core gameplay experience.As of writing this review, Mini Motorways sits at 96% positive reviews, so evidently I'm in a slim minority holding a very unpopular opinion, but nonetheless I haven't really enjoyed the game in its current state. I'm cautiously hopeful that continued patching will resolve or mitigate enough of my complaints to placate me, and I'll be sure to revisit this game further later down the line to see how it's going.

natural difficulty (although that's a factor) but because it's absolutely nothing like how actual city traffic worksthe game is pretty fun for most of the time but personally i can't really get higher than 600ish trips before it turns into a gnarled ugly mess and is no longer humanly reasonable to re-organize, satisfying to look at, OR even really that possible to fix beyond just pausing the game and re-routing roads for 20 minutes. the portion of the game leading up to that is relaxing and nice to look at, but i wish the game had a better focus on relaxing/satisfying gamemodes/difficulties rather than its almost exclusive focus on high scoring and hyper-optimal routing. the visuals and sound design are very finely tuned and make the game (mostly) relaxing and nice to look at, though once the inevitable frustration with the difficulty sets in no amount of dynamic synth music and limited color palette can make it relaxing anymore. if you're a puzzle fiend itching for perfect scorerunning, this game will do that for you, but if you want a relaxing city planning sim you should look toward something more broad like cities: skylines.

_childDocuments_.review: A very relaxing and fun game. Easy to learn, with lots of room to master.This is a little more approachable than Mini Metro, which is nice. Level management can get complex, but I'd say it's never overwhelming until much later in a level. The art direction is clean and nice on the eyes, but not so simple that you miss crucial details. There's multiple levels with different gameplay mechanics (for example, in some you'll use tunnels to go through mountains, whereas others you'll need lots of bridges) and unique designs specific to that city. Also, I'm really thankful for the night mode. Only con I can find so far is that when multiple timers start to fill up quickly, it doesn't feel like you're given enough time to sort out issues and get your little city back on track. A loss happens suddenly and without any way to fix it. With practice and better planning I'm sure I'll run into this issue less.  Overall, a very fun and surprisingly deep and addicting game. Highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is simple and addicting. It builds on the successful formula started with Mini Metro and brings the already high production values and design to new levels. Although it's literally the same basic thing every time, it's quite replayable. I find that just getting a few more passengers to their destinations before ultimately failing is incentive enough to play just one more game. I wasn't sure how well a game that's so suited to mobile would translate to PC, but I have an Android phone, so this was my only option for getting this game. Fortunately, it hasn't let me down, and in fact, I don't imagine I would prefer playing this on mobile since it works so perfectly with mouse. If you want a sort of meditative but hectic experience, this might be the right game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve loved Mini Metro forever. When Mini Motorways came out, I had feared it would be more of the same of Mini Metro. Yes and no. It has the same great music, UI, and minimalist of Mini Metro, it has the same week to week flow with decisions between weeks, and it has the same agonizing end of each map in the failure to meet the demands of a unceasingly growing population where your overall score is the amount of successful trips, travelers reaching their destination.Where this differs from Mini Metro is in the way you organize the flow of the population from point to point. Mini Motorways connects the homes of a subsets] of a population (each represented by different colors, say purple) with a public destination. Destination of a specific color require a car to come to it from a home to satisfy its demand. Failure to satisfy demand from destinations ultimately ends the map, unlike Mini Metro where maps end when travelers fail to reach their destination. Optimizations of roads, roundabouts, and motorways between minimal colors, connecting only those houses to satisfy demand, is what helps achieve the most successful trips before the games end.The game is super cozy and I feel like I’m often in a zen-like state where my mind stops thinking and instead focuses on optimizing roads, bridges, and tunnels. There’s a few different levels of mastery as you move from unlocking maps, unlocking expert mode, and then understanding how to achieve even higher scores. There’s some great guides out there so I won’t waste time detailing it here. Have fun!

_childDocuments_.review: At first it seams like the challenge is managing traffic to and from the destination, and that’s fun as the city expands. However, you realize that the shops demand for trips exceeds the amount of traffic that can physically get in and out of one shop. That means no matter how hard you try, you cannot satisfy demand in a REALISTIC game. This goal that grows beyond your capacity to satisfy it; naturally caps the game around a few thousand points, max. You don’t get to keep expanding your city in an ever-complex management structure, your city never grows beyond the size of an I-pad screen. This can be proved by looking at high score city structures, unrealistic matches where users blocked off the entire map so only one color will spawn, they funnel all traffic to one store, and even then, the supply of 15 houses funneled directly into a store in perfect optimization, can barely satisfy the demand of one store. Once this delicate balance is achieved, they let their computer run for weeks racking up points.  The magic of this came melted away when I realized high scores are irrelevant and getting beyond this artificial limit requires you to break the game. Its not an ever-increasing puzzle, it is just 30-min challenges to see if you can get TO the artificial limit. Knowing this, there is no point in going beyond the first few levels.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is too RNG dependent. You would think it is like Mini Metro but with streets and cars. But in this game you build the streets on actual tiles that can spawn houses and hubs (like train stations in Mini Metro). In the end if RNG is not on your side the houses spawn on such far away and isolated places that it is almost impossible to repair your traffic without scrapping all your streets. And this is another minus point for me. It takes AGES to register you just scrapped a street. In late game when you see you have to deroute your traffic in a different way or shape it is almost game over because:1. you dont get your "materials" back (you can't use unlimited streets like train tracks in Mini Metro, they cost actual ressource points) and;2. because the AI is stubborn and not very smart you watch cars go by instead going to the most vulnerable point of interest and so you hope it fixes itself. (which it won't).I am sure with strategy and knowledge all those problems are somewhat more managable but feels too random and cumbersome and not very fun. It doesn't feel right to "meta" the game and block critical spawn points with streets just so you won't get the bad side of RNG. In Mini Metro all those things didn't exist and for me - it doesn't feel good and evolving from Mini Metro. Not every game does have to follow the same formula but the new features and tools don't work well in this one. Plus the tools like roundabouts and traffic lights feel kinda pointless and not really helpful. I am sure they can work and help you but if they do (the game somehow forgets to really explain the benefits of either of the tools) I wouldn't know how to use them to their full potential because traffic AI is terrible and traffic lights and roundabouts in places where they would make sense in real life don't make sense here.I will play all courses so I see all the content there is but it didn't scratch the same itch like Mini Metro and I highly doubt I will come back the same amount of time like I did with Mini Metro.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm very glad I stumbled upon this game today. It's so relaxing, but still really challenging. This is the perfect puzzle game for those lazy Saturdays where you're not in the mood for a grand adventure, but still want the satisfaction of building something creative. I love the art style of the game. The simple design makes even the busiest maps easy to manage, but not so simple that it's a bore to look at.I've not played mini metro yet, so I can't say how this compares. Mechanic-wise this game reminds me a bit of ISLANDERS -- reach a milestone (in this case time survived) and get a new set of items to place. As someone else pointed out, it does feel a little bit like a mini-game version of City Skylines road building. The biggest difference here is that the buildings and houses pop up randomly so you only have control over the roads. This  provides a fun challenge with just the right amount of frustration when that green house pops up RIGHT where you were planning a road!Overall, I'd say the game is worth full price. It's not a giant game with tons of different stuff to do, but I expect to get many many hours of fun out of this game. Each map brings a new challenge and the placement randomness keeps each map from feeling stale. My 4 hour playtime so far is 90% the first map -- I'm having loads of fun just trying to beat my current score.If I had any complaints, it's these three things:1. There's no way to prioritize traffic when using streetlights2. I wish there was a way to hover over a care and see the path it's taking. As the map gets bigger, it can get a little difficult figure out where the inefficiencies are.3. The visual/audio queue when a new business/house pops up is really really easy to miss. Often times I have a house that spawns either under a moterway or in the midst of a bunch of other houses, and I don't realize for quite some time that it's not connected to a road.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be upfront: is it worth $10? If you really enjoy this type of gameplay, absolutely. I've played it 7 hours and I'm still only about 60-70% done with the game, and it's designed to be played long after you "beat" it, complete with daily and weekly challenges. If you're a casual player, however... maybe wait for it to go on sale for $5 instead.Mini Motorways is a conundrum of a game- stressful but relaxing, casual but competitive, simple but complex... however it runs into a few humps that I, personally, can't get over in terms of really getting into it.First, I'll talk about the good, as there's a lot to be said here:- Easy to pick up, hard to master gameplay. Anyone can pick up the game and score a few hundred points, but it takes a lot of deep thinking and planning if you aim to rack up the fat scores. Even just completing the achievements is quite a challenge, much less trying to make it onto the leaderboards!- Beautiful minimalistic graphics. The game is a pleasure to look at even for hours on end, and it's fun to watch your city grow and see the cars all gliding past each other (if you built your roads right). With how complex the game gets in the later stages, it also helps reduce unnecessary clutter.- Similarly, very simple UI and controls make the game very accessible. You can play the entire thing with just your mouse.- Dynamic sounds. Each point scored makes a ding, cars whoosh over motorways, stoplights tick and tock, and this symphony organically grows over the course of a game as you build your city. Each location also has a slightly different sound profile, preventing you from getting bored.- A pause function allows you to think about your next move at your leisure. This turns something that would be a chaotic mess into a relaxing puzzle game.As for the issues I've run into... bottom line is, this is not a fun game competitively. If you're actually playing to optimize for the biggest score, you're very quickly going to run into the weak links and pain points of this game which turn competitive play into a grind for luck. To detail:- There are a lot of random elements which makes the game unreliable. At a casual level this adds interesting dilemmas in terms of how to structure your roads to respond to an unexpected shop or house spawning, but when you get to a competitive level, you realize sometimes the RNG can just screw you over. You can be starved of the parts you need, houses can spawn in locations which make surviving impossible, and double stores will kill your run outright. In addition...- High level play involves extensive RNG manipulation. Placing roads to prevent things from spawning is the name of the game. It feels super janky and I feel like there should be a better solution. The most egregious of these is the Tokyo map, where high level players will fill in the small island with roads so nothing can spawn on it, since getting to and from the island is taxing on resources.- Speaking of, most times what will kill you in this game is trying to work around jank. When you want to move a motorway, for example, there is a massive lag between giving the order to delete the motorway and actually getting it back to place somewhere else. In addition, while you're waiting for the motorway to be deleted, all the cars stop traveling to the original destination, which can kill you late game if you're not careful. This is just one example of how at the highest level you'll be doing more fighting against the system than actually making meaningful and fun decisions.Some other issues include: not being able to connect a house directly to a bridge; not being able to connect roundabouts, stoplights, and freeways to each other; having houses spawn in corners of the map where they can't connect to any roads, effectively making them "dead;" having houses spawn across the map and not being given motorways/road tiles to deal with it; etc.And some small nitpicks:- Traffic lights are near useless in almost every situation, and there's never a reason to take them unless you get more road tiles with them. They need some sort of buff.- This slightly falls into the "issues with competitive play" category, but sometimes the pathing can be finicky. Cars will almost always take the shortest route, so this has to be taken into consideration when building, and sometimes it can screw you over when you'd be fine if some cars would just take the long way around. Maybe there could be a new powerup that adds the ability to change cars' pathing, like one way signs?Overall, it's a fun little romp you can easily spend 10-20 hours on. However, if you aim to get on the leaderboards or even just go for the 2000 trip achievements, you're going to be in for a bit of a slog and I wouldn't be surprised if you come out of it feeling a little burnt out. Still, I think it's definitely worth experiencing!

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 27.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ing minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you

_childDocuments_.review: Mini motorways is not a terrible game, but it is plagued by a few problems.1. The way houses and destinations spawn is completely random, which means your run can end relatively quickly just through sheer luck. An example is having both a cross map spawn (houses on one side, the destination on the other) along with cross-water spawns, where you're stuck with either not enough tiles or having to flip a motorway back and forth between the two destinations, which will generally result in an early fail unless you luck out on a second motorway or bridge.2. Ranking is pointless due to cheaters. You will literally see some scores where they have over 1 billion points. No point in actually trying to compete if that's what you like.3. Traffic light option is pointless. It doesn't have any beneficial factor unlike the roundabout. It causes more needless stoppages than actually solves traffic. The better solution to traffic lights is really to segregate the roads better.For something that's a puzzle 'roguelite', the RNG factor is way too strong and does not give you a good feeling of "you failed because you didn't manage properly" but rather a "I didn't get a bridge two weeks in a row even though there's a spawn on an island"

_childDocuments_.review: Seven years ago now (unbelievably) I reviewed an Early Access build of Mini Motorways' older sibling, Mini Metro, and lauded the fact the game capitalised on "something inherently calming about joining the dots and creating order." Now we have Mini Motorways, which brings us above ground - but thankfully, there are more changes afoot than just this.Not only do we now have a lovely landscape to enjoy, but Mini Motorways eschews its forerunner's shapes that we had to abstract into metro stations and instead presents us with charming little colour coded houses to which colour coded destinations must be linked by road. Straight away, this makes Mini Motorways feel far more involving and immersive than its forerunner as you watch little cars zip back and forth and beep at one another in frustration.Just as in Metro, each Sunday night sees you served with more road tiles (this game's currency rather than the lines of old) and upgrades. Bridges replace tunnels from the last game, while roundabouts, traffic lights and highways are all new and give you ways to better flow, manage and speed up your traffic respectively.Because of course, what starts as a sedate, zen like joining of the dots and creation of satisfaction progressively gives way to mayhem and panic, the nice ambient soundtrack ticking ever more aggressively and destinations filling up with irate passengers. I'd forgotten how alarming it is to note that your screen is ever so slightly zooming out, ready to expand the map and the challenges it will throw at you.So Mini Motorways keeps Mini Metro's best bit: its spirit, but with a lot more theme and outward charm and appeal thrown into the mix. I still encourage you to buy both, if nothing else to observe this fine game's DNA.

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favourite casual puzzle games. Just connect houses to stores / imax locations and watch the cars go about. Sooner or later you'll notice that your city layout sucks and no one is getting anywhere and it all ends. Then you begin again and try to do better. Endless fun to be had especially with challenges and expert as well as daily and weekly challenges to keep the experience fresh. Excellent game to just vibe and chill to. _childDocuments_.review: If what you're looking for is a game where you can strategize and design a complex but responsive street layout to transport citizens around, whilst also being relaxing and entertaining this is not your game; go play Cities Skylines.This game is for those that don't mind getting smacked constantly by an RNG that just doesn't feel like giving you anything but the absolute worst of the worst. This is for those that don't like to strategize around the cards being given, because if you try that, you'll lose pretty quickly. This game is for those that just want to mess around with incredibly restrictive mechanics that let you do just about nothing, that don't care about a game laughing at their faces and that don't expect to win.Or in summary, don't even bother. For this prize you can go buy a soda and have something to drink while you play something else.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game for the most part! Pleasing to look at, works smoothly most of the time, fun overall! Sometimes you'll click on a road to delete it and it'll delete the one next to it. Sometimes you'll click on a grid square to place a road there and it'll place it next to where you clicked. It's not a huge deal but these two things happen. If I had any genuine complaints, it's the car AI. Houses don't go to the nearest store if you have multiple stores connected. They'll just go at seemingly random. You work around this by segregating not only colors but also businesses. Counting how many houses are connected per store. Then a secondary issue starts up, sometimes you'll have enough (or even more than enough) houses connected, with no traffic jams, and they still won't go. I don't understand it and it's infuriating. I have 3000+ points on every level at this point and quite a few attempts have failed despite having an overabundance of available houses. It's almost like the game is intentionally sabotaging the attempts? Or the AI is just broken and doesn't know what to do. Anyway, it's a fun game. It's well worth the money. Just prepare for that frustration. Some runs will just fail due to bad luck.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: One thing I love about city builders is managing the traffic.  So this game is great if I just want to do that.  I love seeing the routes the vehicles take.  I like seeing vehicles take a freeway I set up.  It's great just to have that moment of perfection when everything is running smoothly.The game is great.  While I feel like I have a decent grasp of it, I know it would take dozens of hours to truly master if I feel like sinking a lot of time into it.Small islands.  Right before this review I gave up on a map that had a bunch of houses set up on a small island and going in different directions, and if I wanted to use them, I had to use bridges or highways to connect them.  It's annoying.  One workaround is to put road there so nothing goes on those islands until you can manage it, but it's still a pain.The music isn't that great.  The high pitched tones, or the single tone, just make it annoying.With the daily and weekly challenges, I still go back to it since those can be fun and fairly short.  It keeps the game fairly fresh.I have been a gamer for over 30 years.  I tend to play mostly PC games.  I also bounce around between games A LOT.  I may purchase a $60 game and play it for 2 hours or spend $10 on a game and spend 50 hours on it.  Even if I played a game a short time, it does not mean it is bad.  It just means another game caught my attention.  I also complain about flaws in games a lot, even about the littlest of things.  Keep that in mind when reading my reviews.  If I do not have a complaint, then the game must be special!

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy spacial reasoning puzzle games, don't mind occasionally being shafted by RNG, and can take the frustration of being stuck at a bottleneck in your scores that you can't seem to get past (until you do) then this is the game for you. The core gameplay loop is enjoyable, if at times repetitive, and you can expect ~30 hours of content to 100% the achievements.Overall a very solid game. If you're the type to constantly grind just to one-up your on previous best score (or rise a couple ranks on the global leader-board) then I can easily see this game lasting you a hundred-plus hours.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Mini Metro from the same developer, you'll probably like this. Simple game, simple rule, just the mouse, and barely any buttons to press. You just draw roads between different coloured houses and different coloured buildings (shops? offices? nobody knows). Little cars set off down the road to go shop (or work, nobody knows). That's the basic idea. The challenge is that roads get busy! Houses crop up, buildings demand ever more visitors, faster and faster. The drivers follow some sort of internal rules. And, eventually, if a building isn't getting enough visitors (and they're HUNGRY!) then the city fails and the citizens burn the place down and dance naked in the ashes. That's after the "Game Over" part though, so you don't get to see it. It's city planning against a literal ticking clock! The pressure builds up when you're not looking, and all of a sudden your perfect plan starts to over-run! NO! Don't drive there!So it's part brains, laying out the city at first, and part mad panic, in patching it up, faster than you can even think sometimes. Lots of fun, and lots of different towns to work on. As well as challenges and a leader board. It's the Steam game I play most by far. Watch someone play on Youtube and see if it looks like it's for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Mini Motorways is perfectly suited to bite-sized play sessions - if you have 30 minutes you want to kill, load it up and see how far you can get. The gameplay loop is stress-inducing in a fun way, and the scaling curve feels excellently calibrated - you can sit back and relax early on, scoping out the map, figuring out where things might start to go wrong, and pre-plan to ensure that when the game really starts to ramp up, you're building proactively, not reactively. I'm terrible at this, but even failing to build proactively pretty much every time, it's always very fun to hop in to this game for a little while, do one or two sessions, and pop back out. Clean graphics, excellent controls, a very intuitive UI - it's clear that this was built for mobile, in a good way, and that makes it the perfect game for sporadic playthroughs. Just don't bother with the traffic lights.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this is a recommendation. I really loved Mini Metro and likewise Mini Motorways does a great job hitting similar notes.However, I feel like there are a few significant issues that I hope can be addressed.In my experience there isn't much variety in strategy if you are looking to reach the highest of scores. In particular I simply cannot justify traffic lights. Roundabouts I have also found slow things down when the weeks start ticking by - any slowdown can add up to be deadly. Motorways are always great for skipping over other sections of the map or far off destinations - they are definitely the highlight of the upgrades (as they should be, given the title of the game!). Even motorways have drawbacks that I was not expecting: cars need to all return home before a bulldozed motorway can be placed again.In particular, more than any of this, it feels awkward to have an highly potent strategy around filling up the map with roads and forcing buildings to spawn in a particular way.Once your city has more or less spawned the player has limited amount of agency to control when things start to go awry - this could be regarded as a positive: it rewards good planning. However, my mind shifts to the similar end game play found in Mini Metro: frantically pausing the game, shifting individual trains around, reconfiguring train lines, adding a sudden 'fix it' line on a station about to blow up - I really enjoyed this part of Mini Metro. Mini Motorways doesn't really feature this component of the game, although the motorways themselves feel like they could fill this void.Overall I would love to have more variety in strategy and the ability to try out different city designs, at the moment it feels like there are limited options. Perhaps certain 'hard mode' restrictions (and associated achievements) would help here, as similarly seen in Mini Metro. This all said I will gladly play the game as it stands and, as I started, I recommend Mini Motorways.

_childDocuments_.review: Mini Motorways is a game that instantly reminds me of an app my dad showed me when I was little. I can’t help but wonder if the same creators developed this gem on Steam!
