_childDocuments_.review: I would really like to love and recommend this game. I really enjoyed MiniMetro, but this game has less variety and some fatal flaws.The game is fun enough to play for some hours, but soon the following flaws becomes fatal;1: Deleting roads, tunnels, bridges, and motorways is just way too slow. Especially motorways. It takes forever to regain the deleted items, making the game much less dynamic.2: As soon as the timer starts on a building (indicating that you have too few cars going there), there is just no way to correct it in time before the timer runs out and the game ends. The timer is too quick compared to the slowness of deleting and moving roads (fatal flaw #1).3: The AI is just too stupid. Buildings and shops pop up in a seemingly random way without any thought. Yes, it may be considered part of the challenge, but it frustrates more than it gives challenge.4: Since entrances can't be changed on shops, the fatal flaw #3 becomes even worse, causing all sorts of wierd road construction. If you're unlucky, you don't have enough road tiles to correct it.5: The traffic light seems underpowered. I never opt to get it as a weekly upgrade, and it seldom helps on traffic jams. It seems to make traffic a little smoother when there is some traffic, but in those cases, it will still work without the lights.6: All games regardless of which map seem to play out and end in the same way. You get too much spagetthi, and too large shops demanding more cars than you can supply, and in the moment you see a shop start the timer, you know the game is over. There is no way you're able to remove a motorway somewhere else and place it near that shop in time because of fatal flaw #1. I would love that the maps have some vareity on goals, constraints, play-style, or whatever. The weekly challenges are the most fun part of the game bacause of this. Unfortunately, there's only two challenges each week.7: There should be more variety on the road types. In essence there are only two road types; Roads/tunnels/bridges and motorways. I would love to see a way to upgrade regular roads to 4 lane, or roads with faster speeds, or even the possibility to bridge over or tunnel under other roads (other than motorway). Like using a bridge to cross one other road rather than making an intersection.At least to me, the fatal flaws #1 and #2 is the game's main issues right now. I hope that this will be fixed in a future update, but seeing that most people are very happy with the game as it is....

_childDocuments_.review: Look, this game has great potential, and I first was not going to leave a negative review. But it has ruined me over an extended play period.The end-game is frustratingly abrupt, course corrections take too long to settle in, and the pace will overwhelm you shortly after then anyway. Sometimes the automated placement of buildings will ruin you - this you'll have to accept.There are a litany of irritating bugs that cause road blockages that will bring your city to a halt. Times where cars will not move, times where roads will refused to be used. I have hit these quite often in my short time with the game.I enjoy playing the mid-game, enjoy thinking about the late-game, but the game doesn't want me to play it to a satisfying end.If you want to build a city where everything is connected you are fundamentally ruining your city. The one time I got 7k points with an interconnected city it felt like a fluke, with other times screwing me with poor rewards, bad spawns, and terrible growth.Edit after changing review to negative:This game is rife with game ending bugs that are compounded by frustrating design decisions. As previously mentioned, changes to city planning do not play out fast enough to fix a city's problems, recently I've experienced multiple traffic jams that the game clears so slowly they may as well be permanent. I've had 5 or so runs ended by softlocks. All of this on runs where I could see potential.The recent balance to traffic lights have made them so superior to roundabouts and general intersections it's ridiculous. Roundabouts in this game haven't worked properly, with cars on the circle yielding to those entering, so it's frustrating to see IRL principles go to the wayside even further.The game's been plaguing me with awful spawns and rewards, with runs ended because all destinations are on the opposite side to houses and no motorways are rewarded.I'm frustrated by the way you're not making a liveable city. I'm frustrated that I'm forced down the path the game intends for me, only to see it decide to throw a spanner in the works. Forcing a long detour to be built to overcome a spawn or some jank, only to have that detour suck away all the cars from easily reached destinations in both directions, with cars deciding to go to the complete opposite sides of the map to satisfy the smallest compounding demand requirement.Runs with simply and closely connected structures ending because the demand has overcome the houses spawned on the map. Runs ended because I remove something for a moment only to have a structure spawn right under my cursor.Hell, even runs ended because I didn't see something spawn, the UI doing very little to draw your attention to their demands until it's too late. With volume off or low, or with any distractions you will need to slow down and pause regularly just to ensure everything is connected, it's not something the game will readily alert you to.Anyway, I'm sick of it all, it's been uninstalled, one of the few games I have uninstalled out of anger. I'll maybe come back to see if it's better in six month's time if I remember.

_childDocuments_.review: Mini Metro was a nice relaxing train logistics sim thingy, so seeing this come to steam how could I not buy Mini Motorways?And I'm happy to say, that this is a nice relaxing car/road logistics sim, the mechanics are very different to Mini Metro, but just as simplistic and easy to grasp.The colourful palette for the graphics is pleasing and easy on the eye, the sounds are just the right side of repetitive, bordering on white noise.All in all, Mini Motorways is yet another great game by Dinosaur Polo Club. Right now they don’t seem to put a foot wrong when it comes to casual chill-out games.If I review anything, I try to find flaws to critique – and for this game, it’s rather hard finding anything, but I do have a minor issue with how some of the ‘connections’ are made or limited, and while I acknowledge the game is randomly generated, sometimes the placement or orientation of a new connection feels like a deliberate attempt to really rustle my jimmies.Can it be improved upon? Only in the most tiny of ways, and perhaps only in my entirely subjective opinion.Is this game worth it?Absolutely.9.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: The concept off this game is good.  It has 11 difference scenarios to do and there is some strategy to learn in order to do them well.  There are also leaderboards, BUT the leaderboards are the reasons I'm not recommending this game to new players.  I can't recommend a game where part of it is broken.  The leaderboards are totally broken with the exception of the one daily challenge and one weekly challenge.  The leaderboards are there, but there is no chance of actually competing on them, because the scores are very old and were achieved in a very different game build where cheating was possible, and the gameplay has changed over time.  However, despite people asking for these to be fixed and reset so that the scores on them are related to the CURRENT game, as it stands, the devs just totally refuse to do that.  The highest score you're likely to get is maybe 7,000 approx.  The scoreboard is full of scores up to 200,000 (the score cap).  There is no chance to get anywhere near them.  If the devs actually kept this game CURRENT, and fixed the leaderboards so that new players could use these leaderboards at all, I would highly recommend this game.  However, as it stands, you can do the scenarios, but basically have to ignore the leaderboards.  The one daily challenge and one weekly challenge are okay.  There are only global leaderboards for this game.  You can't just compete with your friends, and you can't even just keep a record of your own scores and watch your improvement over time (only your last score).  If that was possible, at least there would be some aspect of these boards that was functional.  Unfortunately, there's just no use for them at all.So if you're happy to buy this game ONLY for the one daily challenge and the one weekly challenge, then buy it.  But if you're expecting the WHOLE game to be available, the full functionality of the game that you're actually PAYING FOR, it just isn't.  The leaderboards for everything except those two challenges are totally broken.If the devs have a change of heart and actually maintain the game properly, that is, maintain it as a game that NEW players can ALSO enjoy, then I will change my review!
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: This game is overall good, but it has very SERIOUS flaws that prevent me from liking it *fully*. I'll start with the biggest problem I have: 1.) Mini Metro has endless mode, yet this does not. Why? Couldn't tell you. It's what I was looking forward to the most and its absence is seriously hurting my enjoyment of the game since I prefer to be creative rather than challenged. Forum posts reveal that endless mode was planned many months ago but it never came. Incidentally, don't let the release date on Steam fool you, the game may have been released on Steam during summer of 2021 but it was ACTUALLY first released almost two years ago on iOS.2.) Difficulty spikes randomly. I understand that each level is randomly generated, but what really gets me is just how annoyingly stupid the little drivers are. There can be a clear path straight to their destination with low traffic but you can lose the game even if there are many cars en route to their destination. At one point I lost because a building hadn't received any visitors lately AS a car was pulling into a parking spot there. It's also incredibly difficult to notice that a building is in "danger" since the art style doesn't make the notifications "pop" on the screen meaning you often notice the problems too late. I'm not sure where the **** everybody is getting off saying this game is relaxing because the truth is that it jumps from cakewalk to nightmare in a matter of seconds.3.) Leaderboards are FORCED. What if I don't want to upload my score? I can't even use cheat engine to try and create a pseudo-endless mode because my score would be uploaded to a leaderboard and that wouldn't be fair to other players. So that's not even an option.4.) I've had a couple bugs where roads were built but AI cars got stuck and just wouldn't move at all. Needless to say that was not something I survived.5.) You CANNOT MANUALLY SAVE midway through a level. Your level progress is in the hands of autosave.6.) You CANNOT rebind the controls. 7.) There are NO separate volume sliders, meaning you can't play your own music if you want. You're stuck with the game's OST.Overall, I'm pretty disappointed. It wasn't really what I was looking for.  is the more creative entry into the road-building simulator and that provides challenging gameplay that isn't straight up frustrating like this is.In terms of things I do like, it comes down to the clean graphics, sound design, and challenge it provides for those that want a challenge. But, graphics and sound design aren't that important. What's important is providing gameplay for multiple different types of players. I'm apparently not the target audience.If you want a challenging game, this is for you. If you want a creative relaxing game, this is NOT what you're looking for. Sorry developers, you've got some work to do on this title for me to give it a recommendation. Since the game has been out for years, I doubt you're going to change much. FINAL SCORE: 5/10IN A NUTSHELL: MADE FOR THE COMPETITIVE, NOT THE CREATIVE EDIT 11/25/2021: Still no endless mode. I am sad.

_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely love this game! Basically a strategy simulation game where you manage the traffic in a growing city by building roads, roundabouts, traffic lights, and motorways. New houses/passengers spawn at an increasing tempo and it's up to you to keep up and get everyone to their destination. It starts out chill and gets increasingly more chaotic.I've always been a fan of Mini Metro, so was looking forward to playing this game as well, and it didn't disappoint. You can play this game both for a little while where you just do a daily challenge for example, but you can just as well play it for hours and beat those high scores. I keep coming back to this game every now and then. Recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: Simple, but very fun and addicting game.A lot of times, I feel like the game is trying its best to screw me up and I get stressed, but after some time, I start this game again.But there is one problem, IMO.Weekly and daily challenges only register the first score, and don't register any subsequent scores. _childDocuments_.review: Really love this game. I adore the traffic fixing on cities skylines, so this is kind of the super vanilla version of that , with only traffic and roadways as the main focus. _childDocuments_.review: when i was a kid, i always wanted to be a civil engineer. being able to figure out the best ways of creating the most efficient ways of creating roads and cities using statistics and maths. but my grades were terrible and my parents thought i would never be anything in my life. so i thought that i will never fulfill my dreams of becoming a civil engineer. this game made me feel better about myself and proves that i may still have the potential to be the person i wanted to be when i was a kid. look at me now mom and dad. look at me now mrs.henderson. games fun 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly i didn't know what to expect from this game. Something so simple yet a lot of fun. You start with one house and one destination, Both the same color. House's pop up more and more over time at random locations. House's are different colors and have 2 vehicles per house. Different color destinations pop up over time as well in different locations on the map. Orange colored cars go to orange colored destinations, Red colored cars go to red colored destinations, Etc. The car leaves the house from its location, goes to the destination of the matching color and gets a destination pin. After getting the pin it returns home and makes the trip again to another destination of the same color at a different location on the map. The pins the cars pick up are your points. Simple right? Like i said destinations and house pop up at all different locations, sometimes clear across the map. Time is measured by weeks. You have the ability to speed up time x2 only. Each week you will be given a option of either getting a bridge and 20+ more roads or maybe a freeway and 10+ more roads. There's also round about and traffic lights. With that being said you obviously know that you only have a certain amount of roads to link all these together. The key is to provide the easiest points of access for all the cars to get to their colored destinations in time. If a car doesn't not make it to a destination in a while then a timer will form above that destination. Every time a car makes it there while the timer is ticking it will delay the timer a bit. if the timer runs out at a destination its game over. What ever amount of pins you accumulate before the timer runs out is your score. If you don't have a timer run out then the game just keeps going. Every week that you make your choice of a tool (bridge, Highway, Round about, Traffic light, Etc) its meant to help shorten paths for certain cars or maybe help you organize traffic. House's and destinations do not stop popping up. It can get chaotic. Yes you can delete roads and when you do a road will be credited back to you to use where you want to. You can change the direction cars exit their houses but you can not change where cars enter destinations. Some destinations will have 2 entrances but most have one. The game is actually done very nicely. You can change the background colors to your preference and the game is just very polished. At $9 this is a great buy! I don't have much time into the game but i thought about buying it for a while. Hopefully this will give you a understanding of the game. Also there is weekly challenges where you get unlimited round about's, or maybe unlimited bridges. There's a bunch of different maps like NYC, LA, and all the popular city's. Overall they kind of all look the same but its a cool concept. The game is fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: massive improvement over mini metro on pretty much all fronts, but metro is a great game itself. i like that the daily/weekly challenges have different modifiers that change up the gameplay more than mini metro's normal/extreme modes in its challenges. i also like how these modifiers are now embedded into the very recently added challenges for the main maps, which gives a nice challenge or few to do aside from the initial "x amount of trips" achievements. i feel like traffic lights make the flow of traffic feel counter-intuitive though so that's my only complaint. overall a fantastic game that captures the original mini metro but with cars
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: Cities: Skylines started my addiction to building roads, and Mini Motorways enables it. _childDocuments_.review: Don't let its cheerful graphics, tribble sounds, and easily accessible gameplay lure you in.It's the cruel mistress you can't quit: dressed in party balloons; gently whispers sweet nothings that remind you that you're an idiot; and flicks your ear every 30 seconds to remind you that you're about to succumb to the sweet succor of your city's always-impending doom. _childDocuments_.review: It's a lot like Mini Metro, but that's no bad thing. The relaxed, satisfying puzzling remains, with a new look and some new bonus items to help solve your traffic problems. _childDocuments_.review: This game's lack of cultural sensitivity is truly disappointing. It fails to recognize the importance of embracing diversity and respecting different cultures. From the very beginning, it becomes evident that the game's portrayal of various cultural elements is shallow and insensitive.One of the glaring issues lies in the depiction of different colored houses, cars, and shopping malls. Instead of celebrating the rich tapestry of cultural diversity, the game reduces these elements to mere stereotypes. It perpetuates a simplistic and inaccurate view of cultures by using shallow visual cues without providing any meaningful context or understanding.To make matters worse, the presence of tomatoes that eat cultural sensitivity is utterly offensive. Instead of promoting inclusivity and understanding, the game introduces these tasteless characters that mock and exclaim racial slurs. Such an inclusion is not only insensitive but also perpetuates harmful stereotypes and reinforces discriminatory attitudes.It is crucial for any form of media, including games, to recognize the importance of cultural sensitivity. The lack of thoughtful representation and respect in this game is deeply troubling. By failing to address cultural nuances and treating diversity as a mere gimmick, the game sends a harmful message to players.In a time where society is striving for inclusivity and understanding, it is disheartening to encounter a game that disregards these fundamental values. It is my sincere hope that the developers take this feedback seriously and make the necessary changes to ensure a more culturally sensitive and inclusive gaming experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent little city builder "lite". It's like an arcade version of the traffic/road management in Cities: Skylines. So if that was your favorite part of that game (as it was mine) then you'll love this game. It took me 35 hours to get all the achievements and at no point was I bored, so for the absurdly low price point it is definitely worth it. I heartily recommend Mini motorways.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: Similar to another game in an ENTIRELY different genre, Vampire Survivors, this rounds of Mini Motorways start out pretty tame, but then it gets incredibly stressful very quickly. _childDocuments_.review: Mini Motorways is a super fun, super addicting brain teaser. The game mechanics are simple and easy to understand, but difficult to master. _childDocuments_.review: I play a lot of city/castle builders and my favorite part is always the beginning. Seeing an empty randomly-generated world and plotting out the land. Then 30-40 minutes in I realize the magic is gone and I quit. This game basically speedruns that and more or less forces you to loose before it gets too stale.The maps are geographically static but the spawn of houses and stores is random, so you can easily write off a bad game to bad spawns which makes me feel a lot better about sucking at it. Fun little game but doesn't really have that daily log-in vibe to it such as Bloons TD 6. The daily challenge is a map with 2 modifiers and that's it. Knock yourself out.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, as much as I would like to recommend this game, there are a number of issues that prevent me from doing so.- Poor performance on my laptop (capable of running skyrim on lower settings but not this???) and it drains my battery way more than you'd expect for a 2d game which exists on mobile devices.- Forgets the display resolution I set in the options.- Poor touch support...- No way to zoom? Am I missing something?- Most malls only have one driveway, which feels artificially restrictive.- Malls preferentially spawn connected to your preexisting color-coded roadways. I wish they just chose any open non-residential spot.- The only way to control where anything spawns is to place down filler roads, which is jank and annoying (either give me some control, or don't).- No undo button, easy to accidentally delete motorways.- Short timers mean that, after you reach a certain size, if a timer comes up, then there's a good chance it's already too late.- No modding support to fix any of these issues.To be clear, I will continue playing it, but I am disappointed.On the off-chance a developer reads this, I have a few suggestions. Here they are, roughly ordered in likelihood:+ Remember resolution setting+ Undo button+ Pan and zoom+ Improve performance+ Touch support (pinch, drag, etc)+ Back-up saves / create reloadable snapshots of cities+ Move any mall one block any direction from where it original spawned.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really great relaxing game that can be a bit stressful as your city grows. It's very fun and the music / art style is fantastic. _childDocuments_.review: A very good followup to Mini MetroIt may seem similar on first glance, but there's definitely enough to differentiate it (and at this early stage I might even prefer it).It is much harder to save yourself from a failing layout, since you can't re-route instantly for free or pick up the cars like you could in Metro, but it is also easier to see these pitfalls coming a lot sooner down the line, and you have better tools for path management.The game is also notably missing a few features from Metro, such as difficulty modes and the option to continue playing on  a 'lost' map, but it does still have night time and colourblind which are both very welcome additions.Hopefully future updates will bring it more in line with the current state of Mini Metro, but it's still a great little game and worth picking up for the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Getting a good score is 2% skill/stratagy and 98% RNG.  Once you're OK with that it's still a fun game to play. _childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: It's okay. Worth a couple plays. It's cheap enough that you should maybe get it anyway. But I'm not a big fan.Things I like: it's satisfying to see the cars drive around. I like the puzzle of it. Challenges seem like they're not a huge deal, but they actually dramatically change how a map plays, which is cool and adds a lot of replayability and, well, challenge. Maps have thematic color schemes.There are two big things I find frustrating. One is that drops feel so random. You're desperate for a motorway, and you don't get one for four weeks. A new destination gets dropped in a place that has too many houses, so you can't fit in any traffic control on the way to the destination, and now traffic is bad. The wrong destination gets upgraded, and you don't notice, and it spirals downward.The other big thing I find frustrating is that when things get bad, you're probably just screwed. There are two failure modes. One is that cars can't reach a destination. This is not too hard to detect. The other is that cars can't get home from a destination, so they can't get sent back out. You will, ultimately, lose from this, but it's much harder to see until it results in pressure on a destination, and it's too late. This is also hard to detect because congestion can happen *under* motorways, where you literally cannot see it until you pause the game.Once you're in a failure mode, you have to address it, but cars stay on their existing route, so you can't resolve bad gridlock until it disappears on its own, and you will have lost by then. You also typically need to reengineer a whole section of the map (roundabouts won't fit as-is, and both roundabouts and lights have capacity limits, so you probably need to split the intersection, and it's a whole thing), which is just fantastically hard and won't have the needed effect in time. So the bottom line is that by the time you see cars backed up, you've already lost! Isn't that cool.The controls are also a little clunky? It's typically easier to redraw a road by removing and relaying it, but if you do that with even a single piece of a motorway then the motorway is deleted and can't be replaced until every car is off it. Controlling the driveway direction of a house is a pain. _childDocuments_.review: Excellent game in the spirit of Mini Metro, into which I have sunk many hundreds of hours per year since it came out in 2014. (And so have my daughter and many friends to whom I recommended it.) It is similar enough so you immediately feel at home, yet different enough to be a fresh experience after years of playing Mini Metro.For those not familiar with Mini Metro: Mini Motorways and Mini Metro are minimalist, addictive, feel-good, casual games. Don't expect anything deep. There are no levels or winning conditions. You just play until you lose. You could think of them as tower defense games in which the towers are traffic infrastructure and the opponent is the city's increasing transport requirements. Your performance is scored on each run, so you can play competitively. In both games there are daily challenges, where you can compare your score to other players'. The daily challenge is always to play a specific map with a specific combination of restrictions. This works offline as well; you just need to be online for the highscore functionality.Dinosaur Polo Club, a small publisher based in Wellington, New Zealand, have been doing exceptional work for years after the release of their first game Mini Metro, improving the game and adding maps and even some features. This is the kind of publisher I would buy an early access game from unseen, but this game (their second one) is actually what most publishers would consider a completely finished game. Currently, frequent updates are addressing some minor issues that still exist. Based on past performance, I won't be surprised if they add free new features anyway.As of this writing, the maps available are Los Angeles, Beijing, Tokyo, Dar es Salaam, Moscow, Munich, Zürich, Manila, Rio de Janeiro, Dubai, Mexico City. The developers have promised to add new maps regularly.So far, the maps can only be played in standard mode. Mini Metro also has an endless mode. I can imagine that it is a bit tricky to implement for this game (in such a way that it still makes sense, that is), but given how popular it is in Mini Metro, I expect they are working on it for Mini Motorways.Mini Motorways has a refined system for map modifiers that change parameters of the game. Most just change the availability of upgrades. For example, infinitely many traffic lights may be available, or one motorway may be available from the start, but no further motorways offered as upgrades. A special modifier I have encountered makes the trees on the map indestructible. So far, these modifiers are only used in the daily and weekly challenges.Daily challenges otherwise work as in Mini Metro. Every 24 hours a new map is featured, with special modifiers. You can play it as many times as you want, but only the first score is entered in the global high score list. (The top places are always occupied by cheaters with astronomic scores.)Weekly challenges are like daily challenges, except they change once a week only and every attempt counts for the high score list.Mini Motorways runs perfectly on Linux, but very sluggish until you tweak the settings as described on . For me, the recommended launch optionsPROTON_USE_WINED3D=1 %command%together with the recommended Proton version 5.13-6 solved the issue.In general, this game appears to be programmed quite inefficiently. CPU usage is significantly more than would appear reasonable for a leisurely 2D game. This is the case even when you are in the menu and the game shouldn't really be doing anything at all.The number of cars/houses needed to serve a destination (each house provides two cars) depends on how much time the cars spend in traffic: distance and speed. You always get more houses than you actually need; when the houses spawn far away from their destination, you get more of them than when they spawn very close. Circular destinations need twice as many cars as regular, square destinations. To play the game well, you need to keep the number of cars that are in traffic at the same time manageable. This requires keeping travel distances small and speeds high.Traffic can get completely jammed when the capacity of your network is insufficient. Otherwise the main sources of slow-downs are curves and intersections. Even a 3-way intersection will slow down traffic if cars have to wait for each other, but this only becomes a problem when there is too much traffic. 4-way intersections and intersections with more than 4 branches always slow down traffic considerably, even if cars in practice use only two of the branches. Therefore it is often best to avoid them.It is often a good idea to replace a busy 3-way intersection by a triangle and connect each branch to one of its corners. This replaces one 3-way intersection by three 3-way intersections, each of which is a bit less busy, and ideally also makes the paths shorter. A roundabout, available as an upgrade, is the extension of this idea. In the most extreme case, you can think of it replacing an 8-way intersection by an octagon with eight 3-way intersections. However, the traffic through the octagon is one-way only, which increases almost half the travel times but makes the 3-way intersections far more efficient.To achieve a good score, it is usually best to prevent busy routes from intersecting at all. This is easiest to do with motorways, but these are limited. Bridges and tunnels may help with this as well. As in real life, if the traffic at a busy intersection gets too much, you can try to address it with a traffic light or a roundabout. Traffic lights are quite problematic for this purpose because they  increase capacity only very slightly and tend to make the traffic pulsate in a way that often causes other problems. (Basically the only reason for a traffic light is to increase speed on a busy main road going through a more than 3-way intersection with almost no traffic from the other branches.) A roundabout provides a limited but substantial increase in capacity.In November 2023, I can say that in over 2 years since I originally wrote this review, work on the game continued just as I predicted. There has just been a big update, which is why I am updating this review: the introduction of Endless Mode and Expert Mode. This type of game is about getting its players into a flow state. Different players need different levels of challenge for this, which is why the different modes are needed. For some players Mini Motorways will be better for reaching this state, for others Mini Metro will be better, and for some alternating between both games will be best.Other games that are great at creating flow state in a large number of people include Civilization, Stellaris, and Bloons TD. The difference is that (especially when played as single-player games) these bigger games suck you in and try to keep you forever. With Mini Motorways (and Mini Metro), each run of the game is rather short and finally ends with a failure, reminding you to return to real life.Of course they have also slowly added maps (cities), and the game is currently at 15 maps (4 more since my original review) playable in 3 modes. In parallel, they also continued adding maps to Mini Metro, which is now at 30 maps playable in 4 modes. Since Mini Metro has Steam Workshop integration for user-contributed maps, there is a chance that over the next couple of years we will see that for Mini Motorways as well. There is also a chance that the pace of map contributions will increase in connection with this. I imagine they will clean up the game's data format before making it publicly available, and perhaps make it easier for themselves, too, in the process.They have also worked on the mechanics. It is likely that they tweaked many small things, but  notably three-way intersections also slow down traffic now, and traffic lights are a bit more effective than before.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great casual game. The graphics are well polished and modern paired with minimalist UI. It just makes me want to play it just for the sheer cleanness. Another great addition to this game is the color modes, this isn’t just for colorblindness, but also has night and day modes. The game reminds me of a minimalist version of the traffic challenges in Cities: Skyline. I do realize this has a prequel, Mini Metro, but I have not played it. For just $10 on Steam, it’s worth it and more.This game is an endless simulator. The objective is to use roads to connect homes to businesses that are the same color.  The game ends when one of the businesses doesn’t get enough traffic to it in time. Each level starts with a few houses and a business.  As time goes along, your birds-eye view slowly zooms out allowing for more space for homes and businesses to appear. Before you know it there are traffic jams and great distances between houses and businesses they are associated with.  Each week that you survive you get rewards to help you survive the next round, this includes additional roads, bridges, roundabouts, or highways.There is plenty of replayability. Each time you play the same location everything is randomized including start location, rewards, and layout of homes and businesses.  They also have daily and weekly challenges to keep you competing with the community. I have had a few glitches with roads with extra tails that can’t be deleted without deleting other parts of the road. But this is minor when it comes to the overall game.   The only thing I would like is better touch screen support. This game has such a casual feel, that I want to lounge back and play it on a tablet. Don’t get me wrong, it is definitely playable on touch screen but it gets hard to press on details when the level gets large. Maybe adding a zoom feature for touch screens. The other issue is toggling between creating and deleting is tedious.  I find myself doing both constantly but will forget what I am on and end up creating a bunch of roads or deleting a major intersection.My overall grade is an B+.  This game is so well polished. This game has some serious replayability. The touch screen support and the road glitches are so minor to this overall game.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: This relaxing game is very addictive and at times when you're on a deep run, stressful but rewarding. The concept is simple, get cars from their homes to the shop they pick up from when a pickup is ready. As time progresses, the shops generate pickups at a higher rate meaning you'll need to connect more houses to the shops and making sure the flow of traffic doesn't jam. You can't control where these homes and shops spawn (though advanced techniques exist to influence where they will spawn), but you control how the houses connect to the shops and get periodic chances to get more tools to manage the flow of traffic effectively (more roads, traffic lights, roundabouts, bridges, tunnels, and the GOAT: motorways)The maps are inspired by real cities, have a night mode version (thank goodness because I'm playing this at night while I work haha) and contain simple but easily navigable obstacles such as mountains and bodies of water. The fun lies in the restriction of the game. You only get so many roads, bridges, motorways, etc to achieve the end goal of keeping traffic flowing. It becomes a resource management simulator in a way. As you play you learn more tricks such as segregating groups of traffic to avoid jams, that traffic lights are useless (save for the one niche use case for traffic lights at three way intersections), how to branch off neighborhoods so there won't be chokepoints, using diagonal roads whenever possible to conserve tiles, and using excess road tiles to prevent unfavorable building spawns.It's a bunch of simple concepts working together to create an enjoyable experience, and I'd highly recommend it for that reason. That being said, there's still some things holding this game back. In my opinion, if the following were implemented into the game by either the devs or by enabling the mod community to create mods, the game would be PERFECT.- A sandbox mode for experimentation- Let the users create their own custom games with existing mutators- A custom map creator and way to play other user-created maps- A more comprehensive leaderboard system and user statsOther than that, get the game already, it's only 10$!

Once you've figured the good strategies, you'll juste have to hope on a good RNG to enhance your score, because once you've understood how it works (e.g. you should try to separate every color as much as possible), you can't really get better and use new strategies. All the highest score you'll see are people who optimized everything they could, and got a good RNG. There's a point where no more houses or buildings appears, and if your circulation is well designed, you won't be able to do anything but wait for the score to grow up. So, that sucks, but I'm sure developers are working hard on it.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game. Its fun, relaxing, simple graphics and one of those games which is easy to learn but difficult to master. It seems more like a mobile phone game, in that you have to arrange traffic and essentially if you can't get cars to their destination quick enough then you are under a timer and then the game ends... Which is the most frustrating part and what keeps me away. Although the game is challenging, no matter how well you organise your city if the timer runs out... Game Over! And while that is the main concept of the game, it shouldn't be the ONLY concept. It feels very arcadey/appy where it could have more depth and I would recommend the devs to introudce a couple of options...1) The option to have no time limit - you simply get less points overall and your city becomes gridlocked - therefore to get things moving again you have to re-organise better.2) Have pre built cities with timer/no timer option in which you have to manage a large area from the beginning -as having to grind through the early stages of each city becomes tedious.3) Introduce some other options - maybe the financial part or budget or something similar.Overall, its a very good game for a very good price but I would like to sit and relax with this game for a few hours rather than curse at ten timers on the screen and game over.... More options/challenges/variations from the devs would work well on this. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: The games designs feel off and dont mesh well. The games random generation of houses and building seems overly punishing and aggressive with spikes in difficulty at the same exact points in correlation to your score. That is overall fine but since the game will spawn buildings or houses in terrible places, like across the map or on islands next to other colors of houses... That makes you need to constantly reconfigure your city which you feel  punished for doing  so since your limited by road tiles or other tiles like bridges and roundabouts. Which in its self is also fine but your not able to get the refund of deleting tiles to move them until however many cars are trying to use it currently have finished using it. Which in turn means; since your so limited to begin with, your once again limited by having to wait to get your tiles back, which in turn makes the buildings not get cars fast enough... i.e game over. The motorways also block the view of the map making it very annoying to see the traffic congestion or the pins of the buildings regardless of being able to wiggle them to slightly different locations. TLDR:-Game could use a more interesting unlocking mechanic instead of 'Reach a 300 Score" over and over-Music needs to change completely or have a MUTE option-Road tiles need to be refunded immediately instead of having to wait for the tile to not be in use.-Motorways need to be transparent or redesigned. -Traffic lights feel useless and counter productive.-Very much feels like a mobile game port.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing this game for 56 hours at the time of writing this and I'm still pretty crap at it...but it definitely has that 'one more go' factor. _childDocuments_.review: It's a synesthesia simulator, a satisfaction generator, weirdly also a roguelike city-manager? This game should be a case study in UI design - it never sacrifices substance for style while delivering THE most satisfying click-and-drag experience ever. The gameplay is thoughtfully designed - balancing situational micro-managing with slower, more patient moments where you strategize while watching your city hum along autonomously. It encourages an improvisational approach to strategy due to the random generation, much like a roguelike, while also providing a large selection of diverse situations to play in each starting city - each requiring a fresh approach to chase high scores.The cherry on top is the soundtrack, which is not just responsive to player input, but actually generated by events on screen! It's like I'm playing with a modular synthesizer where dragging roads equates to patching new sounds together. One little detail I love is how destroying a tree causes the pitch of all of the sounds to ominously modulate down a half step before slowly returning to their original tune. And that's just one of many little moments that make this game the beautiful, addicting thing it is.Oh what a lovely game, well worth the $10 price tag. Just buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: "Man a traffic control sim game would be cool," I remember thinking half a lifetime ago. As always, if you don't do it, someone else will - Mini Motorways did it, and they did it WELL.You have points of departure and destination, and only a limited number of time, space, and resources to connect point A to point B. You can take things apart and put them back together again to optimize to your heart's content. As the game goes on, the destinations become more demanding, and departures are scattered organically, never where it's convenient, like little pimples popping up on an otherwise carefully curated facade. They must be dealt with. You have to compromise. You have to wait on tenterhooks for the beginning of the next time period, when you'll finally have a chance to grab the piece you're missing to make it all work.Bridge, or freeway overpass? Traffic light sensor, or roundabout? You came so close this time - you have time to make  attempt, don't you?

_childDocuments_.review: What a pleasant little puzzle-ish game.The game play, soundtrack, audio design, UI and visuals all feel like they were specifically designed to chill me out.While I've gotten through all of the content in about 8 hours, the daily and weekly challenges and steam achievements (which are all well within my skill level) are keeping me going.I'm not someone who is usually into puzzle games, but this seems more like a cross between a puzzle game and an incredibly low pressure resource management game. _childDocuments_.review: 1) The vibe phase - Here you find yourself relaxing while sipping your favorite beverage 2) Big Brain Phase - You get a serotonin rush after you make a series of efficient route edits 3) The Face Palm - You really just deleted a motorway rather than move it and now you are stuck waiting for it to come back...Now Finally...4) The ???? Phase - It is in this phase that you feel this game's peak. Your ego is slipping away, you no longer remember why blue is even using the motorway, and all you can do is sit there and wonder where you went so wrong as you watch your city fall to the nuclear traffic timers appearing everywhere at once.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: Traffic management games are always so addictive, and Mini Motorways is no different. You're constantly trying to improve upon the city infrastructure, trying new city builds, newly received modules, newly unlocked cities, and so forth. The game is very challenging and rewarding, making you want to come back for more.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: This is an adorable, small city builder type game that makes its focus the roads (obviously). Simple mechanics, amazing background noise that helps you focus but makes you a little stressed at the same time, and an overall easily replay-able puzzle game that's unique every time you play it!BUT... I personally have to return this game. The map slowly expands as the round continues, and adds more buildings and houses. The devs accomplished this very elegantly by making the map expand super slowly as the game goes on, almost unnoticeable. I noticed it because I got dizzy while playing it... a real shame honestly, I loved this...
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: Mini Motorways feels so similar to Mini Metro yet has so much more going for it. Like Mini Metro, you could play for hours as every game and location feels different and you ever strive to beat your high score in each city. You have the freedom to plan efficient road systems: utilising roundabouts, traffic lights and motorways to keep traffic moving. Challenge mode adds 2 or 3 unique 'scenarios' in each city to tackle with wildcards that keep game play interesting. The design is so simplistic and elegant and soundtracks in each city add a subtle backdrop to your infrastructure planning.Seriously addictive, would definitely recommend, especially if you like Mini Metro.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: A very good game to unwind to, even when you're at 2.5k+ points and all the shops are organizing a riot. The perfect blend of relaxing and chaotic that's honestly hard to find anywhere else. It also really makes you appreciate city planners lol.Not that hard of a game, unless you're aiming for some ridiculously high scores, which then you have to learn niche strategies on how to manipulate spawns and car behaviour. Best played with one game per session, in my opinion. At the end of every game, you'll most likely be mildly angry after whatever catastrophic planning made you lose. Playing several games consecutively *will* make that anger mount.Regardless, I highly recommend this game, even as a little thing to just play once in a while.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely delightful! The visuals and sound design manage to turn nightmarish traffic into relaxing beauty. The lil' honking cars are adorable, and everything bleeps and bloops as your city hums along.The game is simple enough that you can easily play it while watching something in the background, yet there's enough depth and strategy here to be quite interesting.Definitely worth the asking price!
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: It sounds counter intuitive but I play this game just to de-stress. You'd think having to manage a bunch of roads and the vehicles commuting on them would be a stressful situation but in the beginning its nice to watch your small city work in total harmony. But as your suburban sprawl starts and more pick-up points arrive you begin to wonder how to solve your worsening traffic situations. Do you use lights, roundabouts, bridges, tunnels, or motorways...many of them are just a quick fix for a bad situation and as you watch your daily commutes rise and rise you wonder what its really like out there where you can simply walk away after your city has imploded.It's a lot of fun and when you start getting into the thousands of commutes on some of these games after learning the ropes its always fun to brag to your friends about just how many rides you're able to get done before your city succumbs to failure.The daily and weekly challenges are great fun too!
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: This game starts off fun and relaxing but really becomes stressful as your city grows. The game play mechanics are really flawed and ultimately you will always fail. Your final score really rely's heavily on 50% skill and 50% luck of the draw where buildings are randomly placed. When you do notice traffic issues you literally have very minimal time to correct them. Sure you can pause the game but by then if there is a timer on the building it's already to late because making road adjustments takes a minute to take effect. Also, if you don't have the part you need like a road, bridge or highway the game can literally be over for you within a minute because the timers move so fast. Another thing I really dislike is If you don't preemptively place a roundabout you will most likely get blocked later in the game because a house was put there. This can really be a game stopper because you can't correct the traffic problem and you don't get extra traffic control objects to place. If your thinking of getting this game I would catch it on sale...imo its not worth more than 5 dollars.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: If you are missing the road on your day off, or during some family holidays check out Mini Motorways! I gurantee you that you will be swearing on "other" drivers in no time even tho you give them the best roads you can ;-)Jokes aside, Mini Motorways is a fine tactical building game, that keeps your planing skills awake. It is very easy to handle, play and understand - even my senior father was able to play for hours after a 3 minutes introduction to the handling. The grafics are pleasant and simple, it is not overloaded yet well made and has its own finesse with the possibillities to play in dark mode maps as well as rainbow explosion if you prefer that. Mini MOtorways gurantees dozens of hours quick gameplay and is perfect as a go to in between game to relax and get your mind off things for a few minutes!Check it out!
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: I'm glad others can enjoy this game. This is not for me. I prefer planning-style gameplay, or having access to tools that mitigate bad RNG.If you enjoy reactionary puzzles, this game is for you. I could see tetris players getting a kick out of it.If you came into this thinking mini cities skylines, you're going to be stressed out and frustrated.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely addicting game perfect to just get lost in for an hour or so each day. Daily challenges keep it interesting, although things like that aren't what will keep you coming back - it's the satisfying sound design, sleek art style, and rewarding mental stimulation that comes with keeping your city in check. Post metropolitan collapse, you will reflect on the myriad of choices you made and debate which one was the decision that led to your cities demise. Then you will try again...and again, and again.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: For me this game has a perfect balance between strategy and simplicity. It's easy to learn, and has a very minimal interface with simple controls.However, that doesn't mean it's easy to play, you still have to plan ahead, and keep up with all the buildings all the time, and in my opinion they appear just at the right pace. The game is fast enough so you won't get bored, but is still forcing you to take your time and rethink your strategy every now and then.And the game has a lot more to offer, so I highly recommend to try it out for yourself and see.Couple of things I would like to see added:- Having the option to zoom in on the action, and see whats behind a motorway- A control-z key bind, to revert roads etc.- A bigger popup when buildings appear
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: I like the minimalist approach to the game and the simple dynamic of connecting like colors together (cars with destinations)  The Highway system is a neat new addition.  Fun, casual and entertaining.  But frustrating.What I don't like are the following.1.)  No casual mode.2.)  No option to have infinite resources (i.e. roundabouts, bridges, traffic lights and roads) in order to build the dream metropolis.3.)  An algorithm that always (and I mean, in my experience, always) places destinations in the exact location and/or configuration that is THE LEAST advantageous (i.e. the worst possible position) for your game.  It doesn't matter what you planned for, the game mucks your plans up.4.)  No option or ability to alter the location of the new buildings (or even their orientation in relation to the map) to the best of my knowledge.5.)  No divided roadway option to allow two lanes on either side of the median.  (Wider roads, less congestion?  Who hasn't driven in a city and knows the advantages in that?)6.)  No public transportation options (maybe as a passive upgrade to remove some of the congestion?  Trolley cars?  Buses?)I'll keep playing because I do like the game (and want to like it more) but it is frustrating for a casual gamer who wants a session of, well,  casual gaming that will take up less than an hour of my time only to realize that 3 frustrating games later  that 2 hours have passed and I'm pissed at the game for not giving me the options to chose the configuration that I want to play in.Please look into these comments and turn an okay game I want to like into a great game I play all the time.UPDATED REVIEW:  This is a BAD GAME designed to beat you, not to challenge you.  I'd like my money back.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: My my, what a fantastic game.I am very biased when it comes to this game, as I absolutely love roads and transportation in general. So, obviously I am going to recommend this game. This game has amazing graphics (neat, minimalist art style), great gameplay (hard af but keeps you hooked. aka easy to learn but hard to master), and overall a game that shows how much effort was put into it. _childDocuments_.review: Well, the two games Dinosaur polo Club released are Mini Metro and Mini Motorways.Mini Metro is about trains, Mini Motorways is about cars.The sounds and art are of similar to Mini Metro. Your mission is simple.Build a road system and connect the same colour of a house to the same colour of shop.I have waited this game since it is out in Sep 2019 but i do not have apple product. And today, at last, i got a hand on this game. Thanks Dinosaur Polo Club for releasing this on Steam. I have been playing "Freeways" on Android but the UI is terrible, not visually friendly and game-play not as in depth as compared to this.My first try score for all the maps are about at an average of 1500+.I though it is easy but i cannot even reach score of 2000, which some of them in Youtube Videos can scored so much more, 4000-6000.Comparing this with Mini Metro. I felt this has greater flexibility and strategy.It seems easy on video but it is not. The difficult part is the direction of entrance the shops spawn. A difficult spawn is the entrance is opposite of the house, meaning you have to place roads circling around the shop before connecting the house. It wastes road tiles, which are limited, and time to travel which takes slight longer.This games put strategy on these 4 big focus, well-mixed - "Intersections", "Limited road tiles", "Fastest route - based on road type and angles of entry", "Randomly spawned supply and demands". Clever and smart of you developing a perfect solution for these focuses will score yourself high.As in-game weeks get by, more and more random houses and shops spawn at random locations, which can be a motorway nightmare. It is because you unintended create more intersections to cut across from house the destination. Intersections can build up traffics. The more intersections you have, the slower the cars move.Roundabout is good for certain limit of cars, it travels in a slightly smoother and faster then normal intersections. However, once traffics build up, the roundabout cannot magically save you. Therefore, you would need to adjust your roads from time to time to be even more efficient.Motorways/highways can magically helps you to link the furthest house to furthest shop. It can be placed almost anywhere, saving you the bridges, road tiles, and tunnels you may need. But this magical motorway is so limited that you get this bonus motorway once in few weeks.Car travels through the shortest route. Linking your house to shop in the shortest way can relief the demand build up in the shops. Can't get fast enough due to traffic build up or a longer travel route will result in game over, because the demand of those shops will increase as time goes by.I am a fan of cities skylines because of how traffic behaves. I would say this game is the "Causal Cities Skylines without zoning". You can't demolish building, you have limited road types, and I would not say the AI of path-finding is perfect, but it is sufficient to grab your attention of how well and smooth the cars react dynamically. A single lanes two way roads is good because it leans more to strategy puzzle. Some mentioned adding a "One way road" is good - agreed. Some suggested 4 lanes/6 lanes (two way) road - i don't think is a good idea as this game meant to be causal. It will certainly increase the length of the game, which make it easier by having wider roads and limited cars (each house is 2 cars).The price of this game i would consider affordable based on the level of depth and simulation it provides.Good job in creating this. Mini Metro is a hit. Mini Motorways is a better hit. What's next? Mini Air-Traffic-Control?I look forward, maybe few years time, another sequel from Dinosaur Polo Club because i know you guys are full of creativity and ideas.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked Mini Metro very much and I like this game, too. But!The game doesn't run on my iMac, though it claims it has Mac support. It shows me color black and nothing more. Looking closely I realise that the game has ridiculously high minimum requirements for such simple graphics. It's illogical and it's misleading (especially when the previous game - Mini Metro - works just fine on the same mac). I'm not refunding (it's too late for that) and I have a way of occasionally playing it on another PC, but I bought it specifically to play on my mac instead of Mini Metro, and I just can't.(And, btw, the tutorial is either glitchy or too slow or maybe illogical).P.S.: This was a positive review, and now it's not, because there's no way the game will ever launch on my iMac, given the shaders it uses, and I feel cheated.

It can be a little frustrating, if you go down the wrong track with roads and upgrades, and end up with an unplayable situation, but I guess that's the game.  it has pretty good sounds, and graphics, while simple, accomplish their purpose.  Pick it up cheap, and it's good for 5 to 10 hours of entertainment.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: A devious little puzzle game were you're handed a small plot of land with office buildings and homes, you use roads and various traffic circulation tools to keep the work from piling up. But as time progresses, the play area enlarges and you receive more and more pieces; more Office buildings appear, more homes, and more roads and such to connect them. The complexity of your city grows and grows and it's up to you to keep things smooth! It's great in small bursts, and undeniably replayable!
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: Deceptively simple, turned highly addictive. While I by no means have anywhere near top scores on any of the maps, I am steadily improving my strategies and gaining more trips each play through. _childDocuments_.review: Mini Motorways is quite a surprising arcade simulation game. The gameplay is easy to get into, and it has a nice balance with the pace of the action in each map you play on.The randomness of each playthrough is a nice touch, with both the special pieces you get at regular intervals, and the houses and destinations that spawn on the map. And it provides a nice variety of maps to play, especially with the extra ones added in and the extra challenge modes you can do on themThe game's graphical presentation is quite nice - like the dark mode setting you can put it to - and I also like the daily and weekly challenges you can do which add interesting restrictions to playing specific maps in the game. _childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games for when you have nothing too do and need something quick to play or when you are just thinking of another game too play. This game has many advantages without too many disadvantages. Its simple and fun with a lot of under the roots strategy too it.This game is fun for any range of gamer, even the app player that is wanting to break into PC gaming. It takes little thinking if you just want to play for fun, but can take a lot of thinking when it comes too wanting to play for the high score, making it great for most anyone. There is not much of a learning curve to be honest so it makes a game that you can have as a avid player that averages half of the hours your main games play. I do not play it a lot, its something I only play about a hour at a time, but that is also something that makes it fun for me is I do not feel the need to rake hours upon hours into it, it just happens with time. Overall as a easy and cheap indy styled game, I rank it a solid 8.5/10If I was too give it one negative thing, I wish it had multiple difficulty settings, nothing too strenuous, just a easy and pro mode, so people that do not ever want to be good enough to really get past the 4k mark can be seperate from the players that aim for 10-20+k.

_childDocuments_.review: i love the soothing aesthetics.the game is tiny but has been polished to perfection.but the gameplay to me is just too annoying.everything is random. there is no way to plan anything ahead and you will just have to react to newly spawned houses. there is no way to reliably beat level goals. they only thing you can do is proactively trying to block areas with roads so nothing can spawn there. i dislike this design pattern. at the same time everything looks the same and theres basically no variance in level design except some differing obstacles.you will also put yourself at a disadvantage if you try to design aesthetically pleasing cities since the amount of roadpieces are limitedi'm not a big fan of these super short gameplay sessions of 10-20 minutes just to start over again without having any meta progression.maybe it's my own fault for not researching more about the game before buying it. i thought it would be more akin to factorio, which it is most definitely not at all. it's just a flash roguelite minigame.what annoyed me the most is that the way cars move does not make sense at all.they always take the shortest route, meaning trying to add alternative roads to circumvent clogged roads does not work.

The commuters also don't seem to pathfind around heavy traffic, which seems a bit lacking.  Otherwise, a very fun game.  Hopefully DPC will fix these issues in the near future.Also, on the off chance that someone from their team reads this, I have two recommendations:1) Please add Workshop support eventually as you did with Mini Metro.2) Consider allowing the use of bridges to cross over roads without creating an intersection. _childDocuments_.review: There are more than a handful of minimalist puzzle games out there. With so many, it can be difficult to tell the difference between one that is ‘minimalist’ because the developer didn’t care and one that is minimalist because it’s part of the overall design and intended aesthetic. Greater still is the gulf between whether they’re worth playing or not. Since you’ve probably seen the “Overwhelmingly Positive” label, I think you already know, this isn’t one of those ‘minimalist’ bargain bin games you get in a bundle and never install. This is good.Abbreviated Review: Mini Motorways takes after its predecessor, Mini Metro, in delivering a simplistic set of visuals that convey all of the information necessary and little else. The presentation is similar to that of Google maps without the satellite view. A simple white (or dark gray) background with easily discernible roads and a collection of colorful buildings make up the majority of the maps. The only exceptions are a slightly different shade for the impassable mountains and waterways.The game’s maps are meant to represent various major cities, but without any knowledge of the most basic geographies of these locations, it’s not really possible to tell. Water features and mountains will often be labeled for their real-life counterparts as well, though that doesn’t do much for me since I don’t know even vague details about the landscape of Munich or Rio de Janeiro. However, this design element is more for the distinction between the various levels rather than to make you say something like “I can see my house from here!” They could just as well be called City 1, City 2, etc.Yet, even with what would seem like a limitation, the design has a very welcoming appeal. It, of course, runs extremely smoothly on pretty much any PC it can be installed on, but it goes further. The way roads and features snap to the grid to round out corners while still giving you the dexterity to achieve your strategy is nearly flawless. Being able to quickly build, remove, and rebuild roads without being disoriented or overwhelmed by the way information is being presented ends up being a cornerstone of what makes the gameplay work.The core of Mini Motorways gameplay is getting vehicles to their desired location efficiently and effectively. It’s that simple. “Stores” pop up and produce little icons. Houses pop up with two cars ready to head over there and take one of those icons away. If the store produces too many icons without being picked up, it starts a 30-second timer that, when complete, will end your run. All you have to do is connect the houses and the stores and let the cars do the work.This works beautifully at first, but soon cars clog the streets and inhibit one another from getting where they need to go. That’s when you have to come in with traffic lights and roundabouts to make intersections less congested and keep cars moving. Motorways are your strongest tool as they are highways that rise above all of the detritus of roads, buildings, and the chaos they perpetuate – plus cars go faster on them. These, along with the obvious bridges and tunnels to get around and through obstacles are the only tools you need (and have) to keep things running smoothly.However, none of that will carry you very far without the proper strategy. This is where I had some learning to do. At first, I was attempting to build numerous roads and intersections as if everything needed to be interconnected. It wasn’t (too) long before I figured out that you only need to connect similarly colored houses and their corresponding destinations. Even within that, it’s best to avoid connecting extra houses that fit that criteria because it could contribute to extra traffic. Not to mention it may be beneficial to connect those extra houses elsewhere.These concepts along with the randomized nature of building spawns lead to a game that is not only quite deep but very replayable. The result is always going to be a score – whether good or bad. The goal, of course, is to get one as high as possible, but upon reaching 1,000 in each city, you unlock challenges for each. Challenges present the same basic gameplay but put twists in with the nature of traffic, the tools you have available, or the way they work. Each creates just enough variety to make it worth diving back in several times.Along with the unlocks, scores are also tracked via leaderboards. They’re not only available for each map’s general gameplay mode, but the daily, weekly, and map-specific challenges as well. These are complete with global and friend list boards as well as graphs to drive home where you land in the hierarchy of traffic managers.Mini Motorways does an exceptional job of delivering a thoroughly interactive and strategic experience within its minimalist design. It’s easy to pick up but has enough depth and mechanics to learn about to keep you playing for hours. Challenges add another layer of difficulty that can be enjoyable, but striving to try and reach the upper echelons of high scores has been plenty of motivation for me thus far. As the developers add more maps, modes, and quality of life features (like an improved colorblind mode), I’ll continue to revisit this game and recommend it to anyone who wants something easy on the eyes but hard on the spatial reasoning portion of the brain.

_childDocuments_.review: Thank you for this addictive game. I've been playing Mini Motorways on my channel for about 1 year before it was released on Steam and I got addicted to it. Now that is came on PC with some really cool upgrades such as Roundabouts, I love the game even more.If you like these type of city builder games or more like traffic management games, than Mini Motorways is a must play
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: I play this game right before bed after a long day at work. It's just enough puzzle solving to keep me engaged but is simple, soothing, and just right to end the day off. Because of the randomization of zoning, even playing the same map over and over provides new challenges - the dailies and weeklies are fun to do as well! There's really nothing bad about this game and I can only imagine that if someone were to not like it, it's more because they don't like the genre rather than this game itself.

_childDocuments_.review: Not only is this game addictive and fun to play but the developers who made it are a collection of the most down-to-earth, honest and caring people I have ever had the pleasure of meeting. I own both of their games and they are the perfect mix of chill and stressful. Recommend the purchase while it is on launch special.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: Starts simple and gets satisfying complex. Simple rules make the gameplay easier to manage at high levels. Just get cars from X to Y. You may find yourself in impossible situations at times, which will end a run, but careful selection of your tools (highways, bridges) can avoid certain traps once you know what to look for.Relaxing. Has night mode. A round lasts as long as a typical roguelike run, maybe 20-60 minutes depending on your level of success.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: very fun game, but very very buggy at the moment. probably best to wish-list it and come back in a month or two when the devs have sorted it out.just off the top of my head: ive had problems with getting stuck in loading screens, having the game tell me i have 1 or 2 roads, but being unable to use them until i restart the game. issues with not being able to rotate building entrances until restarting game, issues with the drawing roads being sluggish and unresponsive until restart.from what ive heard, the non-PC versions of the game are even worse when it comes to bugs.im enjoying it a lot, but the full price seems a bit steep when its not very polished and ive had this many bugs in under 24hrs.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: I am now 43 years old and have been playing games now 40 of those years. I won't lie, new games find it a tough call to give me a shred of interest these days. However, you get the odd good egg that comes along and keeps me hooked and this is one of them. A very nice "Zen Feel" to the game, nice graphics, cute sounds and above all the playability. For the price I would snap this up instantly.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: "Spirtual Successor" to the amazing Mini Metro, Mini Motorways is again another puzzle/strategy game that each level / instance you play can be played in ~10-20 minutes. Overall if you enjoy the genre, you will enjoy the game - there are a few minor quirks around the UI that need some minor tweaks (game was first launched on iPad) but those things shouldn't stop you from buying this, as the support on Mini Metro was amazing so I expect small issues to be quickly fixed along with new (free) levels (cities) if it follows Mini Metro's support schedule.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: I hyper-fixated on the game and got about 1000 on each map (as of 8/6/2021). Easy game to melt time away and fascinate yourself every time you find a new optimization. This game is great if you have a day to kill or a few minutes. And the art style doesn't take a dent in colorblind or dark mode so your eyes can take a break while playing! Pick up this game if you can, especially the Miniverse Bundle if you have an extra few dollars laying around
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun, but there are a few things that could be improved. New houses that are unused should constantly blink so you know that you haven't connected them. At some point the map becomes bigger and it's hard to see what roads you demolish and what you build, so if you could zoom in to confirm that you've done the correct changes..
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't a road/city management sim. This is a score attack puzzler with random elements based around traffic management.One of the best casual "time-waster" games out there. I'd play this over the hyper-casual crap on mobile stores any day of the week.If you're achievement hunting on this game: slow & steady wins the race for the 2,000 score achievements.Pop on an album while you're at it, as it usually took me 40 minutes to get 2,000 score on a level.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motorways

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't sure if I genuinely love this game or because my obsession of putting things in order compels me to this game.One thing is for sure, this game is the reverse of stages of grief. You start with the acceptance that you're playing another game, again. Then you've become depressed when somehow a structure decides to spawn after you managed to put everything in order for quite some time. You were bargaining, crossing your fingers, offering road tiles so that the next spawn will be at a better place, only to be angered by "why the eff this color spawned right on the center where it has nowhere to go???" at the end of the game, you'll be in denial just how the unbelievably absurd it is to shut down a city just because one car didn't make it through.

Have you ever been stuck in traffic and wished you could do something to fix it?

In Mini Motorways, the city's traffic problems are in your hands.

From the makers of Mini Metro, Mini Motorways is a game about drawing the roads that drive a growing city. Build a road network, one road at a time, to create a bustling metropolis.
