name: Men of War II
detailed_description: FRONTLINE HERO PACK The Frontline Hero Pack provides any true fan of Men of War II with the following perks: • 2 exclusive profile badges and 6 exclusive avatars to make sure you stand out from the crowd • Instant unlock* of 4 collectible tank units to use in multiplayer matches • 10 beautiful desktop wallpapers The Frontline Hero Pack instantly unlocks the following collectible units*: • M4A3E8 “Sherman” o A US Army medium tank, the latest modification of the M4A3E8 with a 75mm gun. It is a beautiful, but deadly war machine with a unique camouflage design, pin-up art, and decorative exterior elements. • Panther Ausf. A o A German medium tank, the latest modification of the Pz.Kpfw. V class with a 75mm gun. A formidable predator with excellent combat characteristics and unique camouflage, capable of intimidating even experienced hunters on the battlefield. • T-34-85 o A Soviet medium tank, the latest modification of the T-34 class with an 85mm gun. It can hold its own and emerge victorious from any battle, since it features a unique camouflage system that distinguishes it from its brothers on the battlefield. In the right hands, it can become a deadly threat to any enemy. • T-34-85M o Soviet medium tank, the latest modification of the T-34 class with an 85mm gun. It features a modified camouflage design and spaced armor which reduces the destructive effect of anti-tank rounds. This is an experienced fighter, ready for any surprises. *all units are available for unlocking via in-game actions as well. About the Game Experience World War II real-time strategy gameplay like never before! Men of War II, the new chapter in the evolution of the top-rated RTS franchise, brings you an unprecedented number of units with different specializations to command, unyielding attention to historical fidelity, new levels of visual and audio excellence, as well as advanced enemy AI. Lead your troops in intense real-time battles on the Western and Eastern Fronts and overwhelm your opponents in epic narrative single-player campaigns and skirmish modes before diving deep into the multiplayer action. Utilize sophisticated military strategies, lay ambushes, capture enemy vehicles or weapons, and show your ability as the greatest military leader of all time. Attain full command of different roles: from Artillery and Armor to Infantry and Support. Blast entire buildings to smithereens or construct fortifications to reshape the battlefield - from trenches and dugouts to bunkers and minefields. Use the Direct Control feature to precisely manage any single unit on the field at any time. Dive deep into classical combat mechanics combined with all-new gameplay features and experience the intensity of one of the longest-running series of WWII games in an exciting new way. Men of War II also boasts a staggering breadth of gameplay options: whether you prefer a realistic take on World War II strategy typical for previous entries in the franchise or enjoy a more casual experience; the captivating stories of narrative campaigns or experimenting with different tactics in ever-changing dynamic modes; challenging other commanders in ranked matches or customizing every detail of each battle in a lobby, Men of War II offers an astounding amount of content to sate your thirst for battle. Experience epic stories told in three narrative campaigns — lead the desperate Soviet defense against the initial brutal onslaught on the Eastern Front; become a US commander in Normandy, having to improvise with limited resources and adapt to unfamiliar ground, in order to overcome the Nazi war machine; or step into the shoes of an old, disillusioned Wehrmacht officer on the retreat to Berlin, inadvertently delaying the defeat of the regime he himself hates. Enjoy a more open experience as you take on Historical Campaigns inspired by the Soviet Operation Bagration and the US Operation Overlord with customizable battalion setups and strategies, or the endless possibilities of the fully dynamic Conquest campaign and the skirmish-like Raids, where no two playthroughs are ever the same. Jump into the biggest and most varied multiplayer mode in franchise history and challenge other players in clashes ranging from 1v1 to 5v5; command a specialized Battalion and find the right synergy with your team-mates; take a more generalist approach with Combined Arms or lead all your nation’s units in the Classic Mode, resembling the Men of War: Assault Squad 2 experience. Take competition to the next level in Match-making and Leagues, tweak a wide range of options in custom Lobbies, or play any part of the single-player content in co-op with up to 4 other players. From nigh-indestructible tanks, devastating artillery, and nimble airplanes to realistic models of infantry armament and military equipment, Men of War II features the most extensive and highly detailed WWII locations, vehicles, and characters roster in the series to date: three armies, 45 customizable battalions, and close to 400 different units await your commands. Experience the classical theater of war from a new perspective: every location comes to life with a unique set of fully destructible objects, realistic physics, and immersive sound design. Men of War II takes audio-visual excellence to a new level for the series, with native support for up to 4K resolution and ultra-wide, 21:9 aspect ratio, Physically Based Rendering, and other enhancements. At the same time, the game’s engine takes full advantage of 64-bit, multithreading processing to ensure the best possible optimization and smooth experience even on lower-spec PCs. Veterans of the series will enjoy the myriad of detailed settings and tweaks available to create a gameplay experience tailored exactly to their liking, with options ranging from turning various UI elements on or off, to the amount of Command Points and Manpower resource available in a match; while others will appreciate the possibility to just jump into a quick match-making battle or use a pre-set roster of units in a mission with no hassle. Create and share your own war scenarios using a special level design and modding toolset for Men of War II, fully integrated with Steam Workshop. Now the choices are up to you: your creativity; your vision; your skills. The tactical possibilities are endless.

_childDocuments_.review: Listen, GOH is good. So is MOWAS2. But honestly despite being constantly online, Men of War 2 is the best single player experience you'll get between MOW2, GOH and MOWAS2. MOWAS2 campaign is just a copy and paste for each nation and GOH is locked with two factions (two more with two seperate DLCs). If you want to play for a singleplayer then play MOW2. If you want to mess around with the editor and/or PVP get GOH2. This game really isnt as bad as people claim, I have played the soviet and american campaigns, both are decent, the soviet campaign being better with the choise of what battalions you want to bring onto the field. Half way through the german campaign right now and its alot grittier than both the soviet and american campaign so far. I'd probably say this game is just that tiny bit better than any other game in the franchise. Sure, alot more arcadey but the fact that you can build trenches and fortify buildings without you having to babysit your soldiers 24/7 to make sure they are actually firing at approaching enemies instead of breaking their spines in 90 degree angles is extremely refreshing.Lowkey dont under stand why people are complaining about it being arcadey. The entire franchise is arcade compared to graviteam or steel division 2, which is fine and which is what makes it fun. Men of war will never be realistic seeing how the best way to play is to just grab one dude and make him a ninja with grenades. People are mistaking realism for historical accuracy- which- once again- men of war will never be with such a small scale battles and grenade ninjas running around.

_childDocuments_.review: MoW II took a bit of a detour from its older siblings, causing the hardcore, milsim, ultra-realistic fans to have a meltdown. Their complaints are like a loud, annoying alarm clock—valid, but way too much noise for what it is. Just hit the snooze button on them.If you ever played the CoH series and wished it had fewer cartoony explosions and more tactical depth, MoW II is your jam. In multiplayer, you won't be drowning in units like in Steel Division. It's more like a cozy squad meet-up than an army convention.Sure, there's a healthy dose of jank, but the game dishes out enough cool mechanics to keep you hooked. Every match feels like a fresh adventure rather than the same old rerun.One of the standout features is the direct control of (pretty much) any unit. This is a lifesaver since the AI's pathing skills are about as sharp as a marshmallow.Infantry might seem squishy, but they can sneak up on tanks like a ninja at a sumo match. Once they dig in, good luck getting them out. Alone, they’re like popcorn—fun but not filling. But pair them with mechanized units, artillery, or air support, and they turn into a full-course meal.Tanks are like goldfish in a bowl—beautiful but fragile. Get too close to infantry and they'll chuck AT grenades and bazookas at you faster than you can say "kaboom." Get spotted, and it’s raining hellfire. And if you're out-tiered, your shells will bounce off the enemy like rubber balls while they one-shot you back to the stone age. Each tank has its role: heavy tanks sit back and snipe, while the nimble ones dance with the infantry.Artillery is a high-stakes game of cat and mouse. You've got to juggle hitting priority targets, dodging counter-battery fire, and launching your own counter-attacks. Fire too much and you'll light up the map like a Christmas tree; fire too little, and your teammates will be the ones getting pounded. Get it just right, and you’re the cat's pajamas.Air units are simpler. Think small planes, big planes, small bombs, big bombs, rockets, and mean meat bags. The catch? Any AA around and you'll lose the gravity war real quick.There are also special units like saboteurs, officers, artillery spotters, and more, but those mechanics are a bit of a mystery (aka I don't fully get them either).So, if you want a game that mixes strategy with a bit of unpredictability and doesn’t take itself too seriously, MoW II is your go-to. Just watch out for those hardcore fans—they bite.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is judged harshly by veterans of the predecessors (Men of War, Men of War: Assault Squad 2, recently Gates from Hell: Ostfront) while it is actually  trying to revive the RTS genre by attracting (new and former) players for micromanagement-heavy gameplay. I personally loved Assault Squad 2 and GoH: Ostfront.  But I have been a former player! I just don’t have the time anymore to invest hours into a super-realistic game and effectively nothing exciting might happen during that time. 😜 Hyperrealism is wonderful and challenging. If you still want tactical depth while expecting exciting situations in most battles you play and a well-crafted feeling of continuous progression on the map and between game modes, you might like MoW2 a lot. I do.
_childDocuments_.name: Men of War II

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a fun war game, not quite as complex as Gates of Hell, but more so than Company of Heroes 3. There is quite a bit of single player content here including a story campaign, historical campaign, dynamic campaign, and a random generated missions mode. The dynamic campaign is the really interesting part here. You pick an army, have a tech tree you can upgrade and choose places on a map to attack/defend with either your infantry, artillery, or armor battalions. You customize each battalion with things you have unlocked through the tech tree. Its slightly more robust than the version in Gates of Hell. All of these are apparently co-op as well. Multiplayer is a lot of fun 5v5 mode where you try to move the front line in your favor using either an infantry, armor, or artillery battalion like in the dynamic campaign. There's some unlocks here in the form of different kinds of battalions that you can earn either in single player or multi. There are some bugs, but i haven't found anything game breaking yet, just some weird path finding and some missions having enemies that are stuck so I had to go search for them. Nothing that won't be fixed over time.
_childDocuments_.name: Men of War II

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a Men of War franchise player since Soldiers: Heroes of World War II in 2004. Men of War: Assault Squad 2 is still one of my all-time favorite games. I was absolutely delighted to see when this game dropped on Steam. Sadly, it's been painful for me to even get to the 30 minute mark with the pure arcade gameplay.  What killed it for me almost immediately is artillery with nearly 100% accuracy, where your soldiers mean nothing and you simply just Zerg rush objectives with riflemen and replace them. I can almost get over the hitpoints on tanks, but I will never get over the always online gameplay. This is how you encourage more sea faring activities, where it doesn't pay to actually support the developer when they don't respect their audience. I give this a solid 3 out of 10 for game play and a nice 8/10 for upgraded graphics.
_childDocuments_.name: Men of War II

_childDocuments_.review: 1. First of all, can I have a full view mode in single player game instead of only having my unit views? One of my greatest pleasure of this game is to see units from all sides moving on the entire map. 2. The vehicle HP is a really, really stupid idea. Let's face it, no one gonna even enjoy multiple player game with it, which seems to be the original idea. For those who playing PVE (which is most of your customers), it is pure shortcoming, literally not a single merit of it.  3. The different PVE modes is confusing for new players, and lack of guidance. The rules under "I" icon does not help at all. It takes me an hour to figure out how to get my units selected, unlocked, put on, and start a combat. All in all, I have watched game testing videos since last year, many productive suggestions have been given by gamer, and sadly none of them are implemented. My suggestion is: drop your crazy obsession about PvP, the studio is clearly not good at it. Do what you did best on "red tide", "redemption", "assault squat 1, 2", explore more on PVE modes. Seeing this studio struggling on multiplayer RTS is like watching CA making its stupid FPS game. Remember this, for this game, PVP mode will only get better if it start having good PVE experiences.
_childDocuments_.name: Men of War II

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played the old MoW games, but I am really liking this one. Not entirely sure what all the fuss is about. The gameplay is punishing, but you start to get the hang of it after a few hours. I highly recommend playing the tutorials first before play otherwise you are just NOT gonna understand how to play this game and get pulverized. My only complaint about the game is the graphics seem very mid and the pathfinding can be wonky at times. Sometimes my vehicles just start to move unbelievably slowly when they get too close to rock outcroppings. Forces me sometimes to manually control them to get them out.Also, the rocket artillery in this game is f***ing awesome!
_childDocuments_.name: Men of War II

_childDocuments_.review: Best current WWII RTS game at the moment, hands down.  Much more realistic gameplay than COH2/COH3, without the painful micromanaging of gates of hell (I still like it though too) - I think its a really good mix of realism / gameplay.Factions are more or less balanced with counters on every side (there are some rough spots like artillery accuracy, but for a first run at balance its suprisingly good.)  Gone are the days of King Tigers showing up in COH2 and everyone GG's - all sides have a fighting chance.  Great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Men of War II

_childDocuments_.review: For me its very good game, especially on tactical level you cant just chage frontally or roll over with your tanks, you have to be smart and plan your steps.Yes of course the game have its minor minuses - like in one of the dialogs they say "russian" tankmen, which by this time no one would say rather would use "soviet", soldiers look bit plastic and etc. But i am sure the team will work to make the game even better.If you are interested in the single play as me you will find variety of missions and interesting gameplay that is worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Men of War II

_childDocuments_.review: Been looking forwards to this game for a long time, and despite what a lot of these reviews seem to say, I believe this game is incredible.  The devs have been nothing but kind in the community discord, responding quickly and letting us know they are actively working to resolve issues players are encountering.  We are only around 48 hours post-launch right now, and they have already rolled out a sizable patch.  I absolutely cannot wait to see where this game goes in the near future, especially with modding which they have made a priority.  In the meantime though, I am having an absolute blast playing the different campaigns and modes in both PVE and PVE.  Keep it up y'all, I forsee myself playing this game for years!

_childDocuments_.review: honestly i think the game is alright after you look past just all the reviews ad ♥♥♥♥ talking of the game. This game is not gates of hell so don't expect it to be. It has its own quirks and gates of hell has its own. yes their is a couple things like costing cp to re man your own stuff that i really don't like or the overall cp you have in other game modes but the game is not bad. personally i prefer vehicles to not have health bars but having health bars does not make the game terrible. _childDocuments_.review: If you loved the original game's from the franchise you might be slightly let down here.While its most definitely an improvement visually, there's quite a lot that feels like its been dumbed down to suit the company of heroes player base rather than any hardcore lovers of the originals.The fact i cant play the campaigns with realistic mode is heart breaking as that was always how i played the rest of the franchise. I do recommend this game however, i recommend you go in with an open mind for what you expect from a MoW game as its very much different now.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me tell you this. Don't care about negative comments. Experience for yourself is the most accurate. Personally, I played and felt through just 1 word. It's addiction. The game offers a lot of content for you to explore from single-player to multiplayer. And I quite like the 1x1, 2x2, 3x3, 4x4 and 5x5 pvp modes, or the very attractive PVE coordination mode. I recommend you to play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: MENU DESIGN: The main menu feels like it was designed in 2005 with it's UI, and many buttons do not have tool tips so you won't know what game mode you'll be playing until you launch it. The "Conquest" map is connected to the main menu which is nice and handy, but is not user friendly, it does not tell you how to move troops, get more troops, or that the map is horribly zoomed (at least for me) with no option to zoom out so only 10% of the map is visible.GRAPHICS: Did you like the graphics of 2010 RTS's? Well you're in luck, this game will bring you the 2010 graphics experience. CAMPAIGN: I only tried the first German mission before giving up. The game will use every single opportunity to tell you how unjust, bad and defeatist the Germans are.   -5 minutes of unskippable opening dialogue while waiting for a train to unload while German soldiers talk about how horrible    their superiors are and they fear for their life.   -You take the first objective and get reinforcements, but the reinforcements run away because if they help you they might get     executed by their commander.   -The first enemy units arrive and your own of officer runs and abandons you to the enemy.Keep in mind this is all within the first 15 minutes of gameplay.After that the mission broke because the AI just stopped pushing the objective I was supposed to defend and held it's ground at my first defensive line while infinite artillery shells were dropping from the sky randomly all around the objective. (I waited for about 30 minutes and the AI never pushed the objective I was supposed to defend while continuously shelling it)EXTRA: There is a direct control function, and you have infinite range with most weapons (huge plus over previous titles imo), however... if your weapon has a maximum range the only way to find out is to try and shoot it and see if it fires or says "Out of range" unlike previous games.

But after playing it for a while, I get the appeal. The game is very polished, and a completely different experience than Gates to Hell: Ostfront. I'll play em both for a different experience

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: If you're looking for a successor to Men of War: Assault Squad 2, play Call to Arms: Gates of Hell as it is by the same developer, Digitalmindsoft; stop bashing this game due to not meeting unrealistic expectations. This game has improved stability, better graphics, and new features such as: soldiers firing while moving, constructing defenses, and varied single-player content. However, it has a more tank-focused gameplay, smaller infantry squads, focus on spotters, and lacks a true combined arms experience.  If you're disappointed by these changes, this might not be the game for you.EDIT: 18OCT2024 - Open Beta for Offline update is live. They're keeping their promise. Also the classic modes return the fun of the combat/assault zones from the orignal MOW experience be sure to give that a chance. I will happily change this to "Recommended" once the developer delivers their promise of a offline single-player update.This game has a much different feel to it than the original Men of War (2008) which is what I'm going to be basing this on as that was the last release by Best Way.There have been significant improvements in the stability of the game engine. I have had 0 crashes with 5 missions completed in one session, and multiple sessions taken place over the last 2 days. My frame-rate is stable and I haven’t had any stuttering issues. I’m unsure why others are complaining about stability.Graphics are better than in previous titles; there are beautiful shadows and reflections. I also have had no artifacts.Other reviews have complained about reused assets, my question to them is why care? I’m sure the latest iteration of Call of Duty has recycled assets from previous titles. No one is seemingly complaining about that and just playing the game instead.Tank Health Point Bars; people must not have put any thought into the design of software systems. Everything is turned into math. There has to be a check at some point to know if something is considered broken. Whether the system be exposed or not is up to the developer. Health Points are on soldiers and no one is complaining about each soldier not having limb components that can be individually damaged. MOW2 still features component damage. I have had a single KV1 during a raid combat survive for countless shots because none of the German guns could penetrate the armor. In a lightly armored T-40; it kept getting pierced by the German Anti-Tank Rifles, but the tank still survived until my crew died due to the placement of the attacks. Did the HP bar matter? No. It seems to only matter when components of the tank are broken, or there is a critical hit on a key system such as an “ammo cache” or “fuel tank”.Soldiers now fire while moving now which helps to assault a position.Squad size, decreased from 8-10 to 5 soldiers on order which is painful when trying to assault/build out an effective defense. It takes minutes to order additional soldiers, the most you can get in a 2-minute period is 10. And with soldiers dropping with 1-2 shots from a single well placed heavy machine gun it's almost pointless to assault with infantry and a player should only advance with tanks assisted by long range of sight units such as snipers, or officers. This is my biggest complaint. When fighting it no longer feels like a true combined arms game and more of a tank battle with infantry as spotters. This has to be the biggest divergence from the original Men of War.Soldiers and support weapons can now make actual pillboxes, dig trenches, hasty positions, and foxholes, which majorly increase the survivability of an individual infantry unit. The camouflaging of tanks/emplacements has always been a thing.The front-line mechanic is a neat addition but it doesn’t really have a major effect to me beyond making an actual representation of something I already imagined in my head when playing the game. With all this said, this game definitely shifts the vision of Men of War towards a more tank focused combat and less combined arms experience. I personally don’t like the tank focus and would like a shift back to a more combined/infantry focus.And yes, before anyone comments on there being an infantry battalion and players focusing on their role. This make playing the single-player content painful as the AI doesn’t always assist where needed for supporting your tanks, and the tanks don’t support your infantry when needed. I personally always go with the tank focused approach as that had better results when I played due to the game seeming to favored tank combat + air support instead of a true combined arms approach.Please don't take this review the wrong way, there are many people who will enjoy this title such as myself. It's just such a different feel from other GEM engine experiences, that it's unfair to directly compare them due to different visions. All I'm trying to say is Star Wars(MOW2) is not trash just because you like Star Trek(GoH). Both are science fiction, but one is a Space Political Opera/Soft science while the other is a Space Exploration Drama/Harder science, different strokes for different folks.

_childDocuments_.review: Certainly! Here is the polished version of your text:---Unfortunately, I will keep playing Men of War Assault Squad 2 as this game isn't there yet. Hopefully, it will be soon!I've been playing the MOW series for around 12 years and have over 400 hours in Men of War Assault Squad 2 (MOWAS2), which I consider the best game in the series. The developers aimed to take the game to the next level with dynamic point tiers, macro strategies, specific unit investments, research, dynamic campaigns, and diverse game styles. However, they fell short and omitted some of the core features that made MOWAS2 one of the best RTS games, especially in the WWII genre.Here are my main concerns:1. Complicated Game Setup: In MOWAS2, starting a game was easy. You just chose a campaign, selected a map, and started. In the new game, the process is very confusing. You need to select a game style, a team based on a "speciality" card, and more. While it's great that the game has different single and multiplayer modes, I had to go online to figure out how to play a skirmish map. 2. Why fix what's NOT broken???:  Why is there no option to play a skirmish map like in MOWAS2? I understand the new features, but did you have to remove the system where we simply had points, spent them on units, and created huge armies? That was the main fun aspect of the game and it seems to be gone.3. Population Cap: One of the best things about MOWAS2 was the ability to build massive armies with dozens of tanks, artillery, and hundreds of infantry. This game has a population cap in every mode, which I found incredibly disappointing.4. Bugs and Lag: The game is laggy and has numerous bugs. In MOWAS2, even with a large number of troops, you wouldn't experience lag unless you used extreme cheats.My basic tips to improve the game:- Keep the exciting new features but don't exclude the core aspects that made the series great: easy access, simple skirmishes, and no population cap (or at least an option to disable it). Use a system similar to MOWAS2 where you earn points, bring in units, and progress. Nice and simple, but incredibly fun.- Simplify the menus and overall gameplay mechanics. While MOW has always been complex in strategy, its menus and game modes were user-friendly, unlike the current game.Until these issues are addressed, I'm afraid I will be uninstalling the game and play MOWAS2 and other RTS games. What a pity, I was incredibly excited and one of the gamers that purchased the game as soon at it came out (and I NEVER do this). Hopefully the developers will listen to the main asks of these feedback posts.

_childDocuments_.review: MEN OF WAR II i am definitely enjoying it and love the depth of detail such as every individual soldier having their own inventory and being able to dig trenches of different heights. Digging my first trench i accidentally made it so deep my soldiers could not get out of it ha ha. Being able to zoom in to a sweet up close ground level as well as first person views with increased detail seen is a exquisite sight to behold.The blood and gore is off the charts and very welcomed. I could not believe when i saw the blood flowing and the body parts flying everywhere sending a visceral adrenaline filled shock to my senses as i suddenly was taken to another level of battlefield realism. Also seeing soldiers dying and or slumping over after being caught in a explosion is very nice. The fast pace at which everything occurs is exhilarating capturing that hectic feel of battle. The amount of content is also incredible with Battalion Mode, PVP, PVE, the main campaign etc. The reinforcement timer is very well done adding to the tension and tactical thinking where troops have to last and not just thrown into a killing field to be slaughter. The long range combat element is a delight to behold giving that sense of death coming out of nowhere as well as concealment where the more you shoot the more likely you are to be revealed and open to enemy fire unless you periodically stop firing. Things like camouflage can help in staying hidden and in cover for a longer period allowing for an increased fire rate.As for as comparison to the previous game it is different for sure and much more hectic in a good way without feeling overwhelming while the previous games were a bit more slow paced and stealthy. Many people are calling MEN OF WAR II a hardcore version of COMPANY OF HEROES on steroids. There is also a classical mode i have not yet played which is supposed to be more like the previous games. The Devs are also planning to add a Offline Mode in a upcoming patch which am looking forward to since i only play single player.Pretty amazing to see two fantastic wargames come in the past two months with HEADQUARTERS WORLD WAR II (turn based) and MEN OF WAR II (real time). Happy days, happy days.MEN OF WAR II graphics are stunning and a visual joy to behold with sharp detailed models flowing with unit authenticity bringing the heroism and violent battlefield action of a 2024 war game in this incredible renaissance of our gaming hobby. Music and dialogue hits all the precision pin point tones of audio poetry inspiring wargamers to battle on as artillery screams thundering down with earth shattering death and bodies shredded in a furious fusillade of burning lead give out their last agonizing gasp.MEN OF WAR II, Buy it! Play it! Embrace a video game battlefield come to THRILLING BOMBASTIC EXPLOSIVE LIFE!!! like no MEN OF WAR game has ever before!!!

_childDocuments_.review: I appreciate the amount of content that is given on release. The game modes are really fun and unique (my favorite being conquest).When it comes to the gameplay, however, it needs some work, the vehicles move around too fast, taking turns too quickly and some even drive too fast for what they are, especially while carrying artillery. The infantry movement feels clunky. The game overall is too fast-paced. Seems to be aimed more towards an online competitive audience than a hardcore realistic one, which is honestly disappointing, and I hope they aim to change that and slow the game down a little or implement a game mode that changes these things.The game play isn't the only issue, though the voice acting is weak if not cringe, even the sound of the game overall (artillery engine's guns ect) is lacks luster to say the lease and the Ingame UI/HOTBAR needs some work as well.It's not all bad, though the menu UI is amazing, the tech trees are fun and the game is rewarding for unlocking new units as you go along, and the gamemodes are by far the best part. But as it stands right now, I can't recommend it as the type of player that I am. They're trying to mesh the grand scale battle hardcore realism with competitive/casual fast-paced RTS gameplay, but they don't do it really well. As of right now, I'd say just go play the gates of hell if that's what you're looking for.I am hopeful for this game though and will continue to support it in hopes they will make it into something better.

_childDocuments_.review: From what little I've played of it so far, . Not sure why everyone is complaining about the "arcadyness," when not much has even changed mechanically from the past MOW games. HEALTH WAS IN AS2 AS WELL, just hidden from the player. Sure, the voice acting sucks and you have to always be online (), but does that really make or break this game? Not for me. The graphics, sound, and unit variety are excellent. The gameplay is great and feels polished by modern standards. You also don't have to be on 200g of adderall to micro all the units like some other RTS games.People like making comparisons to GOH because of the same engine, but I think both of these have their strong points. MOW2 leans towards multiplayer gameplay, sacrificing realism for usability and enjoyment (which I honestly prefer). It also has replays, a leaderboard, stat comparisons, and a bunch of different multiplayer gamemodes on launch. GOH is heavily focused on realism, but the multiplayer is pretty dead and not balanced well. If you want super realistic and hardcore singleplayer, sure, you may prefer GOH right now. Maybe I'm biased because I was disappointed by COH3 and want a new good multiplayer WW2 to play, but I think this game really stands out. I rarely make reviews, but I feel this game deserves more love than it's getting currently. The devs clearly care about their game. The WW2 RTS community likes to complain about everything before they even play, it seems...

_childDocuments_.review: Man this is a huge disappointment...I love World War 2 games. CoH 2 Is one of my favorite games.Now granted, I never played Men of War 1 but that shouldn't matter. A game should stand on it's own two feet, sequel or not. And for me this game just wasn't that good. It's an RTS but with slow turn based tactical controls. They have different formations, positions, weapons, gear, skills etc. for every single unit but the game moves too fast for you to be able to properly utilize them. Also don't use infantry...they're simply awful. They die super fast and are basically pointless for anything other than defending a spot and even then they could only be slightly effective if their enemies are babies or trees. Maybe then they won't die.Tanks are a bit better but still awkward and unfair. Also you can play as anyone you want despite what team you're on so why not just play as the germans all the time since during this time frame they had the best of everything. I watched a team of mostly germans absolutely destroy my team of mostly allies. The only guy on our team who stood a chance was the one guy playing the germans.the maps are cool and diverse. The sound effects are pretty decent...until their not. And the game looks beautiful.And then with a fast paced RTS it's laggy, jittery/stuttering and jumping around randomly for no reason.The U.I. is clunky and awkward and confusing. The gameplay too fast for this much in-depth controls and unit functionality and just overall I feel like the gameplay and components here were NOT blended very well together thus making a very frustrating, confusing experience.It's a shame because I was really excited for another online pvp ww2 strategy game but this just isn't it. Especially not for 45 fricken dollars!If you'd like a more in-depth explanation with game footage please check out the video on my YouTube Channel (link below).Otherwise thanks so much for reading and I hope I managed to help some of you out there spend your money wisely.

_childDocuments_.review: MOW2 is not like what the bad reviews wanna make it appear. It's not like CoH, and it's different from GoH. I did singleplayer and pvp, never crash, never lost connection. Game runs great at max setting super sharp, no fps drop. -Suppression mechanic : If you bring a tank with infantry to attack a trench line, tanks will suppress the E while infantry will come close to clear. -Combined arms synergy : You really feel the power of combined arms versus other game, even if you micro less.-AI : Your AI troop will mostly know what are the most important target to engage, if your tank sees a medic and an anti tank guy, don't worry.-Maps/Building : Maps are great, they do not feel like a random field and building are real building not just empty asset with 2nd floor and no stairs.-PvP Battalions : Perfect PvP mode to play with friends, and the echelon system is what makes every game special. I did tactical maneuvers with random people, without chat, just because this game makes it possible without having to be in discord and coordinate every single click. It's a crazy sight when you push your infantry with your ally tank to assault a position.Game is realistic, I lost squads very fast while making bad moves. Tanks use penetration system and I never saw anything that made me think ''Wow this is unrealistic'' while some game that praise to be super real had me think that (mostly for AI reasons). OH ; Medics have to bring downed troop out of combat to heal them, no more Rambo revive on the battlefield 10x, so when you see medics coming you know the position is weakenedPLUS, you got so many single player content. From story campaign to historical operations. At first I did all the tutorial which I never do, just cause it was fun, for once. Just try it with a friend or solo, do pvp battalions, use the fun factor to decide if you like the game or not.I bought the game for single player campaign and I'm now addicted to PvP match.

_childDocuments_.review: Well ive played some time now and... First of all i like the game because i see potential for a newer iteration of the MoW franchise. There are some innovations i like, mainly the basebuilding stuff for. The grafic is nicer, but not good. Iam a big fan of the newer itteration of the procedural campaign, even though that could be a bit beefyer. The artillery range and accuracy are fantastic! Sorry to be this kind of person that loves when artillery is done right. The fortifycations are a dream, i really like the sheer amount of options, but you could make Sandbagwalls more organic by now. I mean you did it with the trenches, why not make a similar tool for Sandbags. All in all it is a good start. But the devs need to deliver in the next months. Alot. Cause the game is, and this is a bit obvious, not entirely finished. And there are some balance and logic issues. For example:-Tanks pop out of nowhere, only indicated by trees falling down. Basically increase viewrange and everything is fine.-The infantry slot max is laughable. Everyone knows how fast infantry dies in this game. So 20 max per slot is very very weak. Resourcemanagement is one thing. Getting blasted away by 4-6 Canons another. Especially with the really good Artillery, wich shouldnt be nerfed because ffs just give us more troops for the meatgrinder.-The Pioneers comming from offmap is interesting, i wouldnt necessarily  change that, but let them build more bevore they run off againe. Cause the time they need to get from back to front is pure pain to me. Let us build some kind of Pioneer-Base, where they can restock and let that be their spawnpoint. -Pathfinding is strange, especially rivers ♥♥♥♥ it up.-Give us an accurate Map of... the Map bevore we play on it. Maybe even with the hotspots that we need to devend. I mean how the ♥♥♥♥ should i plan something if i dont know what the terrain is? Of course you could just make some of these issues go away if you would make the game more adaptable. Give us more options to tailor our experienceOOOOOR you could even, at least in procedural campaigns, make some sort of mechanic out of it. Like getting more capacitys with every teretory you conquer, or every mission you absolve. Maybe even implement real challanges to get more stuff. For example commiting to win the battle in 10 min gives you 5000 Money, and the conquered location gives every echelon plus 50 to their capacity. Or work with research even more. Make a second kind of research called "logistical research" that allows you to increase the capacity even more. Let us work and play more with the stategical map instead of just using it to shove divisions around, wich brings me to the next point.Divisions feel incredible... random and a bit like a "jack of all trades". Let us individualize the divisions more. Or when every division says that it is versatile, wich they do, then let us freely, or at least somewhat, adjust the slots for them. I can understand that i am supposed to do everything with the stuff ive got. But lets take AA for example. You need it cause Planes are devastating in the game. But it covers a vital slot that is otherwise occupied with AT or Mortars ect. So you want me to have fun with my divisions? Let them be more adaptable. Let me trade a Tank slot, or an Infantry slot for another big gun. There is so much you could do.Over all I really like the game. But its just the base right now. They should have released the game finished, but who does in our modern age. You can have lots of fun with the game right now. But eventually youll find all the missing stuff, unlogical disign decisions and gaps that the Devs need to fill over the time. And i pray that it wont become another DLC spam.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the genuine follow-up to Men of War: Assault Squad 2 and original Men of War. As a long-time fan of realistic WWII FPS games and someone who’s enjoyed CoH, I can say this title is an exceptional hybrid of RTS and FPS. _childDocuments_.review: I really don't understand a lot of the things people are complaining about.It's not "arcade-y" - infantry dies a little slower than in previous games, but that's basically it; and it's a feature that's needed because interaction between unit groups (tanks, infantry, artillery) is more important than ever. Overall the gameplay has improved quite a lot on a tactical level, it's no longer possible to cheese with certain units.Different battle types and abilities to fortify and camouflage make a variety of playstyles both viable and necessary. I'm very glad they finally moved on from the "run from capture point to capture point" mechanic introduced in the first Assault Squad.Tank HP is not a new mechanic, and it's also not what it sounds like. Vehicles still have individually damageable components; you can't repair a vehicle unlimited times, just like it was in any other MoW game. The change in this is that the overall leftover "health" of the vehicle is actually shown now. This is a UI improvement, not a new mechanic.I quite liked playing this game in CBT when it was still called Arena, and I'm glad they expanded it into a full game. The new frontline gamemode is pretty fun, and makes me actually want to play Multiplayer.Introduction of non-passive and reinforcement-receiving AI troops makes the battlefield feel more realistic and reduces hassle with fog of war, without making deep incursions that more difficult.The deck-building stuff is also quite nice and allows for a lot of long-term replayability.Only issues I have with the game area) forced internet connection (will be removed, developers have already confirmed)b) missing explanations for some meta stuff (how to unlock collector units? how to get new decks in MP? you have to find out yourself)

_childDocuments_.review: I have played the 'Men of War series for a long time; going as far back as the original '1C' (called Best Way back then) Beta-Project back in 2004 "Soldiers: Heroes of World War II." All those games had the same distinct grandiose battlefield tactics gameplay that made the game the legend it was. Even as the community evolved and moved onto its successor, "Gates of Hell," the core gameplay remained. Simply put.........this is not that game! If you gave a bunch of amateur Game DEVs fresh out of college tools and said 'Recreate that game without the blueprint' then this is what you get; trash. The game mechanics are simply not Men of War; they are something else entirely attempting to copy off it. The blocky, skippy nature of unit movements, the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ design of the various armies, the rather poor graphics design even on 'HIGH' settings, the lacking in tactics available to players, and so much more make this a poor quality game. Go spend your money on 'Gates of Hell' if you want an OG Men of War experience. Go play HOI 4 if you want a 4x Grand-Scale Commander experience. But whatever you do I would not recommend buying this product until they either rework it; or until it dies.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to share my own thoughts on the game. Normally, I don't write Steam reviews, but this one is especially important to me.I played the beta before and found the new game mechanics really refreshing. It felt a lot like Company of Heroes (COH) and I had a blast, just like I am now. Most games should be fun, and this one definitely is – just like an RTS game should be and can be, especially one like Men of War. I'm open to new things, and I'm sure a lot of other players are too, as long as they objectively see what you’re trying to do here: reach a broader audience and attract more players. But the typical AAA gamer doesn't buy these types of games anyway, so why not stay true to your fans and be its own niche?However, it was somewhat predictable that the game would end up being too arcade-like and too COH-heavy. I’m not sure about this strategy. Why try to be more like Company of Heroes? That game already exists. If I want to play COH, I’ll play COH. When I want to play Men of War, I want to play Men of War.The game does many things right and even better, like: +how the AI works most of the time (still has room for improvement)+building structures +fortifications +and many other mechanics-But it lacks the mass of manpower on the battlefield to truly be called "Men of War" – this could (and should) be higher. -I also find parts of the UI placement poorly thought out, but you have to admit the old UI of all Men of War games was confusing most times. When you think about it, you can say it was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ the first time you played it, but you got used to it. So now the new UI you think is bad, but it's just because it's new, and you’re used to the old one and can’t accept new things for now. However, the new UI still has room for improvement.-Tank and vehicle movement feels like they're rolling around like those toy cars you pull back and let go, zigzagging all over the place. And health bars for tanks, etc., aren’t necessary, I think...-few bugs (which could also be a plus because there are only a few)I do think the game is good and fun, but it’s different. It’s awesome in its own way. As a die-hard Men of War fan, though, it kind of breaks my heart. It’s tough to see it not being the 100% "Men of War" experience it could have been. This thought frustrates me every time I play.Back during the two betas I played, I gave feedback on Steam and suggested improvements. I mentioned that the game felt too arcade-like and the gameplay was too fast. A lot of other players said the same thing. Right now, it feels like a 50/50 mix of "Men of War" and COH to me, even with the "realistic" mode.I have great respect for the development, the hard work, dedication, sweat, and maybe even tears, and other circumstances and challenges that come with such a process. I can definitely recommend this game, but don’t expect it to be like GOH (Gates of Hell Ostfront) or other Men of War games. For those who haven't played any titles in the series before, I can definitely recommend it. It’s fun, engaging, and enjoyable. In the end, it’s an amazing game!If you could somehow adjust the game to feel more (at least 80%) "Men of War" and (only 20% or less) COH, that would be a HUGE WIN for us (disappointed) Men of War fans! For me, and I think for others, that would be a HUGE WIN and a step in the right direction.If you've always loved COH a bit more than the Men of War series, then Men of War 2 might become your new favorite RTS game and could even make up for the isappointment of COH3.I also appreciate your policy and announcements on how you're moving forward and supporting the community. It’s great to see you listening to us. Your commitment to taking our feedback into account is commendable. If all these points are addressed, the game can only get better. In my estimation, the game is currently a really good one, with a bit of a "BUT" for fans of the series.

_childDocuments_.review: I've now logged more hours into Men of War 2, and while I must admit the game still has some glaring issues, it’s definitely playable, and the recent updates have improved the experience quite a bit. That said, there are still aspects that need serious work, especially in the multiplayer department.The Command Points (CP) system is one of the biggest frustrations for me. It’s really odd that you can’t reclaim your own weapon placements after your men die, even though you’ve sacrificed units to use them. You’re only able to manage 3-4 units at a time, and you can’t squad them up. This limitation feels unnatural, especially when vehicles and weapons seem to get destroyed 95% of the time. It’s frustrating not to be able to repair tanks to regain a solid health pool, and even when you can repair turrets or tracks, they’re often blown to pieces before you can do anything meaningful.Pathfinding is also an issue. Medics frequently get stuck while trying to rescue downed soldiers, and because you can’t manually control them, they often end up dying before you can recall them. Adding to the weirdness, medics and engineers occasionally spawn out of nowhere, which takes away from the immersion. The whole experience feels disjointed when things like that happen.One of the most annoying parts is the destruction of important defenses like gun placements. If you’re hit by just one airburst mortar, your entire fortified position can be wiped out for good. It’s especially aggravating when supply trucks explode from hitting something as trivial as a bush. Vehicles, too, seem to turn way too fast, which feels unrealistic and jarring.The low unit cap is another issue. It doesn’t feel like a full-scale war, which takes away from the excitement. Once you have a couple of howitzers, you can’t do much else, and since the squads are small (4-5 men), calling them battalions feels like a stretch. The PvE experience gets stretched thin by these limits, and it really shows, especially when the AI behaves oddly in the dynamic campaign. During defensive missions, the enemy AI just sends a continuous line of units down the same path, which after a while, feels less like a challenge and more like a chore.Also, a heads-up: You can actually be kicked for being AFK during the single-player tutorial, which is a forced online experience. While they’re working on an offline mode, for now, that’s just something you have to live with.That said, the game is improving. The devs are hard at work, and the recent updates—like the addition of achievements—are super awesome. They also announced that offline mode is coming soon, which will be a relief for many. It’s clear they’re listening to feedback, and that gives me hope for the future of the game.There’s a lot of potential in the dynamic campaign, though it needs more attention. I really hope they add the ability to capture enemy equipment for later use, as it would make the campaign feel more strategic and immersive. Some basic quality-of-life improvements, like an overhaul of the UI or a fix for pathing issues, would go a long way too.Another thing that stands out is the voice acting, which feels a little off and even comedic at times. I’m hoping these are placeholder lines because the tone just doesn’t match the atmosphere the game is trying to create.On the bright side, I still find the campaign enjoyable, and the addition of the reverse command for tanks was a good touch. It shows that the devs are working towards making the game feel more polished, but they still have a lot of work ahead of them.Despite its flaws, Men of War 2 has a good skeleton, and I’m enjoying the game for what it is right now. The game is in a much more playable state than before, and with continued updates, it has the potential to be something special. The developers seem committed to the project, and I’ll definitely keep supporting them and following the progress.For anyone on the fence: if you’re a fan of strategy games and don’t mind some rough edges, it’s worth giving it a shot. Just be prepared for some annoyances, and keep in mind that this is still very much a work in progress.

_childDocuments_.review: With around 14 hours of playtime as of writing this review, I can very confidently give this game a thumbs up. It is probably the best WW2 real time strategy games I've played, though it has a very gritty taste to it (as war should). I've played other Men of War series games and this game is a refreshing update to what is a great system. I'll talk at-large why I like this series, then move to talk about how Men of War to cements itself as a clear leader in the series with it's important updates. All of my gameplay has been PVP, though this game does have a very reasonable PVE gamemode that others enjoy.Gameplay:The Men of War Series is one where your units are very fragile. Soldiers often die after taking a single hit, artillery has very lethal splash damage, and tank duels frequently end with one exchange. It is a series that does a very good job of being a WW2 simulator in creating large complex and chaotic battles where it feels realistic, terrifying, and inspiring at the same time.Another way that the Men of War series shines is through micro management. You can control each individual soldier, giving them very very specific commands, 'live control' them (aka being able to give them raw movement inputs, tell them to stand, go prone, or crouch, and shooting controls, etc)". It can feel really sweet to manually control a soldier to pull out a grenade and manually throw it just the right way to get a massive multi-kill on a squad of enemies. You don't have to use these micro-inputs, but it gives you a extremely large amount of control of manipulating your army. This is often important when angling your tanks or setting up artillery, or even scouting with lone soldiers before an assault.The Updates:Army CompositionsFirst big one is that instead of having access to all of the units in your army in any given game, you have to pick and choose what you want to bring with you to each game. When you're playing Battallion, the default PVP mode, you pick an army type (ie, you could be the 8th Russian Assault Brigade). Based off what you picked you'll over time have access to a unique unit roster. These different armies tend to specialize in certain areas like infantry, tanks, mobile vehicles, artillery, paratroopers, etc. Over the course of playing, as you earn XP and other things, you can customize different army loadouts between matches. So you could swap out having a mortar in the early game to instead have a anti-tank squad, if you wanted. The game uses a point system to denote what/how much you can swap out in each tier of your army (you have three tiers that you gain access to over the course of a game).Battallion is mostly 4v4 or 5v5, and they generally assign teams where each team has a spread of army types. So one person might have tank specialization, another infantry, one artillery, and another air defense. This allows people to play the types of armies they want to play, while having a match that feels like each element of the war effort is being supported. This is a big plus in my book because in previous iterations of the game in the large PVP games sometimes it could feel like everyone on a team all wanted to play one type of role and that lead to less fun games.Gameplay Changes:They changed the scoring metrics of the matches. It used to be in most Men of War titles that you'd basically play either king of the hill similar to Company of Heroes, capturing flags and the person with the most flags would start to rack up victory, or deathmatch - earning points on killing enemy units.In previous Men of War games battles tended to favor the team that had the better defensive setup. Because units are very fragile, having good lines of sight and being able to shoot first and hit your target was very important. This usually led to the defender having a distinct advantage in fights. There were a fair number of games of king of the hill where one team would capture the most central flag location and heavily defend it, and it was very inefficient for the attacker to retake it. In the team deathmatch mode, if one team got a lead, they would sometimes play very defensibly afterwards because the other player would be forced to engage them inefficiently, thus giving over more points to the defender when trying to get kills and score points themselves.In Men of War 2 they eloquently make changes that addresses these issues. Now in Battalion teams play to be the first to reach 2,500 points. Points are awarded on killing units and capturing territory. Territory is not a singular or set series of points on a map. Imaging at the start of the game half the map is your and half the map is the enemies'. As you move units through enemy territory, it converts that territory to yours and you score small amounts of points. Different units take territory faster/some can't take territory. This encourages unit movement around the map, but killing units is still generally better for scoring points.In Battalion, they occasionally offer each side the opportunity to earn 100 points if they can get a single unit to a specific flag location (only offered to one side at a time, a few times per match). In Battalion each side also has a default CPU controlled perimeter army. This is basically a thin number of troops that basically marks out each side's starting area. Those units stay in place and shoot what they can see when they see it. It's not hard to kill these units, but they are helpful because it lets you see if the enemy army is trying to cheese you or flank you early in the game (a problem in previous titles). Over time, these units will probably die to various things, but it allows the game to develop in a natural flow and you can still totally get flanked in the later parts of the game.Air Support:Massive change. As a part of your army composition, you can opt to have charges of Air Support. When you call it in, your cursor changes and you can mark a spot for a plane to fly in and drop various types of bombs and other fire on enemies. There are different types, some are very accurate small bombs, some are very large splashy bombs, some carpet bomb an area for a low amount of damage, some spray a small cluster of bombs, they are effective against different types of targets.This is a very relevant addition to this series because of the aforementioned defensive-posturing the game has had in the past. The combat in the game still slightly favors the defender, but if your opponent starts to focus their defense in a central location you can threaten to punish them with bombs. If you want to be offensive in a certain area, you can use the air cover to eliminate a tank or other defensive unit before committing to the assault.This also coincidentally adds more value to Anti-air vehicles than in previous titles in the series. In past titles, Anti-air vehicles were frequently more used as anti-infantry vehicles, there wasn't really any air units to shoot (rare exceptions), and as a match went on and medium/heavy tanks started entering the field anti-aircraft vehicles felt unplayable because they didn't stand up well to most tanks. Now they have a clear use. Anti-aircraft guns have good range in this game and can cover a healthy area of a map. Depending on the approach of the enemy plane, the AA gun can block the bombing run AND score points for the kill. Sometimes the plane does make it, but dies afterwards.Overall this provides a ton more gamesmanship on the infantry/tank/artillery rock/paper/scissors that proliferated in past games. Some units feel strong, but nothing is unkillable. The additional avenues to conduct offensive operations is a big plus and adds a lot to the gameplay of matches.I highly recommend this title. This does not cover all the changes, but I think on the whole the developers of Men of War have done a good job addressing the previous issues that existed with some online multiplayer matches.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never reviewed a game on steam. With over 2,000 combined hours in MWAS2 and GOH I was utterly disappointed. MOW2 is a crusty love child between COH and MOW that nobody who enjoys the previous titles wanted. (Pros and Cons based off of comparison to previous titles)Pros:          *Solid performance         *New trench building and fortification features         *Squad/Vehicle formationsCons:          * No 1pp controls for units         * 3pp controls are sluggish and lack precise movement         * Somehow the AI got worse (always a complaint with older titles)         * Characters and vehicles seem to have no weight and move extremely quickly and stop on a dime         * AA now has to be toggled between targeting ground and air units with no option to unlock it for both         * Graphics seem cartoonish, explosions from mortars/arty are underwhelming and do not deform the terrain in any           significant manner.          * Tank combat has no grit to it. Impacts make a dink noise and there is no real intensity to a showdown between            armor         * AT/Arty/Machine gun emplacements have no weight. Guns swing around without needing to be cranked and can             snap from target to target as fast as they can see them.          * The reworked UI may just need more time to adjust but from what I saw many things didn't make sense and the             controls were wonky to have units do what you want         * From the two maps I saw, microterrain was basically non existent leaving infantry exposed unless behind assets             placed on the map or trenches         * Vehicles roll right over trenches and through fortifications without reacting to them whatsoever.          * Audio in general has no depth to it. Explosions all sound the same, it's impossible to pinpoint where sounds are            coming from small arms fire just sounds like white noise.          * The general feel of the game is arcadey and fast paced not allowing time to develop well thought out and in depth             plans to maneuver and attack with units, completely shying away from the gritty meticulous play style I've             developed over the years on older titles         * Most of the models and map assets are just copied from the older games.Conclusion: If you expect an improvement over MWAS2 and GOH, don't waist your time. This installment seems to cater to an entirely different demographic, changing the entire feel of the game while keeping the core mechanics as previous titles. Some may enjoy this, as the game itself is not poorly made and could be fun if that's the play style you want to enjoy. As for now, I will stick to GOH.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Has a lot amount of content for 45$ 25 maps, 3 factions, 18 story driven campaign missions (6 each faction), Raids (Co-op PVE with unlocks) 2 dynamic campaigns. It is not a AAA game however and the voice acting reflects that, same with the price. The game is worth it at fill price. Has awesome mod support like past games. Good:-As stated above a lot of content.-All content in the game can be played Co-op.-GEM engine has been updated to DX11, 64 bit, and multi-threaded CPU use game runs super well now RTX 3080 5800X3D 3440x1440 maxed out. -GEM engine added physical based rendering and lighting in the game looks a lot better than MoW:AS2.-Steam Deck support. -Good art style, grounded in a realistic look, not a cartoon game. -Battalions MP mode is a fun way to get new people into playing MoWII in MP. You have less things you have to control but mist work as a team to win.-Classic mode for people who want to MP like they did with MoW:AS2.-Servers are a lot more stable than the older games.-Options, there is about an option for everything in this game. Want to tweak UI or rebind keys you can do this. -Game can run on older PCs.-Sound effects are good, its not Post Scriptum / Squad 44 levels of awesomness but nothing is besides PS.-Realism mode for people who want a more hardcore / cinematic game.-Replay system on launch, you can even watch single player missions.-Direct control system like a GEM engine games is fun.-Fully destructible environments, if you want to drive a tank through a wall you can.-Tanks can crush infantry-Tanks can ram, damage us based on weight so a small tank vs a tiger wont do anything. -Shift + F11 by default for hide all UI if you want to take awesome screenshots.-Mod support, very open engine for modding and not locked down-Game uses MSAA or SMAA, no TAA everything looks sharp not not blurry. Also means no DLSS, DLAA, XESS, FSR support but its not needed in this game. This could be a con if you like TAA. -A MP unlock system that is not micro transactions. It's unlocked by playing the game even the The Frontline Hero Pack stuff is unlockable. Bad:-Voice acting at least in english is bad. -Cutscenes are just using the in game engine and models look stiff.-There are some bugs nothing game breaking.-Shell holes disappear after a time, this is for performance reasons. It would still be nice to have a slider to allow them to stay around longer. -Game is always online but devs are getting rid of this in a future update. -Replays need a toggle fog of war option as well as 2x,4x,8x fast forward. However you can click on the other side player name on the top left or right to see their PoV.-Voice line of the factions when giving orders could be better.Other thoughts: The game will be hard for noobs just keep up with it, it's rewarding once you learn the game systems. Vets will feel at home and should have no issues. This is not a Company of Heroes game, health bars are in all GEM games even if not shown. The TTK is a lot quicker than CoH 2, that being said if you did not like CoH 3 and want something more hardcore buy this and play classic mode. I think this is the most complete RTS to be released on day 1 in the last few years, there is no shortage of things to do in this game. It's also not missing features you would expect from a RTS. If you want the game to be GoH or MoW:AS2 those games already exist and you can keep playing them, MoW2 is its own game.  No this is not a CoH game again as I said its too hardcore for that TTK is too quick.Edit: Typos

_childDocuments_.review: Men of War 2 has some issues and some improvements over previous entries in the series, and the 'spiritual member' Gates of Hell. But it's also the subject of a significant amount of false information dirtying the games reputation needlessly. So here's a list of things that are better in this game that previous titles,, light vehicles and vehicles towing were previously very buggy. Often their pathfinding would collide them with objects and result in the death of the vehicle. Any vehicle towing something was particularly bad for this and required babysitting to move it anywhere.In MoW2 all vehicles are able to destroy basic obstructions like trees and stone walls. It's, very weird.  the oddity of a kubelwagen blowing through a brickwall significantly outweighs that now a truck towing an AT gun can be right clicked half way across the map and will  make it without destroying itself from stupidity., infantry will now automatically mantle over low walls and fences without requiring the player to manually order the squad to mantle over the fence., there is now a more refined concealment system. It's obvious and clear to you when your units are concealed, partially visible and fully visible. It is now quite possible and reliable to have units fire from complete concealment. Camoed AT guns can fire several rounds without even becoming partially visible.This, if you want to keep units concealed, does require you to put in micro. However, being able to keep a unit firing while concealed is a significant improvement.Previous games worked in a similar way, where units could fire and a few rounds before becoming revealed. However now how revealed units are is clear, the system is refined, reliable and easy to understand across various unit types. And partially revealed is a new status for units where they will not be visible, but an indicator of the general position the fire is originating from will be visible., trenches rather than being a set object can now be dug in any shape you'd like and interconnected. Trenches actually feel like trenches, you can really live out your WW1 dreams if you want creating a network of bunkers and trenches., there's a lot. And a lot of it's good. You have, conquest campaign which is very good compared to the implementation in GoH. Singleplayer story campaigns which range from good to meh in honesty. Historical campaigns which are all good. And an escalating skirmish vs AI gamemode in Rush.And an elephant in the room. Have always existed. But what's more important is that healthbars were not particularly relevant in previous titles as they were quite large, and what caused vehicle death more often was random detonation. In previous games an anti-tank rifle can fire at the taillight of a halftrack and in a random number of shots instantly cause it to explode into a huge fireball. It doesn't need to be aimed at a location containing ammunition, the vehicle doesn't even need to have anything explosive, it's a random chance of occurring each time the vehicle is penetrated. Men of War 2 vehicle Healthbars are a change, because vehicle health is now shown to you and consistent. You will know when a tank is 1 shot away from exploding. Shot placement is still relevant for killing crew and damaging components.But, it is not, like constantly claimed, removing 'true simulation where rounds have to hit ammunition to detonate a vehicle'. It's just changing a die roll focused system, to the visible health focused system.I love Men of War, but playing Gates of Hell or AS2 is a constant battle with stupid units, and awkward interactions. Basic tasks like making use of medics, laying minefields, resupplying infantry, just getting a towed gun to the front, all takes a ridiculous amount of your effort.The core systems are still all here, you can still open a man's inventory and load him with every grenade you can find.But now laying mines, using medics, ordering infantry around, all requires less headache and lets you focus more on playing the game.Yeah, maybe a little bit is lost now that I don't have to awkwardly load a man with ammunition and run him to a squad and combine them to resupply them. But, I'll take it, cause after a couple of hours awkwardly mucking around with that stuff gets annoying.

Haven't been this excited to play and RTS game for a long time to the point of looking forward to the evening after work when I will get to play. I'm mostly interested in SP content, so I can master the game's mechanics first but appreciate the rich MP and mods which I may get to later. Sound design and voice lines provide an immersive experience of every battle, however VFX, animations and pathfinding could use more work as they feel janky at times.Overall, the sheer amount of way you can approach each mission, the huge variety of units and solid gameplay mechanics (Direct control/RTS) make this game well worth the asking price. (If you support an affiliate or content creator you can get it for 36 EUR)

MOW2's tech tree is not that long and trivial, but also cover most cannons or tanks in WWII.But I think developers should improve the tank damage mechanism in realism mode to make it more similar to that in MOWAS2 or Gate of Hell, many players including me, can not accept HP bar for vehicles and think the existing mechanism in realism mode is not realistic enough. _childDocuments_.review: Positives:* It's a WW2 RTS game much like Company of Heroes, with a few differences.There's no base building. the entirety of your military is based on a Roster you choose before the mission.Units you deploy are limited by Numbers and Supply. The enemy can win if they kill all of your squads.* It's somewhat realistic. Each unit has ammunition they can deplete.Armored vehicles have armor, penetration, etc. So vehicle orientation matters, as well as accuracy.Most units have camouflage, which is useful if you want to Hide your troops. Spotting is a thing so you can go stealth in certain rare situations.* The overall map design and combat scenarios of the campaign were fun. I love the mechanics of the game where it allows you to take Manual control of any unit. You can command a squad of tanks to assault a position, take control of one tank and lead the assault yourself.* There's also a decent number of unit types and vehicle types. A decent number of support structures and constructions. There's even different ammunition types, which does make a difference when you're fighting with Vehicles.In short it's as if Enlisted or War Thunder was an RTS. Which for me is all positive. Negative:* The AI is dumb. And I don't mean that as an insult, it seriously lacks any logical thinking. You have to babysit every single unit so they don't do something stupid, especially when they're in a large group.Ordered a large squad to take cover in a trench? expect half of them to stand outside the trench.Ordered a group of vehicles to move to a position? expect them to bump into every wall and vehicle on the way there. Finally after arriving at their destination by headbutting their way through... there's a good chance they will position their Rear towards the enemy.It's like your units are brainless puppets and require you to bark orders at them every second. No concept of Armor, cover, or proper positioning.Even their accuracy is often questionable as they seem to aim for Center mass, instead of weak spots.I guess... get good at micro-managing?  If you're commanding a Tank, you're better off controlling it's gun Manually for better accuracy.* The Interface or Game screen is lacking in terms of feedback. It's very difficult to notice certain things like: Your units throwing a grenade, when someone is reloading, etc. You either have to zoom in on the tiny icons above their heads, or just click and hope something happens.* Controls. Jesus. Christ. Look I know Controls for an RTS are difficult because you have 30 different commands, but RTS games are not a new invention, they have existed since the year 2000. If Starcraft, Warcraft, Red Alert, etc can all have a control scheme that makes sense, so can You.There is absolutely NO reason for me to be using the F1-F12 keys in any situation when there's 160 different possible combinations on the W-Z keys.In short, the control scheme is very cluttered and has no alphabetical or priority sorting.* Some of the campaign missions are literally impossible on higher difficulties. To me it feels like the devs tried to add padding to the game, to inflate the play hours just by making you restart missions multiple times. Combine that with the 0 IQ AI and well... good luck.* Lastly, all Campaign characters have AI generated voices. (at least from what I could tell)This for me is a negative. I don't want ChatGPT in my games.I don't like robotic sounding characters with 0 personality.Summary:I don't recommend this because it has too many flaws and it's frustrating having to micro every unit independently in order for them to not be useless. On top of that it feels unfinished and unpolished. For the same price, you can find better RTS games.But I guess if you enjoy the Manual Control gimmick, give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This review summarises what every other review with 10 mins playtime states here with a bit more passion. Buy Gates of Hell; Men of War Assault Squad 2; Company of Heroes 1 and 2 if you want a valid Second World War Experience. Something feels tacky about this release. Please don't fall for the sponsored content like I did. This feels like Fisher Price made a wargame.   After watching hours upon hours of content on Youtube surrounding this game, and being an avid armchair historian of the Second World War, I have to sadly say I'm disappointed. Despite glaring issues in the looks department (I'm a strategy gamer, special effects don't appeal to me.) there is a whole host of other problematic issues at play here, namely: Dreadful feeling to the controls; cheap looking unit icons; half baked voice acting; poor graphics; graphical glitches; dreadful unit animations; clunky UI; always online functionality which forces various load times. I have experienced these issues in 10 minutes of playtime. In all honesty - it felt like a mobile game.   I have played Gates of Hell: Ostfront and very much enjoy it, despite all its wrinkles. It provides a historically accurate, weighty experience. As an Englishman, however, I must say that Ostfront lacks what I desire - to play as the Commonwealth. Therefore I thought given I can get the entire Men of War Assault Squad 2 collection for a mere £7.09, I'd see if it scratches an itch. Playing this, I stormed a bridge at Arnhem as the British; Defended the Philippines with Beaufort artillery and charged Red waves into the Fascists "FOR THE MOTHERLAND." This franchise has truly regressed into a mobile port, tacky feeling COH3 clone since the days of old! To the developer: I have refunded this product based on misrepresentation. In my belief, you were wrong to challenge Rimmy on his judgement and this release has been a PR disaster. The vast array of promotional content and sarcastic review responses have put me off your game, along with its more than apparent lack of quality. I am instead using the funds I receive from this refund to invest in the DLC for Gates of Hell as I feel this will scratch my 'Twilight of the Gods' late war itch. This review is a love letter to a game that didn't exist, in which there were dynamic campaigns and there was a passion for history. In short, until this improves, buy Assault Squad 2 for its immense single player campaign options or Gates of Hell to immerse yourself in the gritty, squelching boots of an entrenched servant of the Motherland. Fin.
