_childDocuments_.review: Please everyone, disregard the negative comments, this is not a regular RTS game.and majority of the negative review are from lazy people that didn't spend 2 hours in the game.Men of War 2 brings a lot of WW2 realism into the game, it is a mix of foxhole complexity with RTS... just the tutorial to learn the game is like 2 hours.To explain it better the tutorial covers:-Basic Controls-Spawning troops-Ammo and Fuel Supply-Infantry Commands (barbed wire, trench and others)-Vehicle control (you can control the tanks like World of Tanks)-Recon (basically you play like commando, go behind enemy line and create a breach into their defenses)-Armour Piercing (Similar to WoT again)-Anti Air Defense-Air Force (Recon, Bombs, and Paratroppers)-Counter Battery FireThese tutorial covers like 50% of the complexity of the game; you need to be prepared to learn a lot but it is super rewarding as you will really understand what to do in the multiplayer game.This game has super deep mechanics and it is a lot of fun if you like WW2 theme.Please thumbs up, give award on this comments to assist new players to understand what exactly is this game as this is not explained well anywhere.Message to the devs:-You really need to improve the combat UI, it is not bad but it is not friendly for new players. -Also it is very difficult to realize that you have "videos" for several things in the tutorial, you could also upload these videos into your official youtube channel to help them.. Relic with COH did an amazing job with content creators creating guides for the game, maybe you could spare a few $$ for the same.-The tutorial could be included in the campaign to explain one step at a time... again, Relic did a good job on that with COH as well... -You guys did an amazing job with this game, we can see the hard work put into it but the average joe would complain after playing for 10min, you really need to make it more friendly for them... it is not that hard to implement QoL, you spent thousands of hours to make a super real game, if 20% of that time was spent in QoL we would have way better reviews.-Your campaign was made for co-op but there are several solo players out there, old people that can afford paying this game would play to chill as hobby and most of them would not have time to play with friends. Have this in mind to make more solo content.

_childDocuments_.review: ### Men of War 2: The Time Machine I Didn't Ask ForLet’s set the stage: The year is 2023, my belly is full of cheap instant noodles, and I’ve just booted up "Men of War 2," a game that somehow managed to invoke nostalgic memories of the early 200s with its graphics and sound design.First off, “Men of War 2” isn’t just a game; it’s an exercise in patience and a time machine that nobody really asked for. The premise? Revisiting the Eastern and Western fronts of WWII. The execution? Eh…**Graphics**: Imagine you’re watching WWII footage on a potato – and not a well-prepared one, but like, an undercooked, barely salted spud. The graphics in “Men of War 2” make me feel like I’ve been teleported back to the early days of the original game’s release. Meanwhile, I’m peeking longingly over at "Call to Arms – Gates of Hell" which is partying with full 4K brilliance, getting all the right swipes on Tinder with its stunning visuals.**Sound Design**:For a game set during one of the noisiest periods in history, the sound design here is akin to stepping on a rogue LEGO – unexpectedly painful and somehow incredibly wrong. It's as if the gunfire and explosions were recorded inside a tin can by someone who's never heard the real thing.**Gameplay**:Speaking of steps, let’s talk gameplay. Imagine yourself taking a step forward, but before you can advance, you have to find a server - yes, even for single-player. So, that's right; if you're keen on defeating Nazis during your third shift or without the steady hand of your home internet, you're fresh out of luck, soldier.User Interface:The interface feels like it's from another era where clunky menus and questionable design choices were all the rage.**Rating**: 🌟🌟I’m giving it a generous 4 out of 10, mostly because I appreciate the effort in making a sequel and I have a soft spot for RTS games. Let's hope the developers get a patch update - maybe borrow some stardust from "Gates of Hell" because, they need some graphics and sound-upgrading magic, STAT.Until then, I’ll be over here, singing praises to the original "Men of War" titles and "Call to Arms - Gates of Hell," reliving my strategic victories in HD and crisp audio without having to hunt down a server for solo play.

_childDocuments_.review: So, up front I will admit that there are some good features they introduced. If nothing had changed from the last game in the series other than them adding in these new features, I would wholeheartedly recommend this game. Unfortunately there are a litany of problems.One, and it's been stated by so many people, is the "always online" feature. Why this keeps getting added is beyond me. Any game that adds it get's generally awful reviews. Unless it's a game that is purely an online multiplayer game, which is not the case here. I only ever played the previous games on single player, especially since I bought a lot of the old games. There's more to say, but others have already stated it much more eloquently than I can.The next issue is unit path-finding. BLUF (bottom Line Up-Front) it's non-existent. When I tell a tank to go somewhere, it takes a direct path, no matter what. So, let's say you have a bunch of crates filled with useful equipment for the mission somewhere in the path, well now that no longer exists. Or how about a wall to use for cover, nope, it's gone. It's also not like it's unheard of to have it the other way. For example in Call To Arms: Gates of Hell, when I tell my tank to go somewhere beyond a wall that already has an opening, it drives through the opening. If I want it to go through I just have to double click the order and it takes a direct path. For reference, that game is almost 3 years older than Men Of War 2. This one is short because there's not much to say about why it's bad design. There doesn't seem to be much difference in vehicle collision. As in, a motorcycle and a tank are both able to drive from the road to the grass and through trees or other obstacles with equal lack of difficulty.This one is kind of minor, but also not since it will be there for every match and throughout your entire game. The voice acting. Men of war has always had fairly bad voice acting, but they only have like 3 lines for infantry to say, and they repeat it every time you select them. Also, if they are in any vehicle, they talk as if they are in a tank. So you'll have a rifleman in a jeep saying the tank is ready to go fight the enemy. Or every time you select the infantry they say the same 5 or 6 word line. All they had to do was add in the occasional "Sir?", "Orders, sir? or some variation of that. Also, maybe have it so the dialogue is locked to vehicle type rather than just being in any vehicle. Again, there is more to be said about this. This last one is only relevant if you are a veteran of the series. If you're new to the series, this actually benefits you. They made the game simpler, and honestly it shows in everything listed above (except maybe the always online feature) The dialogue required maybe 10 people to be in a studio for like 4 hours. The path-finding might as well be non-existent. Every vehicle can just fly through obstacles. All of it is essentially the most basic, lack any work, creativity or complexity options they could go with. It's just disappointing, because I've bought almost every single game in this series and have been playing it almost as long as I've been playing PC games. A lot of well-established companies with great series keep dropping the ball lately. It keeps happening, and I keep falling for it. If this is your first game in the series, have fun. If you're a vet like me, don't buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: The download and installation of the program files was uneventful, as I had expected it would be. Once installed, I ran the program and was immediately prompted with the question of whether I wanted to play the game or launch the editor. I chose to play the game, although I am absolutely thrilled that the game offers a built-in editor. The modding community will, no doubt, create some amazing content for this game.In most games, the first thing that I like to do is dive into the settings menu to look at what options I have for the gameplay, video, audio, key mappings, and difficulty. The game appears to support the latest in graphics technology. I did test the game on a system with an Nvidia 1070 video card and then on a Nvidia 3070 system. The 1070 system was playable once I lowered the levels on most settings. Unfortunately, the game doesn't seem to support a performance testing system for video functionality. This would have saved me quite a bit of time while trying to determine the best settings for my 1070 video card. The 3070, on the other hand, didn't require any modifications after installation from the default settings and ran the game well without any issues.  All that said, the graphics didn't impress me as being anything more than run of the mill. The explosions were adequate as were the unit models and maps. _childDocuments_.review: I have now played two campaigns. And i see all the negative reviews. Believe me. I get your frustration and your anger about the route the devs took. This is it then. MOW 2 is like this and this is what it is. And i think it is ok to do a less Simulation like approach and to take the game in a new direction. Even if i am not fully satisfied with lesser features compared to the earlier games.But then... then i discovered what a developer said. Realism Setting? I searched for it. It is in settings under packages. It removes the HP from the tanks! You can again crush the hulls fo enemy tanks and recover them! This changes the whole game dynamic back to the original! So what they actually did is: They gave us both worlds! You can play in a more direct, easy to get into the game approach like in COH, or you play like you are used to play MOW. Go check the setting. _childDocuments_.review: It's not THAT bad guys. On a scale of 0 = CoH and 10 = GoH, with Realism mode turned on, this is still an 8. It's still plenty close to a traditional MoW experience. I think we can live in a world where we have both GoH and MoW2 in our steam library at the same time. If you're absolutely strapped for cash and can only afford one game, then sure get the better one for you. But this game is not without its merits. This game has single player content that isn't just a few skirmish maps tacked onto a multiplayer game. As someone that basically only plays single player, I appreciate that.Now there are some things the devs have done that are really dumb, and warrant the negative reviews. You must have known the always online would be received poorly. I don't care that a fix is coming soon, you should have had the foresight to take care of that before release.I think it's great that you took the feedback and included realism mode. But what should have happened was, the first time everyone booted up the game, there should have been a huge popup asking the player if they wanted arcade or realism mode,  with an explanation of what each mode did and then offer the option to freely change it in the settings later. This isn't hurrdurr customer too dumb to find the option, it's buried in the options, you wouldn't know where to find it unless you were looking for it. You're getting the negative reviews because of poor UI/UX decisions that you made.Speaking of poor UI, you guys really didn't try with that huh? This transparent minimalism look with ultra small buttons does not look good. The placement of commands almost seems arbitrary between the hotbar and the bottom right window. The customization of some things like the minimap are okay I guess.I'm not sure how I feel about the engineers and medics coming in from offmap to do their thing. I am trending towards negative feelings towards that but the jury's still out. Maybe I can get used to it and see it as a good balance change over microing with a medic trying to revive everyone.I have to play with the vehicles a bit more to get a better feel for them. The T34 in the tutorial moved a little too fast for my liking. The way reinforcements are summoned is fine, but the way the troops are spaced apart feels a bit weird. Like they're standing equal distances apart from each other and it doesn't look natural.Alright that was a lot of negative points but overall it feels like more Men of War and that's still a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a hard decision, but I think it's fair to give this a negative review. It can stand for itself but pales in comparison to any other option, especially considering the bugs, the fact its only online(even in singleplayer) and significantly MORE expensive than other titles.   Call to Arms: Gates of Hell(GOH) is miles ahead in historical and gameplay realism. MOW2 is still a PVP history inspired game, GOH is hand built to be as historical as possible. MOW2 is presented as cheesy and goofy. While tanks dont have "health bars", they do have health pools and damage is defined by RNG, to compare, see GOH blog posts.   Both MOWAS2 and GOH are better options. Quality of life features and game modes in PVP is probably the biggest strong point of MOW2 but you can't build a foundation for a house with furniture: riddled with bugs; online only(ping); cars drifting into the abyss; having 5 guys and a light tank as a ““complete army””; unlocking units like COD skins.Then currently there is NO reason to buy this. It will take at the minimum years for the first big mods to show up, MOWAS2 has a vast and developed selection of mods.There is no reason to buy this game specifically, it’s not bad by itself and does introduces some fun quality of life features to the series. But you have to remember this is competing with MOWAS2, a TEN YEAR OLD GAME(wich also has 2 MORE factions)..

_childDocuments_.review: Lets talk about some of the things nobody is mentioning because wah tanks have healthbars.Maps in multiplayer now start with an AI picket line already set up across the entire front. This means you don't have to spend the first few moments and command points of each game on a bunch of rifleman spread out along the front. It also means you don't get flanked with bazookas hidden in the back field because the 1 new player didn't know to do this.You get shot indicators from where and what your tank got hit by. It is a classic thing in WW2 RTS games that your tank will explode into a fireball because it got hit by an AT gun hidden in a hedgerow 2 screen lengths away. This helps that problem by notifying you with a direction and exactly what shot at you. This makes it easier for new players to understand what just happened and easier to veterans to react without being frustrated by camera controls.Most vehicles and AT guns can fortify or camouflage now. It is done a bit more gamey like CoH with a single click, but honestly improves gameplay and eliminates micromanagement. I don't want to have to manually deploy 3 bushes around my AT gun to hide it like in past games.Nowhere near the flare gun/artillery spam in past games. Aircraft call ins are done almost as an ability and now allow you to select the ordnance used. You can choose different bombs or strafing runs depending on the target as well as direction. Anti Air is an important part of the game now and adds a good layer to it. Para-drops actually work.Engineers spawn in and out automatically and regen mines automatically. Is it more gamey? Yes. Do I miss making my engineers walk over to a supply truck, enter the inventory, transfer the mines, have them go back to laying out the minefield? No.They still spawn in and can be shot if you put them in a dangerous front line situation, it just eliminated boring micro so you can focus on the good stuff.The maps are big enough and designed in ways that the problems in past titles with spawning are largely non existent. In past titles he who spawns big tank last wins. Cause it was going to spawn in with 15 second invincibility and in range of the enemy ready to fire a shot. This just doesn't happen now.The regiments are actually pretty cool. For the most part unlocking units gets you very little as far as bonuses and is really just a prestige thing. People are over-thinking it. What it does do however is allow you to customize your units so you know what you are going in with and get to bring units you actually like. In past games I'll admit to getting lost sometimes of okay, it is Germany on this front for this time period and I'm playing this doctrine, do I have a heavy tank or not? This way you know exactly what you are bringing into battle. Again, great for newer players that don't know every single Sdkfz variant.The territory control gameplay is a great mix of past game modes. Instead of having to focus on specific bombed out points the battles are a lot more dynamic with attacks being viable across the entire front. Being efficient and having good kills to losses still makes a solid impact but players are also rewarded for taking ground. This isn't even getting into the single player content or the best conquest map yet since the original MoW mod.The tank health bars aren't horrible and generally make things a bit less RNG even if it is less realistic. If you hit a light vehicle with a heavy round it is still gonna pop. Things like AT grenades feel less random as they may take a couple throws but you see the impact on health. The same with light vehicles firing into each other. Since they have relatively matched weapons and armor the health comes more into play. You see the bar go down and can judge the situation a little better than just straight RNG waiting for a crit. Again, is it gamier, yeah. But they needed to distinguish this from Gates of Hell and I think they found a great balance without turning it into full on Company of Heroes. Honestly though, I'd play this just cause they gave us a good T35. They finally gave us a late war model with more armor so it can go against other medium tanks or act as a base of fire. They also gave the main gun some really nice air burst artillery rounds. So this review is probably biased...-------------------Original first impression review:Honestly it is a good amount of content with a lot of improvements to make it play more smoothly compared to past titles.By default it does seem like a slight slight step towards CoH style play but that isn't a bad thing. This makes the game play better as an actual game and less as a sandbox with WWII units.If you really want the sim feel, stick with Gates of Hell/mods. I'll be playing and enjoying both.This was the least disappointing strategy title released this month...

_childDocuments_.review: I'm rather conflicted on the game. TLDR; I recommend the game for its innovation despite others said and the dev's hard work but there are design decisions that are either poorly thought out or implemented.I will not going into details on vehicle health bar and other hot topics that are being debated quite thoroughly by others.On one hand there are many thoughtful improvements and features compares to previous entries and Gates of Hell, such as improved AI controls, modernized UI and graphics, easily managed trench building mechanic, etc.On the other hand while I do like the concept of battalion deck building and frontline system, it has many fundamental design flaws that prevents many players from enjoying the game.The current gameplay in its default battalion mode focuses too much on teamplay(which is hard to come by in a random match) to the point it strips player to the bare minimum in terms of properly building a versatile and fun deck.To put in some details, in other deck building RTS/RTT games(namely Wargame and Steel Division), player is abled to build a deck specialized in certain playstyle via bonuses and penalties by choosing a regiment/brigade or whatever it is called similar to the MOWII's battalion system. However in these games they don't just take away all but one type of unit, they incentivize the player towards building a specialized deck. For example you may be having less tanks in a infantry focused deck but never/rarely you will be having no tanks, and you get more slots for infantry or cheaper cost that makes you lean on getting more infantry.This is not the case in MOWII, in MOWII you are not being penalized for choosing tanks in a infantry deck, you simply cannot get any form of tanks or even basic AT emplacement to counter the enemy with your deck only some AA, aircrafts, and bazookas, this design alone forces player into playing with other players that are also being stripped by the current system, yet as I mentioned, teamplay is nearly impossible in a random match because we are all cats and cats cannot be herd.I know there is the combined arms game mode that let you choose whatever you want when building a deck, but that game mode has no specialization bonuses or any proper limitation so you just go for whatever infantry and tank that is the best at each phase.In the end, a good game none the less but I'm having a hard time convincing myself this is the good way to go with its current multiplayer system.

I think it rewards thoughtful micromanagement and the population caps keep that to a relatively manageable level which escalates towards the end, but usually keep the game focused on efficiently attriting the enemy forces. I don't mind any of the so-called 'arcadey' mechanics which are mostly just QoL improvements like relatively well-designed icons to indicate what a unit is doing; the biggest shortcomings are once again the vestiges of old programming and strange choices for keybinds and icon layout in some cases. Accept the game for what it is (with some hope for improvement in the long run) and there's a lot of gameplay to be had.

_childDocuments_.review: Men of War II is not the game I been waiting on. It is like some amalgamation of Company of Heroes and some very tenuous aspects of the previous Men of War titles. This honestly feels like its own standalone game that is unfortunately worse than the previous Men of War titles. If I wanted to play this arcade type war game I would have just purchased Company of Heroes. I didn't though because I was excited for a new Men of War game, been on my wish-list since its was announced. Pros-Literally struggle to think of any that the previous versions of MOW don't already do better. Conquest mode was exciting to see however, that feel flat on delivery almost immediately.The graphics I guess are better... TBH though, couldn't really tell myself if there is a major improvement.Cons-Online requirement to play ( Devs are fixing but still terrible choice for release)Battles are arcade style, quick and very rinse and repeat ( I started by selecting the realism option before even starting any game play and it still is arcady and frankly bad. All in all realism option does not make it like older MOW titles this is something I see the Devs posting to every negative review. This is not the case so beware.)Armor is very weak like paper tanks. Also, there is way too much armor that get called in and can be called in. So many tanks on the field at one time that it negates any infantry strategy/movement. Instead of previous titles where a tank on the field was a focal point of strength and strategy, now its just spam tanks... You Win! or enemy spams tanks on harder difficultly... They Win! Infantry is less outfit-able than previous MOW titles which is huge for me as I loved that aspect in the previous MOW. They can't pick up enemy infantry weapons off dead bodies, they are extremely weak and get shredded quickly in any combat, they have terrible pathing issues, they get lost on map and are hard to find when micro managing other units, lastly they are just overall useless vs previous MOW titles.Conquest mode is lackluster to say the least.. Attack than Defend rinse and repeat. Thought maybe there might be a Steel Division aspect but yet again disappointment. Highly looking forward to this mode too.Multiplayer did not even try it myself as this is not why I play this type of game. Might be great who knows, as it seems as if they are trying to compete with Company of Heroes in the arcady cheese mechanics that has been implemented in this game. Understand why it was added but honestly feels like they lost their way trying to focus on this aspect and forgot why MOW is loved by players to begin with.Summary-If you must buy this game, I highly suggest waiting for it to go on sale. Maybe around $15 max for what this game offers. Me personally would not spend anything as I don't believe this game is going to be fixed to the degree at which is needed. I recommend playing the older MOW titles and just be happy that we have them as this game is never going to meet those standards. Overall Rating- 3/10 across the board. Hate to be so harsh but I just can't see how this is a Men of War title. I really hope companies start realizing that when you have a recipe that is loved universally by fans... Don't mess it up by making something completely new, add to the recipe we all love and innovate on it. This is just a whole new thing that says it's going to taste the same and is sold as the previous recipe but ultimately leaves a bad taste in your mouth.

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty fun, somewhat hefty price tag and a lot of jank, but if you actually play the game modes it's a more casual experience than GOH or COH3, and has a few differences that I find interesting. The battalion system is a cool idea and adds a bit of deckbuilding. Price is a bit high, considering the issues on launch, and always online requirement. EDIT: After playing for a bit I feel that MOW2's strength lies in little minute details and QOL differences compared to COH3 or GOH. The entrenchment and camouflaging system for all vehicles is certainly interesting. There seems to be a spotting/radio mechanic a la Steel Division 2. Conquest has vague continuity. You can attack one area during the day time, and then defend it during the night with the same emplacements, terrain etc. It does not seem that battle damage carries over, but it's a nice touch. Being able to call in medics and engineers to build from off map is weird, but interesting. The battalion deck building isn't as good as something like SD2, but I find it kind of fun. You can retreat units offmap to regroup and heal like in Regiments.The building is really cool, you can make fairly complex defensive lines, and each unit will build different things. A lot of combat and gameplay is simplified, at the expense of realism. For example, vehicles move like bumper cars. This is obviously not as immersive as gates of hell, but prevents issues that have plagued MOW and GOH like Motorcycles and Wheeled vehicles behaving like absolute brainless idiots. Vehicles actually seem to reverse more consistently when you click behind them compared to GOH too, which suprised me. Oh, and there's a reverse option like COH3, which again, GOH lacks. None of this is to completely dump on GOH, the combat is far less intense and immersive, and some of the roles the devs assigned to units seems arbitrary. Pathfinders are described as counter stealth scouting line infantry, but they just seem like 10% better riflemen to me. I don't understand why most games don't give them the same stat block as paratroopers... the US HAD scouts, you can just make the infantry scouts do whatever it is you're trying to do here.  Anyways, I just wanted to insert that (IMO) this game beats GOH in little features and QOL, not as a whole. I don't understand this insanely negative tone surrounding MOW2 in this regard. I don't think it's trying to compete as a GOH replacement, as it would be futile. Oh yeah another comparison, the research trees in conquest.The research tree is a little bizarre, but Gates of Hell's isn't really that good to begin with. I'll be short, but in gates of hell the submersible jeep and browning 50 cal both cost 1 research point. I'm not going to check now but for the Germans in vanilla GOH I think the captured french tanks genuinely take like 12 research points, which will take away from panzers elite infantry etc, it's always had weird balance around expensive useless side grades. In MOW2,  they borrow World of Tanks XP system, you earn "Free XP" as well as XP for each unit. If you use a unit enough, you can get enough unit XP to unlock the next unit in their line for free. If you cannot, the free XP lets you unlock units regardless of whether or not you used the previous version. I genuinely think this is a better system, as in Gates of Hell you can get hard stuck trying to raise like 6 research points for a bazooka man to unlock the rest of your infantry and officer upgrades, whereas you might need that for tanks, artillery, etc. Between the two, there is no reliable way to know how much of a resource you will earn from a battle, so the jury is out on that one.Again, just want to restate that the price is hefty, so I understand people being annoyed at that. TL;DR - Game have interesting features. Game fun, game no realistic, game no immersive, but game enjoyable. Grug no understand seething hatred for game, but game no perfect.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a veteran of Gates of Hell and Men of war, and there is lots of potential here. I'm not going to lie and say that there aren't any problems because there are problems, but none that can't be fixed. Here's a list of my most concerning issues.1. No offline gameplay. The fact that I can't play the game without an internet connection is REALLY DISAPPOINTING. Its my understanding that the devs have said that they will be fixing this issue in the near future, but this should've been released at launch.2. Fewer factions than MOWAS2. In other Men of War titles there have been more factions like Japan, the UK, and also the Ostfront Grüppe. In this game however there are only the Soviets, Americans, and Germans. (And please don't lock content behind paywalls.)3. Hard to understand UI. The UI feels really clunky on the main menu, but once in a battle, the UI feels good and well placed. The only thing I'd change about the battle UI is the weird stance system for infantry.4. Better voice lines, especially for the US, need to be added. The voice lines for the United States are trash, their audio is so bad that it makes me not want to play America. Where is the passion? Wheres the thrilling audio that you'd expect from a WW2 Marine? I've heard more engaged voice actors in Hell Let Loose, (which are just average players btw,) than these PAID actors. How these lines made it into the actual game stuns me.(UPDATE) Although at the moment there is still bad audio in the game, there is a mod you can download to fix the US voice lines. It's not the best, but at least it makes the United States not unbearably annoying to play as. Its called [ACE] Voice Lines, by Skilletti. It gives you a reasonable audio when playing the game, and not as much of the cheezy new vinnila voice lines. But it doesn't entirely root out the old lines from the game, you'll hear them here and there, but it actually gives you the audio you'd expect. It doesn't change the fact that delivering good audio is something the developers should be doing, not freelance modders. Here's a  link to the mod page. 1. Fun Conquest system. The conquest system is amazing, it gives you a group of battalions and challenges to complete to acquire more. Then it sends you off to fight a long battle against the enemy of your choice. I will definitely admit that it was inspired by the Gates of Hell Ostfront conquest system. All of this can be played with multiplayer among your friends. 2. Great front line battles. In this game mode you are given one task, take as much ground as you can. How you do that is entirely up to you. Whether you rush with tanks, soften up your target with arty, or flank with special forces, is all up to you. It is a very fun and addicting game mode. That I think can be more expanded on. 3. Incredibly fun entrenchment system. I can already say that in the one day I've been playing Men of War II that I've built more impressive fortifications, than I have in almost any other game. You get an engineer company that spawns in when you need it, to build defenses. You can dig trenches, set barb wire, construct hedgehogs, build bunkers, pillboxes, and dugouts, you can also place mines of both AT and AA variety, I could go on. I have become the engineer from TF2 on steroids many a time in this game. 4. And lastly unit variety. The level of tanks, guns, artillery, and planes that you can utilize in your game is astonishing. Like you don't just have one variant of a T34, but you have the whole gang ready to kick ass. This makes me very happy to see all the different types of units in the game. I could be wrong about this, so don't quote me, but there might even be more types of units than Gates of hell or MOWAS2. Are there some issues which need to be sorted out yes, but to shoot down this game, and its potential isn't right. I belive that this game deserves a chance, even in spite of some glaring issues. Would I recomend the game in its current state, maybe, but only if you are aware that this game needs some time to take off and be better. I sincerly hope that the developers will listen to their community and not just shun them. Most of the feed back is genuinely trying to improve the game, and shouldn't be overlooked. I have 0 idea if the developers are going to listen to their community or not. But, I am personally having a blast pushing back the Fascists to Berlin. So, yes if you are aware of the issues, and still want it, then get it.

_childDocuments_.review: Having a blast with this game so far, there are so many different modes and the game play is fast-paced and fluid (there are sooo many qualify of life features not found in previous iterations or gates of hell). It's somewhat more arcadey than gates of hell, but still leans heavily towards the realism side of the spectrum (far more than any other RTS not named gates of hell or men of war assault squad 2). Looking forward to playing this game for years to come, it's a refreshing take on the gameplay formula. Ignore the negative reviews, they come from butthurt fanboys who are throwing a temper tantrum that this isn't a copy+paste of men of war assault squad 2 or gates of hell (it's a different game people, it's not supposed to be exactly the same). Most of the criticisms aren't even based on good-faith complaints and lack a basis in realty. The criticisms can pretty much be summed as follows: (1) there is always online functionality --> the developers are already working on a patch so that singleplayer will not require internet connection--it probably should have been that way to start, but hardly a reason to throw a hissy fit]; (2) there are vehicle health bars --> every men of war game + gates of hell has vehicle health bars, they are just hidden - MOW2 just displays it visually. You can also disable vehicle health bars being displayed if you choose. (3) clunky UI and controls --> I have no idea what people are even complaining about here because no one can give any examples. I've played hundreds of hours of GoH and Mow Assault Squad 2, and the UI and controls here are significantly more fluid and intuitive than both those games. Not to mention the amount of quality of life features that are a breath of fresh air for the franchise (such as requiring much less micro to make entrenchments for soldiers and weapon emplacements, less micro to set mines and barriers, highly responsive unit movement, etc.) (4) the game was misrepresented as being something else (aka it's not a copy + paste of GoH or MoW Assault Squad 2) --> they literally had multiple open betas and a flood of information on what this game would be, the only people not knowing what this game was going to be before release were intentionally ignorant. (4)(a) it's not a copy + paste of GoH & MoWAS2 (see the dozens of complaints stating, "well GoH/MoWAS2 does it this way") --> this is a different game, an evolution in the series, it's not supposed to feel exactly like the previous games in the franchise. There would be no point in making a new game if it was just going to play exactly the same as previous entries in the franchise, may as well just make DLC for those games at that point.This game has been a breath of fresh air in the Men of War franchise and scratches a different itch. It's more PvP friendly (including matchmaking, thank god--I was never interested in multiplayer in these games until MOW2) and faster-paced, thereby providing a different and fun-filled experience while being within the same sub-genre as previous entries in the franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: Giving this a thumbs down for now, but stay tuned as this game has potential but was in no shape to leave early access. Most of the negative reviews are from former mow2as / goh players who haven't played the classic mode in this game - so they are unfamiliar to the new battlegroups game mode which the devs have tried to force popularity of. I myself am not a fan of the game mode, as it has numerous problems which I'll cover in detail later. For now though, the game is in a playable state but not without complications.1.) Servers. The lag is slightly better than multiplayer GoH and mow2as, you're mostly playing on dedicated servers. However, I've had matches with 200ms to 7 second lag spikes which made the game just about unplayable. Not sure what's going on there, the devs claim to be working on server infrastructure. "We'll see". Lag has almost always been a problem in the RTS genre, so my fingers aren't crossed that it'll get any better. 2.) Players who disconnect or rage quit. If a player disconnects or rage quits, you don't get their units. The AI will not take over for that player. That is game breaking for me. It happened to me in my 2nd pvp match and I ended up quitting as I did not get an increased income so why play a 2v4? 3.) Lobbies, as of right now you cannot see player rank or win / loss statistics. There is a learning curve with this game, especially those new to RTS and mow2as - and it's extremely frusturating playing with random players on your team against what is possibly a stacked discord team that put in many hours during the beta. There are many password protected lobbies, and the game will not save my filter changes so I am constantly having to apply "unlocked" to the filters so I don't see password protected lobbies. It's a time waste. The lobby screen could be better designed, but works much better than GoH. If you're playing a battlegroups lobby, you'll more often be kicked for being AFK if you're editing your battlegroup. There is no notification system when your editing units to let you know that the lobby is full or the host is ready to start. So, more often than not your sitting in a lobby for 15-30 minutes waiting for the game to start with nothing to do. 4.) The "battlegroups game mode" or whatever this new game style the devs are trying to push. I don't like it. You get 4 units type per phase and there are 3 phases. So 12 units you can field altogether. You can customize each phase to a preset that the devs have designed for each division, while this sounds like a unique and interesting concept - it brings potential problems. One of which, players who have decks that are all artillery - or full of useless ♥♥♥♥ that won't help win a match and end up causing the team to try to clutch burning through their own units to carry that particular player. You can't in a lobby, see your teams battlegroup composition. You can only form a guess and hope that the player is competent enough to create an all round battlegroup that can handle all scenarios. Some battlegroups are lacking anti air, which is a huge problem as plane spam is real and very OP in this game - until you wipe out the planes that is. I like classic mode, as I don't have squads that I can't disband into individual units. I can select a variety of units to meet whatever obstacle comes my way on the battlefield. I can also place more units down. It's basically mow2as. How the game should have been designed in the first place. 5.) Vehicle speed / vehicle movement mechanics. Vehicle speed is all over the place in this game, wildly varying across units. You have scout cars hauling ass performing 90 degree abrupt turns. Anti tank guns that rotate incredibly fast - unrealisticly so that it's distracting and takes away from focus needed in crucial times. I could write more negative bullet points but I'm not going to bother. The game has potential, but it needs A LOT of work. It should have never left Early Access. I think the missions and story line is great. Artwork is on point. Unit models look great. Etc. This is in no way going to dominate Gates of Hell other than the multiplayer - when the servers are stable, actually provide somewhat of a better play experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish I could recommend this. The game itself, judged by itself, is not bad - but is not what I expected or hoped for. Coming from playing the other MoW titles, this didn't deliver on the same level at all. The best and short way to describe the experience was a more mainstreamed RTS with heavy MoW influence.While some mechanics such as air units, formations, fortifying buildings, squads automatically throwing grenades from garrisoned buildings, specifically the trenches in this title, and mechanics otherwise found in mods in previous titles (such as paratroopers) were welcome and a nice additions, the rest of the game fell short. To start off, I'm basing this from expectation of previous titles. The new modes are interesting in their own right and adds what I can only describe as competitive gameplay to a game I wouldn't call competitive. The path they chose for this game is what all other modern titles coming out chose as well. A broader audience and something more standard and competitive with balance at the helm. I'm not calling the other games unbalanced, but this definitely feels like it has taken a Company of Heros 2 side. This feels like 60% of a MoW title and 40% of a CoH title, and I don't believe they should have mixed. I did try the classic mode, and it was at first a hopeful sight into what I was already mixed about. Unfortunately, despite the classic mode being close enough to the original titles, the core game itself still felt off from what Men of War encapsulated. I really do think this comes down to the fine details of what the other games delivered and this one doesn't. The way buildings fell apart and crumbled in previous titles. The ruggedness of micromanaging units and creating your own squads. The viscerality of each firefight feeling so much more realistic. Such examples are things that simply do not deliver in the sequel. Aside from modes, graphically the game has taken a much less grittier tone, and is way more vibrant in color and saturation. The blood added feels as if it was put in simply to say they still have some maturity to it. I'm not saying the premise is docile or anything, but I can't say it comes off as anything but watered down.Mechanically the game has taken a step back and a step forward equally with player agency. Limiting engineers and medics to be entirely AI controlled and calling them in to a task as if they were a script is just an off feeling I can't shake. Then capabilities of said engineers is great though, the extra building options with bunkers and pillboxes is neat. Combining engineers and miners is an odd choice as well, cutting down on different units as well as agency. Maybe this next gripe is my inexperience with the game, but the infantry squads being called in always staying in their own group as a macro on the left side is annoying. Previous titles allowed you to select whatever unit and form them into their own squad/element. If I call in 5 riflemen, they remain the same squad despite separating them or even trying to halve them with another squad or unit. The lack of terrain deformation is also either super underwhelming or no where close to where it should be. Creating your own cover with a large enough explosion so your infantry can lie down in the crater for cover is a much lower possibility compared to previous titles. The game wholely feels more streamlined for broader audiences while catering closer to a competitive side as well. In short the game feels watered/dumbed down from previous titles and lost a lot of it's charm. There are a bunch of other things that I could add but the list is long and I've written enough. The game at this state is not something I can recommend if you're coming for a true Men of War title. If this is your first time playing a Men of War title, you may enjoy it, but this isn't for me.

_childDocuments_.review: As of the time of me writing this, the reviews are Mixed.  If one filters for more than 1 hour of playtime, the reviews then become Mostly Positive.  MoW2 has 12 tutorials that would be tough to finish in an hour and some of them show off features that are seemingly misunderstood by some of the reviews up now.Also, before the game was released, but after streams were available, there was commentary in Steam general discussion about how X feature is better in Y game, but Z feature was better in this game.  And, overwhelming, the position of the community was a rebuke of that.  The rebuttals were ALWAYS essentially, "this genre is very small, we don't take sides, and we love each of the few games we have for their particular strengths."  Then, at release, everything turned tribal.I just wanted to set the table on what I have seen in the first week of release.  Take that for what you will.Personally, I think the game is quite enjoyable, especially with a friend in co-op.  Like the early general discussion vibes, I think the RTT sub-genre under the Gem game engine has many offspring and each of them offer different strengths and weaknesses.MoW2:++Lots of game modes and ALL of them are playable versus AI in solo or co-op++A few of these modes offer technology unlocks/progression between linked missions which is a great way to enjoy co-op++Many options to customize game modes (such as Realism mode or if individual status icons are on--the so called "health bars" for example)++AI of Gem games tends to be pretty iffy. Although MoW2 has some issues, generally the AI is often surprisingly competent to engaging which makes the solo and co-op rather enjoyable.++A refreshingly robust fortification system via off field engineers (but that's in a tutorial I think most skipped)++Territory pushing modes and the Battalion system really emphasized the combined arms element (and composition liabilities)++OUTSTANDING implementation of Ultra-Ultra Wide resolution which is rather rare nowadays on even AAA games (let alone when previous GEM games were released)--As an English speaker, the American voices seem too old for combat age and jarringly campy in their content--Vehicle pathfinding is a bit frustrating--Combat pacing can be a bit fast as vehicle movement speed and scope of the battle can require dividing attention and multi-tasking more often associated with RTS games (which is maybe why some say "arcade-like" though I disagree with that assertion)--UI scaling and positioning options would be nice for higher resolutions (like they did with the map GUI)

_childDocuments_.review: Really don't understand the negative reviews at all, there is a lot of content and pretty good models, the AI is the least jankie I've seen in this title. The game modes are fun and offer endless replay-ability, and streamline a lot of stuff that was annoying in GoH. Always needing to be online IS annoying at times, but I've only had one issue with this playing single player, and I'm literally in a place that needs StarLink in order to be online, So I don't really see the issue here besides people just not having a good internet connection, and also, the devs HAVE said MULTIPLE times they are fixing this mistake. which I agree with, it's a mistake. I play on realistic settings, so I have no idea what people are talking about when they say there are health bars. The sounds are terrible, they sound bad, I highly recommend the BattleField sound mod, its so much better. Combat feels fun, I actual can use scouts to scout positions without the AI just immediately seeing them and sniping them. also the garrison in building options is A LOT better than having to place my soldiers in the perfect position in a building in order for them to have a good shot at the enemy. and being able to have those troops fortify a building is great for holding locations from other infantry. The trench function is great, the only problem is having it cave in on troops and they just die, which is very annoying. but something you need to realize that will happen when you are the commander of troops in The Second World War. I've also seen a complaint about constantly needing to move artillery around because counter artillery and aircraft can track where they are shooting from and fire back at them. Ya, that is how real artillery works. Like look it up. ask a artilleryman what its like shooting and moving all the time. its a MoW title, its hard, you are gonna lose. Learn some defense in depth and hasty ambushes to counteract that. that is what the title has always offered. All in all its not perfect by any means. but I am having an absolute blast playing. and do not believe it deserves the ridiculous, Purist hate it is receiving right now. _childDocuments_.review: As a longtime veteran and fan of RTS and RTT games like age of empires and dawn of war, I really am trying hard to like this game, the explosions are cool, there seems to be a ton of detail in the units and equipment. I don't care so much that the game is "always online" I like the concepts and playing multiplayer with a group of matchmade individuals is neat. What prompted me to write this review? After playing multiplayer with my friends for a couple nights, I decided to try campaign to get better and maybe unlock some stuff. The first mission of the german campaign literally takes over 20 minutes of dialogue in-game before any enemies start attacking. I found myself repeatedly just begging the captain to shut up. Then I saw that on medium difficulty the enemy will spawn about eight tanks and over 30 infantry units, leaving me with almost nothing left. It seems like the structured missions are like that. You get a handful of guys, no reinforcements and the enemy gets hundreds of guys and you have to pick them apart in a really slow and tedious way. My problem with the game is that their UI and actual controls when you get down to it are horrible. Attack move is F5, crouching your units is Page down? Run is U? It's an unintuitive mess of shift and control modifiers and this is the only RTS game I've found where I needed to rebind almost every single key they had in order for it to be ~almost enjoyable. Microing units is the main point of the game and they often just behave erratically, don't shoot, run out of cover. There's no shift queueing commands. I just hit alt f4 after I right clicked my trench of 5 guys to fire at a rifleman that was standing in the open firing at me, and they decided to all jump out of the trench and were obliterated by a single shell.

_childDocuments_.review: I have spent about 6 hours with this game so far - Here are my thoughts after purchasing the game, panic refunding it after 30 minutes of play, and then re-purchasing again the next day after thinking it over: I understand why people are complaining about this game and are comparing it mainly to "Call to Arms - Gates of Hell: Ostfront". Of these two titles, I will say that "Ostfront" is for the more hardcore RTS fan, as it is WAY more realistic, better physics, more immersive, etc.Men of War 2 is quite different, and feels more like an "arcade" or "casual" experience (although the game IS quite complex and full of features). I originally gave this game a negative review because my expectations were set on 'Ostfront', which is clearly the superior title. That being said, this game seems more 'fast paced' and 'cartoony'? It's worth noting that Men of War 2 DOES contain many features that I thought were clever, and the defensive fortifications and trench building are pretty cool. The "front line" that moves with the battle is awesome, and if you go in with the right expectations, I think you will enjoy yourself.My ONLY gripe so far (other than the odd crashes in the menus) is the fact that you CANNOT control infantry in "third/first person direct control". This is a HUGE let down and likely is one of the main reasons people turn away from this title and go for "Ostfront" instead. If they could ADD this feature, it would GREATLY improve the experience.Also, when you select "Direct Control", there needs to be a way to change the DEFAULT CONTROL type, so I don't have to hit TWO BUTTONS every time I want to drive a tank (it defaults to the horrible top-down-from-the-sky Direct Control mode, where as the first person/3rd person should be able to be selected BY DEFAULT). Many other "Best Way" titles have this option, so it was frustrating that it was left out here (correct me if i'm wrong, I could not find a setting to change this).The "Inventory" applet should also remember its position when you hit the "x" button or close it. Each time you bring up the Inventory screen, it defaults back to the upper left corner and blocks the interface. If you are looking for more WW2 gaming action, this one seems to provide a ton of content/missions and actually EXPLAINS each game mode before you launch a Skirmish. This was VERY helpful, as the sheer number of game modes for multiplayer is INSANE and seem fun (although I haven't tried many of them yet).The front line represented by a blue/red shifting boundary was really cool as well; reminded me of watching old WW2 documentaries when they detail how the front line moves around."Ostfront" also takes HOURS to play most single missions, and so far, I think this game will be a more casual experience when you don't want to eat up 3 hours to finish one mission (which IS cool, but not all the time). I don't think this game deserves so much negativity and poor reviews, but it is VERY MUCH NOT at the same level as Gates of Hell. If you go in with this in mind, and don't get scared off by learning the new interface and controls, I think there are hundreds of game-play hours available here... especially with friends in CO-OP mode.I place this game WELL ABOVE "Company of Heroes 3", but it does fall short of "Ostfront" and is far less of a 'simulation' of WW2, as much as it is just a fun arcade version.***SIDE NOTE*** The voice acting is TERRRRRRRRRRIBLE... ESPECIALLY the United States (quite insulting to Americans I would imagine). Why do they have to yell stupid things like "We're gonna spread Freedom like WILDFIRE" *cringe*I live in Canada and I'm STILL embarrassed by the portrayal of the United States Army (voice overs).Other than that... it's worth a buy if it's on sale. Hopefully the rest of the bugs will be ironed out, and the little problems addressed by the developers.I can't really be TOO hard on them, as their offices are in Ukraine and we all know how hard life must be over there.Stay SAFE everyone!

_childDocuments_.review: Well... I must say, im surprised to see so many negative reviews. I understand the frustration of some of the players, i really do, I also played MOWAS2 and this game is not that. but i would not say this is worse. In fact, Id rank this higher than assault squad 2 for several reasons:the first being, the large difference of performance compared to previous games and competitors like gates of hell.the visuals are also so much better, still quite tacky, but an improvement and personally i prefer the brightness and colourfulness of this game. Another plus for this game is the vast amount of game modes and the option to switch between 'competetive' and 'realism' to be able to increase or decrease the more 'arcade' feel to the game. I must say however, i really love the conquest mode. Being a big Pay2Win fan, e.g war thunder, WOT, Enlisted, i love the fact the they included a tech tree similar to MOW:arena when it was out. It actually gives me a sense of progress and thats what i enjoy most about gaming. Some negatives however. pathing is not the best at all, many times i have lost a gun emplacement or cover due to a tank driving through instead of round it. Another thing that annoys me is even in realism, i find it near enough impossible to not 'crush' a tanks hull, burn it down or ammo rack it, therefore leading to being unable to capture it. gates of hell seems to have the cleanest system for this. Also, PLEASE nerf artillery more again. Even AI are getting 100% accurate shots on my tanks within seconds of opening fire.i would like to say tho. great game, well done devs. Theres bound to be teething problems and issues, but i respect your decisions to create what is a new (yet familiar) game with some of the old bits and bobs included. I have to also say again, that this is not AS2, it's just men of war 2, and therefore an opening to the next series of MOW's hopefully. maybe the next AS (if there is one) will be similar to AS2 and that way some people can stop moaning.

_childDocuments_.review: While this game takes many good components from previous games, it does have a decent amount of new concepts. Unfortunately, many of the changes are done to make the game more "arcadey", which is why i believe many people are now comparing this to COH. Multiplayer is only battalions mode, as queuing for a classic game can take a half hour at least. Placing engineer obstacles are often blocked by invisible objects. Units sometimes shoot through hills/cliffs like they dont exist. If you tell your soldier to throw a grenade at someone, and its outside of their throwing range, sometimes theyll just throw it in a random direction, instead of moving in-range to throw it. Unit damage is inconsistent and feels unpolished. Any reasonable distance means your soldiers will have to shoot 1000 bullets to kill someone. Tanks have hitpoints, so even if you shoot at a tank with a very large gun, its going to take 3 hits no matter what. I find that in this game it is much harder to make up for having a poorly performing teammate than in MOWAS2, so if you end up with a dud, you are more likely to notice, even with the AI units. I believe this game is better than vanilla MOWAS2 but is many many steps behind MOWAS2 ROBZ mod. It feels like this game takes a lot of steps back from previous games. Right click IS NOT attack move. I understand this game was made by a different studio than the previous games, but it feels like they didnt even play the other games.

_childDocuments_.review: MoW2 deserves much more praise than its currently given, having mixed reviews at the time of typing this review upThe game has its issues as of launch, having a requirement to always be online and forcing players who play single player to connect to a server still, which is absolutely valid criticism that the developers should heavily consider changing.In my experience so far there are some issues here and there such as pathing can occasionally be a bit odd to a point where it can possibly lead to the loss of a unit. I have also seen some UI bugs with displaying the correct resources available to you in the technology tree and barracks.Of course there are some other small issues that i have forgot to mention here but nothing that has been game breaking so far.On the positive side, playing MoW2 on release has been pretty refreshing, all content released so far (to my knowledge) is fully playable coop with multiple friends (up to 5 i believe). With a variety of new yet familiar game modes to tackle.The performance of the game compared to MoWAS2 and previous titles is far better from my own experience, with experiences in the past titles dropping me well below the 60 mark even while on top end hardware. The always online feature has never shot me in the foot so far, not experiencing any lag or disconnects while playing both with and without friends.Developers have shown to take action on community feedback and have communicated intent to continue. If the price tag is too steep or your not ready for the changes to the IP that MoW2 brings, crack on with Assault Squad 2 until either the game seems to be in a state your happy with or it goes on sale. The negative feedback although warranted shouldn't cloud the good things that the developers have been doing for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally write game reviews but this game seems to have received a lot of sub 1 hour reviews on release day from Gates of Hell fans that are simultaneously claiming the game shouldn't exist as its just a copy of GoH whilst also complaining the game is nothing like GoH... Very weird.The default gamemode in MoW2 is a lot faster paced than the original game, Assault Squad and GoH iterations. The gameplay lands somewhere between Assault Squad and the original Company of Heroes. Personally I prefer this as it means the multiplayer matches are pretty fast paced with little downtime. It keeps you engaged for the duration of the 30ish minute match rather than slowing to a crawl as the older games tend to.There have been numerous quality of life updates that automate some of the more tedious micro-management that that older games are famous for. You can still access the inventory of each unit and micromanage at that level if you want however the new UI does not make this clear or simple to do and if someone is unfamiliar with the previous games they are unlikely to even know the functionality exists. There is serious room for improvement in the GUI.There is a realistic gamemode for those that prefer something closer to the classic MoW experience but it is not well advertised on the game menu and you have to enable it via an option buried in sub-menus. There is also a custom game lobby with tons of customisation options that is also weirdly not highlighted in the menu. Similarly to the in-game GUI, the menu system could do with some serious redesign to improve readability and properly advertise the features to new users.Ultimately the gameplay is good, the multiplayer is well paced and fun. The battalion gamemode reminds me of World in Conflict and Wargame, restricting the player to a subset of units and encouraging teamplay. Its early days yet and I have not put in enough hours to identify balance issues so I cannot comment there, but it does feel like good plays are rewarded and bad plays lead to your units getting annihilated in short order.The menus and GUI readability is rough and I imagine one of the major causes of people seemingly misunderstanding or simply completely missing some of the games features.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really looking forward to this release, but sadly I was disappointed. The UI is very confusing, the gameplay modes do not always make much sense, and the combat mechanics are very cartoonish compared to Gates of Hell. There are also only three factions in the game. I do not want to discourage the developers; they clearly put a lot of work into this release and it shows. But frankly, many of the design choices are strange. As several reviews have mentioned, there seems to be an attempt to make Men of War play a lot more like Company of Heroes or Wargame. That is a grave mistake. In short: the game has great potential, but it needs around another year of development to get where it needs to be if the developers wish to salvage what is here. There are some very interesting and quite innovative features on offer (matchmaking, campaign modes, various XP tracking, customized battalions, etc.). The good does not outweigh the bad here. Right now, MoW II just comes up short.

_childDocuments_.review: Men of War has finally reached the modern era. The graphics have been updated, sounds, animations and UI especially. But the biggest improvement has been to the gameplay. Especially in the quality of life department. Men of War was known for being more convoluted than complex and that problem has been finally addressed. No longer do you manually set up defenses, emplacements or other tactical implements. The game now gives you the option to order your troops to do those things rather than forcing you to direct control or fiddle with menus. Another great change is also the ability to retreat troops that are no longer needed at the front. You now get all the tactical depth of the original series but are now able to play it without requiring a 200 hour crash course.Another great change is the many modes to play the game. You have classic PVP from the old school, the modern Battalion system which is more small scale and focus. PVE. 2 campaigns, the rush missions and the ability to play in CO-OP any single player content. If you are a fan of RTSes and especially MoW I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Disappointment, is the order of the day! As a seasoned aficionado of the Men of War series, I was eagerly awaiting this latest rendition. Alas, it's as if they've injected it with some bizarre concoction that's left it in a state of malaise.Here's the rub: the pace is off. Infantry units drop like flies, and tanks—get this—come with health bars! It's like they're trying to turn a strategic masterpiece into a run-of-the-mill arcade game. Where's the challenge? Where's the depth?Craters from explosions can’t be used as cover as they could in the past, in fact it looks like the men just float over them.At present there are only 3 fractions (US, Germany and Soviets) the Allies and Japan are not in the war yet ... I’m sure they will arrive, but at what cost?In the solo campaign the change speed button might as well be a decorative paperweight. You're stuck hurtling through missions at breakneck speed, with no chance to catch your breath or formulate a decent plan.And the cherry on top? The darn thing requires an internet connection at all times. I don't know about you, but I like my games —offline and pain-free ... unless multiplayer is the order of the day and I'm the one bringing the pain.In short, what we have here is a promising concept marred by a series of inexplicable missteps. It's enough to make even the most stoic of gamers want to toss their keyboard out the window.That said, I do have hope that this game will make a recovery and get back on track with some updates to fix these problems and then some ... till then a thumbs down sadly!

_childDocuments_.review: yIKESEDIT: I believe this games UI is a bridge to far in the wrong direction. I'm not opposed to innovation, it's just that I believe previous titles had nailed this aspect down. Honestly, its a bit hard to read sometimes because its all scattered out so much and there isnt that banner at the bottom of the screen holding it all together anymore. Infantry handle very oddly. They feel like they're floating along the terrain, they feel like vehicles almost. The most important thing for me was the dynamic campaign. Damn, it was completely butchered into oblivion. The variety of missions in the campaign is cool for sure, but this is the only pro among cons. No more constructing your battalion from scratch anymore, just choose from the presets. In GOH, you had to build your forces from the bottom up, managing your research, munitions, stars, and supplies in order to defeat an enemy growing in tech just as you. The strategic resource management was taken out almost completely. The battles dont feel like they're connected at all, every battle you're basically using completely different units from the last. There's just a sliver of context connecting the battles to one another, just enough to call it a campaign at all. Another thing, the AMERICAN VOICE ACTING. It is a disaster. At least with the run of the mill units anyway. It feels like voice acting from the very first ww2 rts ever created, it completely takes me out of the immersion 110 percent. Whenever I hear it I just wish there wasn't any voice acting at all. Last but not least the online only aspect. Back when I was a freshman in high school, I looked forward to coming home and playing MOWAS2 on my pc. The only problem was, I didn't have internet access. I had to take my entire PC to the library in order to download the damn game. Today if I still didn't have internet access at home, order to play MOW2, I would need to take my PC to the library every day after school to play the game. That would really suck, Id be stuck watching diplexheated videos. I have over a thousand hours in the MOW series, and hopefully I have another thousand on the way. I got really burnt out playing GOH for so long, the dynamic campaign was very robust, but repetitive. I was hoping this game was going to take everything good about GOH's dynamic campaign and tack on even more features and replayability. As I explained above I probably wont be touching it anytime soon. I understand It's easy to critique games from a player's perspective. I tried to not be a complete azz explaining why I cant enjoy this game to its fullest potential rn. I love the MOW series and the developers behind it, I just couldn't in good faith recommend this game to a MOW fan atm.2nd EDIT: Da germans are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ blue3rd EDIT: I just wanted to say, after playing GOH for another 100 hours or so, I have no idea why this game exists. Who is this game designed for? Not for me. Not to be an insufferable entitled gamer or anything, but I feel like I can comfortably represent the fan base of MOW after growing up with it. (It's even my most played series of all time) The multiplayer is whatever, I've hardly played multiplayer at all across the MOW games becuase I dont like to sweat every time i play the damn game. But, I have many questions. Why doesn't this game feature as many or more assets for the editor than GOH? Why is this game's dynamic campaign a pathetic excuse for a gamemode? (See above for gripes about this) And again who is this game made for? It's almost as if the MOW series tried to conceive some unholy, unwanted, unloved baby with COH. I cant stress this enough, PLEASE DO NOT COPY NOR TAKE INSPIRATION FROM COH. you will deny it, but everyone and their inbred cousin knows that this game was designed to be more accessible to the general audience. Well, it turns out, arcade WW2 RTS games are a dime a dozen, and the only reason MOW stuck out was because of its mods, and the fact that the gameplay was more gritty and realistic than the competitors. Congrats for becoming the ultimate mid-tier ww2 RTS. I hope the execs are proud of their mistakes. Sincerely, the entitled gamer.

_childDocuments_.review: I own one of the earlier games but never got around to playing it. Bought this one on launch (before the reviews dropped) looked like it could've been a potential diamond among the garbage that's been dropping lately. No spyware anti-cheat or DRM? Nice! ...Oh. It's always-online, even for local singleplayer missions. Right. Of course it is. Had to ruin it somehow. Apparently, the devs are going to "fix" the singleplayer connectivity requirement eventually, if their unprofessional and occasionally petty responses to other negative reviews is anything to go by. If that actually happens, I'll re-visit this review. In the meantime, FQ, here's a pro tip: being petty or hostile in review replies is only going to make things worse.I've also heard that modding has been restricted in this game compared to prior releases. That's a hard "no" from me. I don't have to have experience with previous releases to recognize that as a bad thing in its entirety. I watched as Relic locked down their engine more and more with each subsequent COH title. It didn't help them, and it's not going to help you. I get why you're doing it. You want to make sure modders can't compete with your DLC. Every dev team who allows modding goes through this. Paradox Interactive is currently fighting a war against itself over how to handle it. But the conundrum has already been answered by games like Rimworld: if your DLC is of high enough quality, you don't have to compete with modders, they'll be lining up in droves to make their content work alongside every new DLC released.I'll put this one on ice for now. Recommend holding off until the devs address some of the concerns raised by others.

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of series since Faces of war and one who has almost 3000 hrs in MoW AS2, I must admit that this part is a huge dissapointment. Not only because it start reminding me of Company of Heroes in some way. But let's start with positives. The first one is the idea of setting your own troops and there specialty, that’s something I missed in AS2. The next one is the scale of maps, ofc in a previous part we also had big maps, but now they are playable and more important, they are a main idea of the game. Also the idea of taking land, not specific points is interesting, but I would keep a game mode with flags as well. Adding planes, more weapons and most important, ability to building more fortifications! I would only change the look of some of them because they look weird, like in COH. That’s the end of the positive changes.... Now it will be bitter. First of all, the graphic design of the game, doesn’t really look better than AS2. It looks as if creators really wanted to make a game like Company of Heroes, maps are washed out of colour, vibe and climate. Buildings are boring and remind me of nothing. Because of that it’s really hard to play, no joke, units are so bad to navigate, now I have problems with finding them... even after I remove grass in options. Also the design of units remind me of COH, tanks and stuff look more squat, heavier etc.. Why weren’t the proportions from the previous edition preserved? About the look, the interface is now less readable. You added more options, I get it, but even though it’s bigger you make it totally illegible... The only thing that keeps the level is a mini map. Moreover, graphic design of it is outdated = illegible and making it more transparent doesn't help. Now, let's talk about the game mechanics. First of all, playing infantry is worthless, infantry now is more like nice addition to a battlefield with spectacular animation of death, than useful. You tried to make it realistic like in a simulator, so now they die after almost one shoot... Moreover, the idea of battle groups without ability to split them is ridiculous. In this part, soldiers don’t have raison d'être. In AS2 you think about every single soldier, taking care of him and his eq, now they are just some groups that could be killed by one medium tank HE. I really miss having fun playing soldiers. Concerning units, personal setting squads before the game is fine, but splitting them in three Eszelons is not so. For example, a unit of AT rifle squad, where are 4 guys with pzb, nothing else... etc. That’s bad, that you reduced fractions to only 3 in very weird, mixed up way.  As for tanks and other heavy stuff, now a tank fight's look more like in COH again... you add more notifications about damage parts, so when you shoot all you see is a bunch of yellow and red unimportant letters.... too much of this. Now tank battles looks like in Coh. Mechanic of damage was a way better at AS2. Now it more looks like bullets exchange until someone’s health bar ends. As for battlefields, fights are now so dynamic that you can’t focuse on anything, there are now more explosions, more than in Michael Bay’s film. Infantry is fragile, so the map becomes empty very quickly and turns into fight between artylery and planes. Regarding planes, they make so much mess right now that the battlefield is turning chaotic very fast. I like that the artylery is now visible while shooting, that is huge plus,  but mostly is too overpowered. It’s really hard to focus on battlefield, vechicles are too fast (after one patch, I saw you make them a bit slower, good change.) I really wanted to write about all the problems I have with this game, but to be honest, it's too exhausting. MOW AS2 was a great game, good continuator of your fantastic series that have uniqe approach to real time strategy games. Ofc there was a lot of problems, mostly with engine, lack of maps, poor multiplayer, balance etc. You really had an opportunity to continue the series with dignity, to upgrade previous one in many ways. What I see here is a try to make something different mostly with ghosting COH. It was really nesessary. Now it’s just an average game from steam COH wannabe, chaotic, with attention spam like on tiktok, and effects like in B class action movies... I’m really dissapointed, as a turbo fan of the series. That’s my opinion after intense gaming, If it weren't for the name, I wouldn't know I was playing MOW. I'm sorry for such a harsh opinion, but I hope you will read it and take it seriously, because it comes from the heart. Greetings from Poland, Slava Ukraini!

_childDocuments_.review: Many opinions are floating around about this being a rendering of Men of War into mainstream... "it's too arcade-y," "it's fisher price," "it's too much alike CoH," are just a few of the comments I've seen.I would like to address these with the fact there is a great plethora of options to make the game alike it's ancestors. i.e. classic mode (making the primary play aspects more like Men of War: Assault Squad 2), and realism. (making the damage thresholds for vehicles and infantry more alike classic MoW. i.e. no health bars, just area based damage.)Moreover. The commitment to quality on this product is satisfactory. They are not EVER going to add micro-transactions. There is a wide range of content that is unlocked quickly through just enjoying the game-play... your first lot of PVP matches will unlock something basically every time.There is next to no bugs whatsoever; I haven't seen a single glitch so far, check my hours. And, the content provided, if it seems silly, or cheap in any way, is easily because this is not a AAA company.Lastly, the devs are passionate and want to continue improving MoW2. It's a solid game. It's primary modes are not exactly alike MoW: AS2, but far less "arcade-y" than games such as CoH2 (to which I've played a lot of).If you like MoW, you'll enjoy this game. Supporting it means a lot as the devs are not an arm of a mega-company like SEGA. They are passionate about making an excellent WW2 simulator, and a fun video game.Stick that in your pipe and smoke it!
