_childDocuments_.review: Following the same pattern that other games have failed forcing players to be online constantly, just like the other games this one has failed, needing access to constant wifi isnt a issue for most but i personally am constantly downloading games, with this forced online status it causes me to load considerately longer looking for a match when im just trying to play the campaign solo,speaking of campaign, soldiers die way to easily when playing the game in normal and you have no way of bring them back to life, in other games you'd have a medic in the group but not this, you play each part of the mission and expect the game to give a decent amount of troops for the next great push but you are left with nothing having to try to finish the mission with the few remaining soldiers.The HUD is really odd, in previous games they did it where all options were in the bottom right of the screen, making it easy to figure out what you want to do as you aren't trying to remember where what is and searching the screen for things, example, in vehicles, the dismount vehicle is on the far left side next to the map (which took me a while to find) and your fire modes are on the far right corner, but to set up sandbags they stuffed is down the middle bottom of the screen, They do this with normal foot soldiers as well which starts to make it look really clustered cause you have 15 different options on the middle bottom bar, now to note this can be easy to deal with if you just learn the keybinds. but that shouldnt be a requirement otherwise what's the point of showing all the bottons, it would be better to clean up the hud and make people learn the keybinds from the beginning. The tutorial is also a bit outdated for a game released in 2024.not giving us a physical show and tell tutorial is just outdated, i know lots of people that don't want to spend 6 hours reading text when it pops up on their screen, it's easier to have someone voice over the text and allow us to learn by doing.just my rant ofc, im not going to say i recommend this game yet, but if they manage to fix up the hud then i'd recommend the game, the other issues stated aren't big issues and most people will just adjust around it, but the hud is a make or break in my opinion

_childDocuments_.review: Men of War II? A Grand Return to WWII Battlefields! (ฅ'ω'ฅ)"This game excels with its detailed WWII strategy and immersive campaigns, though it struggles with UI complexity and voice acting, making it a must-play for RTS enthusiasts."Men of War II, the highly anticipated sequel to the acclaimed RTS series, offers a rich and immersive World War II experience. This game excels in combining historical accuracy with action-packed gameplay, featuring new units, locations, and campaigns across both the Eastern and Western Fronts. With its advanced AI and detailed visual and audio presentation, Men of War II sets a new benchmark for the series, providing a diverse range of strategic options and gameplay modes.Men of War II builds upon its predecessors by introducing an extensive array of units, each with specialized roles. Players can lead their troops through intense real-time battles, employing sophisticated military strategies, from laying ambushes to capturing enemy vehicles. The Direct Control feature allows precise management of any unit on the field, adding a layer of depth to the gameplay. Whether you’re commanding artillery, armor, infantry, or support units, the game’s mechanics are finely tuned to provide a challenging and rewarding experience.The game offers three narrative campaigns that immerse players in different perspectives of WWII: defending the Soviet Union against the Nazi onslaught, commanding US forces in Normandy, and experiencing the Wehrmacht’s retreat to Berlin. Additionally, historical campaigns inspired by Operation Bagration and Operation Overlord provide a more open-ended experience. The multiplayer mode is expansive, supporting battles from 1v1 to 5v5, with various modes including ranked matches and customizable lobbies. This breadth ensures that both single-player and multiplayer enthusiasts find ample content to enjoy.While Men of War II impresses with its realistic models and detailed WWII locations, it sometimes falters in visual clarity during hectic battles. The UI, although customizable, can be overwhelming, making it difficult to manage units efficiently. The game's voice acting also leaves much to be desired, often feeling lackluster and out of place. However, the overall sound design and ambient effects enhance the immersion, providing a gripping wartime atmosphere.Men of War II successfully continues the legacy of the series with its blend of historical fidelity and dynamic gameplay. Despite some issues with UI complexity and voice acting, the game's strategic depth and variety of content make it a must-play for RTS fans. Whether you're a veteran of the series or a newcomer, Men of War II offers a comprehensive and engaging WWII experience that is both challenging and rewarding. Its expansive multiplayer and modding support promise longevity and replayability, solidifying its place as a standout title in the RTS genre.Interested in discovering great Steam games? The design of the maps isn't too bad, a problem i do have with the game though is the HP system on the tanks, like yes this could be done for balancing purposes but when my IS-2 blows up because a rock fell on it when it was at 1HP, its kinda silly, so i believe if it worked more like Gates of Hell with a more modular based system it would significantly improve the value of tanks since they just seem like unstable pieces of machinery in their current state. I ended up discovering "Call to Arms - Gates of Hell Ostfront" and realized it is basically the same game as Men of War 2 but for a much cheaper price (on ♥♥♥) and a living online community. Despite improving on Assault Squad 2 engine and gameplay, the devs have dropped the ball on the release of this game and some fundamental architecture that make for a poor online matchmaking experience.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing a few different game modes, mostly cooperatively with friends, I think this game is a good (but not great) follow up if you are like me and liked the Assault Squad MoWs in the past, but never really did the non-assault squads.The default mode, battalions, is different and seems much more fast paced and focused around each player having only a handful of units. This makes coordinating with your team mates very important, and we have found the normal difficulty to be quite challenging to get the hang of in this game mode coming off of assault squad.However, the game has a "classic" mode and a "realism" option, that through my experience and the post release community post from the devs is much closer to the assault squad experience. It feels like it moves a little slower, and offers the much larger amount of units per player I am used to.I like the ability to switch between these modes and think the breadth of options are good, the only thing I truly miss is I cannot find out which game mode (if any) is the assault squad campaign classic of taking a series of points as the attackers vs AI defenders.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing 50 or So hours, i think i can make my mind of the gameI am suprisingly very happy with it. i was a bit scared at first with the first row of reviews, but i am glad to discover that i at least had a good time with it.//not native english sorry if its hard to read sometimes//Offline mode is supposed to come out soon soon tm (the devs have warned people before the release that the Offline mode would come out after some time, if people were a bit more carefull in what they buy , they wouldn't be shocked ). The AFK in solo is going to get fixed , the devs seems very active so far in the release and have addresed those points very quickly in the last patchnotes/devsnotes , and for this i can only apprieciate the work. i truly hope that it continues this way !----------------------------------The game has sadly a few issues that during my gameplay and my way of playing popped out a bit more than others-tanks pivoting in a wierd angle after arriving to destination, wierd path finding or getting stuck on seemeagly flat terrain. i'll bring up a few moreI wish the tutorial was in it's own ONGLET in the menu instead of " LEARN ", i wrongly assumed that similar to MOW:AS2, the tutorial would be semi-incorporated into the first campaign missions, while the campaign does explain you a few things here and there ( like mow:AS2), it lacks a lot of information, information that is better explain in the  tutorial missions, those are really well done and explain everything nicely. it's a shame i wasn't carefull enough to notice them sooner and i am sure a lot of people might have went over it ( and thus are missing a lot of information about the game ) In MOWAS2 , you could order a unit to do multitask back to back, by pressing shift, you could give a order that would be executed after the first was done. this allowed a bit of planning for some units, this seems to be gone, the tutorial doesn't address it ( or i missed it ), and i cannot find a key that would replace this feature that is very important to me. Self explanatory, both of those are missing, i assume they will either come later in form of DLC's or update. while it is certainly dissapointing, it is not THAT bothering. from my quick understanding and glance at the available units. ( could be wrong but it looks this way to me after a quick wiki check for mowas2 )  US GER AND CCCP seems to have more units than MOWAS2 US GER CCCP, they also have WAY more solo/co op content. so it makes up for the lack of UK & Japan. i still hope to see them and maybe other nations ( new nation or units incorporated in already existed nation ). added to the game with solo missiosn as well !i wish it was a lil cheaper, it would surely make more people willing to get it, and make up for the smaller price tag by having more people jump on it.------------------------------the solo/co op content difference between MOWAS2 & MOW2 is pretty much light and day. While MOWAS2 come with 8 missions per nation + 1 bonus mission. ( 41 in total )Those lack narritive story telling or focus on characters with names or anythign that would push you to give more interest in what you are doing on a bigger scale. And that missions really look like each other inbetween nations, in general following the  ( tutorial mission > cap point > Defence > Cap point > Stealth mission > cap point >  defence > Cap point ). MOW2 present itself with mutliple options :TUTORIAL = 12 missionsSTORY = 6 mission per nation  HISTORICAL = 7 missions each for CCCP & USA + 6 bonus missions Conquest = 16 mission each for US & CCCP + 32 mission for Germany ( randmoly generated campaign ) RAID =  16 missions for US & CCCP + 32 for Germany  ( randomly generated campaign )STORY & HISTORICAL will be missions with a narrative story telling ( 38 in total ), CONQUEST AND RAID are generated chains of missions in a order without the narrative story telling of the first two modes , the german campaign and US campaign were in particular VERY intersting due to the characters and events that happens during those them.I  praise this system enough, those 50 hours i have have been mostly playing campaign, i am having a amazing time. Simply put it's just way better, in all shape and form than MOWAS2, it's not even close as well, everything reads much easier, the information is way more clear and fits the visual of the game better.Something new that i welcome a lot is the battalions/regiment system. for those who have played wargame red dragon, or know how decks work in this type of strategy game, you are presented with a similar idea. You pick a nation and a battalion, this battalion come with advantage and disadvantage and discout modifier. Each nations has **15** different Battalions . EXEMPLE :  the CCCP 1st artillery regiment will allow you to field more powerfull support guns than other regiments/battalions, but lacks specialized units and increase the rank modifier of basic infantry and lack proper turreted tanks. PS : If you do not like this new sytem (  i was sketpitcal at it at first, but learnt to love it. ) there is the classic mode, that uses a more similar deployment system as in MOWAS2.The new spotting system is great or at least i personnaly like , it adds a certain layer of management to the stealth of your units.  When a friendly unit ( lets take a field howitzer for exemple ) shoots outside of the visual range of a enemy unit, it start filling a spotting bar which has 3 levels :Green light bulb = The unit is still concealed and unspottedRed light bulb = the unit is still concealed but the enemy will see small flash of lights in the area of the unit showing a wide location where it could be Red Eye = The unit is now spotted and the enemy can see it even without direct unit line of sight. the Bar empties itself after not shooting for a bit.  This rewards taking a few accurate shot  instead of shooting willy nilly and force you to relocate if you have been exposed too many times, and this also prevents getting counter spg'd as soon as you fired your first round, but make counter spg much easier if you keep revealing your position. Concealing your unit / using folliages decrease the speed at which this bar fills up, the bar fills up depending of the caliber and type of gun, big units with high caliber guns will get spotted very quickly, compared to smaller guns who could sometimes shot many rounds before being revealed. A lot of new options to help manage units and QOL have been added, ability to order units to stay in certain formation ( horizontal or vertical line , rectangle, spearhead, Etc ) .The auto vault system where infantry automaticly vaults over fence instead of having to manually make them do it, and a bunch of other stuff i forgotFor the campaign and multiplayer ( outside of classic mod ) units are unlocked in a tech tree system similar to World of tanks and Warthunder, i do enjoy it a lotit makes you play with weaker units to unlock better ones ( or keep them ), and pretty much will make you use a lot more units that you most likely would if you had already everything served to you in a silver plate. Non the less, going up those tech is rather quick, and not that difficult. it gives me a ""long"" term objectif and i like that a lot .

_childDocuments_.review: Its trying to do something different so you cant blame it too much but there are some just entirely unforgivable things I cant overlook that just make me outright not enjoy the game.-Extremely clunky, complicated and unintuitive UI and Menus... especially with the whole batallion things, and the way you play the conquest mode one. Which sucks because Conquest is one of my favourite ways to enjoy men of war games.-You cannot just repair vehicles anymore. You can repair when a module outright breaks (like you get tracked) but the tanks overall health just goes down consistently. Your only option Im aware if its low HP is to send it away off map. Annoying, and takes out a lot more strategy than it provides.-This is a HUGE one but commanding and even FINDING your units is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ impossible. They have no circle, outline or any form of indicator. If you throw your troops in a forest, in a trench or anything of the kind you have to rely on the minimap and look for them like wheres waldo.-Additionally, I couldnt figure out a normal way to split troops from a squad. Something that was easy and obvious previously, where all you had to do is individually click on a troop to select him individually is now gone. Even if you select one person to go to a building or such, youll click on the squad and order them to move and the one person in the building will leave it to follow your move order. Idk maybe I missed something, but even if theres a way to do it the fact that its so unintuitive is a bad mark to me.-Further still, putting infantry in cover doesnt feel right. Where previously I had a preview and could go behind cover almost anywhere, behind almost anything and even in tall grass I had feedback when placing units... in MOW 2 half the time the game didnt let me put units where I want them to take cover even it just made perfect sense. Like boulders or wrecks. And worse still, when the game *did* let me put them into cover often times it didnt line up with the preview, or they just went out and did their own things or just stand in the open. I dont know whats wrong here but this kind of stuff just didnt happen in previous games. Just sad.-In conquest, its not just you playing an RTS against the enemy, you have waves of friendly AI rushing the frontline from your spawn constantly. It honestly feels like theyre the main force and youre just clearing obstacles for them. Extremely unsatisfying. It feels super cheap to just have an army of friendly troops keep rushing the enemy with no input or cost from you.-I dont even exactly know how this works, so take this point with a grain of salt but you cant even use all the units when playing matches. Loads of units are 'consumable' one time use which you have to unlock with either challenges or purchasing with an ingame currency. They could have made is camos or something but they outright make units consumables if you want to use them per match. I dont know how hard it is to get the necessary currency to keep using the units you want so maybe its not a massive issue but it just doesnt feel right. Im playing for fun with friends, let me us what I want to use damn it.-A lot of the impact is extremely poor. All the shells, bullets and especially explosions are extremely underwhelming. Coming to this from Gates of Hell where youll shoot a tank and ammo rack it for a brutal explosion, huge fireball, screenshake, crater in the ground and tank parts flying around... in MOW2 he shells and explosions look like a firecracker.Idk if its salvageable. I hope it is. It *does* have a bunch of interesting concepts but all in all its just not fun to play. Its just not what men of war is supposed to be. Its trying to be a funny haha casual game and its just not working.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a good game, note many of the complaints regard the more arcade hp bars and such, which you can change by checking the realism mode option in the settings although the devs would do well to make this far more visible. With realism mode enabled the game feels great, it is assault squad with better graphics and an undeniably large amount of content. 3 campaigns, conquest mode, multiplayer and coop left and right. Still able to steal weapons from the dead and directly control units means that even if you encounter some questionable pathing you can as the player can fix that on the fly with a 2 second bout of direct control. which is fantastic when you are using halftracks.Combat feels good and artistically I do not feel the cartoon aspect that others do. However voice acting is atrocious and I suspect some of it was put through an AI with a half assed German accent, verbally there little to no inflection in the voices, its off putting. I overall recommend this as the there is a large amount of content and with realism mode active it feels natural for MOW veterans. Omit the voices entirely and the game will be enjoyable. Future content will hopefully make the game even better including the removal of always online which is planned.

_childDocuments_.review: I looked forward to this games release for such a long long time, and when it finally arrived, i was a bit hesitant on getting it, the game itself can be fun, some of the games missions are pretty fun while some are just annoying to play through, the Raids were something I've not seen before in a Real Time Strategy before and i love the idea of them, but you can easily mess yourself up if you don't pick the right units to research for the later battles, but changing the difficulty doesn't seem to lower your received research points so you can farm completed missions quicker, which is nice, out of all of this, I'd say the most fun I've had with Men of War 2 was its Historic battles, i just wish there were more of them, now after saying all of that, I've come to the nail in the coffin so to speak, everyone talks about it and now i will too, the game always has to have a internet connection, i get why they do this but it makes the things i talked about above and even more very frustrating, even a small disconnection causes your mission to halt, and even more times then not, fail to reconnect forcing you to restart, currently there is no way to play offline, this really sucks for pretty much anyone playing and pretty much throws playing this game during a trip out the window. My analysis, the game needs some work, the need to have a stable connection is beyond annoying and sometimes makes solo progression big time annoying if you aren't saving every 10 minutes, reviewing doesn't allow me to rate a game on scale, but i give Men of War 2 a 4.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Men of War is an excellent game that appeals to classic players seeking a playstyle similar to Assault Squad 2, as well as those who enjoy competitive gameplay. The dedicated servers enhance smooth gameplay, and custom lobbies allow for game customization to our preferences. Additionally, the ability to play the entire game in co-op mode for up to five players is a fantastic feature. The reconnect feature is a long-awaited addition to the MoW series, ensuring you can rejoin the game if disconnected.I also appreciate the option to hide or show health bars, which I prefer to have in multiplayer games and hide in single-player for better immersion. The game offers extensive single-player content, and the water physics are the best in the series. The moving clouds add a new level of detail not seen before in MoW games. Performance is smooth, with my RTX 3070 averaging 60 FPS at 4K resolution and my RTX 4080 achieving 80-100 FPS.Overall, Men of War is a great game with significant potential for future improvements.

_childDocuments_.review: A weird time where I'm happy to give it a thumbs up even if my opinion is mixed, namely from a slew of confused reviews bombing the game from issues mostly on their end. I've definitely been enjoying it, though I would hesitate to recommend it to friends until a sale or a few patches in (unless they're massive MoW fans.) I have a thicker skin for some of the things people are whining about.To address the big complaints:- Tank HP always existed in the franchise. Now you can see it. Not sure why that drives people so crazy. I'm also very glad to see that tanks in this are fragile and require support, and aren't the mindless powerhouses they are in other titles. The ability to recall units in Battalion mode to repair their hull is a cool feature that makes the fights more dynamic.- The other game, GoH, is an entirely different developer. MoW:AS2 is 10 years old. It wasn't entirely clear at first that this was the evolution of MoW:Arena, but that's fine - especially if the SP features are decoupled from the servers down the road. Know what you're getting into and adjust your expectations accordingly.- Yes, there's an online component for single player. No, that's not cool. The developer stated they will be removing it. Fine. It does clearly feel like it existed more as a F2P PVP game that evolved into this, and it's still shedding some of that even on release. It's not a game breaker, but a fair complaint. There's no MtX or premium currency, but the cost of the special units for your battalions seems extremely high.- The voice acting (at least for US) is atrocious, and some of it is recycled from older MoW games. It doesn't bother me, and some of it is as endearing as it is goofy, but I can see why people wouldn't like it.- The UI is small (2K Resolution) and some of the default bindings are very weird and clunky. A lot of the shortcuts and features are the same from other titles, so it's not too hard to adjust, but it could be overwhelming for newcomers.- The tutorial really doesn't cover some core and specific mechanics as well as it should.- The spotting mechanics take time to get use to and the game can be extremely frustrating until they click - you will get bodied and have things destroyed without seeing what happened, if you're not paying attention. When you do get it, and play carefully, it's very rewarding.- The direct control for Infantry not having GoH's third-person-over-shoulder view is disappointing, but the vehicle view is still there. Like the other games, direct control really pushes your units to their potential because they really don't enjoy shooting beyond certain ranges when under AI control.- The inventory system is still there and has lead to some really unique and fun campaign experiences where stolen munitions and emplacements turned the tide in an otherwise hard mission.Overall, it's fun. $45 fun? Maybe not for most people. Maybe it will get there - but if you like MoW/GoH and know what you're getting here, it's good for quite a few hours. The campaigns (despite the voice acting complaints) give you some flexibility to do neat stuff in what would otherwise be a very scripted, bland mission in other games. Excited to see where this goes after a few patches.A slight edit after another 10 or so hours - the AI is rough. Units outright ignoring orders and making bad decisions in the heat of combat. Infantry is paper thin, which is fine, except the AI can micro them perfectly and you're left fighting yours constantly. Manageable in skirmish missions, but makes the single player story, infantry-only sections a living hell where if you so much as glance away or click wrong, entire squads will be wiped out instantly. Not fun to have to quicksave so often in an RTS because of this. I finished a few of the stories and longer SP content, but am putting it down around now because of how exhausting it gets. Maybe some patches or mods will fix it down the road.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm new to Men of War- series, it's a fresh and more realistic take to WW2 tactical RTS coming from Company of Heroes. There are good bones, but developers need to focus on few things from here, before any new content comes into question:1) Guarantee reliably server connection without disconnections. I've seen this happen few times today, where multiple players are ejected from an onlien match without a recourse to reconnect back. It's not a massive problem despite what more critical reviewers here might lead you to believe. Single-player content needs to be available with or without server connection.2) It'd be  nice to have a post-game inspection mode after the match timer ends, and the victory/defeat splash screen pops up. I mean, a way to look around the full revealed map and chat with other players. Nothing like a nice round of GG's. This is how it works in Age of empires 4 and CoH3. Replay mode is no substitute for this.3) Work closely with notable livestreamers (Twitch, youtube) past the paid promotional period, for them to keep streaming and drive overall engagement up in coming months. It means listening to critical, expert feedback, and work to deliver it. These people play various video games for living, and carry over valuable experience and vision, that may not be as obvious in the close-knit development circle.

_childDocuments_.review: I have removed my original review and changed my stance.First off, Always Online will be patched out soon, so anyone worried about that can rest easy.I do recommend this game. Conquest Mode is simply fantastic, but needs a lot of work.I don't play PvP, so I won't speak on it.Conquest Mode needs more sandbox options. We need to be able to change what tiers of units are allowed, how many units can be deployed per echelon, preparation time modifiers, stuff like that.Units need veteran levels that can be acquired through combat that carry over mission to mission.Let us scavenge the battlefield after victory and repair enemy equipment to use in the next fight.Let both players use their own unlocked decks and purple units in Conquest. Right now only the Host can use purple units, and the Host's decks are the only one's available to the teammate.In many ways MoWII is vastly superior to GoH. Sadly, in many ways it's far more surface level and half baked.MoWII could be an 8.5-9 out of 10 if it provided the depth necessary for practical immersion, but in it's current state it's no higher than a 6.5.If you like MoW / GoH and are interested in this game, go in with an open mind, but don't expect to be blown away.

_childDocuments_.review: Bottom Line Up Front: MoW2 is the best WW2-theme Real Time Tactics game I’ve played since the original Company of Heroes (CoH) and also compares favorably to the earliest titan of the WW2 RTT/S genre, the Close Combat (CC) series.  In fact, I would probably rank MoW2 above CoH or the CC series for one simple fact, I can play MoW2 campaigns co-op with friends. MoW2 has the graphical style of CoH (if a little less polished) and the game play “feels” like Close Combat in terms of pace and tension or “gives Close Combat vibes” as my good friend puts it. Where I’m coming from:As someone started playing WW2-themed video games in the days of SSI’s Panzer General and Atomic Games/Microsoft’s Close Combat series in the mid 90s, and having put hundreds of hours into the original Company of Heroes and CoH2, I generally rate any WW2 RTT/S or turn-based strategy game against the Old Guards of the genre.  I have generally compared every WW2 RTT I’ve played against Close Combat and every turn-based WW2 strategy game against SSI’s Panzer GeneralIt’s not MoWAS2, and that’s ok:Unlike many of the more devoted MoW fans who gave negative reviews for MoW2 primarily because it differs too much from the earlier games in the series, I personally could never get into the earlier games to the extent I have MoW2, precisely because I felt the micro-management was too heavy and the UI too clunky compared to the streamlined feel of either the CoH or CC series. As far as I can tell, the biggest difference between MoW2 and earlier games in the MoW series is that the developers made a conscious decision to reduce the micro-management and lower the learning curve for newer players to the genre, which I personally view as a positive.Pros:There is a tremendous amount of content in this game in terms of units/vehicles/guns, mission and campaign types as well as the “tactical options” available to your forces in the form of different ammo types, different small arms, different grenades/explosives and different squad compositions along with the ability to customize your in-game playstyle to a much greater degree than either CoH or CC.It also has in-campaign progression with the inclusion of faction-specific tech trees that allows and encourages you to make meaningful decisions about how you spend your in-game currency/credits to configure your combat force (something I always loved about CC) and decisions on how you spend your XP to unlock troop type upgrades in both single player and multiplayer campaigns/modes.The flow of game play, combat mechanics and general atmosphere of MoW2 are excellent.  Infantry suppression, explosion dynamics from artillery and airstrikes, variable damage modeling on vehicles/guns (everything from ricochets to crew and mobility kills, main gun disablement and ammo explosions), the fully destructible environment, and the ability to do things like assault a building with infantry where the soldiers actually engage in hand-to-hand combat (like in CC) is all very immersive and incredibly fun/rewarding.MoW2 has the best engineering system, I've ever seen in a WW2 RTT/S, you can create truly complex obstacle belts and layered fortifications, including mines, wire, hedgehogs, bunkers and much more.  Most importantly the trenching system/mechanics are incredible. You can connect all of your trenches to create layered trench lines.Co-Op Campaigns are a blast with friends. Especially when they do things like take screen shots of your assault engineers rushing a tank with a satchel charge that goes off in a massive explosion.Cons:I acknowledge people are frustrated by the online requirement (which the devs have stated they are fixing) but, personally I’ve not been affected by the issue.The voice acting/dialogue is atrocious, as many have noted. I run a Mod that changes the voice overs.Game stability still needs work.  I usually will crash while loading a mission at least twice a “session”, so perhaps one crash for every 2-3 games.  I don’t understand why this is the case but I will say that the devs do have a very good system in place to auto-load you back into your game, this works in both single player and multiplayer, as soon as you restart the game.Path-finding needs work.  Vehicles especially struggle to maneuver around various objects on the map, especially if there are more than one vehicle attempting to move in close proximity with each other.

_childDocuments_.review: There are two ways of looking at Men of War 2:1. As a WW2 wargame meant to have a relatively close resemblance to reality at the tactical level.2. Or as a competitive team-based RTT game set in WW2.If you're looking for #1, you're probably like a lot of the reviewers here and may be disappointed. Though, in all honesty, the previous entries to the Men of War series have never been the best tactical WW2 game. That honor belongs to the Close Combat series made by Atomic Games, or the Combat Mission series later made in homage to those by Battlefront, due to both of those series actually portraying the effects of morale. So if you're looking for that and you haven't played those, go buy one of those. I'd recommend starting with Close Combat: Last Stand Arnhem if you're looking for a game set on the western front.But if you're looking for #2, this is the game for you, and I think that's the real intent behind it. There are single player modes and mod support available, but the emphasis here is clearly on the matchmaking and ranking systems for the online 4v4/5v5 Battalion gameplay modes, and those systems truly do stand out compared to other games in the genre. For instance, the automatic matchmaking system, reduction of emphasis on unit spam, and more zoomed in camera for more granular levels of micro unit control are very much more enjoyable than Steel Division 2 for me personally. And the emphasis on realistic weapon penetration, more realistic open maps that allow space for flanking, and just general accuracy of the art style are just as much more enjoyable in comparison to Company of Heroes. This game stands above both of those as a multiplayer competitive RTT, so check it out if either of those are your thing.

_childDocuments_.review: Game has a lot of potential and even more problems. Cannot recommend it in its current state due to issues mostly mentioned in other reviews. A few cons id like to emphasize: -the AI is somehow worse than previous installations-vehicle movement is way off -artillery is far too accurate and lethal, especially against vehicles, and the AI tends to spam it in conquest-UI is confusing and strange-voice acting is awful-units are historically inaccurate in many minor but annoying ways (US marines in European Theater, German "grenadiers" being a top tier, elite unit, instead of their regular infantry, etc.) it feels almost like a fictionalized version of WW2-No Commonwealth/Japan or North Africa/Pacific Theaters (I'm sure they'll be added as DLC but still)There are also many pros, including the entrenchment system, reinforcement/recall system and the general design of the campaign. Battalions are a cool idea and I've had some real fun playing around with unit compositions. Also, one of the things other reviews complain about, vehicle hull health bars, have actually been in the franchise for a while, albeit invisible. Still, this game really needed more time in the oven and better direction in several departments, and I cannot recommend it in its current state. I sincerely hope they take to updating and improving it, because it could be a truly fantastic game with a dozen or so updates and patches, plus mods. Ill change this review if that happens.

_childDocuments_.review: Men of War II:~~~~~~~~~~~ So far, in 2024, I have had the pleasure of playing a few strategy games set in the World War II era, all of which were turn-based. So, when I was offered the opportunity to play Men of War II, a real-time strategy game, I jumped on it like there was no tomorrow. Sixteen hours of gameplay down the track and I’ve barely scratched the surface of the game due to its vast content. Well, here are my two cents worth regarding Men of War II.Men of War II is a real-time strategy game developed by Best Ways and published by Fulqrum Publishing on the 16th of May 2024 on the Steam platform. The first thing that impressed me when I launched Men of War II was how much content this game had. If you enjoy playing singleplayer campaigns, you'll have access to various missions and modes for all three factions (Germans, Russians and Americans) available in this game. Four different campaign modes, three of which have a combined 102 missions and the conquest campaign, which is an offensive and defensive skirmish type of gameplay. There are four scenarios, and each map has a faction HQ at each extremity and around 15 locations to conquer. Each faction will take turns making an offensive at the closest location on the map, and the other faction will defend it. If all locations are gained by one faction, it’s game over. It’s fun and interactive and can go on for ages. And if multiplayer action is what you are looking for, you'll have three PVPs and one PVE mode at your disposal. On the other side of the spectrum, I don't think it’s necessary to force players to be continually online during singleplayer campaigns, which this game requires. To give you an idea, I was AFK for three to five minutes for a coffee break, and when I returned, a popup menu was up telling me to click on a button to continue my game or I would be kicked out; the timer was nearly out of time. The other thing that struck me was the sheer speed of the gameplay and the fact that you have no options to slow it down. I was quite overwhelmed seeing all AI units AI (friendlies and opponents) moving so fast while I was just trying to get my bearings on the map and beginning to implement actions. So, it might be a good idea to first launch the tutorials, which, by the way, are excellent. You also earn experience points and supplies and can use the latter when you play a PVP game. You earn experience points, supplies, and money after each successful mission, and you use the money and experience points to unlock new units and purchase these new units for your battalions, divisions, etc.  The gameplay is good, and I like the interface as all the commands are just a click away. Depending on what campaign you select, some missions will have only a certain number of units, while others will give you access to reinforcements, which are called echelons in this game. As far as I can see, there are up to three tiers of echelons, and in some missions, there is a certain amount of time to wait before the second and third echelons can be utilised. I am unsure if there are more than three tiers of echelons, as I haven't played all the missions. What was clear to me very quickly was that you have to give orders to every soldier, tank, and canon. Yes, you can select a group of soldiers and give them orders, too, but I found that I was having fewer casualties by strategically moving and placing each unit one by one on the map. All foot soldiers come in groups of various numbers; for example, the infantry units will come with a group of five soldiers, and each soldier will have their own weaponry, ammunition and helmet in their inventory. Infantry units can dig trenches and foxholes, while engineering units can erect barbed wire and place mines and anti-personal mines as their main perks. But you can view fallen soldiers' inventory and pick their gear and ammunition. There are also boxes to be found; you can inspect their contents and pick up what you might need, although because of the speed of the gameplay in specific missions, it is quite hard to do. There is a huge number of units for all three factions, from infantry units to tanks, cars, sidecars, trucks, canons, artillery cannons, anti-air defences, planes and all guns, machine guns and rifles from the era. In terms of realism, I think the developers excelled here. Pretty much everything can be destroyed on the map, and the animations of fallen soldiers are top-notch. You can see where every bullet and ends up. The AI is pretty smart, and you can play each mission on the easy, normal or hard difficulty.Yes, there are gameplay issues, such as the occasional infantry units getting stuck and being unable to be used. I had a few problems with some units that were shaking for a while. In my view, the loading time is a tad too long. I had a few games at the online PVE and I did have fun, but I haven't tried the PVP mode as it is not my cup of tea.The graphics and sound effects are excellent. Unfortunately, the voice-overs are average, and the German and Russian accents are lousy. Overall, the game is very sound and offers massive replayability for both solo and multiplayer campaigns, but I don't understand why we must be connected to play campaign modes.Positives:~~~~~~~ +	Great graphics+	Good Sound effects+	Three factions with large numbers of units +	Three campaigns with 102 missions and one conquest campaign mode+	Great tutorials+	PVE and PVP modes+	Hundreds of hours of gameplayNegatives:~~~~~~~~ -	Must be constantly connected to play the campaign modes-	The gameplay is too fast, and you don't have an option to slow it down-	Several bugs here and thereMen of War II has a massive amount of content and realism that will appeal to veterans as well as newcomers to the genre. Get ready for hundreds of hours of gameplay.7/10 Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

_childDocuments_.review: I am not surprised by the reviews. Seems to be a common thing these days. Initial review bombs then it levels out when people play it for more than 10 minutes and don't have catastrophic tantrums. Whatever. I have all the MoW games , CTA, and GoH. I really enjoy this game!It runs really well so far. The graphics and QOL is great. People saying it is a CoH clone with MoW title..are dramatic. It is literally MoWAS2 just with updated engine, QoL, and more units/game modes. No complaints there. Especially for the price. There are a lot of nuances that they fixed from prior installments that were an annoying micro. For example, support squads from off map that have no impact on command point (CP). They will essentially build fortifications, emplacements, mine/wire obstacles etc. with a quick click of a button and not result in annoying micro. You can now easily set infantry squads into numerous formations i.e. wedge, column, file, etc. Finally. Also you can set the desired spread with easy click and drag like prior games. Inf squads can build fairly intricate trenches along with other fortifications.I know it was in older games but it is less clunky in this. Again, nice QoL addition. Emplacements and hotkeys for units is nice. Little displays show the progress and usually just one click then the unit will automatically perform the function - again less insane micro when it gets crazy. There are a bunch more things I could mention - but keeping this short. Singleplayer missions , campaign , conquest mode , skirmish , multiplayer. Full mod support. It is all here. The online always decision - I get the frustration from players. Not a huge fan of that choice but it is whatever. Not a huge deal.  I think the game is a great evolution of the MoW/RTS series. Still the old school tactical style game play but with some huge QoL improvements - primarily in micro. I don't mind the micro as it is what MoW is known for but some of it was too much. They addressed that. As a long time fan of the series I highly recommend this game. I think people hold on to nostalgia a bit too much and expect every game to be the exact clone. The devs kept the good, kicked the bad, and enhanced what needed TLC. Good work.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has collectively around 1000 hours in the men of war series and its spin offs, having played all of them,yes even the god awful Vietnam and Cold War one and the Men of War 2 beta I can not recommend this game at its current state and price point. The game is just a newest installment that is the men of war jank. It doesn't add anything new to warrant its price point. Everything new they added is something the old guard like myself dont care about. Battalion PVP and PVE are gamemodes that cater to a more casual crowd, where micromanagement isnt really necessary. The OG game mode know as "classic" in game is something that has been relegated to lowest tier if importance, hidden behind the lobby system, which I must give credit to actually works and allows connections unlike the god awful one found in Gates of Hell. The original Men of War games supported a healthy modding scene which went further with the game in terms of realism like the valour, robz realism and GSM, so it makes the choices of making the game more arcady all the more confusing.The real improvements of Men of War 2 are the improved performance over assault squad, which wasn't a high bar to begin with, and a better building system over previous installments. Thats pretty much it, everything else are small improvements that you cant really market as decisive feature, like for instance the grenade range indicator.If you are someone who is more causal player it might be worth it for the PVE and PVP battalion games modes, but if you are someone who when launching  mowas2 was expecting either to play assault zone game mode or load in a realism mod. I suggest you wait and see how the modding scene develops. Also game has Always online which is something ill never support

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of Men of War: Assault Squad 2, I was really excited for Men of War II. I spent many hours playing MoWAS2 and loved it, so I expected MoW2 to be even better. But when I first tested MoW2 when it got publicly released for testing, I was very disappointed.The new user interface in MoW2 was confusing. It was hard to figure out how to do even basic things. The mechanics were also complicated and felt very different from MoWAS2. It seemed like a mix between MoWAS2 and Company of Heroes, but not in a good way.I hoped these problems were since it was a testing phase and would be fixed, by the official release. So, on release day, I bought the premium version, excited to play. Unfortunately, nothing changed. The graphics, textures, and models looked fine, but the gameplay was still confusing and frustrating and didn't give me old MoWAS2 vibe.I was hoping for an improved/revamped version of MoWAS2 64 bit version with better graphics and new units, but MoW2 didn’t deliver most of that. It didn’t feel like the game I loved. Because of this, I asked for a refund and went back to playing old good MoWAS2, which is still much better (It's kinda sad I need to get stuck again with 32 bit version, because I can't play some of my favorite mods without crashing). Even Call to Arms: Ostfront is a better game than the current MoW2 and I recommned buying it if you want something newer than MoWAS2.In short, Men of War II disappointed me personally. It tried to change too much and lost what made the original great. I can’t recommend this game for now.

_childDocuments_.review: To counterbalance the knee-jerk negative reviews, here are my initial impressions.If you're like me and hated CoH for being too arcadey and having little content and GoH for being too hardcore to the point of being frustrating to play, this game is a happy middle ground and exactly what I was looking for in a WW2 RTS. There's plenty of content, a lot of it co-op enabled with cross-progression, and the balance/feeling of the battles is on point though air and artillery seem a little too accurate/OP. The music bumps. The GEM engine is updated and is no longer crashing under load. Mod support right at release which signals that the devs care about the right things. I am greatly looking forward to the Warhammer 40K mod that's already in development.Some negatives, Reused audio from the older games.In-battle UI seems basic and non-congruent, almost like it's still placeholder.Missing FPV for infantry but this is really minor and there's likely to be a mod for it like there is for GoH.

_childDocuments_.review: My friend and I played all day, and only had 1 disconnect.   It was after a mission ended, and we kept all progress. We got back in right away.There are lots of PVE modes, story, conquest, skirmish, raid (rouge-lite).  And they are all fun.  Your also earn things in every mode, and can use those things in PVP.Edit:I would really consider researching the game yourself and not basing it by the mixed reviews here.  Most of those reviews have les than an hour played, and complain about things that are incorrect.-Vehicles always had a health bar in MoW.  IIRC, The Valour mod showed the health bars, the vanilla game did not.  And, of course, if you dont pen, you dont do damage.  -There IS indeed a first and third person control mode for vehicles. it is just not mapped by default. I personally like them, but dont think i will use them much.-The "always online" thing hasnt bothered me much. Ive had only 1 disconnect in 20 hours, and lost no progress.  I have noticed a few vehicle rubber banding though, but this was only a few times, and usually doesnt effect gameplay.  Im sure this will get fixed as time goes on.  This also helps prevent cheaters, and people who would get cracked/bootleg versions of the game.  And the developers said they are going to remove it for single player stuff.-The UI to me is pretty clean. I dont understand the issue here. Maybe im used to it from the betas, but it gives you A LOT of information, while still looking clean.  Its VERY similar to MOW AS2, so i dont understand peoples complaints here. You can also customize the UI with '{' or '}', IIRC.-I personally LOVE the battalions thing.  It give more reason to cooperate, a meta progression, and a way to build your "deck' to bring the units YOU really like to use.  I really think this is a great feature. but if you dont, you can still play "combined arms" which lets you use any units from a faction.Now for stuff this game has that MoWAs2 does not:-unit formations (allows you to keep that 1 AT unit in your mixed squad, in the middle of your formation, or you can do line, column, wedge, ect)-dragging when moving, to allow you to specify the tightness of your formation, or to spread units out over cover.  I have NEVER seen a game let you drag to select multiple cover points near your cursor, this is a HUGE advantage, and is VERY intuitive.-Choosing which units you want to bring into a game.  This is HUGE, and has a lot of strategy to it. not only do you want to choose your role, but how many of each type.  In MoW2, you have a limited amount of units, and you need to decide if you want a few strong units, or more weaker ones.  This makes every decision in game more important, because sacrificed units will never come back, meaning you need to plan accordingly.-Raid, and conquest modes, which each have you fight though several missions, earning money and tech, which u can use to research and buy better units.-Trench digging, pill boxes, MG towers, and more.  All given to you in a much easier way than the way old engineers worked (even with mods).  Instead of using precious CP to have engineers and trucks out in the field, you simply deselect all units, and then you can build anywhere, and the units will spawn nearby (if no enemies are close), and start to build.-Infinite range for all units.  MoWAS2 had range limits for every unit, that was increased when controlling them yourself.  This lead to a lot of issues where you couldnt shoot at a unit, because it disappeared (from line of sight or whatever), or if they are moving and you cant aim at the ground near them.  This also lead to people purposely aiming at the ground, hoping to miss, to shoot further than normal.  In other words, people could cheese the range, and shoot further, since the bullets/shellls dont disappear.  Now everyone has infinite range, but penetration and accuracy go down.  Now this overall make the game more fun IMO, however i remember in the beta, that artillery was very OP.  I havent played PVP since the beta, so im not sure how strong it is now.-Real planes and airstrikes.  Easy to use, each plane has several weapons to attack with, and the angle can be changed, however it will change the end of the flight path, possibly causing it to spend more time in range of enemy flak, so theres a balance too.Im sure i will think of other things and add them, but for now i recommend you just try the game, and return it if you dont like it.  Dont judge it based on its reviews right now, because it is A LOT of fun, despite being quite different from AS2.

_childDocuments_.review: Men of War 2 is a game I have tried so hard to love, and to find at least one thing that I enjoy about it. Yet at it's core is a recycled failed live service game, risen from the ashes of MoW Arena. I find it difficult to believe the developers are even aware of what made Men of War great, or have any idea what the community wants anymore. The arcadey gameplay, barebones aesthetic and always online requirement is a constant reminder that this was originally going to be a free to play sweatfest with an ingame storefront. This newest entry is painfully confused on what it wants to be, as Best Way makes an attempt to make the series more competitively viable. Some aspects of the free to play model still remain as they were hard-coded into the DNA of the battalions gamemode (it's kind of strange to have special 'collector' units in an RTS game until you realize you were likely going to have to pay for these at some point in development). The battalions game mode is a welcome addition and new mechanics such as digging trenches is great, but sadly overshadowed by frustrating gameplay and questionable design decisions.Having played the original betas for this game's predecessor Arena, I can safely say not much has changed since then besides minor balancing patches, some additional single player missions, and co-op content. Tank combat feels terrible compared to Assault Squad 2 and Gates of Hell, and is a test of frustration in it's own right. Infantry are now simplified to just "SMGs" and "Riflemen" with barely any diversity of squads or differences between factions. Proper squads do exist but are no longer able to be separated so you are forced to blob them together. Maximum range has been lifted on all units, so artillery is able to abuse this and sit on the sidelines of the map, and matches are quickly decided by who can completely shut down the opposing team from the comfort of spawn. Aircraft make an appearance to everyone's dismay; it devolves matches into point and clicking whatever unit you want to disappear. AAA can work if you plan ahead, but with how spammable planes are I've seen more anti aircraft guns die to aircraft rockets than I've seen them shoot down planes.In short, I may return to this game someday if Best Way and Fulqrum figure it out and find a way to fix how broken MoW2 feels. But it's looking pretty unlikely, so just go play AS2 or Gates of Hell instead.

_childDocuments_.review: I genuinely cannot express my disappointment. I waited, and waited, and waited for this game for years. I sat there through constant delays. And what was the reward? A downgrade to a previous game from 2014. This feels more like a fan game than anything, and its heartbreaking. I love MOWAS2, its easily one of if not my favorite RTS games. And they took all of that, went through like 10 years of development, and made it worse. Please, if you see any redeeming quality in this mess, go play Assault Squad 2. Its old but somehow better than this. So overall complaints out of the way, a list.- Good things -1. Slightly more up to date graphics and animation. Really not saying much given the previous games.2. Extensive content.3. Much better looking UI. In some places, ill get to that.4. Less brain damaged AI. Again, a low bar.5. Better reinforcements. As in sandbags etc.- Bad things -1. Ingame UI is ABYSMAL. It looks and runs like literally nobody tested it.2. Camera is subpar.3. Armored vehicles got World of Tanks'd. What moron thought health bars were a smart idea?4. Most of the MOWAS2 problems and gripes are still around. Think unit names being jank.5. Multiplayer unit rewards. You are not Company of Heroes. Stop trying.6. Everything is online, even the singleplayer. People are saying that's temporary, but it really shouldn't exist at all.7. Poorly designed missions. Things like pacing, terrain, and even just size are awkward and poorly done. There are dozens of mods alone for MOWAS2 that blow it out of the water completely.8. MASSIVELY delayed. I think 2-3 years if i recall correctly.9. A bit overpriced. Even if it were good, that's kind of a lot.10. Art, subtitles, and VA are literal trash. AI would've been better even.- Other Thoughts -I'm sure there are other positives i missed, and i'm sure there are countless negatives i did too. Honestly? Its not worth your money. I'm gonna go refund this after i get a screenshot of that disgusting UI for my friends. Even if its on sale i would still advise avoiding it. The first mission i played i was bored within the first few minutes, probably one of the worst things that you can say about a game. And for reference, i have about 250-270~ hours in MOWAS2 in just singleplayer, i can play those PvE campaigns and missions all day and be happy. So for ME to get bored of a brand new one? That's just sad.- TLDR -MOW has fallen, billions must play COH.Seriously though, they not only dropped the ball, they fell on it and broke their head open. Do not buy.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game - this game has a fair share of things to work on / improve, but I think it has solid foundation to build on. Some of the criticism this game receives is unwarranted IMO. The devs have gone out of their way to implement various game modes and settings (like realism mode) that should make this game accessible and customizable to everyone, no matter how casual or hardcore they prefer their games.I've been a part of the closed beta testing and I really appreciate how the devs listen to player feedback -  I personally asked for new unit voicelines for each faction - which they did implement - albeit the quality is severely lacking. A for effort and listening to player requests, F for quality. 1) One thing I wished for was the overall art direction / theme of the game (i.e. the storytelling and voicelines) were much more serious, realistic, gritty, and war-like. A lot of the voice actors are wayyyyyy too relaxed, like they are literally reading off of a script. There is no emotion, no fear of death, or urgency in any of the voicelines, which severely hampers any sense of immersion. Take the unit voicelines from Company of Heroes 1 for example - you will see a clear difference in immersion.2) The unit uniforms and the different vehicle variants are definitely lacking when comparing this game to GoH, but I think these are minor issues which will hopefully be upgraded further down the line. If all else fails, the modding scene will come to the rescue.3) Another issue I have with the game are the gun and tank engine FX - they are very lackluster. I want tanks and guns to sound scary and distinct - the audio leaves a lot to be desired. (also - there needs to be more terrain deformation when an artillery shell lands - there are no massive craters that are formed which could create cover and unique battlefield scarring).4) Perhaps the strongest feature of MoWII (and most importantly), the multiplayer aspect is much better than any of the previous titles and its competitors. I've never been a fan of multiplayer for RTS games, but MoWII changed my perspective - massive battles, terrain scarring, trench / fortification building, destructible houses, etc.TLDR; I think this game has a solid foundation to build on - multiplayer is great, but the fine details such as voicelines, tank/gun FX, and unit detail / customization needs to be upgraded to truly make this game a fan-favorite.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good, just not what i imagined.Pro:-Lots of content, unit diversity-Better technology, no performance problems - short loading times, 2k + UI support-Matchmaking MP-New gamemechanics: dynamic territory conquest etc.Neutral: -Graphic style,  rather colorful but good textures- Switch between normal and realistic mode (more on that later)- I don't like the new UI, I prefer it to be more realistic and clearer- infantry formations too orderly.- Currently only three factions: US, Ger, RusCon:-Animation on the whole is worse than GoH-Sound of speakers (Ger) and tanks, weapons not particularly good, the MG sounds like a popcorn machine.- Gameplay too fast overall, vehicles and infantry should feel a bit slower and bulkier. (realistic mode)- Infantry textures are much too simple compared to GoH. Little equipment, missing helmet emblems etc.Overall, my impression is mixed.Personally, I would have liked the best of the games MOWAS 2, GoH and MOW. with slower tactical gameplay and more relayism. (for the realistic gamemode)The sounds and animations definitely need an overhaul. UI is a matter of taste.Despite everything, I see the effort of the developers and hope for future improvements and content. hence a thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a solid improvement over the old MoWs (I played them extensively).Playability is as good as the old ones, but on the top of this the new battalion mode is very enjoyable (the is also the classic mode).To be honest I'm not getting the reason for the other bad reviews, I'm seriously questioning whether a majority of this are bribed/payed for by "others". Also because this game is superior to Gate of Hell and there are not many competitors (I'm not at all a fan of Coh either, too arcade).The Pros:-Large number of maps.-Innovative gameplay, customizable battalions.-Great graphic.-Emplacements, bunkers, watch towers, all buildable in game.-Interesting weather system.-Larger variety of troops.-Good balanced matchmaking, a bit slow because of the bad reviews (thumb this up!), average 6-8min depending on your rank.Negatives:-Unsplittable squads. It is not a deal breaker but I hope this will be improved.-Possibility to choose team size battalion matchmaking, maybe also 3v3/4v4.

_childDocuments_.review: It is really unfortunate that the first game was so good! Is the second game better? Nope. Does not mean it's bad. But I am disappointed. The developers somehow made it feel older than the previous game. Some mechanics aren't there anymore, or they are less user-friendly. A big part of the first games was stealing vehicles, looting better guns from enemies, and being all tactical and sneaky behind covers, micro-managing your squads. You CAN do that in this new game too, but it's not as smooth. They took mechanics from the old game and made them... clunky. It almost feels like it isn't the same studio that made the first one, but a sort of Temu copy of it, made by some other studio.So, if you play this without playing the first game, you will be unaware of the flaws. And you might enjoy it. But for those of us that have 100+ hours in the first games, this is a disappointment. I want to support this little studio and I wish them success. So it is a thumbs up. Buy it, try it. Don't like it? Well, follow your heart.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun challenging war sim, but singleplayer is needlessly connected to online to the point where there is a loading menu when selecting units to play with in singleplayer. _childDocuments_.review:
Experience World War II real-time strategy gameplay like never before! Men of War II, the new chapter in the evolution of the top-rated RTS franchise, brings you more units with different specializations to lead, pinpoint historical accuracy, and new levels of visual and audio excellence, all combined with the series' original heart-pounding action. Lead your troops in intense real-time battles on the Western and Eastern Fronts and overwhelm your opponents in epic narrative single-player campaigns and skirmish modes, before then diving deep into the multiplayer action.

Utilize sophisticated military strategies, lay ambushes, or use brute force to show your ability as the greatest military leader of all time. Attain full command of different roles: from Air and Armor to Infantry and Support in fast-paced battles packed with action. Men of War II brings significant visual improvements, destructible environments, and an advanced AI, to create the classic real-time strategy game fans have been waiting for.

name: Medieval Dynasty
detailed_description: Roadmap About the Game Find a piece of land where you could build your home. You start as a simple farmer or a hunter, but after you gain more experience, learn and hone your skills, you can become the head of a prospering town. Design, build and improve your house - from a simple hut to an extensive farm. Convince people to join your village. Find your true love and create a family, ensuring the continuity of your dynasty. Play solo or team up with friends and explore the beautiful but harsh medieval world in the Co-Op Mode together. An expansive, open world awaits you. Face hot summer months and cold winters and make sure that neither you nor your people lack anything. Medieval Dynasty will captivate you with its unique genre combination for the ultimate medieval experience! Defy the seasons: Make sure that neither you nor your population starve or die of thirst. Hunt wild animals, plant crops or trade resources to be ready for anything. It is in your hands: Without the right tools, you won't get far – whether you're hunting, chopping trees, harvesting or building. But watch out for wear and tear so that your pickaxe doesn't become unusable in the middle of nowhere. Live and learn: Develop your character, specialize, or become a true jack-of-all-trades as you interact with NPCs, care for your family, explore the lush world, or complete tasks for others. Start a village: You are a town planner, builder and warden all in one! Co-ordinate the layout, manage the residents, gather resources, produce goods and trade to help the community grow and prosper. The medieval world, with its dangers and gorgeous surroundings is in your reach! Realistic Open World: Explore two expansive maps, the Valley (Solo) and The Oxbow (Solo and Co-Op) in a beautiful open world. Cooperative Multiplayer: Team up with up to 4 friends for a cooperative gaming experience. Character Customization: Personalize your avatar with a detailed character creator. D ynamic Environmental Realism: Immerse yourself in a complete 4-season cycle with dynamic day/night transitions and realistic weather, all while actively engaging with the environment, from felling trees to exploring caves. Structural and Interior Diversity: Create a diverse range of over 25 buildings, from humble shacks to sturdy stone houses, and personalize them with a selection of over 120 furniture and decoration pieces. Extensive Crafting: Craft 300+ pieces, including weapons, tools, furniture, and clothing. Wildlife Interaction: Encounter wolves, boars, deer, wisent and more wild animals populating the forests. Survival Mechanics: Monitor your food, water, health, and stamina levels. Skill Tree: Develop your character by buying new skills. Unique Events: Experience dynamic events and decisions with direct gameplay impact. Quests and Economy: Engage in quests, trade, and economic activities. Social Dynamics and Family Building: Create connections with NPCs, establish your own family, and develop relationships that may lead to the joy of parenthood in the game and provide you the opportunity to pass your legacy on to the next generation. Interactive environment: You'll be captivated by the expansive landscape that dynamically changes with your actions. Cut down trees, collect resources or explore mysterious caves: Everywhere you’ll find something new to discover.

_childDocuments_.review: I always measure my games by this system : $1=1 hour. Did I get my moneys worth? Absolutely! I have clocked in almost 70 hours at the time of this review and I have reached the point where there is nothing else to do. I have finished the entire main questline and my village is running at full efficiency and capacity, so it's not as endless as many people would think. Additionally at it's current stage, doing a re-play is going to be boring since the mechanics from beginning to end are linear and you'll just get bored quickly. However, I would still recommend the game just because of the cheap price and easy to learn mechanics. Give it a try!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game.If you like base building but don't want to follow the road too often used in terms of survival games, if you want to take things at your own pace even with customisation to make it as easy on you as you want and if you like the era, just go for it.The devs have been nothing but helpful all along EA, they did good on their roadmap and they'll probably keep fine tuning the game now that It's in full release.Sure, you'll see some that are unhappy with some changes and yell at the fact that It's released as "unfinished". Trust me, It's more "finished" than most current AAA release state (looking at you CP).- You want to build houses? you can- Pick people to live in them? yes- Decorate? It's ongoing, that wasn't part of the original RM- NPC occupation? yes and with a well oiled machine you can self sustain your village- Combat? Not required, you can disable but there are bandits- Grind? up to you, you can customise a lot of option if you want to get hungry, thirsty, what amount your villagers require and so onIt's a very fun game and being in possession of many, many EA titles, I'll tell you this one is part of the rare few that actually delivered.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best game I've ever played!! Can't believe this is still an early access. Before you buy this game, you might believe that this is quite similar to forest, however, whilst playing this game, I've got to realize how much the developers put their thoughts into the mechanics of this game. Compared to The Forest, you actually feel like you are creating a town, a heartwarming place to stay, where you gradually build up an affection to it.Pros: 1. Story is quite fun to read. Writers did their best to make it interesting.2. Gathering resources and Constructing a building is actually fun! There's so much you can do.3. Unnecessary mechanisms like "carry logs to the construction site back and forth" is gone! Gathering material is time consuming and a hard grind work, but this game makes you feel worth it. (you just carry in your inventory, and there's no maximum capacity as long as your maximum carry weight allows you to. To me, The Forest "pick and carry" mechanism was a pain in the ass".Cons: While using controllers, there were times where the keybinds felt little awkward. It would be nice if the developers update the keybinds into:1.  Two Wheel keys opened by L3 and R3. 2.  Arrow Left and Right changes tools you carry.Also, when you change your tool via R3, since you have to change tools with R stick, everytime when you change the tool, screen is flying off to the corner. So, maybe get rid of the neutral bind?Again, this is an amazing game. Period. It is obvious that the developers are doing fantastic job for this game, I can't wait for the further development. It has so many potentials. (Is there going to be VR support?

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of mechanics.Crafting, farming, selling produce, managing a settlement, hunting & survivalIt looks good but also runs fine on my ancient Radeon R9 390.Very entertaining in the short term but sadly the mechanics are quite shallow.Definitely a good deal when on sale.The Negative:"Medieval realism", The gaming aspects really get in the way of the realism.(Skip if you dont care about this aspect)The game doesn't have a single church, temple or mention of religion.The progression from copper over bronze to iron tools makes no sense in the setting. Iron is more common than copper, tin is not found in areas that have copper deposits.The houses are too big with much unused space.The mechanics are VERY shallow.The crafting progression from cooper to iron tools is gamey and makes no sense. It is a lesser version of the minecraft system. In this game the tools are identical apart from damage and tool life.Iron is hard to come by but copper and tin are found easily and in the very same cave.Hunting is very easy. There are so many animals you can feed a small settlement by half a day of hunting. The animals drop meat, either pelts or leather and skulls you can sell as trophies. Bones, sinews and other parts are not included. Also hunting is not really tactical. Just spam spears or arrows and you are fine. You don't need to sneak or ambush your prey, the animals only run away if you get very close.Farming is also quite simplistic. Take a few hundred units of the metric tons of meat you made from hunting and let it rott in open wooden boxes (it's not like you can eat it all anyways). Don't worry having huge piles or rotting meat in your settlement has no effect at all, no rats, no flies, no sickness and certainly noone will complain about the stench. When you got a steady supply of rott you can buy seeds and produce fertilizer. you mastered farming. if you really want you can automate it further by having some pigs, farm hands  and grow grains that can be used as animal feed. The pigs produce ♥♥♥♥ which is an alternative to the piles of rotten meat. You don't need to look after the fields just plow, seed, plow, wait and harvest. Alternatively just watch your farmhand do the same in slow motion. Basic things like soil quality, crop rotation or use of animals are not in the game.Building is cool but it doesn't really matter where you place stuff. Just place the pigsty between the houses, it's fine. Also Material is transported magically so don't worry about this aspect of logistics. Just place stuff where it looks good with a few exeptions the fisher needs to be placed in water, mines need to be placed where caves are and i think wood sheds need trees in the vicinity.Managing the settlement is underwhelming as well. Put your settlers in a simple house and give them work, let them produce fire wood, food and fetch water. That's enough to make them happy. My people had nothing but dryed meat and water for over a year and noone complained. The rest goes to commodity production. Fur capelet and shoes, bread and a good portion of the dried meat can be sold for profit.Managing your herbalist and fields to accommodate the changing seasons is tedious to a point i just don't bother, just set and forget. In case of the fire wood you can just overproduce and sell the surplus in spring.The economy is a extremely simplistic, too. Goods have fixed prices. So it doesn't matter if you sell your mass produced fur capelets in the summer or a single one in the winter it's the same price. That makes overproduction and blatant mismanagement a good idea. Even low tec goods can easily pay for your taxes. If you have problems transporting bulk goods just build a storehouse in the near of Gostovia or any other village. Later you can sell directly in your settlement but i fail to see the need for this. It just binds up a part of your workforce that could be used for even more production (not as if that is needed).All in all it's still a fun game even if it doesn't go deep enogh in my opinion. Workshop support and a few good mods would really go a long way.
