_childDocuments_.review: Medieval Dynasty checks many of my favorite gaming boxes. Sandbox, crafting, survival, management, town sim. Check-checkity-check. The more of these boxes you would check, the more you are going to love this game. First-person Banished is the most concise description of what you are in for. I strongly recommend discovering how the game works yourself. Figuring out how to go from crafting stone tools to build your first wattle shack to obsessing over making sure your thriving town is 100% insulated and has chests stuffed with every conceivable amenity is the sheer joy of this game. It is a micromanagement fantasy, but you can also give your villagers a quick, rudimentary plan and they will quite easily keep the town functioning while you traipse off to do whatever non-micromanagers do with their day. You will get your $30 or equivalent out of this game as long as this is the type of game you are looking for. If you want twitch combat, if you want to be king or god's chosen hero instead of village headman, this isn't for you.But there is a hard limit on what you are going to get for your money, even if all the boxes are checked. I personally feel I got from it exactly what I paid for it and not a cent more. The problem is late game grind without purpose. Through the early and mid-game, the pacing is rewarding. You unlock skills, buildings, equipment, recipes, and even mounts at a sensible pace that keeps you engaged and putting in just one more hour for hours on end. But the points needed to unlock grow exponentially, and you realize that the payoff for unlocking the 2nd tier of a building that you don't even bother using the 1st tier of is no longer an incentive. Where you were once just unlocking by playing, now you are unlocking by grinding. I knew I had reached the end of the game when I started setting my character to craft huge stacks of goods while I texted on my phone or browsed the web. Not good. It was time to move on.And now for the outright awful parts of the game that would make me not recommend it. Since they are avoidable, I still recommend the game, but there is some dark messed up stuff that requires a warning label on what could otherwise be a PG rated experience.The story quests may be there to give purpose to those tired of the sandbox. However, I found the story-characters in this valley to be thoroughly unlikable. And I resented the way my otherwise silent character childishly interacted with these degenerates and played into their sad world. It is disturbing that the only people with personalities of their own in this valley are ruined shells of human beings. I predicted the end of the story during my first interaction with the character who starts the main quest, and it was just as unpleasant as I thought it would be when I reached it.Half of the Steam achievements are problematic, making pursuing achievements itself a problematic endeavor. Get the character 100% drunk. Alcohol poisoning sure is an achievement! Have the character run around naked all winter. Puerile. Get caught stealing 50 times. Stealing from desperately poor peasants - another amazing achievement! And the sickest - "impale an animal with 4 spears while it's still alive." Seriously - what is wrong with the developers that they thought that was an "achievement"?

_childDocuments_.review: Other than some small economy balancing issues, this game is really really fun.  I didn't think I would enjoy it half as much as I have, and really need to take a break as I have been playing none stop since I got it.An example of the economy balancing challenge is that the buying price for manure is crazy and seems to exceed the sale price for the wheat and or flour you can grow after paying for the manure and the wear and tear on the scythe and the land tax.  Hunting doesn't bring much cash to the table either, so it's hard to get anything happening.  You are better off gathering and selling sticks than you are hunting if you want to make money.Other interesting feature is that you have to cook meat before you can put it out for your villagers, I haven't yet been able to work out if I can get someone to do that for me or if I an just supposed to do it.  I think from reading that if you put things in the boxes in certain places the village is supposed to run it's self, but I haven't been able to get that happening as of yet.  Overall if you love building games where you can make your own village and resource manage your villagers, this is the game for you.  Like someone one said before.  It is banished blended with Kingdom Come with hunting to replace the fighting.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfinished, unsatisfying, and despite some quite interesting ideas an unmemorable journey to disappointment.If you have a couple of friends where one is really into spreadsheets and the other into home decorating, this might be the space to bring them together in. In general, the experience is greatly improved when seen as a lobby for hanging out with friends and not as a video game with goals, mechanics, or ... a point.Otherwise, it's a rather dull and dragging experience that has glimpses of great game design and balancing; but also one where the devs moved on to the next installment in the series before finishing up this one, choosing to extend the shelf life of it through repetitive tedium instead of engaging content.Given that the publisher has "Vampire Dynasty" and the very similar looking "Sengoku Dynasty" on Early Access, I wouldn't expect much from the upcoming updates. The developers have done a great job with the Coop update, bringing it in line with basic expectations for Steam games. All players now get achievements in multiplayer (well, some of them) and you can join via Steam as of a few days ago.The upcoming roadmap doesn't look like it will change much of the core gameplay. So what you see is what you buy, and if you want to play this with friends, go for it if you've exhausted more polished options.

_childDocuments_.review: Combines survival, crafting, and city-building elements in a medieval setting, creating a unique and immersive experience. Players start with nothing and must gather resources, hunt, and build to establish a thriving village. The game offers a satisfying blend of realism and strategy, where managing your settlement, forming alliances, and growing your dynasty are key to success. Its detailed world, dynamic seasons, and engaging mechanics provide endless opportunities for exploration and development. While the early grind may feel slow, the sense of progression and the freedom to shape your own destiny make it a rewarding journey for fans of survival and simulation games.

_childDocuments_.review: How I learned to stop worrying and love the Village.TBH, after playing the EA version for quite a while, I didn't think I would play it again. The game just felt a bit limited. It still is in many ways but it is very pretty, the sounds and soundtrack are immersive and actually it is, in many way a sort of SimMedieval Village. Your only real competition, is yourself. Just occasionally I like a game where I'm not threatened every minute by being ripped to shreds by beasties/outlaws/aliens etc. This is a refreshing change of pace. Okay there is a modicum of peril in wolves and bandits but they aren't too difficult to manage and you have to go looking for trouble to find it. Usually. It is a bit grindy if you want to really bootstrap your village - but hey that is your call. If you let your woefully inefficient workers accumulate resources for you it will take longer but that lets you focus (if you want) on the little quests. The game is still being expanded (tick) so expect more content and a little more depth - it will never be a CK3 style game - I don't think it is intended to be despite the title. The milieu is a romanticised abstraction of European medieval village life - minus plague, disease, poverty, squalor, filth, brutality, a strict feudal system and generally, short lives and sudden death. Okay, so maybe not really medieval but hey. Character stubs toe - gets septicemia and dies age 19 - so much more satisfying right? It's all about finding a nice picturesque spot, arranging your houses and the industries and services and decorating it - whilst nominally progressing the story line. Don't be in a rush to do the latter - it is a bit limited at the moment but it is definitely improving. Alright there is a lot of chopping trees down - not just to get resources but also as a prelude to stump removal to clear the ground. "I'm a lumberjack and I'm okay...." should definitely be on the soundtrack. With a little thought you can manage roughly the needs of your villagers and their production. You can always top up villagers production occasionally with a little manual intervention and I heartily recommend using the fast craft option. If I were new to the game I would recommend not investing too much into your first village until you worked the game out  - then start again. There is a huge amount of helpful community info our there for specifics. starting afresh There is a thread for improvements - and there are literally hundreds of great ideas there so I won't say anything on that here. There is only one issue that keeps me awake at night (no I'm not that old). The voice actor for Racimir in the intro, at least in the English language version, seems to have an American accent - I'm not sure but I don't recall the Americans having a middle ages let alone a medieval period. :)

_childDocuments_.review: I have only been playing this game for about 3 days, though I feel like I know it much closer than that due to the number of gameplay videos I've watched before buying it.Why, you ask? Well, I was initially put off by 2 things. First of all, I have always been a 3rd person player, never much cared for 1st person. Second of all, being female myself, I always choose female characters in games, just a personal rule of mine.Now after hours of watching other people play to get a good feel for the game I decided I can't live without trying it out myself, and boy oh boy, am I glad I did.The way the 1st person works is not bothering me too much. The character runs quite smoothly without a 'rabbit bounce', and the field of view is good and doesn't make you feel claustrophobic, like some games do, when you feel like you can't see what's around you. This information might not matter for 1st person veterans but I thought I'dd put it out there as it may be important for someone more picky like myself. As for the lack of female characters, yes, I would like it if there was an option, of course! But I do understand how it might have been difficult to make that work, considering the way the plot, questlines and whole mechanic of the game work. But honestly, it isn't too bad. 95% of the time you can't see any part of your character at all so you are mostly admiring axes and spears and hammers in front of you, so it makes little aesthetical difference. Of course it would still be nice if devs found a way to implement it in the future.So this is as far as my initial worries go.As for the game itself... oh my! I haven't had so much fun in a long time. It's a brilliant cross between a survival game, crafting game, city builder and sim management game. It's like someone has taken all the things I like and smashed them into one thing. The environment it pretty, realistic and ever changing, There is enough challenge to keep things interesting but not so much as to make it a complete grind and annoyance. The mechanics are interesting, and I have really been enjoying learning and exploring all the management aspects.Added bonus, you can customise the game at the beginning, with things such as shorter or longer seasons, more or less taxes to pay or animals dealing less / no damage - depending on if you prefer your gameplay regular, stress free or nail biting. Of course it is an early access game so there are and will be issues and bugs, however there is a very active discord and devs seem to be great at quick fixes. And there seems to be plenty of content coming all the time, including things put to popular vote on discord, which shows the devs care about what we want.TLDR: Buy it, you most likely won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: Medieval Dynasty is a game for you if you enjoy:Life Simulation: The game offers a detailed life simulation experience where you manage various aspects of your character's life, from daily chores to long-term goals.Historical Settings: If you are fascinated by the Middle Ages and enjoy games set in historically inspired environments, Medieval Dynasty's setting will appeal to you. It immerses players in a realistic medieval world.Survival Mechanics: The game includes survival elements such as hunting, gathering, crafting, and managing your character’s health and resources. Fans of survival games will find these mechanics engaging.Building and Crafting: Medieval Dynasty features a comprehensive building system. You can construct homes, farms, and entire villages. Crafting tools, weapons, and other items is also a significant part of the gameplay.Economic Management: Managing your village’s economy, trading goods, and ensuring the well-being of your inhabitants is crucial. Players who enjoy economic strategy and resource management will appreciate this aspect.Open-World Exploration: The game offers a vast open world to explore, filled with diverse environments, wildlife, and resources. Explorers will enjoy discovering new areas and finding hidden treasures.Role-Playing Elements: Medieval Dynasty allows players to take on various roles such as a farmer, hunter, craftsman, and leader. Role-playing enthusiasts will enjoy developing their character’s skills and making choices that affect their dynasty.Dynasty Building: One of the unique features of the game is the ability to establish and grow a dynasty. You can start a family, have children, and ensure your legacy continues. This adds a long-term strategic element to the game.Realistic Seasons and Weather: The game features a dynamic weather system and changing seasons, which affect gameplay. Players need to adapt their strategies based on the time of year and weather conditions.Story and Quests: Medieval Dynasty includes narrative elements and quests that provide structure and goals. These quests often involve interactions with NPCs, adding depth to the game’s world and your character’s journey.Detailed Crafting and Farming: If you enjoy intricate crafting systems and realistic farming mechanics, Medieval Dynasty offers a rich experience with a variety of crops to grow and items to create.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed Medieval Dynasty! Played co-op with my wife on the multiplayer Oxbow map and solo on the singleplayer map. After a good 200+ hours I can honestly say this is an easy recommend. It's immersive, it's addicting, and with a bit of creativity (and patience) you can build some gorgeous-looking villages.Mind you, I couldn't shake the feeling this game felt like an Early Access title. Case in point: the map my wife and I started on wasn't yet fully fleshed out with a story line, and certain quest types from the singleplayer map were not implemented here. The voice acting and general writing of the dialogue are also among the most cringe-inducing I've ever come across, to the point where they feel like placeholders. There's also a gaping, combat-sized hole in this game. The combat itself is janky as hell, and the lack of bandit or animal raids on your village would've added a really interesting new dimension to the game.Finally, in my 200+ hours split across 2 playthroughs I also never got to the point where my heir was old enough to take over from me. He simply takes too long to mature on the game's standard speed. That's kinda disappointing for a game which touts this as a major feature.Nevertheless, these things were minor in comparison to the fun I had building and developing my villages. I'm glad to see the game get major content updates every once in while though, which is definitely encouraging because there's a lot to like here. If a future iteration can improve the QoL issues, fix combat, and add more late game content, I'll definitely be coming back for more!

_childDocuments_.review: Ever wanted to know what it was like to live in the feudal era?? Me neither, but this game is pretty great! I've invested some time into this, working on building my settlement, hunting, gathering resources, paying taxes (which I'll get to), and running for my life from wolves, boars, bears, and other animals I have managed to aggro. I like the mechanics of speech and how each person is different, making a player have to study what an NPC likes and dislikes. Another great thing is the seasons and how farming is affected, such as what crops can be planted when, etc.There are a few issues I have ran into however. One, in my playthrough, NPC's did not carry an inventory in their chests within their homes nor their workshops (when I have watched other playthroughs, NPC's carry some nice equipment, not to steal, just borrow *wink ). Another issue is the taxing system, not that the taxing system is broken, just that the taxing system is not explained. From what I understand, the more you build and the more citizens you have, the larger the tax which is fine. However, I just got super build happy with maybe 40 gold to my name in the first season and had to pay nearly 800 gold. I was literally crafting any tools I could in order to sell them to vendors to pay my taxes in time. The final issue I had was just figuring out how to make different things, trying to figure out what buildings I needed, etc.Aside from the somewhat frustrating issues I ran into, I would still highly recommend this game. This game still has a lot to offer and I hope to see it grow into something better. If you liked KCD this is kinda similar but more pacifist. 8.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Initially, I gave this game a thumbs down because it did not allow residents to play as themselves.  I turned the game over to my grandson, Jamie, because there was no option for a female character. Not my favorite thing to do, but what a powerful game. Even this old woman enjoyed playing it (well, except for having to kill the deer). Anyhoo, we both, Jamie and I, eventually wore the game out: built 3 or 4 towns each, always trying to find unique location and modeling them a bit after our own preferences (with a church, as so often was found in the middle ages). Now we've moved on to a mmorpg but it's not nearly as realistic nor as much fun as Medieval Dynasty! And  we keep thinking, "how wonderful it would be if Medieval Dynasty were a mmorpg! We'd play it forever!" If we could make new friends in game and travel back and forth to player-made or resident-made towns, that would be amazing! And, to the Developers, it would most certainly sell! Please let me know, message me, if ever there are plans to mmorpg this game! I'll buy it (and a copy for Jamie....smile).

_childDocuments_.review: Without the new settings tweaks, this game is GRINDY... like INSANELY GRINDYIt's more grindy than a full on multiplayer survival game like Ark or Conan, but without the benefit of other players to spread the load. You work very very very hard to accomplish... nothing of real note anytime soon.No way to accelerate time, except to wait it out, which could easily include leaving the game running while you go watch TV for an hour or two until the next season changes.Moving across the map involves bursts of speed followed by being tired... ad nauseum.Resource harvesting involves about 20 trips to increasingly far away locations to build a basic house.They dial up the realism at the expense of fun. _childDocuments_.review: With full release here, it's time to say that this game is very fun and worth consideration if you're looking for a cozy medieval survival craft-'em-up simulator. I won't say that it's the greatest title in an over-saturated genre, because first-person management build-athons are a dime a dozen, but this game is a quality contribution and if you can get into its medieval european vibe, then you can easily sink many comfy hours into building your village and growing your family.I've played since early access first released on Steam, and the developers have proven their commitment to engaging with community feedback to refine its many interlocking systems and keep adding more detail and content. The game has grown to incorporate a lot of systems involving your crafting, building, eating, surviving, etc.. Some of the mechanics, such as the villager occupations, can be arcane at first, but the full release so far has detailed tutorials and quests to guide you through learning the systems; it seems much more accessible than before. In one of my earliest files, I played at least a dozen hours before realizing none of my villagers had been working, then stumbled upon a sub-menu devoted entirely to that function. There are lots of things to discover and figure out in this game, and I'm optimistic about what they'll continue to add.I'm at a loss to detail any criticisms, because the fundamental gameplay is solid, the visuals are excellent, the game is smooth and not buggy. The only thing I find myself wanting is "more".

_childDocuments_.review: It starts off interesting, but gets boring in the mid-game. I was telling myself I'd get to the end of the production tech ladder as a goal, but I think I'm going to set it aside because it's become tedious.The early game is a somewhat simple survival game. It's mostly about building yourself a house, and some workplaces to do things like cut longs into planks. You need to accumulate enough money to buy warm clothing by winter, or you'll start seriously freezing every time you aren't at a campfire. Money making early on mostly involves doing a lot of hunting, and then drying the meat and making simple leather bags for sale.From there it moves on to building a village. Unfortunately, villagers have very low productivity. For many tasks, like cooking or smithing, you can craft as much in 30 seconds as they'll do all day. The villagers help *some*, but there's a nagging feeling that you could do 90% of the stuff yourself without any villagers at all. Even when you've got 40-50 villagers working for you, most of your income comes from crafting stuff yourself for sale. By that point the villagers are feeding themselves and provided you with raw materials like copper and tin ore, but if you want do get much done, you have to do it yourself.There's tech progression in 4 different branches, but it largely doesn't matter since, once you have substantial cash generation, you can always buy anything you want from vendors. It doesn't matter that you can't make things like the best bows or the food with the highest bonuses, because you can just buy it. You don't really *need* an iron pickaxe, since a stone pickaxe will mine anything. The iron version is just more convenient because it works faster and lasts longer, and of course you can buy it.Building up the village is interesting at least until you get past the hump where you have enough cash to buy anything you want. It's just that past a certain point, your improvements to the village don't really do much beyond increase profits, and profits don't matter much if already have enough to buy everything.

_childDocuments_.name: Medieval Dynasty

_childDocuments_.review: Because this game is in early access I'll give it a thumbs up with the hopes that over time it improves, but as of now it's just ok. There is a lot of potential for this game to be great. There's a decent amount to do, it's just that it doesn't really mean anything. The premise of the game is that you slowly build up your own little town and invite other villagers to live with you, but honestly the world is just lifeless. The NPCs are super stiff and just stand or sit there doing nothing. When you invite them to your village, they don't really do anything. Sure you'll see them doing the job you assigned them to do, but when they're not doing that, they literally just stand in one spot. The dialogue/relationship system is also a bit irritating because you have to press the right option for your relationship with them to go up and you can only interact with the same villager a couple times a day so it takes a few days to built up your relationship so that they want to move to your town.  I want to see this world come to life a bit more and the NPCs have more character. I'd also like to see larger towns in the game. I know that this is no Kingdom Come Deliverance but they must have some of the same assets available and can easily build bigger cities.
_childDocuments_.name: Medieval Dynasty

_childDocuments_.review: I'm 30 hours in and I can say I really enjoy this game, however I find it needs optimization. It's really clunky for me on my laptop, which makes things like hunting really difficult, that's the big thing stopping me from playing it more often.. Not any bugs that I have noticed though and the game looks nice. It has a tonne of potential. Some quest givers seem hard to locate and the seasons go by fast which takes some time getting to understand, seasons seems very important in terms of what food is edible and when items sells at a higher price, etc.. If you have a lower end p.c you may want to wait to purchase until it gets optimized but overall  I'd recommend it. It seems to strike a good balance between survival and village building, the survival aspect keeps you busy but isn't overwhelming, which is awesome compared to some of the other survival games out there. And there seems to be lots of options when it comes to the village building aspect. Lots of stuff to do, decent chill music, I just wish it played a bit smoother for me ;-)
_childDocuments_.name: Medieval Dynasty

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is very, very funny.Although the developer - or at least the Steam Community Moderators the developer decided to be represented by - and the community are rather condecending.This game's strength is the survival, the free building, the freedom to do whatever you want to do in a medieval setting.The game's weakness is absolutely the dynasty building; you gotta "talk" to your wife, you gotta do very, very stale fetch quests to make her happy so she doesn't go away.So I thought like: Easy solution, jsut ask around if you could mod out the dynasty thing. Just have a wife, an heir and go with it (or even get rid of age all the way), focus on the game's strengths and get rid of the stale "dynasty" thing - would make the game much better.And there it was that I got all the toxic: The game's name says "Dynasty", I was just too bad, yaddayadda.Really, the game would be an absolute banger and absolutely a recommendation if you wouldn't be forced to do absolutely stale fetch quests that are in the game just for the sake of being in the game. The whole dynasty part doesn't serve a purpose and is too far away in the future of your character to serve as an objective.So while I built cool villages at several points and tried to find solutions to the randomly chosen (by myself for challenge) village location, I was always taken out of immersion by "Go to X and give me jewelry Y from village Z." every now and then to accomodate a random pixel wife that doesn't even have a voice.Just get rid of that and you get the recommendation again.Until then, this is kinda like a game-breaking bug: It doesn't allow you to play on despite you waste your time with doing things that are utterly boring. Game-time stretchers like walking throught he whole map for a single item your wife wants.Update: The multiplayer update map is basically based on a lot of my ideas I sent the developer in a mail that they never reacted to. Cool, cool. Recommendation isn't coming back anyway: That update also brought loads of bugs like wolfs that bite an infinite number of times per attack (Yes, wolfes have a chance to deal infinite amounts of damage to players.).

_childDocuments_.review: Very solid game at first glance. After a first addiction however, it becomes super repetetive and grindy, along with many many balancing problems and a lack of long term motivation and reward. The so called "full release" felt very much unfinished and basically like open beta 2.0. The so called "dynasty" aspect means nothing to me as of now, because why would i keep playing for 200h doing the same stuff all over every day just to finally see my child reach adulthood? And no real benifits of having an heir in the first place, because continue playing with him would just mean keep doing the exactly same stuff for another 200h?What this game needs the most is workshop support, so the community could add content (like additional buildings or alternative skins, more crafting recipies, addiitonal crops, more weapons/armor and fighting, rebalanace mods or even total conversions). Sadly, the developers seem to be pigheaded about that question, despite how much that would profit their game.Until then this gets a thumbs down from me. When you love the grind aspects of survival-crafts you might still want to grab this on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of Kingdom Come Deliverance but don't enjoy heavy combat or want more freedom to customize, this is a great game for you. If you like building and survival simulators and cozy vibes, this is the game for you. If you need complicated and in depth story lines with a lot of voice acting, this is not the game for you. If you like games like Green Hell, Stranded Deep, The Forest simply for their highly customizable building, this game is not for you. This game offers a very cozy atmosphere with a strong survival aspect (fall/injury damage, sickness, hunger, thirst, weight limits, exhaustion - but no sleep needs) and a lot of freedom. You immediately have the right to build but your building limit is based on completing one of the main quests. The main & side quests are cute and quirky, sometimes easy and sometimes challenging, and add a sense of liveliness to the game.Your success in this game is based a lot on your reputation as a citizen of this valley and how well you treat others. You can invite people to your village based on their skills and your needs, and can romance (but this takes time, tact, and money!), but you need to take care of every villager's needs or they will leave. You must provide food, firewood, water, jobs, and shelter. In return, they give you free labour and you can quickly develop a self-sufficient village that requires only a little maintenance from you.The environments are beautiful. There are open fields, deep forests, mountains, a lake, rivers, caves, and ponds. There are tons of animals, crop types, and different tasks and occupations. There are a lot of different money-making routes. There are some bandits but you can turn this off. Mostly you need to worry about your survival needs, and wolves and boars. I genuinely have become obsessed with the idea of doing building challenges in the different terrains.Overall this has become an ultimate comfort game for me and I highly recommend it if you like cozy games without being too cutesy and has some realism.

I did enjoy the overall experience but I am a big fan of simulator and realistic type games. That being said it was a bit dull at times. I do think its worth the money if these types of games are your thing. Its starting on a great foundation and will continue to get better over time.

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool game.  I love the idea of it, to build your own community.  At first it is simple to just do it all yourself but as it grows you are going to need help.  Then you sit back and tell everyone else what to do and you go off and do your thing.  Very nice map.  Not to big.  The hunting is a lot of fun.  Keep in mind this game has a lot of growing to do.  I will be following it and great excitement to new updates.  I just played this for well over 30 hours and I was not bored once.  This is city builder meets medieval.   They are so close to getting everything right.  A little few little tweaks on the building, hunting, farming, food, and it will be amazing.6 months later and 100 hours.I didn't play for 6 months.  Seen there were a few big updates and thought I would give it a try again.  Started from scratch and I could remember at of the story so I kind of flew passed all that.  Decided to set up a village in a different place then last time.  I love the fact that you can now decide 3,5,10 days per season.  Also some other things to can decide on to help with the game.  Very cool.  BUT, I wish I could maybe go back and change something if I want.  Example, 3 days is to fast and 10 is sort of long so 5 days per season is good.  I made it 10 days and I wished many times I could lower it.  The graphics are amazing.  The game play is amazing.  I have so much fun hunting.  The best part is the people you get to join your farm all have their own jobs and they actually do it.  That is so cool.  The chat menus are a little hard and do need some work.  Thing to remember this is a game that is still being build and the updates are quite often and are amazing.  I really do enjoy this game and it is very addictive.  I am looking forward to what is going to be added.  I 100% recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Best Alpha I've ever played of anything. The only bug I've encountered is when you try to use a workstation someone is already using and you get stuck. But the unstuck button fixes it. Seems a very well-planned game, and I've been struggling to do anything else after work for the last few days. It's crazy addictive for a farming game, and the mix of doing it all yourself or assigning someone to for example craft things or get wood is so easy to manage. The concept seems so well-thought out. Really excited to see extra content. Best value I've gotten out of a new game for years. If they would eventually release a multiplayer where say 5 people can work on the same save, it would be amazing fun and you could play with your friends. The only negatives so far is the building limit. You have to continue a questline to build more buildings, and I'd rather just build my village, but it just feels like something boring I have to do to get a bigger village. Secondly there is like an ominous music that plays way too much. I just turn it off and put on some youtube music so its not a big deal. Really enjoyed this game, and if it was finished I'd give it 9/10. As it stands I'd say 11/10!

_childDocuments_.review: I was skeptical at first.  I really like valheim and have enjoyed games like Ark and Conan exiles, all very combat focused games.  My wife showed me this, she's always the one fishing and gardening in all the games we play.  If they don't have a very good system for either of those, we usually end up finding mods to cover it.Despite not having the most polished combat system in the game, I mean it's largely just hunting and the odd bandit, this is quickly rising to the top of my favorite games of all time list.  It may be because it's such a great game to play with friends though.  They recently came out with the oxbow map which introduced multiplayer, and needless to say, it was a little buggy at first, really bad lag etc. but within days of playing, it seems our problem has been fixed.  I'd still love it if we could connect via LAN instead of the randomly generated 8 character game id.It isn't super easy, and can't be played like any of those other games I listed.  If you go out and try to take on 3 wolves with a couple copper spears, you will probably die, at least until you figure out how to handle wolves.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: A few hours into this game and it's a bit of a love hate. I'll start off by saying, this is a cool game, another review was on point, its not great at anything in particular but with all the things it puts together, it's actually quite fun.Building/Survival/Hunting/Exploration/Discovery are all somewhat mediocre by themselves but as a whole, it comes together nicely.I really only have 2 gripes so far;1. I had to turn voices off, now I imagine they will change this but the voices are mix and match for instance a woman of 23 who I was romancing to be my wife, her initial voice is.. Ok, i guess but if for instance you say goodbye her voice turns into some old hag voice with something like "BYE NOW" and its just fairly jarring. I hope that changes soon but with voices off its fine.2. Ill try not to spoil anything but im not far ahead in the story.But Racimir, the player character is portrayed to be a strong, smart young man in the opening cinematics, resourceful too, but while talking to your uncles friends the options you have to respond with are very childish, such as "Please please please please please" or when told hes annoying you can respond with "No, I'm not!".I mean, its not a big deal but I find it unrealistic and fairly cringy to read that I pretty much skip everything.Anyway, I am having fun with this game and I am keen to jump back on, so while it does have a few cringy things its very good at drawing you in. _childDocuments_.review: I sunk several hours into this game some months ago and I did enjoy it very much. There were a few annoying bits and pieces as well as mechanics I did not really understand or notice. At some point I stopped playing.A few days ago I started again to see what had changed. And I was pleasantly surprised. A lot of mechanics were implemented and improved (eg hunting feels way more intuitive, used to be very clunky). The progression system and economy has been overhauled (or actually been designed for the first time 😅) and it actually feels good. It created this perfect "just one more thing to do before I stop" effect: The perfect balance between too many options and nothing to do but waiting.I definitely recommend to watch some YouTube videos where to start your village because your location will influence your playstyle a lot especially in the beginning (which resources and villages are nearby).I haven't gotten to the point of mules and horses yet but so far, this is a great game already and in a very, very good state for something like a version 0.5.There are a only very few really annoying things left:- No notification when tools of workers break (you have to manually check ev es day...)- No custom markers on the map possible (eg for animals, bushes, mines etc.)- No fast travel (the flora and fauna and world is not as interesting as Read Dead Redemption 2 - and never will be as a not AAA title - so it doesn't really make sense to force the player to walk for 3-5 minutes to another town). The fast travel function of Kingdom Come Deliverance would be an option in my opinion since the progression of time is important

Quests are either Fetch Quests or Kill Quests and you need to grind a ton to unlock the building types which mainly just are better variations of the previous iteration. You will spend a lot of time crafting spoons or just simply roaming to find enough cash to afford the fence or fence gate blueprint to decorate the village you are building. _childDocuments_.review: At around 220 hours of gameplay with default setup i finally reached to the point where the next generation reaches adulthood and Racimir starts well-earned retirement.The game itself left me with mixed feelings, first fifteen years was interesting, building new stuff and getting things rolling. But after that, i found myself asking the question: "So, what now?" And the endgame was just painful money hoarding and selling lots and lots of stuff.Heres my gameplay in nutshell:years 0 to 5: Getting first steps on survival, furiously crafting with sticks and stones and setting up first buildings. And a lovely snob and arrogant wife :)years 5 to 10: My son was born, and my village was upgrading, had some farms and stuff to craft and sell. Also completed main storyline somewhere in this time period.years 10 to 15: Mines, more crafting and more farming. Enjoyed nice sidequest with my bossy wife picking fight against lowly vendors and "peasants". I even laughed couple of times :)years 15 to 18: The sudden frustration... Waited for experience to build tavern, while selling loads and loads of flax seeds and excess iron. Population had reached over 100, making it a bustling little town. The pain of grind hit hard and fast...years 18 to the end: Lots of market stalls, wine industry and mead industry. Just waiting time to pass... and finally giving everything to my son.Pros:+ nice scenery and change of seasons.+ If you ignore steam achievements you can enjoy relaxing gameplay. You are not in hurry. Really, you dont have to rush.+ Aging of people is well made and smallest details can be seen.Cons:- Lack of voicelines, this seriously breaks immersion of the story.- No tutorial, allthough game itself is not hard but the game lacks basic starting information.- Main storyline is boring af and its just running from one side of map to another, delivering messages from npc to another.- Food has no meaning. dried meat or fancy pies, its all the same.- NPC's are dumb. and act like mindless drones.- Bandits suck, big time.And one important hint for new players: Dont restart. There can be "optimal" location for your village, but seriously. The whole valley is your village, anywhere you build, you can have a good gaming feeling, just like i did. (Just north of Borowo)

_childDocuments_.review: The good:The game looks absolutely amazing, and it's incredibly deep and detailed for an early access game.  There's always things to do, whether it be gathering material to build your buildings, hunting for food, talking to your neighbors and completing quests, or just getting out to explore for a little bit.  The game is a little slow paced, but that's to be somewhat expected for a dynasty style game...you're never intended to complete everything in one character's lifetime, you need your line to continue on what you started, which is a pretty cool touch!The bad (keep in mind that this IS early access and most of these will probably be addressed along the way)There's no danger at all outside of wildlife, and healing plants are STUPIDLY common, so unless you're caught completely unprepared the odds of you being at any sort of risk out in the wilds is minimal.  That also means there's no real need for palisades or anything like that outside of aesthetic purposes.  Speaking of which, the amount of aesthetics available is currently pretty low, you can't put roads in your town or build much in the way of furniture like you see in the NPC villages.  This also means no customization in your house.  The diplomacy system is very easy to game and to some extent you can spam a conversation choice with an NPC to get their approval rating with you up quickly.  And the game is VERY grind heavy...low (but realistic) carry weight combined with high resource requirements to build buildings and fragile tools early game leads to a lot of slog in putting together the first elements of your village.Overall, though, the game is a lot of fun to play around with, there's enough depth already to keep you busy for quite some time, and if you have the patience to wait for new additions, balances, features, and tweaks, I would expect almost everything in my "bad" category (except for the grind...as I said in the "good" section, this IS a dynasty game and you're intended to be in it for the long haul across multiple generations) will be addressed.This has the potential to be a 40-50 dollar game on release.  Get it now and support the developers!

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game and a massive amount of promise. It's like a mix of Banished with a first person survival game. Only a few minor bugs so far but generally pretty smooth launch for an EA game. Unfortunately, this one needs to bake in the oven a bit more before I play again. The main issue is the day / season time. EVERYTHING feels rushed and is about 3 times faster than it should be. How fast food decreases, how fast time goes, and the seasons only last 3 days. It seriously feels like the developers sped up the game speed to test the seasons and then forgot to turn it off. I started the game, explored the village and then started looking around for a spot to start my village. Before I could even do any real scouting, the first day was over. So 1/3 of the Spring season was gone and I wasn't even sure where I wanted to live. So I sprinted around the 2nd day until I found a flat part and built like a mad person. Barely got my house built on day 2 and then was planting crops on day 3 in the dark before it turned into summer, since some crops can only be planted in the spring. Just way, way too rushed. It also suffers from the balance issues that a lot of other survival games like this have, where they make it artificially hard by making food worth hardly any nurtional value. For example, you can kill a big buck and you'll get 3 or 4 meat. When you cook that meat, each piece will be worth 5 or 6 food (out of 100). So an entire stinking deer barely even registers as a snack. Overall though, I can deal with the minor bugs and the other balancing issues but the speed demon day / seasons timers are just a deal breaker. It's not fun and I honestly, truly cannot comprehend how the developers thought that was a good idea.Great potential, will be keeping it on my hard drive to try again later, but for now I can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: As of writing this, I have just over one hour in the game so this will be more of a first impressions review.I can see that this truly is still an early access game, there's things that are still needing work. That said, I am enjoying what I'm seeing so far and I hope they keep refining this and do a full release.This very much feels like Animal Crossing meets Minecraft in dark ages europe and at face value it sounds a little silly, but this was a "I didn't know I needed this until I played it" kind of experience.The game startup was dead silent. While I appreciate them not blowing my eardrums out with some super loud music like some studio logos do, I think they could use the time to start the menu music softly and slowly ramp up the volume until it hits full at the menu screen. As it is, the music suddenly starting without a short fade-in is a little jarring.I looked through the menus and at this point the only complaint I had is that the options in the menus were in a strange order and the names of some of the things in the menus were a bit confusing.Starting the new game:I like the look and design of the intro of the game, it's simple, straight forward, and it shows that the team making this knows what they're doing. The meanest things I can hit them with are:1) use a european voice actor. If this takes place in poland (as another reviewer suggested) then have a narrator speak english with a polish accent. The american narrator breaks the immersion.2) The cadence of the narration is a little weird. There's a few pauses in the narration that don't work well in english and break the flow and tension of what's being said.If I have to get that technical just to provide criticism, please take it as a sign that the devs are doing great work!At first it was odd that I was just plopped down so far away from the settlement, but I can look past it if they adjust the spawn to be more story based. Perhaps add in that the main character was riding in a wagon with a kind stranger who was passing by, they reach a branch in the road, the main character hops off, they exchange a little dialogue, then the cart owner heads off while the player heads to town.I enjoyed looking at the landscape, it was pretty, but I wasn't sure where I was headed because the quest log on the main screen is a little vague and I didn't know at the moment if I had access to the map or not. Once I got my bearings and got into town this is where I could see that the game was still in early access. You can tell that the NPC's are not quite all there. They're walking along what appears to be very specific paths as opposed to behaving like people. The town lacks atmosphere. People should be talking to each other interacting, doing work. This all sets up the player's perception of the community and helps the player build bonds with the characters. The models are reasonably detailed and I like the addition of the little approval rating when you opt to talk to them. It's a quick way to tell if someone likes you or not.The castellan I talk to for the first quest is good, but unrefined. I like that there's a dialogue tree and I think they need to expand on this. There's HUGE mileage to be gained from being able to have dynamic relationships with people as this opens options for having good and bad townsfolk who you can work with or screw over. I don't know if they have this in the game because I'm only 1hr into it. Where the castellan intro quest struggles is in the opening moments you meet him. He was sitting on a bench in a completely empty house/shop(?) as though he were forced to sit there until I cam to him. It was immersion breaking because he didn't feel like a person, he felt like a quest hub interface. I would say that in his case, the building needs to be stocked and active with people doing things and he needs to be an active participant in the world around him. Is he supposed to be running this shop? or, is he supposed to be going about town collecting taxes? or, is he supposed to be a community leader who talks to people? or, is he supposed to be listening to people who have legal problems (this neighbor took my wheat sack, please dispense justice!) and proclaiming verdicts? Let him do things while I'm on the way there and my presence can be a break in his daily routine. That way I can see I'm entering a community.From here, the biggest technical problem I cam across is that there's no clear base guide to using the craftign system or the menus, you're just kinda expected to know. This is good if you already know the game, but I'd say to install an option for tutorial text if someone is new to the game. The second biggest technical problem I had was the mouse. I'm not sure what's up, but my mouse settings are fine for my computer and my games, but in this game it dialed up my mouse sensitivity so high that moving my mouse just 1/4 an inch turned my character 180 degrees to look behind him. I dialed the in game sensitivity down to 0.2 and it's STILL hard to target anything because the cursor moves so fast.Once I got the hang of the crafting system, I had more fun with crafting, but for a little while there I was really struggling to  build my tools and house.Gathering and building was fun, but a little tricky. There was so much ground decoration (unusable foliage and grass) that I spent a good while trying to find simple stones so I could craft my base tools. Other side of the coin, I LOVE how they do logs when I chop down a tree. In The Forest trees look mostly the same and when you chop one down ALL logs are identical. Here, when I chop a tree, the logs I get look wildly different and I enjoy it.Building the house was misleading. I followed the quest and gathered the logs and the sticks and stuff, but that wasn't enough to build the house and it took me a minute to figure out that the quest only gave me enough to build the foundation and a single segment of wall. An alteration to the quest to make it a multi-step quest ("build foundation", "build walls", "build roof") would make that smoother.I tried to hunt a wild animal, but after 10 minutes of wandering around the hillside I never saw a thing. Luckily my rabbit trap worked. Problem was the food did almost nothing. I could understand need to eat 2 cooked rabbits to fully restore health, but my food supply was nearly wiped out after 2 days and the reality is that meat is one of the most filling things you can eat, even dried meat. So I was surprised when I had to eat the rabbit I caught plus 11 pieces of dried meat and an apple just to refill my hunger so I could get back to work. Overall, I'll give this a 7.5/10 with room to go higher. I would like to see more story to this game and a more immersive social structure along with a little cleaning of the translation. I'm looking forward to the game in full release!
_childDocuments_.name: Medieval Dynasty

_childDocuments_.review: This game is extremely addicting but has some flaws, in order to build certain buildings you have to level up your "Technology", this mechanic is clearly meant to do nothing but timegate you. While there is an option when you start a new game to increase technology gain rate, as a new player you most likely wont know about this or simply don't realize just how long it takes to level up your technology so you wouldn't know to increase this setting. So please learn from my mistake, WHEN YOU START A NEW GAME INCREASE THE TECHNOLOGY RATE (Also be aware that you can only adjust these settings when starting a new game at the main menu, you cannot change these settings once you're in game!) Another setting I would suggest turning off is inventory weight, the reason being is that when you are trying to place new structures you have to have  a certain amount of logs in your inventory, and logs weigh a lot, and when you are overburdened you move either incredibly slow or not at all, which makes maneuvering around to place a building exactly where you want it extremely difficult or even impossible. I would also suggest increasing season length to 5 days but that is not that big of a deal. But all in all I definitely recommend getting this game, just remember to change those settings!
_childDocuments_.name: Medieval Dynasty

_childDocuments_.review: This games feels and plays like a prototype. Every feature is overly basic and lacking. I haven't see anything that sets it apart from other games. I enjoy RPGs and a heavy grind, but this game makes every moment of it become grueling. I had no fun nor was I excited for anything.The GUI is also awful for a game like this. There is no sense of direction. I'm not asking for someone to hold my hand, I'm well aware of how a sandbox works. However most sandboxes push you to do this or do that in order to progress or simply stay alive, meanwhile I've never felt or seen anything like that here. Like really, what is the point of the game?To do fetch quests? To build a city filled with the same building model over and over? To have a lot of money, just to have it? I read a lot of reviews saying eventually you can create a self sustaining village, more reason to not continue playing. There is a new season every three days, which reflects exactly what you will expect from the game. There are just many better games out there that offer far more features, replayability, depth, and purpose.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid village builder/management game, not so much a survival. A bit tedious in pacing and mechanics. Can be challenging up front but quickly becomes easy-mode once a few key buildings are in place. The survival aspect is really more of an issue in the first year as by year 2, provided you don't run into a pack of wolves or a bear, it really just remembering to eat/drink every so often and throw on the proper clothes based on season (part of the up-front challenge is getting proper clothing in time for winter)You WILL spend most of your time for the first several hours running back and forth between town, your village, and whatever resource you're grinding. Even with pouches and backpacks, the act of collecting enough mats for a stone-walled house is probably more time consuming than it need be due to weight requirements (such as needing 3-4 trips to bring everything needed for 1 house). This gets MUCH easier once your village is grown enough that the AI does it for you.Two things I'd love to see added that should be simple would be a skip day function because there's definitely a time you're really just waiting til the next day/season or process or event to complete. The other is instead of pure unlimited carry weight, make it a slider between normal and unlimited. Double, for example, would be soooo much better of an experience as opposed to the other two, especially as it takes a bit of time to really increase carry capacity.

_childDocuments_.review: Step into Medieval Dynasty, where the journey from humble squire to satirical sovereign is as uproarious as it is ingenious. Prepare yourself for a medieval romp filled with more laughs than a jester's performance and more surprises than a catapult-loaded cow!Ever dreamt of ruling your own kingdom? _childDocuments_.review: So first of all, i recommend this game 100%, almost everything about it is amazing that it doesn't even seem nor feel like an early access game. There are bugs but none of the bugs that i've come across are game-breaking they're just minor bugs that happens with any games. I've seen triple A games with more bugs than this. Now onto the more in-depth reviewGame looks absolutely stunning (Ultra graphics)The game has so much content in it for an early access game (I've played 30 hours and only scratched the surface of contentHas a well thought out system and is very satisfyingHas a huge amount of grinding (I like to grind but it can become tedious even to me, but not once when playing this game have i felt the grind to be tedious, its actually very fun and rewarding)NPC's and characters look amazing as do the animals.Things i feel should be added:You have horses and donkeys in which you can ride and have carry items for you which is good, but there are also carts in this game which are around the map. I feel its a good idea to add buildable carts or carriages into the game to allow you to transport alot more items. This could be a late game item, but it would allow diplomacy and trading to become alot better. Players could become merchant villages or traders and earn a profit by selling items to different villagesI also think different villages should buy your items for different prices. So you could sell your wooden spoons to the closest village for a certain price, or you could sell them to a far away village for a larger price. This would increase trading and merchants in the game as the player could make money from trading too.I think in a distant update they could add bandits and weapons to combat the bandits. Such as swords. Bandits can randomly raid your village and you have to defend against it. You can lower the chance by building defences such as walls or watchtowers in which you can assign workers to. Or have a barracks where you have soldiers equipped with armour and weapons to fend off attackers. There needs to be more dialogue options and more personalities for the characters. From what ive played so far there are only 3 and its always the same dialogue options that it becomes rather repetitive. NPC's need more presets as most of the women are the same face and the names become very repetitive as you see alot of duplicate names. Possibly add voice acting for the NPC's although its not necessary it would be nice to have a voice telling you things instead of just reading text all the time. There needs to be more diplomacy stuff. There are currently no buildable building which have the diplomacy trait. Maybe an embassy for a neighbouring country or something.Of course these are just my ideas of what i think would go well. Overall im extremely impressed as a fellow game developer and surprised about how this game is still in early access when its so good. I would happily pay triple A game price for this game. I thoroughly hope you pick up this game as it is so good. Well done developers, thanks for entertaining me and i look forward to the future updates!

_childDocuments_.review: Run of the mill village sim. Very in-depth and many cool features. Currently have 76 hours played and am just starting to get bored. One thing I think the game could expand on is adding more items to unlock through future generations. I played on 5 day seasons and unlocked everything by time my first character was 22. If I played on the recommended season length my character would still only be about 25-27. It would be cool if the next generation of your dynasty progressed on the timeline. For example you unlock a basic wooden plow to attach to Horse/Donkey in later generations. It would be hard to implement but I think it would improve the game drastically, and give it a lot more playtime for the community. 8.7/10 would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Medieval Dynasty

_childDocuments_.review: I find this game very soothing. It's not on par with Subnautica, but only because instead of the gentle sounds of water, we have palatial noises that get interrupted quite often by downpours and the constant rain gives me a headache. Which says absolutely nothing about the gameplay itself. I don't mind the construction process, I find it fairly realistic. I enjoy the collecting aspect of things, running around picking up stones and sticks and herbs, etc. There are improvements that can be made, of course - I think more crops would be excellent as well as more variety for things like decorations. Also, making decorations more attainable would be nice. I've been playing for over 100 hours and I still haven't gotten around to purchasing the animal skull decorations, since food items, tools, and weapons also need to be purchased. There are tutorials for how to quickly monetize your village, but I'm not playing for the fastest route to money. I enjoy the mechanics and honestly, it seems like this is something that's meant to be played slowly. If I plan to get one of the last achievements, which my little completionist heart requires, I need to play until my heir is 18 and can take over. Considering my heir is currently barely two, it's gonna take a while.Anyway, I recommend this game for the graphics, the ambiance, and the quasi-realism. I feel like the overarching quests could use some better pacing and there could, quite frankly, be more variety to them, but for a sim involving survival, crafting, and city-building? It hits all the right notes for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Medieval Dynasty

_childDocuments_.review: Fair warning: i give this game a thumbs up, but my description will be largely negative.The issue is the current balancing level.For starters at the beginning you quickly realize that farming wont be an option for a while .... you create a field, "plough" it and then ... realize that you HAVE to fertilize it before you can plant anything. Now you can only get fertilizer by walking across the map to the 1 or 2 NPC who sell it ... just to realize you have no money. Other option would be a pigsty ...but that opens another 2 issues. Issue 1 is you obviously need pigs which cost a fortune. Issue No.2 is that you need to unlock the building first. It requires 500 farming skill points. Now considering that most actions grant a meager 1-2 skill points, you basically have to turn the whole map into farmland just to unlock it.Other balancing issues. The biggest field you can make it 16x16 tiles. Ploughing that field reuires 6 or 7 wooden hoes (they break insanely fast) ... the only hoe you have at the start. Considering that each hoe needs a log and a tree nets 3-4 logs we are talking about 2-3 Trees just for that. Other (early game) tools last about as long as that.Most likely food in the beginning is gathering mushrooms .... 0.1kg mushroom adds 1 to the food gauge which caps at 100. So you're guy needs to eat 10kg mushrooms to be no longer hungry ... and he needs to do that twice a day. Similar for other food. 0.2kg of roasted meat adds 6 food, meaning you need to eat 3.2kg of roasted meat... actually the return on mushrooms is so poor, you might actually starve to death WHILE running through woods literally eating the shrooms from the ground.Village management.You have to build everything yourself, no way to get the ppl in your village involved. A new guy is joining the village ? He will become unhappy and leave if you dont build him a house. Cutting down trees for wood or hunting for food sounds like a good idea ? Other then the player your villager bots are incapable of hunting without having a hunters lodge build (which you have to unlock first..) nor can they cut down tree's without a woodcutter's lodge (which you need to unlock as well) even if only to sustain themselves. You spent ages just carrying materials from A to B, mostly because you can only carry 35kg (which includes tools, food and your cloths) and the game has no carriages eitherVillager management.Noone will ever come and settle in your village. You actually have to walk across the whole map and "convince" an unemployed hobo, that having a house and work in your village is better then sitting at the campfire all day. To do that you need (global) dynasty reputation and personal reputation with that guy... why i don't know.Why do you have to be of a famous bloodline and a good friend to convince an unemployed hobo to join a village where he can have a house and work...Not like it matters. Once (s)he joine (s)he will immediately complain. He is still homeless (which he strangely did not care about before he joined your village) ... so yes, you actually have to personally build him a house. Then he will complain that there is no food  ... or firewood . Generally you have to build a ressource and fodd storage.This opens another issue ... you always have a build limit. At first it's 1 .. you build your own house. Then it is 4... look above you need  your house (#1), villager house (#2), food storage (#3) and ressource storage (#4) ... can't build anything where your villager can work....and you have to manually supply food and firewood ...until you unlocked a bigger build limit.Storage.Now this is the biggest issue. Your character can carry 35kg. Axe, Hammer, Cloth , food (remember your character eats like 6-7kg roasted meat per day), potentially water, a weapon.... 35kg is nothing. Now since you have to build everything manually you spent ages carrying building materials. You cannot build from the village storage either...so you carry logs from storage to new building, walking the distance multiple times per house. It gets worse if you have to chop the wood yourself. Naturally tree's dont instantly regrow ...so with every tree you chop, the walking distance increases.This doesn't get better with the village. Building chests or storages is not possible. Instead you have a single chest in the house ... which can hold another measly 50kg. The "storage" buildings aren't much better. The basic ressource storage is a rather big "barn" ... but the inside is completely empty except for a single measly chest... which at least can hold 200kg.And i'm not done. You are incapable of building anything within a very generous distance of exiting npc villages ... and even the meager hut of the hunter counts as village. Also you cannot use anything you have not build yourself. The "starting" village has a woodcutters which is needed to make planks ... but you cannot use it. So you can't make any tools or materials unless you actually unlocked and build the building yourself ... which is insane considering the points required for most of them. It gets worse though .... the game has no "pass time" function. So you reach a village late evening ... nobody wants to talk to you anymore. The only way to skip time is to sleep in a bed or at a campfire ... bot of which exist in town but you cannot use either, or to build your own ... which you can't anywhere near a village, So you either have to walk out into the wild so you can make a fire...or wait w/e amount of real world time is needed for the game to reach day again.Other issues include weapons and crafting. You need 1 log to make a single hoe or wooden spear .. now i reckon a spear that requires a full log as material cannot be lifted by mortal men.... same with damage. A meager fox requires 2-3 wooden spears (around the size of a man) to the face before he dies. Seeing a tiny fox with 2 giant spears through his head comming for you is kinda.... gets worse when you fight Wisent or bears .... those still come with you when they have 6+ spears stuck in their head. That gets mildly questionable when you kill the bear with 3 or 4 meager stone arrows....I'm sure i missed stuff that needs fixing and minor details ... so thats not even the full list.So why the recommend ? Well, it's still in developement.The game is largely stable. I have encountered no crashes and only 1 bug so far (my wife was reduced to a non-targetable robe sliding across the ground). Stuff mostly works with only minor issues. Day/Night cycles are working fine, it looks the job.In short the basics are all good, the issue mostly lies with the details and those can easily be changed. A decent survival game in a "kingdom come" world.Addendum:Spawning peasentsCurrently the game is set to spawn a fixed amount of free peasents at the camp fires of the villages and the peasents actually migrate between those . It would be easy to allow the player to build a "spawn campfire" as well and spawn/migrate peasents there..Hiring new villagersit would be easy to change that villagers without a job have no upkeep. This reflects the fact that without a job he has 24hours a day to care for himself. This would balance itself since a villager without job does not produce anything ... and once you assign a job he requires upkeep.Building They could just define a certain area around your buildings as village and allow you to directly build/craft from storage while on village ground ... or add a range check. They can just add worker slots to unfinished buildings for builders, using the crafting skill and material from storage ... just like any other craft.So even if it's not on their roadmap, most of the issues could be "fixed" during lunch break...On a sidenote i made some videos about what it looks like:

_childDocuments_.review: Love, Love, Love this game! its beautiful to look at, your day is your own .... want to hunt, take a crossbow and hunt some deer, want to build some houses, gather logs, stones and twigs, grab a hammer and knock a few nails together and erect a beautiful home.... yes there are quests to do, but generally the time limits allocated to those quests dont make them overly pressing.... so choose how you want to spend your day/season, its basically a medieval life simulator where you face challenges in a time where technology was limited..... and there are lots of ways to spend it....... word of advice, take it slow, let time pass (i.e sleep).... some quests are better accepted after you have developed your village, somewhat ... i.e you may need to provide pants to a local vendor.....have you got a hunter in place gathering leather? have you got a farmer gathering flax to turn into linen thread? have you got a tailor to make the pants in? .... there are many ducks to line up in a row before you can achieve certain things .... so, let time pass, dont rush, build your village up consistently and enjoy yourself! This game has provided me hours of entertainment and I am no where near bored ..... things are expensive to buy, Im assuming to motivate you to make it yourself in your village, but generally you end up with a bit of coin, which you can spend on some crucial items .... make stone knives in the beginning and simple bags out of 3 leather once you get a hunter ... they will provide good coin.... also selling flax seed is a good money spinner.... iron crossbows are lethal (but expensive) and remember to aim for the head (headshots generally kill).... the quests are a bit of a let down, but its not the focus of the game and forgivable ..... I am not a big survival game fan, but I love this game. Cannot recommend highly enough and the developers are working on it more and more! Cant wait to see what is to come.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game. Got it at EA release day, devs pushed functional updates and fixes daily which I absolutely like. Beware, there are still bugs and many features not implemented (date now is september 19th 2020) but overall this game has much to explore and to do. Build what you want wherever you want. Your townsfolk currently seems nonfunctional except for field workers but they sometimes bug. Did not yet try marriage but the talking interaction and reaction system is superb! You must remember what topics people like and dislike to succeed in getting friends and lovers. Also some peeps hate to talk about the nice weather in winter because it is too cold for them. Berries are OP for trading. Fields currently cannot be dismantled so think twice where you put them. Seasons are ultimate superb! Really, if any dev or designer of you is reading this: The ♥♥♥♥ winter landscape is a dream came true! That atmosphere with the fog... that sound of running on the snow *-* Overall, the devs delivered (for now). Game has more features and placeholders in early access than some other games in their EA state. Graphics superb (I play on medium). Ambience sounds superb (I shut off music). Magic mushroom effect when poisoned superb.I hope for many more decoration objects and benches for my peeps to sit around the campfire to arrive, soon! My village looks so empty right now...EDIT: It is saturday evening and they keep pushing updates like crazy as I play. Really lovely to see that they are fully in it.

_childDocuments_.review: 7.5/10 (bugs/balancing would improve score)For a survival game, it's got smooth game play, good graphics (for it's category), and it progresses well in terms of achievements. It's a grind to maintain money for taxes to support town along with buying necessary items for questline or early game survival forcing you to do some remedial tasks to upkeep the coinpouch. No visible xp drops so levelling skills is a mystery and seems a bit slow for the speed of gameplay/progression of questlines. The biggest thing needed imo is more time in ea season to make necessary progress in later gameplay. Early game, the time in ea season is ample, but as the game progresses you're in a much harder grind to maintain what you've built, sometimes spending half your season on maintenance, leaving little time for quests.Possible improvements:  - Seasons need increased from 3 days to 5(?) - Some building bugs that require a reset to last save that need to be fixed - XP gained per action to clarify how the xp system works - Better balance of quests to player skill levels in later years      - On this note I feel like I'm ALWAYS doing something productive but not gaining levels fast enough to keep up with some of the quest items that are required for small rewards. (EX: Hand in a recurve bow for a quest line when recurve is very far away from my level to make)  - More chat options or predictability gauge on pos/neg outcome because persuasion mech can be hit/miss

In my opinion they did more than an excellent job with their first game..

_childDocuments_.review: Well I really hate how the quests and NPCs voice lines are written. It completely break the immersion of a medieval simulator. Sometimes they do jokes that would never exist in the medieval ages, referring to modern times. Specially in the first map. I started to play on it and hated the game because of this immersion breaking thing. But then I gave another change and played the second map, that for me it is changes a lot. It feels like the devs were more experienced and grounded when they created Oxbow, including map design, decorations, locations and quests. It's a pitty that there are not voice overs for the quests. Now going back to the survival part of the game, it is really good. I really wish you had more customisations for the buildings, because your town is gonna be looking like a copy/paste since there are not many variations, specially for the houses. But if you are careful enough, it is possible to overcome this by placing it correctly and using tons of decoration, to make it more realistic and immersive. The default map configs for technology (unlocking buildings) and seasons are very weird. It takes soooo long to unlock a sitting bench or any basic decoration or buildings. Also everything is super expensive in the beginning. But since it's a map config, you can always adjust the gameplay to your needs, like increasing tech gain to 500% or so, meaning that this problem is easy to solve. The NPCs are a bit stupid but just the fact that they can be your settlers it's amazing. But overall the game is super good, it reminds me a lot of Kingdom Come Deliverance and From the Ashes DLC. I still have to play more to unlock a few things, but I already recommend this game because it's exactly what they promised it to be. Just don't start your first game in the first map, like I did. xD I really hope they don't abandon the game, and that they add more combat features for late game.
