_childDocuments_.review: VERY fun, takes time to develop and gain abilities, levels, reputation etc.If you enjoy a long chill journey, def recommended! :)You can also customize the games settings such as xp gain, days of seasons etc.You can play 1st or 3rd view by pressing P.If you're mass buying or selling, select the item and hit these F-E-F to fill the maximum amount to sell/buy fast.Advice on buildings:When you're bulding a house you have an "E" prompt to edit walls and roof, you can actually select types of materials to use to make houses stronger to have less damages every season, after you farm some materials!This along with internal decorations increases inhabitants mood.Adjusting any buildings that aren't houses isn't possible.Resource buildings share their inventory and increase weight limit together, other buildings don't.Advice on animals:Cows/Goats are adorable but pretty much useless, they produce milk. You need to wait one season for the milk to spoil a bit in order to make Quark and mix it with fresh milk to create Cheese.Both of them aren't used in any recipes.Donkeys: Do nothing just cute.Horses: Fun for those who like a riding challenge, but mostly useless since you can "fast travel" or just chill, run around on your own and hunt.I'd suggest having only Chicken/Goose buildings for eggs, and a Pigtesy for manure which is turned into fertilizer that is needed for crop fields every season by barn workers.The Tavern isn't a useful building to have, workers only create beverages if supplied materials and cannot sell them nor food. However, this allows some additional visitors to your place. (who needs them?)I hope for more content, maybe more of the storyline and missions, but mainly more types of buildings/services, maybe more crops and trees, AND PLEASEEEEEE an increase in buildings limit because i want to take in every single person and have a huge city family.I'm literally unable to 'catch them all' cause i'm on 130/130 on the 200% limit (sadge).Cons:- No character customization, which is kinda lame cause it's 2022 c'mon..- As the main character, you're only allowed to have 1 child, a son (your heir) and no second child.All NPC's can have 2 kids(btw they can have 2 of the same gender).- Limited buildings amount. You cannot have as many stations/houses and families as you want.- Massive fps drops near your owned animals/their houses & fields in which wheat/rye/oat are grown.- The Tavern is useless.- No option to assign barn workers to plant specific seeds in selcted fields.Rants because i can:- You can hire up to 8 barn workers, in reality only 3-4 per barn do anything ever, tf??- Some vendor NPC's sound like robotic psychopaths.- Not many places to visit in order to buy/sell stuff, or build your community. The map is too small basically, you can barely find an 'even' enough ground to base in.I'll keep you all updated if i find more positive/negative stuff <3Aside of that, now that i'm rich, gotta step up the design game -> in the making.

_childDocuments_.review: - Dialogues - very plain, simple, not voiced, at least yet.- Quests - there are two quest lines I am aware of, and they are not exactly the longest ones. They get padded by often having to wait for the next day or the next season, which is imo actually a fairly clever and nice design - if done right, we could see characters and world progress and develop over the years, which could be very satisfying, but right now, the game is only ready for such design, not really there yet.- Graphics - it's not AAA next-gen, but looks overall good. I really love trees, they do look like the real things. However, I would appreciate more tree models, all trees of the same kind seem to be just 1 model, with only varying scale. In general, more variation to the buildings would also be appreciated, all houses look the same. Their size can change with levels, but does not vary across one level, and their shape is always the same, which gets boring, especially in a building game.- I really like the attention to detail in production lines. It's complex, without being too much. However, I'd appreciate some compost building which would allow for food to get rotted faster, because initially, it is very tough to get enough fertilizer without buying it for quite a sum.- There is not much to do really. You run, you build, you farm resources, you kill animals. That's it. Not even bandits in this game or anything like that.- There are quite a few weapons and tools which can be crafted, but no armor, only clothing, and no military in the game in general.- The villagers look mostly more or less the same. Couple of faces, couple of hats, and those get repetitive fast. No variation in height, body shape. All animals look the same as well.So, overall, the game looks as a solid platform to build on and can have a very good potential if it gets some engaging stories, quests, more variation in items and buildings, people and animals, and if it introduces more things to do in general. Right now, it seems promising, but is still very, very bare bones. It's EA, so, we shall see.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I proceed to rip this game apart, I just want to highlight the fact that at its' core it is an amazing game with boundless potential considering that it is still in early access.In it's current state I feel like there are some major missed opportunities, some basic features I would have expected for the genre and some quality of life improvements that I would love to see; The amount of variety of Mushrooms is on point, the way it has been implemented is immersive and I love it. But compared to berries I just get confused. Maybe the dev team just really like mushrooms or perhaps they are allergic to berries, I don't know. But I would have loved to see blackberries, forest/wild strawberries, raspberries, lingonberries and gooseberries.I can accept the fact that there seems to be a lack of wildlife diversity considering the small region the game is played out in, but I would have liked to have seen more critters such as squirrels, mice and birds.You are literally convincing immigrants to enter into indentured servitude for nothing but food and shelter until the day they die of old age while you reap all of the rewards. *cough* voluntary slavery *cough* This is a big annoyance to me personally, walking through my town I keep seeing the same house again and again and again and again and again. I would have loved to see that each wall type would have 10-12 variations, a bit of Ivy on one, a cross beam on another, a bit of moss here and an oddly colored stone in another. It seems like something that wouldn't be overly difficult to implement in all honesty and a massive missed opportunity to create an engaging and immersive experience.Why can I not dig a well? It seems like a fairly common object to find in a medieval village.Why can I not build a watchtower? Hopefully this'll come with bandits.. It seems like another missed opportunity considering villagers will actually patrol at night, let them go to a watchtower instead. Maybe the building is purely aesthetic, maybe it increases happiness to villagers that live withing 50m, doesn't matter, it would have been immersive and given the players more range to create amazing things.Why can I not build a gate? What's the point of walls when you have to leave openings all over the place?Let me hire a villager to be a groundskeeper, someone who'll simply walk around and make sure that all buildings in a range around his "shed" is fixed up at all times.Let me hire a villager to be a scribe, let it cost me 5000 to send that villager off for a year to learn the trade. Once back, that villager should improve the level of information available in the management tab including details such as wood, food and tool usage per day/season/year vs (expected) production per day/season/year to allow me to make better decisions regarding what to build, where to assign villagers etc.The scribe should also allow the player to send them on trade missions to far off places, making agreements on the export of goods. I cannot stress how much this would improve the late game where often I have to throw away stuff at the end of every season because all the vendors are broke and I am out of storage.In a northern European, medieval setting, not seeing a single church, abbey or monastery strikes me as odd. Perhaps the setting isn't medieval at all but more late bronze/early iron age, but then there surely would be some pagan shrines or buildings of worship no? Add it, please. I would love to be able to build a church as part of a challenge from the King once my town reaches a certain size, committing me to pay wages to a member of the clergy, maintaining the church and providing it with the required materials to operate. All in exchange for a large boost to the mood of the villagers.Allow walls (and buildings) to snap to grid and each other.Allow villagers to be assigned to move soil to level bumpy areas. While placing buildings allow hotkeys to lock them in certain directions such as facing north while the player freely moves around. Detach foundations of buildings from the buildings themselves and treat the foundations as fields when being placed.Add clutter to building interiors!Allow players to dig up "Sticks" (the small saplings of the 3 types of trees) and re-plant them (without fields/orchards!).

_childDocuments_.review: Survival and city building with mild narrative. You are a commoner that must deal with farming and pigs, not an epic tale. Knighthood and shiny armors won't come. There's almost no combat.Initially you have to grind a lot of resources to live another day, then you have to grind a lot of resources to develop a village. At this stage your villagers will grind resources for living and you grind resources to expand and develope your village.You will also have to drag the resources you have grinded across the map several times at walking speed.Well, if all of this is your cup of tea, then it's really well made and unique. For sure it is my cup of tea, I love sandboxes that make me relax and grind at my page and where I have the freedom to build everywhere. That's when emergent storytelling comes out and I'd already have a lot os little stories to tell about the beginning of my glorious peasant village covered with mud.TL;DR if you like sandboxes and don't mind grinding at your pace to build your stuff the way you like absolutly don't miss this one. If you are looking for an epic narrative and a lot of dramatic storytelling and cut troath combat look away.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game. A slow paced game about everyday life in the medieval period is appealing to me. A welcome break from like every other medieval game which seem to center around combat.It didn't work for me. The tech tree progression is too weird and unrealistic. The game has different areas like farming, hunting, and crafting, which is cool, but you're only allowed to do extremely basic versions of those things at the start. Then if you grind them the game unlocks new tiers. But even after you unlock new tiers, you still have to spend in-game coin to unlock individual items to craft.A really simple example is cooking. You build your first house and it automatically comes with a cooking pot (more on this later). Can you use it? No. Even though you're surrounded by wilderness full of mushrooms and other edibles you can pick and in any sane world you could drop them in the pot. I mean, eventually if you grind cooking enough by roasting meat—and only meat—over an open fire, you unlock the option to buy the ability to use a recipe to be able to put ingredients in your cooking pot. As if it's secret rocket science to try putting vegetables in a pot. Total immersion-breaking unrealism!I get that a game like this needs progression. It needs an excuse for you to make and sell things, in this case so you can get coin and unlock progression. But  as part of your progression mechanic.My other complaint about this game is the cookie-cutter structures. You get to pick the location and orientation of the structure, but otherwise all structures of the same type look identical, including the interior (cooking pots and all). It's hard for me to put my finger on exactly what I dislike. For example, I don't mind that all the structures are the same in Satisfactory. But there you just plop them down and they're built. In Medieval Dynasty, you plop down the blueprint, but then you still have to individually "hammer" each separate section of the structure (after going back and forth to get supplies cause you can't carry enough to make an entire building in one go). That kind of tedium is rewarding when you have the ultimate power to customize how everything looks, like Minecraft, but here it's just unfun work. A good example of a game that got medieval-style building right is Valheim. Honestly working on my village in this game just makes me want to go play that game. Valheim doesn't have the cool village inhabitant subsystem, but the building of the village is much more satisfying.It's a shame, because other than the areas I've called out, this game is pretty solid all around for what it is. The graphics are noticeably above-average for the genre. If the things I called out aren't that important to you, I'd actually encourage you to give this game a try.However if you want a game with good technology progression, I recommend TerraFirma Craft. It's not medieval era—unfortunately I don't know any other medieval era games like this—but it is focused on primitive technology (farming, metal working etc.) so it might scratch the same itch for you. That game also has a slow, grindy start, but the slowness is grounded in a historically realistic tech progression, not arbitrary restrictions for the sake of progression, and I think that makes all the difference.

_childDocuments_.review: Before we get started, I have to tell you, and I'm almost sure of it!I have never played such a well-executed village management game!Perfectly matching graphics, atmosphere and gameplay!Simple yet helpful tutorial.You can set your world separately, how you want it and with what settings to play.The fact that you can play in singleplayer and in coop with several people is also a huge plus point.The looting, exploration, survival and survival elements in the game just fit so damn well with this game!The first time I tried it, I played it for 7 hours with a friend, the game is amazing!The fact that you can tell people who lives in your village should do what, and you can have a wife and partner, you can have children because you get old and then you need someone to take your place, well, that's a damn good idea!The fact that there are events that happen in the game so that the gameplay doesn't get stuck at a fixed point is also damn cool!There are different seasons with their associated problems and benefits.The seasons are pretty damn spectacular.There is a system that if you steal, cheat others, or are a jerk, people will hate you and this will lead to negative things, e.g. you can't trade in the city, etc.Hundreds of hours of content, but more like thousands, there is no question that the price they ask for the game is, I repeat, well worth it!I can only recommend this game! Amazing and nice work!

_childDocuments_.review: It's far from a perfect game. There are many glitches and strange things that happen, but the developers seem to be updating the game very frequently (Sometimes twice in one day) to fix issues. I like this game, but it might not be for you. Many of the mechanics that I like, you may find annoying. It's a grind. There is encumbrance and you will reach that limit very quickly. It makes everything you choose to do actually important because the seasons last 3 in game days. Do you gather food to store it for the winter or will you hunt for animals to survive? Once you start inviting people to your new settlement and assign them to a job, it really opens up and allows you to focus on what area of the game play that you like. Until then, you have to do it all. I recommend that you watch someone play it and pick it up if you wan't a different take on the survival genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a rare gem among many games of similar kind. I always enjoyed the games like banished or the like. What they lacked was immersion for me though, being your own character and just enjoying the gameplay from first-person perspective. This game? The immersion is over 9000!Pros:- There is no rush anywhere, you can relax while playing this game.- Great survival aspect, very realistic.- No game breaking bugs in early access- Building is a chore, but at the end of a few seasons, you look at what you have built little by little and truly feel a sense of accomplishment.- Devs keep in touch with community and provide frequent updates.Cons:- Lack of character customization for greater personalization, especially if the game is not voiced. Ability to let players have their own name would be welcomed.- A bit generic yet, but it is still early access so understandable.Overall it is too soon to rate it yet, as this is still early access, but so far the Devs do terrific job. It is a diamond in the rough that can be initially rated 9/10 due to how much promise it shows. The end rating might change with time, depending on developer but so far I love it :)
_childDocuments_.name: Medieval Dynasty

_childDocuments_.review: Good game with fun elements. More fun then Life is Feudal as there is much less grind (though some still present). Biggest annoyances are long travel time between cities. When horses are enabled then may seem less significant but as of now I spend a lot of time bouncing around the map. Mutliplayer would also make this game better. I think thats also on the road map
_childDocuments_.name: Medieval Dynasty

_childDocuments_.review: Beginner Tip:- If you are new to this game, customise the game settings. Specifically the percentage you gain skill and technology skill points. I did 1000% because I want to unlock everything and still play at my own pace. Otherwise it is an absolute GRIND.This game is a beautiful blend of grinding and exploring. There is always something to do. I find that even with quick skill gaining, it has still taken me a long time to get someone into a routine with my town of 4 people. I mainly enjoy the farming process and animals and also enjoy crafting items to sell. I play on 3 day seasons and find this keeps everything flowing quickly. Crops won't grow until the season change so longer seasons means you have to plan your crops out better to go without for longer. I always make sure to get a woodcutter hut and a lumberjack worker ASAP, as those logs are the most precious resource in the entire game (it also doesn't cut down trees). Besides that, it's a great game to relax and play and I'm looking forward to seeing the new content that is being added in future updates.
_childDocuments_.name: Medieval Dynasty

_childDocuments_.review: So, II will keep my feelings out of this review so it is more a mathematical approach and not a OMG ITS FANTASTIC.Graphics- I run a ryzen 7 with 64 gigs DDR4 and a RTX 3060.The game is installed on  a nvme terrabyte.All settings maxxed ultra and i run 180 fps.In its current iteration there are very rare "hiccups"For its price it is more than acceptable.Gameplay- If No mans Sky was set in the medieval era, had a child and made it grind a whole day for a meal let alone a house, they nailed it. (side note you can greatly reduce alot of grinding in the beginning setup if you have a job and cant play 155 hrs before you have a settlement.)This type of neutering normally has the effect of making the game a day endevour and then dust bin of history mode. My 15 hrs is in one sitting and ive only broke the crust. 5 stars Dev.The amount of present content and freedom of game play is astonishing, I hope the skill and tech sectors are increased to accommodate of type of career path that allows more unique choices for your character but it works for base standard.The map is small compared to red dead 2 or skyrim but it works.Building a settlement is a little clunky but enjoyable nonetheless.If raiders were to attack settlements and you could form a settlement militia I think id never turn this game off.To summarize, I've never wrote a review this long and I am compelled too.If you like a FPS that you can build unique settlements anywhere you want and manage them like a life sim, explore and hunt and mine and fish and court/marry/have a sire to your throne then you will not be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I stopped playing once I figured out what it takes to make Bows a sustainable option. Everything breaks, so you have to make new ones. And the steps required are many and stupid. It's a far cry from a good bit of wood, a knife, fire, and sinew. Same goes for arrows multiplied by fifty. You can't make one (1) arrow. You have to make them in batches of fifty (50).  Why? I don't know. To keep them out of the hands of the poor, I guess. The amount of effort required to be able to make a bow and fifty arrows doesn't equal the increase in power one gets compared to throwing a sharp stick. Game balance, it ain't.
_childDocuments_.name: Medieval Dynasty

_childDocuments_.review: I'm editing my review since my main issue previously was that there was no option to play as a woman. They've since added that, which is awesome! It's nice not to have to play as Racimir specifically, and they've added a whole new area and quests for those that want a more customized experience for such a sandbox game.The game is very fun, quite immersive in a lot of respects, and has a lot of survival elements I enjoy. At the same time, it isn't too brutal about accidentally dying to say, getting mauled by a bear in the middle of a deep lake. You have to worry about heat and cold, dirtiness, hunger, stamina, and thirst. You have to eat a pretty reasonable amount, not constantly but not once a day either. There's lots of variable gather/hunt/purchase quests that give you something to help you stay motivated, and it has a lot of opportunities for you to sort of create your own story around your player, and add your own challenges for plots.For example, in my current save, I only recruit new people to my village once a year or so, one at a time, so I can get used to them and not build up a huge place all at once.I'll always support them if they add more variation in character options, different body builds, more skin tones, more romance options like same-sex marriage with adoption instead of traditional childbirthing. I like a lot of the effort put into realism, but there's so much room in a story like this to be creative and provide options for players to customize their games. I'd also love more customization with clothing? Dyes maybe, or different styles of outfits. Dresses or skirts and blouses for people or even just women to wear would be nice too instead of making women wear the same default tunic and trousers meant for men. Even some elements of childcare would be cool, since the main point of the game is continuing your "dynasty" but you don't currently have to do too much for that to happen.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is in fact  lovely and challenging. The idea of creating a town of your own with farms, hunters etc is  fantastic. However there are some features to be improved. First of all, to be able to have tenants  you have to convince homeless people sitting idle in front of a camp fire in each town and you need a certain amount of approval evel to do that. On the other hand, the speech options are limited and you can only ask a few questions in one day. This makes hard to find villagers for your own settlement.The same problem occurs when you want to flirt with a woman. Another problem is while hunting even after hitting the deer with 4 or 5 spear it stil can run away and sometimes it stops running and you can start hitting by spear. So to hunt a small dear could take a long timeç It would be much more better if they could die off bleeding just as in Long Dark.Another problem with hunting is you cannot   seem to find the hunting areas unless you come accross wild animals by luck. It would be better if we could learn hunting areas for different types of animals by speaking the locals. There şs a speech option in which you could ask "have you heard any rumors lately?" could guide you to new hunting areas, even to new quests.The game also encourages to steal items as they are too expensive to buy especially in the beginning. Also, even if you can craft a leather bag you cannot seem to use it for fertilizers or seed  so you have to either buy a ordinary bag or steal one.Quests are a bit dull, and you need to walk from one village to another and it takes too long. This makes difficult whether to focus on building or crafting or finishing quests to get rewarded dynasty points.The music is humdrum and I usually turn of the music sound during game play. Despite these problems, this is the game designed for survialist and crafters.  It has great potential and since it is still in the early access phase, I guess they can make the gameplay better, design lively NPC's and write more realistic dialogs and increase the variety of quests.,

_childDocuments_.review: Oh how I love and hate this game.  Love the creativity, the open world to explore, finding the PERFECT spot for your house. _childDocuments_.review: So far I've had a very relaxed experience. I survived for one whole 'year' which is all seasons. One of the things that hit it out of the park for me was the option to ask someone to get out of your way. I know it seems like a small thing but I've been traumatized by certain games (ahem LYDIA) by getting trapped in rooms or buildings with no way of getting the person to move. The resources are pretty common but you have to use or store them smartly to get you through the winter when there aren't many available. If you're looking for more hardmode survival this isn't for you. That being said, it's a great game to build, interact, flirt, and just be sort of casual which is just what I need sometimes. The one thing that's sort of a negative is the seasons can seem kind of short to be able to complete all your tasks in a timely manner. Definitely not game-breaking. I can't wait to see the further development!

_childDocuments_.review: Yes. I would recommend. I like the way this game takes me to another time / world to invent my own little narratives while I play, that said - I toyed with the main quest lines, been there done that. I am more sandboxer and I do NOT re-do, repeat.... I don't even want to wash dishes at reality (obviously you have to, but the point is made), because that job is never done. But mostly the high dislike I got for repetitive tings that demand physical energy is because I am ill and retired for health reasons, I don't have capacity like I used to even for small things. Even gaming has been less possible with my issues, which is why I don't have more hours in the game. I do like it. And for balances sake, what I don't like is how damned tied you are to having to do quests, lack of full sandbox mode and generally - above all else - only 140 top building limit and that is already 200% of the standard. I would need 300% aka 210 buildings for what I recently wanted to build. I got the space; my computer is running smooth and well - so what if some folk need to keep to the 70. That's fine by me, but idk why the top limit has to be just twice as much. I am into 2 years of 20 day seasons - and I am full with buildings 140 most of which have NPC to them. And I don't have heir yet, because I am training the husband - lol - he needs to have great stats before I will make any babies - lol. Ah but that aside, I don't think I will be able to finish the game I started to get to what I wanted to do with it because of that 140 limit. I have ton of space inside the town yet - I mean here I wanted to build, to which extend. My end goal has got nothing to do with the quest lines - the rude oxbow leader can cry rivers for all I care. I just wanted to make a large, well positioned, automated and well earning - above all very nice looking a town. And as that meant a lot of NPC, lot of houses, large plan.... so on - if bit too tired to bother to calculate to stay in parameters of game's 140 limit. Just wanted to have fun, rather than care for such. Well did not get to do the fun part, which is finish the placement of houses, workshops, all buildings, fields orchards and THEN fully decorate and make it all look cool. I know I could reduce number of wells, number of mines, number.... of.... but that is not what I want to do. I do not want to be limited in my ability to collect mats to do what ever I want. I don't care about the struggle, when I just want to build and make nice looking a town. And so - why do I tell you this here, even if I like the game and would recommend it? Because this game has what can give you the ability to imagine those all sorts of little stories of your own - for me it hits right era, a lot of right. No, you wont get to build castles or be some lord per se. What you do get is two pretty regions to build on and decent variety of things to do with all though we can all hope for more and devs are still doing stuff for it and mind you - you don't need to pay for extra parts, from what now is in store if I am not wrong. But dynasty type games do have also a bit too many limits to them. And in case of this one it definitely is in having to follow quests or more directly not having sandbox and having too small building count limit for those of us who like to go beyond and have the computer to handle it, because we know what our way of playing demands. And so, this game is there, in between – perfect setting, look and in-game feel to too limited, even if you can 'simulate' sand box with certain setting changes. I actually don't mind having to trade, to set up production lines, doing some random side quest - as long as I get to do what ever I want to use the building mechanics for. And there aren't many games that put you in right period of time for that. And so many of them come with too much fighting - frankly I don't want my built place to be attacked and destroyed, even if I would gladly fight some bit to get mats and find stuff and feel like things happen about the map. For example, I find it a great pity how every one of the broken buildings in the maps have nothing new to them, once you have been there - or not often enough. It doesn't take me even a day to empty them all. On oxbow, that can take you easily to a considerable starter coin purse. But just like those 'random' finds of broken carts, camps and bandits around the map - one should really see bandits return into those empty broken hideouts more. Should see other people in them more too on occasion. Random passer by, or yes this does happen NPC to hire - but very rarely, like at other locations too. I found those without any quests, you know, the special NPC.  But do we not all have little wishes. It is still being worked, and yet the quest lines are pretty well done, if a bit silly and purposefully annoying at times. But when you really enjoy the design, the placement, making things run and above all, once all is done as large as you want (hopefully, rather than large as you but can) decoration... it runs into a bit of limits which funny enough isn't in lack of stuff or fear that there would not be more of such things eventually. It is that building limit. But that does not mean the game is bad - it means that it is so good than it does not let you enough to do with it.

_childDocuments_.review: played for 40+hrs so far, the game is super awesome tho its a bit graphic card and ram consuming. I can run it at lowest of setting.Positive: awesome graphics, nice sound, nature/lake is nice. love some of the npc especially female hair braids etc. love it when they change the dress style in winter and summer.I really love the tiny creeks and big rivers. looks quite realistic. The game has a ton of possibilities.I have put off this game because of the few negative reviews but I really regret not buying then. personally I don't mind few of the negatives. as far I know this game is quite addictive and I don't know how much time goes by when I play it.Con:- the game has several glitches especially when it comes to npc. they often get stuck in tables, chairs, fence and hilariously some times on the roof etc. worst part about npc is some of them sleep during day time and its quite worse when you are in real bind for food and the shop keeper is asleep and let you die of hunger. some quest npc sleep in day too so you have to wait extra hrs. also needs a good tutorial or guide cause something you have to fail a lot to understand how it works.Time/Seasons/Year/day-night pass by too fast. 24 min=24 hrs in-game and 72 min(72 hrs)=1 season(3 month) and 4 season =1 year so 4.8 hrs is 1 year. I really didn't like that but now they updated to max of 30  days per season(or was it a month?). I thank the creators for that change.Marriage in this game is bit hard, it would take 10 days to 2 years in-game to woo a girl to marry. also when you start in village you are 18 and there is very few single 18 yr old girls available to marry in any village(tried to woo few but they don't have marriage option) and all the 19 yr old's are already married. so please add more marriageable 18-20 yr old girls/women. also lower the difficulty to woo a women.  If you can could you add like gift or pay certain lump-sum to the girls father(isn't it like 8-10 sheep for women in African countries or something? :P) so you can cut the time to get married.  few tips from me.  if you find your self in bind when overwhelm by mobs pres esc and press unstuck and you get teleport'ed back to the location where you started.(I've heard they removed that) do not harvest unripe berries wait for summer and get edible berries as it has no poison.  first thing you should unlock is the ability to scan food and herbs everywhere using left alt. A good way to make good money is making lots of knives as it has the most profit per resource.when you do side quest make it as the active quest to check if it is timed. I've failed 3 so far cause I didn't know it was timed and lost prestige.  best place to make house is near beginner town a bit to the west near clay deposit next to forest and river so you have access to lumber,clay and water. you can move later when you find mining cave. conclusion:- game is great and has a lot of possibilities but it needs to nerf few npc issues then you got good game. to make it a great game add voice to every npc shop and non quest npcs.also thank you very much for seeing mine and many peoples reviews and adding bags for more storage space.few suggestions:- have craft'able cart so we can hold more ores or wood etc. since there is already horses and Donkeys, please add horse carriage to hold least 100-300 kg of wood/ores. also have a traveling merchant that goes to every town via the road where you can have them come to your town if you add market. perhaps you should be able to ride in their wagon to cut short on running time to get to every towns(for quests,buy and sell goods) I have more ideas but I'll post it when I remember them.Thank you very much creators of this game for adding the changes I've previously asked for.ps: could you add personality change to the girl you marry? cause even after marriage she still treats me as a stranger often and very cold towards me despite her mood at 70%.  there should be more romantic words or sentence to say to her so she would be more loving towards me character and we should actually be able to go near river(my town is next to river) to have picnic as promised during the courtship.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an escape to simpler times. It's not all about quick-fire combat, but planning, growing, enjoying life. You can take a wander through the trees (assuming you've completed your chores for the season) or go and chat up the local waitress in the pub. Yes, there are beasties that will like to take a bite out of you, but avoid them and life can be fun. I am amazed at how much satisfaction I get from crafting a new bow, clothing, or even a wooden spoon! Recommended to builders, planners, people with stressful lives!

Rinse repeat as you build an entire village and "automate" food production, animal husbandry, farming, mining, fishing, crafting, cooking and... pay your taxes.

_childDocuments_.review: In short - a very good game.It's under survival/building categories in steam. I'd call it building/survival.It felt like survival is secondary in the game. Can be pretty difficult at first, but can be overcome very early and easily with no learning curve. From that point on it's just doing stuff with very little resistance from the game-world.I get that it's a sandbox game, but still - the biggest downside for me is a lack of quests and direction. The story quests can be completed rather quickly and side quests start repeating themselves real soon. I completed all the story quests and did every side quest multiple times before even unlocking a significant portion of buildings and recipes for item crafting.Village management is pretty straightforward and intuitive, but lacks a challenge there as well (played on medium).Sound is great. So is the ambience music. One of very very few games I play with native music on. What I missed the most in sounds was narrated interaction with NPCs. They say "hi" and "bye" and everything else is reading. Quite a bit at times.Crafting takes unusually a lot of game time and kinda forces you to have villagers craft a lot of stuff for you, Same goes for resource gathering. I really liked that part. You can do a lot of things yourself in a small village or manage a big one and spend more time practicing to shoot a bow or do side quests.I loved the graphics and the world itself. It looks beautiful and feels quite alive with day/night cycles, changing seasons, all the wildlife and villages. Good attention to details.Good controls. Not superb but good. Due to controls and item management mechanics, some actions are very repetitive and feels like they could've been not so much.There are options to get unstuck and have an NPC move if it's blocking something. Good thing I didn't need those much, as game has very solid mechanics and physics, but it helped here and there.It's not an action game. Hunting CAN get rather exciting, but it's not an action game in any way. Very relaxing and pleasant, which makes it not for everyone I guess.If I could give a single advice for new players, it would be: to start small and take it slow, which I didn't.In-game time seems to work against you at first, but trust me - you have more time than you need. I prioritised main quests and completed all story quests plus all the different kinds of side quests multiple times, all that BEFORE my character reached age of 24 (you start a 18).I'd give the game 8 or 9 points out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so its still in early access & there are a few bugs but, overall, it's a challenging & engaging survival/city builder game. You cannot rush thru it unlike a lot of similar games, you have to plan carefully & save before you talk to the npc persons you want to attract to your village/town. Following the main quests are very important as it will unlock the amount of buildings you can build. As for buildings, i found (after 3 restarts) that you need to start with 1: house 2: food storage 3: mats storage 4: hunters lodge, there may be better options but if you want to attract atleast 1 npc to your village, you need to keep them fed & happy. Talking to the free npc daily is a must so you can build up a rep with them (remember to save before talking) & if you get a negative response, reload & try with a different question. Also, it's best to google anything you are not sure of such as animal or resource locations as this will speed up what you can do each day.The biggest issue you will encounter is the lack of time per day/season so you need to get as much done as possible as the seasons change every 3 days (or so it seems) so keep following the main quests before you do the mundane things such as felling trees or hunting etc.Remember to wash before entering a town & interacting with the npc (you can make a wash tub from your crafting menu) as you stand a better chance of getting a positive reply. As for making money, well, there are plenty of you-tube videos to check out regarding this. Remember to use the steam guide to sellers so you know which npc sells what. I would recommend you go to LESNICA asap and trade with Teobald (iron tools) & Gizela (weapons & bows).In summary, this game is sure to be a good investment for the future & its is already proving a headache for me with 20 hours playtime which is keeping me interested & playing. I hope this review is helpful & good luck should you take the time to play it :-)

_childDocuments_.review: Medieval Dynasty is a survival simulation game set in medieval times that offers a unique gameplay experience. The game allows players to take on the role of a peasant who must build a village, establish a dynasty, and navigate the challenges of survival in a harsh environment. The game's graphics and sound design are impressive, and the attention to detail in the game's mechanics and systems is exceptional. The game offers a range of activities, including farming, hunting, and trading, and the player's decisions have real consequences on their survival and the prosperity of their village. However, the game can feel slow-paced at times, and some may find the lack of direction or guidance overwhelming. Overall, Medieval Dynasty is a fantastic game that offers a fresh take on the survival genre, and it's well worth playing for anyone interested in medieval history or simulation games.

_childDocuments_.review: Update 1.0.0.6: This game still has MAJOR pacing issues.They improved some of the issues (animals run a little slower when injured; updated some incorrect text; et cetera). The animals/enemies still have terrible pathing, but the main issue I have with it is that it just doesn't feel "fun." You're meant to level up your skills and technology, but the ways to do so are repetitive, tedious and require SOOOOOO many of these repetitive actions (I've been playing for nearly 60 hours and I'm not even halfway through most of these technology trees). The seasonal quests are extremely generic fetch quests. The rewards aren't even that great, which really makes you ask yourself why you bothered to run across the entire map. The world itself feels pretty empty (I understand that this is realistic, but that doesn't mean it's good game design). Crafting takes so long that I regularly start a queue and walk away from my computer because you just have to sit there for several minutes, staring at a progress bar. Lastly, I've come to despise walking (this is coming from someone who completed and loved Death Stranding). What's that? There are horses you can ride? That's true, but that looks like it's going to require about 100 hours to unlock...I should have stopped playing when I was 20 hours in, but I fell victim to the sunk cost fallacy. I'm uninstalling and walking away from this one.Original review:This game was not ready to be released. This is so far from polished and there are still bugs that cause hard crashes.The 1.0 release fixed a bug that crashed my game 3 times in 10 hours, but there are plenty of old issues and new issues that should have been resolved before releasing this title.The first issue is with the main storyline: The game allows you to build up to your maximum number of buildings. But the way to unlock more building slots is by building specific buildings prompted by a quest. If you forgot, or didn't know (the game doesn't show you how many structures you have or your current limit inside the main building menu), then you have to destroy a building or two so you can build the building you need to unlock more slots. This means you end up wasting a ton of time and resources for no sensible reason.None of the new potions have proper text. It's all the same text that looks copied and pasted from one of the grain descriptions.Hunting is also really annoying, which might not be a big deal if it wasn't such a huge part of the game. Animal movement patterns are completely unpredictable and janky as hell. To make matters worse, they also run away at full speed when injured. I'm pretty sure I've seen some injured deer despawn as they run away, but that could be drawn distance (even though my settings are maxxed out). It did not seem to be that hard to track down injured animals in the version right before release. Certain animals also seem to have more HP. All-in-all, hunting feels pretty frustrating.One of the main quests required me to plant crops and it happened to be winter, which made me waste the seeds and fertilizer. Why...?I get that this isn't a game that wants to do much hand-holding, but a lot of these things just feel bad when they happen. It's not the fun kind of failure state where it feels deserved and motivates your to get better. This game unintentionally asks you to do some and these things, then punishes you for it. I suspect this is just an oversight by the developers who have probably played a lot of this game and don't know what it feels like to be a new player anymore, which is why a lot of these new changes to 1.0 should have been test in EA.I've played and loved games like The Long Dark, The Forest, Valheim, et cetera. I'm no stranger to survival games that give you very little direction. What direction Medieval Dynasty does give isn't very help at best, and may set you back at worst.The leveling system is also just...not fun. Every skill tree has 1 or more talents that increase the speed of your experience in each tree. This means that you are probably going to spend your first 3 skill points in each tree on a totally boring, talent instead of something that actually feels useful. Why not just remove those talents and slightly reduce the xp requirement for all skill trees?The management UI is also a bit of a nightmare. It's also missing a lot of "quality of life" things like: how many total types of each resource is needed to complete a blueprint you've placed; not using resources when you initially place a blueprint, so you can confirm it before wasting resource, then realizing it's not actually where you wanted to place it; being able to see how much money you have when you're about to confirm a purchase.I'll probably play a little more, but I would not recommend this game in its current state to anyone expecting a polished final game experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun gameplay. I'm 8 hours in and it still feels like there is so much to discover about this game! My humble village of 3 people barely scratches away a living off the land. However, I just learned how to start sewing new clothes, which I began to sell to the neighboring villages for immense profit. Maybe I will get run through by an angry bison, maybe I will succumb to the harsh winter, and maybe (just maybe) I can build a dynasty to last the test of time. I highly recommend buying this game, it plays as a medieval animal crossing with a lot of emphasis on survival and networking. The graphics are beautiful, the gameplay is entertaining, free roaming medieval Europe has never been so exhilarating. Some people are reluctant to buy an early access game starting at $30, and I can completely understand that. Many games on Steam are early access and with that you expect a game that is incomplete and has much more to offer in the future. However, this game plays like an actual completed product. I can only anticipate what else the developers plan to hone and add to this beautifully made game. If you have read this far, you should just buy Medieval Dynasty! Try it out and if you don't like it (which I highly doubt) you can always return the game through Steam's refund policy. There is no time to waste, your dynasty awaits!

_childDocuments_.review: Again, as many have said in many reviews, I wish there was a middle option. I think this game WILL be fantastic, but it is not finished yet. And that's perfectly ok because it is "early access."   This game is taking the survival game to the next level. Because you are not just surviving, you are actually creating a village, and a dynasty. I have merely scratched the surface, but let me say what I like and dislike so far. Likes:- Interacting with neighbors, and doing quests for them. - Hunting is not difficult, and is fun - Buildings are pre-designed layout, and once built, come furnished with workbenches, etc. Dislikes: - Needs some way to show ALL materials needed to build a building before you build it. (If this can be found somewhere I can't find it)- Interactions with villagers is repetitive. Needs more dialogue options. - Progression is a bit wonky.  (e.g. It tells you to build a barn, but you need to raise farming skill first, but you need the barn to create fertilizer to do farming; I cheesed this a bit by building fields, working them with my hoe, then destroying them over and over until my skill was high enough to build a barn) Things that are just weird:- Every season lasts exactly 3 days. - Your carrying capacity is by weight, but you can chop down 3 trees and just carry all the logs no problem.- I can throw a spear right through the brain of a boar, and it just gets mad and comes at me with a long pole sticking out of its head. Summary: I tend to not buy early access games, but I bought this one. I definitely see the potential for a fantastic game in the future. Right now it is playable, but it can get frustrating and needs a lot of polish.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an enjoyable and chill village builder where you can shoot bears in the butt with arrows.Mornin’. Nice day for fishin aint it, hu-hah!This game really makes you FEEL like a medieval peasant.It's always a breath of fresh air when a medieval game is just historical medieval, and not filled with dragons and fireballs. As I grow older I'm becoming more into lifestyle games like this.Medieval Dynasty is like Skyrim and Banished fusion, but it lacks in both departments. While those games have nearly unlimited replayability, Medieval Dynasty gets quite boring after some 50-100 hours, it's still fun, but I wish it had more.I love survival games but often create and gather too much. I've always wanted to be able to play with others and trade, however in games like Ark players just destroy your home often times. I also play at a slow pace and enjoy exploration.This game has provided a lot of what I enjoy. I can craft, gather, build, get married, have children, trade, hunt, explore, and quest. Any time I get bored with something I can go do another thing. Having villagers lets my production stay up so I can go gallivanting off in the countryside.The ability to customize my game play on the fly has been awesome too. If I want to up the ante while hunting no problem, if I want to take it easy and get my village together right quick I can do that too and I dont have to restart.I just like how relaxing it is and how you can actually see your work pay off. It's a grind fest, yeah. I usually read or listen to podcasts in the background with it. I just have always wanted to play something like this. Low effort and chill. Plus I always wondered what it would be like to live back then. Even though this isn't even close to how it really was, it's still nice.It has excellent foundations. The concept of building a dynasty is wonderful. The fact that it is a town management sim played from a first person perspective is great as well.The biggest flaw is that after 1 generation or 2 depending on how quickly you progress, you effectively can't advance further. You've grown your village as much as you can. Which does kinda pull the rug from under the whole "dynasty" aspect to the game.I'd love to see your village be able to grow into a proper town. To have the ability to grow your manor into a keep while further fortifying the surrounding area.I think I like this game because it just scratches so many itches for me. Crafting/survival/RPG questlines/city builder and management is a ridiculously specific combination of genres, but it's all in Medieval Dynasty, in one package. The problem is that, while the game has all those features, they're all still too basic and shallow. The game is an excellent foundation as it is, and that's what has carried it this far, but a foundation alone isn't a complete game.That said, Render Cube has been really good with communication and have so far delivered on every feature they've promised in roadmaps and more, which is a good track record to set. MD is far from a complete game right now, but in time it will be.Over all, I love the game and do a new play through a few times a year. If you're into town building games and enjoy the medival aesthetic, then you'll enjoy yourself. However, it is an indie game still in development, so a bit of expectation management is in order. This won't be the one and only game you play for the next 5 years, but it's definitely worth sinking a few weeks into as you watch your hut and field grow into a sprawling city.10/10 Would shoot bears in butt again.

_childDocuments_.review: Out of concerns I pointed my thumb sideways in the beginning, because I still had the bad animations and partly bad conversations from Farmers Dynasty in mind.Now back to Medieval Dynasty. I can say that it is currently my favourite game, but I can not hide the fact that some was still a bit unbalanced and messy in this game in the beginning. It were typical Early Access problems. I am used to those because I do a lot of early access reviews in my curator group and on YouTube. Bugs did appear while playing and if you saved the game very often almost all of them could be avoided by reloading the game before they happened. On the other hand there are still a few constant small problems too, like too few storage room and any quest might not want to work for you, but those are rather tiny problems.  Meanwhile the game was a lot improved and you clearly see the progress. The developers added a lot that was asked for by the community and fixed most bugs. I did not encounter any anymore and I played this game more than 700 hours. I think the main content will be there when the game gets out of Early Access now. They really did a great job and you can feel in every detail how they put their love into the game. They did not give up early just to get fast money from this title. You may expect a DLC somewhen later after release.I personally love the game because it has just this brilliant theme to build a life and village up in the medieval times. It has survival aspects to it and RPG elements as well as management tasks to handle your villagers. Another fact you need to know is that your crafting and building abilities ( there are only prebuild blueprints for buildings) largely depend on development of technologies, that ask you to farm yourself, hunt yourself, but also build constantly buildings and even tear them down to get points for that research. I disliked this a bit, because it was partly a pain to get those points. I did in the end quests, that leveled those missing skills, especially for mining.The main story ends after a few years. You could critisize that the side quests are not really very compelling, rather short and superficial, like "get me 5 meat, I'm starving". They could have put some more attention into those and it shows that their main focus is not the RPG part, it is rather a nice addition to the building and raising your own village. I still enjoyed the RPG part too.The game is still addictive and I played it with a lot of fun, in the beginning some stress to earn enough money for my taxes and do some quests, even more worry to handle asides my village, the decay of my buildings and problems to understand all mechanisms without guide. The decay was meanwhile reduced and is well balanced. To be fair I have to say that the game turned out to be very nice and is absolutely worth its money. They are planning to add more to the game and then it could turn out to be really genius. I love the beauty of its nature and the little details they did add and I do recommend this game to you. Most is rather relaxing and the survival part is rather easy. Especially when you gain some villagers to live with you and help you at the work it gets pretty easy. The animations of children on the street and your villagers in the tavern are still missing, but I assume they will also change this to let the surrounding look more alive and real.I hope it helped you to decide if you want to get this game. A thumb up would cheer me up :)  More reviews especially for survival and simulation games are on my Top or Flop page if you are interested: And a lot of videos about Medieval Dynasty are here: Happy gaming guys :)

_childDocuments_.review: Although obviously not perfect, Medieval Dynasty is more than your generic survival/simulator game.The fantastic medieval setting and the addicting(Although grindy) Village building, maintaining and growing system are great and will keep you playing with that "One more day" approach trying to get progress another goal.The music is awesome.The game is quite pretty to look at.There's many tasks you can and need to do such as woodcutting, mining, farming and various crafting (Smithing,Sewing, cooking Potionmaking and so on).There's a very obvious sense of progress, when you unlock better tools, have new type of buildings and generally have better and better automization for many of the possible tasks by recruiting more and better villagers.There's actually very impressive sense of realism to many mechanics.There's decent questing.You actually have to put in quite a bit of thought into the management of the jobs, the type of inputs they provide and how to divide your workforce efficiently.Combat exists only in the form of some aggressive wild animals that are easy to avoid and rare spawns of bandits. This allows for a very relaxing and chill playtime.Some issues that I hope they do improve upon are:1) The villagers themselves are rather hollow, they don't really exist as "human" beings but just boring robots strolling along between their jobs and bed time.  Hopefully this would be further fleshed out and the villages themselves would look more lively thanks to it.2A) Although there are many different crafting stations and things to craft, i never really saw a point to most of it.For example, as far as i know, clothes only really matter for the main character and has temperature stats, yet there's so many different crafting options for them (Which also require a fairly decent amount of money to buy the schematics for).There's far more efficient items to craft and sell, and you can pretty much manage your temperature by just wearing straw hat and investing in a skill that negates it. Why would I bother learning and crafting these items when there is no real benefit here. It would be just cheaper to buy the complete item from a vendor anyways. 2B) At the same time the game lacks crafting that allows for more placeable items that give us the option to make our village pretty and unique. It would be nice that instead of numerous of useless potions and clothing we would get more placeable crafting than some tables, chairs, torches, baskets and a wheel.3) The "Default" settings for the game feel too grindy.Although it does give a sense of progression when you unlock something new or build more thing, the experience gain, technology gain and limiting factors such as carry weight are a VERY big burden that only exists to artificially extend the playtime. Luckily the devs have added a way to customize almost every aspect of the game.There's a slider for pretty much anything - Food/water requirements, Unlimited weight/Stamina, faster/slower exp gain, damage taking and so on.The final issue is sort of universal for any game of this nature. By being a sandbox, the game has no real "point" or end.You either reach what would be considered a "Complete" village and are left with only the desire to make the village prettier(Adding fences, stone walls, upgrading buildings and so on) or you could decide you already built enough and move on, after all there is no way to "Win" or any real resolution.Overall the game is good for it's price, especially so if you're already a sort of person that enjoys titles from this genre.There are some things that needed to be improved upon, but the game only recently left Early access and is still being actively updated as far as i know.

_childDocuments_.review: I really hope this game will be improved after getting out of EA. At this point, this game is not much more than the generic open world survival template. You start by crafting your first crude stone tools which enable you to collect more materials, mostly cutting trees (this is what you might be doing for about 90% of the playtime since you need a lot of wood).The one thing that is supposed to set Medieval Dynasty apart from the countless generic survival-games seems to be the part into which they put the least effort so far: the village building and establishment of a village community and dynasty. There are two quest givers and three quest lines, one of which is basically a tutorial. The other two are essentially some fetch quests. You can build a village and invite people to automate some of your crafting and collecting, but the process and result is barely rewarding since settlement development has not been fleshed out in many aspects.
_childDocuments_.name: Medieval Dynasty

_childDocuments_.review: I have really enjoyed my time playing Medieval Dynasty. The graphics are amazing, the world is stunning. Their is a story, mainline of quests to play, but you're also not really racing against the clock to play it. That said, there are some things about this game that won't suite every kind of gamer. This game rewards patience. If you love fast, first shooter games with explosive action, I'm betting you're not going to like this game. There is action; there's animals to hunt, and bandits that periodically roam the land for you to contend with. But, it's not overwhelming, or constant. Above all, you are faced with a very detailed game of resource extraction and management, especially when you start building your own town and inviting NPCs to come live with you. They do their tasks slower than you, but the pay off, is that everything they do, you no longer have to do yourself. But every person is an extra mouth to feed, and you'll have to pay higher taxes the following Spring. This game can also be VERY grindy. There are ways to minimize the intensity of how much you want to grind to level up your character and to advance in the game. (You'll find that in the "Customize Game" settings.) But even after customizing the game, it can take a while to feel like you're making real progress. This where I say that this game isn't for every gamer. But I will say, that it's also well balanced. Take for example, that you start off on foot. The map is fairly large, and running from one end of the map to the other on foot can take you a whole game day. That's IF you don't have any large predators, aggressive animals, or bandits to deal with along the way. There are horses, but they are QUITE expensive to acquire. When I finally managed to save up enough to get one, after having spent a good portion of my time running around on foot, the pay off was IMMENSE! It wouldn't have been the same, if that horse was either given at the beginning, or if the horses were a lot cheaper to acquire. So the bottom line, this is a slow-paced game, that rewards players for taking their time and putting in the work. If you want to instantly get to the top, you will be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is definitely worth trying. I want to start there, because I'm about to complain a whole bunch. If you like the idea of building up your own little village in a medieval open world in a choices-matter sort of way, you'll enjoy dozens of hours with this game. There's even a story to get you out exploring the valley the game is set in.If what you're expecting is a simulation with some teeth, this isn't it. There's a duality here that makes this hurt extra bad. On one hand, the economy is the focal point of the game once you've finished the three or four storylines you access fairly early on. On the other, the economy is utterly ♥♥♥♥♥♥. The player is hundreds of times more productive than experienced workers in most roles. You're heavily incentivized to grind out items that your neighboring villages don't actually need because prices are static and unrealistic. Villager control is awkward, but easily papered over by just doing the work yourself. Once you've come to terms with all of that, the difficulty completely falls away. You can easily become richer than every other person in the valley combined, except it doesn't matter. It makes the game as a whole lose a lot of luster once you're past the main storylines.So, in short: worth playing through the story? Yeah, if this sounds like your kind of game, you'll probably get dozens of good hours out of it. Early settlement building is fun and rewarding, the story is decent, and as long as you're not a completionist, that's all good stuff. If you want an open world version of a city management game, though? This isn't it. I'm not saying the devs couldn't add enough features to get there, but I'm not holding out hope for it. That feels more like a sequel than a patch or DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: Its not a terrible game, but the game suffers from balance issues that make no sense.  I want to like it.  I put it down for a year and tried again, but I still can't get into it.You have to cut down a whole tree to get a log to make one wooden spear, which is bonkers.  The sticks and logs needs a middle ground like a "long stick" that a spear can be made from.  If you throw a spear, it instantly wipes off 25% of its durability.  That's too much, it should count as one hit.Small game meat doesn't replenish very much; you need to eat 20 rabbits to get full for a day.  It feels like you have to constantly gather food to do anything.  I get that they want you to build up to more complex foods like stew and bread, but its a constant struggle considering how fast food depletes.  5 small game to full for a day seems more balanced.  Give complex foods day-long buffs to entice progression.The days are very short, and a season is just 3 days.  If the days were longer and sleep was required, it would make more sense.  But, you can lose a day just walking around and suddenly its next season.  You can change it when the game starts, but a better balance should be the default.The combat is just mindlessly swinging until someone falls over.  You can really only take a few hits before you die, so entering combat means you're probably going to die and have to restart back to your last save.  It needs an overhaul so that strikes, blocks, dodging, and positioning are more tactical.Co-op would be great, but its just not here yet.  Maybe I'll try it again when its in.  Until then, I have to put the game down again.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't a bad game, but really make sure it's for you before you buy it.  It's got a lot of enjoyment to be had, but suffers from excessive realism and dissapointing progressionMedieval Dynasty is actually somewhat enjoyable, but it quickly approaches ♥♥♥♥♥♥ mobile game tiers of slow progression.  It's grindy, and designed to be played on one save for hundreds of hours.  The mechanics are all simple, but slow.  It adds to a sense of realism, but what survival games often offer alongside progression are quality of life upgrades.  Exponentially increased carry weight/space, faster modes of transportation, and automation of some of the game's more tedious elements so you can focus on other things.  In fact, often times I ended up with more simple tedious BS to do from the game's progression system.Medieval Dynasty only offers minor ailments to the grindyness (around 10%-20%) in the most late stages of the game.  At no point does the work required of you become much less tedious.  You only have the option to assign it to high maintenance NPCs who work slower, and even then, things like the egregious map travel times ever become alleviated.  Production offers pocket change for 2 straight minutes of crafting, not including the gathering of materials.Satisfactory and Factorio use crafting times as an incentive to automate processes, but MD has very little automation in comparison, so you'll always be sitting through long crafting times anyways.Terraria has travel times that reach several minutes, but you naturally become faster and unlock access to more modes of transport just playing the game.Rust has absurdly demanding and slow progression, but is made interesting by the PvP elements.On top of this, the game becomes annoyingly unclear what you're expected to do if you miss a pop-up.  NPCs range from decently interesting, to Oblivion level copy-pastes.  There is so little cosmetic customization I know it sounds shallow but I was so sick of my character and all my villagers aesthetically before my first Winter.The game is decently rewarding though, and its mechanics are unique enough to keep me somewhat curious, but often times you're left, for minutes, holding one button.  Sometimes you can go make food IRL while your character works automatically for five minutes so you can buy something to eat other than garbage.This game doesn't just feel unfinished, it shoots itself in the foot in regards to game design to serve some vaguely defined standard of realism, that's constantly broken by quest-markers and compasses and NPCs repeating the same lines in each town.

_childDocuments_.review: At this point - I really can't recommend the game. It has some interesting potential, but many of the things that are currently broken don't seem to have an easy fix (or speak to a larger decision to take an easier path during development):However, even with all of that - what really kills it is the AI. The AI is in theory the backbone of this game - without it, you're just randomly around collecting berries and wood. You'll often find your villagers just standing around stuck in some sort of loop. I recently spent a good 3 minutes watching a villager draw her bow, relax her draw, and repeat. When villagers are bringing you any benefit, it looks almost like they are magically generating and teleporting resources rather than actually taking an action (eg, assign them to a certain job, out pops X amount of Y each day). And if they are supposed to actually complete actions, the whole thing needs to be rebalanced - it takes my villager a whole season to walk to and from the mine she's supposed to work at.I could forgive the rest of that list if the AI worked... but I'd stay away until it's fixed and I'm not sure that's something they can easily address.

_childDocuments_.review: It could have been great....Got this on sale because it seemed like it had potential.The concept seemed really interesting. Survival game with a marriage / inheritance system attached? Great, sign me up!Then I started playing. Graphics are decent, especially for an indie studio, gameplay seems solid enough, no gamebreaking bugs right of the start. Responsive controls. Off to a good start.Basic gameplay, collect stones, gather sticks.. craft tools... ok, not very original, but it works...Got into the first village, dialogue with NPC's is very basic/generic. No real character in anyone, but then again, dynasty system, so that can be expected, they tried to implement other people at least. No voice acting but meh, who cares.Building my house, nice! They actually have a system of building homes that is used friendly and easy to get into.Then got into combat with a fox, whoops, didn't pay attention to spear durability so it breaks.All good, it's a fox and I got a knife and an axe and a pickaxe, I should be fine right?Nope, none of those tools do a single point of damage and the fox, shy as they are, kept chasing me to the end of the world to kill me.This seemed.... shabbySo then I went and took a look at the game studio that produced this early access game. will they fix the kinks? Will they improve the game? The updates say yes, but I worry when I see that they are busy working on some clones of this game with different themes to milk the crappy engine for cash instead of putting full focus in improving it. Wild west dynasty, farmers dynasty, lumberjack's dynasty.... really guys? 2.2 hours playtime :( that's 0.2 hours too much for a steam refund.... damn...

_childDocuments_.review: It's times like these I wish there was a neutral option for reviews. But then I remember the full price is $35 and that puts it solidly in "not recommended" territory.Survival mechanics are standard and the UI is legible. The main thing that puts me off is how abysmal the customization is across the board. The character creator makes the bg3 one look deep. Here, you can create a handful of variations of the same white guy, some of which are girls. There's really not much you can do in terms of customizing your settlement either. You can pick which wall the window goes on, and if you work really hard and accumulate enough technology points, you can build a scarecrow. There's something about the technology point system that really encapsulates how sparse the game feels; a lot of the higher-point unlocks are really basic stuff. It seems like they were just trying to stretch playtime.You can't be gay. Maybe I wanted to be gay. Anyone trying to make the historical accuracy argument about that one should note that this game makes no attempt to be accurate to any historical period or culture, it's just going for a general vibe, which ultimately is not very immersive.The most fun I've had in this game has been with multiplayer, which can be more attributed to my friends than this game. Almost anything can be fun in multiplayer. In my solo game, I was trapped in my house by 3 buffalo clipping through the walls and repeatedly killing me until I gave up.If this game was like $10 I'd say, give it a shot. Otherwise, things that would be more fun and immersive than this: try out survival mode on your old copy of Skyrim, or just go into the woods with the homies & hit each other with sticks.

_childDocuments_.review: What I like most about Medieval Dynasty is that you can play it as a survival game as well as just focusing on building and decorating your own village. You can choose if your character needs food and water, if he loses stamina or HP or if he's practically immortal. You can choose if you want to have bandits that can attack you, you can choose if your villagers need food, water and firewood and you can change those options any time you want. Some changes happen immediatly, for some you have to move on to the next season. But it's all in your hands. And I think that is great. Of course there are still a few things that could be added to the game like I would personally love a tool that allows you to flatten terrain that otherwise is to steep to build. Or the possibility to build or buy your own fast travel point for your village. But even without those features, Medieval Dynasty is a unique game. It is a survival game but then again it's not just that. It is a city builder but you are not some invicible god that lookes down from above. You are a character living in this world, building your own home. You raise your own little family and you have to care for them, otherwise they will leave you and I think it is amazing. Can't wait for the Coop to finally start.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing 34 hours in this game, all I can say is that it has potential. It looks great and the idea is great, but...It's a walking simulator with quests. The timecycle is very rushed. A season in the game last 3 ingame days and an ingame day last like 20 minutes. So within an hour and a half, a year has gone. Walking to one of the far away towns takes almost an entire day. I know it's all about living a life and continuing as your heir, but this is just rushed and stressful. The town management aspect is not working optimal at the moment, as you spend more time reassigning your villagers from job to job to get them unstuck from standing still or tear down buildings because they get stuck behind the fireplaces inside them. The Woodcutter does little good as you still need to cut several trees each day to meet the wood demand and farmers are stuck at fertilizing without a bag on the same spot for days. In short you can do chop down 10 trees, sow 2 9x9 fields and hunt 10 deer in the same amount of time it takes 3-4 villagers to do the same.I really like the idea of the game and I know it's early access, but right now I can't recommend it.EDIT. A year later and 29 hours of playing I can say that a lot of the issues has been fixed and options for longer seasons and days has made a huge change. It's still a lot of walking and grinding, but the game is certainly worth the money now, if you like colony sim games.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: I now have a sprawling village, a wife, an heir and most importantly a pig. Most of my day is spent helping with chores to keep the village happy. I cut trees, kill wolves, make some meat and gravy dishes, fertilize, and lay down with my pig since my pig currently does more for the village than my wife back at home. Still would highly recommend with ONE BIG GRIPE: They must fix the automated chores. Most of my workers I employ just stand and do nothing. Hunters, farmers, miners and lumberjacks are worth it early but do not expect great things from anyone else. Fantastic grind with a wealth of game play. I'm always on my toes trying to accomplish tasks with the time I am given and it is obvious after 10 hours that i will be well into the 100s before having any resemblance of a dynasty.
