_childDocuments_.review: Here's a good way to quickly figure out if this game is for you. Go to YouTube, look up the Tales from Off-Peak City soundtrack and listen to it. If you vibe with the music, you'll vibe with the game.This is because at its heart, Tales from Off-Peak City is a music game. It feels like an interactive music video, its jazzy upright bass-led tracks arguably more central to the game's immersive quality than its surrealist visuals. So when you move past a wall mural of a jellyfish riding a cow, which is unremarkable only because it's situated next to a giant animated paper mache dog head that pants and breathes with synth stabs, you're getting a video game world that is more interested in reacting alchemically with the creative parts of your brain than actually making any coherent sense. When you look through the shop windows of a building for rent and it's flooded top to bottom, sharks swimming with floating mannequin torsos, and if you stop and appreciate it for the off-kilter dreamlike imagery that it is, then you are hopefully, where consciously or not, letting the music affect you. It's exactly how a music video functions.The gameplay is very much a secondary consideration here, consisting mainly of talking to characters, solving some very light puzzles, and delivering pizzas. The pizza oven is a casual mini-game for creatives - you assemble the pizza toppings however you wish, and then walk to a specific address to deliver it. No matter what pizza you make, the recipients all react delightedly to your creation, going on long praise-filled monologues about which toppings you chose or how much sauce you used, and it keeps the pizzamaking light-hearted and fun. (Delivering plain cooked pizza dough with nothing on it is funny every time.)Characters speak in musical tones synchronized to on-screen text, so you get the flavor of what they're saying without any actual recorded dialogue. There's a story there and it's surprisingly lore-dense, and while the game will only take a couple of hours to finish, a second playthrough reveals lots of hidden details and clues that you will likely have missed on your first run. This is where attentive players will realize that a lot of the strange visuals of the game actually serve a function in its world-building, hidden in plain sight amongst the fever-dream nonsense.Despite this, the story is unfortunately incomplete, acting both as the first volume of a planned series of shortform games and also a sequel to two previous games from the same developer in the same universe. It doesn't stand very well on its own.And it might be because of this middle-ground status that Tales from Off-Peak City Vol. 1 doesn't reach the heights of its predecessor, The Norwood Suite, which has you exploring a single hotel. That game's focused environment, interconnected secret passages, and eclectic mix of artists to intermingle with, feel like playing Clue while tripping on mushrooms. Comparatively, Tales from Off-Peak City takes place on two small city streets and a handful of building interiors, and they're not quite as synergistic in their layout, and thus less interesting to explore.Beyond the pizza mechanic, there isn't anything new here to distinguish this entry from the previous game, which is a shame. The visuals, despite their creative ambition, still lack detail and refinement, and the mechanics are still only minimally interactive. I believe this series could benefit from having a bit more to do.But all of those minor gripes don't take anything away from the sound. This is a Sound game. The tiny play area is incredibly dense - not graphically, but audibly. There are unique sound cues just about everywhere that most players who aren't already sensitive to audio won't notice. In one store playing an amazing proggy groove, after I had spent a few minutes with my real-life hands in the air dancing at my real-life desk, I moved my character to an area behind the counter, at which point a low-pass filter swept over the music to give it a more muffled, distant sound. Why? Because exploring your environment ALWAYS changes the audio. Another small room later in the game features a buzzing synth track meant to disturb you, but if you approach a specific locked door, and we're talking maybe one square-foot of play space, those buzzing synths transform into intense subbass rumbling that will annihilate your subwoofer. This audio cue was created for a one-square-foot play area that most people will miss.This is what I mean by audio density. Walking down the street, passing many buildings you won't even get to enter, you can still appreciate audibly what is happening on the inside, because every building features its own unique piece of music and sound. Think about that - how many developers would create a building by its sound first and foremost, without even crafting its interior visually? The audio conveys so much character!So if you love music or sound design, I cannot recommend this game (or this series) enough. Fans of adventure games like Grim Fandango might also appreciate its low-key psychedelic atmosphere, but won't find much to chew on in the puzzle or gameplay departments. This is more of an "experience", bordering on the "walking simulator" faux pas, but one that creatives and hedonists shouldn't miss.So kick off your shoes, pour yourself a glass of wine (or other vice), and let yourself vibe to this game. It's great.

_childDocuments_.review: CosmoD creates a very specific kind of game. They're hard to classify, at once as much a musical experiment as a game. Yet it all comes together perfectly. Exploring these surreal locations, and uncovering the mysteries linking all of them together is something to behold, and it's why CosmoD is one of my favourite indie developers.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: Cosmo D has really outdone himself with this one. I've been a fan of his work since seeing PewDiePie play Off Peak and his work has always captured my imagination with the experimental music and the eclectic motifs that decorate his games. Off Peak was a great experience but ultimately lacked a lot of gameplay, but it was a free game. Norwood Suite, his next release developed on it and was much more ambitious. This time he sought to make an overarching story, not losing sight of the vignettes which made Off Peak so special. Norwood Suite added some puzzle mechanics but didn't really hit its stride. Off Peak City is certainly the most matured and developed game so far. The pizza making mechanic was cool but I wish it really mattered to the story how you made the pizza. I wish pizza making was a fully fleshed mechanic to build around. Tie that in with some more sophisticated puzzles and I'd be sold. Especially with the ability to purchase items, I think this game could've gone really far with what it had but it ultimately fell a bit short. Cosmo D has certainly refined the atmosphere of the game which is what shines the most. Archie Pelago amazing as always and the interactive details really make Cosmo D games special. The story shined as well. The connection to Off Peak was less clear to me, which was disappointing considering that it was the namesake. I actually found that it connected most to the Norwood Suite which was really fun and interesting. The most fleshed out story so far, yet it still feels too overly cryptic at times. Though I would say take that statement lightly as I believe there will be more to come based off the "Vol. 1" part of the title. I am excited to see where the story continues and I would love to see my favorite and always charismatic indie dev, Cosmo D, hit his stride and make a fully fleshed masterpiece. Please do not pass up any of these games! They are so fun and following the development of them has been a treat.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: This game sets a fantastic mood and energy and had me thoroughly enthralled from start to finish. Cosmo D's skills as a game designer show clear improvements over his last titles, but bring the same weird, funky vibe that brought me in in the first place. The pizza creation aspect is a fun little addition and clearly builds on the sandwich making of The Norwood Suite in a good way. While I do wish the game were longer, it's understandable when both DLC and further volumes are planned. I really got the urge to explore more of the vast, sprawling city beyond and I can only hope we get to explore it more in-depth in future installments. Nods to the previous games were varied and interesting, but the game never requires the player to have experience with the other games.If you enjoy awesome music, weird, surreal visuals, and/or a strange atmosphere to get lost in and explore, you will enjoy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1 is a thoroughly weird walking sim that is completely unafraid of being a thoroughly weird walking sim. You get exactly what it says on the tin. You walk around and talk to people. There are no dialog choices. They all spout meaningless nonsense at you. The city is full of bizarre little secrets. Kind of gross. Kind of hip. There is jazz music. It's capital-A Art and that's just fine. If you played the previous Off-Peak game you know exactly what to expect. Surreal. Ridiculous. Don't take it too seriously and you will have fun. Or take it too seriously and be a pretentious ♥♥♥♥. It's all good. I'm so glad people can make odd games like this and we get to play them. Walking sims forever.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: Another great surrealistic installment from Cosmo D! Alongside the entire style and atmosphere in the game I have to say I really liked the story in this one, it feels more involved than the previous 2 games in the series from Cosmo D.The entire atmosphere brought forward by the characters, story, music, sound effects, and environment is awesome and exactly what I was expecting.I can't wait for more games in this series to be released. The story in this one makes it seem like the developer is finally figuring out exactly how they truly want these games and future games in this series to be like, and I have to say I'm a fan of it. I believe it goes without saying that if you enjoyed  or  this is a must-play for you.Like Off-Peak or The Norwood Suite, this game is yet another that is kinda difficult to explain or properly convey with any words, like a bizarre dream you had that is impossible to explain properly because just can't fully convey the feel and atmosphere of the entire experience.I understand that some people just might not  and dislike this game, but keep in mind that it's also kinda the point that you're not supposed to fully understand it or . It's supposed to be off-kilter and 'out there'.However I do feel that most people just know whether or not they're into these types of games before making a purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome music, interesting plot, and an immersive world that is so strange and beautiful. The characters are decent and dialogue is as well. If you are curious about what to expect and want a taste, check out Off Peak on steam which is free and is made by the same developer "Cosmo D", also check out The Norwood Suite because I'm pretty sure that both have direct lore links to this game. _childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best entry from the Off-Peak series so far. Compared to the last two games, this one has the most refined storytelling and characterisation. The music is, as always, superb and oddly hypnotic at times, which complements the uncustomary but well-crafted environment that I got familiar with and attached to. This game might have slightly less freedom in the exploration aspect compared to Off-Peak and a smaller map than Norwood Suite's, but in here there's a level of polish that I can respect the craft of.Frankly, there's this fascination with the game and I really didn't want the said game to end, it was like the game was chill and it had it's own character that grew on me. The story this time around is a bit melancholic but more dynamic as you progress on with the story. The 3-D models, decals and assets are highly detailed and they fit in with the game's art style very well. There were a very few, small and subjective issues I've had with this experience; one was the camera, there wasn't really much purpose on having to use this camera, other than being able to customise and replace paintings. It would've been very cool if it could've been used to reveal a hidden clue to a puzzle, using one of the filters, but I guess being able to document your journey through this game is nice. Second is ... well, this pizza thing, I don't know, but I think the reason for the pizza making thing, was to kind of pander towards Vinesauce, considering that Vinny likes pizza, I guess and he is very close to Cosmo D's work and always streams them, on or before release, but I don't know if that was intentional or not. Lastly, is that the game is a little short, but there is skill to making a game such as this and it must've been very difficult and time consuming, and the more compact the game is, the more memorable it is and higher the quality, I guess.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a very enjoyable experience. No other games or developer that I have encountered are capable of making games as surrealistic and creative. Theres always something strange and surprising around every corner, always something special to see. I would advice anyone to play The Norwood suite first, as there are some crossover lore.

_childDocuments_.review: Forget "the earth is flat", that's for babies. The adults in the room ponder if the cosmos is pizza-shaped, because if we're all just "moving food", then there will always be something missing: the mouth. Thus, ambition, greed, and violence run rampart in this little corner of the world called Off-Peak City, where wind instruments you never see played are the key to society. Relax, press play, and figure out the will of pepperoni.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: Cosmo D makes some of the most original experiences on Steam. In essence these are traditional adventure games, with an inventory and a cast of characters to interact with and simple puzzles to solve, but the writing and execution are unlike anything else. Despite the expressive visual style, dialogue is largely naturalistic, with music fully integrated into each scene as a principle component (see the bandcamp page for albums, which are great). All three of Cosmo D’s games are rewarding, but the second, The Norwood Suite, is especially essential to understand the narrative of Tales From Off-Peak City, and highly recommended for those that haven’t played it. “Study the form, embrace the formation.”

_childDocuments_.review: Cosmo D's second follow up to his freeware cult classic 'Off Peak' is another "off peak" and off kilter jaunt through an art exhibition come to life. Every corner of this game drips with symbolism and the game doles out mysteries like it's dealing out playing cards. I've found myself missing additional "objectives" in my excitement to move along to the next insane mystery Off-Peak City holds. It is, after all, a LOT to take in. It doesn't seem like Cosmo D's games are designed with the enjoyment of gamers specifically in mind. They are each a playground, but with few gameplay aspects; it's a walking sim with rudimentary puzzles and fetch-quests. Off-Peak felt like it was incidentally a game, but what higher purpose it served was anyone's guess. Other walking sims had sacrificed gameplay to tell stories or address themes of humanity and existence. However, Off-Peak didn't want you to do that or to think too hard on any one thing, meanwhile it hit you, in a good way, with everything.Tales From Off-Peak and its predecessor The Norwood Suite are vastly superior, each entry has really pushed what its predecessor has done, and each has been masterful in its own way. The series aesthetic since the first game has been funky but high concept sound and music design with funkier and even higher concept visuals, and this game's further inclusion of music as a concept and a mechanic creates an utterly joyful experience. Cosmo D is beginning to create something very promising here and I for one will await their next offering, whatever it is, very keenly.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. There's nothing else like it (Except, I suppose, Off-Peak and The Norwood Suite). It's set in a strange world with a lot of magic ingredients but it feels consistent and the stories remain surprisingly grounded. There's a really consistent off-kilter feeling you can probably tell if you'll vibe with right away.Also: having every person you deliver a pizza to respond to the exact combination of ingredients you put on it is a killer feature!
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: What a wonderful game!Utterly hooked by the story, it's surreal and odd but very human about a life long passion to one's passion and family.The world and artistic direction in my opinion is awesome, many will be put off by the clear contradictions of style, unlike other games (*cough* Yandere Simulator *cough*) it seemingly comes together very well, I personally think this is because of the uniqueness of the architecture, the twisting warped nature of the city, the different historical layers you can see of the buildings themselves and how normalised the weirdness seems.And this game doesn't rely on "I'm so random" as its selling point. Truly play this game for the story, I was hooked from start to finish. Talk to as many characters as you can and buy / find as many ingredients as you can (seriously the pizza making component of this game is strangely very satisfying)Finally, you can't not talk about the music and sound design. Every building has its own soundscape, every character talks in a distinct musical note, the city is overflowing with noise and it's just wonderful to wonder about. Truly one of the best designed video game cities ever, certainly up there in atmosphere with Rapture, Anor Londo and (my own personally weird favourite) the Seirra Madre Casino.I implore you to buy this game and to check out Cosmo D's other work!
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: Intriguing, somewhere between a Bioshock/We Happy Few style atmospheric puzzler with a good helping of Cronenberg's Naked Lunch in an ambitious tech-demoette crossover of a psychedelic vibrant noir fever dream that kept me pretty enthralled for the 3 1/2 hours it took to go through. With the heavy use of beautiful musical effects its important you play this loud, or with headphones, or in a field maybe. (Musical pizzas lol). Definitely looking forward to future off-peaks. *edit, there's another one already!? Go get that too.

_childDocuments_.review: The Off Peak series just keeps getting better with each entry. Tales doesn't deviate from the previous games too much mechanics-wise but it hones it better than the previous two. The atmosphere is still bizarre and off-kilter in all the right ways and the writing is actually starting to come together, tying in events from the two previous games which starts making a clearer picture in its own absurd way. Definitely recommend it for narrative exploration game fans and I'm looking forward to the next volumes.

_childDocuments_.review: I followed this game since I saw it on itch.io a while ago. I knew it had something special. _childDocuments_.review: Cosmo D is the MAN! He makes some trippy, fun things that really take you out of the Triple A spoilmanship (if that can be a word). Many of you deserve a great game, and Cosmo D even makes me want to get back into game reviews/streaming/videos. I hope to get more from them in times to come.Enjoy the surreal and strange. The insidious, ominous and comical. The aloof characters and callbacks, cross references of old fans and even new jokes and clever writing. If this game looks intriguing, then by all means GET IT. Don't waste your time spoiling it or seeing if it tickles your fancy. Steam always gives the 2 hour refund policy and it's more than enough time to see if it's your style (unlike other games that try to eat that up with tutorials and cutscenes).

_childDocuments_.review: TFOPCV1 is immediately engaging. The music keeps grooving, the characters are entrancing, the creative photographic opportunities are infinite. Plus pizza. If you dig the trailer music you should pick up the OST as well. Amazing work across the board from a talented dev. This game can be digested and enjoyed without knowing about its predecessor The Norwood Suite. You'll appreciate it a little more if you do. The game has a leisurely pace and is well-designed to let you pick it up and revisit again when you're in the mood. I've played through the main story a couple times now and I still have a desire to play more and to take more snaps. A great rainy weekend experience. My only complaint is that navigating the in-game album of photos I've taken is a bit cumbersome.

_childDocuments_.review: I streamed Tales from Off-Peak City Vol. 1 on my Twitch channel, and I think it's a great game to stream if you like doing your own voice acting, but is probably best played on your own.A follow-up to both Off-Peak and The Norwood Suite, which I strongly recommend you play first. This game is very keen to reconnect to the levity of the first game while keeping with the principle depth of the second. I would like to think it more or less accomplishes this. As in prior entries, the question is really the nature of creative work, though we've expanded and pivoted focus once more. I would argue that my impression at this point (and I intend to replay it to investigate further) is that this game is really asking questions about the true costs of 'selling out', when you should do it, and what happens if you don't, with further questions about the nature and roots of our communities. I found the themes much more challenging, but in that challenge, there is reward.As others have noted, if you enjoy the work of David Lynch, you will find yourself at home here, and I urge you to play the other games of this series.. You don't need any assistance to beat it and would deprive yourself of the joy of exploring it to do so.Personally, I'll give this game a 98/100. As in prior entries, the game excels at creating characters to deliver its big-picture concepts, and has a beautiful visual and auditory experience to treat your senses - my biggest gripe is that I found the  mechanic fun, but underutilized. (Some would argue that's the point, but that doesn't mean I have to like it.)

_childDocuments_.review: Ok. So the original Off-Peak was a masterpiece. When I found out about the Tales, I was so hyped, cause the original game only left me wishing for more. But as it goes with a lot of sequels... they are just not that great. And in this case... especially if you are coming from a place of admiring the first game... well... it's pretty much just not it. There's 0 obscurity, no mystery, nothing to unravel and moreover nothing's left to your imagination. This is just your regular walking sim, where you are surrounded by a bunch of avangard piece of art and um... yeah thats pretty much it. If this game was the original game in the series, no one would have even noticed it. it does have the same ... I mean, it would be too much to say it has the same vibe as the original, but um... there's a little sniff of it somewhere in the air while you are playing it lol. So um... I dunno... The dev dfntly lost what they have found while creating the first game. Oh well...Little objective criticism: - The story line is boring af. Not engaging, not captivating, very blend and uninteresting. There's no thrill to it, and most dialogues feel like boring ass fillers. - Worldwise it's a .... It has something from the original game. Obviously. It has some pretty artworks hang around. It um... Is dfntly a unique setting, BUT. And this is an important one. It's trying to be something it is not. Trying to convey some story by simply laying it out for you, not leaving anything for interpretation, elimintating all the charm and um... the distant feel of the world that is presented in the game. - music wise its good, but having all the voicelines have a certain "noise" to them is a poor choice. Cause those sound queues do not sound like a voice, they clearly are just noises made with a musical instrument, which makes it overlap the actual score that is incessantly playing in the background. So yeah... I've trying to give this game as fair chance as possible but i don't think i'll be finishing it, cause every time i come back to it I'm unfortunately met with another filler of a character with a bunch of boring, unrelating, unmoving lines.

_childDocuments_.review: You've been at a party all night, dancing like no one’s watching (but they definitely were), when you realize someone’s slipped something… extra into your drink. Not wanting to stick around and find out what, you decide to make the responsible choice — stumble your way home. After a heroic 45-minute journey through the dark streets, full of wrong turns, questionable life choices, and muttering at stray cats, it hits you: not only are you drunk, but paranoia has decided to crash your party too. Oh, and you're starving.It's now 3:00 a.m., the witching hour, and you burst through your front door like a spy on the run. First order of business? Close every blind, curtain, and towel you can find, because who knows who could be watching. Second order of business? FOOD. Desperation hits hard, so naturally, you order the most chaotic pizza imaginable: garlic, whale meat, anchovies, pineapple, seafood, and artichokes with cheese on top— a masterpiece of tasteful confusion.Around 3:40 a.m., the delivery guy arrives, looking at you like he's just witnessed a crime scene. You hand over the money with shaky hands, possibly from hunger or sheer existential terror, and he makes a swift exit. As you guard your apartment like a hawk, convinced the shadows are moving, you decide the best way to relax is to blast some free jazz. You know, the kind that sounds like three musicians fell down a staircase while playing instruments? Perfect.By 3:50 a.m., after devouring your strange pizza concoction like it's the last meal on Earth, you decide there’s only one thing left to do: play chess... against yourself. Because really, who else could you trust at this point?

_childDocuments_.review: Although I wouldn't put this above Off-Peak gameplay wise, what Tales From Off-Peak City lacks in gameplay it makes up for in story. For those who enjoyed Off-Peak, love weirdcore, or are just really interested in exploring surreal but fun worlds without having too much pressure put on them while doing so, the world of Off-Peak City is an absolute paradise. Although some dislike the idea of being a "tourist" when playing games, I personally enjoyed the more dialogue and aesthetic focus of this one. From the get go, the game starts with plenty of intrigue and sets the player off in the right direction, but doesn't force their hand in this. Instead, from the moment the player is put into the game, they have free reign to explore the city without restrictions. I felt the game had no qualms with me taking my time and checking everything out before starting the main story line. But even when I did do this and no matter what part of the story I was in, the game never restricted this freedom, letting the player become fully immersed in the setting and allowing for a strange sort of freedom in a considerably linear story. I was allowed to create my own stakes and dedication in this world. In this sense, I found the game and its unique environment oddly relaxing, the same way Off-Peak felt like some bizarre home away from home. You really are a tourist, allowed to take in all the twists of the narrative without the sense of danger, yet this helped me feel safe enough to thoroughly explore and the characters were all so charming I quickly became invested.Unlike Off-Peak, there's been great improvement on the writing, and players are actively rewarded for sticking around and hearing all characters have to say, whether through direct conversations or eavesdropping. Dialogue feels much more relevant, with little tidbits about other characters you'll meet along the way, ones you might have met in past games, and the world put out there in a very natural way. I also loved that every important character could be both eavesdropped on and talked to directly, the most requiring characters having different dialogue each time, really helping to flesh them out. The edition of certain hints helped as well, with players being given the option to replay dialogue once it had run out, and "..." indicating the character has more to say if the player waits or continues doing a certain action. So it didn't feel like the game was trying to hide its lore, but instead rewarded them for patience and intrigue. I found it really endearing that characters would become comfortable enough to open up to you the more time you spent with them and, therefore, the more interest you showed. Even without dialogue options, I as a player was still given choice and could characterize my player character in certain ways with the actions I chose throughout. It really encourages you to play around with the items you can get to trigger all sorts of dialogue. As for the story, I don't want to spoil anything nor will I pretend to completely understand it myself. However, the mystery at the forefront had me hooked the entire time, and the game has very good pacing when it comes to it. Details and answers are added on slowly through the course of the game as players make their pizza deliveries, and the interconnected nature of the city becomes more clear the more NPCs you talk to. This world felt so alive to me that finding the missing pieces to the puzzle wasn't tedious at all. Every character feels genuine in their motivations for living their and how the main point inevitably ends up affecting them, so even for players that may not understand its more "symbolic" and "out there" story telling methods, there's still enough presented at the surface level to keep one interested and invested. I think this game's biggest weakness is the gameplay. Making pizzas and delivering them became tiring after a while because the streets and buildings weren't as clearly marked as they should be, in my opinion. Most of my playtime was spent just trying to find some of them. Its a small map, and yet, it can be surprisingly confusing with the nature of it all. This might have been intentional, but I found it really annoying after a while. I also really loved the pizza making mini game with the comedic and musical nature of it. So I wish there was more to it than just putting the pizza in the oven and waiting for it to be packaged up in an animation that can not be skipped. With the unique nature of it, I wish there was more player interaction put into this, as it would have been fun to cook and further prepare the pizzas in similarly strange ways. It was fun seeing the NPCs reactions to each of the ingredients along with collecting them, but this was probably the most dull part of the game if I'm being honest.Still, if players can get past that one little road bump, I think they'd enjoy the zany characters, the mind blowing and surreal setting, and the surprising amount of lore that goes with it and has made me fall in love with this world. I'd highly recommend it to those who don't mind more dialogue focused games and value exploration over gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Like Cosmo D's previous game, The Norwood Suite, Tales From Off-Peak City is a brief and bizarrely surreal walking sim. _childDocuments_.review: After playing The Norwood Suite last year and loving it, I wanted to immediately play this but decided to hold off, just so I knew I could experience something later on when the mood struck. Well, that happened last night at 2 AM, and I played this all the way through.Cosmo D did it again. You wander around a block of Off-Peak City, talking to its inhabitants about the nearby Factory and the crumbling infrastructure, all the while taking in the surreal sights and wonderful music. Wonderful, upbeat while somehow being unsettling at the same time, though maybe this has something to do with the subject matter. It's something special either way.Mostly all you do is walk up to people and read what they have to say to you, or not walk up to them and "overhear" what they do, as well as finding items and using them in the right place. This isn't to say you have adventure game puzzles to solve; Steam tells me I spent 3.4 hours playing (I think I walked away for at least 30 minutes of that), and I think the whole time there was one part where I wasn't sure what to do, which turned out to be my fault. (Hint: There is a 26 Yam Street AND a 26 July Street.) But this game, as is the case with Cosmo D's previous games, is much more than the sum of its parts. There's something about it that moves my brain, opening up joyous nerve pathways that I had forgotten about after years and years of disuse.I do think I'd give The Norwood Suite the edge here, but only slightly. Maybe I just like to explore a good mansion, or that this is, despite being a complete story, also the first in a series of other stories and not quite as standalone.Anyway, this is a precious gem, and I'm excited to play Betrayal at Club Low!

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Off-Peak, and I loved The Norwood Suite. Guess what? I loved this one too. I bought it when it was released, but for some unknown reasons I've never gotten around to playing it until now.Like in the two previous games, Cosmo D's style just draws me in and keeps me there until the end. There's so much about this world in all it's beautiful quirkyness and surrealism that just appeals to me on so many levels. While it's not necessary to have played the two previous games to enjoy this one, I highly recommend it because of all the small references and "throwbacks" if you will, that you'll miss if this is your first time stepping into Cosmo D's wonderful reality.So this time around, you find yourself in a boat with a woman and a man who have got their eyes on a priceless saxophone which belongs to Caetano Grosso, the owner of the local pizza place on the corner of July and Yam. He used to be a master musician who played with none other than the great Peter Norwood himself in his glory days. They need you to steal this invaluable piece of music history, and have planned out an elaborate heist. A Grand Theft Sax. This involves document forgery, infiltration, cunning, persuasion, a knack for pizza baking, and a sprinkle of fearlessness, due to the ever watching eyes of the people who are in charge of this city.The pizza making process is oddly satisfying, and the puzzles you'll encounter are clever, but pretty easy to figure out. In addition, the music matches the game's vibe and atmosphere perfectly, just like in Off-Peak and The Norwood Suite. You'll meet lots of interesting people, there are a few items you can find, and of course you'll discover something new and surprising all the time while you're out delivering pizzas and snooping through drawers and cupboards. Oh, and don't mind the dog.I finished the game in a couple of hours, but could probably have spent even more time finding every item and eavesdropping to uncover all the secrets. Crossing my fingers for Vol. 2 to be made soon, but for now I'll be looking forward to Betrayal at Club Low, as I'm sure it will help satiate my hunger for some more Off-Peak City and pizza.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: Another surreal, intricate hit from developer Cosmo D! Tales from Off-Peak City - Vol. 1 picks up after the events in the previous two games, Off-Peak and The Norwood Suite, and feels just the same. The strange, dream-like imagery works together with the intricate, over-arching and musical storyline and it feels like home. I love how the storyline in this game connects seamlessly to the previous games yet it's something almost completely different. We learn of the pizzamaker and former-musician Caetano Grozzo, his tragic past, his connections to the notorious Peter Norwood, and their role in the plans set in motion by the city's cutthroat government, Human Resource Horizons. I really enjoyed my trippy time between Yam St. and July Ave. and am very excited for the next game! Keep the weirdness coming, Cosmo D, it makes my brain happy.Also, the camera and different filters (film rolls) were a nice touch. Got some really good shots I'm now using in my desktop rotation.

_childDocuments_.review: Years ago I played a little free game called "Off-Peak", I enjoyed it so much, I remember thinking "I hope the developer makes a full game like this". Then I got this game in a bundle and it was like a dream come true! More of the surreal graphics, art and dialogue. There's no voice acting, but I can hear the character's voices in my head. The very nature of the text displayed during dialogue conveys rich emotion. Although it's a very short game, the amount of visual and auditory art will keep you occupied and amazed for a good long time. The soundtrack is very clever and conveys different feelings in various situations. Anyone who's into Rene Magritte or Salvador Dali's artwork will feel fully at home here. This game is a real gem and I can not recommend it highly enough!
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the strangest POV adventure I've ever been on. It mixes creepy and frightening and artistic and beautiful and wild and it's exactly like a video game that I'd try to make. It's just an experience. So incredible. The story is hard to follow, and that's the best part. The weird gameplay elements feel very unique, and the music is unmatched.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: Very glad I didn't sleep on this. The music is fantastic as expected and the game engine isn't nearly as janky as in Off-Peak. Should play Norwood next.These games just radiate character and it's easy to tell how much care and passion was put into making them. Easy recommendation for people who like these games.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: Off-Peak City is a fascinating experience, everything about it oozes personality, and Cosmo D's background in music is undoubtedly the linchpin of the entire thing. I think this is something you really have to experience for yourself, few games or interactive pieces of art have ever really managed to capture what Cosmo creates.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy weird adventure games like this. I realized I had missed some story so I replayed it to see it all - if you're a little more patient you should be able to see it all in around 2-2.5 hrs and not need a replay.I am excited to see what the next adventure is like, assuming one is still coming. There is still a bunch of intrigue that hasn't been revealed.+ It's weird+ It's odd+ It's strange- It's short - 2 hrsI highly recommend Paradise Killer if you enjoyed this game - mechanically it's similar. Lots of weird but a better story and larger, more interesting world to explore.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: Another bizarre entry by Cosmo D.  Prepare for a world where nothing makes sense, set to some jazzy funk beats.  Cosmo D games are a mixture of art and game, suffused with an acid trip.  But, even more than the Norwood Suite, there is a bit of a mysterious story here.  Who exactly ARE the inhabitants of the neighorhood?  Why do so many seem to have something to hide?And what toppings make for the perfect pizza, anyways?
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece. You start in a weird boat with some beat playing and they tell you what you are going for right in the beginning. The story is pretty good and clever and the camera makes exploring even more worth it to get that nice picture. If you like weird interesting story games then this is a game you really need to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: Easily one of the most unique games i've played, from a visual presentation standpoint, gameplay, soundtrack, UI, story, etc. The game's mechanics have been built further from The Norwood Suite, where you earn money by making pizza's and delivering them to the various residents while moving the story forward in the two city streets the game takes place in.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: Holy cow, how far Cosmo D has come. I love the elements in this game that sets it apart from the others. The use of money, the camera, the expanded map, and all the new surreal art. The plot was great and can't wait for more games in the future. I will say that the use of different instruments that play whenever characters talk was a bit annoying at first, but it grew on me and I do think it's very creative.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely game. The atmosphere is in the goldylocks zone to where its surreal, but not the "random is funny" surreal. The music is wonderful, especially coming from the point of view of someone who loves and plays jazz. It's a bit pricey for an about 2 hour long game, and that's with getting most of the dialogue, but definitely worth getting on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: werid but also great. It has a quality and atomsphere to it that I can't describe other than unsettling in the most interesting way possible. It was able to make me feel like I was in a real city from all the personality the enviorment and graphics have and has a suprisingly good story. Only thing is it doesnt have much replay value and the movement doesnt feel the best 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 would be a pizza delivery person again.If you liked Paratopic you will like this. A bit more streamlined than Paratopic and way less creepy, it still nails the surrealist vibe. You can play it one sitting of ~2 hours. Probably worth a replay a while after to get the bits of story you don't get on the first run.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of "surreal" games typically feel like they're desperately trying to be random for the sake of randomness, but this isn't one of them. This feels like a living, breathing, completely absurd universe that the player gets the opportunity to visit for a short while. The story is pleasantly detailed for a game of this size, and never feels like things are just being shoehorned in to maximize weirdness. If you find the trailer/screenshots even a little bit intriguing, you won't be disappointed by the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: Tales from Off Peak City Vol. 1 is a shorty but extremely enjoyable surreal narrative adventure game. It takes place on a single street corner over the course of one day, and it manages to pack a lot of intrigue, character development, humor, and pizza making in that short period of time. It has almost a noir detective feel to it with a very strange mystery to unravel over the course of it. I can't wait for volume 2!
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: Like the rest in the 'Norwood' series of games, this is as surreal as a beatniks mushrtoom trip. It's not long, nor complicated, but it is fun. The graphics look like something from 20 years ago, which adds to the overall weirdness of this game. While it won't be to everyones liking, There's a demo you can try. Personally, I loved it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: Not very long, but very cool. I'll definitely want to return and experience it all over again at some point!My only regret is that after having played through it, I realized that this game would have been even better if I'd played it in the dark with headphones on. It relies a lot on music and the atmosphere created by the trippy visuals and mildly unsettling, offbeat cityscape and it's inhabitants. I'll have to remember that next time: Go for full immersion!I kind of don't want to explain what the game is even about. It's what you'd call a walking simulator, but with very interesting music, arty visuals and a couple unusual game mechanics. I loved getting NPC reactions to my pizza recipes... umm... yeah.Buy it. Now.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: This game makes me angry. Cosmo D has the gall. The chutzpah. The cojones, to create a game with a surreal-yet-easy-on-the-eyes aesthetic, a bizarre-yet-charming soundtrack, and a mundane-yet-deep storyline. The characters, while not fully-fleshed-out, are interesting, the music is lovely, and the gameplay, while minimal, is enough to make one chuckle a bit. And yet the game has to _end_. And it has to end so _soon_. I'm getting the shakes, Cosmo D. Give me more. MORE.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: There aren't a ton of games that I would classify like Tales from Off-Peak City, but I wish there were more of them. It's not really an art game or a walking simulator, because there's some actual choices, mechanics, and tasks to do. There's more friction than those sort of games. The closest thing in tone that I can think of is Jazz Punk, though Off-Peak has a less abrasive and more likable style to it. Beyond anything else, I enjoyed just working my way through this bizarre environment interacting with strange devices and uncovering weird scenes. It's time well-spent, and I'm definitely going to check out the earlier games by this developer.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: If you've never played a Cosmo D game before, Tales from Off-Peak City Vol. 1 has you navigating a surreal world, interacting with strange characters, and hearing cool music like the two previous games from the developer.What sets this game apart is its scope. Whereas Off-Peak and The Norwood Suite are each set in one location, a train station and a hotel respectively, Tales from Off-Peak City Vol. 1 takes place in a whole neighborhood where you discover a rich culture of weirdness that's being slowly but surely hollowed out through corporate machinations enforced by wealthy property owners, both of the intellectual and real kinds. That narrative is a through-line across all three games, but it's explored more thoroughly here with its bigger cast and more varied environments.It echoes the deft transitions from unpredictable absurdity to warm humanity to low-key menace in its character writing and atmosphere setting that Cosmo D's older works achieve, only that it all rings a little louder this time. You can tell the yearning and the struggle of residents trying to get by amid the increasing gentrification of their home, whether it's through art, play, or good work and a bit of everything with the main pizza-making mechanic, and you'll be very much onboard with the plan to strike back at the powers-that-be.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: The first one was a digital art Installation.The second one was a playable abstract story.And this one, this is where it all comes together as story, game and art. This is SO good. But please, do play the first two "games" in this world first, or else you will miss out on so much of the "lore". And if those two are to your liking, you will definitely love this. Also, it needs no repeating but my GOD, the music in all these is amazing.  Good weird vibes all around.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: This game is visually spectacular. I'm a very "goals" oriented player so sometimes I need a little help with world exploring. Like I love poking around but usually it helps if I know what I'm after. This game has a great momentum to it but I feel like going back just so I can get a better look at all the incredible detail that went into the world building and musical shifts. Wish it was longer!
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: The good- Such a unique artistic approach. It looks like a messy, crappy collage. It initially looks like a mistake but after a while you will get immersed in its world.- The atmosphere is unique. It is so weird that you will always have a feeling of awkwardness while playing.- The characters are so cringe.- Really bizarre story with a lot of intrigues and mystery.- The non rhythmic music and the scattered strange sounds fit perfectly to the rest of the aesthetics.- The making of pizza is funny.- If you need help you can ask a music band for some hints.- You will find yourself inside some really surreal situations.The bad- I know it's mostly because of the aesthetics, but it feels too amateur especially on the gameplay mechanics and the animations.- I missed a run button especially in places that I have been before.- The automatic dialogues should be slower. Sometimes I struggled to catch up.- It is about two hours long and it is only the first of more episodes coming I assume. Maybe it should be a little bit cheaper.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this, I had a good time. I'd have liked it to be longer -it only took me 2.5 hours- but if I'd have done more of the task things, then I'd have doubtlessly seen more and I intend to go back. The game has a nice atmosphere to it and there's a lot of different music giving lots of different moods and such. Nicely made and put together, hoping for a Vol.2 somewhere down the line. Or just another game from Cosmo D. Either way, have a go on this if you fancy a friendly and intriguing gaming sorbet to refresh your palate.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: This game is... different... Pros:Really like the game design: i would find myself walking around contemplating this mysterious and gorgeous environment.The immersion: the story twists and the characters are very well thought and done  Note: If you enjoyed Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1 I recommend "The Norwood Suit" released by the same publisher.Cons:Min system requirement to play this game: a bag of weedCosmo D you got another loyal fan waiting for further releases.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: A joy from start to finish, Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1 is a short but sweet adventure game that lets you get lost in a small forgotten city street corner populated by interesting characters, weird architecture and intricate details wherever you explore. An intriguing plot is guided along by an excellently cool soundtrack and small windows into the characters' lives. My only regret is this game isn't longer. Make pizzas, take photos, get the saxophone.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: As usual, this is short but phenomenal. Play Cosmo's other games first, they just keep getting better and better, dripping with atmosphere and colour and clever direction, with this weirdo conspiratorial plotline pulling together threads from all three games. The music is amazing, and taking pictures in this world is so much fun. It's so surreal and unusual, it gives me a feeling I can't really describe. These games are quickly becoming some of my favourites, I cannot wait for Volume 2.Plus, you get to make pizza and jazz simultaneously.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: God I wish more people played Cosmo D's games. They're hella unique, this one's no different. The weird sounds and textures all work together somehow, the characters all talk about their own lives while making sense of the story, and you can make pizzas in here. Seriously, the pizza-making is great and the moment I discovered it I became upset that it was locked behind doing pizza deliveries for people (why wouldn't it be, of course?). I kind of wish there was a pizza-making music game now.Seriously, check the game out, it's got a demo and you'll get a good feel of the game from it alone.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: Cosmo D's most involved experience yet. More coherent in a narrative sense than the first two, with a much prettier locale, and the game itself runs better on top of that. I wish this part of Off-Peak City had the same interconnected feeling that the Norwood Hotel from his prior game had, but aside from that it is better on practically every front. If you like surreal games or walking sims, then you owe it to yourself to try out Cosmo D's games (especially because the first one is free!)
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: Cosmo D and Loiste Interactive should have lunch together sometime. I feel a bit of a common soul behind Open Sewer and Off-Peak City.WRT this game, awesome! It's like a surreal amusement park. With an amazing soundtrack that's uniquely integrated into the experience.I hope volume 2 grows the city, this can become the wackiest open-world-ish experience ever. I'd love to see more of the Norwood Suite "nook and cranny" micro-experiences in this game's future as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly interesting story, amazing soundtrack and a really creative artstyle that really grows on you. Looking forward to the next volume! I loved the premise and the fact that the town 'wasnt as simple as it seemed' was really entertaining and the ending was a really nice twist, can't wait for the next one!
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: I can confidently say that this game has some of the best sound design I've ever heard. From the moment I walked along the corner of Yam and July during the demo and got so extremely immersed that one of the oddest sights on the street didn't even surprise me, I knew this game would be something special. The way you build the soundtrack while you build pizzas is so mesmerizing as well. The game is quite short if you only go for one playthrough, but it's got me thinking about some of the things I've uncovered and wondering what more information I missed. I'll almost certainly be going back to check other avenues I missed and discover more about Off-Peak City.also this game's WEIRD and I dig it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: This game. Is amazing. I love it. Even though I might be a bit biased since I'm absolutely addicted to these games since Off-Peak, but this has been the best one out of all three games (Off-Peak, Norwood Suite & this one). I love how you can see the world and the story behind it develop more and more with each game. Needless to say, I'm absolutely hooked and can't wait for the next game! The surrealism gets even more intense and I loved every weird aspect of it. Tbh I kinda rushed through the game since I reeally wanted to find out the truth behind all the weird happenings, so I have to play it again to pay more attention to all the details. I feel like you have to play all of the Off-Peak games more than once for this reason. Something I think (not sure tho) I already wrote in my review for the Norwood Suite is how the characters' voices are all played by different music instruments. Really adds to the atmosphere.Games like this prove you don't need super-hyper realistic graphics or a big world or a huge team of developers to create a great game with a good story, interesting charcters and an amazing world to explore. In conclusion, this one goes straight to my favorites.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: Normally the world ‘eldritch’ is promptly followed by ‘horror’, ‘god’, or ‘nightmare’ and certainly all of those words to describe this game… But you can also say fun things too like ‘pizza’… ‘Eldritch Pizza’! What a world we live in!I like to picture this creator as the sentient pile of debris left from a traveling orchestra’s tragic plane crash. Their withering souls gleefully welded to the white-hot metal goo that was once the brass section. How it learned to code is beyond me, but sure as rain in Seattle, I am just thrilled that it did.Trying to describe this masterpiece is like my dad; doesn’t work! All I can say is that if you go in with expectations, any expectations, they both won’t and will be met. If that isn’t enough to sell you, then I recommend you check out some of the other works this fine creator has available and then come back when your third ear has been tuned.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: Tales From Off-Peak City is the perfect follow-up to Norwood Suite (If you haven't played that one yet, go do that first). The world of Off Peak is full of quirky characters, dark mysteries, and some very creative level designs. What I love about Cosmo D's Off Peak series is that it has simple, relaxing gameplay mechanics, accompanied by mesmerizing world design, and an intriguing story. I'm looking forward to Vol. 2, and can't wait to discover more of the fate of Off Peak City.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this. It was weird and so cool and fun.I already played the developer's previous games, Off-Peak and Norwood Suite, and knew what I would be seeing in this game. I loved the previous games and loved this one too. I'm not sure if I prefer this one or Norwood Suite but they're both solid games and different enough from each other. I'm a really big fan of the surreal artstyle and the soundtrack like the previous games is great.I really recommend this game if you want a weird but cool experience.It's also a great pizza making sim, so you can have some fun with that.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: I have to support the absolute genius that is Cosmo D. Beautiful visuals, excellent music, amazing story that is getting slowly revealed through this game, Norwood Suite and the future additions of Off-Peak City. The less said, the better. Just get it already.Edit: There was an update to the game adding content and it's every bit amazing as everything else in the series. Better yet, it gives a bit more insight to the future events. Very excited to see what's next.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an experience I never knew I needed in my life. Tales from Off-Peak City (as well as the rest of the series it is a part of) has an entirely unique atmosphere that I just adore and a soundtrack that delivers an unsettling calm. If anything about this game appeals to you then I highly recommend you check it out!
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: What a total gem! Each installment in this series is great and they just keep getting better. This game feels like free jazz in game form. Everything from the environments to the music, dialogue, quirky character and building design is charming and full of life. The act of making a pizza in this game is one of my favorite artistic moments in a piece of media in recent memory. Getting to conduct my own pizza band as I throw excessive amounts of toppings on my pie is everything I want out of this type of game.  It's cool to see the progression of this through the other games. I'm reminded of the ramen guy in a previous game, Offpeak, that waxes lyrical about each part of a bowl of ramen equating various ingredients to horn sections and basses and strings. In this game, I am not just told how food could be a symphony, I am SHOWN it. I love that I am physically made to feel the same way about my pizzas that the ramen guy talks about it. Great game design!
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: I just played this and Norwood Suite back to back and loved them both. In this game you get to explore a surreal-magical Brooklyn-esque world (Gowanus on acid?) by making and delivering pizzas to a host of bizarre and funny characters in trippy apartment buildings. The pizzas you make may include ingredients such as synthetic brains and chocolate chips, and when you deliver them, your customers will respond to each ingredient with gusto. It's a short game and not difficult -- a few hours, maybe more if you knock out all the achievements, which I haven't done yet -- but it's cleverly put together and enjoyable. If you like casual exploration games that are more about the ride and the atmosphere than the challenge, you may enjoy this one. The world is memorable and very unique -- and I enjoyed the weird humor of the characters. I'm looking forward to seeing more games from this team.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: I dont really know how to start this review but here goes. Massive spoilers.Tales From Off-Peak City Vol 1. is an "Egg-Like" masterpiece. If you have not yet purchased and are a fan of the genre, highly recommended. This game makes you feel things. Under the surreal whimsey that is the surface of this game, there's an element of borderline horror. Yes, horror. If you haven't played any of the devs previous games, you might not get every reference. I certainly didn't get everything but I think that's more to do with me being a big dummy dumb.  The sound is of course detailed and layered like a fine pizza pie.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: The game is amazing! I feel like the music in The Norwood Suite was more memorable, but that does not really taint this game in any way, if anything its a testament to how good the music was in The Norwood Suite. Its weird, its "artsy" its confusing, its beautiful, its simple and complex. That probably sounds like a snobby way to review a game, and maybe it is, but i think all of those descriptors are true. The game is a trip, and you should see it for yourself. Cosmo D, keep making games, I will buy them all.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: Great for anyone looking to see some weird and fascinating stuff. The sound design is top notch, and though some assets are janky looking, they feed into the game's style enough to feel intentional. The story and dialogue is pretty good, but I recommend you play or watch Off-peak and/or the Norwood Suite first in order to appreciate the connections between those games and this. As far as criticisms go, the game feels a bit unoptimized. It won't deter your progress, since you can take your time exploring and interacting with things, but if you use a low-end computer or laptop, it can feel slow, even at low resolution and graphics settings.Additionally, a lot of the development seems to have gone into replayability. There's plenty of interactions and neat details for you to discover, some of which might require multiple playthroughs. (I.E. Different pizzas to see how customers react.) As a side effect however, I felt the game ended sooner than I had anticipated. There were plenty of locked rooms I never got to go in, and considering the length and elaborate nature of the Norwood Suite, I expected a single playthrough to let me explore more of the world than I ultimately did.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: Play this game, live in it's world.I simple cannot put it more simply. This is an immersive experience, and the more you put in, the more you'll take out.The game is short, but it's meant to be a smaller part of a larger story. Explore everything, as though you're a child, and this was the only game you got for Christmas.You'll thank me.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing sequel to an amazing game series! This game was so much fun to play from taking cool photos, making crazy pizza's, hearing more amazing music, and feeling creeped out but astounded by the weird character and building designs. I can't wait to see what part two of this game will show! Cosmo D is an amazing game developer and I want to see more weird and crazy games from him soon!
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game. Really hard to describe the experience itself. It's one of those games where it's best not to know about the story and just play it yourself. Basically you go to a town, talk to people, make pizzas and take pictures. Slowly you start to unravel the secret truth behind why everyone loves drinking the local energy drink in Off-Peak City. This is Cosmo D's most intricate game. The camera system is perhaps one of the most enjoyable in any game I've played. The characters are all very interesting. The world feels like you're in Rocko's Modern Life. It's all strange, weird, and lovable. My only complaint is that it ended just as it started to ramp up in drama. I wanted to spend more time exploring the world and characters, plus I only got 75% of the achievements so there was some dialogue I missed. However, this didn't ruin my overall enjoyment of the game.Highly recommend for anyone who has played Cosmo D's previous games, or anyone who likes bizarre first person adventure games .
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: i love this game serie it's an surreal comfy gaming experience that blows your mind open haha it kinda reminds me of the music band the residents.i feel like a child again when playing this gamesi loved the norwood suitehowever this one felt a bit unfinished, i appreciate the improving in story however the map felt a bit empty for example the hollways. if you played the norwood suite you would get what i mean with this ;)also what was the casino section ? i would give this one a 7/10 and nordwood suite a 9/10.hopefully the next one will have a better improvementstill enjoyed the game and would recommend it to everyone to experience this.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: (Disclaimer: I've got the game from Humble Choice, spent about an hour in it - then decided to buy and finish it on Steam. I think this can tell you something too...)This is essentially the same as The Norwood Suite, Cosmo D's previous game - the same style, the same form, the same quality. And although I've given The Norwood Suite only 7,5 points out of 10 in review, in Tales from Off-Peak City I've felt much more captivated by the world, the story, the characters. That's because I've treated this game as the third part in the series (there is also freeware Off-Peak).So that's my advice for you: play Cosmo D's previous games first (or at least The Norwood Suite) and then come back for Tales from Off-Peak City. You'll be in for . There is nothing like it out there in the entire Steam catalog.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent, beautiful game. I'm starting to love these developers, they even integrate the Norwood Suite universe here. Simple yet mesmerizing graphics, story gathered from all around, trippy sequences, and an overall incredible atmosphere. You really feel a part of the environment and it's got a great touch of personality. It's amazing how many different things can happen, each pizza you deliver, the customer comments on everything you puton it and mentions stuff you didn't. I highly recommned this and the Norwooed Suite.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: A strange game that uniquely pieces together minimalism and an interesting story. The artistic style creates a sense of uneasiness while also setting it apart from any other game I've played in a good while. This is definitely worth buying if you like something that stands apart from others. Can't wait for future volumes.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: As ever, Cosmo D comes back with another stunningly mystifying, amazingly odd, and strangely beautiful game, with new additions to gameplay that make it even more enjoyable, this "chapter" is not greatly long, but it is definitely worth the pricetag, and there are plenty of secrets and easily missable details that will keep you coming back, I was so hooked I played it through on the first day, truly wonderful.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: Cosmo D yet again offers an amazing and surreal experience in a new but equally enjoyable setting. The best features from the previous games are present in this one with new additions. The soundtrack is once again amazing and truly brings the city to life, along with all the characters and the unique environments. If you liked Off-Peak and The Norwood Suite this is the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

_childDocuments_.review: On the corner of July Avenue and Yam Street, all is not what it seems. What role will you play in a city's fate?
_childDocuments_.name: Tales From Off-Peak City Vol. 1

name: Bookbound Brigade
detailed_description: What if all the protagonists of books lost their memory? Venture into their world and beat the hell out of historical and literary characters you studied in school! Bookbound Brigade is a new take on the established Metroidvania genre where classic stories and well-known characters get the video game treatment, and where the player gets to lead a colorful bunch of real and fictional heroes through a 2D side-scrolling platform-adventure in a quest to battle overwhelming hordes of monsters and bring order back to the literary world. • Explore, fight, backtrack, grow your skills and tackle challenging quests and puzzles, as in any Metroidvania game worthy of its name, but get ready for a twist… • There is no single hero in Bookbound Brigade: you play as a party of unique characters, each with their own traits and skills, who move in formation and fight as one • Expect to meet some familiar and less familiar faces, as all the characters, both playing and non-playing, are drawn from the pages of history and literature  • Enjoy distinctive hand-drawn visuals, inspired by book illustration from all time and straying far from the pixel art dominating the Metroidvania genre

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? This one is a winner! A Metroidvania, but one with a special mechanic. You do not play one hero, but a group of characters who move and fight as one. You can switch formation any time (if there is enough space), from a line formation to venture through tunnels, to a column to reach higher places or a wheel to move very fast. Your party consists of heroes from history and literature, from Count Dracula, Robin Hood, King Arthur to Queen Victoria. All of them have lost their memory (but not their individual character). Same for the 50+ NPCs you meet on your travels, who all have something to say, which often leads to grotesque situations. Your first quest is to find a fire-proof armor for Jeanne d'Arc (who has a little fire-phobia since meeting the British...), then you meet Don Quixote who of course fought windmills just for fun... and so on. There is always something to smile at during your breaks of fighting hordes of monsters on your quest through 5 worlds. The frequent dialogues might be considerably less funny if you haven't read the original books (or at least seen a good movie adaption) or if your history knowledge is very limited. And yes, there are texts to read. A bit hard to read when you play on a TV, btw.Explore, fight, backtrack, grow your skills and tackle challenging quests and puzzles, as in any Metroidvania. Fighting is a bit unusual, best jump on an opponent and mash the attack button. This is very funny, especially the sounds your heroes make, but might not be liked by purists. The game starts easy, but gets rather hard later on, especially the boss fights are no cake. While checkpoints are frequent at the start, they seem to become more spread later on.Funny Metroidvania for literary people and with unique play mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Bookbound Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: Bookbound Brigade is a 2D Metroidvania set in the world of history and literature. You control a band of characters from around the world who need to save B.O.B, also known as The Book of Books, which has been stolen from its place. Without it, all the world of literature is at risk.As you venture through the world of literature, you'll run into a large number of different characters, some historical, some made up, and this is where most of the games humor comes from, the dialogue between your party of characters, and the people you run into. While some of the dialogue can be a bit funny, it can also feel a bit stilted, and the game has a tendency of lingering on jokes that don't quite land, and having King Arthur say "LOL" is more likely to make people cringe than laugh.Bookbound Brigade has a distinct and consistent art style, and the character designers have done a good job, because despite being heavily stylized, most characters, even less famous ones, are easy to identify. All the different areas also look quite different, but sadly different rooms within the same area tend to look very similar, which makes it hard to remember where you've been and where important objects that you have to return to might be. Luckily the map marks the rough locations for different objects, but this also takes away a bit from the sense of exploration.Sadly, Bookbound Brigade's biggest issues are related to its gameplay. You control a "blob" of characters, that move as one, and you can change formation in order to get past different obstacles or fight enemies, and while the idea is fun, controls feel unresponsive. If you try to change formation in a place where the new formation would not fit, you get a red outline showing this, but quite often the game won't respond to commands to change formation, despite repeated key presses. This is extra bad in areas where you rapidly need to switch between formations, to avoid hazards. Combat is requires a lot of mashing. So much so that I started experiencing physical pain while playing the game, something that's never happened to me before, not even in notoriously mash heavy games, like Mario Party. So I could not see the final parts of the game. Bosses are the main issue, they're massive damage sponges, and while there are ways to deal damage other than just directly attacking them, like with abilities, you don't deal enough damage this way to kill them, and you still need to do a lot of mashing to get through. So sadly, with the unresponsive controls and the mash-heavy combat, I can't recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Bookbound Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: I want to love  this game, I really, really do. I simply cannot recommend it. The concept is great, playing as numerous literary figures, and the group mechanic is somewhat akin to The Wonderful 101, where you move a whole group at once. The devs clearly put a ton of heart into this.However, the flaws simply cannot be excused. The main issue is control, the controls are not only severely unresponsive, but extremely floaty when they do work. Combine this with the attrocious platforming and it makes for an exercise in frustration. In the very first world, the island world, you'll encounter and area where you have to jump over moving spikes, which apparently have hit boxes four times bigger than they are. Your characters jumping is slow and often don't jump at all when you press the button. To make matters worse, the art designer apparently decided to place numerous foreground objects in the way. If you get past this you'll eventually come to a lake where you jump over moving platforms, again fighting the awful controls along the way, it gets to the point where it just isn't fun at all. This would be ok if it were raw challenge but it's not, you're fighting controls and other preventable issues. This game apparently also has numerous bugs, but I cannot speak to those as I never made it far enough to even encounter them. This one needed a few more minutes in the oven. I hate that I am giving this game a negative review, there is a good game buried herein someplace.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a sidescroller with a difference. It has the chance to be great with its cool and unique concepts but just falls off short when it comes to gameplay. Sidescrollers are many these days and to make a game worth playing in this saturated market it needs to stand out in many aspects just not one or two.* The art style is fun and simple makes you feel like you are in a kids cartoon which i like for this game perfect fit.*There are plenty of characters that you can meet and join your brigade. * Carrying on from the characters each one that joins your brigade has a certain skill. may it be draculas double jump or robin hoods song. This creates dynamic in walking around the world and in combat.* The World your basically in a story/tale which is fun and i like it.* The soundtrack and sound effects are on point with the music like a classic traditional fairytale soundtrack and on hit sound effects like your in the cartoon so they match.* Now in Sidescrollers combat is a main issue and in this early game it is the best of button bashing for a combo but later on this is effected by the abilities of your  characters so keep that in mind.* The hitboxes can be annoying to say the least. When it comes to fire in your stacked formation you cant't be one pixel off or it kills you there is no room for error, and for this casual type of platformer it just does not fit.Overall this game is not bad and is worth the try fun and engaging dialog from the characters and a nice new addition to the platformer world, It also has the power to grow with added characters and more "Story worlds" But falls short of being memorable as a great platform with it's mediocre combat, and a few head frustrating things would still recommend if you are a fan of platformers.7.5/10
