_childDocuments_.review: I've played about 4 hours in, and seen two of the game's dungeons/major areas not counting the prologue thusfar, and I was not given any sort of promotional copy or anything. I came across this game via some random upcoming indie game video on youtube a couple weeks before its release.Graphics: 9/10 For a pixel art game, this game is absolutely gorgeous. The lighting effects especially on your way to the first dungeon are absolutely sublime. The characters are done in a high rez pixel style, and reminded me of games like the Ys series. Top quality pixel art here.Sound: 8/10 The sound, while I've yet to encounter any earworms that stick with me after I close the game, I found to be rather pleasant. Sound effects are good, the music ranges from calm and relaxing to gripping at the right times, I've no complaints here.Aesthetic: 9/10 They picked a style and went with it, and what a nice style it is. The game, as you might expect from seeing the screenshots on the store page, is very much Meso-American themed, as advertised. This is such an under-utilized theme, that it's refreshing to see a game set in it, though during the first dungeon, you see hints at there being something else underneath it all, but I won't spoil it here.Mechanics: 7/10 When I say mechanics, I am talking about player progression, level ups, equipment, that sort of thing. So far, Itorah seems to be focusing on Metroidvania-style gameplay, giving you new abilities to help you overcome obstacles in your path. It doesn't seem like equipment is going to be a thing, but rather you buy upgrades for your health, energy, and healing ability unless they introduce something else further down the line. It's a bit simple, but yet this is nice sometimes. Not every game needs mechanics stacked ontop of mechanics that need to be grinded for (Bloodstained, as much as I like that game, does get a little harsh with this). It's a simple side-scroller, that tells a story and shows you some amazing visuals while doing it.Control: 7/10 First off, I'm going to dock a point here for lack of D-Input support. The game will see a D-Input controller, but I couldn't seem to get the game set up properly for one. It's a sidescroller, and a mechanically simple one at that. We shouldn't need a gazillion buttons and two axes for a game like this. TBH, I'd fix the issues with D-Input controllers, and let you bind freelook to a button that you hold down to pan the camera around rather than requiring a 2nd axis for that. Also, for some strange reason, the UI movement is not the same as character movement, when I bound the character movement to the D-Pad on my PS2 controller, the UI still would not respond to such inputs (but it yet it does with the 360 controller).Anyhow, this is one of those games where your character feels like she has weight and momentum, and when you make a jump, you're mostly committed, though you can slow your horizontal movement mid-jump, but you definitely can't turn around in mid-air. Combat feels somewhat iffy, I found hit boxes to not always be accurate, but that wasn't such a big thing, because....Challenge (combat): 8/10 Normal mooks and terrain does not do a whole lot of damage, and if you fall into an endless pit, you only take a moderate amount of damage and are sent back to whatever solid ground you touched last (kinda like Hollow Knight for example). This is refreshing. I found that bosses had some mild challenge to them, but yet once you learn the patterns, they became rather easy. Maybe this changes later in the game, but for the first 3 bosses, that's what I found. It's more about pattern recognition rather than pixel perfect precision or frame perfect dodge timing.Level Design: 5/10 Aesthetically, the level design is amazing. Mechanically, though... the first dungeon was fine. Some trap based puzzles, some timed dodge rolling, all good. The second dungeon was an utter nightmare. Lots of jumping puzzles, lots of enemies hitting you in mid-jump, downstriking to bounce off of things, grabbing onto hanging vines, etc all while enemies attack you. I found it rather frustrating, and I'm really hoping that's the only dungeon like that in the game. I really hope they don't keep doing stuff like that throughout the entire game.Conclusion: 7/10: This isn't going to be the new Bloodstained. I know I mentioned that game a number of times in this review, but a lot of people are going to look at the trailer, see a side scrolling metroid vania with unlockables, items, etc and they might think that it's going to be similar to that game. While it shares some elements with it, it's just not that. Nor does it need to be. The game stands on its own merits. It has some flaws, but yet there's more than enough beauty here that I'd recommend it. It's a neat little indie package that I am glad I stumbled across a week or two ago randomly and overall (outside of the puzzles in the 2nd temple), I've very much enjoyed my time with it.

_childDocuments_.review: is a reasonably well-made Metroidvania. The story follows the last human (who is also a child) named Itorah and a talking axe named Koda (neither name appears too often) who are trying to find out what happened to the humanity and fight against the plague which is threatening the present not-humans (anthropomorphic animals, like Mickie Mouse, and living masks with limbs).The level design is functional - there are very few optional secrets and most of the maps must be explored in order to proceed. The movement controls are tight, rebindable (but limited to the keyboard only), responsive, and comfortable. All actions were executed perfectly. The character development system consists of health, stamina (required for some, but not all, attacks and actions, such as sprinting), the number and the potency of the healing items. In order to upgrade, some XP and material components (very few, fixed position on the map) are required, while the upgrades themselves can be done only in the main hub. Most areas loop back, and it is reasonably easy to reach the town on the way to the next objective. Since there is no fast travel, it is as convenient as it gets. From what I can tell, there is only one ending.The combat can be described as functional as well. There is 1 ground combo, singular directional and aerial attacks, and dodging (consumes stamina). The bosses are diverse and some of the encounters consist of running, instead of combat. However, they do not have visible health bars and there is only one difficulty. On the other hand, it is usually clear when the battle progresses and phases change. The saving system is checkpoint-based and there is usually one right before bosses.The graphics and visual design are beautiful - painted 2D images and backgrounds, though seeing the interactive objects occasionally was challenging. The soundtrack is rather good as well, the voice acting is limited to some noises to indicate who is talking.No bugs were encountered during the playthrough (Steam says 10 hours).Overall, it was a positive experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Itorah is the perfect casual 2D action platformer ('metroidvania') and here's why.First of all it's super simple and relatively easy, you will never get stuck on areas for too long and if you die it's probably your own fault. The checkpoint system and healing are super generous and the game makes it very clear where to go next. Due to this the game is for the most part linear (which is why metroidvania is between "s). There's no real reason to go off the beaten path either because there's apart from a few exceptions, very little collecting to do. All of this makes the game very casual and enjoyable if you're either feeling lazy and just wanna relax for a bit or if you're not very good at video games (which is fine!) Based on this alone i would recommend this game for 6-12 hours of fun. However while it's a perfect casual game, it's not a perfect game.The game does nothing wrong, no horrible bugs or performance, no massive design flaws or stupid mechanics. However the game doesn't do anything amazing either, it's all pretty basic. All of it is just good or solid but nothing to make it stand out (apart from the visuals, the game looks absolutely amazing). The movement feels good (jumping, wall jumping, double jumping, air dashing, etc...) so does combat (light attack, heavy attack, stomp, ranged attack, airial attack, ...) However there's nothing crazy unique, it's just basic solid stuff but it works. Upgrading is limited to upping your estus flasks amount/healing or your stamina/health, so it helps but it's nothing super exciting. Story is kinda weirdly presented but it's allright, nothing too memorable. Music is weird, not my cup of tea and not sure if it works with the game but i can live with it. Level design is pretty basic although there are some genuinly fun parts, however with such linear levels going from area to area can take a while so the game would've probably benefited greatly from some sort of fast travel system. There's also a nice variety in areas to visit from forests & plains to temples and ruins. Enemy variety is on the low side with a lot of copy and paste between areas, i think if they added more unique ones that would've helped a lot with the overal feeling of repetition that the game sort of has. Boss fights though are VERY fun, they're easy but they got unique mechanics and ideas and are satisfying to beat (especially the fire boss, which was my highligt of this game)In the end i'm still super happy that i played this, i very much enjoyed every minute with the game and would also recommend anyone play it. It won't be your favorite game, you might even forget it, but you won't regret having played it. Also the devs seem genuinly awesome people so go ahead and buy a copy to support their dream :)

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start by saying that I do recommend this game specially if you have not played a mv in a while and are looking forward to it.I really wished I had not grabbed this game immediately after finishing Tunic, cause the comparisons between the two are what threw this game down for me.I really wanted to like this game been waiting for it for a while, the art style is beautiful, enemies and the creatures in the village have a lot of varied designs but even if they are each one unique at the same time they all share a particular style so there's aesthetic coherence in and on itself. The animation of mc (The Human) is rather fluid in its movements like running and climbing and dodging, the same with the attacks there are several different of these like slashing up, forward, a three strike combo and a charged attack. The movement is a little stiff but without being annoying or unresponsive instead you can feel the weight of the character as she jumps or attacks which imo it's a possitive.That said, the game didn't really click with me, the scenaries are beautiful but somehow barren, at least what I have played (so far just got to the village) and the combat is pretty basic, almost dull. The monsters don't pose a challenge so even if you have some different attacks you're not really encouraged to use them instead you can just to spam the attack button.It's not a bad game by any means but all the time while playing I felt as if I was playing an old genesis game like The Lion King, which again it's not a bad game but rather plain and in this age when platformers and mv have progressed with new and unique mechanics and each one has their own identity this game will have a hard time to stand out above the rest. That's why I regret having played it not a day after finishing Tunic, which is an unique and immersive experience that makes the mystery of the story a fundamental part of its very gameplay.Still I cannot say I don't recommend it, this game might prove perfect to scratch your mv itch if you have not played one in a while, that happened to me with the Alma (Legacy and Awakening) games, neither is anything exceptional but I enjoyed them just fine cause I haven't played a game like that in a while. I expect I'll go back to this game in a couple of moths and I quite probably enjoy it and even finish it, at least I certainly hope so

_childDocuments_.review: Itorah is a game that tries to deliver an intriguing story with engaging gameplay mechanics. Unfortunately, the game falls short in both aspects, leaving the player with a lackluster experience.The story and characters in Itorah are incredibly dull and cut-scenes are slow to go through. I found myself quickly losing interest in the story and skipping as fast I could every time they tried to make me go through more boring dialogue.The gameplay mechanics in Itorah are passable enough, with enjoyable platforming and combat elements. I found myself unable to progress to the Storm Archives due to either a missed objective, upgrade, or a bug. I could have missed something in a cut- scene but I was bored, lost, and directionless.I found the combat ridiculously easy which made me think maybe the game was made for a younger audience. It's seems attempts to balance this may have been made by just making all the enemies take a bunch of hits which only makes things feel clunky and slow.In conclusion, Itorah is a game that fails to deliver a satisfying gaming experience. The dull characters and storyline, technical issues, unbalanced difficulty, and lack of direction make the game a difficult one to recommend. While the gameplay mechanics may provide some entertainment, the game's flaws hinder the overall experience, making it a forgettable addition to the gaming world.

_childDocuments_.review: ITORAH:~~~~~~ Your name is Itorah, and you wake up suspended in a cocoon made of spider webs somewhere in a cave. To make things even stranger, a talking axe is trapped in the same chamber, and it cannot escape either. It takes all your remaining strength to free yourself and rescue the talking axe that refers to itself as the Greatest Warrior. Both of you come to the same conclusion: it’s time to find a way out of this predicament. But that’s not the worst of it, as Itorah discovers that she is the only human left alive in a world inhabited by fluffy talking creatures facing extinction due to, as they call it, the Black Plague.  Itorah is an action platformer game developed by Grimbart Tales and published by Assemble Entertainment on the 22nd of March 2022 on the Steam platform.The game consists of six levels, including a semi-tutorial blended into the first stage and five others where you will need to beat four Nahucan guardians and the source of the Black Plague. What a beautiful game. The Aztec artwork is colourful and a pleasure for the eyes; gorgeous from start to finish. It’s been a while since I have experienced such eye-catching artwork in a platformer game. The levels are pretty good too, but if you are looking for a challenging platformer game, you will be disappointed as Itorah offers only one difficulty level. Even if the levels are well-structured and of reasonable length, you will probably push through them without dying until you reach a boss fight. Then, you might die once or twice until you figure out how to dispatch each boss. This is due to two things. The first is that there are several campfires in each stage where you can save your progress. It is excellent, and yes, Itorah will receive all her health back, but these campfires are too close to each other and there are probably a few too many per level. The other is that Itorah will run for a while before facing enemies. But don’t get me wrong, you’ll have a lot of fun when she does! And, I really enjoyed the different types of enemies, from the spiders wearing Aztec masks, to the flying Aztec bees with armour, to the Black Plague enemies.  I also like that Itorah only has a few skills available to her at the start of the game. Dashing, jumping and using the talking axe to slay enemies will be her first few skills. Each level has a shrine, and this shrine holds a dark crystal called an Echo. When she finds it, she will gain access to other skills such as double jumping, dashing while in the air, uppercut attack and throwing the talking axe.Ahui is the Indiana Jones of the fluffy creatures that Itorah will meet early on in the game. She lives in a village called Chimali where Itorah will need to visit after finishing all the first five levels. There, she will be able to upgrade her health, stamina and healing potions. For this, you’ll need leaves, crystals and shards. She’ll often receive shards after killing an enemy, and she’ll sometimes find them in chests. Leaves and crystals can only be found in chests. As I mentioned above, the graphics are fabulous, as is the gameplay. But the game is lacking in terms of difficulty. You’ll probably finish the game within eight to eleven hours, taking your time. You can play with the keyboard in terms of controls, but I recommend playing with a gamepad. Itorah can be played in eleven different languages: English, French, German, Spanish, Italian, Chinese and a few others. I enjoyed my time playing Itorah, but wished there were different levels of difficulty to increase replayability.Positives:~~~~~~~ +	Stunning artwork+	Great gameplay and good for a newcomer to the genre+	Interesting enemies+	Full control support+	AchievementsNegatives:~~~~~~~~ -	No trading cards as yet-	Only one level of difficulty decreasing replayabilityItorah has stunning visuals from start to finish! It might be on the easy side of the platformer scale, but an experience you’ll never forget! 7/10Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

_childDocuments_.review: What an amazing little gem of a game. However, set your expectations right, it's not a Metroidvania in the amount of exploration and secrets hidden throughout the game. However, what it feels like is a retro adventure game; something more along the lines of Battle of Olympus. It's fairly linear overall but that doesn't take away from how fun the game is overall. The dungeon designs are pretty solid (the latter ones have some great platforming sections). Movement isn't as fluid as something like Hollow Knight but it's not clunky by any means; you just need to learn to play by its rules. I think this game will occupy a place in my mind for many years and I'm really happy I took the plunge and gave it a shot. Highly recommended for those looking for a nice and contained adventure with a beautiful aesthetic!

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my playthrough of Itorah and thought it was overall okay.  The world and art design are the best part of the game, with beautiful areas and expressive character designs.  Thought that some of the backgrounds and concepts for areas were very well done and it was a beautiful game to look at, and the story was fairly interesting even though it takes hours to really get into it.  Where the game fell flat for me was in the repetitive enemies, forgettable bosses, overly basic combat, and lack of real exploration.  The joy of a true Metroidvania is opening a new skill and backtracking to old areas to find collectibles or new areas.  Itorah by and large had a huge amount of backtracking, but it was always just to walk back to the “hub” after completing each objective.  Overall a very linear experience that I have no intention of ever playing again, but also one I didn’t mind sinking the 6 hours I did into it.  Buy it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The hand-drawn art style is absolutely gorgeous and adds a unique charm to the game. Exploring the lush, vibrant world was a visual treat, and the fluid animations made every movement feel smooth and satisfying.The gameplay is a solid mix of platforming and combat, with a good variety of enemies and challenges to keep things interesting. I particularly enjoyed the responsive controls, which made navigating the levels and battling foes a lot of fun. The boss fights were well-designed and provided just the right amount of challenge without being frustrating.If I had to point out a downside, it would be that some sections felt a bit repetitive, but this was a minor issue in an otherwise fantastic experience.Overall, Itorah is a beautifully crafted game that I would highly recommend to fans of action-adventure platformers. It’s clear that a lot of love and effort went into making this game, and it shows in every aspect.

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't go as far as saying the game is not worth your money like some other reviewers, but bear in mind that this game is very short and somewhat linear and straightforward. It might seems like a metroidvania to some extent, but despite the interconected rooms there's no heavy backtracking like the majority of the titles of this genre.To my opinion, Itorah is a game that's crafted with the will to tell a good story, and this is mostly seen from the art overall (characters, worlds, items, animation and music). The game dabs in a lot of stuff, but most of them are treated very superficially. Platforming could be better, navigation too, combat is kind of poor, with enemies not posing as great of a threat as their are a nuisance.Unfortunately I feel that the game falls short in terms of programming and game design, with some mechanics, controlls, enemies and QoL in general needing a little bit more of experience, attention, or love. The story itself felt kind of lost between my two sessions to finish the game, but was an O.K experience after all.Recommended, though buy it at a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: A weak recommend. Everything about it is okay-to-good, but there's nothing particularly outstanding. Most of the fighting is meaningless because you just get fully restored at every savepoint, which feels like a bit of a design flaw, like there should be some kind of cost to being clumsy throughout the game. There were also some pretty long sections of essentially just walking. The stamina was a bit weird; running using stamina seems like a mistake because making travel take longer with no actual gameplay going on is awful - luckily it's also flawed in that if you jump while running you go at the same speed but your stamina doesn't go down, which essentially renders the running-stamina-drain moot, which is another point in favor of "running just shouldn't have been using stamina in the first place".It felt like the only time mistakes matter is during the final boss fight, which swung a bit in the opposite direction - it was hard to avoid taking damage, the damage was much larger than from anything before, and there wasn't really any joy to it. It would have been super annoying to have got there without maxed out health and healing.But these are fairly minor objections. I played it all the way through, and had fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend! The graphics are excellent and help bring the story and world to life. The narrative is engaging and keeps the player invested in the experience. Gameplay is well-crafted, with thoughtful save point placement and mechanics that feel balanced throughout most of the experience. Some scenarios are similar in Ori but is more accessible overall. The first few scenes are not difficult allowing player to become familiar the game. The final two scenes provide a nice challenge, as I barely defeated the last boss with only a few hit points remaining. A few drawbacks, there is only one weapon option available throughout the game.  Moreover, it does not support cloud saving for sync across my PC and steamdeck.  Overall, this is a game I would strongly suggest based on its strong visual presentation, enjoyable storytelling, and solid core gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: "A good sample platter of the metroidvania genre"I thought Itorah was great. I understand some of the mixed reviews though. Look, if you want hardcore NON LINEAR 2d platformer, metroidvania, Hollow knight, souls-like and all that other hard core stuff...this aint the game for you. I found this to be a great time killer. I didn't need to be overly invested but I was still curious enough to continue playing. The art work, time period of the story and retro inspired game-play was beautiful. I found myself being challenged a bit on the platforming aspect. Not to the point of extreme frustration but just enough to fix mistakes. The game does a great job of holding your hand for bit and then letting you fly. Puzzles offered easy to moderate challenges which made wanting to progress a bit more fun as well as wanting to see how the story unfolded. The enemies don't offer much of a variety as you pretty much face the same type in each world but the abilities you acquire to reach new areas or areas you couldn't access before is fun and offers unique platforming and combat combinations.Itorah is a game that isnt going to BLOW YOU AWAY but if you are looking to get into this genre of gaming then I think this is a great starting point that anyone can pick up, play and enjoy. It's about 10 hours or less if you are fast. I took my time however I won't be going back to acquire 100% achievements. If you find the game on sale I do recommend a play through, although $20 bucks isnt an unreasonable ask for this game so. I give Itorah a 7.0 out of 10Great job to the devs!

_childDocuments_.review: I would use the word Metroidvania Loosely for this game. Itorah feels like an action adventure 2D platformer more than a metroidvania. The platforming aspect side of it is a bit rough. I really love the combat abilities you receive over time in this game. You can really dash through levels, and do all these flips and dash down onto enemies and obstacles. Of course all this will cost you stamina. As you're running, and dashing through the game. Your stamina meter will diminish. But that's all that I'm doing in this game, just dashing through to get to the next part. The only thing thats really slowing me down is when I stop to look at the surrounding & backgrounds. This game is BEAUTIFUL, I had to take a moment and appreciate the amount of detail that went into the art of this game. As I'm appreciating the art in this game, I suddenly realize that I have no clue what the story is even about. It's a bout a girl Named Itorah who is on a journey to cleanse this world with crystals. Not much is known of her origin. She finds a stone axe that can talk to her and leads her on her way. You meet other characters along the way. But the truth of the matter is, the story is a bit flat. The thing thats gonna keep you to play this game is the beautiful environments, the fun abilities which allows you to dash through levels. The first half of the game I was fighting as many enemies as possible but the other half I'm running past them. Some parts of the game sort of over stayed it's welcome. The bosses were okay, nothing too crazy. Itorah is a good game, the art style really blew me away. And it's nice to know that assemble entertainment is taking 10% of the proceeds of this game and putting it into Save the World Edition to Survival International in support of indigenous people around the globe!If there ever was to be another game, or something similar. I hope they improve upon the world building, characters, and their meaning. Story is very important, and when you have players dashing through it without understanding whats really going on. That's not a good sign. BUT I did like this game, I really did. Art style, and soundtrack is phenomenal in this game. Gameplay is okay, story is alright. Nothing I haven't seen before. I feel like this game was sort of inspired a bit from zelda/ There's a boat in this game that looks like king of red lions from Legend of zelda windwaker. If you consider this game a Metroidvania, then this is definitely one of the weaker metroidvanias compared to the likes of hollow knight, symphony of the night, super metroid, and others.BUT if you just want a 2d action adventure platformer thats inspired by South and Central American landscapes, with nice visuals, a memorable soundtrack. Decent gameplay with some different unique twists. I'd recommend this for you.But this is a slightly above average game with some highlights here and there. 7/10 wait for a sale kind of game.

_childDocuments_.review: Most noteworthy part of this game is the animations and illustrations. Itorah is quite possibly one of the most beautiful 2D games I've played to date. The Meso-American setting and artistic expressions were a refreshing detour from the status quo. The world seems massive and transitions through various climates with corresponding obstacles and enemies. I'ts TRULY breathtaking. The game isn't exactly child's play either as players must meticulously time their attacks, dodges and jumps to successfully nail fast moving enemies and clear difficult gaps. The upgrade system is comprehensive and well -paced as well. As the game progressed, a heart warming feeling overtook me. I honestly fell in love with Itorah.
_childDocuments_.name: ITORAH

_childDocuments_.review: Receommended with some caveats. Itorah is a search-action (metroidvania) through and through, and is as such quite enjoyable. It leans a bit on the easy side compared to other games in the subgenre, which makes it a decent starting point for players curious to learn it. There is a decent story going on that tugs on players' curiosity. It's supported by colorful, cute characters, a very pretty art direction, and pretty decent music to boot. All in all, it's a decen package with a lot going for it. There are of course flaws too though. The main gripe people seem to have with Itorah is the controls. I agree to a certain extent that there are some smaller hickups, mainly in how far back the game detects an attack-input and how it interprets some directional inputs. These you mainly get used to, however, and by the end you'll be zooming through the last parts like nobody's business. Another gripe seems to be a perceived style over substance. As stated before, the story is decent, but it does mainly play a background role to the showmanship of the game. Ori this is not. My personal gripes are mainly with the fact that no fast travel is ever unlocked. At times I find myself fine with this, but by the end the world is a decent chonk to chug through, and a fast travel option would be a huge QoL. The other gripe, that almost turns to a grudge, is the fact that a lot of dungeons are non-reenterable after you've beaten the boss there. While no dungeon contains missable items besides the occasional money chest, not being able to reenter them for farming purposes is rather alien to me in a metroidvania game.Overall, Itorah is an A-grade indie game. It lacks some final touches and polish that could make the game AA and shine a lot brighter. As it stands though, it's a dim star, a bit of a diamond in the rough. One diamond I myself ended up enjoying a fair amount.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good looking game with good sound design creating a world that you want to love but can't. _childDocuments_.review: Itorah is a solid classical linear 2D metroidvania platformer for genre beginners which misses the chance to really stand out of the masses of similar games.Difficulty ★★★★☆☆☆☆☆☆ (very fair and forgiving mechanics)Itorah's absolutely strong points is the beautiful handdrawn graphics and awesome sceneries you visit throughout her journey. Lovely details and characters in a marvelous aztec fantasy type setting. The battle system itself is rock solid intuitive with a fancy full-invu evade roll and easy to predict enemy attacks. Making the fighting experience not something luck based like in other genre type representive games. The soundtrack is very fitting, but unfortunetally not too much remarkable. The level design from a platforming perspective could be a little bit better and is too repetitive on some parts.I know this is the first game of this indie team, and for this it is very good to begin with, but nothing comes with some downsides because of the lack of experience of the devs I guess. But I have to point them out as well: The absolute biggest flaw of this game is the movement system. Walljumping can be a hassle because the hitbox is not properly working (this is mentioned by a lot of players). Also, especially on moving platforms, the hitbox Itorah connects to hang on an edge will sometimes trigger when it shouldn't and vice versa, making especially speedrunning a big pain in the ***. Also the air control is awkward. You will loose momentum on situation you don't expect it to do, or you can't control Itorah anymore properly (this is especially true for the upward midair axe attack later on, control feels horrible). Not to mention that sometimes Itorah just glide-walked on air or completely teleported to an edge while throwing my axe to it (for example in the water palace).I already mentioned it before, but Itorah is not a true metroidvania, because it is too linear for it. There is no chance to shortcut story elements or do the element quests in different orders. This is not a real issue, just a missed opportunity. The overall difficulty is way too easy for this genre type. You can mostly outtank enemies/bosses with the sheer energy bar you will get if you upgrade properly. I was able to play this game through in under 10 hours without dying on my very first run. Only Quetzacotl and the final boss were a close call as I had no healings left.Speaking of healings. I also expected all the time that I will get some kind of offensive (haste or extra damage aura) or some defensive power (temporary shield) I can cast with the magic stones you unlocked. I don't get the concept in it only to be used as a healing portion. This mechanic is quite useless as you would have gained the nearly same effect on just increasing the life bar even more (or decrease the incoming damage by a multiplier). The healing system is not really necessary. I would have liked other usage of the containers so that you have to decide strategical for what you will use them.Speaking of weird mechanics. Everything does need stamina, but jumping does not. Although you can upgrade stamina, there is no need to do so for about 80% of the game as you can just frogjump in full running speed to not use stamina at all. A wasted game mechanic.The game does lack a difficulty setting. Because there was none, and the game was super easy, I always expected that there will be a new game+ or hard mode after beating the game once. There is none, which is dissapointing. Yes, the under 5 hours run is more difficult, and you can do an artificial no upgrade run by yourself to beef things up if you want to. But still the devs missed this easy to implement thing of a difficulty selection.Ah, and I was able to meet myself after I reached the final gate to the boss realm. Just travel back to the village to still see you standing there :) The game does not want to be a unique metroidvania that stands out, or just missed a lot of opportunities to do so. And it has some bugs here and there. But the outstanding world and graphics created, and the solid fighting system does make it still enjoyable. When I bought this game I wanted just some entertainment and expected a metroidvania type game. The game delivered exactly this and fulfilled my expectations with it. Yet it cannot compete with many other games of the genre, but I do see the potential of this indie team and hope to see new games from them.

_childDocuments_.review: Itorah is a pretty solid platformer with very minor metroidvania elements, set in an open world, however there's little reason to backtrack, other than singular collectibles. There's no difficulty options, nor there's much to explore, really, so the replayability is pretty limited, achievements being the only real reason to try again. Platforming can be a bit slippery, at times I didn't feel in control, making the tighter platforming sections a bit more annoying. When it comes to platforming sections themselves, if you played Captain Claw, you will feel right at home - moving platforms, sequences of disappearing platforms, projectile traps, so on... Game is a bit buggy at times - charging bull enemies can hit you after their death, you can go out of bounds in certain spots, Combat could use more fleshing out, your moveset expands a bit with gameplay, but more moves could help make fighting through monsters more engaging. Some of the moves are bit finnicky, Audiovisuals are great - love the music, sound effects are fine. The graphics however are a highlight, vibrant colors, each location looks different and pretty in it's own way. Sometimes game forgets you're playing on 16:9 screen, or some other ratio, and you can spot the missing backgrounds and seams here and there.Despite it's flaws and jank, Itorah all in all is still a pretty solid title, and I can recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Quick:4/5.  Itorah is a great game.  The art is fantastic, the music is even better, and it is enjoyable from start to finish.  A mix between metroidvania and 2D platformer, Itorah is a simple yet well designed game that is perfect if you're looking for something relatively short, yet engaging.  It took me around 8 hours to beat this game, and in my opinion it was well worth my money and my time.  I recommend that you buy and play this game.More.The game begins with the titular character trapped in some sort of dungeon.  You play as the young girl Itorah.  You meet your companion at the start, a sentient melee weapon that is full of character, and you immediately set off figuring out what this beautiful world is all about.  Throughout your journey you encounter various characters.  All of them are strange and interesting, and breathe life into the game.One of the main reasons that I think this game is great is because almost every aspect of it is very well done.  The artwork in this game is absolutely fantastic.  It looks like it belongs in a game that is much more grand in scale and scope.  This is AAA art design in my opinion, and the only complaint I have is that there isn't more of it.  Itorah is full of color, clever enemy designs and animations, and gorgeous backgrounds.  Looking at this game just feels great.The audio is amazing as well.  I was constantly surprised by how much I was enjoying it.  For almost a year I waited for this game to release, after playing the demo, and I was apprehensive that it could meet my expectations after that.  This game far exceeded my expectations.  The music is just one of the aspects that seems like it belongs in some expensive movie or multi-million dollar game.  It is very well done.There is only one area of game-play that I was not ecstatic about, and that is the controls.  They aren't bad or anything... just a little bit unresponsive.  You eventually gain the ability to wall jump in this game.  Jumping off of walls takes some getting used to, because Itorah takes a second to actually 'stick' to the wall before you're able to jump off of it.  This feels a little weird at first but when you actually get used to it, it's just as smooth as wall-jumping in any other game.  There is also an ability to throw your melee weapon.  When you throw it, Itorah is able to move yet not fully while the weapon is in flight.  Sometimes it seems like you're unable to double jump while the weapon is flying.  When it returns to her, there is an animation that she does where she catches the weapon, and it stops her dead in her tracks.  This leaves you vulnerable to enemy attacks, and unable to move until the animation finishes.  Though it's not game-breaking or anything, it doesn't feel great, and you really have to get used to it.  A lot of the combat in this game has a 'Souls-like' feel to it.  Which I am usually not a fan of, but it is done well here.  The difficulty in this game does not spike, and you are given plenty of generous checkpoints and save-spots if you need to take a break.  Bosses can be surprisingly difficult, but they do have well telegraphed attacks and somewhat memorable attack patterns.  It feels great to fight them because they are challenging, but not overwhelmingly difficult.This is a simple game.  It doesn't rewrite the book on game design, or anything like that.  It's elegantly designed and perfect for what it is.  The level design is generous, as it loops back on itself in the dungeons, and it's very fun to navigate them.  The over-world is a little bit more lacking in that department, however you don't have to traverse it too often, and it looks great while you're doing it, so it feels welcome the few times that you have to travel.  I think this game is fantastic, and I eagerly await this studio's next release.  Hopefully it is everything that Itorah is, but better.

_childDocuments_.review: ITORAH has gorgeous art enhanced by outstanding lighting and a fantastic soundtrack, and the gameplay is mechanically polished enough to be enjoyable, but the game does feel lacking in some ways. Overall, I don't regret buying this game; the gorgeous visuals and dynamic soundtrack put a huge smile on my face multiple times. The game is worth playing once, but you probably won't get too much out of it after that.The game is a metroidvania action-platformer but the opportunities for exploration are scarce, which is fine. There is no reason to revisit old areas with new upgrades; the only time you're backtracking is when you're returning from an area because there is no form of fast travel, which is also fine. I actually found it quite fun to speed through the levels instead of exploring every crevice; movement in this game feels nice as long as you aren't required to be precise. You eventually get multiple upgrades that allow you to significantly extend your air time in various ways, which at times lets you be a bit creative with how you navigate the environment. I discovered that you keep your momentum while airborne, allowing you to attain a very high speed if you jump after sliding down a slope and chain together abilities that keep you in the air. Unfortunately the game is not designed with this trick in mind, and you will often immediately launch into a wall, enemy, or pit when you try it, although it's understandable that it wasn't expected.The game's greatest flaw is its low difficulty. Over time you will be able to upgrade your health and stamina, and at a certain point you will amass so much health that you'll succeed no matter how recklessly you play. The game has a nice variety of enemies and the bosses have interesting mechanics, but their attacks have such little consequence that enemy attack patterns can be largely disregarded. Defeating enemies is rarely required, and I often opted to ignore them whenever I wasn't locked into combat. The character's attacks are also a bit inconsistent and unreliable, adding to the feeling that I got through the whole game playing recklessly. Melee combo attacks often knock enemies just out of range of additional combo attacks, frequently putting you at risk of being hit by a long range attack such as a lunge. Attacking while airborne is usually fluid and does not cause interruptions, but if you happen to land while the attack is still being performed, you will get stuck in a recovery animation after landing, possibly causing you to get hit. The character's weapon, after being thrown, is immediately affected by gravity, making the aiming indicator quite deceptive because you will probably miss if you expect the projectile to travel in a straight line. The projectile's trajectory also isn't curved enough for it to feel intuitive as an arcing projectile either, so it's somewhat difficult to adapt to. On top of that, while the weapon is traveling, your movement abilities are significantly reduced and you will be locked into a recovery animation after catching the weapon.Overall, this game was still a very enjoyable experience. Every now and then you will notice the game's flaws, but you will just as often be awe-struck by the overall aesthetic.Oh, and you can rearrange the UI positions of gamepad buttons. I use a Nintendo Switch Pro Controller which has a different layout from the typical controllers so that feature was extremely appreciated. More games need to have that feature.

_childDocuments_.review: Itorah is a decidedly fun and enjoyable time, more in the vein of something like Dust: An Elysian Tail than Hollow Knight. I think a lot of folks who were disappointed went in expecting some kind of souls-like metroidvania, and were disappointed that this wasn't the case. There's a stamina meter, a dodge system, an estus-flask analogue, bonfires... but Itorah is approachable. It doesn't want you to senselessly die just to prove a point. You will have plenty of time to read big boss swings, and it will take rank and file enemies at least several swings before they get through your health bar. There are a few shortcomings when it comes to things like movement responsiveness, that don't feel like they were an intentional flavor choice by the developer. I played on keyboard, and it definitely feels like a game that's more built around having analog sticks for input. Combat is fair, but the different attack combos aren't super intuitive to figure out. But all of these things are minor gripes. The gameplay is solid, the visuals and music beautiful, the story fun, the characters lighthearted, and... the game is there for you to have a good time. It doesn't ask for perfection, it wants you to feel engaged and play the game and have a good time. It's easy to recommend this game. It's a simple feel good adventure and exactly what I need to unwind.

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about this game is absolutely stunning. From the breathtaking visuals to the uplifting and inspiring music, the game's humour and the amazing cast of characters. Balancing of the levels' length and difficulty was on point. I only ever had a small amount of health left right before reaching a bonfire which felt especially rewarding.The only minor criticism I want to mention is the mechanical design and the placement of some enemies. While the beginning and the end of the game have a rather nice variety of enemies, the middle part felt somewhat repetetive. The bossfights are fun but the difficulty was a bit inconsisent.However the platforming experience is where Itorah truly shines. The creativity that went into the levels and the different skills that you can learn is just fantastic. There are just enough so that the game keeps you entertained at all times while not being too demanding. You will need and use all of them.All in all 10/10 would play again.This is not only a great game for a studios' debut. It is simply a great game.Looking forward to Grimbart Tales future releases.

_childDocuments_.review: Eeehh... if steam had the much-needed "meh" option I'd be giving this game that, but I'm gonna err on the side of positivity as I liked more about this than I disliked, but. Well, for one. The game is very visually pretty. Gorgeous visuals, great animation, even a very pleasant soundtrack, in terms of aesthetics it's undeniably top-notch stuff. And the story is... solid! A bit vaguely told until the end but with some solid emotional beats. The gameplay though... hmm.  Everything feels just a bit too stiff, mostly. Attacks feel slightly too slow, jumps are often committal and the way momentum works in the air is frustrating - if you aren't running when you jump you move much slower and have no way of getting that momentum back. Speaking of, why is there a run button (and why is it tied to stamina???). Please do not include run buttons in your games in 2022 it's such a bad mechanic. I'm fine with dodge rolls and stronger attacks having a stamina cost but there's like, no reason to not be running all the time and tying stamina to it just makes things tedious.The game ultimately feels "fine enough" when doing platforming and there's a lot of good platforming moments, but the combat tends to let it down. Lots of flying enemies where you barely have the air control to deal with them, lots of repeated enemy types and lots of higher tier enemy types that are way, way too tanky - you can never upgrade how much damage you do, either, so even the basic enemy types will still be taking the same 2-3 hits by the end of the game, with the tankier ones upwards of a dozen - and in particular some late-game enemies and bosses assume you have way more mobility than you're ever really given - and overcompensate by giving you way too much health for them to ever be a threat.  I only died one time, towards the start of the game, due to a long stretch of level without any checkpoints (mixed with a combination of the downstab occasionally having trouble registering).The game is also... not a metroidvania. Levels are vaguely nonlinear but there's only the very occasional side path on a linear but winding main path and the only four chest rewards are 1. experience (the only viable way to get experience, too, as most enemies give you next to no exp vs. chests holding thousands of them each by the end), 2. cure upgrade tokens (not upgrades), 3. health/stamina upgrade tokens (also not upgrades), 4. keys to the dungeon you're currently in. There is no backtracking necessary at all, either. Areas often feel way too large and empty, as well, lots of long stretches of admittedly very pretty scenery with nothing going on. And the overarching map is one central hub region with six linear paths branching off of it. It's essentially a linear platformer with a slightly non-conventional structure at best and exploration rewards never really feel rewarding because the only place you can upgrade is in town and you need both enough EXP and a token to do so.I don't think the game overall plays -terribly-, it's competent enough for this kind of action platformer, and there's fun to be had here, and the game is of a satisfying enough length, but the real appeal of this ends up lying mostly in its aesthetics at the end of the day, and it's maybe a bit light on content to justify a $20 price tag, as well. Again, a meh review with a slight positive lean despite how much I've criticized it, but you can do much better in the genre, too.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fine, but it has room for growth in pretty much every department. Visuals are great. Areas are varied and beautiful. Characters design is great as well. The music is bland though. The only song I remember is the one from the trailer. It's subjective of course, but it's my review, so....The story is nothing. It practically do not exist until the end. You spend 90% of the game with just 3 characters: One of them do not talk much, the other do not talk at all, and the last one could be removed with no harm to the story.This game is basically Ori. It's a metroidvania, but your progression is fairly linear. There is combat, but the main focus is on the movement and platforming. Enemies are functionally moving obstacles that you should try to avoid rather than fight. The problem is that Ori is better than this game in almost every aspect.The gameplay is very easy and boring in its first half. There is nothing to explore. The only stuff you can find are hp upgrades,,, and the game is already too easy. The levels are primarily long corridors. The enemy variety is lacking and yet the game ctrl+c/ctrl+v some of them. The bosses are boring and easy. Your move set is very basic until later into the game.Controls are stiff: you move faster or slower than you expect, rolls work incorrectly on slopes, your swings stop your momentum when you're on the ground, but not when in the air, your axe throw stops your momentum as well, the list keeps going. Also why crouch is in the game? Also why stamina is in the game? Also why backtracking is in the game? Like I said the game has a room for growth.Yet, despite all of what I said, I still recommend this game. It's not straight up bad, the game is fine. You can play it for visuals alone if you like them. It just takes too long for the game to start being complex and fun to play. But in the last two or three areas the game does just that...The level design gets solid. The complete move set is fun to use. The platforming and combat get a bit challenging. The bosses are... at least feel like bosses unlike what was before. Especially the 4th guardian (had big Hollow Knight vibes). She was a lot of fun, but only because I decided not to use healing, seriously, the game has problems with hp. So yeah, the last half of the game was enjoyable. But everything until that was boring. I wish developers got latter areas and made them into early ones and build on that foundation.Just my suggestions:If your game is about platforming make controls just right. You shouldn't lose momentum for no good reason either. The most fun I had was to try sprinting through the levels without a halt (except the stamina bar was preventing it, delete it please). If you make a metroidvania then give us a reason to explore. Add more systems for your progression, this way there will be always something to find.Your move set is solid, but still a bit basic. You need something unique and creative, something that will steal the show. Bosses' move set was too shallow and boring. Give them more interesting complex moves, not just gimmicky stuff. The last 2 bosses were good, they should be the base line.Make more enemies as well, even if they're not the main focus. This way the game will feel more varied.Can't really give any suggestions about the story, sorry.I hope this will help devs when they read it... Your game is good.
_childDocuments_.name: ITORAH

_childDocuments_.review: I would 100% recommend this game to anyone who is looking for a casual yet challenging game involving exploration and platformer. Loving the game so far!! Colorful vibrant world and visuals. Although I felt like the jumps are a little floaty. It is a platformer after all and I have no idea how to explain it with words( this is neither a complaint nor an issue, just my thought on what I felt) Enjoying the game. Hoping to see more games from the same team.
_childDocuments_.name: ITORAH

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, the polish.  Super tight controls and some excellent story telling going on already. Brings back memories of both Dust and Bastion, but only in terms of quality as it's totally its own thing otherwise.  After just over hour I can tell I'm definitely going to go for 100% on this one.  Very forgiving so far but I wouldn't be surprised if it destroys me later on, and I think I'll be fine with that.
_childDocuments_.name: ITORAH

_childDocuments_.review: My full review: This is a beautiful 2d platformer, with just a dash of Metroidvania elements thrown in. Overall, a pretty fun game! The controls can feel a little stiff compared to other platformers, but it's nothing you won't get used to (though I still don't entirely feel comfortable with the dodge mechanic yet).The beginning of the game, you're thrown into this spider lair area and it's a great showcase of the dungeons you'll find in the game. However, the land of the overworld is a different story. Some of the land feels a bit too big and sparse where I think there is just too much land/ground to cover versus events/secrets to experience. You'll run through long stretches of platforming where nothing super challenging or eventful happens (and none of the few secret areas seem to matter), which is odd, considering the first half hour of the game is a great introduction.The dungeons are where the game truly shines though. Where you can tell the team focused their energy on creating events, chase scenes and challenges. By the time you reach the 2nd dungeon type setting, which you'll see in the video, If you don't mind a little slog in between dungeons, I think you'll dig this.
_childDocuments_.name: ITORAH

_childDocuments_.review:
Guide Itorah through a fantastic world inhabited by strange masked beings.

Mankind has vanished and Itorah seems to be the last of her kind! To uncover her past she will have to pick up her loud-mouthed axe and fight her way through lush forests, dangerous temples, stormy cliffs and more hand-painted biomes.

Their innocent quest for knowledge quickly turns into a mission to save this strange new world from its biggest threat: A mysterious plague that threatens to consume everything.

name: Sisters Royale: Five Sisters Under Fire
detailed_description: The first new game in 12 years from Alfa System, the team that brought you.the Shoot 'Em Up 'Castle of Shikigami III' in the 'Castle of Shikigami' series. Five uniquely talented sisters are squabbling over which of them will marry the angel Yashin. Enjoy the heroic(?) strategies of all five! The Tension Bonus System (TBS) means your score and number of coins multiplies based on your distance from enemies and their attacks, and the Powershot System changes normal attacks into strong attacks, further ramping up the tension! Plus, once the TBS has multiplied by two within a certain time, Secret Fairies will be hidden somewhere in stages for you to find. Master these systems and set new high scores!

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the chibi mobile bait fool you, this game is solid.It's essentially Shikigami no Shiro 4 in all but name.Sonay=Kohtaro, Selma=Kim, Ece=Emilio, Nur=Sayo, Lale=Niigi, and Ode=Fumiko.The game is extremely approachable for newcomers, since its difficulty isn't too bad and gives you tons of resources to brute force your way through. The real game is in score play, as 90% of its design and different character playstyles is based around this, so get grazing and push those bosses into overtime.Ode (Fumiko) is still best girl.
_childDocuments_.name: Sisters Royale: Five Sisters Under Fire

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played this for a few minutes, but there aren't any reviews so I'm going to leave one.  It's a STG from the creators of the Shikigami no Shiro series.  Much like Shikigami no Shiro, Sisters Royale employs a grazing based score/shot power system.  The more you hug bullets the better.  Give it a try if you're into that sort of shmup.
_childDocuments_.name: Sisters Royale: Five Sisters Under Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Really great intro bullet hell for those interested in the genre. Great character variety, a scoring system that is simple yet satisfying, a solid training mode, and loads of game-modifier options that let you customize how the game plays. Sisters Royale doesn't do anything too crazy or unique but what it does do it does well.(Playtime listed isn't entirely accurate, been playing since the JP release on Switch. Just saw it had few reviews and wanted to help correct that.)
_childDocuments_.name: Sisters Royale: Five Sisters Under Fire

_childDocuments_.review: This is the sort of shmup that looks really hard, but it actually isn't so bad. Although there are a lot of bullets onscreen, the patterns are easy to understand and avoid. Dodging them feels good!The various characters feel different, and trying out new ones is fun. The scoring system has a lot of complexity, but it isn't too hard to figure out. It really rewards risky behavior, but scoring also earns lives and bombs, so going for a high score helps with survival too.
_childDocuments_.name: Sisters Royale: Five Sisters Under Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Fun shmup by the developers of Castle of Shikigami. Very accessible to beginners and quite generous with resources, depending on how willing you are to score. The scoring system, mostly based on grazing, is very fun to engage in and causes different characters, who have very unconventional and distinct moves, to be rewarded for wildly different playstyles.That all being said, I don't see myself playing it for much longer because it doesn't feel as exciting as I've come to expect from shmups, especially of the bullet hell variety. The slow scrolling, goofy music and cute artstyle don't exactly build a lot of the tension and thrill of other bullet hells. Overall I'd say it's a good and well done game, but it's not very exciting.
_childDocuments_.name: Sisters Royale: Five Sisters Under Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Reviewing for J-Indie Arcade, Sisters Royale is a vertical bullet hell STG from veteran indie dev AlfaSystem that features detailed visuals and a wide range of playable characters more than the average game in the genre.Stages are short and sweet, meant more to sap your resources or build chains as a prelude to the bosses. The bosses themselves offer familiar danmaku patterns that fit the characters' personalities.The real reason I recommend this game is the wide range of playable characters. each of them has a unique bullet pattern, unique summon attack and unique bomb attack. The real challenge of the game is learning the capabilities and weaknesses of your own character's abilities and taking them through the stages and bosses which will quickly become familiar but must be approached differently for each character. It really makes the ♥♥♥♥-talk in the cutscenes between everybody hit a lot harder.
_childDocuments_.name: Sisters Royale: Five Sisters Under Fire

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun shmup by the developers of the Castle Shikigami series. Graze bullets, shoot everything with your secondary shot, have fun. Easy mode feels like a good difficulty mode for people who are brand new to the genre, especially if you pick Sonay (the beginner character).As a more experienced player I felt like the gameplay was a bit on the bland side at first, but I immediately starting enjoying the game so much more when I moved away from Sonay and tried out the other characters. There's a huge difference between just sitting at the back of the screen playing Sonay for survival, and aggressively speedkilling enemy waves and milking bosses as the other characters. So I highly recommend picking Sonay if you're new, and I highly recommend trying the other characters as soon as you get bored.Playing for score makes the game much more interesting too. It really encourages you to get aggressive, speedkill as many enemies as possible and milk lucrative boss phases, all while constantly grazing bullets. The game really is as simple or as complicated as you want it to be.Here's my hard mode 1CC as Ece:My least favorite thing about the game is the environmental gimmicks, but at least they can be routed around to an extent. Wind only applies when you stop holding a direction, so you can ignore it by moving through it without stopping or by pushing against the bottom edge of the screen and moving left and right with diagonal inputs. Ice...appears early enough in the game that you can just bomb through it and earn more bombs afterwards. It's not ideal but it doesn't ruin the game for me.Anyway, I recommend giving it a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Sisters Royale: Five Sisters Under Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little bullet hell dating simulator where the boss fights are your romantic rivals? Pretty good shmup with a cute cast and catchy tunes and great game play! But what sets this apart is the zany story lines of each character, such a hoot! NOTE: THIS IS NOT A MOBILE GAME, its really solid and its meant for a gamepad/fightstick/KB, not one of those touch screen ports.
_childDocuments_.name: Sisters Royale: Five Sisters Under Fire

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game on the Nintendo Switch, and I absolutely love it. If you're into bullet hell shmups, this game is a must buy! The game is very forgiving if your bad at video games. The stages and bosses are pretty short, it's a game that respects your time and is priced accordingly. I love it! I've never played Castle of Shikigami, but I did love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Sisters Royale: Five Sisters Under Fire

_childDocuments_.review: This game is nice and has a cute PSP style (not in a bad way) and I like the idea of having a "walking character shoot'em up" (basically like Ikari Warriors but with an auto-walk or a top-down Chelnov/Atomic Runner) where you get environmental elements that are either fans that pushes you or slippery ice which makes bullet dodging harder (but is very unbalanced when playing purely for the score).The story is silly but it is a nice change to see that all of the protagonists are both bosses and playable (albeit the last one). But I consider it inferior to Castle Shikigami 2 and 3 (while still being better than the first). I just hope we get a sequel that fixes some of the issues and improves upon this game and that we'll finally get the third Shiro on Steam very soon.Tl;Dr get the game in sales.
_childDocuments_.name: Sisters Royale: Five Sisters Under Fire

_childDocuments_.review: It's cute and fun, however: 1) You will need to manually cap your own gpu's framerate at 60fps via Control Panel, or the game runs way too fast- this should not happen in a release in 2021. 2) The maximum resolution is 1080p, so get ready for a blurry fullscreen, or tiny windowed mode...can the developer please add higher resolution options? 3) There are a lot of grammar errors. 4) Some of the 2D art work isn't of the greatest quality in my opinion, there's something a little off/rough about the way the characters are drawn. But as I said, it's cute, and the gameplay is a lot of fun, so I would still recommend it overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Sisters Royale: Five Sisters Under Fire

_childDocuments_.review: When I first purchased this game, I was very new to shmups in general, having only real experience with Touhou. I was surprised to see so many recommendations for this title considering it seems to do pretty much everything I've now been taught is terrible within the genre: momentum based stage gimmicks, visual obscuration, do-nothing enemies that come in predictable blobs, uninspired scenery and samey music, etc. etc... All of that not mentioning the technical side of things, which is for some reason a rule in shmups, where rebinding the controls or even getting the game to recognize your controller properly is a feat in and of itself. For some reason the 'skip cutscene' key is also hidden and not able to be rebound, so have fun hunting around for that.Aside from the cast of the characters and their portraits being somewhat interesting, the story is as meaningless as you'd expect it to be, and none of the bosses stand out in terms of mechanics or patterns. I will say that the grazing mechanic which powers up your shots when you're close to a bullet is cool, but it's not enough on its own to redeem what is otherwise a lukewarm flop of a game. Gave it more than a few tries, but it just doesn't hold up to other stand-outs in the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Sisters Royale: Five Sisters Under Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Hmm. On the one hand it's basically Shikigami No Shiro 4, which is good, on the other it's chock full of stupid loli waifus (pro tip game devs: women actually play these games too!) and cheap deaths (some bullets can't be seen against certain backgrounds. The frozen level's a bit cheap too.Meh. I got a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a shmup beginner and not enjoying this one. So, long story short, PICK THIS UP IF ONE OF THE FOLLOWING IS TRUE:1) you already played its spiritual predecessors, Castle Shikigami, to death. Castle Shikigami 2, a classic, is easily available on Steam or on PS2/GameCube if you prefer to play an older version. 2) You somehow love the aesthetic (more power to ya)3) You are hardcore into shmups and need something quality to play I originally got Sisters Royale because I thought the game would be more accessible and lighthearted, but idk, I'm not a fan of the visuals at all. The harem anime thing is funny but not my style either. Music is good, score system is fun and "juicy," but idk everything just looks so bland and cheap. I've played sparse shmups but this game is kind of just an eyesore with its saturated colors. Idk if it's just me, but I also felt like my character's hit box didn't have that razor sharp clarity it does in the Shikigami seriesAlso as a bonus I wanted to play this on my old potato laptop and it struggled, where older shmups seemed to run just fine. Kind of disappointing

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great entry into Castle of Shikigami. I find it a lot more approachable. I highly recommend this to shmup fans and shiki fans, but also to people who generally aren't into shmups, because the character variety of this game (and the Castle of Shikigami series, of which it is a spiritual successor) leads to very different playstyles compared to "usual" shmups and bullet hells.

_childDocuments_.review: Basicaly it is castle of shikigami 3. The game is good, the music and graphics are good. They look like a premium mobile game with big and cutsy characters, bright colors like a casino. The bullet visibility is good (ememy bullets change color) but  could be better. some bullet colors could contrast more with the background.  The game is certainly superior to cs1, but inferior to cs2. It has some stage gimicks that are original (ice, lamps, etc) t but i don´t find amusing.There is also many characters to choose that have different mechanics from eac hother and adds replayabilty to the game.  It is a original game and it is a pitty that this mechanics are not used in other games outside the series.  The dificulty on normal setting is easier than previous entryes but not a walk in the park. It is a underrated shmup and i Strongly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Sisters Royale: Five Sisters Under Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Never played a Castle Shikigami game but if they're half as good as this one then I really ought to correct that. After 9324837924628687 hours spent on 2hu and Mushihimesama the dodging isn't too terribly hard but where the game excels is in getting you to confront danger; being close to enemies and bullets multiplies both the coins dropped and the score you gain from them upon collection by up to x8. The score difference between cowering at the bottom of the screen and cruising at the top near all the bullets can be as much as 2 or 3 entire digits at the end of your big number, and you're gonna need some big numbers to get extends. Extends happen to be as valuable as gold when your health bar is shorter than a dust mite, which keeps the game's balance of risk and reward super duper satisfying. Despite its lack of sheer hair-ripping difficulty in the actual dodging you're kept very much on edge by the fact it only takes 3 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in close proximity to lose the run altogether. Thoroughly recommended for shmup newbies and autists alike.

name: CHRONO CROSS: THE RADICAL DREAMERS EDITION
detailed_description: Reviews & Accolades 'Excellent' - GAMINGBible 'A legendary RPG' 85/100 - Hobbyconsolas_com '…one of the best JRPGs of all time' 10/10 - Siliconera 'a must-play game' 9/10 - Noisy Pixel '...the preservation of two important moments in gaming history...' 4/5 - Screen Rant 'The return of a timeless work.' 80/100 About the Game 'CHRONO CROSS: THE RADICAL DREAMERS EDITION' is a remaster of 'CHRONO CROSS'. The 3D models have been upgraded to HD, new illustrations have been added, and all kinds of new features are now included. Additionally, the game that formed the bedrock of the story, 'RADICAL DREAMERS - Le Trésor Interdit -', is included in this edition! CHRONO CROSS is an RPG that transcends time and space, unfolding across two interlinked parallel worlds. With over 40 party members to meet, people and dimensions will intertwine in this epic drama about the planet itself. Utilising an innovative turn-based style battle system, CHRONO CROSS is a unique RPG that follows the protagonist “Serge” as he crosses time on his quest to save himself dying in a parallel universe. Those who purchase the game will also receive a CHRONO CROSS wallpaper! New Features in the Remastered Edition ・3D models converted to HD ・Refined character illustrations ・Higher-quality background music ・Switch enemy encounters on or off ・Background filter feature ・Battle enhancement features to make combat easier ・Auto-battle function ・Switch between imitation pixel font and HD font ・Change screen resolution RADICAL DREAMERS - Le Trésor Interdit - 'RADICAL DREAMERS - Le Trésor Interdit -' was released in 1996 as a standalone game, and has not been easily accesible for play in recent years. Players can experience the story that went on to become the basis for CHRONO CROSS in an audio novel format. Here, an alternate story of the RADICAL DREAMERS, a group of three thieves - Serge, Kid and Magil - unfolds in a parallel world. *You can switch between the new and old versions of the 3D models and illustrations. *The 3D models, illustrations, font and background filter cannot be toggled separately. They will all be switched together.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I think people expect too much sometimes, but to each their own. I am a regular critic of SE and some of their greedy practices, but this isn't nearly as bad, in my opinion, as some other "remasters". As a long time fan of this title, there's gonna be some bias, but I think its fine for a release day product. Does it have some frame rate issues? Yes. Are they as egregious as some seem to make them out to be? Personally I don't think so (and yes my experience may be vastly different than that of other systems). At the least, I expect a Square remaster to be the base game with some added features and fidelity. This product checks both boxes. So for those simple asks and the relatively low price, its a recommend from me. I will still look forward to them addressing issues, making this the best possible product it can be, but until then will continue to enjoy what I have.

_childDocuments_.review: -GREAT GAME WITH AN EASY FIX TO THE LAG-Don't let the negative reviews stop you from getting this. People seem to review bomb when there are easy fixes to things.Yes, Squenix messed up a few things and a PS games lags on a Killer PC, but there is an easy fix.If you're using a controller, Press the Left D-Pad in and LT at the same time, that will bring up the in-game audio/video menu.Go under VideoGo down to Anti-Aliasing (Post Filter)Turn it offThat Should fix it for you, if not one more thing you can do, another person posted. If you have Nvidia, go under you Nvidia Settings.3D SettingManage 3D settings-Max frame Rate 60-120 FPS--Triple Buffering On--Vertical Sync ON-Both these fixes have improved gameplay greatly and it runs like it should.This game is a classic and tells an amazing, rich story, The characters are incredible and all have unique personalities.They don't make games like this anymore.Don't let a bit of fixable lag stop you from playing.Hopefully Squenix will fix this properly, but until then don't give up on this great game.

_childDocuments_.review: The mechanics and story get better as it progresses so anyone who might initially be disappointed that it is not quite like chrono trigger, at about half way through the story it links more to chrono trigger and it actually ends up a more complex story. Also as there isn't an MP system as such it makes regular battles more interesting as you're not just saving up MP for boss battles. Nevertheless I would say that the characters don't quite have the charm of the chrono trigger ones, although that is partly because of the much larger cast with about half of them being some form of joke characters.Generally an accessible and not particularly difficult game (although there a couple of bosses that are a bit more challenging). A gorgeous soundtrack is another plus.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the way I think of it, the game is $20, so you're gonna get $20 effort put into it. This is a full fledged game that will suck up hours of your time especially if you are trying to obtain all the characters, and endings. Not to mentioned this comes with the elusive Radical Dreamers Audio Novel. The story of Chrono Cross starts off a bit slow like most JRPGs but it starts to kick off when you get closer to ACT II. The game adds a feature where you can avoid all side battles, the reason I say "side" is due tot he fact there are no random battles. All enemies are out in the open, and you will only trigger a fight if you run into them, or if they come after you.Also they added a feature, named "battle boost" where all your characters instantly gain 100% evasion, and everything misses. So if you just want to go through and get the story in, (or you are that grind to get the endings done) you can just turn on both those settings, and zip through the game. I rarely use them, but I find them helpful when trying to get done with a puzzle area, or an area that tends to get on your nerves... come on, we all have those areas of games we loath!They also have a speed up and slow down time function, and unlike the emulators out there, this feature doesn't effect the play timer. However it does not help with load times since it only effects the game, not the actual hardware your system is running on.I have also been enjoying the updated character portraits, and updated character models. Now in regards to the Censorship, and everything, we only have ourselves to blame for that, and the world we live in now. Can't blame them for the world being too sensitive. Things were different back then.For $20 this game is worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: CHRONO CROSS: THE RADICAL DREAMERS EDITION

_childDocuments_.review: Simply put, the game itself is awesome.The story line is A+ Battle mechanics A+Replayability A+Nostalgia A++As a port, they really could have done better.I haven't run into any frame rate issues like others, although there has been screen tearing and the sound will clip sometimes.You can tell they've upscaled the backgrounds using AI, and its fine.The new 3D objects look way better than emulated versions I've run before.The speed up mechanic is great for when you are trying to get rare drops, like when trying to get the moon glasses.The negative reviews are way over the top. So take them with a grain of salt and the understanding that gamers are a fickle bunch.Would I have liked it to be more stable? Yes. But I also want this game completely redone from the ground up using modern graphics. I'd gladly pay the $60 price tag for it.PSSST! SQUARE! GIVE US CHRONO BREAK!
