_childDocuments_.review: A passable port of a classic game.Port features are minimal, but it has a few. Visual improvements like better framerate, higher res assets, antialiasing. A fast forward toggle to reduce monotony. A no encounter toggle if you're just exploring.The game really is better than I remember it. When I first played it, I bought it on the day of its North American release, I was 14 and hyped out of my mind that Chrono Trigger was getting a sequel. I was somewhat disappointed because, this is not a true sequel, it barely references Chrono Trigger.Today I'm able to take it as its own game. This does have a fairly charming plot and characters, amazing music, and fabulous character art and scenery. The combat is interesting, though there are some deviations from normal JRPG formula that one might find detrimental - level ups are gated behind story progression, there's no MP and magic has a weird system, all weapons and armor require crafting.While the character art is amazing, character development is not, many characters get two lines of dialogue, then they join you and that's it. There's a lot of weird fruity characters, like little pink blobs that would probably have annoying high pitched voices if the game had VO, a j-rocker who fights with a guitar, a guy that fights with a fishing pole, and on and on. All lines they say during story are generic dialogue run through a script that alters the text with word replacements to make it seem like the character is using their particular accent, dialect, etc. but essentially, they're all just saying the same stuff. It's a neat idea at least.The game's 40 something characters can't be acquired in a single playthrough and instead you get a new game+ feature, and eventually you can recruit characters acquired in previous runs. The whole game is one big mess of missable not-so-obvious interactions and event scriptings, backtracking and going places other than where you're told to go is heavily rewarded, so...play with a guide or experience 30% of the content. Google for "Chrono Cross walkthrough" and find yourself a gamefaqs page.

_childDocuments_.review: Chrono Cross is a great game, and if this is the only way you have to play it then... it is passable. But, as both a port and a remaster, it falls quite short. The modding community has created better remasters through fan-made content. And, if you want the original graphical experience, then this era of game looks a LOT better on original hardware with a CRT TV.This version has performance issues and poorly AI upscaled textures. It is running in an emulator and uses scripts to do some swaps on models and textures. This extra processing causes the frame-rate to drop quite significantly in some places, and does not appear to be fully overcome no matter the GPU used. Fan-made projects for the original game have produced much better visual quality and performance for the game using these same methods. The 'original' graphics mode has less issues, but still has some frame drop when compared to the PS1 release.Additionally, this game has been hit with censorship in a few places. I am only aware of one graphical change, but there were several changes to dialog. The changes seem so unnecessary, that it appears someone was trying to justify their job. Unfortunately, that is what you get when it is someone's task to find 'problems'.At the end of the day, the primary perk of this version is convenience. It is on Steam and current generation consoles. It is $20. That's all it really comes down to. But, here is a full break down of what this remaster has to offer over the original:Good Updates:-New character portraits look great-New character models are good-Ability to swap to old graphics-Includes the text-based game Radical Dreamers, previously exclusive to Japan on the Super Famicom through the Satellaview.-Some new art and music were made, which are used in the launcher.Bad Updates:-Inconsistent frame-rate, especially in the updated graphical mode. -Quality of AI upscaled backgrounds is poor. Very bad in some places, with significant artifacting.-There have been several reported stability issues. I did not run into them, but enough people have reported them that buyers should be aware.-When swapping to 'original' graphics mode, it renders 3d at a higher resolution than the original. This results in having pixelated background, but very smooth model renders. It clashes badly, especially in combat sections.-At least 1 instance of graphical censorship.-Multiple instances of text/dialog censorship have been identified for both English and Japanese settings.Even disregarding the technical issues and unnecessary censorship, this is a very lazy 'remaster'. When it comes to modern remasters, I expect at least some of the following:-60 FPS-Widescreen-Menu Updates-New end game content-Runs in native environment. Not emulated.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing games for a long time and one of my favorite JRPGs of the PS1 era is Chrono Cross. I've played and replayed it so many times for its great story, vast playable cast of characters, and fantastic gameplay. When RD Edition was announced, I was super excited to play it and grab it ASAP. I played it on stream with an old friend and was happy that it was just like playing the PSX version...and that's the problem.You play as Serge. The opening of the game has you playing through a dream sequence where you are hunting someone named Lynx. Upon exploring this strange dungeon, you reach the top and it ends with you killing a woman who was in your party. When you wake up, you are sent on an errand to collect seashells for your childhood friend/girlfriend. Once you're on the beach and talking to her, Serge passes out and finds himself in an alternate world where he no longer exists. What happened? How'd he get here? And can he find his way back home?For those who have not played Chrono Cross, it is a turn-based RPG  that has an interesting combat system. You have a stamina bar that works off of three types of attack, light, medium, and heavy. Each one will have a percentage of how likely you can hit the enemy and deal damage. While doing this, each successful hit will give you access to your element grid. This is where your spells and abilities come into play. While the grid starts small, it expands as you defeat bosses. It's a lil complicated at first, but as you play it, it starts to make sense. Like classic RPGs, there are elemental weaknesses as well as innate color weaknesses. Each party member is an elemental color and so when facing enemies with the opposing color, you'll deal more damage.Speaking of party members, this was one of the biggest draws of Chrono Cross. There are tons of party members you can recruit into your party. You can only battle with up to three party members but the number is ridiculously high. Each member has their own special moves and animations of attacking which made it so fun to try and get as many as you can. For some of the more obscure ones, you'll have to find certain items or do certain side quests to get them which is one of the reasons I replayed this game a lot as a kid. Unfortunately, many of them don't really matter to the overall plot of the story so aside from a throwaway line or two, you won't see them really interact when big story beats go down.Now speaking from someone who has played Chrono Cross for many years I will say that in most of the other reviews I have seen, I have to agree with them. This Radical Dreamers Edition doesn't really do enough to warrant any real hype. Yes, the character sprites do look better. Yes, they did update the pictures for the dialogue boxes and made the text look smoother. And yes, they did add a fast-forward button as well as some cheat buttons in case you want to bypass some hard bosses and skip lengthy magic spells. But, the game still feels slow and not that polished. I dare say you could get better quality from an emulator. IF, however, you have never played Chrono Cross before, then this is a perfect way to play the game. I only believe that the gripes I have with this game are there because I have played this so many times in the past and I was hoping for more from this port. Having the Radical Dreamers visual novel is nice and all, but, playing this still makes me feel like I'm playing on an old PSX. It has the same laggy feel and old jank as it did in the classic version and that's just disappointing.Final verdict? If you have never played Chrono Cross before and want to experience an amazing classic JRPG, I recommend this game. If you have played it before and, like me, were expecting a nice update to the classic, you're seriously better off just playing an emulated version that can truly upscale everything. Don't get me wrong, it's nice to be able to play Chrono Cross again on my PC, but this port deserved more work on it. Thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: Don't listen to the naysayers, many of them are just review bombers mad that the game isn't exactly what they demanded in every little way and unwilling to admit that any problems running it might be due to their system setup and whatever other programs they have open rather than the game itself. Many others, however, myself included, have had little to no trouble running the game and have been enjoying it just fine. Screen tearing and framerate issues can be fixed in the Nvidia panel (for those of you who have a GeForce card) and likely in the similar panels for other graphics cards.CC: RDE is a great way to rediscover this classic without the hassle of configuring an emulator and comes with extra content, features, and an enhanced soundtrack that the original version simply doesn't have. _childDocuments_.review: So I am going to start out by saying my PC specs, so that people know exactly what I am working with in regards to this review:GPU: NVIDIA GEFORCE RTX 3070RAM: 16GBProcessor: 3.6GHz Intel Core i7-11700KFMem: 1TB SSDI have played emulated versions in the past. I have played the OG release (just last week actually, so I had a good understanding of what state it was in back then and to compare to now), and I can say without a doubt, this is a disappointing "Remaster".While yes my time in this remaster is limited so far, the first 20-30 minutes is already giving me red flags on how the rest of the game is going to perform, especially since the game gets more "intense" as the storyline progresses, which makes me concerned at this current time.Let's start with a few good points with this:-  They are great looking. If you take a side-by-side of the old ones and compare to the new ones, it is night and day. The characters look more human, their faces don't look as "squished" as in the OG, and barring a few model issues (such as hands being attached to incorrect parts of the body, which is especially apparent with Miki's right hand and the ring it is attached to. Pay attention to it during her idle animation in combat and you will see what I mean-  Whoever redid the portraits for all the characters should get a big pat on the back, because they look great! I love them and don't really have an issue so far, based on what I have seen.-  It's nothing to really write home about, however it does at least modernise well enough in comparison to the old version, which of course was more pixelated due to the hardware at the time it was made.Now, I sadly have to list the cons of this Remaster-  Yes, this is something that cannot be made to upscale up to 60FPS or anything crazy like that, due to the time the game was made, however what I find most egregious, is the stuttering during both walking and running animations. I think the real issue with the FPS, is that due to the stuttering from movement, it makes the game FEEL like it has less frames, when it's really a visual issue with the game and not so much the FPS itself. It is an extremely noticeable visual issue and will no doubt prove to be extremely annoying as you try to play for more than a few hours. It just makes the game feel extremely buggy and is an overall unenjoyable thing to witness, even when you switch to the OG version that is, thankfully, included with this release.-  I didn't really think this would be a problem for me at first. But the more I looked at them, the more I was disheartened by the apparent lack of care devoted to the backgrounds. These are what make the world up. If they don't look good, the world is cheapened by it. It is very noticeable to me that they simply plopped each background into a Upscaler AI and called it a day. If you want an example of CORRECT up-scaling of old PS1 backgrounds, look up the "The Legend of Dragoon Upscale Project" on YouTube, because THAT is how you do an upscale. I won't say it was the devs fault on this release, because this says to me, more than anything, that Square Enix had maybe 1 or 2 employees "working" on the backgrounds and on a time crunch to push this out ASAP, so they had to do what they could to keep the pipeline moving and Upscaler UI was the solution.However with all that in mind, they just don't look good. They look muddy and washed out, and even LOSE details. A Remaster is meant to improve a title, not take 2 steps back and that is what has happened here. Seriously, go compare the old graphics to the new ones and you will see what I mean. (I really wish I could post screenshots in reviews on Steam, because they would help emphasise my previous points).-  I think this needs to be stated separately, because outside of combat is one thing, but the main part of the game that the player will also see, is in-combat. And sadly, the clunkiness continues here and, in some cases, is even worse. Now I could excuse this if you decided to play the OG version, because that is what was there on release and you can't change that. However the fact new models are in the game, means that they could have taken the steps necessary to make combat animations much smoother. Sadly, it is apparent in even the very first fight in the game, that was not what they decided to do. I can almost certainly say they took the new models, attached them to the old skeletons for them (with a few tweaks to make nothing un-playably broken) and called it a day.- I wanted to play this and safely say that the critical reviews were BS or even just down to people's hardware, however I have to agree with them for the most part. This is a pretty shoddy attempt at what I would even hesitate to call a remaster and more of "Slightly Enhanced" version of the OG game. While I love the new models and portraits (I cannot comment on the OST as of yet, since that requires a deeper dive I have yet to still do), I cannot say this "Remaster", in it's current state, is worth the asking price. However if you REALLY want to have everything Chrono Cross, I wish you the best of luck and hope you enjoy what is here.

_childDocuments_.review: Chrono Cross has been one of my favorite games since it first came out in the States, and even in 20+ years that hasn't changed, so I can't profess to offering an impartial review. That said, while this is pretty much a straight 1:1 upscaled port of the original, the ability to play it again at all is worth the price, and being able to share it with friends in countries where it was never released is genuinely wonderful.SPOILERS BELOW!This is a port of a PS1 game, and I think people playing it need to keep that in mind to temper their expectations. It's not like the multiple Chrono Trigger rereleases that included extra cutscenes, boss battles, content and alternate endings—Chrono Cross has always been the less-loved of the two, and that unfortunately shows here quite dramatically. That's a disappointment to be sure, but considering it's been over 20 years since they did literally anything with the title, it's no surprise. There is a secret alternate "ending" that's accessible via the credits in the launcher after completing both Chrono Cross and Radical Dreamers at least once, but that's more extra content for Radical Dreamers than it is for Chrono Cross. There are a few corrections to the translation (a particular ghost now uses the words "no longer alive in this TIMELINE" instead of "no longer alive in this WORLD," which clarifies something people have been complaining about for decades), and the mixing up of names during the second act is finally fixed (the majority of other party members no longer refer to Serge as "Lynx" during the bodyswap except at plot-relevant points), which is honestly more than I ever could have hoped for in a simple port like this.Allowing access to the Time Shifter from jump is a nice touch for people who want to get through the more grind-heavy portions of the game a little faster (I usually use it when running across maps or when a character I don't care about starts a monologue), and the inclusion of what basically amounts to an invincibility toggle is also nice for people who want to experience the storyline without getting stuck in battle too often. Overall they're excellent quality of life improvements, and I'm glad they were implemented.Finally getting a chance to go through Radical Dreamers is also exciting, I don't recommend it for people who don't know the storyline of Chrono Trigger. While Cross can be played without knowledge of Trigger thanks to the extensive monologues mentioned above, Radical Dreamers really can't, so keep that in mind. (Trigger has been rereleased like a dozen times, though, so it's fine.) I'm on the fence over whether it's best played before or after Cross, although I obviously played it after considering I played Cross on initial PS1 release when I was a literal child.Overall I still love this game and I'm thrilled that it's been rereleased for a new generation—with the hope that people realize that it's a product of its time and that this is not a REMAKE. Nobody complained about Chrono Trigger's multiple rereleases still being in pixel graphics and having a terrible translation (it's never been fixed to this day), so I don't see why Chrono Cross is getting the third degree for being a prettied up PS1 game that still acts like a PS1 game. It's a classic late-90s/early aughts JRPG, and it behaves like it. Enjoy it for what it is instead of going in looking for the things you know it's not.

_childDocuments_.review: Edited since last patch to a posisitive review, the world map still looks like crap on a 4k screen but at least the frame rate is no longer vomit inducing. _childDocuments_.review: It's Chrono Cross. What more needs to be said?Personally, I don't get all the complaining about it being a bad port or about censorship. Let's run down a few things:- The only platforms this game is available on without emulation is the PSX original and the PSN digital version that works on PS3, PSP, and Vita. Making this game available at all to modern players who may not (or cannot) turn to emulation is in no uncertain terms a good thing.- It is a no frills package. It's also only $20 and comes with a game that we never received in English before, and even many Japanese players probably didn't get to play. Stop devaluing old games, this is perfectly fine.- There's a lot of talk about the game's poor performance, and... I dunno. I don't see it? The game runs just like I remember it running on PSX and PS3. Are people comparing it to emulation? Because that's an inaccurate comparison.- There's also talk of censorship, which is about the most idiotic thing I can imagine. Here's what was changed: You no longer can look up a 9 year old girl's skirt, and a 20+ year old script was touched up. These are normal things, not censorship. If these were changes imposed forcibly by an outside agency, that might be considered censorship. But this? No, this is normal.Don't let the mixed reviews or whiners dissuade you. This is still the amazing game it always was, with one big addition and a few smaller ones. Enjoy it for what it is: A cheap, modern way to revisit - or play for the first time - a fantastic and legendary PlayStation RPG.

_childDocuments_.review: So many dumb reviews of this game here. This is a perfectly acceptable $20 remaster. Portions of the game's source code and many of its assets have been long lost, so Square did what it could. A remaster is an archival effort, not a remake. It's the game, as you played it on the PS1, with a few updated backgrounds, textures, and bonus tracks + Radical Dreamers, which is honestly worth at least half the cost of entry on its own if you're not from Japan.For those complaining or concerned about the frame rate, I mean, that's how the game looks. It's a PS1 game, the frame rate was like 15-24 fps back then and since this is just the original game it will be bad now. The janky animations are there too, just as you remember. This was a late-cycle PS1 game and the developers probably pushed the system too far. The result is what you see here, bad FPS in fully rendered 3D environments.I just don't understand the complaints. It's like complaining that Super Mario Bros doesn't have widescreen support on the Switch or whatever. This isn't a remake, the problems you're experiencing are just the problems the game has always had.People calling this port "lazy" don't know what that means -- every background and texture have been upscaled and often painstakingly manually redrawn (because again, the original assets no longer exist), Radical Dreamers has a complete localization that has never existed before. This is a remaster and a port. It's not a remake. It's just not!Some actual annoyances: I wish the original OST was available. I wish you could change between old and new graphics without exiting the game (though there are legit technical reasons for this, it's still a little sad). I wish they'd found a way to speed up the transitions a bit.Overall I recommend this. For 20 bucks and given the history of this game's archival issues I'm not sure what y'all were expecting. Chill and enjoy the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Chrono Cross: The Radical Dreamers remasters "Chrono Cross" from the PS1, and Radical Dreamers - which was previously unreleased outside of Japan. Chrono Cross (CC) is a sequel to Chrono Trigger (CT) from the SNES. I have only ever played CT for the SNES and never played the CC on the PS1, so this remaster is my first experience with the game. Radical Dreamers is not a JRPG and plays as a text adventure instead, meaning most of the time you will simply be reading a story with some occasional text prompts requiring you to choose from a list of options. Rather than jump through multiple periods of time throughout the story like in CT, in CC you will be swapping between two parallel versions of the same world. In order to recruit certain party members, complete certain quests, and progress the story will require you to jump between these two alternate worlds. The worlds are pretty similar in most areas, so traveling through time felt more dynamic and interesting in CT. Though there were several choices in CC that led to divergent paths.The story of CC started off strong, but towards the end fell apart as it got too muddled in its own lore. In the last 25% or so the story becomes heavily referential on CT's story/characters. Most of the game has good pacing and storytelling as you are an active participant in the plot. By the end of the game, you are given huge exposition dumps referring to characters, events, & places that you never encounter throughout the game - but they make it integrally woven into the game's story. I hadn't played CT in about 10 years, so I felt I was missing some important context and got a little lost when they big info dumps/references to CT were made. In both CC and CT you control 3 characters in combat. In CT, there are 6 recruitable characters, each one unique and with their own abilities. There were also combo attacks wherein 2-3 party members could unleash a power combo move. In CC, there are 45 party members. While most of them are nowhere near as memorable as any of the cast from CT, I will say the game does a decent job at making them feel unique. When playing through the story, party members will respond in that character's unique syntax - which impressed me because it would have been way easier for the Devs to simply make them all respond generically regardless of the party member, or have them say nothing at all. However, the element system allowing near complete selection of all party members' abilities leads to most of the party members feeling samey. Besides differences in innate element type, and base stats, - each party member only has 3 abilities that are unique to that character. In CT, combat was interesting and required strategically using certain attacks based off of enemy and party positioning, because certain attacks could only hit in certain ways (such as attacking in a straight line, or a full aoe). In CC, there are just single target and aoe abilities that target all enemies for offensive abilities. Instead, CC has you changing the element of the battle field based off of what color element your just cast. There are 6 elements and each one as a direct opposite for which they deal extra damage against (and receives extra damage from). For example, Red/fire elements do extra damage to blue/water element enemies. If you fill the field red by casting fire elements, all red-based attacks do more damage, while all blue-based attacks deal less damage. I found the games difficulty to be very easy. I feel the game's combat tutorial to explain the element system spend a lot of time poorly explaining the system - so for much of my beginning playthrough I poorly understood how to fully take advantage of the combat system. But even then, I still easily go through the game - even when I was incorrectly using my elements. After I understood the system, the game became even more of a cakewalk. The number of challenging battle in this game could probably be counted on one hand - and even then I probably only wiped in battle even less than that. In fact, in one dungeon in the game I added a new party member to my team and forgot to equip him with any gear or elements to use before I found myself in a gauntlet of 2-3 subsequent boss battles that I still won with effectively only 2 out of 3 party members. The remaster comes with updated visuals/graphics, but there is an option in the launcher to use the original visuals instead. As I never played the original on PS1, I did my playthrough with the new graphics. The visuals were beautiful and crisp, which still having that classic/retro feel to it. I feel they did a great job at delivering graphics that look like how you think you remembered PS1 graphics looking like as a kid.The remaster also comes with several quality of life features:*Starting with a "Time Shifter" item that lets you slow down or fast forward gameplay (apparently this was an item that you would normally get on New Game+, but you get it right away).*The ability to turn off random battles (enemies still appear in the world, but touching them does not start combat).*The ability to turn on auto-battling (note: characters only use melee attacks and not elements).*The ability to enhance combat power (party starts with full element power each turn, and all enemy attacks miss them).These quality of life features are great, and I found myself using them quite a bit. As the game was pretty easy, and I did not find the combat too interesting - I found myself using the auto-battler and/or the avoid random battle features a lot. Especially because you only level up after beating certain bosses, I found very little reason to fight trash mobs. And the ability to fast-foward the gameplay was a boon. I found myself having this turned on almost the entire time as this made getting through battles and traveling on the map even faster. Major disclaimer: during my time playing there would be times when the game would randomly freeze: the music would keep playing, but the screen would be frozen and the game would not respond to any inputs from my controller or keyboard. When this happened, the only thing I could do is hard close the game, and reload from my last save. This freeze occurred randomly. I could not find any pattern that led to this happening. Sometimes I could play the game for 2-4 hours straight with no issues at all, while other times it froze and I had to reload my game 3-4 times in about an hour. I noticed this issue on both my Windows PC and my Steam Deck that is still running the base Linux OS. I looked online and I couldn't find anyone that found a fix for this, though some people said using the original PS1 graphics reduces issues.While this issues was very frustrating when it did happen because you could lose a fair amount of gametime from it because there is no way to predict when it will happen. I just made sure I saved every chance I got, and would back track at times to a save point just in case the game would freeze on me. Thankfully the game has the fast forward and battle features, so even if the game did freeze on you after a difficult boss battle, you could simply reload, fast forward, turn on auto-battle, and turn on the enhance battle - and then go AFK  and come back later instead of having to re-fight a difficult fight again. Despite my annoyance with the game freezing on me, and my disappointment with how the game's story declined towards the end, I overall enjoyed CC - even though I still feel CT is the superior game. *CC took me just under 38 hours to beat CC according to the in-game clock.*Radical Dreamers took about 3-3.5 hours complete.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: As of this time, a patch has been released to address the frame rate problems. The game now runs at somewhat inconsistent (20-30) frame rate outside of battle, and a constant 60 while in battle. This isn't ideal, but does make the game playable. With this single change, I would recommend this version of Chrono Cross, as the frame rate was the most unforgivable thing about this port. Keep in mind, however, that it took almost a year for a basic frame rate patch to be released. I have no idea what difficulties the devs had when it came to this patch, but good frame rate is the bare minimum standard that should be demanded of game developers. Whatever issues they had, whatever problems the original code presented, all of that is irrelevant in the year 2022; they easily could have done better.----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Original Review:Chrono Cross released in 1999 for the Playstation. In 2022, we now have the only version of the game officially released on PC, and the game not only performs similarly to how it did on original hardware (meaning mid 10s fps and frequent frame drops and stutters, even in the opening level), its resolution options do not seem to be optimized for modern screen sizes; by default, the game displays in letterbox, and switching to full screen stretches the image, meaning the port, for whatever reason, was not made with full screen in mind. I've seen people say that this isn't a native PC port, and is instead just an emulated version of the PS1 game with some texture re-working, but I don't know how true that is (I've also heard it's running on a custom compatibility layer, similar to WINE, but, again, I don't know how true this is, so take this last sentence with a grain of salt).As a PC release that has been touted as being a "remaster" with updated graphics and improvements, this is absolutely the worst effort that could have been put forth. The updated textures, illustrations, and music are nice touches, but are entirely irrelevant to me. Had this version of the game been released on PC and the only things it had was true fullscreen and smooth 30 fps, I would not be leaving this review, nor would I be refunding my purchase.I'm going to keep my eye on this, as Chrono Cross is one of my favorite JRPGs and I would love to have an officially released PC copy, but I cannot recommend anyone purchase this game in its current state. I have doubts that SE will bother to correct any of the issues the game currently has.

_childDocuments_.review: Chrono Cross was one of my childhood favorites. That being said this is a subpar port. Frame rate issues that really shouldn't exist. The double speed they added doesn't work well as your input is imprecise and run into enemies who gun at you at mach speed. That being said, it is completely playable and I never had any crashes or major issues.The story is has some very interesting concepts. I love the idea of this other world and exploring the different reality. The story starts off pretty light but gets much more complex. The dialogue gets overly verbose and convoluted towards the end.  Serge is a typical OP blank slate main character. You can recruit 40+ characters and that was a cool concept as a kid. Coming back now and it feels like most of the characters aren't worth looking twice at. Once I had my party, I only switched it up mid game after the story forced me to use some other characters. I wish there was a reason to use some more of the playable characters and that more of these recruits had interesting backstories.The gameplay is a nice twist on the turn based style with a stamina system that has a risk reward. You have 1,2, or 3 stamina attacks. The more stamina used the harder you hit, but your accuracy goes down. When you hit, you charge up for elemental attacks. The elements are a system of magic basically and the game explains it well. The biggest issue I had with the combat was that random encounters with basic enemies got annoying - you can run but it still eats up 15 to 20 seconds each time. I did enjoy most of the boss fights as that's where the game was most interesting.I had fun playing Chrono Cross and it is a classic Playstation One JRPG.   I feel like you should play Chrono Trigger first because there are some story elements that tie the games together. Overall, I recommend this game to anyone who has played it before or is looking for an old school turn based JRPG.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't listen to anyone else about this remaster, they're flat out lying about it.Chrono Cross: The Radical Dreamers Edition is the ultimate way to experience the classic from the late 90s. A lot of people have negatively recommended this game saying that it has "framerate issues", but that is really far from the truth. The things they're talking about are things that are hardcoded into the original game, such as certain model animations and the fact that the original camera is pretty jittery because of how early of a game it was. If you have problems with the camera, you can switch to dynamic camera when playing in battles and you always get a smooth 60fps. Please buy this remaster. Everyone deserves to experience one of the best JRPGs ever made and not allow it to be forgotten like it was by countless people when it was a new game. I want the Chrono series to live on and people blatantly lying about the series isn't helping it any.

_childDocuments_.review: Crashed my entire PC while I was trying to adjust settings, par for the Square-enix course.Also: 20+ years of asking for a Chrono Trigger remake, one of Squares most successful titles, only to be met with silence and ports. But its thoroughly reviled sequel, its gross 3/10 weirdo brother gets a graphical remake out of the blue one day. Years of C&D's at fans doors... I dont even have the words, so I am just going to review this stinker:Chrono Cross is one of the worst video game sequels of all time, in the foremost sense of it being a sequel. It is very different beast entirely, in spirit, identity, and focus. Whereas Chrono Trigger focuses on story telling, creating woven and carefully told narratives and plots all well explained and connected to eachother Cross throws around poetic nonsense and hopes that its enough to tide over childlike minds through its lack of explanation throughout everything. This includes many moments such as where the player would need to go next, why they would want to go to said place, and what their end-goal is at any given time. Even the final boss is something you can't really guess at until much later in the game because so much of this game is fumbling around until you hit the random plot-progression spot of the hour.The gameplay of Cross isn't quite a terrible turn-based combat systems but it almost is, heck during some of the low points of the game it is. The dumb tic-tac-toe Elements system makes melee combat mandatory to get spell casting done, turning players away from magic caster-centric characters (each spell can only be cast once per battle btw) and instead going after a meta of chasing down the all-round best ones, not to mention the new and weird level system just doesn't compensate if you want to make your favorite characters all that great, there is no stat maxing and the leveling is weird, vague, and awful. Its low effort design full of micromanaging player stats. Keep in mind, this is the game that went out of its way, to its detriment, to make 100 or so characters recruitable, I don't know why they did it doesn't do this game any favors beyond collectathon nonsense.Music is pretty good for the most part, alot of the good tracks are centered on calming and relaxing vibes. It doesnt blow me away or anything though.The graphical improvement is the absolute definition of mid. Some things look good but others are unintentionally freakishly uncanny. I prefer the fan graphics mod.The plot itself is an incoherent placeholder of a mess, there are just so many times in this game where individual(s) would swing by and present new information or challenge you to a fierce fight or reveal a sort of revelation and you'd expect the protagonist(s) would have something of value to talk about, flavor the conversation up with their take, or even just add something to. If I sound crazy let me say that it feels like 1/3 of the dev team was missing on this one and the creator of Cross is on record as saying that he hates Chrono Trigger, a fitting destiny for him to have made this, much like how its fitting that the sequel to Cross is a very different game with a very different title and being a mobile gacha game, much like how Chrono Trigger is very alien from Chrono Cross. FFX-2 was a faaaarrrr better sequel game, by leaps and bounds. I will maybe mention Radical Dreamers at a later date but such seems like a waste of time to have not been released as widely as Cross wayyy back when Cross was originally released.Edit: Crono died on the Khross for our sins

_childDocuments_.review: There is a lot to like about Chrono CrossThe graphics and art style. It is beautiful. It is impressive that this was on the original PS.The gameplay. The gameplay is well done, in that it doesn’t punish you, in the normal JRPG way, for not knowing what element or moves a boss had before the fight. You can just run away at any time, redo all your moves and go back into the fight. You can also heal really easily, even free, after fights, so no endurance matches. The combat is complicated, but relatively clear. You can do the more complicated parts without a lot of understanding. I do not like how it does the thing where there is something weak against an element, and it punishes you for trying to use the thing its weak against. 'Haha. You used the only strategic element open to you in combat, which is taking advantage of type weakness. Now I am going to do a hugely damaging counter.' This wouldn’t be too bad, but due to the way that enemy attack timing is unclear(it has random attack timing), a lot of the time I didn’t even realise it was doing a counter attack. I thought it was just doing a normal attack.However the story lets it down a huge amount. I appreciate story. It is very important to me. When I say I appreciate it, I don’t mean it has to be serious or dramatic or funny or complex. It can be any type of thing, as long as it is thought through. It should have some emotional resonance. It should be pretty logical. Chrono Cross has a bad story, In the sense that it doesn’t seem particulary clear on what it is about.First, the motivation of the characters. The Main character doesn’t appear to have a motivation. They end up in a situation, but they don’t seem to have an opinion about it. This isn’t necessarily a deal breaker. Many stories have a relatively blank protagonist so that the player themselves can feel or not feel whatever they wish. However, in these situations, there is usually a somewhat apparent course of action. Say, for example, that the bad guy is killing innocent villagers. The main character might not express an opinion, but we can reasonably assume that every player would feel compelled to intervene in that situation. And even if they don’t feel personally compelled, they could atleast believe that most people would feel compelled. However, this doesn’t happen in Chrono Cross. A massive, possibly traumatic, event occurs, but you just kind of go off with no real goal or concern. There is no clear thing to do next. And so you just wander around. But you don’t wander around like an open world, which might make sense. You wander around aimlessly in a very linear manner. As in, you must do things in a certain order according to the story, but why you are doing that and not something else doesn’t really seem clear. And if the things you did served some kind of benefit to your current needs, and not your overall needs, you might also understand why that thing was done. But its just seem arbitrary. This happens within an hour or two. You just don’t seem to have any reason to do anything. But there is a very linear set of events you must do because it is how the story goes.Now, lets assume it makes sense to wander around aimlessly as a single person. In your wanderings, like 50 people decide to follow you on your vague, pointless journey of nothing. It seems you, and so many other people, have nothing better to do in their lives than form a massive group of people that wander around aimlessly. Not only do you wander around aimlessly, but you also don’t even complete the task you are doing at any one time. To make up an example. You want to go for a walk. You bump into someone who wants to get chips, so you both head to get chips. You head to get chips, then you bump into somebody who wants to go surfing. So all three of you decide to go surfing, but when you get to the beach, somebody wants to return a book to the library. So all four of you head to get the book from the guy’s house. After you get the book, his sister wants to get some earrings, so all five of you head to the shops. You just have this vast snowball of people that have things they have a slight interest in achieving, and willingly ignore it in favour of someone else’s vague ideas. And so, by the end, you have 50 people, and you suddenly remember we didn’t get the chips for the first guy, so we go and do that now.It is maddening. Now, this might make a level of sense if kept to one place, but then you have science fiction stuff , where linear time is made much more complicated. I honestly couldn’t even remember what I was doing an hour ago, the path was so convoluted and without sense. And you couldn't just rely on boring old linear time to remember. And there was never a strong indication of where you were even trying to go right at the moment, much less the ability to form a logic chain of how you decided to do this thing now. Something could be brought up and literally not come up for another 20 hours. And at such time, it was considered that you would remember that stuff, remember exactly what you were supposed to do, and know that the right time to return the library book was before getting the chips, but after getting the earrings. Because ARE YOU INSANE! OF COURSE THE LIBRARY BOOK COMES FIRST. WHAT ARE YOU STUPID?Now this might seem ridiculous, and it is, because its even worse than this. Because at least in my example, you knew you were trying to return the library book. In Chrono Cross, you don’t really know what you are trying to achieve at nearly any point in the story. So you must do something at some certain time for some reason. And you’d better remember! Most people don’t even have a vague reason to join you. It's like they value their own time so little that instead of simply wasting their own time, they want you to do it for them.As I said earlier on, there were times when something would come up 20 hours later. This was pretty uncommon. It was more common for things to just not come up again. It's not that important plots points were forgotten. It's just that you perform a lot of actions, and you assume they are important even if you don't currently know why, but they don't get mentioned again. And you wonder if there was something you missed, but no, you just did something for the hell of it, apparently. You don't really get a reason. On rare occasions you might get something tangentially related, like you find out the name of the book that the guy needed to return. But that doesn't explain anything, its just linked information.If the main character simply said 'I am going to risk my life in this dangerous task becaue I feel like it', that would actually be a big improvement.I couldn’t believe that I played for 40 hours, and nearly nothing that had come up once seemed to come up a second time. This is ridiculous when you considered the original. The original had a huge amount of stuff happen, and all in a concise manner. So I had played Chrono Cross longer than Chrono Trigger could even go if you did absolutely everything, and I still had no idea what I was trying to achieve. I was a bit over half way, I believe. I watched Youtube videos of the rest, and nearly all the story happens after the point I got up to. And it barely connected to nearly everything that came up earlier in the story. To be fair, the story can be quite good when it happens. But there is just so much stuff that is irrelevant to the story as a whole. The first half is organised around the principle of 10 minutes of interesting important story, then 10 hours of barely connected stuff. You could cut large sections out of the game and it would make as much sense. But as it is, it is a big slog.Anyway, if you don’t care about story, then you could find a lot of fun. If you expect any kind of sense or logic, this is a maddening game to play. And make sure to get the fan fix for the frame rate. It runs much better.

_childDocuments_.review: Lovers of mediocre late-1990s JRPGs will love returning to El Nido, probably as much as we wish for something new and worthwhile that'll scratch the same itch.I didn't appreciate  when it came out; I enjoyed it for what it was, but at the time it felt like a poor successor to (what remains) one of my all-time favorites and one of the most fun JRPGs I'd played until then. Playing through it (fully) a couple decades later has been a fun trip, and I'm happy that porting older games to PC has made them more-accessible to more people, but: 1. Chrono Cross is still, in my opinion, pretty mediocre, 2. Its mediocrity still soars above most present-day, JRPGs, and 3. I think Square-Enix knows this.GAMEPLAY: has a whole lot of neat gameplay elements. In an attempt to eliminate grinding, there's really no leveling-up; you get big stat boosts from each boss, which is as close as it gets, and for the first few fights afterwards, you can get smaller stat boosts. This makes the game's pace pretty nice.The downside to this is that non-boss battles feel pointless and even frustrating. Besides stealing (there are almost no unique steals, even from bosses) and the aforementioned tiny stat boosts (that quickly dry up), you get gold, crafting reagents (which you'll rack up FAST), and sometimes elements (slottable "spells").STORY:The game's story weirds me out. While most of it is pretty straightforward (especially in the first half), late-game revelations become confounding, confusing, and frustratingly-trivial. It is completely possible, and even likely, than the average player will overlook some of the biggest plot elements/twists in the game. It's furthermore bothersome (though expected from games of the era) that almost every "big decision" you make is ultimately inconsequential; the story will move on as it otherwise would.CHARACTERS:There are too many to care about. Serge is a mute "everyman" whose only attachments prior to the game's beginning quickly become unimportant. Lynx is an enigma until...you stop caring about him, at which point the (missable) revalations about his character are boring and ho-hum and buried within lengthy monologues. Kid is cool and interesting enough - especially when the story (finally) unfolds - but even this is happens, like too much of the overall story, via lazily-dumped late-game exposition. Many of the characters have some sort of interesting involvement in the game's plot, but once they're in your party, they're completely interchangable with anyone else. All the other ("filler") characters who have less involvement have, at best, some neat lines (which are variations on lines you'll hear the other characters say, anyway) and maybe about five minutes' worth of unique interaction during some paltry quest to get their highest-level techs. At best.

_childDocuments_.review: I will have to say, I am a very satisfied gamer! I remember playing this game back in 1999 when it was first released and it took me through an incredible journey and a very compelling adventure through two different worlds, hydro marshes, forests, palaces, pirate ships, forts, and much more. The battle game play is quite different than your traditional RPG, and it has its stand alone style. I really felt connected to the characters. The backgrounds and atmosphere were very well done and well thought out. I was astonished when I came across this remaster and had to check it out. It brought back my teenage nostalgia and great memories. The 3D models were remastered and looked incredible! Much better than the originals and super adorable. I also like the new paintings of the characters as they also had higher quality than the originals and yet stayed true to the originals. I also like the fact that after you beat the game, you can also warp to the last battle at any point in the story and beat it before the game is over. Each time you end up with an entirely different ending than the first time you played it. You can make different choices and have different outcomes. Great RPG. It is a joy to see that this masterpiece has not been left behind. And I think it is awesome that it is being re-introduced to a new generation of young people so they can feel the magic we did when we first played it back in the 90s and early 2000s. I highly recommended it to any RPG fan out there looking for a great compelling story.

_childDocuments_.review: This sure is a weird one. First of all, yes, it is a good game. Yes, the port has many, many problems, but the modders have already fixed it, thankfully.As a sequel to Chrono Trigger... this works? It's only real links with Trigger are the plot itself - systems, characters and even world are barely related at best - but it's a kinda weird, kinda messy PS1 RPG in many, many ways. The battle system is somewhat experimental, and it mostly works, if maybe a bit too slow. The leveling system is also very experimental - only bosses level you up - but the pacing is very off, and there's a RNG aspect on the level ups that mess everything up.The plot itself is a bit confusing, tries to complicate something that was somewhat simple, and doesn't work in many ways, but still, it's intriguing enough to keep you playing. The extra endings and alternative paths add to the replayability, but by the end it felt more like a chore than anything, for me.It's... an imperfect, but very interesting game for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to play Chrono Cross, I believe this version is fine and would recommend it. For remakes, I tend to not discuss my personal opinion of the actual game, but I will say that this is not Chrono Trigger, and only loosely serves as a sequel. The plots are connected to a degree, and while Cross builds off of Trigger and isn't wholly separate, the two are only tangentially related. The gameplay is also very different, as is the plot, setting, and the use of characters. If you're coming into this from Chrono Trigger without any knowledge of Cross, just be aware that they are very different games. I think the game is worth experiencing, but I would strongly recommend not using Chrono Trigger to set your expectations. Cross is a good, if flawed, game.I completed the game after approximately 50 hours and did not experience any crashes across 3 computers and windows 8, 10, and 11. I believe most problems with the game have been resolved, but I did still see a fair amount of comments about crashing. I had consistent 60 FPS throughout. There is/was mention of the background art being AI up-scaled and not being up to par.This game is another in a long line of Square re-makes/remasters where the game is buggy on launch. I personally wish Square treated their IP with more care.I believe this version is superior to the original version and is much, much more accessible due to digital availability. There are a few, small graphical anomalies, but overall the sprite reworks are very well done. I enjoyed the updated portraits, and the rest of the game was smooth and handled fine. I don't feel I'm well equipped to discuss the version changesI did not play the bundled Radical Dreamers, but I am happy that this game is now commercially available to the public.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDRA classic RPG with a great soundtrack and an interesting storyline (providing you've played Chrono Trigger!). Performance may vary but I had no real issues with latest updates. Unusual battle, leveling and party system which is likely to be divisive. Recommended for fans of classic 90s RPGs, but unlikely to persuade those who aren't a fan of the genre.PerformanceLots and lots has been said about this. I played this in 2024 after all the patches and alternated between my ROG Ally and my desktop PC. Barring some screen tearing, which was fixed by forcing on V Sync and switching to borderless windowed instead of full screen, I had no issues and the game ran smoothly. I didn't use mods but I also limited the frame rate to a maximum of 60FPS just in case. The game was fine on both the ALLY and the desktop. Probably looked better on the ALLY as the smaller screen doesn't expose the dated backgrounds as much!GameplayThe battle system is a bit odd - it's not quite turn based and uses a stamina system. There is an easily missable tutorial in the first village that explains the basics. It took me a while to get my head around it and to be honest I think there's a reason we've not seen anything like it since - it's unnecessarily convoluted in my opinion. The levelling up system is also a bit different, with an overall level awarded by beating bosses and then small stat increases awarded through the regular battles. These stat boosts are finite, so it means there is little grinding, but then also it can be pointless fighting these battles in long stretches between bosses. Unlike many JRPGs, there are also many part members you can recruit (over 40!). Personally, I didn't really like this as it meant you don't get to know the characters as they don't really respond uniquely to most scenarios in the game and it feels like many characters are very similar and as you can only swap them out at save points or on the world map, there isn't really an incentive to do so regularly. These do level up with your main party thankfully, but as far as I'm aware don't gain the stat increases from the regular battles. Chrono Cross is clearly an ambitious game, trying to be different and it succeeds in that regard - but definitely won't be to everyone's tastes.StorylineTakes a while to get going but poses some interesting questions about the meaning of life, what happens when one interferes with timelines and even natural selection (which as a biology teacher I did very much enjoy!). Chrono Trigger fans will get more out of it - I've heard people say that Chrono Cross works as a standalone title, but I think much of the ending would be lost on you if you hadn't played Chrono Trigger and therefore the storyline would lose a lot of its impact. The story provides enough intrigue to keep you playing and provokes thought post the ending which is always a mark of a good storyline in my book. I also enjoyed the story of the Radical Dreamers visual novel that was included and one could argue that this more closely links to Chrono Trigger. There is also a brand new secret ending that you can unlock after viewing the endings of both Chrono Cross and Radical Dreamers - you can see it by watching the credits in the launcher. Overall, I liked it (mainly for the storyline, Chrono Trigger references and soundtrack), but I'm not rushing back for a new game plus as I never really came to love the battle system or character progression.

I changed a couple of Nvidia settings -- turned on v-sync, set it to high performance mode, etc. After a little tweaking, the framerate was mostly stable and most of the stutter is limited to fights, which is easily mitigated with the fast forward function. The game looks fine, the new features like fast forward and whatnot are honestly a big help, and I've only been impressed, considering this port barely managed to see the light of day. Ignore any review by players who couldn't bother to optimize their experience themselves and only spent 10 minutes in game. Yes, this port needs work, but I'm quite satisfied so far with not having to find and download an emulator just to play the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Chrono Cross: Radical Dreamers edition is a classic JRPG that has been beloved by fans for decades. The new modernized graphics bring a fresh take to the game, while still retaining the same nostalgic feel that fans know and love.The updated graphics are stunning and really bring the world of Chrono Cross to life. The vibrant colors and intricate details make every scene feel like a work of art. The character designs have been updated as well, with each character having their own unique look and personality.The gameplay itself remains largely unchanged, which is a good thing. The combat system is still engaging and challenging, and the story is just as captivating as it was when the game first came out. The addition of new side quests and hidden areas adds even more replay value to an already great game.One of the standout features of Chrono Cross: Radical Dreamers edition is the music. The original soundtrack was already amazing, but the updated version takes it to a whole new level. The orchestrated pieces are breathtaking and really add to the emotional impact of the story.Overall, Chrono Cross: Radical Dreamers edition is a fantastic update to a classic game. The modernized graphics bring a new level of immersion, while still retaining the nostalgia of the original. The updated music, side quests, and hidden areas make this version of the game a must-play for both longtime fans and newcomers alike.
_childDocuments_.name: CHRONO CROSS: THE RADICAL DREAMERS EDITION

_childDocuments_.review: The original was the first game I ever bought for myself as a kid so it has a very fond place in my heart. Having it released again decades later was a wonderful surprise to me. Though I may not have much time put into this version, the game remains true to the original, so I can use my experience from both to help form this review. The soundtrack as always is absolutely outstanding and will always remain as one of the best I've ever had the pleasure to listen to. The gameplay is fun and the fighting system is a different take on the age old turn based RPG style so it's a nice departure from the norm. The story is pretty good and pretty long so you have plenty to look forward to and the cast of characters you can recruit is massive. The game may not be for everyone but I absolutely recommend it to someone looking for a wonderfully sounding, beautifully crafted world with lots to do and places to explore. I'm sure you'll enjoy it too.

_childDocuments_.review: This port can run like trash at times.  If I enjoyed this game overall it wouldn't be bad enough to thumbs down, but it is bad enough to gives a heads up imo.The story of this game failed at making me feel attached to any of the main characters.  Any character building and meaningful dialog other than moving the plot forward was slim.  While the idea of having the option to obtain a lot of characters sounds neat, it doesn't offer any extra enjoyment.  If anything it adds to the problem I just mentioned.  The main chars don't seem to have a lot of thought put into them and the dozens of extra characters pretty much have no personality of their own.The combat is fine.  It is typical turn-based for the most part, but offers enough of a change-up to feel newish.  However, it is still your basic attack or magic turn-based classic rpg.  There isn't anything wrong with that, but the combat style doesn't really offer enough to make the fighting style of different characters stand out. I bring this up because one of the big features of this game is all the different party members you can collect, but the combat doesn't make it where any of those characters offer anything unique.  The attacks or spells might be a different element, but that's it. So, this isn't something terrible, but it just adds to the  pointless reasoning to have a billion characters.Graphics are neat.  I have always loved the hand painted look the backgrounds had and for a ps1 rpg I think the character design was better than most rpgs that came out slightly before it.  But yeah, whether you view this as a Chrono Trigger sequel or just as its own thing, the story is very blah. This late in the ps1 cycle there were plenty of rpg games that went deeper into characters and offered good dialog, but this game barely measures up to even some 16 bit era rpgs when it comes to that. Having a silent protag definitely doesn't help.  That isn't always a bad thing, but all the other characters offer so little that the silent main char stands out as a bad thing a lot more.The port has the whole speed-up option stuff that is convenient, but other than that the original version probably runs better, lol.I just can't really recommend this to anyone. I wouldn't even thumbs down if I thought fans of old square games might like it, but this is one of the worst rpg released by Square during the ps1 days.Music is nice.

_childDocuments_.review: Radical Dreamers is a thoroughly enjoyable text adventure that initially debuted on the Satellaview which was a Japanese-only peripheral for the SNES.  It also started Nintendo's trend of taping two consoles together as though trying to create a Voltron robot.For its age, it's still very enjoyable.  The puzzles can be head-scratchers and even if you manage to finish it, there are multiple endings.  The text adventure is accompanied by some impressive pixel art sequences and the dialogue is incredibly well written....Oh, you want to hear about Chrono Cross?It's flipping *Chrono Cross*.  I have neither the time, nor the words to really do the thing justice.  It was a passion project by some of the most talented people Square ever employed.Like I said up toward the top somewhere:  Not the best port of it, but for all the random stuttering, slowdown, and giving the impression the game's about to croak and die... it never did.  It just reaaaally wanted to.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't touched the text adventure yet and I'm not sure I'm going to, so consider this an in depth technical review of the Chrono Cross's improvements and problems at launch. I'll update my review if they fix the screen issues I'm listing. This isn't much of a review of the game itself since I'm writing this for fans of the original game like me and not newcomers. They'd best listen to someone else's opinion.Largely the game is the same as you remember it, with a nice painting style filter over every background, gorgeous new portraits for the characters that keep the artistic spirit of the original, and improved field & battle playable character models. If I had to criticize any of the art so far, its the length of Kid's neck for her battle model, since its rather off putting and crane like now thanks to how her head was changed.The music is mostly untouched and the same, but the sound effects could be hit or miss. However, I've played this game on emulators so much anyway that I can't really tell the difference. Unfortunately this means that the battle music still sounds like clowns molesting you in hell. Hopefully a mod gets released that replaces that particular track all together.Anyway, the only serious problems I have with the game so far are its screen options.Full screen Standard/Zoomed views have a gradient in the background instead of full black. It's bad for OLED screens to have such a large static image taking up so much of the screen alike this because it contributes to burn-in. At 4k It sort of shifts to the right in full screen for me also, but 1080p seems to be fine and, let's be real, 4k is overkill anyway,There's no widescreen option to speak of either, but most of us expected that probably. Screen tearing is also an issue here, along with an annoyingly pointless limited vram warning when I start the game because my laptop dynamically uses its graphics card instead of iGPU only when something warrants it.Please guys, just dump the background gradient or let us turn it off easily. The release has its problems, but I'm happy with it so far otherwise.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, there are technical issues as expected from a game that's over 20 years old.However, you are acquiring a gem.It is not nostalgia for me, as graphics have never been a priority to decide if I'm enjoying a game or not.But the frame rates aren't smooth. Don't expect to see fluid movement nor combat animations in the game as this is a port of the ps1 with some fancy backgrounds.There are small delays on combat sometimes which will block stop you from queueing 3+ actions quickly.Sometimes for the upgraded graphics, you can see some clipping but this is just because you would be looking for them, otherwise they will go unnoticed.Yet this is but nothing compared to the story this game will take you through.Before purchasing, please think what type of gamer are you and how much graphics impact your enjoyment. There is nothing wrong with preferring 60+ and is normal now. But back then this is what we had and just the non 60 fps wavy sea and music from the intro, is enough to throw me back to the days I was just back from school and booted the game on the ps1 while eating lunch because I loved the start menu music.It is a literal trip to the past for many of us and it still keeps the performance of the past. Those who are willing to overlook this will find a marvelous story that shouldn't be lost.It could have been better maybe, many of the original data was lost. But luckily for Square Enix, what Square Soft did back then, crushes such mistakes with its story and gameplay.Remember this is not a fps game, it isn't a moba nor a game which a slow framerate will punish you. It's totally acceptable if this drives you away, but do not fear to get into it either. You will love what you will find.To end this, I remember the first time I saw the beach cutscene. I was surprised of how good it looked, I was astonished on how this game could show such smooth video. Seeing the original cutscene again made me smile and realize how far games have improved nowadays. For me, it still looks good.

_childDocuments_.review: Anyone having issues getting this extremely poor "remaster" working without stuttering, should use Kaldaien's SpecialK, found here for now. Nothing else I tried (ISA's FPS hack, HxD, etc worked for me.) SpecialK was drag and drop and it runs flawlessly now.As for the game itself, it's a timeless classic and apart from approximately 2 lines of dialogue that people scream were censored and a missing accent filter for one side character who doesn't talk much anyway, this appears true to the original with improved models, some models (2) were adjusted for decency reasons.This "remaster" includes options for old and new graphics, as well as stretching or zooming the field of view to match aspect ratios bigger than 4:3.It includes useful options to speed up or slow down the game, and some cheats built in such as auto battle, etc if you just want to play through and enjoy the story.The FMV quality is -abysmal- however can easily be fixed with a mod on Nexus Mods called "Snooty AI Upscale" which brings them to excellent quality even on a high resolution monitor.Do I actually recommend this? Again I wish steam had a "Neutral" option, if you're willing to tinker with it a little to get better performance (it's borderline unplayable out of the box), then yeah, sure. Shame on Square Enix for not touching this port since it's release though. Get it on sale to give them less money, donate to the modders actually fixing this thing.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Chrono cross back in the day, my friends all hated it because "it's not the Chrono Trigger sequel they wanted" But ignore thoughts like that because CC is a wonderful game both on its own and as a sequel to CT. I'm not saying its a perfect game. (personally i wish they trimmed down the recruitable characters and focused more on fleshing out a smaller cast) but it has a nice battle system. graphics that aged well. (even without the HD) and one of the best soundtracks of rpg history. I reccomend CC to fans of CT who might have missed it, or folks who just like PSX era JRPGs.That being said this version needs some work. Its only day 1 so some bugs might be expected, but this is Square Enix were talking about, they should have enough talent to prevent terrible Day 1 issues ive experienced with this rerelease. First time i launched it i got a warning about "low Vram may cause the game to not work properly" Found out it was trying to use my internal graphics card, not my Nvidia. once i fixed that, it rand without crashes so that was nice. But the game still lags in places, on some of the "busier" areas, and during combat (both entering) and during characters physical attack animations. I've tried turning off settings to make it smoother but it dosent seem to make a difference, even with all the extras off.Hopefully SE can/will adress these issures quickly because the current state is hard to enjoy. I will change my review to positive when/if SE manages to iron out the problems.TL:DR Chrono cross is a great game that all should enjoy. The price is great, you get the Sateleview "Radical dreamers" for the first time in English (officially) But maybe wait for some patches to help iron out the rough spots.

_childDocuments_.review: Chrono Cross and Radical Dreamers were both in my top 5 of the games I wanted the most to be re-released and here they come together in a bundle, just like a dream. This is perhaps my favorite from all the steam games I have.Pros:-Radical Dreamers is available for the first time officially translated!-New music tracks in the opening menu. My favorite is the Radical Dreamers theme song, which is amazing.-The new character portraits are gorgeous and fit the atmosphere and style of the game so well, as much as the characters's personalities.-The new options to avoid enemies encounters and to speed up time from the beginning are very pleasing additions.-The new models look cool and better and the paint-like filter on the backgrounds fits the game very well, and I think it could look better on a smaller screen like that of the steam deck or Nintendo Switch. Anyway, you can switch to the old backgrounds too, so that's perfect.-The partial capacity to change to the old version of the game makes it nice for preservation.-Now with the new patch, the game runs smooth as butter (60FPS)Cons:-No drowning Squaresoft logo at the beginning. It's a Square Enix logo instead.-The character portraits from the original version when they are talking are not identical, but I'm not sure if it's a problem or not, since the original were more pixelated and less defined. Now I'm waiting for the other classics, like Xenogears, Parasite Eve and Vagrant Story!

_childDocuments_.review: It's very hard to be positive about this release.On one hand, Chrono Cross is finally on PC after over 20 years. It's one of Squaresofts best games; it's difficult to argue that CC doesn't have the best soundtrack in the history of video games (because it does) that mixes classics from Trigger with new material like On the Beach of Dreams or Chronomantique; it has a unique combat system that blended materia with stamina costs; and it has a good story mixed with beautiful world art. Let's not forget the branching story and the huge cast of recruitable party members that lead to different experiences when you play.On the other hand and maybe five more hands, this port is absolutely just terrible. It runs worse than the PS1 game does on a PS1. It runs worse thjan the PS1 game does emulated. They did a lazy job using an AI upscaler on the backgrounds when, for years, there has already been a mod that shows them the right way to do it (the 4k upscale gigapixel mod). Worst of all, the frame tearing is nearly unavoidable even if you force Vsync or GSync or Freesync in your settings, enable low latency mode, etc.  The controls also seem to have regular issues where movement input won't be detected or you'll end up running into a wall.The game also has its own splash launcher just like every single Square Enix RPG on PC has had for a decade which isn't a big deal but it's annoying for couch gaming and likely causes DRM issues if you aren't online.It's "Only $20" but that doesn't excuse Square Enix from once again not learning from or employing any of the lessons they should have learned from every single Square Enix RPG release in the past 9 years. For PC players who may not have played this game when it was new, this is an extremely poor presentation and just another reason for people to avoid AAA gaming.I only recommend it because yes, it is playable with minimal tweaking, but it's not a definitive experience and I expect modders to once again step in and fix another cash grab.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: You need the mods or it's ACTUALLY UNPLAYABLE. It's a lazy port but CC didn't need much done to it. If this goes on sale for even 20% off it's something you should set your sights on. The definitive way to play Chrono Cross.>>>Go to nexusmods and get these: isa FPS Hack, Snooty A.I. Upscale. <-- keep this in mind for later.<<<>>>YOU *NEED* THESE MODS<<<This is more a review for the remaster, not a review of the game itself (TL;DR I freaking love this game)This will be the definitive way to play and enjoy the game, the art with sharper graphics is soooo beautiful. It certainly feels like a remaster and plays quite similarly to the original game, save for a few differences here and there.The story has a few branching paths the more effect what characters you have in your party, but adds more to replayability as quite a few characters have dialog and input throughout story events. The characters are quite likable, though there are some that are forgettable, it's not hard to find characters to love in this game. With 45 characters that can be used, there's a lot of different options for battles and interesting moments in the story.After completing the game, you can unlock the ability to challenge the final boss at different parts in the story, which unlocks various different endings. You can even get an item that unlocks all the characters from your previous run, allowing you to access the older characters while taking on different paths in the story.The story is pretty good for the time the game was released. Without spoiling too, the story involves the concept of different worlds that branch based on certain events that occur before the story, and the player must travel between the different worlds to save the two worlds while discovering more of who they are. The different worlds means you can have characters from one world meet their otherworldly counterpart for some more interesting dialog. There's a lot of hidden moments in this game that adds a lot more to the concept of exploration that keeps me coming back for more.Overall: It's a really nice remake of a pretty good game that has a lot of replayability. The gameplay, story, and characters are all really good and worth checking out, especially for fans of the JRPG genre.
