_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed, but leaning positive feelings about this port, I'm gonna real quick write up some pros and cons, from doing the intro segment.Pros:+Minor tweaks similar to the many FF PC ports, like encounter toggles+First official release of the excellent Radical Dreamers VN EVER+New character artwork actually looks pretty nice IMO+Higher quality audioUnchanged but needs to be mentioned:=Framerate appears to be identical to the PS1 version. Even on PS1, the game still runs at 15-30 FPS, this is because on actual hardware, the game would just duplicate frames 2 or 4 times to reach the NTSC 60 Hz requirement, like what FF7, Mario64, and Ocarina of Time did. Many older emulators say they run at "60" FPS when they mean that it's outputting 60 frames like a PS1 would, but the game's hardcoded to run lower than that. MOST modern emulators actually can tell what framerate the game's actually running at and display that on the side, or even have 60 FPS patches. I don't know if Chrono Cross has one, but I've played OTHER RPGs like Digimon World 2003 on Duckstation multiple times.=I don't know how, but Shadowplay literally lies about the game's framerate, I THINK this version is still doing the "duplicate frame outputs to reach 60Hz" trick, but I'm not sure.=I'm adding this one later just to make sure I covered EVERYTHING, apparently some character's outfits were altered to be less revealing, I don't care, but it's worth mentioning, because some people REALLY care. I can't even find much data about precisely who's design or what was changed because it's drowned out by the brigade of people complaining about censorship in general. I mean yeah it's bad but please actually provide examples while complaining, and if it's THAT big of a deal, mod the game, this is a PC game, you can mod things like models even on emulated "ports", because you can swap the disk image of the game with an altered one. This is how people modded the Castlevania Advanced Collection on Day 1.EDIT: Kaldaien, someone far more knowledgeable than me about the technical aspects of PC games, has said that the UI apparently renders at 60 which is where the false frame counter number comes from. This checks out.EDIT EDIT: Special K, a multi-mod that can be put into any game made by the aforementioned Kaldaien, now has a special submenu for Chrono Cross to unlock the framerate and change the render resolution of the game.Cons:-Graphical glitches because of poor graphical emulation, and poor out of the box framepacing (Special K's latent sync fixes framepacing.-Textures aren't upscaled well, probably using a poor machine upscaler and either untouched or lightly touched up, ESPECIALLY in the dungeons. Modern unofficial emulators do this much better.-FMVs are totally untouched.General Advice for Framepacing: If you are experiencing poor frame pacing, going into your Nvidia driver settings and turning "Low Latency Mode" for the problem game to "Off" or "On", instead of the generally advised "Ultra" may help, DX11 games don't actually control the amount of buffered frames, and "On" assures at least one frame is buffered, and "Off" allows for more frames if needed. DX12 and Vulkan games actually decide how many frames should be buffered themselves and the driver has no say, and this setting does nothing for those games.I actually haven't tested this with Chrono Cross in particular, in part because I wanna wait to see if Square actually patches this release. But this advice is good advice overall and I actually used it to fix my stuttering with Lego Star Wars Skywalker Saga. The downside to doing this is a single frame of latency, or about ~17ms on a 60Hz display, which isn't advisable for a rhythm game or a fighting game or anything competitive, but it's fine for a casual game or turn based RPG.FINAL REMARKS:All in all, if I had to pick a version of Chrono Cross, it WOULD be this one if only because of the new gameplay options and the better portrait artwork, and it's totally possible for people to mod this version, just like how the PS1 version has texture packs for specific emulators. BUT, Square should be ashamed for not trying harder. IF mods are made to fix things or upgrade things, I'll update this post to point you in that direction.EDIT: Check the steam guides for good mod info, there's a lot of it now at this point. A lot of good upscaling mods, and nice tweaks in general exist. A lot like the PS1 FF PC ports, these are the best versions if you put in the work to fix them. PCGamingwiki is a good resource for a lot of games and I recommend checking there first.A currently good modlist is here:

name: Frozenheim
detailed_description: Become famous as the legendary hero of your Viking clan and notorious as the scourge of other jarls. Your exploits and deeds will be legendary. However, every legend has a beginning and yours begins on the shores of Frozenheim. For your village to prosper, you will have to make the most of the seasons by hunting, fishing, farming land, and gathering resources before the winter. Exploration will be key as the lands are as bountiful as they are dangerous. Once you have the lay of the land and a steady supply, you can start planning out and managing your city. In order to vanquish your enemies, you will have to raise your warriors and utilize their unique skills. Form shield walls and pin down foes with volley fire, then send your berserkers to crash into the enemy lines. Depending on how you develop your clan, you will be able to enlist powerful heroes, build devastating siege engines and imposing longships or even evoke the power of Ragnarok! Whether you prefer the fields of combat or the strategy table, Frozenheim has a mode for you. Relax yourself with the free-build mode or challenge yourself in the arena of the Jarl's tournament. Put your building skills to the test in survival mode or discover the story of Frozenheim in the campaign mode told from the perspective of the four major clans: Wolf, Deer, Crow, and Bear

_childDocuments_.review: Good mix between a City Builder and an RTS.LikesLove the graphics, especially the fire, the weather, the seasons and the paths that are generated in the snow. Although not at all unique I really like the ability to fast forward time in single player if you're waiting for some resources to come in. Somehow the game feels chilled out (probably due to the music) and allows you enough time to place things in the positions you'd like without feeling like you're about to get stormed by your opponent which allows you to consider things a bit (although I haven't played multiplayer yet). Dislikes/ (Suggestions)They need to work on the path finding and selection (especially of units) a bit as it's a bit glitchy but not unplayable for an early access game. Units against buildings are a bit OP so rush tactics would work too well I think. If you're looking for a good viking RTS then you're just going to play Ancestors Legacy so my view would be for the Devs to go slightly more into the city builder side of things. It does feel like the game needs a little more depth and perhaps customisation for example more options on the ships would be great or more building types. I found I went through the resources in my base quite quickly and then there was really nothing else to do except kill the enemy - which kind of loses the city builder element. Maybe the ability to build a small forward camp to collect resources and regenerate troops or alternatively a bigger build radius. Definitely need more maps and some randomisation on the map generation but I'm sure the devs will get there. All in all quite impressive for an early access release and the low price. The first couple times I played it I enjoyed it more than a number of A-Grade titles but can't see myself playing 100hrs plus unless the above suggestions were taken into account.

_childDocuments_.review: Tl;Dr:If you are into fairly straightforward RTS games you might enjoy the game, but if you prefer complexity, this becomes boring very fast. A mix of classic RTS and City building, but too simple to be good at either of those things.What I liked:- You can only build within a limited distance of a main building, so you'll have to set up outposts to expand further.- The city building part is pretty enjoyable, similarly to the Anno series where you need to reach a level of happiness for upgrades.What I didn't like:- Unit management is horrible. They refuse to move in formation so your archers will consistently position in the frontline.- You have one faction, the vikings, which means you won't be choosing from too many unit types or various buildings. The upgrade paths are linear as well. After playing a single match you can say you've seen it all and there is very little strategic depth.- Discontent increases from things like running out of food, but won't start decreasing naturally after you have fixed the problem. You need to put in extra resources to get rid of it in the form of feasts and similar. It is also mostly unrelated to happiness, so even with a high happiness level your people will be discontent and riot. Doesn't feel like it makes too much sense.

_childDocuments_.review: Having only played a 2-3 skirmishes and started the campaign, my review on this is mostly first impressions. Core Concept: Norse RTS reminiscent of AOE 2 with some LIGHT settlement mechanics.Visuals/sound: The visuals are striking, as most the skirmishes and the campaign map are clearly a work of love with beautiful fjords and water renders and details like stone faces that make it feel like the world is old. The downside is that it can be very hard to read what is going on. Unit banners stack up in a scrap, making it hard to see how a fight is going, and the underlying terrain is impossible to read under tree-cover making it very hard to place buildings if you haven't clear-cut a section.  Sound however is stellar with the minor annoyance that there isn't more tracks outside of combat to keep things super fresh. The sound effects are awesome and unit voices are great.Visual/Sound Score: 3/5Gameplay: So lets talk about the bug-bear in the room. This game has been tagged as a "city builder" which is not accurate. Everything constructed is a resource gathering mechanisim that is meant to fuel your war effort, down to building houses to get more people to recruit into your army. At its heart it is a RTS Focused game with the settlement you're constructing being prioritized to benefiting your army ala AoE 2.  This in itself isn't too bad and can be engaging, however the game does have some issues as an RTS.1. Unit variety is very, VERY thin. with 5 Core units that any clan can use, and then some unique units for each of the clans. 2. the controls are CLUNKY. Those who are expecting Starcraft or AoE 2 responsiveness are going to be dissapointed as the units in my experience (ESPECIALLY SHIPS) forget what they were doing and then potato in a random spot. Top this with a semi-unresponsive mini-map that ignores clicks unless you orient your camera just-right makes for a frustrating Macro game. Also- Units set on aggressive, will NOT attack hostile buildings by default. You have to manually tell them to attack a structure which in a RTS where "destroy the main building" is the objective is unacceptable.3.  As noted in visuals- Banners stack on one another, making it very difficult to tell what's going on at a glance and making micro very hard. 4. Siege equipment in this game is absolutely not required, as 9 times out of 10 the entire match is gonna be decided by infantry who then can burn down most things with some patience and gumption.There are elements that I like in here, the mini-quests and sites of interest are very reminiscent of 4x game goody huts where you never know what you're gonna get. The campaign as far as I've played is written as a saga which gets major theme points from me. I also like how all units other than militia have a special ability unique to that unit.Gameplay score: 2/5Overall- I want to like this game. It is obviously a labor of love and on the surface is a cool concept. But with how clunky it is for the player to interact with the core of the game makes it very hard to recommend. It looks pretty, it sounds GREAT, but its just not backed up strong enough through the gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Summary: It is worth getting, especially when it is on sale. It is a solid RTS with a strong emphasis on resource management set in the Viking settings. I just finished all the campaigns and must conclude I enjoyed Frozenheim, For an RTS I think the game was somewhat slow-paced, but I did like the chill building and exploration. Below are more detailed points.Things I like about this game:+ Four short campaign paths, one per clan. Each one of the paths tells a distinct story showing the strengths of the clan without dragging along for way too long. Each scenario brings something different to the table instead of just stating "defeat enemy clans" in the beginning.+ Smooth building system. The building mechanics feels very nice and allows you to construct your clan's settlement in neat lines or scattered around however you prefer.+ Pleasant graphics+ Viking themeThings I consider could use some love from the developers:- Pathing and AI. This was my biggest source of frustration in the game especially when it comes to units raiding enemy buildings. When you set your units to sneak up on enemy village using the cover of the trees and make them wait they go BURN THE HOUSES and blow their cover. When they are then attacked by defenders instead of defending themselves they go BURN THE WELL! Even when enemy towers and siege machines bombard them they go BURN THE WOODCUTTERS HOUSE! Maybe it is just a Viking thing to love burning things down, but I would expect them to have some sense of self-preservasion. It is also usual for the units to get clumped between buildings and doing nothing (or going back to burning buildings)  when instructed to attack enemy units.- Some of the unit special abilities feel a bit clunky. For example when activating an aggressive speed/attack buff the unit stops in its tracks instead of continuing pathing towards enemy unit it was going for earlier.- I expected the clans to be more different. This is a very minor point and I concede more variance makes balancing more difficult.- The Village and Gord achievements seem broken on 16/17 campaign scenarios. I only got them to trigger in the final scenario while it is easy to gain them in the first few.

_childDocuments_.review: I need to first start out by saying I have never written a review for a game before. With that being said, I felt Frozenheim really deserved one, especially after I read a review from “FACED,”… dudes a fool. I'll allow comments too just in case he wants to pop in. I have been an avid RTS player my whole life, and over the last five years, I have not found one game that brought back the nostalgic feeling of some of my favorites: Lord of the Rings Battle for Middle Earth 1 & 2, Dawn of War, Age of Empires, and Command and Conquer. However, Frozenheim does just that.While still being in early access, Frozenheim has already produced a AAA game with stunning graphics and a plethora of building options, technology trees, and even runes you can find around the map that unlocks blessings from the Norse gods. While bugs still do remain, remember that this is in early access and has already created a masterpiece.When playing skirmishes, Frozenheim has a unique battle landscape. Not only are the battles on land, but in true Viking form, you can build a boat and sail out to raid your enemy’s village. With the assistance of tech upgrades, the boats can be equipped with a ballista and better sails so that you can get your pillage on faster. When it comes to ravaging the high seas, be sure to look out for enemy longships as they can ram you and then board for a fight to the death. Building in Frozenheim is also very user-friendly. Use your mouse wheel to rotate buildings, walls that are “magnetic” and attach to one another when you drag your mouse and curve, making you feel like a master builder. The buildings are separated into categories, so it is very easy to find what you are looking for. With all the negative reviews, I think these people have a stick up their ass. This game has been out for seven days, and people are losing it. I.e., one psycho name “FACED” (0.7 hours of gameplay or 42 minutes) said he found better city building in mobile games. Ok, bud… He cited that the game was advertised as a city builder – even though we all know it is a user-defined tag, not the actual company’s tag. Furthermore, this dude said RTS 10% rating and Strategy 20% rating LOL. I played a 1v1 on hard difficulty and got smoked because I focused on the wrong strategy as a beginner. I can say I have the strategy down stat with hours played, and it is no cakewalk. Additionally, the RTS portion is sick, units level up, you can upgrade armor, damage, etc., at the weapon smith, and each unit has its own ability. It is a lot of fun when you begin to master this.Overall, this game is a masterpiece, and I have been dying for something like it. You cannot beat the current price, and it will only help the game to grow if you do end up buying Frozenheim while it is in early access.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is severely unbalanced even for an Early Access (v 0.4). The AOE for healer's hut is very small, so you need 5-10 huts for moderate-size settlement. The wells (needed to extinguish fires) require people to assign, so if you don't do it, everyone just calmly go back and forth nearby a burning building. Have you ever heard of medieval firefighters? Moreover, AOE of wells is also very small, you basically need to build one well per 3-4 buildings. In the end there will be a town of healers and firefighters.Resource management is horrible. In 20 minutes you will get 1000+ meat (only from 3 fishing huts) and 1000+ wood (from 4-5 trees that seem to be immortal). Why bothering with other food production buildings? And this is on NORMAL settings. Production chains are almost absent, only simple ones exist (hunters -> skins -> axemen). This is not a city management game at all, even Stronghold offered a better system, not mentioning Banished, which is a golden standard.Finally, combat. You have some glimpse of a tactical squad system, where you manage groups instead of single units. But you cannot fine-tune their settings, and I did not notice any difference between Defensive and Agressive stances, as I could not order my units to retreat in any of them. Archers sometimes forget that they have arrows and launch a melee attack. All unit textures tend to merge themselves into a Megatron-like fighter on a 1 m2 area, which is even more disturbing to see due to exactly the same timeline animation. Sounds they produce when you click on them are very funny and resemble ancient chinese warriors (Ho! He! Hu!) rather than vikings. And you can replenish units in the AOE of a healer's hut without spending your population (forgotten viking's cloning system?)I know a lot of games on EA (M&B Bannerlord, Kerbal Space Program, UBOAT, Medieval Dynasty) that offered much more gameplay at this stage. This is more at an alpha stage. I do hope that they will upgrade it with time, but I don't want to spend my money so much in advance.

_childDocuments_.review: Hey folks,I bought this game today, and I beat the campaign missions today as well- and I have to say this game does *incredible* things for the RTS genre. The exploration feels like you're exploring a serious turn-based RPG like Pillars of Eternity, and there are mini-quests and all sorts of things you have to do to get places- all the while you are buffing troops, expanding settlements so you can afford to recruit them, and making sure you won't clear areas so you're out of things to collect. It can be a bit tricky to get a village up off the ground, but if you look around the buildings a bit you see why they're needed, where they get bonuses you can really make massive settlements with really, really smart placement systems, ship-building, palisades. Really, really fascinating stuff, way ahead of other RTS's in the genre at the moment. Maybe years ahead in development.The assets the game uses, the voicing, all fantastic. You feel like you're in here. You can watch troops grow, etcetera. My only suggestions would be: Let troops 'fill' eachother if you have multiple groups of 2/3 and instead of (or being unable to) refill them at the moment, just let them group up into 1 group- but maybe matching the lowest EXP group so you can't use that to just keep a veteran level troop?Difficulty rating-- you seem to be able to scale up on how many resources you get *vastly* as a settlement expands to the point to where you couldn't ever expend them all, and can build like 5 of the biggest ships possible and fill out a whole tech tree/all of the nodes in the weaponsmith in like minutes once you're rolling, maybe negatives for a larger population?That's all, its really fantastic for the price, just wow.

_childDocuments_.review: Fronzenheim is a visually stunning game, that really lacks depth. Imagine playing the demo version of a new Anno game. There only is a sinlge island. You have a total of 7 different resources - including manpower.  You start by building a basic infrastructure: a fishing pier, a woodcutter's hut and a gatherers den for stone and iron. Then you start building a village. Instead of using coins to pay your workers, as you'd expect in Anno, you directly use your manpower in Frozenheim. a unit of 5 axeman will use 5 manpower, thus investing in an army early on can lead to a shortage of workers in your village. To unlock more building and upgrades you have to upgrade your main hall first, which also has to be unlocked by getting the average happiness above a certain threshold. This is done in a similar way to Anno as well, by building certain buildings, like a tavern or a temple, to meet the demands for happiness of your villagers. The main difference here is that citizens will only consume meat for the whole game and not require any other resource after advancing.There are more similarities to Anno, like the fact that the main building sends out carts to collect goods. The main building also has a zone of influence. You can construct outposts to expand the zone of influence. Destroying one of these buildings will level anything built within this zone to the ground as well. The combat is pretty unoriginal. You have half a dozen of different units. Archers, Axemen, Spearmen, Shieldbearers, Scounts and some units you unlock with a tech tree. You can also upgrade their stats by using a blacksmith. I haven't seen any possiblity for the use of tactics and such. Despite different stats you send your units into a big pile where they melee until someone won - archers excluded. You could rush archers to force them in melee and withdraw low units to save their experience and some costs (similar to Company of Heroes). I don't want to label this game as an Anno-Clone because there are a lot of things it does different, too. I like the seasons, I like how streets are generated automatically based on the paths of your villagers like in the old settlers 3/4 and I really like the visual style. But a visually appealing game isn't enough for me. I was looking for a viking citybuilder with some combat and exploring, but Fronzenheim plays more like Age of Empires or Anno than Banished.

_childDocuments_.review: Hey,I love RTS games and I enjoy city buildiers.I didn't have high expectation for the game but I definitely have expected something more.I have a feeling that description promises a very different game than the one I have ended up getting.I would not recommend this game, maybe on some hard discount if you don't have any alternatives - you can play this and listen to a podcast.Below are Pros and Cons in my opinion:Pros:- Base building is enjoying (although pretty simplistic and time-consuming rather than skill-consuming)- The art style fits the Norse fantasy - graphics and models are very nice, I think that was the most enjoying part while playing.- I like norse mythology.- Supported by GeForce Now.- The game did not crash even once and was loading exceptionally fast.Cons:- I would say it is neither city builder and colony sim or solid RTS - both of those aspects are at very very very basic level.- There is supposed to be something like "discontent mechanic" but my villagers where always happy while I did not give a $%^& about them.- Villagers are essential for development and yet ... vikings can't kill them or enslave or sell or whatever something.- Poor storytelling with a very linear approach to progression: 5 campaigns, 4 missions each + 1 additional/final mission -> there is no particular long story so you can identify with a particular clan.- Missions are too slow and take between 30 minutes to an hour on average. Most of them requires player to do exactly the same things in the same order (is strategy even required?).- You can't set mission difficulty.- As steam page says: "Prepare for brutal real-time combat that will put your tactical skill into a test" - I think I played different game or I am so damn good at this because I haven't even started using my tactical skills and I beat the game easily.Combat is very simple, basically click right mouse button on the enemy and that's all ... (and here I had another Total War in my head but in Viking scenery).AND BTW THERE IS NO ATTACK MOVE! (nice RTS)- AI is dumb as $%^&, I prayed for it to attack me so I was leaving my guard wide open. I didn't train any soldiers and was using my lone hero to take care of all the "atacks".- Not only enemy's AI is dumb, but my units are even dumber - If I give them order to attack everything in sight, they will for example focus on the building while enemy is hitting their heads with sword and axes.- The only fighting mechanism is that you can hide units in trees -> no bonuses for surprise attack, flank attack, use of terrain etc.- There are seasons but they don't affect the game - as other claim that "you need to struggle to survive autumn and winter". _childDocuments_.review: A simple RTS with numerous problems.Pathing is really bad, units get stuck on stuff or will start heading in the wrong direction for no reason, the biggest offender being gatherers getting stuck on their own gathering building and sitting around doing nothing without telling you.You can't hotkey buildings.The basic harvester building (wood) requires its own resource to be built.There is no way to get enough limited goods (iron, stone, etc) long term without trading in the marketplace building, which requires a limited resource (stone) to build. Forget to build it soon enough and you're screwed.The camera behaves very badly when you have to move it over high ground, which is a frequent occurrence. Picking one squad out of a larger group centers the camera on that squad. So if you are trying to manage individual squads out of a hotkey group, your point of view will get jerked around for no reason. If you are trying to refill a squad but you can't for any reason, the game will not tell you why. So you have to figure out which resource you're short on, or maybe you're just not in range of the healer which for some reason is the only place you can refill your squads.If you have multiple squads of different types selected at once, you can only see one squad's abilities. This means efficient hotkey groups are limited to one type of unit.The game will not warn you when your buildings are under attack, your units will silently sit still and die to an enemy shooting them from out of their line of sight, but you will get blasted with noisy notifications at you any time a ship appears in your area of vision.You can't unload units from boats without emptying the whole boat. Extra annoying if you accidentally put a wrong unit on a boat, because then you have to launch and then re-beach to try again.You can't set production limits on resource refinement buildings (i.e. skins to clothes). This is a big problem because some things need the raw resource, so you have to manually toggle those buildings on and off all the time.For such a basic RTS there are way too many flaws to make it worth your while. Look elsewhere in the genre, this one is a hard pass.

_childDocuments_.review: This game started off pretty well and I enjoyed the tutorial in the campaign until it started getting incredibly frustrating. Even on so called "easy" difficulty, the campaign steadily became unplayable for me. There is a ton of tedious resource grinding to keep villagers and military units happy. If you don't keep them happy, they all split and desert you. There are also way too many limitations on what you can build and how many troops you can create. My troops were also always getting quickly defeated by even a freakin' pack of wolves. My base was also getting burned to the ground every time I would send out a unit to explore the surrounding area. I finally gave up on the campaign and tried a custom game. And then the boredom hit and wow this game gets super boring in my opinion. Traversing the terrain is painfully slow to the point where you will constantly want to speed up the game. There are also tons of mountains and the camera zooms to the ground when passing over them. It's basically just clicking and waiting and running troops into the occasional wolf pack, bear, or camp of bandits and then watching the battles and moving on. I finally realized that I really wasn't enjoying this game so I cannot recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing for hours in skirmish mode and building up my Clan to the maximum in every aspect here are my impressions:+ Absolutely gorgeous visuals/graphics, I love the atmosphere, the map visuals the ease of navigating the map, the straightforward interface.+ Great music, arts, assets, props. Love the design of the buildings units, gates, ships+ Great city building system, not as complex as I feared, straightforward to learn and applyMy issues with the game:- Combat is for me the most important aspect of the game, unfortunately it is absolutely poor. Units just hack and slash without any regards to their safety, no actual combat. Units do not engage in 1 to 1 fights, with counters, animations, kill moves,..etc This combat system stems from the early 2000s strategy games... - Very poor AI. In skirmish mode they repeatedly just spam units and send them over to the enemy's location, in Kamikaze mode. Meaning they just throw their units, non stop to the enemy's base. They keep dying, yet the AI just continues this strategy. - Poor path finding sometimes, I have seen the enemy AI getting stuck between two of their ships, getting stuck behind their ship, unable to land their ship on shore, so they just stay idle.Conclusion: Overall the game has big potential, I think if the AI and combat system was re-worked, improved this would become a very good strategy game. _childDocuments_.review: I echo the sentiments you see in the other reviews. This is very much an Early Access game. While still playable, it doesn't offer much in replayability. The graphics are gorgeous, but the single music track gets tiresome after a while (feels Skyrimy). City building is far too simple, more akin to StarCraft than any kind of city/management game. It's trying to be a bit like the Anno series, but it's far to simplistic in its current iteration. Combat is also quite simplistic. Units sometimes get stuck or simply don't follow orders, and trying to micromanage while in battle is a pain. There's the beginning of a campaign, but there's no voice over so it feels a bit lack luster.Conclusion: I don't think I will revisit this game for quite some time, 14€ is too much for this little content, but I have high hopes for the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Frozenheim, a game borrowing a lot of fun and interesting features from games like Age of Empires. Both in a good and a bad way, but for a game that calls itself a "city builder", it does it very poorly at the current stage. While the city building is fun and exciting, it lacks common buildings other city builder games have. Frozenheim also put water and foods into one requirement, which is fine, however, it would've been nice seeing a meat, water and vegetables requirement giving you more of a challenge to balance the diet of your settlement. Especially since they have a well in the game. While water isn't a direct requirement for survival, it's tied into a requirement to unlock more buildings. As it stands right now, you're forced to be where the game starts, meaning you can't freely place your longhouse where you want. This is something I'd like to in the future, and perhaps a few places to chose from. While it makes sense to have a set location in the story mode, it does not in the survival mode.As for combat, it's a lot, it's clear that there's a huge focus on combat, which is fair enough. But I somewhat feel that the focus of the game lands more on making sure you have a huge army to tackle the influx of waves and other enemies. You're constantly rushing to expand so you can produce more warriors. The combat is however very fun and it does what it's suppose to and it does that very well.Then we have the seasons in the game, there's 4 of them like you would except from a European-ish setting. They all pass very fast, meaning that in just a few hours you've seen winter a dozen times. And that is if you leave the game on real time. With that said, I never really felt the need to speed up the game at all. I just wish each season lasted for a few hours so you had more time to take in the beautiful maps they created. Talking about maps, there's a handful. Each looking better than the other.Apart from all that, the game could really benefit from having a port, where you can dock ships and invite merchant to trade with. It really needs several different animal farms added, cow, sheep and chicken farms for example. A Yule fest site could be very nice to give some time for relaxing in between battles. Faith plays a tiny part in the game as well, so to see a few options for viking churches would be nice.Fozenheim is a top notch game otherwise, it really makes a Norse lad like me very happy to see more love to an almost forgotten time. I would 100% recommend the game at the moment, it's fun, challenging at times and most importantly very beautiful. Another plus is that the games comes with a full fledged photo mod featuring sliders and values to make your screenshots stand out. Screenshots taken in game are saved in %appdata% > local > Frozenheim by the way.

_childDocuments_.review: I watched this game closely and waited patiently for a full release. Well, I should have played under two hours so, I could refund it. The game is great, don't get me wrong. Beautiful, everything seems to work, didn't encounter any bugs. The whole thing, that completely turned me off of this game is the "spawning". I am not sure if it different in any other play modes other than campaign (which I played), but it absolutely turned off from this within the first few hours. Yes I know it is a game, but have a little realism. Troops appear out of no where. Literally appear.... They are not spawned from a barracks, or training camp, they just spawn in the forest next to your base and start attacking. You can run around your base looking for some sort of camp, there is none. They just spawn. Completely takes away the feel of the game. If they add, something like forward camps that you have to destroy to stop the spawning, I would happily change my review. Even if they aren't destroyable due to their power or mission type, would be fine. But just randomly appearing out of thing air, no. As the game is at full release, doubtful it will change. I was looking forward to this game, but it will just be uninstalled and hidden along with the rest of the games that have ruined my hopes.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Very early in but feels like a great blend of city builder and Old School RTS8ish in. Beat the campaign, which is really just a glorified tutorial though it was enjoyable enough. There are some pretty big game play issues, ships will get stuck and unable to do anything, both yours and the enemies. The combat loses it's charm once you start dealing with larger invasions and some of that streamlining I talked earlier is needed for things like the tiny radius around the healing hut to heal reinforce your squads. I was mistaken, units do gain veterancy but I think it was just a one time done thing, no levels. Which I prefer. Overall I enjoyed it and iirc it was fairly cheap so worth it EA or not, just don't go expecting a full blown game yet. 2ish in. Some of the flaws are coming through but it is still EA and they are more 'needs improving' than fixing. The combat animation and logic are sorta terrible. Example, flanked a set of archers with a unit of axe men. They stuck with ranged combat, hopefully they just haven't gotten around to that, seems to be mostly aesthetic; the archers got slaughtered but did manage to kill an axe man from the main group. _childDocuments_.review: The serenity commonly offered by city-building RTS games has been lost on me as of late. Frozenheim initially promised me a trip through memory lane, a best-of collection containing all the greatest mechanics and features I’d come to know and love through my time with city-building titles. However, upon further inspection, Frozenheim reveals itself to not only be a phenomenal example of how to release a game into Early Access but also how to innovate upon an overburdened genre.“Frozenheim’s core gameplay is unbelievably satisfying.”Regardless of whether I was in the heat of combat; watching as my poor scouts were torn to shreds by my enemy’s axes, or simply surveying my peaceful riverside village; as my people awoke with the rising sun, the birds chirping on the thatched roofs as the snow melted away and spring took hold, I was completely and utterly immersed.Frozenheim’s world is filled with wonderful minutiae that help bring its fantastic setting to life. Whether it’s the blink-and-you’ll-miss-it animations that occur all across your settlement or the way the seasons dynamically affect your world, the sense of realism pervades throughout. This is all in due part to the phenomenal visuals.Frozenheim is perhaps one of the best looking city-builders I’ve ever played. From the way the trees sway gently in the morning breeze to the snow parting as the rugged wheels of a cart are dragged through it, there’s a complete and utter devotion to capturing a sense of magic realism. The setting is, at times, fantastical, with monolithic monuments scattered around the map, but the dedication to crafting beautifully rendered visuals means that it never feels cartoony or aesthetically unpleasing.Frozenheim retains a lot of what made the original city-builders fun but modernises enough that it drops the cumbersome mechanics of old.Inspration of Ork's, and Humans, Dawn of Man, and a little Frostpunk sprinkeled in.Fortunately, Frozenheim isn’t just a superficially wonderful game. Its in-depth mechanics, even for Early Access never failed to impress. From the multitude of building options to the technology tree which opens up additional avenues for each playthrough, Frozenheim continually kept me engaged.On top of the general city-building aspect, there’s also combat and missions. While these lack a little depth right now, they add an additional layer of entertainment to the proceedings. Within my first hour of playing, I was completely drawn in. It was incredibly enjoyable watching as my village expanded from a few houses to a vast bustling settlement. Frozenheim completely nails the serene aspect I was looking for, as developing your city is a relaxing endeavour.One of the most stand-out aspects of Frozenheim is the way it takes conventions and mechanics from the city-builders of old and innovates upon them. It is not that everything in Frozenheim is streamlined, there’s certainly plenty of complexity to go around. It is just that the process of constructing your city never feels overburdensome or fiddly.Whenever there was an issue, such as a fire breaking out or a resource having been depleted, I never felt as if I was left in the lurch wondering why everything was failing. Frozenheim does a good job of making the UI easy enough to understand. So much so, that even a novice to the genre could wrap their head around it. Frozenheim manages to retain a lot of what made the original city-builders fun, all while modernising it enough that it never feels cumbersome.You’re already getting your money’s worth with what’s available. But, with a few more additional maps I can really imagine myself sinking in hundreds of hours.Frozenheim is far more polished than I was expecting.It offers an extremely polished experience with enough content to satiate your city-building real-time strategy needs. Sure, there are some inconsistencies here and there, but for the most part, Frozenheim is a shining example of how to take an overburdened genre and breathe new life into it. This is a genuinely brilliant strategy game with a lot to offer, and one I cannot recommend enough.

_childDocuments_.review: From the 6 hours so far, I can say it looks amazing and it's definitely a fun game. The game (to me anyway) feels like more of an exploration/RTS game. There are buildings you can create around a (small) area and produce resources for troops to explore, it's a good concept and I can't wait to try multiplayer (although I heard it's buggy atm). There's also tech trees like most RTS games and things to unlock more abilities to help in combat and exploration. The combat is pretty cool too although somewhat basic and each unit has different abilities making for a lot of different possible engagements. You can also find different things around the map which give you advantages, it makes you feel like you're actually building a viking settlement which is cool.There are some complaints though, with the biggest being the campaign is literally just 2 missions which took me an hour each to beat while taking my time. That could have been done better, even on early access. There's a freeplay mode which seems to be a 1v1 against an AI and a skirmish mode where you can have multiple AI on the on the map (which I haven't tried yet). There's a few bugs I encountered as well, sometimes a unit will get stuck and you'll have to move it around to free it but it hasn't been game breaking to me (yet), although sometimes the camera freaks out for no reason usually getting stuck on something (it's expected the day after launch). Another thing I'm dissapointed about is the building area, you get a main building with a circle around it where you can build things inside, you can't build outside of the circle so you don't have the freedom like in Age of Empires or Starcraft. It's definitely not as building heavy as they claim the game to be and definitely comes off being more about RTS exploration/strategy combat, which is fine but I was expecting to be able to build a huge viking empire when I picked the game up, and was sad when I found I could only squish about 15-20 buildings in the circle (which can't be moved either from what I'm aware of) There's also only 6 units to build in the game to fight with and although I'm aware they will be adding a lot more in the future, the abilities are nice but more variety would make it a lot more interesting. Also, the AI is predictable (will always come by boat by 20 mins) and the units need some balancing work (archers beat shield bearers in melee..?) might need to be look at.Overall it's pretty good for the price right now but not a dollar more. It definitely seems like a fun game with friends and when they add things in the future it will be even better. It doesn't really qualify to me as a 'city builder' because of all the restrictions, but it's a fun game to put on when you want to kill an hour or two and feel like exploring nice 'Norse' looking landscapes, or wanna mess around with friends. It definitely seems very limited right now with what you can do but that's expected on launch day and it's a super nice looking game at the very least. The tutorial was a little unclear but after experimenting I was able to figure it out and it was straight forward from there. All in all, it's a good game with a couple downsides and a lot of work ahead of it but honestly this game will likely be 40$ in a year when it's fully released and polished up and I have a feeling it'll be a good one (if the dev's care).TLDR: Beautiful looking game with a lot of potential that isn't being fully realised just yet. There are many things that could be done to improve the current state of the game, such as improved building options, more combat units/strategies and more things I haven't even mentioned here I'm sure. If you like exploration/combat RTS games with a touch of city building you will likely enjoy your time on this game but don't expect a masterpiece just yet, perhaps that will change with future updates. I will also update this review as patches come out. Overall, it's not bad but not amazing. I'm excited to see where this game goes with time.

_childDocuments_.review: *Foreword: I've only played 2 and a half of the campaigns for this. Got this game in a Humble Bundle.Tries an interesting amalgamation of city building and medieval RTS, but really ends up mediocre for both.City building/resource management can be summarised into deforestation simulator as wood is pretty much staple for every point of the game with natural tree regrowth so slow I don't blame one for questioning if it exists in the game itself. The options to quicken this growth are not always available in missions (including ones that involve prolonged base building). There is a marketplace that allows resource trading, although at negligible amounts at the higher tech levels. Other notable resources include rock and iron, both finite resources, with iron able to be refined to a higher product , food which consists of a variety of sources, some with a catch that they cannot be operated in winter. However, with multiple of these sources (2 mills (T3), 2 orchards (T2)), food is never a resource I've really needed to worry about. T1 food is either fishing docks (which is only relevant in the early campaign, with the 2nd and 3rd ones not really having them) and hunting lodges which rely on animals being present, which is way less than one would expect.The end result for missions is a repetitive rushing of the tech tree to getting higher tech food options and the marketplace to get wood to spur that rush, afterwards building the bank of disposable resources to keep selling for wood. At that point begins the constant cycles of waiting for that wood bank to slowly build up so you can progress to either build up your city and/or your army, or research technology. While there is an option to speed up the game, it doesn't remove the fact you will still be idly waiting around for a lot of the game. But hey, perhaps the RTS part won't be too bad. Unfortunately, the RTS element is pretty awful. The control scheme for this game is both bare bones and unpredictable. Units have 3 stances, aggressive (kill everything), defensive (supposedly hold ground), and default (tooltip suggests that this is a balance of the other 2). There is also an Attack move, which is weirdly bound to Left Control. In actuality, it's a complete mess. Units in defensive stance may not attack units in its vicinity at all even if it is being attacked. Attack move seems to have some issues with building priority over units resulting in units bypassing enemy units for that opportunity to burn a house down. Setting units to Aggressive stance is pretty much attack move on steroids. Default is the "ideal" stance with units engaging enemies nearby and holding ground but I've seen the AI for that break and units switch to the aggressive stance anyways. In all, the underlying pathfinding/AI makes unit control incredibly clunky and unpredictable. The UI being buggy and many commands lacking hotkeys aggravates this even further.There isn't really much depth to the strategies either. Due to the way battles work, melee units enter giant slogs against each other where bigger damage number win with ranged units helping to tip the favour to their side. The unit abilities are interesting on paper, but in practise the strategy is simply popping self-buffs as your units engage to get damage numbers up. In summary, very drawn out base building/resource management with frustrating unit controls and lackluster RTS elements. Sitting through repetitive missions of resource buildup to really subpar combat ran its course for me leading me to drop this mid-campaign. For USD$20, I'd argue it's a bit steep for what you get and there are still really weird bugs that pop up that result in crashes. The only redeeming factor is the campaign narrative was interesting for the stories I completed.

_childDocuments_.review: When I was skimming through the upcoming releases,  immediately caught my eye due to its promising premise of developing your own Norse colonies, which was supposed to be spiced up by the inclusion of themes from their folklore. Throw in some ground and naval combat, as well as a bit of exploration, and you have a solid foundation for a Nordic-themed city-builder; hence, I was naturally excited to give it a go.Unfortunately, my dissatisfaction appeared swiftly, partially because of the questionable marketing on the . While I understand that I should not overdo it with my assumptions, I still expected to play a proper city builder, as the lovely “rich settlement management” catchphrase promoted. Alas, instead I got a game filled with subpar combat-oriented content that became repetitive during the very first campaign, yet I had to endure through four more.For sure, the price of seventeen euros and the apparent lack of resources within the studio will not guarantee the qualities of triple-A titles. However, in such a case,  should have leaned in one and only direction, either focusing on settlement management or on more complex combat. Instead, it fails at both aspects, delivering a half-baked, tiresome experience. Because apart from the gameplay loop, there is nothing else worth elaborating on: the narrative exists just so the various clans could fight with each other, and you can forget about some philosophical or artistic themes right away. Not that their omittance would be a negative per se, but since the gameplay is in the state it is, then such parts could help it to become more bearable to play.Let us elaborate on the abovementioned issues then, shall we? The management of your colony has the foundations you would expect: you construct buildings that gather various resources, such as food, wood, stone and more; apart from that, there are craftspeople and, of course, military-oriented structures. Yet, there is no variety whatsoever! For example, food counts as the same resource no matter whether your villagers go fishing, hunt deers or harvest wheat. Where is the promised “rich settlement management” that would influence the happiness or health of my people based on the variety of meals? That is saddening, especially since jarls even fought over these from time to time.Truthfully, the complexity is just not there. Again, that would not be a problem if the game would not market itself as something it is not, leaving me with these ambivalent thoughts. The only management aspect you will find here is assigning villagers to their respective workplaces; even their happiness level, required for getting access to higher-tier buildings, is not complex at all. I would even dare to say that I did not have to focus on maintaining it, as it increased on its own anyway. Nevertheless, that does not mean that the mechanics do not work — they do in their simplistic way; there is just not much depth in it.The combat is nothing to write home about either. There are only a few types of units, ranging from regular axemen to armoured shieldbearers, as well as archers and spearmen, operating on the classic rock-paper-scissors principle. Each has some ability, such as stunning opponents for spearmen or higher precision for ranged units, disabling the friendly fire for a few seconds. For a so-called city-builder title, it is a simple yet effective system. Unfortunately, the actual encounters are not enjoyable, mainly due to the semi-broken responsiveness of units. They tend to not follow your lawful orders, rushing to the nearest enemy despite me clicking like crazy and so on. Perhaps they were deceived by Loki? Who knows.Moreover, the artificial intelligence behaves feebly-mindedly, being capable of escapades like rushing towards your army just to suddenly retreat and then rush back at you. Thus, it is not really challenging to deal with them. It can be annoying at times; that is, however, due to the campaigns’ scripts, as they tend to spawn a bunch of enemy units at the most random, inconvenient place possible just to slow you down. To give an example, I destroyed a supportive base of the near village, so I would not get flanked. Nevertheless, the game infinitely spawned up to three units there, forcing me to go around and launch my assault elsewhere, as they were not smart enough to follow me nor defend their home. Such an artificial way to increase the difficulty is not exactly challenging nor enjoyable; it just horrendously prolongs my playtime.Apart from that, there is a bit of exploration, allowing you to find some stashes scattered around the map, as well as barbaric camps or animal lairs to clear; all of that rewarding you with bonus resources for your lovely colony. An occasional side quest is present to spice things up a bit, too. It is not much, but it is sufficient enough for such a title, and your opponents tend to interact with these too, which might lead to interesting situations at times.Sometimes you have to leave the ground and set sails, which surely is an intriguing addition. Regrettably, the control of naval units is quite clunky – the fights are even worse – so I mostly ignored them unless it was mandatory for finishing the mission. I mean, it is kinda hilarious to purposefully avoid the naval aspect in a Norse-oriented title, but it is what it is, eh? Artificial intelligence is even more annoying during these encounters, as it constantly tends to flee from you unless it has a massive advantage.You will engage in all of that both in the campaign and other scenarios, such as skirmishes or modes related purely to the settlement management. Sadly, despite the different objectives, it all felt kinda same to me, mainly due to the lack of variety. Even the playable clans are not that diverse, only differing in some minor abilities and upgrades, so even some variety between the factions is rather non-existent.While expected, the audiovisual aspect is a bit underwhelming, though I would not call its visuals ugly at all, and after a while, I started adoring them for being at least quite colourful, as the scenery changes based on the current season. However, the way some people look is just not Norse-like, but rather a wanna-be take on mainstream Vikings, which is a shame. Lastly, the audio is subpar, filled with repetitive sounds and a lacklustre soundtrack.Overall, I truly cannot recommend , as it feels like a weird mishmash that tries to do everything but fails at being at least mediocre in its respective aspects. That is saddening, especially because of its exciting premise. Alas, after the introductory two or three hours, I basically saw everything the game had to offer and then just proceeded to sink more time in its repetitive gameplay loop. I can only hope that the potential sequel or another title will be much, much better.

_childDocuments_.review: Even though this game is in early access stage, you can clearly see there is a lot of potential here. The graphics are excellent for a modern rts game-not the cartoon graphics you see in other rts games which is great. The building mechanics are interesting and fun. The music and atmostphere is good.  However, the current version of the game is quite bug ridden and the controls aren't very responsive. The combat also seems not right.  Movement around the map seems stiff and the scroll with the camera angles isn't great. All in all though most of these issues can easily be fixed during updates which are coming soon and I have seen enough so far to impress me enough to continue checking out the game and watch it develop. I would recommend to buy this as it has the potential to be a great rts in the future but have patience with the devs as it is a work in progress. Overall, I am happy and recommend it for any rts fans out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Frozenheim

_childDocuments_.review: Considering its Early Access, its a fun game. Deffently needs more, but the concept is really good. Bugs are almost not noticeable, just got some troops stuck, and you can get camera stuck on a mountain. Runs very smooth, and is a simple game to pass the time. Can me Diffacult, you can littraly be raided and destroyed if you dont have an constant flow of troops, once you able to out pace the raids, you can wipe them out pretty fast. Will keep playing, Cant wait for more content.
_childDocuments_.name: Frozenheim

_childDocuments_.review: In my modest opinion Frozenheim is a really decent game. Played through it a bit and will keep playing.It really has a nicely balanced mix of RTS elements inspired from Relic games and city building, allowing for fun matches or a a decent campaign.It's a shame that most negative reviews come from people who expected a standard city builder where you grow and keep growing but I would also blame this on the presentation of the game on steam which describes it as a city building sim more than a "Norse AoE with more advanced mechanics".The only cons so far from my side: Voices, they sound scarily robotic.
_childDocuments_.name: Frozenheim

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like a unpolished gem. It's already good. Performance is amazing, it looks and sounds immersive. A must buy for the price.Edit: Before anyone complains about the lack of mechanics or features some other games have: Look at the damn price! What do you expect?This is still indie. Good looking idie!
_childDocuments_.name: Frozenheim

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful RTS game that delights slightly more often than it frustrates. It still needs work in balancing and VERY buggy ships. Campaign is a really mixed bag, too. There's some exciting challenges and several extremely boring games. Here's the hoping the developer keeps working on this game. It has a lot of potential.
_childDocuments_.name: Frozenheim

_childDocuments_.review: First impressions:It's totally fine to NOT recommend this game but as it's early access I'll be giving a benefit of a doubt and be recommending.It totally has potential but there's a few things that hit your eyes straight from the beginning.The game needs graphics optimisations. I have gtx 1060 6gb but it still requires quite a lot of juice from the card. The recommended card is 1070 but it shouldn't be so taxing as it is on a 1060 but oh well, whatever.Gameplay is where it needs most love though. 1. The pathfinding is terrible. Often part of your units won't go anywhere for some reason which is major let down in this kind of a game. In the campaign my scouts somehow went from a cliff in to water and got permanently stuck there. 2. Archers do friendly fire which brutally annihilates your own units. This is of course "realistic" and there's an option for "hold fire" but it only increases micro-management. There's no option to disable friendly fire. The mini map isn't of best quality so it's not as easy to react to enemy forces attacking your units and pressing the hold fire in order to avoid your units being annihilated by your own. It becomes annoying and not fun to constantly manage archers. As also it's not clear when do they fire arrows. Might be more clear on maximum settings but I can't play on them without overheating my gpu.3. Small things like rotating buildings with middle mouse button is kinda slow. It can be sped up with shift clicking as it rotates to be in direction with closest building but sometimes it bugs out and places it inside the other building half way. 4. Building is overall limited and resources are fairly easy to come by early on. The system feels underwhelming and without any deep meaning to it or challenge. You can't build outside your main building radius which is both good and bad.5. Some things aren't explained enough in the game. Unit stats are confusing. For example what's the "stats" difference in practice between axemen and spearmen? Are spearmen just "better" because they have overall better stats or do they function differently? How much do archers do melee damage vs ranged damage? Stats and information presentation is not user-friendly at all. There's some short "tips" given but they're always lacking some crucial tid bits. 6. When enemies are near your gate it can't be opened for neither side. So your melee units have to go through another gate to the other side and the enemy units tend to follow your units along the wall. 7. Double clicking the unit command group hotkey (1-9) doesn't bring your camera to the unit as it usually does in all rts.Game feels and plays half baked. If it won't change for better as developers promise close to or at release, I will change to negative.

_childDocuments_.review: Great RTS game, reminds me a bit of Age of Empires (but with vikings!). Honestly though, these guys have done a great job implementing viking culture into the buildings, units, perks, overall environment, etc... really making it a nice and unique game. Unit pathing and combat can be improved, but I'm sure that's coming.
_childDocuments_.name: Frozenheim

_childDocuments_.review: It is a nice, relaxing Age of Empires styled game, settled in the Viking universe. It is not great, not bad, but fun for a while. The mechanics lack a bit and rarely you got a unit stuck in a boat on the water. Enjoyed it! Do I recommend it? Well, if you like the village setup and once in a while a little bit fighting it is good. Yes. I do. The AI does not challenge you.
_childDocuments_.name: Frozenheim

_childDocuments_.review: I waited several months to play the official release and I can say I'm quite disappointed. It looks like there were several ideas what game to make and they decided to take a few small features from each, but not make anything deeper than that.- City building and resource managment is very basic.- RTS elements are very standard, nothing stands out.- Exploration is very lackluster- Storytelling is quite bad, you don't really understand what is happening. Even some names are just generic - "His father, Jarl died", "the evil clan is no longer a threat" and so on.The only thing that I really like is the music to be honest
_childDocuments_.name: Frozenheim

_childDocuments_.review: Very beautiful crafted game with a lot of potential. I played through the campaign and also completed one normal game (single player, find all rune stones and defeat the enemy village), but I didn't touch multiplayer. While the core mechanics are implemented and the game is definitely in a playable state, there is certainly still a lot missing and a lot of improvements to be made.  The enemy not having an AI was the case for "New Game". I have now also played the Skirmish mode with three enemy AIs and this time they actually attacked me pretty quickly. The replayability is nevertheless not great at the moment.That being said, I nevertheless had 7ish hours of fun and am definitely looking forward to seeing what this game will become.Which is also the reason I am giving this an positive review.So in conclusion, if you're looking for a completed game which offers countless hours of gameplay, you should probably wait a few months. However if you don't mind the limited content and are excited to follow this game and give feedback to developers, it might just be worth a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Frozenheim

_childDocuments_.review: I really can't recommend this to anyone.... It's kind of a stale combination of Northgard and AoE, but I'd rather play either of those instead, because this just feels like a knock off in many ways (you know when a game feels like a mass produced mobile game that has all kinds of systems or looks nice, but has no real depth to it). The visuals are great, which are the main reason I grabbed this from a sale, but it's got nothing new to bring to the table and gets boring after just a short while. Simply just not worth my time and I regret not asking for a refund while I still had the chance.
_childDocuments_.name: Frozenheim

_childDocuments_.review: Feel like i have to have my 10 pence worth as i feel the bad reviews are a little over the top. Firstly i paid £12 for a EA and yes the town hall radius was terrible on the first day (they have now patched it)Graphics are lovely the game play is fun i play with a good friend and we have had some really cool Skirmishes .This game will be very good in the future so id suggest paying early price and coming back to this in a few months and you would have a £30 game for £12
_childDocuments_.name: Frozenheim

_childDocuments_.review: The fundamental concept and mechanics of the game are great, the sound is good, the graphics are amazing and it’s a heap of fun to play.  The way resources are gathered and villages assigned I think is really smart, it allows you to focus more on controlling your troops, scouting for loot and microing in battle, which is awesome. All units having special abilities also add a nice flavor. It’s not as APM intense as AOE though this is actually refreshing and gives it more of a chill vibe to play. I’II agree, it does need more work to be polished, the pathing is a little buggy and frustrating and the AI is very underdeveloped and underwhelming to play against.  All in all, it’s well worth the price and I would highly recommend. I really hope development continues as this game is already good but has so much potential to be outstanding!
_childDocuments_.name: Frozenheim

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the campaigns and I absolutely love this game. Coming from a fast-paced RTS background, I wasn't sure how I'd feel about it, but it's a really nice change of pace. It's perfect for zoning out and listening to a podcast while you build up your economy and defend from the occasional enemy raid. My only complaint is that unit micro still feels very clunky. The maps can also be a bit disorienting if you're used to more cartoonish graphics, but you get used to it pretty quickly. I'd definitely recommend giving it a try if you're in the market for a new RTS.
_childDocuments_.name: Frozenheim

_childDocuments_.review: I appreciate the effort the devs have gone into for this game. Looks very nice, however it just plays 'jagged'. So what I mean by this, is that it's not fluid. The scroll is too quick, the shift rotation is too quick, units walk very stiff 'with little real animation'. Combat feels dead, with no emotion or intensity. The AI is not great, my warriors stand behind the other characters and stop attacking. The game has depth and attempts to merge games like banished, Northgard, settlers and others into itself. It almost seems overly complicated. I feel like I am playing with robot characters. Basically the game looks nice, and has potential, it just falls short for me due to the lack of immersion and life that it fails to bring.
_childDocuments_.name: Frozenheim

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing RTS games for over 20 years and this game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ solid. I grew up playing AOE1,2,3 Empire Earth 1,2,3 Lord of the Realm 2, Knights and Merchants etc etc. With that being said this game feels like a great classic RTS game with a tight little spin and its fun as hell.The developers are very active, they have their own discord, I've asked numerous questions and I have had at least 3 developers talk to me within minutes of asking a question or submitting a bug or even just chit chatting.This game has UNLIMITED AMOUNTS OF POTENTIAL. It does need some work. What is released though is solid. There are some very minor bugs but the game plays well. IT IS EARLY ACCESS and it does feel like an Alpha but only in lack of content. The game LOOKS polished minus the content which is coming in later updates.10/10 for graphics9/10 for building (I absolutely love the building and you can customize your longships, its actually bad ass)7/10 for combat (the combat is very plain) you can click and drag formations but you never need to8/10 for sound (you have to zoom in a little to hear anything and its really annoying my biggest complaint actually)This is all I'm going to rate for now because the game is in an alpha state and it just wouldn't be right.For 16.99 you're getting 2 campaign missions and 3 skirmish maps with various spawns on each map. The developers have already said in their discord more maps and content is on the way with the next update.I have really high hopes for this game.(Things i would like to see) this is for the developers :P-At least 20 more multiplayer/skirmish maps-add factions/clans (you pick your "clan" KIND'VE but I would like their to be various clans with unique units.-I think it would be cool if they added more clans and clan benefits (would also be cool if each clan had their own banner like the ship building)-I would like to see the buildings upgrade as you age up minor things like adding stone to the trim of the buildings or something-I would also like to see more unit diversity among your soldiers (different hair styles or something) and also see their armor upgrade as you level them up too. When i upgrade their shields/spears/armor i would like to see that reflected on the soldiers models-the AI on medium does feel a bit meh like the game is abnormally easy-The maps feel a big too tight when building, i know its apart of the strategy and city development but it almost feels a bit to tight and you kind've have to squeeze ♥♥♥♥ in and it just doesn't feel right. I ABSOLUTELY LOVE how you can form the shape of your own farmland and walls though...THEY DID SUCH a good job with that. The building they have is very intuitive.-I would also like to see bigger maps with up to at least 6 players-The sound effect range is a bit tight as well you have to zoom in to hear your men fighting which im not overly fond of. ( you dont have to zoom all the way in but its enough to be an annoyance)

_childDocuments_.review: It's a typical low budget RTS. There are literally hundreds of games similar and this game offers zero edge against the others. There's nothing clever about it and nothing particularly charming,Additionally, there are bugs and errors to contend with including crashing and graphic jolts. Other bugs are gameplay related and often require starting the mission again.There are a bunch of loosely connected missions which are very samey and become dull quickly.The music is okay but repetative.The voice acting from the VERY american sounding female is just horrible. It would be better to turn her off all together. Seriously, is it difficult to find an actress who sounds even slightly nordic?!?!? There are hundreds of thousands of Danes, Finns, Swedes and Nords who would have done the narration job, in English with a wonderfully attractive and appropriate accent.The graphics are average for the game and suffice to make it enough to look at.The game play is clunky and un-intuitive.The writing of the campaign levels is poor and half finished.There is zero enduring progress i.e. you start at the beginning of development every single mission and there is no progression of skills or development (Warcraft: Orcs and Humans smashes this game to pieces on that front and it was released in 1994!)In short it is another weak attempt at and released into a market with FAR too many cheap and weak games in it it's almost impossible to find anything good.In short, I wouldn't bother with this game and I won't be going back to it again. Waste of time and energy.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this is great game, especially considering its early access status. It presents a solid platform for the developers to tweak going forward. Here are some humble suggested improvements from a long time player of the genre:Resource Management: While the actual structure of the resource production is fairly straightforward it would be helpful to see exactly how much of each resource you are producing in the positive daily. Example: I have 1200 food stored, while producing 120 food a day, and consuming 118 food per day, my daily net is +2. I don't need all of that data, but simply seeing 1200 food (+2) would help me to manage expansion of the village.Camera Control: More zoom features with less abrupt movement would be beneficial. The terminal as it stands sometimes becomes erratic when you get near large land features as it tries to move the camera lower to compensate. Map Movement: There currently, unless I didn't find it, doesn't appear to be a function to move quickly between areas of the map.Unit Grouping: A grouping feature by highlighting certain units and numbering them as a group. (Typically accomplished in RTS games by highlighting and using ctrl + #) This could work with the movement function to allow you to fast travel to each army group.Unit Selection/Movement: The unit selection and movement keys are fairly clunky at this point and require refining for the final product. Again, all of the above are just suggestions. I am thoroughly impressed with the product you have put forward and look forward to following your franchise in the future.

It plays just like similar games with added "this button makes you shoot faster for 7 seconds" and nothing else strategic.In the end, it was boring.  Combat was boring enough to be pointless, exploring was a little interesting, building was not overly complex, management was possible but not really necessary.Beautiful graphics, not much going on in complexity or engagement.

Fairly simple at the moment, so maybe not one for the people who like to build complex spreadsheets about Anno and the likes.It's get a couple of quirks, as one might expect from an early access game, but they seem to get addressed pretty quickly, and the devs seem to be pretty responsive in general.

_childDocuments_.review: I like mostly everything about this game but the only thing where it falls short is the difficulty. It is far too easy. I even tried starting a map where I chose to have 8 other teams of enemy at the hardest difficulty. all I had to do was secure the perimeter with a few towers and a wall, from then on the AI didn't have a chance and felt like I was playing some sort of creative mode. I let the game run for a long period and the AI never ramped up their attacks also.. didnt start bringing in the heavy artillery and just stuck to sending a few people now and then.. which were killed within seconds of approaching the base. TLDR: Great game but dont expect a challenge at the moment.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was quite fun but with the recent introduction of the discontent mechanic it's now just irritating. The discontent rises way too quickly compared to how quickly you can gather the resources for a feast which is supposed to reduce discontent. Oh and during a feast which 'reduces' said discontent you get notifications to state discontent is rising. Also the feasts don't reduce discontent to the level stated within the game. _childDocuments_.review: A simple building game with some combat, It feels a little bit like a bunch of older games, settlers/anno, age of empires and a bit of warcraft 3 because of hero characters with abilities.The combat itself isn't too impressive and heroes make it alot easier, the naval battles are kinda bad.The small survival aspect of the game is not difficult either food is easy to come by.Overall its a fun game, at one point I said i'd play for an hour then it was 2 hours later, just building my little town, where I could have finished the campaign mission ages ago, but just building a town to your liking is still fun.One negative is where the AI does cheat, sometimes they have a whole side base up in a matter of seconds in some missions.

_childDocuments_.review: Can't select enemy units to know why the ranged archers are kicking the ass of my axemen in melee range.I don't know nothing buggy was happening but the combat felt... inaccurate of the results that kept happening.May come back to this at a later date but probably not. Too many of these games are coming out that do a better job at first impressions and execution.The pictures that are shown I don't reflect the reality of how you would build, The game is more RTS and less simulation which is how the videos/screenshots portray it more as a simulation type game
_childDocuments_.name: Frozenheim

_childDocuments_.review: After 2.8 hours of play, I can say that the game is good. The graphics are very nice and the mechanics are learned very quickly.So and all those who complain about the game is unbalanced and there would be not much content .. Hello? This is an early access game! This means that the developers are still working on the game and gradually improvements will appear, so stop crying and don't give the game bad reviews right away! Oh and to the people who were hoping for a city builder here .. you should keep playing Sim City -.-The game has a lot of potential and if the developers make an effort and regularly bring patches and new content into the game, this game could be really awesome. And let's be honest, 14 euros isn't that much for a game with such great potential.All these bad and stupid reviews just make sure that other players don't buy the game. This in turn ensures that the developers hardly make any sales and in the end the game is never finished because at some point the developers run out of money. In this way, quite a few good games with a lot of potential have never been completed.My advice is to buy the game if you're interested, but keep in mind that it's an Early Access game, so be patient with patches and new content.

_childDocuments_.review: It's got a long, long, long way to go, but if you can pick it up at a sale for a soft price, it's a great investment. Combat and unit selection are still a bit iffy, but they'll get around to it in time.So to reiterate: get it at a sale, and build yourself a cool Nordic settlement!
