_childDocuments_.review: Looking good for the price of the game. I can see this is going to be a decent foundation for what I hope to be an amazing game in future. It's worth picking up, now, if you want to see more about what it's like or you could wait for development later down the road, as I imagine this will turn into an amazing game, if raised correctly.Notes for the Developers:1) Some of the units move in an odd fashion. My axemen will go straight West and then South if I click a location directly South of them. It could use some polish.2) Sometimes I'll order multiple teams of men to a location and sometimes one team will simply freeze in place halfway there. 3) My camera slams into the ground if I dare to get too close to the mountains. I can understand stopping me from moving further into the mountain but I'd rather not slide down it, if possible.4) Fires happen randomly, it seems, which is odd, since I figured the game would give a reason for it. At the same time, the people in charge of a fire seem to treat handling a fire as the same as taking a leisurely stroll. 5) I really hope we get some good narrator for the cutscenes in the future, perhaps a enchanting female voice or a gruff old viking voice. Also consider slowing down the cutscenes a small bit since I was barely able to read everything in time, at the beginning, and I do believe I am a fast reader, so others may struggle.6) The building rotation wasn't very precise and I had to hit R and T a bunch of times to align a building how I wanted.7) Cover isn't very well defined. 8) I'd like an option to cancel a building in construction.9) Soldiers seem to die very quickly in fights. I used 15 axemen and 10 archers on a group of 5 axemen and still lost two axemen in the process. Perhaps make all units more chunky? Scouts practically die from a cold breeze on their necks. 10) It's only my preference but an option to enlarge the unit banners would be great, both when they are selected and on the move. Also, I had issues when I wanted to isolate one team from the group as it took several clicks to single one out. 11) Include in the tutorial about team abilities and the well's importance to not lose your entire village to fire.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good Age of Empires style RTS game with a Norse skin. (Edit: I have noticed as of July 2nd, references on the Steam page changed "City builder" to "colony sim", which is still misleading and inaccurate. I have no idea where this nonsense is coming from. The devs? The publisher? Some unpaid intern they have writing their blurbs? But it's utterly bizarre to me that even after changing things, they have no idea what kind of game they're selling. Rest of the review is unedited.)It is ABSOLUTELY NOT a City Builder and that is why it gets the thumbs down. The marketing verbiage is very misleading and quite deceptive unless you look for videos on the gameplay itself. They really should lean harder into the RTS aspects, that it's similar to Age of Empires. Those are not bad things and are quite appealing and enjoyable. There is a discontent/happiness system for your population, and for the life of me beyond outright starving them I have no idea how anything can actually upset them enough to have a tangible gameplay impact. The entire mechanic can be outright ignored, leaving the game just a pure RTS.I do like the game, I intend to keep playing it, but it very much feels like I ordered a steak and was served chicken. Good chicken, mind you, but not what was on the menu. From other reviews, it very much seems that their marketing materials and Steam page descriptions misled many others regarding what kind of game this is.Again, good game, good RTS, really enjoyable, just absolutely not a city builder.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to say, i like what i see, the foundations are solid, but it still has long way to go, feeling of clunkyness is everywhere, especially when trying to get on and from boats, somethimes soldier just get stuck or refuse to board, or even worse, they put your new warship to torch and burn it down, i guess they were cold or something. Also, the build area around your main building is really small, i started skirmish and  20 minutes in, i run out of building space = could not create better and efficient neighborhoods (i love the population idea in this game, around summer, you have the biggest pop booms, but in winter not so much, and you recruit your army from your pop, so you need to carefull not to stretch too thin, humans are resource too!), so i end up slamming housed everywhere, where i could, to feed the meatgrinder, that is valhalla. But it was not nearly enough.But overall, this could be something really awesome, i love the feel of the game. We shall see!

_childDocuments_.review: 4+ hrs, that is how long it took to see everything this game has to offer.Theres 2 very short tutorial style story campaigns, with I assume a 3rd not yet added?  After finishing the first two levels your only choice afterwards is multiplayer, skirmish or new game single player, which I was bitterly dissapointed with, for the simple reason that as soon as you find and wipe out the rival clan, thats it, youve won, the entire new game consists of your starting village for you to build up while constantly being raided by an enemy about 4 troop units at a time (maybe it scales up larger given a longer time) but once youve built your own ship and troops to find the rival clan your essentially finished, there is a couple side quests like find 6 runestones for blessings/special abilitys, and random villager quests to kill random bandits nearby. but as I said above, as soon as you find and destroy the rival clans longhouse thats it, you can continue playing to uncover the map but theres nothing left to do.You cant expand territory beyond your longhouse zone, so if your resources run out you need to rely on trading via markets, even though theres random deposits of resources all over the map that you cant claim or mine which makes no sense, an outpost option might have added a little more to the base building in enemy territory but you can literally complete a new game within 30 to 60 minutes.I bought this on sale for just under £13 and really cant say I feel I got my moneys worth,  the game is good in terms of looks and gameplay, theres just not enough in it, the entire game feels like a one off skirmish mode and I cant see any real replay-ability unless they add a whole lot more to do,  even adding multiple rival clans would have been better than just one that ends the game as soon as their defeated.

_childDocuments_.review: Tough call.Its kinda ok-ish.Lets ignore the pricepoint.I ever rather pay a bit more for a properly done and polished game, especially when it comes to RTS Games that need a lot of attention to detail, gameplay mechanics and design, to engine and presentation or usability.What can slip through and might not be noticed in your typical FPS as a problem, can cause a major issue in RTS games.Frozenheim provides a solid basis to build on, but falls short in the long run.It has interesting gameplay overall, picking a few aspects of different games here and there, but then stops before any of them become interesting enough.Like the season mechanic, could have been a great influence from games like Frostpunk, Northgard and Banished.The game could have had different croptypes for farms that age better or worse depending on the season, winter would need you to have firewood and thus depletes your wood reserves etc.But its just a minor buff or debuff. Not at all interesting, impactful or meaningful to your gameplay.I actually never care about the seasons, AT ALL.Winter can become a major threat in Northgard, here its just a timeframe that makes your units a bit slower, the rest is meaningless.Fisherhuts can still get fish from the sea, hunters still get enough game and there is a way to make cropfields run in winter.I tend to stock up thousands of foodunits and actually never care about food ever again and even outright sell it in larger quantities on the market.Winter? I dont care.There are many of these things that hold Frozenheim back. Where the developer could have been more bold and experiment with meaningful upgrades.Actually the beta version of Frozenheim had much more interesting upgrading. You could combine two clans with each other.What a great idea to experiment with different upgrade combinations, Wolf and Deer? Some foodbuffs, Berserks and faster military production?Cool.But that was scrapped.Upgrading your townhall does nothing special, doesnt give you unique upgrade options to choose from and define your playstyle.Upgrading units is also linear. Plus some damage, plus some speed, plus some defense.Thats it.There is no "Equip your axemen with Two Handed Axes OR pick throwing axes and make axemen ranged units".Would be an interesting choice, but doesnt happen.Survival Mode is ok-ish too.Misses ways to customize your experience.Mutators would have done the trick to make that replayable.Presentation is also somewhat there and then somewhat absent.Ambient sounds arent playing when zoomed out, you have to zoom your camera into the houses to hear your smith hitting the anvil or a dude smashing rocks with a pickaxe.That creates an eerie and weird atmosphere, where you only hear music and a few confirmation sounds when clicking buttons.Graphics are fine, but also relatively flat. Too less wildlife, too less happening.I have 300 people in my village, but only see transporters picking up goods and a few people chopping wood or whatever.People sitting around, chatting with each other, praying?Didnt see any.Birds, sheep, ox, goats running/flying/whatever around?Nope.They dont even eat chicken, i couldnt find any.Economy is also ok-ish but then again is super flat.There are no different food types, just different food sources.Which means, you generate "meat" (the icon), whether its a fishinghut, a cornfield, a hunter or an orchard.Its like Rust all over again, everything is chicken, even fruits.Same goes for other resources.2 or so are processed by buildings like Leather into clothes. But clothes dont actually do anything more than increase "Happiness".I guess.I actually didnt care at all.Happiness was never a factor i had to take care of.There are tons of upgrades etc increasing happiness or preventing "unrest".I never got into a situation where that happened or where it was important at all.And im pretty sure that happiness is a flat mechanic without much of a meaning anyway.Thus resources also only are used to create things, like a new building or unit, but nothing beyond that.There arent any service resources, like lets say Teapots (Pottery) or Mead.Mead is technically there, but only indirectly and not of much use except as a resource you pay with.Its not necessary to please people, make them happy and when they are happy they work harder, fight stronger or unlock new techs.The campaign is pretty cringe.Not in terms of writing. Thats your typical "Oh fantasy norsemen do their fantasy norsemen stuff like praying at trees (of life), killing magical bears, praying at dead stones with holes, ALL TO GET REVENGE.Its basically Northgards story all over again."Uhh those dudes got us off our homeland, now we have to gather, become stronger and fight back to finally live in our homeland again and pay them a lesson."Lame.What makes it cringy is the way its presented.And unrelated woman tells me something about some dudes, while the camera floats a bit and shows me units standing around (with their ingame selection markers shown for some reason) and a dude walking, really weird as if his armor is really scratching his nuts, slowly.Thats your intro scene to a mission.Your reward for winning is the camera showing a tree and that woman talking some generic nonsense about how holy that tree is.Thats it.Im dead honest, AoE2DEs campaigns are absolute narrative masterpieces compared. Presentation should be "refurbished" a ton to not come too cringy and fun.It takes itself serious, and thats fine, but only works when its not just laughable the entire time.I should care about them being kicked out of Homeland. But actually i won the first mission by wiping the enemy clan off the map. So who gonna kick me off now?I cant care, because the campaign is not at all well narrated or presented, or written.What is left:Well, some content to have you playing for a few hours, some gameplay that at least kinda works but is unbalanced and flat.A flat and uninspired upgradesystem.A survival mode, skirmish, a generic campaign and multiplayer with experimental matchmaking and not enough people.Its ok-good looking.Music is great, although it could need a few more tracks.If you search for a game to waste a few hours on, its fine enough to be played.Its not super bad, but it also likely wont become the best strategy game you played.It possibly wont be the game you frequently return to, because you still have to try this one combination or strategy.If you search for a game to waste a few hours with to play with a friend in survival or skirmish, the game offers enough ideas to also keep you busy.Yet the AI is super incompetent or outright idle sometimes, there are no mutators to tweak your challenge or options to make some phases more interesting, like starting only with a settler unit to pick your own starting spot.Its ok.Which is kinda showing in its pricing.At least they know its ok and shouldnt be priced any higher.If you have some spare money left over and desperately search for some fresh RTS air to breath before jumping back into more complex games and possibly invite a friend to mess around with you too, then Frozenheim is a great pick and i can recommend it.If you are by any chance the developer reading this, then i hope you invest some more time to tickle the potential out of this game that it has.With some major polishing and additional features this could actually become a MUST HAVE.Be more bold when designing upgrades and add more options to tweak your base, clan, units, playstyle.Get some mutators in, some more (starting) options for multiplayer and polish presentation.You are close to get the game into the 20-30€ area if you do that.

_childDocuments_.review: If we first get out of the misconception that this IS NOT a Citybuilder, but an old school RTS, we can also consider Frozenheim a good game. Fast, difficult, with a limited number of resources which, however, can be replenished using the temples and "mana" wisely, with aggressive enemies (too much) depending on the campaign maps... enough to guarantee about 40 hours of play at least.But, I must repeat, this is not a city builder.There are structures to be built but there is no micro-management of the community: at most you can decide how many people to assign to the production of a given resource (for example, to cut trees rather than to produce wheat). A little bit to be considered a citybuilder.So: as a citybuilder the game is inexorably rejected.Like RTS, if you like old school games it's worth a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Got this from a bundle deal and was very excited to play it. However, in its current state, I cannot recommend this game (and especially not for $30AUD). It has nice graphics, a good concept, nice mechanics, and seems to be optimised well. It's shallow in both city builder and RTS, but I have fun playing it when it works. Unfortunately, I've just had to quit. I got through the first character leg of the campaign despite the slight bugginess and a few crashes. However, during the third mission of the second campaign leg, my key character died and the game put me halfway through the first leg - an entire two campaign missions back - so that's where I tap out. It's a fun game but this was the final straw, unfortunately. Some other things that bothered me and demonstrate the lack of polish: - The opening cutscene (which seems to be the final video on the steam listing as of today) shreds my poor old computer every time I open it, even though the game itself runs fine. Why??- Upon completion of a campaign mission, the game presents you with "continue" or "main menu". If you click main menu, when you next load in, you will not be taken to the next mission. You will instead be taken to your last save. If you can't get the game to load in on the next mission, take away that main menu button! I don't want to replay things I've already done!- Loading in messes with the discovered/undiscovered objects and units, applying the glitter to already discovered watchtowers and erasing or doubling units seemingly at random. This combined with the last bug is extra frustrating.- The automated resource flag placements is not great, especially for hunters or woodsmen. Many times a wood hut will complain it's unable to find resources when there's stuff just a bit further out.  - The camera. The hills and such make the camera zoom in and out wildly a lot of the time, and it's very irritating. I personally just want to play zoomed out like a civ game, please stop putting me on the ground when I'm trying to oversee military operations. I am LOATH to give a negative review but I'm hoping this encourages the developers to at least fix the bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as i would love to provide the developers with constructive feedback, there is too little to give feedback upon. The game currently does not qualify as a city builder or an RTS and has barely has any content, the features that would be expected of it in this day and age are in their infancy or not there at all including multiplayer which does not work at all.What concerns me is that the game is scheduled to leave the EA as soon as early 2022, which means it has about half a year to make a journey from 0.0.1 all the way to 1.0. I do not believe they are capable of it becase they are grossly overestimating what they can do with a pathetically small team in such a short amount of time.The game is very unimaginative in everything from combat to winter effects to dynamic roads and is extremely boring to play. I cant help but perceive it as an abomination, made of glued together concepts, elements and ideas sawed off other strategy games of the past 1-2 decades.While I could wait and give it a chance my concerns are not just with bugs or lack of content, but core game design and gameplay loop.The state the game is currently in is not acceptable for an early access game, even by early access standards this is shockingly bad. Charging money for this level of incompleteness is dishonest.I have requested a refund - Do not waste your time/money or support bad game developers.

I know maybe is a indi studio and all, not care much about explication, just want to add, hopefully some input that might help in the future:-> The interface gives me mobile game vibes, plasma with 50% opacity. Icons are decent though. -> Campaign is very bad scripted. The first mission is very important, is setting the stage. Mumbles of camped vikings overlaping the main narator voice. The narator script feels mechanic and soulless, doesn't match the atmosphere at all. The story is telling me I need to run from the island even if I got a giga village and army. I left behind a well armored village just to see it burning 3 sec after; immersiveness ruined. Going further same Amelia Black from AOE3 voice that's telling me mechanically what to do. At this point i would be happier if i saw text like in frostpunk and drawings that introduce me to the atmosphere with a sound that match the impact. -> Mechanics are simple and you get bored easily and none of the events feel like they mater. When I choose bear, nothing happens. When I use the temple to make trees grow, nothing again, just trees popping out, same when I up the town center, same when I feast.Kinda mediocre. I would recommend it if it was cheaper, but at nearly 20$ I expected more dedication and artistic vision

_childDocuments_.review: Frozenheim!OK So Frozenheim is a city/colony/sim builder type.   It's pretty fun and I'm glad it's still in Early Access as I have a few thoughts.So you start the first mission and there are challenges, nothing insurmountable.   You have available villagers based on your number of houses, and you assign them to work in buildings.  But you can't have too many houses or your population gets too high and people starve.  I don't know if this first mission is the tutorial or what, but it sort of doesn't really explain how to play, it took me about 30-45 minutes just figuring out what I should be doing, and HOW to do it.So this game has a "neighbourhood" thing going on with the houses, this took me a while to understand.  Unlike other games, where you can just put houses where they fit or where ever is aesthetically pleasing to you, as you like.   In Frozenheim though, your houses appreciate other houses in close proximity, they get a "neighbourhood bonus" which adds to your overall happiness.   This is calculated, at the start, based on how many houses close together you have, and how many water wells.  Later it adds Healers Hut, Temple, etc. all these buildings you need in close proximity of your houses to increase happiness.So, it takes a little bit of getting used too.   My issue is with Mission #2 where after playing the first mission for 3 hours and thinking this is an awesome game, you get into Mission #2, thinking Wow I'm a ragtag force of shipwreck survivors stranded and have to rebuild my society from nothing, this is awesome!   So you get in there, kill a few wolves, find a few more bedraggled and weary shipwreck survivors, and you find your settlement and save them from bandits.  This is great!   So you start building up resource gathering, a Woodcutters Hut and Stone Gathering.   Your men are still beat up but you can survive.  That is until the constant wave of attacks starts.   These bandits start attacking me every 2 mins I swear.  This is less fun!   At least at first I thought I could fend them off.   I begin hastily figuring out if I can construct a healer's hut to heal my forces.   But no, my men are already dead and the bandits are attacking my buildings, I'm through.So I started again!   I went back into this mission with a particular focus on getting a healers hut as quickly as I could, thinking this would save me.   But no, alas.   In order to replenish troops through a healers hut, you need SUPPLY, and at this stage of just starting the mission, we don't have production of iron, leather skins, or clothing to supply soldiers in order to replenish.Not sure why Mission #2 needs to have constant attacks on auto right at the start like this.  But they could turn it off for a few minutes and at least let a guy get some production built up before he is slaughtered.    I am just of the feeling that difficulty should ramp UP in games like these.   Nothing much happens at the start for the first 20-30 mins but THEN you can have auto attacks and start slaughtering me.   Just give me a few minutes to where I feel like I played it at least.With all that being said this is a really fun game, the 1st mission I was pretty excited because it felt like I'd really found a game I enjoyed and it was pretty fun.  But I think Mission #2 could use a few tweaks.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll give it a thumbs-up because I think this game has a lot of potential. I played the classic Command and Conquer and Battle for Middle-Earth style RTS games, as well as city-builders like Stronghold. Frozenheim combines elements from each, but ultimately does fail to reach the peaks that either genre can get to. My number one complaint is on the combat side of things. First and foremost, the troop variety is horribly lacking. With 4 basic unit types, some peasant militia and a single unit you can get by dedicating yourself to one of the deities, there really is little room for strategy and specialization. There needs to be more troop variety, and I'd love to see this come from dedicating yourself more and more to one of the deities. These should not just give 1 unique unit; provide more to really create better differentiation and create almost sub-factions within the game. The AI also needs some major improvements, because right now they're only a threat in the mid-game, and they soon run out of resources and can no longer attack you.Graphically, the game is beautiful and it runs very smooth for me (Intel i7, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060) and the audio is great. I love the little side missions that add flavor as well as the runestones to fight over. The naval combat is reminiscent of Battle for Middle-Earth 2, but less arrows and more boarding. I like it the way it is, but more customization for your ships would be appreciated.Overall, it's a middling RTS and city-builder, but if the developers keep putting effort into it, I think this game has great potential.

I'm looking forward to seeing where this game goes in the future and I'm glad to be a part of the community that will shape the final product. _childDocuments_.review: There is potential but a very long road ahead. Why would i NOT recommend this to anyone - well It's certainly not a city builder, and it's not an RTS, so what is this game? Things you would expect a city builder and/or an RTS to have, that Frozenheim doesn't:- Resource management. Sure there are resources, but they require no thought or effort to acquire or manage. There's no balance and no reason to spend efficiently, so there's no reason to have a strategy or even vary your approach from game to game (2/10)- Population management. This is a big miss, there's so much depth in terms of diplomacy, living conditions and a hundred other on-theme markers that Frozenheim has missed. As above, just build houses and ignore completely (1/10)- Diplomacy. Simply does not exist. (0/10)- Tech and progression paths. There are 3 that i can discern in Frozenheim (buildings, combat units, faith) none have any depth and feel like an afterthought (3/10).- Combat focus. This is where Frozenheim completely falters, for a multitude of reasons:   * Unit options are shallow at best and don't seem to offer any dynamic combat options   * Units have special abilities that do nothing but distract from the next and most crucial point   * Combat is right click and move on. the AI is terrible (pathing, responsiveness, targeting and everything else), there's no real ability to interact with units in combat or to have any meaningful approach to it at all.   * Building a single watchtower seems to single-handedly defeat ever enemy army in single player modes.Combat score (-10/10). It honestly ruins the game and would be better to remove it and focus on other areas.I hope the creators can rescue this before launch, but needing a total reconstruction of the combat system, as well as tonnes of new content and balancing for resource management and progression pathways has me skeptical this will ever be more than it is.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like city building and resoource management games such as Banished, RTS combat with squads rather than single units such as CoH or Ancestors: Legacy, and love viking themes, then this is for you. If I had to tell what game this is more similar to, it would be Northgard.The game is still in Early Access (0.8.0 when I'm writing this) so expect some bugs, especially when using ships. None of them are critical or blocker, but expect bugs here and there. However, for an Early Access title it has already enough content to enjoy it for hours.- It has 4 clans with unique heroes, each of them having 3 different weapons, 4 abilities and 3 stats.- You can build your ships using different settings and raid your enemies!- All units gain XP over time, leveling up your squads (no abilities though, except for the hero). Not only that, you can improve their armors, weapons, speed, etc- It's not a historically accurate game, which is good because Old Norse mythology is way more fun if it's explicit (you can summon powers/spells from Freyja, Loki, Odin, etc)- Its pacing is great, at first you are more focused on creating a solid foundation for your village, while exploring around and completing simple quests from nearby AI towns such as clearing up a bandit's camp. To me this lasts for about 15-20 min. Then you start creating your army and start exploring the sea, raiding the enemies or defending from them, and this takes about 30-45 minutes more. At least this is my experience so far. I guess you can rush things up and end a game in 30-40 minutes or even less, but I personally enjoy taking my time.- Resource management is quite balanced and has some cool helpful stuff like checking out your what your transporters are carrying, or hoy many workers you have assigned to each building by simply holding ALT key. It doesn't have a lot of micromanagement, which is fantastic since you have lots of things to do.- The developers are strictly following their initial roadmap, and they frequently reply to threads (thanks a lot!).Unless you want a 100% free of bugs game, don't hesitate and dive deep into this awesome .

_childDocuments_.review: Greetings!  Today I’ll be looking at “Frozenheim” a hybrid RTS and City Builder that brings forth the old school feelings of Age of Empires.  As always we need to be mindful that this game is in early access meaning that much of the content may not be finalized.  But, the question always remains; is it worth your time?  Let’s discuss!You have my Shield:  At the core this game is more RTS than City Builder.  Like in many old school RTS the economy is less of the focus even though it is more of the work.  You gather resources; you refine the resources and ultimately purchase defenses and warriors of various flavors.  These warriors have abilities and are enjoyable to watch fight (when they work properly).  The unique element of this game is supposed to be the raiding; which doesn’t seem to be anything more than sending your ships to the shore of another camp and attacking them…which you could do via land in most cases.Loki is always up to something:  This game is in early access, so there are a lot of bugs, I watched trees just pop out of the ground and roll around, some screen tearing and other cosmetic bugs.  But the biggest issue was the combat.  Many times you’ll have multiple groups of warriors just stand nearby an enemy because they are fighting something else and no one will help.  This normally isn’t a huge deal but leads to damage that isn’t needed and time wasted.  The game also has a lot to work on in the realm of audio, the music (when it plays) is fairly boring and the sounds of combat and alerts next to non-existent.  I understand that the game is in early access but there are baseline features that are completely missing for such a standard game.I want my share of the Treasure:  When it comes to games I tend to look at price as secondary to enjoyment.  That is to say I don’t care if the game is free or $60.  I say this as I feel that my time (and yours) is worth more than the dollar amount tied to any game.  Why does this matter?  Well, I love RTS and City Building games and I felt bored after the first mission.  The game is uninspired; it promises this Viking world but is ultimately just an Age of Empires with less polish.  Maybe I’m missing something?  Maybe there is a point where the game unlocks into something grand but I’ve just yet to see it and for a game to be good it has to do something to grab the player.Ultimately, this game wants to be a next generation city builder with survival and RTS elements but ends of falling short and honestly feels more like a Viking Age of Empires Mod.  Sorry to say that I’d suggest you pass on this until some more work is done and the game finds itself.  Enjoy!

I liked the way most used paths became treaded to the ground and the piling snow. But I need to point some untested and unpolished stuff. In PL text doesn't fit the UI in some places and it's cut off which is weird because devs are PL. Units sometimes clip through the terrain and are stuck. Destroyed watchtowers sometimes shoot infinitely even when there is no building. There is no way to remove troops from beached boat unless it is driven into the water and parked again. Grass and snow doesn't show up ever again in pathways or places it was  removed. So after a while you end up with squares of mud and multiple forking pathways where the woodcutters decided to just branch out xDI feel like there could be more stuff in this game. Some stuff is useless. I used some units and buildings very rarely or never. Hunter hut and orchard have no purpose when you have windmill and pigpen. I think there should be more buildings and resource chains. Why food is just food? And every battle can be won with archers behind shield wall. There is no significant change if your hero uses one weapon or another. Temple blessings are useless apart from regrowing trees. It's easier to destroy your enemies than collect all stones to start ragnarokThere are no women and children villagers. There are heroines and i think elite shield warriors had a female voice Death sometimes has negative consequences and most of the time not. _childDocuments_.review: It is average, not bad, but not good either. After 11 hours I don't really feel like playing it anymore. I guess you can try it when it's on sale, and set a timer to 1.5 hours, so you can still refund if you don't like it. Gameplay wise it is probably better to play the old Anno 1503 or Stronghold 1. Somehow they felt more engaging. Or maybe I just got tired of this type of game.There are a few things that are a bit broken/not sufficiently functional also:1. If the enemy makes holes in your walls you often cannot just fill them in, but have to destroy parts or make some weird geometry to close the gap.2. Disembarking troops from ships goes only through "landing", meaning that if you put the wrong troop in a ship, you have to sail away, come back and land to get them out again. No just clicking an icon to disembark, even when the ship is landed.3. The maps feel tiny for some reason. Especially due there being a naval aspect. Even the sole 8v8 map felt small for a 1v1, imho. It is just a single big island. No invading another island. The maps also cannot be previewed in skirmish setup afaik.4. The battles also end so fast the special abilities kinda feel useless. They might not be, but I just end up hitting all the buttons quickly during the start of a messy battle and then a few seconds later it is over. There is very little time to position units or analyse what you need. Maybe this is one of the main reasons it doesn't feel as engaging as e.g. stronghold. There it was kinda slower and I would always have time to place swordsmen at the front and archers at the back.The units somehow don't feel right. I generally don't like squads, but in some games they feel ok (like in Stronghold). I like the old original Cnc "recruit a single infantryman at a time" thing. Like how it is in Anno 1503. You can only have 20 squads of 6 units max, so might as well make them individual units. Also the hero unit, while somewhat fun, is overpowered and I feel the game might be better without them.A minor nuisance: The scout's eagle acts like a drone, like in the recent AC games. Doesn't make any sense.The graphics are nice, but the rest kinda feels meh. It is not bad, and in my experience there aren't a lot of bugs as some reviews claim. (I've had a unit disappear once or twice after disembarking in 11 hours) It is playable, but just not very engaging, at least not to me. It is like something doesn't feel right and I can't really tell what it is. I guess it lacks some polish and some features that differentiate the good, fun games from the average ones. But this could just be due to the fact I got used to more complex rt4x games or rts games that are closer to rt4x. Games like Supreme Commander: Forged Alliance, Cepheus Protocol, Executive assault 2, Ultimate Admiral: Age of Sail, Anno 1503 or Star Wars: Empire at War, I have each played for more than 50 hours. This will not happen with Frozenheim.If I could still refund, I probably would. Still I feel it doesn't deserve a negative review. I guess 6/10. With bigger, better maps with multiple islands (and map previews), slower more engaging combat and after fixing the wall and disembarking issues, I think it could maybe be 8/10 or more. A neutral review would be best, but since there's no such option I'll give it a positive review. Hope the review is helpful to people.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated review:I continue to play skirmish mode on repeat because it's graphically gorgeous and hands down my favorite RTS! Some specific notes that I keep thinking over that could use some refinement are:* AI Mechanics - Increasing difficulty on bots will effectively just increase the frequency of waves they send at you. If you defend them off the first time you essentially win. They just build super basic bases and do not expand either  to create outposts or larger armies than about 6-8 units from what I experience. Additionally, they do not capture points of interest (watch towers, rune stones, etc...) or attack them if you occupy. Go scout for all of them then burn that enemy city. * Ships docking - Ships have gotten stuck on land w/o any interference from buildings or walls but I have not had  too many issues with this. * Lumber Mill - It would be nice to include an upgrade where they plant seeds and or try to regrow deforested land rather than relying on capping and holding rune stones. I guess that is the exploration aspect. * Building variety - feels limited but understandably so. Potentially adding a school to train more end-game skills or talents. * Shipyard upgrades - Adding upgrades with shipyards to include travel speed on the water and/or more effective navel combat techniques. ex) Reinforced stitching for sails to increase movement speed for ships. * Heros - Love this and have had a lot of fun trying them all out. Would be nice to have more spec options for the hero itself past weapon and 4 abilities. _childDocuments_.review: Frozenheim is a promising early access 'grand scale' RTS.  What's a "grand scale" RTS? why it's a game like Rise of Nations or Sins of a Solar Empire,  an RTS that has a much larger map, and will generally focus on long term play over short, rushing actions.  In Frozenheim, you spend several in game years setting up your towns infrastructure and economy; exploring your local area, completing small "quests" and scavenging resources, and building customizable Viking Longships till you are ready to launch an attack on your enemies village (Or resist an assault they've launched while you were busy doddering around with your units on the far side of the map).The Positives:The game is gorgeous, especially for an early access title from a small team.  They included a 'photo mode' in their menu, they know what they've got.The level of detail and variety (even for an early access title) is fantastic.  This game has a deep bench of buildings and upgrades to choose from already, with more planned down the road.Economy wise, the game has a pleasant ramp for building; I never had starving peasants or anything out of Frostpunk, but you will notice the seasons and your local resources shift as you expand your town, with a quirky auto-road tool constructing roads where your NPCS most walk.The Negatives:Unit Pathing is Poor.  Units will generally go where you instruct them, but they respond sluggishly, or will need to have the command issued a couple of times to get the correct pathing.  You generally only control military units, but it is noticeable for micro management.Balance on combat is a bit wonky, especially siege damage.  It takes longer to kill four men than it does to burn down a giant mead hall, or house, or ship yard, or any other structure you care to pick.  Healing is confusingly labeled/explained, as units have both "health" and a unit count, similar to COH.Lack of upgrades on structures themselves.  This is likely to be smoothed out as early access continues, but while there are a load of unit upgrades and tech to unlock, most buildings are one time constructions that you set and forget, would like to see the houses evolve over time to effect their stats, or being able to change wooden walls to stone etc etc.Overall this game has alot of promise, and is already a pretty fun purchase.  In a genre that is fairly starved for content, this game really brightened the horizon for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Frozenheim is playing in a field that hasn't be much popular outside of the usual triple As : RTS. For the first time, you can play an RTS game based on the Viking era and I got admit, this is refreshing. As it is still an alpha, there are the usual bugs you can imagine when it comes to early developing games and for the cost of 14€, I would say it is reasonable. For sure, it still requires balance, correction, voice acting, proper cinematic transition at the end of campaign missions and more, but bear in mind: if you want to buy the game, it is worth it at this price at the moment. Graphics are amazing. It is really refreshing to see that much vegetation and colours and even the grass is awesomely detailed. The camera has difficulty to tackle the different altitudes on the map, so sometimes you will suddenly see the it fall to its death and kissing the flowers but nothing the devs can't fix. The water needs to be improved as it looks more like a transparent blueish filter rather than real water but that should come soon. The landscape, as beautiful as it is, looks sometimes unnatural especially the way some gorges and cliffs are cut but it does not ruin the immersion. Models are greatly detailed but the infantry ones are fairly repetitive. Different shields, different faces with female warriors would be great to add more diversity to this viking era. However, for an RTS, it is almost the first time I see realistic human models being that detailed. The resource system is interesting, trees repop fast but I understand people complaining that they repop at all. In my opinion they shouldn't like most RTS games. Fighting is still at its early stage with animations not being that subtle while changing from moving to fighting, models stack over themselves instead of trying to move around to get into the fight, sometimes your units heal in combat but otherwise, it is enjoyable. I haven't tried the multiplayer yet as I am not interested in that sort of thing. Finally, the music is great but should perhaps be a bit more inspired by Wardruna for example to give the game a Vikinger atmosphere.

_childDocuments_.review: This one is kind of an oddity. It's unique, for sure. Being honest- I've been going through a "viking phase", so of course, i'm in. Without regard to future updates, we'll talk about what you're getting right now (14/June/21). To start with, the description oversells the depth of the game, and what you're getting. I think the most fruitful way to review this game is going to be by taking that apart, so let's get started. Is there some rts elements? Sort of. It's "Rts style" the same way something like "They Are Billions" is RTS styled. I'm not 100% sure where all the "Anno" refrences come from, but i'd say this is closer to a "Age of Empires" more than Anno or (Insert RTS here). The ability to "starcraft" up your base is there, but with the build space limit in place. . . well, it just doesn't lend itself to building strategy. Tactical combat (ala Total War)- No. The unit diversity isn't high enough for a real "This unit counters that" type of decision making, and the thought process that come with that. At least currently, the most effective "meta", is to just zerg units in. Seasons/time- There are season changes, but really it just feels like a throttle on your progress more than having meaningful consequences.Survival- Thus far I've only seen one positive, and no negative "events", from good and poor "survival" (IE- Having a surplus of food). It's worth noting that the popup event for surviving well seems to be just that, a text popup. No tangible effect, despite it telling me some of my villagers decided to "join the army". Set sail, explore, conquer- Ehhhhh this one is another "Kinda". The maps i've played so far are mostly "Multiple island" type maps. So boats end up being *mainly* annoying troop transports. Especially if you're building at any heavy clip. "Exploration" doesn't yield any useful reward (Outside the blessings), and your primary goal is to conquer the other clans? You'd be better served by sticking some scouts in a rowboat to find the enemy, then just pushing straight into them. Overall Impressions- It's a viking skinned, graphically updated, Age of Empires. With some of the depth sacrificed to the Gods of Pretty Video Games. Their goal *seems* to be to combine Total War, AOE, and FrostPunk. The problem with trying to appeal to everyone, is you usually end up appealing to no one. I'm recommending this for people with an AOE itch that they wanna scratch without the graphical downgrade. But really. . . come back in 6 months. Personally, i'll be leaving this one shelved for a bit, and checking in on it every couple months.*Bugs* I do wanna point out I only ran into 3 bugs, 2 that was in multiplayer and one that also happened in single player. The first was a permanent black screen after tabbing out to discord, that forced me to restart my entire PC. The second was a minor connection issue that resulted in the above black screen, again. The third is pathing. I'm gonna call this a bug, in the hopes that the Devs didn't attempt to make the pathing atrocious. But it is atrocious. God help you if you wanna land more than one boat on a shore at a time.

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't played that much but i want to give an honest opinion especially for the devs.We bought this game as 4 players to play together, or rather against each other.Things that were good about this game:- The graphics are fancy, the music is nice and the multiplayer maps in general seem fair enough, though not being random in anyway with fixated spawnpoints does press negative on replayablity, which we would not do rn anyways.- The Settlement Building itself seemed nice, not too complicated either. We just noticed that on normal quanitity of resources we were mostly flooded by them more than we could spend, so we turned it down making the game slower in a more comfortable pace.Things that weren't very good but ok:- Several crashes throughout the main menu or trying to load into the game on always different individuals (so it wasn't a pc issue).- People end up in different playerslots on their client so you cannot actually distribute teams as they kind of turn out random anyways.Things that were staightup bad and made us not replay it:- Combat is a Horror, atleast in a PVP scenario, you command units to move somewhere, they first run into random directions for ages or in circles, before eventually making their way where they are supposed to be. Ships tend to just randomly stop midway to their destination and needed to be commanded again. In general all the unit movement and getting a ship on shore was very tedious and not nice. Also units sometimes got stuck temporarely or permanently in terrain like forests or hills/mountains.- Archers... We have checked keybindings and well, haven't found any solution to it, when you tell Archers to attack a unit or building, they first run up melee range before starting to do anything, which is very bad for obvious reasons. Your best bet would be to set them to offensive/aggressive behaviour, so they attack anything in sight and then just command then to walk close enough and stop them there so they'll automatically attack, this doesn't allow to focus any specific units tho and HOWEVER this does not work for Buildings, so my friend had a wood fence with watch towers behind, and i tried to attack the watch tower with my archers which was an impossible act as they just tried to run melee into it without finding a way, leaving them there with offensive/aggressive stance made them afk infront of the fence as there wasn't a unit to attack while the watchtower happily kept shooting on them.- Defeat, yes... defeat is very horrible in pvp, not because you lost, but because of two things. FIRST, there is no spectating, but you need to stay in the lobby as a host regardless or the game will immidiatly stop. SECOND AND THE WORST, if 1 player is defeated, another one entirely independend loses the game aswell for no reason.If the devs manage to fix all those bad points, its a game with great potential and fun for short playing sessions as rounds in general wouldn't take as long. But as the gamestate is right now, i strictly recommend against buying this if you come for multiplayer pvp. Singleplayer i can not judge at this point.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright. Veteran RTS Player here who plays a lot of city builders, RTS, colony survivors. You name it.  I played this on stream as well actually and I am an extremely hard critic because I have high expectations for RTS in general.  Unfortunately Frozenheim really didn't rub me in a good way and I felt like I had a cactus stucked up my ass for the past 3 hours and 30 minutes.However, this is an early access game and I will not refund in hopes my poor mans money will maybe make a difference in update as well as this review.The Good:- They decide to combine: Anno, Frostpunk, Total Wars, and alittle of Age of Empires in one game and give you a city builder Real Time Strategy- The environment is beautiful. Absolutely beautiful, especially when the rain and snow comes in. I felt truly alive when seasons hits you.- The music is pretty decent. I'm not really a viking instrumental artist so I can't compare the music to our ancient times of viking conquest.  It was enjoyable.- Game always have something to keep your mind busy, no emptiness, music plays in a great tone. You have nature magically speaking to you in the trees or the seasons.- Unique City Builder, you don't really see a viking city builder type- The game barely crashes which is always a good thing in my book.The Bad:- They tried to combine: Anno, Frostpunk, Total Wars, and alittle of Age of Empires in one game. The thing is, this is extremely hard to do and very hard to accept in multiple ways.  Its like going quantity over quality.  There wasn't really any quality in any of the multitude of the games mentioned in this.  They tried to copy total wars map movement which is horrible for an rts that has building at the same time especially in a multi-sense combat and failure of navigation for effective RTS-PvP experience.  It was great in total wars cause it was mainly only units on the map and knowing your map is great.  but if the map starts scrolling the right and I'm moving on the map to the left confuses the living ♥♥♥♥ out of me especially if you're trying to pin point enemy movements towards your city or to theirs. The units also form a squad instead of individual units.  All they really got from anno was the carriage system for resources really since everything is automated with assigning peasants to collect resources.  I added in Frostpunk because everyone compares this to frostpunk with the circular way of building in a limited amount of space.  The features of this game is literally just all over the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ place with no optimization or bother of making things fluent.- Unit interaction is horrible.  I can shift right click to queue unit movements only to click on an impassible terrain that completely stops the unit in track and cancels all queue commands.- Battle AI in the game is horrible. I've watched units go for the furthest back warrior while their frontline starts butchering my own units.- There really isn't any battle animation besides the valheim animation of a woodcutter on a tree except on a human this time.  I do enjoy the finishing move, too bad they get to live longer during this animation which relates to BAD AI, as in my units literally can't ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ kill the dude doing a finishing animation while his squad is literally decking on mines. An extremely bad thing to do in an RTS scenario- the pathing in this game is absolute cluster ♥♥♥♥.- AI response is really slow and I'm pretty sure because of the spaghetti code that is in the background causing massive delays. But this could be easily be optimized.- The hell are with the ship battles? Doesn't even really feel like a ship battle, but I do like the realism of boarding to engage the enemy, its also pretty cool to watch my frontline go for their backline(archers) while their frontline is bashing on my frontline at the same time.- Ship burns after winning a ship combat? Why don't I get the option to capture the ships instead?- I can't cancel an elder house upgrade, because clicking them on accident wasn't a thing in the past ever.- Having no food doesn't affect your colony much, it just won't let you recruit units. I expect my people to starve.- Barely any citizen interactions, but I guess this isn't super focused on city builder as they would want.- TECHING is locked behind resources. All of which is easily obtainable. There isn't really a tech tree for this RTS.- Theres also no teching for buildings, like upgrading an existing building to a higher tier.- The only tech you get is from a blacksmith which allows you to upgrade your troops.- Its pretty realistic for archers to shoot your own troops in the back, but that's absolute ♥♥♥♥ on an rts setting, especially with how garbage the pathing is.- Some buildings can't even fit in an area because it requires a square but somehow shows the circle icon??? We're talking about the religion building.- Ships tend to burn themselves because theres another ship on top of them :)- Ships also like to get stuck and can't automatically get around ships in combat. Again bad pathfinding.- Multiplayer is off and off. It is peer to peer, meaning if the host dies, the game is over.- Theres a ping block apparently and if that player bypass the ping, the game crashes.- I get stuck in a loading screen while trying to join a multiplayer game sometimes? I am assuming that the game is already running instead of in waiting lobby. This game fits my definition of why graphics of a game isn't everything especially when gameplay is non-existent.Does the game have replayability? As of now. ♥♥♥♥ no. But it is an early access but who knows?I truly think that this game shouldn't have gone early access and this is typically what kills the hype of the game in the future.  I would give this game maybe 2 to even 3 more years to make it come to remotely close to being playable.Editted Addition:I also forgot to mention that the love of RTS is the power to expand, theres no reason to move out and explore besides finding the enemy to kill which makes the game incredibly dull.  We're stuck in one small ass circle that gives me claustrophobia with resources only around your area.Another thing to add. I review base off of current game state not what I think of the future. If they manage to hit what makes them have potential, then I will give it the review it "deserves." All I have to say is if you want to test your games, make an alpha/beta sign up. Get actual testers to help build your game. Hell if I didn't have to pay a cent for this game, I would've privately message constructive criticism while testing (not playing) the game.Save your 15$ and buy yourself a pizza. The pizza could probably give you more fullness in 3 hours than this game could.Thanks for reading.

The map is small and there's no other reason to explore or set up camps, and because of some ai features that don't really separate settlements resources or needs you can't really even expand and have a reason to play it as a regular city builder* maybe i'm  just picky as a designer, but there's a lot of button gameplay issues where it's not intuitive or just outright buggy on how to click, what to press, etc for certain actions or movements. _childDocuments_.review: *EDIT 8/11/2024, Read Below this post*So, when I first saw this game, I fell in love with the concept of a Viking City Builder mixed with RTS elements. However, I stayed my hand on purchasing it because I saw the reviews were less than stellar. It gave me pause, but I still put it on my wish list.Fast Forward to now, after it has gone on sale, I can say.. There is a pretty decent game here. It captures the feel rather nicely. The atmosphere, the graphics, the changing seasons. It's pretty visually spectacular. The systems in game however, are rather.. basic? Or a bit clunky I should say. Yet that doesn't stand for all the systems. It has a fairly good building/resource system in place, its when you get to things like combat where you start seeing some problems.The Ai can be a bit wonky at times and there is the occasional bug, but I still think this game is worth giving a shot.To put things in perspective, I can get lost for a few hours in this game and not realize that time has passed me by. It's fun building up your little viking civilization and grow it all out (Though again the Ai leaves a bit to be desired).I'm never good at writing these reviews, putting my thoughts into words, or laying things out in detail about pros and cons. What I can say is that I think Frozenheim is worth at least giving a try. Steam has a 2-3 hour guaranteed Refund Policy, I think you can get a good idea in that time if this game is for you or not. Personally, I hope the devs keep working on it, hammering things out, and improving the game. They have potential gold here, they just need to work on the game a bit more. Polish it up, clean up some systems, maybe even rework some systems. Add more buildings, maybe slow down the units a bit (Because I have noticed they can make Sonic the hedgehog look slow at times), tone down unit damage so abilities can have more impact, etc.----------EDIT--------Devs have basically abandoned this game, paying pretty much no attention to it other than announcing it in bundles or sales. The game is in rough shape, the devs have basically abandoned this game in a fairly incomplete state.

_childDocuments_.review: The camera is great allowing for quite a bit of zoom in/out, and rotation of viewing angles. Story is generic but enough to keep you interested. The graphics are not top of the line, but are fairly nice upon full zoom in. What I found bad, was that the building format apparently is tight, I mean tight, basically all houses, wells, healer huts need to be right on top of each other for them to be useful. This clearly is a developer choice, but I would like to suggest that Civ builder games allow for a little bit of city planning for both aesthetic and strategy reasons. While having your "city" a tight packed tinder pile of ready to burn buildings at the drop of a hat. Oh did the dev's mention that if your buildings are burning from enemy attack - that there is not any type of indication/notification (no noises or anything besides the visual), so if you have to look away from your settlement (which is kinda important), you better get your eyes back on it every 5 seconds. This is not the part that makes the game unplayable. What makes it unplayable is the micromanagement of the rest of the game. Military units do not move in formation (I mean that's silly right?), there is no attack move, just 3 stances (aggressive, defensive, and hold fire/no attack). Now at first you think what's the problem? The problem is that at any stance your units if sent somewhere will ignore being attacked all the live long way to their destination. So you need to micromanage your troops during their entire march (oh are you looking at your settlement every 5 seconds? if not it is likely on fire), which is annoying as there are no formations, and you need to stop all the time to let the slow units catch up (I mean unless you like being slaughtered). Also you need to manually stop them and select an enemy to attack - so the annoying part of micromanagement. Also, the production buildings are varied and interesting, however the auto-placement of the yield does not work, so you always have to tell lumberjacks what wood to get, what mine to use, etc. If there were military formation (or at least 1 - stay together), attack move, and some sort of notification when you are under attack, this game could start to shine.

The 2nd part was even worse, you touch a stone and win the game? Not to be rude with 'spoiling' the story as it's literally 45 minutes of messing around with buildings and research leading to nothing. There is now a community assumption that all early access games are to look the best but perform terribly in the long run to only be a cash grab. I do not wish to write a review this way but it's what I am seeing. _childDocuments_.review: 9/10 Would recommend to anyone that likes a good RTS. The ONLY reason I'm giving it a 9/10 is because the controls feel a little stiff sometimes. The graphics(overall), music, and scenery(maps and cut-scenes) are beautiful; the tutorial is by no means overbearing like in most RTS games, which is kind of nice when you're figuring out the game cuz it adds a bit of mysticism that's rewarding; the combat is okay but you've gotta micro the hell out of units because they cant just swing through each other and the path finding is kind of dumb-fire, so be sure to pay attention in battle; the element of winter creates a small challenge during early game but more importantly it creates a sense of immersion. A $60 game can feel stale as hell right out of the box but this game feels crisp & refreshing for a meager $16.99. Hats off to the devs for making such a pleasant game for so little coin. This is all first impression feedback after only 2.6 hours of game play, so I haven't tried survival mode but if it's anything like what I'm picturing it to be, then thank you for the neat game mode rarely seen in RTS games. I hope to see an update in the near future that addresses the unit/building selection and movement issues.

_childDocuments_.review: tldr; The game requires some work and is short, but is promising. I think the key to this game is remembering that it is very early in terms of early access. I would not recommend this if you want a completed and polished game because it is far from that. There are bugs, buildings may float in the air, units may fall into the water and instead of dying or swimming, get stuck and fill up your unit cap. These are fixable and for under thirty bucks, comes with the territory. I truly believe that the developers will make a good game and, if their response to feedback is anything to go off, they will succeed in doing so.The Positives: - Building mechanics are good.  At the current moment, there are a few buildings that form various functions and for how limited this game is early on, there is a fair bit to work with. - Resource management goes beyond that of an Age of Empires game which from memory, only uses natural resources where as this requires to you refine iron ore and turn hide into clothing. - I enjoy the fact that units create their own paths after traversing a certain area enough and I would like to see an upgrade option be incorporated into this to boost worker productivity/speed.- The graphics are also quite appealing and really gives off major Frostpunk vibes, especially with how the lighting and snow works. I did have some issues with black spots showing up when I zoomed out but I can't confirm if that is because of the game or my computer. - Boat Building also has an nice customisation feature which I wasn't expecting allowing you to adjust hull and sail size, mast head and other features. The Negatives:- Combat Mechanics and AI path-finding is where I feel this game is let down the most. I know that the friendly fire is on but truly, the archer is useless when it gets one volley off before it is overrun by enemy AI. Even when this doesn't occur if you aren't paying attention your archers are more likely to kill all of your melee combatants than the enemy is. - I found at times that my boats were getting stuck in the second campaign mission. I would select a destination and they would just freeze after moving a few metres. It wasn't game breaking but meant I had to spend time and manually moving them myself instead of managing my village.  - The number of units available at the current moment is small, I would like to see more than 5 in future, even with some customisation like with the boat building. - I find that the building space really confines your ability to construct certain buildings. - I believe a warehouse should function more like a resource outpost so that all of your resource management does not have to be confined within the building area. Alternatively, introducing an outpost building which can extend your building area but create a cap on how many of these you can construct. - The story line is vague and doesn't really explain much. Additionally, with only 2 missions to speak of, people getting a bulk out of there playing hours have to rely on skirmish mode. Overall there is both some good and bad in this game. Currently it has some great, solid foundations and what's required next is fine tuning and feedback to begin bringing this game to a level that is suitable to be called a finished product. I look forward to seeing where this game is taken in future and would recommend it to those who enjoy games like Frostpunk and Age of Empires, with the warning that at the moment, you may not get a huge amount of game time in.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been watching this game for a while, waiting for it to be released on steam. Here's the thing: its an early access game. This means that content is being developed and actively released for it. There is an established road map from the developers for the next several months.With that being said, the game is beautiful. If you can stop dodging spears for more than a season or two the maps are GORGEOUS. Seasonal effects are amazing, water and light levels are wonderfully done, unit description and detail are amazing.Multiplayer does work. The AI are dumb as hell, but fun to play with if you want to get used to fending off attacks in, and I mean LITERALLY in, every way possible. Get a few friends together and it can be a blast. Been there, done that.Now, content aside (as its still being developed) there are a few bugs such as ships sinking, naval combat sometimes bugging out and a few others. The single biggest challenge that the early release faces right now is pathing. Pathing has always been and always will be the grand poobah of evil bugs in RTS gaming.Outside of that one detracting pathing factor and the game is well on track. I can safely recommend this as a purchase now if you want a low key time sink in single, multiplayer or campaign. Keep in mind its early access so there will be bugs. Probably many more than what I mentioned above.Its easy to learn, its fun, and I have single handedly reduced the viking population in Europe several times over.Some personal wants of mine as it stands with the early release? More maps. The whole "centralized archipelego lake" repeated on each map is a tad old. Spice it up. Keep my attention. Since you have a few existing maps developers, its easy enough to make a few more in different varieties. Easiest content drop ever. I would know. Ive made a few.Anyway, awesome game, would highly recommend as is and in the future. Cant wait.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright. So this is my first ever review and i felt it was much needed due to the all the negative comments ive seen given to it. So to begin, i initially bought the game because of the review saying it was a reminder of age of empires and command and conquer. I absolutely loved those games and for the chance of reliving some of those nolstagia, well it was worth giving it a chance.ANNNDDDD Ohhh boyyy, it definitely brings back the amazing feeling of the old school RTS, the game is simply beautiful, graphics are gorgeous. the game play is also good. it has so much potential to be amazing and a top all time game, the same way age of empires 2 sits in the hearts of many even after all this time. Dont get me wrong here, this is amazingly high praise i dont give lightly. Now for the issues i came across, the game unfortunately did crash a couple of times. it was hard to progress in the 'campaign' as it was ridiculously unforgiving. There didnt seem to be a way to heal buildings or units either for that matter. The fast forward mode of the game play seems off, it goes through a couple of seasons before i had even completed making a new unit(?) At the moment, ignoring all the glitches, i would say the game sits in a similar place of stellaris, a gorgeous game that feels so un-intuitive that most people wont go far into the game simply because of the steep learning curve. a bit of an exaggeration maybe but while  i love stellaris, however its hard to play when there isnt a story line, and hard to get your friends involve when the learning curve is so steep. This may be harsh and ill admit, the frustration having to restart the game a couple of times or restart the campaign when youve died without warning did have an effect. Another bug I just remembered was the zoom. I was stuck in a zoomed in mode for a lot of the map instead of being able to zoom out or stuck in a angled view. hopefully that gets fixed too In saying all that, ill reiterate, this game has so much potential. A game like this would be amazing with a good story line, something between star craft 2 and age of empires. I would love to follow the campaign and story line of viking raiding the old world. perhaps with the guidance of a god against other vikings or even empires.A great story line is always a good way to make a player get invested into a game. with the gorgeous graphics and views, an amazing story line with good cutscenes, I could see this game being an absolute masterpiece. A better guide would be amazing too. Cant wait to see what the final product looks like! :)

_childDocuments_.review: The game feels a bit like what I'd expect an arcade version of a citybuilder to be. Very short, easy campaigns even on the largest map, I don't think I've spent more than maybe 2 hours on any campaign. The Ai doesn't seem to know how to deal with throwing large raiding parties at it, and because of that, even on hard it's pretty easy to overwhelm them by turtling for a bit then wiping the map with your 15 squad raiding group. The pathing for ai could use some work, as I find that even in small groups, if the pathing lines take your units near water, they just don't know how to walk past it, so you have to manually make them take a very wide berth around it. Annoying when you're sending them to a relatively far away point and expect them to be there when you check in to give them new orders. There are also parts of the map that just seem unable to be accessed even though there's no obstacles and it's on the same plane as your units. This is problematic when there's a village there that has a quest, or a runestone, since you literally cannot access it. It also seems like for some reason, even if the shore is empty, it won't let you debark from a ship in some areas, meaning even if there's no buildings on the shore, you just... can't send warships to conquer a settlement? All of this just artificially increases the amount of time the game takes. Once this issue of places being inacessible for no reason and the pathing get fixed, I can't imagine this game will take much more than an hour and a half at most for experienced rts players. Maybe the Ai will improve and it'll be a bit more challenging, and the game will feel a little less arcadey, and it won't just have pretty graphics going for it. For now I can't reccomend.

_childDocuments_.review: A nice, cozy and comfortable city builder who focuses more on the combat aspects rather than empire builder in my opinon.While its strength is in the diverse units and how diverse your amry can be depending on which of the four clans you choose, the city building aspect isn't lacking too far behind. Sure, it's simple. You put your houses close together with enough space to push in bonus buildings that boosts happiness and safety, both big and small buildings. You gather resources that can be rather scarce and can go on raids!At the time I'm writing this, I've finished the first campaign of four "chapters", the last one took me an hour though that was mostly due to me being a little too comfortable...The most negative pointer I would have is the rather lacking naval combat. The two ships bash into eachother, then awkwardly shuffle alongside eachother in while your soldiers on board try to fight the other. Yes, you have some minor customizing to do on your ship, the size of cargo, able to heal onboard sailors etc, but I find it lacking and cluncky at best. Other than that, the targeting with certain abilities (such as beast taming) took a moment to get used to, but then it was smooth sailing from there.The best part of it? Well the graphics are amazing for an RTS of this type! I strongly suggest playing this game if you find it on sale, although for 17 euro full price, it isn't to far off the "strong suggestion to buy it" for me.I'll most certainly put many, many more hours into this game the coming days!TLDRAmazing looking RTS with focus on combat, while the city building doesn't lack behind!Naval combat is rather lackluster, but the rest of the game make up for it.

Sure, there are a few bugs, pathing can be annoying and there is a clear lack of content. I feel though that this still gave me enjoyable gameplay where I cannot wait till this game is fully fleshed out. Fighting with viking ships and interesting supply chains make it a different RTS. _childDocuments_.review: At the price point, it is probably a fair buy. They have a  solid foundation in place and hopefully they can quickly expand upon it, I'll give it a thumbs up but I likely won't revisit this until there is much more content. Hopefully by 1.0 this will end up being a really solid City Builder RTS. Based on the road map, the devs committed to monthly updates. Which sounds great on paper but I suspect this is too much pressure. Even now, its July 31 and the game hasn't seen an update this month. I don't personally have a problem with this but you should be cautious about making statements on timelines. You can commit internally to hitting monthly updates but saying that to the general public and then not hitting it is bad form. The Bad:My expectations were high since it was tagged as "City Builder" and "RTS". On the city aspect of things, you mainly place down a limited number of buildings. Nothing really seems to matter too much on the economics side nor is it particularly challenging to build said city. Unless I missed it, you won't be expanding outside of your small boundary and can only expand said boundary by a marginal amount. I would like to see the ability to setup smaller camps for gathering resources or just to be able to manage more than one village. I didn't see any way to gather more stone or iron once your starting resources were depleted which seemed a bit silly really. More production lines and resources would bring the economic side of this to a bit more life. The whole experience of building your village is quite shallow really but is a solid foundation to build on. The Good:The RTS side is pleasant enough. The game is in early access so I excuse a lot bugs that you can read about in other reviews. A major concern I have is if you destroy the Jarl's House, you win. You can just ignore all the troops and go straight for it. Even with a Hard AI, this is an easy task to do. The environment itself is also very nice and looks visually stunning at times.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a bit in the middle with this game.It obviously has the foundations to be such a good RTS/City builder game. But missing so many fundamentals that should have delayed a release. - Units will suddenly disappear after attacking, even with a full stack. - Some Gates are useless - I think if they are built on a slight elevation peasants and troops will refuse to use it and go to another gate. - My scouts overpowered enemy axes? I mean, come on.... - No tutorial. The 'story' mode acts as one, but its not as in depth. I wouldn't even call it a story mode. - Multiplayer - Unless you expect to play with friends is useless. Add some competitiveness to it so people can look at different builds. - Look at farming times, My build gets my village up and running quickly with Wood and Food, but the time difference to then Stone and Steel is very slow. - Please fix the troop movement. Troops get stuck when you click somewhere and there is a wall/cliff/elevation in the way.Like I said the foundations of the game are excellent and it can be made into a really competitive RTS game, but the above need to be fixed ASAP imo.

And let's not talk about the constant attacks against your city. I played for a grand total of about 30 minutes and finally turned it off. I was looking forward to this game and now I'm sorely disappointed in it. My suggestions? Give a real tutorial, give players the option to just build and not deal with combat if they want (you ARE pegged as a city-builder, after all), or at least give players the option to change the difficulty. It's horribly unbalanced when it comes to combat. My city was raided within the first three minutes of playing the game. Burned to the ground and I couldn't do anything about it. _childDocuments_.review: This is a reasonably enjoyable RTS with a city builder twist. It resembles Shiro Games' Northgard, but with the added element of playing as casually as you want in Scenario mode. Much of Frozenheim's game mechanics also resembles Northgard, though the option of choosing which clan you want in Scenario makes it more replayable. The main drawback is the relatively short campaign. Five sagas, each with four missions, plus a final one for a total of 21 missions. I've not heard of its developer Paranoid Interactive until now, but presumably if it's an indie setup, then the short campaign length can be forgiven. They should also be commended for working to ensure Frozenheim exited Early Access with relative punctuality, and also ensuring the game is mostly bug-free. Something that is becoming sadly uncommon with the rushed releases of games out of EA & riddled with errors.If you enjoyed Northgard but desire the option for something more casual & slow-paced, then Frozenheim is quite suited to your needs.
