_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game, but it is not perfect. Here are few pointers:- Playing the game revolves completely around the campaign. While every chapter gives you a new character, many things stay with you. There is no specific freeplay chapter, but you can play any of the numbered chapters as long as you don't finish the story missions and if you do, you can return to previous chapters any time. There is only one "save slot" but you can back up the save files very easily.- The game "requires" a controller or joystick, and I am sure that it fits most people. Never the less, I played with mouse and had great time. Actually, I was able to map all essential gameplay controls directly to my gaming mouse. It also gave me a hearty accuracy boost, not complaining.- Most of the systems in game are easy to understand through intuition, but very few things are actually told. For example, how much ammo you have can in principle be seen by the brightness of the ammo pots on your bird. However if you want to get more info, you must land in a place where you could sell that ammo and compare the price you would get to the pots max value. Better to just shoot and reload as the need arises. The minimap gives some good information, but it also misses many crucial details, like where there are enemies, fish to restore health or rising winds to lift you.Also bigger stuff is obfuscated: How much do biomods change yor stats and who knew you can remove them from your bird, but only if they are class 3 stars or less. Or that there is a whole system of piracy with its own missions. Or all those permits, where can you get them (Spoiler: ). Or what stuff stays between landings, deaths, chapters or forever. Not so obvious. Now I suppose its fine to keep that stuff hidden. Its nice to find unexpected things and apparently many of those things were added after the game launch, incorporating them to the campaign hard. However since there is an game guide that claims to explain this stuff for sale for 4€, to this I give the biggest stink eye of them all!- Graphics look nice, even really beautiful at times. However, barring few set pieces, the scenery gets repetitive pretty quickly and when you think about it, the somewhat low draw distance and ample clouds prevent seeing the grand vistas you might expect from a flying game. Also the characters remind me of runescape to a distracting degree.- Flying is fluid and responsive. It doesn't have that much depth but it works for what it is.- Fighting works once you get the hang of it, tough at the start on lower levels, it is easy to get swarmed and enemies on your tail can be a quick death sentence. There is variety in weaponry, but nothing really stands out and options for specialization or situational tools are limited.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game quite a bit. It's not super long, it's beautiful to look at, and is actually better than I was afraid it was going to be, based on some reviews and my general aptitude for fighting.That said, here's some things I loved, and some things I didn't. (TLDR at the bottom)The art of the general world is great! The people look like they're in a PS1 game, but you don't really need them to be fancy. The voices were nice, even though some of the lines were skipped. Flight feels wonderful! It took a bit to get the hang of, since I am on a computer and it's optimized for a controller, but if you turn the mouse sensitivity down and set the flight control (not camera) to mouse, it works pretty well. The story, while a bit dull in the beginning (I think the "intro to the game" missions went on a bit too long), got pretty interesting in the last half, and was actually neat. It had a kind of abrupt and anticlimactic ending, though. It definitely has potential, and I'll probably reinstall and play it again at some point.Things that irked me tho:If you start a time trial, you *have* to finish it for it to reset, so if you know you're not going to make the time, you have to touch every single torch on the route. This gets real old, real fast. Especially if some of the torches are hard to reach, or particularly high up (looking at you, Imperial Peak). Adding a reset button somewhere would be a boon, it could even just be a blue flame toward the start of the track or something. There's a lot of lovely birds, shame only like 2 are decent in the endgame. I wish you could re-skin the bird you want to use to one of the other options, cuz I like the look of some of the birds, and have all the DLC, so it's a shame that the Fenix,  Ptero, and Ormir are really only good in the very early game or to get you to the place where you can buy your preferred bird again. It would be nice if some of those were added into the mix of ones you could buy with each stat selection, cuz I was disappointed that the best bird ended up just being a plain brown/black one (the most expensive is not necessarily the best). As one of the main selling points of the game, and a huge part of the experience, being able to customize a little more visually would be amazing.The world is big and empty. I understand, that's kind of the point a bit in the story, but there's so many tiny islands around with nothing on or around them, the side quests are all pretty much just "go here, fight these guys, go there, pick up thing, go home". There isn't really a whole lot to do, and what is available, there isn't really an incentive. It doesn't seem to have any effect on the story, and money is basically useless once you get your preferred chants/weapon/bird. The chants and weapon transfer (thank goodness, I'd be annoyed if they didn't) but your bird doesn't, so every chapter pretty much begins with *maybe* 1 mission where you try out your newbie bird if it's one you haven't used yet, and then you fly over to your preferred one and buy it for however much, and then you never buy anything again unless you want a change of pace and swap out what type of ammo you're using, or *maybe* your weapon, or you try to increase the stats of a bird you like the look of so it can somewhat keep up with the better birds (You'll have to do any bird stat customization over in the next chapter).Speaking of weapons: it would sure be nice if it displayed the stats of a weapon in the store window when you were trying to figure out what you wanted to use. It only shows your current weapon, and then a 1 sentence explanation of whatever gun you're looking at. Nothing telling you about the stats or rate of fire unless you act like you're going to buy it, and then all it tells you is if it thinks it's an upgrade or a downgrade, not what changes it will make.EDIT: The dev has responded and advised that you can, in fact, switch between male and female characters by clicking the appearance tab, but I was unable to get this to work when I tried it, that could just be user error or a bug on my end.That said, I had a great time, it was very enjoyable, and I'm the kind of person that generally likes repetitive gameplay, so doing the same thing over and over again wasn't too much of a chore for me.TLDR: Repetitive quests, empty world, beautiful to look at and neat designs, flying is fun, grievances with the Time Trial system, and you mostly just end up using 1 bird even tho there's a variety. Story gets interesting halfway through. Combat not as hard as I expected it to be. Some UI nitpicks in the sales screen. Money is mostly useless after like, the first or second chapter unless you plan to try to improve your bird's stats a little bit, so not really any incentive for sidequests, they're the same as the main quests, but faster. Works decently on a keyboard and mouse, I had no issues.Oh, also, I liked the music quite a bit.All in all, I enjoyed it, and it gets a 3.5-4/5 stars for me.

_childDocuments_.review: A cool little title, but I don't feel it's worth anywhere near the money being asked.  Some of the design decisions as well as gameplay mechanics are also significantly problematic.Positives:+ Very cool world with beautiful, minimalistic visuals that really work. + An interesting take on delivering the lore of the gameworld.  It's got my attention!+ The overall concept is fun and engaging.+ Classic "Freelancer" approach to gameplay: pick a ship, customize your guns, missles and components, dive into quick missions that don't take long to finish.  (Except here, ships are "birds", weapons are "lightning lances and steampunk rockets", and components are mutagens for your giant flying steed.)Negatives:- It's obtuse in far too many places.  Simple things like, "How to fly your mount," or, "How do I land?" or, "What did this character just tell me to do?" will likely require numerous trips to the internet to figure out.  It makes the game staggered, disorienting, and frustrating at exactly the point it should be sinking its talons into you and getting you hooked.  There's a big difference between luring players into the world with deep, intuitive mechanics that allow for improvisation and discovery...and simply not telling the player that you don't need to hold the use button to use something you were just specifically instructed to use.  Or specifically telling the player to avoid combat, then making it so that if the player escapes from combat...the mission will not continue.  They have to...remain in combat...while not fighting...to escape the combat...but you're allowed to leave the combat zone...which is wrong...  Wha???  Far too many moments like this, and I'm only 4 hours in.- Controls are seriously janky, with even more things that don't seem to make any logical or intuitive sense.  Camera movements (whether using M+K, gamepad, or flightstick -- I tried all three) are twitchy, imprecise, and prone to taking control away from the player for constant, nonsensical reasons.  Not only will control be forcibly yanked from players' hands if they fly too close to a new point of interest, even while in combat, but the game also makes the time-worn mistake of almost constantly introducing "cutscenes" during action-based missions, repeatedly interrupting the action and letting the player get shot up so the camera can be yanked away to focus on a ship or something for 4 seconds of dialogue.  It's pretty silly.- Very quickly repetitive and boring.  While there's enough here to make it really interesting...it simply...doesn't.  Missions boil down to: a.) fly to location and kill the target. b.) fly along waypoints and kill all targets along the way.c.) go get thing and bring it back.d.) land on perch, listen to narrative, fly away.That's...apparently it.  4 hours in and I haven't seen a single deviation from the formula.  Except for a few missions where you do one of the above tasks while also listening to NPCs yap on about tired, uninspired "freelancer" tropes.  The world's a mess...can't trust anyone...omg, we've been betrayed...look, though, now there's intrigue -- our enemies may actually be our allies...oh wait, there's some mysterious power pulling the strings...*yawn*.  It doesn't seem like the game is doing much of anything with the idea of ~Falconeers~ -- the remnants of a legendary, fallen order, honor-bound by a code to fulfill some higher purpose...you know...that the game itself creates and introduces?  No?  Just grunts and mercenaries now?  Oh...okay.In conclusion, it's not a bad game, but I can't justify $30.00 for this.  I'd say $9.99 is a much better price for what the game actually delivers.  It's a cool idea and gorgeous visualization of an interesting world!  But its core mechanics are simply very shaky, and there's nothing gameplay-wise that many other titles in the genre haven't done noticeably better.  Definitely a "grab on sale" title!  And that I would recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: Falconeer is a gorgeous game that provides the player with a true sense of flight.The game's lore, art style, and environment are all outstandingly crafted and unique.The gameplay is that of an aerial dog-fighting style using birds instead of planes. _childDocuments_.review: This is an impressive little game for a solo dev, though it's not without its flaws.  The music is wonderful, and the art style, while simplistic, is still beautiful in its own right.  The flight is generally pretty fluid and feels just right and the combat is fun though pretty standard for an air-combat game.  The gameplay can get a little repetitive, though I personally found it enjoyable enough to not see this as an issue.One of my main criticisms would be that the world feels just a little bit too empty, particularly when exploring, which leaves lots of time where you are just doing nothing but flying. There doesnt really seem to be much in the way of random encounters, and generally the only way you'd find enemies is by flying into territories of opposing factions.  That said, becoming a pirate helps with this to a degree since everything on the map aside from other pirate-controlled locations becomes hostile and therefore you're much more likely to engage in combat while exploring.  What's also nice about going pirate is that it's easy to get rid of the pirate levels and resume the normal faction if need be.  Focusing on the story/side missions can also be fairly engaging, particularly in the later chapters.Another main criticism is the control layout, namely with the dash/roll and brake/dive functions sharing the same buttons. I'd end up rolling when trying to dash, which was especially problematic for the time trial races as it would usually cause me to hit a wall and bounce around instead of dashing, and same sorta thing with braking when trying to dive. I feel like it would have been better off if roll and brake were on their own separate buttons (such as L3 / R3) with dive + dash remaining on the L bumper/trigger. Despite this though, I'd say this is mostly a nitpick as it's had minimal impact on the majority of my gameplay, and only found it to be the most problematic during the races.The last main issue is simply that I feel the game could be a little bit better with explaining mechanics and just generally how things work.  Most of the stuff is pretty straight-forward to figure out though, so this is more of a nitpick than anything.Overall, I'd say that even with its flaws, it's worth giving this game a shot if you're into relatively chill aerial combat type games, especially if you can grab it on sale.Note: slightly edited my original review to reflect my opinion after spending some more time with the game

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game. It is mainly made by one person and gee whiz I love it! I will discuss game play, the world, music, sound, the story and voice acting below. I will also give my negative nitpick, some advice for new players and touch on saving for whatever that is worth.This game has scratched an itch I've had for manoeuvring flying animals around the place in a video game. The birds are very fun to control and fight with. Such experiences have been some of the most cathartic I have had in a video game. Essentially you fly a giant bird in 3 dimensions and use a gun to shoot things from it's back. Gaining potential energy by flying higher before making a dive is a welcome and unique mechanic. There are also means of upgrading your weapons and your bird.The game world is beautiful and highly immersive. Sometimes I can taste the salt in the air and feel the cool breeze that carries it. Along with the game play is the excitement of exploring this vast ocean which doesn't seem to end anywhere. The fast travel is a convenient mechanic that can relieve boredom however, the vastness of the sea can be enhanced without it. This is a game where you can just fly and enjoy being above the clouds.The music in this is highly unique and moving from action cues to tranquil sparse instrumentation when watching the stars. How often do you get to hear harmonic throat singing in a soundtrack? The sound effects of storms, harbours and the assortment of sounds weapons enhanced the feelings I had greatly.The story of The Falconeer focuses on the self destructiveness of war and learning from it. It features arrogant warmongers as well as more sympathetic protagonists. But however noble the motivation is, war escalates. The playable characters themselves are interchangeable cogs in the machinations of important people; you choose your appearance, humble background and the bird you fly. These characters are realised with a talented voice cast giving you impassioned orders from a warlord or cries of desperation from an aerial opponent. The end of each chapter is punctuated by a big event that changes things for everyone in the Ursea.Regarding the self destructiveness of war, it even features in the mechanics of the game. Any upgrades you make to your actual bird are not labelled in terms of effectiveness but rather in terms of toxicity. The best potion you can buy to make your bird as fast as its body will allow is labelled "fatal" (presumably fatal in a year or two).My negative nitpic:After installing new DLCs, the new content in the game is not obvious to find. There is no special announcement that the game has new content, it is just there... somewhere. The DLCs are not essential for a good experience but they were worth the purchase.Advice for new players.There are some side missions available at the start of the game where you can help some cartographers map out the ocean. These are simple exploratory missions where you can earn some good money and become familiar with the ocean without being shot out of the sky. You might save yourself some frustration while getting used to the controls and saving up for some upgrades.Regarding missions and saving.If you die in a mission, you must start over again. This was fine with me since I didn't die a lot and the missions while huge in height and distance don't take a long time to complete. This is probably a bit of a taste thing.If you enjoy flying around spitting fireballs at sheep driving UFOs in Spyro 2, you'll love this game.

_childDocuments_.review: is a game where you'll get to ride on the back of a mighty warbird and engage in intense aerial combat in the skies. Now, I've tried playing the game with both controller and keyboard+mouse, and I still feel like the controls here are lacking and awkward. It's not as easy to navigate on a warbird in this game than say a spaceship in Everspace. Ended up opting for the keyboard and mouse since that's the one I'm most familiar with. The Falconeer has some issues too like cross hairs just disappearing during dogfights, making me a sitting duck basically, or that stamina doesn't seem to regenerate fast enough, especially when you want to quickly cover huge distances. It's very hard to aim in this game too. I've struggled a bit in Everspace but at least I'm hitting something most of the time. In this game though, I'm barely making any hits. With that being said, the game has plenty of good stuff going for it - It has a huge open ocean world with some interesting POIs and natural occurrences like waterspouts and thunderstorms that you are free to explore; lots seemingly randomly-generated quests to farm money from (besides the chapter-based story quests); well-varied though somewhat limited weapon and warbird upgrades to buy; and if you've completed the necessary prerequisites, you can even buy yourself a new and better warbird. **Adding that I sometimes get motion sickness from playing certain games - I'm looking at you Mirror's Edge - but I'm happy to say that this isn't the case in The Falconeer. Hope this helps! After giving the game a shot, I'm convinced that this game isn't for me. Flying my warbird during combat just feels like I'm struggling - futilely I might add - against the game, and perhaps the game just has a higher skill ceiling that I can't reach at the moment and I just don't have to patience to sit through hours of trial and error just to get the hang of its dogfights. However, if you're a veteran space sim player, I reckon this game might pique your interest. It's not space-themed but it's still a game with some pretty intriguing world-building and beautiful graphics. Might be worth a look.

_childDocuments_.review: The Falconeer is an indie action-adventure game developed by Tomas Sala and published by Wired Productions. It was released in 2020 for Microsoft Windows, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S.The game is set in a beautiful and immersive fantasy world where players take on the role of a Falconeer, a warrior who rides atop a giant bird of prey. The game features an open-world environment, where players can explore different regions and take on various missions.One of the standout features of The Falconeer is its unique and compelling gameplay mechanics. Players control their Falconeer and their bird, using a combination of aerial combat and exploration to progress through the game's story. The game features a variety of different weapons and abilities that players can use to take down enemies, such as harpoons, missiles, and bombs.Another great aspect of The Falconeer is its stunning visuals and immersive world. The game features breathtaking environments, from soaring cliffs and sprawling cities to expansive oceans and deep caverns. The game's art direction and soundtrack also add to the immersive experience, creating a truly memorable and unique game world.However, the game is not without its flaws. The game's combat can feel a bit repetitive at times, with some players finding it difficult to distinguish between enemies and allies. The game's story also feels a bit sparse and underdeveloped, with some players wishing for more fleshed-out characters and plotlines.Overall, The Falconeer is a unique and engaging game that is definitely worth checking out. Its beautiful visuals, immersive world, and unique gameplay mechanics make it stand out from other games in the genre. While it may not be perfect, it is a great example of what indie games can achieve, and a fun experience for anyone looking for something different in their gaming experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Above the clouds, freedom must be boundless... or not, as The Falconeer shows us. Our falcon makes it only just above the clouds. Most of the time we fly either very close to the ground or at cloud height, but not much higher. That makes sense, because it's damn cold up there and the oxygen is a bit scarce. In the game we take on the role of a hawk rider, a warrior of the air, who glides across the water on his huge war bird and fulfills missions. The oversized falcon is equipped with a forward firing lightning rod. With his grabbing feet he can pick up and transport things from the ground.The Falconeer is set in a world that consists largely of water (the Ursee). On rocks rising out of the Ursee are small villages or monuments. Warships and merchant ships sail over the water, airships and hot-air balloons fly in the air. Huge fish jump majestically out of the water, rocks rise from the sea whipped up by the wind, a lightning flashes above us in the sky - and we fly with our bird just above the water surface. The Empire rules over the Ursee, with the Empress at its head. However, there are also other rival factions, such as the powerful Mancer Order or the House of Borgia. As a player, you can explore the entire map at any time and fly around as you please. It's fun to just sit on your falcon and fly around and admire the different places. A special feature is the so-called gorge, a large valley in the middle of the sea, on the sides of which the water stands as if held by a ghost's hand, releasing the seabed and on the edge of which there are settlements and huge monuments. In the course of the game you can also explore the underwater world. Basically the game is played on the back of a flying animal. At some places you can land, but this only takes you to a menu and you can choose between more or less options - to fly again afterwards. To move around on foot is not possible.From the beginning of the game, the first four campaigns are unlocked, you can switch between them at any time. A fifth campaign must first be unlocked. At the beginning of each campaign you choose your character for the respective campaign and thus your appearance and character values. However, and this is somehow strange, you take the money and inventory from the other campaigns already (partially) played, as well as the locations revealed on the world map (in other campaigns). Somehow this makes no sense. The campaigns build on each other in time, so it's impossible to understand the story by jumping back and forth. I don't quite understand this design decision.The first campaign begins in the run-down little smuggler village of Dunkle, which is located on a small rock in the middle of the Ursee, on the edge of the empire's sphere of influence. We play a young mercenary (and his war bird) who offers his services to the highest bidder; or at least to the one who pays anything at all. Currently, this is mainly the scribe of Dunkle, who sends us on various missions for the small village. The missions are initially simple and short. We are sent on patrol, have to transport important freight, go on escort missions, find missing buoys, fight pirates and then return to Dunkle to get our payment. The story is mainly told during the (very) short briefings before and after each mission. In the second chapter you play on the side of the Empire, in the third chapter for the House of Borgia and in the fourth chapter for the Mancer Order. In many of these missions you don't fly alone, but have an ally at your side.Besides the story missions we can also visit a merchant to improve our war bird. By injecting a mutagen, its mobility, speed or stamina can be increased and in some places blessings can be purchased. With enough money you can also buy a better lightning thrower or other weapons. Trading licenses can also be purchased from the trader. Besides the trader, you can also regularly meet people who offer additional missions, which do not advance the story, but can be quite lucrative. It is also possible at any time to simply fly around freely. The game saves after completion of each mission. If you die, you will be transferred back to the start of the respective mission.Our war bird moves at a steady speed through the air with almost no effort. Only when we fly upwards does he have to exert himself a little, the steeper we want to go up, the more. We can also encourage him to fly as fast as possible over short distances, but this uses up his stamina very quickly. In descending flight his endurance increases again. If he has enough stamina, we can also perform acrobatic rolls to the left or right, which is very useful to avoid enemy projectiles. The weather has comparatively little effect, but gusts of wind always influence our direction, so we have to be careful to stay on course. Upwinds and downwinds cause us to suddenly gain or lose height.The aerial fights with the many enemies take place like already in WW I - the birds circle each other and try to shoot down the opponent from short distance. Our flash cannon sets enemy birds or other (animal or mechanical) flying objects on fire, which is graphically beautifully depicted. The most advantageous position in battle is of course to be above your enemies. Then you are able to fly down on them with increased speed and quickly escape from the range of their weapons again, if they have survived the attack. Most of the time, however, you will spend circling your enemies and trying to get them in your crosshairs.The Falconeer is a good-looking action game in an open world and consists mainly of dogfights - exciting, fast-paced aerial battles in a confined space. By completing a variety of different missions, the story of the rival factions of the Ursee is told in a world full of mysterious technologies, ancient relics, gigantic monuments and legendary mythical creatures. Or it would be, if the game doesn't crash. I'd wait for a few patches before buying.

_childDocuments_.review: I got the base game as part of a bundle with a purchase from EVGA. This review, however, is my own. I've also purchased all the DLC on my own dime.I like this game. I like it quite a lot. It's not something that I really enjoyed right away, truthfully--but it grows on you. Give it some time, both to get used to the controls and to let the story start to really draw you in.The atmosphere and music are very well done. The voice acting can be a bit uneven in terms of audio normalization--some had professional equipment, and I feel some had less so--but I like the delivery and variety of voices. Some of the help prompts could be a bit larger to stick out more for people like me who are so transfixed by the content that we can't figure out how to land for 30 minutes... but that's a minor quibble at best. I've learned to make sure I'm looking at the whole screen, for sure, and the more I play, the more I keep learning.Very enjoyable!

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely a very underrated experience. As a lover of Ace Combat and Project Wingman, playing a flight game like this is a lovely new touch to the airspace. Mainly having the floor being a mechanic that works with your bird, and not just instant death, is a weirdly specific feature that I am very much in love with.Goes without saying that the artstyle, worldbuilding and general vibe of this game is top notch. Not even "for an indie dev", but genuinely very interesting and fun to live into. The only real jankiness exists in menu responsiveness and repetitive voicelines but I only bring these up to mention how the rest of the game makes those minor issues a non-factor for enjoyment.Good video game!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is everything it promised to be. To preface, I don't usually like dogfighting games but I could not pass up on giant bird / dragon flying games and it looked so nice. For some things, I will suffer ( playfully, here ) through combat because it's worth it. I don't have to be the best at something to enjoy it and that's very much the case for this game. It's just so much fun. I Installed it with the intent to just look at it, see what I might be getting into and immediately lost almost two hours in the game just flying around. Learning controls. Trying to fish - I am the worst fisher. It's just such a pretty, lovely game. This might accidentally turn into a bird flight sim for me. There are neat things to find, quests to take that aren't combat related, and I just enjoy it.// So I've put about 7 more hours into the game since I reviewed it and I've jokingly called this a 'mini-skyrim'. I've spent so much time flying around, doing various quests - a lot of exploring, killing pirates, talking to people... I know there's a story quest, but I keep getting distracted! In a good way, mind. I'm enjoying the game immensely. It can be a chill way to fly about or I can hunt around. Either way... I've only fallen in more love with it.

_childDocuments_.review: General    Fun game, little repetitive, flying bug enemies make me angry. Controls   I would only play this game with a controller since the mouse an keyboard controls feel weird to me. Atmosphere   Simply amazing, would like some more music tracks. I enjoy just flying around.World   Exploring the world, for me, was fun. However, when I found a new enemy and killed it, I didn't get much in a reward.Clouds   Fluffy clouds are Fluffy.Exploring   Exploring was fun for me but there is not much reason to do it unless you like then environment and set pieces.Overall   Fun game if you like dog fighting and exploring. There are a lot of  awesome environmental set pieces and cool visuals. The story is entertaining and some of the side quests can be fun but a little easy. I wish exploring the world had more reward like cosmetics for birds. Great pick up if you like airships, giant birds, tight turning dog fights but with birds, and a interesting hand crafted world.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is unique and strangely satisfying. This is like Dredge only up in the air and with far less guidance. With keen patience and a curiosity for what this tenacious Dev has envisioned I believe this "quirky"(as the Dev himself in fact coined) experience is laying the groundwork for something quite extraordinary...though I cannot place my talon on exactly what that is? Either way this gorgeously stylized, at times contemplative, mostly gently confusing, albeit enticing, meditative, at times combatant, visually and atmospherically rich experience unfolds slowly but surely into something that I couldn't get out of my head at work today and, well, as soon as I sat down and began to explore? Strangely but fervently satisfying. I wish I could be less nebulous regarding this title. What I do know is that I will fly that bird until I understand the entire thing. Kudos to the Dev all the way.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this based on new VR mode, never played title before.  Enjoy having some third person sit down VR games/experiences to play mixed in with more interactive ones.  This is a perfect get comfy with a controller type game where you get to sit behind a well animated bird in a beautiful environments.  Currently playing Moss II and I can see this complimenting play sessions of that game because genrewise they are wildly different, but they both feature luscious worlds you can soak in.  Gameplay reminds me of Star Fox 64, not really to huge into games in this genre so I read plays similar to Crimson Skies, had recently played Rogue Squadrons in VR and honestly The Falconeer may feel similar to elements of those games, but the whole world and art style and being behind a bird which does effect a couple of elements of gameplay that feel natural when you figure it out (see: landing for the first time).   Will be going back to this one, if getting for VR, recommend trying at the least, there is a full fledged title here that could have been released today as just a VR game on a standalone headset and would sell a ton.  Maybe dev should consider a Pico / Quest release.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't hate the game, but I'll just list out the things I loathe in the game.Mouse and keyboard: It's just cringe why does the camera twitch? Very helpful when I'm trying to aim at a flying target. I have skill issue with controller, so if you intend to play mouse and keyboard better be invested.Flying feels wonky: perfectly fine during normal flight and battles, BUT in the game there are flying challenges to unlock new mounts, and bumping into things are way to strict. _childDocuments_.review: The big draw of this game to me is the beautiful world and compelling story. It seeks to present a Water World like Post Apocalypse with giant falcons, dragons, steam ships, and a bit of magic. It then tells a story of rival factions and imperial intrigue. As an exploration game with light combat elements it is a success.Where the game is a bit of a disappointment is in the combat and flight modeling. This game falls heavily on the arcade flight physics end of the spectrum. It keeps new players from splattering themselves all over the scenery but doesn't leave much in the upper end for mastery. On top of this the areal gunnery system is very unsatisfying. The game takes place from the 3rd person with an aim reticule that hovers a set distance out from the forward vector of the players lance (main gun). It is hard to determine where the shot will land while in the swirling dogfights that characterize combat in this game. The game gives the player a lead point indicator, but there is no correlation between putting the cross hair on it and making a hit. There is also a slight auto aim, but once again this does not increase hit rates, and in some cases, I am convinced, have lead to misses for shots I think may have hit.When I purchased this game I was looking for a world to explore, and on that this game has delivered in spades. It is not however does not stack up well against more dedicated air combat games I have in my steam library.

For those LOTR lovers, this is the closest thing to flying those eagles.Would be nice to have co-op, but considering that theres only one coder developing, thats wishful thinking.PS: The campaign is a bit dry, wouldnt be surprised if people would leave the game because they wanted a strong story instead of a sandbox with directions.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: The Falconeer features immersive and finely crafted gameplay, has stunningly beautiful scenery, is a sheer pleasure to explore, feels like it has hours and hours of content to be played through, BUT might come across as not one's cup of tea. I totally dig it and suggest buying at full price with DLCs.UPD: I finished the entire thing and collected every single achievement. That probably says something about the possible enjoyability of this game. I must say that this game is not to be overlooked.The Falconeer is some amazing species. This is a game I was dreaming of for the last couple of years.First: NATIVE FLIGHTSTICK SUPPORT!!!Then, the open world. To my taste, it works and plays well. The game world offers an absolute, unlimited freedom of progression and travel. It is worth exploring the map early in the playthrough to get the gist of things and learn how to play the game properly, and the game totally lets you do so, providing you with numerous additional storylines to complete. The game highly encourages you to fly around and do whatever you please which comes across as a great pleasure. Yeah, completing an endless barrage of stock side quests feels a bit grindy. But for me personally this kind of grind is enjoyable, as you opt for it voluntarily and it is tangibly rewarded. I dunno when I will finally get to chapters other than the first one, as the first chapter offers well enough side stories and quests to complete! And last but not least, the views are stunning. It is a sheer pleasure to cross the skies on the back of your warbird. The game world is definitely something to be admired and immersed into. Feels like escapism, in a good way.Having to figure out a lot of stuff, which is eventually successful, feels very rewarding. Normally I look for wiki articles on game elements when I'm playing through a game I enjoy, but with The Falconeer I feel strangely countermotivated to do anything like that. It lures me to find everything out on my own, to master and learn every single gameplay feature using only my trusty flightstick. It feels great to try every single weapon and every single mechanic with your own hands, especially considering that swapping items and weapons is made easy The combat is a bit primitive but customizable enough (although I'd love to have a wider selection of ammo and weapons), and still takes time and skill building to be mastered, as it does involve a certain amount of strategy (which is awesome in my book), especially if you're no expert in flight sims. The arcade-ish dogfighting combat style is absolutely my cup of tea. Easy to pick up but hard to master.The story. Well, I'm the kind of player that focuses on the gameplay, normally the plot and the lore stay totally out of my focus  The Falconeer is no exception here. Like yeah, factions and whatnot, I did read the game guide for the sake of basic understanding of the lore. What I'm trying to say is -- I dig titles that are able to maintain immersion through the gameplay and not the plot, and The Falconeer manages to do just that in flying colors (sorry for the pun). Fun fact, I've read a plethora of reviews online that highlight the lack of a story -- hence that's a thing of taste and personal preferences I guess??But there IS a thing I totally and utterly hate about this game. ONE WORD.RACECOURSES.Ooooh this is some AVGN grade stuff. The third attempt to conquer the Port Remit course summoned flashbacks to the good old Superman 64 episode. I could record the footage of like 46289174649 attempts of mine at this racecourse and swap the audio to the Nerd's voiceover from the aforementioned episode, maybe clipping some bits out. I was more successful with some of the other courses (with the Nerd yelling his curses at the back of my mind, yet). But regardless... The racecourses in general...  Well, nothing is perfect after all. But some of the warbirds that come as a reward for your suffering are Formula 1 class, legit (and I highly recommend to swap the stupid stock bird for anything else asap). If the racecourses were a mandatory step in story progression,  And oh boy we got bugs. The Glitch Gremlin does have his bloody nest in this game's code, albeit none of the bugs that I encountered so far were game-breaking. But the in-game menu, the freaking selection of menu items doesn't work properly, you have to click any of the items anywhere between 2 and 10 times in order to finally, say, get your damn world map whipped out! Such details get extremely frustrating.In spite of my personal frustrations, The Falconeer is a great experience. I hope I will enjoy every single one of the potential gameplay hours (which are indefinite considering the huge amount of questlines and absolute freedom within the game world), and wish you the same.
_childDocuments_.name: The Falconeer

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, here's the dealio, I saw this game before it was released and was instantly enamored by open world flying and dog fighting mechanics (something I've dabbled in before and liked). I followed it very closely until it released and bought it almost immediately when it was available. At first I used a controller to play the game, unsure if keyboard and mouse worked (my preferred method), it was a bit wonky and the controls took some time to get used to. While the game says its not keyboard and mouse supported I play it keyboard and mouse anyway, my fingers are not suited for basic controller controls so when it can be keyboard and mouse that is my go to any and every time regardless if its made for it or not. Using my preferred control system does increase my enjoy-ability to play the game (because duh I can actually PLAY the game this way). Despite the odds, I absolutely love this game. For other people its hit or miss because of some of the mechanics and overall game play, some of these things I find I have no issues with because they just don't stand against the fact this game is amazing regardless. Here's some things I find everyone has issues with, one if not all of these are the reason its a hit or miss for some people.  Flight controls-- Wonky or not it can and will impact the players enjoyment. I have seen from release until now flight controls has improved quite a bit and I personally do not see this as a problem anymore. Even with my keyboard and mouse I feel more control than with a controller (and I don't have a flight stick) and they're familiar controls. Some players blame the controls if they die, I too have died because it registered a bank instead of a roll, or just not turning when I say so. However, if I never wanted to die, I would have played on easy mode. I like a little challenge and I actually like negotiating with the controls, makes me feel like I'm negotiating with the bird rather than a computer. Too many times I see people upset with a game because the controls for a beast (your bird in this case) don't do exactly what you want them to do. This is the wrong conclusion to come to. The controls are the way they are and you cant fix that so if you want to play the game you gotta muscle up and get around it. To me that is not a downside, that's part of the experience of getting good at a game rather than being perfect at it right off the bat because that's not satisfying. It's about give and take and what you can do and what the bird will already do/is willing to do. If you want total control over your animal, this is not the game for you. Plot-- Yes plot is kinda weird and sometimes doesn't make too much sense but that's kind of the point. The plot plays out like a tragedy, nobody seems to win and you yourself find yourself on so many peoples sides who you want to see win. Again I find no problem with this, if that's the story the game wants to tell I'm not going to complain about it because they do it very very well. The plot is structured in 'chapters' where you the player are backing a certain group during that chapter. It feels disjointed and that's on purpose because spoilers. You are seeing every side to the tragic equation while you yourself seem to be in the middle of it all just watching helplessly even though you're the one going on the missions and making stuff happen. To me, that is compelling writing. Maybe the dialogue isn't fantastic, but hearing one pirate yell 'I WILL HANG YOUR SKULL AROUND MY NECK" at random points in battle always manages to make me smile if not giggle. I really like it if I can kill him mid-sentence, he's just screaming about my skull and his neck and it abruptly cuts off. Its not a perfect game, its not a perfect plot. But there is beauty in its failings, none of these issues are deal breakers for me. It IS open world and if you do fire on friends you will be branded an enemy and be attacked if you get too close. Pacing/missions-- In the beginning there is a bit of grinding to do to actually hold your own in some of the plot missions. This can be time consuming but it lets you get used to the controls and the layout of the map. I find no issue here, in fact I will wait to do story missions until I've got the best bird and gear and just fly around because flying around is awesome. Tip, (non-story) mission difficulty is stated by the amount of skulls on it, except sometimes its wrong, that's because the skulls is the EXPECTED difficulty. You might not encounter any enemies (unless told so like in the story missions) or you might encounter a little or an entire armada, but I find that a fun part of the experience. You are a warrior atop your mighty falcon, you also have no idea what you're getting into and that is a common theme throughout the entire game. It is EXPECTED to get in over your head. All in all, this game is much more of an experience for me than it is a game. I love birds, I love flying, I love helping people and I love taking things slow and appreciating this wonderful beautiful world. Some would call the world bland or dead, I find that fitting, it is a cold hostile world where everyone has a chip on their shoulder and truth and honor and justice is harder to find than a landmass bigger than a small island. Its a world of tragedy, and like any tragedy, its beautiful. Seriously, this game has an incredible photo mode and I have hundreds of shots of just scenery and birds and action shots and its so much fun to mess with time and depth of field and zoom out and feel how small your bird is in the vast giant ocean you're set in. This game has more emotion in it than it does anything else and I find that much more important than any mechanic so yes I will play this game over and over because I can't get enough of the feelings I love from this game and I wish everyone could feel this way about this game but I know my way of appreciating this game is different from most people's. If you take nothing away from this review other than my passive contentment for meritocracy I'd like to prove you wrong. This game is an experience, its a feeling more than anything and I love it. I hope people give this game more credit because it really deserves it.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Finally circling back around to change this review.The game is finnicky. It wants you to spend a long time finding your control scheme, and a long time getting used to said control scheme. I don't think that's great, and it was the primary reason I gave it a thumbs down initially. But I came back to try it again, and I ended up liking it. Its a unique game, full of banking, rolling, acrobatic flight unlike anything else I've played, but its also a very pretty game, set atop a bleak salty sea. The story structure, while decidedly weird and often jarring, contains some solid plot writing, even if the dialogue is pretty bland. All in all, after coming back to it, and enjoying it, my final complaint was that while the game teased open world missions and thrilling action, a full 50% of the time it instead delivers poorly paced escort missions and frustrating deaths at the hands of clunky controls & unintuitive enemies that force you to load at the start of the mission.All in all, worth the price, but I don't think I'll be putting more time into it than I have.Old review is below---------------------------I really wanted to like this game, and I will likely come back and purchase it when its on a steeper sale, or perhaps when I have more free time. Until I come back to it and try it again, I'm going to have to leave a negative recommendation. I ended up refunding the game because I had spent over an hour trying to make the flight/camera controls feel decent, and I was running out of refund time to actually play the game itself. I guess the developers wanted to have the game feel meaningfully different than dogfighting games (because you aren't flying a jet/spaceship, you're flying a bird), but the result is that flight feels pretty constrained/sluggish on all three axis of rotation. This combined with the camera's hyper sensitivity means that the flying never felt good for me.I spent a long time ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ around in the controls menu, and I tried flying with a controller, and with a keyboard, but no matter what I was using the controls were unintuitive, and the camera was borderline unusable.  A light tap on one of the WASD keys (default camera control for pc) seems to rotates the camera 90 degrees, and I had similar problems with controller. Regardless of what settings I ticked, my options for camera control seemed to be "looking straight ahead" or "looking uselessly far in either direction".That being said, the game is very pretty, and while the narrative structure is a bit confusing when when you first hop in, I'm hopeful based on the other reivews that say the game has a well written/told story. I like the concept a lot, and this game seems to execute on most of it fairly well. I actually think my frustration was increased because I could tell I would really like this game if only the controls felt less antagonistic.

Never move the players head for them=Sickness2. Always keep the head horizontal as in there should never be a time when I'm looking straight in the real work and my view in game is slanted=Sickness3. Left and right movements are akin to "Smooth Turning" which 95% of the user base will feel sick when it happens which is all the time. _childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game. The aesthetics are gorgeous and the world is full of small details that make it vibrant. The music is really good too, tribal/chanted, perfect for the setting of the game. The flight / combat mechanics are satisfying if you're into the arcade-kind of gameplay.There are some rough edges (overall I find the game slightly too easy, I think. If you're a somewhat experienced gamer, you should go directly to the hardcore difficulty ) :1. the economy is a bit off, I find it a bit too easy to get access to the best gear 2. some mechanics aren't explained / tutorialised, which means you have to refer yourself to the wiki or the discord chat.3. The missions could do with a bit more variety, but that's something that's kind of specific to the dogfight genre I think.4. There's a number of really cool ideas that are somewhat underexploited. HOWEVER : the developer is extremely responsive, and the negative points I find do not reduce my enjoyment of the game. I was looking for something with great aesthetics and an engaging setting and got just that and more. There's a sense of bliss that comes with controlling these birds that's really satisfying, and the story is engaging enough to make me want to see more of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Please note that I only played the base game at the time of review, so this does not include the DLC.Nice game that is however not without some (minor?) annoyances. If you have any doubts, I suggest waiting for discounts. I still feel more inclined to recommend the game than not, hence the thumb up.The pros:- Visually a pretty game, especially the water, the clouds and the weather effects.- Immersive music that hits the right atmosphere, whether it is during a dogfight, general exploration or going to a location during missions.- Palatable story, albeit one wherein there is a bit of faux mysticism and some need to suspend disbelief.- I did complete the game once at the time of review, but might go for another run in order to e.g. complete more Steam Achievements or play with different birds. So I think there is some replayability but I do not now for sure how much.The cons:- When for example in the middle of certain fights, allies or enemies joining the fray briefly lead to a sort of cutscene in which you lose controls and sight of where you are going.P.S.: Please see the advice from the developer in their official response below. It appears one can turn this off.- The controls are (besides the issue mentioned previously), even with mouse and keyboard. However, I would suggest that players put aiming under the same hand as flight (but using the mouse to look around). Most if not all weapons (more or less) play as if they are attached to the bird anyway, so this may be slightly easier than the default mouse/kb settings. This may be a matter of preference though, so trying what works in the prologue mission (I mean the Imperial Peak chapter, not the Dunkle one) may be a good idea.- Somewhat repetitive missions and gameplay, although it is possible to focus on the main missions to keep things a bit more interesting (more story elements that introduce gameplay elements).- Voice acting could be better. Some characters have somewhat silly voices, and pronouncing "Ursee" a bit more German (instead of how USonians would have a try at it) might have made the voice acting more palatable (and help immersion a bit).

_childDocuments_.review: This review will probably change as the game moves on in development.I can't recommend this game due to it's inherent control flaws across all platforms, the buggy and insanely annoying menus, and the very poorly written and organized story that I assume is supposed to be seen through the eyes of many; all of whom we play as at some point.The controls feel... just bad. On controller, aiming is insanely sensitive with no real way to turn it down. Flight stick felt okay, camera controls can't really be used with it (not like you should use the camera). Mouse and Keyboard, despite not being fully supported, genuinely gave me the best experience. The fact that the game claims to be optimized for controller and flight stick but felt infinitely more stable and smooth using a mouse and keyboard doesn't sit well with me, almost making me feel like the dev's were too lazy to really make sure the game controls well at all. The camera and lock-on cameras are awful, snapping your neck to whichever side you want to look rather than it being analog for free movement, and the lock-on will force your bird to dive no matter what, making you fight the camera for control over your bird.The menus. Why do I have to hover my mouse cursor over a specific pixel an inch away from the actual text box in order to select certain menu options, but only sometimes? The actual selection itself feel super jittery and the sharpness of the menuing actions completely break you out of the intended smooth nature of the game, and this is coming from someone who has played BDO and PSO2 which is menu hell. The story and voice acting feel effortless and bland. Everything being narrated through nonsensical rhyming and riddle makes it hard to actually know what the important bits are. NPC's don't talk enough, and when they do it's usually one of two or three voicelines their NPC type has.I really want to love this game. It looks amazing, the concept is amazing, and the gameplay has insane potential. All that needs to happen is the dev's have to figure out if this is an arcade or simulation flying game. Right now, they're dropping the ball on both. I'm going to keep coming back to the game on periodic fixes in hopes that things get better and a sense of direction is established.

_childDocuments_.review: ok, i think i tried this game when it released after liking the concept, but wasnt sold in pancake mode. however, ive now started playing in VR and the game has suddenly come to life for me. great atmosphere, clearly lots of gameplay, and story to trawl through. great sound track, a really great vr experience. I will give you this advice, try playing at 40% world scale in the steamvr settings, and scale the UI to i think roughly 75%, with the camera smoothness all the way up. this enhances the toy scale feel, and puts the UI in a fairly unobtrusive place, bare in mind you can hide it by clicking in the stick on the joypad. it also for me at least makes the twisting and diving when dog fighting a little less sickly, you will still need decent vr legs, but its worth it.the only thing i wish, and would like to suggest to the dev, is that the "fly ahead press A" message and the mission complete return home message could be hidden with the UI. id love to be able to disable the fly ahead option altogether, i just want to enjoy swooping to my destination in vr without an obtrusive ui banner in the way.other than that (which isnt an issue most of the time) im enjoying myself.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been really enjoying this game over the past week. I tend to really enjoy my open world games where I can explore with missions that are short and varied enough to keep me from feeling like there's a constant grind. I'm also a sucker for sea-worlds and multiple warring factions. At the start it was kinda difficult to manage and adjust to flying and fighting, but doing some side quests really helped me get a handle on it. Whenever I got stuck on a story mission I just used that as an opportunity to explore and see what was around. I'm really glad that I stuck with it and got to see more parts of the world and learn about the factions and stories.The game runs incredibly well on my computer with little to no loading time, super satisfying in those times where you're a little impatient. The fast travel they got going is buttery smooth and I'm where I wanna be instantly.Very few minor bugs, any that I got weren't game breaking and didn't last.They added a Pirate DLC before I bought the game, I just wrapped up the story and played some of it and it's a great time. Not sure if more DLCs are in the works, but this one is real fun and I like how it fleshes the world out a bit more.I don't normally write reviews, so now I'm just gonna give some tips/pointers I guess?-You can turn off the HUD by clicking the Right Analog stick down, I don't like having a mini map there all the time, so I just click it a couple times to remove it when I don't want it, the compass HUD is enough.-Pyro Pots recharge when you land at a perch and not from storms like regular ammo.-It was really difficult for me at around the mid point when I picked up a fast mount with low hp.  After dying a lot in a row I went exploring and found other birds I could get and that really helped me out of my death   loop I found myself in. If you're stuck, play side missions and try prepping more, you'll get through itThat's it really. I'm having a good time with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Full disclosure: I'm a friend of the developer. This doesn't guarantee a positive result in terms of reviews. In fact; I hold my developer friends to a high standard, and am generally more critical towards them and their products then I am to other developers and their games. There might be bias, however, and I want to be transparent about it.TL;DR: Great and surprisingly deep game play, fantastic graphics (if you like yours with an indie abstract twist), good narrative/mission and specifically world building and great voice casting. For an indie title it over delivers and manages to spark the imagination. It delivers seemingly casual game play with strategic choices not often apparent in flight combat and as such earns a stern recommendation to anyone moderately interested in flight combat. Longer version:I recommend this game because I love a lot of things about it. There are a tons of reasons to love it, and some reasons to dislike it. I'm a huge fan of dog fighting/aerial combat games.  I hold them dear, from playing "Red Baron", " Deep Strike" ,the "Rogue Squadron" games on N64 & NGC and Microsoft's seminal "Crimson Skies", there is something that appeals to the freedom of flight to me, especially combined with enemies that try to outmanoeuvre you and,subsequently, that exhillerating feeling when you manage to get on top of them and finally getting them squarely boxed into your target reticule after some evasive manoeuvres. Imagine squeezing off a couple of lighting bolts whilst your enemy, a rider on a gigantic bird, plummets to the depths of a hungry ocean, shedding particles of charred feathers, whisked away in stormy winds in the process. This is the very essence of " The Falconeer".    Dog-fighting games usually come down to a rinse-and-repeat affair where you circle your enemy in tightening circles to get the drop on them. "The Falconeer"  doesn't suffer from this. The bird your rider commands can cleverly, and quite naturally, stall mid-air, or zoom abruptly, circumstance permitting, allowing enemies to zoom by and get caught in a surprise attack from behind. Barrel-rolls can also be initiated if enough energy has been charged, which the rider can do when he commands his majestic bird to swoop down. Wind currents can be strategically employed to build additional momentum, demanding from the player to survey his immediate surroundings before committing to a certain type of attack strategy. Missions vary, from offensive to defensive. At the same time the player discovers a magical world, with a variety of cities, abandoned islands and mystical locations commanded by different factions that the player gets to explore. The lore is deep, helped by convincing voice actors and thoughtful writing. The soundtrack deserves a special mention. From soothing ambient tracks whilst you explore the cloudy skies with rolling waves beneath to up-tempo beats with haunting voices rythmically accompanying your fights with pirates, raiders and other warring factions: it all fits perfectly.Brave the skies. This game is worth it. Support a unique developer, and embark on an adventure like nothing you've experienced before.

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game!There's a little confusion as you hop in that lots of people seem to get stuck on - it doesn't do the best job of communicating its mechanics, but the mechanics themselves are finely polished and incredibly fun.This is nothing to say of the worldbuilding and the little flavor-jobs you can do on the side on many places.Bonus points for quality and ingenious features such as map zooming out the higher you fly, or the fantastic way the braking/cobra is implemented - so many games tried to accomplish just that and failed miserably. 10/10 need more
_childDocuments_.name: The Falconeer

_childDocuments_.review: Everything is awkward at first. Controls, presentation, visuals. But I grew to like the gameplay loop and visuals. I mean it's nothing next gen but it's a one man project and I encountered 0 bugs or performance issues. If anything it plays wonderfully. The story is lacking, but at least it's not intrusive. Even voice acting isn't bad. This game released as a launch title for the XBOX ONE X as a benchmark for high attainable fps rather than super high fidelity graphics. All in all, a good experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Falconeer

_childDocuments_.review: If you have already played air combat games before and you have a flight stick then the sky above the Ursea in The Falconeer is right for you. It is astonishing that this game is created just by a single developer and has the art style and entrancing music that enable you to quite literally get lost in the clouds for hours when you need to get out of the real world. It is a game where the playtime can be as long as you give yourself to exploring all the secrets and lore of the Ursea. It does not hold your hand and shepherd you down a specific path, it is easily possible to take a break from the set missions and explore the map to discover new locations, Merchants to upgrade your gear or temples and relics that tell the lore of the world. If you find a nice location, or want to capture the explosion of a giant airship then there is a photo mode from the pause menu that will freeze the world allowing you to pan around, change focus, zoom and even change the passage of the day to get the perfect angle and conditions for that shot, the resulting image is then able to be shared with your friends as proof of your feats in battle.
_childDocuments_.name: The Falconeer

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful, mythical, mystical flight combat simulator with heart. Flight mechanics are simple but enjoyable. You can get lost just soaring, to the point where missions almost feel like a chore. The world is just tons of fun and visually gorgeous, with a really distinct art style. Honestly? The only drawback with this game is that there just isn't enough of it. I would absolutely lose myself if this game expanded slightly in size and scope.
_childDocuments_.name: The Falconeer

_childDocuments_.review: A very atmospheric little gem.There are some bugs but most of them can be avoided easily. Most concern escort missions, the main one is: do not leave the ship you are escorting or you might chase/aggro enemies further away which flee and leave you unable to complete the mission.The controls and the game mechanics are not explained well but easy enough to pick up (with a bit useful wiki that fills the last gaps).The story is presented nicely and the voices are pretty good but it gets a bit... stupid? weird?... in the last chapter. Subjective, of course, so you might like where it is headed.That being said, everything about the game itself works really nicely if you do not expect tripleA production value. Good, fun flight games like this (in the Tie Fighter/Wing Commander tradition) are rare and this is well worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Falconeer

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting take on aerial combat and a nice break of the "space combat" with ships. Switching them out with bids - and space with a flooded world is just a genius NEW thing to do.-The graphic is something... new - if you can get used to it, you will definitly enjoy flying over the ocean to explore, guard ships, fly missions and find out more about the background story.-The music is very nice in the background and doesnt get annoying over time.-The controls (im using mouse/keyboard) are definitly working nicely - and the devs are still working on finetuning it. im in nearly 20 hours - and i am far from having seen everything.I also didnt come across any gamebreaking bugs.The people working on it put in a lot of love into details and continue doing so!the only downside for me:i was hoping for a little more rpg stuff, bonding with your bird - but who knows what will come.For the price tag, definitly worth it! And a must see for people interested in the theme!
_childDocuments_.name: The Falconeer

_childDocuments_.review: I'm still dipping my feet in but I can definitely say this game is fun. The dev also seems to be showing a lot of support which is always a good sign.I've played, I think, every single game the developer listed as their inspiration for this game. This game seems to capture the feel of Crimson Skies (the xbox version) and Robotech very well. The combat is very arcadey but there's enough nuance to really make it shine. You can get into boring turning fights on easy or bump up the difficulty and find yourself in a fun dance that really keeps you on your toes. I am seeing a fair bit of people complaining about the difficulty and I, honestly, have no idea where this is coming from. Hardcore is very tough in the beginning but normal is almost too easy. I've only died once and that was because I set the game to hardcore and charged into a bounty as the very first thing I did. I would humbly advise to ignore anyone complaining about this game's difficulty. Normal has been a cake walk, and I don't even want to imagine how easy is. I just found a bird that forgoes all HP for really great base stats and I'm excited to try it out on hardcore. It reminds me of playing Ace Combat 6 on the hardest difficulty, flying that DLC F-22 (Mobius) with stupid high stats but no defense. I would die if I was sneezed on so I had to go through a whole level without a scratch. I'm hoping I'll find the same level of challenge in The Falconeer. I will admit that there are some elements the game doesn't explain very well. I have no idea what a higher star lightning tank (or whatever it's called) gets me. It took me a little bit to realize what "ENG" meant.  These are things that I can see being a downside to a one person team. I'm sure everyone has had moments where they've done something that makes perfect sense to them, only to have others be completely perplexed. Sometimes you need someone else to stand in and admit that something may not make sense. Performance has been great. I haven't crashed or run into any noticeable bugs that have broken the game. That being said, I do find the game somewhat lacking visually. It's not bad, by any means, but it looks a bit dated. Although I will confess that I can run games like Red Dead Redemption 2 completely maxed out, so I'm spoiled. I'm terrible at reviews so I'll leave it at is. Bottom line is I think this game is very enjoyable so far. It doesn't give me the urge to binge the whole game, but did have me excited to get home from work and play it today. That's something big AAA games haven't been able to do for me in a very long time. This game, like the game sit draws from (Freelancer, Crimson Skies), will be as fun or boring as you let it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Falconeer

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful and enjoyable game.The visuals, are stunning and the game can be quire relaxing if you choose to just fly around and explore, the world creation is spectacular with lots of strange and unusual things to see.Combat is fun, (think arcade world war 1 fighter like wings) but with more interesting opponents and the story and world building are great. There were some very gifted people working on this project, and they've made an incredible world in which to adventure upon a soaring war bird.Definitely an engaging game.In relation to a couple of negative reviews, I admit that I struggled a little with the controls (mouse and keyboard) but it really didn't take long to get used to the slightly different system. I tried the joystick controls, and while they were fine, I actually returned to the mouse/keyboard and am quite comfortable with it.Secondly, the complaint regarding a lot of flying with short instances of fighting, followed by a lot of flying never really was an issue for me. The game provides a couple of fast travel options, and I never really felt bored moving from place to place. I have to admit though, that I get a lot of satisfaction flying my magnificent bird around this beautiful world.A couple of items of feed back for the developers though.1. It really would be great to store items in a location, It kind of sucks having to give up a sublime level  weapon to try out a different type.2. Some kind of a journal or indication on the map to tell us which shrines/temples we've visited in each chapter so that we can fulfill the sea witches requirements.3. A key binding for access to the map world map directly.
_childDocuments_.name: The Falconeer

_childDocuments_.review: A positive surprise.This game is a fantasy-style reimagination of classical retro WW1 aerial combat shooters. Dive-bombing ships and intense dogfights just like back in the days, before twin stick shooters. Easy to learn, hard to master. It is amazing, what one man achieved just by programming hard. Solid graphics, tight controls and a seemingly deep background story. This one is good, not just by the standards of indie games. If it weren't for the voice-over storytelling, it would be comparable to gems like Panzer Dragoon (which didn't have that), especially if you switch the CAMERA SETTING TO MOUSE CONTROL AND AIM. Those who complain that it doesn't play like modern games don't know what retro nostalgia is like.After a relaxing stroll over open waters, you ride your warbird through a stormcloud before crushing some pirates while listening to a marvelous soundtrack.  Then you dive into the seas to grab massive bombs, which you throw at their ships. You return into the stormclouds in order to recharge your weapon. Afterwards, you're sad because the battle could have lasted longer, no matter how long it took. If this game has a downside, it's that it's hard to let go of.

_childDocuments_.review: Like many games lately, The Falconeer had a rough launch. The developer definitely cares about the game and has worked on improvements through free patches with QoL, new content, and balance changes.This is no AAA game, it is a game by a solo developer born of passion. Its target audience is someone looking for a good story and a casual dogfighter experience with some exploration.Here's the rundown:---{Graphics}---☐ You forget what reality is☑ Beautiful☐ Good☐ Decent☐ Bad☐ Don‘t look too long at it☐ MS-DOSFor a solo developer, the graphics are really quite impressive. It is not realistic, but comes with a distinct and consistent visual style. Screenshots from this game are gorgeous.---{Gameplay}---☐ Very good☑ Good☐ It‘s just gameplay☐ Mehh☐ Watch paint dry instead☐ Just don'tIf you're looking for a realistic or complex dogfighter, this isn't it. There is a relatively small selection of weapons, ammo types, passive upgrades, and stat upgrades. The combat is enjoyable although repetitive once you master it.---{Audio}---☐ Eargasm☑ Very good - Music☑ Good - SFX☑ Not too bad - Voice acting☐ Bad☐ I'm now deafI've seen lots of other reviews note the voice acting as being painful. Yes, not all of the voice actors are equally skilled, but I didn't think it was anything to be upset over. Just don't take them too seriously.---{Audience}---☐ Kids☐ Teens☐ Adults☑ All---{PC Requirements}---☐ Check if you can run paint☐ Potato☑ Decent☐ Fast☐ Rich boi☐ Ask NASA if they have a spare computerThis game is well optimized. Runs smoothly even on a decent laptop.---{Difficulity}---☐ Just press 'W'☐ Easy☐ Significant brain usage☑ Easy to learn / Hard to master☐ Difficult☐ Dark SoulsThe steam store page says mouse & keyboard is not supported. This is not true, however a controller is highly recommended. If you want to play with m&k, mess with the control options (there are a lot!) and see what works for you best. I've played through the game on hardcore with m&k and had no issues, it just takes some getting used to.---{Grind}---☐ Nothing to grind☐ Only if u care about leaderboards/ranks☑ Isn't necessary to progress☐ Average grind level☐ Too much grind☐ You‘ll need a second live for grindingYou might need to play some side missions if you die a lot (losing money) or if you want that shiny new weapon immediately. Grinding for it is optional though, you could just play the story missions and eventually get enough.---{Story}---☐ No Story☐ Some lore☐ Average☐ Good☑ Lovely☐ It‘ll replace your lifeIt takes a bit to get warmed up to, but the story is one of the best parts of this game. If you don't care about story or the world lore, don't bother to read mission briefs, or don't listen to dialogue, you will be very bored.---{Game Time}---☐ Long enough for a cup of coffee☐ Short☑ Average☐ Long☐ To infinity and beyondCurrently, there are 4 chapters with 10 story missions each. There are repeatable side missions and lots of locations to explore otherwise.---{Price}---☐ It’s free!☑ Worth the price☐ If u have some spare money left☐ Not recommended☐ You could also just burn your moneyI feel that the price is reasonable, especially after the recent updates.---{Bugs}---☐ Never heard of☑ Minor bugs☐ Can get annoying☐ ARK: Survival Evolved☐ The game itself is a big terrarium for bugsI've encountered a few bugs, although they have been fixed now. The developer is very responsive to bug reports and feedback.Hopefully this review helps you decide whether this game is right for you. Comments are enabled, feel free to ask any questions there.

And it took me around 10 hours to finish the 'main story'. There are a few con's though. I personally found the story boring. The world feels empty. And the game is very repetitive.
