_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed beta testing this game and I can't wait to dive in again this weekend. The Falconeer is a very wellrounded, enjoyable game to play. The graphics and art style are simple yet elegantly done, and the game itself can run smoothly on my Surface laptop without bumping the framerate down, which was a super pleasant surprise. The lore of the world is interesting and I really have enjoyed exploring Ursee. The flight mechanics, coupled with the minimal but pleasing soundtrack, make for a very soothing experience.I personally struggle with fighting based games and the combat here is challenging! There's a high learning curve which, in my opinion, makes it worthwhile to play as well. It definitely takes a few hours to get it down.I definitely recommend it if you're looking for not only a combat game but an exploration flight sim as well.
_childDocuments_.name: The Falconeer

_childDocuments_.review: A great little game, fairly priced and very polished, with an interesting and unique fantasy setting and excellent subtle worldbuilding. The developer is very responsive to feedback and clearly passionate about the game.There isn't a ton of content for the long term, and the upgrade system and difficulty scaling could be a little better fleshed out, but what's there is a great time and I'm looking forward to supporting the dev by getting the DLC.Besides, the game looks and sounds amazing. Riding a giant bird over open ocean is about as cool as one might expect the concept to be.Crimson Skies was cited as an inspiration for the game on the forums, and I can certainly see the resemblance to one of my favorite older-generation games. There's also quite a bit that's reminiscent of Dishonored and The Wind Waker, in the best ways. Still, the lore has its own distinct flavor and doesn't come off as derivative.Performance is pretty good on a modest gaming laptop running Coffee Lake and a GTX 1070. Some hitches at 120fps, but that's likely to be due to hardware thermal issues, seeing as the game runs very well at all other times. A tip for PC players: Play with full mouse controls, not WASD. Seriously. The game is clunky without analog controls, but with the full mouse control scheme it handles nearly as well as a HOTAS setup - excellently programmed and very smooth.I just wish the dev had enough of a budget and team to make this twice the game it is now, with more expansive systems and activities. Buy the game so we can have a Falconeer 2 one day - for anyone who wants a proper successor to the 2000s-era, third person arcade flight sim/shooters, this is the best we've got.

_childDocuments_.review: Read this review and others The Falconeer is the title presented by the mind of Tomas Sala, who as a solo dev, has created his story around aerial combat and a fantastic world overwhelmed by the immensity of the ocean and breathtaking skies.The adventure follows the world of “The Great Ursee”, full of small archipelagos, mountains, and maritime chasms, mirrored all around the corner. This title is also marked by a story with many intrigues, in the style of Game of Thrones.The player wears the skin of a Falconeer, a pilot who holds the reins of a huge bird where his main objective is to perform tasks for several island nations, in a partially open world. As the name shows, the biggest part of the game involves driving the bird itself, in order to fulfill a certain objective. Of course, things are not so linear, as it involves combat mechanics against enemy factions.The controls are accessible and quite simple, but there is a learning curve that will accompany the player throughout his missions. At your disposal, the player has the attack button and the possibility to perform defense maneuvers, more precisely the possibility to dodge enemy attacks. In addition to this action, which after a while can become a bit monotonous, there is also the possibility of picking up floating bombs and printing damage to enemy boats. These are the two main types of enemies, boats, aircraft, and other Falconeers.That said, its gameplay becomes super repetitive over time, but what drives the player to continue his adventure is really his story. This title attempts to demonstrate all sides of the barricade, as it places the player himself as an agent of change on opposite sides of the conflict. A little confusing, but in fact, the game changes its perspective as you dive into its lines of thought. There are a lot of soldiers coming from different islands with different cultures, which enriches their entire environment.There are two types of missions, the main ones that accompany the narrative and the secondary ones that are mostly designed to collect money. It is interesting to make improvements to the warbird, with descriptions that are really little seen. It is possible to use mutagenic items to improve certain aspects, giving access to passive effects that can, for example, improve its ability to fly, or make the bird itself in a state of permanent fear.Unfortunately, the checkpoint system in this title can make things quite frustrating. The missions usually last a long time, since they have several stages. The problem is that even with the difficulty of the game in normal, our bird is very fragile and it is very easy to lose the notion of life bar when our concern is to knock down all enemies and not crush against rocks or even enemy ships.Although the whole environment is stupidly well brushed, most of it is practically empty. Yes, it has brilliant sunsets, water effects, and very good clouds, but that’s it.The soundtrack captures perfectly the lonely feeling of an approaching storm.In short, The Falconeer will have a hard time trying to please all the players, but thinking that this title was produced by just one person it gives a whole other taste to take our own bird and break the winds and tides.

_childDocuments_.review: So my original rating for this review was negative, as on launch this game was incredibly disappointing and I have not really looked back at it since. However, I'm changing it to a positive, because the developers seem to have been actively working upon fixing the problems and addressing issues that were raised by reviewers. This clearly shows that the devs really do care about this game- but not only that... They also care enough to be willing to take their time to let people who pointed out these issues and were left dissatisfied know that they updated some things and are working on improving the game. I'll likely pick it up again in the future to try it out in its much more improved state.I had big hopes for this game as I had been itching for a fun aerial combat game that wasn't just airplanes, but I couldn't really enjoy this game at all because of the faults it has so early on.First off: The game audio is all over the place. Some SFX was incredibly loud, other ones incredibly soft, and there were no separate settings for music and SFX. I select for voices to be at half volume and yet randomly it would have certain npc's play it at nearly full volume. Some voices end up being too soft at that volume, other ones are still too loud- and the voice acting does not help. It feels like there were maybe only three, four people that did the voice lines for each npc in the game that isn't the narrator, and the accents chosen for the characters are honestly ear-grating and very.... I would say immersion-breaking. As an example, one of the accents seems to be intended to be the "gruff guy" accent, but it doesn't SOUND like a gruff guy, it sounds like someone doing a joking impression of a gruff guy. I didn't play this game for long enough to probably get into the grit of things, but honestly I don't... want to. There's little fun or draw into the game early on- you just get thrown into it with no explanation of the world setting or your character's place in the world. At some point I suddenly had to select a new character because I think I accidentally failed my first mission and just had my character straight up die or something? I wouldn't know, because there's literally no explanation for anything. Some games are capable of pulling off the "Throw you in and explain later" shtick fine, but it does not work here. There's no story to pull you in at the start, nor is the gameplay explained properly (nor are you eased into it well enough) to keep you wanting to play to find the story. The learning curve seems to be incredibly hard because you don't get a chance to learn at all, no small set of tutorial missions to get you used to things.There's also an unholy amount of exposition dumping over a flat, boring, map early game that pretends like you know everything, and it just makes it incredibly confusing. It does not help that the character introducing you to everything has little personality as well. There is supposedly a story somewhere, but the story is absolutely not introduced in a way that makes it easy to follow and find.Here's a little list of gripes I had in my first 60 minutes of the game.- On the top right, when you lock a target, every single person is displayed in red as if they were an enemy, even if they are friendly. This confused me when I was trying to do a mission that had friendlies helping me, because I thought they were enemies and i kept shooting them, and there is barely a visible indicator when you are not locked onto them. (the indicator is only that the lock shows up blue, not red.)-On top of that, target locking seems to do very little to help you. The camera doesn't turn with the thing you're locked on, I was expecting at least SOMETHING to help me be able to keep track of who i'm shooting at! - Can't really tell when you're "dashing", as the very slight indication of wind stripes took me a while to notice. Even then, this does not really... feel like a dash. More like "fly a little faster", rather than a dash.-Can't combat roll when holding an item... Meaning that protecting yourself and the item you're carrying is incredibly difficult. -Landing at a location is a mess. The amount of times I smacked myself into a wall because I didn't press A fast enough to land at the TINY spot it shows me the prompt at was frustrating.-Map markers are confusing, and there is no way to put a point on a map so you can easily travel to it without having to constantly open the full map.-No proper indicators of when you are supposedly overheating. Is it the power packs turning yellow? Is that it? Because that is miniscule and you don't pay attention to that when you're in the middle of a storm trying to figure out which direction the enemies had gone off to since they seem to enjoy spinning around you, while also trying to avoid smacking into a wall.-Ran into an issue during the "dropping a mine" tutorial(?) where I destroyed the ship I was supposed to drop a mine onto with my regular fire, causing the tutorial to cut off early and not teach me how to pick up and then drop mines onto targets.It's sad, I really would have liked to enjoy this game but a pretty artstyle and decent flying mechanics really can't make up for all the gripes I experienced in only the first hour of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game, put it simply, is fantastic. Not only is the world beautiful, but the soundtrack and combat in this game are also wonderful. The lore and story is both direct, and silent/subversive at the same time, making the player really have to think about what's going on. _childDocuments_.review: Moving this to the top as I am going to give it a thumbs up but state that you should wait and pick this game up on sale as it does offer some enjoyment, unless your like me and wanted to support the Dev in hopes of a squeal as I played this on Xbox Game Pass first.I want to love this game, I really do, there are just to many little things that come add up to where I mostly just like the game.-= Warning this will contain some spoilers =-For starters... Its told across multi-pal chapters that have you controlling different people so I cant really immerse myself into the story as just when I start getting into it the chapter is over and now your playing someone completely different.  Honestly this is the biggest thing I have against the game that annoys me to no end.The second issue I have is the main story-line, the further on you go it ends up with so many plot holes you could fly a 747 through them.. The main "Bad Guys" by the end do so many things that would turn others against them, on top of having there most powerful forces wrecked, manage to overthrow the imperial government and take over?!?  And the rest of the Imperial forces just seem to go with it?!?My third issue is really a bunch of minor issues rolled into one.   For starters your equipment for your bird and rider is basically non existent, No armor for you or your bird, which kind of dumb founded me.  You can buy different guns from I think was 4 or 5 choices, and it has this really weird ammo system where you can buy different types of "ammo" but you cant switch ammo types, just use it in the order its stacked on your saddle, which of course is never explained to you.   Poor base and ship meshes.  Through many fights you need to attack bases or ships where you can attack turrets or other specific locations, though even using an explosive weapon half the time I couldn't even damage the item I had locked on unless I was straight above it.  One side mission I was on I suddenly needed to fire a rocket pod to proceed with no warning before hand I would need to.. I had one but had already used it earlier in the fight... which is just another part of the super poor tutorial and mechanic info this game has, hell the game doesn't even teach you how to LAND!  I ended up having to pause and look it up on the net.  I also purchased the Bounty Hunters writ but never could find any special bounties other then what the game normally has..  Also the Salvage and Pirate add-on's to the game, Honestly forgot all about them as once again theirs no in-game direction about them.  The dragon add-on is just a separate class/person to pick to get the one dragon from what I can tell as I haven't seen anywhere else in the game offering dragons for you to buy.This game had SO much potential but it feels like it was rushed out the door without being gone over and touched up or polished any.I love the world and the idea behind it all and I really hope it does get a sequel, though with maybe a larger team to properly flesh it out and make a proper story-line.  I do understand that this game is made by one man and honestly I probably wouldn't of even written a review talking about the different points about the game if it wasn't a series of short stories instead of a normal story-line...  Yes I HATE short stories that much. lolNow that I have all that out of the way I did enjoy the game to a point, I just didnt lose myself in it like I so often do with the game I play, again due to the short story esk route it took.  If this would have had your normal create a character where you play all the way through I would of happily been scouring every nook and cranny and chasing after every side quest I could find but as is there were a few towns I didnt even bother with due to my lack of immersion.  At the end I would give this game a 5 out of 10 as it does do some things right, creates a world that has so many possibilities for story telling in it and honestly if there is a Falconeer 2 I can guarantee I will be looking at it in hopes it is a larger world with a single story to be told to me through my character!

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played for a little bit, but I'm really enjoying being a Falconeer. The visuals are absolutely stunning, and the FPS is flawless. Technical bits aside, the gameplay so far feels like old school open-world mission games like Freelancer. I can perch my giant falcon at any friendly harbor, pick up any job I have the reputation for, and earn all the splinters I need. There are some pretty clear factions, and your reputation determines where you can travel safely and what jobs you can pick up.The world and mechanics are pretty awesome, too. You "reload" your ammo by getting struck by lightning, you can dive to catch and eat fish to heal up your falcon, and there are all kinds of exploration treasures and rewards if you stray a tiny bit away from the beaten path. But don't go too far, there are some dangerous things lurking in the water.I haven't gotten too far into the storyline so I can't really speak to it, but I just like idly soaring from island to island, taking jobs and killing pirates. _childDocuments_.review: Loving it so far.Pros:-Gorgeous graphics-Gamepad controls are smooth and responsive-Open world is truly open-Campaign grabs you and missions are short early on, which keeps the plot and action moving-Deep lore/factions/systems/story, all of which means there's something new to see/do/learn pretty much everywhere you go.-Interesting relationship with falcons (mutagens aren't exactly healthy for the birds, creating a moral ambiguity that I hope the game explores as I progress)-Engaging sound effects/music and really strong voice acting (and LOTS of it)!Cons:-Combat could offer more variety, but to be fair I haven't seen a ton of the game yet, and there are lots of weapon types I can't afford yet, not to mention different ammo-Camera can be a tiny bit finicky, but that's really nitpicking-Controls with keyboard/mouse are not great, but I knew that going in, and this type of game doesn't lend itself to kb/m anyway in my opinion, so this is nitpickingOverall, so far, I'm super satisfied with this purchase.  This game scratches an itch I can't get anywhere else right now.  It's like aerial exploration in old-school WoW with flying mounts combined with aerial dog fights that remind me of Divinity 2: Director's Cut, but it's even better than the sum of those parts.  And to think this was designed essentially by one person?  Amazing/much respect!  I fully expect this game to be lovingly cared for by the developer, and any minor nits I've noticed so far will almost certainly be updated (especially if the developer's past track record with mods is anything to go by). _childDocuments_.review: I've never really been interested in aerial combat games before, but I was really interested in the aesthetics of this game, so I decided to check it out and I'm very glad I did.This game is an incredible mix of fantasy, steam-punk and a bit of Lovecraft thrown in, the setting reminds me a lot of Sunless Sea. The writing is great, although it falters in some places. It gives you a sense that the world you're in has a long past, shrouded in mystery. The voice-acting, similarly, is very engaging, and does a lot to pull you into the story, although in a small handful of places the audio quality of some speakers was noticeably worse than the rest of the game.The story itself I actually found really interesting.  Without giving too much away, you're given the story in bits and pieces, some of which are told to you, others of which you experience first-hand. It's not always given to you in order, and you'll come across pieces of information that reveal a new side to information you thought you knew, or fill in the gaps of something that didn't seem complete. There were a few times where what I thought were off-handed comments by characters actually turned out to have deeper significance. Some deeper parts of the lore you're never told, it's all about your ability to link scraps of information to a larger history. Early in the game, you begin to encounter the creation myths that serve as the foundation to the world's dominant religion, and as you play, you not only feel more connected to the world through learning these stories, but you also learn not to simply dismiss them.As a result of this, I'd say you should finish the story missions in as few sittings as possible, because you'll really miss out if you don't play for a week and forget the information told to you, as there's no journal or log where the information you learn is written down, and as of right now, you can't replay any story missions except the last ones of each chapter.The graphics are their own style, low-poly but good quality, and I never really found myself wishing for more detail. The actual world itself is quite expansive, and at times it feels a little empty when you fly for a while and don't see anyone or anything going on. There is meant to be a war (or something close to it) going on, but outside of the missions, the world itself felt very peaceful. I would have liked to see more fighting between conflicting factions, or just see more ships, zeppelins and fellow falconeers going about their business. I know it's possible too, because in some missions, you really do feel like you're taking part in massive battles, so the capability to have a good number of NPCs on-screen seems to be there.The combat itself is simple, but very solid. I never really felt as if it were repetitive, and while I do wish some things were spelled out more clearly (such as the fact that dying takes money away from you and replaces the ammo you bought with the default loadout), it is mostly intuitive and easy to pick up for someone who has never really played aerial combat games before like me. I feel like the devs meant for tactical retreating to be a useful part of combat, but I always found that as soon as you turn around to retreat, the opponents become suspiciously accurate as you flee, and since you're limited as to how often you can dodge, turning and letting them get behind you is almost a certain way to die fast, so you're better off just staying in the fight. If you hit a mission that's a roadblock, it's not always that you're just unskilled, it could be a sign that you need to take some time and do side missions, races and other tasks to improve your equipment, which also serve as an avenue to get you out there and exploring the world.Overall, I'd say this is an incredibly good game, from the combat to the writing and the worldbuilding. I was shocked to learn that it was developed by just one person. He could have gotten away with doing a lot less, and in some ways, I think the good quality of this game works against him, since my first instinct is to compare it against games from much larger studios with much higher budgets. I'm definitely going to be looking out for more content for this game!

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to give this game a chance, but I can't get used to flying. I'm using keyboard and mouse, which I understand the dev message says is not what it was designed for, but the remapping option in the controller settings is nearly impossible to deal with. If I try to pick a conflicting key to remap, rather than clear the other button, it requires the user to remap the next button, and then remap the previous button, and then remap another button. The option can't even be backed out of. You'd think "just hit ESC and you'll get out of the remapping" but no, it remaps to the ESC button. There are two modes for keyboard and mouse movement. In one, the mouse moves the camera, in the other, the mouse aims the bird, in both the game will have a tendency to lock in inverted controls, which I don't want. I was able to get out of that by swapping through the controls until in was on regular again, but it doesn't always stay where I left it, because ESCing out of a menu is not the same as "save and close"ing out of a menu. I didn't get past the tutorial mission. I currently regret buying this game. Maybe I'll give it another try later, but this was a bad first impression and I'm not eager to do so. _childDocuments_.review: Great game so far. Really enjoying it. Great atmosphere, decent graphics and a nice, smallish open world to fly/glide around in. The story is decent and the controls are relatively easy to get used to, especially for a guy like me that doesn't like to use a game pad for anything bar flying/racing/fighting games. (Which i don't play very much)The game consists of several chapters, in which you begin with a basic bird, weaponry etcYou also level up your bird gathered from missions and earn coin in order to progress your bird each chapter. Don't get too attached though because you can and will lose some birds depending on the chapter you are starting.Missions consist of your typical, fetch, assault, defend or escort (May be more later on i dunno)But vary enough so that most battles do feel unique in some way or another.If you die, you lose a little bit of gold (Possibly experience though i didn't notice when i died) and whatever upgraded ammo pots you had, but restart from the last checkpoint.The dev is extremely nice and helpful. I asked a question in the forums and about 5 mins later the dev responded personally with perfect advice. The only 2 things I could possibly speak of in a negative manner is that $42 Au is maybe a tad too much. If it were say $30 Au, I believe that a lot more people would pick it up. But tbh if i paid $40 for this, so far i would feel that i am getting my moneys worth. The second is that the voice acting is hilariously bad. But it really didn't bother me apart from 1 character. Mostly it just made me laugh and cringe.Overall this is a very relaxing, beautiful & some times hectic game that I've really taken a liking to. Not to mention that it is kind of unique in it's own way.Thumbs up mate. Well done.

_childDocuments_.review: An arcady aerial combat game with combat falcons - Enjoyable but with noticeable weaknesses or: A fantasy freelancer-like game with falcons instead of spaceshipsI really enjoyed the world in the beautiful comic like graphics, it's just too bad, that it's actually pretty empty. The regions that are not just water are really enjoyable (you can see some of them in the screens on th shop site) everything in between was just so empty. In my 10 hours playthrough (normal difficulty) I never had the actual need to rise higher than the flying height of the airships in game (that's not pretty high). Most of the gameplay is just bound so close to the ground/sea, you don't need to fly super high. If you do though, the only thing you can find are jet streams that speed you up for a short time. Getting up there often takes more time than just flying straight forward (the speed bonus is negligible if you count in the time you need to get up that high). I wished there was more gameplay in bigger heigths.While a story of espionage, sabotage and war unfolds through the chapters and is somewhat enjoyable, the conclusion was somewhat anticlimactic. While there's some interesting developments going on in chapters 3 and 4 all the builtup is not used in the last few missions of chapter 5 at all. The lore is mainly told though some kind of prophecies/writings on shrines you can visit, unfortunately most of them are written in a such mystic way, that it's hard to get your hands on the lore at all. I'd so loved to learn more about the world, the life in this world, and the discoveries made in the later chapters ...Many of the story missions involve escorting ships that are just slightly faster than the falcons slowest flying speed. While this wouldn't be an issue if there was just a handful of these missions, there's just so many of em. Give me fight's like the one in the last mission of chapter 1. There's also some kind of stealth mechanic in the game but it is neglected until the very last 2 missions of the whole story. I wish some of the gameplay mechanics were explained a bit better in game (e.g. give weapons more readable stats than stars, give an option to show numbers instead of bars when it comes to pilot/falcon stats)This review may sound harsher than it's meant to sound. I enjoyed the game and I'd love to love it, but can't because of the reasons given above. The pricing is fair (I rushed through the story as soon as i got a weapon with max star rating), but I don't recommend getting the game guide in its current form, as it's not having enough content (lore!!!) to justify another 4€ spent. The soundtrack on the other hand is superb and totally worth the money!For some reason I had to think of the space game freelancer the whole time. While the scenario may be totally different, the core gameplay with it's progression system and the missions just felt so similar.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like the Falconeer, but there's just not enough to it to hold my attention for very long. The majority of gameplay consists of flying in a straight line through a beautiful but monotonous seascape. Dogfighting, when it did occur, did a poor job of making me feel like I was riding a falcon. Your actions consist of a roll, a trigger button, and a secondary attack. There's no stooping, stalling, wingtip turns, using your claws, or any of the other maneuvers an actual raptor might perform. You're functionally piloting a biplane or a downgraded Starfox 64 fighter, except that collisions have no consequences.I didn't quite make it to the end of the first chapter, but I found the "open world" so far consists mostly of a few fixed landing points that offered merchants and fetch/kill/escort quests. Thus far, I only encountered enemies when they specifically spawned for a quest.  The voice acting was surprisingly professional and the actors certainly seemed to have enjoyed their roles. However, I found the whole tone of the game dissonant. A setting where everyone is one bad business deal from starvation gels poorly with pirates bellowing PG nautical insults at you. Graphically, the sea is pretty, the fog and clouds are lovely and actually quite impressive (but overabundant), and everything else is rendered in the plastic style that's become the 3D version of pixel art. It's intended to disguise a limited budget as an artistic choice. Your mileage may vary. The bigger problem is the ocean setting. Flying through mountains to deliver mail might at least be an interesting exercise. If you have to make everything happen over water (due maybe to the aforementioned budget limits), being able to see more of it at a time and making it more varied would have helped.  So would having more to do.

_childDocuments_.review: I give this game a rank C (60-65%)Okay game - not bad but you can skip it or try on sale.See my profile for more details about my reviews.I stand at a crossroad where I fit all the criteria to get a refund on The Falconeer: bought in the past 2 weeks, played less than 2 hours... and not satisfied with my purchase. The reason I won't do it is simply because the game is 1) super cheap on sale 2) not so bad after all and 3) remarkably genuine, authentic. And I have a tendency to praise genuineness and authenticity in art. The Falconeer has been made with so much love, so much effort, so much attention AND intention to do something unique, different, rich and generous in lore, style, etc, that even if I doubt I will ever put more playtime in it, I could not reasonably give it less than 60%. Some people might even love it just because it has a personality, for sure!It is not for me - yeah it is not bad, it's okay, it's fine, but... I need so much more at my level in life, and The Falconeer has just too many flaws, so many clunky, awkward and clumsy stuff in its design that I doubt I will ever like it.The lore? sure, it is rich and omnipresent... but so confusing! Who is what? uh? it needs some serious editing and streamlining, as of now it is quite hard to digest all that.The art? it is pretty and quite personal, and at the same time I get so tired nowadays of this overused "flat shading" style since Massive Chalice, Ashen, more recently Windbound, etc... just too many games like that. It ends up being so generic and deja vu.The level design? it seems big and has some very fascinating parts (the chasms in the water, whirlpool style). But after 20 minutes you're bored, it feels big and empty.The gameplay? I REALLY wanted to like a modern tribute to Panzer Dragoon/Lylat Wars gameplay, that was such a cool and not-so-often-used concept... but this one felt quite heavy, slow and boring. (Also, I never saw the tutorial instructing me of the buttons... the main buttons should always be displayed on the side of the screen and removable in options, or something).The overall UI, menus, interactions? so clumsy! so non intuitive! I have no idea what I am doing. You choose stuff during your choice of character of missions? some stuff appear, you have no idea, and the narrator dictates everything each time you select something else!Also, talking about the voices and the dialogues, oh my god, it just keeps talking, the voice over is okay-ish, a bit amateur and not very enticing except for some, but it just blabbers and blabbers about stuff you don't really care about, not really meaningful lines... the actors must have felt it, because they barely express anything. Too abstract!It is sad, because the world was so promising, and the work is tremendous in this game - but it needed some streamlining, a better art direction, and writing editing... I truly think the dev is a remarkable artist with great ideas, now I believe they need some craftsmen around to do an amazing, solid, efficient next game. is  on  on  on

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 would falcon pilot again.Seriously. This is a great game if you're looking for an interesting, chill, dogfighter/trader game set in a very intriguing setting. For me the game fills the same sort of niche as Sunless Skies, except quite a bit less heavy on the narrative and text. It's a great game to just run jobs for the various islands and explore the setting. The main story wants you to be invested in the political situation of the setting, which I recognize isn't for everyone. And on top of that: it doesn't really do a great job of easing you into the political situation, basically just thrusting it upon you from the get go with only a little background, so you have to be predisposed to enjoy that kind of drama. For example: In the first chapter you are working for one of the last independent islands, Dunkle, and the plot surrounds Dunkle's lease on an extremely valuable mining outpost not being renewed. You are very much sort of a side character in each life, subtly impacting things from the sidelines as things unfold and happen to the world around you.

_childDocuments_.review: + The graphics are fairly simplistic but gorgeous+ Every single item you can buy or sell (except Mutagens) sell for the original price. This means that you never waste money when you no longer need a weapon, or want to test out other weapons+ You can instantly teleport to a closer location when you are done with a quest (cuts down needless downtime, which is superb)+ Weapons feel impactful, and the ammo refilling system is unique (you need to enter storm clouds to refill your vials)+ The atmosphere is immersive, and the soundtrack compliments it greatly+ Lore is actually intriguing and immersive+ Taking a screenshot (or going into the photo mode) in the game is very easy since pausing the game freezes it instantly+/- The game is mainly made by one developer. Kudos to him for such a feat+/- Difficulties actually make a difference, instead of just making things have more HP and damage. Enemies are more accurate and friendly fire is more deadly, for example+/- Most if not all quests are repeatable (unless it's the last quest of the current chapter, apparently)+/- Voice acting could have been better. The variation isn't that great but it's passable+/- You can't remove some mutations yourself if they are at or higher than a certain quality, but you can buy another bird and repurchase your previous bird to reset them+/- There is flight stick support if you are one of the 7 people who happen to both have one of those fancy things AND bought this game at the same time+/- Time-attack racecourses are sort of meh. I never liked time-restricted content in games, but this one isn't bad enough for me to count as a negative+/- The game might not be motion-sickness friendly. Personally, I had no issues+/- Controls are responsive but take a little getting used to (I played with a controller)+/- It's fairly repetitive, but I found it calming in general apart from some combat encounters (mainly the ones that absolutely kicked my ass)- There is no achievement for getting all other achievements (I'm one of the 10 people who care about achievements like those)- Lack of numerical statistics, like amount of HP, Energy, Ammo, Currency (in the HUD), current EXP, EXP gained from quests (or maybe enemies?), damage dealt/taken, Mutagen bonuses, distance to current waypoint in meters or kilometers (or distance to ANYHWERE, really), current stats and other minor Quality of Life things like not being able to change the order of equipped gear. You also can't see how many splinters (currency) you lose upon death, or how many splinters the enemies drop. TL;DR: General vagueness- You can't gauge the power of an enemy (or rather, how weak you are) until the moment one of their shots hit you- Selecting a character and a mount could have been more streamlined by letting us see the entire selection in grid or list form- Spotting certain carryable objects in the water is sometimes borderline impossible. Mines have lights, but other things like "money boxes" that some pirate ships drop can be easily missed- Your mount sways in a circle if you let go of the movement. There is no way to disable this as far as I know, and it really sucks that I can't enjoy the scenery while flying in a straight line without having to press anything. Would have been a nice way to pass the downtime between quests- The world is mostly empty. While understandable (since the entire thing is like 97% ocean), it still is a big negative- Collision and physics are sometimes inconsistent- Voiceovers play every damn time (noticable when talking to NPCs in towns or when selecting a chapter)- The text that is narrated when you land on Shrines don't scroll fast enough to follow the narration- You drop whatever item you are holding like a rock when you deliver it for a quest (it would have been better even if it just despawned) Dev's own post that explains Hardcore difficulty. No wonder I was losing so much currency when trying to do that one pyramid quest. In case you didn't find some of the locations, this will helpMSI GTX 1060 6 GB Gaming XAMD Ryzen 5 2600X at 4.00 GHz16 GB DDR4 RAM at 2933 MHzGame runs flawlessly at 144 FPS. No issues whatsoever. I used a controller to play.-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------You won't have a good start if you neglect mutations and go for weapons. Just up your Agility and Speed a little to kickstart your adventure. You can thank me later.The wiki lists numerical values of many things, like mutagens. Why are these not in the game to begin with?I think customizable difficulty would have been more fit for this game. Like, I want the enemies to be tough, but I find getting ammo tedious (even though it's usually on my path anyway) so being able to enable/disable specific things would be nice.For some unknown reason, "The Falconeer: Warrior Edition" isn't available in my country. Steam redirects to the main page despite me seeing (and owning) the game and all DLC. Strange, really. Tested with a VPN, and it does show up, so it has to be a region issue.

_childDocuments_.review: So far I am enjoying my time. _childDocuments_.review: I decided to recommend it BUT...What can I say about this game?The graphics are good, the music is relaxing and overall pretty good, the story is also quite interesting if you can get into it which I think won't be the case for everybody. The world is intriguing and you do want to know more though.Now, the game is said to be designed with controller in mind but I really hated playing with a controller !!!!!!!-I think the game works a lot better with the mouse as flight control as it is easier to target enemies during those eratic flights.-There's camera control but honnestly, I never used it, except if you want to try photo mode which is there for people who like that sort of thing. Other than that, do not care about camera control and leave it as "default" behind your mount.-It's too bad the devs were not able to create a correct control schemes... Also, when the flight controls are set to the mouse, you cannot invert them for some reason which is really stupid and frustrating.-Overall controls are bad but you do eventually get used to them.Control problems aside, the game is a fun dog fight style game.-You do various mission, get money and upgrade your mount (falcon, dragon, pteranodon or phoenix)-Upgrades consist of new guns, ammo cannisters (you need to charge them in the storm clouds), and some kind of runes giving you passive perks. (there are also various "pass" to buy to get access to some cities and better loot)+chemical boost which "mutate" your bird to be more effective (it will become a bit scary though once fully drugged)-A good thing is that when you complete a chapter, the next mount / pilot you chose is going to keep your money and your upgrades (gun, ammo cannisters, pass and runes) but you'll have to buy chemical boost once again.You also keep your map unveiled with all locations and shrines for fast travel.-Each chapter is 10 missions and there are 4 chapters (add another one if you take the DLC)-You will finish the game in between 10 and 15 hours I believe, more if you want to do all side quest, many quest are repeatable too.-There is some replayability as the game is an open world with various missions in each major cities giving you access to new mounts, credits or pass for doing business with other places. I highly advie to try to find most shrines as soon as possible as they unlock those cool runes (there are 14 shrines, one only unlocks during the mission 8 in chapter 3, 2 other shrines only unlock during chapter 4, mission 4 and 5... so you can find 11 shrines by flying on the open world at the begining while knowing that one of these 11 shrine is pretty well hidden, but I found that area pretty cool, if you can't find it, one of the main mission gives you a hint where it is)Okay, really, that's it ! It's pretty fun and there are some amazing locations.... BUT !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!-You can replenish your life by diving into the water, catching a fish in certain spot and eating it...HOWEVER they made those fishing spots so small that 1. they're hard to see2. getting a fish from it often requires you to start over 2 or 3 times-You can't change the targetting reticle color making it quite hard to see in the mess of enemies, not knowing exactly where you fire but luckily, most of your weapons are gimballed.-Travelling accross the map is VERY slow but luckily, the game has some kind of fast travel system you can access from the map or it's automatically asked during missions.-Your bird has a stamina gauge allowing it to fly faster (some kind of "run" button) but this stamina depletes waaaaaaaay too fast. To replenish stamina, you need to "dive" while flying, then go up, dive, ... making your flight looks like a roller coaster. IT'S NOT FUN !!!!!!!-Your mount is very fragile... it's annoying, your death are often stupid or you lose life and you're not sure why or where the damage is coming from.-Whily flying faster, you can go left or right for you bird to do a barrel roll... The problem is, since rolling is not assigned to a key, you often roll while you do not want it... and when you want to do it, you can't do it -_-Why can't we map roll left - roll right? Would have been so much better.Detailed controls would have fixed so many issues the game have.-You can go up faster and gain energy by flying into ascendant air currents which look like small tornadoes but they're not easy to see.-To fly faster, you can also take horizontal air currents which are high up in the sky but they're waaaaaaaaay too high and reaching them quickly gets boring + those currents rarely go in the direction you want to go.-Tutorial is not that great.-You can dive to take a mine and throw it on enemies but this system is rather clunky.-You can target sub-systems but it's useless.-No map button, to see the map you need to press "Esc" to get in the menu then select the world map option-Upon dying you lose quite a lot of money, doesn't happen much but still, for a game that is supposed to be relaxing.-At first, if you fly in a storm to recharge your ammo, there's a chance your cannister overload and breaks forcing you buy a new one (or you can dive in the water to try to avoid overheating but it's not that effective, more effective, to fire randomly to empty your cannister so it doesn't get full) BUT luckily, there is a rune preventing this overheat... This is the first thing you should try to aquire before starting the campaign as this is the best item.... but you'll need to fly around quite a bit.-There are temporary runes which gives you some pretty cool boost but they disappear once you land in a city it seems... this makes them totally useless as during a mission, you cannot land in a city (unless specified) or the mission will be considered failed. I have trouble understanding what are their exact purpose since you need to land somewhere to get the rune, fly away, land to take a mission (goodbye rune) AND you cannot go back to the rune place to get new ones as the game doesn't want you to.TLDR: Well, there are a bunch of frustrating things to mention, you can certainly get used to them and still enjoy the game but it's still frustrating nonetheless.It's not a bad game it's enjoyable but it's not developped anymore while it lacks of quality of life which probably made people quit rather than trying to go further in the story.Original price is pretty high for this title, recommend taking it while on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: ngl it feels like a lot is still unpolished (as most people have already said. solo game dev. massive props), but if you're willing to put in a bit of work to figure out your controls and experiment with your approach to gameplay then this game has a lot to offer.I tried using mouse and keyboard initially for precision aiming, and maybe I just didn't put in enough effort to properly customize the control setup, but it was pretty unusable for me. that being said, the auto-aim is pretty generous so controller aiming shouldn't be a problem once you get familiar with aerial combat. sure, I could complain about what everyone else has already complained about: the relatively empty space between point a and point b when doing quests (though playing as a pirate actually mitigates this massively. raiding ships is so fun), or the slightly janky physics (I keep getting caught on the stupid mine balloon ropes and once I clipped partway through the water and had to restart the misison), and the balance between damage and health is definitely a little funky (I passed the dps threshold and now instead of getting one-shot I usually am doing the one-shotting)but I love the old simple art style, I love the classic combat mechanics, I love the ability to customize your loadout and even your mount, and I love the way the story slowly reveals the lore and worldbuild. I'm still only on chapter 3 (4 if you count turning pirate and then earning amnesty) and I love it. It took a little bit of time to really settle into vibing with the game, but it's genuinely a ton of fun and worth the purchase.~well I finally I finished it. a very fun 12 hours. the lore at the beginning felt a bit over the top but as the story got revealed it was honestly pretty engaging to follow. realizing that the shrine tales actually meant something instead of just being vague myth was the moment I got sucked in. once again, a lot of little things could have been polished up (a few typos, pronunciation of words from the voice actors, scene transitions and music cuts, etc.) but honestly overall a very fun experience and I'm definitely gonna play through this again and go for all the achievements and explore any npcs and quests I didn't do on my first playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not going to lie - it took me a couple of hours to start enjoying this game. It felt really hard to maneuver the falcon at first, and aiming was really hard to get the hang of. If you bump into anything, no matter how small it is, it bounces you back at awkward angles and it can be hard to recover from that. If you're in the middle of a couple of obstacles then you ping pong around for a while. This becomes an annoying issue during the time trials that you need to finish to unlock new falcons.However, once I switched to a better falcon, the game got significantly more enjoyable. I started having a lot of fun in the battles, and found myself clearing them much more easily. I also finally figured out how the aiming and targeting system worked, so the whole game was much easier to play. The world is beautiful, and the story is interesting enough. Flying around and clearing enemies was my favorite part of it all.Speaking on battles - they feel incredibly well polished. The ally AIs are able to take down enemies on their own, the enemy AIs are challenging enough to fight, and there's some good variation in the types of enemies you see every battle. Like I said, once I upgraded my falcon and got a hang of the aiming system, I started having a lot of fun with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The Falconeer is a really fun and interesting game. The combat has just enough nuance to remain fun through out the games lifespan, the story gets you involved in the world building very quickly and wraps you, and exploring the rolling tides on the back of a dragon doesn't get old.The Locations and world are a beautiful spectacle of cramped functionality and regal design, all covered in variety. whether it is the tiered city of west gate, the winding roads and lofty heights of the imperial seat, or the thin-stretched dunkle.The game, for a single dev to have created, is a work of wonder. However, the game suffers in those three aspects i mentioned before rather a lot:- The combat is fun, but it is easy to game via exploits and a poorly planned economy. There is a huge difference between early game gear and late game stuff, but the price isn't reflective of it, nor is there a gap in when you can buy that very powerful endgame gear. It is only limited in the challenges you complete, the locations discovered, and how many splinters- the worlds currency- you are willing to easily exploit how the quests reward to obtain.- The quests and such are rather fun, despite following similar structures for the most part. fly to a place, shoot something and someone, repeat, fast travel home. Where the nuance comes from is the context for the shooty bits, that while interesting, the story as a whole needed a second draft, as it is confusing in some areas, and contradictory to itself in others. Quests also never stop giving you splinters, no matter how many times you complete them, and it becomes clear very quickly that the proportion to how difficult the challenge is doesn't equate to higher rewards or unique items.-The world of the Ursee is the best part of the game, whether it is the traders moving across the seas that you can be subcontracted to assist, the very real ability to become a pirate hunter or a hunted pirate, or the surreal worldbuilding and locations. However, it is marred by an easily available and janky fast travel option to get around a world you cant be a true part of, only do the quests for. Who are the heads of the great houses? Who are the great houses? Who is the empress? why do they follow the imperium? What are their opinions and stances of the brewing wars? who leads the mancer order? What are the arbiters doing in the conflict to help bring it to a peaceful resolution? The game doesn't have answers, only the next quest.These issues if in isolation wouldn't be condemning, but like a Gordian knot, they are tied together. The importuned quest rewards on quests that don't stop giving rewards, the ease of fast travel, and the unblocked and unbalanced economy all come hand in hand, and allowed me to remove all challenge within one hour of playtime in the first chapter without ever touching the main quest.In conclusion; The Falconeer is far from great, but for a solo dev, is a damn good release, and is worth the 15.99 it is currently going for. Easily a 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to know how it probably is to learn to fly and how bad ass it is to master, buy this game.Fun title in a beautiful world that feels alive and lived in. Give yourself about 1.5 hours to really get the hang of flying and then start crushing everything. I can't say enough how the flight really feels right. Once you upgrade a few times you will have to crank the difficulty to hard to keep the game play interesting, but even then it's not bad.I tried a controller, but sucked at it and once I turned my mouse sensitivity down KBM was great. VR mode would be awesome for this title.I haven't beaten it yet so unsure total time to complete. Buy it on a sale, but even at full price you will get your money's worth.Goods- Gorgeous world - Awesome flight physics and feel- Fun aerial combat at harder levels- Lots of different mounts and upgrades to go throughBads- Open world is a bit sparse - Only a few enemy types with different skins- First hour may be frustrating get your bird not to crash into everything
_childDocuments_.name: The Falconeer

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot of promise in this game but I sadly don't think it's realized; traversal, combat, and narrative are lacking.The Ursee is a vast ocean with small islands dotted throughout, meaning there's a lot of travel. This is an issue on two fronts: the open world, and the missions. There's a stamina system that acts as expected with the player losing more as you ascend and gaining more as you descend, but there's very little you can do to accelerate traversal. There are small updrafts on the ocean surface and longer air-streams high in the sky but neither of these are fun to engage with. The air-streams are far above the stamina limit any of my mounts had, which made them more of a nuisance to use. There are fish to catch for health or stamina, but I was rarely able to successfully catch a fish. There's a vast ocean that is constantly asking the player to run back and forth but doesn't offer any interesting way to engage with it. Something that would boost acceleration that could reward high skill would be great, but it isn't present here, so while it may be scenic, it easily became dull. There are a few band-aid fixes applied to travel which are convenient, like a teleport to home button and a fast travel to the next quest marker button, but it doesn't make travel any more engaging. On top of this, about a third of the missions in this game are escort quests that have ships much slower than the player character, which is just frustrating. Slipstreaming could be a fun way to boost the speed of escort quests while still being engaging.There's a lot of discussion surrounding the controls, but after acclimating myself with the controls on mouse and keyboard, I had no issues. There are a lot of different ways to play the game that it shouldn't be a concern. The larger issue is how repetitive combat is. There are a few key scenes that are exciting, but they are far and few between. Most of the time, you'll deal with enemy falconeers and ships/air-ships, rinse and repeat. They don't offer any unique challenge as they all are over the open ocean, and they all play out relatively the same. Pyro pots are very strong and quickly destroyed any large enemy with ease. The few larger encounters at the end of each chapter are probably the game at its best, but there's also 9 fetch or escort quests you must do beforehand.I actually don't think the narrative is bad, but it's not personable per se. The narrative is almost more about the lore of the world than it is about characters in particular which made it hard for me to connect to. There's some interesting ideas involving the Maw and Oberon, but jumping between factions left me unconnected to one particular group. I think the largest faults concern House Dunkle and the Empress. House Dunkle is introduced in the first Chapter, goes on for too long, and serves very little purpose overall and has no representation in the rest of the game, which is confusing. The Empress of the Imperium is just not present in the game? This is even more puzzling when  I think the worldbuilding is cool but I don't think there's any characters I ever felt attached to.Up to this point, this review has been very critical but there are a few redeeming factors. The visuals, music, and sound design are great! The fact that this game has no textures is an insane feat and I think the overall presentation is great. I'm sure this game is better on a flight stick and is crazy with VR. There have been consistent updates that make the game better and there's a lot of respect I have for solo developers like Tomas Sala.Not as much as I hoped, sadly. The core gameplay and mission design is limited. Perhaps I could look past it if the narrative really hooked me, but I could never connect with any characters. Perhaps The Falconeer will resonate better with others, but I can't say I would recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Falconeer

_childDocuments_.review: The game doesn't allow you to save and load, which is a dealbraker for me.Accidently hit a friendly? Well, you're a pirate now, bye bye story, better start all over again if you want to continue... Otherwise the game is pretty funEDIT: Apparently there is a way to go back to the storyline if you became a pirate. The game does save and load, but you can't save at will. The game will autosave (and overwrite previous saves) when you land. So no savescumming (which I like to do).
_childDocuments_.name: The Falconeer

_childDocuments_.review: I am jaded as ♥♥♥♥ and never actually review games but this game really caught me off guard.I haven't gotten far enough into the game to really give true observations but immediate first impressions are that the world building is done very well and the core gameplay loop is actually fun.I am getting strong Sea of Thieves vibes from the world but am looking forward to proper progression and lore. The flight mechanics are quite forgiving given the nature of birds and being able to just stop and turn around, the upgrades and weapon variety displayed immediately also inspire confidence that this game is worth sinking some time into. If you have any interest in a Sea of Thieves styled world but instead with aerial dogfighting on birds, get this without hesitation.
_childDocuments_.name: The Falconeer

_childDocuments_.review: The Falconeer is a game developed by Tomas Sala and published by Wired ProductionsThe game offers some nice graphics and a nice aesthetic, although some ugly glitches here and there, it is pleasant all the sameThe game does suffer with some repetitiveness at certain areas of the game but a fun game nonethelessThe Falconeer overall, however, is a fun game to play, yet sometimes repetitive and it does get boring if being played for a long time, but is a really good story-rich exploration adventure game to play in short bursts!
_childDocuments_.name: The Falconeer

_childDocuments_.review: I've rather enjoyed this game thus far. It's a gentle and soothing sandbox game that has helped me relax with it's soothing music, atmosphere, and fluid feeling of flight. The combat can be quite difficult if you take on a challenge before you're ready, but it is not so overly complex and does not demand unfathomable skill to get through.Falconeer has an openworld where you can freely roam on a large bird over the oceans, or take on specific challenges and goals, and is not very confusing with direction. The story is easy to follow with brief to the point dialogue and quests that do not flood you with the urge to hit the skip button, or make you wish things would just get on with it. I did run into a difficulty spike, but that was a result of me just flowing through the story without even realizing it, and had neglected to explore and purchase upgrades (silly me).Overally, I am really happy with the layout of the game, and the flight model deserves quite a lot of praise. I use controller as is highly recommended for this game (you may have difficulties with K&B as I hear, but I have not tried that), and the flight feels so natural and fluid I really feel like I'm flying atop a large beautiful feathered creature, or am just the bird, since the character is pretty small in comparison :)If you're in the market for soaring above the ocean, and engaging in some aerial combat in a natural manner that differs from metal and wirring, this might be a game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Falconeer

_childDocuments_.review: Fun for around 10 hours, before the gameplayloop becomes too repetitive and boring. Impressive work for one person, but I wouldn't recommand getting it for the full price.EDIT: Wow, now I will recommend the game, if the dev is so not-salty about a negative review! If you look for a fantasy air-combat game, I advise everyone to look at "Century-Age of Ashes"- it's free and the combat system is smooth like baby skin.
_childDocuments_.name: The Falconeer

_childDocuments_.review: I loved everything about this game! The visuals, the game play, the lore, the story, and the fighting all amazing! My only wish was that there was more to do, more to see, more to upgrade, and more ways to play. If this game was made on only a quarter of the scale as say skyrim I could log hundreds and hundreds of hours in this game. But where it is at now, only about 26 hours can be played before literally everything has been done. 10/10!
_childDocuments_.name: The Falconeer

_childDocuments_.review: The controls are easy to learn and the game gives players new to flight games enough time to get used to the dynamic of this genre. More experienced players can start out in Hardcore mode (even tho it really gets difficult at some point). The soundtrack fits the game and the world well and the story is quite interesting in my opinion. There are different classes with different playstiles and you can also customize your weaponry and ammo, as well as upgrade your bird with some chemistry injections (PETA does not approve). Overall a nice game to chill and to explore the world of Ursee!
_childDocuments_.name: The Falconeer

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot believe this was a one dev production. I jus bought it and thought i would check the flight system and graphics and omg it is astounding how one person managed to do all this. I though the history would be text but there is VA and i hold no assessment to their abilities. the flying takes a nit used too i thought i kilted my falcon when i dove into the water but phew! its takes a bit of time to get accustomed to it and i know this game is gonna be worth the time investment
_childDocuments_.name: The Falconeer

_childDocuments_.review: It's an open world arcade-y flying game - remember the old Xbox game Crimson Skies? Well, this an open-world steampunk version; with giant falcons armed with cannons and lightning guns flying between islands on a vast (somewhat empty) ocean world. +Nice graphics/art+Good worldbuilding- Controller required- Rather empty/barebones (see: most reviews 10 hours or less)Recommended? Only on a 50% off sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Falconeer

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked how the main plot is presented. The smaller quests are so-so in terms of presentation, but I do enjoy the world. The controller auto-aim being generous is appreciated. There were a few controls I missed somehow during the tutorial such as switching targets, but as soon as I figured out it was X I felt a lot better. So far this is an solid B experience just 60 minutes in. Hopefully things pick up a little bit later on.
_childDocuments_.name: The Falconeer

_childDocuments_.review: I love the simplistic and smooth graphics of this game! It makes for a really nice aesthetic and can provide a lot of beautiful moments mid flight. For example, the bird you can purchase at Dunkle has a beautiful yellow hue in certain lighting! Truly a beautiful game, I've never gotten bored of the endless ocean because of this.Each "village/city/town" in the game is small and can often feel repetitive. The main area for the Mancer Falconeer really spiced it up though, and felt like an interesting landmark because of its uniqueness. Despite this, I still enjoy flying around aimlessly and exploring all these different homes, and there are more that have a certain niche to them too, such as Witchrock. When I first saw it I loved it because I felt like the visual of the area matched its name. Areas like shrines are wonderful, however, and really bring diversity. The Maw is a wonderful and intriguing addition to the game, I haven't looked into the lore much, but The Maw really piques my interest!The keyboard and mouse controls can be difficult to get used to, considering it isn't yet fully optimised, however as I progressed in the game I got more used to them and I personally don't have that much of an issue with them. It's just a steep learning curve if you don't have a controller or flight stick, which I presume to be easier to control, however I have neither of these so I wouldn't really know. The only issue I have with the keyboard and mouse controls (once you understand how to move your falcon and your camera without circling all over the place) is how the camera will sometimes move suddenly when you try to aim at a target. I've had it happen many times and it's quite annoying as it puts off my accuracy.As for combat and what you can do as certain factions, I'm enjoying fighting all the different enemies and what they bring with them, like the weavers and each faction brings a different type of "wingman" which I really like. The only issue I have in terms of this is that there could be more different types of enemies to bring variety and diversity to the game and the "pirate" faction could be expanded on more, maybe as an alternative storyline if you take up the faction willingly like you normally do, which could potentially change depending on what chapter you do this. However, I know that is a lot to ask for, but just some more interesting expansion on the Pirate faction would be enough for me!Overall, a beautiful game with addicting fights but with decent keyboard+mouse support at the moment. Definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Falconeer

_childDocuments_.review: I am not a huge "flying games with dog fights" kind of guy but I must say this was really fun.Firstly, the amount of lore and voice acting is overwhelming, the accents are funny/have a lot of character.If you want to delve into this strange world of magic and giant eagles you can totally get immersed in it.However, the tutorial and basics of fighting in a flying based game is *barely* taught to the player during the tutorial. Since you have a ton of AI team mates on the tutorial level you can mostly completely suck at the actual fights, and finish the tutorial then thrust into a world with quite challenging opponents. None of the upgrade system is tutorialised and I had no idea I could buy a slow firing but very strong (my style of playing since I can barely land any hits) until I'd failed the first couple of missions.I had a lot of fun with my time in the game the main missions are crafted and there are several chapters/world maps to go through allowing for many different scenarios.Recommended for people wanting a challenge (if you dont normally play flying games) or for people familiar with flying based games who want a more magical lore than the typical "planes go bang bang" world war or "wow im in space!" style flying shooters.
_childDocuments_.name: The Falconeer

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been a pleasant surprise if i'm honest. I wanted to experience the 'next gen' but sadly was unable to secure a console so its been great being able to experience that on hardware i already have. It runs stable at either 60 or 120 fps and the controls work great with an xbox controller.  Graphically it looks fantastic especially during the stormy weather or when the sun is reflecting and credit where its due, i can really dig the art style. (special mention, the photo mode which normally i tend to pass on, looks great as it enables you to change the lightning to get some really nice quality looking stills) i also like the fact you can shoot through the pirates sails and not only does it create a hole, it also give a surrounding burn. sadly there are parts that have frustrated me so far and that is mainly with the moveability. Mostly, its great however i personally hate the fact i cant roll and change direction backwards. its frustrating fighting others and they fly past you and you have to turn instead of flipping round. On a positive note, you can barrel roll!What also has annoyed me and this is tedious, the bird doesn't seem to flap its wings when casually flying around unless its carrying something. I want to be reminded i'm riding a bird not a plane.Ultimately, the game is great. the story (although seemed tedious at first) is shaping up to be an interesting one and i genuinely am looking forward to putting more time into it over the next few days/weeks.I rate the game 7.5/10. Its worth a buy but sometimes i feel the areas can be slightly bland (although seeing pools of fish etc is cool) and although i love gaming alone, multiplayer would have been fantastic as both team death match/ challenges / races and a co-op mode would also be welcome.I also cant help but feel it would be a great addition to the Nintendo switch as it would be a great game to play on the go whether you only have time to complete a mission or 2 or have the time to go full free roam.
_childDocuments_.name: The Falconeer

_childDocuments_.review: The Falconeer is a game that lets you explore an epic Oceanic world called Ursee with a ton of secrets ranging from hidden treasure to some really interesting sights. The story-mode is quite fun as-well letting you do lots of different tasks from different factions and has a lot of lore behind all of them. You’ll learn as you progress and I can’t wait to keep on hearing more.The graphics are really good, I have a pretty old PC now and it runs really smoothly with no frame drops at all, yet the game still looks amazing. I also found the gameplay really easy and quite simple, it’s dogfighting birds, the controls can be a bit sensitive sometimes but it’s a game you can just lose a lot of time in, whether you want to do the story or just free-roam.£22 is not a bad price for a game like this and I can’t believe it’s just from one developer, it has been quite a ride. Apart from a couple of hiccups here and there I really enjoyed my time with The Falconeer.
_childDocuments_.name: The Falconeer

_childDocuments_.review: I am greatly enjoying the game. I haven't ever played an aerial combat game before. I gave this game a try simply because it had giant birds and was set in an ocean world. So here are what I felt where the pro's and con's after playing several hours of the game so far. Pros:-Lovely and beautiful environment. Big open oceans, wales jumping in the waves. -Playable with a controller. Controls are smooth.-Music is fantastic!-The lore of the world is fascinating, and fun to gather over time as the story unfolds with each chapter completed. -Combat gets intense and has lots of action.-Calm, relaxing when out of combat. -Open world. You can play it how ever you want. You can just fly around just taking in the world and relax. Or you can take on a variety of different level missions for some action. Cons:-Has no check points for missions. Mainly an issue if you die on super long missions. Its a tad daunting to redo them from the beginning.Overall, I would recommend this game. Honestly, I already recommended it to two of my friends who are tired of your typical plane or space  aerial combat game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Falconeer

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying the game so far!Fights are brutal and you die really quickly if you don't play them smart. Controls can be a bit finicky at first but I found that I got used to them after a while, playing mouse and keyboard even.The developer is super responsive as well, there's a few bugs right now but I doubt they'll stick around for long.
_childDocuments_.name: The Falconeer

_childDocuments_.review: Played beta, and have played now.  If you like classic old-school shooters, this is the game for you.  First point you need to know - the first chapter is good, but things really kick off in the second chapter.  Fedex quests don't progress the story - if it's not voiced, you can safely skip it unless you need to get more resources, or happen to be going in that direction.  And the dev is committed to improving, listening to feedback and ramping out fixes and patches, so if you've got an issue, drop onto the discord and raise it - I can guarantee you'll get a listening ear from the (sole dev) guy who wrote this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Falconeer

_childDocuments_.review: Was fortunate enough to win a free key from the launch day stream give-aways.Only played a few hours and not enough to make a full review but initial impressions are good enough to keep playing.Mouse and keyboard took a little bit of managing to get set up for comfort but after dropping the sensitivity and adding profile to the mouse it's all good now and is reminiscent of older dogfight games of coasting along in the ether with the occasional moments of insanity when engaging multiple enemy.
_childDocuments_.name: The Falconeer

_childDocuments_.review: WAIT!!! BEFORE SKIPPING MY REVIEW!!! (HAS BEEN EDITED)Please read. Originally I gave this game a thumbs down. However, due to the very quick and amazing effort from the singular developer in improving this game and fixing the number 1 issue with it. I am now giving it a thumbs up. It is NOT perfect. But it is a really nice little game.In all honestly this game has a lot going for it at an affordable price. It doesn't miss many beats in the development department. It just has a few minor negatives and then for me personally a really big negative which they have since release fixed so...yeah...So please read in case you missed some important info in your other reviews or the steam page.The view in the game isn't all that magical and great like I thought it would be. It's mostly bland, boring environments that you're flying around in. And the overall plot-line and direction is lacking. But besides those two minor inconveniences and with the mouse controls more or less fixed, I think its actually a decent little game.If you want more info with some real gameplay then check out the video on my youtube channel (link below). Thanks for reading!
_childDocuments_.name: The Falconeer

_childDocuments_.review: Generations of poisonous decisions and treason swirl in the deep, as factions collide. Become the Falconeer and soar through the skies aboard a devastatingly powerful Warbird. Uncover secrets lost to the sea as you join or oppose different factions and clans scattered throughout The Great Ursee. Take advantage of multiple Falconeer classes with individual stats, weapons and warbirds that can be upgraded through winning battles, completing quests, discovering secrets, or applying Mutagens or Chants. Use ocean thermals and energy to dive, dodge, barrel-roll, and twist to gain an advantage. The Falconeer is an open-world air combat game, featuring fast, brutal aerial dogfights and deep exploration of an incredible fantasy open-world set not only above the clouds, but also amongst the waves and down through the sunken, ocean depths.
_childDocuments_.name: The Falconeer

name: King's Bounty II
detailed_description: LORD'S EDITION LORD'S EDITION NOW INCLUDES: Rod of Deception (weapon) Frosthammer (weapon) Staff of Harmony (weapon) Tyrant's Sword (weapon) Armor of the Hollow (armor set) Heroes & Villains Premium Pack (skin pack) King‘s Watchdogs DUKE'S EDITION DUKE'S EDITION INCLUDES: Rod of Deception (weapon) Frosthammer (weapon) Staff of Harmony (weapon) Tyrant's Sword (weapon) Armor of the Hollow (armor set) Heroes & Villains Premium Pack (skin pack) King‘s Watchdogs Digital Artbook Digital Soundtrack About the Game Darkness descends over the world of Nostria. Conspiracies, sabotage, and necromancy are overshadowing the country. But maybe a saviour – the kingdom's last hope – is already here, to fight back and finally restore peace and order in Nostria! King’s Bounty II is the long-awaited sequel to the legendary King’s Bounty video games franchise, one of the most iconic representatives of the turn-based RPG genre. Expanding on this legacy with an entirely new epic story, factions, enemies, and new features to forge an open and breaking fantasy world Antara. With the kingdoms in disarray, counties demanding independence, bandits prowl the roads, all the overseas nations have denied the King’s authority over them, and blighted creatures lie in wait for the unwary, new accidental heroes emerge as a last hope. They are determined to bring order to the chaos. Play as one of them, recruiting, developing, and commanding your personal army on a non-linear adventure of betrayal, sacrifice, and survival. Fighting for your own future, outsmarting enemy in uniquely turn-based combat, making difficult decisions, and experience the intensity of one of the classic sagas in an exciting new way. IMMERSIVE AND CHARACTER-DRIVEN EPIC STORY Play as one of three main heroes, rescuing and building your personal army in a journey of leadership, survival, and sacrifice. Every decision you make has profound and lasting consequences. UNIQUE MASSIVE WORLD TO DISCOVER The world of Antara is wide open and ripe for exploration. Unearth hidden places and dangerous enemies — Antara is a vast home to a thousand wonders and secrets for players to discover. CUSTOMIZABLE SQUAD AND EQUIPMENT Each army squad has its own set of skills and visual appearance. Build armies of different creatures who will fight with you throughout the majority of your adventure. TACTICAL DEPTH ON THE BATTLEFIELD The environment and landscape matter in King’s Bounty II. Players will encounter diverse terrain types, directly impacting battlefield tactics. Every battle is unique in its own way.
