_childDocuments_.review: I never played any of Kings' Bounty games before, and i do not draw any comparisons here. For what it is, i would fully recommend the game. I did not notice any of the complaints there were regarding the release version. Traveling pace is feels exactly right. The backtracking does not feel tedious. The world is beautiful, the quest stories are credible and engaging. The encounters are not frustrating (i played on easy). For people who like exploring the game has enough to offer.  If you like Questing and Heroes of Might an Magic - get this gem on sale. Solid double A title, worth every adventurer's collection.
_childDocuments_.name: King's Bounty II

_childDocuments_.review: What do they do to my game ?I was waiting for this game but maybe I had too big expectation ? After 150h I’m sitting and crying. You are walking more than playing. I’ve finished the game as Warrior and Mage. 75 h each but half of this you are just walking. Hero is moving like a snail. I’m losing so much time on moving even after last hotfix. What can I say … not sure if this game can be fix. If you want to play in Kings bounty better install some older game.
_childDocuments_.name: King's Bounty II

_childDocuments_.review: It baffles me how they could take 3 steps back with this sequel. The previous King's bounty games are way better. I don't understand the decision to go 3D when it makes the game worse.. Especially when the game is like 80% running back and forth between errand quests very slowly. That being said, the game is still fun. Combat is fun, the skill tree is interesting, and the spells/units/combat is fun. I enjoyed the game playing through it, but have no desire to do it again. So even if this game is like 40% as fun as the previous King's bounty games, that is 40% of some of the best games I ever played, at least worth a playthrough if nothing else.. Please do a better job in King's bounty 3 -_-
_childDocuments_.name: King's Bounty II

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing game, too bad development stopped and players didn't appreciate it.It's very beautiful, thought out, there's a wonderful story, dialogues, animations, music, a lot of attention to details, it's something to behold.The only two bad things about it are: UI - it's terribly inconvenient and roaming on the map. There's no need for the horse, it's 100% redundant, map traversal just should be twice as fast. I've encountered a single side mission so far which necessitates the horse (you need to catch a wolf).If you're a fan of Heroes of Might and Magic or King's Bounty, that's the game to play.Various junk loot makes zero sense - you need to sell it. Why not just give the player gold?---I first said, "Sadly it's impossible to complete the game at the hard difficulty level without losses. It's possible at the beginning, then after completing a few missions (roughly 12 hours of play time), enemies become insane and simply destroy you. That's my biggest concern and bummer".Looks like it was because either I played suboptimally or playing using a mage this way is not possible. There are walk throughs published on youtube where people complete the game at hard difficulty without losses using a paladin and warrior.I'll restart the game to try to complete it without losses. Darn, 40 hours lost.
_childDocuments_.name: King's Bounty II

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played the other old version but I feel the negative reviews may put people off what is a good game lots of choices questing mix and mash different unit types and you don't feel locked in the main characters class if you want a warrior wizard go for it if want wizard who can only use scroll magic but has super powerful army nothing stopping you.  I like how a lot battles reflect the map its self and choices do matter Only things i would is negative game feels a little short and looks clearly like DLC will be added where game has dead ends guards barring a gate to another zone etc some paths are slightly harder at start game due forcing a order army on you earlier game and focusing magic tree makes some battles a lot harder than they should be and mana resource is to little charging to learn spell in book is way to high, Line sight needs a rework tends favour meele more, Being able cast spell first seems make massive difference
_childDocuments_.name: King's Bounty II

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot of backlash about this being too different, but as a big fan of the series who owns and has played every single KB game, this feels to me like an authentic Kings Bounty experience so far. The game world, skills, units, combat, questing... all feels familiar. The main difference is the perspective, and I personally like the switch to 3rd person.I also like that there is more exploration and less combat. My only beef with the other KB games is sometimes it feels like you just rip through one combat after another after another until you've cleared enough space to explore and get treasure. There's still plenty of combat in this game but less for sure, and I like being able to explore, find loot and take my time with it.I also hear people say it's linear... like what? Did you make it past the intro section before you reviewed this game? In my quest log right now I have 2 story quests and like 12 side quests. 90% of my gameplay so far has been roaming about doing side quests.The controls and UI... okay you got them there. Much could be improved in that regard. It was frustrating at first but I just kind of got used to it. Haven't encountered any bugs yet in my 6 hours but check out the horses front legs if you want a laugh.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game more of nostalgia of the first King's Bounty series hopping that maybe I could relieve some of the experiences I had as a child. Unfortunately this game way to different and not as story driven.What I did like:-> The combat system feels more refined and I do like that they have added 3D elements like hills-> The 3D map is welcomed even if it feels quite old-> There is more balance between the classes What I did not like:-> The dialog compared to the original series are quite simple without that much lore as I used to have-> The new mana system is not explain I do understand that is used to balance but we need to be aware of it or we might be in a deadlock-> The morality system is quite poor, there are 4 routes for morality that should represent each class but there are only 3 classes, would have been cool that all there will have been representatives for each class-> Factions like elves, pirates, nagas, demons, underground and so on are missing-> Fewer troops-> fewer interesting items

_childDocuments_.review: 7 out of 10.  I sort of recommend this game.  Overall enjoyed the game however there are little aspect that detracted from the overall enjoyment.On the positive I felt the character development, story line, and quyality were good. _childDocuments_.review: Seems decent so far.The environments looks nice and it can look charming at times but voice acting, lip syncing, animations and all those little details that help sell the presentation is clearly a step down compared to what triple A games have.So far i have found the gameplay quite charming and i like the mix with exploring, doing quests, and combat encounters. The story hasn't been great though and i haven't gotten far enough to determine if the combat will hold up yet. So far it is decent and i like that they have spread out the encounters quite a bit and don't overdo it by throwing tons of combat encounters on you.So far i am cautiously optimistic that this will be a decent budget roleplaying game, i will update this review as i get further into the game. _childDocuments_.review: I played all former Kings Bounty games a LOT. The music and the arrival at new islands was fantastic, and the feeling of slipping past some unbeatable enemy to get that vital stat increase or a little extra coin was amazing. The Boss fights were really good, forcing you to mix up your playing style and perhaps focus on specific units to counter whatever the Boss threw at you.Kings Bounty 2 had the same dilemma as so many other games: "Do we keep making more of the same or try and renew everything with better graphics, real dialogue etc".Unfortunately the chose the later which resulted in a fairly small world where graphics and strory was at the center, and army building and exploration was somewhat second place. The great music from the previous games have been completely neglected.The skill system is great and the troops that are rewarded and also level up is a great idea together with the fact that you often have 2 choices in how you want to complete a quest.But unfortutely the 3D graphics means that you often get stuck in a branch or similar because you are looking for hidden loot. The horse you can mount/dismount is one of the most clunky and annoying horses I've ever seen. You get stuck, you can't turn, you dismount on a box etc. It's very poorly made.There are no Boss Fights and a very limited amount of units, which means you use the same 10 units all game and fight against the same 10, while some are never used or never seen.Overall I enjoyed the game... ONCE, and then I went back to previous Kings Bounty games. Too many negatives with this game, it was a swing and miss unfortunately. Hopefully they will make a 3rd game with the skill/unit XP system from this one and more of the good old.
_childDocuments_.name: King's Bounty II

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting evolution of the franchise changing to third person world wondering and fully voice actws all NPC interactions. The world feels a lot more alive and real than previous entries. The trade off is it feels much smaller. The combat is still great and progression never stops til the end so if you are fan of epic turn based strategy games its hard to go wrong with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: King's Bounty II

_childDocuments_.review: I really tried to like this game as much as the first kings bounty.  I put some hours into it but it was mostly because I loved the previous games and wanted to like this one. I just couldn't finish it.  I do recommend it, but it wasn't for me. Pros:Decent quest system.  Some effort was put into some of their quests and I like how they set up their quest markers.I also like their new system with your choices on how you handle quests to effect your character building. It adds more meaning to your choices.I can also appreciate the fast travel they put in.  Once I experience going through an area for the first time and exploring every corner, I just want a fast way to come back if I need to.  They set this up nicely.Now for the bad:I hated getting on my horse.  I would run almost every time instead. Very hard to turn around and navigate. Maybe this was intentional but it was an added grief for me. Traveling on foot is not perfect either. Got stuck too many times in the environment.  I would hit the corner of something like a log or a fence and get stuck on it only to spend a few minutes trying to find the exact path needed to get back down. Very Annoying!Leadership! what did you make that dreadful change to leadership for? Capping army limits ruined some of the fun for me.  No longer can I search everywhere for the piece of armor or treasure that will give me just enough to add 1 more dragon to my army! Now it is capped..Sigh..Speaking of armies...I get some units that I like and I go into battle. I do well but lose a few soldiers and I cant replace them because the vendor only sells a few. This is the case for most of the good armies. I can guess this is done for added difficulty but all it did was add to my anger. Too many times I had to restart a battle because I lost a unit I could not replace. Re-doing every battle until I get a flawless victory was fun at first and made me want to vomit by 50 hours in. They did this some with their previous games but not nearly this bad.Just because this was not my thing i can appreciate the work they put in.  I would play any other Kings bounty before this one but If you are thinking about buying it, I would say wait for it to go on sale and give it a go.
_childDocuments_.name: King's Bounty II

_childDocuments_.review: The short: Great game if you play it as its OWN game and not expect it to be like the first game. I know it is King's Bounty 2, but they should have just given it an entirely different name and not made it part 2 of the series. It is a mashup:Exploration portion of the game is VERY similar to Dragon Age. You wander around in a gorgeous 3D world looking for shiny clickables in the hopes of getting phat loot. Combat is classic KB turn-based with army units, which is what you do expect.Verdict: Pros outweigh the cons, I would recommend it. Game is WAY overpriced, so if you can't afford it just wait for a sale. IF you are bored and can afford it, then go for it. The longer review:Story: The story is good, but it will not win any awards. Everything is voice acted, and that is really unnecessary. I see why they did that since most games today shoot for that level of storytelling, but most of the voice acting is pretty terrible. Bad animation and lip syncing detract from the actual storytelling, but not so bad it breaks your enjoyment or immersion.The three main characters are... well, hard to describe. The countess so far is my favorite, while the mercenary is second. The paladin is just terrible having watched her in another player's play through, so I have not chosen her yet. You don't get to customize any of the three, aside from armor choices which are a huge plus. If you pick up a hat, they put the hat on and wear it. Hat conforms to the hair, so there was a lot of attention to detail put into the character models. Full customization of looks, etc, is not present. I get that as the story would be harder to write for the characters if you could change their genders or backgrounds. Still, I am unclear of their past motivations, but you get to drive their present development through extensive alignment choice. Gameplay: Linear. As stated in the summary, Dragon Age seems to be the driving influence for the exploration and travel portion of the game. You won't get lost, and fast travel shrines are dotted around the map to make things a bit easier. You are given a horse, but the drawback is you can't interact with anything while mounted so you have to constantly get on and off of it. I just stopped using it altogether, unless I am travelling through a fully explored area. PLEASE FOR THE LOVE OF ALL THAT IS HOLY LET US INTERACT WITH THINGS WHILST MOUNTED.Combat is difficult. An upcoming update will add difficulty settings, so there is that to look forward to. Why this is not in launch boggles the mind. As of right now the game is just basically throw troops at the enemy and hope for the best. There is a small rock/paper/scissors system, such as archers/hunters doing more damage to beasts, or undead being vulnerable to fire, but it has not appeared to have much of an affect on the gameplay. You WILL lose units, which sucks, but there is no cap on reserves and you can heal after a battle for a pretty hefty sum. I would also like to see a difficulty measure on battles, as of right now you just save, go in, and if you die just reload and try a different part of the story. Unit customization is pretty limited, but there are a large number of units in the game. Each unit has three ranks, and they do change their appearance with each rank. I bought the lord's upgrade, but have no clue if the skins are applied since there is no toggle for turning skins on or off. The units do look good, though.They really need some sort of flanking system in the game as the battlefields are pretty restrictive and just being able to flank an enemy is difficult to do. They should also add a system to allow the player to plot a unit's path, as right now you either move to the spot you want, then attack if you still can, or just straight run to the enemy and attack from a position you don't want to be in. Controls: Game is NOT optimized for keyboard and mouse, but updates are incoming to make keybinds and such. Right now it is easy enough to get used to, but still annoying.Graphics: Rather immersive. While the world is linear, it is very well hand-crafted. It is a great looking fantasy world and does a good job of pulling you in. Units look great, animations look good and are overall pretty smooth. There are some glitches, like enemy archers not animating when they fire. If you take phantom damage just assume the enemy archers fired at you or you are the recipient of a confusion spell. Horse's front legs get pretty janky when parked on an incline, so that needs fixing.Quests and Leveling: So many damn quests... a lot. So many it seems like they intentionally slowed the leveling process to accommodate the number of quests you get. Leveling is agonizingly slow, and you rarely get notified if you did level up. Just remember to check your skill tree window to see if you have talent points to spend. Quest system does a good job of fleshing out your character. My sorceress is full finesse and anarchy, so how I solve a quest is usually played out in a way to enhance those traits. I am still a little confused as to how the overall system works as the explanation of it is pretty weak.Overall: I sat on this game for a minute, and it was mostly the price that turned me off. I pulled the trigger and I don't regret it. Like I said, this should be titled King's Bounty: "Something Something" instead of part 2. The game has really changed enough that a lot of folks do not like it, but to me it is an evolution that was inevitable when you look at the tactical RPG genre. Anyhow, have fun with it.

_childDocuments_.review: The most noticed deference from the previous kings bounty titles is the change from the traditional iso to a 3D 3rd person point of view.  Once you get over the shock of this change you realize that is also vastly inferior to all its predecessors concerning the variety of creatures , spells, choices, maps and strategic depth. For example you cannot escape from enemies during the battle, there are not treasure chests in the battle map, traveling with ships and flying horses and much much more - the catalog is endless!! But because I want to be fair there are a few new interesting concepts like traveling monoliths, heal your units after battle and ideologies. I cannot say the same for the useless trash concept - what is the point to have such a variety of objects in the game once there only purpose is to sell them for money.   Also the game has a serious optimization problem and a lot of crashes and technical bugs, for example sometimes the hero levitates, sometimes hits on a small obstacle and cannot move, traveling with your horse is a pain in the ass and much more. Especially the continuous crashes can seriously damage your game experience. As I said the game is rather simple comparing with the previous kings bounty games but at the end of the day and despite all of its drawbacks is quit enjoyable and the battles have lot of fun.So thumbs up (barely) only with a serious discount and only for fanatic players of might and magic universe. Personally  I preordered the Duke's edition because I generally want to support sequels of games that I adore but if I want to be honest at its current stage I cannot recommend it at full price. Let us hope for future patches that will correct some of the technical issues and DLCs that will add some more content in this game. The game could be much more better with a little more effort from the devs.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the previous King's Bounty games and, to be honest, I did enjoy this one; but I can't recommend this game to anyone. If you haven't played King's Bounty before, you're going to find this game clunky and unpolished (play the other ones first: The Legend, Armoured Princess etc.). If you have played King's Bounty before, you're going to find this game frustrating. The systems in this game are poorly explained, even if many of them are present in the previous King's Bounty games (albeit with different names).One thing I will say, though... the lack of polish in this game does make for some unintended comedy - like it's so bad, it's good kind of thing. Here's a list of weird stuff:* All but about 2 of the men in this game have facial hair - including men who are meant to be 'young'. At one point you offer to rescue a blacksmith's lazy apprentice, and when you eventually find him, he looks older than the smith.* The dialogue you overhear from the NPCs repeats whenever you move away and back into range of characters. I don't know how many times I've heard the phrase "We must summon my eagles". Now I say this whenever things get a bit too hard.* When you run into any of the wealthy men, they say "you rumpled my best suit". I ran into a lot of wealthy men.* You get a horse! When you whistle for it to come, it always spontaneously appears behind you .* The ending... I can't find the exact video that captures it, but .

_childDocuments_.review: Just played a bit, I think the game is alright in general, although I won't recommend buying it at full price.> Graphics at ultra setting is kind of OK. It feels like something out of 2015, definitely not next gen but graphics isn't that important for strategy game anyway.> Combat is fine, typical HOMM/KB style so not much to say. It is a bit bland at the moment and I expect it to get more interesting as more powerful units and spells become available.> The RPG aspect of game (movement, interaction, etc.) is passable. I agree that it really takes away the feel of the original KB series (or HOMM series). Since the story doesn't seem to connect with the previous titles, I am basically playing it as a completely new game rather than a sequel to KB legend. I wonder why they didn't take the opposite approach with traditional KB overland map but zoom in 3D combat, like that PS2 HOMM game (something something dragon staff or stick).> A lot of people criticize the voice acting. While I don't find it outstanding also, this is not a deal breaker for me.> Control is not well optimized. I thought KB&M was bad so I changed to controller but controller had some serious problems as well, for example at the talent menu. For some reason the selection doesn't stay at the talent you choose and always jumps back to the one in the middle. Combat is much better using KB&M and adventure is better with controller so there is always something frustrating no matter what you use.Some tips to improve the gameplay:1. Turn ON V-sync if your game is lagging/stuttering. It was almost unplayable when I started the game and lowering graphics settings did nothing, turning on V-sync fixed the problem for me.2. Install ReShade and check Levels, DPX, LumaSharpen, Tonemap and Vibrance (or others if you know what you are doing). This drastically improves the color scheme of the game (original colors were really bad) and makes it look much better.

_childDocuments_.review: Summary: Not quite as good as past games in the series, but it introduces a solid foundation for the next generation of King's Bounty games.The big change in KB II is of course the graphics.  Not only is the environment much more lush and detailed (and in higher resolution), we are given a more intimate perspective.  Like previous KB games it's still 3rd-person, but instead of being an overhead "god-cam" view, KB II has a much closer over-the-shoulder camera.  The effect is that we feel more like we're travelling around the game world ourselves, as opposed to moving around some subordinate like a pawn.In addition, the dialogue is much better (and less cringey) than previous games, and it's all fully voiced, with generally good voice acting.  As a result, outside of combat the game is more like a traditional RPG.The devs obviously put a lot of effort into this new game engine and it is definitely a big improvement.  The problem is that it comes at the expense of other aspects of the game.  In particular, combat is less interesting than previous games, which is a bit of a problem since tactical combat resolution is the heart of this whole game series.  I had considered it to be state-of-the-art in previous KB games, but honestly it's only mediocre in KB II.But I feel like the combat resolution mechanism can be tuned and improved relatively easily compared to the basic game engine.  For example, KB II lacks a "combat companion" that provides tactical flexibility like you had in previous KB games, but I'm betting they can tack one on pretty easily.  Likewise, additional/improved spell effects and combat abilities can be added piecemeal as time allows.  Assuming there is a sequel or DLC, I'm expecting they'll be adding things like that.In the mean time, the game is perfectly serviceable.  I've encountered no bugs or crashes or broken quests (which were a common problem in previous KB games), and while the combat isn't quite as fun, I think the improved game engine mostly makes up for that.  I'm looking forward to seeing what they can do with this foundation in the future...

_childDocuments_.review: It's really not as bad as many folks are making it out to be. I've played all of the KB games since The Legend. There were definitely some decisions made (like the camera and menus) to make it more console accessible, and yes some texture work isn't great, and not all voice acting is created equal. The animation can be a bit stiff, and the world movement is pretty rigid.Okay, with that out of the way, the actual combat is what you remember for the most part. The arenas have more variety, the encounters so far have felt less grindy and more tailored. You still customize how your player plays and most of the actual unit mechanics are what they always have been for the most part. Walking is a bit slow, but things are pretty close together and there is fast travel. There are some obvious things to "find" as well as some much more hidden things for folks that want to scour the map. The world feels very bespoke and hand crafted.You can preview EVERY combat encounter and prepare before fighting. I don't know why folks say its so hard to gauge the difficulty of the encounter, every unit has a clear indication of its tier if you check the stats page of it. Units do level up and when a party of them wipes you can lose some progress there, but seriously, upgrade your u nits to new ones as new tiers become available anyway... leveled up low tier dudes won't stand much of a chance. Some reviewers seem to want to play this like Pokemon where they just overlevel their favorite thing. You are supposed to be actively re tuning and swapping units out encounter to encounter. Approach this more like solving tactical combat puzzles in an rpg lite fantasy world and not a hugely deep role playing experience that happens to have tactical combat. You can choose outcomes with actions, but not dialogue trees. Dialogue is never really that long so it hasn't bothered me too much, I never went in expecting Mass Effect or Witcher style exchanges.I think if you know this is your kind of thing, you know already if you'll have fun even at the current price. If you aren't sure, wait for a sale and some patches, but I think there's fun to be had. I don't regret my purchase so far in the least. Aside from a little texture pop-in/object settling on loads, I've had a pretty bug free experience as well.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the slowest games I have ever played. I don't mean that in an "I've never played a turn-based strategy game before" way; I mean that there is an absolutely overwhelming amount of nothingness between battles or plot points. Quests have you ping-ponging across the map a dozen times talking to people, and progressing your character and army is painstakingly slow. I'm at the 15-hour mark right now and it feels like I've in maybe week 3 or 4 of a game of Heroes of Might and Magic.Overall, meh. The world looks great (with NPCs being a painful exception), and impressively, every single battlefield is unique and hand-crafted. The core strategy gameplay is fine if a bit boring, but the RPG side of things is bad and that's what they've leaned into hard. The joy in this game is just spaced out too much.

Most quests don't have real meaning except to move you around the map.This is certainly a good way to move forward from KB1 in terms of game mechanics, but it lacks in finesse for now.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm so sorry Fulqrum Games! I tried to give it a chance, i really did my best  to NOT give this game a thumbs down but you guys ...well , it's all because of the price tag.    First of all, when i bought the game, i was expecting the "old russians" from 1C Entertainment  to deliver something on the same level with previous original King's Bounty, regarding QUALITY , sound track, graphic design etc. but what can i say?! YOUR GAMES I WAS PLAYING 10-15 YEARS AGO ARE A LOT BETTER !!!Anyway. I understand that you couldn't come with any more original ideas for the old released King's Bounty games but , at least you could have find another name for this game, as it has nothing to do with that superb fantasy world, and the fact you guys mixed elves with dwarf, humans , dragons, undead and some "such-a-cliche" chaotic "race" it's ridiculous ! It supposed to be medieval ...or something, not fREAKINg aliens!!!  Almost 70 hours into the game and when things were getting relatively interesting , of course, game is ending. Here are some reasons why this game is overpriced:Cons--it feels like a game it should have been released 10 years ago. from graphics and mechanics point of view;-buggy enough to press load/save button quite often, as i got stuck in trees,rocks, blah blah bla;-terrible voice acting;-bad soundtrack (compared to amazing but repetitive ones from old King's Bounty games)-most of the characters look the same and somehow reminded me of Elder's Scrolls Oblivion, which was released 17 years ago. Come on ! You can't release a game in 2021 with most of the male characters looking like clones. It's not called Clone's Bounty. -not so complex upgrade character upgrade system for a 2021 game release- ZERO option for weapons upgrade , not to mention most of the weapons found were ... Legendary. Yes. First game i ever played where Common/Uncommon/Rare/Epic/Legendary/Unique ratio is 1/0/1/0/9/0 . Of course, i do not expect from a game to implement this classical type of weapons but seriously?! Most of the weapon/armor drops Legendary ?! You just annihilated my vibe! The satisfaction! That feeling when you're finally rewarded with something powerful after a strong fight or boss and struggling to build something to be proud. Nah! Not in this case. Devs were very generous. Let's give them only Legendary weapons because they (we) paid 35£(40 $) ! Yaaaaaaaay. Everybody wins! Except idiots like me which prefer to deal with something more challenging and complex. Btw , i like your sense of humour regarding that Maximilian set item with -600 Leadership deduction. I was like wtf. Unexpected, loved it. Just this bit.-just 2 maps and one of it ridiculously small-disastrous puzzle system -one of the saves was compromised because of some error regarding Epic Games failed connection , when i don't even have epic games installed on my PC-the run in game ...boring and the WALK option totally useless-controlling that horse on the PC version is ... MAN! I would have fed that poor horse to ancient wolves if i had the option! I can compare that horse with the developers of the game: going in the right direction but no jumps, slow progress and getting stuck most of the times. Now i really miss Roach from the witcher but i will try not to compare a diamond with a simple rock.-no one likes sudden end games but this one it felt like i'm watching a mediocre movie and all of the sudden the power went off-when i finally bought dragon, game ends-hard mode...not that hard!-finished with 160k gold and wondering what will i buy in 5 years or so when next DLC comes in. Intriguing.PROS:-side quests are non-repetitive -enjoyed some moments in the game-nostalgia. reminded me of old classics like gothic, elder's scrolls and few others-good building designs, artI have all or most of previous King's Bounty games which i loved and earned my respect for developers long time ago, maybe that's why i'm extremely disappointed they have not provided what i was expecting this time, which made me be subjective and much more aggressive regarding criticism and highlighting weak spots. _childDocuments_.review: Please do not believe in the bad reviews. This is a good game. It is the same concept with different graphics and UI. I'm having a blast so far.Impressions after over 15 hours in: I was for some time having a feeling that I had seen some of this before, specifically when you arrive near the battle area which has a radius, and the enemies look at you and start preparing; Guess what? I figured it out, it is very, very similar to an older game from 2007, also from 1C, called Ascension to the Throne, which was a very good game, by the way. Third person RPG, with tactical battles (the battle area was larger there); obviously the graphics are much better now. So now I cannot shake the impression that I'm playing ATTT 2  instead of KB 2, but I'm still having fun, since I really liked the older game.

_childDocuments_.review: *Note: mana and gold are finite, if you spend too much of each you can kill your run. However, it is easy to manage mana and gold to have a surplus.*I just finished my first playthrough with a mage build (all quests). 53hrs total.I plan to do 4 playthroughs in total for each unit specialization (order, power, finesse, and anarchy).I really like the battles. However, I found difficulty inconsistent. To progress in the game you often have to fight battles to get to the next area. In two area's in particular, I had a difficult time getting past the battle even after doing all the quests and battles I could in the areas I had unlocked. Only to find the next few battles to progress significantly easier. I also wish it was possible to determine the Line of sight for ranged units not on your side.The movement in this game is really janky, it is very easy to get stuck on random stuff like rocks and branches. The horse is really hard to control and has a terrible turn circle. I wish the  horse could turn in place without running forward (like in every other game with a horse).Graphics aren't too good either, and I often saw the same face asset used on many npcs. The voicing acting wasn't very good, except for the main characters. This isn't really a big deal for me, but might be for others.The story is ok, but It is easily predictable at times. Quests often require to keep going into new areas that are locked behind battles. This really frustrated me in the early game as I'd have to stop doing the quest and do other stuff to level up to get to the next area. Luckily, this becomes less of a problem in the late game.Overall, I had fun with the game, especially with the battles. They carry the game and I wish there was more of them. Based on previous titles, there could be more features added to battles, and I hope that future dlc adds more things to spice the battles up.

_childDocuments_.review: Disappointing compared to its exceptional predecessors.So much unrealized potential in this space but wasted on basic failures.KB2 delivers tactically, improves on story and visuals, but misses the mark -badly- with all the rest.No polish, not even an ending after the final boss battle -_-'...and guys, please, we don't want a *running simulator*!Players have spent half of all their game time just to run from A to B.Even the horse seems to have a mild bout of COVID; clunky and annoying.More examples of extremely basic failures that could easily have been fixed on day 1: - Not providing a simple visual cue when an ability has been activated- Not popping up information for some of the important mouse-overs- Popping up info panels when the mouse is NOT over an item (spellbook & units screens) - a constant annoyance- Not adding transparency to objects while the player is helplessly lost in a jungle of fauna while trying to desperately find some maliciously hidden loot in the underbrush- Shortsightedly limiting major (choice) player choices later in the game - players are forced to choose options to avoid being screwed over by combat oddsIt makes one wonder whether they even read the playtest feedback...Was an unfinished product pushed out because some fop of a manager decided they knew better?Indignant ranting aside, the game was also enjoyable and properly scratches the tactical itch.Many of King's Bounty's concepts have also been faithfully inherited.The good stuff is just tragically marred by all the other terrible design decisions (or lack thereof), and probably in general, a rush job.So many players have complained about basic failures but their feedback is not taken seriously.If designers and managers don't want to listen to valuable criticism, then serious fans are forced to answer in the only way they can: a thumbs downIt's harsh, but hopefully that helps dissuade other gamers from wasting money on what could and should have been a (much) better game

_childDocuments_.review: Verdict: King's Bounty II is relaxing and fun to play BUT, at the same time, slow, badly paced,  often frustrating with getting stuck on literal pebbles and, most importantly, with an unfinished main story.  Get it on sale if you are ok with all of that. +Steam trading cards (4 drop, 7 to make a badge)Steam achievements (49, requires 3 full playthroughs)A solid variety of units (5 types, about 55 units in total)Pleasant soundtrack (especially the last vocal song)The combat is really funQuest log is well done and you will never get lost thanks to itPlayer characters have unique voice lines that show their charactersLove the new style, unit design and overall world If you pass a cache, chest etc and don't collect it, it will appear on your map which is really nice Your character will react according to your prior choices in the late game -The DLC items are really powerful. I have finished the game with Armor of the Hollow and Staff of Harmony equipped Full of bugs that were never fixed - you will constantly get stuck on terrain, and some items are going to be hard to interact with There is an unused slot in inventory for some reason The story is bland and full of clichés Travelling in the overworld is really slowThe ending really shows there was supposed to be DLC or another instalment as it is really unsatisfying Everything boils down to "good vs evil" and "magic vs brute force"The game is terrible at communicating things - e.g. your characters are going to get passive bonuses to magic/warfare etc but that is not stated anywhere when you pick them. This literally locks some spells from being learned.Mandatory exploration - your losses in early battles cost nearly as much as what you getLiterally, every sideway has a boring treasure chest (it is always gold + items to sell) which makes it necessary but dull as heck If you want to buy more units you will spend dozens of minutes backtracking while trying to figure out who exactly sold whatExtremely dull puzzles - 90% of them are "click on braziers in the correct order" Your character doesn't have the ability to sprintTerrible inventory management - there is no sort of possibility and searching for boots in armour is unnecessarily complicated Edit 1: Mage playthrough 1) difficulty is not balanced across the board. Once I got the last ability in mage tree together with chain lightning I just breezed through every fight with no losses 2) inventory is terrible as there are no indicators for what spells you have in the bank or have learned which causes me a lot of reloading 3) Scryer's trials are not rewarding for mage as the rewards are more tailored towards the warrior BUT the last trial has the best mage trinket in the game so you kinda have to suffer through them4) the mage is very sarcastic but NPCs are reacting in the same way as toward the warrior which often feels out of place as the replies feel off 5) majority of the quests are just an illusion of a choice. I am now running Anarchy instead of Order and there were only 2 differences so far (one small location locked itself out and one main quest NPC had a different voice actor for a bit)Edit 2: 100% finished the game as all characters1) yup, choices don't matter at all2) the game just doesn't have an ending (it even says "to be continued ...") 3) chain lightning is broken as hell so I just rushed to the vendor who had it4) the best sets are either rng drops or you need guides to get them - either way terrible design decision5) the game ignores even your side choices at the end (e.g. it still acts like you gave the stone to a troll, know some secret identities etc)6) good lord, the horse is utterly useless besides one quest. It is literally slower than you in cities 7) the last song is still amazing

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game, including literally all the quests I could find.So... thoughts:The good: Is not a bad game. It has a decent story decent talent tree, decent combat. They left room for a sequel.The neutral: I did like the idea behind limiting number of units in squad though the implementation was... meh. Since you end up with only 2 possible options in endgame (all units from one faction - meaning that you get the morale but except the T5s you waste ton of leadership - and I played as a mage... lowest leadership and still ended up with thousands extra for most troops; and the other option is combine races and unless you invest in order you go negative morale). Would've like to see some options of more than 2 ways of building end game army - multiple T5 options or whatever (remember KB1 green dragons and giants... great units but they hate each other; but you can go red / black dragons + giants, or green + dinos... or... many... I played that game in tens of combinations). Basically... I think the idea is good but needs a ton of polish (or get back to not limiting).There are some attempts at humor that I enjoyed but the voice acting kind of ruined it.The bad: It lacks... depth. The quests are rather generic with a few exceptions, the dialog is lacking. But I've seen worse. There is no jump... you can't even go down a minor cliff - and when I say minor... I mean like 10 cm blocks your path; This feels bad in 2022 - like really bad.The horror: The ending. For me it felt like at some point during development someone said "you know what... just add a combat and call it a day". Seriously... the only worse ending I've ever seen was in ME3 (and even that one had better cinematic).Comparison with KB1 (any of them):As I mentioned before... it lacks depth. Except some quests that gets you maps for secret areas there are no real secrets / wow moments (remembering the old shoes / clay pot / ink / ww skin? there are none of those kind of items here). In kb1 I was literally pressing D every step. I was not selling anything because it may have had a secret somewhere, and when I was finding it it was so fulfilling. No idea why not keeping this in here.There are no dialog choices, and the only way you make decisions is by going to a guy or another.It is imo... fully unrelated with the original series. And inferior (to be fair the original series had like 10 years to get polished - maybe kb will get some much needed love in future updates).Replay value: I don't see much replay value (I finished KB1 games, all of them, at least 5 times each in order to check different story options, secrets, armies, etc.; will probably not finish KB2 a second time - at least not for a long time). There are some meaningful choices, I don't say they are not but... so few...Personal verdict:Despite having more negative things on the list.... I did enjoy the game. I do recommend the game if you want to burn a few hours on something. It definitely does not worth the full 60 EUR price, but if you get it on a sale... is ok.

_childDocuments_.review: King's Bounty 2 answers the question "how could we make King's Bounty work on the XBox 360?" The answer? Smush the perspective from top-down to third person, make an interface designed to be played on a TV with a controller, and remove any semblance of the original's difficulty.It fails to answer the question why anyone would  King's Bounty 360.  Or, for that matter, any other question you can think of, like "what the hell is the plot," "did humans actually write this," or "do you actually bother to pay these voice actors?" The result is a B-list game straight out of the XBox 360 bargain bin. Like many titles of that era, it's a clumsy console port, the result of platforms like Unreal and Unity making multiplatform releases easy and Steam eliminating the upfront cost of PC distribution.Just replay Crossworlds. This isn't worth your time, let alone whatever you might pay for it.

_childDocuments_.review: The KB series is best at tactical battles. This instance is in almost all aspects a step back from the previous titles (and I am not talking about bugs here).- You have to run around in console third party view (instead of just clicking where you want to go)- I have not seen much of the brilliant (and often dark) humor that was present in the previous incarnations of this series.- Enough is said about the skill tree in other reviews already- And the Minimap. Apart from not being able to use it for traveling (like - you have to RUN there), you also don't see enemy armies there and how strong they are. So - if you back of from a fight because to come back later with a stronger army... you actually won't know and have no chance to find out - how strong this army actually is. Apart from... well.. RUNning there again to find out. This is an absolute unnecessary design decision - probably by the art department being proud of the movement animation while running.- English voice acting is lacking but that is the most easy part to ignore.- Army Management is a joke. Why on earth can't i just use the mouse? I mean - I get it, you want this game to be playable on a nitendo switch (or whatever other reason you had to castrate the UI in such a way), but ... this handling is just ... worth a refund alone, without all the other aspects.- Personally I liked the comicy style of the battles more. The units are to small, why even bother with animation. They could have just used Icons. It would have been much better, to just use ONE model of each troop-type and display this at an actual seeable and enjoyable size.

_childDocuments_.review: A reasonably enjoyable game, but I think the main issue is the price point raises a certain expectation of quality that the game fails to meet. Graphics are reasonable, but the models, texturing and lip synching aren't at the level they should be for a £40+ game. The voice acting is extensive, but unfortunately it mostly detracts from the game experience as the dialog seems very idiosyncratic - as the developers are Russian maybe something has been lost in translation. The gameplay is quite  simplistic - again not terrible, or completely lacking merit, but not quite the experience you'd hope for when paying this much for a game. Overall, I will probably continue to play this game on and off until I've finished it, and in that sense, for me at least it may be worth the price (since there does seem to be a lot of content). That is really the sole reason I am recommending the game. However, be aware that I can generally overlook things that would drive others crazy, so if you cannot bear the many faults the game has, then it is largely irrelevant how much content the game has since you will never play through it to completion.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine Heroes of Might and Magic, but where instead of it being turn-based, and instead of building up your city, and instead of everything being 2D sprites (or a bird’s eye view like in the less popular, later titles), you turn it into a real-time, third person RPG. So basically, the idea of you, a hero on horseback (or not), traveling through the land escorted by an army that isnt visible until combat starts, usually at a chokepoint on the map you need to get past, but said combat retaining the heroes of might and magic formula of being a hex-grid style, turn-based combat where the unit stacks you field, clash against enemy monster stacks, while being augmented by your spells.That’s basically what King’s Bounty II is. A spiritual sequel to Heroes of Might and Magic. And viewing it in this lens, it really is a good game. The reason why this game received so many negative reviews is from a mixture of King’s Bounty I fans expecting a sequel to THEIR game, and finding out this looks and plays different, and people complaining about the (at release) triple A title pricetag when in reality, this game’s engine is clunky and outdated by at least a decade. For instance, the hero cant swing their sword. Or even jump. The hero cant even hop down a small ridge they find themselves standing on. Cant swim (or even enter a body of water). Instead, the game world’s pathfinding is as bad as an early 2000s PS2 game, full of invisible barriers. HOWEVER, to compensate, this has been coated over with beautiful graphics based on beautiful art design, a rich color palette, and traditional fantasy RPG tropes, all of it giving the illusion of a pretty game world, until you get reminded of the engine limitations. Think of it as Diablo: quest-givers stand frozen in place with an exclamation mark above their heads and don’t move around like NPCs. Same with merchants. Each settlement has a few that cater to your army and equipment needs. The NPCs that do move around, you cannot interact with, but they occasionally greet you or tell you off when you bump into them. So even though it is beautiful, even TES IV: Oblivion from 2006 had a far more interactive game world than King’s Bounty II.That being said, if you once again put your Heroes of Might and Magic glasses on and view this game from that lens, and see it as a ground-level representation of a HOMM map, it will become a lot more familiar. You travel around the world picking up loot, some of which are gemstones but which arent required by any unit as they all only cost gold to recruit, and thus loot that you have to then sell for gold at NPCs called Vendors. These vendors also offer wargear like armor and weapons, that however are useless to you, the player character, as you don’t fight yourself, but instead, wearing them boosts the stats of your army units, just like the artefacts you find and equip on your hero in HOMM.You can field 5 different units in your army, and the maximum amount of members a unit has, depends on your leadership skill, which increases as you level up. Each unit belongs to a faction: Order (good guys), Power (wild animals), Anarchy (outlaws and undead) and Finesse (magical creatures). Having all units from one faction gives a boost to their morale which can allow affected units to attack twice in the same turn, while the more varied factions your army is composed of, the harsher the morale penalty will be, to the point of affected units skipping their turn entirely. Units are also classed into quality "Levels". A level 2 unit is generally superior to a level 1 unit, and this isnt just reflected in their stats or special abilties that can be a bit confusing to compare, but also in the gold cost per member. You purchase these units from NPCs called Recruiters. If you purchase more than 5 different units, subsequent units get moved into your reserve.After a battle, a partially damaged unit (that has lost some members) can be healed back up to full strength for a small amount of gold. But should you completely lose a unit in battle, the empty slot can, right after the battle, only be filled by one of the units you had in reserve. While traveling, you may not know where the next Recruiter is, so having 1 or 2 units in reserve can keep you going even after a tough battle. However, the game world isn't big, because there’s a new quest almost around every corner, and you often come across “town portals” that fast travel you back to the town where you can restock your units.Let’s talk about the magic system next. Casting spells requires mana, a finite resource. Think of it as something like the premium currency in mobile games. You find small amounts of mana as loot, and larger amounts by touching a blue mana stone. To be able to cast spells, you need to first find them – usually in the form of spell scrolls. Each scroll is single use, but you can carry multiples of the same spell. Casting a single-use spell scroll doesn’t cost mana, but consumes it in the process. However, what you can instead do when outside of battle, is learn a spell from a scroll, so that you can cast it for some mana as often as you like. To learn a spell you need to be a mage of sorts, and this talent is represented by your Arcane Knowledge. The more powerful a spell, the higher the Arcane Knowledge (and one-time high mana cost) needed to learn it. Once learned, it can then be cast forever for smaller amounts of mana. So hold on to at least 1 spell scroll of each type of spell you find so you can study it later. Once per combat turn you can cast one spell.During combat, next to moving up a certain amount of hex-tiles and/or attacking, you can also order a unit to wait and have the enemy come to them before moving up and attacking, or focus on defense and gain a bonus. Melee-oriented units project a “control zone” of 1 tile around them, so anyone moving too close to get past them gets auto-attacked once. Ranged units need line of sight to be able to fire at their target, so making good use of battlefield obstacles is key to success with/against ranged units, who are weak in melee. Then you have things like movement speed (in amounts of hex tiles) and initiative (when it's your unit's turn to do its thing) as well as armor (resistance to physical damage), Resistance (resistance to elemental damage), and HP (of each member of a unit, added up to a total unit HP, with the whole unit's total healthbar then divided into segments with each member making up one segment) - and thus, healing can only restore one such segment but not bring back those already dead and is thus more effective when used on high HP, but low squad member units. Many units also have a special attack that usually can only be done once per battle, but does extra damage and has some additional effect like bleeding or burn, and in turn, each unit has special rules some of which are passive abilities like skeletons & golems being immune to bleeding while zombies can’t be poisoned.So as you can see, the combat sounds very familiar to old classics like the HOMM series, while the movement around the game world, talking to characters and doing quests for them is inspired by traditional RPGs like Witcher, The Elder Scrolls and Dragon Age. I understand though why King’s Bounty II has found itself stuck between a rock and a hard place for having tried to mix two popular genres that have nothing in common, save the fantasy setting, i.e. turn-based combat games that are fun only when played as “scenario maps” in short RTS-style sessions rather than as a continuous RPG, and traditional RPGs but where your hero is supposed to fight enemies on his own, but can’t here. Heck, you cant even go inside houses in a town and can only wander the streets. Still, I cant shake the feeling that this game will be a cult classic one day, and its title (numbered sequel of a franchise it has little in common with) is the only thing holding it back from reaching a much larger audience.

_childDocuments_.review: Just about any veteran strategy gamer out there will be able to tell you about their experience with the King’s Bounty series. I first jumped into it with King’s Bounty: The Legend but its roots go all the way back to 1990 and I’ve often been told by the gaming elders that it was an impressive experience that stood out in its time. That said, even with its long history, King’s Bounty was a series that you knew what to expect with each new release.King’s Bounty 2 has taken a giant step away from the template set by its predecessors and completely replaced the campaign elements. Whether this is a hit or a miss is likely to deviate from player to player, though at least the battles continue to carry on the legacy of the venerable series.Our tale begins with the most classic of choices: warrior, paladin, or mage? Though choosing your class has always had a significant impact on gameplay, King’s Bounty 2 offers three entirely separate characters that represent each of the classes. Are you a grizzled ex-royal guard with a talent for strengthening his units? Are you a ruin-hopping mage with a knack for supporting her troops with powerful spells? Are you an inspiring commoner with an innate talent for leadership who can field a larger army than her compatriots? The choice is yours and it will set the tone for your game. Old habits die hard for me, and as I was drawn to the warrior, I spent the earliest part of my quest being pardoned from the dungeon to serve the new liege in a story that had a mix of high and low points. With each skillfully crafted segment, it felt like there was another that didn’t quite fit in with the rest of the setting or that was unimpressive with its development overall.King’s Bounty 2 leans away from its heritage and breaks out a new style of gameplay for the campaign portion of the title. Instead of moving around on an overland campaign map in a way most famously recognized as the Heroes of Might & Magic method, King’s Bounty 2 has us take a third-person view of the shoulder of our hero. This gives the experience overall far more of an RPG feel than a strategy one. If you’re picturing something like Skyrim but with a bit more jank and battles that break away into turn-based tactical battlefields with multiple units per army, you’re probably not too far off.There’s plenty of dialogue, maybe even too much for those who want to dive right into the action, though the world is quite interesting for the lore hounds among us. Among the treasures you’ll discover, you’ll find books and scrolls that deepen the setting as you progress through your quest. I found most of these interesting, a rarity for me, though some of the dialogue was a bit corny even by King’s Bounty standards.My key complaint is what seems to be the growing pains of the swap from a far removed overhead strategic map to a third-person RPG perspective. The world itself is designed well enough and much of the scenery is legitimately exciting to explore, though your movement through the world is far from optimized. There’s quite a bit of territory to cover outside of battle and doing it by foot never feels as if you’re moving as quickly as you’d like. Your mount is noticeably faster, though the mounting and dismounting animations take some time which is particularly inconvenient when you can’t interact with the world from horseback. Though there are certainly worse issues that could plague a gaming experience, it does slow down the action quite a bit and turn traveling into a bit of a slog, especially since even your horse’s speed slows to a crawl inside of certain environments.Combat encounters and character development are strikingly similar to the King’s Bounties of old, at least in the mechanical sense. Every unit is a bundle of attributes that gets increasingly stronger the more of them that there are in their stack. Ten swordsmen, for example, will deal ten times the damage of a lone one, though they’ll also weaken as they’re cut down to size. Units also have an impressive number of passive and a smaller number of activated abilities that differentiate them from other unit types on top of these varying attributes. A crossbowman has more differences from an archer than just a few altered statistics and they excel in different scenarios.There’s plenty of choice when it comes to deciding on the composition of your army. Obtaining new types of units and replenishing those who had some of their members die is most often done via a recruitment merchant. A new convenience that’s been added is that you may immediately purchase and recover a good portion of your losses after a battle as long as you have the gold on hand and they weren’t completely obliterated. This is extremely useful and cuts down on the amount of time that you travel from recruiter to your current adventure and then back. It’s a good thing this exists, not only for the streamlined convenience but also due to the less-than-stellar movement that we’ve already discussed.Unit alignments and experience are two elements that are likely to flavor your judgments on army composition overall. Alignment isn’t a new concept with units being aligned to the four discussed previously, anarchy/order and finesse/power, and stacking units outside of their preferred alignment comes with a morale penalty unless you’ve learned the skills necessary to reduce it. On the other hand, experience and leveling have been implemented which allows a unit’s base attributes to increase with use. A unit that isn’t particularly exceptional might be something that will work with a given strategy as long as you boost its level. Army levels cap at level three though, so don’t get too excited about pulling out dragon-killing spearmen. However, the fact that units have a far narrower spread of skills does mean that a healthy unit of lower-tier troops can put up a decent fight against a single powerhouse as opposed to just being absolutely worthless at a point like the old days.Your hero plays a large role on the field of battle even if they don’t hop in swinging their sword alongside the rest of their followers. Though you can only bring in five units, your leadership skill determines how large each unit stack can be. The paladin has a talent for being able to lead the largest stacks, the warrior provides the most significant attribute boosts, and the mage forgoes having as impressive of an army so that they can throw a variety of powerful spells into the mix. Heroes share a generic skill tree, though your choices along the way unlock tiers via an alignment system between anarchy/order and finesse/power. Veterans of King’s Bounty will be the most pleased with how the legacy of battles has been preserved, though the loss of any kind of mechanic for your hero to actively engage in the battle outside of magic feels like a missed opportunity. Farewell, rage, we hardly knew ye.Interestingly enough, battles don’t tend to be as frequent as they were in the series’ past iterations. A battle is representative of your encounters with the hostile forces of a small region so there’s usually some amount of a narrative tied to each one, whether it’s dialogue or simply a quest location. For the most part, back-to-back battles are incredibly rare and almost every combat encounter is the quest objective.(Thanks to Steam's character limit, the conclusion of this review is in the comments)

_childDocuments_.review: tl;drI can't recommend this game except to the most die-hard of King's Bounty fansQuick Pros and Cons:+Same enjoyable turn based combat you'd expect from King's Bounty-Unfortunately, does little to evolve that formula in any meaningful way-Unit variety is at an all time low-Battle UI lacks clarity and visibility+Improved visuals overall-Uninspired art direction and lackluster aesthetic means the world is extremely forgettable-Poorly optimized with very few graphics settings to adjust+Controller support is quite nice, and works very well-Lack of quick save hot key, among other oddities with keyboard & mouse controls+Light RPG elements to help break up the tedium in-between fights-Overworld is incredibly frustrating to navigate, character moves at a snails pace, the mounted controls are half-baked, and the character can get stuck on the most random and trivial terrain-Most quest choices are meaningless and simply award points that have little to no effect on gameplay or character growth-Story will likely have you yawning and mashing the skip dialogue option

_childDocuments_.review: Biggest dissapointment of the year for me.One of the biggest selling points in the original series is the Heroes of MM heilcopter perspective, the slightly chidish / fantasy'ish graphics and the monsters chasing you on the map.This game went in the completely opposite direction, removing absolutely everything that was fantastic about the first one. I could compare this to Dragon Age 1 vs Dragon Age 2, as was an equally abysmal transition.In addition to turning it into a FPS type of adventure, the graphics are not very good, the voice acting is absolutely from the lowest shelf and the game itself is so dumbed down it feels like an insult. Everything is litteraly pointed out on the map for you. Find the secret entrance you say? OH WAIT, THE QUEST MARKER POINTS RIGHT TO IT.  Also the running speed of the hero makes me want to find a wild flock of ravens and have them peck my eyes out. I can imagine the board meeting where this was decided. "You know the running speed that would make it so that people are not bored? Reduce it by 50%! All in favor saye AYE! I will play through it, but this is a pre-order i will regret. As a HUGE fan of the first games, completing every one, my only recommendation is to not buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is an absolute glass of dumpster juice on a hot day, unpolished to the point of absurdity. It feels like it was released a century ago, yet it still lacks the basic gear you'd expect, throwing balance out the window. The skill tree is as if it was designed by someone who detests clarity, and every quest is a monotonous cycle of fetch and slay. The puzzles are insultingly simplistic, akin to something you'd expect in a toddler's playbook: just press three buttons in the right order. Following the first installment, it feels like the developers decided to cash in on our expectations without any effort. I'm just relieved I snagged it at a 90% discount for a trial run, rather than wasting full price on this debacle.

_childDocuments_.review: I played all the previous titles to death (except the very first one), I managed to finish most of them on impossible no-loss difficulty. Kings bounty 2 is an amazing game and I love it as much as I did the previous ones if not more. I love the world and the story telling, and the third person perspective worked out really well. The "morality system" and how that ties in with the talent tree is especially well thought out. The graphics might look like its from 2014 but the aesthetics is perfect. Overall incredibly immersive game.A few minor issues I have is: cant use fast travel points while mounted. Since it takes a while to mount/unmount i realy feel you should be able to use fast travel while mounted (staying mounted on the other side as well) Your character whether mounted or not also gets stuck in weird places way too often.The interface is a little unintuitive and frustrating. things like tooltips getting stuck and hiding information below it forcing me to "hide tooltips" is anoying, items cant be dragged and dropped instead you have to use spacebar to equip items and then the previous equiped item goes to the very bottom of your inventory instead of switching places. In general the UI could have been much better.No difficulty setting. Now, fortunately the game is not easy so it is challenging me on my first playthrough (currently level 24 so I'm pretty far in), But I would love to play it again and I wont be able to unless they add higher difficulty settings, it can be as simple as previous titles. just a multiplier on enemy stack sizes and your gold gain. I do hope they patch this in, especially since the choices you have in game makes this game so replayable, I have a order/finesse character and I want to play the game again as power/anarchy

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of Pro's: good graphics for a turned based game, a good story line, and the Normal game has a lot of gold and item caches, so money is never a problem. There are also plenty of places to purchase additional troops.The Con's to the game though: are the horse cannot back up (which leads to getting stuck, in tight places), linear story progression like Assassin's Creed, limited story options based on which character you choose, and limited character selection (male fighter, female Wizard, or female Paladin).Overall, the game is fun to play, and a good addition to the King's Bounty Franchise. It just needs some more fine tuning.

_childDocuments_.review: I played and enjoyed the previous KB games, loved them, gameplay wise I still regard HoMM 3 to be on top but for story is definitely the KB series. With that said KB 2 is highly disappointing. Let’s start with the good because that is easy to cover.Gameplay is actually good, is annoying sometimes when you have ranged units which target enemies all the way at the end of the grid, camera does not zoom out all the way (not on all maps) which means you have to position it in the right way to see properly. Graphics also , it actually looks alright.And that is pretty much it for the good, told ya its gonna be fast, so let’s get to the bads:-	Biggest gripe with this game was the world, it feels like a big demo, you are stuck in a region (not counting the tutorial one) which keeps you traveling back and forward in it. For those who played the previous games you know it takes place all over, from elf forests, to dwarfs underground, to hell, etc… well none of that epic journey here, you are just stuck in a human forest with villages and cities -	Story, while that main plot is interesting the way it told it is just horrible, the dialogs, the characters, everything… The characters are unlikable including the main character you play with (I played with the paladin and she was an arrogant Karen.. hated her). The way plot moves forward is just crap, most of the time characters just seem to ♥♥♥♥ out portal, appear out of nowhere and do some narration. The side quests aren’t better either, suffering of the same faults. And all in all, it’s just a mess.-	Sound, the previous KB games had a wonderful audio, with beautiful OST which I can still listen to. Well, all that is washed away in KB 2, music does even play in background most of the times, even when it should like action packed cutscenes. The only good one was the main menu theme.-	Navigation, while you cannot jump doing some exploration off the set paths can be an issue because you can get stuck in rock, branches, all kind of things, and you should do some exploring if you wana find extra loot. Also, the lack of a mini map, you are stuck with a compass hud and to see the paths you need to reach a certain you gotta keep opening the main map.-	Controls, it kept picking up my Xbox controller and could not remove it, so instead of plugging it in and out I played with it, it felt alright, went most of the game with it, but it did impact me in a puzzle, speaking of which…-	Puzzles, are braindead, they offered barely any thinking and felt more like they are implemented to waste time.-	Units, since you are stuck in a human region, most units are humans, you will find undeads, dwarfs, beasts and elementals, with just 2 dragons and the end. And even those are few and boring.-	Fights, while I did praised the combat gameplay, the fights compared to the previous games felt forced and scripted, you can no longer run by battles and escape them, there are no other heroes roaming the map, and the biggest L is that interesting boss fights, like the spider queen which took 1/3 of the grid in the previous games, none of that here, even the last fight, you get to fight this big threat and instead its just a hero which casts spells.-	Horse, ♥♥♥♥ that horseOverall, a huge disappointment, and I played it 2 years after it launched so by now it should’ve been fixed but instead its filled with bugs and glitches. Don’t even recommend it for free…

_childDocuments_.review: Writing first impressions, might change later, including the verdict.I understand authors wanted to provide bigger change than main protagonist and settings. Sadly, for me, the change was very much for the worse. It's ironic that the game seems to be very much the same, but change in perspective caused these:- The graphic went from beautiful hand drawn to uninspiring 3D. It's not outright ugly, but it's far from good looking and the magic is entirely lost- The same goes for combat UI, characters are small, hard to distinguish and the graphical presentation is really bad. Also it seems that everything "extra" (chests, hazards) was removed- The character is running corridors. I've considered and realized that in previous incarnations of the game, character was also running corridors, but it somehow didn't matter because I could see where I'm going and what's around. Here I run like I run perpetual gauntlet- I'm not sure if it's a feeling or reality, but the world seems to have shrunk. Areas I explore are tiny and boring- In relations to previous two points, I'm not sure if I should laugh or cry when it comes to riddles. "You must activate the crystals, but the witch's magic has made me forget how to do it. If only I could remember!" Solution - pick up a crystal, take three steps to a an altar, insert the crystal. Wow- To give proper "skyrim" feeling, character has a horse. Every time I run to something explorable, I have to dismount, which takes a while. Then I realize the horse is blocking me and I have to mount again, move a little, dismount again. To make sure you don't ignore the horse, the character is moving super slowly without himThe game seems to have generally changed towards more serious narrative, which is not really a bad thing, but I'm missing humor and beauty of the originals. A lot of points are lost because of comparison to them, it's not entirely bad, but a lot of things that were done right before are now pretty much wrong, so I'm very disappointed so far.

_childDocuments_.review: Do not believe all the Troll reviews, I have been having an excellent time in game ever since i started playing it. I will agree with some that this is definitely not the Kings Bounty I've played before, but I really like the new 3rd person prospective on the hero. The Voice overs are well done and the cut scenes are great. I even liked the story enough to read the quest lines :) The Blight battles are the hardest challenge but definitely fun. _childDocuments_.review: So I decided to refund. But first, of course, I will write a review.It looks like everyone focuses on "This is not kings bounty!!!!!111", but not reviews it on it's own merits. I for one did not expect next Kings Bounty despite the name, but I expected a fun game. Which IMHO I did not get.Optimization:Right off the bat first thing I noticed is terrible optimization. It is Unreal Engine 4 and despite what everyone is saying, games on UE always had terrible perfomance for me. I checked settings, while GPU fans started spinning menacingly. This was in menu without anything to render other than static picture. Temperatures quickly raised as if there was some kind of bitcoin miner. So I dropped graphics from fantastic to medium just to stay under 70 degrees.Graphics:Never cared much for graphics, but the style they were going for is obviously Witcher inspired. Not only in graphics. But unlike Witcher, everything looks static. Trees are static, snow has no effects when you walk on it, bushes don't move when you walk through. Animations are ok, but sometimes choppy looking.Gameplay:The core of gameplay is walking simulator. Your run speed is very slow and horse is barely faster. You can't interact with anything on horse, so you must dismount with slow animation if you noticed something. I understand that they made it to artificially increase playtime and make players go over 2 hours so Gabe will not give your money back. But hold on, we are playing Turn Based Strategy, right? Uhhh... For 1.5 hours that I played I had only 4 easy battles that took maximum 5 minutes to beat each, which leaves us with 23% combat. Easy combat which not even takes that much time.Other 77% is running around in an empty world, getting stuck in a random props and doing such interesting quests like finding letters(run around the village with no enemies to fight and search every corner), activating sigils(run around the same village, you got the idea) and bruteforcing badly made puzzle with 6 variants.But wait, maybe it gets better like some astroturfers said? Nah, watching gameplay it stays the same. Most of the time you still running around.One of the absolutely "brilliant" decisions is lack of difficulty options, so whole game will be either too easy or too hard for you. From 1.5 hours it was too easy and looking at some videos it barely gets better.No dialogues with choices, you only speak with someone and that is all you can do.UI and controls:Made for console, basic combat information is hidden from you in multiple menus, horse controls are absolutely worst making you hit everything in your path combined with very long turn times(plus linked relative to camera direction).Finally:It can't really hold on it's own even without comparison to its previous parts. If you want walking simulator, try Stanley Parable. If you want an actual turn based strategy try Fantasy General 2, Dominions 5, X-COM2, Thea 2, Sanctus Reach, previous King Bounties, Fantasy Wars or anything else, really. Refund here I come.Edit: forgot to mention that items/soldiers in packs and from preorder are actual game changing troops and items with actual stats, which is P2W. You will never get items from preorder and they are forever exclusive. Still returning it though.
