_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game and i thought that the game was quite good. I feel that a lot of the negative reviews are harsh and undeserved.  Whilst i understand that not everyone likes change, not all change is good and "if its not broken, don't fix it" but i personally welcome the change to 3D and open world. I see it as King's Bounty meets The Witcher. The graphics are really quite good. The world is very beautiful and detailed and you can tell that a lot of effort was put into it. The apparel looks good. If you want to be critical, some NPC's have the same face.  I think the voice acting is decent over all.  The combat is quite good and at times quite challenging. The puzzles are mostly easy but there were a couple with no real hint, just try every combination until you guess right.  The story is good/decent. I really liked the graphics of the environment. And i liked how there is loot everywhere so exploring is rewarded. I don't understand why people feel the game is boring or tedious so much? At times it is but no more or no less than most RPG's that require a lot of back and forth, lots of side quests and repetitive missions. Aren't all/most RPG's like that? Personally i found some of the other older King's bounty games to feel like that at times. I am a long term fan of the franchise. I hired the old one on my Sega Mega Drive/Genesis back in the day and thought it was cool. I've played and completed a couple of the newer ones on Steam. Even got the 4th highest score on one of them. And i liked this one quite a bit. The music is good. Even though there is not a whole lot of it. I don't think the horse is useless. like I've seen suggested. And i hated Roach in The Witcher lol. Admittedly, when the game first came out i was put off by the price tag and my initial impression was not good, i thought it did not look like Kings Bounty or very good.  I cant speak on if the game was buggy at launch but in its current state its not very buggy at all. It's an absolute steal at the 75% discount.

_childDocuments_.review: I will straightly point out a few things briefly.The perspective and style that they tried to bring into the King's Bounty Franchise carries a huge potential, but the fact that the game also designed to be a console game too is ruined it.First of all, the control of the movement of the horse is terrible. God forgive me but it is. So many times switch my character between walking and riding in order to collect stuff around the world but it was not well connected. Sometimes it was so hard to use the horse in specific places, and sometimes I needed to walk all around in a path to collect all the loot.Secondly, I love the new skill tree stuff. Collecting points with doing specific things in the quest lines, gives at least one more run to play (unfortunately, at least in theory). But the skill tree gives you very low amount of choices. AND, AND, THE MOST IMPORTANTLY, the skill tree and the item's properties basically prevents you to play mix of warrior&mage. In the previous games, you can boost your army or skill book independently the class you choose. In a warrior build, I was able to use haste, heal, trap, etc in order to increase my advantage (even though the skill levels were 1&2). In this game, I played warrior and therefore I focused warfare ability. In the middle game, I was barely able to use level 1 heal and stone skin 1. Forget about the haste or other basic spells like fire or poison ones. And due to the limited skill points (you can only get one type's final skill in the max level) you cannot spend your precious points into the magic stuff, not without giving up MORE necessarily attack boost traits.Last but not least, the game is unfortunately incomplete. Both in the gameplay and storyline. Due to the problems with the horse, there are some places that you can be stuck. And the storyline leaves you with like "feel free to roam around the world, the story will be continued". I guess the recent events about the developers left this game to be root (I am not fully aware of the situation but long story short the game is no longer supported for further updates or etc). In conclusion, if you want to feel a different gamestyle of King's Bounty (if you played the previous games), I suggest you to play the game, just to have the experience so that you can criticize it. That is why I bought the game and played to be honest, I was hyped first, but due to the lack of time I couldn't play the game. So when I heard the recent news, I just buy the game for this reason. But if you never played any King's Bounty game before, I STRONGLY not recommend it! If you really curious about the franchise, look into the past games (they are a bit old but if you are into the genre, you will love it, at least more than this). Long story short, no curiosity, no play. Have a cat instincts? Try it :)

_childDocuments_.review: REVISED UPDATE AT END: I'm not done with the game (20+ hrs currently @ lvl 15 as Warrior) and this game is hella fun.With average reviews hovering around 65%, you'd think this game was trash. I'm not seeing where the hate comes from at all.I highly paused before purchasing given all the middling/down votes and reviews - but glad I ignored them and bought it.There's nothing wrong with this game. It definitely doesn't deserve the hate. It's Kings Bounty through and through. I finished the older KBs and expansions and those were great too. This one does change it to a more 'mature' 3rd person exploration game and 3d battlefield - but it does it well and I've thoroughly enjoyed the freedom of strolling around the world. It's relaxing and pretty to look at. It's an explorers dream like the original KBs. There's always a reason to explore every bush and corner to find treasure or a buffing landmark or a new quest or even hidden areas. The graphics are great, the sound effects are great (horse clops are great) and even things like the loading screens are very well done. There's cutscenes and side quests and a decent story.The talent tree seems on par with the original game talent trees and units are interesting. So far the minor nits have been that you can occasionally get hung up on clipping on rocks or ledges in the world - and that when you teleport it takes you off your horse so you constantly need to re-summon. Turning on the horse is a bit wonky and some of the loot in the caches is just simply gems to provide money so the items found aren't really exciting. There are however armor/weapon sets, set rewards and one of the DLCs (if on sale) offers some more items that's not amazing, but also not bad. If on sale, I thought it was worth for early weapon. Lastly, I tried 2 classes, Mage and Warrior (voiced by Geralt of Rivia!) on Normal.  Mage is for people who want a very difficult challenge! Warrior has been fun and just right. Haven't tried Paladin. This game is a huge thumbs up for me at full price - and if on sale it's double thumbs up easy.Too much fun wandering and exploring, with nice tactical battles, great graphics and sounds and an overall enjoyable KB (3rd person) experience.UPDATE: I just completed the game and the excitement wore off hard core. I'm tempted to give a thumbs down rating but will keep it thumbs up as I enjoyed 90% of the time I spent in the game.WARNING: The end is utter BS. Both the final battle (unless you have tailored your army accordingly) as well as the half baked "ending" (eg nonexistent ending).At the end - the final boss is all about mind control. I played on Normal using Order units and felt real strong, able to beat every fight with good tactics. The final battle is impossible with Order units as they get MC'd easily (save 1). However, you can dispel MC , right? No. It doesn't work if its from the Mages or lvl 1 Spell Book. I'm not sure if Lvl 2 works or not because I was a warrior and put all my points in Order and Power tiers so never had enough magic to get lvl 2+ dispel to save my units. Game also bugged so you can't morph them with the polymorph spell either. So all my units would be MC'd and taunted. Tried the fight 6-8 times and got walloped. What's also super dumb is you can't go back to the world to try and level up units or buy units you want that aren't MC'able. WTF.Top that off with the way I won was to walk around last zone and find a few vendors and I bought all the non - MC'able units I could which included 3 or 4 tier ONE units because of course you can't level them up! I got lucky in the fight that my tier 1 red dragon got 3 enemy units lined up for two passes as flame strike and also more importantly the unit I had that got MC'd was my Cavalry and I had only 1 guy left in and he died and I have the perk that respawns the whole first unit that dies so I got a fresh new set of horses with no MC. My tier 1 non - MC'able units did hard work while 3 of the 5 of my tier 3 Order units that cruised all game long rode the bench for the final fight (except Mages/Cavalry).Seeing as how if I look at the achievements for completing the game, it shows roughly 10% completed with Warrior, 10% with Mage and 10% with Paladin for 30% total who finished game - shows how bad the final design was.TLDR: ENDING RUINED THE GAME (BOTH THE FIGHT MECHANICS AND TERRIBAD DESIGN AND THE STORY) 5/10. Play at your own risk.

_childDocuments_.review: Is it a fun game and well made game? YesIs it a great King's Bounty game? At timesAfter 50 hours I've got 3 characters with thematic builds up to lvl 22-24. The first run can be quite slow when exploring the world. To be exact you explore every bush and rock for loot and coins to afford an army. Which can get quite tedious for some. However I find it enjoyable due to amazing world building and atmosphere. People who say the graphics are from the early 2000 are just looking to bash and troll. The graphical assets are fairly high quality. What the devs do with them when put together is just amazing with beautiful vista's, dense lush woods and forests, dungeons with a very fantastical vibe and atmosphere. This is definately one of its strengths.The units you can choose, from four different "Factions", are quite decent. As long as you don't go for dedicated thematic builds that is. When you do that it becomes clear that there is a deficit of unit options here and there. A pure beast army is near impossible in the later part of the game. Simply because there are not enough high tier units for those. Same for Bandit themed builds. If you just take the highest available unit for the given "faction" you'll do just fine however.This game is also a great entry point for new players for this genre as a whole. In the past you had to be very carefull about spending money and buying units. Losing a unit could quickly spiral into a game over back in the day. Using cheese tactics was often more a necesity to get through fights. None of that is present here. Money is readily available and you need to really ♥♥♥♥ up badly for it to become a problem. However the tactics in most fights is quite simplistic. Try to practice on using the "Delay" turn properly and you pretty much master this game.The three heroes are pretty decent. They are the ones that define the difficulty of the game basically. With Paladin you don't have to worry about much and you can do pretty much everything. Providing a very easy playthrough. Warrior is a medium challenge but using the Mages, Flamethrower Dwarves and the Red Dragon...you'll got a lot of Pyromaniac synergy going. Mage can be quite challenging early on when you just start. Once you then learn spells such as Blind you pretty much won the game.Beyond that the game has a fair amount of "jank". Little things that aren't game breaking. However some, related to AI of ally troops, can be a mess. So bad that you don't need enemies anymore in some cases. Such as the Chimera in the final boss fight. Which you just need to Teleport straight into the middle fo the enemy and hope they'll actually contribute in some way. Instead of wiping out your own troops for some stupid reason.There are also puzzles, but they're so simplistic. Not really worth mentioning. Just a change of pace to get more loot.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a product of passion. It's very much like the older King's Bounty. This is very much like Heroes of Might & Magic during battle, but nothing like it in Exploration Mode. During combat, the game is turn-based. Unlike Heroes, during Exploration Mode, this game is third person and isn't turn based.Exploration Mode has you walk around beautiful areas picking up and completing quests, talking to people, learning more about the lore of the land, et cetera. It pulls you into the world with beautiful vistas, music, lore and quests. But that's all you can do in Exploration Mode: you walk, you talk, buy gear, sell trash and recruit your army with accumulated gold. That's it. You use WSAD for walking, E or F for interacting, X for summoning your horse and that's it. If you expect some Assassin's Creed third person action, or something similar to Gothic, you're very much mistaken.And that confusion is where much of the bad reviews are a product of. People expect something this game isn't and never pretended to be. The turn-based action is during combat, and in third person Exploration Mode you're just running around just taking in the world.I love it. This game knows what it is. I'm sucked into the beautiful world and interesting story. I can't wait to progress further into the story and grow as a hero/army. Is there bad stuff? Not really. There's mediocre stuff though. Much of the voice-acting is so-so. Dialogue lines are sometimes weird. Running back and forth can sometimes become a little bit boring, because the world is very static -- as you'd expect if this wasn't third person but like Heroes or the earlier King's Bounty games.Maybe the devs shot themselves in the foot with this ambitious Third Person Exploration Mode. Kids these days look at one trailer and probably thinking they're looking at a game like Dragon Age: Inquisition. But it's not. It's King's Bounty II. And I F'ING LOVE IT!

_childDocuments_.review: This game made me appreciate the previous games a lot more.On its own this game is a fine enough game, but it does what a lot of modern rpg sequel games does.The graphics are technically better, the game got voice acting and it has a higher production value. But the trade of for that was what made the previous games fun.I was never a big fan of the king bounty games, i played through "the Legend" and "Northern warriors" when they came out but i still remember them well. The moment you start the first game you can explore the world, the side quests are fun and interesting plays on the fantasy franchise like how the dragon and princess are going through relationship problems. You can start a family by courting ladies like the pirate queen by slaying the Kraken or you can just kiss a frog and have a frog princess wife, but then you will half frog-human children and if you divorce your wife she will take the children and 50% of your gold. Comparing this game to those games might not be entirely fair, but when the game is the official main sequel you can't avoid making these comparisons. Stuff like that was fun and interesting that i still remember years later despite only playing through the games once. In this game however it feels like a lot of the fun has been sucked out. The side quests are the same boring side quests i have done in every rpg, an striking artstyle has been replaced with the drab realism look, the main protaganist feels like a plank of wood (which is a shame considering he is voiced by the man who voiced Geralt) and you feel boxed in unable to truly explore the world depending on where you are in the story. I also wonder if the technical bump up might also not be worth it since the lesser technical limitations of "the Legend" allowed the team to have several sequels/spin off games where we got to see more of the world. With this game i don't think this will be possible unless this game sells well. I am a little conflicted if i i should give this game a thumbs up or a thumbs down.In one way this is a downgrade from the previous games in almost every single way.But on its own it is a fine enough game, "fine" being the optimal word since it is not amazing nor terrible, it is just average from what i have experienced so far. If i could i would give this game a "mixed" rating, but judging this game on its own separate from its previous entries i think most rpg fans will like this game if you don't go in with the "baggage" of having played the previous games, so i will reluctantly give it a thumbs up. But my advice would be to buy the previous games instead since they are cheaper, better and you can get almost the entire pack of all the previous games for the price of this single game.

_childDocuments_.review: Have played quite a few of these Kings Bounty games, and I must say the graphics in this one are quite outstanding. It's a bit different to the previous little hero on the horse that gallops from place to place seeking battles, and plundering chests, that was viewed from the top down. Now you're actually in the map, as a 3rd person adventurer. There's an interesting story line that follows the main quest, and numerous additional side quests to keep you occupied and bring your XP levels up. Talent points are awarded, and you can boost your abilities via the skill page, and replace weapons/armour etc via the inventory.  The choices of army are still the same, Dwarves, Soldiers, Elementals, Animals, Golems and Undead, although I have not yet come across any Demons, or Druids. (Maybe later on?) I'm really enjoying this game, and it's got a few interesting puzzles, so be sure to read the notes and scrolls. Plenty of treasure chests and caches along the way too.  If you choose your army carefully and observe the terrain, it's possible to win 'strong, and very strong' battles with minimal losses. Do I prefer Kings Bounty II ? No, because it doesn't feel like I'm playing Kings Bounty, but then again, it does feel like I'm playing a typical RPG, and I'm enjoying it!

_childDocuments_.review: You'd be hard-pressed to find a RPG that has more generic quests than this one has. You probably wouldn't mind so much if the game had stuck to its original 'Heroes of M&M' concept. In that kind of environment, you don't expect too much. But the developers took a chance and created a fully 3D world. It is that world that is the most desirable aspect of King's Bounty II but it doesn't have many other redeeming qualities.My chosen Champion sounded like a 13 year old girl, which accurately reflects the choices made for most other voices - almost everything is overdone. Combat is a lackluster affair in which you continuously question how stacks work (the leadership mechanic is badly implemented). The 3D maps are pretty but it plays just awful because you end up scrolling and rotating to find the remote target for your ranged units, and you'll regularly miss-click trying to move a unit. And that is possibly the most damning aspect of KB2: the miss-clicks are because it's not been made for PC. It was made for consoles. You're constantly struggling with the interface, particularly so when hiring units and trying to buy equipment. In the end, the beautiful 3D world and cutscenes are simply not enough to rescue this King's Bounty from everything else that is failing it.Oh, yeah, can reviewers please stop comparing this game with The Witcher 3!? They have absolutely nothing in common. While I am not impressed with King's Bounty II, any such comparison is both ridiculous and unfair to King's Bounty.

_childDocuments_.review: Short take: it’s a great game for turn-based RPG lovers. Pros: Exciting battles, engaging level progression, tons of option, an interesting story.Cons: Outdated graphic, slow movements, no difficulty levels.It’s called King’s Bounty 2 so let’s start with that: if you loved (like I did) the King’s Bounty series (and not just from Legend, the older ones as well) you either will hate the new direction or will love that they innovated but kept the essence. I am for changes in life – and to say the truth after Legend, Armored Princess, Crossworlds…. The series started to grow stale on me. Yes, the formula is great, but you can take cute graphic and a narrow isometric world with no story only so many times. This is why I am glad they tried something new, keeping the essence of what makes King’s Bounty interesting. Also, I must admit that many years ago, when turn-based games where less popular, my vision for an ideal game was pretty much what they realized now in KB 2. The new approach makes the world much more interesting, keeping the battles as engaging and challenging as always. It seems that the budget for the game was low, so don’t expect Baldur’s Gate 3 kind of graphic, animation, and attention to details. I still play Might and Magic VI so clearly the graphic is not that important to me. Nevertheless, the game has its moments with spell animations and breathtaking views of distant mountains. The three main Characters are cute and each with their distinct personalities. If character customization is a must, this game is not for you. To me the main protagonists are just vessels for talents, spells, and armies, so I am fine with them. I liked that the Paladin is so nice and cute, the Mage is a countess who does not tolerate people (Go Girl!), and the Warrior a brute. There are many choices you can make to personalize your champion, each with a distinct impact on the battlefield. Units and battles are the main strength of this game: they have many interesting abilities, can create synergies, increase in experience, and fight in ever changing arenas. In previous iterations, the optimal path to maximize your army strength became clear quite soon. I did not find this to be true in this game so far, which is good, but I haven’t the thousands of hours of experience I had in the other games, so it’s early to say. Also, a cap on how many units you can field makes battles more balanced and interesting.Other flaws are typical of most new games – bugs, odd development choices (like no quicksave), but they are minor in my book. If you think you cannot leave with a quicksave because pressing a few more buttons it’s the end of ‘fun’ for you, well than you should not play KB 2.Overall, I see myself enjoying this new world for hundreds of hours and hope the developers will treat this venerable series with the reverence it deserves. We waited a long time for KB 2 and this could very well be the beginning of a new era for it. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: My honest review as someone who has played King's Bounty before,I will start with I have played all to modern KB games and besides Dark Side being buggy I am a huge fan of Warriors of the North. I also got to the final boss in KB2 but couldn't be bothered to finish the game.I will start with the changes I liked, even some that are so good that I think the lack of will make plating WotN hard to play.PROsFirstly I love the heal mechanic. Unit doesn't die? spend some gold to get them to full as long as your enemy doesn't have some form of execute. This was by far my favorite change that changed the why I played the game. I no longer needed to baby a unit because they are limited and if one dies, I won't have many more to replace them. This really was a game changer, It changed how I approached combat in a positive way. If someone modded this into WofN or DS, I would bet a lot of people would be on those games again.Modernized TBS playing field. The fact that you did more damage attacking from the high ground really changed how I approached combat as well. This changed my combat tactics from little more then face rush or turtle and spell bomb. You now have a reason to take the high ground, as well as a reason to move or remove the enemy off the high ground. This made the fights more fluid and less the same ol.NEUTRALsMagic. I played the mage, and there is a ton of spells but I really only used 6. and some of those became obsolete as I for new spells. Any ray spell, portal, Madness, fireball, rain of fire. Why buff when I can just teleport your slow bruiser to the back by your range and kill half of them with a RoF? I also rarely had to worry about elemental dmg type. Either they are immune or not.They made a lot of hype about wherever you meet an enemy would decide the battlefield, and it did, kinda, in a dishonest way. What you really have are prebuilt arenas littered all over the map that has a duplicate on the walking overworld map. That is where all fights will happen. Killed a group and passed it to get to a graveyard and the new quest has undead spawn? It spawned all the way outside the graveyard in the chokepoint you just cleared. Is this approach bad? Not at all. But i seem to remember thinking, cool. maybe I will be able to lure to a more favorable spot for harder fights.The music, voice cast, and graphics. They were alright. This is the best and worst I can say about them.The bugs. I expected some bugs, and I didn't ever run into any game crashes or game breaking bugs. It was all cosmetic bugs and like 1 spelling error that I remember.CONsThis is what ruins the game for me, the list of cons.Movement, we have to talk about it. When I first opened my inventory I saw a slot for a horses head and thought, oh, maybe I get better mounts to make up for the stupid slow speed. No, no you don't. This game has few fights and a TON of just moving back and forth. Add on to it, the fact that you can not interact with anything besides fights and scripted cut scenes that start at approach. Also no mini map so you need to open your map ALOT to see if you missed treasure you ran by or to find your way. It honestly feels like this was all kept this way to pad the game. And does this game need padding.Items. I feel like the items were both dumbed down and simplified. Old WofN had a ton of different effects for a ton of different playing styles. Wanted to run elves/demons/undead/whatever you have items galore. Here it mostly was just ohh, bigger numbers. There are a few exceptions to this rule, but it mostly dealt wither higher level 6 or 7 piece sets, but honestly more mana and magic power trumped any of those sets, and was way either to get.Creatures. This was a huge let down. I think we had 72 units available and it blows how much they pruned this. This was such a frustration. You pick your poison and pretty much stuck to it. Sure you could swap it up, but exp and gold is limited so you can only spread yourself so thin. The options are thin on the ground and if you tried to stick to a theme you end up using the same army for more of the game. I was finesse and pretty much always ran ice, fire, earth elementals and the 2 golems. Older game you had so many choices, and this one one, you have like 10ish options per path. And you have to stop using the lower level ones because of the limit cap and them getting straight up wiped every fight after a hit or two.The fight script, aka the starve. This was by far my biggest pet peeve. The game is designed so you are locked into an area, and to unlock the next area you need to fight boss A, but boss A is to strong so you have to do most if not all side quests to have the power to beat boss A, now you have boss B, he is to strong, do all the side quests and beat him. Rinse and repeat. It wouldn't have been to mind numbing if there was more content or areas to go and explore but there is not a lot to this game, just a lot of space, a slow movement speed, and a need to find as many caches for gold as you can because late game a fight that kills all of a unit means spending like 15k.Overall I give this a 4/10. Yes it had some improvements that I enjoyed but it feels like a gutted game that saw games like the witcher and skyrim and decided that what made those game so popular and cash cows are it being 3d.Does it look better then older KB games? Absolutely. Is it a real King's Bounty? Technically., yes. Is it a good King's Bounty game? No, no it is not.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all: I never played KB I, so if you look for a review that is comparing it to KB I - thats not me :-)The basic game idea follows very much the good old base line of turn based strategy, tries to be inventive, ...and sadly makes all the wrong turns you can imagine. Many ideas are good ideas, but horribly implemented. Examples? Here you go:- First person exploration: Good idea basically, but in this game this means a walking simulator. You know all the places where fights are very soon, and then you walk to find fights you can take on. That means walking. A lot of walking. Strawling. Moving your body around the map. ...aaaand more walking. Cause basically there is nothing to explore that justifies the FP style play. The map is merely made of linear follow this way to next battle design. No sidethings to explore, no unexpected things or battles or whatever. Its just an environment to move towards your next already known hexfield battle, by... you got it... WALKING- Ok but dont we have port stones? Yes you do. But you can't port to those like in normal games, ...yep you got it... you gotta walk there. That means more walking!- But there are horses: Yep. If you mean the thing that has a turn angle of an old nissan bluebird, spawns in places where it is stuck, or spawns in you so you see the inside of your horse, or can't manage to jump a 30cm stone on the way, stops from galloping to 0 in 0,00001 seconds making you expect to fly over the horses neck, then, yes, there are horses. I rather walk ingame, which is a pain in the ass- see the above...- Ok but its a world to explore right? Thats what RPG elements are designed for right?: Well here comes my main critic. The game fails completely at generating immersion to the game world. NPC's are there but act like in games from 20years ago (yes im standing in the city throughout the game saying the same sentance over and over if i am passed by the player - or i stare at a wall, for decades or so...) Landscapedesign is horrible, the character finds himself stuck all day cause the environment is not thought through. Characters and their backstories are so unbelievable boring that you find yourself skipping dialogues cause uninteresting as hell, gimme the battle already. The whole 3D first person world is designed only as a substitute for a hex map where you directly move to the next battle. And therefore is completely useless and is merely a stone of hinderness on the way to the next battle. Thats a design problem, the said to a hexfield gamedesigner - make it a 3D FP world! Thats like telling a car mechanic to repair your dog. I never got sucked in the world like in other turn based games where there is an immersive world that is seemingly thought through and believable. Its just a moving simulator to get to the next fight. There is basically one set of items for each of the 3 characters you save credits for, the rest of the hundreds of collectable items are stuff without eaning that are just for selling to a merchant, so now i search the map and mobs for better loot stuff either. Its an immersive desaster. Nothing you do in this first person world really matters to anyone, even yourself. Its just a walking simulator to the next battle.- Ok, so the FP thing is ♥♥♥♥, what about the key thing. The turn based battles...!?: Well there comes my second major point of criticism. Nothing new here, the units, the weapons, the skill progression system, it has all been there already decades ago. Which doesn't necessarily have to be bad. I mean there are good games that sell old wine in new bottles but are good anyways. Not KB II. I never ever, ever, ever before, felt in a turn based strategy game, that my decisions and tactical formations and preparations were so irrelevant like in this game. The fights are, to sum it up, 80% coincidence, 20% your job. The same fight can be incredibly hard and - after reload, incredibly easy, as they are driven by statistically coincidence. You can make all the right tactical decisions and loose horribly, as well as making all the wrong decisions and win with a clean sweep, all in the same fight, reload does it all. Also there are lots of spells and abilities, that are basically a waste of time cause irrelevant in a fight and you find yourself 5 battles deep into the game using the same spell order in every fight cause other combos suck and you win easily with the same stereotypy play over and over.- Uh, but there are hard fights, right?: Yes there are. But they are not hard because of clever acting AI or enemy or special tactical finesse, nope its more like chess problems, where you have to figure out a special move order and nothing else will work until you found that move order. Its frustrating as there could be other solutions to the situation but nah, you have to use this now in this order and you have to reload 15 times until you found that 1 move order. Sucks!What else there is to say. Bugs, lots of bugs. Clipping into literally anything all day. Quests can't be done cause the object of interaction is not responding. Action and result animations are sometimes 3-4 seconds apart, including sound errors. Mount spawning in area it can't move away from. Summary: I do not recommend this game. If you are a masochistic millionaire with a decent love for dissapointment - go ahead. If you think i may over exaggerate things, go for it when its at a budget level. I seldom feel i wasted money on a game. Here i do.

_childDocuments_.review: There's good talent involved in the game. Specially when it comes to level design and music. Some changes could've worked, giving the player a new perspective into the world of King's Bounty, improving combat, etc. But, in the end, too many decissions against not only the fans of the saga, but newcoming players as well, ruined a great oportunity to revive the franchise. In the end, we get a game with a decimated unit variety (much more focused on humans) and lots of restrictions that punish experimenting and encourage min-maxing.The game is not unplayable or absolutely worthless, so here's the list of things that ruined the game for me so you can decide if you want to play it anyway:🚧  In this game you have 4 ideals (order, finesse, anarchy, power) that will affect your story decissions and your skill tree and, separatedly, your army.Most missions give you a choice using 2 of these ideals (power vs finesse, order vs anarchy). The first problem is that you have to commit to 2 and once you commit the game won't let you choose the opposite (if you focus on anarchy you won't be able to choose order options after a while). Another issue on top of this is the fact that decissions are very inconsistent. Like at first anarchy will force you (if you choose this path) to side with child murderers but later on it might be the only way to help a tormented troll (if you chose the order path you won't be able to). Story choices also give you ideal points which are used to unlock higher levels on the skill tree for each ideal-related skills. So if you want a power-based character you have to make power-based decissions.🚧 Unit variety not only has been reduced drastically (check the bottom to see more) but also encourages using only a handful of units throughout the adventure. Unit stacks are limited now. Low tier units cap at 10 or 8, higher tier at 6 or 3, etc. Also, you have to level up your units, you can't buy them already leveled up, so if you want to try a different composition it's going to be hard to keep those new units alive because they need to kill to gain XP but also survive the encounter being underleveled.🚧  Loot and gear system is not good. Most loot is useless trash (labeled that way by the game) that has to be sold in exchange of gold. Gear doesn't have much variety but hear this: some set pieces can only be obtained AT RANDOM as a reward for missions. Meaning that you could perfectly never find all the pieces for a set in a playthrough.🚧  There's too many problems with cluster objects. You can get stuck on any rock or branch and be unable to move, forcing you to load a previous save. Also controls on horse are horrible.🚧 Music is beautiful but often there's no music or stops abruptly. A lot of cinematics don't have music making them less epic.🚧  Nothing happens for 3/4 of the game. You arrive late to all parties and someone else tells you about what happened. Your mission? Cleaning up the mess. Most of the game is about fetching quests of the lowest order (go to quest giver - go to points A,B,C and D and gather items - back to quest giver that sometimes moved somewhere else). Many puzzles as well, some obvious, some mildly fun and a few tedious ones. This gets worse towards the end. The game keeps stretching the ending with fetching quests, constantly sending you to the same areas you've been before to gather items before they let you fight the next pre-final boss. It ruins any tiny bit of tension that the game managed to build up. All this to end on a cliff hanger. For what? You guessed it, they planned to sell you a DLC, that never came out, so you could get closure. All this while most of the game the main plot is frozen so you can be an errand boy for NPCs.🚧 Content density is very low. You have a relatively big map to move around but fights are very limited and you run around the same areas for a long time, going back and forth often. You can perfectly spend a whole hour with no combat. Also you have to constantly travel around to restock units when needed and there's no way to be reminded (in game) of which merchant sells what units so sometimes you'll have to go around looking for the right one.🚧 Some of the main missions are more like puzzles than battles. You have to fight with a given army rather than yours and you have to figure out what did the devs want you to do with those troops/spells.🚧 RNG can ruin a fight. Fights in general can be a circus sometimes. You don't get giant bosses like in the previous games but some enemy heroes have spells that can decimate your army in one round if you're not careful. Plus morale seems to favour enemies more than allies (you can get 1 extra round the whole battle while the enemy gets 1 or 2 per round with the same morale). Fights are only hard mid-late game though. The last few battles are very easy.The game is playable and can be fun at times. Fights are supposed to be more meaningful that spammy and the battlegrounds are bigger and more eclectic (you have higher grounds, choke points, etc). But the game is extremely generic, restrictive and abuses things that are against the player (like blatant padding through fetching quests, uncompleted story to sell DLC later, butchering content from the original saga, etc).There's not a lot of competition for this game and it's 5 bucks on sale every now and then, so it's up to you. But don't get it at full price, the game is not worth that much in my most humble opinion.: Royal army (humans), dogs, "angels" and some elementals.: Elementals, golems, gargoyles and chimeras.:  Animals (wolves, bears and eagles), griphons, trolls, dwarves and red dragons.: Bandits (humans), undead (including undead dragon) and cultists (humans).

_childDocuments_.review: This is not the game it should be. There are enough King's Bounty games that we have a certain expectation as to what it means when a new one comes out. I was excited when I saw they were making something new on a new engine, with better graphics! I had hope that it would be more of the same stuff we loved, but with a new coat of paint.... but that's not what this is. This game is quite linear, at least in the ways that matter. In the older games I loved exploring, being able to reach a map to unlock a new area before I was really supposed to; a lucky find of an item in a shop that wasn't there the last time I played, or a powerful new type of unit that could work well with my rag tag bunch of units I've been able to scrape together at this point... this can't really provide any of this things.It seems very curated, and the second area is more open, but there's really no point in exploring... not really. And the items that you find are just garbage that you can sell to shops. There is no mystery or excitement in exploring or even finding a new shop with new units, really. My hope is that they will take this new engine and make something that is faithful to the old games, something that has a ton of replay value and is exciting to explore with rewards for doing so. _childDocuments_.review: Tricky one to review. It's Kings Bounty but not as we know it.It certainly takes a bit of getting used to but if you enjoy the combat of the Kings Bounty games you will probably enjoy this.The game plays like any previous Kings Bounty game. You wander around a map with a few main quests, many side quests, collecting units and random treasures before fighting in tactical combat. The main difference is that you are now playing in 3rd person over the shoulder, the result being that you get a real feel for the size of the world but there are negatives.The Good:The world feels big. Whilst at first I wasn't overly fond of the story, it has drawn me in.Tactical combat is more or less the same as the previous games.Army building is still thereLeveling / perks system provides decent character building options.Gear also gives versatility to play style.Fights all take place in a tactical battle view that mirrors the actual world view.The Bad:There is a lot of time walking around between quests. Whilst you can travel on horse and fast travel between areas, I have spent hours just walking around in "towns". Walking around is not fun.The random treasures that you would find dotted around in previous games are still here. Why is this bad? Because you spend time exploring off the path through foliage that you can't really see in case you missed any. most of the treasures like this don't contain anything good. It feels more like just a time sink that creates even more time just running around.The variety in number of units is not as high as previous games. This basically means you will sometimes swap one unit out for another but it is rare that you find a vendor that has units that suddenly allow you to play in a different way.A lot of spells at the start are very similar.There are not enough battles. I've spent about an hour running around a dungeon doing puzzles with 1 fight at the end. I wouldn't care if some of the fights didn't perfectly match the outer world, but I shouldn't be playing a Kings Bounty game, exploring a new area and not have fights.Really there are only a few things that I would like to see to improve the game.Make walking speed in cities faster.Make mounting a much smoother process. Just press the button and you are on the horse and off you go. I don't want to have to mount the horse and then wait a few seconds before I'm moving.Allow fast travel from anywhere to one of the fast travel points.As you can see, most of my real issues are from the amount of time I spend walking around.Apart from that it's a solid game, but if you are looking for a Kings Bounty game and are new to the series, Armoured Princess or Warriors of the North would still be my pick.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has the potential to be really good, but it's held back by the commitment to 'hardcore' aspects of game play that don't fit with the design. The combat is a hex grid, isometric, turn based battle with up to 5 units vs 5 units. Each unit can be upgraded to increase its power & how many of the unit go into battle. As units level up, they may get new skills to utilize in battle as well. This is where the familiarity stops. For a RPG, this game feels & plays weird. The movement feels like it was out of the N64, your character can get stuck on rocks, small ledges, fallen trees, and uneven surfaces. You can either walk (crawl), or jog. On release the character moved so slow that the wildlife would pass you in the streets of the city. Your horse magically appears behind you, and very frequently gets stuck doing so. By far the biggest problem this game has is the limited resources that are available. At any point in the game, you can have one or a few bad battles and run out of money effectively bricking your save as you will no longer be able to afford to heal your units or purchase new ones. EVERY resource is limited. Gold, mana, trash on the ground, combat encounters, all of them are finite resources. You are at the mercy of your gold, which you use to buy equipment, units, and to heal your units after battle. The overlap in the need for gold combined with the very high cost of purchasing almost anything leaves you with the choice of either save scumming fights to loose less units, forgoing equipment upgrades, heading into battle unprepared without a full unit roster, or running around hoping to avoid battles and find some barrels with trash to sell. This leads to a very unsatisfying game play loop that detracts from the otherwise enjoyable combat. The 'reputation' system is also a relic of the past. There are 4 types of units that can go in your army, mixing units lowers their morale and causes them to miss turns at the mercy of RNG, the opposite is true with stacking similar type units. You will likely spend 60% of your time running back to different vendors to restock your units when they level up or you increase your leadership. Fast travel stations are few and far between, and the vendors are not marked on the map indicating what they sell so good luck remembering. The voice acting is horrid. Dubbed shows on Netflix have better voice acting. Popcorn reading in a 5th grade classroom will yield more vocal inflection than is present in the voice acting in this game. You are better off playing on mute. Overall the game tries too hard for it's own good. The parts that are great are severely overshadowed by the tedious management of your units, and lack of resource availability in the world. If you look past the glaringly unpolished movement and voice acting, and disregard the time you will spend back tracking to vendors, the combat can be an enjoyable experience. Unfortunately, that's not enough to save it or make it worth purchasing unless it's free or at a steep discount.

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting new approach for a classic series, but unfortunately it falls short in many aspects at this stage, and also presents some new issues. Despite the official launch months ago, it still feels unfinished and just recieved massive balance changes alongside a basic difficulty selection feature. Its also fairly short and doesn't have much replay value.Units appear as troops with individual animations, which is a nice change in theory but also caps every unit type at a max of 10, making basic troops useless later on, but the game also frequently struggles with individual units disconnecting from the unit tile or updating with significant delays. Battle progress in general seems to stall for several seconds after some actions.General level progression has been reworked fairly significantly and quests frequently offer a few different routes to solving objectives, with the choices affecting the morality system or ideals. Although there are 4 ideals, its only ever a choice in the same grouping, with one often being easier than the other with no drawbacks or consequences to the game overall besides earning points for the chosen path, which in turn determines which higher skill tiers the hero can access.3 of these Ideals map closely to the 3 types of skill trees found in the older games and are assigned as the prefered path for one of the 3 playable Heroes in practically the same way. Anarchy is the odd one out, providing a mix of economic advantages and combat benefits. Unlike older games, Heroes don't have exclusive skills, but are locked into a certain set of base skills and have different stat priorities while leveling.Since skill or talent points are only obtained through levelups and the level cap of 30 is fairly easily reached, and the more powerful skills also still have skill requisites on top of being more expensive themselves, the system doesn't actually provide much room for choice if the goal is to obtain one of the 4 top abilities. A lot of skills are also fairly situational and some are practically useless after a while.These ideals also form the basis for troop factions, rather than the races found in previous games, though in practical terms its a rather similar setup. Order troops are the usual Human type units, Power comprises Dwarves, Ogres and most animals, Finesse troops are magical beings such as golems and elementals, Anarchy is home to Bandits, Assassins and the Undead.Which leaves out a ton of creatures from the older games. Demons, Elves, Orcs, Lizardmen and the like are completely absent. There is a sort of 5th faction, though it mostly uses corrupted versions of existing units and its inaccessible to the player.Similarly, there are now 4 schools of magic rather than 3, each comprising of two sub-schools (though that doesn't really matter much in practical terms outside of elemental damage attributes. Learning and upgrading spells works roughly the same as before, except for the addition of Arcane Knowledge requirements and for some reason, crystals have been removed in favor of mana as a general resource (while the amount of total mana available per fight is determined largely by the Arcane Knowledge stat). These stat requirements are as such that only the mage hero can even learn all the spells, nevermind being able to actually upgrade spells fully.One of the perhaps more unique advantages the new engine has is the ability to explore the world from a more direct perspective and interact more directly with various puzzle elements, which the game features a lot of. Often as quest objectives, but some puzzles are just sitting in the world to find and solve to obtain a treasure chest. That being said, they almost always boil down to activating torches or buttons in the right order based on simple text clues or symbols, or just brute-forcing with no penalty for wrong guesses other than wasted time.One somewhat worthwhile exception are a series of combat trials with a fixed setup, attempting a sort of chess puzzle challenge. Unfortunately, random factors and AI behaviour can still make these frustrating, and changes made to the game have thrown off the balance of these tests as well.Another fresh approach to the world is that most battles take place on the overworld, rather than the same basic battlefield based on the terrain where the battle was initiated in the older games. The downside to this however is that fights can only happen in often very obviously designed parts of the world map and can't be bypassed. These areas also tend to be very empty in terms of exploration for hidden goodies or other interactions. Sometimes they will at least be populated with some NPCs after the battle but few have anything to say or offer. Some of these areas are also reused for another fight later, sometimes in relation to the same quest, but some repeats are also purely optional. Any combat arena with enemies is also shown with a clear yellow outline at the border, though some fights are more like hidden ambushes... but even then the game not only autosaves right before it, you can always back out from the battle preview screen.Portals also often lead to seperate maps with their own combat arena, where the game's approach is a bit inconsistent between just leading straight into the fight and moving back to the regular map or giving players the option to actually explore the arena after the fight (for no actual purpose other than just picking up a quest item).Compared to the many different areas in the older series, KB II only really has one main map with a pretty standard layout of a few towns, villages, farms etc with some mines, ruins and caves. The tutorial starts in a seperate map with snow, but its a lot smaller and can be fully completed the first time. It is far less open for exploration too, with broken bridges, barricades and other obstacles which only go away when the main story says they should. In one case, a broken bridge was suddenly fixed when I finally found my way to it from the other side very late in the game.Navigation in general feels quite a lot more cumbersome from this setup. There is a horse to ride around for faster movement, but it handles rather awkwardly for turns. Fortunately, Fast Travel is also available from many locations, though this always dismounts the player and the monuments that define fast travel points are always located outside of towns and other areas of interest. Movement is also somewhat awkwardly stilted compared to other games with this kind of perspective. The player character can't jump, can get stuck on some terrain, the horse can get in the way and some interactable objects can only be approached from certain directions. The map isn't always very readable in terms of elevation either and can sometimes even lack some important information (one quest I put off for later didn't have any map indicators showing up as the objective was behind a portal). Merchants and Recruiters are labelled only by their name on the icon, which isn't helpful.One last comparison worth mentioning is the overal quality of the game compared to older ones. Though I ran into a very odd problem with the game's installation bugging out on the Direct X package, this game has so far avoided the various quality issues the older games had. No crashes, no inconsistent translations, bugged quests or mechanics of note. Even with the addition of voice acting for every piece of dialogue, I've not noticed any significant mistakes. Its not particularly great voiceacting, but not terrible either.Overall, I think this new approach definitely has some potential. Many of my gripes in terms of what is missing from the older games might not even detract from the game from a newcomers perspective either. But its also a very short game for the full price and needs a lot more work.

_childDocuments_.review: I've long been a fan of this series, though weirdly never gotten quite as much play time out of it as I feel like I have.  Maybe it's just a really sticky game in my memories.  So, King's Bounty 2 drops (2?) and I'm like: hell yeah!  I'm a bit concerned because of the Mixed reviews, and the lack of Katauri Interactive.  Well, let's just say that my fears were well founded but ultimately aren't a deal breaker.King's Bounty is no sacred cow to me, ultimately what I want is a fun game and what has generally appealed me to this particular franchise is the class and army based gameplay.  I think most people can state that Crossworlds continues to be the pinnacle of the series.  However, if we set those games aside and focus on KB2 for its own merits it gets a lot of things right.  First off, the classes are differentiated in multiple ways, and the fights are a little less tedious thanks to being able to use your winnings to "heal up" after it's been completed.  Plus, I'm a sucker for any game with character customization and since almost every piece of equipment or artifact you find can be visually seen on your character, I'm willing to put up with the absolute worst menu system that's ever been created.  So, if your question is: will I enjoy this as a King's Bounty fan?  Probably.But let's talk about that interface.  KB2 is a game that can be generously described as good enough.  Some things it does well, such as the aforementioned character customization, but many things it does migraine-inducing poorly.  Menus are the worst offenders.  Anyone used to the spell book in previous games would be justified in sending hate mail to the UI designer.  In fact, the UI in general is what I would expect the programmers to create for debugging the game.  Calling it serviceable is accurate, it will get the job done, but as an interface the player is expected to use?  It's atrocious.  No drag and drop.  The book tabs are now at the top of the screen, but you also can't just change pages.  You have to store troops to buy other troops because you can't just buy directly to the reserve and so on and so forth.  It's definitely the worst part of the game by a significant margin.It's not a deal breaker, but it's hard to understate how important UX is and how bad it is here.  Still, I can recommend it in spite of this because everything else is serviceable or better.  I can't say it's unseated Crossworlds but if they go on to do a King's Bounty 3, I'll be interested to see it.

_childDocuments_.review: First thing you should understand - this is not an old good “King’s Bounty”, you probably remember. I would not call it a sequel. It would be more correct to say it is a new game in the same genre.This is a RPG, where we travel around an open world, interact with citizens, complete quests and so on. But unlike the most such games, while fighting enemies the hero does not do it himself, but instead he commands a small army, which jumps out of the pocket. So the main gameplay aspect is a tacticals turn-based battle.Being inside this gameplay genre is almost the only thing, which this game shares with the original “Kings Bounty”.In comparison this sequel creates a more mature appearance. You will not find references to famous fairy tales or cliches here. The world is less magical and more realistic, filled with politics, plots and so on. Overall atmosphere reminds of “Witcher” rather than the original game. For example: dwarves appears like second-class citizens, facing xenophobia, behaving like barbarians. While in origin they were a race of brilliant engineers with respected independent kingdom.Whether such a change of scenery is good or bad everyone decides for himself. Personally, I would make it more like the original game, because (surprise!) It is less common nowadays.Unfortunately, besides cosmetic changes some main game features were also lost:- Rage skills/spells have been removed. There is no “rage” in the battle. There is no box of rage spirits or magic dragon of rage, which can be used to unleash special attacks on the enemy. I consider this to be the main loss, as it was a feature, which separates the original game from the other ones in this genre.- There are no special giant bosses, like giant turtles, digging machines or something. Previously they provided a good diversity requiring special tactics.- Gremlins and everything connected with them have been removed. There are no artifact affiliations or upgrades through battle with internal guardians. The concept of gremlins being behind magical mechanisms was one of the charming features from the original game. Although some may disagree…We can choose from 3 different playable characters: a fighter, a paladin and a mage. Besides class differences, each has its own appearance, story and personality, which affects some dialogs. Still it would be better to have a character creation/customization feature instead, where we can pick the class, the gender and appearance. In this way you would be able to create your own avatar as you like, which provides a better “RPG” feeling.Speaking about classes and skills, we stumble upon 4 branches: “might”, “magic”, “order” and “anarchy”. In order to learn advanced skill in some branch, we should first of all gain enough related points. For example: if you want to master “enhanced summoning” you should have 18 points of “magic”. While the character gains the experience in an ordinary way: through the battles and quests - the branch points can be gained only by a particular quest event.For example: in the quest we need to pass through the golems guarding the road. We can simply crush them in battle and gain a 1 point of “might” for it. Or we can find their supervisor mage and ask him for the passage instead, gaining 1 point of “magic” for it.“Magic” opposites “might” and “order” opposites “anarchy”.While such gameplay mechanics look fresh, it was not a good idea. It provides a choice and different ways to complete the same quest, which is good. But in reality you pick the choice guided by the skill you wish to master instead of moral or financial gain.Also while choices between “order” and “anarchy” look more or less equal, for the “magic” and “might” they are not. “Rush into a battle right away” or “summon a squad of magical creatures to aid you”? What kind of idiot would choose the first option?The original “King’s Bounty” gained its name from the character's ability to sense hidden treasures underground. In the new game there is nothing similar. We sweep the world taking everything we can find from barrels, boxes and chests right under the noses of the citizens. Some treasures are hidden in the way you will not notice them unless you are attentive enough, but it is still a simple forage. Maybe it would be better to have some magic artifact, which makes noise while approaching a hidden chest or something.Also we have a lot of puzzles, blocking the way to the quests or treasures. That would be very nice, but they are too simple, like “pull 3 levels in the correct order”. While the game itself “matured” the puzzles seem to be created for the little kids…The storyline is quite ordinary: the great evil from beyond is going to destroy the world. It is absolutely unremarkable, but it is not a crucial part for this game genre.Map is small as well as a story. There is no diversity among the regions: there are no trips to elven gardens, dwarf dungeons or demon worlds. We spend the entire game around the capital, tower of mages and several villages.The battles were done well enough. They are quite challenging, provide different tactics options and sometimes force you to seek a correct solution for the win. If you like turn-based tactic games - you will not be dissapointed.Many people complained over gameplay speed (especially about running speed). I found it to be not a concern. It seems the patches did their job, and game speed is at least “acceptable”. Although I must say that it would be better, if the character simply had a sprint instead of a horse. Another thought: the character should summon a horse and straddle it by a single press of a button, instead of two separated actions, like it is done in “Darksiders”.Despite all the patches the game still contains several bugs. Also during the battles you often encounter strange pauses in 1-3 seconds between turns. It feels like the game “thinks” too long over simple things.Graphic is basic. Can’t say it is bad, can’t say it is good or realistic. For the game, which main feature is tactical battles shown from the height, it is acceptable.There are some glitches like collisions in clothing.Music and sound is unremarkable. I wonder what happened with Lind Erebros...Overall it is 6-7/10. This is definitely not a masterpiece, but I would not call it a failure either. You should not compare this game to the original “King’s Bounty”, but give it a fresh look instead and you may like it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really a King's Bounty game in name only and not much more than that. It seems the developers mostly ignored what made the previous games so much fun and instead opted to make a third person type game in the hopes of making a quick buck off console gamers. There were a number of design decisions made in this game that just boggle the mind completely.....- To begin, the Rage mechanic has been removed from the game completely. That means you are somewhat nerfed if you choose to play as a warrior.- However, you're also somewhat nerfed if you play as a mage, as you no longer regenerate mana. Instead, mana is treated as a limited resource, much like gold. You use it up casting spells and you can then only regain mana from these spell crystals or else in small quantities as rewards for finishing quests or battles or else as random loot in chests.- No more gremlin towers or upgrading of magic items either.- You're railroaded as to where to go as an enemy blocks off an entire road, so you have to fight them to pass. There is no more clever kiting of enemies to avoid fights to get to other areas like in the old games.- You're forced to constantly upgrade your troops as your stacks are limited in size owing to the game having to display each individual member of each stack on the battlefield. For example, I liked to use archers in the older KB games, where you could have a huge number in a stack, limited only by your leadership. Now you can only have a max of 10 archers in a stack, regardless. Some troop types (eg stone elementals) only allow 3 units in a stack! Like the previous KB games though, you're still limited to 5 army stacks max.- The morale system has been changed so that stacks no longer gain bonuses to attack if they have high morale. Instead, each level of high or low morale gives your stacks a flat percentage to either gain a bonus action or miss an action. This is incredibly annoying as for some reason, the bonus action seems to trigger more frequently for the enemies than it does for you. I have had numerous battles where my morale was higher than the enemy forces but my bonus action was hardly ever triggering, yet it triggers for them at least once every round.- As you level up, you choose to gain skills in the ideals of either Finesse (mage skills), Power (warrior skills), Order (paladin skills) or Anarchy. You gain points in these areas by completing quests based on these ideals, eg. you might choose to side with criminals (gain Anarchy points) or the authorities (gain Order points). You need higher points in each ideal to choose the higher level skills within that ideal. This means that in order to optimise your character, you are often forced to choose the ideal that your class skills fall under when deciding how to resolve certain quests, instead of roleplaying your charcter when making choices. Also, a lot of the Power quest options involve engaging directly in battle, which can make playing as the warrior a bit more work.- The story is incredibly dull, so much so that I eventually started looking at the news on my cellphone when yet another wooden-faced NPC was talking to me. Basically you have been framed for the attempted assassination of the king and you're freed from jail and told to investigate something or other at some place called the mage factory, but you're never really given any incentive to particularly care about anything or become invested in the story. After a point, I was only really travelling around looking for the next battle, and even though these take place on a 3D battlefield, the battles in the older KB games were still more fun for me.- The graphics look like something from about 10 years back. There is no day/night cycle, and NPCs will often just stand around staring blankly into space or repeat the same lines of dialogue over and over and over again each time you walk past them.- The control system can't decide on whether you should be using the keyboard and mouse or the controller. Navigating a lot of the menus can be fiddly with the controller, yet it is more comfortable to use when moving around in third person. However, you move pretty slowly either on foot or on horseback, and for some reason, if you use the keyboard to move, you move faster than you do with the controller, so you find yourself constantly switching between the two at times which gets tedious.- Half the game will literally be spent wandering around the countryside or town looking for sacks, crates, boxes, chests and garbage piles so you can find random gold and valuable items which you can sell, as you will need the money in this game to purchase gear and troops. This wasn't a problem in the older games as looting chests was quick due to the isometric view but that is not the case here.I preferred playing as the mage as I normally play as the mage class in KB and her voice acting is probably the best of the three characters. However, she is hampered by limited mana, choice of spells to learn and army size. I eventually reached a point where I couldn't go anywhere else and had to choose between fighting an opponent who was rated as 'deadly' or fighting an opponent who was rated as 'very strong'. I went with the 'very strong' opponent and quit the game in disgust when he kept pelting me with awesome destructive spells and his troops continually kept getting bonus actions for high morale while mine got hardly anything. In summary, this is not a terrible game, but it's not really a good one either. I really wish they had evolved the previous generation of KB games and kept the core gameplay elements instead of going in an almost completely different direction with this one. Pick this up on a steep sale (at least 60% off) or better still, get the older KB games for a pittance now and play those instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Fans of the series will be happy there's a new game, now in 3rd-person 3D-perspective.  Minimal to zero dialogue options, though a few path-decisions primarily used to level-up your character.  The mage is "squishy" throughout, and a decent challenge, though you'd expect the mage to be weak early on and a powerhouse at the end, this is not the case.  You won't be able to max-out your spellbook, which is a shame.  You cannot "grind" either and max-out at level 30, though this is normal from the KB series as there's a limited number of opponent groups to engage and that's it.  No re-spawning enemies.  Even completing every quest and side quest will leave you valuing every turn towards the end.  The blight-trials are non-important, only giving you Maxmillian armor.   A maxx'ed out mage will not be able to have any dragons at the end to fight with unless you focus on law for morale points and then wear morale-building buff armor.  If you play as anarchy/mage you'll struggle every step of the way.  Undead are very weak as well, even with the Necromancer complete armor set.  There's no necromancy spells which is what I was hoping for as I built-up.  The ending is sort of empty like you've failed somehow, even though you complete every quest and collect every treasure hidden in the map.  Music is not as good as the previous KB series, which is a shame.  Wish there were more enemies to fight and a higher level to achieve than 30.  Starting out you'll deal with something like 40 side-quests all jumbled and start to not care about them because you can't reach those locations until much later and forget about them until you randomly talk to someone and enter a dialogue path you weren't expecting.  No choices on dialogue most of the time make the mage seem cold.  NPCs have only a few face differences like Daggerfall, and there's only 1 female face mold-pattern.Still, interesting an adventure to find hidden bits, but it feels a bit unfinished and in the end, I felt empty.  A good 40 - 50 hours of gameplay, though I searched around for a dungeon that didn't exist for about 5 of those until I realized it was a bug/glitch in the inventory.  Wish there was more KB series references too.  No King Cobras?!  Aw.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely not worth the price. I guess it will have a deep sale rather soon or even be in a Humble Choice bundle.One of the tags says "strategy" but there's nothing strategic about KB2. It feels like I'm playing a mediocre TPP RPG rather than a sequel to a brilliant predecessor. Graphics and animations look like 10 years ago, characters are forgettable, the story is nothing special. However the worst offender is UI: it's clumsy, overcomplicated and generally terrible, you can tell it was designed for a controller. Nothing is simple or intuitive, even the simplest action requires multiple clicks and/or key presses (no, you can't play KB2 with just a mouse). I feel like every time I try to do something I need to fight the UI.The strongest part of the game is combat. It's deep and tactical and truly fun. You really need to think and plan your actions or you'll be decimated. However the issue is you only get 1-2 fights per hour, the rest of the time is spent in TPP running boring errands and talking to boring characters.If you're looking for a good sequel to King's Bounty this is not it. If you're looking for a good TPP RPG this is not it. If you're looking for a good, tactical combat this is it, but there's only about 10 minutes of it per hour.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like the assignment you finish an hour before the deadline and submit it unfinished, unpolished and unnecessarily bad.As someone who has 0 experience/exposure to previous King's Bounty games - I came into this game optimistically waiting to be surprised as this was similar to other games I played. Right off the bat, this game does not inform the player the back story at all. Instead you just find yourself released from jail and you have to piece all the information together somewhat halfway through the game. Game mechanics is also terrible with walking at immensely slow speeds with no sprint option. Difficulty of this game is ridiculous as battles within your 5km radius from the moment you leave the jail are overpowered. You are left broke (from losing and buying new troops) and running in circles, finding ways to gain gold through other means such as doing fetch side quests. Stories throughout the quest line are random and voice actors sound like they give no effort. As of now, it seems the decisions you make in-game don't really affect the experience.This game is literally unplayable unless you use mods. It is shocking that a game is priced this high for its current quality.  I would NOT recommend this game for anyone unless the company does a huge do-over. It is an Early Access game AT BEST.3/10

_childDocuments_.review: It's difficult for me to really recommend this game, but I also can't reject it either. Right off the bat I will say the voice acting isn't very good. You can tell a lot of the VA's are amateurish with some standing out more than others. Something else I noticed is that the male character can't use magic (or that's what his class description says) but then there is a talent tree that let's him "spec into" using magic so I don't really get it. Something else I don't like is that the game let's the player choose how to handle certain situations, for example, your first decision will be to either kill some hunters/guardsman harassing some dwarfs for serving a warden and his prison, but the dwarfs say they live peaceful with the humans and trade with them. The hunters/guardsman want to destroy the prison and free the prisoners because the warden is a "bad man" so you have to choose to either kill the dwarfs or kill the hunters. Depending on your actions and approach to situations your character will be "locked into" a morality path. There are four in total, and eventually you won't be able to break your moral code once it's locked in, at least that's what the game claims/states, so this means you can only follow a set path of choices for the rest of the game. Something else I didn't like is that you might HAVE to do something you don't want to do, but you have no choice because your character doesn't have the right moral path or something to do what you want to do, so the game will be like "Oh sorry you can't do that." For example, I encountered some golems on the road. I didn't WANT to fight them, and instead resolve the conflict peaceful, but I couldn't resolve it peacefully because my character didn't know magic and couldn't parley with the mage controlling them, so what was my only option? To fight and kill the golems. It's not what I wanted to do but the game basically didn't give me any other choice. Oh, and you can't choose what your character says. There are no dialogue choices, so you're not really "roleplaying" anything except a moral code I guess? A lot of what your character says is scripted and the only "roleplay" element is deciding how your character might handle certain situations, that is if your character meets skill/moral requirements, which they probably won't. Now I can say the visuals are decent, not spectacular but I had no issues with the game. I'm getting 110 FPS in 1440p resolution with everything set to ultra. Combat seems...simplistic and the animations leave a lot to be desired. It's nothing fancy/over the top, though I'm early in the game, so maybe you get cooler stuff later on. Now something I've noticed is YOUR CHARACTER DOES NOT FIGHT, so I'm not sure what the point of giving him weapons and gear are when he can't actually engage/attack the enemy, maybe I'm not doing something right, but your character is more like a general/commander that gives orders to units on the battlefield, but he can't personally fight. So you can deck him out I guess in fancy shiny armor and give him a cool sword and it's all for show? I hope that's not the case, but if it is then that's a MASSIVE NEGATIVE blow for me personally, not sure why the devs would do that? Overall after the first 40 minutes I considered refunding it or dropping, but kept playing for a bit and it began to "somewhat' grow on me. I suppose I'll keep it and attempt to finish it. I'm not hating the game but I'm also not loving/liking it as much as I thought I would. Some of the other reviews are criticizing the game harshly for what I consider "trivial" things, though my complaints might seem trivial to some as well.
