_childDocuments_.review: King's Bounty II Falls Short: A Disappointing Mix of Technical, Gameplay, and Performance IssuesKing's Bounty II, the highly anticipated sequel to the beloved strategy RPG franchise, has unfortunately left fans and newcomers alike feeling disappointed and frustrated. Despite its promising premise and potential, the game is marred by a myriad of technical, gameplay, and performance issues that significantly hinder the overall experience.One of the most glaring problems lies in the technical department. From the moment players launch the game, they are greeted with a plethora of bugs and glitches that range from minor annoyances to game-breaking issues. Reports of frequent crashes, animation hiccups, and quest-related errors have flooded online forums, leaving players questioning the state of the game's development and release.The gameplay, a critical aspect of any strategy RPG, also suffers from notable shortcomings. The combat system, once a highlight of the series, feels clunky and unpolished in King's Bounty II. Tactical decisions are often thwarted by inconsistent AI behavior, making battles frustratingly unpredictable. Moreover, the game's progression system lacks the depth and nuance that fans had come to expect, resulting in a less engaging and immersive experience compared to its predecessors.Performance issues further compound the disappointment. King's Bounty II struggles to maintain a consistent frame rate, even on high-end gaming systems. The choppy performance not only disrupts the flow of the game but also detracts from the visual splendor that the developers aimed to deliver. Long loading times between scenes and areas exacerbate the problem, disrupting the otherwise immersive world the game attempts to build.While the narrative and world-building elements showcase potential, these positives are overshadowed by the technical and performance hurdles that plague King's Bounty II. The disappointment is particularly palpable for fans who were eagerly anticipating a modern iteration of the classic series. It's disheartening to witness a game with such potential fall short of expectations due to a lack of polish and refinement.In conclusion, King's Bounty II's technical, gameplay, and performance issues significantly detract from what could have been a triumphant return for the franchise. As it stands, the game fails to live up to the standards set by its predecessors and leaves players yearning for a more polished and enjoyable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm mostly reviewing this product because I feel the current review score for it on Steam is woefully low compared to how nice the product actually is. Some of the other reviews for the items go over the flaws for it, and others go over the positives, and I agree with many of them. There are some design decisions which can't simply be patched out, which will be hit or miss depending on your thoughts on the previous games. One such example is unit stacks sizes being limited in battles to account for each stack actually showing the full models of the troops. This means no more peasant mobs with tens of or over a hundred thousand in a mob. Another is that there is a significant amount of backtracking required in some cases, more than the previous games in general. Yet another is that if you don't like the voice acting or graphics as well, it's not like those will be easily patched. Not that I really understand the complaints regarding graphics anyways, but I'm the kind of guy who can play anything from pixel games to Dragon Ball Z Kakarot, or Doom Eternal, and enjoy pretty much all of it. Another small one I don't see mentioned too much is the fact that fights are basically unavoidable - in the older games you could dodge a lot of fights on most maps by simply squeezing by them just right, which let you get to some content earlier than you should have been able to otherwise. This would sometimes let you buy or find an item you wanted earlier, or hire a unit stack that wasn't available on other maps. Fights here have gigantic engagement circles here with no way to bypass them.Many problems that people cite can eventually be corrected in patches or future releases though. The move speed and item pick up issue can likely be patched, such as adding the ability to teleport and pick up items from the horse, and speeding up walking and mounting/dismounting in general. Lack of key rebinding is something the developer is adding as well, for those people who need it. Difficulty levels have been discussed as well, for the people who want to replay the game. The lack of features (rage, marriages, achievement hunting for perks, challenges, item leveling, etc.) can be re-added in future iterations, or DLCs to this game, perhaps standalone versions similar to how Armored Princess had Crossworlds. I can see why this is a negative for some people, they miss those features, and don't want to have to pay more to see them again. The core game play loop is still the same. You wander around solving a main quest, tackle a number of side quests (or don't) in the process, and grow stronger as a leader to field larger, or more powerful armies. You field 5 unit stacks per army in this game, just like the previous games, though the enemy armies tend to always be limited to 5 as well. Properly maneuvering your units can lead to no losses in fights, and even with healing after combat being present it's needed as some unit stacks can outright kill your units through that healing, so trying to go for no loss wins is still highly encouraged rather than brute forcing your way through. There are a variety of battle maps depending on where you're fighting, with most of them actually matching the terrain you're fighting in - if you start a fight in a city, the city itself and all its obstacles are where your units are fighting. Same as when you're in a graveyard, that graveyard is actually where you're fighting. No more teleporting off to a seemingly random background and battlefield layout. The game generally leans toward ranged combatants having more advantageous battlefields, just like the originals, but there are a decent amount where the number of obstacles in the way make using ranged units more difficult. A good number of reviews say it's not worth $50, and I can see why some would think that. For me as long as I'm getting roughly an hour per dollar spent, I find a game worthwhile. Due to the negatives for this game I could see it being better priced in the $30 or $40 range for people who are on the fence. The $50 price tag was fine for me, as I don't mind the lack of features all that much. The game would be better with them, but they're not required. I personally just see this as a starter iteration of the same formula. The engine is in place, they have a great stock of units to move to future releases, a decent level up system, and the battles flow smoothly. It can only get better from here.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; I highly recommend this but at a discounted price. Good but underrated game. Could be great with some more fine-tuning and additional content - which is unlikely to happen. Therefore its not worth the (expensive) full price but at 50+% off its very well worth itI found this the be quite a good game and a lot of fun and believe the mediocre rating is undeserved. The source for the resentment seems to be a) its not like KB1 and b) the initial release was a bit of a mess (but nowhere near as bad as some reviewers make it sound). I consider a) a good thing and for b) a large part of the balance issues and bugs have been fixed. I feel like the developers actually tried to address the majority of criticisms from the first series: The ridiculous stories, the underdeveloped RPG and equipment aspect, the dated graphics and the cheesy gameplay. And - in my opinion - they did fairly well:In the end it is still a strategic battle ground game - more than an RPG - but both aspects are (in my opinion) well done and enjoyable. Unlike the previous KB Games, this one is not easy. (Not a bad thing). This time you can't just kite your way to better stuff, you actually need to have a look at your stats, your equipment and your troop composition. I found this refreshing.Overall, this was genuinely enjoyable. I wish this could have been a next step in the KB series. But the initial release burned to many bridges of goodwill with a really sub-par initial release. Sad, really.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a glorious game that fans of the Kings  Bounty series will find nostalgic and fulfilling. The dry humor and added cheese throughout (e.g. voice acting and characters like Dwayne the Treasure Hunter) are true to Kings Bounty form! The landscapes and surroundings are beautiful. The turn-based tactical combat is a bit updated but similar to the previous games, which was always the meat and potatoes of Kings Bounty games. The roaming/adventuring  RPG element has been updated greatly so that it is now akin to games like The Witcher 3. Is the game flawless? No. For example, the tutorial is lacking, the combat to roaming ratio is unequal, the horse walks worthlessly slow in towns, and you can't interact with people and objects on your horse. But I am sure some of these things will be addressed in patches (indeed the developers have already said the first post-release patch will fix some of these things). Even with its flaws, the game is a joy to play, especially if you are a King's Bounty fan.I am thoroughly enjoying this game. The original Kings Bounty games, which I have clocked hundreds of hours playing, made me fall in love with the turn-based strategy genre. I highly recommend this game to both turn-based strategy and Kings Bounty fans. It delivers.

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to say that under most circumstances I wouldn't recommend this game. It's priced like a triple A title but looks and feels like an indie game. This would immediately preclude it from being recommended until the price was lowered but there are a few things in its favor; there is nothing like this game out there, it is a hodge podge of different gaming experiences all mashed together, it is both a third person open world rpg and a 4x tactical game and it has varying degrees of success actually realizing the potential of both. It is a unique gaming experience but it is hampered by some pretty terrible mechanics like the fact that you will never feel powerful no matter how much you level up, improve your party, or get better equipment and you will have to cheese your way through almost every battle just to barely win. You will pick up swords, spears, wands, maces, and staves but your character just straps it to their back and never uses it throughout your entire gameplay experience. I get it you're a commander and not a common soldier but I feel silly walking around with a legendary sword strapped to my back the entire game that I never draw for any reason. Why even give me a weapon? You are given a horse that is almost useless; it can't run in town and out of town you have to get off your horse every two seconds to pick up random garbage off the ground and interact with things because you can't interact with things while on your horse and it takes two seconds to get on your horse and two seconds to get off. Your horse is one the most annoying features in the game and I feel that If the character that you are playing in game could sprint then the game could be beaten in half the time. The half run half walk thing that your character does also very annoying. It's a good looking game; the background, cities, and even the grass look good but the characters look awful. It's pathetic, there are two faces in the game one for boys and one for girls with the exception of the main characters and a handful of villains. If you have seen two characters in the game then you have seen all the characters in the game because they recycle the same face a hundred times. Very lazy. I have several more gripes about the game but I'm not going to get into it right now as it would seem nit picky. The game doesn't suck, It's a unique experience and can be enjoyable if you are willing to overlook some lazy design problems and game play balancing issues that make you feel as if you were constantly at level one the whole game. Buy it when its on sale because its not worth 40 dollars.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of drawbacks and its not the same King's Bounty that you would expect from Katauri Interactive. But it's certainly has its charm and, most importantly — very engaging and challenging battle system.Cons: - RPG element (exploration, open world, quests) is outdated- Moving around the world is tedious and takes a lot of time, horse is an uncontrollable mess- Awful voice acting (both russian and english)- Writing is mediocre- Same 2 or 3 models for males and females (remember The Witcher 1?)- Interface is designed for consoles and treats KB+M as a second class citizen- Exploration music is ok, but it is bugged — sometimes just stops abruptly and never plays again- Only one battle theme, prepare to listen "catchy" drums track for every 70+ battlesAll of that is overshadowed by amazing battles. Its just that good and engaging, and keeps the challenge all the way to the final boss. If you want an extra challenge — play Katherine (mage).Also the game is quite lengthy, with plenty of side quests which can be resolved in 2 different ways (power/cunning or order/anarchy, and the choice is tied to your skills progression). Overall, if you enjoy TBS games — there is fun to be had here

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, the first hour of the game is a not a good experience. The game starts confusing, no explanation about anything, controls at start seem a little janky and the FPS viewport is not what King's Bounty players would expect. In addition to this, the first 1h is EXTREMELY linear tutorial.All of that could and SHOULD be fixed quite easily by first of all, letting player know it is just the tutorial, give a better explanation on the World and the events to give a motivational driver right from the start. It is given, but only AFTER the tutorial, which makes little sense, since those events are continuously referenced during the tutorialOk, now that that is out of the way. The actual game is actually very good and beautiful. Once you get out of the linear tutorial, the open world aspect of the game opens up. The the diversity of units, their levels (which bring in new abilities) and whole different tier units in each faction is pretty amazing and the FPS view of the game does actually work very well, once you get used to the idea. And some of the views and art is breathtakingly beautiful (just remember to raise your view from the ground from time to time and look around)Biggest problem I've had with the game after the tutorial, which was trash, has been the mount. The mount takes way way too long to mount up and dismount to be bothered with since you can't interact or loot from it. So 99% of the time, you waste more time mounting up than just walking there. Also in the most boring and repeatably visited places, the cities, don't allow you to gallop with the mount! making any visit to town a painful experienceThe actual combats are very well done, diverse and has a lot of tactical hidden depth to them that you might not initially notice, since the combat tutorial is absolute trash and fails to mention NONE of the important combat featuresEspecially when you progress in the game, the combat becomes more and more complex and interesting with more advanced abilities you and enemy have

_childDocuments_.review: If you like HOMM, previous King's Bounty games, or others like it, this is a great addition to the genre. It's a new concept to these type of games. There's an RPG first-person aspect, but then you still get to control your armies with the classic hex style turn-based combat. I have yet to experience a single crash. Ignore all the critical naysayers, this is a very good game and it's obvious so much development time has gone into it.PROS:Amazing voice acting. Whether it's the quest givers themselves or just people idly chatting, there are so many unique voices and they are well done.Combat is great. Plenty of unique characters with unique styles of combat.Graphics. There is so much detail all over the place even on par with games like Skyrim.Quests. They're all unique and typically have good stories. (not fetch X of this)CON:Combat animations and spell animations I feel could have been better.Mana system is weird. You use mana to both learn new spells and to actually cast spells in battle. With a limited supply of mana, the system is awkward. I'm not sure whether to learn new spells sometimes out of fear of how much mana the game will offer me. They should have separated this in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: It`s a good game, which can be very tough, at least on the hard difficulty.I completed the game as the caster, mana is finite (in general and per fight), but so are the enemies.You really have to search and loot the whole map and do all the sidequests to stand a chance, and of course level and pick your army wisely to counter some hard enemies.Keep an eye on that mana, and save at least 300-600 (last third of the game), also scrolls can help to buff before fights and in fights regarding damage etc. Gold is also important, but not that big of an issue, since you can sell loot you won`t need.It`s also used to heal units after fights, which is cheaper vs buying new ones.Each unit can level up 3 times, they only get experience if they survive, but this makes a huge difference cause they gain HP, stats and abilities. They also stay leveld up, if you have to recruit new ones.Last but not least leadership is worth mentioning, it determinates your unit size, you gain it via leveling up, the skill tree (a little) and items - strong units like dragons need a lot of it.Also there are 4 types of unit alignments, to mix and match them, for example undead and humans,you have to invest a few points into the ralated skills, so they won`t get debuffed.I went nearly pure magic, you get pretty powerful at the end, like turning dragons into chickens, summoning strong creatures, or casting two thunderstorms in a row.Story and presentation wise it`s pretty descent for this genre and the replay value is also very high (new character, abilities, units, story decisions). The artwork is good, it plays some nice tunes and the world is well crafted and fun to explore.So are there some negative things?A few i would say - characters are a little wooden and so is the world in general, riding feels stiff and some mechanics are not very well explained. In a sense that you might get stuck if you have low or no mana, or it`s even possible to spec in a wrong way i guess, but you can respec, which costs 10000 gold the first time. Save often - you can also always retreat from battles to search for easier fights to gain a level or two, before a hard boss encounter.I think they balanced it pretty well and if you really watch what you`re doing, the hard mode is rewarding, which is also a good thing - you won`t get a trophy, but it felt too easy on normal mode, which I tried after beating it.I would rate it 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the lack of polish, a really fun B-Tier Open World RPG with challenging Combat!Currently about 40% of the way through exploring the Royal Realm map.TL;DR: If you enjoy Hex Based Combat (Endless Legend, Eador, Wesnoth) and Open World Games (Xenoblade, Amalur) **and** you have a controllerthen King's Bounty is for you! I personally enjoy all types of RPGs. Just keep in mind this isn't by an AAA studio and you are golden.Treat keyboard controls as if playing a game on an emulator and don't use mouse for anything but camera movement.On Price: If you want to support the company and franchise I recommend buying it if you will enjoy this type of game. Watch some lets plays. If you lack money to do so, just wait for the price drop. Not everyone can buy original price for non AAA games, I get it.Pros:1) Amazing world building, world detail, in game lore. (can we re-read in game lore books somewhere)2) Map design is very good, and there isn't too much backtracking. You are rewarded for exploring3) Difficult but fun combat, this game isn't dumbed down. Some may want difficulty sliders though4) Quests are well written compared to other RPGs and remind me of the charm from the previous KB games.5) Game is stable and does not crash on release. Pretty rare for a new game in 2021.  - If the horse collides with you and you can't move, save and reload. If you get stuck in hitbox, wait a bit and it will reset you.6) Developer is reading our feedback which is nicePlease Improve:1) Movement is too slow, horse controls terribly, can't interact while on horse.2) Many things not explained properly or explained incorrectly online. - Mana Overflow (when interacting with first shard) - Talent Reset is NOT free every level up - In battle mana usage won't reduce mana from overworld - How do I level up equipment? Description says equipment can be upgraded - Sometimes unclear new parts of map opened up - What weapon can be used with shield unclear3) UI for PC needs improvements. Army Management, Comparison of Units/Items are very hard to use. We have a mouse, let us use it.4) Why is there no minimap very annoying.5) In battle UI lacks information that could be there since this is PC. For example, active debuffs, health amount, skills and cooldowns.Cons:1) Sometimes a bit hard to traverse invisible wallsIssues other players have reported:1) The mage's personality, I found her tolerable, Paladin has better personality.2) Very high CPU/GPU temperature, supposedly a frame limit fixes this. Does not affect my desktop, but laptop is affected.3) Voice acting is perfectly fine. Previous Kings Bounty had no VO. There are 3 possible main characters. Give the studio some slack.4) There's plenty of battles after the initial tutorial zone and first castle. Tutorial zone has 8 battles (some skippable). There are many different units available too, tutorial section not what the game is like in terms of battle density5) I would've liked stylized fantasy art like in previous KB too but the current art is fine enough.Other:1) Story/lore wise difficult to justify taking Might options2) Interacting with things seems to ignore z-axis (height), can lead to odd teleportation or unexpected actionsHope for Future:1) Please improve QoL so I can enjoy a second playthrough with a different character2) Don't get discouraged, the game is very fun overall.3) More quests?

In short, take the first interactions and 2 battles in Armored Princess, and stretch it out to a 2-3 hour session.Tons of dialogue, story, reading, trying to find nooks and crannies for loot and very little combat. I ONLY recommend yes for people into storytelling NOT for people that liked the previous games and wanted more like myself. Or maybe you're into both, in which case you'll probably love it.The game will get a lot of hate because it's definitely not what fans of the series want, myself included, but my initial impressions are that it's a good game for the right person and someone that has a lot of free time.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game, but do I recommend it to everyone? That dependsIf you liked let's say Armored Princess, well you will be kind of disappointed.A lot has changed in this one, camera is TPP, combat has been rebuilt (there is no rage stat anymore), encounters are fixed to the places ( no more juking the enemies), talent system was completely rebuilt ( no more runes)KB2 has a lot of issues and most of them are actually devs choises, let me describe you how talent system works.When you level up you are getting talent points which you can allocate to one of the 4 different sections of the talents: Order, Power, Anarchy i Finesse.Each of them are divided into 4 tiers and at the beginning you can only allocate point to one of the tiers, you would think that the more points you allocate to the tree, another tiers will open, well not exactly.There is other subsystem that actually counts the points you have in each of the tree (not talent points) and these points are gained by doing quests that usually have choice on how to do them (ex, kill somebody will give you power point, finding what happened will give you order point).This system makes that you stop playing according to your beliefs, but what you actually need to open up new possibilities in the talent tree and although I appreciate the idea, it is implemented in such way that it actually hinders gameplay.Another thing is movement and UI.Although movement is just kind of clunky and slow, it does not fit for mouse and keyboard, it was designed for controller in mind, that not bothers me that much.UI on the other hand this is just kind of bad, as again this was desinged for console and wasn't properly ported to PC.Simple things like hovering cursor over unit, does not show you information, you have to click everything to gain information, double clicks usually don't work too, as ceratin actions like equiping or comparing items are bound to buttons.Honestly this can be simply fixed, as a QOL patch to accomodate this game better for PC.Last one complain, game lacks in explanation department.There are a lot of moments in this game where you are wondering ex. why my archers cannot go past 10 units in the stack. Well I have enoguh leadership for 2 more, but game doesn't allow you that, as maximum number per stack is 10.If you played previous games, most of the concepts will be known to you, but even I had an issues with some things and had to basically guess why game is treating something in a particular way.Now for the goods.Game has it's heart in the right place, just like KB:Legend (I think that one was polished better) this has good base for future endevours.Some are saying that graphics are not that great, I honestly like them, there are nice vistas, fantasty style is a bit on a generic side sometimes, but world is really nice.Exploration is big in this game, sense of wonderment is something that I really love and this one delivers on that front.Combat, although this was changed, as right now there is no Rage stat, combat is much more tactical and you cannot just build a super army with OP units and just expand it when you have leadership, which eliminates stagnation in the build.Fights are tailored to the environment, as they are fixed to the positions, each battleground is different and each one offers something unique.Overall I think that KB2 is bold step to a different direction, is that direction better? Not neccessarily, but that doesn't mean that Game is bad.I recommend it maybe in the later stages of it's lifecycle, when some of the bugs and issues will be fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: 1) This might be a disappointment for 60, but if you can get it around 30, its a worth the price. 2) No its' not "same-old just better graphics" (go play EA games for that), it's a reimagination of series;  core aspects remain the same and are improved.2a. 3 gender locked classes, offerring 3 differrent playstyles. (it would be nice to be able to pick between M/F but not needed.) It as it was in previous games, and no, you wont be able to get all the best things on 1 character (this aint skyrim). Picking a path and keeping it is highly encouraged. It is also improved by  a morality/faction system.2b.  Units  belong to 1 of 4 differrent factions, and while you can mix them up, it wont be optimal and affect their combat capabilities. (which is again, the same as in original  KB series). Upon tiering up (1-3)  they spruce up their appearance and gain new skills (it would be nice to see greyed out unlockable unit skills to see if theyre worth  leveling up tho). Endgame (T5)units unlockable via quest chains so you wont miss out based on your rp choices ^^2c. Hero upon leveling up gets  skillpoints, so you can actually somewhat mold it  the way you like (it wasnt a thing before)3. Creature models and animations are beautiful (love gryphons, gargoyles and dragons-beautifully delivered mass of creature); world is pretty albeit..artificial feeling, especially the flat sky.4. Horse..is there( bcs you always had a horse older games  I guess) but not really needed as you will most likely run on foot to loot all or use teleportation stellas. Its nice to ride around, and like in any other  game, requires some getting used to. Bigger issue is invisible walls, no ability to jump (i got stuck on rocks so much), and shift-to-walk (please make it a toggle instead.) You only actually need  walking on 1 quest..so just why?

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of King's Bounty and Heroes of Might And Magic series, I've to say that, this game should never have been called King's Bounty. What was the developers' goal? To confuse fans of the previous installments? It was pretty well done. Attract new players? Barely. I suspect they've gathered more complainers with this game than fans. No wonder.I hated it because:- Unrelentingly slow character movement.- You have a horse, which is often teleported into the middle of an obstacle by the engine.- Moving around town on a horse is exactly as slow as walking.- It is horribly unoptimized. In 4k resolution with Ci7 10700, 32 GB 3200 MHz, SSD, 3070 TI OC, this game is inhumanly chugging, loading, jerking, while drastically more beautiful and modern games run beautifully on this PC.- What they did to the combat is bloodcurdling. For example, you can't attack from another direction you are facing your opponent in a TBS game? Are you guys normal? What is wrong with you people?- They took out a bunch of stuff from the previous parts that worked well, e.g. rage, diplomacy, faster moving on the map, better view while in combat, etc.- There are 2 maps, of which the first one is the tutorial and the main map. And that's it! The whole game can be beaten in 30 hours, which is half the playing time of the previous parts, while being open at the price of AAA games.- It's irredeemably annoying that you can put only one marker on the map and you can't write anything on it!- It's silly that there's no "fog of war" on the map, so you have no idea where you have and haven't been.- After a while - even if you have a very high leadership skill -, you can't have more than 10 of even the lowest ranking friendly units! Now imagine a big army with 10 archers. Ridiculous.- It wants to be an RPG, but it doesn't suit it very well, because the whole world is disturbingly static. A lot of times you see NPC characters standing still and looking at the wall. Or vendors you can never, ever speak a single line to, the trade screen comes on immediately.- Under every wretched bush the game forces you to look under, because that's where barrels, crates, bedpans, spittoons, trash cans are hidden, containing gold and jewellery, and sometimes even equipment. It's simply ridiculous that the saviour of the world is not on the road, but on the side of the road in the nettle shed. - Tons of species and units are missing, which were there in the previous episodes, thus guaranteeing enough variety.- 1-2 skills are a bit broken. This is most embarrassing when used on you. E.g. I' ve a unit taunted, but it's surrounded by terrain and enemy, ergo it can't move towards the unit issuing the taunt, ergo it should attack the unit in its way. Well, they don't! You can't do anything with it, unless you have a debuff.- On the map, it says "battle". You put the mouse/arrow on it, and? And? Nothing. You can't see the opponent's unit, you don't know how strong they are, there's no skill, no item, no nothing. The only way to find out is to charge at it, then refuse to accept the battle, and back away from the battle. Why wasn't the old, perfectly working solution good???- Pretty wobbly balance.- Kindergarten level puzzles.- It drives me crazy that I get stuck on a lot of things! I don't even understand why the hell my character can't jump a branch?- Despite the colourful appearance, the overall effect of the game is somewhat reminiscent of the 2010s, and I mean that in the most serious way!- The textures are incredibly low quality in many places.- Rare, very forgetable music.- Lots of same character model.I loved it because:- It's been a long time since Dark Side... shock, but it's been 7 years! Ergo, we were really starved for a King's Bounty episode and this is trying to be it in traces.- Colourful high-fantasy look.- Quite a fair look in places.- Can be controlled perfectly with a controller, finally no need to crouch in front of the screen, you can play it lying down.- I dared to bet that it would be filled with nothing, but silly fetch quests and luckily I was wrong. There are quite fair missions in it, with multiple outcomes and even choices.- The issue of attitude is interesting, although you can very quickly find yourself in a situation where your character refuses to take a particular path, saying it is far from their character. Ok, but it's supposed to be a kind of ROLE PLAYING GAME, let me decide what I want!This is not a King's Bounty game! It's a mediocre TBS-RPG game, that if they hadn't stuck the King's Bounty name on it, no one but a narrow group of people would bother with it. This direction, in this form, is a serious mistake, a fatal error! Say goodbye the designer, he was clearly unfit for the job.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished my first playthrough of the game and here's what I have to say about it:Pros:-The gameplay and mechanics are fun and rewarding. Ultimately, this is a game of strategy and resource management and every aspect of the gameplay lead to decision making which create consequences and opportunities.-The story is, I would say, reserved. There aren't any wonky crazy characters that are vying for attention a la Dragon Age. Each of the 3 characters you can choose from are characters who want things and as such quest taking is transactional for the most part. Why should I help you? You can supply my army with trolls? Okay, sounds like a fair deal. You have to balance what you lose by undertaking a sidequest with what you hope to gain from it.-The morality system within is particularly interesting. Essentially for the first half of the game, you can make choices for your character until your character is a 'character' such that they make their own decisions later on.-The voice acting is good. Nothing fantastic, but not distracting either. I played the count of Rigern as my first playthrough and she was very well voice acted but I can't say anything about the other two.-The world is big and jampacked with things to do, decisions to make, people to talk to. All of the quests are connected to each other in one way or another.-With how many troops there are to recruit from the 4 main factions, differing equipments and the 3 main characters, there is a lot replayability within. My first runthrough had me specializing in long range elementals with spells to augment how much damage they did. My next one will probably be an aggressive dwarves and trolls in your face sort of playthrough.-I have encountered a grand total of zero bugs, gamebreaking or otherwise-When you start a battle the arena is one that is within the environment, not a separate instance.cons-the graphics look a little bit outdated and the animations are wonky at times.-there is very little handholding and it is completely possible to make poor decisions in the beginning that softlocks you out of the game.-sometimes you will have to go back to places you have gone before to re-up on your army and you only have your memory for help if you can't remember where a certain piece of armor or a given unit resides.Ultimately, for me, this game is worth the price and then some. I have a lot of fun strategizing my army and playstyle and managing my resources for the next battle. The graphics are a bit eh, but I'm here for the gameplay anyway.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally giving up on this. Although most everything has already been said, I decided to add my voice to the reviews because, even though I think this is a veritable car crash, it may not be entirely irredeemable. As things stand, very little of it works:- The over-the-shoulder, walking simulator would have been unnecessary even if it worked (speed, pathing and all the problems others have explained in detail). It is quite obviously a time filler as the game is actually quite void of substance (battles, units etc.). Obviously this cannot be chucked away and the engine will be like something the 00s threw up. Maybe just speed it (WAY) up, allow for travel to landmark posts from anywhere etc. - One of the best parts of the original series (constructing armies that evolve in size/capability, over time), has been killed. Again the details have been covered in depth. A curious point to completely miss, as it  one of the three core pillars of the original games. There are not enough units, not enough to recruit and the new leadership mechanic has rendered leadership irrelevant. As I always play the leadership-oriented character first, this has particularly damaged my experience. However -and crucially- this should be rather easy to fix. Of course it will require a ground-up rebalancing but, well, I don't think this was ever done in the first place anyway.- Following from the previous point, not only there are curiously few battles, all things considered, in the world, their difficulty gradient is bizarre. You may have a horrendously difficult one blocking a side of the map, followed by a trivial one there. Another one that is an utter miss, but could be easy to fix. This links to the next point on combat.- I think the combat mechanics engine has all that is necessary for a successful system. However, it is rather obvious that it was not playtested, ahem, thoroughly (to be kind). This is especially jarring in the "Trials" missions but obvious everywhere. It is exacerbated by the lack of replacements, which means that, if you have any favourite units, you have to win with zero losses. Again - and this is the theme of my review-, a miss; but not an unfixable one.- The items/suites of equipment. Another hallmark of the series, another embarrassing miss. They are awful. Not only there are very few of them, completely gone is the dynamic of different suites enabling different styles. I think they are also going for a "bonus/malus" system which is very unrewarding. You have probably guessed what I will say next: Complete miss but, again, not unfixable.- The story is actually not bad. Could even get into it although I have minor ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with how it has been implemented. However, not happy with the attempt to link story choices to earning points towards the skill tree branches. These choices feel incredibly forced. - Following from the previous point, the skill tree is rather interesting. But I would have liked greater ability to mix and match without the aforementioned railroading. It also feels stingy and I will not stick around any more to find out how much of it you can actually access on a single play-through. Again my perception is somewhat biased by the fact that the leadership section of the tree (as everything else) is rubbish. - A curious interlude: You may have picked that I felt, throughout my playthrough, that my selection of path/character (Leadership) was particularly bad. Have seen some others say the same about their (different) choice. Could be just personal bias, or it could be that the others are worse than I think!Overall, there is a theme in the reviews that the game feels rushed and unfinished. It certainly felt that way to me, as well. Some design choices are simply wrong, in my view, and that cannot be helped. However, there may be enough here to salvage a series that many of us loved and would see credit done to. My recommendation is to stay away from it until a serious overhaul (which I would likely be very disappointed, and would not touch, if it appeared as an -expensive- DLC).As a last generic point, more to myself, this was the first time - in a long time- that I pre-ordered a game. I was THAT confident (last time I think was the Fallout76 debacle). So maybe I jinxed it and its all my fault. Definitely not worth preordering anything these days and it's mistake I will not make again.

_childDocuments_.review: A good take on the series though it is different.Pros:•	Yay TBS combat•	Sound effects are nice•	Varied monsters•	Mostly voiced•	Majority of the text notes are brief and enjoyable•	Less snowball due to maximum unit over all cap•	Nice world visuals•	Lots of find-able skill points for the rather large passive tree•	Interesting take on the moral system that doesn’t push the player, at least not via gameplay•	Revolutionary map lotting system that notes down exploration loot that you were close to but didn’t grab, other game dev’s need to learn from this.Cons:•	Movement speed far too slow•	Units have no sprint animation in combat•	Voice acting is good but the voice itself feels out of place often•	“Legendary” equipment seems to outnumber common in variety•	“Trials” fights are far too tedious, I may be doing something wrong•	RIP couple at the MageFactroty :’(•	Need more content, there is a lot here but I demand moreOver all the gameplay direction does feel lacking compared to its previous instalments in the series but this is likely a player bias due to having fond memories of the originals.P.S. to the Dev team:For the love of god release expansion packs that continue the story and allow me to expand on my progress I'm happy to pay full game price for such expansion. DLC that requires a new character are a hard NO from me, I will hard pass until a few months have gone by and enough people said same volume of content is present. - do not kill this potentially amazing instalment by doing what Spell Force 3 did, they did not learn from why spell force 1 & 2 were so good with their expansions.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, I pre-ordered the game and when I read all the negative reviews I was depressed but decided to give it a try anyway. What I found is an enjoyable game which is entirely a King's Bounty game unlike what most of the negative reviews claim.Comparison and responses to common complaints:No character customisation: There wasn't any in any previous titles and in this one your appearance actually changes based on what you equip making it a step up.Graphics are bad: They're not really, sure it's not going to tick an epic beauty box but neither did the previous titles and it's a lot prettier than they were.Horrible console port: I'm not really seeing it, ok there's no quick save which is a little annoying and I guess if you really like a unique keyboard remapping option then you're going to be disappointed but for your standard wasd and mouse it's fine.Camera angle omg how could they: Like seriously? It's got a 3rd person view instead of the top down, gosh how will we survive? It doesn't really take away from the game for me at all. you can adjust the camera in combat basically it's like the change from heroes of might and magic 3 to 4 in a slightly more 3d view and the addition of more terrain all of which is good for me.No run option: And? you move fine on foot for short exploration and quickly on horse to get to places, it also has fast travel, I'm someone who really doesn't like walking simulators but this feels like it's been balanced quite well.Voice acting and writing: Voice acting is fine, it's not LOTR but meh the other titles didn't have any voice acting at all so hard to complain, the writing is also fine, it's like people don't remember the other titles and what they were like, it's always been a little cliched and tongue in cheek making fun of the fantasy genre and to be honest the writing in Dark Side was truly horrendous so this is a step up again.Combat speed: yeah it could be faster and that's an option I hope they add.The game itself is what I expected and personally I find it very enjoyable, gone is the need to constantly 'dig' the terrain to find treasure chests, loot is highlighted as are interactables all of which is good, the atmosphere is well created and feels like you're walking through a freezing winter land for instance. I haven't encountered a single bug yet which is always a plus on release, what's really going to make the difference for me is how mod friendly the game is going to be, the other titles were not so much so I hope that's changed. I think the people leaving this horrible reviews should indeed go back and play the older titles for a comparison because I think they've forgotten what they're really like, to me it feels like a lot of things have been improved and a good successor to the series (I played both Crossworlds and Dark Side again last month and while I still enjoy them I'm making some comparisons on recent experience rather than rosy glasses from a few years ago).

_childDocuments_.review: King's Bounty two introduced a 3D third-person world into the HOMM-adjacent turned-based combat formula. The original King's Bounty games are 2D and at first I wasn't sure the transition to 3D would work. Well, it does. I like it. You are much more immersed in the world and have the added benefit of character building and voice acting as a benefit. Bottom line- buy this game. It's good. If I were to quibble, a few mechanical improvements would help: recruitment directly to your reserves and the ability to see specific buffs and debuffs from the battlefield instead of the detail card. You are left to infer how to best match spells and the 4 affinities to counter specific armies. That's not all bad. I found a couple of the puzzles have no hints or are vary difficult without a hint, but others quite enjoyable and you can piece together- so some balance would help. I greatly look forward to additional story chapters as I have completed the campaign and side quests. This is a really fun game and is a no-brainer to anyone who likes this formula.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing almost 20 hours and the game just came out a couple days ago so I think it's time for a review. Clearly I like it. Is the game good? Eh...yeah, it is.Is the game great? Nope. Not by a long margin.Is it a good successor to other King's Bounty games? Nope again.But it's a good game on its own. Hear me out:To enjoy KB2, you have to NOT compare it to other KB games. I haven't played the "original" King's Bounty, but I've played all 4 spinoffs. From what I understand the original game was much closer to the 4 spinoffs than to this game, but that's neither here nor there. This game is nowhere NEAR being like the 4 spinoffs. If that's what you want, you will be sorely disappointed. Therefore, I'm judging KB2 as its OWN game, and when you do that, it actually isn't that bad.Leeeet's do this.Difficulty: 9/10 (Hard)For my first run through the game, I think the game is sufficiently difficult. I think it should have multiple difficulties, but for having only one, it's fine. You can't go into a battle and just randomly click and hope to win. It won't work. You can't go into battles with you roster only like half filled. Won't work. You need to fill your roster, then think during the battle. I like that.Graphics: 7/10 (Okay - Good)The graphics are nothing that are going to make you say "wow, this is the most beautiful game ever made!" but they're not terrible, either. There are a LOT of games I get turned off by just by seeing the graphics, and this isn't one of them. They work for what the game is. You can see things easily in the overworld, and the camera is very easy to manage and see around (if you first start off by making it MUCH less sensitive). During battle, the camera is *mostly* ok, and the graphics and animation are appealing.The game looks like somebody started making it in 2012 and never updated the graphics. That's probably the case. Oh well. It's fine. I have no problem with the graphics.Price: 4/10 (Not worth the price unless you're bored. Wait for a sale if you can.)This game is WAY too expensive. At launch, it was $50 US with options for $55 and $60. This is like an "A" grade price, while the game deserves a "B-". The game should be about half that price; $25 to $30 would be fair, in my opinion. I got the $55 version of the game on a third party website for roughly $40, with no tax. I still think I overpaid, but I was bored waiting for New World to come out (which was recently delayed an extra 4 weeks). This will give me something to do until that comes out! :PGameplay: 8/10The gameplay is OK. It's a turn-based RPG but with more of a story and exploration focus than battles. You run around a map in 3rd-person as your chosen pre-made character. You can chose a male warrior, female paladin, or female mage.You run around the map, talking to people, picking up and advancing quests, picking up loot, and buying items and units. Whenever there's a place for a battle, it's often marked ahead of time and even if not, you have the option to back out before actually fighting. You can go do whatever else you want and come back later if the fight is too hard right now.You have about a dozen item slots or so with which to equip yourself with various gear. Units are from 4 different "factions" -- Order, Anarchy, Might, and Finesse. They have higher morale with their own factions, and less with others.You can learn various spells to cast on the battlefield. The mage can learn stronger spells sooner, and has more mana available during battle. The warrior has stronger units, but less spells. The paladin is in between, but has MORE units.When you get into a battle, you start on the opposite end of your enemy on a somewhat-small hexagonal board, and take turns moving units, attacking, using abilities, spells, etc. You have 5 different units which are stronger the higher your "leadership" stat is. When you level up, you get more leadership and points for passives that you can put into Order, Anarchy, Might, or Finesse.Game length & Replayability: 8/10 (semi-long game, somewhat replayable)I haven't finished the game, so take this with a grain of salt, but it seems pretty big. If you take the time to explore everything, talk to people and actually pay attention instead of rush the dialogue, and do all the battles, the game should be quite long. There's some replayability because of 3 classes and also the fact that you can go a different route with quest options for each game, but playing a second time some things might seem tedious. I'm also not really sure how much "randomness" there is, compared to previous titles.Story: 7/10 (Pretty decent)Here's the story: You were in prison for a crime you didn't commit, but now there's a darkness called "The Blight" coming and the prince orders your release from jail to help him with it. I've only played as the mage but I understand the paladin and warrior are quite similar. The mage is a snobby, arrogant countess. I don't much like her personality, I just wanted to be a mage. *shrug*Bugs: 9/10 (Very few, if any, bugs. No bad grammar [English version], no crashes.)Yes, I put grammar and bugs in the same category. Despite this being a Russian-made game with a history of bad grammar.......I've not seen ANY grammatical errors, which is impressive. The game is FULLY voiced in English, as well as other languages too. I've heard of others crashing or running into minor bugs. I haven't crashed. I've lagged a couple times after long play sessions, but relogging fixed it. (Only twice in like 20 hours.) And I hear there's an exploitable bug but easy to just ignore. Hopefully that gets fixed soon.UI & Controls: 6/10 (Mediocre, at best)Here's a part where this game lags behind. The UI isn't great, but bearable. The controls, however, are abysmal. This probably isn't the first time you've heard this (unless mine is the first review you've read, in which case, that's awesome!) but it's no secret that the speed at which you "run" (and, yes, it IS running, not walking) is super slow. The horse is THE SAME SPEED in town, and BARELY faster outside of town. Plus the summon animation takes forever, and it can't turn around real well, can't go backwards, gets stuck easily, etc. The game really needs some polish in this area.You also can't change the camera angle in battle, and some battles have a bad angle. :-\I've also heard that changing the keybinding doesn't even work, though I haven't tried.Hopefully some of this is fixed soon. I might eventually edit this part of the review if it is, but if I don't change it don't get mad. xDVerdict: Worth a buy, if you have nothing else to play and you're bored. You must REALLY like story and exploration, as they dominate over actual battles in this game. Keep in mind, also, that battles are turn-based AND difficult, so if that's a problem for you, then yeah.

_childDocuments_.review: Based on my first impressoins, the game is not bad per se. But it's lacking in almost every aspect I could try hands-on with my limited time. in the exploration sections are clunky. Walking speed is agonisingly slow, which doesn't stop your character from bumping into random objects from time to time, and the horse riding, while faster, is just awkward. Also, there're bugs.  I mean, I literally had to restart the game when I stuck in the room and couldn't open the door to get out 'cause the interaction button wouldn't respond even after rebinding. It's the first time I had something like this in years, which says a lot. itself leaves a lot to be desired. I don't even know if I could really call it that. The map is pretty much a corridor with some short branches here and there, with side quests/battles or just some loot. And, as far as I know, it stays this way for the rest of the game. Which is a shame, to be honest. is unimpressive to say the least. Half the abilities, at least by their description, are pretty basic and not that interesting, and the fact that they're locked behind your characters' alignment hurts roleplaying aspect of the game pretty badly, because now you're forced to make some choices just to be able to get desired upgrades. feels bland and boring, be it notes, side quests or even main story. There's a lot of info and name-dropping, characters talk about something I have literally no idea about, and that's just not how you make audience interested in your stories. I've spent one hour on it and I still don't even care about what's going on besides "when will I get the next battle". And don't even make me started about the aforementioned moral choices, which are just far-fetched and artificial - the ones I've seen at least. are the only aspect of the game that I liked. It's pretty straightforward, easy to get into, and there're no surprises, good or bad. It's fine, if only a little bit on the easier side, without any way to change the difficulty, and I could see myself enjoying it, but everything in between fights is just an unpolished mess that I can't ignore no matter how hard I try.So, all in all, it's an okay game if the tactical element is the only thing you're interested in, but not right now and definitely not for the full price. Wait for sales and maybe a couple of patches before buying it. If you're looking for something more, then you'll be better to look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I would like to recommend this game I just cannot.- The game feels and plays like cheap RPGs from early 2000- In comparison to the previous entries in the series, the game is not divided anymore into multiple maps and different regions. Now, the game consists of only 2 maps: tutorial map (extremely small - 2 or 3 hours long) and the main one (medium size). Overall, the game seems to be much shorter than any other King's Bounty game (even Armored Princess)- All fights are now scripted - you cannot escape from enemies (and by "escape" I mean that they often stand in your way, so you will have to fight them sooner or later; however, you can still withdraw from the battle before it begins)- As all of the fights are more or less scripted, all of them need to to be tackled in a very specific order. Of course you can still fight with tougher enemies and win, but the losses are not worth it. You also cannot fight random enemies to level up. The only viable way to level up is questing- RPG dominates over the strategic layer - I have played this game for around 5 hours and I have only fought 5 or 6 times. There is definitely too much running around- RPG elements are also quite lacking. The skilltree is simple and almost entirely based on our choices during quests.  I also find it ridicolous that I have to act against my own will during the quests just to get the skills I want- There is a very small amount of usable equipment- Tactical fights also seem much more bland and boring when compared to other strategic games. Also, they now look more similar to the Age of Wonders series (multiple units instead of one representing the whole unit)- The game also feels like it should be at least twice as big, mostly due to the slow plot and character progression (I really hope for the DLC with the additional third map with much more fights). And by slow progression I mean gaining three skillpoints and using all of them to increase the damage of our units by 0,8%. Hooray- Performance is terrible, especially considering the fact that the game just does not look THAT good- Multitude of glitches, graphical bugs and issues with draw distance- With the latest patch, they have introduced difficulty levels (after "just" over half a year...). However, if someone already started a game before the release of the patch, they still cannot adjust difficulty - in order to do so, you need to start a completely new game. <sarcasm> Great idea </sarcasm> [!UPDATE: It seems that the difficulty slider has been finally added in options and can be changed while already playing]- Default difficulty is also completely off. I can imagine that veterans will feel its too easy, but beginners and people who played only some turn based strategy (including me) will find this game hard or even irritating at times (especially "trials" with pre-defined heroes and armies)- I also "love" models for "kids" (shrinked adults - I really hope that was supposed to be a joke - check refugees camp after doing the quest for them) or teenagers (normal adult model with peasant-like moustache voiced by the guy over 40 who tries to sound like minor)+ Still, the game is quite fun to play. I enjoy this slow speed which allows for more thorough exploration+ Stronger emphasis on story (sadly, it is mediocre at best)+ Soundtrack is nice, especially the main theme+ Although extremely linear, the exploration is quite rewarding+ Graphics are ok, nothing spectacular but alright+ Voice acting is decent (at least in my opinion) + all of the dialogues are now voiced+ Both the interface and the overall game's structure seem to be well done and they are quite clear, even for the new players+ Moreover, the game still is a quite unique blend of RPG and Tactical Strategy+ Main characters seem to be quite diverse (sadly, they do not influence the main plot in any way)But all things considered, the game is still extremely inferior to any other King's Bounty game and it requires immense amount of good intentions to accept its numerous flaws.Also, right now, it resembles more Ascension to the Throne game than any KB game.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished the game with the Mage.The game is not finished in a lot of ways, especially the ending. It seems like they rushed the game to sell it, because if you look at the characters and other stuff it's copy paste (for example every character has the same face but with different hairstyle and clothes).The most of the time is running from point a to b for quests.The spells especially the damage ones are most likely powerless, so you use only support skills to win the fight.Most of the spells you will get is in midgame and late game, so you are running min. half the game with apprentice spells.The Influence/Power/Fame/Glory, i don't know what's called in english ingame, you need for units are pretty high, so you will have some tough fights early and mid game.You can get stuck on ground stuff like bushes, stones or other stuff (treasure spots for example) so you need to load the game to save yourself. because the mount (horse) is too stupid to get to you.The mount at the moment is nearly useless, because it's not really faster than yourself + you have teleportpoints/waypoints that you can use.The puzzles are totaly boring especially in the endgame/late game.The scryer Trials are useless, because you need to do a fight with a special character + units and use 1 strategy to finish it. The rewards are set pieces that bring more bad stuff than good except you have the full set.The performance/optimization could be better.In fights there is some problems with range units, for example the enemy has his ranged behind the infantry and you do the same, he can attack your range unit with his, but you don't. Then you can't see sometimes if you are on a higher position than he is.I'm missing some old spells from the first kings Bounty games. The skillsystem is completely different and worse, because most of the passive stuff is not useful at all or give you a good bonus to make a change in fights + you need to fullfil a lot of quests with markers like sword, dagger/flag, book and scroll to get points in this tree to learn something. (max. level is 30 and you can nearly 2 trees)There are not enough fights and the normal fights/skirmishes that are in this game take a lot of space. So if you wanna skip them to fight them later is most of the time not possible.Now that i mentioned the bad stuff, i will tell you about the good stuff:Dialogs and story is for now pretty good, even the writings are nicely done.The graphics are pretty good (depends on taste).Music and sounds are nice.You can decide if you wanna be the good guy or an ass, but i don't know if it change the story.That's all. They told us to fix and change a lot with the first patch and that we get an ending, but we will see.In it's current state i can't recommend this game at all, because it's not really finished and has to many flaws.My personal opinion for the developers is that you shouldn't have gone to 3rd Person so you could have created a better looking king's Bounty 1 with animation for talking with people.

_childDocuments_.review: Its not a bad game, but it not a good game either. By no means don't spend more then $15 on this. I'm pretty sure the writting is meant to be be corny, so its not for everyone. I played the game on normal 80% of the game and its pacing was pretty good, where you will have to go back and fight lower level/side quests before moving on and it was pretty challenging. The sticking point of the game is that i went into this completely blind and read no wiki's, because i wanted to enjoy it and there lies the problem. If you go in blind and just start playing, on normal, you will run into a giant road block. The game has choices and those choices matter, weather it be story choices or party makeup. I got to a point in the game where I had No side quests available and 2 main quests that were impossible (based on game choices). And then everything after that point was full hard mode where i couldn't play the game on normal. Its as if the game dev got hard pressed and made eveyrthing hard mode. The fact of the matter is unless you know about the game before hand you will need to play on easy to just enjoy the game. Lastly there is set gear in the game. Most of which is tied to quests. Those quests don't tell you there is a gear reward and here is the problem. The gear is randomized and weighted toward your build setup at the time. My problem is that at that time I was picking gear to make thing works so my gear was all over. In the end I wasn't able to get a full set of set gear. I think there are about a dozen of them. I did every quest in the game and it was 35 hours, with about 5hrs on the area of being stuck. if you like these types of games and you want something to keep you busy on long weekend. This is not a bad choice if on sale for about 15ish

_childDocuments_.review: For those who are looking for the very same Kings Bounty in this game, there is little left of it here, except perhaps turn-based combat. I can't say it's bad, the game just got different.Not quite a lot of problems - poor optimization (if you take into account the level of graphics), all kinds of non-critical bugs (you can get stuck in textures, the battle may freeze, etc.), a small variety of factions and units (compared to previous parts), a small number fights (here, again, when compared with previous games in the KB series), NPC conversations among themselves, which do not change throughout the game and start to annoy.Of the benefits - interesting fights, beautifully drawn units and magic (by the way, there are a lot of them, but there are a lot of spells similar to each other); not a bad main plot, there were a couple of interesting side quests; a fairly large but sometimes empty world.Conclusion:The game is not bad, especially if you like turn-based strategies and most of the shortcomings can be closed released a large DLC with new units and a continuation of the story. But so far it's a 6 out of 10 for me. I really hope that the developers will take into account their mistakes and release a DLC in which they will correct them.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't listen to the review bombs with less than 2 hours played... I'm a huge fan of all the original Kings Bounty games! The change to 3rd person is a bit shocking at first, but I have really enjoyed the change! The run speed is really slow, but they have a patch coming to fix that soon! The game starts off in a cloudy, snowy, linear tutorial area. Which hurts the graphical look, as there is a lack of HDR lighting here. The slow pacing and linear flow of this tutorial goes against the FEEL of the original Kings Bounty games. So I understand why people are thrown off at first.Give it a few hours! Once you get to the main city. The game is graphically gorgeous. Opens up into a sandbox open world full of choices. You get a ton of customization options around every corner. And the battles get more and more interesting. Your armies will evolve, and the game quickly starts feeling like a Kings Bounty game! It's a bit of a slow burn at first! You NEED to get through 4+ hours to start feeling that original kings bounty take shape. It's a bit of a shame that people are jumping in, playing for 1 hour, then refunding it... _childDocuments_.review: I think this game is borderline exceptional.  I just finished my first run through the game, it took about 70 hours as a Mage focused on Order/Magic (Fire/Earth).  I took my time, I listened to all the random conversations NPCs had throughout the world, I hunted for all the various hidden treasures, and I generally had a blast.  I've seen a lot of complaints about money being too rare (it's not if you search for hidden treasures), and I've seen a lot of complaints about the game being too difficult, specifically the trials (They are challenging), and I just disagree.  I think it hits a sweet spot of challenge and exploration.  I own every King's Bounty game, and I feel this was a superb effort at bringing the IP into the modern age.  Is it the same game as before?  No.  But, there are already five superb versions of that style of game with infinite replayability.  I had high hopes going into this game, and for once, it didn't disappoint.  This felt like King's Bounty mixed with Elder Scrolls, and I'm ok with that.  I love the King's Bounty combat system, and I love the ability to explore a huge world in typical RPG fashion.  So, I thought this game was a smashing success, and I'm going to immediately play through it again.That being said, I do have some nitpicks:1)  The horse takes too long to mount and dismount, and the turning around is awful.  Also, not being able to ride full speed through towns is tedious, as is not being able to buy/sell while mounted.2)  The tutorial could be better.  The descriptions on items could be better.  I horded a lot of sell loot because some said "Trash and sell it", while others did not, and it seems random in retrospect.  I had no idea if future quests would require some of the loot (they did not).  It worked out hordeing the items though as later in the game you can acquire armor sets that increase what merchants will buy items for, so best to horde things if you can.  Also, the mana crystals were a little fuzzy early on, whether you should click them or save them for later (just click them as you see them).  And while mana was never an issue for me (I finished the game with over 5000), it might be nice to let people know in the tutorial that it can be limited and spells in each battle use up your overall pool as does upgrading spells.3)  Not a fan of the hard limit on some army units even if you have enough leadership to get more.  It's part of the strategy (or should be) to choose to focus on leadership to have larger units.  I feel this was a misstep.  4)  The ending of the game.  Huh?  What?  While cool to go listen to some of the conversations NPCs were having with each other after the fact, not having an actual ending is pretty odd.  I assume content packs and/or expansions will fix this one though.  Everything leading up to the end and the final fight was rock solid though.5)  Some of the voice actors were incredibly bad.  Most were decent.  I really enjoyed my mage.  Overall though, thought it was good enough, but a few of them should not have made it through Quality Control.6)  Could use more units and another map.  I get that animations are expensive and world building is time consuming.  There was plenty of content for this game's launch.  I would have loved to see more unit options and more worlds to explore like the old King's Bounty games had.  I assume this is just a financial and time constraint issue, and we will no doubt see much more in the future.  Regardless, was a little sad to not see some of my favorite units I would use in the previous games.  7)  Would like to see more fights.  The strategic combat is the best part of this series, and while it picked up after a slow start, the ratio of fights to running around questing/exploring was off.  Need more fights.  The entire trial line was amazing though.  But the lack of being able to just chain fight after fight like in the previous games is probably the biggest potential risk this new style takes.  I love exploring and questing, I'm a big RPG and MMO player, so this was enjoyable to me, but for people that just want to do the strategic fights, man, there is a lot of running around in between each fight most of the time and it could turn people off.  I love that stuff, and even I found myself wishing there were more battles more readily available, though again, the ratio got much better farther into the game it seemed.8)  The puzzles were a little too easy.  I love adventure games, so I'm used to some pretty hard puzzles to solve.  These struck me as too simplistic that even 10 year olds could quickly knock them out.  I do appreciate you putting them in the game though, but maybe a little harder going forward.  People can always look the answers up if they are too hard, but those who like to be challenged would appreciate it.Still, even with those nitpicks, I loved the game and it exceeded my hopes.  My conclusion is that if people are looking for a game exactly like the old King's Bounty series, they might not like the changes in format.  This game is massive and takes a long time, and plays like a RPG much of the time with exploring and questing.  For someone like me that loves the King's Bounty strategic combat system and also loves RPGs, this was awesome, but it was a pretty drastic departure in terms of playstyle from the older games and is probably more of a modern RPG than many fans of the IP will expect to see.  The spirit of King's Bounty is still there though, just with modern graphics and voiceovers, and I really enjoyed it, but this really is a departure and almost a new genre from what the games were before.

_childDocuments_.review: I have now beaten the game with Elisa/paladin. It took me 29 hours to complete every side quest and the main story. Overall, this game is more of a quest RPG than a tactical turn-based battler like the previous games. There are so many side quests that have you running on all over the map.The game starts out easy and on a small map. After a few hours you will get to the main large map of the game and will have tons to explore and the freedom to do what you want.Postive:-RPG aspects of equipment, leveling up, talent trees, unit leveling-Tactical battles take place as a zoomed out view of where ever you are on the map-Decent variety of units from 4 categories. A lot have distinct stats and abilities.Neutral:-You need to do most side quests and complete most battles to hit max level-Talent tree lets you max 1/4 areas and get maybe 75% of a second area-Battles / enemies don’t respawn so no opportunity for grinding your levels.-Units only seem to gain exp when killing other units (maybe damaging too?) and not just for being in the party when you win a battle-Sometimes you can’t heal your units after a battle due to debuffs, forcing you to have to go and rebuy them.-There is a horse inventory slot on your character that I never used the whole game. Don’t know why it’s there. Maybe they were going to have other mounts, but never added them?Negative:-Horse is trash. Slower than running with your character in cities. Can’t interact with anything. So slow to mount / unmount.-Character is too slow even running.-No easy way to find out what vendor sells what units / equipment.-Some vendors have limited units to sell whereas others will sell as many as you want-Not enough battles early on, though you get more in the last third of the game-Not apparent that you almost need to beat the whole story before being able to finish the paintings  side quest-The Scryer’s Trial quest line is too long and forces you to use weak armies to defeat way stronger ones. I suppose this is meant to be like a puzzle, but too much trial and error.-The difficulty scaling really spikes in the last few battles with enemy units being HP sponges.-Some equipment you can only get by making a specific karma choice during quests. This prevented me from completing a set armor where I ended with 6/7 pieces. It wasn’t apparent at all during the quests that you might miss equipment.

_childDocuments_.review: If you have played the previous Kings Bounty games by 1C, you know how good they were. Despite having entries that had a lower quality like Warriors of the North, or Dark Side, they were still pretty good.You had a huge variety of troops of multiple factions, many artifacts that enhanced your hero and the creatures in those factions and a really wide library of spells to give you a lot of options in your tactics against the enemies.Top that with a very decent progression system and add as an extra the companion mechanic with special effects to cast during combat and you have a really nice turn based RPG. All of that, without mentioning the beautiful artstyle, or compelling stories.And then we have Kings Bounty 2.I have no idea why they called this Kings Bounty 2. It's obvious they tried to make mainstream a niche game, removing all the things that made the original game compeling in the first place.A realistic artstyle that is not outstanding at all and that it looks poor when compared with similar games of the same genre.A different gameplay where you control the  hero in third person in the most clunky control system I have seen in any modern game.A UI that is convoluted and not intuitive at all.A diminute fraction of units, artifacts and spells when compared with previous titles that are less interesting and have worse synergies between them.A voice over that is so bad you will want to disable the voices.And a progression system that doesn't make much sense and doesn't offer much.This is a game that should have never happened. I could understand that they would like to make this more appealing to newer audiences, but this was a huge miss.The only possitive thing I can say about the game, is that the combat itself, is slightly more interesting due to the implementation of proper level design.
