_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, but... I did!  I rarely comment on games, but given all the negativity surrounding this game (even before it was published!), I wanted to see it for myself.  I played through the whole game before reviewing, just in case.  There are some rough edges, but everything considered this is a great game.  It just seems people are expecting a different game, and criticising it for not being enough like the previous installments, or a full rpg like the witcher.  This games takes most elements from the previous kings bounty games, but they made some important changes.  I did like the changes, like how you are now walking around in the world, where also the battles are fought.  At first I didn't like the unit cap they introduced, but then in appeared to me that this opens up new strategies.  You will want to create an army that matches your leadership value.  Things I liked: - walking around in the beautiful game world.  Since the game world is much larger the overview map in the previous games, you spend more time walking around.  I didn't really mind, because I could admire the landscapes, architecture.  The palace in particularly was very impressive.  Sure there are even prettier games, but I found it pretty as well.  There are also teleportation "steeles", which make that you can quickly traverse the map.  I didn't have a problem with the horse either, as many people seem to have.- engaging battles and strategic gameplay.  At first the game appears to be shallow, but there is a lot of strategy involved, especially with the mage.  Different spell combinations, synergy with the troops, how you compose the troops, and your initial setup, all have a big impact on the gameplay.- good story.  The story itself wasn't earth shatteringly profound, but it was fun enough, as a way to link together the battles.  I've enjoyed games with less story, like the age of wonders series.- funny/witty dialogs.  Most they where the standard fantasy stuff, but there where some funny third wall breaking dialogs, like refering to computer  bugs and math.  For sure not worse than your average RPG writing.- good (decent?) voice acting.  I didn't notice any of the supposedly "aweful" voice acting.Things I didn't like:- lip-syncing looked a bit weird.  They also seemed to have reused character models.  I didn't mind that much though...- Inconsistent battle difficulties, at least for mages.  Playing as a mage, most battles where easy, but then suddenly you get to battles which had an "impossible enemy".  Most of these where doable, at a cost of many troops, but a more consistent difficulty would have been nicer.  The castle irok battle was the worst.  It took me like 20 times to beat that map.  I felt beating that map was merely luck.  And after that, every other battle was pretty easy, including the final one.  Since the game is getting a difficulty setting with the update, this could be less of an issue.- Poorly explained mechanics.  I only learned some time in the game that you can "heal" your troops, which essentially resurrects fallen units.  This makes a huge difference, because you will not spend time walking around buying new troops!  Just having "hints" on how to play could make the game more approachable.- The scryers challenge are a neat idea, they are basically like a tutorial on how to play the game, as you get a premade army and spellbook, and have to defaut an enemy army.  However, it was mostly trial and error to find the correct strategy, of which there is only one.  I find that some optional hint system could have made it more enjoyable, especially for more casual players.- Difficulty rating for mage is way off.  You get to an "undefeatable enemy", which can actually be beating consistently!  If they go out of the way to provide a rating for each battle, why not take mage spells into account?  I believe they would be better of not giving a battle rating, instead of a completely wrong one.- The ending felt a bit rushed.  It is clear they are providing an opening for DLCs, but instead the story feels rather unfinished.- Long pauses between moves.  Also there is no way to speed up the enemy animations.In short, behind the flaws and rough edges is an excellent game.  It's not the witcher, but it offers its own set of unique mechanics and gameplay.  You should play this game when you want something new, instead of just another game which is just a copy of existing games.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for another King's Bounty (1) or HoMM-like combat experience...... look elsewhere.The overall graphics are fine, but fail to alleviate that most of the environment is empty and becoming boring and bland quickly. That there's only two overworld maps (one used for the game's introduction) doesn't help. The combat maps in contrast are nicely diverse and make tactical use of sight lines and elevation. Beyond that the strategic part of gameplay feels shallow, with units limited in amount and access linked to RPG story choices, which discourages combinations of playstyles, with synergies between units far and in between.The RPG part is equally lacking depth, equipment and inventory management feel restrictive and set items can be random or tied to RPG decisions, further limiting accessability for combining playstyles.The dialogue and story are neither overly engaging nor entertaining, taking itself rather serious but not delivering on that. From the mid game onwards, tedium sets in and the story just drags on. Travel takes *way* too much time, and you're going to run through empty areas a lot. The ending is equally unrewarding, .It's clear the developers were aiming to expand the game further, but with the state of the game features supporting the story as is, I can't see myself being enthralled to buy another installment.Flawed, but possibly worth your time when on sale

_childDocuments_.review: I'm new to the King's Bounty series, I saw the game featured in a YouTube video from The Spiffing Brit and felt it would be right up my alley.  This game features some quite difficult combat at the beginning of the game, and as you go on, a lot of fights can be super challenging if you don't get good gear quickly.  If you purchase the Duke's Edition, you get access to some very powerful weapons and armor that honestly make combat a breeze (I can take on Undefeatable enemies and beat them 1st or 2nd turn).  If you prefer the challenge, just get rid of the armor and weapons you get from the DLC.  All in all, I wasn't expecting much from the story but it's proven to be pretty interesting (almost done with the main quest), the combat can be difficult at times (Scryer's Trial forces you to fight using specific units, bonuses, and spells, it's really the hardest combat in the game), and the world feels lived-in.  I really enjoy that when you clear out somewhere, you'll start to see people there, or if you clear out a fort, bandits may take over.  Obviously there are parts that seem oddly empty (gates to other provinces of the land), but I assume those are set for DLC expansions of the map.  Really my only complaint with this game is just how long it takes you to mount/dismount the horse before you can start moving again! Definitely enjoyed this game so far, can't wait to see where else the game goes.

_childDocuments_.review: My early impressions are definitely positive. I'll give it a thumbs up now in an attempt to slightly offset the (unjust?) review bomb this game has received at launch from the trigger-happy refund mob. I'll come back and update my thoughts after a full play-through.Below are my thoughts re: commonly raised points in negative reviews.The game can be controlled with a gamepad or mouse and keyboard. Both methods work fine. Some strange design decisions were made around how you deal with trading, as well as swapping units between active army and reserve. When using a mouse in those screens, there isn't as much dragging and dropping as you might like or expect. You get used to it. It's not a huge deal.There is no run button because your character runs by default. There is a walk button. It seems that you cannot ride your horse at full speed while in major cities. You can still dismount and run around on foot.While there is no traditional RTS style minimap, the UI does feature a Skyrim style compass with quest markers and distance indicator. This works great and I don't feel like this game needs a conventional minimap at all.The game setting still feels like King's Bounty. The playable classes are what you would expect in a King's Bounty game. The turn-based combat feels like a mix between King's Bounty and Age of Wonders III (which is not a bad thing). The out-of-combat world navigation feels more like a B-grade version of Witcher III or third person Skyrim navigation (with no jumping and horse controls that are uninspired, but usable).While I seem to be spending more time on the RPG aspect of this game, rather than the more satisfying turn-based combat, this is by no means a "walking simulator". Also you unlock plenty of fast travel nodes.The game seems to range between beautiful and alright, I guess. Overall, I can neither accuse it of being ugly nor of looking "next gen".Both the voice acting and the music seem good to my ear.

_childDocuments_.review: Akin to older RPG's like Kingdom of Amalur or Gothic, but with a different focus, instead of fighting yourself You have an army consisting of 5 different units with each unit increasing in size as You level up and gain leadership. You gain leadership from finishing fights and sometimes from items You can equip. You do have equipment but it buffs your army and skills. You can learn magic from Your spell book if You have a scroll and Mana to spend to research it. Casting the spells will use Mana as well. You gather Mana from Chests, Quests, and Fight Rewards.   In this game You play as one of 3 different characters, Paladin, Mage or Warrior. Each one can spec into any of the trees with no hard restrictions beyond Your choice in how You play.  There are 4 trees, each with different skills and buffs but the way You acquire higher skill talents requires specific choices to be made when completing quests. They also have very different personalities. Generally You will be moving at a jog everywhere or on horseback but with treasure all over the place I find myself sticking to jogging. There is a walk option but not sure why.   The Talent Trees and play styles are in 2 opposing aspects. Anarchy-Yellow is opposed by Order-Green, and Finesse-Blue is opposed by Power-Red. Usually each quest gives at least 2 ways You can handle it between the 2 opposing aspects.  The Game can be a bit hard to get the hang of if You try to be a jack of all trades, with focusing into 2 differing trees like Power-Order or Anarchy-Finesse being ideal.     The Army part of the game can be tricky if You aren't used to games like the newer Age of Wonders games, but at the same time the units are not separated into this is strong vs that, with any unit being more or less capable of tackling any other. Some fights can be borderline impossible but that just means You should try coming back a bit later, or using magic if You can. Units You can acquire are various and split across the 4 aspects.   I personally haven't played all that much but I am having a blast

_childDocuments_.review: Basically a walking simulator with a combat style mini game... such a waste of time...-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Update at 30 hours:As a big HOM&M fan, I am willing to buy anything that's even remotely close to it. KB1 series was of course good enough. KB2 however, while playable, is more of a pain than fun...1) The walking simulator... ok not strictly walking, you also ride a horse that's easily stuck. But the point is, I wish more of the combats and much much less of walking/riding around. The devs improved the speed of the characters and mount, but still too much time was wasted on these meaningless things.2) You can find all kinds of trashes on the map. But almost all of the items can only be sold to the NPC for gold, no other uses. Making exploring the map not rewarding enough. Combined with the amount of time the players are forced to spend on map exploring, it's just a pain... There are other designs quite controversial, personally I don't find those designs too annoying. And I can get away with those. Like unit cap (on top of leadership constraint) or a mana pool for both learning and casting spells. All things combined, I cannot recommend the game... especially at its full price. If there's ever going to be a KB3, please please put more focus on the most important things.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a difficult one, as it was fun and it looks gorgeous but, there's some really glaring and even some gamebreaking issues. I wouldn't really recommend it to anyone I know at the full price point (of 39,99). I was able to pick it up during a 90% sale however, meaning I was able to pick up the Duke's edition at 6,99(ish) and at 6,99 or below I would definitely recommend this game.Pros * Graphics are gorgeous, you'll continually be looking around and loving it.* There's a lot of flavour text all around the game, that sometimes do a decent job at adding depth to the world.* A bunch of random quests from npc's  that fit seemlessly into the world around them.* Gorgeous vista's* Quite a bit of content to explore* fun turn based combat.* Some random dialogues in the world are meant to put you under the wrong impression. i.e.: Cons* Movement is janky as all hell,  you can't jump, your camera follows your character movement (while also following mouse movement) and there's no sprint or crouch.* Riding the horse gave me motion sickness, which I've only ever experienced before on Lethal company. Though this horse was many times worse. Which means getting around was a slow process for me.* I almost got stuck once, and literally stuck the second time. * The map is not super useful. It seems to occasionally forget locations you've already been and teleports you've previously unlocked. There's no naming to locations, so knowing whether you're in the right spot becomes reliant on the naming of points of interest (like npc's/events) and repetition.* Dialogue in many places sounds like they only sent 1 part of the script to every voice actor, causing dialogue to sound bland and disconnected in many places.* When dialogue does match the tone of the conversation, it often suffers from lazy or plain bad writing. The whole premise is that after you're suspected of poisoning the king, the prince needs you to come solve a relatively minor and unimportant murder. Game would've overall benefitted from a topdown approach to movement (since they obviously did not get this type of movement right) like diablo/PoE, a little more clarity on the map and a whole bunch of rewriting.

_childDocuments_.review: Put aside all the hateful posts. I don't know what is going on with people and why they want to rage, but this game is a lot better than what meets the eye and than what many haters here say. I played this game all evening last night and I for one would like to leave a good positive review because the game deserves it. I went into the game with not the best feeling, because it started a bit rocky for me. I tried to change resolution and it bloated outside my screen, none of the buttons were accessible and I was ready to press that 'refund' button. I tried even reinstalling the game, since I couldn't find INI files or CFG files to reset the resolution. Then I finally somehow managed to switch the game into windowed mode by simply poking around with the mouse on the edge of the game screen. Anyway, that experience aside - This game is a breath of fresh air in my personal preferences. I haven't played a similar RPG before and this is what this game is - a really good RPG, where I could enjoy both open world environment and game mechanics and the RTS type of combat. This game does that combination very perfectly. Because of the very unique atmosphere, the game makes you feel like you are playing Heroes of Might and Magic, but instead of the bird view, you actually get to be in that world up close and personal, which adds very immersive feeling into the gameplay, at least it did for me.If you expect another King's Bounty, with a bird view mode and just some different story - KB2 isn't it. It is a game with a top notch voice overs, where you are actually feeling being a part of the world around you and not only controlling a little character on a horse from the bird view perspective. So without the further adieu, here is my scores and justifications: - 9/10I am not a big fan of stylized graphics, but the attention to detail in KB2 and the care they took to design areas, makes me want to give them a bit higher score than what it actually is. Some places have very atmospheric design. The open areas of the world may seem a bit condensing and even narrow, but the closed in spaces, like the specific dungeons and catacombs have been paid very close and careful attention to and have been designed very well. In order to actually see and appreciate the game's design and the graphics, you have to play for at least several hours and cover different areas of the game. - 9/10Music is one of the other things that they paid a good attention to. It is very atmospheric, it grows on you, the same way the game itself does and you eventually start hearing some familiar tunes, that you think you've heard before. Sounds are ok as well, maybe not perfect, but I haven't heard any sound glitches or anything really bad, to give me a reason to give this a less of a score. Both Music and sounds are all well done and fit the world atmosphere and the setting of specific areas. - 7/10I gave this a bit lower score because the world does feel a bit congested. In some cases, it may even feel as if it pushes down on you, considering some narrow areas, which give you a feeling that the game is on rails. You can't step away the boundaries of platforms and places that you can walk on. You can't jump up or down the landscape, which makes the movement sometimes feel clunky and jagged. Unfortunately, even though the world design itself in most of the areas is quite beautiful, the way you move around it deserves to wish for something better. It feels as if some areas of the game were first made to play from the bird view perspective, but then they decided to add a 3rd person view camera into the game and while other areas seem open and spacey, some areas feel very cramped and claustrophobic. It doesn't break the game and can easily be ignored though. - 7/10Nothing probably special to say about the Combat, but the camera felt a bit clunky to me. Even when the Cinematic options are disabled, it still doesn't give you completely free control, until a certain point. I personally like to play while zoomed into the combat field and see my units up close, never was a big fan of fully zoomed out full strategic view of RTS combat. I like the level of zooming in I can do in KB2 during the combat. Combat is OK, at least to me personally. It's not bad, but it doesn't really click with me that much to give it a higher score. I don't consider a combat to be the main standing out element in this game. For me personally, it is the world, the RPG elements, the well done voice overs, the story, etc. I am glad the combat is there and I do enjoy the RTS elements of it, as well as building my army, even though I find it a bit odd to carry my army around the world with me in my backpack though. That is a feeling I get, since I don't see them anywhere ever, just when the combat starts, which kind of giving me a feeling of disconnect from them. - 8/10I don't usually replay the games often, unless they really offer a unique and unparalleled experiences on the next playthroughs. I can't say too much about this part yet, but I tried different characters and they all have different voice overs. The dialogues with NPCs, in some cases, also change depending on the nature of the main character you chose at the beginning of the game. While Elisa, for example, sounds like a strong character paladin, Katharine has more of an ambitious, noble and somewhat snobby dialogue lines and voice overs. Even though you go through the same game content, it may be interesting for some people to investigate the relationship of the main character with the different world events that unfold around them, and characters that play the biggest parts of it. The reactions of main characters to what happens around them are very different and quite unique. - 9/10While this is quite a broad section to cover, I just wanted to focus on basic elements that every game has.  - is quite smooth. If you do all the quests and explore as much as you can, find as many treasures as you can, you won't have many issues building your army and winning the fights. It may get a bit tough, at some point, and may start to feel as if the devs didn't balance the difficulty. You will most likely get that feeling and will even get frustrated, if you start skipping game content, like if you don't explore and only decide to do the story, for example. As less you do in the game, as more difficult it will seem. - Skill tree is also interesting and balances how you can build your army, what your main character can use during the battle, how good your troops' morale will be, if you mix troops from different 'factions', what spells your main character can use, etc. For the sake of replayability, don't mix 'good' with 'bad' skill trees. Try to roleplay your character, and chose only skills that would compliment your chosen character's 'alignment' - Elisa for good, Katharine - evil, etc. You can of course mix and match and just do some hybrid, anything can work, since you have access to all the customization options on all the characters. - I found this part a bit lacking. While there is tons of stuff you can find in the world objects, caves, barrels, chests, etc, those are mostly trash and that is pretty much how you make money - you collect trash by opening anything that can be opened and picking up everything that can be picked up. There is no way to improve your equipment, but there are different tiers of equipment up to Legendary. Those who pre-ordered deluxe or collectors editions, will get some legendary items from the beginning of the game (not the very beginning), but they are level locked, with level 20 seems to be the max level in the game.If you see someone saying that this game sucks - just ignore them and try it for yourself. It's a great RPG + RTS combo in one package.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll get straight to the point:1. The UI is so uncomfortable. There's a feeling like the devs never played it on the PC. It feels like this was a console made game ported to PC while forgetting to adapt the UI. Why do I have to press V to toggle tooltips? It should be automatic to appear/disappear when hovering with the mouse. Why do I have to press and hold Space to initiate combat after placing units? Why are the abilities/wait/defend buttons clickable through? The amount of times I accidentally made unit movement when I wanted to press wait... While I don't mind needing two hands on overworld exploration, but these strategic battles should be playable with just the mouse. It's hard to interact with anything in the UI using the mouse because it's not responding well enough. It's almost like they made the game without mouse support and then on the last day of development thought "Hey wait, this is a PC game! Quickly - put a mouse cursor in there just to tick the box"2. Why. Do. I. Have. To. Dismount. The. Horse. To. Interact. With. The. World?? This is SO tedious. The fact there is weird animation lock when mounting/dismounting that locks you in place for several seconds is just so uncomfortable. There is a lot of objects of interest to find and interact with but HEY GET OFF THE HORSE FIRST. I pretty much stopped using horse 30 minutes in the game because no point. But then your running speed is so slow. Artificially adding dozens of playtime hours just because of this. I get it's for immersion but like... there should be a way to make it less annoying. First person perspective, with a lot of running around. Looks pretty good, but there's so many invisible walls which Fable had as well. And a reputation system that in KB 2 is more shallow but still has consequences.. kind of. It effects your skill progression more than how NPCs react to you. As for looks, I chose the Paladin one and I swear every time she was talking to a NPC she looked like she was autistic, like Asperger level. Where it really shines is the combat. It takes the HoMM/KB concept and improves on it in every way. Your battle maps are that same areas you've been running around on. Only a 3D isometric perspective that really uses height and cover the way the earlier predecessor games could/should of IMHO.Lastly I bought it on sale for 75% off. _childDocuments_.review: A "okay to decent" King's Bounty. Compared to earlier iterations the tactical options in KB2 are much steamlined / simplified by: 1) Taking away "kiting" on the overland map. Mobs now have a zone of control. Touch the outer line of the zone and you'll automatically engage with the mob. You can still run away, but there's often no bypassing this zone (for example when the mob's guarding a bridge) as the zone of control is *huge*. Mobs now are literal roadblocks. A nice new feature: after winning a battle you can opt to replenish your troops. This is only available when at least one member of the squad is alive. Replenishing costs gold, but doesn't take away units from the overland pool.2) There are no trashmobs anymore, only fights that matter. So there's much less fighting, but the fights themselves feel more unique. The arenas are an almost exact representation of the location you engaged the mob on the overland map, which is a nice touch.3) Members per squad have a maximum limit, even though your leadership permits a bigger squad. For example: the limit is three troll chiefs in a squad. It doesn't matter your leadership permits a squad of four troll chiefs, three will always be the maximum. The squad can't grow beyond that limit.These are all big changes compared to earlier KB games and I'm not wholly sold on them. It doesn't make a bad game, but it simplifies things so much I often struggle to find tactical depth in KB2. The fights themselves are still fun and in many cases even challenging, but by taking away all trashmobs you're often spending a lot of time travelling on an empty map looking for the next quest objective or an extremely easy "puzzle". It's a good thing the overland map itself is quite beautifully designed. It's what I would envision a fantasy medieval eastern europe would look like. Very pittoresque. The music is impressive too.I will still recommend this game, but only because I'm hoping for another King's Bounty game. I'd like to see a follow up with more tactical depth. This iteration certainly is interesting for those new to the series, although in that case I would also recommend checking out earlier titles as well. When possible get this game on a sale.Rating: 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of the previous entries of the King's Bounty series.  I held off getting this game because of the bad reviews, but finally picked it up on a big sale.It had the potential to be a pretty good game but fell apart in several ways.I get that they wanted to make it look fancier than the cartoony graphics of the previous games (which, for the record, I had no problem with the graphics of the previous game.  It worked well for the series and would have been happy if the sequel had those same graphics), but they did a half assed job in that regard.  Now on to the real problems.It's like they took the previous games and used almost none of the stuff that worked well in that game.OK, you've got your standard Leadership system that gates how many creatures you can control at once.  Makes sense.  Oh, cool, you added rank upgrades for unit types that make them slightly more effective if you use them in combat more and keep the whole stack alive.  That's a good change.  Another nice change is the addition of replenishing your unit stacks at the cost of gold at the end of a battle.What's this, you have limited the number of units per stack?  Your basic Spearmen/Dogs of War/Archers are limited to 10 units per stack.  10!  I guess what they want you to do is switch to higher tier units as the game goes on.  Gone are the days where you can amass 100 Guardsmen and boost the minimum damage or HP to make them viable in the late game.  The annoying part is you spend all this time to upgrade your units, and then you have to toss them aside.  Not only that, but the higher tier units have an even LOWER limit of units per stack.  I got up to tier 4 units, and they're limited to 3 or 4 units.  Not only that, higher tier units just don't feel powerful.  Units don't have any sort of offensive or defensive stats, so you no longer have the big high attack or defense units that are barely scratched by lower tier units.  They take the same damage and deal the same damage no matter who they are attacking/defending.The combat system is mostly the same from the previous games.   They did a nice job of making more interesting battlefields since all battles take place in a static area.  Though it does kind of suck you can't run past a high level area to get the treasure that a high level mob is guarding, like you could in the old games.  Though gone are the hazards and random treasures from the previous games.Unit variety is craaaaaaaaap.  You get basically 4 factions.  Humans, Bandits, Undead, and Dwarves.  There are a few "neutrals" like some flavors of golems or elementals, but nowhere near the variety that the original games had.  These factions correspond with the 4 ideals: Order, Anarchy, Power, and Finesse.  Certain quests will give you points in one of these ideals based on the decisions you make.  Your skill tree is gated based on how many points you have in these ideals.Item stats are fairly boring.  1 Warfare = 1% more unit damage.  1 Arcane power = 1% more spell damage.  There are items sets, but they are few and far between and most of them, so far, have needed at least 4 items per set.The spells are fairly similar to the previous games, though there are less of them.  However, the status effects like Burning, Poison, etc are worse than the previous games.  They are static damage numbers so are useless against higher numbers of units or higher hp enemies.  At least before, they were % based.The quests are much more interesting than the previous games.  There are some that are simple and only take 1 or 2 steps to complete.  While others span the entire area of the map you're in with a dozen steps.  Rewards are often just experience, gold, and a pieces of equipment.  Sometimes it's new units or unlocking higher tier units in certain unit shops.  However, and here is what made me quit the game, some quests give you items that are required to complete the quest, and these items are just part of your regular inventory.  Which means, they can be sold.  And there is no buy back method.  So, 25 hours in, I realized i had sold some equipment that I needed for a quest.  I had done this many hours before, so there was no way I was going to go back to a previous save to redo everything I had already done.I am sad that we got a sequel to this series and it turned into such a mediocre game.  I'm just glad I got this on a super sale and so don't feel so bad about the money I spent on this.

Moving the camera around, positioning units and effectively zooming in or out takes a bit of getting used to as well.The troop rosters, layouts, stats, magic library (learning stuff etc) and the lot are a bit different than we were used to but i think it's fine once you get the hang of it.. People are so easy to complain and judge nowadays without even trying first... It's nice having the option to explore freely on foot or horseback, while there are plenty of locations with puzzles and loot to be found doing so.The horse's movement is a bit simplified (doesn't allow you to walk backwards) but while holding a button it's movements become far better controllable imho.Furthermore the graphics are okay, and so are the overall sounds and musical score albeit not outstanding in any regard.I'm currently giving this game a "half" recommendation but it should be mentioned that i aswell expected far more than this, so the recommendation should be met with a little bit of caution so to speak.One hour in, and i'm enjoying the game so far honestly..Is it worth it's current asking price, NO! I'd say 30-ish for the normal edition sounds about right to me.Might it get better due to continiously updating and patching? Well, i can only hope so, because this game certainly has potential to be rated higher.That's it so far after my first and quick session.Hopefully others might also have a more open view about this game as i have.Current score: 7/10 (moderately recommended)

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of the original King's Bounty then I don't recommend this game for you. I have over 200 hours in the first one and have replayed through it many times. Here are my Pros, Cons, and Tips for King's Bounty II.Pros:+Fully Voice Acted: genuinely did a good job on this.+Combat: This was really enhanced since the first one and now includes great character models, attack animations, and spectacular spells. The combat is really fluid, strategic, and at times intense and satisfying.+Hand-Crafted World: Every corner and dead end you come down has a barrel, cache, or chest to be looted and even roaming back through old areas causes new combat encounters to be had. So exploration is your friend!+Talents and Unit Ranks: the talents feel rewarding to achieve and for the players that like to play many different kinds of units will be rewarded with more talent points for ranking them up. It's possible to get enough talent points to max out both of your specialty trees: Order or Anarchy and Power or Finesse.Cons:-Character Movement: This is a big one for a lot of other reviews that I've seen. Your character moves relatively slow and getting on and off your horse feels  like a long drawn-out animation that is almost not worth it at times. Your horse moves slower in town so that's not fun to deal with for the impatient gamer. Also, you get caught on every single rock and log in the game. Sometimes your character gets to a weird spot where you cannot move in any direction and must stop moving altogether and wait for the game to "sink" your character through the object that is causing you to get stuck and hopefully you can get out. I have not gotten permanently stuck yet thank goodness.EDIT: They are fixing a lot of these movement issues in the upcoming patch so as long as it works properly, this will not be an issue anymore.-Unit Acquisition and Unit Numbers: One of my favorite units in the game is the Order unit called Celestials. I have not found a way to get them and neither has anyone else that I've looked up on the subject so I assume there is other units as well. Some units you cannot obtain if you picked the wrong path in a quest line ie you picked Power over Finesse and now do not have access to the Chimera, a powerful Finesse unit. Another part of the game that felt bad was that some units became entirely useless less than half way through the game because the max amount you can have was 10 or 8  or lower in some cases. And since you have no way of selling them, they sit in your Reserve forever becoming clutter unless you use them as fodder in a battle and lose on purpose. One thing I loved from the first game was that there was no max unit size, so a unit that I enjoyed early on like the peasants could reach be hundreds in size and stay a part of my army the entire game if I wanted. That was changed and I don't believe this is for the better.-Puzzles: if you can call them puzzles. Every puzzle is a "choose the right order" puzzle and the vast majority of them give you the answer right next to the puzzle or can be brute forced since there is only a few combinations to choose. While I understand that it might be fun for some to play a puzzle, this is not the game for it. They feel out of place, lackluster, and ultimately unrewarding since a large portion of them give you a single uncontrollable unit for the battle you have to do anyway.-UI Design: Some UI functions of the game don't feel very good to use and tend to get in the way, such as the tooltips that automatically popup when viewing units and items. You are forced to press a button (V by default) to turn them off, but you have to press V every. single. time. you click on anything. Also, did you know you have to scroll to see some of the units in the unit shops? It wasn't until late in the game when I was looking for a particular unit that I KNEW was in this guy's shop did I scroll to find it. It's not very clear that the shop can have more than 5 units available for purchase.TLDR and wrap-up: I am one of many fans that bought and played this one because I loved the first game. I believe I speak for many people when I say we were let down in many ways. This does not feel like a King's Bounty game and does not deserve the title because it took the concept and world lore into a different kind of game. It's okay, but I don't want to really play it and feel cheated out of a sequel to a game I enjoyed.Now for some tips and tricks for new players:~Play lots of units and rank them up by killing units with them for extra talent points.~Talent tree can be reset once for free, then costs 10,000 and then jumps to 50,000 at max level, so save before you place them!~If you feel your aren't prepared for a battle, press esc on your keyboard before it starts and you will exit before combat with no penalties so you can swap out units as needed.~Keep enough gold on hand to replace your army should you have a difficult battle.~Avoid hitting the magic number 28 in your talent if you want some benefits from another tree. ie If you want the life steal talent from Anarchy then get some points in anarchy before finishing quests to unlock the last Order talent. Your character will simply not allow it.~Try not to spend gold on units early game unless you plan to use them immediately. Money can be tight early on so don't be afraid to put some talent points into the bonus gold talents in the anarchy tree then exploring for all the chests, caches, and bags of gold early to start stacking some gold for a rainy day, it's not required though.Good luck and have fun if you play!

_childDocuments_.review: Clearly there are devs on this team that do really care about this series. The passion to make a great game is there, but, what it is currently lacking is polish. If you are a fan of the series and aren't sure about the game now, come back in a month or two to check in and see if things have gotten better. _childDocuments_.review: This is another one in which I wish there was a neutral option, at least for now.I, for one, am glad that a developer, for once, has chosen to focus their effort more on the gameplay and mechanics than making their game look pretty. Having said that, there is nothing wrong with the game's graphics. Sure, they're not super realistic and you won't be mistaking any NPCs for your mother any time soon, but they're nowhere near as bad as people are claiming.What I have played so far has been interesting, though the negative reviews aren't entirely full of nitpicky babies whining about nothing. - The UI has clearly been designed with console players in mind, as a lot of the time it doesn't register you clicking things with a mouse.- The camera is janky as hell. There is absolutely nothing smooth about it.- Walking. Walking everywhere. It isn't as bad as some reviews would have you believe, but I can see why it annoys some people. You have a horse, but after a couple of minutes, you'll prefer the slow pace. *The upside to being slow is you're unlikely to miss the plethora of loot. - I don't know about consoles, but the game definitely could use a bit of optimization on PC. I've been getting frame drops randomly throughout the game regardless of what settings I have on, the cutscenes being the worst of them.Goods things... characters are interesting, the story hasn't bored me tears yet and the combat is relatively straightforward, and neither too easy nor too difficult.I dunno about previous games in this series and how this one compares, but if you like RPGs and don't mind the idea of RTS combat, I recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: King's Bounty II

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, clearly one of the best i played in several years. Easily triple A next gen experience and a masterpiece.Game currently has more than 70 unique battles, each of them carefully tuned to reflect difficulty curve. I played mage with no loss challenge, so each battle felt like a unique game of chess vs AI. Sometimes i was barely able to progress further, but eventually you can do this challenge if you like difficult tasks. Since i'm kind of completionist, and my challenge kinda called for it, i appreciated every smallest detail game has to offer, from beautiful landscapes, to awesome battle animations, unique for each unit, to npc gossip and rumors which change and add up as you progress through the story. It is fun to hear craziest rumors here and there about events your participate in. Main character who seemed cold and arrogant at first, actually became a good and charming person, talking with people with deep knowledge of the world and human personalities. Now i actually wanna replay the game and see if the anarchy way shape a different person in the process. The single fact that developers cared about these details that many players will probably just miss, because you need to actually revisit some locations to experience them is a clear 10/10 from me.I don't know who came up with the idea of fighting exactly in places you can explore, but it's great, in few battles you can even use terrain to your advantage by attacking enemy from different side. I wish there were more of these battles. Amount of exploration, preparation, quests and battles is perfect. Basically there's no repetitive battles, each of them is unique. It is not too much exploration either, even though map is huge, it is shaped in a way you can conveniently explore each next area if you want to. Perfomance is mostly good, perfect in battles, but in some areas of exploration could be better. However i'm not running top hardware here, so can't really complain. Music and atmoshpere is amazing, give me more of those tracks. There are two systems in the game which is kinda weird to me: it's loot and puzzles. I wish it would be somehow more rewarding to find and open chests and hidden caches. Main issue with puzzles is that they are too easy, like read the scroll or tablet in the puzzle area and just do the sequence easy. Even though i like the methaphores used to describe what you need to do, it's still too easy. I hope those areas of the game can be improved in future expansion to better reflect triple A experience.Overall developers did a great job on the game, please continue doing this well in the future, and looking forward to an expansion!

_childDocuments_.review: As many others are saying this just doesn't hit the mark when it comes to previous King's Bounty games. After having played it for almost 8 hours the game appears to be lacking in every single aspect. What it seems like they did, was try to expand into other gameplay styles but had the same amount of resources available to them as previous games. This stretching of resources ended up making the typical King's Bounty gameplay loop hollow and much more pedantic than previous entries. The areas they expanded into are also subpar and do not add to the experience. The voice acting is poor, the quests are flat, etc etc. Every aspect from the previous entries has either been hollowed out or removed. There is no longer an engaging progression system or a unique character resource. The maximum amount of any type of creature you can have in your army is 10. One of the strengths of the paladin type in previous entries was massive numbers, not a thing anymore.  For those of you who played previous King's Bounty entries, sometimes you had to look around for an appropriate fight to be able to advance your armies to fight harder enemies. This might take a minute or two but typically it was a fast endeavor and wasn't particularly notable, until you find yourself in King's Bounty II. This concept is still there, where you have to fish around for a good fight, but instead of a quick check around, imagine a poorly designed open world movement system (the horse's poor capability to move is just criminal) where the camera likes to break your neck. Not only does it take longer to get to these various fights, but it also is a jarring experience. The world treasure hunting is also just tedious and doesn't add anything to the game besides feeling like you need to look around every tree for that extra bit of gold. Unfortunately, this is a lesson in the challenges of hybridizing a genre. They tried to do more with King's Bounty II without actually putting more into the development. Instead they cut corners everywhere.3/10 - Do Not Buy

_childDocuments_.review: King's Bounty, but not.  So far, I'm liking the change in perspective.  It does feel like KB, but a fresh take because of the 3rd person view.  It's also got a ton of voice acting, though some of it is cringe worthy.  From all the negative reviews, I expected something worse, but it is surprisingly good.  Does it need some polish?  Sure.  Does it seem like there was a ton of effort put into it?  Definitely yes.  Things I like:32:9 support - has 5120x1440, though it's a tad bit off, especially during battles - the UI needs some adjustmentOption to change the FOV - helps with the above res a bitEvery quest has VAPretty long campaignEquipped gear actually shows up on the main character - a really nice touchThings I don't like:Most quests are pretty fetchy (as with most quests...)Doesn't tell you what some stats do or give you a number, like critical chance; just 14 for example.  *this appears to be percentElisa's VA is horrendously bad - 99% of the voices in the game are better acted. * I watch some other videos and the others are worse.  LOLGetting stuck on mismatched invisible surfaces -  I should be able to 'fall' off a 6 inch ledge instead of having to go aroundThe mount - super difficult to navigate - your mouse actually controls it; wait for the screen to fix back to the rearQOL asks:Mouse speed adjustment - it's still extremely high on the lowest settingBetter battle map viewing - Cannot rotate or move far into the battle maps - looks like you can move as far as your units.Ability to sell back unitsIncrease the % of gold you can acquire as units become unattainable with that and leadershipRe-spawning enemiesA training area to level up your unitsMerchant unit restocking.  Ability to reset your skills at willGive it a chance.  It's not Armored Princess, but it's just as good.

_childDocuments_.review: It's slow, it's tedious, the 3D open world makes no sense at all and you can safely skip every single line of dialogue. _childDocuments_.review: Many reviews say you can’t choose a mission option path if one of the two opposite alignments are too high; order vs anarchy or power vs finesse. These reviews fail to mention that as long as you don’t max out your alignment (max 28) your free to still choose either or of the two option paths. I imagine this is to limit your character’s ability to acquire all four elite alignment talents. The game does need some quality-of-life updates and in my opinion a balance pass. Your almost stuck with the starting available units. You’ll read many reviewers state that they played with order units throughout the game. There is a good reason why. Attempting to level (newly unlocked) low tier units once you progress from the starting area is absurdly difficult. Thus, it’s easier to stick with your starting army until you find the overpowered units. That is if you want to win battles and save gold. A legendary chest piece can be purchased as soon as you leave the starting area, but will cost you 50,000 gold, WTF were the developers thinking. I guess they wanted to tease you, lol. Also, many of those preorder weapons and armors can’t be equipped until you reach level 15 and 20; which is 10+ levels you’ll need to earn after leaving the starting area. At least you can sell them for gold if you don’t want to use them. The game is decent and I recommend it. I’m sure many issues that reviewers have complained about will be addresses and hopefully fixed soon. however, for the few reasons I mentioned, the game can be frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: I have a hundred hours in older King's Bounty titles so I was pretty excited for this. However my first impression, I'm pretty disappointed:-In the first 1 hour there has been quite a bit of off-putting immersion issues. The most glaring example for me is when you first leave the prison you encounter a broken statue with no arms and my character says "I've heard about this statue, I need to find its arms". OK, uhhh, weird. I walk up to it and it's arm is literally sitting about 3 feet away, I pick it up and my character says "where did this come from?". Nice.-Character already moves slowly, and there is a walk button yet no run button-Battle animations are also slow and it seems there is no way to speed them up at all-"Soliders" has appeared in multiple different places instead of "Soldiers" within the first 1 hour, which in itself is not a big deal but it is pretty alarming-Settings for mouse sensitivity when walking around the world only go in large increments (I get motion sickness so I need to change my mouse DPI specifically for this game every time I start it up), and then as a result my sensitivity for menus/in battles is off-No difficulty settings as far as I can tell. I'm not far enough into the game where this has seriously affected me, but it is concerning (the first few battles can be beaten easily without using your brain, which is kinda disappointing but I can give a pass since it's only the start of the game)-On that note the learning curve seems a bit overwhelming as well, in the tutorial battle I have two different units with 3-4 passive abilities each and I fight an enemy with 4 passives and an active ability. One of the appealing parts of the tactics genre is taking all the info, calculating it to make the correct decision, but like this is way too much stuff at the start to know if I am making the right choice. But again as mentione above, it doesn't matter yet because I can do anything and it works.I am going to play more and am open to amend review if I enjoy it but in my experience, I tend to not have issues in the first 1 hour for most games.~~~~Played another hour and encountered many more similar issues, decided to refund. Replies to some comments (now disabled due to several racist/homophobic personal attacks, which is regrettable as most of the comments were good):1) "Why leave a review without finishing the game?" The game developers experienced the same first few lackluster fights/zones of the game that I did and still shipped the game. It is completely understandable- the release was already delayed to what was desired, and there is a balance between the devs shipping the game and working on it forever- especially with external pressure. But through thousands of hours of gaming I have learned that if I do not enjoy the first hour of the game, it is extremely likely I will not enjoy the game later. Quality tends to be consistent and one of the main purposes of the beginning sections of the game (alongside tutorial, exposition, etc.) is to preview how the rest of the game will be like. I figured this was important to respond to, but I also understand people will complain no matter what, if I finished the game I undoubtedly would receive responses of "why did you play 50 hours if you didn't enjoy it?"2) "You are hurting the developer with a negative review!" I'm not a professional game reviewer, I'm literally one random guy on the sharing my experience.I do not work for 1C Entertainment (who have released 100+ games on Steam alone) but I bet they prefer players leaving honest reviews about how they feel rather than hitting the thumbs up button even if they did not enjoy the game. 3) "But the game is not broken?" I never said the game is broken. It runs fine for me. I simply would not recommend this game to my friends like I did for KB Crossworlds.

_childDocuments_.review: So far it seems like a decent game. As other reviews point out, the voice acting and dialogue is quite average. The combat is decent, the arenas seem a bit small which limits tactics a bit. However the game is terrible at explaining very important information.After leaving the prison, when buying units, you can shift the units into reserve and then buy more. This is useful for when your leadership skill grows and allows you larger stacks. Just remember you also need the money for this.The game does not tell you how much mana it costs to learn or upgrade spells. This costs a lot of mana so be careful (learning spells seems to cost anywhere from 30-100 mana).Some quests have 2 solutions. These different paths reward you an affinity point. If you want to max out your order skills, for example, make sure you complete any order solutions to quests. Also the three classes seem to develop affinity points as they level. I've only started as mage but mage gets some order and finesse affinity to start. This affinity system replaces the rune system of KB1.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game is pretty good. The annoying thing about it is that its unforgiving with RNG. If you have high morale, the only way to get additional turns seems to be when you use up all your action points, eg move and attack or cast 2 of the units skills. If you end turn with only using 1 action, you dont get the additional turn. I like the difficulty of the game for battles. But the scryer's trials are a whole other level of annoyingly hard. Another thing, why can't i get all the pieces for the immortal king set/serpentine king set/hero set? Also the amount of gold you get without using the scroll buff and talent buffs sucks hard and even with the buffs isnt that great. makes you choose between buying units or gear or just restarting every battle you lose a unit in. The only point i see to this is the make you decide what types of units you will use thoughout the game, eg only order and power/ anarchy and finesse, etc. Overall I like this game alot. shame it ended so quickly

_childDocuments_.review: This game has the Witcher 3 RPG style mix with enhanced Turn-Based Combat. I applaud this direction but the game is somewhat under-delivered. The content was lacking. It only took me 40 hours to beat the game compared to around 200 hours in the previous titles.The RPG element and story telling of this game is only about 40% of the Witcher 3's. Fortunately, the combat system is improved significantly compared to previous King's Bounty installments. The most notable and positive change is how the units are no longer "stacked" into 1 model with a number below it. Each unit is now represented by 1 model and there is a cap at how many units you can bring with you (beside the Leadership cap). What you see is what you have. This way each unit feel more unique and you are forced to pay attention to each model in combat.Overall I'm very happy with the direction that the game is taking (both the Witcher RPG element and the enhanced Turn-based Combat), but I'm not at all satisfy with the amount of content that the game offered. To conclude: A very sweet but short experience. I'm dying for more, please be quick, devs.

_childDocuments_.review: Buyers beware: This game is more of a sequel to "Ascension to the Throne" than any of the King's Bounty games. This game does not feature the depth of tactical combat those games do. This game does not have the variety of fights, nor the diversity of allied fighters or enemy combatants. And most damningly it does not have the easy charm,  the laid-back attitude, the fantastical atmosphere, nor the great soundtracks that the actual King's Bounty games have aplenty.Plus the dev/publisher is being taken over, support for the game is dead. And this after the game ended with some obvious sequel-bait too. Play this only if you have nothing else.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is my "Best Seven" of the year. It is very obviously flawed, won't ever be remembered as one of the greats, and doesn't do anything terribly exciting, it's not more than a 7/10. But I love it. You might not.KB2 keeps its tactical combat but moves the top-down view during exploration from the near-identical set of previous iterations to third person and puts more focus on light RPG mechanics and exploration.  Like much of this game, it's solid but has some issues. There are tons of little containers hidden all over, but most of them just contain a few gold pieces and vendor trash, there's the occasional scroll as well and rarely an actual equippable item. You'll find such containers in almost every little corner which means you'll want to explore every little corner.  And that's where the first issue lies: Your character's movement speed is rather slow. Even just trying to clear a small village of its lootables takes a few minutes. While you can summon a horse which moves at close to twice the speed, the animations for doing so, mounting, and dismounting each take a bit. And since you can't interact with anything while mounted, it's not worth it when actually exploring a new area.  So the horse is really only useful for backtracking for quests or after hitting a dead end. And despite the fast-travel system which also exists, you'll be doing a fair bit of on-foot/-horse back-tracking.Each quest is fully voiced, though the quality of VA and writing is inconsistent at best. The animations that play during the cutscenes are also rather wooden and the whole thing isn't helped by the ever-same camera angle. Heck, when equipping a large shield on your character, they'll wear it on their back and it'll obscure the other party in half the scenes. I feel like the dev team had grand ambitions here but bit off more than they could chew.  The actual quests are mostly 'go there and bring me that' or 'go there and talk to the guy', often with a mandatory battle in-between you and the objective. Plenty of quests have two ways to complete them, each associated with one of four ideals. There's "Power", the direct approach which usually involved combat and its opposed ideal of "Finesse" which will find a way around the fight or at least tilt the odds in your favor. The other pair of ideals are "Order" and "Anarchy", basically aligning yourself with the rulers of the land or bandits and other shadowy figures. Depending on how you choose to solve a quest, the outcome and your rewards will often differ. These ideals also tie into the skill trees to the point where many player will want to pick one of each pair and stick with it.  I like that most of the side quests are interwoven with the main storyline. Many quests so far deal with the fallout of a catastrophe at the Magefactory. Your first main task - after the tutorial area - is to find out what happened there.  Like in the 1C King's Bounty games before it or the Heroes of Might and Magic series, the battles are fought on a grid-based system with stacks of units: If your stack of three spearmen attacks the enemy's three skeletons, they might deal enough damage to kill one so that you're only counterattacked by two skeletons. In combat, you control up to 5 stacks of different units which act according to their stats: From initative and speed to damage, health, and armor - there's enough to differentiate the unit types. Each of them also has a number of passive abilities such as ignoring enemy counterattacks or increasing stats the more damage the unit takes. Many units also sport one to three active abilities which often take up either their movement or attack action. These are things like healing allied units or applying buffs to themselves. With the fifty or so unit types in the game, I feel like there's plenty of depth and variety here.  During fights, your hero can support by casting one spell each round, either from a scroll or one that was previously learned and will cost mana. A modicum of magic knowledge is basically needed since your hero can't use that action to attack directly.  You can recruit units into your army by spending gold and recruiter NPCs, each of which only has a limited selection. Your hero is also limited in how many units they can bring in a stack by how much Leadership they have: With 700 Leadership, you can only bring seven 100 Leadership units per stack or three 200 Leadership units. Unlike in previous iterations or HoMM, units in KB2 also have a maximum stack size. Even for the smallest units, you can't ever have more than 10 in a stack. That means no 2,000-peasant-doomstack - early game units will quickly fall off in effectiveness. This forces you to regularly adjust your army composition instead of just getting more of the same dudes as your Leadership increases.  Something that counteracts this phenomenon a bit is that units can level up twice, gaining a significant amount of stats and sometimes new abilites, as well. This level-up applies to all units of the type, so even if your stack gets wiped, the newly recruited one will retain the higher level. But this makes it so that changing to a new unit of higher tier but lower level will often weaken your overall strength. Yet, as I stated earlier, you have to switch eventually. It feels a bit off, to be honest. At least you now have an infinite potential reserve of units where you can just park your old units or ones you don't want to use yet. And you can choose to revive all fallen units at the end of each battle for a small fee instead of having to run all the way back to the recruiter each time.As your hero fights and completes quests, you gain experience, gold, and mana.  Experience provides level up which increase Leadership and, depending on which hero you picked, some of your stats. These stats, in turn, either increase the power of your army or your spellcasting ability in battle. Equippable items provide similar bonuses and allow for further customization. Leveling up also provides a skill point (more than one on higher levels) which can be spent on one of four skill trees. These harken back to the ideals I mentioned before and higher tier skills require you to have made several choices in favor of that ideal in addition to having unlocked some other talents in the tree. These double requirements don't feel quite right to me and I wonder whether it would have been better to require a sum total of x points spent in the skill tree and/or gained from choices instead. The skills themselves feel appropriately impactful for the most part, with the final ones in each tree being particularly juicy like the ability to cast a second spell each turn or resurrecting the first unit that dies each battle.  Gold is simply used to buy more units or items - whether gear or scrolls. Mana, finally, is used to learn spells from scrolls and upgrade them to a higher level. Noteably, overworld mana is independent from combat mana, the latter being refilled for each fight.  One last note on difficulty: You better get a grip quick in this game. You can probably win most individual battles without trying too hard, but going from one pyrrhic victory to another will absolutely leave you starved for gold. Eventually, you'll be unable to replenish your army, not to mention buy higher power units. You can absolutely soft lock the game this way because there are only finite resources on the map. However, there are definitely ways to cheese the AI and the mechanics using some of the higher tier abilities.I've pointed out a ton of problems this game has but I have little issue looking past them. It hits the right spot for me regardless. There's just something about wandering through a fantasy world, slowly clearing it of enemies and looting everything. That feeling when you come out of a tough fight without losses certainly helps, too.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like King's Bounty as a concept, so I force myself to keep playing this game, because at some point, I hope I will see the light.BUT 10 hours in, I am still not convinced.The Good:I love the battles. The battle mechanic is recognizable from the previous games and I just love the more detailed and colourful details of casting magic etc.The graphics are an improvement from the old games, but are by no means up to the standard of todays top games.The Bad:There are som small annoyances (like, why are you slowed down, when riding your horse in towns), but the single most problematic thing is the lack of "casual-ness".What really got me attracted to the previous games, was how they were more casual. You could click at a point in the overview map, and the hero would move there (more or less) while you (IRL) could talk to others or do other stuff. In the previous games, you often had a lot of grinding to do, where you had to travel between a lot of places to rebuild your army... Tedious, but being casual meant, you could commit to doing other stuff at the same time, which helped removed the negative feeling of wasting your time.In this new game, you are no longer seeing the world top down, but you are controlling and moving the hero in 3D. This means if you stop pressing the forward key, the hero stops moving. The result is, that you have to have your eyes glued to the screen to make sure you navigate your hero around obstacles - that you have passed a 1000 times. This is so boring and really promotes the feeling of tediousness - and of wasting your time.If I was granted one wish, it would be, that we were given the option of using the map for navigation.

_childDocuments_.review: I have finished the game and enjoyed completing it in 93 hours while doing all the quests. I definitely recommend it although it has some downsides but overall it is a great game. I bought it on preorder and it did not disappoint! The good: - Beautiful graphics compared to the previous games (it`s not Cyberpunk 2077 or Assassin's Creed Valhalla still very beautiful graphics, much love for the detail of the areas, there are a lot of objects that are placed in a way that everything feels alive and believable, although textures are sometimes low res - There are a lot of areas with nice vibrant colors, filled with light, that make you feel relaxed and happy (hope for an elves specific map with this design), something that is missing from a lot of games today that have only dark/heavy/unhappy feeling areas - Combat is really fun and the animations and effects are nicely done - There are different skill trees and depending on your choices you can explore some parts of the tree while locking others (makes you want to make more runs) - You find a lot of loot in every bush/corner of the road, makes you explore not only the cities but also the surroundings while watching the beautiful landscape - Small distances between areas, you don`t have to walk too much if you don`t want to - I like that unit group`s HP bar is the sum of all units and you can`t just heal to full for much of the game (makes you want to take care of the units and play more strategically) - Units can also level up and they sometimes get new abilities besides stat increases, also units are of different tiers - I don`t mind the speed of movement (except the horse should not be walking in the cities so everyone has a choice of what speed they want to move at) as it gives you time to explore the nice graphics and the relaxing views plus distances are pretty small between objectives and there is always a fast travel point nearby (if you want to travel that way) - The music tracks are very good, i hope they will add more of them in the futureThe bad: - There are very few fights and lots of walking and questing. I would really want more fights in the game. I heard in the live stream that the devs said they don`t want more repetitive fights but more quality fights. If they want that it is fine, but quality fights does not mean LESS fights. I also don`t mind repetitive to a degree. Also there are no boss unit fights unfortunately - The game has NO CLEAR ENDING. I thought game was bugged as i had no more main quests and i continue playing with no indication that the game has ended. Never ever experienced something similar, not even in a under 10€ game. After searching for new clues/quests and nothing more being available i found out from YouTube that the game really ended. That is very weird - I played the Mage class and when i picked it up it said: "Your nephew Maurice had taken over your county and you are going to take it back" than i did all the game`s quests AND YOU NEVER EVER HEAR AGAIN ABOUT HAVING TO GO AND TAKE YOUR COUNTY BACK. I MEAN THAT IS THE PURPUSE OF THE MAGE FROM WHAT YOU READ WHEN YOU PICK IT! That is again super weird (Story seems to be incomplete/unfinished unfortunately) and this is a 60€ game on preorder - The main story is pretty interesting at the beginning and pretty bad afterwards, i hope they will work on it more/rewrite some of it, make the player emotionally attached to it, make it believable and give me real reasons why i want to experience it more (especially since a lot of the game is a story driven RPG) - The game is basically a console exclusive port where they enabled the mouse but serves no function (no mouse hovering info, you have to enter with the keyboard in 2-3 screens to see the stats of the units instead of having mouse hovering). Also interface overlaps in combat and you can`t see stuff as it gets left behind other menus - There are no dialogue options when talking to the NPCs, the main character and NPCs only talk by themselves (i would like to see dialogue choices in the future that also impact the game`s outcome when you choose a dialogue option over the other). Right now you only change the outcome by doing certain actions or picking where to go or who to talk to - NPC faces are a lot of times the same, a bigger variety/uniqueness would be much appreciated - Unit variety and items are on the low side, still the implemented ones are of good quality - I was hoping for more content, more maps, more items more units instead of repetitive questing content (see the devs said they wanted quality combat and not repetitive, but on quests sometimes this does not apply). Still a lot of quests are interesting and fun and they finish nice and quickly (they don`t make you grind for hours) - I was hoping for a map for each faction (hope to see elves soon) - There is a ray that has to be guided by reflection in the mirror quest that bugs out and you get stuck there. Need to reload the game a lot to make it work and the ray to reflect as it should - There is a horse equipment slot in the inventory that is never ever used during gameplay, why is there such an option in a finished game that is not usable is just a big mystery and adds to the feeling that the game is unfinished/rushed - The music tracks have some long pauses between them and on the default settings are not that loud, you have to turn them up a bit. I wish there was a setting for the timing/elimination of the pause between music tracks - There are some game replayability options implemented but i wish to see more of these so players will be willing to make a lot more runs in the futureI hope they will add more units, items, spells in the game, more faction maps, more fighting, more replayability options, more music tracks. I also hope they will make the story more interesting and if they say the Mage wants to get it`s county back then let`s see that in the story/action not ignore what they say in the character`s main description. Also i hope they will adapt the game for PC (use mouse features - hover and stuff, key rebinds and so on while letting the console elements just for console, basically making a true PC port as right now the PC version is not optimized for PC, although this series has it`s roots in the PC not on the console)They have a very good base, great graphics, they just need to finish the game and refine it a bit more (hope the next King`s Bounty games will be released in a finished state that makes sense). Great job devs, even if it`s not perfect i enjoyed the game a lot and i am willing to go for new runs to get some hundreds of hours in, after you fix the game a bit more. Hope the review helps and much love to you!
