_childDocuments_.review: As a veteran player of the "Hunter: Call of the Wild" and the more recent "Way of the Hunter" games, I can safely say this game is pretty good and can stand up to the rest of them.After a (thankfully) brief tutorial showing you the basics of tracking an animal and giving commands to your dog, the game takes you back to your hunting lodge to buy and pick your equipment and licenses, pick the time and day you want to start hunting at, and which hunting area you want to hunt at. Unlike the other two titles mentioned, there doesn't seem to be (as far as I can tell) a "Day-Night" cycle while you're out in the field so you can stick around as long as possible without having to head back to camp or the lodge and wait or sleep until a specific time.Notice how I said "buy and pick your equipment and licenses". Unlike Hunter: Call of the Wild and Way of the Hunter, you WILL need to purchase licenses to hunt animals and just like the other games you have to use specific ammo on a specific animal you choose to hunt and shoot. If you don't have a license for it, you will receive a fine. So be sure to buy a few licences before you go out and hunt. And YES, you do have to buy specific Game Licenses for specific Hunting Preserves. On the Licenses though, if you hit the info screen it'll tell you what game licences allows you to use what ammo types for these animals, and if you ever forget what licenses you already have while in the field, you can hit escape and check your collection at any time.This Game is NOT for beginners. There is no HUD outside of your compass and a few navigation icons. The game WILL NOT mark need zones, trails, or blinds for you on the map for you as you have to do this yourself. There are tents and camp sights you can discover and fast travel between but that's it. You have to put your own map markers and track the animals yourself or with your hunting dog. There's no special "Hunter Vision" like in Way of the Hunter that will allow you to spot tracks and need zones, and there's no "aura" that pops up when you're near a track like in Hunter: Call of the wild. The tracks you find will have a slight highlight to them as you get close to them and when you examine them it'll tell you what type of track it is, a numerical heading, and how fresh the track is. This game will not hold your hand and lead you to the next track if it's too old, and it's not going to jump out at you like "Blue's Clues".All in all, I found this game to be an interesting simulator. Not as predictable and simplified as Hunter: Call of the Wild, and not as Story Driven and easy as Way of the Hunter. If you're NEW to hunting Simulators, maybe play one of the other titles first to get an idea of how hunting games usually work. If you're coming from any of the other titles, it'll feel very familiar and won't have as many training wheels on it.I give it a double lung shot out of a heart shot.

_childDocuments_.review: I am VERY new to the hunting genre, and I do own this and the "other game" a lot of the other reviews are talking about. First, I'd say, they are different games, they're trying to do different things. This game is a little bit more friendly to newer players, I think, although I do have a few suggestions to consider: When you're buying a weapon and asked to specify the gauge of rifling, it would be nice to see a list of animals that are legal targets for the gauge you're choosing. Also, we need an auto-walk button, that's vital for a game like this and it is missing (I did bind a keyboard macro, but this is an obvious keybind that's needed in the game). The dog mechanic is awesome, I love it. I was never quite clear why I was able to spot animal tracks from 50 feet away in the other game like I'm the freakin' Predator. The dog explains that! I am very excited to buy a Labrador and do some duck hunting. This game is in Unreal Engine, and so the ballistics feel like ballistics feel in the Unreal Engine. It's really that simple. It's hard to get a read on bullet drop and I'm forced to conclude that wind and wind direction simply isn't a factor in this game, as there is no gauge for it or indicator of any kind. Again: beginner-friendly, but maybe not 100% immersive. Personally, for me, that's fine! Also, I feel like the actual walking/locomotion in this game is far superior. The pace of walking is slightly more generous, and I feel (for now) like animals aren't necessarily going to run away at full speed if I step on a twig from 100 yards away. I can see how this might get slightly repetitive, but...what is life but repetition, to one degree or another? Just like actually hunting, the experience is going to be vaguely the same each time out of the lodge, but the exact way things play out will differ. Add a menu option to quick-travel to the cabin, please. When I'm done hunting, I want to be done ASAP. It might be because my family needs me IRL or I have a work project that pops up or whatever, and whatever the reason, I don't want to walk back to the cabin to claim my animals after all the walking I already just did. I really did enjoy the game, and I'll be playing it a lot. For *my* money it's certainly worth what I paid for it, and I suspect that oiver time I will play this game more than the "other" one.

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, at first i was very sceptical.But after spending 80+ hours in this game it´s now time to write a review.Maybe it´s useful to know that i´m playing Deer Hunter 2005 for about 15 years now and i still enjoy it.So my perspective on hunting games in general is surely a little different.Personally i really like Hunting Simulator 2 for several reasons:The weapons and items are accessible from the beginning and not locked behind levels or missions or whatever else.The amount of credits needed is fair and it doesn't requires countless hours to get a decent set of gear to play the game like you want to play it.The dog system is great.I prefer to have my hunting dog beside me than constantly watching a radar or other digital device to track an animal.Visually it's a joy to walk through the forests, meadows and deserts. I like the look & feel of the game, the sounds in the different areas are atmospheric.The latest update improved the lighting and some textures.Overall i´m very happy with the game.As always there is room for improvement so i have a personal wish list with some features and additions:Binoculars and scopes with variable zoom option would be great.Please add a muzzleloader to the arsenal and portable tree stands.The latest update had statistics for trophy comparison. A step in the right direction. It would be great to have detailed statistics on every animal species and your hunting history.In addition to the existing option to set the daytime for your hunt i would love to see the option for different seasons.To have more areas and animal species would be nice, but i´m not a fan of buying dlc after dlc for everything.Overall i like the game and i can recommend it if you want a relaxing and atmospheric hunting game that you can play like you want to.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played this game to its full extent so I believe I am ready to give my most accurate review.First off, I gave a thumbs up because I personally have been enjoying the gameplay. It has ups and downs. The good balances out the bads but things definitely need changed. So I am going to list things piece by piece.Clothing: I love the different styles BUT I would like to see the different camos having effect on animal visibility towards the hunter. I would also like to see the clothing stored in the room at the lodge such as the weapons and equipment. Overall it is minor things I would like to see but all in all clothing is pretty great.Weapons: As people have mentioned before the weapons should feel more authentic. Such as recoil and sound. (Things that have been mentioned in other reviews) Bows are pretty useless in this state of the game. Aiming down sight is brutal. The pins are not effective and arrow drop off is very bad. Ammo situation on all of the weapons seems fine. I like the concept that you need to go back and refill forcing you to make more ethical shots.Dogs: So I still have mixed feelings for the dogs. The retrievers are a MUST to waterfowl hunt and seem like the most superior breed at this time. My biggest thing is that the dogs will spook any animal within 75m. There should be an option to make your dog lay down allowing animals to come in closer. For example, I was hunting in a tree stand while calling in a Grizzly Bear. I never saw the bear because it was behind loads of trees which resulted in it being spooked from my dog before I ever even saw it.Monetary System: This is a BIG deal. Everything in game is very cheap. Especially when you get a cougar license and go hunt the plains over and over again. This needs to be changed. It does not take long to unlock everything in the game.Lodge: The lodge looks FANTASTIC. But the only thing I would like added is to see scores and weights on your trophys so you can effectively change your taxidermized trophys without questioning if it is bigger than your current one.Animals: Rabbit behavior is a little weird to me. They should be flushed out like the birds can but instead they will spook very very easily and you'll never get a good shot. If the behavior is not changed then developers should think about adding a .22 long rifle into the game. Animal models for the most part are great. Sitka deer need a complete remodel. The fur could be changed to look more authentic. The turkeys bodies look painted on and look like wood rather than feathers. (No turkey call either which is disappointing)All in all, this game is fun to me. I also play Call of the Wild and The Hunter Classic a lot. I would love to see improvements made quickly to this game to make it more enjoyable. Multiplayer is also very big in hunting games. I am not sure if it in the plans to possibly let you hunt with a friend or two but I feel like it would be HUGE for this game. I hope the developers and community managers read into these reviews and take them seriously because there is a lot of potential here. My overall rating for this game in the current state would be a 6/10. I will still continue to play it and support it if content is added frequently and changes are made regularly. Hope this review helps anyone looking to buy the game. I recommend it but you also need to take the time to learn it and how to effectively hunt.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, tried this out hoping maybe this would be better or at least different than The Hunter: Call of the Wild but this isn't the game to take your business over to the competition with. While I can't recommend that game either this one's no improvement or even a more action oriented game that I would have been okay with at this point. (COTW was better at getting the player and it's animals together but that's where that title falls apart).In 6 hours of playtime both ambushing and stalking gameplay styles produced no encounters. This sandbox feels dead and unpopulated and like there may have been animals in it a week ago since they've left their ancient tracks around but they go nowhere and don't get any fresher. I have to wonder if this is just a forest environment and a scripted tutorial being sold as a hunting simulation. It would seem that more work than that has been put into this but I really have my doubts about that now.Either this is super deep simulation and 6 hours wasn't nearly long enough (in which case the map scale is way too small for that realistic of a simulation and who really has that much time anymore) or crotchwalk ridgelines glassing down into shady valleys, listening for calls, and hoping to spot a herd or come across some somewhat fresh tracks to follow alternating with calling from concealment on the edge of such valleys I have a good vantage over to try and bring something my way or elicit a call instead isn't an effective play style for this genre.The simulation isn't given any clues as to how I should play it differently if it wants the player to engage with it differently. The dog just loses the trail when you set it on some old tracks since they really don't go anywhere and don't get any fresher. I'm out of ideas how I should play such games.I'll be going back to COTW, I can't recommend that either but at least it can get the player together with it's core gameplay loop in under an hour.Can't recommend this title for working adults.

_childDocuments_.review: If all you want to hear is the answer to the question, "Is this game worth the $40 price tag?"  My answer, sadly, is no.  Not yet, anyway.I have a couple hundred hours in theHunter: Call of the Wild as well as about another 50 or so in the original "theHunter".  I am *not*, however, a hunter in real life.  I fish, but don't hunt.  It's impossible not to draw comparisons between this game ($40) and theHunter:CotW ($20, + a lot of paid DLC).  I will, however, attempt to review this title solely on its own merits - with my measly hour of gameplay behind me and zero interest in a refund.The Positives:+ Nice graphics+ Dog companions are an interesting optional element+ Many different firearms & bows to choose from drawn from the real world.+ A lodge to display your trophies+ Weapon & Item costs are at a good spot.  You're not going to get a new rifle after every kill, but after a good hunt  you'll be able to expand your loadout a little. The Negatives:- The UI/Menu system.  This is the biggest negative to me because it looks and feels like a mobile game.  I paid $40 for a PC game, not a mobile port.  These menus (ESPECIALLY THE RADIALS) need to be reworked not only in looks but in functionality.  They feel disgusting to use with a mouse.- Player animations are, at best, 'functional' - and not entirely that.  The transitions between animations are clunky and look bad.- Maps are so small!  I find it hard to believe people find it difficult to find animals because they're everywhere on very small maps.- How do I zoom/focus with binoculars/rangefinders?  Can you?  I don't know.  I do know I'm somehow unable to spot animals with the binocular/rangefinder combo which completely defeats the purpose of having them.- Animal behaviors are suspect.  I had elk approach me within touching distance but ducks get stuck flying into my cabin.   Yes, that happened.  I came back from a hunt and there were buttloads of ducks flying in the corner.-  The UI again, but there's no HUD.  This game needs one, desperately.  The tracking system is also pretty limited, especially when things don't appear on the (also terrible) map.  I like the idea of putting different markers on the map for when I spot animals - but why isn't it automatic?  My do I have to open the map, guesstimate where the animals were, click to open the markers, select the right marker, then double click it and back out of the map?  The marker is also ENORMOUS on the map, and invisible in the game proper!  What's the point?Overall, I am not going to ask for a refund.  In the few hours the game's been live the devs have been responding to review and comments and that gives me hope for the game.  Right now, it's not worth $40, but ask me again in 6 months to a year and that answer might change.   Currently it's not an actual "Hunting Simulator" so much as an Mobile-to-PC Ported Arcade Shooter w/ "Hunting" Trappings draped over the top.  Does that sound harsh?  Maybe.  But it's still fun.   I do not currently recommend the game for the $40 price tag.  For $15, yeah.  $20 is iffy.

_childDocuments_.review: Actually I've fallen in love with this game despite what most people say about it. At first I was sceptical about it and decided to try "trial version" (if you know what I mean ;)) but I liked it so much so I decided to buy it to support the developers. These guys did an incredible job of turning the weird and unplayable first HS into a decent game that just needs some polishing.Everyone compares it to tCotW but to me tCotW loses in most points. Let's see:1) You can only carry two big guns unlike in tCotW where you can run around armed to the teeth like the Doom Guy and you don't even get exhausted. Here you get exhausted after sprinting with a full backpack and your guns.2) Your arsenal include a lot of beautiful real-life guns, the models look fantastic and animations are great. Also you can look at the guns from all angles and zoom. Meanwhile in tCotW guns are ugly parodies of their real-life prototypes and you can't even look at them to admire. They are always fixed in your hands. The only way you can look at guns in tCotW is buying the African lodge DLC and putting them on stands.3) You can buy rifles in different calibres. Also scopes management is more realistic, you have to put a different scope on a different rifle, in tCotW you just put a scope in your inventory and it magically places itself on every gun you carry and magically disappears and appears immediately after pressing a button.4) Also calibres are suitable for wider range of animals, unlike in tCotW where you need a separate gun for different animals (now it's better than used to be).5) You cannot carry crates of ammo with you (look at tCotW)6) There are no arcade indicators of wind, visibility and noise (praise to theHunter Classic!)7) Most markers can be switched off, and they are not really invasive. The interface hides itself when the info is not needed (like in my beloved theHunter Classic).8) There are many types of animal clues (tracks, feces, urine, blood, disturbed vegetation, food leftovers etc.). Also they don’t tell you the info right away and you have to analyze the clues (like feces are cold and dry for example, so it’s old). Also tracks don’t shine like neon lights at a night club and don’t get pushed into your eyes so much as in tCotW where you can see shiny tracks from another side of the reserve). Also animal clues stay even after their death (in tCotW all tracks and blood drops magically disappear not to confuse the player).9) Unlike in tCotW that’s in fact a FPS, you cannot run around and shoot everything in bursts. First, you need to buy licenses for specific animals, also the game fines you for too many shots, killing some females, poaching (you cannot even claim such an animal and you get a fine), shooting with wrong caliber and if you don’t grab a downed animal. So it leads to more calculated and thoughtful gameplay.10) Animals won’t come back to you again and again after you spooked them, also I’m not sure there are some “need zones” you can farm till you drop. They learnt from the Classic. You can’t hit an animal heel so it will eventually bleed out. Most likely the animal will be lost for you. So aim better.11) DOGS! You just need to teach them and yourself to operate.12) You can customize your character clothes and they really affect your visibility (like in theH:C). Also you can switch to the 3rd person view. And the model and animation are pretty decent.13) The night doesn’t replace the day in an hour of real time (tCotW?)14) The interface is nicely joined with objects in your lodge, the lodge is very comfy.15) Very nice landscapes and nature. The maps are not very big but they give impression of something grand. Also they look photorealistic sometimes. The atmosphere of nature is just great. I mostly hunted in European maps and it feels like home.16) You are not forced to grind. Guns are affordable and they all are available (no DLCs or locked content), so you can run the game any time you want and just RP real hunting.Now, what is BAD:1)	The stupid circle in the middle of the screen cannot be off, also when you shoot with iron sights, you have to aim with the circle and not the iron sights. Just why???2)	Guns look awesome but lack in sound and feeling of recoil, could be more impressive (anyone who shoots IRL understands)3)	You cannot operate the bolt/pump/lever/other kind of reloading mechanism manually and it can’t be switched. The game pulls the bolt automatically. Why? _childDocuments_.review: Simply put, this isn't worthy of having the word "Simulator" in its title... HS2 looked promising based on the trailers and screenshots of playtime on the steam store.  But the game falls quite short of delivering a realistic simulated hunting experience.  I won't wade deep into the game mechanics or ui quality, other than to say they're sub-par considering the price this title is being sold for.  Frankly I wouldn't care about that, if the game actually "simulated" hunting in a realistic way...  That's where HS2 falls way short.  There's so many aspects to hunting that are clearly missed here.  Starting with the low hanging fruit... The firearms simulation is horrible...  It seems the developers only goal was to attempt to give a somewhat accurate visible representation of the firearm make and model used.  Getting licensed makes and models of real firearms was a commendable start.  Beyond that however, everything else was left at the table.  I'd love to see an accurate representation of firearms handling simulated some day.  A hunting Simulator isn't a FPS game.  Fast twitch, unrealistic firearm mechanics inclusive only of a reload button need not apply here...  It would be cool to see a realistic modeling of manipulating a firearms action (use of a saftey, removing/replacing/loading individual rounds in a magazine, opening of an action, zeroing with various types of ammo/optics, for shotguns, choke, shot size, load selection, shell length, slugs, buckshot, ect... ect...  would be very refreshing to see implemented).  I'll digress there, a list of realistic functions related to safe firearms handling could go on forever, I know...  The point is, outside of the listed gauge or caliber, noting else is really simulated with respect to firearms and their mechanics. On the actual hunting side of the game,... well...  This is just pure arcade fantasy.  It amounts to stumble around, follow your hunting companion (dog) and take shots at whatever game animal presents itself (that you have a licence for)...    There's so much missing here.  And so much that decades old PC Hunting Sims simulated better...   There should be seasons, when you start a new game, you should start on a date well in the preseason.  Scouting, use of trail cameras, planting food plots or bait stations, consideration for private property or property lines. ability to purchase property or obtain permission to hunt a property.  There's so much missing here that's part of the actual hunting experience.  All I can say is that it was really a let down... Not to mention the horribly unrealistic animal behaviour... Maybe I set the bar way to high with the over 25 years of hunting and firearms related experience I have...  I know I was eager to pay the extra $3 for the Beretta 486 Parallelo (How cool would it be to have my favorite gun thats in my safe simulated...) and would be willing to pay a lot more for something that actually delivers a realistic hunting experience...   What we need developed here is a simulator that is to hunting,  what Arma 3 and the Ace 3 mod is to small arms combat.  Something developed with a similar level of attention to detail to hunting...   Unfortunately, this title falls way way short.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is therapeutic, Let me explain!I watched a video about this game ("before you buy" type of video) and the guy reviewing the game was describing his experience when hunting his prey as relaxing and peaceful, when I heard that I thought to myself: "Isn't this a hunting game? I made the two Bears I hunted into trophies and a large male Deer into a trophy as well. There are many features I Enjoy in this game. To name a few I love that I have my very own dog to help me hunt (you can also pet the dog!<3) and I like how certain backpacks let you carry 2 Guns.Overall the game is very well made. Good graphics (but not at the cost of lag or bad FPS.) Beautiful maps and great replay value. I would 100% recommend this game to anyone who wants a semi-realistic immersive hunting experience that is relaxing, peaceful, and oddly therapeutic ;)

_childDocuments_.review: What does this game have going for it? Well... it's the first (to my knowledge) in its genre to implement a mechanic involving hunting dogs, which will track, retrieve animals, or interact with animals by distracting them or pointing them out. I absolutely love this mechanic, and wish more games in this genre would consider such a thing in the future.... otherwise... don't bother. While the game is not horrible, it lacks a large amount of fine tuning and polish for such a high price tag. On my first play attempt - I managed to more or less soft-lock myself. How? You can't bag water fowl unless you have a retriever, so if that was your starting tag - and you didn't buy the retriever, you can lose a large amount of money in 'fines' for failing to collect a downed animal. With no money to buy new tags, and the only tag available to you being for animals you can't bag - this makes any further gameplay impossible.In addition to that, the gunplay - which is the single most important feature, I'd suggest, for a hunting game... is severely lacking. There is a range - but the range focuses you on random targets rather than allowing you any stationary ones to shoot at. This makes it nearly impossible to reliably test things such as range, bullet drop, and particularly... shotgun spread.Tracking sucks - many of the tracks are hard to see, and extremely inconsistent as far as distance between each one is concerned (sometimes there'll be no further tracks for miles, other times there'll be like, 20 crammed into a very narrow space). While this can be forgiven by the hunting dogs' ability to track for you - you shouldn't have to rely on it to get things done.Finally... the ammo system sucks. Certain ammo types go to certain animals - however there is no differentiation between shotgun shells... and I'd even go so far as to say that somehow, in this universe, only birdshot exists... as despite the fact that buckshot and slugs are real things - many of the shotguns in the game are only allowed for use on small game. Furthermore, while you don't have to buy ammo (you are given a set amount for free when you head out), the amount you are given seems highly arbitrary... and you can't stockpile - you take what the game gives you, and if you knew for fact you'd need more? Too bad.Most of these are simply polish problems - but there are other titles in the genre which are cheaper, and much more polished already. The only reason I feel the need to be so critical with this review is because of the high price tag. Unless you are a collector who wants as many hunting games as possible I highly recommend looking into other hunting games.

_childDocuments_.review: I had hoped for the best, but this isn't a very good game.There's no sound or wind indicator (unless you buy the wind powder), so you're never sure how close an animal is to detecting you.You get randomly fined, which is fine, whatever, it's how they decided to build their game. It's just kinda dumb.But the worse part is water fowl hunting. You can't enter water, your dog won't retrieve animals in ponds or lakes, and they don't float to the edges. As I type this I have 8 dead geese just stationary in the middle of a 20ft pond. lolI'm out of ammo, and can't bag any of them.Another issue is the tracks. If you have even a 5 year old video card you can run the graphics on "epic". And it looks nice. Not great, but nice. But if you run the highest level of foliage you will **NEVER** see a track. No way, no how.Oh sure, you can turn on the track indicator, and you get a giant arrow over them pointing at it. lolIt's the most generic immersive breaking feature in the game.So the choice is, giant arrow pointing at every track, or intentionally turning down the graphics and making the game look crappier.Or just putting the game on cruise control and have your dog do everything.In short, I went all in, I bought all the DLC and everything. But I'm requesting a refund. The game is just too broken to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Still getting my footing. But here is my early assessment. Watch a YouTube video or two. This game has a short tutorial. Easy. You figure you are going to be a decent hunter your first time out. My experience was that I did not want to spend a lot of money of gear and have no nest egg. So, I armed myself, made sure I had the right ammo, and bought a Mule Deer license. I traveled to Texas. My puppers roamed around and picked up a trail. It's on! After an hour and repeatedly getting lost, my dog ended up walking into a rock and walking in place. I gave up on him. I glassed the hills and finally found my first Mule Deer. It gave me the notification that I did not possess a license. So. I assume after buying it, I needed to equip it. But yeah. I spent an hour finding prey that I could not shoot.EDIT: Turns out I bought the Mule Deer license for the wrong region. I am a moron.The graphics are passable. Not great. I have all setting on epic and see lots of pop-ins at short distances. Trees will flesh out and detail when you are relatively close. Muted and lifeless from even near distances. The Texan desert looks like dirt and scrub from a distance. If you glass the area, you will see tons of foliage. It takes me out of the immersion.Shooting an animal in the tutorial, there is a cartoonish hit indicator when you hit your mark. It looks like something that belongs in Borderlands or another FPS. It doesn't look satisfying here. I would rather track the animal after presuming I hit it and be rewarded with blood. I definitely do not need a cartoonish blip on my reticle.Your doggos pathfinding is decent. But can lead them into walking into a wall, like a mentioned before. This is terribly immersion breaking. Sunsets in the desert seemed to last forever. I am not sure if there is a day and night cycle, but having an eternal golden hour in the desert was a little odd.I want to like this game. So far it feels a lot simpler than tH: CotW. Which is not a bad thing. It lacks some of the personality and quests, as far as I can tell. But I am a novice at hunting games and could use a little hand holding. I am hoping the devs continue to improve this game. I look forward to seeing the directions it takes. If they make QoL improvements and keep it well oiled, I will be buying any DLC that comes down the line.

_childDocuments_.review: Update 1 (1 hour game play - Positive) First impressions are good. There are patches to be had, couple of clunky animations, couple of animal models need some love and the immersion settings could do with a couple more options. I don't doubt they will be implemented in future patches and I look forward to that. Generally though, It's got some really good elements; lots of customisation, really nice looking maps, dogs, general pace etc...I'll update the review after I get more of a feel what's happening but so far, happy I purchased. Update 2 (4.6 hours game play - Negative)Okay, so after the first few hours I can safely say - It's bad, hopefully, just for now.There's a lot of work to be done on this game - Don't even consider paying full price for it in its current state. It's barely worth £10 and in all honesty if it was free to play, I probably would have just uninstalled it and kept an eye on the community feedback. Other people have already listed the specific pro's and con's and I largely agree with the general consensus, so I'm not going to do that. The vast majority of issues could be forgiven with exceptional game play - but that isn't the case. I really want to like it - there are some things in the game I can get behind and some that are just bad. - If you can't even get 10 hours into a game without it feeling like a chore how do you expect people to be happy paying the current price + fork out for DLC. I'll update again and potentially change my recommendation selection based on either getting to 10+ hours game play or an improvement by way of patches etc...Otherwise this game will sit in my library as a reminder of what could have been... I know no one asked but what happened to getting a finished game on release? How has it become acceptable to release (and charge people) for half a game and promise the other half at some point in the future. Bugs, performance issues, general updates - Okay, I understand that. Charging people for half a game, I don't get.Anyway, I hope this helps some people in their decision. Play it safe, keep an eye out for updates and such, and pick it up if they turn things around.

name: Cannibal Cuisine
detailed_description: The recipes for success are varied; find delicious fruits and vegetables, and combine them with freshly chopped and cooked tourists for a truly divine delicacy fit for the God Hoochooboo. Of course the tourists might not offer themselves up freely, the heathens, so you’ll need to master your arcade reflexes and special powers (like fire breathing for baking) to persuade them without getting KO’d! Tour the island Ready, steady, cook your way through many levels in a full campaign across the island. Overcome spikes in mysterious temples, bushwhack your way through tourist infested jungles and stay away from lava in the underground. Other-foodly activities All kinds of extra-culinary skills are needed too to appease Hoochooboo. Skills such as outrunning the Spikey Log of Doom™, defeating waves of tourists and the tour boss in the jungle arena, as well as other challenge levels to prove yourself as the one true cook. Choose your cooking style Special powers are the perfect ingredients for success, allowing you to dash, place healing totems or even breathe fire. In multiplayer each chef can choose a different ability to fit their cooking style. Foodfest or Foodfight Cook your way through hell’s kitchen solo or with up to 4 chefs. Or challenge each other to foodfights in PvP. With so many chefs in the kitchen, chaos is sure to follow. Cannibal Cuisine features: Arcade combat with unfortunate tourists - don't forget your special powers! Navigate varied tropical levels to collect extra ingredients and prepare Hoochooboo’s meals. Many levels of cannibal chaos in the jungle, temple, on the beach, and inside a volcano! Choose your cannibal couture with many options for weapons and accessories. Play solo, cooperatively, or in versus mode with 1-4 players. A new threat: The Scarab King The Scarab King has cursed the land and spawned Hoochooboo all over the desert. Defeat The Scarab King to lift the curse! 'The Curse of the Scarab King' is a free content update that adds 5 regular cooking levels and a challenge level within a new environment. It also introduces new mechanics, extra deadly traps and cosmetics in the new desert theme.

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting take on the ever expanding Co-op multitasking genre, i don't like always comparing these games to Overcooked but often they wear the similarities on their sleeve so it's very hard to avoid. Instead of making delicious pasta dishes in this game you're cutting people up for body parts to cook on a skewer, yeah maybe not as tasty but it does offer an interesting variation in gameplay. You also can choose some abilities for your character that offer some variation such as a healing totem of a flame breath you can use to cook skewers. The maps are set out so the poor tourists you are going to cut up for parts spawn from one side of the map and the fruits you use to combine with the meat are normally the other side. I played this 2 player and we generally stuck to one person slaying and another doing the cooking, this strategy worked for us going for 3 stars on each level. I'm sure other strats work as well but we found this fun.If i had some criticisms i would say the map design relies too heavily on rivers and pits that make traversal annoying to the point where as the person serving food i felt that the dash skill was essential, some moments where picking up and interacting with objects was funky/buggy but that's just par for the course with this genre of games and expected at this point. Only one song for the whole game got really grating but it's a small nitpick.The cannibal aspect is a humorous and interesting take on the genre with this being one of the only co-op multitask games to feature combat albeit very basic. I'd give this a chance on a discount if you like these sort of games, it offers enough new stuff and doesn't overstay it's welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: Cannibal Cuisine

(I'm a big overcooked fans, Full 3s Map)Despite some little bug (dishes not delivered in order if same dishes appear / dashing knock wall / little movement bug / etc), it did not actually impact big on gameplay like what other negative review.I would suggest some improvement needed in UI like:- display what item player grabbed as it quite hard to be notice- make the food icon bigger on campfire (also quite hard to differentiate when multiple ingredient are same color)A big thumb up for the creativity like killing human to get meat XD

_childDocuments_.review: Edit 2: A little more playtime (not much) and I just can't recommend this game - the movement of characters is still unsatisfying - CONSTANTLY falling off the map or clipping edges. Pausing doesn't do anything, timer and map continues going. The sensitivity on cooking time is way too fine - sometimes just 1 second more cooking decreases payout but other times that doesn't seem to be the case. I'd rather re-play overcooked. Edit: I've played more since the latest update (quickly released!) and can say it has made a world of difference! The game is no longer frustrating to play, and offers a fun challenge to attempt 3 stars on each level. Still a little difficult visually to see some elements, but overall that doesn't detract from the enjoyment. I went in hopeful, having loved the overcooked series. This game has a fun theme that appears well done, but it is severely hampered by poor controls. They feel very sloppy and loose, where your character doesn't do what you're expecting. Crossing rivers is hit-or-miss because unless you're aimed just right, you will appear to hit a wall and fall in. There's some levels where your character will move of it's own accord, but only in certain locations. The graphic design is nice, but it is VERY hard to see what food item you're carrying; some of the items like chili peppers are tiny and blend into the background. I haven't played enough to comment on lots of level design, because at this point I don't think i want to play that much.
_childDocuments_.name: Cannibal Cuisine

_childDocuments_.review: Cannibal Cuisine is a cooking game in a similar vein to the Overcooked series. You run around collecting your ingredients trying to beat the clock delivering your order on time.  What makes Cannibal Cuisine stand out is the titular cannibal aspect. Instead of working as a chef in a kitchen you are a tribal jungle person butchering tourists to feed a hungry god. Very simple, small game but fun in co-op. I would definitely recommend this to anyone who is a fan of Overcooked, or similar party games.
_childDocuments_.name: Cannibal Cuisine

_childDocuments_.review: My wife and I are big fans of games like Overcooked, and this is one of the better ones we've played, especially for its low price. I'd definitely recommend it if you like that style of local co-op game. We have 3-starred every level. The added variety of attacking humans for meat and having different power-ups is a neat idea.For improvements to the devs, I'd suggest continue working on the accuracy of control because it's too easy to pickup the wrong item even though the item you meant to grab is right in front of you. I'd also make the icons of the food cooking on the fire larger since they can be hard to see. Perhaps the most frustrating part of the game is when all your food orders are calling for a certain kind of meat and the humans never drop it. There were times we had to kill 10+ humans to finally get a leg, for example. This can ruin some 3-star attempts and it's entirely random/luck based.I hope to see more levels + DLC in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: Cannibal Cuisine is a console ported low poly 3D platespinner game where you're supposed to use console peasant like contollers to run around a lazy low poly arena tapping on people/things/whatever to make food (oh eat people like a cannibal, so edgy, must be worth AAA $13 USD).  Yeah look there's no gameplay here, it's pure trash.  I can sort of understand why Google and Apple rejected this trash, but it's on every console (for cheaper than on Steam, in case you were thinking these console devs weren't out to scam PC gamers).From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.The game features lazy low-polygon "retro" assets, making this look like a barely functional 3D game from the 1990s.  It's unclear why the developers weren't able to arrange high quality, high polygon count contemporary assets for the game, and also irrelevant... what matters is that this looks bad as a result of their decisions, a compromise PC gamers shouldn't have to put up with.PC gamers will be insulted by the presence of console peasant children's toy controller prompts, despite this being on PC.  Developers should try to be aware which platform they're developing for.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.Cannibal Cuisine has the greedy, cash grab price of $13 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games.  This is also competing with over 9,000 free games available on Steam, many of them far better than this paid product.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.I don't know what you want out of a game, but whatever it is, this garbage isn't it.  I guess other gamers have said this is a ripoff of the Cook, Serve, Delicious mobile app... fair enough.  That mobile app is better than this and cheaper on mobile phones.  So... after all is said and done, and knowing this is inferior to better quality mobile apps... why would you spend a ridiculous $13 USD on this?  You won't? Ok great!

_childDocuments_.review: Cannibal Cuisine is an indie gem about killing, cooking, and serving humans to cryptic gods. It's oddly adorable for a game about cannibals, and it has a lot of charm in its mechanics. I played it co-op, and my partner and I had a lot of fun getting three stars on every level. It's obviously not as polished as Overcooked (and no one could expect it to be with only a handful of people who worked on it), but it was one of my favorites of the genre Overcooked spawned. Though many reviews complain about a stiff difficulty curve, I didn't experience this, and I thought most levels were well-balanced with only maybe two exceptions. I'm astonished that this game has so few reviews, so I'll be happy to recommend it since I found it colorful, amusing, and the perfect amount of frustrating to be really fun.

name: Bear and Breakfast
detailed_description: Bear and Breakfast is a laid-back management adventure game where you play as a well-meaning bear trying to run a B+B in the woods. Hank and his friends find an abandoned shack and, equipped with their teenage ingenuity, turn it into a money-making bed and breakfast scheme for unsuspecting tourists. As your business expands so do the mysteries of the forest, and Hank soon finds himself uncovering a plot deeper than the wilderness itself. Build and personalize your inn with dozens of guest rooms, bathrooms, parlors, and entertainment. Each room can be individually customized completely from furniture to fixtures. Bring guests into the forest to stay at your inn. Keep 'em happy to maintain your reputation, earn money and attract new customers! Complete quests and story lines to collect new items and perks for your inn. Moving through the story-rich world of Bear and Breakfast will have you stumbling on dozens of interesting folks and weirdos, much like yourself. Most of them have something to say about your endeavors and if you take some time out of your day to listen, they might help your build your shack to new heights! Not everyone is as helpful or as needy though. Are you bear enough to search deep within the forest and your soul to find the mysteries that lie within?

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR score: 5/10So. The Bear and Breakfast retail release version - 1.0. I've been waiting for this since before the demo came out, and while the demo was promising-but-middling, I was hoping that the full release would fix some of the issues the game had.Unfortunately it did not.Let's start with the good. The art is *beautiful*, the sound quality and elements are spot on, and the game is colorful and vibrant. The 'atmosphere' of the game is enjoyable and my initial reaction is that this is a world I want to live in. However, art and atmosphere can only carry a game so far.When it comes to nuts and bolts, it feels like the developers actually reverted from the demo. I feel like I had less control on the management simulation side, and I still don't have the ability to undo mistakes. If you screw up the placement of a room, you are stuck, and there's nothing you can do about it. That feels REALLY BAD in a management simulation, given that the whole genre is about access to deep levels of micromanagement. Then there's the adventuring side, which just feels so very linear. I can't explore on my own; everything is walled away until it's time to open up. Even in some zones, large sections are just blocked off for no reason and you have to essentially follow the straight line path no matter what.It just feels like the game took the atmosphere from Stardew Valley and draped it over a half-finished, empty framework. And that breaks my heart because I desperately wanted this game to be better than that. It had, and still HAS, the potential to be better than that. But right now, at this moment? I can't recommend it. And definitely not at the $20 price tag they're charging for it.To put it succinctly: I'm not mad. I'm just disappointed. You could have done so much better.

_childDocuments_.review: The game isn't horrible, it has a cute design going for it, is very fun early on as you rebuild and then keep remodeling these different "resorts". But this game becomes a horrible grind later in the game as you need high end materials and recipes that cost outrageous amounts for what you're bringing in.  Sadly the trick to bypassing this is stocking up the resorts that require heat or food, hiring the right help to book your rooms, and then just walk away from the game as your money builds up.  You'll be doing this often, sadly because there's really nothing to keep your busy and entertained in the time that it takes to build up the massive fund you'll need to buy the things you need to upgrade and to offer better foods.  Then there's the story and characters.  The characters don't bring too much.  You'll interact with them once introduced but they won't really offer much shortly afterwards.  You'll need to go back to them at some point to get a quest item, and that's about it.  The guest coming to your resorts and just random nothing npcs. The story beyond playing as a bear, rebuilding these locations and bringing back visitors feels really out of place.  I recommended the game because it has things going for it, but this is really a game that requires an additional options.  There are things you'll probably enjoy about the game if this is the type of game you play, but it is very flawed and has a bit working against it that might turn you off, even if this is your type of game.

_childDocuments_.review: So I just finished this game (the story part at least), and I'd say overall its pretty good. Personally I am hoping they'll still add more to the plot (especially after Barbara), or at least side quests to meet some of the other gods (and do more with Vlad, cause I like Vlad and we didn't get a lot to do with him), but I don't regret buying it. All of the characters had a lot of personality that didn't feel forced or shallow, and I had a lot of fun meeting them all.The walk speed and collecting items didn't bother me very much, the only problem I had was much later in the game concerning iron plates, but it was an incremental issue, where I didn't have enough each day to craft ALL the items I wanted. If you like exploring the environment and collect the things you see as you go, this probably won't be a big inconvenience. I rarely ever ran out of materials other than cooking items. It took me way to long to find out you buy eggs, cheese, pasta etc at Ipswitch's shop though. I don't know if the game said this and I just didn't see it, or if they just expect you to find it if you're buying fuel (which I never did), but I didn't notice this until the Sous Vide Cheesecake questSome small technical things I'd like to see in the game, or if they're already there I couldn't figure out how to do them:- a way to buy several of the same item at once: I used a lot of the same item for decorations for example and it was a little tedious clicking and moving each one to my inventory one at a time- a way to grab one item from a stack or split stacks of the same item, specifically for cooking items: sometimes I want to make roast potatoes AND fries with the same stack of potatoes but I can't- a way to check the ingredients for a recipe remotely: there aren't a lot of places to harvest food that aren't going to be close to a kitchen, but its still annoying, especially when you get the recipe cards and it really feels like you should be able to check those and see what ingredients you need from anywhere in the world- a way to recycle or sell old items: this is one major issue I agree with other reviewers on

_childDocuments_.review: In its better moments, Bear and Breakfast is a pleasant, lite management game that will easily engross players in its combination of foraging, fetch questing and interior design. Many of the characters are charming and their interactions will likely get quite a few laughs from those who give this game a chance. There is enough variety in the rooms you can build and the objects you can place in them that there will be vastly different ways that players will choose to design their resorts, especially the latter two, Winterberry and Pinefall.Unfortunately, with as many hours as I've put into the game, I cannot say that it is a flawless experience.While playing, I've experienced a multitude of annoying bugs. Bugs like the guests being unable to get to their beds despite the player character, Hank the bear, being able to reach them without issue, or the bathrooms being permanently unavailable without anybody using them, which I would have to fix by detaching and reattaching the doors to them. There were times when the trash service would fail to actually clean up messes, requiring the player to either do it themselves or reactivate the service. The guests would never use the movie theater despite the room being considered functional by the game. Worst of all, towards the end of the game I lost the ability to cook food in Pinefall. Any attempt to do so would display a bugged version of the cooking menu that couldn't be closed, softlocking the game.Speaking of cooking, I felt that the game's story could've used some more time in the oven. The developer clearly recognized the value of having some sort of overarching plot to keep the player interested as they progressed throughout the game, and it does do that well enough. However, I felt like the story was unsure of what it wanted to be and that made some of the events feel tonally inconsistent. Like it didn't really know if it wanted to be commit to being family friendly, or lean more into adult humor, or have a serious storyline with tragedies and stakes. Towards the end of the game there is a point where the player is supposed to be emotionally invested in something that happens to Hank. This scene was hurt by the characters using the same goofy, comedic expressions they always do and it creates a disconnect between the text and the imagery.Also of note is the ending itself, which turns out to be much more of a whimper than a bang. The game builds up a backstory  and all of it just culminates in knocking down one last progress barrier, talking to a character and... nothing. No epilogue for the characters, no credits, not even a "thank you for playing!" message.  If it weren't for the achievements popping I would've struggled to know if I had accomplished something at all. It's like some game developers want to have their cake and eat it too. They want to have an engrossing story with loss and struggle and something to fight for, but if the game isn't about fighting or competition there's not much the story can do but fizzle out.All that said, I would still recommend this game for people who want to interact with funny animals while building up a small hospitality empire. Just, maybe wait for some updates and bug fixes if you want a smoother experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Bear and Breakfast is a fun and relaxing experience, it became that one game I can come back to, from time to time just to chill. _childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game but ultimately it falls too short for me to recommend it. The graphics are quite cute, and the concept of the game is great. However, the game is clunky, tedious, and buggy. It is simply just not much fun to play. There are lots and lots of little annoyances that add up to an overall unsatisfying experience. If the game had a total user interface overhaul and some significant quality of life adjustments, it could be a lot more fun.The environments are neat to look at but awful to navigate. Lots of small ground clutter items have collision enabled meaning trying to walk through an area is an exercise in frustration. I was constantly getting hung up on various small rocks or branches. My hand also really started to hurt after holding down the WASD keys so long with this game. There is a fast travel system, but not all areas have it and you have to walk around quite a bit to collect materials anyway. If I didn't get stuck on so much junk in the environment it wouldn't be quite so bad.The game claims to have controller support. With controller enabled, I found walking around less strain on my hands. However, the user interface was not designed for a controller and is extremely difficult to navigate using one. Most of the game is spent in menus to manage the building, crafting, cooking, and other hotel aspects. Thus, I was forced to go back to using keyboard and mouse for this game despite wishing I could use a controller. I couldn't even switch between controller and keyboard while playing because only one is enabled at a time for some reason.The user interface is a total mess. I frequently ran into bugs that duplicated items. The menus are difficult to navigate and often needlessly complicated to use. The cooking interface on the surface is an interesting system using action cards that are filled with the appropriate ingredient. But despite giving you an item to unlock auto-filling recipes later on, you can only cook 1 item at a time using this feature unless you drag over more ingredients for each card in the recipe. That completely defeats the purpose and it's very tedious to fully stock the dining rooms.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: You are a bear! On a walk through the forest with your animal buddies, you discover an abandoned building and a talking shark robot thing, who draws you into a pyramid scheme for developing resorts for tourists. Everything is hand drawn and the dialogue is really funny. Really everything about the game is relaxing and cosy. The gameplay loop revolves around building rooms for guests, meeting their needs for decor, comfort, heat, hygiene and food, whilst collecting their trash, designing special rooms and generally running a hotel business. Although in one regard it's very polished and there's lots of attention to detail, it does suffer a little from pacing and UI issues towards the end.[/b]Pros[/b]- The dialogue is brilliant. Pretty much every exchange had me smiling. Hank (the bear) is adorable.- I love that you're given dialogue options to choose from, but when you speak to the old lady it just says "Excited bear noises", and she still understands what you said- There are controls for different visibility options like walls down, walls up, roof on etc. (although I never used them and always had the walls down)Unlike games like Stardew, you can sleep through the night wherever you are any time after 9pm (but you don't have to)- There are LOTS of decor items in the game... although they get very expensive, and you don't get much trash to buy them with, so I never bought about 2/3 of the itemsBeautiful hand drawn art style and animations. I never got bored of seeing hank amble around the countryside (and you get an item a few hours into the game that doubles your walk speed)- I like the building system. Objects can stand on the floor, go on the wall, and some items can be stacked on top of other items like vases on tables- There's a few monuments in each area which you can fix up to increase the number of guests that request rooms each day. However, the areas are quite large and there's not really much to do in them so I'd love some more monuments to fix up- Over time, you unlock new UI features like the local map, a global map, telling the exact time etc.- Over time, you unlock new management loops for your guest houses such as bathrooms, cooking, dining rooms etc- There are a wide range of pretty environments to build in- The cooking mechanic feels quite unique, at least from the games I've played- Weather effects make the world feel a little more alive like rain, snow and heavy wind- Guests drop rubbish. Rubbish is used to buy decorations from the racoon. It's a nice little cycle that encourages you to keep a constant flow of guests so you can buy more decor. However, there's never enough trash so I always ended up just buying the cheapest smallest decor items to fill up the rooms to get guest scores met. If the decor you obtained was increased by about 50%, people would have a lot more freedom to build pretty rooms- Before we get to the cons, I will say that I think the game is excellent and I really enjoyed it. However, I do think it could do with being 20 hours rather than 30, and the final achievements are a really dull grind compared to the rest of the game.- I don't like the main reason you start the bed and breakfast - as part of a pyramid scheme for a shark robot. It would have fitted the game's aesthetic better if it was something like just because Hank wanted to meet humansIn the early game, there's very little to do during the day. There's nothing to do except wait for the guests to leave- You can't sell anything. Upgrading rooms means buying a constant stream of new furniture and decor, and there's never enough resources to do that at a decent pace, so allowing people to sell things for money / trash might help to offset the pacing issues- I can't see cooking recipes unless I'm in the kitchen, so I never know what I need to forage for or buy when I'm away from the kitchen- I had to google several of the quests. For example, there's a quest to get Tony a "Smol Bear Carving". Hank tells Tony that he's making it himself, which made me think I needed a blueprint and to craft it, but you actually buy it from the decoration vendor.- As you get towards the end of the game, you can hire staff which kind of help, but you can only hire them in one location each (one cook, one thermostat guy). I need to provide food for loads of guests in both Pinefall and Winterberry, and it's a massive chore trying to keep up with it- The end game feels poorly designed. You have to explore a series of caves that are as far away as you can get from a fast travel point, and you have to keep going back and forth to get prospectors tools, logging tools and cooked mealsThe UI is the game's biggest problem I think. For example, the "Organize inventory" button doesn't stack items. You can only buy one of something at a time. To transfer items into or out of the stash, you have to click the item, move it to a slot in the stash and click again over and over again. You can't just shift click an item to transfer it to a container.- There is an arbitrary inventory limit. I'm carrying hundreds of planks and tons of concrete, which is apparently fine, but there's a hard limit on inventory slots. This just gets in the way and has no positive effect on gameplay. I was constantly throwing things away.- Windows currently have no function. That's kinda weird. I can have a guest house with no windows at all and no one cares. Maybe they should be either a requirement for rooms, or add a decor bonus to encourage people to use them.- It's perfectly fine to have the only entrance to a guest's room be through another guest room. As long as it has a door, it's fine. That's weird.- There really needs to be a way to quick transfer items from your inventory to stash. It fills up quickly, and I have to click to pick up then click to put it in the stash- Add shift-click for adding multiple windows and doors at once. It works for furniture, but not doors or windows- The music stops in build mode. I spend a lot of time in build mode so I ended up using Spotify instead of the game music, but it'd be nice to have background build mode music too- When cooking, there is no search or filter, you just have to scroll through a very long list of recipes. I'd love to see some kind of filter to show me recipes that I have the ingredients for- I had a constant shortage of iron plates, even with scavenging the junk yard every time it respawned- I couldn't build a bedroom in Pinefall because it said there were invalid objects in the room, but there weren'tClicking on the fast travel map doesn't select locations properly. It works ok if you use the list view on the right- When you're using the Pager, if you fill all the rooms in one resort, then move to the next resort, it shows you the list of bedrooms, but it's highlighted the list of guest requests, so you have to click bedrooms first, then back to guest requests to get it to work- Sometimes the bathroom door gets a "no entry" sign on it as if there were a guest inside, but it's empty- Some of the quest directions are wrong. Particularly towards the end, the bats refer to "a cave in the east", but it's in the west- When you're assigning guests to rooms, it should show you the guest requirements on the same screen as the rooms. Otherwise you have to look at the guest, remember what they like, then look throught the list of rooms comparing them from memory- If you're in a bathroom when a guest walks in, it locks you in there until they leave- The resort quests often refer to "host guests with the X trait", but the traits are never mentioned anywhere on the UI - you just have to infer that they mean guests who want a certain special room based on the quest description- Sometimes the list shows "no guest requests" even though in the sidebar it says "9 guest requests"

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, B&B has me super disappointed. Laid-back, yes for sure. Management, yes but also no. Adventure, no not really. As most people say, the graphics are super cute. The characters are fun. I can definitely appreciate these aspects. But the rest of the game just isn't there for me. There's a lot of waiting around at the start of the game unless you want to run around and pick up the same materials in the same spots over and over again. You can only sleep at night, but night doesn't seem to be clearly defined because it gets dark and I can't sleep until later in the evening cycle. Controls just aren't clear on adding to or deleting rooms, which made me really frustrated. It seems like the game is just going to be the same throughout. Get to a certain point in your hotel building, then add another location via the Shark guy.I stopped playing after I was waiting around for the next time I could sleep, hit the sleep button, and the game continued to play the sleeping animation for a few minutes. I'm was really hoping for something that was more in-depth. Perhaps it's my fault for putting my expectations so high, but the game just feels like an early access game missing so many elements and QoL features.I'll probably boot it back up and play it some more because I liked the atmosphere, but I'd suggest others to wait to see if updates roll in or not.

_childDocuments_.review: So I renewing my review on this game. I really enjoyed it and would highly recommend. The art style is amazing and truly cozy. If you are someone who likes to take their time and enjoy the slow burn of games then this is for you! There is a mix between fast paced aspects and slow paced aspects of this game. Other than that it is great. I have spent quite some time on this game, although I have all locations unlocked I have yet to beat the entire game. There seems to constantly be something to do and that is amazing. If you are worried the game is inactive now you would be mistaken! The devs are currently working on an update, but it is best to be patient as they are dealing with some personal health concerns. But I wanted to put it out there in the review at least that they are still active just working on their own pace. And even if that was a concern it is also good to note that it is nothing to worry about, as I think you would have to dump thousands of hours into this game before you felt a lack of content in any way! LOVE THIS AND IT RUNS GREAT ON THE STEAM DECK!!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Bear and Breakfast is a game about playing as Hank, a young bear, who has found his calling to be an owner and manager of several bed and breakfast places around his forest home while also having memories of the nightmares they had once (maybe more) and introduced at the start of the game.It is a good game as you collect resources and design rooms that can satisfy the needs of your guests. With more 'management' missions you complete, the more requirements the guests expect of you and you are pushed to build and decorate your BnBs with comfort and design including other facilities that they may ask for. I use the term management lightly because you don't really 'manage' especially at the end of the game.It starts very slow but also ends very slow and the downside I always have with this game is waiting for the management quests to complete with nothing you can do but collect resources. I ended up waiting and idling for several in game days just to progress. I just wish there are story elements being sprinkled all over as you wait. I just wish there is an "okay" verdict for the review. It is a good CASUAL 'management' game with tiny sprinkles of story. However, I'd recommend getting the game if you want something relaxing and chilling to play instead of a full on management game.

_childDocuments_.review: If I could give this game a "MEH" review instead of a down, I would, but as it is, there ARE some good qualities about the game, but ultimately it is rather lackluster. At the time of writing this review, I have played through the entire game as it stands now and collected all achievements.The characters are cute, the artwork is adorable, and I enjoyed the otherwise wise cracks about life that can come up. There were parts that  looked into the current look on our lives and our place in the world. This game even had a promising start, a dark foreboding plot that really captures you. But, that's about as good as it got. I kept waiting for myself to really enjoy this game but it never quite happened.I love management style games, but this one felt disappointing. I never felt challenged and even collecting resources was boring. It was too easy to do what you needed to do and many of the area building quests you could complete one after the other in a short time. The majority of the game too you learn how to do more steps but only find yourself having to combine everything you learned together at the very last area. Plot wise, the story doesn't have an ending. It leaves too many unanswered questions. In fact, you don't even really learn about any of the characters in the game, even the "friends" that the game sells you on about starting a bed and breakfast with never actually involve themselves with the main game. Otherwise, if you're looking for a cute management game where you don't want to really challenge yourself or deal with plot, then this is the game for you. Saying that, it's a great game for if you want to shut off your mind after stressful days at work like me. I do hope the creators work a little more with the game because it holds a lot of promise as it does now.

_childDocuments_.review: I am really happy with the game but I must say the game was advertised a bit differently than the product that was received. I wanted to write this review to help others understand what game they are buying more, while I am heavily enjoying the game I do want to be transparent that the game is not what I thought it will be.The way the description came across I think makes players feel that we will have ONE inn in the WOODS that we can customise and run.Part of the game's description: "Bear and Breakfast is a laid-back management adventure game where you play as a well-meaning bear  Hank and his friends find an abandoned shack and, equipped with their teenage ingenuity, turn it into a money-making bed and breakfast scheme for unsuspecting tourists.""Bring guests into the forest to stay at your inn.""Build and personalize your inn with dozens of guest rooms, bathrooms, parlors, and entertainment."The description makes no mention of multiple inns and the lack of woods so far. The game makes you run multiple inns all over the world, I don't have one in the woods yet, this may come later but it still makes the description misleading.The truth overall is a bit different, we can run multiple inns, they don't seem to be in the woods so far as they are in an abandoned city and we were forced into it by a machine using a fingerprint scanner that locked us into a legally binding contract. It is quite a dystopian future and for anyone looking for a super cozy and lighthearted setting, this one might be a bit more grim. It does give a very different vibe from the game that we were told we are getting.The game is still very fun and entertaining, I am not returning it as the game is still right up my alley but like others I must admit there is some confusion on what type of game this is, it is as others said quite story heavy and not very heavy on the management part.When it comes to the game itself the graphics are beautiful especially the main character's animation is extremely smooth and well done. It reminds me of the game Cuphead with it's fluid movements.The dialogue is well written and all interfaces work well and are nicely designed, it doesn't feel like a badly cooked indie game, it really does feel like the developers poured their love and soul into this game.I have also encountered no bugs with the game which I was quite pleasantly surprised with, I expected a ton of bugs and issues especially for an indie game but apart from some stuttering it all runs smoothly without any issues.The only feedback I have is that night time is very dark in the game and you can only skip it at midnight.. not when it is clearly night time. This means you always have to play during the night a bit. I also wish the bed in our home actually worked so we could sleep in it.

_childDocuments_.review: I got to this game because I was seeking something similar to Dave the Diver and it certainly did not disappoint. I'm looking forward to the next update and wish the devs strength.Overall if you're looking for a way to unwind and relax in a game where you explore and manage hotels, this one is for you.
