_childDocuments_.review: If you want to be a cute derpy bear and manage some inns then this game is definitely for you.- character design and conversations 10/10 (adorable, made me giggle many times)- objective and overall gameplay 7,5/10 (very clear and easy, gets  repetitive after awhile)- end game 7/10 (I was so exited to explore the caves and find out the mysteries but couldn't help but wish for more, I think it was a bit underwhelming how we didn't get closure with one of the characters, hope they will make more updates or a DLC cuz I'd love to play more quests, maybe go to an island and open a resort there, and maybe some eastereggs so there's something to look forward to).Overall bear-y cute and chill game 8/10 mushrooms.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: So I've quite enjoyed the fixes and updates we've been given so I wanted to update my review.I'm done with the main quest and unfortunately, as lovely as this game is, it still has massive pacing problems.So be ready to watch some youtube while you're playing because it's still very much hurry up and wait.There are also some more quality of life issues which may or may not have been reported already.Here are some of my issues:- quest tracker doesn't work if a character is on a second story or in another part of a cave, it will point you to a map exit- you still can't select to make several meals at once, which makes "autofill cards" kinda useless- bough recepies from Julias store only disappear after you open and close your shop- I wish there was a limit on bus signs/tools so you don't waste your money in the game because you stock up too much- I wish the map quests were less depending on each other. You can't spend time on one location to max it out before you advance because the upgrades you need are unlocked with a new map quest
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: This game is impossibly funny. I can't get over how amazing the writing is.It's got a couple of small bugs - but otherwise the game is extremely polished and has a pretty solid and compelling progression. Come for the art, stay for the endearing wholesome qualities of the game.Update:At almost 100 more hours - I wanted to update this. Bear and Breakfast is quite possibly the most endearing and emotionally touching game I've played in years. Any rough edges are immediately forgotten in the extremely compelling game loop, fascinating characters, and the world that just sucks you right in and suddenly a couple of soothing hours have passed as you improved your resorts.I cannot recommend this game enough. It's an exceptional management sim, with note for note perfect writing. I hope it's a huge success and they get to make more Bear and Breakfast, but also more games.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: A super polished, fun experience. The loop of renovating properties to rent to humans is so good and there's even a story with characters you wanna spend time with. The art is so cute and everything is very polished for a game from a smaller indie team. No bugs or issues either. Very excited to play more!!
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Bear and Breakfast is a cozy game with a good and funny story to it! The humour is the best I wasn't expecting it and it just made me love the game more! It is very story driven and you have to do missions/quests to unlock a lot of the features which I found fun since you didn't know when or what kind of improvements to the bear or b&b next! Quests are important to be your best bear self! Which I seen in the reviews of people and you do actually unlock more QOL things through playing the game! Story is funny and engaging! 10/10 Music is relaxing lets me zone out! 10/10 Art style is cute and bear is best! 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Good base but lacks things to do, four hours into the game and still have no way to skip time, which would be fine if there was anything to do besides gather resources. Currency seems to also only have one purpose (for furniture) so you spend to earn spend to earn, but that progression loses its luster after the first time you remodel your motel. Id say wait awhile for updates then buy, in its current state youll get a day worth of play before it sits in your steam library until the end of time.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I like management games and I love bears! This game does not disappoint.Positives about the game - The pacing of this game works very well. The sense of progression feels very rewarding and the new requirements for each bed and breakfast keeps things fresh. Also, the game has a charming sense of humour and a lovely art style.Negatives about the game - it can be a little buggy at times but it seems the developers are aware of the issues and will help to resolve them. Also, if you have a stack of items it can get a little annoying when just trying to select a specific number of that item.(Spoilers!) Tip for beginning tutorial - I almost got soft locked on the tutorial when building the first bed and breakfast. I spent all my money buying crafting recipes I thought would look nice, but only after doing so did I realise that I didn't have enough money to build the first bedroom. Because I couldn't build, I couldn't progress. After looking it up, it turns out if you are low on money you can go back home and ask your bear mum for pocket money. I don't remember this being communicated in game, so I was very confused for 20 minutes.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the coziest game of 2022. My only problem with it is that I want more of the story! Hank and his pals are amazing and I love managing my little hotels and getting to know everyone in town! The mythology is very intriguing and it is overall a world I would love to know more about! I had so much fun this year playing this game, I thoroughly recommend it to anyone curious about it!
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, and it's definitely cute but feels like a chore to play. Mindless fetch quests and no room or requirement to customise anything. Just buying the (usually) one item at each level and putting heaps of the same item in rooms to reach the next level.Unfortunately it's just boring, and my time played is reflective of leaving the game open to churn money to afford higher level items.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: If youre the type like me who enjoys building and having fun with it like the Sims or The Tenants then overall I dont think I can recommend this game. Now this isnt to say the game is bad, I know for a fact a lot of people like games like this, that dont really challange and is just something to sit back with and have a "wholesome" time with.Its just not my flavor of game at all. And when it comes to building and manegement games there are so many much more refined versions out there with much less small annoyances and more polish.In the end the game is fine but I just have so many small nitpicks that pile up for my to have an enjoyable time with it.Ill mention just a few here cos I dont want to be here all day.- The game takes a looooong time to get going. Im 4+ hours in and still feels like is introducing things to me slowly.- Only getting to start with guestrooms, then later introducing bathrooms, then later bars and later kitchens just makes everything seem really slow.- Slow honestly describes this whole game. Everything is very slow, and while you wait for money to come in, you dont have anything to do other than go collect resources. The people you have staying at your places dont really do anything, they just walk around between rooms, sometimes theyll sit at th bar, sometimes at a campfire, but it doesn't add anything since there is no way for you to interact with them at all.- I dont care for most of the characters. From what I got to see they all seem pretty flat and uncomplicated and dont have much to say. - Some of the characters have quests but they just involve you going from a to b or going to gather a specific resource.- Having to walk around the map to gather specific crafting resources is chore, and so is having to manually craft every item before you can place it, rather than just chosing what you want to build and then have the materials be used to craft it automatically.- The map is quite useless as it does not allow you to zoom out very far.- Walking is slow- Exploring the map does reward you with treasure chests and such, but the rewards are small and dont really feel worth the time.So yeah, its not a bad game, but its very slow, quite limited in what you can do, lacks many small gameplay comforts.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: If you search any lists or videos of cozy games, this one will be there. Unfortunately I was unable to enjoy it as in the first 20 minutes of gameplay I ran into a game breaking bug where I couldn't select the recipe I needed from the crafting table (tried with both the keyboard and a controller). This bug literally stops me from progressing in the game. Having checked the forums, I'm not the first one to encounter this bug, which was reported in 2022, so that leaves me wondering if I just got very unlucky and this bug is rare, as it has not been fixed as of today. _childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only 7h in but love it so much! This takes the foraging fun and building fun from a couple of my fave games and mashes with cute style like other favourite games. Although the pacing at the start could use some work, I am finding the missions easy enough to follow, and a joy to complete. I love being Hank!
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I think I wasted my money on this game. Had a lot of faith in it so I had it on my library more than 2 hours after I bought it. _childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy this game, it is cute and easy. Worth $20? Ehhh. It's true that if you do one b&b, you've essentially done them all, and the customization is not super high level. _childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: About 29 hours of playtime to complete the main story line. Pros: - the bear is simply adorable! - good build-up of difficulty in the hotel management aspect- after a while, you'll be able to manage all your B&Bs remotely- easy collection of resourcesCons: - the main story line was engaging at the start, but did not live up to the build-up. A lot of opportunities for deeper investigation into the lore. A lot of questions unanswered. - side characters can't exactly be befriended. Some had interesting backstories - was disappointing to see that this was not unpacked more. Most side characters only get 1 quest, and then you don't see additional dialogue / relationship build-up with them anymore.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game! There are a few things that really bothered me about the game though, so be sure to get it on sale if you'd like to buy.1. the game is not really intuitive on certain things that are really important to the game, like rotating objects (for PC, press R to rotate objects, you'll thank me later) and no real guidance on the best ways to lay out the properties you are building. 2. You think at the beginning there is some sort of plot with your friends, but they vanish pretty early on and soon enough you're taking directions from signs only.3. There is no way to throw away or discard items (that I know of). This is really annoying.4. The put downs that come from the shark that gives you main quests get really old really fast.All in all, a pretty good game but there are definitely improvements to be made. 4/5
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I would have loved a more thought-out layout of the resorts. I want my bedrooms, kitchens, bathrooms etc. to be nicely decorated and also have a logical placement inside the house (all bedrooms in one area for example). This is almost impossible in this game. I somehow have to fit 5 bedrooms and 2 bathrooms, aswell as a kitchen and a dining room inside, while also making the rooms large enough to place decorations inside. The mandatory objects of a room increase in size, the more progress you have with that resort.After an hour of figuring out how the rooms could be placed, I saw that bedroom nr. 3 has a decorational value of -58 because it was placed next to the kitchen. Oh, well I guess its time to hang up like 10 possum-clocks then.I am also angry that bedrooms can rarely be the same size because the number of tiles on one side of the building is always odd and the range of the bathroom (which, in my opinion, is a weird thing to have) is mostly one tile short.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: The game is perfect if youre looking for a casual experience with no time pressure. Theres a ton of items - and youre free to decorate and form each room in your BnB. You will unlock better furniture as you play. One of my fave part of the game is that your inventory is big and everything can stack up to x99, and it is not difficult to keep up with the customers needs.I havent had any gamebreaking bugs, only visual ones if anything (npc's not moving/standing in place and their clothes clipping when they lay in bed).Im looking forward to playing it more!
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a great and cute game. The art and design of the game is so well done and aesthetically pleasing which makes for a cozy atmosphere. It does have a few bugs though. There's a way to duplicate furniture which makes the need to buy more for other rooms not needed. Also, money in the game seems to be a struggle until the end of the game when at that point, you don't need it that much anymore. I also felt the comfort expectations for the rooms raised too quickly and I didn't have the right level of materials to meet the requirements without, for example, putting two wardrobes down. The decoration items are much easier to obtain as you can buy them with valuables, but comfort items you have to craft and are much bigger and harder to fit in rooms. I think the game could benefit by adding some comfort items to took's garbage shop as well just to give rooms that extra boost of comfort to satisfy the harder guest requests a bit quicker. Overall, this game is absolutely adorable and I had the best time playing it despite any minor bugs or faults. I highly recommend it for a chill gaming experience for those who love interior design or just anything cute.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: bear & breakfast is as described - it is a cozy management game! after finishing the game (perfect completion), these are my thoughts:pros- multiple in-game QoL features compared to other life sim games (i.e., fast teleportation, crafting, etc.)- good in-game time progression (i.e., able to progress in-game time if needed, time pauses when crafting/building, etc.)- cute art style and good in-game locales + background music (ties in well with the story line while being distinct from one another)cons- despite being released for 1 year+, this game is still buggy where in-game information will not load properly (e.g., stats about room temperature, food, etc.)- many players seem to have issues with steam achievement syncing, i was able to fix this by enabling steam overlay (disabled on game launch) however this fix might not work for everyone- story progression becomes disjointed at times where you are able to manage multiple in-game locations, but progression in multiple are blocked by certain checkpoints/goals that are either dependent on RNG or the progress in other in-game locations (to where it felt like a large roadblock)**in my situation, i was able to determine that the prestige/rating of my in-game locations were the cause of the roadblock so i suppose being too efficient is a drawback?**other comments (neutral)- not story heavy compared to some other life sim games, especially if you do not plan on achievement hunting- furniture aesthetics are tied somewhat strongly to in-game function- relatively few interactions with NPCs (limited character/relationship building)overall, i would recommend this game (with a grain of salt) if you enjoy management style games and are looking for a casual one to try out!
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I completed the full game- including all achievements. First, the good things were that the game had a cute backstory, the animation was charming, and I enjoyed the overall process of building, decorating, and running the hotels. I also liked the cooking aspect. I did also appreciate the backstory of the characters. This game would be great for a casual player new to video games. That said, I felt like something was missing. When I finished the main storyline, I didn't even realize it was the end, and felt lacking. The gameplay is also quite repetitive - collecting, crafting, decorating, cooking - rinse and repeat. This is not necessarily a bad thing, but in the early game I felt like I was waiting around a lot. I also don't think it was easy to find other quests (museum items) and I had to look them up on the wiki to be prompted. A few small suggestions - as the final unlock, Hank should have infinite bag space. Inventory was difficult to manage, specifically at the end. I would also love to see an option for resale of my furniture - I know you can recycle what you crafted, but specifically for the items you buy from Took's shop, it would be nice to earn some valuables. The map was at times confusing. I did use the world map quite a lot, but it would have been useful when opening the area map to see what locations each area exit led to on your map, so in addition to saying Area Exit, it would say 'Pinefall,' so you can quickly tell from the area map what maps are connected. I wasted a lot of time wandering around because I couldn't remember which areas were connected to which, and had to keep walking up and interacting with the sign to confirm the location. Overall, very cute, very cozy! I hope they continue to build it out more. I don't think it has much for me in terms of replayability unless future DLC/storylines are released.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: An Intensely Charming, Yet Miserably Paced Management Game.I cannot begin to tell you how much I want to love this game. The art, characters and writing are all DRIPPING with charm and an obvious love and care in their craft; if only the same could be said about the gameplay. Between the enchanting vignettes with the colorful cast of characters who are helping you, the titular "Bear" Hank, in creating your B&B business, there is an absolutely dreary wasteland of waiting for something to happen to continue playing the game. Progression in the story-line often requires you to just wait for people to come and go, and the game simply does not provide enough things to do while you wait. This may alleviate somewhat later in the game, but oftentimes I would find myself just leaving the game on while I go do something else, simply so I could continue to play the game later and that is absolutely no way to "play" a game. Sadly, I feel these issues can (and in all likelihood will) be rectified in the future, but as it stands, getting into the game proper is boring at best and simply obtuse at worst. I think the inclusion of a means to advance time more quickly or perhaps a more sandbox-like mode where content isn't gated behind having to wait would go a long way to me recommending this game without reservation, but as it stands, I wouldn't be comfortable saying it's in a consistently entertaining state.That said, the bones of this game are amazing and I think with a little tweaking, we're looking at another Stardew Valley level, laid back game to chill with time and time again.Sadly, at present "laid back" for Bear and Breakfast is just really boring.Edit: My hours played may indicate I've gotten further in the game than I have, but unfortunately, I fell asleep with it on while I was waiting for things to progress. Read into that how you will.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Bear&Breakfast takes you on the journey of Hank the bear.You start with a cheap motel that offers not that much of space, but that is just the beginning.While you decorate and built better furniture for your guests you get to play through the storyline.The characters you meet are cute and silly and help you through a variety of tasks and also demand help from you.After a hard day of managing the motels, you sadly have to wait till the clock hits midnight.You can't sleep earlier as it is now which is sad if you need money from guests for example, or simple want to progress faster through the game.When you do the quests there is sometimes a point where you don't know what to do next.At least to me it wasn't that obvious as you have to run around by yourself without hints on who to talk next to.I spent a huge amount of time running across the map searching for that one character that had a quest for me.Sure, you got your bus stops, but some parts of the late map are mostly reached by walking.The motel quests stay the same and just increase in the amount of difficulty for every new motel you get access to.I had fun decorating, but it felt a bit bland to do almost the same for every motel.Built x- amount of bathromms, get them to tier x or get several 5 star ratings.The story is tragic, but thanks to their charming characters very fun and unique.I'd hit the neutral button if there was one, as the elements that I mentioned and some others are not to my liking but I enjoyed the overall gameplay.

I'd say the only time you'd be waiting is very early game, but it's still highly exaggerated by some of these reviews. Just play casually and enjoy it for the story, you'd probably have a fun time then.My personal rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐✩ 4/5"Menu" specifically the inventory system can be a little bit clunky at times and I feel controller support would also work wonders for this game. _childDocuments_.review: Hank (a bear) ventures away from his home one day to find a mysterious and  shark named Fin that requests him to fix up local dilapidated buildings for the sake of human tourism.     • Hotel/resort management. Involves building various types of rooms to accommodate guests and cooking food for them. Also, there are lots of decorative items.    • Room types: bedroom, bathroom, distillery, kitchen, dining room,  campfire (outside), lounge, utility room, movie theater, museum, arcade    • The game gets easier to manage the longer it goes on. The player can eventually hire characters to do various tasks. Collectible items upgrade various aspects of Hank’s abilities. Upgraded kitchen appliances make cooking much easier.     • Lots of items and upgrades to unlock.    • Lots of mysteries to discover.    • Silly humor throughout the game.    • There’s plenty of space for building rooms, so the player doesn’t feel limited in creativity.     • Didn’t see the plot twist coming. It did have me saying,  though.    • Several cute, fun illustrations for the characters. Nice illustrations for all the locations in the game on loading screens.    • Narratives regarding human greed and disrespect for wildlife.    • Quest markers are out of bounds sometimes. (This seems to happen when the marker is on a character and they’ve moved out of an area by the time Hank got there.)    • Hank is fat and gets stuck on doorways.    • There are a lot of unnecessary impassable objects on the ground that make navigating any of the maps a bit more annoying, especially if one’s paying attention to the mini-map to find something particular.     • The ending is a bit unsatisfying. I felt there should be an epilogue or at least more explanation. It left me with questions.    • Very minor complaint: Even though this story must take place in North America (given the presence of the North American possum or “opossum”), some characters speak in a British manner? Overall, it was a fun game both in its gameplay and story. If you like management sims, you’d probably like this as well. I definitely recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I waited for this game for a long time and it really was worth the wait, I purchased day 1. I love being able to design and build my own inns, and the art is cute. _childDocuments_.review: I was as many really excited for this game, so much so that I didn't wait for the switch release but bought it for the PC, but I am still glad you can now play it with a controller.My biggest issue with the game is the never ending upgrade quests for hotels. Without too many spoilers, you start out in smaller places and find larger places along the way, however your upgrade quests for the smaller places never stop. So in order to continue the game you are basically forced to cram as much ♥♥♥♥ as possible into tiny spaces, just so your star rating goes up and your tiny cabin in the woods becomes a five star hotel (paraphrasing), that just does not make sense. Why not give each place a different final level that it can achieve? That would also allow for cuter designs, better layout managment of hotel rooms etc.This also forces you to constantly travel back and forth and collect ever more ressources, it just never feels like progression. No I haven't finished the game, at this point I am not sure I will b/c I just refuse to turn my b&bs into cramped, full of random knick-knacks, places just so I can keep their star rating going up higher and higher. This could have been a really fun game b/c the design is excellent and adorable and it has so much potential that just falls flat for reasons that it should not struggle with.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: SUCH a cute game! _childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely delightful. It's such a calm game and super easy to play. I adore this game and it's characters, their expressions are the best! _childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty good in the beginning, I tried really hard to like it but I'm noticing new glitches every day (even if they're 90% visual it just feels janky) and multiple times the game has frozen while the bear is sleeping and I've lost progress. The inventory is very hard to manage, I didn't find the delete button until like 10 hours in and even then there's some items you can't delete if you bought too many. Moving items from the inventory to storage is honestly what made me give up on this game. You have to drag each stack from opposite sides of the screen one by one, and usually I'd have to swap 10+ stacks at a time. And if you had two menus open, scrolling would scrolls both menus at the same time which is so annoying and such a weird choice. Most of the inventory system I would call a weird choice. The story is very odd, it starts in a creepy dream sequence that's really interesting but then they just don't mention it until the end of the game and I didn't even realise it was over. There are so so many cute characters but once you meet them there's zero reason to ever see them again. For example you supposedly live with your two best friends in a house with your mum. But after you build the first house (which is the first 10 mins) talking to any of them just repeats the same one line for the rest of the game. The game just feels empty which is such a waste because of how beautiful it is. There's a lot of areas to explore but finding a new person was just kind of sad because you do one quest for them and then probably never see them again.You don't really manage anything, you just build copies of the same room with really limited decorations and then any guest will pay for it even if it says they want something specific. Unlike other reviews in the beginning the time system was alright for me, I spent most nights just picking up extra materials. But now circling the same 2 or 3 areas for the same materials I'm always low on gets boring. There's also nothing to do but earn money so I can buy blueprints to finish quests, so I often just go afk for a bit so I can sleep and get paid in the morning.Overall I'm going to finish it and get all the achievements but I'd wait a while longer for this game, it feels unfinished.

_childDocuments_.review: My review is from that of 1) A new Steam Deck user and 2) A casual gamer who plays on the Nintendo Switch exclusively prior to this review. If you're relatively new to the Steam Deck and this is your first "cozy game", here are my thoughts:**PROS**- The game's art style is super cute and well done. It reminds me of "Cozy Grove" - The story dialogue with characters are amusing and funny and make me want to keep playing to see what happens- This game is inexpensive regularly, but a great buy when it's on sale (purchased during Winter sale 2023)- In game music is soothing and not over bearing or distracting- The pace of the game play is chill, with no rush even with the day/night cycle. There is also no health meter so you never have to worry about tiring out or needing food. You can sleep whenever you want (Sleep only gets you through the night cycle if you want to play in daylight only. That's it!)- Cute little stickers and achievements for your steam profile are easily obtained by just playing the game :)**CONS**- The controls will not be to your liking right out of the box. Ultimately, I decided to play with the pre-set controls by the Steam deck, but there are some User profiles created that you can try. This game, I feel, was originally created for mouse and keyboard so navigating the various menus with Steam Deck controls WILL take practice and getting used to. If you're not a patient person with this type of customization, SKIP this game entirely and find something else. (I knew this was what owning a Steam Deck would be like, so I was already prepared for some level of difficulty)- There are many inventory menus, crafting/building menus and quest log menus. If you're a gamer with poor eyesight (like ME) you may find the on-screen Steam Deck menus to be a challenge playing in hand-held. I recommend docking and connecting to a larger external monitor OR skipping this game altogether if you're committed to hand-held game play more. (It's a strain on my eyes, but I'm enjoying the game too much to back out now, after all I've already gone through figuring out the controls)Overall, I really am enjoying the game and have tanked 6+ hrs into it right from the start. Half that time was just figuring out controls, but overall I have enjoyed the play and I will continue.

_childDocuments_.review: Bear & Breakfast is a really cute and fairly entertaining hotel management game. The art style is seriously soo cute and charming, I love the characters (although I wish the story could have gone a bit deeper into character development and relationships), and the sound design is really well done. I loved the actual hotel management side, especially putting together rooms, but it got overwhelming quickly once kitchens/dining rooms came into the mix. It's also difficult to create actually functional rooms when there's very high comfort and decoration scores to adhere to, which caused a lot of my rooms to be packed full of crap rather than reflect a realistic hotel experience. Having staff manage the grind-y parts of hotel management was very convenient (like Julia cooking for me), but it definitely came late due to me missing certain quests. There were no real indications of what to do next or who to speak to, instead NPCs simply had an exclamation mark over their heads - I found myself quite far behind where I think I should've been in the story compared to my resorts progress due to this, especially NPCs who were in locations not accessible by bus, or were out of the way so I never noticed they had a quest for me. There isn't much guidance in terms of the order of quests or who to speak to and when, which was slightly frustrating and caused me to consult a guide when I really didn't want to. Sometimes there weren't even exclamation marks. Running the hotels gets quite aimless after a while and I spent some time just letting my computer run while doing other things IRL in order to progress quests like "host X amount of guests", etc. There was also no indication that the main quest had ended, it was quite abrupt and wasn't very satisfying. I did enjoy the story and the more mysterious/sinister side to the seemingly picture-perfect facade of the game, but the ending left a lot to be desired. I also wish each character could have been fleshed out more, rather than only having a short and very specific storyline. I would have liked to see some of the NPCs interact as well, and maybe explain how some Humans can literally understand a bear lol. Slightly nit-picky stuff/bugs:- Getting stuck in a bathroom with a guest and having to wait until they leave to be unstuck.- Slight typos in dialogue, which would have made the game feel a lot more polished if these had been fixed. Hire me to proofread next time, or something ;)- It was quite annoying how when I would click on a recipe/blueprint in my inventory to learn it, it would force me to scroll all the way down to the bottom of my inventory every. single. time. - A lot of aimless waiting around. Wish I could skip the daytime as well, not just night. - When I look at the "cabins" tab in Timber Crossing, the camera gets stuck and won't follow Hank around. This also happened after exiting build mode sometimes, regardless of location.- Food scores would disappear/show up as 0 for no reason. Overall, I enjoyed Bear & Breakfast and would recommend it, for sure. 8/10!

_childDocuments_.review: I never thought I'd give this game a negative review, let alone keep it negative after patches. I'd been waiting for it since I checked out the demo and thought it might be my game of the year. My experience may well have been different if the info on the store page had been open about the game being unfinished, unbalanced and full of bugs - basically it should have released as Early Access. As it was, I got hooked on that whole "finish this and that task" loop but felt tricked into helping with development instead of getting the full experience of a finished game. But even putting that aside, there are other games that let me do similar things in much more enjoyable ways. The one thing that makes Bear & Breakfast stand out is that  and people can't get over it. My biggest remaining issue is the time system. Unlike any other management game that I know of, the player gets very little control over time passing - it only stops in the building menu (not during dialogues, guest management, checking out the map or shops...) and it can only be skipped forward after 9 PM (originally midnight). It starts getting dark at 6 for some reason, and you have no way of illuminating your surroundings. A lot of people have been frustrated because things move too slowly for them. I had the opposite problem because I like taking things slow, looking around, putting a lot of thought into how I want to decorate my rooms, which items to buy, which guests (with different preferences) to book into which room, which recipes to buy and which foods to prepare... And while I'm trying to be creative and thoughtful like that... or just struggle with tedious inventories or keep getting stuck trying to get through a door... the days woosh by. There are no deadlines to meet, but I still find it uncomfortable and stressful, let alone immersion-breaking. The devs seem unwilling to give players more control over time passing because somehow it "wouldn't work" but it does for so many other games? Too bad, because with time pausing in all menus I could see myself really enjoy this game. There are a lot of good things and a lot of potential. I love the concept, the art, the characters and the often hilarious dialogues, and I even found the story decent enough though it lacks a real ending and a lot of people were left confused (adding to the whole unfinished feel). If you're neither the very impatient type nor the extra slow and thoughtful (and maybe clumsy with WASD controls) one like me, I guess this game should mostly work well for you now. Me, part of me is still curious about 100%-ing it but it would be so tedious and unfun that I don't think that's going to happen. Oh yeah, and heads up that while this game looks all cutesy and is often very funny, there's also a lot of dark humour and serious background stories, including an NPC talking about . Games with some similar aspects that I actually enjoyed (all are combat-free and very laid-back)- decorating rooms and other spaces, foraging, funny and sometimes dark bear stories:  - managing a bed & breakfast kind of place with humour and overarching story:  - managing villages, some decorating, exploration, loot and treasures, story about trouble with humans: - being a funny animal with dark humour:  - building and managing temporary homes, gathering resources, main and side quests:  - cheerful exploration with quests, restoring a world, half-baked crafting and an afterthought-like fantasy story:  * * * For more chill and story-driven games, check out my curator . You're also welcome to join the .

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start off by saying this is a charming resource management game and I've enjoyed playing it.  The characters are cute and I've enjoyed all the people and animals you meet along the way.  The casual way that the park ranger talks with Hank and nobody blinks an eye at a wild bear managing rental properties is hilarious and I love it.  The aesthetics and sound design are great and wonderfully pleasing.But while the game is enjoyable, it has some pacing issues.  The conversations between characters feel overlong and the banter back and forth has humor that doesn't always land for me.  I enjoy the light snarkiness, but I found myself skipping dialogue because it took so long to get to the point.  I do love choosing Hank's well thought out responses only for him to vocalize the line as "bear noises" which is funny.  So far for me, the bird and the dog friends don't really do anything.  I wish they were more integral to the story since they're part of the opening.The natural progression of the story feels rushed.  At just under 15 hours, I've unlocked most areas without actually building rooms or renting them to anyone in the newest ones.  There may be more and I know there is more to the main story, but most of the map is open now.  I wish that there was a way that enticed me to spend more time at each location and work on interior design and management before rushing me off to the next area to unlock.  I don't have any suggestions on how to accomplish this.  The shark speaker quests were fine and paced well by requiring a certain number of guests and other tasks, but the signpost quests almost seemed too easy.  I almost always had all materials on hand for each one, so I'd plow through a handful of requirements in one sitting the first time I talked to it.  But I'm not sure how to balance that out without making it too grindy on materials.  I haven't gone back to it in a few days because there's less sense of exploration and expansion and it's now reduced to doing the rounds of properties to pick up money and materials which has started to feel like work.  This may be more of a personal preference for how I like to play.  In terms of light engagement for in-game accomplishment, this does scratch a lot of itches for me.The variety of furniture designs is also a little lacking.  I'd like to see see re-skins at least with different color sets for furniture instead of just the single set in each quality level, but that's just a personal preference for decorating.  The room design is a little formulaic, but there's enough accessories to make each room unique.  But these are nitpicky concerns.Overall, this is a great game and I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Bear and Breakfast is absolutely a delight of a game. Despite some hiccups and a bit of a painful opening segment, I'd say it's well worth the 20 dollars.Within the first hour or two of the game, there comes a time where you will have to wait a long period of time for the game to progress. The devs did say they were working on a fix for this and honestly, it wasn't too much of a pain to get up and do a chore for 10 minutes when the rest of the game is such a delight.The first couple hours are a bit annoying but if you "bear" with it, the game melts into a fun and addictive gameplay loop of collecting materials, progressing a story, and designing your properties. If you enjoy management simulation games or enjoy designing houses in The Sims, you will absolutely adore Bear and Breakfast.Pros:- An adorable art style- Quirky characters- A fun gameplay loop that makes hours feel like minutes- Each area feels uniqueCons (more of my laundry list of small issues to the devs <3):- Long-ish loading screens- Having to travel to each location to register guests each day becomes annoying in the late game- Inventory management is a nightmare, there is no way to quickly move items between containers- Balancing issue in availability of materials- No system to sell your old objects once you upgrade to new ones or to sell excess materials

_childDocuments_.review: Basically in this game you run bed and breakfast business. You build bedrooms, dining rooms, kitchens, toilets and more. Across 5 different resorts. You can keep making your resorts better by placing better furniture and decorations. As you play you will meet a colourful cast of characters. It's a fun and relaxing managment game. With more content and gameplay than it may seem. To 100% the game it takes around 40 hours, however you can spend more on endgame improving ur layouts and decorations, as well as getting the best furniture.Time flies while playing it. I would have never imagined spending 20+ hrs on this title. For the most part I had fun, however there are few things that irked me.It's lacking ways to make building layouts easier, like ability to copy and move rooms.You can't sell items. All ur profit comes from the resorts.More decorating options and ability to increase the size of ur hotels would be nice. It would give more reasons to play even after finishing the story.Overall though pros outweight the cons and I would reccomend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: For those considering Bear and Breakfast, as most people reading the reviews are, here is some things to take into consideration:Pros:The gameplay is addictive! It's more of a motel simulator than a bed and breakfast but it's still fun regardless. The graphics are great! There's immersive weather designs, the furniture is SO so cute, and there's even physics with some of the clothing options.The characters are lovable! And the character design is great. I felt like I emotionally connected with all the characters. (Except the old lady, she knows what she did ›:()Did I mention it's addicting? I've spent about 40 hours on this game. It's normally something I play when I need to listen to something and need something to do with my hands.Cons: The mission guiding system is glitched in a few of the mid game/end game quests. It's hard to find some quest items because they aren't being tracked and sometimes you can't find quest items until finishing other questlines. I go to the guides and discussions for a bit of the quests after spending hours looking for quest items…Early on, there is a campfire site which is glitched. Sometimes if you place something in the campsite or try to remove something it'll start placing infinite items onto the ground or in your inventory.Mid/late game there is a significant increase in needs for resources but not a lot of sources and sometimes you can only buy the items, which is rough when you need a bunch of it.Overall, it's a cute game with some quirks. It just needs a few glitches worked out but other than that I can tell the developers and everyone else involved put a lot of work and care into it. I hope this helps for those deciding whether or not to buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: (tl:dr pros and cons below)So on one hand, I recommend this game, on the other hand, I don't. I really wish I could enjoy this game more. I originally set a timer for two hours when I started because I wasn't sure whether or not I'd like this game, so if I didn't, I could just refund. That being said, the first two hours are really enjoyable. I had more pros than cons and I felt like I would want to finish this game to completion. However when I got to about 5 hours in, I was getting bored of it really fast. Don't get me wrong, I have a lot of pros: I love the art style and story line, and it's a great concept for the game and it has great mechanics for the building and management part of the game. However, this game feels very tedious. You're constantly having to run back and forth to get more and more resources. At least one hour of my gameplay was grinding resources I need for building, which become pointless in the next 30-60 minutes when you unlock beefier items and have to grind yet again to get items you need for making furniture. Honestly that's my only real con of the game but the endless grinding only for it to become irrelevant almost immediately after you craft and make the improvements you need just make the game boring. It feels like most of the game is just walking simulator. If they were to add a feature where you could use money to just buy the crafting resources it would literally fix this issue.Pros:-Great art style-Cute Story-Building mechanics are nice-Cooking mechanics are nice-I love management style games where you run your own business and this has great mechanics for that.Con:-Game gets boring fast-Even with fast traveling it feels like a walking sim how often you need to go back for resources (Game should just add a resources shop where you can spend money for it if you want (they could still allow searching for it at same time)).

The only things I have small issues with myself is that the sorting of your inventory is hard and a bit frustrating at times, and the cooking mechanics of the game would be good fun if a) ingredients such as butter, milk, etc weren't so expensive and b) if time froze while you were cooking. Oh and maybe c) some way to have your ingredients from surrounding fridges go into the cooking mechanics because I never had enough space in my inventory to carry the multiple stacks of misc items since I didn't have the recipes memorized for what I needed. TLDR: This game is fun, beautiful, and worth the money.

I've gotten to the point where it's so grindy that I don't want to finish it- it takes a long time to get a good amount of mahogany wood- which you need a lot of to make level 5 rooms. Overerall a great game though!!
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful little experience with some extremely unfortunate bugs that can ruin progression or money generation and thus halt your ability for this bear to build themselves up. Hopefully the devs add in other means to generate cash to work around problems or allow more industrious players to not wait hours until enough guests have came and hopefully, successfully got on the bus to pay you or else Henry's just stuck needing coins that won't come. Like selling items or material we don't need anymore.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: This was a fun game to get really engrossed in. I wouldn't really call it "cosy" in the same way I wouldn't call theme hospital cosy, but the management mechanics provided a strong challenge, and the story missions were cool. Wish I could have spent more time on the story/character missions, as I loved some of the critters like your og friends and Gus the opossum, but you don't get to see them much. Overall, though, kept me occupied and really enjoyed it.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: What a delightful game! Hank is just a nice guy who wants the valley to be its best self. The customization of the cabins is a ton of fun, and the story isn't boring! There are a ton of lil tasks you get to do, and the ending is much more suspenseful and shocking that I would have hoped for!10/10 game and worth every single penny. Bear and Breakfast nation is alive
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Engaging and exciting! I wasn't expecting such an interesting storyline, such lovely characters (I love Charlotte and little tadpole kid lol) and such fun side tasks for a game that I just bought because I wanted to run a bed and breakfast and wind down after work.The illustration and soundtrack are quite something else!
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Aesthetically this game is lovely, as is the music. Over all it's a fun game, but it's not without it's problems. The first is that honestly, the gameplay loop gets a bit boring by the end. From start to finish you basically just do the same thing over and over again, and I can't say that mechanically it changes enough to really feel any different. That said, this didn't really set in too hard till just before the final area. The big thing is the games ending, or honestly, lack there of. What I've seen dubbed as the "Epilogue Quests" were, first and foremost, a tremendously tedious slog of running back and forth between areas with no fast travel and the nearest kitchen. That in and of itself sucked. The other problem was that...well firstly this portion of the story came out of almost nowhere. There was VERY little to no foreshadowing on these events. It didn't really make any sense, and ultimately raised more questions than it did answers. Over all that last stretch just kinda felt like I had stumbled into a completely different game that had nothing to do with what I'd just spent several hours playing. Which left me feeling....dissatisfied. The game up to that point is plenty enjoyable, it just didn't stick the landing.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I found the game to be quite enjoyable.The game does an excellent job of capturing the vibe of North America, and I found myself immersed in the world that was created. The attention to detail is impressive, and the overall atmosphere of the game is very well done.One thing that stood out to me was the game's design. It's incredibly cute and charming, with vibrant colors and playful characters. However, I did find that there was quite a bit of text to read, which is a turn-off for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Definitively recommend <3- Very relaxing. Sooooo laid back and cute! No stress while playing :)- The scenarios are excellent (well wrote, cute and funny!) and promote a fluid transition between quests and conversations.- The game looks good. Every thing has beautiful details and the characters are REALLY creatives and colorful.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I don't often leave reviews, but I wanted to for this game. I've been having a blast playing it. The writers for this game are amazing, not using a fan of text based speech games, but this was hilarious to read through.Sure the game is new and there's bugs and some quality of life improvements I'd like to see in the future, but this game has a great dev team and an active community and things just improve by the day. Give it a try, highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: A cute game where you play as a Bear named Hank that refurbishes old, abandoned buildings and turns them into Bed & Breakfasts with the help of his friends. The art style is wonderful and the different decorations are really cute. However, the dialogue can be long and unnecessary. I tried streaming it for a few days, but the copious amounts of dialogue made it a pain after a while. Definitely much nicer to enjoy on your own. The story is kind of interesting and so are the characters. Some areas of the story are vague and I got stuck a few times and had to google how to get to the next part of the story. I think it's missing some quest hints in some areas, and the info online is very limited, so good luck finding the hints! Overall, I quite enjoyed it and I love winding down with this game before bed. I recommend it if you like cute, indie, cosy games.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: At 35.3 hours in, I am in total adoration of this game. So relaxing, so cosy, so cute and funny. I've been looking for a stardew-valley esque game for a while now. Whilst there are lots of differences between stardew and Bear and Breakfast, it gives me the same feeling of relaxation and contentment when playing it.I bought the game by chance on launch day and whilst there were some bugs and things to be tweaked, the devs were incredibly quick to act - both with fixing bugs and also finding creative solutions to some issues in game. (Mint, I'm looking at you.)I really hope this game gets the recognition it deserves and the devs have the opportunity to expand on the game in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and enjoyable management sim with a cute premise. The game does a good job of getting you familiar with mechanics as you go to each new location to open a new place to stay. While you do need to gather materials it never feels like a frantic race against the clock. You can take your time and explore or figure things out on your own pace. It's fun to see the characters interact with each other, especially with how guests will run at the sight of you until you get some pants on. Strongly recommended if you enjoy management sim games or just want a fun experience managing a B&B as a bear.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Liking the game so far. Very wholesome, cute and great art style. You mostly just run an inn, which is great! However there's a lot of down-times where you just wait and do nothing, but fear no more! Because I got exactly the ideas needed to improve the game and make it a little less repetitive, giving it more replay ability it needs and more fun, and trust me when I say it already is a lot of fun!1. The ability to use furniture. As well as eat and drink. Just more casual interactions for RP purposes. 2. Tasks from guests. Maybe some guest needs you to fetch them a candy bar or something. 3. Save animals from cages. There doesn't need to be an explaination for why they are in cages, but it could maybe make people know there's poachers or a danger in the forest.4. Fishing. Even better if it works as a minigame.5. Ability to bully guests. I'm sorry, but i've just played way too much sims to not want this. I wanna be able to trap guests in rooms by removing the door. Roar at them to scare them. Make them fall in their own litter. Amongst other things. Its just pure fun. Not asking for murder. Also makes for great content for youtubers to mess with.6. Our own plot to build a house. Perhaps let us decorate the outside as well. Maybe with an upstairs portion too. Also our room in the thicket would be nice to decorate.7. Buyable staff that works in the diner, shops ect.8. Minigames with guests. Could be simplistic stuff like connect four or kalaha. Just always fun. Back in the days of club penguin, this was literally something I played for 100 hours on end. So this is something I highly wish for.9. Some random creature to run from. Not fight. Just run from that can spawn at night. I just think it would be fun and add some intensity and scariness to the game. Perhaps if it grabs you, you could just wake up in your bed. Like it was all a bad dream. Maybe leave some small hints to what the creatures could be, but never tell it outright. People love a good mystery afterall.10. Leveling friendships. Maybe even a partner for Hank.11. Famous guests or critics, with more needs.12. More varied reviews. Its always the same text based on stars. Uncertain if its a bug? Would like some that were a bit more quirky or explainative. Like ''what in the world... There's a bear running this place? I'm not even gonna question it. 5/5''13. A shop to sell items or buy back.14. A trophy cabinet for rare items we find, or an aquarium for fishies we catch. I will keep adding upon this review as I get further through the game, but i'm a strong believer that these would do a lot, but i'm also aware its a lot more work than me just typing it here in a review. So I will try to keep my expectations realistic, but still be wishful!Can definitely recommend it to people looking for a fun wholesome game to just relax playing. It doesn't require any enormous brain power. Which is always great, if you feel tapped out after a long day.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I 100% the game a few months agoI'd say that the early game and the late game is really hard to get through because for me both boiled down to waiting a lot. However these sections are minuscule compared to what I did most which was actually actively work on my cabins and also keep hunting for resourcesIt was a fun experience and I really liked the flexibility in designing the cabins, though I would say the editor is a tad bit scuffed.the story was very engaging and the graphics are very cute. Hank is a cutie.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the first 10-15 hours of Bear & Breakfast. Around the middle of the game, the emphasis shifts from designing to managing, which I found noticeably less fun. There are ways to eventually automate certain tasks, but by that point I was already feeling a bit burnt out.I also found the epilogue to be unnecessary and tonally out of place with the rest of the game. There is a good game in here, but there is also a lot of unnecessary padding.I played on Steam Deck and it worked well enough, though I imagine a mouse and keyboard is probably the preferred way to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: The game gets boring and annoyingly repetitive only a couple of hours in. I tried to keep going to see if it would get better, but it didn't. Quests take way too long, and the time spent waiting to be able to complete them can only be spent roaming the simple and minimally interactive map. Additionally, for a hotel managing game, there is surprisingly little interaction with guests.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Right up my alley. A relaxing management game where you don't need to worry about finances, hence you can't fail no matter the quality of your business. The absence of challenge can bother some, but it's something I can perfectly live with since my goal is not to be stressed about money (I have real life for that) but just to have a casual b&b in the woods, work on it however I like and do quests. So far so (very) good.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: After fully completing bear and breakfast, i have mixed feelings. I wanted to love this game. I told all my friends and family how excited i was for it. But overall, it feels like it just wasn't playtested enough and I think it really would have benefited from early access. It's a fun and adorable concept that you really want to like. But the more you play the harder it gets to enjoy it? It has horrendous pacing and the quests don't line up with how you actually play through the story. It's misleading to say that you run a bed and breakfast, because really it becomes you barely managing 5 different properties where each one felt like a waste of time? In the beta you focused more on just the one and making guests happy and cooking. In the full game you do that a little bit until you automate everything and there's no reason to manage anything anymore, and then you move onto the next property? Not to mention the "managing" isn't really great and you have limited options. The story was cute but felt poorly done due to the bad pacing of the game and the story progression. The characters are all really well designed and interesting but once you meet and basically use the characters for what they are meant for, you barely interact if at all, with any of them again. You never talk to your friends again until late game, and once you get the full ending, the story just. Ends. And there is absolutely no reason to keep playing because there is nothing left to do or interact with. No reason to keep the b&b running because you don't need to? It's just so disappointing. But it is a cute world and it's fun to gather and decorate, but it just feels so hollow. I think if you like cozy, less in-depth management games it can be enjoyable to play, but just not satisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Did not expect this game to be as funny as it is. Just what I needed. Loving it thus far. I do prefer playing with mouse/keyboard instead. It's not too controller friendly imo (which I usually use). If you love cute, funny, management games (E.g. Coral Island, Stardew Valley) this is for you! The low price make it okay for the game to not be ''perfect''.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I very much enjoy this game, there's a little bit of bugs but I'm hopefully assuming they will be patched out rather soon.I will say, however, some of the games decoration needs can be a bit tedious, with some rooms requiring a lot of decoration for spaces that are a bit too small for them to handle it all, and the trash collection could also be a bit better as it's a little frustrating sometimes when you're all out and you can't buy decorations. Let it be known I just got to the second area, A24. One really frustrating thing, however, is the bathroom. Why does the bathroom have a sort of like "area of effect" sort of thing? The bar doesn't seemingly have that and affects every room in the building, but having a bathroom in the corner of the building means that the bedroom on the other side apparently has just no hygiene whatsoever? That's a little annoying and quite silly and it would probably be better if that was taken out entirely unless there's MUCH larger buildings. But in the motel? Pretty annoying. Overall, I think it's fun, I'm a big fan of bears and the artstyle is just adorable. I have some gripes with the game, but so far I've been having a pretty good time with it. I hope to see some more quality of life updates to the game in the future, just make it a bit more player-friendly.I'd give it a strong 4/5, fix those problems I mentioned and some of the bugs and I'd gladly give it a 5/5
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice and cozy management game with some issues with quality of life areas and some mechanics that you might enjoy but I didn't.The game is alright, you manage 5 hotels in 5 different areas you unlock during the story each one introducing a new room and sometimes a new mechanic.The issue for me mainly was the cooking, I really didn't enjoy running around finding ingredients, cook and see all the food disappear in 2 days, thankfully you get an npc to cook for you fairly soon, after that you cook only for quests.The other problem was the time, at the end i only had some area quests remaining and just needed time to pass and you are not able to advance time in any way other then waiting, it's a but annoying but I think I read somewhere the devs were fixing it.Aside from this the game is a good enough management game that isn't very deep but lets you make nice rooms
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very relaxing, adorable, and fun game. The pace can be a bit on the slow side, but the characters have funny scripts and you just can't not love this freakin' bear.  HOWEVER! If you don't enjoy and slower pace, LOTS of walking, and crafting, this may not be for you. I actually think the cooking mechanic is really clever, but it can get old really quick when you have to keep on top of cooking for multiple inns. It's a game that takes patience. Cute, but keep that in mind.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute and relaxing game. To go into what some other players were saying: Most people seem to spend 30-40 hrs to complete it but I think that's only for completionist styles. I took 20 hrs and I did a bunch of side quests, so probably you can finish this game in 15-ish hours if you only want to complete the story. The optional side quests are the management type quests that are focused on improving the hotels - the real time sink of the game, but can be largely skipped if wanted. Even at the endgame I didn't think there was too much waiting around, like others said. The only waiting point was when you had to acquire 50.000 coins, other than that there was always something to do.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Did I think this would be my favorite game of 2022? Yes. Is it living up to the expectation? Yes. Is it exceeding those expectations? OH YES!You are a bear. You renovate buildings out in the wilderness. Humans come out and stay in them and pay you money and leave trash. You use those funds to build them better and buy improvements with the trash to make them more beautiful. You even learn how to garden and do plumbing and things that shouldn't be possible for a bear. Yes, even for a bear like me. Your best friends include a walking pigeon, a raccoon salesman, an overly excited adventure fox, a mafia rat, a park ranger, and a construction beaver. What could go wrong?By the end? You're a fully clothed bear running a successful hotel chain out in the middle of nowhere and no one is the wiser.

_childDocuments_.review: I think it's best to think of Bear and Breakfast as a narrative game with management sim elements. If you're expecting a game with extreme customisation for your BnB, you'll be sorely disappointed. However, if you go into it to explore a world with a vibrant cast of characters and a linear story, you'll be much better equipped to enjoy this game.The mechanics of this game are fairly standard for a farming sim game, but they are very well executed. You get recipes and blueprints to deck out buildings in various zones. You can't really influence most of the map, though; your customisation is limited to the buildings. And honestly, I was fine with this, but I know lots of people may have a problem with it. I didn't find the loop of catering to the visitors too tedious; it gives you enough time to do what you need to do and also explore. Of course, in the late game you can dedicate most of your time to exploring the world and narrative, as you gain the ability to automate some functions. I do appreciate that Hank doesn't need to sleep, but can also sleep anywhere, which helps with the pacing of the game. I thought the game was a little too slow at the start, but I felt like it picked up to a comfortable pace once you unlock the A24 zone. The quests were fine; besides Charlotte's quests, I didn't find any of them too fetch-questy and most of them made sense for where they were positioned.The game does a really good job with their characters. Both the dialogue and the design mark each characters as unique and quite likeable. I do wish that you got to know a lot of them more. I especially wanted to find out why they stayed after the disaster. You get glimpses of the past with a lot of the characters, but very few get their full story explored. The ones whose past you do get to find out about, I honestly found it a lot more touching than I expected it to be. To lead onto narrative, I think this game is just one degree off being a banger of a story. The game has a great setting with a great background, but it just needed a lot more of whatever they did in the Epilogue, because I think the Epilogue was just... unexpectedly great. I just wish the whole story could have carried the kind of care that they put into the story of the Epilogue.The art was lovely! The cute style is what drew me to the game to begin with. I love watching Hank bounce around, his animations are so adorable! :D I barely noticed the music, which means it did what it was supposed to do for the game. I do have to bring up that the sound effects were really nice and well thought out- I'm not sure how to explain it but the sound of leaves crunching when you forage or the little ding when you're cooking just really makes my day :D It's not easy to do sfx in games like these without it being annoying, and I think this game did a really good job of it!I would have to say that all in all I'm very neutral about this game, simply because the entire time I played it, it felt just one step down from being something really being awesome. If you know you like these types of games, then by all means give it a go! But I do also think it's a game you can pass on without worrying too much.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! I'm only 6 hours in, but I see myself playing this game nonstop. The pacing is excellent, the tutorials are short and sweet and to the point, and I find myself chuckling at the dialogue. There's so much to do already and I haven't even started the food portion of the game, nor dug deep with each character. I am looking forward to the weekend so I can play longer and really get my motels looking better. I feel like every time I think, "I wish the game let me have/do this..." I complete a quest and get that as a reward instead of it being given to me right from the beginning. It's super fun to earn these things and I am eager to keep going! Great cozy game!
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: This is easily one of, if not my favorite games of all time. The art style is so adorable and full of life, and the game play loop is great! I have sunken so many hours into discovering and interacting with the colorful cast of characters, and would easily recommend for players who love management games. 10/10!
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Nice, whimsical, casual game for people who don't like time constraints and tight linear stories. The idea that people are staying at a hotel run by a bear is hilarious. What's even more hilarious is that you win more and more clothes over time that you can put onto your bear and the customers actually think you're a person. They no longer run away in fear when you're around the various properties and I think that's hilarious. Some aspects I think need tweaking or changed- taking furniture out of a room is a huge pain in the ass because there is no key binding to just put it away into your inventory. you have to actively put the piece of furniture into an empty space in your inventory otherwise it will just stay in the room. this is especially annoying if you're trying to upgrade your room levels and have to switch out multiple pieces at one time. - there is no way to run so going back and forth between quests is kinda tedious. the bus system helps but if you're running back and forth between a property and a quest giver, it can have you running all over the map at a single speed. - there's no way to pass the time except for at night when you're allowed to sleep. this is especially relevant in the beginning of the game where you're just waiting around for customers to stay a night and then leave. sometimes i'd be done decorating or setting up my location before mid day and i'd just have to alt tab and do something else waiting for the time to pass. at that point my inventory was pretty full so there was no use in scavenging. - the way the game is drawn, it's hard to tell what you can or can't walk through. there are textures like rocks and other formations where it's not obvious on whether or not it's an obstacle. especially in the more detailed areas like the forest. - there isn't a way to sell items yet so there was a point where i had to wait for guests to leave because i had no money for my next quest but i had tons of items in my inventory i could have sold for extra cash. same goes with the trash store. there isn't a way to accumulate trash other than guests leaving messes or discovering a new area and clearing out the empty buildings. i hope they implement a trading system so you can get rid of things that are clogging up both the stash and bag. i also had the issue of buying one too many furniture blueprints so that was automatically money wasted. - there needs to also be a deconstruction function where if you have lower level items then you can salvage them for resources. i have tons of level 1 and 2 items that are just sitting in my stash right now doing nothing and they took a reasonable amount of resources to make so being able to get SOMETHING back instead of just trashing them would make more sense. - there needs to be away to see what level a room is. it took me a while to get my dining room to level 2 because i couldn't figure out which pieces didn't fulfill the reqs. in the bedroom menu at the desk, it shows the raw values for each thing like decoration and comfort but it doesn't help you figure out what level the game considers each room. especially since many bedroom items look very similar despite being different levels, i think there needs to be a system or some indication to help make it easier to know if you're fulfilling the requirements for leveling up. - there's no way to split stacks so if you're cooking, you'll cook the entire stack of whatever you put in so i may not want to make 40 bowls of apples. also sometimes the inventory will not collapse and consolidate stacks so you might have like 4 of the same furniture taking up space but you have to manually put them in a stack. overall i'm enjoying the game. i play a lot of simulators and crafting based games and so far i'm impressed. i like the art style and i like how there are different themes to each map area. the characters are likable and the dialogue is entertaining. i'll be on the lookout for updates.

_childDocuments_.review: So after playing this pretty obsessively for about 15 hours, I've got mixed opinions. I think the game is SO cute and very addictive, but there definitely needs to be a little bit more polish around the edges in some places (devs are aware of the bugs, and I feel like some animations/sprites(?) are a bit off in places?)Most of all, I think the game needs significantly more balance, or the ability to move time forward whenever you want.
