_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: So let me be clear, I am enjoying my time with the game, but it shows it's flaws fairly early on with the game.For starters, at the point I am in the game, the building elements are awfully basic and few and far between. Instead you're gonna spend a bunch of time running errands for other NPCs, which will usually either progress the game or award you some item or tool you need to progress the game.The NPCs aren't anything special. Very few of them have much to say, in most cases, unless it's for a quest line, they will quickly begin to repeat themselves.Quest tracking isn't great, they often fail to properly explain what they want, the quest tracker often won't show where to go until you are on specific maps, which leads to wandering around.Some resources like wood will respawn on a near constant basis, while none of the other resource piles do so. The garbage dump was clearly designed to be the resource hub for stuff like nails and screws, but the RNG on getting things you need can often be questionable at best.The game suffers from a painfully slow pace. Early on, I had upgraded the shed to host two guests at one time and did so. After they had already left, I noticed a quest from the shark, which wanted me to have at least +2 more guests. Because it didn't count the ones I've just had, instead I had to wait for more guest requests, then I had to wait at least a day for them to show up, then two days each for them to leave before I could complete the quest.At this time, I literally had nothing else to do, so I just stood there and allowed the game to run in the background, because besides sleeping, which you can only do at specific times in the game, there is NO WAY to increase the flow of time, something that every simulation needs.So I clear that quest, advance the game, unlock the Motel in A24 and guess what? The quests for that place are the same and the extra quests for the old area are nothing more than more and more guests.And these stupid, boring quests are often what you need to do in order to progress in the game. They will otherwise hold you back from making any sort of progression. The rewards of quests more often than not are either minor or used as a vehicle for progress.  Unlock Area --> Collect Junk --> Upgrade Area --> Perform Quests from Shark, rinse and repeat. These quests should either have a meaningful impact or used to teach players how to play the game, not be the entire focus of the game. Finally, they show NPCs helping the Bear out doing stuff, that must be a later in the game because the NPCs do ♥♥♥♥-all otherwise. Heavy on dialog, a collect-a-thon, lite simulation mechanics, poor pacing, lack of direction. There's a lot of stuff here that needs to be corrected before I can recommend this game to anyone else.I see what they were trying to do here, but there's just so little to do and in an attempt to hide that, they locked almost everything behind pointless quests that waste your time forcing you to stand around for day(s) at a time.Edit: Based on the updates and Developer responses, I doubt this is going to be a game that I find myself playing long term. I personally feel like there's plenty of valid complaints about the game and the developers response to these complaints has been disappointing at best. Why do I have to wait a specific time to sleep? Why can't I do it whenever I want? Further, you explaining how the prints work doesn't actually fix player complaints about how often you get prints. This is probably going to be one of those titles I uninstall and never come back to, for me personally I felt like Bear & Breakfast was misrepresented in to what kind of game it was going to be.The game will show you very early on what it's about, which is literally just making loops on different maps to collect junk, to make stuff to keep customers happy, to collect money, to afford more crap.It's apparent that the developers had a very specific idea of what they wanted their games to be and are so dedicated to what they want that they are unwilling to make quality of life updates that have any sort of meaningful impact.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Am loving this game so far, characters are cute, dialogue funny, mechanics pretty straight forward. If you want a cosy management game this is it! the only thing that I could think that needs improvement is, a way to edit the rooms after you've confirmed them. _childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute, decently relaxing, and enough variety to keep you interested if you're into this sort of game. My only complaint is that the building mechanism is really difficult as your buildings get larger. _childDocuments_.review: The ultimate chore simulator. I am perfectly content with the first 18hrs of gameplay, but after that the game becomes borderline insufferable to deal with. I did everything you possibly can (35hrs later), so I can safely say that the quality of gameplay declines over time. _childDocuments_.review: If you want a slow, peaceful game then, yes, you'll like this.Some lacking Quality of Lifes areas have ground away at my willingness to play this, but I suspect I'll cycle back to it. Really it's a sideways-thumb for me. A yes with caveats.Biggest caveat: I tried playing it on controller but found the UI navigation too frustrating. Now for the nitty-gritty complaints:You can see all your rooms stats at the Check In desk.The Build Menu is a separate item that you must walk outside to use. In the Build Menu you can only see a room's name and stats when you hover over an empty bit of floor. Doors interrupt your cursor and cannot be hidden. You can also place carpets and rugs which will interrupt your cursor. An overlay option in this menu to quickly review your rooms without packing and redeploying half your decor would do wonders.I recommend making nice, big, spacious rooms if you play this game. I had fun dividing the resorts into dozens of rooms, stacked with nice comfy footstools, but... Yeah. Probably not the intended experience of a B&B!You spend a lot of time plodding through the environment, scrounging for things to interact with and collect while you wait for progression to be made possible again by guests finishing their stay.My cramped motel has definitely given me enough money to start afresh and make some nice, spacious rooms, but I've lost motivation. Main reason for this is the wish for a more robust filtering system. The different crafting menus and stores share this issue: the broad categories of "Furniture" and "Cooking Ingredients" don't cut it when you need to find the Bedroom specific furniture or just one piece of corn in an ocean of options. An option to filter by item level also wouldn't be amiss.There are some Quality of Life features, like Shift+LMB to split a stack, so maybe there's others I'm unaware of.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: If you have a love of management games, tolerance for moderate jank, and more free time than you'd expect to need to get to the end of the story for a game of this type, you'll probably enjoy this game more than I did.Pros:-Very cute-you have a lot of control over the appearance of the inns and layout of rooms-making rooms and decorating is largely intuitive and satisfyingCons: -the rate of progression is agonizing (many instances of having to wait through in-game time for enough guests to visit to finish a quest, being blocked from doing things that will obviously be necessary later simply because it's not time yet, may have to wait for resources to respawn because you don't have enough of certain materials)-npcs are uninteresting but chatty and you cannot skip dialogues -resource gathering that feels like a chore rather than gameplay-the cooking mechanic singlehandedly made this game far worse in my opinion-locked out of many mechanics that would make these annoyances less irritating until far too late to save it
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Whatever your preconceived ideas are for this game, they're almost certainly correct. It's a really simple gameplay loop of cleaning out old shacks and then drawing in rooms before building up currecny to add nice comfort or decorative items.As the game progresses you'll find customers start to demand better comfort levels and certain amenities but the game paces your progress nicely alongside those demands.Be prepared for some down time once you get past the tutorial threshold, there are times where goals are aligned to completing "stays" so you'll be wondering around just waiting for people to finish their booking to complete a quest and move on in the game. You can fill the time collecting resources and luckily days don't take too long to pass but I think that may leave some players feeling like they're bored.Overall though it's an excellent, cozy game and you play as a bear. The bear is funny, the other animals are funny. The dialogue is very silly and I'd say the humour is more grown up than you'd expect from a cute animal game. Most importantly I can now speak fluent bear. 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: This game starts out very fun and slowly becomes more and more grindy over the course of a playthrough. I feel that the long term gameplay was not sufficiently tested as proven by the fact that Iron Nails are a finite resource required for dozens of late game structures and it is very possible to run out of them almost entirely. There are quite a few bugs such as locking yourself into a bathroom with guests and having difficulty selecting the piece of furniture that you wish to pickup or move. You will also hit a point where you require so much money, and having employees assist you costs souch money, that you will want to keep the game up afk while the gold comes in, as it is entirely impossible to earn money through active participation. I would recommend getting this game once it has been out for a while and patched a few times.Update 8/3/2022 - The devs have been quick to patch the game, and most of the issues I had have been fixed. I am looking forward to the future of this game and am updating my review to a recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed playing this game. _childDocuments_.review: Absolutely adorable, chill, hotel-building and management, sandboxy game without any pressure.The art is adorable and cute, the characters are lovable and the attention to detail is amazing. If you're looking for a game to chill to and enjoy a beautifully crafted world, you're in the right place. You can take all the time you want and need, there is no time limit to anything and gathering resources does not get tedious, even though you have to do it often, because the landscape is so lovely.What others have criticised - that you have a "tutorial" until almost all is done, I can't support. I liked that I got introduced to all mechanics by and by, to not be overwhelmed by everything at once. That adds to the chill factor for me, others find it tedious. However, I did not felt too much hand-held, so to speak.If you're looking for a challenging hotel management game, you're in the wrong place, though. If you want a fast-paced game with risks, then this is clearly also not for you.The only thing that really is a chore is inventory management, as you have to drag and drop items from one inventory to the other, no quick button-mouse combo to get stuff from A to B.Otherwise, can totally recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: I've got mixed feelings about this one, but since I usually enjoy these types of management-based cozy games, I do think that I have had a good time playing this overall.However, that doesn't change the fact that the game has got issues.For some backstory - I love management games. Some of my favorite games have always revolved around some kind of management aspect (ex: Zoo Tycoon 2, Planet Zoo, & various run-your-own hotel mobile games), so this game caught my eye pretty much as soon as it was released. What initially drew me to this game was the adorable art style and the aforementioned management gameplay. I would still say that these aspects of the game are enjoyable. The art is some of my favorite I've ever seen in a game like this, super warm and cozy -- the loading screen art is beautiful and the cutscenes are super cute and unique. The gameplay, too, fulfilled my pressing need for a game of this type. There were some issues, though. Mine started as soon as I opened the game. As a completionist-of-sorts (I'll admit I'm not hugely motivated like some are, but I try) I was super disappointed when I realized my achievements weren't "popping". 15 minutes and a lot of forum searching later, I find out for some reason save slot 3 is the only one that allows achievements to work. Weird, but okay. I start the game for the third time at this point in the correct save slot and fast forward through the cutscenes I'd already seen. All the achievements are working now, so I'm relatively happy but worried for what this means for the rest of the game.I finish my first several quests which takes another hour or so. and then I find I'm stuck on what to do next. This cycle is one that repeats frequently for me in the first two hours or so of gameplay. When you're just starting out, you only have one B&B. This isn't a problem until you realize all the quests in the game are tied to your progression/completion of various tasks surrounding the B&B's you manage (aside from a few 2-part side quests that were basically all already solved by the time I received them). In other words, in the beginning of the game, you have one quest to fulfill, and because these quests build upon each other, you are basically stuck waiting around or collecting what few resources you can while you wait to complete that one quest. I think this flow of gameplay is stunted due to the lack or quality of the first few side quests you receive (all fetch quests) and the fact that you can't access some quests due to you having to complete the one previous to do so.This issue quickly goes away though, like I said, because as you unlock more locations and management properties, you basically have your hands full (paws full?) balancing B&B management, side quests, getting better furniture, etc. that time seems to move faster while waiting for those pesky 'get 10+ visitors stays completed' quests to complete. The beginning is a slog though, I will admit.I think most of my issues with this game seem to stem from QOL problems rather than straight up issues with the game. For example, something that annoyed the [insert chosen expletive] out of me while playing was that you can't, for some reason, zoom out on the map? And it's SUPER zoomed in. It's just little oversights like that that bothered me the most while playing. Unlike most players it seems, I didn't mind cooking or the heating. Once you get *SPOILER* to cook for you, you don't really have to worry about cooking anymore. And the heating for me was just a matter of having two utility rooms per property and a level 2+ heating item. I actually found most of the time I was well above what the guests were asking for, but that has no penalties in this game so most of my guests were frying rather than freezing.I do enjoy this game, though, and I do plan on getting 100% completion. Like I said, I enjoy these types of games, so your mileage may vary if you don't AND you find issue with everything else I listed before. I can tell a lot of care and love went into this game and that with a little more attention, I think it can really shine the way the developers want it to for others.

_childDocuments_.review: I followed this through dev and while it changed, it's a super fun and sweet little chill game where you run several B&Bs and collect stuff and build stuff.I haven't played it since some of the updates, but I'm going to get back into it.Pros: It's chill, doesn't feel as stressful to me as other building and timed games.Cons: I bounded ahead of some of the content early and was confused when I couldn't do some stuff, but then the story caught up and I was ok.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had this wish-listed for so long, and let me tell you...IT WAS WORTH THE WAIT! I was literally bouncing up and down on release day! _childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: A "cozy game" with its heart in the right place, but a lot of problems in the meantime.I found myself walking behind wall decorations, getting stuck in random corners, being unable to see what I'm stuck on in other places and more. What is a "level 2 bedroom" and how do you get one? Apparently its not "fill the room with high decor and comfort items", as that's the only thing you CAN do.Also, the room rating system runs into a problem with entrensic value (sp). If lamp A is worth 1 point and lamp B is worth 4, I would NEVER have a reason to use lamp A ever again. But what if I like how lamp A looks more? With the high and demanding numbers that some customers wanted, I had to JAM rooms full of junk and cover the floors with tons of little rugs making tacky, crowded spaces trying to please them. They were no longer the rooms I wanted to make.This is an "OK" game that you can get for free on the Epic Game store, I'm sorry I spent money on it. It was fun for a few sit downs but I just hit road block after road block and had to ask on the forums over and over about things that really should have been intuitive to do. Cozy games by their very nature should be easy and stress free and self explanitory, and Bear and Breakfast just isn't.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game although it's not without some minor issues. The game play loop was enjoyable. You fix up various locations of bed and breakfasts in kind of a similar way to Two Point Hospital, although not as in depth and more laid back. The art style is very nice and cozy. Progression of unlockable items felt good and timely. It has a bit of a back story, but in all honesty, I didn't really get it. To me, it felt like chunks of it were missing, but it doesn't effect the game play so it didn't bother me. There is a weather system which I didn't really care for. In my play through snow and rain consistently blew across the entire screen even when indoors making it hard to see, particularly at night (fyi, you can sleep through the night) Just wish there was a on/off toggle for that. Quests were a bit ambiguous at times, but luckily a quick search usually brought the answer of which direction I needed to head for. My only other gripe is the cooking system. I like the way it worked because it's unique from other games but without the ability to select a number of dishes you want to make it quickly became tedious for me. All in all I really enjoyed this game, none of my gripes were bad enough to make me not want to keep playing and I definitely think it's worth checking out if you like these sorts of games.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: If you're the kind of person who relentlessly slams your controller buttons/keyboard keys, and sounds like your hyperventilating as your playing PC games, this is probably not a game for you, as it is not a fast pace game. This game is RELAXING. If you're the kind of person who is used to playing high intensity FPS games, then do not fault this game as "not having enough going on." I personally love this game, and feel that as a B&B management game, it does indeed have a lot to it without being overwhelming to a person ridden with anxiety such as myself. The graphic design is cute and easy on the eyes, as you play an adorable teenage-ish grizzly bear renovating old cabins to bring back the hoomans after it was once destroyed by fire. At night there is plenty to do while waiting for customers to arrive at 9am. You can go around collecting materials to build things, and find trash that you use as money to buy decor for your cabins. If you've accomplished those things, you can simply press the sleep at night button that'll bring you straight to check in time. Once a furniture item has no use to you, you must throw it out. Ive seen others wish to be able to sell items no longer needed, but I personally feel with the amount of income I have rolling in, I have no need for extra money, as that will only speed the game up to where it wont be enjoyable. Ive played other relaxing games such as Lake, but was heavily dissapointed in how short the game was. This game has a decent length to it for its kind, and I really love it. I hope that in the future, perhaps there could be some DLC where new locations are added to the map to enjoy. I would be first in line to buy them.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I simply love everything about this game everything about it it's just so darn cute i honestly thought that i won't like it as much but here i am 9 hours in and still playing it and loving every moment of it. There's so much to do in this fun game and there's always something about this game makes me coming back to it everyday to continue the story the fact you're a bear building things is the best part lol. If you are conflicted on rather you should get it or not like i did then stop and just go for it and enjoy the ride. I do highly recommend if you enjoy a cozy games and this game does give you that vibe. This game is such a wonderful experience and it has become one of my top favorites.

_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: So new favorite game! I don't obsess over games often and I love this game so far. played about 6 hours straight so far, and only stopped because I have work in like 7 hours.. (minor spoilers ahead)stuff I like so far:-The art and animations are so cute and easy on the eyes-NPCs feel alive bc of the animations-Havn't noticed any guest names being reused-story and cute commentary-lots and lots creativity while building-being able to explore and adventure freely- progressing and being rewarded for it with useful things-being rewarded for adventuring-crafting!-cooking!-being able to sleep through the night in game-fast travel-really cool designs for every character you encounter-little details like finding wood in the forest instead of chopping down trees (bc u play as a bear) just make sense and is one of those small quirky things in the game that makes me happystuff I don't like so far:-when talking to NPCs their sentences are reused. it can get boring and makes them feel less alive-not being able to talk to guests (so far as as I know)-some small bugs (this game just came out so duh. but there is a forum online that tells you how to fix the bugs you encounter when you click "report bug" in game. which i think is very nice).- I am slow (so far)and thats all my thoughts so far. _childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to recommend this to other players for sure. I think it is so cute and fun. It is a game I definitely see becoming an amazing game that players love.  However, I will point out a huge issue I am running into seeing how this is a new game it is to be expected. I am writing this review to allow developers to know about this issue. When I go to the A-24 zone and start to build on the hotel via crafting table, nothing will come up on occasions, and then it does not allow me to even exit out of the crafting table alone. When this issue is happening I can only build rooms and delete them no doors come available. Nor does it allow you to move items into the rooms.  A first day playing. Due to this issue, I have had to force exit the game more than 7 times already. I hope this can be helpful in some way to point out an issue that can cause more issues down the line. Thank you
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: It's a cute game, but I was not able to continue, finish the story/ quest lines, because when I went back on just recently my save slot said 0 coins and 0 trash (apple icon) like my save had been erased then when I clicked on my save slot (which was slot 3, that's the only save slot that achievements will work on Steam, for whatever reason) the game would not get past the loading screen, so I re booted the game a few more times, at each time, it would be the same issue. _childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Its a beary cute game, Its a relaxing at your own pace game that is easy to pick up and drop without any penalties or game overs which has been perfect for me since I just had a kid a few months back. Only downfall is you can't sell or breakdown things you craft so you end up just deleting the items. Also a shift click to add or remove items from your inventory would be great but over all not having these does not damper my fun playing. I really hope the devs come out with an update or dlc cause after seeing the dark area I need to build a spooky hotel lol
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game, enjoyed decorating, getting all of the quests done, and unlocking all the achievements. Story and characters are done well. If I could erase my memory and replay it again, I would lol. If you like Stardew Valley or animal crossing or games like that you will enjoy this game. Give it a shot! _childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! In-depth management sim, down to guests groaning about your lack of pants! (FREE BEAR!!!) Also delightful story, gives it an RPG feel that really complements the aesthetics. Superb walking sounds and music for each location! I could just fall asleep under the trees. And mid/late-game automation leaves you free to do just that! Adorable, delightful, and mysterious game.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: This game looked so cute. Unfortunately it just fell flat in so many ways. The building/crafting controls are unnecessarily confusing, the quests are boring, the characters just don't *do* anything. Only 5 hours in and I'm already so bored. And unfortunately the art is not as cute as it first appears, and something about the music really turned me off.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I came into this expecting a cozy game. And it is, sort of. But it is also very CAPITALISM HO. The urge to replay Recettear has grown with each passing in-game hour. It's cozy capitalism.+game for people who like to manage things+cute aesthetics & characters+no need to sleep, unless you want to+trash panda furniture store, recycling at its finest~+possum concierge+nice musics-worst inventory system I've seen in ages, unnecessarily small windows for chests, no inventory expansions-micromanaging a lot before you reach enough capital to keep staff paidTo me this game has some very fundamental issues with the inventory and management aspect but despite all that I love playing. The characters, the story, and the world just pull me in. And Hank is the perfect main character.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I love this little game. Its really peaceful, and you can come back to it easily. Cleared it in one go with ~40 hours in.I am considering getting it on switch and replying it in the future.Pros:- adorable concept, art, and game setting- art and sound- witty mechanics - easy to come back toCons:- i am not sure i understood the main story- some bugs -NPCs walking outside the map, getting stuck in clear areas, loosing my game items- sometimes the building walls stay up, and cant be interacted with until game restart
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: The humour in this game is top-notch. The characters are amazing. The gameplay can be a little slow at the first, and then, suddenly there aren't enough hours in a day. Good thing you can hire an opossum! I'm really having fun with the making over of these abandoned sheds and cabins. There are a couple rough spots that are being worked on, but all in all? _childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game as a Christmas present for myself, and haven't stopped playing since! I am in love with the art-style, game-play and just the general vibes. Not trying to compare it with other games, but still, if you enjoy games like the Sims, Stardew Valley, ACNH and are wondering if you should buy this, I'd say go for it!
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Bear and Breakfast is a fun take on a management building sim where you spend your days (and nights) as a bear named Hank who gets roped into helping revitalize the once booming tourist area. I had a lot of fun trying to balance all the different areas and getting the locations just right to make my guest happy. I enjoyed it so much it is only one of two games I have gone for 100% achievements on Steam for. I really hope they come out with some more DLC in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: enjoyable and cozy! The difficulty goes up according to the story so you can catch up very well! The only thing i'd change is that you can't really sort through the crafting inventory and when you get leveled up things you have to scroll through everything to find what you want in the level you want.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I recently had the pleasure of playing Bear and Breakfast and was thoroughly delighted by the game. The game is a unique and charming take on the popular "tycoon" genre, and tasks players with running a successful bed and breakfast for bears.One of the standout features of Bear and Breakfast is its heartwarming and wholesome atmosphere. The game is filled with cute and lovable characters, and encourages players to be kind and compassionate towards their guests. Whether it's making sure that the bears have comfortable beds to sleep in, providing them with delicious food to eat, or simply listening to their stories and needs, the game is a reminder of the importance of hospitality and generosity.In addition to its wholesome atmosphere, I also appreciated the game's simple and addictive gameplay. The game is easy to pick up and play, and offers a satisfying progression system that keeps players coming back for more. Whether you're trying to upgrade your kitchen, decorate your rooms, or attract more bears to your B&B, there's always something new and exciting to do in the game.Overall, I highly recommend Bear and Breakfast to fans of charming and wholesome tycoon games. The game is sweet and delightful, and offers a unique and uplifting gaming experience. Its simple and engaging gameplay make it an excellent choice for players who are looking for something fun and heartwarming.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: A quick, cozy, and story-rich hotel management game with a charming animal theme Bear and Breakfast truly surprised me. While I was expecting an easy and passive sim. game I was pleasantly surprised with the overall story line. Magical and tragic the lore gave me absolute chills while the game play gave me that warm and fuzzy feeling. I was able to complete the main story line in 35 hours however even after the main story line concludes the tycoon aspect of the game itself has high replay-ability and should they ever add more lore I will back playing this game again and again.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Exactly my kind of game :)Cute graphics, management and decorating (creating) rooms.The only thing I could probably complain about is the lack of side quests. During the game (I'm in the third hotel phase so far) you meet quite a few characters, usually do one or two small quests with them and then nothing.I'd really like it if, for example, when I unlock cooking I could cook something for someone and they'd give me one limited decorative item.Or something like that. I've had two times where I've had to wait a day or two for quests like accommodate 6 people and nothing to do in between.As far as decorations go they are awesome, but the only way to get them is through valuables and I haven't gotten any blueprints yet.I recommend this game :).
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an excellent cross section between my love of resource management, and my desire to be a bear. A couple things I'd like for future updates:- When placing items from a stack,  I'd like to keep holding the item as long as there are still items in the stack.- It'd be nice to have a better idea of the size and dimensions of an item without having to buy or make it.Otherwise great and good game :)
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: The game crashes whenever I try to make the bear sleep till the next morning. The screen just freezes and I can't progress unless I never sleep. _childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very easy to understand and comfortable, without being boring. _childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game!! The combination of cozy graphics, nature sounds, and many tasks to complete made it a lovely game to play! The creativity put into it was fantastic. Other than that it's a great game and was worth all the time I put into it. If you like cozy games and Stardew Valley, this game is for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game! Bear and Breakfast lures you in by being an adorable and funny game about being a bear running a b&b. But as I've played the story and the characters genuinely pulled me in. It is very relaxed, and I never felt like I was losing or getting punished (but I also didn't hire many employees). Bear and Breakfast is a video game that feels like a hug. If you're debating playing it and these kinds of relaxing business management/crafting games are your cup of tea, you should definitely check out this game :)
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend the game to anyone looking for a cozy time wasting game with a lot of constant running around, however there are a lot of issues to be ironed out at the moment. Hiring employees for example is an absolute rip-off. fully automating one of the inns I could understand losing 50% to 75% of the profit to be able to ignore it while I work on the biggest and newest Inn that I've unlocked but I barely make anything at all, in fact some days I even lose money on the staff. trash collection is better to just hire for one day every now and then and fire the same day because my god is it expensive and impossible to keep up with. the game is great in style and the Inn side of it to a point but weirdly enough I wish there was less to do. between managing all the inns (or else losing money on the staff), exploring, doing quests, gathering resources (because everything you use will be what you gather), cooking (Also way too expensive to automate), and getting the next inn decorated and functional for the first guests it's a bit of a scattered mess of time management. It's trying to be a bit too much all at once. I'm struggling to keep up, once the heating element was introduced I was pretty much almost giving up at managing all the inns and took the massive hit some of the staff would give me for some form of relief on what I needed to do each day to keep the inns running. it's cozy and cute but a bit stressful if you stress over keeping to all going and getting lower ratings because the staff aren't assigning rooms with guest stats in mind and instead just at random. I personally really enjoyed the game but near the end it just all became too much to juggle at once on top of running out of resources and having to go out to collect more not only for crafting items for the new inn but also to make food for the other inns because automating cooking is ridiculously expensive. I eventually just let the first few inns stop running and just decided to run three of the inns at max capacity to keep it from being as much of a mess with juggling it all. this made it a lot easier to manage but I was also just letting two of my inns be unused which is not preferable. I encountered some glitches as well, the most prominent being when I placed items in storage it just doubled the stack and left me with more, not even at a rate that I enjoyed getting free materials but to the point I was overrun with berries until I finally got rid of most of them.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I wanna recommend this game to others and I was going to hit recommend but I was writing the review and realized I was listing everything I wanted changed or fixed in this game. I don't hate this game and I think it's still worth playing, but if I had to give this game one word on how to describe it would be "headache". This game makes my head hurt. There's just so much to micro manage and very little help. Things I don't like about this game:-Cooking. I wish the game would tell me what I can make with what I have in my storage. I wish I didn't have to run cross map to get milk or butter. I feel like I'm always missing something. More storage is full of food but I'm always missing one thing and I have to run around to find the missing thing. Just such a headache.-Can't sell or recycle items. -Your friend characters you meet at the start that tell you to start a hotel don't help you in any way. You never see them again after the start. I mean you can see them if you go home but there is not reason to head back home.-Introducing characters and never really don't anything with them after you do there quests. I do like the story in this game.-So MUCH running back and forth.There's just a lot of little things that just get on my nerves after a while I could list but I don't want to. I do plan on playing it more because I want to know the end of the story but I probably won't touch this game again after that. Unless this game just gets a lot of life improvements. Which is possible. Day 1 b&b wasn't that great but they really fixed a lot with the first couple of patches. So I have hope that I might get some of improvements I want. I really want to like this game because it's so cute and I love hank. I wanna love it. It has so much personality.
