_childDocuments_.review: As many other reviews have stated, the character design, dialogue, atmosphere and artwork is all 10/10, its all absolutely amazing. However calling this game a management sim is a bit of a reach. The game is so rigid that there's not much to manage, you just do what the next quest tells you and there's typically only 1-2 real ways to reach the quests goal. I'm sure given the reviews some of this will be addressed, however as it stands its probably not really worth the money. I'm super excited to come back to this game in a while and see what they do with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I pushed through this game. I wanted to know what was going to happen, but in the end, it all just added up to nothing. Mysteries remain unsolved, but I've completed the game and it's just... over? What? I don't recommend, there's no fun to the designing and the story never takes you anywhere, though it hints at it.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I don't want to be strong like man who look pretty, I want to be strong like Bear who builds vacation getaways in the forest. Bear and Breakfast is charming, addictive, cute, weird, and downright hilarious. Characters and story have a fantastic sense of manic-sugar-snorting energy and the stylistic design is pleasant to the eyes. I need to get back to this game soon, but this is a weirdly-cozy-cute-odd-delightful game that is well worth the time and money to play. Give it a go, and build strong hotel in wood, like bear.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: My friend told me about this game and after following it on Twitter and getting more invested in the Bed and Breakfast world I can absolutely Recommend this game to anyone who enjoys life style sims and management sims. It's got cute a cute art style and visuals, charming writing, fun characters, a plot with a bit of mystery and a Bear as a main protagonist. You can tell a lot of passion was behind this game and I can stress how much it shows.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun, addicting game, that is 100% peaceful. Can be as fast-paced or slow as you want, really, because there's no time limits for doing anything. Cooking food for guests only takes about 10 seconds for every stack, which is fantastic! You can eventually hire other characters to help manage your B&Bs, which is lovely too. It needs some finishing touches, but is largely a game in great shape. The dev is very quick to respond to people on here, and is listening to feedback. I'm absolutely in love with this cute game!
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome comfy/cozy little game if you are looking for something to chill-out with. Simple enough to relax, but with some challenge to not get boring. Really enjoyed all the cute characters, each of them have their own story to tell some funny while others actually pretty tragic. The charming visual design and especially the catchy music is so well done, definitely a highlight. The endgame was a little drawn out for me, felt grindy. but the game was totally worthwhile, I had a lot of fun with it, even got all the achievements. I do wish there were a few more main story quests to balance the side quests. It's a good game to play to add some calm I play too many intense games and need to play more stuff like this. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Great atmosphere, fun concept, excellent art and design, wonderful soundtrack, and so much more. The only thing even slightly negative I could say about this game is the story's pacing is a little funky, but I suppose that's only par for the course of an "open world" type game such as this, and I know they're planning an update that will expand upon the existing story. All in all, great game, and I can't wait for the update!
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game at 35 hrs. Overall a very cute game, and it hits on that management/collecting resources that i enjoy. Positives: -Art style is adorable. -Inventory and how to select things (after you figure it out on your own cause its not apparently clear) is well organized. Negatives (that are more annoyances): -navigating the areas is sometimes annoying as you cant tell what you can walk through verse what you can not, so you spend a lot of time bumping into things. -no way to re-sell your old items. you can only trash them. It would be great if you could take all your old items back to Took (a cute garbage raccoon) and sell to him. Even if its for like half resources back (example spend 6 wood and 2 glass to make an item, sell back gets you 3/1) -the quests seem either too quick half the time or at the wrong time. There would be quests i unlock BUT i cant do them until a different quest is completed but the quest that needs to be done hasn't been unlocked. (hopefully that makes sense). So I would look up play-throughs cause i was getting so frustrated thinking i was doing something wrong...but nope just strange timing. 1 Big complaint: The story has no conclusion... it just ends. There is not even a banner that appears that says something as simple as "main story concluded". Because it ends by the dialogue just stopping and you're left wondering if there is something else. All of that considered, i still highly recommend this game. It has a ton of appeal and I found myself wanting to play it in all my spare time.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Beary adorable game! The art is amazing, the controls are smooth, there doesn't seem to be any major bugs, the characters are simple(for now at least, there seems to be a deeper lore which I haven't reached yet) but interesting. I've been hyped for this game for over a month and I must say that I am not dissapointed whatsoever!
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I like the game but the two main issues I have with it make it frustrating enough to not recommend it to others. The game functions on a mechanic where you get paid from your customers in the morning, but there's no way to time skip to the next morning if you genuinely have nothing to do. I understand it's set up this way so players don't just spam time skips but it gets annoying. I also think it's a problem if your tutorial is 1 to 2 hours long, since I genuinely don't know if I'm still in it or not. I've also dealt with a lot of lag while the game quicksaves (while your character is walking this happens) and seem to have encountered a bug where a level 2 blueprint just doesn't work. Overall it's a cozy management game that you might find some enjoyment out of if you're seriously interested in playing it but I would recommend finding it on a sale (like this is honestly not worth it for AU$29 compared to other games).
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I completed 100% of the game with every achievement and I can say that I absolutely loved this game, but I feel like it's not for everyone: the gameplay is basically you setting up resorts and dealing with management, chores, fetch quests, decorating, cooking, talking to other npcs, etc. It has everything I love since it's cute, funny, makes me lose track of time and keeps me entertained and curious. I read that some people eventually got bored of the resorts managing gameplay since it's a big part of the game, so think about whether you may like it or not. Having said that, it's very well done and polished and everything is so cute - sometimes in the end it can also be spooky. I hope there will be an update with more content or some sort of sequel <3 I took my time in completing the whole experience because I found myself drifting in decorating and cooking, which I liked very much. You could actually complete the game in less than my gameplay hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Cute, charming, and unBEARably hard to stop playing. There are definitely instances where I got ahead of where the story probably wanted me to be, or going to places before the plot needed me there. But it didn't hinder any game play. It just happens to have an excellent world worth exploring. I highly recommend joining the Discord server as well. It's been great keeping up with the devs about any possible bugs you may encounter. So far, I have not run into any issues. Overall, if you like management sim games and cute animals, it's worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: This game is super cute, not too hard to manage, and a nice way to relax. You can tell how much effort was put into this, and I love playing it, progressing, and becoming the ultimate bear and breakfast entrepreneur! My only gripes would be the opening - and while I've not completely finished the game yet, I cannot see the thinking behind the opening, it was a bit of a slog and I really didn't care about those initial characters - I can't even remember their names - the dog and bird. I was just clicking through to get to the main gameplay.Also, what is up with the heating mechanic??? I have smart heaters now and still can't balance the temp? I can't play in the winter area at all as it's too cold for guests.Overall I do really like this game and I would recommend it, mostly to the other cosy gamers out there!
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I was excited for this game to come out and got it when it went on sale. Love the art-style and decoration options.After a while the game play became boring, repetitive, and no longer much fun. The introduction of food/cooking became annoying to manage. The game requires you to run around the map doing fetch quests, but I would frequently run into solid objects. The story line is dull and doesn't make you feel connected to the characters.Spent lots of time AFK to pass time in game. Finished just for the achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: the management and building aspects of this are very light, and it is a somewhat linear story based game that feels simple and restrictive compared to other building and management games that i like which are more sandbox and focus more on building and management. the quests and the characters are the game. its not a bad game, just not the game i was expecting. if you like games like rimworld, oxygen not included, tycoon games, and city builders, just know this is not as deep as that. it's more like a cute game with casual building and basic management aspects. im sure i havent uncovered all the interesting things, but i dont enjoy following the quests/the gameplay loop so i wont be continuing. wish i could give it a sideways thumb, its not an objectively bad game. i think more casual players who like quests to guide them or children would like it and recommend it only to them. the bear is very cute and funny.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: It hurts to do this but I do not currently recommend this game, however with some QOL changes and fixes with bugs, I would change my review. The game is fun and relaxing but some of these things are well... unbearable.Pros: you are a bearreally great art styledesigning roomsfun storycons:running from the front of the hotel to get tooks garbage/stash for that ONE item you forgot, wasting daylight hourshaving to drag every. single. ingredient. to the inventory and doing the same back makes it tedious and unfun.Stats for guests staying jump around and make it really difficult to understand which is the deco stat and which is the comfort stat.No tutorial for deleting items, took me 15+ hours to find it.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really cute game, however there feels like a lot of wasted potential. The characters are well written but they are just cast away and only have 2 dialogue options outside of the main quest. Overall, the world feels really empty, even when guests are staying in your bnb. I found myself waiting for the days to cycle (which feels like forever) just to finish one mission. There's not much direction and I have explored what I could so the only thing left to do is leave my pc while the day cycles through. side note: spoke to the possum once and then he disappeared. Really strange.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: This is an engrossing game that increasingly challenges you, but always gives you guidance on what to work on next.  I personally liked, the management skills required throughout and the side quests that kept things entertaining while I waited for other things to conclude that required the passage of time in game.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I tried really hard to like this game. But it's just not doing it for me. Maybe my expectations were to high, but maybe not. I love the art style, but that's it. This game feels empty.I'm doing quest after quest, it's a big fetch quest and I'm endlessly smashing the E button. I love fetch guests, but there has to be some variation, a bit of challenge even maybe. This feels way too easy.Building rooms is a bore, everything looks the same and I'm not inspired to customize. My guests are fine with either room no matter how it looks as long at the rating is high enough (??). Guests have no personalities. No dialogue. They walk around like robots.It doesn't feel like I'm actually running a B&B. In fact, I'm never even making breakfast. Sure I get to cook, but I put the food in a room so quests can fetch it for themselves. They don't have personal food preferences and will just take whatever is available. Who cares if I make a soup or put down bowls of apples for dinner, nobody apparently. Nothing feels satisfying. Unlocking furniture feels off. Sometimes I get to buy blueprints from the shop but I buy them all at once. And sometimes I get new recipes right from the blueprint table. What's the point of the shop if there's rarely anything to buy except for when I unlock it through a quest? It's not like the shop has a different range of products everyday that I get to choose from, so I might as well get everything right from the blueprint table. Guests leave around trash that I get to buy furniture from through a dumpster. But at the same time whenever I get furniture upgrades I end up trashing all the old ones with nothing in return. No recycling whatsoever. Everything feels more like an early access than a finished game.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Finished it with all achievements out of spite but I can't recommend it. The game feels like there was a moment in development when all spirit and will was lost and it was 'shaped into somewhat-shipable thing' and sent off.There's way too many 'speed bumps' for it to be fun. Significant lack of quality-of-life UI elements. Multiple-step quests that require you to report back to quest giver with every single minuscule thing accomplished. I just skipped past all the lore in the end because i had no patience.Simple act of moving about the levels was annoying because collision boxes on terrain are visually barely indicated and often form weird 'pockets' that you get trapped into.I spent 1/3 to 1/2 of game time assigning guests to rooms and waiting for resources to spawn in the same exact locations and for the day to pass (you do have to wait).The art is nice. There was love put into this game. But there is no chill experience you might imagine it has.Tedium example:(I think there's a quest like that for every character but it was just so out of place')In the middle of some very grand exposition of weirdly big idea NPC you have to go back to cook something (which was a repeated annoyance). So...Walk to the bus stop to change zones. Go to kitchen to look up the recipe (AFAIK only viewable via kitchen), go pick up ingredients from the storage chest (because limited inventory)Walk to the bus stop to change zones. Go to the shop for stuff you can only buy.Walk to the bus stop to change zones. Go back to kitchen and cook.Walk to the bus stop to change zones. Go back to quest giver and give him his cooked egg or whatever.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best games I have ever played. I ADORE Hank and all the other characters you can talk to. All the dialogue is really funny, and I love the mechanic of having collectibles in the form of clothing for Hank. No matter what, I always want to keep playing and make the hotels even better. Love this game!!
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really sad about not liking this game. I originally bought it when it came out because of how cute it looked, but couldn't get into how slow the tutorial was and how annoying the cutesy dialogue was (maybe I'm getting old, who knows). A few days ago I decided to properly play and gave it my best shot for 13 hours. I'm not sure it was worth it. In the beginning the game is very manageable, but the more locations and features you unlock the more it starts being a chore instead of something to enjoy. It's very repetitive, and what attracted me the most (crafting, decorating) is not really an essential part of the game. I found myself roaming around the map constantly day and night looking for "valuables" (which is the currency used to purchase decorations) and just repeating a loop of collecting resources around various hot spots. Managing the resorts is maybe 1% of your day, the rest is just... filler.It gets old rather quickly. About 13 hours of gameplay quickly. I think the biggest problem for me is with how unbalanced this game feels. Progression goes either super quickly - by unlocking tons of new areas pretty much immediately, so you get overwhelmed with thousands of things to do - or grinds to a halt entirely. For example you're given quests you can't complete because you don't have the necessary thingamajigs/don't meet specific requirements, but you can't meet these until you get the thingamajig or more decorations (which aren't really easy to buy, considering "valuables" are pretty hard to come by after a while). So you end up just running around, completing the same loop without any diversions, and to me it was too much of a chore. I had to step back at some point because I was just playing and playing but I was bored and frustrated. The art and concept are great, but unfortunately it's a miss for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: If you love a good cozy game, this is definitely a game for you. The mechanics are really fun and it has an easygoing pace to it. The decorating is easy to grasp and you can make some pretty cool rooms. There's no right way to do things, so the decorating is very open ended and it was like fitting a puzzle together in order to get the maximum efficiency out of each building. There were a few glitches and issues like guest's wanting heat of 75F and still say its freezing when its 108F in the building, but overall it was a great cozy game to sit down for and relax with for a couple hours a day.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: This game is exactly what they describe on the box. It gives you quests to help you progress but you're never under pressure to make sure they are done right then and there. I'm 30+ hours in and still enjoying optimising my income. It plays how you want it to play.It does have some quirks but recent updates have improved the Quality of Life options and have taken away some of those quirks. For some of the quests I had to look up on how to get the items to fulfil the quest as I didn't realise that these were purchasable from a shop. This did create a significant slow down period for me, but others may not find that to be the case. Yet despite the slow down I found enjoyment in other areas of the game.The game advertises a bit of a mystery/story and as yet I haven't really come across the story as such, however, I have been taking it quite slow and enjoying the management side of things.All in all a really great relaxing but engaging management game.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: 5/10Not a bad game. Not a good game. It's just... a game.I wanted to scratch my Graveyard Keeper's itch and I didn't manage to do so. After ~20 hours you just put the game on afk farm to get the gold and finish the game because the waiting/grind isn't fun and there isn't much to do.Overall it's a fine concept but it wasn't done well enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: This game checks off a lot of things I look for in a game:✔ Cuteness✔ Humour✔ Adorable graphics✔ Adorable characters✔ Chill, relaxed, at your pace progress. ✔ Hours of entertainment✔ Fun decorating and cooking mechanicsI have very much enjoyed the hours I've put into this game and I look forward to being able to put in more. I love this game ♥BEARY♥ much. This game is definitely worth checking out!
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: FOR STEAM DECK AND CONTROLLER:Thumbs down because this game is poorly optimised for playing with a controller. Even after the last update that aimed at improving the controls. It is one of the worst implementations I have ever seen.Generally I can recommend the game. It delivers its promise and is quite fun. Below things I'd like to see improved:- controller support, obviously- the general UI/UX is not good. It's not very user friendly and not intuitive. I often need a moment to understand what needs to be done in each screen.- the music is too repetitive and not unique. While the general ambient noise in the background is good and fitting, I personally do not like the soundtrack.- I'd like to see more options for modifying the house itself. For example change the colour/pattern of the floor and walls, change the layout a bit (maybe adding 1 more floor or a basement).- I dislike visually how the acquisition of resources works. Resources are acquired by basically pickung up junk from the ground. generally this is fine, but they respawn. There is always trash lying around and you cannot prevent this. Obviously I want to create a nice and clean environment for my guests and therefor am interested in removing any trash.- There's too much text in my opinion. The writing is charmful and sometimes makes me giggle. But the amount is about 4 times as much as I'd like it to be.- game breaking bug: I cannot place the campsite "building". When I switch to "outdoor campsite" it automatically switches back to indoor as soon as my cursor leaves the window. Building a campsite is required to continue with the story and therefor I'm "stuck".(good example of bad UI: I needed to google "how to build the campsite" to understand how to switch to the outdoor area as it was very hard to find.)I personally prefer "Traveller's Rest" which is in early access right now, but already has a lot of content. Its gameplay loop is much more captivating. This game leans more towards having a chilled play session though, which is also nice.UPDATE: After half a year and several updates no fix for the game breaking bug above. I will not touch the game again.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: OLD REVIEW:It's a very cute game with lovely art and game mechanics. Unfortunately it is also VERY buggy. Within the first couple hours of game play I had ghost guests in my rooms who had already left, but the game still listed as staying in the room. This meant that I couldn't book anyone else for that room despite it being empty. Also, when building a new room the game glitched and I was stuck in build mode even when walking to different areas of the map. I couldn't exit the build mode without quitting and restarting the game.This is a very good game, but I can't recommend it until these sorts of bugs and glitches are addressed as it grinds the game experience to a halt whenever they occur. However, all of the bugs I've encountered have been solved by quitting the game and reloading so I haven't lost my save or any progress due to a bug at the moment.UPDATE:I've sunk more hours into the game and the bugs I listed before have been solved. There are still many minor glitches (items overlay incorrectly, room stats load in as 0 making guests give bad reviews despite the room being decorated), but the game runs significantly better.Another critique I have of the game is that story progression is EXTREMELY slow, characters are entirely 2D with not much interesting to say, and the game feels clunky to play (you get too many resorts too quickly, it takes too long to gather garbage which you need to decorate your resorts, and automating your resorts is extremely difficult to unlock).However, I have had fun playing the game just to decorate the resorts. The art is BEAUTIFUL and the atmosphere is very cute. If you can get past the flaws I mentioned earlier you'll have a fun time.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: A very sweet game with good humour, cute characters, and chill building of hotels in diverse environments. Lots of unlocking new furniture, upgrading, etc. Good for a week or two of play - I got 100% completion in 28 hours/79 in-game days. - Repeating statements about "humans can be good, but often cause destruction. They caused a huge fire years ago that devastated everything" yet gameplay does not reflect the downside at all- Humans wander, litter (which is a currency, so that's a good thing), and give you money. No downsides- Gameplay effectively says "humans encroaching on nature and littering is good for animals"- Game also has some political message about government control causing the greatest destruction of all? That's a whole other thing I didn't expect to see in my cute bear game- One quest line has an out-of-nowhere unsatisfying end, and the game aknowledges how disappointing it is. There is no further resolution- Towards the end, there's a sudden quest that takes itself VERY seriously. Its themes are , , , , and  - a huge mismatch from the rest of the game's light, no-stakes premise. I think this quest was supposed to end the game, but you can finish it before other quests. Finishing that quest has absolutely no impact on the rest of the game in any way- Most of the game has a few types of quest going at the same time, so you have something to work on- BUT sometimes your only quest is "Host x guests are y inn". The only way to finish these is to wait for time to pass. Sometimes several days- You can only sleep at night, so that's a lot of standing around- You know when you're at the end of the game, and the quests are running out. Suddenly, you're hit with a "why did I do this? Why am I running these hotels anymore? I have no room to build anymore, so why do I need any money or resources?"- You finish the last quest, and then... that's it. Game over. No confetti, no applause, not even "The end". The final quest item disappears, and nothing happens.- Cooking is weird. I really wish you could just hit a button and it would filter for what you CAN make, instead of forcing you to click though every single recipe. - Timing is *rough*. You can only sleep at night, so lots of waiting around. Recycling and cooking makes you wait 10-45s for the process to finish, so you just have to sit there. It's not long enough to do anything else, while not being instant... Just makes it awkward. As mentioned above, there's no way to speed up time (outside of sleeping at night) so looots of wating.- Hiring staff to take care of tasks (picking up trash, cooking, heating, registering guests) each take a lot of your income. Even just two of them take a significant portion- Grindy at times. I spent a lot of time doing laps of map areas to get more wood, more wood, more wood, still more wood.... Oh now I need to cook because hiring a chef is too expensive. Gotta search all over the map for ingredients for food to be eaten in a day... - I wish it encouraged larger rooms. There's so much pressure to squeeze value out of space, so every room becomes so crammedI know all that makes it sound like I didn't like that game. I did though! It's sweet, funny, art is pretty, lots of neat furniture items. Hank is delightful! This is just a list of things that made me say "oh... that bit wasn't great..." while the rest is an enjoyable way to turn my brain off.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo for this game a while back, and was really excited to see that some of the feedback I gave was implemented in the final game. That being said, I have complete faith that these devs will address any minor issues with resources or balancing. They are very attentive but also a small group. Some of these issues probably flew right under the radar until a wide release picked them up. Bear with them! :D The game has some of the best characters I've ever seen in a game. And I don't just say that because there's a bear in my name. What I've seen in three hours is fun, humorous, and charming. It's a very strong recommendation.  *Excited bear noises!*
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Really chill game where you get to be creative ! :)The ambience is spot on, the characters are all really cute and funny and overall very well done of the devs for the music and backgrounds, cause everything's really beautiful. The furniture and scenes are adorable and having that liberty of placing everything is really refreshing from games of this type and range. The game has a long play time that can vary depending on how fast you progress, which makes it way worth the price in my opinion. *Early small advice tho, hire Wade as soon as you unlock him, makes decorating 1000* easier with all of the collected valuables, because picking them up by hand is wayyy too slow*Now for the downsides. Unfortunately, past a certain point everything gets a bit repetitive, sometimes plain-on boring. And i'll be honest, the story didn't stick much by me since it's a bit rushed/glossed over, and honestly quite forgettable. Moreover, certain panels, although beautiful, are a real pain to navigate though due to the layering, which isn't that enjoyable if you have to do constant back-and-forth through an area. The ambient sounds are good (forest, wind sounds etc), but again the lack of music gets a bit boring as well, and very fast. Decorating for half an hour with background windstorm sounds isn't that exciting tbh. And although that's nothing listening to your own music won't fix, most of the game is like that. Most of your playthrough will just be accompanied with wind sounds, and nothing else.Overall it's honestly a really good, fun and chill game for a while - although i'd say be careful of the "hype effect" the game gives off. Playing it is alright, but is it better than what you expected? I'd say it depends, although my answer would be closer to "no".If you're just here for a quick chill game without any intent to 100% it then i'd definitely recommend it - it's refreshing, relaxing and fun, however if you're looking for a creative game to play for a while while finishing it bit by bit i'd say it gets boring fast and has no real replay-ability, so be warned of that.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: One of those wish there was a neutral review. Visually the game is stunning and endearing. The characters just seem to come to life. You'll find yourself wanting to know more about the quirky cast past the few limited interactions and wandering about lush landscapes that you wished had a bit more of a story to them. However the pacing of the game is off to the point that it becomes a glaring issue the more you play and it hinders both difficulty and enjoyment. The amount of idle time presented leaves you with ample time to gather more resources than one could ever need and thus makes progression a mute point. There is no real challenge here in any sense and I think that hurts the gameplay loop overall. It is not a game I would recommend at full price, however it is a reasonable enough game to waste time on and take in the sights.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, after finishing the game at 100%, i have a few opinions on this game. The first being that it is monotonous, so if you are into that, this is a game for you. With that being said, i did finish it, so there is that. Second, the game is very glitchy. There were several things either not working, or time i had to restart the game. Thirdly, the last bit of the story was completely unnecessary. And finally, overall it was a very par game. Not great, but not bad either. Im not sure if it is worth a play through, but it does fill time.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Bear and Breakfast is an adorable little management game full of lovable characters. I have thoroughly enjoyed following Hank around on his adventure in...hotel management. Each of Hank's interactions have made me laugh and I always enjoy his dialogue with the cast of characters he meets. I think the dev has done a great job trying to keep the player busy with challenges and circling back to old sections to improve upon them while you wait to reach even more hotel upgrades in new areas. I am someone who enjoys running around and doing a bunch of little tasks, so if you're the same then you'll likely enjoy it too. All in all, would recommend. 10 outta 10 bear activities.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: OK I was really looking forward to this game and ill say straight out that I love this gem of a management sim! The characters are adorable and the dialogue is so witty and fun. The biggest downside is really how unbalanced the beginning is, when you start out you will be doing a lot of waiting around until you unlock other areas because all the beginning quests want you to do is wait until people check out of the first cabin. If you can get through the boring bits of the beginning its really worth your time to play this wholesome game!!
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a bad game, it's just not as good as advertised.There's a lot of the game that lacks polish.  I've seen graphics issues on every map and most days I ended up just wasting time until night came and I could sleep till morning.  Between the unrefined feeling, a few UI issues, and the poor action economy, I cannot recommend this game
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute delight! I love the artistic style and the playfulness of the story line. As with any release, there are bugs to be expected, but more polished than most games that are released today. I like simplicity of the game and I think it's made for a broad age range, however, for anyone looking for a complex simulator will be left to be pleased. Besides that, the game is enjoyable and very wholesome and hope for more content in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: its an okay game.The game is very charming, and cute.  I wish we spent more time on each individual inn rather than adding more and more inns.  I also feel like i spent 90% of the time doing adventuring compared to 'management'.Again its super charming and wellmade, probably worth the price but I just couldn't get into it.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: It's so much fun! It takes some time to get through the storyline before they let you free, that they let you build and roam around but it is worth the wait. The characters are cute, the conversations are fun and the artstyle is amazing!I've played this for some hours and I'm still making progress! A lot of content for a small price. I do wish there was an option to filter crafteble recipes from the ones you can't make. Because it takes a lot of time clicking through all the recipes. I do like the auto-fill option.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: This is my favourite game of ALL time!! Seriously! It has quest/task lists, ADORABLE characters (especially Hank <3) and its very calming. Much like Stardew Valley, this game repairs buildings and has a very beautiful artstyle/story. BUT what Stardew lacks and BAB has is the simplicity of the game play and the personification of animals in the wild. It is so unbelievably cute and I am absolutely in love with this game. <3333 thank you developers/artists <33333
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: There are some quality of life issues that drive me crazy - like not being able to manage the resorts in one place, but having to travel to each region to assign new guests...  but in general a really cozy game that scratches an itch! Music is awesome. Sound effects and art are *chef's kiss*!!! A new fave for life.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, and I would almost recommend it if not for a bug I keep running into that prevents me from closing windows.  Sometimes I can plug in a controller and mash B to close and escape menus, other times it doesn't work and I lose progress.It autosaves, so it's not much progress lost, but it happens constantly.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and relaxing game, except when you can't put items in the middle of the room because the number of tiles is odd. Also night is way too dark even when the brightness is set to max, beside the snowy area. There're streets light to show where to go, but with random stuffs on the ground sometime it takes time to go around. Game have bugs here and there but not something major. There're lots of random things on the ground that make the character suddenly stands still. Sometime i wish there is an undo button to save time. When placing objects, sometime is hard to tell which is the front because the blue layout is cover all over the obj. All that aside I think the game is very well made. Art is beautiful and music is good. Really recommend for anyone like chill game.Also, the customers wear T shirt and short walking in the snow but they dare say my cabins are freezing ??:D??
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game a lot! There's a ton of things to do and lots of fun to have. The only issue that stands out to me is that there is an inconsistent sleep time. It will be night time and when I go to sleep, it says that i can only sleep at night. It feels like it makes you wait a certain amount of time between sleeps instead of having a normal night/sleep cycle. One time it let me use the sleep option while it was daytime. That was the only thing that bothered me about the game. Other than that it's great! :D-update-i think i was a little harsh about my previous review because i was at the beginning of the game and didn't quite know what to do yet. i still think that the time skip should become an option around at least 9-pm.also, i have noticed multiple glitches happening while playing:(1) there was a duplication glitch of paintings on the wall. i had to get out of the game to get the option of grabbing another painting to get off my screen. i wasn't even in my inventory and the option to grab a painting was just there.(2) the bathroom red sign appeared on a person while they were asleep. this was because the person was asleep on the second floor in highlake and the bathroom was on the first floor underneath.(3) a person was asleep on the floor in the highlake hotel. their bedroom was on the second floor and they were asleep on the first floor. there was no bed, just an unconscious body.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very cute and charming but it lost me after around 7 hours.So far gameplay consists of:upgrade room X Decorate establishment YHave X guests at place Z And that's it you Upgrade a room wait for a sign a person to it wait 1-2 days rinse and repeat.I know there is probably way more to it but currently it just bores the heck out of me and that's why the negative review
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I am back and forth on whether I like this game enough to keep playing. On the one hand its adorable, the art is very well done, and the characters are delightful, on the other hand this game is a constant grind (which I hate) you constantly have to go around and find trash and other valuables so you can upgrade things even though people pay you for their nights stay you still need another source of income (garbage) to decorate in order to get people to pay you more. In the end you end up with a ton of coin you don't need and not enough garbage.  This game is cute and has a lot of potential but honestly it frustrates me more then not.  If you don't mind the grind it out style game and the fact you have to walk everywhere instead of running or something a bit faster then give this game a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: The game was fun in the beginning, didn't mind running around gathering wood and completing quests. Hank is a good character and tries to help everyone, it feels like he gets the short end of the stick. Building in the first few early locations wasn't bad until you have to keep redoing rooms to finish quests, also it forces you to build in preset buildings. The game really makes you cram stuff  in rooms, because you need a score for comfort, decoration. There is a score for the whole building too. Towards the end of the game, I gave up making the rooms look nice and started shoving in junk everywhere just to get the rooms scores up. The people don't use anything in the room except for the bed. Also the way the heating is done in the game is  frustrating; it doesn't stay consistent even if you put top-of-the-line boiler they still complain its too cold. There is no thermostat to control it; just on or off. I let them be cold it wasn't worth trying micromanage the heating. I finished the game but didn't feel like completing the few remaining quests I didn't have the energy to rebuild another room. Towards the end, it felt like Hank was reduced to being a food delivery bear. Everyone wanted him to cook something ,which just made the game drag on. The ending was also a letdown and didn't make much sense.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Delightful, funny, and unexpected. I honestly didn't expect much more than a management simulator going into this game but I was very wrong. The story lines are beautifully written, the characters are unique and creative, and the game play is fun and easy to navigate. The art style is whimsical and well done, and the depth of the story was so unexpected it only mad me want to keep playing. I really thought this would be a game I picked up on occasion for mindless game play but overall It's been extremely satisfying and fun to play. I can't recommend it enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: The game is cute. Running a hotel is satisfying when it works. BUT.The controller support is absolutely awful. Sometimes when buttons are displayed as the ones you should press, they are wrong! The tutorials were clearly designed without thinking of controllers first; it took me ages to figure out that I needed to press "y" first before doing left and right trigger to even navigate the tutorial pages, so I never got past the first page of a tutorial and kept accidentally closing them until halfway through the game. What controls do exist are really clunky, which was mostly just slightly annoying at first, but then I spent a whole day attempting to cook unsuccessfully because I would keep accidentally closing out of the whole menu.Also, this game is not very accessible. There's no option to change text or icon scaling, and things are way too hard to see in the UI or minimap at 4K.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: This is a cute management game that will give you a good 45 hours worth of gameplay (more if you're trying to finish all the quests and not just the main storyline). I found it compulsively playable and it actually does wonders for my anxiety to play an adorable, well-intentioned, accidental inkeeper. The mechanics are simple but varied and the art is just so stinkin' cute. Also, the soundtrack is very soothing. I loved the story, it's got a lot of heart and a little bit of everything: some cute wholesome messages about kindness and mental health, environmental preservation, capitalism kinda sucking, the nature of humans and animals, and y'know, a tiny bit of the supernatural. If you like management games, cute art, and wholesome commentary, then you should give this a go.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Bear & Breakfast has all the elements for a great game but due to poor optimization falls flat at simply good. You cannot dump items, you cannot sell items, you can only use trash to purchase items for decorating, you cannot turn the camera to be able to see properly to decorate or even view your creations. The day night cycle was when guests would leave reviews & you'd get a chance at better guests who might leave higher reviews. I accidentally bought a recipe twice & because I had already used the recipe I had to hold onto a useless recipe card the entire rest of the game.These processes bloated my game time with a lot of waiting around & frustration. The game is so cute & it is fun but a huge pain to get trophies in. I wish the story made me care about the world more but it felt weird & forced to me. I do recommend this game to people who are inside the Wholesome/Cozy Game Genre but to those looking to get into the genre there are simply better games to spend your time with.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted so much to love this game, but as it is I just can't recommend paying for it.  I love the art style and the dialogue.  But the "cuteness" factor only goes so far when there's just not that much to do.  I can tell a lot of effort was put into the art, music, and writing of the game.  But there's a lot that needs to be adjusted.  Firstly, it gets dark WAY before night actually starts.  It makes it difficult to see while walking around, especially when there's a ton of debris that constantly stops you from moving forward.  There's a lot of waiting around, at least in the first few hours of the game.  I wish there was more to do while waiting for the guests to stay at your places.  As it is, you just kind of go around picking up the same wood, rocks, and pieces of trash while waiting for night time to hit so you can sleep.  It really feels like a lot more should have been added to the gameplay before launch.  I hope they adjust some of these things and I'll revisit in the future, because it's adorable.  But for now I can't recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game and the humour within the dialogue. It really hits that cozy game spot for me; however, I do feel that there are a few story progression issues where you receive quests that you cannot complete because you haven't even unlocked a certain level or mechanism within the game yet, so you're just kinda running around wondering how you're supposed to complete it. I've had to google multiple times only to realize each time that I just cannot complete the quest just yet. The game gets a little overwhelming late game as the cost to complete the quests become a little too much compared to what you're making. These issues aside, I still spend hours on end playing and enjoy it a lot!
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very adorable and cozy game and Hank is absolutely delightful. If you are casually playing this game and taking some time to decorate and build your inns, I would say this gives you a solid 40-50 hours to finish the main/side quest and achievements. The story gets suddenly really deep at the end, but it was still interesting nonetheless. The main meat of this game is in the early game, when you have to keep gathering materials (save the mahogany wood!!) and tend to the kitchen. After you unlock the autonomous services that manage the food and heat for your inns, the only thing left really is to optimize your inn rooms and decorate, decorate and decorate. So it definitely falls off and there is no late game content, but this game is definitely for you if you love management and decorating games!On the side note there are some ongoing bugs and here are the ones I noticed most:> Sometimes guests will ask for a bathroom of score of 42 when 36 is the highest> Guests will complain about the food score even if Julia is turned on and its high enough to satisfy them - just go into her management options and click save changes even if you didn't change anything
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: It feels like this game is rushed and unfinished, and it's such a shame.At it's core, the fixing buildings, decorating and booking in guests is really satisfying but there is unfortunately a lot of things that make this game frustrating to play. Firstly, the pacing is absolutely awful. The developers have said that they will fix not being able to sleep until midnight which is a positive, but there's so many things that contribute to the terrible pacing of this game. Dialogue is clunky and it feels so random to which lines you can skip as soon as you've read them or lines that are unskippable and stay on screen for way too long. When coming out of a cut scene, you are stuck within the cut scene for way longer than necessary, just stood in the middle of the screen unable to move. Especially early on, there's not enough to do, despite there being a ton of characters who seem unused and wasted. A lot of things in this game feel pointless, such as the diner, which is again something that feels like it's been added to make the area feel more full whilst serving no purpose. I was somehow able to walk into a river and then, as it was an out of bounds area, couldn't get out of the river. Luckily, the game does have a rescue feature but for some reason it takes a full 90 seconds to put you within bounds. Some quality of life things that should be common sense for a game like this just aren't there and it adds further to the feeling of frustration whilst playing. It would be so much easier to manage all resorts through some kind of main hub, instead of having to travel to every area each day. Having a set spawn point that you could go to would make getting stuck so much less infuriating and would also just make sense in this kind of game.Going back to my point about the dialogue feeling clunky, a lot of the lines feel forced and unfunny and ruin the flow. I'd just like to take a second to mention that, at the beginning of the game, you're asked to go off to find an item for your mother. There's then a point about 5 days later where it's suggested that you should go back to your mother who acts completely unsurprised that you've decided to bring humans back to the valley. She initially acts shocked to see you, even if you do go back to the start area before prompted to, where there's no recognition that you've been gone for a long time. It's just strange.In the first few hours of this game I was willing it to get better and desperately trying to enjoy it but honestly it's too frustrating and feels like it should be in early access.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Game is alright, but not great.If you're looking for a Sim similar to stardew valley, this is not it. The game doesn't really even scratch that particular itch even remotely. It's a half a fetch quest game and half a very limited resort builder. You get access to several properties overtime and each resort has a very limited amount of space to build in. Which at first isn't a big deal, but as time goes on your higher grade furniture gets bigger. So you're left to either try to cram furniture and decorations into your pre-made rooms, or rebuild everything from scratch and have less rooms in general. The property never expands or improves, just the furniture you need to use to get higher pay and achieve quest goals. that part of the game is.. unfortunately really unsatisfying. The quest part of the game also is sort of unsatisfying. Several quests just dead end. the two biggest main quests end in such abrupt and lame ways.  These quests all felt so empty and unfinished it makes me believe they were left that way for a future DLC. Which fine, but it just adds to the very unsatisfying soup they're serving. They also have some moon logic, they frequently tell you to ' find someone' and there's no hint or markers as to who 'someone' might be. I also finished the main plot before I finished any side stuff because I was stuck on Julia's greenhouse quest, I didn't realize the plants she wanted could be bought in the trash menu. Cooking also isn't great. You have very limited inventory space, even with the upgrade you get later on. You are expected to have at least 4 items for most early/intermediate items and 6+ something for later ones. Then you make a generous serving of food or drinks that can only stack up to 10. You'll quickly run out of space and fridges can't hold more then I think item stacks at the highest level. For higher level customer satisfaction you need those ingredient heavy dishes. You'll also need items you can't find in the wild. The game never explains that you need to buy these items from the desert merchant. You just have to know I guess. He previously only sells fuel so there's not a lot of reason to keep checking his shop when you don't even need fuel until close to the end of the game, and another npc in the area you need it in sells it too! inventory space is sort of abysmal. Even with the upgrade I found myself constantly running out of space and my bear stash was always full. The bear stash is even smaller then your regular inventory too. You'll quickly end up with excess wood, lower level decorations and food ingredients without recourse. You can't sell these items either. You have to throw them away, one stack at a time. This again was confusing and very poorly explained. You need to drag a stack directly from your inventory, Then just keep dragging stack by stack into it. It's weirdly hidden and monotonous.Trash is not balanced as a currency. You'll run out of it so fast and it's the only way to buy decorations. Also decorations are kinda ludicrously priced until you've reached end game and gotten the npc who collects it automatically. But by then you don't need it. The game is over and there's really no reason to keep playing. unless you just want to muck around in making perfect lvl 5 rooms for some reason.The npc staff is very helpful, but if you get tripped up like I did you just play a frustrating mid mid game without them, and only get them after the game is over.Overall, it's ok, but I wouldn't buy this unless it's on sale, or they fix alot of stuff. It's just kinda.. empty. Not one part of this game is particularly satisfying or enjoyable. The story is cute but also very basic and bare bones. They just leave every interesting thing about this place as surface level as possible. Great idea, really bad execution.PS. There was one good thing, Sabine.

_childDocuments_.review: I really tried to give this game an opportunity but, when I got to Winterberry and saw the TERRIBLE layout of the place, that just defeated my spirit. Just make a straight wall, for heaven’s sake! Developers, give us actual SPACE to work with instead of trying to get cute with pillars! If this game doesn’t even give me the little consolation of not firing my OCD, then I shall not overlook all its other flaws anymore.Most of the gameplay, specially early on, it’s just a waiting game. Put two pieces of furniture and wait two days. At the half hour of playing, I was already standing with nothing to do but wait. Other than going around picking stuff just because, there’s nothing else to do a lot of the time, and even that can play against you because they put limited inventory space in the game. Most of the “story” missions consist of “Go do X and come back” which it’s exclusively used to pad out gametime. And example: In Winterberry, you meet this guy who knows how you can heat up your new location, he will teach you but first you have to help him, sounds fair. Now, repair the resort, go back to him, he tells you to find sauna rocks, you go elsewhere and find then just laying around, go back to him, he teaches you about boiler rooms, go to the resort, put a boiler room in it, go back to him, he tells you to fuel the thing, go back to the resort, fuel the boiler, go back to him… see where I’m going with this?At some point I sincerely came back to the store page to see if this was an Early Access game, when I was still defending the game in my head. The world feels completely empty, every NPC repeats the same two lines of dialogue again and again and in some cases doesn’t even move from its place. The two characters that are supposedly “best buddies” with the main character disappear completely after you open your first location and don’t reappear in the story at least at the point I left it, the same happens with the main character’s mom and the beaver gent who helps you repair the rundown building. The ominous thing that happens at the very start of the game didn’t came up again in the ten HOURS I’ve played so far. Unlike the animated trailer seemed to imply, there is no interaction AT ALL with your guest, the most that happen is they having a thought bubble with an emoji on it when they see you. Everything in the game is controlled by literally switches, in sign form, that supersede any character interaction, just asking “Want to repair this location? Yes or no” and the bear doesn’t even answer in-character most of the time, just with the same generic “yes” or “no”. It really feels like an unfinished game.There are a lot of things still to discuss, like the excessive quantity of roadblocks that confine the player’s freedom; the fact that progression is poorly paced by delegating mechanics to specific buildings that coerce the player’s creativity; some weird duplication bug that I seemed to stumble upon at random but never was able to replicate… but all that it’s too much already.I really expected to love, and I mean LOVE, this game. The concept has a great amount of charm and the genre is one of my favorites (just look at my profile), but this is just not good at all and that really saddens me. Like seriously saddens me. I can’t understand how Bear and Breakfast has the score it has on Steam.

_childDocuments_.review: The quick version: The story has me intrigued and the environments are vibrant and detailed. If you like building, decorating, and managing BnBs, then you'll have a pretty good time, but be aware of the tedium, maybe one or two annoying bugs, and the fact that we're currently waiting for the story to be finished.The longer version:I enjoyed my time with this game, it's very relaxing and pleasant with a nice sense of exploration and management, and I enjoyed customizing and decorating every room and location. However, there are a few grievances I hold that I would want to see resolved. I wish the UI for managing the resorts was a little more intuitive, like I want to be able to see more easily whether or not the room a guest is staying at fulfills all their requirements, instead of having to click multiple buttons and go in and out of several menu screens just to check on each individual guest. It's not too major of a thing, probably more like a nitpick, but it did bother me a few times. One particularly annoying thing is that there's currently a bug where some guests will want to see a certain amount of points in a stat for a room, but that amount is physically unreachable by the player (note: this only affects the endgame, with the last resort currently in the game). Also, there are a lot of points where the game felt like it dragged due to the sheer tedium and repetitiveness of the day to day gameplay. Some quests will have what feel like needlessly lengthy requirements, and when I say lengthy I don't mean a large involved quest spanning hours of adventure, I mean the kind of lengthy where you have to wait 5 in game days for enough guests to go through your establishment to fulfill what would otherwise be an extremely simple quest. This normally isn't a problem since the game has enough stuff for you to do that the time will pass normally while you're off accomplishing other things, but it's especially noticable in the end game, which brings me to my next point. This may be a particular sticking point for some, but the story has yet to be finished. At a certain point in the game, you get all these clues of something stranger going on and hints of a larger journey ahead of you, and then the game runs out of content. To be fair, the developers have already released a roadmap stating that this would be resolved with a large update coming later this year, but I figure it's worth mentioning for those looking to sink their teeth into this game. Even with all that, I do recommend Bear and Breakfast as it's a very chill game with a fun and quirky premise, and I did thoroughly enjoy my time with it. Something you'll probably be able to notice from all the screenshots and trailers is that the world and its visuals are wonderfully drawn and packed full of detail to really make it feel like a vibrant environment. The characters all have their fun little quirks to them, and I did get a genuine sense of intrigue from listening to the characters talk about the world, the events that took place, and where things might go next. I'll be looking forward to returning to this whenever it is that the content update releases so that I can keep managing more resorts and see the story to its end.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm neutral.I don't regret buying the game, but the cute graphics only carry it so far. You spend so much time standing around, waiting for time to pass, that I got incredibly bored pretty quickly. You can sleep at night, but "night" is a relative term. It gets dark, and you have to keep waiting. And waiting. And waiting. Before it's what the game considers "night," even though it's been dark for a while.It really needs a mechanism to speed time up, especially when you cannot progress the story forward without waiting for guests to enjoy their visit and leave.I'm lucky enough to have two monitors, so I spent half of my 5.7 hours (at time of review) watching Netflix while the game idled through nothingness in the background until I could sleep the night through.Could definitely be improved, but the basic mechanics are there for a good game.

_childDocuments_.review: Bear and Breakfast is an aesthetically charming but somehow deeply cynical and unpleasant game. If you hoped to actually run a sweet bed and breakfast you can customize to your liking, I regret to inform you that you're instead building a slate of sad AirBnBs to exacting specifications delivered through a speaker embedded inside an inflatable shark mascot (yes, really). I suppose you could ignore those instructions and do whatever you want instead, but seeing how unlocks and story progression are tied to obeying Fin's directions, you'd certainly have to work your way up to it.I don't know. I wanted to like this game and tried to be generous with it, but it didn't reward me much for doing so. The controls are poorly communicated and the interface is cluttered. The environments are beautiful, but to what end? You wander around mashing the button to pick up resources so you can build the next tier of furniture to accept the next tier of guests, constantly smashing into walls because the Venn diagram of "shrubbery I can walk through" and "shrubbery I cannot walk through" is a circle. Characters exist. Sometimes they talk. Five hours in, they don't have much to say. There's a story, presumably, but getting to it involves constructing yet another AirBnB, and I can't think of anything I want to do less.[Edit 6/14/2023: I decided to see this game through to its end with a couple friends. I think ultimately the game's fundamental failure is that the management sim feels like an afterthought, despite how many hours you're obligated to spend on it and despite a bear running a bed and breakfast being the entire conceit of the game.Normally, the challenge and motivation in management sims comes from strategizing about your upgrade path. You want to make money so you can unlock the cool new thing that lets you make more money. Progression is baked into the act of playing the sim.Bear and Breakfast gets it backwards. An NPC will go, "Here's your cool new thing. Go install it." And then when you install it and come back, they'll go, "Great! Now host five more guests." And then you host five more guests and come back and they go, "Great! Here's an upgraded version of the thing. Go install two of them." This quickly warps managing your locations from an activity that is rewarding in itself to an obstacle you have to overcome to progress. By the time the game starts to open up, you've unlocked everything there is to unlock and are dying to be done.I've seen other negative reviews suggest that the dull, repetitive gameplay could be forgiven if the visual novel components were stronger or better paced. I disagree. I think overvaluing the (admittedly weak) narrative is what made the game like this in the first place. Why else would it end by shunting the management sim off to the side so four brand new characters can loredump at you for the final hour? It's easy to look at how all the plot suddenly happens in the back third and think the narrative could have used another revision pass. It's more useful to look at how basically everything up to Pinefall is an extended tutorial and realize that the game's pacing problems are much, much more ingrained than that.This is a game that doesn't really understand what it's trying to be, and it shows. Spend your time and money elsewhere.]

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty much perfect for a busy college student. The art is easy on the eyes, the story line is low pressure, and the entire game follows a pretty basic formula for completing various tasks. PROS: Fantastic art style and character design, charming dialogue, and very easy to play once you get the hang of things. The NPCs all feel like their own people (my favorites being Ipswitch and Jax) that have their own lives. Lots of things to collect for any item hoarders like myself. I have yet to finish the story as I am taking my time with the game, but I do enjoy the snippets I have seen so far. As someone in an intense major with mental illness, it is a soothing game to unwind with and genuinely enjoy after a hard day.CONS: This game is not for you if you do not enjoy management games as the game does not stray far from its genre. The NPCs are fun, but you do not get to interact with them much at all beyond their quests. I will say the game can feel tedious at times due to having to wait for guests to stay a certain amount of nights, waiting to unlock new areas, etc. As an item hoarder I do wish there was more storage, but I have not completed the story yet so I cannot say if this is remedied later in the game. I have noticed when I am transferring items from the shark's bin to my inventory (by pressing the Take All button), things will sometimes get deleted in the process when I do not have inventory space. It is not a huge deal, but mildly frustrating for sure.Overall I would rate this at 4.5/5 stars!
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I binged this game so hard over the holidays and unlocked all the achievements, so safe to say I enjoyed the game! Super cozy and chill, easy to play, great art, lots of fun!! Overall loved the game, though now that I have completed the quests I don’t see myself continuing to play much, but will keep an eye out for any future expansions if any!Pros:- The game is really easy to follow and continue to progress- Loved the art, story, and characters- Experienced very few bugs. Had one bug where a door got stuck after removing a room, but was able to fix it. Sometimes I noticed when I picked up an item and it would give me like 5 of that item even though I only picked up 1 (which I gladly kept lol)- Loved the cute outfits you can get - wish there were more!- Decorating and placing rooms was so much fun and easy to do. Trying to balance maximizing the space, planning for future rooms, and making something that looked cute was a good challenge!- Managing the rooms and guests was fun too, especially when you unlock the ability to do that remotely- Having the option for some characters to help remove some daily tasks when you wanted was incredibly nice!Cons:- It's hard to move rooms after placing them so plan ahead!- It's hard to know who has open quests without periodically checking every location and character which was a little time consuming. And traveling to certain locations that didn't have a bus stop was a pain sometimes- At some point you need so much hardwood to upgrade levels, but they're harder to get than the other woods so you will need to grind at times for that. Also you will need silk sheets a lot too, but the only way to get that item is from the shop and it can cost a lot (overall wasn't a big deal once you realize you need these things; you'll just need to forage for wood more and save which is no biggie)- Some trash gets into places the bear can’t get to, so you either need to move items if you can or enable Wade to get it for youSuggestions:- I wish you could add the special rooms to other locations as well and add floors to continue to expand every location. Once I upgraded a location enough for the guests, there wasn't any reason to continue playing in that area and I really wanted to continue to expand!- Once I had Julia help with the cooking I never really touched that part of the game except for a few quests. Would love to see a potential expansion around food farming and more cooking! Maybe even fishing off the ocean or something too.

I found that I've had to slow myself down when playing and that when it does pick up I'm behind on my inventory. Overall it is a nice cozy game, I would give it five stars.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely adorable management game with the underlying "capitalism bad" theme that you gotta love. The story was vague at times but in ways that fit the narrative, a bear can only learn so much about humans after all. _childDocuments_.review: Forced myself to finish the main storyline before reviewing, to see if at any point it gets better. Spoiler alert: it doesn't.I wanted so, SO badly to like this game. I like management games. I like cozy games. I like story-focused games. I even like repeated fetch quest games. Bear and Breakfast is all of these things rolled into one, and somehow fails at all of it.The pacing feels off from the beginning, as you're dragged through what feels like a 7 hour tutorial of how to build and manage your resort(s). However, by the time you've finally been introduced to all of the (extremely tedious) management mechanics, you only have one resort left to open and you're 85% done with the story.Every aspect of managing your resorts feels like a chore, and the devs seem to know this, as they allow you to eventually automate every task. You're either slogging around or doing nothing, never in between. Many quests require you to do absolutely nothing but wait, as you can do nothing to speed up guest generation to satisfy their demands. As other reviewers have mentioned, on multiple occasions I found myself leaving the game open and leaving the room to pass the time so I could advance the story.The visitors to your resorts look fun but lack personality, variety, and interest. I wish you could interact with them in literally any way.Even running around, which this game demands you do constantly, is painful. Some scenery objects are solid. Some scenery objects can be walked through. There is little to no indication as to which is which, and the ground is COVERED with them. After 25 hours of gameplay, I was still constantly running into all of the tiny little things in the way. For a game with so much ground to cover, and so many items to pick up, this was incredibly frustrating.All of this could have been overlooked if the story was engrossing. Too bad.A host of fun, well-designed characters is put to waste in a vague, underdeveloped storyline with far too much dialogue. Most characters appear once, are ignored for 20 hours, and then are suddenly needed again for a final fetch quest. Your sidekicks from the promos and the first quest disappear and aren't useful again until the very end of the game. The ones you're able to recruit for your resorts do not appear at the resorts, they simply remain where you found them. Interacting with characters who don't have a quest for you results in the same boring dialogue line they've always said and always will say.Most underwhelming of all, after you've spent hours deciphering a handful of suddenly vague quest hints after being hand-held with arrows through the entirety of the game up until that point, the story ends completely abruptly and with no indication you've even finished the game. There is no incentive to revisit or replay, especially with the grind of the first few (up to 8 or so) hours looming over you. The only choices you are given are how big to make your bedrooms. There are no end-game goals past the ones requiring you to wait for guest generation. Nothing to keep you coming back.When I first started playing this game, I thought along the lines of some other reviewers - "this might be really fun after a few updates." However, after finishing it, I am convinced that a major reworking of large portions of the game would be required for this to be a game worth coming back to. As it stands, I do not recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm honestly already obsessed with the game! My only complaint is that I usually have quests completed before they are assigned, but that has more to do with how I play games and less to do with the game itself. If you are a completionist who has game ptsd from games that punish you for missing things, rest assured that this game is not one of those. It walks you through everything, nothing will disappear if you miss it, and because of the style of the game you won't be punished ever. Initially I was scared to talk to humans because I was worried they would try to kill me or something, but that's not the case at all. I loved the mobile game Cats and Soup because of the laid back playstyle, but hated the ads and I don't really like clickers because I enjoy stories. This game is like if Cats and Soup and Don't Starve and Stardew Valley had a baby without the high stakes of Don't Starve. It's perfect for me and I love playing it!

_childDocuments_.review: This game was kind of a disappointment! I'd looked forward to it, and it looked adorable, but the game is so railroaded down to the dialogue that I didn't feel like I was doing anything. I didn't stick around long enough to find out.I also have a complaint about the story; the first section of the game ends up not mattering at all, since 'Hank' gets sidetracked by this hotel quest for an indeterminate amount of time, which was frustrating as a player who had gotten invested in that story. _childDocuments_.review: For a simulation game, this one is a little different from others that I've played. While it has the core game mechanics of management here that one might expect, there is also a story to play through which spices things up a bit. I won't spoil any of it for you, but I will say that the story present here does get sort of... strange towards the end. The 'end' of the game felt a bit odd to me, and it is a game that even after you finish the story you can continue to play if you have other achievements to finish. But, there was never a credits roll or anything like that. I got the final story achievement and then that was... it. Nothing else happened to indicate the story had even ended. I actually had to look it up, like, "is that it?" The game is good overall, but is not without it's issues. The inventory was sort of a strain on my patience the further I got in the game. It wasn't until a friend of mine that was also playing finally figured out where the "Delete" option for items was that I could clear things out that I clearly didn't need and didn't want to clog my already overflowing storage spaces (since selling items isn't an option, even old furniture you replace can't be sold). The pacing also starts to get a bit janky towards the end, and could use improvement; for much of the starting bits, money doesn't seem to matter all that much. Then, very suddenly, it matters a lot, too much, and trying to get it then sort of becomes an interesting balance to find the best ways to generate wealth to further the story, while also paying the rather expensive fees that come with keeping customers happy in the buildings you restore in the last few areas in the game (particularly maintaining food and temperature). A positive I can say about it is that there are no alert systems or really anything to be stressed about during the course of this game. It's pretty laid back, and let's you progress at your own pace. So, if you're looking for a slightly different take on a management simulator, with some cute characters and genuinely funny dialogue, then this one might be the game for you. Just be prepared to accept a few flaws.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing this on and off for a bit.  It seems like it's been rushed to just be released and the developers have left us with 0 updates. One of my main complaints is how much it time it takes to walk around the map and collect everything, there is no system to grow the food you want or obtain thinks like eggs/sugar/beard on your own or threw crafting ( which can get expensive ) the last tier of bedroom stuff requires Silk, which you HAVE to buy for 350g a piece, so upgrading all your endgame rooms with take quite awhile. Ontop of that, hiring the " help " is INCREDIBLY expensive. Some of this wouldn't be an issue if you could sell excess items for the excess cash, but you just have to delete them. Instead you're constantly upgrading rooms to meet new demands and having to trash everything you've spent hours collecting to craft those items, just tossed away. This could have been a really great game, but some minor simulation details that have been left out and unbalanced just leaves me to not recommend this.
