_childDocuments_.review: This game is deeply, deeply charming.  The art and the adorable characters are the biggest reason for this, but getting to fix up BnBs and decorate them is pretty fun.  I genuinely love that money and trash are both currencies, and used for different things.  There are some elements that make this feel like an early release, such as the repetitiveness of the many fetch quests, the difficulty with certain mechanics (trying to view a room's value and ending up clicking on the furniture, for instance).  Personally I'd really like it to be easier to view room stats compared with current guest desires- maybe a dedicated page (unless I missed that, I spent a lot of time clicking around comparing guests to room stats).  I think some of these things could affect replayability, but they absolutely did not lesson my enjoyment of the game.I was more intrigued by the themes of the game, and how it explored character arcs as intertwined with environmental concerns.  Makes sense for a game about animals, but I don't think I've seen a game essentially discuss environmentalism and mental wellbeing as interdependent concepts before.  It's a fun management sim, and a surprisingly deep exploration of the impact of environmental exploitation on the individual psyche.  Definitely recommend, and I'll be checking back to see if there's updates I want to play.

_childDocuments_.review: While most people expect a hotel maintenance style game to be solely focused on that element. Bear & Breakfast adds a whole new level with an immersive story mode and main quest-line attached so you truly feel apart of the world. There are days and nights that do go by. Yet, you are not pressured to finish anything by a certain time frame and are allowed to explore freely (helps for keeping up on materials). If you mid-max and try to rush quests you won't have nearly as fun if you explore in-between and collect needed supplies to balance everything out. The developers did a wonderful job and I can't wait to see what they create in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had this game on my wish list for a long time waiting for it to be released and as soon as it was I bought it! At the beginning, it was a lot of fun and I've really enjoyed it. The characters are funny and interesting and I really enjoyed the room designing parts. The downsides - the game does drag sometimes. Maybe it gets better as you get deeper into the game but in the first 5ish hours there's a lot of waiting. The daytime is VERY long and you can only sleep at night but nighttime isn't even when it's dark enough it's hard to see it's much later. If they don't add in a patch to fix the timing of everything adding in a store (or putting it in sooner if it's already there) where you can sell the materials you find for gold would be great. The materials you scavenge show how much gold it's worth at the bottom. Having the ability to sell these to earn gold would be a great way to help solve the dragging - you can spend the days looking for things to sell instead of just waiting around for guests to leave to earn enough money to progress in the day, It's easy enough to find materials for building that you just stockpile them and have nothing to do with all the effort. All and all it's still a fun game and it has some great components. I'd still barely recommend it to people but add in a caveat to just keep it up to waste in-game daytime and do something else to kill time. If there was a patch or a new mechanic to make the days more interesting and feel less of a wait then it would be a 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: + The art style is very cute and the environments are pleasing to the eye.- Each day felt so long and once you have done everything you can only wait for night to come in order to skip time. There is no fast forward button to pass time in the day or make the days run at 2x speed. Some guests stay for a longer duration and you are just waiting for them to leave so you can either edit the space or house a new person. - Building ends up being tedious and grindy for the sake of progression rather than enjoyment. You try to build as many rooms in order to house more people at a time. Most of the quests require you to upgrade a room to a certain level. You just end up cramming as many furniture items in a room just to boost the room rating to complete the quest or to house pickier guests.- You can't demolish old furniture for parts. You can only store it away which takes up inventory space or throw it away which is such a waste. As a result you have to waste more time scavenging for items to build better items that cost more material.- Building menu is a bit difficult to navigate and it could be revised more to make it more efficient and easier to grasp. Editing a tiny portion of a cluttered room is annoying cause you have to move furniture in order to be able to edit the room shape. Toggling between building and removing takes more effort cause you have click the menu instead of holding down a button. You can't move already existing rooms so you have to manually inch the room along or delete the whole area and start over again.

_childDocuments_.review: My thoughts on this game are very similar to everyone else's lists of cons you've probably read already in the reviews, and like others have said, it truly is so upsetting to not want to recommend this game. As much as I love the premise of this game and really enjoy the art (which is something that has carried my enjoyment of games before), the gameplay loop and mechanics really just bog it down so much even this long after its full release + many patches. I enjoyed the first part of the game, and that made me very hopeful for the rest of it, but after only about 10 hours (and probably more like 8 hours because I came back after a year or so of initially playing and made a new save), I feel like I just can't bring myself to open the game again. It has become a series of incredibly simple fetch quests, and waiting around for materials to spawn and for the days to pass. There is only function to sleep through some of the night, and otherwise you just have to wait the day out for the next morning to progress or to get the money you need to upgrade your locations. In terms of decoration and management of the inns, you are kind of trapped into using very specific items and layouts to meet requirements, and with how many different locations you unlock in such a short time the game kind of flip flops between being too overwhelming/confusing or so incredibly boring. The limited inventory space and clunky buying and selling/trashing options also tend to outweigh any potential for designing the inns to be enjoyable after the first couple locations. Obviously there are people who did love this game though, and maybe you will too. I never really got invested in the story and dialogue, and that seems to be something that elevated other peoples experiences and motivated them to finish the game. I think there is some really good concepts here and clearly a lot of love put into it, and so I hope see this teams future endeavours either in updating this game or in their future projects!
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Over all, this is a super cute game that has some good core mechanics. But, it isn't fleshed out enough and is left feeling clunky, especially as you gain more and more properties.Best way I can describe it is if you were forever stuck in the early game of Stardew Valley or something, where nothing is upgraded and it takes forever to do most things. For example, in Stardew: Spring 1 I can barely make it to the mines because there are a lot of things to do and I have to water each plant one at a time. But by Spring 2, I've upgraded stuff so I can explore other places. That's pretty standard for most games, but Bear and Breakfast one kinda misses that. You think you get QoL when you unlock the friends to help you, but they are pretty cost prohibitive and so you just end up abandoning the expensive properties that require a lot of your time (looking at you Ski Cabins and the Captain's Mansion) so that you can advance the game. I did play to the end game though, because if you do just abandon the ones that require cooking/heating upkeep, the game becomes more manageable. And I enjoyed it! Just the completionist/perfectionist in me would love it if I could have all properties going at once.Oh, and playing with a controller is a nightmare. Just don't do it, trust me lol.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: This was my first lodging industry sim. It was an OK experience. The mechanics of setting up rooms/properties and meeting guests needs are a bit too simplistic. Even on the most advanced level, it's effortless to achieve the highest goals and 5-star ratings. That said, if you worry less about winning and more about decorating and creating spaces with actual character and ambiance (instead of just what scores well), there's some depth there that can keep you entertained until you reach the end of the story. The story is a bit wild, which was fun. I don't see any reply value unless there's a significant release of new content / updates. Reminiscent a bit of  but less sophisticated and with more awkward controls.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing this game nonstop for the past couple of days and I am hooked on it! The graphics are so cute and the game is surprisingly really funny. Each character has their own personality and I can't wait to meet more of them. _childDocuments_.review: I've really been enjoying my play through of this game so far!Sometimes i get stuck but I am also an idiot who doesn't know how to read or whatever. Every "mild complaint" (ie: speed, not being able to tell time, Hank not wearing pants) has been solved by further progressing in the story. I don't think I've even brushed the surface of this game yet and I'm still having a lot of fun.The art is absolutely charming. You can tell the devs/artists had a ton of fun with these character sprites. I giggle every time Hank blushes. I would DIE FOR THIS BEAR. I REALLY REALLY wish it had native controller support/cloud saves but its like day one, so who know's what's in store for this bear and co.20 dollars WELL spent. I don't regret this purchase at all. I wish there were more games out there like this because I didn't realize how much of a time waster/enjoyer these kinds of games were.I also played around two hours on the Steam Deck and it worked pretty dang good for not being supported. Sometimes the controller stick would stop working, specifically when load screens happened, but pausing and unpausing fixed it. This does not relate to this review at all and it is NOT a negative since this game isn't even verified to run on the steam deck, just throwing this out there if people ran into the same issues I did :) Some notes for this game:I would not say this is a "hehe life sim" or even compare this to animal crossing, stardew valley and the sorts. This game is a resource gathering, hotel management sim where you're a cute bear. It is HEAVILY directed by the story-- you do not just get let loose and told GLHF; the game IS the story. There is no time fast forward (as of yet? I'm on the third management place and I don't have food unlocked yet.) Sometimes I would find myself leaving it open just to be able to sleep because I've gathered everything and done all I wanted to do for the allotted day.There's really not a point to go back and talk to people unless they have a quest. They have around 3 lines of dialogue each character it seems. It will get repetitive. You don't build friendship, so this really doesn't matter bc like.... there's no reason to talk to em LOL. Not a negative, just don't expect to be building interpersonal relationships with between Hank and Co.I've found myself running out of valuables a lot more than I thought I would; but that could just be my spending habits.... I like pretty things.All in all, I would highly recommend this game if you know you like these sorts of things. I think advertising it as a life sim has done more harm than good for the reviews at the time of writing this, because people just are expecting something completely different. 10/10 would Bear Again tho.

_childDocuments_.review: BnB has a great start but it start dropping fast somewhat due to how the game scores the player. Motels have two core factors and outlier factors that come into play as you progress and unlock more motels. The outlier factors are fine, micromanage x until you can pay someone to do it for you. The problem is the core factors of comfort and decor. These are purely mathematical therefor you cram everything you can into the designated guest rooms to meet their requirements. It's fine if they can't get into the room they'll still enjoy the wall of lamps blocking their entry and leave a 5 star review. The money you get matters very little, I'm told the game requires a large amount at the end but other than that you can unlock everything just off of the first two motels. That being said you'd think these are simple flaws but aside from the gameplay that was mentioned the side quests are few and far between offering very little substance aside from the motel business. Those amazing and funny characters we saw at the start? They're gone after the intro, All this being said it is not a bad game per say it is however very shallow hence why people call it a cozy game. It is charming and very funny at times but at this price it's really not fair to not have more content in such a simple framework.Update: Now with the price increase especially I highly suggest everyone to avoid this title for it has no where near enough content for the asking price. DO NOT BUY

_childDocuments_.review: Would I recommend this game- Yes, but read reviews first. I know I'm not the first one to say most of these things (probably all tbh).The hotel remodeling and decorating feels a lot like Theme/2.0 Hospital (which for me is good because I love those games). The management is tedious until you unlock I think the heating system is broken. No matter what temperature it was my guests all said they were freezing. It was 40c and they said they were freezing. Luckily fuel is fairly plentiful and spawns in the same spots so you can easily go round it up if you need more. I could never afford to pay the dog to do it.The very first achievement is bugged. I was able to get it by starting a new game but I've seen some people saying that didn't work for them.And really, my biggest complaint: There is no way to speed up time, except sleep, which you cannot do until midnight. My playtime for this game is ~39 hours. At least 2-3 of those "playtime" minutes was me doing anything else (crocheting, cooking dinner, watching X-Files, browsing Reddit) while the game ran until I could sleep to advance to the next morning so I could book new guests because the only goal I had was to obtain x number of 5* reviews or needed guests with specific traits to complete their stay. The only reason I fully completed the last resort was because I was determined not to let this stupid bear win.

_childDocuments_.review: Bear and Breakfast has a lot of character, it's endearing and funny. The characters are interesting and the art is very cute. _childDocuments_.review: This game checks a lot of my usual boxes, but after unlocking the fourth location, everything feels very repetitive. _childDocuments_.review: I was so excited for this game before it came out, and I'm so sad with what I've received. The game looks and sounds great; I love the designs and the aesthetic. The characters are charming and 'quirky', and although the dialogue is trying too hard at times I can forgive it. It has a lot of heart and good intentions.However.The pacing is atrocious. It feels so bad that it's hard for me to come up with a solid fix, or even multiple fixes. The days are way too long. The map is too big. I liked how accessible resources were at the beginning, but then it felt like there was nothing to do. You can't fast forward; you can 'sleep through the night', but that option only becomes available at midnight - halfway through the night. It doesn't take nearly enough time in the day to juggle all your resorts, and that's not even when using the bus stop. This is my biggest issue, because the game drags and leaves you bored, purposeless, and with no drive to keep playing. It may seem like my complaints don't go hand-in-hand with each other (the day is too long but also it takes too long to get anywhere?), which is why I said I don't have any solutions at the top.Some other issues; the tutorials are long-winded and often poorly explained. It's not often clear what to do, because the game both holds your hand too much and drops you completely at times. I started a bunch of different quests in the hopes that they would fill time, but I finished them instantly and with hardly any work involved. I've noticed that other reviews mention cooking, which I haven't reached yet (and sadly won't, as I don't want to put more time in), and it feels weird that I can have multiple resorts open and yet not have unlocked all factors of gameplay. The inventory is too small. The process of building rooms is annoying, because you can't switch between crafting and building; if you start making a bedroom but haven't built the furniture yet, you have to completely destroy the bedroom in order to craft the furniture for it. I don't like the way wall hangings float on nothing; maybe walls can be visible when within the building, and not from the outside? The initial resorts feel too small for the guest expectations, and I don't want my rooms looking clunky because they're filled with decorations. The story is weak, and makes little sense. The beaver 'sonny' thing is weird. Full stop. Will is annoying. Full stop. Hank is GREAT.Another HUGE thing: what you can and can't walk through is horribly unclear. Especially in the swamp map, and the forest around your house. Oh my god. It took me so long at the start of the game to just navigate through. Some bushes can be pushed past, some can't. This is the biggest, if the only, design flaw. I'm really sad this game is as clunky as it is, but I'm more sad that I paid 25$ for it. It needs a lot more fine tuning to be enjoyable - right now it's just playable. I appreciate that I have very little time put in so far, but I can't do more than four hours of drudgery, and I think four hours is a generous amount of time to give a game to 'kick in'.

_childDocuments_.review: My feelings about the game are mainly neutral, leaning negative.  I went into this game expecting more of an emphasis on customization, crafting, and management elements.  While I liked some elements, my main issues with the game are the linear progression, limited customizability, and player character.Linear Progression:Another review said that they felt there is only one "right way" to complete the game, and that echoes my feelings exactly.  For example, the quests may require a certain number of bedrooms at a certain level.  The quests are required to complete before additional furniture or locations unlock, essentially holding your hand through how the resort must operate.  Additionally, each resort is limited in the special room types offered.  I might be able to tolerate this if each resort were themed or had a coherent style, but this is not the case, mainly because of the limited customizability.Limited Customizability:You are able to change the size and shape of rooms, alter the placement of furniture, and add additional decorations throughout the resort locations.  That all sounds great, but is essentially the limit of the game.  Each level of room only has one style of furniture with very few (if any) matching decor accessories.  The baroque-leaning higher level rooms do not look good with the bulk of the decor offerings, which have a strong rustic wood cabin feel.  Because of the forced progression, you must pack as much floorspace as possible with decorations, which would be an interesting management task to balance if there were more matching pieces for each style of room.  I would love to make the A24 resort look like a retro motel, but nope, it looks like a wood cabin with baroque bedrooms.  I would love to make Highlake a Shining-esque midcentury nightmare but nope, it is also a wood cabin with baroque bedrooms.Player Character:This is a personal gripe more than an actual criticism of the game, but I felt that playing as "Hank" was unnecessary.  I would love to make my own character, name them, and dress them up.  Hank has no personality and no back-story.  There are some very light outfit collecting and dress-up elements, and I feel it is a shame that they are so minor, because the bear is very very cute and should be focused on more.  Since I not only have to watch Hank move around, but can also see him during dialogue, I think this is such a missed opportunity to add some more customizability.Overall, I will complete the game, but the customization elements need a major upgrade before I could confidently recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Like many others, I have been waiting for 's release since their first announcement back in 2020. The demo released in 2021 during the Steam Next Fest and was immensely fun, captivating, and gave many, including myself, a much needed game to vibe with for a little while. Now we're here! The release has finally come and gone and  remains open to the public! Amazing! Let's dive into the review!~ As of writing this, I have 30 hours in the game and have finished my first playthrough with all achievements completed. It was a long journey but a chill and fun one, and definitely one I might dive back into in the future.   There are  things that make this game phenomenal, so I'm going to list a few things out here: 1. For me, personally,  is a fantastic game in which I can "turn my brain off" and truly vibe for several hours at a time. Chill vibes and even chiller gameplay, especially if you make it to the Winterberry cabin! 2. The character designs and how much personality went into each one is incredible. Usually, you have some side characters that do not get  story given to them other than simply being a resident of a certain area, or being a shopkeeper. With B&B, every character has a story, and every character gets a cute backstory cutscene! True dedication to ensuring all loose ends are tied as neatly as Hank's bear hands could get them. My favorite character designs:  ---> I will also note, as a side thing that I personally enjoy, the artwork that makes each character have super cute facial expressions is incredible! The ability to animate and give a true personality to a shark-shaped speaker is incredible; kudos to the team at GummyCat for this! :) 3. The response time of the developers and the amazing community in the Discord server is phenomenal. I have never seen such a quick and ready response team for a game's launch; issues were being immediately addressed, and they were also quick to fix several issues on the first patch and had acknowledged them since the launch day. Super awesome to see the devs be super active within the community and providing help for those struggling with some things in-game. 4. Questlines are straightforward and are well-written. The writing as a whole is super fun, quirky, and full of personality. It gives the game a very good homey feeling. 5. It is an incredibly good management game because it forces the player to learn how to truly balance everything to properly succeed in their resorts. It took me a few tries in changing my style of gameplay in order to be able to push forward with some of the later resorts, and I view that as a good thing! The changing difficulty levels also allow for players to reconfigure as they need, which is vital in a game like this. Overall, B&B is a super fantastic game. It did, however, have some downfalls that I am going to go into below. - There is no way to recycle or sell old furniture. Late game, this becomes difficult, as you're left just throwing everything away. The devs have mentioned that they're looking into adding a recycling system, but as of writing this review, it doesn't exist yet, so for me, it's a negative point. - Some guest preferences feel a little unobtainable; for me, specifically, I struggled a lot getting 5 star reviews on the guests with a 90 decoration score or an above 50 comfort score, even the 47 hygiene score was difficult for me. I don't view this as a slight against the game, per se, simply as something I struggled with and feel is important to mention. - This was semi-addressed in the patch notes, so I won't harp on it too much, but hiring staff felt super exclusive and very unobtainable for a long stretch of gameplay. They reduced the cost of many of the staff members, which helped immensely, but it still feels a little hard to do, so I had to be super selective in who I hired and where I put them.- Another personal struggle: Refrigerators are not a universal storage option and there's not enough space in them for the entire ingredient list. I kept all of my food ingredients inside the Pawn Voyage storage container (don't tell the guests) because that's where I could keep everything together without running out of space. I know the fridges are likely for storing cooked meals for when the dining rooms are full, so I don't really hold this against the game, either.  Tl;dr: Bear & Breakfast is an incredibly fun woodland management simulator packed with charming writing, cute art, and chill gameplay to keep your brain vibing for many hours at a time. For a first-time debut, GummyCat Studios has truly made a wonderful impression and I am going to be a long-term follower of their work, for Bear & Breakfast is a mark of triumph against the many odds they faced, and I am grateful they went ahead and worked on this game even though it was a daunting task. I rate Bear & Breakfast a solid 25/10 Jack'o'Lanterns. Thank you GummyCat Studios and the Bear & Breakfast community for helping me through some hiccups during my gameplay and for releasing B&B! Please buy the Bear Game. Hank wants more friends. <3

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to give this game a five-star rating, I really do. But there's just enough little hiccups and holes in the wall to keep it from reaching that pinnacle. Still, it's a lovely game with fantastic characters and beautiful art design.First of all: I love Hank and his crew. They're fun and feel diverse and dynamic. I'm a bit sad that most of them only end up having limited screentime, but they really make the world feel like a world and not just a blank canvas with some NPCs.The gameplay is fun, with an engaging gameplay loop that introduces new elements to keep the experience interesting. There's been a lot of tweaks made to the inventory and item collection system since the game first launched, with more to come in the future that will further refine the experience.WARNING: FULL GAME SPOILERS AHEADIf I could sum up the main problem with this game with a single word, it would be Pacing. The game starts off smooth, mixing gameplay and plot with relative ease. But by the third area of the game the overarching plot comes to a screeching halt and doesn't pick up again until the last area. Even within the management aspect of the game, Winterberry is almost completely skipped over, the character being ushered into Pinefall as soon as the player finishes the 'special' mechanic tutorial of the area. This gives the player the daunting task of trying to build two resorts with the resources of one, and it can take a long time to build up enough for it to make a profit. This could be easily remedied by taking the portions of the overarching plot that involve Ciran and Vlad and moving them into the Winterberry section of the game, giving it a bit of padding and some breathing room before being pushed into Pinefall.The other big issue I have with the game is with the guests themselves. Not as a mechanic, but as a collective of people in the world. For a game that is about catering to guests and bringing People back to the Valley, I feel strangely unattached to the NPCs. Except for the ones with absurdly high requirements that I'm not sure are even achieveable within the game, I shove guests into rooms and call it good. I don't feel a need to  about them or why they're visiting. This could be fixed by having a few 'reccuring' NPCs that visit for a specific reason that Hank can interact with. Maybe someone that's researching the "gods' of the world, or studying the forest and how it is recovering after the aftermath of the fire. This could also give the 'overarching' plot a bit more depth and explain the human's side of the Great Fire. Maybe we could even meet Fin!My only other critique/suggestion is to make the 'decoration' need estate-wide and not just room-wide. I don't have an incentive to place decorations anywhere but the rooms, leaving me with a lot of 'empty' space in hallways that could hold shelves or posters to boost that score, but don't.END SPOILER WARNINGAll in all Bear and Breakfast is a lovely little indie that blends management with engaging story. It needs a bit mroe work before it truly reaches its potential, and I look forward to the day that it does.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; left with more questions than answers, unfulfilled, and with a void in me. Buy during a sale if possible. :)-------------------------I tend to hyper-fixate on games and enjoy life-sim/management games (I am probably a Type A), so when I saw this game I was intrigued. On top of the genre, the art style and story line were another selling point. I remember opening this up and playing a bit and thinking to myself, "This is cute but the tutorial bits are just too much" and I had been slightly off put by it. _childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game. I really, truly did.The initial premise is a charming one: you play as a cuddly cartoon bear who along with various other cartoon animals set out to attract humans (and their tasty, tasty rubbish) to their forest by opening charming holiday accommodations, with delicious food and relaxing activities. It almost seems to be trying for the title "peak-cosy game".Unfortunately, like the ageing properties that you renovate in-game there is a lot of problems beyond the charming exterior. The most glaring being that there are "properties" - plural - rather than just one location to focus on. They also have varying standards and amenities depending on their location and how far you have progressed in the game, so you are restricted in what you can do at each.Effort has been made to tie progress through the game to a diverse cast of fellow cartoon animals and quirky locals, but they wind up being little more than nodes for constant fetch quests. Character A wants a sandwich, talk to Character B who has a sandwich and will tell you how to open up the path to the next area if you deliver a letter to Character C etc etc. Key upgrades need to improve locations are given as rewards for these quests, but the order is often jumbled; with some early quests requiring mid-game unlocks from others to complete.The managing aspect of the game is also quite stressful. Each guest must be assigned to a room manually for the duration of their stay, with their needs matched to the facilities at a location. This is manageable when one or two locations are unlocked, but when you have dozens of guests across several resorts the experience becomes akin to spinning plates on sticks that are thrown directly at your adorable fuzzy head. There are upgrades that make managing your guests easier but they are at the end of (you guessed it) long, convoluted fetch quests.Overall, whilst there is some promise and charm here the game is ultimately let down by boring quests, stop-and-start progress and a story that frankly feels like it belongs in a completely different game. Maybe give it a go if it's on sale, but otherwise I would let this one pass.

_childDocuments_.review: Let’s talk about Stardew Valley for a moment.Stardew Valley is a farm sim game. You play as an urban escapee, leaving your big city-slicker life and burnout behind to take over your grandfather’s farm in Stardew Valley. You start small, with just a few patches of crops squeezed between trees, but gradually grow into an automated agricultural behemoth. Along the way, you befriend the denizens of Stardew Valley, perhaps finding romance, or perhaps discovering the platonic joy that is Krobus, and help the valley stand up against the scourge of Joja Corp (this is the only correct ending). You learn to fish, how to forage, and how to slash your way through dungeons, and in the end, you build something that you can be immensely proud of. You turn a swath of wild and untamed forest into a junimo sweatshop home.Okay, now let’s talk about Bear and Breakfast. Bear and Breakfast is a casual crafting game. You play as Hank, who, inspired by a talking shark, decides to turn the rubble-laden sheds in his forest into thriving bed and breakfasts or resorts. You start small, with a shed and a couple of cots, but gradually grow into a resort behemoth. Along the way, you meet the various denizens of the forest, learning their stories and the greater story of why your forest is the way it is. You learn to craft, to cook, and to build, and in the end, build a series of resorts that you can be proud of, full of glowing reviews and smiling guests. You turn a swath of wild and untamed forest into a home. I’m being a bit tongue-in-cheek. Stardew Valley and Bear and Breakfast are very different games. However, I think the spectre of Stardew Valley looms low over the entire casual management and casual crafting genre. I’ve seen it in games like Cat Cafe Manager, but it’s also present here. There’s this desire to make a game about something as simple as tending a farm or managing a cafe or building a series of resorts something more profound than it is, while also missing what made Stardew Valley so successful in the first place. There’s a desire to recapture that magical moment and make something that explodes into the collective psyche, but it’s lightning that’s difficult to recapture.Much like in my Antioch: Scarlet Bay where I compared Antioch: Scarlet Bay to Disco Elysium, this is not to say every game needs to be a paragon of its genre to be successful. Stardew Valley, like Disco Elysium, is a classic, and not every game has to be it. However, when an entire genre of games have shifted to try to capture what made Stardew Valley so successful, it’s worth considering why that might be, and what they’re missing.There is a lot of Bear and Breakfast that is enjoyable and unique. Bear and Breakfast not only centers around designing and furnishing small resorts, but around crafting. Much of the game’s time is spent roaming through the forest, harvesting the ingredients to make furniture, food, and whatever a thriving resort needs. However, this is both a blessing and a curse.  Thematically, it’s deeply sweet to see a resort grow almost solely out of what can be found in the forest. It is a wonderful ethos of reuse and viewing the world through the lens of the wild. The forest itself, though, is not dynamic enough to support the ethos of the forest as a home. The forest itself is unchanging. Except for resources spawning, there’s nothing new to see or experience in the forest. Once all locations are unlocked, there isn’t much new to explore. Quests can be progressed, but these quests are extensions of crafting. They are what the player would have done anyway, and so don’t provide any meaningful sense that the forest or Hank are progressing.The crafting mechanic itself is also flawed in its implementation. While the idea of gathering resources and using them to craft new things is far from a unique one, both Bear and Breakfast’s crafting and inventory management systems are frustrating. Stacks of items can only be moved one stack at a time, and don’t automatically stack. This leads to a tedious experience of scrolling through the space already taken up in a storage container, hunting for a like object to stack with. Cooking food either makes one stack of a food or all stacks of a food, with the act of cooking taking twelve seconds, regardless of what or how much is being made. Perhaps most confusingly, crafted items can’t be recycled or sold, and must instead be tossed out into the aether. This runs counter to the themes that make the game endearing and the idea of building a forest bed and breakfast from found items. It means as well that there is a disincentive to fully build rooms when you’re close to unlocking a new item tier. Those resources won’t be recycled or reused - they’re just lost. Bear and Breakfast also relies on that fundamental element of crafting games, namely that idea that the player’s creativity governs the end product. While there is some room for creativity, the fixed size and layout of buildings and the furniture within them, as well as the minimum requirements for each room means that, rather than each bed and breakfast being unique, every room looks the same, taking as much advantage of limited space as possible with the same furniture in every room. The challenges the game puts forth are also what make it frustrating. If we are to craft, let the players craft rather than setting out a blueprint for the correct design. This is the true lesson that games that seek to be Stardew Valley haven’t learned. There are elements of Stardew Valley I find frustrating. My house has limited space, and there are ideal layouts for crops or barrels or animals. I am not very good at the combat elements, and I will never make it to the bottom of the mummy’s tomb before the end of the day.But there are enough other things going on in the game that I don’t care about the things I’m not good at or the elements that can be frustrating. Instead, I can be drawn in by those things that work and that appeal to me, and they carry me through the more tedious bits.Once the initial thrill of exploration wears off, Bear and Breakfast is nothing but the tedious bits. It’s nothing but wandering a forest, scouring for resources, and assigning people to rooms. I ride the bus in loops, refilling buffet tables and cleaning up trash without ever feeling like I’m doing something meaningful. Rooms become impossible to upgrade due to space, and all I’m left with is a nearly non-existent story. This game has its moments. The characters are cute, and the idea undergirding it is a solid one. However, in trying to be a crafting game, it misunderstands what makes crafting interesting and fun. In trying to be a forest commune game, it misunderstands what makes that sort of story compelling. In trying to be a management game, it puts too little agency in the hands of the manager, and too much emphasis on tedious gameplay loops. I wanted to love this game. I briefly did. However, once I got a few hours in and realised where I was, I couldn’t love it anymore. All I saw was repetitiveness, when what I wanted was a cute bear in a forest.EDIT: I ended up changing this to a positive review. I'm still on the fence about this game, but thinking about those hours of fun I had did make me rethink how I feel about the game as a whole. All the criticisms still hold true, but I think the positives ultimately outweigh the negatives.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic! A wonderful balance of gameplay elements in my opinion. I normally don't play tycoon-like games because the high complexity makes it feel more like crisis management than anything else, but THIS game has just the right amount of everything that it eases you into. It has a lot more going on that just the trailers show you, I was surprised by the meatiness. People might at first be disappointed by the inability to change the size of the locales, but fitting rooms into the set shapes is a really fun puzzle element! Rooms end up needing to depend on where they are relative to another and it is a real nice brain teaser. Progress is slow enough that the game doesn't feel like you're rushing and taking it slow is fine since YOU control how many guests you take on.I think a couple elements could be improved here and there. While some may think the tutorials are a tad hand-holdy, they are necessary and in fact I think there could be a little more. I don't think I was ever notified when animal products started being sold so I spent a long while wondering when I would get chickens of all things! Don't worry, I eventually saw them, but a quest leading me back to the store would have been appreciated. The trash slot in the inventory is rather small and I only realized it existed after browsing the game's community tab. As other's have said on there, a way to sell back your old furniture for cheap would be nice, as there can be a pretty fast turnover at times.Maybe that could be done with the trash slot, sorta like the inventory garbage bin in Stardew Valley? Toss it and automatically get 10-30 coins?All in all, a nice variety of quests, fun core gameplay, amazingly charming characters, and something I'm having a hard time putting down!
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: This is certainty a game... that I played.Clearly I enjoyed it so some degree, after all I got all the achievements and did all the side quests, but I don't know if I can say I could recommend it to someone. Despite the fact that it calls itself a "laid-back" management game, for me, managing of all the different resorts ended up being incredibly stressful. This was not at all helped by the horrible menus and inventory. One of the things I was really looking forward to was cooking, only to realize that my inventory was never big enough to carry the ingredients I needed. There were far too many recipes for me to simply remember what I needed, and hopping from the cooker only to realize I was missing an item and having to walk all the way back to my stash every time I wanted to make anything was the most frustrating part of the whole game.There's also an issue with the main story. Even after completing it, there's no indication in game that you've actually completed anything. There's this big climatic cut scene and then you're sent back on your way. I had to check the achievements to make sure that I was, in fact, done with the game.Would I recommend this game to people? Eh, if you want to play it I'm not going to stop you. There are a lot of good things about the game, such as the beautiful art and wonderfully written characters, (I do really love the characters,) but for me the experience is tainted by all the bad stuff. Even still, I wouldn't call this a "bad" game, just one I think could've been better.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Bear and Breakfast invites players into a whimsical world where they take on the role of a bear running their very own bed and breakfast. With its adorable graphics, engaging gameplay, and comforting atmosphere, this game offers a delightful escape for players of all ages. It's the perfect choice for anyone looking for a cozy and charming gaming experience. So grab a cup of tea, settle in, and get ready to embark on a heartwarming journey through the forest in Bear and Breakfast!
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game. It is in the same vein as Stardew Valley, especially with the aspect of repairing old bridges/monuments with resources, but unlike lots of Stardew Valley-esque games lately it is also completely original and doesn't rely on Stardew/HarvestMoon/AnimalCrossing tropes and mechanics. I like the management style a lot- I like to progress slowly, and I am completely free (and sometimes encouraged) to do so, because each business owned has its own (mostly) standalone quests. The only dislikes I have about this game are not large flaws, but little things that make it feel less professional and seamless. For example, it is incredibly slow to move large quantities of items from storage to inventory and vice versa. Other than "take all" and "dump all" there is no quick way to do it. Also, it is frustrating that the humans in the game can fit in spaces that fatty Hank can't, so there will be trash you cannot get to and have to move furniture to remove, every single time. I do feel the game progresses a little too fast, but like I said the player is completely able to continue working on the same business(es) for as long as they want. I haven't finished the game yet, but I've played 12 hours over two or three days alone, and I know I'm very pleased. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, easily addictive and brain numbing in the good sense ;) Stayed for the management system and quests, not so much for the plot, still all characters look cute and the art is amazing.If I had to complain about something it would be how it eventually crashes, which doesnt usually hurt much of your progress but is still annoying nonetheless (imagine building 5 whole rooms and then it crashing on you).Aiming for all achievments B)
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very fun and amusing. I got this because I was extremely bored and none of my friends were active on Discord. This was the PERFECT pass-time! I am actually obsessed with this game right now! The quests and need for materials (to build/decorate) keep you busy so there is always something to do. The story part of the game is interesting as well. It is 100% worth your money and your time!

_childDocuments_.review: If We Bare Bears opened a B&B vibes! Great cozy game! It was cute, and I loved the art style! It's more fun if you take your time and don't try to rush, but you also don't need to completely finish an area before moving on. There were some glitches, but every time it was solved for me by just closing the game and reloading it. Mostly the glitches were for achievements not registering right away. I enjoyed the outfits and the furniture options, however some of the mechanics caused the rooms to be more crowded than I would prefer due to having to meet guest requirements. I wish there had been multiple art/color styles for each comfort level of items (bed, bathroom stuff, etc.). The characters are great, but the character development felt more surface than I would prefer ideally.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I was waiting for this game for a while. It worth every penny spent.Game is about building, quest (not adventure) and discovery.So far 3 hours in the game, 2 hotels, 9 rooms, still find it cute and fun.The tutorial is more for unexperienced players, trust me you can skip it if you can read these lines.I'll probably post another review when I reach 10 hours of play, my guess is that game can last 50 hours
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: The fun part is the first few hours.I really enjoyed my first half of this game. There were some fun writing and the mechanics were fairly interesting.But at my 20th hour, I really wanted the game to end.The game starts to feel like a slog halfway through.As you unlock the mechanics, they start to feel more cumbersome than rewarding.You start automating some of them but there's also the fact that certain materials for building will need to be farmed each day in the game where you have to keep walking and looting the same areas over and over again as you wait for a small amount of materials to respawn so you have enough to make a small number of higher level objects that you need to satisfy the customer.You also do the same thing to progress the story.You gotta keep walking back and forth to NPCs doing a mechanic that you thought you already automated.On top of that, the player path is not very clear and has so much obscure obstacles that simply walking gets frustrating because you keep running into things that you can barely make out slowing you down.At the end, it felt like there was less of the enjoyable part, (building management) and more of the other things that were not very enjoyable. (Walking to farm materials and waiting each day to farm the same things because they barely give you enough.)I'm writing the review because I'm almost finished the story and really wish I'd stopped playing. I kept pushing just because I wanted to see how it ended but it really just wasn't that interesting. I'm almost at max Level objects for my cabins but I'm done with the game because I know that even though there's only one more level, the amount of farming I have to do would probably take me more than 10 hours for a very miniscule reward.TLDR: Cute but overstayed its welcome by becoming a chore to play rather than enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute game and there are a lot of things I love about it! I'm a big fan of the art style, the dialogue is fun and the backstory is interesting, and I find the whole system of crafting and decorating satisfying, and I wouldn't mind the cooking system either if it were a little less frustrating. And that's where I seem to be at with a great deal of the aspects of this game. Crafting and decorating is fun until you start taking on new quests to improve the comfort level and realize that the furniture gets bigger the higher its level, which makes it difficult to reach the level you need and also keep the decoration level high unless you want the room to look more like a storage space than a bedroom, especially when you're looking at some of the smaller properties or have a minimum for the number of bedrooms.The cooking is fun until you find yourself having to keep three different properties stocked, at which point you begin to realize how tedious collecting ingredients and making dishes can be. The heating system is so broken that I eventually resigned myself to the fact that I would be getting no five star reviews from the winter resort starting out, because keeping it at the required temperature with the starting heater is damn near impossible. Apparently you can eventually hire roles to make these two things easier, but it comes at a hefty cost, while chances are you're already also paying for someone to collect 'valuables' for you so you can have even a hope of affording new decorations.None of this is to say that I don't find the game delightful, as I noted at the beginning. This game has so many good ideas and the concept is absolutely adorable, I just wish it were balanced better to make it more of a relaxing experience and less of a keeping the balls in the air experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Game just wasn't for me.Art style is fantastic, concept is a 10/10. However, I really wanted a fun management game, instead the management seems very hands off and boring. You end up waiting around for long stretches on the early game for guests to come and go with no interaction at all. Real shame.But that's just me, others will love this game. Just don't expect alot of depth to the management.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. Is it difficult? No. Is it enjoyable? If you like completing quests, designing rooms, and getting upgrades this game is great. The art style is absolutely adorable and I love all of the different characters you meet. I love that the basis for everything in this game revolves around collecting/buying/trading/crafting trash, It feels like you are recycling and helping maintain the environment around you. Super adorable game.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so much fun and it literally sucks up all my hours without me even realizing it. There's so much to do that it might feel intimidating at times, but over time, with new things you learn and other resources you get, it gets easier. ***Fun bear noises***There are a lot of quests, and they run parallel to each other depending on which location the quests originate from. At times, I felt like I didn't know how to progress on one, so I tried working a different one first, and eventually it looped back to the one I missed, so don't worry if it feels like you're stuck. The only quest I had trouble so far was the one where you had to build 2x level 1 bathrooms in the A24 motel, but by the time I reached that quest, I had 2x level 2 bathrooms and it didn't recognize that I finished the quest lol... I can't wait to keep playing! I have to pace myself because I lose track of time whenever I play.

_childDocuments_.review: Super cute game. There's always lots to do and decorate. Love the characters. The only thing I really don't care for is once you buy something with valuables, you can't sell it or trade it in. Which is kind of a pain when you're trying to raise your prestige and what not. Otherwise, great casual game with an engaging story line. Highly recommend. <3

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR:  This is a very cute game that's good for about 2-5 hours.  Unfortunately, those 2-5 hours aren't anywhere near enough to finish the game, and at a certain point the game's highlights fade away under a mountain of small janky bits that culminate in an overall dreary experience.  By the end, the game feels unfinished; this is at best an early access title without any indication of such.This is going to end up as a ramble if I don't bullet each cut that contributed to the death by a million cuts, so let's go from the top:* The game's story makes no bones about the fact that gentrification and the rise of AirBnB is a bad thing, and as a leftist I agree, but then the entire game is about managing a swanky BnB chain/empire. It brings down the mood quite a bit to constantly be reminded that you're buying into a very corrupt system while I'm just trying to build nice hotel rooms, and the game fails to ever truly reconcile these conflicting ideas. In fact, by the end of the game, it stops caring about your business altogether and begins to tell a completely unrelated story about the evils of zoos and animism being real.* When you're crafting furniture, there are filters for functional furniture and decorative furniture. However, you cannot craft any decorative furniture.* You can drill down further on the functional furniture filter, but the UI for this isn't particularly clear, and there's no tutorialization for this.  I had to read the Steam forums to discover this.* There's no way to sell crafted items; the only way to get rid of things you don't need is to throw them away.  Throwing away items is a tiny icon in your inventory, and there is no tutorialization for this.* When you choose to build a new room in your BnBs, you choose from categories: "comfort," "hygiene," "dining," "utility," and "special." However, three of these categories only ever have one room type under them, and "Special" has six.* Taking care of management aspects takes only a few minutes, and days are much longer than that. You can spend the rest of the day gathering items, but gathering isn't very exciting (every point is two clicks, and all points are predetermined) and by endgame you have more stacks of crafting mats than you know what to do with (except for 3 specific bottleneck materials).  By endgame, I was leaving the game window open in the background and doing something else just to churn guests.* The cooking minigame is a little confusing/convoluted, and then the recipe card unlock makes it mostly just a time waster.  The cooking recipe list is far too small a dialogue window to view recipes easily, and there's no way to sort or filter this list, so good luck finding what you need to make for quests!* Mid- to late- game guests will request room stats (notably in hygiene) that are impossible to hit.  Not impossible in a "this takes too much effort" way; impossible in a "there is a hard cap on the number you can achieve and the guests ask for more than it."  This is a known issue that is lessened but still present as of the 1.2 patch.* The material bottleneck/money sink in early endgame is ludicrous; I think I got to the final resort at about 10 hours in and couldn't build a single room in it for many more hours.  Bedrooms with the highest quality furniture costs a minimum of 1400 gold to make (1800 in 1.0) at a point in the game where you're fortunate to have 2,000 to play with after maintaining all your other resorts at the highest quality. This game was not playtested with the mindset of "I want to build a really nice resort for the first guests," but by the time I realized that, I was in too deep into playing the game wrong to course correct.* There are no decoration variants, so all your endgame hotel rooms look basically the same. You can't even change the flooring or wallpaper, or even make recolors of the same items.* Late-game decor objects are focused almost entirely on bringing the score of special rooms up.  This raises your hotel prestige, but you are likely to cap hotel prestige without having any decor in endgame special rooms.  Conversely, there's very few options for decor that makes sense to put in guest bedrooms, which have ludicrously high demands in late game.* Late game story feels buggy.  I'm pretty sure I somehow missed an entire cutscene that was supposed to explain what I was doing post-hotel managing.  Late-game quests didn't track properly and weren't even marked in the journal as story quests. The last bit of dialogue had an obvious typo in it.The devs are very active and seem very enthusiastic about making the game better. That's great! But I do QA as my day job, and I bought this with the expectation of a mostly finished experience that might get some content updates in the future. As it stands, though, this game is far from finished, and the earnest but unfocused mess that's present might never coalesce into something great.  I'd say check back in a year or so, but definitely stay away for now.

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to start by saying that this game is super charming, and has really promising base for what it's going for but...   Just couple hours in and I already have downtime in-game where all I can do is wait for the clock to tick to evening so I can progress to next day by sleeping. The fact that you cannot go to sleep to move on to the next day whenever you want, is probably the biggest problem here;  You get sidequests but if you're like me and collect absolutely everything you see, you end up completing them as soon as you get them (At least in start and second B&B building area).     Collecting resources in first few areas does not take much time at all, and is honestly a bit boring because of how slow Hank moves around.   This leads to you waiting for the guests to sign in and out, without much to do other than stare at the in-game time indicator that will allow you to skip the night.   I would love to see devs at least add an option to skip the day/proceed at anytime you wish, or at least after it become dark 'enough' to sleep, not just at when I assume there's midnight in-game.  That's honestly my biggest problem with this game; too much downtime.

_childDocuments_.review: When the game starts there is a lot of downtime that you'll wish you could speed up. As you progress this won't be an issue since you'll be juggling multiple rentals. I completed 100% of the game and still feel like it didn't really have a solid ending. I actually wasn't sure if I even beat the game lol.That being said it was a really fun game if you like trying to optimize profits and that sort of thing. Plus its all super cute and the characters are fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Fun! It's meant to be chill, so - honest advice here: try not to dive in with a speed runner's mindset. In my opinion, Bear and Breakfast is best played with a laid back vibe where you slow yourself down. The game lets you explore and collect, and you'll find some items miles ahead of when you'll actually need them to progress the story. There are no timed events, so there's zero reason to rush ahead and do all the things. Different areas around the map are locked to story and resort progress, anyway, which can make it feel punishing if you try to race ahead to the next thing. Kinda like running face first into a door.I completed the game in 56 hours. Loved almost every minute of it. The art style is sweet and suits it very well. The music is great. The characters are quirky and fun. The controls are easy to use (keyboard/mouse). For the players who have a TL;DR mentality and hit space to speed through conversation: One of the most asked questions I see is "How do I rotate furniture?" It's one of the first tips given when setting up your first resort (press the R button). I recommend turning on tips for new players (or players like me with the memory of a goldfish). They're well written and help explain new features as you unlock them.All in all, chill with Hank's amusing ignorance of the world and vibe to the music while you build up your cozy Bear and Breakfast empire.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: This game is perfect.Not technically perfect, mind you - it's got a couple of bugs, a few hinky things that you get used to pretty fast. But that's not what I mean.To me, this game is simply perfect. The art style is ADORABLE and so consistent. The story is lighthearted and funny but also has plenty of depth to it if you want to let it take you there. It's got some minor time pressure so it's not like you're going to idly wander around staring into space, but neither is it OMG WHAT TIME IS IT? IS THE STORE STILL OPEN? WHAT IF I DON'T MAKE IT BACK TO MY FARMHOUSE AND PASS OUT??? levels of anxiety. There are enough decorations and pieces of furniture to choose from without it being completely overwhelming. The design aspect is challenging  enough to keep me engaged but never so challenging that I get frustrated.If you've got a couple of days to a week where you're sick, this game will keep you perfect company until you feel better.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun and I'll admit, it's very addicting! I love all of the little ways you can customize and decorate. There is a bit of a grind but I rather like that, and it's not a difficult grind either. It's highly rewarding and once you get the hang of things, it's a breeze to manage everything. These types of games are my favorites and I'm totally gonna get even more mileage out of this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Cute, funny and simple game with challenges. You can go full min-maxing and spend hours designing and decorating each room or play casually. Perfect for winding down but you can also spend hours on end without noticing it.Great dialog too:"You are not playing with a full deck, are you?""I don't like gambling"
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I came into this game expecting the name to be an accurate summary of the gameplay. The "Bear" part of the name was extraordinarily accurate, in fact being not only the first thing you experience, but also always being a part of the experience. This part was incredibly entertaining, fun, and immersive. However, the "breakfast" part is slightly misleading. After 6.5 hours of playing the game, I was still left with no breakfast. So, while the "Bear" part of the game was a 10/10, with an excellent art  style and fun gameplay, the lack of breakfast brought it down to a 5. HOWEVER, this feeling would not last, as 6 hours and 37 minutes into "Bear" as I began to call it, I finally achieved it. I finally discovered "Breakfast". This game would be a 10/10 if it delivered on its promise of "Breakfast" sooner than 6.5 hours into the game, however, despite all the other praises I have given it, it does deduct a few points from the overall review. From an objective, "Bear and Breakfast" receives a 9/10 (100% for the "Bear", but only 80% on the "Breakfast" front).
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I love the art style of this game, and the whole vibe of it. I went in thinking it would just be cute, relaxing, and enjoyable... and I easily sunk HOURS into it right away. It's such a great game. You have so much creativity in designing the B&Bs. Want to change something or start over in that area? Sure, just remove the rooms with one click. This game is great after a stressful day. It's so satisfying, and wholesome. I also love the characters a lot, and the whole world just looks so good. It runs super well too. Great sounds, though the door squeak when changing locations is sharp on the ears if switching between several in a row. The story isn't anything huge, but it's peppered in nicely and adds to the experience. It's all very well-balanced, though I would like to see a bit more diversity in the guests -- body types and styles are nice, but not a lot skin colour variation.There's a real sense of progression throughout the game, and a surprisingly nice amount of strategy to max potentials. You start with the basics, then unlock new features at new locations. Then new furniture or decorations, of which the options get better over time. The grind is minimal; I recommend constantly picking up stuff, like wood, whenever you see it. You need a lot later on, and early collection makes all the difference. Everything constantly respawns.You can play at 100% your own pace, even expand when you're ready to or put off things without impacting gameplay or story too much. I will say, it was a bit misleading in that it seems like we have one place but in the game you actually have multiple B&Bs with differing requirements. As things get further along, there's a lot of running back and forth to maintain them. I stuck with it and once again that progression kicked in; you unlock new ways to manage stuff, and simplifying tasks. If an aspect gets tedious just hang in there, as the game will absolutely help you out.I highly recommend this game. It's a bit of a hidden gem, to be honest. Not perfect, but the devs are amazing. There's more updates coming, and they really listen to player feedback. A lot of love went into this game, and I have a fun time playing it. This game is a perfect blend of chill without being too easy, visually pleasing, excellent progression system, and creativity that allows your own style with lots of options. If you're having a rough time or looking for something chill, this is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Was a joy to play through, and originally caught my eye due to my love for eg. Stardew Valley. It was nice to not have to think about any fighting elements, so you were pretty much casually just unlocking new areas and managing your hotels along the way. Some quests were not very clear to understand and follow, not to mention some actions not being very clear. While I understood why we wanted nights in the game, it was very tedious to play around those times due to poor visibility. Also, I felt like due to the gameplay I can't really skip nights as there is so much to do and keep running (especially after locking food). Most annoying part is NOT easily understanding what items or areas on a map that block or don't block you. I kept running into things or getting stuck, as it's definitely not clear. Eventually you'll learn in some places, but it was frustrating at times. Rotating items also sometimes annoying as you can't most of the time clearly see how they are placed (as you can't move the camera angle), not to mention difficult to pick up trash that is hidden behind decor. I also only at the end realized that trash in rooms made the decoration value of the room go down - why wasn't this explained early on?Nevertheless - I liked the game more than some aspects annoyed me. Casual, not too hectic, nice look and feel, and definitely worth the money. Do play if games like this appeal to you! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Animation is absolutely adorable, the characters are pretty charming, and I like the concept of the game. Farming recipes and materials to make upgrades is an interesting formula, as is having managing multiple areas at the same time.Cons:There's WAY too much free time. It's not really a management sim as I expected. Yes, you invite guests and can upgrade your hotels, but there's nothing to do in between. This is more like a farming simulator because farming materials is all you can really do to pass the time. Maybe this changes further into the game, but when I'm so bored that I don't WANT to play further, it's a problem.I'm pretty let down, because I had this game on my wish list for a VERY long time, and really wanted more. If the game had a speed up button, it would help immensely. That being said, that won't take away the fact that  there's little to do - it will only mask it. I guess if you're looking for something SUPER casual (like something to play while you're trying to queue for another game), it would work. But it's not anything that can hold my attention.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: A management game i can get into. Its full of beautiful artwork and lots of different animal friends. Like what more can i ask for.It scratches the righ itch on my brain with wanting to make beautiful rooms for people and also do resource collecting. Also the bears name is Hank, that's already like the best.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I think with a bit more work on the game it could be good. Very quickly into playing it you will hit a wall of having no more objectives as you wait a full day night cycle for guests to arrive. Very often you have to wait on guests, and while you can sleep through the night, you can only sleep at a specific TIME of night FAR into the evening. You should be able to sleep day or night to progress time if you have nothing to do currently, which you will often. The game has more than a few bugs that cause guests to get stuck or behave strangely, sometimes it may be due to the way you can place items that you won't immediately realize are preventing your guests from checking in with no indicator of this. Indicators in general are too vague in general or sometimes either don't appear at all, or appear on another guest that is not obstructed at all.Waiting for currency is sluggish and boring at early stages with no way to hasten in game time. The dialog is also long in the tooth and can quickly become boorishly cumbersome when you want to get into the building aspects of the game. If you want to upgrade a room with improved furniture you unlock farther into the game, you CANNOT sell old items for any amount of coins or trash which is the stupidest design decision I've seen in quite a while. Having NO sell mechanics and lots of buy mechanics is absolutely unheard of. So prepare to work hard for items you can only delete for NOTHING as you progress through the game. I hope you also didn't build a room you want to move somewhere else because you CAN'T DELETE ROOMS after they're placed. This is basic building design 101, how are these not functions in the game?!This game was not ready to come out yet and needed some serious redesign to be as appealing as it's trailers suggest it is. Should have noted the red flag when the devs only releasing a demo for a week and then took it down before the game's release. I really hope this game gets some serious overalls. I love the idea but the execution is shaky if not bitterly laughable at best.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very fun and relaxing game. As its new, it has a lot of bugs to be worked out but they seem quick to fix the game breaking ones. They're also actively listening to their community which is always a great sign for a game. I look forward to seeing where this game goes from here, and any new additions to it later on.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I saw a cute hotel management game and that’s what I got. I love the characters (Hank is a really satisfying and cute protagonist), the dialogue is funny, and the whole concept is definitely worthy of the “cosy” title. It’s fun and addictive and I enjoyed it enough to play it through to total completion.    I am aware that fixes are being looked at and added as time goes on and the developers appears receptive to feedback, so I don’t feel the need to be critical. However, my main feedback is that the game in it’s current form can be overwhelming due to the inventory management and lack of ability to sell or stack larger quantities of items. I also found the scarcity of resources more frustrating than challenging as a full junkyard rarely covered the crafting needed to keep up with objectives. I was also left with the final goal of achieving 30 5-star reviews at Pinefall which meant I was essentially leaving the game running so I could restart the day and refresh the junkyard materials.    However, it was overall really positive. The dialogue is genuinely hilarious, and the story is engaging enough for a short game. I’d love to see the overall mechanics and gameplay shift slightly more towards challenging rather than stressful, but at the same time it did mean you always had something to do until the last bit. I’d recommend purchasing if you enjoy management games.

_childDocuments_.review: 4/5. Good game. The dialogue is cheeky. The building is easy. Would have been nice if some of the quests didn't take so long to complete. _childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: The art style is very cute! And that's about the only good thing I have to say about it. The charm wears off very quickly and you're left with gameplay that gets more tedious with each new feature. The maps are big and unpopulated, making resource gathering slow and boring. When you're not dealing with either of those, you're just waiting for time to pass. The one-note characters seem important and then disappear from the plot entirely. The story is predictable, leaves no impressions and then ends with so little fanfare that you're left wondering if that's it. Which is unsatisfying, but I'm glad it actually is over.I played using a controller, which was pretty clunky and I occasionally got a glitch where I couldn't interact with anything upon opening build mode. Closing and re-opening the game resolved this, so it's a good thing you can save at any time. That's all.
_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.name: Bear and Breakfast

_childDocuments_.review: I have been looking for a new game and was pleasantly surprised by what I found with Bear and Breakfast.
