_childDocuments_.review: There is a mathematical beauty to the structure of puzzles in Filament. While playing I feel as if I'm constructing theorems about curve topologies. It is quite engaging if you're into that kind of stuff. That's not to say university-level mathematics are required to appreciate the game. But it doesn't hurt.The amount of content in Filament feels quite generous. There are a lot of puzzles, a good number of secrets, and quite a bit of lore. Full disclosure: I haven't beaten the game and I certainly haven't found all the secrets. But I've decided to post a review regardless because I don't know how long it will take to finish the remaining puzzles as some of them are rather challenging and some secrets appear rather tricky to decipher. There is a hint system if your sole interest is story completion but I have yet to enable the feature and don't intend to out of principle. And while there are a number of challenging puzzles only the most stubborn players should feel truly stuck through most of the game due to its structure, as the game contains a lot of mechanical variation among puzzles and generally does not gate access to these variations. If you can't figure a puzzle out there you can just go down a different hallway and start solving puzzles which feel vastly different.The story is fairly compelling, particularly for a puzzle game. The main character, Juniper, whose exposition drives the narrative has a wonderfully soothing voice. The soundtrack is simple but pleasant and chill, well suited for sitting back and contemplating how to satisfy the many constraints inherent in the more complex and difficult puzzles.While I consider this game to be quite good it's not without some technical issues, which can be particularly frustrating during the first ~10 hours before you've internalized these "quirks" so they will be more easily foreseen and avoided. For example, the filament-bot's 3D model does not seem well matched to its collision geometry. Many times have I created corridors, which I intend to utilize later in the puzzle, only to find out they were too narrow for the filament-bot to pass through. The filament can also snap to pillars in somewhat unexpected ways. Thankfully, with enough time spent solving these puzzles these "jank" mechanics are fairly predictable and will not surprise seasoned players.I was able to accidentally soft-lock a  puzzle, forcing me to exit and re-enter the level. That was rather annoying but such a glitch only seems possible in a small fraction of the game's levels and it was not hard to avoid in future attempts.Despite these imperfections I think Filament is a very special game.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: This game doesen t receives the atention that it should... the music, the secrets and the puzzles are something unique (at least for me) this game its a relaxing/stressing experience whit allways the satisfaction of winning the puzzles... i really love this game. It has a special places in my heart .
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: This game only lives for people who are puzzlers. My issue is if you are not a puzzler than you will just be redoing the same puzzle you can't solve. It just causes frustrations that makes the very weak hold of playing the game into a challenge itself. In fairness the art style and layout of the game is well done and the music albeit repetitive was good that makes me want to seek out the soundtrack. As much as it might break the immersion a hint feature would be nice touch even if it was just one per level or which side to start on. The top down view is nice but isn't enough in a room that is dark to begin with. Filament would be worth sharing to my friends who live to solve puzzles but to other's who would have trouble It's best to avoid.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: This game takes advantage of what I call "artificial difficulty". Levels just get bigger and more complex instead of "harder". When two different colors isn't challenging enough, they introduce a third color. It's as if a crossword had a mix of English and Spanish words.The Witness had me staring at a 4 x 4 grid thinking "I'm convinced that this puzzle is impossible".
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Refunded after an hour of gameplay. There is no strategizing or thinking, it's just trial and error. I rather mindlessly mash buttons than run around in circles trying to solve some unnecessarily complicated 'puzzle'. The developer seems to think that requiring complex solutions to progress somehow adds substance to the gameplay. Complexity does not equal intelligent design. Nor does it contribute to the game being fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Puzzle games should be both challenging AND fun.  Filament is challenging, but it sure ain't fun.  Solving a puzzle gives me zero satisfaction and no sense of accomplishment.  The Witness is significantly more obtuse and difficult, but figuring a puzzle out is FAR more satisfying.  Filament is well made and clearly passion went into it.  However... I hated playing it so I cannot recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Playtime: 55.2 hrsA hard and challenging puzzle game that I think was a bit above my level of puzzle-solving skill. But still despite the difficulty it was quite a good puzzle game with very nice graphics and even an interesting story that panned out bit by bit finished with a surprising twist at the end. I must admit I referred to the guide a few times before the bridge but got really stumped by quite a bit of the puzzles in the bridge part especially the last few ones. Still exercising my brain this way felt cathartic at the time. I also went to the discussion forum for some insights regarding the ending. There were quite a few theories that sounded interesting and pretty convincing. Overall, it took me a long time to finish this game, but that journey was quite memorising, and I wish the dev will make more challenging but fun games in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: This is a well-made and unique puzzle game, and for that reason alone, I cannot give this a negative review. That said, if you do not find the first few puzzles satisfying, in my experience, it only goes downhill from there. Puzzles all eventually boil down to a game of trial and error, and with no features to know which patterns you have and have not tried before, it is very easy to become stuck. And no, it is not the kind of stuck that is solved by pen and paper thanks to the unique puzzle type or by walking away and coming back later; all that will do is wipe your memory of what you've tried before, and you quickly find yourself stuck in an infinite loop. Unfortunately, that is where I am now. In the end, I have tried to get into this game multiple times, but each time I get stuck and bored once again. I know this game has more to offer, but at least for now, it is not for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Just a genuinely pleasant cats-cradle of a puzzle game that feels like it flew under the radar. After a few months away, just returned to a puzzle that'd been driving me up the wall and solved it quickly. That said: getting some weird graphical glitches with the UI on Steam Deck that weren't there at launch.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Filament is a great game with some flaws, but worth your time if you enjoy puzzles and a challenge.Keep in mind this is more about trial and error than using logic or thinking about solutions, so it's not exactly for everyone.As for the flaws, at times it can be REALLY frustrating and I find the ending area extremely hard, IMHO it should have been a bonus area and not part of the main story.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: The storyline is pretty good! I love a little mystery and different personalities handling unexpected situations.The puzzles are tough, really tough! It's easy to understand what you need to so, but after the first few puzzles figuring out HOW to do it is not easy at all. Some puzzles are incredibly long, so don't expect to solve them in your head. The last few puzzles are insane. I admit that quite a few of those were very much above my skills, and I do have some puzzle skills XDA great surprise was the amount of hidden codes and puzzles. Recognizing you're looking at a code is the first step, decoding what you see into a useful string is the second step. The game has a lot of those, and I love these kind of hidden codes.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Oh, I so loved this game for the first 18 or so hours! It has a truly engaging plot that always leaves you wanting more information (I won't spoil it, but it sounds like everything you might want). It has excellent puzzles with a great learning curve that brings you up to speed in no time. As I explored the ship, many times I thought I'm close to completion, only to find entirely new mechanics and new puzzle sequences around the corner, with many cute aha moments inside. I had collected almost all messages before going to the bridge and couldn't bring myself to wait and get them all before proceeding further. I was fully expecting the story to end as I entered the bridge......and there I found basically another chapter of the most complex puzzles in the whole game, which could easily take another 6-8 hours to complete. Sounds like more of a good thing, but the problem with hard puzzles in this game is that they are extremely tedious and not at all satisfying. Maybe it's just me, but I just can't hold the whole puzzle in my mind when, e.g., the hue of the cord is changing as it elongates, or when the puzzle has a dozen different colored pillars that you have to clear in a particular order. It also doesn't help that you don't see the whole picture when you move, you have to stop and press a button to get a bird's eye view. So for me, hard puzzles basically mean a lot of rote enumeration of possibilities, a lot of backtracking, and not a lot of creative thinking (as opposed to easier puzzles that I can actually grok and solve in my head). Maybe I would train myself to do better in another 10 hours, but I lost all motivation to do so, so I just walked through the bridge by solving what I could solve quickly and looking up solutions to puzzles that seemed especially tedious. Then I got the ending... which really did not explain anything and left several different explanations open. So the last part of the game significantly brings my score down -- for the first 15 hours it was an easy 9-9.5/10.I also have to note bugs on Steam Deck -- the game plays well but it has a lot of visual bugs (broken 3d geometry flickering in and out) that doesn't really prevent you from playing but is extremely annoying. Still, it's a clear thumbs up!
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Beautifully made with puzzles ranging from "mild tickle in the brain" to "fiendishly hard" and a well written, if somewhat inconclusive, story that unravels as you play, Filament is among the best "pure" puzzle games out there (e.g. The Witness, Baba is You). The main mechanic is simple: you wrap a cord of filament around sets of pillars, creating an intricate web to activate them all. Frequently changing modifiers introduce new rules and challenges. I've read some reviews decrying the puzzle solving process in this game as "nothing more than trial and error" and have to disagree. While you certainly can brute force the solutions, this approach gets less and less viable the further the game progresses. Instead, Filament challenges you to think about things like turn directions, inner and outer routes and angles of approach. It's certainly possible to deduce how a puzzle or subsection thereof needs to be approached after getting the hang of that.If you're a fan of puzzle games, Filament is well worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles are fresh and unique and progressive which I like. There are a bunch of different puzzle mechanics which can sometimes be frustrating to figure out since there is not a lot of hand holding but eventually you get there in the end. I absolutely LOVE all the little secrets and hidden codes and passwords, I eat that ♥♥♥♥ up. I took a lot of paper notes to figure things out and it was just really fun : )I don't like the hints system. First of all, I didn't know it existed until poking around the controls and seeing that H is for hints, but didn't realize you had to turn it on under gameplay. Also 2 hints per level is barely enough and I wish there was an option for unlimited hints. Sure you can cheese it by exiting and re entering the level but that's tedious and loses your progress.Overall I do recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: About halfway through at this point and this game is taking over my dreams. It's difficult but it's not impossible. Take the puzzles one step at a time, look at them big picture and you can do it without it feeling like you're brute forcing it. There is logic here. A nice nod to something like The Witness if you're looking for something similar.EDIT: The bridge was impossible. I did use a guide after doing about half of it without one.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Why is this game so good? I bought this game on sale, without much expectation, but its been truly a challenge.  Not in the 'I hate this' way, but in the I'm not going to finish the game in 3 hours kind of way.  It's relaxing so far, no challenge has had a time limit which is nice.  The music is relaxing and the story is intriguing. Not gonna lie though... the captain is giving me GlaDOS vibes...
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Really interesting concept for the puzzles. It can get pretty hard, though.You also gradually discover the story of what happened on the ship, but... kinda out of order. It's really hard to get the "big picture" from the scattered logs. It is an intriguing story buried there, though.It also has a ton of easter-egg-like hidden codes that get you more lore and whatever, but they're super hard to pick up on... I looked up most of them.I guess my point is that it's worth playing, but be prepared to look up answers to some of the harder puzzles.PS it has great music
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: : A challenging puzzle game with a lot of content and an engaging sci-fi story:- Hard but fair, plenty of content and variation- Looks great for a three-person indie project- Interesting story and retro-futuristic setting- Wonderful soundtrack:- Some of the puzzle variations aren't as good- Perhaps  much content, weaker endgame- Graphical glitches on the Steam DeckFilament is an abstract puzzle game. In each level, you control a little robot with a glowing rope extending from its butt. This rope grows as you walk around, and your task is to wrap it around all pillars in the room before making your way to the exit. The game soon starts to introduce variations on this basic concept, such as black pillars that the rope cannot touch, elements that force you to touch the pillars in a specific order, or levels with more than one robot.While the basic concept is simple, the game does get very challenging, and it wasn't uncommon for me to spend more than ten minutes on a single level. For the most part though, it's a fair challenge; you soon start to recognize patterns that either work or don't work, and you barely ever have to resort to blind trial-and-error if you don't want to. One point if criticism is that it's often not immediately clear whether there's enough room between the rope and a wall or pillar for your robot to squeeze though; most levels don't require such tight squeezes, but the lack of visual clarity still resulted in a couple of frustrating moment.While there's a lot of variation in the different puzzle gimmicks, some of them don't work as well as others. In particular, the final area of the game is home to some of the more outlandish variations, with a lot of them feeling like one-off experiments that maybe should've been left on the cutting room floor. There's also arguably too much content; even with liberal use of spoilers towards the end, I ended up spending more than 25 hours on this game, and by the end (especially combined with the weaker final area) I was very much ready for it to be over.The puzzle levels are accessed from an overworld, in the form of an abandoned spaceship. After a brief tutorial area you're free to explore most of the ship, and you can tackle the various clusters of puzzles in whatever order you like. As you do, you'll slowly uncover the story of the spaceship and its missing crew, both through radio messages from the sole remaining crew member, and through reading archives containing emails and logs. I found the story to be surprisingly engaging; the writing is solid, with each crew member having a distinct voice and personality, and the game does a good job of slowly revealing the underlying mystery. The game's also set in 1983, which gives it a cool (if somewhat inconsistent) retro-futuristic aesthetic.One other thing I want to shout out are the secrets. Without giving too much away, if you are a fan of the way games like The Witness and Tunic handle secrets, this might be a game for you. There's a lot of secrets to uncover (although the rewards are fairly irrelevant), ranging from the obvious to the wonderfully obtuse, and if you're into secret hunting you could probably spend almost as much time on this part of the game as on the actual puzzles.Overall, I had a good time with Filament, and it's an easy recommendation for any fan of puzzle games. It maybe overstayed its welcome a bit for me personally, but it's really well made, and the story and setting add a lot.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: A very challenging puzzle game, with lovely graphics and music, and surprisingly good voice acting. It is absolutely not for the faint of heart or for anyone who does not want to spend twenty to thirty minutes staring at one puzzle trying to figure it out. Especially on the last level, when sets of rules get combined in novel ways to form whole new challenges.Although all of the games are about drawing lines with wires to link nodes, that has been explored here in so many different ways that there is none of the sense of sameyness that can affect other games.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very difficult puzzle game, but fantastic.  The characters are all very well developed, despite only getting to know most of them through their emails and details around the ship.  With slowly uncovering bits of story, and the calming music, this is a peaceful and relaxing game to play.  Expect to need to take a lot of breaks and come back to it later- the puzzles can be extremely tough, but coming back to them fresh after a little break always seems to help.  There's a section of puzzles towards the end of the game that are on a whole other level of difficulty, so be prepared.I love puzzle games, so I don't mind that this was a game I had to keep putting down and coming back to.  If you like burning through games one at a time for story, the puzzles might be pretty frustrating.  I think it's still worth it for the story as well, although if I was using guides and flying through the puzzles, I don't know that I would have taken the time to really absorb the story elements throughout the ship, or reading all emails and log entries.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: I'm so torn on loving and hating this game. (Puzzles, amirite?)I love the music and the visuals. I like the controls. I like the puzzle concept. I like the story.And yet I find it to be such a frustrating puzzle game. There is a good amount of variety so far, too.Seeing the solution to a puzzle is quite satisfying, much like a twisted reverse of untangling a knot. Getting to the solution? Not so much... much like untangling a knot.II find that it relies heavily on bruteforcing possibilities due to the 3D equivalent of being a pixel off from activating a pillar. Despite the presence of an overhead view to take in the whole puzzle, that view is still very much 3D and rather useless in figuring out exactly what lines are possible to take, so you have to test a lot. A whole lot... only to realize your approach still included a line that isn't possible because you can't keep the information in your head.I wish I could apply more reason to the puzzles. Maybe there's a lot of depth of reasoning I am missing, but if there is, then I want to say this puzzle game is a horrible teacher. It does slowly introduce you to the mechanics, but I don't feel like it has taken any steps to teach me how to solve those puzzles. It does have a hint system, but that's more like 'this is wrong' rather than 'you can tell a cable has to wrap around this pillar on that side because of x and y'.I don't mind hard puzzles. But I hate that I feel like I am not solving the more complicated puzzles, but just stumbling into solutions by finally trying the right thing since I lack both the visual and strategic tools to chip away at the problem piecemeal.I hope that I'll get a better feel for it as the game progresses, since I really do love the rest of it.Edit: I finished the game after a months break so I could let me frustration pass me by a bit. Perhaps I forgot some problem solving skills (or never learned them), but in general I immediately ran into the old 'bruteforce and hate the perspective' wall all over again because the puzzle mechanics were not something I could theorize about.For me personally, the last third of the game was the worst. It combined earlier mechanics like many puzzle games tend to do, but unlike those, I felt like almost every puzzle was a combination that included a variety I strongly disliked. Admittedly, I did not need to accomplish all the final puzzles to reach the ending, but you still had to do the majority and those puzzles were just too dominant. In the end, I can only admit to enjoying some of the ending puzzles. That said, the story ending was satisfying to me, but perhaps less-so to others.The early puzzles, story, music and visual polish deserve a positive recommendation. They were worth the money. But as a complete product for a 100%ing individual, I can only recommend to stay away. The frustration for this mixed bag of madness that is the remainder of the game is probably not worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: For how hard this game is, I am really proud to use tips for only 2 times, in the end game puzzles. I've spent more than half hour for solid dozen of them and some of them I had to come back and try again another day when my brain was "fresh". I also couldn't come up with the solutions for a few , but the ones I figured were satisfying as all hell.Your creativity, logical thinking and imagination will be put for a serious test.I recommend and wish you good luck!
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not gonna lie: These puzzles are hard, sometimes requiring me to look at a walkthrough to help me finish some levels. However, I still found myself enjoying every bit of it and uncovering the lore even more. Every little new thing that I came across made me excited to see what new bit of the story I unlocked, solving the mystery further each time (at least what I believe the story to be). This game is truly on the level of The Witness, and I might argue that it is even above it. Can not recommend this game enough!
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: If you're tired of puzzle games where you just glide right on through, and would rather pull out your hair and smash your keyboard, this is the game for you. The game will feed you a few easy levels when introducing a new mechanic and then it shoves you to the floor and kicks your teeth in. A solid hour was spent figuring out one ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ level (with 2 people). In terms of map, we have no map. Wander around the gigantic labyrinth of a hub. Want to go back to a level that you previously gave up on? Cross your fingers and toes, wish on a shooting star, and be born with photographic memory. I'm only being a tad hyperbolic. Seriously though, this game is great and I do recommend it if you're into actually challenging puzzles. This game will make you feel stupid, in the best way possible.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Puzzle game with over 15 hours of gameplay. The core gameplay is that you are pulling a wire, but each sequence of puzzles has you tackle the environment in a slightly different way. Some puzzles are really long and take some trial and error, but they change up frequently enough that it doesn't get boring.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome puzzle game. The puzzles are all based on one central concept, but there are many variations of this concept to keep it fresh. Each 'set' of 15 puzzles typically has 5 easy puzzles, 5 medium, and 5 difficult ones. This game will really make you think. It is hard at times, but it is certainly fair, nothing in here is impossible. In addition it has a long story and lots of easter eggs to find. At minimum 25-30 hours of core game puzzles and probably another 5-10 hours of side puzzles and easter eggs. Well worth the price of admission.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: I had no idea what I was getting myself into when I started Filament.  I generally enjoy difficult puzzle games, but I wasn't emotionally prepared to struggle so hard so early on!  It's been really fun to figure out all the rules of the puzzles and to discover little secrets here and there.  I don't want to say too much for spoilers, but so far the game has good puzzles and an interesting story and I recommend it to anyone who likes challenging puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing puzzle  game, but really really hard. It can be the Dark Souls of puzle game, now that everythig is measure by Dark Souls ^^.Huge amount of puzzles, lot of diferent mechanics, but again, very very hard.Have an interesting story, but its like Lost. lot of "what will happen next?", but its a "think your own end" gameHave enough content to be be buyed at full price, but, be carefull, its diabolic hard, so if you are not a patient, thorough and stubborn person, you may drop the game and its not a cheap game
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Game starts out simple - rope is tethered to you, walk around towers, light up all the towers.  But wow!  They really go a lot of places with it.  The music is great and the story is surprisingly compelling.  Fair warning though, some of the puzzles are quite hard, which can be frustrating if you aren't willing to look up hints / solutions when you get stuck.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful, absolutely beautiful story, visuals and OST.The puzzle mechanics are simple in essence but can create really complex puzzles. Not done with all of them yet, but pretty close to the end, and not using the help button has been a challenge, although I managed. Many of the puzzles require taking a break and trying again with a fresh mindset and forgetting the way you previously thought the solution would look like. Not only the order of circling the pillars is very difficult to determine, it is very difficult to foresee how the path travelled will affect the angle of the "rope" which then again will make it possible to go through some hoops and loops when a slightly different path would not leave enough space due to only the slight change in the angle of the "rope". Must have taken ages of planning.Definitely play this if you enjoyed Witness, this is very similar game atmospherically, even though the settingis quite different and puzzles don't use the environment in the same way. The music, have to reiterate, is just such a masterpiece, I listen to it doing other stuff constantly (definitely get the soundtrack edition for this, it's not much more and support the devs). The sadness in it, combined with the story of the game is just.. touching in so many ways. Filament / 10
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Too hard for me. Requires massive brain to play (which I don't have). The game has a problem of ramping up the difficulty too drastically. When you enter a new area, you get to learn a new type of puzzles. But after the first two levels, the game immediately gives you a complex one, while you're still trying to figure out how exactly the new puzzle type work. Imagine you just learned the multiplication table and then the teacher gives you a 3-digit multiplication question. That's sorta how it felt when I played this game. Most of the time, I solved the puzzles by somewhat brute forcing. So when I finally solved it, I just felt tired and not satisfied at all.I think the difficulty curve should be adjusted and more easy levels should be implemented in each sections to make the game easier to digest and feels more satisfying to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: This game *almost* gets there for me. I love the tone, setting, and art style, but the puzzles just aren't that fun. I'm curious to know what happens in the story, but I think I'm done playing because the puzzles become more and more of a slog the deeper into the game you get. The central mechanic is interesting, but the more challenging puzzles require a lot of trial and error and don't give that satisfying sense of accomplishment when you solve them -- it's more of an "oh, okay, I guess that was right" feeling.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of different 'puzzle' types to be found here. But never once did I feel like I was really completing puzzles as much as I was brute forcing a combination. Which is a shame. I kept waiting for the moment when it clicked, but it never did.Story seems interesting and the atmosphere is great! It's a shame that the core gameplay revolves around such tedious puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: So many puzzles. Puzzles everywhere. It gets addicting. A few of the mechanics are a bit annoying, and a handful of things in the game really obscure, not clear or have really confusing clues. The story pulls you along, but they designed is to you end up reading the same "emails" over and over which is also annoying. Overall, because of the over 300 puzzles definitely still worth picking up.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed playing this game. The mechanics are well thought-through and the main ideas allow for surprisingly interesting variations. It has a lot of depth and manages to avoid getting boring and repetitive due to little tweaks in the puzzles. Although many other reviews mark this as a difficult game, it felt very intuitive for me. Yes, you could sit down and think each solution through on paper first, but just winging it with what feels right will almost get you there. All in all, beautifully executed game concept.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Unique connect-all-pins puzzle game that makes you drag a cord through a maze of pilars where you have to touch all of them without getting tangled up. There are many different variations of the puzzles and the puzzles themselves are a challenge to complete.Between the puzzles you explore a space-ship whit a voice over explaining what happened on board, plus a lot of backstory in the form of email/chat logs on terminals scattered through the ship that you unlock bit by bit by solving the puzzles.Some puzzles are really hard to solve and require a bit of trial and error to get an understanding of the layout. Though if a puzzle seems too hard you can try a different area of the space-ship first.May feel tedious at times as you can get stuck on puzzles easily and overview is missing at times, but a definite yes if you like to have a casual puzzler with a steep learning curve.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Inherently, the main puzzle mechanic have very large search space. Exhaustive search is the only reliable strategy. Pattern recognition only applies on small scale. Unfortunately for you, the developers failed to sufficiently restrict neither the search space nor search time. Many levels are unnecessary big and additional puzzle mechanics worsen the problem. Trying out a solution by moving the character is time consuming.  I highly suspect that the main puzzle mechanic have exponential or factorial the time complexity. This can quickly become intractable even for computers. The developers really should have taken account of time complexity when making this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: If you wanna get a good puzzler with an (arguably) even better setting and story to boot, get Filament. Since Filament is definitely at its strongest when you go in blind, I'd call the following spoiling yourself. So take heed.To get a bit more specific: the primary puzzle-game is great, although some of the latter puzzles can turn into pure trial and error, and not so much puzzle-solving - that's not to say that a lot of the puzzles will have you feeling like a genius for figuring them out, and overall I had a lot of fun completing the game.The part that, to me at least, might be even better is the environmental puzzles. They are a bunch of optional, tough but extremely satisfying puzzles to solve, as they require you to recognize patterns and solve systems in the quasi-open world of the game. Finding and solving most of these throughout my playthrough was definitely one of the highlights. Like the main-puzzles however, some of these are also absolutely ludicrously tough to figure out, and so ultimately I turned to a walkthrough to get the last 10 or so done - which is of course unfortunate.Additionally, the story and setting is absolutely phenomenal and was definitely made the experience much more fulfilling.Overall, I got more than my money's worth, and I'd recommend Filament to others who want a good puzzler with an intriguing story to boot.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Even if you want to make a difficult puzzle game, even if the only way to solve the puzzles are trial and error just don't make a individual puzzle so long that there are 50 ways to start the puzzle and you discover 30 minutes in that you should lite one point 34 moves before and now change the whole strategy and if even that's the right start, better to make different kinds of puzzle than make a puzzle with 4 mechanics and the individual ones too long, the secrets are neat but the puzzles get ridiculous
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: The game shines with quite the depth, as well as insanely convoluted puzzles, and meta-puzzles, where you need to obtain several clues from various other parts of the game. The overall complexity made me think of the game Fez several times.The overall effort is pretty amazing. However, one should be aware that solving all puzzles (even with a guide) is quite the commitment.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal game. I've done 50% of the puzzles so far. They come in sets of 10 to 20 and each set adds something different to the core mechanic. The variations force you to think about the same puzzle in new ways. Some variations lead me to new understandings of the core mechanic.What's more, the atmosphere is top notch. The visual structure, the voice acting, the music, and the attention to detail taken in populating the game with small hints of the ships crew and their past.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: It's a cool idea for a puzzle game. They have all the atmosphere and graphics, but it could have been made as a minimalist puzzle game. Most of the time is spent solving puzzles of a similar nature. I would suggest waiting for a sale, so the price is more in line with other puzzle games. You basically drag a cable through a series of pillars, and you have to touch some and not touch others, and touching some opens doors to reach others. It's all about logically planning the route. You never die or fail, you can just back up a little and keep trying, or hit R to restart the puzzle at the beginning. Don't expect adventure-type play.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Every level-based puzzle game has a few rooms that are monstrously difficult. You'll sit there for hours trying to figure it out, feeling like you've tried everything, while knowing perfectly well that you have not. It consumes every ounce of your brainpower until you solve it, and when you finally do, it feels like you've been released from a years-long prison sentence, and you are finally free to enjoy the world again.This game only has those levels.10/10 my brain is toothpaste oozing from my ears and I love it
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolute gem of a game! Other reviews have said exactly this but it really is half Tacoma and half The Witness so if you like unravelling space mysteries AND solving increasingly complex, seemingly-simple puzzles that you gradually realise spill out into the overworld then this is for you!Also to reiterate what a whole bunch of other reviews say: this game is *brain-melting* and will make you feel a lot more stupid than you probably are.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: If you are stubborn and like hard puzzles, then this is for you. If not, you will probably get frustrated soon and give up. The graphics are beautiful and the voice acting is great. The story is captivating and the non-linear story-telling is interesting. Some annoying spelling mistakes, but one could argue that they are intentional since they are in the characters' mails and notes.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Filament is certainly not for everyone. Puzzles might feel overwhelming and excruciatingly difficult, but every time you finish a set of them the sensation of completion is worth it. So if you’re ready for your brain to boil a little bit, while solving what might be one of the most unique puzzles you’ll ever see, give it a try. The concept behind these knot-weaving tasks is really flexible MOST times and is definitely worth checking out.Now, the details. Puzzle-solving is indeed rewarding most of the time, but sometimes it feels like  some in-between simpler levels are missing and you encounter a task that seems a bit unintuitive, since you’re missing some necessary experience.Also, though flexibility and variability might be a good thing, there are times when it’s hard to realize when you can pass through a particular place and when you can.I’ve seen people complain that gameplay is basically a rando solution search algorithm in your execution, but I do not think so. While some of the gameplay involves trial and error, this is not the whole deal. Puzzles require an understanding of a bigger picture and of smaller details at the same time. You need to approach them from different perspectives and apply different techniques. There is also the Witness-like search for environmental puzzles. It’s undoubtedly more enjoyable than the main part of the game, since the majority of them does not require you to think too much, but there are some clever ones too. You can also look for little cards with similar purpose, but searching for them is akin to pixel hunting.Music is something that's really bad. I’ve counted two-three distinct tracks and they grow old fast. The in-puzzle music, I think, is supposed to invoke a feeling of progression and pondering, which kinda pisses me off when I get stuck on a level for too longUnfortunately, I can’t say anything about the story. It is conveyed to you when you complete a set of puzzles, and you can probably imagine the level of my mental fatigue at those points.Visual part is ok, it’s simple, descriptive and does the job it needs to do.I’ve noticed at least one frequent bug: when rewinding, the robot’s cable can get stuck on walls. Nothing fatal - when you’re rewinding you most probably want to reset the level anyways.Overall, Filament is mildly flawed, but rewards patience, experimentation, careful planning and attentiveness. I urge you to give it a go, if you’re not scared of highly difficult puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Hard puzzle game, not for everyone, persistence required! The story told through text and narration was interesting and got me thinking. Would have given up the game half way through without it to be honest!In some respects this game is like The Witness, in that it teaches the puzzle rules by offering simple puzzles to figure it out on your own then ramping the complexity up. I enjoyed the more logical puzzles where once I'd figured out a rough order of what I needed to do, then also figure out how to do that with getting tangled up. However, there are a lot of puzzles that require solving by trial and error, which were not that fun. Felt like I got most of the way through the game without a walkthrough, but I lost patience at the end with the super complex puzzles, fair play to those who could do them on their own!
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the "Hard" discourage you from playing these puzzles. The music and immersion make playing this game absolutely stellar, even while you're struggling on a puzzle or two. The game also does an AMAZING job of introducing rules for puzzles and you can very easily leave a puzzle and try a separate one. That's not to say some of the puzzles aren't difficult. The game starts off easy but has a very high skill cap, while curiosity gives you incentive to keep going. Only reason I stopped playing was because I got to something close to the ending (I think?) and the puzzles got to a difficulty level that was too high for me, but I don't think I got past 50% of the stuff this game has hidden inside it.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked the puzzle style, it was different and creative and had a lot of cool variation and a nice difficulty progression (all very autodidactic instead of hand-holdy too).The music is very chill and relaxing and just yes.I also love the glimpses into the characters and universe, always nice when it feels like there's a reward for solving little 'extra' puzzles too, even if plenty of the corrupted were too much for me to bother with.I was very confused by the end but well. it just be like that sometime.All in all a very pleasurable experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say about Filament? A damn good game. If I would have to characterize it using other games I would say it's a cross between The Witness and The Talos Principle. The Witness for the style of the main puzzles where you basically do the same thing (connecting pillars), but you learn different mechanics that influence how you do that; as well as for the environmental puzzles. The Talos Principle for the atmosphere and the touch on deep philosophical questions.Add to that some secret puzzles that will really bring out your netbook in order to solve them. And out of those only a few of them feel really unfair if you don't know certain things from the real world (the transistor puzzle is the best example for this). But I can forgive those because they're not the main point of the game and the rest is wonderful.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Get this game if you enjoyed The Witness.It doesn't always help to compare one game to another, and this is no clone of The Witness, but it shares its epic scale. Scratch the surface, and you will be losing yourself down Rabbit holes and discovering layers of complexity within the environment.Although each set of puzzles take on a new set of rules, they are all a riff on a common simple mechanic: join together a set of pillars in the right order. My experience is that some Puzzle sets click easily in the mind and are solved in a few fluid strokes in a number of seconds, while others are a struggle of trying numerous permutations that can take hours. All the puzzles however are solvable, and in those head banging wanna throw the controller out the window moments, it is worth remembering that.(There is also a hints system available in game)Although the puzzles are the main focus, I recommend taking the time to follow the story, which I found well written and emotionally affecting.In the answer to the question "Can a Puzzle game have too many Puzzles in it?", the answer in both The Witness and Filament is a resounding Yes.  Good god, the last sets of Puzzles were nearly the straw that broke my will. 67 hours I put into this game, sixty....seven...hours.Don't say I didn't warn you.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: There is a Sprint Toggle Button for Puzzles that the game doesn't tell you about (Shift on Keyboard).Would have been nice to know about before you accidentally found out 15 hours in.The Puzzles are good, stimulating and fun in a challenging way, but the story is based on an unreliable narrator where you basically only get the true story in a community guide.But all that doesn't matter when you know a solution to a Puzzle and it takes you 30% longer than it otherwise would have because the UI doesn't tell you about the Sprint Button.The Story presents itself as intriguing, making you find the puzzle Pieces yourself, but the thing is that gimmick doesn't work when you need 95% of the pieces for the story to make any sense and is otherwise gibberish.Since I had decent fun cutting my teeth on the puzzles it's still an overall good for me, but the story and the F-ING SPRINT BUTTON YOU CANNOT IMAGINE HOW FRUSTRATING THIS IS LIKE WHAT THE HE---
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: One of the more difficult and unique puzzle games that I've played. It's simple at its core but but there are a ton of different mechanics added to keep it interesting. 1. Wrap a wire around each pillar2. Wrap a wire around each pillar a certain number of times3. Don't let the wire touch certain pillars4. Make the wire go between two pillars a certain number of times.5. Wrap multiple wires around different colored pillars.6. Wrap a single group of pillars at a time.7. Some pillars can only be touched after previous ones.etc.It's a cute game with decent chill music and a slightly amusing story. There's also some collectibles and what seems like a final puzzle that you are working towards.My only complaint is that the puzzles are mostly solved through trial and error because there's way too many possible solutions. You can also miss a solution very slightly because of your first move and then you have to redo the whole thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: The music is amazing, and the puzzles are intuitive and engaging. It doesn't go through a ton of tutorials, instead you figure out how the puzzles work as you go, but the mechanics involved are intuitive and simple enough that that works, while still allowing challenging and engaging puzzles to be crafted.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really great puzzle game. The puzzles are similar to the witness, but I do think that later on there isn't very many strategies you can apply to solve them. The last puzzles seem to be trial and error, I could totally have missed something. I absolutely loved the meta puzzles. I really don't want to spoil anything, so stop reading here. There was an insane twist ending, I couldn't figure out what happened so I went and read some theories, which helped a bit. The theorized ending was actually very sad :/ I personally don't like the stories that end with more questions, It's probably better from a game design perspective. I really wish there was some sort of true ending after getting all meta puzzles, emails, and voice recordings.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Over time, the vast majority of puzzles in games have gotten easier. Bucking that trend is what makes Filament so great! There's zero explanation, zero hand holding, and zero hints. Just hundreds upon hundreds of (mostly) intuitive puzzles that will easily absorb dozens upon dozens of hours of your time. The variety of puzzle types throughout is phenomenal, with each section exploring a new set of rules, or a combination of the rules you've learned. By the end the complexity is insane! Filament knows what it wants to be: a long form puzzle game. In doing so, it finds some very rare air atop the puzzle game genre, reminding me of very few games outside of The Witness. Its challenge will make your brain grow and turn to mush repeatedly, in the best possible way.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, I usually mute the in game audio and put on some other music to chill to and only turn on the game audio for the dialogue.Very relaxing to just mess around with, ran around completing the easy levels first and then came back for the harder ones later, it can get frustrating, but fairly so.One of the best puzzle games I have played.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: The wrap around puzzles in this game get real difficult real fast. They get more and more complex as more and more rules are introduced. The game doesn't hold your hand on how these rules work and trusts that the player can figure it out on their own by introducing it in a simple situation. Very reminiscent of the The Witness including The Witness' spoiler mechanic but in a different way. If you are looking for something different from the usual sokoban style puzzle games, Filament has got you covered.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: What a charming and fun game solving puzzles and finding out what happened to the crew on a giant space ship. Filament has some really good a varied puzzles that will make you want to solve without being frustrating. The key is to wrap a cord around these modules in a specific way in order to power up a certain section of the ship. Great backstory too. Highly recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game, and has a lot more content than you would expect for a $17 game.The story is engaging, and the environments are excellently designed to provide extra narrative.There are a lot of different mechanics to play around with, and the puzzles can get pretty challenging. However, it seems a lot of the challenge comes from complexity and obscurity. For me, a good puzzle is like untying a knot, where you come to small conclusions to unravel the bigger picture. A lot of the levels seem to throw a lot of pointless complexity at you out of the gate (pointless in the sense that you need to test the possible routes, but they end up being obviously false once you do). Some mechanics are more guilty of this than others, but it seems to be a theme.There's also a lack of exposure to emergent behavior from the mechanics, which is what separates good games from the great like The Talos Principle, Stephen's Sausage Roll, and Baba is You. It's still there, but the game seems to rely more on modifying the mechanics or introducing new ones instead, leaving you with the feeling that there was more the learn before moving on. In summary, there is a lack of elegance in a lot of the levels, however it still provides a fun challenge.My only other negative is that I got stuck for several hours because a bug wouldn't let me pass the level even though I had the correct solution. It mysteriously fixed itself at some point after trying the only possible solution for the umpteenth time.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommended. But be warned, it is hard sometimes.If you are into sudoku style puzzles, this is for you. Very chalanging. Most new types of puzzles do have nice introduction, and usually the difficulty increases slowly which is good, but there are spikes in progression, which can make you stuck. Just take a break, and come back to it again. Some puzzles do have more than one solution too, but differences in variations are small between these solutions.Not sure how many puzzles are there, but around 150. Game gives about 10 of each types, then throws you a new mechanic, or a net set of 10, that are on another level. In later stages, puzzles combine mechanics from previous types, which is really fun and hard. Later stages also involve lore of the game, with some codes, that would be required to solve some puzzles. Also later on, there are some crazy stages, with moving things, which I didn't get too much yet, but looks fun. There is a bit of branching in what you can do after completing each section of puzzles, so it is not fully linear, and can switch between them.There is no hint system in the game, so you need to be determined, try many times, or use internet to find some hints, when you are really super stack. At least that is what I did.The game works technically also work very well. I play on Linux, and it uses 64-bit Unity, and Vulkan! 110 fps easily on 1920x1920 screen (AMD Fury X on Mesa 20.2.0). Keyboard and controller work flawlessly. Also in options one can switch the  "focus mode" to be a toggle.There are subtitles (can be changed in options), as well support for color blindness, so colors are indicated by various icons.Music is ok, but there is not much variety, and it is a bit monotone, great for relaxing, but could be tedious too. On the other hand environment sounds are good, and voice acting is very good. There is real world and world of puzzles, and a bit of lore / story (via dialog, and pieces of story found on computers, or some items you can interact), which is nice.Graphics and other stuff are well polished. Puzzles doesn't seem boring or gimicky too much. You control the robot, and also have ability to restart the level, or do a rewind (like a continious undo), but I usually undo manually as I think about puzzles. There is also a top down view ("focus mode"), which shows entire puzzle (and your current attempt to solve) more in a grid fashion.I am not sure if there is level editor, because that would be cool, or some extra challanges (like time maybe, or shortest length for these that can be solved in many ways), but I know there are some hidden levels here and there.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: The story is nice. The puzzle are nice (some of them seem a bit far-fetched (Since the solution is not common).Some corrupted enigma are badly made. (I think particularly on the cipher card who is not really readable. So, how you want me to solve it if i can't read it correctly !)Anyway, it's a great game. It's worth the price. Some minors updates would have just made it more comfortable to play.The bridge puzzle are really too much difficult. Even if i've managed to handle most of the puzzle of the game, the bridge was really awfull to play. Not really fun. The ending need more explanation. Not enough. But i think than you keep it for a 2nd opus.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles are great and overall difficulty is pretty good. Though the last batch really is a bit of a slog.With just what is being told to you by the narration, you don't really get much out of the story and the ending doesn't really make any sense. So expect to be reading all of the log entries and finding the hidden ones, then connect the pieces for what turns out to be an amazing construct with a huge twist.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't expect a puzzle game about threading wire around nodes to be so intriguing.  I like puzzle games, but I sure am bad at them, but I keep coming back to it, because I want to know what happened to the crew aboard The Alabaster.  Completing puzzles unlocks text logs and emails sent from each crew member, and it's interesting to see the petty squabbles and panic behind each person.  It has the same problem as The Witness, in that being able to start any puzzle sequence is kind of a problem, since there are much harder types than others.  The music is nice and calming, very good Puzzle Game music.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really beautifully simplistic game, with focus on art story and gameplay. Easy to understand and navigate, with (really!) challenging puzzles and a story that's drawing me in (haven't finished yet), I also love the voice acting, it's really well done.The only drawback I found was that the story only advances when you complete a module of puzzled, and if you get stumped in them, the story will advance rather slowly and you'll lose track of where it stands.Other than that it's a game I wholeheartedly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Review written when I'm around 50% complete (IIUC).Decent puzzles, from easy to fairly hard, sometimes harder than they look.Story is kinda different, but I'm enjoying it so far.Graphics are reasonable, story mode graphics are slightly better than puzzle graphics.Worth buying if you like innovative puzzlers.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: While I do recommend this game overall, it's with one caveat: contrary to what other reviews say, it will not scratch quite the same itch as The Witness. There are similarities, certainly, but the core philosophy with which the puzzles are designed is very different. In The Witness, the challenge was often not in actually drawing the line, but in figuring out what even constituted a valid solution; it joyed in constantly changing the rules to perplex you. In Filament, the puzzle is very much in the puzzle itself. While there is an element of deducing the rules of the puzzles through experimentation, Filament spends much longer on each of its concepts, so it is an occasional rather than constant challenge. While I enjoy The Witness's puzzles slightly more, they're both very well crafted - they just have slightly different appeals. If it sounds like the kind of puzzles you like, then by all means give Filament a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Great puzzle game, Puzzles scale from 30 IQ to 300 IQ.The story and the music are epic, I just had to know what happened.I would highly recommend you try going through as much of it as possible without a guide. Use brute force tactics. Don't give up. Wrapping_3_03 and Constellationwrapping_02 literally gave me nightmares.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: My total time played was in just two sittings... Yup, thats about 16hrs almost non stop with the odd food break.The puzzles and the emerging narrative is that absorbing. When first introduced to the puzzle mechanic of wrapping a cable around numerous pillars, it looks incredibly simple. Oh how cunningly deceptive the devs are. And masters at puzzle crafting as just when you start to get comfortable, you get a humbling slap in the face.They keep changing up the rules, introducing new and fresh takes to keep you on your toes. I am almost certain many were driven mad trying to solve them (I know I came close).Besides the meticulous puzzle designs, the narrative that runs through bit by bit is brilliantly delivered by Abigail Turner. It feels natural and conversational, which makes it all the easier to empathise when things take a dramatic turn.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: i started this game after an exhausting day at work.  I played for 6 hours.  This game was bought on a whim because the graphics looked nice and it was cheap during the Summer sale.  Holy cow I am floored by the polish.  For being a simple puzzle game I don't understand why the graphics are so refined, why so much effort was put into the writing, and how they found such a great voice actor for the main character you interact with.  I never expected it to be this good.I tried to race through the puzzles as an "I am smart!" competition.  They're really creative.  You have to illuminate certain posts in the right order, or understand that pairs are linked together, or complete both colors.  The ones that really got me were the drawings on the floor where it's saying you can only make a connection between these posts, but not those over there.I got stumped and I went looking around.  I found just the right level of storybuilding detail tucked into the smaller rooms of the ship, and I spend 2 hours just reading through logs and emails to understand the crew.This is really cool game.  It is absolutely worth playing, and the devs should be very proud.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Pleasantly challenging! No time limit for the puzzles, just pure patterns, lines, and the nitty grittiness of good puzzling. I spent longer than I thought on this game, and was pleasantly surprised by it. The story was lacking a bit for me, but the atmosphere, the color palette, and the soundtrack were pleasant. I'll be honest, my initial reaction was that the puzzles were too linear, making it difficult for me to understand the patterns. After spending enough time in the game, I saw the progression of difficulty and used trial and error to help me understand the patterns presented. It felt tedious at times but always felt itching to play more. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Charming, challenging and surprisingly engaging.I'm not usually one for puzzle games, because I'm terrible at them, but I actually found myself having a lot of fun with this game. The puzzles are very challenging, but do make sense and feel fair. What caught me off-guard, however, was the story. I actually found myself very interested in the story of the game, and while I don't love the ending, there's enough mystery to keep you going if you're someone not particularly interested in the puzzles, like I am. The soundtrack is also lovely, and the art is unique and charming.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun puzzles. You'd think the solving style would get old fast, but the variety implemented into the different puzzle types keeps it fresh. Also liked that the game uses intuitive tutorials, i.e. simple puzzles to teach you the rules without spoon feeding. If you're one for bonus lore secrets, the game delivers on this front too. Personally, I just care about the main game-play, which was more than sufficient.Only issue I ran into (shortly after release, so maybe fixed by now?) was when running to certain rooms to progress the story, nothing would happen. After a quick game reset things worked fine, but other than this it was a smooth and stimulating experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Simple controls, mind boggling puzzles.Each "set" of levels have their unique twists to the basic puzzle, that'll keep you entertained without the puzzles simply increasing its step count.The world/story is apt, nothing mind blowing but enough to set the atmosphere.Cleverly hidden environment puzzles are also a nice break from the main puzzles (though somewhat tedious at times).A very nice, quiet , non-input heavy puzzle game that'll keep you busy and coming back for more.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game. The graphics are just amazing, the controls work well and the puzzles are interesting, neiter too easy nor to difficult (some parts are very tricky and it's likely to quit in the process). It's a really stylish and balanced game with amazing soundtrack as well. Really like it :)Also to have a story accompanying the puzzles is kinda awesome as well. Definetly a must have.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Very good puzzle game with some rock hard puzzles. By some I mean most. You connect to these anchors and you move the little lightbulb around so that your cable touches the pillars, you can't cross over the cable and when they are all lit up the door opens, straight forward enough. The puzzles get harder with more rules, you must join the same colours, the cable must pass through a gate and finally your brain melts.As you complete pillars, you find cards that unlock messages and logs to figure out the story and its a good story. The crew is well written and Juniper adds a good companion to keep the story ticking over. You can unlock the pillars in nearly any order and with the fact that the story is in emails and messages means that you might find it a bit fragmented. it would be great if there was an easier way in the computer to read the story in an order, instead of going from mailbox to mailbox and week to week. There are also corrupted messages that can be unlocked by noticing patterns of cables etc.The new hint system is brilliant and really helps. It gives you two hints to get you over a hurdle and the number resets if you exit the puzzle, so for the ones where two hints is not enough I would remember where I was, exit and go back in and use the hints again. There are also a couple of great guides with visuals of the completed puzzles if you are really stuck.The ship looks beautiful to walk around, and they did a great job of making it looked lived in. If you like puzzle games, this is a must buy
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: I was not expecting this to be a story-rich puzzle game, but even though I started for the puzzles, I've actually found the most fun piecing together the story. The puzzles quickly became difficult - I consider myself an experienced puzzler and have really been wracking my brain on many of these. The community has some really helpful guides in a variety of levels from hint all the way to full solutions, though the in-game hint system was confusing. The puzzles are creative and end up with some delightful twists that have kept them fresh. There are some really great environmental puzzles that are simply world-building, and they require some really out of the box thinking. Overall, I recommend this for even experienced puzzle gamers.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the setting of the game and the slowly resolving (hopefully) mystery. I am halfway through the game and I wonder how much of what happened will be revealed. It's really motivating to finish a few puzzles and have a bit of a story reveal as reward.The puzzles have different themes but require similar thinking and lack some variety for my personal taste. Then again I've never solved puzzles like these before and so it's nice to have a whole bunch of them to test your wits.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I thought the game was pretty good. The game is usually pretty nice about introducing some nice game mechanics. It's ~similar~ to the witness in the sense that they give you a vaguely similar basic puzzle mechanic (start at the beginning, satisfy the requirements, get to the exit), and then immediately gives you a ton of interesting variations on it. I also enjoyed running around in the hub world, and the story was engaging (you do need to play quite a bit to figure it all out).That being said, there's a few issues. There were some levels with elegant solutions, and others where the solution felt cheesed. Some awkwardly placed pillars (a small minority) will sometimes light or not light depending on how you run past them. The puzzles feel like they spike in difficulty a bit chaotically. Plus the game started to glitch out for me in the late game (the game froze on me 2-3 times, and I got flashes of the station from out of bounds). None of these absolutely ruin the game, but sometimes make it a bit annoying to play.Overall, if you like puzzle games with a bit of story to them, I'd say this is a pretty solid game to get.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: This game was absolutely beautiful and I enjoyed every second of it. The puzzle design is genius and incredibly frustrating to play, but the music was so calming it made even those frustrating moments relaxing. The story was incredible and I cried for a full hour at one point during my gameplay, which is not something I do over video games often much less for an hour. I got so into it, desperate to find out what happened, I stayed up until 8 AM just to try to finish it. I didn't that night, but if it weren't for the fact that I couldn't keep my eyes open, I would've. I bought the game 3 times, once for myself and twice for my friends, and I would absolutely do it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: W A R N I N G - If you play casual puzzle game you do not wanna play this.Filament is the hardest puzzle game I have ever played by a clear mile.I solved all the puzzles untill the bridge area and the puzzles although at times repetitive and hard were well balanced and started with easy ones to exsplain the mechanics.When I got to the bridge area I just had to give up and thats ok I have to problem when the game and its puzzles outsmart me.To be honest I suck at these kind of puzzles but in my opinion most of the players will struggle with bridge puzzles.You might think that I dislike this game but that is not the case.I like this game and think its on of the best puzzlers in recent years.It This is a definition of a hardcore puzzler and the hardcore puzzlers will love this game for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Filament is a fantastic indie puzzle game that plays very similarly to other fantastic indie puzzle game The Witness. You, a space traveler, board the Alabaster, and after a short intro section to show you the ropes, are left to roam the ship and crack though anchors (where all of the puzzles in the game are contained) as you work to free the trapped pilot Juniper and figure out what went wrong. The game gives you free reign over the order in which you challenge the various areas of the game, which is where the comparisons to The Witness mostly come from. However, everything is in very close proximity, and it only takes a couple minutes to walk from one end of the ship to the other. The puzzles, which have you controlling a little robot connecting a lit wire (a Filament) between pillars until all pillars in the room are lit up, are also very well-designed. Each anchor introduces new mechanics and restrictions that make you think differently about how you solve each puzzle, and the openness of the ship allows you to leave puzzles that you're struggling on, and come back to them when you finish. Furthermore, the Bridge, which is where Filament's endgame lies, takes the concepts introduced in the earlier rooms to the next level and pushes them beyond what you might have thought to be possible. Furthermore, the story is extremely engaging, and I would constantly go hunt for story bits whenever I was struggling on a tricky puzzle.Pros-Great puzzle design (what else does a puzzle game really need?)-Interesting puzzle variations-The Bridge-Lore is very engaging-Juniper's presence helps your journey feel less lonely-Being able to leave and come back to troublesome anchors is really helpful-Exploration doesn't feel like a chore-Soundtrack is very relaxing-The lore has catsCons-You have to clear a large amount of anchors before gaining access to the bridge, but the game doesn't do a great job of telling you how many-The lore is so good that some of the anchors felt like a chore to work through-Especially difficult anchors made that lore even harder to access-You do not get to interact with the cats mentioned in the storyIf you liked The Witness, you will like Filament. Filament is a stellar puzzle game, as it combines great puzzle design with an engaging story and an overworld that is consistently fun to explore. Every puzzle game fan should pick this game up.

_childDocuments_.review: Having a great time with this game so far! The puzzles are challenging and there are a ton of different kinds of them throughout the game, it looks like each section of the ship introduces something new to learn and master. The music is really nice and the visuals are also great. Overall a fantastic puzzler and I'm looking forward to getting to the proper brain teasers
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: A puzzle game reminiscent of Witness framed within a story similar to Tacoma, Filament will test your spatial reasoning skills while providing snark and exposition via the well voice acted Juniper. The spaceship you explore is well realised with spaces that feel lived in and it is all rendered lovingly. If you enjoy digging through text logs and emails, there is also a hefty amount of writing for you to sink your teeth into and learn about the crew. Between the puzzles and the story, Filament offers a lot to those willing to fully immerse themselves in its world of corporate expeditions, crew relationships and mind bending puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: It is difficult not to compare the style of puzzles to The Witness.  Many similarities and differences, but anyone who played that will feel at home here, I would say the puzzles here are less abstract and mechanics of puzzles are introduced more clearly, but both games require interesting ways of thinking.  The environmental puzzles and secrets are really intelligent, and the environment itself has so much detail and love poured into it.  Finding objects around the ship is fun and there is great sense of humour in the written text.Some very casual players may find this tricky, maybe it would be nice to have a 'hint' option to at least show the starting pillar after puzzling over a level for a while.EDIT: THE DEVS ADDED A HINT OPTION in update, legends.All in all it is a difficult but strangely relaxing puzzler.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: The closest comparison is The Witness. The core idea is incredibly simple, but the game cleverly builds upon it in many different ways. And unlike many other puzzle games, Filament nails “tutorial” puzzles: they are informative and small enough, but not obvious. Also it’s just fun to explore game’s environment, uncover its story and trying to solve some of its optional hidden challenges.If you have any interest in puzzle games, don’t miss this one. Filament is one of the best entries in the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: Filament is an amazing puzzle game.  Easily 40+ hours of content for under $20.  Variety, secrets, challenge, with a solid plot as a bonus.  If you enjoy The Witness, you will like Filament...  there are a lot of similarities, and it's clear that game was a major inspiration for this.  But it stands on its own.  The Filament Corporation is waiting for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: An array of mechanics will  keep you jumping with joy, pounding the table with frustration while you attempt 300+ deceptively complex line puzzles. An array of varying mechanics shine bright as the game progresses.An overarching "walking simulator" sub-plot breaks up the sure to arise frustration from some of the games harder puzzles. A hefty bounty of trinkets scattered around the ship add an extra level of challenge to players seeking to uncover the full truth of what happened upon the Alabaster.10/10. Great ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game.
_childDocuments_.name: Filament

_childDocuments_.review: The initial puzzle premise feels like it will wear out its welcome pretty quickly, but it's iterated on in many interesting ways and I was particularly delighted to find a late game room which contained a panoply of new ideas and extra-challenging puzzles just when I thought the game was out of ideas. Piecing together the narrative is both a puzzle in and of itself, but also a potent motivator to push through any roadblocks and uncover more of the story. The characters are delightful and I've greatly enjoyed my time on the Alabaster, piecing together the mystery that brought me here while I soak in the atmosphere.
