_childDocuments_.review: Okay... in overall, I enjoy this game a lot. The futuristic artwork mixed in a design of multi-culture even brings back some nostalgia on me, reminds me of a futuristic place called  in . The characters reminds me of a short machinima they made in a place called  in Second Life too (about 10+ years ago), if you are interested, you can find the short video under the title  on youtube...  And those "Cyber Junkie" reference in the game feels eerily real when we've seen the real "cyber addict" in Second Life... These guys actually exist, and over two decades by now...The game has a really nice story to tell, and told it well imo. The puzzles are pretty meh imo, not hard just irritatingly troublesome, like making a long way between the maps and going back and forth places to get things done (intentionally designed that way). So most of the time we are on the move rather than standing there solving puzzles. And talking about move, although this is a point and click adventure game that uses a mechanism similar to most classic point and click games we've seen. It still has it's problem, like unable to recognize the distance between object, so it's always using "walk" when it should be using "run" making some of the interaction.. well... not friendly. And minor stuffs like won't continue walking when holding down mouse button.. yeah,, minor stuffs that doesn't really effect the overall game play i guess.The hint system is like none-existence... do not bother to use it and it won't be telling you anything useful. Even the Spacebar to highlight stuffs like in most puzzle games doesn't really work well in this one, that whole part is half-heartedly made... yup badly made. You might actually goes easier to spot the items without them highlighting it to blend into the color of the background making them even harder to spot. And no, space bar doesn't show interaction points, they just show you items that can be picked up. So don't waste your time enabling it, do the game without it and save time for a 2nd run to grab the achievements (that require a run with no hint). Trust me, it's easier without the hint system.

_childDocuments_.review: Video Review: Score 6/10Play as Tina a nine-year-old orphan and her nanny Bot Sam-53, Living in 2062 Neo Berlin a dark megalopolis controlled by major corporations, and where many of the inhabitants spend most of their time and are addicted to virtual space. A VR world to help them escape from the terrible reality's they all live. Tina and Sam are just trying to survive until they find a hidden message encrypted in to Sam’s hard drive, one video of her father needing her to set out on a quest to save the city and its people.Encodya first and foremost is your classic point and click adventure game with finding objects and solving puzzles by using the items or combining them. There can be some head stumpers throughout your journey, If you play on the easy difficulty you can ask Sam for hints but don’t think they will always be helpful. Through my playthrough I needed at minimum 20 hints to figure things out, now this could just be because I haven’t played a classic point and click game in a few years I believe it was 2017 when I went back and played “day of the tentacle” but this has a lot of the same classic elements from the classic Lucas arts games. Another element to the game is being able to switch between Tina and Sam, where Tina can Do some of the smaller things and Sam needing to do the heavy lifting it’s a nice shake up to bring two character in to the fold. The downside that I was not a fan of was the size of certain sections of the map. Going through the game you will find areas that are larger than what you can see on your screen, that once you get closer to the edge, the camera slightly pans. This really messed me up in the beginning because I was Kinda lost on what was going on and couldn’t find the items I needed till I noticed there was more to the area then what I could see. Also, in tight narrow hallways you have to do a lot of extra clicking to get down the hall because the hall is not fully in frame, instead doing the camera shift leading to Tina doing a lot of stop go motions instead of just going to the end of the hall. It wouldn't be an issue if it followed fluidly with Tina but its slower than her and leads to the stopping.  Story wise, Its nice not the greatest I have seen but the overall plot has some nice dips and curves in it. The ending was a nice touch to the game but was also kind of expected. It's not going to invoke a lot of feeling from you but it delivers decent world building and more world building if you talk to the inhabitants of Neo Berlin, giving their stories and struggles. The backstory of some of the individuals are well detailed and they give the characters life but I do wish they would have given a little more story behind the city but I guess who is really going to be talking about that to a 9-year-old girl.Graphically it has its highs and its lows for me the landscape and backgrounds remind me of an updated monkey island or star trek with well detailed almost hand painted look in some areas.Overall, the world around the characters looks amazing. The Characters are where I have my negatives, they look plastic and really remind me of the mid 2000 cheap strait to DVD 3d animation movies that ripped off bigger Animation companies like Kira the brave. It's just a stark difference it is really just jarring. The Sound is a plus in this game with great sound effects and music that gives great feeling to the game as long as you don’t look into tinas eyes.Encodya is not a bad game but not a great game, the mechanics to me are pretty solid maybe some tweaks need to be made but nothing game breaking. The story is what kind of made me think a little less of the game, it just feels like it was missing something, I don’t know what that something is but I didn’t feel it was complete, the character design I can see that getting to people but I was able to overlook it after about an hour because I was truly enamored by the environments. Encodya I think is for people who love the classic point and click games with that difficulty and accomplishment of finding the solution, The negatives in that aspect will disappear, but if you are someone who dabbles in this genera you may not be so inclined to look away from the flaws, but that decision is up to you I had a head splitting fun time and if this game does look interesting to you it about 5 to 8 hours of game play depending on how often you struggle because it took me about 8 hours they have set a price for the game 25 dollars which may be steep for people that are unsure of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice crafted game with a dystopic story about an orphaned, almost 10 years old girl with a nanny robot. The two live a low life in a futuristic city governed by a corrupt and arrogant major.Eventually they find out they have a mission given by her missing and now proclaimed-dead dad which changes the lives of everyone in the city.I like story games like this. There is no brute-force, blood or other violence caused by the player - remember, you control a 9.5 year old girl. Occasionally you have to do things using the robot but his programming also doesn't allow violence.Some puzzles are tricky and require looking for and using found resources, but there is nothing you have to think around more than one corner. Bad thing is the recources you need for a task can be everywhere where you have access to, so look around thoroughly.Achievements mention you can complete the game in less than four hours, but I really recommend to play it the first time the enjoying way - talk to everyone about everything and look everywhere and everything.

And after that you have to search again in that same hole. And the hints of the robot are so vague that only make sense after you've completed the mission. I don't have patience for these games. I won't be spending endless time moving the mouse over every inch of the screen and then imagine, try and discard every possible combination of objects. It feels more like climbing a mountain than playing a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Set in a Cyberpunk world, ENCODYA is a point and click adventure game where you can control 2 characters, Tina and her robot guardian SAM-53. Gameplay is not overly complicated with two modes available to choose from at the start, easy or hard. Playing on easy provides you with assistance and hints from SAM-53 if you are stuck on tricky puzzles or what to do next.  As with many point and click adventures, there are many ways things can be easily missed if you don't speak to or try options with both characters as each of the main characters have their own special skills and abilities. The game does have randomly generated puzzles that keeps the game interesting.Graphically, ENCOYDA is visually appealing to anyone that enjoys that dark cyberpunk feel, with many stunning locations to explore and incredible cinematic cutscenes.Characters you meet along the way are quite charming and funny. The game's voice acting is very well done.There are slight issues when controlling the characters, such as SAM-53. As he is a big character on screen, he can sometimes get in the way of important items that you might need to pick up.  Of course, moving him out of the way is always the best thing to do, but he can also get stuck if Tina is in his way.  This is not in any way a major issue, but can get be a little annoying at times.Music, sound effects, and voice acting in the game are of great quality and help set the vibe of exploring Neo Berlin.If you're a fan of point and click adventures set in a cyberpunk world, do give ENCODYA a go. You'll be pleasantly surprised in what you'll find waiting for you in Neo Berlin.You can also check out the first 40 mins of gameplay for ENCODYA here:

_childDocuments_.review: the difficulty options don't really balance things out properly. normal is too easy, hard is too esoteric.The latter offers no clues, or hints. the former gives you force-fed clues and hints, and highlights every object you can interact with ahead of time. there's no happy medium, and the solutions to the " puzzles " are often times as bizarrely out of place as you can think.It never told me I could combine items, or even why it might be a good idea to try it.There's also an issue I have where ( since it's a point and click ) having trouble navigating to stuff. Sure, you can doubnle click, and hold the mouse button down to speed up your character -but if you want to interact with a ting on the other side of the screen, your character will slowly plod over to it, and then use it. or you can double tap and hold mouse to bring them there, and interact with the object up close. same goes for navigation, you can double click the edge of a screen to instantly move ot next screen - but some screens are several times wider than 1 screen- so you can do the " hold mouse down to speed up the running " thing, only you hit the edge of the screen constantly, and have to triple tap and hold the mouse for short periods of time. Thanksfully, there doesn't seem to be too many areas built this way, but I'm only about 1.5 hours in.the puzzles, and clunky UI ( due to character swapping, movement, and the need to speed them up ) and the weirdly off-balance " difficulty " system make this a hard sell to ppl that aren't fond cof these antiquated PC era of P&C games. everything else is enjoyable. the art direction, the settings, and the atmosphere is good. Reminds me of Heart if Darkness in terms of visual style. if you liek P&C's this is for you. if you're into cyberpunk stuff, this may not be for you.

_childDocuments_.review: A game that gets progressively worse. Before anything else a wall-of-text disclaimer is shoveled to you face, something between trigger warning and code of conduct. Fine, fine, "no discrimination blah blah blah" let me play. Now into the game... soon you see "Mr Rupmf" poster on a wall and inspect it, protagonist comments "orange man bad". Repeat on every occasion. Ok ok developer doesn't like Drupmpf and decided to write a story evolving around him instead of creating their own character. Moving on. Clearly SAM is big strong looking robot who can solve tasks Tina can't. But but... item is too far, you say  with those long hands? It's stuck? Too heavy? Door is locked? You who look like skipped every leg day can't bend a simple piece of metal. At least you got quantum brains. Wait what, you CAN'T use that computer terminal because it's too COMPLICATED?  Just ♥♥♥♥♥♥ repurpose yourself then, as your only ability is to take half of the screen space. And why even have two characters if they can't work together? Even their private dialog is useless "hey how was your day?" How about "have you any ideas how to proceed?" (EDIT: I read somewhere that in easy mode SAM's dialog has more hints) Speaking of dialogs, as if these puzzles weren't unlogically hard enough, every response to wrong solution is simply "Wrong",  "No" or "That's not correct" without any hint of why.There's 30+ years of history of point and click and this game is collection of nothing learned with addition of contemporary BS.The praise- exemplary cell shaded graphicsThe nag- unoriginality- SAM is your co-op but mostly useless

_childDocuments_.review: Even if a lot of us can't play through this ourselves, we're going to need to watch someone else play it just to find out what happens.If you want to watch me embarrass myself playing the beginning of Encodya, click on the link above. Encodya is a beautiful world with good sound design that's marred by the typical point-and-click problems. Puzzles are obscure, paths are confusing, and unless you're already very familiar with the genre you'll be left bashing your head against a wall. The backgrounds seem way more detailed than needed even "taskless" floors are pretty. ▼ Which brings me to the issue about the same topic: They don't always . Like... you can like the general style or not - that's fine. But a background with extremely busy textures and animations is distracting - especially if it makes up 97% of most of the screens and the part you actually  is nowhere to be found. ▼▼ Not to mention how I got an immediate "Ihh, bah" feeling just by looking at the horrible lighting on Tina's face for the first time.▼▼▼ Gameplay: If usable objects are sometimes extremely obvious and the very next item can't even be found without an external guide because it literally disappears into the ground or background... That is just very bad game design. ▼▼▼ . So when the appearance of "pick me up's" is rare (1 to 3 every second screen on average) in comparison to the interactive's - which are at least 1 to 5 per screen - It is simply annoying and tiresome.▼▼▼ Characters: Every character feels incredibly stiff, because they all try to teach you a "politically correct moral" (except the Asian guy for some reason. Another piece of political correctness? Who knows), the animations don't really fit their style, all they do is talk. And for the size of the characters you'll see them in they are just not detailed enough. Plus... if you really want to make a game that has the premise of "English replaced the German language" you shouldn't put the voice actors with a horrible German accent into the beginning of a game. And pay them better so they actually try their best to feel the character (Looking at you, Eku).▼▼▼ Story: Somebody obviously ran out of time here - the end is too fast and... somewhat...  perfect.  The actual, short part that tells you about the game's title ("Encodya") is relatively interesting though – in context with the rest of the story it's a big missed opportunity here.▼▼▼ And lastly about the "Easter Eggs" (Not counting the collectibles here):They are  too German, even for me - a German. That entails mostly badly written 4th-wall-breaks and an obvious, constant "Just one more joke! LET'S ADD JUST ONE MORE JOKE"-pressure that will leave you stuck with an annoyed grimace after the third character- and approx. seventh object interaction. Not to mention the forced "OH THIS STREAMING ADDICTED YOUTH" moral which kept reappearing time and time again... Just... Urgh.

_childDocuments_.review: I once wrote a review for an online Indie magazine about this game (that to be said, I got it for free for review purposes). I gave it a bad rating and I was very straight-forward on what I did not like about Encodya. But the time passed, I got more experienced in the genre, and I thought "Maybe try it again and see if it is that bad at all". Well, yes and no. But yes.Back at the time I critizised a lot of things I would not critisize anymore. The graphics for example, I do not like them, but they are not bad either. Only Tina, main protagonist and "emotional centerpoint", looks like a doll straight out of a horror game. Her emotions don't reflect on her enormous face. But the athmosphere is okay. The Cyberpunk aspect is transported via rain, reflecting water puddles, a lot of neon and some flying cars, very cliché, but it does the job.The game's speed is another point, it is splitted in tiny areas that you cannot cross quickly because of loading times. Tina and Sam, her steady companion robot, at least can run. But the construction of the levels makes it hard to navigate what I would call seamless.So, these are the points that I am willing to accept. But there is no story that grasps me, no interesting world to explore. Everything focusses on the puzzles, the very core mechanic of a point and click adventure. But the puzzles feel like heavy rocks on your back, not like fun parts of the gameplay. They are annoying, exhausting. It always goes like this: enter an area - talk to everything - talk to the piece that must be opened/activated/etc. - talk to everything again - find someone who is willing to trade something useful - go and do tasks/find something for that person - success - return - repeat several times - open/activate the thing from the beginning. And all of that running and searching is not fun, it is a burden. There is no highlighting mode (at least I didn't find one, could be wrong though, but then some hidden achievements would lose their point), so every screen must be searched diligently. Most of the items that are needed just lie on the ground, with no reason at all why they are at that point whatsoever. That's just lazy puzzle-building! It feels endless until you do some progress and then it starts all over again, just with another map. The map areas do not feel connected, even the screens do feel like I passed a portal. I am disappointed by the design most of the time. And the riddles are tough, I used a Walkthrough Guide because otherwise I would have stopped playing after 20 minutes. There is no shame in using a guide, I did it to experience the story.But there is the next disappointment. I hate to say it, but the story sucks. It features a generic villain (Rumpf, the developers deny it is referring to Donald T., but I am sure this is the case) with a generic accent (I can tell, as a German myself) and a generic "power" goal that remains cloudy. The story never catched me, and Tinas tragic story never touched me neither. First, I liked Sam and his interactions with the world. But then the story progressed and it got more and more bumpy, the pace felt off, the emotions were off, the cutscenes felt like pieces of paper floating across the screen and I began to wish it's over. No, I wouldn't recommend playing it for the story. Plus, there is no escapism for me as it pictures a saddening political future that may not be as far as I wished. And funny or witty moments are scarce. No reference got me smiling, no items took me back. Everything feels forced, like it was build from a model kit.The conclusion is: My opinion didn't change. I cannot recommend this game. Please go and play   instead, it has much more of what Encodya is painfully lacking!

_childDocuments_.review: Picked this up on a special, and it definitely felt worth the price. It's an interesting world, effectively asking what it would like to be an orphan streetkid in 's cyberpunk dystopia. It makes some thinly-veiled political commentary, but the core message about media manipulation is worthwhile (if it's somewhat odd to be playing a game that's telling you not to spend too much time playing games...)Having two characters is an interesting choice, though I often found I would forget to try things with the other character, which perhaps took away a little from the immersion of roleplaying. A few of the puzzles are a bit janky (i.e. even after looking them up, I couldn't see how you were meant to have guessed the connections), and sometimes objects could do with differentiation from the often-busy backgrounds, but it lets you use hints and there are always walkthroughs.Typical for the genre, it is full of oddball humour and meta-jokes, including plenty of callouts that fans of classic adventure games and science fiction will appreciate. The art style feels distinct and consistent, and the music and effects do a great job of building atmosphere.It's not a long game – I finished it in around 12 hours – but much longer would probably feel stretched, so I appreciate that it doesn't try and pad out the length more than it needs.Despite you playing as a child, I think the story is probably only really going to be appreciated by older players, so it seems hard to know the intended audience. Having said that, its content should be fine for any child old enough to work out the puzzles (or follow hints or walkthroughs).Overall, I think it was an experience worth exploring. It's impressive too that it seems most of the game was created by one person. If you enjoy point-and-click classics like , or if you're looking for an introduction to the genre, give it a go.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on 90% sale and I thoroughly enjoyed it. It's a nice tribute to old fashioned point & click quests. Interactions here are based on using items and talking to NPCs (as opposed to solving mechanical puzzles, where you have a dozen of levers to arrange something in a particular pattern). The game is good. Not great, not brilliant, just good - I'd say 7/10. All elements are nicely tied together and do work, but not at the level which would make you awe or remember it for years to come. I'd say the game is rather easy. It always clearly states what you need to do, if you explore surroundings with both characters they almost always give hints of what needs to be done, all items are always used logically. if you're stuck that's 80% because you've missed an item blended with the background somewhere, and 20% is you need to return to an old NPC and convince them to help you (the amount of stuff people you've just met are ready to give you is mind boggling). Locations are fairly sparse, so even though it seems like you're walking through a dozen of screens, each of them only has a handful of interactive elements, so you're never overwhelmed and have a pretty good idea of where the solution should be. The only location I didn't like at all is residential block area - you literally have to brute force your way in one of flats by going through the list of nonsensical dialogue lines with random npcs, I don't think the game gives you any hint on where the right door is. Encodya (location) on the other hand is actually very good and offers some memorable locations. Story is simple but serviceable, probably due to 9 year old protagonist who doesn't challenge plot holes ) It peaks at act 4 and I think somewhat stumbles in the end. Some quests you have to do in chapter 5 are so misplaced that even characters themselves are questioning why are they doing these. The game likes to break the 4th wall quite often in general, trying to sneak some jokes in, though I personally didn't find it particularly amusing.Overall I can say the game is good. I don't think there are many fresh titles in this genre and this one is definitely not bad. All points are primarily in missed opportunities territory - I miss creative use of items in a non-conventional way, or coordinated efforts with two characters when you have to do something with one character while another character creates a distraction (there is pretty much a single moment like that in the whole game). It is a solid 10 hours laid-back adventure (probably half of that on easy) where you need to carefully analyse the surrounding areas and apply basic logic to progress. it scratches all necessary nostalgic P&C itches and ends before you become bored of it. Not sure I'd be equally happy about it had I purchased it for the full price, but on a sale it's a good game to have in the library.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Lovely art. Some of the nicest non-pixel art I've seen in a P&C game in a long while.- Good voicework. Dialogue is sometimes clunky but voice actors did a good job with it. SAM was especially good.- Good world-building. I recently played another cyberpunk P&C (Virtuaverse) and everything was so awful, including the protagonist. This game avoids that with some humor and a young protagonist who doesn't get too bogged down by how miserable everything actually is.Cons:- Horrid pixel-hunting. Pixel-hunting is the wooooorst. If I knew this was why there's a difficulty adjuster at the beginning, I would've chosen easy mode. I don't want to spend an hour looking for a rock (can you just pick up any rock? No you have to pick up a very special one!).- Clunky political commentary. I just finished playing Disco Elysium last week, so to go from that level of political commentary to this was jarring. There's a lot of jokes and commentary that are going to feel really outdated in a few years (tbh it already feels outdated). IRL, Trump is out of power and everything is more garbage than ever. Knowing that makes the ending feel hollow. Overall:I would still recommend getting the game on sale because the parts I did like were really good, and the parts I didn't like were tolerable. I look forward to what the developer comes out with next and I hope they improve their future games.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fine. The story is a bit weak and cliched (typical post-(VR)-apocalyptic world), but it's executed well enough; characters are alright (none too remarkable, but also none too awful); gameplay-wise, it's the typical puzzle point & clicker, most puzzles are fine, some are obtuse (it definitely suffers from the all-too-common nonsense of requiring a very specific thing to accomplish something, when in real life you could do the same with several of the items you already have), and some are outright illogical (I'd recommend the devs to read a little more about how electricity works xD). Voice acting left a bit to be desired, to be honest. We could also use more saveslots (I don't see why limiting them to three is necessary). In spite of these things, I may still replay it someday, to get the achievements I've missed. I was expecting more from this game, but what I did get wasn't all that bad, either.It's definitely not my favorite point & click game, and I got a bit bored at times, but overall, I liked it enough, and can recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: An enjoyable adventure game. The setting, the characters and the atmosphere are all very nice. The art is good. The story's interesting and intriguing enough. The puzzles are fairly decent on average.Being able to switch between two different characters, while promising, is perhaps not quite as interesting as it could have been. There are some things that Tina can do while Sam can't and vice versa, but which character will prove more useful in a given situation is almost always quite obvious and requires little thinking. The different points of view and the interaction between the two are nevertheless enjoyable.I saw the very last scene coming, but it still felt like a punch to the face.

_childDocuments_.review: I rally wanted to like this game, and thought it might be a hidden gem. Unfortunately, I can't recommend it.I thought it looks great (especially the 2d backgrounds, I'm less of a fan for 3d character models but that could be a personal preference), it carries the cyberpunk atmosphere well, and I loved that it offers "hard mode". In fact, the hard mode is the primary reason I purchased this game: so many adventure games these days tend to be too easy and focus primarily on the story.Unfortunately, the "hard mode" is harder for the wrong reasons. Almost always when I was stuck, it was due to missing a tiny object that blends in with the background, which I guess is an equivalent of pixel hunting in high resolution games. Still, I wouldn't mind that if the game offered good puzzles otherwise. Unfortunately, many of the puzzles could be described simply as fetch quests and there are even some of the "collect X number of something" type. They come across less as puzzles and more as filler content. It feels like, in the first half of the game, the designers didn't really have ideas for the puzzles. It improves somewhat in the second half of the game, but at that point it was too little too late to really recommend the game.As a side note, I think the "2 playable characters" idea was underutilized. Instead of the puzzles that force the characters to collaborate and the player to think outside the box, sometimes one character will simply say "I think the other character should do this" or something to that effect and that will be the end of it. Additionally, the robot character takes a large amount of space on the screen which makes it hard to see clickable objects behind him. This is the main reason why I played most of the game as him - to make it easier to get him out of the way.

_childDocuments_.review: A point and click adventure that lets you experience a ray of hope in a cruel and dark futuristic world where the rich corporations feed off the poor.Tina, a 9-year-old orphan who lives on the streets and can take care of herself, is the embodiment of this ray. Her lone companion is SAM-53, a robot who has been with her since she was born. Tina is destined for greatness, and it doesn't take long for a player to realize this. She decides to find out who she really is after learning that the cops are after her and that she has a real father.Encodya isn't trying to reinvent the wheel when it comes to adventure games. The left mouse button is used for both walking and interaction. The cursor changes when you hover over an interactable spot, and you can perform a variety of actions. It's a pity that the right mouse button is never used. If there was a "look" command stuck to it, I believe the gameplay would be much more smooth.What breaks the mold slightly is the fact that you control Tina and SAM. Not both at the same time, of course. You can swap by clicking on their image or pressing the TAB key. Tina takes center stage as the story's hero while exploring and interacting with people. SAM, on the other hand, is the one who has to take command when strength it required or when you need to talk to robots.Robots, as in any other futuristic story, are viewed as tools rather than something people are worried about. I enjoy how both characters have different opinions on things and topics of conversation. Because you never know which hotspot will reveal a clue, you must interact with each one twice. I found it a bit strange that Tina has to jump through extra hoops to accomplish something when her robot is right there. In one situation you have to steal some keys.  The robot can reach it but refuses due to rules in his programming, and Tina is too small, so she has to make a long stick.? Why isn't the robot able to simply lift her up? This occurs frequently throughout the game, but I eventually learned to accept it once I recognized that this is the universe and laws that the devs created.Unfortunately, Encodya is guilty of the most terrible sin a game can commit: pixel hunting. If you want to avoid this, you can choose the easy option that allows you to highlight hotspots. But having difficulty options in a point and click game shouldn’t be an thing in the first place. Every purposefully hidden object in the backdrop feels cheap, as if it were an artificial means of extending the game's length. They're sometimes so effectively hidden that it's difficult to tell what's junk from what's genuinely useful. There were some issues with objects hidden behind the robot. However, this was quickly forgotten because you can detect objects right through your buddy. Inventory management should be better. Because the bar at the bottom of the screen doesn’t show all the items, you’ll have to press left and right arrow to move between them. This is frustrating when you want to combine items. First you need to click an item, choose “use”, scroll to the item at the end, and do it all over again if the combination doesn’t work. For me , the most important thing in adventure games is that solutions make sense. Encodya doesn’t force you to combine stuff that never works together. Furthermore, it puts a strong emphasis on speaking. You might talk to someone and unknowingly unlock new conversation with a person or robot with whom you already talked.Although you won't see anything you haven't seen in other neo-future games, the art is very nice and the world you get to explore is interesting. There are a lot of odd billboards, flying cars, rubbish on the street, and human zombies connected to cyberspace, which you get to see in the second part. The voiceover is also excellent. Only a couple of characters seemed stiff to me, but the good news is that Tina doesn't have that unpleasant whiny voice. Same goes for SAM.I like the pause screen that shows the completion percentage, secrets, hits and time played. This doesn’t mean anything to a casual player, but for someone like myself, who tries to get as many achievements as he can, it’s a nice little excuse to play the game a second time. While I enjoyed some of the secrets, such as the item in your inventory that changes the graphics, I hated the one where you had to find a button, a single pixel, on a completely uninteresting screen. I’m not ashamed to admit that I had to look for a guide.  Rating: Make 👍Reviewed by:

_childDocuments_.review: A decent game that doesn't quite live up to its potential.I was looking forward to this game when I saw the trailer. I liked the dystopian graphics and the ability to play as a robot. But you don't get to interact with the environments as much as you should. While good and sad, the story doesn't hit the mark like it would if the game had developed the back story further. Unlike other people, I didn't think the game was political or racist. Irony Curtain was way more political, and I even thought that was fine. Remember, video games are art, and all art has a message.My biggest complaint was finding items. Half the time, I missed something, either because it blended in with the environment or the giant robot blocked it. Other puzzles were more complicated than necessary because the character said, "It doesn't work." Yes, I see that. Perhaps if you had said it's dusty, it would enable me to fix it. Then there's the pixel hunting.Despite being giant, clicking on the majority of SAM does not enable you to interact with it. Only half of its head. For other objects, you have to select the precise pixel to use it. There's a button you need to press for a secret, and I saw it and pushed it like five times. I was about to give up, but the walkthrough showed a picture of the button, so I started moving the cursor around the button until one pixel finally highlighted the button. This is not something that should be happening in 2021.All in all, a decent eight-hour point-and-click adventure game you will enjoy if you like the genre. If you don't, it's probably not worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: ENCODYA

_childDocuments_.review: For first 60 minutes (on Hard) I didn't notice that many real-world political themes crammed in, and I feel people find connections where they'd want them to be. If this changes, I'm definitely joining the camp of not wanting armchair activist politics crammed into a very, very lovely game.The graphics are top-notch, and control is smooth and good. Puzzles, so far, aren't too crazy, but not as easy as I noticed all other modern adventure games have. You also don't get too many tips at the places you'd expect them - item examination. The tips are sort of hidden in conversations with right NPCs.I don't mean game-breaking/cheating tips (which you can get on Easy mode).You collect MANY items, and some are real pixel hunting: however, this game isn't running in 320x200, and graphics are very crisp, so if you just _look_ at the scenery, you can deduce objects that look like they aren't just random props. I found this 'interactive hunt' a part of the experience, and a fun one.One thing, which game succeeds at very very well, is in conveying its intro text:developers say that the game is a work of fiction, and all characters are made up. Some world parallels are pulled simply to try and make you think about how corporations bla bla bla... you know the drill.Thing is, as cute and great looking the game is - you play a 9y old orphan. You dig around garbage. People give you rotten food for free, and expect you to be grateful.If you get immersed into the game -and I did- this isn't cute and fluffy any more... it is disturbing, and sort of starts becoming depressing. You even meet an NPC who makes a joke of you digging trash all day long with your robot.The only negative remark I have - but its a pretty strong one - is that game too often breaks the fourth wall. Like, character explaining that its just stuck in an animation loop to save disk space.These work super well in a more lighthearted game (and always make me chuckle) - in Encodya, they just break the immersion, and I don't find them funny but annoying. I wish I could disable them.All in all, I do believe its very well worth your money - unless, as I said, embedded armchair activism politics start to show their ugly face down the line.
_childDocuments_.name: ENCODYA

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful soundtrack and world building. There are a few rough edges, but they don't take away from an engaging experience. The game has memorable worlds. I'd say the world and environments are the strongest feature. And whoever designed SAM did a great job - I think the robots stand out more than any of the people, in terms of character design. Overall, Tina and Sam's story was engaging. I'm a bit older than the target audience, but I could see this game being enjoyed by middle schoolers on up. However: some of the puzzles are tricky and there's at least one I definitely needed a hint on, on 'outside the game' hint. A few had that crazy RPG adventure game logic, and I didn't feel bad looking up a walkthrough to avoid the pain of endless guessing. But the story is what takes center stage. My cons: some of the characters were obvious send offs of current political figures. There was one character that felt a bit like a stereotype, but they don't have a large role. The only other con is some of the background NPC figures that walk the city streets - I liked this element, but I almost wish they'd been made less distinct. You'll see the same 8 or so figures slowly parading the city streets/alleys as you enter them. Still: blade runner inspired world and gorgeous score? Cute, gentle giant robot friend, with an adventurous little girl? All great elements. I recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: ENCODYA

_childDocuments_.review: Fun adventure game, would recommend. I'm glad people still make point-and-click adventures, and this is not a bad specimen.TL;DR: The pros far outweigh the cons. What I liked:+ Fair puzzles. For the most part they're just the right level of difficult+ Nice graphics and artwork+ Beautiful and fitting soundtrack+ Excellent voice acting+ Okay story. Nothing unheard of, pretty standard, but engaging enough+ Shout-outs to Lucasarts classics. Almost obligatory in the adventure genre+ Fun easter eggs+ When quitting from within the game it quits properly, rather than going back to the main menu. Why aren't all games like that?What I didn't like (that much)- Interface could be better. E.g. right-click for looking at things would be nice. Mostly I disliked how the inventory is handled. You have to click items once to select, and then again to interact with them. Makes trying out combinations a bit tedious, particularly since the item doesn't stay selected after trying to combine or use it.- After entering a new screen the game is unresponsive for maybe half a second.- One or two of the puzzles don't seem to make all that much sense and require trying random combinationsI'm struggling to find proper negative aspects to balance the review. It's a good game. Get it, if you like adventures at all.
_childDocuments_.name: ENCODYA

_childDocuments_.review: What a delightful little game. Encodya is the story of one orphan girl and her nanny robot as they scavenge and scrounge on the streets just to survive. Of course, another day in Encodya's beautifully drawn and scored (yet repressive) Neo Berlin of 2062 gives way to a conspiracy that little Tina must unravel with SAM-53's help.If you miss the good old point and clicks of yore - your , your  - this is for you. Not only does it nail the gameplay (combining disparate items into wacky new gadgets, pixel hunting for that one item or clue you missed and gradually tying seemingly disparate map locations together) but the characterisation and voice acting are generally excellent, and the game crucially balances moments of humour and levity with real profundity and sadness.Expect to spend upwards of 3-4 hours in Encodya - 5 if you go hunting for all the secrets and Easter eggs. Encodya's well-paced story and puzzles that were just the right balance between obscure and logical meant that none of that time felt padded or like a drag, and the 5 act narrative makes it feel like a nice, full game as well.I can't recommend this enough.
_childDocuments_.name: ENCODYA

_childDocuments_.review: A solid adventure game in the old LucasArts mode. I give it thumbs-up for a huge number of gorgeous environments & items and pretty good (if cheesily-written!) voice acting, but be warned: it does fall into the trap of making you hunt for the magic pixel or combine totally arbitrary items together to progress. I did play it without hints, but still -- a few of the puzzles are hard in a not-clever way, which was frustrating. And that's made worse by there being a huge number of items and environments, even if those things are themselves really nicely done!4/5, enjoyed playing but wish some puzzles were more clever and less...vague.
_childDocuments_.name: ENCODYA

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really good game if you focus on story and take your time solving puzzles. But if you want to complete all steam achievements or unlock all secrets, it's probably impossible without following a guide. The game is A bit too artificially challenging at times. Well, you can't except much better from a kid's game.
_childDocuments_.name: ENCODYA

_childDocuments_.review: This is point and click at it's best, great artwork, good voice acting, a dash of humor and a truly heartfelt story.  I played the demo almost a year ago and was enchanted then, but after finishing the game I have to say I really love it.   Some people may shy away because of the higher price and the shorter length, but I can say unequivocally the price is worth is due to the high production values and the great story telling.  I was only stumped once and this was due to missing an accessible area so move your mouse everywhere.  I really hope this creator releases more games, I would gladly support them.  5 stars!
_childDocuments_.name: ENCODYA

_childDocuments_.review: Encodya is a great adventure game.Even if the story is not very original and there are some bugs, it still didn't prevent me from enjoying myself.Beautiful art style, interesting puzzles (some of them pretty brain-wrecking as it should be in an adventure game) and plenty of references to the classics make you feel like you are a legitimate companion of Tina and Sam on their journey.
_childDocuments_.name: ENCODYA

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the demo for ENCODYA when it first appeared, I had a feeling we were in for something pretty special. It had a wonderful classic point and click feel to it, and it's always nice to have every character fully voice-acted. Needless to say, I backed the Kickstarter pretty darn quickly!When the full game landed in January, I couldn't wait to get stuck in. Elements of the original demo were tied into the full game, which was nice as it helped keep things a bit familiar, so it hardly even felt like I'd been gone!The scene designs of Neo-Berlin really are breathtaking to look at, a true dystopian nightmare of a place full of characters, all with their own motivations and backstories. It's also full of puzzles to be solved, some more fiendish than others for sure, but in the end the clues are all in place for you to work your way from scene to scene as you strive to find out more about yourself and your family as you wander the streets of the city with only your robot SAM for company.The game is always shifting and changing, and there are always new places to explore as the mysteries of your past are uncovered. It all leads up to quite an excellent final scenario, and although the ending feels a tad rushed, the experience on the whole was pretty amazing.I'm happy to say that I helped this game spring to life, and I honestly can't recommend it enough for fans of point and click puzzle adventure games!(Please note my playthrough linked below starts with Part 4, as the first 3 parts were the demo and not indicative of the completed version of the game).
_childDocuments_.name: ENCODYA

_childDocuments_.review: Let’s start with the story. You are a 9-year-old orphan girl with her nanny bot SAM-53, living on the streets, getting by however you can. In this world, the government started a plan that with every child born, a family was gifted a nanny robot to look after them. I’m not sure how this was affordable or why to start such an initiative, but it was interesting, so I didn’t question it. The story is a light-hearted one.Moving on, we are introduced to the villain of the story, Mayor Rumpf. He is a short-tempered little man who is trying to find you and SAM-53. Without spoiling too much, I felt he was not a necessary character, that the story would have been stronger with the focus on the true villain- humanities dependency on technology.The characters you meet have well-written dialogue that built up the world-building, making me wish there was more to learn and explore.  Of course, I absolutely adored the art and the cityscapes. There is a lot of world-building through dialogue and exploring, but it all felt like a window into a world I wanted to explore more. I hope they do continue stories within this world. I had a lot of fun, as long as you don't take the story too seriously, I recommend it. Looking forward to more from this studio and hopefully more from the Encodya world.
_childDocuments_.name: ENCODYA

_childDocuments_.review: fun polished cyberpunk-ish (think bladerunner film sets  meet ready player one)  XD  point n click set in neo berlin.  reasonably good lateral thinking. towards the finale , some of the logic was too much "pixelhunt", which i m not a fan of (raspberries took me forever) .   good story.  some nods to the oldschool, monkey island day of the tentacle.  many adorable androids and robots, which is good. 7.5/10 bit pricey got a decent amount of time out of it, i think 6 hours first playtrhough if you are not as bad as me. XD
_childDocuments_.name: ENCODYA

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent point and click adventure that calls to mind similar games and experiences of past years, while offering very clever writing and voice acting, with tongue in cheek commentary about current events, and even a random break of the fourth wall at times. Some of the puzzles are more difficult, resulting in a hidden object hunt, but overall not so difficult that you won't be frustrated (a hint guide is available in the forums if you must). Definitely had me hooked to the end, even past the credits.
_childDocuments_.name: ENCODYA

_childDocuments_.review: A true love declaration for Point&Click games!A cute cartoonish Blade Runner-style city, Neo Berlin, filled with funny characters that are straight out of a Studio Ghibli movie.You follows the adventures of Tina and her robot S.A.M. who are trying to discover the secret about her past.The game is the typical point&click where you have to explore many locations in order to find hidden objects that you have to use and combine in a certain way to unlock the next step,You need to talk with many characters of Neo Berlin and the dialogue options you are presented are different depending if you talk as Tina or as Sam.The story is full of references and Easter eggs about videogames (including the classic Lucas Art adventures), pop culture, anime, comics and movies. Some are really hilarious and they made me smile more than once.Voice acting and music are also very well done and are definitely one of the highlights of this game.PS: considering this has been made by a small indie studio the result is great! I can totally recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: ENCODYA

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not usually writing reviews, really, however, in this case, I want to spend a little bit of my time giving my opinion about Encodya.I'm totally enjoying the game, as a veteran Point and Click adventure gamer since the good old glory days, I have to say that Encodya definitely feels like a love letter to classic graphic adventures.Technically, the game is fantastic, music, environment, art style, and so on are top-notch.In terms of gameplay, the story unfolds gradually and it does perfectly blend with the cyberpunk Neo Berlin environment.For a veteran gamer, the puzzles are a little bit on the "easy" side, classic objects manipulation/inventory combining puzzles (which for me it's a plus), however, I'd say that the game focuses a little bit more on storytelling than on the difficulty itself.    On the good side, the puzzles feel logical and not totally abstract, as in Deponia, for example.Would I recommend the game? Damn yes! Go and get your copy, if you're into classic adventure games you won't regret getting Encodya, we do definitely need more quality Point and Click games like this one :)
_childDocuments_.name: ENCODYA

_childDocuments_.review: Neo Berlin 2062. Tina – a nine-year-old orphan – lives with SAM-53 – her big clumsy robot guardian –in a rooftop makeshift shelter in Neo-Berlin, a dark megalopolis controlled by corporations.

name: Black Book
detailed_description: Check out new game from Hypetrain About the Game A fusion of card-based RPGs and Adventure games, “Black Book” is a haunting tale of a young sorceress, who gave her life to serve the dark forces. Dive into the cold, yet alluring world of Slavic folktales - and uncover the secrets that hide in the darkness. A young girl named Vasilisa, destined to become a witch, decides to throw her fate away and marry her beloved - but that dream is shattered when her betrothed dies under mysterious circumstances. Aching for her lost love, Vasilisa seeks out the Black Book - a demonic artifact, said to be powerful enough to grant any wish to the one who uncovers all 7 of its seals. Join Vasilisa in her adventures across the rural countryside, as she solves the woes of common folk by confronting demons and performing exorcisms. Uncover the seals of Black Book Unleash hellish spells on your enemies! Collect spell cards and new skills as you progress. A Historic Adventure Solve riddles and complete side-quests as you learn more about life in the Slavic countryside. Lead a Demonic Flock Send demons to do your bidding, but be careful - idle demons will torture you if you don’t find them something to do! Myths and legends Explore a world based on Northern Slavic mythology. Learn from an in-game encyclopedia, created with the help of expert anthropologists - and find all folk tales hidden within the game!

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun and immersive story driven RPG type game! The art is simple and beautiful, the music is soulful gives a very authentic flavour to the game, and the game is very rich in lore that has been researched by the devs from real life Russian folk tales. I have learned a lot from playing so far!The card system for fighting evil spirits is easy to pick up but full of potential for developing strategies, the game feels polished and I have encountered no bugs or issues. If you like this type of game, you'll love Black Book
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellently crafted game, but you should know what you're getting into. I had the expectation that it would be a game like slay the spire, but its really not, it only retains the foundations of the card battler. This is a much more story focused (around 30 hours of story gameplay), era-accurate game with details that go into details. Once you pass the 2nd chapter, you will realize how large the game really is. There is a lot of reading, and you do have to pay attention to what is being said for later down the line, so its not a VN which you can skip the dialogue and hope for the best.Gameplay is great. I thought i had an overpowered deck but the final boss whooped my ass. Enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Truly a hidden gem. Stunning visuals, exceptional writing and narration. Turned out a ton better than I expected. I have been playing it for over 10 hours and I haven't yet finished chapter 2 (there is 7 in total as the game states) so the game length is pretty long although I don't imagine it being much fun to replay once finished. One more thing to note is the more seals you break (finish a chapter) the more cards you get to discover and add to your collection which allows you to play in a lot of various ways and get creative thus making the game more fun as you progress.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: my best first hour in a game in 2021. (GREAT AS DEATH'S DOOR)hand drawn landscape tell a beautiful mythical story, while you voyage inside living paintings and find useful objects for your fights againts demons and others creatures. CARD FIGHTS! really well done.the game i had always dreamed of.it's like the nephew of slay the spire with a lot of interesting histories all around.....magical atmosphere. this game is really full of love and attention to details.absolutely YES!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Final Review.Overall, its a Thumbs up.Most of my interim review stands.  The biggest negative remains that the cards and artifact information are severely lacking.  It can be very frustrating to establish a strategy and not understand why it is not working.  The in-combat descriptions only add to this frustration.To finish the review on a positive,  I really  like what they did with the historical and religious context in the game.  It would be great to see them improve on this formula in another game medium.  For example, it would be interesting to see this art style and storytelling approach to an  RPG medium, for example. Interim Review. Very borderline thumbs up. The lore is amazing.  Graphics and music are suitable and fit the mood well.  Voice acting is hit or miss.  For some reason, the worse voice actor is used for multiple characters.The instructions of the card and item status really sucks.  It is often unclear to me if a status effect is applied to me or the enemy.  Given how important this mechanic is to the game, this is a real problem.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving Black Book a positive review since it exceeded my expectations. This game features a simple card based combat system, but it complements it with a compelling storyline, fun facts, and a mini game similar to the western poker to add positively to the experience. (Also the OST is very nice.) Boss battles need proper strategy, and it challenges you to create the appropriate decks for specific situations. In this game you'll learn about Slavic traditions, superstitions and folk customs from the pre-revolutionary period in Russia. In game there's an interesting database (encyclopedia) about the creatures, and myths, that you find in your adventures. The DLC and the supporter pack are great bonuses to add to the game, while they're not absolutely necessary to get a good experience, I consider they're a nice bonus to support the creators. I enjoy games which have a cultural background behind, with a spooky / occult spice as a plus.This title is near to what I'd been looking for into witchcraft / sorcery videogames since a while ago. I highly recommend it. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant game. Even with obvious limitations to budget and resources, the art, music and narrative of the game are all amazing. There are a few nitpicks I would point out, like how some animations are hard to apreciate during battles, or somehow wanky controlsduring some segments, but it's honestly so minor that I doubt hardly anyone will care.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for February 2022.   If you are interested in the game and it's before March 1st, 2022, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.I’d probably just read something else. Black Book starts at a lightning pace.  You’re married to a man who suddenly dies and you have to break the seven seals to get him back from hell.  It’s a quick setup that works, but after that point, Black Book slows down to a crawl.  Everything in this game takes a long time to discuss and talk about, and this is a story about a woman becoming a witch and trying to break the seven seals.  There are a lot of elements in this game. The core combat in the game is based on Slay the Spire’s but this isn’t done in the same progression.  There’s a strange point and click system that feels unnecessary to have been added, and the gameplay is more decision-based than combat-based. However none of these features mesh together, and the story almost put me to sleep for some reason, it lacked any interesting moments for me to grasp. Pick this up if you want to learn about Russian mythology in the slowest way possible.  Admittedly this game is popular, I just don’t understand why.  It’s one of those games where reviewers seem to be harsher, whereas Steam reviews are extremely positive.  I’m willing to consider that I had a different experience but I’m not interested in returning to this title. If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Captivating story, atmospheric and deep dive into culture and mythology in pre-soviet times.Interesting roque card game mechanics.Still a few kinks, but the dev team actively working on it.This game is not for you if you are the type of player skipping cut scenes, are in need to get explicitly told what to do or do not like to read.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: It's a comprehensive learning experience for the folklore of one eastern region, ranging from local legends, terms, to pleasant songs. Very linear progression and turn-based fights using cards. Most fights are fairly easy, but bosses are significantly tougher. I got stuck in the second chapter, impossible to defeat the boss, hence I can't continue the story. It's rather frustrating to be blocked, but at the same the very repetitive nature of the game made it ok to just uninstall it and move on.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game for its niche. Great story for both, main and sides lines. Humor, horror, mystics, routines - all great, and perfectly placed in context of insane local mix of pagan traditions and Orthodox Christianity.Variety of battle situations is well-balanced in general, but most of bosses could be easily smashed after their  cast cycles understanding. Preparation of own deck according to chapter specifics seems most important thing for battles.Battle interface is OK, but sometimes card and statuses descriptions doesn't fit the screen. It's could have huge impact in battles with predefined decks. And... sometimes cards descriptions are not clear.Cards mechanics becomes more and more complex following new book's chapters opening.Voices are great. At lease Russians.Visuals simple but pleasant. Just one thing really annoying - face of main character in 3D. Not a big deal as it's rear-visible, but frustrating a bit.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a surprising amount of content considering that it's a "small indie game". The deckbuilder component is decently fun, although you'll quickly hit upon some sort of OP card combo that trivialises most of the fights. With that in mind, I appreciate how the designers tried to ensure that some of the boss fights would hard counter some deck archetypes - this means that you might have to swap to a new deck to beat a specific boss, which is a nice touch.The music and Slavic folklore elements are where the game excels. Without even realising it, I've learnt so much about chorts, kolduny, banniks, leshys, banyas, izbas, etc just by solving puzzles in the game. The story was pretty good too, and the characters are fleshed out enough for your to feel invested in them.The only negative I could find was that the English version seems to have been translated from Russian, so some of the sentences and word choices can be a little awkward and hard to read. That being said, I was still able to follow the story quite easily, so it's a very minor issue.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: I've recommended Black Book to a number of people at this point and will continue to. I enjoyed the gameplay and story a lot, though the ending feels comparatively abrupt relative to everything else. Once you figure out a play-style you enjoy and build around it the game gets significantly easier. The history and folklore woven into the game make it feel really special and like an intimate experience with the stories being told and legends being shared. The voice acting being in the original language reinforces the game's aesthetics well. I think it'd feel wrong to listen to it in another language, given what Black Book is.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: This game absolutely whips ass. It's got a powerful aesthetic, a beautiful low-poly style, a moody soundtrack, and overall immaculate vibes. The card game combat is fun and the progression of unlocking more cards made it fun to occasionally re-tune my deck.I can't say enough good things about this game's style. It looks and sounds amazing and has an aesthetic that you don't see a lot - there just aren't enough games set in mid-to-late 1800s rural Russia centered around the local folklore and mythology. Both the 3d and 2d art of the game is striking and evocative but I feel like the game really shines in its environments. Each place feels so specially crafted and the camera so carefully placed. The developers clearly have a strong sense of cinematography and that comes through the most during the cutscenes which are, across the board, gorgeous.The difficulty spikes from time-to-time in a way that sometimes feels like I would need to go back and customize my deck to prepare for a specific fight but other times just felt like an encounter's numbers were just too high to deal with. The options menu does allow changing the difficulty at any time so I was able to drop it down to Easy when necessary, and it even has a Skip Battle button for when something got to be too frustrating (and it doesn't punish you for using that - a mistake that I feel a lot of games would've made).Don't sleep on this game, I think it's a genuinely incredible thing that deserves way more attention than what it's gotten so far. And, hey, at the time of review it's getting to be Halloween season and I think this would be the perfect game for that time of year.Also there's a card game in this card game so you can card game while you card game.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: What this game different from other Roguelike-Deckbuilding games is it's Russian Dark Witchcraft Lore! the storyplay. Its awesome! I myself kinda learn some of Russian words from playing. It's Dark, cute at the same time. It creepy and informative, but fun in its own way.Made me want hold up playin, I dont want this game end too quick for me LOL.Graphics : 4 / 5Basic, simple, plain in a good way. I got high taste in games graphic with my RTX3060. But this game make me humble myself. Simple graphic sometime brings joy too.Audio : BGM + Narrator's Dialogue. 4.5 / 5It give peace. it give chill. It play it roles deeply.Gameplay : 4 / 5. If you familiar with Roguelike-Deckbuilding games, it's of of those kind. Has it's own unique recipes and twist. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I had no idea coming in that the game would be this long, or this in depth with the amount of lore alone, its damn impressive. Everything was voice acted which I appreciated, and felt that it made the game more real. It is a visual novel with combat aspects.With this review, I want to focus on what I really enjoyed about the game, mechanics wise, as there was very little in the game that I disliked.The map system on how you go through every chapter/day is really unique. I love how you have a choice where if you don't want to follow side quests, you can just barrel through. A word to the wise about the battles, I struggled during one part and once I figured out that some battles need a curse build, and some need a waste build, I was just flying high. However, the developers are AMAZING and if you fail a battle like 3 or 4 times they give you an option to skip. AND they didn't make it an achievement that you had to 100% each battle without skipping. This small detail meant so much to me since I'm really bad at games and usually just stick around for the plot.I enjoyed the ending, and thought it really tied everything up. I would estimate the game is about 80% lore and 20% combat, so if you love a visual novel with some deck building sprinkled in, its definitely the game for you
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: A dark fantasy fairy tale which will lead you through the very atmospheric story with all kind of slavic demons. And it's not about good vs evil, but much deeper.For the gameplay... well, sometimes it requires flexibility and otherwise will be punishing. It's still worth playing even if you don't like the gameplay, just lower difficulty.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: It is a proper Russian witcher experience. A deep dive in Russian Slavic mythology. A rare chance to learn about Russian cryptic critters originating from a unique mix of archaic believes and Russian Orthodox Christianity. The game is actually made very well. The only downside is English translation/voiceover missing a lot of flavor text/facts. A most likely made to cater to western audience but also cutting away project's appeal It is 10/10 from me
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: [this was written after 10 hours with the game, final impressions at the end]Currently after about 10 hours in (completing the first major story arc, seemingly out of ~6), I can safely say that I love this game. It started a bit slow and at first seemed a bit shallow, but then it turned out that it's far from that.Basically, after 10 hours, to me this game feels like a distilled Witcher 3 experience, without the open world, and with a card-based combat. Remember the quests in Witcher 3 which were related to all those supernatural creatures, like the Hym quest or the Towerful of Mice quest? Well, imagine if you take stories like those, replace the combat with a card-based implementation (and an interesting one, at that) and get rid of the open world (so that you move via an overworld map between the story encounters). Well, this is what Black Book feel like after 10 hours. And I love it.The story and characters are well-written, and I love the art style. I'm also a huge fan of the card-based combat implementation this game has. At first it doesn't seem very deep, but there are actually lots of different mechanics and synergies, and you have to think in order to figure out what works best. Also after completing the first major story arc you get more cards with new mechanics; apparently this happens after completing each major story arc. Note that you can change the composition of your deck at any time. In particular, you can remove any cards from your active deck to your stash (there is a requirement on the minimal number of cards in the active deck though), thereby increasing the chance of appearance of the remaining cards in your hand during combat. It's very important to only keep the cards in your deck which synergize well with the other cards, removing the cards unneeded for your current strategy.All-in-all I highly recommend this game to everyone who likes games with interesting stories and characters and/or games with card-based combat.EDIT: after completing the game I can fully support what I said above. This is really one of my favorite games now.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting but very slow paced.  Slay the Spire and other similar games have quick combat loops, but this game lacks a lot of the fast-paced cardslinging of those games in favor of a heavy story that isn't well voice-acted. Everything in this game works on paper but needs ironing to be the game I want it to be.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: A story-rich DBG. Not recommended for someone like me who don't really care for story in DBGs. To be fair, the art style is decent, though I hold-to-skip most of the cutscenes. But the gameplay is not. There are just way too many boring combat events, which may look fun for the first few hours but will become a chore over time, especially when you've already built an ideal deck. Even if you stick only to the main path/quest, you still need to go through tons of obligatory fights until you meet the boss.DBGs don't usually work that way. Black Book is more like a story driven AVG that includes some deck building elements.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: At times dark, at other times very dialogue heavy (and rewards those who actually READ everything, lol). But one thing is for sure, Black Book is finally a fresh take on the Deck-Builder genre. 9/10. The game has some standard DB mechanics: drawing cards each round, acquiring relics that give specific bonuses, fighting bad dudes, etc. It also has SO much more: --an actual story of epic length (7+ chapters? each chapter unlocking more available cards). --Cards are played into specific slots each round... Scrolls vs Keys (2 scroll slots and 1 key slot to start); which then gives way to SO many new mechanics--like "Firm X" (card will stay on the board X rounds) or "Eternal" (card always on the board). --Black vs White cards allows for additional mechanics based on similarity of color (more black/white makes card X more powerful)--While the game has several common status effects, it introduces MANY new ones, especially "second order" status conditions--status conditions that create status conditions. --"Dual" battles against other NPC "Summoners" (vs monsters) have unique rules based on how many cards you vs NPC plays on their board--side missions and minigames. --An ACTUAL story, with ACTUAL choices, and a morality system that isn't always obvious.My two big "complaints":--Pacing: the game begins to drag on around Chapter 5/6. The battles started to blend together by this point. --Similar to above: by chapter 5/6, I was getting cool new cards but my desire to experiment was very low. I had found a very cool deck I liked. It worked well. and I wasn't finding any reason to stop it. Tbf, I have not beaten the game; so it's possible future chapters will force me to change (this has happened repeatedly), but I like feeling like I can experiment. So, not a perfect game, but definitely interesting and a welcome breath of fresh air for the genre. Will keep you playing for a long time.  Likely has at least 1 full replay in it for me due to the morality system.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: I look back now and see how much time I spent on this game.This one is going to a be a bit hit or miss and really depends on your personal tastes, I personally loved this as I have an understanding of Russian folklore and I have family in Yugoslavia which gave me a bit of personal stake and understanding.This game is in essence a card based deck builder RPG with very light elements of exploration and an emphasis on decisions and dialogue with the main character throughout the course of the game being bale to collect a fair amount of lore. This gets presented in 2 formats with one being excerpts of folk tales to the more direct breakdowns of the cultural beliefs and folklore that was the spiritual centre of the Russian peasant of the time.Before we even get to the game I enjoyed the heck out of this. Russian folklore is some of the more intricate and overlooked in general beside things like  LOOK, THE TSAR HAS A BEEEEG HAT AND A SILO FULL OF VODCHKA!!!!!.The game play in of itself is fairly amusing but nothing ground breaking though it does make effort to change things up and i will say that the the boss fights are pleasantly challenging.The story and especially the visuals late game are pretty damn beautiful even though the graphics are basic.This game feels like one of those where the devs had a dream that they brought into reality against the odds and i can only imagine as I have to have done so often how epic this would have been with the budget that gets thrown into so many unfinished AAA cash cows.8/10- Slav magic
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so enchanting. The turn based system is extremely well designed. The storytelling is really good - but I would advise you to use the russian audio, as it is a LOT better than the English audio. It can be a little tedious in the beginning, but once you get a hang of the game, it's a lot of fun to even do the side quests. It's also got multiple, equally satisfying endings depending on how you play Vasilisa. Even the ending with the most amount of sin is an interesting one!
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Just... Wow.The best game I've played in some time. It is a card battler, yes. But you get some point and click added to the mix, actual choice that matter and have consequences, great foklore, and even some riddles!In terms of replayability, you basically have an "evil" and "good" playthrough. I just finished, in normal difficultly, the "evil" playthrough and I really want to do the good one now!  It is a great game. The engine is... well, it is basic. At least at first glance. Do not be detered, as the art is great.This was really a great surprised and a great card game, all the way up with Slay the Spire and Roguebook!

Maybe I had to restart the game? Anyway, not for me but if you like more challenging games it might be more for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Cool art style and ideas, the card mechanics seem interesting but repetitive and overly simple, while the mechanics that should've been simpler are drastically more complicated. Lots of text and story that some people may enjoy but I just found it boring quite frankly. Lots of potential but after an hour and a half of playing I was just wanting to move on to a different game.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: I do not recommend this game, but I REALLY want to recommend it anyway. I love the art style, I love the card interactions, and I love the battling, but I am about halfway through the third seal and there has been absolutely zero difficulty to the game past about the first like 10 fights. At this point, by turn three, I can deal obscene damage while perfectly protecting myself. I have been playing on nightmare mode from the beginning, by the way. It definitely shouldn't be like this.I love the art style, but the 3D portions can be clunky and are overall unnecessary, but I find them cool nonetheless. The story is cool and I LOVE that you are learning Russian folklore. I LOVE the dub, but I really wish I knew there was an option to have it be Russian with English subs from the beginning. I would have selected that if I knew it was an option from the start.In any case, this game is not worth $25 because the combat becomes so dull so quick. By about the end of seal 2, I was practically falling asleep from both the combat and all the encounters that just don't have that much substance to them. I'd say it is maybe worth 10 retail and hope to get it on sale for 5. If you consider the story and how Russian folklore really hasn't been done before, it is worth more, but I can't value it like that because I care about the combat so much. So, take my review as you will. I really wish I could recommend it, since I loved the interactions in the combat and the folklore, but the fact that the combat gets so easy so quick, even when starting from Nightmare, makes it not recommended from me. Like I've got over 1000 roubles with nothing to spend it on, and that's with me already spending money frivolously.
