_childDocuments_.review: Throughout the playthrough of , my feelings have been really mixed, it was a rollercoaster of various emotions and thoughts because I've enjoyed some aspects of this game, but also this game has plenty that is annoying and quite bad.I feel like  in his review described certain things that were bothersome to me as well, so there are at least two of us who find issues with the morality system, managing chorts, and the boss battles. The combat system is either super easy, especially in the latter stages of the game - which was wonderful, or it gets super annoying and you have to (re)build decks specifically for that one boss - which wasn't wonderful at all. However, what I did appreciate in this scenario was the fact I could just skip through the battles once the game realised my efforts are going nowhere (might have been my difficulty setting perhaps), so that at least protected my sanity and it gave me the willingness to finish the game... which I definitely wanted to do and see how the story concludes, but I certainly won't replay, despite the fact, there's a lot to discover in terms of story, characters, playstyles, deck builds, different endings etc. also has plenty of moments that genuinely impressed me in terms of visuals. So much so, screenshots have been made and I could see many images as beautiful framed pictures on the wall, only for that feeling to be diminished by the poor & unappealing art style during the visual novel-esque parts of the game; these sequences were also heavily crippled by voice acting that was all over the place, but I have to confess,  the cat, sounds like  and it was cracking me up the whole time. The characters in general were quite good, I really wanted to see where the story takes them, how will  story end, what fate I as a player will concoct for her (intentionally or not). But even here nothing is 100%. Some story beats seemed kinda underwhelming, underdeveloped, certain plot points just seemingly ended abruptly when I expected there to be a battle for example, character moments many times came off rather strange as the morality system isn't that deep, some choices and actions seemingly didn't connect later for some reason... but I have to disclose that also could be my fault, as I was meddling with save files, to rollback to previous locations. Speaking of saves. The save system is quite bad, it felt counter-intuitive, oftentimes you are forced to take a single choice and live with it as going back to replay is not a convenient or viable option - which was the #1 cause for much of my frustration as I'm a player who likes to experiment with different scenarios before committing to my default goody-two-shoes playstyle. Several times happened that a dialogue choice ended the whole thing and I was back in the izba with no way to go back, which again, suck for my way of playing, for getting achievements, or just simply going back to replay individual areas. Having in the main menu a menu of individual chapters, individual days even would be from my point of view so much better and much favourable option.The facet of the game I enjoyed the most was the mythology, the lore. Going through those stories, engaging with various characters based on myths & legends from this part of the world - I'm a sucker for these kinds of things, so this was the most rewarding part of my playthrough. Definitely, something I would like to take a closer look at, and I hope the other work from  -  will have something more from the  region.Overall, I'm still torn, as I really want to like , I feel like it has the perfect combination of "game stuff" I personally like and gravitate towards, but to me, almost everything just misses the point, sometimes slightly, sometimes big time.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Was very powerful and much better than I was expecting.Be advised this is a very dark experience with mature themes and possibly disturbing content.The card battling was a bit too easy even on hard, but I had a very tuned deck. Multiple viable builds, but when I say it is too easy, that is only if you put thought into building a potent and focused deck.The story and atmosphere was incredible, especially toward the end of the game. Choices and decisions had more depth and possibility than I realized during the first two chapters and then I started doing some things differently. This was prompted by the words of an in-game character; excellent writing. Voice acting was great, graphics were rough but they worked and intense scenes still had powerful impact. Proof for me that quality graphics still isn't an essential element of a great game even in 2024.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Charming and addictive game with amazing atmosphere. The fairly simple graphical style does not keep the story from pulling you in, and in fact some of the environments look downright lovely. The story is unusual and engaging, and deeply steeped in Russian/Slavic folklore, much of which will be familiar to fans of the Witcher games and books. The card battles are fun and challenging, too. While the characters look very basic during gameplay (they're more nicely drawn in the frequent dialog screens), the audio really shines, and every line of dialog is fully voiced. I recommend playing with the Russian audio and English subtitles (unless your Russian is way better than mine) for extra immersion. A true gem that's hard to put down. I got it during the holiday sale but it's well worth the full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best i've played. very atmospheric, the lore and main story is very interesting and didn't get me bored not one bit. the music was fitting. i loved how many words and stories were based on real life myths and not just made up. i wish there was more to romance but i understand the whole premise behind it all is saving the husband that we get to see at the end, it would've been better if there was at least some more interactions with him overall. my only suggestion would be to have a way to organize the inventory based on price, type, date etc. other than that all good <3
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of issues, particularly around movement it feels quite terrible. But it is very much worth it if you enjoy a game that immerses you in a different world and has a lot of story. I quite enjoyed it, and the choices do seem consequential. The card games are interesting, but there is essentially no information in the game on how things are supposed to work, not is there really a lot of information online. _childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a moderately exciting story and is full of foreign terms that you have to look up in an encyclopedia. After about 9 hours of playing time, I got to the point where puzzle battles had to be completed. I have no idea how to solve these, because there is no tutorial or explanation. Apparently you have to use a certain order of certain cards, but which ones? If you fail a few times there is an option to skip these fights, but this is a poor solution. I would rather understand how exactly puzzle fights  work. There is also no hint system. Furthermore, the card descriptions are inadequate, confusing and poor translated, so you don't know exactly what each card does. That wasn't a big problem, because I played on the easiest difficulty level. But it's still something that could be improved. The card game that you can play with friends or occasionally with enemies from time to time is also not explained, at least I couldn't find an explanation for it anywhere, so I kept losing. This is very frustrating. It's a real shame that my fun was ruined for the reasons stated above.

_childDocuments_.review: honestly? love this game. it lacks some polish, sure, but makes up for it with overall fantastic art direction and sound design, unpredictable and very cool story, immersive world, and pretty satisfying card battler mechanics (speaking as a person with over 1200 hours in slay the spire).pros:- fully voice-acted, which i usually don't care for, but hearing all these old russian words actually spoken makes a huge difference for immersion- the worldbuilding in general. i feel like i learned so much about pagan russian folklore, and for that alone i deeply appreciate this game. (though i wish we had more lore for some of the cards. why is pryzor sticky, for instance?!)- love the art direction! shoutout to the card art, not just in the book, but for all the enemies' moves as well. fantastic adaptation of the permian animal style- speaking of art direction, the cinematography of each cutscene is actually amazing. i'd love to someday see a remastered version of this game with really polished graphics in the cutscenes- lovely sound design as well as soundtrack. love all the little flourishes and ui sounds with the folk instruments- good assortment of battle mechanics; i especially like the setup of koldun battles, even if they are the most annoying battles in the game. i suspect most players are split on whether puzzle battles are good or not, but i personally enjoyed themcons: - some ambiguous card text and tooltip text making it unclear what some cards or effects actually do- adding onto that, the computed zagovar damage is not always correct: it doesn't take your current bless stacks into account, nor does it correctly show how much damage an individual enemy in a group of enemies would take. so computing your actual damage every turn is difficult, which is not great for a card battler!- i suspect that there's only one viable deck strategy, maybe two - english translation is somewhat rough around the edges (though considering the amount of text in the game, i can understand the difficulty); voice acting sometimes reads different words than what's displayed - too many different art styles presented initially: when starting the game we go from nice 3D rendered book to nice 2D painted scenes to 3D point-and-click section to dating-sim-like 2D image dialog. a jarring series of transitions- 3D point-and-click graphics are fairly unpolished and i wish there had been a more natural way of showing the boundaries of each zone, rather than invisible walls for most of those segments- also, the fixed camera in the point-and-click sections can be disorienting when it moves. this is at its worst in the kickstarter backer graveyards (RIP to all those people btw)- i think the chorts could have been more punishing when idle. maybe they are on the highest difficulty?- [SPOILERS] i still don't *quite* understand who cursed the wedding, or what really happened to the beloved; i feel like the narrative didn't fully close the loop on thosestuff i just really liked:- the folksongs! what a great touch. props to the singers and whoever had the idea to include them. also the encyclopedia and bailichkas in general- proshka and karnysh! i love a good set of witch's familiars- also, shoutout to my two favorite one-off npcs: pierre and the "oh, what a life!" susedko
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who's always been really into world folklore, I'm pretty sure I've recommended this game to everyone I know. A great concept for a game where knowledge really is power. Depending on if you are accustomed to deck-building games like this, you might find this game quite easy or very challenging. My advice to anyone who is brand new to this gameplay style (or who just gets frustrated easily, like me) is that it's okay to die several times during boss battles and that sometimes less (cards) is more. Try not to get too discouraged even if a battle seems impossible at first. The sin system is also done in a really interesting way. Especially at the start, you accrue sins less through being openly malevolent and more often through inaction or passivity; choosing the option that makes things easier for you in the short term at the cost of knowing your actions will hurt other characters that you've likely never met and don't care about. It's very easy to think of it as a necessary evil when you don't see the consequences of your choices. On that note, however, I will admit that sometimes choices are worded in such an ambiguous way that you really have no way of knowing that you're committing a sin because you're not even sure what the option is implying. These instances feel less insightful and more frustrating. In a similar vein, this confusion in wording also extends to several other instances where you are given multiple choice answers to a question, but the answers are so short and vague that you can't tell what Vasilisa will actually say when you select that answer. I'm not sure if this is a result of troubles in translation or if it's by design. Overall, a great game if you like a somewhat dark folklore based game with some neat mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Watch my 6 minute review here (or read at your own pace below): Rewind from 2021, where being a witch is rather commonplace, to the late 1800’s, and you’re looking at quite a different political and religious climate.  In Black Book, you play as a young witch, or koldun, and explore Cherdyn, a land brimming with demons and spirits to be slain or trained into your service.  With so many choices to make and stories to follow, this deck-building card battler plays out more like a D&D adventure than any card-based game I’ve played.Story-Vasilisa is a budding koldun, a young woman learning the ways of a witch, and with the help of her grandfather Egor and some other friends she meets along her journey, will not only learn the ways of the Black Book, but the history and lore of Slavic mythology.  As she compiles new spells in her book and writes observations in her journal, her strength will grow, along with her influence over the area as she employs more chorts to do her bidding.  Vasilisa is a woman burning with the desire to revive her deceased husband, and she will stop at nothing to bring him back to the mortal world.  However, there are many obstacles standing in her way, the greatest of which are the seven seals preventing her from opening the Black Book, which will grant her wish to revive her beloved.  There is a bit of a morality spectrum here as you can choose to commit sins, sometimes unknowingly, or do good and help people.  The further you go in either direction, the more choices will be available to you in interactions.  And let’s talk for a moment about the interactions as Vasilisa goes on her quests.  These feel very much like D&D scenarios, with the setting and characters laid out to you, and you’re given several reactions to choose from.  Oftentimes you can rely on information gleaned from Vasilisa’s journal in order to make an educated decision, but even so sometimes the scenarios do not always play out as intended, and this can lead to some fun (or challenging) surprises.  Outside of the adventure scenarios, you will also have many encounters with people, some of which will stay with you throughout Vasilisa’s journey, like her grandpa Egor, who you can gain a lot of backstory and journal entries from.  He in particular reveals much of the history of the area and the Slavic mythology from which Black Book draws.Gameplay-While Black Book is a deck building card-battler, featuring some devilish monsters to overcome, this is one of the most intuitive and easy to learn card systems I’ve encountered, even though many of the card names are not in English.  Instead of discarding your hand at the end of each round and drawing a new hand as you would in a traditional deck builder, in Black Book you draw random cards, or spells, from your spellbook.  The larger your deck, the smaller chance that you’ll draw each card, and when you are at Vasilisa’s home, you have the ability to purchase more copies of cards you have discovered, up to a maximum of 4, or remove cards from your current deck.  On each turn, you can play up to two scroll cards, and one key card, as denoted in the upper left corner of the card, and the more cards you acquire, the more you’ll be able to learn and use some fun strategies.  For me, I liked to build my deck with as many black cards as possible, and utilize the “Well-versed” effect which makes cards more powerful for each black card played that turn.  Combined with some Firm cards which remain in play for multiple rounds, I was able to deal some massive damage and make quick work of some baddies.  You can also use some traditional witches items, like herbs which you can use once per round, and you can equip up to 3 enchanted items which will give you passive benefits. Overall, I found the battling system very intuitive and easy to learn, without having to deal with discards, and one-time-use cards, and the card choices kept me coming back to my spellbook and trying to optimize my strategy.Character Progression-There is some light skill progression available as Vasilisa gains experience through each battle and encounter.  With each level gained, you can increase a skill from across 4 different categories, with some abilities like adding equippable item slots, increasing the damage done by certain card types, or the skills that I leveled up early on which decreased the penalty for asking for a hint during conversational encounters.  These give you some added incentive to make the most of each opportunity, as you’ll gain more experience by doing more things, and even by pursuing optional quests.Art/Graphics-The art and graphics were both excellent and a bit of a let down.  The scenery and mood was fantastic, with dark shadows dominating the battle scenes, and flashes of light and magic breaking the darkness.  The landscapes outside of the battles were also lovely, with some light exploration even taking place where you can look around for hints and some spare herbs to pick.  Both of these scenes share in common some fantastic lighting, with some dull rays of light sneaking through the gnarled tree branches above.  Where the art let me down a bit was in the character design.  Everything in the game is built with a low-poly style, but there were times when the character models just felt a bit lacking, like I could see the cracks between their polygonal joints, or maybe it is the way they moved that just looks unnatural.Music/Sound-However, the music in Black Book is quite outstanding, with orchestral tracks featuring plenty of stringed and woodwind instruments, some chimes, and a lot of deep, foreboding tones.  It’s exactly what you would expect to hear as you adventure through the Russian countryside under the cloudy moonlight.  I haven’t mentioned this yet, but the characters are fully voice acted, and I really enjoyed Old Egor’s character in particular.  I think the pacing could use some work, as the narration is painfully slow and I found myself skipping it after an hour or so, although I did occasionally sit back and listen to the newly introduced characters spinning their yarns.So the question is, should YOU play Black Book?  I recommend it, and I would even suggest it to those not too familiar with the deckbuilding genre.  Although the language of the cards can be a bit difficult to understand at first, I think the lack of discard and draw new hand mechanics make this an accessible game for newcomers to the genre.  Plus you get a haunting story that you can skim or dive headlong into as you wish.

_childDocuments_.review: It's extremely good; One of the best turn based RPGs I've played since Darkest Dungeon. It's full of content and interesting lore, and if you do all the reading you'll come out of it knowing way more about Russian folklore than you once did. The combat is super strategic and interesting, and might have you staring at your pages a lot but that's fine by me. Just do yourself a favor and pick it up, and don't forget that you can stack statuses to high heaven. Amazing game, really hope to see more from these devs in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun to learn about Russian folklore with certain choices affecting some storylines. The card game aspect was new to me and somewhat interesting but I missed something and the difficulty spiked hard and I had no idea how to overcome the enemies and was effectively stuck in the mud with no hope. _childDocuments_.review: Dear Lord Yes. Incredible music. A hell of a story of Russian Folklore. Great Art Style. Above all that: A really fun and well thought out card game/deck builder on top. That ending though. Whew. It's so great to see games that really stick the landing. I'm putting this one near Inscryption for "What deckbuilders can be."
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: It took me 29 hours to finish this and that was with doing almost all of the side-quests. There is A LOT of game here for an indie-kickstarter project. It's no surprise to me that this game is always on the edge of "Overwhelmingly Positive".The biggest thing for me was that I actually LEARNED a lot about Easter European folklore when I played this, which is saying something since my only hobby is reading about creatures/stories/folklore from around the world. I'd say that I didn't know the fine details behind the origin of many demons, creatures, etc about 50% of the time here and that alone was worth the time. You actually have to read the in game journal or take notes as you play in order to answer questions correctly, which I think is pretty sweet.The only gripe I have is that puzzle battles mostly suck because when they occur you often have cards that you've never seen or played before, so you don't even know where to start. But, fortunately you can skip them, which is something that was not avail on launch day. The voice acting is a little janky but i don't really have any issue with it because I feel like it kind of fits the characters. Narrator grew on me over time.If you like card battlers, RPGs, long stories or any combination of those you'll probably really enjoy this. All things considered I'd say this is probably in my top 3 games of the year for 2021.  I enjoyed the story, I enjoyed unlocking cards, I enjoyed choosing the "light" path over the "dark" path.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably one of the most innovative story based game I've played in a while. It is innovative because of how much cultural depth it goes into. I don't know how accurate all the lore is, but it feels really accurate. It feels like you could play this whole game and then get a minor in Russian Mythology or something. It's so cool how in-depth it is and I can tell whoever wrote it really loved making it. It plays and reads just like an old fairy tale. People just spew out nonsense (ah yes, you forgot to cross your dishes! That's why you have a demon in your house!) in such a fantastical way. And you are rewarded for not only reading the lore but retaining and deducing answers through the lore. You get XP in certain parts when you have to deduce what the issue is in a certain case. Like why people are doing a ritual or what kind of demon you're dealing with. I love that. It makes me more interested in educating myself on the particular piece of lore I'm given instead of just skipping through it all like I normally do. This is a deckbuilder, but it also is basically a visual novel in gameplay. There are RPG elements, you level up your character for example. I'm about 14 hours in to the game and on Chapter 2 so it is a longer game than I anticipated it would be. Questlines can go on for several levels and characters reappear throughout- I really love that. They also attempt to ensure the content doesn't get same-y by throwing in battle puzzles every so often. Also, as you unlock seals, you are given more varieties of card sets to remake your deck with- so the creators were really dedicated to ensuring you would have some reason besides just lore and story to push you through the 30-40 hours of gameplay. I can't fault this game for much of anything, this is definitely a 9/10 game for me. The only reason I don't think it's 10/10 is because I am not in love with visual novels in general- reading isn't my favorite pastime. But still, that's more of a personal preference than a complaint. If you like story-rich deckbuilders that aren't your cut-and-dry typical story, this is really worth a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Very unique card game, RPG, and adventure. None of those labels do it justice though. The translation isn't perfect but its very good. The songs are genuinely incredible recordings.

_childDocuments_.review: It is very clear that this game was made with a lot of love. There is much lore and I've learnt so much about Eastern European mythology, especially Russian and Komi-Permian ones. There were some English voice acting mistakes like actors repeating lines and some of the voices did not suit the characters in my opinion, and the 3D animation look of the human characters were horrible. Best strategies involve using a curse and ocean depths build or a build that uses waste and curse.Favourite sound track is Boss of the Evil Spirits, music suits the game, its pretty hard to get good battle themes but this game did well.There are a few bugs though. -back buttons on controller occasionally don't work and sometimes -restart battle doesnt work and leaves a blank area forcing you to reload.

_childDocuments_.review: I like the Slavic Folklore element, and the art-style; which is quite abstract/minimal; combined with the more storybook illustration in the cut-scenes.The game so far has a lot of voice-over; which is nice - though if you may find yourself skipping at times if you read the accompanying text quickly.The combat system is pretty cool; turn-based deck-building - but with the addition of allowing you to string multiple cards together in one turn - cards also synergise; adding an additional tactical layer.the game is split into two phases - your home base; where you can prep, learn about the world, and characters - and the exploration phase; which has you traversing a map with various points to visit.During these, it feels reminiscent of adventure books that I used to read as a child; you get a plot point, and make a decision, then read the outcome - it's a nice touch.It's still early days, but I've enjoyed what time I have spent playing enough to recommend it.Definitely worth the money, I would say.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros and cons are down below) Don't forget to drop a like if it was useful! Check out the prologue of the game here:+ The concept is amazing! I wanted to see something based on russian legends and folklore for a long time! Being a russian gal, I can tell that everything this game features is pretty accurate: from the spirits people used to believe in to the rituals they actually performed. The game kind of reminded me a lot of the cartoons of my childhood: The Three Bogatyrs and Prince Vladimir.+ The card part of the game is exciting as well! It is simple but unique at the same time. Reminded me of Slay the Spire. I experience the fighting of the Koldunya level of difficulty and it seemed manageable but pretty tense when it comes to bosses. I’m really excited to play more and try building different decks, I’ll update this comment when I do.+ I also like the text-based part of the adventure as well. I like that some parts of it require to study Russian lore (which is not text-heavy, just 1 small interesting paragraph) and lead to different scenarios so your choices affect all little encounters you have and the ending as well. + The art style is absolutely amazing! I especially love the little animations performed during spell casting.- The card part of the game, as exciting as it is at the beginning, might get repetitive after a while as people have pointed out in other reviews. Moreover, I want to add that some card effects lack explanation and can be understood only through trial and error which is not necessarily bad but can be frustrating at times.- Also, there is such a mechanic as “Puzzle Fight” which reminds me a lot of puzzles that Thronebreaker used to introduce. These parts can cause a lot of frustration even tho after a recent patch, they can be skipped after several failed attempts.Overall:This game reminded me a lot of Witcher 3 only without open world and with card-based combat. And a lot of Thronebreaker as well. And that is a good thing in my opinion. Slavic folklore makes this enjoyable experience unique and absolutely fascinating. I can’t wait to play more and update this comment if my opinion changes. As for now don't hesitate - check the game out! Also, please, like this comment if it was useful (I hope it was), so it can be useful to other people as well)

_childDocuments_.review: Linear young witch (Koldun) story with some roll playing elements, demon management (chorts) and a card based (spell pages) combat system. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a real gem.  The lore is unique, I learned so much about Russian mythology.  The card game is challenging and fun.  You can employ a lot of different styles of play and it helps to adapt your deck to certain fights.  There's math, lots of math.  To me that's a plus.  It's  long too, you get a lot for your buck.  10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: The story, the folklore, the characters - all very well done. I thoroughly enjoyed them.Lots of ways to resolve encounters, which I appreciate.I liked the idea behind the puzzles, but I feel like the implementation is poor. Too exacting with the card puzzles, pixel perfect accuracy with the narrative puzzles, and no way to check the encyclopedia in the middle of a dialogue puzzle (i.e. I failed them sometimes because of something my CHARACTER would know, but I didn't remember offhand).However, this game bills itself as a card battler, and there it's only so-so. I like the ability to change my deck so easily, but card removal is too easy and it always seemed optimal to make a small but boring deck. Normally I would be ok with that - just don't optimize the deck that much - but the difficulty has HUGE spikes and the optimization feels necessary. I'm fighting bosses with 150 health that do 15 damage a turn when I can block 5-10 and do 4-8 damage a round. Some fights are very tough very early on.The fights are also kind of repetitive - I didn't see too much variation in mechanics, enemy moves, enemy team composition. So each story beat was several boring fights with one really hard one.Overall, if you want the story/narrative experience, this is a good game for it. But don't go into expecting a good card battler like the tags say.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the most enjoyable experience I've had in gaming for a really long time.Before I say anything else, if you don't enjoy turn-based or "card games" you won't enjoy the gameplay here. That being said, here are my thoughts for what they're worth! Others have covered the premise of the game in nice detail already! However, I will say that the level of attention to Russian folklore remains incredible even halfway through the game. The music that is in the game is beautiful and a sincere joy to come across! Despite some of the more low fidelity scenes owing to the graphics style the entire game still oozes with charm.If you're even the slightest bit interested in Russian religion and folklore, this game is for you! I rarely if ever buy supporter packs and the like, but I happily got it for this game.So much love to the developer!

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, a very good game and would recommend it for those who enjoy RPGs, card battles (skipable after four failed battles), and Slavic mythology. Hopefully the developers have fixed these glitches, but as of (July 28, 2023) the card Blood & Clot stopped working half way through the game (health loss != defense), unable to save the game at a particular stage of the map, Rebirth from Priputnik Herb did not work during the battle with grandpa, some dialogs were not translated into English, and a number of other minor but noticeable glitches. _childDocuments_.review: An enchanting Russian-inspired interactive visual novelIt's probably best to introduce it as an interactive visual novel. Sure, it's assembled of different parts (roguelike deck-building, resource-management, some detective work), but what you'll be doing the most really is reading.The game throws you right into Russian names and traditions, so if you want to be even decently competent - you start reading the encyclopedia. But still, as someone who was fascinated by it all, it worked for me. The art is nicely done in this folk style. The voice-acting is beautifully done (love the accents), and it really helped the immersion into the lore of this world. The characters were also a lot of fun to help, and by the time the game ended, I was a bit sad to be saying goodbye to all these friends.Some things got repetitive, like walking around. I wish there was a way to just skip the damn map traveling animation or character dialogs for replayability. But the combat was always compelling, as each chapter unlocks new cards and new tricky foes that required exploring a new deck. There were even new puzzle fights later on, so the game was able to successfully keep things a little fresh in that aspect. All in all, a really interesting mix of different game mechanics. Just note that it's all tied together in a stunning visual novel, and some parts can get a little repetitive.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: If I ever get my own wish of working on a video game, I’d want it to be something akin to what Morteshka created with Black Book. I’m not necessarily talking about making a deck-building RPG, set in the Russian countryside of the 19th century, but something that showcases the passion and effort invested into its creation with every second it spends on your screen.The setting, historical background, and themes of Black Book are more than a backdrop on which the story is told. Rather, they thoroughly shape everything the game has to offer. Whether it be the 3-D portion of the visuals - reminiscent of traditional Russian rag dolls; the soundtrack – comprised of instruments characteristic for the time period and a capella; or the story itself – influenced heavily by Russian folklore, so much so that you wouldn’t be entirely off the mark for calling it an adaptation of the various folk tales from the era. Some of these elements may remind players of The Witcher, but here they are presented in a more grounded, supernatural way, so as to provide the game with a grittier, less fantasy-oriented atmosphere - one of its strongest aspects, further enhanced by the amazing lighting, particle effects, and scene design. The only things hurting Black Book visually are scene variety, some clunky camera work, and a lack of anti-aliasing.The story of Black Book is powerful and heavy, packing an impactful finale and a writing style evocative of the folk tales that inspired it. It also gets sincerely funny at times, with a great, dry sense of humor to it. Sadly, the number of grammatical errors in the English subtitles brings it down a bit, and while the VO is fine, it’s incomparably worse than the Russian one. I'm perplexed as to why it’s the default option. You’ll be doing the game a huge disservice if you don’t switch it out immediately.The pacing itself is a bit questionable. Structured much like a TV show, each chapter presents a standalone arc that only further in becomes thematically and pragmatically tied to the overarching narrative. What kicks off the plot is left vaguer than it should be, making these arcs much more interesting than the whole. The story offers a lot of opportunities to learn about Russian culture and folklore, including an extensive in-game glossary. Still, some things are left unclear as a lot of entries go by the same name. The glossary also plays a part in the gameplay, as you’ll sometimes be asked questions relating to these terms. There is a hint option that can help you out, but it occasionally bugs out and doesn’t work.The gameplay is divided into three portions: exploration, conversations, and combat. It has issues, but it’s still a satisfying gameplay loop. You begin each day at your  (home) where you can talk with your companions, peasants looking for advice, manage the Black Book, and demons in your service. After that, you’re presented with a map, marked with your goal for the day, as well as several other locations you can visit on the way to it. Each location will have some sort of encounter to it, either combat or an opportunity to roleplay, usually in relation to your side quests. Roleplaying is fun, but becomes formulaic at a certain point, with there only being up to 4 options in a conversation at a time, one of which is "leave" and some of which are poorly defined, leading to you doing something you only intended to inquire about. The decisions you make during these roeplaying segments can sometimes increase, or in much rarer scenarios decrease, your Sin counter – a poorly explained and implemented morality system that determines which sort of ending you can get.The Black Book represents your deck, with each card being a page within it. Passing certain milestones within the story provides you with new sets of cards, which you combine in combat to create a spell. You can also use herbs and other equipable items to your advantage. However, as things get more complex, the explanations provided don’t suffice, leading to unexpected interactions between the various effects. There’s also a leveling system composed of multiple skill trees, though it may as well have been included within the linear progression. In-between missions, you can send your demons to perform various tasks for you, which will always result in someone getting cursed and you receiving Sins for sending them out. If you refrain from it, you’ll get cursed instead, which makes you weaker in combat during your next quest. However, none of the tasks you send your demons out to do are presented as necessary. Aside from there being a lore reason to have your demons, they never do anything relating to the story.Almost all of Black Book’s characters are strongly defined and easy to connect to, even if they don’t have much to do with the story itself. Certain characters can even join you as companions, each with a unique ability that can help you out during combat. Unfortunately, they ultimately end up underutilized, as they rarely impact the plot outside of the quests you meet them in and the loyalty quests you unlock later after talking to each companion enough. Sadly, the deckbuilding is somewhat constrained as well, with a UI I can only describe as claustrophobic. You can also save up to three decks, but can’t swap them out mid-battle – only when you lose, which sort of defeats the purpose, as you can rearrange your deck at that point anyway. You’re also restricted to the same max number of cards in your deck for the entirety of the game, meaning you’re not really expanding your deck as you progress, as much as changing it out entirely. Versatility isn’t the name of the game. The difficulty doesn’t increase aside from the boss fights, some of which will be pretty much impossible with certain builds, leaving intentional defeat so you can swap out your deck the only option. With regular encounters almost always being a breeze no matter your set-up, the ~45 hour-long journey is sadly not exciting all the way through. Puzzle battles (encounters with a fixed selection of cards, requiring to be beaten within a time limit) try to add more variety but are too few and far in-between to have a notable impact.Just like the Russian VO, the soundtrack of the game is great, if a bit lacking in variety and spectacle. You’ll come across some amazing a capella folk songs as collectibles, but these tie into what’s happening on-screen at only one occurrence.  Performance-wise, the game ran at a stable 60 FPS at max settings all the way through, except during the final battle, where the intense rain effect swallowed up about 20 frames. Other than the clunky camera work during the exploration segments, there’s also some terrible pathfinding to watch out for, leading to temporarily getting stuck or walking off-screen. The save system is rather awkward, always resetting a scene to its beginning should you load from it, even if the option to save is present throughout. Also, whatever you do, do not roll your mouse wheel during conversations, as each tick skips a line of dialogue, with no way to read them later.Overall, Black Book is an enjoyable effort of much love. The lack of variety and depth in its mechanics make the game feel a tad too long, but it's the narrative that'll win you over. Swap to the Russian VO, crank up the difficulty, and try not to burn yourself out – and you’re in for an unforgettable journey.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very, very good.Combat-wise it's very close to Slay the Spire, but, what is much more important, it has incredible grimdark vibe of Slavic folklore, sort of like Witcher, but much more realistic and dark.Story is also great, you are invested and care for what is going on, which is pretty rare in nowadays games.Definetely give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: My personal favorite of 2021. The game has an amazing story set in XIX century Russia. it focuses on Slavic myths and somewhat reminds me of the first Witcher game. The amount of effort put into researching all those myths and creating the story is truly impressive.My only complaint is the game balance. The first third of the game is fairly balanced and challenging but soon after the game becomes super easy even on max difficulty. I finished the game using much less than half of the available cards. There was barely any need to try anything new.But the story and characters is definitely where it's at. If you like this kind of genre or setting, you'll enjoy this game a lot.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Though it is technically a card game, I think of it more as an RPG.Most combat encounters have you using a deck of cards that determine what attacks, defense, or status effect cards you have available when fighting. Occasionally you'll be asked to solve a "puzzle-battle", which involves a preset deck that you'll have to use to kill the enemy within a preset number of turns.In between combat encounters, you'll be presented with a variety of events where you'll have 1-4 choices that effect the outcome. Now and again, you'll be given a sort of multiple-choice question to see if you've been paying attention to the story, and if you answer correctly you get some sort of reward.The voice acting is ok, the art is ok too, and the game is spoon feeding information on Slavic culture, AND I find it all absolutely fascinating.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this game with very little expectations, so I feel extremely rewarded!Loved how deeply the creators went into Russian regional folklore and dialect, it´s not your standard Baba Yaga game - even as a Russian you get to learn a lot. The game is quite slowly paced, but I didn´t mind it at all, collecting little pieces of lore was a lot of fun. There´s a lot narration instead of being able to explore yourself, which would be a downside for many, but it kind of works here.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: I played on the difficulty above Normal.- Liked the card gameplay, even if it confused me a bit at first. Felt easier to learn the nuances than something like Slay the Spire.- The folklore confused me the most because of all the weird things people had to do to avoid evil spirits etc and many of the words and concepts were very foreign to me. It gave a feeling of "playing in old times" though, which was the point to immerse yourself. - The art was alright but I disliked the 3D version of the characters. Looked like something from a mid 90s 3D game. The world looked alright in comparison, since it just seemed like a stylistic choice.- The voice acting ranged from good to pretty bad. Words in English were often mispronounced but I could excuse that as "the Russian way of saying them". Thankfully the main voice actors did fine (like Vaselisa and the main narrator).Over all: I grew to enjoy it a lot.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a gem. It is visually pleasant, the voices of the characters are well mixed and add life to the game. The background music and the traditional songs are magnificent. I'm not usually a card game player but on this game the handling is fluid although it is complete. The story itself is well written and it's a good idea to leave several paths that lead to different endings.In short, this game is accessible for any type of player and immerses you in its atmosphere. I highly recommend it if you want to discover or re-discover Slavic mythology.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR;Pros: Story, cultural references and real mythology, choices matter, interesting deck choices (including exponential growth options), lots of items and effects to choose from.Cons: Combat gets very easy very quickly and the character can become massively overpowered by making the right deck-building choices.  Items can serious reduce difficulty even further.  A few very minor bugs that can easily be ignored.Very interesting game - solid story, choices make some difference, but also very linear.  Characters you save turn up later in the story.  There's a great deal of real mythology in the game, and if you're interested in real world culture, this game has a fair amount of it from a region that doesn't see much popular portrayal, at least in the States.Combat is pretty easy - you can develop a very effective deck pretty easily and the enemies just can't keep up, even at the highest difficulty.  Using the right item set, you can wipe out most generic encounters before the enemy has a chance to take a turn.  By turn 3 in the final boss battle, you can viably hit him for damage an order of magnitude beyond his max HP with no need for worry about randomness while being utterly impervious at the same time).  That said, there are a number of battles where this strategy won't work and there are some puzzle events where you fight with a fixed deck and a fixed number of turns, sometimes with only 1 solution.There is some complaint about the clicking move mechanic, and its annoying.  That said,  just use WASD controls.  There is minimal moving the character around, so even if this were a valid complaint, it wouldn't impede most players' enjoyment of the game in any noticeable fashion.  There are a couple of puzzles that also made me wonder what the devs were drinking when they wrote the UI, but they were still understandable and the tasks were done with quickly.There are some bugs that could be worked out.  In 2 conversations (outs of hundreds), the character speaks in English, but the text is displayed in Cyrillic.  Under particular conditions involving redrawing cards, you can also cause some cards to display in their "effect in your spell" display in cyrillic as well.  But as far as I saw, nothing game-breaking, or even especially annoying.  By the time you get the card that allows you to redraw your hand, you probably won't need to check what your result is going to look like, both because you've already played enough to know what it'll do, and know for sure the enemy you're hitting is very dead.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: point and click for not many reasons, could've left this out and had cutscenes on autopilot ( as they mostly do anyways ) it's all voice acted, I guess? mileage may vary. from the comments i read here, a lot of the voice acting in English is sub-par. I have no frame of reference, so take it for what you will, All I know is they allow you to automatically advance the text for dialogue so it doesnt cut the audio - which is great for me for rrecordings. other than this, this is a pretty good card game. they mix up the tried-and-true Slay the Spire formula, and have their own creative jukes on the genre. it's dripping with that other-worldly, not-quite, but-sort-Earth-like atmosphere - and you are given tons of lore for ( what i assume to be Russian folklore ) terms and phrases, such as chorts - demonic aides of Witches. The combat is very STS, and it mixes it up by allowing you to combin cards into spells that change how they operate. Other than that, same thing - advanced warnign on intended enemy actions - items you can use and the like. You also have a skill tree in this game, which allows you to raise certain aspects. IN addition to this, you also have a morality gauge - you can sin, or not - and the choices will affect later choices, and lock you into others. ( devs had said there's at least two endings based on morality so far ) the graphical style is nice - albeit, a bit stunted when they shift to the 2nd still drawings ( which do a good enough job to represent the characters - but look really, really bad compared to the stylized low-poly versions - just my personal taste - if you're jonesin for some Slay the spire like gameplay, but with a russian twist involving demons, witches, and sending chorts to curse people - maybe this will suit your fancy.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Great story and characters.- Turn-based combat is fun and actually gets really challenging towards the end.- I also really liked the deck-builder gameplay that ties into the turn-based combat.- A lot of the monsters are from the Witcher so this felt like a fun cross-over.Cons:- The game economy is badly balanced. I always had too much money that I don't know what to do with. Wish there were more high-value equipment to buy near end-game. Overall, 8/10. Great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Overall yes I'd recommend the game. Great stuff: 1.  A lot of Slavic folklore, cool tales and mythical creatures such as mermaid, leshiy, werewolves etc2. Good story line and variety in endings3. Characters you can sympathise with, nice voice acting4. A lot of variety in choices, you can fight an enemy or try to persuade them or even play cards with them to have it your way (keep a close eye on details, if you choose correctly you can avoid a lot of fights!)5. Cool sin mechanic, ordering devils around is kinda nice6. Card game - played it  a lot in my childhood, really easy and fun game (but beware sometimes opponents may cheat, especially supernatural folk)7. Nice puzzles - when you have to win in few rounds or under other conditions8. Interesting fights - a lot of variety with cards. I generally dislike card games but this one is somewhat interestingNot so great stuff:1. Save system is bad, you can't save before an important choice and then load game and try again if you failed. You get rolled back quite a bit sometimes. I do recommend however to save before each location just in case.2. Moving is cumbersome at times.. I had my character get stuck in terrain many times. Or I couldn't move out of some corner3. Graphics... The game design is quite interesting, however it feels unfinished. Like textures for the models were drafted and this is how they went into production.. Specifically during cut scenes - it's just ugly (in my view). Some monsters look better than the others. 4. Some chapters feel more long than the others, and feel somewhat boring. Would be nice if it progressed a bit faster.Another thing is - localisation.. I'm lucky to be fluently speaking few languages. Don't get me wrong, English localisation is very good, however the expression and the feel of some conversations is very different to the original. It's more 'flat' and emotionless than in Russian if that makes sense. One of the reasons is using a lot of words and expressions from predecessor language. Another reason is words that just cannot be ideally mapped to English words. Again, English localisation is great, but if you can understand Russian I'd recommend switching to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Great story and setting, while deckbuilding is a bit lackluster. Plenty of choices to make, and they often come with consequences later in the story. I had more fun learning about the local folklore and mythology than I had with the gameplay, since broken builds can be made very easily, making most of the cards you unlock obsolete. Either way, great fun, get it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Such a unique, surprisingly effective blend of story-based adventure and Slay the Spire inspired combat. The localisation nails the vibe for the game, and the underlying mechanics are really well polished. The simple yet evocative art style brings it all together into a pretty engrossing package, I enjoyed this game for a lot longer than I thought I would.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: This story based game is refreshing in the content it covers: it was delightful to learn something about Russian folklore, even if only at a surface level. However it has a lot of major weaknesses that suck some of the joy out of its unique charm.This is not a good strategy game. Combat boils down to "play the best cards, and wear the right immunity item". There are interesting interactions between some cards, but exploring them is unnecessary: only once did I ever feel like building a deck around "waste", and never bothered to touch mechanics involving curse, or self damage. All I ever needed to do was draw lots of cards, and then play them all, using the "gesture" mechanic.The puzzle sections are no exception. These are all damage optimization problems, and while some are challenging, none are interesting. What lessons they teach need never apply to the regular combat in the rest of the game. The over-world aspect of the game is severely lacking in polish. Just walking around and picking up herbs feels clunky, and incredibly unresponsive. You struggle to click the "right" spots on the ground. This is also how you control the camera angle, enhancing the frustration. To the developers credit, if you manage to get wedged behind something, collision with the object will turn off after around 15 seconds, so you can un-stick yourself. I suspect the fact that most of the game is spent staring at a 2d map, instead of the 3d locations, is that the developers understand the weakness of these sections, and wisely chose to break them up. However this doesn't fix the problem that they're no fun.As a hard-core fan of deck building games, and as someone who enjoyed the story, I felt compelled to finish the game. While the choice of endings available to you are at least consistent with what is set up throughout the story, none of them are surprising, or especially satisfying.I write this long, ranting review, because I feel like there was real thought and effort put into crafting this, and I wish I could see more of it shine through. The style of the 3d set pieces seems like a great choice for an indie developer: background areas are unique, and there are a lot of them, the low resolution assets allow the designers to paint in broad strokes, and it works pretty well. The writing, and voice acting, are very good, and are only ever bogged down by slow pacing, or the repetitive nature of some encounters. The mechanics involving resources, pages, and items are very interesting, it's just that the game doesn't push you to explore them. Anyway, out some delusional sense of self importance, I would end this rant with a wish-list of things I wish had been different: - Add a UI to the 3d areas that controls where you walk. No more clicking on the ground. Herbs and items are collected when you click on them, from any distance, using the actual bounding box of the herb. - Add sections to the game that reward you for pushing you deck as far as it can go. (How many chorts can you defeat in three turns? How much damage can you deal in a turn?) These sections could help push players to try out different archetypes. - Integrate the 2d map, and the 3d set-pieces into one screen. Too much time is spent staring at a black sketch of some woods and ponds, when you already have so many wonderful set-pieces! - Let me remove all the pages from the book when I want to start fresh, and implement the 13 page minimum by refusing to let me start a battle until said limitation is met. Clicking on something and failing to remove it is annoying. - Record a description of sins and good deeds in the black book, and let me see how they cancel each-other out. This could also be a flavorful and satisfying way to allow the "sin" counter to go above zero. - Real curses! The in game results of encounters are somewhat limited. (Money/sin/miss out on exp) If wrong answers could curse you, the same way that the chorts in your pester do, the different kinds of demons you encounter, and the consequences of angering them, would feel way more real. Ok that's all. Now that I'm finished with this negative review, I'm off to steal milk from a cow.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: A charming dive into Slavic folklore with captivating visuals, rife atmosphere, engaging cultural education, impactful decision-making, and exciting narrative progression. There is a LOT of game here. My only major irk was one particular boss that made me completely build another deck [the ethereal ghoul], though I was having a grand, fun time with the one I had so painstakingly assembled. It put a halter on some momentum that had carried me through the previous two hours of gameplay in a blurred flash of fun. (Also sometimes the words didn't match what was being said, and some VO hiccups that got neglected, but I'm not faulting them heavily on that)
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: The combat does not allow for a great variety of combat.  Three hours in and on the second main quest every card either does damage or adds shield points. Some cards will restore health points or remove debuffs but that's it.  The game constantly gives you blocks of text about Slavic folklore and then punishes you if you don't remember it when they quiz you later.  The game keeps track of "sins" but it doesn't tell you what is a sin before you take an action and a lot of the time it's really unclear what they're even asking.  In the prologue the giant burning skull asks "how many demons will you take on" that's what the game is about right? I'm going to take on every demon and win. No they actually meant how many demons will you take with you to terrorize the villagers and bring you cash.  More sin points for me.  Pick up a handful of dirt near an empty grave SIN!
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: absolutely fascinating, unique and awesome game!! the russian/slavic lore is deeply integrated into the game and it was great learning about it, i appreciated so many mechanics in the game, including the ability to test your knowledge! i typically don't like deck building games but i made an exception for black book because it looked really cool, and i am so glad i did! artstyle is amazing, story was great, you have a cat, really interesting mechanics to the game. loved it, will definitely come back and replay in the future to try and get a different ending. the balance of story to fights/cutscenes, etc, was perfect imo. i would definitely recommend giving it a shot if you're on the fence!
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was having a blast with this card building game. The theme was original enough. Then came "battle puzzles". Those are not games with your deck. It's a puzzle with a fixed deck, fixed cards, and you have to do exactly what the game expect you to do in a timely fashion, or game over.The game is so much aware of the fact that it's ♥♥♥♥, that after some fails, you will get a nice "skip puzzle" button. I do not want to skip. I want to understand what I can do that i'm not seeing. Since almost all guides I found around this battle are not up to date, I'm left wondering if I'm facing a bug and an unbeatable puzzle, a missing description on the card (which may well be possible, since the game is not in english originally and lot of information seem to have been lost in translation from russian) or me being absolutely stupid (which i would not dismiss, but before that one battle, I had no real trouble with other puzzles).Yeah, I'd suggest to you:; "skip the game" or buy it only at big sale price. Also don't expect to find support; most guides are not up to date, and most (useful? i don't know) posts on the forums are in russian.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: It is no exaggeration to say that Black Book is my favourite game of 2021 so far. The story is engrossing and employs traditional Russian folklore to great effect in telling a moving and fascinating narrative. The card-combat system is extremely addictive, too, and allows for a great deal of variety between combat sessions, never letting things become stale or boring. My only complaint is that the purpose of the cards in combat was sometimes a little unclear, which I suspect was down to a translation problem, but otherwise I would HIGHLY recommend this title. After work today I will likely restart again for another playthrough, as even after 27h of playtime I don't think I'm done with this wonderful game.9.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to recommend this game because it seemed like a decent deck builder with a great atmosphere, but its flaws just get in the way of the good stuff.Here are my two main issues with the game:I will maybe try this game in a lower difficulty, to see if these issues might be less problematic this way, but right now this does not make me recommend this game despite the fact that it seems like a very interesting and polished game.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Promising card battle game with a lengthy story based on Slavic Myths. You play as a witch who can use the black book to cast spells. She can use this to defeat enemies in battle, but also on people to help them or curse them if they are annoying you. This allows you to play good or evil, which can affect the outcome of the story.The combat is rather mediocre because the strategies you can use are rather limited. While there are several innovative gameplay mechanics, most battles can be won by just debuffing the enemies in combination with standard attacks. You unlock new cards every chapter, but lots of these are stronger versions of cards you already own, while enemies get stronger as well. I ended up finishing the game, but this was mostly thanks to the story and setting.Despite the simple graphics, the game looks amazing. The use of colors and lightning is extremely well done. The game world exists of small areas where you can run around freely. This is a nice addition, but the invisible walls and uncontrollable camera are annoying.Black Book is worth playing, but not without flaws.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Fun story driven game with a nice touch of strategic turned-based combat. You play as a Russian witch, for a lack of better words. The game is filled with an enormous amount of Russian folklore that takes the player back to simpler times of wooden houses and stone stoves. I am 5 hours in and gathering from my Black Book, I have many, many hours to go.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: The shortest way to put this is: If you're interested in the setting, you will enjoy the game. The highlight is definitely experiencing the atmosphere, learning the lore (+ for gameplay purposes), and unlocking stories/songs. If the setting does not interest you, this is probably a skip.The other mechanics are not bad by any means. Combat ranges from serviceable to pretty good (albeit a bit easy), but I haven't tried the roguelike mode. It's a deckbuilder but with a small twist compared to other games with the same combat mechanic.I only tried English VA to check how it is. Ranges from serviceable to very good, depending on the character. Nothing groundbreaking but it does the job and didn't have any random, glaring issues like some characters in Gothic for example. The only truly subpar aspect of the game is in 3D models which are laughable at times. It does suck you out of the immersion/atmosphere for some specific assets, but exploring an area is such a minor part of the game that it's not a big deal.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, what an adventure that one was! I was sucked in from the very first seconds that I spent in this game. The atmosphere, representation of folklore, music, voice acting (Russian ofc), and story were all superb. Though, a few times the story did unnecessarily slowed down I still believe it was masterfully crafted and presented.For the weak points, I would mention clunky point-and-click controls in open-ish locations and an absolute lack of challenge on normal difficulty.I put 30h in the game, while I usually get tired with most of the games after about 10-12h, so it should tell that it does not get boring.Yeah, you should play it. 9.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Black Book is a game about Slavic folklore with a deckbuilding turn-based gameplay, so what's the big deal about it? the game creates such an intense story-telling and atmosphere that will draw you into it, and you will immerse in the world designed for youthe game is fully voice-acted; hearing all these old Russian words being actually spoken makes a huge difference in terms of immersionthere's a huge depth to its lore ,explore and reading them is really intresting ( leshen in witcher 3 is here for example )plenty of actions with consequences, moral choices and different ways of solving the problemscharacters are all mysterious and worth your time to speak with all of themso after all I love this game, and it's a 8.5/10 for me recommended 👍
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: PROS- Full Voice Acting- Gameplay Relevant Lore- Multiple Endings- Huge variety of cards- UI lets you build backup deck conformations and save them- If you die, you can restart the battle after fixing your deck and choosing new items to equip- Plot with loads of dramaCONS- Despite being a roguelike, i don't think its very replayable.While I couldn't play this game for long swaths of time, I did find myself always wanting to pick it up and keep picking at the story. It's not very stressful, and the creativity and style of the slavic folklore world always made me curious to see what's next.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: At its core, it's a deck-building game. Combat is fun and the cards are pretty, and if combat gets a little tedious after a while, you can experiment with different builds. The game also gives you lots of options to solve conflict without fighting. But what really sets the game apart from other deck-building games, is the atmosphere and a gripping story. This is one of those games that make me completely forget the time, like a book I just can't put down. It's also a fun way to learn about Slavic folklore.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: I am still on edge between nay or yay, been switching the directions of those thumbs for a while. My main difficulty to truly recommend this is the disconnect between the atmosphere of the lore and world's artwork. While the Slavic folklore is intricate and filled with various spirits, traditions  and rules, the minimalistic world, where they are supposed to live in, feels empty with few herbs scattered around. But don't get me wrong, it ain't a baaaaad game. It has great lore and deck building mechanism is very well done, kudos for that. If you enjoy reading short stories and card battles, go ahead with checking out the game. For me it needed that extra special setting of overall world atmosphere, which would piece everything together as one.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: I haven´t finished the game yet, but after 34.8 hours of playing I must say: great game! 10/10 Engaging story, very interesting setting with slavic mythology and folklore theme and gameplay isn´t repetitive, you can find yourself in the middle of the game and stumble upon new mechanics (for example, in one chapter, you play "detective", questioning people and try to figure out the villain). You also unlock new cards in time and need to rebuild your deck facing different enemies. (Major) card battles are challenging enough, but not too hard. Of course, you can set difficulty at the beggining of the game. The game has also some classic RPG mechanics as items collecting, skill building or sin system based on your decisions. The game gives you different solutions to the problems sometimes, for example, you can choose to hop to the battle or persuade the opponent or to play hazard card game for your soul.Athmosphere of the game is beautiful, it has a nice artstyle and graphics is simle, but effective. Original voiceacting is great (I play with english subtitles, but you can set english dabing if you like).
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Great story line and very interesting fleshed out characters. The folklore is seamlessly weaved into the story and makes the world you are in seem huge! The songs are beautiful. The combat involving card/deck building is fun and easy to understand even for a newbie even when slow at times.Charming chorts and demons!The only negative is the walking mechanic where it's easy to get stuck. Also walking around with no idea where the edges of the room/space may be is quite frustrating, with the game giving no tips.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this game is really something. It's unbelievably faithful to Slavic folklore and mythology. The setting itself is really cool with a lot of historical accuracy too. Music fits the theme beautifully and includes some folk music too. The combat is pretty easy but tbh I think most people would play this game for the story and setting rather than gameplay. Too early to comment on the story itself but it's looking very interesting with some really cool characters. My single only gripe is that the English voice acting is a bit....Off...It's not bad, but the intonation and writing seems to 'flow' better in Russian, I think the voice actors for both English and Russian may be the same for a lot of characters, too. I'd highly recommend setting the voice acting to Russian if you understand the language or want to learn it.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. Provides an interesting and very informative introduction to Russian folklore for those interested, and the game even compiles all the legends and details you learn so you can read up on them later. The combat is excellent, and it is very satisfying to chain together different spells in horrible ways to wipe aside your foes.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing story and a game. Reminded me a lot of slay the spire in the way that you get to choose where you wanna go, you choose how you wanna handle a certain situation and it's also a turn based card game. However here you have a plot that's actually somewhat interesting. You get to experience insane amount of Russian folklore so if you are somewhat into that then 100% grab this game. Voice acting is great for both Russian and English language. If you are ever stuck on puzzle - I mean try it, they are not that difficult tbh but if anything just look up a guide there are plenty of them.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: I took a decision to support this game on Kickstarter after playing the demo, and I was not disappointed. While the game has its share of flaws which stem from the fact of it being made by an small Kickstarter-funded team, anyone playing this game can see that the team took the job seriously and delivered a unique game which is a masterpiece in its own right.Having recently read Gavriel Savit's novel The Way Back, which is centered around themes of Jewish demonology in 19th century Eastern Europe, I found many of the themes expressed in this game to be remarkably similar to and resonant with the novel's, albeit in a world of Slavic Paganism and Orthodox Christianity instead of Judaism. Another underappreciated(in my humble opinion, of course) game with somewhat similar demonic themes and atmosphere that comes to mind is Hard West, which is somewhat a "contemporary" of this game in terms of the historical timelines, but occurs in the American Old West instead of Russia.  So if you are looking for a story and settings centered around demons and demonology, this game will definitely scratch your itch in that respect.In terms of gameplay, the game consists of deckbuilding for battles, in which you will pick the card that will serve you best on your way to victory against demons of various forms, shapes and sizes,  while between battles it is mostly a visual novel with certain elements of "choose your own adventure" genre along with slight point&click elements sprinkled in for good measure. Having played it on the Koldunya difficulty, which is the second most difficult, I found most of the regular battles not very challenging and yet not boring, because they did require some planning and strategizing on my part to build a proper deck, while most of the boss battles I found to balanced just right. Especially the final boss battle, which while was quite challenging, was not frustratingly difficult. All that being said, this game does have its share of flaws. Most notable is the English localization in general and English voice acting in particular, where the game's budget is showing. Although I am fluent in Russian, I chose to play the game in English, which is my default language for games, and the English voice acting, while not abysmal, has obviously been done on a shoestring budget. The low budget of voice acting is most glaring in the dissonance that occurs when the voice actors pronounce certain Russian words which sound much more "natural" to their accent compared to the rest of the English text. Another flaw are some occasional textual and translational inconsistencies that occur throughout the game, but those are all minor, and I can't recall anything particularly egregious at the moment of writing this review.And depending on your point of view on the subject, it is obviously very easy to solve all the dialogu riddles in the game by utilizing save-scumming. Although in my early days as a game I developed a strong personal code against old-school cheating, in those old days save-scumming was far less relevant in the games that existed back then, so I never got mysel to develop any personal code against save-scumming, so that does not bother me much personally, but others may understandably find this problematic.So the bottom line is, if you're looking for a game with dark and demonic atmosphere and enjoyable card battles, this game is just right for you, so go grab your copy now to get your daily dose of Slavic folklore!

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to accurately describe in text- how to convey- the haunting, charming, and the evocative nature of Black Book. By the time you listen to the second or third song in-game, it becomes apparent what measure of love, what craft was put into this piece of art as an interactive media. When Black Book’s rendition of “Little Fir Tree” fades in, I’d place on a similar level to the Suicide Mission track from Mass Effect 2. If you're a fan of the Witcher games and lore, notably Thronebreaker, Black Book will blend masterfully into your library. The terms and monsters will all be familiar, a kind of kin mythology, and even similar switches (in a delightful way!) between the voice acting having fascinating/engaging accents and tonal inflections to the odd character having uk english accents; I think the voice acting is wonderful, again harkening back to the Witcher or Iron Harvest.There is a game here, there are puzzles; but what Black Book has in spades is music, myth, and story. It’s a journey, maybe closer to Journey. And you would be remiss if you didn’t check this title out. Godspeed Vasilisa! Your tale is here -I hope it becomes legendary- it has an audience enthralled!...weeks and months later, I still find myself booting up the OST. The music really does stick with you.

_childDocuments_.review: This is more of a neutral review, but if I had to choose I would lean more on not recommend.While the game has many positives, such as:-beautiful environments-good dialogues, fully voice acted in russian with good voice actors-leans heavily into russian pagan mythology, which is fascinating and the biggest strength of the game-as such, quests are varied and make use of the various demons and legends to create interesting narrativesthat is all well and good, but I see massive flaws after a few hours, those being that:-combat never really evolves, deckbuilding is nowhere near as satisfying as other similar games-there are large balance issues, as combat becomes incredibly hard in some encounters, with bosses dealing 50% of your maximum HP in one turn, if you don't draw shield cards on that turn you are screwed, and even spending your whole turn shielding (and thus dealing 0 damage) you STILL cannot shield the whole attack. i dont mind difficulty as long as the player is given options to outmatch the challenge, this is simply not the case here, it is a number's game, if the enemy's numbers are bigger, you lose, and there is nothing you can do about it. you also CANNOT grind in this game, so farming mods before a hard boss is not an option.-on top of that, according to average playtime, this game is about 30 hours long. for a game that doesn't seem that it will introduce any new elements in its gameplay loop, that is way WAY overstaying its welcome. I couldn't bring myself to play 25 hours more of the same combat while praying that against difficult encounters I would not get dumpstered by RNG.overall the game certainly has quality(ies), but the large and frankly scary issues about combat and how long I would have to suffer through it to see the ending turned me off.
