_childDocuments_.review: Where to start? There are so many aspects of Black Book to love!A reader recommended Black Book to me because it reminded them of one of my novels, which is just a heap of compliments. Since the game builds heavily on ancient folklore and historical concepts of black magic and the occult, I had high expectations and wasn't let down. The game is by turns folklore-rich RPG, deck builder/card battler, management game, and choose your own adventure.The Russian Revolution isn't my favorite era - it's one reason Help Will Come Tomorrow didn't hit for me. Not only does the game weave around the more crushing, politically infuriating parts of the era, it manages to capture a medieval feel I associate with other games based on Slavic and Eastern European lore, like Witcher. If not for references to the revolution, you could easily feel you were in a small village circa 1400. The brilliance is, this allows some modern conceits but keeps the mystical feeling front and center.The story is a tried-and-true tale. Vasilisa, our protagonist, is destined to become a witch- a fate she attempts to thwart by marrying the man she loves. When Vasilisa loses her love under mysterious circumstances, she's forced to embrace the dark arts. With the assistance of her grandfather Egor, she summons the devil and takes the plunge. The play loop is pleasingly structured. You journey along your map to the present objective, exploring side areas and occasionally discovering a unique encounter. Each sub-area offers choices for how to proceed. Your choices affect what you discover and how your encounters play out, and never feel rote. It's worth visiting as many places as possible for the opportunity to gather resources and reagents. Vasilisa travels throughout the night which adds wonderful atmosphere. On her arrival home, a cozy cottage she shares with Egor, there is a queue of villagers to assist and your demon helpers must be sent out to do their mischief.  I usually prefer the 'good' playthrough the first go and was initially put off by some of the mechanics. This is a place to be patient if you're a good-ending player. For example, you're forced to acquire demon servants as you progress. Demons must be kept busy and this is usually at the expense of innocent villagers. Not only does this brutalize your neighbors, it causes you to rack up sins or pay the price for idle minions with a bit of your health bar. But the game quickly introduces an option for demon busywork, as well as perks for having a few sins on your hands, and the opportunity to eventually clean up.Black Book's underrated strength is a breathless sense of excitement and trepidation that lasts throughout. The world feels fantastical, more so because its set on the edge of modern-day. We worry for Vasilisa and at the same time cheer for her and believe she can succeed. But what if she's in too far over her head? If she can't master the darkness she's summoned, all is lost. The story does a superb job of keeping us on the edge of our seats, breath held, hoping for a happy ending despite Vasilisa's dark pact.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: To preface this otherwise it won't be clear just how great this game is. I'm Canadian, and know very little about Russian folklore and history though not for lack of trying to learn about it. I have a reasonably global grasp of mythology and have been seeking to fill in the gaps. So that was large in part why I picked up this game, I had been burned by Russian games before presenting that they'd teach about the culture and totally failing. I also don't like anything to do with the Bible, call it the principle of the thing.However this game blew my expectations out of the water. It presents culture so well and teaches with a very hands on method that very rarely actually hurts you if you guess wrong. That I really warmed up to it, I went from disliking the presented religion to being fine with it. I really enjoyed learning about it's rituals, all the effort that goes into a wedding for example. I came out with a much better understanding then I went in with. Not a great one mind you but the game isn't about it, it's about the kuldons which I didn't even know were a thing. I learned about Slavic folklore hand over foot and I loved every minute of how it was presented.I enjoyed the gameplay though I doubt it will appeal to everyone but if you like Gwent or Magic the Gathering this will be right up your alley. As a whole you can build your deck however you wish, I enjoyed cursing the ever living heck out of everything. But there are many other builds you can do and the game often makes it's combat encounters into puzzles to encourage you to branch out. I didn't always like the puzzles but I always learned something new about the mechanics with them. One thing I'll give the developers props to is that after something like 5 tries at a puzzle they give you the option to skip it. Don't get me wrong I don't mind beating my head against a wall till it breaks Dark Souls style but having the option to move on the story was extremely appreciated. I'm not sure I would have finished the game without this option. There were some puzzles I just did not get, whether that was me or the puzzle not being clear I don't know but I like that the developers guessed that this would happen. I can't sing the praises of the story enough, I won't say to much here beyond that it is great and while I've only finished one play through there was plenty of signposting indicating multiple endings. Also it handles choice very well, some things that might seem meaningless end up not being meaningless so always think about what you're doing before you do it. And that I'm still embarrassed for getting a changling and a mermaid mixed up. But you play a knowner so learning things is part of the job.Graphicly it's nothing to write home about, it serves it's purpose and I don't find it takes away from the experience. I do however love the character art while you are talking to a character, that really made all the difference. For a future game, it would be nice to see improvement but I don't think it should be a focus. Keeping the story and folklore aspects in the forefront is much more important to me at least then the graphics.In conclusion even if the culture presented don't appeal to you on the surface, give this game a try. It's never preachy and is very real feeling in it's presentation of culture. The combat is fun and very satisfying when you do crack the puzzles. The story is fantastic and I will be eagerly awaiting the next game from this developer.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Story: Great story! Superb english voice acting. You can choose between being a goody-two-shoe or curse anyone that looks at you weird, and this contribute to a "sin" counter that impacts the plot a bit.Game length: It's a 20 hours play through for me, though I did reload a lot to see different dialogue options.Game play: It's similar to slay the spire, except the limiting resource is the # of cards you can play each turn rather than mana.Most of the cards cost 1 space to cast, though there are also a few quick action cards that don't take space. This difference is not too big if you think about it... it's like if every card cost 1 mana). The # of spells each turn increase at higher levels. There' are many chapters, at the start of each chapter you unlock new cards that can be added to your deck (and by fighting mobs in that chapter). They are on average much stronger than cards from previous chapters, therefore your deck always feels new and unique.If you have experience in this type of games, you WILL break the game balance pretty quickly (at day-2, since that's the first chance to add new cards to your deck), and become nearly invincible on the later 40% of the game (difficulty doesn't change this fact since the broken interaction is not changed). So you really are mostly watching a novel at mid to late game. It's a REALLY good novel though, and overall I recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: The Good-AestheticsAnimation and art styleCard and Idle game mechanics.The average--The walking segments seem almost uneccesary and a bit janky. There are reasons to explore but the point and click is just a bit off for me. Not sure where I can walk or what I can click. Need to get close to something to be able to click but you just zoom past most the time.-UI is ok but may need more tooltip helpersThe Bad-The Writing - Comes across as a concept and story written by a young adult/teenager. Core concepts are really just dove into with superficial reasoning. Everyone seems to be on board with the whole premise but the setup makes it seem like this should not be the case. I feel like this could've been elaborated on with some more emotions from characters around the morally grey and additional contention against the main characters mission. The Voice Acting - Mixed with the poor writing the voice acting, It definitely seems off emotionally and is very amateur sounding. Inflections are missing and the VA is almost flat and monotone at times you think there should be some feelings behind the tones.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful, well researched deck builder set in late 19th century Russia. * The devs poured their heart into this thing. You can feel it from the attention to detail in every little piece. * Multiple valid strategies to build your deck. I.e. you are not locked into the one thing that works. * Beautiful hand drawn characters in 'talking' sections (where you'll spend 30% of your time). * The original voice acting is excellent. * The Durak card game. So much fun, spent hours playing just it. * The devs managed to maintain the quality of storytelling throughout the experience, no empty or dull moments whatsoever. * The design of the mechanical progression is excellent all the way into late game. * Huge amount of historical research went into this thing. An optional encyclopedia provides a lot of materials for the players to (optionally!) peruse. * Slavic folklore songs recorded by a Permian orchestra. * Skill progression system does not allow the player to unlock everything, forcing the player to think about progression and specialize according to their playing style. * Did I mention that the story is great? All arcs have conclusion and are logically built out within the rules of the world. I was very happy with my experience as I reached the end screen. * Creative item design ... but I was set fairly early on and found most equipable items pointless. To be more specific each build is supported by a group of items. The devs could have done more with providing items that give in trait and take in another. * The graphical fidelity of the world sections, where you spend <10% of your time, is low.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: It's a gem of a game, play it :)I'm not going to list everything good and bad about the game. I only want to mention 2 things:1. The animated 3D backgrounds are absolute blast, especially during the dialogue screens.2. There's one downside for me — the vagueness of dialogue options. You can never guess what each of them would do from what they say, until you pick it. But that's not a huge problem.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Black Book is a handheld (Nintendo Switch)/console game that's also been put on Steam as a bit of an afterthought, as it's very much designed for the handheld/console gaming audience.  This Nintendo Switch game is a hybrid screen tapping adventure with a card based "puzzle combat" system that might work well for some casual gamers, but the problem is that while such gameplay is clearly aimed at more casual gamers, the design of the combat is deliberately obtuse and frustrating.  Way to locate your target audience and aim your game in completely the opposite direction.It's narrative heavy but overall the game "works", but it's not my cup of tea and, being a Nintendo Switch game, isn't going to meet some of the minimum quality standards that PC gamers are used to. From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.The game features low-polygon "retro" assets with a cel-shading type shader effects instead of doing their job properly and texturing the game assets, making this look like a barely functional 3D game from the early 1990s.  This visual style is a method that lazy devs often use when they have a lack of interest/capability to create highly detailed, high poly models and instead use shader effects to disguise that shortcoming under the name of "art", or "We made it look bad on purpose", which really isn't something gamers should have to put up with.  It's unclear why the developers weren't willing to arrange high quality, high polygon count contemporary assets and high resolution textures for the game.  It's far below the state of the art visuals gamers expect as a result of their decisions.The controls can't be customised because the game has such a dumbed down, simplified interface that it's just point and click stuff like a browser/Flash game.  The fact that the interface is this dumbed down might be seen as a problem in itself, however... this is a fairly shallow experience if you're the kind of gamer that likes to play games with deep, rich control schemes and interaction.  You'll get none of that here.Because this is designed for handheld/portable gaming appliances, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the low power handheld gaming appliances that the game was designed for.  These are unfortunate compromises and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was a second thought for the mobile game developers.  The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for low power handhelds forces upon a game.  While this might run well on a Steam Deck, we must remember the vast majority of gamers here are gaming on PC.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.The poor quality of this game is reflected by how many people spent time with it.  At the time of this review, SteamDB shows the all-time peak player number was only  players.  This is a remarkably low number, and now, the only player activity occurs once or twice a month, presumably someone loading it up to see what it is then quickly uninstalling it.  Considering there's over 120 million gamers on Steam and well over 100,000 games for gamers to choose from, the overwhelming lack of interest in this low quality game is to be expected.So, should you buy this game?  Is this one of the best of the 100,000+ games on Steam?Black Book has the insane price of $25 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.For comparison, the $25 asking price for this game could get you games like "Elden Ring", "Cyberpunk 2077" or "Day-Z".  Quality, professionally made games like those are frequently on sale cheaper than this.Unfortunately Steam reviewers aren't presented with a "Maybe" option... if they did, that's what I'd choose.  This isn't a completely bad game, but it's also not one of the best.  As always, if you read my review and you can overlook the negatives I've called out, or they just aren't important to you, then by all means go ahead and buy this.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful card drafting RPG, heavily steeped in rich Slavic folklore and superstition. The story is interspersed with encounters where choices made can either either benefit or harm you, or impact the overall story, and makes for a nice change of pace, so it's not a constant "grind fest" of card battles. The atmosphere is a dark, brooding, encompassing dread with breaks of tranquility, making it a great game for the Autumn/Halloween season as well. Expect to spend about 30 hours into this title, many of which may be done past your bed time.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: This is a highly immersive deck-building game experience. I fell in love with the game's story, art and music from its trailer, played its fascinating Prologue and decided to invest in the game.Its perfect for lovers of dark mythology, and is an absolute love letter to Slavic lore. I really enjoy the dark ambiance of the game when my lights are off and the game's soundtrack is enabled. It helps me enter a dreamlike state, which can at times be on the verge of a nightmare. Also the unlockable folk songs are absolutely exquisite, some of them had me in tears at their beauty.I love that I can experience the game on multiple levels, depending on my mood, energy levels and time:- From a storytelling perspective, via its unlockable library of myths and legends- From a player perspective, via Vasilia's adventures and choices to serve troubled villagers- From a deck builder's perspective,via the card battles- From a cultural explorer's perspective, via the game's unlockable encyclopaedia.Though I wish the in game battle art could match the beauty of the conversation and promotional scenes, I truly enjoy every moment of this game, especially the interactions with the vibrant characters of the NPCs. Though I find deck building games to be intimidating at times, the learning curve to build a battle ready deck is great for players of ALL levels.I do look forward to making different choices to explore variations of Vasilisa's quest and mission to help her people.Thank you Morteshka for creating such a magnificent game!
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: There's lots to like in this game but it's unfortunately spoiled by a few things which don't match up to the same quality level of the rest of it.I love the art style, especially when walking around and exploring the world.  The battles look really nice.  The music is subtle and moody and really adds to the dark, earthy feel of the game.  Unfortunately the voice acting is a bit over the top and distracting and doesn't match the understated tone of the game.  I tried switching the voice language hoping it was just a problem with the English recording, but it was the same.I like the Slavic terminology and folklore, it makes a nice change from all the tropes we're used to and I was keen to explore the world and learn about how magic works in this universe.If you like a lot of reading, this won't be a problem for you but the amount of text you have to read near the start of the game is really overwhelming.  There's a lot of dialogue with not much feeling or soul in it, the father figure who raised you from childhood talks to you like a quest giver and not like you're his daughter, casually sending you into a maw of hell at the start to become a witch, which you just do as if it's a casual errand.You're presented with a lore encyclopedia containing long passages of text and one of the game's mechanics requires you to be familiar with it in order to make the right choices for in-game bonuses.  The game also doesn't let you review the encylopedia while you're presented with these choices, you just have to remember all of it.  This creates a kind of awkward meta-game where you're rewarded for tabbing out of the game to look up the answers.There's a glaringly obvious UI issue during combat, where you can't see the effect or numerical values of the cards in your hand at a glance unless you mouse over each one individually.I really want to like this, but it seems like it's a team of very talented artists and programmers held back by the writing and design.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunate puzzle battles aside, this is one charming deck-builder with a heavy narrative focus, great folk Russian ambience and an eminently likeable protagonist. 9/10edit: Late game stealth mechanics and a poor English localization (a word that already implies a shoddy translation effort) can make the whole experience drag a bit. Hopefully they will fix it? One hell of an ending, though!
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I can oversell this game. Everything from the setting and visuals and music to the story and the gameplay is spectacular. If you've any interest in Slavic folklore, deckbuilding games, or simply a good story, do yourself a favor and pick this one up! At time of review, I have completed one playthrough, having explored pretty much every branching path I came across and collected a lot of the encyclopedia entries and cards (but not all of them!).With several different endings based on a few choices you make through the game, I definitely plan to give this one another run just to see what might happen if I change my mind on a few critical points in the final chapters of the game. It's one that you can definitely get a good story out of playing just once, but it also has a good reason to play again for people like me who love the game and would like to give it another go knowing a few details that you don't find out until the end. Each run probably has a solid 15 hours of gameplay (though my first one took me 18 because I literally explored everything). Very enjoyable and definitely worth the price, in my opinion!
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Black Book taught me a lot about Slavic mythology! Slavic mythology is woven throughout the story, and I found myself wanting to learn more as often as I found myself wanting to play the actual game. That feels uncommon these days; outside of visual novels, I usually want to decrease exposition in favor of more gameplay. With Black Book, I generally wanted both more play time and more story time, which honestly just feels good in a game.It's tough to play a deckbuilder without comparing it to other notable deckbuilders. For deckbuilding enthusiasts, just note that this isn't Slay the Spire, or Monster Train, or the first level of Inscryption. The deckbuilding is good enough, and it has its own merits, but it needs to be said that you'll play Black Book for the story and subsystems as much as you'll play for the deckbuilding elements. I highly recommend the game based on its merits, and was gently surprised at just how much I enjoyed playing the game through to the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: is a deck-builder with simplistic gameplay of "add shield values", then "add attack power values".But the aesthetic of  a witch, mixed with demons and some cool lore, makes the package stand out.Definitely has an indie vibe. But with voice acting, interesting text (chorts, hell, demonic stuff), large maps, many events, and even companions along your journey, it's a relaxing adventure through a dark world.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Thank you the devs for this wonderful game. I really enjoy the story as well as the well-established cultural atmosphere! The setting, the characters, the story...feels real, like it actually had happened long time ago, and we had traveled back in time to witness the events with Vasilisa . The game also sparks my interest in Slavic indigenous folklore, tradition & religion. As for the gameplay, I don't mind trying card-based game. The battle system is quite interesting. But the story is what makes the game for me. Truly a wonderful experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: It's good, playable on the steam deck, but I do have some qualms about quality of life things, mainly:- When you try to skip/make the dialogue complete faster on a choice scene, it will select the first choice. This makes it a slog in that you have to replay the scene and/or battle in order to select the choice you actually wanted.- As many people have mentioned, the battle puzzles -- fun when they work, but when the solution seems a little bugged or too out there, I'd like an option to just skip right away.- The pathfinding/animation in the 3D scenes -- wheeeeeeew boy. They've constructed a gorgeous low poly world but Vasilisa basically just wanders around and gets snagged on things... which can get a little hilarious at times. You select something for her to observe and she ends up running in the opposite direction because she needs to be in a specific farther spot to comment on it. LOL.- The saving system -- I know this might make the game larger in file size but I would love to have multiple (many more) auto saves to select from. Either that, or scene/story/missiob skips -- in the current state, if you want to achievement hunt, you might have to slog through the whole game again. I can't LOL. I can't imagine doing this twice LOL. At least not without some updates. (Maybe available in NG+? I haven't gotten that far though, and I'm already at 13+ hours.)Other than that, this is a pretty fun and challenging card battler! The characters are cute and the English voice acting is so fun. I feel like I am finally getting used to the words but don't quiz me on anything. LOL.

The story does drag on a bit.  Most importantly, this is the first functional implementation of Durak in any video game I've ever seen and for that along this game is going on my favorites list.

_childDocuments_.review: dunno why i never gave a review but i love this game. the worldbuilding and characters are great, love the soundtrack, combat system and map have a nice feel to them, .. i don't know, the whole atmosphere of this game just draws me in. as for downsides, sometimes a puzzle wants you to do a very specific thing but will explain it weirdly. i got stuck two or three times because i misunderstood the rules of a puzzle and couldn't solve it as i understood the assignment. also, the saving system is a bit messed up. remember to move to the next area if you gambled your life away for some cash and items cuz they will be lost otherwise. technical stuff being annoying mainly. but 10/10 for its heart

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty neat game, enjoyable deckbuilding antics and a lot of interesting bits of real world mythology mixed together and presented nicely. It helps that the dialogue is voiced and that the game is broken up between fights, card games, fixed locations and explorable locations.If you're at all familiar with card games I'd recommend playing on the hardest setting, it's very easy as these games go and the penalty for failure is usually "Retry battle (optional: rebuild deck first)"
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Quite the unique game. The Slavic folklore flavor is very original and present not only in the story but also other aspects of the game, such as gameplay and design. It's simpler than other deck builders (maybe less so once you unlock the last tier of cards), and also not a roguelite (which is a breath of fresh air for the genre). It's also fully voice acted.If I had to improve anything about it:* I'd add more than 3 deck slots to make it easier to try out more archetypes* I'd tie the equipped artifacts to the deck slots* you can't edit your deck when you restart a battle, only when you lose it. This makes it so you have to waste your time losing on purpose so you can change your deck, which is sometimes necessary due to some enemies completely countering some deck archetypes (e.g. enemies with Ethereal, Warlock)
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:+ Wonderful atmosphere+ Great storytelling+ Deep lore based on real-world mythology+ Puzzles reward you for exploring the lore+ Adds a few new twists to the deckbuilder genreNeutral:: The map management part of the game is innovative, but I'm not sure it's in a good way. It is very much in keeping with the tone of the game, but at the same time it always feels bad. Like, I get it and even admire it, but I don't want to participate.Cons:- Weak voice acting, dialogue awkwardly written at times- Too many "gotcha" moments where you're arbitrarily punished- Too little explanation of certain systems until after they become relevant -- then it's too late- Being a witch kinda sucks in this world, and that really does take some of the fun out of it- (Subjective) I have card battler fatigue, and this game isn't special enough to overcome thatOverall, I'd give it a sideways thumb if I could. If you like the pros more than you're bothered by the cons, you will absolutely love the game, I'm sure. But for me, it's the opposite. I don't hate the game, but it makes me feel bad often enough that I just don't care to stick with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: What I enjoy about this game: The lore and story element is interesting, the atmosphere and some of the characters I grew attached to, and of course the card elements. The game hits a sweet spot in terms of its intensity - it´s not a hyper fast paced game and neither is it a narrative game which feels to slow or with too little interactions. Misconceptions around the game/what to expect: The game is often marketed amongst card battlers - and it certainly is. But it´s also what it says in the title - a book. I´m not normally a novel-reading gamer (prefer to just read an actual book) but this story is interesting enough to keep me coming back. I think a lot of the negative reviews here are from people playing the game with the preconcieved expectation it will be on a par with games like Slay the Spire and other deckbuilding card battlers. It is way more laidback than these games. I prefer to treat black book like a TV series of russian/slavic lore with deckbuilding I can drop into and binge for a few hours - finding out what new and strange, mythical developments have happened to the witch and which new characters and challenges have popped up. a few sections are fairly predictable on some level - it has a structure where you follow a map, search areas and solve a mystery, inevitably fighting against various Chorts and demons along the way. However, many "episodes" can take you strange journeys to underworlds, into the mist of places trapped by demons and so on. How do I play this? I play it when I´ve been bashing roguelikes and higher intensity, fast paced games for a long time and I need something to kickback with which is way more interactive than tv. I found after taking a break from the story for sometime, it was much easier to get back into than I thought it would be. I like the puzzle solving element of restructuring your deck for different bosses.Beginning the game I didn´t feel like the card elements were explained super well, and it took me a bit of fiddling around to see what each effect had and how they were stacked - but hey, imagine using your brain and not having everything spoon fed to you. The game is lengthier than i expected, so you get a lot of content for your moneys worth. Just don´t go into thinking you are getting Monster Train or Slay the Spire etc - this is also about the story as well as the cards.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: The card game is fun but jesus, this game is unbearably long. The plot and folk events make no sense and I am ethnically russian. I am not even half way through and i logged in 20h. If they just cut off the filler, it would be a really nice dive into a lesser known culture (rural Permian late 19th century tsarist russia) but it's frankly a slog.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: The game puts a new spin on  a turn base action game, as it tries to build upon it mythology story. The Slavic folk horror game with card based combat, great atmosphere, interesting characters and plot. If you would like to check out the game before buying it, visit this link for a pre view of the the game
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: I recently finished the game on hard mode whilst doing as many optional tasks as possible. The game has a hiccup here and there but nothing serious. The team is continually remedying  these minor things with regular updates since the game's release. I would recommend speeding up the animation in the options section--just a thought. I enjoyed the card play AND THE PUZZLES. The story is well written and encompasses not only the character's story but that of Russia and the advent of the industrial age, therefore there are some interesting moments to contemplate. The songs are a nice touch. Hopefully, there is some DLC in the works. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: A very charming game, with beautifully animated scenery, delightful folklore, and interesting card-based combat. If you're familiar with Slay the Spire, you'll be able to slip right into to combat. The weakest part is the voice acting, but even that has its charms. The folksongs you occasionally earn are quite lovely.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: While the 3d graphics may look "Out of this World" (as in, the 90s game), there is a massive amount of folklore poured into this game, which serves as a good visual novel and a passable deck battler (some fairly obvious combos break any difficulty curve, if you choose to go that route). Play it in Russian for the complete experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: I'm still just in chapter five, but this game is great, therefore already want to recommend it. In this game you are a witch that solves tasks to open the seals of the black book. The game happens day by day. Every day you wander around (sometimes in large area, sometimes in small) in the dark and solve different things: sometimes you just find things, you battle demons (using a card battler system) or solve riddles. At the end of each day is some kind of boss you have to defeat (or just some puzzles). You get XP to learn/improve skills and you get money to buy more cards, items or herbs. Every day starts in your house where you have dialogs, can play a card game named durak and have to deal with your imps by sending them on tasks (which gives you sins - negative) or by accepting the torture (debuffs) they otherwise cause to you.Following points are based on what I've seen so far:Positive:+ a nice and simple card battler+ tries to combine card game, RPG and adventure in one and i think it does it well+ fantastic atmosphere+ graphics are okay, although i don't really like the faces of the characters (in 3d scenes)+ durak is funNegative:-  -> the devs fixed that- i always have the feeling to miss somethingAll in all - of what i've seen so far - a fantastic game that i can fully recommend.P.S.: A pitty that I don't have my steam deck yet, this game is for sure perfect for the deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game in the beginning, but to me it feels poorly balanced. I can live with having bad luck sometimes and some fights being harder than others, but right now I'm at a point where I'm in a boss fight and can't find any way to defeat him. I already looked up strategies and they all rely on cards that I don't have yet. I did all previous sidequests so far so either those cards are a random drop and I didn't get them or they were sold by a vendor but I didn't have the money for them at the time.I've even retried two previous saves to see if I can get any of them somehow, but neither did they drop nor did any vendor have them.In many other games you could just do sidequests until you feel ready for a boss but in this game that doesn't work, you can't just re-visit older quests. Once you're at the boss, you're at the boss.So apparently I'm at a point where I would have to start more than 2 hours back to have a chance to get the right equipment for the boss fight (or not, if the rng system is deterministic, I don't have a chance to finish this run at all).
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Great game that need to get more recognition.I am not a fan of deck-builders, but story and setting in this game is gripping.Plot twist are not so obvious.Game has some replayability factors, like your approach to situations (battle, puzzle, skip), moral choices (spare, punish etc) and sins-meter, that defines some ending choices and rewards during playthrough.  (But I watched all "bad" endings on youtube =])Folklore is charming, art is awesome, story is gripping. If you have some time between major releases, definitely play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Very nicely done simple deck builder strategy rpg. Interesting quiz mechanic that makes you read and understand the lore in order to win plot-related challenges. It has simple mechanics, but they get involved when stacked up so it's not TOO simple. Also, it's very immersive because they really paid attention to the little things (music, lighting, voice acting) to draw you into the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: This is very beautiful game.Mix of Banner Saga, Thronebreaker and Slay the Spire in Russian mythology setting.Story and setting are the strongest sides of the game.Setting is very unusual and is created with accuracy and attention to details. Mix of Slavic paganism with orthodox Christianity of 19th century Russia is perfect background for adventure of a young witch who tries to resurrect her dead fiancé. For each episode developers provide a lot of lore (historical facts, customs descriptions, folklore or even songs) which explains, what is going on and allow you to learn a lot about life of common people in central Russia of 19th century. This lore is also used in later episodes in a quiz-type decisions makings which brings character bonus XP. Card-based battles is core of the gameplay and it is implemented well enough to keep you in a game. Mechanics is simple but gives you enough options for different strategies and diverse opponents strategies encourage you to experiments. Some balance issues exist - common enemies are week and some bosses are unproportionally strong and some mechanics look much better than others, but generally it looks very solid.Character development is very primitive and is obviously can be much better, but it doesn’t require lot of time or attention, so, it doesn’t actually spoil the game.Graphics is basic, but stylish and looks pretty and support game atmosphere really well. Really good for indie project.Side mechanics also not very bright or useful but also is good to have features. Durak card game could be confusing for people unfamiliar with it, because in-game tutorial is not descriptive enough. But in most cases, it is optional, although allows to skip couple of battles and get some minor bonuses. Demons management also not deep, but makes “evil” path a little bit easier and “good” one a little bit more challenging, so add some replayability.Lot of people complains about translation and this could be a problem. Original Russian text is complicated, because it contains a lot of old words and dialogs are written in old central-Russian dialect style. This adds some immersion to the game if you play in Russian language, but creates a lot of complexity for translators. So, if you can – play it in Russian.Summary: if you interested in atmospheric story-driven games in unusual settings and can tolerate non-ideal translation (or know Russian) this game is highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game where you play as a young slavic witch on a mission to bring her beloved from hell with the help of the black book, filled with Slavic folklore and traditions (something we dont see much in games ). -you got your main quests where you have to break 7 seals of the black book ( 7 chapters ) to get more powerful and get side quests along the way, your actions and choices will have consequences and affect the story and the ending .-gameplay is a mix between card game, visual novel and point and click with some RPG element on top .-the voice acting is really amazing .-works fine, didnt have any problem wasn't expecting the game to take me +20h to finish and to be that much fun, i recommended even at full price .7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable deckbuilder game.I found the very engaging and entertaining. The setting and story are unique. Combat will be easy for any Slay the Spire veterans, but still rich. I thoroughly enjoyed having to read all the literature the game gives you to find the correct answer to dialogue options.Yes, the game is a little rough around the edges. The voice acting could use work and the point and click movement is very quirky. But those problems aren't enough to detract from the overall high quality game Black Book is.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Great atmospheric game with touching story. There is one caveat, I had much better experience after switching from the English to the Russian version because characters and stories use an old dialect which could be lost in translation and that dialect greatly affects the atmosphere of the game.Your experience might vary, I'm not a native English speaker.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a bad game, but there's too many things that bother me personally: bland English voice acting, the amount of same situations/fights you get into, the 'clean' art style of the dialog screens that does not fit the rest of the game, ... and after 5 hours of super easy fights there was one enemy that was very hard to beat. Go play Inscryption if you want an excellent dark-themed deckbuilder, it's far superior to this game.  (sorry devs)
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: A well done single player, story driven card game.  The card system is pretty well done, and is complex enough to keep it interesting throughout the game.  You unlock new tiers of cards as you progress through the story as well.  Note that being pure evil does make the game easier as you can make tons of money and get all the cards and items you want, while being good means having to handicap yourself to an extent.  It does make a good playthrough more challenging/rewarding though.  The story is pretty good overall, and I enjoyed learning about the lore of this time period.  Overall a solid game and it is often on sale so cheap to pic up.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Love it so far. I took an interest in Slavic folklore when I played Quest for Glory 4 so many, many years ago now. The setting is perfect, the music is on point, and battles are fantastic so far. As you learn and explore about the world, there are entries in an encyclopedia which you can read to learn more about the folklore and approach / answer situations with better clarity and understanding.There appears to be some depth to the card battle system and I'm looking forward to seeing how it evolves. Art style and visuals are great. I read some of the reviews that the English voice acting was poor, so I've opted for the Russian voice acting with English subtitles and I'm loving the experience.If you're a fan of card games like Slay the Spire and it's many clones, and you have an interest in old folklore in general, I think you'll really enjoy this. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: As a Slav I really, really, REALLY wanted to love this game but at the end couldn't. While the game has fantastic settings and pretty okay gameplay it is way to padded and just drags for so long. After over 8 hours I was just barely after Chapter 1 and lost interest since the game is not really evolving much after prologue and after a while it just feels like MMO grind. Check the demo first and if you like it and if you are really into Slavic folklore (which the game admittingly have plenty of and it is well presented) and like card battlers a lot then sure go ahead, but skip otherwise.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely amazing, Slavic Folklore inspired, card-based game. What it lacks in technical prowess it makes up in amazing art direction and aesthetic. Unlike most card-based games you can rebuild your deck very frequently to try out new combinations - which is good because there are a lot of effects on those cards so you can go crazy with some of those. Want to stack 120 armor points every turn? Nerf the enemy's damage to the ground and then deal damage equal to how much you removed from them? You can do that here. In general - the card mechanics are clever and well thought-out.I would also like to say that the game is far bigger than I expected: multiple unique quests, locations and encounters - many of which are optional but offer great rewards. The main story itself takes you through multiple areas with a lot of boss battles that require you to actually use your head and plan well to get past them, and it keeps throwing new stuff and mechanics at you right until the very end. Overall, I was pleasantly surprised with the scope.There are some minor bugs here and there - one of them almost stopped me from being able to beat a boss but the developers managed to fix it fairly soon after me and other players pointed it out so I trust some of those will be fixed in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Slow-paced but beautiful and richly realized card-battler set in an Old Russia where spirits and devils cause hardship for the local people and it's up to 'cunning women' like Vasilisa to defeat their schemes...or harness them to her own ends. Vasilisa's quest to break the seals on the Black Book and gain her heart's only wish takes the player on a winding path from her own era, to the Otherworld, and into the very heart of evil itself. Will not be regretted by anyone who longs for a unique tale of magic and a journey along the treacherous fault lines between ancient beliefs and the modern, mechanical era.  Gameplay can be a little rough at times (the difficulty spike from normal to boss battles may take the unwary player by surprise. Most bosses have a trick to beating them, which may need a special deck. Fortunately, you can also just turn down the difficulty and get back to the story). The artwork is spare but charming, and the a cappella folk music songs performed by the Student Choir of Perm State College of Arts and Culture are well worth meandering off the main path to find. I recommend playing with the original Russian audio for the best experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: I couldn't finish this game, mainly because of all the text you have to read to understand everything going on. There's a lot of it, and as someone with poor sight, it unfortunately became unplayable. Still, I love the fact that it exists, and what little I did see of the lore seemed accurate, so if you want to learn more about slavic folklore, and you don't have any trouble with reading a lot, this game is for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Black Book is a fun adventure game set in Russia in which you play a witch that fights demons in turn-based combat with a card deck of spells. The story and setting are interesting and quite unique, the combat is enjoyable and is just challenging enough to not be trivial, while also not getting in the way of the rest of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: So good! Story, artwork, voices, game mechanics. If you would have asked me before now I would have said no to a card-battle game - did not enjoy the witcher one. But this one felt right/good. It is like a point and click adventure game with a dark setting. I really enjoyed being a witch and helping people with this and that, and having to use my knowledge. Choices and consequences game. Just finished it now and it feels like putting down a really good book. If you like storydriven games like me just play it. Hope they make more.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: I did somewhat enjoy the game and I wish there was a neutral option. The good is that we explore an underrepresented mythology rooted in slavic/ russian folklore, so learning about it through piecing bits of information around the story was great.I like the card game battle mechanics too, just been a fan of card games all my life and I like ones that have a story and are more than just PvP or Roguelike.However, there are issues:-The story has its twists and turns, but there are over 100 characters (apparently), and it's quite difficult to keep track of everyone. I lost a bit of interest towards the end.-The 3D point-and-click section is really poor and janky. The puzzles are really not difficult and you find everything you need in the same or adjacent rooms. Could have been skipped I think.-Every one of the book's 7 seals unlocks basically another "expansion" of cards. However, they still remain black or white, with no distinction (not even a symbol). Doesn't feel like you unlock new content, which could have been visually represented in some ways.And this would have been all right, except for the biggest "sin" of this game:-no balancing. Yeah, the game gets too easy. After about a quarter of a game, it stopped being challenging. Due to no deckbuilding restrictions, and you can make a very concentrated deck of 13 cards (you can have up to 33, but I cannot see a reason why you would), you have some combos that at first deal 100 damage in one turn, then you can scale to obscene levels doing 600, 100+ damage through different strategy (like cursing the enemies, or buffing your multi-attack cards, or stacking a lot of defense, doubling it four times, and then bonking the enemies with it).I believe that a game that has card battles at its core should be challenging. It should encourage you to explore multiple strategies, die many times and trying different ways around different opponrnts. Having said that, if you are on the fence and don't mind cruising through the story, it's still somewhat enjoyable and satisfying. The soundtrack is good, the voice acting suffers a bit but it's passable. I would rate this a solid 5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Voice acting is woodtierGame on hardest difficulty is only kinda hard with the first boss, and a mob before him that kills you instantly, and you can maybe not get enough damage to kill him first.after that, you can pretty much come up with 2 potential combinations with the few cards they give you to make a deck so easy if feels like your playing pokemon or something mindless.puzzle battles, have only one solution, that requires you to know what the mobs are going to do in latter turns. horrible design.so far game is fun.10/10 if you have bad internet.(right now my internet is bad and i cant really play any of the games i want to play)
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: So take Slavic folklore, sprinkle in some simple Slay the Spire card-battler system, mixed them with a good story and you get this game. Those who played Witcher will recognize the lore.A really nice game, has its flaws but I sure do not regret it playing from start to finish. It is one of those games where the choices matter at the end; well when it comes to the choices for the others, as for your own fate, you choose it at the end.Was underwhelmed by the end combat, because the final unlock you get some really OP cards, ofc its your choice if you wana use them and build a deck, but heck, they are there so why not use them, anyway, this made passing through the final zones way too easy, but up until then, difficulty was just right.Speaking of the cards, there is also the fact that with each unlock some of the cards just feel the same, I mean some just give +damage compared to the previous ones, and slight stats which you will not even notice.While I am not a fan of the card-battle, it was alright, however the game made it up with nice character development, good story and narrative and audio. VA it was decent at best for English, but if you want a great experience use the original language and EN subtitles.Art, might not be for everyone, the 3D models just did not looked as good as their 2D counterparts (because during dialogues the characters are 2D), still I didn’t mind the style.Regarding localization, there were some flaws, there were times when the voices did not matched the subtitles. The way it saves you gotta get used to it, to make it simple it save every time you enter a new location (or pass a loading screen), however when you load it takes you at the beginning, so don’t bother managing your deck and then saving and exiting, cuz it will reset, just pass into the next location and then exit.The game knows how to build up the atmosphere and immerse you, I also liked how if you hover over highlighted words during dialogue, it will not move forward, neat attention to detail which I appreciate it if you want to learn the lore. What can i say, give it a try.Some tips: if you need to check the encyclopedia during dialogue click top left, map icon. Puzzle battles can be skipped after failing 3 times in a row (and yeah, some of those do suck). I would say keep those sins in check, their number will count during final battle, however like I mentioned earlier you get some OP cards so it should not be a problem.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: The previous game from this developer — The Mooseman - was a walking simulator about the mythology of Perm area. It had a charming atmosphere and magic of myths of the Finno-Ugric tribes. But I didn't like it because of gameplay. As the story was interesting as the gameplay was boring.This one has the same problem for me. The gameplay became better, but isn't enough. This is a deck building card game. We need to cast spells with magic words and the magic black book we have. Two types of words —attacking and defending.Sometimes we can play another card game in this card game — "Fool". I often used to play it with my grandma in my childhood. So, I know rules and tactics here very well. But here, probably because of my experience or of stupid foes I never lost it. That was an easy way to farm money for herbs and amulets. Sometimes instead of fights you can play Fool with monsters and unholy spirits. If you win — you'll take the same reward as you fight them with words. If you lose… So, I don't know about consequences.The game's graphics are not exactly stellar. Low-poly models don't look great. They are poor and faded. It is unsightly. But the gamedesigner has done everything to smooth the edges with a splendid level design. Really, villages and woods here are incredibly atmospheric. Folklore game from a capital letter. Fantastic Slavic tales and mythology (mostly Russian, Perm area), where feel fresh and novelty. Very rarely Russian game dev gives us gems like this. I have already told about difficulty. And The Black Book has big problems with it. First time my choice was a hard level. And I couldn't beat the second boss. I tried mane times, but, eventually, gave up. After that difficult was changed on normal (first time for a long period). And I still had issues with strong enemies from time to time, but it was acceptable. Till the 4th chapter... Then my character got stronger, and the game became so easy that I defeated some bosses in a three or four turns. And that was ok for me, because I didn't like a gameplay, but fell in love with the story.Because it is here is a masterpiece. I heard a lot of these creepy tales in my childhood. And it was a fantastic experience to solve riddles in the game with a knowledge based on folklore from your childhood.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, that deeply immerses you in a well-built world of myth and folklore. Play through the adventures of a witch-in-the-making that aspires to revive her lost lover. This ~20h campaign set in the russian countryside [EDIT:before] the first world war is mainly filled with well-paced dialogue, building a detailed environment the player wanders along where folklore and superstition are reality. If you love story and atmosphere, go for it! If you came for an amazing card battler, better read the full review and make a informed choice afterwards, especially considering the higher price for a card battler game.-  Even without any prior knowledge of permian-/russian-/slavic-mythos components you will find yourself being sucked into this new and strange world, where various kinds of demons and curses are as important as the various sections of a hut and their meaning.-  As a "knower" (=witch) people ask for your help in otherworldly matters, placing you together with your grandfather in a position with very believable agency. A good deal of exposition is done by you explaining stuff to other people, which feels very natural and helps building the world step by step.-  Accompanying Vasilisa through her ordeals in becoming a witch is simply great. A lot of decisions you take throughout the story will resurface later on, although the impact of each single decision on the story is usually not that severe. -  If you are only/mainly looking for a good card battler that will challenge you in the style of Slay the Spire or the like, I do not recommend to buy this game. The card battler is functional and brings some neat ideas to the table, but will lack real depth if you know how to build very strong decks, making encounter battles more a nuisance than a real challenge. That being said, I had fun with it and love the creativity that was put in it, with highlights being battling other mages and bosses. The variety of items and cards allows for a range of different playstyles, so you can always switch between decks (3 of the can be stored, you can change decks almost any time).  The few card puzzles did not really do it for me.-  If you have seen the trailer, you know what to expect of the graphics. For me, the simple art style did the trick and let me tell you, the developers know how to pull up some astonishing scenery with their style. These grand shots are often accompanied by folklore choires, weaving a deeply moving atmosphere, so for me this was a plus point, but I can see people being put of by this.-  Is tedious, but that is literally what it is supposed to be lorewise. So again something that worked for me, but I can see people disliking this feature.-  Playing the Black Book requires a bit of effort, to read up on the small bits of lore trivia that you unlock all the time. It requires even more effort not to loose track of the meaning of the terms to remember, especially if you took some time away from the game. More often than not, the respective terms are highlighted and explained, but I can see that this can feel overwhelming. I learned to love the short catch up sequences at the start of a new day, where Vasilia retells the happenings of the previous day to her grandfather, making these the perfect time to take a break.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: I was looking forward to playing this one for awhile, but I simply can't get myself to finish this game. After about 12 hours I was so bored with the mythology stories being read by horrible voice actors, but I kept at it, trying to enjoy it. After almost 21 hours, I am going to uninstall it. The deck building was super easy  but the puzzle battles were actually really fun to figure out. The mythology was pretty interesting at first but the pace is so slow and, I think I may have mentioned it, the voice acting was horrible. The English narrator sounded so inappropriately toned throughout the entire game. His voice was almost joyful, and the setting is really dark, so it makes no sense at all. Also the subtitles didn't match the words being said quite often. If you're looking to read or listen to a Slavic mythology story for 30 hours, this game is for you. Deck building is barely a challenge and the puzzle battles are skippable after failures. 5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: A really neat little card-based RPG that draws on the mythology of a specific region of northern Russia. You're a witch in a world where everyone correctly believes that watermills and steam engines work by magic, and you go around solving (or worsening) people's problems on your way to saving your beloved. There's a lot in it: deckbuilding, choices that affect the world, a bit of point-and-click puzzling, a small management layer where you send your imps to cause problems for other people so they don't cause problems for you. None of the mechanical aspects are too hard, and you'll be prompted to skip a battle if you die more than once or twice: it's much more about the story and the world. Definitely recommended for anyone who likes story games or folklore.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.user: The Last of the Star Makers
_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, the graphics are just so-so and the whole fixed camera nonsense is hella aggravating when trying to explore an area. Aside from that, the game really nails atmosphere and storytelling. I appreciate a female protag, love the Slavic theme, and enjoy solving puzzles. I don't expect the kind of replayability that I got from something like Slay the Spire, but this game has far more plot than games like that could ever hope to have. I do expect to run through the game twice (I'm probably about halfway through the first run of the story at present with my ~16 hours) and that'll add up to a decent amount of playtime in the end for the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very original game:It fuses a classical card battler with a nice, interesting story which introduces you to the slavic/russian pre-christian folklore. The visual style is rather simple but pleasant. Some incursions in folkloric music are timeless little pieces of marvel.I recommend it for people who wish to discover an interesting piece of well-build adventure into eastern, archaic Europe, at least for westerners.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly great indie game! I really enjoyed the story and the fighting system, which is not something I can say for many games. Graphics are rudimentary and some mechanics are clunky. But an engaging story, likable characters and a highly customizable battle system make Black Book more fun than many triple A titles. Definitely worth a buy for RPG fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent storytelling with a solid foundation in Russo-slavic folklore. Deckbuilding is comprehensive, allowing for three different saved decks as the need arises. Combat is also challenging--once a player is familiar with base cardplay new challenges are introduced--puzzle fights, where one has limited time and cards to complete the battle, and koldun fights where if you use more cards than your enemy you lose initiative. As for the minigame, Durak, it's simple and fast-paced so makes a fun diversion.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Eh again, I wish there was a 'neutral' review option.Nothing about this game is egregiously bad or tedious to play but for me, it did not hook me strong enough for me to finish the game out.The deck building, world building and folklore are the games strongest features and if you're even remotely interested in the topic, you will really enjoy your experience. I could not have cared less but still found myself reading all the notes, and pieces of folklore dropped in here and there.I've just finished a very long section of the game (~4 or 5 hours) and found myself losing patience towards the end. Imagine my shock when I see that I've only finished chapter 1 and broke one seal...I have 6 more seals to break.idk man, the game isn't bad but it does nothing for me to want to keep playing to finish. It feels wrong giving this game a negative review because it is a clear labour of love and, for the right person, may be the perfect game. The only battles that were fun and engaging were the boss battles however, those are too few and far between it seems. The game loves littering your path with weak mob-like enemies who you can burst down with your eyes closed. It just gets a bit boring.For me, I'd just much rather play slay the spire.Not a positive review; not a negative review. Just a review.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: As a Slav myself, I'm more than delighted to play a slavic mythology game done right! I've always been very interested in the mythos of my cultural heritage and it's such a breath of fresh air to see them represented in the video game ganre as well. I fell in love with this game the moment I started playing and it keeps on being even better. Thank you so much!   ♡
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely wonderful game, maybe not for everyone. The greatest strength is the lore about Slavic mythology and tales, if you liked the setting of the Witcher, Yaga, Inscryption, etc, you'll surely enjoy it too. As an Eastern European who grew up in a village, the lore texts actually gave me a lot of information about the customs I've never paid much thought, like why does old crosses have little roofs on them or why does certain things considered bad omen. The historical lore is also great, like how the industrialisation affected the people on the countryside or how was salt extracted. The immersion is flawless, the minimalistic graphics strangely enhance it. Gameplay mechanic wise, it is kin of basic, but still brings some tweaks into the classic deckbuilder formula with orders, keys, action number. The items and allies are also really useful, and help both the immersion and the variety.Its completely optional, but I really loved the card-based minigame, especially that you can use your magic to cheat. My only nitpicking that the card list is a little different then the standard, and could've used a single popup window during the tutorial with the card values. I also had hard time to distinguish the jacks and kings, but that is only me.The only negative thing in the game is the cumbersome controls and camera in the free movement sections. Using the keyboard to move helps, but its still clumsy and doesn't really add anything (there is exactly 1 section in the game where you need to sneak, so the movement is critical).
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: So far I'm loving the game. I like that it has a little of everything. Its super fun to learn about some of the folklore, but I really enjoy that its doing that with a bit of an RPG vibe. I like choices matter type games, rpgs, and card games. This is kind of an amalgamation of all those things. It is lovely dark and atmospheric, a little bit whimsical, and just a good bit of fun. It's been a bit since theres been a modern game I really get immersed in, so this has been satisfying.  I like that its kind of up to you how you play and what skills and strategies you employ.  I feel like at the moment, I would play it again. I'm not super far in, but I've very much enjoyed it. It kind of drew me in much the same way as Civilizations has the "just one more turn"  aspect, I am "just one more quest or map area" here. Give it a shot if you like slightly darker games, rpgs, crpgs, card battlers, or any adjacent style games. I super dig it.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: This game is story heavy! I don’t play many card-based games, but this game makes it pretty easy to learn how to use the cards and get by without going ham on making the perfect deck. I love the amount of folklore in this game, and I enjoy the characters a lot as well, they had a lot of love put into them. The art is unique, with just the right vibe for the slightly eerie overall feel and the more intense horror moments. The gameplay is well paced in my opinion, not too fast and not too slow. New mechanics are introduced to you thoroughly and separately so you don’t get overwhelmed. It’s very satisfying to figure out a combo of cards that does a lot of damage all on your own. Did I mention all the cool folklore and mythology? All in all this game is great, I love it, thank you devs for creating it.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: This is a solid game. Not the greatest roguelike I've ever played but it's quite enjoyable the further you make it. Potential for varied deck builds when paired with artifacts you find along the way is what's keeping me engaged. Story is meh. Decently entertaining enough but that's not what's keeping me playing. I do like how they bring back characters from previous chapters and keep them involved in the story though. Biggest Con: Walking around/trying to interact with anything outside of combat is terrible lol. Luckily you're not walking around a ton otherwise this would be a deal breaker. So yeah. A solid recommend from me. I still want to keep playing after 14 hours and the game gets better as you progress with more cards/artifacts and new buffs/debuffs to manage in battle
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Music A+.Art style A+.Very haunting and melodic look into late 19th century Russia, politics, and folklore.  At first, I thought the game took place in medieval times.  But gradually you are exposed to signs of modernity like telegraphs, railroads, and hints of upcoming WWI and Communist revolution.The battles can be difficult but if you keep losing then the game allows you to skip with an auto win.  This option was fine for me as I was  more interested in the story than game mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Engaging and extremely atmospheric story, choices that matter and multiple variants to build your deck of spells - what's not to like about this cozy stylish game? Awesome voice acting brings extra pleasure!Appreciated addition of some puzzle elements as well!Some of the encounters could be brutally punishing and require to adjust your decks pretty often.Highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really good! If you are looking for a great story with deckbuilding fight style its even more directed to you! Definitely RPG.Few words before I list what I like and what I dont. You are a witch(knower or koldun in game) who wants to release his beloved from hell. There is a unique "SIN" factor which increases if you made something bad or decreases if you help characters/souls etc. that you meet during your adventure. You start as a "blank page" and MOST of choices affect the world and futher story till the very end .  You move from location to location until you reach a final one. Then you get back to Izba(home) and prepare for another task. I finished game on a 3rd difficulty level out of 4. PROS:- Great story- Lots of reading as the game world is really well desigend and you can dive into it deeps. - Based on mythology- Very good graphics with its own soul. - You can be good, bad, middle(Im not sure if middle is counted as bad, but definitely not good) - Music- Devils (Chorts :D)- Dark climat- Replyability - Good combat mechanic- You can play "Durak" - card game in card game :)GOOD or BAD(you choose):- story contains many uncommon english vocabulary - its not only armor, damage,buy and sellCONS:- Sometimes I was getting tired as I felt game is getting too long- Your 3D character movement can sometimes be a bit frustrating- I wish I had more options in character tree when leveling (I think you can totally skip it and still finish the game...however it will be much harder for sure)- Statuses above your character while in combat could be displayed in a different way, as when you have to many - its getting crowded (maybe your character statuses can be moved to the top of the screen...)- Animations in combat still to slow even on fastest speed - I wish I could have a possibility to make them faster then the fastest(much more)Note: 8/10 P.S: I was AFKing a lot so its around 30 - 40 h of gameplay depending if you read and tires to do everything.P.S: I will try it on hardest level later in the future, but right now its to many games that I need to check :P
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic little gem with over 30h for your first playthrough. Good story, great writing, very interesting lore and many cool gameplay mechanics. Game has a lot of decisions as well and they can impact the narrative, characters and even their life or death. There is a ton of dialogue and each line is voiced and done with an authentic accent, which is pretty exceptional.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable game. I've always been fascinated with folklore, and intrigued by Slavic folklore, and this game doesn't disappoint. Someone had made  the comment about switching to from English commentary to the Russian, and I agree. It makes more of an immersible experience, and the voice acting is 10 times better. If you love myths, legends, folklore, or are interested in Slavic words and stories. This is an amazing game.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: If you are hoping for "Slay The Spire" but in Russian mythology look elsewhere. This game is not that. This is a narrative first experience where you have seemingly very little input on the visual novel the game puts your through in order to get to the game play portions.The visual novel is kind of your run of the mill Slavic Dante's Inferno style affair or something. Instead of like actually deciding how good or bad of a person you are you just sort of listen to the voice actors read off their scripts.There is a vestigial management portion of the game where you have to send your demons out or else they get restless, but I dont really know why I want the demons to start with its not like they actually give me anything. It seems that all I get from them is "Sin" and cash money. The worst part is that you are sending them out to Curse people and no one ever yells at you for having a bunch of demons running around town terrorizing folks. I was genuinely trying to clear the map as often as possible and yet people were still acting like Im this kind wholesome loving medicine woman instead of a demon summoner sending demons to raid everyone's pantries or what have you.The card battles are where the game gets good with interesting visuals and kinda fun mechanics that are very basic Slay the Spire style stuff. The thing is you spend so much time in between them listening to the Baba Yaga fan-fiction that it feels tedious to play. What I would personally love is a like "Road to Hell" mode that lets you play the card game with minimal story interjections. Maybe like a line or two between battles to explain what you might find ahead but thats it.As it stands I recommend this game if you enjoy Visual Novels with unique stories because Black Book definitely does that well. Vasya is this kind endearing character who has to make some choices that might be considered difficult and there does seem to be slight story deviations depending on how wicked you want to be.But like I said if you are looking for another Slay The Spire that focuses on Gameplay give it a miss.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: A good deck building game.Goes into Russian mythology with detail this includes mythical beastsextensive detail terms and phrases some explanation on how it came about (how Christianity mixes with the pagan faiths there.)Its a darker game which fits the darker mythology.There is choice, and your choices have effects on game playyou may play with only your own interest, gaining a lot of Sin in the process but the game gets easier as a resultor you can play to minimize sin causing the game to get much harder. You can even walk between both sides not a Saint but not a Demon either. The art style is fitting and done well. I love how they want to immerse you in the gameto the point of even adding songs from this region. Most of which are beautiful to the point of rivaling Latin songs (in my opinion) A solid 10/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: I did a big complain Review, then changed my mind as it really is a good game, then got stuck again and changed my review to a negative, but...If u can work out what the cards mean, it is a truly good and artistic game with awesome lore to feast on. My main criticism and the reason I originally changed it to a negative review TWICE was because of the Puzzle battles. U cannot grasp what the cards exactly do because of poor translation. BUT it really is a great game anyway and if u really want to u can understand the mechanics, its just I cant do that with the puzzle rounds, they only allow a specific choice. What the devs did was allow u to bypass the puzzle rounds after a couple of tries, thats great and really helps u progress. I love the world building and lore, the many many card fights and the little additions like the card game to win money and thinking about the chort army I have...though at the beginning I thought PLUS Sins was a good thing so I had my chorts get maximum SINs...my own fault really, but I hope I havent gained enough sin for the bad ending. Ive heard u get the bad ending over 200 Sin and I have 190+ atm. Fingers crossed I can complete the game with less than 200 sin and then its been a mostly positive experience. Some fights u may need to really go back a save game and change ur cards to win, whether its more curse cards or more poison cards or whatever. Its a great game but still, plenty of the card explanations are really difficult to work out because of a non english team. Its a good game that could be tremendous if the translations were really good. Still, I would implore u to buy this game if u like good card battlers and decent stories.
