_childDocuments_.review: A really solid card battler game. The biggest draw of this game is its interesting and original setting in Slavic folklore, making for some story arcs that are refreshing and, at times, unpredictable.The game is also quite generous in length, for an indie, with several highly fleshed out chapters, all completely hand-crafted (no procedural generation here). The card battling itself is competent, though there are only really three styles (straight damage, curse, and waste). The game is balanced such that its better to just go hard on one style, rather than try to create interesting hybrids. The game has several interesting and new mechanics, such as the Chorts vs. Sin system, and it has a strong "just one more turn" hook.On the downside, the English localisation is a bit choppy at times. There were two scenes where Russian subtitles came up instead of the English ones. I noticed some English spelling and grammar mistakes, and also sometimes, I couldn't really follow what the characters were saying (it was like they were having two different conversations), I suspect due to translation issues. Other times, the VA and subtitles just wouldn't match up at all, and in one or two cases, this could lead to confusion during game play (e.g subtitle says go right, but VA says go left). There are also some minor balancing and bug issues, such as cards getting stuck in the hand when using gestures. I also had a big issue with the boss at the end of Chapter 6. I felt this battle was extremely drawn out and forced you into a straight damage/defence shootout due to the fact that you could only play 2 cards at a time against it. Overall, though it's a really solid and interesting game.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: A charming game, an interesting mix of visual novel and card battler. It was cool to get some exposure to slavic mythology. I played half the game in english and switched to russian for the rest. I definitely recommend picking russian from the start. I think the game is rough around the edges and felt like it was a bit too long (though I did pretty much every optional task). Combat wise I didn't find it too difficult once I got a bless build going, though the puzzle fights weren't my favorite. At the least if you lose puzzle fights a couple times, you can skip it with no punishment. Overall very solid and was impressed with what the fairly small dev team was able to accomplish
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy to read, if you enjoy folk lore, cryptid's, demon's, myths and magic then you will find this to be what your looking for when Youtube runs dry i wont say much about the combat since it is card battles you already know what to expect. its not just about being stronger in a battle. it is a game about knowing things, you are a knower after all. The more you talk, the more you read, the more information you retain, makes it easier for Vasilisa on her dark journey towards earning her wish. She may be a witch, but that does not mean she is a bad person, there is a reason for her to have taken on the burden of the devil and his chort's. Like witches, not all demons are bad some will help you some are just lost souls in need of help but of course there are those who want nothing more than her blood.It is up to you on what you choose to be, curse people for money, let your underlings reek havoc on innocent people become a evil witch but those actions, well its not up to me to tell you what will happen nor will i be able to as one is trying to be as good of  that i can which is a difficult task with the responsibility Vasilisa has taken on.I am so happy i purchased this and have nothing negative to say of it, the art style is cute the lore is amazing the songs are powerful and beautiful, the characters are deep and emotional everything is just 11/10  i will say switch the speech to its native Russian to get the best experience and emotion of the characters.

_childDocuments_.review: I have only played through most of the first chapter. but this game seems like quite something. It isn't breaking any new ground with deckbuilding games or anything, but it is unique enough while remaining streamlined to allow for your own strategies, and you are importantly not forced into card "packages", like in some lesser deckbuilders. It reminds me more of an online card game, where collecting the cards isn't so much of the issue as refining your deck to be as effective as possible. As for bugs, they are negligible and none game-breaking, and the developers seem dedicated to fixing them with quick updates.The more impressive part of this game is the art design and lore. If you are a person who likes reading all of the encyclopedia entries and notes in open world games, this game will be heaven. Even as a person who normally ignores most of that stuff, the game encourages you to read it all by not making it too long and by requiring the information from the knowledge in order to have favorable outcomes when dealing with the demons that they are about. This game oozes more Slavic culture than even something like Pathologic, and keeps to their traditions more closely while still creating a down-to-earth fantastical world of their own. Oddly, it sort of reminds me of the feeling of watching Spice and Wolf. The game isn't impressive as far as graphics are concerned, but it works for what the game is going for.TLDR; Solid deckbuilder, great lore reading and storytelling, play with Russian voiceacting on, 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: the game is a pretty unique combination of genres - a story RPG + deckbuilder + puzzles + built-in russian card game. the deckbuilding part is quite solid overall, with bosses being reasonably challenging for the first part of the game (at least on the highest difficulty), and even later the game still throws a curveball at you here and there. there's perhaps a shortage of "effective" decks, but at least you'll see it shift from one to another as the game progresses (and sometimes you'll still have to re-adjust the deck for a particular opponent). "battle puzzles" are probably the most unique addition in this game. they basically ask you to find a way to maximize your effectiveness with a fixed set of cards in a fixed amount or turns. it's an interesting way to use the main mechanic for something else (and they are now skippable for people who hate them)the RPG part is done well i guess. there are some interesting characters and choices, and it's based on an "exotic" mythology.i was concerned about its save system at first, as it only saves when you enter a new location, but decided to give it a try and in the end it didn't bother me much (and "checkpoint" saves are a  pet peeve of mine), since the amount of stuff you might have to repeat really is minimal. also, an option to immediately replay a fight was added later. couple of tips though: - even though the game seemingly lets you save anywhere, what it does is copy the last checkpoint into a named save (normally there's a single automatic checkpoint save). so if you want to save after a big fight, move to a new location and save there- you can skip dialogs with a mouse wheel, which is much faster than clicking.as for the cons, they are endemic for games made by tiny studios - poor 3d graphics (it's heavily stylized, but still quite poor), somewhat imperfect balance in both cards and enemies, some mechanics are not very interesting (e.g. the chort system). some cases where you have to find the correct answer in a dialog feel like pure guesswork (although most of them are either reasonable or could be looked up in the journal, and in any case they are trivial to save-scum around). also, if you play it in english it'll throw a lot of transliterated russian terms at you (to keep the authenticity), which you may or may not appreciate. also, card descriptions are sometimes too vague.

_childDocuments_.review: "While I was playing this game, my uncle said it was not very good. He said there were no such things as Chorts, and he did not cross himself when he said that. The next day, my uncle died." (New Bailichka!)This is a neat card battle game, allowing you to do all kinds of fun stat attack packs, combination packs, curse packs and the such. I'd like it okay for that, but the great bonus of the game was the story and the background of old Russian folktales at the turn of a century before the world changed. There is a push-pull throughout the whole game, between Orthodox Christianity and paganism, budding modernity and the inertia of centuries, and of course the paradox of being a witch, an essential part of the community but also pretty much the source of most miseries and curses around. I will be playing again one day, I'm sure, this time with an evil approach just to see the difference :)

_childDocuments_.review: It's definitely worth it as a journey into the Slavic folk lore and culture, but the game itself might be a bit on the weak side. Grab this for for the unique setting, story and culture that you'll experience, but don't expect the next Slay the Spire.The core gameplay is centered around deck building. Unfortunately, it's neither very creative nor balanced. I would strongly recommend playing the game on easy  to enjoy more of the environment, rather than spending too much time playing one identical battle after another. Bosses and puzzle encounters can definitely be interesting, but 90% of the time you 're just applying the same strategy over and over. Often you even end up dragging the combat out longer in order to use healing cards. Health does not reset between encounters.One of the key gameplay elements is answering lore related questions. As some reviewers have pointed out, the game does not explain the lore before you may need to apply it. In such events, don't be ashamed to reload the save after failing.Being in a good position to compare original Russian and the English localisation, I can say that it's unfortunately rather mediocre. It sounds like English voice actors really didn't have any context for the lines, so they often sound out of place. That's even a problem with Russian voice, but not to such an extent. The translation is not amazing either. It really could've used some QA and polish. Having some chiorts at your disposal is a key gameplay mechanic. While there is no direct translation, it does not help the player when they are referred to as chiorts, devils, gremlins or demons interchangeably when specifically explaining the mechanics.There is a game feature that highlights key words in a conversation that might need explaining. This helps in Russian because a lot of the words and terms are archaic. It's also great for localisation because it gives translators an opportunity to explain additional things as well. Unfortunately, it appears underutilised and often shows inattention. Highlighting Leshiy in text and giving an explanation for Leshy is an example of where both are valid, but someone should've made a Style Guide and had some QA run over it.Running Russian voiceover along with English subtitles shows that English may not have been working with the final version of the text. Some names and events don't quite match. It's not a translation mistake  because you wouldn't accidentally translate Mother as Natasha.Finally, while the English translation is overall well written, it shows some errors in understanding of the Russian meaning. A lot of the nuance in this game is about old superstitions. If you don't quite understand what it's about, you end up with translations that make sense, but miss the point. An example would be translating "vampires can't cross a river" as "vampires can't swim". It might make sense, it might work in the context of events, but something important got lost.Despite some localisation issues, I would still strongly recommend this game. It may have been the best effort so far to bring the Russian folk lore to the western audiences.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty fun game if you focus on the story! _childDocuments_.review: I would like to thank the developers for this game. _childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Warning!! Long review ahead! To be short: I liked this game very much, it took 40 hours for me to play it, it can be challenging, and it is card game with story, nice music and visuals and folklore collectibles.    My favorite game of 2021. Even though I haven't played many of them that year.  The core gameplay of Black Book is a cardgame with deckbuilding. You took quests, travel across the lands of Cherdyn region and fight different enemies (undead and demons usually). I can't say what game Black Book is similar in gameplay, but it is quite interesting to build your own deck, fight against different enemies and trying to find a best tactic against specific enemies and bosses (who can be really challenging in my newbie opinion, but I finished game on 3 difficulty and sometime it was quite difficult).   However, this game is not all about deckbuilding. There are also small walking locations there you can talk with characters,  play with them in real russian card game, called "Fool" (which is really interesting and could easily eat a few hours from you), find something interesting (like lore texts similar to ones in Valiant Hearts) and admire lowpoly landscapes of Russia. And if you play the game as I did with trying to research and visit everything, it will take you 30-40 hours to walk through the game.  The story of Black Book is simple but yet interesting. You play as a young girl named Vasilisa living in the Cherdyn region near the cities of Perm and Solikamsk in Russia. Sudden change of her life - death of her beloved one push her to become a witch, challenge demons and open all 7 seals on the infamousgrimoire called Black Book to make her wish come true. As I already said the story itself isn't something great, but it is interesting, believable and helps you to keep interest in your travel across nineteenth century Russia.   And now it is good to mention one trait of Morteshka studio games which makes them so special as games (in my opinion). They are made with love to their homeland - Perm region (and Cherdyn region is a part of it). The developers based Black Book on local fairy tales and myths of nations which live in that land. And their culture is not just part of visuals, names and appearance of characters and mobs. The developers wanted to share story, folklore of their land with other people. And so, as I mentioned before - like in Valiant Hearts you can obtain many stories, tales and even hearable songs during your travel. All of them is provided with Glossary because some words are old-fashioned or local (and for foreign, non-russian speakers without dictionary can be difficult to understand). And this is amazing!   As you can see on screenshots and in trailers, game can't be prided for modern graphics. Yes, it is simple, but charming and I have no doubts that the developers did their best to impress the players. But they did it in an unusual way. Sprites of characters in dialogs and items in inventory are good. As for the design of cards with spells - it is wonderful. They can be an art just by themselves.  The last thing I want to mention - translation. I'm a Russian native speaker and unfortunately I hadn't played the game in English. So you should better read some other review =). But I guess it is fine. However, if you want to study or practice your Russian in this game, it can be a bit difficult. So be ready.  So, do I recommend this game? Yes! Not only because as Russian I love that game (it is really amazing to go through all the stories which are the part of your nation's folklore) but also as a player. It is interesting in gameplay, in story- and lore-telling, music and even visuals. So if you are interested in some new Russian, new card or deckbuilding game I highly recommend it to you.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: It's good!  The highlight here is the Russian folklore setting and the Russian voice actors.  Almost every line of dialog is voiced.I'm not generally a fan of 'deck building' games, but the mechanics here seemed decent enough.  The mechanics support the story well enough and I was forced to adjust my deck, (or build alternates), at least a few times through the story, (normal difficulty).Acting quality is inconsistent, but generally the main characters are solid enough.  There are occasional translation errors, but not enough to obscure the meaning of the dialog.I give it a B+
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Hmmm very hard to rate for me.  The typical "Well, YES, BUUUUT" Rating...Altough its a really good game for what it costs, (dont expect a Tripple AAA Title) it does have a huge "problem" for me :If you are a somewhat experienced Deckbuilder Player, you will find the game 95% of the Time way to easy. Or, to put it in other words : The Systems and Cards are not really "balanced" Since there are no "Costs" , (every Card takes up 1 Slot in your "Spell" ), it becomes very obvious which cards are stronger than others. . After about 9 Hours i am in Chapter 2 (the Game seems to be pretty long if you read all dialogs and so on... ) , but my Deck stayed the same pretty much from the first hour. (Never use more than the minimum 13 Cards, and stack that Blessings and Wards , you pretty much "Instakill" every normal encounter in Turn 1 or at most Turn 2 , dealing 20+ damage to all enemies on screen per attack, with multiple Hits (which is usually their whole HP-Bar), and/or Tank like a champ :DThis might change in Chapter 3 or later, but i am not sure if i am going keep on playing, since every "standard" encounter plays pretty much the same, and even the bosses take just 1 or 2 turns longer.  And after 10 hours that gets a bit boring...I did play on the "experienced" Difficulty, the third of the 4 ones.  Might be harder on the fouth one, but the problem with the balance stays regardless, it would probably just take 1 turn longer on averageHOWEVER as i said, that might just be me, as i have a LOT of experience with those kind of games and different Card mechanics. And i don´t think the Game was ment to be a "hardcore "Min--Maxer" Experience. It does have its own Charm, and the Setting is something you don´t see that often. Overall i would still recommend it to the "average" Card Gamer :)
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved Black Book! The Russian folklore was fascinating and the songs, oh the songs, were lovely. While most of the graphics/animations are on the simplistic side, there are also some stunning cutscenes.This was my first card RPG and I needed several tries for some battles. They can be quite tricky, because you can't use the same strategy for every enemy or battle type but that's also how it should be to keep it interesting.This game has got a lot of substance to it and kept me thoroughly entertained, 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Great game in terms of story, atmosphere, interesting combat mechanics. I just wanted to keep playing it till the end.I play a lot of card games and Black Book's combat system was a breath of fresh air. Of course it's hard to invent something really new in the genre, but I truly think this is innovative enough. Maybe a bit of a let down was that I figured out a really powerfull synergies right at the beginning and was basically steamrolling all opponents all game long, didn't really have to switch up cards in deck that much. Maybe I should've played at the hardest difficulty, dunno. At the same time it was still fine, as it felt good to be so powerful)
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: + cards used in a single turn have very strong synergies+ deck split into two types and during each turn you draw from both and can use specific number of card of each type+ unique setting +/- combat is good during boss fights and bad during ordinary fights+/- buffs and debuffs are extremely powerful+/- there is a 4x action speed modifier, but eventually it still becomes too slow- it's too long for what it is, which makes both the combat and story get progressively more boring (especially after you create a good deck). It would have been so much better with most of the non-main story cut out and just leaving deck building and interesting boss fights- sometimes there are no boss fights for prolonged periods of time - and these are the only combat encounters I am interested in!- I once got a massive sin penalty (affects your ending) for saying that a raven talked with me in the forest. Sure, the raven told me to not say anything, but I made no promises and it was sketchy! The penalty was equivalent to spreading disease on my command in nearby villages by a chort for like a week, it made no sense- chort management is busywork and the reward is that you get less bad outcomes- actually it's worse - so bad in fact that it made me abandon the game - if you forget to manage your chorts you get massive penalties (e.g. some buffs do not work on you), which can destroy your build. You have to either reload a save or create a new deck on the fly with the scraps you have just so you can survive. I didn't feel like doing either which speaks volumes about my overall enjoyment of the game
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: - music, sounds- slavic folklore based story carries the title hard- fun combat system combining cards into spells- the monotony of the core duo (card-battles and heavy rpg dialogue) is frequently shook up by optional activities (), point’n’click style collecting and light puzzling- use of Slavic expressions, but attaching a hover-over explanation- art direction, especially humanoid characters/faces- constantly found myself missing a proper Slavic accent from the voice-over- frequent mismatch between subtitles and voice-over- UI design issues (important things with low opacity, tooltips occasionally unreadable)- missing some quality-of-life features (frequently used buttons hidden, having to re-send chots on a daily basis, encyclopedia entries ordered seemingly randomly, can’t just restart puzzle battles, usually have to go through previous dialogue over and over again)- Filimon fight is flat-out busted- having beat the game, I still don’t entirely understand how the card-based battles work If you feel that’s something you’d be interested in as well and you wouldnt be annoyed by all the reading to be done, knock yourself out!For more detail on the above points and a look at gameplay, please join me as I elaborate on my thoughts in this video:.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a delightful surprise. I think I watched like half of the trailer before buying it, assuming it would be a typical short 6hr story driven game to pass the time. Come to find out it took me over 30hrs from getting obsessed with the story, combat, & slavic mythology in general. I have even been playing Durak(card game) IRL every chance I get to teach someone.If you are interested in decently difficult(played on hard) deck battling combined with old "choose your own adventure" type decisions, along with a rich chunk of slavic lore, then this game is for you.The voice acting/translation can be a LITTLE off sometimes and there were a FEW bugs here and there but other than that I was thoroughly impressed. This was a seriously good game. Great job. A couple things that could improve the game:- let players save different decks/item sets to switch between quickly (this would be huge)- provide an option for instant casting or at least increase the animation speed even further than currently allowed. (some of the boss fights can be very long if your deck isn't perfect)
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: When an indie video game does more for sharing Russian cultural heritage with the world than the Ministry of Culture. A beautiful, loving ode to Perm Krai, its peoples and mythology. Black Book is definitely a must for everyone curious about Eastern Europe. As to the gameplay - nothing too fancy. Similar to CD Project Red's Thronebreaker and the likes, it's a deck-building game where the combat is card-based with lots of opportunities for puzzles. A handful of puzzles and bosses might make you break a sweat, especially on higher complexity - like finding yourself facing against an ethereal foe that takes no damage for the first time - but overall it's smooth sailing. In the end, there's not much room for depth of strategy. The game offers nothing ground-breaking - Black Book is simple, straightforward, and fun. The story is interesting, with lots of colourful characters, and the Russian VO is on point. The game builds a strong atmosphere and lets you immerse yourself in late 19th century Russia. The plot hooks you in, like a good book. Overall, definitely worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: This game is more like a visual fairy-tale than a card battler. The game consists of: Actually I really enjoyed my time with this game. Great soundtrack, very good voice acting (original). Interesting and funny dialogues. Too bad that english translation (subtitles) isn't very best and dialogues lose a lot of expression and color compared to the original language.Every single bit of information is important in this game. It's very rewarding if you're paying attention to every single bit of information. I really liked the story, the setting and overall aura of this game. As the story continued however, it started to drag a bit and get a little bit less interesting, only because the story wasn't going anywhere for quite a while.The biggest downside - damage calculation after various buff/debuff effects. On the screen you get one number, but once the battle starts - you actually do more damage than it was shown. I usually over-killed most of my enemies because of this. Anyway. Nothing tooooo game-breaking.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: This is an INCREDIBLE game (for a particular niche that I happen to fit perfectly). It is very plot-driven and interested in creating real mechanical incentive to choose amoral or immoral actions. The level of detail that went into assembling information about Permian and Finn-Ugric pre- and post-Catholic cultures into a coherent and interesting narrative is astonishing. Many games that base themselves on various indigenous cultures' myths do so clumsily - this makes it look easy.The gameplay is clever - having played Slay the Spire, Dicey Dungeons, etc it has a good sense of balance and interesting card interactions and loops. There are very few fights that feel completely one-sided, and boss battles are (so far) all uniquely challenging. The low-poly style (ala For The King) is REALLY well-used. I am constantly impressed at the ways they chose viewing angle/framing, background noise, and color to make environments feel not just adequate but lush. The voice acting is top-notch (I suggest setting the dub to Russian, leaving the subtitles English). The music is immaculate, every time I find a new song I stop and listen to the entire thing. I'm less than a third of the way through the game, and I've already started vocally recommending it to everyone I know.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Although it can seem foreign at times, the authentic view into 19th Century Russian life makes this game one of a kind. Anyone who likes deck-building games, supernatural epics, chose-your-own adventure, or mystery should get this game. The lore, haunting choral soundtrack, and English and Russian voice acting were top notch. I can only expect the game to get better as it becomes more balanced over time.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Black Book tells a great story. I also liked the deck building and choices. Sometimes I would enter a fight just to find out that my deck is unable to beat the battle. When this happens I chose to restart the battle, when I did that I restarted with the same deck so I had to sit around and wait to lose the fight so I could change my deck. I would like an option to die instead of restarting the battle so I could get access to the option to build or change my deck. i would also like load-out options for items. When I changed my deck type I often had to change out my items to ones that went with that deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent storytelling and a great deal of work to teach about the Russian mythology. The voice acting was really good too and using the old words even with the English text created a real mythological feeling.The combat system is also pretty unique, I think this could be interesting even as a player versus player card game, although of course balancing should be carefully applied (white is pretty underpowered imo despite a few "combat tricks"). The combat, however interesting, could have been more difficult still I feel, I played the game from the start with the hardest difficulty and only needed to retry a few fights, and those as well because my deck lacked a certain effect without which I couldn't deal damage. Herbs are really powerful although I barely used any as no need. Additionally getting money is way too easy, I guess there is a lore aspect to it but still it becomes a bit meaningless after the early game, especially with infinite money from card games if you like.Speaking of card games, bringing Durak into the game was a great experience, never played it before but now I really like it, and it is implemented quite well too (didn't use cheating though, that's a bit off imo).The scenery is also beautiful and well animated. The music fits the theme and the story in most places, although I am personally not fond of the religious hymns : d. The progression through the game is also interesting, the nodes work well and the maps are nice-looking and descriptive, and the patterns (shop appearances, healing zones etc.) are well placed. It is also nice how there comes new nodes based on your route and actions, so it is always a surprise what the map will hold for you next. Only criticism is maybe that many of the nodes would simply let the player leave the area instead of exploring it, and this is not something you should want a player to do playing the game, so I am not sure why the option exists in so many nodes (basically do you want to do X or do nothing choices).I am also a point-and-click lover, however many of the scenes with that mechanic in the game left a lot to be desired: either they were so short that there was not really any point in having them, or there were no meaningful choices or actions to be made during them. Additionally, the path-finding was sometimes pretty awful when interacting with things and had to wait ages for the MC to walk into a random spot far away from the interactable target.But otherwise, a really well made experience, with a story that feels like you have some agency in it.9 / 10
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: If you want story, get it.If you want a nuanced card game, pass.The graphics are interesting, and the story is neat. The cards are too simplistic to be engaging for anyone who has played a lot of CCG's, and that's where the game falls apart for me. I was hoping for a game like the old Magic: The Gathering RPG; this is not that. Even at the highest difficulty the game is not challenging or varied enough to hold my interest.Refunded shortly after purchase. Marked as received for free because of this.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: After first 10 hours of the game, its beautiful game. Story is great, its dark and sad but also with lot of hope.Deck build is simple as there is not many different cards, and after every kill you getting same cards over and over again. But gameplay is easy and kind of addictive. I am playing on second most hard difficulty and gotta say its not that hard for experienced player. 8/10 so far just for the mood and story of the game.Will update this when I will finish the main story.So far so good, definetelly worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Astounding and amazing. Exceeded all my expectations.I started it just to pass away the evening and couldn't put it down. Gameplay, lore, and the story blend perfectly together. Your choices matter. Characters, even minor ones, keep reappearing, enhancing the feeling that everything is interconnected. I played as a goody-two-shoes and was very happy with how the game rewarded it near the end. But I am also very excited to see other endings (not through replaying, though: too little time for that).It is also a must-have for all folklore nerds: tons of information about traditional Slavic (or should I say Komi-Permyatskij) beliefs and superstitions, creatures hostile or not and the rules of dealing with them.Two minor quips: 1) I am not a fan of voice acting (in Russian), but considering that the game apparently had a microscopic budget...2) A card game veteran will find the regular difficulty too easy. I don't understand a thing about card games, and still battles became trivial after chapter 3. For me, it was okay, because I focused on the story. But if you want challenge, go to the nightmare level.1 bigger quip:The saving system. You can save manually, but it always takes you back to entering the location / the beginning of a dialogue. Thus if you have rearranged your cards / talismans, etc., you must go to the next location / story stage, otherwise all changes will be annulled. This can get annoying.Otherwise - a great exprerience.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: The atmosphere and story are fantastic. The animations are charming. However, the game has been plagued by chorts--the game's version of mischievous if not outright malicious demons--who have obviously taken it upon themselves to make the game frustrating in many ways.The English voice work is can be laughably bad. The puzzles and questions posed often expect you to rely upon knowledge, but semi-frequently the game either doesn't provide that knowledge or only does so after you needed it. Fortunately, the game's save points will return you to the beginning of encounters so even if you're forced to answer blindly and miss, you can go back and then repeat. Unfortunately, encounters often have lengthy dialogue you'll have to click all the way through to get back to wherever it was you left off.At a certain point in the game, you will reach 'battle-puzzles'. These involve a pre-selected deck of cards combined with an inability to use items and a severely limited number of rounds (ex: 2 or 3) to defeat opponents... or you die. Some of these can be avoided--by playing a mini-game, or just leaving the encounter area and giving up on any potential rewards. Others cannot.  Edit: battle-puzzles have since been patched to allow players the opportunity to 'skip' a battle-puzzle (count as a 'success') after a certain number of defeats; however, be prepared, because in the event you feel you must restart the encounter for any reason, you will have to repeat the battle-puzzle for the requisite number of defeats all over, again.In as much, despite having kickstarted the game with high hopes, I would not currently recommend it, although I suspect I will change that recommendation at some point in the future. It IS a charming game and a delightful premise. But it still needs a fair bit of work on the part of the game studio to resolve issues that will, like chorts, doubtlessly plague the game's players.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: The black book is a complete game and as good in it's own way as Disco Elysium. If you like card battlers (you can adjust difficulty if you have troubles, or choose to skip a battle if you are stuck) and RPGs it's a very good game. High points: How immersive the Slavic folklore/traditions and devil-dealing/cursing are, how your choices matter and change the your journey, it is all truly amazing. The characters and the plot are so good it shames the rest of the video game industry to catch up.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a huge card deck rpg vet, but i really enjoy this one. Love the setting/characters and story....oh and the music is amazing.  I dig the simplified art style and overall aesthetic, but i imagine it won't be for some. Voice acting is pretty good (i played the game w/ russian voice acting and english subs). The game is a bit short (one play through is probably about 12 hours on normal) but there are a few different ways to play thru the game (morally and deck-wise) for different endings. I've played both the "holy" and "sinner' paths and found each enjoyable.a controversial aspect of the game are the "puzzle battles", where you get a set deck (separate from your own) and all your items are disabled.  in these, there is only one way to win the encounter...and the puzzle is for you to figure them out.  i LOVED these.  not only did they challenge my brain, but they introduced me to the mechanics of cards i never would have thought to use. and in most modes, you can skip them if they're too difficult for you...so they don't hold up the game you were enjoying w/ your finely crafted/predictable deck.i'd highly recommend if you enjoy deck-rpgs and slavic/russian folklore (and even if you don't).
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like the trailer over-sold it a little. It's captivating, though. Kind of cute, and I've really started to enjoy it, but I feel like it's become difficult REALLY quick, and a bit unfair. When the fights get tough, there's not much you can do about it. Like it'd be nice if I could have access to a merchant for herbs more often. And even though you have the ability to change the pages of your deck, they are still random, and much of the time if I need some protection zagovers, they aren't there. If I need to do some heavy attacking, they aren't there. Just luck of the draw.I also really wish I could name my saves. I don't think it was worth the price I paid, maybe less and it would have been worth it. All in all, I'm having trouble playing because it is way too linear and it's impossible to be resourceful.

_childDocuments_.review: Combat is a turn based card game, the gameplay involves you going through multiple stages (forests, creeks, houses, etc.) each day as you traverse the map on your way to complete a quest such as protecting a wedding or recovering an artifact, when you get to the last stage of the map for the day you control the character in a fixed camera world where you look for clues in the environment, and usually fight a boss, followed by a rest period that plays like a visual novel. If you don't like turn based games, or reading a lot of lore and having a narrative experience over gameplay it may not be for you, otherwise it's a good time sink.You can tell who made this was passionate about the subject. It has a lot of slavic lore embedded in it that you can read to solve riddles or puzzles. Ever since I played and read the Witcher games/novels I was curious about slavic lore but never really bothered to look, this gives you some basic understanding of it. In fact the koldun (what you are) concept seems a lot like a witcher (sans the silver sword or mutations), peasants give you offerings and ask for help to exorcise something or heal someone. It also gives you a perspective on how a superstitious 19th century peasantry saw the world.The game could be considered repetitive at face value, but in the grand scheme of things the adventure is unique, each day is different and each stage has different dialogue, it seems great care went into it. The game is fun, entertaining and the amount of love that appears to have gone into it contrasts with the current state of triple A gaming.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a great deckbuilding strategy game, but even better than that is the story. It almost has a telltale games feel to it but even better. When I played this game I felt so engrossed by the world it created it would remain in my mind in my dreams and I couldn't stop thinking about it. Absolutely amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: - An elegant union of story, card-battle strategy, and superstition. results in a compelling game that leaves you more knowledgeable than when you started.  - Graphics focus on art and atmosphere, instead of fidelity, to great effect.- Laced through with beautiful, traditional Russian folk music.- Recommend this game for more cerebral players that enjoy planning, reading, and thinking.- More enjoyable with Russian dialogue and English text (English speaker here).

_childDocuments_.review: It is a pretty awesome mix of your (now) usual Slay the Spire clone with solid story, great characters and overall new setting and world. _childDocuments_.review: This was an AMAZING game. HIGHLY recommend.  What a simply ingenious way to learn about Slavic medieval folklore.  I played it on the second difficulty bc I have experience with deck building and it was still pretty easy so I may try to play on the nightmare difficulty.  I got the good ending! _childDocuments_.review: I absolutly love this game! Beautiful and pretty simple story with different endings. Graphics is simple, but still eye-catching, russian voice actors did amazing job. A lot (and I trully mean it) myphology and folklore of different nationalities, and walking through game you can see how much it influenced on life of simple people in Tsarist Russia. Battles not dissapointed - in the first 2/3 of the game you can play around different abilities and strategies, but later you should more rely on deckbuilding depending of boss.Alos I'd like to thank devs for durak card game. I've never felt so nostalgic :D
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: I was a backer of Black Book, and I am very happy about the way the game turned out to be.Let's be honest about a few things: the game 3D-graphics is awful. Main gameplay mechanics are decent, but not something extraordinary: the card battle engine allows to have interesting battles and employ varying decks and tactics, but it's not what makes the game great. 2D graphics and music are OK. What really makes the Black Book outstanding and worth every minute are the writing, the lore and the plot. It's based on a very serious etnographic studies, and this gives the game the level of depth and flavour which is simply unachievable for widespread generic settings, be it orc-slaying high fantasy, laser-shooting sci-fi or superhero hurlyburly. In no other game I was looking forward so eagerly to unlocking new pieces of lore or game encyclopedia; in no other game the knowledge of how not to get tricked by leshiy in the woods was so handy. So, in a nutshell: a good game, a great piece of writing, a unique opportunity to learn about the slavic and finno-ugric myths and belief, that existed in Perm region in XIX century.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like this game has a lot of heart. It's heavy on the lore and it makes me believe (though I haven't gone and checked) that the lore in the game is actual slavic lore. Another focal point of this game is the story (though second to the lore, imo). The game rewards you for *actually reading* every little thing and comprehending the lore and the story. It's not for me. My feelings about this game overall are something like "I really enjoy that the game exists, but I don't want to actually play it". The actual process of building and maintaining decks, managing resources outside of the battles, and ultimately playing cards are... fine. I will say that there are some aspects of the card game that are original and fit the theme very well. Personally I play deck building games to build decks and fight. While that is a thing you do in this game, it's not the primary draw or focus. The other issue I have is that after taking a few days off, I forget all of the vocabulary and story that I need to know to answer questions correctly. Because of this, I find myself just looking at the game -- installed -- and not opening it up because I'm too anxious about either a) not knowing what I need to know or b) knowing I'll need to spend several minutes re-reading the encyclopedia entries to remember.  If I'm not going to play the game, then I can't very well recommend it. That being said, even with this thumbs down review, hopefully it has provided enough of an idea of the type of game it is that somebody who would like this type of game would still go ahead and get it.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: For some reason, the playtime counter is off. I played about 3 hours.I would have chosen "meh" if there was such a rating. The game plays a bit too slow and there's A LOT of reading involved. Less exposition and bad VO please (yes I know I can change it but I only speak English) and more actual gaming.The fact that they went through SO MUCH of dialogue with the voice actors is actually very impressive. A lot of love and effort went into that, obviously. Just that the actors weren't very good, the voices were forced and sounded like they were from a children's cartoon or something. I ended up just clicking through everything to get to the game.But then it turns out that you need all that information to actually play a simple little card game, and to manage your annoying minions (thanks for that "gift", grandpa...)Great music, lovable graphics, beautiful atmosphere, lots of love for the lore and the characters obviously, all great. Just not a very enjoyable game for me... Too bad!
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very much not about the graphics. They're really bad, yeahBut if you speak Russian or in any way, shape or form want to learn about slavic myths, this is a great game. It's atmospheric, it's very good at showing what the life of russian peasants was like and most importantly, it's incredibly interesting to follow. _childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly can't think of a single bad thing in this game (I say that from the POV of someone who absolutely loves both dark fantasy and this kind of game genre), except for one tiny gripe: The graphics IMO first required some getting used to, but became charming fast, especially after demons started showing up.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Many positive reviews for a reason! Don't be afraid to grab this game even if it is not on sale. I can tell this game takes a while to complete. Even at about 12 hours, I do not think I am halfway. The writing in the game is very interesting and you feel like you learn a lot of old Russian words. Enjoy comrades
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Black Book is an excellent Russian indie game!It is a kind of fusion between a card game and a visual novel.The Slavic pagan mythology is under-represented in gaming, we got a taste of it in the WITCHER series which is Polish.Black Book is a well crafted picture of olden times of superstitions and folklore in Russia!More specifically, the ethnic minority groups like Perm and Komi, which were later conquered by the Rus.You get to play as an inexperienced rural Witch that does NOT wield godlike sorcerer fireball spells or control necromancer armies, but instead resorts to curses, prayers and herbs for combat. Very unique and immersive!The combat is done through cards, as you build various decks and synergies for specific situations.Very cool take on combat, something for everyone, depending on your taste and style.(there is a very handy "speed-up combat" button in Options menu)I just have to mention some worthwhile features:1) Historical information and real life tales given through notes, provide actual clues which help dealing with riddles.2) Traditional folk songs can be found in villages. Very immersive and beautiful.3) They added the traditional Russian card game "Durak" (Fool) as a minigame. Adding it is historically accurate and further increases immersion!Despite the simplistic indie graphics, such features as the visuals, scenery and atmosphere, as well as sound design are simply excellent!PRO TIP! For maximum immersion, change the DUB to Russian.The native and authentic voice acting of these 18th century ethnic groups is superb!Black Book is such an immersive game! I played it non-stop, even fell asleep, hence the 80+ hrs on record.worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic concept let down by everything being slightly off or clunky. the art style between gameplay and dialog don't match, the english translation moves too quickly, too slowly or pronounces things just differently enough to throw off my comprehension, the in-universe explanations and information vary from not-at-all to quite interesting lore at random, and the actual card battling is very solid but lacks a hook that differentiates it from every other card battling game.Its almost there in almost every way, and I want to love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Here's the short version:PROS :- Super rich lore, even better; they definitely outdone their job at research- Plenty of playstyle available regarding the cards- Choices matter, adds more character- Top notch bang for the bucksCONS :- Lacks some QoL in items sorting- Characters 3D model could be better- Some typo and maybe mistranslation in Englishnow here's the long part:I am a fans of slavic folklore and myth myself, so when I heard this game is about slavic culture and myth wrapped in unique art style, I'm immediately sold. The setting itself is fresh and original. I have known Moscow, Stalingrad, Leningrad and the like and it always comes down to bullet and steel in my memory. But this game introduces a whole new part of Russia : Perm, with its forest and all the myths. The amount of cultural and historical value brought to this game is immense. I'm impressed by the amount of research the developer did. It features many historical and cultural narration to the most practical extent, all beautifully weaved into this game with pretty art style too.As with the gameplay itself, this game utilizes deck building style good enough. It has battle puzzle also for variation. Riddles to further dive down into the lore. You are given a few choices of how to interact with NPCs affecting the storyline, adding more value into the gameplay. The further you dive into the lore the more this game rewards you.I hope Morteshka grows and develop more story rich game featuring Slavic folklore like this. I'd be smashing that add to wishlist button
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: This is a story driven game. You have to want to learn a lot about Eastern European witchcraft. Personally, I love it and I almost never like the story in video games. The combat is better than people are giving it credit for. You've got a fair number of options for how you handle battles. You unlock more cards as you progress further into the story. You also get some skill upgrades, but there isn't a lot of variety there. They have fairly generic effects. Items, however, do let you optimize or tinker a bit more in addition to how you build your book. It's good for the type of person who wants to build several decks and try lots of different options. Otherwise, it probably does get stale.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely gorgeous. I'm simply blown away by the art direction, it's one of the best I've ever seen.I't always nice to see a setting based on Slavic folklore. Especially when it's done with such creativity.I have to mention the monster designs. They are great.The gameplay is fun and the story is engaging, I had trouble putting the game down until I finished it. Honestly, I still want to play more.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Although deck building games are not my cup of tea, I liked this game due to its unique setting and moderate difficulty. Some parts of the game mechanic was poorly described, but I could manage my way through the obstacles. I had a lot of fun with the game exploring the Siberian folklore, and the mini (card) game was also nice.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying this game! I love Slavic mythology, it's so dark. The game is also very pretty and definitely has a unique visual style. There are a few idiosyncrasies, such as how you're a witch and summon demons, but are always saying things like "God bless!", but maybe that's just cultural affectations I'm not really understanding. The translation at times can also be a bit "off" and slightly confusing, but nothing I can't figure out, and it kind of adds to the charm. Combat is smooth and fun, I really like the way you can chain together spells to create different effects. With card-battle games, you never know if the implementation is going to be smooth, or needlessly gimmicky. I'm glad that this game got it right. Lastly, although this game has spoken English set as the default, I would highly recommend you set it to the native Russian. For one, it adds additional flavour and depth, and second, the English voiceovers are terrible.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Simply incredible. Well told stories, awesome lore, fantastic gameplay. There are some glitches and such, but they're not gamebreaking. Random Russian text on cards / in speech. But, the entire game is voiced, everything said. It's a long game. I played through twice, once on hard and once on nightmare. Only thing I don't like is that there is no achievement for beating it on nightmare. But, overall epic game. Love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Book

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:1. So much rich content. I feel like I’m learning a lot of interesting things.2. The characters and plot so far are aces. 3. The card game and demon cursing are both fun little things.4. The puzzle levels are great.5. The songs!!!! 😍😍😍😍6. There might be other cool things coming, but the last one I encountered was the backer cemetery.Cons:1. This is not an intuitive game. Ideally every time you learned a new spell you would learn how it worked. I had to google to beat one demon and it was 0% clear what I should do.2. Perhaps this is a style preference, but I feel like your knowledge of spells would not go along with a deck builder. I could see gaining new spells and maybe having a cost to casting them each turn that could grow over game (and gain more powerful spells). But I see no reason why you wouldn’t have access to all your spell knowledge at all times.3. I don’t always mind the minimalist design but I wish it varied (i.e. not the same animation for different areas).4. I wish the songs did something other than just be beautiful. Maybe they will?5. The English voice acting is not the best.6. The English translation/writing is not the best.Additional:1. This game makes me want an Open World Skyrim/Witcher like game with all the same characters and facets. _childDocuments_.review: first thing you should know is block book is VERY story heavy. the story bits are voice acted but you're expected to read the notes you keep getting and retain most of it because the game keeps quizzing you on it or just use the guide tab and find the one that lists all the outcomes (i found this mid way into the game and wish i had found it sooner). these q&a's net you some xp but if you use a "hint" (they don't help in any way just highlight key words) you only get about 40% of the xp and if you fail you get none.you'll start missions by talking to people at your house, sending imps out to do mischief to get rid of their debuff, talking to visitors that sometimes add places to visit on the map, then managing your upgrades and deck. you can also play a card game that is a lot like war and i did everything i could to avoid playing it.once you go on a mission you'll see a map with nodes but before you pick the first place to go you can pick a companion that can help a bit in fights and sometimes give an extra option during events. your goal is to get to the ! node but nodes are locked until you visit the one near it but you can go to any open node no matter how far away. when you go to one you'll get an event or a walk about. the event can could end in items, shops, or even fights. walk abouts are a small landscape you can move about to collect herbs, look at things or, talk to people. finally when you click the ! node you'll move to the next story part and when completed you'll go back to the house to repeat everything.the card fighting is like a simpler slay the spire or neoverse. play cards to attack, damage over time, defend, defend over time, or use a curse (there are more and later you'll get cards they play off others but this is your main cycle in the beginning). you can also use herbs and if you have items equip they will automatically do their thing. if you win you'll get some xp, bread/coin, and a new card (out of 3).the games got charm but your in for a long story time and though i really liked the story it can feel as if i drones on if you don't take breaks. the fighting is more to break up the story bits and so are the q&a's. the q&a's are also a bit annoying because since this is a Slavic fairy tail the names are unfamiliar and some feel misleading. overall the game is nice but its more of a visual novel than constant fights.

_childDocuments_.review: Black Book is a gem.I really enjoyed playing the game and really can recommend to play the game, but it is special and certainly not interesting to everyone.This game could be something for you, if you...- dont mind roughly designed graphics. The gamedesign is not detailed, rather blurred and concentrates more on allusions, but this on the other hand leaves space for your imagination.- are interested in a deep story. The story is quite linear, so the game is more like a graphic novel, but often has decisions, that you have to make and which can influence the further developement of the story. if you like, that your decisions have consequences, the game might be something for you.- interested in russian folklore and tales about witches, ghosts, good and bad spirits etc. - card collecting games. The game is centered around your spellbook which gets larger over the time and leaves you more and more choices to design up to three different battledecks. In the course of the game, the spells become more powerful, bringing more tactical choices for the needed build setup, as well as artefacts that interact with them.Some reviewers compared "Black Book" to "Slay the Spire" which is in some aspects similar to "Black Book", like you collect cards and use them in battles, you can visit traders, chose different paths and meet boss monsters. But that is on the surface."Black Book" is not just a rogue-like game, in which you play as far as you get, earn benefits which maybe carry over to your next playthrough. It is more like a graphic novel, where collecting spellcards and finding the right combination for the challenge ahead differs from "Slay the Spire", as you are able to recomposition your spells and you are not just forced to use the spells you have accumulated. Later in the game it is possible to buy missing spells or needed duplicates quite easy.The difficulty of the game is fair, meaning you have a fair chance to beat challenging situations. there are some "riddle"-Situations in which you have to find the right solution for a predefined set of spells for a certain situation. After several fails, you are offered to skip situations in which you didnt succeed. But if you want to best these situations aswell without skipping, it sometimes takes some will and patience to find the right solution or the right setup. At one riddle in the late game, I needed two days, trying something and leaving it be several times, to find the right solution.Especially in the late game you get into more and more challenging situation. I was happy, that there is a save and load option in the game which i used ,in the late game to have the opportunity to adjust the deck according to the situation.The game has beautiful vocal music from a women's choir, singing traditional folk music which adds nicely to the gloomy, rough land life in 19th century russia.I recommend playing the game with the original vocing and english subtitles. It was really agreable to listen to the well spoken text and helped a lot immerse in the story.So if you are more interested in the story content and not in aesthecical perfection, if you are interested in metaphysical beeings and russion folklore, this game might be worth a look. I, personally, enjoyed it very much.

_childDocuments_.review: That was really good. It had its weaker moments, for sure, some flaws and mechanics that would leave me rather bewildered, but it was worth embarking on this long, long journey. So, the pros.First and foremost the culture. In found myself soaking in all the atmosphere and delighted about the exploration of myths and traditions of the old. Story was engaging and kept me intrigued for the most part - even though the start is pretty hard to get into.The characters are well-written, easy to like (even those with some sins behind their ears) and sometimes surprisingly complex. I liked the 2D style for their depictions and 3D for the environments. Still not sold on the 3d character models, though.  Music was atmospheric and pleasant to the ears. I appreciate the folk songs addition as well.Puzzles were clever and not impossible to get for the most part. I liked the riddles the most (Pierre, my swan-guy! My dear toothy swan!)Gameplay was decent enough,although the combat mechanics left me scratching my head on more than one occasion. I have finished the game and battled hundreds of battles, yet I'm still absolutely perplexed about how some of the spells work.So, speaking of, while there are many other pro-s, there were definitely cons as well.The aforementioned combat-mechanics, for one. Either I'm entirely dumb and just missed the explanations for some of the spells&effects, or there were never properly explained in the first place. Of course, you can go trial and error, but there are so many factors, combinations and spells influencing each other and mixing the effects that it sometimes makes you unsure about what actually happened. I would like some short notes on things like sweep, for example. Same ones as you get for effects (like waste, curse, etc).I feel like the battles can be uneven and unfairly punishing for the players. The difficulty changes based on luck-related events and prior-knowledge, especially when it comes to the bosses in the beginning. Let me explain. Most of the casual encounters tend to be rather easy, so you oftentimes find yourself sweeping the enemies left and right on your path to the boss. This doesn't encourage exploration of different battle styles or investment in spells and items (especially since you need to spend money wisely). But if you don't roll the favorable spells on your journey, you can be truly screwed in some of the boss encounters. I found myself especially stumped during the mermaid battle. She was dealing massive damage (almost my full hp) each turn and receiving only insignificant damage in return, no matter which spell combinations I tried. Later, however, I discovered that I was simply unlucky in getting my spells and items (even though I did 100% exploration, though passed on some combat encounters in favor of solving them diplomatically). Later, when I obtained more beneficial cards, this fight seemed trivial in comparison. And so did all the future boss encounters. I don't think I had real problem with even one of the later-game bosses, even the gatekeepers at the final level, who couldn't even hurt me after setting-up with mostly some 3rd-4th circle curses.  So, the balance just isn't there and could really use some polish.The combat mechanics were fun, though, as well as the battles.There were also some other minor issues, nothing as big as this imbalance though. Just a tiny note, some of the written dialogues are not translated in the English version (although the voiced lines are all fine). There was also - what appeared to be - L0D issues with some 3d models, flickering on the screen based on the distance. Didn't matter much though.All in all, a surprisingly engaging game. I recommend giving it a try! A really well-made and rather unique game. Well done!

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game through and through. For people who like to experience other cultures, learn myths, lore, and legends, and bask in music and the lived experience of others, this game is pure joy. For gamers who like card battlers, this game is definitely intriguing, and there are some interesting combinations you can build up as you go with 3-4 main strategies around ongoing damage, self buffing for damage, self buffing for defense, and debuffing the opponent with curses. I tried both curses and blessings, and ended up smoking opponents quickly through the power of the heavens.One of the well designed elements here is that there are multiple avenues to complete your goals. Run into guards? You can win a riddling contest, mow them down with the power of your Zagovers, rely on a clever companion, or wager your soul in a game of witching Durak. It encourages a role-playing approach, where you choose the way you interact with the world and see the results reflected in future options, the weight of your sins, and in the powers you choose to embrace.10/10 would pause the game to listen to the choirs sing again.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this game is a hidden gem. I'll admit it's like, slightly broken and has elements that feel unfinished, but I still had a blast playing it. The balance issues that others have alluded to felt mostly minor to me. I will say that the final chapter and final boss battles were a letdown in that they were not terribly challenging, but for the rest of the game, I felt like there was the right amount of continuous pressure to improve my deck/strategy throughout the game. Many other reviews have complained about the chort management system and the sin counter and how hard it is to , but I didn't find it annoying or problematic at all, and managed to . The game is quite well-written, despite the translation inconsistencies. The story is fun and engaging, and this is one of the only games I can think of with a lore encyclopedia that's actually worked into the game in a way that feels satisfying. The player is often posed questions which can be answered by either reading their collected lore, remembering information from previous dialogue, applying some common sense, or sometimes guessing. The variety of methods engaged to arrive at correct answers really creates a nice experience there. A couple more notes:- The English voice acting quality is all over the place, but honestly when it's bad its bad in a way that I found charming- The save system is...not great- The collectable songs were a lovely touch. Beautiful stuff. A great game despite its mostly-superficial flaws.

_childDocuments_.review: Black Book is an OK card game at best. It's based on Slavic folklore but aside from the story, it's only superficially woven into the game's mechanics. That being said, it's not a horrible game either, but to break it down:The game does not have a ton of cards to work with and most of the effects are rather basic, either focused on dealing or mitigating damage. This leads to both deckbuilding and card play feeling very simplistic. Also progressing to new chapters can be painfully slow and this is important because each chapter unlocks new card sets.Both theme and story are heavily based on Slavic (Russian) folklore. To the point it throws Slavic terminology basically in every other sentence. The terms are explained and it's not difficult to understand it, so if you are interested in Slavic mythology it does a good job in teaching it throughout the game.The story follows the young witch protagonist in her quest to save her husband from hell. A husband who is mentioned at the start and then seemingly forgotten. Each chapter of the story is focused on one main quest around some demon, so the stories are typically self contained. The stories themselves are fine. I rarely skipped dialogues so that's always a good sign, although the dialogue itself is not always written great.Finally, outside of the main character, the voice acting in this game is downright silly. Most of the time it's not unbearable but often it prevents you from taking any of the things they say seriously. Occasionally you would get words pronounced incorrectly but at that point you should have already made peace with the B list voice acting.The enemy variety is the low point of the game. Most of them just do damage and it's not uncommon to wipe out encounters in a round or two once you have a strong deck. The bosses on the other hand are more interesting and can be challenging. For experienced card players the game does no feel challenging enough.The part of the game I absolutely did not enjoy are the quizzes. Once in a while you are quizzed on some Slavic mythology whose answers you need to find within an in-game encyclopedia that has no search feature. It's entirely annoying and unfun, but thankfully you the penalty is some less exp.Speaking of exp, you can level up in this game, but some level up upgrades are clearly better than others and they don't change the dynamic of game that much. They just make you slightly better at one thing over the other.Finally, you have the ability to control chorts (familiars), but it sounds more fun than it is. Essentially you just send them out to pester people or they will pester you. Both options are are bad for you so instead of all the cool things that could be derived from having familiars, this is what you will get instead. Tied to this is the sin mechanic. Whenever you do some evil, mildly bad stuff or send familiars you will get sins. The game says this will impact some scenarios that happen you during the game, but doesn't really tell you when it does so essentially you are never ware of the consequences of your actions.  + Unique Slavic theme setting. * Mediocre and limited card play and deckbuilding.* Good boss design but uninteresting normal enemies.* Very long campaign that doesn't introduce new content fast enough.* The story is ok. The voice acting is equally entertaining and distracting. -  Quizzes. Game teaching you some real world knowledge is fine, as long is not punishing you for opting out of it. In this case it leaves you no choice.- Pointless mechanics like familiars and the card game (yes, there is a card game within a card game) feel entirely unnecessary and are there just to push the Slavic theme further. Overall Black Book is not an experience I hated, but neither loved. In the plethora of great card games out there, it's nowhere near the top of the list. However, if you like Slavic Mythology it might be game worthy trying out. For others, the game is fine, but skippable. Careful recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: I was very torn about whether to give this a thumbs up or a thumbs down. I think it heavily depends on how patient you are about jank. If you really love to read about folklore, that could also redeem the game for you.The card mechanics are interesting, but balancing is an issue. Most mob battles are extremely easy. Bosses are a mixed bag. Either quite tedious if they happen to be immune to your status affliction of choice/dish out a status affliction every round or extremely easy if you equip one trinket to cancel out their gimmick. Sure, customizing your deck for a boss should indeed make it easier, but if you just need to swap one thing out, it feels trivial. And if this was intentional, it seriously lacks quality of life management. You can't change your deck after the fight has started. But you're allowed to, after you die. At the same time you're allowed to restart a battle anytime, but restarting alone doesn't allow you to change decks. So if you want to adapt to the boss , you'll need to die or reload the whole scene to change your deck in the dialogue before the battle start.The movement of the protagonist can be janky as hell. She barely has any awareness of her surroundings, so you need to be careful that no people or little ledges are between her and the point you want to guider her to, otherwise she’ll just continuously run against her obstacle. Then there's times where she'll start running in a different direction or even in circles before she actually goes for the spot you marked with your mouse. Sometimes you can stand directly next to a herb but the prompt to pick it won’t appear until she stands in a specific spot you have to figure out with finicky clicking.  A lot of times she also only strolls languidly to a spot instead of running to it.That's all a little irritating in the overall game but wasn't much of an issue because there was no time sensitive events. Until a section towards the end, which honestly played quite a big part on why I ultimately gave a thumbs down. It’s your run of the mill obvious spotlight searching for the player minigame. You just need to behind some pillars while the spotlight pans back and forth before moving to the next pillar. Except the janky movements largely stayed the same as before so Vasilisia would usually still walk slowly while she was supposed to dart from cover to cover. And quite often she wouldn’t stand still behind the cover but walk past the point you clicked/walk circles and right into the spotlight. This section killed me more times than all battles combined. It was so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ frustrating, I’m still a little salty about it.The folklore excerpts were cool, but if you open the tab for that, it’ll automatically change the order of the excerpts and open an unread one, which will mark it as read. If you accidentally click out of/on the tab, it can be hard to keep track on which ones you have actually already read. I wish there was an option to only mark excerpts as read if I mark them myself, I usually like reading lore in batches as stopping to read for every single excerpt ruins the game flow for me. While there's a lot of stories, they don't cover all the necessary knowledge/folklore/traditions needed to answer all riddles.
