_childDocuments_.review: Finished one thorough playthrough in 36.5 hrs over 3 days mind you, which is very close to my playthrough of Thronebreaker (35.4 hrs). Accomplished 44/50 achievements, but steam did not record 2 which I think were during an update. You can probably do it faster if you don't gamble too much with Durak lol.What is it? Rating 8/10- Think Witcher (Thronebreaker) format of play, but as Yennefer instead of Geralt (Sorcerer). You traverse the wilds/rural farms of turn of the century industrial Russia, where superstition and god fearing folk are rampant. You provide shaman-esque services whilst pursuing your quest to see your beloved husband who had passed. Game mechanics and Lore are what hooks you in. Middling voice acting and artwork. Needs improvement on UI/some card tweaks.GOOD:+  Lore/Writing/Story and consistency: Some very interesting insights into Russian folklore which I presume are well researched by the developers (not that I can really call out inaccuracies). Basically, everything morally considered "bad" has a Chort (Demon) behind it, unseen by humans other than Koldun (sorcerers). The clashing systems of belief between modern industrial Tsar Russia and rural life are prevalent here. The Story as a whole is consistent, and while straightforward, is written well and as engaging as Thronebreaker IMO.+ Decisions: Something that is usually overlooked, but the game does allow you to fail non-essential tasks. I actually like this since the minor decisions are reflected way later in the game in a mostly meaningful way. Most new games tend to baby the player into making decisions, but Blackbook does give you room to make choices, moral or not (except for the main story ofc).+ Combat/Deck building system: Appears shallow at the start, with limited customization, but builds open up once about 1/3   through the game. Once the reins are off, you can pretty much build whatever silly deck you want up to a 33 deck limit. The card mechanics are engaging enough to hook you once you get the hang of it, similar to Gwent. Durak (a minigame cardgame in a cardgame game) is VERY frustrating at first as the rules/videos are not exactly clear, but once it starts to "click", it is additive. By endgame, I still managed to hold my own against demons with no cheating.- Extra tip: My midgame/endgame deck were pretty much status effect builds (Waste/Curse) as the speed at which you can rack up both offence/defence is insanely quick. I switched from a waste deck as someone called EZ mode to a Curse/Blessed combo deck for extra spicy memes, reaching 3000 damage in a single turn.- Extra tip: Developers did not put too much emphasis on Knowledge (Skill tree) and you can pretty much survive 3/4 of the game with midgame cards with little invested in the combat skill trees.MIDDLE + IMPROVEMENT+ Voice acting (English): The game is fully voiced acted in ALL scenes and you can tell work went into it, but the tone/character matching is sometimes really off that it feels like the Devs pulled the nearest available person from the street to voice a character. You could very well say some characters were the same VA trying his very best to mimic a sound that he does not make naturally lol. - What irks me sometimes is that you have a switch between a really good Russian local accent, to a UK slang (Russians use the word lad?) and it feels off. A recommendation here for future titles is to consider a primary language to save costs, and just do an excellent job matching characters once. IMO, I read most of the text anyway, and wouldn't mind a stronger "Russian" VA experience to increase immersion.+ Artwork/Scenery: To be honest, this looks like a Unity game, with low poly characters and really basic scenery. What is strange is that the 2D elements (Cards/Map) are really well done, with its own unique vibe. I can understand that the costs to do every scene/area in the style of 2D drawings are probably higher than the 3D jank.- Recommendations for the future: I'd actually say that the game will elevate to an easy 9/10 with upgraded full 2D elements (like Thronebreaker or Darkest dungeon) instead of a hybrid 2D/3D format. I think that the lore allows the artists to really come up with great designs, and this is a game which can benefit from true artistic creativity. NEEDS IMPROVEMENT- Translations/Card texts: This may be a result of localization/translation into English, but I'll split the improvements into 3 parts:A. Translations: The Lore/Folklore stories that you use to make educated guesses to questions are actually not intuitive and a bit hard to comprehend. I did like the help text highlights for both the card texts and general subtitles, they really help alot. IE: Somewhere in the story, there was a "fiery serpant" type demon, and I had absolutely no idea where it came from or what it was, despite our character having the knowledge to answer the question. IMPROVEMENT: Could consider putting in a Bestiary based on what your main character has learned over the years. For undiscovered enemies/demons, you could put a general description of what they do so that it is easier to reference than folklore tales. B. Card texts: This could be a translation issue, but sometimes the hard descriptions on cards are difficult to accurately determine what they do and in what order. IMPROVEMENT: Help texts do assist here, but I only found them useful for explaining the text itself, and not the order at which it is executed. Consider adding a "Game Board" explanation to explain order of status effects and executions and/or add examples of how a card is played as a tooltip.C. MAP: This is a minor quality of life recommendation, but a prompt that tells you "Please finish your exploration, this is a point of no return" would be extremely useful on the map where the final destination is not the end of the map.- IE: Due to the way autosave works, once you hit the end area scenario of the map, you cannot return to the previous areas to finish exploring if you missed anything. You will then have to reload a prior manual save, and that can be quite far behind.

A fusion of card-based RPGs and Adventure games, "Black Book" is a haunting tale of a young sorceress, who gave her life to serve the dark forces. Dive into the cold, yet alluring world of Russian folktales - and uncover the secrets that hide in the darkness.

A young girl named Vasilisa, destined to become a witch, decides to throw her fate away and marry her beloved - but that dream is shattered when her betrothed dies under mysterious circumstances. Aching for her lost love, Vasilisa seeks out Black Book - a demonic artifact, said to be powerful enough to grant any wish to the one who uncovers all 7 of its seals. 

Join Vasilisa in her adventures across Russian countryside, as she solves the woes of common folk by confronting demons and performing exorcisms.

name: Heavenly Bodies
detailed_description: Heavenly Bodies is a game about cosmonauts, the body, and the absence of gravity. Discover the ever-changing nuances of weightless motion in this challenging physics game. Wrangle control of your cosmonaut’s arms with the left and right thumbsticks to push, pull, and clamber through fully physically simulated scenarios aboard a scientific research station. Your celestial duties await You have been entrusted to bring into operation Earth’s proudest feat of engineering. With only radio contact with mission control as your aid, you will have to use your sharp mind and dexterous limbs to assemble space telescopes, maintain delicate solar arrays and research cosmic botany. But without gravity, nothing is still, nothing is secure, and nothing is simple. Controller highly recommended Heavenly Bodies has a highly unique movement system designed to use a dual-analog joystick controller. Rebindable keyboard and mouse controls are technically supported, but they do not provide the intended experience. Features: A collection of stellar scenarios inspired by the feats of space explorers and researchers throughout history. Expressively control every limb of a weightless cosmonaut to perform challenging and delicate maneuvers. Play single player or with a friend via local-coop. You'll be able to play missions either solo or with a space friend. Play online with Steam's Remote Play Together. Manipulate incredibly expensive space vehicles and elaborate machinery. Stylised 70s visual aesthetic influenced by archival space photography and technical illustration. Customisable control mode difficulty Rebindable controls Accessibility A comprehensive list of accessibility features and notes can be found at the Family Gaming Database.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a game for everyone, but will explain why its a game for me and why I recommend it, based on my very first playthrough.  First off the basics directly related to the game, graphics were perfectly fine for me, seems well optimized, steam remote play did have a couple of issues here and there, but nothing we couldn't work around. I usually go by a $1/hr rule when purchasing a game, by default.  Exceptions are made for highly entertaining games, whether great story or just an insanely fun time.   If a game gives me such a value, I'll gladly make an exception.  In this case i spent $20 and got about 4.5hrs of playtime out of this game on the easy setting in a two player runthrough.  There are options for harder difficulties related to how the physics interact which I would like to test/try.  My friend and I had a blast at the level of detail in the game, the hilarity of the navigation, our impromptu physics based jank space fist fights as we attempted to blow each other out of airlocks, navigate the map, complete the various tasks or otherwise other shinanigans.   While we were repeatedly brought to tears from how hard we were laughing at the various outcomes of our impromtu fights, our SO's were laughing at our reactions and various ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ we'd levvy at each other (while we were having fun, those not familiar with us would think we hated each other).   Overall I had an absolute blast, and even if the game is relatively short,there is replayability and I would love to see either additional content added, whether DLC or sequels (although preferably free future updates).   It was insanely fun to play.    This is the first game i actually decided to use a controller with a PC game, and as a primarily Keyboard/mouse user, i'd highly recommend it, if available.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this with an online friend through remote play, which worked really well. Because they did not have to buy the game, they cannot review it, so this counts for both of us.First of all, the theme and gameplay:As a space nerd, i just absolutely loved it. We played on "newtonian" moving difficulty, so the only way we could move in 0G is using the laws of physics. The game's really cool puzzles were a plus, but yeeting each other into deep space just never got old.Multiplayer:This game supports local co-op, and online through remote. Me and my playmate live on opposite ends of the continent, and their internet infrastructure dates back to the Stalinian Era. Hence, lags lasting multiple seconds often happened, but given the relative slow pace, they never really were an issue, only causing one of us to slowly drift away.   Difficulty was fine, and more forgiving movement modes are at your disposal if needed, which you can even pick differently for each player.This is one of the best multiplayer games i've ever played. Short but sweet, leaving you yearning for more.  If you're interested in space and know someone you'd enjoy spending the time with, it's a must buy.

_childDocuments_.review: Heavenly Bodies is a physics-based game where you control a cosmonaut through various scenarios, where without gravity,  a simple task can turn into a frustrating one. Set in the 1970s, you embark on a journey about a scientific research station. Using only the mission control as your aid, you will have to use your keen senses and dexterous limbs to assemble space telescopes, maintain delicate solar array, research cosmic botany and many more.If you want the the best experience in this game, it is highly recommend that you play it using a controller. I don't think this game can emphasize it more, it's a must. Sure, there are there is an option for rebinding keys, but I doubt you'll have fun using a keyboard and a mouse compared to a controller. You can play this game as a solo or with a friend via local co-op. Unfortunately, online co-op isn't featured in this game. But luckily for us, Steam users, there is this feature called . This allows us to stream the game to someone as if we're both playing locally. Even with this feature, I can see this as a deal breaker to some. Playing a game via Remote Play feature won't unlock any achievements for the person on the other side of the stream. The missions are done well in this game. I find myself getting more invested as I go through each of them. As usual, they start of with simple tasks and then gradually piles on as you progress. Though the game can be finished in singleplayer, I still think this game shines when played by two people. Especially on the later levels, I see how it would've been easier and less troublesome during co-op. Overall, I highly recommend this game to anyone who loves a challenge, physics-based games, and especially to those who finds outer space fascinating. I love everything in Heavenly Bodies, from its aesthetics, sounds, and the gameplay it self.

_childDocuments_.review: So, originally... my review for this game was negative. The full negative review can be seen at the end of this review. What caused me to change my opinion? Even after I left a negative review, I still felt an urge to play this game.The thing is, I didn't play the later levels: The first two are really straight forward, and there is not much fun to be had, as you get used to the controls, trying to do something over and over again. HOWEVER, the later ones are more creative, and with more personality put into it. It's not just "bring this here" or "rotate this thing"; no, you actually BUILD something, then release it. To me, this feels way more accomplishing. You have more control over what to do, even though the end result is essentially the same for every player. It's about the journey, but getting to the end is fun too.A big turning point that made me realize "Wait, maybe this game isn't all that bad"... was on the fourth level. I'm going to hide it in spoilers for new players. Even though it took me quite a long time to figure out a solution to this problem, it still felt... fun. Engaging. I was able to try multiple options (even though they didn't work!) and try to solve it without the gaming telling me "hey, you need to use this".But by far the most fun I had before this review was just after what had happened:  I had a good laugh for a little while. And that's the very moment I decided to change my review.I still think that there is some valuable information in my negative review, however. Most of it could still hold true to an extent. As such, I have left it here.The ORIGINAL negative review:11 people found this helpful.3 people found it funny."It's really exhausting to play. Most of the time spent in the game is trying to move something that won't budge, or won't go in the right direction.I am not saying that this game is all bad. If you like goofy physics and are willing to try to overcome the controls, then yes, go ahead and get this game! However, I don't have a lot of fun with it."

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the funniest game I've played this year. Qwop in space with all the goofiness of something like Mount Your Friends, but with actual objectives in an interesting setting where it kinda makes sense. However you choose to play, it is intentionally frustrating to move anywhere while you try to complete a series of relatively mundane tasks. The presentation for each chapter is great, featuring a nicely drawn instruction manual like you're assembling ikea furniture.I went my entire first playthrough using the newtonian controls, and after watching a few streams of different people using the normal, swimmy controls, I think both control modes are great for what they are (the assisted mode seems good too). Watching someone swim around and/or kick their feet around is always hilarious, and sometimes very necessary to not die or complete certain challenges. On the other hand, I think the harder mode feels better if you can wrap your mind around to it. While it takes a lot more patience to get used to, it definitely feels more realistic, and the ways you have to use everything to get anywhere makes the simplest tasks an interesting challenge. Its more punishing for sure, but in many ways it was just as goofy if not more from the ways you can mess up. Every time i had to restart it was because of something incredibly dumb I did, including at one point literally getting stuck in the middle of a room.Its certainly not for everyone, especially if you don't have the tolerance for the inherent frustrating nature of these types of games, or extra time it takes to do anything, but I had a great time with it. The music is pleasant, the different environments in each level look cool, the many different sound effects are great, there are fun easter eggs in every level, and the overall story is light but nicely done with a satisfying ending.
_childDocuments_.name: Heavenly Bodies

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, what an absolutely brilliant, witty name! I genuinely adore it, and I can say the same about the absolutely fantastic Space Race-era aesthetics (those manuals and schematics are incredible!), and wonderful music. Also, I hope I have assumed correctly that the two players' space suits are inspired by Soviet and American suits? I found that so-so charming. Quick note on the co-op: I do think it would have been better as an actual  screen, not a shared screen, so both players could adjust their cameras independently. Alternatively, it would have been absolutely perfect as an online co-op experience. As it is now, I prefer Heavenly Bodies as a solo game. It was a pleasant surprise that I didn't find the controls frustrating at all; the game actually made me feel quite zen instead. And I'm saying that as someone who has picked up a controller just a couple of months ago for the first time.  There's neither a time limit nor any punishing mechanics, so you can explore and fool around as much as you like. If you find the hands confusing, I suggest adjusting your camera more frequently and moving one hand at a time: it actually makes you a lot more intentional and precise with your movement. The singular time I've felt frustrated was on the last level,   It is a valid challenge, though, so I don't think it's an issue of game design. Really, the only thing I'd "change" is adding more levels. (Which is how you know it's a great game: it leaves you wanting more!) I've discovered and completed Heavenly Bodies literally as the DLC came out, which felt like a blessing. Unfortunately, after completing HB: Cleanup, I can't praise it nearly as much as the main game. However, I'll be writing a separate review for it.To finish on a positive note, HB was an absolute 10/10 indie experience for me. If it looks like your thing from the trailer, I'm sure you will get a ton of enjoyment out of it!

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that is frustrating yet fun to play. I swear that my fingers hurt every time I finished a level because of how hard it is to control the astronaut. This is both a good thing and a bad thing. It's good 'cause it's meant to be that way but it's also bad because more often than not what I would think is the logical movement for my analog stick ended up doing the complete opposite on the arms. I don't know if it's meant that way but I'd have drastically benefited of inverted X-Y arm controls. That is my biggest complain regarding the controls and UX of the game.Despite all of that, the game looks very good, the levels are original and the existential dread of being stranded in space is real. I had my dose of fun playing this; it's just 7 levels long, each completely different than the previous one. And since the astronaut takes a fair amount of dedication to control, you're gonna be stuck for quite some time even if the level is "easy" per se.I played this solo but I think it's best if you play it with a friend or loved one. You're definitely gonna beat it faster than me. One of the levels in which you have to extract minerals from astreoids in particular is EXTREMELY frustrating with just one player.I think a more explicit storyline could have helped the game a lot. I don't think that needs more levels, although I believe people would appreciate some DLC or just replaying the game with newtonian physics instead of the "classic" mode.Overall, I'd recommend although it's not gonna blow anyone's mind. It's decently fun and well made.7.5/10 - Good!

_childDocuments_.review: "'Getting Over It' in space" will be over-used to describe this game, but it's fairly apt. A challenging, sometimes frustrating physics puzzler that rewards fine-tuning your motor control and reflexes. It starts out comical and slapstick but with a certain elegance that comes from floating in to zero G. As you figure out how the game works and the controls become easier it gets more fun to dance around the levels and explore.The environments are beautifully made, and are the highlight of the game. They do sometimes seem to put aesthetics over gameplay as it's not always immediately clear what surfaces you can grab, which block you, and which you pass through. It seems like the olive green ones are the only passable and grabbable ones but it's a subtle color cue and I'm not sure it's used consistently. Some levels are also annoyingly claustrophobic, and the struggle is sometimes to fit a fat astronaut through a narrow corridor, rather than any real physics type problem, but the puzzles are well made and a joy to figure out.While the game is *very* light on story, characterization, etc, the subtle environmental humor and details are well placed and welcome. That said, it still sometimes feels like a tech demo waiting for someone to fill in the world with some personality and details that give us some context or a goal or even a clear setting. While "Getting Over It" replaced story with some personal voiceover and music, there is no such compensating factor in in Heavenly Bodies, so the focus is all on the gameplay. Still the core gameplay is fantastic and I loved just about every minute of it. I wish there were more of it! Its biggest weakness is its short runtime. Most of the levels are quite small, but take about 30-45 minutes to complete due to the challenge of learning the puzzle and the slow, floaty physics. At 7 levels, it took me about 4 hours to finish the game. Completing the additional challenges adds some replay value but mostly just by cranking up the difficulty. The only levels that really sprawl out are the mining mission and and the final level, but you don't really get a big open world to explore. A DLC of new levels would be most welcome, as the core concept is very fun, and new levels built around challenges like flying with the improvised jetpack, navigating one-handed, completing timed challenges would be a great fit. I can see this game being very fun for speedrunners and I look forward to seeing players try to race through it.

_childDocuments_.review: Heavenly Bodies is a game that defies expectations in the best way possible. At its core, it's a "tricky physics" simulation that's all about the absurdity of zero-gravity physical comedy. Developed by 2pt Interactive, this indie gem offers a unique and sometimes hilarious experience that keeps you on your toes.Navigating zero-gravity environments as a cosmonaut isn't as straightforward as it seems. The game's attention to detail is both endearing and relentless, and it creates moments that swing from beauty to humor to anxiety-inducing uncertainty. You'll have independent control over your character's arms and hands, leading to instances of spinning, contorting, and inadvertently annoying your co-op partner.Heavenly Bodies' gameplay revolves around mastering the physics of movement in space. While the controls may feel finicky at times, they never feel purposely frustrating. Different control modes cater to varying levels of challenge, and once you get the hang of it, the game becomes a joyous exercise in mastering zero-gravity antics.The heart of the game lies in its co-op mode. Playing with a friend introduces an extra layer of hilarity and chaos as you navigate levels together. The game's puzzles are cleverly designed, requiring coordination and communication. The seven distinct scenarios offer memorable challenges, all underscored by the game's meticulous art direction and detailed illustrations.The game's co-op dynamic brings both laughter and shared frustration, making it a perfect fit for the experience. Despite a few control quirks and screen-sharing constraints, Heavenly Bodies' co-op mode shines as its highlight. However, this isn't to say that solo players won't enjoy the game; its intuitive mechanics and puzzle-solving nature are engaging in their own right.Heavenly Bodies proves that even in the vastness of space, you can find a unique and engaging gaming experience. Its quirky physics, attention to detail, and co-op fun make it a standout title that's well worth the journey. While it may be a struggle at times, it's a struggle that's undeniably fun.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s a frustrating game, in the sense that frustration is the game. It’s not about clever, intricate puzzles or breathtaking vistas, and it definitely isn’t about teaching players about realistic space habitation (apparently this particular space station has a diesel generator spewing exhaust into the air system). This game is about spending five minutes to get your stupid legs through a stupid small corridor because the stupid engineers who designed this stupid place assumed astronauts’ legs actually worked in zero G (as said, it’s not quite as realistic as the trailer seems to portray). This game is about spending an inordinate amount of time doing what seems like it should be a simple task and the catharsis that washes over the player when they *finally* succeed. It’s not a game play loop that works for everyone, but I enjoyed it, at least enough to suggest that you share in my frustration. It is a little on the short side, but personally I think it’s a good length for this kind of game, it doesn’t overstay its welcome, and if you are into self-punishment and want even more frustration it does have a number of optional challenges to pad out the runtime.I would also add that I enjoyed it far more in single player mode than multi-player. More risk of hurdling off into the uncaring void, fewer pairs of useless legs clogging up corridors.

_childDocuments_.review: Heavenly Bodies is a delightful and challenging physics-based puzzle game that my friend and I completed, earning all the achievements in 9.9 hours. If you’re looking for a unique cooperative experience with a touch of zero-gravity shenanigans, this game is a stellar choice.An Engaging Zero-Gravity ExperienceThe standout feature of Heavenly Bodies is its fantastic physics engine. Navigating through the game’s various puzzles in a zero-gravity environment was both fun and challenging. The space physics are spot on, providing a very playful experience that kept us very entertained from start to finish.The puzzles themselves aren’t overly complicated, but the real challenge lies in the zero-gravity mechanics. Maneuvering through space, grabbing objects, and solving tasks together required communication... This added a layer of difficulty that made the game both frustrating and incredibly rewarding at the same time.Co-op Fun at its BestPlaying with a friend is where Heavenly Bodies truly shines. The cooperative aspect of the game enhances the experience, making each task a shared adventure. Whether it was navigating tight spaces or figuring out how to operate a piece of space equipment, having a buddy by my side made every moment enjoyable.Short but SweetAt just under 10 hours for a complete run with all achievements, Heavenly Bodies isn’t a long game, but it’s perfectly paced. The developers have done a great job of creating a concise and engaging experience without unnecessary padding.Minor NitpicksWhile the game is fantastic, there are a few minor things I wish it did. A bit more variety in the puzzles and objectives could have added to the replayability. Along with possible additions such as interactions with more items and more missions like the Asteroid map would have been great. All in all the game has a great foundation to expand.Final ThoughtsHeavenly Bodies offers a refreshing and engaging take on puzzle games with its unique space physics and cooperative gameplay. It’s a perfect game to play with a friend, providing plenty of laughs and challenges along the way. If you’re looking for a short but memorable co-op adventure, Heavenly Bodies is well worth your time.TLDR: Heavenly Bodies is a wonderfully challenging physics-based puzzle game best enjoyed with a friend. The space mechanics add a unique twist, making for a fun and rewarding experience. Highly recommended for those looking for a cooperative cosmic adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: While 20 bucks for an experience you can finish a few hours, but I really appreciated this little gem. Getting a grip on the controls can be frustrating (even more so with 2 people when you have to share one visual orientation), but overall I found it a very satisfying physics puzzle game. The controls made me think of OctoDad, but while that game had an overtly comedic tone, the comedy in the game is more sparse and understated. Sometimes I laughed because of something I did to myself (like overlooking the manual and not realizing I needed to ATTACH the loose thrusters to my ship's frame to fly properly. Instead I flew madly through space with thrusters whipping around like angry hoses for half the mission before I realized!), sometimes the game would set you up for a gag directly, like having you have to activate a rock tumbler from inside it. The ending of the game in particular had me cracking up, and I appreciated how the humor was tied directly to the gameplay. So while humor isn't central to the game, I thought it worth mentioning.

_childDocuments_.review: In Heavenly Bodies, you play as an astronaut in (you guessed it!) space. You, and optionally a friend, are thrust into various missions where you have to do astronauty things like adjust solar panels, mine asteroids and repair satellites.What makes this interesting is that you can't control your character directly, but you do have some limited control over their "Heavenly Body".You use each analog stick to move your astronaut's arms around, you use the triggers to grab onto walls or hold onto objects and you can use the bumpers to bend your knees closer to your body.That's it.Remember you're in space, there's no friction. So you if you start gaining momentum in a certain direction, you're going to keep moving in that direction unless you grab onto something. At least that's the case when playing on the Newtonian difficulty, other difficulty levels make things less "realistic" but more accessible.Controlling your astronaut is difficult but as you play, you gradually gain more familiarity with the initially awkward control scheme and eventually it becomes second nature.Each mission requires you to complete increasingly challenging tasks encouraging you to gain mastery over the way you control your astronaut.There's beauty in a game like Heavenly Bodies that gradually reveals itself to you as you become more familiar with it. I really love easy to learn yet hard to master games like this. I liked this one so much that I chose to play it as my first speedrunning gameAlso, the music is very "spacey" and meditative. Sometimes you just let go of whatever you're holding onto and float.Immersing yourself in the atmosphere, or lack of it.

_childDocuments_.review: In Heavenly Bodies, the player becomes an astronaut to accomplish missions and tasks in space. It sounds fairly straightforward until the player experiences the lack of gravity and limiting, intentionally awkward controls. A task as simple as flipping a switch can become an unexpected obstacle. It left me with a keen sense of respect for actual astronauts after playing this physics space game by 2pt Interactive. The controls are fairly simple. Astronauts can move their legs and arms and grab onto items. Some objects players must work with can attach to a loop on the belt of their space suit. Don’t get too excited because one will quickly realize sometimes items themselves can end up causing problems or impede the mission. A tethered item can cause a door to jam or cause an astronaut to be wider than the space necessary for a corridor. The challenge definitely comes with working with all the nuisances that come into play, all while having no gravity to hold the astronaut down.Heavenly Bodies as a single player might be enjoyable, but I definitely recommend the game for playing with another. My partner and I laughed, commiserated, and discussed our way through all the problems and missions the game presented to us. Whoever you choose to play the game with, be sure your gaming partner is up to a bit of teamwork, frustration, and communication because it’s going to be necessary to get through this fun space game.There are several missions and tasks astronauts must complete and each mission has a challenging collectible for the player to hang onto if possible. The game provides enough fun and challenges for replayability options. Players can play in normal mode or another more difficult mode where the controls are much more difficult to master while in space. Also, if the player is stuck on what to do for a mission, there is an instruction manual very reminiscent of looking at an Ikea guide. The aesthetics of the game are beautiful. The music is atmospheric and connects with the themes of space and exploration. I took many screenshots because of how pretty the game is and because of the ridiculous positions I found my partner and I in while trying to solve simple problems during a mission. As you play through the game one might think it’s just 2D graphics, but there are some instances where other objects exist in a layered 3D environment, adding to the challenging gameplay. Heavenly Bodies is an enjoyable challenge with many frustrations and laughter. I found the game easy to come back to because of how much fun it is to play with another person. I definitely suggest this one if you’re looking for a fun cooperative game. It’s available on Steam for PC and also Playstation Store. Thank you Indie Game Collective for allowing me to showcase the game and providing the code! I really enjoyed sharing Heavenly Bodies to our community.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is sweet, and has a lot of soul to it but I can't bring myself to play it anymore.I find the "Newtonian" mode (hard mode) to be too frustrating to play, but I couldn't enjoy the "Classic" mode (normal mode) because I learned a terrible secret.That I could Forced between either knowing I could easily abuse this exploit at anytime (including inside the ship) or having to switch a more frustrating mode I didn't want to choose.The game also suffers from a lack of a proper "push" command, you can pull but you can't push very well with your hands. This makes it unnecessarily difficult and annoying to get around.I stopped playing the game, once I got the rocket ship mission in which the rocket kept floating away from the stuff I was supposed to mine. The ship tries to stay in the same spot but it does a very poor job at it. The mission is obviously intended for 2 players. I ended up quitting the game with the last auto-save being "48 minutes ago", as you can't save the game manually. I haven't gone back since.This game was also solely focused around solving puzzle-like tasks when I would have much preferred to play an open-world (open-space?) ship management game instead, something like Barotrauma in space.Overall, I enjoy the concept. However, I don't like the puzzle focused missions and I didn't have anyone to play it with.If you can get it on sale with a friend, you might have some fun, but if you are on your own I would skip it.Maybe I will return if one of my friend's purchases the game, however that is not likely.I will be keeping an eye on what this studio produces in the future (if anything), as they show a lot of promise.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me say up front that I played this game couch co-op with my girlfriend and had a pretty good time. She found the possibility of drifting off into space too anxiety inducing to continue past level 2 but I think that speaks highly of the game. This review is more about single player using Newtonian physics.I had good memories from the couch co-op session but only recently managed to get back to playing. The game didn't quite hold up sadly. It is very cool, there is a lot of really great stuff in it like the music, sound effects, the physics and the little instruction manual you get for your objectives that is like a physical book that you can page through and zoom in on. Just the whole concept really. But where the game falls down is that the controls are just a bit too clunky. This time, I decided to play with "Newtonian" physics, which I guess are close to the real thing. Meaning if you accidentally send yourself floating away into space (even incredibly slowly) there is basically nothing you can do about it. Also it makes getting around the ship quite difficult because you can't do breast stroke or any of the other tricks I had previously used. After a while I got very frustrated with it and tried "classic" physics which is somewhere between the arcade "assisted" physics and realistic Newtonian. But it felt very fake being able to stop one's momentum instantly so I immediately went back. The main problem I had is that you don't have good enough control of your arms for Newtonian physics to work as a game mode. You can't put your arm straight up or down, it has to go in an arc like when you are making a snow angel, and while you are doing that, it always catches on stuff and blocks you or sends you spiraling off in the wrong direction.Also, there is a strong preference for grabbing items instead of handrails or supports. At one point I was trying to get into a room and four times in a row I grabbed a loose crowbar instead of the wall and went sailing off past my destination. It was infuriating. It's annoying because the game is so close to being amazing, but they just didn't quite stick the landing. There are also weird bugs, like the checkpoints are sometimes way off from the latest task you did, or it might remember the last task you did but the map will reset to a much earlier state without all of the intervening tasks completed. Like at one point I flew away from the antenna tower that you have to construct on the last step. When I loaded a check point all but one of the antennas had been activated, but I had to rebuild the tower that they are on. Also reloading checkpoints resets the map, so if you have opened boxes or moved things, the state of the space station will not be as it was when the checkpoint was saved. Some of these bugs feel so basic that this far from launch, it feels like the game was just never finished.

_childDocuments_.review: A neat little puzzle game about managing (more or less realistic) astronaut duties in zero gravity.You control your character’s limbs and have to pull yourself around, grab objects, attach stuff to your suit and interact with levers, buttons, sliding doors and more. Given this, the game’s difficulty comes mostly from its literally floaty controls. The game is divided into levels, each with a new space station location and unique tasks for you to complete, keeping the experience fresh and even telling a basic story.Heavenly Bodies also challenges you with finding collectibles, fulfilling additional tasks for each level and completing the levels with realistic physics, meaning less room for messing up. Everything can also be experienced in co-op mode, making for even more fun, as up to 4 players stumble around and get in each other’s way. Having only experienced two player co-op, I’d consider that to make for the optimal experience, with four players probably getting in each other’s way too much and being limited by the missions’ design not providing enough to do for everyone at once. That said, I see a lot of potential fun arising from the chaos of trying to coordinate four people stumbling around space.Graphically, the game looks beautiful, which, alongside the great ambient sound, gives it a unique feel and makes the game surprisingly immersive. The levels are certainly challenging, but manage to not become frustrating either, although I’d recommend taking a pause every couple of levels to relax.There’s a DLC available for Heavenly Bodies, which essentially gives you another 7 missions to complete, this time around with the added twist of all of them taking place on the same map, which expands as you progress through the missions. While this is obviously a bit more boring, with you having to move through the same space station over and over again, the DLC does a good thing of shaking things up and overall presents a unique spin on the game’s formula, which I quite enjoyed.That being said, I felt the big map presented throughout the missions to not be ideal for co-op play, as players trying to work on different tasks will quickly leave the shared screen’s boundaries, making for a suboptimal playing experience. Unlike in the main game, there are no additional challenges for the new missions; however, there are once again some collectibles to find around the map, giving you a bit more to do.All in all, I very much enjoyed Heavenly Bodies and definitely recommend buying it, especially if you have someone else to play it with.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, so this is one of those "frustrating but fun" type of games. Many games of this type will lean too far into the "frustrating" category ("Look at how silly the [whatever] is when you use the clunky controls!"), but this one strikes a very fair balance between being challenging and yet achievable with minimal toasters chucked through monitors/screens/steam decks being thrown out the window. (Yes, it is running fantastic on my Steam Deck... though it's a little easier to play when I use the dock on the big monitor & use a controller.)So what's the idea? You're an astronaut in space, doing astronaut stuff. You know, repairing things, installing things, working machines, opening airlocks, blah blah blah. The challenge here is that you only have control of his two arms. I mean, yeah, you can have him tuck his legs, but I haven't really found this very useful except in a few circumstances - so mostly, I'm just controlling his arms. Left stick controls left arm.. right stick controls right. Left trigger controls left grip.. and right, right. Pretty basic. Oh, but it's all in zero-G, so, hang onto something.The POINT of the game is INTENTIONALLY to be a bit clunky, so naturally sometimes it's a little testy to get the guy to do what you want him to do - but at the end of the day, it still feels more or less "right," so it's not so clunky as to be a huge bummer during gameplay. There are a few things that irritate me sometimes... (Such as when I'm strapping a billion things to myself, but can NEVER get my hand to grab the RIGHT tool! Someday, the game KNOWS what I'm reaching for and won't let me grab it! Or, sometimes my arm might get "stuck" behind a tool, and then in the process of getting my arm unstuck, I fling myself to the other end of the room, and have to get back. ugh.) But these things are not irritating enough to discourage me from continuing play.For the price, it's got a fair amount of content... 7 missions, each of which take a decent amount of time, since it takes a decent amount of doing even to do simple things. As far as the "should I pay full price?" question, I think that one's up in the air. I bought it on sale, but I think I would have been ok paying full price. Some people, though, if this isn't something they're super excited about, I think should wait for a sale - because if you're not just dying to play, it might not be worth full price to you in the long run. There is an $8 DLC which adds 7 more missions which seem to be just as much, if not more content... so for $28, you can have pretty much double the base game. Worth it? Again, I think it's going to be a toss-up. This is one of those games that I think for some (like me), it's going to click, and for some it won't be great.It's not action-packed, but stays at a decent pace. You do occasionally have some uh-oh moments (whoops, forgot to cycle airlocks properly) but is otherwise quite slow-paced and methodical.. just as you'd expect in.. you know... space.There was one part that had me dying, and that's when you make it back down to Earth. This isn't a spoiler, I don't think, so I'm not going to hide it. You splash down and find that your legs are still more or less useless. Extracting yourself from your capsule, in 1 G, with the bare minimum of leg use is.. hilarious. I don't know if the developers were trying to be funny. I found it funny. (I also think King of the Hill is funny, so I guess I don't have high standards.)I really do enjoy the graphics and the sounds - despite looking a little cartoonish, it's easy to get lost in the play and feel like it's real-ish. I also like how much creativity is allowed. When I began getting more tools and straps and stuff, I started wondering how the game was going to limit me.. maybe, "only one thing can hook to one thing," etc - but quickly found out that the only limit is the amount of space you have available. I have made some rather ridiculous-looking tether/tool/etc arrangements, tugging things behind me like a train as I go from spot to spot.Overall, I'm very pleased. It's a fun little game. It hasn't given me a new purpose in life, but neither did the pizza I ate the other day, and I'm still glad I ate it. That's this game - a nice, deli-refrigerated pizza with stuffed crust. It won't change your life, and it's probably not on par with a Pizza Hut pizza, but if you're like me you won't be sad you ate.. uh, played... it.Yes, I recommend :-)

_childDocuments_.review: The good- Gorgeous cartoonish visuals with nice colors, atmospheric lighting conditions and many neat details.- Fantastically designed space station with a lot of different places to visit and various machinery to deal with.- Unique concept and gameplay mechanics. The way you separately control arms and legs trying to coordinate their movement is very clever. The way you try to deal with lack of gravity is very challenging and sometimes it looks like swimming. You feel on your fingertips the tense and struggle of movement under these conditions. There is a constant danger of making a mistake and get lost in space. If only controls where more precise it would annoy you less at times.- Great physics and collisions system that feels consistent, realistic and responsive. It's so pleasant to watch your character bouncing here and there, wires and objects floating and hitting the walls of the station.- Awesome atmosphere. You'll feel the loneliness of being in a space station, stranded and far from earth. It has something unique.- Cool music that enhances the eerie atmosphere.- The missions aren't too deep or complex, but they are well designed and have fun.- There are many extra things to discover and some small challenges that enlarge a little bit the actual playtime.- Co-oping with friends is so entertaining. You'll face some frustrating but really funny situations when trying to synchronize and coordinate your movements. It can get very challenging.- Well designed operations manual with nice sketches that look like blueprints and provide all the necessary information in great detail .- When (and if) you get used of the controls it can be a relaxing and hilarious experience.The bad- There are a lot of clunky moments and some of your character's poses are weird. Some times controls feel awkward or imprecise and a lot of experimentation is needed in order to achieve some actions. It can get very annoying when trying to perform small, accurate movements. Especially at the beginning it needs a lot of patience until you get used of the controls. If you're not a patient guy better leave it.- Legs movement isn't as important as arms. In fact you can easily finish the game without using legs at all. It would give the player more options and freedom if legs' movement really mattered.- There is no main story at all. You just follow orders mechanically and do maintenance jobs without a specific goal. The main character doesn't have a background and feels generic. A small plot could make it more interesting.- Missions are well designed, but there isn't an actual puzzle that requires creative thinking. They just require exploration and movement coordination while just following manual's instructions.- There is no online co-op mode, just local. Steam remote play supports four players co-op, but is problematic with much delay.- Although the goal and the tools of each mission change, the actual gameplay doesn't really evolves so after a while it may get a little bit monotonous.- Some more missions and bigger duration would be nice.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a wonderfully chill but challenging game. The missions are about 40 minutes in length each. Each one has well defined goals that give you manageable chunks that are individually challenging and satisfying, but add up to something rather considerable. Each mission builds off of the previous, adding new tools and mechanics and scaling up the size and difficulty.I originally watched CallMeKevin play this and he made it look like uncontrollable mayhem. I don't know if that's just the YouTube gimmick, but it's not nearly as bad as he made it out to be. Sure, it's difficult to control yourself and sometimes things can be get out of control, but a bit of planning and patience makes it much easier than it first seems. There's no time limit, so take your time, stay in control, and just work through things one step at a time.I'm just over two hours in and so far I'm loving this. Normally I play games long enough to get the hang of them and then move on, but even now that I feel I'm proficient at this game, I still want to keep playing. The missions still feel fresh and I really enjoy the slow and methodical pace of the game combined with the tension of knowing that one wrong move could really mess things up.All in all, I'm really happy with this game. I only wish I had found it sooner!

Flinging your character through space. Just grabbing the corner of the structure and whipping into it instead of drifting out of signal range. Constantly daring the empty void with truly unreasonable acrobatics.I love it so. I've planted a flag on an asteroid. Pried open a broken airlock with a tennis racket. _childDocuments_.review: So far I'm loving this game. I've heard from other reviews that the game is short but I do think it's worth the money since it really is an experience.I do have some suggestions though:-Endless mode: This would help add more replayability to the game. You are located on a space ship that's slowly falling apart and have to fix parts as they break. This spaceship could incorporate gameplay elements from all of the levels. For additional spice, the ship could be on a course and players would have to check a radar and control the ship to stop it from crashing or even getting some valuable resources. I might iterate on this idea once ive completed the game.-Split screen: I've seen some people complain about this and I just think it would be a great customization option to tailor to people's preferences as well as eliminating the problem of things getting too small when players are apart.-Toggle grab overhaul: The current toggle grab is difficult to use. An option to keep grabbing after letting the button go only if a player has held the grab button down for a few seconds would help to make a middle ground between the 2 play styles.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I almost refunded this game. I had seen clips and videos of it, thought "that looks like fun!", so decided to pick it up. I went 'Newtonian' straight off the bat, discovered that mode was the opposite of fun, and whinged to my friends a lot.Returned to the game and went with 'Assisted' mode, and had a much better time. After completing the game fairly quickly with the assisted controls, I turned my eye towards doing the challenges and achievements. One of the challenges is completing every level in Newtonian mode. I was afraid, the fear had returned.However, getting to grips with the feel and physics of the game in assisted mode had me better prepared than I initially thought I would be. Don't get me wrong, the game is much harder without assisted controls; lots of planning and thought is required (tow ropes are your friend), and if you mess up and go flying out into the darkness of space then that's on you, buddy. Even more frustrating is missing your target and just being stuck in the middle of a space station, flopping around like a fish out of water.Having just now gained the final achievement in the game, I can safely say that Heavenly Bodies is great fun. It's about as close to going to space as I'll ever get.

_childDocuments_.review: I mean, man, it's a silly space game where you can ♥♥♥♥ with your friends and annoy them, or try to speedrun levels on the newtonian movement style, only to have one of you "CODE RED!!" and begin floating away from the station.     It's a wonderful game, it's short, however. It is so much fun to replay with different friends, different difficulties, etc. 100% worth the $20 if you enjoy space and a bit of a funny challenge. If you're good at the game, it's beatable in probably 4-6 hours on your first playthrough (obviously depending on how much you mess around). Other factors that attribute to the game's replayability are the challenges you get after completing missions, collecting each collectible, and relatively "easy" trophy hunting.     The game is playable through Steam's Remote Play, meaning only one of you has to own the game to play together, there is no "matchmaking" in-game.     10/10 would recommend this game to someone looking for a fun co-op game!

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. Playing it with keyboard and set to Newtonian, at first I was like a drunken space-fish thrashing QWOP-style in space with no skill at controlling my limp noodle body to achieve any mission goals. But the struggle continues long enough, and the technique starts to shine through. Movement in this game is a dream, once you get the knack for it. Given that my favorite part of Kerbal Space Program is orbital docking, this game is a cornucopia of slowly-drifting-together maneuvering and ecstatic union. I confess I haven't played the whole thing yet, but loving each mission so far - they are quite well conceived and I can't wait to rope some poor sod into cooping it with me! UPDATE: The last mission is a bit of a letdown since it's just a boring obstacle course. I love the ones where you're interacting with complex machines or especially the space capsule one! Since a fool can dream: imagine this game's mechanics expanded to a online multiplayer (say 4 players total) environment in the style of a simplified Barotrauma or even Space Station 13. Semi-randomized sandbox space environment, where you and your buddies face off against unpredictable crises and malfunctions. At any rate, even with 7 missions this game is pure class. More please!

_childDocuments_.review: I'd sum this one up as frustrating fun. Considering the very unique controls that can make you feel so powerless, it makes completing a level extremely satisfying. The game looks incredible, and the level design is so clever and allows you to solve things any way you want to. All of the little details and game physics adds that extra level of polish. I really wanted more in the main story outside of going back and doing the extra objectives. Haven't had a chance to try the co-op mode, but I'm sure that could be double the frustrating fun. I can't knock much off on this game because it executes on what it sets out to be so well. Can't wait to loop back and give this one some more attention. Wont take more than 5 hours to beat but is a fun ride along the way. 9.3/10
_childDocuments_.name: Heavenly Bodies

_childDocuments_.review: Do you remember QWOP?Did you ever want that with objectives and co-op in a space station setting?Well, you've found your game. This is your stop, get off the train and enjoy the sights and attractions.This is a silly game. Relatively short but full of equally frustrating and hilarious missions. The mechanics are simple and the objectives are straightforward, the "manual" you get every mission is like Ikea crashed into K'NEX set instructions. It's a very endearing game and it's pretty fun to play. It takes a lot of time to grow accustomed to the controls, but the missions slowly ease you into the myriad of challenges that those mechanics present. The missions get progressively more difficult to navigate, the objectives grow more annoying and finicky to complete. For better or for worse, what you see in the game trailer is essentially 80% of the game.It might be remote play/local co-op only, but the experience for me and another friend was buttery smooth. Nary a bug in sight during my playthrough.This is a ~4 hour experience for a single playthrough, maybe more if you try to speedrun or achievement hunt it.
_childDocuments_.name: Heavenly Bodies

It's probably more fun to play with your friends but it's still pretty fun playing on your own. Overall enjoyable experience 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Heavenly Bodies

_childDocuments_.name: Heavenly Bodies

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game; great simplistic graphics, the physics create a simultaneous sense of peril, challenge and achievement, nice level design that introduces you to the game mechanics without 'mothering' you and enforces the need to plan out your movements right out of the gate.A really enjoyable game (thanks to Buggs and ZH for bringing it to my attention!) and I hope that one day we see more content for this game as I truly enjoyed playing through this !(PS - I've not tried Newtonian physics yet but I have played assisted while drunk and I'm not sure which would be a more challenging playthrough - nevertheless hilarious)
_childDocuments_.name: Heavenly Bodies

_childDocuments_.review: Accidentally untethered from my companion and was hurled into space... kept my composure and assessed the situation... out of options... at 99% signal loss, tossed one end of the tether back towards the ship... momentum reversed... long slow fall, spinning back to safety... finally within reach my partner pulled me back inside. But the job's not done. Rock-paper-scissors to decide who goes back outside to try again...
_childDocuments_.name: Heavenly Bodies

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing with my brother for a bit more than 3 hours with gamepads. The game is very neat and can be pretty similar to Human Fall Flat in term of gameplay.You can play with 3 different types of controls, an easy, medium and newtonian mode.Since we only played newtonian mode for realism I can't tell how hard the rest is.The ambient music is immersive and chill, everything you achieve in this game is satisfying because of how hard it is !There are many optional challenges but the game is pretty short : we are at final level (without every challenges) after these 3 hours.The game is very good and fun to play with a friend, I can only recommend it because to me the only bad thing is that you want more in the end. :)Can't wait for a sequel !

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, so this is most definitely a game that's better to play with friends.  I played with one over Steam's remote play, and it was quite fun. This is NOT a game for those who get frustrated easily, in my opinion.  There are moments where you want your character to do something, and it resists, and that can be enraging.  With my friend, this happened frequently enough that they had to stop playing multiple times.I found the game enjoyable enough to complete all of the achievements for it, which was frustrating for me.  However, a large portion of those looking at this game are likely not going to be doing that, so it's no big deal.All in all, I enjoyed the game!  Again, highly recommend playing with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: -I played the first three levels in local co-op mode with a friendPros: Fiddly, fumbly shenanigans in space. It's fun to grab things and pull them around, especially your friend. Graphics look nice. When you get skilled at movement it feels triumphant.Cons: It feels frustrating 80% of the time specifically in co-op because there is no option to make arm controls relative to your body, as opposed to relative to the screen. This causes a constant situation where Player 1 has screen re-orientation control and Player 2 just has to control upside down. The physics can also be frustrating in unintended ways (objects getting in the way, nothing ever passes through other things, this causes situations where you can get stuck. Could be funny, could be frustrating). Also, the objectives in the levels are just ambiguous enough that you and your friend will likely know the solution to puzzles, yet be unable to progress in the specific way the game requires. The levels are also far too long, and when you finish you will likely be done playing, not begging for more. By the Level 2 the game already asks new players to do perilous and complicated tasks that will likely take over an hour to complete.Overall: It's a decent game but better control options and shorter and/or simpler levels with less ambiguous objectives would help the good times roll in multiplayer.

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah it's basically QWOP in space.I completed the game entirely in co-op with my girlfriend. Compared to other games of this genre I felt the controls in this game were kinda hard to get used to and never felt completely right even after 100% completing the game, They just felt wrong whenever your character is upside-down.Thankfully you can automatically rotate the camera with the press of a button but it would've been nice if you could rotate it manually in either direction to suit both players.Maybe I just couldn't get used to it, but it felt like the controls just wouldn't work properly relative to the camera like you'd expect, though it's not really an issue on the easiest control scheme (assisted) as you can basically fly around with that setting just by pointing in the direction you want to go to.There's 7 chapters in total, each chapter offers a different kind of gameplay experience in some way, except for the last one - which was kinda disappointingly easy and straightforward. In some way it was a refreshing change of pace, but it left us wanting more. I can't praise the other chapters enough though, there's some really awesome and fun gameplay mechanics that surprised me.The game is short (probably around 2-5 hours for completion, but there is a few extra challenges, collectibles and achievement hunting), maybe not the best bang for your buck but I think the experience was absolutely worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is something I've been waiting for a long time. I love tinkering with mechanisms, I love systems that interact and have purpose. This game completes Kerbal Space Program - I wish they would collaborate ;dI love the Classic mode - it really provides perfect ballance between experiencing 0-G and keeping the character controllable.I love how simple tasks suddenly become complicated (like opening a crate with a crowbar - on Earth easy, in space not that trivial).And they managed to put a little story in the missions that keeps them connected. _childDocuments_.review:
Heavenly Bodies is a game about cosmonauts, the body, and the absence of gravity.

Discover the ever-changing nuances of weightless motion in this challenging physics game. Wrangle control of your cosmonaut's arms with the left and right thumbsticks to push, pull, and clamber through fully physically simulated scenarios aboard a scientific research station.

You have been entrusted to bring into operation Earth's proudest feat of engineering. With only radio contact with mission control as your aid, you will have to use your sharp mind and dexterous limbs to assemble space telescopes, maintain delicate solar arrays and research cosmic botany. But without gravity, nothing is still, nothing is secure, and nothing is simple.

Heavenly Bodies has a highly unique movement system designed to use a dual-analog joystick controller. Rebindable keyboard and mouse controls are technically supported, but they do not provide the intended experience.

name: The Big Con
detailed_description: Let's Get Rad About the Game Hustle and grift your way across America in the ‘90s as a teenage con artist on a crime-filled road trip adventure. Play as Ali, a curious and sarcastic high schooler who ditches band camp to go on a cross-country road trip. But this isn’t a joyride! Ali is on an all-important mission to save her family video store from the nasty loan sharks trying to shut their shop down. Swindle strangers, pickpocket people, and con commoners across a wacky America of the ‘90s. And – it should go without saying – lie to your mom about all of it. Choose who deserves to be conned and who might need a helping hand. The world is your oyster (and hey, pearls are worth a lot!). One Con Doesn’t Fool All Con people your way! Wear disguises, sneak around, eavesdrop on conversations, and learn how to approach each mark. Maybe you think you can make enough cheddar just by pickpocketing. Or seek out more complex grifts that involve breaking and entering, smooth talking, and more. It’s up to you to outsmart everyone and lockpick everything that stands between you and saving your mom's video store. A Coming-of-Age Comedy If there’s one surefire way to discover yourself, it’s by setting out on an adventure. Luckily for you, you’ve got the aid of an expert grifter to coach you in the elusive art of charm. But a life of crime is no laughing matter! Not unless you turn on the laugh track and make it a criminally funny sitcom. Get ready to talk your way into deals, hearts, and trouble. And don’t forget to call home every once in a while to check in with your mom. Sure, you might argue with her sometimes (most of the time?), but you’re a teenager - that’s kind of your job! The Weird and Wack 1990s the Way You Remember Them Whether you were a ‘90s kid or not, this game is brimming with nostalgia. It offers you the perfect opportunity to relive your own awkward high school years, or if you sadly missed out on the ‘90s, finally experience all of the classic teen movies that feel so old and outdated. Plaid, payphones, VHS tapes, and malls – THE BIG CON has got all of the outrageous fads you remember (and some you want to forget) from the 1990s. But most importantly – you can ride the Hormipillar as much as you want!

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a lot going for it, it's designed with optional content in mind, the locations are fun to explore, the aesthetic is very captivating, the soundtrack constantly changes to match the environment, and it has funny characters that create a grounded, but enjoyable narrative. I think the story had a good pace to it, if you take into consideration all of the things that can grab your attention, they managed to keep it together very well. You can casually complete the game around 5 to 7 hours, there are many optional achievements and cosmetic trinkets, although it would be nice to have the ability to replay specific chapters. Having played the game only once, I am not sure how much impact the narrative choices actually have, the only thing I can confirm is that certain quests have more than one soluton. It's not a difficult game in terms of puzzles and mechanics, there is usually a place to get hints, and sometimes the game offers you a way to skip a puzzle with a payment. As for the 'thief' gameplay, there is not much to it, it's just a simple timing event with little to no punishment for the failure - I guess it does not make for a deep con game, if you were expecting that. To advance between stages you need to collect a small amout of money with con activities, it's generally a much lower number than what you can get by fully exploring the stage, so be careful not to advance too early - the game does not give you a good warning when you are about to move on (not on every stage anyway). I thought the side quests were pretty good, I already mentioned that some of them have different solutions, but I also like how the dialogue was designed with multiple choices, it helps if you pay attention. I don't feel very strongly about the main story, if anything I think it was just decent, but some of the random characters like the PawnShop owner added a lot of flavor to the narrative, it has many good moments. To be fair, I think the dialogue was enjoyable, and the game is very playful with the responses, it has that sense of self-awareness which I really like. The ending had a good sense of closure, even though I expected something more unique. There are a few small polish issues like the foreground obstructions and poorly placed boundaries, they are not too common, but it happens often enough and I thought I should mention it. I also noticed that those ear dropping areas can be unresponsive, like I will stand and spam the button and nothing happens for like 30 seconds. Aside from that, I don't have much critique for the actual game and how the story was implemented. (+) There are a few aesthetic elements that I want to elaborate on. I really like how you manipulated the music to match different stores, like you will have the same song remixed to complement the theme of the location, in general the soundtrack was very good. Obviously the game is very pretty, nice colors, lots of detail, fun to explore. Furthermore, it has a nice UI design, not just some random panels, it actually looks clean and easy to understand. (+) I think the game is very much designed with optional content and rewarding curiosity, and for me that was the highlight of the game, doing what I wanted to do, and finding things because I looked for them. If you were stuck for whatever reason, there are hints and ways to skip some time-consuming puzzles. You can also get cosmetics and hidden trinkets. (+) I don't think the story by itself was anything special, but with all of the fun dialogue that surrounds it, I had a good time. I love the corn guy, he carried the game by himself. There were many funny moments, if you look for them.  - there is a problem with foreground and not having proper invisible walls. It's mostly cosmetic, but you know, it should still be fixed. Those areas with ear signs can be a bit junky, sometimes it's hard to trigger them. Not sure if you intended for the player to instantly do the 20.000 contest, it uses money you already earned too, so I don't see the point. - for the level 1 and 2, you should add an obvious YES/NO before you advance the stage. It would be nice to have waypoints to chapters once you beat the game (I am not 100% sure if you don't have them, if you do I could not figure out how to use them). How come you don't get to keep cosmetics? You could put them in a different panel in the inventory so you can always use whatever you like.I really feel sorry for the devs, I think the game is much better than their ability to advertise. If you just like optional achievements and looking for secret interactions, it's a really good game in terms of exploration. Aside from just having cool art style and dynamic soundtrack, I also think the dialogue was very fun. In general, I think it felt different from most narrative games because of the angle on the exploration. With a few small technical nitpicks, I had a good time from start to finish.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy.Let's start off with the positives:1. The art style is amazing. Makes me wish the 90s even though I wasn't alive for it.2. Music is pretty good, too. Not great but decent enough.3. Ali is an interesting character, same goes for Ted. The Bad:1. There is only one mini-game throughout the entire game. Just one QTE for stealing and that is it. For a game about being a confidence man, I was surprised there weren't more mini-games. 2. Puzzles are rather simplistic, with very minimal thought being required to solve them.3. Entire game is basically a glorified fetch quest. More often then not you simply talk to the person/eavesdrop, then either give them what they need or go steal whatever it is they just revealed. The Meh:1. This game could benefit from a map. Not too big an issue but still, would be nice. Especially for Las Vegas2. Game is kinda glitchy. I was able to make a rather large amount of money in the mall by simply talking to an NPC over and over. One quest ended up not working so I was unable to do that part of the game.In Conclusion:Really eh, the same pickpocketing mini-game gets pretty boring (and it's not really that hard in the first place.) The game is almost entirely carried by its art style. I like the idea of this game, but the lack of properly fleshed out gameplay really ends up making this game feel like a 2.5D walking-sim. Also the fact that the game is 3.5 hours long for a $15 is almost criminal (which I guess is fitting).Not terrible but also not really good or even that engaging or funny.Pick it up for $5 one day.

Nah not worth it.Great time for $5, get it on sale for sure. A-

_childDocuments_.review: when i first played this game, i am reminded of my favourite tv series:  but in a 90's setting with much smaller cons to pull off with a predictable ending. that does not mean it's a mediocre game which has no creativity, no, it actually makes you feel satisfied jotting down those ka-chings until you reach your goal (or go over it!) (:pros (being a pro con artist is one XD):- one thing i love about this game is that the developers are still active in steam discussions (: even though they take awhile to reply to questions, they are active and the guide they made is easy to follow!- the colour scheme is splendid! it gives off a major throwback into the 90's with vibrant colours. the colour palettes also do hold significant meanings such as the faces of each character you come across. for example, green represents 'evil' characters (not all but most).- the gameplay is bemusing with lots of side quests that are mostly eavesdropping on others to find out codes for their bags and multiple hunts for valuable items to trade of for cash (obviously). what i find the most fun throughout my playthroughs is the casino poker side quest :p- the 'tips' ted gives you do apply in real life; especially with 'changebreaking'... it's apparent the developers did their research well (;- having a companion who constantly motivates you (albeit doing something morally wrong :p) is comforting. being in a situation as a teenager who travels across the country to earn $97,000 to ensure the safety of you and your mother can be really tough... if i was in that situation i would've broken down in an instant. but having Rad Ghost to lift up my spirits made me feel like i wasn't alone and i could save the store!- RAD GHOST. enough said. he is my spirit (literally)... animal (blanket???). neutral:- when you've already been caught 3 times, you might not be able to complete certain achievements in one playthrough. for example, failing murray's conversation will lead you to not be able to interact with him further. as such, you will miss the achievement related to him and another playthrough is required to obtain it.- some 'timed' interactions are vital to move onto the next scene but you might not always need to trigger it. for example, the code for the lead car required you to eavesdrop a guy at a certain time. i had not figured it out in my first playthrough so i needed to watch a walkthrough on YouTube to find the code. the story still progressed smoothly but it bugged me why i did not have any hints for the code.cons (no, the cons are not one):- sometimes when you're eavesdropping, the dialogue for that person suddenly disappears. in my opinion, i am guessing that it's because i'm clicking too fast. can be solved by just simply pressing the 'X' button (i'm using an xbox controller) for the conversation to begin.- ali's walking pace might make the player disinterested to continue playing. would love for her to be able to walk slightly faster sometimes since it's kind of tricky to catch up with certain characters to eavesdrop :pto conclude, my 10.5 hours on the big con is worth every second. i enjoyed every interaction from pick-pocketing strangers to confronting ali's feelings... the compass of morality does spin wildly in this story. this game isn't a stockholm syndrome romance nor is it mr krab's insatiably love for money; it's a story of how much you are willing to sacrifice your morality for the sake of your family (':
