_childDocuments_.review: Thank you guys! I really enjoyed my time with your game.This game was fantastic! You really captured the pure radness of the 90s!The Writing & Story: Hella Phat!The Art: Da Bomb!The Music: All that and a bag of chips! (I can't get the theme song out of my head)Alright, seriously though, now that I got all those 90s phrases out of my system, you guys did a great job here. I had a wonderful time. I would love to see some more of Ali in the future. I especially loved how you had Ali and Linda's shop be a video rental store. This gives a certain ominousness to their future considering what we now know happened to video rental stores in about 10 years. I'd love to know what happens to them in the late 90s and early 00s.I also loved how you referenced the difficultly of running a Mom & Pop shop and how easy it is to lose to the larger-moneyed interests in your industry. [spoilers]When I saw how Bean Spirit took over Two Scoops when I returned, it broke my heart. [/spoilers] I currently run a tiny little restaurant and we have to fight every minute to differentiate ourselves from all the giant chain stores around us. I really felt this on a personal level. Thank you for mentioning this.The only negative criticism I can give is that I did run into a few bugs on my play through. The bugs mostly seemed related to events not triggering that should trigger: The mall cop not opening her door after I gave her popcorn forcing me to get the PIN # from the internet, the Horm guy not disappearing after I won his contest (letting me win it infinitely), Sneaky Dee's part of the sneaker quest disappearing from the game after loading. Normally something like this wouldn't be a issue, but your save system exacerbates the problem by not letting me have multiple backup saves just in case. I'd strongly recommend you avoid doing this kind of stuff in future games. It's just too easy for a single small bug to ruin an entire game.Also, and this isn't really criticism, but I wouldn't have minded if the game had at least one or two more levels. Especially in between your two visits to Las Vengaza. I felt like the story would have played a bit better if this section was expanded somewhat... but I do understand that budgetary concerns mean that games can't be infinitely long and you have to spend your money on the things you can accomplish. So, not so much a criticism so much as a desire to have spent more time in you world!Aside from that, to anyone out there wondering if this game is worth your time... I'd wholeheartedly say yes!

_childDocuments_.review: I gotta say, I rather enjoyed my time with this game. It's a simple point and click about a young girl learning how to pickpocket and swindle various people, though there is a good reason for the lead character deciding to become a runaway con artist. I won't exactly spoil it here.While the story itself is a bit cliche, which I believe was the point since this entire game is embracing 90's cliches to the fullest extent, it was still enjoyable. There were moments where I actually did laugh and had a smile on my face.The "twist" in the story is also a cliche, which again seems to be expected, but cliches can be good if you use them properly. I feel like this game does use every single one it uses well.The only negative things I will say (though I will still recommend the game) is: Firstly, that it's a little short, with me being able to beat it in under 6 hours (with some of this leaving the game on, idle, while I went AFK). Some people would deem this too short to justify a 14.99 price tag, but I'm not one of those people.Secondly, The pick pocketing mechanic is far too easy. Even though there is an option to automatically disable it, it's kind of pointless. Even the "harder" to time targets were still fairly easy. They only time I had any issues was with a walking target and even then, I barely failed.Thirdly, there are technical issues such as Ali (the player character) not properly going behind buildings that are meant to be in the foreground and if you catch an NPC walking to the edge of the map, some will not stop at the obvious barrier and walk out into the void, then off screen. This is more of a nitpick though as it doesn't prevent any progression.Finally, I would say the lack of waypoints or the ability to go back to a previous level at all works a bit negatively in this game's favor. If you don't do everything before moving on, there is no way to go back without making a new game and starting all over (that I'm aware of). This is what I found out when I became annoyed with a couple of fetch quests and decided to move on. There were some instances that it was not clear on what or where to get something (at one point I randomly found an item behind a video shelf at a Videoville in Mallton but there was literally no indicator anything was back there other than suddenly a pop up for the Use icon when I walked behind it since I was wandering aimlessly).Yes, I'm aware I have listed negative aspects in a positive review. I still recommend the game and very much love it, but everything has its flaw. Remember, there's no such thing as perfection.I really look forward to what Mighty Yell has in its pipeline, whether it be a sequel with the homegirl Ali Barlow or an entirely new game.

_childDocuments_.review: The Big Con is a game with a strong presentation, an okay story, middling gameplay, and some egregious technical issues. It comes off as just above average to me.First, let's talk about what I liked about The Big Con. The Big Con is very striking in its presentation. The aesthetic of The Big Con is a massive throwback to the 90's, with things that like that retro color scheme, that background with all the squiggles, and the fact that the scene transition is the S symbol. Mighty Yell worked hard to make an aesthetic this ridiculously 90's and it shows.The story is alright. Ali comes to find out that her mother's video store is being foreclosed upon by a sleazy businessman, and, after meeting another sleazy fella, decides to hitchhike across the country lifting wallets until she gets to score big. The story is reminiscent of a kid's or teen's movie from the 90's, kind of like one of those Disney Channel Original Movies, and I think that's the vibe Mighty Yell was going for making this game. The story isn't going to blow your mind, but that's not what this game was aiming for to begin with.The Big Con is not without its flaws, some minor, some major. Obviously, since the story is a simple one, story lovers may not get their fill from this game. The Big Con is probably most defined as a adventure game, mostly just walking around and quick time events, so gameplay lovers aren't going to be mindblown by this game. These issues were both pretty negligible for me, as I was deeply immersed by the aesthetic. What really drove me insane were the technical issues. Most were small - like a character walking in a fountain, a character with a speech bubble that's offscreen, being able to pickpicket someone on a balcony while Ali's on the street, or Ali clipping through the foreground. The major bug I encountered was being unable to move to the next level, instead teleporting to an area out of bounds. Since I couldn't progress, I had to restart and speed through the game, despite having made it to final level. The Big Con really tested my patience at times. For some reason though, I still came out liking The Big Con; it just isn't entering my favorites game list any time soon.TLDR: The Big Con fought hard to make me both like and dislike the game at times. If you're interested in a casual playthrough of what is a very immensely charming short game, you should give The Big Con a play. If you're someone who wants a complex story, meaty gameplay, or something that won't infuriate you as you try to 100 percent it, this is not going to be the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Hustle through the 90s in THE BIG CON, an adventure game where you're an awkward teen hustling to save her family video store from gangsters. Play as Ali, a high school junior gone AWOL from band camp to seek revenge on the loan sharks that threaten her mom's video store. (Fighting with your mom is YOUR job. No one else gets to do that.) Maybe you'll profit from the latest collectible plushie craze, and make an interesting friend or two along the way.

name: The Dark Eye : Book of Heroes
detailed_description: Based on THE DARK EYE license, Book of Heroes puts you right into the fantasy world of Aventuria where you can raid dungeons and experience adventures, together with friends or alone, that you can only overcome with combined skills and forces. • Play with up to 4 players where you combine the specialties of the different species and professions to overcome enemies, puzzles and challenges in the myriad of procedurally generated maps. • Choose from 12 different professions such as Assassin, Mercenary, Blessed one of Rondra, Knight or Black Magician and one of the four playable species: elves, half-elves, dwarves and humans and individualize the appearance of your character as you see fit. • Enjoy extensive character development opportunities and item crafting in addition to common, improved and legendary items lootable throughout the game. • Play with friends or alone in single-player mode with eight individual storylines. Hire a few companions at the Inn of the Black Boar for your adventures. • Based on the popular THE DARK EYE (TDE) License and rules (5th Edition), the game is developed in close cooperation with the rights owner Ulisses Spiele. TDE is a role-playing system plunging groups of players into the fantasy world Aventuria. TDE has a long tradition, with the first Edition appearing in 1984.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a little shocked by how primitive this game is. You can't control your companions so basically you just walk around the map, into combat and hope for the best. Not sure if I'm just too early in the game but there is literally nothing to do but watch as everyone poke whatever they please. No formation, no targeting, nothing. There is also no difficulty settings which I guess is irrelevant when the encounters are this pointless. So far there is no story other than completing mission objectives. There are games a hundred times more developed at this price point. Am I asking for too much?? Think I'm too late for a refund and I might be desperate enough to keep playing. _childDocuments_.review: This game would have been... "okayish" back in 2010. We're in 2020 and I can't believe someone actually decided that this game was decent enough to be released. - It's ugly. It's seriously ugly. There was some good art during character creation but that's about all. Once you stop building your character with the cards and customize its appearance, it's a massive disappointement. Textures are ugly, characters are ugly, some of them aren't even properly displayed (one of my henchmen did not have a torso ?) and the art direction is poor.- The gameplay is boring and unfun. You just run, click on a mob, wait until it's your turn to hit... It's not fast-paced at all, which would be fine if the game was turn-based, but no, it's real time. Enemies will frequently leave melee once they are outnumbered, get a ranged weapon, shoot you, then come back in melee, then rince and repeat. You have... "puzzles" ? Put statues on pressure plates that are located within the same room and in plain sight to open doors.- The UI is terrible. I did not find a way to change key bindings in the options. Maybe there is not, maybe there is ? The fact that you can't find it tells a lot. It means if you have a non-qwerty Keyboard, or just want to change some bindings because you're used to them... Well you won't. You need to maintain a key to display your map as well. Why ? There may be a key to display it at all time but since I didn't find a keybindings menu, I can't tell you. Awesome.- For a game with such poor graphics and no physics whatsoever, you could imagine it runs smoothly. Well it does not. Alt-tabbing means either a crash, or various softwares like Discord or even your Steam Library will need to be killed in Task Manager so you can restart them.This game is definitely not worth 25$ and it's not worth 5$ either. The base idea was awesome: I was looking forward to grind dungeon with friends or strangers, in different environments, while gaining new abilities or powers based on what my character would accomplish. The execution is terrible. This needs to be either reworked from scratch, or will need years of fixing and I doubt this will compensate the very poor state the game is in right now.Do not waste your money on this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Dark Eye : Book of Heroes

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game to anyone, in it's current state. Watching the trailer made me think this game was trying to stay close to pnp source material, however, the truth turned out to be the exact opposite.  Everything is dumbed down and oversimplified, while character advancement solely relies on randomly rewarded cards! CARDS!!!  That's right-you lvl up your character by pulling a card out of deck, as a reward for completing dungeons! You earn AP, which you use to cash-in earlier mentioned card. And you get to pick one card out of three random ones. So having any build or any character advancement depth is out of question. In it's current state, the game belongs more to mobile market, rather than PC.

_childDocuments_.review: In an interview, the lead designer said: "We were to small to get a D&D license, so we took The Dark Eye, when it was offered to us" (or something along these lines). True, they are asking for a moderate price, but is the game worth even this small amount of money? I think not.

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game!It's a very unique experience that is stained by unfortunate bugs. The way the system works is you choose an origin story on character creation which will give you a series of objectives. As you complete quests from the bounty board, you will be able to access and complete parts of your origin story. Completing runs gives you cards that will allow you to upgrade many different skills and stats.Completing your origin story allows your character to access a unique quest area in the bounty board and unlock more origin stories. There are a total of 8 origin stories.The amount of stats and skills is incredibly overwhelming first time you play and will create a learning curve until you get familiar with the way the systems work.The combat is tactical and slow paced, so you cannot simply run into a room like a madman as you will risk getting party wiped, but this works great and to the advantage of the game.Plenty of puzzles and randomization is core to the gameplay as the cards you get are randomized, and so are the dungeons.The illustrations are definetly the highlight of the game for me as they really reflect the style and concept the devs are going for and they are absolutely gorgeous! Any of them could be a painting at my house anytime!Overall it's an incredibly unique game and it's a shame it released with so many bugs, although the devs have been very quick to address most of them and already have plans to fix even more!I will update this review once this is the case but even now, if you want a very unique and new cRPG experience, grab this. Even with the bugs and steep learning curve, it's still an extremely fun game, made even more fun with friends or other players. Itemization is rare and you have to take risks and higher difficulty dungeons to get better gear, but it feels great when you get that rare sword or platemail!My coop partner was frustrated with the start of the game as many people reviewing negatively also are, but as we went along we fell in love with it. After finishing our first 2 origin stories, we're now rolling 2 more characters with new origin stories and doing it all, all over again!
_childDocuments_.name: The Dark Eye : Book of Heroes

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, this will be a first impressions review.I went into the game expecting to get a gameplay experience comparable to sword coast legends or shadowrun boston lockdown. In other words a streamlined (cynics would say dumbed down) version of the game, hub based missions with randomly generated dungeons. Basically a dungeon crawler boardgame on my pc, playable with random people. And I got exactly that so I am happy.Critics point out that this game does not have the scope of the dark eye pen and paper. While this is true, the dark eye pen and paper level of detail is small animal tormenting insane! Any game trying to replicate such a level of detail would be a full priced and would put off people who are unfamiliar with the pen and paper variant.The pen and paper feel for me was captured by the following points:The character sheet looks like a pen and paper sheet - all the attributes are there 3 attribute skill checks attack/parry rolls in combatCharacter creation is rudimentary - a few beards, a few haircuts, some sliders but you can work with it and get a personalized portrait. Unfortunatley I have not been able to alter the portrait after character creation so make sure you are cool with it! Still, you CAN create a personalized look for your avatar instead of every fighter or dwarf having the same icon on screen.Gameplay - again very comparable to sword coast legends, your abilities have a cooldown, events unfold in real time. Difficulty differs wildly upon your character class - fighters are cake, the rest is squishy which means you NEED at least 1 fighter to finish missions as mages are very weak in the pen and paper game.The experience system is a tad annoying as you get a pick of tarot (inrah) cards to use right away for a small bonus or to upgrade and then use for a bigger bonus. There seems to be a bit of randomness involved but I expect lists of the cards and where to find them to pop up after a couple days so you can better map out your character.Missions can be replayed, the story hook remains the same (kill the evil necromancer) but the layout changes so there is some variation.TLDR:if you liked sword coast legends, shadowrun lockdown and similar games give this a try.

_childDocuments_.review: This one totally flew underneath my radar and when I first saw it, it was already dicounted, with overwhelmingly negative reviews. I hesitated, but finally gave it a shot and I am damn glad I did. So glad in fact, that I bought a second copy of the game after 20 hours of playtime and gifted it to a friend.Since then, we played it in COOP, where this game really shines (and what RPGs are all about in the first place). Now, I finished the game with all Storylines and 100% Achievements and had 254 hours of fun, but I surely took my time to write these lines. I wanted to be sure to give you a foundated insight and no "below-2-hours-playtime-review" that comes along like I know all about this game.And after 250 hours I know a lot, but still not all. Even on my last day, I found 2 new items and some occurences are still a riddle to me. There are still some bugs, one even borderline gamebreaking, but one thing is for sure: Book of Heroes certainly does not deserve so much hate.So it is said, that this game has no Story what is absolutely not true. In fact, it has 8 storylines, that are embedded in a timeframe, where an uprising of Orcs and cultists of the Nameless God take place (the intro video draws the picture). This and the henchmen-behaviour is quiet unrivalled in the genre, at least nothing I can think of.The various stations of such storyline consist of a number of adventures (like gamebooks/modules) and the detective work to follow the hints where the next adventure takes place. So Yes, it is no "Start-to-Finish-All-Epic-One-Man-Show-to-Rescue-the-known-World-and-all-the-Rest" and No, it is not a storyless and bland game, but has some smaller stories that might fit better into schedule with getting together with friends for cooperative roleplay and high replayability. Choose what you like best.If you have no friend at hand, you have to resort to henchmen, which first set is displayed in the Cover Artwork. The first ones join you on an adventure for free, stronger ones have to be unlocked and charge you a fee per adventure. If you don´t look too close, they behave like human players, opening doors (or smashing them down), searching for valueables (but not looting) or engaging enemies. I would have liked it, if the thief took more initiative and disarmed traps without telling him to do it, or at least give the player a proper command in the chat-wheel instead of doing it via the map, but ok. If the nosey sorceress is going to scout the dungeon, you can tell her to stay put. You can even use it to your advantage, if your character is a little meek himelf, staying behind and drawing back further to initiate a rest when things get ugly. Unless human players, henchmen don´t need to be in the same room for resting.Shaping your Character is done "Ultima-Style" with Inrah-Cards (kind of Tarot) at your friendly ♥♥♥♥♥-next-door. While I really like this approach (and generally getting rid of the dusted AD&D-like Level-system) there needs to be more variation in the cards (maybe 5 cards). There are squires that raise general skills and Lords for the main attributes. In addition each Arch-Class has its own type of card. Fighters get Knights, Mages get Mages, and Blessed-One get Seers. My Blessed-One of Rondra (sort of Crusader/Paladin) got lot of Seer-Cards, but not a single Knight for his two-handed sword (only one for daggers). So he never got any better with his weapons. Good that my buddy could do the tanking with his elven archer. With such a devastating feedback it is highly unlikely that the devs will work further on this project despite it´s potential (additional classes/adventures). I never regretted playing this game, like others, that start promising and then put you in an endless grind until I forgot, what it´s all about. Have a shelf full of this...

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: A very hollow and unfinished game.Okay. Lets put the Good stuff first: 1.: I like the design, and i even like the simplified character Creation. Yes you dont get the detail in character creation, or all the options of classes and races that exist in the lore but you dont need to. Its just not that kind of game.2.: If you lose an adventure you dont loose anything, and basically get resetted before the adventure. I put that as a positive because of Negative 4.And i think thats it already.Before i Delve into the Negatives i want to say that i dont think the game is the worst. I think there is a lot of potential, and could be a lot of fun, but as it is right now, after playing for about 3 hours it just gets more and more frustrating with all the points following adding up. Please take another year to flesh out the game more and turn this around.Well then the negatives: 1.: Simplified character creation or not, Being able to personalize your characters at least to an extend is a must. If you play a character, and character Progression is SO slow, you need to be able to choose at least some skills, especially with the "crafting system" in place.2.: Mages and Blessed ones have very Limited Abilities. That in itself is fine. But they need at least a good chance to Succeed in their Spells and Blessings! Being able to only waste your Karma or Mana in 75% of times is really frustrating.3.: Character Progression: After each Adventure you are rewarded with 3 random Perks you can choose from. If you need or like it or not. You basicly have literally to no choice of what your charater will be skilled at.4.: Dungeons: Ive played 3 Succesful missions so far with a friend. The only reason because its only three is because we BOTH HAD TO MAKE FIGHTERS to even survive any combat. With other character we died every Mission. 4.5.: I played Drakensang, and i Hated it there too. You just CANT put the Way Characters Fight like in the PnP into a Computer Game. Or at least Hide it properly. On Pc it jsut feels BORING and Frustrating if you just sit there for a minute, waiting for your character to Hit an enemy. Its not fun.5.: Every Map feels the exact same, because all enemies seem to act the same. The maps are empty, until enemies show up, and then its the same back and forth. So far no riddles, no intresting traps or options other than: Kill all enemies. 6.: Enemy AI: Its intersting to have enemies run away from you. But its stupid if they start wobbling in and out of your Sight, keeping you locked in combat, basicly forcing yo to chase them. That wouldnt be that bad, if you would be able to hit them while they run. We flanked enemies why they tried to run, locking them in place. But as long as they are "retreating" it is just not possible to hit them.7.: Friend who played with me was complaining about very hard Lag issues. Cant completely confirm if its due to Connection or the Game, but it was an issue.8.: Golbins wanting to send me to Golgari?! Absolutely no excuse there. This Screams for Stadardized Shouts for all enemies. Which is a hard NO GO if you use a world that has so much existing lore and background. 9.: Some control issues, things that are unclear or feel weird, like the character doesnt jsut run where you clikc on the map if its too far away, and that you cant see your friends on the minimap. Small stuff like that.There are probably more points i have forgot by now, but i think its a good summary of all that was bothering me.I really hpe the Devs get more time and this game will be good some day.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game, I love the dungeons that have random layouts and give different rewards for completing them multiple times, I love the difficulty which is very hard but encourages tactics and planning, I love the progression system (the cards you get are small increases but soon start to stack making you feel very powerful by the end of the game).There are some things I also dont like about the game, this game is buggy and although the devs are working hard and they did release a patch that fixed a lot of bugs it is still very buggy, the spells feel lacking when you first get them (I was playing an elven white mage and felt like my best spell was the first spell I got and the other spells were underwhelming) but that is mostly it.I feel like if you are looking for a good dungeon crawler to play with a couple of friends this game is great and with a little patience I believe that many people can enjoy it as much as I do

_childDocuments_.review: Love at 2nd sight.If you have friends to play this game together, it is a great way to chill out after work while enjoying a good dungeon crawl. I appreciate the fact that it can be played solo (with NPC henchmen), and it certainly provides sufficient challenge in that, but it really shines when played in coop mode together as a group of 2-4 players. An adventure in a dungeon can usually be finished in less than 20 minutes, depending on how thorough you are in exploring, and this makes it easier to organize a quick online meetup between friends and to squeeze in a short game session between other responsibilities. There are over 20 different adventures and dungeons, each with their own theme and goals. Since they are procedurally generated, no two adventures will be identical, so there is enough variation to keep returning for more. A little-mentioned aspect that won me over by surprise, is the inclusion of subtle details that are easy to overlook during first play, such as ways to succeed the mission without combat if you are observant to your surroundings for example. Or, that non-combat related skills can have great impact on mission success or implicit mission difficulty. Embedded within the deep lore of The Dark Eye and using its challenging and sometimes merciless ruleset, I can recommend Book of Heroes to anyone who goes in with an open mind and likes cooperative adventure games in a fantasy setting.
_childDocuments_.name: The Dark Eye : Book of Heroes

_childDocuments_.review: Henchmen AI is clearly broken. Rogue henchman doesn't even try to disarm a trap which is right in front of him, even after being issued to disarm it. There's a lot of other glarring issues other people have mentioned. Unfortunately I wasn't really able to complete even the first dungeon after the tutorial one, so I refunded the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this small game - there is advanced background/class/race character creation which gives you background and personal quests to pursue - that is a feature I was missing in many RPGs  for roleplayers, then it generates numerical stats itself based upon that -again something I'm OK with as I play not a perfectly min maxed character, but a character based on a chosen background. Then I love the group of adventurers - simle party (for solo play, for coop it is replaced). I don't control them, so it looks a bit funny how they wonder around on their own, but it could be annoying in more tense combat. I do like the system of choosing skill cards at the end of dungeons, which will become permanent if you choose to, and simple potion/accessories crafting.  I like those random events in dungeons where I can use my other than combat skills. I like the music and overal feel of inn full of adventurers setting off to their own goals. Also point and click movement/interactions feel smooth. I'm OK with simple narrator/non voiced dialogues.  EDIT after playing longer:Pursuing my own personal quest does sound interesting, but sadly the game isn't finished and instead there is cheesy complete 10 dungeons to unlock something, which is the most hated online feature and I believe that was a mistake made because of the coop implementation decision. I wish they would focus on singleplayer aspect instead and flesh out the group of adventures, implement better progression and instead of number of dungeons to complete, make story dungeons unique and others could be just random dungeons on the way. I believe it does have low score because of Dark Eye fans and those MMO repetitive mechanics, because the new dungeons reuses the assets and the game is not strategic enough to make something that much better/different the next time, but you get random cards as rewards, so the next time you are stronger, and you meet different encounters, but they don't repeat as they should have and they seem to be unfinished/too few. I wish some of those encounters would become permanent - like hiring new kind of adventurers and level them up. So I hope for more singleplayer focused sequel, but it doesn't have to be named Dark Eye, because it doesn't use anything from the setting anyway.

_childDocuments_.review: DSA, I have not only played the system but created a lot of content and had countless hours of fun  as a GM with my groups over the years. I was a bit sceptical looking at the reviews of this game but even if it isnt a RP experience in the typical sense I can see some value in the game even if it has some flaws and you can feel the devs didnt have much DSA knowledge.Speaking of the flaws: IF the deveolpers tried to find a new way to drive players mad the KI they used for the NPC characters are at a supreme level of anoyance. I couldnt have imagined it even after reading the reviews so someone has to tell you more clear whats going on and its ME who is doing it.Imagine you want to have all characters in the same room to rest at a campfire but nearly all of the characters dont feel like resting and run in the opposite direction. Not only that, one or two of them are breaking doors 4 rooms away to get to room number 5 you havent discovered yet to die seconds later. YES your party refuses openly to follow any guidance and goes aggressively dungeon exploring. I cannot imagine any KI which would do something like that without purposefully programming it that way so one of the devs is a massive ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and we should acknowledge that.I am pretty sure with human players it can be a lot of fun and you dont have to let the KI ruin your gaming evening. For a price of 25 Euro this game is sadly not enough to justify the spending especially as you need 3 other friends to invest to make it playable without going into a rage mode.

_childDocuments_.review: Game has potential to be a fun pseudo rogue-like dungeon crawler. The rogue-like aspects come from the random ability cards and random loot. You can't really plan a character build, as the upgrades you get are random, and that by itself I'm not totally against, but as I'll explain below causes problems. The character creation process is pretty neat in its presentation.However, the problems this game has are .A couple things that I found to be subjectively bad are the graphics and the skill mechanics. Graphics just look terribly dated. Not really bad, just not what I'd expect from this type of game made today.The skills system is needlessly convoluted (you roll 3 dice for every ability, want to roll low instead of high, and add 3 attribute/skill modifiers but you're really more subtracting, because again you want low totals). The mechanics I can't really fault them, as that's just how the pen and paper game rules are, so I don't include that as a negative in my review, just saying it's a very confusing and obtuse system to someone who's been playing D&D and other pen and paper RPG's for decades.Here are some objectively bad problems:

_childDocuments_.review: Sorry to say so, but this game has to be considered a failed gaming project. I wouldn't even rate it, and if forced certainly below 60/100. So sorry.I love the world of the Dark Eye (German: Das Schwarze Auge). It is certainly one of the coolest and deepest fantasy worlds I have encountered. I played the pen and paper RPG and a number of the older PC games set in this world.Book of Heroes is supposed to be a sort of action RPG I guess using procedurally generated maps, They use some of the more recent rules, but progressing the characters is basically coincidental as you have to find cards which you can use to invest your adventure points (=xp) in the abilities or skills on said card. Not really possible to make a proper build like that.The character generation started promising though.Quests are boring, the maps are too simple. As your characters and the henchmen can hardly die the game is also not really exciting. Pathfinding is a pain too. After five missions the game ended for me, no more missions would be presented although I bested all maps. Didn't bother to try it with another character.The game seems to aim at children below 14 years or so.Sorry to say so, but this game is unworthy of the title "Dark Eye". It is also unworthy of your time, unless you are said young child and your parents want to introduce you to the Dark Eye. I don't know what the developers and publishers were thinking. I guess they might have thought that the Warhammer universe has many fans too and those guys get by producing mostly only average (or rather bad) games too...Better alternatives within the world of the Dark Eye are Blackguards 1 and 2 or the very old Das Schwarze Auge: Schicksalsklinge, Sternenschweif and Schatten über Riva. Drakensang was also ok.

_childDocuments_.review: It needs to go back in the oven for about 1 more year. Broken and Buggy. Lazy attempt at henchman and a poor excuse for reasons for not have custom Henchman. Honestly if this was released back in 2005 it would of been acceptable but still fall short to IWD/NWN and other Isometric RPGS. While i know this was going to be a Random Generated crawler i was hoping for some lore not generic fantasy tile plates. Its a great shell tho. They have core concepts down but fall short on everything else. 29.99 US is was to much to ask for a product that still feels like its in early beta.

_childDocuments_.review: This game certainly has potential! Its rpg element includes a very interesting character building system. You draw 3 cards after aech adventure and have the option to upgrade them. If you like them you can then use those cards to upgarde your character stats. (this includes stats like strength, skills like swords or even extra training like stunning blow etc.) In short you can create your very own and pretty unique character thats suits your playstyle. After almost 30 hours of gameplay I have  only encountered 1 bug (my character lost all her hair --- must have been stress-related doing all those dungeons). The developers are very engaging (really fast replies on posts in forum). So if you like rpgs you might want to give this game a try. I am certainly enjoying it!

_childDocuments_.review: I like the Dark Eye system and have had some fun with games that use these rules in the past (Realms of Arkania, Drakensang, Blackguards...).  However, this game just isn't very good.  On the store page they advertise "Play with friends or alone in single-player mode with eight individual storylines", which might lead you to assume that there is a story or that the random missions are connecting in an overarching plot.  However, they aren't connected.  It's just procedurally generated dungeons filled traps and monsters for you to fight.  It's more of a board game than a RPG.You don't even have control over how you develop your characters, because that's handled by cards that randomly drop at the end of a mission.  You get your pick of 1 of 3 cards, and you can spend your AP to add the benefits of the cards to your character.  It's a mechanism designed to make you grind missions until you get the cards your character needs.  However, beyond improving your character, there's no incentive to grind the generic missions in this game.If you plan on playing solo, you better really plan on playing solo because the henchmen are horrible.  You can give them commands on mini-map, but not in the game itself and they run around like hamsters on crack engaging enemies in rooms you haven't explored and generally being more trouble than they are worth.  If you played NWN, they behave a lot like the henchmen in that game, only there's more of them and you have less control over them.If you played the random dungeons in Sword Coast Legends, or Infinite Dungeons in NWN you've got a basic idea of what the game is like.  It's currently less polished than either of those experiences.  While the devs are patching the game, remember that this is not an early access title.  The devs consider this a complete release.  While you may get some patches and maybe a few QOL updates, you aren't going to see any significant changes to the game.  Unfortunately, what you see is what you get.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: great idea, poorly optimized, lacking content, and clunky controls.I can appreciate the idea behind the game, but there are a plethora of poorly-chosen design elements, I don't even know where to begin, but the game reeks of a lack of experience and a lack of knowledge. I fault the publisher, too, for even letting this game get released in its current state -- make them get a couple content creators and have fix the bugs for a year, and you will have a much better title. Nevertheless, maybe this was a sunk-costs sort of thing, I don't really know. In its current state, it is worse than most early access titles. I feel scammed for buying it as a result.The GPU optimization is horrible for a modern NVidia GPU. It uses more GPU memory and RAM than SSD space.The content is severely lacking. The tavern and tutorial lacked original and distinct character models. Character creation is lacking in diversification, but it seems to have its heart in the right place. There were more pen-and-paper elements in Realms of Arkania. Hell, the character models in Arkania reacted quicker to my mouse clicks, and that game was turn based and written for MS DOS. How hard can it be to buy "The Dark Eye" ruleset and just implement it in a library?The interface is horrible. I feel locked out of interacting with the game every step of the way, the time it takes for the UI to respond is insanely long. And this is when it isn't throttling my GPU; for example, it wants to be a "real-time" game, but at the same time, there are breaks and pauses in the interactions; it's like my mouse click occurs asynchronously, but is processed in the same thread as the attack animation of the enemy, so it has to wait for that animation to finish before my character's action begins. The developers have a long way to go. Just spend some time playing your game, get a feel for it, and don't be afraid to extend release dates by five years so you and your team can earn your undergraduate degrees in game development.Maybe there is an interesting story underpinning this game's clearly early release -- If this game provides an API for adding mods, I would be way more OK with the current state as an early access title. My feeling is that a single ambitious student in a college course on game design would produce something better than this, so I just have trouble believing it is the end result. Since the game is basically 2-D, I have seen better than this at hackathons.

_childDocuments_.review: Me: Can we get Drakensang 3?Universe: We have Drakensang 3 at home!Drakensang 3 at home:Ok… despite the little comedy bit up top I never believed it to be a proper RPG (like some of the trailers make it out to be) but just a fun little dungeon crawler. But let's not beat around the bush and go straight to the big mistake this game makes. The cards… Instead of allocating points once you level up or using them to increase their value on the fly (like in Drakensang) you basically select one of three tarot-like cards. These can be interchanged or upgraded afterwards. You do not get to choose how to advance your character the way you like for it's mostly up to RNG. And the upgrading is inconsistent. For example: You get a card that gives you +1 Impact Weapon Proficiency and purchase the upgrade for the card. But you end up losing the original bonus and get something you did not want. Nothing warns you what the change in the card is going to be, and to add salt to the wound, there are cards that retain their original bonus after upgrading! The in game glossary contains no info on upgrade paths so you need to experiment and remember/write down all upgrades. And even then some carts give several abilities that are given once every purchase. So if you get one undesired ability from a card there is no way to know if another is present that you do like to have. This is possibly the worst upgrade system I've ever seen in not just RPG’s but in any game with character stats. Then there are your npc companions. You have no control over them (you can give them some simple commands via map markers) but they are somewhat helpful by looking around for loot locations. But mostly they will go into rooms full of enemies ahead of you getting themselves killed. If you want to prevent this you have to constantly press the Follow/Stay button so the AI resets its (personal) priorities.Apart from some strange combat behavior from NPC’s I did not encounter game breaking bugs… in the beginning that is. In the beginning it was just “NAME” in the event log instead of a proper name and an examination text being obviously wrong (Torch is missing while there is definitely an active torch pressend) that sort of thing. But It was at “The Forge of Agrimoth” where I encountered a game breaking bug. There is a Rostrum present where you need to offer up several items attached to the cards it shows (yes more cards…) so I give it my selection but nothing happens. The magical barrier that is supposed to be lifted remains and I can't get the items out. I restarted the Adventure and looked up a guide for the correct answers. And once more nothing happened, the level is completely bugged and unfinishable for me.And so I came to the decision to lay the game down. The concept of a quick bite dungeon crawler is compelling but this is not the one.

_childDocuments_.review: This is clearly not a game that will match everyone's taste. But it does that what it sets out to achieve rather well. You won't find an epic story here. Rather, I consider it between a mix of independed NwN modules and IwD dungeon crawling. I can recommend Book of Heroes to people with an understanding of the TDE ruleset. But maybe not to the casual RPG or D&D player.The things that positively stood out for me were the cosy environmental art of the tilesets, the for Aventuria typical music and especially the entertaining character creation process. Henchmen are in singleplayer mode both a gift and a curse, however. You will get better ones once you sufficiently proceeded inside the game, true. But until then the "free" mercenaries are at best walking meatshields. Most of the time I simply opt to run the missions as a solo character. I recommend people who are fed up with mecernaries in singleplayer to do the same. I at the very least found being solo the most enjoyable style of play.Things I wish for the developer to add in the (near) future:- Readable books and other TDE literature.- Ultra widescreen (21:9) support for GUI elements. As well as larger dialogue/tutorial boxes.- A toolset/editior to guarantee the long term survival of this game. Please don't let it disappear inside the River of Time devs!- More alchemy/blacksmithing blueprints. Especially for creating our own arms, armours and magical items.- Ironing out of the occasional performance drops.

_childDocuments_.review: Edited this review after more play time.  Game does not get better as you progress which is frustrating.  If anything the poor design choices become more glaring.  IT finally put me over the edge and i cannot recommend this game.  If some big changes were made I could get behind it, but the randomness to the progression really makes it difficult to build a decent character, and there doesn't seem to be any change in henchmen or anything as you go through the game.  Just boring, boring, same, same.I guess I'm one of the few people who can recommend this game.  I think some of the people complaining here didn't read anything about the game before buying it or just don't pay attention in general.  I see people complaining about the fact that you cant control the henchmen:  It tells you in the game description that they are AI controlled.  If you didn't like that feature, you shouldn't have bought the game.  Some other complain about their character waking up in random places in the dungeon:  This is a part of the character creation process not a bug.   If you choose the Spirit Child card during character creation, you will randomly spawn in dungeon after sleeping.  Is this a useful trait?  Not really, but at least pay attention.  I know there might have been tremendous expectations around this product if you are part of the Dark Eye fan base, but much like with Sword Coast Legends a few years back, player expectations are often wildly out of sync with reality.   This game seems to be a basic dungeon crawl game that you can play with friends or solo if you want AI controlled characters.  The game tells you to be careful which ones you choose and look at their characteristics before you choose them:  (people are also complaining about the way the AI characters act)  The graphics aren't cutting edge, but as someone who has been playing CRPGs since the early 90s the graphics are fine.  The real time combat is pausable and feels like Baldurs Gate.  Character creation is like Ultima with the fortune teller displaying cards for you to choose which dtermine your path.  I have only played the first three missions, but i am enjoying it so far.  I am hoping that i will be able to find better loot in the dungeons and that the vendors will sell better items.  Right now it does feel pretty basic and I hope if the developers decide to keep adding content to the game, that at least some of it is for free.  This game needs a dungeon editor, more character customization options, and a character creator which skips past the fortune teller and gives you lists of things to choose.  The game still needs work, but for now it seems to be serviceable.

_childDocuments_.review: I had previous given this game a negative review but after giving it some more time, now I have changed my mind and will give it a positive review! I would only recommend this to D&D fans and those who love CRPGs. If you're a casual gamer who requires amazing graphics, this isn't the game for you. BUT if you love games similar to Baldur's Gate and want to play together with your friends online then this GAME IS A MUST! However, if you want a great single player experience then I wouldn't recommend this game since there are so many better single player CRPGs out there.Pros: -Detailed custom character creation system (at least in this game, you can choose how your character looks and their own unique background).-Fluid multiplayer (when i hosted a public multiplayer adventure, there were no issues).-Fun with friends (DO NOT CHOOSE THE SPIRIT CHILD CARD DURING CHARACTER CREATION! that card causes too many problems if you play with friends like spawning you in different areas after a rest. if you have friends who enjoy D&D and CRPGS then you will have a good time together but make sure your friend enjoy those types of games before you make them buy it!)-Grinding (if you like games that require you to clear dungeons to collect points so you can improve your character, then this is the game for you).-Dungeons are never exactly the same (procedural generated maps).-The game has great potential if the developers decide to update and patch it.Cons: -Not friendly for casual players (my friend hated this game since he doesn't play CRPGs and he didn't look at the card effect details during Character Creation, he chose SPIRIT CHILD and it caused him to spawn in different in points on the map after a rest which was extremely frustrating and made us think it was a BUG).-Some levels are way too difficult (for example I hosted a group of 4 human players and at the paranoid occult nights level , where the last group of mages can wiped our party easily by blasting at once instantly killing my whole party).-The story is not very detailed or developed. (You get one main quest from the cards you choose during the character creation and the rest of the map are made up of side missions).-The graphics and combat animations are very basic, feels more like an early access game.-You can't control the AI companions and sometimes they can be very stupid.

_childDocuments_.review: I think most of the negative reviews are from people who did not know what to expect. This game is no Baldur's Gate, no Drakensang 3 and not even a remake of the Northland triology of games. It is a mission based action game set in the world of the Dark Eye and is definitely best played Co-op with your friends.Get 4 people together, everyone plays one character, fire up some discord and it is a great laugh. Also the Dark Eye touches are great. Even whilst playing Co-op in someone else's game can you drive your own characters story forward. There are still a few hiccups here or there, and the XP system can be a little fickle, but as long as you don't actually expect a FULL cRPG in the style of Divinity original sin or Skyrim you should be fine.We played for 4 hours today and have already arranged the next date to continue the quests.

I hope it gets better and maybe there are things I haven't discovered yet.   But as of now I can't recommend the game. _childDocuments_.review: First impression review:This seems--just like the Drakensang series--a frail imitation of better party-based RPGs it is clearly designed to look like. Like those earlier games,  the writing is so bad that it is unsettling.After a few battles, a few conversations and a trip to the inexplicable adventure board, it simply isn't fun. I'm a bit shocked by how clunky the user controls are, and how limited the character design options seem to be as well. Graphically, this looks like Pathfinder: Kingmaker--I'm assuming it is running on the same engine--but, where that game made up for some of its deficits with passably interesting plot line, this one appears to operate more like a series of one-off adventures with loosely threaded, character-specific plot thrown in.People aren't drawn into this genre without enjoying being a part of an engaging story. I am not sure why developers imagine their hard work on RPGs will pay-off without investing in top-quality writers--yet they frequently do. It is a tough lesson, but, as a professional writer, one I hope may eventually be learned.If your taste is anything like mine, this is not worth the time it takes to install. Should the game pick-up in quality after another couple adventures, I will be delighted to amend this review. I would not hold my breath.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the perfect example of how NOT to make a CRPG. Not only are you not allowed to roll your own character (i.e you must choose a preset), you also cannot directly control any of the NPC companions the game gives you. You are able to give them basic orders like "explore this general area", "attack enemies in this general area (but not specific enemies so no way to focus fire)",  or "disarm traps in this general area (but you have no control over which NPC actually does the disarming, so it could be the rogue who actually has the skill ranks to do it or it could be the wizard who does it and end up failing and hurting herself). You are also completely unable to customize these NPCs in any way. You cannot change their gear or raise their stats at all. Additionally you are unable to distribute loot to them (for example, if you're playing a wizard/cleric you have to carry that sword you found instead of giving it to the fighter despite him having better encumbrance than you and the fact that holding iron hinders your spellcasting). The only way to alleviate this issue is to play the game with a group of friends instead of using the NPCs.  The other major flaw with this game is the character advancement system where instead of being able to freely distribute your Adventure Points in the stats you wish (like in the actual ttrpg) you get a choice between one of three random cards given to you at then end of an adventure with random stat increases that range from slightly helpful to completely useless. TL;DR this is a awful CRPG because in a genre all about player choice and control the player is given almost none of either.

_childDocuments_.review: The Dark Eye: Book of Heroes was released on Steam June 9th of this year. The game was developed by Random Potion Oy and was published by Wild River Games. It is a fantasy role-playing RPG game that allows players to choose their own adventures and multiplayer co-op parties. This game stems from the original game, The Dark Eye, which is a German RPG created in 1984 by Ulrich Kiesow. Other features of the original game, such as the fictional world of Adventuria, have made their way into other PC games and novels. As stated by Wild River Games on their official website, The Dark Eye: Book of Heroes has a “plethora of well-known places, characters and enemies from The Dark Eye universe.”As mentioned before, The Dark Eye: Book of Heroes takes place in the fictional fantasy world Adventuria, home to dwarves, elves, orcs, and more popular creatures of the fantasy genre. Like most fantasy games, there is a lot of interesting lore that helps carry any adventure found in the game. The game starts off by letting players choose which species they would like to be out of the four options: dwarves, elves, half-elves, and humans. Each species comes with certain physical attributes that are meant to affect your character’s physical capabilities in the game play. From there, players go on to build their characters even more by choosing things like their back story, trauma, and ambitions. I found building the character to be the most enjoyable part of my play through because of how thoroughly thought out some of the options were and the number of options provided.The style of the game in terms of graphics and design is very true to the classic (but maybe outdated) RPG adventure game style. I did not particularly like the character designs or dungeon designs for this reason. I don’t have anything against going for the classic style, but for me, it did not work in The Dark Eye: Book of Heroes due to other problems with the game play that I will discuss below. The dungeons were not very interesting to look at and were kept very simple with repetitive features. A major problem that I had with this game was my overall lack of interest in my adventure and what I was doing. Initially, when I chose the adventure, I was excited to see what was to come with the quest and story. However, once it came to playing it, it felt as if the game was missing something, or several things, that would have made it more fun to play. It felt disorganized and as if there wasn’t enough time spent getting the story ready for play.Aside from the graphics feeling outdated, the controls and features of the actual game play were also lacking in modernity. It is a game that can be played with friends and still has some of the endearing characters of fantasy RPG games; however, unless you already have a liking for other games of this style (think Dungeons and Dragons) in their oldest and most classic forms, you will probably not enjoy The Dark Eye: Book of Heroes very much.

_childDocuments_.review: The more I play this game, the more I want to keep playing it.It definitely cannot be compared to any AAA titles, of course, but I personally am a TDE player and I love how the devs actually managed to incorporate the rules of the PnP game. I believe that especially gamers who know the TDE franchise can have a lot of fun with this game. I've been playing solo and in a group and I enjoy both.Sure, the game does not offer a tremendous amount of missions, items or lore so far, but I'm hoping that there is more to come. Also, there already is enough incentive to just keep playing the same missions over and over again. First of all, they are not completely identical and the rewards for the missions become better and better the more often you finish them, like for example more AP (ExP), which brings me to another thing I really like about the game.Since I'm used to TDE's slower character progression, I actually really enjoy the comparably faster character progression in this game. But even more fun than simply increasing the character's stats over and over again, is to actually get new skills and spells. Those are pretty rare and I'm delighted whenever I get to learn something new. I'm only twelve hours into playing it, or already twelve hours, depending how you feel about the game, but I have not even started a level 3 mission so far. I am pretty sure that I will keep having fun with this game for at least another twelve hours, which, in my opinion, will make the game worth it's money.I do not know how this game will feel to those who do now know TDE, but I would recommend to give it a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: Note:  to be fair this is an early review without having read all of the instructions and available guides and just diving straight into the game.NEW INFORMATION:I am changing my initial thumbs down to up to give this a game a chance and try to understand it better. I may have jumped the gun, because it is a different style of game with different rule-sets.Mana is called Arcane Energy and it's associated Potion is called Magical Potion with AE below.  Originally I could not get it into the quick use bar, but started game today and it was in a slot in the quick use bar.  As a mage/wizard It still is not enough to keep you in a fight without burning through it fast.Stats in this game are very different than other D&D style games.  Uses a different Rule Set associated with Dark Eye.  The Dark Eye stats and rules can get complex.  Just now trying to understand it.Also, if going the mage route, get rid of your Iron in your inventory as it has an impeding affect.I am not recommending that you do not try this game, but I do recommend reading the instructions and guides first.The game is a slightly angled top down game similar in style to the Baldur's Gate or Icewind Dale.Characters are created and built based on cards sort of like a Tarot deck.  These cards create character elements such as race, class, skill type within class, character background, etc...In addition the game appears to generate differing stories/quests based on your character creation.First Impressions:What the heck is this mess?  Limited armor and accessory slots.Traps every 5 centimeters or inches. Rest appears to ALWAYS attract enemies, found out later about sleeping bags and tentsYour party members (called Henchmen) appear to have zero AI and so far I have not located the AI adjustment, sometimes the henchman will not attack (even when ordered), the henchmen also just wander off on their own, away from the group, and still no AI controls found just yet.  Their wandering can get them into battles you may not want to be in, but you need to provide support when it happens.The early game appears to not have NO ability to regenerate mana or take a mana potions. No leveling system that I can see just yet.  My Mages/Wizards Staffs have zero magic power so far and unable to find weapons worth a crap.Mages can carry and use blade weapons and other weapon types, but their stats do not lean toward a front line fighter.  Since henchmen kind of do their own thing, and wander everywhere, protection for mages can be challenging.  The bad part is your spell ability is burned out after a couple of mage shots and with no way to restore except when camping/resting, the mage is useless, he has to run up and do the Yoda thing with his staff and bang on a few enemies.  It is definitely a dice roll oriented game.I am still giving this game a chance and will try and read the instructions and guides and hopefully  decipher how this game should be played.  Started out as a mage and get no physical defense spells (just sorcery defense), two shots with my magic and mana is drained with no way currently identified to renew or restore mana except to camp/rest, nor does it rebuild on its own over time.But the traps, the traps are everywhere, feels like every 2 to 5 inches in different quests runs.  So far have not been able to direct my henchman rogue to disable the traps, so I try - sometimes with success, most times no success.Henchman suck, or most of the time are practically useless (i guess that is what you get for using free henchmen).  Is this real time or turn based, at times it is difficult to tell, for movement it is action point based, but strikes feel like either timed or turned based.Still working my way deeper into the game and may modify my first impression.  But first impressions are difficult to overcome.  First AD&D style game I have had to stop and try to read documents to figure out how to play.I so wanted this game to succeed, but struggling to figure it out.This feels more like it should be played on a server (which it supports) with real players who can work together.But all of the TRAPS!!!!  Really, this many traps starting off in the various quests?As I proceed, I may change the thumbs down to a thumbs up, but keep the middle finger on the traps.I am not recommending that you do not try this game, but I do recommend reading the instructions and guides first.  This is a different style of game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great. Yes, it is. When we see a game of this genre, we immediately think of several linked titles, such as Divinity, Baldurs Gate and so many others that you probably played before too.But here the business is different.You are just one more, who initially doesn’t release rays all over the place or has that legendary sword already bought by dlc, you’re just one more.The air of confidence that games usually push us to give the false sense of power here does not exist. You will die in the first dungeon, yes you will.You go after hours and hours of game to get better armor than yours and in the next room you die to a trap because you were too confident and maybe, you will never see that armor again.The game will punish you for your carelessness in looking for traps, finding a better combat position or simply trying to unleash a spell where the prerequisites are the lowest statuses on your character sheet and you didn't even realize it.The feeling of progression can be slow, very slow at first. But when the results start to appear, the sensation is very gratifying, because you know it was not easy to get there.You will not be multi-tasking. You are the guy who will crush the enemies or the guy who follows this guy to be able to collect his herbs and make potions in peace. (Well, he can fight too, but he definitely won't even go near the guy who smashes enemies)Every step counts. Don't get tired of searching all the corners and objects. Even if you have passed a perception test, there may be more than one interesting thing in the place.Do not give up. Today's games always give you an "invisible hand" sometimes so you don't lose your edge. There is no such thing in this game, it will be brutal with you all the time. Just don't give up and move on.You will not become "mister full epic items" or you will get the "Flaming vorpal dragonslayer that spit acid at midnight sword". Your equipment (with luck) will make you look a little more robust than a generic npc, and that's what you are, just one more in the world.And yet after this review you still think that this game is not for you, it is because it is not. But if you move on, try hard. For the minimum of achievements will be an immense satisfaction. Be strong.But not everything is perfect...The game itself has several bugs to be fixed, yes and really, playing with the henchmans is a test of patience.You have two options: solo mode, which will be incredibly difficult and depending on the class you pick up practically impossible or have one to three more friends and have fun at party which is the best option possible and will only add even more fun to your game.

name: Ghostrunner
detailed_description: Crime Boss: Rockay City Join the community on Discord About the Game Ghostrunner is a hardcore FPP slasher packed with lightning-fast action, set in a grim, cyberpunk megastructure. Climb Dharma Tower, humanity’s last shelter, after a world-ending cataclysm. Make your way up from the bottom to the top, confront the tyrannical Keymaster, and take your revenge. The streets of this tower city are full of violence. Mara the Keymaster rules with an iron fist and little regard for human life. As resources diminish, the strong prey on the weak and chaos threatens to consume what little order remains. The decisive last stand is coming. A final attempt to set things right before mankind goes over the edge of extinction. As the most advanced blade fighter ever created, you’re always outnumbered but never outclassed. Slice your enemies with a monomolecular katana, dodge bullets with your superhuman reflexes, and employ a variety of specialized techniques to prevail. One-hit one-kill mechanics make combat fast and intense. Use your superior mobility (and frequent checkpoints!) to engage in a never-ending dance with death fearlessly. Ghostrunner offers a unique single-player experience: fast-paced, violent combat, and an original setting that blends science fiction with post-apocalyptic themes. It tells the story of a world that has already ended and its inhabitants who fight to survive.

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite games this year! Ghostrunner is a perfect blend of first person fast paced platforming, sword combat and one hit one kill difficulty (both you and the enemy). The game plays surprisingly smooth and the hiccups I made along the way felt like that of my own (and not the mechanics of the game). The sci-fi universe and story telling seemed to compliment Ghostrunner fairly well in creating an interesting universe. In all honesty I do wish game had a little more investment into the storytelling, but the gameplay really made up for that. Best way I can describe this game is Mirrors Edge meets Bladerunner. Highly suggest picking this one up for yourselves!

_childDocuments_.review: Now that I've had time with Ghostrunner, I really enjoy it but there are some really glaring issues that tarnish what could be a perfect game. The cyber void puzzles really break up the pace of the game as if the developers went "Are you enjoying cutting through people and running along walls while listening to good music? Are you having fun? How about we take that all away and make you do some Tetris? NERD!". Another issue I have is the inconsistency of how the gymnastics trigger. You could approach a wall at the very same angle you have a dozen times before (because you will be doing the same wal lrunning against the same wall at least a dozen times) and some times the wall running will not trigger, sometimes the wall running will trigger with the slightest of an angle. Jumping from one wall to another also has a lack of consistency that I found frustrating. I'm okay with difficulty, I'm okay dying a billion times from my mistakes but I'm not okay with dying and being punished for what feels like jank. I would say if you're a fan of difficult games in the vein of Hotline Miami, have a love for the Cyberpunk setting and do not mind some degree of jank, I would recommend this.EDIT: After beating the game the replay value greatly diminishes as input bugs occur. If you restart a level the "R" key no longer works. Making it impossible to reset without quitting the game, this combined with the severe clipping I experience in the final Cyber Void level in which the game forces you to rely on it's janky mechanics makes this a wait until it's on sale. EDIT Since Update: Everything has been tuned and playing it from the beginning the wallrunning seems a lot more tuned and the input bug is fixed. 9 Mountain Dews out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: Did you like Mirror's Edge? Do you like samurai swords? Do you like cyberpunk settings? Do you like all damn three of them?! If so, you've come to the right place, as that's what Ghostrunner is!You will die. A LOT. But it's so rewarding once you complete a combat/puzzle/jump section that you won't mind. Plus, the game is so fast and smooth (including reloading after death) that there's no wait time at all. Honestly, never a more optimised game of this calibre have I ever played.I can highly recommend Ghostrunner for the above. The only downside is that the plot, whilst welcome, is predictable and minimal. It doesn't drive the gameplay, it's just sort of...there.

_childDocuments_.review: You all remember Titanfall 2, right? No? You don't? Alright, go buy that too. What this game does, is take what made being a pilot in Titanfall 2 so satisfying in idea (going fast, hitting hard, and being a complete badass with enough practice) and turned it into its own game. Ghostrunner is exactly the kind of challenge that Dark Souls players love in the format of Doom (Eternal more than 2016) with the beauty and crispness of the most triple A game you can think of. If you recognize any of the titles I have listed, This Game Is For You. If you didn't, you should consider giving it a try anyway because the way the game teaches you is so seamless that it won't feel like you are working at all. Just, Having, Fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostrunner is a great game. Took me about 7 hours to finish the story so it isn't super long but I would say it is a good length, since you are suppose to replay levels to improve your time and stuff so in the end you can spend a lot of time in the game. Speaking of story it isn't anything great but if you come in to this game expecting a good story then you picked the wrong game. It is all about that sweet gameplay, which is really fun.Pros:+ Very satisfying game when you nail your execution.+ Many enemy types+ Challenging+ Visuals+ Soundtrack, just listen to that banger.+ Performance is decent(most of the time).+ Cool abilities+ Fast equals fun!Cons:- Boss fights. First one being the best one in my opinion. Second was way too easy and the third one was just boring.- Story, predictable.- Rails can be a bit annoying at times, since you somehow don't always grab them.- Last level was a huge disappointment to me. I was expecting to truly put all the abilities and skills to the test. But it really didn't deliver that. Just wallrunning and dodging big ass orbs. Not a fun level at all, only level that made me feel a bit frustrated. Oh and the performance in this level was really bad for me. I usually had around 120fps in most levels but in this one my fps dropped down to 60s. This is not a level I wish to ever play again.- Some enemy types felt a bit annoying, but the ones that made me feel like that didn't show up too often.- Cooldown of abilities, because of this I rarely used abilities which is a real shame. I pretty much only used Tempest since there is an upgrade for it that resets the cooldown if you kill more than 1 enemy with it. Really strong. Overall I had a great experience with the game. It might look like there are many cons but these are minor things in my opinion. Well most of them.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostrunner is a game set in the far future with a cyberpunk theme to it. You play as the Ghostrunner a cybernetic killer ninja with only a few weapons in your arsenal. A sword, a few abilities, and agility.You are immediately thrust into the game and taught the basics of what you need to do to be an efficient murderous cybernetic ninja. Though the walking does feel incredibly slow which caught me off guard as I went into this with the assumption that this is a fast-paced game, I was immediately corrected as you learn your movements, you get your speed from various interactions such as wall running, sliding and dashing which gives you that feeling of speed.About halfway into the game, you get a solid grasp and understanding of what you're playing. It's a trial and error game where you go into a section and die repeatedly until you perfect it and figure out how to kill everyone and get through it smoothly, quickly, and efficiently all in one fell swoop. Completing sections feels incredibly satisfying as you go through them untouched and killing everyone in what feels like an effortless manner.After having beat the game you'd have fully unlocked your arsenal and reached your peak in the game. From there you can replay the game for any secrets you have missed or hidden swords to gather.Ghostrunner is a good game but it is far from being perfect. It has a few flaws that do add up starting with its puzzle sections in between the action. - The puzzles are incredibly boring and uninspiring and felt like they take away from the game. - The abilities are far too overpowered and can make sections of the game far easier and in turn much less fun.- The plot for Ghostrunner is incredibly boring with forgettable characters, it is very predictable and uninspiring.- The game is very short, I personally have beaten the main game and Project_Hel campaign within only 7 hours of playtime if not less.The game is very fun however the mentioned flaws take away from the game.I recommend getting the game and the Project_Hel DLC when it is on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostrunner is a rhythm game with the most unclear and unpredictable judgement line I've ever seen.Die, repeat your actions, randomly enemies behave differently.Your hitbox is as wide as three men and you always die in one hit.Even the platforming controls are variable based on angle of approach, mantling (or more like... mostly never mantling), deflections and angles can be aimed but its not easy when every enemy can prefire you.Later they introduce melee units that would have been far more forgiving to start off against, as they are actually negligible unless paired with an enemy who can shoot.I was going to push myself through to the campaign's end, but the game is mechancially too frustrating for me to bother.In terms of other aspects: graphics look great, framerates are great, soundtrack is OK but not stellar, story is typical low-grade cyberpunk garbage that I'd be shocked if anyone actually cared about.

_childDocuments_.review: The story is pretty basic and predictable but interesting enough not to bore. Very fluid and reactive combat that is only improved with additions to new types of enemies and new skills to keep things fresh. Only problem I have with combat is that there is potential to abuse game mechanics through the sensory boost (slow time) but if you want a challenge yourself you wont use this as often as you could. Unrestricted parkour that allows for use in combat and maneuvering throughout the world. Even after beating the game I found myself still enjoying the combat as well as collecting all the skins for the sword, also you can clearly tell the devs designed this game for speed-running as the time for completing each level is recorded which makes for a fun time trying to clear a room as quickly as possible. While the content is a little lacking outside of beating the game the combat is incredibly fun and if you are a person who likes beating levels as fast as possible then i can highly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, fast paced and super satisfying when you string together enemies in that punishing combo. Game can be tedious in some portions but overall the 1 hit death/kill mechanic forces players to keep on the move and stay one step ahead of their enemy. Campaign is somewhat reasonable length, 6-8 hours but due to the fast paced gameplay it feels like enough but would've been better if it had a few more hours in it. The final boss was a bit eh, would I call it a boss? Probably not. Soundtrack is awesome, as well as the overall game aesthetic. Cyberpunk ninja whats not to love? Would love additional content like Challenges/endless modes/DLC/PvP or maybe even custom maps. Game being purely a campaign/story with only level select replayability could be considered lacking. Considering the studio/team that put this game together, well worth the money and a great singleplayer experience.
