_childDocuments_.review: Ghostrunner is a first person platformer/melee combat game with a great concept and fun core mechanics, however it is let down by a few poor design decisions, poor boss fights and some inconsistencies that add a lot of frustration.First the good!-Movement feels great-When it flows, combat feels amazing-Good enemy variety-Beautiful graphics-Interesting story that kept me engagedNow I would love to recommend the game, but a fair few issues have sapped away my enthusiasm for it and are significant enough problems that it stopped me from wanting to finish the last few levelsThe Bad-Common missed mouse inputs meant that I often died due to the game not registering an attack or grapple.-Boss fights are mostly pretty bad, with TOM being a solid idea that just needed to be toned down or placed later in the game, while Hel was a boring as heck boss involving spamming the parry/attack button til you learn her weird patterns, after which you just stand infront of her, parry til you get to hit her once, then chase after her 3 more times.-Later enemy types completely kill the game's flow by forcing yo u to stand still to parry or run away til they explode, neither of which works well with the game's idea of constant movement flow to survive.In conclusion, I want to recommend this game once the input bugs are fixed, but there's still significant issues that just made me give up by the end.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: - fast paced- high risk ( you die from one shot)- a beautiful world and world-building- fluid gameplay - there are many different approaches to levels- variety in level design (it doesnt feel monotonous)- Has a decent story (not mindblowing just ok )- Well executed boss fights (there is emphasis on movement and parkour for most bossfights except maybe Hel) Cons:- dialogues feel off sometimes- the parkour isnt challenging ( it would have been better if there were difficult to reach places to challenge your parkour skills)- levels rarely challenge your parkour skills (to beat a level you need to just find the right path and use the correct abilities. The parkour skill requirements are low)All in all, this game is very fun and you wont feel burned out from it due to the  large variety of playstyles.  I just picked up GR2 on sale and i hope its as good as its predecessor.Score: 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Let's see:Graphics? Check, state of the art, cyberpunky, high fidelity, no complaints.Sound? Satisfying and impactful, and whilst the music isn't too varied, the themes fit the game and don'T become too repetitive. Though having to jump off-rhythm made some passages of the game harder.Story? Nothing extravagant, but adequate and interesting. Very good pacing for the exposition.Gameplay? Spot on. A tough first-person-platformer, where combat is mostly about positioning and timing, and both platforming and combat levels feel adequately satisfying to beat (after several dozen deaths each).Bonus shout-out to the skill upgrade system: Instead of experience or levels you gain slots on a small grid by progressing through the game, and then get to install upgrades of your chosing (always freely replaceable in an instant) on that grid. The gimmick: Upgrades have specific forms and thus the number of upgrades you can install at once is essentially limited by your progress int he game (grid size) and your ability at playing Tetris. I got to point out most of the upgrades don't make a big impact on the gameplay, since you'll be clearing most of obstacles (be it enemies or platforms) with your default move- and skillset.. but it's a nice touch.Now, does this game have downsides?I would label 3 issues I have with the game here:1. The game is short. Check my timer, 6 hours to completion. And whilst I could now replay levels to find all goodies (mostly sword skins and some random items / sound files that provide a bit more background lore), that's about the extent of the replayability. Oh, and speedrunning, I suppose. But since neither of that attracts me, 6 hours (of good entertainment!) is what I got out of the game. And maybe I'll replay it in a year or two, who knows. (Note that I still value a good, short game over a mediocre, long one, but I feel like a 6 hour playtime is an important factor to list in a review).2. Difficulty. Don't get me wrong, I enjoyed the game, both the highs of being an unstoppable cyber ninja, and the downs of dieing (and this is the exact number the game provided me after level completion)  times to the same platforming boss (you'll know which I mean when you encounter it). But the game IS tough. And there isn't a difficulty slider because, frankly, there's no real way to make the tightly knit platforming "relevantly easier". As well, there's only minimal degrees of tutorial/instruction, primarily when you gain new skills, and figuring out efficient ways to traverse obstacles, and how to defeat certain enemies, is all left to the player. I liked the challenge, but I feel like I should mention it in this review as a relevant point.(3. Technically not within the game, so you're free to put parenthesis around this point: Don't bother with the steam community forum. It's a hellhole of Elitist thinking that is very pronounced due to the game's difficulty, and insults anyone asking for advice with either 'git gud' or 'fake gamer'. If you aren't here for the community aspect anyways, this point is probably irrelevant for you.)Overall, I'll rate this game a8.5/10Solid gameplay that delivers exactly what's on the label, at a tough, but not nailbitingly-tough difficulty, with the only serious issue being that of length and replayability. (And whilst the game is solid, there's nothing that really marked it as outstanding to me, so take that for what you will.)I can't recommend this game to EVERYONE, but if you like platformers, or generally difficult games, and don't have to limit yourself to great $-to-h ratios, this game will not disappoint you.

_childDocuments_.review: The setting is just picture-perfect. The music, feel, and overall vibe is phenomenal.  Gameplay is frenetic and challenging but never, ever feels ridiculous or unfair. The tools are all there and restarting a tricky area is immediate, which is crucial for this type of gameplay.  Far too many games with challenging platforming or combat sections make the player wait FAR too long to retry an area they struggled with, leading to frustration and eventually giving up on the game.  Ghostrunner understands the importance of mitigating that frustration by immediately restarting you right where you died or screwed up.  Graphics and music are very well done and the feel of the movement and sword combat is tight, responsive, and exhilarating quite often. Just an excellent game all around.  I can't wait to play the new one.

_childDocuments_.review: COOL GAME AND IDEAS BUT NEEDED SOME MORE POLISH. TRY BEFORE YOU BUY! LAME FINAL ACT. Dear god, I WANTED to love this game I really did! But after putting in the time to actually PLAY it I...just can't recommend this to anyone as if (tho I do think it's mostly great and worth playing once fore sure). The style is fantastic, the music is spot on and the visual design is something else (it is SO COOL!). My praise doesn't end there either, a big chunk of this game is all about speed, precision and one life hard mode and I get it... I just wish the major problems had been ironed out more because it was borderline unfinishable for me (I actually don't even know HOW I managed to beat the end bit but I will get into that further down).So let's get the story out of the way... it was fine. I wish we could have played through the intro bit instead of a cutscene but it was fun none the less.  Some of the lore bits were neat and they did a great job at making a dirty, lived in world that has the after burn of the tech of the future installed within it's walls. Neat stuff. Now for some specific issues that make me give it a unfortunate thumbs down (Spoiler warning) :- What is up with the jump pads? SOMETIMES they send you in roughly the right direction, sometimes they don't even register your input and you just roll right off, some times you are flung into space (don't think these were balanced/tested enough and it makes the game suffer for it) - Combat is good and all but Enemy AI can certainly have advantages such as perfectly nailing me with a shot BEFORE I have ANY chance to even react at all as a round a corner. I understand the game being difficult and all but there is a difference between "man this is a tough challenge" to "oh the AI just knows my every move at all times" and the latter ISN'T fun at all. - The game demands precision for the wall running and dashes but doesn't always up hold it's end of the bargain. Don't ask me to be pixel perfect if your wall detection is sub par and gets confused on if i am touching the wall at all half the time. - This issue is continued with the grapple points, being in line of sight is one thing, being in range is another thing, being in both and the grapple decided you AREN'T WORTHY to grapple mid animation and kills you instantly? Bad design! - Had a glitch where the little runner dudes that explode (whatever they are called) would just not explode? Like they just kept infinity chasing me until they touched me and I instantly die without them exploding apparently so no clue what was up with that.  With the smaller things out of the way, there were two more major issues I had with the game over all:The first boss had me soft locked for a little while (I had to look it up so I know it wasn't just me being awful). You start the fight dogging the laser waves as you climb up to cut the wires. This was crazy but kind of fun honestly, I really enjoyed it after figuring out the pattern. My problem came once you hit phase 2 and you have to climb back up by wall running and hook shooting. See the first couple of walls have a pattern because of the fire pouring up so you jump between while you continue to climb.The very next part where the fire branches up more had me actually soft locked for half an hour.  You have to do the same thing again, but this time you start on a platform so you can get a hang of the timing first. I must have died in a weird way getting to that point, cause every time I tried to climb and start wall running I would die without even being near the fire! I kept running into this issue until I just restarted the entire fight. That is a bad sign in a boss fight when you can end up in a broken loop and don't even know how you got there. My other issue was the ending, the fight with MARA is fine and all but the voice work needed another pass for sure, it sounded like test audio but was a surprisingly easy fight.  My real issue was with the "second" boss in virtual space. What should have been an epic final bit was paced super poorly, (I died a bunch on the FIRST PART because it was just too fast to make it across) then you throw in all the wall jank from before with detection problems and launchpads not working right, and it took me FOUR hours! FOUR HOURS to do 3 sections!  - The first part is too fast! Pace is just super weird (like it was too slow before so they sped it up but didn't test to see if it felt right?- The wall ruining only half worked most of the time due to the game having trouble with me and walls- Once the red orbs are introduced good luck getting a feel for what your hit-box is because if you even SNEEZE towards them you die- You don't even get all the story until the last ten minutes of the game where it's all crammed in there and you don't even fight the second "villain"- Despite defaulting to the highest settings and having NO ISSUES at ANY other point, the game crashed TWICE towards the end for me This game has a cool look and cool ideas but is plagued by a few SERIOUS technical problems that really limit the enjoyment. If you want a "constant reset till you get it perfect" kind of experience then go for it! The game has a demo so PLEASE try that first to see if it's for you! I loved most of this and I honestly think the devs put in good work just not enough were it was needed most (I'm not saying it's all on them I;m sure they had time limits and what not but still). I hope the sequel fixed all of this and refined it into something amazing cause then I will jump on it for sure!

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't sure whether to recommend or not recommend this game, but I settled on recommending it. I think the core idea is good but I don't think the execution is for me.Here are some reasons why:- For context, the default mode you play through first is where you slowly unlock upgrades and abilities as you play, and took me around 4 or 4.5 hours, and I'm going to be basing all of these comments around the "standard mode".- The core gameplay loop is really great actually. The main problem I have is that so much stuff is locked from the start and you have to unlock it. Since the game might only take someone like 4 or so hours, most of the game you likely don't even have some of your "fun" abilities. It is inexcusable that things like dashing twice or reflecting projectiles are upgrades you have to allot space for. Them not being unlocked at all times feels like a cop-out from the developers to give a false sense of progression at the cost of making it less fun- I actually sometimes found myself fighting the controls. The two main examples I have are that dashing + time-slow-motion-in-midair are the same button. If you are someone who is a little sloppy with their keypresses (i.e. maybe hold down a button for slightly too long), this can actually result in your character doing something you didn't intend, solely because by default those two completely separate things are the same key. The other example I have is, while I very much enjoy the wallrunning aspect, the developers in my opinion did a really poor job with making the levels actually nicely traversable. That's not to say it was difficult, but that on some walls if you find yourself running against them, you will just start running into things and getting stuck. I realize that the intention was to only wall run in specific parts, but it seems like a huge missed opportunity to not let the player have more of a choice in how they play.- Some of the hits that enemies are able to get on you are kind of ridiculous. For instance, one of the common enemy types carries a sword around, and they lunge at you. This is all well and good, however if they swing a sword *somewhat close* to you, you can die, even if there's no reason it should have hit you. This actually happens with a few different types of enemies. I guess this is sort of balanced by enemies having very generous hitboxes when you go to attack them, but frankly even though that's the case, it feels unfair, and I would prefer both were just realistically small.- Some of the enemy designs are just absolutely ridiculous and run counter to how the developers seemingly want you to play the game, especially depending on what upgrades you have selected. The most egregious instance is, there is an enemy (I think the last one introduced) that runs at you and suicide-bombs. The problem is that the way you handle this enemy is so different from every other enemy, you end up having to completely shift gears on how you play the game (in a very much less fun way), in order to not die.- As said above, the core game (not including challenges or "hardcore mode" is only like 4 or so hours). I would much prefer them to have spent time making a solid 7 or so hour game, rather than the "package" being that you are allowed to replay the same game/levels in a few slightly different ways. (This doesn't even count that some levels have incredibly long boring platforming sections that also feel like padding). This yet again feels like a cop-out by the developers to just make less game and package it as more than it really is.I know in my points it seems like I'm trashing it, but I really do enjoy the core game, and I think a certain type of person that likes the constant replaying to perfect the levels, it will very much appeal to them. However, to me personally, I was left wanting a bit more

_childDocuments_.review: I have something of a love/hate relationship with  (GR) in that there's a certain groove that is indescribably rewarding when it's all clicking. I was a big fan of the  games because the focus on chaining together different moves to find the most fluid path from point A to point B was both relaxing and oddly rewarding. But I think GR is a much less forgiving game by any measure and devolves into frustration pretty quickly when it gives you so little clue as to what to do and understates what it does tell you.For example, the opening sequences teach you only the most very basics in a very minimalist way. When in reality that first time-distorting move you learn (pressing the 'Shift' key on a PC keyboard) is pretty much  move you will master or die endlessly. And there are many subtleties to its use, as there are to virtually every seemingly simple move: wall-running, jumping, dodging, you name it. I found some of it immediately intuitive, but I really had to work to figure out some of the intricacies.I've had that same feeling multiple times as I work my way through the game too, encountering some new thing that doesn't work like anything else I've seen. I'm sure I could probably just do a quick web search or look on YouTube and watch somebody else solve it for me, but I don't want to do that. Some of these things are pretty tricky. Some of the "puzzle" levels are downright incoherent and illogical and deliberately so. I've made it roughly halfway through the game now after about eleven hours of play, and in part that's because I had to beat my head against certain sections  of times before I could figure out what to do. GR is consistently amazing how it adds something entirely novel into the mix that often makes the situation seem completely impossible at first, yet then by the end of that same level you've been forced to adapt to the point where it's just another voice in the mix.I also cannot overstate the degree to which changing up your load out and using different skills can completely change the feel of the game. There was one section in particular where I kept dying to the same trio of enemies. No matter what order I tried to take them in they shot me in the air every time. I couldn't find any way to deal with them and gave up more than once before cooling down and coming back to it. But then I went looking through my load out and tried a skill that let me reflect projectiles: the impossible situation almost immediately became trivially simple. I could easily murder two out of the three foes with their own fire!Not long after I unlocked the "blink" ability, and now I've more recently unlocked "tempest", and they lend themselves to  different styles of play. And that's a good thing given some of the much harder enemies that appear by the time you're halfway into the game. I don't want to spoil much of anything, but there are some tricky environmental bits and a few outright slaughterhouses you're going to be forced to endure, death after death until you find the way.So here's the thing. I'm at the point in life where I have very little time to play anything, so when I do sit down to play I want to have fun. I don't usually find very punishing games fun because they require a skill level that my responsibilities will simply never allow, so they're the kind of thing I try and usually refund or walk away from pretty quickly. And yet despite how punishing GR is, and how "cheap" some of the deaths and last-minute architectural stumbling blocks are in some maps, . And while I'm improving slower than I'd like, I am still improving. I think that says something about it.Unfortunately, I don't know how much more I'm going to get out of it. I've run into the first real "boss", and it's completely ridiculous garbage. I don't believe there is  level of skill that makes it possible to navigate that absolute crap-fest without hundreds of pointless, repetitive, deaths--and that assumes you don't stroke out completely from epilepsy given what's on the screen at that point. There are boss fights that are hard. Difficult. Punishing. But this might as well be labelled "Push Buttons 1,000 Times In Sequence Properly With Blind Luck". Having said that, I don't want to leave my review at that point. The game also deserves huge credit for its fantastic visuals, perfect audio, style, controls, etc. It is truly a pleasure to play in all its basic mechanics and presentation values. There's so much I like about it, I find it frustrating that I've made it to a certain point, and there's essentially no way I will ever make it any further. There is no amount of patience or improvement or anything but goodness knows how many hours of blind trial and error that will  get me through the next level.In short, if you're easily frustrated, this game is probably not for you. But if you're more like me, I think you'll easily get your money's worth out of the game, even if you don't finish it. I've enjoyed my time enough with it to be happy I've bought it. I just wish it didn't involve such ridiculous nonsense at points.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostrunner is a first-person action game set in a cyberpunk world with movement mechanics similar to Titanfall and the difficulty and gameplay style of Hotline Miami. And let me just start by saying I absolutely loved those games and I enjoy a cyberpunk setting so I definitely had a good time with this. That's not to say there is nothing to fault here and I will definitely point it out. But this was such an enjoyable game even with its downsides, that I ended up playing through twice. So, let's cut deeper into the game.  You start out with an opening cutscene as the Ghostrunner is slicing his way through a handful of enemies to get to female cyberpunk Doc Ock (Mara). For her to deactivate, rip off his arm, and throw him out of a building. You then wake up at the bottom of the tower without any recollection of your past, and guided by a voice in your head begin your ascent up the tower to take Mara down as you decapitate 100s of enemies on your journey.  Honestly, who cares about the plot? I didn't. Yes, while there is a story to it. It is pretty uninteresting and predictable. What I think is good though is that the storytelling is actually done through characters conversing in Ghostrunner's head. So, for those that are like me and just want to get straight to the combat and platforming are able to do so uninterrupted without cutscenes breaking up the flow. However, if you like to hear the nuances of the story you can still listen, take your time and look around.  The gameplay on the other hand is what I was more interested in and is definitely the highlight of the entire game. It consists of about 45% fast-paced combat, 45% fluid platforming and 10% boring cybervoid levels. Overall, the gameplay was a blast to play, it was full of variety and never felt stale, minus the cybervoid.  In combat you will be using your katana to slice-and-dice your way through enemies, all while wall running, dashing, sliding, grappling and using abilities. The difficulty is quite brutal and involves a one-hit kill mechanic for both yourself and enemies, similar to Hotline Miami. So, if the thought of having to repeatedly go through the same section while trying to clear it flawlessly makes you want to hit your head against a wall, then maybe steer clear of this. But if you are a bit of masochist then I'm sure you'll enjoy it. And once you do begin to master the mechanics and begin to flow seamlessly between kills it becomes satisfying as "H-E-double-katana-blades". Apart from your trusty sword, you have four different abilities to help which include: Blink, Tempest, Surge and Overlord. Blink is your simple dash attack, line up a few enemies and slice through them all. Tempest is best described as a force push, but instead of channeling mysterious spiritual energy, it's caused by rapid micro vibrations in your inner hydraulics... Um, what? Sure, sounds just as magical. Surge is your ranged attack, it'll allow you to swing your sword and emit an energy blast at enemies. And Overlord allows you to hack into the brains of enemies, turning them against each other. These abilities could have been implemented better, they feel more like an afterthought and I mainly used them for style points to make myself feel more bad-ass. For example, in the tutorial for Blink and Surge they have enemies conveniently line up for you, but this rarely happens in actual combat. There are a variety of enemies which range from pistol wielders, shields, katana wielders and more including those god awful creepy explodey dudes. It's great that they are constantly introducing these different enemies to you, just when I thought I had mastered one particular type I am thrown against a new enemy with different mechanics that required me to adapt my playstyle. Yet it never felt like I was out of my depth, they ease you into each by placing you against a single enemy allowing you to familiarise yourself with them, then increasing their numbers and finally incorporating them into a big section with all different sorts of enemies, all requiring different approaches.  Boss fights were ... decent, the problem with them is that since you die in one-hit you are only able to learn a little bit more on each attempt which can lead to a frustrating time. And, I think I have "Welcome to Amida Elevator Station" permanently imprinted in my mind now. The platforming takes up the rest of the gameplay and it is a challenging, fluid and fun experience ... when it works. A few times I noticed that the Ghostrunner's feet wouldn't "attach" on the wall as I tried to initiate a wall run or sometimes the grapple left me just short of the intended location. However, I will note that the platforming sections aren't jarring and don't feel out of place, the neon billboards, conveyer belts, hooks, fans all make sense given the surrounding environment. What absolutely hurts the game however is the cybervoid sections where you gain and learn your abilities, these levels just completely break the flow of the fast-paced game with these slow, drawn out platforming sections while you collect cubes, solve puzzles or wait for platforms. I would've preferred if there was more combat/platforming and the abilities were introduced through other means, perhaps an enemy/boss could have utilised an ability and once defeated the Ghostrunner was able to take out a chip to obtain that ability.   It's your typical cyberpunk dystopian future with bright neon signs, streets littered with rubbish and rain, of course. The game looks gorgeous especially in the later levels as you progress through the city and it really showcases some stunning visuals and atmosphere. The environments are incredibly polished with a high level of detail to make a pretty immersive world.  The music brings in some synthwave goodness that just adds and accentuates the thrilling gameplay, very much like in Hotline Miami. My friend likes to troll me constantly because I talk up game soundtracks that I enjoy a lot, but you know what I'll happily take all the jokes to promote this OST. Apart from that the rest of the sound design is decent and serviceable, voice acting is done well and the sounds of combat, like the impact from the sword and abilities are satisfying.  In conclusion, I had a great time with this game, it filled that void of Cyberpunk 2077 delay disappointment and scratched that Hotline Miami itch. There are certainly some shortcomings in this game and I can't see everyone enjoying this game but if you are a wanting a first-person, fast-paced game with a high difficulty and don't mind repeating sections to perfect them then I would definitely recommend this. And I challenge anyone to attempt a full deathless run. Good luck! If you enjoyed my review and like to see more like this, you can follow me at my curator page, .

_childDocuments_.review: I had Mirrors Edge on console and it was more fluid than this.Things that break the flow of the movement;1) The rails that you grab onto (think bioshock infinite) if you are going down a decline and you look behind you it throws you off and back on a few times which is glitchy because it doesn't do that mid rail (I know this because I found it found to jump 180 mid rail but to my surprise doing it at the end of the rail bugs it out.2) Crouch slide over the hazards can be unreliable, setting this to toggle sort of fixed my problems? But I don't like toggle but it was the only way to make it reliable3) Jumping doesn't feel like it has enough velocity and is unreliable ... to get more velocity you're usually better off dashing before the edge of a platform and then spamming jump and dash again which yet again sometimes doesn't work, logical thinking you'd want to jump off first and then dash mid air but that seems to be even less reliable compared to dashing off first.4) Dashing between quick successions of vertical walls on opposing sides is really bad ... (think left, right, left, right, left, right) It becomes even more painful to bear near the end of the game, the way around this is you have to look slightly upwards and pray that you'll land slightly higher than before otherwise you'll drop off and not reach the next vertical platform to wall run onto ... easy fix would be to increase velocity and distance of the dashes or if that would break a lot of levels perhaps have it so that when you wall run you can control going up or down the wall depending on where you look that way the rest of the levels wouldn't need tweaking and it would be an almost seamless fix.5) Exploding enemies AKA Gremlins? the bomb on their back glows brighter the moment before they explode except ... sometimes they don't have visuals to show any glow at all on rare occasions and sometimes the glow from the bomb doesn't change and they just explode!6) Parry ... this game slaps you in the face and teaches you to parry wrong for the first half of the game, you can parry projectiles from enemies (the enemies for the first half of the game that is lol) then you fight a boss and you can parry the attacks from the boss but the problem is if you parry normally the boss will be invincible so instead you have to parry at the very last second otherwise it doesn't count properly??? No joke it changes the rules of parry for this one boss until you brute force yourself to unlearn all the muscle memory you've developed so far (if you're a person who parries early) and then parrying bullets feels weird after that boss fight so you have to unlearn the 'late' parry ... But wait there's more! There is a Moa/bipedal type enemy that has a wide laser burst that I was able to parry 2/5 of my first attempts and then I thought "cool I'll learn the timing of this" but I died about 50 times trying to get the timing down and have never successfully been able to parry that 'Moa' again so I'm assuming it was a glitch during the first encounter? I'm certain that this Moa parry was a glitch because later there are even more enemy types with projectiles that can't be parried, but the ones that you are introduced to for the first half of the game can still be successfully parried every time.-Final thoughts?I wanted to enjoy this game but felt like I had to force myself to compensate for the bad mechanics here and there, it needs more polish other than that I had fun but the inconsistencies really ruined the fun for me. I wanted to finish the game properly to write a in depth review for anybody else that really enjoyed Mirrors Edge and was hoping for something similar ... in my opinion stay away from this game until you see some sort of patch that fixes the issues I've mentioned if you want to play this game more than the one time.I'm the type of person when a game has very good fluid free running mechanics I'll play it over and over and over and if I make a mistake I can wear it as my own fault that isn't the case with this game from my experience at the time of writing this review. Another suggestion would be to have some sort of endless combat mode with procedurally generated levelsMaybe just really well designed endless combat levels or maybe a map maker tool in game where people can share their maps on the steam workshop? That would be awesome!

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostrunner is the most awaited game of the year in the genre of first-person runner game. It is going to change the graphics industry forever. It provides a sufficient length of content with varying levels. This fast-paced action with violent combat is a full package challenging experience. You will run on walls, grapple towers, slice enemies, use abilities, and encounter punishing bosses. The devs clearly mentioned that Ghostrunner mainly targets the hardcore audience, but don’t feel too stressed as there are enough checkpoints to keep you engaged in the game. The entire game follows the principle of single swing kill, following with one hit death too. The AI is pretty smart and ferocious, making the game a treat for speedrunners. Sweet Cyberpunk theme track is just a cherry on top.There are many more promising segments that the game offers apart from the basic hack and slash genre. It’s a complete package of astonishing visuals with great level designing. You play as a Ghostrunner who exhibits magnificent speed, accuracy, and strength. Your aim is to eliminate Mara, who holds tyranny over people living in Dharma city. As the land is hit with a world-ending cataclysm, it bounded them to stay in the tower, and now they require your help to fight back for survival. The narration in the game feels like a filler segment. It executes most of the focus on controls and challenges. Story and narration are just added for the sake of giving gamers a motive to continue.During the well-made tutorial, you will learn the basic controls/mechanics of the game. You will duck, slide, wall run, jump, strafe, kill, and whatnot. The game allows you to feel like a free runner with its easy to remember controls. You will fail multiple times, but each failure is an experience that will increase the satisfaction level on completing a level. A lot of levels will have various ways of completion, so it’s up to you how you synchronize the situation and execute the plan. The only right way is - where you are not dead. Because of the pre-determined jumps and strafes, you will need to calculate your movements beforehand. You will encounter a lot of frustrating moments that will make you want to quit, but that’s what the challenge is meant to exhibit. A wide variety of enemies, ranging from shooters, crawlers, hostile melee, fearless ninjas, and laser shooting mech keeps the difficulty fresh. And of course, 3 ferocious bosses that will give you a hard time.Along with brand new segments like magnetic zipline and deflecting bullets, you will also learn abilities ranging from slowing time, cutting through enemies, or delivering an energy wave. You can also hack objects and change their directions or make it appear fully to use it for a wall run. Sometimes you will have to quickly throw ninja stars at power plates to open a door and dash through it before it closes. The sole purpose of the game is to keep you engaged for as much time as possible. Each level also contains unique collectibles like artifacts, audio logs, and swords to provide a small reward to players. Hands down, Ghostrunner has the best graphics available in the market alongside cyberpunk 2077. According to the released graphic requirements, it should work on a medium rig too, which is a huge plus point for any game franchise. Each corner of the game is highly detailed and stays tip-top all around the game. It’s a pleasing experience with an astounding cyberpunk theme and polished character modeling. The player will experience well-made animations ranging from slicing enemies, grappling hooks, deadly lasers, and a lot of body dissecting gore. Unlike other games, the map elements are not just go-through objects. They are actually present there and can interact with your character. Each level has a distinct set of vivid colors, which makes the game highly pleasing. Luminous maps keep your visibility high at every corner. Other than the hardcore levels, you will also encounter some soft parkour map with an abstract environment. Prefer mouse and keyboard for this game because of the high accuracy requirement. Don’t quit if you die multiple times, as it takes time to get a hold of the gameplay. You can re-run any levels and use map upgrades to locate collectibles on the radar. The game allows you to assemble skill upgrades in a Tetris theme layout. As you will unlock more levels, you can fit more blocks over time. The game features 3 hardcore tough bosses ranging from laser tower, hostile ninja, and multiple arms kill machine. The devs made sure the difficulty of bosses remains essential, even with one hit kill ideology.If you think campaign isn't challenging enough, then how about a time trial mode for exclusive skins? But only the best of the best can survive. Kill the enemies and earn medals, and during this madness, how about taking your time and start photo mode to capture the beautiful scenery?This easily attains the spot for “Game of the year” nomination. Smooth gameplay, action-packed runs, astonishing graphics, and numerous levels enhancing your gaming experience. We are curious to see some speedruns over this beautiful game experience. Claim each checkpoint and save the Dharma city!Rating: 9.5/10Ghostrunner #69.

_childDocuments_.review: "Make no mistake, this fight won’t be easy. But at least it will be fair."- Architect With numerous developers showcasing their vision through various game iterations, the cyberpunk genre has recently attracted a lot of attention. However, nobody has ever made a quick-paced neon-platformer that would live up to the fantasy of becoming a cyborg killing machine. For our benefit, Polish ingenuity has once more shattered the bigger scenes by releasing Ghostrunner, a superb platforming experience. Dharma Tower: the future of humanity’s survival is sheltered inside this vast skyscraper. Yet in the backbones of this ambitious construct lies a deeper purpose, a deeper meaning shattered and twisted by people valuing their own progress by any means. The Ghost Runner protocol was made in hopes of countering such inadequacies in the system—a sort of firewall that would protect Dharma and its citizens from harm. Only one remains! Its mission? Kill the Keymaster… In contrast to its more sophisticated gameplay approach, the main plot is very straightforward. You are the last surviving Ghostrunner, and your main objective is to bring back order. With no recollection of previous events, the game's linear structure allows you to piece together its lore gradually, primarily through internal dialogue. Despite the fact that I find the presentation to be somewhat lacking, the plot is very promising, adding many layers of speculation that can personalise the experience. Sure, some things can become quite predictable, especially when the narrative cleverly hints at certain events, but overall, they fulfil their purpose by both setting the atmosphere and the tone without killing the mood.  The acrobatic routines and lethal manoeuvres serve as the foundation and the icing on the cake of the entire experience, making Ghostrunner unique despite its minimal storytelling. To put it lightly, combat shines like a bright star, and every detail surrounding it works according to the needs of the glorious dance of death.Dharma Tower is a maze full of obstacles that can become brutally unforgiving if you do not pay attention. The structures of every level are carefully placed in a way that encourages boldness, skill, and strategic thinking. There is more than one path to follow, each with different restrictions and difficulties. You may, for example, choose the safest approach that offers more cover but less fluidity or simply dash through the most challenging sections, which require fast movements and a little bit of luck. The tango of swords and slashes becomes even more difficult with the addition of a minor but significant mechanic: elegance. The game is about movement, and what a perfect way to encourage platforming precision when there is a sense of danger in the mix! Ghostrunner is extremely fragile, as even one hit can lead to his demise. Consequently, the high-reward encounters become even more satisfying, and every section feels tense. Fortunately, should you screw up that one jump that could lead to a perfect execution, the game blesses your soul with frequent checkpoints and almost negligible loading times. Death is, after all, a frustrating yet fundamental loop. If you want to overcome it, you need to embrace it. In hopes of balancing the learning curve, the game slowly introduces new enemy variants. The higher you climb the Dharma Tower, the stronger your adversaries become, with unique buffs and certain weaknesses that can be exploited. The most memorable of the bunch are the katana warriors, deadly henchmen trained in the ways of the sword, or the kamikaze spiders that explode the moment you enter their vicinity. Once you have gotten the hang of their attack patterns, the developers spice things up by adding even more variety, mainly through environment alteration. There are some sequences, for instance, where you need to navigate through moveable objects or time your jumps carefully since the interactable surfaces rotate ninety degrees every few seconds. On top of that, the Cybervoid was a very welcome addition to the flawless formula, where the player can experiment with different abilities and solve puzzles, all while helping the story and gameplay unfold. The only thing that I found extremely underwhelming were the boss fights (excluding the first one), as they become rather flat when you figure out their main mechanics.When the streets of this tower city are full of violence, the trusty sword is nothing more than a stick with a sharp edge. In order to even the odds, the Ghostrunner is equipped with special abilities that allow you to enrich your arsenal. On one hand, we have the in-game powerups that enhance your performance either by slowing time, offering a jump boost, or unlocking shurikens through which you can reach tough places. The permanent upgrades, on the other hand, come in the form of tetris-style blocks that can be arranged in a unique grid with constrained spaces. Every block is a different passive improvement, ranging from enabling the ability to deflect projectiles to adding an extra dash. Since you cannot possibly equip every available upgrade that you unlock automatically throughout your different runs and sessions, you need to prioritise certain builds that favour specific facets, as each amplifier can vastly alter your playstyle. While the premise opens the door to countless opportunities, its execution is beyond perfect. Even though Ghostrunner is a fast-paced game that heavily relies on pinpoint precision, sometimes it overwhelms itself and some carefully executed manoeuvres may not be rendered properly, leading to infuriating moments.For an indie studio of such scale, the visuals should be praised. The animations are fantastic, the graphics are stunning, and the overall combat feels satisfying. The sometimes colourful, sometimes grim dystopian ambiance will instantly itch that cyberpunk fanboy feeling as it checks every box on the wishlist. It is by far among the most trippy and engaging environments that I have ever witnessed, with many secrets and hidden areas to explore around every corner. There are numerous reasons to praise Ghostrunner; the audio direction is one of them. The electronic beats sprinkled with techno pieces add lots of charm to the environment that fits perfectly with the speed and power of the post-apocalyptic city. As far as voice acting is concerned, the Architect’s soothing voice and charming persona steal the spotlight. In hindsight, the audio approach provides some seriously excellent content, but it is nothing compared to the nearly flawless gameplay components. Ghostrunner is the pinnacle of fast-paced combat that stands out from the crowd thanks to its stunning visuals, excellent gameplay design, and beautiful soundtracks, making it a constant joy to play. It's the kind of experience that bridges the indie genre with many AAA mechanics that appear to work well within the cyberpunk framework. A punishing but fair adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: Movement-wise, this game is awesome.  You'll have no issues with trying to fight your character into doing what you tell him to do.  He moves like greased lightning and responds to input very, very well.Environmentally and aesthetically, this game is gorgeous.  From the textures, to the lighting, geometry, finer details, and so forth, this game is a slam dunk in the visual department.Oh and the audio is just... pristine.  The voice acting and sound effects are great, but that soundtrack is just... incredible.  Fans of cyberpunk/retrowave music NEED to at least check out this game's soundtrack.However, mechanically, the game has some issues.  Some really, really annoying issues that need to be fixed, that I can't reconcile until they are indeed fixed.  Let me preface my annoyance with the fact that this game is AWESOME.  But what I'm about to mention are issues that severely disrupt the game's flow.  Ghostrunner is clearly supposed to be a skill-based game that the player is expected to want keep coming back to in order to optimize his or her runs through each level.  In order for it to succeed at that, the following must be addressed:The timing and hit registration for your attacks against the melee enemy type (which is the latest enemy I've reached so far) is all over the place.  And that's really, really annoying, because you NEED good timing to reliably and consistently kill that enemy type.  But as it stands, sometimes you'll swing WAY too early and magically kill one while he's still over 20ft away from you, and other times that won't work at all.  Sometimes you can kill one by swinging when he gets real close, but other times you'll somehow miss and die, even with the same frame timing.  Considering you will very quickly be facing rooms containing 3 or more of these guys, in addition to multiple armed enemies, with shield buffs, you will very quickly get extremely frustrated as you keep getting killed by these enemies that you see coming at you, but you just have no means of judging and reliably landing attacks on.Beyond that, one of the game's biggest strengths - its tight movement and instant/buttonless/seamless wall snapping/running - ironically becomes a weakness in very specific areas.  Namely, the ones where you're in or at the end of a tight corridor, or sandwiched between 2+ walls, well above an enemy or group of enemies.  In these scenarios, you have to plummet down onto said enemies, while dodging their projectiles, and kill them.  Inherently, that sounds like a great combat layout.  But with so many walls so closeby, and such quick/seamless wall snapping baked into the controls, requiring no button input to do so, what happens is that you keep accidentally snapping to and running along walls as a result of you trying to dodge incoming projectiles.  You can't just plummet straight down, because you'll fall right into their bullets.  You have to shift and shimmy around mid-air, which inevitably just sends you into other walls.  There aren't THAT many spots where this is an issue, but where it is an issue, it's really annoying.I guess my complaints just stem from the fact that I want to get really into this game and master it, but I'm never going want to do that if the game has inconsistencies within some of its core mechanics, like hit registration.  Anything that disrupts the player's ability to reliably blast through a level on skill alone is bad, and that's what the 2 aforementioned problems are.  There is a TON of potential replay value here, much like how Portal has replay value.  Ghostrunner just needs to clean up these couple problems and it will be a thumbs up from me.

_childDocuments_.review: First big thanks to my buddy Chris for gifting me the game. This review would not be possible without him. Thanks my dude!Forbes called the game a mix of “Titanfall, Dishonored, and Superhot.” PC Gamer says it's in between “Mirror's Edge a nd Dishonored.” For me, add Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance to the above, and bam you have Ghostrunner. I’ve played all of those above ~~Well… Dishonored I still need to finish but that’s neither here nor there.~~After an assassination mission has gone wrong(You need to watch the intro cutscene starting before you reach the main menu to display a prologue of events. Kinda like Vagrant Story. Please don’t miss it.) You(Jack) are somehow alive and must climb Dharma Tower to defeat the Keymaster. A ruthless being ordering the people to work so hard, she’s milking them until they bleed while the rich stay rich. That’s the jist you need to know. Interesting companions here as you climb to the top. And honestly, it reminds me heavily of T2's structures where you’re not alone in your fight. Greatly enhancing my experience and making my main goal not so daunting anymore.Give me a sharp katana, good parkour, cyberpunk setting, and you have my attention. Ghostrunner(GR) embodies all these traits and I am extremely thrilled to report the sheer momentum of slashing unaware enemies is satisfying, movement feels smooth as my time in Titanfall 2(T2), and the story kept me intrigued. Teasing me with Alan Turing's ideas.Environments are plentiful here. Industrialized factories are knit tightly together with turbines and a hodgepodge that works of uneven steel apartment buildings littering areas to traverse as you hop around rooftops and swing about like Tarzan. Felt like I was back playing Cyberpunk 2077. The setting fits. Jumping from wall to wall as I collided past each billboard was not boring at all. Levels range from less than 5-10min to finish early on and can bloom to 30 minutes later on for those who check their surroundings carefully. These areas are carefully designed to induce almost an illusion to make you think they’re larger than intended despite following a linear path. Collectibles, tucked away in places you wouldn’t expect, reward those who search every nook and cranny and offer a nice blurb of lore exposition.Combat is the bread and butter here. You can’t shoot with a gun sadly, but who needs a gun when you have a katana that can delete your foes in a single blow? Parry this you filthy casual. If you are a master at parrying from a popular Souls franchise or katana-wielding games like Raiden from some dude named Kojima who created the Metal Gear series, you’ll thrive here. Unfortunately, I suck at parrying. And yet to my delight in GR, they're not super strict on windows to retaliate. Play a Tetris-like upgrade system and equip them. Some blocks increase your chances of reflecting an attack. Add another dash or blink, etc. Or activate more options in assist mode, I’ll touch on this later. Under the circumstances, a bumbling dude like me can turn the tide. Incredibly satisfying witnessing a gunner trying to shoot me only for me to pull a reverse uno with my sword and slap the projectile back! Hah! I think dying in one hit, as a rule, is a tricky feature for developers. Lean hard and players will think it's too punishing. Go too easy and breeze through like a cakewalk. Ghost of Tsushima and Superhot tread the fine line for better or worse. Thankfully, GR is smack dab on the edge of the better side. With Assist Mode, someone like me who sucks at intense action-packed titles can somehow become an expert. Consisting of three features: One extra life, the second a shorter cooldown to use abilities more, and slower gameplay speeds for more leeway in reacting. The mode single-handedly and substantially changed my experience as I sped through slicing and dicing. I was frowning heavily, during the early parts since I felt the difficulty was a bit too tough and challenging. Once I turned on some of those options my whole expression turned 180. I’m grinning like a loon and nodding my head to the beat of the music(composed by Daniel Deluxe, and man does his name roll off the tongue) where the rhythm and synth wave work in tandem to the combat. Creating a pleasant tempo to listen to throughout. I did feel some tracks were repetitive. Although, after re-listening to the OST it works in its favor. Offering systematic beats that feel familiar like a physical manifestation of your heart beating. Hm hm hm hm.Level design for the most part is solid to a degree, I find myself reminiscing about Mirror’s Edge and T2. Both employ excellent sequences using parkour and unique elements. By taking advantage of environment placement and visual hints. GR is much the same. There is a frenetic pace from which you slice, parry, dodge, and adjust your balance to the course of platforming segments. Not too large and not too small either. Designed well to keep you focused, without throwing a hard curveball in your direction. The checkpoint system is very fair and respawning instant. I also love how wall running is slighter better here than in T2. Over there, I can wall-run until I petered out in the end. Here, I can continue forever. Moving on. I have to talk about my mixed feelings. Not a positive or a negative. But for the sake of transparency, I'm noting them down. More often than not, I am blocked by forced enemy encounters in some sections. These encounters require me to beat a variety of enemies before I can progress. I don’t like this method, because it enforces a design to halt pacing and force players to eliminate everyone within a room or decently open-sized areas. Fighting through trial and error until you get it right. And while this is a fine idea in theory, the execution leaves much to be desired. You constantly retry to win against these enemies forcing yourself to die when I think the developers could’ve taken different avenues instead of killing everything. Why not stealth? Eliminate some, then move on. Find a key while eliminating some baddies, then continue to your next objective. Why can’t I travel and evade my way to victory? Aim for higher platforming and perhaps lose my skills to force a no-power handicap. Or even to the point where there is a large open area and all you have to do is find any path to get there. Embracing diverse amounts of unique sections and in effect creates more player freedom than constrained enemy encounters. Would run in parallel with the constant momentum the game tries to inject. Additionally, I think extending the campaign to flesh out the worldbuilding, villain, and characters would work. More bosses too, since there are a few here. Nonetheless, how One More Level(the developers of GR) conducted them was fairly balanced and unique in my books. As a result, I don’t see a reason why more were not included. They offer creative ways to think outside the box and provide a satisfying feeling when beating them.With all that said, I don’t think my mixed feelings bring the whole game down a ton. I didn’t experience any bugs, crashes, or glitches. If anything, the intriguing story, slick combat, tight balance of difficulty with solid-level design, and gorgeous cyberpunk aesthetic left me hungry for more. A very generous checkpoint system and fitting synth wave OST takes care to almost override nearly all blemishes I had. And while the campaign is short, I clocked in at a little over five hours. There is a bleeding edge of content in store for newcomers or veterans looking for fast parkour action. And Ghostrunner fits the bill. And hey! If you do, You can be excited with me when the sequel launches later this year!7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for April 2022, this is part of my coverage of the bundle If you are interested in the game and it's before May 3rd, 2022, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Mirror’s Edge with a fresh cyber ninja-style gameplay I’m sure I’m not doing Ghostrunner justice here. Ghostrunner is a fast-paced game where you fly around a level, run across walls, and slaughter enemies all while avoiding their attacks and trying to do it with style and skill. I’m not sure that an hour is enough time to truly master this game, and that’s understandable. The one thing I can say is Ghostrunner has an amazing ability to make you feel like a ninja as you fly through a level and just nail each move such as running on a wall, and then a few seconds later make you feel like an utter failure when you miss what you consider a simple jump. This is something that happened more than a few times, but I never felt fully discouraged by this but rather felt a desire to improve my abilities and continue working on my skills to become better with the mechanics here. Pick this up if you like Mirror’s Edge or just want to feel like an absolute badass. This is a challenging game that has a high skill level and while it is designed to be speedrun, this is also really solid for normal players.If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: I finished the game and now I'm writing a review, having some second thoughts after reading some reviews saying the story was lackluster and short, the combat too hard and the physics all wacky, i decided to give it a shot. From the first level the game looked amazing and my movements felt fluid and concise. The cam just made you FEEL cool. The game never got boring either, with it adding new enemies and abilities as you progress, making it more hard but adding more tools to your disposal. And while the level geometry was a bit wack at times, every bit of every level being climbable and being able to wall run on it, i can;t remember a point in the game where it frustrated me. Don't get me wrong, the game is no walk in the park and some levels will make you take a step back, but whenever you die its never the game's fault but your own, some levels require pixel perfect accuracy and the game kicks your ass as well, but once you get the hang of a level after dying countless amounts of times it always feels rewarding. While the cybervoid elements of the game (another world where its mostly puzzle solving) did slow down the pacing a bit, they never lasted very long.The story, while it wasn't anything groundbreaking, definitely added a level of depth into a game i wasn't expecting, the lore dumps and exposition don't get in the way of the flow of the game, and i was genuinely interested as the story was reaching its climax, the writing is smooth an humorous at times and the voice acting is definitely believable, and by the end of the game, while it did leave many question to be answered, it didn't feel hand-fisted in there just to add some sense to why you're running around killing guys.So in conclusion, i do think it was worth the money i paid and it adds a certain amount of replayability with collectables and a hardcore mode with reworked levels and enemies to make the game harder, so ill be coming back to this game time and time again. In terms of a rating, id say its a solid 8.5/10. Get the game, be a cool cyber ninja.

_childDocuments_.review: So honest review.Starting off with the good:- The game looks very pretty- The learning curve of the game is both simple and easy to expand with practice- The enemies pose an interesting challenge from each other making you have to think about what you have to do before running between all of them and slicing and dicing- Plenty of parkour mechanics to keep you on your toes- A neat leveling system that consist of a puzzle and each part is a special ability. Change it up anytime when you need to and unlock more slots as you progress. By far one of my favorite things about it.Now for what makes me not recommend this game fully:- The story is pretty bland and simple, nothing terrible just nothing interesting either- No health, so restarting happens often.- Some map mechanics are a little clunky and have yet to be fixed: Wall riding on a wall you dont wanna connect to, not connecting to a wall at all when you clearly should have, trying to stop wall riding and your stuck in a limbo jumping between walls- Most of the regions are pretty linear so not a lot of options are available for how to take down a area- Most enemies dont move so every time you restart a level, there isnt any secondary thing to expect to change the outcome of your game.- It has some frame drop issues. But I hear my PC (3060RTX, i7, 16gb Ram) dying when trying to play this game compared to any other title. Maybe a optimization issue, idk? Just not normal for it to happen.- Game audio lags often, sometimes dialog plays and you'll see subtitles but hear non of the narration- My biggest criticism is the boss battles, which is something I was hopping to be the saving grace. They just didnt feel exciting or fun at all. For example: the first boss you fight is HEL and she is both simple but annoying. Nothing about the battle is interesting considering you have to fight her by timing on a weird movie-like QTE (Quick time event), of which if you fail, it resets the entire QTE with no other hazard besides getting a finger cramp spamming the attack button. The QTE as well has no distinct notification of when exactly to hit. Afterwards she jumps to a different platform uses some scaling attack speed ranged abilities. In which you just have to navigate to her (there is always three options of approching her so dodging the ranged attacks aren't too too hard) and get into another QTE again. And have to do that 4 times before you finally defeat her. I wish the fight actually utilized the abilities you learned before hand instead of having to get into a animation/interactive-cinematic lock with the boss. As well, if the game didn't want to give you a health bar through the entire thing, they could have at least gave you one during this battle, especially considering any of your active abilities are disabled, of which the game treats of special abilities.Final opinions:I think the game is okay, but not worth $30. It doesn't seem like a lot of the mechanics are fully flushed out. As well as, I don't think the story is horrible, just personally if the narrative was a little less bland or so often, hell even just fully removed, would be better for the feel of the game. Lastly I feel as if there are mechanics missing inside of the game: health bar, enemy health, better boss battles, stamina maybe, allowing more key binds to different abilities instead of multiple being locked to one key, unlockables actually worth it (minus the voice log unlockables since I take those as extra lore which is always a nice touch), just SOMETHING to save the game from feeling like it had little TLC to it.Recommendation: Wait for it to go on sale for a price that suits you and give it a try. Personally I am going to complete the game cause again, I don't think its all around horrible. Just.... a mess.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this. I really did, but it's annoying. There is a demo, so go ahead an try it. If you feel that ♥♥♥♥♥♥ that it's not quite right, do not commit. It does not get better.Respawning is *fast*. It is probably the single biggest credit to the game. You'd think it wouldn't be hard to just check if the player is in the same area as they're loading a checkpoint for, and put them and enemies back in a few second (or less) but apparently it's really hard and almost no games do it. This is really important because you're going to die a lot. A *lot*. Make a mistake: Dead. Misclick: dead. RNG: dead. Platforming. dead.Bringing down the respawning in some platforming areas the checkpoints are quite far from each other, and first person platforming is always f$&%y at best, so fall respawn, and then a bunch of running to get back to the current challenge set. If you're up to one of the layered puzzle sections falling does not always kill you. SO slip, oop, tap tap tap r.... just standing there. Kay. Thanks. Let me find another edge to throw myself off, or escape, down down down, restart from checkpoint. Why?And then the "COMBAT". Enemy AI does not exist. They either stand in one spot, or pace around a small area, the whole time perfectly aiming at your centre mass. They will literally never hit you if you're moving laterally to them. They cannot miss you if you're next to them. Running circles around them because you missed with a swordstrike is an automatic death, which might be quite a large room sprinkled with guys on platforms.You have cool things like air dodges, flash strikes, time dilation (but only in the air), bullet parry.Did I mention the first person platforming? Because first person platforming is always s$&%, and this game is no exception, I should probably repeat that. Sometimes the checkpoints are weirdly far apart. So long sections which are often easy are failed due to a late or early jump. But how can you tell, there's a lack of awareness. Air dashes do not noticably extend your jumps, and often cause you to fall short. There does not appear to be any coyote-time (being able to jump a moment after you've left a platform)So you fall, and tapping r, and oop you landed on a bit of geometry. Better throw yourself off the edge to respawn, or escape down down down retry yes. DID I ALREADY MENTION THIS ONE? Yeah I did it's real annoying.I guess I could mention the graphics? Bad. Initial impression is good, but it quickly wore thin. Concessions are made for play ability, but even with those I still often found myself standing there wondering where I could go. So you're left with a world that doesn't feel like a real place because of all the parkour things placed strategically around, but also the puzzle sections it's not always easy to tell at a glance where is important for the single path through to keep up the tempo the game is going for. And you never seem have a choice of how to approach a puzzle. Arenas are open, and you can choose the order you want to take out the enemies.Meh/yuck.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible. I was lucky enough to pick this up for only £10 on sale, but I would easily pay the full price. While not being the longest story-wise, Ghostrunner more than makes up for this with its phenomenal graphics, perfectly crafted soundtrack and movement that fast-paced players will love, and still providing enough incentive to come back and play again to perfect your runs.The best way I could describe Ghostrunner is a mix of Titanfall's movement along with Doom's playstyle, all whilst playing as Genji from Overwatch in an amazing, dystopian/cyberpunk environment; Ghostrunner hits all the marks. The gameplay offers enough of a challenge, whilst providing enough checkpoints to not frustrate you too much when you lose progress. I personally found the game hard to master, some aspects feel inconsistent between runs, but once you get the hang of the mechanics, it's easy to sink into. The movement and intense soundtrack make you feel like a god, especially on the runs that go perfectly first time. My one criticism of the game are some of the puzzle/parkour levels intersecting in the stages, as some feel like they slow the pacing at parts.Overall a great experience, absolutely recommend picking this up, especially if on sale. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostrunner

_childDocuments_.review: This is hard.This is satisfying.You'll alternate between these two moods endlessly as you fly through endless of unfair one-shot killing ennemies that are out for blood.But you walk on walls. You grapple ♥♥♥♥. Your dash slow time. You're a copulating gender-neutral parenting person ninja. The electro-cyberpunk-rythm-bass music will keep you coming back for more.Honestly if you're into platformers, this is it. It's hard. Really hard. But it's sooo well executed, it's crisp, fast, beautiful, the controls are solid, dying because of something other than lack of ninja skills happens (like a glitch), but VERY rarely. Go watch a tutorial or two on dash-slide-jump and ledge jumping before, these mechanics are way to valuable to overlook, and they are never explained in the game. I did almost all of the game wondering why sometimes I had insane burst of speed without really knowing how to recreate them.

All I can say is I haven't had a more enjoyable 7 and a half hours in a LONG ass time

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics: 8/10. Overall a fantastic looking game. The environments in particular look great, if a little repetitive sometimes. The RTX support doesn't seem to add much, though, at the cost of a big performance hit.Gameplay: 9/10. Super tight controls and gameplay loop. The more you play it, the more fun it becomes. Highly challenging, but also consistent and fair.Sound: 7/10. Great music, and some quality voice acting as well. Nothing to write home about, though.Story: 7/10. Cliche-ridden, but also some great dialogue. It won't surprise you, but it's competent enough and kept me playing.Replayability: 7/10. Depends on how much you're interested in time trials, leaderboards, and collectibles. Definitely some solid replay value in that case. The levels are very replayable and there's a new game+ mode that is great fun.Tilt: 9/10. This game is full of character and personality, and in spite of wearing its influences on its sleeve it feels fresh and unique.Final Score: 8.0/10. Fantastic indie title. Absolutely recommended for gamers who enjoy a challenge!

_childDocuments_.review: This game boasts high-octane, momentum based platforming and high risk combat that connects seamlessly with other elements of gameplay.But it falls short at every corner, The platforming is fast and enjoyable, but massively let down by the drastic tug back, brick wall combat. Early game it isn't too bad, one or two hostiles that you can cut down with a well timed dodge or dash. But quickly comes to a sudden halt when you have to deal with shockwave sending melee enemies, stop moving for seconds at a time to wait for a warden to deflect them or use your focus to blink through a sentry and hide behind objects like a cut and dry cover shooter without a gun from snipers.The only respite comes in the form of slow dreary platforming segments that have you collecting pickups like a common MMO, all without any of your powers and no momentum to speak of.The only good parts of the game are the dialogue interactions between the Architect and the girl I never bothered to learn the name of being the devil and angel on Jack's shoulder, of which you don't get to pick the decisions Jack makes so it's just fun to listen to.TL;DR Awful pacing with dull combat that stops you in your tracks and dull minigames.Good character design.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate this game so much.The kinda game I went into believing wholeheartedly I would love- and I did, for the first hour or three. Combat and movement were satisfying and kept delivering novel depth through masterable abilities. Levels had a degree of freedom and approachability, heavy on the grappling hook targets. Soundtrack and story pretty average most of the time but otherwise it delivered on exactly what I wanted it to.Then the levels got more on-rails (literally? whoever designed the rails I'm sorry but ♥♥♥♥ you the snapping is so not sensitive enough and how you get flung off is so hard to control) and execution-testy. They introduce more annoying enemies with excessively specific or unreadable timing. They abuse the oft uninteresting cyberspace sections which usually amounted to platforming sections (already exist in the real world) but without dash. The stupid ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ core boss. Worse and worse and worse. What a contrast.I just wish this game gave you more breathing room (the aforementioned boss being an egregious example of the opposite). I feel like levels would be so much more interesting if they were designed with multiple approaches in mind and encouraged a degree of experimentation. Instead you grapple the wrong way, you climb on top of the free floating wallrunning wall- you fall awkwardly or get shot in an instant. It feels like they almost have to keep levels small and tight in intended path because you'd get 1-shot across the room constantly otherwise. Part of me says make dash longer, make it easier for momentum to carry between states, maybe make dash reset charges on land or the assassinate close gaps from further. But without adding more leeway with getting back up or more support for additional routes this might just expose how inflexible the levels are.---EDIT: I finished it. Was tempted to switch to recommend at first cause I genuinely like the core of this game and felt guilty but nope. QTE autoplay boss #3 followed by unnecessary braindead frogger + walljumping section with hardly any tolerance. ♥♥♥♥ this. 6/10 don't finish it.

You basically have to study each area by dying again and again to find the correct path to kill everyone. Each checkpoint becomes a chore because of that. This gameplay mechanics is just the opposite of the definition of fun for me so I won't bother with its DLC and the next game too.

_childDocuments_.review: now let me explain my negative review, i do like this game it looks great the levels are fun and the idea is great but its not executed that well..first the game runs rather poorly and i have a 9900k and a 2080ti and between frame drops and a sort of input latency it feels cumbersome not like the fluidity of movement shooters like tf2 or the other tf2second the fighting is also very flawed your hitbox is weirdly big. when i play i catch bullets i duck under or clearly dodged all the time and i am VERY experienced with movement games like this, it gets very frustrating very quick. also the enemy ai is very poorly done there is no stealth, if the enemy can at all possibly see you they do and immediately start shooting. the ai dont time shots they dont even lead shots its not very fun especially when the game introduces the machine gunners. i really feel like most of the difficulty in this game is in maneuvering your oversized hitbox around.lastly my abilitys dont feel great i got to the dash to enemies and kill along your path ability and got stuck for a while as the game does not explain how to use it properly and to be frank it kinda sucks to use. the base dash move also feels terrible to use its too short and will gain you almost no height.final thoughtsfor such a movement based game it feels too slow, my abilities feel underpowered and unsatisfying, and the difficulty feels centered around my massive hitbox instead of increasingly complex areas and enemies. its still pretty good just get it on sale dont pay full price.

_childDocuments_.review: While a great idea for fast paced *don`t get hit* type of combat, mechanics ruined the game for me.Combat was fine, levels are decent at best and music was appropriate. However, why I can`t recommend this is is because of the unpolished movement, especially with walls and zip-lines. Over 75% of the deaths I had in the game was from this. MC not grabbing a wall, glitching through one, failing to grab a zip-line etc. Firstly I thought that I was the problem and that I had to improve my skills, but seeing the finish times and the amount of deaths I had compared to my other friends relinquished that thought. And the longer I played, the more these things poked me in the eye. So many times did I have a really good combo going on, just about to hit a checkpoint, only for MC to not grab a wall to do a wall jump and fall into the one below it, hitting the kill box. This happened so many times...Other than this, the game is really short. 17 levels and 5h of average time to do them all. Not to mention, some levels can be done in under 5min.What I don`t understand is the `puzzle` levels. Every so often, you are thrown into an artificial world where you have to do a few puzzles before you can go back. There puzzles have nothing to do with movement or skills you practiced beforehand, and because of that just ruined the pace of the real game-play. I don`t get the point of adding puzzles to an very fast paced game. 5/10

_childDocuments_.review: First off, without any spoilers, this game is a masterpiece. Starting off with the fluidity of the movement, to the impeccable soundtrack; this game is perfect. The game keeps the basic formula of run, stab, and jump, but changes it up enough to keep it from going stale. They make this happen by adding several mechanics that keep the game fun, fresh, and a great experience overall. This is something that I've seen very few games execute properly, and it's not even the best that the game has to offer. The voice acting is perfect, and fits the mood of the game perfectly; along with the plot and story that comes with it. The movement and fighting is the best part of this game. The movement in this game feels like absolute butter, and the fighting feels exhilarating and has managed to keep me on the edge of my seat throughout my entire play-through. The only thing that I have to take away from this game is the checkpoint saving. When closing the game, the checkpoints do not save, and makes you redo the level from the start. Although I might not be an experienced critic nor a hardcore gamer, I know when I'm playing a great game. This is one of the best games that I've ever played, 10/10.
