_childDocuments_.review: Steam deleted my review that took an hour to write so all you're getting is a "No". I refuse to rewrite the entire thing so the below is just a random spooling of the short amount of patience I have left.Janky, repetitive, uninspired, overpriced, frustrating, short game.I'm not sure I would pay £25 for ANY 6 hour game, never mind this mediocre mess.Also how does a 6 hour game take up about 34GB worth of my harddrive?AND having the 2 hour DLC be £12.50 makes it obvious to me that this game is just a cash cow. Combined with the fact that the small DLC packs are ludicrously overpriced for content that should have come with the game. At this point they are just taking advantage of their drooling audience that will lap up anything that is mediocre and has a cool theme. Minimum effort - Maximum returnsAlso if you disagree with this review and like anime then your opinion is biased and invalid. You're the perfect audience for them to take advantage of, no matter how mediocre the game is.I did state the positives I had with it in the deleted review but I'm not writing that again.It looks good, sounds good and plays ok sometimes. That's all.Good voice actors except for Mara.Also, it's not hard. All these negative reviews that are saying it's too hard or they don't like that you die all the time are just plain wrong. The game is hardest at the beginning, once you understand it, it becomes not only easier, but trivial. Not only that but checkpoints are often generous. It's annoying for the game's actual issues to be hidden behind people just not being very good at it. I completed it with no issue regarding difficulty. The first boss is cruel for inexperienced players but since that is the hardest part of the game, that is just a testament to how little the game designers understand difficulty and pacing regarding balancing their game.I despise the "Get Gud" mentality. But when your only complaint is that it's hard with absolutely not context or reason as to why it may be due to bad game design or genuinely unfair, that is your problem. Feel free to not like it for those reasons, but reviewing it based on that it honestly petty and misguided.For example, parrying not working frequently, getting stuck on walls, getting stuck on obstacles, not wallrunning when you should have, dashing in a different direction to what button you're pressing, suicide bomb enemies, getting shot when the bullet clearly missed, mantling forces you to launch yourself into the abyss rather than on top of the obstacle, these are all good examples of things that make the "difficulty" unfair. Sucking isn't one of them.Also the void sucks and should be removed entirely. If I wanted flashbacks to the feeling of playing as Desmond outside of the Animus I would have just turned on Assassins Creed and then swiftly deleted it after realising I didn't know which Assassin's Creed I was playing since they've been the same game since 2007.When I Stopped Playing:Completed it, won't be doing New Game PlusRating:6.4/10It's fine but since its such a janky mess, the decent gameplay can't warrant the ludicrous £25 price point. I already refunded it once for being so janky and expensive then bought it again cheaper. The price was more to my liking but the jank and bad game design remained.PS: Steam fix your reviewing system so that changing my review from "Yes" to "No" doesn't delete the contents of the textbox my 1 hour review was in. I literally made a point of how I was going to give this game a luke warm positive review but I had to change it once the list of negatives built up, but obviously that action deleted the entire thing. _childDocuments_.review: OK, so this game might not be for everyone cause its a fast paced game. If u like games such as Quake or Titanfall 2, you should fit right in. Also if u like to play as Genji from Overwatch, u will feel right at home.There is some depth and complexity to the game and some players might not even like the play-->make mistake-->die-->repeat cycle. But to me personally, its a chance to improve my reflexes. In each of the levels the game amps up the difficulty and the quick decisions you have to make in order to progress and it is very rewarding to be able to beat the challenge. Also the game has tech that you can use which quite frankly you will have to look up on YouTube, but it was def worth since not only will it help you beat your previous time on a level but also increase adds more fun to the game. For example, if you do the dash slide tech you are gonna be zooming and will reach areas that aren't reachable by normal means.The game's music also compliments the aesthetic cyberpunk retro look of the game. _childDocuments_.review: Ghostrunner starts off strong. Its graphics and worldbuilding had me hooked from the start. Even four years later the graphics still look like something that could come out today. It truly felt like I was in a cyberpunk dystopia. However, the beginning is pretty much the best part it has to offer. It all goes downhill from there. Most of the content is just "figure out which order to kill things". This requires a lot of trial and error, since any one hit kills you, and it very quickly erodes any enthusiasm the strong intro brought in. This focus on speedrun-like, perfect execution makes the game tedious and frustrating at times.The combat levels are interspersed with some puzzle/platforming levels; the latter providing some relief from the monotony of the former. Some of the puzzles are genuinely good, while others are genuinely infuriating. If you've already beat the game, then you know which ones I'm talking about.The combat and platforming itself felt incomplete. Both are somewhat consistent, but there were many times that it felt inconsistent. Sometimes you would still die after parrying correctly. Other times your character might vault over something you didn't want them to. All these tiny inconsistencies are a stark contrast from the perfectionist attitude the game expects from you to progress.Lastly, the lack of levels themselves was disappointing, especially so when juxtaposed to the price of the game. Even with all the learning from dying, I still beat the game in less than nine hours? Yet the asking price is thirty dollars?Overall I felt like I was playing a beautiful technical demo, rather than a full game. It's visually very pretty, but those visuals hide a plethora of issues.

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really wanted to like this game but I just can't. The one hit kill/death mechanic feels like it holds the game back more than it does to benefit it. It makes the combat encounters tense while also really revealing a lot of the flaws the game has by not allowing the player to have any margin for error, thus making them to push the game to its limits only to find the cracks in its foundation. From mechanics that don't work all the time, random geometry in levels that is able to be climbed on for no reason, awkward hit detection, or the fact that most of the abilities you get are worthless filler to cover up that the only variety in how you kill people is the pieces that you chop them into. 95% of combat encounters in this game can be done completely without the use of them. The upgrade system while being a fun little game of tetris with your upgrades, has about twice the depth that this game will even let you experience in one playthrough. All in all I think the movement and the soundtrack were the best parts of this game.The story sets up this conflict of how life as it is in the tower is not sustainable as there's not enough resources to go around but life outside the walls is also equally as dangerous as the surface has become unlivable, so you'd think that they'd actually address this with the ending, right?NOPE!!!This entire dilemma is promptly forgot about entirely during the ending and humanity lives happily ever after. Because I guess they just expected you to forget about the imminent starvation of the human species. Ok bro I'll just forget about it.Now let me tell you about the absolute worst part: The Boss fights.Holy Lord the boss fight suck massive throbbing ♥♥♥♥, because of the one hit death mechanic, and the overall fast pace of the combat, the boss fights basically devolve into playing Dance Dance Revolution with a sword fight. Which at its very core is essentially "push button at right time for reward" gameplay, that I find to not only be a tedious exercise in repetition but to also be insulting to basic human intelligence by treating me like im some monkey in a cage being trained to press button for a banana. Out of all 2 boss fight this game has to offer that's basically the gist of how you win: Goo goo ga ga press button when game want for reward.(I'm not counting Tom as a boss fight because the things required to be a boss fight are a boss and a fight. Got the boss, but you spend most of your time platforming the worst laser section ive ever seen with no fighting.Honestly a health system tied to a difficulty selection that allowed you to take hits with some Invincibility frames in between like casltlevania or super mario bros would do a lot to improve the game in my opinion.Example:Easy -  4 hitsMedium - 3 hitsHard - 2 hitsGhost - 1 hitGiving players a margin of error to learn the rhythm of the game rather than killing them every time they miss a beat, as players grow more familiar with the games' mechanics and combat they can bump up the difficulty and play again accordingly, lessening the margin of error until they achieve perfection.But nothing like that has happened or ever will because the elitist crowd has already dug their nails in the game and treat anyone who criticizes it like they've committed a cardinal sin so now we're stuck with a game not as great as it could be worshiped by a sycophantic crowd of fanatics that will screech at anyone or anything that they feel threatens them.Thank you gaming community, very cool.

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly wanted to love this game. I mean, I love katanas, gore, cyberpunk and slo-mo. The game has it all. What can go wrong? I tell you what: pacing. When I dived into this game I was expecting something fun and straight-forward as the games that this one looks like: Mirrors Edge and Katana Zero. But instead you have like one really interesting fight room (that you will complete in less than a minute) and then you do platforming for ten minutes. And sometimes it takes some time to understand WHERE to go rather than HOW. And it breaks pace for me. I may be stupid, but I had no problems with Katana Zero (where you always go right) and Mirrors Edge (where you go where it's red). In this game I've been finding myself lost way to many times. And thats especially disappointing when you just had extremely fast and fun ffight and you filled with adrenaline but you have to roam around and try to cross the gap, dying like 20 times in process because your character decided that jumping is not his forte right now.I haven't completed the game, I refunded it, so MAYBE (and thats a really huge maybe) later in the game it changes pace. But I doubt it.The game apparently is short and makes stress on replay value, but In 2.6 hours I plaed, I had only two episodes that I would want to replay when I get good. And that's ~4 minutes out of that ~3hPaying so much for a game that I probably will never replay is not an option for me.And mind that, I see that the game is well made, people who developed it really cared of what they are doing and it could be one of the best games of this year, but not for me.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot going for it but the I really dislike collectables in these types of games. The whole point of the game is to get from A to B as fast and stylishly as possible with the fewest number of failures. So what is the point of me having to stop my flow to examine the map for nooks and crevices where something could be hidden?The only reason I would want to retry a level is to get a better time, not look for collectables. Bear in mind the way levels are designed means they are broken into many no return segments so you can't backtrack if you thought you missed something.All the collectables do is give a little bit of extra lore and some cosmetics, they could have easily tied the cosmetics to in-game achievements like deflect 5 bullets in a row and as for the lore they could have "shown" it in the story missions instead of "telling" you in the menus.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent aesthetics, worldbuilding, voice acting, music. Lovely bits of humor (especially regarding the swords and sword-wielding enemies). On the other hand, the platforming is often imprecise, many of the enemies break up the flow of a combat encounter is unsatisfying ways, the boss fights are themselves all entirely disappointing, and the game is very short. I completed it at 6.5 hours despite spending a bit of time wandering around picking up artifacts, looking at the modules, and admiring the game world. It would not be difficult to complete it faster, and additional playthroughs don't really offer any change in the experience. The climax of the game is a showcase of everything wrong with the imprecise first-person platforming. That's not to say it's bad, but it does highlight every flaw extremely well. All taken together, I wouldn't recommend Ghostrunner at full price. It's just too short, its combat a bit too clunky, its platforming a bit too fiddly to be offset by its otherwise excellent music, enjoyable (if predictable) plot, and wonderful visual style. When the game hits right, it feels like a 3D Cyberninja Hotline Miami. It just doesn't hit right enough, and the lows feel all that much lower when juxtaposed with the highs.

_childDocuments_.review: To give you an idea of my basic expectations going in, when I looked at the trailer again after having this game for a long time, I thought "This looks like Dishonored". It isn't. So here's a review from someone who was hoping to play a game with stealth. This game has a lot of great stuff that is good for people who like to grind movement based games, but the difficulty level and some specific taste differences kill it for me.1.  Being killed by one shot at any time is just not something that I find fun in games. I prefer tension that rises and falls instead.2. The game doesn't really telegraph where to go on platforming sections at the pace the movement asks it to be played. I found myself having to look around several times either because I couldn't see the next location or because I was put in a weird spot after failing a jump.3. The game gives you the blink power, and during the tutorial is uses a cooldown. Great, so I can't reuse this power quickly while learning because it wants me to get used to the cooldown. Except it uses a different cooldown system afterwards, and doesn't start active. Also I didn't understand at first that it used a sweeping attack, so I thought I had to lock on to enemies to kill multiple at first. Really a lot of the problems could be solved by having the architect explain things more.4. The dash. It has bullet time in the air, but not on the ground which make kill enemis from ground level a system of jumping and dashing which is annoying to me because I just want to run up on enemies with strafing to be sufficient. Also the dash is no longer directional when you strafe into a wall run which is so easy to do on accident because the mid air bullet time gives you a lot of movement ability.5. In the intro cut scene it shows Ghostrunner hitting projectiles back at enemies, but you do not get access to this power until about 15-20 minutes in, which is an annoying few deaths of figuring out that you can't do it yet. Additional the projectiles move fast enough that timing is too precise to be worth it, especially with audio being not perfectly timed with the blast.This is by no means a bad game. It just appeals to a specific kinda of audience that is willing to look past flaws and relishes things that makes the game difficult. As more of an average player that is not masochistic enough to play games that don't make you feel like you do better, I cannot recommend this game for most people. I don't usually write reviews like this, but if I find myself complaining about small stuff the whole time I play a game and am not having fun, I'd like to give others a chance to know what to expect.

_childDocuments_.review: DISCLAIMER UP FRONT:Only buy this game if you like platforming section. Long, unforgiving platforming sections. On to the review.This is what you get when you have a great game with a great concept and awesome stylish combat and dilute it with unnecesary stuff until you lose what could have been an amazing game from start to finish.First off: This game looks and sounds incredible. The graphics, models, lighting and visual effects are something to behold. And my god, the sounds and the music are amazing as well. The combat (when you get to enjoy it, that is) is stylish, fast, gory and amazingly satisfying in general.IT'S EVEN BETTER THAN THE DEMO, which was amazing as well.BUT this game makes you put so much time into platforming, puzzle solving and an absolutely forgettable story that, after 7 hours I have to say that I enjoyed maybe 30% of this games runtime. When it works, it works amazingly. It's basically Katana ZERO in 3D (and if you haven't played Katana ZERO, do yourself the favor. You're welcome.). But so much of this games content simply falls flat on it's stomach because it is NOT. FUN. TO. PLAY. Which brings me to the bosses.Oh, man. The bosses. These must have been the most sad, uninspired, laziest designed and most agonizingly boring bosses I ever fought in a video game. The best comparison I can make right now is an amazing game called Fury. Imagine Fury, where you learn the intricate patterns of the bosses and the timing to deflect there attacks and then beat them in a stylish way that feels so accomplishing, its amazing. Yeah, imaging that but without any of the challenge, without ANY OF YOUR SKILLS THAT YOU LEARNED DURING THE CAMPAIGN and without any feeling of growing as a player because the boss fights are completely disconnected from any other combat scenario. These bosses are so bad, if you removed them from the game, your end product would become better.The platforming is hit or miss for me. The game basically does everything for you. You have to press no buttons at all to activate wall runing, grappling or vaulting. That makes it easy to pull off stylish moves and effortless to feel like an absolute badass while slashing dudes in half but the platforming sections become so complex after a few levels that you are basically begging for more buttons to press because it can feel like the game simply decided to fling you off the map or don't activate wall run when you need it to.All in all, this game was pretty disappointing for me. The core is amazing and when you get to clear rooms of deadly enemies while slashing, wall running, dashing and deflecting bullets with a sword you get to feel like a real badass. But for some mind boggling reason they decided it was a good idea to make more than half the game platform and puzzle sections that are so boring and/or infuriatingly tricky, they almost made me refund it. The bosses are of the same quality as the platforming: Mind boggingly boring. Also: No difficulty settings, which is sad because replaying the campaing is almost pointless besides no-death and speedruns.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. This wouldn't be an issue with saves that could go to the individual checkpoints in a level, but that's not the end of the world.The pacing of the game can be strange, with the segments where they take away your dash/wall run (puzzle time, so no cheaty) feeling slow and painful. _childDocuments_.review: Ghostrunner was a pleasant surprise. It's a short and fun action platformer that keeps you busy with challenging but fair stages, while smartly mixing things up throughout the experience. It's not quite as great in telling its story as it is with its movement and combat, and it can be frustrating at times, but when everything works well together, it's a satisfying and fun skill-based action game. If you are looking for a linear and challenging game, pick up Ghostrunner.

_childDocuments_.review: Worst implementation of dodge movement I've ever seen in a videogame. It's inconsistent (I have no idea when the game lets me enter slow-mo and when not, feels very random), it's imprecise (it's not directional, you dodge only forward, unless you enter slomo mode) and frankly the slomo just throws off my timing. _childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game so much but I feel like every step of the way it puts something in my way to dampen the experience.- Combat is fast and fluid- Level Design is good for the most part* where there's lots of ways you can approach a problem (especially in the later parts of the game) *I say most part as some levels have a clear "best way" of doing something regardless of options- If you like Daniel Deluxe he did the music for this game- The world itself is quite nice to look at, good graphics and the like. Very good visuals to let you know what part of the tower you're in aswell (though the final area doesn't really make sense from a realism/believability  point of view)- Load times are incredibly fast, I've played graphically simpler games with longer load times - The story is very exposition heavy and very predictable, which is sad since the setting is incredibly interesting and pretty unique for a cyberpunk setting to also be post-apocalyptic, would just like the characters to maybe tone it down with the ham-fisting. - 3 of the 4 abilities you unlock fill the exact same purpose with varying ways in which they do the same thing i.e kill a bunch of enemies with one attack, the only difference is the range you can use them at. This is more a personal issue but I was hoping for more utility focused abilities like active camo (since it's hinted at in dialogue) , or if the power ups replaced these as actual abilities for more options.- Upgrades are frustrating to say the least, it's a tetris style puzzle block system, meaning if you want to experiment with new upgrades, you have to do a new puzzle every single time, its fun the first time, not so much on the 8th.- The many, many Puzzle/platforming sections that pad out the game and add nothing of substance are boring at best and incredibly frustrating at worst, the final one is the worst of these as the collision in this game can very often decide that bounce pads either don't exist or don't actually bounce- The Boss fights are not good, incredibly bad even. They also distract from the core gameplay while adding nothing of substance.     ~ 1st Boss;      ~ 2nd Boss;      ~ 3rd Boss; I really do want to like this game, the aesthetic and style is just so good with the main character being so well designed but I just can't recommend it with all the problems I had playing through it.

My only complaint is that I wish they would've added more enemies that take a few more interactions to eliminate than the typical ones throughout the game (ex. a less extreme version of Hel).  Other than that, I consider it a masterpiece when it comes to gameplay/mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: This is by far the buggiest, and most broken game I have played. Let me explain:1. The graphics, visuals, and performance, is fantastic. Its like the developers focused solely on a good looking and feeling game, but they obviously suck at developing a game that actually WORKS.2. The movement mechanics are beyond broken. Sometimes your commands will work, sometimes they wont. Sometimes you will jump, or try to, and it does something bizzare and unnatural. There are too many times where I felt the game just wasn't polished enough, as if hitboxes were broken, ai was retarded or overly ruber bandy (sometimes the ai is dumb af and sometimes the same freaking guy has 2000iq and hits you 360 no scope, sometimes the ai will literally just walk over and sit on the objective, completely negating any thing you do). Grappling is kind of broken since sometimes it will double grapple and swing you back forcing you to redo your run. When there are more than one grapple in your field of view, you never know which one the game will pick, and when an a fast run, this is terrible when the game decide to screw you over.3. The general flow the game is kind of trash because of the above stated. You are constantly having to redo missions not because you made a mistake, but because the game straight up doesn't register your inputs. Wanna jump from one wall to another? Well guess what, sometimes it will sometimes it wont, it just picks and choose's when it wants to be broken or not. You learn to expect certain things are a given, like if I am within a few pixels of landing on a panel, that it should just intuitively grab, no I have to over compensate for the game's bad design using mechanics that were not intended to be used this way, or I have to change my entire run to be more conservative because of the fact that I can't take a 50/50 chance on whether the game will or will not decided to comply.4. The general runback is kind of stupid. This isn't a souls like or anything so why aren't there more check points? Why are levels 2-3 hours long with no way to save or pause to come back later? Its utter BS since a level that should take 15-30 minutes ends up being 3+ hours ONLY because the game decides to screw you over with what I said in point 2 and 3.I cannot recommend this game to someone who things this is a free flowing easy going vibe game all about the cyberpunk theme with great music. The game itself, is ♥♥♥♥, the music and visuals, great. And not, don't tell me to "get good", I have played and beaten souls games on speed runs and games like sekiro are a piece of cake, so this one is just broken and needs fixing.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like an E3 Demo; all style, no substance.The game looks, runs, and (mostly) sounds great. However, it tries to do far too many things without giving consideration to how any of them interact with each other and form a cohesive package. (One example of this is a personal gripe: the world-design. The levels look great. They are extremely stylish and match the gameplay concepts perfectly. However, they have no cohesion. Every level looks like the same semi-industrial, cyberpunk, dystopia that completely lacks believability and, by extension, immersive qualities. Every space *feels* like it's in a video game. This isn't a problem inherently, mind you. Games like Doom Eternal do an excellent job of designing game-y levels that service the gameplay in such a way as to only enhance the game experience. However, GhostRunner simply throws the player into - what feels like - a linear level block-out made in late Alpha that lacks ANY reward for exploration or even just attempts to approach a challenge differently.Also, abilities unlocked throughout the game are near useless due to a large cool-down placed - and shared - among them all. This is worsened by how it is simply more rewarding to stick to just your sword).There are a few reasons someone *would* be interested in GhostRunner after seeing it though. As such, here are a list of other, better games that satiate your desires MUCH more:The movement-UltraKill-Doom Eternal-Titanfall 2-Stride VRThe Hotline Miami gameplay loop-Katana Zero-Ape Out-Hotline Miami itselfThe swordplay-Furi-Katana Zero-Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance-Sekiro: Shadows Die TwiceThe story/lore-Bioshock-Katana Zero-Half-Life: Alyx(I'm sure there is more, but I am not being paid to write all this.)TLDR: GhostRunner is a SUPER shallow game in every regard. It really plays like the perfect "smoke and mirrors" E3 Demo that would be shown to promote a new console generation's capabilities rather than a fun game idea. It has a little bit of everything, yet lacks any identity of its own. If you want a game very similar to GhostRunner that I assure you will fulfill your expectations infinitely more, play Katana Zero.P.S. If you came for a movement-shooter type game go somewhere else. There is nothing rewarding about GhostRunners' movement beyond what can be gained from a YouTube video.

_childDocuments_.review: i think I'd describe this game as "uncreative." Let me elaborate.First of all the story is uninteresting blah blah blah, let's ignore that. You are a super cyborg ninja trying to get revenge on a super cyborg Doctor Octopus with your new friend, Cortana Except It's A Guy. The aesthetic, while beautifully rendered with some of the best graphics I've ever seen in an indie game, is generic cyberpunk dystopiaville.The gameplay is what's important here, and I'd describe it as... Predictable. Businesslike. Every level is a series of linear corridors where you have to press the right buttons precisely at the right time in order to progress, broken up by somewhat freeform combat arenas where you have to press the right buttons precisely at the right time in order to progress.You could argue all games are just that. The difference between a good game and a bad game is whether or not you notice the button pressing.You might like it, but it's not for me. I feel like a player being railroaded in a D&D campaign, or an actor who has to do a bunch of cuts before getting their scene right. Maybe I just haven't "gotten gud" yet, but I don't really care about that if it just means I can press buttons more precisely in order to run through linear corridors more efficiently.Edit: Finally got around to completing this game. My review changes from "don't bother" to "it's a tentative recommendation if on sale."The story is... Lukewarm. Still completely predictable but it has a nice arc.My thoughts about the gameplay remain. It's a puzzle game cavorting around as a movement shooter. There are some ways you can get clever and take shortcuts with the engagements, but for the most part, it's just a matter of making the right moves at the right movements. There's no expressiveness. There's no alternate solution, or very much room for player agency. The developers have given you these 9 combinations of routes to win the arena. Go, kill the bad guys.And on top of that, because of the low expressiveness of the game, there is a needed "tightness" to make it feel difficult. The game focuses on precision of execution, doing things almost exactly right. But the  isn't well-made enough to support that kind of difficult. The movement system is inconsistent, especially when attacking mid-air enemies. Timing on parries and parry cues is just... Off, it feels wrong, compared to something like Elden Ring or Ultrakill where parries are difficult but consistent and fair.At times it almost feels like this game wasn't designed, just developed. I think the biggest piece of evidence for that is the bossfights, all of which involve so much freaking  for obstacles to clear or enemies to become vulnerable. I don't want to wait for your stupid laser beams or robot arms to finish their slow ass movements so I can kill you. Movement shooters aren't about waiting, they're about going fast and kicking ass.All that being said, it isn't bad... Just frustrating. One of my least favorite things is missed potential, and that's what this is. If Ghostrunner was just a bit more free-form, a bit more expressive, derived a bit more of its challenge from clever enemy and level layouts, instead of excessively precise timing and poor UX, i.e. lack of good telegraphs, audio cues, visible effects, I think it could've been a masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the Demo a lot and was really hyped for the game. When it released, I instantly played it and I must say I'm impressed. The Demo was very good, but the full game was even better. I expected way less features, since in the Demo you could already dash, slow time slide and slice with your sword. This would've been enough for the game to be enjoyable. But then 4 extra abilities show up and you can do even more. A very interesting upgrade system (like Tetris) hits you and new enemies show up for you ton slice. Usually a game like this doesn't need a very good story or bossfights, since you just run around, so I didn't expect a lot. Turns out, the story is pretty good and the bossfights are way better than bossfights in a lot of other titles I've seen. The game is a bit short, took me about 4:45h (although since I already played the demo a lot this time is pretty good). It will probably take longer for you, because the game is very very hard. I died a lot and some sections took me 50+ tries, even though they all are very short. The graphics are fantastic, the cyberpunk feeling definetly improves the game and RTX!!!All in all, I can fully recommend this game if you seek a challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10My original review was negative and I will leave it in quotes in the bottom.This game shines with top tier rig and ultrawide monitor.Try to survive this game until after the first boos and it becomes MUCH, MUCH better in every aspect.Now that I actually finished it, and knowing the above,I can highly recommend it.This is probably the only 3d game in "speedrun" genre that does not look like a potato.The only negative thing I have to say is slow start, and bugged 2nd boss 3rd phase. Boss has no animation, just try to wiggle left right and spam lmb to parry, that worked somehow.___________________________________________Original review:"The level design, the gameplay, the story, basically everything else gets very repetitive after about 2 hours. Don't get me wrong, i love the feeling of 'grind to perfection', the feeling of overcoming the difficulty and getting the win after countless failures. But in this game I don't get that feeling at all. When i finish the level i just realize that by sheer trial and error process that took me anywhere from 5-15 minutes I have found the order of platforms/enemies that devs intended me to find. There is no feeling of improvement, no 'I learned something new'. In the next 'puzzle' you will be stuck just the same until you find that perfect order of platforms/walls/enemies. This is not hard or 'hardcore', this is just button mashing until you find what creators intended you to find.Sometimes the controls are annoying, your ninja tries to climb something that is not there, fails to dodge etc.. For the game where the gameplay IS the game this is unacceptable.The level design is VERY generic. Sometimes in some levels that require a little of backtracking it sometimes can be hard to even understand if you are going 'forward' or 'backward'.Graphics and fps are good.Story is predictable and not engaging.I would love this game to be Hotline Miami 3D, but it's not. In HM the situation turned into sheer chaos and you, the player, could always find some unique way of getting out alive. Here you just find the right order to do things. Might as well have Mario's mushrooms or Sonic's rings as a 'hint' from the devs.Overall get it on the sale, you will love it during first few hours and then (unless you enjoy doing speed runs) drop it."

_childDocuments_.review: Read this review and others The universe around the cyberpunk genre seems to be reaching its peak in 2020. Ghostrunner is a very ambitious title that was born at the hands of the Polish studio, One More Level, in cooperation with two more studios and lets the player free his whole ninja side.Ghostrunner is a first-person action platform title set in a future cyberpunk atmosphere, which brought to mind several times a mix of past titles. Between “Katana Zero”, a bit because of the way he punishes the player, since if he suffers damage he will have to repeat the section, and “Mirrors Edge” for the adrenaline and form of movement of the character.The game puts a Ghostrunner in the hands of the player, who was woken up by the “Architect”, a prisoner who found no other solution to save himself than summon Jack. Now, after freeing the Architect, it is necessary to climb the Dharma Tower where the last known humans are found after an apocalyptic disaster that tried to kill the ruler at the time, better known as Mara. Along the way it is also possible to find Zoe, even if only by voice, a member of the resistance group against Mara.The whole story is passed through interactions between the player and the Architect who is present as a voice in Jack’s head. It is not a story that we have not seen before. The need for a ruler to be overthrown so that humanity has its space and can return to survive without major evils. But is it really so?The gameplay is undoubtedly the most attractive in this experience. Ghostrunner’s powers were designed to make the player feel like a real ninja from the future, but it is important to keep the momentum or the section will have to be repeated again. It will certainly happen many times, but that is not why it will cause any kind of frustration. It is a fun learning process, especially because it is possible to find new lines of passage or attack. The number of choices is more than many, since it is possible to run across the wall, use the grappling hook on specific places, slide down ramps like Sonic and use up to four special skills. All this while using a katana as a form of attack and cutting enemies like leaves.Despite having a very fluid and fun gameplay, this is not a title that you will end easily. There is a very high learning curve, which was very rewarding for me, but for those who don’t like challenges will find great difficulties. Not because of the difficulty of the enemies themselves individually, they all have attack patterns that are easily circumvented and presented in a balanced way throughout the adventure. But the difficulty of finding a room full of different enemies is where it can get more complicated. I confess that I had to stop a few times, for brief minutes, to review certain available movements and possible escape points. All enemies are killed with one attack, but as I mentioned earlier, the player is also vulnerable to this premise.It is thus possible to easily take 40 minutes on just one level, as it happened to me. At the end of each section, it will appear how long it took to finish that section of the game. This can also push the more hardcore players, who want to beat the previous time.This title also features battles against “Bosses”, which challenges players to put all their knowledge of the skills learned and the use of the environment around them.Speaking of the environment, it is not just combat that can put some obstacles in front of the player. Some segments of the environment are also quite challenging in their own way, as it challenges to think a little outside the box and the dexterity of each one’s fingers. Between jumps and sections that seem to have a right path, but it is necessary to find an alternative path.The whole layout is very simple, leaving the screen open for all the action that unfolds in a surprisingly successful environment. In the lower left corner, a skill bar is displayed and the availability of using one of the skills.The skill tree is presented in a very interesting way, just like Ttris. Weird? Not really. It is not possible to choose all available sections, so it is therefore important to choose the ones that matter most among the spaces available for them.In short, this is undoubtedly a title to take into account, with a formula that pulls a lot by the dexterity of the players and perfectly set both by its level of graphics and the soundtrack that makes anyone vibrate. Ghostrunner has a very specific intention, between sections of parkour and difficult gameplay, is aimed at the most courageous.

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really, REALLY wanted to like this game. It looks great, has a great soundtrack, has some interesting combat, and the platforming is excellent when it works. But it doesn't always work, and some of the combat scenarios are so unbelievably frustratingly bad that 125 deaths and an hour later, I'm not much closer to finishing an encounter.The platforming is interesting enough when it works. You can tell they were going for a Titanfall 2 vibe, which they mostly nail in the sections without combat. The upgrade system is fairly unique, and I like how you can change out your loadouts based on how you want to play a specific section. But gaming shouldn't make me feel this frustrated or irritable after playing. I die too often because close-up attacks don't register, or you die from someone in a completely blind spot with a ridiculous angle, or you miss a wall run or jump at the worst time because of the geometry of a level or the game or a last second ledge that forces a fall to your death. What can be really great and fun has just too much frustration. Far too often I die and feel like it couldn't have been avoided, as opposed to more polished difficulty in Souls games or Hotline Miami. Save yourself the hassle and play Titanfall 2 instead. What a let down.

_childDocuments_.review: The movement is great but the combat is trash. Often the only way to beat a hard fight is to play it over and over again because whether you live or die depends on completely random factors. That isn't "hard". It's just bad gameplay design.Just to explain the game, this isn't like a hack and slash game or something. You die after one hit, and each encounter is more like a puzzle you have to solve. You will have to dodge gunfire and each move must be executed perfectly or you will die.The assist mode options (like being able to take an extra hit) help some, but that's not really what the issue is. The issue is that certain factors like enemy movements seem to actually be random either intentionally or unintentionally, so you cannot develop a strategy that's 100% effective. Some particular encounter might require you to make a jump at some exact angle while dodging projectiles, but you will always die sometimes making that jump because two enemies just happened to shoot at the same time or some other stupid thing.There's a move that lets you slow-mo midair and dodge but you can only use it once per jump and it only lets you dodge some types of projectiles. Other projectiles move too fast, are too large or the enemy shoots too many to dodge so most of the time you have to plan your jumps out ahead of time. Most encounter designs will require you to make jumps at very specific angles with split-second timing. There's no room to fudge things and recover if enemies do the wrong thing.Another example is that there is a move that lets you kill multiple enemies at the same time, provided they are lined up. Certain encounters will require you to use this, but the AI movements actually seem to be often randomized, so your setup for the move will fail because one enemy randomly walked away. Again, it's just bad design. I don't understand why they did this. In a game like this I would have expected the enemies to move relative to the player somehow, but after studying enemy movements for a bit I found they actually just seem to walk randomly from point to point most of the time. Super annoying for a game that requires so much planning and has so few ways to recover.In hardcore mode there's a fight where there are 4 platforms arranged like this:□.□□.□There's one enemy unit on each platform, and 3 more teleporting randomly from platform to platform. All of them shoot projectiles at you, although there's a range limit so only about 3 or 4 are ever shooting at you at the same time. All this means that at the start of the fight you will have enemies shooting at you from behind pretty much no matter what, whether it's because you are jumping towards a corner or because one teleported behind you. This is just obviously horrible design because you can't dodge projectiles that you can't see. I don't think I'm exaggerating when I say that like 90% of the effort on this fight is just re-rolling because you get killed by something behind you. I actually beat this fight because I happened to re-roll it enough times (trying to beat it the honest way) that the 3 teleporters all happened to teleport onto the same platform right in front of me and I killed them all in one shot with an ability.It's otherwise a good game, but you will hate it if you hate playing things over and over.If the game really depended on reflexes or something, that would be one thing, but I don't think it actually does all that much. There are only a few reflex-oriented aspects, such as sword-wielding enemies that jump at you which are fine. The Hel boss fight is also great and well-designed. (The Hel boss fight has a little randomization, but not in a way that detracts from the gameplay.) This game is otherwise almost all puzzle-solving with an emphasis on choreographed movement. Randomization is okay in a true action game with real combat, but this is not a game like that. This is a game about movement, strategy and memorization.Obviously the difficulty of this game makes it unplayable if you are not good at FPS movement which is a problem since the game doesn't actually have an easy mode, but I am talking about the design beyond that. I'm good enough at FPS games that I will play on hard mode if I like the game enough. I just get ticked off at high-variance randomized gameplay. It's the same reason I hate stuff like Hearthstone.I got about 1/2 way through hardcore mode before I eventually just got bored with the game because I found the vast majority of my time playing was spent just re-rolling encounters due to randomized crap. Hardcore mode also doesn't save your progress in each level, so you can't pick away at it. You have to play an entire level in one sitting or pause the game and leave it open. Super lame. It's 2022 and I have a job.I feel like there will be die-hard fans of a game like this that think it's "hard" and don't realize they are just spending all their time re-rolling encounters for a random win. Starsiege: Tribes was hard.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a pretty good overall. The game that I can immediately compare it to is Katana Zero. If you've played that game, you'll understand a lot of what you're up against in this game. The enemies feel fun to take on, the platforming and navigation of level space feels pretty good overall, and the narrative doesn't disrupt the rhythm of the gameplay. Without revealing too much about the game itself, I'd give it an 8/10. The controls and feeling of movement have some issues, and that's most of what prevents me from giving this game a 10/10 rating. The game features wall-running and ledge-grabbing, but sometimes the sort of "grabbiness" or magnetism between the character and a wall/ledge is very inconsistent. This inconsistency can be very annoying to deal with because it can force you to have to repeat a platforming segment or combat encounter as you inadvertently fall to your death (because of death pits or a stray bullet, there's no falling damage). For a game like this, having consistent and reliable level-space navigability is crucial to how good the game can feel to play. Sometimes the character feels like he's moving incredibly slow while running, and sometimes it doesn't feel like you have enough control over the direction in which the character dodges. For example, you might be holding "A" to move left, but you'll still dodge forward as if you're still pressing "W". Hopefully there will be an update at some point that might fix the source of some of these issues. When these issues aren't happening, however, the game feels amazing and satisfying to play. The game is very difficult, but there are times when you'll find a natural rhythm to everything you're doing and it will just "click". Like Katana Zero, you'll often find yourself repeating a segment of a level quite often, but it's generally pretty easy to figure out what went wrong. The only real issues that I came across consistently had to do with player movement and control, but these issues are rare, though quite infuriating when they do occur. A huge plus with this game is that there's a free demo, so you can immediately determine if this game is for you at no monetary cost. Ultimately, I would highly recommend this game.*Do not play this game if you're distracted or tired. It demands a lot of your attention and energy.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't really recommend Ghostrunner.  I found several things I didn't like about the platforming and combat mechanics:After getting my first upgrade in the Cybervoid, the platforming section that followed took a good 15 minutes to run through the first time.  The wall running mechanics were really not that intuitive to me, and it wasn't until I realized that the wall run happens automatically that I was able to even get past this section.  Maybe I'm too used to the Overwatch wall riding mechanics, but I feel like these could have been better explained.  I encountered this feeling again when obtaining the blink ability.  Simply highlighting the enemies and pressing the attack button was not the correct way to use the ability.  The enemies need to be lined up with each other, which isn't mentioned in the ability tutorial.On the combat side, it appears that you die in one shot to any enemy, making the sections with multiple machine gun enemies very frustrating.  Even more so if you need to first hunt down shield generators while being shot at.  When you get blink, it takes a minute or more to use it after the first use, even with all other ability slots empty, so this skill seems pretty useless when you get it.  Not sure if this is this is the case after further upgrades.After about two hours of playing, it just felt like I was banging my head against a wall.  I can see it's possible to get really good at this game, but I don't think the amount of dying and frustration necessary to get there is worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: I beat this game on my old account and decided to give this game another run and will try to 100% it this time. This game is easy to learn but hard to master. This game is a must have if you're into the cyberpunk genre / mirrors edge / punishing games. I will update my review once I finish this game (again) but on this account.Update: I 100% this game about a week ago and messed around a bit after. This game is exactly what I remembered it being like back when I played this last year on my old account. Ghostrunner is the first game I 100% and turned me into an achievementhunter. This game is extremely addictive and once you learn the mechanics, you start stringing different things together to be as fast and efficient as possible. This game was made truly with speedrunners in mind and it's nice to get to experience a taste of that. The story is pretty solid but I wish they put faces on certain voices. The story is a bit short but there is major replay-ability especially now with the new wave based mode.If you're trying to 100% this game as efficiently as possible, just watch a guide for each level's artifcacts/audio logs/swords other than that, just enjoy the game for what it is and you'll have a fantastic time.I remember a time when I was waiting for this and Cyberpunk 2077 to both release (this being in October 2020 and Cyberpunk 2077 in November) and Ghostrunner has become my favorite cyberpunk experience of the two.Pros:- Really fun- Easy to learn- Great replay-ability- Speedrunner friendly- Solid story- Good boss fightsCons:- Short story-mode- Can be frustrating with the amount of times you die- Cosmetics could be betterTLDR; great game, good replayability, short story mode, and somewhat frustrating 1 shot life. I recommend this to anybody that likes: Parkour, Mirror's Edge, Cyberpunk genre, FPS games, having a fun time feeling like a bad a$$ cyber ninja.

_childDocuments_.review: Saying Ghost Runner is a fantastic game is a major understatement, along with fantastic settings and themes, Ghost runner also has some great characters. The combat system is phenomenal, I really like the fact that you use a sword against enemies with guns. The movement system is possibly one of the best I have experienced in a game to date, the wall running is done very well and traversal is fast and satisfying. Now lets talk about how the game looks. You'd be hard pressed to find a game in this genre that looks as good as Ghost Runner. The amazing graphics really shine in the Cybervoid and the cityscapes,  the light that comes off of the neon signs looks quite realistic and is very satisfying to look at. The cosmetic system is quite simple, you find different swords scattered throughout the levels. Each of these swords look great in their own way and mostly fit in with the atmosphere. So in conclusion, if you can, buy this game. It gives you a great challenge, a very fun gameplay style, and an amazing and satisfying story. Very cool.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is my 1 hour experience with the game, I got through 3 Levels before I got frustrated with it.From what I've seen, Ghostrunner looks like a rapid-paced platformer, but it didn't feel like it..f you do get the movements down and operate at a high skill level, you can move fast and restart quite quickly (if you turn on that gameplay option), quick restarts are essential for making a platformer feel quick and fluid.It's impressive what speedrunners can do with this game, but I would've had to play it a hell of a lot more to get to a satisfying level of skill.The evenly placed checkpoints can contain long pathways, so every time you screw up, you hold forward for a few seconds before getting back to the weirdly spaced walls. And Since the game expects you to have story dialog running, it often lacks music, which is fine. Though after a few retries, it stops repeating itself but doesn't add any music, this made it seem even more monotone and repetitive to me.Missing a Platform or falling off a wall felt horrible to me. I honestly had more fun when I used to play platforming levels in minecraft..I might've been spoilt by playing Celeste, a masterpiece in my opinion, but I honestly got really frustrated while playing Ghostrunner, which doesn't usually happen.These issues might not apply to you, but I recommend trying the demo before you buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: After completing the game, unlocking all collectibles and obtaining all achievements - It's time I give a review.Ghostrunner features fast-paced gameplay and mainly revolves around it. I don't really like to compare games to other games out there, as I feel every game deserves to be recognized solely for itself - as if nothing can compare, but if I were to do a comparison. I'd say Ghostrunner is like a 3D Hotline Miami.It is harsh and brutal in the beginning, but after a few levels you get better and better. It is also very rewarding once you finish off a group of enemies and recount all the meticulous steps you took to ensure victory. Enemies aren't impossible and all have a work-around or a weakness - making it fair, yet rarely forgiving. (That's why checkpoints exist.)However, like a comment I read awhile back of various people out there looking for easy ways to do this or that in Ghostrunner. The satisfaction and fun comes from figuring it out yourself! I completely agree and am very proud to say that I never looked at a single guide to finish the game or find any collectibles or acquire any achievements.If you pick up Ghostrunner, you will not regret it! I've never played a game like Ghostrunner and I don't regret playing it. I enjoyed every moment and will continue to play the game and the future ones some day when they are released!In short, Ghostrunner is a gentle, though still difficult fast-paced, parkour filled game. There are various things to collect that add to the decently long story as well as other things like eyecandy swords - and a story itself that doesn't require you to study it for months to understand. The game holds your hand very rarely and leaves you to develop your own method of tackling issues that face you along your journey.|All in all, it will forever hold a spot in my top 10 best games of all time. (Personally of course, but why don't you try it out to see for yourself?)

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 27.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you

_childDocuments_.review: I think a lot of hate this game gets is just because people are bad at the game. If you're not willing to pick yourself up from the dust and want the difficulty lowered for you, this is NOT the game for you. I saw from the trailers exactly what kind of game this was, so I honestly have no idea why some people are surprised at the product they get- it's exactly as you see.Fast paced, UNFORGIVING, but fair. If you die, it's literally because YOU ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up. I didn't have a single death where I felt like I got cheated by some insane hitbox. If you die, you missed the timing, the aim, or mismanaged your resources. Every time. This is a game that is perfect for anyone who has an appreciation for hack-and-slash ninja cyberpunk aesthetics, and doubly moreso for perfectionists. Are you competitive with your friends? This game will show you their run times and death counters! After spending a good few days beating the game on the first playthrough, I'm actually going back through trying to get the fastest 0-death completions of each level, and BOY is that a good mental exercise to control yourself and endure... If you're weak, this is not the game for you. If you're bad, this is not the game for you. If you're a baby, this game is not for you. My only criticism about this game, is there is a certain unit you encounter in later levels, which are essentially suicide bombers. That by itself would be fine, except they spawn INFRONT of you in levels, and run towards you. You CANNOT kill them in melee without dying, and so it seems like a contraindicated game design choice in a game that otherwise promotes expedient and continual forward progress through a level; you don't really backtrack, so why not implement the suicide bombers as a timing pressure? Spawn them BEHIND the players, that they have to OUTRUN! I don't understand strongarming the player into running in circles or using a certain upgrade to deal with them. But, that's my only gripe.All in all, 9/10. Judge the game for what it is, and if it's incompatible with YOU for the kind of player YOU are, that's on YOU, not the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Is Ghostrunner "3D Katana Zero"?...Yes. But does stand on its own? Absolutely. Soaring across the mesmerizing landscape, parkouring from nail-biting edge to certain death over and over never gets old. Dying is a regular occurrence, but is seldom distracting. With the press of a button, you are immediately back in the fight perfecting your chosen path or experimenting with a new one.  Even then, that process never gets old mainly due to the absolute knee slappin, aviator sunglasses-wearing, flickering neon bulb soundtrack by Daniel Deluxe. This soundtrack puts you in top gear and keeps your adrenaline pumping nonstop throughout the game. There a few times where it stops and goes quiet, leaving you like a kid in a grocery store who lost his mom. The personality of the game is halved without these tunes. That being said the game is not perfect. Sometimes there is just so much happening on screen it is hard to pay attention to everything. Most of the time I completely missed the story because I could not focus on the parkouring, precision executions, soundtrack, and endless world at the same time. I wanted to know more, but Katana Zero's story is a winner here. And, as wonderfully constructed as this world is, it is remarkably empty. Nothing you hit is interactable, I never saw another person walking around, and it lacks a "lived-in" quality.  These reasons did take me out of the world from time to time. Gameplay and style are king here and if you see any of the marketing or played Katana Zero and thought "huh...that seems like something I like" then you absolutely will. At $30 base price it is worth every penny. Now I gotta go slice the **** out of some veggies for dinner to the "Infiltrator OST" track.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostrunner is a AAA title in disguise. It went totally under the radar this year and it's a shame, because it's a masterpiece. In short, here are 3 reasons why:1. Movement:Much like in the DOOM franchise, movement is key. Ghostrunner has the "Move or Die" rule that DOOM games have, but tuned to 11. One bullet and you're dead. Besides feeling like a badass; utilizing the walls, rails, pickups, sliding and everything in between can be the difference between life and death. That makes it all the more difficult, fast-paced, and badass.2. Combat: ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ does this game give you options. It's hard to summarize how good this portion is, because of how much depth it has. The game has a multitude of enemies; too many to count without googling it, and the modular system used to customize your playstyle makes it all the more fun. I personally ran a deflection/ranged build. Replayablility, consistent difficulty and instant restarts means you have the perfect package for a high octane game.3. Pacing/Progression: Encounters in this game get harder and harder as time progresses, but it never gets to a point where you're feeling lost in all the content here. The pacing in this game is phenomenal, and even better than the greats like DOOM Eternal. Even with tons of enemies, tons of mods, tons of ways to move, tons of customization both asthetic and functional, you never feel like you're falling behind. You're always kept at the front of the race, and that makes it all the more smooth for when you get that picture perfect finish.Combine 1,2&3 together in a fight and you start to get addicted, fast. In my opinion, this should've been GAME OF THE YEAR 2020

It's not fun having to replay a fight over and over again, or dying at the fricking last enemy in a fight, having to do everything again. This is extreme in boss fights. Those are so annoying and pure trial and error.Btw. devs added an "easy" mode which gives you the possibility to play the game with a second life in each fight. Sounds good? _childDocuments_.review: In Ghostrunner you play as a cyborg ninja in a cyberpunk dystopian future. It has a core element - first person platforming - and it executes it almost to perfection. You run on walls, grapple hook through the air, dash, dodge or deflect bullets, and hack through enemies with a katana. Virtually every enemy can be killed with one blow, but the same applies to you as well.The game does a great job at constantly and with good pacing introducing new platforming elements, enemy types, level layouts, etc., which varies the gameplay enough to never make it stale. And because the movement is so fluid, the levels are so well-constructed, and the combat is so satisfying (who doesn't like slicing dudes into bloody giblets?), Ghostrunner has great replay value - especially if you're interested in going for fewer death / speed runs. I'd highly recommend picking this game up.It also features a really good synthwave soundtrack by Daniel Deluxe, perfect for fast-paced cyborg ninja-ing.9.4 / 10

It is very unforgiving, at least in my experience, although I don't think that's a bad thing.  One shot from enemies will kill you, a slight misstep during the parkour segments will kill you, etc.  That said, I very much enjoyed the feeling of improvement during each combat.  I might run in and die without a kill the first time, then adjust my strategy and timing a bit the next time around and do a bit better.  Each time, I was able to fine tune a bit more until I was able to clear the combat.  Combat never really feels stale either, as the game does a great job of changing map designs to mix up combat strategies, and introduces new enemies every couple levels, which forces you to rethink the strategies you've been using previously.Soundtrack is fantastic in my opinion.  Very cyberpunk soundtrack, and I often found myself vibing to the soundtrack while playing.  Art direction is also great, and really captures the cyberpunk aesthetic.Story is solid.  It's no Mass Effect, but it's interesting enough to hold the game together.  The story is typically told through the dialogue between your character and others, and that dialogue typically happens during the parkour parts, which helps give something to focus on during those sections while not distracting you from combat.  Voice acting is good too.In terms of replayability, I could definitely see myself playing through again in the future.  I periodically play through Mirror's Edge despite knowing the story and the levels, and I am still entertained.  I would consider this to be similar.  The parkour and combat is entertaining enough to keep me interested, and there are multiple ways to approach every combat.  You can enter combat from different areas and mix up your strategy, and you can build your character differently to change the playstyle.  If you want to focus more on reflecting bullets, you can do that, and it's a very different playstyle than if you built your character around pure speed and agility.Overall, I would say I very much enjoyed the game.  I do wish it was a bit longer, but as I discussed above, there is enough replayability that I'm not too disappointed about the length.  Would definitely recommend to anyone who likes cyberpunk, platformers/parkour games, or is just looking for a challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: This game looked really cool. I love games with emphasis on mobility. Parkour, wallrunning, grappling hooks, and quick decapitations? Sign me up, especially for 50% off!Unfortunately, this game feels very very clunky. Constantly the game's pacing grinds to a screeching halt by forcing you to do lame, generic puzzles that feel out of place in contrast to the fast paced action. The bosses also felt really generic. You'll constantly get stuck on objects or inexplicably your character won't move the way you want it to (most frequently for me it was my character not jumping off the walls and not sticking to walls). The timings are absolutely awful for things like parries, especially for the ninjas. You have to time everything earlier than you would expect because the game's depth perception is just wrong. The grappling hook is really lame, you can only grapple to pre-determined locations, and I found it very frustrating you couldn't air-dash sideways.I'm also not a fan of the difficulty. I'm not sure how much of the game was supposed to be frustrating by being hard, because most of the difficulty and frustration to me comes from the aspects mentioned above, but this is a game where you'll constantly get cucked, you can be stuck doing the same section of a level spamming retry, and levels are extremely linear, boring, repetitive, and frustrating. Sometimes it's really unclear as to where you're supposed to go so you have to spend a minute backtracking and finding the next objective, which grinds the pace of the game to a halt.There are, of course, some things I like. The upgrade system is unique. The abilities are okay, but you don't really get to use them that much. The world is decently interesting and I didn't have any complaints about the music. When I'm not being frustrated, the game is quite fun and even addicting.I know I missed more stuff but yeah...Even at 50% off, I don't think I would recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: i would absolutely recommend this game with a few caveats. Don't get me wrong this game is awesome. It might be my new favorite game. It's fast as f**k, edgy and just generally badass. The aesthetic is awesome, and manages to actually tell a pretty decent story. Consider it the content that was cut from Cyberpunk 2077.However, that being said, there are some caveats. This game is hard. Not Sekiro hard, but maybe Dark Souls hard. The difference is that you have quick respawn because the game understands that you're going to screw up, and when you do you have the chance to retry. This game goes down a lot smoother when you think about what you're doing and approach things methodically. However, even with that in mind, it can often feel like you don't have a chance to get lucky in this game. Sometimes there are moments in other games where the button mashing works out. This is not one of those games. Particularly, the basic early game enemies will "cheat" shooting in a way their typical shooting rhythm doesn't allow if you do something like walk in a straight line for more than .5 seconds, or take a fight in a way you aren't supposed to. It feels like the game has a tendency to push you to approach things in a certain way, and that can take the difficulty to unfun levels sometimes. There are also a variety of puzzles and movement encounters that don't have any intuitive logic behind them besides throwing yourself at a wall until you figure them out. Figuring out the approach to these sorts of things should feel rewarding, and give you that "click" feeling when you finally get it. But with this game, more than a few times, there are moments where you will say "oh, that's what I'm supposed to do. That's dumb."But really that's all nitpicking. This game is freaking awesome, and really pushes the speed of a single player game. If you like Cyberpunk, badass Katanas, parkour, and oneshotting s**t, this game is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Going in having played the demo 10 times over and experimenting with strategies over and over I was more than excited to buy and play this game upon its release. This game outshines the free demo in spades and is recommended to anyone who enjoys tight, and challenging platforming games. The story is relatively deep, and it is clear the development team truly made the project they wanted to make and did not buckle under any pressure to change their vision. The music is great and super “synthy” to fit the amazingly realized cyberpunk aesthetic incredibly, and the visuals look more like a Triple A title more than a $30 game. A game that is styled like this I went in expecting a 4-to-5-hour campaign; a short but sweet game with little lore and focusing completely on controls and moment to moment game play. However, with the story previously mentioned being more complex than I thought, so was the game itself. Taking all the roughly 8.8 hours played to complete. There were moments of glitching and clipping through the floor that caused a death or two that felt a tad unfair. More often than these however were wall jumps you could swear you grabbed, and you saw the collision, but the game just did not think you connected to that wall caused a fall, and a death. The most aggravating part, however, was the final section post fighting the final boss. Up until this point, the game had been challenging, but also fair in its difficulty; the game shows you its challenge and allows you to overcome it with little to no “cheap shots”. The final platforming section feels like the compete opposite of this ideology to me however, as the part has a sort of optical illusion that messes with one’s eyes, causing the walls flying at you to feel confusing and makes it hard to gauge your jump resulting in a lot of time on this one section alone. The phasing through walls and not wall jumping was most prominent in this spot than any other part of the game as well. Despite these glaring issues however, I can easily recommend this game from its high-octane non-stop thrill ride of a game. The main character has an amazing move-set, and the game is at its best when fighting on rooftops jumping from drones to slice through an enemy, grapple across to a wall run, dash through another enemy, and make that perfect run through an onslaught of various enemies. If you are not sure if this game is worth your time and your money, play the demo and if you like it even a tiny bit, the whole game adds so much content it is an easy justification of $30.

_childDocuments_.review: This game really feels like it was made specifically for me - fast paced first person movement akin to Titanfall 2, one-hit one-kill room clearing with a lot of open ended ways to take down your opponents with skills or different movement, an interesting cyberpunk world and a pretty good synthwave soundtrack. I feel like this game doesn't expand on its ideas as much as it could - but I mean that in the best way possible. I mean it in the same way I feel like Mario Odyssey doesn't reach its full potentional, where a lot of the gameplay and mechanics are just so good that I want to see them pushed way more, and I feel like you could totally just make another game or expansion just built off of the ideas used in the first game pushed in more fun and interesting ways. It'd be amazing for this game to have some DLC or even better, a level editor.I did have a few honestly nitpicky issues with it for the most part. For one, the audio mixing on the sound effects and voice acting at some points can be kind of bad. Most of it is character dialogue being way too loud clean and crisp during some story moments, and it took me out of it a bit but it's not that big of a deal and hopefully an easy fix.I've noticed some people not saying the combat is entirely consistent, and yeah, when you start going really fast with bunnyhopping slides and gaining lots of moment hitreg can get kind of janky at some points, but throughout playing the entire game while trying to bhop as fast as possible through most combat encounters, I never felt like I got killed in a place I shouldn't. The enemies aren't 100% consistent - the melee enemies especially, but I feel as if they're consistent enough to play around when going fast (except the katana dudes, sometimes they just dont attack for some reason) and it's probably pretty hard to get them totally consistent from a programming standpoint. This might be an issue for some people looking to get into this games speedrun scene, but I'm sure that it'll make more sense as we learn more about the game.The level and setting design for the game is incredible, and the worldbuilding and story concept is super interesting, but sadly it doesn't really go anywhere that I haven't seen done before in most cyberpunk media before. It's still enjoyable and I think that Jack and Architect are written and played very well, but it's by no means groundbreaking. Shoutouts to Jack's voice actor for sounding like David Hayter.Despite my minor issues, Ghostrunner's amazing gameplay base that kept me playing for hours at my peak gamer preformace enough to get some eyestrain headaches from just how insanely fun it is to play still makes me give it a solid reccommendation for anyone who enjoys heavy movement shooters like Titanfall and extremely fast paced OHOK games like Hotline Miami. I really hope to see more from this series!

_childDocuments_.review: So you don't have to read my long-winded review: this game is amazing, and I strongly recommend a purchase. The gameplay is fast-paced and feels beautifully smooth. The game operates on a one-hit kill system (for both you and most enemies) which fulfills that power fantasy and the literally non-existent load times (on my PC) ensure you are quickly back in the action when you die. The graphics are also very impressive, the environments are pretty even though you often run by them quickly due to the nature of the game. If you do stop, you pick up on a bunch of scenery and fun Easter eggs that are a nice touch. Finally before I get into my minor critiques I want to touch on the very nice music by Daniel Deluxe, it's atmospheric but still with a cyberpunk/synthwave flair. The first minor critiques is the upgrade system, which requires you to find space on a grid for tetris-like collections of squares. This is more confusing than bad, I was able to fit everything I wanted to but I also felt like there should have been an simpler way to handle them. The next minor issue was the collectibles, which consist of blade skins, audio logs, and little trinkets with lore attached to them. The problem is that they are both well hidden and it's somewhat hard to explore in this game, with the movement being fast and levels sometimes locking doors behind you. There's an upgrade that highlights them on the map which is basically the only way to find them, but even then it only shows a vague direction which if you happen to wander through a sealing door kinda sucks. You want to find the logs and trinkets though because with out the audio logs the story lacks some depth, and the lore built through the trinkets also helps flesh the game out. It's not game-breaking and I was probably able to fine 90% of them by myself, but it just felt like a strange choice to sometimes stop the action for minutes at a time to find a collectible.
