_childDocuments_.review: This is another one of those "I wanted to love this game" reviews, but give me a second to explain why.I've gone through the positive and negative reviews, and this is what I think to be true:Positives: - Good Visuals- Good Soundtrack- Somewhat Interesting Story- Fun MechanicsNegatives: + Slow Pacing- One of the tags for this game is "Fast-Paced," but I didn't feel that this was fast paced at all. The movement feels slow even when wall running, and I think they misrepresent how fast you travel in the display video.+ Clunky Movement- I feel that movement is everything in a platforming game, and I didn't feel like the movement was fluid. This was an issue that disappointed me even in the demo. + Bad Direction- While there are plenty of useful indicators in the game, I feel that there isn't always a clear direction for moving forward. There are a lot of needless platforms that only serve to confuse you. Sometimes you can skip platforming segments by grappling ahead.Final Thoughts:  I didn't have an issue with the game's difficulty at all. My main issue was the movement itself: it's too slow and boring in my opinion. The Cybervoid was especially boring and slow, and the main character doesn't seem excited to be there either through dialogue. At one point there's a puzzle that feels so out of place, and it was at this point that I realized I wasn't excited to go back to the main scheme of things either. It's possible that there are upgrades for movement later in the game, but I strongly prefer upgradeable combat over speed in a game like this. I think I'll refund this if I still can.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot rate this game neutral so I will unfortunately have to go with negative as that is how I felt at the end of my first playthrough.I went into this game believing it would be a fun, fast-paced slash game where it would be non-stop action and constant parkour, while yes, 90% of the game is that, this game almost weeded me out at the first boss which completely turned the gameplay counter clockwise and it only got worse after that.I beat the game and now I'm stubbornly trying to beat hardcore mode without trying to rip my hair out.EDIT: I gave up on hardcode mode, it is just not worth trying even if you do not get angry easily, this mode tests your patience and just wondering how much ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ you're able to take until you give up, I do not recommend this difficulty even if you found the base game easier than me, the only positive thing is that almost all the dialogue is muted, the unnecessary/slow puzzles and segments are disabled and you also have all your skills and abilitiesthe good: - core gameplay is fun, outsmarting your enemies and killing back to back is immensely fun, the parkour moments are also insanely satisfying - abilities are fun and all have their own purpose - unique skill system so you can't just grab all the good ones and beat the game easily - almost no rng, it is just purely your skill (except for one enemy) - unique enemies, all of them have their own weaknesses and strengths and they don't repeat up to the end of the game (except the same one enemy that also gives you the rng bull) - the game doesn't reward nor punish you for thinking outside the box, there are minimal amount of death barriers and no invisible walls, you can parkour completely differently than intended and still progress likewise you can beat combat encounters differently than intended as wellthe bad:  - bugs, parkour system can ♥♥♥♥ you over just for the sake of it, sometimes you do not kill the enemy even if you hit them - aimbot enemies up close, if you miss your timing on dash or sensory boost, you will get shot 100% of the time and you have to repeat the combat scene - enemies ranging from just annoying to downright broken (almost no in-between) - bosses are completely useless in this game, they are there just for the sake of the story (final "boss" after what you thought was the final boss is decent) - tutorials and mechanics explained at start, later on just thrown at you and you're expected to know - projectiles are way too fast and sensory boost just doesn't feel like it's enough to avoid them (in hardcore mode especially)the ugly:  - this game is , you will die in one hit and you will kill in one hit, and you WILL die often, no avoiding it - without a skill, enemies can be easily missed and you can die without knowing they were there - indicator to show you where to go will straight up just be missing and you have no idea where to go - you can easily get lost without knowing where to go as well - unlike mirror's edge where highlighted objects are easily discerned so you know where to go, in this game they blend in with the environment and you have no idea where to go some of the times - ziplines are completely awful, they have the tiniest of hitboxes so you just miss latching on and fall into a pit- don't bother with hardcore mode, finish the game once and don't touch it at all.I'm rating this game at 5/10, when the game is fun, it is immensely fun but when it starts going sour, you feel like you want to smack the ♥♥♥♥ out of the level and enemy designer(s) of this game. If you have really high patience and have no anger issues, pick this game up 100%.If you however struggle with parkour games and get easily flustered, avoid this game at all costs, not even assisted mode will save you from 50% of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ this game will throw at you.

_childDocuments_.review: ConflictedThat's probably the best way to put my thoughts on this game.  On the one hand, it's got amazing speed and really makes you feel amazing during combat; on the other hand it's poorly optimized and will probably be far more frustrating than fun your first time through.The Story is solid, the voice acting is done well and the game is extremely pretty, but due to it's poor optimization, you're unlikely to see just how pretty it can be.  My Rig can handle just about every AAA title these days at max settings minus Ray Tracing on an ultra-wide monitor and run at a consistent 60 FPS or higher.  yet in this game, I had to bump all the setting down to mid to run at consistent frames (even after capping them) and even after that I still ran into frame drops on a regular basis.I'm not really a graphics snob or FPS evangalist, I think a consistent 30 FPS is great for almost any game, but Ghostrunner is an extremely fast FPS that focuses on first person platforming and melee combat, when a frame is dropped, you're dead.  So, because of this, I really had some negative moments in my playthrough.Now, if you drop the settings down a bit, you're likely to run the game fine for the most part, so you'll run into the second major issue I have with the game: it's very inconsistent with it's rules and it doesn't properly explain it's rules either.  One of the things that killed me more than anything else was inconsistencies in game mechanics.  Sometimes I'll swing, see the swing go through a bullet or enemy, and die.  Other times I'll obviously have mistimed my attack and kill the enemy.  Sometimes the enemy tracking will be spot on and I can avoid being hit reliably, other times the enemy will spray so far wide that I'll be hit, even though I'm doing what the game wants me to by wall running to avoid bullets.As for not telling you what to do, most enemies require a specific method to dispatch, but the game won't explain what that method is, so you'll likely do some really dumb things to deal with it.  I finished the game and still ran circles around the shield enemies to kill them because I couldn't find a better way, but with the speed and precision the rest of the game requires, that can't be the correct approach.  Several times, you will be wall running and need to dodge off the wall, then return to that same wall to live.  How you do this is never explained, so I did what I thought I should by dodging in the air back at the wall after the obstacle.  This didn't work reliably, and it wasn't until the final level I discovered that you are supposed to look at the wall while in the air and dodge straight ahead towards it.  This resolved all my issues with wall running and it would have been really nice to have been told this was an intended mechanic.All in all, this is a fantastic game that has some major pitfall in exocution.  If you want a game like Katana Zero but in first person, this is that game.  If you want something with high difficulty, but a high skill ceiling, this is a great game for that.  If you want a game to just have fun with, this game will probably end with you smashing your keyboard instead.PS, Screw those exploding enemies near the end, they don't add anything but annoyance to an already frustrating game.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Changing the review to "Recommended" after playing more. It gets better and, overall, I feel like I came in with the wrong midset, expecting the game to be a fluid runner rather than a melee-based kill-them-all affair (speedrunners do contactless runs, but those require an uncanny ability to scale unmarked walls). Also, technical improvements happened.The good:* Perfect execution looks great.* Swords.* Synthwave music.* Cyberpunk aesthetics (outside of cybervoid, of which we shall not speak).* You can use upgrades that modify your skills. They range from practical to great.* It's not $60.The bad: * Early levels feel somewhat cramped and full of annoying mechanics like the invulnerability spheres placed on surfaces you must parkour to.* The first boss fight is overly reliant on silly dodge moves.* Your dash button is also slo-mo, but only when airborne. If you're on the ground or on the wall, you get a dash instead of slo-mo. Or nothing at all if you weren't holding a direction.* Collectibles. They do not add much but... Take you out of the flow occasionally. You don't have to hunt them unless you're a completionist, of course.Buy if you like trial and error gameplay with satisfying finishes. You  have to persevere until the second third of the game where it becomes more open and freeform.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, the game itself is fine. It's frustrating but satisfying for the most part, but there's just one design choice that makes it unplayable for me. _childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic. The atmosphere it generates is simply amazing. The music, (most) of the gameplay, the story, it all creates a vibe that you are a robot ninja hellbent on slashing everything that opposes you. There's a few GLARING flaws that really pull this game down. For the most part the gameplay is flawless and has a lot of fun elements sprinkled into the dying over and over. This game lack almost any visual and audio cues. Navigating the levels is essentially you walking around the same square after you killed all the dudes there because you can't find the exit. In some instances, there are no clear indicators that tell you where you need to go. I felt lost on multiple occasions because I did not know there were platforms behind that wall or above that building. Similarly, the boss fights seem like a chore because of how precise you have to be to dodge an attack after it making no sound or its animation barely changing before you have 5 frames to not die. I have sat around for a few minutes not understanding what exactly I'd needed to do because of how little direction the game gives you. This difficulty is appreciated sometimes, obviously it shouldn't have to hold my hand, but for a first playthrough it feels incredibly tedious. Maybe I'm the only player that's experienced this kind of problem but I would say a few of my deaths are because the bosses or enemies make basically no noise when attacking, or I fell to my death during a platforming section because I had no idea where to go.Another huge problem is the inconsistency in which the platforming elements function. The grapple doesn't seem to work properly over half the time i use it. It either flings me in a direction I wasn't facing when I used the grapple, sends me completely backwards, or doesn't allow me to wall run following a grapple (which is used way more often than you'd think). I've run into multiple occasions where climbing doesn't work where it's supposed to, or I climb when I touch the ceiling of the arena I'm in (???????). The wall climb in some sections feels like I can go 2 ghostrunners high but in other sections I can't climb something my height. Wall running in some cases seems to glue the player to the wall and the player has to find some other way to finish the section because the game is just not compliant. Finally, in the later sections there is a zipline rail thing that I've run into many difficulties grabbing onto. I would say well over half of my deaths would not have happened had it not been for these platforming issues. These are the issues that can be patched out. If they are I will delete this section of the review and switch to recommending. With the platforming bugs this game is VERY VERY frustrating. It obviously didn't ruin the game and eventually you can pass through but god did it piss me off.This is probably something that can't get patched out, so it just comes with the territory of this game. It really isn't gamebreaking but the combat has so much redundancy it definitely sours some of the game. Early in the game you're introduced to walking robot enemies which I contend as some of the most difficult enemies in the game, because you cannot approach them head on. They get a small section to themselves and you learn a lot about their inclusion in fights and what priority they should have in combat. This is fun and important because the player will be fighting these enemies for the remainder of the game, its important experience they will get to use. Later, a sniper enemy is introduced in about the same way, but you fight them three times in almost identical sections and they NEVER APPEAR AGAIN. Also, some enemy types have no introduction but stay for effectively the whole game. The combat abilites have incredibly long cooldowns and all basically do the same thing (kill multiple enemies within an effective range) so there is no real variety in the way you can tackle certain sections. Because the abilities feel the same, the upgrades for these abilities also lack variety.Obviously this game is meant for replayability as opposed to first time experience. Its only a few hours long after all. But until the platforming bugs are fixed it probably isn't worth buying at all. I still had a good time, but I can't recommend the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is in a two part. The first is me mid playthrough, with a bit past initial thoughts, second is right after finishing the game for the 1st time. MID PLAYTHROUGH: I like the atmosphere, the nice flowing sections, the cinematic badass moments, but some sections feel like a fat f*****g cheap chores more than anything. I beat celeste, supermeatboy, and it felt like i had more control over my deaths there. Idk if its just the 3 hours total i have speaking right now, maybe i was blessed by Titanfall 2's movement, but sometimes you feel soooo sluggish and feels like your stuck in mud. Also not being able to continue sliding while holding crouch when landing sucks. You HAVE to hold W otherwise you hard stop. It would be fair but then when you wallrun, you dont need to touch W at all. So many inconsistencies. Will update review when i play moreAFTER BEATING THE GAME REVIEW UPDATE: Alright, game's fantastic. I still have my gripes over some movement mechanics that are inconsistent depending on if you are midair or grounded, like cant side boost mid air but you can grounded. I also have no idea why you NEED to press W when landing crouched to keep the momentum going but you dont need to press W while wall running. Sometimes the air acceleration/deceleration can be very jarring too. That's the only complaints i got. Also the big mechas that shoot massive walls, they can kiss my metal 4SS. APART from those complaints, and they are minor in the grand scheme of things, the game is just really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good. Difficult enough, sometimes cheap but its not THAT bad once you get how to do it. Music is beyond good too. Very fun, a bit short but i dont mind it. I do recommend the game for sure, 8/10, loses two point due to inconsistent movement techs and some cheap sections that are more of a "did you get lucky on that try or not"

_childDocuments_.review: From its jaw-dropping visuals to its pulse-pounding gameplay, every moment of this cyberpunk masterpiece is a thrill ride like no other.Let's start with the visuals. The neon-soaked world of "Ghostrunner" is a sight to behold, with its futuristic cityscapes and sleek cybernetic designs creating a stunning backdrop for your high-octane adventures. Whether you're leaping between skyscrapers or slicing through enemies with your razor-sharp katana, every frame is a work of art that immerses you in a world of pure cyberpunk bliss.But it's not just about looks. Oh no, the gameplay is where "Ghostrunner" truly shines. The controls are tight and responsive, allowing you to dash, slide, and parkour your way through each level with precision and finesse. And then there's the combat, which is fast-paced, challenging, and oh-so-satisfying. With your trusty katana in hand, you'll slice and dice your way through waves of enemies in a ballet of violence that is as beautiful as it is brutal.And let's not forget about the story. Set in a dystopian future where humanity is on the brink of extinction, "Ghostrunner" tells a gripping tale of rebellion, revenge, and redemption that will keep you hooked from start to finish. With its memorable characters, thought-provoking themes, and unexpected twists and turns, it's a narrative rollercoaster ride that will keep you guessing until the very end.In conclusion, "Ghostrunner" is a must-play for fans of action games and cyberpunk aesthetics alike. With its stunning visuals, tight gameplay, and gripping story, it's an experience that will leave you breathless and begging for more. So grab your katana, jack in, and prepare to ascend to new heights in this electrifying journey through the neon-lit streets of the future.Consider checking my gameplay before making your purchase

_childDocuments_.review: This was a letdown, to say the least. This is sold as a speedrun game, but in reality you have many long sections in which you lose all of you skills and need to solve endless 3D first person jump puzzles. What joy. _childDocuments_.review: This game does first person platforming right! It pairs fast paced jumping, wallrunning and zipping around with equally fast combat that will let you feel like a badass... after you die a bunch. The game is hard. But well placed checkpoints along with a killer soundtrack will keep your adrenalin up and will see you wanting to jump straight back into the action!Once you beat the game, it offers a ton of replayability through some collectibles, but most importantly through encouraging you to finish each level in less time and with fewer deaths. Finding shortcuts is a blast, as you can run on pretty much every wall, sometimes skipping entire rooms.If you enjoy fast paced gameplay that tests your skill without being too frustrating*, treat yourself and pick up this game.Also anyone that thought Mirror's Edge needed better combat, give this one a shot!*Unless you need to leave in the middle of one of the longer levels. The game doesn't save your progress until you finish a level, so if you need to turn it off before then, it can be annoying to have to do the first half again.

_childDocuments_.review: This game ticks many boxes for me. The combat is fluid and juicy, the parkour elements are fast and smooth. Story exposition happens during the platforming, which is great because it keeps up the pace. The soundtrack is amazing, too. When everything clicks, clearing an arena is an amazing and empowering experience. If I would have to describe this game to a friend, I'd say it is a mix of Hotline Miami and Doom - which is an achievement by it's own, well done developers.There are issues however:* Some of the core gameplay is not polished. I died or got my game-flow interrupted way too many times because of weird level geometry, and the wallrunning, ledge-grabbing and chain-hooking mechanics misbehaving.* In my opinion the story is predictable and the quality in writing fluctuates

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Imagine Superhot crossed with Mirrors Edge. My only serious gripe with the game is that it is deceptive in how you approach arenas. With the mechanics at play here, you could do anything, but they are basically courses that you can run around with enemies dotted about. It does force you to use the mechanics in combat which is a strength. With the quick paced music, it feels like a series of time trials. It would be better if you could at least enter the arenas from different angles or something to give you the feeling of choice. You can block a bullet if you time a slash right which might prove helpful - later upgrades to deflect.I spent the first few levels changing my controls to find what worked for me and finally got there. There are a few weird decisions like Q being the ability button which means you need to take one finger off WASD (A for me) and in this game, movement is key. That was changed to the back button on my mouse. You may also find changing dash to right-click useful and moving grapple to the foward button on the mouse. This assumes your mouse has these. Dash, Slash and Jump are your best friends in this game.The wall run is still a bit weird in that you need to hold space for just the right amount of time so that you initiate the run, or you will fall off. It should really just initiate on contact. Apart from that, I found that it eventually clicks.You will get your money's worth if you enjoy trial style games. Lots of replay value to perfect stages like in something like Mirrors Edge or Superhot. I have seen it for sale (as of release) for about 40% in at least 2 reputable places, and at that kind of price, it's worth it imo.You will fall off the map. Happens.

_childDocuments_.review: It's tough to rate this game. I love virtually every aspect of it, the problem is it's main aspect falls on its face. It seemed like this was meant to be a cyberpunk Mirror's Edge and that it gives you stats relating to time and number of deaths at the end of each level implies it is meant to speed run. The issue is that it's far too inconsistent for a speed run. The controls are no where near responsive or accurate enough. The enemies are too random. The timings always feel slightly off. When you have a good run and are making fast progress there is always something to block your path and undo the lead you gained on yourself. Moving parts of the level and aerial drones that don't fire at you once, but then fire at you another time leading you to either die or deflect the shot back at it, destroying the thing you needed to traverse a massive gap is just frustrating.I recommend this game if you intend to have a bit of fun. I don't recommend it if you intend to speed run it or really push yourself, it just isn't accurate or responsive enough to handle it.PS - whoever designed that elevator level with the lasers is an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.

_childDocuments_.review: Ah yes, Violence, Speed and Momentum: The game.Ghostrunner was the game meant to keep us occupied until Cyberpunk released, but ironically in the end it turned out to be a better more solid game than Cyberpunk.It’s the only game where the actual speed run might be faster than this review.Brutally difficult combination of Mirror's Edge, Dishonored, and Hotline Miami/Katana Zero. Died 100 times on stage 6 alone. No matter how many times I died I always kept coming back for more cause it was fun. It’s a very fast platformer/fps style slasher where failure is common. There is a lot of playtime here to enjoy. Single player delight with great mechanics, intense but fair difficulty curve, fun story and no online nonsense. Great game. I have adhd so it's these types of games that challange my lightning reaction times and my lack of patience for video games, and that just feels incredible. The time trials are pure pain and suffering. I drove my self insane trying to master them all. It’s something l'd absolutely recommend to people who like a challenge. I can't think of many games in recent times where there are no cut scenes, its just a linear game and the way the game presents the story is just through dialogue as you play. I like these types of games because cut scenes or moments where control is taken away from you feels like the pacing just slams into a brick wall. I loved this game because it reminded me of some of the classic single player linear fps titles, and aside from Doom Eternal we havent gotten many of those recently.It’s great, I loved every minute of it, my eyes were bloodshot half the time and I learned there are new types of radiating wrist pain that go to my f**king chin. It's one of those games where you gradually get better and better at it to the point of doing some cool ninja sh*t every few minutes. And the game's one-hit kills help make that possible. The gameplay is tight, responsive and fluid. The levels are interesting and there is enough enemy variety to keep things fresh. It never felt like it was repetitive because it was the different combinations of enemies together with the different topographical configuration of the levels that provided the variety. Aesthetically they’re all very similar but in reality there’s so many different levels that are mechanically distinct.The cyberpunk vibe is very well achieved too. Also the DLC is fantastic with the amount of power it gives you, so much fun. The story was straightforward and simple, but decently executed. I expected nothing from a game of this type, so I was actually positively surprised. The voice acting is good for the most part, which helps things. The bosses are kinda hit or miss though. I liked the final one, but not so much the other 2, at least they have fair checkpoints in them.It was hard but honestly most of the sections were fair and not cheap. Sure it has some difficulty spikes here and there but they don't ruin the experience. I didn't mind the trial and error gameplay, it felt good when I eventually cleared the room perfectly. Also I found that it's much more fun on a subsequent playthrough when you already know what you're doing and you just fly through the levels - that's where the game is at its best IMO. I played through it all and then the ultra hard mode because, yes, I am a masochist!Also, playing through project hell again right now, cause I'm too poor for the second one yet. Some of the most fun\frustrating times of my life! Also thought the tetris skill tree was a great touch, too! It has its flaws, but the overall product was actually impressive I'll say. I think they mostly succeeded in what they wanted to offer.If you are on the fence about the difficulty, let me say this. When it comes to video games, I do like a fair challenge, but I am in no way a masochist ALL the time - Dark Souls was not made for me at first either. BUT, after nearly 500 deaths in just under 6 hours, I beat the game and... I loved it. The reviews are right, there are moments where you'll be stuck - take a break, breathe, and come back to it later. Really fun game, and what an awesome challenge.All I have to add is that if you’re even remotely interested, you just have to try it. the gameplay, the voice acting, the fluidity of the movement, the story, graphics, the aesthetics and the unforgiving difficulty... it's an excellently made game and definitely worth every penny on my book. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostrunner has exceeded my expectations so far.  It's like Hotline Miami, Mirror's Edge, and Ruiner had a tube baby and perhaps surprising some, it was a beautiful tube baby.It has its imperfections, such as dropped inputs, pathing issues, not sticking to walls properly, and randomly losing momentum but they definitely don't ruin the experience at all.  It will push you to be perfect and get that perfect run through a level and force you to learn mechanics and exit your comfort zone perhaps sooner than you would like.It's a difficult game.  It does not hold your hand and you will die.  Over and over again, you will die.  Checkpoints are generous, but there are certain parts of levels that are frustrating because of how much damage vomit is on the screen that require perfect timing or you're back to the beginning of the area.  It's rewarding in this regard, because you'll see yourself breezing through parts after dying through them multiple times.  It's a type of progression that feels most rewarding; you actually see yourself improving minute to minute.If you enjoy one-mistake-and-you're-dead types of games that reward being flexible and thinking outside of the box, you owe it to yourself to give this one a shot.It is fantastic and I thank the developers for giving us something this punishing and rewarding.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostrunner is your chance to play Katana Zero in 1st person. If you're a jungler in League, think "Master Yi simulator." Ghostrunner has brutal but fair difficulty and requires lightning fast reflexes at all times. The tutorial for this game is at least 5 times harder than the hardest parts in Titanfall, and some of the endgame here almost gave me carpal tunnel. I died a hundred plus times on some levels, but it was always my fault, and the checkpoint restarts immediately.Slick combat that makes puzzles out of parkour centered skirmishes is only part of the fun. This cyberpunk world is lush with neon lens flare, robotic voices, and virtual reality dreamscapes full of non-Euclidean geometry. The plot is typical but competently executed. This game is a must-play if you like punishing difficulty, parkour movement (Titanfall, Mirror's Edge, etc.), and cyberpunk. P.S. there's a demo!

_childDocuments_.review: The trial and error in its glory... This game is beautiful and figuring out the fighting paths and strategies is actually fun sometimes. _childDocuments_.review: Ghostrunner is the ultimate “cyberpunk ninja parkour simulator” that will have you zooming, slashing, and yeeting your way through a neon-soaked dystopian skyscraper like the edgiest anime protagonist you always wanted to be. Developed by One More Level and 3D Realms, this game combines the heart-pounding speed of Mirror’s Edge with the intensity of Dark Souls—all while looking like Blade Runner turned up to 11. Here’s why Ghostrunner is the adrenaline-fueled challenge you never knew you needed but absolutely can’t resist.Gameplay: Zoom Zoom Slice SliceImagine this: you’re a cybernetic sword-wielding assassin who’s faster than Sonic and deadlier than Sephiroth. You’ve got one-hit kills on enemies, but guess what? They’ve also got one-hit kills on you. This isn’t a game; it’s a precision-speedrun simulator. Every encounter is about dashing, wall-running, and perfectly timing every single attack or else… You. Go. Splat.Expect to die, and die a lot. But every respawn is faster than your heartbeat when you’re about to dodge that final bullet—making every retry feel less like failure and more like a hyper-speed tutorial in becoming a cyber ninja god. Think you’re done with the tutorial? Nope. The game will hand you more skills like time-slowing and grapple hooks that will make you feel like you’re Neo, but with even better wifi.Story and Setting: Cyberpunk 2077 But With Functional MechanicsThe story is a vibe. You’re “Jack,” a Ghostrunner, taking orders from “The Architect,” who’s essentially a cyber version of JARVIS if he was grumpy and hellbent on overthrowing a supervillain. You’re climbing the Tower, taking down corporate goons, and slicing through a dystopian mess of neon lights, oppressive tech, and rogue AIs. The aesthetic is straight-up cyberpunk overload—glowing cities, rain that probably costs as much as rent, and enough synthwave beats to make you feel like you’re streaming on Twitch, even if you’re alone in your room.Graphics and Sound: Like If Daft Punk Were SamuraiThe visuals are chef’s kiss, dripping in neon and dark, gritty details. Every corridor, rooftop, and enemy feels plucked straight out of an AI’s dream about the perfect cyberpunk world. It’s as if the devs thought, “What if we made the entire game look like the best moments of every sci-fi movie trailer?”And the soundtrack? Absolute banger. It’s like someone took the DOOM OST, dunked it in neon goo, added some synthwave, and sprinkled in an unhealthy dose of adrenaline. Each track will keep you in the zone, like you’re locked in a TikTok loop of high-energy beats and relentless action.Difficulty: Git Gud SimulatorIf you thought Dark Souls was hard, Ghostrunner is here to tell you, “Hold my cyber sword.” Every enemy encounter is a deadly dance, every mistake ends in respawn, and every successful wall run makes you feel like a glitched-out ninja legend. There’s no “easy mode” here. You git gud or you git dead.Ghostrunner wants you to memorize every move like you’re trying to impress that one kid in middle school who swore by Guitar Hero. By the time you finally get through some of the tougher levels, you’ll feel like you’re not just playing the game; you’re transcending it.VerdictGhostrunner is a lit experience wrapped in a rage-inducing difficulty that will test your reflexes, patience, and ability to meme through the pain. It’s brutal, beautiful, and absurdly rewarding. If you want to know what it’s like to be a katana-wielding speed demon in a dystopian world, strap in and press start. Just be prepared to die… and laugh… and die again.Rating: 9/10Ghostrunner is here to make you feel like an unstoppable cyber-samurai—even if that means you’ll die about 500 times first. But don’t worry: every time you hit respawn, you’ll get just a little closer to becoming a true ghost in the machine.

_childDocuments_.review: I really really wanted to like this game. The thing is though, I do but only because it's got great ideas that weren't executed correctly (or that just shouldn't even be in the game period). There are some major improvements that could be made to make this game so much better. When I first played the demo I thought to myself, "Now THIS is going to be such a fun game." because whether it was running on walls or jumping from here to there, the combat complemented it nicely. The game FLOWED; unfortunately, this is not what I could say about the official game. I am constantly finding myself having to restart back to the checkpoint because of stupid reasons: Either I cannot react or precisely play in the way the game wants me to, or the basic mechanics for movement just do NOT work. For a game that requires such precision, it's absolutely necessary that I should be able to move or attack without having to worry about it working. I am completely confident in my abilities and understand the effort it takes to play a game like this, but just not when I don't have confidence in the game itself. At times the combat, the movement, everything feels great but then you reach that one point in the level and it all goes downhill from there.Here is what I believe is affecting the flow of the game:- Enemies: Get rid of all the tedious ones that either make you run in circles trying to kill them (EX: enemy with the shield) or that have such a wide range of fire (EX: T.O.M.)- Movement: Grappling, wall running, wall jumping, [unintentionally] climbing,- Level Design: Walls or unclear pathways that obstruct or cause you to fall to your death because you're going too 'fast' in a "fast-paced" gameThere may be more to mention but those are the main aspects of the game that irritate me the most. All of these mess up the whole flow of the game. You literally CANNOT just run into a battle. You have to play this game the way it was designed, however, it's quite hard to do even that because movement doesn't work half the time.

_childDocuments_.review: The sound design is awesome, it's exactly what you'd expect, and it is consistently of high quality. Same goes with the visuals, pretty much everything looks amazing. Slashing the heads off of enemies, and all the rest of the animations are sweet. The parkour is great most of the time, even if it has some occasional hiccups. Restarting after a death is instant, assuming the nearest checkpoint is close enough to the fun.Puzzles. The puzzles are really bad. Fortunately, they are far and few in between, so you won't be spending too much time on them :). The story is... lackluster at best.  and  are decent characters, but far from exceptional. And  is just badly written at best.The enemies... oh boy the enemies. Half of the game involves combat, and only one enemy is not extraordinarily unfair (flying turret... cause it rarely attacks...). For example, the grunts: They will 360 no scope you. I am not kidding, you can go behind them and they will turn around in an instant and shoot you with pinpoint accuracy. If you have aggro on them, they will snipe you in the back of your head from across the map. Almost every ranged enemy suffers these same problems, except an additional problem added on top. Wider shots so you are more likely to get hit by stray bullets, or more bullets to so you can't dodge via dashing or parrying. The melee enemies are even worse. The first ones you meet have invulnerability when they jump to you, and can't even be parried. The  are walking invulnerable quick time events that home from behind...Generally, the combat itself is frustrating. I often found myself getting shot by an off screen enemy, shot by enemies with superhuman turning speed or hit by an invulnerable enemy. I more often than not felt that a death was due to the game being unfair than my own fault, just to restart and slam my head into the metaphorical wall and getting shot by another off screen enemy. And don't even get me started on the bosses...TL;DR: The game looks, feels and sounds amazing, until you get shot in the back of the head from across the map.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice action game with a very stylish feel. You die often, but checkpoints are frequent and reloading is fast so there is no particular problem with trying the same battle 20+ times before succeeding. I find battles to be almost puzzle-like in their design, with you trying to figure out the best way to approach a shooter from behind, then wall-sliding around a second to hit a shield generator first, etc. Overall, interesting gameplay with fun gimmicks. Felt really rewarding for me to go through the early levels once I beat the game to see all the progress I've made in mastering it. Expect 10 hours of gameplay to get through, then you have the hardcore mode and bonus levels.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: the game is good, performs well, enemies are alright, but has a meh story. Not much for replayability and there is a lot of randomized things for something that feels like it should be speedran. There's a couple bugs but not many, one main one being me CTDing with something to do with my graphics card iirc. I believe running in Dx 11 mode fixed this though I didn't play in it long enough to notice. I don't feel the game is worth the full $30, maybe pick it up on a 50% off sale. While I recieved the game for free from a friend, I was close to spending ~$25 on it and would've likely regretted it.The Overall) The gameplay is quite fun, having a 1 shot death is quite interesting and adds some level of challenge, though it doesn't make it extremely hard on it's own. Performance is alright, with a 3800XT and 2070 Super, frames averaged around 120 on epic settings with Ray Tracing off, so compare that as you will. But the main issues I have with the game come from the story, being relatively lackluster given what the whole cyberpunk genre is at their disposal. The enemies are also extremely annoying in some cases and feel very random, while the game feels it should be the same each time, as it seems a perfect candidate for speedrunning.Minor spoilers below.The Enemies) So the enemies in this game are alright at best. There are a couple enemies which I found extremely annoying during my playthrough. I'll start with their accuracy, as it applies to all enemies, and it felt very hit or miss. They would be either snipers or not able to hit the broad side of a barn. Onto all enemies, the first of which is the machinegunner-type one who shoots blue bullets, as I found them relatively difficult compared to the rest. Their rate of fire seemed extremely high and difficult to deflect and actually survive, which was sometimes necessary to kill them. The next is the shield, which is a good enemy all around, though if you hit their shield it would send you through the sky and was quite annoying sometimes. The next enemy, and my least favorite, were these weird crawling things that were pretty much only there to forward the plot (I'll call them monsters in the section about the plot), and were basically suicide bombers and were quite annoying, because you have no way of killing them unless they go a certain distance specific to each enemy or use an ability, which recharges way too slow compared to how often they appear. The next enemy wasn't really explained much, and pretty much was the epitomy of random. They would teleport randomly when you get close, unless they haven't finished firing. sometimes it'd go five feet infront of you, and other times it'd go to the opposite side of the map. There was also this sniper and a sentry turret which were barely in the game and felt like their goal was just to slow the game down some.******Major spoilers below.******Story) So first I'll say what was good about it. They chose to go for the cyberpunk genre, which gives you a lot of freedom, and the story they went with is pretty good, and the character development is alright, though that's pretty much all there is.Being a cyberpunk genre game, I came in pretty much expecting a story that has a hard moral dilemma in it, because the cyberpunk genre as a whole embodies that, though the game was extremely linear, with no options to do anything at all, your character spoke for you the entire time. Not a bad thing in it's own, but I'd like to have some sort of control over dialogue paths that maybe prioritized one character over another, which would make it feel more personal. A basic rundown of the story is this Architect finds you -somehow- and can communicate with you -somehow- and some exposition is explained through the character slowly remembering things. You are the Architect, or Adam's, security and the main antagonist of the game, the Keymaster, or Maara as I will refer to her from here on, backstabbed Adam and you. You end up working with the Architect to kill Maara. There is also another character, Zoe, who is only in the game for exposition. She is the last known survivor of the Climbers, a rebellion group wiped by Maara, and gives you some lore throughout the game. She also makes you do a mission to save a certain level iirc, but in the end it barely has any effect on the story. She is pulled away near the end of the game because of some supposed meet with another resistance member, but this avenue is never explored despite seeming like a trap, and nothing ever happens from it. She is alive in the ending scene so IDK what it was about. It is revealed that you are in a tower, despite the admittedly good looking environment making it seem like a city, and the rest of the world is just inhospitable, for whatever reason. Never explained, or if it was it was very brief and skipped over quickly. You then go through the game and near the end, where the game becomes more annoying then fun. The monsters from earlier are made entirely to paint Maara as a bad guy, or at least it felt that way, because without them and the insane babbling there would actually be a good moral choice, who is right, Adam or Maara. In the end it doesn't matter because you are forced into a fight with Maara, then Adam turns on you and you kill him as well, saving the day. I expected the Architect to become bad, as I do with early allies in most cyberpunk media, though his reveal to be evil was predictable and uninteresting. In the end I recommend the game because it is enjoyable, though only if bought on sale and if you don't care much about story.

_childDocuments_.review: Positives▫️Parkour with Combat▫️MusicAnnoyances▫️Tutorials - A tutorial should never be a progression blocker if tied to the story▫️Colliders - The Game should allow the player to recover their flow if they made a jump too high or low as long as they perform a sane collision. Adding animations specific to recovery allows the game to have more depth.▫️Clipping - The Game should make sure that the player is following “a path”, and should not throw them in dead-ends or unrecoverable clipping that is not immediately a game-over trigger.▫️World Building - Objects and set-pieces within the world should be logically and organically setup unless the game is purposefully trying to be irrational. Each object interacted by the world should flow through time, otherwise the world will communicate that it was illogically hand-crafted e.g. Parkour is mostly Shipping Container (Plates) hung to make the traversal walls. But to the world around, it doesn’t make sense for someone to go around neatly hang it on an industrial scale.▫️Spawn Points - A spawn point should always direct the player towards the objective and should not have interruptions.▫️Physics - Unless the game is geared towards fantasy, the physics of the game should be consistent. e.g. For a slide mechanic where the floor is going down should never slide to the right, left, or worse up.▫️Enemy AI - AI Tracking should be advanced enough to observe and react and have the necessary blind-spots such that they are never invulnerable against the playerImprovements to consider▫️NPC - Players should be allowed to use NPCs against each other e.g. Using an NPC as a shield to gain an advantage.▫️Evasion - The game should not cheat the player out of an evasion, Dashing should have IFrames to enable recovery.▫️Story - Don’t nerf the player controls to introduce puzzle or story elements. Don’t make story exposition dumps.

PLAYER GAMING REQUIREMENTS:💼Platforming.💼Fast Paced.💼Action.VERDICT:I was on the verge on giving up on Ghostrunner but seeing all the positive reviews, I battled through it and once you get the hang of the fast gameplay and controls, it's a very enjoyable game. It's not for players who get frustrated easily since you will die a lot during missions, the one positive about this is there's plenty of checkpoints and different ways to attack your enemies, you'll learn how to beat this game if you are consistent enough with it. Soon enough you'll be familiar with the speed of the game, it's challenging but rewarding once you've beaten a difficult stage.Another big part to this game would be the 3 bosses you come up against, the first boss is about platforming and dodging, working your way up this machine. The next boss is all about timing (The one I died the most to), one simple mistake and it's all over and no checkpoints half way through. The final boss who I found the easiest is a combination of the two, all bosses are very enjoyable.I did run into a few bugs when jumping around on walls and sliding around but this is easily fixed by resetting to the last checkpoint which is usually not very far away from where you get stuck, as I've stated above, there's plenty of checkpoints because the game knows you're going to make mistakes, everything is about timing in the game.This is the best fast paced game I've played to date and I don't think many games can pull this type of thing off without their players getting too frustrated. The price is also very reasonable since there's chances to replay the story and other modes for the hardcore Ghostrunners. The only downfall is, if you're naturally good at these type of games, you'll finish this quickly.Total Score = 91/100.GAMEPLAY:As Jack the Ghostrunner, the player must traverse dangerous environments by dashing, jumping, wall-running, and grappling. The player will also encounter enemies, which must be handled carefully, as both enemies and the player can be killed in one hit. Jack can use a mechanic called Sensory Boost, allowing him to slow down time and dodge and deflect bullets in midair. As the player progresses through the story, they will unlock new abilities and upgrades, which they can apply using tetromino-like pieces on a grid system.SIMILAR GAME LIKE THIS? / REVIEWER PREVIOUS EXPERIENCE:Cyberpunk 2077, SCARLET NEXUS ■■■■■■■■■□ 9 / 10I get a Zer0 vibe from this guy.RECOMMEDED SPECSOS: Windows 10Processor: Intel Core i7-6700K / AMD Ryzen 5 1500X Memory: 8 GB RAMGraphics: GeForce GTX 970 / Radeon RX 5700Storage: 22 GB available spaceReview to Ghostrunner 2:

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to enjoy this, the game concept is awesome and definitely something I would normally enjoy playing. But the further I get into the game the more frustrating it becomes because the game demands near perfect execution despite its mechanics being extremely unpolished and inconsistent. If the game was brand new it could have been excused, but it has been 1 year since the game's release and it's still just as janky.You can watch a playthrough yourself and see people fail what should be extremely basic tasks despite going through other sections of the game just fine. It's easy to pass it off as the player being bad when watching a video, but after actually playing the game you will know this happens because Ghostrunner decided to not wallrun on the wall, or didn't grapple to a location despite pressing the button,  or Ghostrunner decided to wallrun when the player didn't want to wallrun(it's automatic, you don't have control over it), etc. If it happened every now and then it wouldn't be so bad, but when the majority of the deaths can be blamed on the game not doing what you want it becomes infuriating.The 30€ price is also way too expensive. Even ignoring how janky it is, it's way too short to justify the price. If you want to buy this game because it looks awesome or you think you would enjoy playing it, buy it on a sale. If you have a lot of patience you can still get some enjoyment out of it (the soundtrack is pretty good at the very least).Personally I would recommend you to check out a game called Katana ZERO instead. It's very similar to this one but is 2D, you are 100% in control of your actions and the story of the game is actually unique and interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: If Katana ZERO (one of my favorite games of all time) and Mirror's Edge (a game that has inspired a lot of these action/parkour games) had a baby.- Graphics/Art style are great- Soundtrack is great- Movement is some of the most fun I've had in a game ever- A great speed game- An interesting, if shallow story (that will hopefully be expanded upon)- Pretty low hardware requirements- The bosses aren't great, but you don't learn without taking risks.- Short (This being a con depends on how you look at it really). I beat it in  and got most of the collectibles. $30 isn't a bad price point, It's currently on sale for $24 which I think is great. It depends on how much you'll play it. If you plan to speedrun/replay it, the price isn't bad. The core gameplay is fantastic. The movement, 1-hit kills for both you and enemies, the level design, it's all fantastic. The game gives you abilities which it fails to make much use of (they're not required of you to beat the game even. They're more like upgrades that make it easier rather than Zelda-like items that unlock new areas for you). They're hard to use because of how long they take to charge until the end of the game and by that point it's already over. The boss design is also not great. There are only a few, one of which I enjoyed but it needs some tweaking and the others were just boring. Again, the attempt is nice, and I would love to see some cool new bosses implemented in DLC or something. There is also a really cool enemy that doesn't even really get an introduction and is only in 1-2 levels.All of those are minor complaints. Like I said, the core of the game is fantastic, it just has a few flaws that are really only annoying because of how great the rest of the game is. They could easily be fine tuned to make the game even better. If I had to give this game a score, it'd be a 7/10. I really hope there is DLC or a sequel in the works, because this IP has so much to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: **Ghostrunner** is a fast-paced, first-person action game developed by One More Level and published by All In! Games. Released in 2020, it combines elements of platforming and combat in a cyberpunk setting. Players take on the role of a cybernetic ninja who must navigate a dystopian world filled with enemies, obstacles, and deadly traps.Key features of **Ghostrunner** include:- **Fluid Movement**: The game emphasizes parkour-style movement, allowing players to dash, wall-run, and climb through intricate levels at high speeds.- **One-Hit Kills**: Both players and enemies can be taken out with a single hit, which adds an intense layer of challenge and encourages precise timing and reflexes.- **Unique Combat Mechanics**: Players can use a variety of abilities, including a katana for melee attacks and special powers to manipulate the environment and slow down time.- **Immersive Storyline**: Set in a futuristic megastructure, the narrative unfolds as players uncover the mysteries of their world and fight against oppressive forces.The game has been praised for its fluid gameplay, stunning visuals, and engaging soundtrack. If you enjoy action games that require skill and precision, **Ghostrunner** is a thrilling experience. Have you had a chance to play it?

_childDocuments_.review: The game is visually and aesthetically pleasing: it taps all of the classical cyberpunk themes (up to and including the "life is short and bloody" which is often overlooked in modern cyperpunk titles), and blends them together well, combined with a lacing of good old post-fall dystopian scifi in the writing. The plot is fine: not great, not horrible, if you've consumed any dystopian scifi, the weave of the tale will hold few surprises. But that's not what you're here for in this game, so it serves it's purpose well enough.The voice acting is mostly good, outside of the atrocious 'murican accent Japanese that the Guardians garble out (when I pointed to the game taking  cyberpunk aesthetics, I meant .)Ghostrunner is basically parkour with a will to kill. If you wanted to play a more honed Mirror's Edge with more blood and dark mode enabled, this is your stop. Everything (outside of Project Hel - a worth it addition if you like the base game) kills you in a single hit, but the same rule applies to the enemies. The basic rule of speed based games apply: if you stop, you're probably dead. This causes some irritation unless you are very good at getting a read of a room at a glance, as "what the hell killed me" is quite a usual situation going through an encounter for the first 2-50 times. Speaking of dying: I'm not great at speed games, but I would consider myself around average. That said, prepare to die a lot on your first playthroughs of the maps: I averaged to around 50 on the first round, then anything from 0 to 30 on the second (for those maps I reran). The game has a basically instant replay and (usually) well positioned checkpoints, so while dying to the same  Mech for the 100th time in a row will make you want to crack your controller in half, you can at least squeeze all of those deaths in less than 5 minutes.There are a few "puzzles": basically all of them are about getting the lay of the area and understanding visual cues. I found them fun enough, and not too flow or immersion breaking. Your mileage may vary.Overall, the gameplay is fast, satisfying and brutal, exactly what you would expect. However...Ghostrunner is rough around the edges. And not a bit rough, a lot rough.There's a luck based element to some encounters due to the enemy AI and behaviour: it's around 90 % consistent, and then there's the 10 %. Especially Enforcers and Mechs have a habit of glitching, and all enemies also have a weird spin pivot habit that doesn't happen all of the time, but enough to sometimes grind your gears (basically snap aiming to your silly chrome face immediately after boosting behind/around them). Guardians also have a habit of clipping each other and not attacking you, causing... frustrations.The bigger irritation, however, is the environment. It's quite usual for you to run up to a wall panel only for Ghostrunner to decide not to grab to it, instead falling to his doom, or jump of a rail immediately after grabbing it. Of course, the environment is also a source if unintended hilarity, when you end up running between the wall and a billboard, inside some pipes or skipping whole sections of the travel puzzles because some random piece of wall happened to be runnable. Sensory boost is also somewhat directionally aligned, but only somewhat: you can boost a bit upwards, a lot downwards, or directly side to side, but this felt untrustworthy to me. In any case, be prepared for some environmental irritations while playing.The game is also quite short: personally, I don't mind, but this may turn some people off. The 13 hours at the time of writing includes me running through the base game and Project Hel, sniffing out all of the collectibles and replaying for 100 % achievement completion. Your mileage will vary, but I would guess the base came nets between 5-8 hours depending on your skill level and interest in collectible hunting, with Hel being a 2-4 hours on top. For me, I would say 7+3, and another 3 for achievement mopup.All that said, highly recommend: the game incites many curse words and frustrations, but it's deeply satisfying when you finally get it right.

_childDocuments_.review: THIS ONE’S A WINNERI’m going to cut straight to the point with this review: I absolutely love Ghostrunner. Having spoken to the developers a few weeks ago during the virtual Gamescom event, I knew I was likely to enjoy it, but I didn’t expect how enthralled I’d end up being with just about every part of the experience. If you want to save yourself some time, feel free to stop reading here and consider this my whole-hearted endorsement of this post-apocalyptic cyberpunk slasher.Ghostrunner doesn’t waste much time jumping into the action either. In lieu of a long narrative opening, the game starts with a brief cinematic. The titular Ghostrunner is in the middle of a fight with a woman that bears a striking resemblance to Doctor Octopus, and, failing to take her down, is thrown out a window, falling unconscious after an impact on his way down. When he wakes up, it becomes his task, with the aid of a mysterious AI in his head called The Architect and one of the few surviving rebels left in the city, to climb back up the megastructure and save the city from the woman that defeated him.BRINGING A SWORD TO A GUN FIGHTThe gameplay is fast and brutal, a revolving door of combat and platforming puzzles that take advantage of the Ghostrunner’s ability to run on walls and grapple to connection points. The kicker is that both enemies and the player die in one hit, turning each encounter into a puzzle of navigation, ability utilization, and environmental awareness. It’s a tough task, especially given that the player’s only starting tools against gun-toting enemies are a sword and the ability to temporarily pause time, but fantastic level design makes it so everything works extremely well. It’s incredibly challenging, but it’s incredibly fun, and I found myself having an equally good time with the arena-style combat scenarios and the inventive environmental traversal puzzles.Part of what makes Ghostrunner so successful is that it absolutely nails its difficulty curve. Games like these, which ask the player to keep mental track of quite a bit, can too often chuck way too much out there at once in the name of “challenge.” This isn’t the case here. Each time something new was added to the game, I experienced the same progression of “oh gosh, I forgot how to use my keyboard,” “ah, that’s how this is going to work,” “well, this is kind of cool,” “I’M AN UNSTOPPABLE CYBER NINJA, BABY.” The game never sits on either end of the spectrum, making the player feel helpless or overpowered, for too long, which kept things from growing overly frustrating or overly stale.HARD, BUT FAIRSpeaking of challenge, I expected to get a lot more frustrated with a game that had me dying well over a hundred times each level. I mean, I really died a lot. We’re talking Super Meat Boy levels of death. It’s tough not to make this kind of game-flow grating. It can boring, frustrating, and just plain un-fun to have to replay the same encounter dozens of times before moving on, but a number of elements come together in Ghostrunner in a way that never really became frustrated with the game more than I was frustrated with myself. The main reason, I think, is that my deaths never felt cheap. The controls are super tight, hitboxes seem spot on, and there aren’t many “gotcha” moments that I couldn’t see coming, so every time I died I really did feel like I was learning something and getting better. A few other design decisions help, too. First, there’s absolutely no loading time between deaths. When I died, I’d click the R button and be back at the last checkpoint (which are intelligently and frequently placed) in a literal blink of the eye. Narrative dialogue also persists between deaths, meaning, if one of the NPCs was explaining something to me over comms during a fight and I died, the conversation continued after I respawned instead of starting over. I’m sure there are other games that do this, but it’s rare, and it goes a long way towards taking a repetitive annoyance out of death.  A TREAT FOR THE SENSESAll of this is made even better by the fact that Ghostrunner absolutely kills it in the presentation department. The narrative is far more engaging than I expected to be, boosted by a small cast of great voice actors that bring a lot of life to the dialogue. There’s a lot of worldbuilding that goes on, and I actively found myself playing for longer each session than I had planned just to keep the story going. The environments look absolutely beautiful, too. Taking place mostly inside of a megastructure city, each room is packed with grungy, industrial detail that looks ripped right out of Blade Runner or Dredd. Interspersed between levels are also segments that take place in a virtual environment. It’s in these areas that the game really lets loose, experimenting with more surreal puzzles and architecture. It’s all a treat to look at and play in, and it’s made better by an electronica soundtrack that absolutely bops (the soundtrack is on Spotify, and you should absolutely play it next time you’re going for a drive in the dark).This month marks my 10-year anniversary writing for Hooked Gamers, and, in that time, I’ve only given one game a 10. With its beautiful visual design, quality voice acting, tight controls, interesting mechanics, and engaging world-building, I have absolutely no hesitation adding Ghostrunner to my exclusive club of top marks. It’s rare to find a game that succeeds so well in everything it does, and the result is a game that absolutely everyone should check out.

_childDocuments_.review: lasagna 👍1. Preheat the oven to 350°F. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add the lasagna noodles and cook until al dente (firm) according to package directions. Drain, rinse under cold water, and set aside.2. Meanwhile, in a large skillet or Dutch oven, brown the beef, sausage, onion, and garlic over medium-high heat until no pink remains. Drain any fat.3. Stir in the pasta sauce, tomato paste, Italian seasoning, ½ teaspoon of salt, and ¼ teaspoon of black pepper. Simmer uncovered over medium heat for 5 minutes or until slightly thickened. Taste and season with additional salt if desired.4. In a separate medium bowl, combine 1 ½ cups mozzarella cheese, ¼ cup parmesan cheese, ricotta, parsley, egg, and ¼ teaspoon salt.5. Spread 1 cup of the meat sauce in a 9×13 pan or casserole dish. Top it with 3 lasagna noodles. Layer with ⅓ of the ricotta cheese mixture and 1 cup of meat sauce. Repeat twice more. Finish with 3 noodles topped with remaining sauce.6. Cover with foil and bake for 45 minutes. 7. Remove the foil and sprinkle the top of the lasagna with the remaining 2 ½ cups mozzarella cheese and ¼ cup parmesan cheese. Bake uncovered for an additional 15 minutes or until browned and bubbly. Broil for 2-3 minutes if desired.8. Rest for at least 15 minutes before cutting.9. Enjoy C:Notes:*Note on the sauce: In this recipe, each layer has about 1 cup of meat sauce. If you prefer more sauce in your lasagna, increase the pasta sauce to 48 oz. Salt needed may vary based on the brand of pasta sauce used. Taste and season after simmering.Cheese Layer: The cheese layers are thin; if you’d prefer a thicker layers cheese, divide the cheese in half and put on the first two layers, and add just meat sauce to the third layer. We tested this with extra ricotta cheese and found it overpowered the lasagna. Time-Saving Tip:  Use fresh lasagna sheets found in the deli area and skip the boiling step! Fresh lasagna doesn’t need to be boiled first. Let the lasagna sit/rest for at least 15 minutes once removed from the oven (even 30-45 minutes is fine). This will keep it from becoming runny and help it to keep its shape when cut. Resting is not required when reheating.Substitutions:Ricotta cheese can be replaced with cottage cheese.Use all beef (or even ground turkey) in place of sausage if needed. If using all beef, add ½ teaspoon Italian seasoning to the meat (and ¼ teaspoon fennel seeds if desired).

_childDocuments_.review: The pace of the combat is what makes this game. There is no feeling like dashing around the place slicing enemies up in this game, dodging projectiles and parrying enemies just feels satisfying. There are so many approaches that can be taken to each level that give each one replay value and the abilities add a new layer of depth. The game is very hard but the instant restart makes it so the difficulty never makes you angry, because you are always back in the action a second later. The game requires flawless movement and is unforgiving, but pulling off a cool play just feels incredible as a result. The art style and aesthetics are awesome looking and the cyberpunk setting is explored better than it is is the game titled cyberpunk. The soundtrack is a frenzy of synth-wave headbangers that compliments the setting and aesthetic and makes whatever crazy play your pulling off feel even more epoch. The story is bare bones, it touches on themes of identity and morality but never explores any of them very deeply. This is fine as all I expect from games like this is a story that enables nutty gameplay, and it well and truly delivers on that front. My only complaint is some of the platforming mechanics are janky and inconsistent. Stuff like not wallrunning despite being extremely close to a wall, or not using the zipline despite being close to a zipline. However these are the only issues I had, and in every other instance the game was fair and my deaths were my fault and not the game's. This is a must play for anyone who enjoys fast paced, deep and cinematic gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostrunner is a slick, parkour based action platformer where you have to use your abilities and skills to defeat the enemies in your path and ascend the tower, where a single misstep leads to death. It looks great, has a well thought out and tight control scheme, a well-paced story and pumping synth soundtrack. I highly recommended it.Set in a dystopian future, the Earth’s ecosystem has been ruined by an unexplainable catastrophe, forcing humanity to live in the Dharma tower, the last bastion where humanity can survive. You play as a Ghostrunner, a cybernetically enhanced member of the elite security and peacekeeping force of the tower who were destroyed when Mara, partner to Adam who built the tower stages a coup and kills him, assuming control. You awaken 20 years after the successful coup by the architect, a copy of Adam’s consciousness who urges you to ascend the tower and finish what you started -defeat Mara and free the people of the tower. The story makes a late game twist, where characters motives aren’t what has been portrayed, and where some of the body horror elements start making sense, but fits the dystopian theme really well.Gameplay involves you traversing each stage by running, sliding, wall running and zip lining while dodging attacks and hazards and defeating enemies scattered throughout each area. The game is forgiving as it saves frequently so deaths aren’t a large setback. Each stage is designed really well, and while there is effectively only one path to follow, the large spaces allow for different techniques and attempts at combat.Combat is fun and usually challenging, with different types of enemies slowly introduced, each requiring different tactics or styles to fight against. It becomes frantic when versing multiple different types, while trying to dodge the attacks or traverse the environment where a single hit results in a death. The base games combat areas are forgiving in the sense that there are usually only a handful of enemies in each area, and only a few of the enemies seem to randomly change their behaviour. All the enemies fit the game, though I think the suiciding crawlers near the end seem to be out of place with their attack sequence (their body horror element fits perfectly). Theres a matrix that slowly unlocks which allows you to add bonuses to your 4 skills, or enhance your existing abilities. Each enhancer fits onto the board like a Tetris piece, and it can become a game of trying to cram as many abilities onto it vs adding few that you really want. These can be switched and changed at any time, so if something isn’t working you can change and try something different at any point.The game caters to those who want to speed run, as well as those who just want to experience the game for its story, by comparing your time and death count to anyone in your steam friends list who has played the game. There are collectables hidden through-out each stage, a few which explain how things to be where they are, but most are cosmetic or just add to the background story of the world.The game lives and dies by its tight controls. And it doesn’t disappoint. The controls are simple, responsive and work well on controller or keyboard. It absolutely nails the cyberpunk feel of a future gone wrong. Humanity is crammed into tower, and like all good settings, the working class lives in the filth at the bottom, while things get progressively better as you move up. In somewhat of a divergence, the upper floors aren’t for the super-rich, but the scientists who made the tower possible.Each of the enemies look great, and while they are carbon copies of each other they look great. There’s a fair amount of detail for each enemy. Depending on how you kill them or where you slice them they are bisected in different parts and spill apart differently.There is a photo mode, where you can change the camera angles, colour gradients, remove the UI and add or remove other effects to create some impressive pictures.The synthwave absolutely raises this game from great to amazing. The music fits the game like a glove, and is one of those few tracks you could happily put on in the background and listen to (if sythwave is your thing). The voice acting is also great, and though there are only a few characters conversing, all of them sound professional and polished. In something that needs to happen in more games, if you die while conversing it continues from where the dialogue was, rather than restart. This doesn’t sound like something major, but hearing the same dialogue loops multiple times can become frustrating, and Ghostrunner completely bypasses that problem.If you are chasing 100% achievements, then you need to purchase the DLC and do a fair bit of practise. While most achievements will come naturally some require perfect runs or long streaks with no deaths.For more reviews please visit

_childDocuments_.review: This game is hard and so is writing a review for it. I'm still not sure if I should love or hate it...After finishing it and doing some extra runs I' rather recommend it but there are definitely some drawbacks. But one after another.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Pro:It's challenging. You die as soon as you are hit. No extra life, no shield. Only your agility to evade enemy attacks and your ability to block some attacks if your timing is right. Some special attacks may help you on your crusade but you have to get them first and their use costs focus which needs to regenerate after use. Nevertheless, the fights seem fair.It's fast paced. At least during combat it's either you or them. And you will know the result very soon.There are some hidden extras. So outside of fights you can explore the area to find audiologs or items which give some deeper insight in the story, eastereggs or swords. The swords can be equipped for cosmetic reasons and are actually well designed, I really enjoyed looking for them and switching between them. Some of this stuff is found easily while some is very well hidden. You can use a perk to assist your search or do it without it.The perksystem is kinda funny. It's somehow like tetris but without erasing lines. You start with a small field and only a few available upgrades. Every upgrade has a different shape and you arrange them on your field. You can rearrange/switch perks at any time. If you leave fields free it increases your focus regeneration, but you can also try to squeeze in as many upgrades as possible. Your choice. I liked it as I never experienced something like that before.Movement feels good, most of the time your ghostrunner is doing what you would expect him to do, wall runs and grappling usually works fine. There's almost always more than one route to your goal, depending on your skill.Soundtrack also kicks in.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Contra:Frustration. While it's ok for a game not to be too easy, accumulating hundreds of deaths within one level can be quite annoying. And that happened for almost every level. The quick respawn compensates a bit for that, as you can instantly respawn, even while still being alive. There are a lot of checkpoints so you don't lose much progression. But still not what I'm used to...Sometimes it also feels a bit random. Doing a wallrun and there's an enemy waiting at the end of it, it happened sometimes that I was shot down in the middle of it, sometimes at the end of it still being in mid air or I could finish the run before the first shot. Some mechanics seem not to reset with a respawn so you may find different start conditions after death. Maybe I'm wrong about this but I definitely got this impression.It's rather short. I completed it in about 10 hours with around 70-80% of the stuff found. A few hours later I got everything except the steam achievements. Maybe I'll try hardmode (or is it hardcore?) soon but at the moment I do not really feel that motivated to go for it.The game probably only gets really rewarding if you manage to perfect your movement in an early stage of the game. There are some tutorials in game but they are short. I somehow reached the last level and got stuck there. I then watched a guide, realized that this player was doing some stuff completely different and by using that knowledge even earlier levels got much more easier. I usually avoid this approach as you risk spoilers.There are some puzzles in certain levels. In my opinion they break the flow of the game. Some may find them nice as they are different from the rest of the game. After you solved them once, they are just annoying.Gloves: Like the swords there are also gloves available to customize your ghostrunner. Well, in fact there is the standard model and if you buy the DLC, you get a second one. That's ridiculous and not worth an extra section for customization.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Conclusion:It was fun, a short gap filler. But I don't think I will reach 50 hours within this game, probably not even half of it. The story was ok, but the ending was obvious already in an early stage.
