_childDocuments_.review: I'm sure a lot of people simply adore this game. I wanted to. I'm good with 1 hit kills, I'm good with ducking projectiles, I'm good with timing parries, that's all fine. Here's what I'm not good with: Platforming that only works kind of.If platforming is center stage among your mechanics, I do need it to work. I need to be able to navigate reliably, I need your wall running hit detection on point, I need the game to preserve momentum when appropriate, I need the grappling option to make contact and not just kind of play the animation, then decide it didn't actually want to do stuff, I need your launch pads to put me where they're supposed to, because hey guess what: I don't have control over what they do!Games like this demand a lot of a particular kind of player. I'm usually that guy. I love New Doom. I adore new Wolfenstein. Superhot's great.  The list goes on and on and on, and there's a throughline running there. If I die in any of those games, it's my fault. I missed a jump, didn't catch an incoming projectile in time, so on and so forth.When I die in Ghostrunner, it's because my robot boy's feet got stuck in the wall, and I can't jump away from it now. It's because I've triggered the grappling hook, only to have it yank me all of two feet, then give up and drop me in a hole. It's because I've watched my dude clip directly through the rail he was supposed to ride, refuse to grab it, and again, wind up in said hole.It's because the fun launch pads on your last level fling me into oblivion, no matter what angle I approach them from.A few times, it was because I was attempting to play jump rope with first lasers, then tentacles, but for unknowable reasons, my metal idiot just didn't tuck enough for something.This is a game that, from the outside looking in, seems to want to put a ton of control in the hands of the player, and say "Hey, figure it out." I am incredibly down with that. But at no point during my 6 hour long attempt to love Ghostrunner did I feel like I was in the driver's seat. Taking a bullet I didn't see coming is fine. Bouncing off a guy's head, watching the sword path through them, and then being told I died because he shot me is not.I hope you, reader, didn't encounter these issues. I hope your playthrough was everything you wanted it to be. I hope you consider your twenty dollars well spent.Me, I've looked at green or blue or sometimes orange out-of-map area and asked "Where the ♥♥♥♥ am I?" as I stand on nothing for the last time. I've said "I don't actually know where my hitbox is, and I have no way to even gauge that, because I can't see my feet to determine roughly how tall I am" for the last time.I've definitely laid eyes on Weeb Tron and been introduced to the void within for the last time.Have fun, folks. I tried to, and it didn't work.

_childDocuments_.review: The game feels like a cyber punk version of HotlineMiami and Mirrors Edge put together in a slick package, when you really get into the zone of this game you feel like a absolute turbo killer, this isn't a very complex game but requires you to be complex in your strategy, I wouldn't recommend this game to someone with slow reaction times or someone who hates 1 shot kill mechanics, as even though it takes 1 hit to finish your opponent you die just a fast as they, the game seriously rewards those who not only put in the time to learn the mechanics of the game but master them also. My only draw back I would say for someone who enjoys games like this is the enemy's called Wardens, in my opinion they really bring the break neck pace of this game to a crawl as you literally have to wait for them to attack you before you can counter them, considering their attack is done in a literal blink of an eye it becomes extremely frustrating to be slicing people at warp speed only to have to wait for a dude to initiate his attack while you have to dodge and block 100 different other dudes in order to survive. Beyond that this game is totally worth your time, story is pretty predictable but does a pretty good job of world building so you feel like you have some form of motivation to go from point a to b, the boss fights are actually extremely well done each of them testing if you cheesed your way to get there or payed attention to all the nuances. if I needed to give a score for this game it gets a solid 8/10, as I'm looking into running though the game again on it's "hard mode" or new game + mode, game goes on sale a lot also so next time you feel like giving lord gaben some of your hard earned dollaz throw some at Ghost Runner

_childDocuments_.review: This game genuinely fascinates me with how incredibly "fine" it is. Perfectly serviceable. B tier. Real "$45 at GameStop" energy. Every single thing about this game is fine in concept, but just okay in execution. It's genuinely shocking how consistent in quality it is. The gameplay is fun, but riddled with just enough weird inconsistencies and awkward systems to never truly sing. The story is okay, it doesn't get in the way but the characters are flat and the ending is almost a nonsequitur. The world is completely bland, a standard Matrix-type cyberpunk affair stuffed to bursting with weird orientalist white-guy-obsessed-with-Japan details, but executed well and with good art. The final bosses, built up as being these impossible machine intelligences, are instead a normal white dude in a suit we've never seen before and a big-titty robot with Doc-Ock arms that looks designed for p*rn instead of for a cool visual. The voice acting is mostly good, especially on Ghostrunner and the Architect, but sometimes is really weird - all the enemies speak English through a radio filter except the samurai sword guys, who shout stereotypical Japanese phrases in a clear voice. The music and sound effects are good, but certain effects are way too loud for some reason and the music is never really amazing. Even little details are ultimately "just okay" in execution, like the naming of things after Buddhist mythology (Mara, Dharma, Amida, Samsara) that seems to set up some kind of thematic idea but ultimately never goes anywhere. I'm worried this review is making this game sound bad. It isn't. It's a good game, worth your time if you like reflex-based action puzzles. It just genuinely fascinates me how *every single aspect* of this game is like 80% of the way to perfect, but ultimately settles into a mid sort of quality.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a $30 game. It's short and incredibly awkward, between the pacing and the movement being just janky enough to mess you up often enough that it's frustrating. I wouldn't mind the length if parts didn't just feel like filler. This game has sections that fueled an adrenaline rush I've never felt from playing videogames before, but then quickly killed that with random puzzle sections that slow the incredibly fast pace down to a snail's crawl. The game is at times pretty and at other times, absurdly unoptimized, with fairly poor particle effects that nuke your framerate. On average, I had about 80 FPS through most of the game. The last level, I averaged 30, because why not have platforms shoot particles all over the place? And why not have terrible particles all over your screen that follow your head movement instead of existing in the environment? This game is still worth the good experience it offers, but understand that you'll also have to slog through some parts that just aren't that great. I'd recommend it if it were $20. Probably best to wait for a sale

_childDocuments_.review: GhostrunnerA short, 3-4 hour first-person, movement-focused hack-and-slash set in a neat, cyberpunk setting with an emphasis on speedrunning, complete with timers (that compare you to any of your friends who've played through the level), and death counter, along with a NewGame+/Hardcore mode available on completing the main story once.It's good. It's really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good. Mechanically, the game is basically perfect. The only mechanic that I found underutilized was probably the first power that you get, which lets you kill a couple enemies that are standing in a line together, which is honestly kinda useless and I only ever used it once or twice in the entire playthrough. Thankfully, you get three more abilities later on that are far better than it. Other than that, there's absolutely nothing bad I can say about this game mechanically. It feels great parkouring from wallrun to wallrun, slingshotting on cranes, and jumping from flying saucer to flying saucer like it's metal gear rising.Visually, the game is stunning. Especially the early-mid game, where you're in a more part-residential, and part-industrial area. It screams cyberpunk dystopia. The only area that is kind of bland is the very late-game laboratory areas, which are whatever. They still look great, and the maps themselves are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fun as ♥♥♥♥ to sprint around, but it just kinda looks like a big, boring warehouse. This should, by no means, be a dealbreaker.My only real "complaint" beyond that like, two missions kinda look bland (but are still fun as ♥♥♥♥ to play), is that the difficulty pacing for the game can be kinda off. The first boss you fight was (for me), far, far tougher than the the second, or third (final) boss, but this might just be due to the fact that by the second and third boss, I'd already been playing the game for three-four hours and had the controls and movement mechanics down pat.The character writing is good! It's not completely amazing; since there's really only four characters, one of which is you, your AI companion, whose with you for the entire game, a friendly rebel, whose there for three quarters of the game, and the main villain who only directly speaks to you in the final two or three missions. They aren't groundbreaking by any means, but they're fun, and they perfectly fit the setting. The actual "plot" is that you were found destroyed, got rebuilt, woke up, saved your AI companion, and then with the help of it, and the friendly rebel, you're on the hunt for the main villain, looking to kill her.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me just get something out of the way.The writing is ass. It's predictable, it's lame, it takes itself seriously to a borderline offensive degree. It's exactly what you would expect from videogame writing, with all the horrible implications that phrase entails.That being said, if bland stories and pained exposition usually don't bother you, they won't bother you here either. It's not especially egregious, just bad.And you're not here for that anyways, you're here for a fast-paced skinnerbox that keeps outputting cool ♥♥♥♥ in return for your time. And that's something this game is pretty good at.It's got its problems, quite a few actually, raytracing doesn't seem to make use of RTX cards, or at least not efficiently, and you may have to override High DPI scaling behavior for the game, or it might just ignore mouse inputs at random intervals, which is seriously annoying in a game that often requires super precise timings. Your grappling hook feels 'off' somehow, your slow-motion move is often necessary, but honestly feels like it breaks the flow of the game.BUT:Damn, you get to run around real fast and kill dudes in one hit. There are some interesting choices in the level and enemy design, from a gameplay perspective, and while you'll be blowing through all the content relatively quick, those will keep them interesting during replays, especially if you're trying to outperform your friends, their times and deaths for stages will be visible at the end of a run, a great way to let players motivate themselves without giving them explicit goals, which can often cause burnout.And all the while the soundtrack just keeps egging you on, pushing you to go a little faster, to play a little more recklessly...The game's short-ish runtime is pretty easily justified by its replayability and cost. It's no masterpiece, but if the trailer looks fun to you, I guarantee it will be a lot of fun to play.

_childDocuments_.review: So, 6.3 hours of playtime (probably closer to 6, I was afk for a bit) is my end time for completing this game. If I want to, I do have some collectibles to go back and grab, so let's be generous to my incompetence and say another 2 hours of time running around grabbing secrets. So, with some variance, 8-10 hours for total completion of the game for the average player, I would say.Is it worth it? HELL YES IT IS.I don't do formats well, so rambling it is.To begin with, the outstanding. The level design in this game is beyond fantastic. The visuals give you clear indications of where to go without ever breaking the feeling of the surrounding areas, and the world is consistent throughout, with an insane attention to detail that can only be achieved with a clear sense of love and dedication to the world beyond the play area. The sound design in this game is also incredible, as it's one of the few games I actually play listening to the soundtrack as opposed to my own music. It's upbeat, scenery-appropriate, and never slows you down. It lets you know the time to move is now, and the direction to move is forward.Next, the good. The combat is rewarding on a visceral level, with some arenas designed to give you one path forward, and other arenas giving you many paths to choose. The variety of powers and upgrades you unlock along the way let you try to master the base move sets, or incorporate some variety into the way you clear rooms. The story is nothing new, but both engaging and "realistic" (in quotation marks as any futuristic/dystopian storyline must be), with a small but strong cast of characters with individual feels to them and apparent character motivations.The boss battles in this game are all challenging in their own sense, and built in such a way as to almost be tests of the skills you acquire through the base gameplay, which in my opinion is the best method to build out a boss battle.The design choice of tightly packed checkpoints with no respawn animation/timers allows you to keep the fast pace going even when you've gotten knocked down. And anything will knock you down, you may be an insanely skilled cyborg ninja, but guns will still kill you. The game is a testament to the mentality of skill determines your ability, not any sort of stats.Finally, the "negatives."I encountered a single bug throughout my playthrough. I glitched through the mesh of the game area, and had to restart from a checkpoint. Which was directly before the glitch, so I lost maybe all of seven seconds. Nothing major, not game-breaking, but it was there.I put this in the "negative" category because I usually like games that allow for slow methodical play, and there are several enemies in the game which do not allow for that, and are specifically designed to keep your ass moving. Personally, I prefer a bit more of a parkouring about while occasionally striking, and there are specific enemies later in the game which kept me moving out of sheer panic (The sounds they make, good lord). That being said, they were reflective of a solid design philosophy, so I can't fault the developers too much for their placement, they served their purpose well.The last thing was that physics wise, I felt a little floaty. Which worked REALLY well for most of the constant movement, but in certain sections got a little frustrating when I would land on a platform and my momentum would carry me straight off. I don't code, so I don't know if this was a sacrifice that needed to be made for the rest of the game, but it was a minor annoyance.Overall: If you like high skill, high speed, high...I really tried to find another "s" word to put there but it's escaping me, game, then this is it. It's well priced for the content provided, exceedingly polished, and really brings me back to the great old days of gaming (well, my great old days. I'm talking Prince of Persia, Portal, and Legend of Zelda, although if I were doing a comparison I would put Mirror's Edge in the place of Legend of Zelda)....fine, you can have a numeric score. Plebs. 9/10. Just below perfect, and a bit short, but for the time it's here, it's the life of the damn party.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostrunner is a solid combination of MIrror's Edge and Hotline Miami, combining the first person platforming of the former with the one hit kills of the latter. This gives every encounter a puzzle-like quality as you try to work your way through a room at speed without dying.But you will die. Probably a lot. The good news is the your sword and powers feels great to use, with enemies being appreciably sliced apart or blown to bits. The bad news is the parkour is a little uneven and the combination of platforming, wallrunning, sliding and dashing never feels as tight as it should. If that was all the game was I'd feel comfortable recommending it. However, the inclusion of "Cybervoid" segments brings the game down as it introduces all the worst sorts of puzzles to the game. These areas frequently feature frustrating  design elements such as forcing you to walk backward to proceed, areas where you have to guess the correct order of doors to go through while each mistake throws you back to the beginning, and mandatory collectathons on rotating platforms eager to drop you into the abyss.Every time the game forces you into one of these areas the pace screeches to a halt--and these segments come as frequently as every other level. To make matters worse, your moveset is reduced dramatically in these areas. There's no wallrunning in the Cybervoid apparently, nor dashing, nor air-dashing, and no real enemies either.If the Cybervoid levels were removed this would be a fun game to pick up and play. As it is, their continual interruption to the far more fun fights and liberal use of frustrating puzzle design won out over my desire to finish the game. Slashing baddies in Ghostrunner never gets old, but the puzzles where my abilities are taken away sure do.

_childDocuments_.review: *INCLUDES SPOILERS*Imagine playing a game where you're a ninja fighting mostly ranged enemies but you can't reflect shots back at people, not because your character physically can't, but because you have to press the deflect button at the perfect time and have the right upgrades AND the game doesn't make that clear at all, and even when you do successfully execute it, it doesn't register and then you fall off a building because your freerunning ability broke in the middle of that process.That's what it's like playing this game the entire time.Before I rant, I just wanna say that the art style, animation, environment and theme of the game are all very cool and executed nicely. The collectible swords/artifacts containing lore pages and the soundtrack are also big positives. The music is heavily reminiscent of the Tron: Legacy OST. But to put it bluntly: If you enjoy Doom: Eternal on Ultra-Nightmare or Dark Souls challenges with no upgrades, then this is the game for you because it literally requires that level of focus and memorization. There's nothing fun about this.To expand on this: I really, really wanted to like this game, and at $30 it wasn't much of a loss, but I simply do not enjoy this game. It is not what you might think it is. I've put about 6 hours into it and already fought 2 "bosses", if that's what you wanna call them, but I honestly don't think I can bring myself to finish the game after literally dying for the hundreth time on the same part and have had this happen at least once a level. I thought, "Maybe later in the game you'll get more powerful?" but no, you just get more worthless abilities that are impossible to execute within the game's combat arenas. This isn't just a matter of "Git gud, scrub." Any amount of memorization and repetition in the game will make you good at it, but that IS this game. There's nothing else to it. Literally nothing else. You learn to do it right, you can do it again a million times assuming the damn controls work for you, which they won't, and that's the most frustrating part. And then they throw in the exploding zombies. Don't even get me started about the exploding zombies. You just feel so powerless against these stupid things.The game is simply unfair on purpose for "challenge" but the control response and freerunning is so bad it doesn't even matter. The challenge vanished for me when I got to first "boss." This boss was just a tower with lazers shooting out of it and this was easily one of the worst experiences of my life. There is no memorization value, and if there is, I simply just do not care. I'm not taking the time to learn it. The story itself is somewhat captivating but it's not very fleshed out so there's no reason for me to replay your game and painstakingly memorize non-fun, insta-kill bosses. I will say that the 2nd boss was nowhere near as bad as the first one, though. That boss at least made sense...If I had expected this level of difficulty going into this, I probably wouldn't have been so disappointed, but I went into this ready to have fun and it failed miserably.

_childDocuments_.review: blends Titanfall-ish parkour with ninja-style melee combat, set in a dark dystopian cyberpunk universe. You are the last standing member of the Ghostrunners, an elite guard force, that hitherto preserved the order in the humanity's last refuge from some undescribed apocalypse, the Dharma Tower. Awakened by one of your deceased creators, you are now tasked with making your way to the top of the tower and neutralising the tyrant in charge of the tower's operations. At your disposal you have: a katana with a single-type slash attack, 5 different abilities (3 of them quite similar in their usage), and insane agility.  The movement and parkour systems appear to be pretty tight and, for the most part, feel right. Wallrunning, ziplining and sliding around at high speed feels splendid, specially when you manage to clear most of the arena off enemies while doing so, without losing velocity.  The combat system itself isn't too compelling or complex - you do have just one attack type for your katana, after all. What's more noteworthy, is the skill upgrade assignment, executed in a slot-based system, the same way the invetory works in, say, Resident Evil games. Each upgrade has its' own unique geometric form, which you then must fit into your allocated slot space. It lets you experiment with different upgrade combinations, while not making you too powerful, were the game just to let you activate all upgrades at once. And some of these upgrades indeed are quite powerful - you can end the game having 4 dashes with invincibility frames, projectile deflection with greatly decreased ability cooldowns, or enhanced abilities that can be used multiple times in quick succession. Each of the builds provides more or less distinctive playstyle and tactics during fighs.  Moving on to the game difficulty: it's not really all that challenging, considering all the nifty stuff you're being given in the earlier chapters. The invincibility frames during dashes, for instance, is an incredibly potent build, that let's you dodge most enemy projectiles with ease. The time dilation mid-flight has a very fast cooldown rate, with rather lengthy uptime. Furthermore, you are rarely fighting more than 6-8 enemies at once, and most of those are easily disposed of. You do get to fight some of the more subtle enemy variations, like samurais (blocking normal sword attacks, can only be killed after a successful parry) or splitters (as implied, a gunner splitting into 5 independent doppelgangers of himself), but battle scenarios where they can actually put their stronger features to use are pretty rare. There are 3 bosses in the game, and 2 of them are a bit of a travesty, with predictable, scant and easily dodgeable attack patterns. All things considered, it's only fair for the player to have just 1 HP - the game is not super-challenging, though you'd have to get used to moving fast and preferably not in a straight line.  There is one important, much significant flaw with the control responsiveness for mices, though, which extends to both parkour and combat - some kind of input ghosting that oft completely ignores the sword attacks and grapple inputs. I got killed far too many times thanks to this, and it's really irritating.  Summing up, Ghostrunner is a pretty decent game, and a bit of a novelty too, since we don't commonly get melee parkour first-person action games these days. It has some issues, is a bit on the short end, but can and will provide a good deal of amusement while it lasts.

_childDocuments_.review: In short: an okay game but it needed more polishing. I'd only recommend it if it's on sale and you really like cyber-future-dystopia themes. Otherwise, the platforming starts out great but gets stale, the combat isn't varied enough, and the game crashed often enough that it significantly detracted from my experience.Ghostrunner has a great aesthetic including some rad music, and when the platforming sections are on, they're *on* and it feels really slick, which is about 60-70% of the time. The other 30-40% of the platforming was a bore, and I felt its only purpose was to inject unsubtle story dialogue. Introducing some new platforming mechanics later in the game would have really helped, but you see 90% of the platforming in the first 10 minutes of the game, so it runs out of steam toward the end.The puzzle solving was sometimes dynamic and rewarding, but it fell short because it was so combat-oriented. As others have mentioned, the combat is repetitive as there are only a few enemy types. It can also be super frustrating; I don't mind banging my head against a puzzle repeatedly, but I know that type of friction isn't fun for a lot of folks. Unless you have outstanding reflexes, expect to die quite a few times in the same rooms (especially later in the game), and be ready to face the "I definitely pushed the button in time" frustration that comes along with dying 15+ times in a row to the same enemy.The story is not compelling. The voice acting is okay, but the writing lacked nuance and was predictable.I also had stability issues. For me the game crashed every 45 minutes on average. if I went even slightly out of bounds while exploring in most places (which seems to be encouraged based on the existence of collectibles) the game often crashed for me. Tried both Dx11 and 12, adjusting settings, framerate, etc. and it continued to crash if I ventured slightly too far off-course. If the crashing weren't an issue, I'd give it a 6/10, but the instability was really disruptive to a game that leans heavily on flow. If this game were in early access with the promise of slight improvements to combat, some of the platforming, a deeper story, and most importantly, stability, I'd recommend it. But it's not, and as it stands the game is lacking too much for me to suggest others pick it up.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostrunner is a lot of fun but way more difficult than I expected. Perhaps the hardest non-Soulslike games  I've played in recent memory that didn't also have a difficulty setting. Enemies kill in a single hit, and are the most accurate I've ever seen AI be, even able to anticipate movement to a degree. The movement usually feels great, but you can wallrun on any surface, including ones that you really don't want to, and the only way off is to jump, which isn't always what you want, but it's very satisfying when it works. It very often makes you jump onto something you didn't want to, however, and then you die, whether to an enemy that you would have killed had you landed correctly or falling into a pit. Very fun though, and the aesthetic is fantastic.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostrunner

_childDocuments_.review: The game just wasn't my cup of tea. You may enjoy it a lot more than I did if you're really into platformer-esque parkour, but I ended up requesting a refund. (Note: This is a subjective opinion that is obviously limited to the portion of the game I played before calling it quits; your mileage may vary. )Pros:1) Good looking graphics and a well developed cyberpunk aesthetic.2) Responsive and easy to learn traversal controls.3) A comprehensive checkpoint system, meaning that messing up doesn't mean you have to repeat giant sections of the level.Cons:1) The parkour parts (at least to me) soon become a bit of a chore. It would have been fun if the ratio of the combat vs parkour was more balanced.2) Since the game is so heavily based on parkour, the level design is constructed solely around that concept. It doesn't feel like you're in a cyberpunk city, it feels like you're in a cyberpunk obstacle course. The aesthetic is good, the level design isn't.3) Your attacks feel clunky at times.

_childDocuments_.review: The things I LOVED about the game:-Puzzles-Graphics-Cyberpunk theme-Characters-Voice acting-Story-MusicThe things I didn't like so much about the game:-Endless parkour-1 hit and you die-Start all over again if you mess up-Counts how many times you mess up-Not always has waypointsThis is a hybrid game that mixes skater/parkour/puzzles/slasher elements into a very nicely done cyberpunk themed world where you're an urban ninja cutting everyone in half exactly the same way over and over again. Seriously, you slash everyone. Every single person through their midsection the exact same way that if you collected every person you killed in this game, they would line up exactly the same way perfect...sliced in half. You can mix and match their bodies upper and lower sections, sew them together with other people and have them fit so evenly that you wouldn't tell the difference... Its so perfect that they have entry-level cyberpunk detectives go out and try to figure out who killed these guys and Ghostrunner is the correct answer and the success rate of the test is always 100%.The game is not what I expected in a good way and a bad way...Part of me loves it because there is so much gratification to be had when you run through these obstacles courses perfectly.  The entire game is basically a parkour/skater park obstacle course where you are not only trying not to F-up and fall short of a ramp, you are trying to avoid guys mess up your flow, ruin your style and KILL you. If you are not messing up the obstacle by falling to your death, you are getting shot in the toe and having to do it ALL OVER AGAIN...and again and again and again and again. This is understandable and is a good way to learn each obstacle and the placement of enemies so the next time around you can figure out where you need to go and who you need to kill on the way except that the game discreetly punishes you for this at the end of the level showing you how many times you F-ed up kind of making you feel like crap. This doesn't make the game bad if this is what you like. Its basically a skater game where you need to land tricks.I am a bit torn because it is REALLY COOL. But I was looking for more in terms of combat and not so much of the parkouring around on ramps. I think that aspect is cool, but the only way to traverse the world is doing these obstacles and the game doesn't really tell you where you need to go or jump leading to a lot of deaths until you figure out that the way was actually DOWN and not always UP. Oh yeah and it will count how many times you fell to your death too.You do pick up new abilities as you go making for a more robust set of ways to kill your enemies. But you still end up dying by getting what seems to be like getting GRAZED by a bullet. Its so frustrating. Its like you are made of glass! Again these are the things that I didn't like so much about the game and doesn't make it a bad game. The game usually had me at the edge of my seat because of the THRILL of being killed so easily and kind of makes for an anxious playthrough until you make it to the next checkpoint maybe some people are into that kind of thing.I was expecting a bit more combat and less parkour. I want more back and fourth between enemies where you can deflect bullets and hand out finishers that have you not only slashing them in half, but maybe elbowing them to drop their guard, spinning around behind them and decapitating them. Maybe even doing a finisher coming from above like in the very beginning of the game! Maybe use someone as a shield? There isn't any of that! Its just jump, jump, jump, slash, jump, run, jump! You're essentially playing tag with a katana! I'm just ranting. I really like this game, but I want more of it. The story and voice acting is engaging and the music is to die for. I love the atmosphere of every level especially with RTX ON. The surroundings are super immersive and makes me wish you could go into more of these buildings.Not a bad game. I think it can be expanded on. Looking forward to more updates or additions that maybe address some of the above I mentioned.I definitely recommend the game if you just want a parkour challenge with the cyberpunk future aesthetic and music.

_childDocuments_.review: A parkour death-simulator. It's a cool idea and for the most part a well executed game, but it's not without flaws. It took me 10 hours to finish the game, though there are tons of collectables that I haven't found, and I may well replay a few levels to try and complete them faster and with fewer deaths. For the most part, it's all about speeding through levels while figuring out how to get from A to B, making tricky jumps, slides, grapples along the way, and fighting off a ton of enemies with your sword and four 'special moves'. The whole game is one-hit-kills, whether that's you on enemies, or enemies on you. You will die. A lot. I think I must've died about 2,000 times. That's just part of the game, as you try to learn, trial-and-error, what the path is to victory and how to take out your enemies without getting hit. Generally it all works very well, it feels fluid and fast paced. But there are times when the auto-attach to walls you're trying to run along, or rails you're trying to grapple onto, just fails. Totally inexplicably you'll just fail to attach, which is incredibly frustrating near the end of a perfect run. A game like this lives and dies by one thing: is your failure to complete a challenge down to poor play, or the mechanics of the game? 90% of the time it's the former, which is great. It means you can go at it with the mindset of wanting to improve, or tweak your routes and plans of attack to achieve a smooth and satisfying victory. But the other 10% lurks in the background, where failures on the game's part make it incredibly frustrating. One thing I'd have liked to see is the inclusion of a few more 'simple' parts after a complex puzzle. I know it'll be a conscious decision on the developer's part, but there's never any time to feel like you achieved something, because you're immediately met with the next puzzle or challenge. Games like this should be rewarding through a sense of achievement, but the pacing of Ghostrunner means it ends up feeling a little oppressive. But ultimately I did enjoy it, I found myself eager to play it between sessions, and I'm glad I completed it. I think it's worth the asking price, and that'll be even more true if they patch in a few corrections to the auto-attach for walls/rails etc. Finally, a point on how it runs: generally butter-smooth on my AMD 390X and i7 6600k, right up until the very last level. For some reason the game started lagging and I encountered such bad frame drops that the level was literally impossible. Once I lowered my settings I breezed through it. Might want to look into that, Devs!

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get me wrong, Ghostrunner is a worth the time to play through of the campaign. That being said, as a fanatic of fast paced movement shooters, and cyborg ninjas (being one) I'm actually not the hugest fan of Ghostrunner.For a few reasons, Ghostrunner feels a little unfinished. The plot feels rather bare-bones, and some of the stages and levels have parts of them (platform spacing or distance) that make them feel either inconsistent or not yet fine-tuned. Sometimes the objective is very unclear and you have to guess -- It just feels a bit like it's still in Beta.In terms of mechanics, I think the game really takes the most hits. Movement feels rather forced, and (while a kind of funny parallel of being a cyborg can be drawn here), a lot of the automatic movement makes you do things you don't want to. In a way, you feel like you are not fully in control of what you're doing. Very often I'll latch on to a wall I don't intend to and start wallrunning into projectiles, instead of dropping down alongside it. You will also miss many sliding rails that feel like they're in range. The dash movement mechanics also seem rather convoluted- when you're on the ground, you can dash once, and that's it, but if you jump, the dash resets, unlike most games which regenerate things like double jumping or dashes on the ground, when and if you can dash is not shown by any icon on the screen. This makes the game feel frustrating not because it is hard, but in a "Bennet Foddy" frustrating of feeling like you're not in control.(I do like the B-hopping mechanic, which hilariously enough makes the final boss really easy)In many ways, you feel withheld and kind of weak - personally I prefer a bit of health over a "no-hit run" kind of game, but there's no room for error here. As a result, you spend most of the game dodging and very little of it fighting. I'm even a fan of the very early (and tough) platformer "Final Ninja Zero" (one of my all time favorites), which incorporates only 3 bars of health, while sometimes feeling like not nearly enough, is far better than no-hit (this same 3-heart mechanic in Neon White, my top game so far, works very well). So, you're a bit of a glass cannon -- And speaking of the cannon, your abilities are very cool and well thought out, but the amount of charge time it takes to use just one of them makes them used only once or maybe twice per level. As someone who wants to just go and fly and let loose the ninja, with the abilities and movement, this game can feel very limiting.Lastly, a lot of timing feels really off. The windows for parrying projectiles or certain enemies feels like guesswork at times, and can be very frustrating. Sometimes it feels like one run you just get lucky with parries and other times you get clipped by something completely random, or miss something you feel like you totally hit. In that way, the parrying feels inconsistent. Bossfights are mediocre at best.Okay, enough with the bad -- here's why you SHOULD play the game:THE AESTHETICS. THEY ABSOLUTELY NAILED THE AESTHETICS.This game is GORGEOUS. The detail, the map creation, the enemy design, the character appearances are all 110% spot on amazing and brilliant. The MUSIC that matches it is perfect for the environment. I love the main character appearance, all the sweet custom swords you pick up, the level just perfectly captures the "cyber-punk" aesthetic wonderfully.Additionally, the aesthetics of the combat aren't bad, when you're in combat and are fighting, the visuals are on point, it feels great jumping off a wall run and slicing through an enemy. The time-slowing dash mechanic is also visually very well executed (while feeling like it needs a little bit of tuning).---TLDR: The game is good, but feels unpolished, and can feel frustrating or inconsistent. If you're playing it, you're paying for the aesthetics, which is spectacular.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't hate it, but some of the balancing and design choices are frustrating.It really breaks any flow when you have to slowly strafe or dash around a shield enemy because you can't jump over them; or when you have to just sit there waiting, because the weeaboo sword enemies can only be countered; or when you have to awkwardly pause your approach with the wave-shooting robots, because you can't dodge their attacks within a certain range; or when you die to the leaping enemies because cutting them midair is frame-perfect, if possible, despite how fast you can slash in other instances of the game; or when you have to waste specials on the kamikaze cyborgs or else otherwise awkwardly run away or wait them out, completely killing the pace; or when you have to throw bodies at an area for recon, because there's a bunch of overlapping shield generators and moving platforms and such, like this is a puzzle game.These "perfect-run" action games are fun, and are a refreshing dose of adrenaline; however, frequent interruptions kill that high.  It's frustrating when you reach that flow and then suddenly find yourself in a puzzle platformer, or are presented with a wall of an enemy.  I wish I could give a neutral review.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw this game get announced at Gamescom I was very interested at its gameplay and when the demo rolled out to play I jumped on it as soon as I could. After playing for about two minutes, I was immediately hooked! The movement in this game is so unbelievably fluid and smooth, bouncing from wall to wall, dashing to get that extra bit of distance just when you think you can't make it and landing successfuly feels oh so satisfying. The addition of the grapple while traversing is possibly the most fun I've had with mid air movement in a long time.Then the combat comes into play, the one hit KOs that you deal as well as receive always keep you on your toes. You are always aware of your vulnerability and constantly need to be moving to survive. After playing the demo I really hoped that there would be a decent enemy variety and the full release follows through on that with different tactics to deal with each one. The sensory boost is extremely fun to use as well as being a big safety net, just when you think you're gonna get nailed, go slow-mo, maneuver around and fight or flee (Fight is the correct option imo unless you're a coward). If you do get killed, who cares! The basically instant respawn at a nearby checkpoint is a godsend and really is one of the most addicting parts of the game. Play. Run. Kill. Die. Respawn. Learn. With each attempt  your reflexes improve and you perform that tiny bit better. The abilities that you gain through the game helps to keep combat fresh and provides a great assistance when you're dealing with a particular difficult room, the variety amongst them helps in numerous scenarios and some can be more useful than others in certain rooms. The upgrade system for the abilities is very dynamic and not restricting allowing you to constantly change what abilities can be buffed at any given moment. The "puzzles" in the Cybervoid are a little strange to have in this game especially considering its a fast paced platformer, while they are few they do tend to twist up the pacing a little bit. The more successful puzzles are tackling the combat rooms in the right manner at first but then you think what you could have done better, faster and smoother and then slowly improving your reflexes and then showing significant improvement in handling foes. The story is nothing too fancy to write home about, it's quite intriguing and definitely works well in delivering a narrative, but its very clear that its secondary to the gameplay. The environment, level design and the soundtrack do such a good job of keeping you hooked on this game so effectively. Only one boss battle was not very inspired and in fact a bit boring in comparison to the rest where the others focused more on traversal and having to be smart about your movement. Having proper leaderboards with friends make this game so entertaining, being able to compare the different methods of tackling rooms as well as challenging each other for the fastest time with minimal deaths adds to this game's replayability tenfold! Being a huge platformer and movement fan, this game delivered a thoroughly satisfying experience and I junkied this mofo immediately!

_childDocuments_.review: Quick and informal review!Top-tier synthwave soundtrack and cyberpunk world. Graphically the game is very impressive both in art direction and graphical fidelity. 80-90% of the game takes a "realistic" environmental approach, but near the end it takes a weird arcade-y shift to it, Kind of like the change in art direction from Doom 2016 to Doom Eternal. In terms of art direction, it felt weird to me, but it provided a lot of fun gameplay right before the gameplay loop started to get stale.Speaking of gameplay - the most important part - it flows very well and has some of the most satisfying gameplay I've experienced in recent memory. Fast-paced, and while it is unforgiving in that all enemies can one-shot you (and you one-shot them), checkpoints are plentiful, and there is no down-time or loading screens when you (are ready to) restart.The story is meh. It gets the job done, establishes purpose for all characters involved and helps make the universe feel lived in, but both the characters and their journey lacks noteworthy depth. While it's not insultingly bad, it's completely forgettable. The gameplay is what you'll remember and come back for, and they have additional modes you can try out if you haven't had enough once you finish the story.For those with a flexible budget, this game is worth the full price in my opinion. For most other users, a sale bringing it down to $20-25 USD would be more reasonable.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get me wrong, this game is top quality as far as I'm willing to say, but the game... it's just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ridiculously difficult.Now I am known to have a generally short temper when it comes to video games, but this takes it to whole new level, there are some segments in the game (especially in rooms filled with enemies) that bring out the babyrage in me.Now I get the game wants you to learn the layout of a room and what paths to take before executing a plan in enemy filled rooms, but I die about 50+ times every time there is more than, oh idk 5 people there.It gets to the point where even if I have a strat down I'll still die 70% of the times I try to pull it off and it pisses me off to no end.On top of that, I've reached a complete roadblock with the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Kamikaze enemies. Seriously, they decide to throw a new enemy type that is basically unkillable without using tempest or something that is quicker than you, climbs on walls and explodes when it gets near... in great numbers... with other generally difficult enemy types.This has completely killed my motivation to finish the game in the forseeable future.On a more positive note, this game does so much right.It's a visual masterpiece throughout, nailing that neon-cyberpunk aesthetic perfectly, especially in the city stages with the blues, hot pinks and oranges.All the sword models are beautifully modelled and textured, with some nice inspect animations to show them off with, hats off to the modellers that developed those assets. Bravo!Sound design is generally good across the board.MOST enemies feel fair to fight, but sometimes they become too overwhelming in larger numbers.The customisation of abilities with chips is very innovative, I like the concept.The movement is generally smooth, I wouldn't say Titanfall 2 levels of quality parkouring but it's certainly up there.I'd rate this game a 6/10... I've had near 10 hours of decent fun, but its become a slog, and I've damn near lost motivation to continue playing.Movement is good, the game is decently challenging (sometimes too much so) and I personally lack the reaction times for some scenarios in this gameEDIT: After 3 or so more hours of persevering I finally managed to beat the game after not playing for literally 11 and a half months of putting the game down.JESUS. CHRIST. WHO DESIGNED THE LAST ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ LEVEL OF THIS GAME.*Spoiler* so the Mara bossfight was decently challenging, but very boring and predicatable with like 3-4 attacks on repeat (I died more times than I'd like to admit on this stage), but afterwards comes the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ crowning jewel of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ GAME DESIGN I have seen in recent years.The last level "The Monster" takes all the jank and issues with the game and puts em on full display here, I've never been more miserable finishing a game in my life. It took me 30 minutes to finish a stage that should have taken at most 15 with good parkour, but all the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ I encountered in the game up to this point appears and cranked itself up to 1000%. These red orbs sections are absolutely atrocious and difficult to avoid, I swear they veer towards you when you get within a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ kilometre of them too. ♥♥♥♥ the last mission, less so ♥♥♥♥ the rest of the levels (some were actually a lot more fun than I remember too) my godEDIT: Ghostrunner 2 plays 100000000% better, if you endure this slog you'll have a wonderful experience with the sequel

_childDocuments_.review: Buyers beware, this game is hard, VERY HARD and frustrating. Try before buying, and maybe see some playthroughs first. My review was made before the NEON update, which has a more lenient difficulty.If you've got the patience and skills to navigate the controls (I used a controller) and gameplay, this could be a fun, fast and visceral game. The game requires you to react fast and move just as fast, since I didn't have it, that meant slogging through each level, sometimes dying as much as 150+ times, the final level took me closer to 200 tries. The checkpoints in this game are occasionally generous and other time outright unfair, and if you don't complete a level, you have to restart it next time you play again, there's no picking up from a checkpoint mid-level. 4 skills are picked up in the course of the game, but see limited use, as the skills are mostly one use with long cool downs between usage. I also encountered a game breaking bug with a button that hindered progress and almost had me restarting the entire level, until I discovered a workaround on youtube.Visually, the game is great, the cyberpunk aesthetics are great, the decay, the industrial dystopia, with all its neon signs really sells the setting. Audio wise, the sound effects are good, with each slash, jump, gunfire, NPC dialogue being distinct and adding to the immersion. The music is a highlight, I never got bored of the music.In the end, the game didn't work for me, while I did complete the main story I didn't feel the sense of accomplishment, sheer stubbornness had carried me to completion of the game on normal, and I had no further desire to play further. At some point even before the 1st boss, I begun to question how much fun I'm having.Imagine having to fill up a multiple choice question answer sheet where you have to shade in your answers with a pencil, they give you a fine tip HB pencil and tell you to shade the answer sheet darkly and precisely, you'll have to shade each answer for at least 3 seconds, and if you fill in the wrong answer or shade past the boundaries, you can't erase your mistake, take a new answer sheet and fill it in from the start, all 300 of the questions you need to fill.This game has definitely found its audience, as the number of positive reviews can attest to, I'm just not one of em. Again caveat emptor, I strongly recommend trying before buying and maybe checking out non-perfect playthroughs so you understand just how difficult the game is.

_childDocuments_.review: While the experience is let down on occasion by its eagerness to wall-run/grab on to EVERYTHING, the majority of the game is fast, fun, precise, and empowering. Some later levels and enemy compositions are a bit ridiculous, but in general there's as many solutions to every puzzle as you could think of- even without using skills... except for the boss design. I respect the difficulty in designing bosses for a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cyborg ninja, but the glorified quick-time events and playground jump-rope that is the boss fights is a bit jarring and I might have preferred a game of tag instead. Still, I don't mean to focus on the negative- the visuals, music, story, general gameplay, progression, tools, extra game-modes, collectables, and more are likeable enough to warrant a 9/10... it's just so close to perfect that I couldn't help it! If that isn't a positive review, I don't know what is.

_childDocuments_.review: I think the best way to understand it is that it's a movement based game. The way you move is the core mechanic. It's an extremely difficult game but at the same time the checkpoint frequency is extremely forgiving, so that balances out well into micro situations that you will die a whole lot at, sometimes hundreds of times, but yet in a way that isn't discouraging. There's even an "instant restart" option that lets you return to the same checkpoint instantly, without going through any menus. The game encourages you to fail frequently and immediately try again, and because it's so well broken up into single encounters for each checkpoint this never makes you want to quit. In a lot of ways it feels like a puzzle game with FPS mechanics. It reminds me a bit of how I felt about the game Red Hot except this one is extremely fast and adrenaline pumping. It's the same adrenaline high I get from playing something like Doom, but it feels much more like a puzzle. Doom is chaotic with enemy movement a lot more dynamic. Restarting from the same save over and over will have enemies do wildly different things. This one is much less dynamic and much more intentional. The enemies will always be in the same place and always be expected to do the exact same thing each time, and so handling them feels more like solving a puzzle, but still requires quick reflexes and good hand eye coordination.In case someone is reading this and doesn't know, one of the core mechanics is that everything dies in one hit, including you. Every enemy dies in one hit, but you die in one hit too. So in each room, you have to find that way to dispatch half a dozen or more guys without taking a single bullet.It's not easy. But it's super fun and super addicting. 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics don't make up for how janky the entire experience is. Wallrunning and dashing (90% of the game) feels clunky and sometimes leads to death for no reason. The AI is too sparse and too powerful for combat to feel satisfying. Level design is is unintuitive and I found myself often falling to my death because the path forwards is not immediately always obvious. The parkour is heavily railroaded. Don't be fooled by how open some of these environments look, the game is very linear. Don't even get me started on the laser boss. The gameplay loop is just not for me. I don't think the "Hotline Miami" type of gameplay works for a first person shooter. You get hit once, and it's over. That means if you're trying to run away, you're dead. If two or more enemies see you, you're dead. It just doesn't work in a 3D environment. The demo feels way better than the full game. If you find yourself 2 hours in and hoping it gets better, it doesn't. Save your money if the game doesn't immediately and consistently captivate you.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played a couple hours of Ghostrunner, I found it to be an enjoyable game.  In terms of the type of game, it's pretty unique but I would classify it as mostly a platformer that is heavily based around reaction time/quick button events.  Mechanics:  The mechanics in this game are great but not without its flaws.  You can deflect abilities (unlocked early into the game), dash, and have 4 abilities to use.  You also only have one attack button.  That's about it to this game.  The enemies are not complex at all - they either shoot projectiles at you or they try to melee you.  Try to either deflect/parry or dodge/dash to defeat them.  Story: The story is extremely weak.  With the loud music pumping in the background and no effort being made to really draw you into the world, the story can be ignored for 100% of the game and still be enjoyable.  Although I tried to listen to the "important" dialogue it really needs more fleshing out to really be more immersive.  Don't play this game for the story.Consensus: I don't think this game is worth $20-30.  It really isn't.  The gameplay is great and fun, but I really can't recommend this game in terms of just the gameplay itself.  For someone like myself who really enjoys competitive games, this fills that niche of playing extremely repetitive gameplay to perfect very little detail.  If you also want to feel like a badass running on walls, dashing, and slicing, then try this game out.  But for anyone looking for any semblance of a story or more complicated game mechanics, this really isn't the game to purchase.  In-depth: The graphics are decent, the gameplay is extremely repetitive, story is non-existent.  There are some parts of the game where you dash against walls and the character just doesn't "stick" or try to wall run anymore even though it's consistent about 95% of the time.  In terms of the ziplines, it feels awkward to not be able to jump off the zip, move to the side and then dash back onto the zip.  It doesn't change any of the gameplay, but it definitely feels more "natural" as I would expect someone to be able to let go of a zipline and grab it again rather than just fall to their death.The gameplay feels more tedious than providing value/fun because there are only a limited number of ways to play against the extremely limited amount of enemies you face in this game. Projectiles have a tiny window to be deflected unless you have the upgraded perk and when taking on multiple enemies it seems much more picking off one enemy at a time than fighting them like a badass ninja.  I find myself always relying on phase shift (slowing time) to deal with multiple enemies as there really is no way to deflect all of the projectiles at once.  One enemy later on in the game is a suicide bomb type of enemy and there is no way to really use your blade against them so you are forced to use one of your abilities (which has a cooldown).  For someone who enjoys repetitive games and wants to perfect every detail, this game is great for me.  But on the premise of offering an in-depth combat system and a fully fledged story, look elsewhere for $30.  I would easily pick up this game for $10-15 but not for $20-30.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun game for the most part. Quite difficult as well. There are parts which feel quite out of place such as a section at the end which was entirely a dynamic obstacle course that felt far too different from the rest of the game to the point of frustration. I did not find that part fun at  all.The controls are extremely tight to the point where you need to be very precise with timing and aiming. This made the game a bit of a unique experience but at times very frustrating as one slightly different movement, resulting in you being faster or slower than your previous attempt or moving in a different direction, can change the future state of the enemies an catch you off guard. There were some encounters where I could engage in almost the same way every time and I would be noticed by enemies in some attempts but not be noticed in others. This is another case where enemy behaviour was so inconsistent that you would have to adapt your plan on the fly. In some cases, this was good as it meant I was always on my toes but it was also frustrating at points. Consistency is not something this game does well despite it needing to IMO. Your basic toolbox the game gives you is a sword, a dash, wall running and a matrix-esque time-slowing skill for dodging stuff that ends in a dash. The game also gives you a number of abilities unlocked slowly as you progress through the game. I tend to be quite conservative when it comes to abilities like these, only saving them for the odd situation which I can't do with the normal toolbox. You can probably finish the whole game without the unlockable abilities. This could make for an interesting challenge but I'm not patient enough for that.The boss fights left a lot to be desired. There are 3 in total. I'll try not to spoil them. The first one was great but the other 2 felt a little out of place. Also, the final boss is essentially just a female cyberpunk Dr Octopus. Not necessarily a bad thing but I think they could've done better.The story is alright. It felt like background for the gameplay. Outside of Mr Robo-samurai, there are 3 characters: AI dude you're helping, Mrs Dr Octopus and a rebel who nopes out of the story half way through. I got the feels for the rebel when she does nope out but forgot about here later. At the end of the game, the narrator (who is the rebel from earlier in the game) emphasises how Mr Robo-samurai made a choice. It's a little generic: the machines rising up against their creators kinda deal. What would've been nice to see is if we, as the player, actually got to make that choice. I kinda would've liked to see what would've happened if the other thing happened. Not a huge deal but acceptable for a game of this scope and price. I'd also like to mention that the voice acting is pretty good for the most part, aside from for Mrs Dr Octopus. I couldn't quite put my finger on it, but it kinda sounded like she was speaking with a mix of american-english, chinese and canadian accents and somewhat inconsistently.I think my largest gripe with the game is how long it is. 6 hours. Now I could make the replayability argument. I thought I would before I started playing but if I'm honest, I don't think I want to replay this game. It's fun for what it is but I don't think it's exceptional and worth the additional play through. The game doesn't offer any additional game modes; you have the story and that's it. No challenges, no new game+, no modifiers, nothing. There's collectables so you could go back for those but they only come in the form of sword skins and random items which do jack all. Assuming you looked for them all in your first run, that might net you another 2 hours of playtime. I'd recommend getting this on a sale. At the time of purchase which was on release day, the game was £20 (£25 with 30% off). At £20, let alone £25, I can't see this being worth it for a number of people given the lack of content. It's a good game and unique enough to give a solid recommendation. There's a demo as well, so I'd suggest giving that a go before buying. 7/10, too many walls to run on.

_childDocuments_.review: The slashing is cool and the visuals look nice, and the music fits well. I also enjoy the skill "tree" aspect even though it only slightly changes your gameplay. Nothing else stands out and there are some key issues reduced my enjoyment.Most importantly Ghostrunner needs to give the player more direction on what they are supposed to be doing or where their objective is. More often than not I was left wondering what I was supposed to be doing in any given part of the game, even in areas that should be straightforward. Platforming sections sometimes have an objective of where the finish line is (and sometimes not which is inconsistent) but other objectives like the key to unlock the door or a boost to get past a fan I am left wandering around.New mechanics with no explanation are thrown in with a difficult platforming section so you don't even know if you're doing the mechanic wrong or the platforming (it was the platforming, silly me thinking I had to use the new ability).The mid-game boss fight is another cyber ninja and you don't have your abilities but your main attack only blocks, and there is no clue or audio hint on what you should be doing. After ten minutes of looking around and trying different things I looked it up, and you just have to block perfectly several times in a row to get a counterattack.....The puzzles in "cybervoid" did a horrible job at "show don't tell" puzzle style. The first puzzle in the game the solution was a differently-colored pattern in the floor, which did not catch my eye (no color blind mode, probably wouldn't have even helped), and the only hint the voice over gave was "You need to figure this out." The second had some switches that rotated some lines on the wall but there was no explanation or hints so the puzzles seemed really out of place in an action-focused game.In the third one there's just invisible walls and the voice tells you "just hurry up" and you say "this place is impossible to navigate" and their response is "good" I know the gameplay needs to be padded out because just the cool combat would make the game really short but it could have been done in a much better way.You get an ability that charges up on kills, but doesn't charge up at checkpoints, so sometimes after using the ability on the next section it would be really nice to have it again but there's no way to turn around and charge it so you're just going to have to do the section over and over without the ability, making it feel like a trap to use.The controls did not feel fluid to me and were awkward to get the hang of. Early on you get a dash that is very short range and leaves you vulnerable if you use it on the ground, but if you're midair it slows time and allows you to strafe to dodge bullets and then dash in, so why not have that be the same while you're on the ground? It's just strictly better to bunny hop and then dash so you can slow time and strafe while closing in but that felt stupid to meThe story could have been dialed back, since it is just voice lines from two characters they could have just said "Hey get to the top floor, I'll see ya in 17 levels" but at just about every checkpoint one of the two has something to say for no reason. It got to the point where any time either of them started talking I just wanted to mute the game, even moreso when they talk during combat and when I die their voice line restarts so sometimes I listen to the first five words a dozen times in rapid succession and finally just end up standing still until they are done so I don't have to hear their broken record audio lines.Even if there wasn't all this filler from random platforming between combat sections, dialogue, and puzzles, the core combat areas aren't great. Overall I would rather just play Superhot.

_childDocuments_.review: A promising IP within an upcoming mainstream genre, Ghostrunner offers a scratch for that cyberpunk itch with it's high-octane levels of one-hit violence and platforming delivered in a tight 5-6 hours, replayability is subject to fast times and low deaths.The world (the levels) while samey, creates a claustrophobic concrete playground for you to exploit and manoeuvre and you WILL be rewarded for having the wits to save yourself from a fall or finding a quicker, alternative path. To add, enemy variety provides much needed respite from the monotony.The story serves it's purpose in creating a believable world, with key details obscured as to pique your interest without suffocating the player, I would definitely like to see it expanded upon in any future titles or dlc.My only issues is that there were times of frustration during the puzzle sequences, they can drag out for too long at times and aren't particularly fun, perhaps if there was more platforming and combat akin to the regular levels (but still focusing on the puzzle elements) I feel like that would be an improvement, the second issue is more personal to me, but I felt that there were times I should have clearly performed a wall-run, only to fall to my death or vault off things I want to precisely jump on, but I could also say the movement is focused on "flow" rather than precision.Did I mention the soundtrack is absolutely killer?All in all, I really enjoyed this game, i'm glad I had the opportunity to play it and hope it encourages more studios to explore the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely amazing game from start to finish. No meaningless padding - just top quality at all times. The power fantasy is incredibly well done. You really feel like a cyber ninja that's capable of carving his way through opponents while leaving them confused about what's happened.New power unlocks are gradual and well paced, letting you get accustomed to mechanics and become adept at using them. The flow of combat and the animations are top notch; the wall running especially FEELS right. The way the camera moves gives you the impression of the Ghostrunner's body being angled correctly, even if his feet aren't rendered/part of the model (one of the only 2 gripes I have with the game). Between combat encounters, you have a masterfully done mix of platforming and parkour, and even some relatively simple yet engaging puzzles (with the exception of only one, which is my other gripe with the game; that puzzle can go ♥♥♥♥ itself 10 times out of 10; it was the toughest boss of the game, lul). Speaking off, boss fights are really, really great. They will not be what you expect, except for the final boss perhaps, which is very fun nonetheless. There are 3 bosses in the game, and each one feels very different from the other. General combat works on the premise of 1 shot = dead - for both you, and the enemy. This makes the combat lovingly challenging by introducing real stakes. Thankfully, checkpoints are perfectly implemented, and loading times are instantaneous (at least with my M2 SSD). The story serves its purpose very well too. It won't blow you out of the water, and neither will the characters, but it's properly written, very well voice acted, and it has great characters for what the game is and what narrative it wants to drive. The atmosphere is super spot on. It felt way more cyberpunky and "bleak future" in around 10 hours than Cyberpunk did in 122.You also get a few skill upgrades spaced out throughout the story too. They present some variety, allowing you to "slot" the upgrades you wanna use that complement your playstyle.All in all a very solid experience. I highly recommend the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostrunner is a first person platformer with strong action sequences and combat.The game consists of two parts: the first is running and climbing, where you can use special moves like wallrunning or a grapple hook. The second is combat, mostly with your sword but also with four special skills that are unlocked throughout the story.Both of these parts are combined brilliantly and fused to an almost perfect game. As you die very quickly (one hit) you will be moving the entire time and several different enemies with very special skillsets are going to test your reflexes and mastery of the mechanics.You are going to die a lot during this game but most of the times you know your error and will be able to fix it.Unfortunately, there are some sequences (e. g. the entire last of the 17 levels) that are frustrating at times. And the cybervoid - a much slower alternate universe where you unlock new skills - is boring as hell.But fighting and jumping through the levels is amazing and will keep you going.Ghostrunner is even improved by some smaller details as the great soundtrack that gets into your head and pushes you forward or the skill system, where you have to arrange your skills like Tetris boulders on limited space. Of course, the setting, a dystopian cyberpunk future, is great as well and the graphics and atmosphere match the game perfectly.Overall a fantastic game with incredibly high pace and a trial and error system with just minor problems.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun as all hell. In short, I'd give it a 3/5When it comes to the main gameplay, this game merges the thrilling speed of the Doom reboots (2016, Eternal) with tactics driven melee combat most similar to games like Katana Zero (Devolver Digital 2019). After reading some reviews from steam on release day, I've mostly seen complaints about shielded enemies and lengthy and meaningless platforming sections. There is some truth to the dubious platforming claim, but it is tolerable in the early stages of the game because it serves as an efficient side task during expository info dumps that I found pretty interesting. However, at the tail-end of the game there are some wall running sections that are completely superfluous and removing them from the game would improve the final product. Otherwise the other 90% of this game is highly polished and immersive, and anybody even remotely interested in this game should buy it.-SPOILER TERRITORY-UPGRADE SYSTEM: The upgrade system in this game is a game within itself. It's a tetris game in which certain upgrades hold forms that take up a given number of spaces, and it's your job as the player to select which upgrades you value most, and manipulate your pieces in effort to fit as many upgrades as you can. In my opinion, this system has a lot of potential, but falls short due to the content of the upgrades themselves. Each upgrade seems interesting at surface level, but in practice most of them are useless. Any of the upgrades related to the four skills you unlock throughout the game are essentially worthless, and take up too much space on your upgrade board to impact your play in any meaningful way. The map upgrades (yellow in-game) are pretty useful and give the player a good idea of where enemies are in relation to walls, climbable objects, and other obstacles. These are actually quite helpful, but in my opinion the skills and benefits they produce should be available in the player's fundamental tool kit. The only other slightly meaningful modifications are the dash upgrades, of which 4/5 are useless. These four are the extra dashes, resulting in a possible of four in total. However, only one dash can be used midair before touching the ground or wall running again, so avoiding these upgrades is the best move unless you intentionally want to miss out on the actually meaningful map upgrades. BOSSES:There aren't many bosses in the game, but boy do the first two pack a punch. The first boss is by far the strongest boss battle I've seen in a 3D platformer in a while, as there is no actual combat, but instead a combination of platforming challenges and moving obstacles that is executed quite well. The second boss is more of a mixture of platforming and combat to a degree, but it largely falls short. The platforming in this section isn't challenging, and the obstacles being fired at you are too predictable and easy to avoid without using a dash. Most unfortunate is the final boss battle. It's deficient in the use of verticality that the game builds itself upon so well in every other section. The boss doesn't move. Instead, it's doctor. octopus-like tentacles slowly fling themselves at you while the boss stares blankly. You cannot attack this boss or interact with it in any meaningful way until you dodge for MINUTES. This usually isn't an issue for me, as I'm a pretty patient gamer <3, but in a game built as intentionally on speed and intentional movement, the meaningless meandering this boss has the player doing is boring and highly uninteractive.STORY: The story is good, although you hardly see the effects of the player's actions throughout the game until the end credit animated sequence. I'm not gonna spoil it, play it yourself and do your best to pick up the optional collectibles to read for LORE.FINAL GAMEPLAY SECTION: The game really falls off at the end due to the dubious platforming complaint voiced by most of the negative reviews on steam. The post-final boss platforming section is boring, uninspired, and begins to hurt my youthful eyes after a few minutes of play. The lack of dash upgrades makes it really difficult to do this section the way I think the developers intended. Oversized red balls (which you see nowhere else in the game) attach themselves to the walls and surfaces you're supposed to run on, hindering the fluid movement this game executes so well everywhere else.

_childDocuments_.review: TRY THE DEMO, IT'LL GIVE YOU A GOOD VIEW OF WHAT THE WHOLE GAME IS LIKETL;DR: Really fast movement with excessive mobility, satisfying game mechanics, however occasional issues such as with some platforming and puzzle levels that take too longI can't think of any firstperson game with more speed to the game than this one. + Pretty good music, it's not too obnoxious, it flows well with the game+ Movement I can compare mostly to Titanfall 2, except instead of a double jump, you get a dash and some other mechanics like grappling points+ Game gives you tons of mobility options. Then even more, then even more after that+ Sword is just lenient enough that it's fun to use but isn't too easy+ 1-hit KO for both you and enemies excluding certain bosses+ Lots of fun, varying enemy types, except those dumb suicide bombers which you can just run past and ignore+ Interesting looking levels (the game's graphics are VERY good, even on the lowest settings)- There are a few frustrating and slow levels, which are clearly not optimized for speedrunning (such as forcing you to wait at the start of a level to not die) AND- Slow puzzle rooms that require you to do stuff such as SLOWLY rotate pieces in a puzzle, or slowly walk along a bunch of platforms with dash and wallrunning disabled- I know the last level has RNG for sure (the red orbs) and I'd be willing to bet there are other forms of RNG, which I hate for games like this.- Extremely cliche and predictable story. Not a single even happened in a way I didn't predict from the very start of the game- You need to hit a wall with enough speed and not be looking at it for it to "grab" it- Grapple points don't forcibly pull your character to them so sometimes you'll grab it and sometimes end up in inconsistent spots- Ziplining is weird and sometimes just doesn't grab it despite being practically in the center of it- Weird mechanic that makes your character pull himself up if he falls just short of a wall.... Which happens on moving platforms and even ones where the level is rotating, causing you to sometimes climb up walls for no reason (which can launch you off the map)+ Running along walls is really fun, being able to dash constantly is fun, sliding and all the mechanics of dodging and stuff are really fun and well polished

_childDocuments_.review: Decided to download the demo of the game and the moment I heard the soundtrack for the intro before the main menu I was sold on the game. The music is awesome and perfectly compliments the gameplay. Speaking of which, I'd like to say that as a person who never plays platformers, I really enjoyed this game, since it had a bit more depth, different ways of handling the same situation and general diversity in the playstyle(certainly a lot more than I expected from the game). The story and the world were also (imo) well built and interesting to watch/listen to.That being said, there are some points that really rustled my jimmies: for starters, the "kamikaze" enemies were overkill in my opinion - the game's enemies up to that point were spot on and always felt fair, having different ways to defeat. For those little ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, you just have to run around like a madman and hope they don't clip you. In addition to things, that I feel like they were overkill(small SPOILER): the last level after defeating the boss was tedious and repetitive and really felt like rinse and repeat more than actual timing or skill. I usually don't care about dying a lot in a game, but the way the platforms worked in the last level just drove me insane(mainly because of the clunky clipping when jumping from wall to wall.TLDR: it's a cool game that has some cheese added to it for extra difficulty. I'd recommend it, though, since it's a good concept with amazing gameplay and a soundtrack to back it up.
