_childDocuments_.review: Everybody seems to love this game, but honestly I almost do but I don't.The combat is fast paced - too fast. You don't get to see any of the actual combat, you're there and you slash and you might have seen some blood? And then you're already gone and past that enemy. It's very anime 'nothing personell kid'. But honestly, I'd like to see some slow-mo dismemberment as I'm flying past. Maybe focus at the right time? But that shoots you forward and potentially of an edge.  There should be a slow-mo key like focus but not a dodge.The enemies have perfect aim and they don't tell you off the bat that you can block shots by swinging your sword at the right time, so once I get close, I spam sword because if I don't, even if I dodge, they track perfectly and kill in one shot. It should have a timed block or parry mechanic with right click.The levels are extremely linear and because of how fast you move and how your path is painted in yellow (except when it isn't) exploring doesn't feel right, it feels like I should be moving. Obviously there are some artifacts or swords or collectibles somewhere. The soundtrack is cool, and it takes the fun wall running from titan fall, but part of the fun of titan fall was being able to shoot and see your combat effectiveness.This game is very simple and limited in its scope, which makes it that much more of a crime that it gets some of those things wrong. Maybe I'll give it another shot later, and maybe the mechanics I want are in there but not introduced yet, but for now, it's a no from me.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy extremely iffy controls that make up the entirety of "difficulty" then sure, it'll be fun. Having your character randomly decide to magnetize to a wall around a corner out of nowhere or not grab onto a ledge, or not responding to your inputs isn't "oh it's just a difficult game". No, it's just awful controls and lazy implementation of mechanics. Sometimes your character will lock on to an enemy when you click, sometimes you'll either spaz out or nothing at all happens.Terrible controls =/= difficulty, it's just terrible controls. If your character actually did what you wanted him to do all the time instead of like 30% of the time, this game would be fun and still challenging.The game gives you this feeling that you're supposed to be rushing through every area, yet half the time you have no idea where the hell you're supposed to be going. It has good music at least but everything else is just straight up stupid.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty cool setup, but as you play it gets pretty repetitive.Characters are constantly spouting loredump exposition in the same monotone voice as you play, and you're forced to keep going through these weird cyber world levels that physically hurt to look at because of how obnoxiously bright the effects are.The combat gets pretty boring rather than challenging because you're forced to run around killing these shield spheres which make the enemies invincible. Seemed like a cool mechanic to draw more attention to the parkour at first, but later on you get encounters where have to destroy one shield to destroy this shield to destroy another shield and ONLY THEN can you actually start fighting back at the dudes who've been shooting at you this whole time.

_childDocuments_.review: It will be a no for me, the music and tempo made me hope for a feeling like Doom2016 but thats so far from what this is. The description of this as an action game is misleading it more of a puzzle platformer. Sure you slash enemies but the enemies are nicely spaced out so that you can take one of the two paths that most levels offer you and then go down the path killing them one at a time. Every level is designed to have 1-2 solutions to where you go and which enemy you kill in which order.This becomes painfully clear once you start the levels were all enemies are shielded by a robot ball, you need to platform jump-wallrun-slingshot yourself to the robot ball just to realize this robot ball is shielded by another robot ball (>_>)Yeah really, you need to platform to one ball to kill it and then platform to another to kill that one to then be able to fight the actual enemies that one hit kills you. One mistake you're dead time to restart the platform puzzle err I mean restart the intense action combat....Its actually a good game but its not something I enjoyed and I will refund

_childDocuments_.review: If you thought you were getting a fluid and fun game that focuses on adrenaline pumping gameplay, you're not. The game has awful animations and even worse it's on rail and clunky feeling. This is the main, HUGE problem with this game that makes it fall flat on its face.- You walk next to a wall? You're automatically going to run alongside it without holding or even pressing anything down. - You're near an edge? You'll climb it whether you want to or not.- You want to attack an enemy? Your view will be moved and locked onto the enemy during the attack animation.It feels super cheap and clunky. It takes precise control from you in order to do pre-set cheap looking movement and animations that OFTEN bug out and you end up stopping or gripping onto the wrong thing. In a game that is meant to be all about gameplay (because the story in this is just listening to audio while you struggle with the controls from what I've seen), it's the thing that it fails at the most.The music is decent, the overall graphics are serviceable even though I was playing at 144hz, 2k, max graphics it still wasn't that interesting visually after the first 30 minutes.Oh, and there's also some weird, silly and very boring "platforming" and "puzzle" sections where you're literally jumping from one platform to another for 10 minutes...Refunded it after an hour, not even worth £20.

Grappling to a vent should never have your character somehow grab onto the top of the vent and be put awkwardly there. Icons for grappling shouldnt even appear if its not something you can reach or bare minimum it shouldnt be just a different shade of blue. Having a slow mo dash in air but not on the ground is just weird. Power ups later in the game probably fix it but it just feels janky. Through the hour I played there were way to many times in simple parkour areas that it just didnt properly convey where you needed to go. "The Climb" is the best example. Plenty of places where im doing a 360 scan to figure out where the next area is. Ai even seems to have a set distance where they just cannot miss. _childDocuments_.review: While the setting, atmosphere and music are top notch, the gameplay itself is kind of lacking. I've beaten Hotline Miami and Katana Zero, so I'm used to the trial and error style of gameplay, but I think that this game leans a bit too far into it, as those two allow for SOME improvisation when it comes to level clearing. Ghost Runner doesn't have that, as you have to throw yourself at a level over and over until you find the exact way to clear it. It doesn't help that probably HALF of my deaths were due to the wallrunning system NOT working and falling into the pit. And sometimes the jump pattern being consistent, and others it will force you into about HALF power of the jump. And sometimes you will just be short on a wallrun, no matter what, and you will fall to your death, even if you see it coming. I wanted to like this game, it had some parts that really got me pumped, but the problem is that the game fought me every step of the way to get me to like it. I hope the sequel fixes some of the mechanics that don't work as well as they could.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is best described as cyberpunk Mirror's Edge with a bit of combat. The levels are linear, and the main focus is on the parkour/platforming. There's a generic sci-fi story going on in the background, but you can't make any choices that affect it. You die in one hit, so the game is more about trying the same section over and over again, sometimes with very precise timing, until you can do it perfectly, rather than improvising solutions.The parkour is good. It feels fast and the controls are nice and smooth, once you get the hang of them at least. Flying through the air dodging bullets and then landing on a guy and chopping him in half is really fun, even when you have to repeat it exactly the same 30 times in a row. I do wish, though, that you had a few more moves. Here you basically just have wall run, slide, dash, and a grappling hook to pre-determined points. Mirror's Edge also had vaulting, swinging, vertical wall runs, balance beams and probably some other stuff I'm forgetting, and that game wasn't even sci-fi. What's there is fun but they could have added a lot more.Combat really feels like another platforming challenge with some added pressure, rather than a fight. Since you die in one hit, and most enemies don't move, a combat encounter is basically just figuring out the optimal way to move through the environment and kill everything, and then trying again and again until you get it right. If you hide behind a box, you can wait there as long as you like to figure out your next move. There are a couple of special moves you unlock which kill enemies from a bit further away, but they have a very long cooldown so you can only really use one per encounter, and they end up feeling more like 'get out of jail free cards' in case you find one section too difficult, rather than proper weapons you would use on the fly. Most of the time I forgot they existed.Just to drive home the fact that the game is not about combat, the final boss of the game isn't even a boss, it's just an extra-difficult platforming section with no enemies.The environments all look good, but none are particularly memorable, and something about the way everything is composed of these very large, sometimes nonsensical platforms makes them start to feel like they're not really real places, just testbeds made by a game designer. By the end of the game (about 8 hours), I was pretty sick of being in them.I definitely recommend using mouse + keyboard. To do certain moves you need to flick your mouse around quite precisely and I have no idea how you'd do it with a controller. Low framerate also makes the game a lot harder - I had to stop streaming and lower the graphics a bit just to make combat playable (I have a GTX 970).Overall, I'd give it 3/5: an enjoyable 8 hours if you like the cyberpunk setting or want some fast-paced action and have already played DOOM Eternal. Worth picking up if it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: It's quite good. Well developed, good music, visuals and the combat is exciting af. The story is okayish. _childDocuments_.review: This is like playing , , and  while cracked out on Russian Dubstep.  You will die.  A lot.  Or maybe you don't suck as bad as me, and you won't.  But I doubt it.   is a first person parkour cyberpunk platformer that is completely unabashed in flaunting its influences.  The story is ham fisted and derivative, and honestly I had a hard time following it just because I was so enamored in the gameplay.  The music is intoxicating electronica that really sets the mood.  More than once I felt that if a camera were trained on me, the scene would be like one of those hacker montages from classic movies of the 80s & 90s, complete with dilated pupils and quick cuts of keystrokes and mouse wrist flicks as my character leaps from surface to surface, bouncing from kill to kill.Until I get tagged by a goon and die in one hit.  And then I hit a key to immediately restart from a convenient checkpoint.  Try again!The achievements are pretty straightforward, nothing is missable.  Several are skill based.  The base game has an obnoxious challenge for killing 23 enemies in a row, while the DLC furthers the sadism with a complete no-death level run.  But we are talking an hour or two max to get these done, the rest of the difficulty is just clearing the story naturally.  For those that have played , the entire experience was akin to my time trying to clear the  trophy.  Often times frustrating, but immensely rewarding.

_childDocuments_.review: While it wasn't what I expected i was still interested when starting Ghostrunner. It's closer to hotline miami than a traditional movement FPS. Each room is solvable using multiple different forms of movement and it definitely starts out as a fun experience where you feel like a cyber ninja. The freerunning segments are fantastic and the movement is well done. The game starts to lose its luster during combat when you realize that no matter how much flippy dipping you do some enemies will track you through walls and shoot you anyways.There was seriously a point where I realized that circle strafing dodged more ranged attacks than using my sweet ninja abilities and that was very frustrating. Each encounter is like a mini puzzle but some of the pieces aren't playing fair. If you're a player who likes rehearsing and repetition so that you can get everything exactly right, this is a perfect game for you. I wanted a power fantasy with all the movement but dying in one hit to enemies that don't react realistically to you zipping around broke the illusion for me.also the cybernet levels are dog ass. Who decided to take your cool parkour abilities away for a seek and find level?

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game and its second part, so I'll tell you about it and why it's worth playing it.Let's go through the main aspects by which you can evaluate the game.The picture looks juicy, all textures are in good resolution and it's nice to play on any graphics settings, regardless of your PC.This game is made in the cyberpunk style, which everyone is already tired of, especially after everyone who could have watched and played Cyberpunk 2077, but this game is a little different. The plot of the game takes place in a large tower, where there are several floors, it is impossible to live outside this tower, and those who live there are stuffed with various body modifications, which is why they have degraded. You play as a "running shadow". that is, a robot that was essentially raised and created to kill. There are neon signs everywhere. All opponents are also packed with mods. Everything is almost like in Cyberpunk 2077, but if you delve into this setting, the picture becomes completely different.The music is perfectly chosen, which is why I want to thank the one who wrote these soundtracks separately. Each musical theme fits the level and the situation.This game is a platformer. but what's difficult? And the fact is that any opponent kills you with 1 hit, and some levels and opponents are built on the fact that you need to sweat to get close to him or pass him.In fact, there are 3 game modes + an add-on.The main company, which is divided into ordinary complexity and complex, where opponents from later levels appear already at the first levels.Arena mode, where you need to clean up the arena, then choose an upgrade and move on.And the race mode, where you have to go through some kind of time trial and get a medal.The game has skins for katana and hand.To get skins, you either need to search the map, or go through the race and the arena, or buy.This game is very interesting, challenging and good in terms of music and graphics in all its parameters. I rate the game at 8/10, because there are bugs in the game that clearly interfere with the game. The simplest example would be passing through textures in a race, which is why you had to restart the race more than once.I recommend the game to be played.Good luck and have a good game.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Went back to give it another try. For those of you having trouble with the Hel boss fight, try disabling raytracing, since the parry indicators are really hard to see with it enabled. Although I still think she should have checkpoints like every other boss fight in the game, being able to actually see the parry cues let me beat her on my third try.It also seems that most of the movement issues have been patched since my original review, making the parkour aspect more enjoyable. Nice to see devs fixing this stuff up, and without the frustrating issues I initially saw, I had a blast playing through the game. Working my way through hardcore mode now.Overall, expect 20-30 hours (assuming you play through both normal and hardcore) of very, very challenging yet engaging gameplay. While it can be frustrating at times, the feeling of satisfaction when you finally overcome a particularly difficult level makes it all worth it.Original review:The first 3/4 of the game was great-- gradual increase in difficulty, interesting environments and abilities, and very, very engaging combat. I did have a number of issues with movement (ex. character climbing on top of a billboard instead of wall-running, and character attempting to wall run but just... not, falling to their death). Focus mode also seems to have some issues, activating only against normal (shooting) enemies. Thankfully, these bugs weren't too obtrusive until later in the game.Sadly, one thing had to come along and ruin the game (or, at least block my playthrough of it): Hel.See, the game syncs her "damage inflicted" code with animations, instead of physics; for instance, my character could have just dodged her strike, standing two meters away, but he still dies when she flips her sword in the air. Once the attack animation is started, you *have* to parry, and it has to be at innane time (see below)In another case, she might be winding up for an overhead strike, and you would instinctively want to parry as soon as she swung. Nope! You can only parry once her sword is embedded in your character (literally clips thru the camera), because only that part of the animation is glowing (which allows you to actually parry).Finally, you have to beat her in 4 stages, the later of which force you to move around the arena-- by the time I could reliably get to stage 4, I was dying more to movement bugs (as above) than I was her.Unlike Dark Souls and family, it didn't really *feel* like I was fighting the boss. It felt like I was fighting some animation with random shiny lights thrown in, lulling me into a pattern of "see shiny lights, press button, traverse between platforms praying my character remembers to grab the zipline or start a wall-run, lest I be forced to restart everything again." Just wasn't fun.And before the inevitable "git gud" when complaining about a character's implementation: From the comments, most people take over an hour to beat her, even if they had no trouble playing prior. For me, personally, I have no interest in spending an hour or two of punishing, repetative "gameplay". This could be addressed by adding checkpoints after each stage of the bossfight (like was done for the 1st boss), as this minimizes the time lost from bugs/bad luck/glitchy animations. Until then, I'm out.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostrunner is a hardcore FPP slasher packed with lightning-fast action, set in a grim, cyberpunk megastructure. Climb Dharma Tower, humanity’s last shelter, after a world-ending cataclysm. Make your way up from the bottom to the top, confront the tyrannical Keymaster, and take your revenge. The streets of this tower city are full of violence. Mara the Keymaster rules with an iron fist and little regard for human life. As resources diminish, the strong prey on the weak and chaos threatens to consume what little order remains. The decisive last stand is coming. A final attempt to set things right before mankind goes over the edge of extinction. As the most advanced blade fighter ever created, you’re always outnumbered but never outclassed. Slice your enemies with a monomolecular katana, dodge bullets with your superhuman reflexes, and employ a variety of specialized techniques to prevail. One-hit one-kill mechanics make combat fast and intense. Use your superior mobility (and frequent checkpoints!) to engage in a never-ending dance with death fearlessly. Ghostrunner offers a unique single-player experience: fast-paced, violent combat, and an original setting that blends science fiction with post-apocalyptic themes. It tells the story of a world that has already ended and its inhabitants who fight to survive.

name: The Persistence
detailed_description: The Persistence challenges you, a clone of security officer Zimri Eder, to survive aboard a doomed deep space colony starship, overrun with horrific and murderous aberrations. You are the last survivor. Your mission? Restore functionality to the ship and somehow make your way back to Earth. The Persistence Enhanced brings improved lighting, particle effects and further UX & UI refinements along with DXR RayTracing implementation for supported graphics cards & NVIDIA® DLSS. For VR owners please take note Motion controls are not supported. Navigate an ever-changing labyrinth A malfunction in the ship’s macrostructure means the layout of the decks will shift and change configuration periodically. Each and every expedition into The Persistence will be disorienting and different. Use darkness and cover Avoid being overwhelmed by the ship’s deadly new inhabitants. Move stealthily, strike from the shadows and deflect any onslaught of counter attacks with your personal shield. Explore, unlock and upgrade Harvest DNA material to improve health, toughness and defensive capabilities and loot materials & schematics for weapon upgrades and suit customizations with perks. Death is just the beginning If Zimri dies, her consciousness is uploaded into a new cloned body, ready to try again with any upgraded stats, suits & weapon schematics kept for the next attempt. Asymmetric Multiplayer Connect a phone or tablet running IOS or Android to the game for up to 2 players to take control of ‘Solex’ – the ship’s engineering system. Once connected, they will be able to take control of the ship’s systems in realtime, including abilities to lure creatures, open doors and disable any of the ship’s internal security defenses. IOS or Android compatible device and 'The Persistence' application required for Asymmetric Multiplayer to work. Data charges may apply. VR Headset support Compatible with Oculus Rift, HTC Vive, Valve Index and WMR headsets. Features tailored control settings and comfort options for VR and non-VR play. Motion controls are not supported.

_childDocuments_.review: Review based on VR version - using original HTC Vive.Having played The Persistence quite a bit on PSVR a year or two back, it was an instant purchase for me on Steam, in the hope of getting a perfect version of the game at last.  As with most PSVR titles, while still a top notch game and visually impressive - the graphics could feel a little blurry on the PS4 and wasn't quite reaching its potential.  I haven't had a chance to play much tonight but I've played the original enough to confidently review this already and can already see some of its shortcomings.The Good:  The Persistence is a fantastic stealth horror action game with some light rogue-like elements in regards to character upgrades over multiple plays/deaths - and some randomisation to the specific decks/levels you visit.  While there are lots of comparisons to be made to System Shock, Alien Isolation and Dead Space, its definitely its own unique title.  While definitely firmly in the stealth horror camp, it feels more arcadey (in a good way) than other titles in that genre, so I find it quite a fun "one more go" kinda gameplay - rather than outright terrifying :D  The combat can feel simplistic (and at times totally OP if you're having a great run and stocked up on items/weapons along the way) - but it can also be incredibly punishing, especially in the early game when you're learning the ropes and more prone to panicking when a creature jumps out at ya!  Oh and draining the enemy of their precious genetic code is always totally satisfying ^^The Meh:  Unfortunately at this time (launch day on Steam) the game doesn't seem to have altered much from the original PSVR release.  It should only be played seated, and ideally with a joypad, i'm using an old x360 controller without issues there.  The majority of actions in-game such as interacting with buttons and picking up items are done by staring at the item in question (Gaze interactions) - as such there is permanently an icon in the dead centre of your vision so the game knows what you are looking directly at.   Motion controls unfortunately are not supported (even using the joypad style controls on them) and neither is room scale movement - making it one of the more inanimate VR titles to release in 2020 :)  Now thats not necessarily a bad thing as sometimes you want a great VR game to play without needing the energy to run a metaphorical mile - but it does feel like the Devs have missed a trick by not updating the engine to support actual motion controls - picking up items by hand, using weapons directly etc.  The level of immersion would be increased dramatically and it would help declutter some of the UI in-game (for example item names could appear over the item in your hand rather than popping up whenever you look at it in the world).  Graphics options in-game are entirely missing - no way to increase textures, supersampling isn't making a noticeable difference and theres a heavy level of antialiasing which muddies the visuals giving it that PSVR look.Final Thoughts:  It might look like the cons outweigh the pros above - but bear in mind the majority of these are just additions to the existing game I would have hoped to see in the PC version.  The fact is that the base game, even if directly ported across from PSVR, is really tight and a whole lotta fun...I'm just glad its even got a PC release so that more people get a chance to try it for themselves :)  I can highly recommend it, just know what you're buying into controls-wise.  Hopefully the Devs can still make some significant updates that could improve some of the above issues.  While I really REALLY hope they can eventually bring out support for tracked motion controls, I wouldn't buy into this expecting that to happen - the entire game was constructed around seated joypad control and the Gaze based interactions so it would require significant reworking of the entire games systems to support that.  Hopefully graphics options are added to the game soon so we can boost the visuals, with that i'll be more than satisfied with the purchase :)

_childDocuments_.review: Be warned, several things in this port are just plain broken. Allow me to list the issues I had in the 30 minutes I tried to play.1. I played the game for the first time in VR. Couldn't select anything in the menus. Turns out, it doesn't support motion controls. Okay, fair enough. That's on me, I didn't read carefully enough. 2. I switched to keyboard and mouse with snap turning (a necessity for me, as smooth turning in VR gives me migraines). This is broken and apparently has been since release. Because the game doesn't have a turn button (it only recognizes moving the mouse side-to-side, which is disabled in snap turning), you're stuck always facing forward if you try to play snap turning with a mouse and keyboard. My choices were to switch to smooth turning (not happening) or try it with a gamepad.3. I went with the gamepad option. This worked and I could actually play the game finally. I ended up dying pretty quickly, however, because I don't typically play first-person games with a controller. Aiming shots was rough, especially with snap turning. Another thing broken.4. Now my only option to play the game was in non-VR mode with mouse and keyboard. Non-VR mode is a little weird but it works. I bought the game because it's VR, however, so it felt pretty disappointing to have to lose out on that. But I kept on going and got caught up to where I died while playing in VR mode and got through that with trusty mouse and keyboard controls.  I went into the next room from there and the game crashed, losing everything I had picked up that run.The game's discussion board is full of people complaining about problems since day one and the developer just asks people to submit feedback to their website. According to SteamDB, this game hasn't been updated since June 2020, a little over a month after the game's launch, but they're still selling this broken, crappy game to people. I bought it from a third party so I can't even get a refund. What a bunch of nonsense.EDIT - Oh, and I forgot to mention that the game not only doesn't support 21:9 monitors (the game's aspect ratio is off if you select it), you can't even use standard 1080p, because the game stretches itself to horizontally to fill the screen regardless of your resolution choice, so the top and bottom of the screen are cut off. The only solution I found was to set the game to 1080p and play in windowed mode. That was still covered up at the bottom by Windows' taskbar, but at least I could see what I was doing.EDIT 2 6/12/21 - In light of this game being re-released as an "Enhanced Edition", I wanted to update this review, but it turns out I don't need to. It has the exact same bugs as the non-enhanced edition. The only reason I know that it actually upgraded is because I now have a ray tracing option that I didn't have before. Everything else seems identical to the previous version, and it's still crashing on the first floor. Oh well.

_childDocuments_.review: REVIEW OF THE NONVR VERSIONGreat System Shock Clone!Although the controls take some getting used to, and there are some QoL things missing, the core gameplay loop of system shock is there. _childDocuments_.review: Review for the non-VR mode:The Persistence is a first person roguelike with some survival horror elements mixed in, originally the game was released as a PSVR title and the VR game design shows throughout the game - some of the things translate pretty well outside of VR but unfortunately some of the control/interaction mechanics feel a little out of place and more importantly the horror atmosphere doesn't adapt that well to non-VR mode.My run though the campaign took roughly 5.5 hours (with 21 deaths) and I got what seems to be the best ending, although the game has some replay value with different modes, unlocks/leveling and the campaign maps being generated from a tileset every time you die - I have absolutely no desire to play the game again.Campaign has the player tackle a few objectives that are split between 4 decks of the ship you're on board of, along with a small area for the grand finale. During the first portion of the game, my impressions were reasonably positive - despite some minor issues.However during the latter portions of deck 3, the repetitive nature of the game was starting to take its toll and during deck 4, it became obvious that rather than introducing new challenges - the last portion of the game was padded out to extend the campaign length in the worst possible way: Add lot, a whole lot more of the same enemies while being a lot more stingy with giving the players the opportunity to craft the actually functional weapons.Rather than being an enjoyable challenge, the 4th deck became an annoyance - one that ultimately started to highlight the flaws of the game. Minor things such as the lack of environment & visual variety (as you might expect from a starship), automatically switching to a weapon each time you pick one up and giving you the same introductory voice line about it (making you go back to menu to select your actual main weapon again), some enemies being able to spin 180 degrees in a split second when you teleport behind them, some of them lacking any sort of hit reaction when hit by some of the weaker weapons - became more and more annoying.Along with some more major issues like the clear lack of balance between weapons and equipment as some of them are far superior to others - and too bad if you upgraded ones that are next to useless in the "endgame", I guess you could grind out more resources to upgrade the worthwhile ones.Would I recommend the game? No, definitely not at a full price, there are much better roguelike games out there. For the fans of the genre, I'd recommend waiting for a sale or if the dev team patches out some of the issues and takes a look at the weapon/equipment balance in general.
_childDocuments_.name: The Persistence

_childDocuments_.review: The Persistence is easily one of the best horror roguelike experiences I've played to date and it gets huge bonus points for being completely playable in VR (without motion controls though sadly, but don't let that put you off trying this out!)Forced to die over and over again only to be reborn in a freshly cloned body each time you're tasked with completing a series of escalating tasks on board an ever changing space station filled with murderous zombie clones (the cloning machine was probably a bad idea). With each run you'll collect resources that can be used to grab permanent upgrades to your stats, unlockable blueprints for new items, upgrades to those items and a whole host of great beneficial things that will help you progress further each time you die & need to start all over again.Fans of roguelikes or just those looking for a solid scifi horror experience should definitely check this one out, it's an absolute blast in VR! - Enhanced Edition VR gameplay with ray tracing!
_childDocuments_.name: The Persistence

_childDocuments_.review: NOT A VR REVIEW---------------------------------------------------------------------------UPDATE: After spending more time in-game, there is a lots of qualities to that title.The rogue-like mechanism is really well implemented and allow you to progress further each run, the arsenal and upgrades are also very well thought out and fun to play with.One of the best point is that damn spaceship, which seems to have a will of his own when it comes to throw traps at you every time you relax!Finding other bodies to pick DNA from is rewarding exploration and an interesting way to expand the lore.Still get all the problems i talked about in the original review, but i give it a thumb up for the immersion, as the dev team seems to be responsive and willing to improve! ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- The game is ok and is clearly inspired by System Shock.BUTIt is a bad port from a VR title to non-VR.Everything is thought to be played in VR and is non intuitive if you dont.The worst part is that you cannot handle more than 2 items at once, and to switch to other items you constantly need to open your inventory. It would be nice to have the option to assign hotkey to items, to have a seperate hotkey for weapons and grenades,and to have the possibility to switch from all your weapons without having to select them every time from your inventory.An other problem for Ultra Wide screen users, the bottom of the interface is half-hidden (weapon, health-shiled-teleport bars), and there is no FOV option.TL;DR, the game is ok but the VR interface weight it down (change the interface for non-VR users please!)
_childDocuments_.name: The Persistence

_childDocuments_.review: The Enhanced version simply has the best lighting and shadows of any VR game, not even Alyx comes close.My Index hmd is at Valve due to RMA, so used my Rift CV1 ss 2.0. Then again, this is a very dark game, and it looks awesome using an oled hmd.Using Rift CV1 ss 2.0 (17 mill pixels per image) might be somewhat bold, and enabling all ray-tracing effects, ray-traced reflections and DLSS Quality, I no longer got 90 fps with the Asus Strix OC RTX 3090. But the ray-traced reflections did not look right, caused some strange shimmering, and image quality with deactivated ray-traced reflections looked much better, at least in VR with the CV1. Enabling all ray-traced effects and DLSS Quality I got close to solid 90 fps - only a few places couldn't keep up with the 90 fps. Maybe with the RTX 3090 DLSS Balanced with all ray-tracing effects enabled would be optimal (and ray-traced reflections disabled) - at least when using Rift CV1 ss 2.0. Gamepad is bad, but I forgot about it after a few minutes. I actually like picking items up by looking at the for about 2 or 3 seconds, very convenient. Aiming with the hmd works fine too. And the graphics are second to none. Using raytraced effects and DLSS the flashlight is simply mind-blowingly awesome!This is Cosmodread done right with about 50 times better graphics ;-)Not sure the VR version is for everyone though, had a bad scare last night, lol - this game is truly VR horror.Thus this game is the first VR game with full locomotion supporting both RTX raytracing and DLSS, and it has the best lighting of any VR game. That's truly an awesome experience, and having to use a gamepad certainly will not keep me from playing this game. And beneath the graphics, there's actually an awesome System Shock like game with many weapons and upgrades. I don't think cpu matters much for this game, but it'll chew up all the gpu power it can get, lol.Btw, the Steam version supports native Oculus drivers. One error though, the game no longer remembers the VR setting, it now constantly starts in 2D, at least when starting the Steam version from Oculus Home.Also having to finish one deck before saving is annoying.My rating: 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Huge fan of immersion sims, really want to like this game but unfortunatley it lacks even most basic VR controls!I'm NOT talking about motion support - thats understandable, hard to implement, no financial gain from doing so.But couple of relatively simple tweaks:1: Option to orient controller movement towards HMD. As in, when I turn around via HMD (playing standing VR) and then move the thumbstick on my controller up - I should move TOWARDS where I'M LOOKING, not my imaginary "FORWARD" position (major)2: Stick the UI to the HMD view as well (major)3: Some options to customize\fade UI (minor)4: Allow users to make 3D reticle invisible or have dedicated button to fade it in if some interactions require it (minor)5: Physical crouch.. In an intro cutscene I was able to crouch, but in-game it fades my view to black (minor)6: Language selection (minor)And voila, you have support for Standing VR! Until then - can't play it unfortunatley, the movement scheme is very confusing and I don't see a point in playing VR seated and staring in a single direction. Also, separate camera controls are quite nauseating for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Hi there. I can see some folks gettin' real fussy about this one. ESPECIALLY if they dare play it in non-VR, but I don't get the problem whatsoever. I spent about eight hours, on and off, just having a blast. If anything, this game makes me think the devs really loved System Shock. Which is a huge compliment, let me add, because System Shock was fantastic. There's a heap of really quality things about this game, down to the decks, the weapon variety and the fact it touches on some cool things you just don't see in games of this type. It's not often that I get a chance to play in space horror ever since we lost hope for Dead Space, so getting to play around as Zimri's clone and get spooked in the dark was pretty rad.You should definitely jump in on this one. If you're nostalgic for the space horror without the Dark Souls-esque Returnal on PS5 not being accessible, you should come play around here in The Persistence. Hell, if you enjoyed how constantly changing games like Hades are but want something more suited to your FPS (and VR) space horror mainstays -- this is what you should be playing. Every run is different and I really appreciate that.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE 17 DEC:Just completed the Main Campaign. I found the campaign to be well-balanced; it often took various attempts to get through each level, but the game fortunately saved major accomplishments as you went through the level, so you never had to replay too much of the current level.  Ultimately,there was a steady sense of progression as you played the game, with the only exception being the final part of the game where you had only a single life left (HINT: Use the Captain's DNA to double your health).Even though rogue-like games have a certain amount of repitition the longer you play them, this game did better than most where the randomly-generated levels left 'just different enough. Even the enemies seemed to be randomly generated  enough to where I never felt like I could predict exactly what i would be getting into.This game would benefit a great deal if motion controls schemes used in most modern FPS shooters were applied hereIt was a joy to play, and I'm currently trying to go through the Challenges.Although the game has GAME+ modes, and a Perma Death Mode, I can't say I would go through the campaign again if I had to start over from ground zero.================================================ A Wonderful Premise With Some Outdated Control Implementation (played on a Valve Index, i7-8700, 16GB RAM, GTX 1070Ti).This is a rogue-based space shooter that has influences in Dead Space, Dead Effect 2 VR, and Alien: Isolation. I could see this as being the outer space equivalent of 'In Death'. You have a decent level of narrative in the form of a story to give you a goal to strive, you have grinding/leveling up to build up stats/attributes to better your character (and the improvements stay with you even when you die), and the rogue-based level design that gives you different pathways to the next objectives.Where the game falters slightly is in the control implementation.  Not being a fan of keyboard/mouse for a VR game, all that was available was a gamepad.  The gamepad default controls work reasonably well for myself, but I have two issues: (1) Gamepad controls are not configurable (As far as I can tell), and (2) no VR controller implementation.  My beef with (2) is based on recently completing Alien: Isolation using the Index Controller, which helps immersion slightly, but more importantly, allows you to look one way where your smooth locomotion that you in another (trying this in The Persistence makes me feel like I'm going diagonal instead of straight).I don't know what the level of effort would be to convert to control like that for Lone Echo, or Dead Effect 2 VR,but it would be something to see.The concept of the game is straight-forward, and it's goals are clear.  The leveling up of your stats is helped by the different level structure each time you play, which keeps it relatively fresh.  The environment has a good sci-fi feel.  The gamepad controls are acceptable, but updating them to today's standard might increase commercial appeal (especially in the days of Oculus Quest 2).As long as there is a tangible sense of progression (in both skills and narrative), I see myself as continuing to play this game.  For an older game, this is a pleasureable find.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a cool sci-fi horror rogue-lite with some really elegant UI/UX design, sort of reminiscent of Dead Space, and a fun clone conceit to contextualise your infinite respawns. There's a lot of resource collection/management and lots of equipment and genetic upgrade trees to level up, and exploration involves quite a bit of sneaking and some slow-ish paced, deliberate combat - this definitely isn't a run 'n' gun action game, much more like an immersive sim. The visuals are nice and clean and the audio adds a lot of atmosphere (the voice actor for your companion/guide isn't annoying, which is a relief as she talks to you quite a bit with objectives, tips after deaths etc.).The original PSVR version is a few years old now and this shows a bit in the port, mainly with the lack of Oculus Touch (or equivalent) controller support - it's gamepad only in VR mode, which may be a turn-off for some. Aside from that though, the VR features are good, with lots of customisable comfort options and a slick 'look-at-to-interact-with' UI/UX system. This port adds a non-VR mode though, which I actually prefer: the UI system translates very smoothly to non-VR, and I find it a lot easier to play for longer stretches (I'm very prone to VR sickness even with comfort options, and VR headsets are heavy and sweaty).Overall, a solid game with some cool ideas and satisfying gameplay. Would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: It feels like an early access title.It's clear that the game was designed around VR, and made to work without it. Very little graphic options, doesn't look the best. I initially thought the game had defaulted to 1080 as it looked bad but nope, had defaulted to native res (1440).Combat is pretty meh, block with your shield then hit. Was very slow and clunky. _childDocuments_.review: What a great surprise is The Persistance VR !Is too early to give a definitive review but so far I want to give this game a big thumb up !I Recommend this for VR players.So far the game is an 8/10 for me.Here is a good gameplay video that shows different mechanics: And here is an updated video of the new ENHANCED version in VR and RT: The game has a main story where the player is embodied on clones that can evolve in stats, and the player can unlock blueprints of new weapons and features. With those premises the game generates a procedural level with the current objective of the campaign. The levels are BIG, full of surprises, resources, blueprints, weapons, or machines that allow to invest resources to pull specific weapons or tools that were previously discovered. The catch is that the roguelike factor plays with each life, recreating the level with a new life but retaining stats and blueprints unlocked, but you will need to get the guns and tools in the new generated level again.The gameplay itself in VR is handled by the gamepad but the view of the player in VR is blended with these controls, so you can aim with your view, pick things with your view, open doors, etc.The gameplay uses a First Person view and a similar slow pace like Alien Isolation, but here you have some weapons to have good shooting parts mixed with melee combat + shield that covers brief instants and you have to time correctly. The player as a result can use different tactics, starting from stealth ones that have additional rewards for silently taking enemies, or using guns (so far I unlocked 3 of them), grenades with different effects or some exotic ones, or evolve the melee approach. But there is more options that I do not want to reveal yet as I have still plenty more to unlock.There 2 things that I think the game could probably have in the future that will make this a much better game1) Full VR controls support instead of gamepad + VR View. The game was created with gamepad in mind, not sure if this was because it was also for PS4. Do not get me wrong, I got used to the controls just fine and enjoying the game seated a lot, but It is clear that if developers in the future add full VR Controls the game would be uber amazing jejejej2) There are no Video Options to configure at all. The game looks great, has great visuals, but I think I would always prefer to have a way to disable AA and adjust other options, once again this could be because it was in PS4 as well? not sure.I understand now why some Non-VR players are not enjoying this so much as I'm, because clearly the VR way to view naturally improves the gameplay a lot.Bonus: The game allows some assymetric couch multiplayer where the 2nd player can download a mobile phone client called Solex App to assist the player that is playing, I will update this soon with more detais.

_childDocuments_.review: This one is strange. TBH its a good game somewhere underneath, but some design decisions are dragging it down. I just checked it cos there were some similiarities to System Shock/Bioshock.Cons: - No proper inventory system. Sorry, but looting and hunting only for (boring) resources is getting old after 30 min of gameplay.- Melee weapons that have couple "uses" and are useless after and need "reload". srsly ?- Too scripted , and way too many jump scares/enemies. Jump scares work when there are scarce...if you get enemy in every corner , and pipes explode 90% of time, and also you get same spooky sound ambient every 10 sec - You go doom mode and ignore those. - Too dark, Systemshock didnt have a flashlight and they managed to keep it tense. - Enemies are not affected (from what Ive tested) by light/dark in any way. So If your in dark corner without a flashlight, its the same as if your using flashlight and in full light. - You can get like 10 + weapons after 10 min of gameplay... each with 2-3 bullets. I understand that it forces stealth gameplay, but thats not how it works. You go Amnesia stealth or Deus Ex, not both in same time.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was designed to be played in VR, and it shows.The regular configuration works rather fine, but has been implemented quickly, more like a feature than anything else.That being said, I didn't play the title in VR, but I believe it's quite good for the support.About the regular controls version, well, it's average, on the positive side though. The biggest problem is that it lacks a good polish.The game has a nice atmosphere, very similar to Doom 3. It's not an action game though, you got a nice arsenal and different boosts to help you on your journey, but you can't go all guns blazing. If you're not careful enough, you'll get rekt quite fast.The rogue-lite elements works well and are nicely justified by the scenario, which is simple, but functional.Visually, it's so-so. Without RTX, most shadows will look UGLY, lightings are okay and textures are simple.Playing with RTX, it can look quite good, and I'd say it adds a lot to the atmosphere, the shadows are really good looking with the option on, but I believe the game is poorly optimised for RTX, I have a fairly decent rig and the performances take a huge hit with it - more than usual, at least.Any decent player will take between 8 to 12 hours to complete the main campaign, which is short, but intense and difficult near the end.If space-horror is your thing, and you can look beyond its flaws, The Persistence is a fine experience, I don't think I'll revisit this one in the future, but it was pleasant for the price I paid.Wait for a good sale though: the base price is quite steep for the impression the game left me.Fine, but far from a classic.

_childDocuments_.review: (game was played on PS4 more for purpose of the review)The Persistence is a very interesting mixture of Virtual Reality and Survival Horror. The game was originally released for the PS4 but has now arrived on PC and can be played in both a V.R. and Non-V.R. environment which makes it an ideal game for those looking for V.R. style gameplay without the hardware.The game is set about The Persistence which has experienced some very unfortunate incidents in deep space. You play a cloned version of someone who was killed prior to the events of the game and with the help of the ship’s A.I. you are able to be respawned and are guided throughout the ship to collect objects and complete tasks.There are several dangers facing players from ship systems and deadly beings who have been spawned from the former crew. Faced with a shield to block attacks and counter-attack players must be able to defend themselves as they look for the optimum angle to deliver impactful hits on their enemies. As they explore they will gather weapons, health, resources and items which they can use at various terminals to update their abilities and to better enhance their chances for survival.Since the game was designed for a V.R. setting; players will have to get used to a control system that is different than one who has not played many V.R. games would be accustomed to.If you can endure the early challenges with combat, navigation, and such; the game offers some good tension and an enjoyable experience.The graphics will seem a bit dated in parts but remember this is a product of the V.R. as you will not get games to have state of the art graphics in this environment.What the game does offer is some tense gameplay and plenty of action in setting that should keep fans of the genre happy if they are willing to temper their expectations.3.5 stars out of 5
_childDocuments_.name: The Persistence

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game and was surprised it got a mixed review. FWIW I played the Enhanced non-vr version.I thought it was a good story, with a great concept. It reminded me of Returnal (for obvious reasons really) however I never really enjoyed that game. It was too sprawling and disjointed (imho). I enjoyed this game because it was confined to a single ship (albeit with an always changing layout) and introduced various enemies on each floor. I can appreciate a lot of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that some of the mixed reviews mention regarding QoL, however I found if I took my time I could usually get past the level if I .One thing I do agree with is that it is possible to purchase an upgrade which quickly becomes under powered and there is no way of recouping those funds. I think a better approach would be to have the ability to dismantle them and receive a percentage of the fab tokens to re-invest elsewhere.I will admit I did get stuck in one place and in the end I took the option to use the assist mode which I thought was excellently incorporated, allowing you to set the amount of assistance at an extremely granular level. It does prevent achievements, but that didn't bother me. One thing that does make life easier is searching the map for specific rooms as these hold artefacts that can make subsequent runs quicker.Without going into too much detail, I really liked the acquisition of additional DNA and the traits they provided.So overall I really enjoyed it and would look out for other games made by the same devs.

_childDocuments_.review: At launch there are a couple bugs (occasionally when I boot the game the framerate is like half of what it should be, others it's fine, and the window can become deselected randomly and I have to click it in the task bar), but I'll happily put up with them for what's basically the greatest playstation VR exclusive.  The graphics are pretty good, but the atmosphere, enemies, environments, combat, stealth, and sound design are all perfect. It has this sort of bioshock/dead-space feel and I really wish we had more games like this in VR. I do hope for hand-tracking eventually, but with the intentionally slow melee combat I'm not sure how they'd handle that.

The game tells the story of Arietta and her family, visiting their Grandmother's cabin for the first time after her passing away a year prior. However, the family trip takes an unexpected turn when Arietta meets a mysterious new friend and gains the ability to see strange spirits that inhabit the island. _childDocuments_.review: Talk about a blast from the past. Arietta is an incredibly nostalgic, charming action adventure, but with a twist. When I got this title in my hands it felt like old memories from the days of isometric zelda on the SNES with a new age touch. Everything from the sound effects, music, visuals and feel of the game were all so perfectly done to really reference back to pay tribute to those old titles without losing it's own identity. All of the elements you'd expect to find in a top notch love piece are here.Aside from all of the gameplay elements being spot on, the story here is very touching. Your character's name is Arietta, who finds herself going back to a familiar place where she had spent much time through her life as she was growing up. Once there, the story really grabs a hold of your emotions and gives the character's adventure a real sense of purpose. Although you are given a good amount of information in the beginning, it is not obnoxious and drawn out. It is perfect for what the story needs and the story is trickled to you in a perfect flow as you play.The secondary shining star is as stated a little earlier, the gameplay. More specifically, the combat mechanics, which are perfect. As you find yourself engaged in battle, you will see a great assortment of enemies and bosses, all of which you really do get a good sense of personality from the enemies. They are not all just bland copy cats that sloth along doing the same thing as one another with slight variations. Each enemy has their own way to be handled, which I really found enjoyable.Arietta of Spirits is a must buy title for those of us who enjoy some fun gameplay and story. When you play this game, you will thank yourself time and time again as you lose track of the time being sucked into this great adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: Arietta of Spirits

_childDocuments_.review: Arietta of Spirits is a charmingly beautiful, pixel art narrative adventure. It combines its simple game mechanics with a vibrant, retro world that helps in delivering a truly poignant experience. It is an experience I highly recommend to Indie enthusiasts who enjoy light combat amongst a well-told story that does not overstay its welcome.Playing as a young little girl named Arietta, the game begins on the annual family road trip to a cabin on a small island. The cabin belonged to Arietta's grandmother, but this is the first year she will not be joining them due to her sudden passing a year prior. Arietta's parents are determined to still keep up family traditions, believing  grandma would have wanted this as well, but understandably, the cabin is filled with past memories and evokes feelings of sadness within the household.Despite the wave of gloom clouding the air in the cabin, Arietta meets a peculiar entity named Arco that grants her the ability to see and interact with spirits on the island. From here, she begins her journey of discovery, helping many others along the way.Arietta of Spirits is a narrative driven action-adventure game with a simple, yet heart-warming story. Lasting around 4-5 hours, it is not a lengthy game and is not designed to be one. I found the few characters to be well constructed with their own individual personalities, bringing a lot of life into the game. The story is charming, and the game does not overstay its welcome. The store page very clearly states the estimated gameplay time of ~5 hours and thus expectations should be firmly in place, prior to playing or purchasing the title. I did not find that the game ended abruptly, like I have been told by others. Instead, I believe it leads up to the ending well, with no filler or unnecessary fetch quest gameplay and is clear when the story is reaching its conclusion.Playing as Arietta, players explore the small island with our trusty sword, fighting any enemies in our path, from wasps to Roamers (angry spirits). There are simple dodge/roll mechanics, attack and later on, a shield. There is no intense level up system or anything of the sort, but after defeating enough Roamers, more lives can be unlocked. There are a handful of enemies which do slightly different ranged attacks, but none pose too much of a concern and can all be defeated easily with the sword or using the shield to deflect damage. There are also a few side quests around the island such as finding 20 hidden critters throughout the different areas, locating items for a merchant and more. Generally, the game is very linear and pushes players onto the correct paths for the main plot, but there is still room to explore if players wish. Centred around the cabin, there are a few different paths to explore the island from, with extra "hidden" caves to discover. There is no ingame map and admittedly, I was a bit confused where to go at one stage, when I was taken back to the cabin, having to go back to where I was before in the new day. A  simple map would have been appreciated, just so I know I am not running in the wrong direction. However, the island really is quite tiny and even for those people who lack navigation skills like myself, forgetting which direction I had just come from, it is still fairly easy to get by without a map.Whilst the title does integrate combat throughout, the game is pretty easy. It is not hardcore or unforgiving, but story-based and relaxing, which understandably may not appeal to everyone. The autosave system saves at every new screen with an abundance of extra lives to be found when smashing through barrels or bushes. The difficulty is fairly consistent throughout the game, until the final boss, which was quite the change of pace, in comparison to the rest of the game. Although, it is not "challenging" by any means, but with limited health drops and longer attack scenes, it was a welcome change up. After finishing the game, an extreme mode does unlock which may appeal to those looking for a greater challenge. Regardless, I enjoyed the simplicity of the games mechanics and was immersed into the narrative from start to finish.The game is stunning. With its retro-pixel art, it felt like I was back playing Pokémon on my Gameboy Advance. The forests were especially nostalgic to me, but there are a number of different environments to explore. The majority is played in the luscious green forests, but there are also dark mines to uncover and a slight change of scenery with the beautiful forest in autumn, showcasing the gorgeous yellow flora. Sound is equally as impressive with an elegant and captivating original soundtrack (also available for purchase as DLC). Once again, the retro inspiration is in full swing in the sound department as well, with those characteristic high beep sounds when giving/picking up items, dramatic upbeat music in boss battles and more. I found myself stopping many times just to appreciate the wonderful audio which is integrated so seamlessly, with no abrupt stopping or starting.Arietta of Spirits was an absolute treat to play. Featuring a heart-warming story, easy game mechanics and a gorgeous pixel world to explore, it made for an enjoyable, relaxing experience. Despite being relatively short, taking approximately 5 hours to complete, the game is extremely well polished, and I recommend to all Indie lovers looking for simple gameplay with a decent story.This review copy was provided to the Devils in the Detail curator.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like eating bread? Just bread without anything on it. Bread sure is good as a basis but if it's the entire game then somethings gone wrong. I wont complain about the game length. There are many games I would call my favorite games that are even shorter. But those game actually offer an experience worth your time rather than nothing. In fact through out the game I was thinking: when does this game finally end? Which is not a thought I should be having in a 4 hour game. Pixelart is nice and the thing that probably sells you on the game. Since you look at screenshot of the game and go: "Yeah, this looks nice. I have played zelda likes before, this wont be much different." Except this zelda like is only combat. No puzzles, no items, no upgrades. Just swing your sword and dodge. And one hour in you already saw every enemy in the game including bosses since all bosses are the same: they are just constantly invunerable until they let you attack once and repeat. Normally you don't play zelda likes for the combat since that's the lackluster part. But it is literally all that's here. The "emotional" story is actually just exposition the game. "The bound, Roamers, Conduit..." If you cut out all the meaningless technobabble you have one scene where you say goodbye to grandma and 2 funny jokes with your parents. That's the story. Also if someone comes in the middle of the night and tells me I am his bound then that conjures completely different pictures in my mind. If you want to play an actually good zelda clone, play Ocean's heart. Or the sleeping king. Both cost as much as this game but have twice the length and ten times the content.

_childDocuments_.review: is short retro-style action-adventure with an emphasis on storytelling. The story and the pixel art really stand out for this little gem. Overall it is a casual game with predictable enemies and patterned bosses that take around 3.5-4 hours to complete. After a single completion, a new Extreme mode becomes available that will provide a significantly more difficult challenge.The game looks like, and plays like a Zelda-inspired action adventure, but the combat is made a bit more simple and straight forward, without so much progression, items, or strategies. In a way, I can see people lamenting how the game is not complex enough, does not have enough additional content, etc. I found the game to have enough variation of enemies and the bosses were interesting enough to keep me engaged. The NPCs were designed well and each had their own personalities, even though they were few in number. In addition, we have to keep in mind that the development team from Third Spirit Games is a core group of 3 people, one person on the pixel art, one person on the programming, and one person on everything else.Even though the game is short, it is very well designed. There is linear progression through the game, with most rooms only having one entry and one exit, but that is to keep the player on task and keep moving forward. There is no grinding, no leveling up, etc. You just play along and do the main and side quests in order to power up on your way to seeing how the story plays out. The game is open to re-exploration just before the final sequence, and if you accidentally step through and finish the game, you will be able to restart your save file from the beginning of that final act/day, which is really convenient for people looking for the completionist run.As mentioned above, the game unlocks an Extreme mode that lets the more serious gamer go after the final challenge, which is dealing with one-hit deaths, as you can see here:This is a really nice balance for everyone who wants to play the game. And the most casual of gamers should be able to finish the game and get 29/30 achievements on Easy or Normal modes, but that final one is going to take some dedicated time and effort. Both controller and KB work well, I typically favor the controller in these styles of games, and so that is what I used. The default settings worked without any trouble. You only use the joystick/D-pad and the face buttons, so it's not impossible for every very casual gamers. The pixel art and details in this game are very well done. Every artistic flourish seem to fit in well with the overall game. Quite charming, especially the NPCs, their homes, their expressions and animations, etc.I found the music to fit in with the theme quite well. There are some sombre moments, there are other joyful and still emotional times, there are times of calm exploration, and there are cacophonous jolts of conflict.This game has something to offer to almost all players, especially if they enjoy a good story or a retro-style adventure. The only people I would tell to stay away are those who want only a hardcore experience and those who do not like pixel art.Even though the base price set at $14.99 US seems a bit high for a game that does not last so long, I can confidently say that it is worthwhile for you to check out, especially if you have read this far. There is a demo to try out, so you could see for yourself what it's like. If you  want to wait for a sale, it's definitely reasonable as well. But don't let this game fall off your radar!You can look at this video for the content from the very beginning if you are interested, or you can check it out for yourself. is indeed an IndieGem and I hope you all will eventually try out the game, be it now or later when the price is right for you. It's a casual adventure for a raining weekend, and it leaves a lasting impression.Score: 8/10, for leaving the player to wish for more.Thank you for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: 10h+ 9/10 2 I wrote  0 on Steam Hunters No Yes, it has a few missable achievements, but the game is short, so the missable achievements are easy to unlock Yes Yes Yes Yes No Yes, you have to complete a second playthrough on extra hard (aka zero hits mode) NoThis review is very hard to write... because for me the game has 2 sides.. on one side a good game and on the other side a lot of flaws that shine through because of one specific achievement. I'll explain first my experience after just playing through the game for the first time and not worrying about that last achievement. In the end, I'll explain how my opinion of the game changes when I take that one achievement into consideration. I enjoyed this game a lot on my first playthrough. The controls feel a bit sluggish but overall the game is great. A lovely story, which leaves the door open for a sequel. Enjoyable characters with a lot of charm and fun gameplay. the game saves every new screen you enter, so taking a break from this game is easy. This run was a lot of fun and if the game had only those 19 achievements I would only feel a lot of enjoyment for this game...So what ruined the experience is that it makes it so hard to review this game...? The achievement for completing the game on extra hard, this mode unlocks after completing the game for the first time. In this mode, you can not get hit. If you get hit you gladly go back to the last checkpoint but even with those frequent checkpoints it can't hide the flaws this game has and which can get you in a lot of trouble during this mode. The flaws became more clear and clear while I was trying to go for this last achievement (still trying but stuck on the last boss for now) and explains the "sluggish" feeling I already had during my first playthrough, but because you have more health it isn't such a big problem:1. You can only do one move at a time, can't interrupt and it has a very short window after the animation stops but not a new animation starts.2. At a lot of spots the wall is a bit more on the inner layer of the floor than you would think, which can make dodging an enemy attack a problem. I have hit many inviable walls, which I would expect would be a few mm more at the outer layer of the floor. 3. Enemies see you earlier than you see them, so they prepare already their first move while they aren't visible on your screen. And sometimes they even anticipate where your next move will end and attack there while you're doing that movement. I normally already dislike such hardcore achievements, those are not my style, but because I liked the game so much on my first playthrough I wanted to try and go for completion... even already realizing during my first playthrough that it would be a challenge. I'm not sure I should have tried because now I feel a love/hate relationship with this game and it might have been better if I just had quit after getting the first 19 achievements. See this review as positive when you don't worry about achievements at all or are not bothered by completing them all. If you're an achievement hunter... I would give this game a mixed review, but steam doesn't even give me that option. EDIT: finally got the last achievement. The second playthrough took me around 10h of which 8h on that last boss, what a hell was that, but I managed to defeat him in the end :D

_childDocuments_.review: i feel bad leaving negative reviews for small indie games... it's not like this game is -bad-, but in the very literal sense, i certainly would not recommend it.it really has remarkably few flaws. it's a smooth, basic aRPG combat system under a lot of very cute pixel art, female protag is always a bonus, didn't really encounter any notable bugs when playing... like it's well-made on all the technical senses, right?and yet.despite all of that, there's nothing terribly interesting about it either. the combat is a wonderful foundation to build on, but there is no building on it. there is only (effectively) mandatory progression and one ability to get besides the basic attack/dodge roll. there could be a lot of room even in this short game for optional bonuses or unlockable attacks from completing collectible missions, but none of that exists. it is what it more or less from beginning to end, and so it feels flat and shallow.if it had an engaging story, i would also still recommend it. but it doesn't. it -does- have a story, but even after finishing the game, i couldn't tell you any personality traits or flaws of the protagonist except that she lied to her parent's faces one time towards the end of the game. i think there was a lot of room to make this into a narrative about the risks of prioritizing fancies of adventure and productivity over sharing tender moments with people close to us. i think that could have been easy to spin in. the protag already ignores a phone call from dad in favor of fighting a boss but it just comes off as for laughs. i don't know; missed potential.as it is, it is not particular deliberate about hooking the player in, begging questions, or giving us reasons to feel strongly about any characters. i think the most emotionally invested in this game was with the character who's personality is he yells at you a lot. because i wanted to help him and see if he'd stop yelling. and he kind of did. but not really. not in a way that was shown to be meaningful-- only told to be. if it had either a more charming / emotional story, or more options to innovate and expand on the gameplay, i would happily recommend this. unfortunately, as it is, the game is just kind of flat. pretty, but flat.

_childDocuments_.review: Arietta of Spirits is a cute-looking action-adventure game. I thought that it is going to be a rather calm, but relaxing experience. I have been very wrong. It took me several months to finish this game. I was not able to play it for a long time during one session. I needed monthly breaks from the game, because it was that boring and that bad.Let's start with big empty map where everything looks the same and where one is forced to fight monsters every 5 steps. The map is full of annoying monsters with even more annoying mechanics. Every time one enters or re-enters previously cleared locations, the monsters will be back. One will enter and re-enter locations plenty of times throughout the game and will have to deal with those annoying monsters every time. Not to mention that the player will often get lost on this big empty map, because it is so unintuitive.The characters in this game are awful. The adults here are like children and behave no better, One gets the impression that these characters are just brainless. The main character Arietta, who is obviously a child, is much more mature and smarter than the adults. It is as if the children wrote this game. What I found frustrating is inability to skip cutscenes. In this game you waste a lot of time waiting for... nothing. These cutscenes get incredibly long and often nothing is happening during them. You can somewhat skip dialogues, but if there is any movement or whatever, you have to wait for them to finish it before you can procceed. That's a total waste of time. Undoubtebly, the worst aspect of this game is the combat itself. To put it mildly, it is really bad and does not work as it is supposed to work. You can swing your sword and hit a monster staying 5 metres away and you can swing a sword standing literally next to a monster and miss. The swing itself will cause the character to make a step forward and if the swing is missed then the character will likely die when they touch the monster by moving into it. Missles and trails left by the monsters last very short period of time, then they dissapear. Well, not always. Sometimes they dissapear but the hitbox of the missle or a trail remains in that area which can cause (and caused in my case) a ton of unnecessary deaths. The monsters shots go straight for the player. It doesn't matter if the player is moving, the missle will go where the player will be, not where it was shot. It is as if they had some sort of aimbot. This makes dodging feel useless and one will often be forced to use a magic shield to block such missle. The shield itself doesn't work as it should either as I have had experienced a lot of deaths by being hit while protected by the shield which shouldn't be the case if mechanics of the game worked properly. The majority of the situations and my negative experiences come from my second playthrough on Hardcore Mode for the last achievement. Normal mode was very forgiving and I went through it very quickly. I didn't pay as much attention to combat then and all those not working mechanics and bugs did not bother me. Everything changed with Hardcore mode due to one life. I have had at least a hundred unnecessary deaths caused by the things I listed above. Another hundred came from the final boss fight with Sunken Behemoth. One could think you can learn the mechanics and basically perfect the boss fight, but that couldn't be further from the truth. It is a total lottery. Throughout the whole fight missles will drop from the sky. They can't be predicted and they are rather hard to spot and difficult to avoid. When one swings the sword, the character cannot do anything for half a second. They cannot move and they cannot activate the shield. All it takes to fail another attempt is to swing a sword and have RNG shot a missle where one is currently standing. If the character is frozen in that moment, they will have no time to get away from the missle or react in any way. They're just waiting for their death. In my opinion, the game from graphical side is great, but I feel like it is the only positive thing about it. The game is actually pretty expensive for around 5 hours of gameplay. It ain't worth the price. Perfecting the game achievement-wise will force you to replay it and basically experience all the bad I experienced. The combat completely ruined the game for me and at times made me really frustrated. This is not the experience I was looking for and I regret playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this game enough to re-buy it on Steam for Steam Deck portability after having already bought and finished it on the Xbox when it first released last year. It's kind of superficially similar to one of the isometric Zeldas like Link to the Past but pared down and more combat-oriented, without much in the way of puzzles etc. Combat is simple--you have a sword attack, a defensive force field, and a dodge roll and that's it--but it makes up for it with a nice bit of challenge; it's not super hard but the sword attack has a slight delay between swings that can leave you vulnerable if you miss the enemy, the force field can only stay up for a couple seconds at most, and the dodge rolls don't have i-frames, all of this adding up to mean that you really have to be aware of all of your surrounds and pay careful attention to your timing and positioning which keeps things interesting. On top of this it also has a pleasant soundtrack, a nice art style reminiscent of Stardew Valley, and just a lot of charm and heart in general. It's also only 4 or 5 hours long (my playtime says 8 hours at the time I'm writing this but I'm really bad about setting my Steam Deck down while it's still running and wandering off and forgetting about it so 3 or 4 of those hours are AFK) so I see myself replaying it a lot over the years as a bit of a "comfort food" game. I'd really recommend it to anyone who likes these sort of indie games.
