_childDocuments_.review: A charming little game that is again on the shorter side, but that's fine because it's one of the most quality four hours of gameplay (insert the obligatory Angry Joe meme here) you'll ever get to experience.The story is engaging and heartfelt, and in my opinion parallels a lot of the current (and let's face it, as old as humanity itself) world issues, serving as a great cautionary tale. Gotta get that quota of politics in video games up high, boys. In this case it's even funnier because it's gonna fly over the heads of your average gamers™, just like any metaphor would.The graphics is sublime, definitely one of the best looking indie games out there. There's crazy attention to detail in every little corner of the island you get to explore.The gameplay is light on game mechanics and that's fine for such a focused experience. If you played the old Zelda titles you'll be immediately at home here. The game doesn't really have puzzles though unlike the latter, and that's fine too. One notable thing is that getting health back is quite easy as it seems like less health you have increases the chances of you getting a heart. Therefore I suggest starting on the hardest available difficulty, as the game is somewhat on the easier side, so that way you'll get enough challenge on your first playthrough.Arietta of Spirits is certainly an indie gem that you shouldn't miss, especially when on sale.

On the other hand, despite its short length it gets slightly repetitive; it has a lack enemy and quest variety; and it has character dialog that constantly interrupts the action with inane banter.Overall the game is on the "short-but-sweet" side of things, but it's missing that extra something-something to make it truly special.

_childDocuments_.review: There’s plenty of 16-bit Zelda clones on the market, but few are as charming and heart-warming as Arietta of Spirits. Things start off on a rather sombre note. Your Grandma has recently passed away, and so the family take a nostalgic trip to her home to get affairs in order. As Arietta, or Arrie, you quickly discover a hidden spirit realm that allows you to walk between the living and the dead. You befriend a strange ghostlike creature called Arco and, equipped with a wooden sword, set out on a quest to slay the monsters of the land. To say any more would spoil what is a very story driven game. The game captures the glorious 16-bit era perfectly. The colourful, chunky pixel art, text boxes, and top-down level design are very reminiscent of Zelda’s Link to the Past and other games in the series that released on the Game Boy and DS. Combat is typical of the genre; you have a slash attack and dodge roll, and later get other moves such as a spirit shield that allows you to block enemy projectiles. There’s a few fetch quests and collectables to be found, but progress is mostly linear. Without an overworld map, your start menu checklist gives you clear instructions of where to go next. Arrie’s world is not all that big, so you won’t find yourself getting lost or overwhelmed. There are various difficulties to choose from, with an ‘Extreme’ mode available after completing the game. If you’re a veteran to these types of games, I’d recommend starting on ‘Hard’, as I found ‘Normal’ quite easy, and only died a couple of times in my first playthrough. It’s also quite a short game, clocking in at around 4-5 hours. Arietta of Spirits is a beautiful game, with some adorable character animations. Gameplay is enjoyable, but definitely takes a back seat to the emotional story.  If you’re looking for a Zelda-lite, with emphasis on the ‘lite’, I’d strongly recommend picking this one up now on PC, Switch, PS4 or Xbox One. And if you love achievements, there’s a comical one here involving your dad in the outhouse and some toilet roll!

_childDocuments_.review: Arietta of Spirits is a top-down action-adventure game about a girl and her spirit otter communing with ghosts.  Beat it using a game controller in 3.7 hours on Normal difficulty.  This game has multiple difficulty choices.Gameplay: You slash a sword and dodge your way past angry blobs and angrier bees through a handful of areas on an island.  There's no jumping or running.  Sometimes the way is blocked and you need to find an alternative route!  I had a little trouble judging the slash range with some enemies, but it didn't really get in the way of playingGraphics: Charming and smooth.  The graphics are polished.Story: It's there.  There's an island.  There are badguys.  Every character definitely has a personality.  The characters are chatty and I found a lot of dialogue revolved around abilities.  The ghosts make up for it.  Feel the story and gameplay balance each other out pretty well.  Some parts have feels.  The story's about as warm as a camping trip with family and eating apple pie.Music: It's also there.  Nothing really stuck with me.  Has a piano, violin, rpg, lowkey vibe.Collectibles: Arietta has four types of collectibles to flesh out the game.  Two involve finding things, one involves powering up stuff, and the last involves achievements.  It becomes clear near the end that the game is almost over, and there's room to roam around taking care of the first three collectibles.  Getting all the achievements requires playing more than once.  Difficulty: Easy, Medium, and Hard.  Once you beat it you unlock Extreme.  The difficulty curve is fair and gets a little bulley-helly at the very end but is doable.  Saving: The game auto-saves when you enter different areas.  ** Epilepsy Warning ** : You're warned at the very beginning that it's flashy.  Impressions:  It's a nice little jaunt, and a nice little game.  You can beat Arietta of Spirits in roughly 4 hours.  You can play and win it without much trouble, though Achievements require multiple playthroughs.  Nothing broke or crashed during gameplay, and the enemies were fair.  Wish there was more, like more ghosts to help, spirit helpers, or places to go, but there's nothing wrong with what's on the plate.   That said, nothing really spoke to me in any deep way, either.  This feels like the sort of game you'd enjoy the crap out of on a car ride.  It's there, within reach, quick, and leaves a sense of fulfillment when you beat it.Noticed other reviewers complained that Arietta of Spirits isn't as cool as Zelda.  And yes, this clearly isn't some big-name AAA title like Zelda.  It's extremely unfair to compare it to that.   It's a mid-brow action-adventure game.  Noticed other reviews complain that the dialogue goes on forever, and nothing stuck out to me in regards to that.  I will say that due to the length you should get this one on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a tragedy that I found this game through Humble Bundle. Indie games like this deserve a bit more spotlight.The Good:The game has a very light story. I found myself enjoying the interaction between characters. The dialogue was written well and allowed for a bit of development for the protagonist. Every step of the way, the game continues to build on the story of what happened on the island years ago. The combat is fluid and didn't have very many moments that left me upset.The Bad:This may be an issue I have with judging distance, but I felt like I was hit by enemies due to my lack of being able to judge distance. This hasn't always been a problem for me, but I found myself avoiding combat once I had unlocked all of the hearts in the game. Combat felt pointless after that, outside of the required sections. The collectibles were a little annoying, but I didn't have to go back to the same area twice to get them all. Without a map, I felt a little lost in some areas.Overall:The game is short, sweet and to the point. It doesn't overstay its welcome, giving you enough of an experience to want more, but letting it have a moment of closure. I did find myself sad at the end that there wasn't more, but seeing that the game is $15, I understood. This game gives me a "labor of love" feeling and opens up the possibility for more, if the developer can see some success from the title.If you can look past the short playtime and absorb it as an indie experience, this would be a refreshing take on top-down pixel art action games.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun 2D action game with a great storyline.A lot of the negative reviews point to the play time (about 5 hours), but I really don't think that's a problem. The game respects your time and none of that 5 hours you're playing feels like filler. You may have to back-track if you want to do the two optional side-quests, but doing the main story will feed you new content before you have a chance to get bored with what you're doing.The combat in this game is pretty simple at it's core, you can dodge, perform a melee attack, and later in the game you can also block attacks. A lot of similar games try to flood their combat with heavy attacks, light attacks, ranged attacks, combos, and other features. I understand the charm to that approach, but personally it's not my cup of tea. I really appreciate Arietta of Spirits combat system, since the addition of too many features would make the combat stressful and unfun for me.That being said, the combat system isn't flat in the slightest. There are many many different types of enemies you'll come across on your adventure, and each of them will have you react in different ways to fight them. Some enemies charge at you, some shoot you, some act like mortars, some have shields, some shoot homing blasts, some act like obstacles, the enemy design is honestly really really good. Finding and fighting new enemies throughout my adventure was very exciting. There are 6 boss fights in the game, they all play well and have all have very unique sets of attacks that set them all apart.The story is very charming in a lot of ways, although at some points it does play with some rather dark themes. The characters are well designed and have a lot of charm to them. The pixel art is good, especially the larger sprites of the boss enemies.The last thing I'd note, is that this game really isn't an incredible challenge if that's what you're looking for. I wouldn't say it's incredibly easy, but I played through on hard mode and I only ever had trouble with the final boss fight. I died at most once or twice during the other boss fights, and rarely ever died to regular enemies. The game does offer an extreme difficulty after you beat it though, so you can play through that if you'd like (although I don't really know how hard it is since I haven't played it yet).

_childDocuments_.review: Writing this review a few minutes after finishing the game the first time.I had been following this game on twitter for quite a while (a month or two it feels like), and I was pretty excited for it. So I decided to pick it up shortly after release and I'm glad I did. It was a fun, albeit short, Zelda style adventure with some cute little "family moments" thrown in there in the downtime between exploring the island.I have some minor gripes, mainly with the combat. Enemies can aggro onto you from offscreen, and start attacking before you see them (stupid bats...). The ranged type of roamer seems to be able to occasionally attack immediately after being hit, which is different from every other enemy in the game having their attack cooldown reset on being damaged. And rats, are... well, rats. Small and irritating, lol. But these are all very small things that didn't bother me too much, personally.As for all of the things I loved, well.. I don't want to get into spoiler territory, but I enjoyed all of the dialogue. Some of it was funny, some of it was sad. A lot of it was emotional. The sprites were really well done and showed a lot of emotion where necessary, same with the portraits during dialogue. I didn't end up crying during some of the sadder parts, but I came pretty close.Overall I would absolutely recommend this game. I will say, again, that the game is relatively short, so don't expect more than a handful of play sessions at most. I did this in one sitting tonight. If the short play time bothers you, wait for a sale, I suppose. I personally thought it was worth it, but I also put a lot of value in well written stories, which this has.

Give this one a try right away!

_childDocuments_.review: Arietta of Spirits is a poorly made GameMaker Studio 2D retro pixel top down brawler that makes NES games from the 1990's look like works of art.  Gameplay consists of highly mediocre console-esque 2D top down brawling, dodging, and wondering why you spent thousands building a bleeding edge gaming rig when apparently this is the best the gaming industry can manage to dump out lately.From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.A choice was made to use obsolete, decades old retro pixel "art" as a substitute for contemporary PC graphics.  It's unclear if this is due to lack of budget or talent, regardless, the overall visual quality of the game is extremely low as a result.There's no options to change the resolution for the game or customise the graphics settings.  There's no way for gamers to ensure this is running at the native resolution of their displays... there's no guarantee this game will look right on any PC as a result of this hamfisted design decision.  There's no way for gamers to try improve the low quality graphics. Some of the defects in the game can be attributed to the choice of using the GameMaker Studio construction kit/toolset.  This is a very poor quality toolset favoured by amateur developers as it's cheap and requires little in the way of development skill, but unfortunately has very limited capabilities.  Just as you can't make a silk purse out of a sows ear, you can't make a great video game if you use a terrible engine.  GameMaker Studio is often used to make retro pixel shovelware and cash grabs.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.Arietta of Spirits has the laughable, eye-watering price of $15 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games, let alone the sheer number of free games available on Steam.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Arietta of Spirits – Charming, but Content is LackingLet me start with the positives: Arietta of Spirits definitely has charm. The graphics are beautiful and nostalgic, and the game has a cozy atmosphere that draws you into its world. There’s something appealing about the simple aesthetic and the emotional story it tries to tell.But unfortunately, that’s where the positives end. When it comes to content, the game feels incredibly empty. There are no upgrades or meaningful progression to make the gameplay rewarding. The monsters you encounter are basically the same throughout the game, making combat quickly feel repetitive and lacking variety. And the map? It’s flat, repetitive, and far too empty to be interesting to explore.This is a game that had the potential to be so much more, but it feels like the developers stopped halfway. Without any real depth in mechanics or a world that genuinely engages you, it’s hard to recommend Arietta of Spirits.If you’re still curious, wait until it’s on sale. At full price, it doesn’t deliver what you’d expect from a game in this genre. Charm can only take you so far – without substance, it’s a pretty short journey.

My only gripe is that some of the plot points seem a little contrived, but that's purely my opinion and it's still a fun story!Heads up to my fellow impatient gamers: There is what feels like a TON of slow, click-heavy dialogue at the beginning, and they really control the pace in a few other spots, which got frustrating to me. _childDocuments_.review: So far it is an absurd amount of dialogue with really bad combat going over repetitive maps. I just got bombarded with three different sidequests each with copious dialogue. I'll revise if I play more and get more enjoyment since there is some cool stuff here--great music and some of the visuals are really nice, but... the core loop is not doing it so far. There is also a stamina system for the roll which is like... just give it a cooldown at that point stamina sucks outside of the context of an RPG.Edit: Wound up going back and finishing it. Honestly I have extremely mixed feelings. On the one hand the Minish Cap vibes (both in sound design and visuals) are really nice, and the combat gets a little better after you get the shield (the stealth roamer boss was also pretty cool) but most of the game was just kind of whatever. Getting experience from killing Roamers did make my initial problem with having no reason to ever fight get mitigated, but overall despite the game being under 3 hours it still felt a bit long. The parts where you're actually in a dungeon are reasonably fun but the game would have benefitted from variety like puzzles. Also you get Herbicide and can use it as a "key" for some plants blocking caves but why can't you use it on the laser-shooting plant enemies? Also the sidequests give you no reward unless you collect every collectible it seems, so felt like a bit of a waste. All in all, I guess I don't recommend it but when it is on a mega sale like when I bought it there's worse ways to spend a few hours. Also, I played on Hard mode which was pretty easy so I imagine going lower than that would be way too easy for most.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little game with a good atmosphere and simple, satisfying gameplay, though not without some points of friction. All in all, it took me 4.30 hours to complete my first playthrough on normal. Another five hours, give or take, to finish the game on extreme difficulty and unlock all achievements.I Liked:- The atmosphere: the accumulation of art style and music.- The gameplay; it was simple to learn but took a bit to master.- The extreme mode; it offered a challenge and a reason to replay the game.- The collectibles: They offered genuine rewards and weren't a hassle to find, requiring only mild backtracking to earlier zones.I was Ambivalent About:- The story. It was all right. It dealt with loss to a degree but too superficially to make much of an impression on me. Where it did excel was at making you feel like a young tomboy playing in the wilderness to distract herself from the loss of a recently departed family member, and as a way of processing that loss. Even if the game makes it clear Arietta isn't imagining the supernatural occurrences.I was Annoyed By:- Some of the enemies attacked without providing proper warning. The Charger Bad was a special offender; it would often charge at you from off-screen, which left no time to react, especially if you were moving in the direction from where it appeared. Not a big deal on my first playthrough; however, it became a source of annoyance when I played on extreme where you only have a single health point.- The slow pace of the dialogue. This was not an issue on my first playthrough either when I paid attention to the story, however, it became a source of aggravation the second time around. Fortunately, the game has an option to make the dialogues pass faster. Unfortunately, you can't skip cut-scenes altogether.In Conclusion:Arietta of Spirits is a fun 2D action-adventure game that I enjoyed but wasn't enthralled by. Personally, I consider it worth the investment since I bought it on sale. Although I admittedly am not the target audience; I bought the game on the recommendation of a friend since he highlighted it as an example of a certain gameplay style. With that said, Arietta made me curious to play other games in the same category.

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely little Zelda-like with a runtime of only five hours.  The story is poignant, even if they went kind of nuts with the amount of dialogue.  A young girl vacationing on an isolated island with her parents discovers a hidden world of spirits around her.  She gets caught up in an investigation into a surge of malevolent spirits and learns about the island's past.The action is fast and fluid, and the fights never feel unfair.  The controls are simple and responsive, although I found they need adjustment: I recommend you leave the WASD keys for movement and switch the attack and shield keys to H and J (or J and K; whatever you prefer with your right hand).  You won't need your mouse.

_childDocuments_.review: 'Arietta of Spirits' is a light and stripped-down but nonetheless highly enjoyable RPG.  It will especially to more casual players of the genre, but might be a little too easy or repetitive for experienced players.  (I played on 'Easy' mode so please read my review in that context.)PROS:*  Beautiful pixel animation and lushly rendered environments which make the whole game beautiful to look at*  Lovely music and sound design to go along with it*  A very simple and stripped-down combat / movement system which is very intuitive to pick up and lets you dive head-first into the gameplay*  Similarly, a very simple level-up mechanic which lets you just kill enemies to get stronger*  A couple of the boss fights in particular were quite imaginative and required me to think outside the box to defeat them*  A couple of scavenger hunt quests on the side*  Just enough of a charming little story to keep the gameplay moving alongCONS:*  The gameplay did get repetitive after a while (thread your way along a path, hack and slash the monsters as you go) with little to vary it; I eventually took a long pause before coming back to finish the game*  Though made of lushly-rendered assets, the environments (particularly the forest paths) also got repetitive and made it easy to lose my way in between missions; it makes you less inclined to go back to areas you've already played just to farm energy or complete the scavenger hunts (although luckily you can complete everything on your first playthrough if you're diligent)*  The story / world felt a little underdeveloped; what was there was intriguing but I left wanting more (particularly in terms of a more fleshed-out island environment to explore)All-in-all I'm glad I played it and did have fun along the way so if you're looking for a game to scratch that itch, 'Arietta' might do it for you

_childDocuments_.review: What a great find! Got this in a bundle and wasn't sure at first but honestly this may have been the best game out of the pack.Sprite animation is great, the art style is pleasing with some pokemon/Zelda nostalgia going for it. Combat feels satisfying with skills/abilities that get added throughout the game. And there is just enough little hidden paths and offshoots to make you feel like you're not forced down this linear funnel with the collectibles (and reward for finding all of them) making it well worth exploring. The story is powerful, but doesn't stick around too long or get stale. There is no really fluff or anything added to artificially extend the game length and it felt just right. One thing I found difficult is fighting certain enemies at specific angles almost always resulted in taking damage when it felt like it shouldn't, but I feel like that's partly just due to the orientation and type of game being played. This is definitely not a type of game I typically play but it was easy enough to figure out and adjust.There is also a WIDE range of difficulty in the settings between easy - being very forgiving in a large health pool and lots of heart drops - and Extreme which is literally 1hit = death insanity. On my second playthrough now and did find it almost easier to dodge past some of the enemies rather than fight (playing it safe on extreme mode) but quickly found that it broke the immersion of the game. Overall - super happy with this title and would love to play a sequel if the devs ever feel like extending this story!!

_childDocuments_.review: Arietta Of Spirits is a very old-school Zelda-esque adventure, and I gotta say, once the credits rolled, I was left quite satisfied. The gameplay here is nothing to write home about in my eyes, but it is solid especially when it comes to combat as you can't just spam the attack button and win. You need to have a little patience, avoid or block attacks, and strike when you think you have an opening. The real star of the game here, for me, was its surprisingly good, and in some ways, even relatable story. Arietta is a girl who, one year after her grandma's passing, goes to visit her old cabin with her parents for the summer. It's clear the place has a lot of memories tied to it and the family is doing their best to stay strong but it's equally clear Grandma's passing has left a big hole in their lives. Before long, however, Arietta meets and befriends a being named Arco who becomes her Spirit Guide and together they start to help lost souls while fighting against the more nefarious forces in the Spirit Realm. I felt the story struck a good balance between its more fantastical elements and more real-world matters such as dealing with grief and loss, which together, kept me invested.The story even has a handful of pretty good plot twists that I won't spoil here, and moments that genuinely struck a chord with me. The game as a whole also doesn't overstay its welcome as, like advertised, I finished the whole thing and got almost all the achievements in roughly 5 hours, and this was all in the same day.I also do like how even with the way it ends, they still leave open the possibility of a sequel, especially with all the bits of world-building they sprinkle throughout the game. I honestly would like to see where Arietta's story goes next, and once the credits roll for you, I think you'll feel the same way.
_childDocuments_.name: Arietta of Spirits

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun game that is very reminiscent of Zelda especially The Minish Cap due to the art style. _childDocuments_.review: A nice short game with pixel art graphics and zelda like combat.I enjoyed the story and combat on normal difficulty, but on hardcore (or however it's called, where you have 1 hp) the contact damage on enemies and lack of i-frames gets annoying, because some enemies will both charge you and have a separate attack animation (why have an attack if they deal damage by just moving?)The graphics are really cute, with very good looking environments and easily distinguishable enemies/hazards.There is no map screen/mini map, but the world is not that big, and there are a few shortcuts that you unlock as you progress.

_childDocuments_.name: Arietta of Spirits

_childDocuments_.name: Arietta of Spirits

_childDocuments_.review: If I could leave a thumbs in the middle rating, I would for this one. There is a lot of good to it, from the 16 bit style being polished as hell to the gameplay being satisfying, but there's a lot of bad as well, especially in the story. It starts off promising with an emotional gut punch, but the ending is so abrupt and unsatisfying that it leaves a little bit of a sour taste. SPOILERS BELOW///Especially with how the last hour is, when you meet a woman who was burned for something she didn't do, but we never see her again after she freaks out when it's written like there was more to her story. On top of that, the game ends when it feels like there's at least another hour of content to go, from the story arc to the feel of the dungeons. ///SPOILERS ENDAll in all, this is the kind of game where if it was even 30 minutes longer, it would be much easier to recommend. As it stands, best to get it on sale. I didn't hate it but I couldn't get over the feeling that this was incomplete, sequel tease at the end or not.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game back when it was a demo on Gamejolt and have followed it every since. Arietta of Spirits will take you on a very fun little adventure. _childDocuments_.review: I showcased this for IGCollective. I had an intrigue, but initially no intentions to play this. Despite that, I ended up going into depth about the metaphysical topics in the game, which I found genuinely intriguing and genuinenly... well, authentic. If you'd like I've posted some more in depth coverage and personal thoughts on my blog if you want to check it out: The game is all in all a monster RPG with story-rich themes. Generally, I would find the spiritualist theme of an RPG a bit eyebrow raising. Sheesh, I need to lighten up in this intro, but honestly, it re-kindled some interest in the subject that had withered with the period in question's slaps in my face. Overall, I enjoyed the dialogue and pixel graphic world to explore. It was cute and, sort of, funny. I'd rank its top quality as being its wholesomeness. Sure, the spiritual stuff is a bit lofty, but it's a fun indie with the usual indie quirks and a nice easily progressible plotline.Here's some gameplay I recorded around launch time for my showcase: If the game interests you based on these descriptors or the steam page itself, I recommend the investment! _childDocuments_.review: Arietta of Spirits is a lovingly crafted, beautiful pixel art adventure RPG. It's kind of like a "my first Zelda" game. However, I think I echo many others when I say the game feels kind of short and rushed at the end.I finished the game in 3 hrs and 41 minutes -- and I don't think I was really rushing through. I did try to find as many secrets as I could along the way. Basically, if you're a seasoned RPG vet, this game probably won't take you very long. Also, the hit boxes are a little bit weird, so I don't see myself ever trying this game on "Extreme" which is one hit death mode after you beat the game.I liked the world that was built. I just kind of wished there was more of it before the end game.Arietta of Spririts is a fun little trip --- albeit a bit short.The game and gameplay get a 8/10 -- easily. Unfortunately, the game feels too short and rushed at the end and I can't give it my recommendation at the full price of $14.99.However, if you can pick it up on sale fully understanding that you can beat it in a single sitting or maybe two -- then you'll be happy you did. Just remember, not every game has to be 20+ hours. There is a lot to be said for a loving crafted, beautiful short game and that is where Arietta of Spirits falls for me.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is short, but well worth your time to play it.  For sure give the demo a go first, it is a nice sample of what is coming. The game takes place over the course of a few days,  which I like instead of a one-day and done deal. The friendship with Arco and Arietta feels a little rushed but still genuine and real. Gibb's was an unexpected favorite character for me, I knew I'd like Minerva from the get-go. Gibb's situation is relatable, and, of course, "BIRDHOUSES!". That cracked me up and still does. Minerva's fate crushed my heart- the game went dark and stayed that way with no apologies. I really like that, and hope Minerva isn't left stuck where she ended up. After the final boss, the whole scene had me hoping for something so cheesy I could print out the dialogue, dip chips in it and comment on how cheesy, but, alas, the game stayed true and kept dark.The ending leaves wide open for a sequel and I sincerely hope one is made.When I went in, because of my own fault I did not know the games length(played demo on switch, bought on pc to stream without looking at steam page properly), but I was not disappointed. I like the length, and this felt like a nice taste of something more.Combat is simple, you'll find Midri's items along the way while exploring the areas which is worth it for the boost, make good use of your shields and dodge roll. Visually, it's nothing over the top, but major props to the sound team. This isn't a negative thing, it fits with the games style and looks quite nice, gives me comfy SNES nostalgia and I love that so, so much. I appreciate the inclusion of hearts in the bushes along the way. Saved my butt many times! Over all, this is a very charming game and I recommend it if you want something you can beat in around 5-7 hours. Devs, please say Minerva isn't stuck in the end game place. The ending scene showing the empty and run down places was a gut punch(the broken bridge). Arco's fate. My heart can only take so much. Should you make a sequel, I will be throwing my money at you to play it as soon as possible! Have a fun time and good day!

_childDocuments_.review: Arietta of Spirits is rather charming game and I can tell a lot of love was put into it! There's a lot of polish and small details that I really appreciated when I discovered them. Although I'm fond of the overall story and characters, it never sank its claws into me the way I wish it did. But there are a couple of moments where Arietta absolutely shines. The ending was one such moment, because the soundtrack, visuals, dialogue, and gameplay all work together to build up a great climax for the adventure.Overall, Arietta of Spirits is a lovely and well-crafted story game. The combat and story don't wow me, but it's comfortable and familiar in a way where I feel like almost anyone can have a good time with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Arietta of Spirits

_childDocuments_.review: Arietta of Spirits is a lovingly crafted story-heavy game with an attention to detail. Gameplay-wise focuses heavily on combat which is well-tuned to suit the general aesthetic of the game, but can feel a bit punishing and slow to some.A sweet and short game which was not made artificially long. The game as well-placed shortcuts and jumps to skip boring backtracking, while still having the option to revisit old areas for purely optional less story-heavy content. It feels nice to not be forced to complete the fetch quests just to advance in the story. On the other hand I think I'd like to return and see whether I missed something :)Though I wish there was a map to make that a bit easier. Also, I got really lost at one point of the main story. But otherwise the map was well-crafted, too.Completed the game on normal difficulty and felt that it was well balanced. Additionally, the game seems to have a "soft" elective difficulty setting in form of bushes which can drop health items, and nothing else. So no extra grind looking for rupees! It's up to the player to choose how much to utilize this mechanic.The game perhaps starts a bit slow, but  emotionally. Almost too much so. Very well done, anyway. It's a pity that the game isn't able to keep up the emotions all the way through. But there's plenty of good scenes!As mentioned, the combat probably splits people to two camps. I personally don't like how attacking roots the character in-place, or how even just touching an enemy is a hit. Or how dodging and blocking can't override the attack animation. This slows down the combat and forces a more deliberate stance - which does suit the game a lot better, I do admit. But I'd prefer a more fluid system nevertheless.Regardless, the boss fights in the game are well done, and function very well with the combat system. Bosses have plenty of unique mechanics to be discovered - though sometimes it can take a few deaths to figure them out. So difficulty seems to be on point :)So, overall a nice little lovingly crafted experience that can be completed in a single evening, especially if not going the completionist route.

_childDocuments_.review: Game was mostly alright, didn't encounter any bugs, the pixel art is great and the sound design is good, tho the story felt like it wanted to expand more than it really did... especially with that ending.But man, the combat sucked. Stiff and slow, you're committed to your attack animations and there's no attack combos to deal with multiple foes in a row, plus your "dodge roll" doesn't even appear to have any i-frames, so you need to use it ahead of time... which is tough when, again, you're committed to your attack animations. Not to mention anytime you accidentally hit an object like a tree or something it causes you to recoil, which is -more- frames of being vulnerable. All that, and you don't even get anything from fighting things, excepting the so-called Roamers which drop stuff that you use to expand your maximum health... but only so long as you have a "Roamer Core" to put the stuff in, otherwise you can't collect it.If there were a middle-ground recommendation option, I'd pick that, 'cuz it's really not a bad game overall, just not as good as I'd hoped. But if you don't mind the issues with combat, then by all means go for it.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: I really like this game, but I have personal hang-ups on how the failed event outcomes are written and portrayed. If you want my full thoughts on that, read below. Recommended (with caveats)More Monster Prom with a different name. At launch, there's still some things missing (mostly cosmetic things like gallery and voicelines), but it's the same game you know and love. There's new romances and a couple new mechanics, as well as the (thankful) removal of the Money stat. One thing that hasn't been removed: failed event outcomes.I backed the Kickstarter and put additional money into the Backerkit when that went up, so I got updates throughout develpment. If I recall correctly, devs talked about how they wanted failed events to be fun to read through, despite losing. As far as I can tell, the failed endings do feel a lot more thought out than in Monster Prom, with lengthier events and more jokes to make your loss "worth it." But you still lose a sum total of 3 stats, either -1 and -2 to two different stats or -3 from one, as well as lowering your chances with your romance, making failed events  "one step forward, two steps back" sort of thing.I get it, you should be rewarded for correctly guessing (I seriously can't think of a better word of describing what choosing the right option is), and they did put effort into making the fails fun too, but I really don't think they are. At least for me. I'm making this review right now because maybe there's someone out there who will feel the same as me and should just know what these endings are like.An event is some kind of dilemma your romance gets caught up in and you have to correctly guess which of the options utilizes a stat you're good at. Both options can result in success, but both can also result in failure, all depending on how much of the associated stat you have. The more you play the game, the more you'll get used to what options use what and the "language" of the game. But, even after tens of hours and nearly all the secret endings in MonProm, I stopped playing because each run was only getting more and more stressful. Especially when seeking a secret ending, a single failure can spoil an entire run.But the part the gets me the most about these is the failure event itself. The MonProm failures were usually fast but cruel. The game let you know you messed up, with sound effects that are reminiscent of the jingles from when you fell off ledges in platformers of yore, stat losses, and worst of all, the disappointment of your SO.With Monster Camp, it really hammers home the concept that all these characters are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Their love is conditional and fleeting, favoring comedy over continuity. I only play this game alone and I assume the game's a lot more fun with friends. It's the multiplayer dating sim and you're meant to have a riot.For me, the failures give me second-hand embarrassment from watching my PC fail spectacularly, then I get to see how cruel the romance is and no one else involved in the event gives your character the benefit of the doubt. It brings back the feeling of being pushed into the mud at school and being wet on the ground while everyone else just points and laughs. I guess if you like Hangover-level humor, these can be fun sequences, but I always skip them. If I'm shooting for a secret ending, I restart the run. If I'm not, then I'll tolerate maybe two failures (depending on what stats I lose) before throwing in the towel.I remember having fun runs in MonProm where I failed to romance someone and ended up getting random events with random npcs because I stopped pursuing my romance. Ended the game not asking anyone to prom and got the good "hung out with friends at prom" ending. I still don't know if there's any such fate in Monster Camp. I got halfway through a run before three failures in a row just made me lose all the steam I had going in. I only read one of the failure endings. It was enough to remind me why I hated seeing them. It just made me feel gross and worthless for not guessing correctly.I still love these games and I'm gonna keep playing Monster Camp until my desire to keep playing dries up, but these endings seriously kill my drive for days if not months. I have generalized anxiety and depression and these event failures do not help. The music, character designs, general game flow, choice, and variety are all great. Once voice interjections are fully implemented, those will be great, too. But I really have to be in the mood to get on this. Looking forward to future content, but I recommend using guides and not bingeing run if you wanna jump into this game. And you're like me, obviously. If all my qualms don't affect you, then awesome. You're stronger than me.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit 3: Hello, as you can see I now recommend this game, albeit a late update, an update to my review anyway. The game still has some problems. The large number of paid DLCs being the main one. But also things such as what should be in the tutorial or found on an info page being locked behind an in game currency. Even with those things though, I think the game is good. It is Monster Prom, but at camp. There are some new elements that can be fun, such as the drinking phase. Some elements are still lacking proper design, but I do not believe that will change. The main one being sitting at the campfire with another player. It just seems hastily done with not as many fun elements. Beautiful Glitch has shown they can make fantastic aspects of games as seen in Monster Prom and in Monster Camp. But this feels like it wasn't polished. I know how creative and fun their ideas can be, but the talking with someone just for a state boost, also, only one player getting to actually interact while the other is more a passive participant, feels cheap. My issues with the game aside, it is fun. It is a proper sequel that stays true to the first game while adding new and fun characters and gameplay. If you enjoyed Monster Prom, you'll enjoy this game too. I standby my statement that as someone who followed and backed the game on kickstarter, it leaves things to be desired, but that is less about this game specifically and more so about a lack of proper communication and timely implementation of kickstarter related things. tl;drGameplay alone this game is an 8.5/10, a few small issues but they don't detract too much.As a supporter from kickstarter though, some things were just disappointing to see.Below this line is my original "negative review" for the game for those wondering about context.---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Let me preface by saying this: If you enjoyed Monster Prom 1, and you are only looking for that same game with a couple new aspects, then you'll enjoy this game. Coming from someone who followed it on Kickstarter, backed it on Kickstarter, and have been hyped up about it by the Devs, I am extremely disappointed.The game is in Early Access. They decided not to list it as such though, for whatever reason. There are key gameplay mechanics missing that are lazily covered up with Meta Jokes about devs working on them. 1 of 4 main adventures (or game modes) are included in the game despite the advertising and dev announcements saying it is all 3 (the 4th being a stretch goal that was hit). There also is to be a 5th that is DLC. Speaking of DLC, all Kickstarter 'exclusives' did not come out with release with no ETA for them. Not to mention all the other game modes have no ETA as well. Despite this, they seemed to have no problem releasing paid DLC for the game on launch. Interesting.Gameplay for Monster Camp is... lazy. Yes, there are the funny and dirty jokes and witty humor from the original that help keep it true to its style, but it overuses lazy political and economical jokes. Probably about 60% of events that happened during play included very forced commentary on political and economic systems and ideals, enough to where it took away from the gameplay and enjoyment.I'm not saying the game is bad. I'm simply very disappointed with the release and the responses from devs and people from Beautiful Glitch. I do plan to change my review to positive assuming the things listed below are actually done. I hope they are and I hope the devs stick with the game because as of now it really is disappointing. Feel free to comment and discuss with me in a mature fashion. Hateful and disrespectful comments will be removed.Things I want to see before changing review to positive:- Game marked as Early Access.- ETA's given for all game modes and all Kickstarter 'exclusives'.- Missing key gameplay features added.- Bugs that detract from gameplay fixed.Edit 1: I notice the game get updates every so often, but no mention of it on their steam feed (in fact no mention of anything there since  June), and no mention of it on their discord. To me this is just unprofessional. A lot of games don't post every minor update, but when you haven't posted anything since June and the game is essentially Early Access (Read above), you really should be keeping your players up to date on what is being done and worked on.Edit 2: Thank you Beautiful glitch for the comment and the response to this. It shows that you guys are willing to go out and look at the community for feedback. As you mentioned some changes in the next couple months, I look forward to this. I do want to leave a positive review, but at its current state I just can't. I respect our differing opinions and ability to communicate in a mature manner about it. As I stated in my comment, I disagree with some of what you said, just as you disagree with what I said. This is just how opinions and perspectives go though. Either way, I look forward to updates to the game.

And I loved the last one, but this one seems to have a lot more heart. I've only gotten to play two routes but there's more. Little moments in this game. One character's little side-quest at the campfire teaching another about poetry feels really sincere and cute. Or how characters will make a lot of jabs at one of the ROs for being a workaholic and then after they joke they'll go off-bit to express genuine concern for their friend. This game feels a lot more adult than Monster Prom did. It's not just the more graphic depictions of horniness or the outlandish violence. It's the little moments of emotional honesty between the characters that kind of existed in the first game but are front and center for this one. Don't worry though, there's still a TON of horniness and outlandish violence and misadventures. All of it feels more concentrated than in the first game.The art and writing are all stunning. I really did almost cry during the credits scene after only getting two runs and the demo with half of these characters.What little detracts from the experience is all small stuff. There's typos in certain dialogues, the Gallery isn't operating yet, and the end screen still says "Ask [RO] to the Prom?" instead of something like "the Meteor Shower". But those are easy patches. I expect most of them to be caught and fixed within a couple of weeks and it honestly pales in comparison.I think you'll have fun with this game. If you liked Monster Prom, you'll love this! If you thought Monster Prom was interesting but felt the tone was too much, pick this game up and just play with the filtering options. You can even remove references to the previous game so that you can enjoy this one without feeling left out!If you haven't bought it yet, pick up a copy! If you've got a copy already, get another for your friends anyway! These games are a RIOT to play in a small party.

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid player (and streamer) of Monster Prom and the Second Term DLC, I was more than excited for this follow-up to the game. The excitement was warranted. More than a few friends of mine checked in to make sure I got hands on this game the day it rolled out. I played for the first time last night and had a wonderful time streaming it. Here are my observations so far.When swapping turns, you're forced to read the prompt instead of being able to go straight to the random button which is often the case for myself and my friends when we're playing online.The only other thing is that some of the terms in the game are ableist (lame, stupid, dumb, idiot, etc) and so I spend a lot of my playing time subbing in words that are less harmful for viewers. With what I've seen in the customization settings for triggering content, I'm hopeful that will be changed in the future and I can't wait to see it! :DThe horny-meter was cranked up at least 10 notches and the new characters are delightful. I can see the lines between the older characters and these new ones and I enjoyed every moment of that. So did the audience. Getting  as a romance option was the glorious moment we were looking for along with .The new UI was smooth. A definite upgrade. Things were easier to read in general, the animated menus and other changes like the note on whose turn it is at the bottom corner was a delight to see. The animated ending gave me anime realness and it was very much appreciated. I also enjoyed the customization settings for triggering content so much .I spent so much of the game scream-laughing at references. The humor was, as always, well-timed and on-the-mark. I appreciate the writers and the artists of this game so much and I hope this brightens your day. Thanks to all of you.

_childDocuments_.review: So I've been waiting for this game since the Kickstarter was announced. 2020 has been a catastrophe, but when I say that this game wholeheartedly makes up for it, I mean that and beyond.First of all, the new mechanics in the beginning seem less predictable right off the bat. I had no clue what to "pack", not knowing the impact, and now I know another way to look into gameplay. This along with other imaginative and easy-to-understand actions make the game seem less like a skill check at each turn. Second, the new characters, romanceable or not, are lovable right off the bat. Even old favorites like Calculester and Damien are welcomed back with open arms. I was afraid that not seeing as much of the previous 8 characters would decrease my enjoyment, but I can safely say that is not the case. Now for my comments on areas of improvement...the first is more nitpicky and technical than anything, but voice-over interjections did not kick in for me until halfway through my first playthrough. Maybe the game just glitched? I'm not sure, but I was concerned. Second, the new drinks mechanic (although the concept and "host" are very enjoyable) has confusing controls. Not much was explained, and I was confused in what my goal was, or how to reach that goal.So I've basically written this essay to confirm again that Monster Camp is a beautiful, heartfelt game. It's goofy, fun, heartwarming, and a labor of love. You can tell from the opening menu to the end credits that the creative team has put in so much energy and thought, and the fans appreciate it. I'll be enjoying this game for the foreseeable future.

Like damn sometimes a ♥♥♥♥♥ just wants to smooch monsters without being reminded every 5 minutes we live in a crapsack world. _childDocuments_.review: 9/10Summer vacation, great time to relax and have fun, and a great option to experience all that youth can provide is a summer camp, together with your friends experiencing fun and totally "safe" activities like walks through the forest full of creatures unknown and potentially dangerous, or our battle arena where any kind of lethal weapon is allowed, or our old mansion where you can meet ghosts or summon evil creatures. This may not seem safe at all, but remember that this is not a human camp, but a monster camp. ^^Yes monsters, our young, unafraid and with no sense of self-preservation protagonists are monsters ready to explore these weeks who stayed at the camp in search of adventures and a chance to be with that special someone, after all they say there will be a beautiful meteor shower in last day of camp, so romantic. But being able to invite someone will not be easy, especially when the goal is none other than one of the six coolest monsters in the camp, each with their challenges to be conquered, and their crazy quirks that will create several hilarious moments. ^^+ Return of the crazy sense of humor found in the first game, now returns with new jokes as crazy and politically incorrect as in the first, especially in the various crazy choices.+ Same art style characteristic of the series returning with new sets, costumes and characters to illustrate.+ Return of the characters from the first game, some even as options to try to date, along with several new characters with their fun moments and dubious personalities.+ It remains without a doubt just as fun as the first game, with lots of special endings to discover and events to laugh at.+ Mini game of drinking that makes matches totally unpredictable, as some of them affect all players when playing in a group.+ A small store with interesting bonuses and some very useful ones, just play the game to earn the currency used in this store.+ DLC that adds new character options for players to use, with their own arts for events and activities.- Basically the same as the first game, no save system, and be patient to see all the events.- Some achievements can be quite tricky to get for those who like to have all the achievements.Taking place after the events of the first Monster Prom, here we have a new environment with several familiar characters and also several new ones for us to meet. This new one has many of the same rules as the first game, such as stats and their functions during choices, but some with changes and some totally new. In the part of the rules that have undergone some change, we have the beginning, where instead of the quiz we can now choose three items that give bonuses to stats and a question at the end to choose the route, and now the event equivalent to lunch as bonfire time, happens after two normal rounds from the start. ^^In the news section we have some very interesting functions. One of these functions only appears when there are at least two players, during which a new bench appears in the bonfire time, which up to two players can sit on, both gain attributes but if the first player be alone, it is not very pleasant. The second is the drinks system, some don't affect the game much, just changing the players' names and other things, some unlock secret endings and others can have beneficial effects for the player or all players, but be careful because some can be harmful, for the player who caught it or for everyone else. ^^Again produced by the Beautiful Glitch studio with its characteristic artistic style, with all the old and new characters, presented a good design with several clothing options as well as the most distinct facial expressions matching the various crazy jokes, congratulations to the artistic team. The soundtrack also follows the same style, full of energy, punctuating the various moments of each match, especially the various hilarious and crazy moments. ^^Monster Prom 2: Monster Camp was the first of three sequels promised by the studio after the events of the first game, and without any shadow of a doubt they've managed to make a sequel that manages to perfectly match the studio's artistic style with already known system plus with new features, familiar characters and striking new characters, and the totally wacky, incorrect and acid sense of humor, making this campground an unparalleled source of moments that will make players have fun and laugh like a hyenas. ^^

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Camp is every bit as hilarious as Prom and the amount of effort put into it really shows. Especially if you like Prom.Like with Prom, it is a game I like when I play solo, but it is a game I love when playing with friends. However, there are some differences that make Camp very much its own entity. For one, it seems you are tied to one love interest from the beginning with which all your events form with (or else we have yet to earn enough affection to change that; me playing to "win" and my friend chasing the teachers). I can see why that was added since your could be pulled in so many directions with Prom, but if I get stuck with a character I do not like they feel impossible to shake.One of my favorite changes with Camp is all the little additions like the meta shop and the mixed drinks. Not to mention the packing items taking the place of the quiz was a great touch. Altogether with the new events, dialogue, and characters: Monster Camp stands on its own two feet.

_childDocuments_.review: Backed on Kickstarter. Reviewed #3 and realized I forgot to review #2.Monster Camp is just more Monster Prom, but in all the right ways. Monster Prom was a very basic game with a simple to understand set of systems, but was more about nailing the style, humor, and basics of the series. Monster Camp expands on all of it. Adds lots of options that more games need like Trigger Warnings for certain types of content, a built in alternative "streamer mode" end theme to avoid copyright, while maintaining the vibe.More characters both playable and non-, appear here and is super inclusive on all fronts.The crew are amazing at continually creating fun and engaging characters and events, but listening to and including their community in the development process.(Shout out to the main storyline being a meteor shower, which I suggested in the Discord when they were previewing/deciding the base ending polaroid pose and both variants either featured looking at the sky as a key element. I suggested "Hey, if there is a big meteor shower predicted for the last day of camp, that's a reason to want a date, but could be easily overlooked for a bigger ending." It makes the game a little bit more special to me, but hey, it's just one example of the MANY things people have suggested and gotten included.)Seriously though, if you like "mature" humor that doesn't feel childish, and characters that will eventually feel more nuanced and deep than most in other works of fiction, or if you just really want to jump Calculester's circuits, play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent continuation of the first game's great writing and charming art style, Monster Prom 2 exactly what a sequel to a game like the original Monster Prom should be. I was never one for Visual Novels, and I'm still not entirely keen on the genre as a whole, but the original Monster Prom was a distinctly funny and charming experience throughout, which is a promise that the sequel definitely delivers on. While not every character will appeal to everyone (I, for the life of me, cannot figure out why Damien is so beloved), and not every joke will land, the overall experience is eminently enjoyable and its safe to say that there's something in here for everyone.After having played quite a bit of this via Discord streaming, I can also wholeheartedly recommend this as a fun game to play with friends. Having everyone put on voices only adds to the experience, and makes it all even funnier.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Prom 2: Monster Camp

_childDocuments_.review: Dear Terry (*wink*, don't worry you'll eventually get it)This game is honestly amazing. Been waiting for it for quite some time and damn was it worth it, The new packing system for the stats is as hilarious as the quizz was and honestly love the references to Monster Prom here and there. The ability on multiplayer to sit with someone else is also genius, kinda brings out cooperative play (speaking of, some drinks do that oo, and that's quite nice). What else, the humour is just great as always, honestly not disappointed here, I do like the opportunity to custom set the kind I want or would rather not seei n the menu, it's great you thought about people's sensitivty, but to be honest I should have expected it. Now, on to the romanceable characters, while I'll miss mmy favorite gorgon for a bit longer, I was stocked to be able to learn more about Joy, Daliah and Aaravi  (especially Daliah, but Hell (no pun intended) words couldn't begin to drescribe how much I love that character). Nice to see two old favorites of mine as well. Now let's be honest, I wasn't sure about Milo at first. Then they started appearing in some of my other plaaythroughs, here and there.... and you know what, they grew on me, and I must say I'm definitely fond of them by now.As someone who has a... let's say "problematic relationship" with alcohol, the drinking part of the gameplay isn't really my favorite because of its themes. HOWEVER I do like the lore behind each cocktail and the effect some have (every action gives every player stats? SIgn me up! More cooperative gameplay!) so it's really just me having to pretend those are all virgin cocktails or doing my best to pick up the swarm of bees (HELL YEAH)Do I recommend this game? YES, a hundred percent yes. And keep in mind that review is written before quite a lot of features are implemented and/or fixed, like, day 3 or something, and with me having played that game onl 6 hours in a day so far! The solo game is enjoyable, the multiplayer game makes that game shine ever brighter, honestly, why are you still reading that message? You could have been playing that whole time! Hell why am I still writing instead of going for another playthrough like right now?

_childDocuments_.review: Tl;dr - I recommend the game because I love the franchise and characters. If you played the first game, just be prepared for a lot of differences, which are subjectively better/worse. Wait to buy if you want a full game or don't want to start off with Damien/Calculester/new characters.I have been waiting for this game for so long that I bought it without thinking twice. If I could rate this on a scale of 10, I'd probably give it a 5. My score is based on a few things, one of which was feeling let down with how much was released up front, it isn't the full game, or even half of the game. If you don't want to romance Damien or Calculester, or any of the new characters, I'd wait until later to buy. And even then Damien seemed different. I felt like he was a lovable idiot in the first game but I felt that he got more dumb and innocent? He didn't recognize a sex toy, which seems kind of uncharacteristic with how sexual the last game was? I don't know, he felt different and so I'll just have to adjust to that I suppose. Its a personal preference and might not bother most people.I also have a love/hate relationship with the selection process of who you pursue. You get locked into one character from the get go and can't deviate from it, unlike the first game. I think I miss that freedom, but on the plus side you get to hear more from the character you're pursuing versus having to hear a lot from the others you don't care about as much for that route. This game is significantly more vulgar than the last, I appreciate that it has a trigger filter so you can censor it a bit. I suppose that only matters to some people though, I just thought it was a nice addition.If they charge for the other additions to the game for the other characters I don't think I'd buy them. Maybe its my trauma from EA and how they charge for everything, but I'l still kind of upset they didn't release a finished product. But at least we have something to play while we wait for the rest. I hope the personalities for the other characters stay consistent with the last game. If not I hope I can fall in love with what they have turned into. I can't wait to see more of Polly~I love the addition of an androgynous character to pursue. The inclusion of pronouns and different sexual orientations being allowed in a game is always refreshing as I'm used to hetero based games or ones too scared to openly let anyone be in anything other than a hetero relationship. In the end I say try it out, especially since its on sale right now! c:

_childDocuments_.review: So as many did, got the first game, as a "joke" game. "Haha a funi-written date-sim with multiplayer". Yeah. Thing is this is actually funny. I got hooked into the first game and easily played it, mostly alone cause I don't has that many friends who'd play this type of game. And after finishing two games and Calculester telling me to leave a review since I enjoyed the game.Obviously I had to get Monster Camp since now my favorite character, the Slayer, aka Aaravi Mishra is finally a normal date-able character that actually has more chances to appear than to just try to murder everyone. Aaravi best.Really fun game, really nice funny writing, lots of different events, game encourages you to play different routes. However the first question you get asked in the game, locks you in the character. Regardless of what you do, the game won't let you change the events to the character you want to be with, hopefully this is changed or shown more clearly so that people who want Character A events will get said character.Then we got Juan, the Small Magical Latino Cat. We finally get a look at this cute little fellow. And is on a randomized drinking minigame where you pick a random item, like a dumpster fire, manhattan or a cosmopolitan. It will drastically affect your stats and help you a lot, or destroy any little chances you had to  be with the character you'd like.Regardless, really funny characters, writing. And as always an amazing song to finish the game, this time it is mostly animated, seeing our avatar(s) do different things as well as the shenannigians of the other campers and their usual stuff.Really fun sequel to an already cool game! Can't wait to continue reading, laughing and enjoying it. I was afraid they might have failed to capture the feel of the original, but all these outlandish, dumb, cartoon situations really make this game feel like a show you'd watch every week to see what they come up with next.If you enjoyed Monster Prom, what are you waiting for? For 10€ its a really nice, high quality game, that can be played either locally or online with your friends!

_childDocuments_.review: Sigh, I knew that a review was imminent after the first play-through. How do I even explain what I find so interesting about this experience...well, you know how you've got a type, like the kind of person you know you're into? Whether it's gender, looks, personality traits, there's something you feel like you naturally gravitate to in another person--especially someone you think you could potentially fall in love with. I can tell you after playing the last game, then enjoying my first run here with an unexpected Aaravi choice, along with her forced bunkmate Hex, on a journey to find a mystical dungeon/bagel shop and thwarting a goblin to choke on his own poisoned cream cheese, ending in me forming a last day union with BOTH of them, I believe it's safe to say that Monster Prom and Camp have a miraculous ability to make you appreciate all types. No matter how you didn't think they could possibly work in the first place. Every romance feels like a win. I don't want one special someone...I want them all. And I don't know how it happened all over again this time around, but it's Beautiful.You got me, guys. You got me good. Now let me know when that Minotaur becomes an available RO.

_childDocuments_.review: If you loved the original Monster Prom, I can happily say this game does not disappoint.It has all the whacky hijinks of insane suggestions and murderous/lustful times of doing your best to make choices based on the hopes that its Creativity but nooo its Fun and you just looked so uncool man what are you even doing with your life .The main 8 of game 1 has only Damien and Calculester as dateables (though thus far I have seen Polly and Scott appear as well), but judging by what I saw when I loaded up they plan to make more games with 2 of the OG cast alongside 4 others, so never fear if Arson bad boy and Wholesome Bot weren't your favorites; they WILL come back.  And also hinted at a Reverse Prom where you try to get the 4 PCs dated instead.There are toggles as well to keep some content away if its not for you, such as what they consider the most graphic violent/sexual descriptions, antagonists being awful 'people', and references to game, which I don't think I'll use but I think is a nice touch.There is 1 con I must bring up, however.  The tongue-in-cheek 4th wall breaking narrator talking about how you want to boink your classmates happens a bit too often to the point that between him doing that and the sheer overuse of the word 'horny' it seems a bit TOO meta and can be annoying to have mentioned once an in-game week.Regardless, the charm of the writing and characters is still there, Aaravi is an adorable tsundere, and if for some reason you havent played the OG game and are looking to buy it, I'd highly recommend it.  'Competitive Dating Simulator' is not entirely inaccurate even in spite of you losing without anyone elses help most of the time, and if you enjoy a bit of vulgar language, pop culture references (some more obscure than others).  Go buy it now, and be amazed as your friends shrug/laugh and say sure before getting sucked into it.  You shall not escape, it is too late.  Join the fanbase already~

_childDocuments_.review: For those who've played the original Monster Prom, this is more of the quality content you love (I sort of assume... seems odd that someone would be investigating this sequel if they played the first game but hated it), so you can pick it up to enjoy new content or just support the devs of some pretty rad games.For those who haven't played the original, this game plays like a comedic multiplayer dating sim, and makes for my favoirte party game by a wide margin... I have a number of friends that love the title, and I'm unsure I've ever played it with anyone who didn't at least enjoy it enough they didn't regret it as a "try-it-once". It's particularly fun if one (or more) people in a playgroup have a penchant for voice acting and are willing to go for the gusto reading lines aloud. It's a highly humourous diversion with charming writing and amusing surprises abound (Monster Camp's "Drinking games" are particularly unpredictable in the best ways).Game has ample QoL considerations, including couch co-op, online play, and remote play together, seperate or shared controller play, save features, fairly extreme replay value, very inclusive (freeform sexuality, pronouns, etc), planned gallery modes for the charming artwork... the game is presently in a fairly aggressive state of Early Access, with 4/5 of the subgames not yet present and certain features (such as gallery mode) still in development... if that's a huge issue for you, I'd point out the first game is an extremely fleshed out experience that is fully available, so feel encouraged to pick that up to try it first... this installment is more for if you're through that content and dying for more, or like the content enough you're happy to put a downpayment for the devs to work off of (or both, in my case).Basically, if you haven't played the first game, it's pretty fair to start there instead for a similar but more complete experience... but definitely consider one or the other. These are definitely games worth having if you ever are entertaining guests (whether in person, or remotely, since I for one am writing this in the weird times of the pandemic)

_childDocuments_.review: I am sorry but I cannot recommend this game.It is not very good.The dialogue erratically jumps around like the hormones of an emotionally unstable, yet horny teenager.The writing tries to be everything at once.At times it is inappropriate, woke, pseudo-intellectual, alt-right, virtual signalling, hipster and camp but in the end falls short of anything cohesive thus managing to achieve nothing for me.The humour is barely digestible, like the stale lunch your mom lovingly made for you. Yet you forgot to eat it during lunch-break the last four days never throwing it away either.Most of the time it is referencing something without any further joke attached. “Haha, look we made a reference, that’s funny, haha. “That does not work for me and in combination with the unhinged writing, I often was not sure whether what I read was another reference that flew over my head or it was just me lacking an American background or being of the wrong generation to be able to laugh.What about the characters? Well, I find most forgettable, ugly and bland. I didn’t feel anything for them, I could not relate to them and I could not care less about their questionable actions, cringy motivations and missing depth. Sadly, their trope-ridden love interests you get assigned (not chose yourself) were nothing to write home about either.The whole gameplay reminds me of your own pimples-ridden face and no matter how you look at it you’ll never find any beauty in the reflection, only angsty existential dread with a hint of yearning to belong somewhere else.Most of the time you pick one of two dialogue choices to move the unsatisfying story along. It feels more like being at school than playing a video game.As usual the teachers want you to understand their message. You don’t get to think by yourself, you just regurgitated what was being said earlier.Maybe the choices need some traits to succeed, maybe not, the rules are unclear and obfuscated and with only so little to do, other than to read, I assume replayability will be as boring as the monotonous voice of your geography teacher.All in all, the whole game somehow was able to make the memories of my teenage years even worse. Being a teenager wasn't great, but this, this is a whole other level.I feel genuinely sorry for the friend who gifted me a copy so that the three of us could play this together. We all tore the game apart in frustrating hilarious hysteria, just like friends tend to bond over shared horrible experiences of camping trips gone bad.So just as the venerated Dreadnought Total Biscuit once said:“Even cancer is nicer with friends.”
