_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Murder By Numbers will absolutely scratch your murder-mystery-visual-novel itch if you have one. It's really good.Drawing comparisons between MbN and the Ace Attorney series is inevitable, so getting it out of the way:1) Murder by Number tackles more "adultish" and contemporary themes than Ace Attorney.2) The gameplay is more similar to the Ace Attorney Investigations games than Ace Attorney, as there are no trial segments. Instead, the main gameplay takes the form of Picross puzzles. The Picross puzzles are difficult enough to be satisfying, but never unreasonable to solve without using hints.The most important part of any visual novel is quality writing, and Murder By Number has quality writing. Cases are usually able to keep you guessing until the very end, which is nice.KC is cool but he's not my type.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Avoid.The game overstays its welcome, the art is ok, but dialogue and the linear plot are tedious and uninspired, characters are shallow and uninteresting. The music seems to be a single looped track, that you are going to have to turn off at some point to keep your sanity.The amount of picross puzzles is satisfactory, but at the same time, they are mostly small and quite abstract. The size might be a deliberate choice to make the puzzles short, but the abstractness makes the task vapid - you are simply filling in squares as an abstract pattern [based on the picross rules] which then is miraculously turned into an object you were supposed to find as a clue in your investigation.Works well on the Steam Deck [alas, at some point the option to show inventory items to interrogated characters disappears and you have to go to a menu and exit the menu to bring it back].
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: The (non-pixellated) animation and artwork is great, it's what drew me to the game initially, and that continues throughout.  The pixel art is hard to tell what they're depicting a lot of the time.  The story/themes are pretty bad, except for SCOUT's, but if you're just here to do some minor mystery solving and play picross boards, it's cool!  Achievements: There are only 1 for completing each of the cases, so it's simple to get them all, but read on..."SCOUT's Memories": If you complete the main storyline case boards without hints or errors, you get higher grade  (up to maximum of "S") and unlocks some of SCOUT's Memories, which is an extra set of boards and story.  I unlocked the first 2 memory story scenes fully, but not for cases 3 or 4, and I do not intend to replay through the whole dang thing to try to get higher scores, so I will just have to miss out on those!  Beware if you intend to unlock them - if you screw up on a board, just restart the whole thing.  Not bad, but I'd wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Being a big fan of Picross style game and of Phoenix Wright, when I saw that game, I thought to myself "Well, it seems neat, let's give a try"And after completing it (The main game with 4 cases including a various number of Picross puzzles and all the 69 additionnal picross puzzles), I have to say the Picross part of the game is really solid. Thumbs up for that.The detective stuff on the other end, I am a bit more conflicted on it. There are many nice moments but also a lot of clichés especially towards the end. I am not against clichés but when you can see them from a mile around, it takes you a bit away from the game.Speaking of taking you away from the game, the Picross part (while being solid on its own) can sometimes break the flow of the story. Sometimes, you just complete a Picross puzzle and less than a minute later, you have another one. No time for the story to sink in much.To compare it to the Phoenix Wright games, in Murder by Nubmers, there is only the detective stuff and no trial section. While the detective stuff is fun and all, it is the trial part in the Phoenix Wright series that gets you excited. With the "Objection" and "Take that" and the intense music. During the interrogation of the suspects, something that gets you excited like that would have been welcome. As it is, it can feel a bit flat sometimes as there is no way to mess up the dialogues.The music and the characters are really memorable and it is a shame those little things keep it from being an excellent game. It is a good game but it could have been so much more.I seem to be harsh on the game, but it is because I can see its potential if any sequels are in the work.I still recommend it if you are a Picross fan. If you are a Phoenix Wright fan but Picross is not your cup of tea, consider it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Picross, then I would highly recommend. This game is basically some Phoenix Wright-lite combined with a good Picross game. I have been doing a lot of Picross on 3DS and Switch for years, so I wanted to see how they combined that with a story and I think they did a great job of making a light story around the puzzle solving. I would definitely recommend it for fans that want a game to sit back and relax with. It's a good palette cleanser to play in between more robust experiences.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: ok, so overall the game its good, i really like the fact that you actually have to find evidence, even tho it does remind me too much of that mechanic from the phoenix wright dlc, the story is good and the graphics too, however there is so much gameplay that i wouldnt consider it as a game and more as an interactable movie, the choices, dont matter and if you are wrong it just restart from the last text box explaining why its wrong, but there isnt any "punishments" if you get the wrong choice. same goes for the main gameplay, like the only ones i consider actual game play its the timed hacking section because they have a timer and multiple charts to fill, but however there are like 8 different patterns that you can learn and the table and there is no variety to the table whatsoever. the story and characters are awesome especially chapter 3, however the death of scout's creator (im sorry i forgot her name, i mean she does appear like for chapter 4 only) its not really that important and for some reason it doesn't affect the characters, also Honor could have just called the ambulance and not the detective, but fair... speaking of chapter 4 frank wasnt scared of a robot that basically can become the terminator, and a detective in the making (more smarter then the actual detective) but he is scared of a detective. like i said graphic wise the game its amazing, but sometimes the evidence squares are too big or not proprietorially fitted in the box, i mean yes you can understand what they are supposed to be like (after the image its revealed) but sometimes they get cropped in some places that don't make sense, but like i said that is some minority. anyway, game its great, but i don't think it it that worth to play it, if the game play was more fun, yeah sure, but as it is, its just an interactable story-line
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: This game is both a compilation of more than a 100 picross puzzles and also a mystery murder graphic advenure. From these 2 this game prioratizes the picross 1st. What I mean by this is that there's an enormous variety of picross puzzles which escalate in difficulty little by little. Therefore even if you have never tried a picross puzzle before (like me) you shouldn't have problems getting the hand of it. The story is nice overall similar to other games from the same genre like Ace Attorney but it's not as deep or complex, still really enjoyable tho. The characters are really charismatic as well and it's nice and refreshing playing a murder mystery graphic adventure with a more wstern sense of humor and cultural background.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Decent idea, bad execution.Game grinds to a screeching halt in the last case when you just want the story to progress, but it throws one hard puzzle after another, so you have this really awkward pace of drip-feeding story bits between staring at the screen solving nonograms for extended periods of time when the plot is supposed to be developing rapidly.Really bad quality of life features when solving puzzles as well: no way to clear board, no clear indication when you violate constraints.Story itself is passable though and the UI is fairly functional, there are decent amount of bonus puzzles which should extend the playtime significantly.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: A nice visual novel with a lot of nonograms. I mean, a LOT. I think 3 chapters would have been enough, chapter 4 has very little variety, almost every level is 15*15, it gets tedious at the end, feels almost like a chore.The nonogram UI is clean, intuitive, bug free, one of the best of its kind and the game is very professionally made in every aspect. The characters are all cute, the story is okay, there are some good laughs occasionally. The soundtrack is also great, but it's rather short (for this many levels) and repetitive. I have received serious death threats from my gf if I ever play any of the music in the future. Recommended for nonogram fans!
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: 4/10 - WeakYou play as actress Honor (ugh, Honour), and her little AI robot toaster, SCOUT as the two team up to investigate murder cases together and piece together why SCOUT’s memories were wiped and he wakes up in a landfill.The puzzles are alright, it is picross, and a die-hard picross fan will have a day out and half playing this. For anyone else, by case three of four, the puzzles wear very thin and things start dragging out. No joke, the third case has an achievement; “What a drag!” and I genuinely laughed as that’s how I felt by the end of Case 3, it dragged.There’s a colourful cast of characters here, but the game lacks ideas and also fails to really mesh together its plot and characters, everything just seems awkward or ill-fitting. By the third case, the game is throwing numerous puzzles at you and it just becomes a bit exhausting. There could have been more room afforded to the story to break things up a bit as at one point there’s pretty much a chain of puzzles for absolutely mundane things, (like a calling card for gods sake) which makes it feel like filler. Pacing and perhaps intermixing easy puzzles with the more tedious ones would have spiced things up a bit, rather than the more linear difficulty we experience here.The fourth case was also pretty bad for tying things up, a lot of things were pretty obvious, but Honour had to play dumb for plot reasons. In the end, I think this was a missed opportunity for a mixture of puzzles with detective sleuthing unfortunately.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: just wanted to get a picross game but this game really exceeded my expectations. Likeable characters, an overarching story  and loads of puzzles. If you only want puzzles, you might find it's too much dialogue, but I enjoyed it. And it kept me busy for just short of 40 hours, so definitely worth the money
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Got this in the Jingle Jam 2021 Bundle, so that's nice. Charity and all.That said, as someone who was interested in this one for the puzzles more than the murder mystery, this has proven to be interminably slow. Compared to Pictoquest (the other nonogram-based puzzle game in the bundle), the time between puzzles is incredible, and it's couched in far more narrative than I'm looking for.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: People seem to suggest that you will like this game if you like phoenix wright but I slightly disagree. Although it looks and sounds like Phoenix Wright, the gameplay is more like Zero Escape. By that I mean that the Visual Novel part will often be interrupted by puzzles that could take 20-30 minutes to solve and are completely detached from the actual story and mystery. Does that sound frustrating? Maybe this is not for you. If, however, you want to earn the reward of story progression by solving a picross puzzle, then go ahead and try this! I personally enjoyed it!TO THE DEVELOPERS: I don't know if you guys will ever read this, but I felt the price was quite low for the amount of value I got, so if you are thinking of adding a couple of cases through DLC or something it will be a day one purchase for me, just saying. 🙂 Also the minimum GPU requirements to run this game suggested in the store page seem ridiculous. I ran the game perfectly with a Radeon Vega 8.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: If you like visual novel and have played an absurd amount of picross mobile games like I have, you'll love this game. The plot is straightforward, as you play a actress turned detective helping a robot find his lost memories. It gets a little predictable, but the characters are fun and I still enjoyed the story. The puzzles do get difficult over time, and if you've never tried picross before I can see how some of the end game puzzles can get frustrating. However if your a big fan of puzzles or a picross junkie, its just difficult enough to make it enjoyable. Overall I super reccomend giving the game a try and I hope that there will be a sequel in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I've finished the game. It was about 37 hours of gameplay, which was more than I expected to be honest. I really, really wanted to like this game, but ultimately the idea was good but the execution fell flat. In a lot of ways, it was TOO "on the nose". The 80s/90s vibe was kind of like you supercollided Miami Vice and Saved by the Bell, but while that might sound awesomely nostalgically hilarious, it's done with complete unironic accuracy that's actually quite painful to sit through. I had to mute the soundtrack after I found I was giving myself a headache from grinding my teeth so hard. And there's an obsessive use of a set of two or three "smack" sound effects that punctuate virtually every line of dialogue that really limited how much of the game I could take in one sitting. Almost none of the characters are particularly likeable, and many are gratingly irritating. The police procedure aspect is pretty ridiculous along the "proper procedure and process doesn't matter at all so long as you manage to nail the bad person" lines. What really surprised me was how charming the drawn style of the end credits was. If those were the storyboards, they should have really stuck to that style.Things that it got right: Well, there are nonograms in it, so if you're there for the nonograms, they exist. There's, as with every nongram game, an irritating mandatory tutorial at the beginning, but after that point they progress at a reasonable rate, requiring you to use better skills and be more thoughtful as the game continues. Um. Okay, that's genuinely about it. It's a lot of money to pay for a pack of nonograms, and a lot of time spent playing an irritating framing game to get to them. If what you want is an excellent nonogram game on Steam, then I'd recommend Paint it Back. If what you want is an excellent detective visual novel, well, I don't know what that is, but I'm sure it exists, and that you could find it. This was neither of those things, for which I'm sad.There are obvious hints at a sequel at the end. I actually do hope the game does well enough to warrant it, but I also hope that the developers learn from the mistakes of the first game and make a better game in the sequel -- or at least one that's less actively grating.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since I beat Mario Picross on the Nintendo Switch, I have been desperately trying to fill the picross void in my heart. This game fills that void. This game is like ace attorney but with its own unique charm. You solve picross puzzles to uncover pieces of evidence and it makes solving the mysteries of this game so much more rewarding. The characters are charming, the story is great, the puzzles are a good difficulty that even beginners can do, and the soundtrack is fantastic. I hope that a second game will come out in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I Initially only bought this for a quick Picross fix, but the story isn't too bad either!As a picross game, it's perfectly serviceable and the puzzles are mostly interesting and well designed. The interface is a little clunky at times; there's no quick way to place markers on tiles, and it could do with an undo feature too. I'm not a fan of the timed levels either, but thankfully they seem pretty infrequent.The story so far is a pretty standard murder mystery. it won't blow your mind, but it's interesting enough to keep me engaged between puzzles, rather than just skipping the dialogue. There are a lot of bonus puzzles outside the story too, if you just want a game without sitting through plot points.So yeah, if you're just a picross fan, I'd say it's worth picking up.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game for what it was, which is an easy to pick up murder mystery visual novel with Picross that isn't quite as in-depth or complex as say, the Ace Attorney series, or any dedicated Picross game. It's basically Ace Attorney Lite + Picross Lite; it does both of those things fairly well, but neither REALLY well. So if you're looking for something more deep and involved on either count, this might not be for you; if you're looking for a fun ride, I'd highly recommend it!The soundtrack is excellent and does a great job of setting the tone for scenes (I purchased it and listen to it outside the game), the characters are endearing, and the visual design is fantastic. Another plus: the game does a great job of promoting representation without being in your face about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: "A good game which overstays its welcome."Is how I would describe this game, it's just too long for the similar content involved. I went from enjoying the game to becoming a bit fed up of the game by the end. I would have liked slightly less puzzles or easier puzzles to break up the game or a bit of variety in the gameplay, maybe a different puzzle element. Making some of the content optional was a good design choice, however locking it behind a case score rating was a poor one. The sectors are too long to replay to unlock what is missing and it's not very clear how many you are missing or how to improve your score.Overall I'd say if the game was 3 chapters instead of 4 it'd be a very good game and I'd say it's a must buy puzzler, as it is with a few frustrating design choices, this gets a 6/10. It's good but it's not great, there's definitely a good game buried in here.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't been so engaged with a game since, like, Persona 4, and that's saying something.Murder by Numbers is a visual novel/picross game that follows Honor, an actress who's life seems to be falling apart at the seams, and S.C.O.U.T, her newly found robot companion. Together, with a colorful cast of characters, they work to solve murders and the mysteries of S.C.O.U.T's past.I have very little bad things to say about this game. The art is a delight; even the characters that absolutely piss you off look good. The music is very Ace Attorney-esque, and is so much fun to listen to (unless you get stuck on one puzzle for an hour, then... not so much). The story is all connected fairly well, and I feel as if the characters are introduced and talked about in a smooth, transitional way. The puzzles range from a 5x5 grid to a 15x15 grid and DO get pretty tricky, but there's always a way to solve them without using hints.I only have one complaint: if you miss a puzzle or use hints and don't get the S for your detective rank, you have to play the case all over again. I wish there was a way you could pick a section you could go back to instead of having to do the case all over again, but if you don't care so much about unlocking the extra puzzles then this doesn't pertain to you.Overall, I really did love this game and I hope there'll be a sequel coming out! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles are tricky enough to be interesting, but easy enough that the game never loses momentum. The characters have a lot of charm. There's not much puzzling outside of the grid puzzles, you occasionally need to decide which piece of evidence to show to a witness/suspect but it's usually obvious you can try as many times as you want and there's no penalty for getting it wrong. I got about 30 hours of fun out of it so it's got a fair amount to offer for its price.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: good picross / nonogram puzzles - completed main story and don't recall a single puzzle that reached a point where i had to guess to proceed. some of the later puzzles did have me scratching my head for a bit but looking at the numbers closely revealed key squares that could be filled out which then helped progress.plus there were enjoyable story threads in the visual novel built around the puzzles that had me trying to figure out who the real suspect was before the reveal! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I love the player character, Honor - she's the hard-working sidekick in the in-game TV show, playing the straight-named "Detective Oates" alongside the extravert egocentric Becky, who plays the star of the show "Miss Terri". She has a lovely relationship with SCOUT the robot when he arrives, and they quickly become the rightful stars of their own real-life murder mystery - while Becky throws her toys out of the pram! Love it!My only tiny critique is that sometimes it's hard to notice when the speaker's name changes on the dialogue box, especially when a lot of characters are in conversation. Maybe some subtle colour-coding of the names could help, or positioning the name tag adjacent to the character in the scene. On that note as well, very occasionally lines run on into each other, rather than requiring a player action to progress, and I missed some of what was said.But these are minor things in the face of an incredibly accomplished and polished experience. The dialogue presentation is exquisite, and I love how the portraits turn left and right, and even move left and right to indicate visual action in the scene. And those "punch" sound effects and screen shakes when someone is shocked are a great touch - the whole game has a lovely, OTT anime feel.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: A fun mystery/crime solving game, with some enjoyable picross puzzles to solve. Even if your not the best at picross puzzles, the hint system can definitely help, especially for those who enjoy a good story but might struggle at puzzles. Regardless of your picross skill though, I highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Plays like Phoenix Wright, mixing puzzle with visual novel, with memorable character design and plenty of feel-good relationships. But it also has a more realistic portrayal of emotion abuse and gaslighting than the cartoony visuals would suggest (don't worry, Honor can see right through it by the time the game starts), and provides a gentle and unpatronizing intro to current concepts of gender. There's only a handful of musical tracks to back the puzzles, but I haven't tired of them yet: every one is amazing (thanks to Ace Attorney's own Masakazu Sugimori). I hope there's more, because I'll be buying it as soon as there is.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: It's a real testament to the skill of the writers of this game that they managed to create such a wide stable of deeply unlikeable characters.   You have characters that are nails on blackboards, you have characters that are officious dumbasses, you have characters who are argumentative and/or narcissistic; the entire breadth of the negative expressions of humanity are on display here for you to have wildly unpleasant conversations with.On the other hand, it's a perfectly serviceable nonogram game.   Thumbs up.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I encountered a glitch where my cursor would freeze in the top-left corner of the frame every time I tried to check for errors. The only way I could fix it was to either restart the game or place anything over the board if my reflexes were quick enough, not only would the latter option ruin the progress I had made but these processes ended up greatly lowering my enjoyment playing this. I thought I could play this as a casual game but it's too much of a hassle anymore. I also find it annoying that I have to restart the whole case if I don't get an S rank at the end but honestly that might just be a me thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Honor Mizrahi has one of the worst days of her life: getting fired and being a suspect of a crime all in one afternoon. Through a series of bizarre events she becomes a prime crime fighter with her charming buddy SCOUT. You progress through the story by solving nonogram puzzles. After each case you've solved perfectly you can unlock SCOUT's memories, so be sure to get a perfect score.Murder by numbers is a fun little puzzle game for people who like nonogram puzzles, campy humour and hunting for clues. For experienced puzzlers the nonograms themselves don't pose much of a challenge, but the game makes up for it with sheer fabulousness and quirky characters. People who loved the humour of the Phoenix Wright series may want to give this a try.Only downside for completionists: there is a problem in the third case, where you can miss a puzzle so you won't get an "S"-rank. You can't unlock SCOUT's third memory if you miss that puzzle. Multiple users have already commented on this, and there are hints available online.Overall this was a very fun game, would recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I had to replay chapter 1 three times after finishing it once (wanted to see if I could pick the actual killer, restarted out of frustration, and because restarting caused the game to give 1 easy puzzle and prevent me from getting an S score). The fact that there is no skip option for the dialogue and cutscenes meant I was forced to click and read through John and Tully's parts. Finally on chapter 2, but I'm done for the night (it's 3a.m.)
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: The strength of this game is the artwork, music, and, in my opinion, characters and writing. It really feels like a lightly gamified visual novel version of a cheesy 90s procedural show, complete with cartoonishly unrealistic characters and plots, which I personally love. I'm a big fan of nonogram  games, and a casual fan of mystery games. The nonograms in this game are definitely on the easy side if that's a genre you're used to, but I was eager to get back to the story, so I appreciated that none of the puzzles took too much time. The mystery part of the game is also pretty light, you can't fail, it's more of a structure provider for the visual novel elements, and as someone who's not great at hard mystery games, I was fine with how light this element was. The soundtrack is also excellent, the music is boppy but doesn't feel repetitive even though you hear it a lot. Overall, I'd recommend this game if you're looking for something relaxing and story/character focused.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: A fun murder mystery picross game! I have different thoughts on several different aspects of the game, so I'm going to split it up below:This was my first exposure to picross, so I can't comment on how it compares to other picross games, but I found the puzzles to be fun! This was a good introduction game that was challenging at times, but not overly difficult or complicated. There are a couple points where it is possible to miss a puzzle completely, so I would recommend being careful if you are trying to unlock the Scout's Memories puzzles. If you don't get an S rank on a case the first time through, you have to redo the entire case to unlock all extra puzzles. I also had to turn the music off during puzzles because I would get tired of the peppy, upbeat soundtrack if I listened to it for too long.As a big fan of mystery games, I would definitely say this game is more focused on making you think about the puzzles and less on figuring out the mysteries. I felt like I was reading a mystery book or watching a show, where everything happens in a particular order I am not in control of. You move around a lot between the same locations and can only find evidence in a particular order. This leads you to make targeted conclusions that may be revealed to be wrong later as part of the story. I don't think this took away from the game at all, but don't expect this to be a heavy duty mystery game where you can gather all the evidence at once and make your own conclusions. The cases themselves are interesting and I was always curious to find out the solution! I found the first case to be a bit boring, but I think the game really picks up in the 2nd case and on. I loved the characters in this game, and I felt like the developers did a good job at making them two dimensional, even when they were not on screen for very long. One of the reasons I enjoyed solving the cases was getting to know each of the characters a bit better! I also think they did a good job of making Honor's life relatable, especially with her relationships with her family and friends. If you like picross or number puzzles in general I would definitely recommend this game! If you are only here for the mystery and not for the puzzles, be aware that you will spend a  more time on the puzzle sections than the story sections.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: As a person who loves piccross puzzles and murder mysteries, this game was right up my alley. The cast is wonderfully fleshed and the story is very very interesting. I love the game's style and the music is a real bop. My only gripe with this game would be the unskippable cutscenes, dialogue, and tutorial. I tend to be a completionist when playing a game and would love to get Detective Rank S, which also is for SCOUT's memories. So it gets very frustrating replaying a case, or even as a player already knowledgeable with how piccross puzzles work and finding myself just continuously mashing the mouse to try to get it to skip.Though honestly, this game is a wonderful addition to my list of detective games. I highly recommend everyone to play this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Ace Attorney, Professor Layton and the like check this out. It's not QUITE in that standard, thanks largely to the weird pacing where you're doing a whole lot of picross (especially since that's the only type of puzzle there is). There's also nothing like the AA court cases that "turns the investigation into gameplay", the fact that you're walking around with an inventory of evidence and showing it to people is mostly just a way to make that story "feel interactive". Should you get stuck on what to do you can actually just trial and error your way throughThe other criticisms I can think of is that the controls are slightly wonky, and that the music can get repetitive (largely thanks to the picross puzzles that make you stay listening to one track way longer than you'd ever do in AA)Graphics and story are the strongest points, and one of them you can judge by the screenshots here alone. It's all static images but done in an interesting "cardboard cutout" way
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun game built around my favorite kind of puzzle! I played the normal mode, and the puzzles were challenging without being frustrating. The only time I was really stalled was during one of the timed puzzle challenges, but fortunately those are infrequent and you have unlimited chances. The plot line was also well written and entertaining, with enjoyable characters and a really good pacing. I highly recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Murder By Numbers is, in my experience after playing 2 of 4 chapters, just a Picross game with some extra steps. I was initially enticed by the prospect of solving mysteries while also playing a puzzle game, Picross, in between the story elements. The reason that I don't recommend this game is because for me it desperately failed at the mystery solving side of it's gameplay. Without giving any spoilers, in both chapters 1 & 2 I was forced to go down routes of accusation that I knew were wrong simply because that was the way the game was written. If the player isn't allowed to accurately build a case with the evidence they've found and instead must simply follow the predetermined path of wrong answers, then what's the point of engaging with the mystery at all?
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: The picross puzzles are uninspiring and just bland.The difficulty random spikes between 5x5's to 15x15, and just when you think 'finally, a worthwhile puzzle' you're back down to 5x5's for...reasons.The writing is very, very subpar. I found the story (at least in 'episode' one) fairly boring.The scanning system is lazy. You don't actually "scan" anything. Most of the time you're scanning an empty spot on the floor, only to apparently find very important evidence what was...invisible for some reason.Settings didn't seem to work for me - Muting the music did nothing, it keeps blasting at full volume.I *might* finish it, but only because I got it through a HumbleBundle. Otherwise I wouldn't bother continuing
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a fusion of a detective visual novel and a collection of nonogram(aka pictocross) puzzles (kind-of sort-of in the same vein as sudoku or kenken puzzles). I enjoyed it but really can only recomend it if you both have an interest in both visual novels and these types of puzzles (or trying them out). As in, I don't think the half you like would carry the weight of the other unless you had an interest in both. Game was definitely enjoyable though and am glad it finally made it's way of my wishlist and into my library.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent murder mystery, okay Picross.This is a hybrid of Phoenix Wright and Picross.   The detection part is lovely and fair: the writers did a really good job of giving you all the information you need to make the correct deductions.  The characters are wonderful.  The art is striking.  The '90s references are funny.The catch is with the Picross part.  I love doing this sort of puzzle purely by the numbers; I see the picture as a bonus after I finish the tile puzzle.   If you use the picture to help solve the numbers, you're going to be frustrated.  The pixel art isn't simple enough to be perceptible.  One in particular, which resolves to "Passport", is just a blur of colors; in black-and-white there's no perceptible image at all.   Another frustration with the Picross part is that there's no way to reset a puzzle; instead, you have to manually drag over  every square to return the puzzle to being blank.  Third, there's no way to save a puzzle in progress.  If you exit a puzzle, everything you were working on is lost.I am still having a great time, and I'm glad I bought this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Given that  is from the same designer as the pigeon dating visual novel, Hatoful Boyfriend, I was immediately drawn to this new title. You see, I’m a big fan of Hatoful Boyfriend, and I’m sure those who played it can relate since it’s much more than just a dating-sim. This time, however, the genre has shifted to detective adventure, which I won’t complain about. Now all that’s left is to slip on my detective cap and get to slothing.Murder by Numbers takes place in Los Angeles in 1996. The protagonist, Honor Mizrahi, is an actress on a detective show until her boss, and friend at the same time, fires her. Honor is gloomy about it but happens to meet SCOUT, a robot that got thrown away and lost its memories. Things don’t seem to improve for her as her boss suddenly is found dead, and everyone who was in the building is considered a suspect. This leads to Honor getting locked up with several other people, but with the help of SCOUT, she tries to prove her innocence.I found the premise interesting since Honor wasn’t a real detective, she just played one on a TV show. This way, it was easier to relate to her when she suddenly gets pulled into a murder case and attempts to deal with the situation. It creates a nice flow of events as she does her best to piece together all the clues. Nonetheless, SCOUT is a very helpful device that adds to the game’s charm. I mean, a robot with amnesia doesn’t sound normal, but this only made me more curious about his story.Some of the characters in the story take a while to get used to. During the investigation portions of the game, Honor interacts with them, and you learn more about their personalities, which made them all grow on me a bit. Still, the relationship between SCOUT and Honor is the foundation for most of the standout scenes in the story. It was heartwarming to see them together, and I liked that SCOUT came off more human-like during dialogue. Even with his high intelligence, he makes mistakes and can’t always read the situation, but he sure is adorable.Although the game has murder elements, the tone is kept somewhat comedic, but neither is overbearing on the reader. In the beginning, I found the comedic elements odd and a little bit over-the-top, but it finds its footing quickly and becomes the fuel for some of the more memorable scenes. The mixture of serious and comedic moments never made the story feel dry, which I appreciated in the later hours.Murder by Numbers has some interesting features that make the investigating and interrogating portions of the game unique. Talking to people leads to finding clues and new dialogue options containing any learned information. It’s possible to use this knowledge to then solve the case or progress in the narrative.Murder by Numbers is rather linear in that regard since the story only advances when the correct evidence is found. Players must visit and scan several rooms until they are able to move to the next area. I did end up enjoying how the writing made it seem like some pieces of evidence weren’t critical, but over time, their importance came to light.The puzzles in Murder by Numbers are generally based around, you guessed it, numbers. During investigating, solving puzzles is essential to find or obtain an item. These puzzles remind me of sudoku, but it is essentially Picross. The numbers are already given by default, and you solve the puzzle by painting the right squares.This might sound easy, but it turned out harder than I thought during the later puzzles. This was because there are several different options available, but the player has to find the right combination. Sure, it was quite frustrating when I couldn’t solve it, but it usually worked out fine when I took a break and got back to it later.In some ways, the numbers already tell the reader how to solve the puzzle, but the tricky thing here is that there is no way to know what the right combination is other than by trying it out. For every column and row, there are numbers given. So, for instance, when there is a three, the player has to fill out three squares that are tied to each other within the column or row.Multiple numbers are available as well, and there has to be at least one square left empty between the chosen ones. The good thing here is that the order of the numbers matches with the order of the column or row as well. That means that when two numbers are given, the first one has to be fulfilled before the second.Murder by Numbers blends visual novel storytelling and unique puzzle design to create an excellent detective adventure. Getting through the steady increase of challenging puzzles was fueled by the desire to crack the case and learn more about the relationships within the story.Detective fans will enjoy how much interaction there is with the game, but the linear story leaves little room for any real consequences. Although it has a slow start, Murder by Numbers picks up speed with the help of the charming relationship between Honor and SCOUT and their determination to solve this mystery.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: The game started off great but got extremely tedious later on. Nonogram appeared every 5 mins of dialogue, keeping the story from progressing. I gave up halfway through case 4 because I couldn't keep myself from falling asleep any longer. Only buy it if you like solving Nonograms and don't mind the story getting interrupted every few mins.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed my time with Murder by Numbers. The characters are fun, witty, and you can definitely see the Ace Attorney inspiration. Though you can really feel the lack of a fifth case in this game, as some of the characters still felt shallow. The soundtrack is a bop... for the first 4 hours. There's only a few puzzle themes, and you'll probably spend more of your time listening to those few music tracks instead of the ones that play in certain locations while investigating. Those tracks can be a real breath of fresh air after getting stuck on a puzzle, but it's never long until you're back in one. I didn't find the game too difficult, but I've also played a lot of AA and Picross. The main story took me 18 hours, and i haven't done Scout's Memories yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely stellar murder mystery game combined with plenty of picross puzzles to break up the pace. The puzzles might be a tad easy for a seasoned picross enjoyer (most aren't bigger than 15x15). However, with the frequency that the puzzles occur during the story, they actually serve as nice little in-betweens for the story. If you are in any way an Ace Attorney enjoyer or you like picross puzzles and want to combine it with a good murder story, this is an absolute gem of a game worth every penny!
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: They sell this as a Visual Novel but it is best you do as I do and consider this a Puzzle Game first and foremost. Too bad you have to skip through all that trash dialogue in order to play the puzzles. The pixel art could have been better, though. You can't tell what you are working on until it gets revealed when you are done.The VN part has good visuals I guess, some okay character designs and overall the game has very good music. Apart from that, well... I hope you are not playing this for the story. If you could call a paperthin plot like that a story, anyways. The moment to moment writing is also not on par with Ace Attorney. I know, I prefer less pop culture references or adult jokes. And less intrusive gender politics. It's a little off-putting. An additional editor should have gone over the material if you ask me.While it is imperative in Ace Attorney to follow the line of reasoning, because it affects the gameplay, the same is not true for this game. The dialogue has a life of its own. You don't have to understand anything, really. You are only needed to progress the text boxes. And you can only save when you're allowed to roam around, which is aggravating. For example, you work on a puzzle for 20 minutes and want to quit afterwards, but you are assaulted with an array of cutscenes instead.The experience as a whole is not very cohesive. It is very apparent its two sides were glued together. If it wasn't for the puzzles, I would have demanded a refund. The quality of the writing is not on a level to be commercialized - it's equal to a fanfiction written by someone who had no prior training or experience at all. The cases are very poorly constructed and ankle deep at best. The way they solve the crimes is highly implausible. Also how the characters act given their role and the circumstances. The puzzles make it better, but there is no variety and no synergy. It isn't more then the sum of it's parts. One part is just okay and the other just plain inadequate.If you don't find picross mini games fun, I advise you to keep your distance, because you will be doing a lot of those. Everyone else should put on their BS-proof vest before starting this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: When I saw people describe it as Picross (my favorite puzzle game) + Ace Attorney (my favorite game series), I knew I had to play it! The Picross puzzles are pretty mindless but enjoyable if you like Picross, and I really liked the characters! The story and investigations are fine, they're not like amazing but good enough to make you want to play through the whole game. Love the art style too! The only issue I had was with some of the Steam achievements not popping, but I'm planning to play it again for the achievements when I've forgotten the story so it's all good. All in all a fun experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Works great on the Steam Deck!A super charming game that is quaint despite what it isn't: The picross-puzzles don't really look like their answers, the plot doesn't have any real options, and the characters (at first) don't push past sitcom-stock.But it works, and not just for the 90's fabric designs. Not too long in and you're dealing with a new-to-society robot, manipulative ex, overbearing mother, burnt-out detective, and a slew of characters that start to bend stereotypes. All held together by comfy writing and comfier puzzles--puzzles you can work out without random guessing, too. Only one complaint: each chapter has a few speed puzzles. The plot doesn't go on until you pass it, meaning you have to slam against the simple puzzle set until you make time. Annoying but doesn't ruin the whole.All in all a fun ride, and perfect for when you're stuck in-between places. Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Terrible picross game.It forces you to go through some story written by a weeb that can't decide their gender.While trying to click as fast through the story as possible there is also this horrible animation and sound that keeps repeating. HUNDREDS of times your screen flashes, shakes and some dumb slapping sound keeps happening. Even if you care about the story, that has to become extremely annoying very quickly.And then even the picross aren't good. The animation is very slow so it's visually never clear if clicks were accepted on the puzzle or not. You can click through an entire row before the first square gets visually marked. It's not fps cause I'm playing this with a 3090X. It's just people deciding a slow animation looked better than a functional game and they should never be put in a position where they can make decisions again.And after 15 minutes of playing I got a grand total of 4 puzzles to solve. 2 of which the tutorial that forces you to select in a certain order. It's annoying for people who know how to play and it's inadequate for people who don't.Games like these are an argument against a UBI. We would be better off with these people in the labour pool than them making games.
