_childDocuments_.review: if steam had a middle option (instead of positive or negative), i would choose it for this gamepros:-solid soundtrack; songs used during puzzles didn't feel repetitive and were catchy-great art; each character had a unique design and background scenery was certainly detailed-does a really good job of teaching how to play picross; i came into this game with zero knowledge of picross and was able to fully complete it-some lines of dialogue were actually funny to mecons:-an overall alright story; towards the end it becomes straightforward and predictable-picross puzzles themselves aren't too varied at the end; most things become 15x15 puzzles and they got boring after a while
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: As a Picross game neatly enhanced by its story or a visual novel dragged down by unrelenting Picross breaks in its momentum. A little of column A and... It's hard to be scathing of my time when I come out a mostly Picross convert and charmed by its interspersed plot.  Whilst it threatens to be weighed down in favour of the 'numbers' out of sheer frequency, its 'murder' mysteries are strong enough to weather the interruptions.  True to its makers, this is a Hatoful Boyfriend visual novel through and through, right down to its presentation. It's ultra minimalist, from the static backgrounds, cut-out figures and limited emotional range of characters. It's like a digital paper puppet show - characters bobbing in and out of the scene. It works surprisingly well. It's versatile enough that it can carry moments of levity and heavier subjects of murder (as you'd expect), corruption and divorce equally. The writing is such that themes of self-discovery and self-determination after being controlled feel maturely handled. The developed relationships between Scout, Detective Cross and K.C. feel believable and satisfying. Scout in particular is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ lovable. It's good stuff. It's an excellent place to learn it and I had my most fun in the hacking 'minigame,' in which you face multiple small grids against the clock. This isn't just because they're quick and easy, but because there's a critical lack of variation otherwise. You need to be an extreme Picross fanatic not to get frustrated at being removed from the story at pivotal moments for the same grid you've completed a hundred times over. Skipping them out of frustration is neither quick or any fun. Whilst these grids complete pictures of items you're discovering in the world and it ties neatly into Scout's 'scanning' of the environment, there's no way use the item identity for assistance in completing the puzzle and they just end up feeling entirely divorced from the visual novel. This is for Picross players who want to play some grids, but could use some spice, then. Even then, the late-game grids' difficulty wouldn't satisfy a fanatic. What if puzzles held a time limit if you've sneaked onto a crime scene and Detective Cross is going to be imminently back? What if Scout short-circuited and caused the difficulty to spike? What if you have to ascertain what the murder weapon is and do so from the Picross picture shape that emerges? The hacking grids show another way was indeed possible, but the development time clearly didn't permit it or perhaps the intent really wasn't ever there. This would obviously not usually be cause for complaint, but some of the cases, particularly the final one, do drag. In the honeymoon stage of learning the Picross ropes and seeing the early story develop, this isn't particularly bothersome, but my my is the last case hard work. Again, I must stress, perhaps only half the game is really aimed at me. From only the perspective of a newcomer, I can only conclude that I haven't been entirely won over. Then again, I still found experience to be largely positive. Call me conflicted.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: This is a interesting mix of picross puzzle with Phoenix Ace.Puzzle:For those who likes this types of puzzle, the game is a treat. For those who are not familiar, the puzzle might be a bit difficult, but everything is 100% solvable even with using the clues.They did a great job maintaining a smooth difficulty curve on all puzzles, I never feel anything is weirdly hard or easy, though the downside is the puzzles might get a bit repetitive towards the end.Characters and Story:I personally like all the characters. They all have their own different personalities. The main characters' story arc is written well. The murder mysteries sometimes are not as believable in order to proceed the plot, but they still serve their purposes. It was the determination to see the end of the story that drove me to finish the game.ArtThe Art is an interesting mix between anime and western style. Character design and the occasional whole screen drawing works well in the game.Give this game a try if you like this particular type of puzzle. If you want to try out this type of puzzle, the story and characters will definitely be a healthy distraction that helps you complete the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like puzzle games? Do you like Visual Novels? No? Then how did you end up in the review section of a visual novel with puzzle gameplay??? Otherwise, do I have the game for you.Murder By Numbers all uses one puzzle format, Picross. There is a chance you've probably come across it somewhere before but it is a puzzle game in which you are given a grid and numbers that tell you how many numbers in the grid you have to fill in sequentially. As you go on you have breaks in those lines and you have to fill out the grid so that every line matches properly. It's like Sudoku, but with fewer rules but with more moments of you wondering where how on Earth you managed to put that thing in the wrong place 20 minutes ago and you sit and cry in your room wondering where you went wrong in your life and... Wait this was about Picross.Anyway, the Picross works as your way to get evidence in your murder mystery visual novel, which beautifully melds the kind of puzzle game Picross is with the theme of never jumping to conclusions about what is going on in a case. The way pieces start beautifully falling into place once you just find that one piece also beautifully meshes the puzzle and story.Speaking of the story, it's beautiful. Honor Mizhari was an actor on a detective show who is framed for murder and is helped out by a robot who assumes she actually is a real detective. With a cast of amazing characters who make you feel very viscerally about very quickly often to have your opinions change and some very good messages on the naivety of simple concepts of good and bad, it's a beautiful story that will sometimes leave you cheering for the heroes and sometimes leave you wondering whether you made the right choice or not.Please play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Clever little game with puzzles challenging enough to challenge, but never leaves you feeling like you have to guess to progress through the problem.The story's simple but nice; the characters are endearing, ranging from "I know someone just like this" to "you are a cartoon villain and I'm here for it".I wouldn't claim that it's perfect (the puzzle interface badly needs an undo function, for instance, and you never really feel like you see enough of some characters due to the short length of the story part of the game) but an imperfect gem is still a gem.Recommended for fans of Picross/nonogram puzzles, or those who have devoured games like the Phoenix Wright series and need something to tide them over to the next one.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge fan of Murder by Numbers, as my hours show. I find the characters endearing, the puzzles challenging (but with a lot of ways to make it easier for beginners) and the polish to be stellar. There's tons of extra puzzles that you unlock through more challenging gameplay.The few things I don't like about it are the lack of a skip button or any way to speed ahead when the dialogue gets heavy on replays. And I wish there was an undo button for when you go a bit too fast during a puzzle.I sincerely hope they make a sequel! We need more! (Specifically me)
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Nonograms and like mystery stories this is the game for you. If you are looking for decision making during the VN portions, this is not really an adventure game nor does it really branch. You are more of along for the ride and are playing some Nonograms on the side. So, to like this game, I feel like you need to either really like the story or Nonograms, or in my case... BOTH. I love this game. The music is super catchy. I love Honor and SCOUT. The puzzles are pretty fun. I'm glad they went with challenging and cared less about what the image looks like in black and white. Overall, super solid. I hope a sequel comes one day.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: If you don't like picross, this game won't change your mind. If you already enjoy picross, this game adds mild mysteries and passable narratives that, at best, make the moments in-between puzzles engaging, and at worst, don't stick around for too long or ruin the zen of solving puzzles.One's opinion on the quality of the story will likely vary, and I think the 'Ace Attorney' mystery solving elements are half-baked but there are dozens of great, polished picross puzzles found here.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Was initially ok with the story and main puzzle, but it gets really tedious towards the end. There's one main puzzle throughout this game, it's pretty decent, not hard necessarily but can take some time to figure. The problem I had, was this puzzle popped up way too often for my taste. Typically there will be a few lines of dialogue and then bam puzzle. Or you have to search around and there could be 3 of these puzzles to do one after the other. It gets really tedious and repetitive towards the end. It's not hard enough to be actively challenging but it can take a lot of time. Seems I played 44 hours of this game somehow, most of it was that one puzzle. There was also a few things that kind of bugged me about the story. Usually these detective type stories try to give some reasoning as to why the main character is allowed to do the things they are doing. Like I get the idea it's not supposed to be serious, but it's just kind of weird to me how easily this actor just starts working with a cop on crimes. Ace Attorney is a similar type of game that's better I think. There it's a bit silly but they setup  the world and why he's allowed to do the things he can do. The detective aspect was pretty nonexistent for the most part for gameplay, you don't really figure anything out, just it's a vehicle for the puzzles to happen. Additionally in relation to the story, I really didn't like the ex boyfriend thing here. He's written as so  douchy that it's hard to see why people don't immediately avoid the guy, there's not a lot of nuance to his character. It's also a bit of a weighty subject to go into with his character, could be interesting, but it's done too poorly I think to actually hit well. The characters don't seem that memorable now that I think of it, but visually the look like they should be. Not sure if it's the wall of puzzles blanking my mind, but I forgot quite a few characters once they left the scene. I'd recommend getting when it's on sale if you really want it. After playing I personally would have preferred not to have played it at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Murder by numbers is a pretty well done kinetic novel with nonograms added as a game mechanic. Me marking it as a not recommended game is mostly the result of personal preferences and gameplay experience - I felt it has serious issues with focus and timing, making it a challenge to power through it. You may like it a lot more than I did.The game is - surprisingly - totally story-driven, every single nonogram puzzle is related to the story. Originally this felt like a good choice, it builds a proper story with an overarching narrative, after all.  But through the game, it became an annoyance. The story is moving at a snail's pace, it being a mix of investigation and "buddy cop" discussions with SCOUT. A considerable part of dialogues characters just reacting to things with surprise or shock, or repetitions of themes. Overall the story is presented slowly, fragmented between life lessons to SCOUT, Honor (the protagonist) being educated/told off by various characters, including a grumpy detective, her abusive and manipulative ex-husband, her own mother, and basically every single suspect. The game delves into themes of abuse of authority, gaslighting, LGBTQ rights, secrets between friends, the right of making a choice, but all are kind of shoehorned in, between the investigations and the nonogram puzzles. Speaking of the puzzles, while they start out as a game mechanic, the second half of the game uses them as padding. There are parts when you get 2-3 lines of dialogues tops between puzzles, at a point you solve 3 or 4 without a single word being said inbetween.I really can't see this game as bad, rather as a little misguided. The game good things, but there was always a "but".The overarching story was interesting, but at the same time super obvious, they used the most evil guy looking evil guys ever. The investigations were interesting, but 100% linear and without a single thought, or meaningful choice needed. The 3rd chapter had some good base thoughts about gender and LGBTQ themes, but they so forced and set up, like someone cut the motto from some fliers.The nonograms were a nice mechanic to progress the story through finding items, but later on the overabundance and general difficulty made it act like a speedbump to the story. 10 minutes break after half minute story-focused dialogue, repeatedly is ... not good.I think a traditional visual novel would have served better to convey the story, and deal with the themes the developers found noteworthy. The story felt compelling enough to finish the game, but I dislike how much time it took to get how little information, which lead to boredom and an even more inflated gameplay time - this lack of focus on the story in a storydriven game is the main reason of my negative review. Maybe I would have liked it more as a side-game, playing it in short bursts.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely tone-deaf copaganda. When your "good guy cop" is threatening someone with civil forfeiture, it's time to start questioning whose side you're on.  The writing feels very inspired by Phoenix Wright, but at least in Phoenix Wright the corrupt law enforcement system are the antagonists, not your bestest best buds.The puzzles are EXTREMELY tedious for a picross game.  It's like the designers have an allergy to numbers greater than 2, so expect just entire grids of 1 1 1 2 1 1 1 1 1 1 forever to slog through.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: A very good picross game with a four-episode murder-mystery visual novel attached.  The puzzles are very taxing, but allow you to put hints on for no cost to points and you can also ask for help that gives you less ranking.  A bad point is that the picross images are dithered you can't tell what they are until they tell you what it is afterward. The quality of the anime-style visual novel is amazing.  I found myself wanting to get through the puzzles as fast as possible to get back to the story.  The first chapter is a little slow but the story heats up in later chapters.  Anyone that enjoys picross would love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this review mainly for people like me, who saw K.C. and were suddenly filled with dread. Like, "oh, no. This is going to be one of those games that plays LGBTQA+ people for comedy, isn't it? Or kills them off for existing?" The fact that one of the cases takes place in a gay bar that hosts drag shows also made me worried.It's sad that in our society, that's considered the default for how LGBTQA+ folks are treated in the media.But readers, I'm here to tell you that you can breathe a sigh of relief. K.C. and the other LGBTQA+ people in this game are treated with respect, and as just that --  With flaws, strengths, and everything in between. They, and the characters around them, are written very well. K.C. isn't campy because he's filling a stereotype quota -- that's just his personality! And some people are like that. :DThe plot can be kind of predictable, but the CHARACTERS are very well-written. You can tell the writers did a lot of research, in addition to tossing in a fair dash of Phoenix Wright style goofiness. As an avid Picross/nonogram fan, I've been really enjoying the game as a whole.Content warning, though, aside from the murder; one of the main characters has escaped from a controlling, abusive, narcissistic partner, and said partner pursues the character through the game. The abuser DOES get his comeuppance, but he was so believably written that I found myself yelling curses at him through the screen. As someone who had a parent that was like  he brought up a lot of strong feelings, and I could recognize his tactics and angle from experience. Kudos, character writers.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: AMAZING!! 100/10Narrative picross!! If you love mystery stories and picross puzzles (like I do) - this is a dream come true!To me, the game is enormously special. I've played it for literal years on and off, during my uni years, and have only just finished it today. It's been a constantly present comfort, like a book you put down and pick back up again. I loved every moment of it!The puzzles are great, the difficulty is just right! And both the characters and the story are a delight! Wonderful artstyle and soundtrack - what more could you want?The only thing missing is a sequel, and I really hope we get one :)
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Funny little Picross game. Really good story, for what it presents. Of course, don't expect yourself some Ace Attorney Crazyness. I like the visual artstyle of the game itself - the characters and especially the drawn out cutscenes are really well done and draw out the characters traits. Music is also really good. The puzzles themselves are good, and despite only having up to 15x15 puzzles most of the time, they are really hard without some of the hints, but still solvable nonetheless. However, it's really hard to guess the actual picture they represent, even on the bigger puzzles. One negative however: While the individual soundtracks are really great, the puzzle songs are too happy-go-lucky and don't fit the mood of some parts of the game. E.g. when trying to escape a dire situation, game is like "Here, have some happy puzzle-solving music". That really broke the atmosphere sometimes and caused be to mute the game in the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: A quaint puzzle game that combines elements of visual novels with picross. Has a somewhat straightforward story carried by unique and flavourful characters and dialogue. There are also quite a lot of clever puns and references to all manner of media interspersed. The artstyle is charming, reminiscent of comic books, and very high quality. Gameplay revolves around questioning suspects and witnesses in between solving gradually harder picross puzzles that simulate looking for clues. Can recommend to those who enjoy picross and want a story along with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Picross is awesome, especially awesome when the completed puzzles turns out useful for the investigations. There is a lot more sense of achievements and rewards compared to other picross games you see in the app market (especially those mobile ones).Getting numerous puzzles one after another, however, feels like its burning out my brain juice. I imagine that more mechanics (such as animated puzzle helpers like in candy crush etc) could help make the solving more interesting and less intense. Else a timing leadership board of sorts could help reward the brain juice burning. As a picross lover, I still enjoyed this game anyways.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Picross is fun- Soundtrack is amazing- The robot is cute- Also cute girlsCons:- Maybe TOO MUCH Picross? Some times you just want to go on with the story but you are blocked by like 5 or more Picross puzzles before you can go on- Technically speaking the game is barebones and feels "cheap".- Ripped audio effects from Phoenix Wright games - No text log in case you missed something in the dialogueNeither a pro nor a con:- Story is okay at bestOverall way better than I expected
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to play this game until the end to review it and I can easily say that this is one of my favourite games of the year. The story and main cast are all lovable with SCOUT confirming his "I will die for you" status throughout. The nonogram puzzles, although relatively basic in comparison with some out there at a max size of 15x20, strike the right balance of difficulty without being impossible. I personally didn't require the hint system but it is there to assist if you aren't as familiar with how nonogram puzzles work. The art style is great, probably the area this game stands up the most with how the characters are designed to be so unique and recognisable.I would be 100% on board should this game be given a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I like the story. I like the picross puzzles. I don't neccessarily love the combination. I feel that there are times the story is starting to get interesting and the pacing is ruined somewhat by needing to stop for ~10 minutes to do another puzzle (or three), particularly in the later chapters. I do like the puzzles, and they're as good as you'll find anywhere if you're into this genre. I just don't have the mental energy to do 30 puzzles in a sitting even though I would really like to read a whole chapter in a sitting. If you know that you don't like picross-style puzzles very much, I don't think the story content will get you past that hurdle. I also feel that the bonus content puzzles, which you unlock by 100%ing a case on the harder difficulty without using hints, are kind of a pain to unlock (especially with one or two missable puzzles that require replaying a case), and the reward cutscenes they give you are generally pretty short, which was a bummer.However, if you have a reasonable appetite for picross, or perhaps even actively love that genre, this game has what you're looking for, and the story makes it extra lovely.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Murder By Numbers combines a visual mystery novel with Picross-style puzzle-solving. Picross is a spacial logic puzzle where you use numerical hints to fill the correct squares in a grid until a (rough, pixelated) picture is completed.What Murder By Numbers gets right is this smart basic concept--which is well integrated into the story, in the form of your robot sidekick who identifies clues via the puzzles--as well as the game's sense of style, its cute (if light and unserious) dialogue, appealing characters, and the relatively high quality of the crimes you have to solve (there are four cases, each of which is longer than the last). The jazzy easy listening soundtrack, by Phoenix Wright composer Masakazu Sugimori, is also excellent (if a little repetitive). You'll be bopping your head while clicking grid boxes, even if you hate easy listening music. Trust me.These good qualities come with some rough edges: The UI isn't always helpful or as clean and polished as it could be. The way the puzzles are designed, they all end up feeling pretty similar, which if you know a game like Paint It Back, doesn't have to be the case. I also wish the balance of dialogue to puzzles was tilted a little more in favor of the latter, though this mixture gets batter later in the game.But that's it. Just a few rough edges. Otherwise, the game is delightful and worth your time. Picross has always been a wonderful time-waster. The sassy story in Murder By Numbers gives you a greater reward than just passing the hours away.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful detective romp!The characters are fun and distinct, the story is interesting and the music is great. The picros do take some time to solve (and will probably make you feel smooth brained), but the beats keep you engaged!  The only con would be how you can miss finding all the puzzles on your the first go of the chapter - which means missing the S Detective rank and having to redo the chapter and picros if you want to see SCOUTs Memories the legit way. Other than that, i think you should give it a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Well designed hybrid between Picross and a story-driven detective game. You're playing as an actress who gets involved in a real murder case, and is assisted by an AI-driven robot. You can use the robot to scan objects and environments for clues, and that's where the Picross puzzles come in.The story is kind of boring and the culprits are losing huge amounts of objects at every crime scene - including a bullet that links one of them to a 30yo murder case (yes, seriously). But there are a few nice plot twists and the characters are very well done. And most important: the puzzles are great and have a good learning curve. Recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Oh my yes. Yes, yes and thrice yes, you need to give this a go. Taking a lot of cues (and from what I remember, the sound director) from Phoenix Wright, this investigation/puzzle mashup has awesomely catchy music, hilarious and touching writing, and enough puzzles to keep you going for hours. Don't let the picross turn you off, it fits in with the rest of the game amazingly well. Oh, and S.C.O.U.T. might be the best video game character of 2020
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I've never played a visual novel nor a picross game before, and yet I find myself compelled by the snappy writing and the colorful characters. Kudos to the publisher for putting out a game that so seamlessly lets a neophyte like me to thoroughly enjoy genres I'd not have tried otherwise. I am stoked to see what sort of genre and pop culture mash-ups Mediatonic puts out next.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: A wild ride from start to finish.I received this as a gift from a friend, and his pitch to me was "picross meets Ace Attorney". Playing on the difficult mode and using none of the hint systems the game has to offer, it took me about 40+ hours to complete all 4 cases. I lost hours of my life as I worked my agonized my way through every puzzle and clue. And I loved every single minute of it.The art style ranges greatly, but I enjoyed the fact that the characters had a white border, separating them from the environment. While it's may not be everyone's cup of tea, I do think it helps them really pop in scenes when the bigger revelations/reveals hit. The characters themselves, even the ones that seem rather 1-dimensional at first, flesh out fairly well and do a pretty good job of fitting into the larger narrative. I found myself sucked into the drama of good guys, bad guys, and the twists and turns that the various characters take on their journey.Overall, I'm really happy with the complete package. I wish there was more, but I'm happy with what's here. If they ever release a sequel or DLC, I'm getting it. And I'd definitely recommend this to anyone that's even remotely interested in it.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I'll put this pretty simply.If you're looking for a game with an ace attorney-style narrative with humor, this is the game for you.If you're a fan of picross, this is the game for you.If you're looking for Ace Attorney-levels of mystery solving, this is not the game for you. (Not that that's a BAD thing, mind you, but it's good to have expectations going in.)This game is a fun and charming little romp through a rather lovely story. It's close-ended , and has some fun, but short little mysteries for you to enjoy along the way.If you're looking to scratch a picross itch, I honestly can't reccomend anything else. It's more substantial than your usual picross game, having an overarching narrative attached, which is fun to see play out between puzzles. I don't see any reason to not pick this over other picross puzzle games, though it's possible those games may have more puzzles overall? There's plenty to chew on across the 4 cases, with bonus puzzles unlocked if you beat every puzzle in every case. (Tip: That's not hard to do, just keep investigating every location until they're uninvestigateable before moving on in the plot).While not a must-play, it gives you what it says on the tin. The characters are charming to boot, and it certainly helps that it's also quite progressive compared to other narratives with this tone. So, whether you want to distract yourself with puzzles, or enjoy a story about a girl and her robot, give this one a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I wish Steam had an "Indifferent" game rating, but I'll have to settle with a negative one.I was expecting mystery game elements, but the core gameplay of "Murder by Numbers" is really just solving a bunch of nonograms/Picross - Not that there's something innately wrong with that, it's just that it's difficult to award much credit to the developers in the way of originality when the gameplay is plagiarised wholesale.Laid over this core gameplay is a visual novel which is, although competently written, devoid of much in the way of originality. Around two missions into the game, my suspicions were confirmed and I was able to solve every case just by applying the "progressive stack" to the list of suspects, which robbed me of any suspense whatsoever. As a result, I personally don't think intersectionality makes for very interesting detective stories.The nonograms get increasingly frequent to the point where they become an annoyance because the cast is incapable of doing simple tasks such as going to the toilet without having to pull out a 15x15 grid and by the time I finish solving each puzzle, I already feel emotionally detached from the narrative - I'm not sure why the developers thought this was a good idea. Imagine trying to enjoy your dinner except you have to fill out a page of your tax return between every other bite.All in all, the story really is about Los Angeles and it's convincingly executed, right down to the somewhat awkwardly placed lecture on bespoke personal pronouns in the middle of a murder mystery. Sadly I don't think I'm white, nor guilty enough to appreciate this sort of thing, so I'm probably not the correct target audience for this tale (I'm with Oscar Wilde on the idea that all stories with morals should be given warning disclaimers). After I realised the story was literally the Facebook meme about "a strong black woman who don't need no man", I was unable to take it seriously and treated it as more of a surreal comedy akin to trying to solve sensitive American political issues such as gun control and the patriarchy with the power of Sudoku. And I suppose that itself was kinda amusing. Sadly, I'm not American, so I don't resonate with a lot of it.On the bright side, the art is above average and the music is inoffensive and soothing. If you buy this and you love picross, you probably won't be disappointed. If you're looking for a mystery game or an actually thought-provoking story, you might want to give this a pass.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I really like nonograms, they're my favourite form of puzzle so when I saw a game that combined my favourite genre of murder mystery with them I was ecstatic.It wasn't as perfect as I had hoped but this game is still extremely fun, fun puzzles, fun characters, fun dialogue. This game is very fun. It isn't the type to win awards but it's extremely fun and I enjoyed it a lot.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, a very pleasant experience.  I completed all the storyline and extras in the amount of time (although it could be definately completed in less time since some moments I stared/left the screen on too long).  By far the most enjoyable aspect of this game is the story, characters, and music. The style is unique, fresh and thoroughly enjoyable.  At first the puzzles were fun trying to solve.  However, as the puzzles got bigger over time, they really started to disrupt the natural flow that most visual novels have.  There were moments that I was staring at the screen for a very long time to solve it and honestly got a little crazy.  Although they do play music while you try to solve it, hours and hours of listening to the same music drove me into a sort of furvor to finish the puzzles in a crazed state.  In fact, the most fun moments of the game ended up being the timed puzzles since they added urgency to important story moments and maintained the storyline.  Although I could have used hints, etc, that would have lowered my score and prevented getting the top grade to unlock bonus content.In summary, by focusing more on the story/visual format and decreasing the complexity or the number of puzzles a little, i think this could be a very new and exciting ip like Ace Attorney.  If you like Ace attorney and a great story line of unique and fun characters, then murder by numbers is a must have.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Writing falls terribly flat, terrible balance between puzzles/dialogue.Essentially a 6/10 picross game stapled to a 5/10 ace attorney gameThroughout the entirety of the first case, almost none of the characters are likeable, the motivations for your character sticking around are flimsy at best. It feels like the framing device was created before the actual story, and then they never reviewed it and thought "ah this makes 0 sense, lets rewrite that"Now if instead you were lets say a defense attorney who was investigating to protect your client instead of a TV Actress??? It all would make perfect sense.The picross itself is pretty weak and lacks a lot of features that have been standard in picross only titles for a few years at least. Also the way the picross is woven into the narration is very weak, and often feels like "oh ♥♥♥♥ we wrote the story but forgot we need to put puzzle pieces in!" as opposed to being a thing thought about from the beginning.Overall super bummed, was really excited for this game, Picross+Ace Attorney is right up my alley, this just manages to whiff both halves
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed my time with this one. The amount of puzzles it has you do can be a little bit tedious if you want to see the story at the moment, but I thought it was worth it for the story imo. I appreciate that there are bonus puzzles, but also that they aren't necessary for get all achievements and everything because I'm not sure I can go through that many of these puzzles. It's great for those who came for them though. I honestly really enjoyed the timed hacking version of the puzzle, though there aren't many ways to iterate on it just due to it's structure being 5x5 and fast paced. Give it a shot if you like picross, want a good story, and are ok with sitting through maybe a few more puzzles than necessary.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a mix of Phoenix Wright and Picross, two series of which I love. I've currently beaten the first case and I'm about halfway done the second, however, I am having an issue where whenever I attempt to play the game I get black-screened and it does not allow me to play! I've tried task manager, shutting off my computer, logging in and out of steam, and several other options. I like the game so much that it's killing me not being able to play!
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: 99% of the puzzles are 15x15; there's one puzzle in the bonus section that's a 20x15 but that's it. Roughly 130-150 puzzles total, but that's an educated guess because there's no puzzle select.I see a lot of comparisons to Phoenix Wright, but it's honestly closer to Professor Layton. You scan the screen for "clues" which are just picross puzzles. Then you talk to some people. There's no real difficulty here outside of the puzzles because the most it amounts to is "use the clue you just found on the person you're talking to." It's definitely a visual novel broken up by picross puzzles. The story itself is good enough to keep you hooked, but not if you hate or only have a mild interest in picross, because puzzles break it up a lot. Especially in the back half when puzzles increase in difficulty and numbers. It can be a bit off-putting to get to a big story beat only to be removed for 15 minutes by a puzzle. This is especially grating in chapter 3 which  on a bit too long. There are four total cases, each one with its own self-contained story, and one larger narrative that stretches over all four. The best part of all of this is easily SCOUT and pushing through to see his story come to a conclusion will likely be the prime motivator once the puzzles themselves start to get tedious.My total playtime for 100% (all main story S rank and all of SCOUT's Memories bonus puzzles) was a little over 27 hours, so the value is definitely there, but only if you like picross. The story is not going to be strong enough to latch onto you if you do not enjoy picross.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not even half way through the game right now so I'm not sure if my opinion will change but I'm obsessed. I can't explain it but this game gives me big Ace Attorney vibes which are my favorite games of all time. I also adore puzzle type games and have been into nonograms for a few months so this showed up on my discovery queue at the perfect time. If you enjoy quirky fun characters in vibrant environments and nonograms (you will have to like them because you do them A LOT) I would definitely check this game out!
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly despite very good art and an ok story the game is too technically flawed to recommend.There is no way to disable the nauseating camera shake. It hogs the screen in fullscreen: if you want to switch to an app that’s behind the game – good luck. The menu can't be accessed during VN story elements. Nonogram controls are outdated. For example in the tutorial it’s possible to cross out already selected squares in cross out mode. The devs could learn a lot from android nonogram games. There’s no voice acting.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: If you just want to unwind this is the game for you. Solve pixel puzzles that progress from super easy to a little challenging. There are a few time sensitive puzzles, but they're small ones, the rest of the time you can just solve the puzzles at your own pace. I really enjoyed just disengaging from the world and letting myself relax with this game. It has a cute storyline too.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a fan of visual novels and nonograms, so this was an easy buy. Unfortunately, it doesn't quite succeed in either aspect.When you want to play a nonogram, you have to sit through tons of unskippable dialogue, and in terms of the VN writing, it's just not that good. I work in TV/film, so the fact it's set in this industry was a problem because it totally fails to understand or convey the setting. The writing overall felt less like a VN and more like a parody of a VN. The characters were unbelievably annoying, and the content was so repetitive. It was like they had a word count target, so they drew out dialogues needlessly in ways that didn't advance the story in terms of plot or character development. And the characters themselves were generally two-dimensional and hard to like.The most engaging story element is Scout's backstory, but that content is minimal in cases 1-3, and then appears more in case 4, but... falls prey to another issue discussed below. The writing overall doesn't strike a good story balance between the murder mysteries, the backstory mystery, character development, and inane attempts at comedy.The other big issue is how easy the mysteries are on cases 3 and 4. Case 3, the answer was obvious the moment the motive was first mentioned, and case 4, the answer was obvious about a quarter of the way through, so then the remaining 75% of the playtime is just waiting for our "great detectives" to catch up. Kind of agonizing to have to sit through a story when you already know where it's going.The Scout backstory, while initially interesting, doesn't end up living up to the initial level of interest because you can figure out what's going on pretty early and then you're just watching a foregone conclusion play out.Don't even get me started on that annoying "smack" sound effect that plays with a screen shake on what feels like 75% of the events. Sets my teeth on edge. Dramatic effects should be used sparingly to highlight moments of actual drama. Here, these effects are totally oversaturated to the point of becoming meaningless.I really appreciate some of what they did in case 3, and the art is generally quite good (with a few notable exceptions that were cringe for a professional game), but this doesn't make up for the general issues in terms of writing quality and how annoying the gameplay can be. It's a real slog to get through, not a fun and engaging story with bonus puzzles thrown in.Glad the achievements were easy to get, though, so now I can uninstall and never think about it again. (The setup for the sequel at the end... I'll pass.)Also, my playtime is inflated because I left the game running overnight. Whoops.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. I have always been a fan of picross/nonogram games and I have been looking for a picross game with a good story for a long time. The music is fantastic, the art is great and the mysteries are fun to solve. The game reminds me a lot of Ace Attorney, the investigative elements are very similar.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: If you like visual novels, murder mysteries, and picross puzzles, then you'll probably like this game. There is one thing that I would personally like to make the puzzles a little more convenient: an undo button to undo the last move you made. Besides that one very small potential improvement, I really enjoyed this game for both the stories in each case and the picross puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game thoroughly! The balance of puzzles/visual novel segments is wonderful. Every time I was feeling like doing a puzzle again, one appeared! This type of puzzle between sudoku and crosswords is very fun.You get attached to the characters, and overall this game feels like a true labour of love for the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this game, but it's hard to really justify a recommendation. The biggest problem with the game is that the campaign is basically 16 hours of 15x15 picrosses spliced with four hours of story. You will spend the majority of your time with this game playing the same exact type of puzzle with no attempts to make them feel different. If that alone isn't enough to turn you off, you'll probably end up enjoying the game. I found the puzzles to be challenging but fair, although according to some reviews this will be too easy for picross veterans. Having finished the game 100%, I can confirm that you will never need to guess, despite what some reviews implied. The music is good, although the game's insistence on only using a few select themes for puzzles ruins most of the game's dramatic moments and will eventually make you get sick of the puzzle tunes. The story, characters, and especially comedy are very hit-or-miss. Honestly, this game lives or dies on whether you can have fun with the incredibly repetitive gameplay loop, and I just don't think very most people will enjoy it for very long.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: What a brilliant little gem of a game.I bought this as a throwaway, it was cheap, figured I'd get 8-10 hours if I was lucky, with minimal expectations.  What I got was 25 hours of satisfying gameplay, an amusing (if not Starshine-winning) story and a guaranteed buy of the inevitable sequel.The puzzles themselves end up being satisfactory -- at first I thought they were all going to be too easy, then it looked like they were going to ramp up into some real challenge, and though they never QUITE got really difficult (with the exception of 2 or 3 15x20 puzzles at the end, they topped out at 15x15), there were so MANY of them that I couldn't complain.If I had one nit to pick, it's the sound/music design.  The sound was .. functional.  A few more sound effects in the story part of the game to decrease the repetitiveness would have been nice.  The music was actually enjoyable, but just not enough tracks.  I spent ~18 hours doing puzzles, with about 5 tracks total repeating during that.  Needed a few more.Don't let my minor negatives distract though, this was an excellent game.  Looking forward to more.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, the reason why I bought this game was because i was wanting some more picross in my life.  There's something relaxing about solving these puzzles - you have to be methodical and take your time.That being said, I wasn't planning on loving the story as much as I did.  I am a fan of visual novels as well, but I just assumed I was just going to keep skipping the dialog to get to the next puzzle.  From the opening "in your face" movie (and music) to Scout and Honor's infectious attitudes, it really drew me in.  They're super likable and there are a surprising number of quotable and heartfelt moments.I did have some downsides, but none of them were enough to warrant not buying this game.- The music was very upbeat and fun, however it does get repetitive when solving puzzles.  I turned it off about half way through (and found that turning it off turns off even the opening movie)- This is sorta spoiler-ish but  - There's no option to skip or fast forward the story.  I don't recommend skipping the story the first time, but if I wanted to go back to replay the game, it would be a bit of a pain.Overall, I really appreciated this game for both the story and puzzles.  It took me about 40 hours to get through the 4 cases plus the extras.  Well worth the money paid.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: The writing is aggressively awful, and the game makes you sit through a ton of it.  I don't mean, like, "this isn't the kind of story I like" or "I wanted something deeper" or "a mystery game should make some sense"... I mean it was done poorly in every way.  The dialog is so terrible and low-effort that it feels like it's a placeholder that they never got around to replacing.  The game's idea of humor is to present a character with a quirk... and that's it.  Like, the maintenance guy is a jock, and his dialog is pretty much "I like to work out!  We should boink, then I will lift some weights again because I'm obsessed with my muscles."  This isn't like, lowbrow humor that I'm too good for or something - it's just nothing.  It's just no-thought garbage.  Again, it's like they had art drawn up of these characters (the art is fine!) and they decided they had to fill 30 text boxes of "conversation" - but they ran out of time before they thought of anything to say.The actual mysteries are, not-surprisingly-at-this-point, piss poor.  If the game intended you to, like, solve a mystery with clues that would be cool.  Or if the story was wacky chaos nonsense to set up funny moments, that would be fine too.  But it is somehow neither.  It just kind of wanders around some "mystery story tropes", with characters behaving randomly, until you do the next puzzle......that they made no effort to fit into the story.  It's not like, "oh, I scan the scene and I think there might be a safe behind this picture" or "I can see a trail of blood leading to this air vent".  No, you just swoosh your cursor around until it turns red.  Oh look, there's an apple on the side of this desk.  There's an invisible doll on this floor.  I guess?Lastly, it's not even a good Picross game.  They somehow made the controls awkward, and the difficulty varies randomly.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: If you like picross games and visual novels, then this game will be right up your alley. The production values are pretty high, the writing is overall good, and it's got quite a lot of content for the price point (my guess at this point is about a dozen hours to complete all four acts plus the bonus puzzles, but it might be more).
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game on a sale and it's been sitting in my library for a bit.Anyways... This game just oozes charm all over the place, and it has taught me how to play pi cross!  The characters are fun and the plot has kept me going!  I quite like everything here so far.  Great puzzles, great characters, and great (if insane) plot so far.Though, in chapter 4 the puzzles all become 15 by 15 at pretty much all times.  It's hard to keep up with the story at this point because I'm in the puzzles so long, that by the time I come out, I've completely forgotten characters, clues, etc.  Those 15 by 15 seriously take up a long time.If anything changes, I'll update this review, if not, just know this is for sure a game worth getting.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I'm always on the lookout for good, simple puzzle games that can be an easy distraction after work. This fits the bill to a tee. I'm about 1/3 of the way through the main story (maybe less), and it's cheesy in a way I really love. More than that, the puzzle-solving has me very addicted, and I'm finding this difficult to put down.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I was expecting a nice mix of puzzles and mystery, all I got was a snooze-fest. The story is extremely boring and written for teenagers; I was just skipping text because the characters are a walking cliché. The game has four cases that keep moving at a snail’s pace towards a bland conclusion. Puzzles are equally tedious and feel forced into the game. The game would actually work better as a VN without the nanograms; at least then you’d know what you’re getting yourself into.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Right off the bat I want to say that if you enjoy puzzle mystery games then this is an easy recommend. The music, art, and writing are great and if you want some puzzles to chill out with then pick this game up without a second thought. To give more then a few other thoughts however, this game is very good however due to that fact, the aspects where it falls a bit standout quite a lot. The story was enjoyable but it goes for the big breakdowns in Ace Attorney and it doesn't really work (This game is actually a lot like Ace Attorney).  Because there really isn't a lead up to the trial you don't have time for things to simmer. It's like trying to squish the drama of the trails and characterization of the investigations into one.Another minor gripe is that there are timed puzzles. They are very easy, but it makes me wonder why would you put them in the game if you knew they'd be an issue if they weren't super easy. It didn't really add any suspense in the story for it to switch from a relaxing puzzle game that I can take my time with into something that just kinda felt annoying.My biggest criticism of this game is that the pacing is awful, all because of the puzzles. There is one moment (no real spoilers here) where someone hands you a business card and you need to complete a long puzzle to see that it's a business card. WHY? It would be one thing if it was really easy and the difficulty of the puzzle was based off of the item, but it's a constant issue with this game. Plenty of big suspenseful moments are murdered by this (although it does help a few).Can't stress that I really enjoyed this game, and I think it's 100% worth it. The issues stick out because everything else extremely well made. It's wonderful :)

_childDocuments_.review: CAUTION! If you have migraines, epilepsy or any kind of sensitivity for flashing lights. This game has white flashes and screen shakings ALL THE TIME, sometimes multiple in a row.Due to the effects being a feature you can't turn off, i can't recommend this game. It's also missing quality of life things visual novels should have, like skipping text or a backlog. Missing puzzles means you have to click through all of the text in a case.In case 1 characters annoyed me, especially Becky. Surprisingly she became my favorite later, and I warmed up to the characters.

_childDocuments_.review: Brief Review:I took about 19 hours to complete this game. It is an interesting way to develop a game about Picross - by linking Picross to the robot sidekick SCOUT, the game of Picross itself takes on a different character. I also appreciated the time-based Picross challenges, although I wish the developers would throw you more than 5 to complete (especially when the stakes in the narrative are high.)I think the game does suffer from a lack of strong characters and/or narrative. As a Phoenix Wright-inspired game, the game also follows the 'core' of Phoenix Wright - Honor, SCOUT, Detective Cross. But that is where the similarity ends, for better or for worse. Cross is very similar to Gumshoe, yes, but KC is no Larry. The characters also don't get enough time to be as fleshed out. I feel as though some of the episodes were written to allow for side characters to be featured in, for instance Case 3 for KC (marginally).  Nonetheless, I appreciate the LGBTQIA+ friendly content in this game, and that is quite novel for such a game. The narrative based on SCOUT seems a bit forced - we only catch glimpses of it throughout, and the rest of the narrative is entirely isolated from SCOUT's character arc (of sorts). I felt like the game could also be longer in terms of narrative - perhaps a 5 case structure would be better (and allows for characters to be fleshed out too)I also think there could be more music. Especially where the stakes are high, the music should be more intense and ideally different. (e.g. when you are hacking, the music should be thrilling and not idyllic).  Characters should also get their own themes where possible, just to make them stand out more. One final issue is that although the Picross puzzles were good, towards the end I found myself getting tired of doing the Picross puzzles. Perhaps some more variation towards the end would be good. Overall I would give the game a 7/10. It's good for beginners to Picross and the narrative is not the worst, but I think it would be best to play the game in small blocks to not tire yourself out.

_childDocuments_.review: What a lazy game.The premise is reasonable: you play as a robot, finding clues to solve murder mysteries using Nonogram puzzles. So much could have been done with this concept, and so little actually was.Despite some stand-out creative character designs, the unanimated, sticker-style, graphics are just bland and boring for the most part. The music is repetitive, and there are mabye 5 total sound effects, which get reused, throughout the entire game. The puzzles are mostly unrewarding, and become tedious, as you as the player become more of a robot than the actual robot character in the game. After finish each puzzle, it's visually impossible to tell what most of the images are until the caption appears to identify it. The devs clearly did not spend much time on any of these components, but that's OK (I mean, it's a Nonogram game) if the story is decent.The story is fine, especially considering the genre, and the target audience. The settings, with their associated backdrops, are interesting. There's a lot of gender-positivity in the story, and it flows naturally from the dialogue. However, the final chapter is written terribly. The quality of the writing plummets, and gets worse as the chapter continues. An eccentric character's poetry attempts to provide cryptic intrigue, but in reality it gives inanity instead of subtlety. A sequel hook is hastily crammed into the final lines of dialogue after the credits roll, as if you were watching a Marvel movie.I can't stress this point enough: this game is just , and is light on graphics, music and sounds. The only thing that makes it different in the genre is that it has a story, and the big climax that the whole story builds up to could have been drunkenly jotted down in crayon on a napkin at 3AM as the writers Murray Lewis and Ed Fear got kicked out of a karaoke bar.It's fitting that this game features on free accessories in . It should be relegated to exist only as a texture on a mousepad in a virtual world.(I received this game as part of a )

_childDocuments_.review: First thing to note, at the time of review I have not completed the game. Might edit later.The writing in the game is excellent. It's funny, but it's usually presented in a realistic manner. The characters can be pretty exaggerated, but the dialogue feels very natural to the character. The main gameplay however, is in the Picross puzzles. They fit perfectly into the world as a game mechanic, as SCOUT, the robot scans an object and tries to determine what it is. I can't say for sure about later on, but in early levels there are no twists to the Picross formula. They are regular Picross puzzles that you could find in hundreds of different mobile games. However, these puzzles are accompanied with some stellar music, so this is clearly the superior choice.I do have 2 things that I dislike, one big, one small.The big problem, for me at least, is that you are only able to access the pause menu at a certain screen. In other words, should you need to mess with the settings or save and quit during and you're mid dialogue or something, you can't. Maybe I'm missing a keybind somewhere, but all the usual buttons didn't work.The second problem I have is with the way the mouse works. There is a game mechanic where the robot, SCOUT, needs to scan the environment. You move the camera with the mouse and click. The issue is that your actual mouse is still visible and still moves. Couple that with the fact that the mouse is not locked into the window and my mouse moved out onto the 2nd monitor.I presume it's even more annoying if you're playing in windowed mode.Besides those 2 problems, the game's great. So far.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a fan of picross puzzle games for a long time, but haven't played a game that weaves in such a detailed story. _childDocuments_.review: (This review contains mild spoilers)Overall Murder by Numbers is a fun game with an entertaining story and a very diverse cast of characters. I had a lot of fun with it. Unfortunately, despite my enjoyment, i simply cannot recommend this game to anyone else.First off, a core issue with this game is the overwhelming amount of puzzles: The game is divided in 4 cases, and you have to complete more than 110 puzzles! (Yes, i counted) Which become extremely repetitive, draining and tiring after some point. That, by itself, makes it difficult to recommend the game to anyone i know, as even the ones that love murder mysteries and fun stories would feel annoyed at the massive amount of minigames that must be completed over and over again. If the developers had added a ''skip'' option for those puzzles, this game wouldn't even last 5 hours. Besides the core gameplay issues, the execution of the story was not very satisfying: Some of the recurring characters, which make an appearance in multiple cases,(excluding Honor, SCOUT, and offic- i mean, Detective Cross) do not go through any real character development: You get to know a biiit more about some, but at the end of their spotlight moment, not only they remain the same person they were before, but they also do not reappear in the following chapter, which i find to be a wasted opportunity to display some character growth.----------mild spoilers start here-------------I was also not satisfied with the way some of the killers were handled. One of the killers only became a killer accidentally, yet, the game equates that person to the culprits who commited premeditated murder(as if the circumstances and context don't matter, only the end result: they caused someone's death). And, worse yet, is that the characters, and by extension the writers, don't seem able to display empathy towards what led any of the murders to actually happen. All they do is brush them off as horrible people and go celebrate because...another case was solved and that's all that matters i guess. Who cares whether the killer suffered decades of abuse which led them to take their abuser's life? We ain't got time for empathy here in LA.Overall i give it a 4/10. Actually, i will give it a 3/10 because the legendary HATO MOA(hatoful boyfriend) worked on this game, yet the developers didn't have her draw a single bird portrait! Not one! How can you hire her for this and not have a single majestic bird appear on my screen? Yet another disappointment to add to the list.If the developers intend on making a sequel, as is implied by the end, i will only consider buying it if the amount of puzzles is significantly tuned down. I would not mind playing through another adventure with these characters, but i DO mind if i have to jump from one puzzle to another every 5 minutes, and feel like i am playing a mobile game that tells me to watch an ad before i can progress with the story.

_childDocuments_.review: I have misophonia & auditory overstimulatiom, and this game has constant "punch" noises for every other line spoken... it's bizarre and incredibly distracting / irritating. And I really do mean constant. Not to mention the neverending screen flashing for no reason. I've seen photosensitive players mention how this makes the game unplayable for them, but the devs never provided the option to turn this feature off. And it's just as common as the punch noises. I turned off the sound effects, which helped me complete the game at least.The story was also very mediocre, unbelievable, and... lazy. >< I've never left a bad review before, but I felt compelled to for this one just because of the lack of accessibility options with no other redeeming features. If you really love nonograms, though, you'll probably enjoy it because this game has a ton of them. :D

_childDocuments_.review: For fans of Picross who also want a bit of story, this is pretty solid!After a quick tutorial on nonograms/picross, most puzzles will run from 5x5 to 15x15 in size, with one 20x15 at the end to test you. There are also a few "Hacking" picross sequences-- they don't form a picture, but are timed to see if you can quickly place lines of 1 to 5 in a 5x5 area multiple times within a minute or so. For players who know how Picross plays, none of these puzzles are ever terribly hard, but are still fun to go through! Once you complete all the missions at S rank, there's some additional puzzles to reforge SCOUT's memory, which is a nice bonus on top of an already hefty amount of puzzles. (I think some puzzles are optional and missable and can prevent an S rank? So make sure "Investigation" is grayed out before you question people!)You then use the puzzles, or evidence as it were, to question individuals and solve cases. This itself is kind of shallow, for lack of a better word, as it's usually pretty obvious what you want to present, to whom, and when. You also can never be wrong about something, so it's really more a gate to make sure the player has found the required puzzles, which may involve needing to jump between different rooms. In the future, say a second game, it'd be nice to see this part fleshed out a bit (with an option to maybe disable it for those who don't want the detective side of this)!The story is engaging enough, though it's usually pretty obvious who is the culprit just based on the situation and characters. The characters are all nicely drawn, written pretty well -- the main protagonists are especially endearing, I found -- and the backgrounds are detailed and fantastic. The UI is clear and easy to read, never getting in your way and fitting the aesthetic well. The soundtrack is pleasant, though can get repetitive in puzzles since there aren't -too- many tracks that differ, and you'll hear the same tune whether you're on the street or in a high security building. For those who hunt achievements, there are only four, and they only check for case completion, so you don't need to stress for 100% unless you really, really want more puzzling!Ultimately, that's sort of how I feel about Murder by Numbers. It's not outstanding or groundbreaking, but it meshes story with puzzle solving in a unique way that picross players, new or experienced, can enjoy, while its case solving could use some fleshing out in a sequel. I would absolutely pay for additional case DLCs, or even a whole second game, myself! The game ran me a bit over 14 hours, so for $15 USD, I think this is a solid purchase, even outside of a sale.You can -count- on having a good, chill time here!(And hey, developers: Thanks for the LGBTQ+ representation in case 3, and in K.C. throughout, who was a personal favorite of mine. Much love, ya'll. <3)

I won't knock it for that, some people will really love it, but after beating the main storyline (and maybe 90% of all the side puzzles) i'm relieved to not do these puzzles again for a long time

_childDocuments_.review: If you love picross, you'll love this game. I'm not a big picross fangirl myself, but the puzzles are fun and challenging (also be sure to use a mouse during the hacking minigames, using the touch pad was torturous).Overall, I liked the story and the characters were fun. _childDocuments_.review: Visuals- Amazing Art and Character motions and mannerisms for a visual novel. GreatMusic- Awesome tracks, a lot of Ace Attorney Vibes but fresh.GreatGameplay- Picross with Hidden Object. But the Hidden Object part is too simplistic and the green look with the beeping detracts from the visuals. The Picross puzzle also was not very challenging. Perfect balance to keep the story flow.Still Good.Story- A bit too straight forward, not much in terms of intricacy or plot twists. Still Good.Programming & Design - The Menus are a bit buggy. No Controller Support but can easily be mapped with Steam Controller configs. The Picross puzzles abruptly change the music from the perfectly nice serious tunes of a scene to the 3 same repetative fun tunes. The music is nice but don't understand why the Puzzle sections need to throw us out of the mood of the scene. It would have been great to have done the puzzles under the more serious music in the last chapter. OkayDefinitely recommended to anyone waiting for a new Ace Attorney, or love playing Picross.Also a great starting point for those interested in getting into Visual Novels or Picross.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was amazing. The story and characters are extremely well written and thought out. I also love the specific puzzle type that this game uses, and I think the difficulties of the puzzles increase at an appropriate rate. My main warning would be to not try to binge and finish the game as soon as possible and as quickly as possible. I have 42 hours in like 3 or 4 days. I was starting to burn out because there are so many difficult puzzles towards the end, and then there are extra bonus puzzles for side content that I also finished. I still enjoyed everything about the game, but I should have chilled and taken it slowly to enjoy it more, and I suggest you all do so as well.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games I want to like and started out liking but suffers from the problem of the core gameplay, that being picross puzzles and mystery solving, aren't very good.   First off the puzzles start out pretty fun but.. by case 2 and 3 they get to be annoying. Not hard, not difficult, just annoying. They pop up way too often breaking the pace of the story but also often don't really seem.. completely solvable with just logic? Often I would get 1/3 or 1/2 of the puzzle completed and then run out of logical steps to complete the rest. Grids would be filled with single dots in a sea of blanks that could reasonably have been anywhere. Resulting pictures would look nothing like anything, even after the puzzle completed with color to 'reveal' what it was.  When your picross puzzle neither looks like an actual picture, nor looks solvable without just brute forcing/using tips then its not really that fun.  Actualy mystery part also kinda falls flat. You don't actually.. deduce anything in this mystery game. You just throw evidence in the face of everyone you meet until they spit out the line of text you need to proceed and continue from there. There is no "You got it wrong, case failed" or "you only got so much time to figure this out before they get away" You again just at worst have to brute force it trying every option with no actual stakes for getting things wrong. Also the mysteries themselves.. seem pretty obvious for the most part. You usually can tell who the killer is before your even a 3rd of the way though but you still stumble around looking at other people and following dead ends all the same. Another problem this game has is that its representation.. kinda... isn't great.. More than a few seem to come off as little more than exaggerated stereotypes and some of the information it puts out there is.. dubious at best? But it seems so proud of itself for the inclusion it does but I'm just sitting here for a lot of it kinda going "okay this is really cringy and wrong and i hope they move on from it quickly." I dunno. Thats just how i feel. I want to complete it just to see the end of the sub-story about one of the main characters but its not.. its not really making me want to play it for any other reason.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the main story and I have to say, I am obsessed with this game. I enjoyed the dynamic of SCOUT and Honor's relationship as it developed throughout the game. The storyline touches some sensitive topics, so be aware of that if you get anxious about situations surrounding emotional abuse or gaslighting especially, as other reviews have said. The Picrosses were very enjoyable, and I loved that they were built into the evidence collection mechanic, rather than the devs putting the Picrosses where they may be inappropriate to the setting of the game. I intend on completing all of the extra puzzles that are unlocked through playing the main story.That being said, I also found the game frustrating at points. After I finished Mission 3, I realized that I had missed a piece of optional evidence, meaning I wasn't able to unlock all of "Scout's Memories", which all also include a unique cutscene. Missing out on a single piece of evidence is detrimental for players who feel like they want to 100% this game, as there is no way to go back and do an individual picross in the main storyline without re-doing the whole Mission. There seems to be a bit of loose ends surrounding Honor's father as well as the cliff-hanger that occurs right at the end of the storyline on Mission 4. This suggests that the devs may be in the process of making a Murder by Numbers 2, which I really hope they do. Although some QoL changes could be made for a sequel, I thoroughly enjoyed this game. I strongly recommend it to anyone who like deductive logic and/or puzzles like sudoku ; you'll pick it up quick.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: The decision to bring in the guy behind Ghost Trick and Ace Attorney's soundtracks single-handedly saves this game from mediocrity.Getting bored of the picross? Joke's on you, the music makes it fun anyway. Turn up the volume and start bouncing to the beat in your chair.Getting bored of the simple and predictable mysteries? Doesn't matter, Masakazu Sugimori's music is still gonna send chills down your spine when you pin down the suspect.It's just a shame about the rest of the game though—all the negative reviews are right. It's obviously designed for beginners of the genre, and the writing reads like fanfiction at times. The picross segments are about as common as puzzles in Layton games, which can be good or bad depending on your interest. (just play the game on easy mode, it just makes the picross puzzles a bit more convenient)But if you're willing to play a game just to jam out to its tunes? This is the game for you.Edit: Okay, as predictable as the story can be, case 4 made me tear up a bit. The main characters both play into the game's theme about losing control over yourself and your identity. Good casual picross game with a heartwarming detective drama attached.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I will recommend this with one big caveat - most of your time in this game will be spent playing picross. If you like picross enough that you're willing to spend dozens of hours on it, with only small story rewards as you progress, you'll like this game.  If, on the other hand, you were hoping for something with a story-to-puzzle ratio more like Ace Attorney, or even Professor Layton, you'll probably lose patience with Murder By Numbers somewhere about 20 hours in.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall enjoyable puzzle game with engaging story and good representation.Story playthrough took me 24 hours playtime, but its very dependant on how good/familiar you are with the puzzles and how quickly you take them.I had never heard of pictocross before this game, but I got this in the 2021 Jingle Jam Games collection and decided to try it out.The game eases you into pictocross while setting up an engaging story and fun cast of characters. As the puzzle difficulty increased, I stuck with it even when I got frustrated because I wanted to see the next part of the story.
