_childDocuments_.review: EARLY REVIEW: I've only completed the first chapter of this game so far, but I'm immediately hooked. I'm not a huge fan of visual novels, but I AM a huge fan of Picross games, and I've been looking for something to scratch the itch of a Picross game with some sort of progression besides "harder puzzles".The writing in this game is pretty good so far. The dialogue is maybe a little tropey, but it's clear the writers were having fun and I'm enjoyin the story. As for the actual mystery in the story, it's unfolding at a nice pace with some early twists and turns, red herrings, the usual mystery fare... but executed very well.As for the Picross puzzles themselves, it's too early to really comment on them. I have hundreds of hours across multiple nonogram games, so the puzzles at this stage are not really a challenge, I'm mostly in it for the story. I will say that I've encountered one timed puzzle so far, which could shake things up later on.My one suggestion for the devs would be to maybe allow a skip of the initial puzzle tutorial in a future update. It was short, but a little annoying to be taught the basic rules of the game without a skip option, and no way to interact besides clicking through dialogue boxes. Maybe only add the skip option for players on Normal difficulty, or make the board interactable so that you can just solve the puzzle and skip the tutorial?Either way, I'm really enjoying this game so far, and I'm excited to get back to it. If you love Picross and want a story-focused game that lets you solve Picross puzzles, this is it. If you're into murder mysteries and/or visual novels, but you haven't ever played Picross before, then this game seems like a great onboarding for the genre of nonogram puzzlers with a promising visual novel to boot.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game about a detective who is inevitably going to get all of his cases thrown out by having a civilian and her robot friend break the evidence chain of custody and contaminate crime scenes.But seriously, this is a very fun game. It's basically the casual puzzle game Picross with a detective story around it. If you don't like Picross, leave now, because that's a great majority of the gameplay. The rest of the game is searching for clues in a crime scene, questioning witnesses, and presenting the evidence you find to further the case or debunk alibis. Your robot pal, SCOUT, is the one doing the scanning of crime scene, which translates to the Picross stuff, the final solution being a pixelated picture of the clue. Difficulty of the puzzles increases as you progress, so by the end you are doing more difficult 15x15 puzzles that take a lot more critical thinking to solve than the early ones.There are four chapters with four different cases, and before I started playing them I imagined that the cases would be 1) completely unrelated, with only the main character to link between them or 2) all done by some criminal mastermind, which is what a lot of detective games do to justify the disparate cases. This game fits in a happy medium, where there are characters, plots, character development and foreshadowing to tie all the cases together in a coherent, story-driven way without seeming completely implausible. The robot sidekick also has a backstory and arc, which I absolutely did not expect but it really ties the gimmick of the robot/Picross into the emotion of the story.I played about 20 hours, including all of the bonus levels, which are harder puzzles than the ones in game (compared to the episode they're unlocked after). Just the main storyline took about 10 hours. However, since Episode 1 has the easiest puzzle, it only took me an hour, Episode 2's puzzles were harder so it took about 2 hours, etc. Each episode has about the same amount of non-Picross investigation, questioning, etc. so all that extra time really is from the puzzles so if you don't like Picross you won't enjoy this game because that's the bulk of the time.All in all, a very fun puzzle game with a surprisingly well-done story.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: First things first: my play time is not accurate. I would often get up and get distracted doing other things since there's no time penalties or time related achievements. Secondly: it's very common to miss a puzzle in chapter 3 and missing it prevents you from getting S Rank. Make sure you check your locations after speaking to the other characters to make sure SCOUT doesn't have more he can investigate in the area. Like others have pointed out, it's more Ace Attorney than Picross, but unlike Ace Attorney the stories are more straight forward. I found myself solving a lot of the "crimes" very early on while Honor was coming up with sometimes outlandish theories and putting the wrong person in custody. But Honor doesn't have the benefit of knowing she's in a video game, so you just kind of have to go along for the ride.  The character design is the biggest reason for the mysteries feeling flat. They're charming but they're also often too on the nose: if they look like a criminal, they're a criminal. I mean, the loan shark literally looks like a shark.Still, if you enjoy Picross and would enjoy reading a story with Ace Attorney Lite style mysteries, it's worth getting on sale at the very least.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun for the first 30-40 puzzles, but it's get repetitive very soon. Unfortunately the story becomes more and more interesting and you feel like puzzles are annoying. There's no real "easy" mode as it just shows you where you're wrong right when you do the move, and the later puzzles are too complex themselves (a lot of empty spaces and you need to look for contradictions etc)First part -- terrific, last part I was mainly doing "hints"-based solving: when you disclose enough random squares the puzzle becomes easy enough to go through. Play this on youtube and see for yourself
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Came for the Moa Hato character designs, stayed for the puzzles.Detective/puzzle game combo is an old classic, and works just as well here. As far as the puzzles go, there's a pretty good range, just don't expect to actually see what you're drawing. Aside from that, only real con is that the UX could use some polish, it's very mouse-centred (you actually have to click the button to get to the menu for example, rather than a keyboard shortcut) which makes it feel a bit like a mobile port, but it's not a big deal.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: *Murder by Numbers**Rating* (5 out of 5 stars)*Pros:**Cute story and likable characters, the puzzles are fun and can get challenging without the hints, and it is a great game to kill time.*Cons:*I can’t think of any, puzzles are not too difficult for me and you can always use the hint feature*Recommendation:*Murdered by Numbers" is an excellent choice for those seeking a fun and portable puzzle game. It's perfect for playing in short intervals, and the sense of accomplishment from solving each puzzle is incredibly satisfying. Give it a try for a great brain exercise and an enjoyable gaming experience!*Summary:*Murdered by Numbers is a delightful puzzle game with a charming story and lovable characters. The game offers engaging and challenging puzzles perfect for playing on the go. With a hint feature available, players can choose to use it or rely on their problem-solving skills to progress through the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Fun characters, an engaging story and a phenomenal soundtrack had me hooked on this game from beginning to end. The gameplay is standard nonogram/picross mixed with an investigation/interaction phase à la  Professor Layton or Phoenix Wright. It's pretty straightforward as you're essentially just exhausting dialogue trees and solving all available puzzles in order to move the story along, however the writing is enjoyably humorous and with just enough intrigue to keep you guessing and serves as a nice breather in between puzzles.If you don't enjoy picross gameplay, or if you don't enjoy reading through long excerpts of dialogue then you probably won't enjoy this game. However if, like me, you enjoy both this game will keep you effortlessly entertained.Should there be any sort of sequel I'd love to see an expansion on the investigative/murder mystery part of the game with more options to interrogate and discern clues as opposed to its current, more visual novel approach.(Received as part of the Jingle Jam bundle)
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent title, especially for people who enjoy puzzles. The story, while somewhat reliant on tropes(a common trait of detective stories) is quite engaging, and makes for an excllent diversion between the pictures. You play as an amateur detective accompanied by a stray robot, and every puzzle you solve is a clue leading you to the solution of the case. The game does very well at building suspense and capitalising on the tempo. I really appreciate how there is an overlapping plot that's advancing between every case and how well the story is structured. It really feels extremely polished and complete.The game takes utmost care to be accessible, with hints and a gradual increase in difficulty. As a seasoned puzzle solver, i didn't need the hints at all, got a perfect score every time, and felt slightly understimulated towards the end, but I finished the game for the story. The hardest puzzles reach just 15x20 grids, so no complex math is involved, or anything like that. The music felt cheerful and engaging, which made every session very pleasant, while the artstyle is very cute and distinct.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I like Picross, so combining this Murder Detective element with it was fun, for sure. My only beef is that if you don't get a perfect score the first time around-- for any reason be it playing on easy, or needing hints.. you can't just replay the puzzles to improve your score - you have to sit through the chapter again. Fine-- some visual novel games have you do that.. but! there's no fast forward option! You can make the text go faster but you still have to click periodically to move along the speech-- (and that's ignoring that you still have to talk/present items to trigger the story, or select dialogue options cuz hey that sometimes happens in visual novel type games but ATLEAST they give you the option of speeding through the previously read text-- stopping only when there's something that needs your input or new dialogue). It makes 100%ing the game more of a chore that it needs to be. I wish they would add some update to fix it-- either a FF option or just access to replaying the puzzles to up the score! It would vastly improve the replayability imho.Oh and they did Honor dirty with that weird 80's print paired with plaid lmao, but that's more of a personal gripe and less a game review.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting mix of minesweeper and sudoku gameplay which will leave you crunching the gear box of a brain over many hours. Love the game mechanics, the story line however can be a bit cliche at times but is actually quite interesting over the four chapters. You play as Honor with your companion Scout to solve a series of murders via a hybrid visual novel style progress with puzzle solving elements in between. Recommended if you have some time and want a bit of mental challenge for a few hours, puzzles generally aren't too hard, there's also a hint system if you are stuck.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I like the puzzle concept here enough that I initially tolerated the buggy controls, not knowing whether they were the fault of the game itself or my own hardware.But when I found myself reaching a prog-stopping bug before I could even get far enough into the story to develop an opinion how much the visual novel portions are cute vs. cringe, at that point I had to call it quits.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good game, wish it was on mobile.This is a fun game with an interesting concept. You solve crimes by solving picross/nonogram puzzles. Kinda fun in an Ace Attorney style.The story and writing are a bit weird at times. The story takes place in 1996, and sometimes it feels like it was written in the 90's and put in a time capsule. It's kinda tropey and cliched so far too. It's starting to get a little bit better, but I just solved the first case and I'm just now starting to see chemistry between the characters. Compared to Ace Attorney or Ghost Trick, that's a pretty slow burn.The Picross gameplay is alright. You scan the room you're in with your SCOUT robot buddy, and there's a simple homing system to let you find clues. Once you find a clue, you have to solve a puzzle to find out what it is. Then the clue gets added to your evidence log like in Ace Attorney and you can present evidence to people while questioning them to cue different actions. So far having just finished case 1 of 4, the evidence presenting puzzles aren't really that challenging. Often you're hinted at pretty heavily who to show the evidence to to advance the story. It's pretty much a straight up take on Picross so far. The main puzzles are pure picross, just like any phone game you might download. The puzzles aren't timed, not even just for your own curiosity or challenge. Hints are available if you need them. There are some different challenges here and there, there's a hacking minigame where you have to solve a series of puzzles under a time limit without using any "X"s to cross out boxes you don't want to fill in. It's a welcome change of pace, but so far not very frequent.So far it's a fairly diverting game, not really pushing the envelope, but enjoyable for what it is. I really wish it was on mobile (iOS specifically) because it's a perfect lazy day game. If the core concept intrigues you, then the execution is pretty good if maybe a bit predictable and cliched at times. But anyone who watches a lot of procedural tv shows will get pretty good at spotting the murderer before the first commercial break, so I can forgive Murder by Numbers on that count.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: The writing is shallow, cheesy, and EXTREMELY stereotypical-anime, lacking any twists and with character designs that tend to beat you over the head with 'this person is a villain'.The puzzles are solid, but the controls NEED some polishing elements (specifically like being able to hold down the 'mark' button to REMOVE marks, WITHOUT also clearing populated X and Fill squares). Could also use a solve-timer, just for your own information.Achievements could be GREATLY expanded from the sad four currently in place (just beating each case, not even a separate one for S-ranking, or S-ranking all cases!) as well as hidden achievements like choosing to be a jerk in dialog options.Worth the pick-up if you enjoy nonogram puzzles and don't mind minor annoyances when solving them. A gripping story though, it is not. At all.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Picross - this game is fantastic! Clever writing combined with a large collection of Picross minigames, basically all of which are optimized for fun.I was worried at first about the small Picross grids making things too easy, but they worked in the right amount of challenging puzzles even so... and it let them keep the interface really sharp.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. If you like Nonograms you are usually stuck to puzzle collections without any story. Here, we get the best of both world, nifty puzzles, and a cool story with grown-up thematics. I loved the diversity and the characters are pure gold. Would love to see a sequel with Scout and Honor in their own detective agency! Go. buy and enjoy
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: It's Picross with a fairly simplistic visual novel attached to it. Not much else to say. The story choices are arbitrary as it is impossible to proceed in a way that doesn't advance the story along its singular path. There is no penalty for incorrect deductions either, it's really just set dressing. It's fun, but the heart of the game is in the puzzles. If you don't like Picross, you won't like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

I've tried updating hardware drivers, reinstalling, restarting, and disabling devices. _childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Tough one to review. I'm giving it a thumbs up because it's well made and does what it intends to do very well. However... I didn't personally enjoy it and won't continue playing. I love picross games and very much enjoyed the puzzles, but the visual novel aspect (which I generally find a bit too dull in a game - give me a proper book instead!) is too intrusive - it felt that was the focus of the game and the puzzles were incidental. That's fine, I just didn't expect it.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like nonograms?  Also known as Hanjie or griddlers (the largest was 20x5), Yes? then this is probably for you. Not put off by a linear story line  you progress by solving puzzles and talking to all characters until you release new content or areas. Yes, then this is definitely for you. It'll probably take you about 10-12 hours to beat. I took 25 hrs to beat it twice because the first time I used a few assists to finish up some late game puzzles that I'd messed up due to tiredness and didn't want to restart. However using assists costs you points , which ultimately means you don't get all the bonus scout puzzles to solve and see the memories. Periodically there were hacking puzzles, timed sets of puzzles to solve, never more than 5x5 than a lot of people in the discussions didn't like, but for the rest of the puzzles take as long as you like. The game   suggests you look for known pattern that fill a 5 length line (5,31,13,22,or111), .I enjoyed playing this and feel I definitely got my moneys worth, but I probably will never play it again. However if there was a sequel or further cases I'd be interested.

_childDocuments_.review: A great puzzle game with an interesting story.  Murder by numbers is, at it's heart, a picross game.  If you hate picross, you're not going to enjoy yourself.  If, however, you like these puzzles like I do, the developers have wrapped a great set of picross puzzles up with an engaging and well told story.  I really enjoyed every hour I put into solving all the puzzles, and I would like to add that at no place in the puzzles do you have to guess.  The puzzles are well designed so you can always figure it out.So - for a fun story with great characters wrapped around a great set of puzzles, check this game out.  It's worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Wouldn't recommend this to anyone looking for a casual or relaxing puzzle game and if you're buying just as a visual novel/ for the story I'd honestly recommend Ace Attorney or Aviary Attorney first. That said, I dig the combo and the devs have done well given their size: not a lot to complain about and what is advertised is largely what you get.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Note: I'm basing my opinion on the first half of the game as I'm not getting around to the second half. Unsure if the story improves towards the end of the game or not.If you look at all the reviews you'll see a lot of people saying you'll need to enjoy picross to enjoy this game. I had never touched picross before this and this game helped me discover that I do enjoy nonograms. I could technically recommend this game on that basis alone, but I don't feel like I should.Both of the main aspects of this game, which are the murder mystery and the picross, feel pretty lackluster in comparison to existing games in those genres. I can find picross on the Google Play store that control better and give better pictures than what this game offers. The murder mystery portion is extremely straight forward with fairly one-dimensional characters, and almost feels like it's more of a vessel to carry the picross puzzles rather than standing out on its own. There's nothing really to write home about here and I honestly can't recommend it unless something about this game really speaks to you and you really love picross.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: This is a cool mashup of Phoenix Wright and picross puzzles that needed just a bit more polish. The characters designs are great, though their writing feels like it could've used a little more work. The music (from the composer of Phoenix Wright) is fantastic , but it gets old real fast listening to a single song on repeat while you solve a puzzle. But I could overlook all those. The bigger flaws are that the game seems to ignore various features common in visual novels and in picross games that make this game a pain to play. It's very easy to skip dialogue boxes and there's no conversation log to go back and check what you've missed. There's a weird little scanner you have to use to hunt down evidence that's reminiscent of pixel hunting in old adventure games, and quite frankly adds nothing worthwhile to the game. The puzzles don't give you the ability to clear the board, and don't lock your mouse to a row/column when you click and drag to mark a bunch of stuff at once. I've also softlocked my game twice and had to edit a save to get unstuck.Overall this game does a lot right, but it just a little too annoying to play at the moment. Even if the usability were better, I'm not sure the concept works. The puzzles never go above 15x15, which isn't that exciting if you're a picross fan, and the writing and VN segments are.. fine, but it gets really tedious when a cool plot revelation is undercut by making you solve a puzzle.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: It's Picross and Phoenix Wright. I love both those things, so I thought I'd love this, but my review obviously doesn't recommend. Why? The issue is that the Phoenix Wright part is really just 'Try all the things you collect from picross puzzles, you can't fail', and the Picross part is 'every time you try to do anything you need to solve a picross puzzle', so if you ever have issues with the picross puzzles ... it's like reading a book, and in the middle of the book you get five picross puzzles. That would be really annoying and distracting from the book, right? Well, that's the entire point of the game.If that sounds great to you, you'll love it! It just really annoyed me, especially at the end where I had to drag myself through for like ... five hours to get story closure :( which is a shame, because the plot's good enough. Just ... the mechanics are frustration in a box.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I expected a fun, cute Picross game, but what I got was an exciting detective game with excellent writing and one of the best soundtracks I've ever heard (and also cute Picross). It delves into serious topics with surprising grace while keeping the tone light and funny. If you like the Phoenix Wright games and you like picross, this is a guaranteed hit.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: It's a decently polished story-driven game, half Visual Novel, half puzzle game.The Visual Novel half is strongly reminiscent of the Ace Attorney/Phoenix Wright series, with its exquisite but charming characters and witty dialogue, so this game is clearly heavily inspired by that series. Now while admitedly this game does not exactly reach that same professional level of game design, it is still a quite respectable attempt in its own right, with serviceable story, decent characters, catchy tunes and whatnot.The puzzle half is mandatory (as a puzzle fan this is fine for me, but maybe not for those who dislike the genre) but I see that there is an easy mode with hints for those who are not fond of puzzles, although I can't comment on that since I played on normal. Now see, I like these kinds of puzzles as they can be enjoyable in short bursts, but since in the game they are mandatory, ait some point they just became repetitive and boring to be honest, and this seems to be a unanymous sentiment even among the high positive reviews and I fully agree.A solution would either to reserve the puzzles only to a few "key" items/pieces of evidence, OR perhaps add other kinds of puzzle types into the mix, for variety's sake. Then again, inserting other types of puzzles would be tricky, since the game was designed to have pixel art representations of items, which are revealed through the pattern of the current puzzles.The conclusion is that the VN half is pretty fine, but the puzzle half not so much due to the amount of repetition.So while I completed the 1st case (of 4 total) with an S rank, I think i'm done with the game. I just don't see myself going through an even greater deluge of constant repetitive puzzles like that, even tough I'm a little curious about how the story would develop from this point on.All in all I can still recomend the game, specially for VN fans. It is not a professional level game, but it is surprisingly polished with its art, writting and sounds. Just be aware of the mandatory puzzles, which while not necessaarily challenging, jsut get too repetitive too quickly.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Although I'm recommending this game, I need to make something absolutely clear: this game is picross (nonogram) FIRST. I highly recommend checking out nonograms if you don't know how they work. If you don't like them, you will not like this game.I went into this game knowing nothing other than that it was a nonogram game. I've played a lot of those on the various Picross titles on Nintendo platforms so I was excited to get into this one. Immediately, I got Ace Attorney vibes and I felt it throughout the playthrough through both the music, gameplay and art style. I was a lot of cool and unexpected nostalgia.After finishing it once, I don't think I'll ever play it again. Instead, I would look for a more dedicated nonogram game for the puzzle aspect or perhaps an Ace Attorney game for everything else.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great cross between Pictocross gameplay and Pheonix Wright style investigation and storytelling. There are several hiccups in it's execution, but nothing that prevented me from finishing it and wanting more. I hope the team behind this gets to iterate on this concept as it is really promising.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: This game definitely caught me by surprise. I was a tad skeptical since I'm really bad at picross, but the soundtrack and murder mystery aspect was enough to reel me in, and I couldn't put it down until I was done. Pros: amazing soundtrack, Phoenix Wright-esque mystery solving, colorful and interesting characters, excellent writingCons: I can't stop listening to the soundtrack and I need more. There needs to be a sequel. Or DLC. Or SOMETHING. Don't get me wrong, the four episodes available are really good and it took me 14 hours to beat, but I can't wait to see what else they do.TLDR: Great game, buy at earliest convenience
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: This is a short 'n' sweet Picross puzzle game with a a lighthearted visual novel attached. If you are a beginner to Picross puzzles, it has a helpful tutorial on the basic strategies you need to tackle Picross. However, for more experienced Picross enjoyers this game lacks a lot of quality-of-life features that you may have come to expect from other games. Highlighted columns and rows, locking your mouse movement to a single row or column regardless of where your mouse drags, etc. Despite this, it's not a dealbreaker.As for the visual novel part, the story is fine. It's not groundbreaking, but it wasn't meant to be - it's a cute story about an actress and an amnesiac robot! Much like the Picross part though, a fewQoL changes would go a long way. There's no backlog (a VN staple), no pause (autoplay seems to be the default?), and clicking ANYWHERE while choices display causes you to pick whatever was highlighted.There's seemingly no config or controls scheme display screen either, so if there was a key to disable autoplay... there's not really any way for me to have known that.One of the big selling points for this game I see being pushed is that it has tracks by an Ace Attorney composer. This isn't wrong, but the OST isn't really what you'd expect to hear when thinking of the AA games. Nothing wrong with that, but don't go in expecting high energy chase themes. MbN's OST fits the type of game it is, and it's fairly relaxed and chill. The game is also not "Ace Attorney but Picross" like other reviews have said, that's fairly misleading and does MbN a disservice by placing unreasonable expectations on it.That being said, all of the above did not deter me from having a good time and enjoying Murder by Numbers. It has beautiful and bold aesthetics, and the puzzles are decent. If you're a fan of Picross or new to Picross, I'd recommend picking this game up in a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I enjoyed my time with this game, despite a few misgivings I had. The picross puzzles made for a cute novelty in this mystery game, though I believe a couple of puzzles could have been cut (especially the one in Case 3 that was entirely optional but stopped me from getting S rank in the chapter so I had to replay it again). The puzzles also sometimes disrupted the narrative flow when a character would be like "I need to show you this" (puzzle starts instead of character just telling you what it is). Murder By Number is a decent game when you play it in short sessions, though it would be nice to have a log or something similar to remember what was happening in the case. The art style was pretty, especially the character designs.My actual main gripe was with the main character's mother:   Overall, a good game with the potential to be even better.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun game for the style of puzzle and has a story with some entertaining moments. The game doesn't have a lot of glitches from what I've found, but the ones there are are game breaking. For instance, sometimes the menu will take forever to open or won't open at all. If you hit the menu button a minimum of twice before the menu loads, it will load multiple instances of the menu, but only one will be interactive, thus softlocking your game. The game's been out for a while so I doubt these glitches will be patched.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: As soon as I started playing this game, I was incredibly hooked on the detective puzzle format. It was a lot of fun and very relaxing to not have to worry about getting choices wrong and just take my own pace at solving the puzzles. I do have quite a few nitpicks and grievances but this game is well worth the price if you love picross and cute stories.Overall, it's a super cute story and I love S.C.O.U.T., Honor, Jena, and Cross, as well as everyone else. The supporting cast were fun to see, but I wish I had gotten more details about them. If you like complete realism in your stories, though, be warned that there's a lot of points that just don't make sense. For example, a civilian getting involved with a murder investigation and not being arrested for interfering with evidence, hacking police files, etc. I also found most of the characters avoiding stereotypes, or at least I thought so, and it helped that Honor is a character of color. However, K.C. was a major 'gay best friend who dishes advice, shade, and style tips' stereotype. I love him still, but he was a walking stereotype for gay men. The 'cut out' look the characters had was very cute to me. I don't know if it entirely meshed with the background but I never had a complaint either. The art was very clean and beautiful to look at, especially the wide shots during action scenes. I loved those moments.I found most of the puzzles not too difficult but not too easy. After a time it did seem the puzzles were all on a 15x15 grid and it was a bit boring to have the same space all the time. I didn't understand nor like the place holder feature as it did not work well for me, so I often just didn't use it (and thankfully didn't really need to), Other mildly frustrating features were not having a back button and trying to do the hacking puzzles.The hacking puzzles were my most hated part of the game. They were often just frustrating and they would come up with no warning. They had no negative effect if you failed, aside from adding more puzzles to do in the set time limit, but I would get frustrated easily with them. I think it would've helped a lot if a space 'locked in' on these hacking puzzles as you can't select the wrong squares anyway. I would sometimes mess up by un-selecting a space because in was in a hurry to finish.There was also a lack of ability to save as often as I would have liked (mid-conversation, for example) and missable puzzles, which was very frustrating and stress inducing. If you missed one, you had to either have an earlier save (of which there are only 3 save slots, which makes no sense with PC but OK) or restart the whole case over and complete it. There was no 'cumulative total' for your detective rank, you just had to get all of the puzzles in one go. In addition to that, there was also missable dialogue. I liked to show everyone everything just to see if there was a reaction, but a lot of times I would accidentally move the story forward and completely miss my chance to.Having the extra Scout Memory puzzles was a lot of fun, however. I loved being able to back out and do more puzzles! Then when I finished case 4, I knew more puzzles were waiting for me too. Having the memory reward at the end was very fun to see.My most frequent trouble came from the UI. There is no back button on the load or save screens that I could see. Since I was saving often (in case I missed puzzles or dialogue), I would try to check my save file info but not actually want to save. More than once I did sections over just because I had wanted to check the info but not save and overwrite something and had no way to exit out. Same with loading. If you accidentally click start game, then you're not given a prompt and you just have to start the game, either playing until you can go back out or quitting entirely and restarting.As someone who works in games QA, it certainly felt like either there was not a dedicated QA team or the bugs were not considered issues. Despite all of this, I still very much enjoyed this game and I really hope to see a sequel. I think I only became so nitpicky about things just because I enjoyed it so much and it's why I'm here writing this review.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I'd say the prevailing problem I have with this game is that the picross puzzles and the visual novel elements don't compliment each other at all. As you go through the visual novel sections you'll basically yoinked out of that experience to play a different game. It makes the visual novel sections feel like they drag more than they actually do and makes the puzzles feel more like a chore than anything else. If you're like me and you're a fan of both visual novels and picross puzzles, you're better off just getting something else that does either of those things solo, cause again, slamming both together does nothing for either of those things.I ESPECIALLY recommend this because you can get better picross puzzles AND visual novels. The story is certainly not awful, on a good day I wouldn't even call it bad. But there's too many characters that are either just outright unlikable or take too long to warm up to you (not SCOUT though, he's a silly little robot, he's categorically impossible to dislike). The story also does nothing to make its murder mysteries exciting. I find myself asking, "where's the locked room mysteries, the exciting turnabouts?" Piecing together the facts should feel exciting but because the process and circumstances are generally just boring, for the lack of a better word, resolving the cases leaves me feeling lukewarm.As for the picross puzzles, I felt like most of them give too little leads to be fun to solve. I found myself looking at even 10x10 puzzles and going "not this ♥♥♥♥ again" when there were no free lines or even just any numbers greater than 5 to help me get started. It makes for a process where finding clues in these puzzles makes me go "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ finally" rather than "nice" because it's all so painstaking; it just goes against the casual puzzling that I like in picross puzzles.Get Pixross/literally any nonogram app and/or one of the Ace Attorney collections. You're not missing anything special here.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Well, after beating the game.. I don't know if I should recommend this to anyone. This game, while being a murder mystery, feels very niche.I think the story, setting and characters are great and I'm a sucker for traditional puzzles like nanograms. However, the game has a lot of shortcomings.The nanograms, while fun, they're basically the only gameplay aspect. The investigation feels very shallow, and you don't really do much outside of the puzzles besides investigate for more nanogram puzzles and maybe talk to a couple of people. The game added a small minigame where you have to solve a couple of puzzles in a row within a time limit. While I enjoyed those parts, I wish there were more creative uses of the puzzles.I liked the story, I really did and it's what kept me going. However, I don't really like the individual mysteries. I felt they were underwhelming, a tad predictable and leaves much to be desired. Pinning the murder on a suspect doesn't feel  satisfying since all of the evidence presented is circumstantial. Not only that, but the game outright does not expect the right answers. (I.E: Case 1) I didn't like how Honor suddenly jumps into conclusions so quick, which hurt the investigative aspect of the game even more. (Not to mention, when interrogating you get choices instead of presenting something.) What I felt that was particularly jarring were the puzzles constantly interrupting the pace of the game. One moment it's a super tense scene, and in the next you have to solve a puzzle that will take you 5+ minutes and the music suddenly changing, which ruins the mood. Character designs, while interesting, they're not very memorable. Except for a select few, ofc. I enjoyed this game for what it's worth, even though the murder mysteries were alright and there were times I wish there were more variety with the puzzle music. It's a solid experience for the main story alone. TLDR; Game's good, could be better.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: A good balance between visual novel and puzzle game with a colorful cast of characters. PIicked this up because the idea looked intriguing and was not disappointed.EDIT: Having now played some other nonogram games, I'm upping my recommendation: I have amazingly fond memories of this one, and have come to appreciate just how finely crafted its puzzles are.  I was able to 100% the game at maximum score, but there were certainly a number of puzzles which made me sweat, picking through for individual dots or crosses until I finally accumulated enough information to make a breakthrough.  The difficulty was hard, but never unfair, and there are various options to help you along if you're locked out of a solution or make a mistake.I should mention one of those in particular: the "hint" option.  All it does is highlight rows/columns where it's possible for you to make some progress and fill in information.  It doesn't tell you what, though, just gives you a starting point.  In the process, it forces you to figure out *why* that row gives you guaranteed squares, making you a better solver.  I didn't properly appreciate at the time just how much that was developing my skills, and if you move on to other games without it, you'll start missing the feature.On top of that, the game's charm hasn't worn off.  I still can't open it without watching the intro end-to-end, and the cast of characters is still immedately memorable years later.  This is one that has definitely withstood the test of time, and it's well worth yours.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent game - if you love picross. I'd estimate at least 95% of gameplay time is spent solving picross puzzles. The murder mysteries with music and sound effects that remind me strongly of Ace Attorney are good, but they are interrupted frequently by puzzles to the point where I sometimes struggled to remember what had happened most recently. I wouldn't buy this just for the Visual novel element if only because the story is such a small portion of gameplay time. But if you love picross and visual novels a la Ace Attorney? It's a must have.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: On the positive side, the game has a charming visual style, and the writing starts off pretty strong. The characters stay mostly consistent, and it's witty and funny. The difficulty for the Picross puzzles scales reasonably, and I managed to get through them without any prior knowledge of how to play Picross, learning more techniques as the game got harder. The soundtrack is good, and it's at a decent price for the amount of gameplay.However, my experience with this game ended up being far more negative than I expected. The game has too many bugs (resetting a puzzle will blast multiple sound effects at once; and I had to turn off my controller emulation software in order to play because that's buggy as hell too), which is hardly excusable for a QA'd multi-person project. The Picross and narrative portions don't mesh well together - you'll often get a few lines of dialogue interrupted by long stretches of Picross. When you solve a Picross, it turns into a piece of evidence, but the sprite maintains the low-res - and some of them are too confusing to even comprehend. The "investigate" mechanic is pretty much an afterthought, with 90% of the time just being a game of hot-and-cold, and should've been simply removed from the game. The Picross puzzles are way too overused - by the end of the second case I got tired of it, and that's not even 40% of the game's length. When you're late into the game, getting pushed into a new Picross puzzle to solve felt more like a chore, and it was more despairing than rewarding. The story and gameplay elements sometimes play well together, but in general, they didn't - and the Picross moments often killed any momentum that the writing has.Speaking of, the story slowly gets worse as you progress, and the fourth and final case is just an absolute mess - people acting out-of-character or just plainly dumb, with contrived and nonsense explanations, and a few central characters and plot points are completely dropped for the sake of poorly written payoffs. I don't mind clichés and plot holes if it serves the narrative, but this game doesn't go anywhere with what should've been a neat conclusion. It was a very disappointing end with abysmal writing for a plot that started off so strong.While I appreciate the unique combination of Picross and visual novel, I think there are better options for puzzle-based visual novels to pick from. If you're only interested in playing Picross, there are probably better games out there, maybe even for free.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I like nonograms. If you like nonograms too you might like this game. That being said if you aren't a fan of picross like puzzles you would probably steer clear. The puzzle aspect of the story is a main driving force for this visual novel. The story is similar to that you are solving murders and have to figure out whodunit. Though unlike the Phoenix Wright series you don't have to pay much attention to the story to reach the conclusion. I enjoyed this game for both the puzzles and it's cast of characters. In addition to solving various murders you are also tasked with piecing together your computer partner's Scout's past. As you play through each case you uncover bits of his memory. My main gripe with this though is that for the amount of work you have to do in order to recover the memory fragments it doesn't add much to the overall story of Scout's past or give much relevant additional information. It's almost negligible. That said I'd still recommend it. I enjoyed the puzzles, characters and story. It wasn't boring but it wasn't genre defining either. I'd like to see more puzzle hybrid VN like this though. It breaks up the monotony of "just reading"
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: This game grades you based on how many puzzles you solve and how much help you need. However some of the puzzles are missable so if you accidentally miss one you have to spend hours completing the whole episode again and redoing all the puzzles. This is poor design and has no reason to exist.Also the plot has issues. The police seem to be blind as they miss evidence that Scout finds without any problem. The host of an award show can somehow be bribed to influence who wins these awards, even though an unbribed committee decides this. The villain in chapter 4 leaves witnesses alive simply because they're named characters, rather than them having a reason to do this.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, not just for the puzzles but the story and the characters a great too! At first I just wanted to get on with it, the initial cutscene and it being unskippable really annoyed me but I wanted to do some puzzles so I patiently waited. Going through the story and getting to know the characters has been fantastic, I've actually laughed out loud reading what some of the characters say. I love K.C's sassy and witty remarks. They put context clues in the dialog and in the animations to tip you off to who the murderers might be, which is a nice touch.Art is pretty good. The game is set in the 90s and SCOUT(The robot) is made out of 90s inspired parts as you can see by the chunky computer monitor he displays his face on, the TV antenna ears and what looks like a VCR as his body. Also Honor's shirt has a very 90s inspired pattern which i was pleased to see.Story is good.Progressive difficulty.ABSOLUTELY FANTASTIC MUSIC!If you like these puzzles and a good story with comic relief, you'll love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: A lovey game!Never seen a visual novel with nonogram mechanics before.Really great visuals, music, and story.Tho I find it very weird, albeing endearing, when BAM! tense music, the murder happened, you talk and discuss gruesome details and then -- quick switch to pleasant jazzy music as you solve a puzzle.Additionally, later in the story, as the puzzles become more difficult, you encounter some larger puzzles. 10x15 is fine, but anything larger than that becomes a bit hard to read and solve.Still I super enjoyed it!
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Murder by Numbers is a game with fun characters and engaging writing. The cases are interesting, and there's some nice twists and turns. The art is consistent and well-done, and the game is well-assembled (I don't believe I experienced any notable bugs in my playthrough).The one place that really drags the game down, though, is the pacing. The gameplay is _so_ separated from the story that it's horribly jarring; it doesn't help that the puzzles drop back to a common set of happy-go-lucky songs, regardless of the situation. Panicked scene where you're trapped in an emergency and need to get out quickly? Have some tense dialogue with good pacing, coordinated with a ramp up in the musical score and changes in the art. Go two sentences later into this emergency, and you need to find something to help save your life in a few short moments - and you get dropped into one of the game's puzzles, with no time limit, no distinction for the frame or decoration around the puzzle that anything is different, and the standard super happy music. This happens all the time, and in the particular emergency I'm thinking of, you need to do this _twice_.These pacing issues only compound as the game goes on. Towards the end of the game, when you're getting the hardest puzzles, the time between lines of dialogue in a particular story beat can be an hour. This game would likely have been more enjoyable, in general, without the puzzles, which is a really painful thing to say.There's a potential fix for this in the game, even - variations on the puzzle structure to have more rapid puzzle solving for situations needing rapid responses. This is used in-game for a few puzzles where you have to very quickly solve a few very easy/small puzzles to hack a computer before being detected. Other more time-sensitive/pressured puzzle variants for these sorts of situations would have helped significantly in reducing how this feels, as would some means of integrating the story into the puzzle gameplay in other situations - even just a little theming to match the current environment would have been nice.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a mix of Nonogram (Picross) and visual novel. If you don't like any of these, this game is not for you.The story consists of 4 chapters and depending on your score in each chapter you can unlock some additional puzzles which unlock additional parts of the story.I enjoyed the first two chapters the most, because they had the right mixture and timing of puzzles and story telling. In the latter two chapters I felt the story progress was very slow and in my opinion the long puzzle sequences interrupted the progress of the story a lot.Altogether, I had fun with the game, but I didn't feel the urge to replay each chapter for the perfect score to unlock all extras (which is rare for me). So it's a 6/10.Pros:- nice and very likeable characters- overall a good story- Nonogram puzzles ;)Cons:- story is (sometimes) very predictable- missable puzzles- choices don't influence the story
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool Ace Attorney-esque game with an interesting, if a bit clichéd, story. The references feel a bit dated but it makes sense, since the game takes place in the 90's.The Picross puzzles are fun but I don't think they blend with the detective gameplay very well because they sometimes slow down the pace of the game a lot, since the later Picross puzzles can take a good 5 minutes to solve.Another thing I didn't really understand is the fact that one of the characters is framed as part of the main cast but is completely dropped halfway through the game and never appears in person again, not even in the ending scene where the whole gang gets together.Definitely recommend this game and I'm looking forward to the sequel since this game ends with a bit of a cliffhanger.

_childDocuments_.review: I was expecting a run-of-the-mill Ace Attorney clone, but I got really invested in the story. I was really impressed with how they handled certain topics, like gender and domestic psychological abuse. This game has great recurring characters, my personal favourites were K.C. and Jena. It still feels like an AA clone, but in a good way.At first I though the music was a bit basic, but then one day I started humming two of these songs while at work and I haven't stopped please send help.The art is cute! I especially liked the sketches in the credits. I like the character designs. Some characters could have done with more dynamic poses.I played the game on Normal mode, because I've played literally all the Picross games available on 3DS so I like to think I'm pretty good at them. The difficulty was good for me. I made some mistakes because 1) the touch pad on my laptop has some issues so it will sometimes press the left button when I'm pressing the right button, and 2) okay fine sometimes I make mistakes. I wish I had played the game on Switch instead of Steam, I think the touch screen is just handy for puzzles like these.I enjoyed the story more than the nonograms. During the final two cases, I was so into the story that I started seeing the puzzles as nuisances... One thing I didn't like about the clues, was that many of them were just "a square object but angled a bit" (like a piece of paper or a folder), so they all seemed pretty similar after a while. Also, I wasn't really into the whole scanning thing: it was just a still image that you had to drag your mouse across, no challenge. It would've been really cool if you actually had to look for the clues, like a Seek-and-Find kind of puzzle. Maybe for the sequel??I had to replay Case 1 because it doesn't autosave after a case, only when you're currently doing a case?? I'mma assume it's a glitch, but after that happened I decided not to tempt fate and I would always save by hand to make sure.I was going to 100% this game, but apparently Case 3 has some missable puzzles. :( After I had to replay Case 1, I learned that you have to manually click through the whole case and redo all the puzzles, and I wasn't about to replay that whole case no thanks. I did some of the extra SCOUT's Memories puzzles, but I'll have to replay Case 3 to be able to play all the Memories puzzles, sooo guess I'm missing out on them for now. I am planning to see all the Memories when I replay the game on Switch in a couple years. Maybe I'll play on Easy then, because I was more invested in the story than the nonograms.TL;DR good game, minor flaws, wanna replay, sequel pls

_childDocuments_.review: As somebody who was really excited for this game, it hurts a bit to write a negative review. I love both Picross and visual novels like Phoenix Wright, so a combination of the two seemed like a perfect match. Unfortunately, I can't help but feel that the end result has been fumbled a bit. For the sake of organization, I'll tackle the game's two halves separately.Purely as a Picross game, the mechanics are somewhat rough. The general cursor movement feels sticky, especially if you use a controller like I did initially. A couple critical quality of life features are missing, such as as a "mark tile" tool. There is technically a way to mark tiles, but the easiest way of doing it (holding "I" on keyboard) is extremely cumbersome. In terms of puzzle difficulty, the game really doesn't pace itself well. In the third and fourth cases you get barraged with large puzzle after large puzzle, gradually wearing you down. I enjoy the puzzles, don't get me wrong. However, in a normal Picross game I can just do a couple puzzles at a time. You'll never progress through the story at a decent pace without marathoning puzzles. This, combined with the disappointing game feel, make the real gameplay feel like a grind.In terms of story, the game is rather decent. Most of the twists are pretty predictable, which could be seen as a problem in a mystery game. You're never able to fail by making a wrong deduction, so unlike something like Pheonix Wright you can get by without paying attention whatsoever. The dialogue is mostly forgettable, but there are some fun character moments sprinkled in. Specifically, I appreciate the game's handling of LGBT+ characters. There are a couple of them featured in major roles, and for the most part they get to be interesting people beyond typical tropes. The story feels like some fun fluff to pad out the core meat of the game: lackluster puzzles.This is by no means a terrible game. In fact, it's probably still worth it on sale. However, I really just don't know who I would recommend this to. Try it out for the novelty of its genre blend, but don't expect those two halves to be outstanding or work well together.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: The connection drawn between picross and murder mysteries is an endearing one that caught my attention in the early hours of my playthrough. The core appeal of murder mysteries is the slow buildup of what might seem like random facts and evidence until that final piece of the puzzle causes everything to fall into place; a process I found myself pondering quite a bit during gameplay.  See, picross puzzles are all about making progress in places you are 100% certain of, no matter how seemingly insignificant. You make small gain after small gain, until you get stuck, staring at the same state of the board for what could be minutes.  Until aha! there is what you've been missing all along.  This revelation cascades into connection after connection, much like a sleuth might do piecing together disparate parts of a case into a satisfying conclusion.  This clever melding makes the game worth experiencing on its own, if just for the novelty of a completely unrelated style of gameplay meshing with its concept so well. Like my experience with the game however, this review was originally going to be much longer, but the further I got in, the less engaged I felt with its core concepts.  It's nothing particularly damning, but for posterity's sake I'll summerize my thoughts quickly so I can at least have my finalized experience written down, albeit in a truncated form.  The mysteries/narratives themselves are not all that noteworthy which would be a fatal flaw if the flow of the game were not wholly carried by the fully formed cast of colorful characters.  And the picross wears itself thin long before the game closes, so much so that, as alluded to, in order to see the game to completion, I skipped the puzzles of an entire fourth of the game just to see how it ends. The details of these two points would have comprised multiple paragraphs, but alas this is as far as I go.Criticisms aside, I really enjoyed Murder by Numbers. There's more good than bad on display, which is indicative of my fond memories despite all of its flaws and the ways I fiddled around with it in order to alleviate those flaws. I can only hope that with the success of Fall Guys, the team at Media Tonic gives this game/concept/universe another crack, because it's brimming with potential.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game with simple to intermediate piccross puzzles, and a good story about trust and being yourself. Admittedly, there's a few characters I wanted to strangle after the second or third time I saw them, but what's a story without a few villains?I will suggest you take the time to check areas that you thought were done, sometimes repeatedly. The third chapter is particularly notorious for adding puzzles into previously-cleared areas, and you can't get an S-grade unless you find and solve them all. But all in all it's a great game. If you're new to piccross this is a good introduction, and if you're an old hand at them the game's simple and relaxing. Enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun. I'm a tad obsessed with nonogram puzzles and have done probably thousands of them, so I love the idea of building them into a story. I didn't find the puzzles all that difficult, but it was still enjoyable. I found the story engaging enough--it's not Sherlock Holmes or anything, but it's a pretty fun series of mysteries that all tie in together. The music got repetitive, and it's too easy to miss a couple of puzzles in the way the story is laid out, but if you like logic puzzles and come across this on sale, it's definitely worth a play.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game which I'm having a bit of a hard time recommending... but I'm doing it anyway. Why the hard time, you ask? Because of how impossibly  the puzzles get as early as the second case. If you can soldier through all that brain boiling you'll be rewarded with a pleasant, if slightly predictable story with likeable characters and decent twists. I'd also say the music is very good too, but eventually I had to turn it off because I had to listen to the same tunes over and over while getting horribly stuck on the puzzles.For the record, I've never played a nonogram/Picross game before, and I've played on normal difficulty, without hints - which might've been a mistake. I had to restart puzzles more times than I'd like to admit, and there were two moments where the puzzle was 99% done but the numbers didn't add up, so I improvised a bit. Otherwise I didn't guess or anything like that, so take that for what you will.So what makes it so hard? Finding a next move. That's it. As soon as the second case hits it becomes very non-trivial; instead of casually filling pixels while listening to bangers, you spend most of your time looking for this one single place where its safe to put something. Once you find it, chances are there will be a pleasant cascade of things to fill, but inadvertently you'll end up hitting another wall soon after. By the final case I was already used to it, but it still didn't change the fact that I couldn't play more than one puzzle at a time without my overheating brain contributing to climate change.It took me 32 hours total to complete the game, but I did also do a bunch of optional puzzles early on (before they got so insanely hard). Also I didn't use any hints because I'm a stubborn fool. This means that I had to redo puzzles from scratch a few times - less than 10, I'd say. But here's the thing - there  hints available. So my advice is that if you get stuck, just freaking use them. If you don't, you'll unlock a bunch of extra puzzles which in turn unlock extra scenes in the novel... but I don't think they're worth it. I only saw one of them, mind, but I'm not going to torture myself with all those testicles crushers to see more.Now, with all that said: there's still a detective visual novel under all those puzzles. Is it good? Oh yeah. The plot constantly kept me engaged, and the way the characters changed and grew was also fun to watch. My absolute favourite was SCOUT, the robot - not only is he adorable, his personal story is quite something. I also liked Detective Cross; an old, gruff, by-the-book cop who's eager to prove that he's not obsolete yet - and to do that, he has to learn all about the world that's changing around him all over again. And finally, there's KC - the turbo flamboyant gay Hollywood stylist who's also British for added flair. He's Honor (MC)'s best friend, and his flamboyance is not something that overshadows his base personality - instead it's used as added flavour to an already charming mixture. On that topic, the game contains some close-up depiction of LGBT communities that I found nice, informative, and above all else interesting.To sum things up: Murder by Numbers is as much of a puzzle game as it is a detective visual novel. You have to like both parts in order to enjoy it. If you're looking for an Ace Attorney fix, get this only if you like nonograms or are interested in learning about them. And vice versa: if you're just looking for a puzzle game, you're going to have to deal with lots of dialogue and knowing what to present to whom. I knew what to expect and I came out very satisfied from playing this. So if you think this strange mixture is something for you - you're in for a treat! Just don't be afraid to use those hints.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game with tons of picross puzzles. Like phoenix wright but it focuses on investigation. It is NOT perfect though. There are three things this game needs for that.1) ctrl + z and ctrl + y. A undo and redo function would be amazing to fix mistakes where you drag your mouse across the puzzle. Had to restart a few because of it.2) skip mastered puzzles. Sometimes you want to go back for missed funny dialog or you missed a puzzle somewhere and you need it for that S rank. Either way re-doing already mastered puzzles is just annoying.3) This is a small thing but you auto cross out 0 rows, can you auto fill 15 rows? Would help with quality of life as they are just chores before you really start the puzzle. This is the last and least important of the three suggestions.If you could please add the first two it would do wonders to make the game so much more playable.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: The artwork and the colorful, detective centered storyline may trick newcomers into thinking this title is similar to the Ace Attorney games (not to mention both games share the same music composer!), but the investigation phase is minimal here. Part visual novel, part nonogram puzzler. Add some great artwork, lovable characters, catchy soundtrack and an intriguing story that can get just as serious as it can get funny. It's a great combo and an excellent starting point for those totally new to anagram puzzles. (I should know! Never touched a nonogram puzzle in my life before, and I was hooked until the game's very end! And I still have al the extra puzzles to solve as well so the game certainly isn't lacking in content!) Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I came to this game wanting something different. And as a result, I didn’t enjoy the ga,e a ton. I thought this game was going to be nonogram game with story for flavor. But it’s a story-driven game that is nonogram-lite. And the detective aspect is fine, but don’t expect to feel like Sherlock Holmes. If you like visual novels, this game is a great one (fun characters and looks great). I don’t know of the story is good because I couldn’t skip the dialogue fast enough to get to the next nonogram. If you’re on the hunt for a good nonogram game, there are better nonogram-focused games.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Great story and great music, but bloody hell that's a lot of Picross. Legitimately, it's like someone went to a game dev and asked them 'I want all of the Picross you have'Even the reward for doing them without assists is MORE 15x15 Picross squares, and if you do aaaall of those THEN you do get another, admittedly charming, bit of backstory to watch.Ultimately, the sheer amount of ultimately samey Picross challenges was a bit too much by the end. But it was chill and relaxing enough to me to persevere over a number of weeks. I found it goes down well in 30 minute lunch break or before bed sessions with a nice cup of tea and a biscuit, but wont be for everyone, and those expecting Phoenix Wright but with some Picross sprinkled in, stay away.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game! The gameplay mechanics are based in the use of picross to find evidence, so If you like Murder Mysteries and Picross this is the game for you! - The animated intro was beautiful.- The music and sound effects were really good.- The art is phenomenal.- The characters are likable and full of life (my favorite is SCOUT).- There were very funny moments.The only thing that I didn't like is the fact that you can accidentally miss some of the puzzles, which can prevent you from getting the Detective Rank S, which is vital to complete all of the memories. And if you want to get that Rank, you have to replay the cases and complete ALL the puzzles again.  I wish there was some option to just play the puzzles that you missed, or at least jump between scenes so you can examine that specific place.With all that being said, I love how  and I would love to play a sequel of this game! I would also watch an animated series of this game, as the studio who made the animated intro did an amazing job.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Murder by Numbers is reminiscent of the Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney games. You play as an amateur detective working to find out who the murderer is, alongside a colorful cast of companions. Half of the game is talking to other characters to advance the plot, and the other half is solving puzzles.Characters are mostly quite good. Well-written, flawed, and with believable motivations.Dialogue oozes with personality. If the game didn't tell you who's talking, you could tell who it was based on how they say it.Production values are mediocre. No game-breaking bugs, but there are annoying UI issues, like not being able to close open windows with the keyboard. You can't save the game whenever you want to, which is a bother.Music score is awful and will drive you insane if you don't turn it off.Puzzles start out fairly straightforward, but get seriously hard.This game is carried by its characters and dialogue. If I had enjoyed those throughout the entire game, I would have given it a thumbs up, despite its flaws. However, the game's third case (out of 4 in total) revolves around drag queens and a gay bar, and that is not my cup of tea. When the only things that were holding the game up (characters and dialogue) started making me actively uncomfortable, I stopped playing.

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid picross player and Ace Attorney fan, this game was right up my alley. The puzzles ramp up slightly in difficulty as the game progresses, but they're never overwhelming.The story is fun to follow and the characters are genuinely engaging, something vital to any visual-novel-type game.Overall, a great game for 20 bucks or so!
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Cute game with fun characters! I was honestly worried they would fall into stereotypes with the drag queens and a gay hair stylist, but it was handled a lot better than I expected! The murder mystery part is easy enough to solve, and if the puzzles aren't your thing there's an easy mode.Is it the most compelling game with the best gameplay? No, but it's fun when I want to de-stress and not have to think too too hard about anything lol, it's quirky and simple nature (plus fun background music!) make it worth playing for meI can tell the developers had fun with the story and it really shows, but if you don't like puzzles do not play as that's most of the gameplay

_childDocuments_.review: Picross with some phoenix wright vibes. Fun game with a nice story. A couple of the later puzzles can take a while to solve, but that's what you'd expect from a nonogram game. There's a hint system if you're not as familiar with these puzzles, but the learning curve is reasonable enough for this to be a good first nonogram game.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Seems like the Visual Novel wrapper was more Kinetic Novel than choices-matter VN, but considering how long just one play through took me without trying different choices I think I was wise to wait to try for other paths next time. But it was quite well written (IMO) and I definitely felt something for a to-that-point-minor character in the back half of Case 4. Maybe a tiny bit more attention to the dialogue could have been taken, though: for a game set in the 90's there are two mildly-jarring spots with idioms used that weren't common before the 2020's (or outside internet subcultures before the 2010's), but that's an exceptionally small nitpick that shouldn't  affect your enjoyment of the game if you like KN and/or number puzzles of this sort.I'll also admit playing on Easy (which, had I changed it, might have changed the KN aspect to some-choices-matter, I don't know), because the tutorial itself says to start on Easy if you're not familiar with this type of puzzle - I'm not, and I mistakenly thought years of Sudoku and other number puzzle experience might provide some logical advantage. And considering how much those hacking puzzles blew up my pulse and heart rate, I think I made a solid choice for play #1 to be otherwise low-risk.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of care went into making the act of doing Picross puzzles fun. Little animations and sound effects and overall design of the puzzles are all great.Of course the character design, writing, and music are excellent too. But if you do play this game, don't play it trying to just get through the puzzles so you can see the story. You should play and do the puzzles because you like doing Picross puzzles, with the narrative as a nice bonus in addition to the satisfaction of having completed the puzzle.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could post a neutral review, but overall I wouldn't recommend this to my friends. Also, if you're looking for an "Ace Attorney" replacement, I would definitely not suggest this game. A "guilty until proven innocent" not-even-a-real-detective kinetic novel with mandatory nonograms.  This is a very "rough draft" of a story.  I absolutely liked the personalities of the characters being built, but the story formula was so terrible.  Terrible plot ideas, such as "how do we move this character to this scene?"  "Let's just completely disregard common sense and make her run back to the guy with the gun."  Or "hey you're connected to the crime, you did it, and I'm gonna shout it to the world and make you look bad."  Basically, the good guys are literally bullying innocent people because they don't get the answer they want.  I just started on the last chapter, but I feel like I'm dragging my feet through the rest of this story to see how everything connects.Characters interrupt for dramatic effect, but if you read too slow, you won't catch what's going on.  Definitely needs a "backlog" for the visual novel element.I wish the puzzles had more random-ness rather than chapter 1 being easy puzzles, and chapter 3/4 being really long puzzles that seem to use "yet again another square object." (E.g., yes nonograms are square, but I'm tired of solving for a box in a box.)I've had a few bugs where I needed to exit the game and relaunch just so I could continue to "investigate."  Seems more QA should have been involved.The artwork is FANTASTIC and AWESOME.  Again, I like the characters and how they support each other.  Jokes are good.Overall needs more polish.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game overall, but for my personal preferences, it was a little too skewed towards the mystery visual novel / dialogue side rather than the picross puzzle side. The story was fine but nothing that engaged me enough to want to spend as much time on it as the game did. The final mystery was probably the most interesting.The art was great, the music was fantastic, and the puzzles & controls were solid. I was trying to get all the bonus puzzles from each chapter by discovering every puzzle available, but I wasn't able to jump back into a chapter after completing it to play puzzles I'd missed, which was a little disappointing. The saves are a little weird. However, no achievements are connected to the bonus puzzles if that's something you care about.If you're looking for a unique picross game, this game hits that pretty well, but there is a decent amount of "down time" in between puzzles at times where you're reading a lot of dialogue.

_childDocuments_.review: A short* but sweet game with four cases to complete. The tone is balanced and the story feels well-paced. The dialogue is natural and the comic relief does its job. Great characters, LGBTQ+ positive, intriguing and dramatic plot.Unless you're very good at picross, you'll be spending a lot more time playing picross than progressing the plot. There are rectangular grids as well as square ones, and they rarely reach 20 long on either axis. I believe there may have been a single 20x20 grid in the entire game. The puzzles are well-designed though, and manage to add complexity within smaller grids.There is an Easy Mode as well as a hints toggle, but there are some bonus flashback cutscenes that require you to complete the main cases without using these assists to unlock. They are not plot-vital though, and you can replay individual cases without playing through the whole storyline up to that point to try again.*= I completed all four cases and all of SCOUT's Memories in about 20 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah!  A fun, colorful, upbeat puzzle game with enjoyable characters and four cases to solve.Note that the gameplay is 99% picross puzzles ... so if you don't like these, you're gonna have a bad time.  If you do like them, there is a great selection with increasing difficulty, as well as "hacking" puzzles which are 5x5 but on a very strict time limit.  I wouldn't sit down and play this game in a single weekend, but it's lovely for picking up and doing a puzzle or two, and advancing the plot a bit.In between the puzzles is dialogue, character building, and a simple science fiction story about an amnesiac robot.  The writing won't win any awards, but I liked the cast, and the story is good enough to justify scanning crime scenes for a million clues, which is where the picross comes in.I was surprised to see that by the end of the fourth case I have clocked over 40 hours with this game!  Even with such a narrow gameplay focus, that seems like a good value at full price.  I would happily pay this price again for more puzzles and to see the continuation of our young detectives' careers.

What you get is the wrath of whoever designed these puzzles, who clearly really likes stacking 1-tile outlines and making cheese holed puzzles that barely have any clues more than 2 consecutive tiles per iota of progress, which can be seen littered throughout  starting from Chapter 2. All of the resulting positions brings in pain and agony.See, this is why every puzzle is 15x15. They're not hard 15x15s, but they're surely all painful and chaotic 15x15s. This is not a  picross game to play; it only brings you struggle after struggle.
