_childDocuments_.review: A neat little puzzlesolving mystery with great graphics, great soundtrack (even if extremely reminiscent of Ace Attorney) with plenty colourful characters and red herrings.The chaptered murders might have been quite clear-cut, but the overarching story of Scout still makes the game intriguing.The puzzle mechanic is impeccable and the hint system is very helpful as there's a steep learning curve and harsh increase in difficulty after case 1.Now to flaws:Music is great, but sometimes someone is dead and cheery puzzle-solving music is playing which totally kills the vibe.There's no clear way to know which character on screen is speaking as sprites don't telegraph that at all.The learning curve is too steep for someone who never had any experience with nonograms and if you play in long sessions, it gets tiring and insufferable. That's there the hint system helps. I am no slouch when it comes to puzzles, but I used the hints when I as too tired of the same and it didn't even lower my rank significantly as the penalty is very small.Overall I'd say it's strong 6/10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: So, how is Murder by Numbers? It's fine for what it is, but it's hard to give the game a lot of credit when its biggest strength is nonograms. If you're an existing fan of these puzzles then Murder by Numbers delivers in spades. If you're hoping for an elegant blending of a visual novel with logic puzzles it fails to really hit the mark by virtue of some serious pacing issues within the story and a general lack of creativity across the four cases you'll be investigating. I appreciate that effort went into providing story context for the gameplay, but it falls a bit flat. At least the characters are charming as heck.Full review here: Additional note: if you're  looking for a picross game consider this a .

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely one of my favorite puzzle games I've ever played. I'm a fan of the Phoenix Wright series, and this has a lot of the same charms without the Point-and-Click logic that Phoenix Wright at times has. Puzzles rank from simple to moderately complex, and is very beginner friendly for newcomers to Picross/nonogram style puzzles. Characters are charming, the plot is easy to follow but full of twists and turns that reward you for paying attention to the clues. _childDocuments_.review: Really great combination of casual murder-mystery visual novel and Picross.Story: 7/10Artwork: 8/10Music: 10/10Fun: 8/10S.C.O.U.T: 11/10I'm a fan of Picross so to have it combined with a story (and a murder-mystery one at that) gives the game a little more depth than just sitting and doing a regular picross puzzle.  I will say, if you're not a fan of Picross, I would potentially give it a miss because it will get quite repetitive and can be quite tedious.It's a pretty casual, short-ish story and an easy read, with only a few components to progress the story, which is perfect for those who want a casual game.There are two difficulty settings, Easy and Normal. Easy will help those who aren't too confident with the game and will auto-fill completed lines when you are done and alert you to most mistakes, whereas normal mode, you have to rely on point-deducting hints.You have the main story mode and then once you complete each chapter (depending on which grade you get overall), you 'unlock' S.C.O.U.T's memories and have extra puzzles to complete as and when you choose.I really do like the premise of the story, so it would have been nice to have gone a little deeper into character development because I do genuinely like the characters you meet in the story. I LOVE S.C.O.U.T! Hands down my favourite character. I ADORE the soundtrack as well. It gives off kinda retro vibes, so that's a big tick for me.All in all, if you enjoy picross and a bit of murder mystery, then this is definitely the game for you!

_childDocuments_.review: Murder By Numbers is probably the most charming picross-based game I’ve ever played. It blends number logic puzzles and visual novel elements to great effect.Solve the puzzles to solve the murders.The game stars TV actress Honor Mizrahi and her robot sidekick SCOUT as they become amateur detectives. When they inadvertently get dragged into a dark conspiracy, they must step up to solve some real-life murder cases. Both are written to be extremely charming, but SCOUT is absolutely the standout. Seeing him grow in confidence as the story unfolds is very satisfying. I never knew I could care so much about a sentient AI robot, but there we go. There are plenty of jokes and tongue-in-cheek moments.Accompanying them on their adventures are a host of diverse larger-than-life Hollywood characters. A shady ex-husband. An eccentric film director. A flamboyant drag queen. A world-weary police detective. Each is a fun addition to the game, and nearly all are potential suspects. Which is to be expected. Hato Moa, (creator of Hatoful Boyfriend) designed them all.SCOUT out the crime scene.During each investigation, SCOUT is used to search the crime scene. This is framed as a first-person view of a static background. Once a potential piece of evidence is found a picross puzzle must be solved. The in-universe reason is that SCOUT must visually process what he’s looking at. And it gets revealed piece-by-piece through reasoning and deduction. That’s why everything is divided into a grid and looks pixelated at first. It doesn’t really change the way the puzzles are solved, but I just think that’s a neat idea.At the start of every chapter, the player is at Detective Rank F. The more accurately and proficiently a puzzle is solved, the more points the player is awarded. There are hints and help available but using them reduces the overall score. Each achieved rank unlocks more puzzles outside of the story, which I think are worthwhile rewards.When an object is found, it can be used during the interrogation sections of the game. During each scenario, there are a host of people to talk to. By choosing from a set of questions, and from an inventory of found items, the player must find out who did it. To the best of my knowledge there is no way to fail, but getting the answers right on the first go is very satisfying.A 90’s aesthetic.Being set in the 1990s, a few of the references and jokes in Murder By Numbers may fly over the heads of some younger players. A bit of mild swearing and the overall premise of the game (Murder!)  may make some parents wary of buying this for their kids. It has a PEGI 12 rating thanks to the aforementioned things and a few others.Visually, the game looks great. Strong designs and bold colours help make each character memorable. They are also surrounded by a bold white outline as they talk, which kinda makes it feel like they are cut out from paper. As with many visual novels, the designs could be pulled straight out of an anime. Despite the visual style, it lacks some of the more unsavoury anime tropes. There are no egregious “fan service” moments and everything is proportioned fairly realistically. All this makes for a very digestible game, suitable for most audiences.The soundtrack is extremely energetic. Famed composer Masakazu Sugimori (Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney, Ghost Trick and Viewtiful Joe) takes centre stage here. A highlight of the entire game is the absolute cheesy banger of an intro song. Combined with a wonderfully animated intro, I would be very shocked if it doesn’t immediately get lodged in the brain. And yes. Unsurprisingly, it is on Spotify, alongside the rest of the killer soundtrack. Just in case anyone needs to know.A big heart in a little robot.As someone who has big love for picross puzzles, Murder By Numbers was a very enjoyable time. The combination of solving a puzzle pixel-by-pixel and questioning suspects really made me feel like I was solving murders. With a substantial story set over 4 chapters, it has enough content to keep people busy for around 20-30 hours. The additional puzzles are a nice bonus too. Overall, a fantastic little puzzle game with heaps of personality! As a result, this is a very easy recommendation from me.Found this review helpful? You can find more on the BestNerdLife website!

_childDocuments_.review: About my personal experience: This game has been so much fun, my friends and I have done the first case and most of the 2nd and it has been an total blast. What we do is I load up the game and have my pals hop onto team viewer so we can take turns doing puzzles and help each other when we are stuck. We also all have assigned characters and voice them so it's really fun. If you have a group that would like to do this, I highly recommend playing it this way. About the game: The story is so cute, and the characters are fun. You can see the clear influence from Phoenix Wright, but in the best possible way. The story is never too long winded, so you are getting to the puzzles and progressing at a satisfying rate. The music is so catchy that I find myself dancing with the cursor when I am doing the puzzles. As for the puzzles, they get pretty difficult which is fun, but there is a easy mode and a normal mode, so if you find yourself struggling there is help. I love this game and I kind of want to make my whole life about it.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't actually  this game. I liked it a lot, and would buy a sequel. But when weighing what I liked and didn't like about the game, the bad parts sadly overtake the good. Let's break it down into gameplay, writing, music and art. Minor spoilers in the Writing section.+ , I think the visual novel style goes well with the puzzle solving.- . I didn't need to use a hint in the whole game. I don't think they get particularly harder as the game progresses either, they just mostly stay the same. In order for this to not get stale in a game that takes 30 hours to complete (30 hours of the same thing gets tedious), you need to change things up sometimes. However, what you shouldn't do is- . Nobody likes speed puzzles. People who seek out games like this want a chill time reading a detective story while solving puzzles at their own pace, they don't want to stress out with a sudden, time limited puzzle that just relies on reflexes rather than actual puzzle solving. Since these puzzles aren't skippable, players with slow reaction time won't be able to play this game.+ .- .- . It feels like the writers just want to tick a bunch of politically correct boxes instead on focusing on the murder mystery. Like, talk about consent, okay, main character has an abusive ex, sure, gay best friend, mhm, explaining drag culture and pronouns to an old man, alright, SCOUT questions its gender... okay, would you stop already? I may agree with the messages the writers are trying to convey in that regard, but I want to read a detective story, not "woke politics for dummies".+ . Probably wouldn't get a best game soundtrack of all time reward, but it does its job.- . You're solving puzzles for 30 hours, but the tracks playing during them are always the same 4 or so. I got sick of the music by the end of the first case. By the last case, I could't even listen to the game anymore. Every case needs its own set of tracks to not get annoying, at least during the puzzles.+ .+ .+  and works well with the tone of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Picross puzzles are good, until they reach a certain complexity where they get repetitive, long and boring. The amount of same puzzles without novelties it's a little bit overwhelming.The story starts nice and certainly interesting, but it falls into the same cliches in every chapter and it is difficult to get you engaged. I cannot help myself to compare this narrative with Phoenix Wright, being the latter a much superior game.OST is not bad until it gets stuck in your head again and again, as the three same tracks keep repeating in every Picross puzzle. Imagine spending more than 20 hours listening to the same three tracks while doing repetitive puzzles. This is it.Therefore, I do not recommend this game unless you are a big fan of Picross puzzles. In any case, you will be eventually fed up with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game, overall. But it does overstay it's welcome for those who wanted to just bookend the story.Story is serviceable, it kept me interested until at least the end. Nothing award-winning, but the relationship between the two leads is nice, if not cliched. Puzzles seem to increase in difficulty at a nice pace, as someone newer to Picross. The main problem is, as one of the rare people more interested in the story than the puzzles, there are so many required to get through a case, and they're the only real gameplay. Yes, I know I bought a puzzle game, but when you just want to get to the next beat of the plot and you're stuck for literally two hours solving puzzles back to back, kind of takes the air out of a lot of scenes.But overall it is a charming game that I would love to see a sequel to with more gameplay elements. Actual investigation and deduction. For the price I paid (I got it in a bundle), I feel it was well worth it. I just feel the main story could have been 50% shorter and the extra puzzles moved to the optional "Scout's Memories" section.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun game but I would only recommend it for people who are really into playing pixel puzzles since that is the main basis of the game.  Some people may find the game to be too repetitive otherwise.  The game has a decent amount of content for the price there are four cases total to solve and prob took me anywhere from 3-5 hours to solve with getting S rank on all of them.  There is also some side content to unlock one of the protagonist's memories so there are even more puzzles for you fellow puzzle gurus to be excited about.

Now that I'm done with the warning, the stories are fun and they sure like to pun a lot, I did like the puzzles, except when they were one after another for no other reason than to expend the content.

_childDocuments_.review: Make no mistake:  You must like Picross to make it through this game.  It's mostly Picross puzzles with story in-between.  Anyways, the story and characters are overall interesting, and the puzzles are good.The only thing to look out for is that if you are going for S-rank in Case 3 (doing all puzzles with no hints, so that you can get the secret memories), there is a MISSABLE puzzle.  I missed it my first time through, and since there is no fast-forward or skip button (and I didn't backup save at the right point), I had to click my through a significant portion of the story and re-solve puzzles to get back to that point, and then solve puzzles all of the way to the end afterwards.  It took some time.Also, the secret memories are only a little interesting, and don't really reveal anything, so only do them if you REALLY LIKE PICROSS.

_childDocuments_.review: presents an intriguing concept by blending visual novel storytelling with nonograms, also known as picross puzzles. Set in the 1990's, the game offers players a chance to solve crimes and uncover mysteries through a combination of dialogue-driven narrative and grid-based puzzle solving. While the idea is promising, the execution leaves much to be desired, resulting in a somewhat underwhelming experience.The game's strongest point lies in its unique premise, as players assume the role of Honor Mizrahi, a TV actress turned amateur detective who partners with a sassy robot named SCOUT to solve a series of murders. The retro aesthetic and witty dialogue capture the essence of the 90's, providing a nostalgic backdrop for the investigation.Unfortunately,  stumbles when it comes to its puzzle mechanics. The picross puzzles themselves are a mixed bag – some are genuinely engaging and satisfying to complete, while others feel tedious and overly simplistic. Others feel almost impossible to solve without the aid of some guide or YouTube video. The difficulty curve lacks consistency and is all over the place, often leading to frustration as players oscillate between breezing through puzzles and getting stuck on obscure logic leaps.The narrative aspect of the game, although intriguing at first, struggles to maintain its momentum. The murder cases tend to follow a formulaic pattern, making the overarching story feel predictable. The character development also falls flat, with Honor and SCOUT's interactions occasionally veering into clichéd territory.Visually,  sports a colourful and vibrant art style that pays homage to the era it draws inspiration from. The character designs are charming, and the game does an admirable job of capturing the essence of the 90's with its fashion choices and environments.The game's soundtrack complements the retro vibe effectively, though it doesn't stand out as particularly memorable. Voice acting is serviceable, but it lacks the depth needed to truly bring the characters to life.In conclusion,  presents a creative blend of genres that ultimately falls short of its potential. While the concept of combining visual novel storytelling with picross puzzles is intriguing, the uneven puzzle difficulty, predictable narrative, and disappointing character development prevent the game from reaching greater heights. It's a decent choice for players seeking a casual and nostalgic experience, but those looking for a more polished and engaging detective game might be left wanting more.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fairly decent game marred by a couple really bad design decisions, enough so where I don't know why I'd recommend it to nonogram fans or VN fans.The good first - the dialogue and characters are pretty good. The art style is nice. There are options to give hints for the main puzzles with a big huge asterisk attachedThe eh - It's not a VN with the occasional nonogram, nor is it a nonogram game with the occasional story, it's pretty evenly split. I say "eh" because it really depends what you're after. I like both those genres but this game doesn't do a great job at eitherThe bad - unfortunately, I could write a lot here. The first big thing I noticed is that for basically the last 2/3 of the game (that is, most of it), almost every nonogram is very very "samey". They're all 15x15 (with a couple of exceptions), and since they're all done in the same pixel style trying to represent some small item, they honestly just feel identical. Randomly generated ones are more interesting than these after the 20th one and there are WAY more than 20 of the almost same puzzle.Additionally, you unlock more bonus puzzles by achieving "ranks" playing through the story - these actually do come in other flavors than 15x15 but you achieve rank by getting score, and you can only get the highest rank by completing a chapter (each of which is 7-8 hours long) with none of the assists on (except the highlight hint, which is not always helpful and actually highlights that some of their puzzles have flawed design where it says you have a known move when actually there are multiple options). You ALSO have to complete EVERY puzzle in the chapters, which is required EXCEPT for chapter 3, where there is one you can miss. If you do that, you can't unlock that extra bonus puzzle without redoing the ENTIRE chapter.On top of THAT, near the end of each chapter (and maybe once or twice sprinkled in), there are randomly generated, 5x5 nonograms that you have to beat a certain number of in a VERY tight time limit. I had to redo some of these over and over and I've cleared Paint it Back and a number of other nonograms on mobile, and 5x5s are EASY compared to those, but the time limit is that bad. There is no option to skip or make those easier, which means you cannot progress through that chapter if you can't do those in a speedrun fashion. I'm sure there are speed competitions for nonogram people but that's not, typically, the point of the puzzles. This gatekeeping, terrible design alone would probably be enough for me to not recommend it (again, why? There are better VNs and much better nonograms) but then you pile on the other issues and it's just... bleh. There's a lot of potential here, I really like nonograms and hope we continue to see more adaption of it into mixed puzzle games, but this just isn't it. The VN as just a VN might have actually been an OK shortish story for a VN game but if the nonogram part was isolated I don't see anyone recommending it that played more than the first chapter.Oh, one last mention on accessibility - there are bright white short screen flashes CONSTANTLY (basically every time a character is surprised or angry at someone which is... not uncommon, let's say). If you have any kind of sensitivity to that, one more reason to stay away.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of Picross, I went into this game expecting to suffer through the story just waiting to get to the next puzzle. However by the time I got to Act 2 I was rushing through the puzzles trying to get to the next story beat. The characters are endearing, the story is decent, and the art style is distinct. The puzzles themselves are fine, same as any other Picross game. Controls for the puzzles leave nothing to be desired, it's simple to pick up and easy to master. If you're a fan of visual novels and Picross then this is definitely the game for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Very good overall.I liked the story and the characters quite a lot although the MC does jump to a lot of conclusions very quickly when solving the cases, almost all of the main cast was likeable and I liked seeing their interactions throughout.The picross part was very good and managed to avoid the trap a lot of them fall into by being less about the art so you can guess how to finish them too easily, and by the end the puzzles were very challenging which I enjoyed immensely. Even the timed hacking challenges were good fun and helped keep the pace upThe major gripe I have is where these two parts overlap sometimes, (mild spoiler but no precise details or names), in case 2 you have to find two items to escape a bathroom that has a fire raging outside it, but these puzzles are kinda challenging and took a few minutes to complete which kinda bulldozed the pacing and made it feel a lot less urgent.More glaringly in case 4 (kinda big spoiler, you have been warned), having unravelled a larger mystery you have a very climatic scene where someone ends up getting shot right in front of you, this was a very effective scene that actually really got to me and I was feeling very empathetic for the characters, but then it's right back into the picross puzzles with that really jaunty upbeat theme and damn that emotional whiplash is SEVERE. There is very little breathing room narratively because after the shooting you have to stop the killer deleting evidence so the story can't really take it's foot off the gas, this really dampened the ending for me because I was still dealing with the circumstances around the shooting by the time the game wrapped up so it felt like a little of a wet squib.Overall however I would absolutely recommend this if you like both Picross and Ace Attorney, the puzzles are the right mix of challenging but not too brutal, the story does a lot right and was very enjoyable, and the soundtrack was absolutely amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun from a puzzle perspective. However, it's a bit rudimentary when it comes to detective work, and the first case was vastly disappointing. I pinpointed the murderer by the way they were acting when presented with key evidences, yet when I suggested the actual culprit, the game told me I was wrong. Lo and behold, the game forces you to pick the wrong answer so the real killer can get away. That's a minor gripe compared to the game-breaking glitch I uncovered for no apparent reason, however, with no fix to date, despite the fact that it has been known for months. The devs have done nothing to remedy the case 2 glitch near the beginning, where the game creates two iterations of the same individual in two different locations. This game needs some TLC, and then I can give it the rating it deserves.Fun music, would not recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed any of the Ace Attorney games and crave more of the mystery solving VN goodness, you'll feel right at home(they even use the same text sound). _childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Murder by Numbers is a story-driven picross game with a murder mystery setting. In order to solve murder mysteries you play picross puzzles to reveal clues that you use to solve the murders.The problem however, is that picross and investigating doesn't match very well. Instead of getting a murder mystery of the ground, you are stuck at an investigation screen, doing as many as three or four large picross puzzles to advance the plot. The result is that you forget what the plot kinda was in the first place while solving the puzzles, and any kind of momentum the plot builds up is immediately lost. Solving the puzzles also negatively affects the mystery gameplay, as there isn't much mystery to be solved as the puzzles give you all the information you need. There isn't much deduction you do as a detective.All in all, Murder by Numbers is a decent puzzle game, but a bad detective game, and I can't help but have this feeling that the two elements of the game hurt each other instead of elevating the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I was thinking I'd love this game coming into it but a couple of things made it completely unbearable only 40 minutes in. 1. Story is cringeworthy, tone is also cringeworthy. When you open the game you're greeted with an animated cartoon opening reminiscent of a Disney Saturday Morning show. It's well animated but it's incredibly corny and, what can I say, I thought it was a little bit juvenile. That's just the start. Things are bouncing around in the first hour between exposition and backstory, setting the tone, and character building and it's honestly just a huge mess. This brings me to the 2nd point2. The sound effects that compliment the cutsences are insanely annoying. Every 30 seconds there's a "Womp womp" or a punching sound which often don't really fit what's being presented. At first they were minor grievances, but when I realized that the game intended on repeating them nonstop, I started to get annoyed, however it was point 3 that made me close the game and request a refund.3. Agenda. This game has the sneaky kind of agenda, the kind that's almost un-noticable at first. There's a lot to go through but I'll talk about the few points that I noticed and ultimately the one that frustrated me the most. Firstly, as the main character goes through a vent, the robot sidekick scans her body measurements. She gets uncomfortable and upset by this in a way which is presented more as a boundary being crossed than a comedic moment. This stunk to me like a commentary on the concept of consent. I won't go into why I feel that it was a silly commentary, but rather I'll question why it was an appropriate moment to add to such an early point in the game. Is this a political game, or a silly light hearted murder puzzle game? I want to play the second, I don't want to play the first, I don't want a light hearted VN puzzle game with political BS in it, I game to escape the real world, not to be reminded of it, yes I get it consent is a topic of importance and controversy, go make a game about that rather than putting it in this one. There's also a bodybuilder who flirts with the main character, wherein she threatens to electrocute him with a cattle prod, again smelled like agenda to me, but the final and most irritating moment revolves around the character of K.C. He somehow is more annoying than Becky, the character who's actually SUPPOSED to be annoying. He whines, talks about needing to pee and makes comments alluding to his sexuality in almost every single line he's given. I tell no lie, when you interview him to progress the story, you ask him around 5 questions, literally every single one includes a mention of his sexual preferences. Again it just seemed like something that was being presented not because it made the story, gameplay or characters better, but just because the author wants to further the inclusion of specific classes in society. I have no issue with this inherently, but here it's done in an irritating, unenjoyable way. As with all "Political" inclusions in games, I have no issue with the message, but the execution. This game is supposed to be about Picross with elements of VNs and puzzles, but it's just not about that, not as much as I was expecting or wanted. If you enjoy this game, the story, and the politics, that's fine, but it wasn't what I expected or wanted, so I went for a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: Murder by Numbers is a mix of visual novel and nonogram puzzle game. For the visual novel part, we follow the story of an actress who finds herself in the middle of a murder investigation, and has to solve it by herself with the help of a friendly robot. The game has 4 investigation cases overall. The story is very linear, although there are some dialogue options that lead to different reactions. Don't expect much of the active investigation work you'd see in point & click adventure games, or even in an Ace Attorney game (which is rather linear itself). The beginning of the game is a bit slow, but as it goes the rhythm gets better.The story is fairly enjoyable, with some connections between the cases, and some of the characters are interesting. At points it managed to be touching. It isn't a masterpiece, but does everything need to be a masterpiece?The nonogram part (if you're not familiar with the term, think Picross) is rather simple. As someone that enjoys nonograms, there were only a few puzzles that were somewhat challenging. However, there is a decent amount of puzzles for you to enjoy.Overall I recommend this game. It might not have the best story out there, but it's a pleasant enough experience for a reasonable price.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I saw a recommendation for this game which said it was "Ace Attorney with nonograms" and I instantly added to my wishlist and bought it at the first sale.All in all, however, it was a bit disappointing.The story is great - SCOUT is just plain adorable and loads of fun. The writing is witty and the cases interesting and it all ties up in a satisfying ending. The art, although a bit limited in scope, fits the game well. I had lots of fun in the first couple cases. But as they got longer and the nonograms just started to pile up... I had to drag myself through it.I love nonograms, but solving dozens of them to get through a single case, it's too much. I wish they had more variety - maybe add some more special minigames, such as the hacking nonogram challenge, or at least make some of them smaller. It unfortunately gets repetitive and very, very tiring.I'd say maybe this would fare better if you played it in short busts, but the mystery storyline wouldn't lend well to that kind of play.If you enjoy solving cases and nonograms, sure, give it a try. There's lot of potential here with the setting and characters. I really hope a sequel comes around to fix the issues with the pace of the game and make it reach its true potential.

_childDocuments_.review: Cute, fun, well-written, gorgeous, simple and clean. Heartily recommended!While I'm not a fan of Picross-style puzzles, this game has a difficulty setting that makes it a non-issue for everything but the post-game bonus galleries. Some of the soundtrack loops get a little grating if you take a particularly long time on a puzzle, but that's about my only complaint. The writing is fun and fits the timeframe perfectly, the characters are A++, Moa's designs bring a ton of life to a (fairly) mundane setting... Murder by Numbers is an easy pick-up IMO.

_childDocuments_.review: Murder by Numbers is a visual novel + nonogram game. There are 4 cases in this game, and in these cases, you progresses the narrative by navigating between a couple of places, speaking with people and showing them evidences. You'll gather evidences by solving nonogram puzzles. These puzzles are what you expect from a nonogram, but the later cases has larger 15x15 puzzles. They are easy to solve in general and no advanced complex rules you might find in a standalone nonogram games. At some instances you might need to solve 5 consecutive time limited 5x5 nonogram puzzles too, which is really the only variation of the puzzles.The story is also your average murder mystery story, nothing really big to shout about. But if you love murder mystery story and nonogram, this game is right up your alley. If you expect actual investigation gameplay like interrogation like in Ace Attorney, you'll be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Murder by Numbers is a murder mystery story wrapper for nonogram puzzles aka picross.In the game you play as Honor Mizrahi, an actress on a hit TV show Murder Miss Terri, who loses her job and gets thrust into a world of murder and mystery when a flying robot, SCOUT, who can't remember who they are asks you for help. SCOUT is great at finding pertinent items, but to do so you'll have to click a hot spot via the investigation mode and then solve a puzzle to analyze the object you found and input the item into your inventory.The presentation is great, the art and designs are nice, the music is amazing, composed by Masakazu Sugimori who worked on Ace Attorney 1 and 2 and Ghost Trick, and the plots themselves are enough to keep you going. But the main draw is the puzzles themselves. They don't get too hard, they cap out at 15x15 generally, although I think there's a 15 x 20 near the end. You fill in the squares in accordance with the number clues on the side. You don't lose points or have to restart for misfilling a square, which is good, and there are some hints if you get stuck, but every puzzle is solvable with the logic presented.There's logic for solving the mystery as well, but it doesn't let you fail. You'll find evidence and have to use knowledge of it to answer multiple choice questions or present it to characters to advance the plot, but there are no fail states or retries needed. But the stories are written decently enough to have fun seeing them play out.Generally, a pretty comfy straightforward puzzle game to play with some nice set dressing.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Ace Attorney and picross (also known as nonograms), then I highly recommend this game. It's high tier. I S-ranked all four cases and intend to do the last 20 bonus puzzles next session. Doing those gives you access to some extra backstory but isn't required for achievements. The story is good and the detective gameplay is...well, I have no complaints. It's functional.I am a picross . That's the whole reason I got this game. I've been playing nonograms for at least 7 years. So comparing the actual picross gameplay to other picross games, this is actually really good. The nonogram implementation is not as good as Pictopix or , not nearly. But it's a hundred times more polished than half the janky mobile picross games I've played. And the actual puzzles are every bit as good as what you'd find in pictopix.One feature it sorely needs is the ability to save and restore a picross puzzle. The feature is important because sometimes (especially with heavily dithered puzzles) there are no valid logical moves, and you're forced to make an assumption to rule out a block or X. But doing so requires you to take the puzzle all the way to the end, where things don't add up, which is where save/restore comes in. GRANTED, I haven't come across a puzzle so far that requires a guess on my part. Every time I've had to reset a puzzle it's because I slipped somewhere and the puzzle was unsalvageable. So props to whoever tested the nonograms because I can tell that they were careful to avoid situations like that. I still think the feature should be there so that you can save/restore at certain parts, so as to avoid having to lose all your progress.Another feature it could use is, well, controller and keyboard support. Having to do it with the mouse is a real wrist-killer.Also, there seems to be a bug in the validator. There was at least one instance where the game didn't recognize a valid solution until I cleared a column and filled it back in exactly the way I had it before. Weird hiccup. I assumed it was "one true solution" validation rather than logical validation before I got it to accept it. Obviously, OTS is a bad method of checking the puzzle because there are plenty of puzzles that have multiple solutions, especially when dithering is involved.I also did not detect any penalty system in the puzzles. Thank you devs for that. Too many devs fall into old game design habits, like adding a limited lives/continue system, or penalties for making a mistake. But penalizing mistakes in picross is problematic because it gives away part of the solution, which is not only bad design, but can also be HEAVILY cheesed. So props to the devs for thinking about that.Also props for keeping the puzzles at 15x15 max (well, ignoring that *one* puzzle that was 20x15). I like 25x25s and 30x30s, but man are they exhausting to do in one sitting. I recognize and appreciate the restraint there. Although next time you make a picross game, chill on the dithering a bit.The hacking puzzles were an interesting mechanic. Gave the devs an excuse to have a penalty system without compromising the meat of the game. Simple 5x5 puzzles that have to be completed under time constraints and without the ability to use X's. The one time I failed one was because my mouse slipped and I got erroneously penalized. Other than that I finished every single one of them with 30 seconds to a minute to spare. I think it could do without the time penalties. An inexperienced player will choke under the pressure anyway, no need to add insult to injury imo. I got heavily penalized in the final one, also because of a mouse slip (my deskpad is warped in an odd way, it's quite frustrating but I guess that's what you get for $15), and yet I still finished it with like, 15 seconds to spare.That said, good game. I enjoyed it very much, even though Honor is a terrible detective that IRL would have screwed up every crime scene and caused all the perps to walk free because of the questionable legality with which the evidence was obtained :3
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: There's been a murder, and only you can solve it because literally every single item and object you find on the floor is just a grid surrounded by numbers! Oh goodness. Can you use the powers of maths, numbers, puzzles and picross to solve murders? Hopefully, as that's... Murder by Numbrs. - Realistically, Murder by Numbers is a visual novel that operates as an excuse to do picross puzzles. Do I need an excuse to do picross puzzles? No. Does it stop them from being fun? No. The game slowly eases you in with a variety of simple puzzles and before you know it you'll be using every possible skill in your picross book to solve crimes. They're just nifty and the puzzles are plentiful and frequent. - That's not to dismiss the visual novel aspect of the game, which is a constantly pleasant parade of characters, primarily focusing on Honor and SCOUT. There's just so many good vibes in this game and watching your two plucky detectives-in-training solve crime and try and work out who they are is just so wonderful. A sense of warmth radiates from the game's story at most turns, and it isn't just simply the pooling blood of the murder victims.- Later on in the game the puzzles do begin to get a little... obscure. Either I eventually suffered some form of puzzle-based face blindness, but you will find yourself going from a single chapter of the game lasting a few hours, filled with 10s of puzzles, to spending an entire hour on about two or three puzzles. There's a lot of sitting down and staring at a screen with not a lot changing, so I'd suggest maybe a podcast for the background noise. - The grand mystery of who did the murder is rarely that grand. From the get go you can normally begin to work out who committed the crime, normally as they'd loudly profess something deeply incriminating that no one else picked up on, falling short of turning to the camera and winking. Mainly because they're 2D sprites and can't turn. You may get a tad frustrated being pulled this way and that when you've long worked out the case. Sure, it doesn't have any Ace Attorney level of last minute twists and turns that could give you legal whiplash, but the game spends a lot of time keeping your obvious declaration just out of reach.The negatives of the game are some deep, niche critiques of an otherwise wonderful puzzle game. It may possibly be worth getting it on something a little more portable, as you will be spending a lot of time just looking at the screen and not much else, trying to solve your way out of a paper bag, but for a delightfully colourful and joyous story filled with quips, gags and fun characters it is definitely worth the go if you're a picross fan!More thoughts !
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I'd give the game a good 4.7. The story was funny and snarky but complete with the serious tones. I struggled a bit with Case 3 since it got harder but Case 4 went way up in difficulty. However, I have no complaints on that, it was still a very rewarding gameplay. This game would be perfect for nonogram beginners and advanced level players as it gives instructions and aids in case a player gets stuck. All around, a good game for it's story and gameplay, missing nothing. I only wish the lab scene in Case 4 didn't go the way it did but the ending was still pleasant.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Some people believe that technology will eventually reach a point where each person's entertainment can be custom-generated to fit their individual taste perfectly. TV shows will be created by artificial intelligence with computer-generated "actors" that don't exist, incorporating everything the viewer loves and avoiding everything they dislike. Games will design themselves around the player, combining all of their favorite mechanics, styles, and other elements into something perfectly suited for them.If that day ever comes, I'm pretty sure the system will send me a version of Murder by Numbers that never ends.This game definitely won't be for everyone. But the people it's for, it is  for. If you enjoy the "components" (Ace Attorney games, Picross puzzles, etc.), don't hesitate to pick this up.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Addictive puzzles + fun visual novel style story = a real good time.This game has single-handedly turned me on to picross puzzles. They are challenging but accessible, and the fact that turning on hints for what rows/columns can be updated doesn't hurt your score means you can still ask for help in a way that doesn't give too much away from the puzzle. The story is honestly very nice and fun, and I can never get enough of the 90s throwback stuff. Highly recommended even if you aren't normally a puzzle gamer, and if you've never done picross but fancy yourself a sudoku every now and again, this game is a guaranteed hit.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of Picross type puzzles and Phoenix Wright investigation styles, this game is DEFINITELY for you.For those with less experience with the puzzle system beforehand, there is a decently steep learning curve, but it's super rewarding once you've learned the ins and outs.I'm only through the first section, but the game's story is, thus far, fantastic.  Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: It's a lot of fun but the target demographic here is pretty small, you not only have to be ready to commit to a LOT of nonogram puzzles and also be into the ace attorney-esque visual novel style. But if you know what you've signed up for, I think you'll enjoy it. Be careful in Cases 3 and 4, as you can easily miss puzzles that would prevent you from getting an S rank without another playthrough of the case. This happened to me in Case 3, and it was quite frustrating not being able to go back and do specifically that puzzle, but the rest of the case as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I was doubting on whether to give this a positive review because some friends liked what I didn't; but if I'm not honest there's not point on doing reviews. The story, characters and graphics are cute and neat, like a fun mystery series, it has enough variety in its settings, and given it's a visual novel I can see why that would be enough for you to enjoy; but the gameplay ruins it for me.The gameplay is mostly an adventure game/visual novel style way of investigating and talking, but when you examine something or by moments in the plot you have to complete a nonogram. There's no new rules to be adapted, just that and a veeeeery granular escalation of difficulty; and that's the problem. I like nonograms but as a brain turn-off thing that after finishing one I'm done with, so having to complete so many of them constantly feels like a chore, there's nothing new or rewarding enough about completing them, it stops the story dead for too long and you end up wishing they weren't there to begin with and just enjoy the story. It's also tonally inconsistent, since the upbeat tone over them carries even in dead serious moments that break the tension of the moment. Unlike a Layton game, where you also do constant tangential stuff to the mystery to advance, there's no variety that feels like a fun different puzzle to resolve, and while those can have a variable duration, many taking you less than a minute, here they will take you the same time, a few minutes, which makes it feel more like they are stalling you.It's not the most tedious thing in the world, so if you want to experience the story because the rest appeals to you I get it; but personally the gameplay made me not enjoy sadly.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I had such a good time playing this game and was sad when it ended.Murder by Numbers is a combination of Phoenix Wright and a type of number puzzle that I had never played before but is apparently a very well-known genre called Nonogram or Picross. The most important thing to help you decide whether you would enjoy this game is whether you would enjoy solving Nonograms, because you will be doing lots and lots of nonograms. If you do (or if you think you might) then I have little doubt you would enjoy this game, because it is provides a very nice interface for the puzzles and adds a cute visual novel story (which is similar to the investigation parts of the Phoenix Wright games). If you wouldn't like solving lots of nonograms then you almost certainly wouldn't like this game: The story is well-done (although occasionally silly), but it is "interrupted" constantly to solve more nonogram puzzles.Nonograms are kind of like minesweeper or Sudoku. You have to solve a grid and decide whether each square should be filled or not, and you do this based on deductive reasoning about how many sequential squares are filled in each row and column. No puzzle in Murder by Numbers requires guessing, although there were times when it can be fairly challenging figuring out how to progress (although I got better by the end; I don't know how the puzzle difficulty compares to other nonogram games). There are a handful of times you will have to solve simple versions quickly before time runs out, but this is the exception; usually you have as much time as you need.I would be remiss if I didn't give a special shout out to the main theme, which is amazing! No matter how many times I heard it I couldn't help but smile whenever it was the soundtrack for a puzzle :)
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: On a superficial level this is Phoenix Wright meets Picross. However, where in Phoenix Wright the characters are so exaggerated that they are all basically caricatures, the characters here are believable (apart from a few side characters). The story and the crime cases also feel real and based in reality - except the fact that one of the main characters is a flying, sentient robot. :)The puzzles are on the easy side and are rarely bigger than 15x15. For a Picross veteran like me they're almost too easy. I was able to 100% the game without hints in 22 hours. On the other hand, having huge puzzles would detract from the story, so I think they made the right call there.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I look forward to a potential sequel, although it will be interesting to see how The storytelling was good, though I do wish there was a faster way to skip through dialogue for when you want to replay cases. Characters were all very unique and funny in their own ways. Scout was obviously my favorite, he is the embodiment of innocence and wonder, which was adorable comic relief at times. There were some interesting twists that I enjoyed (though maybe they were more predictable for other people, I'm not all that good at predicting twists in stories because I just get very engrossed in it) and I even laughed/cried out loud at some points.I liked that there was a positive message behind the story, too.The picross element was a decent challenge but not impossible, so I got to expand/improve my picross skills. I really enjoy picross anyways, so the story element was really just a bonus for me, and I also liked the bonus puzzles for completing the story.I typically don't play games with the sound on so I can't speak to the quality of the soundtrack, but I loved the art and animation. The expressions of the characters in various situations were done quite well, even for the more stoic character of Detective Cross. I really do hope they make a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the storyline and the jokes were so cute. The 90's theme was nice and nostalgic. The artwork was great but the main reason i am giving this a positive review is that the picross puzzles were actually fun. I enjoyed both the puzzles and story so much i did not find i was rushing through either. (im sad i have finished the game!) I would definitely recommend this to anyone who likes these type of puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Hey, do you like Picross (Nonogram) games? If your answer is not a resounding "YES MY GOD YES" then Murder by Numbers is going to be challenging for you. Not just because there are many, many picross puzzles, but also because it throws them at you when you just want to forward the plot an extra sentence. I thought this was an adventure novel kind of game with picross thrown in.No. This is a picross game with an adventure novel game thrown in. Is the story interesting? Yes! Are the characters interesting? Mostly! Does the music slap? Absolutely! It's a shame the game gets in its own way sometimes by reminding you that you came here for picross.Overall I enjoyed it, I really did. But I've done enough picross to last me a good, long time.Would I recommend it? Yeah! But only if you really like picross.Pros:- The music slaps. Hands down I will fight you if you disagree. - Character designs, set dressing etc? All great.- Characters themselves? Mostly good! Some stereotypes are marched _right out_ but overall, pretty good. I legitimately enjoyed (and loathed) characters, so good for them!- It has picross puzzles- Intro video also slaps and is worth a mention- Has a variety of hint/assist systems to help you out**- Lead character is a WoC, which is great!- The game actually talks to the difficulties of the LGTBQ community (both modern issues as well as those in the mid 90s) which I was impressed with.Cons:- it throws picross puzzles at you with every opportunity. The game gets in it's own way sometimes with the puzzles. There are too many conversations that are interrupted mid-scene because someone shows you something, and WHOOPS IT'S PUZZLE TIME.- Whilst the music does indeed slap. there are only 3 or 4 songs played during the puzzle-solving. I put close to 40 hours into this game as of this writing solving all the puzzles, and the music does get old.- There are some plotlines that only progress because characters make extremely silly decisions JUST BECAUSE. It's frustrating.- ** Using the hint systems punishes your score, which whilst I understand, is frustrating because it gates the game to more casual players- There is basically _no_ variation to the picross puzzle formula. You get timed puzzle sequences, and normal puzzles. that's it. It get's repetitive in a hurry. I wish the devs had added like, # of lives in high-stake puzzles, longer timed puzzles, etc. a little variation would go a long way- The story is effectively rail-roaded. none of your choices really matter other than a couple different dialogue lines.- The adventure mode takes zero chances to innovate. It is an extremely thin version of the Phoenix Wright games.- As of the writing of this review: All achievements are broken, which means that despite S-ranking each case, I only unlocked 2 achievements. The dev team have not responded to any of the community posts about it. Bummer.Other:- I hated Ryan and Sharron? Shannon? Honor's mom. So much. So much I hated them.- If you've been in an abusive relationship with a partner or loved one... consider this a trigger warning cause wowzers bowzers do Ryan and the mother make every interaction with them just the pits.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I've ever had a game waste more of my time than this one.  There are a lot of puzzles in this game, and even with that, it's probably 90% bad visual novel and 10% puzzle game.  The amount of story you have to click thru is completely absurd and totally kills the game.  I stopped paying any attention to the story after the first of four chapters and just clicked and clicked and clicked through the dialogue bubbles as quickly as the game would let me, and even doing that I spent hours and hours looking at the stupid story.  It was so frustrating and made getting through this crappy game such a slog.As for the picross puzzles, they sucked.  I enjoy fair picross puzzles.  I consider a picross puzzle fair if it can be solved step-by-step using the information on the board.  If it can't be solved without guessing, then it if unfair.  All the puzzles in the first chapter were fair, so slogging thru the annoying story was tolerable.  But after chapter 1, they are all very unfair.  You can't even begin to solve some of them without guessing and all of them would require multiple correct guesses in a row to get right without a walkthrough or hints.  F that, where's the fun in puzzles that require lucky guesses?
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Murder by Numbers is a fantastic mash up of Phoenix Wright and Picross. I love how the developers were able to make Picross a sensible mechanic in the story.Two problems that need addressing:1) Give a little love to your completists. I finished case 3 and soon after realized that I must have not found all evidence (some evidence is paramount to keep the plot moving, others are just flavor) and did not get a good enough rating to unlock all of the secondary puzzles. To finish those missing puzzles I need to redo the entire case which takes hours. It would be nice to have some way of completing those puzzles.2) During my search for a way to complete said missing puzzles without starting the whole case over I clicked back on case 3. That immediately overwrote my save file meaning that now I think I have to redo Case 3 no matter what. There should at least be a case select screen if you've unlocked them. (there may be already I just might not have found it.)So I am not sure if I will finish the game now...However, it is a fantastic game, it is very fun, but some little problems are nagging at me.

_childDocuments_.review: Murder By Numbers is a genuinely sweet, cute, heartwarming picross game. About murder. If you enjoy that genre, and picross, I think you'll really like Murder By Numbers.The puzzles are fun, and well designed as a picross enjoyer. _childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: On one hand, this is a neat concept, and the general execution (story, writing, puzzle design) is all good. The characters are likeable (or not, when they need to be), the humor is generally on point. it's got LGBT+ positive themes, the mysteries are pretty solid. There's a feeeew contrivances in the narrative, especially in the last chapter, and a few limitations of the game engine (notable in portrait swapping - most jarring with a character who has an injured arm and which arm it is keeps switching all the time).But the two biggest problems I have... one. There's. Too much picross. And the pacing suffers from it. More of this game is spent puzzling than actually interacting with the narrative, and it feels like this gets more extreme the longer the game goes on too. Just in the main game, there's a loooot of puzzles. And then you go past that to the postgame, which... the way of unlocking can be especially annoying, especially when you just miss a puzzle outright and have to replay the entire chapter, puzzles and all, just to unlock the last few bonus puzzles. And the scenes locked behind the puzzles aren't very satisfying rewards, either. I don't mind having the bonus puzzles at all though, they're generally fun and more content that isn't clogging up the story itself is fine.Also, the music... there's like four main tracks for all of the puzzles and only one of them is remotely appropriate for a chill puzzle game like this, and I got so sick of these tracks that I had to start muting the game and putting on my own music in the background because the music itself was getting so distractingly annoying. That's. A bit of a flaw, isn't it.Ehh. It's a cool concept and I think with better pacing it could be executed well, and as far as the VN portions of this game go they're pretty much spot on 99% of the time, but it ends up not fully feeling satisfying just due to the problems it does have. And I don't really know how to solve those problems, either, other than straight up reducing the amount of puzzles per chapter and having to rewrite the story to account for that. I'd still overall recommend it, especially for the price there's quite a lot of game here, but do be wary that it can drag in the later chapters.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game if you love Picross/Nonograms. Most puzzles are 15x15 but 15x20 does make an appearance near the end. The story was enjoyable, but pretty much a straight visual novel. No decisions to make, no fail states, no player impact on the story. Unlike other murder mystery games this one doesn't get bogged down in dialogue and moves at a very snappy pace, quickly getting you back into more puzzles after a nice break. Nice, upbeat soundtrack too for puzzle solving.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute banger of a Picross x Visual Novel crossover which comes with a good 20-30h of content. (Unless you're like me and like to complete/find every puzzle without using hints, then it's about 30h-50h!)I love me a good picross game and I'm happy to say that I have now fully completed the game 100% with no hints and all the extra puzzles. The puzzles are fun and it's got a nice story a la Ace Attorney!Each case is unique and they're all quite enjoyable. Definitely had to giggle here and there. The Artwork of the characters is stunning and god do I appreciate a diverse cast, no one is boring - even while some act like the cliche trope they portray. They're all sooo loveable, especially SCOUT, I became quite attached to him in the end.The entire Soundtrack is very catchy too - I've spent many hours just humming some of the songs simply because they get stuck in your head so much.Only thing that bugged me a lil' is that some picross-art just look fuzzy after completion. I feel like they're a bit overly shaded - which sometimes makes it really hard to recognise what the hell you were actually solving. Just a nit pick though and didn't really take away any of the fun.All in all a great puzzle game, I'd personally pick it up full prize and I'm already looking forward to a sequel! Certainly will give you plenty hours of brain food!

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! Played it all the way through with my girlfriend since we both enjoy logic puzzles. S ranked every puzzle with no hints!Cute story, cheesy at times but still good. The puzzles are really fun and challenging, comparable to sudoku. I wanted more puzzles at the end, I hope there is dlc or a sequel coming! Though by the end we were pretty much experts at solving these puzzles, so the designers might have to shake it up a bit to keep it interesting.Highly recommend if you enjoy solving logic puzzles!

_childDocuments_.review: With cute characters and interesting puzzles Murder by Numbers is a great game for those who like puzzles with something extra on the side.The character designs are all so good, I think the games visuals is one of my favourite aspects as it's well polished and sticks out in my mind. I haven't played a lot of picross and I'm hopeless at those type of puzzles but I really enjoyed my time, it was fun to figure out what I had found as S.C.O.U.T.Only real cons is the gameplay loop can be kind of... grating after a while? But that just might be because I'm not great at picross so I'd take that with a grain of salt, I did enjoy solving the mystery but the last case kind of dragged at the end.I'll sit patiently for a sequel though, who could say no to more S.C.O.U.T?

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a picross addict, so this appeals to me. Only a few minor gripes i have:- There's no pause options during dialogue. (change settings, quit game, etc)- No controller support :(- No option to reset/start over puzzle. (have to quit to title screen)+ Story is okay, so far (chapter 2)+ Lots of puzzle+ Good deal

_childDocuments_.review: This game is essentially Phoenix Wright meets picross. Murder, puzzles, investigation, the whole schbang. Snarky dialogue and interesting characters carry the story, and the picross carry a majority of the game play.  The music is fantastic, and no matter how many times i hear and watch the intro, I never get tired of it. The puzzles start easy, getting harder as it continues. Some of the 15x15 seem like you have to get some incorrect boxes just to figure out the shapes, but all the puzzles are still fun to complete. Where the game stands out is the characters and writing. Each character is unique, and while the story is somewhat predictable, it is still interesting enough to keep me entertained. Where the game struggles in my opinion is the crime part. Unlike Phoenix Wright, where this game seems to take inspiration, questioning and showing evidence seems linear. Rather then question characters and catching them lie, it feels like just asking all the questions, and then when the time to determine the killer is just pick from a list, which by that point, it becomes obvious who it is. Perhaps if the game continues, a more in depth questioning system could be added, making the game somewhat harder and more interestin gin these parts.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Great presentation, but failed execution. The character design / art from the creator of Hatoful Boyfriend is fantastic, the music from the composer for the Phoenix Wright games is jazzy and boppy and marvellous, but the gameplay is very weak picross puzzles that fail to represent anything in terms of pixel art until the puzzle is completely solved, which are unlocked by a tier of tedious image examination below pixel hunting - there's not even anything to FIND in the image you're searching, it's just an invisible hot spot. The items are supposedly objects you identify via the picross puzzle, but none of them are located in sensible places within the image, and none of them are visible. Additionally the writing is both weak and mean-spirited, with the character design work let down by broad stereotyping and unsympathetic, shallow caricatures. I really wanted to like this game, but honestly just get the OST and use your imagination - you'll have a better experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Murder by Numbers is a visual novel styled detective/mystery game, that uses Picross puzzles as its method of gameplay. The story premise starts simple, the main protagonist is a detective-playing actress that gets herself involved in a murder case, after meeting SCOUT, a robot with visual recognition functions, that has mysteriously awoken with his memories lost, they team up together to solve the many incidents they somehow end up getting involved in, taking a mantle of a wannabe detective duo while trying to learn more about the past of SCOUT.The gameplay options are simple and concise. When the situation allows for it you can move through different locations relevant to the current chapter, question people and present evidence to them to get information or reactions. Additionally, you can scan the locations for any suspicious looking spots, here is where the Picross tie in happens, to scan for items, you'll have to solve Picross puzzles that will reveal evidence that may help the ongoing investigation.That is the simple explanation of the game, though I have a few comments about it. Firstly, besides the puzzles you'll encounter through the chapters, there are some extra set of puzzles on the "SCOUT's Memories" section. The way these are unlocked are by reaching different "Rankings" on each chapter, earning points as you complete puzzles. The thing is that if you happen to use hints during a chapter, you will miss out on bonus points, which from my experience of using only a few hints in Chapter 1, will not allow you to get the S rank and unlock all bonus puzzles for that chapter. Forcing you to replay the chapter and beat all the puzzles without using hints if you want to unlock them. This previous realization was annoying as they don't tell you this prior to experiencing it on your own, so it lead to being careful on the remaining chapters and use save scumming if I needed a clue on a puzzle, so that I could clear them "without hints" and get all bonus points.  Even IF you do this, there are a few missable puzzles that can cause this frustration if you progress the story too fast in some situations. Another slight con is that there's no way to replay the puzzles found in the chapters unless you replay them completely, possibly a "Gallery" where you could access them would have been a good addition.Besides these minor gripes the game was very enjoyable, most cases were interesting and engaging, and it wraps up nicely for the few lingering questions that arise through the story. If you're doing the puzzles on your own then most of the playtime will be spent in them, the story on the surface is not incredibly long, but by the end it's interesting enough with its theme and characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: A mix between Picross puzzles and a general "Ace Attorney" vibe with character dialog and plot progression. From the VN side of things, this game is missing the common 'previous dialog' menu which you should be able to review if you ever click past a piece of dialog by accident and want to read it again. It also lacks any means to quickly skip past text you've already seen. Also, its very easy to accidentally lock yourself out of getting an S rank on any given chapter, forcing you to start the entire chapter over for a pretty minor bonus, there should've been a system to let you just play whatever puzzles you didn't solve with the highest possible score in order to get to S rank quickly. Some character designs were alright, some were pretty iffy, and the overall plot seems like it was written for young adults, which seems odd for a game that's covering pretty serious murders at times. Solving the puzzles was the best part, and it was nice to chill out and work through them while listening to something in the background.I'd only recommend for people who really like Picross puzzles, and even then I'd recommend getting it on sale. Hopefully the creators can improve upon the formula for next time, if they wish to continue :)
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: *SPOILER FREE*Pros:- Easy to understand tutorial, 2 difficulty modes ( I do nonograms daily so I went with NORMAL difficulty)- Character & background designs! - Great balance between gameplay and story.- Nonograms/Pictograms, lots of them. Also additional ones that you unlock while clearing the story ( this feature has it's downside too unfortunately). - Except for typical 10x10 and 15x15, the developers threw in some 10x15 and 15x20 puzzles which was FUN!- Art in general. I loved the intro movie and some more detailed scenes whenever important stuff would happen. - Auto-save. Good thing it's there. - The main plot (Scout's origins etc.) was pretty cool. - Funny jokes ;) - It's hard to get stuck, game makes it very easy to move forward. Cons:- No 'undo' button, which would be very helpful when solving bigger nonograms.- No voice-over, makes it harder to focus on the story. - CASE 3 was kinda ... eeeh? Some characters and their stories felt weak. - The soundtrack... It's repetitive and gets soooo annoying after the first couple of hours (same with SFX that would sometimes crash and I would have to listen to scout's radar noise for 15 minutes, driving me to insanity). Sometimes you get SFX only in text but there is no actual sound matched to it in the game which... seems kinda lazy. I muted the game and was listening to YT in the background. - If you use any assist during puzzle solving, you get no bonuses for solving it. Do it ONCE and you won't get the highest score for the episode, which in return makes you unable to unlock SCOUT's memories. If you want to redo this one puzzle... good luck, you have to repeat the whole f**king episode, unless you save your game before every puzzle (no, u don't). - If you use assist it cancels your bonus score even if u reset the whole puzzle. - Almost no achievements. Not necessarily a big con, but I feel like it would motivate me more if I could show of my "finished all nonograms without assist" achievement or sth. Just a suggestion. - Cases seem kind of dragged out.I am happy about finishing this game, but... I don't really feel too satisfied with the ending, as I feel Honor's relationships didn't get enough closure and Nonograms could be bigger in the end. I did enjoy it most of the time, but got bored by the end of it a little. Last Case felt like it was dragging out forever. I did play some "murder mystery" visual novels before (like all Danganronpa for example) so I felt like the story could be more... surprising. Hope that helps anyone!

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game expecting some good picross puzzles and a mediocre story. The story was actually more interesting and engaging than I anticipated. There were times where I was even wanting more of the story and less of the puzzles. The soundtrack is absolutely phenomenal and the artwork is equally great. Definitely recommend to anyone who enjoys picross or even just mystery games (although this does lean more on the visual novel side than true investigation and deduction).In terms of game length, I still have to finish a few of the bonus puzzles from cases 3 and 4 but I have completed the main story as of this review. The game only has four cases, each getting progressively longer. Each case also has a set of unique bonus puzzles that are unlocked based on the rank you got on the associated case (F, D, C, B, A, and S).These times are complete estimates since I didn't keep track but I want to say case 1 was somewhere around 3-4 hours to complete both the case and its bonus puzzles. The second and third cases are both a few hours longer. The final case is significantly longer at maybe 9-10 hours to complete.

_childDocuments_.review: This game deserves way more credit, attention, and acclaim than it has received. For how much effort has been put into this game, it is criminally underrated (No pun intended). For those who are interested in games like the Phoenix Wright trilogy, this game is perfect for you. It combines the exciting world of murder mysteries in a 1990's L.A. with the challenge of completing pictocross puzzles to find evidence and further the story. It's remarkable how well the balance is between the story and the puzzles. Each are given proper time without either overshadowing the other. Where this game shines most has to be the characters. Each character is incredibly well written with a beautiful character design to match. I couldn't help but fall in love with characters like K.C., Detective Cross, Becky, Honor, and especially Scout. There were even minor characters who had me hooked based solely on their character designs, such as Bill, Eiren, and Fran. By all means, if you have any interest in either visual novel games or puzzles, then Murder by Numbers is a game you're practically guaranteed to enjoy. An absolute delight, start to finish. :)

_childDocuments_.review: A hybrid visual novel/picross game. My play time is nearly 40 hours, but I'd estimate the VN parts are only about 10-12 hours of that; I spent most of the time staring blankly at picross boards and erasing/restarting after making a few bad moves. Turns out I'm really bad at picross! But I still found it a satisfyingly fun challenge, and it's a lot more manageable in easy mode.The character artwork is lovely and very expressive, and I'm a fan of how the chunky white outlines make everything pop from the background. The writing is entertaining, with some memorable characters and amusing dialogue. It's very Phoenix Wright-esque; not as over-the-top in tone as Phoenix Wright, but enough so that things like "how exactly do police investigations work in this universe" and "why would the killer do something that obvious" don't really feel out of place. The conclusion of the story is pretty predictable, but there are some surprises along the way.The music unfortunately gets gratingly repetitive during the longer puzzles, but aside from that, my main criticisms are purely technical:- No backlog or skip text options.- No way to skip puzzles when replaying.- No way to undo recent moves or automatically clear the board.- Minor save/load bugs; saving in the middle of a question drops you back to the main investigation screen on loading, and saving in the middle of a puzzle resets all the completion indicators on loading.Hopefully these can be fixed in a future update. The game was enjoyable enough that I didn't find the technical issues too annoying, and I'd still recommend it to fans of casual puzzle games and stylized mystery VNs.
