_childDocuments_.review: Disappointment. Utter disappointment.It was really exciting to come across this game- I love detective games, I love picross. The art looks cool to boot, surely I'll love this! Turns out Murder by Numbers offers the worst of both worlds. Maybe it could be a good stop for tourists to dip their toes in, but it will be a letdown to fans of either genre.The picross half of the game has a unique setting- you are analyzing the pixelated output of a robot's low definition scanner, cool stuff. Using everyone's familiar baseline, Mario's Picross, as a standard the difficulty of these puzzles are in line with Mario's moderate puzzles, they don't quite reach the difficulty of the last few rows but still take effort to complete. Outside of the simpler first chapter, the puzzle complexity remains static throughout. There are actually some cool puzzles here I haven't encountered before, but quite a few are just slight variations of the same object (and there are even a couple exact copy-pastes). The only real problem I encountered with these was the game giving free information when it shouldn't, even on the highest difficulty without hints. The numbers on the side grey out when the pixels on the line are in the correct format. If the line is 5 pixels long and the number is 3 pixels consecutively, any consecutive 3 pixels will grey out the number regardless of placement. Murder by Numbers' system gives away free information by accident. It's hard to explain this in text format but I'll try with this example. Let's say you have a 10 pixel long horizontal line whose numbers are 1 1 1, and a 10 pixel long vertical line near the middle of the puzzle, whose number is 10. For your first move you fill in the vertical line, and Murder by Numbers greys out the 2nd 1 in the horizontal line, even though there is space remaining for all 1s to be to the left or right of the vertical line and nothing to contradict either of those options. This could be solved easily with a patch that prevents numbers from greying out on the highest difficulty, hopefully the devs patch that in.The detective half of the game is a mess. The inventory system exists exclusively to show other characters items, not to examine or use them. You are unable to make any decisions or deductions of your own throughout the entire game. This is incredibly important in detective games, and especially important for visual novels to keep their gameplay and story engaging.  The only thing worse than being thrown on a linear path for a supposed investigation, is being thrown on an incorrect linear path. Your character always solves the case no matter what you do. Even if you choose the wrong conclusions purposefully, there is no lose state or impact on the story- your character just backtracks the conversation until you select the right choice to progress the story. Guess what, that choice you are forced into selecting is always the wrong option even when you know better! There are four chapters in the game, and you are forced to get everything wrong in each of them .  Auto-clicker progressing with the same results as a human player is a sign of a bad visual novel, let alone an investigation game.Oh, and I hope you like the screen shaking and/or flashing white after every other sentence. As for the art style that I initially thought looked great, it attracted me to the game after all, it's a facade. As if the rest of the game hadn't already let me down at this point, the execution turned out to be lazy.  My assumption was that the white borders around the characters was a stylistic choice to make the characters look like paper cutouts. This was invalidated because there are many scenes where the borders are missing- if this had been a stylistic decision they would be consistently present. Turns out the artist was just too lazy to key them out. Who knows, maybe the started drawing the characters on the wrong layer and couldn't be bothered to fix it. Every character just gets mirrored as well- an artifact of memory conservation in retro games, but an indicator of sloppy corner-cutting for the past 30+ years  (especially in a game focused on so many asymmetric detailed characters).Ultimately, I can't recommend it at this price or sale price. Pick it up at a ~90% discount or in a bundle if you are curious. I wasted this weekend's rainy evenings stuck indoors slogging through this and regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: Murder By Numbers is a thoroughly engaging and enjoyable puzzle visual novel. Its characters follow the Ace Attorney style where they are based around a gimmick, but that gimmick is just the basic pitch, and their dialog reveals little clues that flesh out each character. If you like Picross, and cute indie visual novels, this one is a nice little time waster. They don't hold your hand at Picross, but if you want hints and tips, they have a whole section at the top, which is especially good for those who care more about the story.  Big shout outs to the composers and artists, as well. They did an incredible job on this.About my only word of warning is that while the storytelling is good, don't expect a mind blowing plot or series of twists. It doesn't feel like a traditional mystery where the seed are sewed early in, and the confrontation wraps everything up. To use two older shows as comparison, it's a lot less Columbo, and a lot more Murder She Wrote. The solutions to the mysteries usually introduces a bunch of red herrings and then it has one or two pieces right at the end of the case that really lead to who the killer is. It never really effected my enjoyment, but I would just say this more as caution for those looking for an exact Ace Attorney experience. It's not Ace Attorney, but I think Ace Attorney fans will enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: okay to very good if you know what you're getting yourself into. Otherwise: stay clear.So...I admit I got this for my steam deck as an alternative for Mario picross. I was slightly curious about the story campaign, but had no expectations. And I gotta admit: first impressions on either front weren't great.* like many video games, the story starts with character exposition. Quite a lot of text to plow through, and though the writing was better than I'd anticipated, the characters (aside the protagonist) ARE caricatures. But I can't say it bothered me. After all: it's not like I wanted EVEN MORE exposition. :P* the puzzles start basic and ramp up in difficulty. With quite some earlier experience with griddlers, I expected easy puzzles at first. Unfortunately, it misses a few quality of life enhancements. Most notably: there's no indication if you screw up. And with these puzzles, that can mean you might have to restart if you've accidentally misplaced even a single dot.So...the game didn't had the best start for me (note: as a 40'ish male all-round gamer I'm probably not the main audience to begin with). But I've got to be fair: I became intrigued by the story. Maybe despite the characters, but more likely BECAUSE they're so stereotypical, the writing was good and didn't treat the inevitable murder as something downright comedic. And okay: scanning for clues is a gimmick, but questioning people, presenting evidence and multiple dialogue options...it was all more than I expected. As in: Murder by numbers isn't a griddler "with a story", but a game where both aspects get roughly equally much game time and they complement each other.I won't deny it's a bit rough around the edges and could use some improvements, but it's by no means a bad game at all.Still...I've got to stress out this isn't even a "love or hate" kind of game...it's a game for an audience who likes both a whodonnit mystery (you get four cases here) and griddler puzzles. If you like only one of those, I wouldn't recommend it.But as it stands: I like both. So: a (FOR ME!) well deserved thumbs up. :-)
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, I hate to do this, because I am enjoying the game and eager to find out what happens to the characters, but I can't recommend this game. Why? Because they took an interesting story with neat characters... and stapled a picross workbook to it. Admittedly I'm not the worlds biggest fan of picross to start with, but do we REALLY need to a puzzle to reveal a CCTV tape... when a character already said 5 seconds ago that he brought it? Why do we need SCOUT to do these picross puzzles in the first place, it's not like Honor is blind in game. It would make sense if Honor found the object first and then you do the picross puzzle with SCOUT to analyze it, find hidden traces and etc, but as it is it can be hard to know how to finish the puzzle without knowing what the end product is going to look like, and sometimes even when you solve the puzzle you cant tell what it is without the title over it. If you want to play this game, just pull up the steam guide with all the puzzle solutions so you don't pull your hair out in frustration when you realize you've worked yourself into a corner for the umpteenth time.

_childDocuments_.review: For starters I'd like to state that I was a total picross noobie when I started this game and it did take me a while to get a hang of it. But the game has ways tot help a beginner out and it was fun to learn, so I wouldn't let the puzzles deter you from getting this one.Murder by Numbers is a wild combination of a detective game with an Ace Attorney feel (No surprise with the art style and the composer being Masakazu Sugimori, same as the first few Ace Attorney games), picross puzzles and the 90's (both the good and the bad things). And somehow it makes it all work.I'm not going to get too much into the story or individual cases since these are better left for everyone to experience for themselves. However what I will say is that there is a lot more meat to the overall story and especially the sub-plots than one might initially expect from a somewhat silly looking game like this. Something that especially stood out to me is how the year the game is set in, 1996, is represented not just in style or the language used, but also a lot of the prominent problems this time had including some very specific misogyny in different industries or the way certain people groups were talked about or treated. The time and setting isn't just there for throwaway jokes, but has been thought through throughout the game.Additionally the way the picross puzzles are integrated into the game makes a lot of sense. SCOUT, our little computer buddy, scans around in a room to see what there is and the picross part is him putting together what he found. I do have to say though that about 75% of the time I could not tell what I just finished until scout turned it colourful and even then I wasn't always certain I saw the item I was supposed to in it. So sadly you can't use guessing the item as a cheaty way of finishing the puzzle faster.So in conclusion: Whether you've done picross puzzles before or not, this gem is well worth considering if you're in search for a fun story that has quite a lot more meat to it than it seems at first glance.

_childDocuments_.review: Gotta be honest, when I first saw the store page of this game, I didn't think of it much. But turns out,  is actually pretty good!Let me tell you a bit about the plot. There's an actress named Honor Mizrahi, and her life is mostly doing okay, until one day she finds SCOUT — a weird robot that was apparently made for helping detectives with solving crimes. On the same day, a murder happens, so Honor and SCOUT decide to work together to investigate the crime.There are four chapters, which means you'll investigate four different cases. All of this time you will also be learning about what happened to SCOUT before he met Honor. The plot is okay: I can't say that it was mindblowing, but I can't say that it was bad either. I've seen some people say that it's predictable, but I have to disagree on that. You can guess some things, yes, but most of the time the story is so ridiculous, you have no idea what will happen next. The main thing that makes this novel special is that you'll need to solve nonograms to progress. I should confess that I'm addicted to nonograms (as awful as it sounds, yeah), and that was the exact reason why I wanted to try this out. The puzzles are okay, there's not much else to say about them. I was a bit worried that they're going to be too easy, since I've solved a lot of nonograms, but the difficulty level was appropriate.Also I liked that nonograms were explained: basically, when SCOUT sees things, he needs to interpret them first, since he is a robot. You solving the puzzles is him processing the image. I thought that's a cool explanation.+ Great artwork+ Memorable soundtrack+ Funny jokes+ Easy 100% achievements (you simply need to finish all of the chapters, the rank is not important)- No "Skip" button (it's a must in every visual novel, why??)- You can't replay certain puzzles from chapters to get a higher rankI agree with other players saying that the game could be better, but I enjoyed it nonetheless. It has some kind of a nostalgic TV vibe, which feels as if you're watching an old show with characters who are all dear to your heart. And for that, I'm deeply thankful.

_childDocuments_.review: I love Ace Attorney, I love Picross. So you can imagine how excited I was about this mashup. Sadly, it does fall flat a little bit. It lacks the intensity and mystery the Ace Attorney Games, and looking for clues seems a little random. Where in Ace Attorney, you specifically try to target areas of interest, here you're just shoving your cursor across the screen until it starts to blink, upon which a Picross Puzzle starts. It's very arbitrary. Likewise, there's no court or cross examination sections, at all. It plays much more like a visual novel, but without any branching paths at all and a couple of Picross Puzzles here and there. The story itself is alright, but nothing to write home about. The characters are pretty lovable, though. And the writing is decent, too. This definitely has potential.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: I would actually recommend this game, but only if you absolutely love solving Picross-style puzzles. The story is pretty cool, as visual novels go, but there's no other gameplay other than the puzzles and if you don't enjoy them, following the story will become a chore. I started just entering the solutions from a guide during episode 4 because I just wanted to finish the story.My problems with the game:It's a visual novel, but it's missing many features that are absolutely standard for VNs. You can't advance the dialogue without clicking the mouse. My fingers are so sore! There's no way to go back and review the dialogue so if you accidentally click twice you've missed that screen unless you want to reload a save. And if you really wanted to redo the puzzles there's no way to fast-forward through the story like you can in most VNs.There's no way to access the menu except when you arrive at a choice screen. This has implications for my main problem with the game:The hacking mini-game can absolutely get ****ed! In this you have to complete a number of simple 5x5 puzzles against a time limit. But the limit is VERY harsh. Even on easy difficulty you get fewer puzzles to solve, but a lot of people will struggle. Worse is that when you arrive at a hacking mini-game section, if you fail, you have to try again. You have no opportunity to access the main menu. If you need to change difficulty (because playing with easy mode enabled means you'll get unwanted assists during the regular puzzles) - then you have to Alt-F4 the game, reload, change the difficulty in the main menu, then reload the autosave.In addition, while not a problem for me, the above issues (lack of keyboard support / time limited puzzles) means this game gets 0/10 for accessibility.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Great game overall. Fun character dynamics and Honor is a wonderful main character. You can see how she changes and grows from each solved case. Cheesy and over-dramatic fun. Before you play, keep in mind 3 things. 1: You better love nanogram puzzles. I can't speak for the easy mode, but this  a 20+ hour game. Probably not the game to try them out. 2: Take your time and pace yourself. For either visual novels or puzzle games, its best not to burn yourself out too quick.3: Save regularly. To redue a case, you have to start at the beginning and there is no skip dialogue button.I eagerly await a next installment, but I would like some quality of life/UI improvements. 1: A skip dialogue feature (for replay-ability)2: Music select during puzzles (fun energetic music choices but I don't always want that during a puzzle)3: No Back button in the Main/Pause Menu (especially bad if you click Load Game on accident since it might erase progress)4: The Scanning sections, while cute, could add more to gameplay. It feels mostly like a game of hot n' cold since the green filter and close-up makes it difficult to really search. I relied more on the beeping to find clues.5: The Reset Puzzle button lets out a high pitched noise that hurts the ears.Sorry if this just sounds like a list of complaints, but I did enjoy the game and hope the sequel is even better.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay.... so first off.... I handed a tampon to the gay guy K.C. and his response was to say "I will never understand why they don't put pockets in women's clothing. You want me to hold that for you?"So already, as a woman, 10/10 game. But! If you're here for more that "More Pockets In Womens Clothing" support.This is a REALLY solid game so far and I'm quite enjoying myself! I'm not super far into the game, I've been taking my time with it. Enjoying the funny dialogue. So I have no clue if there's gonna be any court room drama, but the game in general gives fantastic Ace Attorney vibes and I love it for that.You search a room and when your magnifying glass turns red, you will open up a Picross puzzle. If you don't know what that is. It's a type of puzzle game where you've got a cube with boxes in it, outside of each column and row of squares is a series of numbers. That series of numbers helps you figure out which squares need to be colored black and eventually when you get the shape figured out, it will reveal a picture that is made with those squares. It's like Sudoku in the sense that you are figuring out what goes or does not go in a square based on the squares in each room and column.If a row has a 1 3 4, it means that there will be 1 square colored, then at least one space, 3 squares colored, at least one space, and then 4 more colored squares. But if there are 10 squares in that row then you have to figure out which spots the colored squares are based on the other rows and columnsI'm sure I made that sound a LOT more complicated than it needed to be. It's easier than it seems. Long story short though, if you like the general game play of Sudoku. Picross gives a similar vibe.But as you solve puzzles the pictures you make are items that you can hand to someone as evidence. Some stuff progresses the story and other times you'll just get funny dialogue (like K.C. offering to hold my tampon).There is of course *muuuuurdeeeeer* as evidenced by the name. It appears that there are 4 stories to play through and I'm looking forward to it.On the difficulty scale I won't say this game is hard. Probably really not difficult (at least in the first couple hours) if you are good like Picross. I... am not good at Picross. I'm still having fun though and nothing has felt so difficult that's frustrating or so easy that it's annoying and brain dead. So unless you are SUPER into Picross I can say that the first few hours are the perfect amount of challenging.Again the general vibe of Ace Attorney is present and it definitely sells the game. From the humor to the general aesthetic of the game. It IS it's own thing though, in no way does it feel like it's copying it. It just gives the *vibe*. Also gives a very mild Professor Layton vibe, but without the riddles.So if you like Picross and games with that kind of vibe this is a highly recommended title so far. I'm having a very good time with it and also kinda realizing I'm worse at Picross than I thought I was lol.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a fan of Nonograms and this is pretty good. Now, unlike others I've played, this one heavily focuses on the logic aspect and can be extremely challenging. There's a few towards the end that feel like it's nothing but 1's and you only have a few lines with any logical lead. Once you figure out the art style, you can kinda guess where the dots are, but you probably won't guess what you're looking at until you complete the puzzle, which are well drawn.  And with the whole story about solving murders with almost nothing to go one save a few tiny clues that eventually lead to the bigger picture, this type of difficultly works to it's favor, even if it feels a bit tedious at times.   Short version: A Good game with more focus on difficulty, but nothing really huge or hard (No 25x25's or above).

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good idea for a game: a picross (nonogram, hanjie, etc) puzzler embedded in a light animated detective game. Think Pictopix meets Ace Attorney. If you've played those games, you probably already know just from that description whether you want to buy this game or not—I did! The puzzles are not very difficult, mostly 10x10 and 15x15, with three 15x20 puzzles at the very end. Still, this is enough to keep the tone relaxed rather than struggling with very difficult puzzles, and ought to be very accessible to less experienced picrossers. The interface is quite usable though it lacks the drag-lock of Pictopix, which would have been a helpful addition. The art is beautifully done, though there isn't that much of it and it is repeated a lot: does Honor ever wash her shirts?! The art for Scout the robot is especially well done, managing to evoke a lot of emotion from a little robot. The game is set in the 90s and has some great retro vibes along those lines. The narrative is engaging and the writing is witty (in the vein of Ace Attorney), albeit the plot twists are very clearly signalled. Though Chapter 3 is quite tediously anachronistic and preachy at first, even there the story ends up more nuanced than it seems like it will from that difficult start. The soundtrack is absolutely banging—I have been singing the theme tune over and over—though as with the art it could use some more variety. Overall, if like me you love the idea of “Pictopix meets Ace Attorney”, this game will give you pretty much exactly what you expect. A recommend from me.

_childDocuments_.review: What a fantastic game! The art, music, and story are all huge highlights. I really loved the character design, story and each of the motives/backgrounds. _childDocuments_.review: Gripping (if at times predictable) storyGorgeous character illustrationsVaried character buildingAmazing soundtrackWide variety (and decently large number) of picross puzzles ranging in difficultyMissable puzzlesLack of accessibility settings for the hacking puzzlesMain menu credits softlockAbility to stray into wrong columns/rows when filling in a bunch of cellsUnskippable tutorialInability to save mid-dialogue (unlike traditional VNs)With Fall Guys being a runaway success for Mediatonic, it can be particularly easy to forget that that game was not the only one they released this year. Earlier, they released this game - Murder by Numbers, which melds picross solving and visual novel into one package.I'm not huge into visual novels, but picross is one of my guilty pleasures. I've played a variety of picross games on Steam over the years, of varying quality. In terms of that, Murder by Numbers slots in into the above half - but there are issues with the picross engine that hold it back from the top. It's great that it isn't that easy to accidentally overwrite filled cells with the opposite type of mark, but it is ridiculously easy to stray into adjacent rows or columns while marking in most of a bunch of cells and ruin the puzzle altogether.The puzzle difficulty is really comparable to most other games, ramping up slowly but gently. The last few ones in the main 'story' can be quite the challenge, but are still ultimately easily solvable, and they never get too big (unlike the 20x20 or larger grids you might see in other games). The 5x5 hacking puzzles are a good change of pace, but multiple people have reported struggling with the time limit required to solve them.As for the story, it is actually rather enthralling, no doubt helped by the exciting soundtrack and the gorgeous character designs. Give me a sequel to this game (though with some much-needed improvements over the first).Easily worth full price for hours of gorgeous picross solving. If both Hatoful Boyfriends are in your collection you can also pick up the Murder Most Fowl Collection bundle for an additional 20% on top.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: perfectly functional game with some serious dissonance between when it wants to be cozy, feelgood, and inoffensive, and when it wants to be gripping, intense, and dramatic. ultimately, it falls flat on its face at both. the lighthearted approach is undercut by how much the game wants you to take its Drama and Tragedy seriously, the serious approach is undercut by an extremely simplistic story, frustratingly tropey characters, and a refusal to engage with the concepts of crime and murder on any level beyond the most bog-standard surface-level mush whatsoever. the fact that the protagonist wrongly accuses someone innocent and gets the police involved with them in  reflects a fundamental misunderstanding of why the Ace Attorney series is as compelling as it is.there are a million little things Murder by Numbers does wrong. on their own, they're things I'd consider personal nitpicks - the cast of every case after the first is too small for a good whodunit, I don't like some elements of how the lgbt+ rep is handled (I am gay and transgender, not some chud getting lightheaded at the mere sight of a man getting a little fruity), character storylines wrap up before I feel like they've even said anything, the themes of legacy and self-determination both try to take center stage but never grapple with each other, so on, so forth. but ultimately, the fact that Murder by Numbers says nothing that I haven't heard  story say before means that this pile of tiny flaws, this mountain of potential avoided at every crossroads by taking the most bland and inoffensive route possible, is what I'll remember it for.that, and the whiplash between seeing a cg of a woman's tragic death, followed immediately by the cheery elevator music that plays when you're solving a puzzle.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: This game has no right being as good as it is. The concept is interesting, the game play is fun and actually fits with the narrative really well, and the stories are good! You'll probably guess the murder on most of the cases, but there are still twists and turns to the story that keep it really interesting! Above all the dialogue is very well written! It's very consistent throughout the game, which makes the world feel complete. There were only a few issues I encountered in the game. For the most part the game does a good job of dealing with the difficulty curve of Picross-style puzzles, but you may get stuck at some point. If you use hints then you don't unlock the bonus puzzles. It can also be kind of tiring at the end when the difficulty is at its highest. This wasn't a problem for me because I really enjoyed doing a couple puzzles and then coming back to it later, but if you're looking for a game you can sit and binge, this ain't it. Finally, it felt like there were some loose ends in the story at the end. Not plot holes, mind you, but just a few characters felt like they kinda disappeared and I was surprised they didn't come back up. I could have done with  altogether, to be honest. But as you can see, these are pretty minor drawbacks. If you look at the game and think you might like it, trust me you will! If you're looking at it and it isn't calling to you, it's probably not your cup of tea.

_childDocuments_.review: I've just finished playing through the 4 cases present in the game, although I've yet to tackle some of the extra "loose" puzzles.This game was such a pleasant surprise and, thus far, the best game of the year. The art is gorgeous and colorful, the writing is fun and enjoyable, the characters are full of personality and the mix of Phoenix Wright with Picross works so much better than what I could've ever imagined.And the soundtrack is absolute perfection!I have no reservations in recommending this game. Do get it as soon as you have the chance!
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Both the picross and the visual novel aspects of the game are quite enjoyable. The picross puzzles may be too frequent, however: each case involve dozens of puzzles. Burnout may set in quickly. You can use easy mode to skip the puzzles, but doing so locks you out of bonus content.A word of caution: Since this game is a cross between picross and visual novel, you need to enjoy both to get through the game. You need to play through the visual novel to get to the puzzles, and you need to solve the puzzles to progress in the visual novel. If you're new to picross, use the 2-hour return window to try out the puzzles to see if you can get the hang of it.As to Phoenix Wright mechanics present in the game, examine/move/talk/present is in the game, but obviously no court segment, no special mechanics except picross puzzles, and all questions are multiple-choice - no presenting evidence as an answer.

_childDocuments_.review: PLEASE disregard the hours; I had a horrible tendency while playing this game to leave it open when I went to sleep.  Don't be me, that's bad for your computer.  I do not do this anymore, but it already racked up ridiculous hours.  This is not that long of a game, LOL.THAT SAID...  I recommend this game with a caveat: if your reaction speed is not that great anymore, mandatory timed parts that are NOT SKIPPABLE and COMPLETELY UNPAUSABLE are going to give you a really rough time.  Yes, no matter how good you are, if your reaction speed is slow, parts of this game is going to be a nightmare.  I grew up playing shooters and tons of games - my reaction speed used to be great, but I'm much older now and do not have the reaction time I did in my teens or early twenties.  These parts were PAINFUL and required getting JUST lucky enough to barely pass the timed segments.  I'm not the only one with these problems either, based on the board.  That said, if the above won't be an issue for you or you're willing to just stubbornly keep at it until you get through like I did?  The story is fun, the art is charming, the puzzles (when they aren't timed) are fun.  I recommend this game so long as the above caveat won't ruin the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Time to Beat Note: Please be aware that my "time played" is NOT indicative of the amount of time necessary to beat the game. It was so enjoyable to play, that I would frequently leave it running all day and grab some puzzles and/or detecting when I could do so. I think around 15-20 hours would probably be the "average" time to beat.I absolutely loved this game. The first impression is great, and it showcases the absolutely amazing writing that is present throughout the entire game. The writing is so good that you will empathize with these characters easily, which makes the deaths and betrayals hit harder than in most games.The core loop is very simple but also very enjoyable. You'll search rooms for clues (which lead to picross-style puzzles), and then chat with people. Your main objectives while chatting are to learn more information about the case, to catch them in lies, and to show them items you have found. Thankfully, both the puzzles and the writing are top notch, so this simple loop should have no problem sustaining you through the entire game.The artwork of both the characters and locations are memorable. These devs know how to build a believable world and characters.The negatives for the game are all fairly minor. I would say that none of them detract from the game enough to detract from the experience. The first negative is that all four of the cases follow a pretty similar pattern. Although the writing is, again, excellent, it does show you how the cases will play out for the rest of the game. This means that it is VERY EASY to figure out who the criminal is for all four cases (especially the latter three once the first is completed). The overarcing plot that ties them together does better at concealing all of its twists and turns, though there aren't too many surprises to be found, unfortunately.The other large negative are the puzzles. The difficulty of these puzzles is way too low. I'm not a picross master, though I have played many picross games, and I feel that the first three cases are just too easy. The final case at least gets slightly more difficult at the end, but there are no head scratchers here.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about this game but overall recommend it.Picross puzzles are fun and challenging, and there's a ton of them. The visuals and soundtrack are great. The characters are somewhat likeable, but mostly forgettable. Honor's character is honestly pretty frustrating. She starts out inexperienced as a detective which makes sense but as the game goes on she doesn't really seem to learn from her mistakes in prior cases. She jumps to accusing the most obvious suspect every time and doesn't consider any other possibilities until there's undeniable evidence to suggest that her initial theory is wrong.On that note, the most disappointing part of this game has to be the mysteries. Each case plays out in an extremely similar pattern (evidence points to initial suspect, who is arrested, suddenly new evidence appears that points to a second suspect who is actually the murderer). Every case lacks any compelling mysteries or depth.Overall, I'd recommend this IF you're looking for a fun Picross game. If you're looking for a murder mystery game this one will disappoint.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a kinetic visual novel with some picross puzzles used as an investigation mechanic. The story is fine, if a bit too predictable, but the characters are great. The conclusion is kinda anticlimactic, but oh well, at least there's a clear path for the second game.Picross puzzles are mostly on the easy side, mostly sitting in the 10x10 and 15x15 range, with 20x15 popping at the very end (and mostly in bonus section).Overall, it's a neat experience with some solid picrossing.

You have to click your way through a billion lines of an uninteresting, boring story that you can't skip to be able to reach a 5x5 pixel puzzle that you can literally solve in 5 seconds. Refunded instantly after I was able to reach the first puzzle in 12 minutes of clicking through dialog.

_childDocuments_.review: Only for Nonogram Superfans!Prior to this I had never played a nonogram/picross type game before. I initially purchased this because I liked the premise of combining puzzle and mystery mechanics and Ace attorney type stuff. I think this game delivers that in spades, the story is fantastically written. But the puzzles jump up in difficulty -very- quickly. The first case took me about two hours to complete while the second case has taken me SIX hours and still isn't done. I had to level up my nonogram skills quickly to keep up, otherwise I'd be very frustrated. to be fair, there are also some options that can make it easier for new players but I haven't caved and tried them yet, so  maybe it helps. I primarily play this game for the great story and I'm worried it will get to a point where I can't finish it because the puzzles get devilish. but if you are good at nonograms already I think you'll like it!

_childDocuments_.review: A detective story? Love them.A visual novel? Like the genre.Attractive, distinctive character art and interesting backgrounds? Great.Nonograms? Right up my alley.And it all adds up to ... a recommendation with reservations. Not quite what I expected to write when I started playing .The gameplay first: I was hoping for more from the nonograms. Unfortunately, I could never tell what image I was creating, and I still couldn't tell at the end until it got filled in with color and labeled. As a result, the experience was rather rote, merely following the logic to completion and getting little sense of accomplishment.As for the writing, it was genuinely amusing in spots, ponderous in a few, confusing in bits, imprecise on occasion. (One bothersome moment: )The story was surprisingly unpleasant, particularly the subplot involving Honor's family life.  As this subplot gets mostly resolved before the conclusion, Case 4 is blessedly free of it and is thus able to wrap up the main storylines in an interesting, now-this-is-a-mystery-thriller fashion.All this is to say that I recommend  mostly with hopes for an improved sequel. Better nonograms, better mystery stories? Yes, please!
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I picked this up on a sale. I was intrigued by the concept of a mystery game where solving picross puzzles is the means to progress.I promptly forgot it in my library for a couple months.When I started it, I was pleased at the basic tutorial offered for picross puzzles. I had worked on picross before but I hadn't had much strategy. Once I got some ideas from the tutorial, it really got my brain in the right state to attack these puzzles.The chapters are nice - each mystery gets longer. The first is quite short and you likely can finish it relatively easily in one sitting. I was a little concerned that this would mean a short game. I was wrong.Each mystery got deeper, the characters developed more, and the puzzles more complex. I really found myself hooked on solving the puzzles and this fast became my Steam game of choice.I have seen others talk about the story and their dislike of the "agenda" in it. While I'm not at all offended by it, I did find it heavy-handed a lot of times. Subtlety is *not* this games strength when it comes to story. I still found the overall story arc enjoyable and it was fun to see where things went. I generally wasn't *too* surprised by plot twists, but it didn't detract from the overall fun. Really, for me it was all about the puzzles.I strongly encourage you to play without hints. You get more points that way, ultimately unlocking more puzzles. If you unlock all 20 puzzles in each chapter, you get an extra cut scene. Suffice to say, I played to completion (and my ridiculous play time reflects this).So, in the end, if you enjoy your picross with a side of story and a dash of mystery, you might enjoy this. It was well worth my money and time. Oh, and it's a fantastic game to play on the Steam Deck. It doesn't drain the battery quickly, and it fits the screen quite well.

_childDocuments_.review: the puzzles become a bit of trial and error when starting them in cases 3 & 4, but they are still very worth doing. If the trial and error time sink gets to you look up the puzzle solutions, but just throw in a couple edge lines then finish the puzzle on yer own (this takes out the drudgery of initial guessing without ruining the puzzle). The story is a lot of fun, and the characters are very entertaining (<3 SCOUT). Would love to see a sequel with more SCOUT & Honor someday.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to give this one a 50:50 rating but on balance it was just a little towards negative for me. The first two cases were by far the better two.
