_childDocuments_.review: Warning: unfortunately the game cannot be played in "I'm just here for the puzzles" mode.I really don't care about the story or all these anime LGBT characters man. I just wanted to solve some Nonograms because I ran out of Nonogram games on Steam. Sadly even with an auto-clicker that skips dialogue ultra-fast I still have to sit through several full minutes worth of dialogue and characters overreacting to everything, only to reach a puzzle that I solve in about 20 seconds or so then do it all again.I tried to get invested in the story but after a murder happens and everyone is ordered to stay in the room while a detective and police the investigate, the very first thing that the protagonist does is distracts others then escapes through a ventilation shaft. In order "to find proof of their innocence" no less. You can't even make a choice to do it, it just happens anyway. That is so bloody ridiculous and backwards I couldn't care less about the rest of the story past that point.Anyway, yeah, this is a "visual novel" first and foremost, I really shouldn't have purchased this for puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that makes me whish for a "meh" option on Steam.It's not a terrible game by any means, I enjoyed solid chunks of it, but it has too many flaws to recommend.It starts with cute and surprisingly high production value intro including the stereotypical theme song and it's sadly just downhill from there. The game just screams for more care and polish, for everything the game gets right there is something else that just feels lazy and careless.There story has some charming moments but those are far in between and it's mostly just cheesy and way too drawn out. It takes forever to get to the first nonogramms. Player choices do not matter . This isn't Picross with a murder mystery framing, this is a cheap looking visual novel with the occasional Picross thrown in to mix things up.That's certainly not what I expected and would have preferred. Fans of visual novels might see this differently, sadly I'm not.The cardinal sin is that there is no dialog skip option: don't care about the visual novel anymore and just want to do some nonogramms? Tough luck, that's not an option. Missed a puzzle and want to go back for it? Well, I hope you enjoy starting from the beginning of the long chapter without any way to move things along or skip anything.The unskippable tutorial, the crummy save system, the fact that it has a bunch of bonus stuff to achieve (a rank system, bonus puzzles) but no achievements for those things, the both incredibly sparse but also incredibly annoying animation - everything just feels cheap and unpolished.The nongramms are solid, though, with a slow but steady ramp up in difficulty. I did quite enjoy many of them. But that's sadly not the meat of the game and I whish that it were.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: The picross in this was so so fun, it never gets super crazy but it starts easy and reaches a pretty challengingish level eventually so probably good for beginners hehe. Also the timed sections were very uniqueThe actual story was a bit hit-or-miss for me though, some parts of the last case were insane copaganda (that poor defense attorney?? he is literally doing his job. a job that is more important than the detective's). I liked the designs a lot and the spritework was very fun/dramatic when it needed to be so idk the annoying stuff didn't really get in the way. I did turn off the music and play my own towards the end though (its nice but got a bit tiring to listen to the actual ost)
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Pictocross, it's a no brainer. Get this game. There's more non-story puzzles than there are Story puzzles. Though it's locked behind story progress. What this means is once you complete a case, you can relax with 12-20 new puzzles per case. Before tackling the story again. The story and gameplay in my opinion does add a nice element to the game. Just don't go in expecting to be a detective, this isn't Phoenix Wright or Dangonronpa. You can piece 2 and 2 together, maybe you figure it out before the main character does. That's it. It's hard to give Pictocross games an inbetween mechanic between the puzzles. Another Pictocross game I played called Pictoquest basically added health / monster mechanics to give you a time constraint. This is much more relaxed and at your own pace. With optional , non-score deducing hints so extra friendly to new players.EDIT: 100% the game, all stories and all puzzles completed max score no hint. Check my hours for a rough idea of the content in the game. My review stands; brilliant game. Some really challenging puzzles in there I had to reset on because I just messed up somewhere or other.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy Picross puzzles but I was sceptical about Murder By Numbers until I saw a stream of it. I liked the characters and the storytelling enough to buy the game at full price and it was just as enjoyable by the end, though some of the last few puzzles were much harder than I expected!There's some good humour in between the serious parts of the story and I enjoyed how Honor and S.C.O.U.T worked together so well through the story.If you enjoy solving Picross puzzles, I would definitely recommend this. If you like Phoenix Wright as well. You should have bought it already!
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: As a big Picross fan, I really liked this game. The story is interesting, and the picross sections are not too easy, which I appreciate. And SCOOT is best boi. The real life commentary was a bit surprising at first, but it's not too hamfisted in my opinion, which is kinda rare nowadays. Although there are some things that need to be impoved to make this game perfect, those did not hinder my fun so much that I would stop playing.I frankly recommend this game if you like picross puzzles.The good :- Challenging picross puzzles, notably the timed sections which will require you to know and quickly apply classic picross patterns- A hint system which will help you if you are not used to picross puzzles (even though you can't 100% the game if you use it)- You can save while doing a main story puzzle, which allows you to resume the puzzle at a later time- There is a "fake filling" system. Although it will count if the row/column is complete and will not allow you to make fake crosses, you can toggle this system in order to fill the pixel without really filling it, allowing you to try some combinations before inputing.- SCOOT smiles at you when you complete a row or a column ♥- Classic yet nice story, with some real life commentary that won't chastise you and a good alchemy between the characters- SCOOT- Cool and original characters, with some good character designs- Some jokes made me laugh- SCOOTThe less good :- Most of the picross pictures don't really make sense, since you are doing a black and white picross of a zoomed section of an object most of the time. You can't really tell what the final image will be like, and sometimes the final image is too hard to decypher even with the colors.- You cannot zoom. This becomes a problem when you start getting puzzles bigger than 10*10.- You cannot undo your moves- There are no button to clear the puzzleThe bad :- I found one puzzle which seemed to be optional for the story, but needed to be done to get an S rank in the case and unlock all bonus puzzles. I had to redo the whole case without knowing which puzzle I accidentally skipped. Be sure to really search everywhere and ask everyone about everything, as some puzzles are started only if you talk to someone or if you show them something specific.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: At its core, Murder by Numbers is just two completely different games constantly switching back and forth - a simple picross game offering nothing that any other picross game hasn't already done, and a very basic Phoenix Wright style visual novel. In my opinion, it does neither of these particularly well. If you're a fan of picross, get a picross focused game. If you're a fan of Phoenix Wright style visual novels, I don't think you'll have a hard time finding one elsewhere. The two concepts are not blended well enough to justify the gimmick.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: It's picross...I happen to enjoy picross.That being said, many of the puzzles, after being solved, don't really look anything like what they're supposed to be. Also, the story lost my interest pretty quickly. I'm sure it's fine, I just wasn't really into it so I ended up skipping pretty much all of the dialogue after a while.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: This "game" is all story and no game.  It would be ok, not good, but ok, if the story was at least decent, but it's not.  Everything about this is stereotypical and horribly predictable.  The characters are either stupid or annoying or both.Tip tip the devs:  Give us a mode to just solve the puzzles and skip 50-100 mouse clicks to get past the high school drama club/dating game show/queer eye episode storyline going on here.  I guess then it would become obvious that there are very few puzzles.I think the production of this "game" went something like this:"Do we still have that book of stereotypes?  Cool.  Let me see it.  Sleazebag Married Boss? Check.  Annoying Friend?  Backstabbing Friend?  We can roll those two into one character.  Stupid Muscled Handyman? Check.  Gay Hairstylist? Check.  Nerdy Fanboy?  Check.  Ok now to the section on obvious plot lines..."Next time you make a game, feel free to spend more than $300 and a free lunch on it.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I've never played a Picross game before, so I can't comment on how difficult it is for veterans but if you're looking for something that would scratch that Pheonix Wright itch, you could do a lot worse than playing this game while waiting for Capcom to release the next compilation.This game features a fun, likable cast of well developed characters.  The game is broken up into cases, much like Phoenix Wright and there is an underlying mystery playing throughout every case you find yourself working on.  Instead of a courtroom setting, you play a TV detective who finds her real passion is being a real detective and partnered with a cute little robot with amnesia.  When you find a clue, you're met with the Picross minigame.  Even as a total beginner, I never had problems with it and if you are absolutely terrible, you can brute force your way through the puzzles.  A few minus points to being able to miss certain things by clicking past a point of no return.  (Aren't those always fun? Save often folks!)All in all, I really enjoyed my time with the game and hope that they're working on a sequel.  These characters are too good to have it just be a one-off and I would love to see the game expanded on and some of the minor issues fixed.Oh and don't sleep on the soundtrack.  It's by the composer of Phoenix Wright and is FANTASTIC.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: - Nice story (just don't expect something very serious, judging by some reviews :/)- Nice puzzles (plenty of them, if you like picross, they're fine).- Mixed with mystery solving stuff.- Very charming characters and visuals.- Very nice music (some may find repetitive, idk, not me).- Optional extra aids (reduces score/rank) and a visual aid to tell you which lines have possible moves (no score cost; for long puzzles).- No control mapping- No undo button/key.- Seemingly "no way" to go back from some menus. Tho you can press the "X" key for this (yeah, not Escape, not Backspace or smt, but the actual "X" letter! Found out way later).- You can tell it was made for phones, with no extra QoL features/no taking advantage of KB+M (except right and left mouse buttons mark and cross respectively).- You can miss 1-2 puzzles when talking to characters and there's no way to go back (losing the full completion/S rating), except re-doing the whole complete chapter (at least in chapter 3).Maybe could've highlighted the speaking character to avoid very minor misunderstandings.Has short, easy, but very quick timed puzzles at times ("hacking").Overall, I really liked it. Part II pls!Surely will get the Collector's Edition on GOG later.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic music, great characters, great art. Sadly, the actual mysteries aren't on the quality of, say, Ace Attorney. You'll likely see the big twists coming even if the characters can't. I found that the characters were charming, so when they were oblivious or obviously barking up the wrong tree, it wasn't frustrating.The Piccross puzzles are the meat of the game, and there are a LOT of them. This is not a mystery story with puzzles, this is a collection of puzzles with a story built around them. I'm a big fan of puzzle games, so I loved this, but if you're more into the Ace Attorney or in-depth mysteries and are hoping the puzzles are just a sidenote, give this a pass. If you like Sudokus and other grandma puzzles, absolutely try this. It's a lot of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended but...The standard review is "Do you like Picross and Ace Attorney? Then this game is for you!" It's much more do you really like grid puzzles, and I mean by the bucket load like them, and will be somewhat entertained by an Ace Attorney homage story? Ace Attorney aesthetic is really well captured especially in sound design and with a soundtrack by the composer of the first Phoenix Wright game. But you do little to no puzzle solving around the investigation. Most of what you do is a LOT of grids. The last case alone has 38 puzzles, only two smaller than 15x15 and 20 bonus puzzles. Quality of puzzles is good and I quite like grid puzzles but that many felt kind of grind by the time I was done.Also regarding the one missable puzzle: FFFFFUUUUUUUUUUU
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I imagine the audience for this game is rather niche - the detective VN and nanogram puzzle sections each comprising half of the game. If only one of these seems appealing to you, there might be games better suited for your time. But if you do happen to fall in that niche I think you'll have a great time with this game
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: This is very specifically for those who love nonograms. I already had a lot of experience with them beforehand and I was a little disappointed that the difficulty was no higher than 15x15 puzzles (with 1 exception I think of a 20x15). Still some of them took a decent amount of time so it was fun overall. My  biggest complaint (after the puzzle difficulty) was that I found the character clothing choices to be very ugly and I thought as much every time I saw them on the screen. Though this did not affect gameplay at all, I would like whoever did the character designs to exclude this from their demo reel.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of Hatoful Boyfriend, I couldn't ignore a new Hato Moa game. I had to learn how to solve picross puzzles, and I had a great time doing it.Sometimes the game gets unintentionally funny during some tone deaf moments - someone finds a dead body, and it's very shocking and terrible, but then the upbeat investigation song starts like it's nothing serious lol - but the whole scenario and characters are very nice and colorful, so I guess everything fits in the dark humor of the narrative.I was kinda expecting some secret ending or NG+, but the whole experience was worth it anyway.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I'm on the third out of 4 chapters, and feel safe to review this now.The game consists of two parts.  The visual novel, and picross.1.  The Visual NovelReally well done!  If you've ever played Phoenix Wright, you'll feel wright at home!  The main protagonist's perspective and setting is a female actress who plays a detective on a TV show.  The writing is entertaining and keeps you wanting to know what will happen next.  When searching for clues, you'll click where you need to and this starts the Picross portion.2.  The PicrossAlso well done!  If you're looking for Picross that will challenge you, by chapter 2 you start getting some that really test your mettle.  However, if Picross isn't for you, don't worry!  You can get the computer to fill in random squares that work for the puzzle until its complete if you want.  You can also set it to easy mode (though I am playing normal).  The only gripe i have about the puzzles is they really don't resemble any picture until after you complete it.  Its not about the picture, its about the puzzle.  All in all, this is a nice little gem of a game with nicely drawn characters, decent writing, and fun puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: This is my favorite picross game on PC and puts up stiff competition for the GOAT - Picross 3D Round 2. That's high praise.On the VN side of the game, it's got a great art style, emotive sprites, and a very tasteful 'fast' text speed. It's missing a chat log though, which is a strange omission considering it's a genre standard feature. On the picross side of the game, I sometimes wonder if developers mistake quality of life features for difficulty modifiers, so it's a little frustrating to see auto-check and most other auto features be locked behind easy mode, and thus a lower score. This comes down to how the game measures error, and I don't feel that penalizing wrongly marked  cells would compromise the difficulty.Further compounding this is the fact that the game is fairly challenging to begin with and otherwise has a perfectly smooth difficulty curve throughout cases and the game as a whole. I also really loved the variety of grid dimensions and the occasional time-trial puzzles. It felt perfect for me as a seasoned picross lover - not too easy, not too hard. What a treat!So then, the approach to difficulty settings is an aberration to the other good design choices of the game. Alas, but this doesn't take away from the fact that Murder by Numbers is a wonderful game and I 1000% recommend it to any picross lover, and puzzle lovers at large.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: If you love picross, and I mean REALLY LOVE picross then this game is great. If you find picross interesting or enjoy it every so often you'll likely stop playing before the end. Either way, I enjoyed it for the time that I played but I doubt I could drag myself to finish the game because I'm not a picross fanatic.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: It's Phoenix Wright meets Picross. Nothing more really needs to be said. I enjoyed the quirky story. Music can get repetitive when you're solving the puzzles, but it's upbeat and cool when it's new! Easy to drop in and out, especially chipping away and the side puzzles you unlock through the main story. I've still got some of the game left to go, but I've really enjoyed my time with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: My biggest critique about the game is that there is no dialogue log. Some of the speech text disappears automatically and there's no way to go back and read what was missed. Changing the speed of the text in settings doesn't help this either. But overall it is a fun and thrilling puzzle game. Very enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Two of my favorite things are picross or nonogram puzzles and visual novels and this game perfectly combines the two. The puzzles are challenging without being too hard to complete (there is even a hint system you can use,) and the story is fun and compelling. I really loved this game. The only problem I had was the missable puzzle in the third chapter which cost me my S ranking, but it was really no big deal I can always play it again.I hope there is a sequel in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to try the game because of the puzzle mechanic, the visual novel kind of thing is nothing that usually draws me in but it kind of worked here. The story is well done, I really liked that all 4 cases/ stories are connected and how everything fit together. The story part was sadly a bit long winded in the end, especially the last case really drags on.Apart from that it's a really nice game. The puzzles are all doable and not too hard. You also always have time to do them in your own speed, only the short "hacking" sequences are time limited (but they are short and very easy).
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid fan of picross/nonogram games as well as Hato Moa's artistic work, this game was a special treat for me! The puzzles are a refreshing challenge from typical fare, especially in Scout's Memories, which are entirely optional but fun to work through. The story and characters are both charming and offer surprisingly good representation. My only major gripe is that if you do not achieve an S-rank on a case, you will have to play through it all over again, which is tedious (especially considering that there are missables in case 3).
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: The Yogscast JingleJam 2021 bundle included two nonogram (picross, paint-by-numbers) games: This and PictoQuest, and this game was far and away the better one, mostly because it doesn't try to staple nonograms to RPG systems. It respects the "spirit" of nonograms and mostly doesn't punish the player for being slow at puzzle solving.This game is split between story parts and puzzle parts. The story parts are passable visual novel style scenes. There's nothing wrong with them, but nothing special. I wouldn't suggest playing this game entirely for the story.The puzzle parts are mostly perfect. There are options for hinds, but they aren't mandatory, and I never used them. It has the option to mark with another color for note taking and counting purposes, which is great, although I think the interface for using it could be improved. My biggest problem with the puzzle parts is that I wish there were more of them and that there could be some harder ones. I beat all of the available puzzles, and I would only calla few of them "hard". The vast majority of endgame puzzles are 15x15; there are exactly three 20x15 puzzles, and I wish there were more of them.Overall, I would recommend this game to anyone who already like nonograms as well as anyone who is interested.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: As a picross game this is really cool, lots of puzzles integrated one way or another into the story, it´s always fun to solve them and that´s great, but as a visual novel OR as a detective-ish game it falls completely flat, the character designs are really well done and I love them but everything else needs a LOT of polish and the story and writing could use some helpAlso, as of when im writing this ALL the achievements are bugged and you can only play with mouse (it lacks any kind of keyboard support), the UI is atrocious, it lacks any kind of backlog or auto mode (which are pretty standard for visual novels), I may change this review once these problems are patched (IF they are patched, since the achievements have been bugged for quite a while) IF you like the aesthetic and can look past the bugs and UI,
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: is a part visual novel, part nonogram puzzle game, and it is an absolute treat to play. Good things come in small packages, and  proves that beyond a doubt.You play as Honor Mizrahi, an actress who gets mixed up in a few too many murders for comfort. Teaming up with a mysterious floating robot companion, SCOUT, the two uncover the truth behind the crimes in the city, friending and fighting with a cast of curious and colorful characters along the way.When I was first thinking of this review, I was going to preface it with a humorous quip--"like  and  had a lovechild"--but after the credits rolled, I realized how right I was about that. Not just with the "not-a-detective doing detective work", and not just the punny names, but also the fact that Masakazu Sugimori did the music for the game. AKA, the person who did the music for the original  game on the Game Boy Advance, back in 2001. That music really comes through in --going from peppy, upbeat puzzle themes to intense visual novel background music. I love it!If you're a fan of puzzle games, you'll definitely enjoy the nonogram segments. As the game progresses, the puzzles get bigger and more difficult, but never too much that you want to quit the game.  also doesn't penalize you for getting a row or column wrong  so it's great even for beginners. has a lot of heart for a relatively short game. Honor, SCOUT, and all of their friends slash foes are interesting in their own ways, and I really felt like the world around them was alive, which some visual novels can struggle with: focusing on main characters and leaving side characters to wither with two or three lines.Overall, I'm glad I picked up this game, and my only problem is that there's no SCOUT plush to purchase!
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: A much better nonogram game than a visual novel. While the puzzles were challenging, the mysteries were not. Only a few of the characters actually stand out, but Honor really bothers me as she never really learns to stop jumping to conclusions. I enjoyed solving the nonograms, but the difficulty curve for them varied a little too much. Still, if you need to scratch that Phoenix Wright glitch, as well as enjoy a nonogram, this is the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Murder By Numbers is a mix between a visual novel, a detective story, and a picross game. It has a great narrative excuse to slip the pircross puzzles into the game, which do a good job to give a break between the visual novel gameplay.The music is amazing, every time I opened the game, I let the theme song play in full, because it was a rocking jam! The background music is also good, not just for the picross portion, but also the atmospheric music that sets the tone for the scenes. This makes the expensive ($14 AUD) soundtrack and artbook DLC worth getting!I have only done one playthrough, but it doesn't seem like the choices you make really have much weight. If you make an unfounded accusation, then the other characters will just point out that it was unfounded and they will let you choose another answer. You can make the wrong choice, but it seems to be written for you to make the wrong choice. This is unlike many other visual novels and detective games which are heavily choice based, but it is still satisfying despite this.The picross puzzles never get too difficult, I played them without hints or anything and I never got stuck for too long. If you are very familiar with picross puzzles, these puzzles never get that difficult, but if you have never played picross puzzles before, you can play on an easier difficulty. The only downside to playing on an easier difficulty, is that you won't be able to unlock all the secret memory scenes at the end of each case.The characters are fun and engaging! And it makes you genuinely hope a character you like won't turn out to be the killer, and sad if they do. There are only four cases, but they get longer with each case, so it's not a short game. I only came across a couple of bugs, mainly being very minor ones that didn't affect the gameplay that much.If you love visual novels, detective games, and have a tolerance for (or love of) picross you'll enjoy this one!
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I never thought I would enjoy a Picross puzzle in any way other than a time-waster.  I was pulled in by the idea that these puzzles were murder mystery themed, but I ended up getting more than that.The beginning sequence when you start up the game is really fun and exciting and is done really well.  Pairing that with the upbeat intro song and I was excited to play it.  The plot for the game is also exciting and keeps your attention every step of the way, from the interactions you get with the characters to the plot twists that show up.  The puzzles themselves are fun and have you guessing what the items are.  Some of the puzzles were a little difficult (though there was a guide thankfully that I could use if I did get too stuck) but otherwise were fun to play.  I got super attached to all the characters, especially K.C. and Scout.  K.C. is such a wonderful character with so much energy, and SCOUT is so dynamic I loved seeing everything that he learns and goes through and he learns how to be the best he possibly can.  He definitely does go through a lot, and I am glad that he has all the support that he does.  Honor also had a lot going on, but she is a very strong, independent woman and I am glad that she advocates for herself despite everything she has gone through and has such a wonderful support group.  Detective Cross also changes a lot throughout the game, and I did end up warming up to him.  Becky...  I get where she's coming from, but she definitely acts like an entitled rich kid.  It's good to know that later in the game that changes a bit, but I never actually see it and wasn't really fond of her character.  Ryan was a terrible person at all points of the game, and it's really sad no one can see how he is with Honor except K.C.  It does go to show though that abusers can come from anywhere and that it's difficult trying to escape from them sometimes.  I was also starting to warm up to Jena, and I was sad to see what happened to her, but she was a great addition to the game and with helping Scout realize his true potential.I did like how the music changed during certain points of the game, but that same energy didn't stay for a lot of the puzzles, so I didn't really like that.  The puzzles had more happy-go-lucky music, and that threw me off especially during the action and suspenseful portions of the game.  I also really hate that there is no back button on the Load Game and other screens in the Menu.  The Reset Button on the Load screen is probably the worst place for that particular button because I accidentally hit it, thinking it was a back button, during my initial playthrough, and I lost all of the progress I had made in Chapters 1 and 2 and with SCOUT's Memories.  I will admit that I stopped playing the game for a few months because of that, though I am glad I came back to the game and finished it without further issue.  Overall, the game is a great game with wonderful visuals, characters, and plot.  I absolutely would recommend playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I went in expecting a visual novel game with some picross and instead I got a picross game with some visual novel. And the two go together about as well as peanut butter and battery acid. I'd be enjoying KC's delightful dialogue one second and then have five absurdly long and repetitive nonagrams for the next hour and a half. It was like being handed a mystery novel with eight pages of sudoku to solve between every one page of story.I wanted to like it. I really did. I tried.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so exactly my jam it's remarkable. The nonograms (aka picross) are well made (though the lack of an "undo" button is sometimes annoying), the music is cute (though I usually mute while solving), and the story is genuinely cute (silly, over the top, corny, but full of heart). And they legit made an anime style intro that is just perfect. Honestly my only critique other that undo button thing is that it's so short and given the runaway success of Fall Guys means we'll never get more of this, and that makes me sad.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Murder by Numbers is a game developed by Mediatonic and published by The Irregular CorporationThe game offers some nice graphics, although some ugly glitches here and there, it is pleasant all the sameThe game does suffer with some repetitiveness at certain areas of the game but a fun game nonethelessMurder by Numbers overall, however, is a fun game to play, yet sometimes repetitive and it does get boring if being played for a long time, but is a great adventure game to play in short bursts!
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: First time i put a review on Steam, but this game is great. I was attracted by the art and because i love visual novels and games like Phoenix Wright. I am in case 2 so far and the story is interesting and i really like the characters. But the real highlight of this game are the Picross puzzles. I have never played a Picross puzzle and right now i am hooked. I am playing on Normal, because i don't want any hints. And it had a nice challenge. It gets harder and harder, but nothing too crazy so far. Quality game.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: More visual novel than nonograms. Also most the puzzles in the story are easy until you get to the last case. Still I'd recommend. On annoying thing is there is a missable puzzle in case 3 that will cause you not to get S rank. There is a work around on the discussions to just change the save file to S rank. Without that there is no way I'd play through that entire case again, feel like that is bad design on their part. If they ever have a sequel or a patch then they need an option to just skip the stuff you have done on previous playthroughs.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: From the studio that brought you Fall Guys, it's... knock off Phoenix Wright with picross?Honestly though I feel like this game is specifically targeted at me. I am a sucker for every part of this concept, and it totally delivers. Good music, although it got a bit stale by the end, cool story, legitimately interesting characters with different backgrounds that were handled well, and fun puzzles. If you like this sorta stuff buy it, I liked this more than most of the Phoenix Wright games.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about this game is charming, especially if you have 90s nostalgia.The only gameplay to be found is in the puzzles, which have a comfortable and intuitive interface. The rest of the experience is very similar to the investigations in Ace Attorney - conversation trees and generous pixel hunts. The developers clearly decided to focus their attention and budget, saving time and money on things like a 3D environment or character animation (aside from an outstanding intro sequence) and directing it instead into 2D art, dialogue, and music. It's a smart decision, and sets the player's expectations in the right way to really notice the beautiful aspects and practically ignore the cheap parts.A great puzzle experience, and a shining example of what indie creators can make.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. I love nonograms (the puzzles) and murder mysteries so this game seemed perfect for me. However, I found that the visual novel segments of the game dragged on way too long, which wouldn't be so bad expect that none of the characters were the least bit likable. At all. They were either bland, a ridiculous stereotype, or so self centered that they were too annoying even for villains. Everything else about this game that might have been fun was ruined by these characters that I did not care about and had to spend so much time with. At the end of it, even though I tried to push through, I could not make myself play this game any longer. There was only so much I could take of the extremely stereotypical Gay Best Friend, or having to listen to the protagonist and her mother bicker with each other, or the protagonist and her ex husband bicker with each other.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Part VN (Visual novel) part logic puzzle. The puzzle sections are a bit like a minesweeper board where you are given numbered clues to the marked spaces in a blank grid and must use that thing in your head to logically work out where they are. So for example if one row has 15 blank spaces and the clue says 4, 4, 5 then it must be 0000X0000X00000 but if it says 1, 3, 2, 1, then you will need to use logic to work out where the marked spaces can be or cannot be by elimination, by filling in adjacent rows/columns.So far the story is okay, i am not very far into it but the cast of characters are pretty eccentric. The puzzles are definitely the best part though. A must for crosswords, skeleton crosswords and minesweeper fans.EDIT: Just finished, did not get every puzzle perfect and you get memories puzzles as well, a sort of gallery loosely linked to each of the four cases that are additional to the main story/puzzles and I am only half way through those. So with that in mind and the four story cases all finished I have racked up 59 hours so if you are looking for value for money I think this is.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of mystery games and nonogram puzzles this is the game for you. The logic questions and presenting the right evidence is fairly easy, but the puzzles can be quite challenging and instead of the classic squares you sometimes also get rectangles of 10x15 which gives it quite the variety. The music can get a bit repetive, but the characters are cute. And the story is engaging enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: A fun puzzle game with a story and framework reminiscent of Ace Attorney. A lot of the characters are obviously beloved by the writers, so some of their moments can come off as irritating if you don't love them as much. But overall a good puzzle game with a story that is solid but may not be to everyone's liking, but it shouldn't impact your enjoyment massively.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice game, interesting plot and unusual mechanics!Solving nonogram puzzles takes most of the time, so people who don't like them probably won't enjoy the game much. Even though I appreciate nonograms and practiced for some time, I sometimes found that solving them takes me out of plot flow for a bit too long, I think dialog history feature and/or more flexible saving (being able to do it anytime, and just more slots) could help.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: It's really good as a story and as a puzzle game. Four cases and the first one lasted me about 4 hours. Epic Gamer Pro Strat: If you don't feel like solving picross puzzles but you wanna move the story forward, just mark all the boxes black and then use the  "search for errors" function to get the solution.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Mystery visual novel meets Nonogram/Picross puzzle with a dash of Pride parade thrown in, nuff said. What got me, however, was the characters - likable and interesting.The puzzles might get  a bit tiresome on the long run, but maybe that's just me not used to puzzle marathons.So if you don't mind some puzzles and a rather weak first episode, this might grab your attention.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: First, let me say that I wanted to like this game. I've always loved solving picross and the Ace Attorney series, so when I heard of a game that seemed to combine the two, I was excited to say the least. But the problems I have with this game are too much for me to overlook.The puzzles get repetitive really quickly; I've reached the penultimate case and I can't bring myself to go on anymore. None of them stand out as being interesting.There was a point in the second case that left me stumped for about 20 minutes longer than it should have. The only way I managed to "solve" the puzzle was to brute-force through my remaining options until I found the solution. The solution is to present a piece of evidence to the suspect TWICE to pressure them into telling the truth. There's no indication given that you could even do this and I'm pretty sure it never happens again in any other interaction you have.Also, the story and characters are very predictable. Every character feels one-dimensional with them fitting all into the cliche archetypes that you would expect from your average slash fiction written in the mid to late 2010's.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: The good: Decent story for the first 3 (out of 4) chapters. Those who have endured narcissistic abuse will identify with the main character. Art is nice, music is great. Has a nice Ace Attorney feel to it.The bad: Visual novel to picross puzzle ratio is much too low in the later chapters. Makes following the story difficult and the game starts to become tedious as you need to solve 5 puzzles to read a textbox. The ugly: No actual puzzles outside of picross. A very linear story with no choices.tl;dr... only get it if you like picross, and I mean really like picross. There is way too much of it towards the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: As a puzzle It's pretty basic but alright. As a story it's just bland. MC is a highly unpleasant, arrogant and self-centered individual who gets into murder investigations of which she knows nothing about... I'm actually not exactly sure why, because she feels like it? Because she wants to prove something to her evil ex and smothering mother? Because she played in detective TV show? Well, she breaks every possible procedure and creates multiple dangers for herself and everyone involved while doing it, like running in blind after an armed suspect through the residential area, with no weapon, no backup and not even telling anyone where she went. The police representative in the story is comedy level stupid guy who wouldn't find his glasses on the top of his head, but at the same time he is a really great guy and a hard-boiled veteran. And while he does periodically lash out at MC for her questionable actions (occasionally proceeding to let her do everything her own way anyway), but in his most touching moments he admits he was just worried for her safety. It's like he doesn't see any problems with random civilian messing the crime scenes except if it's our protagonist and she could be hurt.I'm not sure if I'm supposed to feel connection to these people. It feels like this was meant to be absurd and fun in the way Phoenix Wright is, but it's much weaker and blander to actually be that, though there are some decent jokes.Robo-drama seems stretched but let's not dwell on that since it comes out pretty late in the game.The suspects are not immune to idiotic behavior and keep leaving stange things behind, like hair dye for a quick disguise... excuse me, have you ever tried to colour your hair? It's anything but quick and stealthy. The subject in question, admittedly, wasn't trying to actually use it, just keeping it in his pockets to lose at the murder scene so we could find it, I suppose. The other one managed to lose both boots consecutively in two different places and never thought to retrieve them from suspicious places but actually went to buy another identical pair urgently instead. Maybe the character hasn't even noticed them falling off? That's pure gold.The game has nice visuals barring the most absurd looking characters. Rare fullscreen pictures are beautiful.The music is pretty repetitive and a little bit too energetic for when you are solving a puzzle for 20 minutes, but then it seems to dissapear completely in random scenes. There is no visual cue for the clues searching (called scanning), so this process could have been removed completely without loosing anything. There are some pretty strange introes into scanning, like why would you need to do the scan to... look at a business card? No idea.There is a very poorly thought-out bonus mode by the name of SCOUT's Memories, which makes you solve about 20 puzzles without any story between them and get a little scene in the end. And when I say little, I mean that every single one of them is about 10-line long. And you don't even know how unimportant that is until you actually see at least one of them. So I think it should either be just clearly introduced as bonus puzzles without the unlockable scenes, or the reward should be somewhat bigger and better. There are some features missing which would benefit the visual novel part greatly: the skip function, the backlog and saving the exact state of the game without needing to click through dialogue from the start of the scene. Also the saving in the middle of the dialogue shouldn't be disabled.I don't wanna give the game negative. It's not utterly bad and I got what I was looking for - a puzzle with a little story, but it's a neutral at best.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid nonogram / Picross lover, it's a rare day when I find a neat combo of nonogram puzzles and narrative. Murder by Numbers should have been a home run for me, a perfect combination of genres; unfortunately, repeated technical issues and poor UI design has caused me to shelve this game.Let's start with the good: the game's art is fab. The characters I encountered were brilliantly drawn, with loads of character provided by solid writing. Often, the humour in games like this doesn't land for me, but the jokes were sarcastic and down-to-earth (and I'm a Brit, so obviously that appeals). The puzzles start easy but ramp up quickly in difficulty - perfect for me as an experienced nonogrammer - and I wish I could have seen the game to the end to see how hard they pushed the nonogram formula.However, as mentioned, technical issues have caused me to put this game down after trying to play it three separate times over. On my first go round, an unreliable autosave system has caused me to lose a number of hours of progress. When I tried to play the game on my Steam Deck a few months later, the save data didn't port correctly and I received repeated in-game errors that I couldn't fix regarding save data corruption. I decided to bite the bullet and start fresh, only for my progress to be lost to the poor autosave again when navigating poorly-designed UI.I'd love for Murder by Numbers to receive that extra time in the oven to tighten the screws and ensure the experience is watertight. I'm not holding out hope, though, so for now, I'll be leaving it here. A real shame.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: good story, fun characters, AMAZING intro cinematic & song that always puts me in a good mood, and music in general is very good.but there is no real detective work you do which is sad. only multiple choice questions that are very easy.the only puzzles are nonograms of which there are over 100 and they tend to be on the longer side.not each one of them is mandatory and the game gives you as much help as you need.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I really enjoyed this game. The music is pleasant to listen to as I solve the puzzles, there are a lot of puzzles to solve, and I enjoyed the characters. The difficulty ramps up quite a bit so if you have never played picross before, do not beat yourself up if you get stuck.I do have a couple of complaints. At the beginning of the game, the MC and her friend rate people which I find to be a bit gross. There are also some parts where the dialogue appears and disappears rather quickly to emphasize the point. I really disliked missing some dialogue because I was pausing to drink some water just to realize I missed something and even when I learned to be prepared for the dialogue to go away, some of them would be fast enough I still could not read them in time. I missed one puzzle in Case 3 which meant I had to play through the entire case again to get S rank. Finally, for each case I was able to figure out who the real culprit was early on but I was either not allowed to accuse the culprit at all or the characters would dismiss it so we could go down the wrong path first before finally getting to what I had figured out already.Even with these flaws, it is a charming game and if you are a fan of picross or even just stories with puzzle elements, then this is a game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Visual novel meets picross. Murder by Numbers is a murder mystery visual novel game where you solve picross puzzles to find leads to your case. It has a very compelling story that hooks you from the get go. The characters are all well written and charming, the artstyle is unique and beautiful and the soundtracks are all fantastic. Murder by Numbers has everything set for being a successful series so it is safe to say that there would be a sequel. I enjoyed every moment i had with this game so i don't have many complaints except one thing which is there are ridiculous amounts of puzzles that you have to solve before you can continue the story. I hope they tone down the amount of puzzles, at least spacing the puzzles more instead of solving puzzles back to back in the next game so the story flows better. I recommend this game to everyone who enjoys visual novels and puzzles though you shouldn't expect a full on puzzle game since the story is the main focus here. Murder by Numbers has a bright future ahead, i can feel it.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: This was a surprising fusion of murder mystery, visual novel, and nonogram (picross), and overall it was pretty good! As a picross veteran, none of the puzzles were too difficult, and I never had to rely on guessing, even without hints, which I'd say is a sign that they were well designed.The visual novel side of the game was also quite nice, with characters that all had a distinct personality and decent dialog. By the time I finished the first case, I was genuinely invested in seeing the story to the end, which leads me to my first criticisms.While mostly not too difficult, the puzzles got time consuming by about the halfway point. This meant getting to the next part of the story could sometimes take a while if you had to solve several in a row. These breaks from the dialog didn't just make the game feel slow, but also disjointed, as it was easy to forget exactly what was going on, especially with the lack of a text log which seems to be a common feature in the few other visual novels I've played.All in all, there are quite a few quality of life features missing on both the picross and vn sides, such as saving puzzles in-progress, undoing moves, resetting a puzzle, replaying case puzzles without having to replay the whole case, choosing songs, skipping previously seen dialog, and the aforementioned text log.I mentioned choosing songs, because while each individual track is nice and fits with the setting, you can sometimes hear one song loop a  given the amount of time it takes to finish many of the puzzles. Just having a song selector in the menus would have gone a long way to relieve the fatigue of endless loops.Even with all that said, I  recommend this to fans of picross and murder mysteries because it's still a lot of fun. All the changes I've recommended would take this already good game to great. I'm not sure if there are plans for a sequel, but I'll be glad to continue the story of Honor and Scout if there are!
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: A perfectly serviceable Picross game with plenty of puzzles of moderate difficulty that experts might find lacking but which beginners and those who play Picross to relax (like me) will find just right.The murder-mystery narrative framing the puzzles is likewise perfectly serviceable, following a pair of likable lead characters that are easy to root for as they come into their own. The game purposefully invites comparison to the Ace Attorney series, but one should not go into Murder by Numbers expecting the same level of logical sleuthing or nuanced characterization you'd experience in any of those games.For a good time at a great price, it's hard not to recommend Murder by Numbers, but if you love Picross and love the Ace attorney series, just know that mashing them together in this instance doesn't necessarily make for the 'Greatest Thing Ever'. Sometimes though, a sizable helping of 'Pretty Good' is just what you're looking for. Here's hoping for a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game! Extremely well-written story, good nonograms, and the right balance of plot and puzzles to keep it from getting unbalanced. Also excellent diversity in the character lineup without feeling like it was a stretch - that shouldn't be as unusual as it is, but the positive trans rep and the POC main character made me very happy :-)
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: It's Picross. Do you like Picross? Then you'll probably like this.The story is cute and fun, giving enough motivation to want to see the next puzzle through, and the puzzle content is plentiful - completing every puzzle, including the bonus puzzles, took me around 30 hours. I had never actually done a Picross puzzle before, so your time may vary, but 30 hours of content is a lot!I received this game as part of a holiday bundle - definitely enjoyed my time with it. I wouldn't have discovered it otherwise.It's not perfect - the audio loops that play while solving puzzles are too short, and I experienced a few glitches with sound effects getting stuck on loop. But they didn't sour the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Great puzzle game, cases are fun, characters and story are cute too. Easy to complete and the hint system in place is really good for some of the more large puzzles (did not try the hints that deduct from the score). Decent price too (did not get it on sale). 4 cases with only 1 case being "meh." Will say that there are a few missable things in one case (#3) which is unfortunate since you have to replay the entire case if ya missed it. Soundtrack is pretty good, but gets repetitive after a while. Would recommend if you're looking for a puzzle game.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking for a good Picross game ever since Gemsweeper stopped working on anything newer than Windows 7.  And this is a pretty good one!But.It's not JUST a Picross game.  It's also a visual novel.  And there's a LOT of visual novel stuff between puzzles.  So if you just want Picross this game may not be ideal.  But if you are looking for a visual novel with a bit of Picross thrown in you've found your game!
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I came here mostly for picross and it delivered excellently on that point. I enjoyed the extra "SCOUT's Memories" puzzles that unlocked a new angle of the plot simply by doing a whole lot of picross. The visual novel aspect of the game is less prominent, but what is there is very cute and clever; it's not exactly the most nuanced storytelling but it doesn't need to be. You become attached to the characters and are happy to unravel all the weird new mysteries that spring up. The visual style is  consistently very strong throughout, especially in the character designs -- sort of a combination of Phoenix Wright and TWEWY.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start off by saying that I have always liked doing puzzles including nonograms/picross, so I already knew I was going to like the main gameplay. The puzzles start off easy enough that anyone can learn how to do them, but by the end the puzzles were nice and challenging.What surprised me was the absolutely charming visual novel, with very colourful characters, well-written dialogue, and a good amount of humour. The story is nothing too out there or mind-blowing, but it's still excellent and not too predictable.The music is the icing on the cake, because all of them are earworms that I don't get tired of hearing. Which is why this is legitimately one of my favourite games of all time.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Murder by numbers is basically a glorified picross client and not a very good one at that. The game lacks common picross quality of life options and the sound for hovering over a cell only works sometimes. Also the game seems to have some weird mouse acceleration setting which leads to a sluggish mouse and thus clicking on the wrong square occasionally.The pixel art for the puzzles is often subpar, for a lot of the puzzles it is hard to tell what the image is supposed to be. Even after the game colors it in and tells you what it is supposed to be it often looks nothing like the item in question. This is most likely a deliberate choice because the puzzles seem to be designed for difficulty rather than aesthetics. A good picross game should have both. The game uses mostly 15x15 grids starting from the middle of the second case. The last 2 cases go on for way too long.I’m not the biggest fan of the writing in this game because every case follows the same structure: a murder happens and you are involved you collect insufficient evidenceyou accuse/arrest the wrong personyou go back and collect more evidence you arrest the right personHowever this can be forgiven, what cannot be forgiven is the character design. Every single character is just a stereotype, there is no substance to any of them. While some of these stereotypes are harmless such as “the useless security guard” or the “diva” others are about race and sexual identity. One of the cases plays in a gay bar and pretty much all of the queer characters are portrayed in a tasteless way.Other game mechanics:The scanning is disappointing, at first it seems like it could be fun but you just end up scanning random locations on the screen without rhyme or reason.Sometimes the game asks you to select the correct evidence to progress, however it doesn’t matter what you choose, if you are wrong you can just try again until you are right.Hacking is fine you have to solve 5x5 grids with a time limit and you cannot cross out squares.Showing items to someone is also pointless, you can just show everything to everyone until the story progresses.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Murder by Numbers.  Makes me think of my cousin who was killed when a 42 fell on him.  He was running with an algebra gang, who were always fighting with their rivals, the Trigs, some real radicals.  I suspect it was no accident, and Niven was brought in for questioning, but since it wasn't irrational they had to let him go.But the video game.  Of course.  Murder by Numbers is mostly a visual novel, with the occasional picross puzzle thrown in.  It reads like an old sitcom and looks like everyone is a paper cutout, which makes sense, because the characters you encounter have paper cutout personalities as well.  So far I've seen the world-weary detective, the dim-witted rent-a-cop, self-centered actress, lusty gay guy who constantly makes references to how lusty and gay he is, and a lusty bodybuilder who constantly makes references to how lusty and muscular he is.  Like any formulaic sitcom, it can get a chuckle here and there, but mostly I've been waiting to get to the next puzzle.The plot behind all of this involves looking around the area to find possible clues to the case, then solving a picross puzzle to reveal the item.  You do get to question people, but so far its been a matter of "go through all of the dialog options", and does not seem that you can actually fail in any way.  Everything is pretty casual, and true to the visual novel style, its more watching the story unfold than feeling like a part of the story.It's kind of like a comic book that has a puzzle every few pages, perfect for when you want to relax with a game and not think too hard.  Nothing wrong with that though, so grab a beverage and put your feet up on an ottoman.  I suggest Mehmed VI.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I adore this game. I have spent many hours on this and am so happy to find a nonogram game where I also get a story and beautiful art! The intro song is absolutely charming and upbeat! It makes me want to download the song itself! I appreciate that not only do you have the story mode, but you also have "Scout's memories" where you can freely play nonograms without being tied into the story. I haven't finished it yet; I'm on Case 3 and am excited to finish this game and see how it all ties together. I would definitely play a sequel or similar game if the makers created another one. More than worth it to buy this and enjoy a multi-layered game of calming nonograms, interesting story, and beautiful art.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like logic puzzles? How about visual novels? What about both of them together? If that sounds interesting, this game is for you!I really enjoyed Murder By Numbers! Its the 90s, and Honor Mizrahi is a modestly successful actress on a hit television show. She meets SCOUT, a robot who can't remember where he came from, or what he's meant to do. The two find themselves drawn into a murder case, and decide to work together, to clear Honor's name, and to find SCOUT's purpose!The mysteries were intriguing, and I enjoyed watching the story unfold. The character designs were also great, especially SCOUT's! The gameplay consists of solving nonagram puzzles to find clues, and there are two difficulties available. I have some experience with nonagrams (in fact that's what drew me to this game!), so I went with the tougher difficulty and definitely felt they were suitably challenging! Overall, I'd definitely recommend this game! Though it falls into some "cop-aganda," where the police don't mind breaking some rules to get stuff done, I still felt like the story was good! If you like nonagrams this is a great challenge!
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Ace Attorney with number puzzles!The game was a bit too long but that maybe only seemed so, because I was hooked and binged the last chapters for 9 hours straight at night.There are some minor bugs or missing features like not being able to save during dialogue but otherwise the game was very polished.The characters were likable and the plot kept me guessing.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Chances are if you like nonogram puzzles you will enjoy this game. It has a memorable soundtrack, great art, and a lot of puzzles to play through. It also works well on Linux.If I had a magic wand I would change the following things:- In puzzles it would be nice if clicking and dragging to fill in multiple boxes only filled in a single row or column. I found myself accidentally filling in adjacent boxes I didn't mean to because my mouse didn't move in a straight line. This would be especially helpful during hacking sequences.- It was hard to discern where to look in the investigate screen. Usually there weren't hints on what section of the screen to look at for the next puzzle. Also the screen was visually hard to tell what was going on. I ended up waving my mouse around until I heard beeping.- Add Scout's memories to the trophy list. It's a minor detail but there's a lot more puzzles and some more story after you beat the game, but you wouldn't guess that by looking at your 100% achievement status.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: After having played through the game on Normal difficulty, without the use of hints, the gameplay had a nice difficulty without being too overwhelming. As far as the actual story goes, while predictable at times, I still enjoyed it as it offered a nice continuation between all of the puzzles that needed to be completed.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: This game has an engaging story and fun game play in which you fill out a nonnagram puzzle every time you collect evidence. The puzzles start from being incredibly simple to getting ever harder. I had never played nonnagram puzzles before, but with my love of logic games and the game's way of easing you into them ensured that I was always happy to see a new one.The story of the game is actually good, and you do indeed uncover the happenings behind the various murders as an actress who is down to Earth and a cute flying robot who is trying to figure out his history after waking up in a garbage dump. You see the actress, Honor, progress over the episodes as she starts off as very unsure of herself and dealing with the fallout of a divorce with an abusive ex-husband to someone who develops more into her own person and feels confident with who she is becoming (but not someone who doesn't make mistakes, as her tendency to initially pick the wrong suspect shows). The game gives you a choice between a mode in which the empty squares of the grid are filled in or out in that row if you already filled out the maximum number of squares that the line says can be filled out (as a helpful reminder so you don't accidentally add more squares when that row was basically completed) as well as a mode in which you have to keep track yourself and you can select to fill any square even if it is not supposed to be filled and not hinting that that square is not supposed to be filled in. The game suggests doing the easier mode first if it's your first time playing the game or if you are new to these puzzles, which I also recommend doing as you can feel how, replaying the game to get high rankings and thus complete the optional puzzles, that the game is harder and solving the puzzles is not as easy or quick as before, so doing the harder mode on the first run can take fun out of the game.Not using hints and playing on the harder mode unlocks a higher ranking at the end of a case, with each higher grade unlocking bonus puzzles that you can complete to get four scenes that show bits of Scout's life before the game starts.Last but not least, there are some hacking minigames in which you have to solve a few 5 by 5 square grids with a time limit, and clicking on a wrong square penalizes you by taking some seconds away. These are the easiest to solve grids and have helpful instructions like the row at the middle being 5 squares filled or a row having 4 consecutive squares filled and you know the the first square is filled and thus you do process of elimination. In addition, once you memorize how certain instructions should look (like a row having 3 consecutive squares and then 1 filled squares means you fill out every box in that row except for the second to last one), you find it easier to do them quickly and make fewer errors. They appear about once or twice each chapter.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I love Ace Attorney and detective games. I love nonogram/Picross puzzles.  So I really wanted to love this marriage between the two, and though it does a lot right it also falls a bit flat.The story and writing are pretty good overall, even tackling more mature themes like emotional abuse from a spouse. The main characters are pretty fun and easy to like, even if one of the major ones isn't seen beyond case 2.  However, the overall story lacks a bit of punch.  In fact, the final case, which usually supposed to be the most gripping to leave the player with a satisfying conclusion, is easily the weakest one.  There is little to keep you guessing and the leads are painfully obvious, which is kind of necessary because, frankly, the protagonist is not a good detective.  She's constantly having the wrong people detained and arrested, which is almost comical by the end.  The tone is also a bit all over the place.  Honor unpacking and learning to move on from a toxic relationship is side-by-side with a silly robot and an anime art style that clashes with some of the material.  This could have been handled in a way so that the levity would provide a nice break from the heavier stuff, but it never seems like the more emotional stuff hits hard enough. And the final story was likely going for a more touching emotional conclusion but doesn't feel as serious or important as the other stuff.Ultimately what bogs the game down is the marriage between visual novels and nonograms.  It's great in theory, as the idea of a robot scanning clues being represented as Picross puzzles makes sense in both plot context and as a gameplay hook.  But the nature of nonagram puzzles means that the plot will be interrupted for a long period of time as you work out the puzzle.  It makes less sense in story context when there's supposed to be dire peril and you're farting around with a newspaper puzzle for 10 minutes with no real sense of danger.  More successful are the hacking mini-games, in which several small nonograms are given to you in quick succession with a time limit. I think these are when the combination gameplay that Murder By Numbers was going for actually comes into its own, but are few and far between.For those who strictly want the puzzles, there's a decent amount, including bonus puzzles that are opened up for playing without using the hint system. However, none of them are terribly challenging or meaty until the final case.There's a lot of great ideas and potential in Murder By Numbers, and Honor's personal story and growth are enough for the writing to hang its hat, but ultimately Murder By Numbers is an uneven affair. Here's hoping for a sequel that learns from this game's shortcomings and makes a more well-rounded experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I only recommend the game if you're a hardcore picross connoisseur like myself.   The puzzles themselves are a little underwhelming if you're used to playing Jupiter's Picross series, but the cute artstyle and my down badness for Jena kept me from dropping the game, even though it really drags in the last act. The last case alone took about half of my playtime, and I had stopped being invested in the plot    -picross is fun  -cute artstyle  -investigating crime scenes is fun    -the plot starts to drag in the last act    best visual novel picross game I've ever played.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Picross or even Sudoku puzzles, give this one a look. Its a well written visual novel with Picross puzzles thrown in to break up the story. It eases you in slowly with small grid puzzles, but by the end you are doing 15x15 squares. Some of the puzzles are outright diabolical but all of them can be solved without guessing (e.g. logically).
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Fun nonogram puzzles wrapped in a decent, if predictable, visual novel.Controls could've been better for controllers/Deck, since in the dialogue tree you can't just click on "present evidence" but you have to click on SCOUT with your 'mouse', and playing with gamepad doesn't immediately change this.The narrative aspect is straightforward and predictable. If you've experienced any type of detective story at all, you won't be surprised by any of it. This annoyed me from time to time (but perhaps I'm just not cut out for visual novels). For instance, the toxic ex-boyfriend trope is played so over the top and straight I was expecting them to do a twist and have the main character *actually* be delusional, with perhaps SCOUT just existing in her head. Nope, he's really just *that* controlling.The characters are predictable but fun, though they don't keep them on until the end. The aforementioned toxic ex (who you'll just love to hate), the controlling mom (who never gets any form of comeuppance) and the sassy gay friend are absent from the fourth (and final) case, and the ♥♥♥♥♥♥-but-lovable actress is gone after case two, so in case four only the cold-but-defrosting veteran cop is left.All in all, if you enjoy nonograms this is a fun game to get on a sale, and if you also enjoy corny visual novels it's a must. There's nothing revolutionary going on here but what it does, it does fine.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: This game was obviously inspired by ace Attorney. It has some great humor, fun characters, but far less red herrings for the cases. It's also worth noting that this game single-handedly got me into nonogram puzzles and I have not regretted this purchase. My only dislike is the lack of achievements. I love achievements and there are only achievements for completing the cases. Would've loved to see an achievement for reaching S rank Detective or the like. Hope that gets added in the future :)
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Good game.Only complaints are certain text boxes seem to auto-advance, and if you happen to click during them it seems like it will end up skipping the next text box along with it.There is also another issue where if you unlock bonus puzzles from attaining a certain rank in a case (let's say S), if you reload a save from that case at an earlier rank (for example, to explore dialogue you may have skipped over), and rank up in that old save (let's say C to B), the puzzles you unlocked at the higher-rank will be re-locked by the game (the A rank and S rank bonus puzzles) so you have to redo the rest of the case.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: As an Ace Attorney fan and a Picross lover, there's no way I wouldn't wholeheartedly recommend this game! As soon as the opening song rolled in, I was hooked. The background music is fun and upbeat, delightfully reminiscent of Ace Attorney. The story is pretty stereotypical of those games too, with murders happening around every corner and due process being very low on the priority list. The picross actually has a good difficulty curve -- the first case's puzzles are simpler and often mostly symmetrical; the last cases have bigger trickier ones. It doesn't get too hard, though, and there's no penalty for messing up as long as you get it in the end with no assists!Caveats: Could use a few QoL features, like skipping already-seen dialogue and solved puzzles. And could always use more K.C., because he is an absolute delight (this is not really a caveat.)
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Only recommended if you have the patience for 30+ hours (normal difficulty, including the bonus scenes) of solving nonograms.Difficulty-wise, it starts out easy and ramps up over time. Largest ones are 20 x 15, smallest of course 5 x 5.Dialogue is fun to read, murder mysteries are okay. There are some timed nonograms but they are all 5 x 5 and pretty straightforward if you

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who loves solving picross puzzles, this game intriqued me for sure. A friend told me it had the same composer as Ace Attorney and Ghost Trick, which I enjoy both a lot so obviously I had to check it out. Now what it comes to the gameplay itself: besides the puzzles, it seems a little half-assed. Everything felt a little "underbudget" if you catch my drift. _childDocuments_.review: A fun visual novel with delightful characters and just the right amount of plot to resolve the internal story but leave lots of threads hanging for future sequels.  Sure, it was entirely predictable but that's not really the point.  And the 1996 setting worked well too - recent enough to feel modern but without certain ubiquitous technology that would skew the story-telling.The nurikabe puzzles are bordering on the extremely abstract but they are *very* well designed, so that even the larger grids flow logically.  The lack of a 'clear the board' option is annoying (for when you get far enough to know that you made a mistake but not far enough to be able to just toggle it out) but not really that much of a problem.  I'm still not sure what happened in chapter 3 to deny me the top level - I assume there was a puzzle I missed and considering that the system is pretty good at making sure you don't miss anything, that was a surprise.  Recommended to folk who like engaging stories and characters and don't mind an insanely catchy earworm bugging them for days.  And the puzzles aren't bad either.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so at the time of writing, I have completed all four story chapters, and S ranked 3/4 of them, and done all the available bonus puzzles.This gets, a tentative recommendation. If you want a picross game, this is very good. The picross puzzles are generally pretty well done; the difficulty scales nicely from easy 5x5 tutorial puzzles to very hard 15x15 puzzles, with a few somewhat medium difficulty 20x15 puzzles. The puzzles are fun to do, and generally unfold in a really nice way; but the mono-colour nature of them means that very rarely can you actually figure out what a puzzle is meant to represent without being told, particularly since a lot of the images are meant to be complex, multi-colour things. Hell, even the full colour pictures are not great at conveying what the thing is.The story ranges from 'really good' to 'questionable': the first two chapters, and large parts of the fourth chapter are really good. The third chapter is fine; it's not outstandingly written but it's okay.The music is, ehh. I found it repetitive and turned it off completely mid chapter 2: it's possible it gets better in later chapters but I didn't listen so I don't know.The queer representation in this game feels... shallow at best. K.C. is a pretty main character through the first three chapters, and is... generally a shallow white gay stereotype: he loves drag to the point where it often feels like that's the only thing he talks about; and he spends a lot of the first chapter being thirsty as ♥♥♥♥. The third chapter introduces more representation but it's all framed around a drag bar, and generally is very uh, cis white gay male in nature. I don't really think this is inherently bad so much as it feels like it doesn't really do as much with this angle of the game as it could, particularly since there's nods to e.g. Magellens being generally open for anyone who's queer.
