_childDocuments_.review: Alright, dated references to The Police aside,  is a mystery visual novel (VN) game interspersed with Nonogram puzzles (a.k.a. Picross puzzles).  Many would compare this kind of game to Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney (and rightly so) though I personally would relate this game to the Hotel Dusk series of games for the Nintendo DS (for those who remember them).  The basic conceit of the gameplay is you investigate areas by clicking on points of interest, then solving a Picross puzzle to identify the object/clue.  You also question people in the case to reveal more info and areas to explore.  Once you have enough clues and info, you can interrogate the suspect and solve the crime!  But the real question is, is this game worth your money?Oh, and before I continue, for full disclosure I played the Switch version before purchasing on Steam.Honor Mizrahi is a television actress working on a mystery... drama?  Comedy?  Ehh, whatever.  Anyways, she encounters S.C.O.U.T., a floating computer/robot with a heavy dose of amnesia.  Before she do anything else, *GASP* there's been a murder!  And Honor's one of the suspects!!  Now she and S.C.O.U.T. must work together to clear her name and find out "whodunnit."  And that's just the first case.Now, without going into spoilers, I'd say the overall story is fairly box-standard.  There's some twists, some turns, bad guys get comeuppances, the world goes on.  Where the game really shines is in its characters and writing.  The majority of characters are believable, relatable, and sympathetic.  Honor especially shines through as the protagonist.  While leaving some agency for the player, the writers still made her dry wit and sassy attitude come through in spades.  Also, I cannot recall any video game character before Honor being a divorcee (hardly a spoiler since it's brought up in the first 30 minutes), and seeing a character with that emotional background was unexpected and fresh for me.  S.C.O.U.T., on the other hand, is probably one of the weakest characters.  There's only so many jokes about "What is this?  I have amnesia, so let me wildly and incorrectly guess" that I can take before it gets old and grates.  It isn't until the end that you'll see S.C.O.U.T. get some depth, but until then he is very one-note.  Before I move on, I do want to briefly mention that the main side characters - Becky, K.C., and Detective Cross - are top tier side characters, especially K.C.  I couldn't help but love that glorious man's man!!I'm a big fan of Nonogram/Picross puzzles, so I was hoping that there would be some challenge in this game.  The early game puzzles are easy for people new to Picross puzzles, and the tutorial explains things decently as well.  By the end, though, the puzzles are decently challenging on Normal mode.  So I'd say it's fair for all skill levels.  The rest of the game is standard VN fare; as long as you follow the prompts you shouldn't get too lost.On a minor note, the game is fairly short - my last play-through took around 15 hours to 100% everything.  Make of that whatever you will.Well, there really is no other way to put it - the 90's have vomited ALL OVER this game.  The artists went to ELEVEN in evoking the game's time of 1996, and I have no issue in saying they succeeded in just about every way.  Character designs are also excellent across the board; props especially for S.C.O.U.T.'s CRT head...  Why you looking at me funny?The music, from Phoenix Wright veteran Masakazu Sugimori, is also a stand-out... mostly.  See, there are only a few puzzle themes used though the whole game, and if you're like me, you'll definitely notice the repetition.  It gets particularly bad when you're stuck on a puzzle and you're listening to the same loop over, and over, and over, and over, and AHHHHHHHH MUTE THE VOLUME MUTE THE VOLUME.<breathe>So yeah, the game could definitely use more puzzle themes, or at lease have had better variety of stanzas in the loops. Otherwise, the soundtrack is very good and, I'd say, worth the DLC purchase.  Especially for the character themes. is a great Puzzle/VN game that's great for beginners to the genre.  The by-the-numbers (pun partially intended) story gets a lot of heavy lifting from its characters and art design.  I highly recommend this game for genre fans and those curious about getting into Picross puzzles and VN's.  I'd also recommend picking this up when it's on sale - do not overlook this gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little puzzle game with interesting characters and a mostly-good story. There are four different story sections that take about 2-3 hours each.There are at least 4 bonus puzzles locked behind hard mode S-scores, but you don't need to play them to 100% the achievements, just beat the game.My only real complaints are: One that there isn't a quick-finish "Accessibility" option for when you just want to see the story. On normal you can pretty much just "paint" the puzzle and not get penalized, but that still takes time. Having a button to skip it would do the same thing for less annoyance.And Two: There is a lot of very janky shaking and flashing for dramatic impact during dialogue scenes that you never really get used to. It might be more tolerable on a tiny switch screen, but not on a monitor.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr - If you like the sound of Ace Attorney meets Picross then you'll enjoy this, but you need to really like both already.This is a game where you play as an actress turned detective with a cute robot sidekick. There are phases where you're clicking around the backdrop of settings to find clues, and there are phases where you're in dialogue with other characters and trying to piece things together. In both of these, you will very often have to solve a picross puzzle to proceed. Broadly, the three phases are clue finding, reading dialogue, and picross solving. All three of these in isolation are really quite good. The clue finding isn't simple pixel hunting, there are nice indicators for when you're near a clue and when you've found all the clues in an area. As you unlock different areas you can move between them and ask questions to various characters. Nothing too exciting, but thematically appropriate. Very similar to the investigation phases of an Ace Attorney game.The picross implementation is solid, with some small quality of life improvements and an optional clue system that I personally can't comment on. The puzzles never get too large, but the difficulty increases steadily as you progress through the game through careful clue layouts. I'd say the puzzles do a particularly bad job of having their solutions genuinely "look like" the objects they're supposed to represent, which is understandable given that they need the puzzles to get harder and the objects to be very specific, but that's the one small picross charm that's missing here. The dialogue writing is consistently charming. I don't think the overall plot is anything too exciting, but each character has a well defined personality that leads to regular cute and funny moments. There's a variety of topics that you don't often seen in games covered quite well here, though I don't want to spoil anything specific. The charm of the writing is part of an overall very polished aesthetic - I love the character design and the music especially (composed by the same composer as the first Ace Attorney game, and there's no hiding the influence). These elements create a casual, fun experience that I enjoyed throughout the surprising length of the game (it took almost 20 hours to clear roughly 100%).That said, I do think the core conceit of the game is a really awkwardly designed. What happens when you tie picross and a narrative together is that your puzzles are interrupting your narrative. It's pretty rare that I'm in the mood to both solve a and read a story, and the more I'm gripped by the narrative, the less I want to solve a puzzle to read the next line. This only gets worse as the game progresses, as the puzzles take longer to solve in parallel with the narrative trying to build tension. Despite their qualities, the puzzles and narrative are fundamentally at odds with each other, and it made it hard for me to play for more than 30 minutes at a time. I never got sucked into the overall narrative because of the way the puzzles affect the pacing, and there's really only so many puzzles I want to solve in one sitting. So I don't exactly think they found a winning formula here, but the moment to moment gameplay kept me coming back to it over several weeks, and the well polished aesthetic kept those moments fun. That said, if you don't really enjoy the dialogue and really enjoy picross, the awkward switching between them will almost certainly put you off well before you finish the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game! The characters are fun and well-written, and the story is good! The gameplay feels a bit like the investigation sections of Phoenix Wright with a smattering of Picross puzzles by way of SCOUT identifying objects. I can only really think of two drawbacks:First, and the most minor one, is that the story, while fun, is pretty predictable. The second drawback has to do with the bonus puzzles in SCOUT's Memories. They're unlocked as you complete puzzles in each chapter, and if you complete all the bonus puzzles, you get to view an extra scene for each chapter. For most of the game, this is fine, but in Chapter 3 there are several puzzles that are missable, and, if you miss them and want all the bonus puzzles and extra scene, you have to go back and replay the ENTIRE chapter. Would have been nice if they either weren't missable, or if there was a feature that let you solve missed puzzles ala Professor Layton.Also, one final warning: Honor's ex-husband, Ryan, is AWFUL and may be triggering to those who have been in abusive relationships. _childDocuments_.review: A high quality nonogram/picross game mixed with a visual novel. If you like these types of puzzles, there are plenty to find within this game. You evenunlock puzzles in an entirely different section of the game as you complete puzzles in the main game! If you DON'T like these types of puzzles, you're gonna have a bad time. Besides the detective problem solving between puzzles, the core of the game IS just board after board.I am a huge fan of this type of puzzle so it was a no-brainer for me. The story of the game surprised me and I found myself getting into what was going to happen next. Your character is detective of a TV show who finds out she's out of a job. She ends up finding herself working as a real detective as murders keep popping up. The choices I made throughout the game didn't seem to matter which was a disappointment since I like that aspect of visual novels. In some cases, if not all, the game forces you to pick the 'correct' choice as the other choices provide a bit a dialog before taking you back to the choices again. That didn't really detract from the game too much for me as I still thought it was an interesting story.The art style is fantastic and the game even has its own intro animation as if it were an actual TV show. The song of that intro will likely get stuck in your head as you hear it each time you open the game (it is skippable, though you don't like it). The music during the puzzles was good but got repetitive fast.  Found myself muting it and listening to my own music while working them.I really hope for a sequel!

_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge fan of Picross puzzles and of visual novels. This game was presented as a happy marriage between the two of them, so naturally I was interested. What I was met with was a very delightful and charming game, with tons (and tons) of Picross puzzles, woven together with a story and feel that felt Ace Attorney-inspired with some effort and love across everything. THE GOOD: - There are so many Picross puzzles and I thought the interface for doing them was quite well done. - The characters are nearly all very fun, likable, or relatable in some way. I really thought they were the strength of the story, by far. - There's some creativity in how the puzzles represent evidence and scanning the area, with the game trying to give you a reason for there being so many puzzles. - The game length was longer than I expected, with 4 cases to play and a ton of bonus puzzles/content. - Though there aren't too many songs, the music was perfect for the game and still gets stuck in my head. THE NOT SO GOOD:- For a game presented as a visual novel, I thought the story was a bit...weak. The murderers and methods of murder were fairly predictable, as were most of the story beats. Ultimately, it felt somewhat like there were parts that the story was just there to loosely move you from puzzle to puzzle, as if it were an afterthought. - On a similar note, while this seemed to be pitched as a balance between an Ace Attorney-styled game and Picross, the evidence presentation is fairly limited as well. I think at the core, this is a Picross game with some extra bells/whistles to differentiate it. - The gameplay is essentially just a lot and lot of Picross. This isn't necessarily a bad thing, assuming you like those kinds of puzzles. I went into this as a fan, so I was fine with this. However, if someone didn't like that style of puzzle or was unsure, I don't think the other portions of the game outweigh it. So after all that...what's the point? What's the verdict? This game is a weird, niche title. It satisfies fans of visual novels and of Picross. If you fall in one of those categories, you'll probably get some enjoyment out of this game. If you don't, but are open to it, this could be well worth your time too. If you hate visual novels or hate Picross, definitely pass on this one. That said, the Picross puzzles feature a Hint system and difficulty settings, so seasoned puzzlers or newcomers alike can enjoy the experience. However, if you decide to pursue it, I think Murder by Numbers is a unique experience which is a nice breath of fresh air in an era where games are becoming more and more similar as they come out. While I thought the story portion got a little "meh" at times, the overall charm, effort, and love that the team put into this shined through at all aspects and I never wanted to stop playing.I look forward to going back to it to finish up all the extra puzzles whenever I feel that Picross itch and if you have that itch, I urge you to consider giving it a shot too!

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a neat idea, but unfortunately it's a pain to actually play. Need to knock down the resolution to 1080 to do some of the clue finding, long sequences where you can't save and quit, and most frustratingly, timed sequences where you can't progress if you're not fast enough! And you can't save at that spot either.So many puzzle games have an option to skip sequences that require dexterity and reflexes, it's a real shame this didn't. Also the puzzle gameplay itself is in bad need of a rewind option, so you can don't have to restart the whole puzzle when you realize you've made a mistake a little while ago.

_childDocuments_.review: There is far more story than I signed up for. In the first 18 minutes of "playing" the game I got to solve two VERY easy puzzles after the ones in the tutorial, which I couldn't skip even though I'm already very familiar with these puzzles.  My last four minutes of play time were nothing but story, which I was clicking through as fast as I possibly could before giving up and killing it with task manager. _childDocuments_.review: An excellent Picross game. Great story (and fitting). It gets to be a little repetitive, but that's how this genre of game works. The hint system is a great addition for newer players (without penalizing their score), or for people that wanna go through the puzzles quicker. It's a decent length game as well (Probably 10-15 hours on average). Also, the soundtrack is pretty good.It's not perfect. You can't pause during dialogue. It is possible to miss some points (and therefore not meeting the requirement to unlock all the bonus puzzles), and you can't really go back if you didn't save, so you'd have to start at the beginning of the chapter. I would've also appreciated if they added achievements for completing the bonus puzzles, but it's not a big deal.I recommend this game for anybody looking for a fun puzzle game, as well as a good story to go along with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: The nonogram puzzles are definitely the strong suit of this game. I didn't find a single one that required trial and error - there was always a logical method to complete a puzzle, even for the more esoteric ones near the end.  The music is also pretty nice.The story is acceptable - not the best, not the worst. It's just good enough to string in between puzzles and maintain your interest. Some of the deductions don't actually make logical sense - you can see how everything is linked together, but why the links exist in the first place doesn't necessarily make sense.  But for the most part things flow well. The visual novel aspects are by far the weakest elements of the game. Murder by Numbers is missing some of the basic tenets of a a visual novel - a back log, skip function, etc.  In the visual novel segments, you can't even access the menu at all to save/load. Another strange thing is once you enter the save or load screen you cannot exit back out without saving or loading. People say this is similar to Ace Attorney - I agree to an extent, but once you get to the dialogue, there's no way to check your evidence and you have to go entirely by what you remember. I guess that is mitigated by the fact that, to my knowledge, none of the choices you make actually make a difference - you just get looped back to the choice until you make the one the game intended. That choice is not necessarily the correct choice either.I still give Murder by Numbers a thumbs up.  Play for the puzzles and the story that is interesting enough to keep your attention.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I thought it would be be right up my alley. Picross was my favorite puzzle game so I was really looking forward to this. Sadly the story is about 6 times longer than it needs to be and the repetition is exhaustive. It either needs an editor or needs to test your memory less.Story progress is often random and will move on without you, so you can find yourself without a full score on a story because you made progress by talking to the next logical person. The over arching plot will often stop a story dead to take you away for the larger divorce melodrama that just won't stop repeating the same points over and over again sometimes moving location to restate the same things that last scene did.More frustrating than that are the puzzles. They are only about working the grid and eliminating elements, missing a joyful part of Picross, guessing. Everything pictured is at an angle, so you can't get to the puzzle answers any faster through induction and the result is often quite far from the object pictured. (A round gauge is not pictured round, a shoe looks abstract, a flag is a set of waving lines. Everything is cropped too closely.)There is a lot to like between the (perhaps too broad) characters, the settings and the art style but it all hangs around a little too long saying the same thing. (Please for the love of Jebus can we get LGBTQ rep that's not just a collection of lines from drag race. It's been covered.)If I may recommend an alternative for how to write this kind of game well... Google "KISS U". It's half hour demo had more engaging characters and economical delivery of entertaining content in 30 minutes FOR FREE then this  game delivers over any 3 hour period.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: It's decent. The cases and characters are somewhat forgettable because of the constant nonogram interruptions taking you out of the story. None of the story is really all that captivating, especially with the writing trying to be dramatic but the next second light and cheerful music is playing completely removing any tension or intrigue.I primarily played it just to casually solve the nonograms, with the story being kind of an aside, and for that it plays well. The nonograms are somewhat difficult, though they cap out at 15x15 with only one or two toward the very end of the game being slightly larger. Also, they're all just black and white, there's no color nonograms to make it more difficult. The only slight twist used is in some rare cases, a series of small 5x5 nonograms have to be solved within a short time limit, but beyond that, there's no changes to keep the puzzle-solving interesting if you don't already enjoy nonograms.Grab it on sale if you like nonograms.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Murder by Numbers combines visual novels with picross/nonogram solving, with majority of the challenge coming from the latter. In the game you'll play through four cases, and within each one you'll search different locations, interview people, and reveal evidence by solving picross puzzles.The game does provide a tutorial on picross solving, and at least the puzzles I've played (about 50%) have been solvable without guessing. Most puzzles are normal puzzles with no time limit and no punishments for mistakes, however once in each case you'll get at least one timed section with 3-5 5x5 grid puzzles you'll need to solve within a time limit. Making a mistake will deduct your time, but failing simply allows you to try again. There's also an easier difficulty setting where the game offers automatic hints and different functions to help see if you're on the right track.While listening to the soundtrack, it felt awfully familiar for some reason. Not in the way of having heard the exact tunes before, but rather just the  the music gave. Turns out the reason was the composer, Masakazu Sugimori, who's worked on the Phoenix Wright series among other things. The soundtrack is overall just tasty and upbeat, with most tracks providing a pleasant background to puzzle solving, which is the thing that I personally liked about the Phoenix Wright games that are also available on Steam.Overall this has been an enjoyable game with more casual approach to picross puzzles while still providing a decent challenge, well-crafted graphics, and a great soundtrack to boot.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: 'Nonogram meets murder mysteries', is how I'd describe this game.There are plenty of puzzles to solve. The difficulty builds up per chapter. At first, the puzzles might seem too easy if you're familiar with nonograms, but they get more challenging as you progress in the game. I mainly bought it for the nonograms, but the story turned out to be a pleasantly surprising fun bonus.The cast is very diverse, which kept the game entertaining for me. It also helped my brain relax a bit after one puzzle, before starting on the next one. The story's a little darker than I had expected when I saw the trailer, but it was a fun experience for me!
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I couldn't get past the first twenty minutes in this game because you can't go more than two lines of dialogue without the screen flashing and shaking with thwack noises. Not every line has to be overly dramatic to the point of being annoying. If there was a way to turn this off I'd be fine, but it's obnoxious.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: If you like fiddling about & solving nonograms (or picross) in your spare time, this game is a good fun.The underlying main story is also good despite this being a glorified picross game, just don't expect Ace Attorney-depth; you can't really fail a case per say.The main story can run up to 5 hours or so...depending how fast you solve the puzzles.If you also doing the extra ones in SCOUT's memories, it may double the hours because I'm pretty sure they're a bit more than those in the main story.Puzzle-wise, there's a lot to solve if you're also doing the extra picross puzzles in SCOUT's memories.The 'difficulty' ramps up from traditional 10x10 grids to 20x15 grids.There's also the 'hacking' part where you need to solve a few 5x5 grids within the time limit (around a minute or so).Production-wise it's quite good.Characters look great with quite a bit of artistic license.The BGMs are nice to listen to when solving puzzles.There are minor ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ such as you can't really exit/back out of the Load Game interface unless you actually pick a game save to load.The Hints feature (it highlights which row and/or column you can partially solve with purple color) makes solved numbers revert to unsolved state (unsolved is black, solved is grayed out) when you toggle the Hints feature off.The BGM for some puzzles can also distract you from the story progression because sometimes when the story is in a bit of a sombre part, the puzzle's BGM is like the polar opposite...basically screams "YAY MURDER WHOO".Oh and don't mind the 63 hours I've spent on this game.It really is a 5-10 hours game at best.I just happened to fall asleep often after solving 2-3 puzzles in a row and forgot to close the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyable puzzle game with charming characters and good writing. It could use a couple more features, such as a costume change for the characters when they go to the awards show and probably some additional music. Given how much time you spend in the puzzle screen, it would be nice to have additional songs to listen to. I'd definitely play a part 2!
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Delightful Ace Attorney-esque story with great characters and some good plotting. Is heavily reliant on the main Picross puzzle gameplay loop to continue, so if you're not into that you probably won't find too much here. Wish there was more in the department of cross-examination and interogatting witnesses that wasn't simply presenting evidence to them. Overall I loved the game the entire way through.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: When I started playing this game this weekend, I did not think I was going to sink in 15 hours already. I'm big fan of puzzles and it's been awhile since I played any picross. As others have stated, this is like Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney visual novel narrative mixed with picross to find the evidence to solve the case. I loved the music in this game, it is very catchy but also can be very repetitive especially if you have lingering trouble on a puzzle. Overall, I am happy with my purchase. If you like picross, if you like Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney, and if you like visual novels. You can't really go wrong with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I think the puzzles in the game are too easy, considering that you start playing 15x15 puzzles about halfway through and there's no noticeable difficulty increase from that point on. Most of the puzzles just have way too many squares filled in, so they're not really challenging. There's 15x20 puzzles, but only 3 of them. What I do like, however, is that there's a ton of puzzles, which is the main reason I bought the game to begin with. The story isn't bad, but it isn't great either, so I wouldn't recommend this if you're expecting something Ace Attorney or Uchikoshi standard. It's pretty fun for what it is, though. I also like that there's a bit of freedom in choosing where to go first/whether to talk or to investigate first, etc., so the gameplay doesn't feel too railroaded, but that also means that it's possible to miss out on some puzzles and dialogue.Overall, I give the game a 7/10 and I'm pretty happy with the purchase, considering that I bought it 50% off.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: There's a mandatory disclaimer I have to give in that i am near obsessed with nonograms, and if you don't like that type of puzzle, this game will be a nightmare for you, and you should just skip it. The largest board is 20x15, so they don't get too difficult.The art is great and the gameplay is fine but it must be said that the story is pretty... surface level. Every case is pretty predictable and the red herrings are so obviously red herrings that there's no real twist to it. I can promise you that you will know who the Big Bad is from the moment you lay eyes on them. The characters don't really have much depth to them, but they are all pretty likeable. The character design is nice.I think it's worth mentioning, in the current political climate, that the police officer being portrayed as good is very quick to arrest on little evidence and when the main character inevitably finds contradictory evidence and tells him, he is often dismissive of her concerns. Not... inaccurate to irl ig but that behaviour is never A Bad Thing to the point that it made me deeeeeply uncomfortable whenever it happened.The music is a little... full on. The puzzle music specifically is way too much, it gets annoying enough that I muted the sound.TL;DR:PROS: fun puzzles (if you like picross); nice art; ok charactersCONS: lots lots of picross (if you don't like picross); music gets annoying; story is kind of bland; copsoverall i had fun w it?? which is why im recommending it. but its not perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: A quirky little picross game that actually manages to pack in a lot of character development and growth in a short amount of time while also delivering satisfying puzzles. Combined with catchy (but repetitive) music, Murder by Numbers was definitely worth the sale price of 5.99 USD. I would not consider paying full price for it though, unless they added more content.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: The game is actually pretty good even if it is a somewhat questionable decision to make a visual novel with nonogram puzzles.  The story isn't exceptional and overall relatively stereotypical but still okay. The nonogram puzzles get more and more challenging with each case and in the last case it's only 15x15 nonograms. Solving each puzzle earns you points and a rating. With enough points you can unlock additional Nonogram levels. Overall, I recommend the game if you like nonograms, but at the same time there are definitely better alternatives on steam.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: This was a cute visual novel style game that relies heavily on picross/nongrams to progress the story. If you're not good at them or dislike them, this game isn't for you since you can't skip them (there is a hint button but it just highlights numbers). The store page game summary gives a pretty good idea of this games vibe but it is a very linear story. No move is ever wrong and when you fail the hacking portion, it lets you try again as much as you want. There is some lgbtq representation and some mild gender discussion but nothing too deep. I found the game to be funny but it is very rooted in the time period it is set in (1996), and it might not be as enjoyable for people who don't know who Barbra Streisand is. Not to gatekeep or anything but there were jokes from at least twos generations ago lol it just might not be as enjoyableI found the picross/nonograms to be about medium difficulty at the end (lol if you're looking this sentence and then at my play time: I played this after work and I was pretty drained, as well as letting the game sit while I went to do other stuff). If you've eaten and not drained from work, it'll be fine). While the vibe was generally good, I couldn't help but notice that two of the three fat characters were designed with ill fitting clothes because... well they're fat. Mostly, their button down shirts straining or poorly buttoned. There is also a gaslighting controlling ex-husband that was in the story a little too long for my tastes, as well as an invasive mother that's never pleased with anything. Some game mechanics that were annoying but minor. The game doesn't explain how to do the nonograms or what to do. There are some buttons at the top that will temporarily mark a space but it was never explained nor is it labeled with anything. Dialogue goes by fast if you just rapidly click but letting you hold it down should've sufficed imo. You also can't exit the save menu without saving, which is a weird problem.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like a modern Phoenix Wright, with a pretty fun puzzle game in between. Major highlights of the game are the music, writing, and characters. Lots of decently funny moments, in classic VN-lite fashion.Might annoy those just looking for a classic Phoenix Wright experience without the need to solve a mini-sudoku for much of the interactions, but this one's easily worth it.Edit: The one biggest annoyance so far is that reloading a puzzle to a previous state removes the correctly highlighted number grey-outs that was already in place. Hope they could fix this.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I've been streaming this game for a while now and its a lot of fun, the story/characters are interesting and the puzzles on the harder difficulty aren't too difficult to be annoying, but they're hard enough that I do have to spend time thinking about it, which gives me time to interact with chat, and I imagine on the easier difficulty its a lot more beginner friendly as well. If you like picross puzzles and visual novels, this is in my opinion the perfect mix of both types of games.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: This game is extremely addictive, Picross/Nonogram logic puzzles wrapped in an entertaining murder mystery visual novel. The game consists of dialogue choices, investigating the mystery and completing puzzles to move forward. There are 4 detective cases with an overarching story and subplots. Each case has a number of bonus puzzles that you can attempt from the start menu to unlock an extra cutscene relating to it. I am 20 hours in and have just completed the first case and all the bonus puzzles without hints on normal difficulty, so there is a lot of content.The logic puzzles start of easy, there is a good tutorial at the beginning to get you acquainted with them. But they can get incredibly challenging. I had to look up advanced solving techniques to figure out how to solve some of the higher rank bonus puzzles. Alternatively, if you are more interested in the story you can lower the difficulty or use the hints system. The story is very engaging so far and the characters are awesome and funny, I highly recommend this!
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: You think I'm just gonna sit here and listen to not-Phoenix Wright muzak while playing not-Sudoku? ... If you don't think so, you're sadly mistaken. Never got around to playing Picross, but MbN got me hooked instantly. And don't get me started on the earworms. This is the best, most unreasonably catchy soundtrack of the 2020s for me so far. I'd complain that some of the tunes take the "PW homage" thing beyond the breaking point, but since we're speaking banger after banger in a style that's fairly underrepresented (in my game/music library, at least), I'm afraid all I can do is bob my head. (Edit: Holy moly! I did not realize Masakazu Sugimori also did the original PW soundtrack. These tunes are the genuine article!)The plot and characters are of course not in the same league as Phoenix Wright, but the writing is clearly not sub-par. In fact, it's very polished and slick, always accomplishing what it's going for, even if several characters stand out as infuriatingly unlikable. The visuals and presentation in general are of a very high quality, neatly matching the incredible soundtrack, and the puzzle gameplay is, on top of being fun and addictive, quite merciful with its variety of Help mechanics. Total gem of a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: i like murder mysteries and i like picross puzzles, but to be honest this is not the best of either of its genre. it was frustrating getting through the first case when it was pretty easy to guess the murderer as soon as you got   i also had some issues where clicking and dragging with Xs would replace or erase the filled in squares, and vice versa (that might be my fault though, i guess..) picross games typically only let you click+drag to fill in straight lines, and the fact that this one doesn't feels a bit messy and frustrating.also, even after playing through 3 hours (i think im almost done with the first case?)i dont really like any of the characters except scout.im probably going to finish this game, but mostly just to have something to do while spacing out to lectures.TL;DR: youd probably be better off just playing a picross game and a murder mystery at the same time (maybe during autoplay dialogue? i like picross luna personally). you could buy this game on sale too, maybe!
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Murder mystery story told in a VIsual Novel format with wacky characters and humour mixed in, similar to the Ace Attorney games, where you need to solve picross/nonogram puzzles to move the plot along. This was my first time playing a picross game. The puzzles increase in difficulty at a good rate that allows you to learn as you go along, although later when I got to the harder puzzles I had to refer to youtube videos for general tips on how to solve nonogram puzzles (not puzzles specific to the game) because the tutorial at the start of the game which explained how to solve them really only told you the minimum to get you through the earlier easy stages. The hacking sequences (solving puzzles on strict time limit) were the most difficult as one mistake and you'll lose by running out of time, and the puzzles are random, so I had to always keep repeating until I got lucky with puzzles that were simple were enough to get through fast.I do need to mention that I played on gamepad and during the story there were many instances where the interface got stuck and you would lose the cursor when swapping between locations. Frequently had to use the mouse to point to what I wanted to click on in order to progress. There was also 1 puzzle which was impossible to activate via gamepad as the bounding rectangle that you can move the crosshair while searching for evidence within the scene is inside a smaller rectangle on gamepad than it is on mouse, so I physically could not point to the particular puzzle in question. Again had to use the mouse to progress in this situation. The button to show evidence is also not shown on the screen when using gamepad. Given that this game is also on Nintendo Switch, I'm not sure how the developers could have missed these issues or not patched them after release.Gamepad issues aside, the game has addicting gameplay, nice art style and memorable music which doesn't get boring to listen to. I usually tend to get the bundle that includes the soundtrack when buying games (less so nowadays) but this is one of the cases where I'm glad I did. Recommend picking up with the soundtrack as I've re-listened to it outside of the game as well. Total playtime to complete the story and all side content for me as a noob to this style of puzzle was around 45 hours minus a couple hours being afk with the game open.Would buy a sequel if one was made.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Decent casual game. Good soundtrack.Be warned that it's a lot of reading with no voice acting, but you can get away with spamming through dialogs if you really want to.There's 4 cases that get progressively longer, spanning 27+ hours on the highest difficulty without puzzle assistance, with small breaks, and reading everything.It only has 4 achievements for completing the cases, so difficulty choice doesn't matter, optional puzzle assistance doesn't matter, and case grades don't matter. I wish they would've at least had achievements for S-Ranking the cases...
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Do you love Ace Attorney but wish it had more adult jokes? Do you freakin love puzzles? Especially Picross? Do you want a video game with the atmosphere of a Cozy Mystery novel mixed with a 90s sitcom set? Murder By Numbers will be completely up your alley if you answered yes to any of these questions.The characters are adorable. The mysteries are engaging. The storyline keeps twisting and turning as you unlock each new chapter and case to solve.Seriously though, I've been bedridden for a month and this is the only game that captured my attention long enough to distract me from my godawful symptoms. I ended up pulling an all nighter after weeks of fatigue because I just couldn't stop playing. Murder by Numbers is fantastic and my only gripe is that the campaign isn't longer.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: This game has great picross levels. That's the primary reason to play it, in my opinion. If you're familiar with the Phoenix Wright series or other crime solving games, this game might not be up to the standards you hope for. I certainly enjoyed the mysteries, but they were very simple. I began hoping for more twists, and more things to push the characters to their breaking points. There's lots of humorous dialog throughout the game, and there's some spectacular writing, particularly regarding the behavior of Honor's Ex-husband, Ryan. The story shows how manipulation looks in a way not often shown in story telling, especially in video games.So although the story falls just a bit flat, the picross puzzles are outstanding the whole way through the game. You've got no penalty for resetting puzzles, just for getting hints. I'm not the best at picross, but I was able to solve every puzzle without any hints on the first try. There are also a few hacking segments where speed is key and mistakes are penalized, and these are fun challenges on the two or three times per episode they occur.If there was more detective work involved in this detective game, I'd say 10/10 you get exactly what you pay for. What you end up getting is a point and click game with picross, so I'd say a solid 7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. The setting is amazing. The 90s feel is there in full force, but nostalgia isn't the driving force here. It creates its own atmosphere, with strong characters, visuals and, omg, the MUSIC. The music is composed by the man who did music for the Ace Attorney series. You'll hear the soundtrack for a long time -- puzzles take some thought and patience if you're not using assists -- so amazing tracks are a must.The characters are well done and very realistic, though perhaps a tad too much for the ones with foul personalities; there's a misogynist talk show host, the MC's mother is unbearable, I hate the MC ex-husband's guts as well. The ones who are pleasant, whoever, are very pleasant. SCOUT is adorable, Honor does justice to her name, KC is a cool cat. I sometimes feel the foul/pleasant balance is a bit off, but I think the devs emphasized the world view of a woman of colour, who are inevitably targets of a lot uncivil remarks.The plot is very good as well, though I often thought "you're jumping to conclusions, WAIT". I'm still early in the game, despite being 12 hours into it, but I like the way it is going. It seems that the cases are intertwined in a big, well done story arc.Despite the fact that it is a murder mystery, most of the time in-game will be spent doing picross puzzles to uncover evidence. That means that it is a very relaxing game. The complexity of those scales fast, so it keeps you engaged. The only take away from the game is having no "Restart Puzzle" option. If you made a mistake and don't know when, you either have to reload or manually erase every cell (if you don't want to use assists).tl;dr -Pros:- Relaxing picross puzzles will keep you busy most of ingame time.- AMAZING music.- Good setting constructed through characters.- Complex murder mystery.Cons:- Unlikable characters outnumber the likeable ones.- No "restart puzzle" option.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: In short, it's a bunch of picross puzzles with an endearing little mystery story tacked on.  There's no way to fail the "mystery/clues" part - you just talk to everyone and click on all the items until you brute force your way through when you get stuck.  The puzzles get fairly challenging (mostly 15x15s, with a few 15x20s at the end), but the amount of puzzles you have to do kills the pacing for the final two cases.  Probably around 100ish puzzles in total for 20-30 hours of play time if you're not a picross expert.   I 100%ed it in 44hr with a fair bit of idle time.I would've been nice for the devs to be a little more ambitious (finding a way to make the story more of a Phoenix Wright style than basically just a visual novel, for example,  or having the cases be a little less obvious/predictable (excluding the first case)), or switching up the clue-hunting system from the "scan mode" from time to time, but it is what it is. Ultimately, I enjoyed it.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Nonogram or picross puzzles, this is your game. First and foremost, this is so far my favorite game of this year. Between the setting, the dialog, the characters, and the story, I loved every minute I played. The only thing I would note as a negative, is that there isn't more to play! If anyone from Mediatonic is reading, please push for a sequel or dlc! I'd pick up any sort of continuation in a heartbeat! Thank you for reading my review, and I'd love to hear what everyone's favorite character is/was. Mine was a certain brown haired spitfire. I'd say more, but I absolutely hate spoilers. I'll let you guys take the initiative to learn more. ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: A genuinely great little fusion of Picross and Phoenix Wright. Admittedly I was calling a lot of the plotlines before they came up, but that doesn't mean seeing them play out was any less fun, There's quite a fair number of puzzles to play through, and when paired with that enjoyable story, I can easily recommend the game. Do note that my playtime was probably extended by 15 hours, possibly more as with puzzle games, I tend to multitask and leave the game idle in the background. I also played on normal mode without hints, so that I could unlock and complete all the optional puzzles. Also special credit for the extremely respectful handling of what could've been touchy subjects in Case 3. At least as far as I can tell anyway, as someone who has never been involved in that community or had to figure out the issues discussed therein. An easy recommendation for picross lovers.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I was on the fence for a long time whether I'd recommend Murder By Numbers, but after slogging through the story, I realized I was motivated only by the hope that there'd be a scene where the protag's mother had to apologize for being such a terrible person. But nope, she vanishes from the game somewhere in the third case. Just poof, never mentioned again.The murder mystery story is iffy at its best, and the music while doing puzzles is hilariously out of place. "Oh my god, somebody's been murdered!" *upbeat on-hold music plays as SCOUT pieces together a picture of a gun*
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Has a pretty Phoenix Wright feel to it, with the retro 90's styling and the investigative parts. The nice thing is that it holds your hand a lot, so you're more in a virtual novel than an adventure game and with the amount of text involved that's actually kind of nice. Well worth the money if you're into detective games with puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game to anyone who enjoys picross, but it's not without its own errors. 1) I would say the story is slightly lackluster. I mainly got this game because I was told it was similar to ace attorney (although I did have a healthy love for picross before starting) but each case has significantly fewer twists than an ace attorney game. That's not necessarily a bad thing, but I just think the mysteries were a little simple for a mystery game. Otherwise, I did enjoy the storylines between all the main characters, as well as Honor learning to stand up to her ex. 2) As you'll see looking through the discussion board on this game, it has many bugs/errors. It can be very difficult to navigate through the menu and there are some issues that you have to go back through old saves to avoid.3) I also kind of wish there was an achievement or special cutscene for finishing every case with an S rank and finishing all of the Scout's memory puzzles. It felt kind of anticlimactic! overall, it was a cute, pretty fast game that I would definitely recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I was super charmed by this game. I've always been a sucker for murder mystery VNs, but when you combine that with picross puzzles, I knew it was an instant purchase. I enjoyed the writing, even if the twists were a little telegraphed ahead of time. The characters were fantastic! The puzzles were a little on the easier side from what I'm used to, but still a lot of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Why is the story unskippable? Why isn't the tutorial optional? I just want to solve puzzles, I don't care about the story.  I got this game because I saw NL play a little of it and wanted to try it out. If only I had continued to watch his video I would have seen that after the 2nd puzzle it was 20 minutes of "plot" before the third one. I'm returning the game so I won't suffer the same fate.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game due to its length and lack of novelty. The idea of a picross game with a story you play through is a unique one but it's fundamentally a Professor Layton game with only 1 kind of puzzle, and less charm, (but a better ending). This concept could be done for 2 cases with additional novelty like going hintless for the first 2 cases and using hints then on stretches it for 3 cases, but not 4 cases like here.Also, the structure for some emotional scenes got annoying predictable. Character experiences unexpected problem, then runs away, friend character follows and comforts character with platitudes without solving nor dealing with the emotions the character experienced, sad character recovers to move on, repeat until case is over or root of problem is solved. It just became monotonous.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: One big red flag: (without this problem, it would have been a recommended)mandatory olympic timed puzzles.Puzzle game: relax and casualVisual novel: well known for the arcad...lol, no, also relax and casualMandatory olympic timed event in casual and relax games: it's like strawberry and pasta, they don't mix well. I like pasta, i like strawberry but not together. For games it's the same.Or make them non mandatory, or relax or with medals for really good time, i don't care. I just want to be able to play VN and relax or play Puzzle game and relax. Just give me a way to do it.Another default, but not as big: the game never ends. Whhoa, more than 40 hours (played on epic) and i only played half the memory puzzle (still like 35 40 more puzzles to do). The last chapter takes forever, more than 30 puzzles. That's too long.The story:I liked chapter 3 the most. The good: -  good characters, non generic, they really have their own personalities (most of the time).-  The story touch on intersting and sensible subjects like difficulty of small buisnesses, abusive husband, and the drag queen community is approach with great care and i guess knowledge (i didn't know about the whole mother drag queen thingy for exemple). When the story touched on subject i can reliate to, i really enjoyed it.The bad:-  All the stuff around scout and the big evil corporation and the big evil guy working there. It's parodic and feel more like a mediocre B movie, already seen a hundred times. Mouerf, and it's never ending. Got really bored and didn't like the 4th chapter.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: This game has an odd way of appealing to both children and adults at the same time. At first, you're listening to a cutesy, hoakey intro, and next they're making jokes about tampons and British people pissing into cups.I'm not really sure who the intended audience is for this game, but I guess it's me because I enjoyed it. I almost wanted to hate it at the beginning, but it grew on me.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely, wholeheartedly recommended!This is such a relaxing and wholesome game. I got this game on the Nintendo Switch originally but I loved it so much I bought it again in the Collector's edition on Steam just to support the developer.The characters are hilariously stereotypical and the dialogues are witty and entertaining. Plus, SCOUT is so adorable. The game has a LOT of puzzles and dialogue in visual novel style, and if you're a murder mystery fan like me, you'll love it.I'm definitely not a numbers person and the puzzles are not easy for me but the accompanying soundtrack is so fitting and so relaxing, it makes it extremely enjoyable.Murder by Numbers opened my eyes to how great indie games can be and I really want to thank the dev team for making such an inclusive and unique game. I'm definitely looking forward to a sequel to Honor and Scout!
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Murder by Numbers is a fun and enjoyable game in the style of Ace Attorney and other similiar VNs. It's cliché, it has various humerous characters and the soundtrack, while a bit repetitive, is nice to listen to. It's very much a western love letter to both Japanese VNs and the picross genre.You play as a former actress turned private investigator, solving murders together with a robot that you find. There are four cases where each have its own storyline and characters, but it also has overarching plot where you get to know both the main character, her companion and the recurring supporting cast (such as her mother, a police detective, a stylist, etc.). It all ties together neatly in the fourth and last case. Well almost.The gameplay is interesting as the developers mixes your typical VN together with picross which adds more to the game. With that said, I do think that some of the timed puzzles are very hardcore and at times it felt like pure luck was the reason why I managed to finished them (mainly during case 3 and 4).I definitely recommend this game! It's fun and the picross puzzles aren't too hardcore, but instead enjoyable to solve. I want more of this, and apparently so did the developers as there is a slight hint for a continuation towards the end of the game. However after this game release the studio, Mediatonic, released the popular game Fall Guys and subsequently got bought by Epic Games. I unfortunately do not see the studio working on any other games for a foreseeable future.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Oof, no. The intro sequence is fun and the puzzles (once you get to them) are too... but that's about it. You have to wade through a lot of inane, cringe-worthy dialogue between insipid, annoying, utterly unappealing and dislikeable characters with lots of random interruptions by "slap" noises and screen-shaking for no apparent reason, and the story is just... stupid.  There's been a murder, and so your character's first instinct is apparently to try to escape the room that the detective has locked up all the witnesses in (because somehow he didn't bring anybody to interview them) in order to "to prove her innocence"?  Even the ditziest character there tells her how stupid an idea that is, particularly given she has a really obvious motive to commit the crime. But no, we just go ahead and do that anyway... At that point I gave up and refunded the game. Given the dumb story, characters and tedious conversations with the constant interruptions (and only about 5 puzzles in 73 minutes of play) it just wasn't worth it. You can find nonograms online for free - you're much better of doing those than wasting your time and money on this, even if it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Ace Attorney-style visual novels even a little, and like Picross a lot, this game is amazing. I fit that demographic perfectly, and I loved it. The characters are really fun, and the puzzles are enjoyable. Be warned: there is a LOT of Picross, so if you don't enjoy them, probably not the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there were a 'maybe' button for whether to recommend. The picross puzzles are fairly simple but well-executed, with a smooth and satisfying interface. The graphic novel they're buried in is charming enough but has a humour level roughly equivalent to a Saturday morning cartoon. It feels like it's written for intelligent children. The characters overdo every tiny joke, every quip is accentuated with a sound effect, every time a character is startled there's a BANG sound and the screen flashes white, and there's no way to fiddle with settings to get rid of any of these special effects. And there is a LOT of clicking through lines of dialogue to get to the next puzzle. To find the puzzles you have to pixel-scan a static image until you find what the devs want you to click on. This might be a completely empty area of the picture. Overall a good picross buried in an infuriating wrapper. I don't think I'll be playing more. If these little points don't bother you though, I think this game might be worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great! The writing is hilarious and it reminds me a lot of Ace Attorney in terms of its mysteries -- you'll probably figure out who the killer is before the end of a case, but you'll enjoy the twists and turns in getting the necessary evidence. SCOUT and Honor are both very likable protagonists and I found myself getting pretty invested in their adventures. The art is lovely and the music is great too.I had never played Picross before and found that the difficulty curve was just right for me. If you've played before, the early bits of the game might seem a bit too easy and if you dislike logic puzzles, you might find the challenging later puzzles frustrating, but I thought it was a good balance. There is a hint system that is quite fair and helpful -- your score is penalized for certain hints (filling in random spaces and checking what you have so far for errors) but unaffected if you just toggle on the basic hints, which highlights any rows where it is possible to fill in or cross out squares based on what you already have filled in. This allows you to get a hint when you get really stuck without penalty while still feeling challenged to figure puzzles out on your own. If you solve all of the puzzles in a case without any penalties, you will unlock bonus puzzles. Solving all of the bonus puzzles in a case unlocks an extra scene from SCOUT's memories. These scenes are not necessary to understand the plot, but they are a pleasant extra that makes the extra effort feel worthwhile.All in all, I enjoyed this a lot and hope that they make a sequel at some point!
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a blast!  It's four different cases and all of them were a lot of fun to discover and investigate.  The main selling point of this game is the charming characters as well as the puzzles.  I really love nonograms so this is a no brainer if you're into those types of puzzles.  If you aren't this game isn't for you period as that is the bulk of the actual game play besides some dialogue branches.  I really hope they make a sequel to this game.  Highly recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: I think SCOUT is one adorable character, but the game is a No. Thumbs up just for supporting indie game.For game mechanism: I don't think nonograms game systems blends well with the visual novel adventure game. I find doing the nonograms really boring and tiring, first the puzzle object was not drawn in the background, I have to randomly click everywhere to find them; Second, the puzzle solution -- pixel art of the object -- is always hard to recognize (even after I saw the final pixel art box), ideally we start with the target object in mind, their shape/lines should share some hints for the nonograms puzzle, together with the numerical numbers to achieve a faster solution, but clearly the numbers and art are not that carefully 'tuned'; Last, the non-stop seemly-random nonograms hurt the immersiveness of the story.Storywise: the theme of the story is nice, but the execution is crude. The lovely supporting characters seems disposable after their own chapter, they don't really have any impact on the final moment. , especially the next move in the game was another nonogram accompanied by SCOUT's smiley face and happy uplifting music. Let alone the core crime case design is like a child's play.The game has potential, it could have been better.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: Murder by Numbers feels like a louder and flashier Ace Attorney, with lots of humor and camp. However, the real kicker on if you will this game is whether or not you enjoy nonogram puzzles. Without including the bonus unlockable puzzles, each case has anywhere between 20 to nearly 40 puzzles of differing difficulty. So if constant grid puzzles aren’t your thing, you might want to sit this one out.

_childDocuments_.review: Murder By Numbers is a great visual novel split up in 4 distinct cases. You find evidence by solving Picross puzzles and solve cases by presenting the right evidence. It's a connected plot over the four cases and it's fairly simple to follow and somewhat predictable, but still a good time with some good themes and lessons. The music also absolutely slaps.The only small issue I have with the game is that it's a bit tedious at times. Most Picross puzzles, at least after Case 2, are essentially 15x15 puzzles, which can take up to ten minutes to solve. If you want the best rating to unlock some bonus puzzles and extra story, you also have to solve them flawlessly. It can get a bit tedious at times that puzzles take so long to solve; this could have been broken up by introducing some smaller puzzles here and there and not having most puzzles be 15x15. If you only got half an hour to play, you will  barely be making problems and only solve like three puzzles, so the pacing was a bit off. Anyway, that *is* the point of the game, so maybe this isn't a real problem, but I felt it should be mentioned.There are also some points in which you have to access / hack devices by doing a timed puzzle. I passed all those the first try, but some only barely and I can definitely see those being a problem if you have a slow reaction speed or need more time to think. They aren't too frequent, but still.  It's a great time full of charm and a definite recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great game that incorporates picross (pixel art) with solving murders. You play as a former tv show detective and have a companion that helps you collect evidence which you reveal by solving the picross. If moving your mouse around is too much for you, you can also use your arrow keys, Z to place a block, and X to place an x. The allows hints to help solve to puzzle, but keep in mind that it does take away from your final score of that chapter. It's a great game to relax to. You're able to take breaks without losing your place and it allows you to continue even if you forgot most of the story for that chapter.

_childDocuments_.review: I made it a fair bit into the first "case". It mainly consisted of clicking through un-skipable dialogue broken up by pixel hunting to trigger a picross puzzle. The puzzles are fine, the dialogue is awful. Imagine the most chauvinistic, misogynistic male power-trip and then invert it. A POC female protagonist is surrounded by a cast of 2-dimensional stereotypes that are all written to be completely worthless in different regards. A blonde, white self obsessed ♥♥♥♥♥ who gets all the attention. An obese, nervous and scatterbrained male security guard who literally looks like a pig and would forget his own name if he didn't wear a name tag. A sexist, meathead, bodybuilder, handy-man who outright sexually harasses the protagonist. A sweaty, male, internet nerd with coke bottle glasses and anger management issues. And finally an older male investigator who is angry and aloof and treats every member of the cast including the protagonist as the petulant children they are.The only ALLIES the protagonist (called "Honor" btw...) gets is a gay stylist (is that even a thing?:O) who complains about needing the toilet a lot and a robot with memory loss who fails to tell the difference between a car key and a tampon... Needless to say I prefer nuanced narratives where characters are not cardboard cut-outs with "traits" pinned to the front. I wouldn't mind the poor characterisation if there was not such an overbearing amount of unskipable dialogue. Alas thats mainly what this game has to offer.TL/DR: Don't care for hackneyed, misandrist, male or female power fantasy and cringy dialogue that makes no sense. Since that is what makes up the majority of this game I cannot recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a picross game. Picross is nothing revolutionnary and you can find a million puzzles in game. If you like the game, it's for it's story and plot. It's fine, but I wasn't a huge fan, and it felt at times like it went a bit too slow despite the story being so short. Perhaps it could have used an extra case to spread things out. If you're a fan of detective stories with a cute robot sidekick, maybe you'll like this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Phoenix Wright with Picross! I had a really good time playing this, the story, the cases, and the music are fantastic. Picross was also a lot of fun, if you don't know what it is, it's a little like Sudoku. The game does a good job of explaining how it works and I never needed the hints (although they are there if you do!)My only/main problem with this game is that there were a lot of bugs when it came to launching it/quitting it. According to the forums it sounds like it's due to the Steam Cloud Sync, but basically every time I quit the game from the menu it crashed - and it wouldn't always launch without an error message.  I feel that would be easy for the devs to fix though, and the game itself outside of those tech issues is fantastic!

_childDocuments_.review: Case closed. If you enjoy fun stories with lots of twists, as well as nonograms, this game is absolutely for you! Lots of interesting and unique characters and a storyline that fits seamlessly with one another.I played this game continuously until completion because I've got a cruddy memory and coming back to a storyline later down the road just wasn't going to work for me. It may be a few years before I decide to ever do another nonogram, but aside from being burnt out.. to the point of dreaming of nonograms.. this game was amazing. I felt really connected to everything and I'm really glad I was able to get the game through 2021's Jingle Jam, as although the game was great, it's not one I would have ever thought I would enjoy.Upon beating the game, after the credits play, a sequel is teased.

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really enjoyed my time with Murder by Numbers! I can't stress how well the game handles the mysteries and letting you put the pieces together yourself, while also guiding you towards the correct solution in a way that feels fair. I will admit, sometimes I was able to predict pretty well in advance what was going to happen, but there were plenty of other times I was blindsided by a great twist. I heartily recommend this game to anyone who enjoys nonogram puzzles.My only critique, and this is probably known to the developers, is that by its very nature the game had a pacing issue. While playing, I ended up deciding to collect all the investigate clues before interrogating, which I think led to the smoothest progression. However, there were lots of times I really just wanted to progress the story and instead I had to do a 15x15 nonogram that by the end didn't take forever, but at least 10 minutes and on average more like 20. The climax of the game was lessened slightly by a start-stop-start-stop of nonograms versus plot... by the middle of act 4 I felt like I'd mastered what the game had to offer in terms of nonogram difficulty and would've preferred some smaller, easier puzzles or some twist on the nonogram formula to spice things up. The timed challenges were very tricky, and I felt like they tested my skill much more than the huge puzzles. I would've liked some intermediately sized nonograms with a longer timer to continue that style of puzzle; they were my favorite by far and when I beat them I felt the most satisfaction outside of solving the mystery, which I want to reiterate I really loved.Overall, a hard recommend even if you're new to nonograms like I was and just want to try a cute puzzle game. I am super excited to see if we get a sequel!

_childDocuments_.review: Received in the 2021 Jingle Jam bundle.Mystery solving, point and click puzzles, and picross are all things I like, so I really wanted to like this game. Sadly I only managed to get through an hour of the incredibly cringy dialogue between all the characters, and the plot.Artwork/Art Style: Awesome!Music: Poppin and groovin! (Other reviews say too few tracks for the length of the game)Floating robot (Scout) dialogue: Hilarious! But it seems all effort was focused here, instead of spread throughout the rest of the game.All the other characters: in your face stereotypes, and incompetence. I was spamming left click constantly by the time I uninstalled the game.Picross puzzles: More difficulty levels please. I've been completing 15x15 picross puzzles daily on my phone, just barely big enough for my fingers, for a very long time now. A few of the puzzles in game have unique shapes, so that was a nice surprise, but I was hoping for much larger and more difficult puzzle options. Maybe I missed the button/option somewhere, but not being able to skip the tutorial was also very painful. I was forced to fill out the puzzle in a predefined order, which is great for first time players, but horrible for anyone who already knows what to do.In game UI: Appears it was designed for small screens, so everything is way too large on my PC monitor. It also wasn't very clear if I had found everything or completed a dialogue tree."Investigate" with the floating robot Scout: You move the cursor around a room, and it turns red when you hover over the right spot like a metal detector. In many cases, there is nothing else visibly worth looking at on screen, so you end up just wildly moving around until you find something. There were instance where I got stuck because I didn't know there were still things to "find" with Scout.If none of these things bother you, you might still enjoy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: (NOTE: It's very easy to accidentally get soft-locked/stuck on Case 2. There's a guide for getting un-stuck but you do have to restart the whole Case. It seems like this issue has been in the game for quite a while--many months, at the very least--so I'm not sure why the developers *still* haven't bothered getting a fix out.)Good visual novel + puzzle game. I had actually never played a nonogram game before this, but the tutorial was pretty thorough and I was able to get the hang of it after 3 puzzles or so. If you like Sudoku, then you'd probably like nonogram games, too. I played on Easy with assist mode so I'm not sure how the gameplay fares for more veteran nonogram enthusiasts. The story itself was decent and the main characters were all pretty likeable. The art style is nice and visually appealing.Music was great! I was not expecting it to be so catchy lol.Really, the only bad thing I have to say about this game is the softlock issue. Other than that, it's enjoyable and I would be interested in a sequel!

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a mix between a Phoenix Wright style of game with the added element of Picross every time you find a clue. Whilst the story is intriguing with some colourful characters and some interesting twists and turns. The gameplay lets it down, with the game boiling down to moving a cursor over a static background wait for it to turn red and then playing a 15x15 picross game. Picross solutions dont really resemble the item you have "found" and the background doesnt change or contain these clues in them for you to spot. The game also has one other flaw and that's the music, whilst it is very nice over the course of the 15-20 hours to complete everything it gets very very repetitive so much so I had to mute the game audio and put my own tracks or podcasts on instead.Overall the game is a 6/10 and if I could give it a mixed review I could. But as a huge fan of both picross and Ace Attorney style games, I would give this a pass. In a sequel I would want to see the gameplay mixed up with some different styles of picross to complement the intriguing storyline.

_childDocuments_.review: It's like the investigations phase of Ace Attorney but you solve a Picross puzzle every time you find a clue. Unfortunately, the investigation half of AA is the weaker half, and without the logic puzzles of AA trials for you to figure out what happens, finding evidence doesn't really feel rewarding, and the cases kind of solve themselves. The writing can be hit or miss; getting to know the colorful cast of characters is fun, but a lot of the plot points (perhaps intentionally) require too much suspension of disbelief and hand-waving for my taste. 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: It's like Picross meets Phoenix Wright. The Phoenix Wright part is pretty toned back/simplified gameplay-wise and mostly just serves as a delivery method for the story, but I'm okay with that, as the nonograms are the main gameplay loop here. Brings back fond memories of playing Picross DS obsessively.If you're just looking to quickly knockout a bunch of puzzles, maybe look elsewhere, as there's a lot of dialogue/story to work your way through. I do think the story is fun and compelling though. You do unlock bonus puzzles as you progress the story and you can select any of those puzzles from a separate menu to solve whenever you'd like.
_childDocuments_.name: Murder by Numbers

_childDocuments_.review: You ever hear that something is greater than the sum of its parts? This is the opposite. Everything that went into this game is great: engaging story, colorful characters, attractive 2D art, one of my favorite videogame soundtracks of all time made by Masakazu Sugimori of Ace Attorney fame, but the game is just, not great.I like nonograms, I don't like them enough that I want to do as many as are provided in the story of the game (I skipped all the bonus puzzles). I like mystery games and visual novels, but if you remove the nonograms the visual novel portion is really quite short, and you also lose out on the opportunity to listen to some of the best music in the game like "The Unbeatable Duo".I applaud the developers for trying something unique. I also hope they don't make a sequel with the same nonogram based mechanics because there is literally 0% chance I'd buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: The only good thing to happen involving police in 2020!It's Picross, but also a series of murder mysteries set in the 1990's with endearing characters, and excellent music from the composer behind the music of Phoenix Wright. I enjoy this substantially more than any of the Picross titles on the Nintendo 3DS so far, and the story is really engaging and well written.Well worth the very reasonable price of admission if you like picross, a good whodunit, or adorable amnesiac robot companions with a cathode ray tube monitor for a face.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like pure logic puzzles with a dose of Phoenix Wright "show this inventory item to this person to point out a contradiction" then this is a great game for you. The puzzles can get a little repetitive, there are probably hundreds in the same format with a few "mini speed puzzles" thrown in. Characters and stories are well written, it is much tighter than Phoenix Wright in that the characters don't repeat themselves endlessly so the story between puzzles moves at a fair clip.

It'd be nice to have a more streamlined way of getting into the puzzles without having to interact too much with the story, as the puzzles themselves are quite fun.

_childDocuments_.review: A great game about solving murders while playing picross/nonogram! I enjoy playing picross games in general and this game gave both the basics, challenge and some additional quality-of-life mechanics that made the game all around enjoyable. The story itself is very nice and the characters are charming and fun to interact with. The cases blend in well together to be part of a single narrative, even though they might be a little bit predictable at times.The only real downside to this game is that I've experienced some bugs while using a gamepad to switch locations. Other than that there's a few missable puzzles (I personally experienced one) which prevents you from getting an S rank on the case and having to redo the entire case to get an S rank to unlock the final puzzles necessary for unlocking SCOUT's memory. It doesn't help that you can't skip cutscenes either.I also really appreciate the nod to LGBT+ representation in the game, including a little interaction regarding SCOUT's gender identity as a robot and how they should handle it. It might seem small but means a lot, to me at least.

I recommend playing it on easy mode unless you just really really really like doing the grid puzzles. _childDocuments_.review: Murder By Numbers is definitely your game if you love picross and Phoenix Wright — heavy emphasis on that order. With a seemingly unending amount of picross puzzles at your disposal and plenty of murders to solve, Murder By Numbers accomplishes everything it sets out to do (and then some). With delightful characters woven through intricate storylines that stay interesting, Murder By Numbers will keep you clicking pixels until your eyes bleed to figure out what happened next. Also, the soundtrack is going to live rent-free in your brain for the rest of your life and you’re going to be totally happy with that. If you’ve been dying to get your hands on more well-written detective content, this is absolutely your game, and, from what I can glean, best experienced on Steam. Be sure to give Murder By Numbers a shot — just remember that the auto-solve button is your best friend!

_childDocuments_.review: Achievements: Attainable on all difficulties, unmissable.  Murder by Numbers is a sub-par mystery game, but a great picross game.  Don't expect to have to do a lot of detective work.  The story is very, very linear.  There's only a few choices in the game, mostly about who the suspect is-- and the game never punishes you for choosing incorrectly.  The art is gorgeous, the characters are super lovable, the story is compelling.  The picross puzzles themselves are constructed well, never requiring any guesswork.  While there are a few quality of life features missing like a save mid-puzzle or an undo button, it's still very fun to play.  The game flows surprisingly well despite stopping every few minutes for a picross break.  I would've liked to have more interaction with the story, but otherwise the game was great.  If a picross game with a detective-themed kinetic novel attached sounds good to you, then I recommend this game.  Be aware, while the bonus puzzles are not required for 100% achievements, you'll need to play the game on the highest difficulty without hints to unlock all of them.  If you accidentally skip a puzzle during a chapter, you'll have to repeat the whole chapter to unlock the bonus puzzles.  The story segments that the bonus puzzles unlock are underwhelming, although the puzzles themselves are still fun to complete.  But, again, this is not at all required for 100% completion.
